skills.name: 1d-projection-spatial-averaging-acceleration
skills.search_text: 1d-projection-spatial-averaging-acceleration Use when simulating vendor- and sequence-specific MRS basis sets (PRESS/MEGA-PRESS/HERMES/HERCULES) at 3T where a full 3D spatial loop over every voxel location is too slow and voxel-averaged FIDs suffice. When the target experiment needs full per-voxel spatial fidelity, not voxel-averaged basis functions (the method collapses spatial dimensions by averaging). When simulating STEAM or SPECIAL localization — these are not implemented in MRSCloud and the 1D projection method as described is built for PRESS/sLASER. When the basis set must replicate a specific phantom-measured vendor basis set (e.g. press_te30_3t_01a.basis) whose waveforms and timings are not documented — simulation cannot capture those differences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3423 Accelerates spatially resolved density-matrix simulation of PRESS/sLASER localization by treating the excitation pulse as ideal and collapsing the density matrix via averaging along one spatial dimension after each slice-selective refocusing pulse, so the spatial loop shrinks from ny x nz to (ny + nz)/2 operations while keeping ICC >= 0.98 versus full-loop FID-A. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: Accelerates spatially resolved density-matrix simulation of PRESS/sLASER localization by treating the excitation pulse as ideal and collapsing the density matrix via averaging along one spatial dimension after each slice-selective refocusing pulse, so the spatial loop shrinks from ny x nz to (ny + nz)/2 operations while keeping ICC >= 0.98 versus full-loop FID-A.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target experiment needs full per-voxel spatial fidelity, not voxel-averaged basis functions (the method collapses spatial dimensions by averaging). When simulating STEAM or SPECIAL localization — these are not implemented in MRSCloud and the 1D projection method as described is built for PRESS/sLASER. When the basis set must replicate a specific phantom-measured vendor basis set (e.g. press_te30_3t_01a.basis) whose waveforms and timings are not documented — simulation cannot capture those differences.

skills.description: Use when selected windows of a SMolESY-enhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum are noise-dominated and low-abundance spin systems (e.g. tyrosine, phenylalanine, histidine, creatinine, choline) must be recovered before integration.
skills.name: 1d-spectrum-noise-reduction
skills.search_text: 1d-spectrum-noise-reduction Use when selected windows of a SMolESY-enhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum are noise-dominated and low-abundance spin systems (e.g. tyrosine, phenylalanine, histidine, creatinine, choline) must be recovered before integration. When working with a raw, unenhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum or a CPMG spectrum — smoothing is defined here specifically for SMolESY-enhanced windows, and applying it to a standard spectrum would erode its native resolution without the SMolESY resolution-enhancement trade-off. When the entire spectrum needs uniform noise suppression rather than selected-window recovery — the article's filter is applied only 'within selected NMR spectral windows', not globally, and window selection logic (which bins to smooth) is part of SMolESY-select, not this filter step. When the goal is baseline correction or macromolecule suppression — those are separate SMolESY features; the 11-point filter only denoises, it does not remove broad baseline components or macromolecular signals. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Applies an 11-point moving-average smoothing filter over user-selected spectral windows of a SMolESY-enhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum, suppressing random noise to recover low-abundance metabolite signals such as tyrosine, phenylalanine, histidine, creatinine, and choline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Applies an 11-point moving-average smoothing filter over user-selected spectral windows of a SMolESY-enhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum, suppressing random noise to recover low-abundance metabolite signals such as tyrosine, phenylalanine, histidine, creatinine, and choline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When working with a raw, unenhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum or a CPMG spectrum — smoothing is defined here specifically for SMolESY-enhanced windows, and applying it to a standard spectrum would erode its native resolution without the SMolESY resolution-enhancement trade-off. When the entire spectrum needs uniform noise suppression rather than selected-window recovery — the article's filter is applied only 'within selected NMR spectral windows', not globally, and window selection logic (which bins to smooth) is part of SMolESY-select, not this filter step. When the goal is baseline correction or macromolecule suppression — those are separate SMolESY features; the 11-point filter only denoises, it does not remove broad baseline components or macromolecular signals.

skills.description: Use when a protonated molecular ion structure (.xyz) must be paired with collider gas-atom initial conditions (position, impact-parameter cutoff, velocity scale) to launch collision-induced-dissociation MD trajectories.
skills.name: ab-initio-md-collision-trajectory-setup
skills.search_text: ab-initio-md-collision-trajectory-setup Use when a protonated molecular ion structure (.xyz) must be paired with collider gas-atom initial conditions (position, impact-parameter cutoff, velocity scale) to launch collision-induced-dissociation MD trajectories. The input is an experimental spectrum or spectral library entry — this skill generates collision initial conditions, not spectra or scores (use CIDMD_analysis/CIDMD_compare downstream). The molecular ion geometry has not yet been quantum-chemically optimized (e.g. raw Avogadro sketch) — geometry optimization with unrestricted B3LYP/6–31G* in TeraChem must precede setup. Multiple-collision sequences are required — the paper notes 'In CIDMD, an automatic multiple collision method has not yet been implemented yet.' Sets up CIDMD collision initial conditions by placing an argon collider atom on a user-defined envelope surface around a protonated molecular ion and sampling impact geometries (randomized or Lebedev-deterministic) to generate start.xyz/vel.xyz inputs for NVE ab initio MD with TeraChem. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00760
skills.summary: Sets up CIDMD collision initial conditions by placing an argon collider atom on a user-defined envelope surface around a protonated molecular ion and sampling impact geometries (randomized or Lebedev-deterministic) to generate start.xyz/vel.xyz inputs for NVE ab initio MD with TeraChem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an experimental spectrum or spectral library entry — this skill generates collision initial conditions, not spectra or scores (use CIDMD_analysis/CIDMD_compare downstream). The molecular ion geometry has not yet been quantum-chemically optimized (e.g. raw Avogadro sketch) — geometry optimization with unrestricted B3LYP/6–31G* in TeraChem must precede setup. Multiple-collision sequences are required — the paper notes 'In CIDMD, an automatic multiple collision method has not yet been implemented yet.'

skills.description: Use when a small molecule (<205 Da initially, extendable to larger metabolites) has no experimental MS/MS library spectrum and a protonated ion structure can be built, so in silico CID spectra are needed.
skills.name: ab-initio-molecular-dynamics-simulation
skills.search_text: ab-initio-molecular-dynamics-simulation Use when a small molecule (<205 Da initially, extendable to larger metabolites) has no experimental MS/MS library spectrum and a protonated ion structure can be built, so in silico CID spectra are needed. The molecule is large (>205 Da in benchmarked cases) and you lack a reference experimental spectrum to optimize vfac/collider parameters against. The molecule has many protomers/tautomers — average CIDMD prediction accuracy decreases with increasing numbers of protomers and tautomers. You need a full fragmentation tree with radical ions; no systematic investigation of radical fragment ions in CID has been done. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Runs NVE-ensemble ab initio MD collisions (CIDMD) between a protonated molecular ion and an argon collider using unrestricted B3LYP/6–31G* in TeraChem, to simulate collision-induced dissociation and predict CID-MS/MS spectra for small metabolites lacking library spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00760
skills.summary: Runs NVE-ensemble ab initio MD collisions (CIDMD) between a protonated molecular ion and an argon collider using unrestricted B3LYP/6–31G* in TeraChem, to simulate collision-induced dissociation and predict CID-MS/MS spectra for small metabolites lacking library spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule is large (>205 Da in benchmarked cases) and you lack a reference experimental spectrum to optimize vfac/collider parameters against. The molecule has many protomers/tautomers — average CIDMD prediction accuracy decreases with increasing numbers of protomers and tautomers. You need a full fragmentation tree with radical ions; no systematic investigation of radical fragment ions in CID has been done.

skills.search_text: abf-format-conversion Use when LC-HRMS metabolomics data arrives in proprietary vendor formats and must be made ingestible by a pipeline that only accepts .mzML or .abf input files. Input files are already in .mzML or .abf format and placed in data/raw_data/ — the workflow's input stage already accepts these and no conversion is needed The analysis goal is automated, in-pipeline format conversion as part of Nextflow4MS-DIAL — the paper explicitly lists data file format conversion as a tool not yet incorporated into the workflow Working with non-LC-MS data (e.g., genomics or LC-MS/MS proteomics pipelines) where mzML/ABF metabolomics ingestion is not the target schema http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 A user-mediated raw-file ingestion step for the Nextflow4MS-DIAL LC-MS metabolomics workflow: proprietary vendor RAW files are converted outside the pipeline into the open mzML format with ProteoWizard msConvert, or into ABF format with Reifycs Abf Converter, before placement in data/raw_data/. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00364
skills.summary: A user-mediated raw-file ingestion step for the Nextflow4MS-DIAL LC-MS metabolomics workflow: proprietary vendor RAW files are converted outside the pipeline into the open mzML format with ProteoWizard msConvert, or into ABF format with Reifycs Abf Converter, before placement in data/raw_data/.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are already in .mzML or .abf format and placed in data/raw_data/ — the workflow's input stage already accepts these and no conversion is needed The analysis goal is automated, in-pipeline format conversion as part of Nextflow4MS-DIAL — the paper explicitly lists data file format conversion as a tool not yet incorporated into the workflow Working with non-LC-MS data (e.g., genomics or LC-MS/MS proteomics pipelines) where mzML/ABF metabolomics ingestion is not the target schema

skills.description: Use when annotating drug analogs in hCom (or similar) microbial incubation LC-MS/MS data and a candidate analog must be classified as abiotic vs. microbially propagated, especially when it appears at t=0 or declines over incubation.
skills.name: abiotic-transformation-product-confirmation
skills.search_text: abiotic-transformation-product-confirmation Use when annotating drug analogs in hCom (or similar) microbial incubation LC-MS/MS data and a candidate analog must be classified as abiotic vs. microbially propagated, especially when it appears at t=0 or declines over incubation. The candidate analog increases in intensity from 0 h to 72 h across triplicates — that pattern indicates microbial metabolism, so use the microbial analog assignment workflow instead of the abiotic confirmation procedure. You are screening drug exposures in clinical/fecal cohort samples without paired incubation controls (drug-only and drug-free), since abiotic-vs-biotic classification requires those controls. The feature has already been classified as an artifact and you only need parent-drug annotation — this skill adds no value beyond GNPS Drug Library matching already performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Distinguishes abiotic (chemical, non-biological) drug transformation products from true microbial metabolism in in vitro incubation untargeted metabolomics, using temporal behavior (t=0 presence, decreasing intensity) and drug-only/drug-free control comparisons, as exemplified by the omeprazole analog at m/z 330.127. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5
skills.summary: Distinguishes abiotic (chemical, non-biological) drug transformation products from true microbial metabolism in in vitro incubation untargeted metabolomics, using temporal behavior (t=0 presence, decreasing intensity) and drug-only/drug-free control comparisons, as exemplified by the omeprazole analog at m/z 330.127.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate analog increases in intensity from 0 h to 72 h across triplicates — that pattern indicates microbial metabolism, so use the microbial analog assignment workflow instead of the abiotic confirmation procedure. You are screening drug exposures in clinical/fecal cohort samples without paired incubation controls (drug-only and drug-free), since abiotic-vs-biotic classification requires those controls. The feature has already been classified as an artifact and you only need parent-drug annotation — this skill adds no value beyond GNPS Drug Library matching already performed.

When the input is already an aligned, RT-corrected feature table — re-running coarse alignment would double-correct retention times When you need the fine-grained deep-learning direct matching (steps 3–5: binning, filtering, alignment); this skill only validates the step-2 pseudo warping component via ablation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validates a reconstructed DeepRTAlign pipeline component — specifically the coarse alignment (pseudo warping function) step — by running the pipeline with the component ablated and confirming that the with-coarse-alignment AUC exceeds the without-coarse-alignment AUC, matching the paper's Supplementary Table 5. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5

skills.description: Use when a paper claims performance gains from several newly added components and you must reproduce/verify the per-component contribution breakdown via controlled ablation, e.g. CFM-ID 4.0 on Metlin ESI-MS/MS prediction.
skills.name: ablation-component-contribution-attribution
skills.search_text: ablation-component-contribution-attribution Use when a paper claims performance gains from several newly added components and you must reproduce/verify the per-component contribution breakdown via controlled ablation, e.g. CFM-ID 4.0 on Metlin ESI-MS/MS prediction. The goal is overall spectral-prediction accuracy or compound identification benchmarking, not attribution of gains to individual components — run full CFM-ID 4.0 against CFM-ID 2.0/3.0 without ablation variants. Input spectra come from instruments other than QTOF — the authors note CFM-ID 4.0 currently does not handle MS spectra collected on non-QTOF instruments. You cannot retrain model variants (only pretrained deployments are available), since the ablation requires training each reduced configuration under the same cross-validation setup. Decomposes a multi-component method's reported performance gain by cumulatively ablating its added components (here CFM-ID 4.0's molecular topology features, sequential ring cleavage modeling, and MSRB rules) and attributing metric deltas to each component. Yields quantitative contribution shares rather than a single aggregate accuracy claim. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Decomposes a multi-component method's reported performance gain by cumulatively ablating its added components (here CFM-ID 4.0's molecular topology features, sequential ring cleavage modeling, and MSRB rules) and attributing metric deltas to each component. Yields quantitative contribution shares rather than a single aggregate accuracy claim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is overall spectral-prediction accuracy or compound identification benchmarking, not attribution of gains to individual components — run full CFM-ID 4.0 against CFM-ID 2.0/3.0 without ablation variants. Input spectra come from instruments other than QTOF — the authors note CFM-ID 4.0 currently does not handle MS spectra collected on non-QTOF instruments. You cannot retrain model variants (only pretrained deployments are available), since the ablation requires training each reduced configuration under the same cross-validation setup.

skills.description: Use when reproducing an ablation that isolates a component's contribution: you have two checkpoints (pre-trained encoder vs. random init) for the same conditional generation task and need paired deltas on shared metrics such as top-1/top-10 accuracy and FCD.
skills.name: ablation-experiment-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: ablation-experiment-comparison-analysis Use when reproducing an ablation that isolates a component's contribution: you have two checkpoints (pre-trained encoder vs. random init) for the same conditional generation task and need paired deltas on shared metrics such as top-1/top-10 accuracy and FCD. The goal is to compare different spectra modalities (IR-only vs. Raman-only vs. UV-Vis-only) rather than to isolate the effect of encoder initialization — that is a separate multi-modal conditioning ablation. You lack a pre-trained encoder checkpoint for the component in question; with only a randomly initialized model you cannot form the pre-trained/untrained contrast. You need experimental/laboratory validation rather than computational reproduction — the DiffSpectra validation is stated to be primarily computational. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Quantifies the contribution of a pre-trained encoder by re-running a conditional generative pipeline with two initialization variants (pre-trained vs. randomly initialized) and comparing paired metrics side-by-side, as done for SpecFormer in DiffSpectra's spectral structure elucidation ablation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Quantifies the contribution of a pre-trained encoder by re-running a conditional generative pipeline with two initialization variants (pre-trained vs. randomly initialized) and comparing paired metrics side-by-side, as done for SpecFormer in DiffSpectra's spectral structure elucidation ablation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare different spectra modalities (IR-only vs. Raman-only vs. UV-Vis-only) rather than to isolate the effect of encoder initialization — that is a separate multi-modal conditioning ablation. You lack a pre-trained encoder checkpoint for the component in question; with only a randomly initialized model you cannot form the pre-trained/untrained contrast. You need experimental/laboratory validation rather than computational reproduction — the DiffSpectra validation is stated to be primarily computational.

skills.description: Use when you must attribute a reported accuracy gap (e.g. DeepION COL 86.73% vs second- SimSiam on 98 annotated ion images, 17 categories) to a specific design choice, by retraining the same SimSiam-based architecture with and without that component and comparing on a fixed benchmark.
skills.name: ablation-study-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: ablation-study-baseline-comparison Use when you must attribute a reported accuracy gap (e.g. DeepION COL 86.73% vs second- SimSiam on 98 annotated ion images, 17 categories) to a specific design choice, by retraining the same SimSiam-based architecture with and without that component and comparing on a fixed benchmark. The ion images lack manual annotation, so the 98-image/17-category leave-one-out linear classifier benchmark cannot be constructed for a like-for-like comparison The target task is isotope ion discovery (ISO mode with intensity-dependent missing value augmentation) rather than colocalized ion (COL) representation quality You want to compare architecturally different methods (e.g. SIM-based PCC/R2 vs deep models) rather than attribute a single model's gain to one of its own components http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Runs a controlled ablation in which the full model and a stripped baseline share identical architecture and training settings so that any performance delta can be attributed to a single component — here, DeepION's MSI-specific augmentation (Poisson noise, random missing value) versus SimSiam's natural-image-only augmentation on the rat brain colocalization benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Runs a controlled ablation in which the full model and a stripped baseline share identical architecture and training settings so that any performance delta can be attributed to a single component — here, DeepION's MSI-specific augmentation (Poisson noise, random missing value) versus SimSiam's natural-image-only augmentation on the rat brain colocalization benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ion images lack manual annotation, so the 98-image/17-category leave-one-out linear classifier benchmark cannot be constructed for a like-for-like comparison The target task is isotope ion discovery (ISO mode with intensity-dependent missing value augmentation) rather than colocalized ion (COL) representation quality You want to compare architecturally different methods (e.g. SIM-based PCC/R2 vs deep models) rather than attribute a single model's gain to one of its own components

skills.description: Use when a multi-component deep learning prediction pipeline must be attributed to its parts: train ablation variants (e.g., with/without Gaussian-noise augmentation or contrastive loss) and measure which component drives accuracy gains on a held-out test split.
skills.name: ablation-study-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: ablation-study-benchmark-analysis Use when a multi-component deep learning prediction pipeline must be attributed to its parts: train ablation variants (e.g., with/without Gaussian-noise augmentation or contrastive loss) and measure which component drives accuracy gains on a held-out test split. The goal is end-to-end benchmarking against external baselines (SIRIUS, BUDDY) rather than attributing performance to the pipeline's own components Working with Orbitrap data, where no data augmentation is applied (noise addition lowered similarity for Orbitrap spectra), so a DA-ablation arm is not meaningful The model is a single-component predictor with no post-processing or secondary scoring stage to ablate http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduce component-wise ablation of a deep learning pipeline (FIDDLE on MoNA Q-TOF MS/MS) by training model variants with individual components removed (data augmentation, contrastive loss, post-processing) and quantifying each component's contribution via top-1/top-5 accuracy, missed-atom distributions, candidate coverage, and ROC AUC of confidence scores. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Reproduce component-wise ablation of a deep learning pipeline (FIDDLE on MoNA Q-TOF MS/MS) by training model variants with individual components removed (data augmentation, contrastive loss, post-processing) and quantifying each component's contribution via top-1/top-5 accuracy, missed-atom distributions, candidate coverage, and ROC AUC of confidence scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is end-to-end benchmarking against external baselines (SIRIUS, BUDDY) rather than attributing performance to the pipeline's own components Working with Orbitrap data, where no data augmentation is applied (noise addition lowered similarity for Orbitrap spectra), so a DA-ablation arm is not meaningful The model is a single-component predictor with no post-processing or secondary scoring stage to ablate

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a CVAE-based ST-SM integration model and you must justify design choices (loss function, normalization, decoder sharing) with quantitative ablation evidence.
skills.name: ablation-study-loss-and-decoder-comparison
skills.search_text: ablation-study-loss-and-decoder-comparison Use when benchmarking a CVAE-based ST-SM integration model and you must justify design choices (loss function, normalization, decoder sharing) with quantitative ablation evidence. Input ST/SM data are at single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only You need to integrate more than two modalities — SpatialMETA currently supports only two modalities (ST and SM) The goal is horizontal (cross-sample) integration benchmarking rather than within-sample vertical integration design ablation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3912 Systematically ablates SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM design components — SM loss function (Gaussian vs MSE), SM normalization, and shared vs independent decoders — to quantify how each affects vertical integration of ST and SM data in the ccRCC case. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z

skills.description: Use when you have relative abundance time-course metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec) from a single-compartment intracellular metabolic system, and you need standard-free absolute concentrations by leveraging mass balances and known kinetics.
skills.name: absolute-concentration-inference-from-relative-abundance
skills.search_text: absolute-concentration-inference-from-relative-abundance Use when you have relative abundance time-course metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec) from a single-compartment intracellular metabolic system, and you need standard-free absolute concentrations by leveraging mass balances and known kinetics. Data are extracellular or multi-compartment (e.g. eukaryotic systems with transport reactions across compartments) — MetaboPAC only applies to intracellular samples in a single compartment Response factors vary with concentration (violated linear dynamic range / ion suppression), since MetaboPAC assumes constant response factors The data have substantial missingness — 10% missing values with imputation already reduced inferred-concentration accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 MetaboPAC infers absolute metabolite concentrations from relative abundance time-course GC-MS metabolomics data by fitting response factors using metabolic mass balances, either via a kinetic-equation (KE) approach or biological-heuristic penalties, without requiring chemical standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: MetaboPAC infers absolute metabolite concentrations from relative abundance time-course GC-MS metabolomics data by fitting response factors using metabolic mass balances, either via a kinetic-equation (KE) approach or biological-heuristic penalties, without requiring chemical standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are extracellular or multi-compartment (e.g. eukaryotic systems with transport reactions across compartments) — MetaboPAC only applies to intracellular samples in a single compartment Response factors vary with concentration (violated linear dynamic range / ion suppression), since MetaboPAC assumes constant response factors The data have substantial missingness — 10% missing values with imputation already reduced inferred-concentration accuracy

skills.summary: Internal-standard-based normalization of lipidomics data matrices to yield absolute concentration values per lipid and per sample, as implemented in ADViSELipidomics for LipidSearch/LIQUID outputs.

skills.description: Use when a processed FT-ICR MS peak table (abundances + assigned molecular formulas) needs per-sample chemodiversity quantification grouped by experimental variables, distinguishing abundance-based indices from functional (trait-based) diversity.
skills.name: abundance-diversity-index-estimation
skills.search_text: abundance-diversity-index-estimation Use when a processed FT-ICR MS peak table (abundances + assigned molecular formulas) needs per-sample chemodiversity quantification grouped by experimental variables, distinguishing abundance-based indices from functional (trait-based) diversity. Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must be performed before MetaboDirect, so raw spectra need prior processing (e.g., MFAssignR) Goal is taxonomic/sequence-based community diversity rather than chemodiversity of mass spectrometry peaks The peak table has not been normalized — compute diversity only after test_normalization-guided normalization to avoid intensity-scale artifacts Computes per-sample abundance-based diversity (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1) and functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy) on sum-normalized FT-ICR MS peak intensities with assigned molecular formulas, as implemented in MetaboDirect's chemodiversity analysis step. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Computes per-sample abundance-based diversity (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1) and functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy) on sum-normalized FT-ICR MS peak intensities with assigned molecular formulas, as implemented in MetaboDirect's chemodiversity analysis step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must be performed before MetaboDirect, so raw spectra need prior processing (e.g., MFAssignR) Goal is taxonomic/sequence-based community diversity rather than chemodiversity of mass spectrometry peaks The peak table has not been normalized — compute diversity only after test_normalization-guided normalization to avoid intensity-scale artifacts

skills.description: Use when you need to predict community growth or feasible compositions at a given abundance profile, or enumerate all cross-feeding interactions independent of abundance, from single-organism genome-scale SBML models.
skills.name: abundance-profile-constrained-growth-modeling
skills.search_text: abundance-profile-constrained-growth-modeling Use when you need to predict community growth or feasible compositions at a given abundance profile, or enumerate all cross-feeding interactions independent of abundance, from single-organism genome-scale SBML models. The input is not a genome-scale single-organism SBML model but raw omics data or a pre-built community model without member-prefixed IDs and a shared exchange compartment The goal is single-species (non-community) metabolic analysis, where PyCoMo's compartmentalized community structure and exchange-compartment machinery add no benefit A visualization of an existing community model is needed instead — ScyNet network reduction/contextualization, not model construction, is the right tool http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Build and simulate compartmentalized community metabolic models with PyCoMo/COBRApy that switch between fixed growth rate with variable abundance profile and fixed abundance profile with variable community growth rate, enabling FBA growth-rate prediction and enumeration of exchange metabolites and cross-feeding interactions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: Build and simulate compartmentalized community metabolic models with PyCoMo/COBRApy that switch between fixed growth rate with variable abundance profile and fixed abundance profile with variable community growth rate, enabling FBA growth-rate prediction and enumeration of exchange metabolites and cross-feeding interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a genome-scale single-organism SBML model but raw omics data or a pre-built community model without member-prefixed IDs and a shared exchange compartment The goal is single-species (non-community) metabolic analysis, where PyCoMo's compartmentalized community structure and exchange-compartment machinery add no benefit A visualization of an existing community model is needed instead — ScyNet network reduction/contextualization, not model construction, is the right tool

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS feature has an accurate m/z and an experimental retention time, and you need to enumerate putative metabolite candidates and rank them using projected predicted RTs.
skills.name: accurate-mass-candidate-search
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-candidate-search Use when an LC-MS feature has an accurate m/z and an experimental retention time, and you need to enumerate putative metabolite candidates and rank them using projected predicted RTs. The feature has no experimentally acquired RT (e.g., no chromatographic method to project onto), so ranking must rely on accurate mass alone You need spectral (MS/MS) matching rather than mass-plus-RT annotation — this skill only searches m/z against HMDB and ranks by predicted RT The target chromatographic method has fewer than ~50 identified molecules to fit the quartic RT projection regression http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retrieves all putative molecular identities for an unknown feature by accurate mass search of its protonated/deprotonated ion m/z (10 ppm tolerance) against the HMDB molecules with KEGG numbers, then ranks candidates by RT error so the correct identity lands in the top 3 in ~70% of cases. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Retrieves all putative molecular identities for an unknown feature by accurate mass search of its protonated/deprotonated ion m/z (10 ppm tolerance) against the HMDB molecules with KEGG numbers, then ranks candidates by RT error so the correct identity lands in the top 3 in ~70% of cases.

skills.search_text: accurate-mass-feature-matching-across-platforms Use when an unassigned LC-HRMS feature recurs across instruments/platforms (e.g. positive-mode NIST plasma on Orbitrap Fusion and Q-ToF Impact II) and needs annotation to a named metabolite with an MSI confidence level. skills.description: Use when deisotoped ion m/z values from imzML-based MSI lipidomics data need putative lipid annotations (e.g. DAG, TAG, PC, PE, PS, LysoPC, CE, SM, Cer with [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M+K]+, [M+NH4]+ adducts).
skills.name: accurate-mass-lipid-annotation
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-lipid-annotation Use when deisotoped ion m/z values from imzML-based MSI lipidomics data need putative lipid annotations (e.g. DAG, TAG, PC, PE, PS, LysoPC, CE, SM, Cer with [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M+K]+, [M+NH4]+ adducts). Input is already a feature table with lipid annotations, or the goal is confident identification — an accurate-mass database hit is only the first step and requires MS/MS confirmation Data are not lipids or the lipid classes of interest fall outside the searched classes/adducts (e.g. classes not in the DAG/TAG/PC/PE/PS/LysoPC/CE/SM/Cer positive-mode or PC/PA/PE/PS/PG/PI/FFA negative-mode lists) The m/z list has not been deisotoped and filtered (peakpicker.bin, deisotope), since annotate expects deisotoped ions http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assigns putative lipid identities to deisotoped ions from mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data by accurate-mass matching against a lipid m/z library generated on the fly by massPix (makelibrary) from fatty acid, head-group and adduct combinations. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1252-5
skills.summary: Assigns putative lipid identities to deisotoped ions from mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data by accurate-mass matching against a lipid m/z library generated on the fly by massPix (makelibrary) from fatty acid, head-group and adduct combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table with lipid annotations, or the goal is confident identification — an accurate-mass database hit is only the first step and requires MS/MS confirmation Data are not lipids or the lipid classes of interest fall outside the searched classes/adducts (e.g. classes not in the DAG/TAG/PC/PE/PS/LysoPC/CE/SM/Cer positive-mode or PC/PA/PE/PS/PG/PI/FFA negative-mode lists) The m/z list has not been deisotoped and filtered (peakpicker.bin, deisotope), since annotate expects deisotoped ions

skills.description: Use when LC-HRMS feature tables (MS1 m/z, retention time, peak area) from preincubation (0 h) and postincubation (24 h) human liver S9 incubations are available and candidate metabolites must be confirmed by accurate-mass (±5 ppm) matching against BioTransformer 3.
skills.name: accurate-mass-ppm-matching-metabolite-confirmation
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-ppm-matching-metabolite-confirmation Use when LC-HRMS feature tables (MS1 m/z, retention time, peak area) from preincubation (0 h) and postincubation (24 h) human liver S9 incubations are available and candidate metabolites must be confirmed by accurate-mass (±5 ppm) matching against BioTransformer 3. Input is a raw mzML/Thermo RAW file rather than an MZmine 2.53 feature table — peak detection must be run first. Samples lack a matched 0-hour preincubation control, so the temporal differential criterion (present at 24 h, absent at 0 h) cannot be evaluated. The target metabolite is generated by extrahepatic or S9-absent enzymes (e.g. intestinal or renal biotransformation), which the article notes PharmMet DB is expected to miss. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Confirms candidate drug metabolite signals by matching accurate MS1 m/z within a ±5 ppm mass window against BioTransformer 3.0 predicted metabolites and against the 24-hour postincubation human liver S9 sample, ensuring that each annotated metabolite in PharmMet DB rests on a mass-accurate, time-differentiated detection rather than an unvalidated in-silico prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.dmd.2025.100183
skills.summary: Confirms candidate drug metabolite signals by matching accurate MS1 m/z within a ±5 ppm mass window against BioTransformer 3.0 predicted metabolites and against the 24-hour postincubation human liver S9 sample, ensuring that each annotated metabolite in PharmMet DB rests on a mass-accurate, time-differentiated detection rather than an unvalidated in-silico prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw mzML/Thermo RAW file rather than an MZmine 2.53 feature table — peak detection must be run first. Samples lack a matched 0-hour preincubation control, so the temporal differential criterion (present at 24 h, absent at 0 h) cannot be evaluated. The target metabolite is generated by extrahepatic or S9-absent enzymes (e.g. intestinal or renal biotransformation), which the article notes PharmMet DB is expected to miss.

skills.description: Use when a feature/peak table from HILIC-Q Exactive HF or CSH-Q Exactive HF runs contains accurate m/z, retention time, and signal intensities for features that lack MS/MS spectra, and matching in-house m/z+RT libraries acquired under identical conditions are available.
skills.name: accurate-mass-retention-time-library-matching
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-retention-time-library-matching Use when a feature/peak table from HILIC-Q Exactive HF or CSH-Q Exactive HF runs contains accurate m/z, retention time, and signal intensities for features that lack MS/MS spectra, and matching in-house m/z+RT libraries acquired under identical conditions are available. The feature has an acquired MS/MS spectrum — then precursor accurate mass plus MS/MS matching (or authentic-standard MSI level 1 identification with precursor mass, RT, and MS/MS) should be used instead, since it carries higher confidence No in-house library acquired under identical chromatographic and mass-spectrometric conditions exists for the assay — retention-time windows are only valid under matched conditions The goal is MSI level 1 identification — m/z and RT alone can never reach level 1, which requires authentic standards with precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Annotates metabolite features as MSI level 2 using only accurate precursor mass (ppm-level) and retention time matched against in-house libraries acquired under identical chromatographic and MS conditions, without any MS/MS spectral matching. In the urine untargeted metabolomics study this extended coverage beyond the 578 MS/MS-annotated compounds by six additional acylcarnitines and 201 further low-abundance compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Annotates metabolite features as MSI level 2 using only accurate precursor mass (ppm-level) and retention time matched against in-house libraries acquired under identical chromatographic and MS conditions, without any MS/MS spectral matching. In the urine untargeted metabolomics study this extended coverage beyond the 578 MS/MS-annotated compounds by six additional acylcarnitines and 201 further low-abundance compounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature has an acquired MS/MS spectrum — then precursor accurate mass plus MS/MS matching (or authentic-standard MSI level 1 identification with precursor mass, RT, and MS/MS) should be used instead, since it carries higher confidence No in-house library acquired under identical chromatographic and mass-spectrometric conditions exists for the assay — retention-time windows are only valid under matched conditions The goal is MSI level 1 identification — m/z and RT alone can never reach level 1, which requires authentic standards with precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching

skills.description: Use when prioritizing HRMS features (mzML, ddMS2) for potential PFAS and you want to flag those matching known suspect compounds by exact mass, e.g. NIST- or CompTox-derived lists.
skills.name: accurate-mass-suspect-screening
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-suspect-screening Use when prioritizing HRMS features (mzML, ddMS2) for potential PFAS and you want to flag those matching known suspect compounds by exact mass, e.g. NIST- or CompTox-derived lists. No suspect list is available or the compounds of interest are fully unknown — use KMD and diagnostic-fragment prioritization instead, since suspect screening only flags known exact masses Raw data are not centroided ddMS2 mzML (e.g. profile-mode or vendor-proprietary .d files not converted via MSConvert) — convert or preprocess first Goal is quantitation or confirmation with authentic reference standards rather than screening-level prioritization — accurate-mass matching alone provides only tentative assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Accurate-mass suspect screening of MS1 features against a custom, extensible PFAS suspect list (.csv, NIST-derived and extendable with NORMAN/CompTox entries) as implemented in the PFΔScreen PFASPrioritization module, flagging prioritized features whose exact masses match suspect compounds within a 4 mDa tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-05070-2
skills.summary: Accurate-mass suspect screening of MS1 features against a custom, extensible PFAS suspect list (.csv, NIST-derived and extendable with NORMAN/CompTox entries) as implemented in the PFΔScreen PFASPrioritization module, flagging prioritized features whose exact masses match suspect compounds within a 4 mDa tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No suspect list is available or the compounds of interest are fully unknown — use KMD and diagnostic-fragment prioritization instead, since suspect screening only flags known exact masses Raw data are not centroided ddMS2 mzML (e.g. profile-mode or vendor-proprietary .d files not converted via MSConvert) — convert or preprocess first Goal is quantitation or confirmation with authentic reference standards rather than screening-level prioritization — accurate-mass matching alone provides only tentative assignment

skills.description: Use when correlating in vivo LC-MS metabolite features with in vitro prototype components by accurate mass and retention time, e.g., MDRB step 1 prototype/isomer classification in TCM disposition studies.
skills.name: accurate-mass-tolerance-filtering
skills.search_text: accurate-mass-tolerance-filtering Use when correlating in vivo LC-MS metabolite features with in vitro prototype components by accurate mass and retention time, e.g., MDRB step 1 prototype/isomer classification in TCM disposition studies. When the task is downstream MS/MS-based scoring (MS2 fragment similarity, MS1/MS2 mass defect) of metabolite–prototype pairs — this skill covers only the step-1 accurate-mass/RT screen. When in vitro and in vivo data were acquired under non-comparable chromatographic methods, since the ±25 s RT window that separates prototype matches from isomers would be meaningless. When mouse metabolite features are already annotated with prototype identities or isomer flags — re-filtering adds no information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 MDRB step-1 filtering that matches mouse (in vivo) metabolite features against the in vitro prototype list using accurate m/z within ±5 ppm, then splits matches by retention time (±25 s) into prototype components versus chromatographically distinct isomers. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: MDRB step-1 filtering that matches mouse (in vivo) metabolite features against the in vitro prototype list using accurate m/z within ±5 ppm, then splits matches by retention time (±25 s) into prototype components versus chromatographically distinct isomers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is downstream MS/MS-based scoring (MS2 fragment similarity, MS1/MS2 mass defect) of metabolite–prototype pairs — this skill covers only the step-1 accurate-mass/RT screen. When in vitro and in vivo data were acquired under non-comparable chromatographic methods, since the ±25 s RT window that separates prototype matches from isomers would be meaningless. When mouse metabolite features are already annotated with prototype identities or isomer flags — re-filtering adds no information.

skills.description: Use when you have natural-isotope-corrected, normalized fatty acid isotopologue distributions from 13C6-glucose tracing and need per-cell (or per-pixel) fractional labelling p of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool, e.g. for ACLY knockdown or control conditions.
skills.name: acetyl-coa-fractional-labelling-estimation
skills.search_text: acetyl-coa-fractional-labelling-estimation Use when you have natural-isotope-corrected, normalized fatty acid isotopologue distributions from 13C6-glucose tracing and need per-cell (or per-pixel) fractional labelling p of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool, e.g. for ACLY knockdown or control conditions. When overall substrate usage is very low, e.g. the hypoxia/normoxia experiment — the article states it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction, so the model was only used for ACLYkd data When you need absolute rather than relative contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool — the methodology cannot quantify pool size When the input is raw imzML or uncorrected isotopologue intensities — natural isotope abundance correction and per-cell normalization must be done first http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Estimates the fractional labelling (p) of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool by fitting a 13C binomial model to normalized, natural-isotope-corrected palmitate (C16) or stearate/oleate (C18) isotopologue distributions, per cell or per pixel, from 13C-SpaceM single-cell data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Estimates the fractional labelling (p) of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool by fitting a 13C binomial model to normalized, natural-isotope-corrected palmitate (C16) or stearate/oleate (C18) isotopologue distributions, per cell or per pixel, from 13C-SpaceM single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When overall substrate usage is very low, e.g. the hypoxia/normoxia experiment — the article states it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction, so the model was only used for ACLYkd data When you need absolute rather than relative contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool — the methodology cannot quantify pool size When the input is raw imzML or uncorrected isotopologue intensities — natural isotope abundance correction and per-cell normalization must be done first

skills.name: acmg-rule-engine-implementation
skills.search_text: acmg-rule-engine-implementation Use when re-deriving ACMG classifications from annotated ClinVar variants (two-star review status) to measure how differences between ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP coding-impact/LoF calls propagate into PVS1-driven classification changes. skills.summary: Implements an in-house ACMG 2015 rule engine (mirroring the GDK platform) that assigns PVS1 from loss-of-function coding impact, applies PP3 at CADD > 25.3 or SpliceAI > 0.5, handles PP5/BP6 strength by ClinVar star rating, and excludes PS4, PM3, PP4, BP2, BP5 to quantify how annotation-tool discrepancies change pathogenicity classifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is guideline-compliant clinical ACMG classification including criteria that this GDK-derived engine excludes (PS4, PM3, PP4, BP2, BP5) When variants lack ClinVar star-rating metadata, since PP5/BP6 strengths are applied on a star-based basis When you need disease-specific evidence-weighting or inheritance-model rules (PM2/PM3), as gene inheritance modes from CGD/ClinGen/PanelApp may themselves be inconsistent

skills.description: Use when you have an AEMS run with a table of inferred ejection times and an extracted TIC trace, and you must define each ejection's detection window bounded by flanking local minima.
skills.name: acoustic-ejection-peak-windowing
skills.search_text: acoustic-ejection-peak-windowing Use when you have an AEMS run with a table of inferred ejection times and an extracted TIC trace, and you must define each ejection's detection window bounded by flanking local minima. Input is raw vendor AEMS data with no upstream ejection-time table — this skill assumes ejection times have already been inferred The goal is peak-area quantification or baseline correction rather than determining per-ejection window boundaries Data are conventional LC-MS chromatograms rather than acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) runs Delimits the per-ejection detection window in an AEMS run by smoothing the TIC intensity trace and locating local minima between adjacent ejection times, then recording peak_time and min_time/max_time per ejection (e.g. as ejection_windows.csv). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03730
skills.summary: Delimits the per-ejection detection window in an AEMS run by smoothing the TIC intensity trace and locating local minima between adjacent ejection times, then recording peak_time and min_time/max_time per ejection (e.g. as ejection_windows.csv).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor AEMS data with no upstream ejection-time table — this skill assumes ejection times have already been inferred The goal is peak-area quantification or baseline correction rather than determining per-ejection window boundaries Data are conventional LC-MS chromatograms rather than acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) runs

skills.description: Use when comparing LC-MS data acquisition workflows (e.g. DDA vs DIA/SWATH vs DaDIA) using detected-feature and MS2-feature counts from the same sample set.
skills.name: acquisition-workflow-benchmarking
skills.search_text: acquisition-workflow-benchmarking Use when comparing LC-MS data acquisition workflows (e.g. DDA vs DIA/SWATH vs DaDIA) using detected-feature and MS2-feature counts from the same sample set. When only one acquisition mode was run and no comparative workflow data exists — the skill requires a side-by-side comparison. The metabolite's exact mass is not yet known or the structure database has not been generated/sampled (this skill ranks existing candidates, it does not generate them) The analysis goal requires incorporating MS/MS spectra or retention-time data — this prior operates on exact mass alone, which the paper describes as accurate 'even in the absence of any other analytical data' Evaluating models trained on non-human metabolomes, since the model was trained and evaluated only on human metabolite structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks DeepMet's mass-based structural prioritization against the AddCarbon baseline by filtering generated-structure databases on exact mass (±10 ppm) and ranking candidates by sampling frequency, then computing top-1/top-3/top-10 accuracies on held-out metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Benchmarks DeepMet's mass-based structural prioritization against the AddCarbon baseline by filtering generated-structure databases on exact mass (±10 ppm) and ranking candidates by sampling frequency, then computing top-1/top-3/top-10 accuracies on held-out metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolite's exact mass is not yet known or the structure database has not been generated/sampled (this skill ranks existing candidates, it does not generate them) The analysis goal requires incorporating MS/MS spectra or retention-time data — this prior operates on exact mass alone, which the paper describes as accurate 'even in the absence of any other analytical data' Evaluating models trained on non-human metabolomes, since the model was trained and evaluated only on human metabolite structures

skills.description: Use when you have a peak table exported from MALDI-MSI software (SCiLS/MSiReader CSV or Cardinal peakBinned imzML) and want to estimate what fraction of peaks are adducts rather than true metabolite signals.
skills.name: adduct-abundance-quantification-per-dataset
skills.search_text: adduct-abundance-quantification-per-dataset Use when you have a peak table exported from MALDI-MSI software (SCiLS/MSiReader CSV or Cardinal peakBinned imzML) and want to estimate what fraction of peaks are adducts rather than true metabolite signals. Input is raw full-spectrum imaging data that has not been peak-picked or binned — mass2adduct works on peak lists, so Cardinal data must already be processed with peakBin() before conversion. The goal is structural identification of a metabolite rather than abundance of adduct peaks; this skill flags adduct-vs-parent relationships by mass and co-localization, it does not provide database identifications. Only a single mass spectrum with no spatial information is available — the corrPairsMSI co-localization step requires per-pixel intensity data from an msimat object. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies the fraction of MS peaks in a MALDI-MSI dataset attributable to metabolite–matrix adducts (Na+, K+, 13C, [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+, [M + CHCA + Na]+) by combining pairwise mass-difference calculation, adduct-mass matching, and spatial co-localization of parent/adduct ion pairs in mass2adduct. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of MS peaks in a MALDI-MSI dataset attributable to metabolite–matrix adducts (Na+, K+, 13C, [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+, [M + CHCA + Na]+) by combining pairwise mass-difference calculation, adduct-mass matching, and spatial co-localization of parent/adduct ion pairs in mass2adduct.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw full-spectrum imaging data that has not been peak-picked or binned — mass2adduct works on peak lists, so Cardinal data must already be processed with peakBin() before conversion. The goal is structural identification of a metabolite rather than abundance of adduct peaks; this skill flags adduct-vs-parent relationships by mass and co-localization, it does not provide database identifications. Only a single mass spectrum with no spatial information is available — the corrPairsMSI co-localization step requires per-pixel intensity data from an msimat object.

skills.description: Use when assigning preannotated metabolite candidates (from a reaction-based pseudo-MS1 candidature space) to parent pesticides via an MS2 similarity network, and adduct/ISF-derived spectral artifacts must be filtered before accepting seed-molecule annotations.
skills.name: adduct-and-in-source-fragment-filtering
skills.search_text: adduct-and-in-source-fragment-filtering Use when assigning preannotated metabolite candidates (from a reaction-based pseudo-MS1 candidature space) to parent pesticides via an MS2 similarity network, and adduct/ISF-derived spectral artifacts must be filtered before accepting seed-molecule annotations. Candidate spectra lack comparable parent-pesticide MS2 spectra, so no seed-molecule similarity link can be built and only pseudo-MS1 (RCS) evidence exists. The goal is definitive structural confirmation, e.g. by analytical/stable-isotopic-labeled standards; this filter only removes spurious adduct/ISF links, it does not replace standard verification. The candidate set was not produced by the upstream CMDN RCS layer and lacks accurate m/z, RT, and MS2 characterization required for SSN-based assignment. A filtering step in the SSN layer of CMDN that removes candidate-parent pesticide annotations driven by adducts and in-source fragments (ISF), which otherwise generate spurious high-similarity links, and retains only links with entropy-based spectral similarity ss >= 0.4. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: A filtering step in the SSN layer of CMDN that removes candidate-parent pesticide annotations driven by adducts and in-source fragments (ISF), which otherwise generate spurious high-similarity links, and retains only links with entropy-based spectral similarity ss >= 0.4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate spectra lack comparable parent-pesticide MS2 spectra, so no seed-molecule similarity link can be built and only pseudo-MS1 (RCS) evidence exists. The goal is definitive structural confirmation, e.g. by analytical/stable-isotopic-labeled standards; this filter only removes spurious adduct/ISF links, it does not replace standard verification. The candidate set was not produced by the upstream CMDN RCS layer and lacks accurate m/z, RT, and MS2 characterization required for SSN-based assignment.

skills.description: Use when preparing the Mol2CCS feature matrix (parquet) from METLIN-CCS or CCSBase records: after computing 256-bit Morgan fingerprints, molecular weight, and 35-dimensional Drug Tax counts, encode adduct, molecule type, instrument type as one-hot vectors and the monomer/dimer association as a.
skills.name: adduct-and-instrument-type-onehot-encoding
skills.search_text: adduct-and-instrument-type-onehot-encoding Use when preparing the Mol2CCS feature matrix (parquet) from METLIN-CCS or CCSBase records: after computing 256-bit Morgan fingerprints, molecular weight, and 35-dimensional Drug Tax counts, encode adduct, molecule type, instrument type as one-hot vectors and the monomer/dimer association as a. Running the original SigmaCCS architecture, which consumes only the molecular graph and the adduct without additional descriptor vectors The molecular structure lacks a defined adduct or instrument type label (e.g. generic neutral-molecule properties unrelated to CCS) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Mol2CCS augments the SigmaCCS graph neural network with seven additional one-dimensional feature vectors per molecule, including one-hot encodings of the adduct form, instrument type, and a binary monomer/dimer association flag, to improve generalizability of CCS predictions across chemical spaces. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Mol2CCS augments the SigmaCCS graph neural network with seven additional one-dimensional feature vectors per molecule, including one-hot encodings of the adduct form, instrument type, and a binary monomer/dimer association flag, to improve generalizability of CCS predictions across chemical spaces.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running the original SigmaCCS architecture, which consumes only the molecular graph and the adduct without additional descriptor vectors The molecular structure lacks a defined adduct or instrument type label (e.g. generic neutral-molecule properties unrelated to CCS)

skills.description: Use when curating a reference MS/MS library (e.g. MGF-format spectra with SMILES, adduct, ionization mode, and precursor m/z metadata) where chemically incoherent annotations must be detected and removed before library cleaning or machine-learning model training.
skills.name: adduct-annotation-coherence-checking
skills.search_text: adduct-annotation-coherence-checking Use when curating a reference MS/MS library (e.g. MGF-format spectra with SMILES, adduct, ionization mode, and precursor m/z metadata) where chemically incoherent annotations must be detected and removed before library cleaning or machine-learning model training. Query spectra in a library-search or spectral-annotation workflow — this is a library-cleaning filter, not a search-time annotation validator Spectra lacking SMILES or parent-mass metadata, since the 0.1 Da parent-mass-vs-SMILES check cannot be evaluated and spectra will simply be dropped by REQUIRE_COMPLETE_METADATA/REQUIRE_COMPLETE_ANNOTATION Input that has already passed library_cleaning_2.yaml; re-running the coherence checks on the already-filtered output is the wrong stage in the prescribed pipeline order http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Validates that MS/MS library spectrum annotations are chemically coherent with their own metadata: the adduct must match the precursor m/z within 0.1 Da and the ionization mode, and the reported parent mass must match the SMILES-derived neutral mass within 0.1 Da. In Spectraverse this is implemented as the matchms REQUIRE_COMPLETE_ANNOTATION filter in the second cleaning round, together with a patched _get_neutral_mass that ignores [M]+/[M]− adducts reporting a charge of zero. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06256
skills.summary: Validates that MS/MS library spectrum annotations are chemically coherent with their own metadata: the adduct must match the precursor m/z within 0.1 Da and the ionization mode, and the reported parent mass must match the SMILES-derived neutral mass within 0.1 Da. In Spectraverse this is implemented as the matchms REQUIRE_COMPLETE_ANNOTATION filter in the second cleaning round, together with a patched _get_neutral_mass that ignores [M]+/[M]− adducts reporting a charge of zero.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query spectra in a library-search or spectral-annotation workflow — this is a library-cleaning filter, not a search-time annotation validator Spectra lacking SMILES or parent-mass metadata, since the 0.1 Da parent-mass-vs-SMILES check cannot be evaluated and spectra will simply be dropped by REQUIRE_COMPLETE_METADATA/REQUIRE_COMPLETE_ANNOTATION Input that has already passed library_cleaning_2.yaml; re-running the coherence checks on the already-filtered output is the wrong stage in the prescribed pipeline order

skills.description: Use when you have authentic metabolite standards run in positive and negative ESI mode as mzML files and need to build a within-laboratory RT/m/z library without relying on MS/MS spectral data.

skills.search_text: adduct-annotation-library-construction Use when you have authentic metabolite standards run in positive and negative ESI mode as mzML files and need to build a within-laboratory RT/m/z library without relying on MS/MS spectral data. Your input is already a finished feature table from a targeted peak-picking tool such as MZmine, El-MAVEN, or MS-DIAL rather than raw standard mzML files. You require MS/MS spectral data as a mandatory part of library construction — metScribeR deliberately focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use or require MS2 for building the library. You only have a single-ionisation-mode run (pos or neg) for the standards; the workflow expects both pos and neg mzML files referenced in standards_df.csv (at least one non-missing per row). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Semiautomated construction of in-house LC-MS metabolite reference libraries by extracting adduct chromatograms from positive and negative ESI mzML files, applying peak-quality filters (≥7 data points per EIC peak, width-at-half-maximum >0 s and <15 s, ≤250 peaks per EIC, intensity ≥10,000), resolving the best adduct per standard, and exporting RT, m/z, and quality metrics as a CSV library. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Semiautomated construction of in-house LC-MS metabolite reference libraries by extracting adduct chromatograms from positive and negative ESI mzML files, applying peak-quality filters (≥7 data points per EIC peak, width-at-half-maximum >0 s and <15 s, ≤250 peaks per EIC, intensity ≥10,000), resolving the best adduct per standard, and exporting RT, m/z, and quality metrics as a CSV library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a finished feature table from a targeted peak-picking tool such as MZmine, El-MAVEN, or MS-DIAL rather than raw standard mzML files.
