skills.name: adduct-assembly-combinatorics
skills.search_text: adduct-assembly-combinatorics Use when building targeted lipidomics precursor/fragment transition lists from lipid class definitions and adduct rules, or when auditing how many lipid classes/molecules an in-silico lipid knowledge base covers. The task needs false-discovery-rate scoring or resolution of coeluting/isobaric lipids and peak area integration — LipidCreator intentionally does not address these Target lipids are bacterial/archaeal classes such as acyl-PG or acyl-PE in E. coli — no standards are available and the knowledge base focuses on eukaryotic model systems Distinguishing stereoisomers at large scale — no isotope-coded standards exist for this in the current implementation http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reconstructs LipidCreator's combinatorial assembly of lipid head groups, fatty acyl chains (or long chain bases), and adducts into precursor and fragment m/z values, emitting a targeted-assay transition list covering 61+ lipid classes and ~10^12 lipid molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Reconstructs LipidCreator's combinatorial assembly of lipid head groups, fatty acyl chains (or long chain bases), and adducts into precursor and fragment m/z values, emitting a targeted-assay transition list covering 61+ lipid classes and ~10^12 lipid molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task needs false-discovery-rate scoring or resolution of coeluting/isobaric lipids and peak area integration — LipidCreator intentionally does not address these Target lipids are bacterial/archaeal classes such as acyl-PG or acyl-PE in E. coli — no standards are available and the knowledge base focuses on eukaryotic model systems Distinguishing stereoisomers at large scale — no isotope-coded standards exist for this in the current implementation

skills.description: Use when a set of tumor-correlated m/z peaks (Pearson correlation ≥ 0.7 with the tumor-class prediction map) from MALDI FT-ICR MSI data needs tentative molecular formula and adduct annotation before downstream interpretation or table export.
skills.name: adduct-assignment-mass-spectrometry
skills.search_text: adduct-assignment-mass-spectrometry Use when a set of tumor-correlated m/z peaks (Pearson correlation ≥ 0.7 with the tumor-class prediction map) from MALDI FT-ICR MSI data needs tentative molecular formula and adduct annotation before downstream interpretation or table export. Peaks whose spatial pattern has Pearson correlation < 0.7 with the tumor-class prediction map — these are not considered highly co-localized tumor-associated features and would dilute the annotation table. Input is already an annotated feature table with formula/adduct assignments (e.g. from a prior HMDB/METLIN search) — re-annotation would duplicate effort. Data acquired without prior peak identification from the VAE module (e.g. raw spectra before msiPL peak identification) — annotation is applied downstream of peak selection, not to raw spectral complexity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates m/z peaks selected from the massNet/msiPL VAE decoder by tentative molecular formula and adduct state (e.g. [M+K]+, [M+2K-H]+) via HMDB and METLIN searches, recording the ppm error for each assignment. This links tumor-correlated spatial features to putative molecular identities for biological interpretation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Annotates m/z peaks selected from the massNet/msiPL VAE decoder by tentative molecular formula and adduct state (e.g. [M+K]+, [M+2K-H]+) via HMDB and METLIN searches, recording the ppm error for each assignment. This links tumor-correlated spatial features to putative molecular identities for biological interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks whose spatial pattern has Pearson correlation < 0.7 with the tumor-class prediction map — these are not considered highly co-localized tumor-associated features and would dilute the annotation table. Input is already an annotated feature table with formula/adduct assignments (e.g. from a prior HMDB/METLIN search) — re-annotation would duplicate effort. Data acquired without prior peak identification from the VAE module (e.g. raw spectra before msiPL peak identification) — annotation is applied downstream of peak selection, not to raw spectral complexity.

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether a CCS prediction model trained on one ion-mobility database (e.g. CCSBase v1.3, 16,989 values / 6,744 molecules) generalizes to a structurally different database such as METLIN-CCS (>27,000 unique synthetic small-molecule structures).
skills.name: adduct-aware-ccs-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: adduct-aware-ccs-prediction-evaluation Use when you need to test whether a CCS prediction model trained on one ion-mobility database (e.g. CCSBase v1.3, 16,989 values / 6,744 molecules) generalizes to a structurally different database such as METLIN-CCS (>27,000 unique synthetic small-molecule structures). Your training and test compounds come from the same database/chemical space — the skill is specifically about cross-database generalization; within-distribution accuracy was already reported as high for all models You aim to improve generalization itself (e.g. via fingerprints, descriptors, instrument type, or confidence-model filtering) rather than quantify the drop; Mol2CCS extensions are a separate skill Your data is not ion-mobility CCS paired with SMILES/adduct annotations (e.g. retention time or MS/MS spectra prediction tasks) http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark graph neural network CCS prediction models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) in a cross-database setting: train on one CCS database (CCSBase v1.3 or METLIN-CCS) and evaluate on the structurally different one, quantifying generalization via R2, MAE, and MRE. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Benchmark graph neural network CCS prediction models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) in a cross-database setting: train on one CCS database (CCSBase v1.3 or METLIN-CCS) and evaluate on the structurally different one, quantifying generalization via R2, MAE, and MRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your training and test compounds come from the same database/chemical space — the skill is specifically about cross-database generalization; within-distribution accuracy was already reported as high for all models You aim to improve generalization itself (e.g. via fingerprints, descriptors, instrument type, or confidence-model filtering) rather than quantify the drop; Mol2CCS extensions are a separate skill Your data is not ion-mobility CCS paired with SMILES/adduct annotations (e.g. retention time or MS/MS spectra prediction tasks)

skills.description: Use when an imzML/mzML-derived m/z peak list from spatial metabolomics data (especially MALDI-TOF, low/medium resolution) needs metabolite annotation against HMDB or LipidMaps in a defined adduct/polarity space, and METASPACE/pySM FDR-based annotation is not applicable.
skills.name: adduct-aware-database-search
skills.search_text: adduct-aware-database-search Use when an imzML/mzML-derived m/z peak list from spatial metabolomics data (especially MALDI-TOF, low/medium resolution) needs metabolite annotation against HMDB or LipidMaps in a defined adduct/polarity space, and METASPACE/pySM FDR-based annotation is not applicable. Data was acquired on high-resolution instruments (FT-ICR or orbitrap) and can be annotated by METASPACE/pySM with FDR control, which is the more established route for that setting. Structural confirmation via pseudo-MS/MS or MS/MS spectral matching is required — use the ms1_id engine against indexed GNPS libraries rather than exact-mass-only database search. The peaks are already annotated and the goal is downstream statistics (differential metabolite expression, pathway analysis, SM-ST integration) rather than annotation itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Annotate raw m/z peaks from spatial metabolomics data by exact-mass matching against reference metabolite databases across a defined polarity/adduct space, as implemented in SpaMTP's annotation engine. This works platform-agnostically, including MALDI-TOF data that METASPACE/pySM does not yet support. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Annotate raw m/z peaks from spatial metabolomics data by exact-mass matching against reference metabolite databases across a defined polarity/adduct space, as implemented in SpaMTP's annotation engine. This works platform-agnostically, including MALDI-TOF data that METASPACE/pySM does not yet support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data was acquired on high-resolution instruments (FT-ICR or orbitrap) and can be annotated by METASPACE/pySM with FDR control, which is the more established route for that setting. Structural confirmation via pseudo-MS/MS or MS/MS spectral matching is required — use the ms1_id engine against indexed GNPS libraries rather than exact-mass-only database search. The peaks are already annotated and the goal is downstream statistics (differential metabolite expression, pathway analysis, SM-ST integration) rather than annotation itself.

skills.description: Use when annotating LC–MS untargeted metabolomics features against a compound database in either positive or negative ionisation mode, and candidate metabolites must be scored accounting for the specific adducts they can form.
skills.name: adduct-aware-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: adduct-aware-feature-annotation Use when annotating LC–MS untargeted metabolomics features against a compound database in either positive or negative ionisation mode, and candidate metabolites must be scored accounting for the specific adducts they can form. You already have a curated per-compound adduct list and only need re-scoring — building the all-adducts table from adducts.csv again is redundant The analysis concerns MS/MS spectra comparison only, with no MS1-level adduct enumeration required (MSMSannotation on pre-computed allAdds suffices) Compounds carry exotic adducts or in-source fragments not in DB/adducts.csv and the adduct file has not been modified accordingly http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Computes all possible adducts a database compound can form per ionisation mode and maps them to observed LC–MS features so that isotope fingerprints, mass accuracy, RT ranges and prior knowledge are combined into posterior annotation probabilities using ipaPy2's compute_all_adducts(). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad455
skills.summary: Computes all possible adducts a database compound can form per ionisation mode and maps them to observed LC–MS features so that isotope fingerprints, mass accuracy, RT ranges and prior knowledge are combined into posterior annotation probabilities using ipaPy2's compute_all_adducts().
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a curated per-compound adduct list and only need re-scoring — building the all-adducts table from adducts.csv again is redundant The analysis concerns MS/MS spectra comparison only, with no MS1-level adduct enumeration required (MSMSannotation on pre-computed allAdds suffices) Compounds carry exotic adducts or in-source fragments not in DB/adducts.csv and the adduct file has not been modified accordingly

skills.description: Use when assigning metabolite identities to MS1 m/z features by querying metabolomic databases such as HMDB, and candidates must be filtered and ranked according to ionization mode, adduct knowledge, and compound properties.
skills.name: adduct-aware-ion-annotation
skills.search_text: adduct-aware-ion-annotation Use when assigning metabolite identities to MS1 m/z features by querying metabolomic databases such as HMDB, and candidates must be filtered and ranked according to ionization mode, adduct knowledge, and compound properties. Input is already a curated annotation table with identities assigned — re-running database querying and expert-system filtering would be redundant The task is MS2-only spectral library matching without any MS1 precursor m/z query against compound databases The compound space of interest is absent from CMM's integrated databases (e.g., specialized lipids outside its libraries), since filtering and scoring operate only on retrieved query results http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Expert-system-based annotation of MS1 metabolite candidates in which an expert system uses knowledge of the experimental setup (ionization mode, allowed adducts) and compound properties to filter and score database-query results, producing ranked metabolite annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00720
skills.summary: Expert-system-based annotation of MS1 metabolite candidates in which an expert system uses knowledge of the experimental setup (ionization mode, allowed adducts) and compound properties to filter and score database-query results, producing ranked metabolite annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated annotation table with identities assigned — re-running database querying and expert-system filtering would be redundant The task is MS2-only spectral library matching without any MS1 precursor m/z query against compound databases The compound space of interest is absent from CMM's integrated databases (e.g., specialized lipids outside its libraries), since filtering and scoring operate only on retrieved query results

skills.description: Use when aligning multiple processed LC-HRMS target feature lists against a reference feature list where the same metabolite appears as different ion adducts, and naive m/z-only matching undercounts matched features.
skills.name: adduct-aware-ion-species-matching
skills.search_text: adduct-aware-ion-species-matching Use when aligning multiple processed LC-HRMS target feature lists against a reference feature list where the same metabolite appears as different ion adducts, and naive m/z-only matching undercounts matched features. Input is already an aligned combined feature matrix — MetMatch is for aligning unaligned per-file feature lists against a reference LC-HRMS batches exhibit no m/z or retention time shifts relative to a reference chromatogram, so no correction/alignment is needed The metabolites of interest do not form multiple ion species, and simple m/z matching without adduct handling suffices (though this undercounts adduct-forming metabolites) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Aligns LC-HRMS feature lists across experiments with MetMatch so that differently formed ion species (adducts) of the same metabolite are recognized as corresponding features, combining matched chromatographic peak areas, m/z values and retention times into a single data matrix. Accounting for adducts substantially increases matched features (92 vs 42 of 151 Phe-derived wheat features). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: Aligns LC-HRMS feature lists across experiments with MetMatch so that differently formed ion species (adducts) of the same metabolite are recognized as corresponding features, combining matched chromatographic peak areas, m/z values and retention times into a single data matrix. Accounting for adducts substantially increases matched features (92 vs 42 of 151 Phe-derived wheat features).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned combined feature matrix — MetMatch is for aligning unaligned per-file feature lists against a reference LC-HRMS batches exhibit no m/z or retention time shifts relative to a reference chromatogram, so no correction/alignment is needed The metabolites of interest do not form multiple ion species, and simple m/z matching without adduct handling suffices (though this undercounts adduct-forming metabolites)

skills.description: Use when starting lipid annotation from an MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS feature table (m/z, RT, intensities) and you need candidate lipid species/adducts matched by precursor exact mass before any MS/MS fragment matching.
skills.name: adduct-aware-lipid-library-querying
skills.search_text: adduct-aware-lipid-library-querying Use when starting lipid annotation from an MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS feature table (m/z, RT, intensities) and you need candidate lipid species/adducts matched by precursor exact mass before any MS/MS fragment matching. Input is still raw vendor MS data — feature detection with MZmine/XCMS/MS-DIAL must precede this MS1 matching step Only MS/MS spectral data (.ms2) are available without a peak-picked feature table of precursor m/z values Acquisition is on Waters files or lipid classes outside the library coverage (e.g. LipidMatch does not currently support Waters files) Queries LipidMatch's in silico precursor-ion libraries (over 250,000 lipid species across 56 lipid types and their adducts) by exact-mass matching each feature's m/z from a peak-picked feature table, at a user-defined m/z tolerance in Da, to generate feature-candidate lipid pairs for downstream MS/MS fragment confirmation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Queries LipidMatch's in silico precursor-ion libraries (over 250,000 lipid species across 56 lipid types and their adducts) by exact-mass matching each feature's m/z from a peak-picked feature table, at a user-defined m/z tolerance in Da, to generate feature-candidate lipid pairs for downstream MS/MS fragment confirmation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw vendor MS data — feature detection with MZmine/XCMS/MS-DIAL must precede this MS1 matching step Only MS/MS spectral data (.ms2) are available without a peak-picked feature table of precursor m/z values Acquisition is on Waters files or lipid classes outside the library coverage (e.g. LipidMatch does not currently support Waters files)

skills.description: Use when a list of m/z-to-compound matches (with adduct, isotope label, ppm error, and source database columns) from a MetaboShiny/MetaDBparse search must be prioritized into putative (MSI level 2) annotations.
skills.name: adduct-based-annotation-prioritization
skills.search_text: adduct-based-annotation-prioritization Use when a list of m/z-to-compound matches (with adduct, isotope label, ppm error, and source database columns) from a MetaboShiny/MetaDBparse search must be prioritized into putative (MSI level 2) annotations. When MSI level 1 (confirmed) annotation is required — this step only yields putative MSI level 2 identifications, not standard-confirmed hits. When the input is raw peak data — MetaboShiny explicitly does not accept raw peak files; matches must already come from a database search of processed m/z peak lists. When the compound match table lacks adduct/isotope/source-database metadata (e.g. from a single-database tool that records none), since filtering depends on those fields. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A MetaboShiny (R/Shiny) annotation step that filters m/z-to-compound matches by main-peak isotope and adduct status, then ranks survivors by ppm error to yield MSI level 2 putative compound annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01717-8
skills.summary: A MetaboShiny (R/Shiny) annotation step that filters m/z-to-compound matches by main-peak isotope and adduct status, then ranks survivors by ppm error to yield MSI level 2 putative compound annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When MSI level 1 (confirmed) annotation is required — this step only yields putative MSI level 2 identifications, not standard-confirmed hits. When the input is raw peak data — MetaboShiny explicitly does not accept raw peak files; matches must already come from a database search of processed m/z peak lists. When the compound match table lacks adduct/isotope/source-database metadata (e.g. from a single-database tool that records none), since filtering depends on those fields.

skills.description: Use when building a reference spectral library for lipid identification in LC-MS/MS and you need in silico MS/MS spectra for lipid species enumerated by class and fatty acid composition across defined adducts.
skills.name: adduct-based-fragmentation-spectra-simulation
skills.search_text: adduct-based-fragmentation-spectra-simulation Use when building a reference spectral library for lipid identification in LC-MS/MS and you need in silico MS/MS spectra for lipid species enumerated by class and fatty acid composition across defined adducts. When an experimentally acquired (measured) spectral library already covers the target lipid classes and adducts, since LSG produces in silico rather than empirical spectra. When the target analytes are not lipids — the generator enumerates lipid species by class and fatty acid composition and is not a general small-molecule spectra predictor. When the needed export format is neither '.MSP' nor the '.CSV' precursor/transition list formats supported by LSG. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Generates in silico lipid fragmentation spectra and on-demand (mass)spectral libraries using the open-source Lipid Spectrum Generator (LSG), which enumerates lipids by lipid class and fatty acid composition and then computes spectra for each lipid with respect to its adducts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c04518
skills.summary: Generates in silico lipid fragmentation spectra and on-demand (mass)spectral libraries using the open-source Lipid Spectrum Generator (LSG), which enumerates lipids by lipid class and fatty acid composition and then computes spectra for each lipid with respect to its adducts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When an experimentally acquired (measured) spectral library already covers the target lipid classes and adducts, since LSG produces in silico rather than empirical spectra. When the target analytes are not lipids — the generator enumerates lipid species by class and fatty acid composition and is not a general small-molecule spectra predictor. When the needed export format is neither '.MSP' nor the '.CSV' precursor/transition list formats supported by LSG.

skills.description: Use when a sets workflow combines separately found positive ([M+H]+) and negative ([M-H]-) featureGroups objects with makeSet and the mixed-polarity features must be neutralized before cross-polarity grouping.
skills.name: adduct-based-neutral-mass-calculation
skills.search_text: adduct-based-neutral-mass-calculation Use when a sets workflow combines separately found positive ([M+H]+) and negative ([M-H]-) featureGroups objects with makeSet and the mixed-polarity features must be neutralized before cross-polarity grouping. Data contains only a single ionization mode — a plain patRoon workflow (no makeSet/neutralization step) is appropriate. Feature m/z values are already converted to neutral masses or the features were aligned within a single polarity. The task is adduct annotation of individual features within one polarity (componentization), not cross-polarity combination. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Replaces feature m/z values with neutral masses calculated from ionization-adduct information so that positive- and negative-ionization HRMS features can be aligned and grouped across polarities in patRoon's sets workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04029
skills.summary: Replaces feature m/z values with neutral masses calculated from ionization-adduct information so that positive- and negative-ionization HRMS features can be aligned and grouped across polarities in patRoon's sets workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contains only a single ionization mode — a plain patRoon workflow (no makeSet/neutralization step) is appropriate. Feature m/z values are already converted to neutral masses or the features were aligned within a single polarity. The task is adduct annotation of individual features within one polarity (componentization), not cross-polarity combination.

skills.description: Use when cleaning annotated MS/MS library spectra whose adduct, parent mass, or precursor m/z may be inconsistent with the SMILES annotation — e.g. GNPS entries where parent mass was computed from molar mass or the adduct was misassigned.
skills.name: adduct-based-parent-mass-verification
skills.search_text: adduct-based-parent-mass-verification Use when cleaning annotated MS/MS library spectra whose adduct, parent mass, or precursor m/z may be inconsistent with the SMILES annotation — e.g. GNPS entries where parent mass was computed from molar mass or the adduct was misassigned. When you need plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments — wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass will go unnoticed in this pipeline When spectra lack any resolvable structure annotation (no SMILES and no compound name matchable via PubChem) — the verification filters depend on a valid annotation and the spectra will simply be removed by Require Valid Annotation When you need standardized instrument-type or collision-energy metadata — current matchms filters do not clean or standardize these fields http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A matchms filter sequence that checks and repairs the consistency between a spectrum's structure annotation (SMILES), adduct, precursor m/z, and parent mass, correcting masses computed from molar rather than monoisotopic mass and repairing or removing spectra whose adduct/mass metadata disagrees with the SMILES. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: A matchms filter sequence that checks and repairs the consistency between a spectrum's structure annotation (SMILES), adduct, precursor m/z, and parent mass, correcting masses computed from molar rather than monoisotopic mass and repairing or removing spectra whose adduct/mass metadata disagrees with the SMILES.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments — wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass will go unnoticed in this pipeline When spectra lack any resolvable structure annotation (no SMILES and no compound name matchable via PubChem) — the verification filters depend on a valid annotation and the spectra will simply be removed by Require Valid Annotation When you need standardized instrument-type or collision-energy metadata — current matchms filters do not clean or standardize these fields

skills.description: Use when building a benchmarking set from concatenated GNPS spectral libraries (e.g. 66,646 entries) and you need to restrict spectra to protonated [M+H]+ adducts that carry structural identifiers before InChIKey conversion and de-duplication.
skills.name: adduct-based-spectra-selection
skills.search_text: adduct-based-spectra-selection Use when building a benchmarking set from concatenated GNPS spectral libraries (e.g. 66,646 entries) and you need to restrict spectra to protonated [M+H]+ adducts that carry structural identifiers before InChIKey conversion and de-duplication. Input spectra are [M-H]− or other adduct types and you need a negative-mode benchmarking set — this skill only retains protonated [M+H]+ entries. Library entries lack structural identifiers, so InChIKey conversion and de-duplication are impossible and adduct-based selection alone is insufficient. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filters GNPS library .mgf spectral entries by adduct type — keeping only [M+H]+ protonated adducts with structural identifiers — so that benchmarking spectra are chemically interpretable and comparable across annotation tools. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Filters GNPS library .mgf spectral entries by adduct type — keeping only [M+H]+ protonated adducts with structural identifiers — so that benchmarking spectra are chemically interpretable and comparable across annotation tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are [M-H]− or other adduct types and you need a negative-mode benchmarking set — this skill only retains protonated [M+H]+ entries. Library entries lack structural identifiers, so InChIKey conversion and de-duplication are impossible and adduct-based selection alone is insufficient.

skills.description: Use when preparing files for a GNPS IIMN job with collapsed ion-identity edges: a filtered consensus feature map with adduct annotations must be converted into the adduct-connection supplementary table expected by GNPS.
skills.name: adduct-connection-table-generation
skills.search_text: adduct-connection-table-generation Use when preparing files for a GNPS IIMN job with collapsed ion-identity edges: a filtered consensus feature map with adduct annotations must be converted into the adduct-connection supplementary table expected by GNPS. When running only a plain GNPS Feature-Based Molecular Networking (FBMN) job without collapsed ion-identity edges — the adduct-connection table is specific to IIMN. When the consensus feature map has not yet undergone OpenMS adduct annotation and feature linking, so no ion-identity/adduct relationships exist to tabulate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates the comma-separated supplementary table that describes ion-identity/adduct relationships between features, enabling GNPS Ion Identity Molecular Networking (IIMN) to collapse adduct edges. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: Generates the comma-separated supplementary table that describes ion-identity/adduct relationships between features, enabling GNPS Ion Identity Molecular Networking (IIMN) to collapse adduct edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When running only a plain GNPS Feature-Based Molecular Networking (FBMN) job without collapsed ion-identity edges — the adduct-connection table is specific to IIMN. When the consensus feature map has not yet undergone OpenMS adduct annotation and feature linking, so no ion-identity/adduct relationships exist to tabulate.

skills.description: Use when enumerating within-library compound pairs from MS/MS reference libraries and a pair must be discarded unless both spectra were measured under the same protonated ion (M+H) condition.
skills.name: adduct-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: adduct-consistency-checking Use when enumerating within-library compound pairs from MS/MS reference libraries and a pair must be discarded unless both spectra were measured under the same protonated ion (M+H) condition. Pairs measured under different instrument conditions or with mismatched precursor ion types (e.g. one M+H, one M+Na) — the shifted-peak logic of ModiFinder's MS/MS alignment would be invalid Single-compound tasks (e.g. combinatorial fragmentation or peak assignment) that do not involve comparing two library spectra Cross-library pair enumeration where the source libraries differ — the paper restricts this filter to within-library pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmark-construction sub-step that verifies both members of a candidate compound pair share the same M+H adduct so their MS/MS spectra are directly comparable for modification site localization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: A benchmark-construction sub-step that verifies both members of a candidate compound pair share the same M+H adduct so their MS/MS spectra are directly comparable for modification site localization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pairs measured under different instrument conditions or with mismatched precursor ion types (e.g. one M+H, one M+Na) — the shifted-peak logic of ModiFinder's MS/MS alignment would be invalid Single-compound tasks (e.g. combinatorial fragmentation or peak assignment) that do not involve comparing two library spectra Cross-library pair enumeration where the source libraries differ — the paper restricts this filter to within-library pairs

skills.description: Use when evaluating molecular formula annotation accuracy on LC-MS/MS data with a known ground-truth adduct per compound, or when quantifying how adduct misassignment contributes to SIRIUS/ZODIAC errors.
skills.name: adduct-constrained-msms-annotation
skills.search_text: adduct-constrained-msms-annotation Use when evaluating molecular formula annotation accuracy on LC-MS/MS data with a known ground-truth adduct per compound, or when quantifying how adduct misassignment contributes to SIRIUS/ZODIAC errors. Adducts are unknown and cannot be constrained — the article notes adduct information cannot be reliably deduced from isotope pattern and MS/MS data and must come from high-quality preprocessing You lack a validated ground truth; the paper's evaluation relies on ground truth established by spectral library search and manual validation The goal is de novo formula ranking performance without adduct priors (the standard ZODIAC benchmark rather than the known-adducts ablation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reproduces ZODIAC's known-adducts ablation on the dendroides dataset: each compound's ionization adduct is constrained to the ground-truth adduct before SIRIUS/ZODIAC formula annotation, quantifying how strongly wrong adduct assumptions drive errors (SIRIUS 67.17% vs ZODIAC 99.50% correct on dendroides). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Reproduces ZODIAC's known-adducts ablation on the dendroides dataset: each compound's ionization adduct is constrained to the ground-truth adduct before SIRIUS/ZODIAC formula annotation, quantifying how strongly wrong adduct assumptions drive errors (SIRIUS 67.17% vs ZODIAC 99.50% correct on dendroides).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Adducts are unknown and cannot be constrained — the article notes adduct information cannot be reliably deduced from isotope pattern and MS/MS data and must come from high-quality preprocessing You lack a validated ground truth; the paper's evaluation relies on ground truth established by spectral library search and manual validation The goal is de novo formula ranking performance without adduct priors (the standard ZODIAC benchmark rather than the known-adducts ablation)

skills.description: Use when a Compound Discoverer 3.3 peak table (from .cdResult or .csv) contains redundant unidentified features that correlate with identified lipid features, and you need to filter adducts, dimers, and other spurious features before quantitation.
skills.name: adduct-dimer-feature-removal
skills.search_text: adduct-dimer-feature-removal Use when a Compound Discoverer 3.3 peak table (from .cdResult or .csv) contains redundant unidentified features that correlate with identified lipid features, and you need to filter adducts, dimers, and other spurious features before quantitation. Input is already a filtered feature table where adducts/dimers have been removed Working with raw MS2/MS3 spectra for spectral matching rather than a chromatographic peak table — Spectrum Searcher, not Peak Finder, is the right module http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies LipiDex 2's Peak Finder pairwise correlation filtering to remove adduct peaks, in-source fragments, and dimers correlated with primary lipid features in a chromatographic peak table. On the Nile rat plasma lipidomics dataset (MSV000091033), this step reduced 14,826 unidentified features and 779 lipid identifications to 13,898 unidentified and 719 identified features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Applies LipiDex 2's Peak Finder pairwise correlation filtering to remove adduct peaks, in-source fragments, and dimers correlated with primary lipid features in a chromatographic peak table. On the Nile rat plasma lipidomics dataset (MSV000091033), this step reduced 14,826 unidentified features and 779 lipid identifications to 13,898 unidentified and 719 identified features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature table where adducts/dimers have been removed Working with raw MS2/MS3 spectra for spectral matching rather than a chromatographic peak table — Spectrum Searcher, not Peak Finder, is the right module

skills.description: Use when converting MIST-predicted fingerprint probabilities plus SELFIES targets into train/val/test splits for fine-tuning a spectrum-to-structure model, and the training split must be restricted to a dominant adduct type (e.g. [M+H]+).
skills.name: adduct-filtered-spectra-split-preparation
skills.search_text: adduct-filtered-spectra-split-preparation Use when converting MIST-predicted fingerprint probabilities plus SELFIES targets into train/val/test splits for fine-tuning a spectrum-to-structure model, and the training split must be restricted to a dominant adduct type (e.g. [M+H]+). The input is already a curated split of fingerprint-SELFIES pairs — re-running thresholding or adduct filtering would alter the benchmark's official val/test composition. The downstream task requires spectra from adducts other than [M+H]+ in training, since this skill explicitly filters out [M+Na]+ and other adducts from the training split. You are working with simulated or synthetic spectra rather than experimental spectra, where the MIST-predicted-fingerprint bridging step is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Prepares experimental mass-spectrometry data into train/val/test splits of fingerprint-SELFIES pairs, applying MIST probability thresholding (epsilon=0.2 for NPLIB1/CANOPUS, epsilon=0.11 for MassSpecGym) and adduct filtering so that only [M+H]+ spectra are used for fine-tuning while val/test retain all adduct types. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Prepares experimental mass-spectrometry data into train/val/test splits of fingerprint-SELFIES pairs, applying MIST probability thresholding (epsilon=0.2 for NPLIB1/CANOPUS, epsilon=0.11 for MassSpecGym) and adduct filtering so that only [M+H]+ spectra are used for fine-tuning while val/test retain all adduct types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated split of fingerprint-SELFIES pairs — re-running thresholding or adduct filtering would alter the benchmark's official val/test composition. The downstream task requires spectra from adducts other than [M+H]+ in training, since this skill explicitly filters out [M+Na]+ and other adducts from the training split. You are working with simulated or synthetic spectra rather than experimental spectra, where the MIST-predicted-fingerprint bridging step is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when a raw spectral library contains multiple adducts, collision energies, and replicate spectra per compound, and you need one consistent binary per-compound target spectrum for binary peak-presence prediction.
skills.name: adduct-filtering-spectrum-selection
skills.search_text: adduct-filtering-spectrum-selection Use when a raw spectral library contains multiple adducts, collision energies, and replicate spectra per compound, and you need one consistent binary per-compound target spectrum for binary peak-presence prediction. Predicting peak intensities rather than peak presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately targets binary presence since intensity is less robust across experimental conditions Working with spectra from adducts other than [M+H] (e.g. [M-H]-, [M+Na]+), which are filtered out during this step Library matching against curated empirical spectra (e.g. NIST MS/MS) where no binarized target construction is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filters a raw MS/MS spectral library down to experimental [M+H] precursor spectra and merges all spectra of the same compound into a single binarized 0.01 m/z bin presence/absence spectrum, producing the per-compound targets used to train SingleFrag's per-bin peak classifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Filters a raw MS/MS spectral library down to experimental [M+H] precursor spectra and merges all spectra of the same compound into a single binarized 0.01 m/z bin presence/absence spectrum, producing the per-compound targets used to train SingleFrag's per-bin peak classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting peak intensities rather than peak presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately targets binary presence since intensity is less robust across experimental conditions Working with spectra from adducts other than [M+H] (e.g. [M-H]-, [M+Na]+), which are filtered out during this step Library matching against curated empirical spectra (e.g. NIST MS/MS) where no binarized target construction is needed

skills.description: Use when input is imzML/ibd MS imaging data with MS1 scans only, and the goal is structural (level 2/3) metabolite or lipid annotations — including distinguishing adduct forms of the same molecule — rather than molecular-formula-only assignment.
skills.name: adduct-form-annotation-in-spatial-metabolomics
skills.search_text: adduct-form-annotation-in-spatial-metabolomics Use when input is imzML/ibd MS imaging data with MS1 scans only, and the goal is structural (level 2/3) metabolite or lipid annotations — including distinguishing adduct forms of the same molecule — rather than molecular-formula-only assignment. Input contains genuine MS/MS scans — use standard MS/MS library search or ms1-id's LC-MS/MS annotation (gnps.pkl) path instead of pseudo MS/MS generation Goal is molecular formula-level annotation only (MSI31 level 4) — a tool like METASPACE with target-decoy FDR may be more appropriate Data are LC-MS chromatographic profiles rather than imaging data — spatial correlation and 50-shared-pixel requirements do not apply; use ms1-id's lcms mode with chromatographic (XIC) correlation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates MS1-only mass spectrometry imaging data at structurally resolved adduct level (e.g. PC(16:0/18:1) as [M+H]+ and [M+Na]+) using ms1-id, which builds pseudo MS/MS spectra from spatially correlated in-source fragment ion images and matches them against indexed reference MS/MS libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Annotates MS1-only mass spectrometry imaging data at structurally resolved adduct level (e.g. PC(16:0/18:1) as [M+H]+ and [M+Na]+) using ms1-id, which builds pseudo MS/MS spectra from spatially correlated in-source fragment ion images and matches them against indexed reference MS/MS libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contains genuine MS/MS scans — use standard MS/MS library search or ms1-id's LC-MS/MS annotation (gnps.pkl) path instead of pseudo MS/MS generation Goal is molecular formula-level annotation only (MSI31 level 4) — a tool like METASPACE with target-decoy FDR may be more appropriate Data are LC-MS chromatographic profiles rather than imaging data — spatial correlation and 50-shared-pixel requirements do not apply; use ms1-id's lcms mode with chromatographic (XIC) correlation instead

skills.description: Use when annotating m/z ion peaks from an imaging MS feature matrix against a metabolite library (e.g., a 1269-metabolite mouse brain LC-MS/MS library) and you must report how many ions receive single vs. multiple annotations.

skills.search_text: adduct-form-evidence-annotation Use when annotating m/z ion peaks from an imaging MS feature matrix against a metabolite library (e.g., a 1269-metabolite mouse brain LC-MS/MS library) and you must report how many ions receive single vs. multiple annotations. Input is raw mass-spectrometry data rather than a processed feature matrix in the required CSV format (X, Y columns followed by m/z intensity columns) No metabolite reference library or formula database is available, since the method matches neutral masses against a library and cannot do de novo identification The goal is spatial pattern discovery (metabolite/pixel clustering) or differential analysis rather than metabolite annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates ion peaks in a spatial metabolomics feature matrix against a metabolite library using multi-evidence scoring: parent-ion mass accuracy, isotopic-pattern similarity, and presence of a clear adduct form, as implemented in SMAnalyst's R annotation pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Annotates ion peaks in a spatial metabolomics feature matrix against a metabolite library using multi-evidence scoring: parent-ion mass accuracy, isotopic-pattern similarity, and presence of a clear adduct form, as implemented in SMAnalyst's R annotation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mass-spectrometry data rather than a processed feature matrix in the required CSV format (X, Y columns followed by m/z intensity columns) No metabolite reference library or formula database is available, since the method matches neutral masses against a library and cannot do de novo identification The goal is spatial pattern discovery (metabolite/pixel clustering) or differential analysis rather than metabolite annotation

skills.description: Use when an NP Analyst community contains multiple strong Activity-Score MS features with similar Activity and Cluster Scores but different m/z values, and you need to determine how many distinct bioactive molecules they represent.
skills.name: adduct-fragment-feature-classification
skills.search_text: adduct-fragment-feature-classification Use when an NP Analyst community contains multiple strong Activity-Score MS features with similar Activity and Cluster Scores but different m/z values, and you need to determine how many distinct bioactive molecules they represent. The community has a single clear individual bioactive MS feature rather than a multi-feature stripe needing manual interpretation Features lack comparable Activity and Cluster Scores, so m/z differences cannot be attributed to adducts/fragments of one molecule Input is raw mass-list data that has not been processed into unique MS features (e.g. via MZmine 2 or GNPS peak lists) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Groups high-scoring MS features from an NP Analyst community by retention time into feature stripes, then classifies within-stripe m/z differences as adducts, fragments, or isotopes of a single parent molecule for dereplication. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Groups high-scoring MS features from an NP Analyst community by retention time into feature stripes, then classifies within-stripe m/z differences as adducts, fragments, or isotopes of a single parent molecule for dereplication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The community has a single clear individual bioactive MS feature rather than a multi-feature stripe needing manual interpretation Features lack comparable Activity and Cluster Scores, so m/z differences cannot be attributed to adducts/fragments of one molecule Input is raw mass-list data that has not been processed into unique MS features (e.g. via MZmine 2 or GNPS peak lists)

skills.description: Use when LC/MS compound spectra contain quasi-molecular ion candidates and you want to detect analytes sharing a diagnostic adduct or neutral-loss relationship, such as choline esters identified by m/z differences of 59.074 and 221.126.
skills.name: adduct-fragment-peak-pair-screening
skills.search_text: adduct-fragment-peak-pair-screening Use when LC/MS compound spectra contain quasi-molecular ion candidates and you want to detect analytes sharing a diagnostic adduct or neutral-loss relationship, such as choline esters identified by m/z differences of 59.074 and 221.126. When the compound spectrum contains only the molecular ion and fragment ions with no further adducts — the annotation cannot be made directly unless the neutral loss is added to the rule set. When the input is raw ungrouped XCMS peak lists rather than CAMERA-annotated compound spectra, since the screen relies on deisotoped quasi-molecular ion candidates within each compound spectrum. When m/z calibration drift exceeds the ±0.015 absolute tolerance used for the neutral-loss match, as true peak pairs would be missed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Screen deisotoped CAMERA compound spectra for peak pairs whose m/z difference matches known adduct/fragment neutral losses (e.g. 59.074 for trimethylamine, 221.126 for the choline moiety) within an absolute tolerance, to annotate and enumerate analytes such as putative choline esters. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Screen deisotoped CAMERA compound spectra for peak pairs whose m/z difference matches known adduct/fragment neutral losses (e.g. 59.074 for trimethylamine, 221.126 for the choline moiety) within an absolute tolerance, to annotate and enumerate analytes such as putative choline esters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compound spectrum contains only the molecular ion and fragment ions with no further adducts — the annotation cannot be made directly unless the neutral loss is added to the rule set. When the input is raw ungrouped XCMS peak lists rather than CAMERA-annotated compound spectra, since the screen relies on deisotoped quasi-molecular ion candidates within each compound spectrum. When m/z calibration drift exceeds the ±0.015 absolute tolerance used for the neutral-loss match, as true peak pairs would be missed.

skills.name: adduct-group-mass-difference-search
skills.search_text: adduct-group-mass-difference-search Use when a significant-feature intensity table with columns named as AssayName_RTsec_m/z is available after MB-PLS significance testing (e. The input table is a full untargeted feature table (e.g. all LC-MS peaks before MB-PLS significance testing) rather than a subset of statistically significant features — applying structural search on non-significant features is out of scope and dilutes the analysis. The feature column headers do not encode assay name, RT, and m/z in the AssayName_RTsec_m/z format — the search cannot parse the features without this naming convention. The data is GC-MS or another chromatography technique without m/z differences interpretable as adduct/isotopologue relationships — MAMSI was tested on LC-MS metabolomics phenotyping data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Link statistically significant LC-MS metabolomics features into structural clusters by detecting isotopologue signatures (1.00335 Da mass differences), common electrospray adducts (hypothetical neutral mass matching within ppm tolerance), and cross-assay [M+H]+/[M-H]- links, using the MAMSI MamsiStructSearch tool. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01327
skills.summary: Link statistically significant LC-MS metabolomics features into structural clusters by detecting isotopologue signatures (1.00335 Da mass differences), common electrospray adducts (hypothetical neutral mass matching within ppm tolerance), and cross-assay [M+H]+/[M-H]- links, using the MAMSI MamsiStructSearch tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table is a full untargeted feature table (e.g. all LC-MS peaks before MB-PLS significance testing) rather than a subset of statistically significant features — applying structural search on non-significant features is out of scope and dilutes the analysis. The feature column headers do not encode assay name, RT, and m/z in the AssayName_RTsec_m/z format — the search cannot parse the features without this naming convention. The data is GC-MS or another chromatography technique without m/z differences interpretable as adduct/isotopologue relationships — MAMSI was tested on LC-MS metabolomics phenotyping data.

skills.description: Use when processing nontargeted LC-MS data (mzML or Bruker .d) where many features are co-eluting ions of the same metabolite (isotopes, adducts, ISFs) and a deduplicated, annotated feature table is needed.
skills.name: adduct-grouping-lc-ms
skills.search_text: adduct-grouping-lc-ms Use when processing nontargeted LC-MS data (mzML or Bruker .d) where many features are co-eluting ions of the same metabolite (isotopes, adducts, ISFs) and a deduplicated, annotated feature table is needed. Input is already a curated feature table lacking raw MS/MS spectra — the ISF criterion requires each candidate fragment's m/z to be present in the parent ion's MS/MS spectrum Parent ions were completely fragmented in the ion source so no parent peak is detected — MassCube cannot automatically annotate their ISFs Downstream metabolite identification is the goal — MassCube grouping annotates feature relationships but does not directly perform metabolite identification http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) and alternative adducts within aligned LC-MS feature groups using MassCube's peak grouping module, collapsing redundant ions into unique peak groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) and alternative adducts within aligned LC-MS feature groups using MassCube's peak grouping module, collapsing redundant ions into unique peak groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table lacking raw MS/MS spectra — the ISF criterion requires each candidate fragment's m/z to be present in the parent ion's MS/MS spectrum Parent ions were completely fragmented in the ion source so no parent peak is detected — MassCube cannot automatically annotate their ISFs Downstream metabolite identification is the goal — MassCube grouping annotates feature relationships but does not directly perform metabolite identification

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed LC–MS/MS feature table (featureXML/mzML) with adduct information needs molecular formula and structural assignments for downstream GNPS networking or graph-view integration.
skills.name: adduct-informed-precursor-deconvolution
skills.search_text: adduct-informed-precursor-deconvolution Use when a pre-processed LC–MS/MS feature table (featureXML/mzML) with adduct information needs molecular formula and structural assignments for downstream GNPS networking or graph-view integration. Input is a raw (unconverted) vendor file — file conversion or pre-processing must run first to produce featureXML/mzML with assigned MS2 spectra. Feature table lacks adduct/ionisation-mode information — SiriusAdapter ranking of formula candidates depends on the adduct information supplied from config.yaml. Goal is MSI level 2 library-matched identifications rather than formula/structure prediction — use the spectral-matching step against an MGF/MSP library instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Feeds feature-resolved MS2 spectra and adduct annotations from the UmetaFlow feature matrix into SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID via SiriusAdapter, then maps the top-ranked formula and structure predictions back onto unique feature IDs to produce MSI level 3 annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: Feeds feature-resolved MS2 spectra and adduct annotations from the UmetaFlow feature matrix into SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID via SiriusAdapter, then maps the top-ranked formula and structure predictions back onto unique feature IDs to produce MSI level 3 annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw (unconverted) vendor file — file conversion or pre-processing must run first to produce featureXML/mzML with assigned MS2 spectra. Feature table lacks adduct/ionisation-mode information — SiriusAdapter ranking of formula candidates depends on the adduct information supplied from config.yaml. Goal is MSI level 2 library-matched identifications rather than formula/structure prediction — use the spectral-matching step against an MGF/MSP library instead.

skills.description: Use when you have an IIMN graphml in which multiple ion species (adducts, isotopes, multimers) of the same compound appear as redundant feature nodes and you need a de-duplicated molecular-node network with aggregated intensities.
skills.name: adduct-intensity-aggregation-per-molecule
skills.search_text: adduct-intensity-aggregation-per-molecule Use when you have an IIMN graphml in which multiple ion species (adducts, isotopes, multimers) of the same compound appear as redundant feature nodes and you need a de-duplicated molecular-node network with aggregated intensities. When you need ion-species-resolved analysis (adduct/isotope-level interpretation, ion-ligand complex discovery) — collapsing destroys that granularity When the input graph has no IIN group identifiers to merge on (e.g., a plain MS2-only molecular network without MS1 ion identity annotation) During the upstream GNPS IIMN web-server run itself; this skill is a post-hoc collapse applied to the exported IIMN output http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Collapses an Ion Identity Molecular Network (IIMN) by merging all ion-species feature nodes sharing one IIN ID into a single neutral-molecule (M) representative node, redirecting MS2 edges and aggregating per-sample intensities to reduce network redundancy. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23953-9
skills.summary: Collapses an Ion Identity Molecular Network (IIMN) by merging all ion-species feature nodes sharing one IIN ID into a single neutral-molecule (M) representative node, redirecting MS2 edges and aggregating per-sample intensities to reduce network redundancy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need ion-species-resolved analysis (adduct/isotope-level interpretation, ion-ligand complex discovery) — collapsing destroys that granularity When the input graph has no IIN group identifiers to merge on (e.g., a plain MS2-only molecular network without MS1 ion identity annotation) During the upstream GNPS IIMN web-server run itself; this skill is a post-hoc collapse applied to the exported IIMN output

skills.description: Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS chromatographic peaks (e.g., from xcms findChromPeaks) with candidate metabolites using only MS1 m/z, by matching measured m/z to adduct-derived target m/z from exact masses.
skills.name: adduct-ion-mass-calculation-from-exact-mass
skills.search_text: adduct-ion-mass-calculation-from-exact-mass Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS chromatographic peaks (e.g., from xcms findChromPeaks) with candidate metabolites using only MS1 m/z, by matching measured m/z to adduct-derived target m/z from exact masses. When MS2 fragment spectra are available and library spectra exist — matchSpectra-based MS2 annotation provides higher confidence than m/z-only matching. When a reference table already provides both m/z and retention times for standards — use MzRtParam (ppm = 10, toleranceRt = 7) instead of computing m/z from exact masses. http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes expected ion m/z values from compound exact masses for specified adducts (e.g., [M+H]+, [M+Na]+) using MetaboCoreUtils/MetaboAnnotation, enabling MS1-only annotation of chromatographic peaks against a compound database within a defined ppm tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12020173
skills.summary: Computes expected ion m/z values from compound exact masses for specified adducts (e.g., [M+H]+, [M+Na]+) using MetaboCoreUtils/MetaboAnnotation, enabling MS1-only annotation of chromatographic peaks against a compound database within a defined ppm tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When MS2 fragment spectra are available and library spectra exist — matchSpectra-based MS2 annotation provides higher confidence than m/z-only matching. When a reference table already provides both m/z and retention times for standards — use MzRtParam (ppm = 10, toleranceRt = 7) instead of computing m/z from exact masses.

skills.description: Use when a pixel-by-m/z feature matrix from an imaging MS dataset (e.g. AFAD-ESI mouse brain, 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ions) needs isotope/adduct decomposition before metabolite annotation, and the fraction of adduct vs. isotope peaks must be quantified.
skills.name: adduct-ion-mass-difference-screening
skills.search_text: adduct-ion-mass-difference-screening Use when a pixel-by-m/z feature matrix from an imaging MS dataset (e.g. AFAD-ESI mouse brain, 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ions) needs isotope/adduct decomposition before metabolite annotation, and the fraction of adduct vs. isotope peaks must be quantified. The input is raw MS imaging spectra rather than a peak-picked pixel × m/z feature matrix, since the workflow operates on extracted m/z peak lists The data lack spatial pixel coordinates, because candidate adduct pairs are confirmed via spatial (Moran's I) correlation across pixels and cannot be validated without them The goal is database-driven metabolite annotation (HMDB/KEGG/LIPIDMAPS scoring by mass accuracy, isotopic similarity, adduct evidence) rather than classifying peaks as isotope/adduct pairs Classifies ion peaks in a spatial metabolomics feature matrix as adduct ions by screening for the common positive-mode adduct mass differences ([M+H]+, [M+K]+, [M+Na]+, [M+NH4]+, [M+H-H2O]+) and validating candidate pairs by spatial correlation across pixels, yielding the fraction of total ion peaks attributable to adducts. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Classifies ion peaks in a spatial metabolomics feature matrix as adduct ions by screening for the common positive-mode adduct mass differences ([M+H]+, [M+K]+, [M+Na]+, [M+NH4]+, [M+H-H2O]+) and validating candidate pairs by spatial correlation across pixels, yielding the fraction of total ion peaks attributable to adducts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw MS imaging spectra rather than a peak-picked pixel × m/z feature matrix, since the workflow operates on extracted m/z peak lists The data lack spatial pixel coordinates, because candidate adduct pairs are confirmed via spatial (Moran's I) correlation across pixels and cannot be validated without them The goal is database-driven metabolite annotation (HMDB/KEGG/LIPIDMAPS scoring by mass accuracy, isotopic similarity, adduct evidence) rather than classifying peaks as isotope/adduct pairs

skills.description: Use when you have unlabeled LC/MS feature tables (m/z + retention time per feature) and need to estimate what fraction of features correspond to known metabolites via negative- or positive-mode adduct matching, e.g. to benchmark preprocessing methods.
skills.name: adduct-ion-mass-matching
skills.search_text: adduct-ion-mass-matching Use when you have unlabeled LC/MS feature tables (m/z + retention time per feature) and need to estimate what fraction of features correspond to known metabolites via negative- or positive-mode adduct matching, e.g. to benchmark preprocessing methods. Features already carry metabolite identities (e.g. from standards-based annotation), so re-matching adds no information The goal is batch effect correction or peak alignment quality itself — this skill is a downstream comparison metric, not a correction method The data are not small-molecule LC/MS features (e.g. proteomics peptides or genomics data), where adduct mass matching is inapplicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotate LC/MS feature tables by matching feature m/z values to known metabolites (e.g. KEGG compounds) through allowed adduct ion transformations such as [M-H]-, using xMSAnnotator. This yields a per-preprocessing-method proportion of features explainable by known metabolites, used to compare feature table quality. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: Annotate LC/MS feature tables by matching feature m/z values to known metabolites (e.g. KEGG compounds) through allowed adduct ion transformations such as [M-H]-, using xMSAnnotator. This yields a per-preprocessing-method proportion of features explainable by known metabolites, used to compare feature table quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features already carry metabolite identities (e.g. from standards-based annotation), so re-matching adds no information The goal is batch effect correction or peak alignment quality itself — this skill is a downstream comparison metric, not a correction method The data are not small-molecule LC/MS features (e.g. proteomics peptides or genomics data), where adduct mass matching is inapplicable

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed MSI feature list (measured m/z in the first column) and need to assign metabolite names and adduct forms, e.g. AFADESI-MSI liver tissue data in positive mode.
skills.name: adduct-ion-mz-matching
skills.search_text: adduct-ion-mz-matching Use when you have a preprocessed MSI feature list (measured m/z in the first column) and need to assign metabolite names and adduct forms, e.g. AFADESI-MSI liver tissue data in positive mode. The input is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed feature table — MSIannotator explicitly annotates processed MSI data. The available database's organ or detection mode does not match the MSIdata (e.g. a positive-mode liver database paired with negative-mode brain data). The goal is de novo metabolite identification from MS/MS spectra rather than accurate-mass adduct matching against a curated database. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates measured m/z features in preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data by matching them against theoretical adduct m/z values from an organ-specific metabolite database using MSIannotator.m in MATLAB, with a default 10 ppm m/z error tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Annotates measured m/z features in preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data by matching them against theoretical adduct m/z values from an organ-specific metabolite database using MSIannotator.m in MATLAB, with a default 10 ppm m/z error tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed feature table — MSIannotator explicitly annotates processed MSI data. The available database's organ or detection mode does not match the MSIdata (e.g. a positive-mode liver database paired with negative-mode brain data). The goal is de novo metabolite identification from MS/MS spectra rather than accurate-mass adduct matching against a curated database.

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed spatial metabolomics peak intensity matrix (pixels x m/z ions) from MALDI/DESI-MSI is available and you need to flag which ions are adduct forms and quantify the adduct distribution.
skills.name: adduct-ion-pair-identification
skills.search_text: adduct-ion-pair-identification Use when a preprocessed spatial metabolomics peak intensity matrix (pixels x m/z ions) from MALDI/DESI-MSI is available and you need to flag which ions are adduct forms and quantify the adduct distribution. skills.search_text: adduct-mz-rt-conflict-detection Use when finalizing an in-house LC-MS metabolite standard library built with metScribeR and you must flag adduct pairs whose m/z and RT overlap within the LC-MS method's separation ability before CSV export. The library CSV has already been exported and the goal is downstream identification of experimental compounds rather than library construction. Data are being peak-picked and annotated with external tools (MZmine, El-MAVEN, MS-DIAL) rather than processed through metScribeR's storage_object workflow. The task requires MS/MS spectral matching — metScribeR library building uses MS1 and RT data and does not use MS2 for construction (MoNA spectra retrieval is a separate optional step). metScribeR's 'crossed adducts' conflict-checking step: each retained 'good' adduct from a metabolite standard is evaluated against every other adduct in the library, flagging pairs whose m/z and retention times cannot be distinguished within user-defined tolerances so only separable adducts enter the exported RT/m/z reference library. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548

skills.search_text: adduct-notation-normalization Use when merging spectral-library or feature-table records whose ion-identity annotations appear in inconsistent spellings (e.g. 'M + H', 'M + H +', '[M + H]+') and you need them aggregated as one ion identity before networking or counting. Input records already carry the canonical bracketed ion-species string, e.g. '[M + H]+', so parsing would be a no-op The task is raw-peak feature grouping or adduct *assignment* from m/z differences — that is the IIMN MS1-based ion identity networking step (retention time tolerance 0.1 min, m/z tolerance 0.001 or 10 ppm), not string normalization Annotations contain free-text compound names or InChIKeys rather than bracketed ion-species strings; no adduct parts can be split around 'M' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Parses and harmonizes heterogeneous ion-identity annotation strings from spectral libraries (e.g. the GNPS-IIMN-PROPOGATED library) into a single canonical bracketed ion-species form so that multiple spellings of the same adduct collapse into one identity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23953-9

Input is a merged/de-duplicated lipid species table that has already collapsed adducts into a single molecular species entry You need structural-level identification counts (e.g. fatty-acyl constituent level) rather than ion-level counts, since the convention deliberately preserves adduct-level redundancy Feature table has not yet been annotated by LipidMatch (i.e. no adduct designations present) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Treat every annotated adduct of a lipid species (e.g. [M+H]+, [M+NH4]+, [M-H]-) as a distinct lipid ion when tallying unique annotations from untargeted UHPLC-HRMS/MS feature tables, while separately counting distinct features (m/z + retention time) and distinct lipid types. skills.search_text: adduct-reference-mass-matching Use when you have a binned mass-difference histogram from MALDI-MSI peak pairs and want to count occurrences of known adducts (Na+, K+, 13C, DHB or CHCA matrix adducts) within instrument mass tolerance. Your goal is to verify spatial co-localization of the candidate parent–adduct pairs — mass matching alone does not test whether parent and adduct ion images are correlated; follow up with corrPairsMSI. Your input is an unbinned list of raw pairwise mass differences; adductMatch operates on the histogram, so you must bin first with hist(). The adduct you care about is not in the reference table and you have not built a custom name/formula/mass table — the matching will silently miss it (use topAdducts to survey unmatched high-count bins). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates candidate parent–adduct ion pairs in MALDI-MSI peak lists by matching binned pairwise mass differences against the mass2adduct built-in reference tables (adducts / adducts2), reporting how many peak pairs fall into the histogram bin closest to each known adduct mass. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720

Data consist of raw centroided spectra or a flat XCMS peak table with no retention-time/intensity grouping — grouping (groupFWHM, groupCorr) must precede adduct annotation. skills.search_text: adduct-rule-table-matching Use when grouping has produced CAMERA compound spectra from LC/MS peak lists (positive and/or negative ESI mode) and you need to assign ion-species annotations and propose accurate compound masses from adduct/isotope rules. skills.search_text: adduct-species-simulation Use when you need to stress-test an LC-HRMS feature alignment tool (e.g. MetMatch) against a known ground truth by injecting artificial adduct variants and retention-time perturbations into a reference feature list. The input is already an aligned, merged data matrix — MetMatch's role is to combine corresponding ions and metabolites from unaligned feature lists into a single data matrix You need to detect adducts in real untargeted metabolomics samples rather than benchmark alignment behavior with artificially simulated adduct species Retention-time shifts are unknown and uncontrolled — this skill requires a defined transformation (e.g. the discontinuous simulation 3 with ±6 s jitter) to establish ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates simulated alternative ion adduct species for a subset of LC-HRMS features so that MetMatch's ability to recombine differently formed ion species of the same metabolite during alignment can be benchmarked against ground truth, using F-measures over six retention-time shift simulations. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: Generates simulated alternative ion adduct species for a subset of LC-HRMS features so that MetMatch's ability to recombine differently formed ion species of the same metabolite during alignment can be benchmarked against ground truth, using F-measures over six retention-time shift simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an aligned, merged data matrix — MetMatch's role is to combine corresponding ions and metabolites from unaligned feature lists into a single data matrix You need to detect adducts in real untargeted metabolomics samples rather than benchmark alignment behavior with artificially simulated adduct species Retention-time shifts are unknown and uncontrolled — this skill requires a defined transformation (e.g. the discontinuous simulation 3 with ±6 s jitter) to establish ground truth

skills.description: Use when you need to rank a machine-learning collision cross section predictor (e.g. CCSP 2.0) against alternatives like CCSbase, AllCCS or DeepCCS using held-out test splits drawn from a measured CCS compendium stratified by adduct type.
skills.name: adduct-stratified-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: adduct-stratified-model-evaluation Use when you need to rank a machine-learning collision cross section predictor (e.g. CCSP 2.0) against alternatives like CCSbase, AllCCS or DeepCCS using held-out test splits drawn from a measured CCS compendium stratified by adduct type. Input is a single fixed train/test split or cross-validation fold design rather than repeated random test sets — the skill's rationale rests on 101 paired splits. Your training set does not contain the adduct types needed ([M−H]⁻, [M+H]⁺, [M+Na]⁺); CCSP 2.0's models are tailored to those common adducts, and the method requires enough measured CCS values per stratum to split. You need to predict dimers such as [2 M + H]⁺ or [2 M − H]⁻, or other less common adducts or in-source fragments — current training sets do not support those cases, so stratified benchmarking of those classes is out of scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3335 Benchmark a CCS prediction algorithm against competing tools (CCSbase, AllCCS, DeepCCS) by repeating random 30% test-set splits 101 times within each adduct stratum ([M−H]⁻, [M+H]⁺, [M+Na]⁺), holding sampled test sets identical across all algorithms so median MRE and RMSE rankings are directly comparable. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c03491
skills.summary: Benchmark a CCS prediction algorithm against competing tools (CCSbase, AllCCS, DeepCCS) by repeating random 30% test-set splits 101 times within each adduct stratum ([M−H]⁻, [M+H]⁺, [M+Na]⁺), holding sampled test sets identical across all algorithms so median MRE and RMSE rankings are directly comparable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single fixed train/test split or cross-validation fold design rather than repeated random test sets — the skill's rationale rests on 101 paired splits. Your training set does not contain the adduct types needed ([M−H]⁻, [M+H]⁺, [M+Na]⁺); CCSP 2.0's models are tailored to those common adducts, and the method requires enough measured CCS values per stratum to split. You need to predict dimers such as [2 M + H]⁺ or [2 M − H]⁻, or other less common adducts or in-source fragments — current training sets do not support those cases, so stratified benchmarking of those classes is out of scope.

skills.description: Use when a large tokenised BGC dataset (e.g. antiSMASH-DB domain-tokenised clusters) contains near-duplicate clusters that must be reduced to a non-redundant set before motif/sub-cluster mining.
skills.name: adjacency-index-maximal-clique-deduplication
skills.search_text: adjacency-index-maximal-clique-deduplication Use when a large tokenised BGC dataset (e.g. antiSMASH-DB domain-tokenised clusters) contains near-duplicate clusters that must be reduced to a non-redundant set before motif/sub-cluster mining. The input set is already curated as non-redundant (e.g. a small reference set like MIBiG alone), so clique-based collapsing would remove intentionally similar reference clusters. BGCs lying on a contig edge must be retained — antiSMASH flags these as incomplete and they are discarded before this deduplication step, so results would be biased. Similarity should be judged on full gene order or class-level membership rather than domain composition; this skill explicitly ignores order and counts hybrid-class matches per class. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Graph-based redundancy removal for tokenised biosynthetic gene clusters: BGCs are connected when their domain Adjacency Index exceeds 0.95 or when one BGC fully contains another, and only the member with the most domains is kept from each maximal clique. This collapses near-identical clusters before downstream sub-cluster mining with iPRESTO. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Graph-based redundancy removal for tokenised biosynthetic gene clusters: BGCs are connected when their domain Adjacency Index exceeds 0.95 or when one BGC fully contains another, and only the member with the most domains is kept from each maximal clique. This collapses near-identical clusters before downstream sub-cluster mining with iPRESTO.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input set is already curated as non-redundant (e.g. a small reference set like MIBiG alone), so clique-based collapsing would remove intentionally similar reference clusters. BGCs lying on a contig edge must be retained — antiSMASH flags these as incomplete and they are discarded before this deduplication step, so results would be biased. Similarity should be judged on full gene order or class-level membership rather than domain composition; this skill explicitly ignores order and counts hybrid-class matches per class.
