skills.description: Use when a metabolite/pathway graph is supplied as an adjacency matrix that must feed into Laplacian construction, since the regularized normalized Laplacian and downstream kernel are only valid for symmetric, undirected graphs.
skills.name: adjacency-matrix-symmetry-validation
skills.search_text: adjacency-matrix-symmetry-validation Use when a metabolite/pathway graph is supplied as an adjacency matrix that must feed into Laplacian construction, since the regularized normalized Laplacian and downstream kernel are only valid for symmetric, undirected graphs. The graph is directed or weighted: the validation assumes undirected connectivity with 0/1 adjacency, so a non-symmetric or weighted matrix violates the Laplacian construction assumptions. Graph structure has not been examined: PaIRKAT's authors state it is important to examine the structure of a graph before applying a regularization step, so blind application to an uninspected graph is out of scope. The goal is association testing itself rather than graph/Laplacian preprocessing — this skill covers only the adjacency-to-Laplacian validation stage, not the score test with Satterthwaite approximation. Validates that a pathway's p×p adjacency matrix is symmetric with 0/1 entries before it is converted into the degree matrix, graph Laplacian, and the regularized normalized Laplacian (D + τI)^(-1/2) L (D + τI)^(-1/2) used in PaIRKAT's kernel machine score test. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Validates that a pathway's p×p adjacency matrix is symmetric with 0/1 entries before it is converted into the degree matrix, graph Laplacian, and the regularized normalized Laplacian (D + τI)^(-1/2) L (D + τI)^(-1/2) used in PaIRKAT's kernel machine score test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The graph is directed or weighted: the validation assumes undirected connectivity with 0/1 adjacency, so a non-symmetric or weighted matrix violates the Laplacian construction assumptions. Graph structure has not been examined: PaIRKAT's authors state it is important to examine the structure of a graph before applying a regularization step, so blind application to an uninspected graph is out of scope. The goal is association testing itself rather than graph/Laplacian preprocessing — this skill covers only the adjacency-to-Laplacian validation stage, not the score test with Satterthwaite approximation.

skills.name: adjacency-matrix-tensor-construction
skills.search_text: adjacency-matrix-tensor-construction Use when converting rooted molecular fragment graphs (atom/bond-labeled, rooted at a cleaved-bond atom) into fixed-length topological feature vectors for training or applying CFM-ID-style fragmentation transition models. The input is not a rooted fragment graph — e.g. you need whole-molecule descriptors, fingerprints, or spectral features rather than topological features of cleavage-bond-rooted fragments Fragments whose relevant atoms extend beyond 2 bonds from the root and beyond the N=10 nearest-vertex selection window, where the truncated subgraph loses structurally important atoms You need rule-based rather than learned fragmentation prediction — CFM-ID 4.0's expanded hand-written rule predictor (acylcarnitines, acylcholines, flavonols, flavones, flavanones, flavonoid glycosides) does not use this learned feature representation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds the connectivity-matrix (adjacency-tensor) chemical structure representation used by CFM-ID 4.0, encoding MS-relevant topological features of rooted fragment graphs as a flattened 1-D vector for learning fragmentation transition probabilities. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Builds the connectivity-matrix (adjacency-tensor) chemical structure representation used by CFM-ID 4.0, encoding MS-relevant topological features of rooted fragment graphs as a flattened 1-D vector for learning fragmentation transition probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a rooted fragment graph — e.g. you need whole-molecule descriptors, fingerprints, or spectral features rather than topological features of cleavage-bond-rooted fragments Fragments whose relevant atoms extend beyond 2 bonds from the root and beyond the N=10 nearest-vertex selection window, where the truncated subgraph loses structurally important atoms You need rule-based rather than learned fragmentation prediction — CFM-ID 4.0's expanded hand-written rule predictor (acylcarnitines, acylcholines, flavonols, flavones, flavanones, flavonoid glycosides) does not use this learned feature representation

skills.when_to_use_negative: Sections share actual spots or features between modalities — the article notes the integration problem exists precisely because there are no shared spots or features, so overlap-based label comparison is not applicable Higher-resolution spatial data, image-based sequencing, spatial proteomics, or histological images — the article states haCCA's behavior on such data has not been evaluated and only spatial transcriptome and spatial metabolome data have been used Pseudo-paired data without ground-truth cluster labels on both sections — AC and ARI cannot be computed without Label arrays on a and b_prime

skills.description: Use when AEMS .wiff raw data lacks explicit ejection times and each shot must be associated with its detected peak — e.g. evenly spaced acoustic ejections at a ~1000 ms nominal interval from a 384-well plate run.
skills.name: aems-ejection-time-estimation
skills.search_text: aems-ejection-time-estimation Use when AEMS .wiff raw data lacks explicit ejection times and each shot must be associated with its detected peak — e.g. evenly spaced acoustic ejections at a ~1000 ms nominal interval from a 384-well plate run. The input is conventional LC-MS chromatography with gradient retention times rather than acoustic ejection (AEMS) data — rtmsEcho's sinusoidal shot-to-peak association assumes evenly spaced ejections, and the article notes conventional chromatography is a fundamentally different, chromatographically separated modality. Explicit ejection timestamps or plate/shot metadata are already available for the .wiff file, making sinusoidal inference unnecessary. The run is not evenly spaced (e.g. irregular or aborted ejection schedules), since the method models ejection times as an evenly spaced set. Infers the precise timing of each acoustic ejection in an AEMS run (stored in AEMS .wiff files without explicit ejection timestamps) by fitting a sinusoidal reference signal to the total ion chromatogram (TIC) of total intensity versus time, achieving ~0.01 ms timing precision. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03730
skills.summary: Infers the precise timing of each acoustic ejection in an AEMS run (stored in AEMS .wiff files without explicit ejection timestamps) by fitting a sinusoidal reference signal to the total ion chromatogram (TIC) of total intensity versus time, achieving ~0.01 ms timing precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is conventional LC-MS chromatography with gradient retention times rather than acoustic ejection (AEMS) data — rtmsEcho's sinusoidal shot-to-peak association assumes evenly spaced ejections, and the article notes conventional chromatography is a fundamentally different, chromatographically separated modality. Explicit ejection timestamps or plate/shot metadata are already available for the .wiff file, making sinusoidal inference unnecessary. The run is not evenly spaced (e.g. irregular or aborted ejection schedules), since the method models ejection times as an evenly spaced set.

skills.description: Use when a full 384-well plate of AEMS data in full-scan (PI) mode must be processed end-to-end with rtmsEcho and the elapsed wall-clock time must be verified against the reported <30 s (up to a 60 Da window) benchmark.
skills.name: aems-full-scan-plate-processing
skills.search_text: aems-full-scan-plate-processing Use when a full 384-well plate of AEMS data in full-scan (PI) mode must be processed end-to-end with rtmsEcho and the elapsed wall-clock time must be verified against the reported <30 s (up to a 60 Da window) benchmark. skills.search_text: affine-transformation-estimation Use when two neighboring spatial-omics sections (e.g. h5ad files with obsm['spatial'] coordinates from 10X Visium and MALDI-MSI) share no spots or features and must be registered before spot-to-spot integration. skills.description: Use when benchmarking BGC clustering quality against manually curated MIBiG group labels (e.g., reproducing a V-score baseline), or when non-convex GCF structure is expected and pairwise network-based clustering is affordable for the dataset size.

skills.search_text: affinity-propagation-gene-cluster-family-clustering Use when benchmarking BGC clustering quality against manually curated MIBiG group labels (e.g., reproducing a V-score baseline), or when non-convex GCF structure is expected and pairwise network-based clustering is affordable for the dataset size. Datasets of hundreds of thousands to millions of BGCs (e.g., the 1,225,071-BGC RefSeq-scale run): pairwise comparison is O(n^2) and BiG-SCAPE was estimated at ~37,000 hours on a 36-core CPU — use BiG-SLiCE's Euclidean-space near-linear clustering instead Input BGCs lack antiSMASH-style GenBank/domain annotations and no converter step is possible, since BiG-SCAPE distances depend on domain architecture and sequence similarity http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Clusters biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into gene cluster families (GCFs) by building a weighted pairwise similarity network with BiG-SCAPE and applying Affinity Propagation, which can recover non-convex cluster shapes that Euclidean-space partitional methods like BiG-SLiCE (T = 1,100, V-score = 0.81) miss. Serves as the pairwise-network baseline whose V-score of 0.91 on the 92 curated MIBiG v1.3 groups benchmarks scalable clustering approaches. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa154
skills.summary: Clusters biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into gene cluster families (GCFs) by building a weighted pairwise similarity network with BiG-SCAPE and applying Affinity Propagation, which can recover non-convex cluster shapes that Euclidean-space partitional methods like BiG-SLiCE (T = 1,100, V-score = 0.81) miss. Serves as the pairwise-network baseline whose V-score of 0.91 on the 92 curated MIBiG v1.3 groups benchmarks scalable clustering approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets of hundreds of thousands to millions of BGCs (e.g., the 1,225,071-BGC RefSeq-scale run): pairwise comparison is O(n^2) and BiG-SCAPE was estimated at ~37,000 hours on a 36-core CPU — use BiG-SLiCE's Euclidean-space near-linear clustering instead Input BGCs lack antiSMASH-style GenBank/domain annotations and no converter step is possible, since BiG-SCAPE distances depend on domain architecture and sequence similarity

skills.description: Use when testing whether biomarker–mortality associations hold across age groups, especially where conventional risk factors (e.g., systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol) show opposite associations in the elderly versus middle age.
skills.name: age-stratified-survival-analysis
skills.search_text: age-stratified-survival-analysis Use when testing whether biomarker–mortality associations hold across age groups, especially where conventional risk factors (e.g., systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol) show opposite associations in the elderly versus middle age. The analysis goal is discovery of which biomarkers associate with mortality (the stepwise forward-backward selection over 63 of 226 biomarkers with Bonferroni threshold 2.21 × 10^-4), not consistency checking or prediction within age strata. The input cohort lacks age at blood sampling or adequate deaths within a stratum (e.g., >90 years), making stratified Cox models unstable. You need a clinically deployable score in concentration units — the article notes the per-cohort SD-scaled score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic'. Fits Cox proportional hazards models with age at blood sampling as the time scale to estimate biomarker–mortality associations, then re-estimates them within age strata (<60, 60–70, 70–80, 80–90, >90 years) and sex to verify direction-of-effect consistency, as done for the 14 metabolic biomarkers in this study. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: Fits Cox proportional hazards models with age at blood sampling as the time scale to estimate biomarker–mortality associations, then re-estimates them within age strata (<60, 60–70, 70–80, 80–90, >90 years) and sex to verify direction-of-effect consistency, as done for the 14 metabolic biomarkers in this study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is discovery of which biomarkers associate with mortality (the stepwise forward-backward selection over 63 of 226 biomarkers with Bonferroni threshold 2.21 × 10^-4), not consistency checking or prediction within age strata. skills.name: aggregate-statistics-meta-analysis
skills.search_text: aggregate-statistics-meta-analysis Use when input consists of published per-study aggregate statistics (p-value and fold-change) for metabolites across clinical studies, and compounds must be harmonized across synonym identifiers before combining. You have access to individual-level (raw intensity) data across studies — then a full statistical meta-analysis in a tool like MetaboAnalyst on the primary data is the appropriate route, as in the PR000293 comparison The input already contains a single harmonized compound list with consistent identifiers and no synonym/duplicate problem to resolve Compounds across studies lack any p-value or fold-change reporting, since the method operates on aggregate statistics only http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Meta-analysis of aggregate metabolomics results (p-values and fold-changes from multiple clinical studies) using the Easy-Amanida Shiny app, which wraps the amanida R package and harmonizes heterogeneous compound names with webchem. It supports both qualitative vote-counting and quantitative combination of published statistics without access to individual-level data. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jrsm.1713
skills.summary: Meta-analysis of aggregate metabolomics results (p-values and fold-changes from multiple clinical studies) using the Easy-Amanida Shiny app, which wraps the amanida R package and harmonizes heterogeneous compound names with webchem. It supports both qualitative vote-counting and quantitative combination of published statistics without access to individual-level data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have access to individual-level (raw intensity) data across studies — then a full statistical meta-analysis in a tool like MetaboAnalyst on the primary data is the appropriate route, as in the PR000293 comparison The input already contains a single harmonized compound list with consistent identifiers and no synonym/duplicate problem to resolve Compounds across studies lack any p-value or fold-change reporting, since the method operates on aggregate statistics only

skills.description: Use when auditing a randomized or complete-randomized LC/GC-MS injection sequence for clustered features, e.g. consecutive same-group runs in treatment/gender/age strata.
skills.name: aggregated-feature-run-detection-in-randomized-sequences
skills.search_text: aggregated-feature-run-detection-in-randomized-sequences Use when auditing a randomized or complete-randomized LC/GC-MS injection sequence for clustered features, e.g. consecutive same-group runs in treatment/gender/age strata. The sequence was generated by stratified block randomization with block size 2, where three consecutive same-group runs are theoretically absent — the metric is only informative for unbalanced or complete-randomized outputs. The goal is inter-batch balancing rather than auditing aggregation within a single randomized sequence. Scans a randomized injection sequence for runs of consecutively repeated sample categories (treatment, gender, age group) and tallies aggregation events per category per dimension, as used in the InjectionDesign case study to expose clustering that block randomization avoids. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.02.26.530140
skills.summary: Scans a randomized injection sequence for runs of consecutively repeated sample categories (treatment, gender, age group) and tallies aggregation events per category per dimension, as used in the InjectionDesign case study to expose clustering that block randomization avoids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequence was generated by stratified block randomization with block size 2, where three consecutive same-group runs are theoretically absent — the metric is only informative for unbalanced or complete-randomized outputs. The goal is inter-batch balancing rather than auditing aggregation within a single randomized sequence.

Input is already a preprocessed or converted file (e.g. UIMF or mzML) rather than an original Agilent ".d" acquisition file — the metadata export reads instrument-format data directly The goal is to enhance signal quality (smoothing, saturation repair, demultiplexing) rather than to export acquisition metadata http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Handles Agilent MassHunter ".d" raw acquisition files, including reading and exporting the embedded acquisition metadata (electric field strength, pressure, temperature, voltages) that documents IM-MS instrument performance for the collected data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: Handles Agilent MassHunter ".d" raw acquisition files, including reading and exporting the embedded acquisition metadata (electric field strength, pressure, temperature, voltages) that documents IM-MS instrument performance for the collected data.

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics abundance table carries attached sample study variables (e.g., body mass index, tissue, condition) and you must identify which lipids exert the highest effect in distinguishing those variables.
skills.name: aic-based-regression-model-selection
skills.search_text: aic-based-regression-model-selection Use when a lipidomics abundance table carries attached sample study variables (e.g., body mass index, tissue, condition) and you must identify which lipids exert the highest effect in distinguishing those variables. The imported dataset has fewer than two study variables — LipidSpace's regression/classification model feature analysis requires at least two study variables The goal is structural similarity comparison of lipidomes (MCS/Jaccard, PCA lipid space) rather than explaining study variables from lipid abundances The task is quality control or lipid name standardization rather than feature selection http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Selects the lipid subset that best describes each study variable by heuristic sequential forward selection (SFS) over multiple linear regression models scored with the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), with ROC accuracy added for binary nominal variables. Implemented as LipidSpace's built-in feature analysis module. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Selects the lipid subset that best describes each study variable by heuristic sequential forward selection (SFS) over multiple linear regression models scored with the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), with ROC accuracy added for binary nominal variables. Implemented as LipidSpace's built-in feature analysis module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The imported dataset has fewer than two study variables — LipidSpace's regression/classification model feature analysis requires at least two study variables The goal is structural similarity comparison of lipidomes (MCS/Jaccard, PCA lipid space) rather than explaining study variables from lipid abundances The task is quality control or lipid name standardization rather than feature selection

skills.description: Use when multiple plausible moiety/deconvolution models exist for MS-measured isotopologue timecourses and you must objectively select the model, e.g. ranking 41 UDP-GlcNAc models fitted with SAGA by AICc.
skills.name: aicc-model-ranking
skills.search_text: aicc-model-ranking Use when multiple plausible moiety/deconvolution models exist for MS-measured isotopologue timecourses and you must objectively select the model, e.g. ranking 41 UDP-GlcNAc models fitted with SAGA by AICc. The optimization objective function is an absolute difference matched to GAIMS behavior, where overfitting makes AICc ranking unable to recover the correct model Only a single plausible deconvolution model exists, so no model selection among competitors is required Isotopologue data are heavily degraded (e.g. added normal error with sigma = 0.1 on multi-tracer data, where propagated error reaches roughly nine times the original signal), making model selection unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ranks candidate moiety models fitted to MS isotopologue timecourses using the small-sample-corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc), enabling selection of the optimal isotopologue deconvolution model from a set of plausible alternatives. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: Ranks candidate moiety models fitted to MS isotopologue timecourses using the small-sample-corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc), enabling selection of the optimal isotopologue deconvolution model from a set of plausible alternatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The optimization objective function is an absolute difference matched to GAIMS behavior, where overfitting makes AICc ranking unable to recover the correct model Only a single plausible deconvolution model exists, so no model selection among competitors is required Isotopologue data are heavily degraded (e.g. added normal error with sigma = 0.1 on multi-tracer data, where propagated error reaches roughly nine times the original signal), making model selection unreliable

skills.description: Use when ranking candidate metabolite annotations for features from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS data, where each candidate must be scored by combining m/z error with pseudo-MS/MS fragment matching and AIF-only matches must be penalized.
skills.name: aif-fragment-down-weighting-scoring
skills.search_text: aif-fragment-down-weighting-scoring Use when ranking candidate metabolite annotations for features from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS data, where each candidate must be scored by combining m/z error with pseudo-MS/MS fragment matching and AIF-only matches must be penalized. When the goal is fragmentation-spectrum matching against curated MS/MS spectral databases (METLIN, MassBank, GNPS) from true DDA MS/MS rather than AIF pseudo-MS/MS spectra When input data were not acquired as all-ion fragmentation LC–MS/MS — only AIF is currently supported by MetaboAnnotatoR When the input is already an annotated feature table; this skill scores and ranks candidate annotations, it does not create the feature list http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Composite candidate-scoring mechanism from MetaboAnnotatoR that ranks library metabolite matches per LC–MS AIF feature by combining a bounded reciprocal m/z error term with a fragment-occurrence score in which fragments matched only in the AIF scan (rather than the pseudo-MS/MS spectrum) are down-weighted, reflecting their lower specificity. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Composite candidate-scoring mechanism from MetaboAnnotatoR that ranks library metabolite matches per LC–MS AIF feature by combining a bounded reciprocal m/z error term with a fragment-occurrence score in which fragments matched only in the AIF scan (rather than the pseudo-MS/MS spectrum) are down-weighted, reflecting their lower specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is fragmentation-spectrum matching against curated MS/MS spectral databases (METLIN, MassBank, GNPS) from true DDA MS/MS rather than AIF pseudo-MS/MS spectra When input data were not acquired as all-ion fragmentation LC–MS/MS — only AIF is currently supported by MetaboAnnotatoR When the input is already an annotated feature table; this skill scores and ranks candidate annotations, it does not create the feature list

skills.description: Use when annotating features from centroid-mode LC-MS AIF chromatograms (e.g., xcms/RAMClustR output) against fragment libraries, especially when isotopologues, in-source fragments, and adducts must be labeled and only a statistically significant subset of features needs annotation.
skills.name: aif-lcms-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: aif-lcms-metabolite-annotation Use when annotating features from centroid-mode LC-MS AIF chromatograms (e.g., xcms/RAMClustR output) against fragment libraries, especially when isotopologues, in-source fragments, and adducts must be labeled and only a statistically significant subset of features needs annotation. Data were acquired with DIA schemes other than AIF (e.g., SWATH) — only AIF is currently supported by MetaboAnnotatoR. The goal is exhaustive untargeted annotation of all detected features regardless of statistical significance — the workflow deliberately focuses on a subset of features and may miss low-intensity ones outside that subset. High-confidence MS/MS spectral matching on high mass accuracy instruments (e.g., Orbitrap) is required — although reportedly possible, this has not been tested/validated in the paper. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Automated annotation of isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments in untargeted all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS metabolomics data by combining correlation-based parent–fragment linking with molecular fragment matching, via the open-source MetaboAnnotatoR R package. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Automated annotation of isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments in untargeted all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS metabolomics data by combining correlation-based parent–fragment linking with molecular fragment matching, via the open-source MetaboAnnotatoR R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were acquired with DIA schemes other than AIF (e.g., SWATH) — only AIF is currently supported by MetaboAnnotatoR. The goal is exhaustive untargeted annotation of all detected features regardless of statistical significance — the workflow deliberately focuses on a subset of features and may miss low-intensity ones outside that subset. High-confidence MS/MS spectral matching on high mass accuracy instruments (e.g., Orbitrap) is required — although reportedly possible, this has not been tested/validated in the paper.

skills.description: Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS chromatograms whose parent–fragment relationships must be deconvoluted into pseudo-MS/MS spectra for metabolite annotation of isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments.
skills.name: aif-parent-fragment-deconvolution
skills.search_text: aif-parent-fragment-deconvolution Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS chromatograms whose parent–fragment relationships must be deconvoluted into pseudo-MS/MS spectra for metabolite annotation of isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments. Data were acquired with DIA schemes other than AIF (e.g. SWATH), which the package currently does not support. Input is already a deconvoluted pseudo-MS/MS spectrum or a feature list from another tool with the annotation step already complete. The sample matrix is dominated by nonlipid metabolites (e.g. urine MTBLS816 or amniotic fluid MTBLS666) and the nonlipid fragment library is small, as recall can drop to 10–88%. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs in-source parent–fragment ion relationships (pseudo-MS/MS spectra) from centroid-mode all-ion fragmentation LC–MS data by combining peak-shape correlation deconvolution with molecular fragment-library matching, using the MetaboAnnotatoR R package to annotate isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Reconstructs in-source parent–fragment ion relationships (pseudo-MS/MS spectra) from centroid-mode all-ion fragmentation LC–MS data by combining peak-shape correlation deconvolution with molecular fragment-library matching, using the MetaboAnnotatoR R package to annotate isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were acquired with DIA schemes other than AIF (e.g. SWATH), which the package currently does not support. Input is already a deconvoluted pseudo-MS/MS spectrum or a feature list from another tool with the annotation step already complete. The sample matrix is dominated by nonlipid metabolites (e.g. urine MTBLS816 or amniotic fluid MTBLS666) and the nonlipid fragment library is small, as recall can drop to 10–88%.

skills.description: Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS/MS chromatograms where no targeted MS/MS scans exist, and the goal is to recover parent–fragment relationships and annotate adducts, isotopologues, and in-source fragments.
skills.name: aif-pseudo-msms-deconvolution
skills.search_text: aif-pseudo-msms-deconvolution Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS/MS chromatograms where no targeted MS/MS scans exist, and the goal is to recover parent–fragment relationships and annotate adducts, isotopologues, and in-source fragments. When targeted MS/MS scans already exist for the features of interest — those spectra are higher quality than deconvoluted pseudo-MS/MS. When the dataset was acquired on a non-AIF DIA scheme (e.g. SWATH), which is not yet supported by MetaboAnnotatoR. When the user already has an expert-curated feature table with manual annotations — deconvolution would add redundant processing rather than new information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reconstruct pseudo-MS/MS spectra from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS runs by linking co-eluting fragment peaks to their parent ions, then match those spectra against in-silico fragment libraries (e.g. LipidBlast, MetaboAnnotatoR fragment libraries) to annotate metabolite features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Reconstruct pseudo-MS/MS spectra from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS runs by linking co-eluting fragment peaks to their parent ions, then match those spectra against in-silico fragment libraries (e.g. LipidBlast, MetaboAnnotatoR fragment libraries) to annotate metabolite features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When targeted MS/MS scans already exist for the features of interest — those spectra are higher quality than deconvoluted pseudo-MS/MS. When the dataset was acquired on a non-AIF DIA scheme (e.g. SWATH), which is not yet supported by MetaboAnnotatoR. When the user already has an expert-curated feature table with manual annotations — deconvolution would add redundant processing rather than new information.

skills.name: aird-format-ms-data-loading
skills.search_text: aird-format-ms-data-loading Use when vendor DDA LC-MS files (.wiff, .raw) must be converted to Aird format and imported into MetaPro for multi-batch target search or QC inspection. Data are already converted to .aird/.json pairs — go straight to loading into MetaPro rather than reconverting The downstream analysis tool does not read the Aird format (e.g., pipelines expecting mzML/mzXML) — although AirdPro can export mzML/mzXML, this skill targets MetaPro ingestion Acquisition is a mode unsupported by the AirdPro version in use (e.g., MRM/SRM or wiff2 requires AirdPro V5.1.0 or later, not the v1.1 release referenced by MetaPro) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Converts vendor LC-MS instrument files (TripleTOF .wiff, QE HF .raw) into the Aird computation-oriented format with AirdPro and loads them into MetaPro (backed by Redis and MongoDB) for batch semi-targeted analysis and QC inspection. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-023-02018-6
skills.summary: Converts vendor LC-MS instrument files (TripleTOF .wiff, QE HF .raw) into the Aird computation-oriented format with AirdPro and loads them into MetaPro (backed by Redis and MongoDB) for batch semi-targeted analysis and QC inspection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already converted to .aird/.json pairs — go straight to loading into MetaPro rather than reconverting The downstream analysis tool does not read the Aird format (e.g., pipelines expecting mzML/mzXML) — although AirdPro can export mzML/mzXML, this skill targets MetaPro ingestion Acquisition is a mode unsupported by the AirdPro version in use (e.g., MRM/SRM or wiff2 requires AirdPro V5.1.0 or later, not the v1.1 release referenced by MetaPro)

skills.description: Use when reading, validating, generating, or comparing the metadata/index side of an Aird file pair (.json index + .aird data), or when deciding between JSON and XML for mass spec metadata storage.
skills.name: aird-metadata-schema-handling
skills.search_text: aird-metadata-schema-handling Use when reading, validating, generating, or comparing the metadata/index side of an Aird file pair (.json index + .aird data), or when deciding between JSON and XML for mass spec metadata storage. The task concerns compression or decoding of the binary spectral arrays (m/z via ZDPD, intensity) inside the .aird data file, not the metadata/index document. The input is a vendor file or mzML/mgf/mz5 file that has not yet been converted with AirdPro — no Aird JSON index exists yet. The analysis requires PSI CV-annotated XML metadata semantics by mandate; Aird's JSON index is a text-previewable alternative, not an mzML replacement. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Handles the JSON metadata (index) component of Aird mass spectrometry files using the AirdMetaData.json schema — Aird deliberately stores metadata as JSON rather than XML so the index is smaller (about 65% less text for SCIEX TOF files) and human-previewable. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Handles the JSON metadata (index) component of Aird mass spectrometry files using the AirdMetaData.json schema — Aird deliberately stores metadata as JSON rather than XML so the index is smaller (about 65% less text for SCIEX TOF files) and human-previewable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task concerns compression or decoding of the binary spectral arrays (m/z via ZDPD, intensity) inside the .aird data file, not the metadata/index document. The input is a vendor file or mzML/mgf/mz5 file that has not yet been converted with AirdPro — no Aird JSON index exists yet. The analysis requires PSI CV-annotated XML metadata semantics by mandate; Aird's JSON index is a text-previewable alternative, not an mzML replacement.

skills.description: Use when choosing or validating an MS data storage format for MRM acquisition files, or when replicating decoding-speed benchmarks between Aird and mzML on full-file and random-access reading modes.
skills.name: aird-vs-mzml-decoding-comparison
skills.search_text: aird-vs-mzml-decoding-comparison Use when choosing or validating an MS data storage format for MRM acquisition files, or when replicating decoding-speed benchmarks between Aird and mzML on full-file and random-access reading modes. The question concerns quantification accuracy or manual inspection features of MRM analysis tools (e.g. MRMPro vs Skyline) rather than raw data-format decoding speed The input is already an analysis result (e.g. xlsx identification results or a feature table) rather than raw MRM spectral data in Aird or mzML The data are DDA/DIA/PASEF rather than MRM, since this benchmark is specific to full MRM file reading and MRM chromatogram random access http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A benchmarking skill for quantifying the wall-clock decoding speedup of the Aird mass spectrometry format over mzML for MRM data, reporting approximately 33x for full-file reading and approximately 2.5x for single-chromatogram random access. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05685-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for quantifying the wall-clock decoding speedup of the Aird mass spectrometry format over mzML for MRM data, reporting approximately 33x for full-file reading and approximately 2.5x for single-chromatogram random access.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns quantification accuracy or manual inspection features of MRM analysis tools (e.g. MRMPro vs Skyline) rather than raw data-format decoding speed The input is already an analysis result (e.g. xlsx identification results or a feature table) rather than raw MRM spectral data in Aird or mzML The data are DDA/DIA/PASEF rather than MRM, since this benchmark is specific to full MRM file reading and MRM chromatogram random access

skills.description: Use when aligning two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS datasets with Eclipse's MSAligner and you need to verify that the graph-based feature grouping result does not depend on dataset insertion order.
skills.name: algorithm-order-invariance-testing
skills.search_text: algorithm-order-invariance-testing Use when aligning two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS datasets with Eclipse's MSAligner and you need to verify that the graph-based feature grouping result does not depend on dataset insertion order. The datasets have already been merged into a single complete dataset by an upstream tool (e.g., Gravity clustering or Formation formatting), so no pairwise re-alignment is being tested You are evaluating a non-Eclipse aligner whose algorithm makes no order-independence claim — the invariant comparison is only meaningful if the tool states it is order-independent http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 A validation technique for Eclipse's graph-based LC-MS dataset alignment in which the alignment is re-run with datasets inserted in a different order and the resulting feature group assignments are compared, verifying the tool's stated order-independence invariant for n > 2 dataset alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: A validation technique for Eclipse's graph-based LC-MS dataset alignment in which the alignment is re-run with datasets inserted in a different order and the resulting feature group assignments are compared, verifying the tool's stated order-independence invariant for n > 2 dataset alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets have already been merged into a single complete dataset by an upstream tool (e.g., Gravity clustering or Formation formatting), so no pairwise re-alignment is being tested You are evaluating a non-Eclipse aligner whose algorithm makes no order-independence claim — the invariant comparison is only meaningful if the tool states it is order-independent

skills.search_text: algorithm-runtime-benchmarking Use when several candidate peak-picking algorithms must be compared for reliability vs. wall-clock runtime on LC-HRMS chromatogram data (mzXML), e.g. to choose a MetMatch peak-picking backend. The input is already a processed feature table rather than raw chromatogram data — peak picking (and therefore this benchmark) is unnecessary Only a single peak-picking algorithm is available, so no runtime/reliability comparison can be made The task is metabolite alignment of feature lists, not peak-picking algorithm selection or benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark the runtimes of alternative chromatographic peak-picking algorithms (MassSpecWavelet, Gaussian peak correlation, Savitzky-Golay filter) implemented in MetMatch, which operates on LC-HRMS chromatograms stored as mzXML and requires Java JRE 1.8 or newer. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table rather than raw chromatogram data — peak picking (and therefore this benchmark) is unnecessary Only a single peak-picking algorithm is available, so no runtime/reliability comparison can be made The task is metabolite alignment of feature lists, not peak-picking algorithm selection or benchmarking

skills.description: Use when you need to estimate or reproduce the alignment FDR of DeepRTAlign output — e.g. re-deriving information_target.csv filtering from information_all.csv using the decoy/target ratio with the default fdr=0.01 threshold.
skills.name: aligned-feature-table-processing
skills.search_text: aligned-feature-table-processing Use when you need to estimate or reproduce the alignment FDR of DeepRTAlign output — e.g. re-deriving information_target.csv filtering from information_all.csv using the decoy/target ratio with the default fdr=0.01 threshold. Input is raw LC-MS data (e.g. mzML/Thermo RAW) rather than feature-extraction output tables — feature extraction must be done first with a supported tool (Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder) You only need the final aligned feature table and have no requirement to audit or re-derive the QC/FDR step — simply run DeepRTAlign with keep_temp=0, which yields only information_target.csv The analysis is identification-based MBR alignment (e.g. MaxQuant match between runs) rather than ID-free feature alignment, where the decoy-sample design does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs DeepRTAlign's decoy-based quality-control module, which estimates the false discovery rate of RT alignment results by building a decoy counterpart for one randomly selected sample in each m/z window (default bin_width 0.03, bin_precision 2) and counting decoy vs target alignments at each score cutoff. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Reconstructs DeepRTAlign's decoy-based quality-control module, which estimates the false discovery rate of RT alignment results by building a decoy counterpart for one randomly selected sample in each m/z window (default bin_width 0.03, bin_precision 2) and counting decoy vs target alignments at each score cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data (e.g. mzML/Thermo RAW) rather than feature-extraction output tables — feature extraction must be done first with a supported tool (Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder) You only need the final aligned feature table and have no requirement to audit or re-derive the QC/FDR step — simply run DeepRTAlign with keep_temp=0, which yields only information_target.csv The analysis is identification-based MBR alignment (e.g. MaxQuant match between runs) rather than ID-free feature alignment, where the decoy-sample design does not apply

skills.description: Use when an LC–MS feature alignment output (consensus feature table) must be quantitatively scored against a manually annotated feature dataset, e.g. benchmarking G-Aligner vs OpenMS/MZmine2/XCMS on MTBLS562, QE_HF or TripleTOF_6600.
skills.name: alignment-accuracy-evaluation-metrics
skills.search_text: alignment-accuracy-evaluation-metrics Use when an LC–MS feature alignment output (consensus feature table) must be quantitatively scored against a manually annotated feature dataset, e.g. benchmarking G-Aligner vs OpenMS/MZmine2/XCMS on MTBLS562, QE_HF or TripleTOF_6600. Input is raw mzML data that has not yet been feature-detected and aligned — run feature extraction and alignment first before evaluation is possible No manually annotated ground-truth feature list exists for the dataset — F_ACC/A_ACC cannot be computed and only relative/indirect comparisons are possible The goal is runtime/speed benchmarking rather than alignment accuracy — the paper's own limitation is that G-Aligner's multidimensional assignment (NP-Hard) lacks computing speed, which these accuracy metrics do not capture http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates LC–MS feature alignment quality by comparing aligned consensus features against manually annotated ground-truth feature lists (m/z, RT, area of library analytes), computing TP/FP/TN/FN, precision, recall, F1, feature alignment accuracy (F_ACC) and analyte alignment accuracy (A_ACC). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Evaluates LC–MS feature alignment quality by comparing aligned consensus features against manually annotated ground-truth feature lists (m/z, RT, area of library analytes), computing TP/FP/TN/FN, precision, recall, F1, feature alignment accuracy (F_ACC) and analyte alignment accuracy (A_ACC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzML data that has not yet been feature-detected and aligned — run feature extraction and alignment first before evaluation is possible No manually annotated ground-truth feature list exists for the dataset — F_ACC/A_ACC cannot be computed and only relative/indirect comparisons are possible The goal is runtime/speed benchmarking rather than alignment accuracy — the paper's own limitation is that G-Aligner's multidimensional assignment (NP-Hard) lacks computing speed, which these accuracy metrics do not capture

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how many more peptides or MS features a candidate LC-MS retention time alignment workflow aligns versus MBR-based or feature-based baselines, while checking that quantitative accuracy is not compromised.
skills.name: alignment-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: alignment-benchmark-comparison Use when you need to quantify how many more peptides or MS features a candidate LC-MS retention time alignment workflow aligns versus MBR-based or feature-based baselines, while checking that quantitative accuracy is not compromised. The goal is biomarker discovery or downstream modeling on aligned features rather than comparing alignment tool performance Only a single LC-MS run is available — RT alignment and MBR comparison are undefined without multiple runs You need raw feature extraction optimization rather than alignment evaluation (the authors note alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks a deep-learning retention time alignment workflow (e.g. DeepRTAlign combined with feature extraction and identification tools) against established match-between-runs and feature-alignment baselines (MaxQuant MBR, MSFragger MBR, OpenMS, DIA-NN) by counting aligned peptides/features and comparing quantification accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks a deep-learning retention time alignment workflow (e.g. DeepRTAlign combined with feature extraction and identification tools) against established match-between-runs and feature-alignment baselines (MaxQuant MBR, MSFragger MBR, OpenMS, DIA-NN) by counting aligned peptides/features and comparing quantification accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biomarker discovery or downstream modeling on aligned features rather than comparing alignment tool performance Only a single LC-MS run is available — RT alignment and MBR comparison are undefined without multiple runs You need raw feature extraction optimization rather than alignment evaluation (the authors note alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction)

skills.description: Use when a new or modified LC-HRMS alignment configuration needs quantitative validation against a ground-truth benchmark, e.g. after changing m/z or retention-time tolerance settings or adduct-recombination rules.
skills.name: alignment-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: alignment-benchmark-evaluation Use when a new or modified LC-HRMS alignment configuration needs quantitative validation against a ground-truth benchmark, e.g. after changing m/z or retention-time tolerance settings or adduct-recombination rules. The input is already an aligned feature matrix rather than unaligned LC-HRMS feature lists requiring retention-time and m/z shift correction The analysis goal is peak detection or feature finding rather than evaluating alignment of already-processed chromatograms No ground-truth (or artificially simulated) feature correspondences exist, so Tp/Fp and F-measure cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark an LC-HRMS feature alignment tool (MetMatch) by applying artificial m/z and retention-time transformations to a reference feature list and scoring matches against known ground-truth correspondences using true positives, false positives, and F-measure. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: Benchmark an LC-HRMS feature alignment tool (MetMatch) by applying artificial m/z and retention-time transformations to a reference feature list and scoring matches against known ground-truth correspondences using true positives, false positives, and F-measure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an aligned feature matrix rather than unaligned LC-HRMS feature lists requiring retention-time and m/z shift correction The analysis goal is peak detection or feature finding rather than evaluating alignment of already-processed chromatograms No ground-truth (or artificially simulated) feature correspondences exist, so Tp/Fp and F-measure cannot be computed

skills.summary: Reproduce and stress-test peak-list alignment benchmarks (RANSAC vs Join aligner) from MZmine 2 against Lange et al. ground-truth alignment tables, quantifying how feature-count inflation (e.g. P2 fraction 00 with >6800 aligned rows) degrades RANSAC model fitting.

skills.description: Use when reproducing a multi-dataset LC-MS feature alignment where the number of features found in all datasets and in n≥k datasets must be checked against a published reference table (e.g., Supplementary Table S2 values 976 and 5334).
skills.name: alignment-coverage-count-validation-against-reference-table
skills.search_text: alignment-coverage-count-validation-against-reference-table Use when reproducing a multi-dataset LC-MS feature alignment where the number of features found in all datasets and in n≥k datasets must be checked against a published reference table (e.g., Supplementary Table S2 values 976 and 5334). When a different alignment configuration is being reproduced — the reference counts 976/5334 apply only to Intensity matching disabled and nonclique clustering at diameter=2 When datasets have not already been processed into Feature Metadata + Feature Abundances tables conforming to the BMXP shared schema When fewer than six datasets are being aligned, since the n>=6 coverage count is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Runs Eclipse MSAligner across eleven LC-MS datasets under a specified configuration (Intensity matching disabled, nonclique clustering with diameter=2) and validates the resulting feature-coverage counts (976 features in all eleven datasets; 5334 in n≥6 datasets) against Supplementary Table S2. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: Runs Eclipse MSAligner across eleven LC-MS datasets under a specified configuration (Intensity matching disabled, nonclique clustering with diameter=2) and validates the resulting feature-coverage counts (976 features in all eleven datasets; 5334 in n≥6 datasets) against Supplementary Table S2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a different alignment configuration is being reproduced — the reference counts 976/5334 apply only to Intensity matching disabled and nonclique clustering at diameter=2 When datasets have not already been processed into Feature Metadata + Feature Abundances tables conforming to the BMXP shared schema When fewer than six datasets are being aligned, since the n>=6 coverage count is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have both unaligned and aligned NPP output tables (e.g. XCMS_unaligned_run3.csv and XCMS_aligned_run3.csv) plus a generated benchmark, and you need to quantify peaks lost or misaligned during sample alignment.
skills.name: alignment-loss-quantification
skills.search_text: alignment-loss-quantification Use when you have both unaligned and aligned NPP output tables (e.g. XCMS_unaligned_run3.csv and XCMS_aligned_run3.csv) plus a generated benchmark, and you need to quantify peaks lost or misaligned during sample alignment. No benchmark dataset has been generated yet — mzRAPP's assessment requires a validated benchmark; raw mzML files alone are insufficient. The output to evaluate is not an NPP peak/alignment table from a supported tool (XCMS, MZmine 2, MS-DIAL, etc.) but already a manually validated or targeted feature table. Only a single (aligned) NPP output is available — alignment loss cannot be quantified without the unaligned counterpart. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies how many benchmark peaks are lost or misaligned when non-targeted pre-processing (NPP) outputs are aligned across samples, using mzRAPP to match an XCMS (or similar tool) aligned and unaligned output against a validated benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab231
skills.summary: Quantifies how many benchmark peaks are lost or misaligned when non-targeted pre-processing (NPP) outputs are aligned across samples, using mzRAPP to match an XCMS (or similar tool) aligned and unaligned output against a validated benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No benchmark dataset has been generated yet — mzRAPP's assessment requires a validated benchmark; raw mzML files alone are insufficient. The output to evaluate is not an NPP peak/alignment table from a supported tool (XCMS, MZmine 2, MS-DIAL, etc.) but already a manually validated or targeted feature table. Only a single (aligned) NPP output is available — alignment loss cannot be quantified without the unaligned counterpart.

skills.description: Use when combining three or more independently processed LC-MS feature tables with a sequential alignment tool and you must verify that matched annotations are order-invariant and that spurious annotation mismatches are quantified against a reference alignment.
skills.name: alignment-order-dependence-assessment
skills.search_text: alignment-order-dependence-assessment Use when combining three or more independently processed LC-MS feature tables with a sequential alignment tool and you must verify that matched annotations are order-invariant and that spurious annotation mismatches are quantified against a reference alignment. You are aligning only two datasets, where sequential-order effects of the kind seen for n > 2 dataset combinations do not arise Your features lack a stable cross-dataset identifier such as Annotation_ID, making cross-referencing against a reference alignment impossible The aligner under test uses a graph-based formulation that is inherently order-invariant (e.g., Eclipse's graph-based approach for n > 2 datasets), so an order-permutation assessment adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assesses whether multi-dataset LC-MS alignment results change when the order in which datasets are combined is permuted, and benchmarks the alignment against a reference tool by counting overlapping annotations matched and spurious annotation-mismatch hits (e.g., metabCombiner 26 vs Eclipse 3 on DS1–4). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: Assesses whether multi-dataset LC-MS alignment results change when the order in which datasets are combined is permuted, and benchmarks the alignment against a reference tool by counting overlapping annotations matched and spurious annotation-mismatch hits (e.g., metabCombiner 26 vs Eclipse 3 on DS1–4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are aligning only two datasets, where sequential-order effects of the kind seen for n > 2 dataset combinations do not arise Your features lack a stable cross-dataset identifier such as Annotation_ID, making cross-referencing against a reference alignment impossible The aligner under test uses a graph-based formulation that is inherently order-invariant (e.g., Eclipse's graph-based approach for n > 2 datasets), so an order-permutation assessment adds no information

skills.description: Use when you must quantitatively compare a peak list alignment method's output rows to known ground-truth correspondences, or reproduce the RANSAC vs Join aligner benchmark on synthetic lipidomic and real Lange et al. datasets.
skills.name: alignment-precision-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: alignment-precision-recall-evaluation Use when you must quantitatively compare a peak list alignment method's output rows to known ground-truth correspondences, or reproduce the RANSAC vs Join aligner benchmark on synthetic lipidomic and real Lange et al. datasets. The data are raw LC-MS profiles with no detected peaks or peak lists — peak detection must be done first There is no ground-truth alignment table, so TP/FP/FN counts cannot be established You only need to run alignment for downstream analysis, not to benchmark alignment quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark a peak list alignment algorithm (e.g., the Join aligner or the RANSAC aligner in MZmine 2) by comparing its aligned rows against ground-truth alignment tables and computing precision (TP/(TP+FP)) and recall (TP/(TP+FN)) per dataset, as done for LC-MS/proteomic/metabolomic peak alignment in MZmine 2. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-11-395
skills.summary: Benchmark a peak list alignment algorithm (e.g., the Join aligner or the RANSAC aligner in MZmine 2) by comparing its aligned rows against ground-truth alignment tables and computing precision (TP/(TP+FP)) and recall (TP/(TP+FN)) per dataset, as done for LC-MS/proteomic/metabolomic peak alignment in MZmine 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw LC-MS profiles with no detected peaks or peak lists — peak detection must be done first There is no ground-truth alignment table, so TP/FP/FN counts cannot be established You only need to run alignment for downstream analysis, not to benchmark alignment quality

skills.description: Use when you must reproduce MS-DIAL's aligned LC-MS output (text export and .dcl representative spectra) from source without building a GUI project file or EIC cache, e.g. for large file-count cohorts where the full alignment mode is too memory-heavy.
skills.name: alignment-representative-spectra-export
skills.search_text: alignment-representative-spectra-export Use when you must reproduce MS-DIAL's aligned LC-MS output (text export and .dcl representative spectra) from source without building a GUI project file or EIC cache, e.g. for large file-count cohorts where the full alignment mode is too memory-heavy. When you need isotope/adduct or ion-abundance correlation links between aligned peaks — light mode with 'Alignment light correlation links: False' discards them and collapses each spot to one representative peak. When your input is already a feature/alignment table and you only need downstream statistics, not re-running MS-DIAL alignment. When you rely on the 'Debug/Release vendor unsupported' build to read proprietary vendor raw formats — per the README it only supports abf, cdf, and mzml. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Exports MS-DIAL alignment results in a headless, memory-bounded 'light mode' streaming path: each aligned spot's AlignedPeakProperties is reduced to a single representative peak and MSDec results are written to the alignment .dcl via AlignmentLightQuantValueAccessor-backed exporters, byte-identical to the full-mode alignment export. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-54137-w
skills.summary: Exports MS-DIAL alignment results in a headless, memory-bounded 'light mode' streaming path: each aligned spot's AlignedPeakProperties is reduced to a single representative peak and MSDec results are written to the alignment .dcl via AlignmentLightQuantValueAccessor-backed exporters, byte-identical to the full-mode alignment export.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need isotope/adduct or ion-abundance correlation links between aligned peaks — light mode with 'Alignment light correlation links: False' discards them and collapses each spot to one representative peak. When your input is already a feature/alignment table and you only need downstream statistics, not re-running MS-DIAL alignment. When you rely on the 'Debug/Release vendor unsupported' build to read proprietary vendor raw formats — per the README it only supports abf, cdf, and mzml.

skills.description: Use when simulating DIA-mode LC-MS/MS acquisition over a set of generated or extracted chemicals — e.g. you need fragmentation scans covering an m/z range rather than single-precursor DDA selections.
skills.name: all-ion-fragmentation-controller-configuration
skills.search_text: all-ion-fragmentation-controller-configuration Use when simulating DIA-mode LC-MS/MS acquisition over a set of generated or extracted chemicals — e.g. you need fragmentation scans covering an m/z range rather than single-precursor DDA selections. The goal is data-dependent acquisition targeting single precursor ions — use the Top-N DDA controller instead of AIF A different DIA strategy is required, e.g. SWATH-MS sequential windowed acquisition rather than all-ion fragmentation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Configures and runs ViMMS 2.0's AIF (all-ion fragmentation) controller to simulate data-independent acquisition (DIA), where a range of m/z values is co-isolated and fragmented instead of individual precursors as in Top-N DDA. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Configures and runs ViMMS 2.0's AIF (all-ion fragmentation) controller to simulate data-independent acquisition (DIA), where a range of m/z values is co-isolated and fragmented instead of individual precursors as in Top-N DDA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is data-dependent acquisition targeting single precursor ions — use the Top-N DDA controller instead of AIF A different DIA strategy is required, e.g. SWATH-MS sequential windowed acquisition rather than all-ion fragmentation

skills.description: Use when pixel-level clustering of a brain IMS feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 m/z ions) must be validated against a reference anatomy atlas to confirm clusters recover known tissue divisions.
skills.name: allen-atlas-anatomical-mapping
skills.search_text: allen-atlas-anatomical-mapping Use when pixel-level clustering of a brain IMS feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 m/z ions) must be validated against a reference anatomy atlas to confirm clusters recover known tissue divisions. Input is raw mass-spectrometry imaging data (not yet peak-picked into a pixel x m/z feature matrix) — run SMAnalyst's quality control and preprocessing first Goal is metabolite annotation or differential analysis between ROIs rather than validating spatial clustering against brain anatomy Tissue is not mouse brain (or has no comparable reference atlas), so Allen Atlas concordance cannot serve as a validation criterion http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Annotates spatial metabolomics pixel-clustering results from a mouse brain coronal section against the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas, verifying that unsupervised clusters correspond to major anatomical divisions (cerebral cortex, hippocampus, midbrain, hindbrain, fiber tracts). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Annotates spatial metabolomics pixel-clustering results from a mouse brain coronal section against the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas, verifying that unsupervised clusters correspond to major anatomical divisions (cerebral cortex, hippocampus, midbrain, hindbrain, fiber tracts).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mass-spectrometry imaging data (not yet peak-picked into a pixel x m/z feature matrix) — run SMAnalyst's quality control and preprocessing first Goal is metabolite annotation or differential analysis between ROIs rather than validating spatial clustering against brain anatomy Tissue is not mouse brain (or has no comparable reference atlas), so Allen Atlas concordance cannot serve as a validation criterion

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics table has sparse or missing cross-database identifiers (HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) and records of the same metabolite must be linked across databases despite mismatches and missing foreign references.
skills.name: ambiguous-identifier-aggregation
skills.search_text: ambiguous-identifier-aggregation Use when a metabolomics table has sparse or missing cross-database identifiers (HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) and records of the same metabolite must be linked across databases despite mismatches and missing foreign references. The compound database of interest is outside the five supported databases — the package supports only HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG and LIPID MAPS (METLIN is cited in the paper but is not in the supported list) Input records already carry complete, unambiguous identifiers in every target database, so no empty-field resolution is needed You cannot set up a local PostgreSQL database and download the HMDB/ChEBI/LIPID MAPS dump files, since the cache-based algorithm depends on them A queue-based identifier-resolution method, implemented in the MetaFetcheR R package, that maps sparse primary metabolite identifiers (HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) to identifiers in other databases by filling empty fields and reiterating exhaustively until no further resolution is possible. It stores multiple ambiguous mapped identifiers per compound to avoid the information loss of single-database (e.g. HMDB-only) mapping. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.02.28.433248
skills.summary: A queue-based identifier-resolution method, implemented in the MetaFetcheR R package, that maps sparse primary metabolite identifiers (HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) to identifiers in other databases by filling empty fields and reiterating exhaustively until no further resolution is possible. It stores multiple ambiguous mapped identifiers per compound to avoid the information loss of single-database (e.g. HMDB-only) mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound database of interest is outside the five supported databases — the package supports only HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG and LIPID MAPS (METLIN is cited in the paper but is not in the supported list) Input records already carry complete, unambiguous identifiers in every target database, so no empty-field resolution is needed You cannot set up a local PostgreSQL database and download the HMDB/ChEBI/LIPID MAPS dump files, since the cache-based algorithm depends on them

skills.description: Use when predicting m/z values of amine-derivatized metabolites (e.g. dopamine, GABA, spermidine with AMPP) where reactive sites and the resulting mass shifts must be computed from structural SMILES before annotation.
skills.name: amine-derivatization-site-detection
skills.search_text: amine-derivatization-site-detection Use when predicting m/z values of amine-derivatized metabolites (e.g. dopamine, GABA, spermidine with AMPP) where reactive sites and the resulting mass shifts must be computed from structural SMILES before annotation. When metabolites lack derivatization-reactive amine functional groups (substructure matching will find zero sites and no derivative m/z can be computed) When the analysis target is pixel-level annotation of raw MALDI-MSI m/z features (use Met-ID's identify() workflow instead; this skill predicts candidate derivative masses upstream) When the derivatizing reagent is already the preconfigured FMP-10 matrix covered by Met-ID's built-in database and setup http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Detects derivatization-reactive amine functional groups in metabolite SMILES and computes per-site derivative m/z values by applying one AMPP reagent mass shift per reactive site, extending Met-ID's derivatization-aware annotation beyond the preconfigured in-house FMP-10 matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00633
skills.summary: Detects derivatization-reactive amine functional groups in metabolite SMILES and computes per-site derivative m/z values by applying one AMPP reagent mass shift per reactive site, extending Met-ID's derivatization-aware annotation beyond the preconfigured in-house FMP-10 matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When metabolites lack derivatization-reactive amine functional groups (substructure matching will find zero sites and no derivative m/z can be computed) When the analysis target is pixel-level annotation of raw MALDI-MSI m/z features (use Met-ID's identify() workflow instead; this skill predicts candidate derivative masses upstream) When the derivatizing reagent is already the preconfigured FMP-10 matrix covered by Met-ID's built-in database and setup

skills.description: Use when raw SRM/MRM files from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S serum runs) must be reanalyzed in Skyline to reproduce or audit vendor-reported amino acid concentrations.
skills.name: amino-acid-biocrates-p180-kit-analysis
skills.search_text: amino-acid-biocrates-p180-kit-analysis Use when raw SRM/MRM files from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S serum runs) must be reanalyzed in Skyline to reproduce or audit vendor-reported amino acid concentrations. The data require nontargeted feature-finding, alignment, and identification workflows (XCMS, MZmine, MS-DIAL) rather than extraction of known targets The instrument/workflow is a latest-generation or vendor-specific acquisition Skyline does not yet support, since Skyline may lag behind commercial software until support is implemented The sample data are GC-MS or ion mobility small molecule runs, whose Skyline support is still ongoing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reprocess raw targeted SRM data from the Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 kit (19 amino acids in human serum) in Skyline using the instrument vendor's calibration parameters, then benchmark the resulting concentrations against the vendor software (TargetLynx) by linear regression. skills.when_to_use_negative: The data require nontargeted feature-finding, alignment, and identification workflows (XCMS, MZmine, MS-DIAL) rather than extraction of known targets The instrument/workflow is a latest-generation or vendor-specific acquisition Skyline does not yet support, since Skyline may lag behind commercial software until support is implemented The sample data are GC-MS or ion mobility small molecule runs, whose Skyline support is still ongoing

skills.description: Use when you have a FASTA collection of peptide sequences and need the overall residue frequency distribution to determine which amino acids dominate, e.g., characterizing natural peptide hormone composition.
skills.name: amino-acid-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: amino-acid-composition-analysis Use when you have a FASTA collection of peptide sequences and need the overall residue frequency distribution to determine which amino acids dominate, e.g., characterizing natural peptide hormone composition. The goal is per-sequence physicochemical characterization (e.g., hydrophobic residue percentage per peptide, Fig. 11 histogram) rather than the aggregate residue distribution. The input contains non-peptide sequences or heavy use of non-standard/gap characters that would distort a count restricted to the 20 standard amino acids. The analysis requires positional or motif-level composition (e.g., residue enrichment at peptide termini) rather than the whole-collection frequency profile. http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_0078 Computes the frequency distribution of the 20 standard amino acids across a peptide sequence collection (e.g., HORDB peptide hormone FASTA records) to identify the dominant residues — arginine, glycine, leucine and serine for natural peptide hormones, as reported in Fig. 12 of the HORDB paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-022-01287-5
skills.summary: Computes the frequency distribution of the 20 standard amino acids across a peptide sequence collection (e.g., HORDB peptide hormone FASTA records) to identify the dominant residues — arginine, glycine, leucine and serine for natural peptide hormones, as reported in Fig. 12 of the HORDB paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-sequence physicochemical characterization (e.g., hydrophobic residue percentage per peptide, Fig. 11 histogram) rather than the aggregate residue distribution. The input contains non-peptide sequences or heavy use of non-standard/gap characters that would distort a count restricted to the 20 standard amino acids. The analysis requires positional or motif-level composition (e.g., residue enrichment at peptide termini) rather than the whole-collection frequency profile.

skills.description: Use when GC-MS peak-area tables of amino acids paired with stable-isotope-labeled internal standards are available and you need to compare precision (RSD) across derivatization reagents or report one-to-one ISTD-normalized amino-acid quantities.
skills.name: amino-acid-derivatization-response-ratio-quantification
skills.search_text: amino-acid-derivatization-response-ratio-quantification Use when GC-MS peak-area tables of amino acids paired with stable-isotope-labeled internal standards are available and you need to compare precision (RSD) across derivatization reagents or report one-to-one ISTD-normalized amino-acid quantities. Input is a large-scale untargeted GC-MS feature table lacking paired stable-isotope-labeled internal standards — use SERRF/SERDA-style normalization instead (the paper found neither internal-standard nor sum-based normalization achieved <30% median RSD across 563 annotations). Peak areas come from LC-MS or non-derivatized analyses where the PCF/MTBSTFA/MSTFA reagent comparison does not apply. The goal is batch correction across 1.2 years of acquisitions with column changes rather than derivatization-precision benchmarking on a small sample set. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Quantifies derivatized amino acids in GC-MS by dividing each amino acid's raw peak area by its cognate stable-isotope-labeled internal standard, then computing per-compound RSDs across samples to benchmark derivatization agents (PCF vs MTBSTFA vs MSTFA). It grounds derivatization-reagent selection in measured precision rather than vendor claims. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080944
skills.summary: Quantifies derivatized amino acids in GC-MS by dividing each amino acid's raw peak area by its cognate stable-isotope-labeled internal standard, then computing per-compound RSDs across samples to benchmark derivatization agents (PCF vs MTBSTFA vs MSTFA). It grounds derivatization-reagent selection in measured precision rather than vendor claims.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a large-scale untargeted GC-MS feature table lacking paired stable-isotope-labeled internal standards — use SERRF/SERDA-style normalization instead (the paper found neither internal-standard nor sum-based normalization achieved <30% median RSD across 563 annotations). Peak areas come from LC-MS or non-derivatized analyses where the PCF/MTBSTFA/MSTFA reagent comparison does not apply. The goal is batch correction across 1.2 years of acquisitions with column changes rather than derivatization-precision benchmarking on a small sample set.

skills.description: Use when raw per-tool de novo prediction sets (peptide sequence + tool-specific confidence score) must be filtered to a precision-calibrated subset, using a pseudo-ground-truth peptide list from database search at 1% FDR.
skills.name: amino-acid-level-mass-matching-evaluation
skills.search_text: amino-acid-level-mass-matching-evaluation Use when raw per-tool de novo prediction sets (peptide sequence + tool-specific confidence score) must be filtered to a precision-calibrated subset, using a pseudo-ground-truth peptide list from database search at 1% FDR. When the predictions will be evaluated at the whole-peptide level rather than the amino-acid level — the matched-AA criterion (mass difference <0.1 Da, prefix-mass difference <0.5 Da) will not reflect peptide-level recall or precision. When no database-search reference (PeptideShaker/MS-GF+/X!Tandem at 1% FDR) is available to serve as pseudo-ground truth for precision computation. skills.search_text: annotation-metric-evaluation Use when you have mWISE (or xMSannotator) candidate annotations for LC-MS peaks and a reference annotation table, and you need per-assay sensitivity/specificity/precision/F1 to benchmark a prioritization configuration. skills.search_text: annotation-power-and-tpr-metric-computation Use when comparing metabolite annotations from two annotation methods (e.g., ML vs rule-based) at FDR < 10% against an independent MS/MS-validated LC-MS/MS reference set, to compute MAP and TPR metrics. skills.description: Use when comparing predicted peak-level formula annotations against expert-curated annotations (e.g. NIST20) to score a spectrum-prediction model's annotation quality with recall, precision, and F1.
skills.name: annotation-precision-recall-f1-evaluation
skills.search_text: annotation-precision-recall-f1-evaluation Use when comparing predicted peak-level formula annotations against expert-curated annotations (e.g. NIST20) to score a spectrum-prediction model's annotation quality with recall, precision, and F1. Input spectra lack expert-curated formula annotations, so no ground-truth annotation sets A(m) exist to compare against The goal is retrieval-based MS2C ranking (Top-k candidate scoring by Tanimoto similarity), not per-peak annotation accuracy Spectra are glycan or peptide spectra — the original analysis excluded these and focused on small molecules http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates predicted formula annotations on MS/MS peaks by matching predicted peaks to expert-curated real peaks within a 10 ppm tolerance, then computing annotation recall (AR), intensity-weighted recall (AWR), annotation precision (AP), weighted precision (AWP), and their harmonic-mean F1 scores (AF1, AWF1). This scores how faithfully a C2MS model's formula distribution reproduces the chemical information needed for peak annotation.
