skills.description: Use when benchmarking inference speed and accuracy trade-offs of an autoregressive structure-elucidation model against diffusion-based baselines on the same spectra test fold.
skills.name: beam-width-sweep-decoding-evaluation
skills.search_text: beam-width-sweep-decoding-evaluation Use when benchmarking inference speed and accuracy trade-offs of an autoregressive structure-elucidation model against diffusion-based baselines on the same spectra test fold. Evaluating diffusion-based competitors themselves (e.g. DiffMS, FRIGID), which use diffusion sampling rather than beam-search multinomial decoding and cannot be swept over beam widths Comparing only accuracy without latency measurement — the speed-up claim requires recording wall-clock time per spectrum at a fixed beam width Datasets with restricted access such as NIST23, for which no evaluation data can be obtained http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sweeps beam-search multinomial sampling widths (10–100) during MS-Bart inference on MassSpecGym spectra to measure Top-1/Top-10 accuracy gains and per-spectrum wall-clock latency, demonstrating that latency scales linearly and MS-Bart (~3 s/spectrum at beam width 100) is roughly one order of magnitude (reported 53x) faster than diffusion-based competitors like DiffMS (~160 s). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615

skills.search_text: benchmark-identification-rate-comparison Use when reproducing a published metabolite-identification benchmark on CASMI 2016/2022 spectra, or when comparing a spectral-embedding predictor against SIRIUS or another baseline by ranking candidate structures per query spectrum. Do not use when the goal is a top-1 (rank-1) accuracy claim only — this skill measures top-5 correct-compound ranking, not top-ranked annotation rate. Do not compare rates computed against a differently sized reference database — the README states 'results obtained with a differently sized reference are not directly comparable', so avoid mixing reference sizes in one comparison. Do not apply --precursor_tolerance_ppm 0 for new work; that legacy 3-decimal bucket fails roughly half of compounds and is only for reproducing pre-v1.1.1 results. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Reproduce and compare top-5 correct-compound identification rates of ChemEmbed against SIRIUS 6.0.0 on the filtered CASMI 2022 benchmark, using polarity-specific pre-trained CNN weights and cosine similarity against the 520,083-compound Mol2vec reference database. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Reproduce and compare top-5 correct-compound identification rates of ChemEmbed against SIRIUS 6.0.0 on the filtered CASMI 2022 benchmark, using polarity-specific pre-trained CNN weights and cosine similarity against the 520,083-compound Mol2vec reference database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use when the goal is a top-1 (rank-1) accuracy claim only — this skill measures top-5 correct-compound ranking, not top-ranked annotation rate. Do not compare rates computed against a differently sized reference database — the README states 'results obtained with a differently sized reference are not directly comparable', so avoid mixing reference sizes in one comparison. Do not apply --precursor_tolerance_ppm 0 for new work; that legacy 3-decimal bucket fails roughly half of compounds and is only for reproducing pre-v1.1.1 results.

skills.description: Use when a new pathway-enrichment method must be evaluated against competing topology-based methods, and statistical power needs to be estimated per simulation condition (e.g., by number of dysregulated genes) with standard errors across replicates.
skills.name: benchmark-method-comparison-across-simulation-conditions
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-comparison-across-simulation-conditions Use when a new pathway-enrichment method must be evaluated against competing topology-based methods, and statistical power needs to be estimated per simulation condition (e.g., by number of dysregulated genes) with standard errors across replicates. When the goal is a single-method enrichment analysis on real (non-simulated) data rather than a comparative power benchmark across methods When competing methods require cutoff-based gene filtering and the comparison design depends on no-cutoff configurations that cannot be run When the input networks lack gene-gene interaction structure needed by topology-based (third-generation) methods http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A simulation-based benchmarking skill that compares the statistical power of topology-based pathway enrichment methods (NetGSA.REHE.Cl from the netgsa R package vs DEGraph, CAMERA, and Pathway-Express without cut-offs) across pathway groups stratified by number of dysregulated genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: A simulation-based benchmarking skill that compares the statistical power of topology-based pathway enrichment methods (NetGSA.REHE.Cl from the netgsa R package vs DEGraph, CAMERA, and Pathway-Express without cut-offs) across pathway groups stratified by number of dysregulated genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single-method enrichment analysis on real (non-simulated) data rather than a comparative power benchmark across methods When competing methods require cutoff-based gene filtering and the comparison design depends on no-cutoff configurations that cannot be run When the input networks lack gene-gene interaction structure needed by topology-based (third-generation) methods

skills.description: Use when comparing peak-detection or feature-detection performance of LC-MS processing tools against a ground-truth feature list (synthetic mzML with known single/double peaks) or manually labeled extracted-ion chromatograms, and accuracy metrics must be computed per category.
skills.name: benchmark-metric-computation
skills.search_text: benchmark-metric-computation Use when comparing peak-detection or feature-detection performance of LC-MS processing tools against a ground-truth feature list (synthetic mzML with known single/double peaks) or manually labeled extracted-ion chromatograms, and accuracy metrics must be computed per category. The goal is metabolite identification confidence scoring, not peak-detection accuracy benchmarking — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification. Input is already a processed, aligned feature table with no ground-truth reference; accuracy against truth cannot be computed without labels or a synthetic feature list. Comparing annotation of in-source fragments or isomer detection speed rather than chromatographic peak-shape classification, where different metrics apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute accuracy-style benchmark metrics (per-category accuracy, feature-table comparisons, significance tests) when evaluating LC-MS peak-detection software such as MassCube against MS-DIAL, MZmine3, and xcms on synthetic or manually labeled ground-truth data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Compute accuracy-style benchmark metrics (per-category accuracy, feature-table comparisons, significance tests) when evaluating LC-MS peak-detection software such as MassCube against MS-DIAL, MZmine3, and xcms on synthetic or manually labeled ground-truth data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is metabolite identification confidence scoring, not peak-detection accuracy benchmarking — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification. Input is already a processed, aligned feature table with no ground-truth reference; accuracy against truth cannot be computed without labels or a synthetic feature list. Comparing annotation of in-source fragments or isomer detection speed rather than chromatographic peak-shape classification, where different metrics apply.

skills.description: Use when a generative structure-elucidation model (e.g. MS-BART, DiffMS, FRIGID) has produced candidate molecules per spectrum and you must score them on MassSpecGym or NPLIB1 with Top-1/Top-10 InChIKey accuracy, MCES distance, and Tanimoto similarity.
skills.name: benchmark-metric-computation-tanimoto-mces
skills.search_text: benchmark-metric-computation-tanimoto-mces Use when a generative structure-elucidation model (e.g. MS-BART, DiffMS, FRIGID) has produced candidate molecules per spectrum and you must score them on MassSpecGym or NPLIB1 with Top-1/Top-10 InChIKey accuracy, MCES distance, and Tanimoto similarity. The dataset is NIST23 — access is restricted by commercial licensing, so the metric harness cannot be assembled without the test fold Evaluating fingerprint-prediction quality itself rather than generated molecular structures — use fingerprint bit-level metrics instead of InChIKey/MCES/Tanimoto scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Computes the standard structure-elucidation benchmark metrics — Top-1/Top-10 accuracy by full InChIKey exact match, minimum MCES distance, and maximum Tanimoto similarity (RDKit Morgan fingerprints, radius 2) — to evaluate de novo molecular candidate sets against MassSpecGym and NPLIB1 test folds. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Computes the standard structure-elucidation benchmark metrics — Top-1/Top-10 accuracy by full InChIKey exact match, minimum MCES distance, and maximum Tanimoto similarity (RDKit Morgan fingerprints, radius 2) — to evaluate de novo molecular candidate sets against MassSpecGym and NPLIB1 test folds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is NIST23 — access is restricted by commercial licensing, so the metric harness cannot be assembled without the test fold Evaluating fingerprint-prediction quality itself rather than generated molecular structures — use fingerprint bit-level metrics instead of InChIKey/MCES/Tanimoto scoring

skills.description: Use when several integration methods (e.g. SpatialMETA, Seurat CCA/RPCA, scVI, scANVI, scPoli, spaVAE, PCA) have been run on the same inputs and their embedding-level scores must be collected into one comparable metric table.
skills.name: benchmark-metric-table-compilation
skills.search_text: benchmark-metric-table-compilation Use when several integration methods (e.g. SpatialMETA, Seurat CCA/RPCA, scVI, scANVI, scPoli, spaVAE, PCA) have been run on the same inputs and their embedding-level scores must be collected into one comparable metric table. The task is single-sample embedding or visualization rather than cross-method comparison — no metric table across methods can be compiled from one method alone Ground-truth labels are absent, since the biology-conservation (marker) metric requires H&E-annotated labels passed via the scIB 'label key' parameter Data are single-cell or subcellular-resolution ST/SM; SpatialMETA and this benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assembles per-method benchmark metric values (continuity, marker/biology-conservation, and batch-correction scores from scIB-style evaluation) into a single CSV table, e.g. mirroring Supplementary Fig. 11 of the SpatialMETA paper, so horizontal-integration methods can be ranked side by side. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Assembles per-method benchmark metric values (continuity, marker/biology-conservation, and batch-correction scores from scIB-style evaluation) into a single CSV table, e.g. mirroring Supplementary Fig. 11 of the SpatialMETA paper, so horizontal-integration methods can be ranked side by side.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-sample embedding or visualization rather than cross-method comparison — no metric table across methods can be compiled from one method alone Ground-truth labels are absent, since the biology-conservation (marker) metric requires H&E-annotated labels passed via the scIB 'label key' parameter Data are single-cell or subcellular-resolution ST/SM; SpatialMETA and this benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only

skills.description: Use when a graph-based alignment method (G-Aligner) has been run alongside a baseline workflow (OpenMS/MZmine2/XCMS) on self-extracted features and you must quantify alignment gains in a reproducible metrics table.
skills.name: benchmark-metrics-table-generation
skills.search_text: benchmark-metrics-table-generation Use when a graph-based alignment method (G-Aligner) has been run alongside a baseline workflow (OpenMS/MZmine2/XCMS) on self-extracted features and you must quantify alignment gains in a reproducible metrics table. The features are manually annotated library-analyte features rather than software self-extracted untargeted features — the 2.4%/1.5%/1.7% and 13.5%/10.6%/18.4% gains apply specifically to the OpenMS self-extracted-feature comparison No manually annotated ground-truth feature dataset exists for the data, since F_ACC and A_ACC can only be computed against the deposited manual annotations The task is detection or quantification evaluation rather than feature alignment accuracy — although the same manual annotation dataset can serve those evaluations, the metrics table here is specific to alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generates a comparison metrics table quantifying how much G-Aligner improves feature alignment over a baseline tool's native method (e.g. OpenMS) on self-extracted untargeted features, using F_ACC (fraction of correctly aligned features) and A_ACC (fraction of correctly aligned analytes) computed against manually annotated feature datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Generates a comparison metrics table quantifying how much G-Aligner improves feature alignment over a baseline tool's native method (e.g. OpenMS) on self-extracted untargeted features, using F_ACC (fraction of correctly aligned features) and A_ACC (fraction of correctly aligned analytes) computed against manually annotated feature datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The features are manually annotated library-analyte features rather than software self-extracted untargeted features — the 2.4%/1.5%/1.7% and 13.5%/10.6%/18.4% gains apply specifically to the OpenMS self-extracted-feature comparison No manually annotated ground-truth feature dataset exists for the data, since F_ACC and A_ACC can only be computed against the deposited manual annotations The task is detection or quantification evaluation rather than feature alignment accuracy — although the same manual annotation dataset can serve those evaluations, the metrics table here is specific to alignment

skills.description: Use when a validated benchmark peak set must be derived from chromatographic ROIs of target molecules — i.e., after get_ROIs has produced an ROI data.table and peaks must be extracted, consistency-checked, and filtered before benchmark export.
skills.name: benchmark-peak-extraction-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: benchmark-peak-extraction-quality-filtering Use when a validated benchmark peak set must be derived from chromatographic ROIs of target molecules — i.e., after get_ROIs has produced an ROI data.table and peaks must be extracted, consistency-checked, and filtered before benchmark export. Input is already a finished benchmark (e.g. the reference Benchmark.csv from ucloud) — skip generation and go directly to reliability assessment of NPP output mzML files are profile-mode or not centroided — the benchmark requires centroided mzML input Target molecules lack known retention-time boundaries; user.rtmin/user.rtmax must be supplied (e.g. curated via Skyline) before peak extraction is meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 The find_bench_peaks stage of mzRAPP's benchmark cascade: extract chromatographic peaks with provided RT boundaries for all predicted isotopologues from ROI tables, then apply peak-shape correlation and isotopologue-ratio filters to yield a validated benchmark data.table. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab231
skills.summary: The find_bench_peaks stage of mzRAPP's benchmark cascade: extract chromatographic peaks with provided RT boundaries for all predicted isotopologues from ROI tables, then apply peak-shape correlation and isotopologue-ratio filters to yield a validated benchmark data.table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a finished benchmark (e.g. the reference Benchmark.csv from ucloud) — skip generation and go directly to reliability assessment of NPP output mzML files are profile-mode or not centroided — the benchmark requires centroided mzML input Target molecules lack known retention-time boundaries; user.rtmin/user.rtmax must be supplied (e.g. curated via Skyline) before peak extraction is meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have a validated benchmark (e.g. Benchmark.csv from MTBLS267) plus unaligned and aligned NPP output csv files and need to join them to quantify split peaks, missed peaks, degenerated isotopologue ratios, or alignment errors.
skills.name: benchmark-peak-matching
skills.search_text: benchmark-peak-matching Use when you have a validated benchmark (e.g. Benchmark.csv from MTBLS267) plus unaligned and aligned NPP output csv files and need to join them to quantify split peaks, missed peaks, degenerated isotopologue ratios, or alignment errors. You only have a raw feature table without a benchmark derived from user-supplied target molecules with known retention boundaries and molecular formulas — matching requires the validated benchmark as reference The NPP outputs come from an unvalidated source; run check_nonTargeted_input first and do not match malformed or schema-incompatible csv files Data are not centroided LC-HRMS mzML-derived outputs — benchmark generation and matching assume centroided profile data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Matches peaks and features from a generated benchmark dataset against non-targeted pre-processing (NPP) output tables from tools like XCMS or MZmine 2, providing the non-equivalent join required to compute peak-picking and alignment performance metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab231
skills.summary: Matches peaks and features from a generated benchmark dataset against non-targeted pre-processing (NPP) output tables from tools like XCMS or MZmine 2, providing the non-equivalent join required to compute peak-picking and alignment performance metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a raw feature table without a benchmark derived from user-supplied target molecules with known retention boundaries and molecular formulas — matching requires the validated benchmark as reference The NPP outputs come from an unvalidated source; run check_nonTargeted_input first and do not match malformed or schema-incompatible csv files Data are not centroided LC-HRMS mzML-derived outputs — benchmark generation and matching assume centroided profile data

skills.description: Use when validating a reaction-rules prediction engine against a curated set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions, to report coverage proportions and their statistical significance.
skills.name: benchmark-reaction-set-curation
skills.search_text: benchmark-reaction-set-curation Use when validating a reaction-rules prediction engine against a curated set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions, to report coverage proportions and their statistical significance. The analysis goal is de novo pathway reconstruction from paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data rather than benchmarking rule-set coverage against known reactions The rule set of interest is the loose RetroRules dataset, whose spurious reaction-Pfam links make it unsuitable for strict validation benchmarks The candidate reactions involve stereoisomeric conversions or multi-substrate steps, which MEANtools filters or cannot anticipate (mass spectrometric data does not capture stereoisomers; RetroRules rules are single-substrate) http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Curates and benchmarks a reference set of experimentally characterized biochemical reactions against MEANtools reaction-rule predictions derived from RetroRules, quantifying coverage and testing its statistical significance with a chi-square test. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Curates and benchmarks a reference set of experimentally characterized biochemical reactions against MEANtools reaction-rule predictions derived from RetroRules, quantifying coverage and testing its statistical significance with a chi-square test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is de novo pathway reconstruction from paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data rather than benchmarking rule-set coverage against known reactions The rule set of interest is the loose RetroRules dataset, whose spurious reaction-Pfam links make it unsuitable for strict validation benchmarks The candidate reactions involve stereoisomeric conversions or multi-substrate steps, which MEANtools filters or cannot anticipate (mass spectrometric data does not capture stereoisomers; RetroRules rules are single-substrate)

skills.description: Use when a published tool reports equivalence or ity against a reference method on a fixed benchmark and you need to verify whether that outcome survives systematic variation of an internal configuration choice (fingerprint type, kernel, scoring variant).
skills.name: benchmark-reanalysis-against-reference-method
skills.search_text: benchmark-reanalysis-against-reference-method Use when a published tool reports equivalence or ity against a reference method on a fixed benchmark and you need to verify whether that outcome survives systematic variation of an internal configuration choice (fingerprint type, kernel, scoring variant). The goal is to re-measure raw spectral similarity or re-derive the spectral network itself — this skill assumes the NIST benchmark, seed nodes, and MetFrag candidate lists are already assembled per the original publication. No in silico annotation or structure candidates are available for the benchmark spectra — random-walk propagation requires MetFrag-derived candidate structures plus spectral library match seeds; a spectra-only input cannot be re-analyzed this way. You only need to run ChemWalker's default pipeline once for annotation output rather than systematically testing a configuration axis against a reference method — use the basic ChemWalker workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Re-runs a published pipeline on its reference benchmark (e.g. the NIST 555-spectra benchmark in ChemWalker) while systematically varying one software configuration axis — such as the 27 RDKit molecular fingerprints — to test whether published results and comparisons (e.g. ChemWalker vs. NAP top-10 classification) hold beyond the default settings. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad078
skills.summary: Re-runs a published pipeline on its reference benchmark (e.g. the NIST 555-spectra benchmark in ChemWalker) while systematically varying one software configuration axis — such as the 27 RDKit molecular fingerprints — to test whether published results and comparisons (e.g. ChemWalker vs. NAP top-10 classification) hold beyond the default settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to re-measure raw spectral similarity or re-derive the spectral network itself — this skill assumes the NIST benchmark, seed nodes, and MetFrag candidate lists are already assembled per the original publication. No in silico annotation or structure candidates are available for the benchmark spectra — random-walk propagation requires MetFrag-derived candidate structures plus spectral library match seeds; a spectra-only input cannot be re-analyzed this way. You only need to run ChemWalker's default pipeline once for annotation output rather than systematically testing a configuration axis against a reference method — use the basic ChemWalker workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when a publicly available LC-MS/MS dataset with a published ground-truth feature list (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS736) must be used to benchmark a feature detection, quantification or marker selection pipeline.
skills.name: benchmark-reproduction-against-ground-truth-features
skills.search_text: benchmark-reproduction-against-ground-truth-features Use when a publicly available LC-MS/MS dataset with a published ground-truth feature list (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS736) must be used to benchmark a feature detection, quantification or marker selection pipeline. The input is already a processed feature table and no raw vendor/mzML files are available, so feature detection cannot be re-run against ground truth No published ground-truth feature list or expected marker set exists for the dataset, so detection/quantification/marker performance cannot be scored A new instrument dataset without known secondary metabolites is being explored de novo rather than benchmarking the workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Run an untargeted metabolomics workflow (UmetaFlow) on a public benchmark dataset such as MTBLS736 or MTBLS733 and score feature detection, quantification, and discriminating marker selection against published ground-truth feature lists. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: Run an untargeted metabolomics workflow (UmetaFlow) on a public benchmark dataset such as MTBLS736 or MTBLS733 and score feature detection, quantification, and discriminating marker selection against published ground-truth feature lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table and no raw vendor/mzML files are available, so feature detection cannot be re-run against ground truth No published ground-truth feature list or expected marker set exists for the dataset, so detection/quantification/marker performance cannot be scored A new instrument dataset without known secondary metabolites is being explored de novo rather than benchmarking the workflow

skills.description: Use when a paper reports a concrete quantitative result (peak detection rate, annotation count, threshold behavior) and you must rerun the pipeline with the stated parameters to confirm or compare against those values.
skills.name: benchmark-reproduction-against-published-values
skills.search_text: benchmark-reproduction-against-published-values Use when a paper reports a concrete quantitative result (peak detection rate, annotation count, threshold behavior) and you must rerun the pipeline with the stated parameters to confirm or compare against those values. Your goal is novel discovery rather than validation of a published result — the skill is anchored to reproducing reported numbers, not exploring new datasets. Your data is 1D GC–MS or LC–MS: GcDUO's readFolderCDF and procesData assume 2D chromatography with a defined modulation time. You lack the paper's stated parameters (thresholds, m/z range, modulation time); re-deriving them is a different task than benchmark reproduction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reproduce a published computational result end-to-end (here, GcDUO annotating 85% of the 27 fruitybeer GC×GC–MS peaks) by following the paper's exact parameters and validating outputs against the reported numbers. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbaf080
skills.summary: Reproduce a published computational result end-to-end (here, GcDUO annotating 85% of the 27 fruitybeer GC×GC–MS peaks) by following the paper's exact parameters and validating outputs against the reported numbers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is novel discovery rather than validation of a published result — the skill is anchored to reproducing reported numbers, not exploring new datasets. Your data is 1D GC–MS or LC–MS: GcDUO's readFolderCDF and procesData assume 2D chromatography with a defined modulation time. You lack the paper's stated parameters (thresholds, m/z range, modulation time); re-deriving them is a different task than benchmark reproduction.

skills.description: Use when an article reports headline accuracy metrics (e.g., AvRE) for a method on named experiments and the deposited spectra/data are available, and the task is to reproduce those numbers and compare against reported baselines.
skills.name: benchmark-reproduction-against-reported-metrics
skills.search_text: benchmark-reproduction-against-reported-metrics Use when an article reports headline accuracy metrics (e.g., AvRE) for a method on named experiments and the deposited spectra/data are available, and the task is to reproduce those numbers and compare against reported baselines. The task asks to reproduce qualitative claims or plots rather than the paper's quantitative error metrics — instead consider extracting findings directly. The data deposit does not contain the input spectra or library files needed to rerun the tool, so metrics cannot be recomputed from source data. The metric depends on configuration the paper does not document (e.g., unstated κmixture/κcomponents values), making exact reproduction unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Reproduce an article's reported quantitative benchmarks by re-running the authors' method on the deposited experimental data and recomputing their error metrics, as demonstrated by recovering Magnetstein's per-experiment AvRE values (0.0%, 3.0%, 9.0%, 3.6%, 3.6%) for Experiments 1–5 and tabulating them against MANIQ and ACD/TP baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03594
skills.summary: Reproduce an article's reported quantitative benchmarks by re-running the authors' method on the deposited experimental data and recomputing their error metrics, as demonstrated by recovering Magnetstein's per-experiment AvRE values (0.0%, 3.0%, 9.0%, 3.6%, 3.6%) for Experiments 1–5 and tabulating them against MANIQ and ACD/TP baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task asks to reproduce qualitative claims or plots rather than the paper's quantitative error metrics — instead consider extracting findings directly. The data deposit does not contain the input spectra or library files needed to rerun the tool, so metrics cannot be recomputed from source data. The metric depends on configuration the paper does not document (e.g., unstated κmixture/κcomponents values), making exact reproduction unreliable.

skills.description: Use when a paper or task card reports a concrete quantitative result (feature counts, match rates, tolerance thresholds) that must be re-derived from the deposited datasets and workflow scripts to verify it reproduces.
skills.name: benchmark-result-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-result-reproduction Use when a paper or task card reports a concrete quantitative result (feature counts, match rates, tolerance thresholds) that must be re-derived from the deposited datasets and workflow scripts to verify it reproduces. The input is a single dataset or raw .raw/.mzML files rather than two or more independently processed feature tables — use Gravity for redundant-feature clustering or Chroma for file reading instead Datasets were acquired on different LC-MS methods — Eclipse aligns 'same-method nontargeted LCMS datasets' The goal is drift correction or QC rather than cross-dataset alignment validation — use Blueshift or Formation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reproduces a published benchmark result end-to-end (here: Eclipse's default strict clique-mode alignment of four human plasma LC-MS datasets, DS1–DS4) and validates the output against the paper's reported numbers (3861 combined features; 362/381 = 95% correctly matched overlapping annotations; 3 spurious annotation mismatches). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: Reproduces a published benchmark result end-to-end (here: Eclipse's default strict clique-mode alignment of four human plasma LC-MS datasets, DS1–DS4) and validates the output against the paper's reported numbers (3861 combined features; 362/381 = 95% correctly matched overlapping annotations; 3 spurious annotation mismatches).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single dataset or raw .raw/.mzML files rather than two or more independently processed feature tables — use Gravity for redundant-feature clustering or Chroma for file reading instead Datasets were acquired on different LC-MS methods — Eclipse aligns 'same-method nontargeted LCMS datasets' The goal is drift correction or QC rather than cross-dataset alignment validation — use Blueshift or Formation instead

skills.description: Use when reproducing published molecular-formula or structure-identification benchmark results from LC-MS/MS challenge data using SIRIUS 4 with CSI:FingerID and isotope-pattern scoring.
skills.name: benchmark-result-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-result-reproduction Use when reproducing published molecular-formula or structure-identification benchmark results from LC-MS/MS challenge data using SIRIUS 4 with CSI:FingerID and isotope-pattern scoring. The goal is de novo formula/structure identification on new samples rather than reproducing a published benchmark's identification rates. The data are not LC-MS/MS challenge spectra with known reference formulas/structures, so top-k identification rates cannot be defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces published benchmark results of SIRIUS 4 / CSI:FingerID by re-running formula and structure identification on a challenge dataset (e.g. CASMI 2016) and recomputing top-k identification rates. Validates that the SIRIUS 4 pipeline reproduces the reported rates, such as 93.8% correct molecular formulas at top 1. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8
skills.summary: Reproduces published benchmark results of SIRIUS 4 / CSI:FingerID by re-running formula and structure identification on a challenge dataset (e.g. CASMI 2016) and recomputing top-k identification rates. Validates that the SIRIUS 4 pipeline reproduces the reported rates, such as 93.8% correct molecular formulas at top 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo formula/structure identification on new samples rather than reproducing a published benchmark's identification rates. The data are not LC-MS/MS challenge spectra with known reference formulas/structures, so top-k identification rates cannot be defined.

skills.description: Use when a published software benchmark reports per-dataset success/failure counts or percentages (e.g., '38/41 correct outputs, 92.7%') and the goal is to verify them by re-executing the pipeline on the same study IDs.
skills.name: benchmark-result-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-result-reproduction Use when a published software benchmark reports per-dataset success/failure counts or percentages (e.g., '38/41 correct outputs, 92.7%') and the goal is to verify them by re-executing the pipeline on the same study IDs. The goal is scientific re-analysis of the metabolomics data (e.g., classification), not verification of the conversion pipeline — re-analysis is infeasible when class metadata is unavailable in the repositories. The task is to extend or add data-processing algorithms to the tool — CloMet deliberately leaves processing out of scope. The input is the user's own private/local data routed via the LOCAL tab, which is outside the public-repository benchmark scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Reproduces a paper's end-to-end success-rate benchmarks by re-running the tool's pipeline (here, CloMet's LoadDataset) on the same cohort of public repository studies and comparing aggregate correct-output counts against published figures (e.g., Figures 8B/8C of the CloMet paper). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00602
skills.summary: Reproduces a paper's end-to-end success-rate benchmarks by re-running the tool's pipeline (here, CloMet's LoadDataset) on the same cohort of public repository studies and comparing aggregate correct-output counts against published figures (e.g., Figures 8B/8C of the CloMet paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scientific re-analysis of the metabolomics data (e.g., classification), not verification of the conversion pipeline — re-analysis is infeasible when class metadata is unavailable in the repositories. skills.summary: Applies Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction to nominal p-values produced when BiomiX correlates MOFA factors with clinical metadata (Pearson for numeric features, Wilcoxon for binary features), so discriminant factors can be ranked by clinical association without inflating type-I error across many factor-feature tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No multiple testing is involved — a single factor-feature hypothesis test needs no BH correction The goal is single-omics differential analysis (e.g. metabolomics peak differences use Wilcoxon with FDR in a separate BiomiX module) rather than MOFA factor interpretation MOFA factors are already annotated by the PubMed bibliography-mining or pathway (EnrichR/GSEA) interpretation routes and no clinical correlation table is requested

skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when a differential analysis of grouped NMR peak features produces thousands of per-feature p-values and you need FDR-controlled significance calls comparable across frameworks such as speaq 2.0 and MetaboAnalyst. skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to per-feature p-values from differential NMR peak analyses (e.g. speaq 2.0's 677-feature matrix vs MetaboAnalyst's 245-feature matrix on the onion intake in mice data) so highly significant features can be flagged and cross-mapped without inflating false discoveries across the thousands of grouped peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a table of FDR-adjusted p-values from MetaboAnalyst — re-correcting would be inappropriate The analysis involves a single pre-specified hypothesis rather than a family of hundreds of grouped-peak tests, where no multiplicity correction is needed The spectra are still raw and unbinned; BH correction presupposes the peak-picking and grouping steps (avoiding binning) have already produced the feature matrix

skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to raw p-values from pairwise non-parametric tests so that metabolite-feature-level comparisons (e.g. bile-amidate abundances in IBD vs non-IBD) can be called significant at a controlled q-value threshold rather than at unadjusted alpha.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single hypothesis test is being run (no multiplicity, so no correction is needed) Input p-values are already adjusted q-values from a previous correction step — re-correcting would over-shrink significance The goal is hypothesis-wide family-wise error control (e.g. Bonferroni-style) rather than FDR control over feature-level metabolomics tests

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS metabolomics experiment includes replicate runs (or pooled QC replicates) and you need to score how well a normalization method (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) reduced between-replicate technical dispersion.

skills.search_text: between-replicate-dispersion-quantification Use when an LC-MS metabolomics experiment includes replicate runs (or pooled QC replicates) and you need to score how well a normalization method (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) reduced between-replicate technical dispersion. skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to mine or store candidate BGCs regardless of known function — IMG-ABC or antiSMASH-DB store many thousands of candidate BGCs, whereas MIBiG is restricted to BGCs of known function Query BGCs are already curated entries in MIBiG, since self-hits trivially inflate homology and deflate novelty fractions You need experimentally verified product structures with chemical cross-links only — MIBiG is a BGC-sequence reference and does not replace spectral/chemical databases such as GNPS or the Natural Products Atlas

skills.name: bgc-query-to-subcluster-motif-matching
skills.search_text: bgc-query-to-subcluster-motif-matching Use when tokenised (sub)Pfam-domain BGCs must be matched against pre-trained LDA sub-cluster motifs to predict biosynthetic sub-clusters, or to validate predicted sub-clusters against known SubClusterBlast entries. When gene order matters for the hypothesis being tested — the LDA branch assumes a bag-of-words model where original gene order is not considered; use the PRESTO-STAT co-occurrence approach instead, which uses tokens in their original order When no trained motif model exists and de novo sub-cluster discovery is the goal — this skill queries existing motifs, it does not train them When sub-clusters consist of a single gene — such matches are treated as noise and are not counted http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Query tokenised biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) against a trained PRESTO-TOP LDA sub-cluster motif model to predict which biosynthetic sub-clusters (e.g. methoxymalonate, AHBA) are present, enabling substructure-level annotation of BGCs. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Query tokenised biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) against a trained PRESTO-TOP LDA sub-cluster motif model to predict which biosynthetic sub-clusters (e.g. methoxymalonate, AHBA) are present, enabling substructure-level annotation of BGCs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene order matters for the hypothesis being tested — the LDA branch assumes a bag-of-words model where original gene order is not considered; use the PRESTO-STAT co-occurrence approach instead, which uses tokens in their original order When no trained motif model exists and de novo sub-cluster discovery is the goal — this skill queries existing motifs, it does not train them When sub-clusters consist of a single gene — such matches are treated as noise and are not counted

skills.description: Use when a large tokenised BGC set (e.g. antiSMASH output with per-gene (sub)Pfam tokens) must be de-duplicated before motif/sub-cluster mining, and near-identical clusters (Adjacency Index > 0.95 or full containment) should be collapsed.
skills.name: bgc-redundancy-network-filtering
skills.search_text: bgc-redundancy-network-filtering Use when a large tokenised BGC set (e.g. antiSMASH output with per-gene (sub)Pfam tokens) must be de-duplicated before motif/sub-cluster mining, and near-identical clusters (Adjacency Index > 0.95 or full containment) should be collapsed. The input BGCs are not yet tokenised into (sub)Pfam domains — tokenisation and non-biosynthetic Pfam removal must precede network construction The goal is novelty-oriented comparison against MIBiG rather than de-replication of a mining corpus, since removing near-identical BGCs discards redundant but potentially informative members BGCs flagged by antiSMASH as lying on a contig-edge are present, as their truncated domain content would distort Adjacency Index and containment edges Dereplicates a tokenised biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) dataset by building a BGC similarity network and pruning maximal cliques, keeping only the most domain-rich BGC per clique. Applied in iPRESTO to reduce antiSMASH-DB v2 (152,122 BGCs) to 60,028 non-redundant BGCs. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Dereplicates a tokenised biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) dataset by building a BGC similarity network and pruning maximal cliques, keeping only the most domain-rich BGC per clique. Applied in iPRESTO to reduce antiSMASH-DB v2 (152,122 BGCs) to 60,028 non-redundant BGCs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BGCs are not yet tokenised into (sub)Pfam domains — tokenisation and non-biosynthetic Pfam removal must precede network construction The goal is novelty-oriented comparison against MIBiG rather than de-replication of a mining corpus, since removing near-identical BGCs discards redundant but potentially informative members BGCs flagged by antiSMASH as lying on a contig-edge are present, as their truncated domain content would distort Adjacency Index and containment edges

skills.description: Use when per-domain BGC detector scores (DeepBGC BiLSTM or ClusterFinder HMM) must be thresholded at a calibrated operating point (10% FPR or 80% TPR) and collapsed into discrete BGC regions for genome-scale precision evaluation.
skills.name: bgc-region-post-processing
skills.search_text: bgc-region-post-processing Use when per-domain BGC detector scores (DeepBGC BiLSTM or ClusterFinder HMM) must be thresholded at a calibrated operating point (10% FPR or 80% TPR) and collapsed into discrete BGC regions for genome-scale precision evaluation. You only need raw per-domain scores for training or feature extraction — region post-processing discards per-domain score detail You are comparing against antiSMASH's rule-based BGC boundaries, whose region definition is not produced by threshold-and-merge post-processing of domain scores The detector has already emitted final BGC regions (e.g. deepbgc pipeline's own region output) and you are not evaluating the merging step itself Post-processing skill from the DeepBGC paper: thresholded per-domain Pfam scores are converted into discrete BGC regions, with an optional region-merging step whose effect on BGC-level precision is explicitly benchmarked against ClusterFinder on nine manually annotated bacterial genomes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz654
skills.summary: Post-processing skill from the DeepBGC paper: thresholded per-domain Pfam scores are converted into discrete BGC regions, with an optional region-merging step whose effect on BGC-level precision is explicitly benchmarked against ClusterFinder on nine manually annotated bacterial genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need raw per-domain scores for training or feature extraction — region post-processing discards per-domain score detail You are comparing against antiSMASH's rule-based BGC boundaries, whose region definition is not produced by threshold-and-merge post-processing of domain scores The detector has already emitted final BGC regions (e.g. deepbgc pipeline's own region output) and you are not evaluating the merging step itself

skills.description: Use when you need aggregate counts of curated BGCs — totals, per-class (e.g. Polyketide 825, NRP 627) or per-taxon (e.g. Streptomyces 568) breakdowns — from MIBiG or a similar curated BGC repository.
skills.name: bgc-repository-statistics-extraction
skills.search_text: bgc-repository-statistics-extraction Use when you need aggregate counts of curated BGCs — totals, per-class (e.g. Polyketide 825, NRP 627) or per-taxon (e.g. Streptomyces 568) breakdowns — from MIBiG or a similar curated BGC repository. When you need individual BGC entry records or sequences rather than aggregate statistics — use the repository's per-entry pages or the REST-like API instead When counting candidate (uncurated) BGCs predicted by tools like antiSMASH or ClusterFinder — MIBiG statistics cover only manually curated BGCs of known function When you need programmatically queryable bulk data rather than summary counts — use the mibig-api GitHub endpoint or JSON-formatted data standard http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Extracts and tabulates curated-entry counts, biosynthetic class distributions, and taxonomic distributions from the MIBiG repository's statistics page (version 2.0: 2021 BGCs), cross-checking them against the published article figures. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz882
skills.summary: Extracts and tabulates curated-entry counts, biosynthetic class distributions, and taxonomic distributions from the MIBiG repository's statistics page (version 2.0: 2021 BGCs), cross-checking them against the published article figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need individual BGC entry records or sequences rather than aggregate statistics — use the repository's per-entry pages or the REST-like API instead When counting candidate (uncurated) BGCs predicted by tools like antiSMASH or ClusterFinder — MIBiG statistics cover only manually curated BGCs of known function When you need programmatically queryable bulk data rather than summary counts — use the mibig-api GitHub endpoint or JSON-formatted data standard

skills.description: Use when building the labeled BGC training matrix for NPOmix from antiSMASH .gbk files and BiG-SCAPE pairwise similarity outputs, prior to KNN classification of MS/MS fingerprints.
skills.name: bgc-similarity-fingerprint-construction
skills.search_text: bgc-similarity-fingerprint-construction Use when building the labeled BGC training matrix for NPOmix from antiSMASH .gbk files and BiG-SCAPE pairwise similarity outputs, prior to KNN classification of MS/MS fingerprints. The input query genome/fungal species has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset — the output would contain no answer The metagenome quality is too low for BGC assembly, yielding fragmented BGCs and an uninformative fingerprint You already possess an MS/MS fingerprint testing matrix and only need classification, not BGC feature construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Construction of BGC similarity fingerprints for the NPOmix KNN classifier: each query BGC is represented as a vector of maximum BiG-SCAPE-derived similarity scores (1 − raw distance) against the pooled BGCs of every genome/metagenome, binarized at the 0.7 similarity cutoff, and labeled with a GCF for training. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Construction of BGC similarity fingerprints for the NPOmix KNN classifier: each query BGC is represented as a vector of maximum BiG-SCAPE-derived similarity scores (1 − raw distance) against the pooled BGCs of every genome/metagenome, binarized at the 0.7 similarity cutoff, and labeled with a GCF for training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input query genome/fungal species has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset — the output would contain no answer The metagenome quality is too low for BGC assembly, yielding fragmented BGCs and an uninformative fingerprint You already possess an MS/MS fingerprint testing matrix and only need classification, not BGC feature construction

skills.description: Use when quantifying how many candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links each GCF retains under co-occurrence-only scoring versus chemical-class filtering, e.g. to reproduce or assess manageable candidate-link histograms.
skills.name: bgc-spectral-candidate-link-counting
skills.search_text: bgc-spectral-candidate-link-counting Use when quantifying how many candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links each GCF retains under co-occurrence-only scoring versus chemical-class filtering, e.g. to reproduce or assess manageable candidate-link histograms. When the goal is to prioritise or validate individual links rather than summarise per-GCF candidate-link burden (the ranked-position validation workflow is the appropriate skill instead) When MS/MS spectra lack CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer structure-based class predictions and you intend to keep those links — NPClassScore filtering discards candidate links without structure-based classes When dataset-specific score calibration is needed, e.g. the Nocardia dataset where the standardised Metcalf threshold had to be lowered from 2.5 to 2 to retain validated links http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Counts the number of candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links per gene cluster family (GCF) in NPLinker, before and after NPClassScore chemical-class filtering, to quantify how class matching prunes candidate lists (e.g. from 42 to 270 GCFs with ≤25 links in the Streptomyces/Salinispora dataset). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Counts the number of candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links per gene cluster family (GCF) in NPLinker, before and after NPClassScore chemical-class filtering, to quantify how class matching prunes candidate lists (e.g. from 42 to 270 GCFs with ≤25 links in the Streptomyces/Salinispora dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to prioritise or validate individual links rather than summarise per-GCF candidate-link burden (the ranked-position validation workflow is the appropriate skill instead) When MS/MS spectra lack CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer structure-based class predictions and you intend to keep those links — NPClassScore filtering discards candidate links without structure-based classes When dataset-specific score calibration is needed, e.g. the Nocardia dataset where the standardised Metcalf threshold had to be lowered from 2.5 to 2 to retain validated links

skills.description: Use when paired genomic-metabolomic data (AntiSMASH BGCs, GNPS molecular networking spectra, strain mappings) must be linked and candidate links prioritised by rank, e.g. to reproduce Table 3-style top-n performance comparisons.
skills.name: bgc-spectrum-link-ranking
skills.search_text: bgc-spectrum-link-ranking Use when paired genomic-metabolomic data (AntiSMASH BGCs, GNPS molecular networking spectra, strain mappings) must be linked and candidate links prioritised by rank, e.g. to reproduce Table 3-style top-n performance comparisons. Input omics data lack the strain mapping file (strain_mapping.json) required to associate genomic and metabolomic datasets, so links cannot be validated against known strains The goal is raw GNPS molecular networking or de novo spectrum clustering rather than ranking candidate BGC links No candidate structure set (e.g. MIBiG-associated structures) is available, so top-n ranking against candidates is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ranks candidate BGC (gene cluster) structures against each metabolite's spectrum using scoring functions such as the standardised Metcalf score and Input-Output Kernel Regression (IOKR), then evaluates top-n hit rates and AUC against a randomised-link baseline within the NPLinker framework. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Ranks candidate BGC (gene cluster) structures against each metabolite's spectrum using scoring functions such as the standardised Metcalf score and Input-Output Kernel Regression (IOKR), then evaluates top-n hit rates and AUC against a randomised-link baseline within the NPLinker framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input omics data lack the strain mapping file (strain_mapping.json) required to associate genomic and metabolomic datasets, so links cannot be validated against known strains The goal is raw GNPS molecular networking or de novo spectrum clustering rather than ranking candidate BGC links No candidate structure set (e.g. MIBiG-associated structures) is available, so top-n ranking against candidates is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when building an evaluation set of known BGC–metabolite–MS2 spectrum links: MIBiG records contain no MS2 data and GNPS spectra lack BGC provenance, so pairing must be done through shared compound structural identifiers.
skills.name: bgc-spectrum-pairing
skills.search_text: bgc-spectrum-pairing Use when building an evaluation set of known BGC–metabolite–MS2 spectrum links: MIBiG records contain no MS2 data and GNPS spectra lack BGC provenance, so pairing must be done through shared compound structural identifiers. Input is raw metabolomics (mzML/mzXML) or GNPS molecular networking output rather than GNPS library spectrum annotations — this skill links library entries to BGCs, it does not score links in new datasets. Compounds lacking InChIKeys or with only partially specified structures, since the join depends entirely on first-block InChIKey equality. Cases where stereochemistry of the metabolite matters for the analysis — the first-block truncation deliberately discards chirality information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Constructs a gold-standard set of known BGC–spectrum pairs by joining MIBiG 2.0 biosynthetic gene cluster metadata with GNPS library spectra via first-block InChIKey matching, producing the 2966 validated pairs used to evaluate link-scoring in NPLinker. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Constructs a gold-standard set of known BGC–spectrum pairs by joining MIBiG 2.0 biosynthetic gene cluster metadata with GNPS library spectra via first-block InChIKey matching, producing the 2966 validated pairs used to evaluate link-scoring in NPLinker.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metabolomics (mzML/mzXML) or GNPS molecular networking output rather than GNPS library spectrum annotations — this skill links library entries to BGCs, it does not score links in new datasets. Compounds lacking InChIKeys or with only partially specified structures, since the join depends entirely on first-block InChIKey equality. Cases where stereochemistry of the metabolite matters for the analysis — the first-block truncation deliberately discards chirality information.

skills.description: Use when a trained PRESTO-TOP model with latent sub-cluster motifs exists and the goal is to assign substructure-level annotations (e.g. aminoglycoside, moenomycin motifs) by matching motif instances to validated sub-clusters in MIBiG and antiSMASH SubClusterBlast data.
skills.name: bgc-subcluster-motif-annotation
skills.search_text: bgc-subcluster-motif-annotation Use when a trained PRESTO-TOP model with latent sub-cluster motifs exists and the goal is to assign substructure-level annotations (e.g. aminoglycoside, moenomycin motifs) by matching motif instances to validated sub-clusters in MIBiG and antiSMASH SubClusterBlast data. When the goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery rather than annotation of an existing trained PRESTO-TOP motif library When BGCs have not been tokenised into (sub)Pfam words — PRESTO-TOP requires tokenised gene/Pfam representations, not raw nucleotide or protein sequences When no experimentally characterised sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast or MIBiG) are available to ground the motif annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Annotate PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster motifs with the substructures they encode by matching predicted sub-clusters against experimentally characterised sub-clusters from SubClusterBlast and sub-cluster instances in MIBiG BGCs, yielding a reusable motif-to-substructure library. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Annotate PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster motifs with the substructures they encode by matching predicted sub-clusters against experimentally characterised sub-clusters from SubClusterBlast and sub-cluster instances in MIBiG BGCs, yielding a reusable motif-to-substructure library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery rather than annotation of an existing trained PRESTO-TOP motif library When BGCs have not been tokenised into (sub)Pfam words — PRESTO-TOP requires tokenised gene/Pfam representations, not raw nucleotide or protein sequences When no experimentally characterised sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast or MIBiG) are available to ground the motif annotations

skills.description: Use when univariate association tests (e.g. partial Spearman correlations) have been run for every metabolic feature against a clinical phenotype and a multiple-testing-corrected pFDR column is needed before calling associations.
skills.name: bh-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: bh-multiple-testing-correction Use when univariate association tests (e.g. partial Spearman correlations) have been run for every metabolic feature against a clinical phenotype and a multiple-testing-corrected pFDR column is needed before calling associations. Multivariate models (e.g. PCA/PLS-based screening) are being used where confounders like age and gender cannot be partialled out per-feature — MWASTools' univariate + confounder-adjusted pipeline is the intended route The association model is not univariate hypothesis testing on metabolic features (BH correction in this pipeline assumes per-feature p-values from MWAS_stats) A different multiple-testing family is required (the skill is specific to BH-adjusted pFDR via mt_method='BH') http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate correction to raw p-values from a metabolome-wide association study (MWAS), so that per-metabolite associations with a phenotype (e.g. BMI) survive testing across thousands of metabolic features. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate correction to raw p-values from a metabolome-wide association study (MWAS), so that per-metabolite associations with a phenotype (e.g. BMI) survive testing across thousands of metabolic features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Multivariate models (e.g. PCA/PLS-based screening) are being used where confounders like age and gender cannot be partialled out per-feature — MWASTools' univariate + confounder-adjusted pipeline is the intended route The association model is not univariate hypothesis testing on metabolic features (BH correction in this pipeline assumes per-feature p-values from MWAS_stats) A different multiple-testing family is required (the skill is specific to BH-adjusted pFDR via mt_method='BH')

skills.description: Use when building GGM partial-correlation metabolite networks with DNEA on two-condition metabolomics data and the lambda penalty for glasso regularization must be set — either via BIC tuning (~500+ samples per group) or via the small-sample approximation.
skills.name: bic-lambda-hyperparameter-tuning
skills.search_text: bic-lambda-hyperparameter-tuning Use when building GGM partial-correlation metabolite networks with DNEA on two-condition metabolomics data and the lambda penalty for glasso regularization must be set — either via BIC tuning (~500+ samples per group) or via the small-sample approximation. When either experimental group has fewer than ~500 samples — the article recommends the lambda approximation (Eq. 3) instead of BIC tuning, since BIC tuning requires a large dataset and the approximation reduces false positive unstable edges When the input is not a two-condition, approximately normal feature-intensity matrix (e.g. single-group data, where CorrelationCalculator rather than DNEA is appropriate) http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Tunes the GLASSO regularization parameter (lambda) for DNEA joint network estimation by BIC optimization per experimental condition, using the BICtune() function with a BiocParallel backend, or falls back to the lambda approximation sqrt(ln(features)/samples) when datasets are too small for reliable BIC tuning. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Tunes the GLASSO regularization parameter (lambda) for DNEA joint network estimation by BIC optimization per experimental condition, using the BICtune() function with a BiocParallel backend, or falls back to the lambda approximation sqrt(ln(features)/samples) when datasets are too small for reliable BIC tuning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When either experimental group has fewer than ~500 samples — the article recommends the lambda approximation (Eq. 3) instead of BIC tuning, since BIC tuning requires a large dataset and the approximation reduces false positive unstable edges When the input is not a two-condition, approximately normal feature-intensity matrix (e.g. single-group data, where CorrelationCalculator rather than DNEA is appropriate)

skills.description: Use when combining pairwise subalignment match tables from two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS datasets into a feature graph, and only mutually supported (bidirectional) matches should become edges before clustering into feature groups.
skills.name: bidirectional-edge-filtering
skills.search_text: bidirectional-edge-filtering Use when combining pairwise subalignment match tables from two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS datasets into a feature graph, and only mutually supported (bidirectional) matches should become edges before clustering into feature groups. The input is a single dataset rather than two or more independently processed datasets that must be aligned (Eclipse's scope is aligning multiple same-method datasets) Only one-directional pairwise match evidence exists — these edges will be discarded, so the skill would eliminate rather than reconcile the matches The task is redundancy clustering of features within a single dataset by RT and correlation — that is Gravity's role, not Eclipse graph alignment A graph-construction step in the Eclipse LC-MS alignment workflow where all pairwise subalignment match tables are loaded into a directed graph (features as nodes, matches as edges, match penalties as edge weights), and only edges supported by matches in both directions between datasets are retained, with penalties from both directions summed. This handles complex matching scenarios arising when n > 2 datasets are aligned. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: A graph-construction step in the Eclipse LC-MS alignment workflow where all pairwise subalignment match tables are loaded into a directed graph (features as nodes, matches as edges, match penalties as edge weights), and only edges supported by matches in both directions between datasets are retained, with penalties from both directions summed. This handles complex matching scenarios arising when n > 2 datasets are aligned.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single dataset rather than two or more independently processed datasets that must be aligned (Eclipse's scope is aligning multiple same-method datasets) Only one-directional pairwise match evidence exists — these edges will be discarded, so the skill would eliminate rather than reconcile the matches The task is redundancy clustering of features within a single dataset by RT and correlation — that is Gravity's role, not Eclipse graph alignment

skills.description: Use when you have antiSMASH .gbk BGCs from paired genome–metabolome samples and need BGC fingerprint rows (with GCF labels) to train the NPOmix KNN classifier or to query against its space.
skills.name: bigscape-bgc-similarity-fingerprinting
skills.search_text: bigscape-bgc-similarity-fingerprinting Use when you have antiSMASH .gbk BGCs from paired genome–metabolome samples and need BGC fingerprint rows (with GCF labels) to train the NPOmix KNN classifier or to query against its space. The query organism (e.g., a fungal species) has no BGCs similar to any BGC in the NPOmix PoDP training set — similarity-only features will produce no answer BGCs come from low-quality metagenomes where assembly hinders BGC recovery, leaving fragmented or missing BGCs that distort similarity fingerprints The goal is MS/MS spectral fingerprinting (GNPS modified cosine scores against experimental samples), which is the analogous test-side procedure, not the BGC-side fingerprinting http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Builds BGC similarity fingerprint matrices for NPOmix by running BiG-SCAPE pairwise comparisons over antiSMASH-derived .gbk BGCs and converting raw distances to per-genome maximum similarity vectors (similarity = 1 − raw distance, cutoff 0.7). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Builds BGC similarity fingerprint matrices for NPOmix by running BiG-SCAPE pairwise comparisons over antiSMASH-derived .gbk BGCs and converting raw distances to per-genome maximum similarity vectors (similarity = 1 − raw distance, cutoff 0.7).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query organism (e.g., a fungal species) has no BGCs similar to any BGC in the NPOmix PoDP training set — similarity-only features will produce no answer BGCs come from low-quality metagenomes where assembly hinders BGC recovery, leaving fragmented or missing BGCs that distort similarity fingerprints The goal is MS/MS spectral fingerprinting (GNPS modified cosine scores against experimental samples), which is the analogous test-side procedure, not the BGC-side fingerprinting

skills.description: Use when a set of antiSMASH GenBank BGCs (training set plus query genomes) must be converted into pairwise similarity scores and GCF assignments feeding an NPOmix BGC fingerprint matrix.
skills.name: bigscape-network-concatenation
skills.search_text: bigscape-network-concatenation Use when a set of antiSMASH GenBank BGCs (training set plus query genomes) must be converted into pairwise similarity scores and GCF assignments feeding an NPOmix BGC fingerprint matrix. You need MS/MS-to-MS/MS similarities (GNPS modified cosine scores), not BGC-to-BGC comparisons — that fingerprinting step is separate in NPOmix. Query BGCs have no homolog in the NPOmix training set (e.g. fungal BGCs dissimilar to the PoDP-derived bacterial training data); the downstream output would contain no answer. You only need antiSMASH annotation/prediction without cross-genome BGC similarity networking. http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Run BiG-SCAPE pairwise BGC similarity comparisons on antiSMASH-predicted BGCs (plus MIBiG and singletons) and concatenate the per-class output networks (e.g. hybrids_glocal) into the unified similarity network that NPOmix uses to build BGC fingerprints. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Run BiG-SCAPE pairwise BGC similarity comparisons on antiSMASH-predicted BGCs (plus MIBiG and singletons) and concatenate the per-class output networks (e.g. hybrids_glocal) into the unified similarity network that NPOmix uses to build BGC fingerprints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need MS/MS-to-MS/MS similarities (GNPS modified cosine scores), not BGC-to-BGC comparisons — that fingerprinting step is separate in NPOmix. Query BGCs have no homolog in the NPOmix training set (e.g. fungal BGCs dissimilar to the PoDP-derived bacterial training data); the downstream output would contain no answer. You only need antiSMASH annotation/prediction without cross-genome BGC similarity networking.

skills.description: Use when you have antiSMASH .gbk BGCs from multiple genomes and need a unified pairwise BGC similarity table per biosynthetic class to build NPOmix training fingerprints.
skills.name: bigscape-similarity-output-concatenation
skills.search_text: bigscape-similarity-output-concatenation Use when you have antiSMASH .gbk BGCs from multiple genomes and need a unified pairwise BGC similarity table per biosynthetic class to build NPOmix training fingerprints. You only need GCF clustering memberships and not per-pair similarity scores for fingerprint construction — plain BiG-SCAPE network output suffices without concatenation. Your BGCs come from a fungal species with no BGC similar to any NPOmix training-set BGC, since the downstream classifier will return no answer. You need MS/MS-to-MS/MS similarity rather than BGC-to-BGC similarity — use GNPS modified cosine scoring instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Run BiG-SCAPE on antiSMASH-predicted BGCs (including MIBiG and singletons) and concatenate the per-class pairwise similarity outputs (e.g. *_hybrids_glocal) into a single similarity table that feeds NPOmix BGC fingerprint construction. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Run BiG-SCAPE on antiSMASH-predicted BGCs (including MIBiG and singletons) and concatenate the per-class pairwise similarity outputs (e.g. *_hybrids_glocal) into a single similarity table that feeds NPOmix BGC fingerprint construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need GCF clustering memberships and not per-pair similarity scores for fingerprint construction — plain BiG-SCAPE network output suffices without concatenation. Your BGCs come from a fungal species with no BGC similar to any NPOmix training-set BGC, since the downstream classifier will return no answer. You need MS/MS-to-MS/MS similarity rather than BGC-to-BGC similarity — use GNPS modified cosine scoring instead.

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular network contains a library-annotated seed node (e.g. glycocholic acid, m/z 466.316) and structurally related analogs must be discovered by reading edge mass shifts (e.g. +79.993 Da for sulfation) to neighboring unannotated nodes.
skills.name: bile-acid-conjugate-annotation
skills.search_text: bile-acid-conjugate-annotation Use when a GNPS molecular network contains a library-annotated seed node (e.g. glycocholic acid, m/z 466.316) and structurally related analogs must be discovered by reading edge mass shifts (e.g. +79.993 Da for sulfation) to neighboring unannotated nodes. The evaluation goal is peak-level preprocessing or feature annotation rather than scoring an already-trained classifier against known labels Ground-truth labels do not exist and a manual inspection pass to assign good/poor EIC quality has not been done Inputs are raw MS data files (.mzXML/.mzML) rather than the labeled EIC plot images the classifier was built to consume http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark a binary CNN classifier's end-to-end classification accuracy on a large manually annotated dataset by running inference on every sample image, comparing predictions against ground-truth labels, and computing the aggregate accuracy metric against a reported threshold (here, >90%). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01309

skills.description: Reference for scoring any binary classifier on expert Pass/Fail labels — e.g. MetaClean peak-quality predictions on an independent LC–MS test set such as ST000695.
skills.name: binary-classifier-evaluation-metrics
skills.search_text: binary-classifier-evaluation-metrics Reference for scoring any binary classifier on expert Pass/Fail labels — e.g. MetaClean peak-quality predictions on an independent LC–MS test set such as ST000695. The input is already a feature/peak table that has not yet been scored by a trained classifier — this skill only evaluates predictions, it does not classify peaks. There are more than two outcome classes (Pass/Fail) — F-measures here are per-class for binary labels only. Reference labels come from a different expert or labeling scheme than the training set, since the article notes the ionization mode, analytical platform, and biological matrix affect peak shape and quality, and metrics must be interpreted against comparable labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluate a binary peak-quality classifier (Pass vs Fail) using Accuracy and per-class F-measures against expert labels, and verify performance exceeds a random-label permutation baseline. In the MetaClean framework this is how the AdaBoost + M11 global classifier's generalization to independent test sets (e.g. ST000695) is quantified. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Evaluate a binary peak-quality classifier (Pass vs Fail) using Accuracy and per-class F-measures against expert labels, and verify performance exceeds a random-label permutation baseline. In the MetaClean framework this is how the AdaBoost + M11 global classifier's generalization to independent test sets (e.g. ST000695) is quantified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/peak table that has not yet been scored by a trained classifier — this skill only evaluates predictions, it does not classify peaks. There are more than two outcome classes (Pass/Fail) — F-measures here are per-class for binary labels only. Reference labels come from a different expert or labeling scheme than the training set, since the article notes the ionization mode, analytical platform, and biological matrix affect peak shape and quality, and metrics must be interpreted against comparable labels.
