skills.description: Use when DeepEI (or a similar fingerprint predictor) has converted EI mass spectra into structural fingerprints and you must verify each vector is binary and correctly dimensioned before merging into .msp or saving as .npy.
skills.name: binary-fingerprint-output-validation
skills.search_text: binary-fingerprint-output-validation Use when DeepEI (or a similar fingerprint predictor) has converted EI mass spectra into structural fingerprints and you must verify each vector is binary and correctly dimensioned before merging into .msp or saving as .npy. The fingerprint predictor is being applied to structures rather than spectra — NEIMS handles spectrum prediction from known structures; this validation only covers DeepEI's spectrum-to-fingerprint direction where the analyte's structure is unknown. Downstream steps only need ranked similarity scores and the fingerprints have already been merged into a validated .msp file — re-validating at that stage adds no information. The spectra have not yet been run through DeepEI; validation of predicted fingerprints requires the model output to exist first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates that fingerprints predicted by DeepEI from EI mass spectra are well-formed binary 0/1 vectors of the expected DeepEI output dimensionality before they are stored (e.g., predicted_fingerprints.npy) or merged into an .msp file for downstream PS2MS SMSF similarity ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Validates that fingerprints predicted by DeepEI from EI mass spectra are well-formed binary 0/1 vectors of the expected DeepEI output dimensionality before they are stored (e.g., predicted_fingerprints.npy) or merged into an .msp file for downstream PS2MS SMSF similarity ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The fingerprint predictor is being applied to structures rather than spectra — NEIMS handles spectrum prediction from known structures; this validation only covers DeepEI's spectrum-to-fingerprint direction where the analyte's structure is unknown. Downstream steps only need ranked similarity scores and the fingerprints have already been merged into a validated .msp file — re-validating at that stage adds no information. The spectra have not yet been run through DeepEI; validation of predicted fingerprints requires the model output to exist first.

skills.description: Use when M datasets each carry a cluster label vector c_m with K_m clusters and you must summarise these heterogeneous clusterings into one binary matrix (MOC) before integrative consensus clustering such as COCA.
skills.name: binary-indicator-encoding-of-cluster-assignments
skills.search_text: binary-indicator-encoding-of-cluster-assignments Use when M datasets each carry a cluster label vector c_m with K_m clusters and you must summarise these heterogeneous clusterings into one binary matrix (MOC) before integrative consensus clustering such as COCA. Inputs are already kernel matrices or similarity matrices — in that case KLIC (multiple kernel learning), not the COCA MOC construction, is the appropriate integration route. You need a single clustering per dataset (e.g. one label per observation aggregated across datasets) rather than a per-dataset, per-cluster binary membership encoding. Observations are shared across all datasets with no missingness and identical clusterings, making the indicator encoding redundant. Constructs the Matrix Of Clusters (MOC) — a K̄×N binary matrix encoding each observation's cluster membership across M independently clustered datasets — as the input summarisation step of Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis (COCA). It reconciles per-dataset clusterings with potentially different numbers of clusters before the consensus clustering integration step. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Constructs the Matrix Of Clusters (MOC) — a K̄×N binary matrix encoding each observation's cluster membership across M independently clustered datasets — as the input summarisation step of Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis (COCA). It reconciles per-dataset clusterings with potentially different numbers of clusters before the consensus clustering integration step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are already kernel matrices or similarity matrices — in that case KLIC (multiple kernel learning), not the COCA MOC construction, is the appropriate integration route. You need a single clustering per dataset (e.g. one label per observation aggregated across datasets) rather than a per-dataset, per-cluster binary membership encoding. Observations are shared across all datasets with no missingness and identical clusterings, making the indicator encoding redundant.

Input is already a processed feature/bucket table rather than raw 1D spectral intensity data The task is purely text-based handling where binary conversion cost is irrelevant and datasets are small A non-expert needs fully automatic batch-mode processing with no interactive spectra viewing — the article states such workflows 'have not yet reached full maturity' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Handles 1D NMR spectral intensity data stored in binary format, as NMRviewer does, so that large sets of spectra can be loaded, joined to experimental-design metadata, and rendered (e.g., to PNG via Gnuplot) without costly text-to-binary conversion. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y

skills.description: Use when generating candidate fragmentations for a small molecule (SMILES/SDF, 0–2000 Da) to support spectral matching or in silico database search against tandem MS spectra.
skills.name: binary-vector-fragment-encoding
skills.search_text: binary-vector-fragment-encoding Use when generating candidate fragmentations for a small molecule (SMILES/SDF, 0–2000 Da) to support spectral matching or in silico database search against tandem MS spectra. The goal is predicting complete fragmentation spectra rather than generating fragments for database search scoring — molDiscovery generates fragment graphs, not predicted spectra like QCEIMS or CFM-ID Molecules whose dominant fragmentation requires bond types or rearrangements outside the N-C/O-C/C-C cut set, since molDiscovery 'only covers a limited number of bond types and rearrangement rules' Very small molecules (<400 Da), where fewer fragments are generated and identification accuracy drops http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Encodes mass-spectrometry fragmentation fragments of small molecules as binary indicator vectors over a molecule's atoms, enabling efficient depth-n fragment generation via bitwise intersection after Hopcroft-Tarjan bridge/2-cut detection. This is the graph-construction core that makes molDiscovery's database search tractable for molecules up to ~2000 Da. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0

This is the graph-construction core that makes molDiscovery's database search tractable for molecules up to ~2000 Da.

skills.description: Use when a dilution or mixing-series dataset with known composition fractions is available and you must compare quantification fidelity of LC-MS feature tables from two processing tools (e.g., asari vs XCMS).
skills.name: binned-correlation-distribution-visualization
skills.search_text: binned-correlation-distribution-visualization Use when a dilution or mixing-series dataset with known composition fractions is available and you must compare quantification fidelity of LC-MS feature tables from two processing tools (e.g., asari vs XCMS). The dataset has no known mixing ratios or dilution design — correlation against composition is then undefined. Input is already a feature table from only one tool; cross-tool matching by m/z and retention time requires both tables. Low-resolution data or non-Orbitrap platforms where asari's 5 ppm m/z precision settings are not appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A quantification-quality evaluation that computes Pearson correlations between feature peak areas and known sample mixing ratios, then bins the r values (e.g., from -1 to 1) to compare how many features each tool tracks faithfully, as in Fig. 7d of the asari benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: A quantification-quality evaluation that computes Pearson correlations between feature peak areas and known sample mixing ratios, then bins the r values (e.g., from -1 to 1) to compare how many features each tool tracks faithfully, as in Fig. 7d of the asari benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no known mixing ratios or dilution design — correlation against composition is then undefined. Input is already a feature table from only one tool; cross-tool matching by m/z and retention time requires both tables. Low-resolution data or non-Orbitrap platforms where asari's 5 ppm m/z precision settings are not appropriate.

skills.description: Use when training an MS2DeepScore (or similar Siamese embedding) model on binned mass spectra and you need to augment each training example with moderate random peak-level perturbations.
skills.name: binned-spectrum-peak-manipulation
skills.search_text: binned-spectrum-peak-manipulation Use when training an MS2DeepScore (or similar Siamese embedding) model on binned mass spectra and you need to augment each training example with moderate random peak-level perturbations. On validation or test spectra — augmentation is applied to training data only, so perturbing the 500-InChIKey validation or test sets would corrupt benchmark results On raw (unbinned) peak lists — the augmentation operates on binned spectra after the 10–1000 m/z binning and square-root transformation steps, not on raw peak lists When intensities have not been square-root transformed — the low-intensity removal threshold (pre-transformation intensity below 0.4) assumes transformed intensities, so applying it to linearly-scaled intensities misclassifies which bins are eligible for removal http://edamontology.org/topic_0081 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Data augmentation for MS2DeepScore training that perturbs binned MS/MS spectra (10,000 equal-width bins over 10–1000 m/z) by removing low-intensity peaks, jittering intensities, and adding new random peaks, to increase model robustness. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Data augmentation for MS2DeepScore training that perturbs binned MS/MS spectra (10,000 equal-width bins over 10–1000 m/z) by removing low-intensity peaks, jittering intensities, and adding new random peaks, to increase model robustness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: On validation or test spectra — augmentation is applied to training data only, so perturbing the 500-InChIKey validation or test sets would corrupt benchmark results On raw (unbinned) peak lists — the augmentation operates on binned spectra after the 10–1000 m/z binning and square-root transformation steps, not on raw peak lists When intensities have not been square-root transformed — the low-intensity removal threshold (pre-transformation intensity below 0.4) assumes transformed intensities, so applying it to linearly-scaled intensities misclassifies which bins are eligible for removal

skills.description: Use when a bucket table produced by NMRProcFlow binning (Intelligent, variable-size or fixed-width) contains buckets with weak signal, and buckets must be retained or discarded by signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) before downstream statistics.
skills.name: binning-output-quality-control
skills.search_text: binning-output-quality-control Use when a bucket table produced by NMRProcFlow binning (Intelligent, variable-size or fixed-width) contains buckets with weak signal, and buckets must be retained or discarded by signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) before downstream statistics. The task is upstream spectra processing — ppm-scale calibration, baseline correction, or realignment of ppm areas — rather than quality control of the binning output Bucketing has not yet been performed: this skill operates on the bucket table produced by binning, not on raw FID spectra You need to quantify metabolites in crowded regions with heavy peak overlap; the paper plans local signal deconvolution for that in a future version, not SNR filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quality-controls the bucket table produced by NMR binning in NMRProcFlow by retaining or discarding buckets according to their signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), applicable either during the computing process or at the output step. This removes bins whose signal is indistinguishable from spectral noise before downstream metabolomics statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Quality-controls the bucket table produced by NMR binning in NMRProcFlow by retaining or discarding buckets according to their signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), applicable either during the computing process or at the output step. This removes bins whose signal is indistinguishable from spectral noise before downstream metabolomics statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is upstream spectra processing — ppm-scale calibration, baseline correction, or realignment of ppm areas — rather than quality control of the binning output Bucketing has not yet been performed: this skill operates on the bucket table produced by binning, not on raw FID spectra You need to quantify metabolites in crowded regions with heavy peak overlap; the paper plans local signal deconvolution for that in a future version, not SNR filtering

skills.description: Use when per-cell (or per-pixel) 13C6-glucose isotopologue distributions of fatty acids (e.g. C16 palmitate, C18 oleate) are available and the goal is to quantify relative uptake vs de novo synthesis as a fitted uptake fraction.
skills.name: binomial-fitting-of-fatty-acid-uptake-fraction
skills.search_text: binomial-fitting-of-fatty-acid-uptake-fraction Use when per-cell (or per-pixel) 13C6-glucose isotopologue distributions of fatty acids (e.g. C16 palmitate, C18 oleate) are available and the goal is to quantify relative uptake vs de novo synthesis as a fitted uptake fraction. When overall substrate usage is very low, e.g. the hypoxia/normoxia experiment — the authors state it 'becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction', so it was only used for ACLYkd data. When labelling data are not at isotopic steady state and absolute substrate contributions are required — the method provides only relative, not absolute, contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool. For bulk MS data without natural isotope abundance correction and normalization of isotopologue distributions — the fit requires corrected, normalized intensities as input. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fits a binomial model to natural-abundance-corrected, normalized isotopologue distributions of fatty acids to estimate the fraction of the fatty acid pool derived from uptake versus de novo synthesis, as used in 13C-SpaceM single-cell isotope tracing. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Fits a binomial model to natural-abundance-corrected, normalized isotopologue distributions of fatty acids to estimate the fraction of the fatty acid pool derived from uptake versus de novo synthesis, as used in 13C-SpaceM single-cell isotope tracing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When overall substrate usage is very low, e.g. the hypoxia/normoxia experiment — the authors state it 'becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction', so it was only used for ACLYkd data. When labelling data are not at isotopic steady state and absolute substrate contributions are required — the method provides only relative, not absolute, contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool. For bulk MS data without natural isotope abundance correction and normalization of isotopologue distributions — the fit requires corrected, normalized intensities as input.

skills.description: Use when you have normalized, natural-isotope-corrected isotopologue distributions for a fatty acid (e.g. palmitate M+0..M+16) and need the glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling degree p per cell, sample, or pixel.
skills.name: binomial-labelling-model-inference
skills.search_text: binomial-labelling-model-inference Use when you have normalized, natural-isotope-corrected isotopologue distributions for a fatty acid (e.g. palmitate M+0..M+16) and need the glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling degree p per cell, sample, or pixel. When overall substrate usage is very low, as in the hypoxia/normoxia experiment — the binomial distribution cannot be reliably fitted and the uptake fraction cannot be estimated; it was only used for ACLYkd data When isotopologue intensities are raw and not yet corrected for natural isotope abundance and normalized per cell/pixel — apply the sc_analysis.py correction and normalization steps first When labelling data must be interpreted against pool size (e.g. in vivo mouse tissue where isotopic steady state was likely not reached within the 48-h labelling period) — the model alone gives relative, not absolute, substrate contribution Fits a binomial distribution to natural-isotope-corrected, normalized fatty acid isotopologue intensities to estimate the labelling fraction p of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool (and uptake fraction) from 13C-glucose tracing data. This is the quantitative core of 13C-SpaceM's single-cell isotope tracing analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Fits a binomial distribution to natural-isotope-corrected, normalized fatty acid isotopologue intensities to estimate the labelling fraction p of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool (and uptake fraction) from 13C-glucose tracing data. This is the quantitative core of 13C-SpaceM's single-cell isotope tracing analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When overall substrate usage is very low, as in the hypoxia/normoxia experiment — the binomial distribution cannot be reliably fitted and the uptake fraction cannot be estimated; it was only used for ACLYkd data When isotopologue intensities are raw and not yet corrected for natural isotope abundance and normalized per cell/pixel — apply the sc_analysis.py correction and normalization steps first When labelling data must be interpreted against pool size (e.g. in vivo mouse tissue where isotopic steady state was likely not reached within the 48-h labelling period) — the model alone gives relative, not absolute, substrate contribution

skills.name: bioactive-ms-feature-network-clustering
skills.search_text: bioactive-ms-feature-network-clustering Use when you have a scored bioactive MS feature network (nodes = MS features/samples, edges = bioactivity-weighted associations) from basketed CSV inputs and need community detection and the three NP Analyst visualization outputs. Input is raw unprocessed mass spectrometry data (e.g. raw mass lists) rather than a scored bioactive feature network — run NP Analyst's basketing/scoring pipeline first, since unprocessed input increases the number of candidate bioactive MS features including junk features The goal is to group samples by their activity profiles rather than cluster MS features — communities in NP Analyst are based on bioactive MS feature distribution, not sample activity profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Divide the NP Analyst scored bioactive MS feature network into communities using the Louvain method, then produce the community-annotated graphML network plus rt vs m/z scatter and community views for prioritizing bioactive metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Divide the NP Analyst scored bioactive MS feature network into communities using the Louvain method, then produce the community-annotated graphML network plus rt vs m/z scatter and community views for prioritizing bioactive metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unprocessed mass spectrometry data (e.g. raw mass lists) rather than a scored bioactive feature network — run NP Analyst's basketing/scoring pipeline first, since unprocessed input increases the number of candidate bioactive MS features including junk features The goal is to group samples by their activity profiles rather than cluster MS features — communities in NP Analyst are based on bioactive MS feature distribution, not sample activity profiles

skills.description: Use when NMR (TOCSY/HSQC) data exist for a prefractionated extract library plus bioactivity screening results, and the goal is to locate network hotspots of shared spin system features correlated with activity for NMR-guided isolation.
skills.name: bioactive-prefraction-prioritization
skills.search_text: bioactive-prefraction-prioritization Use when NMR (TOCSY/HSQC) data exist for a prefractionated extract library plus bioactivity screening results, and the goal is to locate network hotspots of shared spin system features correlated with activity for NMR-guided isolation. The library contains compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) — these are precluded because TOCSY cross-peaks with both F1 and F2 < 2.5 ppm are excluded The input lacks bioactivity screening data, so 'hotspots' cannot be defined and the overlay prioritization has no activity signal to attribute Input is already a dereplicated feature table from a different platform without MADByTE spin system features — the network module expects MADByTE-generated TOCSY/HSQC feature data http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Prioritize bioactive metabolites from a prefractionated microbial natural products library by overlaying BioMAP antimicrobial screening data onto MADByTE spin-system chemical similarity networks, then isolating from bioactivity hotspot clusters (e.g., the 2108D/2108E hotspot yielding collismycin A). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Prioritize bioactive metabolites from a prefractionated microbial natural products library by overlaying BioMAP antimicrobial screening data onto MADByTE spin-system chemical similarity networks, then isolating from bioactivity hotspot clusters (e.g., the 2108D/2108E hotspot yielding collismycin A).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The library contains compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) — these are precluded because TOCSY cross-peaks with both F1 and F2 < 2.5 ppm are excluded The input lacks bioactivity screening data, so 'hotspots' cannot be defined and the overlay prioritization has no activity signal to attribute Input is already a dereplicated feature table from a different platform without MADByTE spin system features — the network module expects MADByTE-generated TOCSY/HSQC feature data

skills.description: Use when a proteomics-style LC–MS/MS metabolomics run has per-fraction bioactivity values (IC50 or inhibition groups) in the NP3 Metadata Table and you must rank clean consensus spectra by bioactivity correlation to prioritize natural-product leads.
skills.name: bioactivity-correlation-scoring
skills.search_text: bioactivity-correlation-scoring Use when a proteomics-style LC–MS/MS metabolomics run has per-fraction bioactivity values (IC50 or inhibition groups) in the NP3 Metadata Table and you must rank clean consensus spectra by bioactivity correlation to prioritize natural-product leads. The input is already a ranked feature table without raw LC–MS/MS files or bioactivity metadata — the skill requires the full Metadata Table plus LC–MS/MS data to compute clean consensus spectra and BCCs. The analysis goal is purely chemical (e.g. molecular networking without any bioactivity information) — BCC scoring is meaningless without fraction-level inhibition/IC50 values. Only blank or culture media samples are present — the filter step would remove every ion, leaving nothing to rank. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Computes bioactivity correlation coefficients (BCCs) between clean consensus MS2 spectra and fraction-level bioactivity measurements (e.g. proteasome inhibition), then filters and ranks the spectra so that the ions most correlated with activity surface as drug-discovery leads in the NP3 MS Workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Computes bioactivity correlation coefficients (BCCs) between clean consensus MS2 spectra and fraction-level bioactivity measurements (e.g. proteasome inhibition), then filters and ranks the spectra so that the ions most correlated with activity surface as drug-discovery leads in the NP3 MS Workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a ranked feature table without raw LC–MS/MS files or bioactivity metadata — the skill requires the full Metadata Table plus LC–MS/MS data to compute clean consensus spectra and BCCs. The analysis goal is purely chemical (e.g. molecular networking without any bioactivity information) — BCC scoring is meaningless without fraction-level inhibition/IC50 values. Only blank or culture media samples are present — the filter step would remove every ion, leaving nothing to rank.

skills.description: Use when a MIBiG (or BGC-database) JSON export must be summarised into a coverage table counting compounds with bioactivity and molecular-target annotations per functional category.
skills.name: bioactivity-coverage-tabulation
skills.search_text: bioactivity-coverage-tabulation Use when a MIBiG (or BGC-database) JSON export must be summarised into a coverage table counting compounds with bioactivity and molecular-target annotations per functional category. Input is raw BGC nucleotide sequence or genbank files needing cluster detection (use antiSMASH/GECCO instead, not annotation tabulation) The goal is structural cross-linking of compounds to NP Atlas/PubChem/ChemSpider/LOTUS/ChEMBL rather than bioactivity/target coverage counting The dataset is not MIBiG-standardised JSON and lacks bioactivity annotation fields — term normalisation against the 68 functional categories cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Tabulate per-functional-category bioactivity coverage from MIBiG 3.0 JSON data by parsing every cluster entry, normalising bioactivity terms, and flagging compounds with chemical target annotations. Reproduces the paper's headline coverage figures (1002 compounds, 51 unique bioactivities, 68 functional categories, 95 target-annotated compounds). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Tabulate per-functional-category bioactivity coverage from MIBiG 3.0 JSON data by parsing every cluster entry, normalising bioactivity terms, and flagging compounds with chemical target annotations. Reproduces the paper's headline coverage figures (1002 compounds, 51 unique bioactivities, 68 functional categories, 95 target-annotated compounds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw BGC nucleotide sequence or genbank files needing cluster detection (use antiSMASH/GECCO instead, not annotation tabulation) The goal is structural cross-linking of compounds to NP Atlas/PubChem/ChemSpider/LOTUS/ChEMBL rather than bioactivity/target coverage counting The dataset is not MIBiG-standardised JSON and lacks bioactivity annotation fields — term normalisation against the 68 functional categories cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how many compounds in a biosynthetic gene cluster database carry bioactivity or molecular-target annotations, or when building a per-functional-category coverage table from MIBiG JSON data.
skills.name: bioactivity-functional-category-mapping
skills.search_text: bioactivity-functional-category-mapping Use when you need to quantify how many compounds in a biosynthetic gene cluster database carry bioactivity or molecular-target annotations, or when building a per-functional-category coverage table from MIBiG JSON data. You need bioactivity annotations for BGCs that lack experimentally validated characterisation — MIBiG only contains experimentally validated BGC entries, so the table cannot generalise to predicted/unvalidated clusters You want automated activity prediction from sequence — this skill only tallies manually curated annotations, it does not predict bioactivity (see e.g. the Walker and Clardy ML model for that) Your input is raw GenBank/RefSeq sequence rather than curated MIBiG JSON entries http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Parses MIBiG 3.0 JSON cluster entries to tally compounds with bioactivity annotations (1002 compounds, 51 unique bioactivities) and chemical target annotations (95 compounds), then normalises activity terms onto the 68 standardised functional categories to build a per-category coverage table. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Parses MIBiG 3.0 JSON cluster entries to tally compounds with bioactivity annotations (1002 compounds, 51 unique bioactivities) and chemical target annotations (95 compounds), then normalises activity terms onto the 68 standardised functional categories to build a per-category coverage table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need bioactivity annotations for BGCs that lack experimentally validated characterisation — MIBiG only contains experimentally validated BGC entries, so the table cannot generalise to predicted/unvalidated clusters You want automated activity prediction from sequence — this skill only tallies manually curated annotations, it does not predict bioactivity (see e.g. the Walker and Clardy ML model for that) Your input is raw GenBank/RefSeq sequence rather than curated MIBiG JSON entries

skills.description: Decision support for prioritizing crude or roughly-fractionated natural product extract fractions when measured bioactivity values (e.g., cancer cell IC50-type cytotoxicity) are available and only the most potent fractions should proceed to isolation.
skills.name: bioactivity-guided-natural-product-fraction-ranking
skills.search_text: bioactivity-guided-natural-product-fraction-ranking Decision support for prioritizing crude or roughly-fractionated natural product extract fractions when measured bioactivity values (e.g., cancer cell IC50-type cytotoxicity) are available and only the most potent fractions should proceed to isolation. The fractions have no measured bioactivity (e.g., cytotoxicity) values — ranking cannot be guided by potency and should instead rely on NMR/MS2 annotation alone. The input is already a purified, isolated compound set rather than roughly-fractionated extract fractions — prioritization-by-cytotoxicity is moot once isolation is complete. http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Ranks roughly-fractionated natural product extracts (here, a marine cyanobacterial Symploca extract) by measured cancer cell cytotoxicity so the most potent fractions are prioritized for downstream isolation, as done alongside SMART 2.0 NMR annotation and MS2-based molecular networking in this study. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jacs.9b13786
skills.summary: Ranks roughly-fractionated natural product extracts (here, a marine cyanobacterial Symploca extract) by measured cancer cell cytotoxicity so the most potent fractions are prioritized for downstream isolation, as done alongside SMART 2.0 NMR annotation and MS2-based molecular networking in this study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The fractions have no measured bioactivity (e.g., cytotoxicity) values — ranking cannot be guided by potency and should instead rely on NMR/MS2 annotation alone. The input is already a purified, isolated compound set rather than roughly-fractionated extract fractions — prioritization-by-cytotoxicity is moot once isolation is complete.

skills.description: Use when a MADByTE chemical similarity network of spin system features must be annotated with bioactivity screening data to locate clusters of correlated active samples (e.g., 34 BioMAP-active prefractions) for prioritization.
skills.name: bioactivity-network-overlay-annotation
skills.search_text: bioactivity-network-overlay-annotation Use when a MADByTE chemical similarity network of spin system features must be annotated with bioactivity screening data to locate clusters of correlated active samples (e.g., 34 BioMAP-active prefractions) for prioritization. The goal is dereplication of known scaffolds alone, with no bioactivity screening data to overlay (use MADByTE's dereplication module against an internal library instead) Input is raw 1H/TOCSY/HSQC spectra rather than processed spin system features — the spectra must first pass through MADByTE peak picking and feature generation The sample set lacks paired screening results, so no bioactivity attributes can be encoded as node annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Overlays biological screening results (e.g., BioMAP antimicrobial data) as node attributes onto a MADByTE spin system chemical similarity network to identify bioactivity hotspots among prefractionated natural products extracts and prioritize samples for NMR-guided isolation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Overlays biological screening results (e.g., BioMAP antimicrobial data) as node attributes onto a MADByTE spin system chemical similarity network to identify bioactivity hotspots among prefractionated natural products extracts and prioritize samples for NMR-guided isolation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is dereplication of known scaffolds alone, with no bioactivity screening data to overlay (use MADByTE's dereplication module against an internal library instead) Input is raw 1H/TOCSY/HSQC spectra rather than processed spin system features — the spectra must first pass through MADByTE peak picking and feature generation The sample set lacks paired screening results, so no bioactivity attributes can be encoded as node annotations

skills.description: Use when a feature quantification table with fraction-wise bioassay values is available and you need to prioritize ions in a molecular network by correlation with measured bioactivity rather than by abundance alone.
skills.name: bioactivity-score-node-mapping
skills.search_text: bioactivity-score-node-mapping Use when a feature quantification table with fraction-wise bioassay values is available and you need to prioritize ions in a molecular network by correlation with measured bioactivity rather than by abundance alone. The feature table has not yet been correlated against bioassay values — running the notebook (Step 2, Pearson correlation calculation) is a prerequisite before any node mapping. The molecular network does not yet exist, e.g. the .MGF has not been submitted to a GNPS FBMN Data Analysis job and imported into Cytoscape. The workflow relies on aligned LC-MS/MS features across fractions; it is not applicable when no fraction-wise feature quantification (e.g. MZmine2 'Peak area' exports) is available. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Maps Pearson-correlation bioactivity scores from a fraction-bioassay dataset onto molecular network nodes in Cytoscape, so candidate bioactive ions (e.g. antiviral hits in Euphorbia dendroides) become visually distinguishable features in the GNPS feature-based molecular network. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.7b00737
skills.summary: Maps Pearson-correlation bioactivity scores from a fraction-bioassay dataset onto molecular network nodes in Cytoscape, so candidate bioactive ions (e.g. antiviral hits in Euphorbia dendroides) become visually distinguishable features in the GNPS feature-based molecular network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has not yet been correlated against bioassay values — running the notebook (Step 2, Pearson correlation calculation) is a prerequisite before any node mapping. The molecular network does not yet exist, e.g. the .MGF has not been submitted to a GNPS FBMN Data Analysis job and imported into Cytoscape. The workflow relies on aligned LC-MS/MS features across fractions; it is not applicable when no fraction-wise feature quantification (e.g. MZmine2 'Peak area' exports) is available.

skills.description: Use when a feature quantification matrix from MZmine2 or Optimus must be merged with per-sample bioassay values (e.g. antiviral EC50 or inhibition) prior to running the bioactive molecular networking Pearson-correlation notebook.
skills.name: bioassay-data-integration-into-feature-tables
skills.search_text: bioassay-data-integration-into-feature-tables Use when a feature quantification matrix from MZmine2 or Optimus must be merged with per-sample bioassay values (e.g. antiviral EC50 or inhibition) prior to running the bioactive molecular networking Pearson-correlation notebook. The input is already a bioactivity-augmented table (features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.csv) — re-appending bioassay columns would duplicate or overwrite the correlation input. The goal is plain feature-based molecular networking without bioactivity mapping; the standard GNPS FBMN workflow consumes the unedited features_quantification_matrix.csv and .MGF directly. Bioassay data are not matched to the LC-MS/MS-analyzed fractions (different samples or incompatible identifiers), since the Pearson correlation would then pair feature intensities with the wrong bioactivity values. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Augments the aligned LC-MS/MS feature quantification table (e.g. features_quantification_matrix.csv) with the bioassay measurement recorded for each fraction (e.g. antiviral activity), yielding features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.csv so that the Bioactive_Molecular_Networks Jupyter notebook can compute Pearson correlations between every detected feature and the bioactivity outcome. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.7b00737
skills.summary: Augments the aligned LC-MS/MS feature quantification table (e.g. features_quantification_matrix.csv) with the bioassay measurement recorded for each fraction (e.g. antiviral activity), yielding features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.csv so that the Bioactive_Molecular_Networks Jupyter notebook can compute Pearson correlations between every detected feature and the bioactivity outcome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a bioactivity-augmented table (features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.csv) — re-appending bioassay columns would duplicate or overwrite the correlation input. The goal is plain feature-based molecular networking without bioactivity mapping; the standard GNPS FBMN workflow consumes the unedited features_quantification_matrix.csv and .MGF directly. Bioassay data are not matched to the LC-MS/MS-analyzed fractions (different samples or incompatible identifiers), since the Pearson correlation would then pair feature intensities with the wrong bioactivity values.

skills.description: Use when raw bioassay results (e.g., IC50, percent inhibition, growth scores) from an extract library arrive in heterogeneous per-assay formats/scales and must be assembled into a samples × assays profile matrix before NP Analyst Activity/Cluster Score computation.
skills.name: bioassay-data-normalization
skills.search_text: bioassay-data-normalization Use when raw bioassay results (e.g., IC50, percent inhibition, growth scores) from an extract library arrive in heterogeneous per-assay formats/scales and must be assembled into a samples × assays profile matrix before NP Analyst Activity/Cluster Score computation. The bioassay columns are already normalized to a common scale and assembled into a samples × assays profile matrix The task concerns processing the MS side (basketing, replicate comparison, GNPS/MZmine 2 import) rather than the biological data Interpreting NP Analyst outputs (scatter plot, network, community views) — normalization is an upstream input-preparation step Assembles individual bioassay results for the same extract library into a biological profile matrix whose bioassay columns are normalized onto the same scale, a prerequisite for NP Analyst to compute meaningful Activity Scores and Cluster Scores from the integrated feature–bioassay data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Assembles individual bioassay results for the same extract library into a biological profile matrix whose bioassay columns are normalized onto the same scale, a prerequisite for NP Analyst to compute meaningful Activity Scores and Cluster Scores from the integrated feature–bioassay data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The bioassay columns are already normalized to a common scale and assembled into a samples × assays profile matrix The task concerns processing the MS side (basketing, replicate comparison, GNPS/MZmine 2 import) rather than the biological data Interpreting NP Analyst outputs (scatter plot, network, community views) — normalization is an upstream input-preparation step

skills.description: Use when a bioactive molecular network (Pearson r2 > 0.8, p < 0.05 corrected) must be compared against the molecule list isolated by classical bioassay-guided fractionation to identify newly highlighted candidates.
skills.name: bioassay-guided-fractionation-comparison
skills.search_text: bioassay-guided-fractionation-comparison Use when a bioactive molecular network (Pearson r2 > 0.8, p < 0.05 corrected) must be compared against the molecule list isolated by classical bioassay-guided fractionation to identify newly highlighted candidates. Input is already a merged comparison table or the candidate list has not yet been filtered to r2 > 0.8 and corrected p < 0.05. The extract has no bioassay-guided fractionation result to compare against (no classical isolation report available). Only a bioactivity score visualization in the molecular network is needed; the comparison step is specific to auditing what classical fractionation missed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Set-comparison of bioactivity-score-predicted candidate molecules from a molecular network against the molecules actually recovered by classical bioassay-guided fractionation, to expose missed candidates. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.7b00737
skills.summary: Set-comparison of bioactivity-score-predicted candidate molecules from a molecular network against the molecules actually recovered by classical bioassay-guided fractionation, to expose missed candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a merged comparison table or the candidate list has not yet been filtered to r2 > 0.8 and corrected p < 0.05. The extract has no bioassay-guided fractionation result to compare against (no classical isolation report available). Only a bioactivity score visualization in the molecular network is needed; the comparison step is specific to auditing what classical fractionation missed.

skills.description: Use when raw bioassay measurements (continuous potency values from wild soybean or similar natural-product extracts) must become binary class labels for a supervised classifier such as the MS2toImg-CNN.
skills.name: bioassay-label-normalization-and-binarization
skills.search_text: bioassay-label-normalization-and-binarization Use when raw bioassay measurements (continuous potency values from wild soybean or similar natural-product extracts) must become binary class labels for a supervised classifier such as the MS2toImg-CNN. The bioassay data are already categorical or thresholded class labels — re-normalizing and re-binarizing would discard information or introduce arbitrary cutoffs The endpoint of interest has no natural 0–1 range (e.g. an unbounded continuous physicochemical property) and no article-defined low/high cutoff is specified The task is regression or ranking of bioactivity, not binary classification of high- vs. low-activity groups http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Normalizes measured bioassay endpoints (e.g. DPPH radical scavenging, elastase inhibition, TFC, TPC) to a 0–1 range and binarizes them into low- versus high-activity classes using article-specified cutoffs so they can serve as CNN training labels. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Normalizes measured bioassay endpoints (e.g. DPPH radical scavenging, elastase inhibition, TFC, TPC) to a 0–1 range and binarizes them into low- versus high-activity classes using article-specified cutoffs so they can serve as CNN training labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The bioassay data are already categorical or thresholded class labels — re-normalizing and re-binarizing would discard information or introduce arbitrary cutoffs The endpoint of interest has no natural 0–1 range (e.g. an unbounded continuous physicochemical property) and no article-defined low/high cutoff is specified The task is regression or ranking of bioactivity, not binary classification of high- vs. low-activity groups

skills.description: Use when raw primary-screening assay results (BioMAP-style inhibition/no-inhibition columns, growth assays, etc.) must be assembled into normalized biological profiles before import into NP Analyst for Compound Activity Mapping.
skills.name: bioassay-profile-normalization
skills.search_text: bioassay-profile-normalization Use when raw primary-screening assay results (BioMAP-style inhibition/no-inhibition columns, growth assays, etc.) must be assembled into normalized biological profiles before import into NP Analyst for Compound Activity Mapping. Input is already a normalized NP Analyst-ready profile table or the assay columns are all on an identical scale Input is mass spectrometry data (mzML, MZmine 2 peak lists, GNPS .graphml) rather than bioassay results — those go through replicate comparison and basketing instead The assays cannot be meaningfully placed on a common scale (e.g., heterogeneous assay types with no shared inhibition/no-inhibition semantics) Assembles individual bioassay results from a screening campaign (e.g., 15-pathogen BioMAP inhibition/no-inhibition tables for a 925-prefraction marine Actinobacterial library) into biological profiles whose columns share a common scale, so NP Analyst can compute comparable Activity Scores across features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Assembles individual bioassay results from a screening campaign (e.g., 15-pathogen BioMAP inhibition/no-inhibition tables for a 925-prefraction marine Actinobacterial library) into biological profiles whose columns share a common scale, so NP Analyst can compute comparable Activity Scores across features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized NP Analyst-ready profile table or the assay columns are all on an identical scale Input is mass spectrometry data (mzML, MZmine 2 peak lists, GNPS .graphml) rather than bioassay results — those go through replicate comparison and basketing instead The assays cannot be meaningfully placed on a common scale (e.g., heterogeneous assay types with no shared inhibition/no-inhibition semantics)

skills.description: Use when metabolite identifiers (names or database IDs such as KEGG, PubChem CID, HMDB) must be translated to KEGG compounds and edges are needed between metabolites linked by known biochemical transformations in KEGG RPAIR.
skills.name: biochemical-reaction-network-construction
skills.search_text: biochemical-reaction-network-construction Use when metabolite identifiers (names or database IDs such as KEGG, PubChem CID, HMDB) must be translated to KEGG compounds and edges are needed between metabolites linked by known biochemical transformations in KEGG RPAIR. Measured compounds lack KEGG identifiers or known biochemistry (unknowns) — biochemical edges will be absent; combine with structural similarity (Tanimoto >0.7), spectral similarity (cosine >0.7), or empirical Spearman correlation edges (FDR <0.05) instead The goal is pathway-database-driven mapping of known biochemical domain knowledge rather than pathway-independent associations — a tool like Metscape may be more appropriate Input data are non-metabolomic features (genomic, proteomic, clinical) with no chemical identity that can be translated to KEGG compounds http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs enzymatic (biochemical) reaction networks by mapping metabolites to KEGG compound IDs and connecting those joined by KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs, using MetaMapR's curated lookup table built from over 14,000 KEGG RPAIR reactions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Constructs enzymatic (biochemical) reaction networks by mapping metabolites to KEGG compound IDs and connecting those joined by KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs, using MetaMapR's curated lookup table built from over 14,000 KEGG RPAIR reactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Measured compounds lack KEGG identifiers or known biochemistry (unknowns) — biochemical edges will be absent; combine with structural similarity (Tanimoto >0.7), spectral similarity (cosine >0.7), or empirical Spearman correlation edges (FDR <0.05) instead The goal is pathway-database-driven mapping of known biochemical domain knowledge rather than pathway-independent associations — a tool like Metscape may be more appropriate Input data are non-metabolomic features (genomic, proteomic, clinical) with no chemical identity that can be translated to KEGG compounds

skills.search_text: bioconductor-example-dataset-access Use when an analysis needs a small, citable LC-MS test dataset with matched feature quantification and sample metadata, or when xcms results (peak picking, grouping, retention-time correction) must be converted into one R object for downstream steps. skills.description: Use when building or extending the reference metabolite database behind ROIAL-NMR — e.g., deriving 1H chemical shift and J-coupling multiplet (SRRM) tables from BMRB or HMDB records for biofluids like serum, urine, saliva, or CSF.
skills.name: biofluid-metabolite-library-construction
skills.search_text: biofluid-metabolite-library-construction Use when building or extending the reference metabolite database behind ROIAL-NMR — e.g., deriving 1H chemical shift and J-coupling multiplet (SRRM) tables from BMRB or HMDB records for biofluids like serum, urine, saliva, or CSF. Automated ROI identification or peak picking from raw spectra — the article states 'Automated identification of ROIs is beyond the scope of the current version of the program' Absolute quantification of metabolite concentrations — 'absolute quantification of the compounds is not the primary aim of the program' Collectively identifying metabolites across multiple ROIs — the databases themselves (HMDB, BMRB) lack this mechanism; that is what ROIAL-NMR's match-ratio logic does downstream http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Construct a program-specific metabolite NMR assignment library (chemical-shift table plus spectral region resonance multiplet/SRRM table) from a biological NMR reference database such as HMDB or BMRB, formatted as an Excel workbook that ROIAL-NMR can ingest as a user-selected metabolic database. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/nbm.70131
skills.summary: Construct a program-specific metabolite NMR assignment library (chemical-shift table plus spectral region resonance multiplet/SRRM table) from a biological NMR reference database such as HMDB or BMRB, formatted as an Excel workbook that ROIAL-NMR can ingest as a user-selected metabolic database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Automated ROI identification or peak picking from raw spectra — the article states 'Automated identification of ROIs is beyond the scope of the current version of the program' Absolute quantification of metabolite concentrations — 'absolute quantification of the compounds is not the primary aim of the program' Collectively identifying metabolites across multiple ROIs — the databases themselves (HMDB, BMRB) lack this mechanism; that is what ROIAL-NMR's match-ratio logic does downstream

skills.description: Use when evaluating a spatial multi-omics integration result (ST and/or SM embeddings) and you need to confirm the embedding preserves biological structure, e.g. spatial cluster identity from H&E annotation.

skills.search_text: biological-conservation-scoring Use when evaluating a spatial multi-omics integration result (ST and/or SM embeddings) and you need to confirm the embedding preserves biological structure, e.g. spatial cluster identity from H&E annotation. skills.description: Use when the input abundance table is in BIOM format (e.g., QIIME or mothur output) and a circular taxonomic tree visualization with GraPhlAn is the target output.
skills.name: biom-file-conversion-to-graphlan-format
skills.search_text: biom-file-conversion-to-graphlan-format Use when the input abundance table is in BIOM format (e.g., QIIME or mothur output) and a circular taxonomic tree visualization with GraPhlAn is the target output. Input is already a MetaPhlAn/LEfSe-style tab-separated abundance table that does not need BIOM parsing (though export2graphlan still accepts it, the BIOM-specific path is unnecessary). The goal is an interactive tree explorer rather than a static publication-quality circular figure — tools like iTOL or Krona target interactive analyses instead. BIOM library (ver. 2.0.1) is unavailable and the input cannot be converted, since BIOM input support depends on the biom-format package. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Converts BIOM-format 16S abundance tables (e.g., from QIIME/mothur pipelines such as a saliva microbiome dataset) into the two GraPhlAn input files — a tree file and an annotation file — using export2graphlan, enabling rendering of a circular taxonomic tree with GraPhlAn. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Converts BIOM-format 16S abundance tables (e.g., from QIIME/mothur pipelines such as a saliva microbiome dataset) into the two GraPhlAn input files — a tree file and an annotation file — using export2graphlan, enabling rendering of a circular taxonomic tree with GraPhlAn.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a MetaPhlAn/LEfSe-style tab-separated abundance table that does not need BIOM parsing (though export2graphlan still accepts it, the BIOM-specific path is unnecessary). BIOM library (ver. 2.0.1) is unavailable and the input cannot be converted, since BIOM input support depends on the biom-format package.

skills.description: Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized SCMS metabolomics feature table (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma cell pairs, control and vemurafenib-treated) must be screened for species that differ between groups and annotated as biomarker candidates.
skills.name: biomarker-candidate-selection
skills.search_text: biomarker-candidate-selection Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized SCMS metabolomics feature table (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma cell pairs, control and vemurafenib-treated) must be screened for species that differ between groups and annotated as biomarker candidates. The goal is cell phenotype classification rather than building a differential-species biomarker list — use MetaPhenotype (MAML meta-learning) instead, which was built to classify primary vs metastatic cells from limited SCMS samples The data are raw SCMS spectra rather than a pretreated, peak-aligned, TIC-normalized feature table — the established pretreatment protocol (noise/background subtraction, Geena2 10 ppm alignment) must run first Only a handful of cells per group are available for the new comparison — statistical fold-change/FDR screening is unreliable at very low cell counts, which is the regime MetaPhenotype's few-shot adaptation targets instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects differentially abundant metabolite/lipid species from single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) feature tables as biomarker candidates by combining volcano-plot statistics (fold change ≥ 2.0, FDR-adjusted p ≤ 0.05) with tentative database annotation of significant lipid classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Selects differentially abundant metabolite/lipid species from single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) feature tables as biomarker candidates by combining volcano-plot statistics (fold change ≥ 2.0, FDR-adjusted p ≤ 0.05) with tentative database annotation of significant lipid classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell phenotype classification rather than building a differential-species biomarker list — use MetaPhenotype (MAML meta-learning) instead, which was built to classify primary vs metastatic cells from limited SCMS samples The data are raw SCMS spectra rather than a pretreated, peak-aligned, TIC-normalized feature table — the established pretreatment protocol (noise/background subtraction, Geena2 10 ppm alignment) must run first Only a handful of cells per group are available for the new comparison — statistical fold-change/FDR screening is unreliable at very low cell counts, which is the regime MetaPhenotype's few-shot adaptation targets instead

skills.summary: Evaluates DeepMASS-based metabolite identification on external biomarker MS/MS spectra acquired on instruments not used for training (e.g. Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF), scoring each unknown spectrum against the 662-compound KEGG database and recording whether the structure-related metabolite is the top-ranked hit.

skills.search_text: biomarker-literature-curation Decision support for testing whether restricting raw LC-MS metabolomic input to literature-reported biomarker m/z windows (3 ppm, PC>1/3/8) lowers a trained classifier's accuracy versus the full raw-data baseline. When the goal is biomarker discovery or annotating unknown metabolites via interpretability (RISE heatmaps, metabolite-protein networks) rather than testing whether known biomarker signals alone suffice for classification When input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw LC-MS data, since the 3 ppm m/z-window filtering is defined on raw metabolomic signals When the data modality is not serum LC-MS metabolomics with the corresponding lung-cancer biomarker literature available for curation http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Curates published disease biomarker m/z values (with publication counts, PC) from screened literature and uses them to filter raw LC-MS signals within a 3 ppm tolerance, enabling ablation experiments that test how much unannotated metabolomic signal contributes to DeepMSProfiler classification accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-51433-3

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is biomarker discovery or annotating unknown metabolites via interpretability (RISE heatmaps, metabolite-protein networks) rather than testing whether known biomarker signals alone suffice for classification When input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw LC-MS data, since the 3 ppm m/z-window filtering is defined on raw metabolomic signals When the data modality is not serum LC-MS metabolomics with the corresponding lung-cancer biomarker literature available for curation

skills.description: Use when preparing Nightingale-platform metabolic biomarker concentration tables (with skewness and cohort-specific distributions) for Cox proportional hazards models or meta-analysis, especially when zeroes and cross-cohort scale differences are present.
skills.name: biomarker-log-transformation-and-scaling
skills.search_text: biomarker-log-transformation-and-scaling Use when preparing Nightingale-platform metabolic biomarker concentration tables (with skewness and cohort-specific distributions) for Cox proportional hazards models or meta-analysis, especially when zeroes and cross-cohort scale differences are present. Biomarker values are already on the log scale or already z-standardized per cohort (re-applying x+1/log would double-transform). You need a clinically deployable risk score in original concentration units — the article notes the per-cohort scaled score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic'. Data come from a different metabolomics platform with different scaling behavior and no zero-inflated biomarkers; verify transformation assumptions before applying. Per-cohort preprocessing of circulating metabolic biomarkers (Nightingale NMR platform, 226 biomarkers) prior to survival analysis: add 1 to biomarkers containing zeroes, log-transform, and scale to standard deviation units separately per study so effect sizes are comparable in SD-unit hazard ratios. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: Per-cohort preprocessing of circulating metabolic biomarkers (Nightingale NMR platform, 226 biomarkers) prior to survival analysis: add 1 to biomarkers containing zeroes, log-transform, and scale to standard deviation units separately per study so effect sizes are comparable in SD-unit hazard ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Biomarker values are already on the log scale or already z-standardized per cohort (re-applying x+1/log would double-transform). You need a clinically deployable risk score in original concentration units — the article notes the per-cohort scaled score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic'. Data come from a different metabolomics platform with different scaling behavior and no zero-inflated biomarkers; verify transformation assumptions before applying.

skills.description: Use when you have a cleaned metabolite abundance matrix (e.g. tidyMass peak-area feature table) spanning many samples and need to group metabolites into co-accumulation modules and nominate hub metabolites as biomarker candidates when traditional group-based DAM comparison is impractical.
skills.name: biomarker-metabolite-module-mining
skills.search_text: biomarker-metabolite-module-mining Use when you have a cleaned metabolite abundance matrix (e.g. tidyMass peak-area feature table) spanning many samples and need to group metabolites into co-accumulation modules and nominate hub metabolites as biomarker candidates when traditional group-based DAM comparison is impractical. The goal is a straightforward group-based differential abundance metabolite (DAM) comparison between a few sample groups — the iterative module approach is for population-scale datasets where such comparison is impractical Input is raw LC-MS vendor data requiring peak picking and data cleaning — upstream processing is handled by tidyMass before this module-mining step The input matrix is a .csv/.xlsx file or sample IDs contain spaces, special symbols, or pure numbers — the WGCNA-shinyApp only accepts tab-delimited files with clean sample IDs http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Iterative WGCNA-based clustering of metabolite abundance profiles (as implemented in MetMiner/WGCNA-shinyApp) that assigns every metabolite to a co-accumulation module and flags per-module hub metabolites at kME > 0.8 for biomarker screening in population-scale plant metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Iterative WGCNA-based clustering of metabolite abundance profiles (as implemented in MetMiner/WGCNA-shinyApp) that assigns every metabolite to a co-accumulation module and flags per-module hub metabolites at kME > 0.8 for biomarker screening in population-scale plant metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a straightforward group-based differential abundance metabolite (DAM) comparison between a few sample groups — the iterative module approach is for population-scale datasets where such comparison is impractical Input is raw LC-MS vendor data requiring peak picking and data cleaning — upstream processing is handled by tidyMass before this module-mining step The input matrix is a .csv/.xlsx file or sample IDs contain spaces, special symbols, or pure numbers — the WGCNA-shinyApp only accepts tab-delimited files with clean sample IDs

skills.search_text: biomarker-missingness-handling Use when post-QC, log-scaled UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations still contain plate-level shifts attributable to unexplained technical causes, and outlier shipment plates must be detected and their samples set to missing. No prefiltering of samples or columns should be performed before remove_technical_variation(): the algorithms expect all the data to be present, so plate masking must come last, not first Handling of individual outlier samples or biomarker measurement QC flags — the ukbnmr package performs no filtering or treatment of outlier samples; sample-level QC decisions (UK Biobank fields #23651–23655, #23700–23948) are a separate sensitivity-analysis concern Derived biomarkers and ratios: only the 107 non-derived biomarkers are processed; composites and ratios must be recomputed afterwards with recompute_derived_biomarkers() http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies shipment plates that are outliers of non-biological origin in UK Biobank NMR biomarker data and sets their samples to missing, as the final step of the ukbnmr technical-variation removal pipeline. skills.name: biomolecular-class-assignment-of-unknown-features
skills.search_text: biomolecular-class-assignment-of-unknown-features Use when you have untargeted traveling-wave ion mobility data (feature m/z, charge state, retention time, arrival time) and must assign each feature to small molecule, lipid, or peptide class — and obtain a calibrated TWCCSN2 — without prior identification. When the calibration data set or ionization mode is outside MOCCal's current scope — it is parametrized for positive-ion-mode small molecule, lipid, and peptide calibrations and is not yet extended to negative ionization mode data or other endogenous/xenobiotic chemical classes When features are already structurally identified, since the skill exists specifically to assign unknown features to calibrations without prior identification http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assign unidentified TWIM-MS features to a biomolecular class (small molecule, lipid, or peptide) by calibrating each singly charged feature's arrival time with up to three class-specific power law equations and selecting the calibration whose TWCCSN2 value has the smallest ΔCCS to the DTCCSN2-vs-m/z regression trendline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04290
skills.summary: Assign unidentified TWIM-MS features to a biomolecular class (small molecule, lipid, or peptide) by calibrating each singly charged feature's arrival time with up to three class-specific power law equations and selecting the calibration whose TWCCSN2 value has the smallest ΔCCS to the DTCCSN2-vs-m/z regression trendline.

skills.description: Use when processing traveling-wave ion mobility (TWIM-MS) feature tables where each feature carries m/z, charge state, retention time, and arrival time but no prior identification, and you need an accurate class-specific CCS value (e.g., NIST SRM 1950 extracts spiked with protein digests).
skills.name: biomolecular-class-assignment-power-law
skills.search_text: biomolecular-class-assignment-power-law Use when processing traveling-wave ion mobility (TWIM-MS) feature tables where each feature carries m/z, charge state, retention time, and arrival time but no prior identification, and you need an accurate class-specific CCS value (e.g., NIST SRM 1950 extracts spiked with protein digests). Data are already feature-identified (e.g., annotated lipids or peptides with known CCS references) — MOCCal is designed for assignment of unknown features without prior identification. Data are in negative ionization mode, or features belong to endogenous/xenobiotic chemical classes outside the small molecule / lipid / peptide scope. The acquisition platform is not traveling-wave IM-MS (e.g., drift-tube IM-MS or TIMS), since the power-law calibrations and arrival-time-to-TWCCSN2 relationships are TWIM-specific. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A method for assigning unannotated TWIM-MS features to small molecule, lipid, or peptide (z=1–3) biomolecular classes by comparing each feature's class-specific power-law-calibrated TWCCSN2 value to m/z-binned class trendlines, then selecting the calibration with the smallest ΔCCS. Developed in MOCCal (Hynds & Hines 2024, Anal. Chem.) for multiomic collision cross section calibration without prior feature identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04290
skills.summary: A method for assigning unannotated TWIM-MS features to small molecule, lipid, or peptide (z=1–3) biomolecular classes by comparing each feature's class-specific power-law-calibrated TWCCSN2 value to m/z-binned class trendlines, then selecting the calibration with the smallest ΔCCS. Developed in MOCCal (Hynds & Hines 2024, Anal. Chem.) for multiomic collision cross section calibration without prior feature identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already feature-identified (e.g., annotated lipids or peptides with known CCS references) — MOCCal is designed for assignment of unknown features without prior identification. Data are in negative ionization mode, or features belong to endogenous/xenobiotic chemical classes outside the small molecule / lipid / peptide scope. The acquisition platform is not traveling-wave IM-MS (e.g., drift-tube IM-MS or TIMS), since the power-law calibrations and arrival-time-to-TWCCSN2 relationships are TWIM-specific.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Automated identification of ROIs is needed — this is beyond the scope of the current program; ROIs must be user-defined. skills.search_text: biosynthetic-domain-curation-via-ec-annotation Use when tokenised BGCs (antiSMASH-detected, (sub)Pfam-annotated) contain non-biosynthetic domains that must be removed prior to sub-cluster prediction or redundancy filtering. The BGCs are already tokenised and contain only biosynthetic Pfams/subPfams (e.g. already processed with this skill) — re-filtering would double-remove rare domains. The dataset is too small for frequency-based thresholds to be meaningful (e.g. a single genome or a small MIBiG-only analysis), where dropping Pfams occurring <3 times could strip real biosynthetic signal. The analysis requires non-biosynthetic domains (e.g. tailoring or regulatory-gene annotation) rather than biosynthetic sub-cluster discovery. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Curation step that restricts tokenised BGC genes to the 1,839 biosynthetic Pfams curated via ECDomainMiner, removes non-biosynthetic domains and rare Pfams (<3 occurrences), and discards BGCs with fewer than two non-empty genes before redundancy filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462

skills.search_text: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-error-detection Use when auditing MIBiG or similar BGC records whose linked natural-product structure (PubChem or NP Atlas SMILES) may mismatch the cluster's annotated biosynthesis, e.g. before reusing characterised BGC-structure pairs for benchmarking or training. No characterised reference structure exists for the cluster (i.e. the entry lacks an associated natural product SMILES), so there is nothing to compare RAIChU's drawn product against. Goal is predicting mature natural products from raw antiSMASH output: RAIChU can generate natural product scaffolds but not mature natural products, so fingerprinting-based structure validation was considered but not implemented by the authors. The task requires predicting regio- and stereochemistry of tailoring reactions — these cannot be predicted and users must specify their reaction targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Batch-run RAIChU (backed by PIKAChU's chemically-correct intermediate drawing) over every entry of a BGC database such as MIBiG to catch processing errors and flag records whose linked structure SMILES (PubChem/NP Atlas) disagrees with the cluster's biosynthesis, as demonstrated by the colistin A wrong-PubChem-entry discrepancy. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00898-x

skills.when_to_use_negative: No characterised reference structure exists for the cluster (i.e. the entry lacks an associated natural product SMILES), so there is nothing to compare RAIChU's drawn product against. skills.summary: Validates the syntactic correctness of SMILES strings annotating compound structures and protein-domain substrates in MIBiG 3.0 JSON entries by parsing them with the PIKAChU toolkit, so that chemical structure annotation in a BGC database is machine-readable and error-free.
