skills.description: Use when a batch of MS/MS spectra (e.g. .mgf exports from HILIC- or CSH-Q Exactive HF runs) has been assigned putative compound names at MSI level 3 and you need chemical-ontology class distributions or enrichment statistics rather than single-compound IDs.
skills.name: chemical-class-enrichment-statistics
skills.search_text: chemical-class-enrichment-statistics Use when a batch of MS/MS spectra (e.g. .mgf exports from HILIC- or CSH-Q Exactive HF runs) has been assigned putative compound names at MSI level 3 and you need chemical-ontology class distributions or enrichment statistics rather than single-compound IDs. The compounds are already identified at MSI level 1 or 2 with authentic standards or library MS/MS matches — classification of those verified IDs does not require in-silico class inference and pooling them with level 3 calls inflates confidence. The input is raw LC-MS/MS data (e.g. Thermo .raw or mzML) rather than a list of annotated structures — spectral deconvolution and database search must run first. Only a handful of compounds are being analyzed — enrichment statistics over 21 superclasses/184 classes are unreliable on small compound counts; prefer full per-compound ClassyFire annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Classify MSI level 3 structure annotations from hybrid/in-silico spectral search into the ClassyFire ontology (21 superclasses, 184 chemical classes) and compute class proportions/enrichment statistics over the previously unannotated portion of the urine metabolome. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Classify MSI level 3 structure annotations from hybrid/in-silico spectral search into the ClassyFire ontology (21 superclasses, 184 chemical classes) and compute class proportions/enrichment statistics over the previously unannotated portion of the urine metabolome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compounds are already identified at MSI level 1 or 2 with authentic standards or library MS/MS matches — classification of those verified IDs does not require in-silico class inference and pooling them with level 3 calls inflates confidence. The input is raw LC-MS/MS data (e.g. Thermo .raw or mzML) rather than a list of annotated structures — spectral deconvolution and database search must run first. Only a handful of compounds are being analyzed — enrichment statistics over 21 superclasses/184 classes are unreliable on small compound counts; prefer full per-compound ClassyFire annotation.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of metabolites identified by NMR (Chenomx) or similar profiling and need to report the chemical-class composition as fractions/percentages of the total detected metabolome.
skills.name: chemical-class-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: chemical-class-fraction-quantification Use when you have a list of metabolites identified by NMR (Chenomx) or similar profiling and need to report the chemical-class composition as fractions/percentages of the total detected metabolome. You need pathway-level or network analysis (e.g., MetaboLINK PCA-GLASSO sub-networks) rather than simple chemical-class fractions. Your metabolite list lacks resolvable identities (no Chenomx/HMDB match), so classes cannot be assigned reliably. You want relative concentration changes across developmental stages rather than static composition of the detected metabolome. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotates each metabolite in a detected-metabolome list (e.g., n = 90 metabolites identified via Chenomx 800 MHz NMR peak matching) with its chemical class using HMDB, then tallies per-class counts and computes percentages of the total metabolome to describe class composition (e.g., Figure 2C: 25% amino acids, 18.2% bioenergetics, 18.2% peptides, 11.4% carbohydrates). metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fnins.2024.1520982
skills.summary: Annotates each metabolite in a detected-metabolome list (e.g., n = 90 metabolites identified via Chenomx 800 MHz NMR peak matching) with its chemical class using HMDB, then tallies per-class counts and computes percentages of the total metabolome to describe class composition (e.g., Figure 2C: 25% amino acids, 18.2% bioenergetics, 18.2% peptides, 11.4% carbohydrates).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need pathway-level or network analysis (e.g., MetaboLINK PCA-GLASSO sub-networks) rather than simple chemical-class fractions. Your metabolite list lacks resolvable identities (no Chenomx/HMDB match), so classes cannot be assigned reliably. You want relative concentration changes across developmental stages rather than static composition of the detected metabolome.

skills.description: Use when an aligned annotated molecular formula table (from IDSL.UFA) contains many related formulas and the goal is to collapse them into homologous formula-class clusters (e.g., perfluorinated, halogenated, or lipid chain families) rather than treating each peak independently.
skills.name: chemical-class-grouping-analysis
skills.search_text: chemical-class-grouping-analysis Use when an aligned annotated molecular formula table (from IDSL.UFA) contains many related formulas and the goal is to collapse them into homologous formula-class clusters (e.g., perfluorinated, halogenated, or lipid chain families) rather than treating each peak independently. Input is a raw mzML/mzXML/netCDF file or a peaklist without assigned molecular formulas — class grouping requires formulas as input, not raw MS1 spectra The analysis goal is per-peak molecular formula assignment (candidate ranking against theoretical isotopic profiles) — that is the IDSL.UFA annotation step, not the downstream class-grouping step The chemical space contains only isolated, non-homologous compounds with no constant ΔH/ΔC progressions or shared fixed-carbon Σ(H+halogen) patterns — grouping will yield mostly ungrouped formulas and adds little interpretive value http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Groups annotated molecular formulas into chemical-class sub-structure clusters using IDSL.UFA's class-detection rules: chain progressions defined by constant ΔH/ΔC ratios (2 for polymeric, 1/2 for cyclic chains) and fixed-carbon classes with a constant sum of H plus halogens (Br, Cl, F, I), as used to recover PCB and PBDE homologous series. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00563
skills.summary: Groups annotated molecular formulas into chemical-class sub-structure clusters using IDSL.UFA's class-detection rules: chain progressions defined by constant ΔH/ΔC ratios (2 for polymeric, 1/2 for cyclic chains) and fixed-carbon classes with a constant sum of H plus halogens (Br, Cl, F, I), as used to recover PCB and PBDE homologous series.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw mzML/mzXML/netCDF file or a peaklist without assigned molecular formulas — class grouping requires formulas as input, not raw MS1 spectra The analysis goal is per-peak molecular formula assignment (candidate ranking against theoretical isotopic profiles) — that is the IDSL.UFA annotation step, not the downstream class-grouping step The chemical space contains only isolated, non-homologous compounds with no constant ΔH/ΔC progressions or shared fixed-carbon Σ(H+halogen) patterns — grouping will yield mostly ungrouped formulas and adds little interpretive value

skills.description: Decision support for prioritizing natural extracts whose MS/MS-derived chemical taxonomy (CANOPUS/NPC classes) contains classes absent from literature reports for the same species or genus, as one of four components in Inventa's Priority Score ranking.
skills.name: chemical-class-novelty-scoring
skills.search_text: chemical-class-novelty-scoring Decision support for prioritizing natural extracts whose MS/MS-derived chemical taxonomy (CANOPUS/NPC classes) contains classes absent from literature reports for the same species or genus, as one of four components in Inventa's Priority Score ranking. No CANOPUS/SIRIUS chemical-taxonomy annotations are available for the feature set — CC cannot be computed and the run degrades to the Feature Component (FC) only The taxon already has extensive literature-reported chemistry and the goal is literature-gap assessment rather than unreported-class detection — the Literature Component (LC) is the appropriate score http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Inventa's Class Component (CC), which flags extracts containing a CANOPUS-predicted chemical class not yet reported in the literature for that species or genus, contributing up to 1.0 (0.5 species + 0.5 genus novelty) to the Priority Score. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Computes Inventa's Class Component (CC), which flags extracts containing a CANOPUS-predicted chemical class not yet reported in the literature for that species or genus, contributing up to 1.0 (0.5 species + 0.5 genus novelty) to the Priority Score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No CANOPUS/SIRIUS chemical-taxonomy annotations are available for the feature set — CC cannot be computed and the run degrades to the Feature Component (FC) only The taxon already has extensive literature-reported chemistry and the goal is literature-gap assessment rather than unreported-class detection — the Literature Component (LC) is the appropriate score

skills.description: Use when NPLinker has produced candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links (e.g., via standardised Metcalf scoring) and you need to filter false positives by matching genome-based and structure-based chemical class ontologies.
skills.name: chemical-class-ontology-lookup-scoring
skills.search_text: chemical-class-ontology-lookup-scoring Use when NPLinker has produced candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links (e.g., via standardised Metcalf scoring) and you need to filter false positives by matching genome-based and structure-based chemical class ontologies. Candidate links lack any CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer structure-based class prediction and filter_missing_scores is enabled, since 1988 spectra without predictions would be discarded Large metabolites above the CANOPUS 850 Da mass cut-off, where Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore-style methods may be better suited You need to discover links de novo rather than prioritise existing Metcalf-scored candidates — this score complements, not replaces, co-occurrence-based scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 NPClassScore is an empirical chemical-class matching score that bridges genome-based BGC classes (from antiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE) and structure-based compound classes (from CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer) using precomputed MIBiG 2.0-derived frequency tables, implemented in NPLinker to prioritise and filter candidate BGC–MS/MS links. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: NPClassScore is an empirical chemical-class matching score that bridges genome-based BGC classes (from antiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE) and structure-based compound classes (from CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer) using precomputed MIBiG 2.0-derived frequency tables, implemented in NPLinker to prioritise and filter candidate BGC–MS/MS links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate links lack any CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer structure-based class prediction and filter_missing_scores is enabled, since 1988 spectra without predictions would be discarded Large metabolites above the CANOPUS 850 Da mass cut-off, where Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore-style methods may be better suited You need to discover links de novo rather than prioritise existing Metcalf-scored candidates — this score complements, not replaces, co-occurrence-based scoring

skills.name: chemical-class-propagation-onto-networks
skills.search_text: chemical-class-propagation-onto-networks Use when a GNPS molecular network plus an MS2LDA experiment exist and molecular families lack GNPS spectral library matches, so NAP/DEREPLICATOR annotations and ClassyFire classes can be propagated onto nodes/edges to reach MSI annotation level 3. Input is already a feature table without a molecular network or component index — the motif mapping requires network components (network component index) and shared motifs between connected nodes. No MS2LDA experiment exists and you only need compound classes without substructure motifs — use a chemical-class-only mapping rather than the full motif-propagation pipeline. Molecular families are already adequately annotated by GNPS spectral library matches at MSI level 2, making in silico propagation unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 MolNetEnhancer-style workflow that merges molecular networking (GNPS), MS2LDA Mass2Motifs, in silico structure annotations (NAP/DEREPLICATOR), and ClassyFire chemical classification to propagate compound-class and substructure information across molecular families, raising annotation from single GNPS library hits to MSI level 3 (e.g. 73 Euphorbia diterpenoid features). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: MolNetEnhancer-style workflow that merges molecular networking (GNPS), MS2LDA Mass2Motifs, in silico structure annotations (NAP/DEREPLICATOR), and ClassyFire chemical classification to propagate compound-class and substructure information across molecular families, raising annotation from single GNPS library hits to MSI level 3 (e.g. 73 Euphorbia diterpenoid features).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table without a molecular network or component index — the motif mapping requires network components (network component index) and shared motifs between connected nodes. No MS2LDA experiment exists and you only need compound classes without substructure motifs — use a chemical-class-only mapping rather than the full motif-propagation pipeline. Molecular families are already adequately annotated by GNPS spectral library matches at MSI level 2, making in silico propagation unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you have a canopus_npc_summary.tsv from a recomputed SIRIUS project space plus taxon-level reported-class tables and want to flag extracts whose predicted chemical classes are novel to the species or genus.
skills.name: chemical-class-set-comparison-across-taxonomic-levels
skills.search_text: chemical-class-set-comparison-across-taxonomic-levels Use when you have a canopus_npc_summary.tsv from a recomputed SIRIUS project space plus taxon-level reported-class tables and want to flag extracts whose predicted chemical classes are novel to the species or genus. The extract set has no CANOPUS/NPClassifier output — CC requires predicted chemical classes, not just GNPS annotations; without canopus_npc_summary.tsv you can only compute FC and LC. The goal is novelty of individual compounds rather than chemical classes — the LC component, not CC, handles reported-compound fractions at species/genus/family level. You only want spectral similarity grouping of extracts — the SC component using the MEMO metric serves that, independent of class or literature information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Compute Inventa's Class Component (CC) score by string-set-comparing CANOPUS/NPClassifier predicted chemical classes (filtered by min_class_confidence = 0.8 and min_recurrence = 5) against classes reported in the literature for the extract's species and genus, scoring CCs = 0.5 and CCg = 0.5 when a predicted class is unreported at each level (CC range 0–1). metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Compute Inventa's Class Component (CC) score by string-set-comparing CANOPUS/NPClassifier predicted chemical classes (filtered by min_class_confidence = 0.8 and min_recurrence = 5) against classes reported in the literature for the extract's species and genus, scoring CCs = 0.5 and CCg = 0.5 when a predicted class is unreported at each level (CC range 0–1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The extract set has no CANOPUS/NPClassifier output — CC requires predicted chemical classes, not just GNPS annotations; without canopus_npc_summary.tsv you can only compute FC and LC. The goal is novelty of individual compounds rather than chemical classes — the LC component, not CC, handles reported-compound fractions at species/genus/family level. You only want spectral similarity grouping of extracts — the SC component using the MEMO metric serves that, independent of class or literature information.

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular network (classical or feature-based) needs chemically interpretable node annotation — e.g., nodes colored by CF_subclass in Cytoscape — after spectral library/in silico annotation steps are complete.
skills.name: chemical-class-taxonomy-integration
skills.search_text: chemical-class-taxonomy-integration Use when a GNPS molecular network (classical or feature-based) needs chemically interpretable node annotation — e.g., nodes colored by CF_subclass in Cytoscape — after spectral library/in silico annotation steps are complete. Input is a raw mass spectrometry file (MGF/mzML) rather than an already-created GNPS molecular network — network creation through GNPS must happen first The goal is structural motif discovery (substructureannotation) rather than chemical class assignment — use the MS2LDA motif-mapping workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Integrates automated chemical class taxonomy (ClassyFire annotations) into mass spectral molecular networks so nodes carry CF-prefixed class/subclass columns, using pyMolNetEnhancer to merge class assignments with the GNPS network graph for Cytoscape visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Integrates automated chemical class taxonomy (ClassyFire annotations) into mass spectral molecular networks so nodes carry CF-prefixed class/subclass columns, using pyMolNetEnhancer to merge class assignments with the GNPS network graph for Cytoscape visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw mass spectrometry file (MGF/mzML) rather than an already-created GNPS molecular network — network creation through GNPS must happen first The goal is structural motif discovery (substructureannotation) rather than chemical class assignment — use the MS2LDA motif-mapping workflow instead

skills.description: Reference for constructing or auditing a chemical classification dictionary — when you must choose preferred labels and synonyms for chemical classes (e.g. resolving 'Imidazolines' vs 'Dihydroimidazoles') rather than classify individual structures.
skills.name: chemical-class-term-curation
skills.search_text: chemical-class-term-curation Reference for constructing or auditing a chemical classification dictionary — when you must choose preferred labels and synonyms for chemical classes (e.g. resolving 'Imidazolines' vs 'Dihydroimidazoles') rather than classify individual structures. Input is a set of molecular structures needing class assignment — use ClassyFire's rule-based classification instead; this skill only curates category terminology. The taxonomy already carries stable preferred labels and synonyms and you are not auditing term choices or adding mappings. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Curates the terminology layer of a computable chemical taxonomy: for each of the 4825 ChemOnt categories, it selects a preferred English term (favoured by IUPAC naming, expert-panel recommendation, and recorded usage frequency) and attaches the losing candidate names as synonyms, yielding roughly 9012 English synonyms plus a text definition per node. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Curates the terminology layer of a computable chemical taxonomy: for each of the 4825 ChemOnt categories, it selects a preferred English term (favoured by IUPAC naming, expert-panel recommendation, and recorded usage frequency) and attaches the losing candidate names as synonyms, yielding roughly 9012 English synonyms plus a text definition per node.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a set of molecular structures needing class assignment — use ClassyFire's rule-based classification instead; this skill only curates category terminology. The taxonomy already carries stable preferred labels and synonyms and you are not auditing term choices or adding mappings.

skills.description: Use when an article reports compound-classification counts per database (e.g. '>60,000,000 molecules in PubChem') and these per-database thresholds must be compiled into a verifiable table or CSV without converting them to exact figures.
skills.name: chemical-classification-benchmark-reporting
skills.search_text: chemical-classification-benchmark-reporting Use when an article reports compound-classification counts per database (e.g. '>60,000,000 molecules in PubChem') and these per-database thresholds must be compiled into a verifiable table or CSV without converting them to exact figures. The article reports exact per-compound annotation counts (not comparative thresholds like '>42,000 molecules'), in which case raw numeric extraction without marker handling is sufficient. The goal is to evaluate classification accuracy (e.g. comparing ClassyFire assignments against ChEBI ontology classes via the ontology lookup table) rather than report annotation volumes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Extracts the reported ClassyFire annotation volumes for named chemical databases (ChEBI, DrugBank, HMDB, LIPID MAPS, PubChem), preserves the comparative-quantity markers ('>'), and assembles them into a verified per-database table for benchmark reporting. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Extracts the reported ClassyFire annotation volumes for named chemical databases (ChEBI, DrugBank, HMDB, LIPID MAPS, PubChem), preserves the comparative-quantity markers ('>'), and assembles them into a verified per-database table for benchmark reporting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article reports exact per-compound annotation counts (not comparative thresholds like '>42,000 molecules'), in which case raw numeric extraction without marker handling is sufficient. The goal is to evaluate classification accuracy (e.g. comparing ClassyFire assignments against ChEBI ontology classes via the ontology lookup table) rather than report annotation volumes.

skills.description: Use when you need to enumerate the compound library of a PeakForest instance (e.g. a MetaboHUB demonstrator) and extract per-compound metadata into a flat table for inventory, curation, or downstream annotation reuse.
skills.name: chemical-compound-metadata-extraction
skills.search_text: chemical-compound-metadata-extraction Use when you need to enumerate the compound library of a PeakForest instance (e.g. a MetaboHUB demonstrator) and extract per-compound metadata into a flat table for inventory, curation, or downstream annotation reuse. You need raw spectral data storage or extraction — PeakForest stores metadata related to raw data rather than raw data itself and is designed for metabolite annotation report data Your input data is not cleaned: PeakForest expects users to supply completely-cleaned data following team-edited SOPs and does not include data clean-up or extraction tools You are annotating spectra rather than inventorying the compound library — use external peak matching tools for annotation in biological matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Extracts chemical compound records (identifiers, names, and structural/spectral metadata) from a PeakForest instance via its REST Web services and assembles them into a tab-separated, one-row-per-compound table. This mirrors the demonstrator workflow that reproduced the PeakForest compound collection of 96 biologically relevant compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
skills.summary: Extracts chemical compound records (identifiers, names, and structural/spectral metadata) from a PeakForest instance via its REST Web services and assembles them into a tab-separated, one-row-per-compound table. This mirrors the demonstrator workflow that reproduced the PeakForest compound collection of 96 biologically relevant compounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need raw spectral data storage or extraction — PeakForest stores metadata related to raw data rather than raw data itself and is designed for metabolite annotation report data Your input data is not cleaned: PeakForest expects users to supply completely-cleaned data following team-edited SOPs and does not include data clean-up or extraction tools You are annotating spectra rather than inventorying the compound library — use external peak matching tools for annotation in biological matrices

skills.description: Use when batch-importing large compound lists into PeakForest from the compound-import template file (XLSX, Online Resource 2) and each row must be checked for the mandatory common name, InChI and InChIKey fields before creating compound cards.
skills.name: chemical-compound-record-field-validation
skills.search_text: chemical-compound-record-field-validation Use when batch-importing large compound lists into PeakForest from the compound-import template file (XLSX, Online Resource 2) and each row must be checked for the mandatory common name, InChI and InChIKey fields before creating compound cards. Input is not the compound-import template but raw spectral data files — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data, and this skill only validates compound metadata fields. Only a few compounds need entering — the batch template import and its validation module target large compound lists; single compounds can be imported via the web interface. Rows lack structural identifiers (InChI/InChIKey) and cannot be completed beforehand — the import function will not operate, so records should be curated upstream instead. A validation and serialization procedure for PeakForest's batch compound-import module: it parses an XLSX compound-import template, checks each row against the mandatory fields of the PeakForest chemical compound entity (common name, InChI, InChIKey), and emits structured compound records for database ingestion. It exists to guarantee that only complete, well-formed compound metadata enters a PeakForest instance. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
skills.summary: A validation and serialization procedure for PeakForest's batch compound-import module: it parses an XLSX compound-import template, checks each row against the mandatory fields of the PeakForest chemical compound entity (common name, InChI, InChIKey), and emits structured compound records for database ingestion. It exists to guarantee that only complete, well-formed compound metadata enters a PeakForest instance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not the compound-import template but raw spectral data files — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data, and this skill only validates compound metadata fields. Only a few compounds need entering — the batch template import and its validation module target large compound lists; single compounds can be imported via the web interface. Rows lack structural identifiers (InChI/InChIKey) and cannot be completed beforehand — the import function will not operate, so records should be curated upstream instead.

skills.description: Use when running VInSMoC on run.npanalysis.org and you must pick which chemical database to search against, or associate an uploaded spectrum file with a project so it can serve as input to a database-search task.
skills.name: chemical-database-candidate-selection
skills.search_text: chemical-database-candidate-selection Use when running VInSMoC on run.npanalysis.org and you must pick which chemical database to search against, or associate an uploaded spectrum file with a project so it can serve as input to a database-search task. The uploaded spectrum file has not yet been parsed successfully (pending or error status) — do not associate or use it as input until parsing completes. The task uses a custom pre-processed local database workflow rather than the run.npanalysis.org project data table, since association of databases to projects is done through that interface. The goal is a standalone chemical-library build (e.g. in silico fragmentation outside VInSMoC) rather than selecting candidates for VInSMoC spectral search. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Select and associate an appropriate chemical database (e.g. NPAtlas, PubChem, COCONUT) as the candidate-molecule library for VInSMoC mass-spectral database search, and couple it with a parsed mass spectrum file (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) in a project on run.npanalysis.org. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Select and associate an appropriate chemical database (e.g. NPAtlas, PubChem, COCONUT) as the candidate-molecule library for VInSMoC mass-spectral database search, and couple it with a parsed mass spectrum file (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) in a project on run.npanalysis.org.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The uploaded spectrum file has not yet been parsed successfully (pending or error status) — do not associate or use it as input until parsing completes. The task uses a custom pre-processed local database workflow rather than the run.npanalysis.org project data table, since association of databases to projects is done through that interface. The goal is a standalone chemical-library build (e.g. in silico fragmentation outside VInSMoC) rather than selecting candidates for VInSMoC spectral search.

skills.description: Use when a database release claims compound structure coverage (e.g. '1188 structures with SMILES', '1347→1860 BGCs with structure data') and you need to reproduce those counts and per-database cross-link tallies.
skills.name: chemical-database-crosslink-counting
skills.search_text: chemical-database-crosslink-counting Use when a database release claims compound structure coverage (e.g. '1188 structures with SMILES', '1347→1860 BGCs with structure data') and you need to reproduce those counts and per-database cross-link tallies. The goal is annotating new BGCs or discovering structures, not auditing existing coverage counts — use antiSMASH/PIKAChU annotation workflows instead The input is not entry-level structured records (e.g. raw GenBank sequences without compound fields), so no SMILES or cross-link fields exist to tally Only one chemical database is of interest and no global coverage or per-database comparison is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies chemical structure annotation coverage in a BGC database by parsing entry-level records for SMILES strings and tallying cross-links to chemical structure databases, as done for MIBiG 3.0 across NP Atlas, PubChem, ChemSpider, LOTUS, and ChEMBL. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Quantifies chemical structure annotation coverage in a BGC database by parsing entry-level records for SMILES strings and tallying cross-links to chemical structure databases, as done for MIBiG 3.0 across NP Atlas, PubChem, ChemSpider, LOTUS, and ChEMBL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating new BGCs or discovering structures, not auditing existing coverage counts — use antiSMASH/PIKAChU annotation workflows instead The input is not entry-level structured records (e.g. raw GenBank sequences without compound fields), so no SMILES or cross-link fields exist to tally Only one chemical database is of interest and no global coverage or per-database comparison is needed

skills.description: Use when curating or auditing a natural product database where each BGC record has an associated product structure (e.g. MIBiG/PubChem links), and you need to detect entries whose linked SMILES/structure mismatches the biosynthetically predicted product.
skills.name: chemical-database-curation
skills.search_text: chemical-database-curation Use when curating or auditing a natural product database where each BGC record has an associated product structure (e.g. MIBiG/PubChem links), and you need to detect entries whose linked SMILES/structure mismatches the biosynthetically predicted product. Records where the product is a scaffold rather than a mature natural product — RAIChU cannot generate mature natural products from raw antiSMASH output, so predicted and real-world structures may not have high fingerprinting similarity Database audits requiring fully automated structure validation of all BGCs — fingerprinting-based automatic validation (e.g. Morgan fingerprinting) was considered but not implemented; validation relied on manual curation of select examples http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Batch-validate biosynthetic gene cluster entries in a chemical reference database (MIBiG) by re-drawing each annotated product with RAIChU and comparing the drawn structure to the linked reference (PubChem SMILES), surfacing wrong-structure links such as the colistin A entry. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00898-x
skills.summary: Batch-validate biosynthetic gene cluster entries in a chemical reference database (MIBiG) by re-drawing each annotated product with RAIChU and comparing the drawn structure to the linked reference (PubChem SMILES), surfacing wrong-structure links such as the colistin A entry.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Records where the product is a scaffold rather than a mature natural product — RAIChU cannot generate mature natural products from raw antiSMASH output, so predicted and real-world structures may not have high fingerprinting similarity Database audits requiring fully automated structure validation of all BGCs — fingerprinting-based automatic validation (e.g. Morgan fingerprinting) was considered but not implemented; validation relied on manual curation of select examples

skills.description: Use when reproducing or verifying aggregate counts of a curated chemical database assembled from multiple public sources, or when reconciling per-source entry totals against published unique-molecule statistics after deduplication.
skills.name: chemical-database-curation-audit
skills.search_text: chemical-database-curation-audit Use when reproducing or verifying aggregate counts of a curated chemical database assembled from multiple public sources, or when reconciling per-source entry totals against published unique-molecule statistics after deduplication. Input is already a deduplicated unique-molecule table rather than per-source raw counts — the reconciliation logic would not apply The target database lacks published aggregate statistics (flat vs. stereo totals) to reconcile against, so no audit target exists The analysis goal is structural annotation or property computation (descriptors, fingerprints, classification) rather than count-level database assembly verification http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Audits the assembly of a large aggregated chemical database (here, COCONUT) by rebuilding per-source entry counts, reproducing the aggregation and deduplication logic (stereo-less InChIKey unification), and reconciling computed totals against reported release statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00478-9
skills.summary: Audits the assembly of a large aggregated chemical database (here, COCONUT) by rebuilding per-source entry counts, reproducing the aggregation and deduplication logic (stereo-less InChIKey unification), and reconciling computed totals against reported release statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a deduplicated unique-molecule table rather than per-source raw counts — the reconciliation logic would not apply The target database lacks published aggregate statistics (flat vs. stereo totals) to reconcile against, so no audit target exists The analysis goal is structural annotation or property computation (descriptors, fingerprints, classification) rather than count-level database assembly verification

skills.description: Use when a curated chemical/adduct database is distributed as structure files (.mol/.cdxml) plus a spreadsheet, and you must verify identifier columns are populated and reproducible entry-by-entry.
skills.name: chemical-database-field-completeness-checking
skills.search_text: chemical-database-field-completeness-checking Use when a curated chemical/adduct database is distributed as structure files (.mol/.cdxml) plus a spreadsheet, and you must verify identifier columns are populated and reproducible entry-by-entry. The input structures already carry canonical identifiers and the goal is spectral matching or fragment prediction (CFM-ID) rather than identifier completeness auditing No machine-readable structure files (.mol) are available, so identifiers cannot be independently regenerated and only presence/absence can be checked The task is generating new identifiers for novel adducts rather than auditing an existing deposited database http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Batch-validates that every chemical database entry carries populated, machine-readable structural identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) by regenerating them from deposited .mol files with Open Babel 3.1.1 and diffing against the deposited .xlsx fields. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Batch-validates that every chemical database entry carries populated, machine-readable structural identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) by regenerating them from deposited .mol files with Open Babel 3.1.1 and diffing against the deposited .xlsx fields.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input structures already carry canonical identifiers and the goal is spectral matching or fragment prediction (CFM-ID) rather than identifier completeness auditing No machine-readable structure files (.mol) are available, so identifiers cannot be independently regenerated and only presence/absence can be checked The task is generating new identifiers for novel adducts rather than auditing an existing deposited database

skills.description: Use when raw mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a candidate chemical database (e.g., NPAtlas, COCONUT, PubChem) and the VInSMoC task parameters need to be set to match the input spectra's ion mode, precursor m/z, and expected adducts.
skills.name: chemical-database-search-configuration
skills.search_text: chemical-database-search-configuration Use when raw mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a candidate chemical database (e.g., NPAtlas, COCONUT, PubChem) and the VInSMoC task parameters need to be set to match the input spectra's ion mode, precursor m/z, and expected adducts. The input has already been pre-processed (peaks merged/filtered) — in that case the advanced peak merging and peak filtering settings should not be re-applied, per the README The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than scoring spectra against a database of candidate molecules The input file format is not MGF, mzXML, or mzML or does not match the declared extension (parsing will report an error status) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Configuring a VInSMoC mass spectral database search task — choosing search mode, fragmentation mode, ion mode, precursor/product ion tolerances, maximum absolute charge, minimum score, and spectral preprocessing — so query mass spectra are correctly scored against a chemical database such as COCONUT or NPAtlas. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Configuring a VInSMoC mass spectral database search task — choosing search mode, fragmentation mode, ion mode, precursor/product ion tolerances, maximum absolute charge, minimum score, and spectral preprocessing — so query mass spectra are correctly scored against a chemical database such as COCONUT or NPAtlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input has already been pre-processed (peaks merged/filtered) — in that case the advanced peak merging and peak filtering settings should not be re-applied, per the README The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than scoring spectra against a database of candidate molecules The input file format is not MGF, mzXML, or mzML or does not match the declared extension (parsing will report an error status)

skills.description: Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC spectrum (DeepSAT output) is available and candidates must be retrieved, ranked, and annotated against known-molecule fingerprint databases.
skills.name: chemical-database-structure-retrieval
skills.search_text: chemical-database-structure-retrieval Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC spectrum (DeepSAT output) is available and candidates must be retrieved, ranked, and annotated against known-molecule fingerprint databases. The input is a raw HSQC spectrum rather than an already-predicted Morgan fingerprint — the upstream DeepSAT prediction step must run first. Authentic reference NMR spectra are available and a direct spectral-library search (e.g. peak-shift matching at 0.5 ppm carbon / 0.05 ppm proton tolerance) is the appropriate baseline retrieval. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Retrieve candidate molecular structures for an HSQC query by comparing the DeepSAT-predicted Morgan fingerprint against Morgan fingerprints generated for known small molecules from databases like PubChem, ranking candidates by cosine similarity, and labeling them with cosine-score thresholds (1.0 = identical, >0.8 = similar/annotation). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Retrieve candidate molecular structures for an HSQC query by comparing the DeepSAT-predicted Morgan fingerprint against Morgan fingerprints generated for known small molecules from databases like PubChem, ranking candidates by cosine similarity, and labeling them with cosine-score thresholds (1.0 = identical, >0.8 = similar/annotation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw HSQC spectrum rather than an already-predicted Morgan fingerprint — the upstream DeepSAT prediction step must run first. Authentic reference NMR spectra are available and a direct spectral-library search (e.g. peak-shift matching at 0.5 ppm carbon / 0.05 ppm proton tolerance) is the appropriate baseline retrieval.

skills.search_text: chemical-decontamination-filtering Use when extracting component areas from a spreadOut()-processed GC-MS hit table and you must purge chemicals that lack strong cross-sample library matches, PubChem records, or canonical SMILES before downstream standardization. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 data — uafR's algorithms depend on spectra published in PubChem and do not yet apply to these acquisition modes You need to retain novel or unannotated chemicals that legitimately lack PubChem entries or canonical SMILES — decontamination would silently drop them The vendor export has been renamed from the strict required column names (Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor), which spreadOut() and mzExacto() require unchanged

skills.description: Use when a fitted retention time prediction model (e.g. Retip Keras on HILIC or RPLC) needs interpretation: which molecular descriptors most strongly predict RT, with percentage importance weights.
skills.name: chemical-descriptor-importance-extraction
skills.search_text: chemical-descriptor-importance-extraction Use when a fitted retention time prediction model (e.g. Retip Keras on HILIC or RPLC) needs interpretation: which molecular descriptors most strongly predict RT, with percentage importance weights. When the goal is retention time prediction itself rather than model interpretation — descriptor importances do not replace the prediction pipeline and 1 min MAE precludes discriminating closely eluting compounds in typical 12 min UPLC methods When the target compound domain is outside the training set's chemical landscape (e.g. complex, high molecular weight lipids like triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines were largely excluded from training, so importances may not transfer) When a chromatographic method differs from the training method — the study did not test whether predictions or their descriptor importances can be adjusted for small changes in chromatographic methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts and ranks relative chemical-descriptor importance from machine learning models trained for retention time prediction, as done with Retip's Keras models on the HILIC and RPLC datasets. Reveals which descriptors (e.g. XLogP, ALogP, Basic Group Count) drive retention in each chromatographic mode. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Extracts and ranks relative chemical-descriptor importance from machine learning models trained for retention time prediction, as done with Retip's Keras models on the HILIC and RPLC datasets. Reveals which descriptors (e.g. XLogP, ALogP, Basic Group Count) drive retention in each chromatographic mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is retention time prediction itself rather than model interpretation — descriptor importances do not replace the prediction pipeline and 1 min MAE precludes discriminating closely eluting compounds in typical 12 min UPLC methods When the target compound domain is outside the training set's chemical landscape (e.g. complex, high molecular weight lipids like triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines were largely excluded from training, so importances may not transfer) When a chromatographic method differs from the training method — the study did not test whether predictions or their descriptor importances can be adjusted for small changes in chromatographic methods

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic chemical datasets for multiple samples (e.g. control vs case groups) where each chemical is present in only a subset of samples according to a configurable dropout rate.
skills.name: chemical-dropout-probability-sampling
skills.search_text: chemical-dropout-probability-sampling Use when you need synthetic chemical datasets for multiple samples (e.g. control vs case groups) where each chemical is present in only a subset of samples according to a configurable dropout rate. You need a single shared chemical list with no case-control/dropout design — use ChemicalMixtureCreator for a single chemical dataset instead. You want to simulate the MS/MS acquisition itself (Top-N DDA, SmartROI, WeightedDEW fragmentation schedules) — this skill only produces the per-sample input chemical sets, not scans. You want to extract chemical objects empirically from existing mzML files rather than generate synthetic per-sample mixtures with dropout. Generates per-sample chemical lists for case-control style experiments by applying probabilistic dropout (missing_probability) and intensity-changing (changing_probability) settings to a shared master chemical list, using ViMMS's MultipleMixtureCreator. This lets researchers simulate the biological variability expected across multiple samples before any MS/MS acquisition simulation. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Generates per-sample chemical lists for case-control style experiments by applying probabilistic dropout (missing_probability) and intensity-changing (changing_probability) settings to a shared master chemical list, using ViMMS's MultipleMixtureCreator. This lets researchers simulate the biological variability expected across multiple samples before any MS/MS acquisition simulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a single shared chemical list with no case-control/dropout design — use ChemicalMixtureCreator for a single chemical dataset instead. You want to simulate the MS/MS acquisition itself (Top-N DDA, SmartROI, WeightedDEW fragmentation schedules) — this skill only produces the per-sample input chemical sets, not scans. You want to extract chemical objects empirically from existing mzML files rather than generate synthetic per-sample mixtures with dropout.

skills.search_text: chemical-element-frequency-filtering Use when curating McLean CCS Compendium training data for [M-H]-, [M+H]+ or [M+Na]+ adducts and entries containing rare chemical elements (fewer than five occurrences in the database) must be excluded before model training. When the goal is filtering metabolite annotation candidates by predicted CCS (ΔCCS threshold of 2.8% and 10 ppm mass error) — this skill is a training-set curation step, not an annotation filter When duplicates and m/z outliers have not yet been removed — the element-frequency filter is designed to run after duplicate averaging and the 1 mDa m/z deviation check When the target adduct or molecule class is not represented in the McLean Compendium sheets this filter was designed for (e.g. dimers such as [2M+H]+/[2M-H]-, other less common adducts, or in-source fragments, which the current CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 A data-curation filter from the CCSP 2.0 pipeline that removes McLean Unified CCS Compendium entries containing any chemical element occurring in fewer than five database entries, so that linear support vector regression models are not trained on elements with too few examples. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2022.08.09.503345
skills.summary: A data-curation filter from the CCSP 2.0 pipeline that removes McLean Unified CCS Compendium entries containing any chemical element occurring in fewer than five database entries, so that linear support vector regression models are not trained on elements with too few examples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is filtering metabolite annotation candidates by predicted CCS (ΔCCS threshold of 2.8% and 10 ppm mass error) — this skill is a training-set curation step, not an annotation filter When duplicates and m/z outliers have not yet been removed — the element-frequency filter is designed to run after duplicate averaging and the 1 mDa m/z deviation check When the target adduct or molecule class is not represented in the McLean Compendium sheets this filter was designed for (e.g. dimers such as [2M+H]+/[2M-H]-, other less common adducts, or in-source fragments, which the current CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support)

skills.search_text: chemical-formula-constraint-filtering Use when generating or filtering de novo formula candidates from MS1 precursor masses and you need to know which element-count restrictions are acceptable, or when auditing what fraction of a reference formula set survives candidate-space pruning. When scoring or ranking formula candidates against MS/MS spectra — that is MIST-CF's FastFilter/neural scoring step, not element-space pruning When candidate formulae already come from a database search (e.g. NIST, GNPS, HMDB, PubChem queries) rather than de novo mass decomposition For negative-mode or adduct-switching analyses — MIST-CF models were trained only for positive-mode data and do not consider adduct switching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Applies the SIRIUS mass-decomposition element constraints used by 'SIRIUS decomp' (max 5 S atoms, max 3 P atoms, at most one of each halogen F/Cl/Br/I) to restrict de novo chemical formula candidate generation, and audits how much of a reference formula set (e.g. NPLIB1) remains recoverable under those limits. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Applies the SIRIUS mass-decomposition element constraints used by 'SIRIUS decomp' (max 5 S atoms, max 3 P atoms, at most one of each halogen F/Cl/Br/I) to restrict de novo chemical formula candidate generation, and audits how much of a reference formula set (e.g. NPLIB1) remains recoverable under those limits.

skills.description: Use when featurizing a chemical formula candidate (e.g. a precursor formula from MIST-CF/SIRIUS decomposition) into a fixed-length numerical vector for a neural network, or when reproducing MIST-CF's count-based formula encoder.
skills.name: chemical-formula-count-parsing
skills.search_text: chemical-formula-count-parsing Use when featurizing a chemical formula candidate (e.g. a precursor formula from MIST-CF/SIRIUS decomposition) into a fixed-length numerical vector for a neural network, or when reproducing MIST-CF's count-based formula encoder. The input is already a numeric feature table or embedding — this skill only converts formula strings to counts and embeddings. Only raw spectra are available with no formula candidates — candidate generation (SIRIUS decomp or BUDDY) must happen first. Negative-mode or MS1-only data without an accompanying formula candidate to encode. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses chemical formula strings into per-element integer counts (over the 18 elements MIST-CF considers) and encodes each count via a non-negative sinusoidal embedding, yielding the 144-dimensional Enc(F) vector consumed by the Formula Transformer. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Parses chemical formula strings into per-element integer counts (over the 18 elements MIST-CF considers) and encodes each count via a non-negative sinusoidal embedding, yielding the 144-dimensional Enc(F) vector consumed by the Formula Transformer.

Only raw spectra are available with no formula candidates — candidate generation (SIRIUS decomp or BUDDY) must happen first. Negative-mode or MS1-only data without an accompanying formula candidate to encode.

skills.search_text: chemical-formula-prediction-accuracy-evaluation Use when benchmarking a de novo chemical formula predictor on MS/MS spectra (e.g., NPLIB1 test set) and you need reproducible top-1 accuracy values, especially as a function of how many MS2 peaks are visible to the model. Input spectra are negative-mode, since MIST-CF models were trained only for positive-mode data The goal is prospective benchmarking on CASMI2022 challenge spectra rather than NPLIB1 top-1 accuracy sweeps Spectra are database-searched assignments rather than de novo formula prediction candidates (MIST-CF does not reference spectrum databases) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Evaluates top-1 chemical formula accuracy of MIST-CF on NPLIB1 test spectra, including the Np peak-ablation sweep that restricts each spectrum to its Np highest-intensity subformula-annotated MS2 peaks (Np = 0,1,3,5,10,20,50), with Np=0 serving as the MS1-only baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082

skills.description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra (MGF with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type, collision_energy) from Q-TOF or Orbitrap instruments and need candidate molecular formulas ranked by confidence.
skills.name: chemical-formula-prediction-from-tandem-ms
skills.search_text: chemical-formula-prediction-from-tandem-ms Use when you have MS/MS spectra (MGF with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type, collision_energy) from Q-TOF or Orbitrap instruments and need candidate molecular formulas ranked by confidence. Input is MS1-only data without tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra — BUDDY can handle m/z-only queries but this FIDDLE skill requires MS/MS Spectra are from instruments other than Q-TOF or Orbitrap, or molecules outside the 13 frequent atoms / >1500 m/z / >300 atoms — these are excluded by the paper's data filters Goal is chimeric (co-eluting) spectrum deconvolution — FIDDLE's performance decreases as spectral mixing increases http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Predicts molecular formulas from MS/MS tandem mass spectra using FIDDLE, a deep learning model trained on Q-TOF and Orbitrap spectra, and benchmarks it against SIRIUS (top-down) and BUDDY (bottom-up) by top-1/top-5 formula accuracy. Formulas are the first constraint for structural elucidation of 'dark matter' molecules lacking reference spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Predicts molecular formulas from MS/MS tandem mass spectra using FIDDLE, a deep learning model trained on Q-TOF and Orbitrap spectra, and benchmarks it against SIRIUS (top-down) and BUDDY (bottom-up) by top-1/top-5 formula accuracy. Formulas are the first constraint for structural elucidation of 'dark matter' molecules lacking reference spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is MS1-only data without tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra — BUDDY can handle m/z-only queries but this FIDDLE skill requires MS/MS Spectra are from instruments other than Q-TOF or Orbitrap, or molecules outside the 13 frequent atoms / >1500 m/z / >300 atoms — these are excluded by the paper's data filters Goal is chimeric (co-eluting) spectrum deconvolution — FIDDLE's performance decreases as spectral mixing increases

skills.description: Use when the input is a metabolite with a known chemical formula and the goal is a theoretical isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, ...) under natural or SIP-enriched abundances.
skills.name: chemical-formula-stoichiometry-parsing
skills.search_text: chemical-formula-stoichiometry-parsing Use when the input is a metabolite with a known chemical formula and the goal is a theoretical isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, ...) under natural or SIP-enriched abundances. High-resolution isotopic fine structure is needed — the FFT-based envelope method does not account for fine structure; use Aerith's Monte Carlo multinomial simulation instead The analyte is a peptide rather than a small molecule with a known formula — peptide envelopes are modeled by sequential convolution of monomeric unit (amino acid) isotopic envelopes instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Parses a metabolite molecular formula into per-element stoichiometric counts and uses them to drive FFT-based isotopic envelope simulation in Aerith, where each element's isotope distribution is transformed, raised to its stoichiometric count, and convolved via pointwise frequency-domain multiplication. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Parses a metabolite molecular formula into per-element stoichiometric counts and uses them to drive FFT-based isotopic envelope simulation in Aerith, where each element's isotope distribution is transformed, raised to its stoichiometric count, and convolved via pointwise frequency-domain multiplication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: High-resolution isotopic fine structure is needed — the FFT-based envelope method does not account for fine structure; use Aerith's Monte Carlo multinomial simulation instead The analyte is a peptide rather than a small molecule with a known formula — peptide envelopes are modeled by sequential convolution of monomeric unit (amino acid) isotopic envelopes instead

skills.search_text: chemical-graph-parsing-and-featurization Use when a task requires converting molecular structures (SMILES/MolBlock/SDF from spectral libraries like NIST20) into molecular graphs and heavy-atom-only skeletons H(G) as input to bond-breaking fragmentation or GNN featurization. skills.description: Use when you have a feature table plus MS/MS spectra (MGF) from LC-MS/MS feature detection (e.g. MZmine2/GNPS) and want a fingerprint-based chemical tree for UniFrac-type sample comparison or cross-dataset merging without re-alignment.
skills.name: chemical-hierarchy-construction-from-fingerprints
skills.search_text: chemical-hierarchy-construction-from-fingerprints Use when you have a feature table plus MS/MS spectra (MGF) from LC-MS/MS feature detection (e.g. MZmine2/GNPS) and want a fingerprint-based chemical tree for UniFrac-type sample comparison or cross-dataset merging without re-alignment. Input data lack MS/MS spectra (MS1-only features), since fingerprint prediction requires fragmentation trees and the features would be dropped. You only need spectral-library-match-based annotations for a small percentage of features — in such cases the low annotation coverage may be too sparse to summarize the chemical content of complex samples, and a tree-agnostic metric like Bray-Curtis may suffice. The dataset was already processed into a molecular-network cosine-score hierarchy (e.g. GNPS) and you only want topology-level annotation updates rather than fingerprint-based reconstruction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Builds a chemical hierarchy (Qemistree) over LC-MS/MS features by hierarchically clustering 2936-property molecular fingerprints predicted by SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, so that tree-aware ecology metrics (e.g. Weighted UniFrac) and visualizations in QIIME 2/Empress can be applied to metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00677-3
skills.summary: Builds a chemical hierarchy (Qemistree) over LC-MS/MS features by hierarchically clustering 2936-property molecular fingerprints predicted by SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, so that tree-aware ecology metrics (e.g. Weighted UniFrac) and visualizations in QIIME 2/Empress can be applied to metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lack MS/MS spectra (MS1-only features), since fingerprint prediction requires fragmentation trees and the features would be dropped. You only need spectral-library-match-based annotations for a small percentage of features — in such cases the low annotation coverage may be too sparse to summarize the chemical content of complex samples, and a tree-agnostic metric like Bray-Curtis may suffice. The dataset was already processed into a molecular-network cosine-score hierarchy (e.g. GNPS) and you only want topology-level annotation updates rather than fingerprint-based reconstruction.

skills.description: Use when a .msp mass spectral library file contains records with incomplete metadata (e.g. missing SMILES, InChI, or CAS numbers) and known identifiers that can be converted via public chemical web services.
skills.name: chemical-identifier-conversion-annotation
skills.search_text: chemical-identifier-conversion-annotation Use when a .msp mass spectral library file contains records with incomplete metadata (e.g. missing SMILES, InChI, or CAS numbers) and known identifiers that can be converted via public chemical web services. The input is not a mass spectral library in .msp format (matchms-based IO supports the .msp text format, not general SDF/CSV identifier lists). Records already contain complete metadata and no new identifier fields are required, so no external annotation is needed. No network access is possible and no local conversion applies — the web converters (CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) require live queries; only computed conversions like RDKit molecular weight from SMILES work offline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Annotates records in .msp mass spectral library files with missing chemical metadata (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, IUPAC name, CAS number, formula) by querying external identifier-conversion services (CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) asynchronously and validating results with matchms. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04494

skills.name: chemical-identity-subsetting
skills.search_text: chemical-identity-subsetting Use when you have a categorate() output from uafR and need to reduce a compound list to those matching explicit database, structural, or library-group criteria before downstream GC-MS extraction. Input is a raw GC-MS hit table that has not yet been annotated — run spreadOut() and categorate() first; exactoThese() operates on categorate output, not vendor peak lists You need tentative peak extraction by retention time and match factor from the raw table — use mzExacto() directly with a query chemical vector instead Data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2, which uafR's published-spectrum-dependent algorithms do not yet support http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Subsets chemicals of interest from a uafR categorate() annotation result using exactoThese(), driven by user-specified criteria such as database membership (LOTUS, KEGG, FEMA, FDA_SPL, reactives), FMCS properties, or chemical-library group. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0306202
skills.summary: Subsets chemicals of interest from a uafR categorate() annotation result using exactoThese(), driven by user-specified criteria such as database membership (LOTUS, KEGG, FEMA, FDA_SPL, reactives), FMCS properties, or chemical-library group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw GC-MS hit table that has not yet been annotated — run spreadOut() and categorate() first; exactoThese() operates on categorate output, not vendor peak lists You need tentative peak extraction by retention time and match factor from the raw table — use mzExacto() directly with a query chemical vector instead Data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2, which uafR's published-spectrum-dependent algorithms do not yet support

skills.description: Use when you have one or more trained RNN/CLM checkpoints and need to generate a ranked database of candidate chemical structures (with calculated mass, formula, and InChIKey) whose sampling frequency can prioritize metabolites for discovery.
skills.name: chemical-language-model-sampling
skills.search_text: chemical-language-model-sampling Use when you have one or more trained RNN/CLM checkpoints and need to generate a ranked database of candidate chemical structures (with calculated mass, formula, and InChIKey) whose sampling frequency can prioritize metabolites for discovery. The input is a set of known metabolites to be identified (this skill generates novel candidate structures, not annotations of existing peaks). The trained model was fit to evolutionarily distant chemistries (e.g. plant or bacterial metabolism) where a bespoke model is required. You need MS/MS or retention-time predictions for the generated structures; the article notes predicting these from chemical structures remains an open problem. http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sample large numbers of SMILES strings autoregressively from a trained chemical language model (DeepMet/CLM) across multiple folds and seeds, then aggregate per-molecule sampling frequencies to yield a resource of metabolite-like structures ordered by how often the model emits them. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Sample large numbers of SMILES strings autoregressively from a trained chemical language model (DeepMet/CLM) across multiple folds and seeds, then aggregate per-molecule sampling frequencies to yield a resource of metabolite-like structures ordered by how often the model emits them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a set of known metabolites to be identified (this skill generates novel candidate structures, not annotations of existing peaks). The trained model was fit to evolutionarily distant chemistries (e.g. plant or bacterial metabolism) where a bespoke model is required. You need MS/MS or retention-time predictions for the generated structures; the article notes predicting these from chemical structures remains an open problem.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of tentative compound names (or PubChem CIDs) from GC-MS peak picking and need categorical/functional annotation plus structural matches against labeled chemical categories.
skills.name: chemical-library-categorization-flagging
skills.search_text: chemical-library-categorization-flagging Use when you have a list of tentative compound names (or PubChem CIDs) from GC-MS peak picking and need categorical/functional annotation plus structural matches against labeled chemical categories. Your data are MS2, MS3, or ion-mobility + MS2 spectra — uafR depends on published spectra and does not yet apply to these (deferred until published in PubChem) You need raw peak deconvolution or library matching from vendor output — use Agilent Unknowns Analysis/mzExacto() first; categorate() operates on already tentatively identified compound names Compounds lack published PubChem entries or canonical SMILES — decontamination removes such chemicals before enrichment, so categorate() would return unresolved identities http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Enriches every tentative GC-MS compound with categorical and structural data from PubChem, LOTUS, KEGG, FEMA, MeSH, and FDA/SPL, then flags strong and moderate structural matches against a user-defined chemical library via Tanimoto similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0306202
skills.summary: Enriches every tentative GC-MS compound with categorical and structural data from PubChem, LOTUS, KEGG, FEMA, MeSH, and FDA/SPL, then flags strong and moderate structural matches against a user-defined chemical library via Tanimoto similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are MS2, MS3, or ion-mobility + MS2 spectra — uafR depends on published spectra and does not yet apply to these (deferred until published in PubChem) You need raw peak deconvolution or library matching from vendor output — use Agilent Unknowns Analysis/mzExacto() first; categorate() operates on already tentatively identified compound names Compounds lack published PubChem entries or canonical SMILES — decontamination removes such chemicals before enrichment, so categorate() would return unresolved identities

skills.description: Use when a chemical list extracted from an mzML file (e.g. Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.mzML) or sampled synthetically must be persisted between ViMMS runs so controllers and the Environment can consume it as an alternative chemical source.
skills.name: chemical-list-serialization-pickle
skills.search_text: chemical-list-serialization-pickle Use when a chemical list extracted from an mzML file (e.g. Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.mzML) or sampled synthetically must be persisted between ViMMS runs so controllers and the Environment can consume it as an alternative chemical source. The chemicals are intended as a shareable, language-agnostic artifact — pickle is Python-specific; use an interchange format instead. The chemical set is already available as a persisted pickle from a previous run — reload it rather than re-extracting ROIs from the mzML. The input is not mzML (e.g. aligned MZMine CSVs like multibeers_2_aligned.csv) — ChemicalMixtureFromMZML expects mzML scans for ROI extraction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Persist the list of UnknownChemical objects produced by ViMMS 2.0's ChemicalMixtureFromMZML ROI extraction (or synthetic sampling) to a pickle file via save_obj, so the chemical list can be reloaded and consumed by downstream controllers and the Environment. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Persist the list of UnknownChemical objects produced by ViMMS 2.0's ChemicalMixtureFromMZML ROI extraction (or synthetic sampling) to a pickle file via save_obj, so the chemical list can be reloaded and consumed by downstream controllers and the Environment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chemicals are intended as a shareable, language-agnostic artifact — pickle is Python-specific; use an interchange format instead. skills.search_text: chemical-mixture-configuration Use when you need to produce synthetic chemical datasets (m/z, RT, intensity, formula) for ViMMS 2.0 simulations, either sampled from a database like HMDB or over a uniform m/z range. When the goal is to simulate from empirical data rather than synthetic sampling — extract chemicals from an existing mzML file instead of generating them via ChemicalMixtureCreator When the task is fragmentation-strategy simulation or evaluation (controller classes, Environment, write_mzML) rather than generating the input chemical list When no pickled HMDB compound database or sampler configuration is available and chemical properties cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Configure pluggable formula, RT, intensity and chromatogram samplers and feed them into vimms.Chemicals.ChemicalMixtureCreator to synthetically generate the KnownChemical list that seeds ViMMS 2.0's simulated LC-MS/MS runs. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Configure pluggable formula, RT, intensity and chromatogram samplers and feed them into vimms.Chemicals.ChemicalMixtureCreator to synthetically generate the KnownChemical list that seeds ViMMS 2.0's simulated LC-MS/MS runs.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an MS/MS denoising or spectral-matching algorithm's robustness by deliberately contaminating clean spectra with chemically plausible synthetic noise ions whose intensity can far exceed true fragment ions.
skills.name: chemical-noise-sampling-from-formula-db
skills.search_text: chemical-noise-sampling-from-formula-db Use when benchmarking an MS/MS denoising or spectral-matching algorithm's robustness by deliberately contaminating clean spectra with chemically plausible synthetic noise ions whose intensity can far exceed true fragment ions. The input spectra are already experimental/noisy field data — this skill only manufactures synthetic noise; use the actual spectral_denoising or Denoising Search pipeline instead The mass analyzer is not an Orbitrap instrument — the article notes adapting the method to other mass analyzers requires retuning and validating parameters, so noise-generation thresholds may not transfer No precursor molecular formula or SMILES is available, since formula_denoising and chemically plausible noise sampling both depend on precursor formula information Generates synthetic chemical noise for MS/MS robustness testing by drawing m/z values randomly from a formula_db reference (m/z range 50 to precursor m/z) with Poisson-distributed intensities, then merging the noise ions into clean query spectra via the spectral_denoising package. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Generates synthetic chemical noise for MS/MS robustness testing by drawing m/z values randomly from a formula_db reference (m/z range 50 to precursor m/z) with Poisson-distributed intensities, then merging the noise ions into clean query spectra via the spectral_denoising package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra are already experimental/noisy field data — this skill only manufactures synthetic noise; use the actual spectral_denoising or Denoising Search pipeline instead The mass analyzer is not an Orbitrap instrument — the article notes adapting the method to other mass analyzers requires retuning and validating parameters, so noise-generation thresholds may not transfer No precursor molecular formula or SMILES is available, since formula_denoising and chemically plausible noise sampling both depend on precursor formula information

skills.description: Reference for constructing a synonym table for a chemical taxonomy, especially when resolving competing class names and cross-ontology mappings (ChEBI, LIPID MAPS, MeSH) for classification text.
skills.name: chemical-nomenclature-synonym-mapping
skills.search_text: chemical-nomenclature-synonym-mapping Reference for constructing a synonym table for a chemical taxonomy, especially when resolving competing class names and cross-ontology mappings (ChEBI, LIPID MAPS, MeSH) for classification text. Your ontology is already fully harmonized with the external target vocabulary and every term already carries scoped synonyms — the skill adds value only when alternate or cross-ontology names must be resolved and consolidated. You need to classify individual structures rather than harmonize vocabulary — that is ClassyFire's rule-based structural classification task, not synonym mapping. Names refer to individual compounds rather than chemical classes/categories — synonym resolution at the compound level (e.g. compound names → InChI) is a different task. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3345 Build a comprehensive synonym dictionary that maps alternate chemical class names (including IUPAC, MeSH, and other ontology variants) onto preferred ontology terms, as done for the 4825-category ChemOnt taxonomy underlying ClassyFire. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Build a comprehensive synonym dictionary that maps alternate chemical class names (including IUPAC, MeSH, and other ontology variants) onto preferred ontology terms, as done for the 4825-category ChemOnt taxonomy underlying ClassyFire.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your ontology is already fully harmonized with the external target vocabulary and every term already carries scoped synonyms — the skill adds value only when alternate or cross-ontology names must be resolved and consolidated. You need to classify individual structures rather than harmonize vocabulary — that is ClassyFire's rule-based structural classification task, not synonym mapping. Names refer to individual compounds rather than chemical classes/categories — synonym resolution at the compound level (e.g. compound names → InChI) is a different task.

skills.description: Use when a workflow must persist, reload or hand off ViMMS Chemical objects between pipeline stages — e.g. a chemical mixture generated by ChemicalMixtureCreator needs to be saved as a .p/.pkl file, or a saved chemical dataset is the input to noise/RT-drift perturbation modules.
skills.name: chemical-object-serialisation
skills.search_text: chemical-object-serialisation Use when a workflow must persist, reload or hand off ViMMS Chemical objects between pipeline stages — e.g. a chemical mixture generated by ChemicalMixtureCreator needs to be saved as a .p/.pkl file, or a saved chemical dataset is the input to noise/RT-drift perturbation modules. The object to persist is raw instrument output (mzML scans) rather than a list of Chemical objects — use Environment.write_mzML for scan export instead You need a human-readable or cross-language interchange format; pickle files are Python-specific and tied to the vimms class definitions http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Serialise and round-trip ViMMS chemical datasets (lists of Chemical objects carrying m/z, RT, intensity and chromatogram annotations) as pickle files so they can be loaded by downstream perturbation and simulation steps. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990

skills.description: Use when a deposited, curated natural-products occurrence table (e.g. LOTUS 3_curated/table.tsv.gz from Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5607264) must be tallied for unique structure-organism pairs to validate a reported figure such as 750,000+ pairs.
skills.name: chemical-occurrence-record-deduplication
skills.search_text: chemical-occurrence-record-deduplication Use when a deposited, curated natural-products occurrence table (e.g. LOTUS 3_curated/table.tsv.gz from Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5607264) must be tallied for unique structure-organism pairs to validate a reported figure such as 750,000+ pairs. Input is the raw initial table (2.5M+ pre-validation pairs) rather than the curated 3_curated table — deduplication counts on unharmonized data will not reproduce the reported figures The goal is applying curation/filtering rules (manual validation of 420 pairs, filter_dirty.R, sanitization via MolVS) rather than counting the already-curated output Counts are needed from the Wikidata mirror via SPARQL queries rather than from the deposited flat TSV table Counts unique referenced structure-organism pairs in a curated LOTUS deposit table at full stereochemical (3D) and flat (2D) levels, cross-checking structure and organism tallies to confirm the reported dissemination total of 750,000+ pairs (~30% of 2.5M+ initial pairs). metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
