skills.name: chromatographic-elution-order-comparison
skills.search_text: chromatographic-elution-order-comparison Use when predicted retention times from one chromatographic method (e.g., SMRT reverse-phase) must be made comparable to RTs measured under other experimental methods (e.g., PredRet ECMs), and median absolute projection errors are needed. The experimental RTs and predicted RTs are already on the same chromatographic method/time scale and no cross-method projection is needed Fewer than the ~50 shared molecules with RT in both methods are available for a target ECM, leaving too few points to fit a four-polynomial regression reliably http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Projects deep-learning-model (SMRT DLM) predicted retention times onto independent experimental chromatographic methods by fitting a robust least-squares four-polynomial regression per external chromatographic method (ECM), enabling comparison of predicted and measured RT across chromatographic systems. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Projects deep-learning-model (SMRT DLM) predicted retention times onto independent experimental chromatographic methods by fitting a robust least-squares four-polynomial regression per external chromatographic method (ECM), enabling comparison of predicted and measured RT across chromatographic systems.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental RTs and predicted RTs are already on the same chromatographic method/time scale and no cross-method projection is needed Fewer than the ~50 shared molecules with RT in both methods are available for a target ECM, leaving too few points to fit a four-polynomial regression reliably

skills.description: Use when you have trained retention-time prediction models (e.g. Retip's fit.rf, fit.keras, fit.xgboost, fit.lightgbm, fit.brnn) and experimental RT values for test/validation compounds, and need to quantify what fraction of true positives fall within a fixed RT error window.
skills.name: chromatographic-error-window-coverage-calculation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-error-window-coverage-calculation Use when you have trained retention-time prediction models (e.g. Retip's fit.rf, fit.keras, fit.xgboost, fit.lightgbm, fit.brnn) and experimental RT values for test/validation compounds, and need to quantify what fraction of true positives fall within a fixed RT error window. You are adjusting predictions for small changes in chromatographic methods — the paper explicitly did not test this Predictions are being made outside the chemical landscape of the training set (e.g. high molecular weight lipids like triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines were largely excluded from training) Your chromatographic method uses narrow retention-time search windows in short UPLC runs (e.g. 12 min methods) where 1 min errors cannot discriminate closely eluting compounds http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes and visualizes how well predicted retention times cover true positives within a ±1 min error window across machine learning models (random forest, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras) on HILIC and reversed-phase LC test/validation sets, producing violin plots of prediction error distributions with coverage percentages annotated. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Computes and visualizes how well predicted retention times cover true positives within a ±1 min error window across machine learning models (random forest, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras) on HILIC and reversed-phase LC test/validation sets, producing violin plots of prediction error distributions with coverage percentages annotated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are adjusting predictions for small changes in chromatographic methods — the paper explicitly did not test this Predictions are being made outside the chemical landscape of the training set (e.g. high molecular weight lipids like triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines were largely excluded from training) Your chromatographic method uses narrow retention-time search windows in short UPLC runs (e.g. 12 min methods) where 1 min errors cannot discriminate closely eluting compounds

skills.description: Use when input is MS1-only mzML/mzXML (or imzML) data lacking tandem spectra and the goal is to assemble in-source fragments correlated with a precursor into pseudo MS/MS spectra for structural annotation.
skills.name: chromatographic-feature-correlation-clustering
skills.search_text: chromatographic-feature-correlation-clustering Use when input is MS1-only mzML/mzXML (or imzML) data lacking tandem spectra and the goal is to assemble in-source fragments correlated with a precursor into pseudo MS/MS spectra for structural annotation. Data already contains genuine MS/MS scans — direct library matching of real MS/MS spectra is preferable to pseudo-spectrum reconstruction. Input is an aligned feature table or intensity matrix without raw chromatographic/ion-image traces — correlation clustering needs per-feature XIC or ion-image profiles. Only the spectral-matching step is needed (already have MGF spectra) — use the annotation/matching skill instead of regenerating spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only LC-MS (or MS imaging) data by clustering metabolic features via peak-peak correlation of extracted ion chromatograms or ion images, with isotope peaks excluded, producing MGF files ready for library matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Generates pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only LC-MS (or MS imaging) data by clustering metabolic features via peak-peak correlation of extracted ion chromatograms or ion images, with isotope peaks excluded, producing MGF files ready for library matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data already contains genuine MS/MS scans — direct library matching of real MS/MS spectra is preferable to pseudo-spectrum reconstruction. Input is an aligned feature table or intensity matrix without raw chromatographic/ion-image traces — correlation clustering needs per-feature XIC or ion-image profiles. Only the spectral-matching step is needed (already have MGF spectra) — use the annotation/matching skill instead of regenerating spectra.

skills.description: Use when you have a chromatographic peak table from LC-MS lipidomics (e.g. Compound Discoverer output) with identified lipid features and numerous unidentified features, and you want to filter out co-eluting spurious/redundant features before downstream statistics.
skills.name: chromatographic-feature-correlation-filtering
skills.search_text: chromatographic-feature-correlation-filtering Use when you have a chromatographic peak table from LC-MS lipidomics (e.g. Compound Discoverer output) with identified lipid features and numerous unidentified features, and you want to filter out co-eluting spurious/redundant features before downstream statistics. Input is already a filtered feature table or a feature-abundance matrix without the raw unidentified-feature annotations (RT apex, FWHM, per-sample quantitation) needed to evaluate the RT-window and correlation criteria You want to remove low-abundance or noisy features generally — this filter only removes unidentified features that are tightly correlated with (r ≈ 0.99) a co-eluting identified lipid, not features failing intensity or identification thresholds Working with data formats other than Compound Discoverer (.cdResult/.csv) or mzMine 2 peak tables, or without LipiDex/LipiDex 2's spectral matching results linking lipids to features http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A post-identification filtering skill from the LipiDex/LipiDex 2 Peak Finder that removes unidentified chromatographic features judged to be spurious or redundant byproducts of co-eluting identified lipid features, using retention-time proximity, sample prevalence, and intensity-profile correlation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: A post-identification filtering skill from the LipiDex/LipiDex 2 Peak Finder that removes unidentified chromatographic features judged to be spurious or redundant byproducts of co-eluting identified lipid features, using retention-time proximity, sample prevalence, and intensity-profile correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature table or a feature-abundance matrix without the raw unidentified-feature annotations (RT apex, FWHM, per-sample quantitation) needed to evaluate the RT-window and correlation criteria You want to remove low-abundance or noisy features generally — this filter only removes unidentified features that are tightly correlated with (r ≈ 0.99) a co-eluting identified lipid, not features failing intensity or identification thresholds Working with data formats other than Compound Discoverer (.cdResult/.csv) or mzMine 2 peak tables, or without LipiDex/LipiDex 2's spectral matching results linking lipids to features

skills.description: Use when two peak-detection tools have been run on the same LC-HRMS samples and you must match their detected features, compare peak areas, and quantify correlation (R2) and systematic area-scaling factors.
skills.name: chromatographic-feature-matching
skills.search_text: chromatographic-feature-matching Use when two peak-detection tools have been run on the same LC-HRMS samples and you must match their detected features, compare peak areas, and quantify correlation (R2) and systematic area-scaling factors. Input is centroided-only LC-HRMS data — PeakBot's peak-picking operates on profile-mode data and its area factor quantifies profile-versus-centroid differences You need to train a new PeakBot CNN model rather than compare already-detected features between tools Features have not yet been matched across the two tools and no paired peak-area table exists http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Match and compare chromatographic features detected by PeakBot (machine-learning peak-picking in LC-HRMS profile-mode data) against a second peak-picker such as XCMS, quantifying agreement between the two tools' peak areas. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Match and compare chromatographic features detected by PeakBot (machine-learning peak-picking in LC-HRMS profile-mode data) against a second peak-picker such as XCMS, quantifying agreement between the two tools' peak areas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is centroided-only LC-HRMS data — PeakBot's peak-picking operates on profile-mode data and its area factor quantifies profile-versus-centroid differences You need to train a new PeakBot CNN model rather than compare already-detected features between tools Features have not yet been matched across the two tools and no paired peak-area table exists

skills.summary: Extract per-feature chromatographic metadata (peak areas, metavalues, calibration-fitted parameters) from targeted CE-/GC-/LC-MS(/MS) processing sessions using SmartPeak/pyOpenMS so that downstream calibration, quantitation, and QC can be computed reproducibly.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS/MS MS1 scans (mzML or Bruker .d) and a feature table with complete signal coverage is needed before adduct grouping, alignment, or annotation.
skills.name: chromatographic-feature-table-construction
skills.search_text: chromatographic-feature-table-construction Use when starting from raw LC-MS/MS MS1 scans (mzML or Bruker .d) and a feature table with complete signal coverage is needed before adduct grouping, alignment, or annotation. Input is already an aligned feature table — downstream steps like gap filling or aligned feature grouping reload the .mcraw cache instead Peak detection requiring strict peak-shape quality filtering of features at detection time — MassCube assigns every signal to a feature and imposes no peak-shape requirements; shape-based curation must happen elsewhere Bruker .d data outside the supported profile (e.g. non-TDF2 compression, MsMsType other than 8, non-model-1 m/z calibration, or per-frame pressure-compensated 1/K0) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs MassCube's ROI-based MS1 feature detection: cluster m/z signals across continuous MS1 scans into unique-ion ROIs so that 100% of detected MS1 signals are assigned to a feature, with no requirements on peak shape, signal fluctuation, or scan number. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Reconstructs MassCube's ROI-based MS1 feature detection: cluster m/z signals across continuous MS1 scans into unique-ion ROIs so that 100% of detected MS1 signals are assigned to a feature, with no requirements on peak shape, signal fluctuation, or scan number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table — downstream steps like gap filling or aligned feature grouping reload the .mcraw cache instead Peak detection requiring strict peak-shape quality filtering of features at detection time — MassCube assigns every signal to a feature and imposes no peak-shape requirements; shape-based curation must happen elsewhere Bruker .d data outside the supported profile (e.g. non-TDF2 compression, MsMsType other than 8, non-model-1 m/z calibration, or per-frame pressure-compensated 1/K0)

skills.description: Use when assembling LC-MS mass traces into metabolite isotope features and you must verify that candidate isotope traces co-elute with the monoisotopic trace before accepting a feature hypothesis.
skills.name: chromatographic-fwhm-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: chromatographic-fwhm-overlap-scoring Use when assembling LC-MS mass traces into metabolite isotope features and you must verify that candidate isotope traces co-elute with the monoisotopic trace before accepting a feature hypothesis. Input is already an assembled feature table (use feature linking, e.g. FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT, instead) Traces originate from data lacking continuous chromatographic elution, where FWHM overlap is not defined Identified metabolite isotope profiles must follow a hard-coded theoretical model rather than learned isotope patterns — the SVM approach instead learns plausible metabolite isotope patterns by statistical learning http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Scores candidate isotope-hypothesis co-elution by requiring ≥70% FWHM overlap between mass traces, as part of the FeatureFinderMetabo feature-assembly scoring in OpenMS. Combining this elution-correlation term with m/z-spacing (N_Delta_mz) scoring and SVM classification prevents isotope hypotheses built from non-coeluting traces from being accepted as features. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278
skills.summary: Scores candidate isotope-hypothesis co-elution by requiring ≥70% FWHM overlap between mass traces, as part of the FeatureFinderMetabo feature-assembly scoring in OpenMS. Combining this elution-correlation term with m/z-spacing (N_Delta_mz) scoring and SVM classification prevents isotope hypotheses built from non-coeluting traces from being accepted as features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled feature table (use feature linking, e.g. FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT, instead) Traces originate from data lacking continuous chromatographic elution, where FWHM overlap is not defined Identified metabolite isotope profiles must follow a hard-coded theoretical model rather than learned isotope patterns — the SVM approach instead learns plausible metabolite isotope patterns by statistical learning

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS (mzML/mzXML) data from a gradient run must be reduced to a single separation-performance number (GSI) to evaluate or optimize a chromatographic gradient.
skills.name: chromatographic-gradient-evaluation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-gradient-evaluation Use when raw LC-MS (mzML/mzXML) data from a gradient run must be reduced to a single separation-performance number (GSI) to evaluate or optimize a chromatographic gradient. The task is proposing or optimizing the gradient itself via Bayesian optimization (computeNextGradient/genSearchSpace), not scoring the separation performance of a given gradient's LC-MS run. The goal is MS2-level quality assessment (e.g., spectral purity or dotProd similarity between MS2 spectra with mzTol=0.02) rather than MS1 peak-apex separation encoding. Retention times of top signals are unavailable — e.g., only MS2 or DDA fragment data exist — since SQRTI is defined solely from MS1 retention-time intervals. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Scores LC gradient separation performance by encoding peak apexes of unique compounds into a sum of squared retention-time intervals (SQRTI) and normalizing it to a bounded Global Separation Index (GSI) between 0 and 1, giving Bayesian optimization a single-value objective. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.09.08.556930
skills.summary: Scores LC gradient separation performance by encoding peak apexes of unique compounds into a sum of squared retention-time intervals (SQRTI) and normalizing it to a bounded Global Separation Index (GSI) between 0 and 1, giving Bayesian optimization a single-value objective.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is proposing or optimizing the gradient itself via Bayesian optimization (computeNextGradient/genSearchSpace), not scoring the separation performance of a given gradient's LC-MS run. The goal is MS2-level quality assessment (e.g., spectral purity or dotProd similarity between MS2 spectra with mzTol=0.02) rather than MS1 peak-apex separation encoding. Retention times of top signals are unavailable — e.g., only MS2 or DDA fragment data exist — since SQRTI is defined solely from MS1 retention-time intervals.

skills.description: Use when you must define the candidate LC-MS gradient space before fitting the GP model: you have gradient-definition parameters (dimensionality, time points, mobile-phase settings) and need the constrained gridX/scaledX candidate set.
skills.name: chromatographic-gradient-parameterization
skills.search_text: chromatographic-gradient-parameterization Use when you must define the candidate LC-MS gradient space before fitting the GP model: you have gradient-definition parameters (dimensionality, time points, mobile-phase settings) and need the constrained gridX/scaledX candidate set. When raw LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML) must be processed and separation efficiency computed — that is the downstream evaluation stage (findTopSignals, sepEfficiency), not search-space generation. When experimental data are already available and the task is fitting the Gaussian-process regression model or computing the next gradient via computeNextGradient/computeSecondGradient. When a single predefined gradient needs to be scored; this skill only enumerates the constrained candidate space, it does not evaluate gradients. Generates the first-stage search space of plausible LC gradients for the BAGO framework by enumerating p-dimensional vectors of strong mobile-phase percentage over gradient time points, subject to monotonicity and total-eluting-power constraints. It produces the gridX/scaledX/gradientPct arrays that feed the downstream Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.09.08.556930
skills.summary: Generates the first-stage search space of plausible LC gradients for the BAGO framework by enumerating p-dimensional vectors of strong mobile-phase percentage over gradient time points, subject to monotonicity and total-eluting-power constraints. It produces the gridX/scaledX/gradientPct arrays that feed the downstream Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When raw LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML) must be processed and separation efficiency computed — that is the downstream evaluation stage (findTopSignals, sepEfficiency), not search-space generation. When experimental data are already available and the task is fitting the Gaussian-process regression model or computing the next gradient via computeNextGradient/computeSecondGradient. When a single predefined gradient needs to be scored; this skill only enumerates the constrained candidate space, it does not evaluate gradients.

skills.description: Use when analysing HPTLC coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry data (e.g. mzXML-derived extracted ion chromatograms) and you need to partition ions of interest from background ions before structure elucidation.
skills.name: chromatographic-ion-clusterisation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-ion-clusterisation Use when analysing HPTLC coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry data (e.g. mzXML-derived extracted ion chromatograms) and you need to partition ions of interest from background ions before structure elucidation. The input is not HPTLC-HRMS data (e.g. bulk LC-MS/MS or untargeted metabolomics feature tables) — the method is framed specifically for high-performance thin-layer chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry. You need a fully automated, non-interactive batch pipeline — the sole function of the package launches a Shiny app 'where the user can interactively analyse the data', so it cannot run unattended. mzXML-derived EICs have not yet been generated and you lack the upstream readMzXmlData/Rtsne tooling — the skill presupposes extracted ion chromatograms are already available for clusterisation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Interactive R/Shiny workflow (eicCluster) that separates ions of interest from background ions in HPTLC-HRMS data by clusterising the extracted ion chromatograms, easing structure elucidation in planar chromatography. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.chroma.2018.09.050
skills.summary: Interactive R/Shiny workflow (eicCluster) that separates ions of interest from background ions in HPTLC-HRMS data by clusterising the extracted ion chromatograms, easing structure elucidation in planar chromatography.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not HPTLC-HRMS data (e.g. bulk LC-MS/MS or untargeted metabolomics feature tables) — the method is framed specifically for high-performance thin-layer chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry. You need a fully automated, non-interactive batch pipeline — the sole function of the package launches a Shiny app 'where the user can interactively analyse the data', so it cannot run unattended. mzXML-derived EICs have not yet been generated and you lack the upstream readMzXmlData/Rtsne tooling — the skill presupposes extracted ion chromatograms are already available for clusterisation.

skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-alignment-input-preparation Use when raw LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) must be converted into chromatographic m/z-RT peaklists and an aligned peak table before running the CSA, DDA, or DIA deconvolution workflows of IDSL.CSA. skills.summary: Prepare the input for IDSL.CSA composite spectra deconvolution by first running IDSL.IPA on raw LC/HRMS files (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) to produce per-file peaklists and an aligned peak table, then wiring the peaklists and peak_alignment directory addresses into the IDSL.CSA parameter spreadsheet (CSA0008/CSA0009).

skills.description: Use when processing targeted MS data where peak detection has produced EICs (after airPLS baseline correction and MassSpecWavelet peak positioning) and per-sample peak areas must be computed for a chosen isotopologue or metabolite.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-area-integration
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-area-integration Use when processing targeted MS data where peak detection has produced EICs (after airPLS baseline correction and MassSpecWavelet peak positioning) and per-sample peak areas must be computed for a chosen isotopologue or metabolite. The data are untargeted feature-based workflows where raw features are already aligned and quantified by XCMS-centWave — TarMet is targeted and uses its own EIC extraction and PAFFT alignment Retention-time alignment is not needed because only a single sample or a single injected run is analysed The user needs MS/MS library verification or data-independent acquisition support — TarMet explicitly lists these as future, not current, features http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Integrate aligned extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) peak areas for targeted metabolites and their isotopologues across samples, as implemented in TarMet's quantitative analysis stage, to produce per-sample quantification tables for metabolite and stable-isotope-tracer assays. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Integrate aligned extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) peak areas for targeted metabolites and their isotopologues across samples, as implemented in TarMet's quantitative analysis stage, to produce per-sample quantification tables for metabolite and stable-isotope-tracer assays.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are untargeted feature-based workflows where raw features are already aligned and quantified by XCMS-centWave — TarMet is targeted and uses its own EIC extraction and PAFFT alignment Retention-time alignment is not needed because only a single sample or a single injected run is analysed The user needs MS/MS library verification or data-independent acquisition support — TarMet explicitly lists these as future, not current, features

skills.description: Use when MRM ion chromatograms contain noisy peaks, unevenly sampled signals, or coeluted isomers where connecting nearby valleys (e.g., TargetLynx) misestimates the baseline; adaptive section-wise background reconstruction is needed before peak integration.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-baseline-reconstruction
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-baseline-reconstruction Use when MRM ion chromatograms contain noisy peaks, unevenly sampled signals, or coeluted isomers where connecting nearby valleys (e.g., TargetLynx) misestimates the baseline; adaptive section-wise background reconstruction is needed before peak integration. The input is already a de-noised, baseline-corrected feature table rather than raw ion chromatograms — smoothing would distort valid peak shapes. The goal is a batch-level normalization across samples rather than per-chromatogram baseline reconstruction; use the separate batch-effect correction step in MRMQuant instead. Coeluted isomer peaks need to be resolved into separate transitions rather than baseline-adjusted — use MRMQuant's automatic deconvolution of coeluted peaks feature instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A skill describing MRMQuant's dynamic signal smoothing, in which each ion chromatogram section is expanded or reduced until its signal extent equals 1.2× its background intensity, with background determined as the 30th percentile of the section's signal — this adaptive baseline reconstruction underlies accurate peak integration in MRM targeted metabolomics quantitation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: A skill describing MRMQuant's dynamic signal smoothing, in which each ion chromatogram section is expanded or reduced until its signal extent equals 1.2× its background intensity, with background determined as the 30th percentile of the section's signal — this adaptive baseline reconstruction underlies accurate peak integration in MRM targeted metabolomics quantitation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a de-noised, baseline-corrected feature table rather than raw ion chromatograms — smoothing would distort valid peak shapes. The goal is a batch-level normalization across samples rather than per-chromatogram baseline reconstruction; use the separate batch-effect correction step in MRMQuant instead. Coeluted isomer peaks need to be resolved into separate transitions rather than baseline-adjusted — use MRMQuant's automatic deconvolution of coeluted peaks feature instead.

skills.description: Use when refining the start/stop limits of peaks detected in smoothed CE-MS or HILIC-MS ROI chromatograms (intensity-vs-retention-time traces), after CWT/Mexican-hat peak-center detection but before peak integration of RT, area, and height.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-boundary-correction
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-boundary-correction Use when refining the start/stop limits of peaks detected in smoothed CE-MS or HILIC-MS ROI chromatograms (intensity-vs-retention-time traces), after CWT/Mexican-hat peak-center detection but before peak integration of RT, area, and height. Input is already a detected-peak/feature table (e.g. from MZmine or XCMS Online) rather than raw ROI traces — boundary correction would re-detect existing features The task requires MS/MS spectral networking to connect features across methods — AriumMS explicitly does not implement this (listed as future development) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Two-step peak-boundary refinement used in the AriumMS evaluation pipeline for CE-MS/LC-MS region-of-interest traces: a friction-border rule followed by a moving standard deviation criterion that terminates boundaries where the signal rises above the estimated local noise floor. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Two-step peak-boundary refinement used in the AriumMS evaluation pipeline for CE-MS/LC-MS region-of-interest traces: a friction-border rule followed by a moving standard deviation criterion that terminates boundaries where the signal rises above the estimated local noise floor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a detected-peak/feature table (e.g. from MZmine or XCMS Online) rather than raw ROI traces — boundary correction would re-detect existing features The task requires MS/MS spectral networking to connect features across methods — AriumMS explicitly does not implement this (listed as future development)

skills.description: Use when reconstructing chromatographic peak boundaries from centroided LC-MS data — e.g. when a growing mass trace spans several valleys and must be split so each trace corresponds to one chromatographic peak, or when apex-based boundary definition is needed.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-boundary-detection
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-boundary-detection Use when reconstructing chromatographic peak boundaries from centroided LC-MS data — e.g. when a growing mass trace spans several valleys and must be split so each trace corresponds to one chromatographic peak, or when apex-based boundary definition is needed. Input is profile-mode (non-centroided) LC-MS data — the seeding and recruitment step operates on centroided peaks from P′. Input is already a feature table or assembled features — this skill only defines chromatographic boundaries of mass traces, before feature assembly by m/z spacing, co-elution, and SVM isotope-pattern scoring. Data are single-scan or direct-infusion MS with no chromatographic (retention-time) structure — no RT axis exists on which to detect an apex or split valleys. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Defines the retention-time boundaries of chromatographic peaks within mass traces during FeatureFinderMetabo's mass trace detection: after LOWESS smoothing, the trace apex is located, peaks beyond half a smoothing window (s/2 rule) are pruned, and traces spanning multiple chromatographic valleys are split by a minimum-based rule. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278
skills.summary: Defines the retention-time boundaries of chromatographic peaks within mass traces during FeatureFinderMetabo's mass trace detection: after LOWESS smoothing, the trace apex is located, peaks beyond half a smoothing window (s/2 rule) are pruned, and traces spanning multiple chromatographic valleys are split by a minimum-based rule.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is profile-mode (non-centroided) LC-MS data — the seeding and recruitment step operates on centroided peaks from P′. Input is already a feature table or assembled features — this skill only defines chromatographic boundaries of mass traces, before feature assembly by m/z spacing, co-elution, and SVM isotope-pattern scoring. Data are single-scan or direct-infusion MS with no chromatographic (retention-time) structure — no RT axis exists on which to detect an apex or split valleys.

skills.summary: Detects chromatographic peak positions, bounds and areas in extracted-ion chromatograms (EICs) for targeted metabolites and their isotopologues, using airPLS baseline removal and MassSpecWavelet peak detection as implemented in TarMet, with isotopic-similarity-based selection of the true target peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantified feature table or peak table — no chromatogram peak detection is needed. The analysis goal is untargeted feature finding (e.g. XCMS centWave peak picking itself) rather than targeted isotopologue extraction on predefined compounds. skills.description: Use when MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS raw data (mzML) must be preprocessed into peak intensity tables without manual review, e.g. batches from instruments like an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS needing automatic peak picking and quality control.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-detection
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-detection Use when MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS raw data (mzML) must be preprocessed into peak intensity tables without manual review, e.g. batches from instruments like an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS needing automatic peak picking and quality control. Excessively dirty samples, very-low-input samples, or brand-new LC methods — the article recommends retreating to manual peak review for these special cases Acquisition methods without at least one qualifier transition in addition to the quantifier — automRm performance is suboptimal without qualifiers Data not recorded in MRM mode, or cases lacking sufficient relevant training data — quality similar to manual peak review requires training on relevant raw data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Fully automatic machine-learning-based detection and accept/reject reporting of chromatographic peaks in LC-QQQ-MS data recorded in MRM mode, replacing manual peak review with the automRm R package. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05224
skills.summary: Fully automatic machine-learning-based detection and accept/reject reporting of chromatographic peaks in LC-QQQ-MS data recorded in MRM mode, replacing manual peak review with the automRm R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Excessively dirty samples, very-low-input samples, or brand-new LC methods — the article recommends retreating to manual peak review for these special cases Acquisition methods without at least one qualifier transition in addition to the quantifier — automRm performance is suboptimal without qualifiers Data not recorded in MRM mode, or cases lacking sufficient relevant training data — quality similar to manual peak review requires training on relevant raw data

skills.description: Use when processing raw LC-MS ROI intensity arrays (e.g. mzML or Bruker TDF2 .d via MassCube) and you need to split each mass trace into discrete chromatographic peak segments bounded by start/end edge indices.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-edge-detection
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-edge-detection Use when processing raw LC-MS ROI intensity arrays (e.g. mzML or Bruker TDF2 .d via MassCube) and you need to split each mass trace into discrete chromatographic peak segments bounded by start/end edge indices. Input is already a feature table or aligned peak list — no ROI intensity arrays exist to segment You need smoothed chromatograms in the final report — MassCube deliberately reports raw (unsmoothed) data because smoothing may bias data structures Working with data from a single instrument profile such that vendor's proprietary per-frame pressure compensation is required for mobility-ordered traces (Bruker .d reader records mobility_pressure_compensated == False) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Segment chromatographic peaks within each ROI (mass trace) by applying a 1D Gaussian filter (σ = 1.2) for edge detection only, then cutting the raw intensity array at the detected boundaries. MassCube uses this to achieve 100% signal coverage without letting smoothing bias the reported peak data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Segment chromatographic peaks within each ROI (mass trace) by applying a 1D Gaussian filter (σ = 1.2) for edge detection only, then cutting the raw intensity array at the detected boundaries. MassCube uses this to achieve 100% signal coverage without letting smoothing bias the reported peak data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or aligned peak list — no ROI intensity arrays exist to segment You need smoothed chromatograms in the final report — MassCube deliberately reports raw (unsmoothed) data because smoothing may bias data structures Working with data from a single instrument profile such that vendor's proprietary per-frame pressure compensation is required for mobility-ordered traces (Bruker .d reader records mobility_pressure_compensated == False)

skills.description: Use when an aligned XCMS feature table (m/z, retention time, apex intensity, per-sample intensities) must be partitioned into co-eluting compound spectra as the first CAMERA grouping step before isotope/adduct annotation.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-fwhm-window-grouping
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-fwhm-window-grouping Use when an aligned XCMS feature table (m/z, retention time, apex intensity, per-sample intensities) must be partitioned into co-eluting compound spectra as the first CAMERA grouping step before isotope/adduct annotation. Features were already annotated by another grouping pass (e.g. correlation-based calcCiS/calcCaS) — groupFWHM is the initial step and assumes an unassigned feature table. Data lack chromatographic separation (direct infusion MS), so retention-time windows around peak FWHM are meaningless for co-elution inference. The goal is ion-species annotation (adducts, isotopes, fragments) rather than the initial co-elution grouping — use findIsotopes/findAdducts after this step instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Initial CAMERA compound-spectrum extraction step (groupFWHM) that clusters LC/MS features sharing a retention-time window around each unassigned feature's chromatographic peak FWHM into pseudospectra, iteratively until every feature in the XCMS feature table is assigned. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Initial CAMERA compound-spectrum extraction step (groupFWHM) that clusters LC/MS features sharing a retention-time window around each unassigned feature's chromatographic peak FWHM into pseudospectra, iteratively until every feature in the XCMS feature table is assigned.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features were already annotated by another grouping pass (e.g. correlation-based calcCiS/calcCaS) — groupFWHM is the initial step and assumes an unassigned feature table. Data lack chromatographic separation (direct infusion MS), so retention-time windows around peak FWHM are meaningless for co-elution inference. The goal is ion-species annotation (adducts, isotopes, fragments) rather than the initial co-elution grouping — use findIsotopes/findAdducts after this step instead.

skills.name: chromatographic-peak-integration-rt-area-height

skills.summary: Integrates peaks detected within chromatographic/electrophoretic regions of interest (ROIs) to extract apex retention time, area, and height, as implemented in the AriumMS feature-detection stage for multi-platform CE-MS/LC-MS metabolomics data. It turns raw intensity-vs-retention-time ROI traces into a structured peak table usable for downstream augmentation and chemometrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or peak list with RT/area/height values — peak detection and integration would duplicate existing results Peaks are broad and Gaussian-like rather than the narrow peaks typical of CE-MS separations, where a Mexican-hat CWT approach may be unnecessarily specialized The goal is ROI finding or augmentation/chemometric evaluation rather than converting ROIs into integrated peak quantities

skills.description: Use when you have an xcms result object with centWave-detected chromatographic peaks (e.g. from an mzML LC-MS/MS run like HighIS_Mix07_CE20_POS.mzML) and need the tandem MS2 spectra behind those peaks to compare against a reference library such as an HMDB 5.0 CompDb.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-ms2-spectra-extraction
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-ms2-spectra-extraction Use when you have an xcms result object with centWave-detected chromatographic peaks (e.g. from an mzML LC-MS/MS run like HighIS_Mix07_CE20_POS.mzML) and need the tandem MS2 spectra behind those peaks to compare against a reference library such as an HMDB 5.0 CompDb. Your MS2 spectra already exist as standalone files (MGF, MSP, mzML) — import them directly into a Spectra object with MsBackendMgf/MsBackendMsp instead of reconstructing from an xcms result The dataset is MS1-only (no tandem MS2 scans were acquired) — chromPeakSpectra cannot produce fragment spectra; restrict annotation to matchMz/MzRtParam matching You only need to identify peaks by precursor m/z and retention time (matchMz or MzRtParam) — MS2 extraction is unnecessary for MS1-level annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Extracts MS2 fragment spectra associated with xcms-detected chromatographic peaks from an xcms result object using chromPeakSpectra, producing a Spectra object ready for cleaning (5% BPI intensity filter, ≥3-peak filter, 0–100 intensity scaling) and downstream MS2 library matching with matchSpectra. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12020173
skills.summary: Extracts MS2 fragment spectra associated with xcms-detected chromatographic peaks from an xcms result object using chromPeakSpectra, producing a Spectra object ready for cleaning (5% BPI intensity filter, ≥3-peak filter, 0–100 intensity scaling) and downstream MS2 library matching with matchSpectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your MS2 spectra already exist as standalone files (MGF, MSP, mzML) — import them directly into a Spectra object with MsBackendMgf/MsBackendMsp instead of reconstructing from an xcms result The dataset is MS1-only (no tandem MS2 scans were acquired) — chromPeakSpectra cannot produce fragment spectra; restrict annotation to matchMz/MzRtParam matching You only need to identify peaks by precursor m/z and retention time (matchMz or MzRtParam) — MS2 extraction is unnecessary for MS1-level annotation

skills.summary: Detects chromatographic peaks from HRMS scan data to build an m/z–RT feature table using the Mass-Suite (MSS) function mssmain.peak_pick, which concatenates scans and locates peak indices with PeakUtils, followed by post-processing filters to remove poor-quality features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table — use MSS alignment, clustering (dm.ms_cluster), or source-tracking modules instead of peak picking The goal is MS/MS fragment searching or formula prediction (mss frag module against MoNA MassBank), not chromatographic feature extraction Features must be grouped into chemicals (merging isotopes, adducts, in-source fragments) — MSS explicitly lists feature grouping as future work, so peak picking alone will not deliver it

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (any vendor format compatible with MS-Convert) need MS1 peak picking to build a JPA feature table, or as the PP baseline step before MR and targeted feature extraction in metabolomics/exposomics processing.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-picking
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-picking Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (any vendor format compatible with MS-Convert) need MS1 peak picking to build a JPA feature table, or as the PP baseline step before MR and targeted feature extraction in metabolomics/exposomics processing. Raw data cannot be converted to mzXML via MS-Convert, since JPA only accepts vendor formats compatible with MS-Convert. skills.summary: Extract MS1 metabolic features ('PP' level) from raw LC-MS mzXML data using JPA's embedded XCMS peak picking functions, producing a dataframe feature table plus an MSnbase object that feeds JPA's MS2-recognition, targeted, alignment, and annotation steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an already-aligned feature table — JPA requires one unaligned CSV per single mzXML file ('Aligned feature table is not acceptable'). Raw data cannot be converted to mzXML via MS-Convert, since JPA only accepts vendor formats compatible with MS-Convert. The analysis only needs MS2-recognition or targeted-list extraction without a PP base layer — these levels are added to a PP feature table, not generated standalone.

skills.description: Use when extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) from LC/MS metabolomics profiles have already been peak-detected and individual peaks (or EICs) must be scored, filtered, or classified as good vs. bad before downstream processing.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-assessment Use when extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) from LC/MS metabolomics profiles have already been peak-detected and individual peaks (or EICs) must be scored, filtered, or classified as good vs. bad before downstream processing. No labeled set of curated 'good' and 'bad' representative peaks exists and ground truth peaks cannot be assembled from multiple tools — the paper notes SVM-based automatic peak identification 'requires compiling and curating a sufficient number of "good" and "bad" representative peaks for training samples', which does not yet exist. The input is raw LC/MS profile data that has not yet passed acute EIC extraction and chromatographic peak detection — quality evaluation is a later module, not a substitute for peak detection. EIC-level (not peak-level) quality scoring is the goal for high-background or single-peak EICs — the MCQ index is unsuited there, so use the EIC-related global zigzag index instead of peak-level metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates the quality of chromatographic peaks in LC/MS-based metabolomics data by computing six peak quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, and local zigzag index) and combining them — via individually varied cutoff thresholds or an SVM classifier — to filter out 'bad' peaks more efficiently than any single metric. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Evaluates the quality of chromatographic peaks in LC/MS-based metabolomics data by computing six peak quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, and local zigzag index) and combining them — via individually varied cutoff thresholds or an SVM classifier — to filter out 'bad' peaks more efficiently than any single metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No labeled set of curated 'good' and 'bad' representative peaks exists and ground truth peaks cannot be assembled from multiple tools — the paper notes SVM-based automatic peak identification 'requires compiling and curating a sufficient number of "good" and "bad" representative peaks for training samples', which does not yet exist. The input is raw LC/MS profile data that has not yet passed acute EIC extraction and chromatographic peak detection — quality evaluation is a later module, not a substitute for peak detection. EIC-level (not peak-level) quality scoring is the goal for high-background or single-peak EICs — the MCQ index is unsuited there, so use the EIC-related global zigzag index instead of peak-level metrics.

skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-assessment Use when you have targeted/suspect HRMS data (mzML) plus a compound or mass list and need per-peak QC (MS1/MS2 existence, noise, RT shift) before further identification or spectral upload. skills.summary: Quality-assessment step of Shinyscreen's extraction/prescreening stage: each MS1 parent data point for compounds from a preselected list is scored for MS1/MS2 data existence, noise level, and retention-time shift against user-supplied intensity and shift thresholds before any identification attempt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or peak matrix — this skill operates on raw mzML data for a preselected list of compounds or masses of interest The goal is untargeted peak detection/feature finding across all detected masses rather than QC of listed targets or suspects A complex, fully resource-intensive annotation platform is already being used — Shinyscreen deliberately occupies the niche between low-level programming tools and such platforms, not their replacement

skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering Use when processing LC-MS mzML files of authentic metabolite standards and you need to find peaks on adduct EICs and remove low-quality detections before assigning retention times and m/z for an in-house reference library. Input is already a curated library CSV or a feature table from targeted peak-picking tools such as MZmine, El-MAVEN, or MS-DIAL — peak finding and filtering have already been done. The goal requires MS/MS spectra for library construction — metScribeR deliberately focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use or require MS2. Raw vendor files have not been converted to mzML; the noise parsing and EIC extraction pipeline expects mzML inputs. Filters peaks detected on extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) of metabolite standard adducts using chromatographR-based peak finding plus metScribeR quality thresholds, so only credible peaks survive for RT and m/z library construction. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Filters peaks detected on extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) of metabolite standard adducts using chromatographR-based peak finding plus metScribeR quality thresholds, so only credible peaks survive for RT and m/z library construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated library CSV or a feature table from targeted peak-picking tools such as MZmine, El-MAVEN, or MS-DIAL — peak finding and filtering have already been done. The goal requires MS/MS spectra for library construction — metScribeR deliberately focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use or require MS2. Raw vendor files have not been converted to mzML; the noise parsing and EIC extraction pipeline expects mzML inputs.

skills.description: Use when processing MS1-level LC/HRMS peak candidates (e.g. from IDSL.IPA EIC detection) and you need to discard low-quality or redundant isotope peaks using the seven-parameter peak quality filter before building aligned data matrices.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering Use when processing MS1-level LC/HRMS peak candidates (e.g. from IDSL.IPA EIC detection) and you need to discard low-quality or redundant isotope peaks using the seven-parameter peak quality filter before building aligned data matrices. Input is already an aligned, filtered feature/peak intensity matrix — no per-peak quality re-evaluation is required at this stage You need molecular formula annotation rather than peak filtering — use IDSL.UFA or IDSL.UFAx instead, which consume IDSL.IPA peaklists Peak candidates come from tools other than IDSL.IPA and you cannot supply their chromatographic properties (nIsoPair, RCS, RPW, S/N) needed by the seven criteria http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A post-detection filter step from the IDSL.IPA pipeline that evaluates every chromatographic peak candidate against seven quality criteria (peak height, gap percentage, nIsoPair, RCS, R13C, RPW, and baseline S/N) and retains only peaks passing all thresholds, thereby isolating reliable signals for carbon-containing organic compounds in untargeted LC/HRMS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: A post-detection filter step from the IDSL.IPA pipeline that evaluates every chromatographic peak candidate against seven quality criteria (peak height, gap percentage, nIsoPair, RCS, R13C, RPW, and baseline S/N) and retains only peaks passing all thresholds, thereby isolating reliable signals for carbon-containing organic compounds in untargeted LC/HRMS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned, filtered feature/peak intensity matrix — no per-peak quality re-evaluation is required at this stage You need molecular formula annotation rather than peak filtering — use IDSL.UFA or IDSL.UFAx instead, which consume IDSL.IPA peaklists Peak candidates come from tools other than IDSL.IPA and you cannot supply their chromatographic properties (nIsoPair, RCS, RPW, S/N) needed by the seven criteria

skills.description: Use when raw centroid/profile HRMS scans (.mzML) have been peak-picked and the feature list must be cleaned of low-quality peaks — split peaks, peaks spanning too few scans, and high-baseline-noise features — before annotation or statistical analysis.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering Use when raw centroid/profile HRMS scans (.mzML) have been peak-picked and the feature list must be cleaned of low-quality peaks — split peaks, peaks spanning too few scans, and high-baseline-noise features — before annotation or statistical analysis. The input is already a cleaned feature table exported by another tool (e.g., MSDIAL, XCMS, MZmine) — quality filtering has already been applied upstream. The goal is merging isotope, adduct, or in-source-fragment features into individual chemicals — feature grouping is not yet implemented in MSS and is listed as future work. The target is identification (MS/MS fragment searching against MoNA MassBank) rather than removing poor-quality chromatographic peaks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Post-processing filter chain applied after mssmain.peak_pick to remove poor-quality chromatographic features (split peaks, insufficient scan numbers, high baseline noise) from HRMS .mzML data, optionally augmented by a pre-trained random forest peak quality classifier. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00741-9
skills.summary: Post-processing filter chain applied after mssmain.peak_pick to remove poor-quality chromatographic features (split peaks, insufficient scan numbers, high baseline noise) from HRMS .mzML data, optionally augmented by a pre-trained random forest peak quality classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cleaned feature table exported by another tool (e.g., MSDIAL, XCMS, MZmine) — quality filtering has already been applied upstream. The goal is merging isotope, adduct, or in-source-fragment features into individual chemicals — feature grouping is not yet implemented in MSS and is listed as future work. The target is identification (MS/MS fragment searching against MoNA MassBank) rather than removing poor-quality chromatographic peaks.

skills.description: Use when LC/MS chromatographic peaks have been detected on extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) and you need per-peak numeric quality scores to filter 'bad' peaks before downstream metabolomics processing.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-metric-computation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-metric-computation Use when LC/MS chromatographic peaks have been detected on extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) and you need per-peak numeric quality scores to filter 'bad' peaks before downstream metabolomics processing. Input is already a filtered list of peaks with known-good quality (e.g. after SVM-based peak identification) — the metric computation would be redundant You need to evaluate the quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) themselves rather than detected peaks — the paper's MCQ index and EIC-related global zigzag index address that separate problem The data are not LC/MS metabolomics chromatograms (e.g. GC/MS or non-chromatographic spectra), where the zigzag-nature rationale and Gaussian-shape assumptions may not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes and compares the six chromatographic peak quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, and the local zigzag index) defined by Zhang & Zhao for LC/MS-based metabolomics peaks, so that good and bad detected peaks can be distinguished and filtered. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Computes and compares the six chromatographic peak quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, and the local zigzag index) defined by Zhang & Zhao for LC/MS-based metabolomics peaks, so that good and bad detected peaks can be distinguished and filtered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered list of peaks with known-good quality (e.g. after SVM-based peak identification) — the metric computation would be redundant You need to evaluate the quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) themselves rather than detected peaks — the paper's MCQ index and EIC-related global zigzag index address that separate problem The data are not LC/MS metabolomics chromatograms (e.g. GC/MS or non-chromatographic spectra), where the zigzag-nature rationale and Gaussian-shape assumptions may not hold

skills.description: Use when you have an XCMS pre-processed untargeted LC–MS dataset (getEIC + fillPeaks output) and need numeric per-peak quality features to train or apply a Pass/Fail peak-quality classifier.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-metric-computation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-metric-computation Use when you have an XCMS pre-processed untargeted LC–MS dataset (getEIC + fillPeaks output) and need numeric per-peak quality features to train or apply a Pass/Fail peak-quality classifier. Input is not an XCMS object — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input and is not amenable in its current form to uniquely formatted vendor-processed outputs such as MassHunter Profinder or Progenesis QI results. The goal is targeted-MS peak assessment with vendor-specific transition-level metrics rather than untargeted EIC quality metrics. Peaks have already been filtered (e.g. by RSD < 30% in pooled QC) and only their integration quality remains to be judged — the metric computation is a feature-generation step, not a filter. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes per-peak chromatographic quality metrics (apex-boundary ratio, jaggedness, symmetry, modality, FWHM2base, elution shift, retention-time consistency, sharpness, Gaussian similarity, TPASR, zig-zag index) from an XCMS-extracted ion chromatogram (evalObj) to serve as classifier features for Pass/Fail peak-quality assessment in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Computes per-peak chromatographic quality metrics (apex-boundary ratio, jaggedness, symmetry, modality, FWHM2base, elution shift, retention-time consistency, sharpness, Gaussian similarity, TPASR, zig-zag index) from an XCMS-extracted ion chromatogram (evalObj) to serve as classifier features for Pass/Fail peak-quality assessment in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not an XCMS object — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input and is not amenable in its current form to uniquely formatted vendor-processed outputs such as MassHunter Profinder or Progenesis QI results. The goal is targeted-MS peak assessment with vendor-specific transition-level metrics rather than untargeted EIC quality metrics. Peaks have already been filtered (e.g. by RSD < 30% in pooled QC) and only their integration quality remains to be judged — the metric computation is a feature-generation step, not a filter.

skills.description: Use when evaluating LC-MS metabolomics peak quality for chemical standards: you have EICs from mzXML/mzML files (with optional replicate and blank runs) and need standardized per-peak quality metrics to validate or rank peaks.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-metrics
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-metrics Use when evaluating LC-MS metabolomics peak quality for chemical standards: you have EICs from mzXML/mzML files (with optional replicate and blank runs) and need standardized per-peak quality metrics to validate or rank peaks. When the goal is choosing the optimal mobile phase by comparing resolved-peak counts and asymmetry scores across mobile-phase experiments (use the MetaMOPE mobile-phase determination scoring workflow instead) When peak detection must be done directly on raw, uncorrected profiles — the metrics are computed only after IRLS baseline correction and Savitzky-Golay smoothing of the EIC When the input is already a processed feature table rather than raw mzXML/mzLC-MS chromatographic data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes the eight MetaMOPE per-peak chromatographic quality metrics (MCQ, maximum intensity, RSD of retention time, Std/Blk, jaggedness, asymmetry factor, FWHM, modality) from extracted ion chromatograms in mzXML/mzML files, after IRLS baseline correction and Savitzky-Golay smoothing. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad061
skills.summary: Computes the eight MetaMOPE per-peak chromatographic quality metrics (MCQ, maximum intensity, RSD of retention time, Std/Blk, jaggedness, asymmetry factor, FWHM, modality) from extracted ion chromatograms in mzXML/mzML files, after IRLS baseline correction and Savitzky-Golay smoothing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is choosing the optimal mobile phase by comparing resolved-peak counts and asymmetry scores across mobile-phase experiments (use the MetaMOPE mobile-phase determination scoring workflow instead) When peak detection must be done directly on raw, uncorrected profiles — the metrics are computed only after IRLS baseline correction and Savitzky-Golay smoothing of the EIC When the input is already a processed feature table rather than raw mzXML/mzLC-MS chromatographic data

skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-score-computation Use when preprocessing LC-QQQ-MS raw data in MRM mode and you need per-candidate peak quality metrics (shape, quantifier/qualifier coelution, RT deviation) before ML-based peak reporting. skills.summary: Computation of 20 chromatographic quality scores for candidate MRM peaks detected by automRm, characterizing peak shape, quantifier/qualifier agreement, and RT deviation, which feed the downstream ML peak-reporting model (or are averaged when no ML model is supplied).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not MRM-mode LC-MS with quantifier/qualifier transitions — automRm requires at least one qualifier in addition to the quantifier for optimal performance The goal is final peak reporting on new or very-low-input samples without relevant training data; the paper notes retreat to manual peak review may be needed for excessively dirty samples, very-low-input samples, or new LC methods Raw files are not parseable as mzML (e.g. vendor-native formats not converted)

skills.description: Use when raw MRM-mode LC-MS data (mzML with quantifier plus qualifier transitions and expected RTs in metabdb.xlsx) must be converted into a trustworthy set of reported peaks, i.e. deciding which of several peak candidates per metabolite/sample is the correct one.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-quality-scoring
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-quality-scoring Use when raw MRM-mode LC-MS data (mzML with quantifier plus qualifier transitions and expected RTs in metabdb.xlsx) must be converted into a trustworthy set of reported peaks, i.e. deciding which of several peak candidates per metabolite/sample is the correct one. The acquisition method has no qualifier transition besides the quantifier — automRm requires at least one qualifier for optimal performance, so reported-peak quality will degrade. Samples are excessively dirty, very-low-input, or derive from a brand-new LC method with no relevant training data — the article retreats to manual peak review in these cases. Input is already a processed feature/peak table rather than raw mzML MRM chromatograms — process_batch() operates on raw files. Scores candidate chromatographic peaks from MRM LC-QQQ-MS raw data with 20 quality scores and a trained peak-reporting ML model so that reported peaks can replace manual peak review. Implemented as the peak picking/reporting step of automRm's process_batch() pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05224
skills.summary: Scores candidate chromatographic peaks from MRM LC-QQQ-MS raw data with 20 quality scores and a trained peak-reporting ML model so that reported peaks can replace manual peak review. Implemented as the peak picking/reporting step of automRm's process_batch() pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The acquisition method has no qualifier transition besides the quantifier — automRm requires at least one qualifier for optimal performance, so reported-peak quality will degrade. Samples are excessively dirty, very-low-input, or derive from a brand-new LC method with no relevant training data — the article retreats to manual peak review in these cases. Input is already a processed feature/peak table rather than raw mzML MRM chromatograms — process_batch() operates on raw files.

skills.description: Reference for quantifying the 12C/13C isotope-pair intensity ratio of individual chromatographic peaks and correlating it with molecular formulas or predicted carbon number.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-r13c-computation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-r13c-computation Reference for quantifying the 12C/13C isotope-pair intensity ratio of individual chromatographic peaks and correlating it with molecular formulas or predicted carbon number. When peaks have already been aligned and annotated into a feature table with no isotopologue-pairing metadata (nIsoPair/R13C columns) — IDSL.IPA must be re-run on the raw mzXML/mzML to regenerate these properties. When the analyte set is expected to contain non-carbon-containing compounds, since IDSL.IPA specifically isolates signals pertaining to carbon-containing compounds via 12C/13C ion pairing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes per-peak R13C values (the ratio of cumulated 13C isotope-pair intensity to 12C monoisotopic intensity) from IDSL.IPA peaklists for authentic standards, and validates them against theoretical R13C values from enviPat isotopic profiles to confirm that R13C tracks carbon number. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: Computes per-peak R13C values (the ratio of cumulated 13C isotope-pair intensity to 12C monoisotopic intensity) from IDSL.IPA peaklists for authentic standards, and validates them against theoretical R13C values from enviPat isotopic profiles to confirm that R13C tracks carbon number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When peaks have already been aligned and annotated into a feature table with no isotopologue-pairing metadata (nIsoPair/R13C columns) — IDSL.IPA must be re-run on the raw mzXML/mzML to regenerate these properties. When the analyte set is expected to contain non-carbon-containing compounds, since IDSL.IPA specifically isolates signals pertaining to carbon-containing compounds via 12C/13C ion pairing.

skills.description: Use when raw CE-MS or LC-MS data (converted to .mzXML/.mzML via msconvert) has been peak-detected with the CWT/ROI search step and noise/false-positive peaks must be culled by shape before feature integration, scaling, and mid-level data fusion.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-shape-analysis
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-shape-analysis Use when raw CE-MS or LC-MS data (converted to .mzXML/.mzML via msconvert) has been peak-detected with the CWT/ROI search step and noise/false-positive peaks must be culled by shape before feature integration, scaling, and mid-level data fusion. Input is already a curated feature table (e.g. post-augmentation, post-scaling) — the filter operates on raw CWT/ROI peak tables before feature integration Dataset contains very few detected peaks — the median-entropy threshold is unstable without a large peak population to establish the median Peak shapes are not adequately described by a two-class normal/variant point scheme (e.g. heavily co-eluted or saturated peaks), where entropy no longer separates true peaks from noise http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A peak-shape-based false-positive filter from AriumMS that scores each CWT-detected CE-MS/LC-MS feature with its information entropy H = -p*log2(p) - q*log2(q) and discards features whose H exceeds the median entropy across all detected peaks, removing noise peaks before feature integration and augmentation. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: A peak-shape-based false-positive filter from AriumMS that scores each CWT-detected CE-MS/LC-MS feature with its information entropy H = -p*log2(p) - q*log2(q) and discards features whose H exceeds the median entropy across all detected peaks, removing noise peaks before feature integration and augmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table (e.g. post-augmentation, post-scaling) — the filter operates on raw CWT/ROI peak tables before feature integration Dataset contains very few detected peaks — the median-entropy threshold is unstable without a large peak population to establish the median Peak shapes are not adequately described by a two-class normal/variant point scheme (e.g. heavily co-eluted or saturated peaks), where entropy no longer separates true peaks from noise

skills.description: Use when processing untargeted LC-MS raw data (mzML or Bruker .d) where co-eluting ions must be distinguished as genuine metabolites versus in-source fragments or alternative adducts before quantification.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-shape-correlation
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-shape-correlation Use when processing untargeted LC-MS raw data (mzML or Bruker .d) where co-eluting ions must be distinguished as genuine metabolites versus in-source fragments or alternative adducts before quantification. The parent ion was not detected due to complete fragmentation in the ion source — MassCube cannot automatically annotate its ISFs in this case Input is already an annotated feature table or you only need metabolite identification — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification and this skill covers grouping/annotation of features, not ID A graphical interface or time-series/SERRF normalization is needed — these are not available in the current MassCube version http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) and co-eluting adduct/isotope groups in LC-MS data by requiring a candidate fragment's m/z to appear in the parent's MS/MS spectrum AND its scan-to-scan Pearson correlation with the parent peak shape to exceed r > 0.7. This two-criterion strategy is how MassCube grouped 2604 ISFs and 6055 alternative adducts in the Metabolome Atlas of the Aging Mouse Brain dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) and co-eluting adduct/isotope groups in LC-MS data by requiring a candidate fragment's m/z to appear in the parent's MS/MS spectrum AND its scan-to-scan Pearson correlation with the parent peak shape to exceed r > 0.7. This two-criterion strategy is how MassCube grouped 2604 ISFs and 6055 alternative adducts in the Metabolome Atlas of the Aging Mouse Brain dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The parent ion was not detected due to complete fragmentation in the ion source — MassCube cannot automatically annotate its ISFs in this case Input is already an annotated feature table or you only need metabolite identification — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification and this skill covers grouping/annotation of features, not ID A graphical interface or time-series/SERRF normalization is needed — these are not available in the current MassCube version

skills.description: Decision support for splitting CAMERA pseudospectra that the retention-time window alone left ambiguous — i.e. when features co-elute within one FWHM group but their EIC peak shapes (corval, pval thresholds on calcCaS edges) indicate two overlapping analytes.
skills.name: chromatographic-peak-shape-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: chromatographic-peak-shape-correlation-analysis Decision support for splitting CAMERA pseudospectra that the retention-time window alone left ambiguous — i.e. when features co-elute within one FWHM group but their EIC peak shapes (corval, pval thresholds on calcCaS edges) indicate two overlapping analytes. When the compound spectrum contains no possibly co-eluting features — a single-analyte spectrum separated cleanly by groupFWHM retention-time grouping needs no additional graph split. When only cross-sample intensity correlation is available without peak-shape or isotope information: calcCaS edges require EIC peak profiles, so running the skill on feature tables lacking chromatographic profiles is inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes chromatographic peak-shape correlation (Pearson correlation of the extracted EIC intensity profiles) between LC/MS features within a compound spectrum and feeds the resulting edge scores into CAMERA's weighted relationship graph, which is subsequently split by highly connected subgraphs (HCS) or label propagation (LPC) to separate features of closely co-eluting compounds that survive the initial groupFWHM retention-time grouping. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Computes chromatographic peak-shape correlation (Pearson correlation of the extracted EIC intensity profiles) between LC/MS features within a compound spectrum and feeds the resulting edge scores into CAMERA's weighted relationship graph, which is subsequently split by highly connected subgraphs (HCS) or label propagation (LPC) to separate features of closely co-eluting compounds that survive the initial groupFWHM retention-time grouping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compound spectrum contains no possibly co-eluting features — a single-analyte spectrum separated cleanly by groupFWHM retention-time grouping needs no additional graph split. When only cross-sample intensity correlation is available without peak-shape or isotope information: calcCaS edges require EIC peak profiles, so running the skill on feature tables lacking chromatographic profiles is inappropriate.
