Compounds already identified at MSI level 1 with authentic standards or annotated at MSI level 2 by precursor accurate mass and MS/MS matching — ClassyFire here targets only the remaining MSI level 3 annotations You have no InChI keys or translatable compound names/formulas, so the ClassyFire API cannot be queried in batch The analysis goal is compound identification confidence rather than chemical-class composition of unannotated spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Batch-annotates computationally assigned (MSI level 3) metabolite structures with the ClassyFire chemical ontology, resolving each compound into 21 superclasses and 184 chemical classes to give a chemical-class distribution of previously unannotated spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Batch-annotates computationally assigned (MSI level 3) metabolite structures with the ClassyFire chemical ontology, resolving each compound into 21 superclasses and 184 chemical classes to give a chemical-class distribution of previously unannotated spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds already identified at MSI level 1 with authentic standards or annotated at MSI level 2 by precursor accurate mass and MS/MS matching — ClassyFire here targets only the remaining MSI level 3 annotations You have no InChI keys or translatable compound names/formulas, so the ClassyFire API cannot be queried in batch The analysis goal is compound identification confidence rather than chemical-class composition of unannotated spectra

skills.description: Use when evaluating formula-prediction accuracy across molecular strata (polarity/LogP, mass, ClassyFire superclass) on tandem MS test predictions to flag underperforming chemical classes.
skills.name: classyfire-superclass-annotation-analysis
skills.search_text: classyfire-superclass-annotation-analysis Use when evaluating formula-prediction accuracy across molecular strata (polarity/LogP, mass, ClassyFire superclass) on tandem MS test predictions to flag underperforming chemical classes. Input spectra are chimeric (co-eluting) — FIDDLE performance degrades with spectral mixing, so stratified accuracy would not reflect class-specific effects Molecules fall outside FIDDLE's training scope (e.g., atoms outside C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K, atom counts above 300, or m/z above 1500) The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than benchmarking formula-identification accuracy against known ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Stratifies FIDDLE formula-identification accuracy on held-out NIST23 test spectra by molecular properties — ClassyFire superclass, LogP polarity bins, and precursor mass bins — for Q-TOF and Orbitrap instruments, to reveal where the deep learning model underperforms. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Stratifies FIDDLE formula-identification accuracy on held-out NIST23 test spectra by molecular properties — ClassyFire superclass, LogP polarity bins, and precursor mass bins — for Q-TOF and Orbitrap instruments, to reveal where the deep learning model underperforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are chimeric (co-eluting) — FIDDLE performance degrades with spectral mixing, so stratified accuracy would not reflect class-specific effects Molecules fall outside FIDDLE's training scope (e.g., atoms outside C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K, atom counts above 300, or m/z above 1500) The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than benchmarking formula-identification accuracy against known ground truth

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between CANOPUS and MolNetEnhancer before running chemical class matching (e.g. NPClassScore), or for auditing how much superclass predictions disagree when both tools annotate the same GNPS molecular networking spectra.
skills.name: classyfire-superclass-frequency-tabulation
skills.search_text: classyfire-superclass-frequency-tabulation Decision support for choosing between CANOPUS and MolNetEnhancer before running chemical class matching (e.g. NPClassScore), or for auditing how much superclass predictions disagree when both tools annotate the same GNPS molecular networking spectra. When the goal is BGC–MS/MS linking itself rather than auditing annotation-tool consistency — use the full NPLinker pipeline with NPClassScore instead. When the spectra under study are larger than the ~850 Da mass cut-off that limits CANOPUS coverage, since CANOPUS predictions may be absent and the comparison becomes biased. When only one annotation tool's predictions exist for the spectra — there is no second tool to compare against, so the tabulation is meaningless. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Tabulates the frequency of each ClassyFire superclass category predicted by CANOPUS and by MolNetEnhancer for the same set of MS/MS spectra, exposing systematic discrepancies between the two structure-based ontology prediction tools. Used to quantify how strongly the choice of annotation tool (CANOPUS via SIRIUS on GNPS mgf files vs MolNetEnhancer run externally on GNPS) influences downstream chemical class matching outcomes such as NPClassScore. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Tabulates the frequency of each ClassyFire superclass category predicted by CANOPUS and by MolNetEnhancer for the same set of MS/MS spectra, exposing systematic discrepancies between the two structure-based ontology prediction tools. Used to quantify how strongly the choice of annotation tool (CANOPUS via SIRIUS on GNPS mgf files vs MolNetEnhancer run externally on GNPS) influences downstream chemical class matching outcomes such as NPClassScore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is BGC–MS/MS linking itself rather than auditing annotation-tool consistency — use the full NPLinker pipeline with NPClassScore instead. When the spectra under study are larger than the ~850 Da mass cut-off that limits CANOPUS coverage, since CANOPUS predictions may be absent and the comparison becomes biased. When only one annotation tool's predictions exist for the spectra — there is no second tool to compare against, so the tabulation is meaningless.

skills.description: Use when a package or paper claims a quantitative test-coverage figure (e.g. 'total testing code coverage above 90%') and the claim must be reproduced by running the test suite and measuring coverage per module.
skills.name: cli-command-test-verification
skills.search_text: cli-command-test-verification Use when a package or paper claims a quantitative test-coverage figure (e.g. 'total testing code coverage above 90%') and the claim must be reproduced by running the test suite and measuring coverage per module. The claim under test is a scientific result or data analysis outcome rather than a software-quality metric such as unit-test coverage. The package provides no test suite or continuous-integration coverage configuration, so no per-module line coverage can be measured against a reported figure. You only need functional verification of CLI behavior (e.g. that extract/validate/convert run end-to-end), not quantitative coverage measurement across modules. http://edamontology.org/topic_3372 Verifies a software package's claimed test-suite quality by executing its automated unit-test suite under a coverage measurement tool and confirming that total line/coverage exceeds a stated threshold (here, above 90% for the MESSES package). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13070842
skills.summary: Verifies a software package's claimed test-suite quality by executing its automated unit-test suite under a coverage measurement tool and confirming that total line/coverage exceeds a stated threshold (here, above 90% for the MESSES package).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The claim under test is a scientific result or data analysis outcome rather than a software-quality metric such as unit-test coverage. The package provides no test suite or continuous-integration coverage configuration, so no per-module line coverage can be measured against a reported figure. You only need functional verification of CLI behavior (e.g. that extract/validate/convert run end-to-end), not quantitative coverage measurement across modules.

skills.description: Use when a clinical metabolomics/lipidomics feature matrix has matched patient metadata (e.g. age, BMI, sex, tumor stage, tissue, repeated measures) and subject-specific variation must be minimized before multivariate modeling or feature selection.
skills.name: clinical-metabolomics-data-processing
skills.search_text: clinical-metabolomics-data-processing Use when a clinical metabolomics/lipidomics feature matrix has matched patient metadata (e.g. age, BMI, sex, tumor stage, tissue, repeated measures) and subject-specific variation must be minimized before multivariate modeling or feature selection. Input data lacks patient metadata or subject IDs, so no random-effects structure can be formulated for the LMM The dataset is already a fully processed/normalized feature table and the goal is only raw MS pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) Analysis involves non-clinical samples without repeated measures or biological covariates to model http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 An additional data-processing step that readjusts individual metabolite signals in clinical metabolomics matrices by fitting a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) per metabolite using patient metadata, improving downstream multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA. Implemented in the R package lmm2met on top of lme4. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: An additional data-processing step that readjusts individual metabolite signals in clinical metabolomics matrices by fitting a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) per metabolite using patient metadata, improving downstream multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA. Implemented in the R package lmm2met on top of lme4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks patient metadata or subject IDs, so no random-effects structure can be formulated for the LMM The dataset is already a fully processed/normalized feature table and the goal is only raw MS pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) Analysis involves non-clinical samples without repeated measures or biological covariates to model

skills.description: Use when a task requires combining aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change) from multiple clinical metabolomics studies where compound names differ across sources and per-study raw data are unavailable.
skills.name: clinical-metabolomics-dataset-curation
skills.search_text: clinical-metabolomics-dataset-curation Use when a task requires combining aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change) from multiple clinical metabolomics studies where compound names differ across sources and per-study raw data are unavailable. Input data are raw metabolomics spectra or peak tables rather than published aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change) per compound. The analysis goal is single-study differential analysis rather than combining results across multiple studies. Compound identity must be matched strictly by database IDs and the 'Include compounds IDs' option is required but ID mapping is unavailable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Curate aggregate metabolomics statistics (p-values and fold-changes) from multiple clinical studies and harmonize compound names so they can be combined in an Amanida-based meta-analysis, as implemented in the Easy-Amanida Shiny app. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jrsm.1713
skills.summary: Curate aggregate metabolomics statistics (p-values and fold-changes) from multiple clinical studies and harmonize compound names so they can be combined in an Amanida-based meta-analysis, as implemented in the Easy-Amanida Shiny app.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw metabolomics spectra or peak tables rather than published aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change) per compound. The analysis goal is single-study differential analysis rather than combining results across multiple studies. Compound identity must be matched strictly by database IDs and the 'Include compounds IDs' option is required but ID mapping is unavailable.

skills.description: Use when MOFA factor values and a clinical metadata table (numeric and binary patient features) are available and the goal is to rank discriminant MOFA factors by their statistical association with clinical traits.
skills.name: clinical-metadata-association-summarization
skills.search_text: clinical-metadata-association-summarization Use when MOFA factor values and a clinical metadata table (numeric and binary patient features) are available and the goal is to rank discriminant MOFA factors by their statistical association with clinical traits. MOFA integration has not yet been run and no factor values matrix exists to correlate The second table is an omics feature matrix (transcriptomics/metabolomics/methylomics) rather than patient clinical metadata The interpretation target is pathway enrichment or PubMed bibliography mining rather than clinical trait association http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reconstructs BiomiX's MOFA factor interpretation step in which discriminant MOFA factors are correlated against patient clinical metadata, using Pearson correlation for numeric clinical features and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for binary features, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction pooling all raw p-values. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Reconstructs BiomiX's MOFA factor interpretation step in which discriminant MOFA factors are correlated against patient clinical metadata, using Pearson correlation for numeric clinical features and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for binary features, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction pooling all raw p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MOFA integration has not yet been run and no factor values matrix exists to correlate The second table is an omics feature matrix (transcriptomics/metabolomics/methylomics) rather than patient clinical metadata The interpretation target is pathway enrichment or PubMed bibliography mining rather than clinical trait association

skills.description: Use when you have a serum metabolomics feature matrix (mzLearn-derived MS1 peaks, e.g. 2,736 features) with clinical labels (IMDC class, OS time/event) and need to predict treatment response or survival in a new patient cohort.
skills.name: clinical-outcome-prediction-from-serum-metabolomics
skills.search_text: clinical-outcome-prediction-from-serum-metabolomics Use when you have a serum metabolomics feature matrix (mzLearn-derived MS1 peaks, e.g. 2,736 features) with clinical labels (IMDC class, OS time/event) and need to predict treatment response or survival in a new patient cohort. Input is raw LC/MS mzML files rather than an already-generated mzLearn feature table — use the mzLearn signal-detection skill first. Data comes from an LC mode or ionization mode other than HILIC positive — the pre-trained model is specific to that mode and transfer may be invalid. Goal is de novo compound identification or de-isotoping — mzLearn outputs are limited to the ion MS1 level and downstream annotation must use separate workflows. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fine-tunes a pre-trained metabolomics variational autoencoder (VAE) on baseline serum LC/MS feature matrices to predict clinical outcomes such as ICI response and overall survival in renal cell carcinoma, outperforming randomly initialized and traditional ML baselines via transfer learning. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Fine-tunes a pre-trained metabolomics variational autoencoder (VAE) on baseline serum LC/MS feature matrices to predict clinical outcomes such as ICI response and overall survival in renal cell carcinoma, outperforming randomly initialized and traditional ML baselines via transfer learning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC/MS mzML files rather than an already-generated mzLearn feature table — use the mzLearn signal-detection skill first. Data comes from an LC mode or ionization mode other than HILIC positive — the pre-trained model is specific to that mode and transfer may be invalid. Goal is de novo compound identification or de-isotoping — mzLearn outputs are limited to the ion MS1 level and downstream annotation must use separate workflows.

skills.description: Use when a fitted MOFA (or DIABLO) model contains discriminant factors separating cohorts and you need to interpret those factors by correlating them with clinical/metadata variables and pathway/literature annotations.
skills.name: clinical-variable-factor-correlation
skills.search_text: clinical-variable-factor-correlation Use when a fitted MOFA (or DIABLO) model contains discriminant factors separating cohorts and you need to interpret those factors by correlating them with clinical/metadata variables and pathway/literature annotations. The multiomics data has not yet been integrated (no MOFA/DIABLO model fitted) — run the integration step first The analysis goal is single-omics differential analysis (DESeq2/Limma, ChAMP, TidyMass) rather than interpreting latent multiomics factors No clinical or metadata annotations are available to correlate against the factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Correlates discriminant MOFA factors (e.g., the five IGHV-discriminating factors in the CLL multiomics case study) with clinical annotations such as 11q22.3 deletion, trisomy 12, gender, and TP53/SF3B1/del17p13 status using BiomiX's factor-interpretation module, to assign biological/clinical meaning to latent factors. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Correlates discriminant MOFA factors (e.g., the five IGHV-discriminating factors in the CLL multiomics case study) with clinical annotations such as 11q22.3 deletion, trisomy 12, gender, and TP53/SF3B1/del17p13 status using BiomiX's factor-interpretation module, to assign biological/clinical meaning to latent factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The multiomics data has not yet been integrated (no MOFA/DIABLO model fitted) — run the integration step first The analysis goal is single-omics differential analysis (DESeq2/Limma, ChAMP, TidyMass) rather than interpreting latent multiomics factors No clinical or metadata annotations are available to correlate against the factors

skills.description: Use when you need a curated, review-status-filtered ClinVar variant set (two-star variants) with clinical-significance labels to benchmark annotation tools like ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP.
skills.name: clinvar-clinical-significance-classification
skills.search_text: clinvar-clinical-significance-classification Use when you need a curated, review-status-filtered ClinVar variant set (two-star variants) with clinical-significance labels to benchmark annotation tools like ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP. When the task requires variants of low or unspecified review status (the pipeline is restricted to two-star ClinVar records) When analyzing mitochondrial variants or large indels (≥50 bp) — these are explicitly excluded by the pipeline When the goal is discovery of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) rather than a labeled benchmark set http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Builds a high-confidence ClinVar test set of 164,549 two-star variants with defined clinical-significance labels (Pathogenic, Likely Pathogenic, Benign, Likely Benign) by downloading the January 7, 2024 ClinVar VCF and applying a normalization-plus-exclusion filtering chain. It serves as the gold-standard input for benchmarking variant annotation tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Builds a high-confidence ClinVar test set of 164,549 two-star variants with defined clinical-significance labels (Pathogenic, Likely Pathogenic, Benign, Likely Benign) by downloading the January 7, 2024 ClinVar VCF and applying a normalization-plus-exclusion filtering chain. It serves as the gold-standard input for benchmarking variant annotation tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task requires variants of low or unspecified review status (the pipeline is restricted to two-star ClinVar records) When analyzing mitochondrial variants or large indels (≥50 bp) — these are explicitly excluded by the pipeline When the goal is discovery of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) rather than a labeled benchmark set

skills.description: Use when building a benchmark set from ClinVar for comparing variant-annotation outputs or ACMG rule application and you need only variants with a high (two-star) review status.
skills.name: clinvar-high-review-status-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: clinvar-high-review-status-variant-filtering Use when building a benchmark set from ClinVar for comparing variant-annotation outputs or ACMG rule application and you need only variants with a high (two-star) review status. When the analysis goal is to survey ClinVar records with low or conflicting review status (e.g. one-star or 'no assertion provided' records) — this skill deliberately excludes them. When you need a clinically curated single-submitter variant set where expert panel (three-star) review exists — the two-star filter is a different, broader confidence tier. When the input is already a pre-filtered benchmark VCF (e.g. an in-house high-confidence set) and re-filtering would discard records that lack the two-star string but were independently validated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Filter the ClinVar variant set to 164,549 two-star (high review status) variants so that cross-tool annotation concordance (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) and downstream ACMG/PVS1 impact are evaluated on a ClinVar high-confidence benchmark rather than the full, uncurated ClinVar release. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Filter the ClinVar variant set to 164,549 two-star (high review status) variants so that cross-tool annotation concordance (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) and downstream ACMG/PVS1 impact are evaluated on a ClinVar high-confidence benchmark rather than the full, uncurated ClinVar release.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is to survey ClinVar records with low or conflicting review status (e.g. one-star or 'no assertion provided' records) — this skill deliberately excludes them. When you need a clinically curated single-submitter variant set where expert panel (three-star) review exists — the two-star filter is a different, broader confidence tier. When the input is already a pre-filtered benchmark VCF (e.g. an in-house high-confidence set) and re-filtering would discard records that lack the two-star string but were independently validated.

skills.description: Use when you need a trusted ClinVar reference set of HGVSc/HGVSp and coding-impact strings (e.g., 164,549 two-star variants) to benchmark HGVS output from annotation tools like ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP.
skills.name: clinvar-reference-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: clinvar-reference-annotation-parsing Use when you need a trusted ClinVar reference set of HGVSc/HGVSp and coding-impact strings (e.g., 164,549 two-star variants) to benchmark HGVS output from annotation tools like ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP. When the goal is to annotate novel variants de novo rather than benchmark tool output against a ClinVar-derived reference set When ClinVar annotations are taken from ClinVar web pages rather than the VCF, since inconsistencies exist between ClinVar web pages and its VCF When the analysis targets low-review-status ClinVar entries, which are not the curated high-review (two-star) reference population used to validate this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Builds a ClinVar-derived reference annotation set (HGVSc, HGVSp, and predicted coding impact strings) from high-review-status (two-star) ClinVar variants, then string-matches tool-reported HGVS annotations against it to compute concordance rates and per-tool match fractions. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Builds a ClinVar-derived reference annotation set (HGVSc, HGVSp, and predicted coding impact strings) from high-review-status (two-star) ClinVar variants, then string-matches tool-reported HGVS annotations against it to compute concordance rates and per-tool match fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to annotate novel variants de novo rather than benchmark tool output against a ClinVar-derived reference set When ClinVar annotations are taken from ClinVar web pages rather than the VCF, since inconsistencies exist between ClinVar web pages and its VCF When the analysis targets low-review-status ClinVar entries, which are not the curated high-review (two-star) reference population used to validate this skill

skills.description: Use when the analysis goal is to quantify how annotation tool discrepancies in PVS1/PP3 calls translate into ACMG classification changes, requiring implementation of the 2015 ACMG rule engine with the paper's thresholds on ClinVar high-review-status variants.
skills.name: clinvar-variant-classification
skills.search_text: clinvar-variant-classification Use when the analysis goal is to quantify how annotation tool discrepancies in PVS1/PP3 calls translate into ACMG classification changes, requiring implementation of the 2015 ACMG rule engine with the paper's thresholds on ClinVar high-review-status variants. When the input variant set is not restricted to high-review-status ClinVar two-star variants, as the paper's PP5/BP6 star-based strength mapping is calibrated to that population When the analysis requires rules outside the GDK rule set (e.g. PS4, PM3, PP4, BP2, BP5), which are explicitly excluded from this engine http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Reconstructs the GDK platform's ACMG 2015 rule engine (PVS1 from LoF coding impact, PP3 thresholds of CADD>25.3 or SpliceAI>0.5, star-based PP5/BP6 strength) to reproduce the reported PLP downgrade rates (ANNOVAR 55.9%, SnpEff 66.5%, VEP 67.3%) observed when annotation tool discrepancies alter PVS1 calls. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Reconstructs the GDK platform's ACMG 2015 rule engine (PVS1 from LoF coding impact, PP3 thresholds of CADD>25.3 or SpliceAI>0.5, star-based PP5/BP6 strength) to reproduce the reported PLP downgrade rates (ANNOVAR 55.9%, SnpEff 66.5%, VEP 67.3%) observed when annotation tool discrepancies alter PVS1 calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input variant set is not restricted to high-review-status ClinVar two-star variants, as the paper's PP5/BP6 star-based strength mapping is calibrated to that population When the analysis requires rules outside the GDK rule set (e.g. PS4, PM3, PP4, BP2, BP5), which are explicitly excluded from this engine

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a variant annotation pipeline (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) produces HGVS nomenclature and coding-impact calls consistent with ClinVar high-review-status (two-star) variants, and when quantifying which mismatch classes (NA, position/variant-type, non-preferred syntax) dominate.
skills.name: clinvar-variant-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: clinvar-variant-concordance-analysis Use when evaluating whether a variant annotation pipeline (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) produces HGVS nomenclature and coding-impact calls consistent with ClinVar high-review-status (two-star) variants, and when quantifying which mismatch classes (NA, position/variant-type, non-preferred syntax) dominate. When the goal is metabolomics-genomics linkage or natural product mining — the README context (NPLinker, GNPS/AntiSMASH data) is unrelated to variant annotation concordance. When the variant set is not ClinVar high-review-status (two-star); applying this skill to lower-review-status or non-ClinVar variants will not reproduce the reported concordance thresholds. When the three tools cannot be run on identical reference genomes and transcript annotations; tool-version or transcript-set divergence inflates apparent mismatches beyond what the method can diagnose. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Benchmark ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP HGVSc/HGVSp nomenclature and coding-impact calls against ClinVar two-star variants (164,549 high review-status records), computing per-tool concordance (e.g. 58.52% HGVSc, 84.04% HGVSp, 85.58% coding impact) and diagnosing mismatch categories such as missing NA annotations, position/variant-type differences, and non-preferred HGVS syntax. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Benchmark ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP HGVSc/HGVSp nomenclature and coding-impact calls against ClinVar two-star variants (164,549 high review-status records), computing per-tool concordance (e.g. 58.52% HGVSc, 84.04% HGVSp, 85.58% coding impact) and diagnosing mismatch categories such as missing NA annotations, position/variant-type differences, and non-preferred HGVS syntax.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is metabolomics-genomics linkage or natural product mining — the README context (NPLinker, GNPS/AntiSMASH data) is unrelated to variant annotation concordance. When the variant set is not ClinVar high-review-status (two-star); applying this skill to lower-review-status or non-ClinVar variants will not reproduce the reported concordance thresholds. When the three tools cannot be run on identical reference genomes and transcript annotations; tool-version or transcript-set divergence inflates apparent mismatches beyond what the method can diagnose.

skills.description: Use when a multi-omics cohort (transcriptomics, methylomics, metabolomics) carries binary condition labels such as mutated vs unmutated IGHV, and the goal is to fine-tune a MOFA model to find and interpret the factors that discriminate the two patient groups.
skills.name: cll-ighv-cohort-discriminant-factor-analysis
skills.search_text: cll-ighv-cohort-discriminant-factor-analysis Use when a multi-omics cohort (transcriptomics, methylomics, metabolomics) carries binary condition labels such as mutated vs unmutated IGHV, and the goal is to fine-tune a MOFA model to find and interpret the factors that discriminate the two patient groups. Input omics types outside BiomiX's supported set — proteomics and genomics are not yet supported, so a proteomics-only or genomics-only dataset is the wrong fit Analysis goal is clustering without labeled cohorts — BiomiX's MOFA factor-tuning and discriminant-factor interpretation is designed for cohort-distinguishing models with condition labels Data has not been reviewed by the user — BiomiX strongly recommends manual dataset review before use and performs no automated validation, so blindly feeding uncurated data is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Runs the BiomiX multi-omics integration workflow on the CLL transcriptomics–methylomics–metabolomics dataset to tune a ten-factor MOFA model, identify the five factors that discriminate mutated vs unmutated IGHV patients, and annotate those factors via clinical correlation, EnrichR/GSEA pathways, and PubMed literature mining. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Runs the BiomiX multi-omics integration workflow on the CLL transcriptomics–methylomics–metabolomics dataset to tune a ten-factor MOFA model, identify the five factors that discriminate mutated vs unmutated IGHV patients, and annotate those factors via clinical correlation, EnrichR/GSEA pathways, and PubMed literature mining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input omics types outside BiomiX's supported set — proteomics and genomics are not yet supported, so a proteomics-only or genomics-only dataset is the wrong fit Analysis goal is clustering without labeled cohorts — BiomiX's MOFA factor-tuning and discriminant-factor interpretation is designed for cohort-distinguishing models with condition labels Data has not been reviewed by the user — BiomiX strongly recommends manual dataset review before use and performs no automated validation, so blindly feeding uncurated data is inappropriate

skills.description: Use when you must verify that an acquisition-function implementation (EI over a fitted GP surrogate) reproduces the analytic closed-form values before trusting argmax-based gradient or parameter selection.
skills.name: closed-form-acquisition-numerical-validation
skills.search_text: closed-form-acquisition-numerical-validation Use when you must verify that an acquisition-function implementation (EI over a fitted GP surrogate) reproduces the analytic closed-form values before trusting argmax-based gradient or parameter selection. No peptide-level ground truth is available — conditional entropy of the cluster distribution given peptide assignments requires PSM identifications to label clusters; use it only when peptide labels exist. The goal is computational runtime benchmarking rather than clustering-quality assessment — the article separates quality metrics (completeness, incorrectly-clustered fraction) from performance comparison. Analyzing metabolomics or top-down data with falcon defaults — preprocessing settings (min_peaks=5, min_mz_range=250, min_mz=101, max_mz=500) are intended for bottom-up proteomics and must be adjusted, invalidating the ~1% operating-point thresholds. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 An information-theoretic evaluation of MS/MS spectrum clustering quality: cluster completeness is computed as one minus the conditional entropy of the cluster distribution given peptide assignments, normalized by the maximum entropy reduction those peptide assignments could provide. It enables fair cross-tool comparison of clustering purity at a matched (~1%) incorrectly-clustered-spectra operating point. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a CNN that classifies compound presence in 1D NMR mixture spectra despite chemical shift variation and peak overlap, and an augmentable spectral dataset with binary labels is available.
skills.name: cnn-architecture-implementation-for-spectra
skills.search_text: cnn-architecture-implementation-for-spectra Use when building or reproducing a CNN that classifies compound presence in 1D NMR mixture spectra despite chemical shift variation and peak overlap, and an augmentable spectral dataset with binary labels is available. The task concerns pure single-compound spectra rather than mixtures — the method targets chemical shift variation and peak overlapping among molecules in mixtures No spectral database or reference NMR spectra exist to generate the augmented training data by superposition with random noises Only a small experimental dataset without augmentation is available — reported performance degrades on real data (e.g. ACC = 91.67% on the additional flavor mixture dataset) http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements the pseudo-Siamese convolutional neural network (pSCNN) from Wei et al. 2022 for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures: two identically architected subnetworks with separately trained weights (6 conv layers, 32 kernels of 5×1, ReLU, max pooling) feeding a concatenated 100-unit dense layer with dropout 0.2 and a Sigmoid output. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Implements the pseudo-Siamese convolutional neural network (pSCNN) from Wei et al. 2022 for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures: two identically architected subnetworks with separately trained weights (6 conv layers, 32 kernels of 5×1, ReLU, max pooling) feeding a concatenated 100-unit dense layer with dropout 0.2 and a Sigmoid output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task concerns pure single-compound spectra rather than mixtures — the method targets chemical shift variation and peak overlapping among molecules in mixtures No spectral database or reference NMR spectra exist to generate the augmented training data by superposition with random noises Only a small experimental dataset without augmentation is available — reported performance degrades on real data (e.g. ACC = 91.67% on the additional flavor mixture dataset)

skills.description: Use when you have raw LC-MS/MS data for many biological samples (e.g., 545 wild soybean accessions) plus a binary or binned bioactivity endpoint (DPPH, elastase, TFC, TPC) and want end-to-end activity prediction without compound annotation.
skills.name: cnn-bioactivity-classification
skills.search_text: cnn-bioactivity-classification Use when you have raw LC-MS/MS data for many biological samples (e.g., 545 wild soybean accessions) plus a binary or binned bioactivity endpoint (DPPH, elastase, TFC, TPC) and want end-to-end activity prediction without compound annotation. Input is already an aligned feature table or you have structurally annotated metabolites with per-compound features — this skill is specifically for raw, unaligned LC-MS/MS fragmentation data You need feature-level interpretation (which metabolite drives activity); the image-based fingerprint approach bypasses compound identification entirely Data comes from a non-MS platform or lacks MS/MS fragmentation information (no precursor/fragment m/z pairs) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Trains a convolutional neural network on 2D grayscale molecular fingerprint images rendered from raw LC-MS/MS data (MS1 m/z on x-axis, MS2 m/z on y-axis, intensities encoded as size/grayscale) to predict bioactivity of natural product extracts without prior compound identification or feature alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Trains a convolutional neural network on 2D grayscale molecular fingerprint images rendered from raw LC-MS/MS data (MS1 m/z on x-axis, MS2 m/z on y-axis, intensities encoded as size/grayscale) to predict bioactivity of natural product extracts without prior compound identification or feature alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table or you have structurally annotated metabolites with per-compound features — this skill is specifically for raw, unaligned LC-MS/MS fragmentation data You need feature-level interpretation (which metabolite drives activity); the image-based fingerprint approach bypasses compound identification entirely Data comes from a non-MS platform or lacks MS/MS fragmentation information (no precursor/fragment m/z pairs)

skills.description: Use when raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms (local maxima in rt x mz space) must be separated into true chromatographic peaks versus irrelevant background signals, and peak-center/bounding-box annotations are needed for downstream feature grouping.
skills.name: cnn-chromatographic-peak-classification
skills.search_text: cnn-chromatographic-peak-classification Use when raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms (local maxima in rt x mz space) must be separated into true chromatographic peaks versus irrelevant background signals, and peak-center/bounding-box annotations are needed for downstream feature grouping. Input is already a feature table or peak-picked feature list rather than LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms — PeakBot operates on profile-mode data via local-maxima detection. Chromatograms contain co-eluting isomers within the reference features, since the gradient-descend reference extraction requires no co-eluting compounds (isomers). Fewer than 100 distinct reference features (including isotopologs) are available, so the CNN cannot be trained to high-quality peak-picking results. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Classify every local-maxima-derived standardized rt x mz area from an LC-HRMS chromatogram as a chromatographic peak versus background signal (walls, etc.) using a PeakBot convolutional neural network, also predicting peak-center and bounding-box for true peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Classify every local-maxima-derived standardized rt x mz area from an LC-HRMS chromatogram as a chromatographic peak versus background signal (walls, etc.) using a PeakBot convolutional neural network, also predicting peak-center and bounding-box for true peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or peak-picked feature list rather than LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms — PeakBot operates on profile-mode data via local-maxima detection. Chromatograms contain co-eluting isomers within the reference features, since the gradient-descend reference extraction requires no co-eluting compounds (isomers). Fewer than 100 distinct reference features (including isotopologs) are available, so the CNN cannot be trained to high-quality peak-picking results.

skills.summary: Runs a trained convolutional neural network (MS2toImg-CNN, Keras/TensorFlow) on 2D grayscale molecular-fingerprint images built from raw LC-MS/MS data to predict binary bioactivity class, then scores predictions (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC) under stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

skills.description: Use when a trained NMR spectrum-to-structure CNN (e.g., DeepSAT) needs interpretability: you want to know which regions of an HSQC spectrum drive fingerprint or class predictions, to validate that the model associates chemical-shift peaks with real functional groups.
skills.name: cnn-model-interpretation-nmr
skills.search_text: cnn-model-interpretation-nmr Use when a trained NMR spectrum-to-structure CNN (e.g., DeepSAT) needs interpretability: you want to know which regions of an HSQC spectrum drive fingerprint or class predictions, to validate that the model associates chemical-shift peaks with real functional groups. You need to identify or annotate an unknown compound's structure — this skill only explains model decisions, it does not perform the retrieval or classification itself (use DeepSAT's /api/smart3/search endpoint for that). The model's input format or metadata endpoint has changed — the README notes that model input names must be updated in the code if they change, so interpretability output would be invalid until re-integrated. You require a formal or quantitative attribution metric with error bars — the article notes the occlusion results 'do not fully explain the decision-making process of DeepSAT' and were assessed qualitatively for a single compound. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Applies occlusion sensitivity to a trained DeepSAT convolutional neural network that predicts chemical fingerprints, molecular weights, and structure classes from 1H-13C HSQC spectra, generating per-peak attribution maps that link specific HSQC cross-peaks to molecular substructures. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Applies occlusion sensitivity to a trained DeepSAT convolutional neural network that predicts chemical fingerprints, molecular weights, and structure classes from 1H-13C HSQC spectra, generating per-peak attribution maps that link specific HSQC cross-peaks to molecular substructures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to identify or annotate an unknown compound's structure — this skill only explains model decisions, it does not perform the retrieval or classification itself (use DeepSAT's /api/smart3/search endpoint for that). The model's input format or metadata endpoint has changed — the README notes that model input names must be updated in the code if they change, so interpretability output would be invalid until re-integrated. You require a formal or quantitative attribution metric with error bars — the article notes the occlusion results 'do not fully explain the decision-making process of DeepSAT' and were assessed qualitatively for a single compound.

skills.description: Use when the input is a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (normal or multiplicity-edited) as a peak list with 1H/13C shift pairs, and the goal is to infer a fingerprint, molecular weight, and structure class for later similarity search against chemical databases.
skills.name: cnn-multi-task-fingerprint-inference
skills.search_text: cnn-multi-task-fingerprint-inference Use when the input is a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (normal or multiplicity-edited) as a peak list with 1H/13C shift pairs, and the goal is to infer a fingerprint, molecular weight, and structure class for later similarity search against chemical databases. The goal is exact library matching against curated reference spectra (e.g. MetaboMiner/COLMAR-style search) rather than fingerprint-based inference over chemical databases — DeepSAT's baseline library search on NMRshiftDB achieved under 3% correct identifications, and the CNN approach is designed for database-scale search, not reference-library lookup. The input spectrum is not a 1H-13C HSQC or multiplicity-edited HSQC spectrum (e.g. 13C-only, COSY, MS/MS fragmentation spectra) — the model was trained exclusively on 1H-13C HSQC spectra. A fully explained, mechanistic structure assignment is required — the authors note occlusion sensitivity results 'do not fully explain the decision-making process of DeepSAT', and interpretability was only demonstrated on a single compound (quercetin). http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Run the DeepSAT convolutional neural network, trained on 143,467 1H-13C HSQC spectra, to convert a query HSQC peak list into predicted 6144-bit Morgan fingerprint bit strings, molecular weights, and NPClassifier structure classes that can then be searched against chemical databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Run the DeepSAT convolutional neural network, trained on 143,467 1H-13C HSQC spectra, to convert a query HSQC peak list into predicted 6144-bit Morgan fingerprint bit strings, molecular weights, and NPClassifier structure classes that can then be searched against chemical databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exact library matching against curated reference spectra (e.g. MetaboMiner/COLMAR-style search) rather than fingerprint-based inference over chemical databases — DeepSAT's baseline library search on NMRshiftDB achieved under 3% correct identifications, and the CNN approach is designed for database-scale search, not reference-library lookup. The input spectrum is not a 1H-13C HSQC or multiplicity-edited HSQC spectrum (e.g. 13C-only, COSY, MS/MS fragmentation spectra) — the model was trained exclusively on 1H-13C HSQC spectra. A fully explained, mechanistic structure assignment is required — the authors note occlusion sensitivity results 'do not fully explain the decision-making process of DeepSAT', and interpretability was only demonstrated on a single compound (quercetin).

skills.summary: Fine-tunes a ResNet-50 CNN pretrained on ImageNet with fastai/PyTorch to classify ion images from imaging mass spectrometry as off-sample vs on-sample, reproducing expert tagger judgements with off-sample F1 = 0.97 ± 0.01 on a 23,238-image gold standard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pixel-level segmentation of off-sample regions within an image — the paper states 'our approach does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region' Training-time budget is limited: the deep network requires days on a GPU-equipped power station, so semi-automated biclustering (F1 0.96) or molecular co-localization (F1 0.90) may be preferable No labeled gold standard exists for the domain; transfer learning still requires expert-tagged images for fine-tuning and validation

skills.description: Decision support for quantifying gene-level CNV deletion frequency in GutUDB colorectal cancer data and cross-referencing it against the RNA expression annotation to assess whether copy-number state and transcript level are coupled.
skills.name: cnv-frequency-extraction
skills.search_text: cnv-frequency-extraction Decision support for quantifying gene-level CNV deletion frequency in GutUDB colorectal cancer data and cross-referencing it against the RNA expression annotation to assess whether copy-number state and transcript level are coupled. The task concerns SNP or structural-variation (SV) calls rather than CNV deletion frequency — GutUDB tracks 72,248 SNPs and 1097 SVs separately from its 54,131 CNVs. A quantitative correlation coefficient or statistical test between CNV and RNA expression across a gene panel is required; this skill only captures GutUDB's annotated frequency value and the article's qualitative weak-correlation statement. skills.description: Use when replicate (blind duplicate) measurements are available for NMR metabolic biomarker data and you need to quantify and compare measurement reproducibility (CV%, R2) before and after a quality control or technical-variation-removal procedure.
