skills.search_text: coefficient-of-variation-estimation Use when replicate (blind duplicate) measurements are available for NMR metabolic biomarker data and you need to quantify and compare measurement reproducibility (CV%, R2) before and after a quality control or technical-variation-removal procedure. No replicate/blind duplicate measurements exist in the dataset, so reproducibility cannot be assessed within-sample You intend to assess the QC procedure itself rather than quantify reproducibility — remove_technical_variation() requires unfiltered input and performs no outlier filtering of samples itself You are working with derived/composite biomarkers or ratios, which should be recomputed post-adjustment from the 107 non-derived biomarkers instead Quantifies measurement reproducibility of UK Biobank NMR metabolic biomarkers by computing within-sample coefficient of variation (CV%) via the root mean square approach and coefficient of determination (R2) across 3,169 blind duplicate samples, for the 107 non-derived biomarkers, both on original and QC-processed (remove_technical_variation) concentrations. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: Quantifies measurement reproducibility of UK Biobank NMR metabolic biomarkers by computing within-sample coefficient of variation (CV%) via the root mean square approach and coefficient of determination (R2) across 3,169 blind duplicate samples, for the 107 non-derived biomarkers, both on original and QC-processed (remove_technical_variation) concentrations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No replicate/blind duplicate measurements exist in the dataset, so reproducibility cannot be assessed within-sample You intend to assess the QC procedure itself rather than quantify reproducibility — remove_technical_variation() requires unfiltered input and performs no outlier filtering of samples itself You are working with derived/composite biomarkers or ratios, which should be recomputed post-adjustment from the 107 non-derived biomarkers instead

skills.description: Use when a candidate batch-correction output on multi-batch metabolomics data must be checked for variance inflation: compute per-feature VCs before and after normalization and the fraction of features whose VC increased by >=5% (allowed_vc_increase).
skills.name: coefficient-of-variation-inflation-quantification
skills.search_text: coefficient-of-variation-inflation-quantification Use when a candidate batch-correction output on multi-batch metabolomics data must be checked for variance inflation: compute per-feature VCs before and after normalization and the fraction of features whose VC increased by >=5% (allowed_vc_increase). Single-batch datasets with no reference samples replicated across batches — VC inflation relative to batch effects cannot be assessed as designed Batches that have not first been normalized individually to suppress intrabatch LC-MS temporal drifts, which RALPS-based benchmarking assumes as a prerequisite Assessing a method on VC inflation alone without replicate cross-correlation and qualitative spectrum preservation, which risks selecting an over-shrinking normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantify how much a batch-correction method inflates per-feature coefficients of variation (VCs) relative to the input data, a core criterion in the RALPS benchmark where RALPS was the only method of seven (ComBat, EigenMS, LEV+EIG, PQN+POW, WaveICA, NormAE) to suppress batch bias while controlling VC expansion. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096
skills.summary: Quantify how much a batch-correction method inflates per-feature coefficients of variation (VCs) relative to the input data, a core criterion in the RALPS benchmark where RALPS was the only method of seven (ComBat, EigenMS, LEV+EIG, PQN+POW, WaveICA, NormAE) to suppress batch bias while controlling VC expansion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-batch datasets with no reference samples replicated across batches — VC inflation relative to batch effects cannot be assessed as designed Batches that have not first been normalized individually to suppress intrabatch LC-MS temporal drifts, which RALPS-based benchmarking assumes as a prerequisite Assessing a method on VC inflation alone without replicate cross-correlation and qualitative spectrum preservation, which risks selecting an over-shrinking normalization

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch metabolomics feature-count matrix has been normalized (e.g. by RALPS) and you need QC metrics — batch-wise VC and replicate cross-correlation — to judge whether batch effects were reduced.
skills.name: coefficient-of-variation-qc-assessment
skills.search_text: coefficient-of-variation-qc-assessment Use when a multi-batch metabolomics feature-count matrix has been normalized (e.g. by RALPS) and you need QC metrics — batch-wise VC and replicate cross-correlation — to judge whether batch effects were reduced. Data is raw and not yet batch-normalized — intrabatch drifts should first be removed by normalizing each batch individually before computing cross-batch VC metrics Data contains no replicate or reference sample groups (e.g. NIST 1950 SRM or pooled samples) present across batches, so replicate cross-correlation and within-batch-replicate VC cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assess normalization quality of multi-batch metabolomics data by computing replicate cross-correlations and batch-wise coefficients of variation (VC) of the normalized data, the primary QC metrics used by RALPS alongside clustering criteria. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096
skills.summary: Assess normalization quality of multi-batch metabolomics data by computing replicate cross-correlations and batch-wise coefficients of variation (VC) of the normalized data, the primary QC metrics used by RALPS alongside clustering criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is raw and not yet batch-normalized — intrabatch drifts should first be removed by normalizing each batch individually before computing cross-batch VC metrics Data contains no replicate or reference sample groups (e.g. NIST 1950 SRM or pooled samples) present across batches, so replicate cross-correlation and within-batch-replicate VC cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when a feature abundance table from MS-DIAL (with a sample annotation file labeling QC vs biological samples) needs quality filtering based on the ratio of coefficient of variation across samples vs QCs.
skills.name: coefficient-of-variation-ratio-filtering-samples-vs-qc
skills.search_text: coefficient-of-variation-ratio-filtering-samples-vs-qc Use when a feature abundance table from MS-DIAL (with a sample annotation file labeling QC vs biological samples) needs quality filtering based on the ratio of coefficient of variation across samples vs QCs. Input features have already passed CV-ratio filtering or the analysis goal is imputation/normalization (e.g. probabilistic quotient normalization) rather than reproducibility-based feature removal The dataset contains no pooled QC injections, so the CV(samples)/CV(QC) ratio cannot be computed The data are raw instrument files rather than the two tab-delimited margheRita inputs (feature data file plus sample annotation file) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A margheRita pre-processing filter for LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics that keeps only features whose CV ratio between no-QC biological samples and pooled QC samples exceeds a threshold (default 1), removing metabolites with unacceptable technical reproducibility. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.06.20.599545
skills.summary: A margheRita pre-processing filter for LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics that keeps only features whose CV ratio between no-QC biological samples and pooled QC samples exceeds a threshold (default 1), removing metabolites with unacceptable technical reproducibility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features have already passed CV-ratio filtering or the analysis goal is imputation/normalization (e.g. probabilistic quotient normalization) rather than reproducibility-based feature removal The dataset contains no pooled QC injections, so the CV(samples)/CV(QC) ratio cannot be computed The data are raw instrument files rather than the two tab-delimited margheRita inputs (feature data file plus sample annotation file)

skills.description: Use when a metabonomic feature matrix is accompanied by a per-feature CV table and non-reproducible spectral features must be removed before downstream MWAS analysis.
skills.name: coefficient-of-variation-thresholding
skills.search_text: coefficient-of-variation-thresholding Use when a metabonomic feature matrix is accompanied by a per-feature CV table and non-reproducible spectral features must be removed before downstream MWAS analysis. The dataset has no quality-control replicates or CV table, so no reproducibility criterion can be computed — association-model steps of MWASTools are more appropriate. The feature matrix is not a SummarizedExperiment of metabonomic (e.g. 1H NMR) features; CV_filter expects the metabo_SE/metabo_CV structures. The goal is phenotype association testing or STOCSY metabolite assignment rather than QC filtering of features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Filters a metabonomic SummarizedExperiment so that only metabolomic features whose coefficient of variation (CV) across quality-control measurements is at or below a reproducibility cut-off (CV_th = 0.30) are retained. It is the reproducibility/QC filtering step of the MWASTools pipeline for 1H-NMR metabonomic data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Filters a metabonomic SummarizedExperiment so that only metabolomic features whose coefficient of variation (CV) across quality-control measurements is at or below a reproducibility cut-off (CV_th = 0.30) are retained. It is the reproducibility/QC filtering step of the MWASTools pipeline for 1H-NMR metabonomic data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no quality-control replicates or CV table, so no reproducibility criterion can be computed — association-model steps of MWASTools are more appropriate. The feature matrix is not a SummarizedExperiment of metabonomic (e.g. 1H NMR) features; CV_filter expects the metabo_SE/metabo_CV structures. The goal is phenotype association testing or STOCSY metabolite assignment rather than QC filtering of features.

skills.description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS MRM chromatograms (mzML or vendor-converted raw data) where targeted compounds have coeluting isomers or neighbors on one side of the peak, and accurate per-isomer quantitation requires splitting those overlapping peaks before regression or abundance normalization.
skills.name: coeluted-peak-deconvolution
skills.search_text: coeluted-peak-deconvolution Use when processing LC-MS/MS MRM chromatograms (mzML or vendor-converted raw data) where targeted compounds have coeluting isomers or neighbors on one side of the peak, and accurate per-isomer quantitation requires splitting those overlapping peaks before regression or abundance normalization. Input is already a quantitation table of peak areas and abundances — deconvolution is a pre-quantitation chromatogram step, not a post-hoc table operation. The chromatogram contains only one well-separated peak for the targeted compound with no neighboring tips within the 2.5x HWHM bound; automatic deconvolution adds overhead without changing the result. The tool being used cannot represent split/valley boundaries per isomer (e.g., TargetLynx-style valley-connecting baselines), so deconvolution output cannot be faithfully reproduced. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A quantitative-peak resolution procedure from the MRMQuant targeted-metabolomics paper: detect candidate peak tips in each MRM ion chromatogram with dynamic smoothing, trace valley boundaries with half-width-at-half-maximum (HWHM) and coelution flags, and deconvolute coeluted isomer peaks so their abundances are correctly attributed rather than merged into a single compound. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: A quantitative-peak resolution procedure from the MRMQuant targeted-metabolomics paper: detect candidate peak tips in each MRM ion chromatogram with dynamic smoothing, trace valley boundaries with half-width-at-half-maximum (HWHM) and coelution flags, and deconvolute coeluted isomer peaks so their abundances are correctly attributed rather than merged into a single compound.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantitation table of peak areas and abundances — deconvolution is a pre-quantitation chromatogram step, not a post-hoc table operation. The chromatogram contains only one well-separated peak for the targeted compound with no neighboring tips within the 2.5x HWHM bound; automatic deconvolution adds overhead without changing the result. The tool being used cannot represent split/valley boundaries per isomer (e.g., TargetLynx-style valley-connecting baselines), so deconvolution output cannot be faithfully reproduced.

skills.description: Use when an MRM ion chromatogram contains overlapping/coeluted peaks for a targeted compound (e.g., isomers sharing a transition, like the PC 34:3 isomers at RTs 4.72, 4.84, and 4.92 min) and per-peak abundances must be separated.
skills.name: coeluted-peak-fitting
skills.search_text: coeluted-peak-fitting Use when an MRM ion chromatogram contains overlapping/coeluted peaks for a targeted compound (e.g., isomers sharing a transition, like the PC 34:3 isomers at RTs 4.72, 4.84, and 4.92 min) and per-peak abundances must be separated. Peaks are baseline-resolved with no coelution — simple integration suffices and Gaussian fitting adds assumptions The chromatogram is dominated by noise or has unevenly sampled signal, where deconvolution fits are unreliable (MRMkit and Skyline showed problematic quantitation of noisy peaks and peaks with unevenly sampled signals) The goal is batch-effect correction or standard-curve regression rather than peak separation — other MRMQuant workflow steps apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Gaussian-based deconvolution of coeluted peaks in MRM ion chromatograms, as implemented in MRMQuant: fit overlapping Gaussian models at detected peak tips so the summed signals minimize the difference to the extracted signal union, then use each fitted peak height as the compound's abundance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Gaussian-based deconvolution of coeluted peaks in MRM ion chromatograms, as implemented in MRMQuant: fit overlapping Gaussian models at detected peak tips so the summed signals minimize the difference to the extracted signal union, then use each fitted peak height as the compound's abundance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks are baseline-resolved with no coelution — simple integration suffices and Gaussian fitting adds assumptions The chromatogram is dominated by noise or has unevenly sampled signal, where deconvolution fits are unreliable (MRMkit and Skyline showed problematic quantitation of noisy peaks and peaks with unevenly sampled signals) The goal is batch-effect correction or standard-curve regression rather than peak separation — other MRMQuant workflow steps apply

skills.description: Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' directories plus MS1-level HRMS data and need to group co-eluting MS1 ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments) into composite spectra clusters for chemical annotation without MS2 data.
skills.name: coeluting-ion-correlation-grouping
skills.search_text: coeluting-ion-correlation-grouping Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' directories plus MS1-level HRMS data and need to group co-eluting MS1 ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments) into composite spectra clusters for chemical annotation without MS2 data. When MS/MS fragmentation spectra are already available and the goal is conventional MS2 spectral-library annotation rather than MS1-only composite spectra reconstruction. When chromatographic peak detection/alignment has not yet been performed — the skill requires IDSL.IPA 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' outputs as prerequisites; raw mzXML/mzML/netCDF alone is insufficient. When the analysis is DDA or DIA (MS^E, AIF, SWATH-MS) deconvolution rather than MS1-only Composite Spectra Analysis — select a different workflow in PARAM0001. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Deconvolves MS1-only LC/HRMS data by grouping co-eluting ions into composite spectra (CSA) clusters: seed peaks are ranked by signal-to-noise, candidate neighbors within a retention-time window are correlated on LOESS+cubic-spline smoothed EICs (Pearson >= 0.98), and qualifying ions are aggregated into CSA clusters written to aligned_spectra_table.csv. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00376
skills.summary: Deconvolves MS1-only LC/HRMS data by grouping co-eluting ions into composite spectra (CSA) clusters: seed peaks are ranked by signal-to-noise, candidate neighbors within a retention-time window are correlated on LOESS+cubic-spline smoothed EICs (Pearson >= 0.98), and qualifying ions are aggregated into CSA clusters written to aligned_spectra_table.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When MS/MS fragmentation spectra are already available and the goal is conventional MS2 spectral-library annotation rather than MS1-only composite spectra reconstruction. When chromatographic peak detection/alignment has not yet been performed — the skill requires IDSL.IPA 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' outputs as prerequisites; raw mzXML/mzML/netCDF alone is insufficient. When the analysis is DDA or DIA (MS^E, AIF, SWATH-MS) deconvolution rather than MS1-only Composite Spectra Analysis — select a different workflow in PARAM0001.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS lipidomics peak table contains chromatographic features with multiple isobaric coeluting lipid spectral matches and you must quantify feature purity before assigning a confident identification.
skills.name: coeluting-isobaric-lipid-feature-analysis
skills.search_text: coeluting-isobaric-lipid-feature-analysis Use when an LC-MS/MS lipidomics peak table contains chromatographic features with multiple isobaric coeluting lipid spectral matches and you must quantify feature purity before assigning a confident identification. Features are already resolved and only statistical QC (e.g. QC-sample %RSD thresholding) is needed — Degreaser's automated threshold filtering alone suffices. The input is a single-purity, fully validated MS2 spectrum with no isobaric coelution, where purity estimation adds no information. Working outside lipidomics on proteomics or metabolomics feature tables, where lipid-specific fragmentation templates and purity logic do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Handles coeluting isobaric lipid species in LC-MS lipidomics by measuring spectral purity of lipid spectral matches and using it to estimate the purity of the associated chromatographic feature, so that peak identifications contaminated by overlapping isobars can be downgraded or flagged. Central to LipiDex/LipiDex 2's spectral matching and peak-annotation logic. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Handles coeluting isobaric lipid species in LC-MS lipidomics by measuring spectral purity of lipid spectral matches and using it to estimate the purity of the associated chromatographic feature, so that peak identifications contaminated by overlapping isobars can be downgraded or flagged. Central to LipiDex/LipiDex 2's spectral matching and peak-annotation logic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are already resolved and only statistical QC (e.g. QC-sample %RSD thresholding) is needed — Degreaser's automated threshold filtering alone suffices. The input is a single-purity, fully validated MS2 spectrum with no isobaric coelution, where purity estimation adds no information. Working outside lipidomics on proteomics or metabolomics feature tables, where lipid-specific fragmentation templates and purity logic do not apply.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking isotope-correction methods (ElemCor MDT/ULS, original ULS, NRE, FAM) on simulated or measured FAM for large sulfur- or nitrogen-containing metabolites at high nominal instrument resolution, or when validating 34S/13C correction accuracy for CoA-pathway metabolites.
skills.name: coenzyme-a-fractional-abundance-simulation
skills.search_text: coenzyme-a-fractional-abundance-simulation Use when benchmarking isotope-correction methods (ElemCor MDT/ULS, original ULS, NRE, FAM) on simulated or measured FAM for large sulfur- or nitrogen-containing metabolites at high nominal instrument resolution, or when validating 34S/13C correction accuracy for CoA-pathway metabolites. The compound set contains only low-mass metabolites for which MDT correction is recommended for cost efficiency and ULS is unnecessary The instrument operates at very low nominal resolution where ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor's combinatorial correction, making the resolution-dependent simulation uninformative The tracer element is not present in the compound formula (e.g. selecting C or S for a compound lacking those atoms causes the algorithm to error) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Simulates fractional abundance (FAM) data for high-mass coenzyme A derivatives (coenzyme A, acetyl-CoA, succinyl-CoA, HMG-CoA) under 13C, 15N, and 34S tracers at nominal Orbitrap resolution 280,000, to benchmark ElemCor's MDT/ULS corrections against original ULS, NRE, and no correction. This skill reproduces the paper's large-metabolite validation (Fig. 2a-c) showing that the original ULS method is excellent for 15N but much less accurate for 13C and 34S, whereas ElemCor resolves both. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Simulates fractional abundance (FAM) data for high-mass coenzyme A derivatives (coenzyme A, acetyl-CoA, succinyl-CoA, HMG-CoA) under 13C, 15N, and 34S tracers at nominal Orbitrap resolution 280,000, to benchmark ElemCor's MDT/ULS corrections against original ULS, NRE, and no correction. This skill reproduces the paper's large-metabolite validation (Fig. 2a-c) showing that the original ULS method is excellent for 15N but much less accurate for 13C and 34S, whereas ElemCor resolves both.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound set contains only low-mass metabolites for which MDT correction is recommended for cost efficiency and ULS is unnecessary The instrument operates at very low nominal resolution where ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor's combinatorial correction, making the resolution-dependent simulation uninformative The tracer element is not present in the compound formula (e.g. selecting C or S for a compound lacking those atoms causes the algorithm to error)

skills.description: Use when a MEANtools run on paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data has yielded FCs and you need to check whether genes from known pathways (e.g., GAME, PAL, 4CL, THT, HQT) land in them, or to benchmark clustering against known tomato specialized metabolism.
skills.name: coexpression-feature-cluster-annotation
skills.search_text: coexpression-feature-cluster-annotation Use when a MEANtools run on paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data has yielded FCs and you need to check whether genes from known pathways (e.g., GAME, PAL, 4CL, THT, HQT) land in them, or to benchmark clustering against known tomato specialized metabolism. When the goal is de novo discovery of unknown biosynthetic pathways rather than validating FC content against known pathway genes — for that use the MEANtools prediction step with RetroRules/LOTUS instead. When the input lacks paired transcriptomic-metabolomic samples from the same conditions, since MR-based correlation between transcripts and mass features cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Maps known biosynthetic genes (e.g., tomato HCAA, alpha-tomatine, and chlorogenic acid pathway genes) onto ClusterONE-derived overlapping feature clusters (FCs) produced by MEANtools, producing a gene-to-FC membership table that shows whether established specialized metabolism pathways co-cluster with correlated mass features. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Maps known biosynthetic genes (e.g., tomato HCAA, alpha-tomatine, and chlorogenic acid pathway genes) onto ClusterONE-derived overlapping feature clusters (FCs) produced by MEANtools, producing a gene-to-FC membership table that shows whether established specialized metabolism pathways co-cluster with correlated mass features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo discovery of unknown biosynthetic pathways rather than validating FC content against known pathway genes — for that use the MEANtools prediction step with RetroRules/LOTUS instead. When the input lacks paired transcriptomic-metabolomic samples from the same conditions, since MR-based correlation between transcripts and mass features cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when integrating paired transcriptomic–metabolomic data to group co-abundant mass features and transcripts into overlapping clusters (FCs), e.g. to capture metabolites correlated with biosynthetic genes prior to pathway reconstruction.
skills.name: coexpression-network-clustering
skills.search_text: coexpression-network-clustering Use when integrating paired transcriptomic–metabolomic data to group co-abundant mass features and transcripts into overlapping clusters (FCs), e.g. to capture metabolites correlated with biosynthetic genes prior to pathway reconstruction. The analysis goal is reaction-rules-based pathway reconstruction (e.g. mapping mass shifts via RetroRules/LOTUS) rather than statistical clustering of correlated features The dataset lacks paired transcriptomic and metabolomic samples, so transcript–mass feature correlations cannot be computed Only MS/MS spectral annotation of mass features is needed — MEANtools does not currently support loading MS/MS data or spectral library/networking-based annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Convert pairwise transcript–mass feature Pearson correlations into mutual ranks (MR), transform MRs into edge weights via an exponential decay function, and cluster the weighted network with ClusterONE to derive overlapping functional clusters (FCs) that group correlated metabolites and biosynthetic genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Convert pairwise transcript–mass feature Pearson correlations into mutual ranks (MR), transform MRs into edge weights via an exponential decay function, and cluster the weighted network with ClusterONE to derive overlapping functional clusters (FCs) that group correlated metabolites and biosynthetic genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is reaction-rules-based pathway reconstruction (e.g. mapping mass shifts via RetroRules/LOTUS) rather than statistical clustering of correlated features The dataset lacks paired transcriptomic and metabolomic samples, so transcript–mass feature correlations cannot be computed Only MS/MS spectral annotation of mass features is needed — MEANtools does not currently support loading MS/MS data or spectral library/networking-based annotation

skills.description: Use when implementing or re-running Pickaxe compound property filters (molecular weight range, atomic composition) where cofactor/coreactant entries in the starting-compound list must bypass the thresholds applied to all other compounds.
skills.name: cofactor-exemption-handling-in-filters
skills.search_text: cofactor-exemption-handling-in-filters Use when implementing or re-running Pickaxe compound property filters (molecular weight range, atomic composition) where cofactor/coreactant entries in the starting-compound list must bypass the thresholds applied to all other compounds. When the compound list contains no designated cofactors or coreactants — a plain range filter without exemptions is sufficient When the goal is to filter reactions rather than compounds (e.g. the thermodynamics filter removing reactions with physiological Gibbs free energy greater than 50 kJ/mol) http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Applies Pickaxe compound property filters while exempting designated cofactors from property thresholds, e.g. the atomic composition filter that limits non-cofactor molecules to fewer than twelve carbon atoms. This prevents ubiquitous small-molecule coreactants from being pruned simply because they violate size constraints meant for novel compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05149-8
skills.summary: Applies Pickaxe compound property filters while exempting designated cofactors from property thresholds, e.g. the atomic composition filter that limits non-cofactor molecules to fewer than twelve carbon atoms. This prevents ubiquitous small-molecule coreactants from being pruned simply because they violate size constraints meant for novel compounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compound list contains no designated cofactors or coreactants — a plain range filter without exemptions is sufficient When the goal is to filter reactions rather than compounds (e.g. the thermodynamics filter removing reactions with physiological Gibbs free energy greater than 50 kJ/mol)

skills.description: Use when mapping top predictor features (e.g., genes from CNV, methylation, transcriptomic, or proteomic ML models) onto a genome-scale metabolic reaction network to compute topological overlap with a target metabolite's reactions.
skills.name: cofactor-filtering-in-reaction-network-analysis
skills.search_text: cofactor-filtering-in-reaction-network-analysis Use when mapping top predictor features (e.g., genes from CNV, methylation, transcriptomic, or proteomic ML models) onto a genome-scale metabolic reaction network to compute topological overlap with a target metabolite's reactions. When the goal is flux balance or reaction activity analysis rather than topological proximity of predictor features to a metabolite's reactions When features are already gene-set members of the metabolite's own reactions and no first-degree-neighbor inference is intended (cofactor removal mainly guards neighbor-level overlap) Removes ubiquitous metabolic cofactors (ATP, ADP, water, hydrogen, phosphate, diphosphate) before computing network proximity between ML predictor features and metabolites in Recon3D, so that first-degree-neighbor overlap is not inflated by reactions connected only through common cofactors. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Removes ubiquitous metabolic cofactors (ATP, ADP, water, hydrogen, phosphate, diphosphate) before computing network proximity between ML predictor features and metabolites in Recon3D, so that first-degree-neighbor overlap is not inflated by reactions connected only through common cofactors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is flux balance or reaction activity analysis rather than topological proximity of predictor features to a metabolite's reactions When features are already gene-set members of the metabolite's own reactions and no first-degree-neighbor inference is intended (cofactor removal mainly guards neighbor-level overlap)

skills.description: Use when multiple human raters have independently labelled the same items (e.g. ion images as off-sample/on-sample/unknown) and you must report pairwise or multi-rater agreement coefficients to justify a gold standard.
skills.name: cohen-kappa-computation
skills.search_text: cohen-kappa-computation Use when multiple human raters have independently labelled the same items (e.g. ion images as off-sample/on-sample/unknown) and you must report pairwise or multi-rater agreement coefficients to justify a gold standard. When only a single rater's labels exist — kappa requires at least two raters over the same items When the goal is classifier accuracy evaluation against a single gold standard (use F1-score/precision-recall instead, as the paper does for the deep learning model) When raters labelled different (non-overlapping) sets of ion images — pairwise kappa requires shared items http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies inter-tagger and tagger-vs-curator agreement on off-sample ion image classifications using pairwise Cohen's kappa (scikit-learn cohen_kappa_score) over off-sample/on-sample/unknown labels, complemented by Krippendorff's alpha for multi-rater reliability. Used in OffsampleAI to validate that the 23,238-image gold standard reflects consistent expert judgements. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: Quantifies inter-tagger and tagger-vs-curator agreement on off-sample ion image classifications using pairwise Cohen's kappa (scikit-learn cohen_kappa_score) over off-sample/on-sample/unknown labels, complemented by Krippendorff's alpha for multi-rater reliability. Used in OffsampleAI to validate that the 23,238-image gold standard reflects consistent expert judgements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single rater's labels exist — kappa requires at least two raters over the same items When the goal is classifier accuracy evaluation against a single gold standard (use F1-score/precision-recall instead, as the paper does for the deep learning model) When raters labelled different (non-overlapping) sets of ion images — pairwise kappa requires shared items

skills.description: Use when flux-sampling FFD classifications and transcriptomics-derived RAS scores must be compared against metabolomics-derived RPS signs for the same irreversible reactions, to score per-reaction concordance across cell-line pairs.
skills.name: cohen-kappa-concordance-scoring
skills.search_text: cohen-kappa-concordance-scoring Use when flux-sampling FFD classifications and transcriptomics-derived RAS scores must be compared against metabolomics-derived RPS signs for the same irreversible reactions, to score per-reaction concordance across cell-line pairs. When the user only needs single-omics flux prediction (e.g. pure RAS scoring or pure FFD sampling) without cross-omics concordance — kappa scoring requires all three classification layers (RPS, RAS, FFD) computed on the same irreversible reaction set. The compound class already has comprehensive experimental spectra in public or commercial libraries (fewer than 50 acylcarnitine structures was the trigger for building CarniBlast) You need MSI level 1 identifications — in silico library matches only support precursor accurate mass + MS/MS matching (MSI level 2), not authentic-standard confirmation The analyte class lacks a well-defined core template and diagnostic fragment rules, so fragment prediction from template losses is not defensible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Enumerate chemically diverse lipid structures (e.g., acylcarnitines) combinatorially from a core template plus chain-modification classes, and predict their tandem MS/MS fragments to build an in silico spectral library (CarniBlast, 2,400 acylcarnitines in NIST MSP format) that fills the coverage gap of public/commercial libraries holding fewer than 50 acylcarnitine spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Enumerate chemically diverse lipid structures (e.g., acylcarnitines) combinatorially from a core template plus chain-modification classes, and predict their tandem MS/MS fragments to build an in silico spectral library (CarniBlast, 2,400 acylcarnitines in NIST MSP format) that fills the coverage gap of public/commercial libraries holding fewer than 50 acylcarnitine spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound class already has comprehensive experimental spectra in public or commercial libraries (fewer than 50 acylcarnitine structures was the trigger for building CarniBlast) You need MSI level 1 identifications — in silico library matches only support precursor accurate mass + MS/MS matching (MSI level 2), not authentic-standard confirmation The analyte class lacks a well-defined core template and diagnostic fragment rules, so fragment prediction from template losses is not defensible

skills.description: Use when a method formulates an optimization problem solvable by multiple engines (exact, greedy, local search) and you must quantify which solver gives acceptable accuracy within acceptable runtime.
skills.name: combinatorial-solver-benchmarking
skills.search_text: combinatorial-solver-benchmarking Use when a method formulates an optimization problem solvable by multiple engines (exact, greedy, local search) and you must quantify which solver gives acceptable accuracy within acceptable runtime. Only one solver implementation exists for the optimization problem, so there is no accuracy/runtime trade-off to compare No ground-truth annotation (e.g. manually annotated library analytes) is available to compute accuracy metrics like F_ACC/A_ACC, leaving only runtime comparisons The task is feature extraction or peak detection rather than evaluating alignment/matching solver quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks alternative combinatorial optimization solvers for the same optimization problem (here, G-Aligner's unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem for multi-run LC-MS feature matching) by comparing solution accuracy metrics and wall-clock runtime, quantifying accuracy-vs-speed trade-offs. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks alternative combinatorial optimization solvers for the same optimization problem (here, G-Aligner's unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem for multi-run LC-MS feature matching) by comparing solution accuracy metrics and wall-clock runtime, quantifying accuracy-vs-speed trade-offs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one solver implementation exists for the optimization problem, so there is no accuracy/runtime trade-off to compare No ground-truth annotation (e.g. manually annotated library analytes) is available to compute accuracy metrics like F_ACC/A_ACC, leaving only runtime comparisons The task is feature extraction or peak detection rather than evaluating alignment/matching solver quality

skills.description: Use when building an in silico structure search database by enumerating scaffold × building-block conjugates — e.g., bile acid cores × amino-acid/acyl fragments — to feed downstream structure annotation.
skills.name: combinatorial-structure-enumeration
skills.search_text: combinatorial-structure-enumeration Use when building an in silico structure search database by enumerating scaffold × building-block conjugates — e.g., bile acid cores × amino-acid/acyl fragments — to feed downstream structure annotation. The target structures are already covered by reference spectral databases (MassBank, GNPS, NIST 2017) or the HMDB structure database — COSMIC's novelty pipeline explicitly excluded hits with structures in HMDB. Exact stereochemistry must be resolved — fragmentation spectra cannot establish stereochemistry, so only the two-dimensional structure is considered during enumeration. The task is annotation/ranking of existing spectra rather than generating candidate structures — use CSI:FingerID ranking and the COSMIC confidence-score workflow instead of enumeration. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Exhaustively enumerate all plausible conjugate structures by combinatorially attaching building blocks (91 amino-acid/acyl fragments) onto curated core scaffolds (322 bile acid cores) with SmiLib v2.0, producing the 28,630-structure in silico search database used by COSMIC. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Exhaustively enumerate all plausible conjugate structures by combinatorially attaching building blocks (91 amino-acid/acyl fragments) onto curated core scaffolds (322 bile acid cores) with SmiLib v2.0, producing the 28,630-structure in silico search database used by COSMIC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target structures are already covered by reference spectral databases (MassBank, GNPS, NIST 2017) or the HMDB structure database — COSMIC's novelty pipeline explicitly excluded hits with structures in HMDB. Exact stereochemistry must be resolved — fragmentation spectra cannot establish stereochemistry, so only the two-dimensional structure is considered during enumeration. The task is annotation/ranking of existing spectra rather than generating candidate structures — use CSI:FingerID ranking and the COSMIC confidence-score workflow instead of enumeration.

skills.description: Use when two or more omics-specific p-value sequences (e.g., gene ORA and metabolite ORA over the same KEGG pathways) must be combined per pathway into a single FDR-corrected significance call.
skills.name: combined-gene-metabolite-pvalue-fusion
skills.search_text: combined-gene-metabolite-pvalue-fusion Use when two or more omics-specific p-value sequences (e.g., gene ORA and metabolite ORA over the same KEGG pathways) must be combined per pathway into a single FDR-corrected significance call. Only one omics evidence stream is available, so there is nothing to combine — run a single-stream ORA/eSPIA instead The p-values to combine come from unrelated pathway sets that cannot be paired row-wise into an n-by-m matrix Peak-level tasks like peak identification or concentration calibration are the goal — these are separate SMART 2.0 post-analysis modules, not pathway p-value fusion http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A meta-analysis skill that fuses per-pathway p-values from gene-side and metabolite-side evidence (e.g., ORA results over KEGG pathways) into a single combined significance score using Pbine's Fisher or weighted Fisher p-value combination with numerical integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: A meta-analysis skill that fuses per-pathway p-values from gene-side and metabolite-side evidence (e.g., ORA results over KEGG pathways) into a single combined significance score using Pbine's Fisher or weighted Fisher p-value combination with numerical integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one omics evidence stream is available, so there is nothing to combine — run a single-stream ORA/eSPIA instead The p-values to combine come from unrelated pathway sets that cannot be paired row-wise into an n-by-m matrix Peak-level tasks like peak identification or concentration calibration are the goal — these are separate SMART 2.0 post-analysis modules, not pathway p-value fusion

skills.description: Use when benchmarking molecular formula identification and you need to merge FIDDLE predictions with external SIRIUS/BUDDY outputs to measure combined top-1/top-5 accuracy on the same spectra.
skills.name: combined-method-score-integration
skills.search_text: combined-method-score-integration Use when benchmarking molecular formula identification and you need to merge FIDDLE predictions with external SIRIUS/BUDDY outputs to measure combined top-1/top-5 accuracy on the same spectra. The goal is standalone FIDDLE prediction on new samples rather than benchmark comparison — combined integration requires SIRIUS/BUDDY outputs on the same spectra and adds no benefit otherwise. Spectra contain compounds that overlap the training set by canonical SMILES — these must be filtered out before computing combined accuracies or results will be inflated. Input spectra have precursor m/z above 1500 or fall outside the supported precursor types/adducts covered by FIDDLE's training data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Integrates FIDDLE's deep learning confidence scores with SIRIUS and BUDDY candidate formula rankings on the same benchmark spectra to produce a combined prediction (output_fiddle_all.csv) that raises top-5 accuracy beyond any single method. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Integrates FIDDLE's deep learning confidence scores with SIRIUS and BUDDY candidate formula rankings on the same benchmark spectra to produce a combined prediction (output_fiddle_all.csv) that raises top-5 accuracy beyond any single method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standalone FIDDLE prediction on new samples rather than benchmark comparison — combined integration requires SIRIUS/BUDDY outputs on the same spectra and adds no benefit otherwise. Spectra contain compounds that overlap the training set by canonical SMILES — these must be filtered out before computing combined accuracies or results will be inflated. Input spectra have precursor m/z above 1500 or fall outside the supported precursor types/adducts covered by FIDDLE's training data.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix needs multiple normalization layers, e.g. rlsc signal correction of QC-sample drift followed by median scaling, in the NormalizeMets R workflow.
skills.name: combined-normalization-method-chaining
skills.search_text: combined-normalization-method-chaining Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix needs multiple normalization layers, e.g. rlsc signal correction of QC-sample drift followed by median scaling, in the NormalizeMets R workflow. Only one normalization layer is needed — use NormQcmets, NormQcsamples or NormScaling directly The dataset lacks QC sample run-order information needed by the rlsc signal-correction stage Data is not yet in NormalizeMets featuredata/sampledata format (unique sample names as row names, metabolites as column names) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Chains two normalization methods in sequence using the NormalizeMets package's NormCombined function — by default QC-RLSC signal correction (rlsc) followed by median scaling — for metabolomics featuredata matrices where a single method is insufficient. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Chains two normalization methods in sequence using the NormalizeMets package's NormCombined function — by default QC-RLSC signal correction (rlsc) followed by median scaling — for metabolomics featuredata matrices where a single method is insufficient.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one normalization layer is needed — use NormQcmets, NormQcsamples or NormScaling directly The dataset lacks QC sample run-order information needed by the rlsc signal-correction stage Data is not yet in NormalizeMets featuredata/sampledata format (unique sample names as row names, metabolites as column names)

skills.description: Use when MetFrag2.2 candidate lists already carry per-candidate PubChem patent/PubMed counts (PNP, PPC) or the five ChemSpider reference counts, and these must be converted into normalized scoring terms for ranking.
skills.name: combined-reference-score-computation
skills.search_text: combined-reference-score-computation Use when MetFrag2.2 candidate lists already carry per-candidate PubChem patent/PubMed counts (PNP, PPC) or the five ChemSpider reference counts, and these must be converted into normalized scoring terms for ranking. When the candidate list was retrieved from a local repository (e.g. LocalPubChemDatabase in the MetFragWeb settings) without web-service reference/patent counts, so PNP, PPC or the five ChemSpider counts are unavailable When the goal is the fragment score itself (comparing in silico bond-dissociation fragments with measured product ions) — reference scoring only supplements, it does not replace fragmentation scoring When candidate filtering (element/substructure or InChIKey stereoisomer filtering) has not yet been done and the candidate list is not final, since normalization maxima depend on the exact list Computes the PubChem combined reference score (patent count + PubMed count, Eq. 5-6) and the ChemSpider combined reference score (five reference counts) per candidate, each normalized across the candidate list so reference evidence contributes comparably to MetFrag2.2 candidate ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: Computes the PubChem combined reference score (patent count + PubMed count, Eq. 5-6) and the ChemSpider combined reference score (five reference counts) per candidate, each normalized across the candidate list so reference evidence contributes comparably to MetFrag2.2 candidate ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the candidate list was retrieved from a local repository (e.g. LocalPubChemDatabase in the MetFragWeb settings) without web-service reference/patent counts, so PNP, PPC or the five ChemSpider counts are unavailable When the goal is the fragment score itself (comparing in silico bond-dissociation fragments with measured product ions) — reference scoring only supplements, it does not replace fragmentation scoring When candidate filtering (element/substructure or InChIKey stereoisomer filtering) has not yet been done and the candidate list is not final, since normalization maxima depend on the exact list

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix shows both batch/QC-RLSC-correctable drift and sample-level intensity differences that no single normalization (QC metabolite, QC sample, or scaling) fixes alone.
skills.name: combined-two-stage-normalization-workflows
skills.search_text: combined-two-stage-normalization-workflows Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix shows both batch/QC-RLSC-correctable drift and sample-level intensity differences that no single normalization (QC metabolite, QC sample, or scaling) fixes alone. A single normalization stage suffices — e.g. data needing only per-sample median/mean/sum/ref scaling, which NormScaling handles directly The input is raw peak intensities not yet in featuredata format (unique sample and metabolite row/column names required) or still contains missing values needing LogTransform/MissingValues preprocessing first The first-stage method requires QC-sample or internal-standard annotations (metabolitedata flags, QC sampledata) that are not available for the dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Chains two normalization methods back-to-back (e.g. QC-RLSC signal correction followed by median scaling) using the NormalizeMets NormCombined function, to remove both analytical drift and per-sample intensity variation in metabolomics feature matrices. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Chains two normalization methods back-to-back (e.g. QC-RLSC signal correction followed by median scaling) using the NormalizeMets NormCombined function, to remove both analytical drift and per-sample intensity variation in metabolomics feature matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A single normalization stage suffices — e.g. data needing only per-sample median/mean/sum/ref scaling, which NormScaling handles directly The input is raw peak intensities not yet in featuredata format (unique sample and metabolite row/column names required) or still contains missing values needing LogTransform/MissingValues preprocessing first The first-stage method requires QC-sample or internal-standard annotations (metabolitedata flags, QC sampledata) that are not available for the dataset

skills.description: Use when a pipeline must convert metagenomic profiler outputs (MetaPhlAn v1/v2, HUMAnN, LEfSe results) into tool-specific input formats (e.g. GraPhlAn tree.txt and annot.txt) via shell-invoked CLI tools.
skills.name: command-line-bioinformatics-pipelining
skills.search_text: command-line-bioinformatics-pipelining Use when a pipeline must convert metagenomic profiler outputs (MetaPhlAn v1/v2, HUMAnN, LEfSe results) into tool-specific input formats (e.g. GraPhlAn tree.txt and annot.txt) via shell-invoked CLI tools. The goal is interactive exploration of a single phylogeny with overlaid metadata, where iTOL or Krona may be more appropriate Input data are raw reads or unprocessed profiles rather than MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs already in LEfSe input format http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Chains command-driven bioinformatics tools (export2graphlan, graphlan_annotate.py, graphlan.py) into a reproducible pipeline that converts MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs into GraPhlAn tree and annotation files and renders the final figure. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Chains command-driven bioinformatics tools (export2graphlan, graphlan_annotate.py, graphlan.py) into a reproducible pipeline that converts MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs into GraPhlAn tree and annotation files and renders the final figure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is interactive exploration of a single phylogeny with overlaid metadata, where iTOL or Krona may be more appropriate Input data are raw reads or unprocessed profiles rather than MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs already in LEfSe input format

skills.description: Use when the goal is to reproduce a published GraPhlAn visualization (e.g., the HMP aerobiosis cladogram, Fig. S1) by running the provided shell pipeline in an example folder such as hmp_aerobiosis rather than re-implementing the tool chain manually.
skills.name: command-line-example-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: command-line-example-pipeline-execution Use when the goal is to reproduce a published GraPhlAn visualization (e.g., the HMP aerobiosis cladogram, Fig. S1) by running the provided shell pipeline in an example folder such as hmp_aerobiosis rather than re-implementing the tool chain manually. Your input is raw sequencing reads — this pipeline starts from MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs, not FASTQ files You need an interactive tree explorer (e.g., iTOL-style) rather than a publication-quality static circular figure Your data are not MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs and cannot be expressed as a LEfSe-compatible input matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Execute the bundled PIPELINE.sh script in an export2graphlan example sub-folder (e.g., hmp_aerobiosis) to chain export2graphlan, graphlan_annotate.py, and GraPhlAn/matplotlib end-to-end and reproduce the paper's figures from the authors' own example data. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Execute the bundled PIPELINE.sh script in an export2graphlan example sub-folder (e.g., hmp_aerobiosis) to chain export2graphlan, graphlan_annotate.py, and GraPhlAn/matplotlib end-to-end and reproduce the paper's figures from the authors' own example data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is raw sequencing reads — this pipeline starts from MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs, not FASTQ files You need an interactive tree explorer (e.g., iTOL-style) rather than a publication-quality static circular figure Your data are not MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs and cannot be expressed as a LEfSe-compatible input matrix

skills.description: Use when you need to convert BIOM-format 16S abundance tables or LEfSe-style outputs into publication-quality circular taxonomic trees using export2graphlan and GraPhlAn.
skills.name: command-line-microbiome-visualization-pipeline
skills.search_text: command-line-microbiome-visualization-pipeline Use when you need to convert BIOM-format 16S abundance tables or LEfSe-style outputs into publication-quality circular taxonomic trees using export2graphlan and GraPhlAn. Input is already a rendered GraPhlAn tree/annotation pair — the conversion step is unnecessary. The goal is interactive exploration of large phylogenies or hierarchical quantitative metagenomic profiles, where iTOL or Krona are the article's named alternatives. Input is not a taxonomic abundance/profile format convertible by export2graphlan (e.g., raw reads or non-hierarchical feature tables without taxonomic lineages). http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A command-line pipeline that converts MetaPhlAn, LEfSe, HUMAnN, or BIOM-format abundance tables into GraPhlAn input files (tree + annotation) via export2graphlan, then renders compact circular taxonomic trees with the matplotlib-backed GraPhlAn tool. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: A command-line pipeline that converts MetaPhlAn, LEfSe, HUMAnN, or BIOM-format abundance tables into GraPhlAn input files (tree + annotation) via export2graphlan, then renders compact circular taxonomic trees with the matplotlib-backed GraPhlAn tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a rendered GraPhlAn tree/annotation pair — the conversion step is unnecessary. The goal is interactive exploration of large phylogenies or hierarchical quantitative metagenomic profiles, where iTOL or Krona are the article's named alternatives. Input is not a taxonomic abundance/profile format convertible by export2graphlan (e.g., raw reads or non-hierarchical feature tables without taxonomic lineages).

skills.description: Use when you must gap-fill draft genome-scale metabolic reconstructions for a multi-species community (e.g., D. vulgaris/M. maripaludis or Arabidopsis soil communities) and want to exploit cross-feeding/leakage to minimize the added reaction set while preserving genomic support.
skills.name: community-aware-metabolic-modeling
skills.search_text: community-aware-metabolic-modeling Use when you must gap-fill draft genome-scale metabolic reconstructions for a multi-species community (e.g., D. vulgaris/M. maripaludis or Arabidopsis soil communities) and want to exploit cross-feeding/leakage to minimize the added reaction set while preserving genomic support. When you have a single isolated model with no community context — plain individual gap filling is the correct baseline, and COMMIT's leakage assumptions cannot be exploited When you cannot supply a valid LP solver (IBM CPLEX or Gurobi); glpk is explicitly not recommended and may fail the LP formulations When the community models use non-MNXref identifier spaces without translation — cross-referencing gaps hampered model comparison in the paper http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 A constraint-based modeling skill that performs community-dependent gap filling of metabolic reconstructions (COMMIT) by considering metabolite leakage (permeability) and community composition, so that fewer reactions are added than when gap filling each member model individually. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: A constraint-based modeling skill that performs community-dependent gap filling of metabolic reconstructions (COMMIT) by considering metabolite leakage (permeability) and community composition, so that fewer reactions are added than when gap filling each member model individually.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you have a single isolated model with no community context — plain individual gap filling is the correct baseline, and COMMIT's leakage assumptions cannot be exploited When you cannot supply a valid LP solver (IBM CPLEX or Gurobi); glpk is explicitly not recommended and may fail the LP formulations When the community models use non-MNXref identifier spaces without translation — cross-referencing gaps hampered model comparison in the paper

skills.description: Use when gap-filling multiple draft community member reconstructions (e.g. KBase/CarveMe/RAVEN/AuReMe MNXref models) where metabolite leakage and member processing order affect the total added-reaction set.
skills.name: community-composition-aware-ordering-search
skills.search_text: community-composition-aware-ordering-search Use when gap-filling multiple draft community member reconstructions (e.g. KBase/CarveMe/RAVEN/AuReMe MNXref models) where metabolite leakage and member processing order affect the total added-reaction set. Gap-filling a single isolate model in isolation, with no community composition or metabolite leakage to consider Input models use identifier spaces other than MNXref and cannot be translated — comparison/gap filling is hampered without cross-references http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Enumerates member-model orderings in COMMIT so that metabolites secreted by already gap-filled community members enlarge the shared medium for later members, minimizing added reactions relative to individual gap filling. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: Enumerates member-model orderings in COMMIT so that metabolites secreted by already gap-filled community members enlarge the shared medium for later members, minimizing added reactions relative to individual gap filling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gap-filling a single isolate model in isolation, with no community composition or metabolite leakage to consider Input models use identifier spaces other than MNXref and cannot be translated — comparison/gap filling is hampered without cross-references

skills.description: Use when a set of community-member GEMs (e.g. consensus reconstructions from KBase/CarveMe/RAVEN/AuReMe) must be gap-filled together under a defined minimal medium and you want to minimize the number of added reactions while preserving genomic support.
skills.name: community-dependent-gap-filling
skills.search_text: community-dependent-gap-filling Use when a set of community-member GEMs (e.g. consensus reconstructions from KBase/CarveMe/RAVEN/AuReMe) must be gap-filled together under a defined minimal medium and you want to minimize the number of added reactions while preserving genomic support. When a single isolate model is being gap-filled in isolation and community composition/leakage is irrelevant — individual gap filling is the appropriate baseline. When community members already grow on the defined medium and no gap filling is needed — adding reactions would only inflate the solution. When you need community-level steady-state abundance optimization rather than gap filling — SteadyCom or MICOM-style whole-community optimization addresses that instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 COMMIT-based community-dependent gap filling: conditional, iterative gap filling of consensus genome-scale metabolic reconstructions that respects microbial community composition and metabolite permeability, so that added-reaction sets are smaller than those from gap filling each member individually. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: COMMIT-based community-dependent gap filling: conditional, iterative gap filling of consensus genome-scale metabolic reconstructions that respects microbial community composition and metabolite permeability, so that added-reaction sets are smaller than those from gap filling each member individually.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single isolate model is being gap-filled in isolation and community composition/leakage is irrelevant — individual gap filling is the appropriate baseline. When community members already grow on the defined medium and no gap filling is needed — adding reactions would only inflate the solution. When you need community-level steady-state abundance optimization rather than gap filling — SteadyCom or MICOM-style whole-community optimization addresses that instead.

skills.description: Use when a gene-gene interaction network contains connected components with more than 1,000 genes and weighted adjacency matrices must be estimated per pathway/condition for topology-based enrichment without exhaustive computation on the full graph.
skills.name: community-detection-network-clustering
skills.search_text: community-detection-network-clustering Use when a gene-gene interaction network contains connected components with more than 1,000 genes and weighted adjacency matrices must be estimated per pathway/condition for topology-based enrichment without exhaustive computation on the full graph. The network's connected components all contain 1,000 genes or fewer, so per-cluster estimation is unnecessary and the full adjacency matrix can be handled directly The analysis does not require weighted adjacency estimation (e.g., pathway-agnostic graph visualization where edge weights are irrelevant) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Scales network-based adjacency estimation in netgsa by clustering large gene-gene networks into communities: six igraph community-detection algorithms are run on oversized connected components, the best algorithm is chosen by minimum edge loss, and weighted adjacency matrices are estimated per cluster and reassembled into a block-diagonal matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Scales network-based adjacency estimation in netgsa by clustering large gene-gene networks into communities: six igraph community-detection algorithms are run on oversized connected components, the best algorithm is chosen by minimum edge loss, and weighted adjacency matrices are estimated per cluster and reassembled into a block-diagonal matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network's connected components all contain 1,000 genes or fewer, so per-cluster estimation is unnecessary and the full adjacency matrix can be handled directly The analysis does not require weighted adjacency estimation (e.g., pathway-agnostic graph visualization where edge weights are irrelevant)

skills.description: Use when two interaction-prediction methods (e.g., SMETANA and COMMIT) have been run over the same gap-filled community models and you need to compare them via symmetrized pairwise overlaps, MIP, and shared-metabolite intersections.
skills.name: community-metabolic-model-symmetrization
skills.search_text: community-metabolic-model-symmetrization Use when two interaction-prediction methods (e.g., SMETANA and COMMIT) have been run over the same gap-filled community models and you need to compare them via symmetrized pairwise overlaps, MIP, and shared-metabolite intersections. The models are draft (not gap-filled) reconstructions — interaction predictions on incomplete models would not reflect the community-dependent gap-filling this comparison presupposes The question requires directional donor-to-receiver information — symmetrization deliberately collapses direction into undirected pairwise overlaps Only a single prediction method is available and no second interaction set exists for cross-validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Cross-validation of predicted metabolic interactions: run SMETANA over gap-filled community member models (e.g., COMMIT-gap-filled Schlaeppi community), then symmetrize directed donor-to-receiver metabolite exchanges into undirected pairwise overlaps to compute agreement statistics against a second interaction-prediction method. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: Cross-validation of predicted metabolic interactions: run SMETANA over gap-filled community member models (e.g., COMMIT-gap-filled Schlaeppi community), then symmetrize directed donor-to-receiver metabolite exchanges into undirected pairwise overlaps to compute agreement statistics against a second interaction-prediction method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The models are draft (not gap-filled) reconstructions — interaction predictions on incomplete models would not reflect the community-dependent gap-filling this comparison presupposes The question requires directional donor-to-receiver information — symmetrization deliberately collapses direction into undirected pairwise overlaps Only a single prediction method is available and no second interaction set exists for cross-validation

skills.description: Use when individual genome-scale SBML member models must be combined into a single reusable community metabolic model whose flux bounds depend on member abundance, and the current SBML standard cannot encode variable bounds directly.
skills.name: community-model-structure-reconstruction
skills.search_text: community-model-structure-reconstruction Use when individual genome-scale SBML member models must be combined into a single reusable community metabolic model whose flux bounds depend on member abundance, and the current SBML standard cannot encode variable bounds directly. When flux bounds are fixed and independent of abundance — a plain merged SBML model without bound-free linearization suffices When the goal is only visualization of an existing community model — ScyNet operates on already-built PyCoMo SBML community models rather than reconstructing them When the input is not per-member SBML genome-scale models (e.g. already merged community models without member-attributable IDs) http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Reconstruct a genome-scale, compartmentalized community metabolic model with PyCoMo by merging member SBML models into an openCOBRA/COBRApy-compliant community structure, using bound-free linearization (dummy metabolites encoding flux bounds) so that effective bounds scale with member abundance while remaining SBML-expressible. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153

skills.description: Use when a paper discusses multiple community tools/repositories in the context of programmatic sample-level metadata analysis and you must classify each cited design choice as favorable or hindering for that purpose.
skills.name: community-tool-design-choice-extraction
skills.search_text: community-tool-design-choice-extraction Use when a paper discusses multiple community tools/repositories in the context of programmatic sample-level metadata analysis and you must classify each cited design choice as favorable or hindering for that purpose. The article does not explicitly attribute design choices to the tools — only generic feature lists exist, so a favorable/hindering classification would be invented rather than grounded in the authors' statements. The goal is to standardize or transform sample metadata (e.g., replacing freetext terms with fixed-vocabulary terms) rather than to compare tools' design choices — that is SMetaS's job, not this skill's. Only one tool is under discussion, so a cross-tool design-choice comparison table is not meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 Extracts and valences (favorable vs hindering) the specific software design choices that authors of a methods paper attribute to related community tools with respect to programmatic sample-level meta-analysis. Produces a per-tool, per-design-choice comparison table that future agents can reuse when selecting or interoperating with repositories like Metabolomics Workbench, ReDU, and MetaboLights. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941

skills.description: Use when you have per-peak top-N compound annotations from an LC-MS annotation pipeline (e.g. mWISE top three candidates) plus a reference set of true compounds per assay, and you need entity-level sensitivity/F1/Tanimoto metrics to compare configurations or algorithms.
skills.name: compound-annotation-sensitivity-evaluation
skills.search_text: compound-annotation-sensitivity-evaluation Use when you have per-peak top-N compound annotations from an LC-MS annotation pipeline (e.g. mWISE top three candidates) plus a reference set of true compounds per assay, and you need entity-level sensitivity/F1/Tanimoto metrics to compare configurations or algorithms. You only have peak-to-compound mass matching output (mass-to-charge to KEGG) and no top-N prioritized proposals with which to compute TP/FP/FN. Your reference set lacks compound chemical structures, so the Tanimoto ratio cannot be computed and only count-based metrics are meaningful. You need database-coverage comparison beyond KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB), since mWISE only annotates against KEGG and the metric reflects that limitation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluates the entity-level sensitivity (and F1, specificity, precision, Tanimoto ratio) of an LC-MS compound-annotation algorithm such as mWISE by recomputing TP/FP/FN counts from top-N candidate annotations against reference compound sets, as demonstrated for mWISE's FELLA-network + raw-score diffusion configuration. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: Evaluates the entity-level sensitivity (and F1, specificity, precision, Tanimoto ratio) of an LC-MS compound-annotation algorithm such as mWISE by recomputing TP/FP/FN counts from top-N candidate annotations against reference compound sets, as demonstrated for mWISE's FELLA-network + raw-score diffusion configuration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have peak-to-compound mass matching output (mass-to-charge to KEGG) and no top-N prioritized proposals with which to compute TP/FP/FN. Your reference set lacks compound chemical structures, so the Tanimoto ratio cannot be computed and only count-based metrics are meaningful. You need database-coverage comparison beyond KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB), since mWISE only annotates against KEGG and the metric reflects that limitation.
