skills.description: Use when you have mzML files from multiple DDA controllers run on the same sample (e.g. serum/beer extracts) and need to compare scan counts, fragmentation efficiency, or MS1 cycle overhead to validate an acquisition strategy.
skills.name: ddac-controller-efficiency-quantification
skills.search_text: ddac-controller-efficiency-quantification Use when you have mzML files from multiple DDA controllers run on the same sample (e.g. serum/beer extracts) and need to compare scan counts, fragmentation efficiency, or MS1 cycle overhead to validate an acquisition strategy. Input data are simulated ViMMS runs rather than real-instrument mzML files — timings derived from inter-scan start-time differences validate controller overhead on real hardware, not in silico results You only need theoretical upper bounds on DDA coverage for an injection rather than empirical efficiency of specific controllers http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies and compares DDA controller performance (full-scan, TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) on real LC-MS/MS acquisitions by counting MS1/MS2 scans in mzML files, computing fragmentation efficiency (picked peaks fragmented / MS2 scans) via MZmine2 peak bounding boxes, and deriving per-controller MS1 scan-plus-processing timings from inter-scan start-time differences. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Quantifies and compares DDA controller performance (full-scan, TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) on real LC-MS/MS acquisitions by counting MS1/MS2 scans in mzML files, computing fragmentation efficiency (picked peaks fragmented / MS2 scans) via MZmine2 peak bounding boxes, and deriving per-controller MS1 scan-plus-processing timings from inter-scan start-time differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are simulated ViMMS runs rather than real-instrument mzML files — timings derived from inter-scan start-time differences validate controller overhead on real hardware, not in silico results You only need theoretical upper bounds on DDA coverage for an injection rather than empirical efficiency of specific controllers

skills.description: Use when you have full-scan mzML peak-picking files plus matching DDA (TopN) controller mzML runs and need to measure how many picked peaks were actually fragmented and how the acquisition compares to the theoretical optimum.
skills.name: ddacoverage-and-efficiency-metric-computation
skills.search_text: ddacoverage-and-efficiency-metric-computation Use when you have full-scan mzML peak-picking files plus matching DDA (TopN) controller mzML runs and need to measure how many picked peaks were actually fragmented and how the acquisition compares to the theoretical optimum. skills.description: Use when DDA bottom-up MS/MS spectra (MGF annotated files, immunopeptidomics, metaproteomics, or 'dark proteome' unidentified clusters) must be assigned peptide sequences without a known protein database or to detect variants, PTMs, and foreign peptides.
skills.name: de-novo-peptide-sequencing
skills.search_text: de-novo-peptide-sequencing Use when DDA bottom-up MS/MS spectra (MGF annotated files, immunopeptidomics, metaproteomics, or 'dark proteome' unidentified clusters) must be assigned peptide sequences without a known protein database or to detect variants, PTMs, and foreign peptides. The set of proteins in the sample is known in advance and only standard identification is needed — database searching (SEQUEST/Tide-style) is the appropriate choice, and an open question remains whether de novo outperforms standard database search in statistical power for a given DDA dataset. Input spectra contain too few peaks or are low quality — the min_peaks option discards such spectra, so results on them would be unreliable. Data are DIA acquisitions — this skill targets DDA bottom-up data; DeepNovo's DIA framework is maintained in a separate repository. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Assign amino acid sequences directly to tandem MS/MS spectra without a protein database by treating the task as machine translation with a transformer model (Casanovo), which was trained on 30 million labeled PSMs from MassIVE-KB and outperforms Novor, DeepNovo, and PointNovo on a nine-species cross-species benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-49731-x
skills.summary: Assign amino acid sequences directly to tandem MS/MS spectra without a protein database by treating the task as machine translation with a transformer model (Casanovo), which was trained on 30 million labeled PSMs from MassIVE-KB and outperforms Novor, DeepNovo, and PointNovo on a nine-species cross-species benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The set of proteins in the sample is known in advance and only standard identification is needed — database searching (SEQUEST/Tide-style) is the appropriate choice, and an open question remains whether de novo outperforms standard database search in statistical power for a given DDA dataset. Input spectra contain too few peaks or are low quality — the min_peaks option discards such spectra, so results on them would be unreliable. Data are DIA acquisitions — this skill targets DDA bottom-up data; DeepNovo's DIA framework is maintained in a separate repository.

skills.description: Use when de novo peptide predictions (pNovo 3, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) on antibody MS/MS data must be binned into distinct mismatch/error categories against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs, e.g. to explain tool-specific error distributions.
skills.name: de-novo-prediction-error-classification
skills.search_text: de-novo-prediction-error-classification Use when de novo peptide predictions (pNovo 3, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) on antibody MS/MS data must be binned into distinct mismatch/error categories against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs, e.g. to explain tool-specific error distributions. The analysis goal is overall peptide recall/precision benchmarking rather than a category-level breakdown of incorrect predictions No pseudo-ground-truth PSMs identified at 1% FDR (MS-GF+ and X!Tandem via SearchGUI/PeptideShaker) are available, so incorrect predictions cannot be flagged reliably The task is database-independent antibody assembly with ALPS rather than characterizing prediction errors http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classifies incorrect de novo peptide predictions from tools such as pNovo 3, SMSNet, PointNovo and Casanovo into 11 defined error categories (e.g. last-3-AA inversion, 1 AA replaced by 1 or 2 AAs, more than six wrongly assigned AAs) against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs, producing a relative-frequency table of error types per tool across antibody MS/MS data sets. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Classifies incorrect de novo peptide predictions from tools such as pNovo 3, SMSNet, PointNovo and Casanovo into 11 defined error categories (e.g. last-3-AA inversion, 1 AA replaced by 1 or 2 AAs, more than six wrongly assigned AAs) against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs, producing a relative-frequency table of error types per tool across antibody MS/MS data sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is overall peptide recall/precision benchmarking rather than a category-level breakdown of incorrect predictions No pseudo-ground-truth PSMs identified at 1% FDR (MS-GF+ and X!Tandem via SearchGUI/PeptideShaker) are available, so incorrect predictions cannot be flagged reliably The task is database-independent antibody assembly with ALPS rather than characterizing prediction errors

skills.description: Use when predicting operons from shotgun metagenome or whole-genome data where promoters must be inferred de novo from scaftig/gene-prediction files because no functional annotation or experimental promoter data exist.
skills.name: de-novo-promoter-prediction
skills.search_text: de-novo-promoter-prediction Use when predicting operons from shotgun metagenome or whole-genome data where promoters must be inferred de novo from scaftig/gene-prediction files because no functional annotation or experimental promoter data exist. Promoter annotations are already available from curated databases or experiments and only operon calling is needed Input is raw reads without prior assembly and you only want gene counts — use the gene-prediction tools directly rather than promoter/operon prediction Secondary metabolite or pathway annotation is the goal — the article notes these analyses are performed separately and are not yet integrated into the pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 De novo prediction of promoters from assembled metagenomic or whole-genome scaftigs using BDGP Neural Network Promoter Prediction 2.2 (NNPP), as embedded in the MetaRon pipeline. It supplies promoter presence/absence evidence used together with gene co-directionality and intergenic distance to call operons from shotgun data without functional or experimental information. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12864-020-07357-5
skills.summary: De novo prediction of promoters from assembled metagenomic or whole-genome scaftigs using BDGP Neural Network Promoter Prediction 2.2 (NNPP), as embedded in the MetaRon pipeline. It supplies promoter presence/absence evidence used together with gene co-directionality and intergenic distance to call operons from shotgun data without functional or experimental information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Promoter annotations are already available from curated databases or experiments and only operon calling is needed Input is raw reads without prior assembly and you only want gene counts — use the gene-prediction tools directly rather than promoter/operon prediction Secondary metabolite or pathway annotation is the goal — the article notes these analyses are performed separately and are not yet integrated into the pipeline

skills.description: Use when de novo predictions (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) exist for validated antibody spectra and you must explain recall variation by missing fragment ions, missing cleavage sites, noise factor, or peptide length.
skills.name: de-novo-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: de-novo-recall-evaluation Use when de novo predictions (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) exist for validated antibody spectra and you must explain recall variation by missing fragment ions, missing cleavage sites, noise factor, or peptide length. The de novo predictions lack a validated ground-truth peptide set, so peptide recall per bin cannot be computed The goal is assembling full-length antibody sequences (e.g. with the de Bruijn assembler ALPS) rather than diagnosing per-spectrum recall degradation You need precision-oriented filtering (e.g. precursor mass filtering of predictions) rather than recall-vs-spectrum-quality analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies how missing fragment ions, missing cleavage sites, noise peaks, and peptide length degrade peptide recall of de novo sequencing tools on validated antibody MS/MS spectra, using Pyteomics-based peak labeling into ion-type vs noise classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Quantifies how missing fragment ions, missing cleavage sites, noise peaks, and peptide length degrade peptide recall of de novo sequencing tools on validated antibody MS/MS spectra, using Pyteomics-based peak labeling into ion-type vs noise classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The de novo predictions lack a validated ground-truth peptide set, so peptide recall per bin cannot be computed The goal is assembling full-length antibody sequences (e.g. with the de Bruijn assembler ALPS) rather than diagnosing per-spectrum recall degradation You need precision-oriented filtering (e.g. precursor mass filtering of predictions) rather than recall-vs-spectrum-quality analysis

skills.description: Use when an encoder–decoder RNN has produced k candidate SMILES from a predicted molecular formula and structural fingerprint and you must re-rank them to pick the top-1 structure per MS2 query spectrum.
skills.name: de-novo-structure-candidate-ranking
skills.search_text: de-novo-structure-candidate-ranking Use when an encoder–decoder RNN has produced k candidate SMILES from a predicted molecular formula and structural fingerprint and you must re-rank them to pick the top-1 structure per MS2 query spectrum. No reliable formula/fingerprint prediction is available (SIRIUS formula error rates rise above 50% for individual spectra up to m/z 800), since ranking quality is bounded by these inputs Spectra are in negative ion mode — the model is trained only on positive-mode data and performance is expected to be lower The query spectrum has fewer than three fragment ions, below the minimum MSNovelist processes http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Orders validated and dereplicated de novo SMILES candidates generated by the MSNovelist encoder–decoder RNN, using the modified Platt fingerprint-match score against the CSI:FingerID-predicted query fingerprint (with raw decoder sequence probability as an ablation baseline), to select the top-1 structure per MS2 spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01486-3
skills.summary: Orders validated and dereplicated de novo SMILES candidates generated by the MSNovelist encoder–decoder RNN, using the modified Platt fingerprint-match score against the CSI:FingerID-predicted query fingerprint (with raw decoder sequence probability as an ablation baseline), to select the top-1 structure per MS2 spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable formula/fingerprint prediction is available (SIRIUS formula error rates rise above 50% for individual spectra up to m/z 800), since ranking quality is bounded by these inputs Spectra are in negative ion mode — the model is trained only on positive-mode data and performance is expected to be lower The query spectrum has fewer than three fragment ions, below the minimum MSNovelist processes

skills.description: Use when tandem MS2 spectra must be annotated with de novo SMILES candidates (no spectral-library hit available), and when de novo candidates must be compared to the database (PubChem/KEGG) candidate by modified Platt score.
skills.name: de-novo-structure-generation-scoring
skills.search_text: de-novo-structure-generation-scoring Use when tandem MS2 spectra must be annotated with de novo SMILES candidates (no spectral-library hit available), and when de novo candidates must be compared to the database (PubChem/KEGG) candidate by modified Platt score. Input spectra are negative-mode MS2 data — MSNovelist is trained only for positive-mode data and performance is expected to be lower Spectra have fewer than three fragment ions — the pipeline requires a minimum of three fragment ions The structure is already identifiable via a spectral library or database search — de novo generation is meant for candidates absent from spectral libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates candidate molecular structures de novo from tandem MS2 spectra via SIRIUS formula prediction, CSI:FingerID fingerprint prediction, and an encoder–decoder RNN, then re-ranks the validated, dereplicated candidates by the modified Platt score against the query fingerprint. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01486-3
skills.summary: Generates candidate molecular structures de novo from tandem MS2 spectra via SIRIUS formula prediction, CSI:FingerID fingerprint prediction, and an encoder–decoder RNN, then re-ranks the validated, dereplicated candidates by the modified Platt score against the query fingerprint.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are negative-mode MS2 data — MSNovelist is trained only for positive-mode data and performance is expected to be lower Spectra have fewer than three fragment ions — the pipeline requires a minimum of three fragment ions The structure is already identifiable via a spectral library or database search — de novo generation is meant for candidates absent from spectral libraries

skills.description: Use when computing chokepoint/bottleneck reactions on an SBML genome-scale metabolic model and you need each bottleneck reaction to be balanced by at least one other producing or consuming reaction.
skills.name: dead-end-metabolite-removal
skills.search_text: dead-end-metabolite-removal Use when computing chokepoint/bottleneck reactions on an SBML genome-scale metabolic model and you need each bottleneck reaction to be balanced by at least one other producing or consuming reaction. Input is not a metabolic model but, e.g., a gene expression or PPI dataset — DEM removal is defined only on stoichiometric reaction networks The analysis goal is flux distribution simulation (FBA/FVA) itself rather than topological chokepoint identification, where DEM reactions can carry legitimate flux in some contexts You need the unfiltered bottleneck counts from the input model variant for comparison with the DEM-free variant (the paper computes all four variants in parallel) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A preprocessing step in chokepoint (bottleneck) analysis where reactions containing dead-end metabolites (DEMs) — metabolites that cannot be balanced by any other producing or consuming reaction — are identified and removed from a genome-scale metabolic model using findCPcli before computing chokepoints. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: A preprocessing step in chokepoint (bottleneck) analysis where reactions containing dead-end metabolites (DEMs) — metabolites that cannot be balanced by any other producing or consuming reaction — are identified and removed from a genome-scale metabolic model using findCPcli before computing chokepoints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a metabolic model but, e.g., a gene expression or PPI dataset — DEM removal is defined only on stoichiometric reaction networks The analysis goal is flux distribution simulation (FBA/FVA) itself rather than topological chokepoint identification, where DEM reactions can carry legitimate flux in some contexts You need the unfiltered bottleneck counts from the input model variant for comparison with the DEM-free variant (the paper computes all four variants in parallel)

skills.description: Use when a set of classified natural-product SMILES (e.g. spirotetronate macrolides from NP Atlas) must be split by presence/absence of a structural motif such as decalin and their predicted-potency scores compared between subgroups.
skills.name: decalin-motif-group-comparison

skills.description: Use when comparing discovery regions of reproducibility procedures (e.g., MaRR vs copula mixture model) on paired rank lists, especially to diagnose boundary shape when top signals are near-perfectly correlated and correlation erodes for lower ranks.
skills.name: decision-boundary-visualization-on-rank-scale
skills.search_text: decision-boundary-visualization-on-rank-scale Use when comparing discovery regions of reproducibility procedures (e.g., MaRR vs copula mixture model) on paired rank lists, especially to diagnose boundary shape when top signals are near-perfectly correlated and correlation erodes for lower ranks. Input data are raw expression intensities or p-values rather than paired rank lists — the MaRR statistic Mg=max(Rgx,Rgy) and the copula rejection region are both defined on the rank scale. The goal is to fit a parametric dependence model to obtain discoveries rather than to diagnose/compare boundary shapes; under near-perfect correlation (Simulation B, r0=0.95) the copula-model boundary is overly narrow and omits reproducible signals off the y=x diagonal. There are more than two replicate experiments — the visualization compares bivariate rejection regions in the (Rgx, Rgy) plane. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Simulates two benchmark rank datasets, derives the MaRR square rejection region from the maximum rank statistic Mg=max(Rgx,Rgy), fits the Li et al. (2011) copula mixture model, and overlays both rejection regions on the (Rgx,Rgy) rank plane to expose how model-based boundaries become overly narrow under near-perfect signal correlation. metabolomics/v3 10.1080/01621459.2017.1397521
skills.summary: Simulates two benchmark rank datasets, derives the MaRR square rejection region from the maximum rank statistic Mg=max(Rgx,Rgy), fits the Li et al. (2011) copula mixture model, and overlays both rejection regions on the (Rgx,Rgy) rank plane to expose how model-based boundaries become overly narrow under near-perfect signal correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw expression intensities or p-values rather than paired rank lists — the MaRR statistic Mg=max(Rgx,Rgy) and the copula rejection region are both defined on the rank scale. The goal is to fit a parametric dependence model to obtain discoveries rather than to diagnose/compare boundary shapes; under near-perfect correlation (Simulation B, r0=0.95) the copula-model boundary is overly narrow and omits reproducible signals off the y=x diagonal. There are more than two replicate experiments — the visualization compares bivariate rejection regions in the (Rgx, Rgy) plane.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing the MS2DECIDE knownness score k: multi-annotated MS/MS features from GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS must be ranked by an expert-modeled, piecewise-linear preference function.
skills.name: decision-theory-aggregation-function-implementation
skills.search_text: decision-theory-aggregation-function-implementation Use when reconstructing or re-implementing the MS2DECIDE knownness score k: multi-annotated MS/MS features from GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS must be ranked by an expert-modeled, piecewise-linear preference function. Input consists of only one annotation source (no GNPS/Sirius/ISDB-LOTUS multiannotation), since pairwise agreement terms phi require cross-tool Tanimoto comparisons The goal is a generic machine-learning scoring model rather than reproducing the expert-elicited MAVT preference structure with fixed Table 1/Table 2 parameters Implements the knownness score k of MS2DECIDE as an additive piecewise-linear MAVT aggregation (Eq. 2-3, Tables 1-2) of GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS match scores, encoding expert-elicited preferences into piecewise-linear eta and pairwise-agreement phi terms. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Implements the knownness score k of MS2DECIDE as an additive piecewise-linear MAVT aggregation (Eq. 2-3, Tables 1-2) of GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS match scores, encoding expert-elicited preferences into piecewise-linear eta and pairwise-agreement phi terms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of only one annotation source (no GNPS/Sirius/ISDB-LOTUS multiannotation), since pairwise agreement terms phi require cross-tool Tanimoto comparisons The goal is a generic machine-learning scoring model rather than reproducing the expert-elicited MAVT preference structure with fixed Table 1/Table 2 parameters

skills.description: Use when comparing MS data encoders (ZDPD vs Zlib-only vs other compressors) on m/z arrays and you must quantify decode wall-clock time or MB/s throughput, not just compressed size.

You are benchmarking compressed file SIZE only — use the ZDPD vs Zlib size-reduction benchmark (55% lower size) rather than timing decode throughput The input is raw vendor instrument data (SCIEX/Thermo/Agilent) that has not yet been converted/quantized into integer m/z arrays The comparison target is intensity-array compression (log10 compressor, zero-intensity filtering) rather than m/z decoding speed http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Benchmark skill for measuring wall-clock decoding time (decode throughput) of compressed mass-spectrometry m/z arrays, used to show that Aird's SIMD-accelerated ZDPD compressor decodes in only ~33% of the time Zlib needs (~3x faster, ~400 MB/s). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: You are benchmarking compressed file SIZE only — use the ZDPD vs Zlib size-reduction benchmark (55% lower size) rather than timing decode throughput The input is raw vendor instrument data (SCIEX/Thermo/Agilent) that has not yet been converted/quantized into integer m/z arrays The comparison target is intensity-array compression (log10 compressor, zero-intensity filtering) rather than m/z decoding speed

skills.description: Use when EI GC-MS data has been deconvoluted into individual compound fragmentation spectra (e.g. via MSHub/GNPS auto-deconvolution) and spectrally related compounds must be grouped into molecular networks without precursor-ion masses.
skills.name: deconvoluted-spectrum-network-edge-construction
skills.search_text: deconvoluted-spectrum-network-edge-construction Use when EI GC-MS data has been deconvoluted into individual compound fragmentation spectra (e.g. via MSHub/GNPS auto-deconvolution) and spectrally related compounds must be grouped into molecular networks without precursor-ion masses. Input is LC-MS/MS data where precursor ion masses are known — the standard precursor-based GNPS networking applies instead of this EI-specific configuration Spectra have not yet been deconvoluted from co-eluting GC-MS peaks — run MSHub auto-deconvolution first, since networking operates on individual compound fragmentation spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Constructs GNPS molecular networks for EI GC-MS data by computing pairwise cosine similarity between deconvoluted compound fragmentation spectra, filtering edges on cosine-similarity and matched-peak criteria, and exporting the network as GraphML — all without precursor or molecular-ion masses, which are often absent in EI spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Constructs GNPS molecular networks for EI GC-MS data by computing pairwise cosine similarity between deconvoluted compound fragmentation spectra, filtering edges on cosine-similarity and matched-peak criteria, and exporting the network as GraphML — all without precursor or molecular-ion masses, which are often absent in EI spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is LC-MS/MS data where precursor ion masses are known — the standard precursor-based GNPS networking applies instead of this EI-specific configuration Spectra have not yet been deconvoluted from co-eluting GC-MS peaks — run MSHub auto-deconvolution first, since networking operates on individual compound fragmentation spectra

skills.description: Use when GC-MS spectral-match annotations carry cosine similarity and balance score columns and you need to select thresholds that minimize top-match FDR, e.g. before building molecular networks or validating deconvolved compound identifications.
skills.name: deconvolution-output-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: deconvolution-output-quality-assessment Use when GC-MS spectral-match annotations carry cosine similarity and balance score columns and you need to select thresholds that minimize top-match FDR, e.g. before building molecular networks or validating deconvolved compound identifications. Input spectra are raw GC-MS files that still require MSHub auto-deconvolution — run the unsupervised non-negative matrix factorization pipeline first; this skill only filters existing match annotations. The dataset lacks balance score annotations, e.g. matches produced by tools other than MSHub/GNPS that do not compute fragmentation-pattern reproducibility across samples. The goal is LC-MS/MS molecular networking annotation (GNPS library search on MS2 spectra) rather than GC-MS deconvolved spectral-match quality control. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Assesses the quality of MSHub/GNPS GC-MS auto-deconvolution spectral matches by jointly filtering on cosine similarity (>0.9) and balance score (>60%), or on balance score alone (>80%), and comparing the false discovery rate (FDR) of the top match. This reproduces the Figure 1m,n benchmark thresholds from Aksenov et al. (2020). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3

This reproduces the Figure 1m,n benchmark thresholds from Aksenov et al. (2020).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are raw GC-MS files that still require MSHub auto-deconvolution — run the unsupervised non-negative matrix factorization pipeline first; this skill only filters existing match annotations. Input spectra are raw multiplexed (undeconvolved) SWATH-MS MS/MS spectra — run DecoMetDIA's deconvolution first rather than annotating directly Input is an already-annotated feature or metabolite-identification table — no annotation step is needed The comparison target is deconvolution accuracy itself (spectral similarity to DDA MS2) rather than downstream annotatability http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assesses the quality of DecoMetDIA-deconvolved MS2 spectra from SWATH-MS untargeted metabolomics by submitting them to downstream metabolite annotation tools (MetDNA and Sirius) and computing the fraction of spectra that receive a metabolite or formula annotation, benchmarked against the paper's reported ~90% success rate. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b02655

skills.description: Use when annotating small-molecule LC–MS/MS spectra against a structure database (e.g. PubChem/HMDB) and you must separate correct from incorrect CSI:FingerID hits and estimate FDR, or when calibrating hit scores into posterior-like confidences.
skills.name: decoy-based-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: decoy-based-fdr-estimation Use when annotating small-molecule LC–MS/MS spectra against a structure database (e.g. PubChem/HMDB) and you must separate correct from incorrect CSI:FingerID hits and estimate FDR, or when calibrating hit scores into posterior-like confidences. You need the probability that an annotation is correct — the paper states the confidence score must not be mistaken for this; it is impossible by design. You need to distinguish small structure modifications or stereochemistry from MS/MS data alone — the paper says these are hard or impossible to tell apart. Input is already a spectral-library search result (library spectra matched); the skill targets in silico annotations where no reference spectra exist. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 COSMIC's method for attaching calibrated confidence scores to in silico structure annotations, combining kernel density P/E-value calibration of CSI:FingerID scores, directional linear SVMs, and Platt scaling so that a score threshold can be used to estimate FDR of top-k hits. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: COSMIC's method for attaching calibrated confidence scores to in silico structure annotations, combining kernel density P/E-value calibration of CSI:FingerID scores, directional linear SVMs, and Platt scaling so that a score threshold can be used to estimate FDR of top-k hits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the probability that an annotation is correct — the paper states the confidence score must not be mistaken for this; it is impossible by design. You need to distinguish small structure modifications or stereochemistry from MS/MS data alone — the paper says these are hard or impossible to tell apart. Input is already a spectral-library search result (library spectra matched); the skill targets in silico annotations where no reference spectra exist.

skills.name: decoy-based-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: decoy-based-fdr-estimation Use when DIA-lipidomics TG annotations need empirical confidence estimation — i.e., after LipidIdentifier target identification and a parallel DecoyIdentifier/allDecoys run, when decoy and target hits must be scored and filtered at a fixed FDR (e.g., 0.1) with standards-based validation. The lipid class is not triacylglycerols — DIATAGeR is explicitly for TGs only ('DIATAGeR is for triacylglycerols only', lipid='TAG') Input is raw spectra or an unannotated feature list — target identification (LipidIdentifier) and spectra import (SpectraImport) must run first before decoy scoring and FDR filtering Data are not DIA-based lipidomics feature lists / MS2 spectra from MS-DIAL, Generic-format, or MZMine exports http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Target-decoy empirical FDR estimation for DIA-lipidomics triacylglycerol annotation using DIATAGeR: decoy-database identifications are merged with target annotations, scored by a caret/pROC logistic regression model (ScoreLipids), and filtered to a pre-determined empirical FDR cutoff (FDRCutoff) against a TG standards list. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344698
skills.summary: Target-decoy empirical FDR estimation for DIA-lipidomics triacylglycerol annotation using DIATAGeR: decoy-database identifications are merged with target annotations, scored by a caret/pROC logistic regression model (ScoreLipids), and filtered to a pre-determined empirical FDR cutoff (FDRCutoff) against a TG standards list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The lipid class is not triacylglycerols — DIATAGeR is explicitly for TGs only ('DIATAGeR is for triacylglycerols only', lipid='TAG') Input is raw spectra or an unannotated feature list — target identification (LipidIdentifier) and spectra import (SpectraImport) must run first before decoy scoring and FDR filtering Data are not DIA-based lipidomics feature lists / MS2 spectra from MS-DIAL, Generic-format, or MZMine exports

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a pathway ranking method degrades gracefully as annotation completeness falls, i.e. when missing/noisy peak features must be simulated via decoy-feature injection into background pathways.
skills.name: decoy-feature-injection-benchmarking
skills.search_text: decoy-feature-injection-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a pathway ranking method degrades gracefully as annotation completeness falls, i.e. when missing/noisy peak features must be simulated via decoy-feature injection into background pathways. Input is real experimental data with no known ground-truth pathway activity — decoy injection benchmarks require synthetic target and background pathways The goal is to rank pathways in a single analysis rather than to characterise method robustness across annotation-degradation levels Peak features are already fully annotated so annotation-completeness degradation is not the quantity under test http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks pathway ranking methods (mPLAGE/PLAGE, ORA, GSEA) for robustness by progressively injecting decoy features into background pathways of a synthetic PALS-format dataset and comparing median pathway p-values across 500 repetitions per decoy level (0%–1000%). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Benchmarks pathway ranking methods (mPLAGE/PLAGE, ORA, GSEA) for robustness by progressively injecting decoy features into background pathways of a synthetic PALS-format dataset and comparing median pathway p-values across 500 repetitions per decoy level (0%–1000%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental data with no known ground-truth pathway activity — decoy injection benchmarks require synthetic target and background pathways The goal is to rank pathways in a single analysis rather than to characterise method robustness across annotation-degradation levels Peak features are already fully annotated so annotation-completeness degradation is not the quantity under test

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how robustly pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE vs ORA vs GSEA) behave under missing metabolomics peaks — e.g. annotated peak-feature intensity matrices where you can inject controlled, randomised feature removal and score recovery against known true pathways.
skills.name: decoy-metabolite-set-simulation
skills.search_text: decoy-metabolite-set-simulation Use when you must quantify how robustly pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE vs ORA vs GSEA) behave under missing metabolomics peaks — e.g. annotated peak-feature intensity matrices where you can inject controlled, randomised feature removal and score recovery against known true pathways. You need production pathway ranking on real (non-perturbed) data rather than a robustness benchmark with synthetic missingness The input peaks lack compound annotations entirely — PALS pathway analysis only uses annotated peaks, so controlled annotation-targeted removals cannot be simulated The comparison targets transcriptomics/proteomics Reactome queries (UniProt/ENSEMBL) where 'metabolite-set' decoy semantics and PiMP_KEGG mapping do not apply Benchmarking skill for robustness evaluation of pathway-ranking methods: hold a decoy metabolite-set activity level fixed (100%) while randomly removing increasing fractions (20–80%) of annotated peak features, so mPLAGE, ORA, and GSEA p-values and F1 scores can be compared under controlled synthetic missingness. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for robustness evaluation of pathway-ranking methods: hold a decoy metabolite-set activity level fixed (100%) while randomly removing increasing fractions (20–80%) of annotated peak features, so mPLAGE, ORA, and GSEA p-values and F1 scores can be compared under controlled synthetic missingness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need production pathway ranking on real (non-perturbed) data rather than a robustness benchmark with synthetic missingness The input peaks lack compound annotations entirely — PALS pathway analysis only uses annotated peaks, so controlled annotation-targeted removals cannot be simulated The comparison targets transcriptomics/proteomics Reactome queries (UniProt/ENSEMBL) where 'metabolite-set' decoy semantics and PiMP_KEGG mapping do not apply

skills.description: Use when evaluating annotation accuracy and FDR of network-based metabolite annotation (e.g. MetDNA3 MRN/SMN/FCN propagation) against decoy MS2 reference spectra on Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics datasets.
skills.name: decoy-spectra-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: decoy-spectra-fdr-estimation Use when evaluating annotation accuracy and FDR of network-based metabolite annotation (e.g. MetDNA3 MRN/SMN/FCN propagation) against decoy MS2 reference spectra on Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics datasets. The goal is de novo annotation of unknown metabolites rather than benchmarking FDR/accuracy of an existing annotation run The data are not untargeted metabolomics MS2 datasets (e.g. targeted assays without MS2 spectra) since decoy-MS2 evaluation requires spectral matching No decoy MS2 reference spectra or negative-control spectral entries are available for the metabolite space being annotated http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarking method that estimates the false discovery rate of network-based metabolite annotation (e.g. MetDNA3 propagation under MRN/SMN/FCN topologies) by ranking candidate annotations against decoy MS2 spectra and checking whether the true metabolite falls within the Top 3 candidates. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Benchmarking method that estimates the false discovery rate of network-based metabolite annotation (e.g. MetDNA3 propagation under MRN/SMN/FCN topologies) by ranking candidate annotations against decoy MS2 spectra and checking whether the true metabolite falls within the Top 3 candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo annotation of unknown metabolites rather than benchmarking FDR/accuracy of an existing annotation run The data are not untargeted metabolomics MS2 datasets (e.g. targeted assays without MS2 spectra) since decoy-MS2 evaluation requires spectral matching No decoy MS2 reference spectra or negative-control spectral entries are available for the metabolite space being annotated

skills.description: Use when a CNN/sequence classifier trained on TIC-normalized raw MS spectra (e.g. NSCLC, CRLM, RCC, Canine Sarcoma) needs Accuracy/F1 evaluation on a hold-out split plus statistical comparison against a baseline.
skills.name: deep-classifier-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: deep-classifier-metric-evaluation Use when a CNN/sequence classifier trained on TIC-normalized raw MS spectra (e.g. NSCLC, CRLM, RCC, Canine Sarcoma) needs Accuracy/F1 evaluation on a hold-out split plus statistical comparison against a baseline. Input data is a feature-selected, dimensionality-reduced table rather than TIC-normalized raw spectra — the MSMCE/hold-out protocol expects raw vectors with known spectrum_dim. The dataset is severely imbalanced or too small for deep models to learn embedding representations — the article explicitly flags these as cases where the MSMCE approach may fail. Only a single split without an independent hold-out set is available — the Wilcoxon and bootstrap comparisons require k-fold (N = 6) folds against a baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates deep learning classifiers for raw mass spectrometry data by computing Accuracy and macro-unweighted-averaged F1-Score on an independent hold-out test set, and by pairing results with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, bootstrap 95% CIs, and efficiency metrics (FLOPs/GPU memory) so that MSMCE-style representation modules can be judged fairly. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: Evaluates deep learning classifiers for raw mass spectrometry data by computing Accuracy and macro-unweighted-averaged F1-Score on an independent hold-out test set, and by pairing results with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, bootstrap 95% CIs, and efficiency metrics (FLOPs/GPU memory) so that MSMCE-style representation modules can be judged fairly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is a feature-selected, dimensionality-reduced table rather than TIC-normalized raw spectra — the MSMCE/hold-out protocol expects raw vectors with known spectrum_dim. The dataset is severely imbalanced or too small for deep models to learn embedding representations — the article explicitly flags these as cases where the MSMCE approach may fail. Only a single split without an independent hold-out set is available — the Wilcoxon and bootstrap comparisons require k-fold (N = 6) folds against a baseline.

skills.description: Use when binary class labels (e.g., pathway presence/absence) must be predicted from 1D waveform signals derived from network auralization, and a very deep 1D convolutional architecture with BCE loss is required.
skills.name: deep-convolutional-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: deep-convolutional-architecture-implementation Use when binary class labels (e.g., pathway presence/absence) must be predicted from 1D waveform signals derived from network auralization, and a very deep 1D convolutional architecture with BCE loss is required. The task requires explaining predictions to biologists — NetAurHPD has low explainability, and the article notes it 'cannot provide biologists with a full understanding of its results' Inputs are network features rather than per-node/hyperlink waveform signals — use a GNN-style baseline (e.g., CHESHIRE) or the graph-auralization step first to obtain waveforms The classification problem is multi-class softmax regression rather than binary presence/absence prediction of pathway targets http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements and retrains the M5 very-deep 1D CNN (originally built for environmental sound recognition) as a binary classifier in PyTorch, using BCE loss with the Adam optimizer, to predict pathway presence/absence from averaged auralized pathway waveforms in NetAurHPD. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Implements and retrains the M5 very-deep 1D CNN (originally built for environmental sound recognition) as a binary classifier in PyTorch, using BCE loss with the Adam optimizer, to predict pathway presence/absence from averaged auralized pathway waveforms in NetAurHPD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires explaining predictions to biologists — NetAurHPD has low explainability, and the article notes it 'cannot provide biologists with a full understanding of its results' Inputs are network features rather than per-node/hyperlink waveform signals — use a GNN-style baseline (e.g., CHESHIRE) or the graph-auralization step first to obtain waveforms The classification problem is multi-class softmax regression rather than binary presence/absence prediction of pathway targets

skills.description: Use when you have a pretrained model plus a set of NMR mixture spectra (e.g. from a Zenodo deposit) and need to predict compound identification and compute ACC/TPR/FPR metrics for the whole dataset in one batch run.
skills.name: deep-learning-batch-prediction
skills.search_text: deep-learning-batch-prediction Use when you have a pretrained model plus a set of NMR mixture spectra (e.g. from a Zenodo deposit) and need to predict compound identification and compute ACC/TPR/FPR metrics for the whole dataset in one batch run. You need to train a pSCNN model from scratch or run the data augmentation/superposition pipeline — this skill covers prediction only, not training The input is not 1D NMR spectra of mixtures of small molecules (e.g. chromatography or MS data), since pSCNN was built for NMR chemical shift data You need to solve the chemical shift variation/peak overlapping problem itself rather than score an already-trained model on new spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 http://edamontology.org/topic_3377 Reload a pretrained deep learning model (pSCNN, a pseudo Siamese CNN for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures) and run batch prediction over NMR mixture spectra datasets, then compute ACC, TPR, and FPR per dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Reload a pretrained deep learning model (pSCNN, a pseudo Siamese CNN for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures) and run batch prediction over NMR mixture spectra datasets, then compute ACC, TPR, and FPR per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to train a pSCNN model from scratch or run the data augmentation/superposition pipeline — this skill covers prediction only, not training The input is not 1D NMR spectra of mixtures of small molecules (e.g. chromatography or MS data), since pSCNN was built for NMR chemical shift data You need to solve the chemical shift variation/peak overlapping problem itself rather than score an already-trained model on new spectra

skills.description: Use when comparing model variants that must differ only in one design factor (e.g. single-mode vs. dual-mode training) so observed performance differences can be attributed to that factor rather than hyperparameter drift.
skills.name: deep-learning-hyperparameter-replication
skills.search_text: deep-learning-hyperparameter-replication Use when comparing model variants that must differ only in one design factor (e.g. single-mode vs. dual-mode training) so observed performance differences can be attributed to that factor rather than hyperparameter drift. Input spectra are too few to train from scratch (< ~100,000 spectra); README recommends instead fine-tuning the pre-trained model or merging small custom datasets into a larger public library. The comparison target is a hyperparameter change rather than a training-data change — a different sampling algorithm or metadata input would confound attribution. Spectra come from a very different chemical domain than the reference training data; per-bin loss comparisons to the reference may not transfer. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Retrain a deep-learning model (here MS2DeepScore 2.0, a Siamese network predicting Tanimoto similarity from MS/MS spectra) under identical hyperparameters as a reference model to isolate the effect of a single design choice, such as training on one vs. both ionization modes. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Retrain a deep-learning model (here MS2DeepScore 2.0, a Siamese network predicting Tanimoto similarity from MS/MS spectra) under identical hyperparameters as a reference model to isolate the effect of a single design choice, such as training on one vs. both ionization modes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are too few to train from scratch (< ~100,000 spectra); README recommends instead fine-tuning the pre-trained model or merging small custom datasets into a larger public library. The comparison target is a hyperparameter change rather than a training-data change — a different sampling algorithm or metadata input would confound attribution. Spectra come from a very different chemical domain than the reference training data; per-bin loss comparisons to the reference may not transfer.

skills.description: Use when a trained deep learning model has uncertain which inputs contribute to performance, and you can define parallel model variants differing only in the input features to compare held-out metrics such as RMSE.
skills.name: deep-learning-input-ablation-analysis
skills.search_text: deep-learning-input-ablation-analysis Use when a trained deep learning model has uncertain which inputs contribute to performance, and you can define parallel model variants differing only in the input features to compare held-out metrics such as RMSE. Do not include adduct type as an ablated input feature when preprocessing tools cannot supply reliable adduct annotations — incorrect adduct information could reduce performance, which is why the default MS2DeepScore model excludes it Do not infer that a metadata field will help just because it is conceptually related — one-hot encoded instrument type did not improve performance, so the ablation, not intuition, must decide Do not compare variants trained with different pair-sampling schemes; biased training-pair distributions confound the ablation http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Systematically add or remove input feature groups (e.g. spectral metadata such as precursor m/z, ionization mode, adduct type, instrument type) from a neural network and compare each variant's held-out evaluation metric to isolate which inputs actually drive predictive performance. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Systematically add or remove input feature groups (e.g. spectral metadata such as precursor m/z, ionization mode, adduct type, instrument type) from a neural network and compare each variant's held-out evaluation metric to isolate which inputs actually drive predictive performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not include adduct type as an ablated input feature when preprocessing tools cannot supply reliable adduct annotations — incorrect adduct information could reduce performance, which is why the default MS2DeepScore model excludes it Do not infer that a metadata field will help just because it is conceptually related — one-hot encoded instrument type did not improve performance, so the ablation, not intuition, must decide Do not compare variants trained with different pair-sampling schemes; biased training-pair distributions confound the ablation

skills.description: Use when a trained massNet VAE must be applied to MSI spectra (HDF5-converted imzML, 85,062 m/z variables) to obtain latent codes or downstream 2D UMAP class-separation maps.
skills.name: deep-learning-model-inference
skills.search_text: deep-learning-model-inference Use when a trained massNet VAE must be applied to MSI spectra (HDF5-converted imzML, 85,062 m/z variables) to obtain latent codes or downstream 2D UMAP class-separation maps. No trained massNet VAE is available — training/optimization (100 epochs, 55.7 min) is a separate skill; inference requires existing validated weights Data are not mass spectra in imzML/HDF5 form or have not been TIC-normalized — the encoder expects the same representation it was trained on The goal is peak-level interpretation rather than latent-space visualization — co-localized m/z peak selection at Pearson correlation ≥ 0.7 via msiPL is the appropriate path http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Runs a trained massNet VAE forward (via Keras/TensorFlow) to extract the 5-dimensional latent variable at the Code layer from TIC-normalized MALDI FT-ICR mass spectra, then embeds it with UMAP for 2D visualization of normal vs tumor separation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Runs a trained massNet VAE forward (via Keras/TensorFlow) to extract the 5-dimensional latent variable at the Code layer from TIC-normalized MALDI FT-ICR mass spectra, then embeds it with UMAP for 2D visualization of normal vs tumor separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trained massNet VAE is available — training/optimization (100 epochs, 55.7 min) is a separate skill; inference requires existing validated weights Data are not mass spectra in imzML/HDF5 form or have not been TIC-normalized — the encoder expects the same representation it was trained on The goal is peak-level interpretation rather than latent-space visualization — co-localized m/z peak selection at Pearson correlation ≥ 0.7 via msiPL is the appropriate path

skills.description: Use when you have a parquet dataset of (molecule, spectrum) pairs with columns such as mol_id, inchi, rdmol, cv_id, and spect, plus an expconfig YAML, and need to fit a GNN spectral prediction model from scratch.
skills.name: deep-learning-model-training
skills.search_text: deep-learning-model-training Use when you have a parquet dataset of (molecule, spectrum) pairs with columns such as mol_id, inchi, rdmol, cv_id, and spect, plus an expconfig YAML, and need to fit a GNN spectral prediction model from scratch. You only need spectra for a list of molecules from an already-trained model — use run_rassp.py or the spectroscopy.ai web API instead of retraining. Your molecules exceed the model's supported size (FormulaNet ≤ 48 atoms, SubsetNet ≤ 64 atoms) or contain elements outside HCONFSPCl — preprocessing and the trained model will not handle them. You want to evaluate an existing checkpoint or compute library-matching metrics — that is the job of forward_evaluate_pipeline.py and library_match_pipeline.py, not training. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a mass-spectrometry spectral prediction model (FormulaNet or SubsetNet) end-to-end with the RASSP pipeline by running rassp/forward_train.py against a YAML experiment configuration, producing PyTorch checkpoint and state files that can later be evaluated or used for inference. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Train a mass-spectrometry spectral prediction model (FormulaNet or SubsetNet) end-to-end with the RASSP pipeline by running rassp/forward_train.py against a YAML experiment configuration, producing PyTorch checkpoint and state files that can later be evaluated or used for inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need spectra for a list of molecules from an already-trained model — use run_rassp.py or the spectroscopy.ai web API instead of retraining. Your molecules exceed the model's supported size (FormulaNet ≤ 48 atoms, SubsetNet ≤ 64 atoms) or contain elements outside HCONFSPCl — preprocessing and the trained model will not handle them. You want to evaluate an existing checkpoint or compute library-matching metrics — that is the job of forward_evaluate_pipeline.py and library_match_pipeline.py, not training.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending FIDDLE's formula-identification training: you need to train TCN spectrum-prediction variants and a rescore model on MoNA/NIST Q-TOF MS/MS spectra with GPU acceleration and compare ablation contributions.
skills.name: deep-learning-model-training-gpu
skills.search_text: deep-learning-model-training-gpu Use when reproducing or extending FIDDLE's formula-identification training: you need to train TCN spectrum-prediction variants and a rescore model on MoNA/NIST Q-TOF MS/MS spectra with GPU acceleration and compare ablation contributions. Training on Orbitrap data: FIDDLE did not apply Gaussian-noise data augmentation there because it lowered spectral similarity, and the Orbitrap training set is already large You only need inference on pre-converted spectra — use the pre-trained checkpoints or the msfiddle PyPI package instead of retraining Spectra fail the preprocessing filters (fewer than five peaks, m/z above 1500, rare precursor types, atoms outside C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train deep learning models on GPU(s) for chemical formula prediction from tandem MS/MS spectra, following FIDDLE's TCN ablation setup (full model, no data augmentation, no contrastive loss) plus the secondary confidence-scoring (rescore) model on Q-TOF data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Train deep learning models on GPU(s) for chemical formula prediction from tandem MS/MS spectra, following FIDDLE's TCN ablation setup (full model, no data augmentation, no contrastive loss) plus the secondary confidence-scoring (rescore) model on Q-TOF data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training on Orbitrap data: FIDDLE did not apply Gaussian-noise data augmentation there because it lowered spectral similarity, and the Orbitrap training set is already large You only need inference on pre-converted spectra — use the pre-trained checkpoints or the msfiddle PyPI package instead of retraining Spectra fail the preprocessing filters (fewer than five peaks, m/z above 1500, rare precursor types, atoms outside C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K)

skills.description: Use when you have a labeled metabolomics matrix (samples x metabolites or pathway features, e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) and want to train/compare a deep learning classifier against classic ML baselines under cross-validated train/test splits.
skills.name: deep-learning-neural-network-training-h2o
skills.search_text: deep-learning-neural-network-training-h2o Use when you have a labeled metabolomics matrix (samples x metabolites or pathway features, e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) and want to train/compare a deep learning classifier against classic ML baselines under cross-validated train/test splits. Task is survival/prognosis prediction rather than supervised classification — use lilikoi.prognosis (Cox-PH / Cox-nnet) instead Input lacks labeled class labels (no Label/phenotype column), since the DL module is a supervised classifier — use the exploratory modules (PCA, t-SNE) instead Goal is metabolite-to-pathway mapping or pathway visualization only (use lilikoi.MetaTOpathway / lilikoi.KEGGplot), not model training http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Trains a supervised deep neural network (via H2O) inside the Lilikoi v2.0 R package to classify disease status from metabolomics features, benchmarked against LDA, SVM, RF, RPART, LOG, and GBM. It is the core classification advance of Lilikoi v2.0, enabling metabolomics researchers to test deep learning alongside popular machine learning methods. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Trains a supervised deep neural network (via H2O) inside the Lilikoi v2.0 R package to classify disease status from metabolomics features, benchmarked against LDA, SVM, RF, RPART, LOG, and GBM. It is the core classification advance of Lilikoi v2.0, enabling metabolomics researchers to test deep learning alongside popular machine learning methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Task is survival/prognosis prediction rather than supervised classification — use lilikoi.prognosis (Cox-PH / Cox-nnet) instead Input lacks labeled class labels (no Label/phenotype column), since the DL module is a supervised classifier — use the exploratory modules (PCA, t-SNE) instead Goal is metabolite-to-pathway mapping or pathway visualization only (use lilikoi.MetaTOpathway / lilikoi.KEGGplot), not model training

skills.description: Use when you have 1H NMR spectra of human/mouse plasma (e.g., EDTA plasma csv with chemical shifts in column 1 and one spectrum per sample column) and need automatic metabolite identification/quantification with spectrum-level reconstruction metrics.
skills.name: deep-learning-nmr-spectrum-reconstruction
skills.search_text: deep-learning-nmr-spectrum-reconstruction Use when you have 1H NMR spectra of human/mouse plasma (e.g., EDTA plasma csv with chemical shifts in column 1 and one spectrum per sample column) and need automatic metabolite identification/quantification with spectrum-level reconstruction metrics. Input spectra are not plasma 1H NMR data (e.g. other biofluids) — the authors state a biofluid-specific analysis pipeline for other biofluid samples is not yet developed. You need fully automated removal of false-positive metabolite predictions — NMRQNet lacks automated pre-/post-filtering and requires a final manual visualization check. Samples require dedicated library adjustment or special sample preparation workflows incompatible with rDolphin/Chenomx-style targeted profiling assumptions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstruct 1H NMR plasma spectra and quantify dominant metabolites using NMRQNet, a deep-learning (CNN + GRU) pipeline, and benchmark reconstruction quality (RMSE, Pearson correlation) against rDolphin targeted profiling and Batman MCMC Bayesian quantification. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.03.01.530642
skills.summary: Reconstruct 1H NMR plasma spectra and quantify dominant metabolites using NMRQNet, a deep-learning (CNN + GRU) pipeline, and benchmark reconstruction quality (RMSE, Pearson correlation) against rDolphin targeted profiling and Batman MCMC Bayesian quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not plasma 1H NMR data (e.g. other biofluids) — the authors state a biofluid-specific analysis pipeline for other biofluid samples is not yet developed. You need fully automated removal of false-positive metabolite predictions — NMRQNet lacks automated pre-/post-filtering and requires a final manual visualization check. Samples require dedicated library adjustment or special sample preparation workflows incompatible with rDolphin/Chenomx-style targeted profiling assumptions.

skills.description: Use when validating a deep-learning classifier on bioactivity-labeled metabolomics samples and comparing its metrics (AUC, accuracy, F1) against classical ML baselines across folds.

skills.search_text: deep-learning-performance-benchmarking Use when validating a deep-learning classifier on bioactivity-labeled metabolomics samples and comparing its metrics (AUC, accuracy, F1) against classical ML baselines across folds. Input data is already an aligned feature table intended for Random Forest, PCA, or OPLS-DA baselines rather than the CNN image pipeline Samples have normalized bioactivity values between 0.4 and 0.6 (the article's ambiguous middle zone is excluded from either class) Only a single train/test split is available without enough samples for stratified 5-fold cross-validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Rigorous evaluation protocol for a CNN bioactivity classifier (MS2toImg-CNN) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation on grayscale molecular fingerprint images, reporting accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC-AUC against conventional ML baselines (Random Forest, PCA, OPLS-DA). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Rigorous evaluation protocol for a CNN bioactivity classifier (MS2toImg-CNN) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation on grayscale molecular fingerprint images, reporting accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC-AUC against conventional ML baselines (Random Forest, PCA, OPLS-DA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is already an aligned feature table intended for Random Forest, PCA, or OPLS-DA baselines rather than the CNN image pipeline Samples have normalized bioactivity values between 0.4 and 0.6 (the article's ambiguous middle zone is excluded from either class) Only a single train/test split is available without enough samples for stratified 5-fold cross-validation

skills.description: Use when small-molecule ECFP fingerprints plus experimental reverse-phase RT values are available and the goal is to predict LC–MS retention times, compare ML vs. similarity-based baselines at Tanimoto thresholds, or rank candidate metabolite identities by predicted RT.
skills.name: deep-learning-retention-time-prediction
skills.search_text: deep-learning-retention-time-prediction Use when small-molecule ECFP fingerprints plus experimental reverse-phase RT values are available and the goal is to predict LC–MS retention times, compare ML vs. similarity-based baselines at Tanimoto thresholds, or rank candidate metabolite identities by predicted RT. The RT data come from a different chromatographic method than reverse-phase LC, unless you specifically intend to test projecting predicted RT onto other chromatographic methods No experimental RT labels exist for training — the model requires a large-scale dataset of experimentally acquired chromatographic RT values The task is MS/MS spectra prediction rather than retention time prediction; the paper notes the historical lack of datasets for in silico spectra prediction, which this RT dataset does not address Trains a Keras feed-forward regression model on the METLIN SMRT dataset (80,038 small molecules with experimentally acquired reverse-phase LC retention times) using ECFP fingerprints as input, to predict retention time (RT) in seconds and benchmark it against a naive k-NN median-RT baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Trains a Keras feed-forward regression model on the METLIN SMRT dataset (80,038 small molecules with experimentally acquired reverse-phase LC retention times) using ECFP fingerprints as input, to predict retention time (RT) in seconds and benchmark it against a naive k-NN median-RT baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The RT data come from a different chromatographic method than reverse-phase LC, unless you specifically intend to test projecting predicted RT onto other chromatographic methods No experimental RT labels exist for training — the model requires a large-scale dataset of experimentally acquired chromatographic RT values The task is MS/MS spectra prediction rather than retention time prediction; the paper notes the historical lack of datasets for in silico spectra prediction, which this RT dataset does not address

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is experimental peak-picked feature data awaiting annotation (a feature table or mzML), not theoretical library spectra — the WMYn regenerates library fingerprints, not query spectra The task is double-bond localization of Paternò–Büchi (PB)-derivatized lipids, which uses the separate PB library (PB_PX_H.pkl, common_PX_CH3COO.pkl) rather than the general WMYn corpus Only one similarity search is needed against an existing library — use flash entropy search directly instead of training a regeneration network

Input transients are already full-length high-resolution acquisitions (e.g. the >1 TB '1M' raw files) — reconstruction only adds value for reduced transients acquired with short transient duration (<10% of collection time per transient). The analysis goal is multimodal image registration or single-cell-to-tissue mapping rather than spectral reconstruction — those belong to other MEISTER skills. No trained model weights are available for the instrument/data type; the decoder requires MEISTER weights (e.g. saved_model.zip) trained on matching high-resolution data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A MEISTER deep-learning skill that reconstructs full-length (1M-point) FT-ICR mass-spectral transients from short (64k-point) transients — enabling ~15-fold faster acquisition and >10× SNR gains in MSI and single-cell MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: A MEISTER deep-learning skill that reconstructs full-length (1M-point) FT-ICR mass-spectral transients from short (64k-point) transients — enabling ~15-fold faster acquisition and >10× SNR gains in MSI and single-cell MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transients are already full-length high-resolution acquisitions (e.g. the >1 TB '1M' raw files) — reconstruction only adds value for reduced transients acquired with short transient duration (<10% of collection time per transient). No trained model weights are available for the instrument/data type; the decoder requires MEISTER weights (e.g. saved_model.zip) trained on matching high-resolution data.

skills.search_text: delta-encoding-compression-benchmarking Use when comparing compressed m/z array size or decoding speed between Aird's ZDPD and a Zlib-only baseline across mass-spec datasets, or when implementing quantize-then-delta-then-PforDelta m/z compression pipelines. Input arrays are intensity or ion mobility arrays, not ordered m/z arrays — the 55%/33% metrics apply specifically to m/z data compression Lossless raw m/z fidelity is required — Aird quantizes floating-point m/z to integers at a chosen precision, so the method is lossy at the quantization level Acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility — the paper states these formats were still under development and unsupported at the time http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmark Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD) m/z compressor against Zlib-only compression on mass spectrometry arrays, measuring compressed size and decoding time. ZDPD combines integer delta coding via the SIMD-accelerated FastPfor library with Zlib wrapping to achieve smaller files and ~3x faster decoding. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Benchmark Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD) m/z compressor against Zlib-only compression on mass spectrometry arrays, measuring compressed size and decoding time. ZDPD combines integer delta coding via the SIMD-accelerated FastPfor library with Zlib wrapping to achieve smaller files and ~3x faster decoding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input arrays are intensity or ion mobility arrays, not ordered m/z arrays — the 55%/33% metrics apply specifically to m/z data compression Lossless raw m/z fidelity is required — Aird quantizes floating-point m/z to integers at a chosen precision, so the method is lossy at the quantization level Acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility — the paper states these formats were still under development and unsupported at the time

skills.description: Use when converting vendor MRM chromatogram files to the Aird format and you need to shrink retention-time arrays so hundreds of chromatograms can render quickly on the web.
skills.name: delta-encoding-of-retention-times
skills.search_text: delta-encoding-of-retention-times Use when converting vendor MRM chromatogram files to the Aird format and you need to shrink retention-time arrays so hundreds of chromatograms can render quickly on the web. The input is already in Aird format or another delta-encoded representation — re-applying delta coding to deltas is meaningless. The target format must be mzML or another standards-compliant interchange format, since this lossy quantization (1e-5 precision) is specific to the computation-oriented Aird format. Working with non-chromatogram arrays (e.g. m/z arrays in DDA/DIA spectra), which Aird handles with different combinable compressors such as Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Compresses MRM chromatogram retention-time arrays by quantizing each RT to an integer (1e-5 precision), storing deltas between adjacent RT integers, then applying FastPFor bit-level integer encoding followed by ZSTD compression as part of the Aird format used by MRMPro. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05685-x
skills.summary: Compresses MRM chromatogram retention-time arrays by quantizing each RT to an integer (1e-5 precision), storing deltas between adjacent RT integers, then applying FastPFor bit-level integer encoding followed by ZSTD compression as part of the Aird format used by MRMPro.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already in Aird format or another delta-encoded representation — re-applying delta coding to deltas is meaningless. The target format must be mzML or another standards-compliant interchange format, since this lossy quantization (1e-5 precision) is specific to the computation-oriented Aird format. Working with non-chromatogram arrays (e.g. m/z arrays in DDA/DIA spectra), which Aird handles with different combinable compressors such as Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD).

skills.description: Use when a monotonically ordered numeric array (e.g. a centroided m/z list) contains large integers whose adjacent values differ by small, near-constant amounts, and you need a smaller compressed footprint than generic Zlib-only compression.
skills.name: delta-encoding-of-sorted-spectra
skills.search_text: delta-encoding-of-sorted-spectra Use when a monotonically ordered numeric array (e.g. a centroided m/z list) contains large integers whose adjacent values differ by small, near-constant amounts, and you need a smaller compressed footprint than generic Zlib-only compression. The array is unordered or has large, irregular adjacent differences (e.g. intensity arrays, which Aird instead compresses with options like the log10 compressor or ignores at zero-intensity points) Bit-exact lossless reproduction of the original vendor floating-point m/z values is required, since Aird stores m/z as integers at a user-chosen controllable precision Working with acquisition modes the format does not yet support (the paper states Aird supports only DDA, DIA/SWATH, and PRM; ScanningSWATH and Ion Mobility formats were under development) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compress ordered, numeric spectra arrays (m/z) by quantizing floats to integers at a chosen decimal precision and encoding only the small deltas between adjacent sorted integers, as in Aird's ZDPD (Zlib-Diff-PforDelta) compressor. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Compress ordered, numeric spectra arrays (m/z) by quantizing floats to integers at a chosen decimal precision and encoding only the small deltas between adjacent sorted integers, as in Aird's ZDPD (Zlib-Diff-PforDelta) compressor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The array is unordered or has large, irregular adjacent differences (e.g. intensity arrays, which Aird instead compresses with options like the log10 compressor or ignores at zero-intensity points) Bit-exact lossless reproduction of the original vendor floating-point m/z values is required, since Aird stores m/z as integers at a user-chosen controllable precision Working with acquisition modes the format does not yet support (the paper states Aird supports only DDA, DIA/SWATH, and PRM; ScanningSWATH and Ion Mobility formats were under development)

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-trained VAE over a metabolomics feature matrix plus per-sample demographic labels (disease category, age group) and need to visually assess whether the learned latent space organizes samples by those labels better than the raw features.
skills.name: demographic-label-stratification-assessment
skills.search_text: demographic-label-stratification-assessment Use when you have a pre-trained VAE over a metabolomics feature matrix plus per-sample demographic labels (disease category, age group) and need to visually assess whether the learned latent space organizes samples by those labels better than the raw features. You already have a supervised classifier or want label-driven separation — this skill only assesses unsupervised stratification; the VAE is trained without demographic supervision The feature matrix is raw/unprocessed or not the 2,736-feature robust mzLearn peak set — the pre-trained encoder expects exactly that standardized input shape The goal is de-isotoping, annotation, or MS/MS compound identification — mzLearn outputs are ion MS1 level and downstream workflows handle those steps separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Encodes all samples through a pre-trained VAE trained on the mzLearn MS1 ion-feature matrix (2,736 robust metabolite signals across 20,548 blood samples) and compares UMAP visualizations of the latent space versus the raw, standard-scaled input data, colored by disease and age labels, to demonstrate unsupervised demographic stratification. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Encodes all samples through a pre-trained VAE trained on the mzLearn MS1 ion-feature matrix (2,736 robust metabolite signals across 20,548 blood samples) and compares UMAP visualizations of the latent space versus the raw, standard-scaled input data, colored by disease and age labels, to demonstrate unsupervised demographic stratification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a supervised classifier or want label-driven separation — this skill only assesses unsupervised stratification; the VAE is trained without demographic supervision The feature matrix is raw/unprocessed or not the 2,736-feature robust mzLearn peak set — the pre-trained encoder expects exactly that standardized input shape The goal is de-isotoping, annotation, or MS/MS compound identification — mzLearn outputs are ion MS1 level and downstream workflows handle those steps separately

skills.description: Use when multiple lipidomes have been loaded and structurally embedded in a shared lipid space model, and you need to see which lipidomes cluster by structure/abundance or select a branch of similar lipidomes for reanalysis.
skills.name: dendrogram-visualization-of-lipidome-clustering
skills.search_text: dendrogram-visualization-of-lipidome-clustering Use when multiple lipidomes have been loaded and structurally embedded in a shared lipid space model, and you need to see which lipidomes cluster by structure/abundance or select a branch of similar lipidomes for reanalysis. Only a single lipidome is loaded — the dendrogram relates multiple lipidomes to one another, so there is nothing to cluster You want relationships between individual lipid species rather than between lipidomes — use the per-lipidome lipid space model view instead The clustering strategy choice is not part of the question and only the raw distance matrix values are needed Builds the global lipidome distance model of LipidSpace by applying agglomerative hierarchical clustering to the pairwise Hausdorff distance matrix between all lipidomes, and renders it as an interactive dendrogram (PDF export). The dendrogram is the entry point for sub-selecting lipidome groups for follow-up analyses. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Builds the global lipidome distance model of LipidSpace by applying agglomerative hierarchical clustering to the pairwise Hausdorff distance matrix between all lipidomes, and renders it as an interactive dendrogram (PDF export). The dendrogram is the entry point for sub-selecting lipidome groups for follow-up analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single lipidome is loaded — the dendrogram relates multiple lipidomes to one another, so there is nothing to cluster You want relationships between individual lipid species rather than between lipidomes — use the per-lipidome lipid space model view instead The clustering strategy choice is not part of the question and only the raw distance matrix values are needed
