Input is experimentally acquired spectra rather than predicted shifts — this statistic is defined over in silico predicted 1H signals The goal is dereplicating compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes), which this coverage statistic explicitly precludes High-accuracy shift prediction is required — current lightweight predictors lack sufficient accuracy for direct dereplication http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Classifies predicted 1H NMR signals for a large natural product structure set as shielded vs. deshielded and reports the fraction of molecules with at least 10% deshielded signals and with exclusively shielded signals, establishing whether lightweight in silico shift prediction can support NMR-based dereplication coverage. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Classifies predicted 1H NMR signals for a large natural product structure set as shielded vs. deshielded and reports the fraction of molecules with at least 10% deshielded signals and with exclusively shielded signals, establishing whether lightweight in silico shift prediction can support NMR-based dereplication coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is experimentally acquired spectra rather than predicted shifts — this statistic is defined over in silico predicted 1H signals The goal is dereplicating compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes), which this coverage statistic explicitly precludes High-accuracy shift prediction is required — current lightweight predictors lack sufficient accuracy for direct dereplication

skills.description: Use when you need to classify ion images from multiple DESI imaging MS datasets as off-sample/on-sample and compute per-formula off-sample frequency counts to detect recurring matrix-cluster artifacts.
skills.name: desi-imaging-ms-data-handling
skills.search_text: desi-imaging-ms-data-handling Use when you need to classify ion images from multiple DESI imaging MS datasets as off-sample/on-sample and compute per-formula off-sample frequency counts to detect recurring matrix-cluster artifacts. When the goal is pixel-level segmentation of the off-sample region — the article states 'our approach does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region' When ion images are from non-DESI modalities or you need class probabilities for individual pixels rather than per-image labels When you lack the specific gold standard archive or pretrained model from metaspace2020/offsample — do not substitute arbitrary classifiers without retraining http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A workflow for applying the OffsampleAI deep learning off-sample classifier to DESI imaging MS datasets from the METASPACE gold standard, and aggregating predictions per molecular formula to identify which ions (e.g., DHB matrix clusters like C18H30O3S and C17H28O3S) are systematically off-sample. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: A workflow for applying the OffsampleAI deep learning off-sample classifier to DESI imaging MS datasets from the METASPACE gold standard, and aggregating predictions per molecular formula to identify which ions (e.g., DHB matrix clusters like C18H30O3S and C17H28O3S) are systematically off-sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pixel-level segmentation of the off-sample region — the article states 'our approach does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region' When ion images are from non-DESI modalities or you need class probabilities for individual pixels rather than per-image labels When you lack the specific gold standard archive or pretrained model from metaspace2020/offsample — do not substitute arbitrary classifiers without retraining

skills.description: Use when DESI-MSI imaging data (e.g., .cdf files or Matlab workspace files) of tissue sections must be interpreted at ~50 µm pixel resolution along a linear developmental gradient, such as maize root longitudinal sections.
skills.name: desi-msi-spatial-resolution-handling
skills.search_text: desi-msi-spatial-resolution-handling Use when DESI-MSI imaging data (e.g., .cdf files or Matlab workspace files) of tissue sections must be interpreted at ~50 µm pixel resolution along a linear developmental gradient, such as maize root longitudinal sections. The dataset was acquired at substantially coarser spatial resolution (>100 µm pixel size), so narrow developmental zones along the root axis cannot be resolved The tissue geometry is not a linear developmental axis (e.g., 2D organ-wide imaging), since DIMPLE is designed to leverage the linear root gradient The input is already a processed feature/signature table rather than raw DESI-MSI imaging data (cdf files or workspaces) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Handles DESI-MSI datasets acquired at approximately 50–100 µm spatial resolution for developmental mapping in maize root tissue, ensuring that pixel-level mass spectra resolve biologically meaningful gradients along the linear root axis. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Handles DESI-MSI datasets acquired at approximately 50–100 µm spatial resolution for developmental mapping in maize root tissue, ensuring that pixel-level mass spectra resolve biologically meaningful gradients along the linear root axis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset was acquired at substantially coarser spatial resolution (>100 µm pixel size), so narrow developmental zones along the root axis cannot be resolved The tissue geometry is not a linear developmental axis (e.g., 2D organ-wide imaging), since DIMPLE is designed to leverage the linear root gradient The input is already a processed feature/signature table rather than raw DESI-MSI imaging data (cdf files or workspaces)

skills.description: Use when preparing a wide-format feature table for SECIMTools supervised tools — random forest, SVM, LASSO/Elastic Net — and a design file relating each sample to its group must be joined to the sample columns.
skills.name: design-file-class-label-mapping
skills.search_text: design-file-class-label-mapping Use when preparing a wide-format feature table for SECIMTools supervised tools — random forest, SVM, LASSO/Elastic Net — and a design file relating each sample to its group must be joined to the sample columns. The analysis is a class-label-free step such as blank feature filtering, retention time diagnostics, or run order regression, where the grouping variable is not used to supervise the tool Sample identifiers in the feature table do not match design-file sample IDs, so the join would silently mislabel samples rather than map them The labels to attach are continuous values rather than a discrete grouping variable, since the RF classifier and the binary-label Elastic Net fit expect categorical classes http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Maps each sample in a SECIMTools wide-format metabolomics feature table (samples in columns, features in rows with unique feature identifiers) to its class label via the design file, so the user-specified grouping variable (e.g. treatment group) can serve as the class labels for downstream classification and variable-selection tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Maps each sample in a SECIMTools wide-format metabolomics feature table (samples in columns, features in rows with unique feature identifiers) to its class label via the design file, so the user-specified grouping variable (e.g. treatment group) can serve as the class labels for downstream classification and variable-selection tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is a class-label-free step such as blank feature filtering, retention time diagnostics, or run order regression, where the grouping variable is not used to supervise the tool Sample identifiers in the feature table do not match design-file sample IDs, so the join would silently mislabel samples rather than map them The labels to attach are continuous values rather than a discrete grouping variable, since the RF classifier and the binary-label Elastic Net fit expect categorical classes

Input is raw LC-HRMS data that has not yet been processed into a feature table — peak detection/feature construction must happen first The goal is de novo annotation or discovery of unknown metabolites; this skill only classifies detections of curated PMDB entries with known m/z and retention time The metabolite set has no curated accurate-m/z and retention-time values to match against cohort features http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Stratifies xenobiotic metabolites detected in cohort LC-HRMS data by how frequently each appears across samples (high >50%, moderate 10–50%, low <10%) and computes per-subject detection counts, converting a binary screen result into an exposure-landscape summary. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: Stratifies xenobiotic metabolites detected in cohort LC-HRMS data by how frequently each appears across samples (high >50%, moderate 10–50%, low <10%) and computes per-subject detection counts, converting a binary screen result into an exposure-landscape summary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-HRMS data that has not yet been processed into a feature table — peak detection/feature construction must happen first The goal is de novo annotation or discovery of unknown metabolites; this skill only classifies detections of curated PMDB entries with known m/z and retention time The metabolite set has no curated accurate-m/z and retention-time values to match against cohort features

skills.search_text: developmental-gradient-cluster-interpretation Use when DIMPLE cluster outputs and clustered linescans from root DESI-MSI need biological interpretation — e.g. identifying meristem-localized Cluster 1 signatures, bimodal enrichment, or cortex/vasculature enrichment in B73 and Oaxacan Green. skills.summary: Interprets DIMPLE cluster assignments on root DESI-MSI data by inspecting clustered linescans and the GUI to classify metabolite signatures as meristem-localized, bimodal, or cell-layer-enriched (cortex/vasculature) across developmental gradients and maize varieties.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw DESI-MSI cdf data that has not yet been processed by DIMPLE into cluster assignments and linescans — run the DIMPLE pipeline first. The spatial axis is not a linear developmental gradient (e.g. isotropic tissue or bulk metabolomics), since DIMPLE and cluster interpretation depend on the linear root axis. The goal is quantifying a known metabolite by targeted MS rather than interpreting untargeted spatial enrichment patterns.

skills.search_text: developmental-gradient-mass-signature-clustering Use when you have DESI-MSI imaging data of a root or organ with a linear developmental axis, a pool of redundant per-replicate mass signature detections (e. (2020).
skills.name: dhb-adduct-interpretation
skills.search_text: dhb-adduct-interpretation Use when a set of off-sample matrix cluster ion annotations (e.g., DHB clusters from METASPACE datasets) must be interpreted in terms of a combinatorial adduct/cluster model, or when reproducing histogram analyses of cluster parameters n, p, x, z like Fig. 3 of Ovchinnikova et al. (2020). The ion images are on-sample tissue annotations rather than off-sample matrix clusters — this skill only characterizes off-sample DHB matrix clusters. The matrix is not DHB (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid) — the combinatorial model and the 353 predicted formulas are specific to DHB matrix clusters. The goal is to recognize/filter off-sample images rather than interpret the chemistry of already-recognized off-sample cluster annotations. Interprets recognized off-sample MALDI matrix cluster ions of 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) by mapping their molecular formulas onto a combinatorial cluster-generating model (Keller and Li, 2000) with parameters n (DHB molecules), p, x (potassium), and z (sodium), then profiling the parameter distributions to characterize cluster chemistry. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x

skills.when_to_use_negative: The ion images are on-sample tissue annotations rather than off-sample matrix clusters — this skill only characterizes off-sample DHB matrix clusters. The goal is to recognize/filter off-sample images rather than interpret the chemistry of already-recognized off-sample cluster annotations.

skills.description: Use when a MALDI-imaging dataset was acquired with 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) matrix in positive ion mode and you need to estimate how many annotated DHB matrix-cluster ions are off-sample artifacts that should be filtered before downstream spatial metabolomics analysis.
skills.name: dhb-matrix-cluster-formula-annotation
skills.search_text: dhb-matrix-cluster-formula-annotation Use when a MALDI-imaging dataset was acquired with 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) matrix in positive ion mode and you need to estimate how many annotated DHB matrix-cluster ions are off-sample artifacts that should be filtered before downstream spatial metabolomics analysis. skills.summary: Re-annotates MALDI-imaging datasets acquired with the DHB matrix in positive ion mode using the 353 generated DHB matrix-cluster molecular formulas against HMDB v4 in METASPACE at FDR <= 50%, then classifies the resulting ion images as off-sample/on-sample with the ResNet50 off-sample CNN to quantify how much annotated DHB cluster signal is biologically unrelated (off-sample).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets were not acquired with the DHB matrix in positive ion mode — the 353 formulas are DHB-specific (per Keller and Li, 2000) and do not model other MALDI matrices The goal is pixel-level segmentation of off-sample regions — the authors state 'our approach does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region'; this skill classifies whole ion images only The task is generic off-sample recognition rather than characterizing DHB matrix-cluster contamination — the original skill from the article recognizes off-sample images broadly, not just matrix clusters

When the goal is standard MetaboAnalyst statistical pathway analysis rather than dynamic interaction-network/Jacobian analysis of metabolites. When metabolite IDs are not present in both rows and columns of the input dataset, as required for interaction-network construction.

skills.description: Use when a targeted lipidomics dataset (Skyline CSV export or numerical matrix with sample-annotation table) must be statistically compared across clinical groups, e.g. HighFat_water vs NormalDiet_water or Cancer vs Benign, with or without confounder correction.
skills.name: differential-lipid-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-lipid-abundance-analysis Use when a targeted lipidomics dataset (Skyline CSV export or numerical matrix with sample-annotation table) must be statistically compared across clinical groups, e.g. HighFat_water vs NormalDiet_water or Cancer vs Benign, with or without confounder correction. Data has not yet been imported, transition-summarized, or normalized — run lipidr QC/normalization (box plots, PCA, %CV filtering, PQN) first, since differential results depend on those steps The goal is lipid set enrichment (preferential regulation of lipid classes, total chain lengths, or unsaturation patterns) rather than per-molecule abundance testing — use lipidr's LSEA instead There is no clinical grouping variable or contrast of interest loaded in the sample annotation — de_analysis/de_design require loaded clinical variables to build the model http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Statistical comparison of lipid-molecule abundance between clinical groups using lipidr's limma-based de_analysis/de_design on a LipidomicsExperiment, with results exported as logFC/p-value tables and volcano plots. This is the core re-analysis capability that lipidr provides for targeted lipidomics datasets, including covariate-adjusted (factorial) designs. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00082
skills.summary: Statistical comparison of lipid-molecule abundance between clinical groups using lipidr's limma-based de_analysis/de_design on a LipidomicsExperiment, with results exported as logFC/p-value tables and volcano plots. This is the core re-analysis capability that lipidr provides for targeted lipidomics datasets, including covariate-adjusted (factorial) designs.

skills.summary: Identify differentially abundant lipids between experimental conditions using ADViSELipidomics' statistical-analysis module, which fits models over the normalized concentration matrix under simple or complex designs and visualizes results as MA and volcano plots with lipid-set enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw LipidSearch/LIQUID output or an unnormalized intensity matrix — parse lipid species (LIPID MAPS classification) and normalize with internal lipid standards first. skills.description: Use when you have a two-group (or multi-group) differential lipidomics comparison and want to know which lipid classes or chain attributes are preferentially enriched among the regulated lipids.
skills.name: differential-lipidomics-results-interpretation
skills.search_text: differential-lipidomics-results-interpretation Use when you have a two-group (or multi-group) differential lipidomics comparison and want to know which lipid classes or chain attributes are preferentially enriched among the regulated lipids. You need gene-set style enrichment on generic feature IDs — LSEA operates on lipid annotation sets (classes, total chain lengths, unsaturation patterns), not arbitrary feature sets You have only raw intensities with no differential ranking (e.g. logFC) yet — LSEA requires prior univariate/differential analysis of clinical variables The goal is quality control or normalization rather than interpretation of regulated lipids — lipidr's QC/plotting and normalization steps serve that purpose instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Interpret differential lipidomics results by running lipidr's novel Lipid Set Enrichment Analysis (LSEA), which ranks differentially regulated lipids (e.g. by logFC) to detect preferential enrichment of lipid classes, total chain lengths, or unsaturation patterns, and visualizes the enriched sets. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00082
skills.summary: Interpret differential lipidomics results by running lipidr's novel Lipid Set Enrichment Analysis (LSEA), which ranks differentially regulated lipids (e.g. by logFC) to detect preferential enrichment of lipid classes, total chain lengths, or unsaturation patterns, and visualizes the enriched sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need gene-set style enrichment on generic feature IDs — LSEA operates on lipid annotation sets (classes, total chain lengths, unsaturation patterns), not arbitrary feature sets You have only raw intensities with no differential ranking (e.g. logFC) yet — LSEA requires prior univariate/differential analysis of clinical variables The goal is quality control or normalization rather than interpretation of regulated lipids — lipidr's QC/plotting and normalization steps serve that purpose instead

skills.description: Use when joint spatial transcriptomics–metabolomics data have been integrated and clustered by SpatialMETA and you need cluster-defining genes/metabolites plus metabolite pathway enrichment for one sub-cluster vs. the rest.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-abundance-analysis Use when joint spatial transcriptomics–metabolomics data have been integrated and clustered by SpatialMETA and you need cluster-defining genes/metabolites plus metabolite pathway enrichment for one sub-cluster vs. the rest. Data are single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA is explicitly designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only SM and ST spots have not yet been aligned and KNN-reassigned (rotation, translation, non-linear distortion, spot_align_byknn), so cluster labels cannot be attached to metabolite intensities More than two modalities are present — SpatialMETA currently supports integration of only two modalities http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Identifies marker genes and marker metabolites that define a spatial sub-cluster (e.g. the Imm_4 immune sub-cluster in ccRCC Y7_T) in a joint ST-SM AnnData, then tests marker metabolites for pathway enrichment via a hypergeometric test over HMDB-referenced annotations to establish metabolite-level (e.g. lipid metabolism) signatures. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Identifies marker genes and marker metabolites that define a spatial sub-cluster (e.g. the Imm_4 immune sub-cluster in ccRCC Y7_T) in a joint ST-SM AnnData, then tests marker metabolites for pathway enrichment via a hypergeometric test over HMDB-referenced annotations to establish metabolite-level (e.g. lipid metabolism) signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA is explicitly designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only SM and ST spots have not yet been aligned and KNN-reassigned (rotation, translation, non-linear distortion, spot_align_byknn), so cluster labels cannot be attached to metabolite intensities More than two modalities are present — SpatialMETA currently supports integration of only two modalities

skills.description: Use when a pixel x m/z feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions from AFAD-ESI positive-mode mouse brain IMS at 100 um) has region assignments (auto-clusters or manual ROIs) and you need up/downregulated differential metabolites between two regions.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-abundance-testing Use when a pixel x m/z feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions from AFAD-ESI positive-mode mouse brain IMS at 100 um) has region assignments (auto-clusters or manual ROIs) and you need up/downregulated differential metabolites between two regions. Input is raw imaging MS data (not yet peak-picked into a pixel x m/z feature matrix CSV) — SMAnalyst requires the processed feature matrix, not instrument files No spatial region definition exists (no clusters, no manual ROIs), so the two comparison groups cannot be formed The question requires true biological-replicate statistics across tissue sections rather than within-section pixel-level comparisons, since this method treats pixels in a region as samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Identifies metabolites (ion peaks) whose abundances differ between spatially defined regions of a tissue, using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and fold-change filters, as implemented in SMAnalyst's flexible differential analysis module and benchmarked against Cardinal. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Identifies metabolites (ion peaks) whose abundances differ between spatially defined regions of a tissue, using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and fold-change filters, as implemented in SMAnalyst's flexible differential analysis module and benchmarked against Cardinal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw imaging MS data (not yet peak-picked into a pixel x m/z feature matrix CSV) — SMAnalyst requires the processed feature matrix, not instrument files No spatial region definition exists (no clusters, no manual ROIs), so the two comparison groups cannot be formed The question requires true biological-replicate statistics across tissue sections rather than within-section pixel-level comparisons, since this method treats pixels in a region as samples

skills.description: Use when you have matrices normalized by different strategies (tGAM/rGAM/rLOESS, QC-RLSC, SERFF, TIGER) and need to quantify how the choice of normalization changes the differential abundance hit set.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-abundance-testing Use when you have matrices normalized by different strategies (tGAM/rGAM/rLOESS, QC-RLSC, SERFF, TIGER) and need to quantify how the choice of normalization changes the differential abundance hit set. Input is raw unnormalized data — the skill presupposes matrices already normalized with metanorm() under matched QCcheck = TRUE and batchwise settings Goal is to assess normalization quality directly (QC drift, batch-effect removal in PCA score plots) rather than its effect on downstream differential abundance hit sets The dataset has no replicate or contrast structure supporting differential abundance testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs differential metabolite abundance (DAM) testing on normalized LC-MS metabolomics matrices (e.g., ENVIRONAGE urine, 393 runs × 269 metabolites) produced by alternative normalization strategies, then quantifies agreement between strategies via DAM overlap percentages, pairwise Spearman correlations, and Euclidean distances to benchmark normalization methods on downstream statistical power. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Runs differential metabolite abundance (DAM) testing on normalized LC-MS metabolomics matrices (e.g., ENVIRONAGE urine, 393 runs × 269 metabolites) produced by alternative normalization strategies, then quantifies agreement between strategies via DAM overlap percentages, pairwise Spearman correlations, and Euclidean distances to benchmark normalization methods on downstream statistical power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unnormalized data — the skill presupposes matrices already normalized with metanorm() under matched QCcheck = TRUE and batchwise settings Goal is to assess normalization quality directly (QC drift, batch-effect removal in PCA score plots) rather than its effect on downstream differential abundance hit sets The dataset has no replicate or contrast structure supporting differential abundance testing

skills.description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion peaks) has been pixel-clustered (e.g., UMAP-kmeans) and you must identify metabolites significantly upregulated in one anatomical region versus another, with per-region annotation counts.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-annotation-counting
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-annotation-counting Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion peaks) has been pixel-clustered (e.g., UMAP-kmeans) and you must identify metabolites significantly upregulated in one anatomical region versus another, with per-region annotation counts. Input is not a spatial pixel-level feature matrix (e.g., bulk LC-MS peak tables) or lacks pixel-cluster assignments needed to define the two compared regions Region boundaries are already known and manually drawn as ROIs rather than derived from UMAP-kmeans pixel clustering, where SMAnalyst's manual ROI differential mode may be simpler The dataset is small (< thousands of pixels) such that a simple t-test or limma on ROIs suffices without the Seurat/SMAnalyst pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Performs region-wise differential metabolite testing on spatial metabolomics pixel data (e.g., midbrain clusters 6/1 vs hippocampal clusters 23/12 from a 14,260-pixel × 3,044-ion mouse brain feature matrix) using Seurat's Wilcoxon rank-sum FindMarkers with FC > 2 or < 0.5 and FDR < 0.01 filters, then tabulates annotated metabolite counts per region. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Performs region-wise differential metabolite testing on spatial metabolomics pixel data (e.g., midbrain clusters 6/1 vs hippocampal clusters 23/12 from a 14,260-pixel × 3,044-ion mouse brain feature matrix) using Seurat's Wilcoxon rank-sum FindMarkers with FC > 2 or < 0.5 and FDR < 0.01 filters, then tabulates annotated metabolite counts per region.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a spatial pixel-level feature matrix (e.g., bulk LC-MS peak tables) or lacks pixel-cluster assignments needed to define the two compared regions Region boundaries are already known and manually drawn as ROIs rather than derived from UMAP-kmeans pixel clustering, where SMAnalyst's manual ROI differential mode may be simpler The dataset is small (< thousands of pixels) such that a simple t-test or limma on ROIs suffices without the Seurat/SMAnalyst pipeline

skills.description: Use when comparing two maize root DESI-MSI datasets whose mass signatures were already extracted along a linear developmental gradient by DIMPLE and you need a conserved/unique partition of pooled m/z peaks per variety.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-comparison-between-maize-varieties
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-comparison-between-maize-varieties Use when comparing two maize root DESI-MSI datasets whose mass signatures were already extracted along a linear developmental gradient by DIMPLE and you need a conserved/unique partition of pooled m/z peaks per variety. Input is raw MSI spectra (cdf files) not yet processed by DIMPLE along the linear developmental axis — use the DIMPLE gradient pipeline first to generate per-root mass signature lists. The comparison involves more than two varieties or non-maize tissue where the linear root developmental axis does not apply — the skill's partition thresholds and validation counts are specific to the B73 vs. Oaxacan Green maize root setup. The goal is annotating unknown mass signatures rather than partitioning conserved vs. unique ones — use METASPACE, Metlin Classic, or LOTUS instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Pools DESI-MSI mass signatures from two maize varieties (within a 0.001 m/z tolerance, via DIMPLE peak-compilation in R) and partitions them into conserved vs. variety-unique sets, counting each partition — as done for salt-resilient Oaxacan Green vs. salt-susceptible B73 (91 conserved, 210 B73-unique, 991 OG-unique, Supplemental Table 8). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Pools DESI-MSI mass signatures from two maize varieties (within a 0.001 m/z tolerance, via DIMPLE peak-compilation in R) and partitions them into conserved vs. variety-unique sets, counting each partition — as done for salt-resilient Oaxacan Green vs. salt-susceptible B73 (91 conserved, 210 B73-unique, 991 OG-unique, Supplemental Table 8).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MSI spectra (cdf files) not yet processed by DIMPLE along the linear developmental axis — use the DIMPLE gradient pipeline first to generate per-root mass signature lists. The comparison involves more than two varieties or non-maize tissue where the linear root developmental axis does not apply — the skill's partition thresholds and validation counts are specific to the B73 vs. Oaxacan Green maize root setup. The goal is annotating unknown mass signatures rather than partitioning conserved vs. unique ones — use METASPACE, Metlin Classic, or LOTUS instead.

skills.description: Decision support for whether missing-value imputation choices materially change the differential-metabolite lists and enriched pathways in an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table, e.g. when a case study applied only one imputation method.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-detection-across-imputation-methods
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-detection-across-imputation-methods Decision support for whether missing-value imputation choices materially change the differential-metabolite lists and enriched pathways in an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table, e.g. when a case study applied only one imputation method. The input is raw LC-MS data rather than an already-cleaned feature table — noisy-feature filtering (≤20% MV in QC, ≤50% MV in study groups) and peak processing must happen first. Only annotations below level 2 are available, since the subsequent analysis uses only level-2 annotations. The goal is a single definitive differential-metabolite analysis under one chosen imputation method rather than an inter-method sensitivity comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 A sensitivity-analysis skill that re-runs the tidyMass differential-metabolite and pathway-enrichment analysis under each missing-value imputation method available in massCleaner (BPCA, svdImpute, missForest, zero, mean, median, minimum), then compares concordance of results. It addresses the fact that the colorectal cancer case study applied only K-nearest-neighbor imputation without reporting alternatives. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill that re-runs the tidyMass differential-metabolite and pathway-enrichment analysis under each missing-value imputation method available in massCleaner (BPCA, svdImpute, missForest, zero, mean, median, minimum), then compares concordance of results. It addresses the fact that the colorectal cancer case study applied only K-nearest-neighbor imputation without reporting alternatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-MS data rather than an already-cleaned feature table — noisy-feature filtering (≤20% MV in QC, ≤50% MV in study groups) and peak processing must happen first. Only annotations below level 2 are available, since the subsequent analysis uses only level-2 annotations. The goal is a single definitive differential-metabolite analysis under one chosen imputation method rather than an inter-method sensitivity comparison.

skills.description: Use when raw MS1 LC-HRMS data from paired treated vs. heat-inactivated control incubations (e.g., 1,021 pesticides in human liver S9) must be feature-detected, aligned, and differentially screened to feed reaction-guided metabolite annotation.
skills.name: differential-metabolite-feature-detection
skills.search_text: differential-metabolite-feature-detection Use when raw MS1 LC-HRMS data from paired treated vs. heat-inactivated control incubations (e.g., 1,021 pesticides in human liver S9) must be feature-detected, aligned, and differentially screened to feed reaction-guided metabolite annotation. The input is already an aligned feature table or only MS2/PRM data without paired PG/CG MS1 acquisitions — proceed directly to the RCS or SSN layers instead The goal is targeted quantification of known parent compounds rather than discovery of unannotated biotransformation-derived features Samples lack a heat-inactivated (or otherwise enzymatically inactivated) control group, making the differential PG/CG fold-change screening undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 The differential metabolite space (DMS) layer of the CMDN 'top-down' framework: peak detection, feature alignment, and fold-change/SNR/t-test screening of LC-HRMS MS1 features between pesticide-incubated and heat-inactivated control samples, to isolate biotransformation-derived features for downstream CMDN layers. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: The differential metabolite space (DMS) layer of the CMDN 'top-down' framework: peak detection, feature alignment, and fold-change/SNR/t-test screening of LC-HRMS MS1 features between pesticide-incubated and heat-inactivated control samples, to isolate biotransformation-derived features for downstream CMDN layers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an aligned feature table or only MS2/PRM data without paired PG/CG MS1 acquisitions — proceed directly to the RCS or SSN layers instead The goal is targeted quantification of known parent compounds rather than discovery of unannotated biotransformation-derived features Samples lack a heat-inactivated (or otherwise enzymatically inactivated) control group, making the differential PG/CG fold-change screening undefined

skills.description: Use when a two-condition metabolomics network has been estimated under alternative lambda/regularization settings and you must tabulate total vs case-specific vs control-specific vs shared edges to judge tuning impact.
skills.name: differential-network-edge-count-comparison
skills.search_text: differential-network-edge-count-comparison Use when a two-condition metabolomics network has been estimated under alternative lambda/regularization settings and you must tabulate total vs case-specific vs control-specific vs shared edges to judge tuning impact. The dataset is a single experimental condition — DNEA performs joint network estimation across two groups, so differential edge counts are undefined The goal is pathway or module enrichment (NetGSA) rather than comparing network reconstruction settings Features/samples have not been preprocessed (metabolites missing in >30% of samples not excluded, median imputation and age/sex regression residuals not applied), making edge counts incomparable to the reference results http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies and compares total and condition-specific (differential) edge counts between two DNEA network configurations — BIC-tuned lambda versus the approximated lambda (sqrt(ln(num features)/num samples)) Filigree default — after filtering to |partial correlation| >= 0.2. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Quantifies and compares total and condition-specific (differential) edge counts between two DNEA network configurations — BIC-tuned lambda versus the approximated lambda (sqrt(ln(num features)/num samples)) Filigree default — after filtering to |partial correlation| >= 0.2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a single experimental condition — DNEA performs joint network estimation across two groups, so differential edge counts are undefined The goal is pathway or module enrichment (NetGSA) rather than comparing network reconstruction settings Features/samples have not been preprocessed (metabolites missing in >30% of samples not excluded, median imputation and age/sex regression residuals not applied), making edge counts incomparable to the reference results

skills.description: Use when a DNEA object with estimated two-condition partial correlation networks (e.g. TEDDY metabolomics, 134 metabolites) must be partitioned into metabolic modules and you need to set or adjust the consensus agreement threshold (tau).

skills.search_text: differential-network-module-agreement-thresholding Use when a DNEA object with estimated two-condition partial correlation networks (e.g. TEDDY metabolomics, 134 metabolites) must be partitioned into metabolic modules and you need to set or adjust the consensus agreement threshold (tau). Input is a single-condition network or one-group metabolomics data — DNEA/clusterNet requires two experimental groups for joint estimation before consensus clustering Metabolites are well-annotated endogenous compounds that map cleanly to pathway databases — conventional pathway enrichment analysis may be preferable to data-driven modules Networks are unfiltered and very dense — module detection should follow filterNetworks() edge-strength filtering (percentile or partial correlation threshold) to control network density http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Identifies metabolic modules (subnetworks) in DNEA-estimated differential metabolite networks by consensus clustering over seven igraph algorithms, where the tau parameter sets the fraction of algorithms (default 0.5, i.e. 4 of 7) that must agree on subnetwork membership. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Identifies metabolic modules (subnetworks) in DNEA-estimated differential metabolite networks by consensus clustering over seven igraph algorithms, where the tau parameter sets the fraction of algorithms (default 0.5, i.e. 4 of 7) that must agree on subnetwork membership.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-condition network or one-group metabolomics data — DNEA/clusterNet requires two experimental groups for joint estimation before consensus clustering Metabolites are well-annotated endogenous compounds that map cleanly to pathway databases — conventional pathway enrichment analysis may be preferable to data-driven modules Networks are unfiltered and very dense — module detection should follow filterNetworks() edge-strength filtering (percentile or partial correlation threshold) to control network density

skills.search_text: differential-pathway-activity-t-testing Use when comparing two sample groups (e.g., DM2 vs NGT microarray profiles) to find pathways whose PLAGE-derived activity levels differ significantly, using t statistics calibrated by max-t label permutations. skills.search_text: differential-peak-enrichment-analysis Use when a fitted MSI segmentation exists (e.g., spatial shrunken centroids in Cardinal on imzML-derived pig fetus liver/heart data) and you must report which peaks each segment differentially enriches or lacks. skills.summary: Quantifies which m/z peaks are systematically enriched or absent in a specific image segment (e.g., liver or heart in pig fetus MSI sections) by ranking per-segment t-statistics from a fitted spatial shrunken centroids segmentation, then validating against reported enriched/absent peak counts.

skills.description: Use when trained DiffSpectra/DMT checkpoints and multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) from QM9S are available and the goal is spectra-conditioned molecular generation with reproducible top-k accuracy metrics.
skills.name: diffusion-model-checkpoint-inference
skills.search_text: diffusion-model-checkpoint-inference Use when trained DiffSpectra/DMT checkpoints and multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) from QM9S are available and the goal is spectra-conditioned molecular generation with reproducible top-k accuracy metrics. Input spectra are NMR or mass spectrometry data — the framework covers only UV-Vis, IR, and Raman modalities, and its applicability to other modalities remains unexplored. The goal is training or pre-training SpecFormer (masked patches reconstruction / contrastive alignment) rather than inference from an existing checkpoint. The task requires experimental/laboratory validation of structures — the paper's validation is primarily computational. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Run a trained DiffSpectra checkpoint (DMT denoiser conditioned on SpecFormer spectral embeddings) in eval mode to generate molecules from Gaussian noise via the reverse denoising process, then score generated structures against ground truth for exact-structure accuracy and quality metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Run a trained DiffSpectra checkpoint (DMT denoiser conditioned on SpecFormer spectral embeddings) in eval mode to generate molecules from Gaussian noise via the reverse denoising process, then score generated structures against ground truth for exact-structure accuracy and quality metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are NMR or mass spectrometry data — the framework covers only UV-Vis, IR, and Raman modalities, and its applicability to other modalities remains unexplored. The goal is training or pre-training SpecFormer (masked patches reconstruction / contrastive alignment) rather than inference from an existing checkpoint. The task requires experimental/laboratory validation of structures — the paper's validation is primarily computational.

skills.name: diffusion-sampler-evaluation
skills.search_text: diffusion-sampler-evaluation Use when you have a trained spectra-conditioned DiffSpectra (DMT) checkpoint and QM9S test spectra (spectra_version ir/raman/uv/allspectra) and need to generate molecules and reproduce accuracy/MCES ablation tables. Input spectra are NMR or mass spectrometry: the framework currently focuses only on three spectral types (UV-Vis, IR, Raman) and applicability to NMR/MS remains unexplored. You only need to rescore already-generated molecules: run eval_sampled_mols/base_metrics.py directly instead of rerunning the full diffusion sampling loop. You need experimentally (laboratory) validated structure elucidation: validation to date has been primarily computational on simulated QM9S spectra. Samples molecules from a spectra-conditioned diffusion model (DiffSpectra/DMT) in eval mode and scores them against ground-truth structures using exact-match top-1/top-10 accuracy, MCES, and RMSD. It operationalizes multi-modality ablation questions (e.g., IR vs Raman vs UV-Vis vs allspectra conditioning) on the QM9S benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Samples molecules from a spectra-conditioned diffusion model (DiffSpectra/DMT) in eval mode and scores them against ground-truth structures using exact-match top-1/top-10 accuracy, MCES, and RMSD. It operationalizes multi-modality ablation questions (e.g., IR vs Raman vs UV-Vis vs allspectra conditioning) on the QM9S benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are NMR or mass spectrometry: the framework currently focuses only on three spectral types (UV-Vis, IR, Raman) and applicability to NMR/MS remains unexplored. skills.description: Decision support for choosing the noise-scaling temperature τ when generating candidate molecules with a spectra-conditioned diffusion sampler, especially when generated sets look overly deterministic (low τ) or too random (high τ).
skills.name: diffusion-sampler-temperature-sweep
skills.search_text: diffusion-sampler-temperature-sweep Decision support for choosing the noise-scaling temperature τ when generating candidate molecules with a spectra-conditioned diffusion sampler, especially when generated sets look overly deterministic (low τ) or too random (high τ). The task is training SpecFormer or the diffusion model itself rather than tuning sampling-time noise scale. Only a single fixed temperature is required and no sweep/diversity-vs-accuracy comparison is needed. Spectra are NMR or mass spectrometry modalities, which DiffSpectra explicitly does not support. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Sweeps the sampling temperature τ that scales injected noise during DiffSpectra's reverse-time denoising to map the trade-off between structural diversity and elucidation accuracy, with τ=1.0 as the best setting (40.76% top-1 accuracy). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853

Input is already an aligned feature table or identification-based peptide output rather than raw runs needing feature extraction Feature lists come from a format requiring special handling, e.g. MaxQuant allPeptides.txt (old versions with a 'Resolution' column), where Dinosaur mode is the wrong choice and MaxQuant-specific preprocessing is needed Samples are quite different or contain many features with nearly identical m/z, where the default score-based QC reports very few results and FDR=1 with a score>0.5 cutoff is recommended instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extract MS features (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from DIA-MS runs using the Dinosaur feature-detection tool so that the resulting per-run feature lists can serve as direct input to DeepRTAlign's deep learning-based retention time alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Extract MS features (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from DIA-MS runs using the Dinosaur feature-detection tool so that the resulting per-run feature lists can serve as direct input to DeepRTAlign's deep learning-based retention time alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table or identification-based peptide output rather than raw runs needing feature extraction Feature lists come from a format requiring special handling, e.g. MaxQuant allPeptides.txt (old versions with a 'Resolution' column), where Dinosaur mode is the wrong choice and MaxQuant-specific preprocessing is needed Samples are quite different or contain many features with nearly identical m/z, where the default score-based QC reports very few results and FDR=1 with a score>0.5 cutoff is recommended instead

skills.description: Use when input is raw .mgf, .mzML or .mzXML spectra from direct injection / plasma ionization (DBDI) MS with no LC separation, and a row-per-feature, column-per-scan DataFrame is needed before imputation or adduct detection.
skills.name: direct-infusion-ms-feature-alignment
skills.search_text: direct-infusion-ms-feature-alignment Use when input is raw .mgf, .mzML or .mzXML spectra from direct injection / plasma ionization (DBDI) MS with no LC separation, and a row-per-feature, column-per-scan DataFrame is needed before imputation or adduct detection. Input is already an aligned feature table — align_spectra() can be skipped per the tutorial ('If your data already is formatted accordingly, you can skip this step'). Data comes from chromatography-coupled LC-MS where features are defined by retention time alignment rather than direct-infusion scan-wise m/z alignment. A ppm_window mismatched to instrument accuracy is required — mass alignment tolerance must reflect the mass spectrometer's error (2 ppm was appropriate for FT-ICR, not for low-resolution instruments). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aligns raw mass spectra from direct-infusion (no chromatographic separation) MS experiments — e.g. DBDI-FT-ICR-MS — into a 2D feature table of m/z rows versus scan columns using DBDIpy's align_spectra() over matchms-imported spectra. This feature table is the prerequisite for imputation and adduct/in-source fragment detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad088
skills.summary: Aligns raw mass spectra from direct-infusion (no chromatographic separation) MS experiments — e.g. DBDI-FT-ICR-MS — into a 2D feature table of m/z rows versus scan columns using DBDIpy's align_spectra() over matchms-imported spectra. This feature table is the prerequisite for imputation and adduct/in-source fragment detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table — align_spectra() can be skipped per the tutorial ('If your data already is formatted accordingly, you can skip this step'). Data comes from chromatography-coupled LC-MS where features are defined by retention time alignment rather than direct-infusion scan-wise m/z alignment. A ppm_window mismatched to instrument accuracy is required — mass alignment tolerance must reflect the mass spectrometer's error (2 ppm was appropriate for FT-ICR, not for low-resolution instruments).

skills.description: Use when a compound has multiple candidate ChemOnt categories after category reduction and you need to determine the single direct parent for a taxonomic classification record.
skills.name: direct-parent-selection-by-feature-weight
skills.search_text: direct-parent-selection-by-feature-weight Use when a compound has multiple candidate ChemOnt categories after category reduction and you need to determine the single direct parent for a taxonomic classification record. Input is a single feature mapped to one category with no parent-child overlap — category reduction already yielded one candidate and no tie-break is needed Compounds from a category that undergo reactions (e.g. loss of oxygen, substitutions) that might not match the constraints described in a category description Input is an IUPAC name where parsing rules were insufficient to accurately assign the class — the upstream feature extraction step, not parent selection, is the failure point http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Final classification step in ClassyFire: after category reduction, the direct parent is chosen as the category whose structural feature is largest (by weight), with weight ties broken using structural keys and a manually compiled exception list. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y

skills.description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) must be converted into a per-metabolite concentration/integral table without fitting or deconvolution, relying on SMolESY preprocessing and predefined spin-system bins.
skills.name: direct-peak-integration-assigned-components
skills.search_text: direct-peak-integration-assigned-components Use when raw 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) must be converted into a per-metabolite concentration/integral table without fitting or deconvolution, relying on SMolESY preprocessing and predefined spin-system bins. Input is already a binned/integrated feature table or quantified metabolite panel — no spectral assignment or integration is needed. The spectra are 2D (2D-Jres) or non-standard 1D acquisitions; SMolESY-select requires standard one-dimensional 1H NMR spectra. A problem demands full spectral deconvolution or baseline fitting of severely overlapped regions that fall outside the predefined 24 spin-system bins. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Quantitative metabolite measurement from 1D 1H NMR spectra by assigning spin-system patterns inside predefined SMolESY bins and then directly integrating the assigned components, precluding complex deconvolution and spectral baseline fitting (the SMolESY-select quantitation step, targeting 22 plasma/serum metabolites). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Quantitative metabolite measurement from 1D 1H NMR spectra by assigning spin-system patterns inside predefined SMolESY bins and then directly integrating the assigned components, precluding complex deconvolution and spectral baseline fitting (the SMolESY-select quantitation step, targeting 22 plasma/serum metabolites).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a binned/integrated feature table or quantified metabolite panel — no spectral assignment or integration is needed. The spectra are 2D (2D-Jres) or non-standard 1D acquisitions; SMolESY-select requires standard one-dimensional 1H NMR spectra. A problem demands full spectral deconvolution or baseline fitting of severely overlapped regions that fall outside the predefined 24 spin-system bins.

skills.name: directed-acyclic-graph-tree-conversion
skills.search_text: directed-acyclic-graph-tree-conversion Use when you have a mass distance network of LC-MS feature pairs (e.g. 13C/12C 1.0034 Da isotope steps, 22.9893 Da Na+ adduct shifts) and need to organize ions into per-compound trees with inferred neutral masses. When the goal is complete/deep annotation — khipu output is preannotation; complete annotation still requires contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS data When the input is raw vendor data or LC-MS runs rather than a preprocessed feature table (preprocessing with asari 1.9.2 or equivalent must happen first) When isotope search patterns of the biochemical experiment differ from defaults without supplying custom patterns — users must overwrite defaults via demo-notebook-style configuration http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Converts a mass-distance-network subnetwork of pattern-matched LC-MS features into a rooted tree (khipu/empirical compound) via DAG enforcement plus two-step trunk/branch optimization, then infers the neutral M0 mass by linear regression against the khipu grid. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Converts a mass-distance-network subnetwork of pattern-matched LC-MS features into a rooted tree (khipu/empirical compound) via DAG enforcement plus two-step trunk/branch optimization, then infers the neutral M0 mass by linear regression against the khipu grid.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is complete/deep annotation — khipu output is preannotation; complete annotation still requires contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS data When the input is raw vendor data or LC-MS runs rather than a preprocessed feature table (preprocessing with asari 1.9.2 or equivalent must happen first) When isotope search patterns of the biochemical experiment differ from defaults without supplying custom patterns — users must overwrite defaults via demo-notebook-style configuration

skills.description: Use when two or more independently processed LC-MS datasets must be aligned into a Combined Dataset, and pairwise subalignment match tables are available to load into a graph-based clustering step.
skills.name: directed-graph-clustering
skills.search_text: directed-graph-clustering Use when two or more independently processed LC-MS datasets must be aligned into a Combined Dataset, and pairwise subalignment match tables are available to load into a graph-based clustering step. The input is already a single aligned/complete dataset with no pairwise match tables to reconcile The task is clustering redundant features within one dataset based on RT and correlation — that is Gravity's cluster step, not Eclipse's cross-dataset graph alignment The task is drift correction via pooled technical replicates and internal standards — that is Blueshift's DriftCorrection, not graph-based alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Eclipse aligns two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics datasets by loading pairwise subalignment match tables into a directed graph (features = nodes, matches = edges, match penalties = edge weights), retaining bidirectional edges, and running an iterative group-ranking clustering to form cross-dataset feature groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: Eclipse aligns two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics datasets by loading pairwise subalignment match tables into a directed graph (features = nodes, matches = edges, match penalties = edge weights), retaining bidirectional edges, and running an iterative group-ranking clustering to form cross-dataset feature groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a single aligned/complete dataset with no pairwise match tables to reconcile The task is clustering redundant features within one dataset based on RT and correlation — that is Gravity's cluster step, not Eclipse's cross-dataset graph alignment The task is drift correction via pooled technical replicates and internal standards — that is Blueshift's DriftCorrection, not graph-based alignment

skills.description: Use when a directed reaction network built from mass-shift annotations contains cycles among metabolites and you need per-initial-metabolite DAGs from which the longest valid reaction path can be extracted.
skills.name: directed-graph-cycle-removal-to-dag
skills.search_text: directed-graph-cycle-removal-to-dag Use when a directed reaction network built from mass-shift annotations contains cycles among metabolites and you need per-initial-metabolite DAGs from which the longest valid reaction path can be extracted. The candidate reactions are multi-substrate conversions: RetroRules-based rules in MEANtools are designed for single-substrate reactions only (e.g. p-coumaroyltyramine formation requires two substrates), so DAG edges cannot represent them Accurate stereochemistry is required: mass spectrometric data does not capture stereoisomers, and MEANtools deliberately filters stereomeric RetroRules rules, so the DAG cannot resolve stereoisomeric steps The network is already acyclic per substrate or the goal is generic graph analytics unrelated to mass-shift-derived biosynthetic pathway reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 MEANtools' strategy for converting a cyclic directed reaction network — whose nodes are measured and unmeasured (ghost) mass signatures linked by annotated mass shifts — into one acyclic per-substrate DAG by eliminating the weakest enzyme–metabolite correlation edge inside each same-distance cycle, then extracting the longest valid reaction path. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: MEANtools' strategy for converting a cyclic directed reaction network — whose nodes are measured and unmeasured (ghost) mass signatures linked by annotated mass shifts — into one acyclic per-substrate DAG by eliminating the weakest enzyme–metabolite correlation edge inside each same-distance cycle, then extracting the longest valid reaction path.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate reactions are multi-substrate conversions: RetroRules-based rules in MEANtools are designed for single-substrate reactions only (e.g. p-coumaroyltyramine formation requires two substrates), so DAG edges cannot represent them Accurate stereochemistry is required: mass spectrometric data does not capture stereoisomers, and MEANtools deliberately filters stereomeric RetroRules rules, so the DAG cannot resolve stereoisomeric steps The network is already acyclic per substrate or the goal is generic graph analytics unrelated to mass-shift-derived biosynthetic pathway reconstruction

skills.description: Use when interpreting ReporterScore/GRSA enrichment results on KO abundance data and you need to decide whether reporter score signs can be read as pathway-level increasing or decreasing trends.
skills.name: directed-vs-mixed-enrichment-mode-interpretation
skills.search_text: directed-vs-mixed-enrichment-mode-interpretation Use when interpreting ReporterScore/GRSA enrichment results on KO abundance data and you need to decide whether reporter score signs can be read as pathway-level increasing or decreasing trends. The KO abundance table has been prefiltered to background/significant features only — GRSA is a threshold-free method and requires the unfiltered abundance table The goal is a standard over-representation (hypergeometric/Fisher) analysis of a pre-defined KO list rather than signed, threshold-free reporter scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces the GRSA directed-vs-mixed mode comparison on the packaged ex_KO_profile metagenomic data to demonstrate that directed-mode reporter score signs preserve within-pathway KO trends while mixed-mode signs are uninterpretable due to cancellation of opposing-trend KOs. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116

skills.when_to_use_negative: The KO abundance table has been prefiltered to background/significant features only — GRSA is a threshold-free method and requires the unfiltered abundance table The goal is a standard over-representation (hypergeometric/Fisher) analysis of a pre-defined KO list rather than signed, threshold-free reporter scoring

skills.description: Use when ΔCt qPCR data for metabolic enzyme genes are collected across oncogene-transformed versus control epithelial cells and each gene's direction of change must be tabulated with statistical support.
skills.name: direction-of-change-annotation
skills.search_text: direction-of-change-annotation Use when ΔCt qPCR data for metabolic enzyme genes are collected across oncogene-transformed versus control epithelial cells and each gene's direction of change must be tabulated with statistical support. Data are mass-spectrometry metabolite intensities rather than qPCR ΔCt values — metabolite direction calls need metabolite-level statistics, not Taqman probe annotation Comparisons are not against a common control baseline (e.g. two transformed lines compared directly without a RWPE-EV anchor) — one-sample T-Test against the baseline would be misapplied Tumour-level phosphoAKT1/MYC immunoblot densitometry is the input, since those data are clustered by K-means rather than tested per-gene direction of change http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Annotates qPCR-derived expression of metabolic target genes (e.g. GLUT-1, hexokinase 2, glutaminase, choline kinase alpha) as increased / decreased / unchanged per engineered prostate cell line, using one-sample T-Tests against the RWPE-EV baseline. Encodes the transcriptional counterpart of AKT1/MYC-driven metabolome shifts reported by mass-spectrometry metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1158/0008-5472.can-14-1490
skills.summary: Annotates qPCR-derived expression of metabolic target genes (e.g. GLUT-1, hexokinase 2, glutaminase, choline kinase alpha) as increased / decreased / unchanged per engineered prostate cell line, using one-sample T-Tests against the RWPE-EV baseline. Encodes the transcriptional counterpart of AKT1/MYC-driven metabolome shifts reported by mass-spectrometry metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are mass-spectrometry metabolite intensities rather than qPCR ΔCt values — metabolite direction calls need metabolite-level statistics, not Taqman probe annotation Comparisons are not against a common control baseline (e.g. two transformed lines compared directly without a RWPE-EV anchor) — one-sample T-Test against the baseline would be misapplied Tumour-level phosphoAKT1/MYC immunoblot densitometry is the input, since those data are clustered by K-means rather than tested per-gene direction of change

skills.description: Use when validating whether a structural-comparison tool's double bond position matching is correct, by quantifying mismatch probabilities over high-resolution reference lipid entries from SwissLipids or LIPID MAPS.
skills.name: directional-db-mismatch-probability-computation
skills.search_text: directional-db-mismatch-probability-computation Use when validating whether a structural-comparison tool's double bond position matching is correct, by quantifying mismatch probabilities over high-resolution reference lipid entries from SwissLipids or LIPID MAPS. When the input is user lipidomics sample data rather than a reference database of fully resolved lipid structures — the mismatch statistic requires structural ground truth, not measured abundances When lipid identifiers lack explicit double bond positions (e.g., species-level names like PC 34:1); the comparison is undefined until names are parsed to a higher structural resolution When the goal is lipidome similarity or maximum-common-subgraph distance computation rather than assessing double bond position comparison correctness http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Computes, over a reference lipid structure database (SwissLipids), the probability that two arbitrary fatty-acyl carbon chains share no double bond at the same position, under both counting conventions (forward from the carbonyl carbon and backward/omega from the methyl end), to ground the correctness of double bond position comparisons in LipidSpace. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is user lipidomics sample data rather than a reference database of fully resolved lipid structures — the mismatch statistic requires structural ground truth, not measured abundances When lipid identifiers lack explicit double bond positions (e.g., species-level names like PC 34:1); the comparison is undefined until names are parsed to a higher structural resolution When the goal is lipidome similarity or maximum-common-subgraph distance computation rather than assessing double bond position comparison correctness

When the metabolite and GWAS gene sets are paired from a single metabolomics-GWAS study — metGWAS 1.0 is explicitly designed for independent, unpaired data sets limited to genes with known metabolite interactions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Defines the population universe for metGWAS 1.0's hypergeometric over-representation test by restricting the background to the 'discoverable gene set' — the genes that could in principle appear in both the metabolite-interaction gene set and the GWAS-network gene set — rather than using all known genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523

skills.description: Use when a generative model must output molecular graphs with a prescribed atom count/type composition (formula-constrained generation), by diffusing and denoising bond-type entries of the adjacency matrix.
skills.name: discrete-diffusion-process-design
skills.search_text: discrete-diffusion-process-design Use when a generative model must output molecular graphs with a prescribed atom count/type composition (formula-constrained generation), by diffusing and denoising bond-type entries of the adjacency matrix. The number or type of atoms is unknown a priori — this formulation fixes node features X from the given formula and cannot vary heavy-atom composition Generation is over continuous node/edge attributes or non-graph outputs; discrete categorical diffusion over adjacency entries is unnecessary there (DiGress offers a separate continuous model mode) Working with very large graphs (more than 100-200 nodes) where the dense DiGress-style diffusion is impractical and a sparse variant is recommended http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Design a discrete (categorical) diffusion process over molecular graph adjacency matrices, following the DiGress formulation, so that generation can natively respect a fixed heavy-atom composition imposed by a known chemical formula. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Design a discrete (categorical) diffusion process over molecular graph adjacency matrices, following the DiGress formulation, so that generation can natively respect a fixed heavy-atom composition imposed by a known chemical formula.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number or type of atoms is unknown a priori — this formulation fixes node features X from the given formula and cannot vary heavy-atom composition Generation is over continuous node/edge attributes or non-graph outputs; discrete categorical diffusion over adjacency entries is unnecessary there (DiGress offers a separate continuous model mode) Working with very large graphs (more than 100-200 nodes) where the dense DiGress-style diffusion is impractical and a sparse variant is recommended

skills.description: Use when a tandem mass spectrum plus an inferred chemical formula must be converted into de novo candidate structures, or when reproducing DiffMS-style top-k accuracy, Tanimoto, and MCES metrics on NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym.
skills.name: discrete-graph-diffusion-molecule-sampling
skills.search_text: discrete-graph-diffusion-molecule-sampling Use when a tandem mass spectrum plus an inferred chemical formula must be converted into de novo candidate structures, or when reproducing DiffMS-style top-k accuracy, Tanimoto, and MCES metrics on NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym. Only a molecular formula or fingerprint must be predicted (use the MIST formula transformer / spectrum-to-fingerprint pretraining stage instead of the diffusion decoder). The task is the forward MS problem (spectra from structures) rather than the 'inverse' de novo generation problem. No chemical formula/heavy-atom composition is available to constrain generation, since the diffusion process is formula-restricted by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Samples candidate molecular structures from a tandem mass spectrum using a permutation-invariant discrete diffusion model over the molecular adjacency matrix, conditioned on the spectrum and the formula-derived heavy-atom composition (the DiffMS approach built on DiGress). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Samples candidate molecular structures from a tandem mass spectrum using a permutation-invariant discrete diffusion model over the molecular adjacency matrix, conditioned on the spectrum and the formula-derived heavy-atom composition (the DiffMS approach built on DiGress).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a molecular formula or fingerprint must be predicted (use the MIST formula transformer / spectrum-to-fingerprint pretraining stage instead of the diffusion decoder). The task is the forward MS problem (spectra from structures) rather than the 'inverse' de novo generation problem. No chemical formula/heavy-atom composition is available to constrain generation, since the diffusion process is formula-restricted by design.

skills.description: Use when conditional molecular structure generation requires sampling valid, formula-constrained graphs with predefined heavy-atom composition, e.g. de novo generation from mass spectra on NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym benchmarks.
skills.name: discrete-graph-diffusion-training
skills.search_text: discrete-graph-diffusion-training Use when conditional molecular structure generation requires sampling valid, formula-constrained graphs with predefined heavy-atom composition, e.g. de novo generation from mass spectra on NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym benchmarks. The task is fingerprint prediction from spectra rather than graph generation — use the MIST spectrum-to-fingerprint encoder training instead The chemical formula is unknown — DiffMS is formula-restricted and relies on formula inference tools (SIRIUS, BUDDY, MIST-CF) upstream Working with graphs of more than 100-200 nodes — the DiGress-derived dense diffusion is not designed for large graphs (consider SparseDiff per the DiGress README) http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a permutation-invariant discrete diffusion model (DiffMS, adapted from DiGress) on molecular adjacency matrices with a 5-class bond-type vocabulary (no bond, single, double, triple, aromatic), pretraining the diffusion decoder on ~2.8M fingerprint-molecule pairs and finetuning end-to-end on spectra-molecule data. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Train a permutation-invariant discrete diffusion model (DiffMS, adapted from DiGress) on molecular adjacency matrices with a 5-class bond-type vocabulary (no bond, single, double, triple, aromatic), pretraining the diffusion decoder on ~2.8M fingerprint-molecule pairs and finetuning end-to-end on spectra-molecule data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is fingerprint prediction from spectra rather than graph generation — use the MIST spectrum-to-fingerprint encoder training instead The chemical formula is unknown — DiffMS is formula-restricted and relies on formula inference tools (SIRIUS, BUDDY, MIST-CF) upstream Working with graphs of more than 100-200 nodes — the DiGress-derived dense diffusion is not designed for large graphs (consider SparseDiff per the DiGress README)

skills.search_text: discriminative-metabolite-comparison-across-processing-methods Use when a metabolomics feature table has matched patient/subject metadata and you want to quantify how LMM-based covariate adjustment changes which metabolites pass a VIP > 1 threshold relative to unprocessed data. skills.summary: Compare discriminative metabolites (VIP > 1) selected by PLS-DA on metabolomics data before (M0) versus after linear mixed-effects model (LMM) processing, quantifying how VIP scores shift for key metabolites (e.g. cholesterol, SM (d40:2), acylcarnitines).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack subject/patient metadata (age, BMI, sex, etc.), so a random-intercept LMM per metabolite cannot be formulated The feature table is raw, unpre-processed MS output rather than log2-transformed, normalized peak data ready for multivariate modeling The analysis goal is prediction performance benchmarking (e.g. repeated k-fold cross-validation accuracy) rather than comparing VIP-selected feature sets between processing strategies

skills.summary: Evaluates and compares the discriminative power of reproducibility-detection procedures (e.g., MaRR vs. the copula mixture model of Li et al. 2011) via ROC curves computed on the rank scale, alongside empirical FDR, across a grid of simulation settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real replicate datasets with no ground-truth labels of reproducible genes — ROC-based power comparison requires known truth, which simulation provides but empirical data does not When the analysis goal is raw-scale power or p-value-based power analysis rather than rank-scale discrimination — MaRR operates on maximum rank statistics Mg, so ROC must be on the rank scale When the task is only FDR calibration of a single method with no competing method to rank against — an ROC comparison of two procedures is not needed

skills.search_text: disease-vs-control-cell-comparison Use when single-cell transcriptomics data contain both disease (e.g. AD) and healthy-control cells of the same type (e.g. neurons) and the goal is to identify which predicted metabolites distinguish the two groups. Cells are not matched within the same cell type — comparing mixed heterogeneous cell subpopulations across conditions averages out cell-type-specific metabolic differences The input is bulk transcriptomics with no cell-level disease/control grouping and the goal is cell-type-resolved metabolite comparisons You need context-specific reconstruction of disease/tissue/cell-type metabolic networks — scFEA/FLUXestimator does not yet support this http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Contrast predicted metabolic flux and metabolite concentration (balance) changes between disease cells and healthy-control cells within a single cell type, using scFEA/FLUXestimator outputs to rank metabolites by the magnitude of the disease-vs-control distinction. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkad444

Input is raw unprocessed instrument data rather than a preprocessed [X*Y,P] MSI matrix with a [P,1] peak list The spatial shape of the ion images (X,Y) is unknown, since the 2D ion-image structure is required for representation learning The goal is mass-based isotope annotation from exact m/z deltas alone rather than similarity of spatial ion-image distributions A retrieval procedure that ranks ion images by distance in the low-dimensional (20-D) representation space learned by DeepION, enabling identification of colocalized ions (COL mode) and monoisotope-isotope pairs (ISO mode) in mass spectrometry imaging data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
