skills.summary: Applies electronic-noise removal to MS/MS spectra using the FanzhouKong/spectral_denoising package, as one variant in the Spectraverse preprocessing evaluation. In this study, electronic denoising modestly but consistently decreased the AUROC of cosine-similarity same/different-compound discrimination, so it was excluded from the final preprocessing pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is chemical-noise removal rather than electronic-noise removal — the package targets both noise categories but the AUROC evidence here covers electronic denoising specifically The spectra are already cleaned by matchms filters (e.g., library_cleaning yaml steps, low-resolution or zero/uniform-intensity removal) and the question is redundancy removal, not noise-ion removal

skills.description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum (e.g., from an Orbitrap instrument, loaded from .msp) contains co-occurring 'grass' noise ions with identical intensities that must be stripped before chemical denoising or spectral similarity matching.
skills.name: electronic-noise-ion-removal
skills.search_text: electronic-noise-ion-removal Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum (e.g., from an Orbitrap instrument, loaded from .msp) contains co-occurring 'grass' noise ions with identical intensities that must be stripped before chemical denoising or spectral similarity matching. The noise ions are chemical noise with distinct intensities and chemically meaningful masses — these require formula_denoising against a precursor molecular formula, not the identical-intensity rule The data come from a non-Orbitrap mass analyzer — the paper states the method is optimized for Orbitrap instruments and adapting it requires retuning and validating parameters The spectrum is already clean and only precursor-region trimming is needed — use remove_precursor or remove_zero_ions instead of the noise-identity rule http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Removes electronic ('grass') noise ions from a raw MS/MS spectrum using the Spectral Denoising package's electronic_denoising filter, which deletes any group of more than four ions with near-identical intensities (within ±0.1% relative intensity), a threshold derived empirically from the NIST23 Orbitrap library. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Removes electronic ('grass') noise ions from a raw MS/MS spectrum using the Spectral Denoising package's electronic_denoising filter, which deletes any group of more than four ions with near-identical intensities (within ±0.1% relative intensity), a threshold derived empirically from the NIST23 Orbitrap library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The noise ions are chemical noise with distinct intensities and chemically meaningful masses — these require formula_denoising against a precursor molecular formula, not the identical-intensity rule The data come from a non-Orbitrap mass analyzer — the paper states the method is optimized for Orbitrap instruments and adapting it requires retuning and validating parameters The spectrum is already clean and only precursor-region trimming is needed — use remove_precursor or remove_zero_ions instead of the noise-identity rule

skills.search_text: electronic-resource-inventory-extraction Use when an article claims harmonization/curation from a named number of electronic resources (e.g. 'over 40 electronic resources') and a verifiable, structured source inventory must be extracted from the text. skills.description: Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS metabolomic data with high migration-time variability (e.g. ~105 s drift), where peak alignment or time-warping tools fail on multiplexed runs and mzML files must be annotated against a targeted mass list.
skills.name: electropherogram-peak-annotation
skills.search_text: electropherogram-peak-annotation Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS metabolomic data with high migration-time variability (e.g. ~105 s drift), where peak alignment or time-warping tools fail on multiplexed runs and mzML files must be annotated against a targeted mass list. Input data are untargeted molecular features rather than a targeted mass list — PeakMeister is designed for targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS data Sample matrix is not serum — PeakMeister is not yet validated for urine, saliva, or stool Data are conventional single-injection CE-MS without multiplexed segments — the peak-space-based confirmation step assumes equally spaced peaks from serial injections http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Automated peak annotation and integration of multiplexed MSI-CE-MS extracted ion electropherograms using migration time indices (MTIs) computed from internal-standard landmark peaks, implemented in the open-source R tool PeakMeister. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03513
skills.summary: Automated peak annotation and integration of multiplexed MSI-CE-MS extracted ion electropherograms using migration time indices (MTIs) computed from internal-standard landmark peaks, implemented in the open-source R tool PeakMeister.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are untargeted molecular features rather than a targeted mass list — PeakMeister is designed for targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS data Sample matrix is not serum — PeakMeister is not yet validated for urine, saliva, or stool Data are conventional single-injection CE-MS without multiplexed segments — the peak-space-based confirmation step assumes equally spaced peaks from serial injections

skills.description: Use when ranking candidate structures from HR-MS/MS compound databases (PubChem, ChemSpider) or a user-supplied SDF and isotope signals or prior chemical knowledge imply certain elements must be present, required, or excluded.
skills.name: element-composition-restriction
skills.search_text: element-composition-restriction Use when ranking candidate structures from HR-MS/MS compound databases (PubChem, ChemSpider) or a user-supplied SDF and isotope signals or prior chemical knowledge imply certain elements must be present, required, or excluded. Candidates are already a small, curated suspect list (e.g. STOFF-IDENT entries converted to InChIKeys) where element restriction would discard valid suspects No isotope patterns or prior chemical knowledge are available to justify which elements to include, require, or exclude — an unjustified element filter may remove the true candidate http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 MetFrag2.2's element restriction module restricts candidate structures by their molecular formulas using three modes: filter-included elements, filter-required elements, and filter-excluded elements, applied before fragmentation or as part of candidate ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: MetFrag2.2's element restriction module restricts candidate structures by their molecular formulas using three modes: filter-included elements, filter-required elements, and filter-excluded elements, applied before fragmentation or as part of candidate ranking.

skills.description: Use when you have a formula-annotated aligned peak table (e.g. from IDSL.UFA) and want to detect homologous chemical-class sub-structure patterns such as polymeric/cyclic chains or fixed-carbon halogenated families (PCBs, PBDEs, Cl-PFTrEAs).
skills.name: element-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: element-count-aggregation Use when you have a formula-annotated aligned peak table (e.g. from IDSL.UFA) and want to detect homologous chemical-class sub-structure patterns such as polymeric/cyclic chains or fixed-carbon halogenated families (PCBs, PBDEs, Cl-PFTrEAs). Input is raw MS1 spectra or an unannotated peak list — formulas must already be assigned (e.g. by IDSL.UFA) before element-count grouping. Analysis goal is per-peak formula ranking rather than family-level homolog discovery; use the UFA annotation step instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses each annotated molecular formula into element counts and groups formulas into homologous class clusters using ΔH/ΔC chain-progressions (ratio 2 or 1/2) or fixed-carbon plus fixed Σ(H+Br+Cl+F+I) rules, as implemented in IDSL.UFA's detect_formula_sets function. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00563
skills.summary: Parses each annotated molecular formula into element counts and groups formulas into homologous class clusters using ΔH/ΔC chain-progressions (ratio 2 or 1/2) or fixed-carbon plus fixed Σ(H+Br+Cl+F+I) rules, as implemented in IDSL.UFA's detect_formula_sets function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS1 spectra or an unannotated peak list — formulas must already be assigned (e.g. by IDSL.UFA) before element-count grouping. Analysis goal is per-peak formula ranking rather than family-level homolog discovery; use the UFA annotation step instead.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an element-constrained formula generation space (SIRIUS decomp-style limits) excludes a meaningful share of reference formulae from a spectral dataset such as NPLIB1 before benchmarking de novo formula predictors.
skills.name: element-count-feasibility-verification
skills.search_text: element-count-feasibility-verification Use when evaluating whether an element-constrained formula generation space (SIRIUS decomp-style limits) excludes a meaningful share of reference formulae from a spectral dataset such as NPLIB1 before benchmarking de novo formula predictors. When formula candidates are generated from a database search (NIST, GNPS, HMDB, PubChem) rather than by element-constrained mass decomposition — database entries are not bounded by SIRIUS decomp element caps When the analysis needs isotope-pattern or MS/MS scoring of candidate formulae, not just countability of the candidate space When formulae contain elements outside the SIRIUS decomp search space (e.g. metals) where the halogen/S/P caps are not the binding constraint http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses reference molecular formulae into per-element counts and tests them against a candidate-generation constraint set (e.g. the SIRIUS 'SIRIUS decomp' element limits of max 5 S, max 3 P, and at most one of each halogen F/Cl/Br/I) to quantify what fraction of formulae a mass-decomposition pipeline can actually recover. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Parses reference molecular formulae into per-element counts and tests them against a candidate-generation constraint set (e.g. the SIRIUS 'SIRIUS decomp' element limits of max 5 S, max 3 P, and at most one of each halogen F/Cl/Br/I) to quantify what fraction of formulae a mass-decomposition pipeline can actually recover.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When formula candidates are generated from a database search (NIST, GNPS, HMDB, PubChem) rather than by element-constrained mass decomposition — database entries are not bounded by SIRIUS decomp element caps When the analysis needs isotope-pattern or MS/MS scoring of candidate formulae, not just countability of the candidate space When formulae contain elements outside the SIRIUS decomp search space (e.g. metals) where the halogen/S/P caps are not the binding constraint

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed ICP-MS ionome matrix (e.g. S. cerevisiae mutants profiled across ions like Ca44, K39, Mg25, P31, Zn66 in ppm) must be examined for element-element correlations and relevance networks.
skills.name: element-element-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: element-element-correlation-analysis Use when a pre-processed ICP-MS ionome matrix (e.g. S. cerevisiae mutants profiled across ions like Ca44, K39, Mg25, P31, Zn66 in ppm) must be examined for element-element correlations and relevance networks. Input is raw ICP-MS spectral output rather than tabulated ion concentration values in ppm — IonFlow operates on concentration data frames, not instrument spectra The dataset has no batch structure or replicate measurements, so median batch correction and control-strain-based standardisation cannot be meaningfully applied The goal is element quantification or assay curation rather than studying inter-element relationships and network structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute element-element correlations and extract relevance networks from ICP-MS ionome concentration data using IonFlow's R-based Galaxy pipeline, to quantify physiological relationships between elements (e.g. the high Mg-P correlation) across mutant profiles. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01841-z
skills.summary: Compute element-element correlations and extract relevance networks from ICP-MS ionome concentration data using IonFlow's R-based Galaxy pipeline, to quantify physiological relationships between elements (e.g. the high Mg-P correlation) across mutant profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ICP-MS spectral output rather than tabulated ion concentration values in ppm — IonFlow operates on concentration data frames, not instrument spectra The dataset has no batch structure or replicate measurements, so median batch correction and control-strain-based standardisation cannot be meaningfully applied The goal is element quantification or assay curation rather than studying inter-element relationships and network structure

skills.description: Use when MS/MS peak lists fail to yield the correct structure from a composition-restricted candidate database, e.g. isotope ratios indicate Cl and the correct halogenated molecule is absent from candidate sets.
skills.name: elemental-composition-database-filtering
skills.search_text: elemental-composition-database-filtering Use when MS/MS peak lists fail to yield the correct structure from a composition-restricted candidate database, e.g. isotope ratios indicate Cl and the correct halogenated molecule is absent from candidate sets. The elemental composition is already known and provided — in that case candidates were retrieved directly from the online PubChem service in SDF format rather than by composition-filtered database search. The default C, H, N, O, P, S composition filter already yields the correct candidate — enlarging the database with halogens only increases the candidate pool and subsequent refscore filtering burden. The challenge requires a narrower mass tolerance (e.g. 4 ppm for challenges 4, 5, and 6) — this skill uses the default 10 ppm / 0.002 Da retrieval window. http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Extends a local MAGMa compound database built from a PubChem snapshot (2 December 2013) by relaxing the elemental-composition filter to include halogen atoms, so that candidate molecules containing Cl or F can be retrieved by accurate-mass search for challenges where the C,H,N,O,P,S-only database missed the correct structure. metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033
skills.summary: Extends a local MAGMa compound database built from a PubChem snapshot (2 December 2013) by relaxing the elemental-composition filter to include halogen atoms, so that candidate molecules containing Cl or F can be retrieved by accurate-mass search for challenges where the C,H,N,O,P,S-only database missed the correct structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The elemental composition is already known and provided — in that case candidates were retrieved directly from the online PubChem service in SDF format rather than by composition-filtered database search. The default C, H, N, O, P, S composition filter already yields the correct candidate — enlarging the database with halogens only increases the candidate pool and subsequent refscore filtering burden. The challenge requires a narrower mass tolerance (e.g. 4 ppm for challenges 4, 5, and 6) — this skill uses the default 10 ppm / 0.002 Da retrieval window.

skills.description: Use when constructing metabolite graphs from chemical structures (e.g., a PubChem-derived SDF) as the first stage of the DEREPLICATOR+ fragmentation-graph pipeline before enumerating bond cleavages for spectral dereplication.
skills.name: elemental-composition-node-labeling
skills.search_text: elemental-composition-node-labeling Use when constructing metabolite graphs from chemical structures (e.g., a PubChem-derived SDF) as the first stage of the DEREPLICATOR+ fragmentation-graph pipeline before enumerating bond cleavages for spectral dereplication. Input is already an experimental mass spectrum or peak list — this skill operates on chemical structures, not spectra (spectra are handled later by node annotation and MSM scoring) The goal is spectral preprocessing rather than structure-based graph construction — for spectra, DEREPLICATOR+ instead retains six top intensity peaks per 50 Da window Labels the nodes of a DEREPLICATOR+ metabolite graph: every metabolite bond (C–N, C–O, C–C) is disconnected and each resulting connected component becomes a node labeled by its elemental composition, providing the substrate from which the fragmentation graph is built. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-018-06082-8
skills.summary: Labels the nodes of a DEREPLICATOR+ metabolite graph: every metabolite bond (C–N, C–O, C–C) is disconnected and each resulting connected component becomes a node labeled by its elemental composition, providing the substrate from which the fragmentation graph is built.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an experimental mass spectrum or peak list — this skill operates on chemical structures, not spectra (spectra are handled later by node annotation and MSM scoring) The goal is spectral preprocessing rather than structure-based graph construction — for spectra, DEREPLICATOR+ instead retains six top intensity peaks per 50 Da window

skills.description: Use when you have raw molecular formula strings from a reference dataset (e.g. NPLIB1/canopus_train) and must determine which formulae survive element-count constraints imposed by candidate-generation tools like SIRIUS decomp or MIST-CF.
skills.name: elemental-composition-parsing
skills.search_text: elemental-composition-parsing Use when you have raw molecular formula strings from a reference dataset (e.g. NPLIB1/canopus_train) and must determine which formulae survive element-count constraints imposed by candidate-generation tools like SIRIUS decomp or MIST-CF. Formulae are already provided as parsed element-count tables rather than formula strings, making re-parsing redundant The goal is scoring candidate formulae against an MS/MS spectrum (that is MIST-CF or SIRIUS decomp scoring, not coverage analysis of a reference set) The target dataset is not a natural-products formulae set comparable to NPLIB1, so the 96% recoverability figure would not transfer Parses molecular formula strings (e.g. NPLIB1/GNPS reference formulae) into per-element counts and screens them against the SIRIUS 'SIRIUS decomp' mass-decomposition element constraints (max 5 S, max 3 P, at most one of F/Cl/Br/I) to quantify how many reference formulae remain recoverable under formula-candidate generation limits (~96% of NPLIB1). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Parses molecular formula strings (e.g. NPLIB1/GNPS reference formulae) into per-element counts and screens them against the SIRIUS 'SIRIUS decomp' mass-decomposition element constraints (max 5 S, max 3 P, at most one of F/Cl/Br/I) to quantify how many reference formulae remain recoverable under formula-candidate generation limits (~96% of NPLIB1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Formulae are already provided as parsed element-count tables rather than formula strings, making re-parsing redundant The goal is scoring candidate formulae against an MS/MS spectrum (that is MIST-CF or SIRIUS decomp scoring, not coverage analysis of a reference set) The target dataset is not a natural-products formulae set comparable to NPLIB1, so the 96% recoverability figure would not transfer

skills.description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM/MDV data for natural abundance and tracer impurity at low resolution, or when building the NRE baseline against which resolution-dependent corrections (MDT/ULS) are compared.
skills.name: elemental-formula-tracer-atom-enumeration
skills.search_text: elemental-formula-tracer-atom-enumeration Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM/MDV data for natural abundance and tracer impurity at low resolution, or when building the NRE baseline against which resolution-dependent corrections (MDT/ULS) are compared. High-resolving-power MS (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000 or 280,000 nominal resolution) can resolve isotopologs of the same nominal mass, so including all isotopologs in a purely combinatorial matrix is 'no longer justified' — use a resolution-dependent correction (MDT/ULS) instead Compounds whose formula does not contain the selected tracer element (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N-labeled data) — the ElemCor algorithm reports an error http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Constructs the theoretical (non-resolution-effect, NRE) isotope correction matrix by combinatorial convolution of natural-abundance isotope distributions (C1), tracer-element natural abundance (C2), and tracer isotopic impurity (C3), as used by IsoCor and as the NRE baseline inside ElemCor. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Constructs the theoretical (non-resolution-effect, NRE) isotope correction matrix by combinatorial convolution of natural-abundance isotope distributions (C1), tracer-element natural abundance (C2), and tracer isotopic impurity (C3), as used by IsoCor and as the NRE baseline inside ElemCor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: High-resolving-power MS (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000 or 280,000 nominal resolution) can resolve isotopologs of the same nominal mass, so including all isotopologs in a purely combinatorial matrix is 'no longer justified' — use a resolution-dependent correction (MDT/ULS) instead Compounds whose formula does not contain the selected tracer element (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N-labeled data) — the ElemCor algorithm reports an error

skills.description: Use when a 2D LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a calibrated 56Fe, 55Mn, 63Cu, or 66Zn NumPy array) must be split into tissue and background before quantification or mask-based feature selection.
skills.name: elemental-image-background-extraction
skills.search_text: elemental-image-background-extraction Use when a 2D LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a calibrated 56Fe, 55Mn, 63Cu, or 66Zn NumPy array) must be split into tissue and background before quantification or mask-based feature selection. Input is already a labeled mask or a three-level RGB overlay — thresholding would re-segment already-classified pixels rather than extract background. Peak detection or drift correction is the actual goal; Pew2 separates segmentation from its spike-removal and polynomial drift tools. The sample has no distinct tissue/background contrast (e.g. homogeneous gelatin standard), where Otsu between-class variance has no meaningful separation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Automatically segments an LA-ICP-MS elemental image into tissue/ROI and background by applying image thresholding — notably Otsu's method, mean thresholding, or multi-level k-means — as implemented in Pew2's selection dialog. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Automatically segments an LA-ICP-MS elemental image into tissue/ROI and background by applying image thresholding — notably Otsu's method, mean thresholding, or multi-level k-means — as implemented in Pew2's selection dialog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a labeled mask or a three-level RGB overlay — thresholding would re-segment already-classified pixels rather than extract background. Peak detection or drift correction is the actual goal; Pew2 separates segmentation from its spike-removal and polynomial drift tools. The sample has no distinct tissue/background contrast (e.g. homogeneous gelatin standard), where Otsu between-class variance has no meaningful separation.

skills.description: Use when two or more elemental image channels of identical pixel dimensions from a LA-ICP-MS acquisition need quantitative colocalisation statistics, or when a region-of-interest (lasso/rectangle) selection must restrict the coefficient inputs.
skills.name: elemental-image-channel-registration-for-spatial-correlation
skills.search_text: elemental-image-channel-registration-for-spatial-correlation Use when two or more elemental image channels of identical pixel dimensions from a LA-ICP-MS acquisition need quantitative colocalisation statistics, or when a region-of-interest (lasso/rectangle) selection must restrict the coefficient inputs. The input consists of single-channel images without a second channel to correlate against — colocalisation statistics require at least two co-registered elemental maps. The two channels have different pixel dimensions or spatial registration; Pew2 requires both channels to share identical pixel dimensions before computing coefficients. The data are unprocessed raw vendor files that have not yet been imported, calibrated (gelatin standards), or drift/spike-corrected — performing colocalisation on uncorrected images will misrepresent the spatial relationship. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3344 Quantify the spatial relationship between two LA-ICP-MS elemental image channels (e.g. 55Mn and 66Zn) by computing Li's ICQ, Pearson's R with a shuffle-based probability ρ, and Manders overlap coefficients using the Costes thresholding method. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Quantify the spatial relationship between two LA-ICP-MS elemental image channels (e.g. 55Mn and 66Zn) by computing Li's ICQ, Pearson's R with a shuffle-based probability ρ, and Manders overlap coefficients using the Costes thresholding method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input consists of single-channel images without a second channel to correlate against — colocalisation statistics require at least two co-registered elemental maps. The two channels have different pixel dimensions or spatial registration; Pew2 requires both channels to share identical pixel dimensions before computing coefficients. The data are unprocessed raw vendor files that have not yet been imported, calibrated (gelatin standards), or drift/spike-corrected — performing colocalisation on uncorrected images will misrepresent the spatial relationship.

skills.description: Use when preparing elemental images from LA-ICP-MS data for publication or review and you need to show or justify why the default rainbow (Jet) colormap risks misinterpretation versus a perceptually uniform alternative.
skills.name: elemental-image-colormap-comparison
skills.search_text: elemental-image-colormap-comparison Use when preparing elemental images from LA-ICP-MS data for publication or review and you need to show or justify why the default rainbow (Jet) colormap risks misinterpretation versus a perceptually uniform alternative. The image already uses a perceptually uniform colormap and no colormap justification is needed The goal is quantitative pixel calibration or drift/spike correction rather than visualization choice The input is line/spot-wise raw instrument data that has not yet been imported and calibrated into a 2D image Renders the same LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a calibrated 66Zn tissue image) side by side under a default rainbow colormap (Jet) and a perceptually uniform colormap (Viridis) to demonstrate how nonuniform perceptual contrast in rainbow colormaps can introduce interpretation artifacts that uniform colormaps avoid. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138

skills.description: Use when analyzing preprocessed MSI matrices (e.g. rat brain [X*Y,P] data, 198 x 422 pixels) to retrieve nearest-neighbor ions for a query ion image, especially for low-SNR isotope discovery where PCC/R2 fail.
skills.name: embedding-nearest-neighbor-ranking
skills.search_text: embedding-nearest-neighbor-ranking Use when analyzing preprocessed MSI matrices (e.g. rat brain [X*Y,P] data, 198 x 422 pixels) to retrieve nearest-neighbor ions for a query ion image, especially for low-SNR isotope discovery where PCC/R2 fail. The MSI data is not preprocessed into a matrix/peak-list pair — the pipeline expects [X*Y,P] matrices and [P,1] peak lists, not raw imzML or vendor files. The goal is standard quantitative MSI imaging rather than ion colocalization or isotope identification — this skill produces ranked neighbor lists, not abundance maps. Pairwise co-localization statistics alone suffice (high-SNR ions with strong correlation) — in that case SIM-based methods like PCC or R2 used in METASPACE and rMSI are adequate, and the additional training cost of DeepION is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates dense 20-dimensional DeepION embeddings of ion images from mass spectrometry imaging data via self-supervised contrastive learning (SimSiam/Resnet18), then ranks candidate ions by embedding distance to a query ion for colocalized or isotope identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Generates dense 20-dimensional DeepION embeddings of ion images from mass spectrometry imaging data via self-supervised contrastive learning (SimSiam/Resnet18), then ranks candidate ions by embedding distance to a query ion for colocalized or isotope identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MSI data is not preprocessed into a matrix/peak-list pair — the pipeline expects [X*Y,P] matrices and [P,1] peak lists, not raw imzML or vendor files. The goal is standard quantitative MSI imaging rather than ion colocalization or isotope identification — this skill produces ranked neighbor lists, not abundance maps. Pairwise co-localization statistics alone suffice (high-SNR ions with strong correlation) — in that case SIM-based methods like PCC or R2 used in METASPACE and rMSI are adequate, and the additional training cost of DeepION is unnecessary.

skills.search_text: embedding-quality-metric-computation Use when comparing MS/MS-to-embedding prediction quality across spectral variants (individual collision energy, merged, merged+neutral loss) on a test split, or when validating that a trained ChemEmbed CNN reproduces reported embedding-quality numbers. When the goal is annotation ranking against the 520,083-compound database rather than embedding quality on known test compounds — use cosine-similarity candidate matching instead. When spectra are unmatched or the compound lies outside the 520,083-compound reference database, since no reference embedding exists to compare against. When comparing embeddings across different adduct modes (positive vs negative), because distances reflect polarity mismatch rather than spectral-representation quality. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Euclidean distance and cosine similarity between CNN-predicted 300-dimensional Mol2vec embeddings and reference embeddings from the 520,083-compound ChemEmbed database, to quantify how well spectra (individual, merged, or merged+neutral-loss) map to molecular structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Computes Euclidean distance and cosine similarity between CNN-predicted 300-dimensional Mol2vec embeddings and reference embeddings from the 520,083-compound ChemEmbed database, to quantify how well spectra (individual, merged, or merged+neutral-loss) map to molecular structure.

When spectra are unmatched or the compound lies outside the 520,083-compound reference database, since no reference embedding exists to compare against. skills.search_text: embedding-similarity-retrieval-evaluation Use when you have learned dense representations of ion images from an MSI dataset and need to quantify embedding quality via colocalized-ion retrieval or leave-one-out linear classification. Input is raw, unrepresented ion intensity data rather than learned embedding vectors — train an encoder (e.g., DeepION) first The goal is isotope ion discovery from the same molecule (DeepION ISO mode) rather than colocalization across different molecules (COL mode) You lack ground-truth colocalization annotations, making retrieval accuracy and leave-one-out classification unverifiable http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Evaluates the quality of learned ion-image embeddings from MSI data by reducing encoder outputs to 20-dimensional UMAP vectors, min–max scaling features to [0,1], and performing distance-based retrieval of the top-5 colocalized ions per ion — the protocol DeepION uses to benchmark embedding spaces against SimSiam. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Evaluates the quality of learned ion-image embeddings from MSI data by reducing encoder outputs to 20-dimensional UMAP vectors, min–max scaling features to [0,1], and performing distance-based retrieval of the top-5 colocalized ions per ion — the protocol DeepION uses to benchmark embedding spaces against SimSiam.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unrepresented ion intensity data rather than learned embedding vectors — train an encoder (e.g., DeepION) first The goal is isotope ion discovery from the same molecule (DeepION ISO mode) rather than colocalization across different molecules (COL mode) You lack ground-truth colocalization annotations, making retrieval accuracy and leave-one-out classification unverifiable

skills.name: empirical-bayes-batch-effect-removal
skills.search_text: empirical-bayes-batch-effect-removal Use when a feature table TSV (e.g. an imputed pcpfm table) shows batch-driven sub-clustering in QAQC PCA plots and sample metadata contains a batch designation field to correct against. The input feature table still contains missing values — the finding notes the pyComBat wrapper is sensitive to missing features, so blank masking / rare-feature removal / missing value imputation must come first. Only one batch exists or no batch metadata field was recorded, leaving nothing for empirical-Bayes correction to model. The goal is intensity normalization rather than between-batch adjustment — pcpfm provides normalization as a separate correction operation. Remove systematic batch effects from LC-MS metabolomics feature intensities by wrapping pyComBat's empirical-Bayes correction inside the pcpfm pipeline, using a user-specified metadata field to define batches. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912

The goal is intensity normalization rather than between-batch adjustment — pcpfm provides normalization as a separate correction operation.

skills.description: Use when a log2-normalized metabolomics dataset in CSV format (samples in rows, features in columns, batch levels in the first column) shows across-batch signal drift and you need to correct it and compare empirical-Bayes correction models.
skills.name: empirical-bayes-location-scale-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-bayes-location-scale-estimation Use when a log2-normalized metabolomics dataset in CSV format (samples in rows, features in columns, batch levels in the first column) shows across-batch signal drift and you need to correct it and compare empirical-Bayes correction models. The input matrix has no batch annotation in the first column — L/S estimation requires batch labels and cannot be run on unbatched data The dataset contains more than 2000 features — dbnorm's correction/scoring functions (Visodbnorm, dbnormSCORE) are suggested only for fewer than 2000 variables for computational speed; use the decomposed dbnormBer/dbnormBagging/dbnormPcom/dbnormNPcom functions instead The data have not been normalized and log2-scaled — running the models on raw unscaled intensities violates the documented input requirement and can let high-abundance features dominate technical heterogeneity estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Empirical Bayes location/scale (L/S) batch-effect correction for metabolomics matrices via the dbnorm R package, which runs ComBat in parametric and nonparametric settings (sva) alongside the two-stage linear-regression ber and bagging-ber (n=150 bootstrap) models, and scores each model's residual batch dependence with maximum adjusted-R². metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Empirical Bayes location/scale (L/S) batch-effect correction for metabolomics matrices via the dbnorm R package, which runs ComBat in parametric and nonparametric settings (sva) alongside the two-stage linear-regression ber and bagging-ber (n=150 bootstrap) models, and scores each model's residual batch dependence with maximum adjusted-R².
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix has no batch annotation in the first column — L/S estimation requires batch labels and cannot be run on unbatched data The dataset contains more than 2000 features — dbnorm's correction/scoring functions (Visodbnorm, dbnormSCORE) are suggested only for fewer than 2000 variables for computational speed; use the decomposed dbnormBer/dbnormBagging/dbnormPcom/dbnormNPcom functions instead The data have not been normalized and log2-scaled — running the models on raw unscaled intensities violates the documented input requirement and can let high-abundance features dominate technical heterogeneity estimates

skills.description: Use when standardizing exercise (or other condition-induced) log2 fold-changes against within-population expression variability at the gene-by-tissue level, e.g. asking how many genes' 8-week endurance-training effect sizes exceed 2 SD of GTEx expression variance.
skills.name: empirical-bayes-posterior-variance-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-bayes-posterior-variance-estimation Use when standardizing exercise (or other condition-induced) log2 fold-changes against within-population expression variability at the gene-by-tissue level, e.g. asking how many genes' 8-week endurance-training effect sizes exceed 2 SD of GTEx expression variance. Expression data are raw counts or already inverse-normal transformed — the pipeline specifically requires the pseudolog log2(x + 1) scale for variance estimation The goal is TWAS/PrediXcan disease association rather than effect-size standardization against human expression variability (use S-PrediXcan/MESC workflows instead) Too few samples or genes per tissue to support fitting an inverse-gamma distribution to variances separately for male- and female-coded individuals http://edamontology.org/topic_3489 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Empirical-Bayes estimation of within-population phenotypic standard deviation (SDpheno) of GTEx log2 gene expression per gene-by-tissue pair: an inverse-gamma conjugate prior is fit to pooled sample variances, and exercise differential expression is then standardized in SDpheno units. This converts raw log2FC of exercise training-induced DE into effect sizes comparable to human expression variability. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Empirical-Bayes estimation of within-population phenotypic standard deviation (SDpheno) of GTEx log2 gene expression per gene-by-tissue pair: an inverse-gamma conjugate prior is fit to pooled sample variances, and exercise differential expression is then standardized in SDpheno units. This converts raw log2FC of exercise training-induced DE into effect sizes comparable to human expression variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are raw counts or already inverse-normal transformed — the pipeline specifically requires the pseudolog log2(x + 1) scale for variance estimation The goal is TWAS/PrediXcan disease association rather than effect-size standardization against human expression variability (use S-PrediXcan/MESC workflows instead) Too few samples or genes per tissue to support fitting an inverse-gamma distribution to variances separately for male- and female-coded individuals

skills.description: Use when you must call reproducible genes from two ranked high-throughput replicate lists with error control at a nominal FDR level (e.g. alpha=0.05) and no parametric assumptions on dependence or signal distribution.
skills.name: empirical-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-fdr-estimation Use when you must call reproducible genes from two ranked high-throughput replicate lists with error control at a nominal FDR level (e.g. alpha=0.05) and no parametric assumptions on dependence or signal distribution. Input data are raw test statistics not yet converted to per-experiment ranks; the MaRR procedure operates on the rank scale via the maximum rank statistic Mg. Signals are weak and infrequent (muA=1, pi1=0.1) or there is a large weakly correlated reproducible group (muA in {1,2}, rho=0.4, pi1=0.8): MaRR was anti-conservative or systematically underestimated pi1 there, so the copula mixture model is favored instead. The goal is discriminative-power comparison under model-based parametric assumptions where fitting the copula mixture model of Li et al. Data are already corrected MDVs or enrichments — RMSE against theoretical values would conflate upstream errors; only raw/uncorrected FAM should feed this benchmark No theoretical or known true enrichment exists for the samples (e.g. unlabeled or fully labeled extremes absent) — RMSE against truth cannot be computed and this skill is not applicable The tracer element is not present in the compound's formula (ElemCor reports an error, e.g. selecting C or S as tracer for 15N data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Benchmark isotope-correction methods (ElemCor MDT, ElemCor ULS, original ULS, NRE/IsoCor-style, and no correction) by computing RMSE of corrected fractional-abundance enrichment against theoretical enrichment, then tabulating compound-tracer-method RMSE values (e.g. for CoA metabolites under 13C/15N/34S tracers at resolution 280,000). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Benchmark isotope-correction methods (ElemCor MDT, ElemCor ULS, original ULS, NRE/IsoCor-style, and no correction) by computing RMSE of corrected fractional-abundance enrichment against theoretical enrichment, then tabulating compound-tracer-method RMSE values (e.g. for CoA metabolites under 13C/15N/34S tracers at resolution 280,000).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already corrected MDVs or enrichments — RMSE against theoretical values would conflate upstream errors; only raw/uncorrected FAM should feed this benchmark No theoretical or known true enrichment exists for the samples (e.g. unlabeled or fully labeled extremes absent) — RMSE against truth cannot be computed and this skill is not applicable The tracer element is not present in the compound's formula (ElemCor reports an error, e.g. selecting C or S as tracer for 15N data)

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking GSEA results on the Mootha type 2 diabetes (17 DM2 / 17 NGT / 9 IGT) or airway epithelia smoker datasets, or when validating a pathway-analysis method against published ES values and permutation p-values.
skills.name: enrichment-score-computation
skills.search_text: enrichment-score-computation Use when reproducing or benchmarking GSEA results on the Mootha type 2 diabetes (17 DM2 / 17 NGT / 9 IGT) or airway epithelia smoker datasets, or when validating a pathway-analysis method against published ES values and permutation p-values. You want the paper's own SVD-based pathway activity levels compared by mean t-statistic — that is the PLAGE method, not the GSEA ES computation being reproduced for comparison You lack predefined pathway gene-sets (KEGG/Biocarta); the ES is defined only relative to a fixed gene-set collection You need per-sample pathway activity scores rather than a per-comparison gene-set statistic http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) scoring scheme referenced by the PLAGE paper: rank genes by signal-to-noise ratio, compute an enrichment score (ES) for each KEGG/Biocarta pathway from its members' ranks, and estimate p-values by permuting sample labels and comparing against the maximum permuted ES. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Reproduces the gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) scoring scheme referenced by the PLAGE paper: rank genes by signal-to-noise ratio, compute an enrichment score (ES) for each KEGG/Biocarta pathway from its members' ranks, and estimate p-values by permuting sample labels and comparing against the maximum permuted ES.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want the paper's own SVD-based pathway activity levels compared by mean t-statistic — that is the PLAGE method, not the GSEA ES computation being reproduced for comparison You lack predefined pathway gene-sets (KEGG/Biocarta); the ES is defined only relative to a fixed gene-set collection You need per-sample pathway activity scores rather than a per-comparison gene-set statistic

skills.description: Use when a trained ensemble of deep-learning classifiers on raw LC-MS data (mzML or .npy arrays over a retention-time × m/z grid) must be interrogated to reveal which metabolite signals — including unannotated ones — drive class predictions.
skills.name: ensemble-deep-learning-interpretability
skills.search_text: ensemble-deep-learning-interpretability Use when a trained ensemble of deep-learning classifiers on raw LC-MS data (mzML or .npy arrays over a retention-time × m/z grid) must be interrogated to reveal which metabolite signals — including unannotated ones — drive class predictions. Input is already a peak-picked, aligned, and annotated feature table — this skill operates end-to-end on raw LC-MS signals without conventional peak extraction and identification steps Only point predictions are needed (run_predict with plot_auc/plot_cm) and no model-explanation or biomarker-region localization is required The model is a single network rather than the trained ensemble; the 'ensemble' heatmap mode requires the multi-run job directory output http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates per-class feature-contribution heatmaps from an ensemble of DenseNet121 models trained on raw LC-MS metabolomic arrays using the RISE random-masking perturbation procedure, quantifying which retention-time × m/z regions drive disease classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-51433-3
skills.summary: Generates per-class feature-contribution heatmaps from an ensemble of DenseNet121 models trained on raw LC-MS metabolomic arrays using the RISE random-masking perturbation procedure, quantifying which retention-time × m/z regions drive disease classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-picked, aligned, and annotated feature table — this skill operates end-to-end on raw LC-MS signals without conventional peak extraction and identification steps Only point predictions are needed (run_predict with plot_auc/plot_cm) and no model-explanation or biomarker-region localization is required The model is a single network rather than the trained ensemble; the 'ensemble' heatmap mode requires the multi-run job directory output

skills.description: Use when you have two pretrained spectral prediction baselines (MLP-PD and GNN-PD), a ranking-task training setup, and a candidate-set evaluation (average rank / Rank@K) on spectra-to-candidate annotation.
skills.name: ensemble-model-fusion-evaluation
skills.search_text: ensemble-model-fusion-evaluation Use when you have two pretrained spectral prediction baselines (MLP-PD and GNN-PD), a ranking-task training setup, and a candidate-set evaluation (average rank / Rank@K) on spectra-to-candidate annotation. Input data is EI/GC-MS spectra rather than the ESI/LC-MS-style spectra this pipeline generalizes; the baselines were built as an implementation of the NEIMS model with generalized ESI/LC-MS but not EI/GC-MS data. You need only a single predictor (MLP or GNN) rather than a fused ensemble; the skill's value is specifically the weighted-average MLP+GNN combination. The training dataset or candidate-set composition differs substantially from NPLIB1/NIST-20-style annotation tasks where candidate similarity to the target molecule matters; annotation performance is dependent on the training dataset, the number of molecules in the candidate set, and candidate similarity to the target molecule. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fuses independently trained MLP and GNN spectral predictors into an Ensembled Spectral Prediction (ESP) model trained on ranking tasks, then evaluates average rank and Rank@K on candidate sets. ESP improves average rank by 23.7% (MLP) and 37.2% (GNN) over the baselines on the full NIST candidate set. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae490
skills.summary: Fuses independently trained MLP and GNN spectral predictors into an Ensembled Spectral Prediction (ESP) model trained on ranking tasks, then evaluates average rank and Rank@K on candidate sets. ESP improves average rank by 23.7% (MLP) and 37.2% (GNN) over the baselines on the full NIST candidate set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is EI/GC-MS spectra rather than the ESI/LC-MS-style spectra this pipeline generalizes; the baselines were built as an implementation of the NEIMS model with generalized ESI/LC-MS but not EI/GC-MS data. You need only a single predictor (MLP or GNN) rather than a fused ensemble; the skill's value is specifically the weighted-average MLP+GNN combination. The training dataset or candidate-set composition differs substantially from NPLIB1/NIST-20-style annotation tasks where candidate similarity to the target molecule matters; annotation performance is dependent on the training dataset, the number of molecules in the candidate set, and candidate similarity to the target molecule.

skills.description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows with unique identifiers) is paired with a design file assigning samples to class labels (e.g. treatment group) and the goal is supervised classification plus feature ranking.
skills.name: ensemble-model-training-and-prediction
skills.search_text: ensemble-model-training-and-prediction Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows with unique identifiers) is paired with a design file assigning samples to class labels (e.g. treatment group) and the goal is supervised classification plus feature ranking. The task is unsupervised or exploratory (e.g. visualization via PCA or hierarchical cluster heatmap) rather than supervised classification against design-file class labels Only basic statistical testing is needed, for which SECIMTools provides PLS-DA, ANOVA, t-test, or Kruskal-Wallis instead The input is raw instrument data requiring preprocessing (peak picking, imputation, blank feature filtering) rather than a feature-level table http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Train a random forest ensemble to classify metabolomics samples by a design-file class label, then use the forest to predict class membership (with per-tree vote shares) and rank features by variable importance, as implemented in SECIMTools' random forest tool. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Train a random forest ensemble to classify metabolomics samples by a design-file class label, then use the forest to predict class membership (with per-tree vote shares) and rank features by variable importance, as implemented in SECIMTools' random forest tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is unsupervised or exploratory (e.g. visualization via PCA or hierarchical cluster heatmap) rather than supervised classification against design-file class labels Only basic statistical testing is needed, for which SECIMTools provides PLS-DA, ANOVA, t-test, or Kruskal-Wallis instead The input is raw instrument data requiring preprocessing (peak picking, imputation, blank feature filtering) rather than a feature-level table

skills.description: Decision support for scoring a per-atom modification-site likelihood array Ω from ModiFinder against a known true modification site, when a single metric balancing proximity and ambiguity of the prediction is needed.
skills.name: entropy-based-peak-clarity-scoring
skills.search_text: entropy-based-peak-clarity-scoring Decision support for scoring a per-atom modification-site likelihood array Ω from ModiFinder against a known true modification site, when a single metric balancing proximity and ambiguity of the prediction is needed. When the input is raw MS/MS peak data before ModiFinder scoring — the metric requires the already-computed per-atom likelihood array Ω, not spectra When no known true modification site γ is available (this is a supervised evaluation metric for benchmarking, not for discovery on unlabeled analogs) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes ModiFinder's Average-distance evaluation score, a likelihood-weighted exponential decay metric over per-atom modification-site scores that balances proximity cover (high-scoring atoms near the true site) against ambiguity cover (informativeness/entropy of the likelihood array Ω). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Computes ModiFinder's Average-distance evaluation score, a likelihood-weighted exponential decay metric over per-atom modification-site scores that balances proximity cover (high-scoring atoms near the true site) against ambiguity cover (informativeness/entropy of the likelihood array Ω).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw MS/MS peak data before ModiFinder scoring — the metric requires the already-computed per-atom likelihood array Ω, not spectra When no known true modification site γ is available (this is a supervised evaluation metric for benchmarking, not for discovery on unlabeled analogs)

skills.description: Use when a feature table derived from CWT peak detection contains irregular, likely noise peaks, and you need a shape-based, parameter-light criterion to discard false positives before chemometric evaluation.
skills.name: entropy-based-peak-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: entropy-based-peak-quality-filtering Use when a feature table derived from CWT peak detection contains irregular, likely noise peaks, and you need a shape-based, parameter-light criterion to discard false positives before chemometric evaluation. The input is already a curated, filtered feature table — re-applying a median-entropy cutoff would discard genuine low-abundance features from the lower half of the entropy distribution The task is connecting features across methods by MS/MS spectral networking, which AriumMS does not implement (listed as future development), rather than removing noise peaks Peak shapes are expected to be highly non-Gaussian (e.g. broad or split CE peaks), where the Gaussian-shaped low-entropy assumption underlying the filter may misclassify real features as noise http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A false-positive peak filter from the AriumMS toolbox that scores each CWT-detected peak by information entropy (H = -p*log2(p) - q*log2(q)) and discards peaks whose entropy exceeds the median entropy of all detected features, treating high-entropy (irregular) peak shapes as noise. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: A false-positive peak filter from the AriumMS toolbox that scores each CWT-detected peak by information entropy (H = -p*log2(p) - q*log2(q)) and discards peaks whose entropy exceeds the median entropy of all detected features, treating high-entropy (irregular) peak shapes as noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated, filtered feature table — re-applying a median-entropy cutoff would discard genuine low-abundance features from the lower half of the entropy distribution The task is connecting features across methods by MS/MS spectral networking, which AriumMS does not implement (listed as future development), rather than removing noise peaks Peak shapes are expected to be highly non-Gaussian (e.g. broad or split CE peaks), where the Gaussian-shaped low-entropy assumption underlying the filter may misclassify real features as noise

skills.description: Use when quantitatively ranking MS/MS spectral matches or measuring denoising benefit — e.g. computing entropy similarity of raw vs. denoised query peaks against reference library spectra for compound annotation.
skills.name: entropy-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: entropy-similarity-scoring Use when quantitatively ranking MS/MS spectral matches or measuring denoising benefit — e.g. computing entropy similarity of raw vs. denoised query peaks against reference library spectra for compound annotation. Spectra with fewer than two fragment ions (spectral entropy <0.5) — insufficient fragmentation makes similarity scoring unreliable Scenarios where isomeric compounds or in-source fragments must be distinguished — entropy similarity alone cannot differentiate them and hard thresholding on similarity is suboptimal for annotation When the precursor ion region should be included — the method explicitly ignores remaining precursor ion intensity in all MS/MS similarity calculations http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Score MS/MS spectral matches using spectral entropy and entropy similarity, computed with the precursor ion region excluded, to compare raw vs. denoised query spectra against reference library entries in the Spectral Denoising / Denoising Search workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Score MS/MS spectral matches using spectral entropy and entropy similarity, computed with the precursor ion region excluded, to compare raw vs. denoised query spectra against reference library entries in the Spectral Denoising / Denoising Search workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra with fewer than two fragment ions (spectral entropy <0.5) — insufficient fragmentation makes similarity scoring unreliable Scenarios where isomeric compounds or in-source fragments must be distinguished — entropy similarity alone cannot differentiate them and hard thresholding on similarity is suboptimal for annotation When the precursor ion region should be included — the method explicitly ignores remaining precursor ion intensity in all MS/MS similarity calculations

skills.description: Use when building a validation/reference peak list for metal-assisted (e.g. Ag-sputtered nanolayer) LDI MSI, where expected Ag-cluster and Ag-adduct masses must be derived from isotope abundances before peak classification.
skills.name: envipat-isotope-fine-structure-computation
skills.search_text: envipat-isotope-fine-structure-computation Use when building a validation/reference peak list for metal-assisted (e.g. Ag-sputtered nanolayer) LDI MSI, where expected Ag-cluster and Ag-adduct masses must be derived from isotope abundances before peak classification. The aim is classifying peaks in datasets acquired with conventional organic MALDI matrices rather than a silver nanolayer — the possible/not-possible peak list is specific to AgLDI The input is already a classified peak matrix or a finished validation list (the computation would be redundant) The LDI-promoting material is an element without a distinctive multi-isotope pattern usable for peak-list construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Compute theoretical monoisotopic masses and isotopic fine-structure patterns with the enviPat R package to build the silver-cluster validation list (possible vs not-possible Ag-related peaks) used by rMSIcleanup to classify matrix-related signals in AgLDI MSI experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00449-0
skills.summary: Compute theoretical monoisotopic masses and isotopic fine-structure patterns with the enviPat R package to build the silver-cluster validation list (possible vs not-possible Ag-related peaks) used by rMSIcleanup to classify matrix-related signals in AgLDI MSI experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The aim is classifying peaks in datasets acquired with conventional organic MALDI matrices rather than a silver nanolayer — the possible/not-possible peak list is specific to AgLDI The input is already a classified peak matrix or a finished validation list (the computation would be redundant) The LDI-promoting material is an element without a distinctive multi-isotope pattern usable for peak-list construction

skills.description: Use when building an LC-HRMS benchmark from target molecules with known formulas and RT boundaries: isotopologue patterns must be predicted from SumForm_c entries before chromatographic ROI extraction from centroided mzML files.
skills.name: envipat-isotopologue-pattern-prediction
skills.search_text: envipat-isotopologue-pattern-prediction Use when building an LC-HRMS benchmark from target molecules with known formulas and RT boundaries: isotopologue patterns must be predicted from SumForm_c entries before chromatographic ROI extraction from centroided mzML files. Input molecules lack a defined neutral molecular composition or a main adduct — enviPat prediction requires SumForm_c and main_adduct per molecule Only profile-mode data is available — mzRAPP requires centroided mzML files, so prediction would feed a benchmark that cannot be extracted The goal is generic isotope fine-structure calculation outside mzRAPP's benchmark workflow with RT boundaries — a standalone enviPat session is simpler http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Predicts theoretical isotopologue patterns for target molecules using the enviPat R package, based on molecular composition and instrument resolution, as the first step of mzRAPP's benchmark generation cascade (get_mz_table). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab231
skills.summary: Predicts theoretical isotopologue patterns for target molecules using the enviPat R package, based on molecular composition and instrument resolution, as the first step of mzRAPP's benchmark generation cascade (get_mz_table).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input molecules lack a defined neutral molecular composition or a main adduct — enviPat prediction requires SumForm_c and main_adduct per molecule Only profile-mode data is available — mzRAPP requires centroided mzML files, so prediction would feed a benchmark that cannot be extracted The goal is generic isotope fine-structure calculation outside mzRAPP's benchmark workflow with RT boundaries — a standalone enviPat session is simpler

skills.description: Use when a pathway-metabolite association table (met_path) for significantly altered metabolites must be extended with gene IDs, EC numbers, and reaction roles, e.g. to infer enzymatic activity of altered metabolites in a species-specific KEGG context.
skills.name: enzyme-annotation-of-metabolites
skills.search_text: enzyme-annotation-of-metabolites Use when a pathway-metabolite association table (met_path) for significantly altered metabolites must be extended with gene IDs, EC numbers, and reaction roles, e.g. to infer enzymatic activity of altered metabolites in a species-specific KEGG context. When the species of interest has no KEGG pathways available — MetENP only includes support for metabolite species with available KEGG pathways Before the upstream met_pathways step has produced the pathway-metabolite association table for significantly altered metabolites When only metabolite-class or pathway enrichment scores are needed without gene/enzyme-level annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotates significantly altered metabolites with their associated KEGG reactions, organism-specific genes, and EC enzyme numbers, then labels each metabolite as a reactant (substrate) or product in its associated reaction using MetENP's enzyme_gene_info and react_substrate functions. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.11.20.391912
skills.summary: Annotates significantly altered metabolites with their associated KEGG reactions, organism-specific genes, and EC enzyme numbers, then labels each metabolite as a reactant (substrate) or product in its associated reaction using MetENP's enzyme_gene_info and react_substrate functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the species of interest has no KEGG pathways available — MetENP only includes support for metabolite species with available KEGG pathways Before the upstream met_pathways step has produced the pathway-metabolite association table for significantly altered metabolites When only metabolite-class or pathway enrichment scores are needed without gene/enzyme-level annotation

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics data frame already carries KEGG compound IDs and you need the enzyme orthologies (KO numbers) and genes an organism of interest, e.g. Pseudomonas spp., has to metabolize a compound class such as organic acids.
skills.name: enzyme-metadata-assignment
skills.search_text: enzyme-metadata-assignment Use when a metabolomics data frame already carries KEGG compound IDs and you need the enzyme orthologies (KO numbers) and genes an organism of interest, e.g. Pseudomonas spp., has to metabolize a compound class such as organic acids. Compounds lack KEGG identifiers — KEGG_gather queries the KEGG API by KEGG compound ID, so unmapped/unknown metabolites cannot be gathered (keep_unknowns = TRUE only retains them without KEGG numbers in hierarchy assignment) The goal is compound class/hierarchy metadata alone — assign_hierarchy with KEGG compound identifiers suffices; the two-pass KEGG_gather orthology/gene retrieval is unnecessary Offline or rate-limited environments — the workflow makes live keggGet calls to the KEGG API via KEGGREST and requires network access http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A workflow from the omu R package that links metabolomics compounds (KEGG compound identifiers) to enzyme functional orthologies (KO numbers) and gene annotations for organisms of interest, retrieved live from the KEGG API via KEGGREST, to support hypothesis generation. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00129-19
skills.summary: A workflow from the omu R package that links metabolomics compounds (KEGG compound identifiers) to enzyme functional orthologies (KO numbers) and gene annotations for organisms of interest, retrieved live from the KEGG API via KEGGREST, to support hypothesis generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds lack KEGG identifiers — KEGG_gather queries the KEGG API by KEGG compound ID, so unmapped/unknown metabolites cannot be gathered (keep_unknowns = TRUE only retains them without KEGG numbers in hierarchy assignment) The goal is compound class/hierarchy metadata alone — assign_hierarchy with KEGG compound identifiers suffices; the two-pass KEGG_gather orthology/gene retrieval is unnecessary Offline or rate-limited environments — the workflow makes live keggGet calls to the KEGG API via KEGGREST and requires network access

skills.description: Use when MGF-converted antibody MS/MS files from multiple enzymatic digests must be searched against antibody reference sequences to generate trusted PSMs (pseudo-ground truth) for evaluating de novo sequencing predictions.
skills.name: enzyme-specific-cleavage-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: enzyme-specific-cleavage-parameter-configuration Use when MGF-converted antibody MS/MS files from multiple enzymatic digests must be searched against antibody reference sequences to generate trusted PSMs (pseudo-ground truth) for evaluating de novo sequencing predictions. The goal is de novo sequencing itself rather than building a database-search-derived reference set — in that case the de novo tools (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) are the subjects of the evaluation, not the ground truth generators. Input spectra are not enzyme-digest peptide MS/MS data and no enzyme-specific cleavage parameters can be defined for them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Configure database search engines (MS-GF+ and X!Tandem, run through SearchGUI) with enzyme-specific cleavage parameters matched to each input antibody digest, then consolidate and filter the combined PSMs at 1% FDR in PeptideShaker to yield a high-confidence pseudo-ground-truth peptide set for benchmarking de novo sequencing tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Configure database search engines (MS-GF+ and X!Tandem, run through SearchGUI) with enzyme-specific cleavage parameters matched to each input antibody digest, then consolidate and filter the combined PSMs at 1% FDR in PeptideShaker to yield a high-confidence pseudo-ground-truth peptide set for benchmarking de novo sequencing tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo sequencing itself rather than building a database-search-derived reference set — in that case the de novo tools (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) are the subjects of the evaluation, not the ground truth generators. Input spectra are not enzyme-digest peptide MS/MS data and no enzyme-specific cleavage parameters can be defined for them.

skills.search_text: enzyme-specificity-model-evaluation Use when classifying whether query molecules react with specific human CYP450 isoforms and you need per-enzyme AUROC evaluation, cross-validation, or benchmarking against ADMET Predictor/SMARTCyp baselines. skills.description: Use when you have curated Known enzyme-substrate pairs (plus Random negatives) and need to score them with GNN-SOM + ReactionDecoder and test whether the score distributions separate.
skills.name: enzyme-substrate-pair-scoring
skills.search_text: enzyme-substrate-pair-scoring Use when you have curated Known enzyme-substrate pairs (plus Random negatives) and need to score them with GNN-SOM + ReactionDecoder and test whether the score distributions separate. You want to discover biosynthetic pathways from paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data (e.g. the tomato falcarindiol case) rather than benchmark an existing scoring mechanism against known pairs. Your input is uncharacterized mass features without deposited Known/Random pair files or a pretrained GNN-SOM model state to restore. You need to predict reactions from mass shifts using RetroRules loose/medium/strict rulesets rather than validate GNN-SOM + ReactionDecoder scores. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Computes MEANtools reaction-likelihood scores (GNN-SOM site-of-metabolism likelihoods combined with ReactionDecoder reaction-center prediction) for enzyme-substrate pairs and validates the scoring mechanism by showing Known experimentally characterized pairs score significantly higher than Random pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Computes MEANtools reaction-likelihood scores (GNN-SOM site-of-metabolism likelihoods combined with ReactionDecoder reaction-center prediction) for enzyme-substrate pairs and validates the scoring mechanism by showing Known experimentally characterized pairs score significantly higher than Random pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to discover biosynthetic pathways from paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data (e.g. the tomato falcarindiol case) rather than benchmark an existing scoring mechanism against known pairs. Your input is uncharacterized mass features without deposited Known/Random pair files or a pretrained GNN-SOM model state to restore. You need to predict reactions from mass shifts using RetroRules loose/medium/strict rulesets rather than validate GNN-SOM + ReactionDecoder scores.

skills.description: Use when a chemical list with CASRNs needs toxicity-relevant properties (log P, BCF, HTS AC50/efficacy) harvested from the EPA Chemistry Dashboard to feed composite prioritization scores such as ToxPi.
skills.name: epa-chemistry-dashboard-property-extraction
skills.search_text: epa-chemistry-dashboard-property-extraction Use when a chemical list with CASRNs needs toxicity-relevant properties (log P, BCF, HTS AC50/efficacy) harvested from the EPA Chemistry Dashboard to feed composite prioritization scores such as ToxPi. It is platform-agnostic, working on data from any instrument including TOF analysers where METASPACE/pySM underperform.

skills.search_text: exact-mass-tolerance-filtering Use when filtering metabolomics annotations against a large structure database (e.g. PubChem) and a narrow mass window plus CCS-based ΔCCS threshold (2.8%) is needed to remove false positives. Training sets only cover common adducts ([M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M+K]+); dimers like [2M+H]+, uncommon adducts, or in-source fragments are not supported Data already consist of a curated annotation table with no need for structure-level filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Narrows candidate metabolite annotations by selecting compounds whose exact masses fall within a user-specified mass-error window (e.g. 10 ppm of the target m/z for a given adduct type) before any collision-cross-section prediction is applied. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c03491
skills.summary: Narrows candidate metabolite annotations by selecting compounds whose exact masses fall within a user-specified mass-error window (e.g. 10 ppm of the target m/z for a given adduct type) before any collision-cross-section prediction is applied.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training sets only cover common adducts ([M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M+K]+); dimers like [2M+H]+, uncommon adducts, or in-source fragments are not supported Data already consist of a curated annotation table with no need for structure-level filtering

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare MS/MS library-search methods at finding exact library matches, by sweeping top-N cutoffs and measuring true-positive percentage across recall values.

skills.search_text: exact-match-benchmark-evaluation Use when you need to quantitatively compare MS/MS library-search methods at finding exact library matches, by sweeping top-N cutoffs and measuring true-positive percentage across recall values. When the goal is analogue search (non-identical matches) rather than exact library matches — the analogue benchmark applies different settings and a precursor m/z difference filter of 100 Da. When the library or models have not been checked for training/test contamination — models must be trained so that none of the test spectra were used for training MS2Deepscore or Spec2Vec. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks MS2Query (with no precursor m/z pre-filtering) against MS2Deepscore, cosine, and modified cosine (0.25 Da preselection) baselines on an exact matches test set, by sweeping top-N ranking cutoffs and comparing recall versus percentage of true positives. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks MS2Query (with no precursor m/z pre-filtering) against MS2Deepscore, cosine, and modified cosine (0.25 Da preselection) baselines on an exact matches test set, by sweeping top-N ranking cutoffs and comparing recall versus percentage of true positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is analogue search (non-identical matches) rather than exact library matches — the analogue benchmark applies different settings and a precursor m/z difference filter of 100 Da. skills.description: Use when you have MGF, mzXML, or mzML spectra with known precursor m/z and want to identify the intact candidate molecule (no variant mass shifts) by scoring fragments against a chemical database such as NPAtlas.
skills.name: exact-mode-spectrum-molecule-scoring
skills.search_text: exact-mode-spectrum-molecule-scoring Use when you have MGF, mzXML, or mzML spectra with known precursor m/z and want to identify the intact candidate molecule (no variant mass shifts) by scoring fragments against a chemical database such as NPAtlas. Precursor mass differs from the candidate molecule's mass due to a variant modification — in that case use VInSMoC's variable mode, since exact mode only matches molecules whose masses match the query spectra's precursor m/z. Spectra were already peak-merged and peak-filtered upstream and you cannot adjust the advanced Peak Merge Threshold / Peaks Per Window settings — defaults assume unprocessed spectra. Charge state exceeds 1 — maximum absolute charge of 1 restricts conversion to [M+H]+ or [M-H]-; multiply charged data requires changing this setting, which exact-mode defaults do not address. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Exact-mode scoring of query mass spectra against a candidate molecule database with VInSMoC: only candidates whose mass matches the spectrum's precursor m/z are scored, using adaptive fragmentation-graph expansion, [M+H]+/[M-H]- adduct conversion, and a peak count score. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Exact-mode scoring of query mass spectra against a candidate molecule database with VInSMoC: only candidates whose mass matches the spectrum's precursor m/z are scored, using adaptive fragmentation-graph expansion, [M+H]+/[M-H]- adduct conversion, and a peak count score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Precursor mass differs from the candidate molecule's mass due to a variant modification — in that case use VInSMoC's variable mode, since exact mode only matches molecules whose masses match the query spectra's precursor m/z. Spectra were already peak-merged and peak-filtered upstream and you cannot adjust the advanced Peak Merge Threshold / Peaks Per Window settings — defaults assume unprocessed spectra. Charge state exceeds 1 — maximum absolute charge of 1 restricts conversion to [M+H]+ or [M-H]-; multiply charged data requires changing this setting, which exact-mode defaults do not address.

skills.description: Use when validating or predicting m/z values for derivatization-specific diagnostic ions (e.g. FMP-10 phenolic-hydroxyl and primary-amine fragments reported at 286.122641 and 285.138625) before MS1 mass matching in MALDI-MSI annotation.
skills.name: exact-monoisotopic-mass-calculation
skills.search_text: exact-monoisotopic-mass-calculation Use when validating or predicting m/z values for derivatization-specific diagnostic ions (e.g. FMP-10 phenolic-hydroxyl and primary-amine fragments reported at 286.122641 and 285.138625) before MS1 mass matching in MALDI-MSI annotation. When the goal is similarity-based MS2 annotation rather than exact-mass verification — Met-ID's spectral database comparison of tissue MS2 spectra against standards spectra is the appropriate route When the m/z feature comes from a conventional (non-derivatizing) matrix yielding common [M+H]+ / [M-H]- adducts with no derivatization-specific diagnostic fragment to model When input is already a matched metabolite annotation table — no theoretical m/z computation is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute theoretical singly-charged ion m/z values from a fragment's elemental composition using monoisotopic atomic masses (C = 12.000000, H = 1.007825, N = 14.003074, O = 15.994915 Da) plus the proton mass (1.007276 Da), and score them against reported values by ppm deviation — the dPPM-style quantity Met-ID uses for high-resolution MALDI-MSI mass matching at mass_error = 5 ppm. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00633
skills.summary: Compute theoretical singly-charged ion m/z values from a fragment's elemental composition using monoisotopic atomic masses (C = 12.000000, H = 1.007825, N = 14.003074, O = 15.994915 Da) plus the proton mass (1.007276 Da), and score them against reported values by ppm deviation — the dPPM-style quantity Met-ID uses for high-resolution MALDI-MSI mass matching at mass_error = 5 ppm.
