skills.description: Use when a generative model produces candidate molecular structures (SMILES/coordinates) from spectra and you need to measure how often the exact target structure is recovered and how close near-misses are.
skills.name: exact-structure-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: exact-structure-accuracy-evaluation Use when a generative model produces candidate molecular structures (SMILES/coordinates) from spectra and you need to measure how often the exact target structure is recovered and how close near-misses are. Input spectra come from modalities outside IR, Raman, and UV-Vis (e.g. NMR or MS), which DiffSpectra does not cover You need to evaluate only topological 2D output without any 3D coordinate comparison — the RMSD/Hungarian step requires generated 3D coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Evaluates spectra-conditioned molecular generation by exact-match accuracy (top-1/top-10 SMILES match against ground truth) plus fingerprint-based similarity (Tanimoto on Morgan GNN/atom-pair features, functional-group similarity) and 3D quality (RMSD after Hungarian atom mapping). This is how DiffSpectra's 40.76% top-1 / 99.49% top-10 elucidation claims are quantified. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Evaluates spectra-conditioned molecular generation by exact-match accuracy (top-1/top-10 SMILES match against ground truth) plus fingerprint-based similarity (Tanimoto on Morgan GNN/atom-pair features, functional-group similarity) and 3D quality (RMSD after Hungarian atom mapping). This is how DiffSpectra's 40.76% top-1 / 99.49% top-10 elucidation claims are quantified.

skills.search_text: exact-structure-matching-metrics Use when you have generated molecular structures (e.g., from a diffusion or autoregressive model) plus ground-truth structures and need exact-match top-k accuracy or MCES similarity scores. skills.summary: Evaluates spectra-conditioned molecular generation by comparing canonical structures of generated molecules against ground truth to compute exact-match top-1/top-10 accuracy and MCES distance, as done for DiffSpectra on QM9S.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need 3D conformational fidelity assessment rather than 2D topological identity — use the RMSD/Hungarian-mapping evaluation (rmsd.py) instead Your generated outputs are not full molecular structures (e.g., spectra-only predictions or property values) — exact-match comparison is undefined You are evaluating unconditional generative quality metrics (validity, novelty, uniqueness) rather than recovery of a known target structure

The goal is a single flux distribution for one growth condition — flux balance analysis (FBA), not enumeration of all feasible exchanges via FVA, is appropriate The input is a single-organism (non-community) metabolic model without member-specific exchange reactions or a shared exchange compartment A fixed abundance profile with variable community growth rate is required instead — use the alternative PyCoMo model structure http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Enumerates all feasible exchange metabolites and pairwise cross-feeding interactions in a compartmentalized community metabolic model by running flux variability analysis (FVA) over member-specific exchange reactions under a fixed-growth-rate, variable-abundance model structure built with PyCoMo and analysed with COBRApy. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153

skills.description: Use when a host GEM (e.g., RECON3D in SBML) must be coupled to one or more gut microbiota metabolic models so that microbial metabolite fluxes shift the host model's exchange-reaction lower bounds.
skills.name: exchange-reaction-lower-bound-update
skills.search_text: exchange-reaction-lower-bound-update Use when a host GEM (e.g., RECON3D in SBML) must be coupled to one or more gut microbiota metabolic models so that microbial metabolite fluxes shift the host model's exchange-reaction lower bounds. When the microbiota model shares no metabolite identifiers with the host GEM — no reactions would be matched and no bounds would change. When the goal is to modify upper bounds or internal (non-exchange) reactions — M2R's update applies only to the lower bounds of reactions containing microbiota metabolites. When all host reactions must remain untouched at their original bounds — at α = 1 the update is fully host-scaled, so the microbiota fluxes would be effectively ignored. http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Method from the M2R paper (Bioinformatics 2021) for modifying the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) such as RECON3D, using aggregated in- and out-fluxes from gut microbiota models, via the M2R add-on to cobrapy. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: Method from the M2R paper (Bioinformatics 2021) for modifying the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) such as RECON3D, using aggregated in- and out-fluxes from gut microbiota models, via the M2R add-on to cobrapy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the microbiota model shares no metabolite identifiers with the host GEM — no reactions would be matched and no bounds would change. When the goal is to modify upper bounds or internal (non-exchange) reactions — M2R's update applies only to the lower bounds of reactions containing microbiota metabolites. When all host reactions must remain untouched at their original bounds — at α = 1 the update is fully host-scaled, so the microbiota fluxes would be effectively ignored.

The goal is the actual upload of records to PRIDE or MassIVE — this skill validates SDRF format conformance only, not repository submission The data are not managed in MSConnect (e.g. no SQL-backed database linking raw MS files to their File Uploader metadata) — the ORM-based mapping has no source to read from MSConnect is being used as a standalone analysis tool — per the README it 'is not a standalone data analysis tool' and depends on third-party software for data processing/analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Formally track experimental design for MS-based proteomics by mapping sample metadata stored in MSConnect's SQL-backed database onto the SDRF-Proteomics column schema, emitting a submission-ready .sdrf.tsv with one row per raw MS file for PRIDE/MassIVE submission packages. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c00854
skills.summary: Formally track experimental design for MS-based proteomics by mapping sample metadata stored in MSConnect's SQL-backed database onto the SDRF-Proteomics column schema, emitting a submission-ready .sdrf.tsv with one row per raw MS file for PRIDE/MassIVE submission packages.

skills.description: Use when a filtered NMRProcFlow bucket table must be turned into a samples-by-buckets data matrix whose rows (spectra) carry class-label columns for experimental-factor levels, e.g. before export to MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow.
skills.name: experimental-factor-metadata-annotation
skills.search_text: experimental-factor-metadata-annotation Use when a filtered NMRProcFlow bucket table must be turned into a samples-by-buckets data matrix whose rows (spectra) carry class-label columns for experimental-factor levels, e.g. before export to MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow. Input is still raw FID data (Bruker or Agilent/Varian) that has not been baseline-corrected, calibrated, realigned, and binned by NMRProcFlow The dataset has no experimental-factor levels or experimental design, so there is no class-label metadata to annotate spectra with The matrix is already a class-labeled feature table accepted directly by the downstream statistical tool Attach experimental-factor level information to each processed 1D NMR spectrum so the bucket table exported from NMRProcFlow becomes a class-labeled samples-by-buckets matrix interpretable by statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst 3.0 and BioStatFlow. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Attach experimental-factor level information to each processed 1D NMR spectrum so the bucket table exported from NMRProcFlow becomes a class-labeled samples-by-buckets matrix interpretable by statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst 3.0 and BioStatFlow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FID data (Bruker or Agilent/Varian) that has not been baseline-corrected, calibrated, realigned, and binned by NMRProcFlow The dataset has no experimental-factor levels or experimental design, so there is no class-label metadata to annotate spectra with The matrix is already a class-labeled feature table accepted directly by the downstream statistical tool

skills.description: Use when a model trained solely on simulated spectra (SGNN NMR, Chemprop-IR) must be evaluated on experimental spectral data to measure out-of-distribution generalization and improvement-cycle recovery.
skills.name: experimental-vs-simulated-spectra-generalization-testing
skills.search_text: experimental-vs-simulated-spectra-generalization-testing Use when a model trained solely on simulated spectra (SGNN NMR, Chemprop-IR) must be evaluated on experimental spectral data to measure out-of-distribution generalization and improvement-cycle recovery. The goal is training or fine-tuning the model on new data rather than evaluating out-of-distribution generalization of existing pre-trained checkpoints The compound benchmark differs from the curated 34-compound validation set with experimental spectra, so results cannot be compared against the reported reference accuracies No improvement-cycle models (mol2mol/deep-molecular-optimization checkpoints) or experimental spectra are available, making only the simulated condition runnable http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Benchmark a multi-spectral structure-prediction model (MMST) on a curated 34-compound set under both simulated (SGNN NMR, Chemprop-IR) and experimental 1H/13C/HSQC/COSY/IR/MS spectral inputs, then quantify how much the active-learning improvement cycle (IC) recovers accuracy lost to the simulated-to-experimental domain shift. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/ange.202517611
skills.summary: Benchmark a multi-spectral structure-prediction model (MMST) on a curated 34-compound set under both simulated (SGNN NMR, Chemprop-IR) and experimental 1H/13C/HSQC/COSY/IR/MS spectral inputs, then quantify how much the active-learning improvement cycle (IC) recovers accuracy lost to the simulated-to-experimental domain shift.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is training or fine-tuning the model on new data rather than evaluating out-of-distribution generalization of existing pre-trained checkpoints The compound benchmark differs from the curated 34-compound validation set with experimental spectra, so results cannot be compared against the reported reference accuracies No improvement-cycle models (mol2mol/deep-molecular-optimization checkpoints) or experimental spectra are available, making only the simulated condition runnable

skills.description: Use when a protocol needs a small, citable Thermo Fisher .raw example file for demonstration or testing and the article pins it to an ExperimentHub accession (EH4547) or a MassIVE dataset (MSV000086542).
skills.name: experimenthub-resource-fetching
skills.search_text: experimenthub-resource-fetching Use when a protocol needs a small, citable Thermo Fisher .raw example file for demonstration or testing and the article pins it to an ExperimentHub accession (EH4547) or a MassIVE dataset (MSV000086542). The analysis targets user-supplied or proprietary .raw files that are not registered in ExperimentHub or MassIVE — fetch them directly instead. The goal is conversion of raw data to exchange formats like mzML via ProteoWizard/MSconvert rather than obtaining a curated example dataset. Downstream tools require non-raw formats (e.g. mzML) that the EH4547 resource does not provide. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fetches reproducible example raw mass spectrometry data (e.g. 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw from MassIVE MSV000086542 or resource EH4547) through the Bioconductor ExperimentHub framework so downstream rawrr workflows start from a checksum-verified, locally normalized file path. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.10.30.362533
skills.summary: Fetches reproducible example raw mass spectrometry data (e.g. 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw from MassIVE MSV000086542 or resource EH4547) through the Bioconductor ExperimentHub framework so downstream rawrr workflows start from a checksum-verified, locally normalized file path.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets user-supplied or proprietary .raw files that are not registered in ExperimentHub or MassIVE — fetch them directly instead. The goal is conversion of raw data to exchange formats like mzML via ProteoWizard/MSconvert rather than obtaining a curated example dataset. Downstream tools require non-raw formats (e.g. mzML) that the EH4547 resource does not provide.

skills.description: Use when multiple human raters have independently labeled the same items (e.g., ion images tagged via TagOff) and you must quantify inter-rater reliability before merging tags into a curated gold standard.
skills.name: expert-annotation-aggregation
skills.search_text: expert-annotation-aggregation Use when multiple human raters have independently labeled the same items (e.g., ion images tagged via TagOff) and you must quantify inter-rater reliability before merging tags into a curated gold standard. You only have a single rater's labels and no curator reference — reliability coefficients like Cohen's kappa require at least two raters on the same items Your goal is to train or evaluate the off-sample classifier (ResNet-50/fastai) rather than to validate the human labels themselves The items are continuous scores rather than categorical off-sample/on-sample/unknown tags — kappa-based agreement as applied here assumes categorical labels http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Aggregates independent expert tags of ion images (off-sample/on-sample/unknown) by computing pairwise Cohen's kappa, tagger-vs-curator agreement, and multi-rater Krippendorff's alpha to validate that the aggregated gold standard labels are reliable. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: Aggregates independent expert tags of ion images (off-sample/on-sample/unknown) by computing pairwise Cohen's kappa, tagger-vs-curator agreement, and multi-rater Krippendorff's alpha to validate that the aggregated gold standard labels are reliable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single rater's labels and no curator reference — reliability coefficients like Cohen's kappa require at least two raters on the same items Your goal is to train or evaluate the off-sample classifier (ResNet-50/fastai) rather than to validate the human labels themselves The items are continuous scores rather than categorical off-sample/on-sample/unknown tags — kappa-based agreement as applied here assumes categorical labels

skills.description: Use when multiple independent raters have each scored the same set of files (e.g. qualified/unqualified per instrument run) and you need a reproducible ground-truth label or agreement statistics before training or benchmarking.
skills.name: expert-annotation-majority-voting
skills.search_text: expert-annotation-majority-voting Use when multiple independent raters have each scored the same set of files (e.g. qualified/unqualified per instrument run) and you need a reproducible ground-truth label or agreement statistics before training or benchmarking. Raters produced scores on a continuous scale rather than categorical qualified/unqualified votes, so majority voting is ill-defined without thresholding first Only one annotator is available per file, making agreement statistics meaningless You need fine-grained per-metric disagreement analysis (e.g. which specific QC metric caused divergence) rather than a single consensus label http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregate manual QC assessments from multiple domain experts (e.g. 21 experts scoring 2754 DIA files) into a single consensus label per file via majority voting, and quantify inter-expert observed agreement to establish ground-truth annotations for downstream model training and validation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-54871-1
skills.summary: Aggregate manual QC assessments from multiple domain experts (e.g. 21 experts scoring 2754 DIA files) into a single consensus label per file via majority voting, and quantify inter-expert observed agreement to establish ground-truth annotations for downstream model training and validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raters produced scores on a continuous scale rather than categorical qualified/unqualified votes, so majority voting is ill-defined without thresholding first Only one annotator is available per file, making agreement statistics meaningless You need fine-grained per-metric disagreement analysis (e.g. which specific QC metric caused divergence) rather than a single consensus label

skills.description: Use when ModiFinder MF-R output over a known/unknown analog pair (e.g. Kirromycin-Goldinodox, Naphthomycin A-B) leaves many atoms with high modification-site likelihood, and expert knowledge of gas-phase fragmentation can prune the peak-to-substructure assignments.
skills.name: expert-substructure-ambiguity-refinement
skills.search_text: expert-substructure-ambiguity-refinement Use when ModiFinder MF-R output over a known/unknown analog pair (e.g. Kirromycin-Goldinodox, Naphthomycin A-B) leaves many atoms with high modification-site likelihood, and expert knowledge of gas-phase fragmentation can prune the peak-to-substructure assignments. When the initial ModiFinder likelihood distribution already shows a single dominant high-scoring modification site and no ambiguous substructure assignments remain. When no domain knowledge about likely gas-phase fragmentation mechanisms (e.g. amide-bond cleavage) is available to justify restricting peak-to-substructure assignments, since arbitrary pruning is not expert refinement. When spectra have not been preprocessed per ModiFinder defaults (peaks <1% of base peak removed, normalized to Euclidean norm 1), as raw peak lists will give misleading initial assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Refines ModiFinder's MF-R likelihood distributions by manually restricting which substructures may explain specific MS/MS peaks, combining computational modification-site localization with domain-knowledge expertise to reduce ambiguity in natural product analog pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Refines ModiFinder's MF-R likelihood distributions by manually restricting which substructures may explain specific MS/MS peaks, combining computational modification-site localization with domain-knowledge expertise to reduce ambiguity in natural product analog pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the initial ModiFinder likelihood distribution already shows a single dominant high-scoring modification site and no ambiguous substructure assignments remain. When no domain knowledge about likely gas-phase fragmentation mechanisms (e.g. amide-bond cleavage) is available to justify restricting peak-to-substructure assignments, since arbitrary pruning is not expert refinement. When spectra have not been preprocessed per ModiFinder defaults (peaks <1% of base peak removed, normalized to Euclidean norm 1), as raw peak lists will give misleading initial assignments.

skills.description: Use when you have m/z query results matched against a metabolomic database (e.g., HMDB) and need to filter and rank candidate metabolite annotations under a defined experimental setup (ionization mode, allowed adducts).
skills.name: expert-system-rule-based-filtering
skills.search_text: expert-system-rule-based-filtering Use when you have m/z query results matched against a metabolomic database (e.g., HMDB) and need to filter and rank candidate metabolite annotations under a defined experimental setup (ionization mode, allowed adducts). You need MS2-based confirmation rather than MS1 candidate filtering — CMM 3.0's separate spectral-comparison and spectral quality-assessment services are the appropriate choice Input is already a ranked, scored annotation table; re-applying expert-system filtering would only re-rank existing results Candidate metabolites come from sources without defined adduct/ionization-mode metadata, since the rules depend on the experimental setup specification http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies CMM's expert-system rules — encoding knowledge of the experimental setup (ionization mode, adducts) and compound properties — to filter database-search candidate metabolites and assign rule-based plausibility scores, normalized to the 0–1 range, so annotations can be ranked. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00720
skills.summary: Applies CMM's expert-system rules — encoding knowledge of the experimental setup (ionization mode, adducts) and compound properties — to filter database-search candidate metabolites and assign rule-based plausibility scores, normalized to the 0–1 range, so annotations can be ranked.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need MS2-based confirmation rather than MS1 candidate filtering — CMM 3.0's separate spectral-comparison and spectral quality-assessment services are the appropriate choice Input is already a ranked, scored annotation table; re-applying expert-system filtering would only re-rank existing results Candidate metabolites come from sources without defined adduct/ionization-mode metadata, since the rules depend on the experimental setup specification

skills.description: Use when rerunning khipu annotation with modified isotope/adduct search patterns and you need to verify that the new run explains more features without inflating the empirical compound count (1,775 ESI+ / 908 ESI- expected on the yeast data).
skills.name: explained-feature-count-verification
skills.search_text: explained-feature-count-verification Use when rerunning khipu annotation with modified isotope/adduct search patterns and you need to verify that the new run explains more features without inflating the empirical compound count (1,775 ESI+ / 908 ESI- expected on the yeast data). Input is raw LC-MS data rather than a preprocessed asari feature table — khipu requires a feature table as input The ESI- data has not been quality-filtered (SNR > 100), so the cleaner demo counts of 2,601/2,912 explained features would not be comparable Goal is metabolite identity assignment or benchmarking against libraries — khipu preannotation only infers neutral masses and empirical compounds, not definitive IDs http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 A validation skill for khipu annotation runs that counts explained (grouped, non-singleton) LC-MS features per ionization mode before and after an adduct-pattern expansion, checking that empirical compound counts stay stable while explained-feature counts reproduce reported values (e.g. 6,310→8,049 ESI+ and 2,601→2,912 ESI- on the Chen et al. yeast data). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: A validation skill for khipu annotation runs that counts explained (grouped, non-singleton) LC-MS features per ionization mode before and after an adduct-pattern expansion, checking that empirical compound counts stay stable while explained-feature counts reproduce reported values (e.g. 6,310→8,049 ESI+ and 2,601→2,912 ESI- on the Chen et al. yeast data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data rather than a preprocessed asari feature table — khipu requires a feature table as input The ESI- data has not been quality-filtered (SNR > 100), so the cleaner demo counts of 2,601/2,912 explained features would not be comparable Goal is metabolite identity assignment or benchmarking against libraries — khipu preannotation only infers neutral masses and empirical compounds, not definitive IDs

skills.description: Use when a fitted PCA decomposition must be quantified — after projecting samples onto PCs, to record how much variance each component explains and validate that the component captures the expected share of high-dimensional feature variance.
skills.name: explained-variance-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: explained-variance-ratio-computation Use when a fitted PCA decomposition must be quantified — after projecting samples onto PCs, to record how much variance each component explains and validate that the component captures the expected share of high-dimensional feature variance. The task is supervised — Instant Clue separates (un)-supervised learning, and explained-variance ratios are only defined for unsupervised decompositions like PCA, not for prediction pipelines with estimator/grid-search steps The input is already a PCA score table or the components' explained variance is already reported, so recomputation would be redundant The data contain many missing values that cannot be handled — Instant Clue automatically filters such rows before activities, which would change the variance base; resolve imputation/filtering first http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Compute and report the per-component explained-variance ratios after fitting a principal component analysis on a feature matrix, so that the fraction of dataset variance captured by each principal component (e.g. PC1 on Fisher's iris data, expected ~0.90-0.95) can be used to judge how much dimensionality reduction is justified. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6
skills.summary: Compute and report the per-component explained-variance ratios after fitting a principal component analysis on a feature matrix, so that the fraction of dataset variance captured by each principal component (e.g. PC1 on Fisher's iris data, expected ~0.90-0.95) can be used to judge how much dimensionality reduction is justified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is supervised — Instant Clue separates (un)-supervised learning, and explained-variance ratios are only defined for unsupervised decompositions like PCA, not for prediction pipelines with estimator/grid-search steps The input is already a PCA score table or the components' explained variance is already reported, so recomputation would be redundant The data contain many missing values that cannot be handled — Instant Clue automatically filters such rows before activities, which would change the variance base; resolve imputation/filtering first

skills.description: Use when a PCA has been (or will be) fit on Protomix-preprocessed urine spectra (0.1 ppm rectangular bins, TotalArea-normalized) and you need per-component and cumulative explained-variance ratios, e.g. to justify how many PCs to retain for downstream cancer-vs-BHP analyses.
skills.name: explained-variance-reporting
skills.search_text: explained-variance-reporting Use when a PCA has been (or will be) fit on Protomix-preprocessed urine spectra (0.1 ppm rectangular bins, TotalArea-normalized) and you need per-component and cumulative explained-variance ratios, e.g. to justify how many PCs to retain for downstream cancer-vs-BHP analyses. Input is raw FID or unprocessed spectra — variance ratios on unbinned/unnormalized data are not comparable to the ~92.38% (PC1-PC10) reference; run the Protomix chain (binning, normalization) first The goal is supervised class separation or predictive modeling — explained-variance reporting is an unsupervised PCA diagnostic and does not use PC/BHP labels during fitting You only need spectral preprocessing (peak alignment, baseline correction, binning) — that is the Protomix preprocessing skill, not variance reporting http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3855 Quantifies how much total variance in a preprocessed 1H-NMR spectra matrix is captured by the leading principal components, producing a component-wise and cumulative explained-variance table (and scree-style report) after PCA of the binned, normalized spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Quantifies how much total variance in a preprocessed 1H-NMR spectra matrix is captured by the leading principal components, producing a component-wise and cumulative explained-variance table (and scree-style report) after PCA of the binned, normalized spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FID or unprocessed spectra — variance ratios on unbinned/unnormalized data are not comparable to the ~92.38% (PC1-PC10) reference; run the Protomix chain (binning, normalization) first The goal is supervised class separation or predictive modeling — explained-variance reporting is an unsupervised PCA diagnostic and does not use PC/BHP labels during fitting You only need spectral preprocessing (peak alignment, baseline correction, binning) — that is the Protomix preprocessing skill, not variance reporting

skills.description: Use when you have a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset (e.g., the tomato Jeon and colleagues 2020 dataset) and need to turn raw Pearson correlation values between transcripts and mass features into weighted edges for network clustering.
skills.name: exponential-decay-edge-weighting
skills.search_text: exponential-decay-edge-weighting Use when you have a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset (e.g., the tomato Jeon and colleagues 2020 dataset) and need to turn raw Pearson correlation values between transcripts and mass features into weighted edges for network clustering. The goal is reaction-rules-based pathway prediction rather than statistical correlation-based clustering of mass features and transcripts Input is a single-omics dataset (no paired transcriptomic and metabolomic samples), so transcript-mass feature correlations cannot be computed Only mass-shift or MS/MS spectral-library annotation of mass features is needed, with no co-abundance network intended http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 MEANtools' statistical-integration step that converts pairwise Pearson correlations between transcripts and mass features into mutual ranks (MRs) and then into discrete edge weights via an exponential decay function, producing weighted networks ready for overlapping ClusterONE clustering. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: MEANtools' statistical-integration step that converts pairwise Pearson correlations between transcripts and mass features into mutual ranks (MRs) and then into discrete edge weights via an exponential decay function, producing weighted networks ready for overlapping ClusterONE clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is reaction-rules-based pathway prediction rather than statistical correlation-based clustering of mass features and transcripts Input is a single-omics dataset (no paired transcriptomic and metabolomic samples), so transcript-mass feature correlations cannot be computed Only mass-shift or MS/MS spectral-library annotation of mass features is needed, with no co-abundance network intended

skills.description: Use when building or validating kernel functions for relaxation (T1, T2) or diffusion (D) NMR signals before feeding them to regularized numerical inversion (invert()) or multi-exponential fitting (expfit).
skills.name: exponential-decay-function-implementation
skills.search_text: exponential-decay-function-implementation Use when building or validating kernel functions for relaxation (T1, T2) or diffusion (D) NMR signals before feeding them to regularized numerical inversion (invert()) or multi-exponential fitting (expfit). Signals requiring harmonic inversion (damped oscillations) — these are not implemented in NMRInversions.jl and must be handled by packages such as harminv Fitting real experimental multi-exponential data — use the package's invert() or expfit routines instead of hand-coded kernels http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Implements the closed-form exponential decay kernels for NMR relaxation and diffusion pulse sequences (inversion recovery, saturation recovery, CPMG, PGSE) as checkable Julia functions, mirroring the kernel model forms that NMRInversions.jl's numerical inversion and multi-exponential fitting routines rely on. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.07745
skills.summary: Implements the closed-form exponential decay kernels for NMR relaxation and diffusion pulse sequences (inversion recovery, saturation recovery, CPMG, PGSE) as checkable Julia functions, mirroring the kernel model forms that NMRInversions.jl's numerical inversion and multi-exponential fitting routines rely on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Signals requiring harmonic inversion (damped oscillations) — these are not implemented in NMRInversions.jl and must be handled by packages such as harminv Fitting real experimental multi-exponential data — use the package's invert() or expfit routines instead of hand-coded kernels

skills.description: Use when comparing compound-detection depth of JPA vs conventional peak picking on serially diluted LC-MS exposome standard mixture data (e.g. MTBLS2631 RP(+) mzXML files), to reproduce or re-quantify detection fold-gains per dilution level.
skills.name: exposome-compound-detection-benchmarking
skills.search_text: exposome-compound-detection-benchmarking Use when comparing compound-detection depth of JPA vs conventional peak picking on serially diluted LC-MS exposome standard mixture data (e.g. MTBLS2631 RP(+) mzXML files), to reproduce or re-quantify detection fold-gains per dilution level. Processing full-scan or DIA data sets with the MR (MS2 recognition) step — the README explicitly warns not to use find.level3features on full-scan/DIA data Input is already a per-file aligned feature table from other software (use custom.featureTable instead of re-running XCMS.featureTable on raw data) Data are not serially diluted standards matched against a known compound list — per-compound recovery counts and fold gains are not computable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks JPA's joint feature extraction (peak picking + MS2 recognition + targeted extraction) against XCMS peak-picking-only by counting how many of the 505 exposome compounds (250 drugs + 255 pesticides) are recovered per concentration level in RP(+) mode, quantifying the reported ~2.3-fold detection gain. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212
skills.summary: Benchmarks JPA's joint feature extraction (peak picking + MS2 recognition + targeted extraction) against XCMS peak-picking-only by counting how many of the 505 exposome compounds (250 drugs + 255 pesticides) are recovered per concentration level in RP(+) mode, quantifying the reported ~2.3-fold detection gain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Processing full-scan or DIA data sets with the MR (MS2 recognition) step — the README explicitly warns not to use find.level3features on full-scan/DIA data Input is already a per-file aligned feature table from other software (use custom.featureTable instead of re-running XCMS.featureTable on raw data) Data are not serially diluted standards matched against a known compound list — per-compound recovery counts and fold gains are not computable

skills.description: Use when the goal is to build a large, deduplicated human exposome chemical inventory from multiple public databases and literature sources, keyed by CASRN with SMILES/InChIKey annotations.
skills.name: exposome-database-compilation
skills.search_text: exposome-database-compilation Use when the goal is to build a large, deduplicated human exposome chemical inventory from multiple public databases and literature sources, keyed by CASRN with SMILES/InChIKey annotations. The input is already a small, curated chemical list for a targeted analysis — database fusion and deduplication are unnecessary The downstream goal is toxicity prediction, exposure estimation, or risk-based prioritization of an existing chemical set (SEEM, TEST, ToxPi, ToxCast steps) rather than building the inventory itself Chemicals of interest lack CASRN and cannot be resolved through the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard, so the annotation join will fail Compiles a comprehensive human exposome chemical inventory (>20,000 chemicals) by text mining and fusing public databases (EPA HPV, EINECS, CHEMINV, NIH Tox21, EPA pesticides, Exposome-Explorer, Blood Exposome, dust exposome), then filtering and deduplicating to a unique CASRN-keyed list with structural identifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Compiles a comprehensive human exposome chemical inventory (>20,000 chemicals) by text mining and fusing public databases (EPA HPV, EINECS, CHEMINV, NIH Tox21, EPA pesticides, Exposome-Explorer, Blood Exposome, dust exposome), then filtering and deduplicating to a unique CASRN-keyed list with structural identifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a small, curated chemical list for a targeted analysis — database fusion and deduplication are unnecessary The downstream goal is toxicity prediction, exposure estimation, or risk-based prioritization of an existing chemical set (SEEM, TEST, ToxPi, ToxCast steps) rather than building the inventory itself Chemicals of interest lack CASRN and cannot be resolved through the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard, so the annotation join will fail

skills.description: Use when a built multi-omics network (e.g., MetaNet multi1 or co_net objects) contains gene nodes linked to microbial or chemical exposures and you need KEGG/GO over-representation analysis per exposure class.
skills.name: exposome-transcriptome-gene-set-association
skills.search_text: exposome-transcriptome-gene-set-association Use when a built multi-omics network (e.g., MetaNet multi1 or co_net objects) contains gene nodes linked to microbial or chemical exposures and you need KEGG/GO over-representation analysis per exposure class. The input is a raw feature abundance table (e.g., otutab or multi_test matrices) that has not yet been converted into a built network with exposure-associated gene vertices identified. The goal is network construction, layout, or visualization of the multi-omics graph rather than functional interpretation of exposure-associated gene sets. The gene list is the entire transcriptome rather than the network-derived subset of exposure-associated genes, which would invalidate the over-representation background. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts gene nodes with significant exposure associations from an integrative exposome–transcriptome network built with MetaNet, then runs ReporterScore-style KEGG and GO over-representation analysis separately on the microbial- and chemical-exposure-associated gene lists to identify enriched pathways. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.06.26.661636
skills.summary: Extracts gene nodes with significant exposure associations from an integrative exposome–transcriptome network built with MetaNet, then runs ReporterScore-style KEGG and GO over-representation analysis separately on the microbial- and chemical-exposure-associated gene lists to identify enriched pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw feature abundance table (e.g., otutab or multi_test matrices) that has not yet been converted into a built network with exposure-associated gene vertices identified. The goal is network construction, layout, or visualization of the multi-omics graph rather than functional interpretation of exposure-associated gene sets. The gene list is the entire transcriptome rather than the network-derived subset of exposure-associated genes, which would invalidate the over-representation background.

skills.description: Use when you need to connect exposure-level features (microbial taxa, chemicals) to host transcriptomic features via cross-layer correlations and compare edge-sign distributions between exposure types.
skills.name: exposome-transcriptome-integration-analysis

skills.description: Use when a chemical inventory lacks measured toxicity values and you need a probabilistic exposure-vs-hazard risk score (PrHQ) to rank chemicals for prioritization.
skills.name: exposure-hazard-quotient-calculation
skills.search_text: exposure-hazard-quotient-calculation Use when a chemical inventory lacks measured toxicity values and you need a probabilistic exposure-vs-hazard risk score (PrHQ) to rank chemicals for prioritization. The goal is chronic or subchronic toxicity risk assessment — the LD50-based HDMI may underestimate the risk of chemicals for their chronic and subchronic toxicity Internal dose is required — the PrHQ was calculated using external exposure, and the article states the IVIVE model should be considered in future studies Chemical lacks a CASRN — the high-throughput screening method based on the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard only retrieves domain data for chemicals with CASRN, and SEEM was unable to cover all compounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 http://edamontology.org/topic_2815 Calculates a probabilistic hazard quotient (PrHQ) for each chemical as the ratio of SEEM-based exposure estimates (EHE) to an LD50-derived probabilistic human dose of minimal incidence (HDMI), enabling risk-based ranking of thousands of exposome chemicals. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Calculates a probabilistic hazard quotient (PrHQ) for each chemical as the ratio of SEEM-based exposure estimates (EHE) to an LD50-derived probabilistic human dose of minimal incidence (HDMI), enabling risk-based ranking of thousands of exposome chemicals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is chronic or subchronic toxicity risk assessment — the LD50-based HDMI may underestimate the risk of chemicals for their chronic and subchronic toxicity Internal dose is required — the PrHQ was calculated using external exposure, and the article states the IVIVE model should be considered in future studies Chemical lacks a CASRN — the high-throughput screening method based on the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard only retrieves domain data for chemicals with CASRN, and SEEM was unable to cover all compounds

skills.search_text: exposure-intake-rate-estimation Use when a compiled chemical list (e.g., HExpMetDB's 20,756 human exposome substances) needs predicted population-level exposure/intake values (mg/kg BW per day) from the SEEM consensus model to support exposure- or risk-based chemical prioritization. You need internal (serum/urine) doses rather than external intake rates — the article notes external-to-internal exposure conversion and IVIVE modeling are needed in future work Substances lack a CASRN — the Chemistry Dashboard-based retrieval succeeds only for chemicals with CASRN You need measured exposures rather than model predictions — SEEM provides predicted, not biomonitoring-measured, values Assigns predicted median human intake rates (mg/kg BW per day, with 95% confidence intervals) to compiled human exposome chemicals by matching each substance against the SEEM consensus exposure model (Ring et al. 2019, R2 ≈ 0.8), enabling exposure-based prioritization across the >20,000-chemical HExpMetDB compilation. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Assigns predicted median human intake rates (mg/kg BW per day, with 95% confidence intervals) to compiled human exposome chemicals by matching each substance against the SEEM consensus exposure model (Ring et al. 2019, R2 ≈ 0.8), enabling exposure-based prioritization across the >20,000-chemical HExpMetDB compilation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need internal (serum/urine) doses rather than external intake rates — the article notes external-to-internal exposure conversion and IVIVE modeling are needed in future work Substances lack a CASRN — the Chemistry Dashboard-based retrieval succeeds only for chemicals with CASRN You need measured exposures rather than model predictions — SEEM provides predicted, not biomonitoring-measured, values

skills.description: Use when curating analog (non-library) MS/MS matches from untargeted metabolomics data and you must drop analogs whose parent drug can plausibly arise endogenously or from the food supply, before propagating spectra into a drug-exposure screening library.
skills.name: exposure-source-metadata-filtering
skills.search_text: exposure-source-metadata-filtering Use when curating analog (non-library) MS/MS matches from untargeted metabolomics data and you must drop analogs whose parent drug can plausibly arise endogenously or from the food supply, before propagating spectra into a drug-exposure screening library. When the goal is direct spectral identification of parent drugs already present in the GNPS library — those are handled by library matching, not analog curation filters When screening for endogenous metabolites or food-derived compounds rather than exogenous drug exposure — this filter would incorrectly remove the signals of interest When the input analog matches already passed full curation (e.g., analog_library_filtered.csv) — re-filtering would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A curation filter from the GNPS Drug Library pipeline that removes propagated drug-analog spectra whose parent drug carries an endogenous or dietary-source exposure annotation, so that downstream drug-exposure screening in untargeted metabolomics reflects true exogenous exposures rather than host- or food-derived chemistry. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5
skills.summary: A curation filter from the GNPS Drug Library pipeline that removes propagated drug-analog spectra whose parent drug carries an endogenous or dietary-source exposure annotation, so that downstream drug-exposure screening in untargeted metabolomics reflects true exogenous exposures rather than host- or food-derived chemistry.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct spectral identification of parent drugs already present in the GNPS library — those are handled by library matching, not analog curation filters When screening for endogenous metabolites or food-derived compounds rather than exogenous drug exposure — this filter would incorrectly remove the signals of interest When the input analog matches already passed full curation (e.g., analog_library_filtered.csv) — re-filtering would be redundant

skills.name: exposure-toxicity-integration-ranking
skills.search_text: exposure-toxicity-integration-ranking Use when you hold paired exposure estimates (e.g., SEEM) and in vitro toxicity scores (ToxCast/ToxPi) for a chemical set and need a single risk-based ranking that integrates both dimensions. Chemicals lack ToxCast/ToxPi coverage or SEEM exposure estimates — the SEEM database was unable to cover all compounds in the study, so RI cannot be computed for uncovered chemicals You need internal-dose or IVIVE-based risk scoring — the article explicitly notes the risk score was calculated using external exposure and the IVIVE model should be considered in future studies HTS data retrieval is needed for chemicals without CASRN — the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard-based method only succeeded for chemicals with CASRN http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Computes a risk index (RI) for chemicals in the HExpMetDB human exposome database by multiplying rescaled, log-transformed SEEM exposure estimates by ToxCast-derived ToxPi toxicity scores, then ranks chemicals by RI and cross-validates the ranking against probabilistic hazard quotient (PrHQ) ranks. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Computes a risk index (RI) for chemicals in the HExpMetDB human exposome database by multiplying rescaled, log-transformed SEEM exposure estimates by ToxCast-derived ToxPi toxicity scores, then ranks chemicals by RI and cross-validates the ranking against probabilistic hazard quotient (PrHQ) ranks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Chemicals lack ToxCast/ToxPi coverage or SEEM exposure estimates — the SEEM database was unable to cover all compounds in the study, so RI cannot be computed for uncovered chemicals You need internal-dose or IVIVE-based risk scoring — the article explicitly notes the risk score was calculated using external exposure and the IVIVE model should be considered in future studies HTS data retrieval is needed for chemicals without CASRN — the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard-based method only succeeded for chemicals with CASRN

skills.description: Use when a sample-by-gene expression matrix with sample metadata (e.g. organ, tumor status) needs QC before downstream analysis, and samples from the same biological condition must be checked for consistently high pairwise correlations or abnormally low expression.
skills.name: expression-dataset-exploratory-quality-control
skills.search_text: expression-dataset-exploratory-quality-control Use when a sample-by-gene expression matrix with sample metadata (e.g. organ, tumor status) needs QC before downstream analysis, and samples from the same biological condition must be checked for consistently high pairwise correlations or abnormally low expression. The goal is gene-level differential expression testing (e.g. fold-change ≥ 2 with BH-corrected Mann–Whitney U P < 10−3), not sample-level QC The dataset has no sample metadata to define biological conditions, so within-condition correlation grouping is impossible Input is already a cleaned correlation matrix or a feature/gene table with samples removed http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Exploratory quality control of large expression datasets in MetaOmGraph (MOG) by grouping samples with metadata and computing within-condition pairwise Pearson correlations to detect outlier samples. In the Hu-cancer RNA-Seq case study it flagged a single lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) sample, which was removed so that all remaining within-condition correlations exceeded 0.70. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Exploratory quality control of large expression datasets in MetaOmGraph (MOG) by grouping samples with metadata and computing within-condition pairwise Pearson correlations to detect outlier samples. In the Hu-cancer RNA-Seq case study it flagged a single lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) sample, which was removed so that all remaining within-condition correlations exceeded 0.70.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-level differential expression testing (e.g. fold-change ≥ 2 with BH-corrected Mann–Whitney U P < 10−3), not sample-level QC The dataset has no sample metadata to define biological conditions, so within-condition correlation grouping is impossible Input is already a cleaned correlation matrix or a feature/gene table with samples removed

skills.description: Use when you have a numeric expression matrix (feature rows x sample columns) and need pairwise, non-linear dependency scores between features that may not be captured by Pearson or Spearman correlation.
skills.name: expression-matrix-dependency-analysis
skills.search_text: expression-matrix-dependency-analysis Use when you have a numeric expression matrix (feature rows x sample columns) and need pairwise, non-linear dependency scores between features that may not be captured by Pearson or Spearman correlation. The analysis goal is strictly linear monotonic association, where MOG's Spearman correlation (e.g. threshold >= 0.60 for co-expressed gene pairs) is already appropriate The input is not a numeric feature x sample matrix (e.g. raw reads, metadata tables, or already-computed distance matrices) The matrix is too large for in-memory pairwise estimation; MOG's big-data workflows rely on indexing/buffering rather than exhaustive MI computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates pairwise statistical associations between features of an expression matrix using MetaOmGraph's B-spline mutual information estimator (Daub et al.), a non-linear dependency measure that yields exactly zero for independent features. It complements linear measures such as the Pearson/Spearman correlations MOG applies in its co-expression analyses. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Estimates pairwise statistical associations between features of an expression matrix using MetaOmGraph's B-spline mutual information estimator (Daub et al.), a non-linear dependency measure that yields exactly zero for independent features. It complements linear measures such as the Pearson/Spearman correlations MOG applies in its co-expression analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is strictly linear monotonic association, where MOG's Spearman correlation (e.g. threshold >= 0.60 for co-expressed gene pairs) is already appropriate The input is not a numeric feature x sample matrix (e.g. raw reads, metadata tables, or already-computed distance matrices) The matrix is too large for in-memory pairwise estimation; MOG's big-data workflows rely on indexing/buffering rather than exhaustive MI computation

skills.description: Use when a filtered/assembled expression dataset must be checked against its published dimensions (e.g. 18,212 genes x 7,412 samples for the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset) before MOG analyses.
skills.name: expression-matrix-dimension-validation
skills.search_text: expression-matrix-dimension-validation Use when a filtered/assembled expression dataset must be checked against its published dimensions (e.g. 18,212 genes x 7,412 samples for the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset) before MOG analyses. Input is an unrelated expression dataset (e.g. the AT-microarray-dataset or AT-metab-dataset) whose expected dimensions are not 18,212 x 7,412 The raw pooled TCGA/GTEx resource has not yet passed through the article's filter steps (organ-type sample minimums, duplicate-sample removal, gene intersection), so dimension mismatches would be expected and uninformative The goal is statistical analysis of the matrix rather than structural validation of the assembled MOG project http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validate that a constructed MetaOmGraph (MOG) project expression matrix has the expected reported dimensions — for the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset, exactly 18,212 gene rows by 7,412 sample columns — so downstream MOG analyses operate on a correctly assembled dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Validate that a constructed MetaOmGraph (MOG) project expression matrix has the expected reported dimensions — for the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset, exactly 18,212 gene rows by 7,412 sample columns — so downstream MOG analyses operate on a correctly assembled dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unrelated expression dataset (e.g. the AT-microarray-dataset or AT-metab-dataset) whose expected dimensions are not 18,212 x 7,412 The raw pooled TCGA/GTEx resource has not yet passed through the article's filter steps (organ-type sample minimums, duplicate-sample removal, gene intersection), so dimension mismatches would be expected and uninformative The goal is statistical analysis of the matrix rather than structural validation of the assembled MOG project

skills.description: Use when an expression matrix has samples partitioned into two groups (e.g. leaf vs pollen, early vs late stage, tumour vs non-tumour) and the goal is to flag features whose Pearson correlation with a user-selected target feature differs significantly between the groups.
skills.name: expression-matrix-group-wise-analysis
skills.search_text: expression-matrix-group-wise-analysis Use when an expression matrix has samples partitioned into two groups (e.g. leaf vs pollen, early vs late stage, tumour vs non-tumour) and the goal is to flag features whose Pearson correlation with a user-selected target feature differs significantly between the groups. The goal is differential expression between the two groups, not differential correlation — use the group-comparison test MOG applies on log2 transformed data (Mann–Whitney U test with BH correction, e.g. P < 10−3) instead. Either group has fewer than 4 samples: the Fisher-test standard error sqrt(1/(n1-3)+1/(n2-3)) is undefined when n ≤ 3. The task is sample-level QC — pairwise Pearson correlations among samples from the same biological condition to spot outliers/batch effects (as when MOG flagged one LUAD sample for removal) — which compares samples, not feature correlations across groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Replicates MetaOmGraph's differential correlation analysis: for every feature, the Pearson correlation with a user-selected target feature is computed separately within two sample groups, then the two coefficients are compared via Fisher z-transformation and a two-tailed z-test, reporting P-values on both the Fisher-transformed and the raw coefficients. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Replicates MetaOmGraph's differential correlation analysis: for every feature, the Pearson correlation with a user-selected target feature is computed separately within two sample groups, then the two coefficients are compared via Fisher z-transformation and a two-tailed z-test, reporting P-values on both the Fisher-transformed and the raw coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression between the two groups, not differential correlation — use the group-comparison test MOG applies on log2 transformed data (Mann–Whitney U test with BH correction, e.g. P < 10−3) instead. Either group has fewer than 4 samples: the Fisher-test standard error sqrt(1/(n1-3)+1/(n2-3)) is undefined when n ≤ 3. The task is sample-level QC — pairwise Pearson correlations among samples from the same biological condition to spot outliers/batch effects (as when MOG flagged one LUAD sample for removal) — which compares samples, not feature correlations across groups.

skills.description: Use when a raw gene-by-sample expression matrix (e.g., Mootha DM2 or smoker airway epithelium data) must be standardized and subset to ~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene-sets before SVD-based pathway activity computation.
skills.name: expression-matrix-standardization-and-subsetting
skills.search_text: expression-matrix-standardization-and-subsetting Use when a raw gene-by-sample expression matrix (e.g., Mootha DM2 or smoker airway epithelium data) must be standardized and subset to ~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene-sets before SVD-based pathway activity computation. When the goal is gene-level ranking/enrichment itself (e.g., GSEA signal-to-noise ranking with 1000 permutations) rather than producing standardized pathway-level inputs for SVD. When the input is already a pathway activity score table or the gene-sets are not defined gene lists (e.g., de novo clustered features), since subsetting requires explicit KEGG/Biocarta gene memberships. When sample sizes are too small relative to pathway gene count for a stable restricted-matrix decomposition. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 A preprocessing skill from the PLAGE (Pathway Level Analysis of Gene Expression) method: restrict a gene-by-sample microarray matrix to a pathway's genes and standardize each gene to zero mean and unit variance over samples, so that singular value decomposition of the subset matrix yields pathway 'activity' levels. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: A preprocessing skill from the PLAGE (Pathway Level Analysis of Gene Expression) method: restrict a gene-by-sample microarray matrix to a pathway's genes and standardize each gene to zero mean and unit variance over samples, so that singular value decomposition of the subset matrix yields pathway 'activity' levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is gene-level ranking/enrichment itself (e.g., GSEA signal-to-noise ranking with 1000 permutations) rather than producing standardized pathway-level inputs for SVD. When the input is already a pathway activity score table or the gene-sets are not defined gene lists (e.g., de novo clustered features), since subsetting requires explicit KEGG/Biocarta gene memberships. When sample sizes are too small relative to pathway gene count for a stable restricted-matrix decomposition.

skills.description: Use when you have a vendor-exported peak-area table (e.g. a MultiQuant 3.0.3 export of peak areas and retention times) for a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence and need per-injection concentrations calibrated against external calibration standards, optionally with drift correction.
skills.name: external-calibration-concentration-calculation
skills.search_text: external-calibration-concentration-calculation Use when you have a vendor-exported peak-area table (e.g. a MultiQuant 3.0.3 export of peak areas and retention times) for a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence and need per-injection concentrations calibrated against external calibration standards, optionally with drift correction. Input is raw chromatographic data that still needs peak integration — QuantyFey 'does not provide any integration cabailities' and only works on already-integrated MS data Data are already quantified concentrations and only downstream statistics are needed A drift-correction method is required that QuantyFey does not implement (e.g. proprietary vendor-autoquant correction) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Compute analyte concentrations from already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas via external calibration regression, as implemented in QuantyFey (R 4.2.0/Shiny). Drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based, custom/weighted bracketing) and linear/quadratic regression optimization are integrated so concentrations reflect injection-order intensity drift. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Compute analyte concentrations from already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas via external calibration regression, as implemented in QuantyFey (R 4.2.0/Shiny). Drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based, custom/weighted bracketing) and linear/quadratic regression optimization are integrated so concentrations reflect injection-order intensity drift.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw chromatographic data that still needs peak integration — QuantyFey 'does not provide any integration cabailities' and only works on already-integrated MS data Data are already quantified concentrations and only downstream statistics are needed A drift-correction method is required that QuantyFey does not implement (e.g. proprietary vendor-autoquant correction)

skills.description: Use when you have already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas (e.g. exported from MultiQuant) plus external calibration curves and need to compute concentrations per compound, optionally after drift correction.
skills.name: external-calibration-conversion
skills.search_text: external-calibration-conversion Use when you have already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas (e.g. exported from MultiQuant) plus external calibration curves and need to compute concentrations per compound, optionally after drift correction. The data are not yet integrated — QuantyFey does not provide integration capabilities and expects already-integrated vendor data You need calibration via internal standard correction only when a suitable IS exists; unsuitable IS selection (e.g. 4-hydroxy-proline vs proline) introduces bias You are running on macOS — QuantyFey is compatible with Windows operating systems only (the Apptainer version is slow and difficult to set up there) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Convert integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas into analyte concentrations using compound-specific external calibration regression models, applying the areas as exported from vendor integration software without re-integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Convert integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas into analyte concentrations using compound-specific external calibration regression models, applying the areas as exported from vendor integration software without re-integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not yet integrated — QuantyFey does not provide integration capabilities and expects already-integrated vendor data You need calibration via internal standard correction only when a suitable IS exists; unsuitable IS selection (e.g. 4-hydroxy-proline vs proline) introduces bias You are running on macOS — QuantyFey is compatible with Windows operating systems only (the Apptainer version is slow and difficult to set up there)

skills.description: Use when a targeted MRM/HRMS metabolomics assay (e.g. Biocrates p180 serum amino acids or arginine/polyamine panels) must yield calibrated concentrations rather than only peak areas, using heavy-labeled internal standards or external calibrants in Skyline.
skills.name: external-calibration-quantification-setup
skills.search_text: external-calibration-quantification-setup Use when a targeted MRM/HRMS metabolomics assay (e.g. Biocrates p180 serum amino acids or arginine/polyamine panels) must yield calibrated concentrations rather than only peak areas, using heavy-labeled internal standards or external calibrants in Skyline. The goal is untargeted feature finding, alignment, and identification — use XCMS, MZmine, or MS-DIAL instead of Skyline's extract-known-targets approach Quantification relies on vendor-software-specific workflows where Skyline support lags (e.g. latest-generation GC-MS or ion mobility data) Input is already a processed feature/concentration table requiring no chromatographic re-integration http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Configure Skyline small-molecule documents so compound concentrations are calculated by isotope-dilution/external calibration against heavy-labeled internal standards, then exported with flexible quantification reports. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.9b00640

skills.description: Use when a cross-validated metabolite-prediction model exists and an independent paired microbiome-metabolome cohort is available to test transfer without retraining.
skills.name: external-cohort-transfer-validation
skills.search_text: external-cohort-transfer-validation Use when a cross-validated metabolite-prediction model exists and an independent paired microbiome-metabolome cohort is available to test transfer without retraining. No independent external cohort with paired microbiome-metabolome samples exists — cross-validation alone cannot substitute for external transfer validation. The external metabolome features are unannotated and the evaluation goal requires annotated-metabolite reporting, since IBD annotated SCC (0.309) relies on the annotation file. The goal is internal performance estimation (e.g. model comparison via 10-iteration 10-fold cross-validation) rather than transfer to a new cohort. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Apply a trained MiMeNet model to an independent external cohort (the IBD external test set) to obtain external-validation Spearman correlation coefficients (SCCs), testing that cross-validated performance transfers beyond the training cohort. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009021
skills.summary: Apply a trained MiMeNet model to an independent external cohort (the IBD external test set) to obtain external-validation Spearman correlation coefficients (SCCs), testing that cross-validated performance transfers beyond the training cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent external cohort with paired microbiome-metabolome samples exists — cross-validation alone cannot substitute for external transfer validation. The external metabolome features are unannotated and the evaluation goal requires annotated-metabolite reporting, since IBD annotated SCC (0.309) relies on the annotation file. The goal is internal performance estimation (e.g. model comparison via 10-iteration 10-fold cross-validation) rather than transfer to a new cohort.

skills.description: Use when a structural-similarity scoring model trained on one MS/MS dataset (e.g. MetDNA/DIONysus 40V spectra of KEGG compounds) must be evaluated on independent spectra measured on different instruments (e.g. Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) to test generalization.
skills.name: external-dataset-model-validation
skills.search_text: external-dataset-model-validation Use when a structural-similarity scoring model trained on one MS/MS dataset (e.g. MetDNA/DIONysus 40V spectra of KEGG compounds) must be evaluated on independent spectra measured on different instruments (e.g. Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) to test generalization. Do not use when the question is internal model fit on the training set itself — that is the leave-one-out cross-validation evaluation on the 662 KEGG compounds, not an external generalization test. Do not use to claim identification of an unknown whose structure-related metabolite is absent from the reference database — the paper explicitly states identification is valid only when that metabolite is available. Do not use as a de novo structural elucidation method; DeepMASS only ranks known database structures by predicted similarity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Validates a trained DeepMS/MS structural-similarity scorer on spectra acquired on instruments and sample cohorts disjoint from the training data, by ranking KEGG database metabolites for each held-out MS/MS spectrum and checking recovery of the structure-related (true) metabolite. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05405
skills.summary: Validates a trained DeepMS/MS structural-similarity scorer on spectra acquired on instruments and sample cohorts disjoint from the training data, by ranking KEGG database metabolites for each held-out MS/MS spectrum and checking recovery of the structure-related (true) metabolite.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use when the question is internal model fit on the training set itself — that is the leave-one-out cross-validation evaluation on the 662 KEGG compounds, not an external generalization test. Do not use to claim identification of an unknown whose structure-related metabolite is absent from the reference database — the paper explicitly states identification is valid only when that metabolite is available. Do not use as a de novo structural elucidation method; DeepMASS only ranks known database structures by predicted similarity.

skills.description: Use when validating a spectral-similarity or metabolite-identification model on spectra from an independent instrument or study (external test set), e.g. biomarker spectra from a male infertility study measured on a Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF after training on IT-TOF data.
skills.name: external-instrument-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: external-instrument-benchmark-evaluation Use when validating a spectral-similarity or metabolite-identification model on spectra from an independent instrument or study (external test set), e.g. biomarker spectra from a male infertility study measured on a Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF after training on IT-TOF data. The goal is exact-structure identification with an in-house standard library — DeepMASS's criterion is validity via a structure-related metabolite, not exact matching. The spectra are from the same instrument and study used for leave-one-out cross-validation; use the internal CV evaluation instead of an external instrument benchmark. No trained DeepMASS model or structural database is available and you cannot train one from in-house spectra (the README notes the original experimental dataset was removed, so the package cannot be run directly without your own spectra). http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Runs a trained DeepMASS structural-similarity scorer on MS/MS spectra acquired on an instrument not used for model training (e.g. Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF biomarker spectra) and assesses whether identification of unknown compounds is valid when a structure-related metabolite exists in the database. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05405
skills.summary: Runs a trained DeepMASS structural-similarity scorer on MS/MS spectra acquired on an instrument not used for model training (e.g. Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF biomarker spectra) and assesses whether identification of unknown compounds is valid when a structure-related metabolite exists in the database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exact-structure identification with an in-house standard library — DeepMASS's criterion is validity via a structure-related metabolite, not exact matching. skills.summary: Removes background features from an HRMS sample by matching detected features against an extraction blank: any feature present in both sample and blank (< 2 mDa mass deviation, < 0.1 min RT difference) is dropped unless it is at least fivefold more abundant in the sample, yielding a background-corrected feature list for downstream PFAS prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user supplies only a sample file with no extraction blank mzML — blank correction cannot be performed and features are passed unfiltered to prioritization The input is already a final prioritization results table rather than raw mzML or a pre-prioritization feature list The data are profile-mode or non-DDA spectra — PFΔScreen requires centroided ddMS2 mzML input

skills.description: Use when assessing whether a reproducibility-detection procedure controls FDR at the nominal level under rank-dependent correlation decay between replicate pairs, e.g., pi_1 x r_0 simulation grids.
skills.name: false-discovery-rate-empirical-calibration
skills.search_text: false-discovery-rate-empirical-calibration Use when assessing whether a reproducibility-detection procedure controls FDR at the nominal level under rank-dependent correlation decay between replicate pairs, e.g., pi_1 x r_0 simulation grids. The goal is a comprehensive evaluation of metabolomics pre-processing steps (BPCA/kNN imputation, quantile/median/RUV normalization) — the paper states its goal was only to benchmark comparisons, not to comprehensively evaluate pre-processing. Reproducible and irreproducible components strongly overlap (lack of separation), which the authors note can push true signals into undetectable regions and distort calibration. The true proportion of reproducible signals (pi_1) is very small — MaRR power drops in these settings, so FDR/power curves alone should not be read as a calibration failure. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Empirically calibrates the False Discovery Rate of the nonparametric MaRR maximal rank statistic by simulating replicate-pair data whose correlation decays with rank, then aggregating empirical FDR, power (1-NDR), and bias across settings. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04336-9
skills.summary: Empirically calibrates the False Discovery Rate of the nonparametric MaRR maximal rank statistic by simulating replicate-pair data whose correlation decays with rank, then aggregating empirical FDR, power (1-NDR), and bias across settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a comprehensive evaluation of metabolomics pre-processing steps (BPCA/kNN imputation, quantile/median/RUV normalization) — the paper states its goal was only to benchmark comparisons, not to comprehensively evaluate pre-processing. Reproducible and irreproducible components strongly overlap (lack of separation), which the authors note can push true signals into undetectable regions and distort calibration. The true proportion of reproducible signals (pi_1) is very small — MaRR power drops in these settings, so FDR/power curves alone should not be read as a calibration failure.

skills.search_text: false-discovery-rate-estimation-decoy-search Use when benchmarking DEREPLICATOR+ database search identifications (e.g., on SpectraLibrary or GNPS spectra) and you need a target-decoy FDR estimate to define a significance cutoff for recall/precision measurement. skills.search_text: false-discovery-rate-estimation-from-confidence-scores Use when ranked in silico structure candidates (e.g., CSI:FingerID hits per compound) must be scored for correctness and an FDR estimated for the top k hits, e.g. to pick a confidence-score threshold such as 0.64 for ~10% FDR.
