skills.description: Use when a peak table from CWT peak detection (e.g., AriumMS CE-MS or HILIC-MS runs) contains suspected false-positive features and a shape-based, parameter-light noise criterion is needed before augmentation or mid-level data fusion.
skills.name: false-positive-feature-discrimination
skills.search_text: false-positive-feature-discrimination Use when a peak table from CWT peak detection (e.g., AriumMS CE-MS or HILIC-MS runs) contains suspected false-positive features and a shape-based, parameter-light noise criterion is needed before augmentation or mid-level data fusion. The input is already a curated feature table that has passed a false-positive filter — re-applying the median-entropy cutoff would arbitrarily discard another ~half of the features. You need a blank-control or intensity-threshold-based noise removal rather than a peak-shape criterion, since this filter judges only the disorder of the intensity profile around the peak maximum. Features come from a detector workflow that does not provide the per-point intensity profile around the peak maximum required for the Ju et al. normal/variant point classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Information-entropy false-positive peak filter from AriumMS that discards CWT-detected features whose peak entropy H exceeds the median entropy of all detected peaks, treating high-entropy (disordered) intensity profiles as noise rather than true chromatographic/electrophoretic peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Information-entropy false-positive peak filter from AriumMS that discards CWT-detected features whose peak entropy H exceeds the median entropy of all detected peaks, treating high-entropy (disordered) intensity profiles as noise rather than true chromatographic/electrophoretic peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated feature table that has passed a false-positive filter — re-applying the median-entropy cutoff would arbitrarily discard another ~half of the features. You need a blank-control or intensity-threshold-based noise removal rather than a peak-shape criterion, since this filter judges only the disorder of the intensity profile around the peak maximum. Features come from a detector workflow that does not provide the per-point intensity profile around the peak maximum required for the Ju et al. normal/variant point classification.

skills.description: Use when raw multi-platform untargeted metabolomics data (CE-MS and HILIC-MS of yeast extracts, converted to .mzXML/.mzML) must be filtered of false-positive features after ROI search and feature detection, prior to augmentation.
skills.name: false-positive-filter-application
skills.search_text: false-positive-filter-application Use when raw multi-platform untargeted metabolomics data (CE-MS and HILIC-MS of yeast extracts, converted to .mzXML/.mzML) must be filtered of false-positive features after ROI search and feature detection, prior to augmentation. The goal is single-platform-only untargeted processing with generic tools (XCMS Online, MetaboAnalyst, MetaboAnalystR, MZmine), which focus on one platform and are not designed for augmentation of different separation techniques The input is already a filtered feature table and no ROI search, feature detection, or artifact removal is required The task is to link features detected by two or more methods via MS/MS spectral networking — this is not implemented in AriumMS and is listed as future development Application of the false-positive filter step within the AriumMS pipeline for untargeted metabolomics of multi-platform CE-Orbitrap MS and HILIC-Orbitrap MS data, removing spurious features (artifacts and noise) before mid-level data fusion (augmentation). Correct filtering is validated by reproducing the paper's per-method and augmented target/suspect counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Application of the false-positive filter step within the AriumMS pipeline for untargeted metabolomics of multi-platform CE-Orbitrap MS and HILIC-Orbitrap MS data, removing spurious features (artifacts and noise) before mid-level data fusion (augmentation). Correct filtering is validated by reproducing the paper's per-method and augmented target/suspect counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-platform-only untargeted processing with generic tools (XCMS Online, MetaboAnalyst, MetaboAnalystR, MZmine), which focus on one platform and are not designed for augmentation of different separation techniques The input is already a filtered feature table and no ROI search, feature detection, or artifact removal is required The task is to link features detected by two or more methods via MS/MS spectral networking — this is not implemented in AriumMS and is listed as future development

skills.description: Decision support for selecting an MS1/MS2 mass defect tolerance (mmu range) before MDRB matching of unpredictable metabolites to prototypes, when neither coverage nor false-positive burden can be assumed a priori.
skills.name: false-positive-rate-assessment
skills.search_text: false-positive-rate-assessment Decision support for selecting an MS1/MS2 mass defect tolerance (mmu range) before MDRB matching of unpredictable metabolites to prototypes, when neither coverage nor false-positive burden can be assumed a priori. Metabolites are predictable via Metworks 1.3.0.200 metabolic responses, i.e. they are handled by predictable-pathway matching rather than MDRB's unpredictable-metabolite mass defect bridging. A mass defect range has already been validated for the dataset and only routine MDRB matching is needed — re-running the ±10/±25/±50/±75 sweep is redundant. Only MS2 fragment similarity is available (e.g. MTSF-style single-metabolite matching), since mass defect range optimization requires MS1/MS2 mass defect data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Empirically benchmarks MS1/MS2 mass defect tolerance windows (±10, ±25, ±50, ±75 mmu) in the R-based MDRB metabolite-prototype bridging workflow, selecting the window that best balances pathway coverage, positivity rate, and false-positive bridged pairs for unpredictable metabolite matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Empirically benchmarks MS1/MS2 mass defect tolerance windows (±10, ±25, ±50, ±75 mmu) in the R-based MDRB metabolite-prototype bridging workflow, selecting the window that best balances pathway coverage, positivity rate, and false-positive bridged pairs for unpredictable metabolite matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metabolites are predictable via Metworks 1.3.0.200 metabolic responses, i.e. they are handled by predictable-pathway matching rather than MDRB's unpredictable-metabolite mass defect bridging. A mass defect range has already been validated for the dataset and only routine MDRB matching is needed — re-running the ±10/±25/±50/±75 sweep is redundant. Only MS2 fragment similarity is available (e.g. MTSF-style single-metabolite matching), since mass defect range optimization requires MS1/MS2 mass defect data.

skills.description: Use when evaluating peak-calling quality on nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics peak lists — specifically when you need the fraction of false positive peaks before/after filtering and true positive retention under 'More Restrictive' vs 'Less Restrictive' MZmine 2 settings.
skills.name: false-positive-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: false-positive-rate-quantification Use when evaluating peak-calling quality on nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics peak lists — specifically when you need the fraction of false positive peaks before/after filtering and true positive retention under 'More Restrictive' vs 'Less Restrictive' MZmine 2 settings. The input is already a curated, manually validated feature table with no false-peak population to quantify The peak list was produced by software other than MZmine 2 peak extraction (e.g., centWave or local minimum search alone), where the paper's More/Less Restrictive setting comparison does not directly apply You need to train a new classification model from scratch rather than quantify filter performance of the published models http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Quantifies the false positive proportion of nontargeted LC-MS peak lists generated by MZmine 2 under different extraction stringency (More/Less Restrictive) and measures how machine learning filters (image-based deep neural network, peak group parameter logistic regression) remove false peaks while retaining true positives. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b02983
skills.summary: Quantifies the false positive proportion of nontargeted LC-MS peak lists generated by MZmine 2 under different extraction stringency (More/Less Restrictive) and measures how machine learning filters (image-based deep neural network, peak group parameter logistic regression) remove false peaks while retaining true positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated, manually validated feature table with no false-peak population to quantify The peak list was produced by software other than MZmine 2 peak extraction (e.g., centWave or local minimum search alone), where the paper's More/Less Restrictive setting comparison does not directly apply You need to train a new classification model from scratch rather than quantify filter performance of the published models

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics or GWAS-style analysis yields many correlated raw p-values (e.g., per-metabolite t-tests) and you must control FWER at a fixed alpha (e.g., 0.05) while comparing eigen-analysis-based effective-number-of-tests estimators.
skills.name: family-wise-error-rate-p-value-adjustment
skills.search_text: family-wise-error-rate-p-value-adjustment Use when a metabolomics or GWAS-style analysis yields many correlated raw p-values (e.g., per-metabolite t-tests) and you must control FWER at a fixed alpha (e.g., 0.05) while comparing eigen-analysis-based effective-number-of-tests estimators. Features are independent or uncorrelated so eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation is unnecessary (plain Bonferroni suffices) The goal is FDR (expected false discovery proportion) control rather than family-wise error rate control The test statistics are not per-feature univariate tests with a well-defined correlation structure across features http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Adjust raw p-values from high-dimensional metabolomics tests (e.g., 761 Welch two-sample t-tests of sex vs. metabolite abundances) for family-wise error rate using eigen-analysis-based procedures (PrsCo, Gao, Galwey) enhanced with the distance-correlation-based DisCo P-ad modification from the DisCoPad repository. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Adjust raw p-values from high-dimensional metabolomics tests (e.g., 761 Welch two-sample t-tests of sex vs. metabolite abundances) for family-wise error rate using eigen-analysis-based procedures (PrsCo, Gao, Galwey) enhanced with the distance-correlation-based DisCo P-ad modification from the DisCoPad repository.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are independent or uncorrelated so eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation is unnecessary (plain Bonferroni suffices) The goal is FDR (expected false discovery proportion) control rather than family-wise error rate control The test statistics are not per-feature univariate tests with a well-defined correlation structure across features

skills.description: Use when you need to search one or more MS/MS spectra (a single spectrum or an .mgf file from MZmine or a USI .csv/.tsv list) against indexed GNPS/MassIVE, Metabolomics Workbench, Metabolights, and NORMAN data via the Fast Search API.
skills.name: fast-search-api-query-execution
skills.search_text: fast-search-api-query-execution Use when you need to search one or more MS/MS spectra (a single spectrum or an .mgf file from MZmine or a USI .csv/.tsv list) against indexed GNPS/MassIVE, Metabolomics Workbench, Metabolights, and NORMAN data via the Fast Search API. When you want only a curated domain-specific search (e.g., only bacterial/fungal monoculture data) — the Fast Search hits all indexed public data including samples outside the curated microbeMASST domain, so post-filtering to the domain is required When processing raw LC-MS centroided data or building a feature table — mzmine, not the Fast Search API, is the tool for MS data processing; Fast Search expects already-derived MS/MS spectra in .mgf or USI form When you need deterministic single-run results — Fast Search API calls can fail silently, so a single jobs.py run cannot be treated as complete without re-runs http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Executes a batch MS/MS spectral search against all currently indexed public datasets by calling the Fast Search API, which microbeMASST and the other domainMASSTs use as their spectral matching engine. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Executes a batch MS/MS spectral search against all currently indexed public datasets by calling the Fast Search API, which microbeMASST and the other domainMASSTs use as their spectral matching engine.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you want only a curated domain-specific search (e.g., only bacterial/fungal monoculture data) — the Fast Search hits all indexed public data including samples outside the curated microbeMASST domain, so post-filtering to the domain is required When processing raw LC-MS centroided data or building a feature table — mzmine, not the Fast Search API, is the tool for MS data processing; Fast Search expects already-derived MS/MS spectra in .mgf or USI form When you need deterministic single-run results — Fast Search API calls can fail silently, so a single jobs.py run cannot be treated as complete without re-runs

skills.description: Use when the input is a samples x genes expression matrix (e.g., transcriptomic data from tumoral samples) and the goal is to extract independent, interpretable metagene components that are stable across random ICA initializations.
skills.name: fastica-decomposition
skills.search_text: fastica-decomposition Use when the input is a samples x genes expression matrix (e.g., transcriptomic data from tumoral samples) and the goal is to extract independent, interpretable metagene components that are stable across random ICA initializations. The decomposition does not need to be reproducible across initializations (e.g., a single exploratory decomposition is sufficient and re-computation cost is prohibitive). The input is not an expression/matrix dataset suited to blind source separation (e.g., raw reads or feature tables requiring preprocessing first). Decomposes an omics (e.g., transcriptomic) expression matrix into statistically independent components using fastICA, stabilized across multiple random initializations via icasso-style clustering so that the retained components are reproducible rather than initialization-dependent. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414
skills.summary: Decomposes an omics (e.g., transcriptomic) expression matrix into statistically independent components using fastICA, stabilized across multiple random initializations via icasso-style clustering so that the retained components are reproducible rather than initialization-dependent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The decomposition does not need to be reproducible across initializations (e.g., a single exploratory decomposition is sufficient and re-computation cost is prohibitive). The input is not an expression/matrix dataset suited to blind source separation (e.g., raw reads or feature tables requiring preprocessing first).

skills.description: Use when compressing large numeric arrays from mass-spectrometry chromatograms (e.g., MRM retention times) where delta coding plus bit-level integer encoding (FastPFor) followed by ZSTD must shrink file size for fast web-side rendering.
skills.name: fastpfor-bit-level-integer-compression
skills.search_text: fastpfor-bit-level-integer-compression Use when compressing large numeric arrays from mass-spectrometry chromatograms (e.g., MRM retention times) where delta coding plus bit-level integer encoding (FastPFor) followed by ZSTD must shrink file size for fast web-side rendering. Input arrays are floating-point raw m/z or intensity values that need Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD)/ComboComp m/z pipeline rather than the RT delta + FastPFor scheme Data is not mass-spectrometry chromatogram/spectrum arrays — FastPFor integer coding requires quantized integers, not arbitrary binary blobs A full mzML is required downstream and Aird decoding via AirdSDK is unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Applies the FastPFor bit-level integer codec to delta-coded retention-time integers in MRMPro's Aird-format MRM chromatograms, then wraps the encoded blocks with ZSTD to achieve the >60%/80% size reductions versus vendor and mzML formats. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05685-x
skills.summary: Applies the FastPFor bit-level integer codec to delta-coded retention-time integers in MRMPro's Aird-format MRM chromatograms, then wraps the encoded blocks with ZSTD to achieve the >60%/80% size reductions versus vendor and mzML formats.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input arrays are floating-point raw m/z or intensity values that need Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD)/ComboComp m/z pipeline rather than the RT delta + FastPFor scheme Data is not mass-spectrometry chromatogram/spectrum arrays — FastPFor integer coding requires quantized integers, not arbitrary binary blobs A full mzML is required downstream and Aird decoding via AirdSDK is unavailable

skills.description: Use when you have normalized, natural-isotope-corrected isotopologue intensities (M+0..M+16/M+18) for a fatty acid and need the glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling fraction p (e.g. per-cell p histograms for ACLYkd vs control).
skills.name: fatty-acid-isotopologue-distribution-fitting
skills.search_text: fatty-acid-isotopologue-distribution-fitting Use when you have normalized, natural-isotope-corrected isotopologue intensities (M+0..M+16/M+18) for a fatty acid and need the glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling fraction p (e.g. per-cell p histograms for ACLYkd vs control). When overall substrate usage is very low, such as in the hypoxia/normoxia experiment, where it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction When the input intensities are not corrected for natural isotope abundance (e.g. raw METASPACE isotopologue distributions), as the fitted p would be biased When the goal is absolute rather than relative substrate contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool, since the method cannot quantify pool size http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Fits a 13C binomial model to the isotopologue distribution of a fatty acid (e.g. C16 palmitate, C18 stearate/oleate) after natural isotope abundance correction, to estimate the labelling degree p of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool and an uptake fraction. This is the core quantitative inference step of 13C-SpaceM. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Fits a 13C binomial model to the isotopologue distribution of a fatty acid (e.g. C16 palmitate, C18 stearate/oleate) after natural isotope abundance correction, to estimate the labelling degree p of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool and an uptake fraction. This is the core quantitative inference step of 13C-SpaceM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When overall substrate usage is very low, such as in the hypoxia/normoxia experiment, where it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction When the input intensities are not corrected for natural isotope abundance (e.g. raw METASPACE isotopologue distributions), as the fitted p would be biased When the goal is absolute rather than relative substrate contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool, since the method cannot quantify pool size

skills.description: Use when two TG annotation result sets (e.g., DIATAGeR FDR-filtered output vs MS-DIAL annotations on MS-DIAL alignment feature lists from the same DIA lipidomics run) must be compared by fatty-acyl carbon parity to quantify annotation completeness differences.
skills.name: fatty-acyl-carbon-parity-classification
skills.search_text: fatty-acyl-carbon-parity-classification Use when two TG annotation result sets (e.g., DIATAGeR FDR-filtered output vs MS-DIAL annotations on MS-DIAL alignment feature lists from the same DIA lipidomics run) must be compared by fatty-acyl carbon parity to quantify annotation completeness differences. The lipid class of interest is anything other than triacylglycerols — DIATAGeR explicitly states 'DIATAGeR is for triacylglycerols only' (lipid='TAG'). The inputs are raw instrument files or spectra not exported from MS-DIAL/MZMine in the supported txt, msp, mgf, or mgf_mzmine formats; the pipeline expects MS-DIAL alignment feature lists or the generic feature-list format. The goal is a quantitative abundance comparison rather than identification/annotation completeness — this skill only counts fatty-acyl carbon parity among identifications, not TG signal intensities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Classifies the fatty-acyl composition of annotated triacylglycerol (TG) identifications into even- vs odd-carbon chains and compares the even-carbon fractions between two annotation pipelines (e.g., DIATAGeR vs MS-DIAL) per tissue dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344698
skills.summary: Classifies the fatty-acyl composition of annotated triacylglycerol (TG) identifications into even- vs odd-carbon chains and compares the even-carbon fractions between two annotation pipelines (e.g., DIATAGeR vs MS-DIAL) per tissue dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The lipid class of interest is anything other than triacylglycerols — DIATAGeR explicitly states 'DIATAGeR is for triacylglycerols only' (lipid='TAG'). The inputs are raw instrument files or spectra not exported from MS-DIAL/MZMine in the supported txt, msp, mgf, or mgf_mzmine formats; the pipeline expects MS-DIAL alignment feature lists or the generic feature-list format. The goal is a quantitative abundance comparison rather than identification/annotation completeness — this skill only counts fatty-acyl carbon parity among identifications, not TG signal intensities.

skills.search_text: fatty-acyl-composition-parsing Use when a lipidomics peak table carries fatty acyl compositions (e.g. FA carbon:alkene counts per species) and you need class-level effective carbon number vs. retention time models for Degreaser QC or outlier-identification flagging. skills.when_to_use_negative: Identifications are only sum compositions with no fatty acyl composition to parse (no carbon/alkene counts to extract per class) A lipid class has fewer than the default 5 examples, so the per-class ECN vs. RT regression cannot be fit The goal is fragment-peak annotation of MS2/MS3+ spectral matches (use the LipiDex 2 Lipid Spectral Annotator instead of Degreaser RT modeling)

skills.name: fatty-acyl-peak-ratio-calculation
skills.search_text: fatty-acyl-peak-ratio-calculation Use when MALDI-TOF spectra from macroMS screens (S. cerevisiae colonies or nanoliter droplet arrays) need per-sample fatty acyl ratios, e.g., C16:1/C16 or C16:1/C18:1, to identify colonies or species with shifted fatty acyl profiles. Samples are smaller than 300 μm — the article notes 'For samples smaller than 300 μm, microMS is more effective', so use the microMS workflow instead Input is already a ratio table or aggregate statistics — this skill operates on raw per-sample spectra/peak areas Spectra lack the diagnostic fatty acyl peaks (e.g., no m/z ~253.2/255.2 signal), making the ratio undefined or uninformative Computes per-sample fatty acyl peak-area ratios (e.g., C16:1 at m/z ~253.2 over C16 at m/z ~255.2) from MALDI-TOF mass spectra collected with macroMS, and aggregates them into species- or genotype-level statistics to flag medium-chain fatty acid producers. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.1c00013
skills.summary: Computes per-sample fatty acyl peak-area ratios (e.g., C16:1 at m/z ~253.2 over C16 at m/z ~255.2) from MALDI-TOF mass spectra collected with macroMS, and aggregates them into species- or genotype-level statistics to flag medium-chain fatty acid producers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are smaller than 300 μm — the article notes 'For samples smaller than 300 μm, microMS is more effective', so use the microMS workflow instead Input is already a ratio table or aggregate statistics — this skill operates on raw per-sample spectra/peak areas Spectra lack the diagnostic fatty acyl peaks (e.g., no m/z ~253.2/255.2 signal), making the ratio undefined or uninformative

skills.description: Use when input is a lipidomics table whose row index contains lipid identifiers such as 'PG 18:1/20:1' or RefMet-compliant names, and the goal is to reprocess analyte-level data into per-sample fatty-acid residue counts or filtered residue tables.
skills.name: fatty-acyl-residue-extraction-from-lipid-identifiers
skills.search_text: fatty-acyl-residue-extraction-from-lipid-identifiers Use when input is a lipidomics table whose row index contains lipid identifiers such as 'PG 18:1/20:1' or RefMet-compliant names, and the goal is to reprocess analyte-level data into per-sample fatty-acid residue counts or filtered residue tables. Input is already a residue-count/feature table (rows are residues, not lipid identifiers) — no extraction is needed Lipid identifiers are neither of the form CLASS N:N/M:M/.., mass-isomer bracketed, nor RefMet-compliant — batch-translate IDs with RefMet's online translator first The analysis requires intact individual molecular lipid species rather than aggregated fatty-acyl residues, since this skill deliberately discards the parent-lipid context http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Extracts individual fatty-acyl moieties (e.g. '18:1', '20:4') from complex lipid string identifiers into a residue-count table using the liputils Python module, enabling lipidome-wide tracking of carbon chains independently of their parent lipids. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70259-9
skills.summary: Extracts individual fatty-acyl moieties (e.g. '18:1', '20:4') from complex lipid string identifiers into a residue-count table using the liputils Python module, enabling lipidome-wide tracking of carbon chains independently of their parent lipids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a residue-count/feature table (rows are residues, not lipid identifiers) — no extraction is needed Lipid identifiers are neither of the form CLASS N:N/M:M/.., mass-isomer bracketed, nor RefMet-compliant — batch-translate IDs with RefMet's online translator first The analysis requires intact individual molecular lipid species rather than aggregated fatty-acyl residues, since this skill deliberately discards the parent-lipid context

skills.description: Use when annotating UHPLC-HRMS/MS features (ddMS2-topN, AIF, or targeted MS/MS from Q-Exactive Orbitrap or Agilent/Bruker/SCIEX Q-TOF) to lipid species where identifications should be resolved to fatty acyl constituent level, not just lipid class or precursor mass.
skills.name: fatty-acyl-structural-resolution-matching
skills.search_text: fatty-acyl-structural-resolution-matching Use when annotating UHPLC-HRMS/MS features (ddMS2-topN, AIF, or targeted MS/MS from Q-Exactive Orbitrap or Agilent/Bruker/SCIEX Q-TOF) to lipid species where identifications should be resolved to fatty acyl constituent level, not just lipid class or precursor mass. Input is raw vendor files that have not been feature-picked or converted to .ms2 — LipidMatch requires feature tables and .ms2 MS/MS files, not raw data (Waters files are not supported) The goal is identification by precursor m/z alone or spectral-library search of experimental MS/MS against LipidBlast-type spectra — use a spectral library search instead; LipidMatch matches fragments against in silico libraries with rule-based confirmation Direct identification of lipids outside the library scope without building a custom fragmentation library in Excel first http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Rule-based lipid identification at fatty acyl constituent structural resolution: match experimental MS/MS fragment m/z values against in silico fragmentation libraries in LipidMatch (R), requiring user-selected diagnostic fragments so that lipids are annotated by class and fatty acyl composition rather than precursor m/z alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Rule-based lipid identification at fatty acyl constituent structural resolution: match experimental MS/MS fragment m/z values against in silico fragmentation libraries in LipidMatch (R), requiring user-selected diagnostic fragments so that lipids are annotated by class and fatty acyl composition rather than precursor m/z alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor files that have not been feature-picked or converted to .ms2 — LipidMatch requires feature tables and .ms2 MS/MS files, not raw data (Waters files are not supported) The goal is identification by precursor m/z alone or spectral-library search of experimental MS/MS against LipidBlast-type spectra — use a spectral library search instead; LipidMatch matches fragments against in silico libraries with rule-based confirmation Direct identification of lipids outside the library scope without building a custom fragmentation library in Excel first

skills.description: Use when a draft or Reconstructor-generated SBML model has just been built and must be confirmed functional (nonzero biomass flux) prior to gene essentiality or other perturbation analyses.
skills.name: fba-biomass-objective-validation
skills.search_text: fba-biomass-objective-validation Use when a draft or Reconstructor-generated SBML model has just been built and must be confirmed functional (nonzero biomass flux) prior to gene essentiality or other perturbation analyses. The model is not yet reconstructed or the SBML file fails to load into COBRApy as a valid Model object. The goal is model quality benchmarking (e.g., MEMOTE scores) rather than confirming flux feasibility before perturbation analysis. The model already has published growth/essentiality predictions and only needs comparison rather than revalidation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Validates a newly reconstructed genome-scale metabolic network (GENRE) by running COBRApy flux balance analysis to confirm the model carries nonzero flux to the biomass objective before downstream deletion screening. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Validates a newly reconstructed genome-scale metabolic network (GENRE) by running COBRApy flux balance analysis to confirm the model carries nonzero flux to the biomass objective before downstream deletion screening.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is not yet reconstructed or the SBML file fails to load into COBRApy as a valid Model object. The goal is model quality benchmarking (e.g., MEMOTE scores) rather than confirming flux feasibility before perturbation analysis. The model already has published growth/essentiality predictions and only needs comparison rather than revalidation.

skills.description: Use when you have FBMN annotation results with top-matched compounds and need to quantify how structurally faithful those matches are to the actually analyzed compounds via Tanimoto and MCES scores.
skills.name: fbmn-compound-match-evaluation
skills.search_text: fbmn-compound-match-evaluation Use when you have FBMN annotation results with top-matched compounds and need to quantify how structurally faithful those matches are to the actually analyzed compounds via Tanimoto and MCES scores. When compounds are already confirmed by reference standards or identical spectral match — structural similarity scoring adds nothing for identical structures When input is not structure-annotated (no SMILES available for either the match or the analyzed compound); PubChem Name search fallback may be needed first When evaluating spectral-level match quality (cosine scores) rather than structural plausibility of library annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates the quality of FBMN library matches by computing Tanimoto similarity (Morgan fingerprints, radius 2, 2048 bits) and myopic MCES distances for the top-10 matched compound pairs, classifying pairs as identical or structurally similar when MCES < 4 — the criterion behind the reported 94% identical-or-similar annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0
skills.summary: Evaluates the quality of FBMN library matches by computing Tanimoto similarity (Morgan fingerprints, radius 2, 2048 bits) and myopic MCES distances for the top-10 matched compound pairs, classifying pairs as identical or structurally similar when MCES < 4 — the criterion behind the reported 94% identical-or-similar annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When compounds are already confirmed by reference standards or identical spectral match — structural similarity scoring adds nothing for identical structures When input is not structure-annotated (no SMILES available for either the match or the analyzed compound); PubChem Name search fallback may be needed first When evaluating spectral-level match quality (cosine scores) rather than structural plausibility of library annotations

skills.description: Use when a peak-aligned SCMS feature table (e.g., Geena2-aligned at 10 ppm mass tolerance) must be converted into a ranked list of differentially abundant species between two cell phenotypes, with multiple-testing control.
skills.name: fdr-adjusted-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: fdr-adjusted-statistical-testing Use when a peak-aligned SCMS feature table (e.g., Geena2-aligned at 10 ppm mass tolerance) must be converted into a ranked list of differentially abundant species between two cell phenotypes, with multiple-testing control. The goal is cell phenotype classification rather than differential abundance testing — use the MetaPhenotype meta-learning model instead, since PCA alone cannot discriminate phenotypically similar cells such as IGR39/IGR37 The input is raw, unaligned single-cell peak lists — peak alignment (Geena2, 10 ppm mass tolerance), noise/background subtraction, TIC normalization, and missing-value removal must precede group-wise statistical testing Sample sizes per group are too small for stable p-value estimation and FDR correction to be meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute per-species log2 fold changes and FDR-adjusted p-values from peak-aligned, TIC-normalized single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics feature tables, then apply dual thresholds (fold change ≥ 2.0, FDR ≤ 0.05) to nominate lipid biomarker candidates (TG, Cer, SM, PG, PE) between primary and metastatic melanoma cells. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Compute per-species log2 fold changes and FDR-adjusted p-values from peak-aligned, TIC-normalized single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics feature tables, then apply dual thresholds (fold change ≥ 2.0, FDR ≤ 0.05) to nominate lipid biomarker candidates (TG, Cer, SM, PG, PE) between primary and metastatic melanoma cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell phenotype classification rather than differential abundance testing — use the MetaPhenotype meta-learning model instead, since PCA alone cannot discriminate phenotypically similar cells such as IGR39/IGR37 The input is raw, unaligned single-cell peak lists — peak alignment (Geena2, 10 ppm mass tolerance), noise/background subtraction, TIC normalization, and missing-value removal must precede group-wise statistical testing Sample sizes per group are too small for stable p-value estimation and FDR correction to be meaningful

skills.description: Use when comparing FDR-controlled metabolite annotation methods (e.g., ML vs rule-based scorers) across imaging MS datasets, or when evaluating target/decoy ranking quality via average precision.
skills.name: fdr-controlled-metabolite-annotation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: fdr-controlled-metabolite-annotation-benchmarking Use when comparing FDR-controlled metabolite annotation methods (e.g., ML vs rule-based scorers) across imaging MS datasets, or when evaluating target/decoy ranking quality via average precision. The goal is to evaluate database choice (e.g., CoreMetabolome vs general databases) rather than ranking-model comparison — MAP against databases is a related but distinct analysis Input datasets are QTOF-based — such datasets are underrepresented in the METASPACE-ML model due to lack of publicly available data, making evaluation unreliable The task is single-dataset annotation rather than method benchmarking across a testing corpus — use the METASPACE engine directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks METASPACE-ML, a machine-learning metabolite annotation method for imaging mass spectrometry, against the rule-based MSM scorer by ranking target-versus-decoy ion candidates and computing mean average precision (MAP) per sample type. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-52213-9
skills.summary: Benchmarks METASPACE-ML, a machine-learning metabolite annotation method for imaging mass spectrometry, against the rule-based MSM scorer by ranking target-versus-decoy ion candidates and computing mean average precision (MAP) per sample type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate database choice (e.g., CoreMetabolome vs general databases) rather than ranking-model comparison — MAP against databases is a related but distinct analysis Input datasets are QTOF-based — such datasets are underrepresented in the METASPACE-ML model due to lack of publicly available data, making evaluation unreliable The task is single-dataset annotation rather than method benchmarking across a testing corpus — use the METASPACE engine directly instead

skills.description: Use when filtering GC-MS deconvoluted spectral matches (with per-match cosine similarity and balance score annotations) and you need to choose joint thresholds that minimize the FDR of the top annotation.
skills.name: fdr-estimation-of-spectral-annotations
skills.search_text: fdr-estimation-of-spectral-annotations Use when filtering GC-MS deconvoluted spectral matches (with per-match cosine similarity and balance score annotations) and you need to choose joint thresholds that minimize the FDR of the top annotation. Input is raw GC-MS data that has not yet been auto-deconvolved by MSHub (no cosine/balance score annotations exist to filter on) The analysis goal is deconvolution itself (non-negative matrix factorization of fragmentation patterns) rather than post-deconvolution annotation filtering Matches lack the balance score annotation, since neither the joint threshold nor the conservative >80% filter can be evaluated Estimates the false discovery rate of top-match spectral annotations from MSHub/GNPS GC-MS auto-deconvolution output by jointly applying cosine similarity and balance score thresholds (cosine >0.9 with balance >60%; conservative balance >80%), as benchmarked in the Figure 1m,n test dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Estimates the false discovery rate of top-match spectral annotations from MSHub/GNPS GC-MS auto-deconvolution output by jointly applying cosine similarity and balance score thresholds (cosine >0.9 with balance >60%; conservative balance >80%), as benchmarked in the Figure 1m,n test dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw GC-MS data that has not yet been auto-deconvolved by MSHub (no cosine/balance score annotations exist to filter on) The analysis goal is deconvolution itself (non-negative matrix factorization of fragmentation patterns) rather than post-deconvolution annotation filtering Matches lack the balance score annotation, since neither the joint threshold nor the conservative >80% filter can be evaluated

skills.description: Use when assigning significance categories to metabolites whose many curve-fitted ROI peaks (SRRMs) each get a p-value, preventing uncorrected p<0.05 calls from inflating identifications in NMR metabolomics.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-comparison-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-comparison-correction Use when assigning significance categories to metabolites whose many curve-fitted ROI peaks (SRRMs) each get a p-value, preventing uncorrected p<0.05 calls from inflating identifications in NMR metabolomics. The analysis is a single pre-registered comparison with one ROI per metabolite, so no multiplicity across SRRMs/ROIs exists to correct The goal is validating the accuracy of user-defined ROIs or absolute quantification — the article states ROIAL-NMR was not built to test ROI accuracy and absolute quantification is not its aim Input is raw FID/spectral data without curve-fitted ROI p-values; FDR correction operates on ROI-level significance calls, not on the spectra directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 False-discovery-rate (FDR) correction applied to repeated significance testing across user-defined NMR spectral ROIs and their SRRMs in ROIAL-NMR, so that metabolites remain flagged as FDR-significant when at least one of their SRRMs passes p<0.05 after correction. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/nbm.70131
skills.summary: False-discovery-rate (FDR) correction applied to repeated significance testing across user-defined NMR spectral ROIs and their SRRMs in ROIAL-NMR, so that metabolites remain flagged as FDR-significant when at least one of their SRRMs passes p<0.05 after correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is a single pre-registered comparison with one ROI per metabolite, so no multiplicity across SRRMs/ROIs exists to correct The goal is validating the accuracy of user-defined ROIs or absolute quantification — the article states ROIAL-NMR was not built to test ROI accuracy and absolute quantification is not its aim Input is raw FID/spectral data without curve-fitted ROI p-values; FDR correction operates on ROI-level significance calls, not on the spectra directly

skills.description: Use when thousands of pathway-level importance scores (VIP, MB-VIP, RGCCA loadings, or sparse-DIABLO bootstrap non-zero-loading statistics) must be tested against permutation nulls and converted into pathway detection calls with controlled false discovery rate.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when thousands of pathway-level importance scores (VIP, MB-VIP, RGCCA loadings, or sparse-DIABLO bootstrap non-zero-loading statistics) must be tested against permutation nulls and converted into pathway detection calls with controlled false discovery rate. The analysis involves a single pre-specified hypothesis test with no multiplicity across pathways, so FDR correction is unnecessary The data are real (non-semi-synthetic) datasets with no known target pathway or ground-truth labels, so confusion-matrix AUC cannot be computed The question is conventional ORA/GSEA-style enrichment of differential molecules rather than detection of an enriched pathway from predictive model importance statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to pathway importance statistics derived from permutation-based null distributions (10,000 permutations) when assessing whether PathIntegrate (VIP/MB-VIP) and DIABLO-based pathway models truly detect an enriched target pathway in semi-synthetic multi-omics simulations. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to pathway importance statistics derived from permutation-based null distributions (10,000 permutations) when assessing whether PathIntegrate (VIP/MB-VIP) and DIABLO-based pathway models truly detect an enriched target pathway in semi-synthetic multi-omics simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis involves a single pre-specified hypothesis test with no multiplicity across pathways, so FDR correction is unnecessary The data are real (non-semi-synthetic) datasets with no known target pathway or ground-truth labels, so confusion-matrix AUC cannot be computed The question is conventional ORA/GSEA-style enrichment of differential molecules rather than detection of an enriched pathway from predictive model importance statistics

skills.description: Use when many features are tested independently (one test per metabolomic feature) and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted — e.g. reproducing Fig. 3f-style significant-feature counts at FDR <= 0.2 on batch-corrected ST000868 data.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when many features are tested independently (one test per metabolomic feature) and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted — e.g. reproducing Fig. 3f-style significant-feature counts at FDR <= 0.2 on batch-corrected ST000868 data. Input is still raw LC/MS data (NetCDF/mzML files) — batch-aware preprocessing (cdf.to.ftr pipeline) must run first before any feature-level testing Post-hoc batch correction would be used to 'fix' misaligned feature tables — article notes such methods only adjust signal intensity and cannot correct peak alignment errors Only a single hypothesis test is being run, where no multiple-testing adjustment is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over per-feature two-sample t-test p-values in LC/MS metabolomics feature tables, counting significant features at FDR <= 0.2 to compare preprocessing/batch-correction strategies (two-stage apLCMS vs. traditional apLCMS/XCMS with ComBat or WaveICA). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over per-feature two-sample t-test p-values in LC/MS metabolomics feature tables, counting significant features at FDR <= 0.2 to compare preprocessing/batch-correction strategies (two-stage apLCMS vs. traditional apLCMS/XCMS with ComBat or WaveICA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw LC/MS data (NetCDF/mzML files) — batch-aware preprocessing (cdf.to.ftr pipeline) must run first before any feature-level testing Post-hoc batch correction would be used to 'fix' misaligned feature tables — article notes such methods only adjust signal intensity and cannot correct peak alignment errors Only a single hypothesis test is being run, where no multiple-testing adjustment is needed

skills.description: Use when testing hundreds to thousands of omics features (metabolomics peaks, RNA-seq genes) for group differences in BiomiX-style pipelines and raw p-values must be FDR-corrected before filtering at p.adj thresholds.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when testing hundreds to thousands of omics features (metabolomics peaks, RNA-seq genes) for group differences in BiomiX-style pipelines and raw p-values must be FDR-corrected before filtering at p.adj thresholds. Input is already a table of adjusted p-values or pre-filtered significant hits — re-correcting would be invalid Few (< ~10) hypothesis tests where family-wise correction (e.g. Bonferroni) is more appropriate than FDR Raw metabolomics peak or RNA-seq count matrices that have not yet been tested — FDR correction is downstream of the Wilcoxon/DESeq2 test step http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) correction to raw p-values from high-throughput omics tests — Wilcoxon tests on metabolomics peaks and DESeq2/Limma tests on transcriptomics counts — so that thousands of simultaneous hypotheses can be filtered at controlled adjusted-p thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Apply False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) correction to raw p-values from high-throughput omics tests — Wilcoxon tests on metabolomics peaks and DESeq2/Limma tests on transcriptomics counts — so that thousands of simultaneous hypotheses can be filtered at controlled adjusted-p thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a table of adjusted p-values or pre-filtered significant hits — re-correcting would be invalid Few (< ~10) hypothesis tests where family-wise correction (e.g. Bonferroni) is more appropriate than FDR Raw metabolomics peak or RNA-seq count matrices that have not yet been tested — FDR correction is downstream of the Wilcoxon/DESeq2 test step

skills.description: Use when a between-group abundance test on LC-MS feature tables (e.g. 94 samples, 14 lamprey tissues, negative ion mode) yields raw per-feature P values across thousands of mass features, and a significance cutoff must control the false-discovery rate before filtering.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when a between-group abundance test on LC-MS feature tables (e.g. 94 samples, 14 lamprey tissues, negative ion mode) yields raw per-feature P values across thousands of mass features, and a significance cutoff must control the false-discovery rate before filtering. Only a handful of hypothesis tests are performed — the correction would be unnecessary and overly conservative The downstream claim requires per-feature family-wise (e.g. Bonferroni) control rather than false-discovery-rate control The input is raw spectrometer output (mzML/NetCDF) rather than a quantified feature table with per-feature test statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3395 Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment of per-feature P values from metabolomics between-group tests, applied inside MetaboReport's statistical-analysis module before significance cutoffs (e.g. FDR P<0.001) so that thousands of simultaneously tested LC-MS mass features do not yield spurious hits. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment of per-feature P values from metabolomics between-group tests, applied inside MetaboReport's statistical-analysis module before significance cutoffs (e.g. FDR P<0.001) so that thousands of simultaneously tested LC-MS mass features do not yield spurious hits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a handful of hypothesis tests are performed — the correction would be unnecessary and overly conservative The downstream claim requires per-feature family-wise (e.g. Bonferroni) control rather than false-discovery-rate control The input is raw spectrometer output (mzML/NetCDF) rather than a quantified feature table with per-feature test statistics

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics or multi-omics analysis yields thousands of pairwise correlation P-values (e.g., metabolite-protein Spearman correlations across ~202 shared samples) and edges must be called at FDR < 0.05 with an effect-size cutoff such as |r| > 0.3.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when a metabolomics or multi-omics analysis yields thousands of pairwise correlation P-values (e.g., metabolite-protein Spearman correlations across ~202 shared samples) and edges must be called at FDR < 0.05 with an effect-size cutoff such as |r| > 0.3. The analysis performs a single hypothesis test or a small pre-specified comparison set, where per-test P-value thresholds suffice Raw data have not yet been filtered (samples with >90% zeros, variables with >40% zeros) or normalized to counts per million, so correlation P-values are computed on unreliable zero-inflated variables The goal is building weighted co-occurrence networks without an explicit edge-significance criterion rather than a thresholded correlation network http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Apply false discovery rate (FDR) correction to the large family of pairwise P-values generated in correlation-based network analysis, so that qualified edges (FDR < 0.05, |r| > 0.3) can be selected at a controlled error rate. In iMAP this step underpins the network module built on the 308-sample IBD stool proteomics/metabolomics dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: Apply false discovery rate (FDR) correction to the large family of pairwise P-values generated in correlation-based network analysis, so that qualified edges (FDR < 0.05, |r| > 0.3) can be selected at a controlled error rate. In iMAP this step underpins the network module built on the 308-sample IBD stool proteomics/metabolomics dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis performs a single hypothesis test or a small pre-specified comparison set, where per-test P-value thresholds suffice Raw data have not yet been filtered (samples with >90% zeros, variables with >40% zeros) or normalized to counts per million, so correlation P-values are computed on unreliable zero-inflated variables The goal is building weighted co-occurrence networks without an explicit edge-significance criterion rather than a thresholded correlation network

skills.description: Use when many gene sets (e.g., GO/KEGG terms) have been tested per ICA metagene Sk vector via hypergeometric overrepresentation or GSEA and p-values must be corrected before calling enriched sets.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when many gene sets (e.g., GO/KEGG terms) have been tested per ICA metagene Sk vector via hypergeometric overrepresentation or GSEA and p-values must be corrected before calling enriched sets. Only one gene set or one hypothesis is being tested — no family-wise or FDR adjustment is needed The p-values come from different metagenes but the analysis goal is component-wise exploration rather than a single corrected call list; correcting across all components and all gene sets at once may be overly conservative The input is a ranked gene list that has not yet been subjected to any enrichment test — FDR correction applies to test p-values, not to rankings directly http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction to the p-values produced by functional enrichment testing (hypergeometric overrepresentation and GSEA) of ICA metagene (Sk) gene lists, so that enriched gene sets are called at a controlled false discovery rate across many simultaneous gene-set tests. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction to the p-values produced by functional enrichment testing (hypergeometric overrepresentation and GSEA) of ICA metagene (Sk) gene lists, so that enriched gene sets are called at a controlled false discovery rate across many simultaneous gene-set tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one gene set or one hypothesis is being tested — no family-wise or FDR adjustment is needed The p-values come from different metagenes but the analysis goal is component-wise exploration rather than a single corrected call list; correcting across all components and all gene sets at once may be overly conservative The input is a ranked gene list that has not yet been subjected to any enrichment test — FDR correction applies to test p-values, not to rankings directly

skills.description: Use when a lipidomic dataset is compared across two or more experimental groups with a test per lipid feature (t-test/ANOVA), and corrected p-values plus significance asterisks are needed.
skills.name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when a lipidomic dataset is compared across two or more experimental groups with a test per lipid feature (t-test/ANOVA), and corrected p-values plus significance asterisks are needed. Only a single pre-specified hypothesis test is planned, so family-wise/FDR multiplicity correction is unnecessary The analysis requires multivariate statistics or biomarker identification rather than per-feature univariate group comparisons (use LipidOne 2.0's dedicated multivariate/biomarker functions instead) The data violate the equal-variance Student's t-test assumption and a Welch-type or non-parametric test is required instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3365 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over the family of per-lipid significance tests (Student's t-test or one-way ANOVA) that underlies LipidOne 2.0's bar chart function, mapping corrected p-values to one, two, or three asterisk annotations at < .05, < .01, and < .001 thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction over the family of per-lipid significance tests (Student's t-test or one-way ANOVA) that underlies LipidOne 2.0's bar chart function, mapping corrected p-values to one, two, or three asterisk annotations at < .05, < .01, and < .001 thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single pre-specified hypothesis test is planned, so family-wise/FDR multiplicity correction is unnecessary The analysis requires multivariate statistics or biomarker identification rather than per-feature univariate group comparisons (use LipidOne 2.0's dedicated multivariate/biomarker functions instead) The data violate the equal-variance Student's t-test assumption and a Welch-type or non-parametric test is required instead

Input is a raw unfiltered intensity matrix where no significance filter (e.g. permutation p-value < 0.01) has yet been applied — first run mb_vip_permtest to select significant features Goal is structural clustering based on retention time and m/z adduct/isotopologue patterns rather than co-variance of intensities — use the get_structural_clusters step instead Data are single-assay only where no multi-assay integration or cross-assay linking is intended; MAMSI is designed for multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics Clusters statistically significant LC-MS features by their intensity correlation across samples using agglomerative hierarchical clustering with complete linkage on a |1−rὢ| dissimilarity matrix, with the cluster count chosen by the maximum mean silhouette score. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01327
skills.summary: Clusters statistically significant LC-MS features by their intensity correlation across samples using agglomerative hierarchical clustering with complete linkage on a |1−rὢ| dissimilarity matrix, with the cluster count chosen by the maximum mean silhouette score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw unfiltered intensity matrix where no significance filter (e.g. permutation p-value < 0.01) has yet been applied — first run mb_vip_permtest to select significant features Goal is structural clustering based on retention time and m/z adduct/isotopologue patterns rather than co-variance of intensities — use the get_structural_clusters step instead Data are single-assay only where no multi-assay integration or cross-assay linking is intended; MAMSI is designed for multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics

skills.description: Use when raw mzML/mzXML feature tables must be quality-filtered and the reported before/after feature counts (e.g. dendroides 1,078→784) need to be reproduced or audited.
skills.name: feature-count-reconciliation-across-datasets
skills.search_text: feature-count-reconciliation-across-datasets Use when raw mzML/mzXML feature tables must be quality-filtered and the reported before/after feature counts (e.g. dendroides 1,078→784) need to be reproduced or audited. The input is already a post-filter feature table from the deposited data package with no raw mzML/mzXML spectra to re-filter The goal is candidate-level filtering after ZODIAC scoring (e.g. ZODIAC score >= 0.999, >= 95% explained intensity) rather than preprocessing-level low-quality feature removal The datasets are not among the five ZODIAC evaluation datasets, so no published before/after counts exist for validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reconstructs the low-quality MS/MS feature filtering step of the ZODIAC preprocessing workflow (OpenMS peak merging, fragment-peak threshold, SIRIUS fragmentation-tree intensity coverage) and reconciles the resulting before/after feature counts against the five published datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Reconstructs the low-quality MS/MS feature filtering step of the ZODIAC preprocessing workflow (OpenMS peak merging, fragment-peak threshold, SIRIUS fragmentation-tree intensity coverage) and reconciles the resulting before/after feature counts against the five published datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a post-filter feature table from the deposited data package with no raw mzML/mzXML spectra to re-filter The goal is candidate-level filtering after ZODIAC scoring (e.g. ZODIAC score >= 0.999, >= 95% explained intensity) rather than preprocessing-level low-quality feature removal The datasets are not among the five ZODIAC evaluation datasets, so no published before/after counts exist for validation

skills.summary: Track per-extract feature counts as Inventa's intensity-based and quantile-based filters progressively reduce the MZmine feature table, verifying expected reductions such as 727 → 104 → 26 features for the Pristimera indica roots extract.

skills.search_text: feature-count-reproducibility-assessment Use when the same raw LC-MS dataset (e.g., pooled human plasma mzML files) must be processed by two or more tools to compare feature counts and cross-tool feature correspondence, or to benchmark a new processing tool against XCMS/MZmine. Input is already a processed feature table rather than raw centroided mzML files — re-processing to compare tool behavior is not possible The goal is metabolite annotation or pathway analysis rather than comparing feature detection consistency across tools Data are low-resolution or from non-Orbitrap platforms without re-optimized settings (asari, the benchmarked tool, was mostly tested on Orbitrap platforms and does not work with low-resolution data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies how consistently different LC-MS data processing tools (e.g., XCMS, MZmine, asari) detect and correspond features on the same dataset, by producing parallel feature tables and comparing feature counts and match rates. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Quantifies how consistently different LC-MS data processing tools (e.g., XCMS, MZmine, asari) detect and correspond features on the same dataset, by producing parallel feature tables and comparing feature counts and match rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table rather than raw centroided mzML files — re-processing to compare tool behavior is not possible The goal is metabolite annotation or pathway analysis rather than comparing feature detection consistency across tools Data are low-resolution or from non-Orbitrap platforms without re-optimized settings (asari, the benchmarked tool, was mostly tested on Orbitrap platforms and does not work with low-resolution data)

skills.name: feature-detection-in-mzml-acquisitions
skills.search_text: feature-detection-in-mzml-acquisitions Use when raw Thermo .raw or .mzML flow injection MSn files must be turned into per-file feature/compound detections in mzmine, e.g. to count molecules detected in positive-only, negative-only, or both ionization modes. skills.summary: Mass-spectrometry feature detection within mzML/.raw flow-injection acquisitions (converted by ThermoRawFileParser) using mzmine to generate per-file compound feature lists that feed MSnLib's ionization-mode coverage statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature table or peak list — re-running feature detection would duplicate work and risk inconsistent identifiers. The goal is direct compound identification from MS/MS spectra without per-file feature counting across ionization modes. Vendor .raw files are required without conversion and no ThermoRawFileParser (or mzmine-compatible) reader is available.

skills.description: Use when you have replicate-comparison output — replicated feature peak lists from technical replicate mzML runs — and need to collapse them into a single list of unique MS features for downstream bioactivity integration.
skills.name: feature-error-range-overlap-clustering
skills.search_text: feature-error-range-overlap-clustering Use when you have replicate-comparison output — replicated feature peak lists from technical replicate mzML runs — and need to collapse them into a single list of unique MS features for downstream bioactivity integration. Input is a single unreplicated MS run — replicate comparison and basketing require replicated feature peak lists and cannot be applied to one-shot data Input is already a processed MZmine 2 or GNPS feature table — those platforms' outputs are imported directly via `npanalyst import -t MZmine` or `-t GNPS` and do not need R-tree basketing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Basket replicated MS features in NP Analyst by building connected-component graphs from m/z features with overlapping error ranges across rt and m/z dimensions using an R-tree spatial index, then averaging each component into a single unique feature. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Basket replicated MS features in NP Analyst by building connected-component graphs from m/z features with overlapping error ranges across rt and m/z dimensions using an R-tree spatial index, then averaging each component into a single unique feature.
