skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how faithfully an HRMS peak-detection pipeline recovers known analytes, by matching extracted chromatographic peaks against a spiked-chemical list of known composition (e.g., 398 MS-amenable chemicals in ENTACT mixtures).
skills.name: feature-extraction-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: feature-extraction-accuracy-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify how faithfully an HRMS peak-detection pipeline recovers known analytes, by matching extracted chromatographic peaks against a spiked-chemical list of known composition (e.g., 398 MS-amenable chemicals in ENTACT mixtures). Samples are of unknown composition — there is no known spiked-chemical list to match against, so recovered-fraction accuracy cannot be computed The goal is cross-tool feature agreement rather than known-analyte recovery; for that, MSS reports ~52% overlap with MSDIAL (52 ± 5%) and XCMS (52 ± 6%) instead Input is already a processed feature table — re-running get_scans/peak_pick would be redundant; benchmarking requires raw .mzML scans http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks an HRMS feature-extraction workflow's reliability by running it on samples of known composition (EPA ENTACT mixed chemical standards #505, #506, #508) and computing the fraction of known peaks recovered, following the Mass-Suite (MSS) validation design that achieved 99.5% feature-extraction accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00741-9
skills.summary: Benchmarks an HRMS feature-extraction workflow's reliability by running it on samples of known composition (EPA ENTACT mixed chemical standards #505, #506, #508) and computing the fraction of known peaks recovered, following the Mass-Suite (MSS) validation design that achieved 99.5% feature-extraction accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are of unknown composition — there is no known spiked-chemical list to match against, so recovered-fraction accuracy cannot be computed The goal is cross-tool feature agreement rather than known-analyte recovery; for that, MSS reports ~52% overlap with MSDIAL (52 ± 5%) and XCMS (52 ± 6%) instead Input is already a processed feature table — re-running get_scans/peak_pick would be redundant; benchmarking requires raw .mzML scans

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data (any sample type, acquisition mode, or MS vendor) must be processed for feature extraction but default tool parameters would under-extract true positive metabolic features.
skills.name: feature-extraction-parameter-translation
skills.search_text: feature-extraction-parameter-translation Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data (any sample type, acquisition mode, or MS vendor) must be processed for feature extraction but default tool parameters would under-extract true positive metabolic features. Input is already a feature table produced by a prior feature extraction run — Paramounter measures parameters from raw LC-MS data before extraction, not from processed feature tables. The downstream feature extraction program is not among the software-specific parameter mappings Paramounter supports (article context centers on MS-DIAL-based feature extraction and XCMS CentWave mzdiff). http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Automatically measure universal LC-MS feature-extraction parameters (mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, instrumental shift) directly from raw metabolomics data using the R package Paramounter, then translate them into software-specific parameters (e.g. MS-DIAL) so feature extraction runs in a transparent 'white box' instead of relying on vendor defaults. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c04758
skills.summary: Automatically measure universal LC-MS feature-extraction parameters (mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, instrumental shift) directly from raw metabolomics data using the R package Paramounter, then translate them into software-specific parameters (e.g. MS-DIAL) so feature extraction runs in a transparent 'white box' instead of relying on vendor defaults.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table produced by a prior feature extraction run — Paramounter measures parameters from raw LC-MS data before extraction, not from processed feature tables. The downstream feature extraction program is not among the software-specific parameter mappings Paramounter supports (article context centers on MS-DIAL-based feature extraction and XCMS CentWave mzdiff).

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how relaxing peak-picking thresholds (mass tolerance, S/N) changes JPA-PP vs JPA-MR feature counts and the proportion of features with acceptable chromatographic peak shapes.
skills.name: feature-fidelity-rate-comparison
skills.search_text: feature-fidelity-rate-comparison Use when you need to quantify how relaxing peak-picking thresholds (mass tolerance, S/N) changes JPA-PP vs JPA-MR feature counts and the proportion of features with acceptable chromatographic peak shapes. When processing full-scan or DIA data sets — find.level3features (MS2 recognition / MR) must not be used in those cases per the JPA manual When the input is already an aligned feature table rather than raw mzXML files — JPA requires per-file CSV tables for custom input and raw mzXML for XCMS.featureTable() When the goal is absolute feature quantification rather than parameter-sensitivity comparison of fidelity rates http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reprocesses the same LC-MS mzXML data through the JPA pipeline twice — once with default parameters (ppm=10, snthresh=6) and once with tolerant thresholds (ppm=30, S/N=3) — to quantify how peak-picking (PP) versus MS2-recognition (MR) feature counts and chromatographic peak-shape fidelity rates shift between parameter settings. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212
skills.summary: Reprocesses the same LC-MS mzXML data through the JPA pipeline twice — once with default parameters (ppm=10, snthresh=6) and once with tolerant thresholds (ppm=30, S/N=3) — to quantify how peak-picking (PP) versus MS2-recognition (MR) feature counts and chromatographic peak-shape fidelity rates shift between parameter settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When processing full-scan or DIA data sets — find.level3features (MS2 recognition / MR) must not be used in those cases per the JPA manual When the input is already an aligned feature table rather than raw mzXML files — JPA requires per-file CSV tables for custom input and raw mzXML for XCMS.featureTable() When the goal is absolute feature quantification rather than parameter-sensitivity comparison of fidelity rates

skills.description: Use when you must establish how small a reference feature list can be (relative to a full common-feature list) before retention time shift computation and alignment accuracy of LC-HRMS chromatograms degrade.
skills.name: feature-group-count-threshold-analysis
skills.search_text: feature-group-count-threshold-analysis Use when you must establish how small a reference feature list can be (relative to a full common-feature list) before retention time shift computation and alignment accuracy of LC-HRMS chromatograms degrade. The task is a single routine alignment of LC-HRMS datafiles with a complete reference feature list — no threshold estimation is needed Input is a data matrix of already-aligned features rather than a reference feature list plus target chromatograms The reference and target chromatograms share too few common feature groups to support progressive subsampling (the experiment depends on a large starting list such as 505 groups) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Determines the minimum number of common feature groups (m/z and retention time entries) a reference feature list must contain for MetMatch to reliably compute the retention time (Rt) shift function and maintain LC-HRMS alignment accuracy, via progressive subsampling with repeated alignment runs. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: Determines the minimum number of common feature groups (m/z and retention time entries) a reference feature list must contain for MetMatch to reliably compute the retention time (Rt) shift function and maintain LC-HRMS alignment accuracy, via progressive subsampling with repeated alignment runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a single routine alignment of LC-HRMS datafiles with a complete reference feature list — no threshold estimation is needed Input is a data matrix of already-aligned features rather than a reference feature list plus target chromatograms The reference and target chromatograms share too few common feature groups to support progressive subsampling (the experiment depends on a large starting list such as 505 groups)

skills.description: Use when you need to QC a DeepRTAlign alignment run — i.e., estimate alignment FDR from decoy alignments in information_all.csv and reproduce the post-QC information_target.csv.
skills.name: feature-group-quality-control
skills.search_text: feature-group-quality-control Use when you need to QC a DeepRTAlign alignment run — i.e., estimate alignment FDR from decoy alignments in information_all.csv and reproduce the post-QC information_target.csv. The input is already the post-QC information_target.csv and no decoy alignments (information_all.csv) were kept because keep_temp was 0 — decoy FDR cannot be estimated from target results alone The task is identification-based peptide/protein FDR estimation from PSM scores rather than alignment-level QC of MS feature groups You need per-feature intensity normalization rather than alignment quality control — QC filters groups but does not correct quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimates the false discovery rate of DeepRTAlign feature-group alignments using the tool's decoy-based quality control design: within each m/z bin one aligned group is treated as target and its decoy counterpart is built, and FDR is computed as the decoy/target alignment count ratio at each score cutoff (default threshold 0.01). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Estimates the false discovery rate of DeepRTAlign feature-group alignments using the tool's decoy-based quality control design: within each m/z bin one aligned group is treated as target and its decoy counterpart is built, and FDR is computed as the decoy/target alignment count ratio at each score cutoff (default threshold 0.01).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already the post-QC information_target.csv and no decoy alignments (information_all.csv) were kept because keep_temp was 0 — decoy FDR cannot be estimated from target results alone The task is identification-based peptide/protein FDR estimation from PSM scores rather than alignment-level QC of MS feature groups You need per-feature intensity normalization rather than alignment quality control — QC filters groups but does not correct quantification

skills.description: Use when LC-HRMS features must be grouped across replicate sample analyses (e.g. patRoonData 'standard-X'/'solvent-X' triplicate injections) or when feature-group outputs from OpenMS, XCMS and enviPick must be compared and combined on the same dataset.
skills.name: feature-grouping-across-samples
skills.search_text: feature-grouping-across-samples Use when LC-HRMS features must be grouped across replicate sample analyses (e.g. patRoonData 'standard-X'/'solvent-X' triplicate injections) or when feature-group outputs from OpenMS, XCMS and enviPick must be compared and combined on the same dataset. Input is already a grouped feature table — grouping across samples has already been performed Data are not replicate analyses of related samples (e.g. single-injection runs with no cross-sample equivalence to establish) Goal is annotation (formula/compound assignment) rather than feature-level comparison across algorithms http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 patRoon's harmonized feature grouping step: features with unique chromatographic and mass spectral properties are extracted per algorithm (OpenMS, XCMS, enviPick) and features considered equivalent across sample analyses (e.g. standard-X/solvent-X triplicates) are grouped, enabling algorithm comparison and consensus building. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00477-w
skills.summary: patRoon's harmonized feature grouping step: features with unique chromatographic and mass spectral properties are extracted per algorithm (OpenMS, XCMS, enviPick) and features considered equivalent across sample analyses (e.g. standard-X/solvent-X triplicates) are grouped, enabling algorithm comparison and consensus building.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a grouped feature table — grouping across samples has already been performed Data are not replicate analyses of related samples (e.g. single-injection runs with no cross-sample equivalence to establish) Goal is annotation (formula/compound assignment) rather than feature-level comparison across algorithms

skills.description: Use when large collections of high-resolution MS/MS spectra (mzML, mzXML, or MGF peak files) must be converted into compact numeric vectors suitable for approximate similarity searching or indexing without exhaustive pairwise comparisons.
skills.name: feature-hashing-spectrum-vectorization
skills.search_text: feature-hashing-spectrum-vectorization Use when large collections of high-resolution MS/MS spectra (mzML, mzXML, or MGF peak files) must be converted into compact numeric vectors suitable for approximate similarity searching or indexing without exhaustive pairwise comparisons. Input is not spectrum data but an already-vectorized feature table or identification result — vectorization is redundant Metabolomics or top-down data where the default proteomics preprocessing (min 5 peaks, 250 m/z range, 101–500 m/z window) does not apply; these falcon settings must be reduced/adjusted first Exact cosine distances between every spectrum pair are required — feature hashing only approximates the original cosine similarity http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts high-resolution MS/MS spectra into fixed-length low-dimensional vectors by binning fragment m/z values and applying MurmurHash3 feature hashing, so that cosine similarity between the original spectra is approximately conserved for fast nearest-neighbor searching in falcon. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Converts high-resolution MS/MS spectra into fixed-length low-dimensional vectors by binning fragment m/z values and applying MurmurHash3 feature hashing, so that cosine similarity between the original spectra is approximately conserved for fast nearest-neighbor searching in falcon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not spectrum data but an already-vectorized feature table or identification result — vectorization is redundant Metabolomics or top-down data where the default proteomics preprocessing (min 5 peaks, 250 m/z range, 101–500 m/z window) does not apply; these falcon settings must be reduced/adjusted first Exact cosine distances between every spectrum pair are required — feature hashing only approximates the original cosine similarity

skills.description: Use when you have m/z-binned, TIC-normalized serial-section MSI data (e.g. coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) and need per-section images with morphological contrast suitable as moving images for affine/B-spline registration to MRI.
skills.name: feature-image-generation-for-image-registration
skills.search_text: feature-image-generation-for-image-registration Use when you have m/z-binned, TIC-normalized serial-section MSI data (e.g. coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) and need per-section images with morphological contrast suitable as moving images for affine/B-spline registration to MRI. Input is already registered ion images or a final feature table — this skill operates on the raw m/z-binned pixel x feature MSI cube before registration. Only a single 2D section with no serial-section alignment requirement — a single-section UMAP visualization or supervised classification may suffice and full 3D embedding training may be unnecessary. The target registration reference is not an anatomical image (e.g. histology or a different modality whose contrast is not captured by the first three UMAP dimensions). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generates grayscale anatomical-contrast 'feature' images from a reconstructed 3D MSI data cube by training a parametric UMAP autoencoder and encoding each 2D tissue section, so the MSI sections can be co-registered to MRI atlas slices. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Generates grayscale anatomical-contrast 'feature' images from a reconstructed 3D MSI data cube by training a parametric UMAP autoencoder and encoding each 2D tissue section, so the MSI sections can be co-registered to MRI atlas slices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already registered ion images or a final feature table — this skill operates on the raw m/z-binned pixel x feature MSI cube before registration. Only a single 2D section with no serial-section alignment requirement — a single-section UMAP visualization or supervised classification may suffice and full 3D embedding training may be unnecessary. The target registration reference is not an anatomical image (e.g. histology or a different modality whose contrast is not captured by the first three UMAP dimensions).

skills.description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table plus a design file with class labels are available and the goal is to identify which features differentiate sample groups via random-forest variable importance.
skills.name: feature-importance-rank-scoring
skills.search_text: feature-importance-rank-scoring Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table plus a design file with class labels are available and the goal is to identify which features differentiate sample groups via random-forest variable importance. Input is a peak list or raw instrument data rather than a preprocessed feature table — SECIMTools expects features as the starting point; peak picking/feature identification is done upstream (e.g. by Galaxy-M or Workflow4Metabolomics). The task is regression or unsupervised ordination (PCA, hierarchical cluster heatmap, modularity clustering) rather than class-label classification with a design-file grouping variable. The goal is hypothesis testing on group differences (ANOVA, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis) rather than ensemble-based feature differentiation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Assigns an importance score to every metabolomics feature in a random-forest classifier, measuring how differentiating each feature is, and rank-orders features by usefulness in the ensemble (summarized by the variable importance plot, VIF). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Assigns an importance score to every metabolomics feature in a random-forest classifier, measuring how differentiating each feature is, and rank-orders features by usefulness in the ensemble (summarized by the variable importance plot, VIF).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a peak list or raw instrument data rather than a preprocessed feature table — SECIMTools expects features as the starting point; peak picking/feature identification is done upstream (e.g. by Galaxy-M or Workflow4Metabolomics). The task is regression or unsupervised ordination (PCA, hierarchical cluster heatmap, modularity clustering) rather than class-label classification with a design-file grouping variable. The goal is hypothesis testing on group differences (ANOVA, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis) rather than ensemble-based feature differentiation.

skills.description: Use when a molecular map of feature intensities in 'ili is dominated by a few high-intensity spots, neighboring spots overlap, or the color range obscures spatial gradients in the intensity data.
skills.name: feature-intensity-colormap-scaling
skills.search_text: feature-intensity-colormap-scaling Use when a molecular map of feature intensities in 'ili is dominated by a few high-intensity spots, neighboring spots overlap, or the color range obscures spatial gradients in the intensity data. Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) data, where coeluting fragment spectra do not need DIA-style deconvolution.

Input is still raw vendor mass spec data — run feature detection with MZmine, XCMS, or MS-DIAL first, since LipidMatch consumes feature tables, not raw files MS/MS raw spectra still need peak picking — convert and peak-pick to .ms2 with MSConvert before parsing Data already carries appended lipid identifications from LipidMatch/MS-DIAL/Greazy and the task is comparison rather than table preparation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Load and standardize peak-picked feature tables (m/z, retention time, intensities per feature) produced by tools like MZmine, XCMS, or MS-DIAL so they can be organized alongside .ms2 MS/MS files for LipidMatch's MS1 exact-mass matching and downstream annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Load and standardize peak-picked feature tables (m/z, retention time, intensities per feature) produced by tools like MZmine, XCMS, or MS-DIAL so they can be organized alongside .ms2 MS/MS files for LipidMatch's MS1 exact-mass matching and downstream annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw vendor mass spec data — run feature detection with MZmine, XCMS, or MS-DIAL first, since LipidMatch consumes feature tables, not raw files MS/MS raw spectra still need peak picking — convert and peak-pick to .ms2 with MSConvert before parsing Data already carries appended lipid identifications from LipidMatch/MS-DIAL/Greazy and the task is comparison rather than table preparation

skills.description: Use when you have an MZmine3 feature list with representative spectra from positive ion mode LC–MS/MS data and need molecular formula and adduct assignment per feature, or need to reproduce a reported formula/adduct hit rate.
skills.name: feature-table-parsing
skills.search_text: feature-table-parsing Use when you have an MZmine3 feature list with representative spectra from positive ion mode LC–MS/MS data and need molecular formula and adduct assignment per feature, or need to reproduce a reported formula/adduct hit rate. The input is already a SIRIUS-annotated feature table with formula/adduct assignments — re-running assignment is unnecessary The data are negative ion mode only — this skill is scoped to positive ion mode, where SIRIUS considers common positive-ion adducts The goal is molecular candidate ranking or structure retrieval rather than formula/adduct assignment — use the MVP candidate-ranking workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Parse an MZmine3 feature table with representative MS/MS spectra and run SIRIUS v6.1.0 formula and adduct assignment over positive-ion-mode LC–MS/MS features, compiling per-feature assignment records to compute a formula/adduct hit rate (866/900 in the replicated cultured-vs-conventional meat metabolomics study). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.688047
skills.summary: Parse an MZmine3 feature table with representative MS/MS spectra and run SIRIUS v6.1.0 formula and adduct assignment over positive-ion-mode LC–MS/MS features, compiling per-feature assignment records to compute a formula/adduct hit rate (866/900 in the replicated cultured-vs-conventional meat metabolomics study).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a SIRIUS-annotated feature table with formula/adduct assignments — re-running assignment is unnecessary The data are negative ion mode only — this skill is scoped to positive ion mode, where SIRIUS considers common positive-ion adducts The goal is molecular candidate ranking or structure retrieval rather than formula/adduct assignment — use the MVP candidate-ranking workflow instead

skills.description: Use when an Asari-derived feature table (e.g. preferred_Feature_table.tsv) needs per-sample intensity scaling before statistics, especially when per-sample TIC correlates with feature counts or when samples were acquired in multiple batches.
skills.name: feature-table-tic-normalization
skills.search_text: feature-table-tic-normalization Use when an Asari-derived feature table (e.g. preferred_Feature_table.tsv) needs per-sample intensity scaling before statistics, especially when per-sample TIC correlates with feature counts or when samples were acquired in multiple batches. Data are still raw acquisitions (.raw/.mzML) and have not been preprocessed into a feature table by Asari. The table is already normalized or the goal is a model-based batch correction rather than TIC-based per-sample scaling. The feature table contains only rare/sporadic features, so no features pass the TIC_normalization_percentile threshold and factors would be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Per-sample total ion current (TIC) normalization of LC-MS feature tables as implemented in the pcpfm `normalize` operation, including a two-pass batch-aware variant that scales batches to one another. It corrects run-to-run intensity variation so downstream statistical analysis is not driven by sample-level feature counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: Per-sample total ion current (TIC) normalization of LC-MS feature tables as implemented in the pcpfm `normalize` operation, including a two-pass batch-aware variant that scales batches to one another. It corrects run-to-run intensity variation so downstream statistical analysis is not driven by sample-level feature counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are still raw acquisitions (.raw/.mzML) and have not been preprocessed into a feature table by Asari. The table is already normalized or the goal is a model-based batch correction rather than TIC-based per-sample scaling. The feature table contains only rare/sporadic features, so no features pass the TIC_normalization_percentile threshold and factors would be unreliable.

skills.search_text: feature-table-tsv-io Use when a pcpfm experiment's curated feature intensities must be loaded, filtered, or persisted — every pipeline operation (blank masking, batch correction, imputation, normalization) consumes and emits a TSV feature table under a new moniker. skills.summary: Reading and writing pcpfm/Asari feature tables as moniker-named TSV files (e.g. preferred_Feature_table.tsv, preferred_blank_masked.tsv, batch_corrected.tsv) within an experiment's feature_tables directory, typically with pandas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data (.raw or .mzML) — Asari preprocessing, not feature-table TSV I/O, is the correct entry point The target object is an empirical-compound JSON (empCpd.json) rather than a feature-intensity table The table needs MS1/MS2 annotation added — use the annotation commands rather than plain TSV round-tripping

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing GLEAMS' spectrum encoder and you must confirm the concatenated precursor, fragment-bin, and reference-similarity blocks yield the expected 3010 features before feeding the neural network.
skills.name: feature-vector-dimension-verification
skills.search_text: feature-vector-dimension-verification Use when reconstructing or re-implementing GLEAMS' spectrum encoder and you must confirm the concatenated precursor, fragment-bin, and reference-similarity blocks yield the expected 3010 features before feeding the neural network. You are verifying the neural network output, which is a 32-dimensional embedding, not the 3010-dimensional input encoding Spectra lack reliable precursor charge or precursor m/z, so the Gray-code and one-hot blocks cannot be populated You only need `gleams embed` end-to-end embeddings and will not re-implement the encoder yourself http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Verifies that GLEAMS' per-spectrum input encoding produces exactly a 3010-dimensional feature vector by summing its fixed-width blocks: two 27-bit Gray codes (precursor mass and m/z), a 7-state one-hot charge, 2449 square-root-transformed fragment-intensity bins (50.5–2500 m/z), and 500 dot-product similarities to reference spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Verifies that GLEAMS' per-spectrum input encoding produces exactly a 3010-dimensional feature vector by summing its fixed-width blocks: two 27-bit Gray codes (precursor mass and m/z), a 7-state one-hot charge, 2449 square-root-transformed fragment-intensity bins (50.5–2500 m/z), and 500 dot-product similarities to reference spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are verifying the neural network output, which is a 32-dimensional embedding, not the 3010-dimensional input encoding Spectra lack reliable precursor charge or precursor m/z, so the Gray-code and one-hot blocks cannot be populated You only need `gleams embed` end-to-end embeddings and will not re-implement the encoder yourself

skills.name: featuredata-log-transformation-and-imputation
skills.search_text: featuredata-log-transformation-and-imputation Use when raw metabolite peak-intensity data has been arranged into the NormalizeMets 'featuredata' format (samples as rows, metabolites as columns) and needs log transformation plus missing-value imputation before applying NormQcmets, NormScaling, or other normalization functions. Data is already log-transformed and complete — re-running LogTransform with zerotona=TRUE would introduce spurious NAs and trigger unnecessary imputation The task is QC-sample-based signal correction (NormQcsamples/QC-RLSC) or scaling normalization, which the article treats as separate workflow steps applied after this preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Preprocesses a metabolomics featuredata matrix for the NormalizeMets workflow by log-transforming peak intensities (converting zeros to NA) and then imputing remaining missing values with k-nearest-neighbour (knn) so downstream normalization methods receive a complete, roughly log-scale data matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Preprocesses a metabolomics featuredata matrix for the NormalizeMets workflow by log-transforming peak intensities (converting zeros to NA) and then imputing remaining missing values with k-nearest-neighbour (knn) so downstream normalization methods receive a complete, roughly log-scale data matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already log-transformed and complete — re-running LogTransform with zerotona=TRUE would introduce spurious NAs and trigger unnecessary imputation The task is QC-sample-based signal correction (NormQcsamples/QC-RLSC) or scaling normalization, which the article treats as separate workflow steps applied after this preprocessing

skills.search_text: featureml-peak-export-and-annotation Use when PeakBot peak-picking output from LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms must be exported as a tsv peak-area table and featureML files for inspection/annotation in TOPPView, or as images for user verification. The input is already a featureXML or tabular feature table — this skill only serializes freshly assembled features, not re-encodes existing ones Mass traces have not yet been detected or assembled into features (the stage-1 mass trace detection and hypothesis-scoring steps must run first) The goal is linking coinciding features across multiple experiments — that is handled by FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT downstream, not by this serialization step http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Persist the assembled metabolite features produced by FeatureFinderMetabo into an OpenMS featureXML feature map, storing each accepted feature with its monoisotopic trace, intensities, charge estimate, and non-overlapping isotope hypothesis membership. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278

skills.description: Use when benchmarking or cross-tool comparison requires converting XCMS/CAMERA feature output into OpenMS featureXML maps with monoisotopic isotope values preserved, so FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT can link coinciding features and precision/recall can be computed on identical ground truth.

skills.summary: Converts externally produced LC-MS feature lists (e.g. XCMS+CAMERA output) into OpenMS featureXML feature maps, retaining monoisotopic isotope values so that feature intensities are comparable across tools and can be linked and scored with the OpenMS pipeline.

The goal is raw peak-level conversion (e.g. mzML/mzXML handling) rather than feature-level interoperability between XCMS/CAMERA and OpenMS. Comparing tools that already emit OpenMS-compatible featureXML directly, where a conversion step could alter intensities or isotope annotations unnecessarily.

skills.description: Use when you need to reconstruct, verify, or document the layer-by-layer architecture of released HDF5 Keras/TF2 model files (e.g., NPClassifier's three single-task networks) before reimplementation or reuse.
skills.name: feedforward-layer-enumeration
skills.search_text: feedforward-layer-enumeration Use when you need to reconstruct, verify, or document the layer-by-layer architecture of released HDF5 Keras/TF2 model files (e.g., NPClassifier's three single-task networks) before reimplementation or reuse. You only need to classify a SMILES string — use the deployed /classify?smiles=<> API instead of loading and inspecting model files The models are multitask architectures with shared output heads — NPClassifier was built as three separate single-task feed-forward networks, so a single shared-layer enumeration does not apply The model files are not HDF5 TF2 exports (e.g., PyTorch checkpoints or TF1 frozen graphs) — the Keras model.layers enumeration path requires TF 2.3.0-compatible HDF5 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs the internal architecture of released Keras/TensorFlow DNN model files by loading each model, enumerating its layers, and recording input shapes, hidden-layer activations, dropout placement, and output sizes. In NPClassifier this establishes that Pathway, Superclass, and Class prediction are three separate single-task feed-forward networks rather than one multitask model. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.1c00399
skills.summary: Reconstructs the internal architecture of released Keras/TensorFlow DNN model files by loading each model, enumerating its layers, and recording input shapes, hidden-layer activations, dropout placement, and output sizes. In NPClassifier this establishes that Pathway, Superclass, and Class prediction are three separate single-task feed-forward networks rather than one multitask model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to classify a SMILES string — use the deployed /classify?smiles=<> API instead of loading and inspecting model files The models are multitask architectures with shared output heads — NPClassifier was built as three separate single-task feed-forward networks, so a single shared-layer enumeration does not apply The model files are not HDF5 TF2 exports (e.g., PyTorch checkpoints or TF1 frozen graphs) — the Keras model.layers enumeration path requires TF 2.3.0-compatible HDF5

skills.description: Use when SCMS metabolomics data yield too few cells per phenotype for conventional deep learning and you need to build N-shot meta-learning tasks (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma classification from IGR39/IGR37 single-probe SCMS profiles).
skills.name: few-shot-task-sampling-from-mass-spectrometry-data
skills.search_text: few-shot-task-sampling-from-mass-spectrometry-data Use when SCMS metabolomics data yield too few cells per phenotype for conventional deep learning and you need to build N-shot meta-learning tasks (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma classification from IGR39/IGR37 single-probe SCMS profiles). Input data is raw single-cell mass spectra that still require noise/background subtraction, TIC normalization, and peak alignment before task construction A large training set of cells is already available, making conventional transfer learning or supervised 1D-CNN training sufficient Phenotypes are already well separated by simpler methods such as PCA (note: PCA fails for similar profiles like IGR39/IGR37, which is when meta-learning is warranted) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Constructs MAML meta-training tasks (support/query splits at 1, 5, and 10 shots per class) from pretreated single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics data so a 1D-CNN MAML model can be trained to classify cell phenotypes with limited samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Constructs MAML meta-training tasks (support/query splits at 1, 5, and 10 shots per class) from pretreated single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics data so a 1D-CNN MAML model can be trained to classify cell phenotypes with limited samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw single-cell mass spectra that still require noise/background subtraction, TIC normalization, and peak alignment before task construction A large training set of cells is already available, making conventional transfer learning or supervised 1D-CNN training sufficient Phenotypes are already well separated by simpler methods such as PCA (note: PCA fails for similar profiles like IGR39/IGR37, which is when meta-learning is warranted)

skills.description: Use when few (1-5) labeled single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) samples are available for a new cell group and you need to adapt a pre-trained meta-learning classifier and compare it with transfer-learning baselines.
skills.name: few-shot-transfer-learning-comparison
skills.search_text: few-shot-transfer-learning-comparison Use when few (1-5) labeled single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) samples are available for a new cell group and you need to adapt a pre-trained meta-learning classifier and compare it with transfer-learning baselines. PCA already discriminates the cell groups — the article notes PCA cannot separate phenotypically similar metabolomic profiles such as IGR39/IGR37, so if simpler methods suffice, meta-learning is unnecessary Large labeled training sets are available for the new cell group — conventional deep learning is appropriate and the MAML inner/outer loop overhead is not warranted Data are bulk (population-level) measurements rather than single-cell metabolomic profiles, since the model is trained on SCMS single-cell feature tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Rapidly adapt a meta-trained MetaPhenotype model (MAML with a 1D-CNN/LeNet backbone) to classify previously unseen melanoma cell groups into primary vs metastatic phenotypes using only 1- or 5-shot adaptation, and benchmark against standard transfer-learning baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Rapidly adapt a meta-trained MetaPhenotype model (MAML with a 1D-CNN/LeNet backbone) to classify previously unseen melanoma cell groups into primary vs metastatic phenotypes using only 1- or 5-shot adaptation, and benchmark against standard transfer-learning baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: PCA already discriminates the cell groups — the article notes PCA cannot separate phenotypically similar metabolomic profiles such as IGR39/IGR37, so if simpler methods suffice, meta-learning is unnecessary Large labeled training sets are available for the new cell group — conventional deep learning is appropriate and the MAML inner/outer loop overhead is not warranted Data are bulk (population-level) measurements rather than single-cell metabolomic profiles, since the model is trained on SCMS single-cell feature tables

skills.description: Use when the input is a metabolite molecular formula (with natural or SIP-enriched isotope abundances) and the goal is a simulated whole-molecule isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, ...) rather than fine structure.
skills.name: fft-based-isotopic-envelope-simulation
skills.search_text: fft-based-isotopic-envelope-simulation Use when the input is a metabolite molecular formula (with natural or SIP-enriched isotope abundances) and the goal is a simulated whole-molecule isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, ...) rather than fine structure. When isotopic fine structure must be resolved — the FFT-based envelope method 'does not account for isotopic fine structure'; use the Monte Carlo multinomial simulation instead. When the target is a peptide precursor or its b/y ion series — Aerith models those by sequentially convoluting isotopic envelopes of monomeric units rather than whole-molecule FFT convolution. When the compound's chemical formula is unknown — this algorithm requires a known formula (Miso-style tracer envelopes or user-defined sequences are handled differently). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aerith's FFT-based algorithm computes the theoretical isotopic envelope of a metabolite with a known chemical formula by convolving elemental isotope distributions in the frequency domain, supporting natural-abundance and user-defined SIP-enriched abundances. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Aerith's FFT-based algorithm computes the theoretical isotopic envelope of a metabolite with a known chemical formula by convolving elemental isotope distributions in the frequency domain, supporting natural-abundance and user-defined SIP-enriched abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When isotopic fine structure must be resolved — the FFT-based envelope method 'does not account for isotopic fine structure'; use the Monte Carlo multinomial simulation instead. When the target is a peptide precursor or its b/y ion series — Aerith models those by sequentially convoluting isotopic envelopes of monomeric units rather than whole-molecule FFT convolution. When the compound's chemical formula is unknown — this algorithm requires a known formula (Miso-style tracer envelopes or user-defined sequences are handled differently).

skills.description: Use when a deposited GC-MS dataset is too large for direct NNMF auto-deconvolution in MSHub, and the analysis goal is deconvoluted fragmentation spectra at repository scale for molecular networking.
skills.name: fft-based-scalability-processing
skills.search_text: fft-based-scalability-processing Use when a deposited GC-MS dataset is too large for direct NNMF auto-deconvolution in MSHub, and the analysis goal is deconvoluted fragmentation spectra at repository scale for molecular networking. The dataset is small enough that direct NNMF deconvolution completes without hitting scalability limits, so the FFT-based strategy is unnecessary overhead. The input is LC-MS/MS data handled by standard feature-based molecular networking rather than GC-MS electron-impact data requiring spectral deconvolution. Spectra are already deconvoluted compound features (e.g., an existing .mgf plus quantification table from a prior MSHub job). http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A Fast Fourier Transform-based strategy built into the GNPS MSHub workflow that overcomes the scalability limitations of unsupervised non-negative matrix factorization (NNMF) when auto-deconvolving GC-MS fragmentation patterns across repository-scale datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: A Fast Fourier Transform-based strategy built into the GNPS MSHub workflow that overcomes the scalability limitations of unsupervised non-negative matrix factorization (NNMF) when auto-deconvolving GC-MS fragmentation patterns across repository-scale datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that direct NNMF deconvolution completes without hitting scalability limits, so the FFT-based strategy is unnecessary overhead. The input is LC-MS/MS data handled by standard feature-based molecular networking rather than GC-MS electron-impact data requiring spectral deconvolution. Spectra are already deconvoluted compound features (e.g., an existing .mgf plus quantification table from a prior MSHub job).

skills.description: Use when you have metabolomics summary statistics (log2FC and p-values per metabolite) and want GSEA-style enrichment over KEGG pathway sets, e.g. reproducing control vs mutant lung cancer MetSEA results.
skills.name: fgsea-based-metabolite-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: fgsea-based-metabolite-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have metabolomics summary statistics (log2FC and p-values per metabolite) and want GSEA-style enrichment over KEGG pathway sets, e.g. reproducing control vs mutant lung cancer MetSEA results. Input is only an unranked list of significant metabolites without log2FC and p-value statistics — use the Fisher's Exact Test over-representation module instead, since MetSEA requires a ranked list. The goal is topology-based pathway impact (betweenness centrality / impact score) or the STITCH interaction network rather than ranked-set enrichment. No pathway annotations are available and KEGG REST access is not possible — the package fetches annotations at runtime and does not ship database dumps. http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 MetSEA in EnrichMet runs metabolite set enrichment analysis with fgsea on metabolites ranked by log2 fold change and p-value, against KEGG pathway annotations converted to GMT format, returning NES and adjusted p-values per pathway. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: MetSEA in EnrichMet runs metabolite set enrichment analysis with fgsea on metabolites ranked by log2 fold change and p-value, against KEGG pathway annotations converted to GMT format, returning NES and adjusted p-values per pathway.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only an unranked list of significant metabolites without log2FC and p-value statistics — use the Fisher's Exact Test over-representation module instead, since MetSEA requires a ranked list. The goal is topology-based pathway impact (betweenness centrality / impact score) or the STITCH interaction network rather than ranked-set enrichment. No pathway annotations are available and KEGG REST access is not possible — the package fetches annotations at runtime and does not ship database dumps.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw Bruker-formatted FID data (extract_params + extract_fids outputs) and you need to correct the group-delay artifact, suppress residual solvent, and Fourier-transform each FID into a spectrum before phase/baseline steps.
skills.name: fid-time-domain-preprocessing
skills.search_text: fid-time-domain-preprocessing Use when starting from raw Bruker-formatted FID data (extract_params + extract_fids outputs) and you need to correct the group-delay artifact, suppress residual solvent, and Fourier-transform each FID into a spectrum before phase/baseline steps. Input is already frequency-domain spectra (spectra_df); use phase_correction, baseline_correction, binning, and normalization instead. Input FIDs have not been extracted — run Protomix's extract_params and extract_fids first to obtain acqus_df and fids_df. Data is not Bruker-formatted NMR with an acqus file providing the group-delay parameter, since the number of leading points to delete cannot be determined. Time-domain (FID) preprocessing chain for Bruker 1H-NMR metabolomics data using Protomix: group-delay removal, solvent residual removal, exponential apodization, zero filling, and Fourier transformation to convert raw Free Induction Decays into frequency-domain spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Time-domain (FID) preprocessing chain for Bruker 1H-NMR metabolomics data using Protomix: group-delay removal, solvent residual removal, exponential apodization, zero filling, and Fourier transformation to convert raw Free Induction Decays into frequency-domain spectra.

skills.search_text: fid-to-spectrum-preprocessing-pipeline Use when starting from raw Bruker NMR acquisition directories (acqus files + FIDs) and a cleaned, phase-corrected, baseline-corrected spectra table (samples × ppm) is needed for metabolomics analysis. skills.description: Use when preparing a binned time-domain FID (e.g., 16,384 complex points) for SAND decomposition, before optimization iterations, to curb overfitting via FID truncation and randomized 70/20/10 train/validation/test subsampling.
skills.name: fid-truncation-and-binning
skills.search_text: fid-truncation-and-binning Use when preparing a binned time-domain FID (e.g., 16,384 complex points) for SAND decomposition, before optimization iterations, to curb overfitting via FID truncation and randomized 70/20/10 train/validation/test subsampling. Input is already a processed frequency-domain peak/feature table rather than a raw or binned time-domain FID Late-time FID points carry meaningful signal rather than trailing noise, so discarding points after index 6,000 would lose information The goal is strict cross-validated model selection; SAND's partitioning is explicitly meant to infer a reasonable number of peaks, not to serve as cross-validation A pre-decomposition subsampling step from the SAND workflow: the binned time-domain FID (16,384 complex points) is truncated to the early-time signal-dominated region (first 6,000 points) and the selected points are randomly partitioned into 70/20/10 training/validation/test subsets to reduce overfitting during MCMC optimization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03078
skills.summary: A pre-decomposition subsampling step from the SAND workflow: the binned time-domain FID (16,384 complex points) is truncated to the early-time signal-dominated region (first 6,000 points) and the selected points are randomly partitioned into 70/20/10 training/validation/test subsets to reduce overfitting during MCMC optimization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed frequency-domain peak/feature table rather than a raw or binned time-domain FID Late-time FID points carry meaningful signal rather than trailing noise, so discarding points after index 6,000 would lose information The goal is strict cross-validated model selection; SAND's partitioning is explicitly meant to infer a reasonable number of peaks, not to serve as cross-validation

skills.search_text: figure-panel-reproduction-from-deposited-data Use when a published figure must be reproduced from deposited deconvoluted GC-MS feature tables that carry sample metadata (e.g., body-location coordinates), and the panel depicts per-feature intensity distributions across spatial locations. The task is fingerprint prediction from spectra, not structure generation — use the MIST spectrum-to-fingerprint encoder training path instead. Candidate structures must come from a fixed virtual library with exact matching (library search) rather than de novo generation, since generated structures may only be structurally close matches. skills.search_text: fingerprint-probability-thresholding Use when experimental MS/MS spectra must be turned into discrete fingerprint tokens for finetuning or inference, and a pretrained spectral inference model (MIST) outputs per-bit probabilities {p0,...,p4095} rather than binary fingerprints. When fingerprints are already computed directly from known molecular structures with RDKit (the pretraining fingerprint-molecule pairs) — no spectral inference or thresholding is needed When no pretrained MIST model is available for the spectra's acquisition conditions — fingerprint prediction accuracy significantly limits overall downstream performance When the task is spectrum simulation or forward prediction (spectrum-to-fingerprint direction is reversed); this skill only handles the spectra-to-fingerprint direction http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Converts MIST-predicted per-bit probability vectors for a 4096-bit circular Morgan fingerprint into binary fingerprints and discrete <fp{i:04d}> tokens, bridging noisy experimental mass spectra into the fingerprint-token vocabulary that the fingerprint-to-molecule model consumes. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Converts MIST-predicted per-bit probability vectors for a 4096-bit circular Morgan fingerprint into binary fingerprints and discrete <fp{i:04d}> tokens, bridging noisy experimental mass spectra into the fingerprint-token vocabulary that the fingerprint-to-molecule model consumes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When fingerprints are already computed directly from known molecular structures with RDKit (the pretraining fingerprint-molecule pairs) — no spectral inference or thresholding is needed When no pretrained MIST model is available for the spectra's acquisition conditions — fingerprint prediction accuracy significantly limits overall downstream performance When the task is spectrum simulation or forward prediction (spectrum-to-fingerprint direction is reversed); this skill only handles the spectra-to-fingerprint direction

skills.search_text: fingerprint-random-forest-metabolite-classification Use when evaluating whether a chemical language model's generated molecules are metabolite-like by classifying them against held-out metabolites via fingerprints. When you already have confirmed spectral identifications and only need to compute structural similarity to a reference library. http://edamontology.org/topic_3335 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains a scikit-learn random forest on molecular fingerprints to test whether generated SMILES (from DeepMet/CLM) are structurally indistinguishable from withheld real metabolites; an AUC near 0.5 (chance level) indicates the generator recapitulates the known metabolome. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Trains a scikit-learn random forest on molecular fingerprints to test whether generated SMILES (from DeepMet/CLM) are structurally indistinguishable from withheld real metabolites; an AUC near 0.5 (chance level) indicates the generator recapitulates the known metabolome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is prioritizing generated structures by mass-to-charge ratio for MS/MS spectral matching rather than assessing global metabolite-likeness. When the training set is not human metabolites (e.g., plant or bacterial metabolism) — the article notes evolutionarily distant applications require bespoke models.
