skills.name: fingerprint-retrieval-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: fingerprint-retrieval-accuracy-evaluation Use when a fine-tuned tandem-MS model outputs molecular fingerprints and you must quantify molecular-structure retrieval quality against MIST/FFN baselines on the CANOPUS benchmark (8,000 spectra, 7,000 unique molecules). The goal is library spectral matching by embedding similarity or one of the 44 standard spectral similarity measures — use the retrieval/similarity fine-tuning evaluation instead, not fingerprint accuracy@k The benchmark requires de novo formula or precursor chemical-formula prediction — that is MIST-CF territory, not fingerprint-based retrieval Production-grade fingerprint prediction is required — the article explicitly frames fingerprint fine-tuning as proof of concept, not a production-ready method Benchmark protocol for judging a fine-tuned MS/MS neural network (e.g. DreaMS) by how accurately its predicted 4,096-bit Morgan fingerprints retrieve molecular structures from PubChem, using accuracy@k on the MIST CANOPUS benchmark against the MIST and FFN baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for judging a fine-tuned MS/MS neural network (e.g. DreaMS) by how accurately its predicted 4,096-bit Morgan fingerprints retrieve molecular structures from PubChem, using accuracy@k on the MIST CANOPUS benchmark against the MIST and FFN baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is library spectral matching by embedding similarity or one of the 44 standard spectral similarity measures — use the retrieval/similarity fine-tuning evaluation instead, not fingerprint accuracy@k The benchmark requires de novo formula or precursor chemical-formula prediction — that is MIST-CF territory, not fingerprint-based retrieval Production-grade fingerprint prediction is required — the article explicitly frames fingerprint fine-tuning as proof of concept, not a production-ready method

skills.description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be converted into predicted CDK molecular fingerprints via per-bit libSVM models, and candidate compounds ranked by Jaccard similarity against pre-calculated database fingerprints.
skills.name: fingerprint-scorer-validation
skills.search_text: fingerprint-scorer-validation Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be converted into predicted CDK molecular fingerprints via per-bit libSVM models, and candidate compounds ranked by Jaccard similarity against pre-calculated database fingerprints. You need to predict across all 11416 CDK fingerprint bits — libSVM models only emit predictions within the 2500 occupied-bit subset defined by the bit-occupancy filter Input spectra are not in ChemDistiller's internal hierarchical format and cannot be converted — format converters were not yet implemented at time of writing The analysis is formula/element filtering rather than fingerprint-based candidate ranking — chemdistiller.filters.element, .formula, and .inchi modules are the appropriate entry points instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 FingerScorer-style validation: per-bit binary libSVM models predict CDK molecular fingerprints from tandem MS spectra, and candidate compounds are ranked by Jaccard similarity against pre-calculated fingerprints in the ChemDistiller compound database. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: FingerScorer-style validation: per-bit binary libSVM models predict CDK molecular fingerprints from tandem MS spectra, and candidate compounds are ranked by Jaccard similarity against pre-calculated fingerprints in the ChemDistiller compound database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to predict across all 11416 CDK fingerprint bits — libSVM models only emit predictions within the 2500 occupied-bit subset defined by the bit-occupancy filter Input spectra are not in ChemDistiller's internal hierarchical format and cannot be converted — format converters were not yet implemented at time of writing The analysis is formula/element filtering rather than fingerprint-based candidate ranking — chemdistiller.filters.element, .formula, and .inchi modules are the appropriate entry points instead

skills.description: Use when scoring de novo generated molecules against known ground-truth structures on a spectral elucidation benchmark, or when quantifying how much an ablation (e.g., 2D-only vs joint 2D&3D diffusion) degrades structural fidelity beyond exact-match accuracy.
skills.name: fingerprint-similarity-metrics
skills.search_text: fingerprint-similarity-metrics Use when scoring de novo generated molecules against known ground-truth structures on a spectral elucidation benchmark, or when quantifying how much an ablation (e.g., 2D-only vs joint 2D&3D diffusion) degrades structural fidelity beyond exact-match accuracy. When there is no ground-truth structure to compare against (pure unconditional generation quality assessment needs validity/novelty metrics instead) When evaluating elucidation on spectral modalities outside IR/Raman/UV-Vis (e.g., NMR or MS), which DiffSpectra does not cover When exact atom-level correspondence is the only question — RMSD with Hungarian mapping is the appropriate metric, not fingerprint Tanimoto http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluate spectra-conditioned molecular generation by comparing generated SMILES against ground-truth structures using fingerprint-based similarities (Tanimoto over Morgan/MA fingerprints), functional-group similarity (FGSim), MCES distance, and exact top-1/top-10 accuracy, as done in DiffSpectra's ablation and benchmark tables. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Evaluate spectra-conditioned molecular generation by comparing generated SMILES against ground-truth structures using fingerprint-based similarities (Tanimoto over Morgan/MA fingerprints), functional-group similarity (FGSim), MCES distance, and exact top-1/top-10 accuracy, as done in DiffSpectra's ablation and benchmark tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there is no ground-truth structure to compare against (pure unconditional generation quality assessment needs validity/novelty metrics instead) When evaluating elucidation on spectral modalities outside IR/Raman/UV-Vis (e.g., NMR or MS), which DiffSpectra does not cover When exact atom-level correspondence is the only question — RMSD with Hungarian mapping is the appropriate metric, not fingerprint Tanimoto

skills.description: Use when ranking candidate compounds for an analyte whose fingerprint has already been predicted from an MS/MS spectrum — score each candidate's 528-digit MACCS/FP3/FP4 fingerprint against the prediction and pick the top-ranked candidate.
skills.name: fingerprint-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: fingerprint-similarity-scoring Use when ranking candidate compounds for an analyte whose fingerprint has already been predicted from an MS/MS spectrum — score each candidate's 528-digit MACCS/FP3/FP4 fingerprint against the prediction and pick the top-ranked candidate. Input is not a molecular fingerprint pair but a raw MS/MS spectrum — spectrum-based spectral matching (HMDB, METLIN, GNPS libraries) is the wrong comparison method here Candidate structures are missing or unavailable, so OpenBabel fingerprints cannot be computed for candidates Only a small pre-defined candidate set is already known and no ranking is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes a similarity score between a predicted molecular fingerprint and candidate fingerprints (assembled from OpenBabel MACCS, FP3, and FP4 binary entries) using δ(f′,f) = 1 − Σ|f′−f|/n, then ranks candidates to select the annotation. This is the decision step after MetFID's ANN fingerprint prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Computes a similarity score between a predicted molecular fingerprint and candidate fingerprints (assembled from OpenBabel MACCS, FP3, and FP4 binary entries) using δ(f′,f) = 1 − Σ|f′−f|/n, then ranks candidates to select the annotation. This is the decision step after MetFID's ANN fingerprint prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a molecular fingerprint pair but a raw MS/MS spectrum — spectrum-based spectral matching (HMDB, METLIN, GNPS libraries) is the wrong comparison method here Candidate structures are missing or unavailable, so OpenBabel fingerprints cannot be computed for candidates Only a small pre-defined candidate set is already known and no ranking is needed

skills.description: Use when ranked candidate lists from cosine-only spectral matching leave the true identity below rank 1 (top-1 < 40%) and fingerprint information is available to integrate for improved ranking.
skills.name: fingerprint-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: fingerprint-similarity-scoring Use when ranked candidate lists from cosine-only spectral matching leave the true identity below rank 1 (top-1 < 40%) and fingerprint information is available to integrate for improved ranking. The analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectra in NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG libraries — conventional library screening suffices and the fingerprint-integrated ranking pipeline is unnecessary Input is a raw spectrum with no way to derive a molecular fingerprint (e.g., no DeepEI-compatible GC/EI-MS spectrum), so Jaccard similarity cannot be computed The task concerns spectral generation for known structures (NEIMS in silico prediction), not similarity-based ranking of unknown analytes Computes a Jaccard (Tanimoto) similarity between the DeepEI-predicted molecular fingerprint of an unknown GC/EI-MS analyte and the fingerprints of enumerated NPS candidates, and integrates it with the cosine spectral similarity (SMSF) to re-rank candidate compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Computes a Jaccard (Tanimoto) similarity between the DeepEI-predicted molecular fingerprint of an unknown GC/EI-MS analyte and the fingerprints of enumerated NPS candidates, and integrates it with the cosine spectral similarity (SMSF) to re-rank candidate compounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectra in NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG libraries — conventional library screening suffices and the fingerprint-integrated ranking pipeline is unnecessary Input is a raw spectrum with no way to derive a molecular fingerprint (e.g., no DeepEI-compatible GC/EI-MS spectrum), so Jaccard similarity cannot be computed The task concerns spectral generation for known structures (NEIMS in silico prediction), not similarity-based ranking of unknown analytes

skills.description: Use when a pipeline binarizes predicted fingerprint probabilities into a fixed-length bit vector via a threshold parameter, and you need to justify the chosen threshold or demonstrate insensitivity by retraining/evaluating across epsilon values.
skills.name: fingerprint-threshold-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: fingerprint-threshold-sensitivity-analysis Use when a pipeline binarizes predicted fingerprint probabilities into a fixed-length bit vector via a threshold parameter, and you need to justify the chosen threshold or demonstrate insensitivity by retraining/evaluating across epsilon values. When the fingerprint representation is already binary and no probability vector (hence no binarization threshold) exists When evaluating a single fixed configuration rather than characterizing sensitivity of metrics to the threshold parameter When the downstream model conditions directly on probability vectors rather than thresholded bits, since the epsilon sweep would have no effect http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Sweeps the fingerprint binarization threshold (epsilon) used to convert MIST probability vectors into binary 4096-bit Morgan fingerprints, then measures how Top-1 Tanimoto similarity and related metrics vary across epsilon values to test whether the downstream structure-elucidation model is sensitive to this filter step. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Sweeps the fingerprint binarization threshold (epsilon) used to convert MIST probability vectors into binary 4096-bit Morgan fingerprints, then measures how Top-1 Tanimoto similarity and related metrics vary across epsilon values to test whether the downstream structure-elucidation model is sensitive to this filter step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the fingerprint representation is already binary and no probability vector (hence no binarization threshold) exists When evaluating a single fixed configuration rather than characterizing sensitivity of metrics to the threshold parameter When the downstream model conditions directly on probability vectors rather than thresholded bits, since the epsilon sweep would have no effect

skills.description: Use when constructing a cross-modal pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs and you need a sequence-to-sequence model that maps fingerprint tokens (FP) to SELFIES structures, or when reproducing MS-BART's task ② pretraining objective.
skills.name: fingerprint-to-molecule-sequence-translation
skills.search_text: fingerprint-to-molecule-sequence-translation Use when constructing a cross-modal pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs and you need a sequence-to-sequence model that maps fingerprint tokens (FP) to SELFIES structures, or when reproducing MS-BART's task ② pretraining objective. The goal is de novo generation from experimental mass spectra — after pretraining, spectra must be converted via MIST-predicted fingerprints and the model finetuned on experimental data before use The target representation is SMILES or SAFE rather than the SELFIES vocabulary used by MS-BART's unified tokenizer A pretrained checkpoint already exists and the task is finetuning/alignment (e.g., [M+H]+ filtering, chemical feedback alignment) rather than from-scratch multi-task pretraining http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Multi-task pretraining objective of MS-BART that trains a BART-Base backbone to generate SELFIES molecular sequences conditioned on 4096-bit Morgan fingerprint tokens, learned over ~4M fingerprint–molecule pairs computed with RDKit. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Multi-task pretraining objective of MS-BART that trains a BART-Base backbone to generate SELFIES molecular sequences conditioned on 4096-bit Morgan fingerprint tokens, learned over ~4M fingerprint–molecule pairs computed with RDKit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo generation from experimental mass spectra — after pretraining, spectra must be converted via MIST-predicted fingerprints and the model finetuned on experimental data before use The target representation is SMILES or SAFE rather than the SELFIES vocabulary used by MS-BART's unified tokenizer A pretrained checkpoint already exists and the task is finetuning/alignment (e.g., [M+H]+ filtering, chemical feedback alignment) rather than from-scratch multi-task pretraining

skills.description: Use when building a large-scale pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs from unlabeled molecular structures, where fingerprints must be expressed as tokens in a unified vocabulary rather than raw bit vectors.
skills.name: fingerprint-token-sequence-generation
skills.search_text: fingerprint-token-sequence-generation Use when building a large-scale pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs from unlabeled molecular structures, where fingerprints must be expressed as tokens in a unified vocabulary rather than raw bit vectors. Input is already experimental mass spectra paired with annotated structures — this skill generates pretraining data from unlabeled structures, not from simulated or measured spectra. The downstream model expects raw 4096-bit fingerprint vectors rather than token sequences in a unified vocabulary. The candidate molecules violate the leakage constraints (MCES distance < 2 to test-fold molecules or Tanimoto > 0.5 to NPLIB1) and cannot be filtered. http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts unlabeled molecules into pretraining-ready fingerprint–molecule pairs by rendering each Morgan fingerprint bit as a dedicated vocabulary token and pairing it with a canonical SELFIES target sequence, enabling cross-modal pretraining without simulating mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Converts unlabeled molecules into pretraining-ready fingerprint–molecule pairs by rendering each Morgan fingerprint bit as a dedicated vocabulary token and pairing it with a canonical SELFIES target sequence, enabling cross-modal pretraining without simulating mass spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already experimental mass spectra paired with annotated structures — this skill generates pretraining data from unlabeled structures, not from simulated or measured spectra. The downstream model expects raw 4096-bit fingerprint vectors rather than token sequences in a unified vocabulary. The candidate molecules violate the leakage constraints (MCES distance < 2 to test-fold molecules or Tanimoto > 0.5 to NPLIB1) and cannot be filtered.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing alvaDesc fingerprint bit columns (MACCS166, Extended Connectivity, Path Fingerprints) for the SMRT RT-prediction models and low-prevalence, near-constant bits must be dropped before regressor training.
skills.name: fingerprint-variance-thresholding
skills.search_text: fingerprint-variance-thresholding Use when preprocessing alvaDesc fingerprint bit columns (MACCS166, Extended Connectivity, Path Fingerprints) for the SMRT RT-prediction models and low-prevalence, near-constant bits must be dropped before regressor training. The input is an already-cleaned feature table with no low-variance binary columns left to remove The columns are continuous molecular descriptors rather than binary bits — these require the zero-variance / >0.9-correlation filtering route instead of the Bernoulli p(1-p) threshold Fingerprints were not generated with alvaDesc (e.g. RDKit fingerprints from train_with_rdkit.ipynb), where bit-prevalence properties may differ and the tuned p > 0.9 threshold was not established http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Removes low-variance binary fingerprint bits from an alvaDesc-generated fingerprint matrix (MACCS166, ECFP, PFP) before training retention time prediction regressors, treating each bit as a Bernoulli variable whose variance Var[X] = p(1-p) must exceed a tuned threshold with p above 0.9. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8
skills.summary: Removes low-variance binary fingerprint bits from an alvaDesc-generated fingerprint matrix (MACCS166, ECFP, PFP) before training retention time prediction regressors, treating each bit as a Bernoulli variable whose variance Var[X] = p(1-p) must exceed a tuned threshold with p above 0.9.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an already-cleaned feature table with no low-variance binary columns left to remove The columns are continuous molecular descriptors rather than binary bits — these require the zero-variance / >0.9-correlation filtering route instead of the Bernoulli p(1-p) threshold Fingerprints were not generated with alvaDesc (e.g. RDKit fingerprints from train_with_rdkit.ipynb), where bit-prevalence properties may differ and the tuned p > 0.9 threshold was not established

skills.description: Use when extracted EICs from LC/MS-based metabolomics data must be scored for quality before downstream chromatographic peak detection, especially for EICs with high background signals or containing only a single peak.
skills.name: first-order-derivative-zigzag-quantification
skills.search_text: first-order-derivative-zigzag-quantification Use when extracted EICs from LC/MS-based metabolomics data must be scored for quality before downstream chromatographic peak detection, especially for EICs with high background signals or containing only a single peak. When the goal is selecting or aligning analyte components rather than quality evaluation — the article states the MCQ index, not the zigzag index, is suited for that task When a single metric is expected to give a definitive good/bad verdict for chromatographic peaks — the article recommends combining several peak quality metrics instead When an optimal cutoff threshold for each metric is required as a settled value — the article notes that setting an optimal cutoff threshold for each metric still is a challenge task http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes an EIC-related global zigzag index from the first-order derivatives of an extracted ion chromatogram (EIC), yielding a value in [0, 4.0] that robustly quantifies signal jaggedness for high-background or single-peak EICs where the mass chromatographic quality (MCQ) index fails. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Computes an EIC-related global zigzag index from the first-order derivatives of an extracted ion chromatogram (EIC), yielding a value in [0, 4.0] that robustly quantifies signal jaggedness for high-background or single-peak EICs where the mass chromatographic quality (MCQ) index fails.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is selecting or aligning analyte components rather than quality evaluation — the article states the MCQ index, not the zigzag index, is suited for that task When a single metric is expected to give a definitive good/bad verdict for chromatographic peaks — the article recommends combining several peak quality metrics instead When an optimal cutoff threshold for each metric is required as a settled value — the article notes that setting an optimal cutoff threshold for each metric still is a challenge task

skills.description: Use when working with raw Bruker 1H-NMR FIDs whose points carry the digital-filter group-delay artifact, after extraction of fids_df and acqus_df and before solvent removal or apodization.
skills.name: first-order-phase-artifact-removal
skills.search_text: first-order-phase-artifact-removal Use when working with raw Bruker 1H-NMR FIDs whose points carry the digital-filter group-delay artifact, after extraction of fids_df and acqus_df and before solvent removal or apodization. Data are not raw Bruker FIDs (e.g. already Fourier-transformed spectra) — the leading-point deletion applies only to time-domain FIDs with a recorded group delay in acqus acqus_df lacks the group-delay/DSP parameter, so the number of points to delete cannot be determined per sample The FID has already been group-delay corrected (grpd_df exists); deleting points again would remove genuine signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Removes the Bruker digital-filter group delay ('death time') artifact from each FID by deleting exactly the acqus-specified number of leading data points, correcting the first-order phase error before further preprocessing. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Removes the Bruker digital-filter group delay ('death time') artifact from each FID by deleting exactly the acqus-specified number of leading data points, correcting the first-order phase error before further preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not raw Bruker FIDs (e.g. already Fourier-transformed spectra) — the leading-point deletion applies only to time-domain FIDs with a recorded group delay in acqus acqus_df lacks the group-delay/DSP parameter, so the number of points to delete cannot be determined per sample The FID has already been group-delay corrected (grpd_df exists); deleting points again would remove genuine signal

skills.description: Use when performing metabolomics ORA and you need per-pathway p-values from a right-tailed Fisher's exact test (hypergeometric) on the pathway collection, metabolites-of-interest list, and background compound set.
skills.name: fisher-exact-contingency-table-implementation
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-contingency-table-implementation Use when performing metabolomics ORA and you need per-pathway p-values from a right-tailed Fisher's exact test (hypergeometric) on the pathway collection, metabolites-of-interest list, and background compound set. Pathways contain fewer than 3 compounds — the paper explicitly excludes these from ORA input. The metabolites of interest list has zero overlap (k = 0) with a given pathway — no p-value is calculated. The goal is functional interpretation of metabolomics datasets without a defined background set — the paper shows a non-assay-specific background set yields large numbers of false-positive pathways. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes per-pathway p-values for over-representation analysis (ORA) in metabolomics using a right-tailed Fisher's exact test based on the hypergeometric distribution, as implemented in the paper's custom Python script. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Computes per-pathway p-values for over-representation analysis (ORA) in metabolomics using a right-tailed Fisher's exact test based on the hypergeometric distribution, as implemented in the paper's custom Python script.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways contain fewer than 3 compounds — the paper explicitly excludes these from ORA input. The metabolites of interest list has zero overlap (k = 0) with a given pathway — no p-value is calculated. The goal is functional interpretation of metabolomics datasets without a defined background set — the paper shows a non-assay-specific background set yields large numbers of false-positive pathways.

skills.description: Use when you have categorical candidate-vs-reference gene assignments across curated loci and need odds ratios with 95% CIs to rank which annotation criteria are enriched for true positives.
skills.name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing Use when you have categorical candidate-vs-reference gene assignments across curated loci and need odds ratios with 95% CIs to rank which annotation criteria are enriched for true positives. Candidate gene assignments have not yet been generated (no ProGeM OUTPUT_* tables) or no reference causal gene set is available to cross against The analysis targets trans-pQTLs, where ProGeM's top-down candidate strategy and this enrichment benchmarking design do not directly apply The goal is continuous-score evaluation rather than categorical candidate-vs-non-candidate enrichment; a 2x2 Fisher test is not appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantify enrichment of true positive causal genes among candidate causal gene sets using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact test, as done in ProGeM's benchmarking of bottom-up annotation criteria at 227 curated metabolite QTLs (e.g. nearest-gene set OR=45, moderate-impact set OR=169). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gky837
skills.summary: Quantify enrichment of true positive causal genes among candidate causal gene sets using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact test, as done in ProGeM's benchmarking of bottom-up annotation criteria at 227 curated metabolite QTLs (e.g. nearest-gene set OR=45, moderate-impact set OR=169).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate gene assignments have not yet been generated (no ProGeM OUTPUT_* tables) or no reference causal gene set is available to cross against The analysis targets trans-pQTLs, where ProGeM's top-down candidate strategy and this enrichment benchmarking design do not directly apply The goal is continuous-score evaluation rather than categorical candidate-vs-non-candidate enrichment; a 2x2 Fisher test is not appropriate

skills.description: Use when you have a list of metabolite annotations exclusive to one method (e.g. METASPACE-ML at FDR 10%) plus a background annotation set, each mapped to HMDB taxonomy subclasses, and need to find which metabolic classes are overrepresented.
skills.name: fisher-exact-overrepresentation-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-overrepresentation-testing Use when you have a list of metabolite annotations exclusive to one method (e.g. METASPACE-ML at FDR 10%) plus a background annotation set, each mapped to HMDB taxonomy subclasses, and need to find which metabolic classes are overrepresented. The annotation list is not mapped to HMDB chemical taxonomy subclasses, so no contingency table per subclass can be built You want underrepresentation or two-sided class differences rather than one-tailed overrepresentation of a method's exclusive annotations You are comparing annotation counts rather than set membership overrepresentation — this test models exclusive-vs-background counts, not fold changes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A one-tailed Fisher exact (hypergeometric tail) overrepresentation test, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at 10%, used to identify HMDB chemical-taxonomy subclasses enriched among metabolite annotations uniquely captured by METASPACE-ML versus the full annotation background in animal and plant imaging mass spectrometry datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-52213-9
skills.summary: A one-tailed Fisher exact (hypergeometric tail) overrepresentation test, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at 10%, used to identify HMDB chemical-taxonomy subclasses enriched among metabolite annotations uniquely captured by METASPACE-ML versus the full annotation background in animal and plant imaging mass spectrometry datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation list is not mapped to HMDB chemical taxonomy subclasses, so no contingency table per subclass can be built You want underrepresentation or two-sided class differences rather than one-tailed overrepresentation of a method's exclusive annotations You are comparing annotation counts rather than set membership overrepresentation — this test models exclusive-vs-background counts, not fold changes

skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) must be mapped onto pathway-level biological activity, and metabolite identities are only tentatively matched, so enrichment must tolerate many-to-many m/z-to-metabolite matches.
skills.name: fisher-exact-pathway-enrichment
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-pathway-enrichment Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) must be mapped onto pathway-level biological activity, and metabolite identities are only tentatively matched, so enrichment must tolerate many-to-many m/z-to-metabolite matches. Group sizes are too small or errors are grossly non-normal for the tool's stated assumption of normal, identically distributed errors — the Kruskal-Wallis non-parametric test in the same suite is the alternative.

skills.description: Use when the input is a cleaned/transformed metabolomics feature table of targeted molecule intensities and the goal is regressing each metabolite on specified covariates with fixed effects only (no random effects, no censored values).
skills.name: fixed-effects-linear-model-fitting
skills.search_text: fixed-effects-linear-model-fitting Use when the input is a cleaned/transformed metabolomics feature table of targeted molecule intensities and the goal is regressing each metabolite on specified covariates with fixed effects only (no random effects, no censored values). The study design is longitudinal and requires random effects — use gentab_lm_long's mixed-effects mode (lmerTest) instead. Response values are censored at limits of detection — use the Tobit mode (AER::tobit) with left/right censoring limits instead. The input is raw, unprocessed intensities that have not yet been cleaned/transformed per the vignette workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fit fixed-effects linear regression models per metabolite using GetFeatistics' gentab_lm_long on cleaned, transformed targeted-metabolomics intensity tables, producing effect estimates (beta, 95% CI, SE), adjusted R-squared, P-values and FDR-adjusted P-values for each molecule–covariate pair. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Fit fixed-effects linear regression models per metabolite using GetFeatistics' gentab_lm_long on cleaned, transformed targeted-metabolomics intensity tables, producing effect estimates (beta, 95% CI, SE), adjusted R-squared, P-values and FDR-adjusted P-values for each molecule–covariate pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study design is longitudinal and requires random effects — use gentab_lm_long's mixed-effects mode (lmerTest) instead. Response values are censored at limits of detection — use the Tobit mode (AER::tobit) with left/right censoring limits instead. The input is raw, unprocessed intensities that have not yet been cleaned/transformed per the vignette workflow.

skills.description: Use when the same gene (feature) pair has Pearson correlation coefficients reported in multiple independent studies with known sample sizes, and a pooled per-pair estimate is needed.
skills.name: fixed-effects-weighted-estimation
skills.search_text: fixed-effects-weighted-estimation Use when the same gene (feature) pair has Pearson correlation coefficients reported in multiple independent studies with known sample sizes, and a pooled per-pair estimate is needed. The correlations come from a single study, so there is nothing to pool across studies The per-study effect sizes are not Pearson correlation coefficients (e.g. fold changes or p-values), which would require a different effect-size model Only sample-level data are available and per-study correlations have not yet been computed — compute the pairwise Pearson correlations first (as MOG does) before pooling http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Combines per-study Pearson correlation coefficients for the same feature (gene) pair across multiple studies into a single pooled estimate by weighting each study's correlation proportionally to its sample size, optionally extended to a random effects model with DerSimonian–Laird heterogeneity estimation. This is the meta-analysis mechanism MOG applies when gene pairs are measured across multiple studies. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Combines per-study Pearson correlation coefficients for the same feature (gene) pair across multiple studies into a single pooled estimate by weighting each study's correlation proportionally to its sample size, optionally extended to a random effects model with DerSimonian–Laird heterogeneity estimation. This is the meta-analysis mechanism MOG applies when gene pairs are measured across multiple studies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The correlations come from a single study, so there is nothing to pool across studies The per-study effect sizes are not Pearson correlation coefficients (e.g. fold changes or p-values), which would require a different effect-size model Only sample-level data are available and per-study correlations have not yet been computed — compute the pairwise Pearson correlations first (as MOG does) before pooling

skills.search_text: flavonoid-compound-class-aggregation Use when low-resolution MS2 spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer have been scored with TeFT SMILES fragment tree similarities and outcomes must be tallied per drug class with a minimum-similarity floor per class. Spectra are high-resolution / high-accuracy, where models like SIRIUS4, MSNovelist, or MassGenie are the appropriate comparators and TeFT's low-resolution design is not the basis for classification Compounds outside the flavonoid/stilbene/flavone classes or unknown substances without a class label, since per-class aggregation and Table 2 benchmark counts cannot be meaningfully computed Spectra acquired in negative ion mode — TeFT was trained only on positive ion mode (H+) spectra, so prediction outcomes and similarity scores are not trustworthy for class aggregation Aggregates TeFT de novo structure-prediction outcomes for the 23 purchased substances measured on the miniaturized linear ion trap mass spectrometer by compound class (flavonoid alcohol, flavone, stilbene), reporting fully predicted counts and per-class minimum fingerprint similarity to reproduce the paper's Table 2. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0
skills.summary: Aggregates TeFT de novo structure-prediction outcomes for the 23 purchased substances measured on the miniaturized linear ion trap mass spectrometer by compound class (flavonoid alcohol, flavone, stilbene), reporting fully predicted counts and per-class minimum fingerprint similarity to reproduce the paper's Table 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are high-resolution / high-accuracy, where models like SIRIUS4, MSNovelist, or MassGenie are the appropriate comparators and TeFT's low-resolution design is not the basis for classification Compounds outside the flavonoid/stilbene/flavone classes or unknown substances without a class label, since per-class aggregation and Table 2 benchmark counts cannot be meaningfully computed Spectra acquired in negative ion mode — TeFT was trained only on positive ion mode (H+) spectra, so prediction outcomes and similarity scores are not trustworthy for class aggregation

skills.description: Use when a SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv spatio-molecular matrix contains microscopy-derived fluorescence channels (e.g., mCherry for HeLa, GFP for NIH3T3) and per-cell cell-type ground truth is needed to train or evaluate a metabolic-profile classifier.
skills.name: fluorescence-based-cell-type-labeling
skills.search_text: fluorescence-based-cell-type-labeling Use when a SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv spatio-molecular matrix contains microscopy-derived fluorescence channels (e.g., mCherry for HeLa, GFP for NIH3T3) and per-cell cell-type ground truth is needed to train or evaluate a metabolic-profile classifier. Cells lack genetically encoded fluorescent reporters or matched fluorescence microscopy channels, so no fluorescence-based ground truth exists Input already contains trusted per-cell type annotations, making fluorescence re-labeling redundant The goal is unsupervised discovery of metabolic states (e.g., clustering dHepaRG hepatocytes), where fluorescence labels would bias the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Assigns ground-truth cell-type labels in co-culture single-cell metabolomics by applying a linear decision boundary on microscopy-derived fluorescence intensities (e.g., mCherry-vs-GFP channels) from the SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix, providing labels for classifier training and validation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Assigns ground-truth cell-type labels in co-culture single-cell metabolomics by applying a linear decision boundary on microscopy-derived fluorescence intensities (e.g., mCherry-vs-GFP channels) from the SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix, providing labels for classifier training and validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack genetically encoded fluorescent reporters or matched fluorescence microscopy channels, so no fluorescence-based ground truth exists Input already contains trusted per-cell type annotations, making fluorescence re-labeling redundant The goal is unsupervised discovery of metabolic states (e.g., clustering dHepaRG hepatocytes), where fluorescence labels would bias the analysis

skills.description: Use when analyzing background-corrected two-color live-cell confocal images (e.g. CFP/YFP pairs) to quantify what fraction of a protein resides in a region of interest, or to measure interaction/dissociation kinetics such as Rev-CRM1 after LMB addition.
skills.name: fluorescence-colocalization-quantification
skills.search_text: fluorescence-colocalization-quantification Use when analyzing background-corrected two-color live-cell confocal images (e.g. CFP/YFP pairs) to quantify what fraction of a protein resides in a region of interest, or to measure interaction/dissociation kinetics such as Rev-CRM1 after LMB addition. When FRET is required to confirm direct molecular contact: FRET was negative for the Rev-CRM1 complex presumably due to CRM1's large size (130 kDa), and FRET alone would only detect interaction if the average distance between binding proteins is <10 nm — colocalization quantification does not substitute for FRET in that regime. When images are too noisy or the texture/PSF scale cannot be estimated, since block scrambling depends on dividing the image into blocks approximately the size of the texture or PSF. When only a single channel is available, since the method fundamentally relies on the two-dimensional histogram of paired red/green intensities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3385 An automatic, threshold-free method to quantify protein-protein colocalization in two-color fluorescence images by block-scrambling pixels to build a random-overlap distribution, classifying pixels near the diagonal of the two-dimensional intensity histogram, and computing per-region colocalization proportions. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422
skills.summary: An automatic, threshold-free method to quantify protein-protein colocalization in two-color fluorescence images by block-scrambling pixels to build a random-overlap distribution, classifying pixels near the diagonal of the two-dimensional intensity histogram, and computing per-region colocalization proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When FRET is required to confirm direct molecular contact: FRET was negative for the Rev-CRM1 complex presumably due to CRM1's large size (130 kDa), and FRET alone would only detect interaction if the average distance between binding proteins is <10 nm — colocalization quantification does not substitute for FRET in that regime. When images are too noisy or the texture/PSF scale cannot be estimated, since block scrambling depends on dividing the image into blocks approximately the size of the texture or PSF. When only a single channel is available, since the method fundamentally relies on the two-dimensional histogram of paired red/green intensities.

skills.description: Use when analyzing background-corrected two-channel (e.g. red/green) fluorescence images where adjacent pixel intensities are correlated by texture or the PSF, and you need a statistical threshold separating specific colocalization from random overlap.
skills.name: fluorescence-image-block-randomization
skills.search_text: fluorescence-image-block-randomization Use when analyzing background-corrected two-channel (e.g. red/green) fluorescence images where adjacent pixel intensities are correlated by texture or the PSF, and you need a statistical threshold separating specific colocalization from random overlap. The question is direct protein–protein proximity rather than statistical intensity overlap — FRET, not this colocalization test, is the right assay, and FRET alone would only detect interaction if the average distance between the binding proteins is <10 nm You intend to classify colocalization by selecting pixels closest to the diagonal line in the two-dimensional histogram without the randomization step — the article warns that assuming such selected points are entirely colocalized can overpredict the amount of colocalization http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A significance-testing method for two-color fluorescence colocalization that scrambles image blocks — sized by the texture/PSF autocorrelation width — rather than individual pixels, 200 times per region, to build the null distribution of random overlap from which the colocalization significance threshold is set. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422
skills.summary: A significance-testing method for two-color fluorescence colocalization that scrambles image blocks — sized by the texture/PSF autocorrelation width — rather than individual pixels, 200 times per region, to build the null distribution of random overlap from which the colocalization significance threshold is set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is direct protein–protein proximity rather than statistical intensity overlap — FRET, not this colocalization test, is the right assay, and FRET alone would only detect interaction if the average distance between the binding proteins is <10 nm You intend to classify colocalization by selecting pixels closest to the diagonal line in the two-dimensional histogram without the randomization step — the article warns that assuming such selected points are entirely colocalized can overpredict the amount of colocalization

skills.description: Use when two-color confocal fluorescence images (e.g., Zeiss LSM 510 CFP/YFP acquisitions of live cells) must be background-corrected before building the red-green two-dimensional histogram and computing M1/M2 colocalization coefficients.
skills.name: fluorescence-microscopy-image-background-correction
skills.search_text: fluorescence-microscopy-image-background-correction Use when two-color confocal fluorescence images (e.g., Zeiss LSM 510 CFP/YFP acquisitions of live cells) must be background-corrected before building the red-green two-dimensional histogram and computing M1/M2 colocalization coefficients. The image pair is already background-corrected — the article's workflow explicitly loads 'the background-corrected two-color image pair', so re-correcting would double-subtract and deflate M1/M2 coefficients The goal is absolute fluorophore quantification rather than relative colocalization, since the correction is designed to support overlap statistics, not intensity calibration across samples The data are single-channel or the two-dimensional red-green histogram framework does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 Background correction removes out-of-cell and detector background signal from confocal fluorescence image pairs (e.g., Zeiss LSM 510 CFP/YFP acquisitions) so that downstream pixel-level colocalization analysis, such as M1/M2 coefficient computation, reflects true protein overlap rather than offset or bleed-through intensity. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422
skills.summary: Background correction removes out-of-cell and detector background signal from confocal fluorescence image pairs (e.g., Zeiss LSM 510 CFP/YFP acquisitions) so that downstream pixel-level colocalization analysis, such as M1/M2 coefficient computation, reflects true protein overlap rather than offset or bleed-through intensity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The image pair is already background-corrected — the article's workflow explicitly loads 'the background-corrected two-color image pair', so re-correcting would double-subtract and deflate M1/M2 coefficients The goal is absolute fluorophore quantification rather than relative colocalization, since the correction is designed to support overlap statistics, not intensity calibration across samples The data are single-channel or the two-dimensional red-green histogram framework does not apply

skills.description: Use when interpreting CFP/YFP two-channel 3D confocal stacks from cotransfected fixed or live HeLa cells where the goal is to classify pixels as colocalized versus random overlap and rank interaction groups against FRET ground truth.
skills.name: fluorescent-protein-cotransfection-image-interpretation
skills.search_text: fluorescent-protein-cotransfection-image-interpretation Use when interpreting CFP/YFP two-channel 3D confocal stacks from cotransfected fixed or live HeLa cells where the goal is to classify pixels as colocalized versus random overlap and rank interaction groups against FRET ground truth. When the question is direct molecular interaction at <10 nm distances — FRET alone (not colocalization) detects this, and the article shows FRET can be negative for large complexes like Rev-CRM1 (130 kDa) even when colocalization is real When images lack a second channel or a negative control condition (e.g., free YFP) — the statistical threshold and random-overlap distribution cannot be built When individual adjacent pixels can be assumed independent — scrambling single pixels instead of PSF-sized blocks violates the method's correlation assumption Interpretation of two-channel CFP/YFP confocal images of cotransfected HeLa cells (e.g., Rev-CFP with free YFP, Rev-YFP, or Tat-YFP) to quantify protein-protein colocalization and cross-validate group-level results against independent FRET measurements. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422
skills.summary: Interpretation of two-channel CFP/YFP confocal images of cotransfected HeLa cells (e.g., Rev-CFP with free YFP, Rev-YFP, or Tat-YFP) to quantify protein-protein colocalization and cross-validate group-level results against independent FRET measurements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is direct molecular interaction at <10 nm distances — FRET alone (not colocalization) detects this, and the article shows FRET can be negative for large complexes like Rev-CRM1 (130 kDa) even when colocalization is real When images lack a second channel or a negative control condition (e.g., free YFP) — the statistical threshold and random-overlap distribution cannot be built When individual adjacent pixels can be assumed independent — scrambling single pixels instead of PSF-sized blocks violates the method's correlation assumption

Precursors already have exact mass matches to catalogued PFAS — use exact mass matching rather than reverse fragment screening Data are not LC-HRMS/MS feature tables from mass spectrometry (e.g. non-MS fluorine assays) Analysis goal is general metabolomics or lipidomics — FluoroMatch defaults target PFAS unless Lipid <- TRUE is explicitly set http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Automated non-targeted PFAS annotation using FluoroMatch 2.0 (LC-HRMS/MS), which chains feature detection, blank filtering, exact mass matching to the EPA PFAS list, mass defect filtering, homologous series detection, fragment screening, and reverse fragment screening into a single scored annotation workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Automated non-targeted PFAS annotation using FluoroMatch 2.0 (LC-HRMS/MS), which chains feature detection, blank filtering, exact mass matching to the EPA PFAS list, mass defect filtering, homologous series detection, fragment screening, and reverse fragment screening into a single scored annotation workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Precursors already have exact mass matches to catalogued PFAS — use exact mass matching rather than reverse fragment screening Data are not LC-HRMS/MS feature tables from mass spectrometry (e.g. non-MS fluorine assays) Analysis goal is general metabolomics or lipidomics — FluoroMatch defaults target PFAS unless Lipid <- TRUE is explicitly set

skills.description: Use when LC-HRMS/MS feature tables and MS/MS spectra (e.g. AFFF injections, mzML/raw acquisitions) have been processed through FluoroMatch Modular steps and per-feature PFAS annotation confidence levels (score A) must be assigned.
skills.name: fluoromatch-scoring-framework-application
skills.search_text: fluoromatch-scoring-framework-application Use when LC-HRMS/MS feature tables and MS/MS spectra (e.g. AFFF injections, mzML/raw acquisitions) have been processed through FluoroMatch Modular steps and per-feature PFAS annotation confidence levels (score A) must be assigned. Input is not PFAS analysis: FluoroMatch defaults to PFAS analysis only when both Lipid and TWeen_pos flags are FALSE; set these appropriately or the scoring will target the wrong analyte class. You only need raw feature detection/blank filtering without annotation confidence — the scoring framework is a downstream layer and requires the full screening evidence first. Data are from a targeted suspect-screening release of FluoroMatch (original release) rather than the truly non-targeted FluoroMatch 2.0 workflows. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Apply the FluoroMatch 2.0 scoring framework to LC-HRMS/MS feature evidence (exact mass, mass defect, homologous series, class-based MS/MS and fragment screening) to assign per-feature confidence levels for PFAS annotations. It reduces overreporting by integrating all evidence layers into a single confidence score, e.g. score A annotations in AFFF iterative-exclusion injections. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Apply the FluoroMatch 2.0 scoring framework to LC-HRMS/MS feature evidence (exact mass, mass defect, homologous series, class-based MS/MS and fragment screening) to assign per-feature confidence levels for PFAS annotations. It reduces overreporting by integrating all evidence layers into a single confidence score, e.g. score A annotations in AFFF iterative-exclusion injections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not PFAS analysis: FluoroMatch defaults to PFAS analysis only when both Lipid and TWeen_pos flags are FALSE; set these appropriately or the scoring will target the wrong analyte class. You only need raw feature detection/blank filtering without annotation confidence — the scoring framework is a downstream layer and requires the full screening evidence first. Data are from a targeted suspect-screening release of FluoroMatch (original release) rather than the truly non-targeted FluoroMatch 2.0 workflows.

skills.description: Use when an SBML genome-scale model integrates a virus and host (e.g. iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2) and you need host-optimum vs virus-optimum FBA/FVA flux comparisons to quantify which host pathways the virus hijacks.
skills.name: flux-balance-analysis-of-virus-host-models
skills.search_text: flux-balance-analysis-of-virus-host-models Use when an SBML genome-scale model integrates a virus and host (e.g. iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2) and you need host-optimum vs virus-optimum FBA/FVA flux comparisons to quantify which host pathways the virus hijacks. Input is a single-organism model with no integrated viral biomass/production reaction — there is no virus-optimum condition to compare against. The goal is chokepoint or dead-end-metabolite analysis for drug-target prioritisation — use findCPcli's chokepoint/DEM workflow instead of host-vs-virus FVA comparison. Kinetic or dynamical analysis of the model is required — FBA/FVA only yields steady-state flux bounds, not time-course behaviour. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Runs FBA and FVA with COBRApy/GLPK on the SBML-encoded integrated human airway epithelial cell/SARS-CoV-2 model (iHsaEC21+virus, 3,752 reactions, 4,660 genes) to compare host fluxes at host-optimum versus virus-optimum growth, revealing host viability collapse and pathway-level flux increases (e.g. 277% in lipid metabolism). metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Runs FBA and FVA with COBRApy/GLPK on the SBML-encoded integrated human airway epithelial cell/SARS-CoV-2 model (iHsaEC21+virus, 3,752 reactions, 4,660 genes) to compare host fluxes at host-optimum versus virus-optimum growth, revealing host viability collapse and pathway-level flux increases (e.g. 277% in lipid metabolism).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-organism model with no integrated viral biomass/production reaction — there is no virus-optimum condition to compare against. The goal is chokepoint or dead-end-metabolite analysis for drug-target prioritisation — use findCPcli's chokepoint/DEM workflow instead of host-vs-virus FVA comparison. Kinetic or dynamical analysis of the model is required — FBA/FVA only yields steady-state flux bounds, not time-course behaviour.

skills.description: Use when you have multiple gap-filled genome-scale metabolic models (SBML GENREs, e.g. Reconstructor outputs) and need to compare their functional metabolic behavior by sampling flux distributions and clustering/ordinating the samples.
skills.name: flux-balance-analysis-sampling
skills.search_text: flux-balance-analysis-sampling Use when you have multiple gap-filled genome-scale metabolic models (SBML GENREs, e.g. Reconstructor outputs) and need to compare their functional metabolic behavior by sampling flux distributions and clustering/ordinating the samples. Input is a single model with no comparison set — flux sampling plus NMDS is designed for cross-model functional comparison, not single-model analysis Models lack gap-filling or use inconsistent naming/media across the set, making sampled flux distributions non-comparable Input is raw annotation data (e.g. unannotated .fasta) rather than assembled metabolic models — reconstruct first with Reconstructor http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Samples steady-state flux distributions from genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) built with Reconstructor, so that functional metabolic differences between strains, species, and classes of bacteria can be quantified and ordinated (e.g., via NMDS) rather than inferred from network content alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Samples steady-state flux distributions from genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) built with Reconstructor, so that functional metabolic differences between strains, species, and classes of bacteria can be quantified and ordinated (e.g., via NMDS) rather than inferred from network content alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single model with no comparison set — flux sampling plus NMDS is designed for cross-model functional comparison, not single-model analysis Models lack gap-filling or use inconsistent naming/media across the set, making sampled flux distributions non-comparable Input is raw annotation data (e.g. unannotated .fasta) rather than assembled metabolic models — reconstruct first with Reconstructor

skills.search_text: flux-balance-analysis-simulation Use when a steady-state genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format needs its maximal biomass or growth objective computed, or when host/virus trade-offs must be quantified by optimizing alternate biomass objectives. The question concerns reaction reversibility or flux ranges rather than a single optimal objective value — use Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) to update flux bounds instead The model requires prior refinement (e.g. dead-end metabolite removal or FVA-refined bounds) before meaningful growth optimization is possible The goal is identifying chokepoint or bottleneck drug-target reactions, which findCPcli computes from topology plus FVA dynamics rather than a single FBA optimum http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Run constraint-based Flux Balance Analysis (FBA) on genome-scale metabolic models (e.g. the iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 and iAB-AMØ-1410+SARS-CoV-2 integrated models) with COBRApy 0.16.0 and the GLPK solver to compute maximal host biomass maintenance and maximum viral growth rates, and to test viral non-viability by fixing viral flux at its optimum. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Run constraint-based Flux Balance Analysis (FBA) on genome-scale metabolic models (e.g. the iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 and iAB-AMØ-1410+SARS-CoV-2 integrated models) with COBRApy 0.16.0 and the GLPK solver to compute maximal host biomass maintenance and maximum viral growth rates, and to test viral non-viability by fixing viral flux at its optimum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns reaction reversibility or flux ranges rather than a single optimal objective value — use Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) to update flux bounds instead The model requires prior refinement (e.g. dead-end metabolite removal or FVA-refined bounds) before meaningful growth optimization is possible The goal is identifying chokepoint or bottleneck drug-target reactions, which findCPcli computes from topology plus FVA dynamics rather than a single FBA optimum

skills.description: Use when a gut microbiota SBML metabolic model must be simulated to derive boundary-metabolite fluxes that will modify exchange-reaction lower bounds of a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D) via M2R/cobrapy.
skills.name: flux-balance-analysis-simulation
skills.search_text: flux-balance-analysis-simulation Use when a gut microbiota SBML metabolic model must be simulated to derive boundary-metabolite fluxes that will modify exchange-reaction lower bounds of a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D) via M2R/cobrapy. The model has no external/boundary (exchange) reactions annotated, so no per-metabolite in-/out-fluxes can be extracted. The goal is a standalone FBA of the human GEM itself (e.g. RECON3D) rather than deriving microbiota fluxes to modify its exchange-reaction lower bounds. The input is already a normalized flux table produced by a prior M2R run, so re-aggregation would double-transform the values. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Run Flux Balance Analysis on a gut microbiota metabolic model (SBML loaded into cobrapy) to obtain per-metabolite in- and out-fluxes at external reactions, which M2R aggregates and normalizes (divide by maximum flux, multiply by e.g. 1000) before writing them into the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human GEM like RECON3D. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: Run Flux Balance Analysis on a gut microbiota metabolic model (SBML loaded into cobrapy) to obtain per-metabolite in- and out-fluxes at external reactions, which M2R aggregates and normalizes (divide by maximum flux, multiply by e.g. 1000) before writing them into the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human GEM like RECON3D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model has no external/boundary (exchange) reactions annotated, so no per-metabolite in-/out-fluxes can be extracted. The goal is a standalone FBA of the human GEM itself (e.g. RECON3D) rather than deriving microbiota fluxes to modify its exchange-reaction lower bounds. skills.description: Use when building community metabolic models where member flux bounds must scale with each member's abundance, and the SBML format's inability to represent variable flux bounds would otherwise force hard-coded bounds.
skills.name: flux-bound-encoding-via-dummy-metabolites
skills.search_text: flux-bound-encoding-via-dummy-metabolites Use when building community metabolic models where member flux bounds must scale with each member's abundance, and the SBML format's inability to represent variable flux bounds would otherwise force hard-coded bounds. If flux bounds never need to vary with abundance (a fixed abundance profile suffices), hard-coded bounds in the original SBML are simpler and adequate If the target model format supports variable flux bounds natively, the bound-free linearization adds unnecessary dummy metabolites and reactions http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 PyCoMo converts each genome-scale member model into an equivalent bound-free form in which fixed lower/upper flux bounds are encoded as stoichiometric coefficients of compartment-specific dummy metabolites, coupled to reactions whose fluxes equal the member's mass fraction. This lets abundance-dependent bounds remain SBML-compliant while making effective flux limits scale dynamically with community composition. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: PyCoMo converts each genome-scale member model into an equivalent bound-free form in which fixed lower/upper flux bounds are encoded as stoichiometric coefficients of compartment-specific dummy metabolites, coupled to reactions whose fluxes equal the member's mass fraction. This lets abundance-dependent bounds remain SBML-compliant while making effective flux limits scale dynamically with community composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If flux bounds never need to vary with abundance (a fixed abundance profile suffices), hard-coded bounds in the original SBML are simpler and adequate If the target model format supports variable flux bounds natively, the bound-free linearization adds unnecessary dummy metabolites and reactions

skills.name: flux-confidence-interval-estimation
skills.search_text: flux-confidence-interval-estimation Use when isotopologue distribution tables from a stable-isotope labeling time course (e.g., Arabidopsis roots labeled with [13C5,15N2]glutamine over 0–8 h) must be fitted by INST-MFA to obtain fluxes with 95% CIs and to compare single- vs. dual-isotope tracer designs. Input is raw HRMS spectra or an unprocessed XCMS/MZmine2 feature table — data must first be post-processed with SIMPEL into natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions Data were acquired at nominal mass resolution and cannot resolve dual-labeled isotopologues, since combining multiple heavy isotopes is limited when nominal m/z values are recorded The system is at isotopic stationary state, where INST-MFA fitting of transient labeling trajectories over a 0–8 h time course is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Estimate metabolic fluxes and their 95% confidence intervals by isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST-MFA) in INCA, using isotopologue distribution tables exported from SIMPEL, and quantify how parallel 13C/15N or dual 13C15N tracer designs narrow CIs relative to single-13C designs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42003-024-05844-z

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw HRMS spectra or an unprocessed XCMS/MZmine2 feature table — data must first be post-processed with SIMPEL into natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions Data were acquired at nominal mass resolution and cannot resolve dual-labeled isotopologues, since combining multiple heavy isotopes is limited when nominal m/z values are recorded The system is at isotopic stationary state, where INST-MFA fitting of transient labeling trajectories over a 0–8 h time course is inappropriate

skills.description: Use when you have cell-relative SBML metabolic models (e.g. ENGRO2_MCF102A.xml, ENGRO2_MCF7.xml) already split into irreversible format, and you need a large ensemble of steady-state flux solutions (order 1e6) per sample to compare flux distributions between cell lines.
skills.name: flux-distribution-batch-sampling-management
skills.search_text: flux-distribution-batch-sampling-management Use when you have cell-relative SBML metabolic models (e.g. ENGRO2_MCF102A.xml, ENGRO2_MCF7.xml) already split into irreversible format, and you need a large ensemble of steady-state flux solutions (order 1e6) per sample to compare flux distributions between cell lines. Do not use when the goal is deterministic flux prediction (e.g. FBA) rather than characterizing the full feasible flux region via sampling. Do not use on the generic ENGRO2 model before rasIntegration: the sampling is defined per cell-relative model with RAS and ysi constraints already integrated. Do not use when only a small number of flux solutions is needed — the batch machinery and thinning parameter are designed for very large (order 1e6) ensembles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 Generates feasible flux distribution (FFD) datasets by sampling the steady-state flux region of cell-relative constraint-based models with optGpSampler via COBRApy, executed in configurable batches with a growth-yield lower bound on the biomass reaction, producing per-cell-line sampled-solution CSV files used downstream for Mann-Whitney U testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009337
skills.summary: Generates feasible flux distribution (FFD) datasets by sampling the steady-state flux region of cell-relative constraint-based models with optGpSampler via COBRApy, executed in configurable batches with a growth-yield lower bound on the biomass reaction, producing per-cell-line sampled-solution CSV files used downstream for Mann-Whitney U testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use when the goal is deterministic flux prediction (e.g. FBA) rather than characterizing the full feasible flux region via sampling. Do not use on the generic ENGRO2 model before rasIntegration: the sampling is defined per cell-relative model with RAS and ysi constraints already integrated. Do not use when only a small number of flux solutions is needed — the batch machinery and thinning parameter are designed for very large (order 1e6) ensembles.

skills.description: Use when an FBA solution from a gut microbiota metabolic model must be converted into per-metabolite scaled fluxes to set exchange-reaction bounds in a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. Recon3D) via M2R.
skills.name: flux-normalization-scaling
skills.search_text: flux-normalization-scaling Use when an FBA solution from a gut microbiota metabolic model must be converted into per-metabolite scaled fluxes to set exchange-reaction bounds in a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. Recon3D) via M2R. You need reaction-level or direction-resolved fluxes: aggregation collapses the in- and out-fluxes of each boundary metabolite into a single combined value. Your goal is to modify constraints other than the lower bounds of exchange reactions — M2R's design only adjusts exchange-reaction lower bounds. The model is not a gut microbiota metabolic model loadable in cobrapy (e.g. non-SBML formats or non-metabolic reconstructions). http://edamontology.org/topic_3400 A flux post-processing step from the M2R workflow: aggregate the FBA in- and out-fluxes of every metabolite participating in a gut microbe's external (boundary) reactions, then scale them so the maximum equals a desired value (e.g. 1000) for use in modifying exchange-reaction lower bounds in a human GEM such as Recon3D. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: A flux post-processing step from the M2R workflow: aggregate the FBA in- and out-fluxes of every metabolite participating in a gut microbe's external (boundary) reactions, then scale them so the maximum equals a desired value (e.g. 1000) for use in modifying exchange-reaction lower bounds in a human GEM such as Recon3D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need reaction-level or direction-resolved fluxes: aggregation collapses the in- and out-fluxes of each boundary metabolite into a single combined value. Your goal is to modify constraints other than the lower bounds of exchange reactions — M2R's design only adjusts exchange-reaction lower bounds. The model is not a gut microbiota metabolic model loadable in cobrapy (e.g. non-SBML formats or non-metabolic reconstructions).

skills.description: Use when you need a nonparametric, distribution-free classification of per-reaction flux differences between two biological conditions, starting from constraint-based models whose feasible regions have been constrained by RAS scores, extracellular flux ratios, and nutrient-availability bounds.
skills.name: flux-sampling-mann-whitney-testing
skills.search_text: flux-sampling-mann-whitney-testing Use when you need a nonparametric, distribution-free classification of per-reaction flux differences between two biological conditions, starting from constraint-based models whose feasible regions have been constrained by RAS scores, extracellular flux ratios, and nutrient-availability bounds. When the difference you are testing is on transcriptomics-derived RAS scores rather than sampled fluxes — INTEGRATE uses a parametric t-test (rasTtest) for that layer, not the Mann-Whitney U test When the input model has not been constrained by RAS, extracellular flux ratios, and medium bounds — sampling the unconstrained feasible region would not reflect the cell-relative flux states the pipeline is designed to compare When you lack enough sampled solutions per condition for the Mann-Whitney U test to be informative (e.g. nSamples too small relative to the feasible-region complexity) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Randomly sample the feasible flux region of each cell-relative constraint-based model and run a pairwise Mann-Whitney U test on the sampled flux distributions to classify whether each reaction's flux differs between cell lines (the FFD / flux fold-difference layer of the INTEGRATE pipeline). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009337
skills.summary: Randomly sample the feasible flux region of each cell-relative constraint-based model and run a pairwise Mann-Whitney U test on the sampled flux distributions to classify whether each reaction's flux differs between cell lines (the FFD / flux fold-difference layer of the INTEGRATE pipeline).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the difference you are testing is on transcriptomics-derived RAS scores rather than sampled fluxes — INTEGRATE uses a parametric t-test (rasTtest) for that layer, not the Mann-Whitney U test When the input model has not been constrained by RAS, extracellular flux ratios, and medium bounds — sampling the unconstrained feasible region would not reflect the cell-relative flux states the pipeline is designed to compare When you lack enough sampled solutions per condition for the Mann-Whitney U test to be informative (e.g. nSamples too small relative to the feasible-region complexity)

skills.description: Use when you have a PyCoMo-generated community metabolic model (e.g. SBML) and need to identify which cross-feeding metabolites and member-to-member exchange routes are feasible across the whole space of abundance profiles, rather than at a single fixed composition.
skills.name: flux-variability-analysis-community-models
skills.search_text: flux-variability-analysis-community-models Use when you have a PyCoMo-generated community metabolic model (e.g. SBML) and need to identify which cross-feeding metabolites and member-to-member exchange routes are feasible across the whole space of abundance profiles, rather than at a single fixed composition. You want a single flux distribution at a fixed abundance profile — use standard FBA instead of variable-abundance FVA The model is a single-species (non-community) metabolic model with no member-specific exchange compartment You need to predict the maximum growth rate at a given abundance profile rather than enumerate feasible exchange interactions http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Enumerates all feasible exchange metabolites and pairwise cross-feeding interactions in a compartmentalized community metabolic model by running COBRApy flux variability analysis (FVA) over member-specific exchange reactions under variable community composition, as enabled by PyCoMo's fixed growth-rate / variable abundance model structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: Enumerates all feasible exchange metabolites and pairwise cross-feeding interactions in a compartmentalized community metabolic model by running COBRApy flux variability analysis (FVA) over member-specific exchange reactions under variable community composition, as enabled by PyCoMo's fixed growth-rate / variable abundance model structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want a single flux distribution at a fixed abundance profile — use standard FBA instead of variable-abundance FVA The model is a single-species (non-community) metabolic model with no member-specific exchange compartment You need to predict the maximum growth rate at a given abundance profile rather than enumerate feasible exchange interactions

skills.description: Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 or the Renz et al macrophage model) needs flux-bound refinement before reaction reversibility classification, bottleneck or essential-reaction computation.
skills.name: flux-variability-analysis-flux-bound-refinement
skills.search_text: flux-variability-analysis-flux-bound-refinement Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 or the Renz et al macrophage model) needs flux-bound refinement before reaction reversibility classification, bottleneck or essential-reaction computation. The analysis goal is purely topological chokepoint computation on the unrefined model variant — the article explicitly contrasts the plain model with the FVA-refined variant No LP solver infrastructure is available, since FVA requires repeated LP solves (GLPK in this workflow) The objective is host biomass maintenance in the absence of the virus, which is computed by plain FBA rather than FVA-based refinement Runs Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) on SBML genome-scale metabolic models with COBRApy and GLPK to compute lower and upper flux bounds for every reaction, producing FVA-refined model variants that support downstream findCPcli analyses (bottleneck/chokepoint and essential-reaction identification). metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Runs Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) on SBML genome-scale metabolic models with COBRApy and GLPK to compute lower and upper flux bounds for every reaction, producing FVA-refined model variants that support downstream findCPcli analyses (bottleneck/chokepoint and essential-reaction identification).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is purely topological chokepoint computation on the unrefined model variant — the article explicitly contrasts the plain model with the FVA-refined variant No LP solver infrastructure is available, since FVA requires repeated LP solves (GLPK in this workflow) The objective is host biomass maintenance in the absence of the virus, which is computed by plain FBA rather than FVA-based refinement

skills.search_text: flux-variability-analysis-reaction-directionality Use when a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format (e.g. BioModels MODEL2007210001) must have its flux bounds refined by FVA before reaction directionality classification or chokepoint/drug-target analysis. When the goal is basic Flux Balance Analysis of biomass or growth rate only — FVA refinement of flux bounds is unnecessary When the model has not been checked for dead-end metabolites and the analysis requires that every bottleneck reaction be balanced by at least one other reaction http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Compute per-reaction flux bounds via Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) and use the refined bounds to classify each reaction of a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21) as reversible, non-reversible, or dead, which is the prerequisite for computing growth-dependent chokepoint (bottleneck) reactions with findCPcli. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Compute per-reaction flux bounds via Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) and use the refined bounds to classify each reaction of a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21) as reversible, non-reversible, or dead, which is the prerequisite for computing growth-dependent chokepoint (bottleneck) reactions with findCPcli.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is basic Flux Balance Analysis of biomass or growth rate only — FVA refinement of flux bounds is unnecessary When the model has not been checked for dead-end metabolites and the analysis requires that every bottleneck reaction be balanced by at least one other reaction

skills.search_text: fmp10-derivative-annotation Use when MALDI-TOF spectra acquired with the FMP-10 matrix (or other matrix like DHB) contain unannotated m/z peaks and metabolite identities are needed before spatial mapping or integration with transcriptomics. Data is high-resolution (orbitrap/FT-ICR) SM data where METASPACE or pySM FDR-based annotation is more appropriate — the article notes those tools 'are optimised for SM data generated via high resolution instruments such as Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance or orbitrap analysers' and 'do not yet apply to most data obtained with time-of-flight (TOF) analysers' (reverse: use this for TOF data). Annotations already exist for every m/z value in the SPM assay and only downstream clustering/integration is needed — no re-annotation is required.
