skills.name: gaussian-kernel-regression-agreement-fitting
skills.search_text: gaussian-kernel-regression-agreement-fitting Use when you have matched per-target log2 peak-area tables from two integration methods (e.g., an open-source R pipeline vs. vendor software such as Xcalibur) and need to quantify whether the automated tool reproduces expert manual integration. Input is untargeted feature-table output (e.g., from xcms, MZmine, or OpenMS) rather than matched targeted peak areas from two integration methods There is no vendor/expert reference integration to compare against, so agreement cannot be assessed Peak areas are on the raw (non-log2) scale and no matched QC replicates exist, making Spearman/kernel-regression and CV comparison inappropriate as implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantitative agreement analysis between automated (TARDIS) and vendor (Xcalibur) log2 peak areas, using per-target Spearman correlation, Gaussian kernel regression (R2 and slope), and paired comparison of QC-replicate coefficients of variation across cohorts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00567
skills.summary: Quantitative agreement analysis between automated (TARDIS) and vendor (Xcalibur) log2 peak areas, using per-target Spearman correlation, Gaussian kernel regression (R2 and slope), and paired comparison of QC-replicate coefficients of variation across cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is untargeted feature-table output (e.g., from xcms, MZmine, or OpenMS) rather than matched targeted peak areas from two integration methods There is no vendor/expert reference integration to compare against, so agreement cannot be assessed Peak areas are on the raw (non-log2) scale and no matched QC replicates exist, making Spearman/kernel-regression and CV comparison inappropriate as implemented

skills.description: Use when fitting a calibration curve from calibration-standard injections (per-feature peak_area from a FeatureDB/mzML report) for targeted LC-MS/MS quantitation where a generic linear fit is insufficient.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-estimation
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-estimation Use when fitting a calibration curve from calibration-standard injections (per-feature peak_area from a FeatureDB/mzML report) for targeted LC-MS/MS quantitation where a generic linear fit is insufficient. Data are already quantified (feature table with concentrations) — calibration fitting is the wrong step; move to accuracy/precision or QC reporting. Experiment is untargeted FIA-MS full-scan unknown discovery, where the SmartPeak tutorial workflow is FIAMS_FullScan_Unknowns rather than calibration-based quantitation. A vendor tool's generic linear calibration is adequate and you only need peak picking, not curve optimization. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Non-linear Gaussian-Mixtures estimation of the metabolite calibration curve (concentration vs. analyte-to-internal-standard response), as implemented in SmartPeak's calibration step for targeted metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03421
skills.summary: Non-linear Gaussian-Mixtures estimation of the metabolite calibration curve (concentration vs. analyte-to-internal-standard response), as implemented in SmartPeak's calibration step for targeted metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already quantified (feature table with concentrations) — calibration fitting is the wrong step; move to accuracy/precision or QC reporting. Experiment is untargeted FIA-MS full-scan unknown discovery, where the SmartPeak tutorial workflow is FIAMS_FullScan_Unknowns rather than calibration-based quantitation. A vendor tool's generic linear calibration is adequate and you only need peak picking, not curve optimization.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the noise robustness of computed isotopologue profiles (e.g., single-tracer 13C vs multi-tracer 13C/18O glucose moiety models) and you need simulated replicate datasets at several error magnitudes before renormalization.
skills.name: gaussian-noise-injection-at-multiple-sigma-levels
skills.search_text: gaussian-noise-injection-at-multiple-sigma-levels Use when benchmarking the noise robustness of computed isotopologue profiles (e.g., single-tracer 13C vs multi-tracer 13C/18O glucose moiety models) and you need simulated replicate datasets at several error magnitudes before renormalization. Input is real measured MS isotopologue data rather than a model-computed (Eq. 1) isotopologue profile — noise injection is a simulation benchmark, not a correction step for observed data The error model of interest is multiplicative, count-based (Poisson), or instrument-specific rather than additive and normally distributed The goal is moiety model optimization or AICc-based model ranking of experimental data (that is the moiety_modeling optimize/rank workflow, not the simulation benchmark) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Simulates measurement noise on model-predicted isotopologue intensities by adding thresholded, normally distributed random error at escalating sigma levels (0.001, 0.01, 0.1) across 100 replicate datasets, to benchmark how error propagates in single-tracer versus multi-tracer moiety models. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: Simulates measurement noise on model-predicted isotopologue intensities by adding thresholded, normally distributed random error at escalating sigma levels (0.001, 0.01, 0.1) across 100 replicate datasets, to benchmark how error propagates in single-tracer versus multi-tracer moiety models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real measured MS isotopologue data rather than a model-computed (Eq. 1) isotopologue profile — noise injection is a simulation benchmark, not a correction step for observed data The error model of interest is multiplicative, count-based (Poisson), or instrument-specific rather than additive and normally distributed The goal is moiety model optimization or AICc-based model ranking of experimental data (that is the moiety_modeling optimize/rank workflow, not the simulation benchmark)

skills.description: Use when a paired microbiome-metabolome model has been trained in two configurations (full vs. annotated-subset outputs) and you must quantify whether multivariate learning confers robustness to input perturbation before comparing per-metabolite SCCs.
skills.name: gaussian-noise-robustness-testing
skills.search_text: gaussian-noise-robustness-testing Use when a paired microbiome-metabolome model has been trained in two configurations (full vs. annotated-subset outputs) and you must quantify whether multivariate learning confers robustness to input perturbation before comparing per-metabolite SCCs. When the input metabolome contains no unannotated metabolites — there is no full-vs-annotated contrast to test, so multivariate-transfer benefit cannot be assessed. When the analysis goal is direct method benchmarking against MelonnPan or NED rather than testing the noise robustness of the multivariate-learning hypothesis. When inputs are already perturbed or quality-filtered metagenomic features without the original abundance matrix — additive Gaussian noise re-perturbation on transformed data would confound the CLR/None preprocessing. A robustness evaluation protocol for microbiome→metabolome predictors (MiMeNet) in which trained models are re-evaluated on microbiome input profiles perturbed with additive Gaussian noise, to test whether multi-task learning on the full metabolite set (8848 metabolites) yields a model more robust than one trained only on the 466 annotated metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009021
skills.summary: A robustness evaluation protocol for microbiome→metabolome predictors (MiMeNet) in which trained models are re-evaluated on microbiome input profiles perturbed with additive Gaussian noise, to test whether multi-task learning on the full metabolite set (8848 metabolites) yields a model more robust than one trained only on the 466 annotated metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input metabolome contains no unannotated metabolites — there is no full-vs-annotated contrast to test, so multivariate-transfer benefit cannot be assessed. When the analysis goal is direct method benchmarking against MelonnPan or NED rather than testing the noise robustness of the multivariate-learning hypothesis. When inputs are already perturbed or quality-filtered metagenomic features without the original abundance matrix — additive Gaussian noise re-perturbation on transformed data would confound the CLR/None preprocessing.

skills.description: Use when an ion chromatogram's targeted compound peak is coeluted with other peaks (e.g., isomers sharing a transition with close RTs) and per-peak abundances must be separated rather than summed.
skills.name: gaussian-peak-deconvolution
skills.search_text: gaussian-peak-deconvolution Use when an ion chromatogram's targeted compound peak is coeluted with other peaks (e.g., isomers sharing a transition with close RTs) and per-peak abundances must be separated rather than summed. The targeted compound peak is isolated with no coelution — simple integration/baseline methods suffice Peaks are so noisy or unevenly sampled that Gaussian shape assumptions fail (MRMkit and Skyline had problematic quantitation of noisy peaks and peaks with unevenly sampled signals) A saturated peak — saturated signals are excluded from regression in MRMQuant as unreliable, so deconvolved abundances would not be trustworthy http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Automatic deconvolution of coeluted peaks in MRM ion chromatograms: MRMQuant fits Gaussian models (height + sigma) at findpeaks tip locations so the summed Gaussians minimize the sum of differences with the extracted coeluted signal union, then integrates each fitted Gaussian (after background removal) as the compound's abundance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Automatic deconvolution of coeluted peaks in MRM ion chromatograms: MRMQuant fits Gaussian models (height + sigma) at findpeaks tip locations so the summed Gaussians minimize the sum of differences with the extracted coeluted signal union, then integrates each fitted Gaussian (after background removal) as the compound's abundance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The targeted compound peak is isolated with no coelution — simple integration/baseline methods suffice Peaks are so noisy or unevenly sampled that Gaussian shape assumptions fail (MRMkit and Skyline had problematic quantitation of noisy peaks and peaks with unevenly sampled signals) A saturated peak — saturated signals are excluded from regression in MRMQuant as unreliable, so deconvolved abundances would not be trustworthy

skills.description: Use when a 1D MS signal (e.g., XIC or ATD extracted from an MZA/HDF5 file via mzapy) contains overlapping or noise-affected peaks that need Gaussian model fitting, peak-parameter estimation, or SNR-based peak quality assessment.
skills.name: gaussian-peak-modeling
skills.search_text: gaussian-peak-modeling Use when a 1D MS signal (e.g., XIC or ATD extracted from an MZA/HDF5 file via mzapy) contains overlapping or noise-affected peaks that need Gaussian model fitting, peak-parameter estimation, or SNR-based peak quality assessment. The data is still raw multidimensional MS/IMS spectra — mzapy's peak functions operate on 1D signals; extract an XIC or ATD first (e.g., collect_xic_arrays_by_mz) The peaks are known to be non-Gaussian in shape (e.g., asymmetric chromatographic peaks), where find_peaks_1d_gauss model fits would be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fit and validate Gaussian peak models on 1D mass spectrometry signals (e.g., extracted ion chromatograms or arrival time distributions from MZA/HDF5 files) using mzapy's peaks module, which includes find_peaks_1d_gauss, calc_gauss_psnr, and calc_peak_area alongside local-maximum peak detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c01653
skills.summary: Fit and validate Gaussian peak models on 1D mass spectrometry signals (e.g., extracted ion chromatograms or arrival time distributions from MZA/HDF5 files) using mzapy's peaks module, which includes find_peaks_1d_gauss, calc_gauss_psnr, and calc_peak_area alongside local-maximum peak detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is still raw multidimensional MS/IMS spectra — mzapy's peak functions operate on 1D signals; extract an XIC or ATD first (e.g., collect_xic_arrays_by_mz) The peaks are known to be non-Gaussian in shape (e.g., asymmetric chromatographic peaks), where find_peaks_1d_gauss model fits would be invalid

skills.description: Use when comparing feature counts from LC-MS processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine) and you need an objective peak-quality metric to determine whether extra features are genuinely better coverage or low-quality peaks.
skills.name: gaussian-peak-shape-fitting
skills.search_text: gaussian-peak-shape-fitting Use when comparing feature counts from LC-MS processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine) and you need an objective peak-quality metric to determine whether extra features are genuinely better coverage or low-quality peaks. When input is raw vendor data (e.g., Thermo .RAW) rather than centroided mzML plus an existing feature table — format conversion via ThermoRawFileParser or msConvert must happen first When working with low-resolution data, which asari's mass-track framework does not support When the goal is MS/MS identification or annotation rather than peak-quality assessment of detected features Recompute a Gaussian peak-shape fitness score for each reported LC-MS feature by fitting a Gaussian model to the EIC intensity list over the peak region padded by 3 s on each side, then threshold at 0.5 to separate good-quality peaks from bad ones. This explains why different processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine) report very different feature counts: the surplus features are low-quality, non-reproducible peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Recompute a Gaussian peak-shape fitness score for each reported LC-MS feature by fitting a Gaussian model to the EIC intensity list over the peak region padded by 3 s on each side, then threshold at 0.5 to separate good-quality peaks from bad ones. This explains why different processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine) report very different feature counts: the surplus features are low-quality, non-reproducible peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input is raw vendor data (e.g., Thermo .RAW) rather than centroided mzML plus an existing feature table — format conversion via ThermoRawFileParser or msConvert must happen first When working with low-resolution data, which asari's mass-track framework does not support When the goal is MS/MS identification or annotation rather than peak-quality assessment of detected features

skills.description: Use when performing untargeted GC × GC–MS peak picking from raw CDF files and false-positive blobs (incomplete peak shapes, sub-threshold S/N) must be discarded before deconvolution by PARAFAC/PARAFAC2.
skills.name: gaussian-peak-shape-validation
skills.search_text: gaussian-peak-shape-validation Use when performing untargeted GC × GC–MS peak picking from raw CDF files and false-positive blobs (incomplete peak shapes, sub-threshold S/N) must be discarded before deconvolution by PARAFAC/PARAFAC2. Input is already a feature/peak table from another tool (e.g. ChromaTOF, GC Image output) rather than raw CDF files — this filter is part of GcDUO's blob detection on raw 4D intensities Analytes of interest are small chromatographic signals with too few characteristic fragments to deconvolute — Gaussian/SNR filtering may discard them (non-detected peaks in the fruitybeer dataset were such small signals) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Validation step in GcDUO's Module II ROI selection for GC × GC–MS data: after inverse-watershed blob detection, candidate 3D peaks (with 2D coordinates) are retained only if their signal-to-noise ratios (SNR1/SNR2 thresholds, e.g. 50 in both dimensions) pass and their chromatographic form conforms to a Gaussian shape with a minimum number of modulation points. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbaf080
skills.summary: Validation step in GcDUO's Module II ROI selection for GC × GC–MS data: after inverse-watershed blob detection, candidate 3D peaks (with 2D coordinates) are retained only if their signal-to-noise ratios (SNR1/SNR2 thresholds, e.g. 50 in both dimensions) pass and their chromatographic form conforms to a Gaussian shape with a minimum number of modulation points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/peak table from another tool (e.g. ChromaTOF, GC Image output) rather than raw CDF files — this filter is part of GcDUO's blob detection on raw 4D intensities Analytes of interest are small chromatographic signals with too few characteristic fragments to deconvolute — Gaussian/SNR filtering may discard them (non-detected peaks in the fruitybeer dataset were such small signals)

skills.description: Use when you must project DNN-predicted retention times to a specific chromatographic method using only ~10 identified molecules with predicted-experimental RT pairs, while also getting credible intervals.
skills.name: gaussian-process-meta-learning-prior-optimization
skills.search_text: gaussian-process-meta-learning-prior-optimization Use when you must project DNN-predicted retention times to a specific chromatographic method using only ~10 identified molecules with predicted-experimental RT pairs, while also getting credible intervals. The target chromatographic method has no identified molecules at all — the target-task update needs experimental-predicted RT pairs from ~10 known molecules You need a point RT prediction from chemical structure alone (that is the DNN regression task on SMRT, not the projection between chromatographic methods) Molecules in the dataset are non-retained (RT < 5 min) and were not excluded — including them distorts the learned prior and scaling http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Meta-learns a GP prior over RT projection functions by minimizing negative Leave-One-Out log predictive probability across PredRet meta-tasks, then adapts it to a target chromatographic method from ~10 identified molecules by estimating only the residual variance. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8
skills.summary: Meta-learns a GP prior over RT projection functions by minimizing negative Leave-One-Out log predictive probability across PredRet meta-tasks, then adapts it to a target chromatographic method from ~10 identified molecules by estimating only the residual variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target chromatographic method has no identified molecules at all — the target-task update needs experimental-predicted RT pairs from ~10 known molecules You need a point RT prediction from chemical structure alone (that is the DNN regression task on SMRT, not the projection between chromatographic methods) Molecules in the dataset are non-retained (RT < 5 min) and were not excluded — including them distorts the learned prior and scaling

skills.description: Use when a sequential optimization loop needs a probabilistic surrogate fitted to small experimental data (e.g., LC gradient parameters vs. separation efficiency) to support acquisition-function-based selection of the next experiment.
skills.name: gaussian-process-surrogate-regression
skills.search_text: gaussian-process-surrogate-regression Use when a sequential optimization loop needs a probabilistic surrogate fitted to small experimental data (e.g., LC gradient parameters vs. separation efficiency) to support acquisition-function-based selection of the next experiment. When the objective lacks a probabilistic surrogate requirement — e.g., raw LC-MS preprocessing (mzML/mzXML reading, MS1/MS2 spectrum extraction, top-signal finding) should use the pyopenms-based pipeline instead of the GP model When experimental data are not from LC gradient optimization against a separation-efficiency metric — the Matern32 kernel and encode-then-scale preprocessing are tuned to BAGO's gradient-encoding scheme When paired MS2 comparison tasks are needed (e.g., spectral similarity via dotProd with mzTol=0.02) — that is a separate function outside the GP surrogate http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fit a Gaussian process regression surrogate (scikit-learn GaussianProcessRegressor with a Matern32 kernel) to encoded LC-gradient inputs and separation-efficiency outputs, forming the probabilistic model BAGO uses to score candidate gradients in its Bayesian optimization loop. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.09.08.556930
skills.summary: Fit a Gaussian process regression surrogate (scikit-learn GaussianProcessRegressor with a Matern32 kernel) to encoded LC-gradient inputs and separation-efficiency outputs, forming the probabilistic model BAGO uses to score candidate gradients in its Bayesian optimization loop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the objective lacks a probabilistic surrogate requirement — e.g., raw LC-MS preprocessing (mzML/mzXML reading, MS1/MS2 spectrum extraction, top-signal finding) should use the pyopenms-based pipeline instead of the GP model When experimental data are not from LC gradient optimization against a separation-efficiency metric — the Matern32 kernel and encode-then-scale preprocessing are tuned to BAGO's gradient-encoding scheme When paired MS2 comparison tasks are needed (e.g., spectral similarity via dotProd with mzTol=0.02) — that is a separate function outside the GP surrogate

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI imzML pixel spectra must be denoised prior to dimensionality reduction/segmentation, and pixel-level noise in the spectral image data needs suppression via Gaussian smoothing as part of the MSIght pre-processing pipeline.
skills.name: gaussian-spatial-smoothing-of-msi-data
skills.search_text: gaussian-spatial-smoothing-of-msi-data Use when raw MALDI-MSI imzML pixel spectra must be denoised prior to dimensionality reduction/segmentation, and pixel-level noise in the spectral image data needs suppression via Gaussian smoothing as part of the MSIght pre-processing pipeline. Input is already pre-processed (TIC-normalized, smoothed, baseline-corrected) MSIght output such as preprocessed_msi_data.imzML — re-smoothing would compound the Gaussian filter The analysis goal is MSIght's other modalities (H&E image pre-processing, linear/non-linear registration, or LC-MS/MS peptide confirmation) rather than MSI spectral pre-processing Only LC-MS/MS or histology data are available and no imzML MSI dataset exists to build a pixel intensity matrix from http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 MSIght's MSI image pre-processing step that applies an iterative Gaussian filter (sigma = 2) to smooth spectral image data from imported MALDI-MSI imzML files, suppressing pixel-level noise between TIC normalization and white tophat baseline correction before downstream dimensionality reduction and segmentation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140

skills.description: Use when the input is centroided GC-CI-MS data acquired with isobutane reagent gas (QqQ SIM/NS, GC-qTOF, or GC-Orbitrap mzML) from 13C stable-isotope labeling experiments and all isotopologues of derivatized metabolites need to be quantified.
skills.name: gc-ci-hrms-isotopologue-integration
skills.search_text: gc-ci-hrms-isotopologue-integration Use when the input is centroided GC-CI-MS data acquired with isobutane reagent gas (QqQ SIM/NS, GC-qTOF, or GC-Orbitrap mzML) from 13C stable-isotope labeling experiments and all isotopologues of derivatized metabolites need to be quantified. skills.description: Use when BiG-SCAPE GCF clustering may have missed related BGCs — e.g., fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters split a known family — and an evolutionary, query-gene-anchored view is needed to recover them.

skills.search_text: gcf-versus-phylogeny-discrepancy-analysis Use when BiG-SCAPE GCF clustering may have missed related BGCs — e.g., fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters split a known family — and an evolutionary, query-gene-anchored view is needed to recover them. When BGCs are too divergent from the query — the CORASON conserved core may collapse to only the query gene, leaving no multi-locus alignment to sort by When the goal is genome-wide GCF calling rather than resolving relationships within one targeted family — BiG-SCAPE network clustering at cutoff 0.3 is the appropriate scalable tool When the CORASON alignment comes back empty (score cutoff too strict or taxonomic scope too broad) without manual parameter reduction — output BGCs would be drawn but not sorted http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Builds a CORASON multi-locus phylogeny around a query gene to identify BGCs that belong to a family (e.g., the detoxin/rimosamide supercluster clan) but were pushed into different BiG-SCAPE GCFs by fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters under the 0.3 distance cutoff. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Builds a CORASON multi-locus phylogeny around a query gene to identify BGCs that belong to a family (e.g., the detoxin/rimosamide supercluster clan) but were pushed into different BiG-SCAPE GCFs by fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters under the 0.3 distance cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When BGCs are too divergent from the query — the CORASON conserved core may collapse to only the query gene, leaving no multi-locus alignment to sort by When the goal is genome-wide GCF calling rather than resolving relationships within one targeted family — BiG-SCAPE network clustering at cutoff 0.3 is the appropriate scalable tool When the CORASON alignment comes back empty (score cutoff too strict or taxonomic scope too broad) without manual parameter reduction — output BGCs would be drawn but not sorted

skills.name: gcms-ei-spectral-edge-analysis
skills.search_text: gcms-ei-spectral-edge-analysis Use when you have EI molecular networking output (edges table and annotated spectra/consensus spectra) from deconvoluted GC-MS data and need to test whether cosine-similarity edges reflect structural similarity based on chemical class, despite the molecular ion often being absent from EI spectra. Data are LC-MS/MS spectra with true MS2 fragmentation and intact precursor masses — standard MolNetEnhancer workflows in pyMolNetEnhancer (classical or feature-based, e.g. with MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) apply directly instead of the GC-MS EI edge-propagation adaptation The analysis goal is deconvolution of co-eluting GC-MS peaks rather than interpretation of an already-deconvoluted molecular network — use the MSHub auto-deconvolution (unsupervised non-negative matrix factorization) workflow instead Every node already carries a confident direct chemical class annotation (e.g. molecular ion present and library-matched), making edge-wise propagation of class labels unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Skill for determining what drives the organization of EI-based cosine similarity molecular networks built from deconvoluted GC-MS data, by propagating chemical class annotations across network edges with a GC-MS-adapted pyMolNetEnhancer workflow and quantifying within-class versus between-class edge fractions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Skill for determining what drives the organization of EI-based cosine similarity molecular networks built from deconvoluted GC-MS data, by propagating chemical class annotations across network edges with a GC-MS-adapted pyMolNetEnhancer workflow and quantifying within-class versus between-class edge fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are LC-MS/MS spectra with true MS2 fragmentation and intact precursor masses — standard MolNetEnhancer workflows in pyMolNetEnhancer (classical or feature-based, e.g. with MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) apply directly instead of the GC-MS EI edge-propagation adaptation The analysis goal is deconvolution of co-eluting GC-MS peaks rather than interpretation of an already-deconvoluted molecular network — use the MSHub auto-deconvolution (unsupervised non-negative matrix factorization) workflow instead Every node already carries a confident direct chemical class annotation (e.g. molecular ion present and library-matched), making edge-wise propagation of class labels unnecessary

skills.description: Use when the input is raw two-dimensional chromatography–MS data (GC–MS or LC–MS, m/z vs retention time) and the goal is untargeted marker-feature identification while avoiding peak-picking false detections.

Input is already a peak-picked feature table — NPFimg's core value is bypassing the conventional peak picking process, which suffers from false peak detections The analysis targets 1-D spectra or data that cannot be arranged as an m/z vs retention time 2-D map http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Processes a two-dimensional GC–MS map (m/z vs retention time) with NPFimg — an image-processing plus machine-learning pipeline — to identify and visualize multivariate chemo-/biomarker features without conventional peak picking, demonstrated on the package's human breath case study at parts-per-billion analyte levels. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03163
skills.summary: Processes a two-dimensional GC–MS map (m/z vs retention time) with NPFimg — an image-processing plus machine-learning pipeline — to identify and visualize multivariate chemo-/biomarker features without conventional peak picking, demonstrated on the package's human breath case study at parts-per-billion analyte levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-picked feature table — NPFimg's core value is bypassing the conventional peak picking process, which suffers from false peak detections The analysis targets 1-D spectra or data that cannot be arranged as an m/z vs retention time 2-D map

skills.description: Use when the input is a raw aggregated GC-MS library-hit CSV from peak detection software (e.g. Agilent Unknowns Analysis) and you must decide which tentative compound identifications to keep before aggregating peak areas across samples.
skills.name: gcms-hit-table-filtering
skills.search_text: gcms-hit-table-filtering Use when the input is a raw aggregated GC-MS library-hit CSV from peak detection software (e.g. Agilent Unknowns Analysis) and you must decide which tentative compound identifications to keep before aggregating peak areas across samples. Input is a vendor-native format that lacks the six required columns (Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) and cannot be reshaped to that schema Data are LC-MS, MS2/MS3, or ion-mobility+MS2 spectra; the article states uafR's algorithms depend on published MS1 spectra and do not yet apply to those acquisition modes You already have a validated feature/area table (e.g. mzExacto output) and only need standardization — use standardizeIt() instead of re-filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filter a GC-MS library-hit table (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) down to candidate compounds by Match.Factor thresholds, cross-sample match strength, and PubChem/SMILES availability before extraction. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0306202
skills.summary: Filter a GC-MS library-hit table (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) down to candidate compounds by Match.Factor thresholds, cross-sample match strength, and PubChem/SMILES availability before extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a vendor-native format that lacks the six required columns (Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) and cannot be reshaped to that schema Data are LC-MS, MS2/MS3, or ion-mobility+MS2 spectra; the article states uafR's algorithms depend on published MS1 spectra and do not yet apply to those acquisition modes You already have a validated feature/area table (e.g. mzExacto output) and only need standardization — use standardizeIt() instead of re-filtering

skills.description: Use when a multiclass metabolomic peak table contains internal standards spiked at known levels (e.g. 6/12/25/50 µL classes) and you need to select or validate a NOREVA processing workflow by whether it preserves the true dose gradient.
skills.name: gcms-internal-standard-dose-gradient-analysis
skills.search_text: gcms-internal-standard-dose-gradient-analysis Use when a multiclass metabolomic peak table contains internal standards spiked at known levels (e.g. 6/12/25/50 µL classes) and you need to select or validate a NOREVA processing workflow by whether it preserves the true dose gradient. The dataset has no reference (spiked internal-standard) metabolites — NOREVA states criterion e (LogFC) cannot be applied in that case, so the dose-gradient validation is infeasible. The study is case–control or time-course rather than multiclass — use NOREVA's corresponding time-course/case-control functions instead of the multiclass IS workflow. Input is raw instrument data rather than a peak table — peak tables must first be generated with tools like XCMS or NMRProc Flow and converted (e.g. via Proteowizard to an open format) before NOREVA can be applied. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates metabolomic data-processing workflows against the known dose gradient of spiked internal-standard metabolites in a GC-MS multiclass dataset (fetal calf serum, MetaboLights MTBLS6), reproducing the NOREVA Figure 6 comparison in which the top-ranked workflow HAM+NON+CUT+[CON-RAN] preserves the 6/12/25/50 µL dose gradient of spiked aspartic acid and malic acid while the last-ranked KNN+NON+LOG+[VAS-LIN] does not. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Validates metabolomic data-processing workflows against the known dose gradient of spiked internal-standard metabolites in a GC-MS multiclass dataset (fetal calf serum, MetaboLights MTBLS6), reproducing the NOREVA Figure 6 comparison in which the top-ranked workflow HAM+NON+CUT+[CON-RAN] preserves the 6/12/25/50 µL dose gradient of spiked aspartic acid and malic acid while the last-ranked KNN+NON+LOG+[VAS-LIN] does not.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no reference (spiked internal-standard) metabolites — NOREVA states criterion e (LogFC) cannot be applied in that case, so the dose-gradient validation is infeasible. The study is case–control or time-course rather than multiclass — use NOREVA's corresponding time-course/case-control functions instead of the multiclass IS workflow. Input is raw instrument data rather than a peak table — peak tables must first be generated with tools like XCMS or NMRProc Flow and converted (e.g. via Proteowizard to an open format) before NOREVA can be applied.

skills.description: Use when starting from a raw GC/MS metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., 3226 features x 57 samples) whose columns are sample groups, and a variance-stabilized, centered feature table is needed before metabolite identification or biomarker discovery.
skills.name: gcms-metabolomics-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: gcms-metabolomics-matrix-preprocessing Use when starting from a raw GC/MS metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., 3226 features x 57 samples) whose columns are sample groups, and a variance-stabilized, centered feature table is needed before metabolite identification or biomarker discovery. Input is already a preprocessed (centered and log-transformed) feature table — reapplying centering/log would distort intensities. Data are not GC/MS metabolomics intensities (e.g., raw instrument files such as mzML) — this skill expects a feature intensity matrix, not spectral acquisition data. The matrix dimensions or sample grouping differ from the pipeline's expectation and no adjustment is planned — the validation step (3226 x 57, 27+30 groups) would fail. Applies the preprocessing stage of the MetPC metabolomics pipeline (DOI 10.3390/metabo9050103) to a raw GC/MS intensity matrix, centering each feature and log-transforming intensities to stabilize variance before downstream metabolite identification and fdr2d-controlled biomarker discovery. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9050103
skills.summary: Applies the preprocessing stage of the MetPC metabolomics pipeline (DOI 10.3390/metabo9050103) to a raw GC/MS intensity matrix, centering each feature and log-transforming intensities to stabilize variance before downstream metabolite identification and fdr2d-controlled biomarker discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed (centered and log-transformed) feature table — reapplying centering/log would distort intensities. Data are not GC/MS metabolomics intensities (e.g., raw instrument files such as mzML) — this skill expects a feature intensity matrix, not spectral acquisition data. The matrix dimensions or sample grouping differ from the pipeline's expectation and no adjustment is planned — the validation step (3226 x 57, 27+30 groups) would fail.

skills.description: Use when clustering co-eluted EI GC-MS compounds into similarity networks: deconvoluted spectra exist but molecular ions/precursor masses are absent, so edges must come from cosine similarity of fragmentation spectra.
skills.name: gcms-molecular-networking
skills.search_text: gcms-molecular-networking Use when clustering co-eluted EI GC-MS compounds into similarity networks: deconvoluted spectra exist but molecular ions/precursor masses are absent, so edges must come from cosine similarity of fragmentation spectra. Input is LC-MS/MS data where precursor/molecular-ion masses are known — precursor-mass-constrained GNPS networking applies instead of EI spectral-similarity networking. Input is raw, undeconvoluted GC-MS data — MSHub auto-deconvolution must precede networking; the networking input must already contain deconvoluted compound fragmentation spectra. The goal is library identification of individual spectra rather than linking spectrally related compounds across a dataset into molecular families. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Builds GNPS molecular networks from deconvoluted EI GC-MS fragmentation spectra without precursor/molecular-ion mass constraints (the molecular ion is usually absent in EI). Pairwise cosine similarity of deconvoluted spectra yields per-dataset networks exported as molecular_networks.graphml for downstream annotation and visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Builds GNPS molecular networks from deconvoluted EI GC-MS fragmentation spectra without precursor/molecular-ion mass constraints (the molecular ion is usually absent in EI). Pairwise cosine similarity of deconvoluted spectra yields per-dataset networks exported as molecular_networks.graphml for downstream annotation and visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is LC-MS/MS data where precursor/molecular-ion masses are known — precursor-mass-constrained GNPS networking applies instead of EI spectral-similarity networking. Input is raw, undeconvoluted GC-MS data — MSHub auto-deconvolution must precede networking; the networking input must already contain deconvoluted compound fragmentation spectra. The goal is library identification of individual spectra rather than linking spectrally related compounds across a dataset into molecular families.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing GC-MS metabolomics data (mzML/mzData/NetCDF) with WiPP and needing to select centWave or matchedFilter peak-detection parameters objectively instead of by hand-tuning.
skills.name: gcms-peak-detection-parameter-optimization
skills.search_text: gcms-peak-detection-parameter-optimization Use when preprocessing GC-MS metabolomics data (mzML/mzData/NetCDF) with WiPP and needing to select centWave or matchedFilter peak-detection parameters objectively instead of by hand-tuning. You already have a manually validated, instrument-specific parameter set — although optimisation can still be rerun, the skill targets objective selection rather than refining user-specified values The samples available for optimisation are the same ones used for classifier training — the README explicitly warns to 'choose different samples as we do not want the parameters to be optimized using the same data the classifier was trained on' The data is not GC-MS raw chromatography-mass spectrometry input (e.g. already-processed peak tables or LC-MS-only workflows outside WiPP's scope) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Unsupervised, classifier-driven grid-search optimisation of embedded peak-picking algorithm parameters (centWave, matchedFilter) in WiPP, where every candidate parameter set's peaks are classified by a trained SVM and scored so the best set is selected without manual input. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9090171
skills.summary: Unsupervised, classifier-driven grid-search optimisation of embedded peak-picking algorithm parameters (centWave, matchedFilter) in WiPP, where every candidate parameter set's peaks are classified by a trained SVM and scored so the best set is selected without manual input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a manually validated, instrument-specific parameter set — although optimisation can still be rerun, the skill targets objective selection rather than refining user-specified values The samples available for optimisation are the same ones used for classifier training — the README explicitly warns to 'choose different samples as we do not want the parameters to be optimized using the same data the classifier was trained on' The data is not GC-MS raw chromatography-mass spectrometry input (e.g. already-processed peak tables or LC-MS-only workflows outside WiPP's scope)

skills.search_text: gcms-preprocessing-results-analysis Use when you have per-algorithm classified peak-detection tables from a WiPP run and need to measure whether the merged/integrated high-quality peak set exceeds each individual algorithm's high-quality yield. Input is a single-algorithm peak table with no classifier quality labels — the comparison requires high-quality-class assignments per algorithm plus the integrated set Data was not preprocessed with WiPP's multi-algorithm peak picking (e.g., an LC-MS feature table or an already-final peak list); this skill analyzes result integration, not raw peak picking The goal is training or annotating the SVM classifier (run_WiPP.sh tr / an stages) rather than evaluating the integrated high-quality peak set http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies how much high-quality peak coverage improves when WiPP integrates results across embedded peak-picking algorithms (centWave and matchedFilter) versus using either algorithm alone, by comparing counts of peaks assigned the high-quality class by the seven-class SVM-based classifier. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9090171
skills.summary: Quantifies how much high-quality peak coverage improves when WiPP integrates results across embedded peak-picking algorithms (centWave and matchedFilter) versus using either algorithm alone, by comparing counts of peaks assigned the high-quality class by the seven-class SVM-based classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-algorithm peak table with no classifier quality labels — the comparison requires high-quality-class assignments per algorithm plus the integrated set Data was not preprocessed with WiPP's multi-algorithm peak picking (e.g., an LC-MS feature table or an already-final peak list); this skill analyzes result integration, not raw peak picking The goal is training or annotating the SVM classifier (run_WiPP.sh tr / an stages) rather than evaluating the integrated high-quality peak set

skills.search_text: gcms-preprocessing-workflow-configuration Use when preprocessing large-scale GC-MS metabolomics datasets (mzML/mzData/NetCDF) where peak detection parameters for embedded algorithms (centWave, matchedFilter) must be optimised without manual tuning. skills.description: Use when measured EI-MS query spectra (e.g., compounds absent from the NIST 2017 library) must be loaded into FastEI and identified by embedding-based nearest-neighbor search against IN_SILICO_LIBRARY.db.
skills.name: gcms-query-spectrum-preparation
skills.search_text: gcms-query-spectrum-preparation Use when measured EI-MS query spectra (e.g., compounds absent from the NIST 2017 library) must be loaded into FastEI and identified by embedding-based nearest-neighbor search against IN_SILICO_LIBRARY.db. The query spectra are not electron ionization GC-MS spectra (FastEI is built and benchmarked specifically for EI mass spectra matched against an in-silico EI-MS library) The target compounds are already covered by an experimental library such as NIST 2017, where conventional spectrum matching is expected to work The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than library matching — FastEI only returns ranked library candidates and cannot propose structures absent from the library http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Prepares measured GC electron-ionization mass spectra so they can be matched by FastEI: query spectra are placed in the FastEI 'spectra' directory, converted to Word2vec spectral embeddings, and searched against the million-scale in-silico library via a prebuilt HNSW index (hnswlib, M = 64, efConstruction = 600, ef = 300). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Prepares measured GC electron-ionization mass spectra so they can be matched by FastEI: query spectra are placed in the FastEI 'spectra' directory, converted to Word2vec spectral embeddings, and searched against the million-scale in-silico library via a prebuilt HNSW index (hnswlib, M = 64, efConstruction = 600, ef = 300).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectra are not electron ionization GC-MS spectra (FastEI is built and benchmarked specifically for EI mass spectra matched against an in-silico EI-MS library) The target compounds are already covered by an experimental library such as NIST 2017, where conventional spectrum matching is expected to work The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than library matching — FastEI only returns ranked library candidates and cannot propose structures absent from the library

skills.description: Use when raw GC/MS chromatograms (netCDF or mzXML) contain co-eluting compounds with extensive EI fragmentation and you need pure compound spectra and integrated areas per sample rather than fragment-ion peak picking.
skills.name: gcms-spectral-deconvolution
skills.search_text: gcms-spectral-deconvolution Use when raw GC/MS chromatograms (netCDF or mzXML) contain co-eluting compounds with extensive EI fragmentation and you need pure compound spectra and integrated areas per sample rather than fragment-ion peak picking. When the goal is generic fragment-ion peak picking and alignment without compound-level spectra — peak-picking approaches (XCMS centWave, MetAlign, ChromaTOF) are the alternative; this skill exists precisely because those methods quantitate on m/z value, retention time window and area of fragment ion peaks and leave identification as the bottleneck When the input is already a deconvolved MetaboSet or a compound-by-sample area table — then the downstream skills (alignment with alignComp(), missing compound recovery with recMissComp(), identification with identifyComp()) apply instead When the mass spectral library is only readable with NIST software — eRah requires MS libraries in non-binary format importable via importMSP(); export found spectra to MSP and use MassBank/GMD/HMDB libraries instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Blind-source-separation-based spectral deconvolution of GC-MS chromatograms in R: the eRah pipeline applies compound match by local covariance (CMLC) and orthogonal signal deconvolution (OSD) to resolve co-eluting compounds in electron ionization data into pure compound spectra plus per-sample integrated areas. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.6b02927
skills.summary: Blind-source-separation-based spectral deconvolution of GC-MS chromatograms in R: the eRah pipeline applies compound match by local covariance (CMLC) and orthogonal signal deconvolution (OSD) to resolve co-eluting compounds in electron ionization data into pure compound spectra plus per-sample integrated areas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is generic fragment-ion peak picking and alignment without compound-level spectra — peak-picking approaches (XCMS centWave, MetAlign, ChromaTOF) are the alternative; this skill exists precisely because those methods quantitate on m/z value, retention time window and area of fragment ion peaks and leave identification as the bottleneck When the input is already a deconvolved MetaboSet or a compound-by-sample area table — then the downstream skills (alignment with alignComp(), missing compound recovery with recMissComp(), identification with identifyComp()) apply instead When the mass spectral library is only readable with NIST software — eRah requires MS libraries in non-binary format importable via importMSP(); export found spectra to MSP and use MassBank/GMD/HMDB libraries instead

skills.description: Use when deconvoluted GC-MS spectra are available in a .mgf file (e.g. from GNPS-MSHub auto-deconvolution) and compound identifications are needed via reference-library spectral matching.
skills.name: gcms-spectral-library-matching
skills.search_text: gcms-spectral-library-matching Use when deconvoluted GC-MS spectra are available in a .mgf file (e.g. from GNPS-MSHub auto-deconvolution) and compound identifications are needed via reference-library spectral matching. Input is raw, non-deconvoluted GC-MS data — run the MSHub auto-deconvolution (non-negative matrix factorization) step first to produce deconvoluted spectra. The goal is LC-MS/MS molecular networking rather than GC-MS library search; this skill is specific to GC-MS deconvoluted spectra. No suitable reference spectra exist for the target analytes and no public/user library covers them — spectral matching cannot annotate compounds absent from the library. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates deconvoluted GC-MS spectra by searching them against the GNPS GC-MS reference library (19,808 spectra / 19,708 standards) plus public and user libraries using cosine similarity on fragment ions, with Kovats retention-index filtering. This turns unassigned deconvolution products from MSHub/GNPS into compound-level annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Annotates deconvoluted GC-MS spectra by searching them against the GNPS GC-MS reference library (19,808 spectra / 19,708 standards) plus public and user libraries using cosine similarity on fragment ions, with Kovats retention-index filtering. This turns unassigned deconvolution products from MSHub/GNPS into compound-level annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, non-deconvoluted GC-MS data — run the MSHub auto-deconvolution (non-negative matrix factorization) step first to produce deconvoluted spectra. The goal is LC-MS/MS molecular networking rather than GC-MS library search; this skill is specific to GC-MS deconvoluted spectra. No suitable reference spectra exist for the target analytes and no public/user library covers them — spectral matching cannot annotate compounds absent from the library.

skills.description: Use when top-hit GC-MS spectral match annotations (with cosine similarity and balance score columns) from MSHub/GNPS auto-deconvolution need FDR-controlled filtering, e.g. reproducing Figure 1m,n-style threshold benchmarks.
skills.name: gcms-spectral-match-filtering
skills.search_text: gcms-spectral-match-filtering Use when top-hit GC-MS spectral match annotations (with cosine similarity and balance score columns) from MSHub/GNPS auto-deconvolution need FDR-controlled filtering, e.g. reproducing Figure 1m,n-style threshold benchmarks. skills.search_text: gcxgc-chromatogram-smoothing Use when a 2D-TIC GC×GC chromatogram (e.g., imported from a NetCDF file and baseline-corrected with baseline_corr) still contains noise and must be denoised prior to 2D-COW peak alignment or multivariate analysis. The analysis goal is supervised modeling or dimensionality reduction — for those, RGCxGC exports chromatograms via unfold_chrom for mixOmics or applies MPCA via m_prcomp instead. Applies Whittaker smoothing to a baseline-corrected GC×GC chromatogram via the RGCxGC wsmooth function, running along the first chromatographic dimension (every modulation) with a chosen penalty order (1 or 2) and lambda (e.g., 1e1) to reduce noise before peak alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2020.104830

skills.description: Use when processing raw GC×GC–MS (e.g., CDF files) to detect untargeted features: you need to segment chromatographic matrices into ROIs and filter false-positive peaks by S/N and Gaussian shape before deconvolution.

skills.search_text: gcxgc-roi-selection-inverse-watershed Use when processing raw GC×GC–MS (e.g., CDF files) to detect untargeted features: you need to segment chromatographic matrices into ROIs and filter false-positive peaks by S/N and Gaussian shape before deconvolution. Input is already a feature/peak table from commercial software (e.g. ChromaTOF peak tables) rather than raw CDF files — ROI selection operates on the reconstructed 4D intensity array. You need targeted quantification of known compounds; GcDUO ROI selection is designed for untargeted feature extraction where ROIs are unknown. Peaks are expected to be smaller than the S/N threshold allows — e.g. decane was only detected when the signal-to-noise parameter was reduced from 3 to 1, so overly strict S/N settings will drop real but weak signals. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Segments GC×GC–MS data into rolling windows of modulations and delineates regions of interest (ROIs) with the inverse watershed algorithm, extracting candidate blobs (3D peaks with 2D coordinates), then retains only blobs with adequate signal-to-noise ratios in both chromatographic dimensions and a Gaussian chromatographic form. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbaf080
skills.summary: Segments GC×GC–MS data into rolling windows of modulations and delineates regions of interest (ROIs) with the inverse watershed algorithm, extracting candidate blobs (3D peaks with 2D coordinates), then retains only blobs with adequate signal-to-noise ratios in both chromatographic dimensions and a Gaussian chromatographic form.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/peak table from commercial software (e.g. ChromaTOF peak tables) rather than raw CDF files — ROI selection operates on the reconstructed 4D intensity array. skills.description: Use when two significant metabolite feature lists from GCxGC-TOFMS plasma profiling (named metabolites plus unknown peaks annotated by mass spectrum and retention index) must be matched across studies to classify overlap, direction concordance, and condition-unique features.
skills.name: gcxgc-tofms-metabolite-identity-crossmatching
skills.search_text: gcxgc-tofms-metabolite-identity-crossmatching Use when two significant metabolite feature lists from GCxGC-TOFMS plasma profiling (named metabolites plus unknown peaks annotated by mass spectrum and retention index) must be matched across studies to classify overlap, direction concordance, and condition-unique features. You have a single study's feature table and no second condition/study to cross-reference against — the classification of concordance/discordance requires both significant metabolite lists. The candidate comparison study's unknown peaks lack mass-spectrum/retention-index metadata, so Unknown_### peak labels cannot be matched on identity rather than label. The goal is diagnostic classification of new patient samples (OPLS-DA/ROC biomarker modeling) rather than reconciling which metabolites are shared between published signatures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Cross-references significant metabolites (including unknown-identity peaks) between two GCxGC-TOFMS studies by metabolite identity — matching putatively named metabolites such as glutaric acid and hexanoic acid and unknown peaks via mass spectra/retention index — to determine whether a disease-state signature is unique to one condition or shared, as done for chronic Salmonella gallbladder carriage vs acute enteric fever. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pntd.0006215
skills.summary: Cross-references significant metabolites (including unknown-identity peaks) between two GCxGC-TOFMS studies by metabolite identity — matching putatively named metabolites such as glutaric acid and hexanoic acid and unknown peaks via mass spectra/retention index — to determine whether a disease-state signature is unique to one condition or shared, as done for chronic Salmonella gallbladder carriage vs acute enteric fever.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single study's feature table and no second condition/study to cross-reference against — the classification of concordance/discordance requires both significant metabolite lists. The goal is diagnostic classification of new patient samples (OPLS-DA/ROC biomarker modeling) rather than reconciling which metabolites are shared between published signatures.

skills.description: Use when auditing which GCxGC-TOFMS peaks were excluded from a metabolomics dataset and why — e.g. reconciling an initial peak count (691) against the final metabolite count (195) with per-criterion thresholds.
skills.name: gcxgc-tofms-peak-exclusion-criteria-auditing
skills.search_text: gcxgc-tofms-peak-exclusion-criteria-auditing Use when auditing which GCxGC-TOFMS peaks were excluded from a metabolomics dataset and why — e.g. reconciling an initial peak count (691) against the final metabolite count (195) with per-criterion thresholds. Input is already a filtered feature table where exclusions were applied upstream — this skill audits the filter step itself, not downstream statistics. The analysis is about which metabolites discriminate carriers (OPLS-DA/ROC), not about why peaks were removed — use a modeling skill instead. No peak-level exclusion thresholds are reported or recoverable from the source text — an audit table without thresholds is unverifiable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Audits the GCxGC-TOFMS peak-exclusion and missing-value-replacement pipeline that reduced 691 detected plasma peaks to 195 retained metabolites, recording each filter criterion, threshold, and action, plus the annotation-class breakdown of the retained set. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pntd.0006215
skills.summary: Audits the GCxGC-TOFMS peak-exclusion and missing-value-replacement pipeline that reduced 691 detected plasma peaks to 195 retained metabolites, recording each filter criterion, threshold, and action, plus the annotation-class breakdown of the retained set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature table where exclusions were applied upstream — this skill audits the filter step itself, not downstream statistics. skills.search_text: gelatin-standard-concentration-assignment Decision support for quantifying LA-ICP-MS elemental images against gelatin calibration standards: when raw isotope signal maps (55Mn, 56Fe, 63Cu, 66Zn) plus a standard of known concentrations must be converted to μg/g concentration images.
