skills.description: Use when you have antiSMASH or gutSMASH cluster predictions from a reference genome collection and paired shotgun metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads, and need to test which gene clusters differ in abundance or expression between phenotypes (e.g. Crohn's disease vs healthy).
skills.name: gene-cluster-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-differential-expression-analysis Use when you have antiSMASH or gutSMASH cluster predictions from a reference genome collection and paired shotgun metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads, and need to test which gene clusters differ in abundance or expression between phenotypes (e.g. Crohn's disease vs healthy). The input is already a gene cluster abundance/expression feature table — only the bigmap-analyse step applies, not the full map-and-test workflow. No antiSMASH/gutSMASH cluster predictions exist for the reference genomes: bigmap-family requires pre-computed anti-/gutSMASH output folders as input and cannot start from raw genomes. The data are 16S amplicon or other non-shotgun reads, since the method relies on mapping reads to gene cluster nucleotide sequences. The working environment is not Ubuntu-based, as the README states the tool 'has been only tested on Ubuntu'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Profile metabolic gene cluster (MGC) and gene cluster family (GCF) abundance and expression across metagenomic and metatranscriptomic samples by mapping reads to representative cluster sequences, then call differentially abundant/expressed clusters between conditions using nonparametric tests. This is the core analysis capability of the BiG-MAP pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Profile metabolic gene cluster (MGC) and gene cluster family (GCF) abundance and expression across metagenomic and metatranscriptomic samples by mapping reads to representative cluster sequences, then call differentially abundant/expressed clusters between conditions using nonparametric tests. This is the core analysis capability of the BiG-MAP pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene cluster abundance/expression feature table — only the bigmap-analyse step applies, not the full map-and-test workflow. No antiSMASH/gutSMASH cluster predictions exist for the reference genomes: bigmap-family requires pre-computed anti-/gutSMASH output folders as input and cannot start from raw genomes. The data are 16S amplicon or other non-shotgun reads, since the method relies on mapping reads to gene cluster nucleotide sequences. The working environment is not Ubuntu-based, as the README states the tool 'has been only tested on Ubuntu'.

skills.description: Use when BiG-MAP RPKM abundance/expression tables for grouped samples (e.g. healthy vs. caries, CD vs. UC) have been differentially tested and you need a heatmap of significant gene cluster profiles.
skills.name: gene-cluster-expression-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-expression-heatmap-visualization Use when BiG-MAP RPKM abundance/expression tables for grouped samples (e.g. healthy vs. caries, CD vs. UC) have been differentially tested and you need a heatmap of significant gene cluster profiles. Input is raw metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads rather than RPKM-normalized gene cluster abundance/expression tables — mapping via bigmap-map must happen first The goal is per-sample abundance/expression profiling across samples without any group comparison, where no differential-testing heatmap is meaningful No sample grouping metadata exists, since the ZIG and Kruskal-Wallis comparisons and the group-level heatmap profiles both require defined sample groups http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Visualizes differentially abundant or expressed metabolic gene clusters (MGCs/GCFs) from BiG-MAP.analyse as a heatmap of group-level profiles, using seaborn, alongside tab-separated test results. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Visualizes differentially abundant or expressed metabolic gene clusters (MGCs/GCFs) from BiG-MAP.analyse as a heatmap of group-level profiles, using seaborn, alongside tab-separated test results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads rather than RPKM-normalized gene cluster abundance/expression tables — mapping via bigmap-map must happen first The goal is per-sample abundance/expression profiling across samples without any group comparison, where no differential-testing heatmap is meaningful No sample grouping metadata exists, since the ZIG and Kruskal-Wallis comparisons and the group-level heatmap profiles both require defined sample groups

skills.description: Use when antiSMASH v4 GenBank BGC predictions (optionally with MIBiG reference BGCs) need to be grouped into gene cluster families or clans, or when a BGC sequence similarity network must be built and clustered.
skills.name: gene-cluster-family-clustering
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-family-clustering Use when antiSMASH v4 GenBank BGC predictions (optionally with MIBiG reference BGCs) need to be grouped into gene cluster families or clans, or when a BGC sequence similarity network must be built and clustered. Input BGCs are already pre-clustered into a GCF presence/absence matrix — downstream metabologenomic correlation, not clustering, is needed. The task is phylogenetic ordering of BGCs within an established family — CORASON's multi-locus syntenic core analysis, not BiG-SCAPE clustering, is the appropriate tool. BGC predictions are not in antiSMASH-processed GenBank format (e.g. raw FASTA or RAST annotations), since BiG-SCAPE expects antiSMASH outputs as direct inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Groups antiSMASH-predicted biosynthetic gene clusters into gene cluster families (GCFs) and clans (GCCs) using BiG-SCAPE's pairwise distance network (Jaccard, Domain Sequence Similarity, Adjacency indices) filtered at a distance cutoff followed by Affinity Propagation clustering. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Groups antiSMASH-predicted biosynthetic gene clusters into gene cluster families (GCFs) and clans (GCCs) using BiG-SCAPE's pairwise distance network (Jaccard, Domain Sequence Similarity, Adjacency indices) filtered at a distance cutoff followed by Affinity Propagation clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BGCs are already pre-clustered into a GCF presence/absence matrix — downstream metabologenomic correlation, not clustering, is needed. The task is phylogenetic ordering of BGCs within an established family — CORASON's multi-locus syntenic core analysis, not BiG-SCAPE clustering, is the appropriate tool. BGC predictions are not in antiSMASH-processed GenBank format (e.g. raw FASTA or RAST annotations), since BiG-SCAPE expects antiSMASH outputs as direct inputs.

skills.description: Use when SMASH-predicted gene clusters (antiSMASH or gutSMASH GenBank output folders for a genome collection) contain redundant clusters that must be dereplicated and grouped into GCFs before metagenomic/metatranscriptomic read mapping.
skills.name: gene-cluster-family-grouping
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-family-grouping Use when SMASH-predicted gene clusters (antiSMASH or gutSMASH GenBank output folders for a genome collection) contain redundant clusters that must be dereplicated and grouped into GCFs before metagenomic/metatranscriptomic read mapping. The gene clusters are already dereplicated with a single representative per similarity group, so re-clustering would only add noise The input is raw metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads or a finished abundance table rather than SMASH genome-mining output folders — the correct modules are bigmap-map or bigmap-analyse No prior antiSMASH/gutSMASH run has been performed on the genomes; this module does not predict gene clusters itself Builds a nonredundant representative gene-cluster collection from antiSMASH/gutSMASH output by MinHash (MASH) sketching of cluster protein sequences at a 0.8 similarity cutoff, selecting medoid representatives, and optionally grouping representatives into gene cluster families (GCFs) with BiG-SCAPE. This prevents ambiguous read mapping in the downstream BiG-MAP.map step. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Builds a nonredundant representative gene-cluster collection from antiSMASH/gutSMASH output by MinHash (MASH) sketching of cluster protein sequences at a 0.8 similarity cutoff, selecting medoid representatives, and optionally grouping representatives into gene cluster families (GCFs) with BiG-SCAPE. This prevents ambiguous read mapping in the downstream BiG-MAP.map step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene clusters are already dereplicated with a single representative per similarity group, so re-clustering would only add noise The input is raw metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads or a finished abundance table rather than SMASH genome-mining output folders — the correct modules are bigmap-map or bigmap-analyse No prior antiSMASH/gutSMASH run has been performed on the genomes; this module does not predict gene clusters itself

skills.description: Use when choosing or validating the alignment backend for BiG-SCAPE's DSS index on a growing BGC dataset — e.g. to confirm that Pfam profile-HMM alignment (hmmalign) matches Muscle/MAFFT-based GCF calling while being faster as input BGC count increases.
skills.name: gene-cluster-family-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-family-method-benchmarking Use when choosing or validating the alignment backend for BiG-SCAPE's DSS index on a growing BGC dataset — e.g. to confirm that Pfam profile-HMM alignment (hmmalign) matches Muscle/MAFFT-based GCF calling while being faster as input BGC count increases. The goal is a single definitive GCF clustering on one small dataset where aligner runtime is irrelevant — just run one backend rather than benchmarking The input is raw genome contigs rather than antiSMASH-processed GenBank BGC predictions; BGC and domain prediction must happen first The analysis requires multi-locus phylogenies of a single GCF (use CORASON's conserved-core approach) rather than method comparison across the whole BGC set http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Benchmark alternative domain-sequence alignment engines (hmmalign profile-HMM alignment vs Muscle vs MAFFT) used by BiG-SCAPE for computing the Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index, by comparing final GCF calls and runtime scaling on the same antiSMASH-predicted BGC input set. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Benchmark alternative domain-sequence alignment engines (hmmalign profile-HMM alignment vs Muscle vs MAFFT) used by BiG-SCAPE for computing the Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index, by comparing final GCF calls and runtime scaling on the same antiSMASH-predicted BGC input set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single definitive GCF clustering on one small dataset where aligner runtime is irrelevant — just run one backend rather than benchmarking The input is raw genome contigs rather than antiSMASH-processed GenBank BGC predictions; BGC and domain prediction must happen first The analysis requires multi-locus phylogenies of a single GCF (use CORASON's conserved-core approach) rather than method comparison across the whole BGC set

skills.description: Use when pre-computed BiG-SLiCE GCF models exist (e.g., the T=900 run yielding 29,955 GCFs) and you need to quantify how close each model is to curated MIBiG v2.0 reference BGCs, or to validate feature-space separation.
skills.name: gene-cluster-family-model-distance-querying
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-family-model-distance-querying Use when pre-computed BiG-SLiCE GCF models exist (e.g., the T=900 run yielding 29,955 GCFs) and you need to quantify how close each model is to curated MIBiG v2.0 reference BGCs, or to validate feature-space separation. Input is raw genome/contig data not yet processed by antiSMASH — no BGC feature vectors exist yet to query against You need gene-level pairwise BGC comparisons rather than Euclidean feature-space distances — the article positions BiG-SCAPE as the pairwise network-comparison alternative Working with BiG-SLiCE v2.0 outputs, which switched to cosine-like (l2-normalization) distances, so Euclidean-distance reproductions of the paper's Fig. 3C are no longer applicable Measuring Euclidean distances between BiG-SLiCE GCF model feature vectors and MIBiG reference BGC feature vectors to test whether the Euclidean feature space preserves the biosynthetic signal connecting BGC genomic similarity to chemical similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa154
skills.summary: Measuring Euclidean distances between BiG-SLiCE GCF model feature vectors and MIBiG reference BGC feature vectors to test whether the Euclidean feature space preserves the biosynthetic signal connecting BGC genomic similarity to chemical similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw genome/contig data not yet processed by antiSMASH — no BGC feature vectors exist yet to query against You need gene-level pairwise BGC comparisons rather than Euclidean feature-space distances — the article positions BiG-SCAPE as the pairwise network-comparison alternative Working with BiG-SLiCE v2.0 outputs, which switched to cosine-like (l2-normalization) distances, so Euclidean-distance reproductions of the paper's Fig. 3C are no longer applicable

skills.description: Use when you have one or more new antiSMASH-annotated BGCs and an existing BiG-SLiCE SQLite3 result database, and need to rank-match the new BGCs against precomputed GCF models instead of re-clustering.
skills.name: gene-cluster-family-querying-against-centroid-models
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-family-querying-against-centroid-models Use when you have one or more new antiSMASH-annotated BGCs and an existing BiG-SLiCE SQLite3 result database, and need to rank-match the new BGCs against precomputed GCF models instead of re-clustering. When no pre-computed BiG-SLiCE GCF models exist — query mode requires a prior clustering run stored as an SQLite3 result database; otherwise run a full bigslice -i <input_folder> <output_folder> clustering analysis first. When the BGC of interest is not in (and cannot be converted to) antiSMASH output format — the query input must be an antiSMASH-generated result. When pairwise BGC-level network comparison at fine granularity is required (e.g., BiG-SCAPE-style sequence similarity networks) rather than centroid-based family assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Use BiG-SLiCE's --query mode to place newly sequenced (putative) BGCs into previously computed gene cluster families (GCFs) by matching domain-based features against stored GCF centroid models, without rerunning full clustering. This lets practitioners assess the function and/or novelty of a new BGC in seconds rather than re-clustering the entire corpus. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa154
skills.summary: Use BiG-SLiCE's --query mode to place newly sequenced (putative) BGCs into previously computed gene cluster families (GCFs) by matching domain-based features against stored GCF centroid models, without rerunning full clustering. This lets practitioners assess the function and/or novelty of a new BGC in seconds rather than re-clustering the entire corpus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no pre-computed BiG-SLiCE GCF models exist — query mode requires a prior clustering run stored as an SQLite3 result database; otherwise run a full bigslice -i <input_folder> <output_folder> clustering analysis first. When the BGC of interest is not in (and cannot be converted to) antiSMASH output format — the query input must be an antiSMASH-generated result. When pairwise BGC-level network comparison at fine granularity is required (e.g., BiG-SCAPE-style sequence similarity networks) rather than centroid-based family assignment.

skills.description: Use when you have antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directories for many genomes and need a nonredundant gene-cluster reference set (and optional GCF assignments) before mapping metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads.
skills.name: gene-cluster-redundancy-clustering
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-redundancy-clustering Use when you have antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directories for many genomes and need a nonredundant gene-cluster reference set (and optional GCF assignments) before mapping metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads. The gene-cluster collection is already nonredundant or already carries GCF assignments — re-clustering would not change the mapping reference. The goal is to quantify abundance/expression from metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads — that is the bigmap-map step, which consumes this module's outputs. Only a single genome with one predicted gene cluster is available — there is no redundancy to filter and clustering is meaningless. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Redundancy-filtering and clustering of predicted metabolic gene clusters (MGCs/BGCs) into a nonredundant representative collection, as implemented in the BiG-MAP.family module: MASH MinHash sketching at a 0.8 similarity cutoff for deduplication, medoid selection, and optional BiG-SCAPE grouping into gene cluster families (GCFs). metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Redundancy-filtering and clustering of predicted metabolic gene clusters (MGCs/BGCs) into a nonredundant representative collection, as implemented in the BiG-MAP.family module: MASH MinHash sketching at a 0.8 similarity cutoff for deduplication, medoid selection, and optional BiG-SCAPE grouping into gene cluster families (GCFs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene-cluster collection is already nonredundant or already carries GCF assignments — re-clustering would not change the mapping reference. The goal is to quantify abundance/expression from metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads — that is the bigmap-map step, which consumes this module's outputs. Only a single genome with one predicted gene cluster is available — there is no redundancy to filter and clustering is meaningless.

skills.description: Use when you need topology-based pathway enrichment on gene expression data (e.g. GEO breast cancer or TCGA prostate cancer matrices) and must first estimate weighted, directed adjacency matrices per pathway from curated interaction databases.
skills.name: gene-coexpression-network-estimation
skills.search_text: gene-coexpression-network-estimation Use when you need topology-based pathway enrichment on gene expression data (e.g. GEO breast cancer or TCGA prostate cancer matrices) and must first estimate weighted, directed adjacency matrices per pathway from curated interaction databases. Your genes are not covered by any tested pathway — README advises filtering input data to genes belonging to at least one pathway before running NetGSA You need differential expression testing rather than topology-aware pathway enrichment; DE-only methods like SPIA or PRS may suffice and are computationally lighter You require a quick off-the-shelf enrichment without network estimation — over-representation methods do not need adjacency matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate combined (weighted, directed) gene interaction adjacency matrices for pathways from gene expression data using the netgsa package's prepareAdjMat, then use them for topology-based pathway enrichment with NetGSA. The overhauled netgsa makes this computationally feasible for thousands of genes via REHE variance component estimation and pathway clustering. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Estimate combined (weighted, directed) gene interaction adjacency matrices for pathways from gene expression data using the netgsa package's prepareAdjMat, then use them for topology-based pathway enrichment with NetGSA. The overhauled netgsa makes this computationally feasible for thousands of genes via REHE variance component estimation and pathway clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your genes are not covered by any tested pathway — README advises filtering input data to genes belonging to at least one pathway before running NetGSA You need differential expression testing rather than topology-aware pathway enrichment; DE-only methods like SPIA or PRS may suffice and are computationally lighter You require a quick off-the-shelf enrichment without network estimation — over-representation methods do not need adjacency matrices

skills.description: Use when a Cytoscape network of genes/proteins (e.g. built with a stringApp Disease Query such as query='Rett syndrome', cutoff=0.4, limit=20) needs disease-gene and compound-target annotations added from CyTargetLinker XGMML linksets.
skills.name: gene-disease-association-annotation
skills.search_text: gene-disease-association-annotation Use when a Cytoscape network of genes/proteins (e.g. built with a stringApp Disease Query such as query='Rett syndrome', cutoff=0.4, limit=20) needs disease-gene and compound-target annotations added from CyTargetLinker XGMML linksets. The input is a differentially expressed gene list for pathway extension — use the gene-pathway (WikiPathways) linkset use case instead You need author-article-journal relationships from Wikidata rather than compound-target or disease-gene annotations The network nodes cannot be matched by the 'display name' attribute the linksets join on http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotates a Cytoscape protein-protein interaction network (e.g. a stringApp Disease Query network) with gene-disease associations from a curated OMIM rare-disease linkset, and optionally compound-target interactions from ChEMBL, using the CyTargetLinker 'extend' automation command. metabolomics/v3 10.12688/f1000research.14613.2
skills.summary: Annotates a Cytoscape protein-protein interaction network (e.g. a stringApp Disease Query network) with gene-disease associations from a curated OMIM rare-disease linkset, and optionally compound-target interactions from ChEMBL, using the CyTargetLinker 'extend' automation command.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a differentially expressed gene list for pathway extension — use the gene-pathway (WikiPathways) linkset use case instead You need author-article-journal relationships from Wikidata rather than compound-target or disease-gene annotations The network nodes cannot be matched by the 'display name' attribute the linksets join on

skills.description: Use when a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. sex-consistent F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 states from an 8-week exercise time point) must be prioritized against curated gene-disease associations such as Open Targets.
skills.name: gene-disease-association-intersection
skills.search_text: gene-disease-association-intersection Use when a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. sex-consistent F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 states from an 8-week exercise time point) must be prioritized against curated gene-disease associations such as Open Targets. The gene list is not anchored to a defined differential-expression state (e.g. no sex-consistent F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 assignment) — the intersection loses its interpretive frame The goal is to estimate SNP-heritability or mediated heritability of trait associations (use LDSC or MESC instead) rather than count curated gene-disease targets Associations below evidence score 0.8 are acceptable — the counting logic and reported figures depend on this threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Cross-reference rat-to-human orthologs of sex-consistent 8-week exercise-responsive DE genes against Open Targets gene-trait direct associations at evidence score > 0.8, quantifying disease genes by tissue specificity (tissue-shared = differentially expressed in 3+ tissues) and excluding easily biopsied tissues. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Cross-reference rat-to-human orthologs of sex-consistent 8-week exercise-responsive DE genes against Open Targets gene-trait direct associations at evidence score > 0.8, quantifying disease genes by tissue specificity (tissue-shared = differentially expressed in 3+ tissues) and excluding easily biopsied tissues.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene list is not anchored to a defined differential-expression state (e.g. no sex-consistent F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 assignment) — the intersection loses its interpretive frame The goal is to estimate SNP-heritability or mediated heritability of trait associations (use LDSC or MESC instead) rather than count curated gene-disease targets Associations below evidence score 0.8 are acceptable — the counting logic and reported figures depend on this threshold

skills.description: Use when the goal is to confirm which genes are shared across a defined panel of intestine-related diseases, or to map specific genes (e.g. STK11, SMAD4/BMPR1A) to named syndromes using GutUDB's disease-gene association data.
skills.name: gene-disease-association-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-disease-association-mapping Use when the goal is to confirm which genes are shared across a defined panel of intestine-related diseases, or to map specific genes (e.g. STK11, SMAD4/BMPR1A) to named syndromes using GutUDB's disease-gene association data. The question concerns non-intestinal diseases, since GutUDB's scope is 56 intestinal diseases across six species. The analysis needs raw omics profiles (e.g. the ~9 million generated profiles from eight omics data types) rather than curated disease-gene associations. A validated causal gene-disease relationship is required without further literature curation — GutUDB associations are curated records, not etiological proof. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3402 Extracts and cross-tabulates disease-gene association records from GutUDB (260,790 curated associations across 56 intestinal diseases) to verify which genes are linked to a set of related diseases and to annotate disease-specific exemplar genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Extracts and cross-tabulates disease-gene association records from GutUDB (260,790 curated associations across 56 intestinal diseases) to verify which genes are linked to a set of related diseases and to annotate disease-specific exemplar genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns non-intestinal diseases, since GutUDB's scope is 56 intestinal diseases across six species. The analysis needs raw omics profiles (e.g. the ~9 million generated profiles from eight omics data types) rather than curated disease-gene associations. A validated causal gene-disease relationship is required without further literature curation — GutUDB associations are curated records, not etiological proof.

skills.description: Use when a MetENP analysis has already produced significant metabolites mapped to KEGG compound IDs and you need the downstream reaction, gene, and enzyme annotations for those metabolites.
skills.name: gene-enzyme-annotation-retrieval
skills.search_text: gene-enzyme-annotation-retrieval Use when a MetENP analysis has already produced significant metabolites mapped to KEGG compound IDs and you need the downstream reaction, gene, and enzyme annotations for those metabolites. The metabolites cannot be assigned KEGG compound IDs (map_keggid fails or returns empty) — no reactions/genes can be traced The species of interest has no KEGG pathway/orthology coverage (not in korg) — species-specific gene-enzyme retrieval is out of scope The goal is only metabolite-class or pathway enrichment scoring (metclassenrichment/path_enrichmentscore) with no need for gene-enzyme functional annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retrieves the reactions, genes, and enzymes functionally linked to significantly altered metabolites via KEGG compound/ortholog mapping, using MetENP's rxninfo() and enzyme_gene_info() functions for a chosen species (e.g., hsa). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.11.20.391912
skills.summary: Retrieves the reactions, genes, and enzymes functionally linked to significantly altered metabolites via KEGG compound/ortholog mapping, using MetENP's rxninfo() and enzyme_gene_info() functions for a chosen species (e.g., hsa).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites cannot be assigned KEGG compound IDs (map_keggid fails or returns empty) — no reactions/genes can be traced The species of interest has no KEGG pathway/orthology coverage (not in korg) — species-specific gene-enzyme retrieval is out of scope The goal is only metabolite-class or pathway enrichment scoring (metclassenrichment/path_enrichmentscore) with no need for gene-enzyme functional annotation

skills.description: Use when you have a list of essential genes from single-gene deletion analysis of a metabolic reconstruction and want to map approved drugs onto those targets to prioritize repurposing hypotheses.
skills.name: gene-essentiality-annotation
skills.search_text: gene-essentiality-annotation Use when you have a list of essential genes from single-gene deletion analysis of a metabolic reconstruction and want to map approved drugs onto those targets to prioritize repurposing hypotheses. The model has not been gap-filled/reconstructed and no validated essential-gene list exists from single-gene deletion analysis The drug source is not a curated target database (e.g. DrugBank) with protein-level associations, so gene-target intersection is not possible The goal is de novo drug discovery rather than repurposing drugs already cataloged against the organism's essential genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Cross-references a model's in silico essential genes (from COBRApy single-gene deletion of a genome-scale metabolic network such as P. aeruginosa NCGM2.S1) against DrugBank drug-target associations to classify each drug as a known microbial growth inhibitor or a previously untested therapeutic hypothesis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Cross-references a model's in silico essential genes (from COBRApy single-gene deletion of a genome-scale metabolic network such as P. aeruginosa NCGM2.S1) against DrugBank drug-target associations to classify each drug as a known microbial growth inhibitor or a previously untested therapeutic hypothesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model has not been gap-filled/reconstructed and no validated essential-gene list exists from single-gene deletion analysis The drug source is not a curated target database (e.g. DrugBank) with protein-level associations, so gene-target intersection is not possible The goal is de novo drug discovery rather than repurposing drugs already cataloged against the organism's essential genes

skills.description: Use when you need to compare pathway enrichment methods on human disease gene expression datasets by measuring how highly each method ranks known target disease pathways.
skills.name: gene-expression-dataset-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gene-expression-dataset-benchmarking Use when you need to compare pathway enrichment methods on human disease gene expression datasets by measuring how highly each method ranks known target disease pathways. Input is not human disease gene expression data (e.g. metabolomic or microbiome KO/compound tables) — apply the GRSA application skill instead The goal is to assess specificity or true-negative rates of enrichment methods — the article states specificity cannot be accurately evaluated because true negatives are hard to define Only one dataset is available and cross-dataset median aggregation is not meaningful — single-dataset ranking lacks the benchmark's aggregate medians http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmarks the generalized reporter score-based analysis (GRSA, R package ReporterScore) against six enrichment methods (Fisher/KO_enrich, GSEA, GSVA, GSA, PADOG, SAFE) on the 24 human disease gene expression benchmark datasets, ranking target disease pathways by median rank and median adjusted P-value. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Benchmarks the generalized reporter score-based analysis (GRSA, R package ReporterScore) against six enrichment methods (Fisher/KO_enrich, GSEA, GSVA, GSA, PADOG, SAFE) on the 24 human disease gene expression benchmark datasets, ranking target disease pathways by median rank and median adjusted P-value.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not human disease gene expression data (e.g. metabolomic or microbiome KO/compound tables) — apply the GRSA application skill instead The goal is to assess specificity or true-negative rates of enrichment methods — the article states specificity cannot be accurately evaluated because true negatives are hard to define Only one dataset is available and cross-dataset median aggregation is not meaningful — single-dataset ranking lacks the benchmark's aggregate medians

skills.description: Reference for retrieving the exact expression datasets (type 2 diabetes from the Whitehead deposit and airway epithelia from AGED) needed to reproduce PLAGE pathway-activity analyses.
skills.name: gene-expression-dataset-loading
skills.search_text: gene-expression-dataset-loading Reference for retrieving the exact expression datasets (type 2 diabetes from the Whitehead deposit and airway epithelia from AGED) needed to reproduce PLAGE pathway-activity analyses. If the analysis goal is to rank individual genes rather than score predefined pathway activity (e.g. via SVD) — this skill only stages the datasets, it does not perform the pathway analysis itself If a different disease/condition dataset than type 2 diabetes or airway epithelia is required, since this skill only covers the two demonstration datasets used in the PLAGE article Loads the specific public microarray expression datasets used by PLAGE's demonstrations: the type 2 diabetes profiles from Mootha et al. and the airway epithelia smoker/non-smoker profiles, so that pathway activity analysis can proceed on the exact inputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Loads the specific public microarray expression datasets used by PLAGE's demonstrations: the type 2 diabetes profiles from Mootha et al. and the airway epithelia smoker/non-smoker profiles, so that pathway activity analysis can proceed on the exact inputs.
