skills.description: Use when a gene expression or omics matrix (e.g. heatmap_test.csv) with a matching sample-annotation file (e.g. group_info.csv) must be rendered as a clustered, group-annotated heatmap figure.
skills.name: gene-expression-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: gene-expression-heatmap-visualization Use when a gene expression or omics matrix (e.g. heatmap_test.csv) with a matching sample-annotation file (e.g. group_info.csv) must be rendered as a clustered, group-annotated heatmap figure. The task is differential-expression visualization rather than expression clustering — GraphBio routes that to its volcano plot module with volcano_example.csv inputs The goal is data preprocessing or statistical computing rather than visualization — GraphBio 'specifically focuses on facilitating the generation of publication-ready plots instead of data preprocessing and computing' The input matrix has no matching sample-group annotation file, so sample group annotation cannot be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates a publication-ready, hierarchically clustered heatmap from an omics/gene expression matrix, annotating samples by group using GraphBio's heatmap module, which is built on the R pheatmap package. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fgene.2022.957317
skills.summary: Generates a publication-ready, hierarchically clustered heatmap from an omics/gene expression matrix, annotating samples by group using GraphBio's heatmap module, which is built on the R pheatmap package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is differential-expression visualization rather than expression clustering — GraphBio routes that to its volcano plot module with volcano_example.csv inputs The goal is data preprocessing or statistical computing rather than visualization — GraphBio 'specifically focuses on facilitating the generation of publication-ready plots instead of data preprocessing and computing' The input matrix has no matching sample-group annotation file, so sample group annotation cannot be applied

skills.description: Use when standardizing cross-species (rat-to-human) differential expression effect sizes against GTEx v8 per-gene, per-tissue expression variability and its genetic component via h_SNP^2.
skills.name: gene-expression-heritability-estimation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-heritability-estimation Use when standardizing cross-species (rat-to-human) differential expression effect sizes against GTEx v8 per-gene, per-tissue expression variability and its genetic component via h_SNP^2. The analysis goal is trait heritability enrichment or mediated heritability from GWAS summary statistics — use LDSC or MESC instead; this skill operates on individual-level GTEx expression and genotype data per gene x tissue. The expression data have not been re-processed with the pseudolog transform — the default GTEx inverse-normal transform removes the variance scale needed to compute meaningful SDpheno/SDgeno units. Tissue-specificity or cross-tissue exercise adaptation patterns are not needed; a simpler DE analysis (DESeq2 per sex and tissue) suffices without the heritability machinery. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Estimates the SNP-heritability (h_SNP^2) of each gene's expression at the gene-by-tissue level in GTEx v8 using GCTA-GRM, then combines it with Empirical-Bayes posterior expression variances to standardize exercise-induced log2FC effect sizes in SDgeno and SDpheno units. This identifies where training-induced expression changes can exceed genetic or standing human expression variability. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Estimates the SNP-heritability (h_SNP^2) of each gene's expression at the gene-by-tissue level in GTEx v8 using GCTA-GRM, then combines it with Empirical-Bayes posterior expression variances to standardize exercise-induced log2FC effect sizes in SDgeno and SDpheno units. This identifies where training-induced expression changes can exceed genetic or standing human expression variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is trait heritability enrichment or mediated heritability from GWAS summary statistics — use LDSC or MESC instead; this skill operates on individual-level GTEx expression and genotype data per gene x tissue. The expression data have not been re-processed with the pseudolog transform — the default GTEx inverse-normal transform removes the variance scale needed to compute meaningful SDpheno/SDgeno units. Tissue-specificity or cross-tissue exercise adaptation patterns are not needed; a simpler DE analysis (DESeq2 per sex and tissue) suffices without the heritability machinery.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking pathway enrichment methods on simulated signals: you have a real expression matrix, need ground-truth dysregulated gene groups of varying sizes, and must measure empirical power and type-I error across replicates.
skills.name: gene-expression-signal-simulation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-signal-simulation Use when benchmarking pathway enrichment methods on simulated signals: you have a real expression matrix, need ground-truth dysregulated gene groups of varying sizes, and must measure empirical power and type-I error across replicates. The goal is descriptive differential-expression analysis rather than method benchmarking — no simulation of signals or power estimation is needed Expression data already contain known phenotype labels and no ground-truth dysregulation simulation is required for validation The method under test requires differentially expressed genes as input (e.g., SPIA, PRS), which the paper notes 'may or may not be detected' — a different evaluation design applies http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulates dysregulated-gene signals onto a real gene expression matrix (e.g., breastcancer2012 centered/scaled to unit variance) by adding known mean signals (0.2, 0.3, 0.4) to defined groups of dysregulated genes, enabling empirical power and type-I error evaluation of pathway enrichment methods such as NetGSA.REHE (with and without clustering) and REML. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Simulates dysregulated-gene signals onto a real gene expression matrix (e.g., breastcancer2012 centered/scaled to unit variance) by adding known mean signals (0.2, 0.3, 0.4) to defined groups of dysregulated genes, enabling empirical power and type-I error evaluation of pathway enrichment methods such as NetGSA.REHE (with and without clustering) and REML.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is descriptive differential-expression analysis rather than method benchmarking — no simulation of signals or power estimation is needed Expression data already contain known phenotype labels and no ground-truth dysregulation simulation is required for validation The method under test requires differentially expressed genes as input (e.g., SPIA, PRS), which the paper notes 'may or may not be detected' — a different evaluation design applies

skills.description: Use when expression data must be standardized per gene and pathway-restricted matrices built as input to an SVD-based pathway activity analysis such as PLAGE, or when reproducing metagene results.
skills.name: gene-expression-standardization-and-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: gene-expression-standardization-and-matrix-construction Use when expression data must be standardized per gene and pathway-restricted matrices built as input to an SVD-based pathway activity analysis such as PLAGE, or when reproducing metagene results. Expression values are already standardized or the analysis is not SVD-based pathway activity estimation — double standardization would distort metagene weights The goal is single-gene differential expression rather than pathway-level activity levels; per-gene statistics do not need pathway-restricted matrices Pathway membership files are missing; building Y for undefined gene sets has no basis http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Standardizes each gene's expression values to zero mean and unit variance across samples, then assembles the standardized values of a pre-defined pathway's genes into a genes-by-samples matrix Y. This preprocessing is the prerequisite for computing the pathway's singular value decomposition and first-metagene activity levels in PLAGE. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Standardizes each gene's expression values to zero mean and unit variance across samples, then assembles the standardized values of a pre-defined pathway's genes into a genes-by-samples matrix Y. This preprocessing is the prerequisite for computing the pathway's singular value decomposition and first-metagene activity levels in PLAGE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression values are already standardized or the analysis is not SVD-based pathway activity estimation — double standardization would distort metagene weights The goal is single-gene differential expression rather than pathway-level activity levels; per-gene statistics do not need pathway-restricted matrices Pathway membership files are missing; building Y for undefined gene sets has no basis

skills.description: Use when performing topology-based pathway enrichment and no pre-built pathway network is available: dataset gene lists (e.g. 2784 breast cancer genes) need gene-gene edges harvested from KEGG/Reactome and assembled into adjacency matrices.
skills.name: gene-gene-interaction-curation
skills.search_text: gene-gene-interaction-curation Use when performing topology-based pathway enrichment and no pre-built pathway network is available: dataset gene lists (e.g. 2784 breast cancer genes) need gene-gene edges harvested from KEGG/Reactome and assembled into adjacency matrices. You already have validated pathway adjacency matrices and only need to run the NetGSA statistical test You need differentially expressed gene lists rather than network-informed topology analysis — SPIA and PRS require detected DE genes and are computationally lighter alternatives Your genes belong to no tested pathway — the README advises filtering them out before assembling adjacency matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Curate gene-gene interaction edges from external pathway databases (KEGG, Reactome, PantherDB) and convert them into pathway adjacency matrices with within-pathway gene clustering, so topology-based NetGSA enrichment can run on thousands of genes without expert hand-built networks. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Curate gene-gene interaction edges from external pathway databases (KEGG, Reactome, PantherDB) and convert them into pathway adjacency matrices with within-pathway gene clustering, so topology-based NetGSA enrichment can run on thousands of genes without expert hand-built networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have validated pathway adjacency matrices and only need to run the NetGSA statistical test You need differentially expressed gene lists rather than network-informed topology analysis — SPIA and PRS require detected DE genes and are computationally lighter alternatives Your genes belong to no tested pathway — the README advises filtering them out before assembling adjacency matrices

skills.description: Use when feature names from CCLE omics layers (e.g. RNA splicing Ensemble IDs) must be converted to common gene names or Bigg IDs before matching against Recon3D reactions or SynLethDB SL gene pairs.
skills.name: gene-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-identifier-mapping Use when feature names from CCLE omics layers (e.g. RNA splicing Ensemble IDs) must be converted to common gene names or Bigg IDs before matching against Recon3D reactions or SynLethDB SL gene pairs. Feature names are already common gene names and the target database (e.g. SynLethDB) uses the same identifier namespace, so mapping adds no resolution The analysis targets non-gene feature layers (e.g. metabolites as predictors) where a gene-name-to-BiggID translation is inapplicable Mutations-based feature sets excluded from the random-forest results due to their binary structure — mapping gene space there is moot http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3345 Reconciles heterogeneous gene and metabolite identifiers across omics feature lists, the Recon3D/Human1 metabolic model, and interaction databases (SynLethDB, STRING, TarBase) so that predictor features can be matched to curated gene pairs and reactions. Without this mapping, downstream SL-enrichment and regulome-network analyses in Metab8D cannot join features to pathway entities. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Reconciles heterogeneous gene and metabolite identifiers across omics feature lists, the Recon3D/Human1 metabolic model, and interaction databases (SynLethDB, STRING, TarBase) so that predictor features can be matched to curated gene pairs and reactions. Without this mapping, downstream SL-enrichment and regulome-network analyses in Metab8D cannot join features to pathway entities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Feature names are already common gene names and the target database (e.g. SynLethDB) uses the same identifier namespace, so mapping adds no resolution The analysis targets non-gene feature layers (e.g. metabolites as predictors) where a gene-name-to-BiggID translation is inapplicable Mutations-based feature sets excluded from the random-forest results due to their binary structure — mapping gene space there is moot

skills.description: Use when pathway node identifiers retrieved from databases like KEGG or Reactome must be matched to the identifiers of your input gene set (e.g. ENTREZID to UNIPROT) before assembling edge lists for topology-based pathway analysis.
skills.name: gene-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-identifier-mapping Use when pathway node identifiers retrieved from databases like KEGG or Reactome must be matched to the identifiers of your input gene set (e.g. ENTREZID to UNIPROT) before assembling edge lists for topology-based pathway analysis. Input gene identifiers already match the pathway node identifier space, so no mapping step is needed The analysis goal is pathway enrichment on an already-built adjacency matrix rather than retrieving/matching edges from external pathway databases http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Maps pathway node identifiers from external interaction databases (KEGG, Reactome) into the same identifier space as the input gene set (e.g. ENTREZID to UNIPROT via AnnotationDbi) so retrieved gene-gene edges align with the user's data, as done by netgsa's obtainEdgeList workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Maps pathway node identifiers from external interaction databases (KEGG, Reactome) into the same identifier space as the input gene set (e.g. ENTREZID to UNIPROT via AnnotationDbi) so retrieved gene-gene edges align with the user's data, as done by netgsa's obtainEdgeList workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input gene identifiers already match the pathway node identifier space, so no mapping step is needed The analysis goal is pathway enrichment on an already-built adjacency matrix rather than retrieving/matching edges from external pathway databases

skills.description: Use when raw CCLE/DepMap omics feature matrices mix identifier namespaces (e.g. RNA splicing ensemble IDs, BiggIDs) and feature names must be mapped to common gene names before cross-omics ML training or network output.
skills.name: gene-identifier-standardization
skills.search_text: gene-identifier-standardization Use when raw CCLE/DepMap omics feature matrices mix identifier namespaces (e.g. RNA splicing ensemble IDs, BiggIDs) and feature names must be mapped to common gene names before cross-omics ML training or network output. Input feature names are already in a single consistent namespace (e.g. all genes are already common symbols) so renaming would add no signal The task is training or predicting metabolite values rather than preparing the feature matrices — standardization is a preprocessing sub-step, not the modeling step itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Standardizes heterogeneous omics feature identifiers (e.g. RNA splicing ensemble IDs) into consistent common gene names using BioTools.fr so that features across the eight CCLE biomolecular classes are consistently labeled before random forest modeling and network construction. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Standardizes heterogeneous omics feature identifiers (e.g. RNA splicing ensemble IDs) into consistent common gene names using BioTools.fr so that features across the eight CCLE biomolecular classes are consistently labeled before random forest modeling and network construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input feature names are already in a single consistent namespace (e.g. all genes are already common symbols) so renaming would add no signal The task is training or predicting metabolite values rather than preparing the feature matrices — standardization is a preprocessing sub-step, not the modeling step itself

skills.description: Use when a lipid feature abundance matrix plus phenotype file must be linked to lipid classes (via genes) and analysed for differential lipid class, total chain length and hydrocarbon-chain saturation.
skills.name: gene-lipid-class-association
skills.search_text: gene-lipid-class-association Use when a lipid feature abundance matrix plus phenotype file must be linked to lipid classes (via genes) and analysed for differential lipid class, total chain length and hydrocarbon-chain saturation. The input is a transcriptomic (RNA-seq/miRNA/isoform) count matrix handled by the genes, miRNA or isoform modules rather than a lipid abundance matrix. No phenotype file with defined contrast groups is available, since edgeR differential abundance contrasts depend on it. Lipid identifiers cannot be parsed into lipid-class, chain-length and saturation components by lipidr, so the three lipid feature dimensions cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 The lipidomics module of MultiOmicsIntegrator (MOI), in which LipiDB associates genes with lipid classes present in the data from a manually curated database, while lipidr parses lipid identifiers into class, chain-length and saturation dimensions for differential analysis and enrichment. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae175
skills.summary: The lipidomics module of MultiOmicsIntegrator (MOI), in which LipiDB associates genes with lipid classes present in the data from a manually curated database, while lipidr parses lipid identifiers into class, chain-length and saturation dimensions for differential analysis and enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a transcriptomic (RNA-seq/miRNA/isoform) count matrix handled by the genes, miRNA or isoform modules rather than a lipid abundance matrix. No phenotype file with defined contrast groups is available, since edgeR differential abundance contrasts depend on it. Lipid identifiers cannot be parsed into lipid-class, chain-length and saturation components by lipidr, so the three lipid feature dimensions cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when an XCMS-style feature intensity matrix must be tied to gene function: exact-mass matching of m/z features to HMDB metabolites, removing unannotated features, and testing DAM enrichment among gene-associated metabolite sets.
skills.name: gene-metabolite-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-annotation-mapping Use when an XCMS-style feature intensity matrix must be tied to gene function: exact-mass matching of m/z features to HMDB metabolites, removing unannotated features, and testing DAM enrichment among gene-associated metabolite sets. No feature-to-metabolite mapping is available for the metabolomic system (as for the TIDEX dataset), so exact metabolite identities cannot be assigned Input is already a per-gene score vector (e.g., a finished ME file) — go directly to label propagation instead of re-mapping features Disease-relevant metabolites (e.g., acyl glycines, acyl carnitines used as IEM biomarkers) are not annotated to disease genes in HMDB, so enrichment mapping cannot connect them http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Links metabolomic features and metabolites to genes using HMDB gene-metabolite associations, so differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) can be converted into per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME/DME) scores that seed downstream network propagation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Links metabolomic features and metabolites to genes using HMDB gene-metabolite associations, so differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) can be converted into per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME/DME) scores that seed downstream network propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No feature-to-metabolite mapping is available for the metabolomic system (as for the TIDEX dataset), so exact metabolite identities cannot be assigned Input is already a per-gene score vector (e.g., a finished ME file) — go directly to label propagation instead of re-mapping features Disease-relevant metabolites (e.g., acyl glycines, acyl carnitines used as IEM biomarkers) are not annotated to disease genes in HMDB, so enrichment mapping cannot connect them

skills.description: Use when a pseudotargeted metabolomics dataset over a mutant/genotype panel needs to be mined for metabolite-mutation associations, e.g. ranking mutants by module eigenmetabolite to find genes controlling a specific metabolite like glucoraphanin.
skills.name: gene-metabolite-association-mining
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-association-mining Use when a pseudotargeted metabolomics dataset over a mutant/genotype panel needs to be mined for metabolite-mutation associations, e.g. ranking mutants by module eigenmetabolite to find genes controlling a specific metabolite like glucoraphanin. Input is raw LC-MS vendor data requiring peak picking — upstream processing is handled first by tidyMass within MetMiner before association mining The dataset is not from a genotype/mutant panel or lacks sample metadata linking mutants to abundance columns, so eigenmetabolite ranking across mutants is not meaningful The goal is metabolite annotation itself rather than gene-metabolite association discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Mining of pseudotargeted plant metabolomics datasets with MetMiner's iterative WGCNA strategy to identify gene-metabolite associations, such as F-box mutants affecting glucosinolate hub metabolites, and validate them by mutant/complementation. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Mining of pseudotargeted plant metabolomics datasets with MetMiner's iterative WGCNA strategy to identify gene-metabolite associations, such as F-box mutants affecting glucosinolate hub metabolites, and validate them by mutant/complementation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS vendor data requiring peak picking — upstream processing is handled first by tidyMass within MetMiner before association mining The dataset is not from a genotype/mutant panel or lacks sample metadata linking mutants to abundance columns, so eigenmetabolite ranking across mutants is not meaningful The goal is metabolite annotation itself rather than gene-metabolite association discovery

skills.description: Use when haCCA-integrated Data objects (aligned MALDI-MSI features on 10X Visium spots) are available and the goal is to find genes whose spatial pattern co-localizes with specific metabolites.
skills.name: gene-metabolite-colocalization-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-colocalization-analysis Use when haCCA-integrated Data objects (aligned MALDI-MSI features on 10X Visium spots) are available and the goal is to find genes whose spatial pattern co-localizes with specific metabolites. The data have not been integrated yet — you only have raw MALDI-MSI m/z spectra and spatial transcriptome objects with no shared spots or features; run haCCA's alignment first The gene-metabolite candidate lacks a plausible metabolic link or the metabolite's spatial pattern is dominated by noise/batch effects rather than a genuine tissue gradient http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Identify gene-metabolite associations on haCCA-integrated spatial data by comparing the spot-level spatial distributions of transcriptome genes (e.g. Th) against MALDI-MSI metabolite features (e.g. dopamine, 3-MT), using Scanpy spatial plots on the aligned 10X Visium spot grid. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: Identify gene-metabolite associations on haCCA-integrated spatial data by comparing the spot-level spatial distributions of transcriptome genes (e.g. Th) against MALDI-MSI metabolite features (e.g. dopamine, 3-MT), using Scanpy spatial plots on the aligned 10X Visium spot grid.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have not been integrated yet — you only have raw MALDI-MSI m/z spectra and spatial transcriptome objects with no shared spots or features; run haCCA's alignment first The gene-metabolite candidate lacks a plausible metabolic link or the metabolite's spatial pattern is dominated by noise/batch effects rather than a genuine tissue gradient

skills.description: Use when you have a patient-vs-control metabolite z-score matrix and need to convert DAMs into per-gene enrichment scores via gene-metabolite associations before ranking candidate genes.
skills.name: gene-metabolite-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-enrichment-testing Use when you have a patient-vs-control metabolite z-score matrix and need to convert DAMs into per-gene enrichment scores via gene-metabolite associations before ranking candidate genes. The metabolomic system cannot resolve feature-to-metabolite mapping (as for the TIDEX cohort), so DAMs cannot be assigned HMDB identities for enrichment testing The disease-relevant metabolites are unmeasurable or unannotated in HMDB (e.g., large glycosaminoglycans for the IDS patient, or acyl glycines/acyl carnitines not annotated to IEM genes), making the gene-level enrichment insensitive You only need variant-level prioritization without metabolomic evidence — Exomiser's phenotype-driven ranking alone is the appropriate comparator in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Computes per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME/DME) scores by testing whether a patient's differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) are over-represented among each gene's HMDB-curated metabolite set, then scales the scores 0-1 for use as network labels. This is the pre-propagation step of metPropagate that converts a metabolite z-score matrix into per-gene labels. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Computes per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME/DME) scores by testing whether a patient's differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) are over-represented among each gene's HMDB-curated metabolite set, then scales the scores 0-1 for use as network labels. This is the pre-propagation step of metPropagate that converts a metabolite z-score matrix into per-gene labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolomic system cannot resolve feature-to-metabolite mapping (as for the TIDEX cohort), so DAMs cannot be assigned HMDB identities for enrichment testing The disease-relevant metabolites are unmeasurable or unannotated in HMDB (e.g., large glycosaminoglycans for the IDS patient, or acyl glycines/acyl carnitines not annotated to IEM genes), making the gene-level enrichment insensitive You only need variant-level prioritization without metabolomic evidence — Exomiser's phenotype-driven ranking alone is the appropriate comparator in that setting

skills.description: Use when you have both gene and metabolite feature tables mapped to KEGG pathway nodes and need to compare topology-aware impact analysis (eSPIA) against ORA, or to reproduce SMART 2.0's IOPA breast cancer result (eSPIA: 2 significant pathways vs ORA: 51 at pFDR < 0.05).
skills.name: gene-metabolite-ora-vs-espia-comparison
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-ora-vs-espia-comparison Use when you have both gene and metabolite feature tables mapped to KEGG pathway nodes and need to compare topology-aware impact analysis (eSPIA) against ORA, or to reproduce SMART 2.0's IOPA breast cancer result (eSPIA: 2 significant pathways vs ORA: 51 at pFDR < 0.05). Only a single omics type (genes OR metabolites alone) is available — the original SPIA/ORA single-type setting, not the joint gene-and-metabolite eSPIA analysis. Pathways lack interaction topology (e.g., non-KEGG sources without node/edge structure) — ORA alone is applicable, but eSPIA's perturbation-accumulation statistic requires KEGG pathway topology. The goal is untargeted peak processing (preprocessing, normalization, QC) rather than downstream pathway significance testing — use SMART 2.0's earlier modules instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Contrast topology-aware integrative pathway analysis (eSPIA, an impact-analysis extension of SPIA that jointly perturbs genes and metabolites in KEGG pathways) with over-representation analysis (ORA) on the same gene and metabolite feature sets, since the two methods can disagree sharply in how many pathways they call significant. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: Contrast topology-aware integrative pathway analysis (eSPIA, an impact-analysis extension of SPIA that jointly perturbs genes and metabolites in KEGG pathways) with over-representation analysis (ORA) on the same gene and metabolite feature sets, since the two methods can disagree sharply in how many pathways they call significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single omics type (genes OR metabolites alone) is available — the original SPIA/ORA single-type setting, not the joint gene-and-metabolite eSPIA analysis. Pathways lack interaction topology (e.g., non-KEGG sources without node/edge structure) — ORA alone is applicable, but eSPIA's perturbation-accumulation statistic requires KEGG pathway topology. The goal is untargeted peak processing (preprocessing, normalization, QC) rather than downstream pathway significance testing — use SMART 2.0's earlier modules instead.

skills.description: Use when an analyte list contains both genes/proteins and metabolites and you need their pathway memberships consolidated from multiple pathway databases before enrichment or clustering analysis.
skills.name: gene-metabolite-pathway-membership-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-pathway-membership-mapping Use when an analyte list contains both genes/proteins and metabolites and you need their pathway memberships consolidated from multiple pathway databases before enrichment or clustering analysis. The analytes are already annotated with pathway memberships from a single database and no cross-database integration is needed The goal is pathway enrichment itself rather than membership lookup — use runFisherTest/runCombinedFisherTest on top of the mapped memberships instead You need organism-specific or non-human pathways outside the HMDB/KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways scope RaMP integrates http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Maps input genes and/or metabolites to biochemical and disease pathways by querying RaMP, a MySQL-backed relational database integrating KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB, so that mixed analyte lists can be interpreted through a single unified pathway membership resource. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo8010016
skills.summary: Maps input genes and/or metabolites to biochemical and disease pathways by querying RaMP, a MySQL-backed relational database integrating KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB, so that mixed analyte lists can be interpreted through a single unified pathway membership resource.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analytes are already annotated with pathway memberships from a single database and no cross-database integration is needed The goal is pathway enrichment itself rather than membership lookup — use runFisherTest/runCombinedFisherTest on top of the mapped memberships instead You need organism-specific or non-human pathways outside the HMDB/KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways scope RaMP integrates

skills.description: Use when integrating spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data at spot resolution and you need to select gene–metabolite feature pairs whose Pearson correlation on anchor spot pairs will drive CCA-based feature enrichment before ICP alignment.
skills.name: gene-metabolite-pearson-correlation
skills.search_text: gene-metabolite-pearson-correlation Use when integrating spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data at spot resolution and you need to select gene–metabolite feature pairs whose Pearson correlation on anchor spot pairs will drive CCA-based feature enrichment before ICP alignment. Input data have already been aligned and a shared fcca variate exists — rerunning Pearson correlation on aligned features would double-count information already captured by the high-correlated variables The spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data are from non-adjacent tissue sections with no plausible co-localization, so anchor spot pairs cannot be meaningfully identified The task is general-purpose correlation analysis between two unrelated feature matrices (e.g. bulk omics or image features) with no spatial anchor-pair or Simpson-diversity context http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 In the haCCA workflow, this skill identifies high-correlated gene–metabolite feature pairs by computing Pearson correlations between gene features from a spatial transcriptome Data object (a) and metabolite m/z features from an ICP-aligned MALDI-MSI Data object (b_prime) on the anchor spot pairs retained by spatial-distance and Simpson-diversity (<0.2) filters. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: In the haCCA workflow, this skill identifies high-correlated gene–metabolite feature pairs by computing Pearson correlations between gene features from a spatial transcriptome Data object (a) and metabolite m/z features from an ICP-aligned MALDI-MSI Data object (b_prime) on the anchor spot pairs retained by spatial-distance and Simpson-diversity (<0.2) filters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data have already been aligned and a shared fcca variate exists — rerunning Pearson correlation on aligned features would double-count information already captured by the high-correlated variables The spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data are from non-adjacent tissue sections with no plausible co-localization, so anchor spot pairs cannot be meaningfully identified The task is general-purpose correlation analysis between two unrelated feature matrices (e.g. bulk omics or image features) with no spatial anchor-pair or Simpson-diversity context

skills.description: Use when the input is a GO analysis result table (e.g. chord_example.csv) linking genes to GO terms and the goal is a circos-style chord diagram rendered without programming, via GraphBio's chord plot module.
skills.name: gene-ontology-chord-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-chord-plot-visualization Use when the input is a GO analysis result table (e.g. chord_example.csv) linking genes to GO terms and the goal is a circos-style chord diagram rendered without programming, via GraphBio's chord plot module. The visualization target is not GO analysis results — GraphBio routes other data types to separate modules (e.g. volcano_example.csv for volcano plots, surv_example.csv for survival curves, venn_example.csv for Venn plots) Data preprocessing or statistical computation is required — GraphBio specifically focuses on facilitating the generation of publication-ready plots instead of data preprocessing and computing The user needs custom layouts beyond the module's default parameters and color presets, which the paper does not document http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Generates a publication-ready chord (circos) plot of Gene Ontology analysis results by uploading a GO-to-gene association table to GraphBio, which wraps the GOplot R backend (Walter et al., 2015) to arrange GO terms and linked genes on a circular layout with ribbon connections. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fgene.2022.957317
skills.summary: Generates a publication-ready chord (circos) plot of Gene Ontology analysis results by uploading a GO-to-gene association table to GraphBio, which wraps the GOplot R backend (Walter et al., 2015) to arrange GO terms and linked genes on a circular layout with ribbon connections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The visualization target is not GO analysis results — GraphBio routes other data types to separate modules (e.g. volcano_example.csv for volcano plots, surv_example.csv for survival curves, venn_example.csv for Venn plots) Data preprocessing or statistical computation is required — GraphBio specifically focuses on facilitating the generation of publication-ready plots instead of data preprocessing and computing The user needs custom layouts beyond the module's default parameters and color presets, which the paper does not document

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an integrative clustering (e.g. KLIC vs COCA) better exploits the biological information in multiple omic datasets, by scoring cluster coherence through shared Gene Ontology terms across BP, MF and CC ontologies.
skills.name: gene-ontology-term-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-term-overlap-scoring Use when evaluating whether an integrative clustering (e.g. KLIC vs COCA) better exploits the biological information in multiple omic datasets, by scoring cluster coherence through shared Gene Ontology terms across BP, MF and CC ontologies. When cluster members are not genes or lack Gene Ontology annotations, since GOTO scores are undefined without GO term overlap When only a numeric cluster-quality metric is needed and biological coherence is not in question — average silhouette width alone suffices When comparing clusterings of samples/patients (e.g. pan-cancer subtyping of Hoadley et al. 2014) rather than gene modules, unless GO-based coherence is specifically required http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Computes Gene Ontology Term Overlap (GOTO) scores per ontology (biological process, molecular function, cellular component) to assess the biological quality of clusterings produced by integrative clustering methods such as KLIC and COCA, and to compare them against single-dataset clusterings. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Computes Gene Ontology Term Overlap (GOTO) scores per ontology (biological process, molecular function, cellular component) to assess the biological quality of clusterings produced by integrative clustering methods such as KLIC and COCA, and to compare them against single-dataset clusterings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cluster members are not genes or lack Gene Ontology annotations, since GOTO scores are undefined without GO term overlap When only a numeric cluster-quality metric is needed and biological coherence is not in question — average silhouette width alone suffices When comparing clusterings of samples/patients (e.g. pan-cancer subtyping of Hoadley et al. 2014) rather than gene modules, unless GO-based coherence is specifically required

skills.description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g., selected by an absolute log2 fold change cutoff such as > 1) and want to annotate/link them to curated pathway resources (WikiPathways) as a network extension in Cytoscape.
skills.name: gene-pathway-network-extension
skills.search_text: gene-pathway-network-extension Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g., selected by an absolute log2 fold change cutoff such as > 1) and want to annotate/link them to curated pathway resources (WikiPathways) as a network extension in Cytoscape. The goal is to extend a protein-protein interaction network with compound-target or disease-gene annotations (Use case 1) rather than gene-pathway associations The input is not a gene list from an experimental dataset but, e.g., an author-article-journal bibliographic network requiring the two-step extension mechanism No curated linkset exists for the organism or identifier type of the gene list (linksets cover specific species, e.g., WikiPathways covers 13 species) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Extends a network of differentially expressed genes with gene-pathway associations from curated WikiPathways linksets using the CyTargetLinker 4.0.0+ automation feature ('cytargetlinker extend') in Cytoscape 3.6.0+, as demonstrated in Use case 2 where 65 Mecp2-/y DEGs (|log2FC| > 1) were linked to curated mouse WikiPathways pathways. metabolomics/v3 10.12688/f1000research.14613.2
skills.summary: Extends a network of differentially expressed genes with gene-pathway associations from curated WikiPathways linksets using the CyTargetLinker 4.0.0+ automation feature ('cytargetlinker extend') in Cytoscape 3.6.0+, as demonstrated in Use case 2 where 65 Mecp2-/y DEGs (|log2FC| > 1) were linked to curated mouse WikiPathways pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to extend a protein-protein interaction network with compound-target or disease-gene annotations (Use case 1) rather than gene-pathway associations The input is not a gene list from an experimental dataset but, e.g., an author-article-journal bibliographic network requiring the two-step extension mechanism No curated linkset exists for the organism or identifier type of the gene list (linksets cover specific species, e.g., WikiPathways covers 13 species)

skills.description: Use when a gene prioritization method must be quantitatively validated against known causative genes — via permutation tests, percentile-of-causative-gene metrics, or ablations of the underlying interaction network.
skills.name: gene-prioritization-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gene-prioritization-benchmarking Use when a gene prioritization method must be quantitatively validated against known causative genes — via permutation tests, percentile-of-causative-gene metrics, or ablations of the underlying interaction network. There are no known causative genes or validated diagnoses for the cohort, so percentile-of-causative-gene metrics cannot be computed Candidate gene lists are already so small (e.g., trio WES with parental data) that top-20th-percentile ranking is trivially uninformative — the authors note trio WES shortens candidate lists versus their singleton exomes The goal is discovery rather than validation — benchmarking consumes known disease-gene assignments (e.g., OMIM) and cannot be run on undiagnosed patients http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Benchmarks a gene prioritization method (e.g., metPropagate label-propagation scores) by measuring how often causative genes fall in the top 20th percentile of candidate lists, using permutation controls, head-to-head tool comparisons (Exomiser), and network ablations (full vs physical-only STRING). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks a gene prioritization method (e.g., metPropagate label-propagation scores) by measuring how often causative genes fall in the top 20th percentile of candidate lists, using permutation controls, head-to-head tool comparisons (Exomiser), and network ablations (full vs physical-only STRING).
skills.when_to_use_negative: There are no known causative genes or validated diagnoses for the cohort, so percentile-of-causative-gene metrics cannot be computed Candidate gene lists are already so small (e.g., trio WES with parental data) that top-20th-percentile ranking is trivially uninformative — the authors note trio WES shortens candidate lists versus their singleton exomes The goal is discovery rather than validation — benchmarking consumes known disease-gene assignments (e.g., OMIM) and cannot be run on undiagnosed patients

skills.description: Use when building a draft genome-scale metabolic model from annotated amino-acid FASTA (Type 1) or DIAMOND BLASTp hits (Type 2) and reactions must carry gene-reaction provenance from KEGG annotation.
skills.name: gene-protein-reaction-association-assembly
skills.search_text: gene-protein-reaction-association-assembly Use when building a draft genome-scale metabolic model from annotated amino-acid FASTA (Type 1) or DIAMOND BLASTp hits (Type 2) and reactions must carry gene-reaction provenance from KEGG annotation. Input is already an existing SBML GENRE (Type 3) needing only additional gap-filling — no new GPR assembly from gene hits is required No annotated protein sequences or BLASTp hits are available, so reactions cannot be traced to genes (draft would lack GPR provenance) The task is curating the universal database itself rather than assembling a draft model — use UniversalCreation.py / curateuniversal.py instead http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Assembly of gene-protein-reaction (GPR) associations during draft GENRE construction in Reconstructor: each DIAMOND BLASTp KEGG gene hit is mapped to a ModelSEED reaction (loaded from universal.pickle as a COBRApy Model) and the annotated gene is attached so every retained reaction is traceable to a gene of origin. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Assembly of gene-protein-reaction (GPR) associations during draft GENRE construction in Reconstructor: each DIAMOND BLASTp KEGG gene hit is mapped to a ModelSEED reaction (loaded from universal.pickle as a COBRApy Model) and the annotated gene is attached so every retained reaction is traceable to a gene of origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an existing SBML GENRE (Type 3) needing only additional gap-filling — no new GPR assembly from gene hits is required No annotated protein sequences or BLASTp hits are available, so reactions cannot be traced to genes (draft would lack GPR provenance) The task is curating the universal database itself rather than assembling a draft model — use UniversalCreation.py / curateuniversal.py instead

skills.description: Use when a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. an SBML file such as BioModels MODEL2007210001) must be quality-controlled before or after publication, and GPR coverage, metabolite annotation, or an overall MEMOTE score are needed as evidence of community-standard compliance.
skills.name: gene-protein-reaction-coverage-assessment
skills.search_text: gene-protein-reaction-coverage-assessment Use when a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. an SBML file such as BioModels MODEL2007210001) must be quality-controlled before or after publication, and GPR coverage, metabolite annotation, or an overall MEMOTE score are needed as evidence of community-standard compliance. The model is not a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format (e.g. a kinetic model, PPI network, or expression matrix) — MEMOTE's test battery will not apply. The goal is drug-target identification or bottleneck analysis rather than annotation quality assessment — findCPcli's chokepoint/dead-end-metabolite workflow, not MEMOTE, is the appropriate tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Quantifies the fraction of reactions in a genome-scale metabolic model that carry Gene-Protein-Reaction (GPR) associations, using MEMOTE's standardised test battery so that annotation completeness can be compared against community standards for published GEMs. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of reactions in a genome-scale metabolic model that carry Gene-Protein-Reaction (GPR) associations, using MEMOTE's standardised test battery so that annotation completeness can be compared against community standards for published GEMs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is not a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format (e.g. a kinetic model, PPI network, or expression matrix) — MEMOTE's test battery will not apply. The goal is drug-target identification or bottleneck analysis rather than annotation quality assessment — findCPcli's chokepoint/dead-end-metabolite workflow, not MEMOTE, is the appropriate tool.

skills.description: Use when GWAS summary statistics must be stratified by SNP-heritability enrichment for a gene set (e.g., tissue DE genes from exercise training) and you need to convert a gene list into a partitioned/binary LDSC annotation.
skills.name: gene-set-annotation-construction-from-degenes
skills.search_text: gene-set-annotation-construction-from-degenes Use when GWAS summary statistics must be stratified by SNP-heritability enrichment for a gene set (e.g., tissue DE genes from exercise training) and you need to convert a gene list into a partitioned/binary LDSC annotation. You need expression-mediated heritability (proportion of hSNP2 mediated by expression) rather than annotation-based enrichment — use MESC instead The gene set is not a coherent gene list (e.g., per-gene trait-tissue-gene triplets or TWAS hits) — S-PrediXcan/FUSION-style TWAS is the appropriate skill The DE gene list lacks a matched expressed-gene background annotation, making enrichment uninterpretable relative to baseline expression http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs LDSC-ready SNP annotations from tissue-specific differentially expressed gene sets (e.g., sex-consistent 8-week exercise DE genes) by assigning SNPs/loci within 100kb windows of the DE genes, alongside the LDSC baseline annotation and an all-expressed-genes control annotation, enabling heritability enrichment estimation per trait x tissue gene set. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Constructs LDSC-ready SNP annotations from tissue-specific differentially expressed gene sets (e.g., sex-consistent 8-week exercise DE genes) by assigning SNPs/loci within 100kb windows of the DE genes, alongside the LDSC baseline annotation and an all-expressed-genes control annotation, enabling heritability enrichment estimation per trait x tissue gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need expression-mediated heritability (proportion of hSNP2 mediated by expression) rather than annotation-based enrichment — use MESC instead The gene set is not a coherent gene list (e.g., per-gene trait-tissue-gene triplets or TWAS hits) — S-PrediXcan/FUSION-style TWAS is the appropriate skill The DE gene list lacks a matched expressed-gene background annotation, making enrichment uninterpretable relative to baseline expression

skills.description: Use when reproducing pathway-level gene-expression analyses (PLAGE, GSEA) that depend on a predefined gene-set collection whose memberships must match a historical KEGG/Biocarta version.
skills.name: gene-set-collection-curation
skills.search_text: gene-set-collection-curation Use when reproducing pathway-level gene-expression analyses (PLAGE, GSEA) that depend on a predefined gene-set collection whose memberships must match a historical KEGG/Biocarta version. When gene-sets must be defined de novo from custom biology rather than pulled from KEGG or Biocarta When an already-pinned, article-matched gene-set version is supplied — re-curation from live KEGG/Biocarta would break comparability with the reported ES and p-values When the analysis targets a single pathway of interest rather than the full ~400-pathway collection used for permutation-based significance http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assembles and pins the exact gene-set collection used for pathway-level expression analysis — here ~400 pathways and complexes from KEGG and Biocarta — so that downstream PLAGE or GSEA enrichment scores are reproducible despite continuous evolution of those pathway databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Assembles and pins the exact gene-set collection used for pathway-level expression analysis — here ~400 pathways and complexes from KEGG and Biocarta — so that downstream PLAGE or GSEA enrichment scores are reproducible despite continuous evolution of those pathway databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene-sets must be defined de novo from custom biology rather than pulled from KEGG or Biocarta When an already-pinned, article-matched gene-set version is supplied — re-curation from live KEGG/Biocarta would break comparability with the reported ES and p-values When the analysis targets a single pathway of interest rather than the full ~400-pathway collection used for permutation-based significance

skills.description: Use when ionomics data (e.g. ICP-MS ion concentrations for haploid S. cerevisiae deletion mutants) have been clustered and you need to identify statistically significant clusters and associated biological processes via GO Slim annotation and GO terms enrichment.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when ionomics data (e.g. ICP-MS ion concentrations for haploid S. cerevisiae deletion mutants) have been clustered and you need to identify statistically significant clusters and associated biological processes via GO Slim annotation and GO terms enrichment. The input has not passed through IonFlow Pre-processing (raw, unbatch-corrected concentration data) — the enrichment section requires the cleaned dataset produced by pre-processing first The goal is element-element correlation or relevance network extraction rather than biological-process over-representation of mutant clusters The dataset is not from an organism with available GO/GO Slim annotations compatible with the IonFlow package's bundled resources http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistically identify over-represented biological processes and Gene Ontology (GO Slim) annotations among clusters of ion-profile-similar yeast deletion mutants, as implemented in the IonFlow R/Galaxy pipeline for ICP-MS ionomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01841-z
skills.summary: Statistically identify over-represented biological processes and Gene Ontology (GO Slim) annotations among clusters of ion-profile-similar yeast deletion mutants, as implemented in the IonFlow R/Galaxy pipeline for ICP-MS ionomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input has not passed through IonFlow Pre-processing (raw, unbatch-corrected concentration data) — the enrichment section requires the cleaned dataset produced by pre-processing first The goal is element-element correlation or relevance network extraction rather than biological-process over-representation of mutant clusters The dataset is not from an organism with available GO/GO Slim annotations compatible with the IonFlow package's bundled resources

skills.description: Use when interpreting ICA metagenes (sk vectors) from cancer omics data: you have a ranked gene list per component and need GO/KEGG functional enrichment to name the biological signal.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when interpreting ICA metagenes (sk vectors) from cancer omics data: you have a ranked gene list per component and need GO/KEGG functional enrichment to name the biological signal. Input is a raw expression matrix rather than an ICA-derived sk vector — the ICA decomposition (e.g., via the BIODICA Navigator or the companion notebook) must be computed first Only a short unranked gene list is available without its full sk-vector ranking — GSEA on the ranking cannot be run, only the overrepresentation branch applies The goal is ICA component number selection, stability analysis, or deconvolution (BIODICA stability estimation or DeconICA) rather than functional interpretation of components http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assigns biological meaning to ICA metagenes (sk vectors) from cancer omics data by combining hypergeometric overrepresentation testing of the most-contributing genes with Gene Set Enrichment Analysis on the full sk-vector ranking, against curated GO/KEGG gene-set libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414
skills.summary: Assigns biological meaning to ICA metagenes (sk vectors) from cancer omics data by combining hypergeometric overrepresentation testing of the most-contributing genes with Gene Set Enrichment Analysis on the full sk-vector ranking, against curated GO/KEGG gene-set libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw expression matrix rather than an ICA-derived sk vector — the ICA decomposition (e.g., via the BIODICA Navigator or the companion notebook) must be computed first Only a short unranked gene list is available without its full sk-vector ranking — GSEA on the ranking cannot be run, only the overrepresentation branch applies The goal is ICA component number selection, stability analysis, or deconvolution (BIODICA stability estimation or DeconICA) rather than functional interpretation of components

skills.description: Use when testing whether a defined gene set (e.g., exercise-responsive DEGs) is enriched for trait/tissue associations in TWAS/S-PrediXcan results across many tissue-by-trait cells, with partial pooling and direction-of-effect testing.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when testing whether a defined gene set (e.g., exercise-responsive DEGs) is enriched for trait/tissue associations in TWAS/S-PrediXcan results across many tissue-by-trait cells, with partial pooling and direction-of-effect testing. The question concerns SNP-level heritability enrichment rather than gene-level TWAS hit enrichment — use LDSC or MESC instead, which accommodate linkage disequilibrium and eQTL-mediated heritability. Few or no tissue-by-trait cells have nonzero DEG-PrediXcan intersect counts, leaving the hierarchical binomial model underpowered to partial-pool. The gene set lacks sex-consistent state assignments (no repfdr F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 nodes), so direction-of-effect enrichment cannot be defined as in this workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether exercise training-responsive gene sets (e.g., sex-consistent 8-week DEGs) are over- or under-represented among trait-associated genes from S-PrediXcan output, using both a hierarchical Bayesian partial-pooling binomial model in Stan and frequentist fgsea() per trait-by-tissue pair. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Tests whether exercise training-responsive gene sets (e.g., sex-consistent 8-week DEGs) are over- or under-represented among trait-associated genes from S-PrediXcan output, using both a hierarchical Bayesian partial-pooling binomial model in Stan and frequentist fgsea() per trait-by-tissue pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns SNP-level heritability enrichment rather than gene-level TWAS hit enrichment — use LDSC or MESC instead, which accommodate linkage disequilibrium and eQTL-mediated heritability. Few or no tissue-by-trait cells have nonzero DEG-PrediXcan intersect counts, leaving the hierarchical binomial model underpowered to partial-pool. The gene set lacks sex-consistent state assignments (no repfdr F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 nodes), so direction-of-effect enrichment cannot be defined as in this workflow.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to rank predefined gene-sets (e.g., KEGG or Biocarta pathways) by enrichment score in a two-group comparison and assess their significance by random label permutation.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-score-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-score-ranking Use when the goal is to rank predefined gene-sets (e.g., KEGG or Biocarta pathways) by enrichment score in a two-group comparison and assess their significance by random label permutation. When the aim is to obtain pathway activity levels per sample (as in PLAGE) rather than an aggregate ES and rank per comparison; GSEA produces an ES for a gene-set across samples, not a continuous activity level for each individual sample When the gene-sets of interest are not predefined (e.g., discovery of novel pathways from data alone); this skill requires an a priori gene-set collection When the comparison is not between two pre-defined groups of samples (e.g., survival analysis or continuous covariates), since the ES and permutation scheme as described are formulated for pairwise group comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 This skill applies the Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) method to rank predefined pathways/gene-sets by an enrichment score in two-group comparisons, providing a baseline against which pathway-level SVD methods like PLAGE can be compared. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: This skill applies the Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) method to rank predefined pathways/gene-sets by an enrichment score in two-group comparisons, providing a baseline against which pathway-level SVD methods like PLAGE can be compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the aim is to obtain pathway activity levels per sample (as in PLAGE) rather than an aggregate ES and rank per comparison; GSEA produces an ES for a gene-set across samples, not a continuous activity level for each individual sample When the gene-sets of interest are not predefined (e.g., discovery of novel pathways from data alone); this skill requires an a priori gene-set collection When the comparison is not between two pre-defined groups of samples (e.g., survival analysis or continuous covariates), since the ES and permutation scheme as described are formulated for pairwise group comparisons

skills.description: Use when two gene sets from independent studies (e.g. metabolite-interacting genes and GWAS trait genes) must be statistically compared for over-represented overlap via a hypergeometric upper-tail test.
skills.name: gene-set-overlap-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-overlap-enrichment-analysis Use when two gene sets from independent studies (e.g. metabolite-interacting genes and GWAS trait genes) must be statistically compared for over-represented overlap via a hypergeometric upper-tail test. Input is paired metabolomics-GWAS data (metabolite-GWAS studies) — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for independent, unpaired metabolomics and GWAS studies, and analysis is limited to genes with known metabolite interactions A full rank-based or permutation gene-set enrichment (GSEA-style) test is needed — this skill computes only a hypergeometric over-representation P-value on set overlap sizes Gene sets are defined on different identifier universes that cannot be mapped to the discoverable gene population (GWAS-network discoverable genes), since k, n, m, N must be counts in a common universe http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 MetGWAS 1.0 Module 4 computes an upper-tail hypergeometric over-representation P-value for the overlap between a metabolite-interacting gene set (Module 2) and a trait/disease-related GWAS subnetwork gene set (Module 3), against a discoverable-gene population. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: MetGWAS 1.0 Module 4 computes an upper-tail hypergeometric over-representation P-value for the overlap between a metabolite-interacting gene set (Module 2) and a trait/disease-related GWAS subnetwork gene set (Module 3), against a discoverable-gene population.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is paired metabolomics-GWAS data (metabolite-GWAS studies) — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for independent, unpaired metabolomics and GWAS studies, and analysis is limited to genes with known metabolite interactions A full rank-based or permutation gene-set enrichment (GSEA-style) test is needed — this skill computes only a hypergeometric over-representation P-value on set overlap sizes Gene sets are defined on different identifier universes that cannot be mapped to the discoverable gene population (GWAS-network discoverable genes), since k, n, m, N must be counts in a common universe

skills.description: Use when raw gene-expression data must be translated into per-sample, per-pathway activity levels using predefined KEGG/Biocarta gene sets before group comparisons such as diabetic vs. non-diabetic or smoker vs. non-smoker.
skills.name: gene-set-submatrix-decomposition
skills.search_text: gene-set-submatrix-decomposition Use when raw gene-expression data must be translated into per-sample, per-pathway activity levels using predefined KEGG/Biocarta gene sets before group comparisons such as diabetic vs. non-diabetic or smoker vs. non-smoker. When the goal is to evaluate individual genes rather than group-level pathway activity; the article states the pathway-based results can be complementary to one more focused on individual genes but this skill itself operates on gene-set submatrices. When no predefined pathway/gene-set annotations exist for the organism or platform — the SVD must be run per defined pathway submatrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Decomposes the standardized expression submatrix of each predefined gene set (pathway) via singular value decomposition, taking the first SVD metagene's gene weights and its associated activity-level coefficients per sample as the pathway's activity profile (PLAGE). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Decomposes the standardized expression submatrix of each predefined gene set (pathway) via singular value decomposition, taking the first SVD metagene's gene weights and its associated activity-level coefficients per sample as the pathway's activity profile (PLAGE).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to evaluate individual genes rather than group-level pathway activity; the article states the pathway-based results can be complementary to one more focused on individual genes but this skill itself operates on gene-set submatrices. When no predefined pathway/gene-set annotations exist for the organism or platform — the SVD must be run per defined pathway submatrix.

skills.description: Use when a multi-tissue differential expression study (e.g., MoTrPAC PASS1B rat endurance training, 15 tissues) needs a quantitative measure of DE gene-set overlap and tissue-specificity across tissues.
skills.name: gene-set-tissue-specificity-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-set-tissue-specificity-quantification Use when a multi-tissue differential expression study (e.g., MoTrPAC PASS1B rat endurance training, 15 tissues) needs a quantitative measure of DE gene-set overlap and tissue-specificity across tissues. skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-model-constraint-editing Use when a human GEM (e.g. RECON3D in SBML/XML) must be updated with flux information from gut microbiota models — i.e. host reactions containing metabolites present in the microbiota model need their lower bounds rewritten. The goal is to modify upper bounds, add/delete reactions, or edit host reactions whose metabolites are absent from the microbiota model — M2R only rewrites lower bounds of reactions sharing metabolites with the microbiota model The host GEM and microbiota model share no metabolite identifiers, so no reactions would be matched or updated The input is already a modified/feature-level model output rather than an original GEM plus microbiota flux data Edits the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D) using aggregated in- and out-fluxes from gut microbiota metabolic models, via the M2R Python add-on to cobrapy. This couples host and microbiota metabolism so that microbially consumed/produced metabolites constrain what the human GEM can exchange. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: Edits the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D) using aggregated in- and out-fluxes from gut microbiota metabolic models, via the M2R Python add-on to cobrapy. This couples host and microbiota metabolism so that microbially consumed/produced metabolites constrain what the human GEM can exchange.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to modify upper bounds, add/delete reactions, or edit host reactions whose metabolites are absent from the microbiota model — M2R only rewrites lower bounds of reactions sharing metabolites with the microbiota model The host GEM and microbiota model share no metabolite identifiers, so no reactions would be matched or updated The input is already a modified/feature-level model output rather than an original GEM plus microbiota flux data

skills.description: Use when a workflow requires a simulation-ready GEM (e.g., for FVA-based shadow-price extraction) and only a raw published model file such as iJO1366.mat or Yeast-GEM.mat is available.

skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-model-curation Use when a workflow requires a simulation-ready GEM (e.g., for FVA-based shadow-price extraction) and only a raw published model file such as iJO1366.mat or Yeast-GEM.mat is available. skills.summary: Prepare genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) for downstream constraint-based analyses by curating published reconstructions (iJO1366, Yeast-GEM/Yeast8) with COBRAToolbox in MATLAB, producing irreversible optimized models that support shadow-price calculation in SARTRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A curated irreversible model (ModelIrrevOpt90.mat or yeast_IrrevOpt90.mat) is already available — rerunning curation is unnecessary The downstream task needs original reversible model semantics (e.g., SBML-level model browsing) rather than the irreversible form required by SARTRE's optimization step

skills.description: Use when a constraint-based model pipeline (e.g., SARTRE shadow-price features) must be shown to be insensitive to medium composition — alternate carbon sources or limiting carbon/nitrogen/phosphorus uptake rates — relative to a glucose base model.
skills.name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-media-perturbation
skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-model-media-perturbation Use when a constraint-based model pipeline (e.g., SARTRE shadow-price features) must be shown to be insensitive to medium composition — alternate carbon sources or limiting carbon/nitrogen/phosphorus uptake rates — relative to a glucose base model. The research question concerns prediction performance on other tasks (shared-MPI exclusion, subsystem exclusion, or permutation tests) rather than media-composition sensitivity. The target organism/model is S. cerevisiae (Yeast-GEM) and no medium-perturbation design for that GEM has been defined — this skill's workflow is grounded in iJO1366 media manipulations. The dataset lacks a glucose base model as the reference against which alternate-media metrics are compared. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Robustness-testing skill for SARTRE: perturb the media composition of the curated iJO1366 GEM (alternate carbon sources acetate, fructose, glycerol, mannose, succinate, plus limiting vs non-limiting C/N/P uptake bounds), recompute shadow prices per condition, and compare random-forest classification metrics (accuracy, AUC, F1) against the glucose baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad098
skills.summary: Robustness-testing skill for SARTRE: perturb the media composition of the curated iJO1366 GEM (alternate carbon sources acetate, fructose, glycerol, mannose, succinate, plus limiting vs non-limiting C/N/P uptake bounds), recompute shadow prices per condition, and compare random-forest classification metrics (accuracy, AUC, F1) against the glucose baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The research question concerns prediction performance on other tasks (shared-MPI exclusion, subsystem exclusion, or permutation tests) rather than media-composition sensitivity. The target organism/model is S. cerevisiae (Yeast-GEM) and no medium-perturbation design for that GEM has been defined — this skill's workflow is grounded in iJO1366 media manipulations. The dataset lacks a glucose base model as the reference against which alternate-media metrics are compared.

skills.description: Use when a newly constructed or revised genome-scale metabolic model (SBML, e.g. from BioModels) must be checked against community standards such as MEMOTE before publication or reuse in downstream analyses.
skills.name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-model-quality-assessment Use when a newly constructed or revised genome-scale metabolic model (SBML, e.g. from BioModels) must be checked against community standards such as MEMOTE before publication or reuse in downstream analyses. The goal is functional simulation (e.g. FBA growth rates, chokepoint prediction with findCPcli) rather than structural/annotation quality scoring of the model. The model is not in SBML or cannot be instantiated by COBRApy without errors, so the MEMOTE battery cannot be run meaningfully. Evaluating context-specificity or gene-expression integration — MEMOTE assesses annotation and consistency, not biological context fit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Standardised quality control of a genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) using MEMOTE, which reads the SBML model via COBRApy and scores annotation consistency, gene-protein-reaction coverage, stoichiometric consistency, and metadata. Applied here to the iHsaEC21_SARS-CoV-2 model to verify it meets community standards for a newly published GEM. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Standardised quality control of a genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) using MEMOTE, which reads the SBML model via COBRApy and scores annotation consistency, gene-protein-reaction coverage, stoichiometric consistency, and metadata. Applied here to the iHsaEC21_SARS-CoV-2 model to verify it meets community standards for a newly published GEM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is functional simulation (e.g. FBA growth rates, chokepoint prediction with findCPcli) rather than structural/annotation quality scoring of the model. The model is not in SBML or cannot be instantiated by COBRApy without errors, so the MEMOTE battery cannot be run meaningfully. Evaluating context-specificity or gene-expression integration — MEMOTE assesses annotation and consistency, not biological context fit.

skills.description: Use when predicting metabolite-protein interactions from constraint-based models and you need physiologically grounded metabolite features (shadow prices) instead of, or alongside, chemical fingerprints.
skills.name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-shadow-price-analysis
skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-model-shadow-price-analysis Use when predicting metabolite-protein interactions from constraint-based models and you need physiologically grounded metabolite features (shadow prices) instead of, or alongside, chemical fingerprints. You already have a rich metabolite feature table (e.g. precomputed fingerprints) and do not need constraint-based shadow-price features. No active GUROBI license is available — the optimization step (`optimization.py`) cannot run without it. The task targets a metabolic model other than the curated GEMs and no curation/irreversibility step has been performed on it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Computes shadow prices from flux variability analysis of curated genome-scale metabolic models (iJO1366, Yeast-GEM) using the GUROBI optimizer, and uses these dual values as metabolite features for metabolite-protein interaction prediction in the SARTRE framework. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad098
skills.summary: Computes shadow prices from flux variability analysis of curated genome-scale metabolic models (iJO1366, Yeast-GEM) using the GUROBI optimizer, and uses these dual values as metabolite features for metabolite-protein interaction prediction in the SARTRE framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a rich metabolite feature table (e.g. precomputed fingerprints) and do not need constraint-based shadow-price features. No active GUROBI license is available — the optimization step (`optimization.py`) cannot run without it. The task targets a metabolic model other than the curated GEMs and no curation/irreversibility step has been performed on it.

skills.summary: Simulate and modify a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D) in cobrapy/Python using the M2R add-on, which incorporates gut microbiota metabolism by updating exchange-reaction lower bounds with aggregated microbial in-/out-fluxes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a genome-scale metabolic reconstruction (e.g. you have only a microbiota model and no paired human GEM like RECON3D to modify) You need to modify upper bounds, internal (non-exchange) reactions, or perform other constraint edits outside the exchange-reaction lower-bound update rule that M2R implements Biological plausibility of the modified metabolite pool is the question itself — the article leaves that to expert review; M2R only guarantees the arithmetic of the bound update

skills.description: Use when annotated protein FASTA, BLASTp/DIAMOND output, or a draft SBML model is available for a bacterial genome and a COBRApy-compatible genome-scale metabolic model (SBML GENRE) is needed for FBA, gene essentiality, or flux sampling analyses.
skills.name: genome-scale-metabolic-network-reconstruction
skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-network-reconstruction Use when annotated protein FASTA, BLASTp/DIAMOND output, or a draft SBML model is available for a bacterial genome and a COBRApy-compatible genome-scale metabolic model (SBML GENRE) is needed for FBA, gene essentiality, or flux sampling analyses. Input is raw (unannotated) nucleotide or protein sequence — the tool requires annotated amino acid .fasta, BLASTp hits, or an existing SBML GENRE, not raw assemblies. You need a model with non-ModelSEED reaction/metabolite naming conventions or a hand-curated reconstruction — Reconstructor exports ModelSEED-consistent SBML and is automated, not manual-curation software. The organism is non-bacterial with unknown Gram status and the Gram-classification argument cannot be justified. http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Automated reconstruction of genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) from annotated amino acid .fasta files using the Reconstructor Python package, which applies DIAMOND-based KEGG annotation matching against a ModelSEED-derived universal.pickle reaction database and completes drafts with parsimony-based (pFBA) gap-filling. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Automated reconstruction of genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) from annotated amino acid .fasta files using the Reconstructor Python package, which applies DIAMOND-based KEGG annotation matching against a ModelSEED-derived universal.pickle reaction database and completes drafts with parsimony-based (pFBA) gap-filling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw (unannotated) nucleotide or protein sequence — the tool requires annotated amino acid .fasta, BLASTp hits, or an existing SBML GENRE, not raw assemblies. You need a model with non-ModelSEED reaction/metabolite naming conventions or a hand-curated reconstruction — Reconstructor exports ModelSEED-consistent SBML and is automated, not manual-curation software. The organism is non-bacterial with unknown Gram status and the Gram-classification argument cannot be justified.
