skills.name: genomic-proximity-gene-mapping
skills.search_text: genomic-proximity-gene-mapping Use when you have a set of sentinel variants (e.g. mQTLs or cis-pQTLs with GRCh37 coordinates) and need to prioritize or validate causal gene assignments based on genomic proximity, LD-overlap, or cis-eQTL targeting. The goal is prioritization at trans-QTLs — the article notes the top-down strategy is not applicable to trans-pQTLs and would need a different approach No high-confidence reference causal gene assignments exist for the QTL set, since the proximity/enrichment validation depends on their availability You need functional annotation prioritization only (top-down metabolic scoring), not positional mapping of sentinels to nearest/LD-overlapping genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Maps sentinel molecular QTL variants to their nearest candidate causal genes using ProGeM, then quantifies enrichment of the nearest-gene criterion against high-confidence causal gene assignments via Fisher's exact tests. Genomic proximity is treated as the most reliable indicator of true positive causal genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gky837
skills.summary: Maps sentinel molecular QTL variants to their nearest candidate causal genes using ProGeM, then quantifies enrichment of the nearest-gene criterion against high-confidence causal gene assignments via Fisher's exact tests. Genomic proximity is treated as the most reliable indicator of true positive causal genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is prioritization at trans-QTLs — the article notes the top-down strategy is not applicable to trans-pQTLs and would need a different approach No high-confidence reference causal gene assignments exist for the QTL set, since the proximity/enrichment validation depends on their availability You need functional annotation prioritization only (top-down metabolic scoring), not positional mapping of sentinels to nearest/LD-overlapping genes

skills.description: Use when annotating sentinel (and LD-proxied) variants with positional candidate genes from variant-level data — nearest-gene extraction, LD-range overlap, and biotype filtering around molecular QTL loci.
skills.name: genomic-range-overlap-annotation
skills.search_text: genomic-range-overlap-annotation Use when annotating sentinel (and LD-proxied) variants with positional candidate genes from variant-level data — nearest-gene extraction, LD-range overlap, and biotype filtering around molecular QTL loci. The locus is a trans-QTL: the article notes the top-down positional/annotation strategy 'is not directly applicable to trans-pQTLs and would need a different approach' Only gene-expression evidence (cis-eQTL targets) is wanted and positional proximity is irrelevant — the paper found cis-eQTL data yields ~3 false positives per true positive and is a poor standalone indicator The variant coordinates are not in GRCh37 — the pipeline hard-codes a GRCh37 gene model from Homo_sapiens.GRCh37.82.gtf and would need a lift-over first http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Use GenomicRanges-based interval operations over a GRCh37 gene model (built from Homo_sapiens.GRCh37.82.gtf) to annotate sentinel molecular QTL variants with candidate causal genes: the three nearest protein-coding genes by distance-to-TSS and all genes overlapping the sentinel-proxy LD range. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gky837
skills.summary: Use GenomicRanges-based interval operations over a GRCh37 gene model (built from Homo_sapiens.GRCh37.82.gtf) to annotate sentinel molecular QTL variants with candidate causal genes: the three nearest protein-coding genes by distance-to-TSS and all genes overlapping the sentinel-proxy LD range.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus is a trans-QTL: the article notes the top-down positional/annotation strategy 'is not directly applicable to trans-pQTLs and would need a different approach' Only gene-expression evidence (cis-eQTL targets) is wanted and positional proximity is irrelevant — the paper found cis-eQTL data yields ~3 false positives per true positive and is a poor standalone indicator The variant coordinates are not in GRCh37 — the pipeline hard-codes a GRCh37 gene model from Homo_sapiens.GRCh37.82.gtf and would need a lift-over first

skills.description: Use when you have PoDP project JSON records containing (meta)genome entries with GenBank accession numbers or JGI Genome IDs and need organism names attached per project/genome label for downstream enrichment or filtering.
skills.name: genomic-source-metadata-tabulation
skills.search_text: genomic-source-metadata-tabulation Use when you have PoDP project JSON records containing (meta)genome entries with GenBank accession numbers or JGI Genome IDs and need organism names attached per project/genome label for downstream enrichment or filtering. The genome entries contain only free text entered in 'Other' boxes, which is inherently not machine-readable and has no resolvable public identifier The goal is to link MS/MS spectra URLs or MIBiG identifiers to genomes (BGC–MS/MS linking), not to resolve organism names from identifiers Input is a metabolomics metadata task (MassIVE/MetaboLights accessions, sample preparation or extraction methods) that involves no genomic source identifiers http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs the PoDP project-enrichment step that resolves public genome identifiers (NCBI GenBank accessions or JGI Genome IDs) to official organism names, tabulated per project and user-created genome label. The PoDP web service performs this same enrichment automatically, but agents can reproduce it offline from the Zenodo JSON archive. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00724-z
skills.summary: Reconstructs the PoDP project-enrichment step that resolves public genome identifiers (NCBI GenBank accessions or JGI Genome IDs) to official organism names, tabulated per project and user-created genome label. The PoDP web service performs this same enrichment automatically, but agents can reproduce it offline from the Zenodo JSON archive.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome entries contain only free text entered in 'Other' boxes, which is inherently not machine-readable and has no resolvable public identifier The goal is to link MS/MS spectra URLs or MIBiG identifiers to genomes (BGC–MS/MS linking), not to resolve organism names from identifiers Input is a metabolomics metadata task (MassIVE/MetaboLights accessions, sample preparation or extraction methods) that involves no genomic source identifiers

skills.description: Use when you have a BiG-SLiCE output SQLite database plus genome taxonomy annotations (e.g., GTDB 04-RS89) and need per-taxon BGC class proportions or GCF diversity summaries.
skills.name: genomic-taxonomy-aggregation
skills.search_text: genomic-taxonomy-aggregation Use when you have a BiG-SLiCE output SQLite database plus genome taxonomy annotations (e.g., GTDB 04-RS89) and need per-taxon BGC class proportions or GCF diversity summaries. Input is raw genome FASTA or antiSMASH output not yet clustered — run BiG-SLiCE clustering first to obtain GCF assignments Taxonomy is missing or unreliable for the genomes — GTDB-based joins require valid GTDB assignments; the paper used the GTDB toolkit only when GTDB API lookup failed You need pairwise BGC similarity networks rather than taxon-level aggregation — BiG-SLiCE's Euclidean-space clustering output is not a substitute for BiG-SCAPE-style network analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aggregate BiG-SLiCE clustering results (BGC counts and GCF assignments) per taxonomic group by joining the output SQLite3 database's BGC/class tables with GTDB-derived genome taxonomy tables, enabling global maps of secondary metabolic diversity across taxa. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa154
skills.summary: Aggregate BiG-SLiCE clustering results (BGC counts and GCF assignments) per taxonomic group by joining the output SQLite3 database's BGC/class tables with GTDB-derived genome taxonomy tables, enabling global maps of secondary metabolic diversity across taxa.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw genome FASTA or antiSMASH output not yet clustered — run BiG-SLiCE clustering first to obtain GCF assignments Taxonomy is missing or unreliable for the genomes — GTDB-based joins require valid GTDB assignments; the paper used the GTDB toolkit only when GTDB API lookup failed You need pairwise BGC similarity networks rather than taxon-level aggregation — BiG-SLiCE's Euclidean-space clustering output is not a substitute for BiG-SCAPE-style network analyses

skills.description: Use when a raw ClinVar VCF must be cleaned, normalized, and QC-validated to a fixed variant count and clinical-significance composition before it is used as a benchmark for annotation-tool concordance (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP).
skills.name: genomic-variant-qc-validation
skills.search_text: genomic-variant-qc-validation Use when a raw ClinVar VCF must be cleaned, normalized, and QC-validated to a fixed variant count and clinical-significance composition before it is used as a benchmark for annotation-tool concordance (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP). The input VCF is already left-aligned, deduplicated, and free of degenerate bases — re-applying normalization can shift repeat-region HGVS notation and produce inconsistent annotations. The goal is to annotate novel variants rather than build a fixed high-review-status benchmark set — the strict exclusion of VUS, MT, and indels ≥50 bp would remove variants that are needed. The variant set contains MNVs that have not been phased and normalized — running annotation tools first would yield inconsistent HGVS nomenclature rather than true tool disagreement. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Normalize and filter a ClinVar VCF (left alignment, deduplication, degenerate-base removal, and exclusion of large indels, VUS, mitochondrial, and missing/multi-MC records) and validate the output against the expected 164,549-variant composition (38,278 P / 6,073 LP / 57,081 B / 63,117 LB) before cross-tool annotation comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Normalize and filter a ClinVar VCF (left alignment, deduplication, degenerate-base removal, and exclusion of large indels, VUS, mitochondrial, and missing/multi-MC records) and validate the output against the expected 164,549-variant composition (38,278 P / 6,073 LP / 57,081 B / 63,117 LB) before cross-tool annotation comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input VCF is already left-aligned, deduplicated, and free of degenerate bases — re-applying normalization can shift repeat-region HGVS notation and produce inconsistent annotations. The goal is to annotate novel variants rather than build a fixed high-review-status benchmark set — the strict exclusion of VUS, MT, and indels ≥50 bp would remove variants that are needed. The variant set contains MNVs that have not been phased and normalized — running annotation tools first would yield inconsistent HGVS nomenclature rather than true tool disagreement.

skills.description: Use when pairing genome-mined BGCs (e.g. antiSMASH GCFs from BiG-SCAPE) with GNPS molecular networking MS/MS spectra and you need to prioritise or prune candidate BGC–spectrum links without labelled training data.
skills.name: genomics-metabolomics-link-scoring
skills.search_text: genomics-metabolomics-link-scoring Use when pairing genome-mined BGCs (e.g. antiSMASH GCFs from BiG-SCAPE) with GNPS molecular networking MS/MS spectra and you need to prioritise or prune candidate BGC–spectrum links without labelled training data. The dataset's metabolites are large (>~850 Da) where CANOPUS coverage is limited — Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore-style methods may be better suited You need validated links for compounds without any MS/MS spectrum (as with retimycin and nocardimicin in the Nocardia dataset) MolNetEnhancer classes are required but you cannot run external GNPS jobs, since MolNetEnhancer has to be run outside NPLinker http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Two-stage linking of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) to MS/MS spectra in NPLinker: standardised Metcalf co-occurrence scoring followed by NPClassScore chemical-class matching, which reduces candidate BGC–MS/MS links by on average 63%. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Two-stage linking of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) to MS/MS spectra in NPLinker: standardised Metcalf co-occurrence scoring followed by NPClassScore chemical-class matching, which reduces candidate BGC–MS/MS links by on average 63%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset's metabolites are large (>~850 Da) where CANOPUS coverage is limited — Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore-style methods may be better suited You need validated links for compounds without any MS/MS spectrum (as with retimycin and nocardimicin in the Nocardia dataset) MolNetEnhancer classes are required but you cannot run external GNPS jobs, since MolNetEnhancer has to be run outside NPLinker

skills.description: Use when paired microbial genomics (AntiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE GCFs) and metabolomics (GNPS molecular networking MFs) data must be linked and scored per strain co-occurrence, especially when raw scores must be compared across GCFs/MFs of different sizes.
skills.name: genomics-metabolomics-linkage-analysis
skills.search_text: genomics-metabolomics-linkage-analysis Use when paired microbial genomics (AntiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE GCFs) and metabolomics (GNPS molecular networking MFs) data must be linked and scored per strain co-occurrence, especially when raw scores must be compared across GCFs/MFs of different sizes. When no strain_mappings.json exists — NPLinker cannot build strain co-occurrence vectors without mapping strains to genomics and metabolomics data When ranking links with the Input-Output Kernel Regression (IOKR) score rather than the standardised strain correlation score When the genomics or metabolomics side is not in NPLinker's expected input format (GNPS molecular networking data + AntiSMASH BGCs) http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes and validates strain-correlation (Metcalf) links between gene cluster families (GCFs) and molecular families (MFs) using NPLinker, standardising raw scores against a hypergeometric null so that links are comparable across GCF and MF sizes. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Computes and validates strain-correlation (Metcalf) links between gene cluster families (GCFs) and molecular families (MFs) using NPLinker, standardising raw scores against a hypergeometric null so that links are comparable across GCF and MF sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no strain_mappings.json exists — NPLinker cannot build strain co-occurrence vectors without mapping strains to genomics and metabolomics data When ranking links with the Input-Output Kernel Regression (IOKR) score rather than the standardised strain correlation score When the genomics or metabolomics side is not in NPLinker's expected input format (GNPS molecular networking data + AntiSMASH BGCs)

skills.description: Use when two per-gene prioritization score vectors (e.g., Exomiser phenotype scores and metPropagate LPA-propagated scores) exist for the same candidate gene lists and a combined ranking should down-weight the metabolomics score for highly connected metabolic genes.
skills.name: genomics-metabolomics-score-integration
skills.search_text: genomics-metabolomics-score-integration Use when two per-gene prioritization score vectors (e.g., Exomiser phenotype scores and metPropagate LPA-propagated scores) exist for the same candidate gene lists and a combined ranking should down-weight the metabolomics score for highly connected metabolic genes. Only one score source is available (e.g., no Exomiser phenotype ranking or no LPA output) — the weighted combination requires both score vectors per patient. The network is not STRING (v11) or gene-metabolite annotations are not from HMDB — the p weights are calibrated from HMDB-annotated first-degree STRING neighbor fractions across 19,354 genes and will not transfer. Candidate gene lists are trio-WES-derived and much shorter than the 281–609 gene singleton-exome lists — top-20th-percentile thresholds (rank <= 60) were calibrated on the singleton lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combines Exomiser phenotype-based rankings with metPropagate network-propagated metabolomic scores via a weighted additive model whose weights penalize metPropagate's bias toward genes with many HMDB-annotated first-degree STRING neighbors, improving causative gene prioritization in TIDEX patients. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Combines Exomiser phenotype-based rankings with metPropagate network-propagated metabolomic scores via a weighted additive model whose weights penalize metPropagate's bias toward genes with many HMDB-annotated first-degree STRING neighbors, improving causative gene prioritization in TIDEX patients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one score source is available (e.g., no Exomiser phenotype ranking or no LPA output) — the weighted combination requires both score vectors per patient. The network is not STRING (v11) or gene-metabolite annotations are not from HMDB — the p weights are calibrated from HMDB-annotated first-degree STRING neighbor fractions across 19,354 genes and will not transfer. Candidate gene lists are trio-WES-derived and much shorter than the 281–609 gene singleton-exome lists — top-20th-percentile thresholds (rank <= 60) were calibrated on the singleton lists.

skills.description: Use when expanding a DNA adductomics database beyond literature-reported adducts with suspected adducts from all chemically plausible genotoxicant–nucleobase combinations, needing charged monoisotopic masses [M+H]+/[M]+ and [M+H-dR]+/[M-dR]+, structures, and SMILES/InChI identifiers.
skills.name: genotoxicant-nucleobase-combination-enumeration

When the task is to curate only literature-reported adducts (the harmonization step of the paper), not to expand the database with suspected combinations When computing in silico MS/MS fragments or building a spectral library — use the separate spectral-library step with CFM-ID instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Enumerate chemically plausible theoretical genotoxicant–nucleobase combinations and convert each to a charged monoisotopic-mass adduct record, expanding a curated DNA adduct database (279 literature entries → 582 entries with 303 suspected adducts). metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Enumerate chemically plausible theoretical genotoxicant–nucleobase combinations and convert each to a charged monoisotopic-mass adduct record, expanding a curated DNA adduct database (279 literature entries → 582 entries with 303 suspected adducts).

skills.description: Decision support for tabulating a curated DNA adduct database by genotoxicant and source categories to confirm class coverage or database scope.
skills.name: genotoxicant-source-class-grouping
skills.search_text: genotoxicant-source-class-grouping Decision support for tabulating a curated DNA adduct database by genotoxicant and source categories to confirm class coverage or database scope. The goal is spectral annotation of unknown adduct peaks in raw LC-HRMS/MS runs rather than validating database metadata structure — use spectral matching or in silico fragmentation (e.g. CFM-ID) instead. The input is a raw MS/MS peak list without per-adduct genotoxicant or source annotations, so class assignment cannot be performed without first resolving adduct identities. Only the experimental MS/MS spectra of the 15 reference standards are available, not the full 582-entry database, and the task is fragment prediction rather than class tabulation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Groups DNA adduct database entries by causative genotoxicant class (16 classes reported) and source class (nine classes reported), enabling the metadata structure of the 582-entry adductome database to be validated against the paper's reported classification counts. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Groups DNA adduct database entries by causative genotoxicant class (16 classes reported) and source class (nine classes reported), enabling the metadata structure of the 582-entry adductome database to be validated against the paper's reported classification counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spectral annotation of unknown adduct peaks in raw LC-HRMS/MS runs rather than validating database metadata structure — use spectral matching or in silico fragmentation (e.g. CFM-ID) instead. The input is a raw MS/MS peak list without per-adduct genotoxicant or source annotations, so class assignment cannot be performed without first resolving adduct identities. Only the experimental MS/MS spectra of the 15 reference standards are available, not the full 582-entry database, and the task is fragment prediction rather than class tabulation.

skills.description: Use when you have a multi-tissue untargeted metabolomics feature table with metadata for two distinct genetic disease models (e.g. 3xTg and 5xFAD) and need to compare how well each model's genotype classes separate using supervised PLS-DA classification.
skills.name: genotype-stratified-cross-validation
skills.search_text: genotype-stratified-cross-validation Use when you have a multi-tissue untargeted metabolomics feature table with metadata for two distinct genetic disease models (e.g. 3xTg and 5xFAD) and need to compare how well each model's genotype classes separate using supervised PLS-DA classification. When the dataset contains only one genotype contrast or a single genetic model — the CER comparison between 3xTg and 5xFAD is the core deliverable When the feature table has not been RCLR-transformed per tissue — applying PLS-DA on raw peak areas introduces compositional bias When the goal is unsupervised exploration of genotype-dysregulated molecular classes — use PCA-based quality control and cross-tissue molecular networking instead of PLS-DA classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Fit and cross-validate PLS-DA models separately for each genotype contrast in a multi-tissue untargeted metabolomics dataset, comparing classification error rates (CER) between 3xTg and 5xFAD mouse models to identify which model and tissue yield the most discriminative genotype signatures. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Fit and cross-validate PLS-DA models separately for each genotype contrast in a multi-tissue untargeted metabolomics dataset, comparing classification error rates (CER) between 3xTg and 5xFAD mouse models to identify which model and tissue yield the most discriminative genotype signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset contains only one genotype contrast or a single genetic model — the CER comparison between 3xTg and 5xFAD is the core deliverable When the feature table has not been RCLR-transformed per tissue — applying PLS-DA on raw peak areas introduces compositional bias When the goal is unsupervised exploration of genotype-dysregulated molecular classes — use PCA-based quality control and cross-tissue molecular networking instead of PLS-DA classification

skills.description: Use when you need to learn sub-cluster motifs from tokenised BGCs — each BGC represented as a bag of (sub)Pfam domain combinations — via LDA topic modelling, e.g. to mine antiSMASH-DB scale data for biosynthetic sub-clusters.
skills.name: gensim-online-variational-bayes-training
skills.search_text: gensim-online-variational-bayes-training Use when you need to learn sub-cluster motifs from tokenised BGCs — each BGC represented as a bag of (sub)Pfam domain combinations — via LDA topic modelling, e.g. to mine antiSMASH-DB scale data for biosynthetic sub-clusters. When gene order within BGCs is biologically important — the LDA bag-of-words model discards it; the complementary PRESTO-STAT statistical method preserves original gene order When input BGCs have not been tokenised into (sub)Pfam domain combinations — raw GenBank/antiSMASH output must first be converted to bag-of-words vectors When sub-clusters of length one are of interest — these are almost definitely noise and are not counted Trains a topic model (PRESTO-TOP) over bag-of-words (sub)Pfam domain-combination vectors of BGCs using Gensim's multicore LDA with online variational Bayes, learning 1,000 sub-cluster motifs that encode recurring biosynthetic gene combinations independent of gene order. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Trains a topic model (PRESTO-TOP) over bag-of-words (sub)Pfam domain-combination vectors of BGCs using Gensim's multicore LDA with online variational Bayes, learning 1,000 sub-cluster motifs that encode recurring biosynthetic gene combinations independent of gene order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene order within BGCs is biologically important — the LDA bag-of-words model discards it; the complementary PRESTO-STAT statistical method preserves original gene order When input BGCs have not been tokenised into (sub)Pfam domain combinations — raw GenBank/antiSMASH output must first be converted to bag-of-words vectors When sub-clusters of length one are of interest — these are almost definitely noise and are not counted

skills.description: Use when reconstructing the Word2vec spectral embedding of FastEI: you have a corpus of predicted EI mass spectra formatted as peak-token sentences and need a 500-dim embedding model matching Supplementary Table 1.
skills.name: gensim-word2vec-hyperparameter-configuration
skills.search_text: gensim-word2vec-hyperparameter-configuration Use when reconstructing the Word2vec spectral embedding of FastEI: you have a corpus of predicted EI mass spectra formatted as peak-token sentences and need a 500-dim embedding model matching Supplementary Table 1. You only need to query the pre-built FastEI library — the installation package already ships the Word2vec model and HNSW index, so no retraining is required Your goal is predicting spectra from molecular structures (ECFP inputs) — that is the NEIMS model, not Word2vec spectral embedding You need exact nearest-neighbor similarity over raw spectra (e.g., weighted cosine similarity via faiss.IndexFlatL2) rather than learned embedding-based approximate matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Reconstructs the FastEI spectral embedding model by training a gensim Word2vec model (CBOW) on the paper's spectral 'sentences' of peak tokens with the published hyperparameters: window 1000, dimension 500, negative sampling 5, lr 0.025 with linear decay 0.00025, 60 epochs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Reconstructs the FastEI spectral embedding model by training a gensim Word2vec model (CBOW) on the paper's spectral 'sentences' of peak tokens with the published hyperparameters: window 1000, dimension 500, negative sampling 5, lr 0.025 with linear decay 0.00025, 60 epochs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to query the pre-built FastEI library — the installation package already ships the Word2vec model and HNSW index, so no retraining is required Your goal is predicting spectra from molecular structures (ECFP inputs) — that is the NEIMS model, not Word2vec spectral embedding You need exact nearest-neighbor similarity over raw spectra (e.g., weighted cosine similarity via faiss.IndexFlatL2) rather than learned embedding-based approximate matching

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-trained Spec2Vec Word2Vec model (e.g. Zenodo 4173596, AllPositive) and processed peak/loss-word documents, and need spectrum-level vectors or pairwise spectral similarity scores.
skills.name: gensim-word2vec-model-inference
skills.search_text: gensim-word2vec-model-inference Use when you have a pre-trained Spec2Vec Word2Vec model (e.g. Zenodo 4173596, AllPositive) and processed peak/loss-word documents, and need spectrum-level vectors or pairwise spectral similarity scores. Query spectra far outside the training vocabulary — missing fraction exceeds the ~0.05 threshold, so returned scores are unreliable; retrain or skip. No training data are available for your compound class; Spec2Vec requires training data unlike plain cosine scores, so use cosine/modified cosine instead. Data are GC-MS spectra — the approach was only demonstrated on LC-MS data and GC-MS utility was not assessed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Convert processed MS/MS spectra into fixed-length embeddings by summing intensity-weighted gensim Word2Vec word vectors for their peak and neutral-loss tokens, then compare spectra via cosine of the embeddings (the Spec2Vec inference stage). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Convert processed MS/MS spectra into fixed-length embeddings by summing intensity-weighted gensim Word2Vec word vectors for their peak and neutral-loss tokens, then compare spectra via cosine of the embeddings (the Spec2Vec inference stage).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query spectra far outside the training vocabulary — missing fraction exceeds the ~0.05 threshold, so returned scores are unreliable; retrain or skip. No training data are available for your compound class; Spec2Vec requires training data unlike plain cosine scores, so use cosine/modified cosine instead. Data are GC-MS spectra — the approach was only demonstrated on LC-MS data and GC-MS utility was not assessed.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics peak intensity matrix contains samples grouped by taxonomic/genus-level factors (e.g. Rhamnus vs Ziziphus) and you want to rank Mass2Motif or Molecular Family metabolite sets by differential activity between those groups.
skills.name: genus-level-motif-activity-comparison
skills.search_text: genus-level-motif-activity-comparison Use when a metabolomics peak intensity matrix contains samples grouped by taxonomic/genus-level factors (e.g. Rhamnus vs Ziziphus) and you want to rank Mass2Motif or Molecular Family metabolite sets by differential activity between those groups. Peak features carry no annotations and cannot be grouped into Molecular Families or Mass2Motifs — unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis The analysis goal requires pathway-level queries against KEGG/Reactome/ChEBI rather than user-defined fragmentation-based metabolite sets Input is already a ranked activity table rather than a raw peak intensity matrix needing imputation, log-2 transformation and standardisation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies PALS PLAGE decomposition to user-defined metabolite sets (GNPS Molecular Families and MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) on a peak intensity matrix with genus-level sample factors (e.g. Rhamnus vs Ziziphus), to rank motifs by activity level and p-value and identify which genus overrepresents chemically annotated motif features. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Applies PALS PLAGE decomposition to user-defined metabolite sets (GNPS Molecular Families and MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) on a peak intensity matrix with genus-level sample factors (e.g. Rhamnus vs Ziziphus), to rank motifs by activity level and p-value and identify which genus overrepresents chemically annotated motif features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peak features carry no annotations and cannot be grouped into Molecular Families or Mass2Motifs — unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis The analysis goal requires pathway-level queries against KEGG/Reactome/ChEBI rather than user-defined fragmentation-based metabolite sets Input is already a ranked activity table rather than a raw peak intensity matrix needing imputation, log-2 transformation and standardisation

skills.description: Use when starting a reproducibility analysis of RNA-seq replicate experiments and the raw multi-lab SEQC data must be retrieved from GEO and converted into per-experiment transcript count vectors/rank lists before computing the maximum rank statistic.
skills.name: geo-dataset-acquisition-and-count-matrix-preparation
skills.search_text: geo-dataset-acquisition-and-count-matrix-preparation Use when starting a reproducibility analysis of RNA-seq replicate experiments and the raw multi-lab SEQC data must be retrieved from GEO and converted into per-experiment transcript count vectors/rank lists before computing the maximum rank statistic. The count matrix and the six SEQC comparisons are already prepared and the task is MaRR estimation itself (k-hat, mFDR-hat, pi1-hat), not data acquisition The experiment has no replicate structure or the data are not transcript-level read counts from RNA-seq, since the comparison formation (biological replicate pairs, per-lab count sums) is specific to the SEQC design The analysis requires a model-based copula mixture estimate; this skill only stages data for the nonparametric rank-based MaRR procedure http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Acquires the SEQC/MAQC-III Universal Human Reference RNA-seq dataset (GEO accession GSE47774) and prepares the ranked count-matrix inputs — 43,919 transcripts across within-lab biological replicate pairs (Mayo Clinic, Penn State, NYU Medical Center) and three between-lab same-platform comparisons — required by the MaRR reproducibility analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1080/01621459.2017.1397521
skills.summary: Acquires the SEQC/MAQC-III Universal Human Reference RNA-seq dataset (GEO accession GSE47774) and prepares the ranked count-matrix inputs — 43,919 transcripts across within-lab biological replicate pairs (Mayo Clinic, Penn State, NYU Medical Center) and three between-lab same-platform comparisons — required by the MaRR reproducibility analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix and the six SEQC comparisons are already prepared and the task is MaRR estimation itself (k-hat, mFDR-hat, pi1-hat), not data acquisition The experiment has no replicate structure or the data are not transcript-level read counts from RNA-seq, since the comparison formation (biological replicate pairs, per-lab count sums) is specific to the SEQC design The analysis requires a model-based copula mixture estimate; this skill only stages data for the nonparametric rank-based MaRR procedure

skills.description: Use when a natural product dataset carries organism geographic-location provenance and the goal is to identify which continents dominate (or are absent/sparse among) provenance records and how NPs are shared across continents.
skills.name: geographic-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: geographic-distribution-analysis Use when a natural product dataset carries organism geographic-location provenance and the goal is to identify which continents dominate (or are absent/sparse among) provenance records and how NPs are shared across continents. The task is chemical-structure QC or curation (e.g. 5–210 heavy atom size checks, polyfluorinated compound removal, duplicate merging) — use the COCONUT curation/filter pipeline instead. The input records lack organism geographic-location annotations entirely (COCONUT itself notes locations in pivot tables were 'nullified ... for now', so provenance analysis is only meaningful for the subset with known locations). The goal is molecular descriptor, fingerprint, or substructure/similarity search rather than provenance aggregation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Aggregates natural product provenance records (molecule-organism-location) by continent of organism isolation and computes continent-level overlap of shared NPs, reproducing the Fig. 4 analysis of COCONUT that reveals Asia's dominance and Africa's strong representation among geographically annotated NPs. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00478-9
skills.summary: Aggregates natural product provenance records (molecule-organism-location) by continent of organism isolation and computes continent-level overlap of shared NPs, reproducing the Fig. 4 analysis of COCONUT that reveals Asia's dominance and Africa's strong representation among geographically annotated NPs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is chemical-structure QC or curation (e.g. 5–210 heavy atom size checks, polyfluorinated compound removal, duplicate merging) — use the COCONUT curation/filter pipeline instead. The input records lack organism geographic-location annotations entirely (COCONUT itself notes locations in pivot tables were 'nullified ... for now', so provenance analysis is only meaningful for the subset with known locations). The goal is molecular descriptor, fingerprint, or substructure/similarity search rather than provenance aggregation.

skills.description: Use when auditing annotation coverage of a natural-products database that stores molecules, organism taxa, and geographic locations in MongoDB, and you need the fraction of NPs with known continent-level provenance.
skills.name: geographic-origin-coverage-computation
skills.search_text: geographic-origin-coverage-computation Use when auditing annotation coverage of a natural-products database that stores molecules, organism taxa, and geographic locations in MongoDB, and you need the fraction of NPs with known continent-level provenance. When the goal is structural or chemical annotation coverage (e.g. molecular-property descriptors, Murcko frameworks) rather than provenance (organism taxa, geography, references). When the dataset already provides an explicit per-molecule coverage annotation, e.g. COCONUT's own 5-star annotation-level score, which is computed upstream by the annotation-level pipeline rather than from pivot tables. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Computes the proportion of natural-product entries in a COCONUT-style MongoDB database whose organism's geographic location is annotated, yielding coverage fractions for continent-level origin data against the total number of catalogued molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00478-9
skills.summary: Computes the proportion of natural-product entries in a COCONUT-style MongoDB database whose organism's geographic location is annotated, yielding coverage fractions for continent-level origin data against the total number of catalogued molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is structural or chemical annotation coverage (e.g. molecular-property descriptors, Murcko frameworks) rather than provenance (organism taxa, geography, references). When the dataset already provides an explicit per-molecule coverage annotation, e.g. COCONUT's own 5-star annotation-level score, which is computed upstream by the annotation-level pipeline rather than from pivot tables.

skills.description: Use when an upstream geoRge PuInc_seeker + basepeak_finder result object and an XCMSSet (e.g., MetaboLights MTBLS213) are already available and labeled-vs-unlabeled intensity fold changes must be computed per condition.
skills.name: george-label-comparison-execution
skills.search_text: george-label-comparison-execution Use when an upstream geoRge PuInc_seeker + basepeak_finder result object and an XCMSSet (e.g., MetaboLights MTBLS213) are already available and labeled-vs-unlabeled intensity fold changes must be computed per condition. Upstream PuInc_seeker/basepeak_finder steps have not yet been run — label_compare expects the PuIncR result object, not raw mzXML files The task is isotope annotation against a metabolite database rather than relative quantification — use geoRge's database_query with adducts and the reference CSV instead Only unlabeled samples exist (no labeled condition to compare), so no labeled-vs-control fold change can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Executes geoRge's label_compare step, which compares XCMS-detected feature intensities between an unlabeled control condition and each isotopically labeled condition (e.g., normal vs. high glucose 13C-labeled samples) to yield relative-quantification fold changes for labeled features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: Executes geoRge's label_compare step, which compares XCMS-detected feature intensities between an unlabeled control condition and each isotopically labeled condition (e.g., normal vs. high glucose 13C-labeled samples) to yield relative-quantification fold changes for labeled features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Upstream PuInc_seeker/basepeak_finder steps have not yet been run — label_compare expects the PuIncR result object, not raw mzXML files The task is isotope annotation against a metabolite database rather than relative quantification — use geoRge's database_query with adducts and the reference CSV instead Only unlabeled samples exist (no labeled condition to compare), so no labeled-vs-control fold change can be computed

skills.description: Use when quantifying meiotic recombination foci per nucleus in C. elegans gonads and nuclei must be binned into zone 2 (early), 3 (mid), or 4 (late) pachynema before computing per-genotype mean and SD, e.g. for TOP-3::HA, GFP::RMH-1 or GFP::MSH-5 foci.
skills.name: germline-zone-annotation
skills.search_text: germline-zone-annotation Use when quantifying meiotic recombination foci per nucleus in C. elegans gonads and nuclei must be binned into zone 2 (early), 3 (mid), or 4 (late) pachynema before computing per-genotype mean and SD, e.g. for TOP-3::HA, GFP::RMH-1 or GFP::MSH-5 foci. The data are whole-gonad or whole-animal counts not stratified by meiotic zone, so per-zone binning is meaningless The nuclei come from mitotic or premeiotic tip regions (outside pachynema zones 2–4) or from a non-C. elegans germline whose zonal anatomy differs The question concerns crossover (CO) counts along chromosomes rather than per-nucleus recombination-focus counts, which the article analyzed separately Assigns C. elegans germline nuclei to discrete meiotic zones — zone 2 (early pachynema), zone 3 (mid pachynema), zone 4 (late pachynema) — so that recombination-foci counts per nucleus (TOP-3::HA, GFP::RMH-1, GFP::MSH-5) can be reported as genotype-zone mean ± SD tables compatible with the BTR-complex study's Figures 3–6. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac408
skills.summary: Assigns C. elegans germline nuclei to discrete meiotic zones — zone 2 (early pachynema), zone 3 (mid pachynema), zone 4 (late pachynema) — so that recombination-foci counts per nucleus (TOP-3::HA, GFP::RMH-1, GFP::MSH-5) can be reported as genotype-zone mean ± SD tables compatible with the BTR-complex study's Figures 3–6.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are whole-gonad or whole-animal counts not stratified by meiotic zone, so per-zone binning is meaningless The nuclei come from mitotic or premeiotic tip regions (outside pachynema zones 2–4) or from a non-C. elegans germline whose zonal anatomy differs The question concerns crossover (CO) counts along chromosomes rather than per-nucleus recombination-focus counts, which the article analyzed separately

skills.description: Use when ranking metabolite sets by activity-level significance after SVD decomposition, and an empirically calibrated p-value is needed for the extreme t-statistics produced by a permutation test.
skills.name: gev-extreme-value-pvalue-calibration
skills.search_text: gev-extreme-value-pvalue-calibration Use when ranking metabolite sets by activity-level significance after SVD decomposition, and an empirically calibrated p-value is needed for the extreme t-statistics produced by a permutation test. The ranking method is ORA or GSEA rather than mPLAGE/PLAGE — the GEV calibration of extreme permuted t-statistics is specific to the mPLAGE workflow Peak features lack compound annotations (KEGG or ChEBI IDs) — unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis, so SVD and the resulting p-value would be unreliable A permutation null cannot be generated (e.g. insufficient samples to shuffle group labels for the case/control comparison) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3321 In mPLAGE (PALS implementation of PLAGE), p-values for metabolite sets are calibrated by fitting a generalised extreme value (GEV) distribution, with parameters estimated by maximum likelihood, to the extreme t-statistics generated under a sample-label permutation null. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: In mPLAGE (PALS implementation of PLAGE), p-values for metabolite sets are calibrated by fitting a generalised extreme value (GEV) distribution, with parameters estimated by maximum likelihood, to the extreme t-statistics generated under a sample-label permutation null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ranking method is ORA or GSEA rather than mPLAGE/PLAGE — the GEV calibration of extreme permuted t-statistics is specific to the mPLAGE workflow Peak features lack compound annotations (KEGG or ChEBI IDs) — unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis, so SVD and the resulting p-value would be unreliable A permutation null cannot be generated (e.g. insufficient samples to shuffle group labels for the case/control comparison)

skills.description: Use when you have run calibration-curve-based quantification (e.g. get_targeted_elaboration on intensity and nominal-concentration tables) and need per-molecule calibration curve plots for inspection or reporting.
skills.name: ggplot-visualization-of-calibration-curves
skills.search_text: ggplot-visualization-of-calibration-curves Use when you have run calibration-curve-based quantification (e.g. get_targeted_elaboration on intensity and nominal-concentration tables) and need per-molecule calibration curve plots for inspection or reporting. Data comes from an untargeted study (feature tables from patRoon or MS-DIAL) rather than targeted calibration-curve quantification No get_targeted_elaboration results exist — plotting without fitted regression models has no curve to render http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Renders per-molecule calibration-curve plots from GetFeatistics targeted-analysis elaboration results using the plot_calibration_curves function, with outputs fully customisable via the ggplot grammar. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Renders per-molecule calibration-curve plots from GetFeatistics targeted-analysis elaboration results using the plot_calibration_curves function, with outputs fully customisable via the ggplot grammar.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data comes from an untargeted study (feature tables from patRoon or MS-DIAL) rather than targeted calibration-curve quantification No get_targeted_elaboration results exist — plotting without fitted regression models has no curve to render

skills.description: Use when adding a new plotting method to a Shiny dashboard where users supply tabular omics data (csv, txt, xls, xlsx) and the goal is publication-ready default figures with minimal tuning.
skills.name: ggplot2-plot-wrapper-implementation
skills.search_text: ggplot2-plot-wrapper-implementation Use when adding a new plotting method to a Shiny dashboard where users supply tabular omics data (csv, txt, xls, xlsx) and the goal is publication-ready default figures with minimal tuning. The task requires data preprocessing or computing rather than visualization — GraphBio specifically focuses on facilitating the generation of publication-ready plots instead of preprocessing The user has no tabular input prepared from a reference example file and expects the module to fetch or transform raw omics data itself Non-figure outputs (e.g. statistical tables, model objects) are the primary deliverable rather than a plot http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Implement a new visualization module by wrapping ggplot2 (R 4.0.3) with publication-ready defaults and integrating it as a module in a bs4Dash-based Shiny dashboard, following GraphBio's input/output contract. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fgene.2022.957317
skills.summary: Implement a new visualization module by wrapping ggplot2 (R 4.0.3) with publication-ready defaults and integrating it as a module in a bs4Dash-based Shiny dashboard, following GraphBio's input/output contract.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires data preprocessing or computing rather than visualization — GraphBio specifically focuses on facilitating the generation of publication-ready plots instead of preprocessing The user has no tabular input prepared from a reference example file and expects the module to fetch or transform raw omics data itself Non-figure outputs (e.g. statistical tables, model objects) are the primary deliverable rather than a plot

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC/MS or GC/MS metabolomics matrix contains left-censored missing values attributed to detection limits and requires MNAR-aware imputation before downstream univariate or multivariate analysis.
skills.name: gibbs-sampler-implementation
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampler-implementation Use when a targeted LC/MS or GC/MS metabolomics matrix contains left-censored missing values attributed to detection limits and requires MNAR-aware imputation before downstream univariate or multivariate analysis. When the majority of missing values are MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored MNAR from LOD/LOQ — the default lo=-Inf, hi='min' truncation would impose an unjustified ceiling; use uninformative bounds (+∞/-∞) only if extending GSimp to MCAR/MAR is intentional When missing retrieval from raw spectral data is possible — the authors state 'missing retrieval from raw spectral data will be most recommended' over imputation When the data are not log-transformable (already normalized or contain zeros) without violating the pre-processing assumptions (log-transform → QRILC init → scale → impute → recover → exponentiate) http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implements GSimp, an iterative Gibbs sampler that imputes left-censored (MNAR, LOD/LOQ-driven) missing values in targeted metabolomics data by embedding an elastic net prediction model within truncated-normal resampling. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Implements GSimp, an iterative Gibbs sampler that imputes left-censored (MNAR, LOD/LOQ-driven) missing values in targeted metabolomics data by embedding an elastic net prediction model within truncated-normal resampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the majority of missing values are MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored MNAR from LOD/LOQ — the default lo=-Inf, hi='min' truncation would impose an unjustified ceiling; use uninformative bounds (+∞/-∞) only if extending GSimp to MCAR/MAR is intentional When missing retrieval from raw spectral data is possible — the authors state 'missing retrieval from raw spectral data will be most recommended' over imputation When the data are not log-transformable (already normalized or contain zeros) without violating the pre-processing assumptions (log-transform → QRILC init → scale → impute → recover → exponentiate)

skills.description: Use when a targeted metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g. FFA/BA LC-MS data) contains left-censored missing values attributed to LOD/LOQ (MNAR) and an iterative Gibbs sampler must be configured — iteration counts, initialization method, and upper/lower truncation bounds — before running GS_impute.
skills.name: gibbs-sampler-imputation-parameterization
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampler-imputation-parameterization Use when a targeted metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g. FFA/BA LC-MS data) contains left-censored missing values attributed to LOD/LOQ (MNAR) and an iterative Gibbs sampler must be configured — iteration counts, initialization method, and upper/lower truncation bounds — before running GS_impute. Data are GC-MS untargeted profiles where missingness is MCAR/MAR (e.g. before manual missing retrieval) — set non-informative ±∞ bounds rather than the left-censored defaults, or the sampler will force imputed values below the observed minimum. A non-MetaboAnalyst pipeline (kNN, SVD, PPCA, BPCA, RF) is already chosen and the goal is not left-censored MNAR imputation — the parameterization here is specific to GSimp's Gibbs sampler. The matrix is not log-transformed normal data — running the sampler on raw non-normal intensities without the pre-processing wrapper distorts the truncated-normal assumptions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Parameterization and invocation of the GSimp iterative Gibbs sampler for left-censored (MNAR) missing values in targeted metabolomics matrices: log-transform, QRILC initialization, scale, impute with lo=-Inf / hi='min' truncation bounds, then recover scale and exponentiate. It encodes the iteration counts, initialization options, and truncation-point choices that the article tested on FFA, BA, and simulated diabetes data (160 x 76). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Parameterization and invocation of the GSimp iterative Gibbs sampler for left-censored (MNAR) missing values in targeted metabolomics matrices: log-transform, QRILC initialization, scale, impute with lo=-Inf / hi='min' truncation bounds, then recover scale and exponentiate. It encodes the iteration counts, initialization options, and truncation-point choices that the article tested on FFA, BA, and simulated diabetes data (160 x 76).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are GC-MS untargeted profiles where missingness is MCAR/MAR (e.g. before manual missing retrieval) — set non-informative ±∞ bounds rather than the left-censored defaults, or the sampler will force imputed values below the observed minimum. A non-MetaboAnalyst pipeline (kNN, SVD, PPCA, BPCA, RF) is already chosen and the goal is not left-censored MNAR imputation — the parameterization here is specific to GSimp's Gibbs sampler. The matrix is not log-transformed normal data — running the sampler on raw non-normal intensities without the pre-processing wrapper distorts the truncated-normal assumptions.

skills.description: Use when SIRIUS top-ranked molecular formulas are untrusted — e.g. metabolites above 500 Da in a compound network from untargeted LC-MS/MS — and top-50 candidate lists plus adduct assignments are available for network-based reranking.
skills.name: gibbs-sampling-bayesian-inference
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampling-bayesian-inference Use when SIRIUS top-ranked molecular formulas are untrusted — e.g. metabolites above 500 Da in a compound network from untargeted LC-MS/MS — and top-50 candidate lists plus adduct assignments are available for network-based reranking. Datasets where SIRIUS already shows excellent performance and little headroom exists, as on the NIST1950 and tomato datasets A single isolated compound with no network of related compounds — ZODIAC's Bayesian inference relies on the compound similarity network Cases where high-quality adduct annotations have not been established during preprocessing, since ZODIAC depends on them http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 ZODIAC-style Gibbs sampling Bayesian reranking of SIRIUS molecular formula candidates: it takes the top 50 SIRIUS candidates per compound plus a compound-similarity network and, optionally, spectral-library anchors, to correct formula annotations in untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: ZODIAC-style Gibbs sampling Bayesian reranking of SIRIUS molecular formula candidates: it takes the top 50 SIRIUS candidates per compound plus a compound-similarity network and, optionally, spectral-library anchors, to correct formula annotations in untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets where SIRIUS already shows excellent performance and little headroom exists, as on the NIST1950 and tomato datasets A single isolated compound with no network of related compounds — ZODIAC's Bayesian inference relies on the compound similarity network Cases where high-quality adduct annotations have not been established during preprocessing, since ZODIAC depends on them

skills.description: Use when a mean- and stddev-normalized feature-by-sample concentration table (e.g., NMR metabolomics across developmental stages) needs a sparse network of conditional dependencies, with transition-specific subnetworks extracted per cell-type pair.
skills.name: glasso-sparse-covariance-network-inference
skills.search_text: glasso-sparse-covariance-network-inference Use when a mean- and stddev-normalized feature-by-sample concentration table (e.g., NMR metabolomics across developmental stages) needs a sparse network of conditional dependencies, with transition-specific subnetworks extracted per cell-type pair. The input is raw NMR spectra or peak lists rather than a quantified, normalized metabolite-by-sample concentration table — peak identification (Chenomx/TopSpin) must happen first You need transition-specific metabolite attribution via loadings rather than the network structure alone — pair GLASSO with the PCA overlay step (MetaboLINK) instead of running GLASSO in isolation The pairwise (two-cell-type) datasets are the only input and no fixed alpha is defensible — GraphLassoCV cross-validation is unstable on these small subsets, so the full-dataset CV fit is the preferred route http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit the graphical lasso (L1-regularized precision matrix) to a normalized metabolite concentration matrix to build a sparse covariance network of metabolites, retaining both positive and negative partial correlations as edges, as used in the MetaboLINK (PCA-GLASSO) pipeline on 90 NMR-quantified metabolites across five hESC-derived neural cell populations. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fnins.2024.1520982
skills.summary: Fit the graphical lasso (L1-regularized precision matrix) to a normalized metabolite concentration matrix to build a sparse covariance network of metabolites, retaining both positive and negative partial correlations as edges, as used in the MetaboLINK (PCA-GLASSO) pipeline on 90 NMR-quantified metabolites across five hESC-derived neural cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw NMR spectra or peak lists rather than a quantified, normalized metabolite-by-sample concentration table — peak identification (Chenomx/TopSpin) must happen first You need transition-specific metabolite attribution via loadings rather than the network structure alone — pair GLASSO with the PCA overlay step (MetaboLINK) instead of running GLASSO in isolation The pairwise (two-cell-type) datasets are the only input and no fixed alpha is defensible — GraphLassoCV cross-validation is unstable on these small subsets, so the full-dataset CV fit is the preferred route

skills.description: Use when tumor samples carry both a binary molecular subgroup assignment (e.g. AKT1-high/low, MYC-high/low) and a clinical grade/stage label, and the goal is to test independence of the molecular status from the clinical variable.
skills.name: gleason-grade-clinical-annotation-handling
skills.search_text: gleason-grade-clinical-annotation-handling Use when tumor samples carry both a binary molecular subgroup assignment (e.g. AKT1-high/low, MYC-high/low) and a clinical grade/stage label, and the goal is to test independence of the molecular status from the clinical variable. The goal is to test association of AKT1/MYC status with metabolomic cluster membership rather than clinical grade — in that context the Fisher test was significant (p<0.01), not a null result. Grade labels are graded (e.g. continuous Gleason score) rather than the paper's binary high (4+3/4+4) vs low (3+3/3+4) split; a rank or trend test would be needed. The molecular subgroup is not binary — the 4-group k-means assignment requires the 2x4 or collapsed 2x2 formulation before a Fisher test applies. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Statistical test of whether a molecular subtype assignment (here phosphoAKT1/MYC k-means subgroups) is independent of a clinical annotation (Gleason grade, pathologic stage) using Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables with p<0.05 as the non-association criterion. metabolomics/v3 10.1158/0008-5472.can-14-1490
skills.summary: Statistical test of whether a molecular subtype assignment (here phosphoAKT1/MYC k-means subgroups) is independent of a clinical annotation (Gleason grade, pathologic stage) using Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables with p<0.05 as the non-association criterion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to test association of AKT1/MYC status with metabolomic cluster membership rather than clinical grade — in that context the Fisher test was significant (p<0.01), not a null result. Grade labels are graded (e.g. continuous Gleason score) rather than the paper's binary high (4+3/4+4) vs low (3+3/3+4) split; a rank or trend test would be needed. The molecular subgroup is not binary — the 4-group k-means assignment requires the 2x4 or collapsed 2x2 formulation before a Fisher test applies.

skills.description: Use when you have k-medoids clusters of spectrally similar LC-MS/MS features and a two-level treatment contrast, and you need cluster-wise enrichment testing with reduced multiplicity penalties rather than per-feature univariate tests.
skills.name: glm-based-cluster-wise-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: glm-based-cluster-wise-statistical-testing Use when you have k-medoids clusters of spectrally similar LC-MS/MS features and a two-level treatment contrast, and you need cluster-wise enrichment testing with reduced multiplicity penalties rather than per-feature univariate tests. When the goal is per-feature univariate differential abundance testing without any feature-set/cluster grouping When the input features have not been grouped into spectral-similarity clusters (k-medoids clustering must be done first) When the contrast involves more than two treatment levels without a clear pairwise comparison definition http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Self-contained feature-set testing that jointly models structurally similar LC-MS/MS features grouped by k-medoids spectral clustering, using the globaltest GLM-based framework with Bonferroni correction to identify enriched metabolite clusters. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae584
skills.summary: Self-contained feature-set testing that jointly models structurally similar LC-MS/MS features grouped by k-medoids spectral clustering, using the globaltest GLM-based framework with Bonferroni correction to identify enriched metabolite clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is per-feature univariate differential abundance testing without any feature-set/cluster grouping When the input features have not been grouped into spectral-similarity clusters (k-medoids clustering must be done first) When the contrast involves more than two treatment levels without a clear pairwise comparison definition

skills.description: Use when two organisms' metabolic networks have been reconstructed with MetNet (set or multiset representation) and local pathway similarity values are available and must be aggregated into global Psim, PsimW and Csim similarity indexes.
skills.name: global-metabolic-network-similarity-aggregation
skills.search_text: global-metabolic-network-similarity-aggregation Use when two organisms' metabolic networks have been reconstructed with MetNet (set or multiset representation) and local pathway similarity values are available and must be aggregated into global Psim, PsimW and Csim similarity indexes. The metabolic networks have not yet been reconstructed — this skill presupposes MetNet-built networks from KEGG KGML files and the local SimPi/SimSi values Genomic or experimental data are the input rather than KEGG organisms — MetNet currently works only on KEGG data and does not accept genomic data as input Only a single organism's network is available — the indexes are defined for pairwise comparison of two organisms selected in KEGG http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates the local structural similarity indexes SimPi (and SimSi) computed pathway-by-pathway between two KEGG organisms into the global indexes Psim (arithmetic mean), PsimW (weighted mean by |Ri∪Ri′|), and the combined index Csim = Σ SimSi·SimPi/n, yielding a quantitative pairwise metabolism comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Aggregates the local structural similarity indexes SimPi (and SimSi) computed pathway-by-pathway between two KEGG organisms into the global indexes Psim (arithmetic mean), PsimW (weighted mean by |Ri∪Ri′|), and the combined index Csim = Σ SimSi·SimPi/n, yielding a quantitative pairwise metabolism comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolic networks have not yet been reconstructed — this skill presupposes MetNet-built networks from KEGG KGML files and the local SimPi/SimSi values Genomic or experimental data are the input rather than KEGG organisms — MetNet currently works only on KEGG data and does not accept genomic data as input Only a single organism's network is available — the indexes are defined for pairwise comparison of two organisms selected in KEGG

skills.description: Use when computing pairwise similarity between Biosynthetic Gene Clusters where some clusters are complete and others are fragmented (e.g. from metagenomes or pan-genomes), and global-only metrics would penalize length asymmetry.
skills.name: glocal-bgc-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: glocal-bgc-similarity-scoring Use when computing pairwise similarity between Biosynthetic Gene Clusters where some clusters are complete and others are fragmented (e.g. from metagenomes or pan-genomes), and global-only metrics would penalize length asymmetry. Input clusters lack Pfam domain annotations or antiSMASH 'Core Biosynthetic' gene flags — the LCS seed and filter steps depend on ordered domain strings and those annotations The comparison target is raw nucleotide/protein sequence identity rather than domain content, order, copy number and sequence identity, which is what BiG-SCAPE's pairwise distance is based on A single whole-genome similarity summary is needed, not pairwise BGC-BGC distances for network construction or GCF assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstructs BiG-SCAPE's 'glocal' alignment mode, which seeds each pairwise BGC comparison with the longest common substring (LCS) of their ordered Pfam domain strings and then extends the alignment with match/mismatch/gap scores. This lets pairwise distances correctly compare complete BGCs against fragmented (or merged) ones, which purely global or local similarity metrics mishandle. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Reconstructs BiG-SCAPE's 'glocal' alignment mode, which seeds each pairwise BGC comparison with the longest common substring (LCS) of their ordered Pfam domain strings and then extends the alignment with match/mismatch/gap scores. This lets pairwise distances correctly compare complete BGCs against fragmented (or merged) ones, which purely global or local similarity metrics mishandle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input clusters lack Pfam domain annotations or antiSMASH 'Core Biosynthetic' gene flags — the LCS seed and filter steps depend on ordered domain strings and those annotations The comparison target is raw nucleotide/protein sequence identity rather than domain content, order, copy number and sequence identity, which is what BiG-SCAPE's pairwise distance is based on A single whole-genome similarity summary is needed, not pairwise BGC-BGC distances for network construction or GCF assignment

skills.description: Use when a DIMS peak-intensity matrix has been blank/sample filtered, PQN-normalized and KNN-imputed, QC samples exist, and a variance-stabilizing transform is needed before PCA or other multivariate statistics.
skills.name: glog-variance-stabilization-qc-optimization
skills.search_text: glog-variance-stabilization-qc-optimization Use when a DIMS peak-intensity matrix has been blank/sample filtered, PQN-normalized and KNN-imputed, QC samples exist, and a variance-stabilizing transform is needed before PCA or other multivariate statistics. Input is still raw instrument data (e.g. FT-ICR transient .dat files) rather than an aligned peak matrix — use Sum Transients/Process Transients/Mass Calibration and SIM-stitching first No QC samples are present in the dataset, since the G-log parameters are optimized on QC samples alone LC-MS feature tables processed via XCMS are the target; G-log here is documented within the DIMS cleansing workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Applies the Galaxy-M G-log transformation as the final variance-stabilizing step of the DIMS data-cleansing pipeline, optimizing its transformation parameter on QC samples alone rather than on biological samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: Applies the Galaxy-M G-log transformation as the final variance-stabilizing step of the DIMS data-cleansing pipeline, optimizing its transformation parameter on QC samples alone rather than on biological samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw instrument data (e.g. FT-ICR transient .dat files) rather than an aligned peak matrix — use Sum Transients/Process Transients/Mass Calibration and SIM-stitching first No QC samples are present in the dataset, since the G-log parameters are optimized on QC samples alone LC-MS feature tables processed via XCMS are the target; G-log here is documented within the DIMS cleansing workflow

skills.description: Use when processing raw 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma (e.g. 600 MHz Bruker IVDr format from cohorts like MTBLS395) and spectra must be ppm-calibrated to the glucose anomeric proton at 5.233 ppm prior to metabolite bin search.
skills.name: glucose-anomeric-proton-peak-identification
skills.search_text: glucose-anomeric-proton-peak-identification Use when processing raw 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma (e.g. 600 MHz Bruker IVDr format from cohorts like MTBLS395) and spectra must be ppm-calibrated to the glucose anomeric proton at 5.233 ppm prior to metabolite bin search. The spectrum has already been calibrated to 5.233 ppm (applying the routine again would double-shift the data) The input is not a blood-derived 1D 1H NMR profile (e.g. tissue extracts or 2D-Jres data), where the glucose anomeric proton is not the routine reference signal Automatic spectral calibration step of the SMolESY-select algorithm: every 1D 1H NMR spectrum of blood serum/plasma is calibrated to the glucose anomeric proton signal at 5.233 ppm, the routine reference for blood 1H NMR profile analysis, before metabolite assignment proceeds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Automatic spectral calibration step of the SMolESY-select algorithm: every 1D 1H NMR spectrum of blood serum/plasma is calibrated to the glucose anomeric proton signal at 5.233 ppm, the routine reference for blood 1H NMR profile analysis, before metabolite assignment proceeds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum has already been calibrated to 5.233 ppm (applying the routine again would double-shift the data) The input is not a blood-derived 1D 1H NMR profile (e.g. tissue extracts or 2D-Jres data), where the glucose anomeric proton is not the routine reference signal

skills.description: Use when a pseudotargeted metabolomics abundance table (mutant IDs like MT_205/max2 mapped to metabolite columns) needs per-mutant glucosinolate accumulation profiles to validate hub-metabolite associations flagged by module eigenmetabolite screening.
skills.name: glucosinolate-abundance-profiling
skills.search_text: glucosinolate-abundance-profiling Use when a pseudotargeted metabolomics abundance table (mutant IDs like MT_205/max2 mapped to metabolite columns) needs per-mutant glucosinolate accumulation profiles to validate hub-metabolite associations flagged by module eigenmetabolite screening. Input is raw LC-MS vendor data (mzML/Raw) needing peak picking and annotation rather than a processed abundance table — start from the upstream tidyMass-driven data processing module instead The metabolite of interest is not represented in the pseudotargeted panel or the green module hub metabolite set — glucosinolate profiling here depends on glucoraphanin being quantified Mutant identifiers in the metadata do not map unambiguously to abundance columns (e.g. MT_205/max2 naming broken), since eigenmetabolite ranking and genotype-specific profiling both rely on that mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Profiles glucosinolate (e.g. glucoraphanin) abundance across an Arabidopsis mutant panel from a pseudotargeted metabolomics dataset, and cross-checks the metabolite-level pattern against green-module eigenmetabolite rankings from iterative WGCNA to confirm gene–metabolite associations such as the negative MAX2–glucoraphanin link. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Profiles glucosinolate (e.g. glucoraphanin) abundance across an Arabidopsis mutant panel from a pseudotargeted metabolomics dataset, and cross-checks the metabolite-level pattern against green-module eigenmetabolite rankings from iterative WGCNA to confirm gene–metabolite associations such as the negative MAX2–glucoraphanin link.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS vendor data (mzML/Raw) needing peak picking and annotation rather than a processed abundance table — start from the upstream tidyMass-driven data processing module instead The metabolite of interest is not represented in the pseudotargeted panel or the green module hub metabolite set — glucosinolate profiling here depends on glucoraphanin being quantified Mutant identifiers in the metadata do not map unambiguously to abundance columns (e.g. MT_205/max2 naming broken), since eigenmetabolite ranking and genotype-specific profiling both rely on that mapping

skills.description: Use when you need to identify N-linked glycans from Orbitrap LC-MS/MS (mzXML) or permethylated MALDI-TOF peak lists by matching observed masses to a theoretical glycan mass database at a defined ppm tolerance.
skills.name: glycan-accurate-mass-search
skills.search_text: glycan-accurate-mass-search Use when you need to identify N-linked glycans from Orbitrap LC-MS/MS (mzXML) or permethylated MALDI-TOF peak lists by matching observed masses to a theoretical glycan mass database at a defined ppm tolerance. The glycan of interest is not in the database — the app has no de novo glycan identification capability and is limited to glycans already located in the database The analytes are O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans You need to process multiple mzXML files simultaneously — this is a planned future improvement, not implemented Accurate-mass search that matches observed MS1/MS2 peak masses against a glycan theoretical-mass database to identify fluorescently labeled N-linked glycans in Orbitrap LC-MS/MS and permethylated MALDI-TOF data, as implemented in the GlyKAn AZ MATLAB app. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Accurate-mass search that matches observed MS1/MS2 peak masses against a glycan theoretical-mass database to identify fluorescently labeled N-linked glycans in Orbitrap LC-MS/MS and permethylated MALDI-TOF data, as implemented in the GlyKAn AZ MATLAB app.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The glycan of interest is not in the database — the app has no de novo glycan identification capability and is limited to glycans already located in the database The analytes are O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans You need to process multiple mzXML files simultaneously — this is a planned future improvement, not implemented

skills.description: Use when confirming fluorescent-labeled or permethylated N-linked glycan species from LC–MS/MS or MALDI–TOF peak lists by accurate-mass search against a curated glycan mass database with defined ppm and relative-intensity thresholds.
skills.name: glycan-database-matching
skills.search_text: glycan-database-matching Use when confirming fluorescent-labeled or permethylated N-linked glycan species from LC–MS/MS or MALDI–TOF peak lists by accurate-mass search against a curated glycan mass database with defined ppm and relative-intensity thresholds. The glycan of interest is not already in the database — the app has no de novo glycan identification capability and is limited to database entries The sample contains O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans Multiple mzXML files need batch matching in one run — the app cannot process multiple mzXML files simultaneously http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Mass-search based glycan identification in which observed MS1/MS2 peak masses (mzXML from Orbitrap LC–MS/MS or permethylated MALDI–TOF spectra) are matched against glycan databases of theoretical masses (Da) to confirm N-linked glycan species. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Mass-search based glycan identification in which observed MS1/MS2 peak masses (mzXML from Orbitrap LC–MS/MS or permethylated MALDI–TOF spectra) are matched against glycan databases of theoretical masses (Da) to confirm N-linked glycan species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The glycan of interest is not already in the database — the app has no de novo glycan identification capability and is limited to database entries The sample contains O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans Multiple mzXML files need batch matching in one run — the app cannot process multiple mzXML files simultaneously

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS glycan identification method must be validated against a manually confirmed glycan list, requiring true/false positive counts and RT agreement from MS1 peak calling.
skills.name: glycan-identification-benchmark-validation
skills.search_text: glycan-identification-benchmark-validation Use when an LC-MS/MS glycan identification method must be validated against a manually confirmed glycan list, requiring true/false positive counts and RT agreement from MS1 peak calling. The glycans of interest are O-linked or not present in the app's glycan databases — the app's scope is limited to fluorescent-labeled N-linked glycans and has no de novo identification capability. Input is MALDI-TOF data or raw vendor files that have not been converted to mzXML via ProteoWizard, or you need to process multiple mzXML files simultaneously — the app cannot process multiple mzXML files at once. You need customizable isomer peak RT ranges — the isomer peak retention time range is a fixed value, not user-adjustable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark a glycan identification workflow (e.g., GlyKAn AZ) against a manually curated LC-MS/MS glycan list, counting true/false positives and matching retention times. This validates that automated N-linked glycan peak identification reproduces expert analyst results. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Benchmark a glycan identification workflow (e.g., GlyKAn AZ) against a manually curated LC-MS/MS glycan list, counting true/false positives and matching retention times. This validates that automated N-linked glycan peak identification reproduces expert analyst results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The glycans of interest are O-linked or not present in the app's glycan databases — the app's scope is limited to fluorescent-labeled N-linked glycans and has no de novo identification capability.
