Input is MALDI-TOF data or raw vendor files that have not been converted to mzXML via ProteoWizard, or you need to process multiple mzXML files simultaneously — the app cannot process multiple mzXML files at once. You need customizable isomer peak RT ranges — the isomer peak retention time range is a fixed value, not user-adjustable.

skills.description: Use when a new N-linked glycan (e.g. A2G0M4F, A1G1F) must be added to the MS2 Fragment Database and its B/Y/internal fragmentation pattern and theoretical masses must be derived from its structure string.
skills.name: glycan-structure-graph-parsing
skills.search_text: glycan-structure-graph-parsing Use when a new N-linked glycan (e.g. A2G0M4F, A1G1F) must be added to the MS2 Fragment Database and its B/Y/internal fragmentation pattern and theoretical masses must be derived from its structure string. The glycan is already present in the provided MS1/MS2 Fragment Databases — the app's databases already cover it and regeneration is redundant The sample contains O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans The goal is de novo glycan identification from spectra — the app explicitly lacks de novo capability and only identifies glycans in the database Parses a glycan structure string into a MATLAB graph (nodes = monosaccharide residues, edges = glycosidic bonds) and enumerates B-, Y-, and internal-ion fragments via depth-first search by cutting every combination of one to seven bonds, yielding theoretical monoisotopic fragment masses for glycans absent from the GlyKAn AZ databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Parses a glycan structure string into a MATLAB graph (nodes = monosaccharide residues, edges = glycosidic bonds) and enumerates B-, Y-, and internal-ion fragments via depth-first search by cutting every combination of one to seven bonds, yielding theoretical monoisotopic fragment masses for glycans absent from the GlyKAn AZ databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The glycan is already present in the provided MS1/MS2 Fragment Databases — the app's databases already cover it and regeneration is redundant The sample contains O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans The goal is de novo glycan identification from spectra — the app explicitly lacks de novo capability and only identifies glycans in the database

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics workflow has a fixed list of oxPC precursor m/z values (e.g. oxpc_precursor_mz.csv) and needs each mass annotated with an oxidized PC species name, molecular formula, and expert-system annotation label.
skills.name: glycerophosphocholine-species-mapping
skills.search_text: glycerophosphocholine-species-mapping Use when a lipidomics workflow has a fixed list of oxPC precursor m/z values (e.g. oxpc_precursor_mz.csv) and needs each mass annotated with an oxidized PC species name, molecular formula, and expert-system annotation label. The target metabolite class is not oxidized glycerophosphocholines — the dedicated service covers oxPCs, so other lipid classes should go through the general CMM annotation workflow instead The compound of interest is already present in public databases (e.g. HMDB) — the distinguishing value of this skill is the CMM in-house library of oxidized lipids, which CMM 3.0 added because those lipids are absent from other sources MS2 spectral data is available and the goal is spectral comparison or spectrum quality assessment — those are separate CMM 3.0 services, not the oxPC annotation service http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Maps precursor accurate masses of oxidized glycerophosphocholines (oxPCs) to annotated species using the dedicated oxidized-glycerophosphocholine service in CEU Mass Mediator 3.0, restricted to the CMM in-house library of oxidized lipids that is absent from other databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00720
skills.summary: Maps precursor accurate masses of oxidized glycerophosphocholines (oxPCs) to annotated species using the dedicated oxidized-glycerophosphocholine service in CEU Mass Mediator 3.0, restricted to the CMM in-house library of oxidized lipids that is absent from other databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target metabolite class is not oxidized glycerophosphocholines — the dedicated service covers oxPCs, so other lipid classes should go through the general CMM annotation workflow instead The compound of interest is already present in public databases (e.g. HMDB) — the distinguishing value of this skill is the CMM in-house library of oxidized lipids, which CMM 3.0 added because those lipids are absent from other sources MS2 spectral data is available and the goal is spectral comparison or spectrum quality assessment — those are separate CMM 3.0 services, not the oxPC annotation service

skills.description: Use when building an in silico spectral library for lipid classes of any complexity — variable groups may be fatty acyls, other lipid classes (cardiolipin as two PAs), or biopolymers such as peptides or glycans — and MSn fragmentation patterns must be defined per class.
skills.name: glycolipid-lipopeptide-library-entry-definition
skills.search_text: glycolipid-lipopeptide-library-entry-definition Use when building an in silico spectral library for lipid classes of any complexity — variable groups may be fatty acyls, other lipid classes (cardiolipin as two PAs), or biopolymers such as peptides or glycans — and MSn fragmentation patterns must be defined per class. The target lipid class is a simple glycerolipid already covered by a stock spectral library such as LipidBlast or the Lipid Maps database — use existing resources rather than building a novel class entry Input is already a peak table or .cdResult file to be matched against an existing library — use Spectrum Searcher/Peak Finder, not the Library Generator The library design requires more than four variable groups per class, which exceeds the Library Generator's base template structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Defines lipid-class library entries for classes beyond simple glycerolipids — e.g. glycolipids, lipopeptides, FAHFA, ornithine lipids — by building a base template of headgroup, backbone, and up to four variable groups in the LipiDex 2 Library Generator, then encoding MSn tree-based in silico fragmentation for downstream matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Defines lipid-class library entries for classes beyond simple glycerolipids — e.g. glycolipids, lipopeptides, FAHFA, ornithine lipids — by building a base template of headgroup, backbone, and up to four variable groups in the LipiDex 2 Library Generator, then encoding MSn tree-based in silico fragmentation for downstream matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target lipid class is a simple glycerolipid already covered by a stock spectral library such as LipidBlast or the Lipid Maps database — use existing resources rather than building a novel class entry Input is already a peak table or .cdResult file to be matched against an existing library — use Spectrum Searcher/Peak Finder, not the Library Generator The library design requires more than four variable groups per class, which exceeds the Library Generator's base template structure

skills.description: Use when quantified isotopologue peak areas for 13C6-glucose-traced glycolysis metabolites (e.g. G6P, F6P, FBP, DHAP, Pyr, Lac) from parallel tracer samples need to be converted to fractional labelling and checked against pathway position.
skills.name: glycolysis-metabolite-isotopologue-analysis
skills.search_text: glycolysis-metabolite-isotopologue-analysis Use when quantified isotopologue peak areas for 13C6-glucose-traced glycolysis metabolites (e.g. G6P, F6P, FBP, DHAP, Pyr, Lac) from parallel tracer samples need to be converted to fractional labelling and checked against pathway position. Input is raw EIC data rather than already-quantified isotopologue peak areas — TarMet's isotopologue quantification step must run first. The tracer is not 13C6-glucose / the metabolites are not on the glycolysis pathway, so the upstream-labelled/downstream-unlabeled expectation does not apply. The goal is de novo tracer discovery or MS/MS library verification, which are listed as planned future features of TarMet, not current capability. Summarizes 13C6-glucose tracer isotopologue peak areas (from the TarMet quantification output) into fractional labelling per glycolysis metabolite and verifies the expected upstream-labelled / downstream-unlabeled pathway pattern. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Summarizes 13C6-glucose tracer isotopologue peak areas (from the TarMet quantification output) into fractional labelling per glycolysis metabolite and verifies the expected upstream-labelled / downstream-unlabeled pathway pattern.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw EIC data rather than already-quantified isotopologue peak areas — TarMet's isotopologue quantification step must run first. The tracer is not 13C6-glucose / the metabolites are not on the glycolysis pathway, so the upstream-labelled/downstream-unlabeled expectation does not apply. The goal is de novo tracer discovery or MS/MS library verification, which are listed as planned future features of TarMet, not current capability.

skills.description: Use when a glycan of interest is not present in the GlyKAn AZ MS2 Fragment Database and its theoretical fragmentation pattern (B/Y/internal ions) and monoisotopic fragment masses must be derived from its structure string.
skills.name: glycosidic-bond-fragmentation-enumeration
skills.search_text: glycosidic-bond-fragmentation-enumeration Use when a glycan of interest is not present in the GlyKAn AZ MS2 Fragment Database and its theoretical fragmentation pattern (B/Y/internal ions) and monoisotopic fragment masses must be derived from its structure string. The glycan is already present in the GlyKAn AZ MS2 Fragment Database — use the existing database entries rather than regenerating fragments The analysis target is O-linked glycans, which the app's scope does not currently cover A de novo glycan identification is needed — the skill only derives fragments for structures you can already specify, it cannot discover unknown glycans http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Enumerates theoretical B-, Y-, and internal-ion fragments for a new N-linked glycan by representing it as a MATLAB graph (nodes = monosaccharides, edges = glycosidic bonds) and cutting every combination of one to seven bonds, producing the fragment masses needed to expand the GlyKAn AZ MS2 Fragment Database. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Enumerates theoretical B-, Y-, and internal-ion fragments for a new N-linked glycan by representing it as a MATLAB graph (nodes = monosaccharides, edges = glycosidic bonds) and cutting every combination of one to seven bonds, producing the fragment masses needed to expand the GlyKAn AZ MS2 Fragment Database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The glycan is already present in the GlyKAn AZ MS2 Fragment Database — use the existing database entries rather than regenerating fragments The analysis target is O-linked glycans, which the app's scope does not currently cover A de novo glycan identification is needed — the skill only derives fragments for structures you can already specify, it cannot discover unknown glycans

skills.description: Use when LC-MS compound identification needs CCS values predicted from SMILES/molecular structures, or when building an in-silico CCS database for molecules in PubChem under the three adduct types.
skills.name: gnn-based-ccs-prediction
skills.search_text: gnn-based-ccs-prediction Use when LC-MS compound identification needs CCS values predicted from SMILES/molecular structures, or when building an in-silico CCS database for molecules in PubChem under the three adduct types. Molecules containing elements other than C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se — SigmaCCS cannot predict these Adduct ion types beyond [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, and [M-H]- — only these three adducts are encoded When a descriptor-based or ensemble method is required instead — alternatives like AllCCS (SVR on descriptors) or CCSbase (K-Means clustering) follow different assumptions http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Predict collision cross section (CCS) values of small molecules end-to-end with the SigmaCCS graph neural network, which consumes RDKit-generated 3D conformers converted to molecular graphs plus one-hot adduct encoding. It supports [M+H]+, [M+Na]+ and [M-H]- adducts and enables large-scale in-silico CCS database construction (Zenodo record 5501674). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00939-w
skills.summary: Predict collision cross section (CCS) values of small molecules end-to-end with the SigmaCCS graph neural network, which consumes RDKit-generated 3D conformers converted to molecular graphs plus one-hot adduct encoding. It supports [M+H]+, [M+Na]+ and [M-H]- adducts and enables large-scale in-silico CCS database construction (Zenodo record 5501674).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Molecules containing elements other than C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se — SigmaCCS cannot predict these Adduct ion types beyond [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, and [M-H]- — only these three adducts are encoded When a descriptor-based or ensemble method is required instead — alternatives like AllCCS (SVR on descriptors) or CCSbase (K-Means clustering) follow different assumptions

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether a GNN-based CCS prediction model generalizes across chemically distinct reference databases, e.g. train on CCSBase and test on METLIN-CCS or vice versa.
skills.name: gnn-ccs-cross-database-training
skills.search_text: gnn-ccs-cross-database-training Use when you need to test whether a GNN-based CCS prediction model generalizes across chemically distinct reference databases, e.g. train on CCSBase and test on METLIN-CCS or vice versa. You only need within-database accuracy (train-metlin-test-metlin style splits); the cross-database direction measures generalization, not absolute model quality Your molecules fall outside the small, mostly synthetic structures covered by METLIN-CCS and CCSBase — the paper's evaluation is explicitly restricted in scope to small molecules and specific regions of chemical space You lack one of the two databases formatted with matching adduct, SMILES, coordinates, and CCS columns required by train-test.py http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Trains SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, or Mol2CCS GNN models on one CCS database (CCSBase v1.3 or METLIN-CCS) and evaluates them on the structurally different held-out database to quantify generalization, reproducing the Fig. 3 performance drops reported in Engler Hart et al. 2024. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Trains SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, or Mol2CCS GNN models on one CCS database (CCSBase v1.3 or METLIN-CCS) and evaluates them on the structurally different held-out database to quantify generalization, reproducing the Fig. 3 performance drops reported in Engler Hart et al. 2024.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need within-database accuracy (train-metlin-test-metlin style splits); the cross-database direction measures generalization, not absolute model quality Your molecules fall outside the small, mostly synthetic structures covered by METLIN-CCS and CCSBase — the paper's evaluation is explicitly restricted in scope to small molecules and specific regions of chemical space You lack one of the two databases formatted with matching adduct, SMILES, coordinates, and CCS columns required by train-test.py

skills.description: Use when you have SMILES, adduct, and CCS value columns (optionally 3D coordinates) split into train/test parquet files and need to train and benchmark GNN CCS regression models like SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, or Mol2CCS.
skills.name: gnn-ccs-regression-training
skills.search_text: gnn-ccs-regression-training Use when you have SMILES, adduct, and CCS value columns (optionally 3D coordinates) split into train/test parquet files and need to train and benchmark GNN CCS regression models like SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, or Mol2CCS. Evaluating cross-dataset generalizability (e.g. train on METLIN-CCS, test on CCSBase) rather than combined-dataset training — performance declines sharply outside the training chemical space and the combined-training metrics do not apply You only need prediction with a pre-trained model — use the Model_prediction / prediction scripts instead of retraining Input data lacks SMILES/adduct annotations or has not been processed into the parquet schema expected by train-test.py — run the data_processing notebooks first http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Training graph neural network regression models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) on combined CCSBase + METLIN-CCS collision cross section data to predict CCS values from 3D molecular coordinates, SMILES, and adduct type, then evaluating with R2, RMSE, and MRE. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Training graph neural network regression models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) on combined CCSBase + METLIN-CCS collision cross section data to predict CCS values from 3D molecular coordinates, SMILES, and adduct type, then evaluating with R2, RMSE, and MRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating cross-dataset generalizability (e.g. train on METLIN-CCS, test on CCSBase) rather than combined-dataset training — performance declines sharply outside the training chemical space and the combined-training metrics do not apply You only need prediction with a pre-trained model — use the Model_prediction / prediction scripts instead of retraining Input data lacks SMILES/adduct annotations or has not been processed into the parquet schema expected by train-test.py — run the data_processing notebooks first

skills.description: Use when you need to validate the chemical rationality of a trained GNN model: extract its pooled latent embeddings and check via 2D embedding (e.g., UMAP) whether structurally similar molecules cluster together.
skills.name: gnn-latent-vector-embedding
skills.search_text: gnn-latent-vector-embedding Use when you need to validate the chemical rationality of a trained GNN model: extract its pooled latent embeddings and check via 2D embedding (e.g., UMAP) whether structurally similar molecules cluster together. Molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, Se — SigmaCCS cannot encode their graphs Input is already a low-dimensional descriptor/feature table — UMAP on raw descriptors does not probe the GNN's learned representations The goal is CCS value prediction itself rather than interpreting representation quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Extract the learned 16-dimensional molecular vectors from SigmaCCS's ECC graph convolutional layers (after global sum pooling) and project them with UMAP to test whether the GNN representations are chemically meaningful (clustering by ring content, molecular class, and Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00939-w
skills.summary: Extract the learned 16-dimensional molecular vectors from SigmaCCS's ECC graph convolutional layers (after global sum pooling) and project them with UMAP to test whether the GNN representations are chemically meaningful (clustering by ring content, molecular class, and Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, Se — SigmaCCS cannot encode their graphs Input is already a low-dimensional descriptor/feature table — UMAP on raw descriptors does not probe the GNN's learned representations The goal is CCS value prediction itself rather than interpreting representation quality

skills.description: Use when building a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network whose curated reaction pairs (e.g. ~14,974 from KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB) are too sparse to support network-based metabolite annotation propagation.
skills.name: gnn-reaction-pair-prediction
skills.search_text: gnn-reaction-pair-prediction Use when building a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network whose curated reaction pairs (e.g. ~14,974 from KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB) are too sparse to support network-based metabolite annotation propagation. When the goal is annotation of experimental MS features directly — this skill only builds the knowledge layer; experimental data are pre-mapped via MS1 matching, reaction relationship mapping, and MS2 similarity constraints in a separate step When a formally validated FDR for the reaction network is required — the article explicitly refrains from reporting an FDR for the MRN because non-RPs are undefined When reaction space must be fully open-ended — BioTransformer-generated unknowns are limited by predefined reaction types and may introduce species-specific biases http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Trains and applies a graph neural network to pre-screened candidate reaction pairs to predict additional metabolite-metabolite reaction relationships, expanding a KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB-derived metabolic reaction network (MRN) beyond curated database knowledge for metabolite annotation in MetDNA3. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Trains and applies a graph neural network to pre-screened candidate reaction pairs to predict additional metabolite-metabolite reaction relationships, expanding a KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB-derived metabolic reaction network (MRN) beyond curated database knowledge for metabolite annotation in MetDNA3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotation of experimental MS features directly — this skill only builds the knowledge layer; experimental data are pre-mapped via MS1 matching, reaction relationship mapping, and MS2 similarity constraints in a separate step When a formally validated FDR for the reaction network is required — the article explicitly refrains from reporting an FDR for the MRN because non-RPs are undefined When reaction space must be fully open-ended — BioTransformer-generated unknowns are limited by predefined reaction types and may introduce species-specific biases

skills.description: Use when you have SMILES strings for natural products (e.g. from MIBiG json entries) and need biosynthetically-informed chemical class terms (pathway/class/subclass) to match against BGC class ontologies.
skills.name: gnps-api-npclassifier-classification-retrieval
skills.search_text: gnps-api-npclassifier-classification-retrieval Use when you have SMILES strings for natural products (e.g. from MIBiG json entries) and need biosynthetically-informed chemical class terms (pathway/class/subclass) to match against BGC class ontologies. Input molecules are >850 Da or lack SMILES: NPClassifier requires chemical structure input, and the article notes CANOPUS/structure-based predictions have a 850 Da mass cut-off, so structure-class retrieval is inappropriate there. The goal is MS/MS-spectrum-level class prediction rather than SMILES-based classification: use CANOPUS via Sirius or MolNetEnhancer on GNPS molecular networking mgf files instead. The analysis needs ClassyFire hierarchical superclass/class/subclass ontologies rather than biosynthetic-pathway-informed NPClassifier terms; the two ontologies serve different downstream matching tables. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Retrieve NPClassifier pathway-level chemical classifications for natural product SMILES by querying the GNPS API, as used to bridge MIBiG BGC classes to metabolomics class ontologies in the NPClassScore pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Retrieve NPClassifier pathway-level chemical classifications for natural product SMILES by querying the GNPS API, as used to bridge MIBiG BGC classes to metabolomics class ontologies in the NPClassScore pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input molecules are >850 Da or lack SMILES: NPClassifier requires chemical structure input, and the article notes CANOPUS/structure-based predictions have a 850 Da mass cut-off, so structure-class retrieval is inappropriate there. The goal is MS/MS-spectrum-level class prediction rather than SMILES-based classification: use CANOPUS via Sirius or MolNetEnhancer on GNPS molecular networking mgf files instead. The analysis needs ClassyFire hierarchical superclass/class/subclass ontologies rather than biosynthetic-pathway-informed NPClassifier terms; the two ontologies serve different downstream matching tables.

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra loaded from MGF, mzML, mzXML, or msp files carry inconsistent or missing metadata (compound name, InChI, SMILES, InChIKey, ionmode, adduct, charge) and must be cleaned before intensity normalization or similarity scoring.
skills.name: gnps-dataset-curation
skills.search_text: gnps-dataset-curation Use when MS/MS spectra loaded from MGF, mzML, mzXML, or msp files carry inconsistent or missing metadata (compound name, InChI, SMILES, InChIKey, ionmode, adduct, charge) and must be cleaned before intensity normalization or similarity scoring. The goal is peak-level filtering rather than metadata cleaning — matchms provides separate peak filters (select_by_mz, select_by_relative_intensity, require_minimum_number_of_peaks) for that purpose Spectra are already cleaned and harmonized and you only need similarity scoring (cosine score, modified cosine score) between them The metadata cannot be represented in matchms Spectrum objects, e.g. spectra visualization workflows better served by spectrum_utils http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies matchms's default_filters metadata-cleaning stack to mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra so that inconsistent, wrongly labeled, or incorrect metadata fields are corrected before downstream processing. It is the metadata-harmonization step of a reproducible spectral processing workflow built with matchms. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02411
skills.summary: Applies matchms's default_filters metadata-cleaning stack to mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra so that inconsistent, wrongly labeled, or incorrect metadata fields are corrected before downstream processing. It is the metadata-harmonization step of a reproducible spectral processing workflow built with matchms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peak-level filtering rather than metadata cleaning — matchms provides separate peak filters (select_by_mz, select_by_relative_intensity, require_minimum_number_of_peaks) for that purpose Spectra are already cleaned and harmonized and you only need similarity scoring (cosine score, modified cosine score) between them The metadata cannot be represented in matchms Spectrum objects, e.g. spectra visualization workflows better served by spectrum_utils

skills.description: Use when mzML LC-MS/MS runs have been processed by Optimus and detected features need putative compound identities via MS/MS spectral library matching at GNPS, to be attached by mz-RT matching.
skills.name: gnps-dereplication-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: gnps-dereplication-workflow-execution Use when mzML LC-MS/MS runs have been processed by Optimus and detected features need putative compound identities via MS/MS spectral library matching at GNPS, to be attached by mz-RT matching. Features have already been annotated or a validated compound-annotation table exists — re-running GNPS dereplication would duplicate work The goal is level-1 identified compounds with MS/MS spectral validation — Optimus only provides level-2 putative annotations and does not perform MS/MS validation Data is direct-infusion MS without LC-MS/MS spectra — no MS/MS spectra can be matched for dereplication http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Runs GNPS dereplication on LC-MS/MS runs exported from Optimus to obtain level-2 (Metabolomics Standards Initiative) putative molecular annotations, which are fed back into Optimus via mz-RT matching against a molecules-of-interest list. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nprot.2017.122
skills.summary: Runs GNPS dereplication on LC-MS/MS runs exported from Optimus to obtain level-2 (Metabolomics Standards Initiative) putative molecular annotations, which are fed back into Optimus via mz-RT matching against a molecules-of-interest list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features have already been annotated or a validated compound-annotation table exists — re-running GNPS dereplication would duplicate work The goal is level-1 identified compounds with MS/MS spectral validation — Optimus only provides level-2 putative annotations and does not perform MS/MS validation Data is direct-infusion MS without LC-MS/MS spectra — no MS/MS spectra can be matched for dereplication

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics data (MZmine-processed features with MS/MS spectra) must be screened for drugs, metabolites, and analogs to infer drug exposures empirically, e.g. matching fecal-incubation analogs to community metabolism.
skills.name: gnps-drug-library-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: gnps-drug-library-spectral-matching Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics data (MZmine-processed features with MS/MS spectra) must be screened for drugs, metabolites, and analogs to infer drug exposures empirically, e.g. matching fecal-incubation analogs to community metabolism. Clinical decision-making — the GNPS Drug Library is explicitly not intended for immediate clinical decisions and only supports data-driven exploration Input is a quantified feature table with no associated MS/MS spectra (library annotation requires tandem mass spectra) Data acquired by non-LC-MS/MS modalities or experiments lacking drug-only/drug-free controls needed to separate biotic transformation from abiotic or ion-form artifacts http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Match untargeted LC-MS/MS feature spectra against the GNPS Drug Library to annotate parent drugs, metabolites, and analogs and empirically establish drug exposure records, distinguishing true biotic transformation products from abiotic artifacts using time-course and control evidence. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5
skills.summary: Match untargeted LC-MS/MS feature spectra against the GNPS Drug Library to annotate parent drugs, metabolites, and analogs and empirically establish drug exposure records, distinguishing true biotic transformation products from abiotic artifacts using time-course and control evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clinical decision-making — the GNPS Drug Library is explicitly not intended for immediate clinical decisions and only supports data-driven exploration Input is a quantified feature table with no associated MS/MS spectra (library annotation requires tandem mass spectra) Data acquired by non-LC-MS/MS modalities or experiments lacking drug-only/drug-free controls needed to separate biotic transformation from abiotic or ion-form artifacts

skills.name: gnps-fbmn-export-file-preparation
skills.search_text: gnps-fbmn-export-file-preparation Use when a processed LC-MS/MS feature map (consensusXML after feature detection, alignment, adduct annotation, and feature linking) must be exported to run a GNPS FBMN or IIMN job downstream. When the raw vendor data has not yet been converted to mzML or the pre-processing workflow (feature detection, alignment, adduct annotation, feature linking) has not been run — no consensus feature map exists to export. When downstream analysis uses SIRIUS/MS2Query annotations directly without a GNPS FBMN/IIMN network job — the export file set is not needed. When spectra already exist as a GNPS-ready MGF from another tool; regenerating via GNPSExport would duplicate the clustering step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Prepares the exact file set GNPS requires for Feature-Based Molecular Networking and Ion Identity Molecular Networking jobs by filtering the OpenMS consensus feature map to features carrying MS2 spectra, then generating the MGF, feature quantification table, adduct-connection supplementary table, and metadata table via OpenMS GNPSExport and pyOpenMS. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: Prepares the exact file set GNPS requires for Feature-Based Molecular Networking and Ion Identity Molecular Networking jobs by filtering the OpenMS consensus feature map to features carrying MS2 spectra, then generating the MGF, feature quantification table, adduct-connection supplementary table, and metadata table via OpenMS GNPSExport and pyOpenMS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the raw vendor data has not yet been converted to mzML or the pre-processing workflow (feature detection, alignment, adduct annotation, feature linking) has not been run — no consensus feature map exists to export. When downstream analysis uses SIRIUS/MS2Query annotations directly without a GNPS FBMN/IIMN network job — the export file set is not needed. When spectra already exist as a GNPS-ready MGF from another tool; regenerating via GNPSExport would duplicate the clustering step.

Analysis targets GC-MS or proteomics data where the feature-based molecular networking IIMN workflow is not applicable.

skills.search_text: gnps-fbmn-job-submission-and-network-import Use when an LC-MS/MS dataset has already been processed to a feature quantification table (row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area) plus a .MGF MS/MS spectral summary, and the goal is a GNPS FBMN job and a Cytoscape network in which bioactive nodes can be flagged. skills.name: gnps-fbmn-output-processing
skills.search_text: gnps-fbmn-output-processing Use when the inputs are an MZmine join-aligner output (aligned feature intensity CSV) plus its GNPS FBMN-exported .mgf spectra file, and the goal is an RT-agnostic sample-by-feature presence/absence MEMO matrix rather than an intensity-based comparison. When MS1 feature intensities must inform the analysis — the MEMO matrix intentionally ignores intensity and uses only presence/absence occurrence counting When retention-time information is essential to distinguish samples — MEMO is explicitly RT-agnostic and cannot resolve RT-shift-based differences When the data are raw vendor files or spectra without MS2 fragmentation — the workflow requires MS2 peak/neutral-loss content and the MZmine-aligned CSV + GNPS FBMN .mgf pair http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Convert GNPS FBMN workflow outputs — an MZmine-exported aligned feature quantification table (.csv) and its GNPS FBMN-exported .mgf MS/MS spectra file — into a MEMO matrix of per-sample MS2 peak and neutral-loss occurrence counts for retention-time-agnostic sample comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964

skills.description: Use when a downstream prioritization step (e.g. Inventa FC score) needs a regenerated GNPS FBMN job — node/edge/IIN counts and cleaned spectral annotations — from a MZmine quant table and metadata file for an untargeted LC-HRMS/MS extract set.
skills.name: gnps-feature-based-molecular-networking-rerun
skills.search_text: gnps-feature-based-molecular-networking-rerun Use when a downstream prioritization step (e.g. Inventa FC score) needs a regenerated GNPS FBMN job — node/edge/IIN counts and cleaned spectral annotations — from a MZmine quant table and metadata file for an untargeted LC-HRMS/MS extract set. Input is already a cleaned annotation table — rerunning FBMN would duplicate work; go straight to Inventa's FC computation. No MZmine quantification table is available (e.g. data processed only in another tool) — FBMN expects the MZmine output format with 'Peak area', 'row m/z' and 'row retention time' columns. The analysis needs RT-aware sample comparison rather than feature annotation/network statistics — use the MEMO metric instead, which is explicitly RT-agnostic and compares MS2 fingerprints. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Re-run the GNPS Feature Based Molecular Networking (FBMN) job on a MZmine2/MZmine3 feature quantification table plus GNPS-format metadata to reproduce the ion identity network (nodes, IIN groups, edges, singletons) and library/in-silico spectral annotations needed downstream by Inventa's Feature Component scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Re-run the GNPS Feature Based Molecular Networking (FBMN) job on a MZmine2/MZmine3 feature quantification table plus GNPS-format metadata to reproduce the ion identity network (nodes, IIN groups, edges, singletons) and library/in-silico spectral annotations needed downstream by Inventa's Feature Component scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned annotation table — rerunning FBMN would duplicate work; go straight to Inventa's FC computation. No MZmine quantification table is available (e.g. data processed only in another tool) — FBMN expects the MZmine output format with 'Peak area', 'row m/z' and 'row retention time' columns. The analysis needs RT-aware sample comparison rather than feature annotation/network statistics — use the MEMO metric instead, which is explicitly RT-agnostic and compares MS2 fingerprints.

skills.search_text: gnps-graphml-feature-import Use when the input mass spectrometry data is a GNPS network file (GNPS.graphml) and MS features must be imported and basketed as the first npanalyst CLI step before activity-score computation. skills.name: gnps-library-match-filtering
skills.search_text: gnps-library-match-filtering Use when an aligned feature table with MS2 spectra (.mgf) and IIN edges is available and high-confidence GNPS library annotations must be identified and propagated to co-eluting ion species (adducts, multimers, in-source fragments) of the same compound. Input is raw MS data that has not yet been feature-found and exported to a quantification table plus .mgf — run the FBMN/IIMN workflow first. Goal is de novo annotation or molecular formula prediction (use SIRIUS/CANOPUS-style tools) rather than library-match-based spectral propagation. The network lacks ion identity edges (plain molecular networking without IIMN), so adducts/in-source fragments of the same compound are not connected and propagation would be unfounded. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filters GNPS spectral library matches in ion identity molecular networks (IIMN) using cosine similarity and shared-fragment thresholds, then propagates high-confidence matches to connected ion-identity features to build expanded spectral library entries (e.g., GNPS-IIMN-PROPOGATED). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23953-9
skills.summary: Filters GNPS spectral library matches in ion identity molecular networks (IIMN) using cosine similarity and shared-fragment thresholds, then propagates high-confidence matches to connected ion-identity features to build expanded spectral library entries (e.g., GNPS-IIMN-PROPOGATED).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS data that has not yet been feature-found and exported to a quantification table plus .mgf — run the FBMN/IIMN workflow first. Goal is de novo annotation or molecular formula prediction (use SIRIUS/CANOPUS-style tools) rather than library-match-based spectral propagation. The network lacks ion identity edges (plain molecular networking without IIMN), so adducts/in-source fragments of the same compound are not connected and propagation would be unfounded.

skills.description: Use when an mzmine (>2.53) FBMN feature table (CSV) and MGF MS/MS spectra need GNPS library annotations, and the goal is to compare strict single-query vs iterative weighted analog search InChI return rates.
skills.name: gnps-library-search-execution
skills.search_text: gnps-library-search-execution Use when an mzmine (>2.53) FBMN feature table (CSV) and MGF MS/MS spectra need GNPS library annotations, and the goal is to compare strict single-query vs iterative weighted analog search InChI return rates. The goal is aggregating GNPS annotations with ISDB-LOTUS and Sirius into a K-ranked prioritization (that is the K_estimation step, not the raw library search). Input data is not FBMN-formatted (e.g. not an mzmine export feature table/MGF pair), since the strict/iterative GNPS workflows are launched as FBMN jobs. Only exact library matches are needed and runtime matters: the iterative search takes up to three hours and 27 FBMN jobs versus one strict job. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Executes GNPS FBMN spectral library searches against a GNPS spectral library, either as a single strict query or as the iterative weighted analog search (GNPS I), to assign InChIs/SMILES to MS/MS features such as those from the P. mutica extract (754 mzmine 4 features). metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Executes GNPS FBMN spectral library searches against a GNPS spectral library, either as a single strict query or as the iterative weighted analog search (GNPS I), to assign InChIs/SMILES to MS/MS features such as those from the P. mutica extract (754 mzmine 4 features).

skills.description: Use when the goal is a repository-scale chemical annotation table across public tandem MS files, e.g. reproducing the ReDU compound-by-file GNPS library search matrix or updating ReDU's identification database.

skills.search_text: gnps-library-search-results-retrieval Use when the goal is a repository-scale chemical annotation table across public tandem MS files, e.g. reproducing the ReDU compound-by-file GNPS library search matrix or updating ReDU's identification database. The goal is molecular networking (molecular similarity networks) rather than library-search annotations — GNPS molecular networking has a different recommended file limit of 3000 files. Only files within a user-selected metadata-filtered cohort (G1–G6 via the ReDU File Selector) are needed, rather than all public files in ReDU. Data are not in MassIVE — ReDU only interacts with MassIVE and does not yet incorporate other resources. Retrieve ReDU's pre-computed GNPS spectral library search results (MS/MS spectral library matching with default parameters) for all public MassIVE files and encode them as a binary chemical-annotation-by-file matrix with 1 = detected and 0 = not detected. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-020-0916-7
skills.summary: Retrieve ReDU's pre-computed GNPS spectral library search results (MS/MS spectral library matching with default parameters) for all public MassIVE files and encode them as a binary chemical-annotation-by-file matrix with 1 = detected and 0 = not detected.

skills.search_text: gnps-library-spectrum-preprocessing Use when preparing a downloaded GNPS MGF library (e.g. ALL_GNPS.mgf) as training data or as a cleaned search library for MS2Deepscore/Spec2Vec/MS2Query, so that spectra are uniform and noise-free. Input is already a cleaned, intensity-normalized library such as the pretrained MS2Query sqlite library downloaded via 'ms2query --library ... --download' — re-cleaning is unnecessary and may alter peak lists. The task is peak picking or clustering of query MS2 spectra from LC-MS/MS runs; MS2Query itself does no peak picking, and tools like MZMine/FBMN should preprocess feature-level spectra first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Clean and normalize GNPS library mass spectra with matchms before model training or library matching: filter low-quality spectra, remove noise peaks, cap peak mass, normalize intensities, and standardize metadata. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: Clean and normalize GNPS library mass spectra with matchms before model training or library matching: filter low-quality spectra, remove noise peaks, cap peak mass, normalize intensities, and standardize metadata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned, intensity-normalized library such as the pretrained MS2Query sqlite library downloaded via 'ms2query --library ... --download' — re-cleaning is unnecessary and may alter peak lists. The task is peak picking or clustering of query MS2 spectra from LC-MS/MS runs; MS2Query itself does no peak picking, and tools like MZMine/FBMN should preprocess feature-level spectra first.

skills.description: Use when a public GNPS/MassBank/MoNA .msp library needs reproducible cleaning before library matching or machine-learning training: metadata harmonization, adduct/parent-mass repair, annotation validation.
skills.name: gnps-library-spectrum-processing
skills.search_text: gnps-library-spectrum-processing Use when a public GNPS/MassBank/MoNA .msp library needs reproducible cleaning before library matching or machine-learning training: metadata harmonization, adduct/parent-mass repair, annotation validation. The input is already a cleaned library (e.g. the Zenodo-published cleaned GNPS version with 448,485 spectra); re-running the repair filters adds no information. You need plausibility checks that consider measured fragments, not just metadata: wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass will go unnoticed because fragment-matching filters are not implemented. You need cleaned instrument-type or collision-energy metadata; current matchms filters do not yet standardize these fields. The task is interactive curation during upload to a public library rather than offline cleaning; a dedicated validator tool for that is only proposed as future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Run the matchms library-cleaning pipeline over annotated MS/MS library spectra (e.g. the GNPS public library) to harmonize metadata, derive missing annotations from PubChem, and repair or discard inconsistent structure annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: Run the matchms library-cleaning pipeline over annotated MS/MS library spectra (e.g. the GNPS public library) to harmonize metadata, derive missing annotations from PubChem, and repair or discard inconsistent structure annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cleaned library (e.g. the Zenodo-published cleaned GNPS version with 448,485 spectra); re-running the repair filters adds no information. You need plausibility checks that consider measured fragments, not just metadata: wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass will go unnoticed because fragment-matching filters are not implemented. You need cleaned instrument-type or collision-energy metadata; current matchms filters do not yet standardize these fields. The task is interactive curation during upload to a public library rather than offline cleaning; a dedicated validator tool for that is only proposed as future work.

skills.search_text: gnps-masst-repository-mining Use when KGMN (or similar) has produced putatively annotated unknown metabolites with precursor m/z and MS/MS spectra and you need to test whether they recur in public metabolomics repositories (GNPS/MassIVE) as an orthogonal validation signal. The metabolites are knowns already covered by standard spectral libraries, so library searching (rather than repository mining) suffices for annotation or validation The task is constructing or visualizing the KGMN subnetworks themselves (MetDNA2Vis reconstructNetwork1/2/3, retrieveSubNetwork1/2/3, mergeSubnetwork) rather than testing recurrence of already-annotated unknowns The input spectra lack precursor m/z or MS/MS fragment peaks, making MASST matching impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Repository-mining of putatively annotated unknown metabolites: each KGMN-annotated unknown MS/MS spectrum (e.g., from the NIST urine Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos dataset) is submitted to GNPS MASST and searched against all public data sets in MassIVE to quantify recurrence across data sets, data files, species, and sample types. This leverages public data as a validation route for unknowns that lack chemical standards.

skills.description: Use when dereplicating preprocessed MS2 .mzML query spectra against GNPS, HMDB, and MassBank spectral libraries and scoring candidate metabolite matches per LC-MS2 feature.
skills.name: gnps-matching-peak-scoring
skills.search_text: gnps-matching-peak-scoring Use when dereplicating preprocessed MS2 .mzML query spectra against GNPS, HMDB, and MassBank spectral libraries and scoring candidate metabolite matches per LC-MS2 feature. Input is not tandem MS2 spectral data (.mzML) needing spectral-library dereplication — e.g. when the goal is compound-structure annotation via compound databases, where SIRIUS/MetFrag dereplication or RDKit candidate selection is the relevant step Query spectra are absent or poorly represented in the three public spectral libraries — the article notes there is a large mismatch between experimental spectra in spectral databases and structures in compound databases, leading to a low number of annotated features You need deterministic candidate-ranking thresholds — the article only established score gates for the spectral-database segment, not for downstream in silico annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Spectral database dereplication step of MAW-R that matches query MS2 spectra (.mzML) against GNPS, HMDB, and MassBank spectral libraries inside the R Spectra framework, scoring GNPS candidates with the GNPS altered matching-peak similarity score (threshold 0.85) and HMDB/MassBank candidates with the unaltered dot-product cosine similarity (threshold 0.70), gated by MAW-defined mz_score/int_score metrics at a 0.5 threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00695-y
skills.summary: Spectral database dereplication step of MAW-R that matches query MS2 spectra (.mzML) against GNPS, HMDB, and MassBank spectral libraries inside the R Spectra framework, scoring GNPS candidates with the GNPS altered matching-peak similarity score (threshold 0.85) and HMDB/MassBank candidates with the unaltered dot-product cosine similarity (threshold 0.70), gated by MAW-defined mz_score/int_score metrics at a 0.5 threshold.

skills.search_text: gnps-modified-cosine-fingerprint-computation Use when query MS/MS spectra (e.g., MassQL-filtered siderophore hits) must be converted into sample-wise similarity fingerprints to feed the NPOmix k-nearest neighbor classifier or compare spectra across paired genome–metabolome samples. You need full GNPS molecular networking outputs (cluster edges, library hits) rather than per-sample similarity fingerprints — the README notes 'we did not use the full classical GNPS molecular networking capabilities' The query spectra are isomers or homologs that modified cosine cannot resolve — NPOmix 'does not have the resolution to distinguish between isomers and regioselectivity of the various homologs' There are no paired samples or no spectra similar to the query in the sample set — fingerprints will be uninformative, as with fungal species whose BGCs match nothing in the training set http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes MS/MS similarity fingerprints by scoring each query spectrum against all spectra in every paired experimental sample via GNPS pairwise modified cosine, producing the maximum-similarity vector used as NPOmix's KNN test matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Computes MS/MS similarity fingerprints by scoring each query spectrum against all spectra in every paired experimental sample via GNPS pairwise modified cosine, producing the maximum-similarity vector used as NPOmix's KNN test matrix.

skills.search_text: graph-laplacian-pseudoinverse-embedding Use when two tandem MS spectra (e.g., MassBank MGF entries) must be aligned via a pair-specific fragment similarity built from all pairwise m/z differences within a tolerance, especially when compounds differ by multiple structural changes. The spectra involve adducts other than protonation/deprotonation — the paper states SIMILE 'is currently limited to analysis of protonation/deprotonation' The goal is standard compound identification where established cosine-based scoring suffices — the authors recommend complementing SIMILE with cosine-based scoring, and note some molecule classes may be more appropriate for cosine scoring A single global fragment-ion substitution matrix across many spectra pairs is required — the paper motivates the pair-specific approach precisely because a global matrix would be infinite due to the infinite number of possible m/z values Generates a pair-specific fragment-ion similarity matrix (S) from two tandem MS fragmentation spectra by building an all-by-all m/z difference count matrix, row-normalizing it into transition probabilities, and taking the pseudoinverse of its normalized graph Laplacian. This yields an 'average commute time' fragment similarity that handles multiple structural differences without requiring identical m/z values or shared precursor neutral losses. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-30118-9
skills.summary: Generates a pair-specific fragment-ion similarity matrix (S) from two tandem MS fragmentation spectra by building an all-by-all m/z difference count matrix, row-normalizing it into transition probabilities, and taking the pseudoinverse of its normalized graph Laplacian. This yields an 'average commute time' fragment similarity that handles multiple structural differences without requiring identical m/z values or shared precursor neutral losses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra involve adducts other than protonation/deprotonation — the paper states SIMILE 'is currently limited to analysis of protonation/deprotonation' The goal is standard compound identification where established cosine-based scoring suffices — the authors recommend complementing SIMILE with cosine-based scoring, and note some molecule classes may be more appropriate for cosine scoring A single global fragment-ion substitution matrix across many spectra pairs is required — the paper motivates the pair-specific approach precisely because a global matrix would be infinite due to the infinite number of possible m/z values

skills.name: graph-neural-network-inference
skills.search_text: graph-neural-network-inference Use when you need to score candidate enzyme–substrate reactions with a trained GNN-SOM model and check whether scores differentiate true (Known) from random pairs via a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test. The input is unannotated mass features without predicted metabolite structures — the GNN-SOM scorer requires molecular structures of substrates, not raw m/z features. The goal is correlation-based pathway discovery from paired transcriptomics/metabolomics data (mutual-rank correlation, ClusterONE feature clusters) — use the MEANtools MR/ClusterONE pipeline instead of GNN scoring. The task requires multi-substrate reaction prediction — reaction-rule based prediction in this context is designed for single-substrate reactions only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Applies a pretrained GNN-SOM graph neural network, combined with ReactionDecoder reaction-center prediction, to compute reaction-likelihood scores for enzyme–substrate pairs, and validates the scoring by statistically separating experimentally characterized (Known) pairs from randomly assembled (Random) pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Applies a pretrained GNN-SOM graph neural network, combined with ReactionDecoder reaction-center prediction, to compute reaction-likelihood scores for enzyme–substrate pairs, and validates the scoring by statistically separating experimentally characterized (Known) pairs from randomly assembled (Random) pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is unannotated mass features without predicted metabolite structures — the GNN-SOM scorer requires molecular structures of substrates, not raw m/z features. The goal is correlation-based pathway discovery from paired transcriptomics/metabolomics data (mutual-rank correlation, ClusterONE feature clusters) — use the MEANtools MR/ClusterONE pipeline instead of GNN scoring. The task requires multi-substrate reaction prediction — reaction-rule based prediction in this context is designed for single-substrate reactions only.

skills.description: Use when building or validating a GNN layer for 3D molecular point sets (xyz coordinates + atom one-hot features) where embeddings must be provably invariant to atom ordering, translation, and rotation — e.g. as an encoder for MS/MS, RT, or CCS prediction.
skills.name: graph-neural-network-layer-implementation
skills.search_text: graph-neural-network-layer-implementation Use when building or validating a GNN layer for 3D molecular point sets (xyz coordinates + atom one-hot features) where embeddings must be provably invariant to atom ordering, translation, and rotation — e.g. as an encoder for MS/MS, RT, or CCS prediction. The molecule has no 3D conformer (input is only a 2D graph or SMILES) — MolConv's geometry channels require xyz coordinates, so generate ETKDGv3 conformers first via molecules_to_records/sdf2pkl The task is chiral/enantiomer discrimination with a purely E(3)-invariant encoder — an E(3) encoder provably cannot distinguish enantiomers, so the SE(3) chirality mode is required Geometry is computed from absolute atom positions (the deprecated MolConv1 formulation) — this breaks translation invariance and was removed in v1.4.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements the MolConv layer from 3DMolMS (v1.4.0, molnetpack): a geometry-aware GNN message-passing layer that aggregates over the covalent bond graph using distance and direction filters on relative displacements, giving embeddings invariant to atom permutation, translation, and rotation. This skill covers both constructing the layer and numerically verifying its architectural invariances. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad354
skills.summary: Implements the MolConv layer from 3DMolMS (v1.4.0, molnetpack): a geometry-aware GNN message-passing layer that aggregates over the covalent bond graph using distance and direction filters on relative displacements, giving embeddings invariant to atom permutation, translation, and rotation. This skill covers both constructing the layer and numerically verifying its architectural invariances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule has no 3D conformer (input is only a 2D graph or SMILES) — MolConv's geometry channels require xyz coordinates, so generate ETKDGv3 conformers first via molecules_to_records/sdf2pkl The task is chiral/enantiomer discrimination with a purely E(3)-invariant encoder — an E(3) encoder provably cannot distinguish enantiomers, so the SE(3) chirality mode is required Geometry is computed from absolute atom positions (the deprecated MolConv1 formulation) — this breaks translation invariance and was removed in v1.4.0
