The analysis target is a compound class with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low-MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes), which MADByTE's TOCSY shielded-quadrant exclusion (<2.5 ppm in both F1 and F2) precludes from network construction Input is a raw 1D/2D NMR spectrum rather than an already-built spin-system similarity network; spectral processing and spin-system construction must happen first The goal is quantitative compound quantification rather than structural relationship visualization; the network conveys shared-feature similarity, not concentration Exports a MADByTE chemical similarity network as a graphML file and renders it in Gephi using the Force Atlas 2 layout algorithm so that structurally related compounds appear as visual clusters of shared spin-system features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Exports a MADByTE chemical similarity network as a graphML file and renders it in Gephi using the Force Atlas 2 layout algorithm so that structurally related compounds appear as visual clusters of shared spin-system features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is a compound class with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low-MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes), which MADByTE's TOCSY shielded-quadrant exclusion (<2.5 ppm in both F1 and F2) precludes from network construction Input is a raw 1D/2D NMR spectrum rather than an already-built spin-system similarity network; spectral processing and spin-system construction must happen first The goal is quantitative compound quantification rather than structural relationship visualization; the network conveys shared-feature similarity, not concentration

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing GLEAMS spectrum featurization: you need to build the exact 3010-feature input vector (Gray-coded precursor mass/m/z, one-hot charge, 2449 fragment bins, 500 reference-spectrum similarities) before applying the pretrained GLEAMS embedding network.
skills.name: gray-code-precursor-mass-encoding
skills.search_text: gray-code-precursor-mass-encoding Use when reconstructing or reimplementing GLEAMS spectrum featurization: you need to build the exact 3010-feature input vector (Gray-coded precursor mass/m/z, one-hot charge, 2449 fragment bins, 500 reference-spectrum similarities) before applying the pretrained GLEAMS embedding network. Input is already a 32-dimensional GLEAMS embedding or a GLEAMS_embed.npy array — featurization is only the pre-embedding step. The goal is peptide identification (e.g., an MSGF+ search) rather than spectrum featurization/clustering; GLEAMS featurization supports embedding and clustering, not de novo ID. Spectra are not HCD-style peptide MS/MS spectra with usable precursor mass/m/z and charge — the encoding is trained on 30 million MassIVE-KB (v1) PSMs from human HCD data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reproduce GLEAMS's input feature encoding: each MS/MS spectrum is converted to a 3010-dimensional feature vector combining Gray-coded precursor mass/m/z, one-hot charge, square-root-transformed binned fragment intensities, and dot-product similarities to 500 reference spectra before neural-network embedding. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Reproduce GLEAMS's input feature encoding: each MS/MS spectrum is converted to a 3010-dimensional feature vector combining Gray-coded precursor mass/m/z, one-hot charge, square-root-transformed binned fragment intensities, and dot-product similarities to 500 reference spectra before neural-network embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a 32-dimensional GLEAMS embedding or a GLEAMS_embed.npy array — featurization is only the pre-embedding step. The goal is peptide identification (e.g., an MSGF+ search) rather than spectrum featurization/clustering; GLEAMS featurization supports embedding and clustering, not de novo ID. Spectra are not HCD-style peptide MS/MS spectra with usable precursor mass/m/z and charge — the encoding is trained on 30 million MassIVE-KB (v1) PSMs from human HCD data.

skills.description: Use when MSI pixels have been assigned brain-region labels (e.g. Waxholm Space atlas) and a lipid annotation table exists, and the goal is to identify which lipid species distinguish white-matter structures (corpus callosum, corticofugal pathway) from gray-matter structures.
skills.name: gray-vs-white-matter-lipid-biology-interpretation
skills.search_text: gray-vs-white-matter-lipid-biology-interpretation Use when MSI pixels have been assigned brain-region labels (e.g. Waxholm Space atlas) and a lipid annotation table exists, and the goal is to identify which lipid species distinguish white-matter structures (corpus callosum, corticofugal pathway) from gray-matter structures. The MSI data have not yet been registered to a rat MRI brain atlas or had Waxholm Space atlas labels propagated to pixels — interpret regional lipid biology only after the multimodal registration step produces the volumetric reconstruction. The input is single-cell (SCMS) data rather than tissue MSI; this skill's differential analysis is defined over atlas-labeled pixels, not over isolated cells. Lipid annotations cannot be made because m/z values cannot be searched against LIPID MAPS or similar lipid databases; without annotation, biological interpretation of myelin-related species is not possible. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Biological interpretation of region-specific lipid profiles from registered 3D rat brain MALDI FT-ICR MSI, focusing on the enrichment of myelin-associated lipids (ceramide, sphingomyelin, HexCer) in white-matter structures versus gray-matter structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Biological interpretation of region-specific lipid profiles from registered 3D rat brain MALDI FT-ICR MSI, focusing on the enrichment of myelin-associated lipids (ceramide, sphingomyelin, HexCer) in white-matter structures versus gray-matter structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MSI data have not yet been registered to a rat MRI brain atlas or had Waxholm Space atlas labels propagated to pixels — interpret regional lipid biology only after the multimodal registration step produces the volumetric reconstruction. The input is single-cell (SCMS) data rather than tissue MSI; this skill's differential analysis is defined over atlas-labeled pixels, not over isolated cells. Lipid annotations cannot be made because m/z values cannot be searched against LIPID MAPS or similar lipid databases; without annotation, biological interpretation of myelin-related species is not possible.

skills.description: Use when serial 2D MSI sections need a single-channel anatomically contrasting image (e.g., to register against T2*-weighted MRI atlas slices) from a high-dimensional hyperspectral data cube or UMAP embedding.
skills.name: grayscale-feature-image-conversion
skills.search_text: grayscale-feature-image-conversion Use when serial 2D MSI sections need a single-channel anatomically contrasting image (e.g., to register against T2*-weighted MRI atlas slices) from a high-dimensional hyperspectral data cube or UMAP embedding. Input data are already single-channel intensity images (e.g., optical microscopy TIFFs from the Axio Imager M2) — no embedding-to-grayscale conversion is needed before registration. The goal is pixel-level chemical interpretation of the UMAP embedding rather than image registration — collapsing three UMAP dimensions to grayscale discards chemical separation information. Sections lack a trained parametric UMAP embedding space shared across serial sections; the grayscale conversion presupposes the coherent cross-section embedding from the UMAP autoencoder. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Converts a 2D MSI section's parametric UMAP embedding into a single grayscale feature image by encoding three UMAP dimensions as red/green/blue channels and collapsing them to grayscale, providing anatomical contrast suitable for multimodal image registration to MRI atlas slices. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Converts a 2D MSI section's parametric UMAP embedding into a single grayscale feature image by encoding three UMAP dimensions as red/green/blue channels and collapsing them to grayscale, providing anatomical contrast suitable for multimodal image registration to MRI atlas slices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already single-channel intensity images (e.g., optical microscopy TIFFs from the Axio Imager M2) — no embedding-to-grayscale conversion is needed before registration. The goal is pixel-level chemical interpretation of the UMAP embedding rather than image registration — collapsing three UMAP dimensions to grayscale discards chemical separation information. Sections lack a trained parametric UMAP embedding space shared across serial sections; the grayscale conversion presupposes the coherent cross-section embedding from the UMAP autoencoder.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS feature tables (MS1/MS2 m/z pairs with intensities, e.g. from MS-DIAL output) must be converted into fixed-size grayscale images for image-based deep learning such as CNN bioactivity prediction.
skills.name: grayscale-scatter-plot-rendering
skills.search_text: grayscale-scatter-plot-rendering Use when raw LC-MS/MS feature tables (MS1/MS2 m/z pairs with intensities, e.g. from MS-DIAL output) must be converted into fixed-size grayscale images for image-based deep learning such as CNN bioactivity prediction. Input is already an aligned feature matrix or imaged spectra — the skill is for raw MS-DIAL-extracted m/z/intensity pairs, not tabular features destined for PCA/OPLS-DA/Random Forest A task requires structurally annotated or identified compounds — MS2toImg intentionally bypasses compound identification, so annotations are neither needed nor used Positive-ion-mode or adducts outside the selected set ([M-H]-, [M-H2O-H]-, [M+Na-2H]-, [M-K-2H]-, [M-FA-H]-) where the MS2>MS1 diagonal masking assumption and normalization scheme were validated http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Encodes LC-MS/MS precursor/product m/z and intensity data into a single-channel 2D grayscale scatter-plot image (MS1 m/z on x-axis, MS2 m/z on y-axis) with the physically impossible MS2>MS1 region masked to black, producing CNN-ready 'molecular fingerprint' images without feature alignment or annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Encodes LC-MS/MS precursor/product m/z and intensity data into a single-channel 2D grayscale scatter-plot image (MS1 m/z on x-axis, MS2 m/z on y-axis) with the physically impossible MS2>MS1 region masked to black, producing CNN-ready 'molecular fingerprint' images without feature alignment or annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature matrix or imaged spectra — the skill is for raw MS-DIAL-extracted m/z/intensity pairs, not tabular features destined for PCA/OPLS-DA/Random Forest A task requires structurally annotated or identified compounds — MS2toImg intentionally bypasses compound identification, so annotations are neither needed nor used Positive-ion-mode or adducts outside the selected set ([M-H]-, [M-H2O-H]-, [M+Na-2H]-, [M-K-2H]-, [M-FA-H]-) where the MS2>MS1 diagonal masking assumption and normalization scheme were validated

skills.description: Use when LC-MS mass traces (with apex positions and FWHM extents) must be aggregated into non-overlapping, isotope-grouped features, and the grouping must resolve competing hypotheses that share traces.
skills.name: greedy-non-overlapping-hypothesis-transfer
skills.search_text: greedy-non-overlapping-hypothesis-transfer Use when LC-MS mass traces (with apex positions and FWHM extents) must be aggregated into non-overlapping, isotope-grouped features, and the grouping must resolve competing hypotheses that share traces. Input is already a feature map or feature table — this skill operates on raw mass traces, not aggregated features Traces come from peptide/protein-centric feature detection rather than small-molecule metabolomics; the paper scopes the method to metabolites and a wide range of small molecules (e.g. lipidomics, peptidomics) rather than general protein feature detection A one-pass grouping is acceptable and overlapping multi-analyte hypotheses need not be resolved http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 This skill converts detected mass traces into metabolite features by enumerating isotope hypotheses of up to six mass traces, scoring them by m/z-spacing and co-elution criteria, filtering them with an SVM isotope-pattern classifier, and greedily accepting hypotheses in descending total-score order so each mass trace belongs to at most one feature. It is the feature-assembly core of FeatureFinderMetabo in OpenMS. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278
skills.summary: This skill converts detected mass traces into metabolite features by enumerating isotope hypotheses of up to six mass traces, scoring them by m/z-spacing and co-elution criteria, filtering them with an SVM isotope-pattern classifier, and greedily accepting hypotheses in descending total-score order so each mass trace belongs to at most one feature. It is the feature-assembly core of FeatureFinderMetabo in OpenMS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature map or feature table — this skill operates on raw mass traces, not aggregated features Traces come from peptide/protein-centric feature detection rather than small-molecule metabolomics; the paper scopes the method to metabolites and a wide range of small molecules (e.g. lipidomics, peptidomics) rather than general protein feature detection A one-pass grouping is acceptable and overlapping multi-analyte hypotheses need not be resolved

skills.description: Use when scoring a modified query spectrum against an unmodified library spectrum where the precursor mass difference implies fragment peak shifts and each peak must be counted at most once in the match.
skills.name: greedy-peak-match-selection
skills.search_text: greedy-peak-match-selection Use when scoring a modified query spectrum against an unmodified library spectrum where the precursor mass difference implies fragment peak shifts and each peak must be counted at most once in the match. Query and library spectra are expected to be unmodified, so no charge-normalized mass shift needs to be accounted for — the standard dot product suffices Spectra have not been preprocessed (noise peaks below 1% of the base peak still present, more than 50 peaks, or fewer than 10 peaks / mass range below 250 Da), violating the assumptions of the matching pass The task is candidate selection rather than candidate ranking — the ANN index, not the shifted dot product, is the appropriate stage for narrowing down library spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Scoring procedure within the shifted dot product that ranks all candidate unshifted and shifted peak pairs by intensity product and greedily sums the best matches while enforcing that no single peak in either the query or library spectrum is matched more than once. This yields a sensitive spectrum–spectrum match (SSM) score for modified query spectra against unmodified library counterparts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: Scoring procedure within the shifted dot product that ranks all candidate unshifted and shifted peak pairs by intensity product and greedily sums the best matches while enforcing that no single peak in either the query or library spectrum is matched more than once. This yields a sensitive spectrum–spectrum match (SSM) score for modified query spectra against unmodified library counterparts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query and library spectra are expected to be unmodified, so no charge-normalized mass shift needs to be accounted for — the standard dot product suffices Spectra have not been preprocessed (noise peaks below 1% of the base peak still present, more than 50 peaks, or fewer than 10 peaks / mass range below 250 Da), violating the assumptions of the matching pass The task is candidate selection rather than candidate ranking — the ANN index, not the shifted dot product, is the appropriate stage for narrowing down library spectra

skills.description: Use when a molecular network component contains multiple MS/MS spectra and you need to compute which peaks correspond across all of them, beyond pairwise matching.
skills.name: greedy-transitive-spectral-alignment
skills.search_text: greedy-transitive-spectral-alignment Use when a molecular network component contains multiple MS/MS spectra and you need to compute which peaks correspond across all of them, beyond pairwise matching. Input is a single pair of spectra — modified cosine alone suffices; MMSA is designed for alignment across multiple spectra in a component. Smaller peak alignments (e.g. y2 peaks in the albicidin family) are not fully captured by the greedy multiple alignment, so use a different method if every minor shared peak must be recovered. The analysis targets shifted peaks like the C12 HAA (m/z 239.162) or rhamnose-bound-C12 (m/z 385.219) that MMSA did not capture in the rhamnolipid case. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Builds a minimum spanning tree over MS/MS spectra weighted by modified cosine similarity and performs transitive, greedy alignment of peaks across all spectra in a molecular network component, identifying consensus peak sets. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Builds a minimum spanning tree over MS/MS spectra weighted by modified cosine similarity and performs transitive, greedy alignment of peaks across all spectra in a molecular network component, identifying consensus peak sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single pair of spectra — modified cosine alone suffices; MMSA is designed for alignment across multiple spectra in a component. Smaller peak alignments (e.g. y2 peaks in the albicidin family) are not fully captured by the greedy multiple alignment, so use a different method if every minor shared peak must be recovered. The analysis targets shifted peaks like the C12 HAA (m/z 239.162) or rhamnose-bound-C12 (m/z 385.219) that MMSA did not capture in the rhamnolipid case.

skills.description: Use when comparing survival or cumulative-event curves between risk groups (e.g., MetaboRS tertiles) and you need CI bands to judge whether group curves are statistically separated.
skills.name: greenwood-confidence-interval-computation
skills.search_text: greenwood-confidence-interval-computation Use when comparing survival or cumulative-event curves between risk groups (e.g., MetaboRS tertiles) and you need CI bands to judge whether group curves are statistically separated. You have only the fine-tuned model's probability column and no follow-up time or event labels — CI computation requires duration/event data Groups are not defined by MetaboRS tertiles or a comparable risk stratification with pre-specified cutoffs Input is raw metabolite abundance that still needs imputation and prediction via the metabolome-transformer pipeline before stratification http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes 95% confidence intervals around Kaplan-Meier cumulative event curves using the Greenwood variance formula, applied here to MetaboRS-derived risk tertiles (high >0.66, low <0.33) for 16 chronic diseases in the MetaboLM pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66163-3
skills.summary: Computes 95% confidence intervals around Kaplan-Meier cumulative event curves using the Greenwood variance formula, applied here to MetaboRS-derived risk tertiles (high >0.66, low <0.33) for 16 chronic diseases in the MetaboLM pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only the fine-tuned model's probability column and no follow-up time or event labels — CI computation requires duration/event data Groups are not defined by MetaboRS tertiles or a comparable risk stratification with pre-specified cutoffs Input is raw metabolite abundance that still needs imputation and prediction via the metabolome-transformer pipeline before stratification

skills.description: Use when aligning MRM/SRM chromatograms across samples: EIC peak tables show retention time shifts between acquisitions, and per-sample/per-transition-group drift values must be estimated to enable peak alignment and automatic EIC grouping.
skills.name: grid-search-gradient-descent-optimization
skills.search_text: grid-search-gradient-descent-optimization Use when aligning MRM/SRM chromatograms across samples: EIC peak tables show retention time shifts between acquisitions, and per-sample/per-transition-group drift values must be estimated to enable peak alignment and automatic EIC grouping. Input is already an aligned feature table or a peak-picked matrix with no raw EIC traces — there are no continuous chromatograms to shift and score Data are DDA/DIA (untargeted) spectra rather than MRM EICs, where no per-transition-group reference chromatogram can be defined A quantitative comparison of analysis software output is needed — MRMPro's authors note it 'relies on classical algorithms', and advanced peak-extraction algorithms are only planned future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A two-stage 1-D optimization scheme from MRMPro (BMC Bioinformatics, 2024) that estimates retention time (RT) drifts between MRM samples by first coarsely scanning candidate RT shifts with grid search, then refining the optimum via gradient descent, both maximizing the cosine similarity between a sample's extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) and a reference EIC. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05685-x
skills.summary: A two-stage 1-D optimization scheme from MRMPro (BMC Bioinformatics, 2024) that estimates retention time (RT) drifts between MRM samples by first coarsely scanning candidate RT shifts with grid search, then refining the optimum via gradient descent, both maximizing the cosine similarity between a sample's extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) and a reference EIC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table or a peak-picked matrix with no raw EIC traces — there are no continuous chromatograms to shift and score Data are DDA/DIA (untargeted) spectra rather than MRM EICs, where no per-transition-group reference chromatogram can be defined A quantitative comparison of analysis software output is needed — MRMPro's authors note it 'relies on classical algorithms', and advanced peak-extraction algorithms are only planned future work

skills.description: Use when tuning or validating the A, B, C weight parameters of the metabCombiner similarity-scoring function for LC-HRMS feature alignment, and you have a training set of shared identified compounds with known true pairings.
skills.name: grid-search-weight-region-verification
skills.search_text: grid-search-weight-region-verification Use when tuning or validating the A, B, C weight parameters of the metabCombiner similarity-scoring function for LC-HRMS feature alignment, and you have a training set of shared identified compounds with known true pairings. Input datasets were acquired with disparate chromatographic techniques (e.g. RPLC vs HILIC), where elution order is not preserved and weight tuning cannot compensate. No shared identified compounds exist between the two datasets, so no 'true pairing' labels are available to define the separation objective. Abundance values have been normalized or transformed in a way that removes ranked abundance order information, breaking the abundance-similarity term of the scoring function. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstruct the metabCombiner evaluateParams() procedure by sweeping a grid of feature-pair-alignment scoring weights (A, B, C) on the package's paired human plasma datasets (plasma20/plasma30), maximizing the positive score separation between true FPAs of shared identified compounds and their misaligned pairings. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03693
skills.summary: Reconstruct the metabCombiner evaluateParams() procedure by sweeping a grid of feature-pair-alignment scoring weights (A, B, C) on the package's paired human plasma datasets (plasma20/plasma30), maximizing the positive score separation between true FPAs of shared identified compounds and their misaligned pairings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input datasets were acquired with disparate chromatographic techniques (e.g. RPLC vs HILIC), where elution order is not preserved and weight tuning cannot compensate. No shared identified compounds exist between the two datasets, so no 'true pairing' labels are available to define the separation objective. Abundance values have been normalized or transformed in a way that removes ranked abundance order information, breaking the abundance-similarity term of the scoring function.

skills.description: Use when a 3D NMR dataset is non-uniformly sampled (e.g. an NUScon schedule such as 8.8% sampling) and the unmeasured hypercomplex points must be reconstructed before spectral inspection in NMRViewJ.
skills.name: grins-nus-reconstruction
skills.search_text: grins-nus-reconstruction Use when a 3D NMR dataset is non-uniformly sampled (e.g. an NUScon schedule such as 8.8% sampling) and the unmeasured hypercomplex points must be reconstructed before spectral inspection in NMRViewJ. The dataset is uniformly sampled — no unmeasured hypercomplex points exist, so standard apodization/zero-fill/Fourier transform in NMRFx Processor suffices You need a quantitatively scored reconstruction quality metric; the paper reports only expert qualitative comparison against Fig. 1 with no quantitative metric Reconstruct non-uniformly sampled (NUS) multidimensional NMR spectra with the GRINS algorithm inside NMRFx Processor's Python-driven processing pipeline, reproducing the NUScon Protein A HNCACB spectrum from the NMRFx paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-025-01812-8
skills.summary: Reconstruct non-uniformly sampled (NUS) multidimensional NMR spectra with the GRINS algorithm inside NMRFx Processor's Python-driven processing pipeline, reproducing the NUScon Protein A HNCACB spectrum from the NMRFx paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is uniformly sampled — no unmeasured hypercomplex points exist, so standard apodization/zero-fill/Fourier transform in NMRFx Processor suffices You need a quantitatively scored reconstruction quality metric; the paper reports only expert qualitative comparison against Fig. 1 with no quantitative metric

skills.description: Use when benchmarking feature-correspondence or RT-alignment tools and you need ground truth: simulated perturbed datasets with known feature mappings let you compute precision/recall per shift magnitude.
skills.name: ground-truth-correspondence-matching
skills.search_text: ground-truth-correspondence-matching Use when benchmarking feature-correspondence or RT-alignment tools and you need ground truth: simulated perturbed datasets with known feature mappings let you compute precision/recall per shift magnitude. You have no ground truth or cannot simulate perturbations — real-world alignment evaluation without known correspondences cannot yield precision/recall Your goal is quantitative accuracy assessment rather than correspondence correctness — the article notes alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction Input is raw spectra rather than extracted feature lists — DeepRTAlign requires feature extraction to have been run first http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Evaluate LC-MS feature alignment tools (e.g., DeepRTAlign vs OpenMS) by simulating known retention time shifts with numpy to create ground-truth correspondences, then computing precision and recall per RT-shift sigma level to delineate generalizability boundaries. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Evaluate LC-MS feature alignment tools (e.g., DeepRTAlign vs OpenMS) by simulating known retention time shifts with numpy to create ground-truth correspondences, then computing precision and recall per RT-shift sigma level to delineate generalizability boundaries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no ground truth or cannot simulate perturbations — real-world alignment evaluation without known correspondences cannot yield precision/recall Your goal is quantitative accuracy assessment rather than correspondence correctness — the article notes alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction Input is raw spectra rather than extracted feature lists — DeepRTAlign requires feature extraction to have been run first

skills.description: Use when you have an LC-MS feature-detection result on simulated data whose ground truth is known (e.g. from MSSimulator) and you need recall/precision/F-score per noise setting.
skills.name: ground-truth-feature-matching
skills.search_text: ground-truth-feature-matching Use when you have an LC-MS feature-detection result on simulated data whose ground truth is known (e.g. from MSSimulator) and you need recall/precision/F-score per noise setting. Input data is real experimental LC-MS (no ground truth exists), so precision/recall against truth cannot be computed — use spike-in or replicate-based validation instead. Input is already a scored feature table; only the plotting/rendering step applies. Data comes from a proteomics or other large-molecule workflow outside the small-molecule/metabolite scope of FeatureFinderMetabo's isotope-pattern SVM. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Match features detected from synthetic LC-MS maps against the ground-truth feature list generated by MSSimulator and compute recall, precision, and F-score per noise regime. This is the benchmarking core used to quantify FeatureFinderMetabo's robustness to detector noise, mass error, and chromatographic distortion. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278
skills.summary: Match features detected from synthetic LC-MS maps against the ground-truth feature list generated by MSSimulator and compute recall, precision, and F-score per noise regime. This is the benchmarking core used to quantify FeatureFinderMetabo's robustness to detector noise, mass error, and chromatographic distortion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is real experimental LC-MS (no ground truth exists), so precision/recall against truth cannot be computed — use spike-in or replicate-based validation instead. Data comes from a proteomics or other large-molecule workflow outside the small-molecule/metabolite scope of FeatureFinderMetabo's isotope-pattern SVM.

skills.description: Use when you have SIRIUS/ZODIAC annotation results plus a ground-truth formula file (spectral library search + manual validation) and need per-dataset accuracy, incorrect-annotation rates, or error-reduction factors.
skills.name: ground-truth-formula-matching
skills.search_text: ground-truth-formula-matching Use when you have SIRIUS/ZODIAC annotation results plus a ground-truth formula file (spectral library search + manual validation) and need per-dataset accuracy, incorrect-annotation rates, or error-reduction factors. Annotating a single query spectrum de novo without a validated ground truth — this skill evaluates annotation quality, it does not produce new formula assignments Datasets whose compounds lack spectral library hits or manual validation, so no trusted ground-truth formulas can be established for matching Structure-level (CSI:FingerID) identification benchmarking — this skill operates only at the molecular formula level Benchmarking skill for molecular formula annotation: match top-ranked formulas assigned by SIRIUS (candidate enumeration) and ZODIAC (Gibbs-sampling reranking of the top 50 SIRIUS candidates) against a manually validated ground truth across the dendroides, NIST1950, tomato, diatoms and mice stool LC-MS/MS datasets, then compute per-dataset accuracy and error rates. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for molecular formula annotation: match top-ranked formulas assigned by SIRIUS (candidate enumeration) and ZODIAC (Gibbs-sampling reranking of the top 50 SIRIUS candidates) against a manually validated ground truth across the dendroides, NIST1950, tomato, diatoms and mice stool LC-MS/MS datasets, then compute per-dataset accuracy and error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotating a single query spectrum de novo without a validated ground truth — this skill evaluates annotation quality, it does not produce new formula assignments Datasets whose compounds lack spectral library hits or manual validation, so no trusted ground-truth formulas can be established for matching Structure-level (CSI:FingerID) identification benchmarking — this skill operates only at the molecular formula level

skills.description: Use when building labeled synthetic benchmark data for signal-vs-noise classification on mass spectrometry raw data, especially when no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real timsTOF data is available.
skills.name: ground-truth-peak-labeling
skills.search_text: ground-truth-peak-labeling Use when building labeled synthetic benchmark data for signal-vs-noise classification on mass spectrometry raw data, especially when no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real timsTOF data is available. Input is real timsTOF/TDF raw data with no peak-level ground truth — the article notes no gold-standard peak-level annotation exists, and vendor-selected DDA peaks (N=6902) are a biased reference of likely high-intensity fragmented peptides. Goal is to model self-similar chemical noise: the paper notes chemical noise is self-similar and would be classified as 'true' signal, which the synthetic signal/noise_1/noise_2 labeling scheme does not capture. Output is already a labeled feature/peak table — re-labeling synthetic peaks adds nothing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generates synthetic timsTOF-like MS windows with per-peak ground-truth labels (signal, noise_1, noise_2) so that peak-level classification methods, e.g. LSH vs. intensity thresholding, can be evaluated by ROC analysis without real-data gold standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-022-04833-5
skills.summary: Generates synthetic timsTOF-like MS windows with per-peak ground-truth labels (signal, noise_1, noise_2) so that peak-level classification methods, e.g. LSH vs. intensity thresholding, can be evaluated by ROC analysis without real-data gold standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real timsTOF/TDF raw data with no peak-level ground truth — the article notes no gold-standard peak-level annotation exists, and vendor-selected DDA peaks (N=6902) are a biased reference of likely high-intensity fragmented peptides. Goal is to model self-similar chemical noise: the paper notes chemical noise is self-similar and would be classified as 'true' signal, which the synthetic signal/noise_1/noise_2 labeling scheme does not capture. Output is already a labeled feature/peak table — re-labeling synthetic peaks adds nothing.

skills.description: Use when evaluating chromatographic peak quality metrics on LC/MS data and no curated reference peak set exists, so a consensus-based ground truth must be derived from multiple independent peak-detection tools before computing TP/Recall/Precision/F-Score.
skills.name: ground-truth-peak-matching
skills.search_text: ground-truth-peak-matching Use when evaluating chromatographic peak quality metrics on LC/MS data and no curated reference peak set exists, so a consensus-based ground truth must be derived from multiple independent peak-detection tools before computing TP/Recall/Precision/F-Score. A curated ground truth or manually validated peak list already exists — consensus of three detectors is only a proxy when no curated reference is available The task is EIC quality evaluation (e.g., MCQ index or global zigzag index scoring of extracted ion chromatograms) rather than detected chromatographic peak quality evaluation Evaluating tools whose peak lists feed the consensus itself (XCMS/MZmine/MAVEN) against this ground truth — circularity invalidates the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Establishes a ground truth chromatographic peak list by taking the consensus of peaks detected by at least two of XCMS, MZmine, and MAVEN on the same LC/MS metabolomics dataset, then matches candidate peaks against it (0.05 Da m/z tolerance, 5 s retention-time tolerance) to compute Recall, Precision, and F-Score for peak quality metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Establishes a ground truth chromatographic peak list by taking the consensus of peaks detected by at least two of XCMS, MZmine, and MAVEN on the same LC/MS metabolomics dataset, then matches candidate peaks against it (0.05 Da m/z tolerance, 5 s retention-time tolerance) to compute Recall, Precision, and F-Score for peak quality metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A curated ground truth or manually validated peak list already exists — consensus of three detectors is only a proxy when no curated reference is available The task is EIC quality evaluation (e.g., MCQ index or global zigzag index scoring of extracted ion chromatograms) rather than detected chromatographic peak quality evaluation Evaluating tools whose peak lists feed the consensus itself (XCMS/MZmine/MAVEN) against this ground truth — circularity invalidates the comparison

skills.description: Use when complete source datasets are available and a controlled imputation benchmark is needed — create MCAR-masked replicates at fixed missingness fractions, retaining the complete matrix as the error-assessment reference.
skills.name: ground-truth-preservation-for-imputation-error-assessment
skills.search_text: ground-truth-preservation-for-imputation-error-assessment Use when complete source datasets are available and a controlled imputation benchmark is needed — create MCAR-masked replicates at fixed missingness fractions, retaining the complete matrix as the error-assessment reference. The source data already contains real (non-artificial) missing values, so no complete ground-truth matrix exists for NRMSE/PFC computation — as in the Children's Hospital data where observations with missing values had to be removed first The missingness mechanism of interest is not MCAR (the simulations remove values completely at random, so MAR/MNAR scenarios are out of scope) The matrix to be masked is high-dimensional such that the replicate budget is infeasible — the article reduced insulin simulations from 50 to 10 due to computation time http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate artificially masked versions of complete reference datasets (MCAR removal of 10%, 20% or 30% of entries) while preserving the untouched complete matrix as ground truth, so that imputation error can later be quantified with NRMSE (continuous) and PFC (categorical) metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btr597
skills.summary: Generate artificially masked versions of complete reference datasets (MCAR removal of 10%, 20% or 30% of entries) while preserving the untouched complete matrix as ground truth, so that imputation error can later be quantified with NRMSE (continuous) and PFC (categorical) metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source data already contains real (non-artificial) missing values, so no complete ground-truth matrix exists for NRMSE/PFC computation — as in the Children's Hospital data where observations with missing values had to be removed first The missingness mechanism of interest is not MCAR (the simulations remove values completely at random, so MAR/MNAR scenarios are out of scope) The matrix to be masked is high-dimensional such that the replicate budget is infeasible — the article reduced insulin simulations from 50 to 10 due to computation time

skills.description: Use when preparing a user-defined ground-truth reference feature list (peaks, walls, backgrounds) for training a PeakBot CNN model on LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms, and you need accurate RT/mz/borders/mz-deviation values matched to real chromatographic peaks.
skills.name: ground-truth-reference-peak-extraction
skills.search_text: ground-truth-reference-peak-extraction Use when preparing a user-defined ground-truth reference feature list (peaks, walls, backgrounds) for training a PeakBot CNN model on LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms, and you need accurate RT/mz/borders/mz-deviation values matched to real chromatographic peaks. The data is not profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms (e.g. already centroided feature tables or other data types). Co-eluting compounds (isomers) are present in the reference chromatograms, which PeakBot cannot disentangle during gradient-descend matching. Peak-picking has already been done and the ground-truth list only needs to be consumed, not refined. Extract ground-truth reference features for PeakBot's CNN peak-picking training by pre-detecting chromatographic peaks with a smoothing and gradient-descend algorithm, matching them to a user-defined reference list, and extending the list with isotopologs of the same compound. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Extract ground-truth reference features for PeakBot's CNN peak-picking training by pre-detecting chromatographic peaks with a smoothing and gradient-descend algorithm, matching them to a user-defined reference list, and extending the list with isotopologs of the same compound.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is not profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms (e.g. already centroided feature tables or other data types). Co-eluting compounds (isomers) are present in the reference chromatograms, which PeakBot cannot disentangle during gradient-descend matching. Peak-picking has already been done and the ground-truth list only needs to be consumed, not refined.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS denoising or spectral-matching methods on dilution-series data where clean high-concentration reference spectra of the same compounds serve as ground truth.
skills.name: ground-truth-referenced-spectral-similarity-evaluation
skills.search_text: ground-truth-referenced-spectral-similarity-evaluation Use when benchmarking MS/MS denoising or spectral-matching methods on dilution-series data where clean high-concentration reference spectra of the same compounds serve as ground truth. No ground-truth or high-concentration reference spectra exist for the compounds, so similarity cannot be anchored to known-clean spectra The goal is de novo annotation of unknowns rather than method benchmarking — use Denoising Search against a reference library instead Compounds fail the fragmentation prerequisite (fewer than two fragment ions, spectral entropy <0.5) and cannot be scored meaningfully http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Evaluate MS/MS denoising quality by computing entropy similarity between processed low-concentration spectra and 500-pmol high-concentration ground-truth spectra of the same compounds, then determining the lowest injected quantity reaching entropy similarity >0.75 per compound. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Evaluate MS/MS denoising quality by computing entropy similarity between processed low-concentration spectra and 500-pmol high-concentration ground-truth spectra of the same compounds, then determining the lowest injected quantity reaching entropy similarity >0.75 per compound.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth or high-concentration reference spectra exist for the compounds, so similarity cannot be anchored to known-clean spectra The goal is de novo annotation of unknowns rather than method benchmarking — use Denoising Search against a reference library instead Compounds fail the fragmentation prerequisite (fewer than two fragment ions, spectral entropy <0.5) and cannot be scored meaningfully

skills.description: Use when NPOmix (or another co-occurrence classifier) has produced candidate GCF–MS/MS spectrum links and you need a quantified precision estimate against PoDP validated gene–metabolite links as ground truth.
skills.name: ground-truth-validation-against-podp-links
skills.search_text: ground-truth-validation-against-podp-links Use when NPOmix (or another co-occurrence classifier) has produced candidate GCF–MS/MS spectrum links and you need a quantified precision estimate against PoDP validated gene–metabolite links as ground truth. The candidate set contains no experimentally validated links (e.g. cryptic metabolites absent from GNPS and PoDP) — precision cannot be scored, only structure elucidation can confirm them Query organism has no BGC similar to the NPOmix/PoDP training set (e.g. a fungal species with novel BGCs), which produces no answer to validate The goal is distinguishing isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — NPOmix correlation-based links lack that resolution even when validated http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Scores NPOmix KNN candidate BGC–MS/MS links against expert-validated gene–metabolite links from the Paired Omics Data Platform (PoDP), computing top-1 and top-10 precision with and without the Jaccard co-occurrence threshold of 0.7. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Scores NPOmix KNN candidate BGC–MS/MS links against expert-validated gene–metabolite links from the Paired Omics Data Platform (PoDP), computing top-1 and top-10 precision with and without the Jaccard co-occurrence threshold of 0.7.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate set contains no experimentally validated links (e.g. cryptic metabolites absent from GNPS and PoDP) — precision cannot be scored, only structure elucidation can confirm them Query organism has no BGC similar to the NPOmix/PoDP training set (e.g. a fungal species with novel BGCs), which produces no answer to validate The goal is distinguishing isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — NPOmix correlation-based links lack that resolution even when validated

skills.description: Use when comparing a continuous measurement (e.g., metabolite concentration in µg/g tissue) between two small, independent biological subgroups (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-low n=14 vs. phosphoAKT1-low/MYC-high n=5) without assuming normality.
skills.name: group-comparison-statistics
skills.search_text: group-comparison-statistics Use when comparing a continuous measurement (e.g., metabolite concentration in µg/g tissue) between two small, independent biological subgroups (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-low n=14 vs. phosphoAKT1-low/MYC-high n=5) without assuming normality. When the data are high-dimensional expression or spectral intensities from the untargeted screen (hundreds of features) where a multivariate GSEA or k-means clustering approach is more appropriate When the comparison involves more than two groups or requires correction for multiple testing across all metabolites simultaneously without prior biological selection http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies non-parametric hypothesis testing to compare metabolite concentrations between molecularly defined tumor subgroups, as used in the Priolo et al. 2014 study to validate untargeted metabolomics findings with absolute quantitation. metabolomics/v3 10.1158/0008-5472.can-14-1490
skills.summary: Applies non-parametric hypothesis testing to compare metabolite concentrations between molecularly defined tumor subgroups, as used in the Priolo et al. 2014 study to validate untargeted metabolomics findings with absolute quantitation.

skills.description: Use when a benchmark dataset with controlled two-group structure and realistic inter-variable covariance is needed to evaluate imputation methods on metabolomics data (e.g., MNAR left-censored missingness tests).
skills.name: group-difference-simulation
skills.search_text: group-difference-simulation Use when a benchmark dataset with controlled two-group structure and realistic inter-variable covariance is needed to evaluate imputation methods on metabolomics data (e.g., MNAR left-censored missingness tests). The input is real-world measured metabolomics data (e.g., the FFA/BA targeted datasets) that already contains the group structure to be analyzed rather than synthetic benchmark data The goal is to generate MNAR missingness for evaluation — that is a separate step (e.g., MNAR_gen_imp) applied after the complete simulated matrix exists The goal is missing value imputation itself rather than constructing the ground-truth complete dataset on which imputation methods will be compared http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Generates a synthetic two-group metabolomics benchmark by simulating 80x76 data matrices from a multivariate normal with covariance estimated from the real diabetes dataset (P=76 FFAs/BAs), then stacking two groups to preserve covariance and group differences for imputation-method evaluation. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Generates a synthetic two-group metabolomics benchmark by simulating 80x76 data matrices from a multivariate normal with covariance estimated from the real diabetes dataset (P=76 FFAs/BAs), then stacking two groups to preserve covariance and group differences for imputation-method evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real-world measured metabolomics data (e.g., the FFA/BA targeted datasets) that already contains the group structure to be analyzed rather than synthetic benchmark data The goal is to generate MNAR missingness for evaluation — that is a separate step (e.g., MNAR_gen_imp) applied after the complete simulated matrix exists The goal is missing value imputation itself rather than constructing the ground-truth complete dataset on which imputation methods will be compared

skills.description: Use when KEGG pathway abundance profiles must be compared between genotype groups (e.g. 3xTg vs WT fecal metagenomes) to identify and visualize enriched vs depleted pathways with effect direction and significance.
skills.name: group-difference-visualization
skills.search_text: group-difference-visualization Use when KEGG pathway abundance profiles must be compared between genotype groups (e.g. 3xTg vs WT fecal metagenomes) to identify and visualize enriched vs depleted pathways with effect direction and significance. The question concerns species-level taxonomic differences (e.g. Akkermansia muciniphila depletion, Mucispirillum schaedleri enrichment) rather than functional pathway contrasts — use species-level ANCOM-BC2 directly instead Input data are untargeted metabolomics features (carnitines, bile acids, B vitamins) rather than metagenomic functional profiles Samples come from the Longitudinal fecal cohort, where samples were collected randomly per cage without animal IDs, preventing single-animal genotype-paired testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Summarizes and visualizes differential KEGG pathway abundance between experimental groups — here 3xTg vs WT Sacrifice-cohort fecal metagenomes — producing an enriched/depleted summary table (Figure 5E-style) with effect direction and significance per pathway. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Summarizes and visualizes differential KEGG pathway abundance between experimental groups — here 3xTg vs WT Sacrifice-cohort fecal metagenomes — producing an enriched/depleted summary table (Figure 5E-style) with effect direction and significance per pathway.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns species-level taxonomic differences (e.g. Akkermansia muciniphila depletion, Mucispirillum schaedleri enrichment) rather than functional pathway contrasts — use species-level ANCOM-BC2 directly instead Input data are untargeted metabolomics features (carnitines, bile acids, B vitamins) rather than metagenomic functional profiles Samples come from the Longitudinal fecal cohort, where samples were collected randomly per cage without animal IDs, preventing single-animal genotype-paired testing

skills.description: Use when comparing missing-value imputation methods on metabolomics data with known two-group labels, and you need label-informed metrics (t-test p-value correlation, PLS-Procrustes SSE) rather than only reconstruction error.
skills.name: group-label-informed-metabolomics-statistics
skills.search_text: group-label-informed-metabolomics-statistics Use when comparing missing-value imputation methods on metabolomics data with known two-group labels, and you need label-informed metrics (t-test p-value correlation, PLS-Procrustes SSE) rather than only reconstruction error. The missingness mechanism is MCAR/MAR (e.g., post-missing-retrieval untargeted GC/MS data) rather than MNAR left-censoring from LOD/LOQ — the paper's labeled evaluation targets MNAR-degraded targeted metabolomics data You have no group labels or outcome variable — the t-test and supervised PLS-DA evaluation both require two-group labels (rep(c(0,1), each=80)) You only need raw imputation accuracy (e.g., SOR) without judging preservation of univariate or multivariate group-difference statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A supervised evaluation framework that judges imputation quality by whether group-difference signal is preserved: per-variable two-sample t-test p-value correlation and PLS-DA ordination compared by Procrustes sum of squared errors between imputed and original data. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: A supervised evaluation framework that judges imputation quality by whether group-difference signal is preserved: per-variable two-sample t-test p-value correlation and PLS-DA ordination compared by Procrustes sum of squared errors between imputed and original data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The missingness mechanism is MCAR/MAR (e.g., post-missing-retrieval untargeted GC/MS data) rather than MNAR left-censoring from LOD/LOQ — the paper's labeled evaluation targets MNAR-degraded targeted metabolomics data You have no group labels or outcome variable — the t-test and supervised PLS-DA evaluation both require two-group labels (rep(c(0,1), each=80)) You only need raw imputation accuracy (e.g., SOR) without judging preservation of univariate or multivariate group-difference statistics

skills.description: Use when the input is a metabolite intensity matrix (samples × metabolites, e.g., 234 samples × 113 metabolites) with sample-group labels and the goal is to select the subset of metabolites predictive of the phenotype.
skills.name: group-labeled-supervised-feature-screening
skills.search_text: group-labeled-supervised-feature-screening Use when the input is a metabolite intensity matrix (samples × metabolites, e.g., 234 samples × 113 metabolites) with sample-group labels and the goal is to select the subset of metabolites predictive of the phenotype. Raw spectral data preprocessing or peak picking and annotation are needed — iMAP deliberately did not implement raw data preprocessing and peak picking and annotation modules considering the risk of data security The data have no phenotype group labels, so no supervised target exists for Boruta's shadow-feature importance comparison The goal is unsupervised statistical metabolites-selection (e.g., differential abundance testing) rather than feature selection against class labels in the predictive-model module http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies supervised feature selection (e.g., the Boruta algorithm on iMAP's backend R scripts) to a metabolite intensity matrix using sample group labels (e.g., 66 colorectal cancer patients, 76 polyp patients, 92 healthy controls) to identify confirmed marker metabolites such as the 39-metabolite CRC serum signature including adipate and 3-methyladipate/pimelate. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: Applies supervised feature selection (e.g., the Boruta algorithm on iMAP's backend R scripts) to a metabolite intensity matrix using sample group labels (e.g., 66 colorectal cancer patients, 76 polyp patients, 92 healthy controls) to identify confirmed marker metabolites such as the 39-metabolite CRC serum signature including adipate and 3-methyladipate/pimelate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw spectral data preprocessing or peak picking and annotation are needed — iMAP deliberately did not implement raw data preprocessing and peak picking and annotation modules considering the risk of data security The data have no phenotype group labels, so no supervised target exists for Boruta's shadow-feature importance comparison The goal is unsupervised statistical metabolites-selection (e.g., differential abundance testing) rather than feature selection against class labels in the predictive-model module

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table with two or more phenotype groups needs binary discrimination models per group pair (e.g. CRC vs polyp vs healthy controls) using pre-selected metabolite features.
skills.name: group-pair-discrimination-modeling
skills.search_text: group-pair-discrimination-modeling Use when a metabolomics feature table with two or more phenotype groups needs binary discrimination models per group pair (e.g. CRC vs polyp vs healthy controls) using pre-selected metabolite features. Raw spectral data requiring peak picking and annotation — iMAP deliberately does not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking/annotation modules Only a single phenotype group is present — binary group-pair discrimination requires at least two labeled groups The goal is unsupervised metabolite selection or correlation-based network construction rather than supervised classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds binary predictive classifiers (e.g. random forest) that discriminate between pairs of phenotype groups using selected metabolites, reporting out-of-bag (OOB) error rates per group pair. iMAP automates this pipeline from train-test separation through model construction and validation. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: Builds binary predictive classifiers (e.g. random forest) that discriminate between pairs of phenotype groups using selected metabolites, reporting out-of-bag (OOB) error rates per group pair. iMAP automates this pipeline from train-test separation through model construction and validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw spectral data requiring peak picking and annotation — iMAP deliberately does not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking/annotation modules Only a single phenotype group is present — binary group-pair discrimination requires at least two labeled groups The goal is unsupervised metabolite selection or correlation-based network construction rather than supervised classification

skills.description: Use when you have a superclass-by-organism relative abundance table from ConCISE consensus annotations and need a grouped bar chart to visually compare chemical-class composition across exudate source organisms.
skills.name: grouped-bar-abundance-visualization
skills.search_text: grouped-bar-abundance-visualization Use when you have a superclass-by-organism relative abundance table from ConCISE consensus annotations and need a grouped bar chart to visually compare chemical-class composition across exudate source organisms. The annotation output has not been aggregated to superclass-level relative abundances per organism (e.g., you only have raw per-feature annotations or class/subclass-level tables). The analysis target is a single organism or sample set with no grouping variable to compare across bar groups. You need statistical testing of class-level compositional differences rather than a descriptive visualization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Renders superclass-level ChemOnt relative abundances per organism (e.g., coral vs turfing-algal exudates from MSV000082083) as a grouped bar chart in matplotlib, after ConCISE consensus annotation, to expose compositional differences like organic acids enriched in corals and organoheterocyclic compounds enriched in turf algae. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: Renders superclass-level ChemOnt relative abundances per organism (e.g., coral vs turfing-algal exudates from MSV000082083) as a grouped bar chart in matplotlib, after ConCISE consensus annotation, to expose compositional differences like organic acids enriched in corals and organoheterocyclic compounds enriched in turf algae.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation output has not been aggregated to superclass-level relative abundances per organism (e.g., you only have raw per-feature annotations or class/subclass-level tables). The analysis target is a single organism or sample set with no grouping variable to compare across bar groups. You need statistical testing of class-level compositional differences rather than a descriptive visualization.

skills.description: Use when per-dataset fraction values for several adduct classes (Na+, K+, 13C, DHB or CHCA matrix adducts) must be assembled across multiple MALDI-MSI datasets and rendered as a grouped bar chart to compare platforms.
skills.name: grouped-barchart-reproduction-from-fraction-tables
skills.search_text: grouped-barchart-reproduction-from-fraction-tables Use when per-dataset fraction values for several adduct classes (Na+, K+, 13C, DHB or CHCA matrix adducts) must be assembled across multiple MALDI-MSI datasets and rendered as a grouped bar chart to compare platforms. Input is already a polished Figure 3 image or pre-computed fraction table with no per-dataset counts to reaggregate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assembles per-dataset adduct-fraction counts (e.g. Na+, K+, 13C, [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+, [M + CHCA + Na]+) into a grouped bar chart that reproduces Figure 3 of Janda et al. 2021, contrasting atmospheric-pressure (~31% adduct-driven peaks) vs high-vacuum (~6%) MALDI-MSI platforms. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: Assembles per-dataset adduct-fraction counts (e.g. Na+, K+, 13C, [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+, [M + CHCA + Na]+) into a grouped bar chart that reproduces Figure 3 of Janda et al. 2021, contrasting atmospheric-pressure (~31% adduct-driven peaks) vs high-vacuum (~6%) MALDI-MSI platforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is raw discovery of adduct pairs rather than re-summarizing already-computed fractions — use massdiff/adductMatch/corrPairsMSI directly instead. skills.description: Use when FT-ICR MS peak tables with assigned molecular formulas have per-sample abundance-based diversity (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1) and functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy) values that must be compared across user-defined sample groups.
skills.name: grouped-boxplot-visualization-of-diversity-metrics
skills.search_text: grouped-boxplot-visualization-of-diversity-metrics Use when FT-ICR MS peak tables with assigned molecular formulas have per-sample abundance-based diversity (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1) and functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy) values that must be compared across user-defined sample groups. The input is raw, unprocessed FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must be performed before using MetaboDirect The goal is multivariate statistics, Van Krevelen diagrams, elemental/molecular class composition plots, or mass-difference transformation networks rather than chemodiversity index comparison across groups Peak abundances have not been normalized (the test_normalization/SPANS companion script should first be used to select the best normalization method) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Visualizes per-sample chemodiversity indices (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1, Rao's Q) as box plots grouped by user-defined grouping variables (e.g., phage treatment, incubation condition), as implemented in MetaboDirect's chemodiversity analysis step for FT-ICR MS metabolomic data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Visualizes per-sample chemodiversity indices (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1, Rao's Q) as box plots grouped by user-defined grouping variables (e.g., phage treatment, incubation condition), as implemented in MetaboDirect's chemodiversity analysis step for FT-ICR MS metabolomic data.

skills.description: Decision support for validating that an LC/MS feature-grouping or compound-spectrum extraction step correctly co-assigns features from known standards before trusting it on unlabeled samples.
skills.name: grouping-accuracy-evaluation-against-standard-mixture
skills.search_text: grouping-accuracy-evaluation-against-standard-mixture Decision support for validating that an LC/MS feature-grouping or compound-spectrum extraction step correctly co-assigns features from known standards before trusting it on unlabeled samples. The input is raw spectra or an unprocessed peak list that has not yet been feature-detected and aligned by XCMS — grouping evaluation presupposes an existing feature table. The sample is an unlabeled biological extract with no reference compound identities, so no ground-truth grouping exists to compare against. The goal is to evaluate adduct/isotope annotation rules rather than the co-elution grouping itself; use CAMERA's rule-table annotation checks instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluates how faithfully an LC/MS feature-grouping algorithm (e.g. CAMERA's groupFWHM) reconstructs compound spectra by comparing its group assignments against a reference mixture of known compounds, such as the 39-compound MM39 standard spanning 161–822 Da used in the CAMERA paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Evaluates how faithfully an LC/MS feature-grouping algorithm (e.g. CAMERA's groupFWHM) reconstructs compound spectra by comparing its group assignments against a reference mixture of known compounds, such as the 39-compound MM39 standard spanning 161–822 Da used in the CAMERA paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw spectra or an unprocessed peak list that has not yet been feature-detected and aligned by XCMS — grouping evaluation presupposes an existing feature table. The sample is an unlabeled biological extract with no reference compound identities, so no ground-truth grouping exists to compare against. The goal is to evaluate adduct/isotope annotation rules rather than the co-elution grouping itself; use CAMERA's rule-table annotation checks instead.

The network has not yet been reconstructed — metrics on a partial draft without orthology mapping or gap-filling are not comparable to curated GSMNs The goal is pathway-level inference of new reactions or metabolite structures (use PathModel-type reasoning instead of size metric reporting) http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Compute and report the global quality metrics of a reconstructed genome-scale metabolic network (GSMN) — number of reactions, metabolites/enzymes, genes, and pathways — and benchmark them against published GSMNs of related organisms, as done for the C. crispus network versus E. siliculosus. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100849

skills.when_to_use_negative: The network has not yet been reconstructed — metrics on a partial draft without orthology mapping or gap-filling are not comparable to curated GSMNs The goal is pathway-level inference of new reactions or metabolite structures (use PathModel-type reasoning instead of size metric reporting)

skills.description: Use when you need human-expression-variability-normalized effect sizes for cross-species DE comparisons, e.g. dividing exercise log2FCs by GTEx per-gene, per-tissue standard deviations.
skills.name: gtex-expression-covariate-residualization
skills.search_text: gtex-expression-covariate-residualization Use when you need human-expression-variability-normalized effect sizes for cross-species DE comparisons, e.g. dividing exercise log2FCs by GTEx per-gene, per-tissue standard deviations. Your analysis uses the default GTEx inverse-normal-transformed expression values and does not require variance-standardized (SD-unit) effect sizes The gene x tissue pair fails the IHW alpha = 0.10 heritability significance filter, so its SDgeno estimate is not confidently heritable You need qualitative sex-specific exercise responses rather than sex-consistent standardized effect sizes (the article notes sex-specificity 'fell outside the scope considered here') http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reprocess GTEx v8 expression by replacing the pipeline's default inverse-normal transform with a pseudolog (log2(x+1)) transform and residualizing sex, genotyping PCs, sequencing platform/protocol, and PEER factors, so that exercise log2FCs from MoTrPAC rat training can be expressed as standardized effect sizes in units of human phenotypic (SDpheno) and genetic (SDgeno) expression variability. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Reprocess GTEx v8 expression by replacing the pipeline's default inverse-normal transform with a pseudolog (log2(x+1)) transform and residualizing sex, genotyping PCs, sequencing platform/protocol, and PEER factors, so that exercise log2FCs from MoTrPAC rat training can be expressed as standardized effect sizes in units of human phenotypic (SDpheno) and genetic (SDgeno) expression variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analysis uses the default GTEx inverse-normal-transformed expression values and does not require variance-standardized (SD-unit) effect sizes The gene x tissue pair fails the IHW alpha = 0.10 heritability significance filter, so its SDgeno estimate is not confidently heritable You need qualitative sex-specific exercise responses rather than sex-consistent standardized effect sizes (the article notes sex-specificity 'fell outside the scope considered here')

skills.search_text: gut-metabolomics-differential-analysis Use when a GNPS-derived intensity matrix plus molecular-family annotation table must be compared between two sample groups (case vs control, e.g. >30 vs <10 plant-based foods/week) to find significantly changing metabolite sets at p<=0.05. skills.summary: Differentially analyse GNPS molecular families from gut-metabolomics data (e.g. the American Gut Project plant-based-foods case/control comparison) by ranking metabolite-set activity levels with the PALS PLAGE decomposition in Python, filtering to significantly changing families.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classical pathway analysis with annotated compounds mapped to KEGG/ChEBI IDs — use PALS' database-driven mode (Reactome/PiMP_KEGG/ChEBI) instead of user-defined molecular-family sets There is no case/control design — the PLAGE decomposition here computes activity scores from explicit case vs control comparisons Input is not GNPS/MS2LDA-fragmentation-grouped metabolite sets (molecular families or Mass2Motifs) and grouping is unavailable

skills.name: gwas-catalog-network-gene-set-construction
skills.search_text: gwas-catalog-network-gene-set-construction Use when a metabolomics-only (standalone, unpaired) dataset needs to be compared against GWAS evidence: you must extract disease- or trait-anchored gene sets (e.g. cardiovascular disease, kidney/urine) from the GWAS Catalog network before running a hypergeometric enrichment test. skills.summary: Construct disease/phenotype-specific genomic gene sets from a network representation of the GWAS Catalog (hundreds of studies), restricted to genes discoverable via known metabolite interactions in HMDB, for use as the genomic side of metGWAS 1.0's hypergeometric over-representation test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have paired metabolomics-GWAS data (per-metabolite SNP associations); metGWAS is explicitly designed for unpaired, standalone studies and cannot leverage genotype-level pairing. skills.description: Use when constructing genomic gene-set networks from GWAS Catalog studies, or when extracting disease/trait-specific GWAS subnetworks to serve as genomic gene sets for hypergeometric over-representation testing against metabolic gene sets.
skills.name: gwas-network-construction
skills.search_text: gwas-network-construction Use when constructing genomic gene-set networks from GWAS Catalog studies, or when extracting disease/trait-specific GWAS subnetworks to serve as genomic gene sets for hypergeometric over-representation testing against metabolic gene sets. The analysis requires paired metabolomics-GWAS data from the same subjects — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for independent, unpaired standalone studies and limits associations to genes with known metabolite interactions. The goal is de novo GWAS association testing on raw genotypes rather than over-representation analysis against a prebuilt GWAS Catalog network representation. The disease/trait of interest cannot be matched by keyword to nodes in the GWAS Catalog network, so no primary nodes can be identified for subnetwork extraction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Builds a trait/disease-related GWAS network from a network representation of the GWAS Catalog, retaining edges between GWAS study gene sets only when their Jaccard coefficient is >= 0.5 with FDR-corrected P <= 0.05, then extracts keyword-filtered subnetworks (e.g. 'Kidney', 'Urine') for downstream over-representation analysis in metGWAS 1.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Builds a trait/disease-related GWAS network from a network representation of the GWAS Catalog, retaining edges between GWAS study gene sets only when their Jaccard coefficient is >= 0.5 with FDR-corrected P <= 0.05, then extracts keyword-filtered subnetworks (e.g. 'Kidney', 'Urine') for downstream over-representation analysis in metGWAS 1.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires paired metabolomics-GWAS data from the same subjects — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for independent, unpaired standalone studies and limits associations to genes with known metabolite interactions. The goal is de novo GWAS association testing on raw genotypes rather than over-representation analysis against a prebuilt GWAS Catalog network representation. The disease/trait of interest cannot be matched by keyword to nodes in the GWAS Catalog network, so no primary nodes can be identified for subnetwork extraction.

skills.description: Use when you have metGWAS 1.0 intersection gene sets from a hypergeometric comparison of metabolic and genomic gene sets and need to trace whether each gene is a primary keyword node or a first-neighbour node in the GWAS subnetwork.

skills.search_text: gwas-network-node-classification Use when you have metGWAS 1.0 intersection gene sets from a hypergeometric comparison of metabolic and genomic gene sets and need to trace whether each gene is a primary keyword node or a first-neighbour node in the GWAS subnetwork. skills.search_text: harmonic-mean-pvalue-aggregation Use when a gene-set or enrichment analysis yields multiple correlated subtest p-values (e.g. Bonferroni-adjusted fgsea() results per trait×tissue pair) that must be combined into one FWER-controlled test statistic. The subtests being aggregated are statistically independent — then Fisher's sum-of-logs method (as the paper used to combine male- and female-specific DE p-values) is the more appropriate, more powerful choice. The interaction matrix has not yet been produced by the cross-validated MiMeNet models - clustering raw abundance tables instead of the attribution-score matrix will not yield interpretable modules. Metabolite abundances are being predicted directly rather than analyzed for network structure - use the MiMeNet prediction pipeline, not module biclustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Applies consensus clustering with Euclidean distance and complete linkage to split the MiMeNet microbe-metabolite interaction-score matrix into microbe and metabolite modules, selecting the cluster number via a delta-area threshold of 0.025. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009021
skills.summary: Applies consensus clustering with Euclidean distance and complete linkage to split the MiMeNet microbe-metabolite interaction-score matrix into microbe and metabolite modules, selecting the cluster number via a delta-area threshold of 0.025.

Metabolite abundances are being predicted directly rather than analyzed for network structure - use the MiMeNet prediction pipeline, not module biclustering.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how much recall a deep-learning-regenerated (5th-level) lipid fragment library adds over a truncated 1st–4th-level or MS-DIAL public library, using a dataset with a known reference lipid list.
skills.name: hierarchical-lipid-library-level-truncation
skills.search_text: hierarchical-lipid-library-level-truncation Use when benchmarking how much recall a deep-learning-regenerated (5th-level) lipid fragment library adds over a truncated 1st–4th-level or MS-DIAL public library, using a dataset with a known reference lipid list. The analysis is single-lipid targeted identification rather than a recall benchmark against a known reference lipid list. The goal is Paternò–Büchi double-bond localization, which uses LipidIN's dedicated PB libraries (e.g. PB_PX_H.pkl) rather than hierarchical level truncation. The dataset lacks a ground-truth reference set of reported lipids, so recall cannot be computed. Benchmark strategy from LipidIN that compares MS2 library search recall across truncation levels of its hierarchical lipid fragmentation library (1st–4th vs 1st–5th level, the 5th level being WMYn-regenerated fingerprints) against the MS-DIAL public database on a reference lipidome dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Benchmark strategy from LipidIN that compares MS2 library search recall across truncation levels of its hierarchical lipid fragmentation library (1st–4th vs 1st–5th level, the 5th level being WMYn-regenerated fingerprints) against the MS-DIAL public database on a reference lipidome dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is single-lipid targeted identification rather than a recall benchmark against a known reference lipid list. The goal is Paternò–Büchi double-bond localization, which uses LipidIN's dedicated PB libraries (e.g. PB_PX_H.pkl) rather than hierarchical level truncation.
