skills.description: Use when comparing the computational cost of imputation algorithms (KNN-EU vs KNN-CR vs KNN-TN) on an identical metabolomics dataset, or when quantifying the runtime penalty of truncated-normal MLE estimation before choosing an imputer.
skills.name: imputation-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: imputation-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing the computational cost of imputation algorithms (KNN-EU vs KNN-CR vs KNN-TN) on an identical metabolomics dataset, or when quantifying the runtime penalty of truncated-normal MLE estimation before choosing an imputer. The goal is imputation accuracy (RMSE, MLCI, concordance of significance testing) rather than computational cost — this skill measures runtime only. Metabolite distributions are strongly non-normal, since KNN-TN's truncated-normal MLE assumption is what generates the extra runtime and its validity. Datasets have excessive missingness or very small samples, where truncated mean/variance estimation is unstable and timings would reflect degenerate fits rather than typical cost. skills.search_text: in-house-database-matching-lcms Use when a cleaned feature table (mass_dataset object) from LC–MS untargeted metabolomics needs metabolite annotations, and in-house HILIC/RPLC standard databases with RT information are available for metID matching. The input is still raw LC–MS data or an uncleaned feature table — data cleaning and QC filtering (e.g. removing features with >20% MVs in QC samples or >50% MVs in study groups) must be done first MSI level 1 identifications requiring authentic-standard confirmation are the goal — this workflow only retains and reports annotations up to MSI level 2 No retention-time-matched reference database exists for the chromatographic mode being used, since matching depends on both accurate m/z and retention time http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates LC–MS features by matching accurate m/z and retention time against curated in-house HILIC (71 metabolites) and RPLC (55 metabolites) databases plus a public database using metID within tidyMass, then resolves redundancy by annotation score and retains MSI level 2 identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: Annotates LC–MS features by matching accurate m/z and retention time against curated in-house HILIC (71 metabolites) and RPLC (55 metabolites) databases plus a public database using metID within tidyMass, then resolves redundancy by annotation score and retains MSI level 2 identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is still raw LC–MS data or an uncleaned feature table — data cleaning and QC filtering (e.g. removing features with >20% MVs in QC samples or >50% MVs in study groups) must be done first MSI level 1 identifications requiring authentic-standard confirmation are the goal — this workflow only retains and reports annotations up to MSI level 2 No retention-time-matched reference database exists for the chromatographic mode being used, since matching depends on both accurate m/z and retention time

skills.description: Use when evaluating or reproducing mass spectral search method performance on a benchmark set with known true molecules, such as scoring spectra against a structure database and computing top-k identification accuracy.
skills.name: in-silico-annotation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: in-silico-annotation-benchmarking Use when evaluating or reproducing mass spectral search method performance on a benchmark set with known true molecules, such as scoring spectra against a structure database and computing top-k identification accuracy. Input spectra lack known ground-truth molecule assignments, so top-k accuracy cannot be computed against a reference The goal is de novo structure prediction or spectral library search rather than scoring spectra against a structure database Molecules are outside the method's supported mass/fragmentation range, e.g., super small molecules (<400 Da) or heavy molecules (>1000 Da), where the method is reported to perform poorly or be computationally insufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks in-silico mass spectral database search methods (e.g., molDiscovery) on annotated spectral libraries against structure databases by ranking candidate molecules and computing top-k identification accuracies, validating reproduction of reported benchmark values. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Benchmarks in-silico mass spectral database search methods (e.g., molDiscovery) on annotated spectral libraries against structure databases by ranking candidate molecules and computing top-k identification accuracies, validating reproduction of reported benchmark values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack known ground-truth molecule assignments, so top-k accuracy cannot be computed against a reference The goal is de novo structure prediction or spectral library search rather than scoring spectra against a structure database Molecules are outside the method's supported mass/fragmentation range, e.g., super small molecules (<400 Da) or heavy molecules (>1000 Da), where the method is reported to perform poorly or be computationally insufficient

skills.description: Use when cleaning GNPS molecular networking library annotations or SIRIUS/ISDB in-silico annotation results before computing annotation statistics or novelty ranks for an untargeted MS/MS extract set.
skills.name: in-silico-annotation-cutoff-filtering
skills.search_text: in-silico-annotation-cutoff-filtering Use when cleaning GNPS molecular networking library annotations or SIRIUS/ISDB in-silico annotation results before computing annotation statistics or novelty ranks for an untargeted MS/MS extract set. Input is already a cleaned, filtered annotation table (re-running cutoffs could double-filter and under-count annotations) You only have raw MZmine quantitative data with no annotation source (GNPS library matches, SIRIUS/ISDB or timaR output) — there is nothing to filter You need to preserve all tentative annotations for exploratory spectral review rather than for computing a novelty or annotation-rate score http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filters library and in-silico spectral annotations (GNPS library matches, SIRIUS/ISDB, timaR) using explicit quality thresholds so that downstream novelty scoring in Inventa relies only on high-confidence annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Filters library and in-silico spectral annotations (GNPS library matches, SIRIUS/ISDB, timaR) using explicit quality thresholds so that downstream novelty scoring in Inventa relies only on high-confidence annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned, filtered annotation table (re-running cutoffs could double-filter and under-count annotations) You only have raw MZmine quantitative data with no annotation source (GNPS library matches, SIRIUS/ISDB or timaR output) — there is nothing to filter You need to preserve all tentative annotations for exploratory spectral review rather than for computing a novelty or annotation-rate score

skills.description: Use when building the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network layer of KGMN: you need to expand known KEGG metabolites into putative unknowns via in silico biotransformations before MS/MS-based annotation.
skills.name: in-silico-biotransformation-network-extension
skills.search_text: in-silico-biotransformation-network-extension Use when building the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network layer of KGMN: you need to expand known KEGG metabolites into putative unknowns via in silico biotransformations before MS/MS-based annotation. Applying to non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples without caution, since BioTransformer's predefined reaction sets mainly originated from human metabolic reactions Problems requiring resolution of structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively discriminate Annotating metabolites against general structural/spectral databases (HMDB, PubChem) without the KGMN network context — use library matching or in silico MS/MS tools instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Constructs the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (KMRN) layer of KGMN by merging KEGG RCLASS reactant-pair knowledge with BioTransformer-predicted metabolites, extending known metabolites to unknowns for downstream annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Constructs the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (KMRN) layer of KGMN by merging KEGG RCLASS reactant-pair knowledge with BioTransformer-predicted metabolites, extending known metabolites to unknowns for downstream annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Applying to non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples without caution, since BioTransformer's predefined reaction sets mainly originated from human metabolic reactions Problems requiring resolution of structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively discriminate Annotating metabolites against general structural/spectral databases (HMDB, PubChem) without the KGMN network context — use library matching or in silico MS/MS tools instead

skills.description: Use when you have a peak-picked mzML file of an LC-HRMS/MS run, the parent drug's molecular formula, and need to predict in silico phase I/II biotransformations and detect the corresponding metabolites.
skills.name: in-silico-biotransformation-prediction
skills.search_text: in-silico-biotransformation-prediction Use when you have a peak-picked mzML file of an LC-HRMS/MS run, the parent drug's molecular formula, and need to predict in silico phase I/II biotransformations and detect the corresponding metabolites. Input is already a curated metabolite feature table rather than raw peak-picked mzML data — MetIDfyR mines mzML spectra itself The parent drug's molecular formula is unknown, since MetIDfyR predicts biotransformations based solely on the raw formula of the drug of interest The MS data is not in mzML format or is not peak-picked http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Predict and detect phase I/II metabolites of a parent drug directly in LC-HRMS/MS mzML data using MetIDfyR, an open-source R package that generates biotransformations from the raw formula of the drug of interest and mines peak-picked spectra for matching accurate masses. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02281
skills.summary: Predict and detect phase I/II metabolites of a parent drug directly in LC-HRMS/MS mzML data using MetIDfyR, an open-source R package that generates biotransformations from the raw formula of the drug of interest and mines peak-picked spectra for matching accurate masses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated metabolite feature table rather than raw peak-picked mzML data — MetIDfyR mines mzML spectra itself The parent drug's molecular formula is unknown, since MetIDfyR predicts biotransformations based solely on the raw formula of the drug of interest The MS data is not in mzML format or is not peak-picked

skills.description: Use when ranking candidate molecule structures for a tandem HR-MS/MS spectrum (e.g. Orbitrap product-ion peaks) by how well each candidate explains the observed fragments, without spectral-library search.
skills.name: in-silico-bond-dissociation-fragmentation
skills.search_text: in-silico-bond-dissociation-fragmentation Use when ranking candidate molecule structures for a tandem HR-MS/MS spectrum (e.g. Orbitrap product-ion peaks) by how well each candidate explains the observed fragments, without spectral-library search. The task is library-based identification — the spectrum can be matched directly against MassBank reference spectra instead of scored against candidate structures The mass spectrum is dominated by one or only a few fragments (e.g. a water loss) that most candidates can explain — such spectra 'simply do not contain enough information' to discriminate candidates by fragment scoring Only MSn (multi-stage) fragmentation data is available — MAGMa handles MSn information, MetFrag's bond-dissociation fragmenter works on single-stage MS/MS product ions http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 MetFrag's core in silico fragmentation skill: each candidate structure from PubChem/ChemSpider (or a user-supplied SDF) is systematically cleaved via a bond-dissociation approach, and the generated neutral fragments are matched against measured HR-MS/MS product ions to compute a fragment-explanation score used to rank candidates. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: MetFrag's core in silico fragmentation skill: each candidate structure from PubChem/ChemSpider (or a user-supplied SDF) is systematically cleaved via a bond-dissociation approach, and the generated neutral fragments are matched against measured HR-MS/MS product ions to compute a fragment-explanation score used to rank candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is library-based identification — the spectrum can be matched directly against MassBank reference spectra instead of scored against candidate structures The mass spectrum is dominated by one or only a few fragments (e.g. a water loss) that most candidates can explain — such spectra 'simply do not contain enough information' to discriminate candidates by fragment scoring Only MSn (multi-stage) fragmentation data is available — MAGMa handles MSn information, MetFrag's bond-dissociation fragmenter works on single-stage MS/MS product ions

skills.description: Use when MS/MS or MSn fragment spectra must be explained without reference spectra, e.g. CASMI-style compound annotation where candidate molecules need penalty-score ranking based on in silico generated substructures.
skills.name: in-silico-bond-dissociation-fragmentation
skills.search_text: in-silico-bond-dissociation-fragmentation Use when MS/MS or MSn fragment spectra must be explained without reference spectra, e.g. CASMI-style compound annotation where candidate molecules need penalty-score ranking based on in silico generated substructures. Reference mass spectra are already available for the target metabolite, so peak-to-structure annotation can be done directly without in silico fragmentation scoring. The observed fragment m/z values clearly require neutral-loss ion series that MAGMa's bond-dissociation plus water/ammonia-loss expansion does not cover, and no extra fragmentation depth or substructure expansion is planned. Goal is de novo molecular formula generation rather than ranking a pre-retrieved candidate structure set. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Systematically fragments candidate chemical structures in silico by applying successive single-bond dissociations (up to 3, or extended to 5 for retrospective deep fragmentation), producing substructure sets whose m/z values are matched against MS/MS peaks to score and rank candidates. metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033
skills.summary: Systematically fragments candidate chemical structures in silico by applying successive single-bond dissociations (up to 3, or extended to 5 for retrospective deep fragmentation), producing substructure sets whose m/z values are matched against MS/MS peaks to score and rank candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference mass spectra are already available for the target metabolite, so peak-to-structure annotation can be done directly without in silico fragmentation scoring. The observed fragment m/z values clearly require neutral-loss ion series that MAGMa's bond-dissociation plus water/ammonia-loss expansion does not cover, and no extra fragmentation depth or substructure expansion is planned. Goal is de novo molecular formula generation rather than ranking a pre-retrieved candidate structure set.

skills.description: Use when curating raw spectral library entries (NIST'17, MS-DIAL .msp, MSnLib *_ms2.mgf) into fragment-annotated, training-ready spectra for a bond-cleavage-based MS/MS prediction model.
skills.name: in-silico-bond-fragment-generation
skills.search_text: in-silico-bond-fragment-generation Use when curating raw spectral library entries (NIST'17, MS-DIAL .msp, MSnLib *_ms2.mgf) into fragment-annotated, training-ready spectra for a bond-cleavage-based MS/MS prediction model. Spectra already carry validated fragment annotations and only need model training, not re-curation The target spectra are EI-MS or use precursor/ionization types outside [M+H]+, [M-H]-, [M]+, [M]- Multi-step fragmentation is required — this skill enumerates single-edge (single-bond) cleavages only, which is FIORA's stated biggest limitation http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Systematically enumerate single-edge molecular fragments by cleaving each bond of a compound independently (allowing up to four hydrogen losses to distribute charge between charged fragment and neutral loss), then match the generated fragment m/z values against observed MS/MS peaks to build quality-controlled training spectra for FIORA. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Systematically enumerate single-edge molecular fragments by cleaving each bond of a compound independently (allowing up to four hydrogen losses to distribute charge between charged fragment and neutral loss), then match the generated fragment m/z values against observed MS/MS peaks to build quality-controlled training spectra for FIORA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra already carry validated fragment annotations and only need model training, not re-curation The target spectra are EI-MS or use precursor/ionization types outside [M+H]+, [M-H]-, [M]+, [M]- Multi-step fragmentation is required — this skill enumerates single-edge (single-bond) cleavages only, which is FIORA's stated biggest limitation

skills.description: Use when building a searchable CCS reference library for compound identification from a SMILES/compound list, by predicting CCS values for multiple adduct types with the pretrained SigmaCCS model.
skills.name: in-silico-ccs-database-generation
skills.search_text: in-silico-ccs-database-generation Use when building a searchable CCS reference library for compound identification from a SMILES/compound list, by predicting CCS values for multiple adduct types with the pretrained SigmaCCS model. Molecules containing elements other than C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se — SigmaCCS cannot predict them Compounds with molecular weight at or above 1500 Da, which are excluded by the paper's database filtering Adduct ion types beyond the three encoded ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-); the paper notes encoding more adduct types as future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the SigmaCCS pipeline that converts PubChem compounds (MW < 1500 Da) into 3D conformers, predicts CCS values for the [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, and [M-H]- adducts with a pretrained graph neural network, and writes the results to a CSV in-silico database like the Zenodo record 5501674 deposit. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00939-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs the SigmaCCS pipeline that converts PubChem compounds (MW < 1500 Da) into 3D conformers, predicts CCS values for the [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, and [M-H]- adducts with a pretrained graph neural network, and writes the results to a CSV in-silico database like the Zenodo record 5501674 deposit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Molecules containing elements other than C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se — SigmaCCS cannot predict them Compounds with molecular weight at or above 1500 Da, which are excluded by the paper's database filtering Adduct ion types beyond the three encoded ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-); the paper notes encoding more adduct types as future work

skills.description: Use when a GNPS feature-based molecular networking job has been paired with CANOPUS class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv) and you need to propagate consistent chemical class annotations to unannotated ion features in subnetworks.
skills.name: in-silico-class-prediction-interpretation
skills.search_text: in-silico-class-prediction-interpretation Use when a GNPS feature-based molecular networking job has been paired with CANOPUS class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv) and you need to propagate consistent chemical class annotations to unannotated ion features in subnetworks. When you only have raw spectra without GNPS molecular networking results and SIRIUS/CANOPUS class predictions — the consensus strategy requires both library matches and in silico class annotations. When your analysis relies on NPClassifier ontology output and you need ClassyFire ChemOnt terminology (or vice versa) without confirming the ontology argument, since mixed ontologies are not supported in a single run. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Interprets SIRIUS/CANOPUS in silico structural class predictions by fusing them with GNPS spectral library matches and molecular networking to assign consensus ClassyFire (ChemOnt) annotations to entire molecular subnetworks. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: Interprets SIRIUS/CANOPUS in silico structural class predictions by fusing them with GNPS spectral library matches and molecular networking to assign consensus ClassyFire (ChemOnt) annotations to entire molecular subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only have raw spectra without GNPS molecular networking results and SIRIUS/CANOPUS class predictions — the consensus strategy requires both library matches and in silico class annotations. When your analysis relies on NPClassifier ontology output and you need ClassyFire ChemOnt terminology (or vice versa) without confirming the ontology argument, since mixed ontologies are not supported in a single run.

skills.description: Use when propagating ClassyFire ChemOnt classifications across GNPS molecular networking subnetworks by fusing library spectral matches with CANOPUS in silico predictions and applying per-level consensus thresholds.
skills.name: in-silico-classification-thresholding
skills.search_text: in-silico-classification-thresholding Use when propagating ClassyFire ChemOnt classifications across GNPS molecular networking subnetworks by fusing library spectral matches with CANOPUS in silico predictions and applying per-level consensus thresholds. Subnetworks contain no library spectral matches (singleton nodes without library matches receive no in silico annotation, so consensus propagation cannot be applied) You need compound-level structural assignments rather than per-subnetwork chemical-class consensus — this skill propagates ChemOnt class annotations, not structures You require NPClassifier ontologies at different thresholds — the 50/70/70 defaults were established for ClassyFire ChemOnt levels http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs ConCISE's consensus rule for propagating chemical-class annotations across a molecular subnetwork: superclass, class, and subclass percent-consensus cutoffs of 50/70/70 select the most granular ChemOnt level that passes, which is then exported with its hierarchy and consensus score. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: Reconstructs ConCISE's consensus rule for propagating chemical-class annotations across a molecular subnetwork: superclass, class, and subclass percent-consensus cutoffs of 50/70/70 select the most granular ChemOnt level that passes, which is then exported with its hierarchy and consensus score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Subnetworks contain no library spectral matches (singleton nodes without library matches receive no in silico annotation, so consensus propagation cannot be applied) You need compound-level structural assignments rather than per-subnetwork chemical-class consensus — this skill propagates ChemOnt class annotations, not structures You require NPClassifier ontologies at different thresholds — the 50/70/70 defaults were established for ClassyFire ChemOnt levels

skills.description: Use when DDA controller parameters (e.g., SmartROI alpha/beta or WeightedDEW t0/t1) must be tuned before hardware experiments and full-scan mzML seed data exist for the samples of interest.
skills.name: in-silico-dda-controller-grid-search-optimization
skills.search_text: in-silico-dda-controller-grid-search-optimization Use when DDA controller parameters (e.g., SmartROI alpha/beta or WeightedDEW t0/t1) must be tuned before hardware experiments and full-scan mzML seed data exist for the samples of interest. When the goal is to optimize parameters for a controller other than SmartROI or WeightedDEW, or when the sample's full-scan mzML seed data are unavailable for ViMMS When real-instrument validation data already exist and the grid can be evaluated directly on hardware without simulation When the objective is not coverage of fragmented unique ions (e.g., optimizing for intensity or reproducibility metrics not modeled in the simulation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Uses the ViMMS virtual metabolomics mass spectrometer to grid-search DDA controller parameters (SmartROI alpha/beta, WeightedDEW t0/t1) on full-scan mzML-seeded simulations, selecting settings that maximize coverage before any real instrument time is spent. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Uses the ViMMS virtual metabolomics mass spectrometer to grid-search DDA controller parameters (SmartROI alpha/beta, WeightedDEW t0/t1) on full-scan mzML-seeded simulations, selecting settings that maximize coverage before any real instrument time is spent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to optimize parameters for a controller other than SmartROI or WeightedDEW, or when the sample's full-scan mzML seed data are unavailable for ViMMS When real-instrument validation data already exist and the grid can be evaluated directly on hardware without simulation When the objective is not coverage of fragmented unique ions (e.g., optimizing for intensity or reproducibility metrics not modeled in the simulation)

skills.description: Use when you need to attribute FastEI's recall and throughput gains to Word2vec spectral embedding versus HNSW indexing, by benchmarking the EC and BH hybrid variants against the full FastEI pipeline and the WCS baseline.
skills.name: in-silico-ei-ms-library-querying
skills.search_text: in-silico-ei-ms-library-querying Use when you need to attribute FastEI's recall and throughput gains to Word2vec spectral embedding versus HNSW indexing, by benchmarking the EC and BH hybrid variants against the full FastEI pipeline and the WCS baseline. You only need end-to-end compound identification results and are not attributing performance to specific FastEI components — use the full FastEI pipeline instead of the EC/BH hybrids. Your query spectra are not EI mass spectra comparable to the NIST 2017 test set (e.g. MS/MS or LC-MS data) — the HNSW index and Word2vec model are trained on EI predicted spectra. You need exact nearest-neighbor ground truth on the million-scale library without approximation — HNSW (BH configuration) is an approximate nearest-neighbor method. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ablation protocol that decomposes FastEI's contribution by testing two hybrid configurations on measured NIST 2017 EI-MS test spectra: EC (Word2vec embeddings + cosine similarity via faiss.IndexFlatL2, replacing WCS binning) and BH (weighted spectral binning + HNSW, replacing cosine similarity). It isolates which component drives identification accuracy versus matching speed. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Ablation protocol that decomposes FastEI's contribution by testing two hybrid configurations on measured NIST 2017 EI-MS test spectra: EC (Word2vec embeddings + cosine similarity via faiss.IndexFlatL2, replacing WCS binning) and BH (weighted spectral binning + HNSW, replacing cosine similarity). It isolates which component drives identification accuracy versus matching speed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need end-to-end compound identification results and are not attributing performance to specific FastEI components — use the full FastEI pipeline instead of the EC/BH hybrids. Your query spectra are not EI mass spectra comparable to the NIST 2017 test set (e.g. MS/MS or LC-MS data) — the HNSW index and Word2vec model are trained on EI predicted spectra. You need exact nearest-neighbor ground truth on the million-scale library without approximation — HNSW (BH configuration) is an approximate nearest-neighbor method.

skills.description: Use when Mass2Motif substructure assignments (e.g., ring or tail motifs from MS2LDA) need independent confirmation against in silico fragment annotations before being trusted for molecular family interpretation.
skills.name: in-silico-fragment-annotation-cross-validation
skills.search_text: in-silico-fragment-annotation-cross-validation Use when Mass2Motif substructure assignments (e.g., ring or tail motifs from MS2LDA) need independent confirmation against in silico fragment annotations before being trusted for molecular family interpretation. When the molecular family has no MS2LDA motif assignments to validate (no motif-document relations pass the prob/overlap thresholds) — there is nothing to cross-validate. When DEREPLICATOR or the chosen in silico tool cannot annotate the compound class (e.g., non-NRP/polyketide scaffolds outside its rule-based scope), forcing cross-validation against irrelevant fragments. When the goal is pure chemical-class propagation rather than substructure-level validation — ClassyFire-based chemical annotation through MolNetEnhancer is the appropriate skill instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Cross-validates MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructure assignments against independent in silico fragment annotations (e.g., DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest) to confirm that motif-derived substructures are supported by predicted fragments, as done for the xenoamicin ring and tail motifs in Xenorhabdus molecular families. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Cross-validates MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructure assignments against independent in silico fragment annotations (e.g., DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest) to confirm that motif-derived substructures are supported by predicted fragments, as done for the xenoamicin ring and tail motifs in Xenorhabdus molecular families.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the molecular family has no MS2LDA motif assignments to validate (no motif-document relations pass the prob/overlap thresholds) — there is nothing to cross-validate. When DEREPLICATOR or the chosen in silico tool cannot annotate the compound class (e.g., non-NRP/polyketide scaffolds outside its rule-based scope), forcing cross-validation against irrelevant fragments. When the goal is pure chemical-class propagation rather than substructure-level validation — ClassyFire-based chemical annotation through MolNetEnhancer is the appropriate skill instead.

skills.description: Use when you have ddMS2-topN or AIF high-resolution tandem MS spectra (.ms2 files) and candidate lipid precursors from exact-mass MS1 matching, and need to match experimental fragment m/z values against simulated in silico fragmentation library values to assign lipid identifications.
skills.name: in-silico-fragment-library-querying
skills.search_text: in-silico-fragment-library-querying Use when you have ddMS2-topN or AIF high-resolution tandem MS spectra (.ms2 files) and candidate lipid precursors from exact-mass MS1 matching, and need to match experimental fragment m/z values against simulated in silico fragmentation library values to assign lipid identifications. Data acquired on Waters instruments - the README states the software 'does not currently support Waters files' When you only have precursor m/z without tandem MS data - the identification would fall to level 4 (precursor m/z only) and the fragment-matching step adds no value beyond the MS1 exact-mass matching stage When the in silico library lacks the necessary structural fragments for the lipid type of interest - users must develop their own fragmentation libraries in Excel for full customization, and without the required fragments no identification is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Querying experimental MS/MS fragments against in silico lipid fragmentation libraries (e.g. LipidBlast-derived .csv libraries covering >250,000 lipid species across 56 lipid types) to match observed fragment m/z values within a ppm tolerance and assign binary fragment-presence flags used for rule-based lipid identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Querying experimental MS/MS fragments against in silico lipid fragmentation libraries (e.g. LipidBlast-derived .csv libraries covering >250,000 lipid species across 56 lipid types) to match observed fragment m/z values within a ppm tolerance and assign binary fragment-presence flags used for rule-based lipid identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data acquired on Waters instruments - the README states the software 'does not currently support Waters files' When you only have precursor m/z without tandem MS data - the identification would fall to level 4 (precursor m/z only) and the fragment-matching step adds no value beyond the MS1 exact-mass matching stage When the in silico library lacks the necessary structural fragments for the lipid type of interest - users must develop their own fragmentation libraries in Excel for full customization, and without the required fragments no identification is possible

skills.description: Use when you have untargeted LC-HRMS/MS feature tables (m/z + retention time) plus .ms2 MS/MS spectra and need to annotate lipid identifications by exact-mass matching experimental fragments to in silico library fragments.
skills.name: in-silico-fragment-mass-matching
skills.search_text: in-silico-fragment-mass-matching Use when you have untargeted LC-HRMS/MS feature tables (m/z + retention time) plus .ms2 MS/MS spectra and need to annotate lipid identifications by exact-mass matching experimental fragments to in silico library fragments.
