skills.search_text: in-silico-msms-annotation Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data in .mzML format contains features that cannot be annotated by spectral matching alone, and per-feature chemical structures, formulas, and chemical classes must be assigned and ranked. When all features are already covered by exact spectral database matches (e.g. the betaine case where public spectral databases suffice and are not standardized beyond their contents) When features belong to lipid or macrocyclic natural-product classes (e.g. Marchantin) where SIRIUS false positives and complex fragmentation make in silico ranking unreliable When input is not tandem MS2 data (MAW takes MS2 .mzML files as input in R) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotate untargeted MS2 metabolomics features by combining spectral database dereplication (Spectra with GNPS/HMDB/MassBank), in silico candidate generation (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID or MetFrag), and RDKit-based final candidate selection as implemented in the MAW workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00695-y
skills.summary: Annotate untargeted MS2 metabolomics features by combining spectral database dereplication (Spectra with GNPS/HMDB/MassBank), in silico candidate generation (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID or MetFrag), and RDKit-based final candidate selection as implemented in the MAW workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When all features are already covered by exact spectral database matches (e.g. the betaine case where public spectral databases suffice and are not standardized beyond their contents) When features belong to lipid or macrocyclic natural-product classes (e.g. Marchantin) where SIRIUS false positives and complex fragmentation make in silico ranking unreliable When input is not tandem MS2 data (MAW takes MS2 .mzML files as input in R)

skills.description: Use when building a spectral library for adductomics or metabolomics where reference standards are unavailable and in silico MS/MS fragments are needed for each structure entry.
skills.name: in-silico-msms-fragment-prediction
skills.search_text: in-silico-msms-fragment-prediction Use when building a spectral library for adductomics or metabolomics where reference standards are unavailable and in silico MS/MS fragments are needed for each structure entry. When experimental MS/MS spectra of reference standards are already available for the target analytes, since measured spectra take precedence over in silico predictions. When the goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than populating a searchable spectral-library datatable for known or hypothesized adduct entries. When the adduct structures lack computer-readable identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, or .mol files) that CFM-ID requires. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates predicted MS/MS fragment ions for chemical structures (e.g., DNA adducts) using CFM-ID across three energy levels, then filters and assembles the fragments into a searchable datatable alongside the parent adduct entries. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Generates predicted MS/MS fragment ions for chemical structures (e.g., DNA adducts) using CFM-ID across three energy levels, then filters and assembles the fragments into a searchable datatable alongside the parent adduct entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimental MS/MS spectra of reference standards are already available for the target analytes, since measured spectra take precedence over in silico predictions. When the goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than populating a searchable spectral-library datatable for known or hypothesized adduct entries. When the adduct structures lack computer-readable identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, or .mol files) that CFM-ID requires.

skills.description: Use when annotating a tandem MS spectrum against candidate molecules whose structures are known, and you need pre-calculated fragmentation patterns or per-candidate fragment scores to rank metabolite annotations.
skills.name: in-silico-msms-fragmentation-enumeration
skills.search_text: in-silico-msms-fragmentation-enumeration Use when annotating a tandem MS spectrum against candidate molecules whose structures are known, and you need pre-calculated fragmentation patterns or per-candidate fragment scores to rank metabolite annotations. When candidate molecules lack known structures (no SDF/MOL available), since fragments must be enumerated from a molecular graph When RDKit is unavailable and only fingerprint/SVM-based scoring (FingerScorer) will be used — RDKit is optional in ChemDistiller and mainly used for structure images, so graph-based bond breaking is not possible without it When the input is already a scored annotation table or feature table rather than raw tandem MS peaks requiring fragment matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Recursively enumerate fragment structures of a candidate molecule by breaking one and then two bonds with a ±1 hydrogen correction, build a theoretical fragment peak list, and match it against a normalized experimental tandem MS spectrum for candidate scoring as in ChemDistiller's FragScorer. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: Recursively enumerate fragment structures of a candidate molecule by breaking one and then two bonds with a ±1 hydrogen correction, build a theoretical fragment peak list, and match it against a normalized experimental tandem MS spectrum for candidate scoring as in ChemDistiller's FragScorer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When candidate molecules lack known structures (no SDF/MOL available), since fragments must be enumerated from a molecular graph When RDKit is unavailable and only fingerprint/SVM-based scoring (FingerScorer) will be used — RDKit is optional in ChemDistiller and mainly used for structure images, so graph-based bond breaking is not possible without it When the input is already a scored annotation table or feature table rather than raw tandem MS peaks requiring fragment matching

skills.description: Use when validating putative unknown metabolite annotations from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics (e.g., KGMN/MetDNA2 unknown peaks in NIST urine data) where no spectral library match or chemical standard exists and computational fragmentation support is needed.
skills.name: in-silico-msms-spectral-prediction
skills.search_text: in-silico-msms-spectral-prediction Use when validating putative unknown metabolite annotations from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics (e.g., KGMN/MetDNA2 unknown peaks in NIST urine data) where no spectral library match or chemical standard exists and computational fragmentation support is needed. The metabolites are known/knowns already matched against standard spectral libraries by MS1 m/z and MS2 spectrum search, so no in silico corroboration is required Authentic chemical standards are available, in which case direct experimental MS/MS validation is preferred over in silico prediction The goal is discriminating structurally similar isomers of unknowns (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN and this corroboration workflow cannot effectively resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Corroborates KGMN-putatively annotated unknown metabolites (which are absent from spectral databases and lack chemical standards) by running candidate structures through in silico MS/MS prediction tools — MetFrag, CFM-ID, and MS-FINDER — and scoring candidate-vs-measured spectra agreement per unknown peak. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Corroborates KGMN-putatively annotated unknown metabolites (which are absent from spectral databases and lack chemical standards) by running candidate structures through in silico MS/MS prediction tools — MetFrag, CFM-ID, and MS-FINDER — and scoring candidate-vs-measured spectra agreement per unknown peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites are known/knowns already matched against standard spectral libraries by MS1 m/z and MS2 spectrum search, so no in silico corroboration is required Authentic chemical standards are available, in which case direct experimental MS/MS validation is preferred over in silico prediction The goal is discriminating structurally similar isomers of unknowns (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN and this corroboration workflow cannot effectively resolve

skills.description: Use when you need simulated MS/MS spectra for compounds lacking reference library entries, or when benchmarking fragmentation-prediction quality across NIST/MS-DIAL, MSnLib, and CASMI test sets.
skills.name: in-silico-msms-spectral-prediction
skills.search_text: in-silico-msms-spectral-prediction Use when you need simulated MS/MS spectra for compounds lacking reference library entries, or when benchmarking fragmentation-prediction quality across NIST/MS-DIAL, MSnLib, and CASMI test sets. The query spectra involve multi-stage (MSn) fragmentation beyond MS/MS — single-step fragmentation is FIORA's biggest limitation You need guaranteed train/test compound separation for CFM-ID comparisons — CFM-ID was trained on METLIN17, so this separation is not guaranteed Structures exceed the training filter scope (compounds above 1000 Da or collision energies above 100 eV were excluded during model training) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Predict tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) from molecular structures using graph-neural-network fragmentation simulators (FIORA, with ICEBERG and CFM-ID as comparators), enabling spectral reference library expansion and benchmarking of prediction quality. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Predict tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) from molecular structures using graph-neural-network fragmentation simulators (FIORA, with ICEBERG and CFM-ID as comparators), enabling spectral reference library expansion and benchmarking of prediction quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectra involve multi-stage (MSn) fragmentation beyond MS/MS — single-step fragmentation is FIORA's biggest limitation You need guaranteed train/test compound separation for CFM-ID comparisons — CFM-ID was trained on METLIN17, so this separation is not guaranteed Structures exceed the training filter scope (compounds above 1000 Da or collision energies above 100 eV were excluded during model training)

skills.description: Use when a large set of candidate metabolite structures needs predicted ESI tandem mass spectra in both ionization modes so experimental MS/MS spectra can be matched to structures without experimental reference libraries.
skills.name: in-silico-msms-spectrum-prediction
skills.search_text: in-silico-msms-spectrum-prediction Use when a large set of candidate metabolite structures needs predicted ESI tandem mass spectra in both ionization modes so experimental MS/MS spectra can be matched to structures without experimental reference libraries. Experimental reference spectra already exist for the metabolites — an experimental spectral library will outperform predicted spectra, which remain an open problem per the article The candidate structures come from evolutionarily distant organisms (plant or bacterial metabolism) — the language model behind the candidates was trained and evaluated only on human metabolite structures No tandem MS data are available and only accurate-mass prioritization is possible — use mass-to-charge filtering of the DeepMet resource instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Predicts ESI MS/MS spectra for candidate metabolite structures (e.g., DeepMet-generated SMILES) in positive and negative ionization modes using CFM-ID, producing an in silico spectral library that enables exact-structure assignment of held-out metabolites beyond accurate-mass prioritization alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Predicts ESI MS/MS spectra for candidate metabolite structures (e.g., DeepMet-generated SMILES) in positive and negative ionization modes using CFM-ID, producing an in silico spectral library that enables exact-structure assignment of held-out metabolites beyond accurate-mass prioritization alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Experimental reference spectra already exist for the metabolites — an experimental spectral library will outperform predicted spectra, which remain an open problem per the article The candidate structures come from evolutionarily distant organisms (plant or bacterial metabolism) — the language model behind the candidates was trained and evaluated only on human metabolite structures No tandem MS data are available and only accurate-mass prioritization is possible — use mass-to-charge filtering of the DeepMet resource instead

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolic model (e.g., a Reconstructor-generated SBML GENRE like NCGM2.S1.xml) and need to identify which genes are essential versus non-essential for biomass production.
skills.name: in-silico-single-gene-deletion-analysis
skills.search_text: in-silico-single-gene-deletion-analysis Use when you have a metabolic model (e.g., a Reconstructor-generated SBML GENRE like NCGM2.S1.xml) and need to identify which genes are essential versus non-essential for biomass production. Input is an unannotated genome or raw sequence data rather than a reconstructed, gap-filled metabolic model in SBML format The model does not yet support nonzero biomass flux, since deletion screening on a non-producing model yields meaningless essentiality calls (perform additional Type 3 gap-filling first) http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Generates testable gene essentiality hypotheses by running COBRApy flux balance analysis and single-gene deletion screening on a genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction (GENRE), classifying each gene as essential or non-essential based on loss of biomass production. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Generates testable gene essentiality hypotheses by running COBRApy flux balance analysis and single-gene deletion screening on a genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction (GENRE), classifying each gene as essential or non-essential based on loss of biomass production.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unannotated genome or raw sequence data rather than a reconstructed, gap-filled metabolic model in SBML format The model does not yet support nonzero biomass flux, since deletion screening on a non-producing model yields meaningless essentiality calls (perform additional Type 3 gap-filling first)

skills.description: Use when compiling a training set from public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, LipidMaps) while a separate annotation reference (NIST 20, LipidBlast) will score the evaluation set, to prevent overlap.
skills.name: in-silico-spectra-exclusion
skills.search_text: in-silico-spectra-exclusion Use when compiling a training set from public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, LipidMaps) while a separate annotation reference (NIST 20, LipidBlast) will score the evaluation set, to prevent overlap. When the training and evaluation annotation libraries are disjoint (no shared compounds), the exclusion step has nothing to filter and is unnecessary When the input MSP blocks are already part of the evaluation set (e.g. the experimental MS/MS spectra being annotated), removing LipidBlast/NIST 20 coverage would delete the data you intend to predict on When the goal is in-silico model benchmarking against a single unified library rather than the case-study train/evaluate split described here http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filters a curated training set by removing MSP blocks whose compounds are already covered in independent reference libraries (here LipidBlast in-silico and NIST 20) so that evaluation-set annotations cannot leak into model training. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00804-5
skills.summary: Filters a curated training set by removing MSP blocks whose compounds are already covered in independent reference libraries (here LipidBlast in-silico and NIST 20) so that evaluation-set annotations cannot leak into model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the training and evaluation annotation libraries are disjoint (no shared compounds), the exclusion step has nothing to filter and is unnecessary When the input MSP blocks are already part of the evaluation set (e.g. the experimental MS/MS spectra being annotated), removing LipidBlast/NIST 20 coverage would delete the data you intend to predict on When the goal is in-silico model benchmarking against a single unified library rather than the case-study train/evaluate split described here

skills.description: Use when comparing two or more in-silico lipid fragmentation libraries by enumerating per-class and per-adduct library entry counts and feature annotation counts to reveal coverage gaps such as classes unique to one library.
skills.name: in-silico-spectral-library-benchmarking
skills.search_text: in-silico-spectral-library-benchmarking Use when comparing two or more in-silico lipid fragmentation libraries by enumerating per-class and per-adduct library entry counts and feature annotation counts to reveal coverage gaps such as classes unique to one library. The input is already a per-class count matrix or single-library summary rather than paired annotation/library-composition tables from multiple libraries The analysis targets experimental/empirical MS/MS spectral libraries rather than in-silico lipid fragmentation libraries Only one library is available, so cross-library comparison of entries and annotations is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark in-silico lipidomics MS/MS libraries (MAVEN2's novel library, MS-DIAL, CalicoLipids) by tabulating library entries and annotated features per lipid class and adduct form, and flagging classes represented in only one library (e.g., OxPC only in MS-DIAL, CE only in CalicoLipids). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12080684
skills.summary: Benchmark in-silico lipidomics MS/MS libraries (MAVEN2's novel library, MS-DIAL, CalicoLipids) by tabulating library entries and annotated features per lipid class and adduct form, and flagging classes represented in only one library (e.g., OxPC only in MS-DIAL, CE only in CalicoLipids).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-class count matrix or single-library summary rather than paired annotation/library-composition tables from multiple libraries The analysis targets experimental/empirical MS/MS spectral libraries rather than in-silico lipid fragmentation libraries Only one library is available, so cross-library comparison of entries and annotations is impossible

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark a machine-learned (e.g., NEIMS) EI-MS predictor against experimental spectra before trusting its outputs for library building or matching.
skills.name: in-silico-spectrum-validation
skills.search_text: in-silico-spectrum-validation Use when you need to benchmark a machine-learned (e.g., NEIMS) EI-MS predictor against experimental spectra before trusting its outputs for library building or matching. The goal is fast library matching / compound identification ranking rather than assessing spectrum prediction quality — use FastEI's HNSW + Word2vec matching instead Spectra arise from ionization methods other than electron ionization (EI), since NEIMS was trained only for EI-MS prediction from ECFPs The molecules lack valid SMILES or cannot be parsed into ECFP fingerprints by RDKit http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Validates the quality of in-silico EI mass spectra predicted by the unmodified NEIMS model by computing weighted cosine similarity (WCS) between each predicted spectrum and its experimental counterpart, confirming that ~78% of the 11,499 NIST 2017 test molecules achieve WCS > 0.7. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Validates the quality of in-silico EI mass spectra predicted by the unmodified NEIMS model by computing weighted cosine similarity (WCS) between each predicted spectrum and its experimental counterpart, confirming that ~78% of the 11,499 NIST 2017 test molecules achieve WCS > 0.7.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is fast library matching / compound identification ranking rather than assessing spectrum prediction quality — use FastEI's HNSW + Word2vec matching instead Spectra arise from ionization methods other than electron ionization (EI), since NEIMS was trained only for EI-MS prediction from ECFPs The molecules lack valid SMILES or cannot be parsed into ECFP fingerprints by RDKit

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular network (classical or feature-based) contains nodes lacking chemical class labels and you have tab-separated annotation tables with Scan and SMILES columns from library hits, NAP, or DEREPLICATOR to propagate ClassyFire taxonomy onto the network.
skills.name: in-silico-structure-annotation-integration
skills.search_text: in-silico-structure-annotation-integration Use when a GNPS molecular network (classical or feature-based) contains nodes lacking chemical class labels and you have tab-separated annotation tables with Scan and SMILES columns from library hits, NAP, or DEREPLICATOR to propagate ClassyFire taxonomy onto the network. The molecular network has not yet been generated via GNPS — build the network first, then annotate Inputs are MS/MS spectra without any in silico or library structure annotations (no SMILES available) — this skill needs SMILES-bearing annotation tables You want substructure/Motif-level (MS2LDA) annotation rather than chemical class propagation — use the separate Mass2Motif mapping workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Integrate in silico structure annotations (GNPS library hits, NAP, DEREPLICATOR) into a GNPS mass spectral molecular network, converting SMILES to InChIKeys and retrieving ClassyFire chemical classes to build a per-node and per-molecular-family chemical taxonomy. This skill grounds MolNetEnhancer's chemical-annotation layer for metabolomics networks. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Integrate in silico structure annotations (GNPS library hits, NAP, DEREPLICATOR) into a GNPS mass spectral molecular network, converting SMILES to InChIKeys and retrieving ClassyFire chemical classes to build a per-node and per-molecular-family chemical taxonomy. This skill grounds MolNetEnhancer's chemical-annotation layer for metabolomics networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecular network has not yet been generated via GNPS — build the network first, then annotate Inputs are MS/MS spectra without any in silico or library structure annotations (no SMILES available) — this skill needs SMILES-bearing annotation tables You want substructure/Motif-level (MS2LDA) annotation rather than chemical class propagation — use the separate Mass2Motif mapping workflow instead

skills.description: Use when a ConCISE consensus annotation run must be validated: compare consensus superclass/class/subclass assignments against GNPS-reported compound identities to compute true positive rates and check the >95% criterion.
skills.name: in-silico-structure-classification-evaluation
skills.search_text: in-silico-structure-classification-evaluation Use when a ConCISE consensus annotation run must be validated: compare consensus superclass/class/subclass assignments against GNPS-reported compound identities to compute true positive rates and check the >95% criterion. Input lacks GNPS-reported compound identities for the ion features, so true positive rates against ground truth cannot be computed The consensus annotations were produced with NPClassifier ontologies rather than ClassyFire ChemOnt, so they cannot be judged against the paper's ClassyFire-based >95% TPR criterion The goal is novel metabolite annotation rather than validation of an existing consensus annotation output http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluate the correctness of consensus chemical classifications produced by fusing GNPS molecular networking, spectral library matching, and in silico (SIRIUS/CANOPUS) predictions by computing true positive rates against GNPS-reported compound identities across the ChemOnt hierarchy. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: Evaluate the correctness of consensus chemical classifications produced by fusing GNPS molecular networking, spectral library matching, and in silico (SIRIUS/CANOPUS) predictions by computing true positive rates against GNPS-reported compound identities across the ChemOnt hierarchy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks GNPS-reported compound identities for the ion features, so true positive rates against ground truth cannot be computed The consensus annotations were produced with NPClassifier ontologies rather than ClassyFire ChemOnt, so they cannot be judged against the paper's ClassyFire-based >95% TPR criterion The goal is novel metabolite annotation rather than validation of an existing consensus annotation output

skills.description: Use when you need to rank candidate molecules for an unknown metabolite from accurate-mass MS/MS peak lists without reference spectra, e.g. candidate lists from PubChem for CASMI-style contests or untargeted LC-MS identification.
skills.name: in-silico-substructure-fragmentation
skills.search_text: in-silico-substructure-fragmentation Use when you need to rank candidate molecules for an unknown metabolite from accurate-mass MS/MS peak lists without reference spectra, e.g. candidate lists from PubChem for CASMI-style contests or untargeted LC-MS identification. When no accurate-mass MS/MS or MSn peak data are available and only a feature table without fragmentation is provided When reference spectra exist and a spectral-library match would suffice, since MAGMa is designed for annotating spectra in the absence of informative reference spectra When candidate structures contain elements outside the assumed set (C/H/N/O/P/S) or exceed the mass range, unless the halogen supplement option and candidate database are extended accordingly http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotate MS/MS fragment peaks by matching them against substructures generated in silico from candidate chemical structures, computing intensity-weighted penalty scores to rank candidates — the core of the MAGMa (Ms Annotation based on in silico Generated Metabolites) approach. metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033
skills.summary: Annotate MS/MS fragment peaks by matching them against substructures generated in silico from candidate chemical structures, computing intensity-weighted penalty scores to rank candidates — the core of the MAGMa (Ms Annotation based on in silico Generated Metabolites) approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no accurate-mass MS/MS or MSn peak data are available and only a feature table without fragmentation is provided When reference spectra exist and a spectral-library match would suffice, since MAGMa is designed for annotating spectra in the absence of informative reference spectra When candidate structures contain elements outside the assumed set (C/H/N/O/P/S) or exceed the mass range, unless the halogen supplement option and candidate database are extended accordingly

skills.description: Use when a simulated gold-standard LC-MS/MS dataset is needed: a known FASTA proteome must be converted into a finite, size-controlled peptide list so that identification recovery (PSMs at 1% q-value) can be measured against ground truth.
skills.name: in-silico-tryptic-digestion
skills.search_text: in-silico-tryptic-digestion Use when a simulated gold-standard LC-MS/MS dataset is needed: a known FASTA proteome must be converted into a finite, size-controlled peptide list so that identification recovery (PSMs at 1% q-value) can be measured against ground truth. The input is already a peptide list or peak properties csv — go directly to csv_to_peak_properties rather than re-digesting The goal is identification of real, uncharacterized experimental mzML data — in-silico digestion is for generating gold-standard simulations with known ground truth, not for analyzing measured runs A non-tryptic or modified-proteome digestion is required beyond what the peptide fragmentation/RT setup (PeptideFragmentor, DeepLC) supports http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Digest a reference proteome (e.g. S. cerevisiae) in silico with trypsin to generate defined peptide sets of controlled size, which serve as the ground-truth input for building SMITER peak properties dicts and benchmarking identification rates in simulated LC-MS/MS runs. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/genes12030396
skills.summary: Digest a reference proteome (e.g. S. cerevisiae) in silico with trypsin to generate defined peptide sets of controlled size, which serve as the ground-truth input for building SMITER peak properties dicts and benchmarking identification rates in simulated LC-MS/MS runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a peptide list or peak properties csv — go directly to csv_to_peak_properties rather than re-digesting The goal is identification of real, uncharacterized experimental mzML data — in-silico digestion is for generating gold-standard simulations with known ground truth, not for analyzing measured runs A non-tryptic or modified-proteome digestion is required beyond what the peptide fragmentation/RT setup (PeptideFragmentor, DeepLC) supports

skills.description: Use when working with untargeted, time-resolved direct-injection (e.g. DBDI-FT-ICR-MS) MS data lacking chromatographic separation, and multiple ion species from one analyte (adducts/in-source fragments) must be putatively identified.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-and-adduct-annotation
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-and-adduct-annotation Use when working with untargeted, time-resolved direct-injection (e.g. DBDI-FT-ICR-MS) MS data lacking chromatographic separation, and multiple ion species from one analyte (adducts/in-source fragments) must be putatively identified. Data is LC-MS with chromatographic separation, where coelution rather than temporal-profile correlation drives ion-species assignment Input is already a curated feature table without time-resolved XIC traces — the correlation step requires uniform-length temporal intensity profiles per feature Only a single ion species per analyte is expected and no adduct/fragment deconvolution is needed; use matchms preprocessing alone instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Putative annotation of in-source fragments (e.g. [M-H2O+H]+) and in-source generated adducts (e.g. [M+nO+H]+) in direct-injection plasma ionization MS datasets by combining pointwise correlation of XIC traces with exact mass-difference matching against a customizable rule set. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad088
skills.summary: Putative annotation of in-source fragments (e.g. [M-H2O+H]+) and in-source generated adducts (e.g. [M+nO+H]+) in direct-injection plasma ionization MS datasets by combining pointwise correlation of XIC traces with exact mass-difference matching against a customizable rule set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is LC-MS with chromatographic separation, where coelution rather than temporal-profile correlation drives ion-species assignment Input is already a curated feature table without time-resolved XIC traces — the correlation step requires uniform-length temporal intensity profiles per feature Only a single ion species per analyte is expected and no adduct/fragment deconvolution is needed; use matchms preprocessing alone instead

skills.description: Use when processing raw LC-MS (mzML or Bruker .d) nontargeted metabolomics data and you need to collapse features into groups annotated as isotopes, adducts, or in-source fragments to remove false-positive features.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-annotation
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-annotation Use when processing raw LC-MS (mzML or Bruker .d) nontargeted metabolomics data and you need to collapse features into groups annotated as isotopes, adducts, or in-source fragments to remove false-positive features. The parent ion is not detected because of complete fragmentation in the ion source — MassCube cannot automatically annotate such ISFs Input is already a curated feature table lacking MS/MS spectra and scan-level peak shapes, since both ISF criteria (parent MS/MS membership and scan-to-scan Pearson correlation) require scan-level data The goal is direct metabolite identification — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification, only feature-group annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) and alternative adducts among co-eluting LC-MS features using MassCube's peak grouping module, which combines MS/MS-spectrum membership with scan-to-scan peak-shape correlation. Applied to the Metabolome Atlas of the Aging Mouse Brain it reports 2604 ISFs and 6055 alternative adducts merged into unique peak groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) and alternative adducts among co-eluting LC-MS features using MassCube's peak grouping module, which combines MS/MS-spectrum membership with scan-to-scan peak-shape correlation. Applied to the Metabolome Atlas of the Aging Mouse Brain it reports 2604 ISFs and 6055 alternative adducts merged into unique peak groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The parent ion is not detected because of complete fragmentation in the ion source — MassCube cannot automatically annotate such ISFs Input is already a curated feature table lacking MS/MS spectra and scan-level peak shapes, since both ISF criteria (parent MS/MS membership and scan-to-scan Pearson correlation) require scan-level data The goal is direct metabolite identification — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification, only feature-group annotation

skills.description: Use when input is full-scan (MS1-only) LC-MS data in mzML/mzXML — e.g., files from GNPS/MassIVE lacking MS/MS — and the goal is to generate pseudo MS/MS spectra from in-source fragments for library-based structural annotation.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-correlation-clustering
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-correlation-clustering Use when input is full-scan (MS1-only) LC-MS data in mzML/mzXML — e.g., files from GNPS/MassIVE lacking MS/MS — and the goal is to generate pseudo MS/MS spectra from in-source fragments for library-based structural annotation. Input already contains DDA MS/MS spectra for the features of interest — direct MS/MS spectral matching on real MS/MS is preferred; ms1-id's pseudo-spectrum route is for MS1-only data Data are MALDI imaging runs where fragments below m/z 100 are absent — use the gnps_minmz100 indexed library and the MSI workflow instead of the LC-MS correlation pipeline Features lack sufficient chromatographic overlap (fewer than 4 consecutive shared MS1 scans or Pearson r < 0.80) — pseudo MS/MS cannot be reliably constructed for them http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Clusters MS1 metabolic features by correlating extracted ion chromatograms so that in/post-source fragments co-eluting with a precursor can be merged into pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra, enabling structural annotation of MS1-only LC-MS data via the ms1-id package. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Clusters MS1 metabolic features by correlating extracted ion chromatograms so that in/post-source fragments co-eluting with a precursor can be merged into pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra, enabling structural annotation of MS1-only LC-MS data via the ms1-id package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input already contains DDA MS/MS spectra for the features of interest — direct MS/MS spectral matching on real MS/MS is preferred; ms1-id's pseudo-spectrum route is for MS1-only data Data are MALDI imaging runs where fragments below m/z 100 are absent — use the gnps_minmz100 indexed library and the MSI workflow instead of the LC-MS correlation pipeline Features lack sufficient chromatographic overlap (fewer than 4 consecutive shared MS1 scans or Pearson r < 0.80) — pseudo MS/MS cannot be reliably constructed for them

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature table contains spurious features suspected to be in-source fragments, and you need to flag ISF features and their precursor-fragment relationships from mzXML/feature-table inputs.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-identification-lcms
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-identification-lcms Use when an LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature table contains spurious features suspected to be in-source fragments, and you need to flag ISF features and their precursor-fragment relationships from mzXML/feature-table inputs. The analysis goal is adduct/isotope annotation only — CAMERA adduct and isotope annotation can only be used for XCMS-only ISFrag analysis, not custom feature tables The data are MS2-only tandem spectra without MS1 feature tables — ISFrag operates on MS1 metabolite feature tables, not raw MS2 peak lists A fully validated ISF annotation already exists in the feature table, e.g. the exported table already contains ISF_level, Num_Level2, and Num_Level1 columns http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Identifies and annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) in LC-MS metabolite feature tables using the ISFrag R package, which runs a three-level identification cascade (find.level3 → find.level2 → find.level1) over MS1 features with MS2 annotation support. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01644
skills.summary: Identifies and annotates in-source fragments (ISFs) in LC-MS metabolite feature tables using the ISFrag R package, which runs a three-level identification cascade (find.level3 → find.level2 → find.level1) over MS1 features with MS2 annotation support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is adduct/isotope annotation only — CAMERA adduct and isotope annotation can only be used for XCMS-only ISFrag analysis, not custom feature tables The data are MS2-only tandem spectra without MS1 feature tables — ISFrag operates on MS1 metabolite feature tables, not raw MS2 peak lists A fully validated ISF annotation already exists in the feature table, e.g. the exported table already contains ISF_level, Num_Level2, and Num_Level1 columns

skills.description: Use when annotating LC/HRMS peaks from MS1-only or DDA/DIA untargeted metabolomics data where MS2 fragmentation spectra are absent or sparse, and you want to leverage in-source fragments within composite spectra as surrogates for MS/MS library matches.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-matching-to-msms
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-matching-to-msms Use when annotating LC/HRMS peaks from MS1-only or DDA/DIA untargeted metabolomics data where MS2 fragmentation spectra are absent or sparse, and you want to leverage in-source fragments within composite spectra as surrogates for MS/MS library matches. Every detected peak of interest already has high-quality DDA MS/2 fragmentation spectra that can be searched directly against MS/MS libraries without composite spectra Input is already a peak/feature table without the underlying m/z-RT chromatographic information required by IDSL.IPA/IDSL.CSA (no raw mzXML/mzML/netCDF or peaklists to aggregate) The goal is de novo compound identification rather than library-based similarity annotation of peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates composite spectra (CSA) libraries from MS1-only LC/HRMS data by grouping correlating co-eluting ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments), then matches those in-source fragments against MS/MS reference libraries (e.g. NIST 2020) via IDSL.FSA mass spectral similarity searches to annotate peaks lacking MS2 data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00376
skills.summary: Generates composite spectra (CSA) libraries from MS1-only LC/HRMS data by grouping correlating co-eluting ions (isotopologues, adducts, in-source fragments), then matches those in-source fragments against MS/MS reference libraries (e.g. NIST 2020) via IDSL.FSA mass spectral similarity searches to annotate peaks lacking MS2 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Every detected peak of interest already has high-quality DDA MS/2 fragmentation spectra that can be searched directly against MS/MS libraries without composite spectra Input is already a peak/feature table without the underlying m/z-RT chromatographic information required by IDSL.IPA/IDSL.CSA (no raw mzXML/mzML/netCDF or peaklists to aggregate) The goal is de novo compound identification rather than library-based similarity annotation of peaks

skills.description: Use when processing untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics data (e.g. DDA/DIA/fullscan mzXML from NIST plasma-style acquisitions) where ISF features may be misannotated as real metabolites.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-recognition
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-recognition Use when processing untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics data (e.g. DDA/DIA/fullscan mzXML from NIST plasma-style acquisitions) where ISF features may be misannotated as real metabolites. When CAMERA adduct and isotope annotation is required but the feature table was not generated by XCMS only (CAMERA annotation can only be used for XCMS-only ISFrag analysis) When the MS/MS reference library is not in msp format or the custom feature table does not follow the required m/z, rt, rtmin, rtmax, intensity column order with retention times in seconds When MS2 spectra have not been assigned/annotated to features, since find.level1/2/3 operate on the annotated feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 De novo recognition of in-source fragments (ISF) in LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature tables using the ISFrag R package, which flags MS1 features that are fragments of co-eluting precursor metabolites and could otherwise cause false metabolite annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01644
skills.summary: De novo recognition of in-source fragments (ISF) in LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature tables using the ISFrag R package, which flags MS1 features that are fragments of co-eluting precursor metabolites and could otherwise cause false metabolite annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When CAMERA adduct and isotope annotation is required but the feature table was not generated by XCMS only (CAMERA annotation can only be used for XCMS-only ISFrag analysis) When the MS/MS reference library is not in msp format or the custom feature table does not follow the required m/z, rt, rtmin, rtmax, intensity column order with retention times in seconds When MS2 spectra have not been assigned/annotated to features, since find.level1/2/3 operate on the annotated feature table

skills.description: Use when per-sample MGF clean consensus spectra from LC–MS/MS contain multiple ionization variants of one precursor (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) that must be collapsed to a single [M + H]+ ion entity before molecular networking.
skills.name: in-source-fragment-rule-matching
skills.search_text: in-source-fragment-rule-matching Use when per-sample MGF clean consensus spectra from LC–MS/MS contain multiple ionization variants of one precursor (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) that must be collapsed to a single [M + H]+ ion entity before molecular networking. When the goal is a spectral-similarity molecular network (SSMN) rather than merging ionization variants of the same precursor When input is already a deconvoluted feature table containing only single [M + H]+ ions per precursor, with no adduct/fragment/dimer multiplicity When the rules table does not cover the observed ion mode or chemistry (the article encodes positive-mode shifts; negative-mode handling requires an appropriate rules table) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Groups ionization variants (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) of the same precursor by matching m/z differences and fragmentation relationships against an ionization rules table, then uses an ionization variant annotation molecular network (IVAMN) with PageRank to select a single [M + H]+ representative ion per variant group. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Groups ionization variants (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) of the same precursor by matching m/z differences and fragmentation relationships against an ionization rules table, then uses an ionization variant annotation molecular network (IVAMN) with PageRank to select a single [M + H]+ representative ion per variant group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a spectral-similarity molecular network (SSMN) rather than merging ionization variants of the same precursor When input is already a deconvoluted feature table containing only single [M + H]+ ions per precursor, with no adduct/fragment/dimer multiplicity When the rules table does not cover the observed ion mode or chemistry (the article encodes positive-mode shifts; negative-mode handling requires an appropriate rules table)

skills.description: Use when a RAMClustR-clustered feature table (post-XCMS MS and idMS/MS features with cluster memberships and a feature-by-sample abundance matrix) must be converted into deconvoluted spectra for spectral matching or annotation.
skills.name: in-source-spectrum-reconstruction
skills.search_text: in-source-spectrum-reconstruction Use when a RAMClustR-clustered feature table (post-XCMS MS and idMS/MS features with cluster memberships and a feature-by-sample abundance matrix) must be converted into deconvoluted spectra for spectral matching or annotation. Input is a raw XCMS peak table or xcmsObj that has not yet been clustered by RAMClustR — the spectra step needs cluster memberships to aggregate features Data come from a platform without in-source fragmentation or idMS/MS acquisition, so cluster members cannot be interpreted as co-eluting fragments of a single compound spectrum The goal is per-feature quantification rather than per-compound spectral intensities — the SpecAbund matrix deliberately condenses features into spectra and loses per-feature resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs in-source MS and idMS/MS spectra from RAMClustR feature clusters by computing weighted-mean intensities of member features, then exporting the spectra as MSP files and a condensed SpecAbund matrix of per-cluster spectral intensities per sample. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac501530d
skills.summary: Reconstructs in-source MS and idMS/MS spectra from RAMClustR feature clusters by computing weighted-mean intensities of member features, then exporting the spectra as MSP files and a condensed SpecAbund matrix of per-cluster spectral intensities per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw XCMS peak table or xcmsObj that has not yet been clustered by RAMClustR — the spectra step needs cluster memberships to aggregate features Data come from a platform without in-source fragmentation or idMS/MS acquisition, so cluster members cannot be interpreted as co-eluting fragments of a single compound spectrum The goal is per-feature quantification rather than per-compound spectral intensities — the SpecAbund matrix deliberately condenses features into spectra and loses per-feature resolution

skills.description: Use when building or extending a reference database of metabolite 13C-13C connectivity networks (INADEQUATE-style) from public chemical shift data (BMRB), or when computing per-compound ambiguity (CA/CT) to weight downstream compound annotation confidence.
skills.name: inadequate-connectivity-simulation
skills.search_text: inadequate-connectivity-simulation Use when building or extending a reference database of metabolite 13C-13C connectivity networks (INADEQUATE-style) from public chemical shift data (BMRB), or when computing per-compound ambiguity (CA/CT) to weight downstream compound annotation confidence. The query data are already picked, clustered peak networks ready to be matched — use pyINETA's match step, not the database simulation. The compounds of interest have no BMRB structural information or no 13C chemical shifts, so no connectivity simulation can be grounded. The study requires quantitation or isotope-tracking of 13C enrichment rather than database construction for connectivity matching. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Generates a simulated INADEQUATE database of metabolites from BMRB structural information and 1D 13C chemical shifts, with a per-compound ambiguity score (CA/CT) reflecting assignment uncertainty. This simulated database is the reference that pyINETA matches peak networks against to identify metabolites in query INADEQUATE spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: Generates a simulated INADEQUATE database of metabolites from BMRB structural information and 1D 13C chemical shifts, with a per-compound ambiguity score (CA/CT) reflecting assignment uncertainty. This simulated database is the reference that pyINETA matches peak networks against to identify metabolites in query INADEQUATE spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data are already picked, clustered peak networks ready to be matched — use pyINETA's match step, not the database simulation. The compounds of interest have no BMRB structural information or no 13C chemical shifts, so no connectivity simulation can be grounded. The study requires quantitation or isotope-tracking of 13C enrichment rather than database construction for connectivity matching.

skills.description: Use when you have INADEQUATE 13C-13C NMR spectra from isotope-labeled metabolomics samples (e.g. 13C-labeled amino acid feeding studies) and need automated compound annotation plus fragment information for unknowns.
skills.name: inadequate-nmr-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: inadequate-nmr-pipeline-execution Use when you have INADEQUATE 13C-13C NMR spectra from isotope-labeled metabolomics samples (e.g. 13C-labeled amino acid feeding studies) and need automated compound annotation plus fragment information for unknowns. Input spectra are proton-only (1D 1H or 13C) rather than INADEQUATE 13C-13C correlation experiments — the pipeline's network filtering and database matching depend on INADEQUATE connectivity. No complementary 13C-JRES data exists and the goal is not to match networks against the simulated INADEQUATE metabolite database — the integration step will not add value. The sample cannot be isotopically labeled; the method relies on 13C labeling for the INADEQUATE experiment to provide structural connectivity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Execute the PyINETA end-to-end INADEQUATE NMR metabolomics pipeline: load and reference spectra, pick peaks, cluster them into compound networks, match networks to a simulated INADEQUATE metabolite database, and integrate with a complementary 13C-JRES experiment. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: Execute the PyINETA end-to-end INADEQUATE NMR metabolomics pipeline: load and reference spectra, pick peaks, cluster them into compound networks, match networks to a simulated INADEQUATE metabolite database, and integrate with a complementary 13C-JRES experiment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are proton-only (1D 1H or 13C) rather than INADEQUATE 13C-13C correlation experiments — the pipeline's network filtering and database matching depend on INADEQUATE connectivity. No complementary 13C-JRES data exists and the goal is not to match networks against the simulated INADEQUATE metabolite database — the integration step will not add value. The sample cannot be isotopically labeled; the method relies on 13C labeling for the INADEQUATE experiment to provide structural connectivity.

skills.description: Use when you have filtered networks of picked peaks from an INADEQUATE NMR spectrum (e.g. from PyINETA's cluster/find steps) and need to identify which metabolites from a simulated INADEQUATE database produced them.
skills.name: inadequate-spectral-database-search
skills.search_text: inadequate-spectral-database-search Use when you have filtered networks of picked peaks from an INADEQUATE NMR spectrum (e.g. from PyINETA's cluster/find steps) and need to identify which metabolites from a simulated INADEQUATE database produced them. Query data are not INADEQUATE peak networks (e.g. plain 1D or JRES peak lists without connectivity) — the matching relies on double-quantum relationships between coupled carbons Peaks have not yet been filtered into networks of peaks from the same compound — matching expects network-level input from the find step Input files exceed the repository's provided example size (example2 inputs >100 Mb are not shipped; contact the Edison lab for raw files) http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Match filtered INADEQUATE peak networks against a simulated INADEQUATE database of metabolites using PyINETA's matching module, scoring each candidate compound with hit and coverage scores to identify metabolites present in the query spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: Match filtered INADEQUATE peak networks against a simulated INADEQUATE database of metabolites using PyINETA's matching module, scoring each candidate compound with hit and coverage scores to identify metabolites present in the query spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data are not INADEQUATE peak networks (e.g. plain 1D or JRES peak lists without connectivity) — the matching relies on double-quantum relationships between coupled carbons Peaks have not yet been filtered into networks of peaks from the same compound — matching expects network-level input from the find step Input files exceed the repository's provided example size (example2 inputs >100 Mb are not shipped; contact the Edison lab for raw files)

skills.description: Use when you have an mzmine-processed FBMN feature table with MS/MS spectra and need to benchmark how many features get an InChI from GNPS strict vs iterative weighted analog search.
skills.name: inchi-annotation-counting
skills.search_text: inchi-annotation-counting Use when you have an mzmine-processed FBMN feature table with MS/MS spectra and need to benchmark how many features get an InChI from GNPS strict vs iterative weighted analog search. Your goal is de novo structure elucidation or molecular formula prediction rather than benchmarking library-search InChI coverage. Your input is raw LC-MS/MS data not yet processed into an mzmine FBMN feature table and MGF export — run MZmine 4 feature-based molecular networking first. You need matched MS/MS spectra with exact library hits only (strict precision matters more than return rate); the iterative analog search deliberately trades precision for coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies how many features in an FBMN feature table receive an InChI identifier from a GNPS spectral library search, comparing the strict single-query baseline against the GNPS iterative weighted analog search (GNPS I). Applied to the P. mutica LC-MS/MS case (MassIVE MSV95596), it verifies the reported return-rate improvement from 187/754 (25%) to 650/754 (89%). metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Quantifies how many features in an FBMN feature table receive an InChI identifier from a GNPS spectral library search, comparing the strict single-query baseline against the GNPS iterative weighted analog search (GNPS I). Applied to the P. mutica LC-MS/MS case (MassIVE MSV95596), it verifies the reported return-rate improvement from 187/754 (25%) to 650/754 (89%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is de novo structure elucidation or molecular formula prediction rather than benchmarking library-search InChI coverage. Your input is raw LC-MS/MS data not yet processed into an mzmine FBMN feature table and MGF export — run MZmine 4 feature-based molecular networking first. You need matched MS/MS spectra with exact library hits only (strict precision matters more than return rate); the iterative analog search deliberately trades precision for coverage.

skills.description: Use when raw natural-product structure tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz, nominal.tsv.gz) hold SMILES identifiers or compound names, and a standardized InChI column is required for downstream harmonization or database upload.
skills.name: inchi-generation-from-structures
skills.search_text: inchi-generation-from-structures Use when raw natural-product structure tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz, nominal.tsv.gz) hold SMILES identifiers or compound names, and a standardized InChI column is required for downstream harmonization or database upload. Input records already carry validated InChI identifiers and only need loading — re-running sanitization on correct salts, charged or dimeric molecules will cause an unwanted 'sanitization' step that may degrade them The goal is structure-organism pair filtering or reference validation (the filter_dirty.R stage), not chemical structure standardization Names must be mapped to organism taxonomy rather than translated to structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Standardizes heterogeneous natural-product chemical structure inputs (SMILES strings and chemical names) into InChI identifiers using RDKit parsing, MolVS sanitization, and OPSIN name-to-structure translation, as implemented in the LOTUS lotus-processor pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Standardizes heterogeneous natural-product chemical structure inputs (SMILES strings and chemical names) into InChI identifiers using RDKit parsing, MolVS sanitization, and OPSIN name-to-structure translation, as implemented in the LOTUS lotus-processor pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input records already carry validated InChI identifiers and only need loading — re-running sanitization on correct salts, charged or dimeric molecules will cause an unwanted 'sanitization' step that may degrade them The goal is structure-organism pair filtering or reference validation (the filter_dirty.R stage), not chemical structure standardization Names must be mapped to organism taxonomy rather than translated to structures

skills.description: Use when curating or merging chemical structure collections from multiple provenance where duplicate/same-core molecules must be de-duplicated into one canonical entry while retaining stereochemical variants.
skills.name: inchi-key-based-structure-unification
skills.search_text: inchi-key-based-structure-unification Use when curating or merging chemical structure collections from multiple provenance where duplicate/same-core molecules must be de-duplicated into one canonical entry while retaining stereochemical variants. When the goal is to preserve every stereochemical or tautomeric duplicate as a separate top-level record — the compiler's whole point is collapsing them under one parent entry When input molecules fail ChEMBL/RDKit parsing or carry ChEMBL error code ≥ 6 — those are rejected upstream and never reach the unification step When you only need exact-structure matching including stereochemistry (originalInchiKey), not the stereochemistry-free core grouping this skill performs http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Unifies molecular structures originating from multiple open natural-product sources into single UniqueNaturalProduct entries by grouping on InChIKey identity stripped of stereochemistry, preserving original stereochemical structures as nested variants and assigning CNP identifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00478-9
skills.summary: Unifies molecular structures originating from multiple open natural-product sources into single UniqueNaturalProduct entries by grouping on InChIKey identity stripped of stereochemistry, preserving original stereochemical structures as nested variants and assigning CNP identifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to preserve every stereochemical or tautomeric duplicate as a separate top-level record — the compiler's whole point is collapsing them under one parent entry When input molecules fail ChEMBL/RDKit parsing or carry ChEMBL error code ≥ 6 — those are rejected upstream and never reach the unification step When you only need exact-structure matching including stereochemistry (originalInchiKey), not the stereochemistry-free core grouping this skill performs

skills.description: Use when preparing query and reference libraries for spectral database lookup: overlapping molecules between sides would inflate recall, so InChI-key-based disjointness must be asserted before ranking.
skills.name: inchi-key-molecule-deduplication
skills.search_text: inchi-key-molecule-deduplication Use when preparing query and reference libraries for spectral database lookup: overlapping molecules between sides would inflate recall, so InChI-key-based disjointness must be asserted before ranking. When query and reference libraries are intentionally the same set (e.g. self-match sanity checks) — the strict non-overlap assertion would fail. When the candidate list has no InChI strings available to generate inchi_key hashes, since dedup is keyed on the InChI-derived hash. When deduplicating within a single library for training data cleaning, where cross-side overlap is not the concern being enforced. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Deduplicate candidate spectra/molecule lists by generating canonical InChI keys with RDKit (Chem.InchiToInchiKey) and partitioning the 100-molecule smallmols sample into two strictly non-overlapping 50-molecule query and main libraries, enforcing the disjointness with an assertion before library matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Deduplicate candidate spectra/molecule lists by generating canonical InChI keys with RDKit (Chem.InchiToInchiKey) and partitioning the 100-molecule smallmols sample into two strictly non-overlapping 50-molecule query and main libraries, enforcing the disjointness with an assertion before library matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When query and reference libraries are intentionally the same set (e.g. self-match sanity checks) — the strict non-overlap assertion would fail. When the candidate list has no InChI strings available to generate inchi_key hashes, since dedup is keyed on the InChI-derived hash. When deduplicating within a single library for training data cleaning, where cross-side overlap is not the concern being enforced.

skills.name: inchi-smiles-annotation-checking
skills.search_text: inchi-smiles-annotation-checking Use when imported MS/MS spectra (MGF, msp, mzML, mzXML, JSON) carry inconsistent, wrongly labeled, or missing structure annotations (InChI, SMILES, InChIKey) or ionmode/adduct/charge fields that must be cleaned before scoring. The spectra are already cleaned and the task is peak filtering or similarity scoring (use select_by_mz, normalize_intensities, or cosine/modified cosine scores instead) The metadata problem is missing rather than incorrect annotations that need enrichment — matchms cleaning checks/corrects fields but does not harvest new metadata (consider MSMetaEnhancer for collecting library metadata from web services) Input is not mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectral data with a metadata block to harmonize http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 A metadata cleaning skill from the matchms ecosystem that checks, corrects, and harmonizes key spectrum metadata fields — compound name, structure annotations (InChI, SMILES, InChIKey), ionmode, adduct, and charge — so downstream similarity scoring runs on consistent annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02411

skills.description: Use when reference .msp blocks lack precomputed Fingerprint rows and contain only InChI: entries (or SMILES needing canonicalization), and dash-separated bit-location targets are required for IDSL_MINT transformer decoder training.
skills.name: inchi-to-smiles-structure-normalization
skills.search_text: inchi-to-smiles-structure-normalization Use when reference .msp blocks lack precomputed Fingerprint rows and contain only InChI: entries (or SMILES needing canonicalization), and dash-separated bit-location targets are required for IDSL_MINT transformer decoder training. The MSP block already carries a user-provided dash-separated `Fingerprint:` row — IDSL_MINT parses these directly instead of recomputing from structure. skills.search_text: inchikey-exact-match-accuracy-computation Use when evaluating de novo structure elucidation output (SELFIES/SMILES candidates from a spectrum-conditioned model) and you need the fraction of predictions whose full InChIKey string exactly equals the reference molecule's InChIKey. The evaluation target is structural similarity rather than identity — use Tanimoto similarity (Morgan, radius 2, 2048 bits) or MCES distance instead, since exact InChIKey match gives 0 credit for near-miss analogues. Only the carbon skeleton (first InChIKey block) matters — the paper's metric explicitly uses the full InChIKey, so partial-block matching is a different, more lenient evaluation. The benchmark is NIST23 — access is restricted due to commercial licensing, so this metric as reproduced here applies to the open MassSpecGym and NPLIB1 benchmarks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes Top-1/Top-10 exact-match accuracy on the full InChIKey string, comparing generated candidate structures against ground-truth reference molecules as used to benchmark MS-Bart and competing methods on MassSpecGym and NPLIB1. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Computes Top-1/Top-10 exact-match accuracy on the full InChIKey string, comparing generated candidate structures against ground-truth reference molecules as used to benchmark MS-Bart and competing methods on MassSpecGym and NPLIB1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The evaluation target is structural similarity rather than identity — use Tanimoto similarity (Morgan, radius 2, 2048 bits) or MCES distance instead, since exact InChIKey match gives 0 credit for near-miss analogues. Only the carbon skeleton (first InChIKey block) matters — the paper's metric explicitly uses the full InChIKey, so partial-block matching is a different, more lenient evaluation. The benchmark is NIST23 — access is restricted due to commercial licensing, so this metric as reproduced here applies to the open MassSpecGym and NPLIB1 benchmarks.

skills.search_text: inchikey-exact-match-accuracy-evaluation Use when benchmarking de novo structure elucidation from mass spectra on MassSpecGym/NPLIB1 test folds and you need Top-1/Top-10 exact-identity accuracy over full InChIKey strings for generated molecule sets. The analysis goal is structural similarity or substructure recovery rather than exact identity — use Top-k minimum MCES distance and maximum Tanimoto similarity (Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits) instead Candidates are intermediate representations (MIST-predicted 4096-bit Morgan fingerprints) rather than decodable molecular structures, so no InChIKey can be computed The evaluation dataset is restricted-access (e.g., NIST23, unavailable due to commercial licensing) and has no comparable ground-truth structure annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes Top-1/Top-10 identification accuracy by comparing generated candidate molecular structures (SELFIES decoded via RDKit) against ground-truth structures through full InChIKey exact match, the strictest identity metric used to benchmark mass-spectra-to-molecule models on MassSpecGym and NPLIB1. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Computes Top-1/Top-10 identification accuracy by comparing generated candidate molecular structures (SELFIES decoded via RDKit) against ground-truth structures through full InChIKey exact match, the strictest identity metric used to benchmark mass-spectra-to-molecule models on MassSpecGym and NPLIB1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is structural similarity or substructure recovery rather than exact identity — use Top-k minimum MCES distance and maximum Tanimoto similarity (Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits) instead Candidates are intermediate representations (MIST-predicted 4096-bit Morgan fingerprints) rather than decodable molecular structures, so no InChIKey can be computed The evaluation dataset is restricted-access (e.g., NIST23, unavailable due to commercial licensing) and has no comparable ground-truth structure annotations

skills.description: Use when a merged metabolite table contains multiple InChIKeys that share the same 14-character molecular-skeleton prefix (e.g. palmitate vs. palmitic acid) and entries must be reduced to one non-conjugated compound per pair.
skills.name: inchikey-protonation-layer-interpretation
skills.search_text: inchikey-protonation-layer-interpretation Use when a merged metabolite table contains multiple InChIKeys that share the same 14-character molecular-skeleton prefix (e.g. palmitate vs. palmitic acid) and entries must be reduced to one non-conjugated compound per pair. The input is a single-source table where conjugated base/acid duplicates were already resolved upstream (MMS marks this curation step as optional). InChIKeys are absent or non-standard, so the 14-character skeleton prefix and protonation layer cannot be compared reliably. Rows differ in skeleton or stereochemistry blocks, not just the protonation layer — those are distinct compounds, not conjugate pairs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Identifies conjugated base/acid compound pairs in a merged metabolite dataset by grouping InChIKeys on their first 14 skeleton characters and comparing the protonation-indicating final layer, enabling consolidation of duplicate acid/base forms with preserved source provenance. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13121167
skills.summary: Identifies conjugated base/acid compound pairs in a merged metabolite dataset by grouping InChIKeys on their first 14 skeleton characters and comparing the protonation-indicating final layer, enabling consolidation of duplicate acid/base forms with preserved source provenance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-source table where conjugated base/acid duplicates were already resolved upstream (MMS marks this curation step as optional). InChIKeys are absent or non-standard, so the 14-character skeleton prefix and protonation layer cannot be compared reliably. Rows differ in skeleton or stereochemistry blocks, not just the protonation layer — those are distinct compounds, not conjugate pairs.

skills.search_text: inchikey-skeleton-matching Use when building a ground-truth set of known BGC–spectrum links: you have MIBiG BGC records with structural annotations and GNPS library spectra with InChIKey annotations, but no direct spectral link, and need a chirality-insensitive structural join. The goal is to distinguish stereoisomers or chirality variants — first-block skeleton matching deliberately collapses them, so a full InChIKey match is required instead The metabolomics side lacks InChIKey annotations (e.g., unannotated GNPS molecular networking nodes) — no structural join key exists and the pairing cannot be performed Input spectra are experimental MS2 runs rather than GNPS library spectra with curated compound annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Links MIBiG biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) to GNPS library MS2 spectra by matching metabolite InChIKeys truncated to their first (skeleton) block, since MS2 spectra cannot resolve stereochemistry. skills.summary: Links MIBiG biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) to GNPS library MS2 spectra by matching metabolite InChIKeys truncated to their first (skeleton) block, since MS2 spectra cannot resolve stereochemistry. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to distinguish stereoisomers or chirality variants — first-block skeleton matching deliberately collapses them, so a full InChIKey match is required instead The metabolomics side lacks InChIKey annotations (e.g., unannotated GNPS molecular networking nodes) — no structural join key exists and the pairing cannot be performed Input spectra are experimental MS2 runs rather than GNPS library spectra with curated compound annotations

skills.search_text: inchikey-skeleton-prefix-matching Use when merging metabolite datasets that report heterogeneous non-systematic identifiers and need a systematic key to collapse conjugated base/acid pairs or duplicate entries before manual curation. When the input dataset already contains only unique, canonical InChIKeys with no conjugated base/acid duplicates — skeleton matching would collapse distinct protonation states that the user intentionally kept separate. When the dataset's InChIKeys are missing, truncated, or malformed (fewer than 27 characters), because the 14-character skeleton block cannot be reliably extracted. When the goal is synonym or duplicate detection that depends on name-level equivalence rather than structural equivalence — that is a later curation step ('synonym checking (duplicated information)') in the MMS, not this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Groups metabolite entries across merged datasets by comparing the first 14 characters (molecular-skeleton block) of their InChIKeys, so that structurally identical compounds are consolidated even when protonation state, charge, or conjugation differs between databases. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13121167
skills.summary: Groups metabolite entries across merged datasets by comparing the first 14 characters (molecular-skeleton block) of their InChIKeys, so that structurally identical compounds are consolidated even when protonation state, charge, or conjugation differs between databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input dataset already contains only unique, canonical InChIKeys with no conjugated base/acid duplicates — skeleton matching would collapse distinct protonation states that the user intentionally kept separate. When the dataset's InChIKeys are missing, truncated, or malformed (fewer than 27 characters), because the 14-character skeleton block cannot be reliably extracted. When the goal is synonym or duplicate detection that depends on name-level equivalence rather than structural equivalence — that is a later curation step ('synonym checking (duplicated information)') in the MMS, not this skill.

skills.description: Use when a curated MS/MS library needs unique-compound counts for reporting or validation, and each spectrum carries structure metadata (InChIKey or SMILES) that can serve as the de-duplication key.
skills.name: inchikey-smiles-compound-deduplication
skills.search_text: inchikey-smiles-compound-deduplication Use when a curated MS/MS library needs unique-compound counts for reporting or validation, and each spectrum carries structure metadata (InChIKey or SMILES) that can serve as the de-duplication key. Input spectra lack standardized structure annotations (no InChIKey/SMILES); de-duplicating on precursor m/z or adduct would conflate distinct isomers and compounds. The goal is per-spectrum bookkeeping (adducts, ionization modes, charge states) rather than compound-level statistics. Structure representations have not been harmonized yet; unstandardized SMILES variants (different tautomers or stereochemistry encodings) inflate the unique-compound count. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 De-duplicates MS/MS spectra by mapping each record's standardized chemical structure annotations (InChIKey/SMILES) to unique compound identifiers, so that library statistics report molecules rather than spectra. Used in Spectraverse to verify that 488,630 curated spectra collapse onto 44,237 unique small molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06256
skills.summary: De-duplicates MS/MS spectra by mapping each record's standardized chemical structure annotations (InChIKey/SMILES) to unique compound identifiers, so that library statistics report molecules rather than spectra. Used in Spectraverse to verify that 488,630 curated spectra collapse onto 44,237 unique small molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack standardized structure annotations (no InChIKey/SMILES); de-duplicating on precursor m/z or adduct would conflate distinct isomers and compounds. The goal is per-spectrum bookkeeping (adducts, ionization modes, charge states) rather than compound-level statistics. Structure representations have not been harmonized yet; unstandardized SMILES variants (different tautomers or stereochemistry encodings) inflate the unique-compound count.

skills.description: Use when preparing a candidate structure database (e.g. DNP, UNPD, GNPS libraries) for ISDB spectral matching, where duplicate structures and stereoisomers would otherwise inflate candidate ranking lists.
skills.name: inchikey-structure-dereplication
skills.search_text: inchikey-structure-dereplication Use when preparing a candidate structure database (e.g. DNP, UNPD, GNPS libraries) for ISDB spectral matching, where duplicate structures and stereoisomers would otherwise inflate candidate ranking lists. The analysis requires distinguishing stereoisomers (e.g. enantiomeric or diastereomeric assignment), since the first 14 InChIKey characters collapse them. Input entries lack resolvable biological source information down to species level, which the paper's downstream taxonomic pipeline requires. You are dereplicating at the spectra level rather than the structure level (e.g. merging duplicate GNPS library spectra) — this skill operates on structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Dereplicates candidate structures by converting them to InChIKeys and collapsing duplicate structures and stereoisomers using the first connectivity layer (first 14 characters) of the 27-character InChIKey, yielding a non-redundant structure list for spectral matching and taxonomically informed scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Dereplicates candidate structures by converting them to InChIKeys and collapsing duplicate structures and stereoisomers using the first connectivity layer (first 14 characters) of the 27-character InChIKey, yielding a non-redundant structure list for spectral matching and taxonomically informed scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires distinguishing stereoisomers (e.g. enantiomeric or diastereomeric assignment), since the first 14 InChIKey characters collapse them. Input entries lack resolvable biological source information down to species level, which the paper's downstream taxonomic pipeline requires. You are dereplicating at the spectra level rather than the structure level (e.g. merging duplicate GNPS library spectra) — this skill operates on structures.
