skills.search_text: inchikey-structure-hashing Use when a spectral or metabolite library (e.g., GNPS .mgf entries with structural identifiers) needs unique structural keys so duplicate structures and stereoisomers can be collapsed before benchmarking or annotation. When stereoisomers must be kept distinct — the first-layer (14-character) deduplication intentionally merges stereoisomers When entries lack structural identifiers (e.g., adduct entries without structures) — these are excluded upstream before hashing When the goal is full-structure identity including stereochemistry — use the full 27-character InChIKey rather than the first layer Converts chemical structures from library entries (e.g., GNPS spectral library metadata) to their 27-character InChIKey using RDKit, enabling structure deduplication and stereoisomer collapsing via the first InChIKey layer. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329

skills.search_text: inchikey-unique-count-aggregation Use when ms1-id annotations from multiple LC-MS modes must be reduced to unique-metabolite counts (distinct InChIKey strings) per mode and pooled, e.g. to benchmark annotation yield on a public cohort dataset. Input data already contain data-dependent MS/MS scans — standard MS/MS library search, not ms1-id pseudo-spectrum generation, is the appropriate route The goal is per-feature or per-sample annotation output rather than a cohort-level unique-metabolite tally; stop at the aligned feature table instead of deduplicating by InChIKey Data are MS imaging (imzML) — different cutoffs apply (minimum spectral usage 0.05 instead of 0.20), so the LC-MS count aggregation rules do not transfer directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aggregates ms1-id level 2/3 structural annotations of full-scan LC-MS data into per-mode and overall counts of unique metabolites by counting distinct InChIKey strings, used to reproduce the IBD stool cohort benchmark (3010/293/227/636; total 3802). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data already contain data-dependent MS/MS scans — standard MS/MS library search, not ms1-id pseudo-spectrum generation, is the appropriate route The goal is per-feature or per-sample annotation output rather than a cohort-level unique-metabolite tally; stop at the aligned feature table instead of deduplicating by InChIKey Data are MS imaging (imzML) — different cutoffs apply (minimum spectral usage 0.05 instead of 0.20), so the LC-MS count aggregation rules do not transfer directly

skills.description: Use when a retention-order or molecular-property model has been trained on one reference set (e.g., dataset_87) and you must quantify whether its performance transfers to unseen chromatographic runs before trusting it for annotation.
skills.name: independent-dataset-generalizability-evaluation
skills.search_text: independent-dataset-generalizability-evaluation Use when a retention-order or molecular-property model has been trained on one reference set (e.g., dataset_87) and you must quantify whether its performance transfers to unseen chromatographic runs before trusting it for annotation. The 'independent' datasets overlap compounds or analytical runs with the training reference set — transfer results would be optimistic and the comparison invalid. The task is within-reference-set model selection or hyperparameter tuning — use 5-fold cross-validation on the training set instead of external evaluation. The chromatographic system is outside the model's domain (e.g., HILIC, since ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems). http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Protocol for testing whether a retention-order model (e.g., ROASMI trained with a chosen molecular representation) generalizes beyond its training reference set by evaluating on truly independent chromatography datasets, as ROASMI did with 71 independent RPLC datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Protocol for testing whether a retention-order model (e.g., ROASMI trained with a chosen molecular representation) generalizes beyond its training reference set by evaluating on truly independent chromatography datasets, as ROASMI did with 71 independent RPLC datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The 'independent' datasets overlap compounds or analytical runs with the training reference set — transfer results would be optimistic and the comparison invalid. The task is within-reference-set model selection or hyperparameter tuning — use 5-fold cross-validation on the training set instead of external evaluation. The chromatographic system is outside the model's domain (e.g., HILIC, since ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems).

skills.name: independent-dataset-validation-reporting
skills.search_text: independent-dataset-validation-reporting Use when a new feature-clustering method must be validated against established tools (e.g. CAMERA) on a dataset independent of the one used to develop the method, with clustering-quality metrics reported in a reproducible table. The clustering method is being evaluated on the same dataset used for its development or parameter tuning — an independent dataset is required for unbiased validation The analysis goal is to perform or tune the feature clustering itself (e.g. setting ramclustR st/maxt parameters) rather than to benchmark and report comparative performance The dataset lacks idMS/MS (indiscriminant tandem MS) data, so MS/MS spectral similarity — the primary validation metric here — cannot be computed Benchmarking skill for validating feature-clustering performance (RAMClustR vs CAMERA's groupFWHM/groupCorr/groupDen) on an independent metabolomics dataset, reporting MS/MS spectral similarity, multi-feature cluster counts, and singleton percentages as a comparison table. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac501530d
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for validating feature-clustering performance (RAMClustR vs CAMERA's groupFWHM/groupCorr/groupDen) on an independent metabolomics dataset, reporting MS/MS spectral similarity, multi-feature cluster counts, and singleton percentages as a comparison table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering method is being evaluated on the same dataset used for its development or parameter tuning — an independent dataset is required for unbiased validation The analysis goal is to perform or tune the feature clustering itself (e.g. setting ramclustR st/maxt parameters) rather than to benchmark and report comparative performance The dataset lacks idMS/MS (indiscriminant tandem MS) data, so MS/MS spectral similarity — the primary validation metric here — cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when pre-training a spectral encoder on multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) whose embeddings must be aligned with 3D structural embeddings for downstream spectra-conditioned molecular generation.
skills.name: infonce-contrastive-alignment
skills.search_text: infonce-contrastive-alignment Use when pre-training a spectral encoder on multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) whose embeddings must be aligned with 3D structural embeddings for downstream spectra-conditioned molecular generation. The task is training the Diffusion Molecule Transformer itself for denoising-based structure generation; contrastive alignment is a pre-training step for the spectral encoder, not the denoising network. The spectral encoder will process spectra from modalities outside the three supported types (e.g. NMR or mass spectrometry); the article states applicability to such modalities remains to be explored. Only a single spectrum type is available and no 3D structural embeddings can be produced; contrastive alignment requires paired spectrum-structure data. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Aligns spectral embeddings from a Transformer-based spectrum encoder with 3D molecular structure embeddings using the InfoNCE loss, so that the spectral encoder learns representations suitable for conditioning molecular structure diffusion generation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Aligns spectral embeddings from a Transformer-based spectrum encoder with 3D molecular structure embeddings using the InfoNCE loss, so that the spectral encoder learns representations suitable for conditioning molecular structure diffusion generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is training the Diffusion Molecule Transformer itself for denoising-based structure generation; contrastive alignment is a pre-training step for the spectral encoder, not the denoising network. The spectral encoder will process spectra from modalities outside the three supported types (e.g. NMR or mass spectrometry); the article states applicability to such modalities remains to be explored. Only a single spectrum type is available and no 3D structural embeddings can be produced; contrastive alignment requires paired spectrum-structure data.

skills.description: Use when a high-dimensional per-instance feature table (here, 473 CDK-derived bond features over 679 Zaretzki-derived substrates) must be reduced before training a classifier, and the retained dimensionality should be learned per class via internal cross-validation rather than fixed a priori.
skills.name: information-gain-feature-selection
skills.search_text: information-gain-feature-selection Use when a high-dimensional per-instance feature table (here, 473 CDK-derived bond features over 679 Zaretzki-derived substrates) must be reduced before training a classifier, and the retained dimensionality should be learned per class via internal cross-validation rather than fixed a priori. Input compounds are unlabeled (no BoMX−Y/non-BoMX−Y annotation), so information gain against the label cannot be computed. The prediction target is not the per-isoform reactive-bond binary label defined here — e.g., reactant/non-reactant classification, which CypReact handles, or byproduct generation, which MetaboGen handles. A single global feature subset is required across all nine CYP450 isoforms; this pipeline learns a separate N* and ranking for each D(α). http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Per-class feature reduction used by the CypBoM reactive-bond predictor: drop CDK features that are constant across all [compound, bond] instances, rank the remainder by information gain against the binary BoMX−Y/non-BoMX−Y label, and retain the top-N features with N learned by internal cross-validation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Per-class feature reduction used by the CypBoM reactive-bond predictor: drop CDK features that are constant across all [compound, bond] instances, rank the remainder by information gain against the binary BoMX−Y/non-BoMX−Y label, and retain the top-N features with N learned by internal cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input compounds are unlabeled (no BoMX−Y/non-BoMX−Y annotation), so information gain against the label cannot be computed. The prediction target is not the per-isoform reactive-bond binary label defined here — e.g., reactant/non-reactant classification, which CypReact handles, or byproduct generation, which MetaboGen handles. A single global feature subset is required across all nine CYP450 isoforms; this pipeline learns a separate N* and ranking for each D(α).

skills.description: Use when a randomized LC/GC-MS sample list must be converted into an instrument injection sequence where QC samples are evenly interspersed and QC wells stay confined to a dedicated plate column.
skills.name: injection-sequence-pre-interpolation
skills.search_text: injection-sequence-pre-interpolation Use when a randomized LC/GC-MS sample list must be converted into an instrument injection sequence where QC samples are evenly interspersed and QC wells stay confined to a dedicated plate column. The sample list has not yet been inter-batch balanced and intra-batch block randomized — QC pre-interpolation must operate on an already-randomized sequence The laboratory requires new QC sample types or injection rules not among InjectionDesign's predefined four QC types plus one custom QC The experiment exceeds the configured plate load capacity (e.g., max experimental samples per 96-well plate, excluding QC), so per-plate position design cannot hold the samples Pre-interpolates QC sample types (Solvent QC, Long Term Reference QC, Blank, Pooled/custom QC) evenly in a circular fashion among already-randomized experimental samples to build the injection order, independently of the 96-well plate position layout in InjectionDesign. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.02.26.530140
skills.summary: Pre-interpolates QC sample types (Solvent QC, Long Term Reference QC, Blank, Pooled/custom QC) evenly in a circular fashion among already-randomized experimental samples to build the injection order, independently of the 96-well plate position layout in InjectionDesign.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample list has not yet been inter-batch balanced and intra-batch block randomized — QC pre-interpolation must operate on an already-randomized sequence The laboratory requires new QC sample types or injection rules not among InjectionDesign's predefined four QC types plus one custom QC The experiment exceeds the configured plate load capacity (e.g., max experimental samples per 96-well plate, excluding QC), so per-plate position design cannot hold the samples

skills.search_text: inorganic-and-mixture-compound-filtering Use when a merged multi-source chemical inventory (e.g., fused EPA HPV, EINECS, CHEMINV, Tox21, pesticide, and exposome lists) must be cleaned of non-single-organic entries and deduplicated into a unique CASRN-keyed set. The inventory already contains only single organic compounds with unique CASRN keys (no dedup or class filtering needed) The downstream analysis targets metals or inorganic species explicitly (e.g., IFS HLB prediction is anyway inapplicable to metal-containing chemicals, but a metals-focused study would not apply this filter) Records lack CASRN entirely and cannot be reconciled via the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard, since downstream HTS data retrieval requires CASRN http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 A curation step in the HExpMetDB database-fusion workflow that removes inorganic compounds, organic mixtures, and metals from merged chemical lists, then deduplicates the remaining entries by CASRN and canonical SMILES to yield a unique chemical inventory. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: A curation step in the HExpMetDB database-fusion workflow that removes inorganic compounds, organic mixtures, and metals from merged chemical lists, then deduplicates the remaining entries by CASRN and canonical SMILES to yield a unique chemical inventory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The inventory already contains only single organic compounds with unique CASRN keys (no dedup or class filtering needed) The downstream analysis targets metals or inorganic species explicitly (e.g., IFS HLB prediction is anyway inapplicable to metal-containing chemicals, but a metals-focused study would not apply this filter) Records lack CASRN entirely and cannot be reconciled via the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard, since downstream HTS data retrieval requires CASRN

skills.description: Decision support for classifying inorganic, organometallic, or carbon-exception compounds (cyanides, CO, CO2, carbon disulfide) when structural-rule-based taxonomy categories are needed rather than name- or text-based labels.
skills.name: inorganic-compound-formula-keyed-classification
skills.search_text: inorganic-compound-formula-keyed-classification Decision support for classifying inorganic, organometallic, or carbon-exception compounds (cyanides, CO, CO2, carbon disulfide) when structural-rule-based taxonomy categories are needed rather than name- or text-based labels. Compounds that clearly belong to the organic Kingdom (the 26 organic SuperClasses), which use functional-group-based rather than elemental/formula-based structural keys Text- or name-based classification needs where no chemical structure or molecular formula is available Compounds whose structures are only available as IUPAC names that require the ~200-rule IUPAC name-parsing module instead of direct structural feature extraction http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Reconstructs ClassyFire's inorganic and organometallic taxonomy branch from the ChemOnt OBO file, capturing all 674 inorganic categories keyed by computable structural features (elemental content, molecular formula, oxyanion lists). This fills the coverage gap left by existing chemical ontologies for non-organic compound types. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Reconstructs ClassyFire's inorganic and organometallic taxonomy branch from the ChemOnt OBO file, capturing all 674 inorganic categories keyed by computable structural features (elemental content, molecular formula, oxyanion lists). This fills the coverage gap left by existing chemical ontologies for non-organic compound types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds that clearly belong to the organic Kingdom (the 26 organic SuperClasses), which use functional-group-based rather than elemental/formula-based structural keys Text- or name-based classification needs where no chemical structure or molecular formula is available Compounds whose structures are only available as IUPAC names that require the ~200-rule IUPAC name-parsing module instead of direct structural feature extraction

skills.description: Use when GNPS molecular networking spectra must be linked to candidate biosynthetic gene clusters with a supervised kernel-regression score, or when reproducing the IOKR top-n ranking and AUC benchmarks (Table 3) against a randomised baseline.
skills.name: input-output-kernel-regression-scoring
skills.search_text: input-output-kernel-regression-scoring Use when GNPS molecular networking spectra must be linked to candidate biosynthetic gene clusters with a supervised kernel-regression score, or when reproducing the IOKR top-n ranking and AUC benchmarks (Table 3) against a randomised baseline. The dataset has no paired BGC-spectrum training links (e.g. no PODP or strain_mappings.json ground truth), so the kernel mapping from mass spectral features to BGC classes cannot be learned The input is raw MS data that has not been processed into GNPS molecular networking output (spectra.mgf plus molecular_families.tsv, annotations.tsv, file_mappings) The goal is raw Metcalf-style correlation scoring alone rather than the supervised IOKR ranking of candidate MIBiG structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scores metabolite-to-BGC links using Input-Output Kernel Regression (IOKR), trained on paired MIBiG/GNPS BGC-spectrum data, and ranks all MIBiG-associated candidate structures per spectrum. Within the NPLinker framework this IOKR score is applied alongside the standardised strain correlation score to prioritise validated genomic-metabolomic links. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Scores metabolite-to-BGC links using Input-Output Kernel Regression (IOKR), trained on paired MIBiG/GNPS BGC-spectrum data, and ranks all MIBiG-associated candidate structures per spectrum. Within the NPLinker framework this IOKR score is applied alongside the standardised strain correlation score to prioritise validated genomic-metabolomic links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no paired BGC-spectrum training links (e.g. no PODP or strain_mappings.json ground truth), so the kernel mapping from mass spectral features to BGC classes cannot be learned The input is raw MS data that has not been processed into GNPS molecular networking output (spectra.mgf plus molecular_families.tsv, annotations.tsv, file_mappings) The goal is raw Metcalf-style correlation scoring alone rather than the supervised IOKR ranking of candidate MIBiG structures

skills.search_text: insilico-formula-annotation-sirius Use when MS/MS peak lists (e.g., from a microbeMASST batch search) lack library matches and you need tentative molecular formula and compound-class assignments; applied to spectra with parent mass < 850 Da. Spectra with parent mass >= 850 Da, for which SIRIUS/CANOPUS class prediction was not applied in the reference workflow Spectra already annotated at higher confidence (e.g., MSI level 1) by direct GNPS library matching — this skill only yields tentative level-2 annotations Raw LC-MS/MS data that still requires peak picking/feature detection (first process with MZmine to generate the .mgf) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 In-silico annotation of microbial MS/MS spectra by predicting molecular formulas and fragment trees with SIRIUS and compound classes with CANOPUS, then joining predictions with GNPS library hits to assign level-2 Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: In-silico annotation of microbial MS/MS spectra by predicting molecular formulas and fragment trees with SIRIUS and compound classes with CANOPUS, then joining predictions with GNPS library hits to assign level-2 Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra with parent mass >= 850 Da, for which SIRIUS/CANOPUS class prediction was not applied in the reference workflow Spectra already annotated at higher confidence (e.g., MSI level 1) by direct GNPS library matching — this skill only yields tentative level-2 annotations Raw LC-MS/MS data that still requires peak picking/feature detection (first process with MZmine to generate the .mgf)

skills.description: Use when a positive-ion LC-HRMS lipidomics peak list contains unannotated precursor m/z values and you need additional lipid annotations beyond MSI level 1/2 spectral matches, as MSI level 3 accurate-mass-only assignments.
skills.name: insilico-lipid-library-search
skills.search_text: insilico-lipid-library-search Use when a positive-ion LC-HRMS lipidomics peak list contains unannotated precursor m/z values and you need additional lipid annotations beyond MSI level 1/2 spectral matches, as MSI level 3 accurate-mass-only assignments. When the peak already has an MS/MS spectral match to an authentic standard or library spectrum (MSI level 1 or 2) — use that higher-confidence assignment instead. When precursor mass accuracy is worse than the library search tolerance (e.g. 5 mDa), in-silico accurate-mass-only lookup cannot produce defensible MSI level 3 assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate lipid precursor masses from LC-HRMS peak lists by searching an in-silico lipid MS/MS library (e.g. LipidBlast v49) within a fixed precursor mass tolerance, yielding MSI level 3 annotations that extend spectral-matched identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Annotate lipid precursor masses from LC-HRMS peak lists by searching an in-silico lipid MS/MS library (e.g. LipidBlast v49) within a fixed precursor mass tolerance, yielding MSI level 3 annotations that extend spectral-matched identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the peak already has an MS/MS spectral match to an authentic standard or library spectrum (MSI level 1 or 2) — use that higher-confidence assignment instead. When precursor mass accuracy is worse than the library search tolerance (e.g. 5 mDa), in-silico accurate-mass-only lookup cannot produce defensible MSI level 3 assignments.

skills.search_text: insilico-ms2-annotation-sirius-canopus Use when you have MZmine-processed features with associated MS2 scans (mzML / mgf spectra) from LC-HRMS2 DDA data in positive and/or negative ionization mode and want per-feature in-silico candidate structures, formulas, and chemical classes to merge with ISDB spectral matches and taxonomic. skills.summary: Submit exported MS2 spectra to SIRIUS with CSI:FingerID and CANOPUS to obtain in-silico structural (molecular formula and candidate structures) and substructure/compound-class annotations, which are then reranked and integrated alongside ISDB-LOTUS spectral matches into the ENPKG knowledge graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a feature table or mgf of MS2 spectra without the MZmine-processed per-sample context required by the ENPKG workflow (e.g. raw vendor files not yet converted). When you only need spectral-library matching to known reference spectra and do not want formula/class annotations — ISDB-LOTUS matching in 03_enpkg_mn_isdb_isdb_taxo alone may suffice. When features lack an associated MS2 scan or fall outside the RT 0.5–8.0 min window, as they are filtered out and will not be annotated.

skills.search_text: insilico-msms-annotation-sirius Use when MS2 .mzML features lack spectral-library matches and candidate metabolite structures must be ranked via SIRIUS in silico fragmentation with the 'all' (orbitrap) database inside the MAW containers. skills.description: Use when you have a set of predicted or known metabolite structures plus a corpus of experimental MS/MS spectra and need to measure annotation gains from expanding the reference library.
skills.name: insilico-spectral-library-construction
skills.search_text: insilico-spectral-library-construction Use when you have a set of predicted or known metabolite structures plus a corpus of experimental MS/MS spectra and need to measure annotation gains from expanding the reference library. When the goal is to discover and structurally confirm new metabolites (synthesis and targeted MS/MS acquisition), not to annotate existing spectra against a fixed reference library. When experimental spectra must be annotated with retention time or collision energy metadata beyond MS/MS peak matching — predicting MS/MS spectra or retention times from structures remains an open problem per the article. When the organism is evolutionarily distant from the model's training set (e.g. plant or bacterial metabolomes) and a bespoke DeepMet model has not been trained, since the reference model was trained on human metabolites. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Constructs an in silico MS/MS spectral library from candidate metabolite structures and searches experimental spectra against it via cosine similarity, quantifying how many spectra can be assigned a chemical structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Constructs an in silico MS/MS spectral library from candidate metabolite structures and searches experimental spectra against it via cosine similarity, quantifying how many spectra can be assigned a chemical structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to discover and structurally confirm new metabolites (synthesis and targeted MS/MS acquisition), not to annotate existing spectra against a fixed reference library. When experimental spectra must be annotated with retention time or collision energy metadata beyond MS/MS peak matching — predicting MS/MS spectra or retention times from structures remains an open problem per the article. When the organism is evolutionarily distant from the model's training set (e.g. plant or bacterial metabolomes) and a bespoke DeepMet model has not been trained, since the reference model was trained on human metabolites.

skills.description: Use when a spectral library candidate has CFM-ID (or similar) in silico fragments and a matching experimental tandem HRMS/MS spectrum, and you must quantify/visualize fragment overlap to validate predicted fragments before using them for compound annotation.

skills.search_text: insilico-vs-experimental-spectrum-comparison Use when a spectral library candidate has CFM-ID (or similar) in silico fragments and a matching experimental tandem HRMS/MS spectrum, and you must quantify/visualize fragment overlap to validate predicted fragments before using them for compound annotation. No experimental MS/MS spectrum exists for the compound of interest (nothing to compare against predicted fragments) Spectra come from low-resolution single-stage MS rather than tandem HRMS/MS, so fragment-level matching is not meaningful Predicted fragments were not thresholded (e.g. the >5% relative-intensity filter was not applied), which would inflate apparent overlap with noise peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Per-compound overlap assessment between CFM-ID–predicted in silico MS/MS fragments and experimentally acquired tandem HRMS/MS spectra (here: 15 DNA adduct reference standards on a Vion IMS-qTOF at 20/40/60 eV), used to justify predicted fragments for annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Per-compound overlap assessment between CFM-ID–predicted in silico MS/MS fragments and experimentally acquired tandem HRMS/MS spectra (here: 15 DNA adduct reference standards on a Vion IMS-qTOF at 20/40/60 eV), used to justify predicted fragments for annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No experimental MS/MS spectrum exists for the compound of interest (nothing to compare against predicted fragments) Spectra come from low-resolution single-stage MS rather than tandem HRMS/MS, so fragment-level matching is not meaningful Predicted fragments were not thresholded (e.g. the >5% relative-intensity filter was not applied), which would inflate apparent overlap with noise peaks

skills.description: Use when evaluating a QTOF-trained MS/MS spectral prediction model (e.g. CFM-ID 4.0 trained on Metlin QTOF data) against Orbitrap MS/MS query spectra, such as the CASMI 2016 category 3 dataset of 208 Orbitrap spectra.
skills.name: instrument-specific-collision-energy-mapping
skills.search_text: instrument-specific-collision-energy-mapping Use when evaluating a QTOF-trained MS/MS spectral prediction model (e.g. CFM-ID 4.0 trained on Metlin QTOF data) against Orbitrap MS/MS query spectra, such as the CASMI 2016 category 3 dataset of 208 Orbitrap spectra. The query spectra were already collected on a QTOF instrument, so no cross-instrument energy mapping is needed and predictions can be requested at QTOF 10/20/40 eV directly. A model trained on the target instrument's data (e.g. an Orbitrap-trained MSML model) is available; direct prediction at native energies is preferable to energy conversion. The spectra are EI-MS/MS rather than ESI-MS/MS; the CFM-ID ESI pipeline and QTOF/HCD energy mapping do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Maps collision energies from one MS instrument family to another (e.g. Orbitrap HCD to nominal QTOF 10/20/40 eV collision energies) using the Thermo Fisher Scientific conversion equation, so that spectral-prediction models trained exclusively on QTOF data (such as CFM-ID 4.0) can be scored against spectra acquired on a different instrument. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Maps collision energies from one MS instrument family to another (e.g. Orbitrap HCD to nominal QTOF 10/20/40 eV collision energies) using the Thermo Fisher Scientific conversion equation, so that spectral-prediction models trained exclusively on QTOF data (such as CFM-ID 4.0) can be scored against spectra acquired on a different instrument.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectra were already collected on a QTOF instrument, so no cross-instrument energy mapping is needed and predictions can be requested at QTOF 10/20/40 eV directly. skills.description: Use when refining formula candidates from MS/MS data whose precursor m/z and instrument type (Q-TOF or Orbitrap) are known, and candidate formulas must fall within the correct ppm tolerance of the precursor mass.
skills.name: instrument-specific-mass-accuracy-handling-qtof-vs-orbitrap
skills.search_text: instrument-specific-mass-accuracy-handling-qtof-vs-orbitrap Use when refining formula candidates from MS/MS data whose precursor m/z and instrument type (Q-TOF or Orbitrap) are known, and candidate formulas must fall within the correct ppm tolerance of the precursor mass. Spectra lacking precursor_mz/precursor_type information or an unknown instrument type, so no ppm tolerance can be justified Formulas involving elements outside the frequent-atom set (C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K) or molecules exceeding 300 atoms Chimeric/co-eluting spectra where FIDDLE's performance is known to degrade, making tolerance-based refinement unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Applies instrument-dependent precursor mass tolerances (10 ppm for Q-TOF, 5 ppm for Orbitrap) when refining candidate molecular formulas so that FIDDLE's deep-learning predictions are constrained to formulas matching the measured precursor mass. This mirrors the accuracy profiles of the two instrument families used to train and evaluate FIDDLE. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Applies instrument-dependent precursor mass tolerances (10 ppm for Q-TOF, 5 ppm for Orbitrap) when refining candidate molecular formulas so that FIDDLE's deep-learning predictions are constrained to formulas matching the measured precursor mass. This mirrors the accuracy profiles of the two instrument families used to train and evaluate FIDDLE.

skills.description: Use when raw targeted SRM/MRM data (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S .raw files from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate) already have vendor-software quantification results and you need to verify that an open-source pipeline reproduces those concentrations.
skills.name: instrument-vendor-software-concentration-comparison
skills.search_text: instrument-vendor-software-concentration-comparison Use when raw targeted SRM/MRM data (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S .raw files from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate) already have vendor-software quantification results and you need to verify that an open-source pipeline reproduces those concentrations. The analysis is non-targeted (feature finding in MS1, alignment, identification) — use XCMS, MZmine, or MS-DIAL instead of a targeted extraction/comparison workflow. A concentration/feature table already exists and no raw-file reprocessing is needed — re-importing raw SRM files into Skyline adds no value. The data are GC-MS or ion mobility small-molecule acquisitions, where Skyline support was still ongoing at the time of the paper. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks an open-source targeted quantification tool (Skyline) against instrument vendor software (TargetLynx) by reprocessing the same raw SRM files with matched curve-fit parameters and comparing calculated concentrations via linear regression. skills.summary: Benchmarks an open-source targeted quantification tool (Skyline) against instrument vendor software (TargetLynx) by reprocessing the same raw SRM files with matched curve-fit parameters and comparing calculated concentrations via linear regression. skills.description: Use when two nested or competing risk scores must be compared for predictive value of 5- or 10-year mortality (or similar survival endpoints), and you need C-statistic differences with SEs/P values plus IDI with SEs/P values.

skills.search_text: integrated-discrimination-improvement-reclassification Use when two nested or competing risk scores must be compared for predictive value of 5- or 10-year mortality (or similar survival endpoints), and you need C-statistic differences with SEs/P values plus IDI with SEs/P values. The metabolic biomarker score is based on per-cohort scaled biomarker values and is not yet suitable for clinical patient classification, so do not use these C-statistic/IDI comparisons to justify deploying the score as a clinical classifier. Do not apply this comparison when the new score was trained on the same cohort it is tested in — here weights come from the Estonian Biobank and are tested in FINRISK 1997 specifically to avoid overestimation of predictive ability. Not appropriate for case-control or classification settings without a survival time scale; the method requires Cox models with age at blood sampling as the time scale. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies whether a new risk score (e.g., a metabolic biomarker score) improves prediction of a time-to-event outcome over a conventional score, using C-statistic differences and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) computed with custom R functions in a Cox model framework. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9

skills.search_text: integrated-gradients-attribution-computation Use when a trained transformer model has produced lipid token predictions on MS2 spectra and you need per-peak interpretability: attributing each predicted lipid token back to specific m/z peaks to compare them against known fragment annotations. skills.summary: Ranks candidate NPS identities by combining GC/EI-MS spectrum similarity with molecular-fingerprint similarity (SMSF), using NEIMS-predicted spectra of enumerated derivatives and DeepEI-predicted fingerprints of the unknown analyte.

skills.search_text: integrative-omics-pathway-analysis Use when you have matched gene-expression and metabolomics data from a phenotype study and need to identify significantly perturbed pathways (pFDR < 0.05) using over-representation, topology, and combined p-value evidence. skills.description: Use when preparing augmented ion-image pairs from a preprocessed MSI matrix ([X*Y,P]) for DeepION ISO-mode isotope-ion representation training and the missing values must depend on ion intensity.
skills.name: intensity-dependent-missing-value-simulation
skills.search_text: intensity-dependent-missing-value-simulation Use when preparing augmented ion-image pairs from a preprocessed MSI matrix ([X*Y,P]) for DeepION ISO-mode isotope-ion representation training and the missing values must depend on ion intensity. The goal is COL-mode colocalized-ion augmentation: T_COL uses only color jitter, filtering, Poisson noise and random missing value and must not include the intensity-dependent missing-value step. skills.search_text: inter-batch-variation-assessment Use when you have LC-MS or SRM proteomics runs with pooled QC injections interspersed at a fixed interval (e.g. every 5, 6, or 8 subject samples) and you need to measure and report how much unwanted inter-batch variation remains, before versus after batch correction such as QC-RFSC. The dataset has no repeated pooled QC injections, so RSD in QC samples cannot be computed. You only have a single feature table with no paired pre/post correction matrix — the skill is built around raw-vs-corrected comparison. You want within-subject biological variability rather than instrument/batch precision; RSD across QC injections is not a biological measure. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Quantify how much inter-batch (and intra-batch) signal variation persists in QC samples by computing per-feature relative standard deviation (RSD%) in QC injections and building cumulative RSD distribution curves, as implemented in statTarget for LC-MS metabolomics and SRM proteomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Quantify how much inter-batch (and intra-batch) signal variation persists in QC samples by computing per-feature relative standard deviation (RSD%) in QC injections and building cumulative RSD distribution curves, as implemented in statTarget for LC-MS metabolomics and SRM proteomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no repeated pooled QC injections, so RSD in QC samples cannot be computed. You only have a single feature table with no paired pre/post correction matrix — the skill is built around raw-vs-corrected comparison. You want within-subject biological variability rather than instrument/batch precision; RSD across QC injections is not a biological measure.

skills.name: inter-laboratory-ccs-variation-analysis
skills.search_text: inter-laboratory-ccs-variation-analysis Use when comparing TWIMS (or DTIM) CCS values measured in-house against literature CCS values for the same metabolite/adduct ([M + H]+ or [M − H]−), or when validating that predicted CCS values agree with experimental ones within the ~±3% experimental variation band. The goal is computing CCS de novo from SMILES structures (use the Snakemake CCS prediction workflow with RDKit/ASE-ANI/QUICK/hpccs instead of a literature-variation comparison) The metabolites lack any literature or consensus CCS values for the matching adduct state, leaving no inter-laboratory pair to compare Comparing CCS values from the same instrument and laboratory run, where run-to-run repeatability rather than between-laboratory variation is the quantity of interest Quantifies how much experimentally measured collision cross section (CCS) values vary between laboratories and instruments (e.g., TWIMS vs DTIM) by computing percent relative deviations between locally measured and literature-reported CCS values, and uses the resulting spread to justify an approximately ±3% acceptance threshold for predicted-vs-experimental CCS comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.1c00315

skills.search_text: interactive-dashboard-plotting Use when mzML/mzXML files from untargeted MS-based metabolomics runs are being added incrementally (or a whole batch needs retrospective review) and extracted diagnostic values — observed m/z, retention time, intensity, peak shape, calibrant signal — must be plotted interactively so acquisition. Input is already a processed feature table or a static figure is the only deliverable — the value here is live/interactive re-rendering as new mzML files arrive, not one-off plotting. skills.search_text: interactive-filtering-effect-visualization Use when you need to visually communicate to end users how successive feature-intensity filtering steps shrink a feature table, e.g. per-sample HTML plots of the intensity-based, quantile-based, and sequential filtering effects after running Inventa on MZmine output. skills.summary: Generate interactive HTML plots that show how intensity-based (2% normalized area) and quantile-based (0.75 quantile) filters progressively reduce feature counts in MZmine quantitative tables, as done in Inventa to illustrate per-extract filtering effects.

skills.description: Use when a boolean ROI mask must be derived from an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a 2D NumPy array of a 56Fe pancreatic adenocarcinoma tissue microarray core) by automatic thresholding, and the mask must optionally be combined with or restricted to a previously selected region.
skills.name: interactive-selection-dialog-gui-logic
skills.search_text: interactive-selection-dialog-gui-logic Use when a boolean ROI mask must be derived from an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a 2D NumPy array of a 56Fe pancreatic adenocarcinoma tissue microarray core) by automatic thresholding, and the mask must optionally be combined with or restricted to a previously selected region. The image is already a labeled or categorical segmentation and no further background/ROI thresholding is needed. The user needs manual (paint-style) ROI selection rather than automatic image thresholding — the article states segmentation 'can be performed either manually or automatically using image thresholding' and this skill only implements the automatic path. The input is a full multi-channel or RGB overlay image (e.g. 55Mn/56Fe/66Zn RGB overlay) where per-element masks must be computed separately rather than a single combined mask. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Implements the logic behind Pew2's interactive selection dialog, which isolates regions of interest (ROIs) from the background of an LA-ICP-MS elemental image via automatic image thresholding methods such as Otsu's method, mean thresholding, multi-level k-means, and binary filters like median, optionally intersecting the new mask with an existing selection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Implements the logic behind Pew2's interactive selection dialog, which isolates regions of interest (ROIs) from the background of an LA-ICP-MS elemental image via automatic image thresholding methods such as Otsu's method, mean thresholding, multi-level k-means, and binary filters like median, optionally intersecting the new mask with an existing selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The image is already a labeled or categorical segmentation and no further background/ROI thresholding is needed. A static, publication-style figure is the only deliverable and interactivity is unnecessary — a simple matplotlib scatter of the same 2D coordinates suffices.

skills.description: Use when implementing or modifying the CFM-ID 4.0 fragmentation graph for ESI-MS/MS spectral prediction, specifically to remodel ring cleavages as sequential one-bond breaks while suppressing unstable intermediate fragment peaks.
skills.name: intermediate-fragment-persistence-weight-zeroing
skills.search_text: intermediate-fragment-persistence-weight-zeroing Use when implementing or modifying the CFM-ID 4.0 fragmentation graph for ESI-MS/MS spectral prediction, specifically to remodel ring cleavages as sequential one-bond breaks while suppressing unstable intermediate fragment peaks. When working with legacy CFM-ID 2.0/3.0 code that already implements ring cleavage as a single simultaneous two-bond break with concatenated FV0+FV1 feature vectors — this skill replaces that design, so it is redundant there. When predicting EI-MS/MS spectra or handling MS spectra from instruments other than QTOF instruments — the article notes CFM-ID 4.0 is built around QTOF ESI-MS/MS data. When the fragment of interest is a stable ring-derived product (f1) rather than a transient single-bond-break intermediate — zeroing its persistence weight would incorrectly remove legitimate peaks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A CFM-ID 4.0 technique that models ring cleavage in ESI-MS/MS as two sequential single-bond transitions, assigning a persistence (self-transition) probability of zero to the chemically unstable intermediate fragment f_inter so it never contributes a predicted spectral peak. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: A CFM-ID 4.0 technique that models ring cleavage in ESI-MS/MS as two sequential single-bond transitions, assigning a persistence (self-transition) probability of zero to the chemically unstable intermediate fragment f_inter so it never contributes a predicted spectral peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When working with legacy CFM-ID 2.0/3.0 code that already implements ring cleavage as a single simultaneous two-bond break with concatenated FV0+FV1 feature vectors — this skill replaces that design, so it is redundant there. When predicting EI-MS/MS spectra or handling MS spectra from instruments other than QTOF instruments — the article notes CFM-ID 4.0 is built around QTOF ESI-MS/MS data. When the fragment of interest is a stable ring-derived product (f1) rather than a transient single-bond-break intermediate — zeroing its persistence weight would incorrectly remove legitimate peaks.

skills.search_text: internal-standard-based-ccs-bias-correction Use when IM-MS lipidomics measurements (e.g., TIM-MS) are spiked with U13C-labeled yeast lipids and CCSN2 values show bias against the DTCCSN2 library that must be corrected per lipid class-adduct combination. A lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids detected — regression is impossible, so CCS correction cannot be applied to that combination The lipid class or adduct is outside the permitted combinations (e.g., AcCa, Co, LPE, PG, SPH entries are in the adduct table but not among the 10 correctable classes for correction) The goal is only to monitor/report CCS bias without correcting values — use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the correction workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 An R Markdown–based procedure (MobiLipid) that generates lipid class- and adduct-specific linear CCS correction functions by regressing measured TIMCCSN2 values of U13C-labeled internal standard lipids against DTCCSN2 library values, then applies them to correct CCSN2 of all lipids in IM-MS lipidomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253

skills.when_to_use_negative: A lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids detected — regression is impossible, so CCS correction cannot be applied to that combination The lipid class or adduct is outside the permitted combinations (e.g., AcCa, Co, LPE, PG, SPH entries are in the adduct table but not among the 10 correctable classes for correction) The goal is only to monitor/report CCS bias without correcting values — use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the correction workflow

skills.name: internal-standard-based-migration-time-prediction
skills.search_text: internal-standard-based-migration-time-prediction Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS multiplexed data (mzML) where high migration time variability from nonlinear electroosmotic flow changes prevents peak alignment, and analyte migration times must be predicted per run from internal-standard landmarks. Data is not MSI-CE-MS multiplexed full-scan data (e.g. untargeted LC-MS feature tables) — the MTI scheme depends on serially injected segments with consistent inter-peak spacing The matrix is not serum-like: PeakMeister was not yet validated for urine, saliva, or stool matrices The analyte lacks two flanking internal standards or a stable-isotope internal standard and is late migrating or near the detection limit — these are prone to peak misannotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Predicts metabolite migration times in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs using migration time indexes (MTI) computed from a panel of 11 internal standards, avoiding dynamic time warping or electrophoretic mobility conversion, so that analyte peaks can be annotated and integrated despite large migration time drift across batches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03513

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not MSI-CE-MS multiplexed full-scan data (e.g. untargeted LC-MS feature tables) — the MTI scheme depends on serially injected segments with consistent inter-peak spacing The matrix is not serum-like: PeakMeister was not yet validated for urine, saliva, or stool matrices The analyte lacks two flanking internal standards or a stable-isotope internal standard and is late migrating or near the detection limit — these are prone to peak misannotation

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains samples spiked with one or more internal standards and unwanted sample-to-sample variation (e.g., from extraction or injection variability) must be corrected before statistical analysis or reporting.
skills.name: internal-standard-based-sample-correction
skills.search_text: internal-standard-based-sample-correction Use when a metabolomics feature table contains samples spiked with one or more internal standards and unwanted sample-to-sample variation (e.g., from extraction or injection variability) must be corrected before statistical analysis or reporting. The dataset contains no internal standards, making per-sample scaling by a standard signal impossible — use probabilistic quotient or quantile normalization instead. The input is a raw (unimputed) feature table that still requires missing-value handling before normalization. skills.description: Use when processing targeted LC-MS/MS MRM quantitation data (e.g. SmartPeak FeatureDB.csv from the 5500 QTRAP RapidRIP tutorial) and you want a per-compound IS quality score computed from tailing, asymmetry, and height-ratio metrics before quantitation reporting.
skills.name: internal-standard-scoring
skills.search_text: internal-standard-scoring Use when processing targeted LC-MS/MS MRM quantitation data (e.g. SmartPeak FeatureDB.csv from the 5500 QTRAP RapidRIP tutorial) and you want a per-compound IS quality score computed from tailing, asymmetry, and height-ratio metrics before quantitation reporting. Input is already a quantitation report or a feature table that lacks raw IS peak-height/tailing/asymmetry meta-values — VALIDATE_IS will simply flag everything and no scores can be computed. The experiment is untargeted FIA-MS or DDA/DIA (e.g. the Thermo Orbitrap tutorials) where no IS pairing or transition-level meta-values exist. You only need final concentrations from the calibration curve — IS scoring is an optional pre-quantitation QC step, not a quantitation method. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 An optional SmartPeak workflow step that computes per-compound internal-standard quality metrics (peak tailing factor, peak asymmetry factor, and analyte-to-IS height ratio) from the FeatureDB produced by the targeted MRM workflow and emits a per-compound score table. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03421
skills.summary: An optional SmartPeak workflow step that computes per-compound internal-standard quality metrics (peak tailing factor, peak asymmetry factor, and analyte-to-IS height ratio) from the FeatureDB produced by the targeted MRM workflow and emits a per-compound score table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantitation report or a feature table that lacks raw IS peak-height/tailing/asymmetry meta-values — VALIDATE_IS will simply flag everything and no scores can be computed. The experiment is untargeted FIA-MS or DDA/DIA (e.g. the Thermo Orbitrap tutorials) where no IS pairing or transition-level meta-values exist. You only need final concentrations from the calibration curve — IS scoring is an optional pre-quantitation QC step, not a quantitation method.

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics experiment contains multiple candidate internal standards and you need to assign each compound a suitable IS, using the lowest-RSDQC criterion on batch-corrected compound/IS ratios.
skills.name: internal-standard-selection-rsdqc-ranking
skills.search_text: internal-standard-selection-rsdqc-ranking Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics experiment contains multiple candidate internal standards and you need to assign each compound a suitable IS, using the lowest-RSDQC criterion on batch-corrected compound/IS ratios. When only one internal standard is available per metabolite and no ranking between candidates is needed — mzQuality's doAnalysis handles the single-assigned-IS ratio step directly. When the goal is overall compound-quality triage rather than IS choice — use the RSDqc / background-signal (e-score) classification into High Confidence, With Caution and Low SNR tabs instead. When data are raw vendor peak tables not yet integrated — mzQuality operates on peak-integrated data (e.g. from SCIEX OS) and does not process peaks itself. Selects the best internal standard for each metabolite in a targeted LC-MS dataset by computing the relative standard deviation of QC samples (RSDQC) for every compound/IS ratio after batch correction, then ranking IS candidates by lowest RSDQC, mirroring mzQuality's suggestion logic. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Selects the best internal standard for each metabolite in a targeted LC-MS dataset by computing the relative standard deviation of QC samples (RSDQC) for every compound/IS ratio after batch correction, then ranking IS candidates by lowest RSDQC, mirroring mzQuality's suggestion logic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one internal standard is available per metabolite and no ranking between candidates is needed — mzQuality's doAnalysis handles the single-assigned-IS ratio step directly. When the goal is overall compound-quality triage rather than IS choice — use the RSDqc / background-signal (e-score) classification into High Confidence, With Caution and Low SNR tabs instead. When data are raw vendor peak tables not yet integrated — mzQuality operates on peak-integrated data (e.g. from SCIEX OS) and does not process peaks itself.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS runs where peak annotation depends on internal standards (or other reliable landmark peaks) with sufficient signal-to-noise; verify IS signal adequacy before trusting peak areas or reference ranges.
skills.name: internal-standard-signal-adequacy-checking
skills.search_text: internal-standard-signal-adequacy-checking Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS runs where peak annotation depends on internal standards (or other reliable landmark peaks) with sufficient signal-to-noise; verify IS signal adequacy before trusting peak areas or reference ranges. When the input is already a clean peak-area or reference-range table — this check is upstream, on raw mzML/EIE signals. When the analyte of interest does not rely on internal standards or landmark peaks for migration-time prediction (e.g. purely de novo feature detection outside targeted MSI-CE-MS). When matrix effects or peak misannotation arise from co-migrating analytes (interference.comigration.threshold handling) rather than from weak IS signals. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A quality-control step in PeakMeister's MSI-CE-MS preprocessing that verifies internal-standard signals are adequate (e.g. adequate SNR, lock-mass counts, and migration-time prediction) before metabolite peak annotation; inadequate IS signals are the main cause of peak misannotation and outlier files. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03513
skills.summary: A quality-control step in PeakMeister's MSI-CE-MS preprocessing that verifies internal-standard signals are adequate (e.g. adequate SNR, lock-mass counts, and migration-time prediction) before metabolite peak annotation; inadequate IS signals are the main cause of peak misannotation and outlier files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a clean peak-area or reference-range table — this check is upstream, on raw mzML/EIE signals. When the analyte of interest does not rely on internal standards or landmark peaks for migration-time prediction (e.g. purely de novo feature detection outside targeted MSI-CE-MS). When matrix effects or peak misannotation arise from co-migrating analytes (interference.comigration.threshold handling) rather than from weak IS signals.

skills.description: Use when a GC-MS experiment includes known internal or external standards and automated component-area extraction must be verified for accuracy before compound quantification is trusted.
skills.name: internal-standard-validation
skills.search_text: internal-standard-validation Use when a GC-MS experiment includes known internal or external standards and automated component-area extraction must be verified for accuracy before compound quantification is trusted. The dataset contains no known internal or external standards, so extracted areas cannot be checked against injected amounts Data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 acquisitions — uafR's algorithms depend on published spectra and do not yet apply Data come from instrument types other than GC-MS (e.g., Q-TOF, Orbitrap, TimsTOF HT, Astral, or LC-MS), where uafR is untested http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates automated GC-MS compound extraction and area aggregation in uafR by running mzExacto()/standardifyIt() on known internal standards and confirming that extracted peak areas correlate with injected standard amounts (R2 ≈ 0.83–0.9999). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0306202
skills.summary: Validates automated GC-MS compound extraction and area aggregation in uafR by running mzExacto()/standardifyIt() on known internal standards and confirming that extracted peak areas correlate with injected standard amounts (R2 ≈ 0.83–0.9999).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no known internal or external standards, so extracted areas cannot be checked against injected amounts Data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 acquisitions — uafR's algorithms depend on published spectra and do not yet apply Data come from instrument types other than GC-MS (e.g., Q-TOF, Orbitrap, TimsTOF HT, Astral, or LC-MS), where uafR is untested

skills.search_text: internal-test-set-evaluation Use when retraining or evaluating the BitterMasS Random Forest classifier on subsets of combined MassBank spectra and you need held-out precision/recall comparable to the paper's internal test set (precision = 0.83, recall = 0.90). Evaluating on the external validation sets (106 literature-extracted spectra or the 26 laboratory-measured compounds) — these require the separate external-set protocol, not the internal held-out split The goal is spectrum-to-structure annotation followed by structure-based bitterness prediction (BitterPredict route) rather than direct spectrum-bitterness classification with BitterMasS http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Holds out a fixed internal test set from the combined EI-MS/ESI-MS/MS spectral training data so a retrained BitterMasS Random Forest classifier can be scored with precision and recall, supporting learning-curve analyses of training-set-size effects. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jafc.3c09767

skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating on the external validation sets (106 literature-extracted spectra or the 26 laboratory-measured compounds) — these require the separate external-set protocol, not the internal held-out split The goal is spectrum-to-structure annotation followed by structure-based bitterness prediction (BitterPredict route) rather than direct spectrum-bitterness classification with BitterMasS

skills.description: Use when you have multiple stochastic predictions (e.g., MC-dropout embeddings) per compound pair and must decide which similarity scores are reliable enough to use downstream, or quantify the error-vs-retrieval tradeoff.
skills.name: interquartile-range-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: interquartile-range-threshold-filtering Use when you have multiple stochastic predictions (e.g., MC-dropout embeddings) per compound pair and must decide which similarity scores are reliable enough to use downstream, or quantify the error-vs-retrieval tradeoff. Predictions come from a single deterministic score per pair with no ensemble/dropout distribution, so no IQR can be computed The analysis requires full coverage of all compound pairs — filtering at IQR < 0.025 discards ~75% of scores, which is unacceptable for exhaustive retrieval Input spectra are from compound classes heavily underrepresented in the training library; the article notes spectral libraries are biased toward certain compound classes, so uncertainty filtering will not fix systematic bias http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Filters Monte-Carlo dropout ensemble Tanimoto score predictions (from MS2DeepScore Siamese-network embeddings) by an interquartile range (IQR) uncertainty threshold, retaining only confident scores. This trades retrieval rate for accuracy: filtering at IQR < 0.025 discards ~75% of scores but lowers RMSE from ~0.17 to ~0.11. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Filters Monte-Carlo dropout ensemble Tanimoto score predictions (from MS2DeepScore Siamese-network embeddings) by an interquartile range (IQR) uncertainty threshold, retaining only confident scores. This trades retrieval rate for accuracy: filtering at IQR < 0.025 discards ~75% of scores but lowers RMSE from ~0.17 to ~0.11.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predictions come from a single deterministic score per pair with no ensemble/dropout distribution, so no IQR can be computed The analysis requires full coverage of all compound pairs — filtering at IQR < 0.025 discards ~75% of scores, which is unacceptable for exhaustive retrieval Input spectra are from compound classes heavily underrepresented in the training library; the article notes spectral libraries are biased toward certain compound classes, so uncertainty filtering will not fix systematic bias

skills.description: Use when a task requires confirming which genes (e.g. STK11, CFTR, BMPR1A, SMAD4, NOTCH1, PKD1, MLH1, MSH2, APC, MEFV) are associated with multiple intestinal diseases in GutUDB.
skills.name: intestinal-disease-gene-set-verification
skills.search_text: intestinal-disease-gene-set-verification Use when a task requires confirming which genes (e.g. STK11, CFTR, BMPR1A, SMAD4, NOTCH1, PKD1, MLH1, MSH2, APC, MEFV) are associated with multiple intestinal diseases in GutUDB. The analysis targets diseases outside GutUDB's scope — the database covers 56 intestinal diseases across six species, so non-intestinal disease-gene questions are out of scope The task requires de novo identification of shared genes rather than verification of the published list (STK11, CFTR, BMPR1A, SMAD4, NOTCH1, PKD1, MLH1, MSH2, APC, MEFV) already reported for these nine diseases The task concerns drug-disease interactions or other GutUDB modules (e.g. the 21,984 drug-disease interactions in THERAPY) rather than disease-gene associations http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3324 Verifies a claimed shared-gene list across the nine main intestine-related diseases using GutUDB's 260,790 disease-gene associations, and annotates disease-specific exemplar genes such as STK11 for Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and SMAD4/BMPR1A for Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Verifies a claimed shared-gene list across the nine main intestine-related diseases using GutUDB's 260,790 disease-gene associations, and annotates disease-specific exemplar genes such as STK11 for Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and SMAD4/BMPR1A for Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets diseases outside GutUDB's scope — the database covers 56 intestinal diseases across six species, so non-intestinal disease-gene questions are out of scope The task requires de novo identification of shared genes rather than verification of the published list (STK11, CFTR, BMPR1A, SMAD4, NOTCH1, PKD1, MLH1, MSH2, APC, MEFV) already reported for these nine diseases The task concerns drug-disease interactions or other GutUDB modules (e.g. the 21,984 drug-disease interactions in THERAPY) rather than disease-gene associations

skills.description: Use when a targeted metabolomics run sequence shows run-order-dependent signal drift within a batch/plate (visible in pooled QC or replicate traces over run order) and drift must be removed before between-batch correction.
skills.name: intra-batch-drift-adjustment-of-targeted-metabolomics
skills.search_text: intra-batch-drift-adjustment-of-targeted-metabolomics Use when a targeted metabolomics run sequence shows run-order-dependent signal drift within a batch/plate (visible in pooled QC or replicate traces over run order) and drift must be removed before between-batch correction. The analysis goal is between-batch variation removal — that is handled by RUV-III with embedded sample replicates in hRUV, not by the intra-batch smoother The matrix still contains substantial missing values and no imputation strategy (e.g. the DMwR2/impute packages) has been decided — hRUV expects data without missing values Drift is attributable to pooled-QC degradation over months/years between batches rather than run-order effects within a single plate; the intra-batch smoother does not address that assumption failure http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Corrects within-batch signal drift in targeted metabolomics by fitting, per metabolite, a robust smoother (loess or robust linear model rlm) of log2 signal against run order and subtracting the fitted trend, as done in the hRUV workflow on BioHEART-CT plasma data. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Corrects within-batch signal drift in targeted metabolomics by fitting, per metabolite, a robust smoother (loess or robust linear model rlm) of log2 signal against run order and subtracting the fitted trend, as done in the hRUV workflow on BioHEART-CT plasma data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is between-batch variation removal — that is handled by RUV-III with embedded sample replicates in hRUV, not by the intra-batch smoother The matrix still contains substantial missing values and no imputation strategy (e.g. the DMwR2/impute packages) has been decided — hRUV expects data without missing values Drift is attributable to pooled-QC degradation over months/years between batches rather than run-order effects within a single plate; the intra-batch smoother does not address that assumption failure

skills.description: Use when a batch's samples must be ordered for LC/GC-MS injection such that treatment/placebo or other randomized dimensions never cluster (e.g., no three consecutive samples of the same group) after inter-batch balancing has been done.
skills.name: intra-batch-injection-order-randomization
skills.search_text: intra-batch-injection-order-randomization Use when a batch's samples must be ordered for LC/GC-MS injection such that treatment/placebo or other randomized dimensions never cluster (e.g., no three consecutive samples of the same group) after inter-batch balancing has been done. When preserving the natural numerical characteristics of a sample feature distribution matters more than uniform averaging — block randomization 'completely averages out the distribution of the sample features' When a dimension has too many groups under special numerical distributions, where the optimized block randomization averaging step can cause local aggregation When inter-batch balancing across batches (e.g., by age, gender) is the actual goal — use the inter-batch balancing skill instead Randomizes the injection order of samples within each LC/GC-MS batch using block randomization (balanced dimensions, e.g. block size 2) or optimized block randomization (unequally distributed dimensions), reducing machine drift and batch effect while keeping group distribution even. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.02.26.530140
skills.summary: Randomizes the injection order of samples within each LC/GC-MS batch using block randomization (balanced dimensions, e.g. block size 2) or optimized block randomization (unequally distributed dimensions), reducing machine drift and batch effect while keeping group distribution even.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When preserving the natural numerical characteristics of a sample feature distribution matters more than uniform averaging — block randomization 'completely averages out the distribution of the sample features' When a dimension has too many groups under special numerical distributions, where the optimized block randomization averaging step can cause local aggregation When inter-batch balancing across batches (e.g., by age, gender) is the actual goal — use the inter-batch balancing skill instead

skills.description: Decision support for ranking candidate lipid annotations in LC-MS/MS data when multiple isobaric chain-composition assignments exist within one subclass and only retention order can discriminate them.
skills.name: intra-subclass-unsaturation-parallelism-checking
skills.search_text: intra-subclass-unsaturation-parallelism-checking Decision support for ranking candidate lipid annotations in LC-MS/MS data when multiple isobaric chain-composition assignments exist within one subclass and only retention order can discriminate them. The input is an unannotated feature table with no lipid subclass labels or chain compositions — the rule can only be checked after MS/MS-based annotation has assigned subclasses and double-bond counts. Retention times come from direct infusion, GC, or SFC-MS rather than reversed-phase LC-MS/MS lipidomics, where the intra-subclass RT ordering underlying the rule does not apply. The goal is absolute RT prediction (e.g. via the WMYn model) rather than relative-order conformity checking between candidate annotations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Verifies the second of LipidIN's three relative retention-time rules: within a lipid subclass, lipids sharing the same number of C=C double bonds must elute in parallel RT order as acyl chain length varies. It is the empirical basis for the LC categories intelligence (LCI) module's RT-based annotation confidence. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Verifies the second of LipidIN's three relative retention-time rules: within a lipid subclass, lipids sharing the same number of C=C double bonds must elute in parallel RT order as acyl chain length varies. It is the empirical basis for the LC categories intelligence (LCI) module's RT-based annotation confidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an unannotated feature table with no lipid subclass labels or chain compositions — the rule can only be checked after MS/MS-based annotation has assigned subclasses and double-bond counts. Retention times come from direct infusion, GC, or SFC-MS rather than reversed-phase LC-MS/MS lipidomics, where the intra-subclass RT ordering underlying the rule does not apply. The goal is absolute RT prediction (e.g. via the WMYn model) rather than relative-order conformity checking between candidate annotations.

skills.description: Use when two or more simulated or experimentally acquired MRS basis sets (e.g. MRSCloud vs FID-A, MRSCloud vs MARSS, MRSCloud vs LCModel .basis, or 21/41/101 spatial-point runs) must be compared metabolite-by-metabolite for agreement.
skills.name: intraclass-correlation-coefficient-analysis
skills.search_text: intraclass-correlation-coefficient-analysis Use when two or more simulated or experimentally acquired MRS basis sets (e.g. MRSCloud vs FID-A, MRSCloud vs MARSS, MRSCloud vs LCModel .basis, or 21/41/101 spatial-point runs) must be compared metabolite-by-metabolite for agreement. The inputs are raw in-vivo MRS data to be quantified with LCModel analysis rather than basis sets to be cross-validated — this skill compares simulated/acquired basis functions, not fits. The basis sets use localization or vendor settings outside MRSCloud's scope (e.g. STEAM or SPECIAL), since no comparable simulated basis functions exist to correlate. Waveforms and timings of the comparison basis set are undocumented (as with the LCModel vendor-provided basis set), so ICC differences cannot be attributed to simulation accuracy rather than acquisition differences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A statistical validation skill that quantifies agreement between pairs or sets of MRS metabolite basis functions by computing per-metabolite intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) — and optionally normalized root-mean-square differences (NRMS) — in R/RStudio. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: A statistical validation skill that quantifies agreement between pairs or sets of MRS metabolite basis functions by computing per-metabolite intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) — and optionally normalized root-mean-square differences (NRMS) — in R/RStudio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The inputs are raw in-vivo MRS data to be quantified with LCModel analysis rather than basis sets to be cross-validated — this skill compares simulated/acquired basis functions, not fits. The basis sets use localization or vendor settings outside MRSCloud's scope (e.g. STEAM or SPECIAL), since no comparable simulated basis functions exist to correlate. Waveforms and timings of the comparison basis set are undocumented (as with the LCModel vendor-provided basis set), so ICC differences cannot be attributed to simulation accuracy rather than acquisition differences.

skills.description: Use when two metabolomic conditions are to be compared for differential metabolite-metabolite interaction identification, especially when validating against a curated model (e.g. BioModels BIOM0000000070) and scoring precision/sensitivity/specificity.
skills.name: inverse-differential-jacobian-interaction-validation
skills.search_text: inverse-differential-jacobian-interaction-validation Use when two metabolomic conditions are to be compared for differential metabolite-metabolite interaction identification, especially when validating against a curated model (e.g. BioModels BIOM0000000070) and scoring precision/sensitivity/specificity. Only one experimental condition is available — the inverse differential Jacobian requires two condition Jacobians to differ element-wise. No prior metabolite interaction stoichiometry (interactions_fin) is available, since calculate_jacobian requires it as input. The goal is MetaboAnalyst statistical preprocessing or pathway enrichment only, not dynamic interaction network inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies the MInfer Jacobian pipeline (prepare_data → generate_covariance → calculate_jacobian) to two metabolic conditions and computes the inverse differential Jacobian per Sun and Weckwerth to identify differential metabolite-metabolite interactions, scoring them with precision, sensitivity, and specificity against a curated reference such as the RBC model BIOM0000000070. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cmpb.2025.108672
skills.summary: Applies the MInfer Jacobian pipeline (prepare_data → generate_covariance → calculate_jacobian) to two metabolic conditions and computes the inverse differential Jacobian per Sun and Weckwerth to identify differential metabolite-metabolite interactions, scoring them with precision, sensitivity, and specificity against a curated reference such as the RBC model BIOM0000000070.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one experimental condition is available — the inverse differential Jacobian requires two condition Jacobians to differ element-wise. No prior metabolite interaction stoichiometry (interactions_fin) is available, since calculate_jacobian requires it as input. The goal is MetaboAnalyst statistical preprocessing or pathway enrichment only, not dynamic interaction network inference.

skills.description: Use when estimating per-annotation false discovery rates in imaging mass spectrometry where decoys were generated by SD-sampling of ion similarities, and each decoy carries a standard-deviation value that should modulate its decoy weight.
skills.name: inverse-sd-decoy-weighting
skills.search_text: inverse-sd-decoy-weighting Use when estimating per-annotation false discovery rates in imaging mass spectrometry where decoys were generated by SD-sampling of ion similarities, and each decoy carries a standard-deviation value that should modulate its decoy weight. Decoys are not SD-sampled and carry no standard-deviation values, so the 1/SD weighting is undefined The goal is discrete FDR thresholds from a plain target-decoy counting scheme without weighted decoys or Laplace smoothing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Weight each sample-deviation (SD)-sampled decoy ion by 1/SD of its sampled similarities within the METASPACE-ML target-decoy ranking, so that noisy decoys contribute proportionally less to cumulative FDR, and apply the Laplace rule-of-succession correction to yield smooth per-ion FDR values. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-52213-9
skills.summary: Weight each sample-deviation (SD)-sampled decoy ion by 1/SD of its sampled similarities within the METASPACE-ML target-decoy ranking, so that noisy decoys contribute proportionally less to cumulative FDR, and apply the Laplace rule-of-succession correction to yield smooth per-ion FDR values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Decoys are not SD-sampled and carry no standard-deviation values, so the 1/SD weighting is undefined The goal is discrete FDR thresholds from a plain target-decoy counting scheme without weighted decoys or Laplace smoothing
