skills.summary: A curation skill for untargeted metabolomics putative-annotation tables that recognizes isomers and equivalent compounds, removes redundant annotation entries, and merges remaining rows to shrink massive datasets before manual inspection and metabolite prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation table is already curated and contains no redundant or isomer-equivalent putative entries, so RowMerger/REname would have nothing to merge The input is raw mass-spectrometry data (e.g., mzML) rather than an annotation table — TurboPutative operates on putative annotation tables, not spectra Only compound classification is needed without any redundancy handling — running the full four-module workflow would be excessive

skills.description: Use when clustering preprocessed LC–MS/MS MS2 spectra (e.g. per-sample MGF files from step 2) where co-eluting structural isomers of the same precursor m/z must not be merged into a single consensus spectrum.
skills.name: isomer-resolution-in-spectral-clustering
skills.search_text: isomer-resolution-in-spectral-clustering Use when clustering preprocessed LC–MS/MS MS2 spectra (e.g. per-sample MGF files from step 2) where co-eluting structural isomers of the same precursor m/z must not be merged into a single consensus spectrum. Input is already a set of clean consensus spectra or an MGF library file — re-running isomer-resolving clustering would duplicate work rather than de-replicate. Goal is only to merge redundant spectra of the same ion with no structural-isomer ambiguity (e.g. single-peak features with no co-eluting isomers) — the iterative NP3-shifted-cosine rounds are unnecessary. You need de novo structural annotation of individual isomers — this skill only separates isomeric consensus spectra; structural assignment requires downstream Library Identification (e.g. Tremolo against ISDB/GNPS). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Resolves structural isomers during LC–MS/MS consensus spectrum construction by iteratively re-clustering preprocessed MS2 spectra with the NP3-shifted cosine (a greedy version of the modified cosine) inside the NP3 MS Workflow's Clustering/Quantification/Cleaning steps, so that isomeric ions of identical m/z remain separate clean consensus spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Resolves structural isomers during LC–MS/MS consensus spectrum construction by iteratively re-clustering preprocessed MS2 spectra with the NP3-shifted cosine (a greedy version of the modified cosine) inside the NP3 MS Workflow's Clustering/Quantification/Cleaning steps, so that isomeric ions of identical m/z remain separate clean consensus spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of clean consensus spectra or an MGF library file — re-running isomer-resolving clustering would duplicate work rather than de-replicate. Goal is only to merge redundant spectra of the same ion with no structural-isomer ambiguity (e.g. single-peak features with no co-eluting isomers) — the iterative NP3-shifted-cosine rounds are unnecessary. You need de novo structural annotation of individual isomers — this skill only separates isomeric consensus spectra; structural assignment requires downstream Library Identification (e.g. Tremolo against ISDB/GNPS).

skills.description: Use when an LC–MS/MS dataset shows a single precursor m/z (e.g. m/z 589.31) with multiple chromatographic peaks, and the goal is to count distinct isomers, assign them to spectral clusters, and annotate them via GNPS library spectra.
skills.name: isomer-separation-analysis
skills.search_text: isomer-separation-analysis Use when an LC–MS/MS dataset shows a single precursor m/z (e.g. m/z 589.31) with multiple chromatographic peaks, and the goal is to count distinct isomers, assign them to spectral clusters, and annotate them via GNPS library spectra. When the analysis targets are bioactivity-ranked ions (BCC scoring against blank/culture media) rather than isomer resolution within one precursor m/z When input is already a feature/quantification table rather than raw LC–MS/MS data requiring NP3 preprocessing When the precursor m/z has only a single chromatographic peak and no spectral-cluster ambiguity to resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Resolves how many distinct isomeric species underlie a single precursor m/z in LC–MS/MS data by combining NP3 MS Workflow's spectral clustering (NP3-shifted cosine) with extracted ion chromatogram peak counting, then annotating each resolved isomer against the GNPS spectral database. Demonstrated on the Euphorbia dendroides MSV000080502 dataset, where 11 distinct m/z 589.31 isomers were detected and the associated m/z 607.32 ion was annotated as a 4-deoxyphorbol ester analogue. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Resolves how many distinct isomeric species underlie a single precursor m/z in LC–MS/MS data by combining NP3 MS Workflow's spectral clustering (NP3-shifted cosine) with extracted ion chromatogram peak counting, then annotating each resolved isomer against the GNPS spectral database. Demonstrated on the Euphorbia dendroides MSV000080502 dataset, where 11 distinct m/z 589.31 isomers were detected and the associated m/z 607.32 ion was annotated as a 4-deoxyphorbol ester analogue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis targets are bioactivity-ranked ions (BCC scoring against blank/culture media) rather than isomer resolution within one precursor m/z When input is already a feature/quantification table rather than raw LC–MS/MS data requiring NP3 preprocessing When the precursor m/z has only a single chromatographic peak and no spectral-cluster ambiguity to resolve

skills.description: Use when an LC–MS/MS data set contains multiple isomeric or co-eluting compounds at the same m/z and you need to quantify how many distinct features survive processing, or compare feature/node consolidation between NP3 and GNPS FBMN.
skills.name: isomer-separation-feature-counting
skills.search_text: isomer-separation-feature-counting Use when an LC–MS/MS data set contains multiple isomeric or co-eluting compounds at the same m/z and you need to quantify how many distinct features survive processing, or compare feature/node consolidation between NP3 and GNPS FBMN. The input is already a processed feature/quantification table with no MS2 spectra — isomer re-counting requires the raw LC–MS/MS and NP3's Clustering/Cleaning steps The goal is a single consolidated molecular network with minimal node count rather than isomer-resolved feature enumeration (GNPS FBMN's 0.4% duplication rate indicates stronger consolidation by design) Only MS1 data are available; the NP3-shifted cosine cleaning and isomer discrimination rely on MS2 spectra in MGF files http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Counts and validates distinct isomeric features at a shared m/z in LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics, exploiting NP3 MS Workflow's spectral cleaning (NP3-shifted cosine) and filtered SSMN to avoid the over-consolidation of co-eluting isomers seen in GNPS FBMN. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Counts and validates distinct isomeric features at a shared m/z in LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics, exploiting NP3 MS Workflow's spectral cleaning (NP3-shifted cosine) and filtered SSMN to avoid the over-consolidation of co-eluting isomers seen in GNPS FBMN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature/quantification table with no MS2 spectra — isomer re-counting requires the raw LC–MS/MS and NP3's Clustering/Cleaning steps The goal is a single consolidated molecular network with minimal node count rather than isomer-resolved feature enumeration (GNPS FBMN's 0.4% duplication rate indicates stronger consolidation by design) Only MS1 data are available; the NP3-shifted cosine cleaning and isomer discrimination rely on MS2 spectra in MGF files

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple collision energies (e.g., NCE 1–100%) must be converted into quantitative identification thresholds separating identical isomer pairs from constitutional isomer pairs.
skills.name: isomer-similarity-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: isomer-similarity-distribution-analysis Use when MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple collision energies (e.g., NCE 1–100%) must be converted into quantitative identification thresholds separating identical isomer pairs from constitutional isomer pairs. Only single-collision-energy MS/MS spectra are available, since longitudinal fragment profiles require relative ion intensities of a fragment across multiple collision energies. The goal is general compound annotation against public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, METLIN) rather than establishing quantitative identification criteria for isomer discrimination in the CQMD database. Candidate ranking only is needed — this skill derives acceptance cutoffs via ROC analysis, not candidate lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Establishes identification criteria for isomer-level metabolite identification by computing intensity-based over number-based (I/N) Jaccard similarity ratios for identical versus constitutional isomer pairs, then running per-bin ROC analysis of longitudinal fragment profile (LFP) data to derive optimal similarity cutoffs with sensitivity/specificity. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: Establishes identification criteria for isomer-level metabolite identification by computing intensity-based over number-based (I/N) Jaccard similarity ratios for identical versus constitutional isomer pairs, then running per-bin ROC analysis of longitudinal fragment profile (LFP) data to derive optimal similarity cutoffs with sensitivity/specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only single-collision-energy MS/MS spectra are available, since longitudinal fragment profiles require relative ion intensities of a fragment across multiple collision energies. The goal is general compound annotation against public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, METLIN) rather than establishing quantitative identification criteria for isomer discrimination in the CQMD database. Candidate ranking only is needed — this skill derives acceptance cutoffs via ROC analysis, not candidate lists.

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectral matching produces ambiguous or highest-score-tied identifications for isomers (e.g., leucine vs isoleucine) and multi-collision-energy spectra are available to compute longitudinal fragment profiles.
skills.name: isomer-spectral-jaccard-matching
skills.search_text: isomer-spectral-jaccard-matching Use when MS/MS spectral matching produces ambiguous or highest-score-tied identifications for isomers (e.g., leucine vs isoleucine) and multi-collision-energy spectra are available to compute longitudinal fragment profiles. Only a single-collision-energy (stepped NCE) spectrum is available with no multi-CE acquisition — longitudinal Jaccard requires LFPs across 13 distinct CEs; cross-sectional algorithms like entropy similarity are the fallback. The analytical goal is general metabolite annotation against public databases (MoNA, GNPS, METLIN) rather than discriminating candidate isomers with highly similar substructures. Input spectra have not passed spectrum filtering, invalid fragment removal, and fragment rationality assessment — the upstream preprocessing from 001-007.ipynb is a prerequisite. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 An optimized Jaccard similarity algorithm for matching MS/MS spectra of isomers by comparing longitudinal fragment ion-intensity profiles (LFPs) across multiple collision energies, treating predominant and minute fragments independently. This differentiates isomers like leucine/isoleucine that cross-sectional spectral matching cannot separate. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: An optimized Jaccard similarity algorithm for matching MS/MS spectra of isomers by comparing longitudinal fragment ion-intensity profiles (LFPs) across multiple collision energies, treating predominant and minute fragments independently. This differentiates isomers like leucine/isoleucine that cross-sectional spectral matching cannot separate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single-collision-energy (stepped NCE) spectrum is available with no multi-CE acquisition — longitudinal Jaccard requires LFPs across 13 distinct CEs; cross-sectional algorithms like entropy similarity are the fallback. The analytical goal is general metabolite annotation against public databases (MoNA, GNPS, METLIN) rather than discriminating candidate isomers with highly similar substructures. Input spectra have not passed spectrum filtering, invalid fragment removal, and fragment rationality assessment — the upstream preprocessing from 001-007.ipynb is a prerequisite.

skills.description: Use when enrichment analysis must be run on MS1-level imaging or single-cell metabolomics annotations (e.g., METASPACE formula-adduct IDs) where each ion may map to multiple isomeric/isobaric candidates, and conventional ORA/MSEA would treat ambiguous assignments as fixed.
skills.name: isomeric-isobaric-ambiguity-propagation
skills.search_text: isomeric-isobaric-ambiguity-propagation Use when enrichment analysis must be run on MS1-level imaging or single-cell metabolomics annotations (e.g., METASPACE formula-adduct IDs) where each ion may map to multiple isomeric/isobaric candidates, and conventional ORA/MSEA would treat ambiguous assignments as fixed. When MS/MS or other data resolve isomeric/isobaric structures so each annotated ion maps to a single molecular candidate — standard ORA without bootstrapping suffices When the annotation database/background does not map terms to molecule names or sum formulas in a way that supports isomer/isobar candidate enumeration (e.g., non-LION ontology backgrounds where ambiguity cannot be propagated) When the goal is mere annotation QC rather than term-level overrepresentation or set enrichment testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A bootstrapping-based enrichment approach (S2IsoMEr) that propagates isomeric/isobaric molecular ambiguity from MS1-only metabolite annotations into overrepresentation analysis (ORA) and metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) by randomly sampling one candidate per annotated ion per iteration and aggregating per-term statistics with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf100
skills.summary: A bootstrapping-based enrichment approach (S2IsoMEr) that propagates isomeric/isobaric molecular ambiguity from MS1-only metabolite annotations into overrepresentation analysis (ORA) and metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) by randomly sampling one candidate per annotated ion per iteration and aggregating per-term statistics with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When MS/MS or other data resolve isomeric/isobaric structures so each annotated ion maps to a single molecular candidate — standard ORA without bootstrapping suffices When the annotation database/background does not map terms to molecule names or sum formulas in a way that supports isomer/isobar candidate enumeration (e.g., non-LION ontology backgrounds where ambiguity cannot be propagated) When the goal is mere annotation QC rather than term-level overrepresentation or set enrichment testing

skills.description: Use when MALDI-imaging matrix clusters (e.g., 353 predicted DHB formulas) must be re-annotated against HMDB v4 at FDR <= 50% and checked for exact-formula (isomeric) overlap with non-matrix metabolites.
skills.name: isomeric-molecule-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: isomeric-molecule-overlap-analysis Use when MALDI-imaging matrix clusters (e.g., 353 predicted DHB formulas) must be re-annotated against HMDB v4 at FDR <= 50% and checked for exact-formula (isomeric) overlap with non-matrix metabolites. Annotations are resolved by structural or MS/MS-level search rather than formula search — isomeric formula collisions are then already separated by the method and this skill adds nothing. The MALDI matrix is not DHB — the 353-formula Keller and Li (2000) cluster model covers only 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid cluster chemistry. Ion images lack off-sample/on-sample classifier labels — the isomeric fraction is defined only over recognized off-sample cluster ions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Quantifies how many recognized off-sample DHB matrix-cluster ion annotations share an exact molecular formula with non-matrix HMDB v4 molecules, exposing the 4.3% of matrix signal that formula-level annotation cannot disambiguate from biology. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: Quantifies how many recognized off-sample DHB matrix-cluster ion annotations share an exact molecular formula with non-matrix HMDB v4 molecules, exposing the 4.3% of matrix signal that formula-level annotation cannot disambiguate from biology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotations are resolved by structural or MS/MS-level search rather than formula search — isomeric formula collisions are then already separated by the method and this skill adds nothing. The MALDI matrix is not DHB — the 353-formula Keller and Li (2000) cluster model covers only 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid cluster chemistry. Ion images lack off-sample/on-sample classifier labels — the isomeric fraction is defined only over recognized off-sample cluster ions.

skills.description: Use when a molecule set (e.g. McLean CCS Compendium entries) is represented as neutral InChI strings and must be converted to isomeric SMILES/MOL files to feed descriptor-based CCS predictors like CCSP 2.0, AllCCS, CCSbase or DeepCCS.
skills.name: isomeric-smiles-input-preparation
skills.search_text: isomeric-smiles-input-preparation Use when a molecule set (e.g. McLean CCS Compendium entries) is represented as neutral InChI strings and must be converted to isomeric SMILES/MOL files to feed descriptor-based CCS predictors like CCSP 2.0, AllCCS, CCSbase or DeepCCS. The molecules are already provided as isomeric SMILES — skip InChI conversion and go directly to RDKit MOL encoding and descriptor calculation Structures lack a resolvable neutral InChI in PubChem or are not representable as 2D small-molecule SMILES (e.g. mixtures, polymers, in-source fragments) 3D conformer-dependent descriptors are required — CCSP 2.0's feature space is strictly the 1613 2D Mordred descriptors http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts neutral InChI strings from a CCS reference compendium into isomeric SMILES via the PubChem Identifier Exchange Service, then encodes each SMILES as a MOL file with RDKit so that 1613 2D Mordred descriptors can be computed for CCSP 2.0 SVR-based CCS prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2022.08.09.503345
skills.summary: Converts neutral InChI strings from a CCS reference compendium into isomeric SMILES via the PubChem Identifier Exchange Service, then encodes each SMILES as a MOL file with RDKit so that 1613 2D Mordred descriptors can be computed for CCSP 2.0 SVR-based CCS prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecules are already provided as isomeric SMILES — skip InChI conversion and go directly to RDKit MOL encoding and descriptor calculation Structures lack a resolvable neutral InChI in PubChem or are not representable as 2D small-molecule SMILES (e.g. mixtures, polymers, in-source fragments) 3D conformer-dependent descriptors are required — CCSP 2.0's feature space is strictly the 1613 2D Mordred descriptors

skills.description: Use when a curated database (e.g. MIBiG JSON entries) assigns named substrates to enzyme domains and each name must be backed by a valid isomeric SMILES before counting or downstream ML use.
skills.name: isomeric-smiles-validation
skills.search_text: isomeric-smiles-validation Use when a curated database (e.g. MIBiG JSON entries) assigns named substrates to enzyme domains and each name must be backed by a valid isomeric SMILES before counting or downstream ML use. Input structures are only InChI or plain names with no isomeric SMILES to validate Goal is generic BGC detection rather than validating chemical structure annotations (use antiSMASH/GECCO instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Validates that substrate annotations carry syntactically correct, stereochemically curated isomeric SMILES strings before they are used to build substrate-to-structure mappings (e.g. the 274 unique NRPS A-domain substrates in MIBiG 3.0). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Validates that substrate annotations carry syntactically correct, stereochemically curated isomeric SMILES strings before they are used to build substrate-to-structure mappings (e.g. the 274 unique NRPS A-domain substrates in MIBiG 3.0).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input structures are only InChI or plain names with no isomeric SMILES to validate Goal is generic BGC detection rather than validating chemical structure annotations (use antiSMASH/GECCO instead)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS library-search FDR on natural-product or isomer-rich libraries, where decoy-like pairs differing by one bond must be isolated to measure FDR curves for entropy-similarity thresholds.
skills.name: isomeric-structure-grouping
skills.search_text: isomeric-structure-grouping Use when benchmarking MS/MS library-search FDR on natural-product or isomer-rich libraries, where decoy-like pairs differing by one bond must be isolated to measure FDR curves for entropy-similarity thresholds. When the analysis goal is general library search speed or index building (use Flash/Dynamic Entropy Search instead) rather than FDR evaluation on similar-structure groups When spectra have not been cleaned — raw peaks must first pass clean_spectrum preprocessing or group-level similarity scores will be unreliable When the library lacks compound structure annotations, since one-bond-difference collectives cannot be identified from spectra alone http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Groups library MS/MS spectra into collectives of highly similar structures whose compounds differ by a single bond, so that false discovery rates of spectral matching can be evaluated separately for isomer/isobar-confusable pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01331-z
skills.summary: Groups library MS/MS spectra into collectives of highly similar structures whose compounds differ by a single bond, so that false discovery rates of spectral matching can be evaluated separately for isomer/isobar-confusable pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is general library search speed or index building (use Flash/Dynamic Entropy Search instead) rather than FDR evaluation on similar-structure groups When spectra have not been cleaned — raw peaks must first pass clean_spectrum preprocessing or group-level similarity scores will be unreliable When the library lacks compound structure annotations, since one-bond-difference collectives cannot be identified from spectra alone

skills.description: Use when processing high-resolution GC-CI-MS (GC-qTOF or GC-Orbitrap) stable-isotope-labeling data and the expected isotopologue m/z values and their resolvability must be predicted from a derivatized formula prior to isotopologue quantification.
skills.name: isopattern-simulation-with-envipat
skills.search_text: isopattern-simulation-with-envipat Use when processing high-resolution GC-CI-MS (GC-qTOF or GC-Orbitrap) stable-isotope-labeling data and the expected isotopologue m/z values and their resolvability must be predicted from a derivatized formula prior to isotopologue quantification. Data are low-resolution (LRMS, e.g. QqQ in SIM mode), where isoSCAN does not use enviPat-based envelope prediction and selected ion clusters suffice Formula is unknown or cannot be reconstructed for the derivatized metabolite, so no isotopologue envelope can be simulated The task is chromatographic deconvolution rather than isotope-envelope prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Uses the enviPat R package's isotope table and isopattern function to predict the theoretical isotopologue m/z values and relative abundances of a derivatized metabolite formula, and to assess which neighbouring peaks are resolved at a given mass-analyser resolving power before they are quantified from GC-CI-MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02998
skills.summary: Uses the enviPat R package's isotope table and isopattern function to predict the theoretical isotopologue m/z values and relative abundances of a derivatized metabolite formula, and to assess which neighbouring peaks are resolved at a given mass-analyser resolving power before they are quantified from GC-CI-MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are low-resolution (LRMS, e.g. QqQ in SIM mode), where isoSCAN does not use enviPat-based envelope prediction and selected ion clusters suffice Formula is unknown or cannot be reconstructed for the derivatized metabolite, so no isotopologue envelope can be simulated The task is chromatographic deconvolution rather than isotope-envelope prediction

skills.name: isotope-adduct-annotation-camera
skills.search_text: isotope-adduct-annotation-camera Use when an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics peak table (e.g., Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos benchmark) needs isotope/adduct ion form annotation and a CAMERA-vs-network baseline comparison is required. When the goal is only to assign ion forms without evaluating annotation correctness against the manually curated benchmark — CAMERA grouping alone gives no correct-rate estimate When the peak table is already grouped/annotated by adduct and isotope rules, e.g., an output table from a prior CAMERA run When working with non-model organism or exposomics data where the knowledge-guided layer and benchmark references are not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Runs CAMERA rule-based isotope/adduct grouping on a curated LC-MS peak table to assign ion forms, and benchmarks those annotations against KGMN's global peak correlation network layer (CAMERA: 2297 ion forms at 81.7% correct vs KGMN: 3374 at 97.5%). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Runs CAMERA rule-based isotope/adduct grouping on a curated LC-MS peak table to assign ion forms, and benchmarks those annotations against KGMN's global peak correlation network layer (CAMERA: 2297 ion forms at 81.7% correct vs KGMN: 3374 at 97.5%).

skills.search_text: isotope-adduct-contaminant-false-positive-filtering Use when processing raw CE-MS or LC-MS (mzXML/mzML) metabolomics data with the AriumMS ROI workflow and you need to discard isotope/adduct/contaminant-derived ROI candidates that would inflate the feature list before data augmentation. skills.description: Use when an xcms/CAMERA feature table contains multiple m/z features per compound (adducts, isotopes) and a compound-level count is needed before applying fold-change, intensity, or sample-group filters.
skills.name: isotope-adduct-duplicate-removal
skills.search_text: isotope-adduct-duplicate-removal Use when an xcms/CAMERA feature table contains multiple m/z features per compound (adducts, isotopes) and a compound-level count is needed before applying fold-change, intensity, or sample-group filters. Input is a raw spectral file (mzML) that has not yet been feature-detected and grouped by XCMS/CAMERA — run feature detection first. The goal is isotope-tracing analysis of labeled compounds — Metaboseek's Label Finder, not adduct/isotope removal, is the appropriate module. Features have no CAMERA group annotations, since deduplication is defined over CAMERA-annotated feature groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A Metaboseek-based deduplication step that removes adduct and isotope duplicates arising from CAMERA-annotated feature groups in an LC/MS feature table, so that each detected compound (e.g., the 32 CA-derived metabolites in the hacl-1 study) is represented by a single feature before downstream filtering or annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: A Metaboseek-based deduplication step that removes adduct and isotope duplicates arising from CAMERA-annotated feature groups in an LC/MS feature table, so that each detected compound (e.g., the 32 CA-derived metabolites in the hacl-1 study) is represented by a single feature before downstream filtering or annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw spectral file (mzML) that has not yet been feature-detected and grouped by XCMS/CAMERA — run feature detection first. The goal is isotope-tracing analysis of labeled compounds — Metaboseek's Label Finder, not adduct/isotope removal, is the appropriate module. Features have no CAMERA group annotations, since deduplication is defined over CAMERA-annotated feature groups.

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (feature ID, m/z, retention time, sample intensities) from unlabeled or isotope-labeled experiments and need to group related ions into empirical compounds and infer neutral masses before formula or metabolite-level annotation.
skills.name: isotope-adduct-ion-grouping
skills.search_text: isotope-adduct-ion-grouping Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (feature ID, m/z, retention time, sample intensities) from unlabeled or isotope-labeled experiments and need to group related ions into empirical compounds and infer neutral masses before formula or metabolite-level annotation. When peaks have already been assigned to known metabolites or formulas and only fine-level curation (contaminants, authentic libraries, tandem MS) is needed — khipu is a low-level preannotation step, not a complete annotation. When the input is not a feature table but raw vendor/centroided MS data — khipu expects preprocessed features from a tool like asari. Input data lacks an unlabeled control condition to pair against the tracer-supplemented table — Label Finder requires a pairwise labeled/unlabeled comparison Feature tables are missing the required 'mz' and 'rt' columns, so isotope shifts cannot be computed The question is general comparative metabolomics between genotypes/conditions rather than tracer-derived isotope enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Detect isotope-labeled metabolites in LC/MS feature tables using Metaboseek's Label Finder module in pairwise mode, comparing a labeled tracer (e.g. 13C6-leucine) against an unlabeled control to identify label incorporation and trace biosynthetic origins of lipids. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: Detect isotope-labeled metabolites in LC/MS feature tables using Metaboseek's Label Finder module in pairwise mode, comparing a labeled tracer (e.g. 13C6-leucine) against an unlabeled control to identify label incorporation and trace biosynthetic origins of lipids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks an unlabeled control condition to pair against the tracer-supplemented table — Label Finder requires a pairwise labeled/unlabeled comparison Feature tables are missing the required 'mz' and 'rt' columns, so isotope shifts cannot be computed The question is general comparative metabolomics between genotypes/conditions rather than tracer-derived isotope enrichment

skills.description: Use when isotope-labeled metabolites (e.g. 13C-labeled amino acids) must be tracked across multiple tissues and assigned to distinct tissue-enrichment categories such as liver-enriched vs. co-enriched.
skills.name: isotope-labeled-compound-tissue-tracking
skills.search_text: isotope-labeled-compound-tissue-tracking Use when isotope-labeled metabolites (e.g. 13C-labeled amino acids) must be tracked across multiple tissues and assigned to distinct tissue-enrichment categories such as liver-enriched vs. co-enriched. Data are unlabeled (no 13C enrichment) or tissues are not matched to the same labeled diet, since distribution categories depend on isotope-tracing across the five tissues. The goal is compound annotation from raw INADEQUATE spectra rather than downstream tissue-distribution classification; PyINETA's peak-picking/network-matching skill handles that upstream step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Classifies the tissue distribution of metabolites derived from a 13C-labeled diet by quantifying their representative 13C-JRES peaks across tissues (liver, spleen, pancreas, muscle, lung) and assigning each compound to an enrichment category (e.g. liver-enriched, liver-depleted, co-enriched). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: Classifies the tissue distribution of metabolites derived from a 13C-labeled diet by quantifying their representative 13C-JRES peaks across tissues (liver, spleen, pancreas, muscle, lung) and assigning each compound to an enrichment category (e.g. liver-enriched, liver-depleted, co-enriched).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unlabeled (no 13C enrichment) or tissues are not matched to the same labeled diet, since distribution categories depend on isotope-tracing across the five tissues. The goal is compound annotation from raw INADEQUATE spectra rather than downstream tissue-distribution classification; PyINETA's peak-picking/network-matching skill handles that upstream step.

skills.description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with U13C-labeled internal standards and you must quantify or correct CCSN2 bias against a DT CCS library without extra external calibrant measurements.
skills.name: isotope-labeled-internal-standardization
skills.search_text: isotope-labeled-internal-standardization Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with U13C-labeled internal standards and you must quantify or correct CCSN2 bias against a DT CCS library without extra external calibrant measurements. Samples are not spiked with U13C-labeled internal standard lipids (e.g. only deuterated lipid mixes like EquiSPLASH LIPIDOMIX, which offer a limited lipid count) The lipid class-adduct combination in the data is not supported by MobiLipid's compatibility table, or fewer than 3 heavy lipids exist per combination so linear correction cannot be fit The measured data .csv lacks the required headers or its lipid class/species nomenclature differs from the DTCCSN2 library Assess and correct CCS bias in IM-MS lipidomics by comparing measured CCS values of U13C-labeled yeast lipids against a DTCCSN2 reference library, using the MobiLipid R Markdown tool for lipid class- and adduct-specific internal standardization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: Assess and correct CCS bias in IM-MS lipidomics by comparing measured CCS values of U13C-labeled yeast lipids against a DTCCSN2 reference library, using the MobiLipid R Markdown tool for lipid class- and adduct-specific internal standardization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are not spiked with U13C-labeled internal standard lipids (e.g. only deuterated lipid mixes like EquiSPLASH LIPIDOMIX, which offer a limited lipid count) The lipid class-adduct combination in the data is not supported by MobiLipid's compatibility table, or fewer than 3 heavy lipids exist per combination so linear correction cannot be fit The measured data .csv lacks the required headers or its lipid class/species nomenclature differs from the DTCCSN2 library

skills.description: Use when DTIM-MS lipidomics data contain both natural ('light') and U13C-labeled ('heavy') versions of the same lipid species and you need to compute per-pair DTCCSN2 bias against the U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv, e.
skills.name: isotope-labeled-lipid-pair-matching
skills.search_text: isotope-labeled-lipid-pair-matching Use when DTIM-MS lipidomics data contain both natural ('light') and U13C-labeled ('heavy') versions of the same lipid species and you need to compute per-pair DTCCSN2 bias against the U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv, e. Samples were not spiked with U13C-labeled internal standards (fully labeled yeast extract), so no 'heavy' entries exist to pair against the library The lipid class-adduct combination is outside the supported table (e.g. PC with [M+NH4] or AcCa with [M+NH4]) — such rows will not match library entries The goal is cross-technology bias monitoring (e.g. TIM-MS vs DTIM-MS) or CCS correction via regression functions rather than labeled/unlabeled pair matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Matches U13C-labeled ('heavy') and unlabeled monoisotopic ('light') lipid pairs measured by DTIM-MS against the U13C yeast DTCCSN2 library to quantify the systematic CCS bias per lipid class-adduct combination. It establishes the internal-standardization baseline (≈0.25% labeled-vs-unlabeled shift) that underpins MobiLipid CCS quality control. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: Matches U13C-labeled ('heavy') and unlabeled monoisotopic ('light') lipid pairs measured by DTIM-MS against the U13C yeast DTCCSN2 library to quantify the systematic CCS bias per lipid class-adduct combination. It establishes the internal-standardization baseline (≈0.25% labeled-vs-unlabeled shift) that underpins MobiLipid CCS quality control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples were not spiked with U13C-labeled internal standards (fully labeled yeast extract), so no 'heavy' entries exist to pair against the library The lipid class-adduct combination is outside the supported table (e.g. PC with [M+NH4] or AcCa with [M+NH4]) — such rows will not match library entries The goal is cross-technology bias monitoring (e.g. TIM-MS vs DTIM-MS) or CCS correction via regression functions rather than labeled/unlabeled pair matching

skills.description: Use when a series of 1D or pseudo-2D 1H NMR spectra from isotope labeling experiments (e.g., E. coli fed 1-13C1-glucose, U-13C6-glucose, and 2-13C1-acetate) must be decomposed into overlapping isotopomer multiplets and converted to time-course concentrations.
skills.name: isotope-labeler-quantification
skills.search_text: isotope-labeler-quantification Use when a series of 1D or pseudo-2D 1H NMR spectra from isotope labeling experiments (e.g., E. coli fed 1-13C1-glucose, U-13C6-glucose, and 2-13C1-acetate) must be decomposed into overlapping isotopomer multiplets and converted to time-course concentrations. The spectra are full 2D correlation experiments rather than 1D or pseudo-2D (series of 1D) acquisitions — outside MultiNMRFit's fitting scope The input is already a quantified concentration table (e.g., mM values per isotopomer) rather than spectra — no multiplet fitting is needed A single unsplit resonance with no isotope-dependent multiplet structure must be quantified — simple integration suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Quantifies time courses of isotopic species (e.g., 13C isotopomers of acetate) from series of 1D or pseudo-2D 1H NMR spectra by fitting overlapping multiplet components with MultiNMRFit and converting fitted areas to millimolar concentrations with reported standard deviations. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Quantifies time courses of isotopic species (e.g., 13C isotopomers of acetate) from series of 1D or pseudo-2D 1H NMR spectra by fitting overlapping multiplet components with MultiNMRFit and converting fitted areas to millimolar concentrations with reported standard deviations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are full 2D correlation experiments rather than 1D or pseudo-2D (series of 1D) acquisitions — outside MultiNMRFit's fitting scope The input is already a quantified concentration table (e.g., mM values per isotopomer) rather than spectra — no multiplet fitting is needed A single unsplit resonance with no isotope-dependent multiplet structure must be quantified — simple integration suffices

skills.description: Use when monitoring reactant-to-product conversion of isotope-labeled metabolites (1H, 13C, 31P) across a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra and extracting time-resolved concentrations.
skills.name: isotope-labeling-real-time-kinetics-analysis
skills.search_text: isotope-labeling-real-time-kinetics-analysis Use when monitoring reactant-to-product conversion of isotope-labeled metabolites (1H, 13C, 31P) across a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra and extracting time-resolved concentrations. The data are not a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (e.g., full 2D NMR spectra requiring multidimensional peak deconvolution) The goal is quantitative NMR of a single, static spectrum rather than time-course kinetics of labeled metabolite conversion Signals require multiplet models beyond the built-in ones and no user-defined model has been implemented for the observed spin system http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Quantify real-time conversion kinetics of isotope-labeled metabolites (e.g., uniformly 13C-labeled glucose to glucose-6-phosphate) by fitting multiplet signal models to series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra with MultiNMRFit. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Quantify real-time conversion kinetics of isotope-labeled metabolites (e.g., uniformly 13C-labeled glucose to glucose-6-phosphate) by fitting multiplet signal models to series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra with MultiNMRFit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (e.g., full 2D NMR spectra requiring multidimensional peak deconvolution) The goal is quantitative NMR of a single, static spectrum rather than time-course kinetics of labeled metabolite conversion Signals require multiplet models beyond the built-in ones and no user-defined model has been implemented for the observed spin system

skills.description: Use when assigning molecular formulas to ultrahigh-resolution mass spectra (FT-ICR/Orbitrap) where 13C and 34S polyisotopic peaks must be separated from monoisotopic masses before or after formula assignment.
skills.name: isotope-matched-formula-confirmation
skills.search_text: isotope-matched-formula-confirmation Use when assigning molecular formulas to ultrahigh-resolution mass spectra (FT-ICR/Orbitrap) where 13C and 34S polyisotopic peaks must be separated from monoisotopic masses before or after formula assignment. When the input spectrum has not been recalibrated and isotope-pair mass differences exceed the +/- 5 ppm window — run Recal() first When you need definitive proof of the presence or absence of 13C or 34S in a formula — the README states additional work would be needed and IsoFiltR should not be considered definitive For MS/MS or sparse spectra where the four-step KMD-series logic breaks down due to low continuity http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Match molecular formula assignments to their corresponding 13C and 34S isotope masses using MFAssignR's IsoFiltR and the Iso output from MFAssign, so that monoisotopic assignments are not made on isotope peaks and sulfur-containing seeds are isotope-supported. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.envres.2020.110114
skills.summary: Match molecular formula assignments to their corresponding 13C and 34S isotope masses using MFAssignR's IsoFiltR and the Iso output from MFAssign, so that monoisotopic assignments are not made on isotope peaks and sulfur-containing seeds are isotope-supported.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input spectrum has not been recalibrated and isotope-pair mass differences exceed the +/- 5 ppm window — run Recal() first When you need definitive proof of the presence or absence of 13C or 34S in a formula — the README states additional work would be needed and IsoFiltR should not be considered definitive For MS/MS or sparse spectra where the four-step KMD-series logic breaks down due to low continuity

skills.description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM data and you need the theoretical NRE correction matrix built from compound formula, isotope natural abundances, and tracer isotopic purity (e.g., 0.99 atomic for U-13C6 glucose).
skills.name: isotope-natural-abundance-correction-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: isotope-natural-abundance-correction-matrix-construction Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM data and you need the theoretical NRE correction matrix built from compound formula, isotope natural abundances, and tracer isotopic purity (e.g., 0.99 atomic for U-13C6 glucose). Data come from a high-resolving-power mass spectrometer (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000 or 280,000 nominal resolution) that resolves isotopologs with the same nominal mass — including all isotopologs in the correction matrix is then no longer justified and resolution-dependent (MDT/ULS) correction is preferred The selected tracer element is not present in the compound's formula — the algorithm will report an error (e.g., choosing C or S as tracer for 15N data where compounds lack C or S) The FAM data are already corrected MDVs or the analysis goal is flux fitting (INCA/FiatFlux) rather than isotope correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs the theoretical (non-resolution-effect, NRE) isotope correction matrix by combinatorial convolution of natural-abundance isotope distributions for all elements plus tracer isotopic impurity, as in IsoCor and as embedded in ElemCor's Step 3/4 parameters. It yields the (Nt+1)x(Nt+1) matrix that maps measured fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) to corrected mass distribution vectors (MDV). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Constructs the theoretical (non-resolution-effect, NRE) isotope correction matrix by combinatorial convolution of natural-abundance isotope distributions for all elements plus tracer isotopic impurity, as in IsoCor and as embedded in ElemCor's Step 3/4 parameters. It yields the (Nt+1)x(Nt+1) matrix that maps measured fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) to corrected mass distribution vectors (MDV).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from a high-resolving-power mass spectrometer (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000 or 280,000 nominal resolution) that resolves isotopologs with the same nominal mass — including all isotopologs in the correction matrix is then no longer justified and resolution-dependent (MDT/ULS) correction is preferred The selected tracer element is not present in the compound's formula — the algorithm will report an error (e.g., choosing C or S as tracer for 15N data where compounds lack C or S) The FAM data are already corrected MDVs or the analysis goal is flux fitting (INCA/FiatFlux) rather than isotope correction

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending molecular formula assignment benchmarks on annotated compound sets — e.g. comparing SIRIUS 3.0 vs SIRIUS 4 or isotope-pattern-only vs MS1+MS/MS settings on Supplementary Fig. 6a / Supplementary Table 3 data.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-analysis-evaluation
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-analysis-evaluation Use when reproducing or extending molecular formula assignment benchmarks on annotated compound sets — e.g. comparing SIRIUS 3.0 vs SIRIUS 4 or isotope-pattern-only vs MS1+MS/MS settings on Supplementary Fig. 6a / Supplementary Table 3 data. Input spectra lack high-resolution isotope patterns — SIRIUS ranks formulas by isotope patterns from mass spectra of high resolution, so low-res MS1 data breaks the premise. Goal is structure identification (CSI:FingerID/CANOPUS output) rather than evaluating molecular formula assignment accuracy. Data are raw spectra rather than per-compound top-1 assignment counts aggregated over an annotated benchmark set. Benchmark-style evaluation of SIRIUS isotope-pattern-based molecular formula assignment, comparing top-1 correct and wrongly assigned formula counts between SIRIUS versions and scoring settings (isotope-pattern-only vs MS1+MS/MS) on a 3,965-compound annotated dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8
skills.summary: Benchmark-style evaluation of SIRIUS isotope-pattern-based molecular formula assignment, comparing top-1 correct and wrongly assigned formula counts between SIRIUS versions and scoring settings (isotope-pattern-only vs MS1+MS/MS) on a 3,965-compound annotated dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack high-resolution isotope patterns — SIRIUS ranks formulas by isotope patterns from mass spectra of high resolution, so low-res MS1 data breaks the premise. Goal is structure identification (CSI:FingerID/CANOPUS output) rather than evaluating molecular formula assignment accuracy. Data are raw spectra rather than per-compound top-1 assignment counts aggregated over an annotated benchmark set.

skills.description: Use when you have high-resolution LC-MS/MS peak lists for small molecules and need to rank molecular formula candidates for the precursor ion, especially when MS1 isotope patterns are available or the element alphabet should be restricted.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-based-formula-ranking
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-based-formula-ranking Use when you have high-resolution LC-MS/MS peak lists for small molecules and need to rank molecular formula candidates for the precursor ion, especially when MS1 isotope patterns are available or the element alphabet should be restricted. Input spectra are low-resolution and contain no usable isotope patterns, so isotope-pattern ranking cannot discriminate candidate decompositions The goal is already-determined formulas to be searched as structures in molecular databases, not formula ranking from spectra You need compound structure identification (CSI:FingerID/CANOPUS/MSNovelist) without first establishing the molecular formula http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 SIRIUS's isotope pattern analysis deduces molecular formulas of small compounds by ranking candidate elemental decompositions of the precursor ion against high-resolution isotope patterns from MS1, restricted to a chosen element alphabet (e.g., CHNOPS, or CHNOPS plus BrClFI for halogen-containing compounds). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8
skills.summary: SIRIUS's isotope pattern analysis deduces molecular formulas of small compounds by ranking candidate elemental decompositions of the precursor ion against high-resolution isotope patterns from MS1, restricted to a chosen element alphabet (e.g., CHNOPS, or CHNOPS plus BrClFI for halogen-containing compounds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are low-resolution and contain no usable isotope patterns, so isotope-pattern ranking cannot discriminate candidate decompositions The goal is already-determined formulas to be searched as structures in molecular databases, not formula ranking from spectra You need compound structure identification (CSI:FingerID/CANOPUS/MSNovelist) without first establishing the molecular formula

skills.description: Use when quantifying targeted metabolites or isotope-tracer-labelled isotopologues in LC-MS data and a theoretical isotope envelope (e.g. up to six 13C labels) is needed to match and score detected peaks.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-calculation
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-calculation Use when quantifying targeted metabolites or isotope-tracer-labelled isotopologues in LC-MS data and a theoretical isotope envelope (e.g. up to six 13C labels) is needed to match and score detected peaks. The input is already a verified feature/peak table and no isotope-envelope matching is required. Data are untargeted or MS/MS-based rather than targeted LC-MS quantification (TarMet's README lists MS/MS library verification and data-independent acquisition as future, not current, features). No molecular formulas for the targets are available, since enviPat cannot compute patterns without them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Calculate theoretical isotope patterns of target metabolites (or their 13C-labelled isotopologues) from molecular formulas using the enviPat package, at the resolution of the MS instrument, as the reference against which measured peaks are scored for isotopic similarity in TarMet. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Calculate theoretical isotope patterns of target metabolites (or their 13C-labelled isotopologues) from molecular formulas using the enviPat package, at the resolution of the MS instrument, as the reference against which measured peaks are scored for isotopic similarity in TarMet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a verified feature/peak table and no isotope-envelope matching is required. Data are untargeted or MS/MS-based rather than targeted LC-MS quantification (TarMet's README lists MS/MS library verification and data-independent acquisition as future, not current, features). No molecular formulas for the targets are available, since enviPat cannot compute patterns without them.

skills.description: Use when annotating LC/MS peak lists (e.g. xsAnnotate objects from faahKO/MM39 processing) and you must identify isotope clusters and charge states within each pseudospectrum rather than treating isotope peaks as separate compounds.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-detection-in-compound-spectra
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-detection-in-compound-spectra Use when annotating LC/MS peak lists (e.g. xsAnnotate objects from faahKO/MM39 processing) and you must identify isotope clusters and charge states within each pseudospectrum rather than treating isotope peaks as separate compounds. Input features have not been grouped into compound spectra (pseudospectra) yet — isotope detection within CAMERA operates per pseudospectrum, not on an ungrouped peak table. The goal is adduct or fragment annotation rather than isotope/charge assignment — CAMERA handles those via the dynamic rule table separately. Only the molecular ion and fragment ions are present with no isotopic siblings — as the article notes, such spectra cannot always be annotated directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Detects isotopic peaks within CAMERA compound spectra (pseudospectra) by computing a pairwise m/z distance matrix and flagging pairs whose m/z difference is close to 1.0033/z within ppm and mzabs tolerances plus an intensity-ratio check, enabling deduction of charge states. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Detects isotopic peaks within CAMERA compound spectra (pseudospectra) by computing a pairwise m/z distance matrix and flagging pairs whose m/z difference is close to 1.0033/z within ppm and mzabs tolerances plus an intensity-ratio check, enabling deduction of charge states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features have not been grouped into compound spectra (pseudospectra) yet — isotope detection within CAMERA operates per pseudospectrum, not on an ungrouped peak table. The goal is adduct or fragment annotation rather than isotope/charge assignment — CAMERA handles those via the dynamic rule table separately. Only the molecular ion and fragment ions are present with no isotopic siblings — as the article notes, such spectra cannot always be annotated directly.

skills.description: Use when comparing synthetic or real LC-MS/MS runs of known molecules (e.g. nucleosides Cm, m3C, m5C) to assess how mass-accuracy errors (ppm offsets) affect isotope-pattern match scores and quantification quality.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-match-scoring
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-match-scoring Use when comparing synthetic or real LC-MS/MS runs of known molecules (e.g. nucleosides Cm, m3C, m5C) to assess how mass-accuracy errors (ppm offsets) affect isotope-pattern match scores and quantification quality. The input run was not produced by a formula-based simulator like SMITER and there is no known ground truth (chemical formulas) to compute theoretical isotope patterns against. The goal is fragment-ion (MS2) identity rather than precursor isotope-pattern matching — SMITER's peptide/nucleoside fragmentation models address that separately. Only a single run with no error-free (0 ppm) counterpart exists, so the effect of the ppm offset on quantification quality cannot be assessed comparatively. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Score simulated LC-MS/MS runs (e.g. SMITER-generated mzML files) by matching observed isotope patterns against theoretical patterns to quantify how measurement error — such as a ppm mass offset — degrades quantification quality, as in Figure 5A/B of the SMITER paper. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/genes12030396
skills.summary: Score simulated LC-MS/MS runs (e.g. SMITER-generated mzML files) by matching observed isotope patterns against theoretical patterns to quantify how measurement error — such as a ppm mass offset — degrades quantification quality, as in Figure 5A/B of the SMITER paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input run was not produced by a formula-based simulator like SMITER and there is no known ground truth (chemical formulas) to compute theoretical isotope patterns against. The goal is fragment-ion (MS2) identity rather than precursor isotope-pattern matching — SMITER's peptide/nucleoside fragmentation models address that separately. Only a single run with no error-free (0 ppm) counterpart exists, so the effect of the ppm offset on quantification quality cannot be assessed comparatively.

skills.description: Use when defining target metabolites for MS-based targeted metabolic or stable-isotope tracer analysis and you need theoretical isotope patterns and per-isotopologue m/z ranges from a formula/adduct/resolution.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-prediction-from-molecular-formula
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-prediction-from-molecular-formula Use when defining target metabolites for MS-based targeted metabolic or stable-isotope tracer analysis and you need theoretical isotope patterns and per-isotopologue m/z ranges from a formula/adduct/resolution. skills.description: Use when you have high-resolution MS1 isotope peak lists (masses and abundances) and need to rank candidate molecular formulas by how well their theoretical isotope patterns explain the observed intensities.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-scoring
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-scoring Use when you have high-resolution MS1 isotope peak lists (masses and abundances) and need to rank candidate molecular formulas by how well their theoretical isotope patterns explain the observed intensities. The input is tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra rather than MS1 isotope peak intensities — for that, fragmentation tree computation is the relevant SIRIUS workflow step, not isotope pattern scoring. The goal is structure or database search (CSI:FingerID, CANOPUS, MSNovelist) rather than ranking elemental compositions of the parent ion. Spectra are low-resolution or lack resolvable isotope peaks, so no reliable isotope peak intensities can be extracted after preprocessing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces SIRIUS 4's maximum-likelihood isotope pattern intensity scoring model, which scores candidate molecular formulas against measured high-resolution MS1 isotope peak intensities using a combined relative+absolute Gaussian noise model with defaults sigma_abs = 0.01 and sigma_rel = 0.08. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8
skills.summary: Reproduces SIRIUS 4's maximum-likelihood isotope pattern intensity scoring model, which scores candidate molecular formulas against measured high-resolution MS1 isotope peak intensities using a combined relative+absolute Gaussian noise model with defaults sigma_abs = 0.01 and sigma_rel = 0.08.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra rather than MS1 isotope peak intensities — for that, fragmentation tree computation is the relevant SIRIUS workflow step, not isotope pattern scoring. Spectra are low-resolution or lack resolvable isotope peaks, so no reliable isotope peak intensities can be extracted after preprocessing.

skills.description: Use when a molecular formula annotation (e.g. from SIRIUS/ZODIAC) needs validation from high-resolution MS1 isotope peaks, or when a diagnostic elemental signature such as ~50:50 79Br/81Br must be checked.
skills.name: isotope-pattern-simulation
skills.search_text: isotope-pattern-simulation Use when a molecular formula annotation (e.g. from SIRIUS/ZODIAC) needs validation from high-resolution MS1 isotope peaks, or when a diagnostic elemental signature such as ~50:50 79Br/81Br must be checked. Input is already an MS/MS (tandem) spectrum and the goal is fragmentation-tree or structure annotation rather than MS1 isotope validation — use SIRIUS fragmentation tree / ZODIAC reranking instead. The compound's adduct cannot be reliably deduced from isotope pattern and MS/MS data and no high-quality adduct annotation is available from preprocessing — the paper explicitly warns that adduct information 'is challenging to deduce from isotope pattern and MS/MS data'. The measured mass spectrometer is low-resolution, so isotope peaks cannot be separated and matched within high-resolution mass accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Simulate the theoretical isotope pattern of a candidate molecular formula (e.g. [C24H47BrNO8P + H]+) with SIRIUS and compare it, peak-by-peak, against the observed MS1 spectrum to support or refute formula annotations. This is the diagnostic used in the ZODIAC paper to validate novel formula assignments such as the brominated diatom metabolite at m/z 588.230. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Simulate the theoretical isotope pattern of a candidate molecular formula (e.g. [C24H47BrNO8P + H]+) with SIRIUS and compare it, peak-by-peak, against the observed MS1 spectrum to support or refute formula annotations. skills.description: Use when an LC/MS peak list needs grouping of same-analyte features and ion-species annotation (isotopes/adducts) to yield quasi-molecular ions for compound identification.

skills.search_text: isotope-peak-annotation-lcms Use when an LC/MS peak list needs grouping of same-analyte features and ion-species annotation (isotopes/adducts) to yield quasi-molecular ions for compound identification. Only a single feature (not a grouped pseudo-spectrum) is available and no isotope/adduct context exists, so mass proposal would be unreliable. The goal is purely statistical differential analysis on the original feature list without reducing feature-list redundancy; grouping and annotation are unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate isotope and adduct peaks within co-eluting compound spectra using CAMERA's findIsotopes/groupFWHM/groupCorr/findAdducts workflow, then propose accurate compound masses. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g

skills.description: Use when pre-processing imzML mass spectrometry imaging data and you need to remove 13C isotope peaks (M+1, M+2) from a feature table before lipid annotation or downstream statistics.
skills.name: isotope-peak-deisotoping
skills.search_text: isotope-peak-deisotoping Use when pre-processing imzML mass spectrometry imaging data and you need to remove 13C isotope peaks (M+1, M+2) from a feature table before lipid annotation or downstream statistics. Input is already a deisotoped or centroided feature table with isotopes removed Data are low-resolution spectra where 3 ppm 13C isotope assignment tolerance cannot be reliably applied The analysis is being re-run with different PCA/clustering/slicing settings only (use process = F, which skips pre-processing including deisotoping) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 massPix's deisotoping step identifies molecular ions (M) and removes M+1 and M+2 13C isotope peaks whose intensities fall within calculated proportions of the monoisotope intensity, using average feature intensities computed from a random subset of pixels. It is part of massPix's initial pre-processing of imzML mass spectrometry imaging data prior to lipid annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1252-5
skills.summary: massPix's deisotoping step identifies molecular ions (M) and removes M+1 and M+2 13C isotope peaks whose intensities fall within calculated proportions of the monoisotope intensity, using average feature intensities computed from a random subset of pixels. skills.description: Use when generating pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML) or imaging data (imzML) with ms1-id, before writing correlated ion clusters to pseudo_msms.mgf, to strip isotope peaks.
skills.name: isotope-peak-exclusion
skills.search_text: isotope-peak-exclusion Use when generating pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML) or imaging data (imzML) with ms1-id, before writing correlated ion clusters to pseudo_msms.mgf, to strip isotope peaks. When peaks already derive from true tandem MS/MS scans rather than MS1-only data — isotope exclusion is specific to pseudo MS/MS generation from full-scan in-source fragments. When constructing molecular networking edges after modified cosine scoring — for that step, larger ions above the feature m/z are instead removed, which is a different cleaning rule. When the input is an already-generated pseudo_msms.mgf without MassCube isotope flags; the exclusion depends on MassCube feature-detection metadata. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Excludes peaks that the MassCube feature-detection backend has flagged as isotope peaks from pseudo MS/MS spectra generated by ms1-id, so that in-source fragment clusters represent true co-eluting structural fragments rather than isotope envelopes of the precursor ion. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Excludes peaks that the MassCube feature-detection backend has flagged as isotope peaks from pseudo MS/MS spectra generated by ms1-id, so that in-source fragment clusters represent true co-eluting structural fragments rather than isotope envelopes of the precursor ion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When peaks already derive from true tandem MS/MS scans rather than MS1-only data — isotope exclusion is specific to pseudo MS/MS generation from full-scan in-source fragments. When constructing molecular networking edges after modified cosine scoring — for that step, larger ions above the feature m/z are instead removed, which is a different cleaning rule. When the input is an already-generated pseudo_msms.mgf without MassCube isotope flags; the exclusion depends on MassCube feature-detection metadata.

skills.description: Use when importing centroided MS2 spectra (txt, msp, or mgf exported from MS-DIAL, or mgf from MZmine) into a DIATAGeR DIADataObj and before LipidIdentifier/ScoreLipids TG annotation, to strip isotopes and noise peaks from multiplexed DIA spectra.
skills.name: isotope-peak-filtering
skills.search_text: isotope-peak-filtering Use when importing centroided MS2 spectra (txt, msp, or mgf exported from MS-DIAL, or mgf from MZmine) into a DIATAGeR DIADataObj and before LipidIdentifier/ScoreLipids TG annotation, to strip isotopes and noise peaks from multiplexed DIA spectra. The input is raw uncentroided profile MS2 spectra or a feature table that has not yet had spectra attached via SpectraImport — DIATAGeR expects a DIADataObj with centroid spectra. The goal is lipid-class identification other than triacylglycerols — DIATAGeR is explicitly for TGs only (lipid='TAG'). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Deisotope and denoise multiplexed DIA-MS2 spectra prior to triacylglycerol annotation using DIATAGeR's RemoveIsotopes function, which removes isotope peaks and low-intensity/density-outlier peaks so downstream TG identification against target and decoy databases operates on clean fragment spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344698
skills.summary: Deisotope and denoise multiplexed DIA-MS2 spectra prior to triacylglycerol annotation using DIATAGeR's RemoveIsotopes function, which removes isotope peaks and low-intensity/density-outlier peaks so downstream TG identification against target and decoy databases operates on clean fragment spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw uncentroided profile MS2 spectra or a feature table that has not yet had spectra attached via SpectraImport — DIATAGeR expects a DIADataObj with centroid spectra. The goal is lipid-class identification other than triacylglycerols — DIATAGeR is explicitly for TGs only (lipid='TAG').

skills.name: isotope-ratio-quantification
skills.search_text: isotope-ratio-quantification Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table (X/Y pixel coordinates plus m/z ion columns, e.g. AFADESI mouse brain data) needs an isotopic peak ratio quality metric, or when candidate M+1 isotopic pairs must be validated by spatial intensity correlation. skills.name: isotope-tracer-extraction
skills.search_text: isotope-tracer-extraction Use when you need to quantify target metabolites and their isotopologues from MS-based stable isotope tracer experiments, especially to compare observed vs. theoretical isotope patterns. When the analysis goal is untargeted feature detection rather than a predefined target metabolite/isotopologue panel — TarMet is explicitly a targeted tool.
