skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (e.g. from asari 1.9.2) and need to group degenerate ions (isotopologues/adducts) into empirical compounds with inferred neutral masses, especially for 13C isotope tracing experiments.
skills.name: isotope-tracing-data-annotation
skills.search_text: isotope-tracing-data-annotation Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (e.g. from asari 1.9.2) and need to group degenerate ions (isotopologues/adducts) into empirical compounds with inferred neutral masses, especially for 13C isotope tracing experiments. When you already have an annotated list of empirical compounds with known formulas — khipu is a preannotation step for unlabeled feature tables, not a formula-refinement tool. When the goal is full annotation including tandem MS library matching, contaminants, or authentic-standard confirmation — the article notes complete annotation requires additional resources beyond khipu preannotation. When features are not m/z-resolved peak measurements (e.g. raw vendor files or spectra not yet peak-picked) — khipu requires a preprocessed feature table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotates LC-MS features into empirical compounds (khipu trees) by building mass-distance networks over isotope and adduct patterns (e.g. 1.0034 Da 13C/12C, 22.9893 Da Na+), then converting subnetworks into 2-tier adduct-trunk/isotope-branch trees to infer neutral masses — applicable to both untargeted metabolomics and stable isotope tracing. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Annotates LC-MS features into empirical compounds (khipu trees) by building mass-distance networks over isotope and adduct patterns (e.g. 1.0034 Da 13C/12C, 22.9893 Da Na+), then converting subnetworks into 2-tier adduct-trunk/isotope-branch trees to infer neutral masses — applicable to both untargeted metabolomics and stable isotope tracing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you already have an annotated list of empirical compounds with known formulas — khipu is a preannotation step for unlabeled feature tables, not a formula-refinement tool. When the goal is full annotation including tandem MS library matching, contaminants, or authentic-standard confirmation — the article notes complete annotation requires additional resources beyond khipu preannotation. When features are not m/z-resolved peak measurements (e.g. raw vendor files or spectra not yet peak-picked) — khipu requires a preprocessed feature table.

skills.description: Use when you have normalized, natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions of fatty acids from 13C6-glucose tracer experiments and need to decide whether apparent label reflects de novo synthesis from glucose-derived acetyl-CoA or uptake of pre-existing fatty acids.
skills.name: isotope-tracing-uptake-vs-synthesis-interpretation
skills.search_text: isotope-tracing-uptake-vs-synthesis-interpretation Use when you have normalized, natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions of fatty acids from 13C6-glucose tracer experiments and need to decide whether apparent label reflects de novo synthesis from glucose-derived acetyl-CoA or uptake of pre-existing fatty acids. When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiment) — the binomial distribution cannot be reliably fit to estimate uptake fraction, so fall back to M+0/mean labelling comparison instead of quantitative uptake estimates. When absolute contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool is required — the method provides only relative substrate contribution because the pool size cannot be quantified. When precise de novo synthesis vs uptake proportions are needed per fatty acid in vivo without prior determination of time to isotopic steady state — different fatty acid pools may reach steady state at different times and labelling must be interpreted alongside pool size data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Interprets 13C6-glucose labelling of esterified fatty acids (isotopologue distributions from 13C-SpaceM or bulk MSI/LC-MS) to separate de novo synthesis from uptake, using binomial fitting for parameters and mean-fraction-labelling for qualitative discrimination between conditions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Interprets 13C6-glucose labelling of esterified fatty acids (isotopologue distributions from 13C-SpaceM or bulk MSI/LC-MS) to separate de novo synthesis from uptake, using binomial fitting for parameters and mean-fraction-labelling for qualitative discrimination between conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiment) — the binomial distribution cannot be reliably fit to estimate uptake fraction, so fall back to M+0/mean labelling comparison instead of quantitative uptake estimates. When absolute contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool is required — the method provides only relative substrate contribution because the pool size cannot be quantified. When precise de novo synthesis vs uptake proportions are needed per fatty acid in vivo without prior determination of time to isotopic steady state — different fatty acid pools may reach steady state at different times and labelling must be interpreted alongside pool size data.

skills.description: Use when converting a predicted probability distribution over molecular fragments (subformulae or atom subsets with known exact atomic-composition masses) into a discrete mass spectrum at a chosen integer-Dalton or sub-Dalton resolution.
skills.name: isotopic-abundance-spectrum-computation
skills.search_text: isotopic-abundance-spectrum-computation Use when converting a predicted probability distribution over molecular fragments (subformulae or atom subsets with known exact atomic-composition masses) into a discrete mass spectrum at a chosen integer-Dalton or sub-Dalton resolution. Input is already a measured spectrum (e.g. a NIST 2017 Main Library entry); this skill constructs a predicted spectrum from fragment probabilities, not observed data. The molecule contains atoms outside HCONFSPCl or exceeds the enumeration limits (≤48 atoms for FormulaNet, ≤4096 unique fragment formulae), so the fragment distribution was never produced. You need fragmentation pathways or bond-cleavage mechanisms rather than an isotope-resolved observation model — RASSP ignores exotic fragmentation schemes and bond information beyond atoms. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes the exact observed mass spectrum of a molecular fragment formula or atom subset by convolving natural-abundance isotope distributions with per-element mass defects, then bins the result to a target resolution (1 Da or 0.1 Da) and weights it by the model's fragment probability before summing into the final predicted EI–MS spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Computes the exact observed mass spectrum of a molecular fragment formula or atom subset by convolving natural-abundance isotope distributions with per-element mass defects, then bins the result to a target resolution (1 Da or 0.1 Da) and weights it by the model's fragment probability before summing into the final predicted EI–MS spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a measured spectrum (e.g. a NIST 2017 Main Library entry); this skill constructs a predicted spectrum from fragment probabilities, not observed data. The molecule contains atoms outside HCONFSPCl or exceeds the enumeration limits (≤48 atoms for FormulaNet, ≤4096 unique fragment formulae), so the fragment distribution was never produced. You need fragmentation pathways or bond-cleavage mechanisms rather than an isotope-resolved observation model — RASSP ignores exotic fragmentation schemes and bond information beyond atoms.

skills.description: Use when a GC/EI-MS analyte spectrum matches no reference library and a large enumerated derivative database (e.g., ~422M cathinone-like compounds with precomputed exact masses) must be narrowed to candidates near the analyte's molecular ion M+ mass.
skills.name: isotopic-artifact-aware-tolerance-handling
skills.search_text: isotopic-artifact-aware-tolerance-handling Use when a GC/EI-MS analyte spectrum matches no reference library and a large enumerated derivative database (e.g., ~422M cathinone-like compounds with precomputed exact masses) must be narrowed to candidates near the analyte's molecular ion M+ mass. The analyte spectrum already matches an established reference library (NIST, Wiley, SWGDRUG) — PS2MS is only invoked when no reference match is found in the conventional screening procedure The analyte's molecular ion (M+ peak) cannot be reliably assigned, since it is the sole reference mass for the tolerance window Candidates of interest differ from the analyte by more than the ±5 Da window (e.g., large multi-substituent derivatives), as they would be filtered out before spectrum/fingerprint ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A rule-based mass-weight filtering step from PS2MS that uses the analyte's M+ peak (derived from its SWGDRUG reference spectrum) as a reference mass and retains enumerated synthetic NPS derivatives only when their exact masses fall within tolerance windows (mwf ±1 or ±5 Da) of that reference. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: A rule-based mass-weight filtering step from PS2MS that uses the analyte's M+ peak (derived from its SWGDRUG reference spectrum) as a reference mass and retains enumerated synthetic NPS derivatives only when their exact masses fall within tolerance windows (mwf ±1 or ±5 Da) of that reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte spectrum already matches an established reference library (NIST, Wiley, SWGDRUG) — PS2MS is only invoked when no reference match is found in the conventional screening procedure The analyte's molecular ion (M+ peak) cannot be reliably assigned, since it is the sole reference mass for the tolerance window Candidates of interest differ from the analyte by more than the ±5 Da window (e.g., large multi-substituent derivatives), as they would be filtered out before spectrum/fingerprint ranking

skills.description: Use when you have XCMS peak-picked feature data from paired unlabeled/labeled samples (e.g. 12C vs 13C glucose) in an xcmsSet object and need to flag which features show isotopic enrichment.
skills.name: isotopic-distribution-comparison-between-sample-conditions
skills.search_text: isotopic-distribution-comparison-between-sample-conditions Use when you have XCMS peak-picked feature data from paired unlabeled/labeled samples (e.g. 12C vs 13C glucose) in an xcmsSet object and need to flag which features show isotopic enrichment. skills.summary: Identifies isotopic peak pairs (e.g., M+1 offsets of ~1.0035 Da) among ions in a spatial metabolomics peak table, as implemented in SMQVP's Isotopic Peak Ratio module via the MetaboCoreUtils isotopologues approach, to evaluate the reliability of ion detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw MS imaging data (e.g., IMZML/mzML) rather than a preprocessed peak table matrix with pixel coordinates and m/z columns Noisy ions and background pixels have not yet been removed, since spurious correlations and mass offsets will inflate the isotopic pair count The goal is adduct ion identification rather than isotopologue detection — SMQVP provides a separate Adduct Ion Ratio module for adduct pairs

skills.search_text: isotopic-profile-theoretical-vs-experimental-matching Use when annotating untargeted LC/HRMS peaks (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) with molecular formulas from only MS1-level data, especially when database-dependent tools (MetDNA, SIRIUS, ZODIAC) risk missing exposome compounds absent from biochemical databases. This enables high-confidence MS1-only formula annotation for metabolomics and exposomics studies without requiring MS2 data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00563

skills.name: isotopic-signature-detection
skills.search_text: isotopic-signature-detection Use when the input is a DEIMoS-aligned multi-sample feature table (e.g. example_alignment.h5) in an N-dimensional space (m/z, drift time, retention time) and the goal is to glean ion charge state or identification evidence from isotopic signatures. Input is raw instrument data rather than a processed, aligned feature table — isotope detection in DEIMoS operates on features, not raw spectra, and the article's demonstration loads from example_alignment.h5, not raw files The analysis requires peak detection, alignment, or CCS calibration first — those are separate DEIMoS steps that must precede isotope detection The data are MS2 spectra needing deconvolution — MS/MS spectral deconvolution is a distinct DEIMoS functionality, not isotope detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Detect and annotate isotopologue groups in aligned multi-sample feature tables using DEIMoS's N-dimensional isotope detection, inferring ion charge state from isotopologue spacing and downselecting signatures by m/z error and member count. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Detect and annotate isotopologue groups in aligned multi-sample feature tables using DEIMoS's N-dimensional isotope detection, inferring ion charge state from isotopologue spacing and downselecting signatures by m/z error and member count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw instrument data rather than a processed, aligned feature table — isotope detection in DEIMoS operates on features, not raw spectra, and the article's demonstration loads from example_alignment.h5, not raw files The analysis requires peak detection, alignment, or CCS calibration first — those are separate DEIMoS steps that must precede isotope detection The data are MS2 spectra needing deconvolution — MS/MS spectral deconvolution is a distinct DEIMoS functionality, not isotope detection

skills.description: Use when a pseudo-2D (e.g. 1H-13C HSQC) isotope-labeling NMR series must be decomposed into individual isotopic species and their relative abundances quantified, especially with overlapping peaks.
skills.name: isotopic-species-quantification-from-hsqc
skills.search_text: isotopic-species-quantification-from-hsqc Use when a pseudo-2D (e.g. 1H-13C HSQC) isotope-labeling NMR series must be decomposed into individual isotopic species and their relative abundances quantified, especially with overlapping peaks. Input is a set of individual 1D spectra unrelated to isotope-labeling quantification of isotopic species from an HSQC series The sample lacks a known or predictable labeling pattern against which quantification can be validated A fully automated (non-semi-automated) peak-picking analysis with no user-defined signal multiplicity is required Quantify isotopic species of metabolites (e.g. aspartate) from 1H-13C HSQC pseudo-2D spectra by fitting every peak of each multiplet with MultiNMRFit, a Python 3 open-source tool that estimates intensity, area, chemical shift, and coupling constants with standard-deviation uncertainties. Validated by agreement with predicted 13C-labeling patterns within 1%. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Quantify isotopic species of metabolites (e.g. aspartate) from 1H-13C HSQC pseudo-2D spectra by fitting every peak of each multiplet with MultiNMRFit, a Python 3 open-source tool that estimates intensity, area, chemical shift, and coupling constants with standard-deviation uncertainties. Validated by agreement with predicted 13C-labeling patterns within 1%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a set of individual 1D spectra unrelated to isotope-labeling quantification of isotopic species from an HSQC series The sample lacks a known or predictable labeling pattern against which quantification can be validated A fully automated (non-semi-automated) peak-picking analysis with no user-defined signal multiplicity is required

skills.search_text: isotopic-subnetwork-partitioning Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (e.g. asari 1.9.2 TSV with feature ID, m/z, rtime, intensities) and need to group adduct/isotope-related features into empirical compounds with inferred neutral M0 masses, without prior formulas. Input is raw LC-MS data or centroided spectra rather than a preprocessed feature table — run a preprocessing tool such as asari 1.9.2 first The task requires complete metabolite identification: khipu provides preannotation only, and complete annotation still requires contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS data The experiment uses isotope/adduct patterns absent from the default khipu grid without supplying custom search patterns (e.g. specialized tracing designs) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Partitions a mass distance network of LC-MS feature pairs into per-adduct isotopic subnetworks and converts each into a rooted tree (khipu) to organize degenerate ions around a compound and infer its neutral mass via linear regression on the khipu grid. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Partitions a mass distance network of LC-MS feature pairs into per-adduct isotopic subnetworks and converts each into a rooted tree (khipu) to organize degenerate ions around a compound and infer its neutral mass via linear regression on the khipu grid.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data or centroided spectra rather than a preprocessed feature table — run a preprocessing tool such as asari 1.9.2 first The task requires complete metabolite identification: khipu provides preannotation only, and complete annotation still requires contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS data The experiment uses isotope/adduct patterns absent from the default khipu grid without supplying custom search patterns (e.g. specialized tracing designs)

skills.search_text: isotopic-trace-peak-shape-filtering Use when filtering raw FeatureFinderMetabo output from centroided ddMS2 mzML data to remove spurious or poorly shaped features before blank correction and PFAS prioritization. Input is already a curated/custom feature list (external_feature_list.xlsx) — PFΔScreen's FeatureFinding and this shape filter are bypassed in that path Data are profile-mode or non-centroided spectra; the README specifies centroided ddMS2 mzML input Analytes lack the isotopic structure required for trace modeling (e.g., very low intensity peaks yielding fewer than two isotopic traces) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Post-feature-detection quality filter in PFΔScreen's FeatureFinding tab that retains only features with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) above 1 s and below 1 min and at least two isotopic traces, excluding features with unusual isotopic peak shapes using the OpenMS metabolites (5% RMS) isotope model. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-05070-2
skills.summary: Post-feature-detection quality filter in PFΔScreen's FeatureFinding tab that retains only features with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) above 1 s and below 1 min and at least two isotopic traces, excluding features with unusual isotopic peak shapes using the OpenMS metabolites (5% RMS) isotope model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated/custom feature list (external_feature_list.xlsx) — PFΔScreen's FeatureFinding and this shape filter are bypassed in that path Data are profile-mode or non-centroided spectra; the README specifies centroided ddMS2 mzML input Analytes lack the isotopic structure required for trace modeling (e.g., very low intensity peaks yielding fewer than two isotopic traces)

skills.search_text: isotopically-labeled-lipid-library-qc Use when a workflow imports U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv from the FelinaHildebrand/MobiLipid repository and must confirm the 377-value, 162-lipid-species, 15-class curation is intact before internal standardization. skills.description: Use when time-course stable-isotope labeling data (e.g., [13C5,15N2] glutamate 0-8 h sampling) have been processed into natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions and fluxes with confidence intervals are needed.
skills.name: isotopically-nonstationary-metabolic-flux-analysis
skills.search_text: isotopically-nonstationary-metabolic-flux-analysis Use when time-course stable-isotope labeling data (e.g., [13C5,15N2] glutamate 0-8 h sampling) have been processed into natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions and fluxes with confidence intervals are needed. Only steady-state (stationary) labeling endpoint data are available with no time-course sampling — classic 13C MFA, not INST-MFA, applies Data come from nominal-resolution mass spectrometry where dual-labeled isotopologues produce nominally identical mass shifts and cannot be resolved — a dual-isotope model is not identifiable Isotopologue distributions have not been post-processed (generated and natural abundance corrected) by SIMPEL from the HRMS dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST-MFA) fits simulated isotopologue labeling trajectories to time-course HRMS data to estimate reaction fluxes with 95% confidence intervals, performed here with the MATLAB-based INCA tool on data tables exported from SIMPEL. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42003-024-05844-z
skills.summary: Isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST-MFA) fits simulated isotopologue labeling trajectories to time-course HRMS data to estimate reaction fluxes with 95% confidence intervals, performed here with the MATLAB-based INCA tool on data tables exported from SIMPEL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only steady-state (stationary) labeling endpoint data are available with no time-course sampling — classic 13C MFA, not INST-MFA, applies Data come from nominal-resolution mass spectrometry where dual-labeled isotopologues produce nominally identical mass shifts and cannot be resolved — a dual-isotope model is not identifiable Isotopologue distributions have not been post-processed (generated and natural abundance corrected) by SIMPEL from the HRMS dataset

skills.description: Use when grouping co-eluting MS1 peaks into CSA clusters from IDSL.IPA peaklists/peak_alignment directories and you must decide whether an m/z-shifted neighbor is a genuine 12C/13C isotopologue of the seed peak.
skills.name: isotopologue-12c-13c-peak-handling
skills.search_text: isotopologue-12c-13c-peak-handling Use when grouping co-eluting MS1 peaks into CSA clusters from IDSL.IPA peaklists/peak_alignment directories and you must decide whether an m/z-shifted neighbor is a genuine 12C/13C isotopologue of the seed peak. The goal is peak detection or EIC extraction itself — use IDSL.IPA (this step assumes peaklists and peak_alignment already exist). The data are MS2-based (DDA/DIA) fragmentation spectra; IDSL.CSA supports those modes, but 12C/13C isotopologue grouping is specific to MS1-only CSA cluster aggregation. m/z spacing does not correspond to a plausible isotopologue of the seed (e.g. adduct or in-source fragment spacing); these should be handled through CSA adduct-annotation logic rather than isotopologue handling. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Within IDSL.CSA composite-spectra aggregation, correlating MS1 neighbor peaks are classified and retained as expected 12C/13C isotopologue pairs based on their m/z spacing relative to the seed peak, rather than being discarded as unexplained co-eluting ions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00376
skills.summary: Within IDSL.CSA composite-spectra aggregation, correlating MS1 neighbor peaks are classified and retained as expected 12C/13C isotopologue pairs based on their m/z spacing relative to the seed peak, rather than being discarded as unexplained co-eluting ions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peak detection or EIC extraction itself — use IDSL.IPA (this step assumes peaklists and peak_alignment already exist). The data are MS2-based (DDA/DIA) fragmentation spectra; IDSL.CSA supports those modes, but 12C/13C isotopologue grouping is specific to MS1-only CSA cluster aggregation. m/z spacing does not correspond to a plausible isotopologue of the seed (e.g. adduct or in-source fragment spacing); these should be handled through CSA adduct-annotation logic rather than isotopologue handling.

skills.description: Use when tracer quantification output (e.g. from TarMet's isotope tracer assay on 13C6-glucose samples) provides raw isotopologue peak areas (M+1, M+2, ...) and you need per-metabolite fractional labeling to check pathway-position labeling patterns.

skills.search_text: isotopologue-abundance-normalization Use when tracer quantification output (e.g. from TarMet's isotope tracer assay on 13C6-glucose samples) provides raw isotopologue peak areas (M+1, M+2, ...) and you need per-metabolite fractional labeling to check pathway-position labeling patterns. Input is raw EIC chromatograms or unquantified peaks rather than already-quantified isotopologue areas from TarMet's isotopologue analysis step The goal is absolute targeted metabolite quantification (TarMet's 'Quantitative analysis' workflow) rather than relative labeling within an isotopologue envelope The tracer experiment does not include parallel samples or a defined expected labeling pattern, so the fractional values cannot be cross-validated http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Normalizes per-metabolite 13C isotopologue peak areas from a stable isotope tracer experiment into fractional abundances (relative labeling per isotopologue), so labeling patterns across a metabolic pathway can be compared between parallel samples and validated against expected metabolism rules. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Normalizes per-metabolite 13C isotopologue peak areas from a stable isotope tracer experiment into fractional abundances (relative labeling per isotopologue), so labeling patterns across a metabolic pathway can be compared between parallel samples and validated against expected metabolism rules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw EIC chromatograms or unquantified peaks rather than already-quantified isotopologue areas from TarMet's isotopologue analysis step The goal is absolute targeted metabolite quantification (TarMet's 'Quantitative analysis' workflow) rather than relative labeling within an isotopologue envelope The tracer experiment does not include parallel samples or a defined expected labeling pattern, so the fractional values cannot be cross-validated

skills.description: Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS metabolomics chromatograms and you need to assign isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments across features, especially when focusing on a statistically significant subset rather than the full dataset.

skills.search_text: isotopologue-adduct-annotation Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS metabolomics chromatograms and you need to assign isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments across features, especially when focusing on a statistically significant subset rather than the full dataset. Input is DIA data other than AIF (e.g., SWATH) — MetaboAnnotatoR currently supports only AIF. Data were acquired on high-resolution instruments without centroid conversion — raw profile-mode chromatograms are not supported directly. You need full-dataset untargeted annotation with no statistical pre-selection — MetaboAnnotatoR is designed for a subset of features, not exhaustive annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Annotates isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments in untargeted all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS datasets using MetaboAnnotatoR, a correlation-based parent–fragment linking approach combined with molecular fragment matching. Enables automated, rank-scored annotation of AIF features to replace manual MS spectral inspection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Annotates isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments in untargeted all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS datasets using MetaboAnnotatoR, a correlation-based parent–fragment linking approach combined with molecular fragment matching. Enables automated, rank-scored annotation of AIF features to replace manual MS spectral inspection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is DIA data other than AIF (e.g., SWATH) — MetaboAnnotatoR currently supports only AIF. Data were acquired on high-resolution instruments without centroid conversion — raw profile-mode chromatograms are not supported directly. You need full-dataset untargeted annotation with no statistical pre-selection — MetaboAnnotatoR is designed for a subset of features, not exhaustive annotation.

skills.search_text: isotopologue-distribution-normalization Use when single-cell isotope-tracing data (SpaceM spatiomolecular anndata objects, per-cell ion intensities for fatty acids like palmitate C16:0 and oleate C18:1) must be converted to corrected, normalized isotopologue fractions before binomial-fitting uptake estimates. When the input isotopologue table has already been natural-isotope-corrected and normalized to fractional abundances (e.g. fit_binomial_prediction.csv or IsoCorrector output) — re-normalization risks double-correcting natural-abundance contributions When the goal is absolute rather than relative substrate contribution — this normalization only supports relative quantification, since the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool size cannot be quantified When processing raw imzML for METASPACE-style natural-abundance-only annotations — METASPACE isotopologue distributions assume natural isotope abundance and are not intended for labeled samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts raw per-cell (or per-ablation-mark / per-pixel) fatty-acid isotopologue ion intensities from 13C-SpaceM MALDI-AIF data into fractional isotopologue distributions by first correcting for natural isotope abundance and then normalizing each fatty acid's M+0...M+16 peaks per cell, so that uptake/synthesis fractions can be fitted downstream. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Converts raw per-cell (or per-ablation-mark / per-pixel) fatty-acid isotopologue ion intensities from 13C-SpaceM MALDI-AIF data into fractional isotopologue distributions by first correcting for natural isotope abundance and then normalizing each fatty acid's M+0...M+16 peaks per cell, so that uptake/synthesis fractions can be fitted downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input isotopologue table has already been natural-isotope-corrected and normalized to fractional abundances (e.g. fit_binomial_prediction.csv or IsoCorrector output) — re-normalization risks double-correcting natural-abundance contributions When the goal is absolute rather than relative substrate contribution — this normalization only supports relative quantification, since the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool size cannot be quantified When processing raw imzML for METASPACE-style natural-abundance-only annotations — METASPACE isotopologue distributions assume natural isotope abundance and are not intended for labeled samples

skills.name: isotopologue-distribution-simulation
skills.search_text: isotopologue-distribution-simulation Use when you have a list of molecular formulae and need their monoisotopic masses plus theoretical isotopologue patterns (including adducts and multiply charged species) to target ions in LC-IM-MS or MS data. You already have experimental MS/MS spectra or measured CCS values — this skill only simulates theoretical masses and isotope patterns, not experimental IM-MS measurements Your input is profile LC-IM-MS mzML data without known formulae — CCSfind requires a list of molecular formulae as a compulsory input before targets can be computed You need CCS calibration (Tfix, Beta) or drift gas identity handling — those are separate CCSfind calibration steps, not isotopologue simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute theoretical monoisotopic masses and isotope/isotopologue distribution patterns (A, A+1, A+2) for input molecular formulae and their predicted adduct ions using the molmass library in Python, producing the mass targets that CCSfind matches against LC-IM-MS mzML traces. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040

skills.description: Use when khipu has preannotated untargeted metabolomics or stable isotope tracing data (e.g. U-13C E. coli, 548 empCpds from 3,602 asari features) and you need to extract per-compound isotope-index envelopes for downstream labeling analysis.
skills.name: isotopologue-envelope-extraction
skills.search_text: isotopologue-envelope-extraction Use when khipu has preannotated untargeted metabolomics or stable isotope tracing data (e.g. U-13C E. coli, 548 empCpds from 3,602 asari features) and you need to extract per-compound isotope-index envelopes for downstream labeling analysis. The input is a raw LC-MS feature table that has not been preannotated by khipu - run khipu first to produce empirical compound trees before extracting isotope envelopes. The analysis targets complete metabolite identification requiring authentic standards or tandem MS data; khipu is a preannotation step and complete annotation still needs contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS. The study involves chemical derivatization experiments where the origin and derivatized compounds must be linked by a derivatization m/z shift - this requires a separate khipu-tree linking procedure, not this envelope-extraction skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Within each khipu empirical compound, connected isotope edges are grouped into per-adduct branches, re-aligned to the khipu grid, and used to extract the isotopologue envelope (e.g. 13C/12C*1, *2, ...) per compound, enabling isotope-index extraction from U-13C-labeled LC-MS data such as the E. coli ecoli_pos.tsv set. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Within each khipu empirical compound, connected isotope edges are grouped into per-adduct branches, re-aligned to the khipu grid, and used to extract the isotopologue envelope (e.g. 13C/12C*1, *2, ...) per compound, enabling isotope-index extraction from U-13C-labeled LC-MS data such as the E. coli ecoli_pos.tsv set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw LC-MS feature table that has not been preannotated by khipu - run khipu first to produce empirical compound trees before extracting isotope envelopes. The analysis targets complete metabolite identification requiring authentic standards or tandem MS data; khipu is a preannotation step and complete annotation still needs contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS. The study involves chemical derivatization experiments where the origin and derivatized compounds must be linked by a derivatization m/z shift - this requires a separate khipu-tree linking procedure, not this envelope-extraction skill.

skills.description: Use when LC-MS data from isotope labeling experiments (FAM vectors per compound/sample, e.g. XLSX input) must be corrected for natural abundance, tracer isotopic impurity, and resolution effects before deriving MDVs and enrichment.
skills.name: isotopologue-fractional-abundance-correction
skills.search_text: isotopologue-fractional-abundance-correction Use when LC-MS data from isotope labeling experiments (FAM vectors per compound/sample, e.g. XLSX input) must be corrected for natural abundance, tracer isotopic impurity, and resolution effects before deriving MDVs and enrichment. When the tracer element selected is not actually present in the compound's formula (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S as tracer) — the algorithm reports an error When input is already corrected MDV data or a flux-analysis result rather than measured FAM from isotopolog intensities When correction without resolution effect is desired at extremely low instrument resolution — ElemCor then behaves identically to IsoCor, so a combinatorial corrector suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Corrects fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) from high-resolution LC-MS stable isotope labeling experiments into mass distribution vectors (MDV) via non-negative linear regression of a resolution-dependent total correction matrix, then computes tracer isotopic enrichment per compound. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Corrects fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) from high-resolution LC-MS stable isotope labeling experiments into mass distribution vectors (MDV) via non-negative linear regression of a resolution-dependent total correction matrix, then computes tracer isotopic enrichment per compound.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the tracer element selected is not actually present in the compound's formula (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S as tracer) — the algorithm reports an error When input is already corrected MDV data or a flux-analysis result rather than measured FAM from isotopolog intensities When correction without resolution effect is desired at extremely low instrument resolution — ElemCor then behaves identically to IsoCor, so a combinatorial corrector suffices

skills.description: Use when a measured MS isotopologue profile of a multi-moiety metabolite (e.g. single-tracer 13C UDP-GlcNAc timecourses or multi-tracer 13C/18O data) must be reconstructed from moiety state fractional abundances, i.e. computing I_x,calc per isotopologue mass shift from a moiety model.
skills.name: isotopologue-intensity-forward-calculation
skills.search_text: isotopologue-intensity-forward-calculation Use when a measured MS isotopologue profile of a multi-moiety metabolite (e.g. single-tracer 13C UDP-GlcNAc timecourses or multi-tracer 13C/18O data) must be reconstructed from moiety state fractional abundances, i.e. computing I_x,calc per isotopologue mass shift from a moiety model. The data are raw MS peaks rather than isotopologue profiles of a metabolite decomposable into moieties — the framework assumes metabolite decomposition into moiety units has already been defined Only a single-isotope tracer with no model-structure ambiguity exists and an existing tool is acceptable — note the precedent that 'the MAIMS software handles only 13C single isotope tracer data and does not address model selection', whereas this skill exists to support single AND multiple-labeled SIRM datasets with explicit model selection Reconstructs the forward isotopologue-intensity calculation (Eq. 1) of the moiety modeling framework: the calculated relative intensity I_x,calc for isotope content x is the sum over all isotopologue components ic_v in IC_x of the products of moiety state fractional abundances across all moieties. This is the core forward model that moiety_modeling fits against measured MS isotopologue profiles of single- and multi-tracer SIRM data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: Reconstructs the forward isotopologue-intensity calculation (Eq. 1) of the moiety modeling framework: the calculated relative intensity I_x,calc for isotope content x is the sum over all isotopologue components ic_v in IC_x of the products of moiety state fractional abundances across all moieties. This is the core forward model that moiety_modeling fits against measured MS isotopologue profiles of single- and multi-tracer SIRM data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw MS peaks rather than isotopologue profiles of a metabolite decomposable into moieties — the framework assumes metabolite decomposition into moiety units has already been defined Only a single-isotope tracer with no model-structure ambiguity exists and an existing tool is acceptable — note the precedent that 'the MAIMS software handles only 13C single isotope tracer data and does not address model selection', whereas this skill exists to support single AND multiple-labeled SIRM datasets with explicit model selection

skills.description: Use when you need Monte Carlo benchmarking of how measurement noise propagates through moiety-model-derived isotopologue profiles — e.g. comparing 13C-only vs 13C/18O glucose multi-tracer error behavior at defined sigma levels.
skills.name: isotopologue-intensity-simulation-from-moiety-models
skills.search_text: isotopologue-intensity-simulation-from-moiety-models Use when you need Monte Carlo benchmarking of how measurement noise propagates through moiety-model-derived isotopologue profiles — e.g. comparing 13C-only vs 13C/18O glucose multi-tracer error behavior at defined sigma levels. Input is real measured MS isotopologue data that needs deconvolution or moiety model fitting — use moiety_modeling optimization/model selection instead of forward simulation The goal is metabolic flux analysis from curated metabolic network models (e.g. EMU framework) rather than isotopologue-profile noise characterization You need model selection among candidate moiety models ranked by AICc; this skill assumes a fixed, already-specified model http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Generates simulated single- and multi-tracer isotopologue datasets by adding thresholded, normally distributed error to intensities computed from moiety models (Eq. 1), then averages isotopologue sums across replicates before renormalization to characterize error propagation (Table 8, Fig 6 of the moiety modeling paper). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: Generates simulated single- and multi-tracer isotopologue datasets by adding thresholded, normally distributed error to intensities computed from moiety models (Eq. 1), then averages isotopologue sums across replicates before renormalization to characterize error propagation (Table 8, Fig 6 of the moiety modeling paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real measured MS isotopologue data that needs deconvolution or moiety model fitting — use moiety_modeling optimization/model selection instead of forward simulation The goal is metabolic flux analysis from curated metabolic network models (e.g. EMU framework) rather than isotopologue-profile noise characterization You need model selection among candidate moiety models ranked by AICc; this skill assumes a fixed, already-specified model

skills.description: Use when MALDI imaging data are stored as imzML and you need ion images for all isotopologues of specific molecules (e.g. fatty acids 20:3, 20:4, 20:5, 22:4, 22:5) from an ion list, rather than only the annotated natural-abundance peaks from METASPACE.
skills.name: isotopologue-ion-image-extraction-from-imzml
skills.search_text: isotopologue-ion-image-extraction-from-imzml Use when MALDI imaging data are stored as imzML and you need ion images for all isotopologues of specific molecules (e.g. fatty acids 20:3, 20:4, 20:5, 22:4, 22:5) from an ion list, rather than only the annotated natural-abundance peaks from METASPACE. If you already have the shared SpaceM output (ion images and single-cell data), re-extracting from raw imzML is unnecessary per the README If you need only natural-abundance METASPACE annotations, since METASPACE already generates those without this extraction step If the aim is bulk/MSI isotopologue modelling without imaging — use the simpler 13C_binomial repository instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Parses imzML MALDI imaging files with pyimzML to extract per-pixel ion images for every isotopologue (M+0, M+1, M+2, ...) of target fatty acids, because METASPACE annotations only cover natural-abundance isotopologue distributions and cannot supply 13C-labelled peaks. It is the first step of the 13C-SpaceM isotopologue workflow before natural isotope abundance correction and binomial fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Parses imzML MALDI imaging files with pyimzML to extract per-pixel ion images for every isotopologue (M+0, M+1, M+2, ...) of target fatty acids, because METASPACE annotations only cover natural-abundance isotopologue distributions and cannot supply 13C-labelled peaks. It is the first step of the 13C-SpaceM isotopologue workflow before natural isotope abundance correction and binomial fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you already have the shared SpaceM output (ion images and single-cell data), re-extracting from raw imzML is unnecessary per the README If you need only natural-abundance METASPACE annotations, since METASPACE already generates those without this extraction step If the aim is bulk/MSI isotopologue modelling without imaging — use the simpler 13C_binomial repository instead

skills.description: Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) data where redundant isotope peaks inflate peak lists and only carbon-containing compound signals (12C monoisotopic isotopologues) should be retained.
skills.name: isotopologue-ion-pairing
skills.search_text: isotopologue-ion-pairing Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) data where redundant isotope peaks inflate peak lists and only carbon-containing compound signals (12C monoisotopic isotopologues) should be retained. Input is already a peak-aligned feature table or peaklist from a prior peak-detection run — isotopologue pairing operates on raw full-scan MS1 spectra, not on post-detection tables. Data were acquired in MS/MS (MS2) fragmentation mode without MS1 full-scan spectral information — the approach relies on MS1-level 12C/13C isotope clusters in individual scans. The analysis targets non-carbon-containing inorganic species or pure isotope-label-free flux experiments where carbon isotope-pairing signatures are absent or intentionally removed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Pairs 12C and 13C isotopologues within individual mass spectra of untargeted LC/HRMS data to generate candidate monoisotopic m/z values, removing redundant isotope peaks before chromatographic peak detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: Pairs 12C and 13C isotopologues within individual mass spectra of untargeted LC/HRMS data to generate candidate monoisotopic m/z values, removing redundant isotope peaks before chromatographic peak detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-aligned feature table or peaklist from a prior peak-detection run — isotopologue pairing operates on raw full-scan MS1 spectra, not on post-detection tables. Data were acquired in MS/MS (MS2) fragmentation mode without MS1 full-scan spectral information — the approach relies on MS1-level 12C/13C isotope clusters in individual scans. The analysis targets non-carbon-containing inorganic species or pure isotope-label-free flux experiments where carbon isotope-pairing signatures are absent or intentionally removed.

skills.name: isotopologue-labelling-visualization-of-metabolic-flux
skills.search_text: isotopologue-labelling-visualization-of-metabolic-flux Use when TarMet has produced a peak-area table of 13C isotopologues for labelled samples (e.g. MRC5 cells labelled 5 or 60 min with 13C6-glucose) and the goal is to visualize labelling patterns across metabolites and assess parallel-sample consistency. When the underlying peak areas have not yet been extracted and aligned by TarMet's tracer workflow (EIC extraction, airPLS baseline removal, MassSpecWavelet peak detection, PAFFT alignment) — the visualization depends on that quantification table. When the goal is untargeted discovery of labelling patterns rather than visualization of a predefined target metabolite list of glucose-pathway metabolites. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Render the stable isotope tracer result as a stacked-bar isotopologue distribution figure (TarMet Fig. 2) so that 13C labelling patterns across glucose-pathway metabolites and the consistency of parallel samples become visually verifiable. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7

When the goal is untargeted discovery of labelling patterns rather than visualization of a predefined target metabolite list of glucose-pathway metabolites.

skills.description: Use when building a resolution-dependent isotopologue correction matrix for a compound formula at a given nominal instrument resolution, and you must decide which same-nominal-mass isotopologs (e.g. 17O vs 15N/13C contributions) can be resolved and which correction-matrix columns to zero.
skills.name: isotopologue-mass-difference-calculation
skills.search_text: isotopologue-mass-difference-calculation Use when building a resolution-dependent isotopologue correction matrix for a compound formula at a given nominal instrument resolution, and you must decide which same-nominal-mass isotopologs (e.g. 17O vs 15N/13C contributions) can be resolved and which correction-matrix columns to zero. The instrument resolution is extremely low — ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor's combinatorial correction with no resolution effect, so MDT zeroing has no effect The tracer element is not present in the compound formula — the README notes the algorithm reports an error if the tracer element is absent (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S as tracer) An unlabeled-sample-based (ULS/FluxFix-style) correction is required instead — that path deconvolves unlabeled-sample FAM rather than computing mass-difference limits Reconstructs the mass difference theory (MDT) resolution-dependent zeroing logic of the ElemCor correction matrix: computing the smallest resolvable mass difference (Delta-M) for the analyzer, deriving per-isotope exclusion limits, and applying ElemCor's improved sum-of-mass-differences criterion over isotope combinations. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Reconstructs the mass difference theory (MDT) resolution-dependent zeroing logic of the ElemCor correction matrix: computing the smallest resolvable mass difference (Delta-M) for the analyzer, deriving per-isotope exclusion limits, and applying ElemCor's improved sum-of-mass-differences criterion over isotope combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The instrument resolution is extremely low — ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor's combinatorial correction with no resolution effect, so MDT zeroing has no effect The tracer element is not present in the compound formula — the README notes the algorithm reports an error if the tracer element is absent (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S as tracer) An unlabeled-sample-based (ULS/FluxFix-style) correction is required instead — that path deconvolves unlabeled-sample FAM rather than computing mass-difference limits

skills.description: Use when pairwise LC/MS feature tables from an isotope-supplemented condition (e.g. 13C6-leucine) and an unlabeled control must be compared to find labeled features via a specific mass shift, or to test whether particular lipids derive from a labeled precursor.
skills.name: isotopologue-mass-shift-detection
skills.search_text: isotopologue-mass-shift-detection Use when pairwise LC/MS feature tables from an isotope-supplemented condition (e.g. 13C6-leucine) and an unlabeled control must be compared to find labeled features via a specific mass shift, or to test whether particular lipids derive from a labeled precursor. Input is already a fully annotated isotope-enrichment table with shift calls, so no pairwise labeled/unlabeled comparison is needed The experimental design lacks a matched unlabeled control feature table, since Label Finder requires pairwise comparison of supplemented vs. unsupplemented samples The goal is general statistical differential-abundance analysis between genotypes (e.g. WT vs. hacl-1) rather than isotope-tracing of precursor incorporation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Detects isotope-labeled metabolites in LC/MS metabolomics by comparing a labeled-supplemented feature table against an unlabeled control with Metaboseek's Label Finder, which flags features showing isotopologue mass shifts (e.g. Δ m/z 5.0167 for 13C5). It traces the origin of lipids such as odd-chain 13:1 and 15:1 species to (or away from) labeled precursor metabolism. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: Detects isotope-labeled metabolites in LC/MS metabolomics by comparing a labeled-supplemented feature table against an unlabeled control with Metaboseek's Label Finder, which flags features showing isotopologue mass shifts (e.g. Δ m/z 5.0167 for 13C5). It traces the origin of lipids such as odd-chain 13:1 and 15:1 species to (or away from) labeled precursor metabolism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fully annotated isotope-enrichment table with shift calls, so no pairwise labeled/unlabeled comparison is needed The experimental design lacks a matched unlabeled control feature table, since Label Finder requires pairwise comparison of supplemented vs. unsupplemented samples The goal is general statistical differential-abundance analysis between genotypes (e.g. WT vs. hacl-1) rather than isotope-tracing of precursor incorporation

skills.description: Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS mzXML/mzML/netCDF data with IDSL.IPA and you need to suppress redundant isotope/adduct-like peaks by pairing 12C and 13C signals within each scan, or when troubleshooting why peaks were excluded by nIsoPair/RCS thresholds.
skills.name: isotopologue-pairing-assessment
skills.search_text: isotopologue-pairing-assessment Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS mzXML/mzML/netCDF data with IDSL.IPA and you need to suppress redundant isotope/adduct-like peaks by pairing 12C and 13C signals within each scan, or when troubleshooting why peaks were excluded by nIsoPair/RCS thresholds. When the goal is annotating already-filtered peaklists with molecular formulas — use IDSL.UFA or IDSL.UFAx instead of re-running ion pairing. When peak detection itself is the target rather than pre-detection isotope deconvolution; MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA, and MS-DIAL detect chromatographic regions of interest without the scan-level 12C/13C pairing step. When processing netCDF/CDF data without installing RNetCDF — IDSL.IPA requires RNetCDF for netCDF/CDF inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assess and apply 12C/13C isotopologue ion pairing in each mass spectrum to isolate high-quality, non-redundant carbon-containing peaks before EIC peak detection in IDSL.IPA, so that only the most abundant monoisotopic isotopologues are carried into peak analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: Assess and apply 12C/13C isotopologue ion pairing in each mass spectrum to isolate high-quality, non-redundant carbon-containing peaks before EIC peak detection in IDSL.IPA, so that only the most abundant monoisotopic isotopologues are carried into peak analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotating already-filtered peaklists with molecular formulas — use IDSL.UFA or IDSL.UFAx instead of re-running ion pairing. When peak detection itself is the target rather than pre-detection isotope deconvolution; MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA, and MS-DIAL detect chromatographic regions of interest without the scan-level 12C/13C pairing step. When processing netCDF/CDF data without installing RNetCDF — IDSL.IPA requires RNetCDF for netCDF/CDF inputs.

skills.name: isotopologue-pairing-quality-threshold-evaluation
skills.search_text: isotopologue-pairing-quality-threshold-evaluation Use when comparing IDSL.IPA peak lists (e.g. 20,253 peaks for MTBLS1684 file 003.d) against MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA or MS-DIAL output and you must attribute missing peaks to isotopologue pairing or peak quality thresholds. When the goal is molecular formula annotation or MS2-based structural identification (IDSL.UFA/IDSL.CSA territory) rather than explaining which peaks IDSL.IPA retained. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluate baseline-tool peaks that are absent from an IDSL.IPA peaklist against the pipeline's 12C/13C isotopologue pairing and peak quality thresholds, so that peak-count differences between IDSL.IPA, MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA and MS-DIAL can be explained as threshold-failure rates rather than raw counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: Evaluate baseline-tool peaks that are absent from an IDSL.IPA peaklist against the pipeline's 12C/13C isotopologue pairing and peak quality thresholds, so that peak-count differences between IDSL.IPA, MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA and MS-DIAL can be explained as threshold-failure rates rather than raw counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already an aligned peak intensity matrix or a feature table that has passed all filtering steps — this skill re-evaluates raw candidate peaks against thresholds, not finished data matrices. skills.description: Use when a preprocessed feature table contains unexplained ion groups whose members differ by isotope or adduct mass shifts (e.g. 1.0034 Da 13C/12C, 22.9893 Da Na+), or when annotating U-13C-labeled tracing samples.
skills.name: isotopologue-pattern-interpretation
skills.search_text: isotopologue-pattern-interpretation Use when a preprocessed feature table contains unexplained ion groups whose members differ by isotope or adduct mass shifts (e.g. 1.0034 Da 13C/12C, 22.9893 Da Na+), or when annotating U-13C-labeled tracing samples. Input is raw LC-MS data rather than a preprocessed feature table — khipu expects asari-style feature tables, so preprocessing with asari 1.9.2 must come first. Complete metabolite identification is required, including confirmation against authentic libraries, contaminant handling, or tandem MS data — khipu provides preannotation only and these must be handled downstream. The goal is de novo formula assignment without any prior isotope/adduct pattern knowledge — the method starts by searching user-definable mass-difference patterns and is one of the tools whose annotation of isotopic tracing data remains 'not fully solved'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Groups LC-MS features into isotopologue/adduct ion trees ('empirical compounds') using khipu's generalized tree structure, inferring the neutral mass of M0 by regression; works for regular untargeted metabolomics and stable-isotope tracing data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Groups LC-MS features into isotopologue/adduct ion trees ('empirical compounds') using khipu's generalized tree structure, inferring the neutral mass of M0 by regression; works for regular untargeted metabolomics and stable-isotope tracing data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data rather than a preprocessed feature table — khipu expects asari-style feature tables, so preprocessing with asari 1.9.2 must come first. Complete metabolite identification is required, including confirmation against authentic libraries, contaminant handling, or tandem MS data — khipu provides preannotation only and these must be handled downstream. The goal is de novo formula assignment without any prior isotope/adduct pattern knowledge — the method starts by searching user-definable mass-difference patterns and is one of the tools whose annotation of isotopic tracing data remains 'not fully solved'.

skills.description: Use when performing targeted LC-MS stable-isotope-tracer or isotopologue analysis: you have defined target metabolites, extracted M+H isotopologue EICs per sample, and need to score observed isotope patterns against theoretical patterns at the MS resolution.
skills.name: isotopologue-pattern-matching
skills.search_text: isotopologue-pattern-matching Use when performing targeted LC-MS stable-isotope-tracer or isotopologue analysis: you have defined target metabolites, extracted M+H isotopologue EICs per sample, and need to score observed isotope patterns against theoretical patterns at the MS resolution. The goal is untargeted feature detection rather than targeted quantification of predefined metabolites and their isotopologues (TarMet is a targeted method). Data are already processed into a feature/intensity table without raw EICs, so baseline removal, peak picking with MassSpecWavelet, and RT alignment with PAFFT cannot be applied. MS/MS library verification or data-independent acquisition is needed — the TarMet README lists these only as planned future features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Match extracted-ion-chromatogram M+H isotopologue peaks to theoretical isotope patterns of target metabolites at the instrument resolution, using the isotopic similarity score to confirm and quantify targeted metabolites and their isotopologues in LC-MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Match extracted-ion-chromatogram M+H isotopologue peaks to theoretical isotope patterns of target metabolites at the instrument resolution, using the isotopic similarity score to confirm and quantify targeted metabolites and their isotopologues in LC-MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is untargeted feature detection rather than targeted quantification of predefined metabolites and their isotopologues (TarMet is a targeted method). Data are already processed into a feature/intensity table without raw EICs, so baseline removal, peak picking with MassSpecWavelet, and RT alignment with PAFFT cannot be applied. MS/MS library verification or data-independent acquisition is needed — the TarMet README lists these only as planned future features.

skills.description: Use when you have EICs for a targeted isotopologue across multiple tracer samples (e.g. 13C6-glucose labelling) and need retention-time-aligned peak areas per sample for isotopologue quantification.
skills.name: isotopologue-peak-quantification
skills.search_text: isotopologue-peak-quantification Use when you have EICs for a targeted isotopologue across multiple tracer samples (e.g. 13C6-glucose labelling) and need retention-time-aligned peak areas per sample for isotopologue quantification. The goal is untargeted peak picking rather than targeted isotopologue quantification of known metabolites Retention-time shifts are already negligible (e.g. same run, no cross-sample alignment needed), making PAFFT alignment unnecessary Isotopologue patterns must be derived from raw spectra rather than quantified from pre-detected EICs — use theoretical pattern calculation via enviPat instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Integrate aligned extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) peak areas for a chosen metabolite isotopologue across samples using TarMet's PAFFT alignment and getQuantifiedResult integration, producing a per-sample peak-area table for stable isotope tracer quantification. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Integrate aligned extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) peak areas for a chosen metabolite isotopologue across samples using TarMet's PAFFT alignment and getQuantifiedResult integration, producing a per-sample peak-area table for stable isotope tracer quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is untargeted peak picking rather than targeted isotopologue quantification of known metabolites Retention-time shifts are already negligible (e.g. same run, no cross-sample alignment needed), making PAFFT alignment unnecessary Isotopologue patterns must be derived from raw spectra rather than quantified from pre-detected EICs — use theoretical pattern calculation via enviPat instead

skills.description: Use when quantifying a targeted metabolite and its isotopologues from LC-MS EICs where multiple peaks are detected per isotopologue and the correct target peak must be chosen via isotope-pattern similarity.

skills.search_text: isotopologue-peak-selection-targeted-ms Use when quantifying a targeted metabolite and its isotopologues from LC-MS EICs where multiple peaks are detected per isotopologue and the correct target peak must be chosen via isotope-pattern similarity. skills.summary: Selects the true target-metabolite peak among multiple chromatographic candidates by scoring each detected peak against the metabolite's theoretical isotope pattern (computed with enviPat at the instrument resolution) using TarMet's isotopic-similarity metric (Eq. 1), keeping the peak with maximum similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantified feature/peak table with no chromatographic peak candidates — there is nothing to disambiguate via isotope-pattern similarity The analysis is untargeted feature detection rather than targeted metabolite/isotopologue quantification with a known molecular formula The compound's theoretical isotope pattern cannot be computed (no formula/resolution) or the metabolite is a single isotope peak with no isotopologue series to compare

skills.search_text: isotopologue-ppm-error-verification Use when processing high-resolution (Orbitrap) centroided GC-MS mzML files with isoSCAN autoQ in stable-isotope labeling experiments and you must confirm that the integrated isotopologue peaks correspond to the predicted m/z values within the allowed mass error before reporting enrichment. Low-resolution GC-CI-MS data processed in SIM or NS modes, where isotopologue separation relies on unit-mass resolution rather than ppm error against an enviPat-predicted envelope Spectra produced by hard electron ionization (EI at 70 eV), which fragment compound structures and prevent assignment of a coherent [M+H]+ isotopic envelope http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Verifies that autoQ-integrated isotopologues from high-resolution GC-CI-MS (Orbitrap/qTOF) data match the enviPat-predicted theoretical isotopic distribution by checking the predicted m/z and ppm error columns reported for each isotopologue. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02998
skills.summary: Verifies that autoQ-integrated isotopologues from high-resolution GC-CI-MS (Orbitrap/qTOF) data match the enviPat-predicted theoretical isotopic distribution by checking the predicted m/z and ppm error columns reported for each isotopologue.
