skills.description: Use when assessing peak-abundance quality of XCMS or MZmine 2 pre-processing output against an mzRAPP benchmark — i.e. quantifying what fraction of matched peaks show degenerated isotopologue ratios.
skills.name: isotopologue-ratio-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: isotopologue-ratio-quality-assessment Use when assessing peak-abundance quality of XCMS or MZmine 2 pre-processing output against an mzRAPP benchmark — i.e. quantifying what fraction of matched peaks show degenerated isotopologue ratios. Input is raw mzML without an mzRAPP benchmark — IR bias checks require the predicted isotopologue ratios generated from the target file and enviPat The target molecules have only one detectable isotopologue per adduct — mzRAPP only accepts isotopologues where the most abundant plus at least one additional isotopologue are found The goal is peak-picking recall or alignment-error counting rather than peak-abundance quality — use found/not-found peak counts and assess_alignment()/count_alignment_errors() instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes mzRAPP's isotopologue-ratio (IR) degeneration metric, which judges peak-abundance quality of NPP output by measuring how far measured isotopologue ratios drift from the enviPat-predicted values in the benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab231
skills.summary: Computes mzRAPP's isotopologue-ratio (IR) degeneration metric, which judges peak-abundance quality of NPP output by measuring how far measured isotopologue ratios drift from the enviPat-predicted values in the benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzML without an mzRAPP benchmark — IR bias checks require the predicted isotopologue ratios generated from the target file and enviPat The target molecules have only one detectable isotopologue per adduct — mzRAPP only accepts isotopologues where the most abundant plus at least one additional isotopologue are found The goal is peak-picking recall or alignment-error counting rather than peak-abundance quality — use found/not-found peak counts and assess_alignment()/count_alignment_errors() instead

skills.description: Use when you need to solve the boundary-value inverse problem of fitting moiety model parameters to MS-measured isotopologue timecourse data, and/or to select among multiple plausible moiety models via AICc.
skills.name: isotopologue-timecourse-parameter-optimization
skills.search_text: isotopologue-timecourse-parameter-optimization Use when you need to solve the boundary-value inverse problem of fitting moiety model parameters to MS-measured isotopologue timecourse data, and/or to select among multiple plausible moiety models via AICc. The data are 13C single-tracer profiles already handled by MAIMS and no model selection among competing moiety models is needed (MAIMS handles 13C single isotope tracer data but does not address model selection). The goal is full metabolic flux analysis over a well-curated metabolic network (EMU-style 13C MFA), rather than deconvoluting isotopologue profiles into moiety abundances. The data are NMR-based isotopomer measurements or unlabeled abundance data with no isotope tracer timecourse to fit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit moiety model parameters to mass spectrometry-measured 13C isotopologue timecourses (e.g., UDP-GlcNAc at 34 h, 48 h, 72 h) using the SAGA simulated annealing plus genetic algorithm optimizer driven by a log difference objective function, then rank fitted models by AICc for model selection. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: Fit moiety model parameters to mass spectrometry-measured 13C isotopologue timecourses (e.g., UDP-GlcNAc at 34 h, 48 h, 72 h) using the SAGA simulated annealing plus genetic algorithm optimizer driven by a log difference objective function, then rank fitted models by AICc for model selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are 13C single-tracer profiles already handled by MAIMS and no model selection among competing moiety models is needed (MAIMS handles 13C single isotope tracer data but does not address model selection). The goal is full metabolic flux analysis over a well-curated metabolic network (EMU-style 13C MFA), rather than deconvoluting isotopologue profiles into moiety abundances. The data are NMR-based isotopomer measurements or unlabeled abundance data with no isotope tracer timecourse to fit.

skills.description: Use when isotopologue distributions from a [U-13C6]glucose or similar tracer HRMS time course have already been natural-abundance corrected (NACorrectionFxnII) and the goal is to express enrichment as nmol of 13C-labeled molecules formed per time point for kinetic clustering or precursor-product.
skills.name: isotopologue-to-nmol-13c-unit-conversion
skills.search_text: isotopologue-to-nmol-13c-unit-conversion Use when isotopologue distributions from a [U-13C6]glucose or similar tracer HRMS time course have already been natural-abundance corrected (NACorrectionFxnII) and the goal is to express enrichment as nmol of 13C-labeled molecules formed per time point for kinetic clustering or precursor-product. Input is a raw XCMS feature table or uncorrected isotopologue fractions — natural abundance correction (NACorrectionFxnII) must precede the nmol-13C conversion or amounts will be biased by unlabeled isotopologue spillover The analysis goal is flux estimation via INST-MFA, where SIMPEL tables are exported to INCA rather than converted to nmol product abundances Data come from nominal-resolution MS where dual-labeled isotopologues are indistinguishable; HRMS m/z resolution is assumed by the isotopologue model http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions from SIMPEL-processed HRMS stable-isotope labeling data into absolute nmol abundances of 13C-labeled product molecules, so that labeling kinetics can be compared across lipid species of different pool sizes (e.g., Camelina PC and DAG over a [U-13C6]glucose 0-32 h time course). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42003-024-05844-z
skills.summary: Converts natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions from SIMPEL-processed HRMS stable-isotope labeling data into absolute nmol abundances of 13C-labeled product molecules, so that labeling kinetics can be compared across lipid species of different pool sizes (e.g., Camelina PC and DAG over a [U-13C6]glucose 0-32 h time course).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw XCMS feature table or uncorrected isotopologue fractions — natural abundance correction (NACorrectionFxnII) must precede the nmol-13C conversion or amounts will be biased by unlabeled isotopologue spillover The analysis goal is flux estimation via INST-MFA, where SIMPEL tables are exported to INCA rather than converted to nmol product abundances Data come from nominal-resolution MS where dual-labeled isotopologues are indistinguishable; HRMS m/z resolution is assumed by the isotopologue model

skills.description: Use when building LC-IM-MS (drift tube IM-MS) databases from profile mzML files for a list of molecular formulae, and candidate primary-ion m/z traces must be confirmed by isotopologue matching after RT peak picking.
skills.name: isotopologue-trace-confirmation
skills.search_text: isotopologue-trace-confirmation Use when building LC-IM-MS (drift tube IM-MS) databases from profile mzML files for a list of molecular formulae, and candidate primary-ion m/z traces must be confirmed by isotopologue matching after RT peak picking. Input is already a peak/feature table rather than profile LC-DTIM-MS mzML data — no trace extraction or CentWave peak picking is needed. The goal is untargeted feature detection without a priori molecular formulae; this skill is chemically informed and requires input molecular formulae to derive target primary-ion m/z. Data are not drift tube IM-MS (LC-IM-MS) measurements, since CCSfind's workflow (arrival-time traces, CCS calibration, drift gas identity) is specific to DTIM-MS. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Chemically informed targeted peak picking in CCSfind: monoisotopic primary-ion m/z traces from a parsed mzML file are extracted over retention time, peak-picked in the RT dimension with the tidyms CentWave implementation, and filtered by isotopologue matching confirmation (A, A+1, A+2) before being written to a peak table. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040
skills.summary: Chemically informed targeted peak picking in CCSfind: monoisotopic primary-ion m/z traces from a parsed mzML file are extracted over retention time, peak-picked in the RT dimension with the tidyms CentWave implementation, and filtered by isotopologue matching confirmation (A, A+1, A+2) before being written to a peak table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak/feature table rather than profile LC-DTIM-MS mzML data — no trace extraction or CentWave peak picking is needed. The goal is untargeted feature detection without a priori molecular formulae; this skill is chemically informed and requires input molecular formulae to derive target primary-ion m/z. Data are not drift tube IM-MS (LC-IM-MS) measurements, since CCSfind's workflow (arrival-time traces, CCS calibration, drift gas identity) is specific to DTIM-MS.

skills.description: Use when two isotopomer distributions for the same metabolite are available — one from a classical NMR multiplet fit over a restricted isotopomer subset and one from the deep-learning fit over all possible isotopomers — and their agreement must be quantified.
skills.name: isotopomer-distribution-comparison
skills.search_text: isotopomer-distribution-comparison Use when two isotopomer distributions for the same metabolite are available — one from a classical NMR multiplet fit over a restricted isotopomer subset and one from the deep-learning fit over all possible isotopomers — and their agreement must be quantified. Only one isotopomer distribution is available and no reference/classical fit exists to compare against — use the metabolabpytools train/predict isotopomer workflow instead of a comparison. The two distributions use incommensurable species sets and no residual-summing/renormalisation step can make them directly comparable. The goal is raw NMR spectrum processing (phase correction, segmental alignment, spectral scaling) rather than isotopomer-level comparison — MetaboLabPy's pre-processing workflow covers that. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Compares an isotopomer distribution produced by the deep-learning (neural-network) fit in metabolabpytools against a classically fitted distribution restricted to a subset of isotopomers (e.g. unlabelled, [3-13C], and [2,3-13C] lactate), quantifying per-fraction and distribution-level agreement. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Compares an isotopomer distribution produced by the deep-learning (neural-network) fit in metabolabpytools against a classically fitted distribution restricted to a subset of isotopomers (e.g. unlabelled, [3-13C], and [2,3-13C] lactate), quantifying per-fraction and distribution-level agreement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one isotopomer distribution is available and no reference/classical fit exists to compare against — use the metabolabpytools train/predict isotopomer workflow instead of a comparison. The two distributions use incommensurable species sets and no residual-summing/renormalisation step can make them directly comparable. The goal is raw NMR spectrum processing (phase correction, segmental alignment, spectral scaling) rather than isotopomer-level comparison — MetaboLabPy's pre-processing workflow covers that.

skills.description: Use when peak-area tables from GC-MS amino acid analysis must be ISTD-normalized one-to-one and precision summarized as average RSD to compare derivatization agents (PCF, MTBSTFA, MSTFA) across plasma sample sets.
skills.name: istd-normalization-rsd-calculation
skills.search_text: istd-normalization-rsd-calculation Use when peak-area tables from GC-MS amino acid analysis must be ISTD-normalized one-to-one and precision summarized as average RSD to compare derivatization agents (PCF, MTBSTFA, MSTFA) across plasma sample sets. Normalizing large panels of unannotated metabolites lacking cognate isotope-labeled standards — the article reports that internal-standard normalization did not yield median precision below 30% across all 563 metabolite annotations, so machine-learning normalization (SERDA/SERRF) is the appropriate choice there Input consists of pooled QC samples intended for SERDA/SERRF model training rather than a small-set derivatization-precision comparison Peak areas have already been normalized (e.g., to a total ion signal or batch model), since re-normalization to cognate ISTDs requires raw peak areas Computes analytical precision of GC-MS derivatization reagents by one-to-one normalization of amino acid peak areas to their cognate stable-isotope-labeled internal standards in R, then averaging per-trial relative standard deviations (RSD) across replicate trials to benchmark PCF (2.7%) vs MTBSTFA (8.9%) vs MSTFA (9.6%). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080944
skills.summary: Computes analytical precision of GC-MS derivatization reagents by one-to-one normalization of amino acid peak areas to their cognate stable-isotope-labeled internal standards in R, then averaging per-trial relative standard deviations (RSD) across replicate trials to benchmark PCF (2.7%) vs MTBSTFA (8.9%) vs MSTFA (9.6%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Normalizing large panels of unannotated metabolites lacking cognate isotope-labeled standards — the article reports that internal-standard normalization did not yield median precision below 30% across all 563 metabolite annotations, so machine-learning normalization (SERDA/SERRF) is the appropriate choice there Input consists of pooled QC samples intended for SERDA/SERRF model training rather than a small-set derivatization-precision comparison Peak areas have already been normalized (e.g., to a total ion signal or batch model), since re-normalization to cognate ISTDs requires raw peak areas

skills.description: Use when processing raw LC/MS mzML files where signal-detection thresholds cannot be set manually and must be learned from the data itself until convergence.
skills.name: iterative-threshold-convergence-estimation
skills.search_text: iterative-threshold-convergence-estimation Use when processing raw LC/MS mzML files where signal-detection thresholds cannot be set manually and must be learned from the data itself until convergence. Input is already a processed feature table — the convergence procedure operates on raw mzML MS1 data, not on feature matrices (downstream mzEmbed consumes CSV feature matrices directly) You need de-isotoping or MS/MS identification — mzLearn outputs are at the ion MS1 level only and these steps must be done with downstream workflows You need a fast single-pass method — the iterative learning increases computational time, taking up to 2.5 days on a single machine http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 mzLearn's data-driven, non-parametric mechanism for estimating signal-detection thresholds and rt/intensity drift maps entirely from the LC/MS data itself: rt/m/z space is partitioned into patches, filtered by auto-correlation, and thresholds are learned iteratively from the highest-quality 'pin' patches until convergence (~3 iterations), so no user-set parameters or QC samples are required. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: mzLearn's data-driven, non-parametric mechanism for estimating signal-detection thresholds and rt/intensity drift maps entirely from the LC/MS data itself: rt/m/z space is partitioned into patches, filtered by auto-correlation, and thresholds are learned iteratively from the highest-quality 'pin' patches until convergence (~3 iterations), so no user-set parameters or QC samples are required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table — the convergence procedure operates on raw mzML MS1 data, not on feature matrices (downstream mzEmbed consumes CSV feature matrices directly) You need de-isotoping or MS/MS identification — mzLearn outputs are at the ion MS1 level only and these steps must be done with downstream workflows You need a fast single-pass method — the iterative learning increases computational time, taking up to 2.5 days on a single machine

skills.description: Use when 1H-NMR spectra (rows = samples, columns = chemical shifts in ppm) still show baseline drift after internal referencing — e.
skills.name: iteratively-reweighted-pls-baseline-fitting
skills.search_text: iteratively-reweighted-pls-baseline-fitting Use when 1H-NMR spectra (rows = samples, columns = chemical shifts in ppm) still show baseline drift after internal referencing — e. The spectra have already been baseline-corrected (e.g. you already hold a bc_df from a prior px.baseline_correction call) — re-correcting risks distorting genuine signal. The data are still FIDs (fids_df, grpd_df, apod_df, zf_df) rather than spectra — this skill operates on the frequency-domain spectra_df after Fourier transform, phase correction, and internal referencing. You need a baseline algorithm outside ALS/ARPLS/AIRPLS — Protomix implements only these three from pyBaselines, so other strategies require using pyBaselines directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3892 Baseline correction of 1H-NMR spectra via penalized least squares schemes — asymmetric least squares (ALS), adaptive reweighted PLS (ARPLS), and automatic iterative reweighted PLS (AIRPLS) — as implemented in Protomix's baseline_correction function, adapted from the pyBaselines package. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Baseline correction of 1H-NMR spectra via penalized least squares schemes — asymmetric least squares (ALS), adaptive reweighted PLS (ARPLS), and automatic iterative reweighted PLS (AIRPLS) — as implemented in Protomix's baseline_correction function, adapted from the pyBaselines package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra have already been baseline-corrected (e.g. you already hold a bc_df from a prior px.baseline_correction call) — re-correcting risks distorting genuine signal. The data are still FIDs (fids_df, grpd_df, apod_df, zf_df) rather than spectra — this skill operates on the frequency-domain spectra_df after Fourier transform, phase correction, and internal referencing. You need a baseline algorithm outside ALS/ARPLS/AIRPLS — Protomix implements only these three from pyBaselines, so other strategies require using pyBaselines directly.

skills.name: iupac-name-feature-parsing
skills.search_text: iupac-name-feature-parsing Use when input compounds carry only IUPAC names (no structure strings) and structural features must still be extracted for taxonomy classification, or when name-parsing must be validated against OPSIN-converted structures. Input is already a structure string (SMILES/SDF/InChI) — use the structure-based superstructure search path instead Query compounds need physico-chemical property calculation rather than feature detection Detect structural features from IUPAC chemical names alone, using ~200 regular-expression rules as a fallback when a structure (SMILES/InChI) is unavailable, in support of ClassyFire's rule-based taxonomy assignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
