skills.description: Use when comparing two simulated MRS metabolite basis sets (e.g. MRSCloud vs MARSS) and some metabolites show larger basis-function discrepancies than others, requiring judgment on whether differences stem from complex J-coupling spin systems rather than simulation error.
skills.name: j-coupled-spin-system-discrepancy-interpretation
skills.search_text: j-coupled-spin-system-discrepancy-interpretation Use when comparing two simulated MRS metabolite basis sets (e.g. MRSCloud vs MARSS) and some metabolites show larger basis-function discrepancies than others, requiring judgment on whether differences stem from complex J-coupling spin systems rather than simulation error. When discrepancies involve the LCModel phantom-measured vendor basis set — the article states this comparison is confounded because waveforms and timings of press_te30_3t_01a.basis are not well documented, so elevated NRMS there cannot be attributed to J-coupling alone When the metabolite with high NRMS is a singlet-dominant, weakly-coupled species (e.g. NAA, Cr) — large deviations there indicate genuine simulation or alignment problems, not expected J-coupling sensitivity http://edamontology.org/topic_3418 Interprets elevated normalized RMS differences (e.g. 5–8%) between simulated MRS basis functions not as simulation failure but as expected behavior for strongly J-coupled spins (GABA, Gln, Glu), while applying hard validation thresholds (ICC >= 0.96, NRMS < 9%). metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: Interprets elevated normalized RMS differences (e.g. 5–8%) between simulated MRS basis functions not as simulation failure but as expected behavior for strongly J-coupled spins (GABA, Gln, Glu), while applying hard validation thresholds (ICC >= 0.96, NRMS < 9%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When discrepancies involve the LCModel phantom-measured vendor basis set — the article states this comparison is confounded because waveforms and timings of press_te30_3t_01a.basis are not well documented, so elevated NRMS there cannot be attributed to J-coupling alone When the metabolite with high NRMS is a singlet-dominant, weakly-coupled species (e.g. NAA, Cr) — large deviations there indicate genuine simulation or alignment problems, not expected J-coupling sensitivity

skills.description: Use when 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, 15N, 31P, etc.) contain multiplet signals whose chemical shift, intensity, area, linewidth, and J coupling constants must be quantified, including overlapping peaks.
skills.name: j-coupling-multiplet-structure-analysis
skills.search_text: j-coupling-multiplet-structure-analysis Use when 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, 15N, 31P, etc.) contain multiplet signals whose chemical shift, intensity, area, linewidth, and J coupling constants must be quantified, including overlapping peaks. The spectra are full multi-dimensional NMR correlation experiments rather than series of 1D or pseudo-2D spectra that MultiNMRFit fits The signal shape cannot be captured by the built-in multiplet models and no user-defined model has been implemented Only qualitative peak identification is needed — the skill targets quantitative parameter extraction (intensity, area, chemical shift, J), not annotation alone Fit built-in mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian multiplet signal models (singlet through quadruplet) to 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra with MultiNMRFit to recover chemical shift (xs), total intensity (I), scalar coupling constant (J), linewidth at half maximum (lw), and the Gaussian fraction (a) per signal. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Fit built-in mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian multiplet signal models (singlet through quadruplet) to 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra with MultiNMRFit to recover chemical shift (xs), total intensity (I), scalar coupling constant (J), linewidth at half maximum (lw), and the Gaussian fraction (a) per signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are full multi-dimensional NMR correlation experiments rather than series of 1D or pseudo-2D spectra that MultiNMRFit fits The signal shape cannot be captured by the built-in multiplet models and no user-defined model has been implemented Only qualitative peak identification is needed — the skill targets quantitative parameter extraction (intensity, area, chemical shift, J), not annotation alone

skills.description: Use when building metabolite basis functions for MRS fitting (e.g., PRESS, MEGA-PRESS, HERMES, HERCULES) and the spin-system Hamiltonians — J-coupling values and chemical shifts per metabolite — must be specified before density-matrix simulation.
skills.name: j-coupling-spin-system-parameterization
skills.search_text: j-coupling-spin-system-parameterization Use when building metabolite basis functions for MRS fitting (e.g., PRESS, MEGA-PRESS, HERMES, HERCULES) and the spin-system Hamiltonians — J-coupling values and chemical shifts per metabolite — must be specified before density-matrix simulation. The goal is to model every possible vendor experiment: MRSCloud simulations cannot capture all possible Philips experiments or all disseminated versions of MEGA-PRESS within each vendor. The spin-system parameterization itself must be re-derived or updated: the literature parameters still rest largely on Govindaraju et al. with only minor updates, so novel compounds outside the listed metabolites (e.g., beyond EtOH/MSM exogenous entries) are not covered. Non-brain tissue or non-3T field strengths are the target — this work has only been focused and tested on brain MRS data using 3T scanners, and the exiting version only supports 3T. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Defines the quantum-mechanical spin-system description (chemical shifts, scalar J-couplings, and spin counts) for each metabolite so density-matrix simulations in MRSCloud/FID-A produce vendor- and sequence-specific MRS basis functions at 3T. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: Defines the quantum-mechanical spin-system description (chemical shifts, scalar J-couplings, and spin counts) for each metabolite so density-matrix simulations in MRSCloud/FID-A produce vendor- and sequence-specific MRS basis functions at 3T.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to model every possible vendor experiment: MRSCloud simulations cannot capture all possible Philips experiments or all disseminated versions of MEGA-PRESS within each vendor. The spin-system parameterization itself must be re-derived or updated: the literature parameters still rest largely on Govindaraju et al. with only minor updates, so novel compounds outside the listed metabolites (e.g., beyond EtOH/MSM exogenous entries) are not covered. Non-brain tissue or non-3T field strengths are the target — this work has only been focused and tested on brain MRS data using 3T scanners, and the exiting version only supports 3T.

skills.description: Use when a pathway enrichment result table contains many overlapping enriched pathways (within or across pathway databases) and you need to quantify and cluster their analyte-membership redundancy before interpretation.
skills.name: jaccard-analyte-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: jaccard-analyte-overlap-scoring Use when a pathway enrichment result table contains many overlapping enriched pathways (within or across pathway databases) and you need to quantify and cluster their analyte-membership redundancy before interpretation. The input is an unfiltered enrichment table — apply FilterFishersResults first so clustering runs only on significant pathways You need pathway similarity based on shared function or ontology rather than shared analyte (gene/metabolite) membership The analyte list contains few pathways with little overlap, so partitioning adds no interpretive value over reading the enrichment table directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes pairwise Jaccard similarity of gene/metabolite memberships between significantly enriched pathways and uses those scores as the linkage basis for DAVID-style fuzzy multiple-linkage partitioning clustering in RaMP, resolving redundancy from pathway content overlap across KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo8010016
skills.summary: Computes pairwise Jaccard similarity of gene/metabolite memberships between significantly enriched pathways and uses those scores as the linkage basis for DAVID-style fuzzy multiple-linkage partitioning clustering in RaMP, resolving redundancy from pathway content overlap across KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an unfiltered enrichment table — apply FilterFishersResults first so clustering runs only on significant pathways You need pathway similarity based on shared function or ontology rather than shared analyte (gene/metabolite) membership The analyte list contains few pathways with little overlap, so partitioning adds no interpretive value over reading the enrichment table directly

skills.description: Use when a KNN classifier has returned candidate GCF labels for MS/MS spectra from paired genome-metabolome samples and predictions must be pruned by biosynthetic co-occurrence before computing precision or prioritizing links.
skills.name: jaccard-co-occurrence-filtering
skills.search_text: jaccard-co-occurrence-filtering Use when a KNN classifier has returned candidate GCF labels for MS/MS spectra from paired genome-metabolome samples and predictions must be pruned by biosynthetic co-occurrence before computing precision or prioritizing links. When the dataset differs substantially from the PoDP-derived training set — the article warns the precision score may not be reproducible for datasets not similar to the current training set When the query organism (e.g., a fungal species) has no BGC similar to any training-set BGC — the co-occurrence filter cannot rescue predictions from an empty KNN output When candidate GCFs are legitimately absent from the sequenced genome of the matched sample due to fragmented or low-quality metagenome assemblies — the filter would wrongly discard true links http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A post-classification filtering step in the NPOmix KNN pipeline that removes predicted gene cluster family (GCF) candidates absent from the genome of the matched paired sample, boosting precision from ~81.8% to 92.9% (top-10) using a Jaccard index cutoff of 0.7. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: A post-classification filtering step in the NPOmix KNN pipeline that removes predicted gene cluster family (GCF) candidates absent from the genome of the matched paired sample, boosting precision from ~81.8% to 92.9% (top-10) using a Jaccard index cutoff of 0.7.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset differs substantially from the PoDP-derived training set — the article warns the precision score may not be reproducible for datasets not similar to the current training set When the query organism (e.g., a fungal species) has no BGC similar to any training-set BGC — the co-occurrence filter cannot rescue predictions from an empty KNN output When candidate GCFs are legitimately absent from the sequenced genome of the matched sample due to fragmented or low-quality metagenome assemblies — the filter would wrongly discard true links

skills.description: Use when you have a network representation of the GWAS Catalog gene sets and need to prune non-significant study-study edges and extract disease/trait-specific subnetworks for downstream over-representation analysis.
skills.name: jaccard-coefficient-edge-filtering
skills.search_text: jaccard-coefficient-edge-filtering Use when you have a network representation of the GWAS Catalog gene sets and need to prune non-significant study-study edges and extract disease/trait-specific subnetworks for downstream over-representation analysis. When data are paired metabolomics-GWAS measurements rather than standalone/independent studies — metGWAS 1.0 is explicitly designed for the unpaired setting, limiting associations to genes with known metabolite interactions When building the metabolic gene-set side of the analysis — this skill only prunes the GWAS Catalog genomic network, not the metabolite-to-protein mapping step When you need all GWAS Catalog study overlaps regardless of significance — discarding Jaccard < 0.5 edges removes the majority of weakly overlapping study pairs by design http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Builds trait/disease-related GWAS subnetworks from the GWAS Catalog by keeping only network edges whose overlap of gene sets is statistically significant — Jaccard coefficient >= 0.5 with FDR-corrected P-value <= 0.05 — then extracting keyword-filtered first-neighbour subnetworks. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Builds trait/disease-related GWAS subnetworks from the GWAS Catalog by keeping only network edges whose overlap of gene sets is statistically significant — Jaccard coefficient >= 0.5 with FDR-corrected P-value <= 0.05 — then extracting keyword-filtered first-neighbour subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When data are paired metabolomics-GWAS measurements rather than standalone/independent studies — metGWAS 1.0 is explicitly designed for the unpaired setting, limiting associations to genes with known metabolite interactions When building the metabolic gene-set side of the analysis — this skill only prunes the GWAS Catalog genomic network, not the metabolite-to-protein mapping step When you need all GWAS Catalog study overlaps regardless of significance — discarding Jaccard < 0.5 edges removes the majority of weakly overlapping study pairs by design

skills.description: Use when NPOmix KNN classification has produced candidate gene cluster family (GCF)-to-MS/MS spectrum links and you need a post-hoc confidence filter scored against PoDP-validated gene-metabolite links.
skills.name: jaccard-cooccurrence-filtering-of-bgc-msms-links
skills.search_text: jaccard-cooccurrence-filtering-of-bgc-msms-links Use when NPOmix KNN classification has produced candidate gene cluster family (GCF)-to-MS/MS spectrum links and you need a post-hoc confidence filter scored against PoDP-validated gene-metabolite links. The query genome has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset (e.g., a fungal species dissimilar to PoDP-derived training BGCs) — fingerprint columns will be empty and the filter yields no answer You need to distinguish isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — the correlation-based NPOmix linkage underlying the filter lacks that resolution Your dataset is very dissimilar to the current PoDP-derived training set — the reported precision may not be reproducible http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A confidence-filtering step for NPOmix candidate BGC–MS/MS links: compute the Jaccard co-occurrence index between thresholded BGC fingerprint vectors (maximum BiG-SCAPE similarity per genome) and MS/MS fingerprint vectors (maximum modified cosine score per sample) and retain links passing a 0.7 cutoff. Applying this filter with the similarity and biosynthetic class features enabled top-1 = 81.8% and top-10 = 92.9% precision on the PoDP validation set. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: A confidence-filtering step for NPOmix candidate BGC–MS/MS links: compute the Jaccard co-occurrence index between thresholded BGC fingerprint vectors (maximum BiG-SCAPE similarity per genome) and MS/MS fingerprint vectors (maximum modified cosine score per sample) and retain links passing a 0.7 cutoff. Applying this filter with the similarity and biosynthetic class features enabled top-1 = 81.8% and top-10 = 92.9% precision on the PoDP validation set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query genome has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset (e.g., a fungal species dissimilar to PoDP-derived training BGCs) — fingerprint columns will be empty and the filter yields no answer You need to distinguish isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — the correlation-based NPOmix linkage underlying the filter lacks that resolution Your dataset is very dissimilar to the current PoDP-derived training set — the reported precision may not be reproducible

skills.description: Use when NPOmix KNN votes have produced candidate GCF assignments for query MS/MS spectra and you must score link confidence (e.g. top-1 precision, Jaccard co-occurrence threshold) before accepting a spectrum-to-GCF link.
skills.name: jaccard-cooccurrence-link-validation
skills.search_text: jaccard-cooccurrence-link-validation Use when NPOmix KNN votes have produced candidate GCF assignments for query MS/MS spectra and you must score link confidence (e.g. top-1 precision, Jaccard co-occurrence threshold) before accepting a spectrum-to-GCF link. The query organism has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset (e.g. a fungal species) — NPOmix returns no answer, so there is nothing to validate. The goal is to distinguish isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — NPOmix, a correlation-based approach, lacks that resolution, so Jaccard co-occurrence cannot certify isomer identity. The link will be reported as a confirmed metabolite structure without further work — unvalidated links still require proper elucidation to confirm the metabolite's planar (2D) and absolute (3D) chemical structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Validates putative BGC-to-MS/MS links produced by NPOmix by measuring Jaccard co-occurrence between the GCF labels voted by the k-nearest-neighbor classifier and the expected (known or predicted) GCF labels, e.g. the 100% co-occurrence check for the m/z 780 siderophore link. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Validates putative BGC-to-MS/MS links produced by NPOmix by measuring Jaccard co-occurrence between the GCF labels voted by the k-nearest-neighbor classifier and the expected (known or predicted) GCF labels, e.g. the 100% co-occurrence check for the m/z 780 siderophore link.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query organism has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset (e.g. a fungal species) — NPOmix returns no answer, so there is nothing to validate. The goal is to distinguish isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — NPOmix, a correlation-based approach, lacks that resolution, so Jaccard co-occurrence cannot certify isomer identity. The link will be reported as a confirmed metabolite structure without further work — unvalidated links still require proper elucidation to confirm the metabolite's planar (2D) and absolute (3D) chemical structure.

skills.description: Use when you need pairwise structural similarity of lipid species from molecular graphs, e.g., to verify MCS/Jaccard overlap counts for structurally similar lipids or to quantify how double-bond position information changes lipid-lipid distances.
skills.name: jaccard-index-component-counting
skills.search_text: jaccard-index-component-counting Use when you need pairwise structural similarity of lipid species from molecular graphs, e.g., to verify MCS/Jaccard overlap counts for structurally similar lipids or to quantify how double-bond position information changes lipid-lipid distances. Input is already a feature/abundance table and the goal is purely quantitative comparison — Jaccard on molecular graphs ignores abundance, and the article notes that structural models are 'heavily influenced by low abundant lipid species' when quantitative data is mixed in elsewhere Lipid species names cannot be parsed to a structure (no recognizable shorthand/identifier), since graph construction requires a standardized parsed name via Goslin You only need exact lipid name/identifier matching between lipidomes — the article contrasts structural-similarity matching with 'only exact matches of the lipid species' names/identifiers' http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Computes pairwise structural similarity between lipid species by building their molecular graphs, finding the maximum common subgraph (LaWeCSE-based MCS), and dividing shared components (atoms and bonds) by united components via the Jaccard index — with explicit support for double-bond-position-aware vs DB-agnostic comparison modes. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes pairwise structural similarity between lipid species by building their molecular graphs, finding the maximum common subgraph (LaWeCSE-based MCS), and dividing shared components (atoms and bonds) by united components via the Jaccard index — with explicit support for double-bond-position-aware vs DB-agnostic comparison modes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/abundance table and the goal is purely quantitative comparison — Jaccard on molecular graphs ignores abundance, and the article notes that structural models are 'heavily influenced by low abundant lipid species' when quantitative data is mixed in elsewhere Lipid species names cannot be parsed to a structure (no recognizable shorthand/identifier), since graph construction requires a standardized parsed name via Goslin You only need exact lipid name/identifier matching between lipidomes — the article contrasts structural-similarity matching with 'only exact matches of the lipid species' names/identifiers'

skills.description: Use when comparing the metabolisms of two organisms selected from the KEGG database quantitatively: KGML files are available, reaction sets per pathway can be reconstructed, and global similarity indexes (Psim, PsimW, Csim) are the desired output.
skills.name: jaccard-index-metabolic-reaction-comparison
skills.search_text: jaccard-index-metabolic-reaction-comparison Use when comparing the metabolisms of two organisms selected from the KEGG database quantitatively: KGML files are available, reaction sets per pathway can be reconstructed, and global similarity indexes (Psim, PsimW, Csim) are the desired output. The input is raw genomic or experimental data rather than KEGG-registered organisms — MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and the reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database. The pathways of interest are physical/pathway-of-pathways maps rather than reaction pathways and no interpretation of degenerate SimPi = 0 or SimPi = 1 cases is planned. A single organism's network is needed without a pairwise comparison partner — this skill is defined for two-organism (pairwise) comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3370 A two-level metabolic similarity procedure from the MetNet methodology (PLOS ONE, 2021) in which local pathway similarity is computed as a Jaccard index over the reaction sets of two KEGG organisms' pathways, then aggregated into the global indexes Psim (arithmetic mean), PsimW (weighted mean) and the combined index Csim. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: A two-level metabolic similarity procedure from the MetNet methodology (PLOS ONE, 2021) in which local pathway similarity is computed as a Jaccard index over the reaction sets of two KEGG organisms' pathways, then aggregated into the global indexes Psim (arithmetic mean), PsimW (weighted mean) and the combined index Csim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw genomic or experimental data rather than KEGG-registered organisms — MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and the reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database. The pathways of interest are physical/pathway-of-pathways maps rather than reaction pathways and no interpretation of degenerate SimPi = 0 or SimPi = 1 cases is planned. A single organism's network is needed without a pairwise comparison partner — this skill is defined for two-organism (pairwise) comparison.

skills.description: Use when an IFM image has been warped into the MALDI MSI frame (e.g. via ANTs SyNRA in msiFlow's msi_if_registration_flow) and you need a quantitative overlap metric to validate registration accuracy.
skills.name: jaccard-mask-overlap-evaluation
skills.search_text: jaccard-mask-overlap-evaluation Use when an IFM image has been warped into the MALDI MSI frame (e.g. via ANTs SyNRA in msiFlow's msi_if_registration_flow) and you need a quantitative overlap metric to validate registration accuracy. Registration relies on landmark-based features or laser ablation marks present in both modalities — this mask-overlap metric is specific to msiFlow's automated consecutive-section registration and may underestimate accuracy of feature-based methods The MSI dataset lacks a segmentable, morphologically distinct structure (e.g. urothelium) that can be segmented in both modalities, so no comparable masks exist Goal is lipid annotation or molecular interpretation rather than registration validation — msiFlow explicitly does not include an annotation or interpretation step http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Quantitatively validates automated IFM-to-MALDI MSI image co-registration by computing the Jaccard index (intersection over union) between a transformed urothelial mask from registered IFM and a reference MSI-derived urothelial mask; msiFlow's registration of consecutive tissue sections was reported to achieve an average Jaccard of 0.8. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Quantitatively validates automated IFM-to-MALDI MSI image co-registration by computing the Jaccard index (intersection over union) between a transformed urothelial mask from registered IFM and a reference MSI-derived urothelial mask; msiFlow's registration of consecutive tissue sections was reported to achieve an average Jaccard of 0.8.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Registration relies on landmark-based features or laser ablation marks present in both modalities — this mask-overlap metric is specific to msiFlow's automated consecutive-section registration and may underestimate accuracy of feature-based methods The MSI dataset lacks a segmentable, morphologically distinct structure (e.g. urothelium) that can be segmented in both modalities, so no comparable masks exist Goal is lipid annotation or molecular interpretation rather than registration validation — msiFlow explicitly does not include an annotation or interpretation step

skills.description: Use when lipid species names must be compared by molecular structure rather than exact name matching, e.g. to build structural distance matrices across heterogeneous lipidomes from csv/xlsx or mzTab-M lipidomics tables.
skills.name: jaccard-maximum-common-subgraph-similarity
skills.search_text: jaccard-maximum-common-subgraph-similarity Use when lipid species names must be compared by molecular structure rather than exact name matching, e.g. to build structural distance matrices across heterogeneous lipidomes from csv/xlsx or mzTab-M lipidomics tables. The analysis only requires comparing lipidomes by exact matches of lipid species names/identifiers rather than structural similarity Quantitative abundance effects dominate the question — this structural distance alone is heavily influenced by low abundant lipid species unless abundances are later added and normalized to the variance of the first PC Input lipid names cannot be parsed/standardized by Goslin (unsupported lipid name dialects) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Computes pairwise structural similarity between lipid species by combining the maximum common subgraph (LaWeCSE) approach with the Jaccard index on parsed molecular structures, producing the n x n distance matrix that underpins LipidSpace's structural space model. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes pairwise structural similarity between lipid species by combining the maximum common subgraph (LaWeCSE) approach with the Jaccard index on parsed molecular structures, producing the n x n distance matrix that underpins LipidSpace's structural space model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only requires comparing lipidomes by exact matches of lipid species names/identifiers rather than structural similarity Quantitative abundance effects dominate the question — this structural distance alone is heavily influenced by low abundant lipid species unless abundances are later added and normalized to the variance of the first PC Input lipid names cannot be parsed/standardized by Goslin (unsupported lipid name dialects)

skills.description: Use when MASST matches of synthesized compounds have been joined to ReDU sample metadata (biospecimen/tissue, health phenotype) and you need to test whether sample groups cluster by health status or tissue based on shared detected conjugates.
skills.name: jaccard-ordination-health-status
skills.search_text: jaccard-ordination-health-status Use when MASST matches of synthesized compounds have been joined to ReDU sample metadata (biospecimen/tissue, health phenotype) and you need to test whether sample groups cluster by health status or tissue based on shared detected conjugates. The matches carry no ReDU metadata (biospecimen/health phenotype), so no phenotype grouping can be formed for ordination The question requires quantitative abundance differences rather than presence/absence of shared conjugates — Jaccard discards intensity information Input is raw LC-MS/MS data rather than already-curated MASST match results; run MASST matching first http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes Jaccard distances between samples/groups based on shared bile acid conjugate MASST matches and runs ordination to reveal clustering by health status (e.g. IBD vs healthy), as used to aggregate ReDU-metadata-annotated public metabolomics matches in reverse metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41586-023-06906-8
skills.summary: Computes Jaccard distances between samples/groups based on shared bile acid conjugate MASST matches and runs ordination to reveal clustering by health status (e.g. IBD vs healthy), as used to aggregate ReDU-metadata-annotated public metabolomics matches in reverse metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matches carry no ReDU metadata (biospecimen/health phenotype), so no phenotype grouping can be formed for ordination The question requires quantitative abundance differences rather than presence/absence of shared conjugates — Jaccard discards intensity information Input is raw LC-MS/MS data rather than already-curated MASST match results; run MASST matching first

skills.description: Use when a set of significant 1D NMR peaks (ppm values) has been clustered by Pearson correlation and you must rank HMDB metabolite matches by how well their expected peak patterns overlap the cluster.
skills.name: jaccard-overlap-scoring-of-peak-sets
skills.search_text: jaccard-overlap-scoring-of-peak-sets Use when a set of significant 1D NMR peaks (ppm values) has been clustered by Pearson correlation and you must rank HMDB metabolite matches by how well their expected peak patterns overlap the cluster. The input is raw spectra rather than a peak/feature table — the speaq 2.0 peak-picking and grouping steps must run first The goal is quantitation or spectral alignment (CluPA) rather than metabolite identification via database matching Peaks are not grouped/clustered, so no peak-index set exists to compare against HMDB entries with the Jaccard index http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Scores candidate metabolite annotations from HMDB searches by the Jaccard index over shared peak indices between a correlation-clustered group of significant NMR peaks and the peaks of matched HMDB entries, enabling ranking of database hits for 1D NMR metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Scores candidate metabolite annotations from HMDB searches by the Jaccard index over shared peak indices between a correlation-clustered group of significant NMR peaks and the peaks of matched HMDB entries, enabling ranking of database hits for 1D NMR metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw spectra rather than a peak/feature table — the speaq 2.0 peak-picking and grouping steps must run first The goal is quantitation or spectral alignment (CluPA) rather than metabolite identification via database matching Peaks are not grouped/clustered, so no peak-index set exists to compare against HMDB entries with the Jaccard index

skills.description: Use when ranking candidate compounds for an unknown GC/EI-MS analyte where cosine spectrum similarity alone leaves the true compound below rank 1, and DeepEI-predicted fingerprints (msp-merged) are available for the analyte and enumerated candidates.
skills.name: jaccard-peak-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: jaccard-peak-overlap-scoring Use when ranking candidate compounds for an unknown GC/EI-MS analyte where cosine spectrum similarity alone leaves the true compound below rank 1, and DeepEI-predicted fingerprints (msp-merged) are available for the analyte and enumerated candidates. When the analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectra in NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG libraries, since conventional library screening, not integrated scoring, applies When the candidate structure or fingerprint is unknown/unpredictable — existing in silico prediction methods (e.g., NEIMS) are limited to cases where the chemical structure of the NPS is already known When fingerprints cannot be produced or merged into the msp entries, since the Jaccard term has no input Integrates Jaccard similarity of molecular fingerprints with cosine/spectral (SMSF) similarity to re-rank candidate matches, raising the proportion of correct top-1 predictions from below 40% to more than 50% on SWGDRUG test substances in the PS2MS workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Integrates Jaccard similarity of molecular fingerprints with cosine/spectral (SMSF) similarity to re-rank candidate matches, raising the proportion of correct top-1 predictions from below 40% to more than 50% on SWGDRUG test substances in the PS2MS workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectra in NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG libraries, since conventional library screening, not integrated scoring, applies When the candidate structure or fingerprint is unknown/unpredictable — existing in silico prediction methods (e.g., NEIMS) are limited to cases where the chemical structure of the NPS is already known When fingerprints cannot be produced or merged into the msp entries, since the Jaccard term has no input

skills.description: Use when comparing the reaction content of corresponding KEGG reference pathways in two organisms, and you need a normalized per-pathway similarity in [0,1] computed over reaction sets or multisets.
skills.name: jaccard-reaction-set-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: jaccard-reaction-set-overlap-analysis Use when comparing the reaction content of corresponding KEGG reference pathways in two organisms, and you need a normalized per-pathway similarity in [0,1] computed over reaction sets or multisets. When the goal is structural/topological comparison of pathway graphs (node connections via shared compounds) — use the SimSi index instead When only one organism is involved; the Jaccard overlap is undefined without a second organism's reaction set When metabolic networks are reconstructed from sources other than KEGG (e.g. BioCyc, BioModels, genomic data), since MetNet's parsing and pathway identification are KEGG-based http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Computes the functional-level pathway similarity SimPi as a Jaccard index over reaction sets or multisets reconstructed from KEGG KGML data, so two organisms' metabolic networks can be compared pathway by pathway. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Computes the functional-level pathway similarity SimPi as a Jaccard index over reaction sets or multisets reconstructed from KEGG KGML data, so two organisms' metabolic networks can be compared pathway by pathway.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is structural/topological comparison of pathway graphs (node connections via shared compounds) — use the SimSi index instead When only one organism is involved; the Jaccard overlap is undefined without a second organism's reaction set When metabolic networks are reconstructed from sources other than KEGG (e.g. BioCyc, BioModels, genomic data), since MetNet's parsing and pathway identification are KEGG-based

skills.description: Use when evaluating a sparse-positive molecular site-of-metabolism classifier (e.g. ~5% reactive bonds) where accuracy is mis and per-class/isoform Jaccard scores from external cross-validation are the appropriate metric.
skills.name: jaccard-score-cross-validation
skills.search_text: jaccard-score-cross-validation Use when evaluating a sparse-positive molecular site-of-metabolism classifier (e.g. ~5% reactive bonds) where accuracy is mis and per-class/isoform Jaccard scores from external cross-validation are the appropriate metric. When the goal is end-to-end metabolite/byproduct prediction rather than bond-site classifier evaluation — use the full CyProduct pipeline (CypReact filter → CypBoM → MetaboGen) instead When classes are balanced or the positive class dominates — the cost-sensitive β calibration (0/0/1/β cost matrix) and threshold 1/(β+1) are designed for the ~5% reactive / 95% non-reactive imbalance and may distort well-balanced problems When the input is a generic feature table with no molecular bond structure — the Jaccard-over-bonds framing and per-isoform folds assume η−η bond-level instances http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluation methodology from CyProduct's CypBoM module: score bond-site classifiers with the Jaccard score TP/(TP+FN+FP) under external 5-fold cross-validation, using internal 5-fold CV over a cost-sensitive super-learner grid to avoid accuracy bias on 5%/95% imbalanced η−η bond data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Evaluation methodology from CyProduct's CypBoM module: score bond-site classifiers with the Jaccard score TP/(TP+FN+FP) under external 5-fold cross-validation, using internal 5-fold CV over a cost-sensitive super-learner grid to avoid accuracy bias on 5%/95% imbalanced η−η bond data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is end-to-end metabolite/byproduct prediction rather than bond-site classifier evaluation — use the full CyProduct pipeline (CypReact filter → CypBoM → MetaboGen) instead When classes are balanced or the positive class dominates — the cost-sensitive β calibration (0/0/1/β cost matrix) and threshold 1/(β+1) are designed for the ~5% reactive / 95% non-reactive imbalance and may distort well-balanced problems When the input is a generic feature table with no molecular bond structure — the Jaccard-over-bonds framing and per-isoform folds assume η−η bond-level instances

skills.description: Use when evaluating a bond- or site-level predictor whose output is a set of predicted locations (e.g., BoMX−Y pairs or SoMs) per molecule, and you need a single per-class score that penalizes false positives and false negatives symmetrically.
skills.name: jaccard-score-metric-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-score-metric-computation Use when evaluating a bond- or site-level predictor whose output is a set of predicted locations (e.g., BoMX−Y pairs or SoMs) per molecule, and you need a single per-class score that penalizes false positives and false negatives symmetrically. When the prediction task is binary per molecule (e.g., CypReact's reactant/non-reactant classification) rather than set-valued per bond/atom — precision/recall or accuracy is more appropriate there When comparing tools evaluated on different datasets or with different per-instance matching rules; the Jaccard comparison (e.g., CypBoM vs FAME2 25% better) is only valid when both tools score identical [compound, bond] instances on the same dataset (EBoMD/HDFAME) http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes the Jaccard score TP/(TP+FN+FP) as the primary performance metric for set-valued predictions such as reactive bonds-of-metabolism (BoMX−Y) or sites-of-metabolism, where hits must match both the compound and the specific atom/bond. Used in the CypBoM/CyProduct evaluation to score per-enzyme prediction across the nine major human CYP450 isoforms. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Computes the Jaccard score TP/(TP+FN+FP) as the primary performance metric for set-valued predictions such as reactive bonds-of-metabolism (BoMX−Y) or sites-of-metabolism, where hits must match both the compound and the specific atom/bond. Used in the CypBoM/CyProduct evaluation to score per-enzyme prediction across the nine major human CYP450 isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the prediction task is binary per molecule (e.g., CypReact's reactant/non-reactant classification) rather than set-valued per bond/atom — precision/recall or accuracy is more appropriate there When comparing tools evaluated on different datasets or with different per-instance matching rules; the Jaccard comparison (e.g., CypBoM vs FAME2 25% better) is only valid when both tools score identical [compound, bond] instances on the same dataset (EBoMD/HDFAME)

skills.description: Use when two organisms' metabolisms have been reconstructed from KEGG KGML into per-pathway reaction sets and you need quantitative local and global functional similarity between them.
skills.name: jaccard-set-similarity-on-reaction-sets
skills.search_text: jaccard-set-similarity-on-reaction-sets Use when two organisms' metabolisms have been reconstructed from KEGG KGML into per-pathway reaction sets and you need quantitative local and global functional similarity between them. The organism data is not in KEGG and cannot be retrieved as KGML — MetNet's reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which the authors note 'can be a limit wrt. the represented information' You have raw annotated genomic data instead of KEGG pathway entries — MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data You need structural (topological graph) similarity rather than functional reaction-set similarity — use the Ssim/Csim structural-level indexes instead of Psim/PsimW http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Computes the local pathway similarity index SimPi as the Jaccard ratio |Ri ∩ Ri′| / |Ri ∪ Ri′| over reaction sets of KEGG reference pathways, then aggregates per-pathway values into the global indexes Psim (arithmetic mean) and PsimW (mean weighted by |Ri ∪ Ri′|) to compare two organisms' metabolisms. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Computes the local pathway similarity index SimPi as the Jaccard ratio |Ri ∩ Ri′| / |Ri ∪ Ri′| over reaction sets of KEGG reference pathways, then aggregates per-pathway values into the global indexes Psim (arithmetic mean) and PsimW (mean weighted by |Ri ∪ Ri′|) to compare two organisms' metabolisms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism data is not in KEGG and cannot be retrieved as KGML — MetNet's reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which the authors note 'can be a limit wrt. the represented information' You have raw annotated genomic data instead of KEGG pathway entries — MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data You need structural (topological graph) similarity rather than functional reaction-set similarity — use the Ssim/Csim structural-level indexes instead of Psim/PsimW

skills.description: Use when scoring isomer-pair MS/MS similarity from multi-collision-energy spectra (e.g., NCE 1–100%) to build I/N-ratio-based identification criteria, or when comparing Jaccard vs dot product/entropy sensitivity-specificity on spectral libraries like CQMD.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-computation Use when scoring isomer-pair MS/MS similarity from multi-collision-energy spectra (e.g., NCE 1–100%) to build I/N-ratio-based identification criteria, or when comparing Jaccard vs dot product/entropy sensitivity-specificity on spectral libraries like CQMD. You only have single-CE (stepped NCE 20/40/60% or one NCE) reference spectra — cross-sectional dot product/entropy matching is the appropriate baseline, and longitudinal profiling gains require multi-CE acquisitions Input spectra have not passed the upstream pipeline (spectrum filtering, invalid fragment removal, fragment rationality assessment); the CQMD/CQMU database must be constructed first Candidate compounds lack isomer counterparts in the reference library, so longitudinal fragment-profile matching cannot distinguish them http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 An optimized Jaccard similarity algorithm for scoring MS/MS spectral matches using longitudinal fragment profiles (LFPs) acquired at multiple collision energies, treating predominant and minute fragments independently rather than weighting them together as in cross-sectional dot product or entropy scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: An optimized Jaccard similarity algorithm for scoring MS/MS spectral matches using longitudinal fragment profiles (LFPs) acquired at multiple collision energies, treating predominant and minute fragments independently rather than weighting them together as in cross-sectional dot product or entropy scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have single-CE (stepped NCE 20/40/60% or one NCE) reference spectra — cross-sectional dot product/entropy matching is the appropriate baseline, and longitudinal profiling gains require multi-CE acquisitions Input spectra have not passed the upstream pipeline (spectrum filtering, invalid fragment removal, fragment rationality assessment); the CQMD/CQMU database must be constructed first Candidate compounds lack isomer counterparts in the reference library, so longitudinal fragment-profile matching cannot distinguish them

skills.description: Use when quantifying metabolite-content overlap between pathway pairs — e.g., building a pairwise Jaccard redundancy matrix across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways pathways stored in RaMP to identify which database pairs show the largest overlap.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-computation Use when quantifying metabolite-content overlap between pathway pairs — e.g., building a pairwise Jaccard redundancy matrix across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways pathways stored in RaMP to identify which database pairs show the largest overlap. When the goal is pathway overrepresentation (Fisher) testing rather than pathway–pathway redundancy quantification — use runFisherTest/runCombinedFisherTest instead When overlap should be computed on combined analytes (genes and metabolites together) rather than metabolites-only — the 'together' parameter must not be set to metabolites-only in that case When a single analyte's pathway annotations are needed (e.g., metabolite-to-pathway lookup) — rampFastCata or getPathwayFromAnalyte is the appropriate query rather than an overlap matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Computes pairwise metabolite-content overlap between pathways using the Jaccard index (shared metabolites divided by union size), assembling per-pair scores into full overlap matrices via RaMP's compute_overlap_matrix and updateOverlapMatrix functions to quantify redundancy across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo8010016
skills.summary: Computes pairwise metabolite-content overlap between pathways using the Jaccard index (shared metabolites divided by union size), assembling per-pair scores into full overlap matrices via RaMP's compute_overlap_matrix and updateOverlapMatrix functions to quantify redundancy across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pathway overrepresentation (Fisher) testing rather than pathway–pathway redundancy quantification — use runFisherTest/runCombinedFisherTest instead When overlap should be computed on combined analytes (genes and metabolites together) rather than metabolites-only — the 'together' parameter must not be set to metabolites-only in that case When a single analyte's pathway annotations are needed (e.g., metabolite-to-pathway lookup) — rampFastCata or getPathwayFromAnalyte is the appropriate query rather than an overlap matrix

skills.description: Use when the goal is to quantify how similar the metabolisms of two (or more) KEGG organisms are, either locally (per reference pathway) or globally (whole metabolism), e.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-index-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-index-computation Use when the goal is to quantify how similar the metabolisms of two (or more) KEGG organisms are, either locally (per reference pathway) or globally (whole metabolism), e. The organism is not available in KEGG or you need a reconstruction from non-KEGG sources: MetNet's reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which limits the represented information. You want to reconstruct networks from raw or newly annotated genomic data: MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and would need significant extension. You need per-reaction multiplicity-aware similarity but the pathway reaction content is only meaningfully compared as presence/absence sets — in that case reconsider the 'set' vs 'multiset' choice, but do not apply this skill to non-pathway data (e.g. plain gene lists). http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Computes Jaccard-based similarity indexes (Ssim, Psim, PsimW, Csim) between the metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms, as implemented by the MetNet tool. Pathways are represented as sets of reactions and compared pathway-by-pathway, then aggregated into global whole-metabolism scores used for pairwise or multi-organism clustering analyses. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Computes Jaccard-based similarity indexes (Ssim, Psim, PsimW, Csim) between the metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms, as implemented by the MetNet tool. Pathways are represented as sets of reactions and compared pathway-by-pathway, then aggregated into global whole-metabolism scores used for pairwise or multi-organism clustering analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism is not available in KEGG or you need a reconstruction from non-KEGG sources: MetNet's reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which limits the represented information. You want to reconstruct networks from raw or newly annotated genomic data: MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and would need significant extension. You need per-reaction multiplicity-aware similarity but the pathway reaction content is only meaningfully compared as presence/absence sets — in that case reconsider the 'set' vs 'multiset' choice, but do not apply this skill to non-pathway data (e.g. plain gene lists).

skills.description: Use when you have binary gene membership sets (e.g., per-tissue DE gene lists from the MoTrPAC rat EET study) and need to measure how concordant or tissue-specific the sets are across conditions or tissues.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-matrix-computation Use when you have binary gene membership sets (e.g., per-tissue DE gene lists from the MoTrPAC rat EET study) and need to measure how concordant or tissue-specific the sets are across conditions or tissues. You need signed concordance of direction-of-effect (up vs down regulation) rather than binary gene-set overlap — Jaccard ignores log2FC sign Your DE sets are not ortholog-mapped across species; comparing raw rat gene IDs to human gene IDs will inflate/deflate overlap spuriously The input is continuous gene-level statistics (p-values, z-scores) rather than discrete membership sets — use correlation-based methods instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies cross-tissue concordance of exercise-responsive transcription by computing pairwise Jaccard similarity (|A∩B|/|A∪B|) between differentially expressed gene sets from the 15 tissues of the MoTrPAC PASS1B rat endurance exercise training (EET) study, after mapping rat genes to human orthologs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Quantifies cross-tissue concordance of exercise-responsive transcription by computing pairwise Jaccard similarity (|A∩B|/|A∪B|) between differentially expressed gene sets from the 15 tissues of the MoTrPAC PASS1B rat endurance exercise training (EET) study, after mapping rat genes to human orthologs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need signed concordance of direction-of-effect (up vs down regulation) rather than binary gene-set overlap — Jaccard ignores log2FC sign Your DE sets are not ortholog-mapped across species; comparing raw rat gene IDs to human gene IDs will inflate/deflate overlap spuriously The input is continuous gene-level statistics (p-values, z-scores) rather than discrete membership sets — use correlation-based methods instead

skills.description: Use when query MS/MS spectra are acquired at multiple collision energies and must be matched to multi-CE reference spectra (e.g. Exploris 480 queries vs. CQMD Exploris 120 references) to call metabolite identifications under Figure 2 cutoff criteria.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-scoring-multi-collision-energy-fragments
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-scoring-multi-collision-energy-fragments Use when query MS/MS spectra are acquired at multiple collision energies and must be matched to multi-CE reference spectra (e.g. Exploris 480 queries vs. CQMD Exploris 120 references) to call metabolite identifications under Figure 2 cutoff criteria. Query or reference spectra were acquired at only a single collision energy, so no longitudinal fragment profile (fragment intensity across multiple CEs) can be constructed The task is generic cross-sectional spectral similarity scoring against public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, METLIN) rather than longitudinal profiling-based metabolite identification against a multi-CE reference set Reference spectra lack the matched 13-CE / stepped NCE 20/40/60% acquisition scheme required to align fragment profiles with the query spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Scores query MS/MS spectra against a multi-collision-energy reference database (CQMD, ~180,000 spectra at 13 distinct CEs and stepped NCE 20/40/60%) using an optimized Jaccard similarity over longitudinal fragment profiles that weighs predominant and minute fragments independently. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: Scores query MS/MS spectra against a multi-collision-energy reference database (CQMD, ~180,000 spectra at 13 distinct CEs and stepped NCE 20/40/60%) using an optimized Jaccard similarity over longitudinal fragment profiles that weighs predominant and minute fragments independently.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query or reference spectra were acquired at only a single collision energy, so no longitudinal fragment profile (fragment intensity across multiple CEs) can be constructed The task is generic cross-sectional spectral similarity scoring against public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, METLIN) rather than longitudinal profiling-based metabolite identification against a multi-CE reference set Reference spectra lack the matched 13-CE / stepped NCE 20/40/60% acquisition scheme required to align fragment profiles with the query spectra

skills.description: Use when annotating metabolites from MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (e.g. 13 CEs or stepped NCE 20/40/60%), where cross-sectional scoring misranks isomers with similar predominant fragments.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-scoring-of-longitudinal-fragment-profiles
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-scoring-of-longitudinal-fragment-profiles Use when annotating metabolites from MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (e.g. 13 CEs or stepped NCE 20/40/60%), where cross-sectional scoring misranks isomers with similar predominant fragments. When MS/MS spectra are only available at a single collision energy — no longitudinal profiles can be constructed and cross-sectional matching (dot product or optimal entropy) should be used instead When the goal is feature detection or peak picking rather than spectral matching of already-extracted features against a candidate library http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 An optimized Jaccard similarity algorithm that scores metabolite candidates by comparing experimental versus reference longitudinal fragment profiles (LFPs) — relative ion intensities of each fragment across multiple collision energies — treating predominant and minute fragments independently rather than pooling them as in cross-sectional spectral matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: An optimized Jaccard similarity algorithm that scores metabolite candidates by comparing experimental versus reference longitudinal fragment profiles (LFPs) — relative ion intensities of each fragment across multiple collision energies — treating predominant and minute fragments independently rather than pooling them as in cross-sectional spectral matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When MS/MS spectra are only available at a single collision energy — no longitudinal profiles can be constructed and cross-sectional matching (dot product or optimal entropy) should be used instead When the goal is feature detection or peak picking rather than spectral matching of already-extracted features against a candidate library

skills.description: Use when benchmarking spectral similarity or alignment algorithms and a per-pair structural similarity ground truth is needed for compound pairs with known SMILES from GNPS library metadata or MassBank records.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-scoring-of-molecular-structures
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-scoring-of-molecular-structures Use when benchmarking spectral similarity or alignment algorithms and a per-pair structural similarity ground truth is needed for compound pairs with known SMILES from GNPS library metadata or MassBank records. The analysis goal is spectral similarity scoring itself (e.g., SIMILE z_test, modified cosine) rather than constructing the structural ground-truth benchmark Compound structures lack parseable SMILES, since RDKit molecule objects cannot be built and the MCS search cannot run A ring-aware substructure definition is required, since this skill fixes ringMatchesRingOnly=False http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Computes an all-vs-all maximum common substructure (MCS) Jaccard similarity matrix from compound SMILES using RDKit, producing the structural ground truth against which spectral alignment algorithms (e.g., SIMILE, modified cosine) are benchmarked. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-30118-9
skills.summary: Computes an all-vs-all maximum common substructure (MCS) Jaccard similarity matrix from compound SMILES using RDKit, producing the structural ground truth against which spectral alignment algorithms (e.g., SIMILE, modified cosine) are benchmarked.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is spectral similarity scoring itself (e.g., SIMILE z_test, modified cosine) rather than constructing the structural ground-truth benchmark Compound structures lack parseable SMILES, since RDKit molecule objects cannot be built and the MCS search cannot run A ring-aware substructure definition is required, since this skill fixes ringMatchesRingOnly=False

skills.description: Use when experimental and reference MS/MS spectra are available at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and you must identify metabolites or quantify correct-match rates against an isomer-rich library.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-spectrum-scoring
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-spectrum-scoring Use when experimental and reference MS/MS spectra are available at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and you must identify metabolites or quantify correct-match rates against an isomer-rich library. Only single-collision-energy MS/MS spectra are available — without multi-CE acquisition, longitudinal fragment profiles cannot be built and cross-sectional dot-product/entropy scoring is the fallback The input is already a feature/annotation table with no raw MS/MS spectra to re-score No reference library of spectra at matching collision energies exists, so Jaccard scores would be computed against incomparable profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Scores experimental MS/MS spectra against a reference library by optimizing the Jaccard similarity algorithm for longitudinal fragment profiles (relative ion intensities of each fragment across multiple collision energies), treating predominant and minute fragments independently to reduce isomer misidentification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: Scores experimental MS/MS spectra against a reference library by optimizing the Jaccard similarity algorithm for longitudinal fragment profiles (relative ion intensities of each fragment across multiple collision energies), treating predominant and minute fragments independently to reduce isomer misidentification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only single-collision-energy MS/MS spectra are available — without multi-CE acquisition, longitudinal fragment profiles cannot be built and cross-sectional dot-product/entropy scoring is the fallback The input is already a feature/annotation table with no raw MS/MS spectra to re-score No reference library of spectra at matching collision energies exists, so Jaccard scores would be computed against incomparable profiles

skills.description: Use when QIIME principal coordinates files from replicate (jackknifed) beta diversity analyses plus a metadata mapping file must be rendered as per-sample confidence ellipsoids in an interactive 3D PCoA visualization.
skills.name: jackknife-resampling-visualization
skills.search_text: jackknife-resampling-visualization Use when QIIME principal coordinates files from replicate (jackknifed) beta diversity analyses plus a metadata mapping file must be rendered as per-sample confidence ellipsoids in an interactive 3D PCoA visualization. Input is a single (non-replicated) PCoA coordinate file with no jackknife resamples — there is no dispersion to define per-sample confidence regions, so plain point plotting suffices. The goal is upstream computation of jackknifed beta diversity distances rather than visualization; this skill only renders already-computed replicate PCoA coordinates via EMPeror. The analysis target is not microbial community beta diversity data (e.g. no QIIME-format principal coordinates or mapping file), since EMPeror is specifically tailored to microbial ecologists' QIIME outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Visualize jackknifed beta diversity resamples as per-sample confidence regions (spheroids/ellipsoids) in EMPeror's 3D WebGL PCoA plots, so researchers can assess the statistical confidence in clustering of microbial community samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/2047-217x-2-16
skills.summary: Visualize jackknifed beta diversity resamples as per-sample confidence regions (spheroids/ellipsoids) in EMPeror's 3D WebGL PCoA plots, so researchers can assess the statistical confidence in clustering of microbial community samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single (non-replicated) PCoA coordinate file with no jackknife resamples — there is no dispersion to define per-sample confidence regions, so plain point plotting suffices. The goal is upstream computation of jackknifed beta diversity distances rather than visualization; this skill only renders already-computed replicate PCoA coordinates via EMPeror. The analysis target is not microbial community beta diversity data (e.g. no QIIME-format principal coordinates or mapping file), since EMPeror is specifically tailored to microbial ecologists' QIIME outputs.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics study has preprocessed concentration data, a defined interaction network, and the goal is to quantify metabolite interactions via Jacobian matrices for specific conditions (e.g., 6C vs 16C).
skills.name: jacobian-matrix-computation-from-metabolic-interaction-networks
skills.search_text: jacobian-matrix-computation-from-metabolic-interaction-networks Use when a metabolomics study has preprocessed concentration data, a defined interaction network, and the goal is to quantify metabolite interactions via Jacobian matrices for specific conditions (e.g., 6C vs 16C). When only raw metabolite abundance data is available without an interaction network or MetaboAnalyst-derived MIN (Jacobian computation requires `interactions_fin`) When the study objective is simple statistical differential analysis rather than dynamic interaction modeling (MInfer focuses on Jacobian-based interaction inference) http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes condition-specific Jacobian matrices from covariance matrices and a metabolite interaction network (MIN) using the MInfer R package, enabling dynamic interaction analysis of metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cmpb.2025.108672
skills.summary: Computes condition-specific Jacobian matrices from covariance matrices and a metabolite interaction network (MIN) using the MInfer R package, enabling dynamic interaction analysis of metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only raw metabolite abundance data is available without an interaction network or MetaboAnalyst-derived MIN (Jacobian computation requires `interactions_fin`) When the study objective is simple statistical differential analysis rather than dynamic interaction modeling (MInfer focuses on Jacobian-based interaction inference)

skills.description: Use when raw metabolomic data or MetaboAnalyst-derived metabolite inputs need to be converted into a network of dynamic metabolite interactions via Jacobian matrix computation, with topology metrics.
skills.name: jacobian-matrix-network-inference
skills.search_text: jacobian-matrix-network-inference Use when raw metabolomic data or MetaboAnalyst-derived metabolite inputs need to be converted into a network of dynamic metabolite interactions via Jacobian matrix computation, with topology metrics. When the goal is generic metabolomics QC or peak annotation rather than network-level interaction inference — MInfer is designed to derive a dynamic MIN, not a standard feature table. When input data is already a finalized interaction network with no need for Jacobian re-derivation. When there is only a single metabolite/timepoint with insufficient variation to generate a meaningful covariance matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infers a dynamic metabolite interaction network (MIN) from metabolomics data by computing the Jacobian matrix that encodes interactions between metabolites, then deriving topology statistics (nodes, edges, average neighbors, path length, clustering, density). Implemented via the MInfer R package, which bridges MetaboAnalyst outputs to Jacobian analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cmpb.2025.108672
skills.summary: Infers a dynamic metabolite interaction network (MIN) from metabolomics data by computing the Jacobian matrix that encodes interactions between metabolites, then deriving topology statistics (nodes, edges, average neighbors, path length, clustering, density). Implemented via the MInfer R package, which bridges MetaboAnalyst outputs to Jacobian analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is generic metabolomics QC or peak annotation rather than network-level interaction inference — MInfer is designed to derive a dynamic MIN, not a standard feature table. When input data is already a finalized interaction network with no need for Jacobian re-derivation. When there is only a single metabolite/timepoint with insufficient variation to generate a meaningful covariance matrix.
