Input is only a peak table or raw m/z list that has not yet been annotated and network-reconstructed via PIUMet — annotate peaks and run the Steiner forest step first Input is a single analyte type only (metabolites or proteins alone) where a standard over-representation analysis, not joint metabolite-protein pathway enrichment, is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Joint pathway enrichment that submits metabolites and proteins from a reconstructed disease metabolite-protein network to MetaboAnalyst, identifying metabolic pathways significantly perturbed in disease (here LUAD) at FDR < 0.05. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-51433-3
skills.summary: Joint pathway enrichment that submits metabolites and proteins from a reconstructed disease metabolite-protein network to MetaboAnalyst, identifying metabolic pathways significantly perturbed in disease (here LUAD) at FDR < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only a peak table or raw m/z list that has not yet been annotated and network-reconstructed via PIUMet — annotate peaks and run the Steiner forest step first Input is a single analyte type only (metabolites or proteins alone) where a standard over-representation analysis, not joint metabolite-protein pathway enrichment, is appropriate

skills.description: Use when an aligned JPA feature table must be quality-checked by extraction level — e.g. comparing quantitative precision of MS2-recognition (MR) rescued features vs conventional peak-picking (PP) features across replicate samples before statistical analysis.
skills.name: jpa-feature-level-stratification-pp-mr
skills.search_text: jpa-feature-level-stratification-pp-mr Use when an aligned JPA feature table must be quality-checked by extraction level — e.g. comparing quantitative precision of MS2-recognition (MR) rescued features vs conventional peak-picking (PP) features across replicate samples before statistical analysis. Input is a raw unaligned feature table (output of XCMS.featureTable/custom.featureTable) — sample alignment must be performed first per the JPA workflow Input is full-scan or DIA data processed without MR extraction — no 'level' == 'MR' features exist, so the PP-vs-MR stratification is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Stratifies aligned JPA feature tables by the 'level' column into PP (XCMS peak-picking) and MR (MS2-recognition) features, then computes per-group replicate precision (RSD%) to verify that rescued MR features remain quantitative enough (<15% RSD, ~3 pp above PP) for downstream statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212
skills.summary: Stratifies aligned JPA feature tables by the 'level' column into PP (XCMS peak-picking) and MR (MS2-recognition) features, then computes per-group replicate precision (RSD%) to verify that rescued MR features remain quantitative enough (<15% RSD, ~3 pp above PP) for downstream statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw unaligned feature table (output of XCMS.featureTable/custom.featureTable) — sample alignment must be performed first per the JPA workflow Input is full-scan or DIA data processed without MR extraction — no 'level' == 'MR' features exist, so the PP-vs-MR stratification is meaningless

skills.description: Use when you need realistic simulated 1H NMR spectra (1D or 2D J-Res/COSY) of urine, blood, or CSF for algorithm development or benchmarking, or when comparing a simulated spectrum against a real spectrum (e.g. urine 0.8–4.5 ppm J-Res).
skills.name: jres-skyline-projection-generation
skills.search_text: jres-skyline-projection-generation Use when you need realistic simulated 1H NMR spectra (1D or 2D J-Res/COSY) of urine, blood, or CSF for algorithm development or benchmarking, or when comparing a simulated spectrum against a real spectrum (e.g. urine 0.8–4.5 ppm J-Res). When the input is already a processed/real experimental spectrum and the goal is pure peak annotation rather than simulation — MetAssimulo generates simulated spectra, not annotations. When the target spectrum type or metabolite set is outside the tool's scope (e.g. matrices or spectral dimensions not covered by the tool's urine/blood/CSF 1H 1D and 2D J-Res/COSY simulation). When a fully dense spectrum identical to the real sample is required — the article notes the simulated urine J-Res spectrum is less densely populated (52 metabolites) than the real one. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Generates simulated 2D J-resolved (J-Res) 1H NMR spectra of metabolomic samples using MetAssimulo 2.0 and projects them via a skyline (vertical) projection for direct visual and quantitative comparison with real spectra, e.g. human urine J-Res data from MetaboLights MTBLS12081. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf045
skills.summary: Generates simulated 2D J-resolved (J-Res) 1H NMR spectra of metabolomic samples using MetAssimulo 2.0 and projects them via a skyline (vertical) projection for direct visual and quantitative comparison with real spectra, e.g. human urine J-Res data from MetaboLights MTBLS12081.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a processed/real experimental spectrum and the goal is pure peak annotation rather than simulation — MetAssimulo generates simulated spectra, not annotations. When the target spectrum type or metabolite set is outside the tool's scope (e.g. matrices or spectral dimensions not covered by the tool's urine/blood/CSF 1H 1D and 2D J-Res/COSY simulation). When a fully dense spectrum identical to the real sample is required — the article notes the simulated urine J-Res spectrum is less densely populated (52 metabolites) than the real one.

skills.description: Use when a 2D 13C-JRES spectrum must be reduced to a 1D projection so its peaks can be picked and annotated with compound identities inferred from INADEQUATE networks in a PyINETA run.
skills.name: jres-spectrum-1d-projection
skills.search_text: jres-spectrum-1d-projection Use when a 2D 13C-JRES spectrum must be reduced to a 1D projection so its peaks can be picked and annotated with compound identities inferred from INADEQUATE networks in a PyINETA run. The run is INADEQUATE-only and no complementary 13C-JRES spectrum was acquired — use the standard load/pick/cluster/find/match steps instead No INADEQUATE networks have been established in preceding PyINETA steps, so there is no compound information to transfer to JRES peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 An optional PyINETA integration step that reads a raw 2D 13C-JRES NMR spectrum, projects it to a 1D spectrum, picks peaks, and transfers compound annotations from previously matched INADEQUATE networks onto the JRES peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: An optional PyINETA integration step that reads a raw 2D 13C-JRES NMR spectrum, projects it to a 1D spectrum, picks peaks, and transfers compound annotations from previously matched INADEQUATE networks onto the JRES peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The run is INADEQUATE-only and no complementary 13C-JRES spectrum was acquired — use the standard load/pick/cluster/find/match steps instead No INADEQUATE networks have been established in preceding PyINETA steps, so there is no compound information to transfer to JRES peaks

skills.description: Use when a deposited 13C-JRES spectrum must be integrated against previously constructed INADEQUATE networks (Match output) to determine how many networks have complementary JRES peaks, e.g. reproducing a reported count such as 65 of 67 networks in a 13C-labeled mouse liver sample.
skills.name: jres-spectrum-integration-with-inadequate-networks
skills.search_text: jres-spectrum-integration-with-inadequate-networks Use when a deposited 13C-JRES spectrum must be integrated against previously constructed INADEQUATE networks (Match output) to determine how many networks have complementary JRES peaks, e.g. reproducing a reported count such as 65 of 67 networks in a 13C-labeled mouse liver sample. Input spectra are not INADEQUATE spectra — pyINETA is designed for INADEQUATE NMR spectra, not generic 1D 1H NMR or unrelated 2D experiments No upstream INADEQUATE networks exist yet: the integration step requires the Match output of constructed peak networks, so the load/pick/cluster/find steps must run first (or use -s match+ to resume from matching) The goal is de novo compound discovery rather than validating a reported integration result for an existing deposited spectrum http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Integrates a complementary 13C-JRES NMR spectrum with upstream INADEQUATE peak networks produced by PyINETA, generating a MatchJres table that flags which constructed networks have corresponding JRES peaks. This is the JRES-integration step of PyINETA's INADEQUATE-JRES annotation pipeline for 13C-enriched metabolomics samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: Integrates a complementary 13C-JRES NMR spectrum with upstream INADEQUATE peak networks produced by PyINETA, generating a MatchJres table that flags which constructed networks have corresponding JRES peaks. This is the JRES-integration step of PyINETA's INADEQUATE-JRES annotation pipeline for 13C-enriched metabolomics samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not INADEQUATE spectra — pyINETA is designed for INADEQUATE NMR spectra, not generic 1D 1H NMR or unrelated 2D experiments No upstream INADEQUATE networks exist yet: the integration step requires the Match output of constructed peak networks, so the load/pick/cluster/find steps must run first (or use -s match+ to resume from matching) The goal is de novo compound discovery rather than validating a reported integration result for an existing deposited spectrum

skills.description: Use when you need the annotation content (e.g. experimental properties, solubility, etc.) under a single specified (sub)heading for one PubChem record, returned as JSON or XML.
skills.name: json-annotation-data-parsing
skills.search_text: json-annotation-data-parsing Use when you need the annotation content (e.g. experimental properties, solubility, etc.) under a single specified (sub)heading for one PubChem record, returned as JSON or XML. A PUG-View request cannot take multiple input record identifiers — do not use this skill when you need to retrieve annotations for many records at once. Annotation data under multiple headings for a given compound cannot be retrieved with a single request, unless the full annotation data retrieval is requested — do not use this skill when you need several distinct headings for one record. Do not use this skill for specialized (especially tabular) data that come from other backend service(s) and are not currently accessible through PUG-View. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 A method for retrieving and parsing heading-specific chemical annotations from PubChem records by issuing a PUG-View REST request to https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug_view/ and validating the returned JSON against the PUG-View content model. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-019-0375-2
skills.summary: A method for retrieving and parsing heading-specific chemical annotations from PubChem records by issuing a PUG-View REST request to https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug_view/ and validating the returned JSON against the PUG-View content model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A PUG-View request cannot take multiple input record identifiers — do not use this skill when you need to retrieve annotations for many records at once. Annotation data under multiple headings for a given compound cannot be retrieved with a single request, unless the full annotation data retrieval is requested — do not use this skill when you need several distinct headings for one record. Do not use this skill for specialized (especially tabular) data that come from other backend service(s) and are not currently accessible through PUG-View.

skills.description: Use when JSON-formatted biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) annotation entries (e.g. MIBiG) need their per-entry structure, bioactivity, or substrate fields parsed and flattened into a tabular report for validation or analysis.
skills.name: json-annotation-field-extraction
skills.search_text: json-annotation-field-extraction Use when JSON-formatted biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) annotation entries (e.g. MIBiG) need their per-entry structure, bioactivity, or substrate fields parsed and flattened into a tabular report for validation or analysis. Input data is not MIBiG JSON (e.g. raw GenBank/RefSeq FASTA without JSON annotations) — there are no `cluster.status` or structure fields to extract. The goal is de novo BGC detection from sequence (use antiSMASH/fungiSMASH/plantiSMASH/GECCO etc.), not field extraction from curated annotations. Entries have already been extracted and flattened into a per-entry table; re-parsing the raw JSON would duplicate work rather than add information. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Parse MIBiG 3.0 JSON-format annotations from the mibig-secmet/mibig-json repository to extract structure (SMILES), bioactivity, and protein-domain substrate fields, enabling downstream validation such as SMILES syntax checking with PIKAChU. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Parse MIBiG 3.0 JSON-format annotations from the mibig-secmet/mibig-json repository to extract structure (SMILES), bioactivity, and protein-domain substrate fields, enabling downstream validation such as SMILES syntax checking with PIKAChU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not MIBiG JSON (e.g. raw GenBank/RefSeq FASTA without JSON annotations) — there are no `cluster.status` or structure fields to extract. The goal is de novo BGC detection from sequence (use antiSMASH/fungiSMASH/plantiSMASH/GECCO etc.), not field extraction from curated annotations. Entries have already been extracted and flattened into a per-entry table; re-parsing the raw JSON would duplicate work rather than add information.

skills.description: Use when JSON annotation responses from CMM 3.0 RESTful API queries must be parsed and filtered to HMDB-sourced records so identifier, formula, and exact mass can be cross-checked against public HMDB accessions.
skills.name: json-annotation-record-parsing
skills.search_text: json-annotation-record-parsing Use when JSON annotation responses from CMM 3.0 RESTful API queries must be parsed and filtered to HMDB-sourced records so identifier, formula, and exact mass can be cross-checked against public HMDB accessions. Records are already structured/validated annotation data and no JSON parsing or HMDB-source filtering is needed Target metabolites are absent from HMDB — filtering to HMDB-sourced annotations will yield an empty subset and cross-checking cannot proceed The analysis needs raw annotation across all CMM database sources rather than HMDB-verified records (filtering would discard non-HMDB annotations) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parses JSON responses returned by the CEU Mass Mediator 3.0 RESTful API (ceumass.eps.uspceu.es) for batch metabolite annotation queries, extracting annotation records (identifier, formula, exact mass, adduct, score, database source) into a structured form and filtering to HMDB-sourced entries for verification against public HMDB records. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00720
skills.summary: Parses JSON responses returned by the CEU Mass Mediator 3.0 RESTful API (ceumass.eps.uspceu.es) for batch metabolite annotation queries, extracting annotation records (identifier, formula, exact mass, adduct, score, database source) into a structured form and filtering to HMDB-sourced entries for verification against public HMDB records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Records are already structured/validated annotation data and no JSON parsing or HMDB-source filtering is needed Target metabolites are absent from HMDB — filtering to HMDB-sourced annotations will yield an empty subset and cross-checking cannot proceed The analysis needs raw annotation across all CMM database sources rather than HMDB-verified records (filtering would discard non-HMDB annotations)

skills.name: json-collection-aggregation-into-sqlite
skills.search_text: json-collection-aggregation-into-sqlite Use when cleaned per-dataset JSON collections of experimental CCS values must be merged into one queryable reference database with per-field totals that can be validated against reported row counts. The goal is CCS/retention-time prediction from trained machine-learning models rather than assembling the experimental reference database. This produces a verifiable, queryable experimental CCS reference (7907 entries, 45 lipid classes) underlying LiPydomics identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560

This produces a verifiable, queryable experimental CCS reference (7907 entries, 45 lipid classes) underlying LiPydomics identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is CCS/retention-time prediction from trained machine-learning models rather than assembling the experimental reference database. Input is raw IM-MS lipidomics data requiring statistical or multivariate analysis (use the lipydomics stats/plotting/identification modules instead). The source collections are not cleaned JSON CCS collections with the required fields (m/z, CCS, lipid class, ionization mode, drift-tube type).

skills.search_text: json-configuration-parsing Use when you need to enumerate, audit, or extend the lipid abbreviation input styles supported by a converter such as LipidLynxX, starting from its JSON rule/configuration files rather than from prose documentation. skills.summary: Parse the JSON configuration/rule files shipped with LipidLynxX to enumerate the pre-defined lipid annotation input styles (17 identification programs plus 5 lipid databases) and map each style to its source tool or database.

When surveying general (non-lipid) identifier converters; this skill is grounded in the LipidLynxX JSON rule format and its 26 lipid annotation styles.

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics input abbreviation style or lipid class (e.g. plant or bacterial lipids such as MGDG/DGDG) is unsupported by the shipped converter configurations and a new JSON rule file is needed.

skills.search_text: json-lipid-database-schema-authoring Use when a lipidomics input abbreviation style or lipid class (e.g. plant or bacterial lipids such as MGDG/DGDG) is unsupported by the shipped converter configurations and a new JSON rule file is needed. skills.description: Use when converting vendor MS data to Aird format and you must persist spectrum indexes (retention time, MS1-MS2 DDA groups, DIA/SWATH precursor m/z windows) as a JSON metadata file for fast random access.

skills.search_text: json-metadata-schema-serialization Use when converting vendor MS data to Aird format and you must persist spectrum indexes (retention time, MS1-MS2 DDA groups, DIA/SWATH precursor m/z windows) as a JSON metadata file for fast random access. skills.description: Use when a PUG-View request (e.g. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug_view/data/compound/1983/JSON) returns a JSON document that must be decoded into a Record object, saved to disk, or filtered to specific (sub)headings before downstream analysis.
skills.name: json-parsing
skills.search_text: json-parsing Use when a PUG-View request (e.g. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug_view/data/compound/1983/JSON) returns a JSON document that must be decoded into a Record object, saved to disk, or filtered to specific (sub)headings before downstream analysis. The retrieval target is computed compound properties rather than annotation data — PUG-REST is better suited for specific individual computed properties, and PUG-View responses are not designed for that data type. Multiple record identifiers need to be fetched in one HTTP call — a PUG-View request cannot take multiple input record identifiers, so batching must happen at the request level, not in a single parsed response. Tabular, specialized backend data not served through PUG-View is needed — such data are not currently accessible through PUG-View regardless of JSON parsing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3345 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parses JSON responses returned by the PUG-View REST interface so that annotation content for PubChem compound, substance, or assay records can be programmatically consumed, validated, and reduced to the desired (sub)headings or full-record data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-019-0375-2
skills.summary: Parses JSON responses returned by the PUG-View REST interface so that annotation content for PubChem compound, substance, or assay records can be programmatically consumed, validated, and reduced to the desired (sub)headings or full-record data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The retrieval target is computed compound properties rather than annotation data — PUG-REST is better suited for specific individual computed properties, and PUG-View responses are not designed for that data type. Multiple record identifiers need to be fetched in one HTTP call — a PUG-View request cannot take multiple input record identifiers, so batching must happen at the request level, not in a single parsed response. Tabular, specialized backend data not served through PUG-View is needed — such data are not currently accessible through PUG-View regardless of JSON parsing.

skills.description: Use when you have finished the msFeaST pipeline notebooks (quantification table, metadata, spectral data processed) and need to produce the dashboard-loadable .json results file from the upstream result tables.
skills.name: json-results-serialization-for-dashboard
skills.search_text: json-results-serialization-for-dashboard Use when you have finished the msFeaST pipeline notebooks (quantification table, metadata, spectral data processed) and need to produce the dashboard-loadable .json results file from the upstream result tables. The pipeline has not yet produced the clustering and globaltest result tables — there is nothing to integrate and the dashboard would load an incomplete structure. skills.search_text: kegg-compound-identifier-matching Use when a list of lipid annotations (e.g. shorthand notations like PC 16:0_18:2) must be matched to KEGG compound IDs — or ChEBI/LION identifiers — as a prerequisite for pathway (KEGG, Reactome) or ontology-based lipidome analysis. The input annotations cover plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes (fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) The input is raw mass-spectrometry data (mzML, spectra) rather than already-identified lipid annotations requiring identifier cross-matching Only a unified shorthand format is needed with no downstream database linkage — the Converter or Equalizer module suffices without invoking the Linker http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Uses the LipidLynxX Linker module to cross-match mammalian lipid abbreviations against KEGG compound identifiers (with parallel ChEBI and LION mappings), enabling transfer of experimental lipidomics annotations into pathway and network analysis resources. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Uses the LipidLynxX Linker module to cross-match mammalian lipid abbreviations against KEGG compound identifiers (with parallel ChEBI and LION mappings), enabling transfer of experimental lipidomics annotations into pathway and network analysis resources.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input annotations cover plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes (fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) The input is raw mass-spectrometry data (mzML, spectra) rather than already-identified lipid annotations requiring identifier cross-matching Only a unified shorthand format is needed with no downstream database linkage — the Converter or Equalizer module suffices without invoking the Linker

skills.description: Use when you have an untargeted LC-MS peak list (m/z, retention time, intensity) and need to map each peak to candidate KEGG compounds via adduct/fragment-aware m/z matching before annotation prioritization.
skills.name: kegg-compound-matching
skills.search_text: kegg-compound-matching Use when you have an untargeted LC-MS peak list (m/z, retention time, intensity) and need to map each peak to candidate KEGG compounds via adduct/fragment-aware m/z matching before annotation prioritization. You need to annotate against databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) — mWISE only offers the data to annotate in the KEGG database Input is already a set of candidate compounds with features (i.e. downstream of matchingStage) — use featuresClustering/clusterBased.filter instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 mWISE's matchingStage rapidly matches LC-MS peak m/z values to the KEGG compound database, considering a configurable set of adducts and fragments, producing per-peak candidate KEGG compounds that feed the subsequent clustering/filter and diffusion prioritization steps. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: mWISE's matchingStage rapidly matches LC-MS peak m/z values to the KEGG compound database, considering a configurable set of adducts and fragments, producing per-peak candidate KEGG compounds that feed the subsequent clustering/filter and diffusion prioritization steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to annotate against databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) — mWISE only offers the data to annotate in the KEGG database Input is already a set of candidate compounds with features (i.e. downstream of matchingStage) — use featuresClustering/clusterBased.filter instead

skills.description: Use when you have an annotation matrix pairing peak IDs with KEGG (Cxxxxx) or ChEBI IDs and need to build peak-to-pathway membership tables for metabolite-set activity scoring with PALS.
skills.name: kegg-compound-pathway-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-compound-pathway-mapping Use when you have an annotation matrix pairing peak IDs with KEGG (Cxxxxx) or ChEBI IDs and need to build peak-to-pathway membership tables for metabolite-set activity scoring with PALS. All peak features are unannotated — peaks that do not have annotations will not be used for pathway analysis, so no peak-to-pathway mapping can be built The dataset is proteomic or transcriptomic and maps via UniProt/ENSEMBL IDs rather than metabolite compounds (KEGG/ChEBI); use the protein/gene Reactome database route instead Feature-to-pathway membership tables already exist and only the activity-level decomposition (PLAGE scoring) step is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps peak features with KEGG or ChEBI compound annotations onto metabolite sets (pathways) via the PiMP-exported KEGG compound database (PiMP_KEGG) or a Reactome database instance on Neo4j, forming the feature-to-set membership tables that PALS scores with PLAGE/ORA/GSEA. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Maps peak features with KEGG or ChEBI compound annotations onto metabolite sets (pathways) via the PiMP-exported KEGG compound database (PiMP_KEGG) or a Reactome database instance on Neo4j, forming the feature-to-set membership tables that PALS scores with PLAGE/ORA/GSEA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All peak features are unannotated — peaks that do not have annotations will not be used for pathway analysis, so no peak-to-pathway mapping can be built The dataset is proteomic or transcriptomic and maps via UniProt/ENSEMBL IDs rather than metabolite compounds (KEGG/ChEBI); use the protein/gene Reactome database route instead Feature-to-pathway membership tables already exist and only the activity-level decomposition (PLAGE scoring) step is needed

skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature/peak list must be assigned initial KEGG compound candidates by m/z matching before any biological-context scoring, or when reproducing mWISE's matching stage to benchmark annotators against KEGG-only databases.
skills.name: kegg-compound-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-compound-reference-mapping Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature/peak list must be assigned initial KEGG compound candidates by m/z matching before any biological-context scoring, or when reproducing mWISE's matching stage to benchmark annotators against KEGG-only databases. The target reference database is not KEGG — mWISE only offers data to annotate against KEGG, so matching to HMDB, Lipid Maps, or T3DB requires xMSannotator or another tool The peaks are already matched to a compound database and only require downstream clustering or diffusion prioritization — re-running the matching stage would be redundant No adduct/fragment model is known for the acquisition mode, making m/z-to-compound matching unreliable without additional deconvolution http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Rapidly match LC-MS peak mass-to-charge ratios against the KEGG compound database using mWISE's matching Stage (built on the Genomic Ranges R package) over a configurable set of adducts and fragments, producing the initial candidate-compound annotations that feed clustering and diffusion prioritization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: Rapidly match LC-MS peak mass-to-charge ratios against the KEGG compound database using mWISE's matching Stage (built on the Genomic Ranges R package) over a configurable set of adducts and fragments, producing the initial candidate-compound annotations that feed clustering and diffusion prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target reference database is not KEGG — mWISE only offers data to annotate against KEGG, so matching to HMDB, Lipid Maps, or T3DB requires xMSannotator or another tool The peaks are already matched to a compound database and only require downstream clustering or diffusion prioritization — re-running the matching stage would be redundant No adduct/fragment model is known for the acquisition mode, making m/z-to-compound matching unreliable without additional deconvolution

skills.description: Use when starting an mWISE annotation run on unannotated LC-MS peak lists (m/z features) and you need KEGG compound candidates before applying the cluster-based filter and diffusion scoring.
skills.name: kegg-database-matching
skills.search_text: kegg-database-matching Use when starting an mWISE annotation run on unannotated LC-MS peak lists (m/z features) and you need KEGG compound candidates before applying the cluster-based filter and diffusion scoring. Annotation targets databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) — mWISE only offers KEGG data for annotation Input is already an annotated compound list or post-filter peak set; re-matching would be redundant before clustering/diffusion http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Matches LC-MS peak m/z values against the KEGG database considering adducts and fragments, producing candidate compound lists that feed mWISE's clustering, filtering and diffusion prioritization stages. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: Matches LC-MS peak m/z values against the KEGG database considering adducts and fragments, producing candidate compound lists that feed mWISE's clustering, filtering and diffusion prioritization stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotation targets databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) — mWISE only offers KEGG data for annotation Input is already an annotated compound list or post-filter peak set; re-matching would be redundant before clustering/diffusion

skills.description: Use when the input is an annotated amino acid FASTA (Type 1) and the goal is a KEGG-annotation-based draft GENRE whose reactions are traceable to genes via ModelSEED reaction IDs.
skills.name: kegg-gene-to-modelseed-reaction-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-gene-to-modelseed-reaction-mapping Use when the input is an annotated amino acid FASTA (Type 1) and the goal is a KEGG-annotation-based draft GENRE whose reactions are traceable to genes via ModelSEED reaction IDs. The input is already a BLASTp output (Type 2) or an existing SBML GENRE (Type 3) — use the corresponding Reconstructor input path instead of re-running DIAMOND on a FASTA The input contains no gene annotations (e.g., unannotated nucleotide sequence) and must first be functionally annotated before KEGG-based reaction mapping A highly curated, manually reconstructed model is needed rather than an automated KEGG/ModelSEED-derived draft http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Translates DIAMOND BLASTp KEGG gene hits into ModelSEED reactions to build a draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction (GENRE) with Reconstructor, using the curated universal.pickle reaction database and COBRApy. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Translates DIAMOND BLASTp KEGG gene hits into ModelSEED reactions to build a draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction (GENRE) with Reconstructor, using the curated universal.pickle reaction database and COBRApy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a BLASTp output (Type 2) or an existing SBML GENRE (Type 3) — use the corresponding Reconstructor input path instead of re-running DIAMOND on a FASTA The input contains no gene annotations (e.g., unannotated nucleotide sequence) and must first be functionally annotated before KEGG-based reaction mapping A highly curated, manually reconstructed model is needed rather than an automated KEGG/ModelSEED-derived draft

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics count data frame contains KEGG compound identifiers and each feature needs hierarchical class/subclass metadata attached before statistical testing or figure faceting.
skills.name: kegg-identifier-based-compound-classification
skills.search_text: kegg-identifier-based-compound-classification Use when a metabolomics count data frame contains KEGG compound identifiers and each feature needs hierarchical class/subclass metadata attached before statistical testing or figure faceting. Compounds lack KEGG compound numbers and keep_unknowns = FALSE is intended — those features cannot receive hierarchy metadata and will be dropped The goal is enzyme orthology or gene annotation lookup per metabolite rather than compound class hierarchy — use omu's KEGG_gather instead Input is raw instrument output (e.g. vendor peak lists) rather than a count table already keyed by compound identifier — load via read.metabo first http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates each metabolite in a count data frame with hierarchical KEGG compound class metadata (Class, Subclass_1 through Subclass_4) using the omu R package's assign_hierarchy function, keyed on KEGG compound numbers. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00129-19
skills.summary: Annotates each metabolite in a count data frame with hierarchical KEGG compound class metadata (Class, Subclass_1 through Subclass_4) using the omu R package's assign_hierarchy function, keyed on KEGG compound numbers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds lack KEGG compound numbers and keep_unknowns = FALSE is intended — those features cannot receive hierarchy metadata and will be dropped The goal is enzyme orthology or gene annotation lookup per metabolite rather than compound class hierarchy — use omu's KEGG_gather instead Input is raw instrument output (e.g. vendor peak lists) rather than a count table already keyed by compound identifier — load via read.metabo first

skills.description: Use when the goal is to automatically reconstruct a metabolic network for one or two KEGG organisms from KEGG database information, requiring organism-specific KGML downloads and parsing of compounds and reactions.
skills.name: kegg-kgml-pathway-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: kegg-kgml-pathway-data-retrieval Use when the goal is to automatically reconstruct a metabolic network for one or two KEGG organisms from KEGG database information, requiring organism-specific KGML downloads and parsing of compounds and reactions. When the starting data are raw genomic or experimental gene data: MetNet reconstructs solely from the KEGG database and 'MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data' When a pathway comparison visualization from non-KEGG sources is needed: the reconstruction 'is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which can be a limit wrt. the represented information' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Automatically retrieves the KGML files of every pathway of a selected KEGG organism via the public KEGG APIs and parses them to extract the compounds and reactions needed to reconstruct a two-level metabolic network, using the configuration files organismList.txt and pathwayList.txt. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Automatically retrieves the KGML files of every pathway of a selected KEGG organism via the public KEGG APIs and parses them to extract the compounds and reactions needed to reconstruct a two-level metabolic network, using the configuration files organismList.txt and pathwayList.txt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the starting data are raw genomic or experimental gene data: MetNet reconstructs solely from the KEGG database and 'MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data' When a pathway comparison visualization from non-KEGG sources is needed: the reconstruction 'is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which can be a limit wrt. the represented information'

skills.description: Use when building the functional level of a KEGG-based metabolic network for an organism: you need, per reference pathway, the set or multiset of reactions (and compounds) that MetNet compares between two organisms.
skills.name: kegg-kgml-reaction-extraction
skills.search_text: kegg-kgml-reaction-extraction Use when building the functional level of a KEGG-based metabolic network for an organism: you need, per reference pathway, the set or multiset of reactions (and compounds) that MetNet compares between two organisms. When the goal is the structural (graph-based) level of the network, which is built from pathway relations rather than reaction content. When reconstructing metabolism from raw genomic/experimental data — MetNet is based uniquely on the KEGG database and does not currently support input of genomic data. When the target pathways are physical-mechanism (membrane) pathway maps, since their KGML files contain no reaction information and yield only empty reaction sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Retrieve and parse KEGG KGML files via KEGG's public APIs to extract the compounds and reactions of each reference pathway, building the functional-level (reactions-based) metabolic data for an organism as used by MetNet's two-level metabolic network representation. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Retrieve and parse KEGG KGML files via KEGG's public APIs to extract the compounds and reactions of each reference pathway, building the functional-level (reactions-based) metabolic data for an organism as used by MetNet's two-level metabolic network representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is the structural (graph-based) level of the network, which is built from pathway relations rather than reaction content. When reconstructing metabolism from raw genomic/experimental data — MetNet is based uniquely on the KEGG database and does not currently support input of genomic data. When the target pathways are physical-mechanism (membrane) pathway maps, since their KGML files contain no reaction information and yield only empty reaction sets.

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed LC/MS feature tables (m/z per feature, e.g. from apLCMS cdf.to.ftr or XCMS centWave) and need to quantify how many features can be matched to known metabolites via KEGG.
skills.name: kegg-metabolite-database-searching
skills.search_text: kegg-metabolite-database-searching Use when you have preprocessed LC/MS feature tables (m/z per feature, e.g. from apLCMS cdf.to.ftr or XCMS centWave) and need to quantify how many features can be matched to known metabolites via KEGG. Input is raw vendor/NetCDF spectra rather than a preprocessed feature table — peak detection and alignment (e.g. apLCMS cdf.to.ftr) must be done first Goal is correcting between-batch intensity differences — post-hoc batch effect correction only adjusts signal intensity and cannot fix feature misalignment, so annotation matching is not a substitute for batch-aware preprocessing The study used positive-mode ionization — the specified adduct list ([M-H]-, [M+Cl]-, etc.) applies only to negative mode http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates LC/MS feature m/z values against KEGG compound masses using xMSAnnotator with a negative-mode adduct ion list, computing the proportion of annotated features per preprocessing method (Fig. 3b-style comparison on ST000868). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: Annotates LC/MS feature m/z values against KEGG compound masses using xMSAnnotator with a negative-mode adduct ion list, computing the proportion of annotated features per preprocessing method (Fig. 3b-style comparison on ST000868).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor/NetCDF spectra rather than a preprocessed feature table — peak detection and alignment (e.g. apLCMS cdf.to.ftr) must be done first Goal is correcting between-batch intensity differences — post-hoc batch effect correction only adjusts signal intensity and cannot fix feature misalignment, so annotation matching is not a substitute for batch-aware preprocessing The study used positive-mode ionization — the specified adduct list ([M-H]-, [M+Cl]-, etc.) applies only to negative mode

skills.description: Use when a large phylogeny (thousands of taxa, e.g. PhyloXML) must be annotated per leaf with KEGG module presence/absence or genome-size metadata as external rings in a circular cladogram.
skills.name: kegg-module-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-module-annotation-mapping Use when a large phylogeny (thousands of taxa, e.g. PhyloXML) must be annotated per leaf with KEGG module presence/absence or genome-size metadata as external rings in a circular cladogram. Input is a taxonomic abundance profile (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 output) rather than a per-genome/leaf phylogeny — use the export2graphlan biomarker workflow instead Interactive exploration of large phylogenies is the goal — iTOL targets interactive analyses of large-scale phylogenies with overlaid metadata Hierarchical quantitative metagenomic data without a reference tree — Krona emphasizes hierarchical quantitative information for such profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Maps per-genome KEGG functional module presence (e.g. M00082, M00083, M00086, M00087, M00088, M00157, M00159) and genome size onto a large phylogenetic tree as GraPhlAn external ring annotations, producing a compact circular cladogram with genome-specific metadata. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Maps per-genome KEGG functional module presence (e.g. M00082, M00083, M00086, M00087, M00088, M00157, M00159) and genome size onto a large phylogenetic tree as GraPhlAn external ring annotations, producing a compact circular cladogram with genome-specific metadata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a taxonomic abundance profile (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 output) rather than a per-genome/leaf phylogeny — use the export2graphlan biomarker workflow instead Interactive exploration of large phylogenies is the goal — iTOL targets interactive analyses of large-scale phylogenies with overlaid metadata Hierarchical quantitative metagenomic data without a reference tree — Krona emphasizes hierarchical quantitative information for such profiles

skills.description: Use when you have a full (unprefiltered) KO/compound abundance table plus sample metadata with grouping, and need threshold-free, multi-group or longitudinal KEGG pathway/module enrichment rather than single-list over-representation.
skills.name: kegg-module-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: kegg-module-enrichment-interpretation Use when you have a full (unprefiltered) KO/compound abundance table plus sample metadata with grouping, and need threshold-free, multi-group or longitudinal KEGG pathway/module enrichment rather than single-list over-representation. The feature abundance table has already been prefiltered to significant/background-filtered features — GRSA is threshold-free and requires the full background to remain valid You need organism-specific pathway-gene mapping for a non-human/mouse organism without building a custom modulelist (built-in org pathway databases cover hsa and mmu only) Your question is a classic two-list over-representation test on a pre-defined KO list rather than threshold-free aggregation of genome-wide differential statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates per-KO (or per-compound) differential statistics from omics feature tables to KEGG pathway/module-level reporter scores using the Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) implemented in the R package ReporterScore, then interprets which KEGG modules are enriched per group or time point. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Aggregates per-KO (or per-compound) differential statistics from omics feature tables to KEGG pathway/module-level reporter scores using the Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) implemented in the R package ReporterScore, then interprets which KEGG modules are enriched per group or time point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature abundance table has already been prefiltered to significant/background-filtered features — GRSA is threshold-free and requires the full background to remain valid You need organism-specific pathway-gene mapping for a non-human/mouse organism without building a custom modulelist (built-in org pathway databases cover hsa and mmu only) Your question is a classic two-list over-representation test on a pre-defined KO list rather than threshold-free aggregation of genome-wide differential statistics

skills.description: Use when you have reconstructed the two-level metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms and need to compare their structural level — pathway connectivity through shared non-ubiquitous compounds — pathway by pathway or globally.
skills.name: kegg-organism-network-structural-comparison
skills.search_text: kegg-organism-network-structural-comparison Use when you have reconstructed the two-level metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms and need to compare their structural level — pathway connectivity through shared non-ubiquitous compounds — pathway by pathway or globally. If the goal is to compare pathway reaction content rather than pathway connectivity — that requires the functional-level index SimPi with 'set' or 'multiset' comparison mode. If the organism's metabolic network cannot be reconstructed from KEGG alone (e.g. input is raw genomic data); MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and the article notes this needs a significant tool extension. If you need cross-database comparison: the reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which the discussion flags as a limit with respect to the represented information. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Compute the structural-level similarity index SimSi for pairs of KEGG organisms by comparing pathway graphs G and G' built from KGML-derived compound-sharing relations, producing a per-reference-pathway table of local similarities that underpins MetNet's metabolism-wide structural comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Compute the structural-level similarity index SimSi for pairs of KEGG organisms by comparing pathway graphs G and G' built from KGML-derived compound-sharing relations, producing a per-reference-pathway table of local similarities that underpins MetNet's metabolism-wide structural comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is to compare pathway reaction content rather than pathway connectivity — that requires the functional-level index SimPi with 'set' or 'multiset' comparison mode. If the organism's metabolic network cannot be reconstructed from KEGG alone (e.g. input is raw genomic data); MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and the article notes this needs a significant tool extension. If you need cross-database comparison: the reconstruction is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which the discussion flags as a limit with respect to the represented information.

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end metagenome reads must be converted into per-sample KEGG ortholog (KO) abundance profiles using predicted operon sequences as the alignment reference, e.g. for disease-vs-control pathway association testing.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-functional-annotation Use when raw paired-end metagenome reads must be converted into per-sample KEGG ortholog (KO) abundance profiles using predicted operon sequences as the alignment reference, e.g. for disease-vs-control pathway association testing. When functional annotation from already-predicted genes is available and read-mapping-based KO assignment is unnecessary (MetaRon's 'op' mode operates directly from scaftigs and gene predictions) When the goal is secondary metabolite analysis of operons — the README routes that to antiSMASH, not FMAP When reads cannot be assumed to share sequence identity >= 80% with the operon reference, since the study's FMAP thresholds depend on high-identity mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assign KEGG KO identifiers to metagenomic operon-derived function by mapping raw paired-end reads back to MetaRon-predicted non-redundant operon sequences with bowtie2 and submitting the mapped reads to the Functional Mapping and Analysis Pipeline (FMAP), producing a per-sample KO abundance matrix for downstream differential analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12864-020-07357-5
skills.summary: Assign KEGG KO identifiers to metagenomic operon-derived function by mapping raw paired-end reads back to MetaRon-predicted non-redundant operon sequences with bowtie2 and submitting the mapped reads to the Functional Mapping and Analysis Pipeline (FMAP), producing a per-sample KO abundance matrix for downstream differential analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When functional annotation from already-predicted genes is available and read-mapping-based KO assignment is unnecessary (MetaRon's 'op' mode operates directly from scaftigs and gene predictions) When the goal is secondary metabolite analysis of operons — the README routes that to antiSMASH, not FMAP When reads cannot be assumed to share sequence identity >= 80% with the operon reference, since the study's FMAP thresholds depend on high-identity mapping

skills.description: Use when you have a HUMAnN-derived KEGG functional profile matrix plus a LEfSe biomarker result and need a publication-quality circular functional tree highlighting pathways enriched in contrasting sample cohorts.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-hierarchical-rendering
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-hierarchical-rendering Use when you have a HUMAnN-derived KEGG functional profile matrix plus a LEfSe biomarker result and need a publication-quality circular functional tree highlighting pathways enriched in contrasting sample cohorts. Input is taxonomic abundance data (e.g., MetaPhlAn2 species profiles) rather than functional/KEGG profiles — the taxonomic analog is handled by the taxonomic tree workflow (Fig. 3), not this functional-ontology rendering. You need interactive exploration of large phylogenies with overlaid metadata — iTOL or Krona target interactive analyses, whereas GraPhlAn is command-driven and static. Input files are not LEfSe/HUMAnN/MetaPhlAn format and cannot be converted by export2graphlan (no supported conversion path described in the README). http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Render a compact circular tree of KEGG functional-ontology profiles (e.g., HUMAnN-derived KEGG metabolic pathways for HMP vs MetaHIT gut metagenomes) by converting LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs to GraPhlAn input files with export2graphlan, then annotating and plotting with GraPhlAn/matplotlib. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Render a compact circular tree of KEGG functional-ontology profiles (e.g., HUMAnN-derived KEGG metabolic pathways for HMP vs MetaHIT gut metagenomes) by converting LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs to GraPhlAn input files with export2graphlan, then annotating and plotting with GraPhlAn/matplotlib.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is taxonomic abundance data (e.g., MetaPhlAn2 species profiles) rather than functional/KEGG profiles — the taxonomic analog is handled by the taxonomic tree workflow (Fig. 3), not this functional-ontology rendering. You need interactive exploration of large phylogenies with overlaid metadata — iTOL or Krona target interactive analyses, whereas GraPhlAn is command-driven and static. Input files are not LEfSe/HUMAnN/MetaPhlAn format and cannot be converted by export2graphlan (no supported conversion path described in the README).

skills.description: Use when you have raw fecal shallow shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. the n=666 3xTg/WT Sacrifice cohort deposit on Qiita) and need per-sample KEGG pathway abundances plus genotype-level enrichment/depletion calls.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-abundance-profiling
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-abundance-profiling Use when you have raw fecal shallow shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. the n=666 3xTg/WT Sacrifice cohort deposit on Qiita) and need per-sample KEGG pathway abundances plus genotype-level enrichment/depletion calls. The input is already a KO- or pathway-level abundance feature table — re-annotating raw reads with DIAMOND would be redundant; proceed directly to aggregation and differential testing The goal is taxonomic profiling of species (e.g. the species-level ANCOM-BC2 analysis of Akkermansia muciniphila depletion and Mucispirillum/Helicobacter/Desulfovibrio/Escherichia/Shigella enrichment) rather than functional pathway profiling The samples come from the Longitudinal cohort, where fecal samples lack animal IDs and collection differences confound comparison with the Sacrifice cohort http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Annotates raw shallow shotgun metagenomics reads to KEGG orthologs, aggregates ortholog counts into per-sample KEGG pathway abundance profiles, and tests each pathway for differential abundance between genotype groups (here, 3xTg vs WT fecal metagenomes from the Sacrifice cohort), yielding an enriched/depleted pathway table. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Annotates raw shallow shotgun metagenomics reads to KEGG orthologs, aggregates ortholog counts into per-sample KEGG pathway abundance profiles, and tests each pathway for differential abundance between genotype groups (here, 3xTg vs WT fecal metagenomes from the Sacrifice cohort), yielding an enriched/depleted pathway table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a KO- or pathway-level abundance feature table — re-annotating raw reads with DIAMOND would be redundant; proceed directly to aggregation and differential testing The goal is taxonomic profiling of species (e.g. the species-level ANCOM-BC2 analysis of Akkermansia muciniphila depletion and Mucispirillum/Helicobacter/Desulfovibrio/Escherichia/Shigella enrichment) rather than functional pathway profiling The samples come from the Longitudinal cohort, where fecal samples lack animal IDs and collection differences confound comparison with the Sacrifice cohort

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics experiment (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS136 split by assay type) needs its assay-specific chemical bias quantified as a count or proportion of KEGG human pathways reachable for ORA.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-accessibility-quantification
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-accessibility-quantification Use when an untargeted metabolomics experiment (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS136 split by assay type) needs its assay-specific chemical bias quantified as a count or proportion of KEGG human pathways reachable for ORA. The goal is to test ORA robustness to parameters such as background set, differential metabolite threshold (q <= 0.05 BH FDR), or pathway database choice (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) — those are separate simulations in the reproducible_simulations.ipynb notebook. The dataset already has a well-defined, assay-specific background set and the question is whether ORA results change, rather than how many pathways the assay can reach. The compounds are metabolites with misidentifications to simulate (swapping isobaric ±20 ppm or same-formula compounds) — that is a distinct sensitivity experiment, not an accessibility census. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies how much a metabolomics assay's detectable compound set limits KEGG pathway coverage: convert each assay's identified compounds to KEGG IDs, map them onto the 256 KEGG human pathways, and count how many pathways are accessible (≥2 compounds) per assay. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Quantifies how much a metabolomics assay's detectable compound set limits KEGG pathway coverage: convert each assay's identified compounds to KEGG IDs, map them onto the 256 KEGG human pathways, and count how many pathways are accessible (≥2 compounds) per assay.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to test ORA robustness to parameters such as background set, differential metabolite threshold (q <= 0.05 BH FDR), or pathway database choice (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) — those are separate simulations in the reproducible_simulations.ipynb notebook. The dataset already has a well-defined, assay-specific background set and the question is whether ORA results change, rather than how many pathways the assay can reach. The compounds are metabolites with misidentifications to simulate (swapping isobaric ±20 ppm or same-formula compounds) — that is a distinct sensitivity experiment, not an accessibility census.

skills.description: Use when a KEGG organism code is available and the goal is a graph-based (topological) representation of its metabolism — pathways as nodes, shared-compound relations as edges — for later comparison or visualization.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-adjacency-construction
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-adjacency-construction Use when a KEGG organism code is available and the goal is a graph-based (topological) representation of its metabolism — pathways as nodes, shared-compound relations as edges — for later comparison or visualization. The input is raw genomic data rather than a KEGG organism code — MetNet reconstructs uniquely from the KEGG database and does not yet accept genomic data as input. The analysis target is the functional level (pathway reactions content and reaction-based similarity) rather than the structural/topological level. The organism is not present in the KEGG organism list (organismList.txt), since reconstruction depends entirely on KEGG reference pathway decomposition. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Builds the structural-level metabolic network adjacency for a KEGG organism: pathways become nodes and edges connect pathways sharing at least one non-ubiquitous compound, reconstructed automatically from KEGG KGML data. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Builds the structural-level metabolic network adjacency for a KEGG organism: pathways become nodes and edges connect pathways sharing at least one non-ubiquitous compound, reconstructed automatically from KEGG KGML data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw genomic data rather than a KEGG organism code — MetNet reconstructs uniquely from the KEGG database and does not yet accept genomic data as input. The analysis target is the functional level (pathway reactions content and reaction-based similarity) rather than the structural/topological level. The organism is not present in the KEGG organism list (organismList.txt), since reconstruction depends entirely on KEGG reference pathway decomposition.

skills.description: Use when standalone metabolomics data must be linked to disease/phenotype GWAS results by testing whether metabolite-interacting genes from KEGG pathways are over-represented in GWAS gene networks.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when standalone metabolomics data must be linked to disease/phenotype GWAS results by testing whether metabolite-interacting genes from KEGG pathways are over-represented in GWAS gene networks. The metabolomics and GWAS datasets are paired from the same cohort — metGWAS 1.0 targets standalone, independent studies; paired data support direct SNP–metabolite association testing instead. The metabolites cannot be mapped to HMDB interacting proteins, since the analysis is limited to genes with known metabolite interactions (HMDB 'discoverable genes'), leaving gene sets and the background universe too sparse to test. The trait of interest has no disease/phenotype gene set in the GWAS Catalog network representation to compare against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Network-driven over-representation analysis of KEGG-pathway metabolic gene sets (metabolite-interacting genes mapped via HMDB) against GWAS-Catalog-derived genomic gene sets using a hypergeometric test, as implemented in the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Network-driven over-representation analysis of KEGG-pathway metabolic gene sets (metabolite-interacting genes mapped via HMDB) against GWAS-Catalog-derived genomic gene sets using a hypergeometric test, as implemented in the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolomics and GWAS datasets are paired from the same cohort — metGWAS 1.0 targets standalone, independent studies; paired data support direct SNP–metabolite association testing instead. The metabolites cannot be mapped to HMDB interacting proteins, since the analysis is limited to genes with known metabolite interactions (HMDB 'discoverable genes'), leaving gene sets and the background universe too sparse to test. The trait of interest has no disease/phenotype gene set in the GWAS Catalog network representation to compare against.

skills.description: Use when a metabolite list (KEGG compound IDs converted via MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion) must be mapped to KEGG pathways to find where the selected metabolites occur and ranked by occurrence count.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when a metabolite list (KEGG compound IDs converted via MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion) must be mapped to KEGG pathways to find where the selected metabolites occur and ranked by occurrence count. The input metabolites lack metabolite identifiers convertible to KEGG compound IDs, so MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion cannot produce the KEGG IDs KEGGREST requires The goal is pathway enrichment for gene/transcript identifiers (KEGGREST mapping here targets metabolite compound IDs, not gene IDs) A metabolite-level statistical test (e.g., Repeated Measures ANOVA, linear mixed models) is needed first — this skill operates on an already-selected metabolite list http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Maps metabolites of interest, identified via MetaboAnalyst ID conversion, to KEGG pathways using KEGGREST in MeTEor and produces an occurrence-ranked pathway list with interactive KEGG pathway-map URLs that highlight the selected metabolites in red. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae178
skills.summary: Maps metabolites of interest, identified via MetaboAnalyst ID conversion, to KEGG pathways using KEGGREST in MeTEor and produces an occurrence-ranked pathway list with interactive KEGG pathway-map URLs that highlight the selected metabolites in red.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input metabolites lack metabolite identifiers convertible to KEGG compound IDs, so MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion cannot produce the KEGG IDs KEGGREST requires The goal is pathway enrichment for gene/transcript identifiers (KEGGREST mapping here targets metabolite compound IDs, not gene IDs) A metabolite-level statistical test (e.g., Repeated Measures ANOVA, linear mixed models) is needed first — this skill operates on an already-selected metabolite list

skills.description: Use when a differential metabolomics experiment (e.g., control vs mutant lung cancer) yields a metabolite list or ranked statistics and you must identify significantly enriched KEGG pathways and prioritize them by biological impact.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-enrichment-interpretation Use when a differential metabolomics experiment (e.g., control vs mutant lung cancer) yields a metabolite list or ranked statistics and you must identify significantly enriched KEGG pathways and prioritize them by biological impact. When the input is already a generic gene/feature set without metabolite KEGG IDs or metabolite summary statistics (met_id, pval/padj, log2fc) — MetSEA ranking and the KEGG mapping cannot be constructed When the goal is lipid ontology interpretation rather than KEGG pathway enrichment — the lipidomics extension fetches LION associations at runtime and follows a different mapping path When no topology/impact interpretation is wanted and only a raw unfiltered fgsea run is needed — the adjusted p < 0.05 filter and impact-score combination would discard borderline pathways Interpret KEGG-based metabolite pathway enrichment results from EnrichMet by reading ORA (Fisher's Exact Test) tables and fgsea-based MetSEA tables (NES, adjusted p < 0.05) and ranking pathways by both statistical enrichment and topology-based pathway impact. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Interpret KEGG-based metabolite pathway enrichment results from EnrichMet by reading ORA (Fisher's Exact Test) tables and fgsea-based MetSEA tables (NES, adjusted p < 0.05) and ranking pathways by both statistical enrichment and topology-based pathway impact.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a generic gene/feature set without metabolite KEGG IDs or metabolite summary statistics (met_id, pval/padj, log2fc) — MetSEA ranking and the KEGG mapping cannot be constructed When the goal is lipid ontology interpretation rather than KEGG pathway enrichment — the lipidomics extension fetches LION associations at runtime and follows a different mapping path When no topology/impact interpretation is wanted and only a raw unfiltered fgsea run is needed — the adjusted p < 0.05 filter and impact-score combination would discard borderline pathways

skills.description: Use when preparing pathway-level kernel association tests (e.g., PaIRKAT) on metabolomics data where each metabolite must be assigned to a KEGG pathway graph with reaction-derived topology.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-graph-construction
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-graph-construction Use when preparing pathway-level kernel association tests (e.g., PaIRKAT) on metabolomics data where each metabolite must be assigned to a KEGG pathway graph with reaction-derived topology. The metabolite list lacks KEGG identifiers, so pathways cannot be populated with measured compounds The downstream analysis ignores pathway topography (unstructured kernel machine tests need no graph) Graph structure has not been examined and you intend to apply regularization blindly — the article notes it is important to examine graph structure before regularizing http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Constructs KEGG pathway graphs for metabolomics kernel association testing: fetch human pathway membership with KEGGREST's keggLink, restrict to pathways with ≥10 measured metabolites, and build igraph graphs with edges defined by KEGG reaction database connections. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Constructs KEGG pathway graphs for metabolomics kernel association testing: fetch human pathway membership with KEGGREST's keggLink, restrict to pathways with ≥10 measured metabolites, and build igraph graphs with edges defined by KEGG reaction database connections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolite list lacks KEGG identifiers, so pathways cannot be populated with measured compounds The downstream analysis ignores pathway topography (unstructured kernel machine tests need no graph) Graph structure has not been examined and you intend to apply regularization blindly — the article notes it is important to examine graph structure before regularizing

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains non-standard identifiers (e.g., RI-coded names from GC retention time) that must be converted to standard compound IDs before KEGG pathway enrichment in MeTEor.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-id-resolution
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-id-resolution Use when a metabolomics feature table contains non-standard identifiers (e.g., RI-coded names from GC retention time) that must be converted to standard compound IDs before KEGG pathway enrichment in MeTEor. Metabolites already carry standard database IDs (e.g., KEGG compound or HMDB identifiers) — conversion would be redundant The workflow requires fully automated, scripted identifier resolution — the MetaboAnalyst API is unavailable, so this workaround is manual and introduces a delay The identifiers are not metabolite/compound codes (e.g., gene or protein identifiers) — KEGGREST pathway mapping in MeTEor targets compounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Resolves non-standard metabolite identifiers (e.g., retention-time-coded RI codes like RI1150.81, RI1532.53, RI1557.73) into standard database IDs that can be mapped to known KEGG pathways, using the MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion web service as a manual workaround because its API is unavailable. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae178
skills.summary: Resolves non-standard metabolite identifiers (e.g., retention-time-coded RI codes like RI1150.81, RI1532.53, RI1557.73) into standard database IDs that can be mapped to known KEGG pathways, using the MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion web service as a manual workaround because its API is unavailable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metabolites already carry standard database IDs (e.g., KEGG compound or HMDB identifiers) — conversion would be redundant The workflow requires fully automated, scripted identifier resolution — the MetaboAnalyst API is unavailable, so this workaround is manual and introduces a delay The identifiers are not metabolite/compound codes (e.g., gene or protein identifiers) — KEGGREST pathway mapping in MeTEor targets compounds

skills.description: Use when rebuilding or refreshing metabolomics pathway-analysis libraries from KEGG, or when verifying reported library counts (e.g. ~130 species, ~3700 RaMP-DB pathways) after a knowledgebase update.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-library-construction
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-library-construction Use when rebuilding or refreshing metabolomics pathway-analysis libraries from KEGG, or when verifying reported library counts (e.g. ~130 species, ~3700 RaMP-DB pathways) after a knowledgebase update. Input is already a feature table of quantified peaks — pathway-library construction is a knowledgebase maintenance task, not a data-analysis step The analysis targets a species not supported by the KEGG pathway libraries (~130 species supported); pathway analysis will not apply Only MS2 spectra annotation is needed — use the MS2 Peak Annotation module with the spectra databases (~1.5 million MS2 spectra) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Rebuild MetaboAnalyst's KEGG pathway libraries by querying the KEGG REST API for compound and pathway membership across supported organisms, then validating compound-to-pathway mappings — this underpins pathway analysis expansion from 28 to ~130 species in MetaboAnalyst 6.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Rebuild MetaboAnalyst's KEGG pathway libraries by querying the KEGG REST API for compound and pathway membership across supported organisms, then validating compound-to-pathway mappings — this underpins pathway analysis expansion from 28 to ~130 species in MetaboAnalyst 6.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table of quantified peaks — pathway-library construction is a knowledgebase maintenance task, not a data-analysis step The analysis targets a species not supported by the KEGG pathway libraries (~130 species supported); pathway analysis will not apply Only MS2 spectra annotation is needed — use the MS2 Peak Annotation module with the spectra databases (~1.5 million MS2 spectra) instead

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics workflow has converted compound identifiers (e.g. HMDB IDs) to KEGG IDs via MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion and needs ranked pathway enrichment plus interactive pathway-map links highlighting the query metabolites.
