skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-map-url-generation Use when a metabolomics workflow has converted compound identifiers (e.g. HMDB IDs) to KEGG IDs via MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion and needs ranked pathway enrichment plus interactive pathway-map links highlighting the query metabolites. Metabolite identifiers are raw HMDB/KEGG-unmapped names — run MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion first, as the MetaboAnalyst API workaround is required before pathway mapping Goal is statistical pathway over-representation testing with p-values rather than MeTEor's occurrence-ranked pathway listing Data are not metabolomics feature trajectories processed in MeTEor (the enrichment module consumes MeTEor/MetaboAnalyst output) http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Generates ranked KEGG pathway enrichment output with interactive KEGG map URLs in which the user's identified metabolites are highlighted, as implemented in MeTEor's Pathway Enrichment module via KEGGREST on MetaboAnalyst-converted metabolite IDs. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae178
skills.summary: Generates ranked KEGG pathway enrichment output with interactive KEGG map URLs in which the user's identified metabolites are highlighted, as implemented in MeTEor's Pathway Enrichment module via KEGGREST on MetaboAnalyst-converted metabolite IDs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metabolite identifiers are raw HMDB/KEGG-unmapped names — run MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion first, as the MetaboAnalyst API workaround is required before pathway mapping Goal is statistical pathway over-representation testing with p-values rather than MeTEor's occurrence-ranked pathway listing Data are not metabolomics feature trajectories processed in MeTEor (the enrichment module consumes MeTEor/MetaboAnalyst output)

skills.description: Use when a table of significant metabolites carrying KEGG compound IDs must be associated with KEGG pathways for a chosen species and ranked by enrichment p-value, as in the MetENP ST000915 workflow.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-mapping Use when a table of significant metabolites carrying KEGG compound IDs must be associated with KEGG pathways for a chosen species and ranked by enrichment p-value, as in the MetENP ST000915 workflow. Input metabolites lack KEGG compound IDs or cannot be reaction-linked — met_pathways retains only metabolites with linked KEGG reactions, so counts would be empty or misleading. The species of interest has no entry in MetENP's korg / no available KEGG pathways — the package supports only 'all metabolite species with available KEGG pathways'. The goal is metabolite-class (RefMet category) enrichment rather than pathway association — use metclassenrichment/plot_met_enrichment instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Links significantly altered metabolites (with KEGG compound IDs) to species-specific KEGG reactions and pathways via MetENP's met_pathways (KEGGREST-based), then computes per-pathway enrichment scores and hypergeometric p-values with path_enrichmentscore. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.11.20.391912
skills.summary: Links significantly altered metabolites (with KEGG compound IDs) to species-specific KEGG reactions and pathways via MetENP's met_pathways (KEGGREST-based), then computes per-pathway enrichment scores and hypergeometric p-values with path_enrichmentscore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metabolites lack KEGG compound IDs or cannot be reaction-linked — met_pathways retains only metabolites with linked KEGG reactions, so counts would be empty or misleading. The species of interest has no entry in MetENP's korg / no available KEGG pathways — the package supports only 'all metabolite species with available KEGG pathways'. The goal is metabolite-class (RefMet category) enrichment rather than pathway association — use metclassenrichment/plot_met_enrichment instead.

skills.description: Use when an annotated feature table from LC-MS/MS metabolomics (e.g., GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker/SIRIUS annotations) needs KEGG compound-to-pathway assignment and cross-strain pathway comparison.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-mapping Use when an annotated feature table from LC-MS/MS metabolomics (e.g., GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker/SIRIUS annotations) needs KEGG compound-to-pathway assignment and cross-strain pathway comparison. The feature table has no compound annotations (e.g., raw MZmine CSV without GNPS2 FBMN/ChemWalker/SIRIUS annotation layers) — KEGG cross-referencing depends on already-annotated molecules The goal is spectral library matching or molecular networking itself rather than pathway-level interpretation of existing annotations Features of interest are outside KEGG coverage (e.g., novel natural products without KEGG compound entries) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Cross-references annotated molecular features from LC-MS/MS metabolomics of actinomycete strains (BRA006, BRA010, BRA177) against the KEGG database to assign metabolic pathways and compare shared pathways across strains. In the source study it mapped 39 annotated compounds to KEGG pathways, revealing shared purine metabolism with strain-specific intermediates. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Cross-references annotated molecular features from LC-MS/MS metabolomics of actinomycete strains (BRA006, BRA010, BRA177) against the KEGG database to assign metabolic pathways and compare shared pathways across strains. In the source study it mapped 39 annotated compounds to KEGG pathways, revealing shared purine metabolism with strain-specific intermediates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has no compound annotations (e.g., raw MZmine CSV without GNPS2 FBMN/ChemWalker/SIRIUS annotation layers) — KEGG cross-referencing depends on already-annotated molecules The goal is spectral library matching or molecular networking itself rather than pathway-level interpretation of existing annotations Features of interest are outside KEGG coverage (e.g., novel natural products without KEGG compound entries)

skills.description: Use when MetaboAnalyst outputs ('name_map.csv' and 'pathway_results.csv') are available and KEGG pathways with FDR ≤ 0.05 must be populated with their member metabolites annotated as HMDB IDs.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-metabolite-retrieval
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-metabolite-retrieval Use when MetaboAnalyst outputs ('name_map.csv' and 'pathway_results.csv') are available and KEGG pathways with FDR ≤ 0.05 must be populated with their member metabolites annotated as HMDB IDs. The input metabolite list already carries HMDB identifiers and its member metabolites per pathway, so no KEGG call-out is needed. No MetaboAnalyst 'pathway_results.csv' is available, or no KEGG pathway passes the FDR ≤ 0.05 threshold, leaving nothing to annotate. The analysis involves paired metabolomics-GWAS data rather than standalone datasets, which is outside the unpaired-data scope of metGWAS 1.0. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Module 1 of the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow: after MetaboAnalyst flags over-represented KEGG pathways by FDR, this skill retrieves the metabolite entries for each significant pathway via an RSelenium browser call-out to the KEGG database and maps them to HMDB IDs so downstream gene-set construction can proceed. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Module 1 of the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow: after MetaboAnalyst flags over-represented KEGG pathways by FDR, this skill retrieves the metabolite entries for each significant pathway via an RSelenium browser call-out to the KEGG database and maps them to HMDB IDs so downstream gene-set construction can proceed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input metabolite list already carries HMDB identifiers and its member metabolites per pathway, so no KEGG call-out is needed. No MetaboAnalyst 'pathway_results.csv' is available, or no KEGG pathway passes the FDR ≤ 0.05 threshold, leaving nothing to annotate. The analysis involves paired metabolomics-GWAS data rather than standalone datasets, which is outside the unpaired-data scope of metGWAS 1.0.

skills.description: Use when building species-specific metabolic networks from KEGG layouts and NCBI-RefSeq annotations and refining them with empirical metabolomics data to flag missing or disconnected reactions.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-network-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-network-mapping Use when building species-specific metabolic networks from KEGG layouts and NCBI-RefSeq annotations and refining them with empirical metabolomics data to flag missing or disconnected reactions. Input is a fully annotated, closed metabolic network (e.g. a validated genome-scale model in BiGG) where no missing-reaction discovery is needed Analysis goal is purely genomic annotation without metabolomics overlay, since the method requires empirical flux/intensity data to infer missing reactions http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Maps empirical metabolite intensity and boundary-flux data onto organism-specific metabolic networks built from KEGG base pathway layouts plus NCBI-RefSeq annotations, then flags missing or disconnected reactions. This enables empirical refinement of genome-predicted networks where database annotations are incomplete. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Maps empirical metabolite intensity and boundary-flux data onto organism-specific metabolic networks built from KEGG base pathway layouts plus NCBI-RefSeq annotations, then flags missing or disconnected reactions. This enables empirical refinement of genome-predicted networks where database annotations are incomplete.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a fully annotated, closed metabolic network (e.g. a validated genome-scale model in BiGG) where no missing-reaction discovery is needed Analysis goal is purely genomic annotation without metabolomics overlay, since the method requires empirical flux/intensity data to infer missing reactions

skills.description: Use when assembling pathway sets from KEGG (or Reactome/BioCyc) as ORA input for metabolomics data, to exclude pathways with fewer than 3 compounds from the over-representation analysis.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-set-filtering
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-set-filtering Use when assembling pathway sets from KEGG (or Reactome/BioCyc) as ORA input for metabolomics data, to exclude pathways with fewer than 3 compounds from the over-representation analysis. The goal is pathway-database comparison or visualisation rather than ORA, where pathway-size summaries may themselves be of interest rather than a filter criterion The pathway collection is a custom metabolite set designed by the user with intentionally small sets (fewer than 3 metabolites), which the >=3-compound rule would discard Pre-filters KEGG pathway sets (e.g., KEGG release 96 human pathway sets) to retain only pathways containing at least 3 mapped compounds before running ORA, so that Fisher's exact tests are not computed for degenerate, nearly-empty pathway sets. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Pre-filters KEGG pathway sets (e.g., KEGG release 96 human pathway sets) to retain only pathways containing at least 3 mapped compounds before running ORA, so that Fisher's exact tests are not computed for degenerate, nearly-empty pathway sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pathway-database comparison or visualisation rather than ORA, where pathway-size summaries may themselves be of interest rather than a filter criterion The pathway collection is a custom metabolite set designed by the user with intentionally small sets (fewer than 3 metabolites), which the >=3-compound rule would discard

skills.description: Use when deciding between the KEGG organism-specific human compound-only pathway set (261 pathways, mean size 30) and the KEGG reference compound-only set (377 pathways, mean size 45) for ORA on metabolomics data, and you need quantitative evidence of how much more/larger pathways in one set drive.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-set-property-characterization
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-set-property-characterization Use when deciding between the KEGG organism-specific human compound-only pathway set (261 pathways, mean size 30) and the KEGG reference compound-only set (377 pathways, mean size 45) for ORA on metabolomics data, and you need quantitative evidence of how much more/larger pathways in one set drive. skills.summary: Characterize and compare the structural properties of alternative KEGG pathway sets (organism-specific vs. reference) — pathway counts, mean sizes, and overlap coefficients — before choosing one for over-representation analysis (ORA) in metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to compare pathway databases other than KEGG (e.g., Reactome or BioCyc) — the article states an extensive comparison of pathway databases is beyond the scope of the paper. When the task is to simulate metabolite misidentification or evaluate its effect on ORA results — this skill only characterizes static pathway set properties, not misidentification-driven changes. When a ground-truth set of enriched pathways is available and you can evaluate ORA accuracy directly — the authors note no such ground-truth dataset exists, so this skill cannot be validated against known enriched pathways.

skills.description: Use when two KEGG organisms' metabolic networks have been reconstructed from KGML files and you need quantitative pairwise comparison scores (SimPi, SimSi, Psim, PsimW, Csim) in [0,1].
skills.name: kegg-pathway-similarity-index-computation
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-similarity-index-computation Use when two KEGG organisms' metabolic networks have been reconstructed from KGML files and you need quantitative pairwise comparison scores (SimPi, SimSi, Psim, PsimW, Csim) in [0,1]. When no organism pair has been reconstructed yet from KEGG — the indexes require KGML-derived reaction sets and pathway graphs as input When you need reconstruction from raw genomic/experimental data rather than comparison of KEGG-listed organisms (MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data) When the organisms are not both available in the KEGG database, since the reconstruction is based uniquely on KEGG http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Compute MetNet's local (SimPi, SimSi) and global (Psim, PsimW, Csim) similarity indexes that quantify structural and functional similarity between the metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms. The indexes are Jaccard-based at the pathway level and aggregate pathway-by-pathway results into organism-level comparison scores. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Compute MetNet's local (SimPi, SimSi) and global (Psim, PsimW, Csim) similarity indexes that quantify structural and functional similarity between the metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms. The target network is already complete in the reference database and no boundary-flux-inferred gaps exist to tabulate. Only gene-homology annotation (e.g. plain NCBI-RefSeq BLAST results) is available without empirical metabolomics/boundary-flux evidence, since the method's core is metabolomics-driven gap identification. The analysis targets a non-metabolic annotation gap (e.g. missing genes in a pathway file) rather than reactions absent from KEGG purine, pyrimidine, or nicotinate metabolism. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Tabulate reactions identified as missing from the KEGG database via MINNO-based boundary-flux inference, recording each reaction's pathway (purine, pyrimidine, nicotinate), the Borrelia species in which it is absent, and whether primary literature supports its existence. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501

The scores are not one-dimensional dissimilarity values from matched metabolite pairs (the validation logic assumes a single unimodal-to-trimodal score axis) You only need clustering or assignment of scores to mixture components, not a density-vs-density agreement check A fitted mixture is already benchmarked against a known distribution, making a non-parametric KDE redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Non-parametric density estimation of matched-pair metabolite-identification dissimilarity scores using a Gaussian-kernel KDE, used as an independent check that the EM-fitted three-component normal mixture in the MetPC pipeline captured the score distribution correctly. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9050103
skills.summary: Non-parametric density estimation of matched-pair metabolite-identification dissimilarity scores using a Gaussian-kernel KDE, used as an independent check that the EM-fitted three-component normal mixture in the MetPC pipeline captured the score distribution correctly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scores are not one-dimensional dissimilarity values from matched metabolite pairs (the validation logic assumes a single unimodal-to-trimodal score axis) You only need clustering or assignment of scores to mixture components, not a density-vs-density agreement check A fitted mixture is already benchmarked against a known distribution, making a non-parametric KDE redundant

skills.description: Use when a feature intensity table (features in rows, samples in columns) needs normalization factors and you want a density-based fold-change estimator robust to imbalanced percentages of up- and down-regulated features.
skills.name: kernel-density-fold-change-estimation
skills.search_text: kernel-density-fold-change-estimation Use when a feature intensity table (features in rows, samples in columns) needs normalization factors and you want a density-based fold-change estimator robust to imbalanced percentages of up- and down-regulated features. When serial QC samples are available for MS signal intensity correction and full high-quality feature selection — use the MAFFINNorm main function pipeline instead of standalone MDFCNorm on an uncorrected table When a large fraction of features are unchanged and the up/down-regulated balance is not a concern only if comparing estimators — median FC (MedianNorm) is a simpler alternative, though the article shows it is biased (1.39–1.63 vs true k=1.5) under imbalance http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates a metabolomics sample normalization factor by fitting a Gaussian kernel density to per-feature log2 fold changes against a reference sample and taking the fold change at maximal density (MDFC), which remains accurate even when up-/down-regulated features are imbalanced where the median FC is biased. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac355
skills.summary: Estimates a metabolomics sample normalization factor by fitting a Gaussian kernel density to per-feature log2 fold changes against a reference sample and taking the fold change at maximal density (MDFC), which remains accurate even when up-/down-regulated features are imbalanced where the median FC is biased.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When serial QC samples are available for MS signal intensity correction and full high-quality feature selection — use the MAFFINNorm main function pipeline instead of standalone MDFCNorm on an uncorrected table When a large fraction of features are unchanged and the up/down-regulated balance is not a concern only if comparing estimators — median FC (MedianNorm) is a simpler alternative, though the article shows it is biased (1.39–1.63 vs true k=1.5) under imbalance

skills.description: Use when raw in silico structure-candidate scores must be converted to calibrated P values so that correct vs. incorrect annotations can be separated — e.g. building COSMIC-style confidence scores from CSI:FingerID hits.
skills.name: kernel-density-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: kernel-density-pvalue-estimation Use when raw in silico structure-candidate scores must be converted to calibrated P values so that correct vs. incorrect annotations can be separated — e.g. building COSMIC-style confidence scores from CSI:FingerID hits. You want a literal probability that an annotation is correct — COSMIC's confidence score 'must not be mistaken as the probability that an annotation is correct' Input is raw MS/MS spectra rather than candidate scores — de novo formula assignment (SIRIUS 4, 10 ppm) and CSI:FingerID ranking must run first Estimating FDR for annotations far outside the reference-spectra training distribution — the authors note accurate FDR estimation from small-molecule fragmentation spectra will remain highly challenging http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Calibrates raw structure-candidate scores (e.g. from CSI:FingerID) by fitting a kernel density estimate to the proxy-decoy (wrong-candidate) score distribution, converting each hit score into a P value that becomes a direction-constrained feature for the COSMIC confidence-score SVM. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Calibrates raw structure-candidate scores (e.g. from CSI:FingerID) by fitting a kernel density estimate to the proxy-decoy (wrong-candidate) score distribution, converting each hit score into a P value that becomes a direction-constrained feature for the COSMIC confidence-score SVM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want a literal probability that an annotation is correct — COSMIC's confidence score 'must not be mistaken as the probability that an annotation is correct' Input is raw MS/MS spectra rather than candidate scores — de novo formula assignment (SIRIUS 4, 10 ppm) and CSI:FingerID ranking must run first Estimating FDR for annotations far outside the reference-spectra training distribution — the authors note accurate FDR estimation from small-molecule fragmentation spectra will remain highly challenging

skills.search_text: kernel-kmeans-clustering Use when samples are represented by one or more N x N similarity/kernel matrices (e.g. consensus matrices built with Monti et al. 2003) rather than raw feature tables, and you need cluster assignments, optionally with per-dataset or per-sample kernel weights. skills.description: Use when assessing how much kernel-association testing power depends on pathway graph fidelity — i.e., simulating Barabasi-Albert pathway graphs, permuting a known fraction of edges, and estimating empirical power of the PaIRKAT score test.
skills.name: kernel-machine-score-test-power-estimation
skills.search_text: kernel-machine-score-test-power-estimation Use when assessing how much kernel-association testing power depends on pathway graph fidelity — i.e., simulating Barabasi-Albert pathway graphs, permuting a known fraction of edges, and estimating empirical power of the PaIRKAT score test. Real-data analysis on the full COPDGene cohort (>1,000 observations) — the paper shows method p-value differences were indistinguishable for datasets with over 1,000 observations; performance differences were demonstrated via random subsets of 100–500 subjects, so power simulations on small subsets, not full-cohort testing, are the appropriate setting. The pathway graph is disconnected or sparse and has not been examined first — the paper states it is important to examine graph structure before applying regularization, and the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered performance on disconnected graphs. The goal is real metabolomics data processing (run-day median normalization, kNN imputation with k = 10, covariate adjustment) rather than simulation-based power assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Empirical power estimation for the PaIRKAT kernel machine score test (τ = 1) under simulated pathway-structured outcomes, quantifying how testing power degrades as incorrect (permuted) pathway edges are introduced at 10%, 40%, and 70% mismatch levels across pathway sizes p = 15, 30, and 45. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Empirical power estimation for the PaIRKAT kernel machine score test (τ = 1) under simulated pathway-structured outcomes, quantifying how testing power degrades as incorrect (permuted) pathway edges are introduced at 10%, 40%, and 70% mismatch levels across pathway sizes p = 15, 30, and 45.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real-data analysis on the full COPDGene cohort (>1,000 observations) — the paper shows method p-value differences were indistinguishable for datasets with over 1,000 observations; performance differences were demonstrated via random subsets of 100–500 subjects, so power simulations on small subsets, not full-cohort testing, are the appropriate setting. The pathway graph is disconnected or sparse and has not been examined first — the paper states it is important to examine graph structure before applying regularization, and the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered performance on disconnected graphs. The goal is real metabolomics data processing (run-day median normalization, kNN imputation with k = 10, covariate adjustment) rather than simulation-based power assessment.

skills.description: Use when testing phenotype–pathway (or feature-set) associations for metabolomics or similar high-dimensional 'Z' features whose dependence on the outcome is modeled as a kernel-weighted random effect rather than fixed covariates.
skills.name: kernel-machine-score-testing
skills.search_text: kernel-machine-score-testing Use when testing phenotype–pathway (or feature-set) associations for metabolomics or similar high-dimensional 'Z' features whose dependence on the outcome is modeled as a kernel-weighted random effect rather than fixed covariates. The graph is disconnected and you plan to use the unregularized normalized Laplacian kernel — the paper shows this hinders testing performance; use the regularized version or ignore topography You only have fixed covariate effects with no kernel/random-effect structure — ordinary linear regression suffices The full cohort exceeds ~1,000 observations and you expect to discriminate between kernel variants on a single full-data test — p-values were indistinguishable at that size; use downsampled subsets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits the semi-parametric kernel machine model g(Y)=Xβ+h(Z)+ϵ and computes a variance-component score test p-value, where h(Z) is a random effect with covariance proportional to a kernel matrix (e.g., a Gaussian kernel built on pathway features smoothed by a regularized normalized Laplacian, as in PaIRKAT with τ=1). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Fits the semi-parametric kernel machine model g(Y)=Xβ+h(Z)+ϵ and computes a variance-component score test p-value, where h(Z) is a random effect with covariance proportional to a kernel matrix (e.g., a Gaussian kernel built on pathway features smoothed by a regularized normalized Laplacian, as in PaIRKAT with τ=1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The graph is disconnected and you plan to use the unregularized normalized Laplacian kernel — the paper shows this hinders testing performance; use the regularized version or ignore topography You only have fixed covariate effects with no kernel/random-effect structure — ordinary linear regression suffices The full cohort exceeds ~1,000 observations and you expect to discriminate between kernel variants on a single full-data test — p-values were indistinguishable at that size; use downsampled subsets

skills.name: kernel-score-test-statistic-computation
skills.search_text: kernel-score-test-statistic-computation Use when testing association between a phenotype (e.g., log FEV1/FVC ratio or percent emphysema) and kernel-transformed, graph-regularized KEGG pathway data and a pathway-level p-value is required under H0: tau=0. The pathway graph structure has not been examined first — the article stresses it is important to examine graph structure before regularization, and the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered testing performance on disconnected graphs The pathway has fewer than 10 measured metabolites (the real-data analysis restricted to 28 KEGG pathways with measurements on at least 10 metabolites) The response is not a continuous phenotype appropriately modeled by the semi-parametric kernel regression framework with Gaussian covariate adjustment http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes pathway-level significance in PaIRKAT by evaluating a kernel-weighted quadratic-form score statistic Q on covariate-adjusted partial residuals and obtaining p-values via Satterthwaite's moment-matched scaled chi-square null distribution. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821

skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway graph structure has not been examined first — the article stresses it is important to examine graph structure before regularization, and the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered testing performance on disconnected graphs The pathway has fewer than 10 measured metabolites (the real-data analysis restricted to 28 KEGG pathways with measurements on at least 10 metabolites) The response is not a continuous phenotype appropriately modeled by the semi-parametric kernel regression framework with Gaussian covariate adjustment

skills.description: Use when an integrative clustering analysis combines multiple consensus-matrix kernels (e.g., four omic layers or simulated datasets A–D) with KLIC and you need to read the learned kernel weights as evidence of each dataset's relative information content, alongside ARI-based cluster recovery.
skills.name: kernel-weight-interpretation-across-datasets
skills.search_text: kernel-weight-interpretation-across-datasets Use when an integrative clustering analysis combines multiple consensus-matrix kernels (e.g., four omic layers or simulated datasets A–D) with KLIC and you need to read the learned kernel weights as evidence of each dataset's relative information content, alongside ARI-based cluster recovery. Only a single dataset/kernel is available — kernel weights require combining multiple datasets, and there is nothing to distribute weight across The integrative method is COCA (Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis), which does not learn per-dataset weights, so no weight interpretation is possible Input is raw feature data rather than consensus-matrix kernels — kernels must first be built via Consensus Clustering before weights exist http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Interprets the per-dataset kernel coefficients learned by KLIC (Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering) as a diagnostic of each dataset's informativeness and dispersion: equal, similarly dispersed datasets receive roughly equal weights, while noisy or less informative layers are down-weighted. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Interprets the per-dataset kernel coefficients learned by KLIC (Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering) as a diagnostic of each dataset's informativeness and dispersion: equal, similarly dispersed datasets receive roughly equal weights, while noisy or less informative layers are down-weighted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single dataset/kernel is available — kernel weights require combining multiple datasets, and there is nothing to distribute weight across The integrative method is COCA (Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis), which does not learn per-dataset weights, so no weight interpretation is possible Input is raw feature data rather than consensus-matrix kernels — kernels must first be built via Consensus Clustering before weights exist

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate or validate that a multiple kernel learning integrative clustering method down-weights noisy datasets: i.e., you have kernels from datasets with identical clustering structure but graded cluster separability and want per-dataset kernel weights.
skills.name: kernel-weight-separability-analysis
skills.search_text: kernel-weight-separability-analysis Use when you need to demonstrate or validate that a multiple kernel learning integrative clustering method down-weights noisy datasets: i.e., you have kernels from datasets with identical clustering structure but graded cluster separability and want per-dataset kernel weights. The datasets do not share the same underlying clustering structure — then kernel weights reflect genuine structural differences, not robustness to noise You need the real-data pan-cancer (Hoadley et al. 2014) analysis rather than the simulation study — use the klic-pancancer-analysis repo pipeline (Preprocessing, COCA, Kernel, KLIC) instead You want COCA (Cluster-of-Clusters Analysis) behaviour; this skill probes KLIC's multiple kernel learning weights specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A simulation-based diagnostic for KLIC (Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering, Cabassi and Kirk 2020) that verifies its multiple kernel learning step assigns larger weights to datasets with clearer clustering structure, by combining synthetic datasets that share a structure but differ in cluster separability (noise levels 0-3). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: A simulation-based diagnostic for KLIC (Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering, Cabassi and Kirk 2020) that verifies its multiple kernel learning step assigns larger weights to datasets with clearer clustering structure, by combining synthetic datasets that share a structure but differ in cluster separability (noise levels 0-3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets do not share the same underlying clustering structure — then kernel weights reflect genuine structural differences, not robustness to noise You need the real-data pan-cancer (Hoadley et al. 2014) analysis rather than the simulation study — use the klic-pancancer-analysis repo pipeline (Preprocessing, COCA, Kernel, KLIC) instead You want COCA (Cluster-of-Clusters Analysis) behaviour; this skill probes KLIC's multiple kernel learning weights specifically

skills.description: Use when you have a precomputed GWAS Catalog network object (e.g. GWASnetwork_discoverableGenesOnly RData) and need disease/trait-focused subnetworks around specific keyword-matched nodes for metGWAS 1.0 over-representation analysis.
skills.name: keyword-based-subnetwork-extraction
skills.search_text: keyword-based-subnetwork-extraction Use when you have a precomputed GWAS Catalog network object (e.g. GWASnetwork_discoverableGenesOnly RData) and need disease/trait-focused subnetworks around specific keyword-matched nodes for metGWAS 1.0 over-representation analysis. You need to build the GWAS network from raw GWAS Catalog records rather than reuse the precomputed discoverableGenesOnly network object Your trait of interest has no node matching the supplied keywords in the GWAS Catalog network (keyword filtering will yield no primary nodes) You require edges below the significance thresholds (Jaccard < 0.5 or FDR-corrected P > 0.05), which this workflow discards by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Extracts disease/trait-specific GWAS subnetworks from the metGWAS 1.0 GWAS Catalog network representation by retaining only significant edges (Jaccard >= 0.5, FDR-corrected P <= 0.05), filtering nodes by trait keywords, and pulling out each keyword node plus its first-neighbour subnetwork. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Extracts disease/trait-specific GWAS subnetworks from the metGWAS 1.0 GWAS Catalog network representation by retaining only significant edges (Jaccard >= 0.5, FDR-corrected P <= 0.05), filtering nodes by trait keywords, and pulling out each keyword node plus its first-neighbour subnetwork.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to build the GWAS network from raw GWAS Catalog records rather than reuse the precomputed discoverableGenesOnly network object Your trait of interest has no node matching the supplied keywords in the GWAS Catalog network (keyword filtering will yield no primary nodes) You require edges below the significance thresholds (Jaccard < 0.5 or FDR-corrected P > 0.05), which this workflow discards by design

skills.description: Use when running MetaboPAC's kinetic-equations approach on time-course relative-abundance (concMatrix/timeVec) data and a subset of kinetic terms for the reaction network are known a priori, so fluxes needed for penalty calculation must be inferred from metabolite rates of change.
skills.name: kinetic-equation-integration-into-flux-calculation
skills.search_text: kinetic-equation-integration-into-flux-calculation Use when running MetaboPAC's kinetic-equations approach on time-course relative-abundance (concMatrix/timeVec) data and a subset of kinetic terms for the reaction network are known a priori, so fluxes needed for penalty calculation must be inferred from metabolite rates of change. The data are not intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment — MetaboPAC does not consider transport reactions across intracellular compartments in eukaryotic systems No kinetic terms are known and the underdetermined systems cannot be constrained — the pseudoinverse solution requires known kinetic terms The goal is flux analysis on measured fluxomics data rather than inferring fluxes from time-course relative-abundance data, since MetaboPAC does not assume fluxomics data are available http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates hard-coded known kinetic rate equations into MetaboPAC's flux-calculation routines (calcFluxWithKinetics_generic.m and solveRF_KEapproach_generic.m) to convert smoothed concentration-derivative data into reaction rate profiles via the stoichiometric mass balance S·v = dx/dt, solving determined systems exactly and underdetermined systems via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Integrates hard-coded known kinetic rate equations into MetaboPAC's flux-calculation routines (calcFluxWithKinetics_generic.m and solveRF_KEapproach_generic.m) to convert smoothed concentration-derivative data into reaction rate profiles via the stoichiometric mass balance S·v = dx/dt, solving determined systems exactly and underdetermined systems via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment — MetaboPAC does not consider transport reactions across intracellular compartments in eukaryotic systems No kinetic terms are known and the underdetermined systems cannot be constrained — the pseudoinverse solution requires known kinetic terms The goal is flux analysis on measured fluxomics data rather than inferring fluxes from time-course relative-abundance data, since MetaboPAC does not assume fluxomics data are available

skills.description: Use when time-course relative abundance metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec) are available for a metabolic network whose kinetic equations are at least partially known, and absolute concentrations or response factors must be inferred without chemical standards.
skills.name: kinetic-equation-response-factor-optimization
skills.search_text: kinetic-equation-response-factor-optimization Use when time-course relative abundance metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec) are available for a metabolic network whose kinetic equations are at least partially known, and absolute concentrations or response factors must be inferred without chemical standards. Data are from extracellular or multi-compartment eukaryotic samples — MetaboPAC only applies to intracellular metabolomics in a single compartment and does not model transport reactions across intracellular compartments The metabolic network has no known kinetic equations and no additional biological constraints can be supplied (percKnownKinetics = 0 performance degrades relative to negative controls) Concentrations span a range where response factors are non-linear (ion suppression / limited linear dynamic range), since response factors are assumed constant with concentration http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Optimization-based inference of GC-MS response factors (and thus absolute metabolite concentrations) from relative abundance time-course data by exploiting metabolic mass balances and known kinetic equations, as implemented in MetaboPAC's kinetic equation (KE) approach. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Optimization-based inference of GC-MS response factors (and thus absolute metabolite concentrations) from relative abundance time-course data by exploiting metabolic mass balances and known kinetic equations, as implemented in MetaboPAC's kinetic equation (KE) approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from extracellular or multi-compartment eukaryotic samples — MetaboPAC only applies to intracellular metabolomics in a single compartment and does not model transport reactions across intracellular compartments The metabolic network has no known kinetic equations and no additional biological constraints can be supplied (percKnownKinetics = 0 performance degrades relative to negative controls) Concentrations span a range where response factors are non-linear (ion suppression / limited linear dynamic range), since response factors are assumed constant with concentration

skills.description: Use when producing KiNG-format 3D kinemage plots from a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file — e.g. as the legacy export for discrete or gradient coloring, or as the size/load-time baseline benchmarked against EMPeror.
skills.name: king-kinemage-file-generation
skills.search_text: king-kinemage-file-generation Use when producing KiNG-format 3D kinemage plots from a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file — e.g. as the legacy export for discrete or gradient coloring, or as the size/load-time baseline benchmarked against EMPeror. skills.description: Use when a paper reports k-means-derived subgroup counts (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-high 6/60) that must be re-tabulated into 2x2/2x4 contingency tables and tested against a clinical covariate such as Gleason grade.

skills.search_text: kmeans-subgroup-count-reconciliation Use when a paper reports k-means-derived subgroup counts (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-high 6/60) that must be re-tabulated into 2x2/2x4 contingency tables and tested against a clinical covariate such as Gleason grade. The clinical variable is continuous or ordered with more than the two reported grade levels, where Fisher's exact 2x2 setup is not appropriate. Subgroup counts are unavailable or do not sum to the stated cohort size, so margins of the contingency tables cannot be verified. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reconciles published k-means subgroup counts (e.g., 6/21/9/24 phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-low strata of 60 T2 prostate tumors) against grade/stage contingency tables and reproduces the reported Fisher-test independence conclusion. metabolomics/v3 10.1158/0008-5472.can-14-1490
skills.summary: Reconciles published k-means subgroup counts (e.g., 6/21/9/24 phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-low strata of 60 T2 prostate tumors) against grade/stage contingency tables and reproduces the reported Fisher-test independence conclusion.

skills.search_text: knn-gcf-classifier-training Use when paired genome–MS/MS samples are available and the goal is to classify query MS/MS spectra (reference or cryptic) into candidate GCFs via a k-nearest neighbor model over BGC similarity fingerprints. The query organism has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset (e.g. a fungal species dissimilar to PoDP-derived bacteria) — output will contain no answer The goal is to distinguish isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — the correlation-based approach lacks this resolution The dataset is not similar to the NPOmix training set — precision scores may not be reproducible http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Train and apply the NPOmix k-nearest neighbor classifier that links MS/MS spectra to biosynthetic gene cluster families (GCFs) using similarity BGC fingerprints built from BiG-SCAPE scores and MS/MS fingerprints built from GNPS modified cosine scores. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Train and apply the NPOmix k-nearest neighbor classifier that links MS/MS spectra to biosynthetic gene cluster families (GCFs) using similarity BGC fingerprints built from BiG-SCAPE scores and MS/MS fingerprints built from GNPS modified cosine scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query organism has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset (e.g. a fungal species dissimilar to PoDP-derived bacteria) — output will contain no answer The goal is to distinguish isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — the correlation-based approach lacks this resolution The dataset is not similar to the NPOmix training set — precision scores may not be reproducible

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (e.g. the cancerCell MetaboReport demo dataset) contains missing values from MNAR (below-detection-limit) or MAR mechanisms and you must restore a complete, NA-free intensity matrix before statistical analysis.
skills.name: knn-imputation-feature-table
skills.search_text: knn-imputation-feature-table Use when a metabolomics feature table (e.g. the cancerCell MetaboReport demo dataset) contains missing values from MNAR (below-detection-limit) or MAR mechanisms and you must restore a complete, NA-free intensity matrix before statistical analysis. The input is already a complete feature table with zero missing values — imputation would alter observed intensities unnecessarily. The goal is MetaboReport's full preprocessing-to-HTML-report workflow (statistical analysis, visualization, reporting) rather than imputation alone — use MetaboReport's run_app() Shiny app instead. Missingness requires model-based methods beyond the five MetaboReport supports (single value, 1/5 min, mean, median, KNN) — these are the only methods this skill covers. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs MetaboReport-style missing value imputation for metabolomics feature tables, covering k-nearest neighbor (KNN) imputation via the VIM package alongside single-value methods (constant 1, 1/5 minimum, mean, median) that target different missingness mechanisms (MNAR vs MAR). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Reconstructs MetaboReport-style missing value imputation for metabolomics feature tables, covering k-nearest neighbor (KNN) imputation via the VIM package alongside single-value methods (constant 1, 1/5 minimum, mean, median) that target different missingness mechanisms (MNAR vs MAR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a complete feature table with zero missing values — imputation would alter observed intensities unnecessarily. The goal is MetaboReport's full preprocessing-to-HTML-report workflow (statistical analysis, visualization, reporting) rather than imputation alone — use MetaboReport's run_app() Shiny app instead. Missingness requires model-based methods beyond the five MetaboReport supports (single value, 1/5 min, mean, median, KNN) — these are the only methods this skill covers.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics concentration table (CSV/.xlsx uploaded to Viime) contains missing values heuristically classified as MCAR per metabolite per group, and a neighbor-based imputation is preferred over missForest, mean, or median.
skills.name: knn-imputation-for-metabolomics
skills.search_text: knn-imputation-for-metabolomics Use when a metabolomics concentration table (CSV/.xlsx uploaded to Viime) contains missing values heuristically classified as MCAR per metabolite per group, and a neighbor-based imputation is preferred over missForest, mean, or median. Missing values are classified as MNAR (below-detection metabolites missing by group) — Viime imputes these with zero or half the minimum concentration instead of KNN The concentration table contains error conditions Viime flags, such as non-numeric concentration data or a missing/non-unique primary ID — these must be corrected before automatic imputation No OpenCPU/R backend is available (e.g., pure-Python environment), since KNN and missForest imputations in Viime are implemented with R packages, not Scikit-learn http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Imputes missing values in metabolomics concentration tables that have been classified as MCAR (Missing Completely At Random) using K-Nearest Neighbor imputation from the R 'impute' package, as one of the MCAR methods offered by Viime alongside missForest, mean, and median. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Imputes missing values in metabolomics concentration tables that have been classified as MCAR (Missing Completely At Random) using K-Nearest Neighbor imputation from the R 'impute' package, as one of the MCAR methods offered by Viime alongside missForest, mean, and median.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Missing values are classified as MNAR (below-detection metabolites missing by group) — Viime imputes these with zero or half the minimum concentration instead of KNN The concentration table contains error conditions Viime flags, such as non-numeric concentration data or a missing/non-unique primary ID — these must be corrected before automatic imputation No OpenCPU/R backend is available (e.g., pure-Python environment), since KNN and missForest imputations in Viime are implemented with R packages, not Scikit-learn

skills.description: Decision support for choosing among KNN imputation algorithms when a metabolomics dataset has missing values (MVs) arising from both MNAR (below LOD) and MAR mechanisms, and RMSE/MLCI comparisons are needed.
skills.name: knn-imputation-method-comparison
skills.search_text: knn-imputation-method-comparison Decision support for choosing among KNN imputation algorithms when a metabolomics dataset has missing values (MVs) arising from both MNAR (below LOD) and MAR mechanisms, and RMSE/MLCI comparisons are needed. When the dataset has no missing values or missingness is purely MAR/MCAR with no LOD component — the truncation-based machinery of KNN-TN offers no advantage and the article shows simpler methods can be equivalent (e.g. 'on the African Race data set there was no significant difference between any of the KNN imputation algorithms and mean imputation'). When metabolites have >75% missing values — the cleaning process removes them before imputation, so benchmarking KNN variants on them is inappropriate. When the user needs a non-KNN or non-truncated-distribution approach; this skill only covers the three KNN procedures described in the paper. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3365 A comparative evaluation skill for metabolomics missing-value imputation that benchmarks truncation-based KNN (KNN-TN) against correlation-based (KNN-CR) and Euclidean-based (KNN-EU) KNN procedures using RMSE and the metabolite list concordance index (MLCI) on simulated and real datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: A comparative evaluation skill for metabolomics missing-value imputation that benchmarks truncation-based KNN (KNN-TN) against correlation-based (KNN-CR) and Euclidean-based (KNN-EU) KNN procedures using RMSE and the metabolite list concordance index (MLCI) on simulated and real datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset has no missing values or missingness is purely MAR/MCAR with no LOD component — the truncation-based machinery of KNN-TN offers no advantage and the article shows simpler methods can be equivalent (e.g. 'on the African Race data set there was no significant difference between any of the KNN imputation algorithms and mean imputation'). When metabolites have >75% missing values — the cleaning process removes them before imputation, so benchmarking KNN variants on them is inappropriate. When the user needs a non-KNN or non-truncated-distribution approach; this skill only covers the three KNN procedures described in the paper.

skills.description: Use when a per-metabolite permeability or rule-based property classification requires XLogP3, but the descriptor is missing for the large majority of PubChem-mapped metabolite identifiers and correlated descriptors (MW, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RB) are available.
skills.name: knn-imputation-of-missing-xlogp3
skills.search_text: knn-imputation-of-missing-xlogp3 Use when a per-metabolite permeability or rule-based property classification requires XLogP3, but the descriptor is missing for the large majority of PubChem-mapped metabolite identifiers and correlated descriptors (MW, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RB) are available. When XLogP3 coverage is already adequate for the metabolite set — imputation only becomes necessary because 89% of MNXref entries lack an associated XLogP3 value. When metabolite identifiers cannot be translated to PubChem CIDs at all (no feature vector for kNN); in that case the article's convention is to classify the metabolite as not likely permeable rather than impute. When the analysis needs experimentally measured membrane permeability — this pipeline produces a Lipinski-style rule proxy, not a biophysical permeability measurement. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Fills missing predicted octanol/water partition coefficients (XLogP3) for MNXref metabolites by k-nearest-neighbour imputation over the other PubChem molecular properties (MW, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RB), because only 11894 of 110266 PubChem-mapped MNXref compounds (11%) carry an XLogP3 value. The completed property table feeds the Lipinski-style permeability classification used by COMMIT to mark transport reactions as candidates for reduced cost. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: Fills missing predicted octanol/water partition coefficients (XLogP3) for MNXref metabolites by k-nearest-neighbour imputation over the other PubChem molecular properties (MW, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RB), because only 11894 of 110266 PubChem-mapped MNXref compounds (11%) carry an XLogP3 value. The completed property table feeds the Lipinski-style permeability classification used by COMMIT to mark transport reactions as candidates for reduced cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When XLogP3 coverage is already adequate for the metabolite set — imputation only becomes necessary because 89% of MNXref entries lack an associated XLogP3 value. When metabolite identifiers cannot be translated to PubChem CIDs at all (no feature vector for kNN); in that case the article's convention is to classify the metabolite as not likely permeable rather than impute. When the analysis needs experimentally measured membrane permeability — this pipeline produces a Lipinski-style rule proxy, not a biophysical permeability measurement.

Input is raw LC-MS data (e.g. mzML) requiring peak picking and grouping first — tidyMass expects a processed feature table for the data-cleaning stage The feature table has not yet been filtered for noisy features (features with >20% MVs in QC or >50% MVs in all study groups should be removed before imputation) The table is already complete/imputed or is destined for a non-tidyMass pipeline whose data structure differs from the mass_dataset class http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 KNN-based imputation of remaining missing values (MVs) in an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table, performed with the massCleaner/massdataset tidyMass workflow after noisy-feature removal and before SVR normalization. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: KNN-based imputation of remaining missing values (MVs) in an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table, performed with the massCleaner/massdataset tidyMass workflow after noisy-feature removal and before SVR normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data (e.g. mzML) requiring peak picking and grouping first — tidyMass expects a processed feature table for the data-cleaning stage The feature table has not yet been filtered for noisy features (features with >20% MVs in QC or >50% MVs in all study groups should be removed before imputation) The table is already complete/imputed or is destined for a non-tidyMass pipeline whose data structure differs from the mass_dataset class

skills.description: Use when a DIMS/LC-MS peak table (X matrix of sample × m/z intensities) still contains missing values after Blank Filtering, Sample Filtering, Replicate Filtering and probabilistic quotient normalization, and a complete matrix is required before G-log transformation and PCA.
skills.name: knn-missing-value-imputation-peak-table
skills.search_text: knn-missing-value-imputation-peak-table Use when a DIMS/LC-MS peak table (X matrix of sample × m/z intensities) still contains missing values after Blank Filtering, Sample Filtering, Replicate Filtering and probabilistic quotient normalization, and a complete matrix is required before G-log transformation and PCA. Input is already a complete feature/peak matrix with no missing values (e.g. after Replicate Filtering removed sparse peaks) — imputation would be a no-op or add noise Missing values are so pervasive that most rows lack data; KNN imputation relies on having informative neighbours among the retained peaks You are working on raw spectral data (e.g. transient .dat files or unaligned peak lists) rather than the post-alignment, post-normalization X matrix — the article positions imputation in the data-cleansing stage after peak picking and alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A data-cleansing step in the Galaxy-M DIMS metabolomics workflow that fills missing peak-intensity values in the filtered X data matrix using K-nearest-neighbours (KNN) imputation on the filtered and normalized matrix, so that subsequent G-log transformation and PCA operate on a complete matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: A data-cleansing step in the Galaxy-M DIMS metabolomics workflow that fills missing peak-intensity values in the filtered X data matrix using K-nearest-neighbours (KNN) imputation on the filtered and normalized matrix, so that subsequent G-log transformation and PCA operate on a complete matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a complete feature/peak matrix with no missing values (e.g. after Replicate Filtering removed sparse peaks) — imputation would be a no-op or add noise Missing values are so pervasive that most rows lack data; KNN imputation relies on having informative neighbours among the retained peaks You are working on raw spectral data (e.g. transient .dat files or unaligned peak lists) rather than the post-alignment, post-normalization X matrix — the article positions imputation in the data-cleansing stage after peak picking and alignment

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an ML retention-time predictor (e.g., a Keras regression model on ECFP fingerprints) against a structure-free nearest-neighbor baseline over METLIN SMRT-like RT data stratified by Tanimoto similarity thresholds.
skills.name: knn-retention-time-baseline-regression
skills.search_text: knn-retention-time-baseline-regression Use when benchmarking an ML retention-time predictor (e.g., a Keras regression model on ECFP fingerprints) against a structure-free nearest-neighbor baseline over METLIN SMRT-like RT data stratified by Tanimoto similarity thresholds. Validation molecules have no training-set counterpart above 50% Tanimoto similarity — the nearest-neighbor RT estimate is meaningless at near-zero structural similarity The task is RT prediction itself rather than benchmarking — use the trained DLM, since at most thresholds the k-NN median is only a baseline that the DLM significantly outperforms Retention times were measured under a different chromatographic method than the training set, as the paper's projection-across-CMs analysis shows models may not transfer directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A naive k-NN baseline (k=3) that predicts LC-MS retention time as the median experimental RT of the three most Tanimoto-similar training molecules, used to benchmark deep-learning RT predictors (e.g., a Keras DLM on ECFP fingerprints) via threshold-stratified paired Wilcoxon tests. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: A naive k-NN baseline (k=3) that predicts LC-MS retention time as the median experimental RT of the three most Tanimoto-similar training molecules, used to benchmark deep-learning RT predictors (e.g., a Keras DLM on ECFP fingerprints) via threshold-stratified paired Wilcoxon tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Validation molecules have no training-set counterpart above 50% Tanimoto similarity — the nearest-neighbor RT estimate is meaningless at near-zero structural similarity The task is RT prediction itself rather than benchmarking — use the trained DLM, since at most thresholds the k-NN median is only a baseline that the DLM significantly outperforms Retention times were measured under a different chromatographic method than the training set, as the paper's projection-across-CMs analysis shows models may not transfer directly

skills.search_text: knn-spot-reassignment-sm-to-st Use when ST and SM data come from adjacent or serial tissue sections at different spatial resolutions and a unified spot-level metabolite-by-spot matrix (MIM) is needed before vertical integration. Data are already measured on the same tissue section at matching spatial resolution, so no cross-section alignment is needed Single-cell or subcellular resolution mapping is required — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only Aligning more than two adjacent sections or building 3D spatial omics — multi-section alignment is not implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reassigns spatial metabolomics (SM) spots from an adjacent tissue section onto spatial transcriptomics (ST) spot coordinates via K-nearest-neighbor matching and intensity aggregation, unifying both modalities to a consistent spatial resolution prior to SpatialMETA integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Reassigns spatial metabolomics (SM) spots from an adjacent tissue section onto spatial transcriptomics (ST) spot coordinates via K-nearest-neighbor matching and intensity aggregation, unifying both modalities to a consistent spatial resolution prior to SpatialMETA integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already measured on the same tissue section at matching spatial resolution, so no cross-section alignment is needed Single-cell or subcellular resolution mapping is required — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only Aligning more than two adjacent sections or building 3D spatial omics — multi-section alignment is not implemented

skills.description: Use when metabolomics or other high-dimensional mass-spectrometry data contain missing values arising both from metabolites below the detection limit (MNAR) and from random technical failures (MAR), and the analysis goal is to impute them accurately before downstream statistical testing (e.
skills.name: knn-truncation-imputation
skills.search_text: knn-truncation-imputation Use when metabolomics or other high-dimensional mass-spectrometry data contain missing values arising both from metabolites below the detection limit (MNAR) and from random technical failures (MAR), and the analysis goal is to impute them accurately before downstream statistical testing (e. Data contain no meaningful detection-limit truncation (e.g. purely random missingness with no LOD) — the article notes KNN-TN was no better than KNN-EU imputation in one of the three real data sets, where the MNAR component is absent or weak. Metabolites have more than 75% missing values — these are removed in the cleaning process, not imputed. Sample sizes are very small or missingness excessive, making truncated normal mean/variance estimation unstable and inflating RMSE variability for KNN-TN relative to KNN-CR. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A KNN imputation algorithm (KNN-TN) for high-dimensional metabolomics data that standardizes each metabolite against its truncated normal distribution — with the mass-spectrometer detection limit as the truncation point — to jointly account for MNAR (below-LOD) and MAR missingness, outperforming Euclidean- and correlation-distance KNN baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: A KNN imputation algorithm (KNN-TN) for high-dimensional metabolomics data that standardizes each metabolite against its truncated normal distribution — with the mass-spectrometer detection limit as the truncation point — to jointly account for MNAR (below-LOD) and MAR missingness, outperforming Euclidean- and correlation-distance KNN baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain no meaningful detection-limit truncation (e.g. purely random missingness with no LOD) — the article notes KNN-TN was no better than KNN-EU imputation in one of the three real data sets, where the MNAR component is absent or weak. Metabolites have more than 75% missing values — these are removed in the cleaning process, not imputed. Sample sizes are very small or missingness excessive, making truncated normal mean/variance estimation unstable and inflating RMSE variability for KNN-TN relative to KNN-CR.

skills.description: Use when input is an unfiltered KO abundance table (rownames = K numbers, colnames = samples) plus metadata with at least two groups, and per-KO statistics are needed before pathway/module enrichment.
skills.name: ko-abundance-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: ko-abundance-statistical-testing Use when input is an unfiltered KO abundance table (rownames = K numbers, colnames = samples) plus metadata with at least two groups, and per-KO statistics are needed before pathway/module enrichment. The input abundance table has already been prefiltered, since GRSA requires background feature information and prefiltering biases the threshold-free statistics. The input features are not K numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers (e.g. unstandardized metabolite IDs), because ID-to-feature matching against the modulelist will fail. The goal is a single-feature differential expression report rather than pathway/module-level enrichment; ko.test alone provides no pathway aggregation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Per-KO differential statistical testing of a KEGG KO abundance table against sample metadata grouping, using ko.test from the ReporterScore (GRSA) package, producing per-KO statistics that feed pathway-level reporter scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Per-KO differential statistical testing of a KEGG KO abundance table against sample metadata grouping, using ko.test from the ReporterScore (GRSA) package, producing per-KO statistics that feed pathway-level reporter scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input abundance table has already been prefiltered, since GRSA requires background feature information and prefiltering biases the threshold-free statistics. The input features are not K numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers (e.g. unstandardized metabolite IDs), because ID-to-feature matching against the modulelist will fail. The goal is a single-feature differential expression report rather than pathway/module-level enrichment; ko.test alone provides no pathway aggregation.

The input is already a KO (K number), compound (C number), or microbial-taxonomy abundance table — mapping would be redundant; use the matching built-in database instead The abundance table has been prefiltered to a candidate list, since GRSA requires the full background feature set to be threshold-free Feature identifiers cannot be resolved to gene symbols resolvable by the organism pathway database (e.g. unknown species without a KEGG org entry) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps gene-level (or compound/microbe-level) abundance tables onto KEGG Orthology (KO) identifiers using the ReporterScore package's gene2ko() function and organism pathway databases, so that generalized reporter score-based enrichment analysis (GRSA) can be run on pathway/module KO-level inputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116

skills.summary: Nonparametric differential-testing route of BiG-MAP.analyse: Kruskal-Wallis testing of cumulatively-sum-scaled (CUSUM) RPKM gene cluster abundance/expression values across sample groups, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, used where the zero-inflated Gaussian (ZIG) parametric route is inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when a normalized metabolite-by-sample concentration table must be converted into a conditional-dependence network, and sparse structure (zeroed metabolite pairs) plus both positive and negative partial correlations are required.
skills.name: l1-regularized-precision-matrix-estimation
skills.search_text: l1-regularized-precision-matrix-estimation Use when a normalized metabolite-by-sample concentration table must be converted into a conditional-dependence network, and sparse structure (zeroed metabolite pairs) plus both positive and negative partial correlations are required. Input data has not been mean- and stddev-normalized; the MetaboLINK GLASSO fit assumes the normalized table produced by the PCA-preprocessing step. The goal is to identify cell-type-specific sub-networks directly from raw concentrations; MetaboLINK first combines PCA loadings with GLASSO, so raw-table clustering without the PCA layer deviates from the method. A dense covariance or correlation analysis (no sparsity) is desired — L1 regularization intentionally zeroes out metabolite pairs with no conditional dependence. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimate a sparse inverse covariance (precision) matrix among metabolite features using the graphical lasso with cross-validated L1 regularization, then derive an edge list of partial correlations. This is the GLASSO step of the MetaboLINK pipeline applied to NMR metabolomics of hESC-derived neural cell populations. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fnins.2024.1520982
skills.summary: Estimate a sparse inverse covariance (precision) matrix among metabolite features using the graphical lasso with cross-validated L1 regularization, then derive an edge list of partial correlations. This is the GLASSO step of the MetaboLINK pipeline applied to NMR metabolomics of hESC-derived neural cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been mean- and stddev-normalized; the MetaboLINK GLASSO fit assumes the normalized table produced by the PCA-preprocessing step. The goal is to identify cell-type-specific sub-networks directly from raw concentrations; MetaboLINK first combines PCA loadings with GLASSO, so raw-table clustering without the PCA layer deviates from the method. A dense covariance or correlation analysis (no sparsity) is desired — L1 regularization intentionally zeroes out metabolite pairs with no conditional dependence.

Input data is already quantified concentration-based images — recalibration would double-correct signal No calibration standards of known concentration are available; the regression cannot be constructed without assigned standard values Performing drift correction or spike removal rather than intensity-to-concentration conversion — those are separate Pew2 tools (drift correction by polynomial fit, local mean/median filtering) http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Construct calibration curves from gelatin standards of known concentration to convert raw LA-ICP-MS signal intensities into quantified elemental images, as implemented in Pew2's built-in standardization tool. Regression per isotope yields intercept, gradient, r² and Sy,x coefficients used to transform sample signal data (e.g. 55Mn, 56Fe, 63Cu, 66Zn) into concentration-based images. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Construct calibration curves from gelatin standards of known concentration to convert raw LA-ICP-MS signal intensities into quantified elemental images, as implemented in Pew2's built-in standardization tool. skills.description: Use when an imported LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. 66Zn, 56Fe, 55Mn from Agilent/Thermo/PerkinElmer data) shows isolated pixel-scale spikes or regions of extremely low or high signal from instrument noise, and you want to suppress them without smoothing the rest of the image.
skills.name: la-icp-ms-image-noise-mitigation
skills.search_text: la-icp-ms-image-noise-mitigation Use when an imported LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. 66Zn, 56Fe, 55Mn from Agilent/Thermo/PerkinElmer data) shows isolated pixel-scale spikes or regions of extremely low or high signal from instrument noise, and you want to suppress them without smoothing the rest of the image. Input is already a filtered or calibrated image where spikes have been removed — reapplying the filter will not change valid pixels and could smooth real features. Spike removal is the wrong choice when the goal is drift correction across the acquisition direction; use Pew2's drift tool (polynomial renormalization within a user-defined background slice) instead. The artifact spans a contiguous region larger than the chosen local window — a local median filter cannot distinguish extended features from noise. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Mitigate instrument-noise artifacts in LA-ICP-MS elemental images by identifying individual pixel spikes against a local (mean or median) filter and replacing only the outlying values, using Pew2's Filtering tool or pewlib arrays. This preserves genuine spatial signal while removing sporadic high/low excursions caused by the instrument. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Mitigate instrument-noise artifacts in LA-ICP-MS elemental images by identifying individual pixel spikes against a local (mean or median) filter and replacing only the outlying values, using Pew2's Filtering tool or pewlib arrays. This preserves genuine spatial signal while removing sporadic high/low excursions caused by the instrument.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered or calibrated image where spikes have been removed — reapplying the filter will not change valid pixels and could smooth real features. Spike removal is the wrong choice when the goal is drift correction across the acquisition direction; use Pew2's drift tool (polynomial renormalization within a user-defined background slice) instead. The artifact spans a contiguous region larger than the chosen local window — a local median filter cannot distinguish extended features from noise.

When manual delineation of the ROI is preferred over automatic thresholding — Pew2's selection dialog supports both manual and automatic segmentation, and Otsu's method assumes a bimodal tissue/background distribution. skills.summary: Isolate regions of interest (ROIs) from the background of a LA-ICP-MS elemental image by thresholding the pixel intensity array, as implemented in Pew2's selection dialog with methods such as Otsu's, mean, and k-means thresholding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When manual delineation of the ROI is preferred over automatic thresholding — Pew2's selection dialog supports both manual and automatic segmentation, and Otsu's method assumes a bimodal tissue/background distribution. skills.description: Use when visualizing 2D LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g., 66Zn, 55Mn, 56Fe) for publication or interpretation and you must choose a colormap that does not introduce false perceptual boundaries or obscure signal structure.

skills.search_text: la-icp-ms-image-visualization Use when visualizing 2D LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g., 66Zn, 55Mn, 56Fe) for publication or interpretation and you must choose a colormap that does not introduce false perceptual boundaries or obscure signal structure. The image is a scalar map where a nonuniform colormap is deliberately used to highlight a specific threshold (e.g., segmentation masks from Otsu or k-means) — use a binary/qualitative palette instead. The data are 1D line scans or spot-wise profiles rather than a 2D raster image, where colormap choice is irrelevant. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Render LA-ICP-MS elemental images with perceptually uniform colormaps (e.g., Viridis) rather than default rainbow maps (e.g., Jet), so that displayed color transitions accurately reflect signal changes and perceptual artifacts from nonuniform contrast are avoided. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138

The data are 1D line scans or spot-wise profiles rather than a 2D raster image, where colormap choice is irrelevant.

skills.search_text: labeled-chromatographic-peak-classification Use when automRm quality scores for metabolite-sample pairs (qslog.tsv) exist and expert labels (0 = do not report, 1 = exclude from training, 2 = report) are available in manual_peakcheck.xlsx, and a peak-reporting ML model must be trained. skills.search_text: labeled-internal-standard-matching-across-platforms Use when LC-IM-MS data contain U13C-labeled internal standards and you need to quantify CCSN2 bias of measured CCS values against a DTCCSN2 reference library across ion mobility technologies or ionization modes. skills.description: Use when you have a large symmetric distance/similarity matrix (e.g. lipid-vs-lipid structural distances) and need only the few principal components for projection or visualization.

skills.search_text: lanczos-pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have a large symmetric distance/similarity matrix (e.g. lipid-vs-lipid structural distances) and need only the few principal components for projection or visualization. You need the full eigenspectrum or more than a handful of leading components — the Lanczos method is tuned to computing only the first n' < n principal components. The matrix is not symmetric/Hermitian — lambda-lanczos explicitly calculates eigenvalues/eigenvectors of symmetric (Hermitian) matrices. The input is raw abundance data rather than a distance matrix — LipidSpace builds the structural distance matrix (MCS + Jaccard) before PCA, so PCA directly on raw intensities is out of scope for this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes a principal component analysis on an n x n pairwise structural distance matrix using a header-only Lanczos-method implementation (lambda-lanczos), so that only the first n' < n components (default 7) are extracted instead of a full eigendecomposition. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes a principal component analysis on an n x n pairwise structural distance matrix using a header-only Lanczos-method implementation (lambda-lanczos), so that only the first n' < n components (default 7) are extracted instead of a full eigendecomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the full eigenspectrum or more than a handful of leading components — the Lanczos method is tuned to computing only the first n' < n principal components. The matrix is not symmetric/Hermitian — lambda-lanczos explicitly calculates eigenvalues/eigenvectors of symmetric (Hermitian) matrices. The input is raw abundance data rather than a distance matrix — LipidSpace builds the structural distance matrix (MCS + Jaccard) before PCA, so PCA directly on raw intensities is out of scope for this skill.
