The analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference library (NIST, Wiley, or SWGDRUG) — PS2MS enumeration and filtering is only triggered when no reference match is found in conventional screening The chemical structure of the NPS is already known — in that case spectrum can be predicted directly (e.g. NEIMS) with no need to subset a derivative database http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Reduces an extremely large enumerated derivative database (PS2MS enumerated ~422 million cathinone-like compounds) to a tractable candidate subset using rule-based filters: M+ mass-weight windows around the analyte's reference peak, drug-like criteria, ring-complexity rules, and synthesis-difficulty (SCScore) thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Reduces an extremely large enumerated derivative database (PS2MS enumerated ~422 million cathinone-like compounds) to a tractable candidate subset using rule-based filters: M+ mass-weight windows around the analyte's reference peak, drug-like criteria, ring-complexity rules, and synthesis-difficulty (SCScore) thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference library (NIST, Wiley, or SWGDRUG) — PS2MS enumeration and filtering is only triggered when no reference match is found in conventional screening The chemical structure of the NPS is already known — in that case spectrum can be predicted directly (e.g. NEIMS) with no need to subset a derivative database

skills.description: Use when a large-scale cohort metabolomics experiment (e.g. over 1,000 human plasma samples run over 44 days on an Agilent 1260 Infinity HPLC with Qtrap5500) yields a raw abundance matrix that must be filtered, drift-corrected and made complete before hierarchical RUV-III correction.
skills.name: large-scale-feature-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: large-scale-feature-matrix-processing Use when a large-scale cohort metabolomics experiment (e.g. over 1,000 human plasma samples run over 44 days on an Agilent 1260 Infinity HPLC with Qtrap5500) yields a raw abundance matrix that must be filtered, drift-corrected and made complete before hierarchical RUV-III correction. The input is already a complete, drift-corrected matrix with batch annotations—this skill would duplicate the filtering and imputation steps described in the hRUV workflow The study is a small single-batch metabolomics experiment where pooled-QC-based drift correction and inter-batch replicates are unnecessary; the method was designed for multi-batch cohort-scale studies The data matrix is derived from untargeted spectral features rather than targeted metabolite abundances, since the 50% detection filter and replicate-embedding design were validated on targeted LC-MS/MS panels http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 This skill handles the pre-processing of large-scale targeted metabolomics feature matrices (samples × metabolites) so they are clean, drift-corrected, and batch-annotated before inter-batch unwanted-variation removal. It covers filtering metabolites with >50% missingness, removing outlying QC measurements, imputing residual missing values (hRUV requires complete matrices), and organising batch/replicate design information from 96-well plate layouts. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: This skill handles the pre-processing of large-scale targeted metabolomics feature matrices (samples × metabolites) so they are clean, drift-corrected, and batch-annotated before inter-batch unwanted-variation removal. It covers filtering metabolites with >50% missingness, removing outlying QC measurements, imputing residual missing values (hRUV requires complete matrices), and organising batch/replicate design information from 96-well plate layouts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a complete, drift-corrected matrix with batch annotations—this skill would duplicate the filtering and imputation steps described in the hRUV workflow The study is a small single-batch metabolomics experiment where pooled-QC-based drift correction and inter-batch replicates are unnecessary; the method was designed for multi-batch cohort-scale studies The data matrix is derived from untargeted spectral features rather than targeted metabolite abundances, since the 50% detection filter and replicate-embedding design were validated on targeted LC-MS/MS panels

skills.description: Use when raw high-throughput LC-MS/MS MRM data from a large targeted metabolomics study (e.g. thousands of samples in dozens of batches, with BQCs) must be loaded and prepared for automated quantitation.
skills.name: large-scale-metabolomics-data-ingestion
skills.search_text: large-scale-metabolomics-data-ingestion Use when raw high-throughput LC-MS/MS MRM data from a large targeted metabolomics study (e.g. thousands of samples in dozens of batches, with BQCs) must be loaded and prepared for automated quantitation. The input is already a quantitated feature/abundance table rather than raw or mzML/mzXML MRM chromatogram data The data are untargeted (DDA) or otherwise not MRM ion chromatograms with a targeted-compounds method file Only a tiny single-batch run with no QC samples is involved, so batch-effect correction and large-scale ingestion machinery add no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Ingests large-scale targeted metabolomics MRM datasets (thousands of samples across many batches) into MRMQuant by converting vendor raw files to mzML/mzXML with msconvert and loading them with a targeted-compounds method file, producing loadable MATLAB MAT data and xlsx quantitation outputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Ingests large-scale targeted metabolomics MRM datasets (thousands of samples across many batches) into MRMQuant by converting vendor raw files to mzML/mzXML with msconvert and loading them with a targeted-compounds method file, producing loadable MATLAB MAT data and xlsx quantitation outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a quantitated feature/abundance table rather than raw or mzML/mzXML MRM chromatogram data The data are untargeted (DDA) or otherwise not MRM ion chromatograms with a targeted-compounds method file Only a tiny single-batch run with no QC samples is involved, so batch-effect correction and large-scale ingestion machinery add no value

Embeddings already exist as a GLEAMS .npy/.parquet pair — run only `gleams cluster`, not `gleams embed` The task is standard peptide identification of a small dataset, where a direct database search (e.g. MSGF+) is more appropriate than clustering millions of spectra The environment lacks a CUDA-enabled GPU, Linux, or Python 3.8, which GLEAMS requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Convert very large collections of MS/MS spectra (tens of millions, delivered as MGF/mzML peak-list files) into 32-dimensional GLEAMS embeddings and cluster them to group spectra generated by the same peptide, enabling joint analysis at a scale that defeats per-spectrum search tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1

skills.search_text: large-scale-smiles-set-processing Use when a hydrogen-to-functional-group enumeration step yields a very large SMILES set that must be reduced by per-molecule rule evaluation (drug-like filters, messy rings >7 SSSR, ΔSCScore) before downstream prediction. Input is a small curated compound list where full medicinal-chemistry filtering is unnecessary and would discard valid candidates The analyte spectrum already matches a reference library (NIST, Wiley, SWGDRUG), so no synthetic NPS database needs to be built You need spectra prediction or similarity ranking (NEIMS/DeepEI steps), not derivative filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Rule-based screening of very large enumerated SMILES sets (here ~422 million cathinone derivatives) using RDKit ring perception and 57 drug-like criteria from Virshup et al., plus ΔSCScore thresholds, to reduce derivatives to a manageable synthetic NPS database. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Rule-based screening of very large enumerated SMILES sets (here ~422 million cathinone derivatives) using RDKit ring perception and 57 drug-like criteria from Virshup et al., plus ΔSCScore thresholds, to reduce derivatives to a manageable synthetic NPS database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a small curated compound list where full medicinal-chemistry filtering is unnecessary and would discard valid candidates The analyte spectrum already matches a reference library (NIST, Wiley, SWGDRUG), so no synthetic NPS database needs to be built You need spectra prediction or similarity ranking (NEIMS/DeepEI steps), not derivative filtering

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a repository-scale collection of unannotated MS/MS spectra (e.g. mining MassIVE GNPS .mzML/.mzXML files into GeMS-style HDF5 subsets) to serve as self-supervised pre-training data for spectral models.
skills.name: large-scale-spectra-dataset-reconstruction
skills.search_text: large-scale-spectra-dataset-reconstruction Use when building or reproducing a repository-scale collection of unannotated MS/MS spectra (e.g. mining MassIVE GNPS .mzML/.mzXML files into GeMS-style HDF5 subsets) to serve as self-supervised pre-training data for spectral models. The input is already a curated reference spectral library (e.g. MoNA or NIST20) rather than raw repository-scale unannotated spectra — those libraries are annotation targets, not mining sources. You need spectra from conditions the mined collection does not cover, such as negative ionization mode or multiply charged precursor ions. You need MS1-level features such as isotopic patterns or adduct distributions — the mining targets tandem MS/MS spectra and metadata only. Reconstructs the GeMS (GNPS Experimental Mass Spectra) dataset by mining ~250,000 LC-MS/MS experiments from the MassIVE GNPS repository into a compact HDF5-based binary format of roughly 714 million unannotated MS/MS spectra, organized into quality-filtered GeMS-A, GeMS-B and GeMS-C subsets for deep-learning consumption. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Reconstructs the GeMS (GNPS Experimental Mass Spectra) dataset by mining ~250,000 LC-MS/MS experiments from the MassIVE GNPS repository into a compact HDF5-based binary format of roughly 714 million unannotated MS/MS spectra, organized into quality-filtered GeMS-A, GeMS-B and GeMS-C subsets for deep-learning consumption.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated reference spectral library (e.g. MoNA or NIST20) rather than raw repository-scale unannotated spectra — those libraries are annotation targets, not mining sources. You need spectra from conditions the mined collection does not cover, such as negative ionization mode or multiply charged precursor ions. You need MS1-level features such as isotopic patterns or adduct distributions — the mining targets tandem MS/MS spectra and metadata only.

skills.description: Use when an agent has embedded an independent MS/MS dataset (e.g. mzML files through `gleams embed`) and must validate the derived positive/negative spectrum pair counts against published figures before using them for evaluation or training.
skills.name: large-scale-spectrum-pair-dataset-verification
skills.search_text: large-scale-spectrum-pair-dataset-verification Use when an agent has embedded an independent MS/MS dataset (e.g. mzML files through `gleams embed`) and must validate the derived positive/negative spectrum pair counts against published figures before using them for evaluation or training. When the goal is to train GLEAMS on MassIVE-KB v1 data rather than verify pair statistics of an independent evaluation dataset — training uses 30 million PSMs compiled from MassIVE metadata TSVs, not pair-count verification. When spectra have not yet been embedded: pair generation presupposes completed `gleams embed` output and PSM identifications; applying this check to raw vendor files or unconverted data is premature. When no PSM identifications (peptide labels) are available for the dataset, since positive/negative labeling depends entirely on same-vs-different peptide sequence assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Verifies that a large-scale spectrum pair dataset generated from GLEAMS embeddings (e.g. from an independent phosphoproteomics dataset like PXD015943) matches the reported scale and labeling logic: positives are PSM pairs with identical peptide sequences, negatives are distinct-peptide pairs within a precursor mass tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Verifies that a large-scale spectrum pair dataset generated from GLEAMS embeddings (e.g. from an independent phosphoproteomics dataset like PXD015943) matches the reported scale and labeling logic: positives are PSM pairs with identical peptide sequences, negatives are distinct-peptide pairs within a precursor mass tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to train GLEAMS on MassIVE-KB v1 data rather than verify pair statistics of an independent evaluation dataset — training uses 30 million PSMs compiled from MassIVE metadata TSVs, not pair-count verification. When spectra have not yet been embedded: pair generation presupposes completed `gleams embed` output and PSM identifications; applying this check to raw vendor files or unconverted data is premature. When no PSM identifications (peptide labels) are available for the dataset, since positive/negative labeling depends entirely on same-vs-different peptide sequence assignments.

skills.description: Use when raw chemical tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz with SMILES, nominal.tsv.gz with compound names) need harmonization into standardized InChI identifiers before joining or publishing structure-organism records.
skills.name: large-tabular-chemical-data-handling
skills.search_text: large-tabular-chemical-data-handling Use when raw chemical tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz with SMILES, nominal.tsv.gz with compound names) need harmonization into standardized InChI identifiers before joining or publishing structure-organism records. Input is already a validated, InChI-bearing structure table — re-running sanitization can degrade correct salts, charged or dimeric molecules through an unwanted 'sanitization' step Records rely solely on chemical-name strings that are ambiguous or organism-tissue names — OPSIN name-to-structure translation relies on predefined rules that do not cover all cases and can commonly lead to incorrect translations http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Standardizes heterogeneous chemical structure inputs from large tabular natural-product datasets (SMILES, InChI, or bare compound names) into sanitized, dimer-free InChI representations, as done in the LOTUS curation pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Standardizes heterogeneous chemical structure inputs from large tabular natural-product datasets (SMILES, InChI, or bare compound names) into sanitized, dimer-free InChI representations, as done in the LOTUS curation pipeline.

skills.description: Use when building or retraining a protein chemical shift predictor from a large set of BMRB/PDB-matched proteins, or when reproducing/validating per-atom-type predicted-vs-experimental shift RMSD and MAE benchmarks against SHIFTX+.
skills.name: lars-regularized-linear-regression-training
skills.search_text: lars-regularized-linear-regression-training Use when building or retraining a protein chemical shift predictor from a large set of BMRB/PDB-matched proteins, or when reproducing/validating per-atom-type predicted-vs-experimental shift RMSD and MAE benchmarks against SHIFTX+. The target shifts are for RNA: NMRFx trains its RNA chemical shift predictor with FM models via stochastic gradient descent (Tribuo library), not LARS-regularized linear regression. The proteins contain non-standard residues or paramagnetic centers: these were explicitly excluded from the 1480-protein training set, so the fitted models are out of scope. You need an out-of-the-box shift prediction without retraining: use the existing NMRFx chemical shift prediction feature directly rather than refitting the regression models. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Trains per-atom-class LARS-regularized linear regression models that predict protein NMR chemical shifts from structural and sequence attributes, as used in NMRFx's protein chemical shift predictor, which was benchmarked against SHIFTX+ on the 61-protein ShiftX2 test dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-025-01812-8
skills.summary: Trains per-atom-class LARS-regularized linear regression models that predict protein NMR chemical shifts from structural and sequence attributes, as used in NMRFx's protein chemical shift predictor, which was benchmarked against SHIFTX+ on the 61-protein ShiftX2 test dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target shifts are for RNA: NMRFx trains its RNA chemical shift predictor with FM models via stochastic gradient descent (Tribuo library), not LARS-regularized linear regression. The proteins contain non-standard residues or paramagnetic centers: these were explicitly excluded from the 1480-protein training set, so the fitted models are out of scope. You need an out-of-the-box shift prediction without retraining: use the existing NMRFx chemical shift prediction feature directly rather than refitting the regression models.

skills.description: Decision support for selecting the subset of metabolomics features that discriminate between sample groups in a wide-format feature table.
skills.name: lasso-feature-selection-interpretation
skills.search_text: lasso-feature-selection-interpretation Decision support for selecting the subset of metabolomics features that discriminate between sample groups in a wide-format feature table. The goal is peak picking or preprocessing rather than statistical variable selection — use Galaxy-M or Workflow4Metabolomics for upstream feature identification instead. Only one sample group exists (no binary grouping variable), so penalized discriminative regression has no class to fit against. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 SECIMTools provides LASSO (and its companion Elastic Net) as advanced variable selection methods for metabolomics feature tables, using penalized regression to identify the best subset of discriminating features for a grouping variable. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1

skills.description: Use when imputing missing values in standardized, continuous-only datasets of moderate dimension where sparse linear regressions are appropriate, or when a lasso-penalized baseline is needed to compare against missForest or KNNimpute.
skills.name: lasso-regularized-em-imputation
skills.search_text: lasso-regularized-em-imputation Use when imputing missing values in standardized, continuous-only datasets of moderate dimension where sparse linear regressions are appropriate, or when a lasso-penalized baseline is needed to compare against missForest or KNNimpute. The dataset is high-dimensional such as the Insulin gene expression data (p=12,626 genes), where the paper states computation of MissPALasso is not feasible. The data contain categorical or mixed-type variables; for those the paper uses MICE or dummy-coded {-1,1} KNNimpute instead of MissPALasso. You need an imputation method without tuning parameters — the paper notes missForest has no such parameter, whereas MissPALasso requires cross-validated selection of λ. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run the MissPALasso imputation algorithm, which regresses each set of missing variables on the observed ones using an l1-penalty (lasso) within an alternating imputation scheme, and benchmark it against missForest and KNNimpute on standardized, continuous-only data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btr597
skills.summary: Run the MissPALasso imputation algorithm, which regresses each set of missing variables on the observed ones using an l1-penalty (lasso) within an alternating imputation scheme, and benchmark it against missForest and KNNimpute on standardized, continuous-only data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is high-dimensional such as the Insulin gene expression data (p=12,626 genes), where the paper states computation of MissPALasso is not feasible. The data contain categorical or mixed-type variables; for those the paper uses MICE or dummy-coded {-1,1} KNNimpute instead of MissPALasso. You need an imputation method without tuning parameters — the paper notes missForest has no such parameter, whereas MissPALasso requires cross-validated selection of λ.

skills.description: Use when you have a corpus of MS2 fragmentation spectra (e.g., MGF from GNPS or Mass Bank) and want unsupervised extraction of recurring molecular substructures without prior compound identification, or when testing that a spectral dataset decomposes into a target number of motifs.
skills.name: latent-dirichlet-allocation-topic-modeling
skills.search_text: latent-dirichlet-allocation-topic-modeling Use when you have a corpus of MS2 fragmentation spectra (e.g., MGF from GNPS or Mass Bank) and want unsupervised extraction of recurring molecular substructures without prior compound identification, or when testing that a spectral dataset decomposes into a target number of motifs. Data are simple mixtures with few metabolites or information-poor MS2 spectra (not generated by ramped or stepped collision energy) — the paper states MS2LDA works best on complex mixtures with information-rich spectra You need automated spectral matching that includes neutral losses — losses are not supported by spectral matching tools and had to be omitted in annotation A fast, simple tool suffices — MS2LDA is computationally more costly than simpler tools (though 'not prohibitively so') http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Adapts latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), a text-mining topic model, to mass spectrometry fragmentation data: MS2 spectra are converted into bag-of-fragments documents and decomposed via variational Bayesian inference into Mass2Motifs — co-occurring fragment/neutral-loss substructures — enabling unsupervised substructure discovery in metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Adapts latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), a text-mining topic model, to mass spectrometry fragmentation data: MS2 spectra are converted into bag-of-fragments documents and decomposed via variational Bayesian inference into Mass2Motifs — co-occurring fragment/neutral-loss substructures — enabling unsupervised substructure discovery in metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are simple mixtures with few metabolites or information-poor MS2 spectra (not generated by ramped or stepped collision energy) — the paper states MS2LDA works best on complex mixtures with information-rich spectra You need automated spectral matching that includes neutral losses — losses are not supported by spectral matching tools and had to be omitted in annotation A fast, simple tool suffices — MS2LDA is computationally more costly than simpler tools (though 'not prohibitively so')

skills.description: Use when you have latent embeddings (e.g., from ConditionalVAESM, Seurat CCA/RPCA, scVI, scANVI, scPoli, spaVAE, or PCA) computed on multiple spatial samples and need to quantify which integration balances batch correction and biology conservation.
skills.name: latent-embedding-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: latent-embedding-quality-evaluation Use when you have latent embeddings (e.g., from ConditionalVAESM, Seurat CCA/RPCA, scVI, scANVI, scPoli, spaVAE, or PCA) computed on multiple spatial samples and need to quantify which integration balances batch correction and biology conservation. When ground-truth labels are unavailable or cannot be manually annotated from H&E histological features, since the biology-conservation metric depends on them When evaluating embeddings from single-sample data with no batch structure — batch-correction metrics are undefined or trivially satisfied When the data are single-cell or subcellular resolution, as SpatialMETA and its benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scores integrated latent embeddings from spatial transcriptomics/metabolomics integration methods using scIB-style continuity, marker (biology conservation), and batch-correction metrics, after removing batch-biased features. This enables quantitative benchmarking of integration tools such as SpatialMETA against horizontal/vertical integration baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Scores integrated latent embeddings from spatial transcriptomics/metabolomics integration methods using scIB-style continuity, marker (biology conservation), and batch-correction metrics, after removing batch-biased features. This enables quantitative benchmarking of integration tools such as SpatialMETA against horizontal/vertical integration baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ground-truth labels are unavailable or cannot be manually annotated from H&E histological features, since the biology-conservation metric depends on them When evaluating embeddings from single-sample data with no batch structure — batch-correction metrics are undefined or trivially satisfied When the data are single-cell or subcellular resolution, as SpatialMETA and its benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-trained metabolomics VAE checkpoint and an mzLearn MS1 feature matrix, and need to visually verify that learned latent representations stratify samples by disease or age labels versus raw intensities.
skills.name: latent-space-umap-embedding-visualization
skills.search_text: latent-space-umap-embedding-visualization Use when you have a pre-trained metabolomics VAE checkpoint and an mzLearn MS1 feature matrix, and need to visually verify that learned latent representations stratify samples by disease or age labels versus raw intensities. The cohort was acquired in a mode other than HILIC positive LC — the released pre-trained encoder is specific to HILIC positive mode, so latents are not transferable. skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an aligned feature table — this skill evaluates reference-list sufficiency for alignment, not the alignment itself The LC-HRMS data have no retention time shifts relative to the reference chromatogram, so alignment accuracy is insensitive to reference-list size The goal is de novo feature detection rather than alignment against an existing reference feature list

skills.search_text: lc-im-ms-feature-count-comparison Use when comparing replicate-consistent feature counts between original and preprocessed LC-IM-MS data to quantify whether smoothing increased reproducible feature detection in a lipidomics or omics workflow. The data are raw MS files rather than already-generated feature lists — this skill evaluates downstream feature counts, it does not itself find features (use Lipid Annotator or a feature-finder after preprocessing with the PreProcessor). The analysis goal is lipid annotation throughput (e.g. the 19.4% increase in annotations for features found in at least 2 replicates) rather than replicate-consistent MS1 feature detection counts. Input data are not replicate LC-IM-MS runs (e.g. single-shot acquisitions), so replicate-set intersection across 3 replicates is undefined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Quantifies how multidimensional smoothing of LC-IM-MS raw data (via PNNL PreProcessor) changes the number of MS1 lipid features consistently detected across replicates, by intersecting replicate feature lists for original vs preprocessed data and computing the relative percentage increase. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: Quantifies how multidimensional smoothing of LC-IM-MS raw data (via PNNL PreProcessor) changes the number of MS1 lipid features consistently detected across replicates, by intersecting replicate feature lists for original vs preprocessed data and computing the relative percentage increase.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw MS files rather than already-generated feature lists — this skill evaluates downstream feature counts, it does not itself find features (use Lipid Annotator or a feature-finder after preprocessing with the PreProcessor). skills.search_text: lc-im-ms-multidimensional-smoothing Use when raw LC-IM-MS TOF profile data (e.g. Agilent 6560 IM-QTOF MassHunter .d) shows poorly defined low-abundance peaks, and you need a 3-point IM x 3-point LC moving-average smoothing before feature finding. The input is already a feature table or peak list — smoothing operates on raw profile-mode intensity values of TOF spectra The dominant problem is truncated high-abundance ions due to detector saturation — that requires the PreProcessor's saturation repair algorithm, not smoothing The number of requested smoothing points would equal or exceed half of the average base peak width (risk of destroying narrow IM peak resolution) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs the PNNL PreProcessor's multidimensional moving-average smoothing for raw LC-IM-MS TOF profile data, smoothing first in the IM (drift bin) dimension then the LC (frame) dimension to improve peak shapes of low-abundance ions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: Reconstructs the PNNL PreProcessor's multidimensional moving-average smoothing for raw LC-IM-MS TOF profile data, smoothing first in the IM (drift bin) dimension then the LC (frame) dimension to improve peak shapes of low-abundance ions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature table or peak list — smoothing operates on raw profile-mode intensity values of TOF spectra The dominant problem is truncated high-abundance ions due to detector saturation — that requires the PreProcessor's saturation repair algorithm, not smoothing The number of requested smoothing points would equal or exceed half of the average base peak width (risk of destroying narrow IM peak resolution)

skills.summary: DEIMoS processes LC-IMS-MS/MS metabolomics data by performing feature detection, feature alignment, CCS calibration, isotope detection, and MS/MS spectral deconvolution on N-dimensional m/z, drift time, and retention time data simultaneously, leveraging all dimensions to improve detection sensitivity and mitigate convolution artifacts in tandem mass spectra.

skills.summary: Apply a log transformation to the feature abundance matrix of a preprocessed LC-MS metabolomics dataset (stored in a MetaboSet object) before downstream statistical analysis, because log-transformed data better match model assumptions and avoid practical issues in notame's pipeline.

skills.description: Use when building an in-house LC-MS metabolite reference library from authentic-standard mzML data and retained adduct peaks (assigned m/z and RT) must be checked for distinguishability before export.
skills.name: lc-ms-adduct-annotation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-adduct-annotation Use when building an in-house LC-MS metabolite reference library from authentic-standard mzML data and retained adduct peaks (assigned m/z and RT) must be checked for distinguishability before export. Input is an already-annotated feature table from experimental (unknown) samples rather than authentic-standard mzML data — this skill builds the reference library, not downstream identifications The goal is de novo RT prediction transferable across different LC-MS methods — the article states RT is not yet consistently transferable across laboratory- or method-specific conditions The library must be built from MS/MS spectral data — metScribeR deliberately does not use or require MS/MS data for library construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Conflict-checks each retained adduct from authentic-standard LC-MS data against all other adducts in the library using user-defined m/z and RT tolerances, then annotates the exported library table. Ensures the final reference library contains only adduct peaks that can be confidently separated by the LC-MS method. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Conflict-checks each retained adduct from authentic-standard LC-MS data against all other adducts in the library using user-defined m/z and RT tolerances, then annotates the exported library table. Ensures the final reference library contains only adduct peaks that can be confidently separated by the LC-MS method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an already-annotated feature table from experimental (unknown) samples rather than authentic-standard mzML data — this skill builds the reference library, not downstream identifications The goal is de novo RT prediction transferable across different LC-MS methods — the article states RT is not yet consistently transferable across laboratory- or method-specific conditions The library must be built from MS/MS spectral data — metScribeR deliberately does not use or require MS/MS data for library construction

skills.description: Use when an in-house LC-MS standard library built with metScribeR contains metabolites or adducts with several 'good' labeled peaks at different RTs, and ambiguous entries must be flagged or excluded before exporting the library CSV.
skills.name: lc-ms-adduct-conflict-detection
skills.search_text: lc-ms-adduct-conflict-detection Use when an in-house LC-MS standard library built with metScribeR contains metabolites or adducts with several 'good' labeled peaks at different RTs, and ambiguous entries must be flagged or excluded before exporting the library CSV. Input is raw mzML data that has not yet been through metScribeR EIC extraction, peak finding, filtering, and manual peak review — conflict detection operates on the reviewed peak state, not raw chromatograms MS2-dependent library construction is required — metScribeR focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use MS/MS spectra for library construction A standard has only one labeled 'good' peak, or all competing peaks are below 50% of the primary peak's apex intensity or within the user-defined RT tolerance — no conflict exists to resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Detects 'crossed adducts' in a metScribeR metabolite standard library: cases where a standard or adduct has multiple manually labeled 'good' peaks at distinct retention times. Ambiguous entries exceeding intensity/RT thresholds are flagged and removed from the final library. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Detects 'crossed adducts' in a metScribeR metabolite standard library: cases where a standard or adduct has multiple manually labeled 'good' peaks at distinct retention times. Ambiguous entries exceeding intensity/RT thresholds are flagged and removed from the final library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzML data that has not yet been through metScribeR EIC extraction, peak finding, filtering, and manual peak review — conflict detection operates on the reviewed peak state, not raw chromatograms MS2-dependent library construction is required — metScribeR focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use MS/MS spectra for library construction A standard has only one labeled 'good' peak, or all competing peaks are below 50% of the primary peak's apex intensity or within the user-defined RT tolerance — no conflict exists to resolve

skills.description: Use when you have DeepRTAlign output (information_target.csv in mass_align_all_information) and need to map quantified peak areas or intensities to aligned feature groups for biomarker panels, classifier scoring, or targeted validation (e.g., sPRM/Skyline peak areas on an independent cohort).
skills.name: lc-ms-aligned-feature-result-parsing
skills.search_text: lc-ms-aligned-feature-result-parsing Use when you have DeepRTAlign output (information_target.csv in mass_align_all_information) and need to map quantified peak areas or intensities to aligned feature groups for biomarker panels, classifier scoring, or targeted validation (e.g., sPRM/Skyline peak areas on an independent cohort). Input is raw vendor or mzML spectra requiring feature extraction or RT alignment itself — run DeepRTAlign first; this skill only parses its result files. Downstream analysis requires peptide/protein-level identifications — this skill works on ID-free aligned MS feature groups (m/z, RT, intensity), not annotated peptides. The alignment result folder contains multiple projects' outputs — DeepRTAlign overwrites results in mass_align_all_information when projects share a folder, so parsed files may be mixed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Parses DeepRTAlign alignment outputs (information_target.csv and related mass_align_all_information result files) to extract per-sample aligned feature groups — sample, time, mz, charge, intensity, score, group — so aligned features can be mapped to targeted biomarkers and fed into downstream modeling such as the 15-feature HCC early-recurrence SVM classifier. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Parses DeepRTAlign alignment outputs (information_target.csv and related mass_align_all_information result files) to extract per-sample aligned feature groups — sample, time, mz, charge, intensity, score, group — so aligned features can be mapped to targeted biomarkers and fed into downstream modeling such as the 15-feature HCC early-recurrence SVM classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor or mzML spectra requiring feature extraction or RT alignment itself — run DeepRTAlign first; this skill only parses its result files. Downstream analysis requires peptide/protein-level identifications — this skill works on ID-free aligned MS feature groups (m/z, RT, intensity), not annotated peptides. The alignment result folder contains multiple projects' outputs — DeepRTAlign overwrites results in mass_align_all_information when projects share a folder, so parsed files may be mixed.

skills.description: Use when you have paired pre-dosing (blank) and post-dosing LC-MS/MS data from biological matrices (plasma, lung, urine, feces) and need to strip endogenous/background peaks to retain exogenous, dosage-related components non-targeted.
skills.name: lc-ms-background-subtraction
skills.search_text: lc-ms-background-subtraction Use when you have paired pre-dosing (blank) and post-dosing LC-MS/MS data from biological matrices (plasma, lung, urine, feces) and need to strip endogenous/background peaks to retain exogenous, dosage-related components non-targeted. The input is already a background-subtracted, exogenous-only feature table — re-running subtraction would discard components The goal is bridging prototypes to metabolites in already-identified components — MDRB data post-processing (m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, MS2 fragment similarity) is the appropriate next step, not background subtraction A targeted approach is preferred that requires prior prediction of the structures of herbal components and their metabolites http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Non-targeted LC-MS/MS background subtraction (PATBS) that identifies exogenous, dose-related components by comparing post-dosing sample feature lists against pre-dosing blank matrices, without requiring prior prediction of herbal component structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Non-targeted LC-MS/MS background subtraction (PATBS) that identifies exogenous, dose-related components by comparing post-dosing sample feature lists against pre-dosing blank matrices, without requiring prior prediction of herbal component structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a background-subtracted, exogenous-only feature table — re-running subtraction would discard components The goal is bridging prototypes to metabolites in already-identified components — MDRB data post-processing (m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, MS2 fragment similarity) is the appropriate next step, not background subtraction A targeted approach is preferred that requires prior prediction of the structures of herbal components and their metabolites

skills.description: Use when targeted dMRM LC-MS metabolomics data spanning multiple batches (e.g. a 419-sample, six-batch CoSTREAM plasma run) show batch-boundary drift in compound/IS ratios that must be corrected before statistical analysis.
skills.name: lc-ms-batch-correction-with-pooled-qc-samples
skills.search_text: lc-ms-batch-correction-with-pooled-qc-samples Use when targeted dMRM LC-MS metabolomics data spanning multiple batches (e.g. a 419-sample, six-batch CoSTREAM plasma run) show batch-boundary drift in compound/IS ratios that must be corrected before statistical analysis. Data is untargeted/open-source peak-processing output (e.g. mzML feature tables from OpenMS or MZmine) rather than vendor-integrated dMRM areas with compound/IS pairs — mzQuality processes peak-integrated data, not peaks. Only one batch is present or no pooled study QC (SQC) samples are distributed across batches — there is no SQC basis to derive between-batch correction factors. The goal is correcting variation that is biological rather than technical; mzQuality's IS-based and SQC-based adjustments target technical sources (e.g. sample 209's low median area was correctable via IS, indicating a technical cause). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Corrects between-batch drift in targeted LC-MS metabolomics by estimating compound-specific correction factors from pooled study quality control (SQC) samples and applying them to compound/IS area ratios, as implemented in mzQuality. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Corrects between-batch drift in targeted LC-MS metabolomics by estimating compound-specific correction factors from pooled study quality control (SQC) samples and applying them to compound/IS area ratios, as implemented in mzQuality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is untargeted/open-source peak-processing output (e.g. mzML feature tables from OpenMS or MZmine) rather than vendor-integrated dMRM areas with compound/IS pairs — mzQuality processes peak-integrated data, not peaks. Only one batch is present or no pooled study QC (SQC) samples are distributed across batches — there is no SQC basis to derive between-batch correction factors. The goal is correcting variation that is biological rather than technical; mzQuality's IS-based and SQC-based adjustments target technical sources (e.g. sample 209's low median area was correctable via IS, indicating a technical cause).

skills.description: Use when multi-batch LC/MS metabolomics raw files must be preprocessed so that between-batch differences do not corrupt peak detection, RT correction, feature alignment, or weak signal recovery, and when post-hoc correction will be applied to intensities.
skills.name: lc-ms-batch-effect-correction
skills.search_text: lc-ms-batch-effect-correction Use when multi-batch LC/MS metabolomics raw files must be preprocessed so that between-batch differences do not corrupt peak detection, RT correction, feature alignment, or weak signal recovery, and when post-hoc correction will be applied to intensities. Data are from a single batch with no batch structure, so batch-aware preprocessing and correction have nothing to adjust You already have an aligned feature table and only need intensity adjustment — post-hoc correction can adjust signal intensity but cannot fix misalignment or incomplete weak signal recovery You cannot reprocess raw data and only have a legacy feature table whose alignment errors were introduced by single-group preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A two-stage LC/MS metabolomics preprocessing skill that addresses batch effects at the peak detection/alignment stage (via batch-aware apLCMS) and can be combined with downstream batch effect correction (e.g., WaveICA, ComBat) for between-batch intensity differences. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: A two-stage LC/MS metabolomics preprocessing skill that addresses batch effects at the peak detection/alignment stage (via batch-aware apLCMS) and can be combined with downstream batch effect correction (e.g., WaveICA, ComBat) for between-batch intensity differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from a single batch with no batch structure, so batch-aware preprocessing and correction have nothing to adjust You already have an aligned feature table and only need intensity adjustment — post-hoc correction can adjust signal intensity but cannot fix misalignment or incomplete weak signal recovery You cannot reprocess raw data and only have a legacy feature table whose alignment errors were introduced by single-group preprocessing

skills.description: Use when LC-MS metabolomics data contain identical biological samples run in subsequent batches (between-batch replicate pairs) and you need to quantify which normalization restores cross-batch intensity correspondence.
skills.name: lc-ms-batch-effect-quantification
skills.search_text: lc-ms-batch-effect-quantification Use when LC-MS metabolomics data contain identical biological samples run in subsequent batches (between-batch replicate pairs) and you need to quantify which normalization restores cross-batch intensity correspondence. Data contain only pooled QC samples and no biological replicate pairs run across batches — replicate concordance cannot be computed, and the article explicitly flags reduction of QC-sample relative standard deviation as a benchmarking pitfall proxy Goal is differential abundance testing rather than quantifying cross-batch replicate correspondence; the article shows normalization choice produces distinct differential abundance results, which is a separate downstream analysis Input is a single-batch data set with no between-batch replicate structure, so the rescaled-difference MAD metric cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies residual between-batch LC-MS intensity differences by computing the MAD of rescaled intensity differences between between-batch replicate pairs under each normalization approach, benchmarking robust methods (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS) against QC-based and multivariate normalizers and an unnormalized baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06841
skills.summary: Quantifies residual between-batch LC-MS intensity differences by computing the MAD of rescaled intensity differences between between-batch replicate pairs under each normalization approach, benchmarking robust methods (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS) against QC-based and multivariate normalizers and an unnormalized baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain only pooled QC samples and no biological replicate pairs run across batches — replicate concordance cannot be computed, and the article explicitly flags reduction of QC-sample relative standard deviation as a benchmarking pitfall proxy Goal is differential abundance testing rather than quantifying cross-batch replicate correspondence; the article shows normalization choice produces distinct differential abundance results, which is a separate downstream analysis Input is a single-batch data set with no between-batch replicate structure, so the rescaled-difference MAD metric cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when a batch of raw LC-MS (or LC-IMS-MS, DDA/DIA, infusion) files needs a fast, omics-agnostic global quality assessment to spot outlier runs or instrument drift prior to targeted peak-metric analysis.
skills.name: lc-ms-batch-inspection
skills.search_text: lc-ms-batch-inspection Use when a batch of raw LC-MS (or LC-IMS-MS, DDA/DIA, infusion) files needs a fast, omics-agnostic global quality assessment to spot outlier runs or instrument drift prior to targeted peak-metric analysis. The goal is targeted, precursor-level QC (mass error, RT/arrival-time error metrics) rather than global batch-level inspection — PeakQC's auto-tracked/user-specified ion pipeline covers that. The input is already a feature table, peak list, or image set — this skill operates on raw MS1 signal from individual instrument files. The analysis requires resolution of individual chromatographic peaks from the image; the log-transformed time-vs-m/z rendering deliberately distorts intensity and does not resolve individual peaks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Batch-level visual inspection of LC-MS runs by rendering each sample as a log-transformed time-versus-m/z image from MS1 data, then running PCA over the batch to flag globally anomalous samples before deeper targeted QC. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00146
skills.summary: Batch-level visual inspection of LC-MS runs by rendering each sample as a log-transformed time-versus-m/z image from MS1 data, then running PCA over the batch to flag globally anomalous samples before deeper targeted QC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is targeted, precursor-level QC (mass error, RT/arrival-time error metrics) rather than global batch-level inspection — PeakQC's auto-tracked/user-specified ion pipeline covers that. The input is already a feature table, peak list, or image set — this skill operates on raw MS1 signal from individual instrument files. The analysis requires resolution of individual chromatographic peaks from the image; the log-transformed time-vs-m/z rendering deliberately distorts intensity and does not resolve individual peaks.

skills.description: Use when re-implementing or verifying how MetaboAnnotatoR computes per-feature match scores and ranks candidate metabolites from AIF pseudo-MS/MS fragment matches and m/z error, or when cross-checking rankScore/searchLib outputs.
skills.name: lc-ms-candidate-scoring-formula-implementation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-candidate-scoring-formula-implementation Use when re-implementing or verifying how MetaboAnnotatoR computes per-feature match scores and ranks candidate metabolites from AIF pseudo-MS/MS fragment matches and m/z error, or when cross-checking rankScore/searchLib outputs. Input is a DIA scheme other than AIF (e.g. SWATH) — MetaboAnnotatoR only supports AIF, so pseudo-MS/MS inputs would not be produced The feature table already contains final annotations and only needs summarizing — no candidate scoring is required Data were acquired on higher-mass-accuracy instruments such as Orbitraps without validation, since the scoring was tested on the article's serum datasets, not Orbitrap data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implements MetaboAnnotatoR's composite rank score that combines a bounded reciprocal m/z error term (S_mz = min(1/E, 1)) with a fragmentation-occurrence score (S_ma) over pseudo-MS/MS matched fragments, then ranks candidate metabolites per feature. Faithful replication of this scoring is needed to reproduce the package's ranked candidate lists. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Implements MetaboAnnotatoR's composite rank score that combines a bounded reciprocal m/z error term (S_mz = min(1/E, 1)) with a fragmentation-occurrence score (S_ma) over pseudo-MS/MS matched fragments, then ranks candidate metabolites per feature. Faithful replication of this scoring is needed to reproduce the package's ranked candidate lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a DIA scheme other than AIF (e.g. SWATH) — MetaboAnnotatoR only supports AIF, so pseudo-MS/MS inputs would not be produced The feature table already contains final annotations and only needs summarizing — no candidate scoring is required Data were acquired on higher-mass-accuracy instruments such as Orbitraps without validation, since the scoring was tested on the article's serum datasets, not Orbitrap data

skills.description: Use when raw centroid-mode LC–MS mzML files need chromatographic peak picking and feature detection prior to feature table generation in untargeted metabolomics.
skills.name: lc-ms-chromatographic-peak-detection
skills.search_text: lc-ms-chromatographic-peak-detection Use when raw centroid-mode LC–MS mzML files need chromatographic peak picking and feature detection prior to feature table generation in untargeted metabolomics. Input is already a preprocessed feature table or data matrix — peak picking has already occurred downstream of this skill The raw files are in profile mode or in a vendor format (e.g. Waters RAW) that has not been converted to centroid-mode mzML via msconvert The goal is post-detection data curation (Rt filter, blank filter, RSD filter, D-ratio filter) rather than locating peaks in raw chromatograms http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies TidyMS's continuous wavelet transform (CWT)-based peak-picking algorithm to raw LC–MS chromatograms and spectrum peaks via the MSData interface, enabling feature detection as (Rt, m/z) pairs in centroid-mode mzML files. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Applies TidyMS's continuous wavelet transform (CWT)-based peak-picking algorithm to raw LC–MS chromatograms and spectrum peaks via the MSData interface, enabling feature detection as (Rt, m/z) pairs in centroid-mode mzML files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed feature table or data matrix — peak picking has already occurred downstream of this skill The raw files are in profile mode or in a vendor format (e.g. Waters RAW) that has not been converted to centroid-mode mzML via msconvert The goal is post-detection data curation (Rt filter, blank filter, RSD filter, D-ratio filter) rather than locating peaks in raw chromatograms

skills.description: Use when raw, high-dimensional MS vectors (e.g., binned to 12000 m/z features, TIC-normalized) must be classified end-to-end with a learnable representation module and compared against baselines via cross-validation.
skills.name: lc-ms-classification-model-training
skills.search_text: lc-ms-classification-model-training Use when raw, high-dimensional MS vectors (e.g., binned to 12000 m/z features, TIC-normalized) must be classified end-to-end with a learnable representation module and compared against baselines via cross-validation. Severely imbalanced class distributions — the article notes MSMCE performance 'may still be limited in extreme cases, such as severely imbalanced class distributions' Very small sample sizes where deep models may fail to learn embedding representations, per the article's discussion Input is already a curated feature table suited to default-parameter traditional ML (SVM, logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost) without deep representation learning http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains deep learning classifiers (ResNet50/DenseNet121/LSTM/Transformer) on TIC-normalized, binned raw mass spectrometry data with the MSMCE multi-channel embedding module, using stratified k-fold cross-validation, early stopping, and a fixed hold-out test set to benchmark against traditional ML baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: Trains deep learning classifiers (ResNet50/DenseNet121/LSTM/Transformer) on TIC-normalized, binned raw mass spectrometry data with the MSMCE multi-channel embedding module, using stratified k-fold cross-validation, early stopping, and a fixed hold-out test set to benchmark against traditional ML baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Severely imbalanced class distributions — the article notes MSMCE performance 'may still be limited in extreme cases, such as severely imbalanced class distributions' Very small sample sizes where deep models may fail to learn embedding representations, per the article's discussion Input is already a curated feature table suited to default-parameter traditional ML (SVM, logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost) without deep representation learning

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS quantification experiment has been processed with multiple drift-correction/quantification strategies and you must quantify their agreement (e.g. test whether non-IS strategies correlate at Pearson r > 0.9).
skills.name: lc-ms-concentration-result-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: lc-ms-concentration-result-correlation-analysis Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS quantification experiment has been processed with multiple drift-correction/quantification strategies and you must quantify their agreement (e.g. test whether non-IS strategies correlate at Pearson r > 0.9). The data are raw peak areas or intensity drifts that still need correction — QuantyFey works as additional software to already integrated mass spectrometry data and does not provide integration capabilities; first run quantification, then correlate. The goal is fitting or optimizing calibration regression models (linear/quadratic, weights, standard levels) rather than comparing agreement between already-computed concentration results. Only one drift-correction strategy was applied, leaving no pairs of method columns to correlate. Cross-method agreement analysis for targeted LC-MS/MS quantification: compute pairwise Pearson correlations between concentration tables produced by different drift-correction strategies (default bracketing, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing, IS correction) to determine which strategies yield concordant results. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Cross-method agreement analysis for targeted LC-MS/MS quantification: compute pairwise Pearson correlations between concentration tables produced by different drift-correction strategies (default bracketing, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing, IS correction) to determine which strategies yield concordant results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw peak areas or intensity drifts that still need correction — QuantyFey works as additional software to already integrated mass spectrometry data and does not provide integration capabilities; first run quantification, then correlate. The goal is fitting or optimizing calibration regression models (linear/quadratic, weights, standard levels) rather than comparing agreement between already-computed concentration results. Only one drift-correction strategy was applied, leaving no pairs of method columns to correlate.

skills.description: Use when two separately peak-picked LC–MS metabolomics feature tables (samples × features with RT, m/z, FI) must be combined or compared — e.g., batch combination, discovery validation, or multicohort integration.
skills.name: lc-ms-cross-dataset-feature-matching
skills.search_text: lc-ms-cross-dataset-feature-matching Use when two separately peak-picked LC–MS metabolomics feature tables (samples × features with RT, m/z, FI) must be combined or compared — e.g., batch combination, discovery validation, or multicohort integration. The input is raw LC–MS data rather than separately peak-picked feature tables with RT, m/z, and FI per feature (peak-picking, e.g. with XCMS, must be done first). The two datasets are not similar LC–MS experiments or batches of the same type of samples — the method models inter-dataset shifts in RT, MZ, and FI and assumes features behave consistently with those shifts. Features have not undergone QC or RT trimming — the paper notes that improper QC prior to matching leads to poor matches. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Method for finding feature correspondence between two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics experiments or batches using only features' retention time (RT), m/z (MZ), and optionally feature intensity (FI) values, implemented in the M2S (Match 2 Sets) MATLAB toolbox. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03592
skills.summary: Method for finding feature correspondence between two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics experiments or batches using only features' retention time (RT), m/z (MZ), and optionally feature intensity (FI) values, implemented in the M2S (Match 2 Sets) MATLAB toolbox.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC–MS data rather than separately peak-picked feature tables with RT, m/z, and FI per feature (peak-picking, e.g. with XCMS, must be done first). The two datasets are not similar LC–MS experiments or batches of the same type of samples — the method models inter-dataset shifts in RT, MZ, and FI and assumes features behave consistently with those shifts. Features have not undergone QC or RT trimming — the paper notes that improper QC prior to matching leads to poor matches.

skills.description: Use when two peak-picked, conventionally aligned untargeted LC-MS data sets were acquired under different conditions (e.g. different gradient elution) and you need to determine overlapping features and concatenate abundances.
skills.name: lc-ms-dataset-pair-alignment
skills.search_text: lc-ms-dataset-pair-alignment Use when two peak-picked, conventionally aligned untargeted LC-MS data sets were acquired under different conditions (e.g. different gradient elution) and you need to determine overlapping features and concatenate abundances. The datasets were acquired from excessively disparate chromatographic techniques, such as between an RPLC dataset and a HILIC dataset Input datasets were acquired in different ionization modes (positive vs negative), or samples lack biological similarity and metabolomic overlap Abundance values have already been normalized or transformed in a way that removes ranked abundance order information http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Align a pair of disparately acquired untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data sets by matching known and unknown <m/z, retention time> features through metabCombiner's five-step workflow, producing a combined table of intersecting feature measurements with a reported weighted per-compound matching accuracy of approximately 90% on plasma data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03693
skills.summary: Align a pair of disparately acquired untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data sets by matching known and unknown <m/z, retention time> features through metabCombiner's five-step workflow, producing a combined table of intersecting feature measurements with a reported weighted per-compound matching accuracy of approximately 90% on plasma data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets were acquired from excessively disparate chromatographic techniques, such as between an RPLC dataset and a HILIC dataset Input datasets were acquired in different ionization modes (positive vs negative), or samples lack biological similarity and metabolomic overlap Abundance values have already been normalized or transformed in a way that removes ranked abundance order information

skills.description: Use when targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas (e.g. exported from MultiQuant 3.0.3) show intensity drift across injection order and internal standards are unavailable or unsuitable, requiring QC-based drift correction or calibration bracketing.
skills.name: lc-ms-drift-correction-bracketing
skills.search_text: lc-ms-drift-correction-bracketing Use when targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas (e.g. exported from MultiQuant 3.0.3) show intensity drift across injection order and internal standards are unavailable or unsuitable, requiring QC-based drift correction or calibration bracketing. Raw, unintegrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey works as additional software to already integrated MS data and provides no integration capabilities Datasets with no observable intensity drift across injection order, where standard internal-standard correction suffices Non-Windows environments where the standalone version cannot run and Apptainer setup is impractical (e.g. macOS, described as slow and difficult) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantify targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas against external calibration while correcting intensity drift, using QuantyFey's four strategies: internal-standard (IS) correction, statistical QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, and weighted bracketing, followed by linear/quadratic regression optimization. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Quantify targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas against external calibration while correcting intensity drift, using QuantyFey's four strategies: internal-standard (IS) correction, statistical QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, and weighted bracketing, followed by linear/quadratic regression optimization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw, unintegrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey works as additional software to already integrated MS data and provides no integration capabilities Datasets with no observable intensity drift across injection order, where standard internal-standard correction suffices Non-Windows environments where the standalone version cannot run and Apptainer setup is impractical (e.g. macOS, described as slow and difficult)

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence has been quantified under one or more drift correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) and you need to test whether injection-order-dependent bias remains.
skills.name: lc-ms-drift-residual-correlation-testing
skills.search_text: lc-ms-drift-residual-correlation-testing Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence has been quantified under one or more drift correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) and you need to test whether injection-order-dependent bias remains. The data are integrated peak areas rather than final quantified concentrations — QuantyFey performs quantification first and does not provide peak integration capabilities itself The goal is to compare correction methods on accuracy metrics (mean bias, limits of agreement, Passing-Bablok regression) rather than to detect residual injection-order drift The input comes from untargeted/untreated MS data where no external-calibration quantification table and no defined injection order exist http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies residual intensity drift after LC-MS/MS drift correction by computing Spearman rank correlation between injection position and determined concentration per compound, per correction strategy, using stats::cor.test in R. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Quantifies residual intensity drift after LC-MS/MS drift correction by computing Spearman rank correlation between injection position and determined concentration per compound, per correction strategy, using stats::cor.test in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are integrated peak areas rather than final quantified concentrations — QuantyFey performs quantification first and does not provide peak integration capabilities itself The goal is to compare correction methods on accuracy metrics (mean bias, limits of agreement, Passing-Bablok regression) rather than to detect residual injection-order drift The input comes from untargeted/untreated MS data where no external-calibration quantification table and no defined injection order exist

skills.description: Use when you must benchmark QC-based LC-MS normalization methods (QC-RLSC, rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) on simulated data with known drift ground truth and injected outliers, scoring median squared prediction error.
skills.name: lc-ms-drift-simulation-data-generation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-drift-simulation-data-generation Use when you must benchmark QC-based LC-MS normalization methods (QC-RLSC, rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) on simulated data with known drift ground truth and injected outliers, scoring median squared prediction error. You need to normalize a real experimental LC-MS dataset for downstream analysis — call the metanorm normalization workflow directly instead of generating simulations No drift-free ground truth is available — the squared-prediction-error benchmark of this skill cannot be computed on unlabelled real data You want to simulate from observed data via resampling while accounting for cross-metabolite correlations — the article proposes this as a different, more realistic simulation strategy not covered by the sine + Gaussian-noise scheme http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates in silico LC-MS runs with a known sine-based drift ground truth (Gaussian noise sd 0.3), injects 0–4 feature-specific outliers with 20–100%+ deviations at QC densities of one and two QCs per 10 samples, and benchmarks QC-RLSC, rLOESS, rGAM and tGAM by median squared prediction error across 200 runs. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Generates in silico LC-MS runs with a known sine-based drift ground truth (Gaussian noise sd 0.3), injects 0–4 feature-specific outliers with 20–100%+ deviations at QC densities of one and two QCs per 10 samples, and benchmarks QC-RLSC, rLOESS, rGAM and tGAM by median squared prediction error across 200 runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to normalize a real experimental LC-MS dataset for downstream analysis — call the metanorm normalization workflow directly instead of generating simulations No drift-free ground truth is available — the squared-prediction-error benchmark of this skill cannot be computed on unlabelled real data You want to simulate from observed data via resampling while accounting for cross-metabolite correlations — the article proposes this as a different, more realistic simulation strategy not covered by the sine + Gaussian-noise scheme

skills.description: Use when multiple LC-MS run feature tables (CSV with m/z, RT, area columns) must be aligned into consensus features beyond naive nearest-neighbor matching, i.e. all potential cross-run feature correspondences must be considered jointly.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-feature-alignment-algorithm-implementation Use when multiple LC-MS run feature tables (CSV with m/z, RT, area columns) must be aligned into consensus features beyond naive nearest-neighbor matching, i.e. all potential cross-run feature correspondences must be considered jointly. Input is raw mzML/MS data rather than already-extracted feature lists — G-Aligner only supports feature extraction results in CSV format with m/z, RT and area columns A fast, low-latency alignment is required — the multidimensional assignment problem is NP-Hard and G-Aligner's main limitation is lack of computing speed A pairwise nearest-neighbor alignment against a single reference run is sufficient, as in MZmine2's approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implement the G-Aligner three-step feature alignment pipeline for untargeted LC-MS metabolomics: after coarse RT registration with RANSAC and OBI-Warp, build a multipartite relation graph of features (nodes) and potential correspondences (edges), split it into connected components, and solve multi-run matching as an unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem with three combinatorial optimization algorithms. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Implement the G-Aligner three-step feature alignment pipeline for untargeted LC-MS metabolomics: after coarse RT registration with RANSAC and OBI-Warp, build a multipartite relation graph of features (nodes) and potential correspondences (edges), split it into connected components, and solve multi-run matching as an unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem with three combinatorial optimization algorithms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzML/MS data rather than already-extracted feature lists — G-Aligner only supports feature extraction results in CSV format with m/z, RT and area columns A fast, low-latency alignment is required — the multidimensional assignment problem is NP-Hard and G-Aligner's main limitation is lack of computing speed A pairwise nearest-neighbor alignment against a single reference run is sufficient, as in MZmine2's approach

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how an RT alignment tool degrades as retention-time shift variability increases, using simulated feature lists with known ground-truth correspondences.

skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol for evaluating LC-MS retention time alignment tools (e.g., DeepRTAlign vs OpenMS) on simulated proteomic and metabolomic feature lists with controlled RT shifts, quantifying precision and recall to establish generalizability boundaries of alignment performance.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-feature-alignment-evaluation Use when you need to quantitatively evaluate how accurately a feature alignment method (e.g. G-Aligner, MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS) aligns consensus features across multiple LC-MS runs against a manually annotated reference. skills.search_text: lc-ms-feature-correspondence-mapping Use when aligning feature lists from Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder, or TXT/CSV (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) across a large cohort of LC-MS runs where RT shifts are present and existing match-between-runs or warping tools fail. Input is already an identified peptide/protein table aligned via match between runs — DeepRTAlign is an ID-free feature-level correspondence method and its aligned MS features complement, not replace, identification-based alignment Samples are all from a single run or RT shifts are absent — no correspondence mapping is needed and the coarse alignment step would add no correction You need to improve raw quantification accuracy — the authors note alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction; this skill maps features across runs, it does not re-extract or re-quantify them http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Maps corresponding MS features across multiple LC-MS runs by reconstructing retention time shifts — combining a coarse alignment (pseudo warping function) that corrects RT drift piecewise against an anchor sample with a deep-learning-based direct matching model — so both monotonic and non-monotonic RT shifts are handled before quantitative or biomarker analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Maps corresponding MS features across multiple LC-MS runs by reconstructing retention time shifts — combining a coarse alignment (pseudo warping function) that corrects RT drift piecewise against an anchor sample with a deep-learning-based direct matching model — so both monotonic and non-monotonic RT shifts are handled before quantitative or biomarker analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an identified peptide/protein table aligned via match between runs — DeepRTAlign is an ID-free feature-level correspondence method and its aligned MS features complement, not replace, identification-based alignment Samples are all from a single run or RT shifts are absent — no correspondence mapping is needed and the coarse alignment step would add no correction You need to improve raw quantification accuracy — the authors note alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction; this skill maps features across runs, it does not re-extract or re-quantify them

The dataset contains no QC injections (e.g. QC-free studies) — use shiftCor_dQC with MLmethod = 'Combat' instead of the QC-RFSC pipeline, though KNN imputation via imputeM still applies in statAnalysis. Missingness exceeds what the 80% rule (Frule = 0.8) permits — features failing the filter are removed before imputation and should not be force-imputed.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-feature-table-annotation Use when you have a feature/peak table with accurate m/z, RT, and intensities from a fixed LC-MS assay (e.g., HILIC- or CSH-Q Exactive HF) plus a same-condition in-house m/z+RT library, and MS/MS spectra are absent, sparse, or not required for level 2 annotation. MS/MS spectra are available and matched — precursor accurate mass plus MS/MS matching alone annotates 578 compounds at MSI level 2 in this study, which is the stronger evidence route; m/z+RT-only matching is the fallback for features without usable MS/MS. The in-house library was acquired under different chromatographic or mass-spectrometric conditions — RT windows are then meaningless and matches would be spurious. You need MSI level 1 identification — this skill's output is level 2 by definition and cannot substitute for authentic standards with precursor mass, retention time, AND MS/MS matching. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate LC-MS features at MSI level 2 by matching accurate precursor m/z and retention time against in-house libraries acquired under identical chromatographic and MS conditions, explicitly without MS/MS spectral matching. This recovers additional annotations (e.g., six further acylcarnitines and 201 low-abundance compounds in urine) that MS/MS-only workflows miss. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Annotate LC-MS features at MSI level 2 by matching accurate precursor m/z and retention time against in-house libraries acquired under identical chromatographic and MS conditions, explicitly without MS/MS spectral matching. skills.description: Use when an XCMS-derived peak intensity matrix (retention time, m/z, peak intensity) shows batch or injection-order drift (visible intensity drift over run order, dispersed QCSs) and the corrected intensity matrix must be rebuilt without batch labels.
skills.name: lc-ms-intensity-matrix-reconstruction
skills.search_text: lc-ms-intensity-matrix-reconstruction Use when an XCMS-derived peak intensity matrix (retention time, m/z, peak intensity) shows batch or injection-order drift (visible intensity drift over run order, dispersed QCSs) and the corrected intensity matrix must be rebuilt without batch labels. The task still requires per-peak annotation or feature detection — this skill operates on an already-preprocessed XCMS intensity matrix, not raw mzXML/.d files. The analysis goal is biomarker discovery (PLS-DA, FDR < 0.05, VIP > 1) rather than batch-effect correction of the intensity matrix. A batch label is available and the original WaveICA (F-test, P < 0.05 threshold) is preferred, since it achieved a slightly shorter average distance among QCSs in PCA. Reconstructs a batch-effect-corrected LC-MS peak intensity matrix by inverting a MODWT (maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform) decomposition after removing batch-related independent components, as implemented in the WaveICA_2.0 R package for untargeted metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01839-7
skills.summary: Reconstructs a batch-effect-corrected LC-MS peak intensity matrix by inverting a MODWT (maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform) decomposition after removing batch-related independent components, as implemented in the WaveICA_2.0 R package for untargeted metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task still requires per-peak annotation or feature detection — this skill operates on an already-preprocessed XCMS intensity matrix, not raw mzXML/.d files. The analysis goal is biomarker discovery (PLS-DA, FDR < 0.05, VIP > 1) rather than batch-effect correction of the intensity matrix. A batch label is available and the original WaveICA (F-test, P < 0.05 threshold) is preferred, since it achieved a slightly shorter average distance among QCSs in PCA.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-intensity-noise-modeling Use when simulating synthetic LC-MS/MS peaks in mzML and noise standard deviation must scale with signal intensity (e.g. reproducing SMITER's noise model or validating a replacement injector).
