skills.description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics data matrix (rows = compounds, columns = samples) shows signal drift over acquisition order and batch effects that QC-only or non-robust normalization fails to fix, especially with outlier-contaminated features.
skills.name: lc-ms-metabolomics-batch-correction
skills.search_text: lc-ms-metabolomics-batch-correction Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics data matrix (rows = compounds, columns = samples) shows signal drift over acquisition order and batch effects that QC-only or non-robust normalization fails to fix, especially with outlier-contaminated features. When QCs are not representative of biological samples and the discrepancy is genuine biology rather than artifacts — metanorm's QCcheck flag will flag this, and forcing QC-RLSC on QCs only can distort biological signals (the paper recommends including both QC and replicate samples). When filtering decisions such as RSD/CV cutoffs on QC samples are the goal — the article warns that differences between QC and biological samples may invalidate RSD-based filtering, so this skill is for normalization, not QC-RSD feature filtering. When downstream multiple-testing correction of differential abundance results is needed — the article explicitly places multiple testing correction outside the scope of this normalization workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Corrects acquisition-order signal drift and between-batch effects in LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices using robust, QC- and replicate-aware normalization (tGAM as default, with rGAM, rLOESS and QC-RLSC alternatives) from the Metanorm R package, chosen for outlier resistance and verified via per-compound plots and PCA. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Corrects acquisition-order signal drift and between-batch effects in LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices using robust, QC- and replicate-aware normalization (tGAM as default, with rGAM, rLOESS and QC-RLSC alternatives) from the Metanorm R package, chosen for outlier resistance and verified via per-compound plots and PCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When QCs are not representative of biological samples and the discrepancy is genuine biology rather than artifacts — metanorm's QCcheck flag will flag this, and forcing QC-RLSC on QCs only can distort biological signals (the paper recommends including both QC and replicate samples). When filtering decisions such as RSD/CV cutoffs on QC samples are the goal — the article warns that differences between QC and biological samples may invalidate RSD-based filtering, so this skill is for normalization, not QC-RSD feature filtering. When downstream multiple-testing correction of differential abundance results is needed — the article explicitly places multiple testing correction outside the scope of this normalization workflow.

skills.description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics matrix (compounds x runs) shows signal drift, batch effects, or occasional disproportionately high/low outlier intensities that deteriorate QC-based normalization, and you need batch-aware robust correction with QC-sample representativeness checking.

skills.summary: Robust normalization of unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics feature matrices using the Metanorm R package's tGAM (default), rGAM, or rLOESS models, which fit cross-validated thin-plate-spline/LOESS drift curves with outlier downweighting, batchwise fitting, and a QCcheck hypothesis test that triggers re-fitting on biological samples when QC samples are unrepresentative.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When QC samples are known to be fully representative and you specifically require the prescribed QC-RLSC drift fit driven by QC samples only (QConly = TRUE) rather than robust sample-based normalization When input is not a raw unnormalized feature intensity matrix (e.g., already normalized data or a peak table lacking per-run order and batch annotations) When applying downstream multiple testing correction for differential abundance inference — the article states this is 'not in the scope of this work'

skills.description: Use when a detected chromatographic peak list from LC/MS metabolomics data must be quality-filtered before downstream statistical analysis, and true positives can be validated against a ground-truth peak list.
skills.name: lc-ms-metabolomics-peak-filtering
skills.search_text: lc-ms-metabolomics-peak-filtering Use when a detected chromatographic peak list from LC/MS metabolomics data must be quality-filtered before downstream statistical analysis, and true positives can be validated against a ground-truth peak list. Input is still raw LC/MS profile data with no detected peak list — this skill operates post peak detection, after the acute EIC extraction, EIC quality evaluation/filtering, and peak detection modules The goal is evaluating the quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) themselves (e.g., EICs with high background signals or a single peak), which is handled by the MCQ index / global zigzag index EIC-evaluation method instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filters 'bad' chromatographic peaks from LC/MS metabolomics data by scoring each detected peak against six quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, local zigzag index) and applying cutoff thresholds, combining metrics for higher Recall/Precision/F-Score than any single metric. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Filters 'bad' chromatographic peaks from LC/MS metabolomics data by scoring each detected peak against six quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, local zigzag index) and applying cutoff thresholds, combining metrics for higher Recall/Precision/F-Score than any single metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw LC/MS profile data with no detected peak list — this skill operates post peak detection, after the acute EIC extraction, EIC quality evaluation/filtering, and peak detection modules The goal is evaluating the quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) themselves (e.g., EICs with high background signals or a single peak), which is handled by the MCQ index / global zigzag index EIC-evaluation method instead

skills.description: Use when building a deep-learning peak-quality classifier for LC-MS feature lists and you need labeled EIC plot images spanning diverse sample types, LC and MS conditions, with each plot manually inspected to assign good or poor quality labels.
skills.name: lc-ms-metabolomics-training-data-preparation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-metabolomics-training-data-preparation Use when building a deep-learning peak-quality classifier for LC-MS feature lists and you need labeled EIC plot images spanning diverse sample types, LC and MS conditions, with each plot manually inspected to assign good or poor quality labels. You only need to score an existing feature table against an already-trained EVA/pyEVA model — in that case run the classifier rather than rebuilding a training corpus. Your EIC plots are exclusively from a single sample type and LC/MS condition; the skill's value comes from curating plots across diverse sample types, LC and MS conditions. Ground-truth peak quality can be obtained from an objective chromatographic metric rather than human judgment — manual inspection of every plot is the labor-intensive step this skill mandates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Prepares a manually labeled extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) image dataset from LC-MS metabolomics projects to train a CNN classifier (as in EVA) that discriminates good versus poor chromatographic peak shapes, with the goal of flagging false-positive metabolic features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01309
skills.summary: Prepares a manually labeled extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) image dataset from LC-MS metabolomics projects to train a CNN classifier (as in EVA) that discriminates good versus poor chromatographic peak shapes, with the goal of flagging false-positive metabolic features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to score an existing feature table against an already-trained EVA/pyEVA model — in that case run the classifier rather than rebuilding a training corpus. Your EIC plots are exclusively from a single sample type and LC/MS condition; the skill's value comes from curating plots across diverse sample types, LC and MS conditions. Ground-truth peak quality can be obtained from an objective chromatographic metric rather than human judgment — manual inspection of every plot is the labor-intensive step this skill mandates.

skills.description: Use when raw MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS data (e.g. mzML files from an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS) must be processed into quality-scored chromatographic peak reports without manual peak review.
skills.name: lc-ms-mrm-preprocessing
skills.search_text: lc-ms-mrm-preprocessing Use when raw MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS data (e.g. mzML files from an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS) must be processed into quality-scored chromatographic peak reports without manual peak review. The data are not MRM-mode LC-MS (e.g. untargeted DDA/DIA or GC-MS data); automRm is specific to MRM preprocessing Only a quantifier transition without any qualifier is available — the article states optimal performance requires at least one qualifier in addition to the quantifier The sample batch is excessively dirty, very-low-input, or from a new LC method with no relevant training data — manual peak review is the recommended retreat http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Fully automatic preprocessing of LC-MS data recorded in MRM mode using machine learning for chromatographic peak detection and quality-controlled peak reporting, as implemented in the automRm R package, replacing manual peak review. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05224
skills.summary: Fully automatic preprocessing of LC-MS data recorded in MRM mode using machine learning for chromatographic peak detection and quality-controlled peak reporting, as implemented in the automRm R package, replacing manual peak review.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not MRM-mode LC-MS (e.g. untargeted DDA/DIA or GC-MS data); automRm is specific to MRM preprocessing Only a quantifier transition without any qualifier is available — the article states optimal performance requires at least one qualifier in addition to the quantifier The sample batch is excessively dirty, very-low-input, or from a new LC method with no relevant training data — manual peak review is the recommended retreat

skills.description: Use when a margheRita mRList from MS-Dial LC-MS/MS profiling (e.g. the Urine dataset) has passed QC/filtering and sample abundances must be normalized, with PQN or log/reference methods.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-ms-feature-abundance-normalization Use when a margheRita mRList from MS-Dial LC-MS/MS profiling (e.g. the Urine dataset) has passed QC/filtering and sample abundances must be normalized, with PQN or log/reference methods. mRList$metab_ann already contains a 'reference' column, so calc_reference() should not regenerate the PQN reference profile The dataset lacks QC samples, since the default reference profile is built from medians of QC samples The data is a raw MS-Dial export that has not yet been loaded and quality-controlled (e.g. m/z, NA and CV filtering) in margheRita http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Normalization of LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature abundance matrices using the margheRita R package, in particular probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) of a filtered mRList object derived from MS-Dial output. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.06.20.599545
skills.summary: Normalization of LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature abundance matrices using the margheRita R package, in particular probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) of a filtered mRList object derived from MS-Dial output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: mRList$metab_ann already contains a 'reference' column, so calc_reference() should not regenerate the PQN reference profile The dataset lacks QC samples, since the default reference profile is built from medians of QC samples The data is a raw MS-Dial export that has not yet been loaded and quality-controlled (e.g. m/z, NA and CV filtering) in margheRita

skills.description: Use when you have MCNs derived from multiple mass-spectrometry data types (e.g. LC-MS/MS and EI GC-MS) and need to assess whether network-level properties such as modularity or scale-free degree behaviour are consistent across platforms.
skills.name: lc-ms-ms-gc-ms-network-comparison
skills.search_text: lc-ms-ms-gc-ms-network-comparison Use when you have MCNs derived from multiple mass-spectrometry data types (e.g. LC-MS/MS and EI GC-MS) and need to assess whether network-level properties such as modularity or scale-free degree behaviour are consistent across platforms. When the input is a raw spectral file (mzML, .d, .mgf) rather than an already-built MCN graph — building the network is a separate upstream skill. When the goal is to compare community *membership* between platforms (e.g. shared metabolites) rather than network-level statistics such as modularity or degree distributions. When only a single data type (one LC-MS/MS run or one EI GC-MS run) is available and cross-platform consistency cannot be evaluated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Compares the topology of molecular community networks (MCNs) built from both LC-MS/MS and EI GC-MS untargeted metabolomics data, quantifying modularity and power-law degree distributions to test whether community structure is a general property across mass-spectrometry platforms. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Compares the topology of molecular community networks (MCNs) built from both LC-MS/MS and EI GC-MS untargeted metabolomics data, quantifying modularity and power-law degree distributions to test whether community structure is a general property across mass-spectrometry platforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is a raw spectral file (mzML, .d, .mgf) rather than an already-built MCN graph — building the network is a separate upstream skill. When the goal is to compare community *membership* between platforms (e.g. shared metabolites) rather than network-level statistics such as modularity or degree distributions. When only a single data type (one LC-MS/MS run or one EI GC-MS run) is available and cross-platform consistency cannot be evaluated.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-ms-quality-control-job-configuration Use when Thermo Orbitrap .raw files are being written during an active LC-MS/MS run and you need near-real-time QC (instrument sensitivity, retention time shifts, mass accuracy) against a sequence .csv and library .msp. skills.search_text: lc-ms-ms2-feature-recognition Use when processing DDA LC-MS metabolomics mzXML files where conventional peak picking (XCMS-style) misses low-abundance or bad peak-shape features, and you want to quantify or recover those lost features via their MS2 spectra. skills.summary: Rescue metabolic features missed by conventional peak picking by detecting features with poor chromatographic peak shapes that nonetheless have MS2 spectra, using JPA's MS2 recognition (MR) strategy on raw LC-MS mzXML data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use find.level3features when processing full-scan or DIA data sets — MR extraction requires DDA data with MS2 spectra. Do not use when the goal is multi-sample alignment-driven analysis without per-sample rescue quantification — alignment (peak.alignment) applies only after feature extraction across samples. Do not use when features already exist in the table (PP or MR); duplicates are not re-added.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-mz-to-pathway-mapping Use when LC-MS peak lists of m/z features (optionally with MS2-annotated compound names from pooled-QC spectra) need to be interpreted as pathway-level biology, e.g. identifying pathways changed between treatment groups in untargeted metabolomics. skills.summary: Maps LC-MS m/z features (and MS2-annotated compounds) onto metabolic pathway sets using the mummichog algorithm as implemented in MetaboAnalyst 6.0 / MetaboAnalystR 4.0, combining ORA/hypergeometric and rank-based GSEA enrichment to identify affected pathways without requiring named metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a list of already-named metabolites rather than m/z features — standard metabolite set enrichment analysis is more appropriate than mummichog's m/z-based mapping Input is raw MS vendor files still needing peak picking — this skill assumes an already-extracted LC-MS peak list (spectra processing is a separate upstream module, e.g. asari/OptiLCMS) No pathway-level question exists and the goal is only univariate statistics or biomarker analysis on the feature table

skills.description: Use when processing LC/MS profile data (e.g. Agilent HPLC–Q-TOF Premier) where extracted ion chromatograms must be quality-scored and filtered prior to CWT-based chromatographic peak detection, or when detected peaks need to be ranked by sharpness, peak significance level, or zigzag index to.
skills.name: lc-ms-noise-zigzag-assessment
skills.search_text: lc-ms-noise-zigzag-assessment Use when processing LC/MS profile data (e.g. Agilent HPLC–Q-TOF Premier) where extracted ion chromatograms must be quality-scored and filtered prior to CWT-based chromatographic peak detection, or when detected peaks need to be ranked by sharpness, peak significance level, or zigzag index to. When the EIC already has high background signals or contains only a single peak and the MCQ index alone is being used for selection/alignment — the MCQ index cannot fairly evaluate these; use the global zigzag index instead. When peaks are already ground truth (detected by at least two of XCMS, MZmine, and MAVEN) and no further quality filtering is needed. When the goal is a machine-learning classifier (e.g. SVM) for peak quality — the curated training set of good and bad representative peaks does not yet exist. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Evaluates quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) and detected chromatographic peaks in LC/MS metabolomics data using the MCQ index, a global EIC zigzag index derived from first-order derivatives, and six peak metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, local zigzag index), ranking them by F-Score to filter 'bad' EICs and peaks before downstream peak detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Evaluates quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) and detected chromatographic peaks in LC/MS metabolomics data using the MCQ index, a global EIC zigzag index derived from first-order derivatives, and six peak metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, local zigzag index), ranking them by F-Score to filter 'bad' EICs and peaks before downstream peak detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the EIC already has high background signals or contains only a single peak and the MCQ index alone is being used for selection/alignment — the MCQ index cannot fairly evaluate these; use the global zigzag index instead. When peaks are already ground truth (detected by at least two of XCMS, MZmine, and MAVEN) and no further quality filtering is needed. When the goal is a machine-learning classifier (e.g. SVM) for peak quality — the curated training set of good and bad representative peaks does not yet exist.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics dataset (e.g., in vitro S9 incubation peak tables with MS2 spectra) has been annotated with KGMN and you must report per-mode known/unknown peak counts.
skills.name: lc-ms-peak-annotation-counting
skills.search_text: lc-ms-peak-annotation-counting Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics dataset (e.g., in vitro S9 incubation peak tables with MS2 spectra) has been annotated with KGMN and you must report per-mode known/unknown peak counts. The dataset is a single pooled sample without both positive and negative ionization mode data, making per-mode counting meaningless Peaks are already fully annotated (e.g., a feature table with metabolite IDs); the skill counts KGMN-known vs -unknown assignments, not re-annotation The sample comes from non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles, where the article advises caution because organism-specific reaction databases are not incorporated Counts how many LC-MS/MS peaks are annotated as known versus unknown metabolites per ionization mode using the KGMN three-layer network workflow (MetDNA2Vis), and reports per-mode peak totals against published values. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Counts how many LC-MS/MS peaks are annotated as known versus unknown metabolites per ionization mode using the KGMN three-layer network workflow (MetDNA2Vis), and reports per-mode peak totals against published values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a single pooled sample without both positive and negative ionization mode data, making per-mode counting meaningless Peaks are already fully annotated (e.g., a feature table with metabolite IDs); the skill counts KGMN-known vs -unknown assignments, not re-annotation The sample comes from non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles, where the article advises caution because organism-specific reaction databases are not incorporated

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-MS peak lists (mass-to-charge ratios with adducts/fragments) need to be annotated to KEGG compounds and a small prioritized proposal per peak is required, especially when standard annotation tools like xMSannotator underperform.
skills.name: lc-ms-peak-annotation-prioritization
skills.search_text: lc-ms-peak-annotation-prioritization Use when untargeted LC-MS peak lists (mass-to-charge ratios with adducts/fragments) need to be annotated to KEGG compounds and a small prioritized proposal per peak is required, especially when standard annotation tools like xMSannotator underperform. When annotation against databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) is required — the article explicitly notes mWISE only annotates in the KEGG database, an important limitation relative to xMSannotator. When the input is already a curated annotated feature table with no need for candidate prioritization — the diffusion stage adds value only when multiple candidate compounds must be ranked per peak. When LC-MS peaks have not been pre-filtered (features with no signal or zero intensity not removed via the 80% rule) — the matching and clustering stages assume cleaned input peak lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 A three-stage mWISE pipeline that matches LC-MS peak m/z values to the KEGG database, clusters and filters the candidate features to suppress false positives, and then diffuses score labels over a biochemical network (FELLA or RClass) to produce a per-peak prioritized annotation list. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: A three-stage mWISE pipeline that matches LC-MS peak m/z values to the KEGG database, clusters and filters the candidate features to suppress false positives, and then diffuses score labels over a biochemical network (FELLA or RClass) to produce a per-peak prioritized annotation list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When annotation against databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) is required — the article explicitly notes mWISE only annotates in the KEGG database, an important limitation relative to xMSannotator. When the input is already a curated annotated feature table with no need for candidate prioritization — the diffusion stage adds value only when multiple candidate compounds must be ranked per peak. When LC-MS peaks have not been pre-filtered (features with no signal or zero intensity not removed via the 80% rule) — the matching and clustering stages assume cleaned input peak lists.

skills.description: Use when importing tab-delimited peak-integrated metabolomics data into mzQuality and you need to verify the presence of mandatory columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) before downstream quality analysis.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-peak-area-column-validation Use when importing tab-delimited peak-integrated metabolomics data into mzQuality and you need to verify the presence of mandatory columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) before downstream quality analysis. skills.summary: Validate and read tab-delimited peak-integrated LC-MS metabolomics data with mzQuality's readData function, verifying mandatory columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) before constructing a SummarizedExperiment via buildExperiment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a SummarizedExperiment — mzQuality accepts this directly and readData's tab-delimited column validation is unnecessary. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table (e.g. from MZmine/MS-DIAL export) — skip reprocessing and proceed directly to statistical modeling. skills.search_text: lc-ms-peak-detection-and-feature-alignment Use when raw LC-MS/MS chromatogram files (e.g., beer extracts in positive and negative ionization modes) must be converted into a bag-of-fragments matrix with MS2 features as rows and MS2 spectra as columns before LDA inference. Input is already a feature table or preprocessed peak matrix — no raw chromatogram peak detection or MS1–MS2 pairing is needed Data are simple mixtures with low-information MS2 spectra (e.g., fixed collision energy producing few fragments) rather than complex mixtures with ramped or stepped collision energy Downstream tool does not accept neutral losses — MS2LDA motifs include neutral-loss features that spectral matching tools currently omit http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Detect and align LC-MS/MS features from raw spectra using XCMS, PeakML/mzMatch, and RMassBank, then build the MS2 feature-by-spectrum integer count matrix that downstream unsupervised substructure discovery (MS2LDA) requires as input. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Detect and align LC-MS/MS features from raw spectra using XCMS, PeakML/mzMatch, and RMassBank, then build the MS2 feature-by-spectrum integer count matrix that downstream unsupervised substructure discovery (MS2LDA) requires as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or preprocessed peak matrix — no raw chromatogram peak detection or MS1–MS2 pairing is needed Data are simple mixtures with low-information MS2 spectra (e.g., fixed collision energy producing few fragments) rather than complex mixtures with ramped or stepped collision energy Downstream tool does not accept neutral losses — MS2LDA motifs include neutral-loss features that spectral matching tools currently omit

skills.search_text: lc-ms-peak-integration-quality-prediction Use when an XCMS-processed untargeted LC–MS feature table (e.g., from Metabolomics Workbench ST000726/ST000695-style data) contains poorly integrated peaks you need to flag automatically, and RSD < 30% QC filtering alone is insufficient. skills.summary: Predicts Pass (high-quality) vs Fail (low-quality) labels for chromatographic peak integrations in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics data using a machine learning classifier — the MetaClean global classifier, AdaBoost trained on the 11-metric M11 peak-quality metric set — as an objective alternative to manual visual assessment or RSD filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a vendor-processed output in a uniquely formatted file rather than an XCMS object — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input The data come from a substantially dissimilar analytical platform/method (e.g., Test 2-like datasets with few peaks passing RSD < 30% and small IPO peak widths), where classifier performance degrades, especially for low-abundance Fail peaks The goal is pure reproducibility filtering rather than integration-quality assessment — a simple RSD < 30% cut-off on pooled QC samples is the cheaper alternative

skills.description: Use when an LC–MS feature table contains pooled quality-control (QC) sample injections and noisy, low-reproducibility peaks must be removed with a simple, unsupervised reproducibility filter before statistical analysis or classifier training.

skills.search_text: lc-ms-pooled-qc-rsd-filtering Use when an LC–MS feature table contains pooled quality-control (QC) sample injections and noisy, low-reproducibility peaks must be removed with a simple, unsupervised reproducibility filter before statistical analysis or classifier training. When integration-quality (not just reproducibility) must be judged — RSD filtering performed worse than the MetaClean global classifier and cannot flag badly integrated peaks that happen to be reproducible in QC. When the dataset has no routinely injected pooled QC samples, since RSD must be computed on pooled QCs. When vendor-processed outputs or non-XCMS feature tables without QC injections are all that is available. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filters untargeted LC–MS metabolomics peaks by computing the relative standard deviation (RSD) of each feature across routinely injected pooled QC samples and retaining only peaks below a pre-set threshold (typically RSD < 30%), removing noisy, poorly reproducible features before downstream statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Filters untargeted LC–MS metabolomics peaks by computing the relative standard deviation (RSD) of each feature across routinely injected pooled QC samples and retaining only peaks below a pre-set threshold (typically RSD < 30%), removing noisy, poorly reproducible features before downstream statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When integration-quality (not just reproducibility) must be judged — RSD filtering performed worse than the MetaClean global classifier and cannot flag badly integrated peaks that happen to be reproducible in QC. When the dataset has no routinely injected pooled QC samples, since RSD must be computed on pooled QCs. When vendor-processed outputs or non-XCMS feature tables without QC injections are all that is available.

skills.name: lc-ms-qc-based-normalization
skills.search_text: lc-ms-qc-based-normalization Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., runs x metabolites with QC annotations and batch labels) shows signal drift, batch effects, or outliers that degrade replicate concordance and downstream differential abundance testing. Input is already normalized (the workflow starts from a raw intensity matrix such as example.RData rawdata) Data contain no QC samples or QCs are not representative of biological samples — metanorm() with QCcheck = TRUE is designed to flag such QC-vs-sample discrepancies before normalization The goal is automated outlier detection/removal prior to normalization rather than outlier-robust fitting; the paper treats outlier removal as a separate, non-trivial alternative http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Quality-control (QC) sample-based normalization of LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices, extended with three outlier-robust methods (rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) implemented in the Metanorm R package, with QC-representativeness checking, batchwise correction, and diagnostic visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Quality-control (QC) sample-based normalization of LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices, extended with three outlier-robust methods (rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) implemented in the Metanorm R package, with QC-representativeness checking, batchwise correction, and diagnostic visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized (the workflow starts from a raw intensity matrix such as example.RData rawdata) Data contain no QC samples or QCs are not representative of biological samples — metanorm() with QCcheck = TRUE is designed to flag such QC-vs-sample discrepancies before normalization The goal is automated outlier detection/removal prior to normalization rather than outlier-robust fitting; the paper treats outlier removal as a separate, non-trivial alternative

skills.description: Use when multi-rater quality annotations of LC-MS files (e.g., qualified/unqualified per metric or per file) must be collapsed to a single consensus label and reproducibility (observed agreement) must be quantified per instrument.
skills.name: lc-ms-qc-consensus-labeling
skills.search_text: lc-ms-qc-consensus-labeling Use when multi-rater quality annotations of LC-MS files (e.g., qualified/unqualified per metric or per file) must be collapsed to a single consensus label and reproducibility (observed agreement) must be quantified per instrument. Input consists of raw vendor files (.d/.raw/.wiff) rather than existing expert annotations — the conversion and metric-extraction workflow applies, not consensus labeling. Only a single annotator's assessment is available — majority voting and observed-agreement statistics require ≥ 2 raters. Goal is to train or evaluate the AI model itself rather than to derive or audit the ground-truth consensus labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces the majority-vote consensus labeling of LC/MS file quality from multi-expert annotations of DIA QC files and quantifies inter-rater observed agreement, establishing the ground-truth labels used to train iDIA-QC's AI models. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-54871-1
skills.summary: Reproduces the majority-vote consensus labeling of LC/MS file quality from multi-expert annotations of DIA QC files and quantifies inter-rater observed agreement, establishing the ground-truth labels used to train iDIA-QC's AI models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of raw vendor files (.d/.raw/.wiff) rather than existing expert annotations — the conversion and metric-extraction workflow applies, not consensus labeling. Only a single annotator's assessment is available — majority voting and observed-agreement statistics require ≥ 2 raters. Goal is to train or evaluate the AI model itself rather than to derive or audit the ground-truth consensus labels.

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS peak table (tab-delimited with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) contains pooled QC samples (SQC/LQC) and you need a per-compound QC-reproducibility metric for compound filtering.
skills.name: lc-ms-qc-rsd-calculation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-qc-rsd-calculation Use when a targeted LC-MS peak table (tab-delimited with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) contains pooled QC samples (SQC/LQC) and you need a per-compound QC-reproducibility metric for compound filtering. When a compound is not detected in LQC or SQC samples it is assumed not present and will not be reported by mzQuality, so RSDQC cannot be computed for it Data that have not been peak-integrated to a compound-by-sample area table (mzQuality processes peak-integrated data independently of vendor software and does not process raw peaks like OpenMS or MZmine) When sample-level outliers, not compound QC reproducibility, are the target — the Rosner Test on QC samples is the corresponding sample-based check http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the relative standard deviation of pooled QC sample peak-area ratios (RSDQC) per compound in mzQuality, after batch correction and outlier exclusion, to quantify compound-level QC variability and underpin compound confidence classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Computes the relative standard deviation of pooled QC sample peak-area ratios (RSDQC) per compound in mzQuality, after batch correction and outlier exclusion, to quantify compound-level QC variability and underpin compound confidence classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a compound is not detected in LQC or SQC samples it is assumed not present and will not be reported by mzQuality, so RSDQC cannot be computed for it Data that have not been peak-integrated to a compound-by-sample area table (mzQuality processes peak-integrated data independently of vendor software and does not process raw peaks like OpenMS or MZmine) When sample-level outliers, not compound QC reproducibility, are the target — the Rosner Test on QC samples is the corresponding sample-based check

skills.description: Use when a dashboard or QC pipeline needs to escalate per-internal-standard QC results into a specimen-level 'Warning' label using Rapid QC-MS's dropout-threshold and IS-Warn-fraction rule.
skills.name: lc-ms-qc-rule-implementation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-qc-rule-implementation Use when a dashboard or QC pipeline needs to escalate per-internal-standard QC results into a specimen-level 'Warning' label using Rapid QC-MS's dropout-threshold and IS-Warn-fraction rule. Input is already a specimen-level label table with no per-internal-standard intensity or designation data to aggregate Data was not processed through the Rapid QC-MS pipeline (MSConvert raw-to-mzML conversion plus MS-DIAL processing), so IS dropout counts and per-IS QC designations are unavailable The goal is per-raw-file alerting or notification (Slack/email) rather than reproducing the specimen-level escalation logic itself Reimplements Rapid QC-MS's specimen-level 'Warn' escalation rule, in which a specimen is flagged 'Warning' in the dashboard Specimen Table when either IS intensity dropouts reach 75% of the user-defined threshold or >=50% of its internal standards individually carry a 'Warn' designation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Reimplements Rapid QC-MS's specimen-level 'Warn' escalation rule, in which a specimen is flagged 'Warning' in the dashboard Specimen Table when either IS intensity dropouts reach 75% of the user-defined threshold or >=50% of its internal standards individually carry a 'Warn' designation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a specimen-level label table with no per-internal-standard intensity or designation data to aggregate Data was not processed through the Rapid QC-MS pipeline (MSConvert raw-to-mzML conversion plus MS-DIAL processing), so IS dropout counts and per-IS QC designations are unavailable The goal is per-raw-file alerting or notification (Slack/email) rather than reproducing the specimen-level escalation logic itself

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics study was measured in multiple batches and you need to verify, via PCA of sample types and batches, whether pooled QC (SQC) samples become aligned and centered across batches after batch correction.
skills.name: lc-ms-qc-sample-pca-visualization
skills.search_text: lc-ms-qc-sample-pca-visualization Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics study was measured in multiple batches and you need to verify, via PCA of sample types and batches, whether pooled QC (SQC) samples become aligned and centered across batches after batch correction. For untargeted metabolomics peak tables processed with tools like OpenMS or MZmine rather than mzQuality's SQC-based SummarizedExperiment workflow — this skill depends on mzQuality's batch-corrected 'ratio_corrected' assay and sample-type annotations. When you only need per-compound QC relative standard deviation (RSD) checks rather than a multivariate view of between-batch alignment; the RSDqc <= 30% threshold tabulation is a separate evaluation. When samples are not measured in multiple batches with pooled QC (SQC) samples, since the PCA's purpose here is comparing SQC vs study samples across batches. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates PCA plots comparing study samples and pooled study quality control (SQC) samples across batches in mzQuality, before and after between-batch correction, to judge whether batch effects on a targeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset have been successfully removed. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Generates PCA plots comparing study samples and pooled study quality control (SQC) samples across batches in mzQuality, before and after between-batch correction, to judge whether batch effects on a targeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset have been successfully removed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: For untargeted metabolomics peak tables processed with tools like OpenMS or MZmine rather than mzQuality's SQC-based SummarizedExperiment workflow — this skill depends on mzQuality's batch-corrected 'ratio_corrected' assay and sample-type annotations. When you only need per-compound QC relative standard deviation (RSD) checks rather than a multivariate view of between-batch alignment; the RSDqc <= 30% threshold tabulation is a separate evaluation. When samples are not measured in multiple batches with pooled QC (SQC) samples, since the PCA's purpose here is comparing SQC vs study samples across batches.

skills.description: Use when a DIA-MS raw file (.raw/.d/.wiff) from Orbitrap, TripleTOF, or timsTOF instruments must be assessed for LC/MS run quality and receive an automated qualified/unqualified prediction.
skills.name: lc-ms-qualified-prediction
skills.search_text: lc-ms-qualified-prediction Use when a DIA-MS raw file (.raw/.d/.wiff) from Orbitrap, TripleTOF, or timsTOF instruments must be assessed for LC/MS run quality and receive an automated qualified/unqualified prediction. Input files are DDA or SRM acquisitions — the models were trained on DIA metrics; SRM-based QC tools 'cannot be directly applied to large scale quantitative proteomics experiments' The instrument is a newly emerging model outside the Orbitrap/TripleTOF/timsTOF series covered in the study The run has already been manually assessed and only archive-style reporting of existing metrics is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Run the iDIA-QC pipeline to convert multivendor DIA raw files (.raw/.d/.wiff) to mzXML via msConvert, analyze with DIA-NN (v1.7.15), extract 15 numerical QC metrics, and feed them to pretrained machine learning models that assign qualified/unqualified LC and MS performance labels with fault-cause guidance. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-54871-1
skills.summary: Run the iDIA-QC pipeline to convert multivendor DIA raw files (.raw/.d/.wiff) to mzXML via msConvert, analyze with DIA-NN (v1.7.15), extract 15 numerical QC metrics, and feed them to pretrained machine learning models that assign qualified/unqualified LC and MS performance labels with fault-cause guidance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are DDA or SRM acquisitions — the models were trained on DIA metrics; SRM-based QC tools 'cannot be directly applied to large scale quantitative proteomics experiments' The instrument is a newly emerging model outside the Orbitrap/TripleTOF/timsTOF series covered in the study The run has already been manually assessed and only archive-style reporting of existing metrics is needed

skills.description: Use when Thermo .raw files are being acquired across a specimen sequence and per-specimen IS-derived RT, intensity, and Δm/z values must be tabulated to expose acute QC failures or gradual drift over hours, days, months, or years.
skills.name: lc-ms-quality-control-metric-extraction
skills.search_text: lc-ms-quality-control-metric-extraction Use when Thermo .raw files are being acquired across a specimen sequence and per-specimen IS-derived RT, intensity, and Δm/z values must be tabulated to expose acute QC failures or gradual drift over hours, days, months, or years. Data is in a vendor format other than Thermo RAW — MSConvert/mzML conversion is supported but the pipeline has only been tested extensively on Thermo acquisition sequences and RAW files, so other vendors may hit bugs The goal is deep post-hoc statistical analysis of a completed feature table rather than continuous, per-file QC monitoring during acquisition Running on a platform without MSConvert and MS-DIAL installed manually (e.g., a headless Linux cluster); Rapid QC-MS was designed for Windows because of these dependencies http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extract per-specimen internal standard (IS) quality metrics — retention time, intensity, and Δm/z — from LC-MS/MS raw files using the Rapid QC-MS pipeline (MSConvert → MS-DIAL) so that instrument sensitivity, in-run retention time shifts, and mass accuracy drift can be monitored during an analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Extract per-specimen internal standard (IS) quality metrics — retention time, intensity, and Δm/z — from LC-MS/MS raw files using the Rapid QC-MS pipeline (MSConvert → MS-DIAL) so that instrument sensitivity, in-run retention time shifts, and mass accuracy drift can be monitored during an analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is in a vendor format other than Thermo RAW — MSConvert/mzML conversion is supported but the pipeline has only been tested extensively on Thermo acquisition sequences and RAW files, so other vendors may hit bugs The goal is deep post-hoc statistical analysis of a completed feature table rather than continuous, per-file QC monitoring during acquisition Running on a platform without MSConvert and MS-DIAL installed manually (e.g., a headless Linux cluster); Rapid QC-MS was designed for Windows because of these dependencies

skills.description: Use when processing already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak-area data (calibration standards plus samples) and you need per-compound automated calibration-curve regression without manual model/level tuning.
skills.name: lc-ms-quantification-linear-quadratic-modeling
skills.search_text: lc-ms-quantification-linear-quadratic-modeling Use when processing already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak-area data (calibration standards plus samples) and you need per-compound automated calibration-curve regression without manual model/level tuning. Raw, un-integrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey works only on already integrated MS data and 'does not provide any integration capabilities' Datasets needing manual control over model choice, weights, or standard levels — use the Interactive Regression Model Optimization module instead Non-Windows local desktop use of the standalone version, which is Windows-only (Linux users need the Apptainer version) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Automatic Optimization Module of QuantyFey that, per compound, selects a linear or quadratic regression model (with weighting) for external-calibration quantification of targeted LC-MS/MS data and iteratively removes unsuitable calibration levels. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Automatic Optimization Module of QuantyFey that, per compound, selects a linear or quadratic regression model (with weighting) for external-calibration quantification of targeted LC-MS/MS data and iteratively removes unsuitable calibration levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw, un-integrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey works only on already integrated MS data and 'does not provide any integration capabilities' Datasets needing manual control over model choice, weights, or standard levels — use the Interactive Regression Model Optimization module instead Non-Windows local desktop use of the standalone version, which is Windows-only (Linux users need the Apptainer version)

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS peak groups (e.g. MZmine 2 extracted features from nontargeted metabolomics runs) must be represented as images to train or apply a DNN-based true/false peak classifier.
skills.name: lc-ms-raster-image-representation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-raster-image-representation Use when raw LC-MS peak groups (e.g. MZmine 2 extracted features from nontargeted metabolomics runs) must be represented as images to train or apply a DNN-based true/false peak classifier. The goal is a purely parametric peak-quality filter using the original 59 peak-group parameters (e.g. medRelFWHM) — the article's logistic regression / Random Forest models already cover this; the raster-image skill is needed only for the image-based DNN path. Peak lists are already curated true/false annotations or the peaks lack sample-level shape data, so no raster image can be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Converts LC-MS peak group shape information into raster images — each pixel an intensity, each row a sample, each column a retention-time bin — so an image-based deep neural network can classify candidate peaks as true or false. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b02983
skills.summary: Converts LC-MS peak group shape information into raster images — each pixel an intensity, each row a sample, each column a retention-time bin — so an image-based deep neural network can classify candidate peaks as true or false.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a purely parametric peak-quality filter using the original 59 peak-group parameters (e.g. medRelFWHM) — the article's logistic regression / Random Forest models already cover this; the raster-image skill is needed only for the image-based DNN path. Peak lists are already curated true/false annotations or the peaks lack sample-level shape data, so no raster image can be constructed.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (e.g., DDA data from an exposome or metabolomics mixture) need conventional XCMS peak picking as a feature table before JPA's MS2-recognition or targeted-list extraction steps.
skills.name: lc-ms-raw-data-peak-picking
skills.search_text: lc-ms-raw-data-peak-picking Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (e.g., DDA data from an exposome or metabolomics mixture) need conventional XCMS peak picking as a feature table before JPA's MS2-recognition or targeted-list extraction steps. Input is already an aligned feature table — JPA requires per-file CSV feature tables for multi-sample analysis, and aligned tables are not acceptable Running find.level3features for MR features on full-scan or DIA data is inappropriate; but note the PP step itself is the required first stage — do not skip it when only MS2-based rescue is wanted http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Extract MS1 peak-picking (PP) metabolic features from raw LC-MS mzXML data using JPA's embedded XCMS functions, producing a dataframe feature table with mz, rt, rtmin, rtmax, maxo, sample, and level columns that serves as the baseline for downstream MR/targeted feature rescue. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212
skills.summary: Extract MS1 peak-picking (PP) metabolic features from raw LC-MS mzXML data using JPA's embedded XCMS functions, producing a dataframe feature table with mz, rt, rtmin, rtmax, maxo, sample, and level columns that serves as the baseline for downstream MR/targeted feature rescue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table — JPA requires per-file CSV feature tables for multi-sample analysis, and aligned tables are not acceptable Running find.level3features for MR features on full-scan or DIA data is inappropriate; but note the PP step itself is the required first stage — do not skip it when only MS2-based rescue is wanted

skills.description: Use when a study deposits or generates hundreds to thousands of vendor LC-MS raw files spanning multiple acquisition modes and instruments, and the goal is fully autonomous, mode-conditional identification without manual per-file intervention.
skills.name: lc-ms-raw-file-batch-processing
skills.search_text: lc-ms-raw-file-batch-processing Use when a study deposits or generates hundreds to thousands of vendor LC-MS raw files spanning multiple acquisition modes and instruments, and the goal is fully autonomous, mode-conditional identification without manual per-file intervention. MSConnect is not a standalone data analysis tool — if you need a specific search engine itself, deploy that engine directly rather than expecting MSConnect to provide analysis software or licenses If the data set is small (a handful of files) or already reduced to feature tables / identification matrices, a queue-driven batch pipeline adds unnecessary infrastructure overhead If your instruments or acquisition modes require a search engine for which no ODP processing app/wrapper has been set up, first follow the processing-module/wrapper setup tutorial before attempting automated submission http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Batch process thousands of vendor LC-MS raw files end-to-end by routing each file through mode-appropriate search engines (FragPipe/MSFragger for DDA and wide-window DDA, DIA-NN for DIA) inside a queue-driven platform that automatically downloads raws from a server, invokes the engine CLI, and returns PSM/peptide/protein-group identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c00854
skills.summary: Batch process thousands of vendor LC-MS raw files end-to-end by routing each file through mode-appropriate search engines (FragPipe/MSFragger for DDA and wide-window DDA, DIA-NN for DIA) inside a queue-driven platform that automatically downloads raws from a server, invokes the engine CLI, and returns PSM/peptide/protein-group identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MSConnect is not a standalone data analysis tool — if you need a specific search engine itself, deploy that engine directly rather than expecting MSConnect to provide analysis software or licenses If the data set is small (a handful of files) or already reduced to feature tables / identification matrices, a queue-driven batch pipeline adds unnecessary infrastructure overhead If your instruments or acquisition modes require a search engine for which no ODP processing app/wrapper has been set up, first follow the processing-module/wrapper setup tutorial before attempting automated submission

skills.description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS1/MS2 spectral files (e.g. mzML/CDF vendor conversions of untargeted metabolomics or exposomics runs, including pooled-QC SWATH-DIA acquisitions) and you need feature detection, quantification, and MS2 deconvolution before annotation or statistics.
skills.name: lc-ms-raw-spectra-processing
skills.search_text: lc-ms-raw-spectra-processing Use when starting from raw LC-MS1/MS2 spectral files (e.g. mzML/CDF vendor conversions of untargeted metabolomics or exposomics runs, including pooled-QC SWATH-DIA acquisitions) and you need feature detection, quantification, and MS2 deconvolution before annotation or statistics. Input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw MS spectra — proceed directly to MS2 Peak Annotation or Statistical Analysis modules instead Targeted metabolomics data that do not need untargeted MS1 feature detection or DIA MS2 deconvolution MS2-only fragments without precursor/pooled-QC context, since DIA deconvolution requires reconstructing fragment-to-precursor associations from pooled QC spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Process raw LC-MS/MS spectral files (MS1 peak detection/quantification plus MS2 DDA/DIA deconvolution) using MetaboAnalyst 6.0's Spectra Processing module powered by the asari algorithm, as the entry point of the unified metabolomics workflow from raw spectra to compound identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Process raw LC-MS/MS spectral files (MS1 peak detection/quantification plus MS2 DDA/DIA deconvolution) using MetaboAnalyst 6.0's Spectra Processing module powered by the asari algorithm, as the entry point of the unified metabolomics workflow from raw spectra to compound identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw MS spectra — proceed directly to MS2 Peak Annotation or Statistical Analysis modules instead Targeted metabolomics data that do not need untargeted MS1 feature detection or DIA MS2 deconvolution MS2-only fragments without precursor/pooled-QC context, since DIA deconvolution requires reconstructing fragment-to-precursor associations from pooled QC spectra

skills.description: Use when a raw mzXML/mzML standard-mixture file and its extracted library table must be screened so that only metabolite peaks passing Std/Blk ratio, RT RSD, and intensity thresholds enter the validated reference library.
skills.name: lc-ms-reference-metabolite-validation
skills.search_text: lc-ms-reference-metabolite-validation Use when a raw mzXML/mzML standard-mixture file and its extracted library table must be screened so that only metabolite peaks passing Std/Blk ratio, RT RSD, and intensity thresholds enter the validated reference library. The goal is mobile-phase optimization (peak quality scoring across candidate mobile phases) rather than validating metabolites for the reference library Input data is not replicate LC-MS standard-mixture chromatograms (mzXML/mzML) with accompanying blanks — the Std/Blk and RT RSD criteria cannot be computed The library table already carries a validation column with confirmed entries and only needs counting, not threshold-based re-validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Validates metabolites in an LC-MS reference library against user-specified peak-quality thresholds computed by MetaMOPE (MCQ, maximum intensity, retention-time RSD, Std/Blk ratio, jaggedness, asymmetry factor, FWHM, modality), and verifies the resulting library count (571 metabolites for HILIC LC-MS). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad061
skills.summary: Validates metabolites in an LC-MS reference library against user-specified peak-quality thresholds computed by MetaMOPE (MCQ, maximum intensity, retention-time RSD, Std/Blk ratio, jaggedness, asymmetry factor, FWHM, modality), and verifies the resulting library count (571 metabolites for HILIC LC-MS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is mobile-phase optimization (peak quality scoring across candidate mobile phases) rather than validating metabolites for the reference library Input data is not replicate LC-MS standard-mixture chromatograms (mzXML/mzML) with accompanying blanks — the Std/Blk and RT RSD criteria cannot be computed The library table already carries a validation column with confirmed entries and only needs counting, not threshold-based re-validation

skills.description: Use when aligned LC-MS feature tables across many runs show retention time drift (e.g., tens of seconds in RPLC negative mode) and features must be mapped to a common RT scale before statistical analysis or phenotype prediction.
skills.name: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment
skills.search_text: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment Use when aligned LC-MS feature tables across many runs show retention time drift (e.g., tens of seconds in RPLC negative mode) and features must be mapped to a common RT scale before statistical analysis or phenotype prediction. Input is already a fully aligned feature table or you only have a single run/chromatogram with no inter-sample RT drift to correct The dataset lacks QC pool samples containing unique, high-quality model peaks needed as anchors The goal is metabolite identification — MassCube's alignment module does not directly perform metabolite identification http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Anchor-based retention time alignment for LC-MS feature tables as implemented in MassCube: high-quality model peaks in QC pools serve as anchors, and linear interpolation corrects nonlinear RT shifts across chromatograms in large-scale studies. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Anchor-based retention time alignment for LC-MS feature tables as implemented in MassCube: high-quality model peaks in QC pools serve as anchors, and linear interpolation corrects nonlinear RT shifts across chromatograms in large-scale studies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fully aligned feature table or you only have a single run/chromatogram with no inter-sample RT drift to correct The dataset lacks QC pool samples containing unique, high-quality model peaks needed as anchors The goal is metabolite identification — MassCube's alignment module does not directly perform metabolite identification

skills.description: Use when you have per-run feature lists (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder or TXT/CSV, need to align corresponding features/peptides across many LC-MS runs, or compare against MBR-based tools.
skills.name: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment
skills.search_text: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment Use when you have per-run feature lists (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder or TXT/CSV, need to align corresponding features/peptides across many LC-MS runs, or compare against MBR-based tools. Your tool already performs MBR-style alignment and identification jointly (MaxQuant, MSFragger, DIA-NN) and you only need identification counts, not cross-run feature correspondence You have no feature lists yet — DeepRTAlign requires prior feature extraction (e.g. Dinosaur on DIA runs) and does not process raw LC-MS files Samples require quantification improvement from alignment alone — the authors note alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Retention time (RT) alignment/correspondence of LC-MS feature lists across large cohorts using DeepRTAlign, which combines coarse alignment (pseudo warping) with deep-learning direct matching to handle both monotonic and non-monotonic RT shifts in proteomic and metabolomic data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Retention time (RT) alignment/correspondence of LC-MS feature lists across large cohorts using DeepRTAlign, which combines coarse alignment (pseudo warping) with deep-learning direct matching to handle both monotonic and non-monotonic RT shifts in proteomic and metabolomic data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your tool already performs MBR-style alignment and identification jointly (MaxQuant, MSFragger, DIA-NN) and you only need identification counts, not cross-run feature correspondence You have no feature lists yet — DeepRTAlign requires prior feature extraction (e.g. Dinosaur on DIA runs) and does not process raw LC-MS files Samples require quantification improvement from alignment alone — the authors note alignment has less influence on quantification than feature extraction

skills.description: Use when XCMS-class single-warping-function alignment has produced misaligned feature groups in LC-MS profiles — detected by ncGTW's p-value-based misalignment detection — and the goal is compound-specific realignment before re-grouping and peak-filling.
skills.name: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment
skills.search_text: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment Use when XCMS-class single-warping-function alignment has produced misaligned feature groups in LC-MS profiles — detected by ncGTW's p-value-based misalignment detection — and the goal is compound-specific realignment before re-grouping and peak-filling. Features are well-aligned by XCMS's single per-sample warping function — ncGTW targets only detected misaligned groups, and over-warping risks peak shape distortion (the paper notes distortion must be corrected by a post-processing module). Input is already a feature/peak table without raw profile data — ncGTW realignment operates on extracted-ion profiles (loadProfile), so profile-level raw data must be available. You need simulation of acquisition modes or fragmentation chemistries outside SMITER's default models (several peptide fragmentation methods, two nucleoside models, one lipid model) without implementing a custom module.

skills.description: Use when aligning per-sample precursor (MS1) and fragment (MS2) m/z/intensity feature lists exported from MS-DIAL across many LC-MS/MS samples into one feature table for downstream multivariate or machine-learning analysis.

Input is already a single merged feature table or aligned matrix — re-alignment would be redundant The task is direct bioactivity prediction from raw spectra without alignment — use the image-based CNN pipeline instead, which bypasses alignment Sample set is small or has distinct features with no expected cross-sample duplicates — the 0.8 similarity threshold would incorrectly merge distinct features http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Merges per-sample LC-MS/MS feature lists from 545 wild soybean accessions into a unified feature table by scoring MS1 m/z, retention time, and MS/MS spectral similarity, treating features as equivalent when the average of the three scores exceeds 0.8 with a 1-minute RT tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Merges per-sample LC-MS/MS feature lists from 545 wild soybean accessions into a unified feature table by scoring MS1 m/z, retention time, and MS/MS spectral similarity, treating features as equivalent when the average of the three scores exceeds 0.8 with a 1-minute RT tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single merged feature table or aligned matrix — re-alignment would be redundant The task is direct bioactivity prediction from raw spectra without alignment — use the image-based CNN pipeline instead, which bypasses alignment Sample set is small or has distinct features with no expected cross-sample duplicates — the 0.8 similarity threshold would incorrectly merge distinct features

skills.summary: Annotates an LC-MS/MS feature table with molecular formula and structural identifications at Metabolomics Standards Initiative level 3 by running SIRIUS formula ranking and CSI:FingerID structure prediction on feature-assigned MS2 spectra via OpenMS SiriusAdapter in UmetaFlow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need MSI level 2 identifications via spectral library matching from an MGF/MSP/mzML library - use the separate UmetaFlow spectral matching step instead. skills.description: Use when running the specXplore importing pipeline on .mgf MS/MS feature lists (e.g. wheat or urine exposome data) and you need a scale sanity check — wall-clock preprocessing time and post-processing feature count — before opening the dashboard session.
skills.name: lc-msms-feature-count-validation
skills.search_text: lc-msms-feature-count-validation Use when running the specXplore importing pipeline on .mgf MS/MS feature lists (e.g. wheat or urine exposome data) and you need a scale sanity check — wall-clock preprocessing time and post-processing feature count — before opening the dashboard session. The input is raw vendor data that has not yet been converted to .mgf format — convert it first with vendor software or MZmine3's GNPS/FBMN/IIN/MN export options before any feature-count validation is meaningful. Your goal is to reproduce the absolute runtime of the dashboard itself (e.g. t-SNE rendering or network redraw under liberal settings) rather than the importing pipeline — the paper only anticipates dashboard scalability to ~5000 features and provides no dashboard-side benchmarks. The dataset comes from an application domain poorly covered by ms2deepscore training data — a feature-count check would not catch that the ms2deepscore predictions are out of domain. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Validates that a specXplore importing-pipeline preprocessing run completed successfully by checking runtime and feature counts against the paper's reported scales: wheat LC–MS/MS <15 min and <1000 features, urine metabolome <75 min and <4000 features. Runtimes are compared by component (MS2Query local library search vs. pairwise similarity computation). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Validates that a specXplore importing-pipeline preprocessing run completed successfully by checking runtime and feature counts against the paper's reported scales: wheat LC–MS/MS <15 min and <1000 features, urine metabolome <75 min and <4000 features. Runtimes are compared by component (MS2Query local library search vs. pairwise similarity computation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw vendor data that has not yet been converted to .mgf format — convert it first with vendor software or MZmine3's GNPS/FBMN/IIN/MN export options before any feature-count validation is meaningful. Your goal is to reproduce the absolute runtime of the dashboard itself (e.g. t-SNE rendering or network redraw under liberal settings) rather than the importing pipeline — the paper only anticipates dashboard scalability to ~5000 features and provides no dashboard-side benchmarks. skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS runs in .mzML or .mzXML format from untargeted metabolomics experiments must be converted into features (precursor ion, adduct, isotope peaks) with merged fragmentation spectra per feature before de novo formula and structure annotation.

skills.search_text: lc-msms-feature-detection Use when raw LC-MS/MS runs in .mzML or .mzXML format from untargeted metabolomics experiments must be converted into features (precursor ion, adduct, isotope peaks) with merged fragmentation spectra per feature before de novo formula and structure annotation. The LC-MS runs contain spectra in profiled mode — the paper discards these before feature detection Only negative ion mode spectra are available, or the fragmentation spectra have at most one peak, since such spectra are discarded before processing The goal is targeted quantification on an already-generated feature table rather than de novo annotation of unknown spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Detect molecular features in untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics runs (mzML/mzXML) and assign each fragmentation spectrum to its precursor, adduct and isotope peaks — the preprocessing step that turns raw runs into feature-associated spectra before SIRIUS 4 formula and structure annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Detect molecular features in untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics runs (mzML/mzXML) and assign each fragmentation spectrum to its precursor, adduct and isotope peaks — the preprocessing step that turns raw runs into feature-associated spectra before SIRIUS 4 formula and structure annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The LC-MS runs contain spectra in profiled mode — the paper discards these before feature detection Only negative ion mode spectra are available, or the fragmentation spectra have at most one peak, since such spectra are discarded before processing The goal is targeted quantification on an already-generated feature table rather than de novo annotation of unknown spectra

skills.summary: Step 1 of the bioactive molecular networking workflow: process fractionated LC-MS/MS data with MZmine2 (v2.31) or Optimus (OpenMS-based) to produce an aligned feature quantification table and an MS/MS spectral summary (.MGF) that feed downstream bioactivity correlation scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A feature quantification table (features_quantification_matrix.csv) already exists — proceed directly to Step 2 (Jupyter notebook Pearson correlation) instead. skills.search_text: lc-msms-feature-mz-rt-matching Use when a preprocessed margheRita mRList (MS-Dial-exported features with m/z, retention time and MS/MS spectra) must be matched against a reference spectral library to produce feature-metabolite associations up to level-1 confidence. skills.summary: Assign metabolite identities to LC-MS/MS features by matching feature m/z, retention time and MS/MS spectra against a reference spectral library of standards, yielding level-1 confident identifications in margheRita.

skills.search_text: lc-msms-feature-network-edge-overlay Use when a globaltest-prioritized LC-MS/MS differential feature must be inspected in its spectral-similarity network context — e.g. to check whether its strongest neighbors (top-30 edges) reach beyond its small k-medoid cluster. skills.summary: Builds a top-N neighbor edge list (feature_A, feature_B, spectral-similarity) for a prioritized LC-MS/MS differential feature and overlays it on the msFeaST interactive feature network to assess whether connectivity extends beyond the feature's own k-medoids spectral-similarity cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No pairwise spectral similarity matrix is available for the LC-MS/MS features (edges cannot carry pairwise similarity information). skills.search_text: lc-msms-untargeted-metabolomics-data-processing Use when an agent must reproduce or extend KGMN annotation of known and unknown metabolites from untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics output (e.g., NIST human urine positive/negative mode) and quantify how far annotation expands beyond seed metabolites. Input is raw LC-MS vendor data not yet processed through KGMN/MetDNA2 — this skill visualizes and reproduces existing KGMN annotation output, not raw peak detection Samples from non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles, where organism-specific reaction databases are not incorporated and the article advises caution Scenarios requiring discrimination of structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduce KGMN (knowledge-guided multi-layer network) global metabolite annotation from knowns to unknowns on LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data, using MetDNA2Vis to rebuild the three-layer network (KMRN, knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network, global peak correlation network) and tabulate known/unknown peak counts per ionization mode. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Reproduce KGMN (knowledge-guided multi-layer network) global metabolite annotation from knowns to unknowns on LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data, using MetDNA2Vis to rebuild the three-layer network (KMRN, knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network, global peak correlation network) and tabulate known/unknown peak counts per ionization mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS vendor data not yet processed through KGMN/MetDNA2 — this skill visualizes and reproduces existing KGMN annotation output, not raw peak detection Samples from non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles, where organism-specific reaction databases are not incorporated and the article advises caution Scenarios requiring discrimination of structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively resolve

skills.description: Use when raw LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics files (e.g. mzML from a Bruker Impac II qQToF or similar) plus a Metadata Table describing samples/sample groups must be converted into quantified, cleaned consensus spectra, library annotations, and a filtered SSMN.
skills.name: lc-msms-untargeted-metabolomics-processing
skills.search_text: lc-msms-untargeted-metabolomics-processing Use when raw LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics files (e.g. mzML from a Bruker Impac II qQToF or similar) plus a Metadata Table describing samples/sample groups must be converted into quantified, cleaned consensus spectra, library annotations, and a filtered SSMN. Input is already a feature/quantification table or clean consensus spectra — the skill targets raw LC–MS/MS data processing from step 2 onward The goal is a purely targeted MS/MS experiment (e.g. MRM/SRM) rather than untargeted feature detection, clustering, and molecular networking A plain GNPS FBMN comparison is wanted without NP3-specific steps such as NP3-shifted cosine cleaning, IVAMN [M+H]+ deconvolution, or K-most-similar-neighbor damped pruning http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 End-to-end processing of LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data with the NP3 MS Workflow, a Nextflow-based open-source pipeline (steps 1–10) that detects MS1 features, clusters and cleans MS2 spectra with the NP3-shifted cosine, identifies compounds via Tremolo against ISDB/GNPS2, and builds [M+H]+ IVAMNs and filtered SSMNs for natural-product-based drug discovery. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: End-to-end processing of LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data with the NP3 MS Workflow, a Nextflow-based open-source pipeline (steps 1–10) that detects MS1 features, clusters and cleans MS2 spectra with the NP3-shifted cosine, identifies compounds via Tremolo against ISDB/GNPS2, and builds [M+H]+ IVAMNs and filtered SSMNs for natural-product-based drug discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/quantification table or clean consensus spectra — the skill targets raw LC–MS/MS data processing from step 2 onward The goal is a purely targeted MS/MS experiment (e.g. MRM/SRM) rather than untargeted feature detection, clustering, and molecular networking A plain GNPS FBMN comparison is wanted without NP3-specific steps such as NP3-shifted cosine cleaning, IVAMN [M+H]+ deconvolution, or K-most-similar-neighbor damped pruning
