skills.name: lc-msms-workflow-result-integration
skills.search_text: lc-msms-workflow-result-integration Use when raw PSM tables from LC-MS/MS peptide searches must be filtered (unique peptides, unique monoisotopic mass, >=5 peptides/protein) to confirm putative MSI identifications or replicate Figure 4-style filtering cascades. Input is already a filtered protein/peptide table (e.g., only proteins with >=5 unique peptides) — reapplying the cascade would double-filter Data are unfiltered MSI spectra (mzML/imzML) requiring pre-processing or registration rather than LC-MS/MS PSM filtering — use the MSI pre-processing or H&E registration workflows instead Identifications come from targeted LC-MS/MS rather than the untargeted global approach MSIght is designed for http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A method for turning untargeted LC-MS/MS PSM results (e.g., MSFragger/FragPipe output searched against the Mus musculus proteome at 1% protein FDR) into a confident set of peptide identifications used to confirm and annotate MALDI-MS images in the MSIght pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: A method for turning untargeted LC-MS/MS PSM results (e.g., MSFragger/FragPipe output searched against the Mus musculus proteome at 1% protein FDR) into a confident set of peptide identifications used to confirm and annotate MALDI-MS images in the MSIght pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered protein/peptide table (e.g., only proteins with >=5 unique peptides) — reapplying the cascade would double-filter Data are unfiltered MSI spectra (mzML/imzML) requiring pre-processing or registration rather than LC-MS/MS PSM filtering — use the MSI pre-processing or H&E registration workflows instead Identifications come from targeted LC-MS/MS rather than the untargeted global approach MSIght is designed for

skills.description: Use when a complete LC-MS/MS run yields multiple MS/MS spectra with associated retention times and scored candidate lists from an MS/MS-based predictor like IOKR, and the goal is to jointly identify a set of metabolites by combining MS/MS-based scores with predicted retention order.
skills.name: lc-retention-time-layer-ordering
skills.search_text: lc-retention-time-layer-ordering Use when a complete LC-MS/MS run yields multiple MS/MS spectra with associated retention times and scored candidate lists from an MS/MS-based predictor like IOKR, and the goal is to jointly identify a set of metabolites by combining MS/MS-based scores with predicted retention order. Only a single MS/MS spectrum is available (no set of spectra to layer); the graph degenerates and the joint identification via shortest path is not applicable Retention times are not measured or not available for the MS/MS spectra, so layers cannot be ordered by increasing retention time The IOKR scored candidate lists or the RankSVM weight vector are missing — the edge-weight formula requires both the MS/MS-based score y and the retention-order predictor w http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Constructs a layered shortest-path graph for joint metabolite identification by ordering each MS/MS spectrum layer by increasing retention time and sorting candidate nodes within each layer by decreasing IOKR score. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty590
skills.summary: Constructs a layered shortest-path graph for joint metabolite identification by ordering each MS/MS spectrum layer by increasing retention time and sorting candidate nodes within each layer by decreasing IOKR score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single MS/MS spectrum is available (no set of spectra to layer); the graph degenerates and the joint identification via shortest path is not applicable Retention times are not measured or not available for the MS/MS spectra, so layers cannot be ordered by increasing retention time The IOKR scored candidate lists or the RankSVM weight vector are missing — the edge-weight formula requires both the MS/MS-based score y and the retention-order predictor w

skills.description: Use when vendor raw LC-SRM/LC-MS files must be converted into quantified analyte concentrations via scheduled SRM transition extraction, peak picking, and isotope-dilution or external calibration in Skyline.
skills.name: lc-srm-chromatogram-peak-integration
skills.search_text: lc-srm-chromatogram-peak-integration Use when vendor raw LC-SRM/LC-MS files must be converted into quantified analyte concentrations via scheduled SRM transition extraction, peak picking, and isotope-dilution or external calibration in Skyline. The analysis is untargeted/nontargeted feature finding rather than extraction of known targets — use XCMS, MZmine, or MS-DIAL instead The data are GC-MS or ion mobility small molecule acquisitions, where Skyline support is still ongoing A vendor-specific latest-generation workflow is required where Skyline may lag behind commercial software http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Integrate targeted LC-SRM ion chromatograms in Skyline to quantify small-molecule analytes, using retention-time-scheduled transition lists, heavy-labeled internal standards, and calibration curves to produce per-analyte concentrations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.9b00640
skills.summary: Integrate targeted LC-SRM ion chromatograms in Skyline to quantify small-molecule analytes, using retention-time-scheduled transition lists, heavy-labeled internal standards, and calibration curves to produce per-analyte concentrations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is untargeted/nontargeted feature finding rather than extraction of known targets — use XCMS, MZmine, or MS-DIAL instead The data are GC-MS or ion mobility small molecule acquisitions, where Skyline support is still ongoing A vendor-specific latest-generation workflow is required where Skyline may lag behind commercial software

skills.description: Use when a recurring unassigned LC-HRMS peak (e.g. a specific m/z in positive mode, such as m/z 247.1441 in NIST plasma) must be resolved to a metabolite annotation and its MSI confidence level across instruments.
skills.name: lchrms-annotation-extraction
skills.search_text: lchrms-annotation-extraction Use when a recurring unassigned LC-HRMS peak (e.g. a specific m/z in positive mode, such as m/z 247.1441 in NIST plasma) must be resolved to a metabolite annotation and its MSI confidence level across instruments. Input is already a curated feature-annotation table with confirmed metabolite identities and MSI levels rather than raw or partially annotated spectral records The task requires raw spectral data storage or data clean-up/extraction from vendor files — PeakForest stores metadata related to raw data rather than raw data itself and 'does not include data clean-up or extraction tools per se' The spectra are NMR rather than MS, or require 2D NMR matching or MS-MS matching capabilities beyond current PeakForest matching features http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extracts and cross-checks LC-HRMS/MS metabolite annotations (observed m/z, ionization mode, metabolite identity, MSI confidence level) for a recurrent unassigned signal across multiple instruments, using the PeakForest Web services and the source article as ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
skills.summary: Extracts and cross-checks LC-HRMS/MS metabolite annotations (observed m/z, ionization mode, metabolite identity, MSI confidence level) for a recurrent unassigned signal across multiple instruments, using the PeakForest Web services and the source article as ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature-annotation table with confirmed metabolite identities and MSI levels rather than raw or partially annotated spectral records The task requires raw spectral data storage or data clean-up/extraction from vendor files — PeakForest stores metadata related to raw data rather than raw data itself and 'does not include data clean-up or extraction tools per se' The spectra are NMR rather than MS, or require 2D NMR matching or MS-MS matching capabilities beyond current PeakForest matching features

skills.description: Use when raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms must be converted into chromatographic feature lists, or when comparing peak-picking tools (PeakBot vs XCMS, MS-Dial, peakOnly) on a shared dataset such as the PHM porcine hepatic microsome data.
skills.name: lchrms-peak-picking-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: lchrms-peak-picking-pipeline-execution Use when raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms must be converted into chromatographic feature lists, or when comparing peak-picking tools (PeakBot vs XCMS, MS-Dial, peakOnly) on a shared dataset such as the PHM porcine hepatic microsome data. Input is already a centroided feature table or peak list — only alignment/grouping is needed, not profile-mode peak picking. Fewer than 100 reference features are available and no pretrained PeakBot model exists — the CNN cannot be trained to high quality. Data are not profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms (e.g. GC-MS or pre-processed centroided data), which the local-maxima-to-standardized-area workflow does not target. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Executes an end-to-end LC-HRMS profile-mode peak-picking pipeline (PeakBot CNN-based detection, or equivalent tools such as XCMS, MS-Dial and peakOnly) to convert raw chromatograms into aligned feature lists, and quantifies cross-tool feature overlap as validation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Executes an end-to-end LC-HRMS profile-mode peak-picking pipeline (PeakBot CNN-based detection, or equivalent tools such as XCMS, MS-Dial and peakOnly) to convert raw chromatograms into aligned feature lists, and quantifies cross-tool feature overlap as validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a centroided feature table or peak list — only alignment/grouping is needed, not profile-mode peak picking. Fewer than 100 reference features are available and no pretrained PeakBot model exists — the CNN cannot be trained to high quality. Data are not profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms (e.g. GC-MS or pre-processed centroided data), which the local-maxima-to-standardized-area workflow does not target.

skills.description: Use when geoRge's PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder have produced labeled base-peak m/z values on an XCMS feature table and you need putative metabolite identities with adduct assignments in negative-ion LC/MS.
skills.name: lcms-adduct-annotation
skills.search_text: lcms-adduct-annotation Use when geoRge's PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder have produced labeled base-peak m/z values on an XCMS feature table and you need putative metabolite identities with adduct assignments in negative-ion LC/MS. Input is raw mzXML or an XCMS xcmsSet that has not been processed by PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder — the skill expects the geoRge labeled base-peak object, not raw features. Data are acquired in positive-ion mode and no negative-mode adduct list is available — the pipeline as documented uses adducts_negative.txt. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Annotate isotopically labeled LC/MS features detected by geoRge's basepeak_finder with putative metabolite identities by matching measured m/z values against a metabolite database and negative-mode adduct masses (e.g. -H, +Cl) within a user-defined ppm tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: Annotate isotopically labeled LC/MS features detected by geoRge's basepeak_finder with putative metabolite identities by matching measured m/z values against a metabolite database and negative-mode adduct masses (e.g. -H, +Cl) within a user-defined ppm tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzXML or an XCMS xcmsSet that has not been processed by PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder — the skill expects the geoRge labeled base-peak object, not raw features. Data are acquired in positive-ion mode and no negative-mode adduct list is available — the pipeline as documented uses adducts_negative.txt.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the m/z offset detection accuracy of an LC-HRMS alignment tool by injecting known m/z shifts into a reference feature list and comparing imposed versus detected offsets.
skills.name: lcms-alignment-benchmarking
skills.search_text: lcms-alignment-benchmarking Use when benchmarking the m/z offset detection accuracy of an LC-HRMS alignment tool by injecting known m/z shifts into a reference feature list and comparing imposed versus detected offsets. The goal is to align experimental (naturally shifted) batches rather than to benchmark offset-detection accuracy with synthetically imposed shifts The input is already an aligned, combined data matrix of chromatographic peak areas, m/z values and retention times Retention time (rather than m/z) offset accuracy is the target, since this benchmark protocol as sourced covers the m/z offset test of Figure 8 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A benchmarking protocol for quantifying how accurately MetMatch detects artificially imposed m/z offsets (−10 to +10 ppm in 1 ppm increments) when aligning LC-HRMS feature lists to a reference chromatogram, validating software alignment accuracy at 0.01 ppm resolution. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol for quantifying how accurately MetMatch detects artificially imposed m/z offsets (−10 to +10 ppm in 1 ppm increments) when aligning LC-HRMS feature lists to a reference chromatogram, validating software alignment accuracy at 0.01 ppm resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to align experimental (naturally shifted) batches rather than to benchmark offset-detection accuracy with synthetically imposed shifts The input is already an aligned, combined data matrix of chromatographic peak areas, m/z values and retention times Retention time (rather than m/z) offset accuracy is the target, since this benchmark protocol as sourced covers the m/z offset test of Figure 8

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered peak list from an LC-MS assay with m/z, RT and adduct/fragment information, and need a KEGG-based, context-prioritized compound annotation per peak rather than a simple mass matching.
skills.name: lcms-annotation-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: lcms-annotation-workflow-execution Use when you have a filtered peak list from an LC-MS assay with m/z, RT and adduct/fragment information, and need a KEGG-based, context-prioritized compound annotation per peak rather than a simple mass matching. When annotation targets databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) — mWISE only offers KEGG, a limitation relative to xMSannotator When the input is already an annotated compound table or spectral library match — this skill starts from raw peak-to-KEGG matching, not from pre-annotated features When the peak list has not been pre-filtered (features without signal removed, 80% rule applied where intensity equals 0) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 End-to-end execution of the mWISE LC-MS annotation workflow: matching LC-MS peaks to KEGG, clustering and filtering candidates, and diffusing labels in a FELLA or RClass network to produce a prioritized per-peak candidate list. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: End-to-end execution of the mWISE LC-MS annotation workflow: matching LC-MS peaks to KEGG, clustering and filtering candidates, and diffusing labels in a FELLA or RClass network to produce a prioritized per-peak candidate list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When annotation targets databases other than KEGG (e.g. HMDB, Lipid Maps, T3DB) — mWISE only offers KEGG, a limitation relative to xMSannotator When the input is already an annotated compound table or spectral library match — this skill starts from raw peak-to-KEGG matching, not from pre-annotated features When the peak list has not been pre-filtered (features without signal removed, 80% rule applied where intensity equals 0)

skills.description: Use when you have an XCMS feature table from UPLC/ESI-QTOFMS data (positive and negative ion mode) and need to group co-eluting, adduct, and isotope features into per-analyte compound spectra before compound identification.
skills.name: lcms-compound-spectra-extraction
skills.search_text: lcms-compound-spectra-extraction Use when you have an XCMS feature table from UPLC/ESI-QTOFMS data (positive and negative ion mode) and need to group co-eluting, adduct, and isotope features into per-analyte compound spectra before compound identification. When the input is already a deconvoluted compound spectrum or a list of quasi-molecular ions — grouping is redundant. When the analysis goal is targeted quantification of known analytes rather than untargeted feature-list reduction and ion annotation. When the MS detector is saturated (m/z and RT centroids shift and peak profiles truncate), which CAMERA assumes does not happen. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extract pseudo-spectra (compound spectra) from LC/MS feature tables by grouping features derived from the same analyte and annotating isotope, adduct, and fragment peaks to reduce feature-list redundancy and propose accurate compound masses. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Extract pseudo-spectra (compound spectra) from LC/MS feature tables by grouping features derived from the same analyte and annotating isotope, adduct, and fragment peaks to reduce feature-list redundancy and propose accurate compound masses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a deconvoluted compound spectrum or a list of quasi-molecular ions — grouping is redundant. When the analysis goal is targeted quantification of known analytes rather than untargeted feature-list reduction and ion annotation. When the MS detector is saturated (m/z and RT centroids shift and peak profiles truncate), which CAMERA assumes does not happen.

skills.description: Use when two or more independently processed same-method nontargeted LC-MS datasets must be aligned to form a complete dataset, and you need pairwise Source→Target subalignment match tables.
skills.name: lcms-cross-dataset-feature-matching
skills.search_text: lcms-cross-dataset-feature-matching Use when two or more independently processed same-method nontargeted LC-MS datasets must be aligned to form a complete dataset, and you need pairwise Source→Target subalignment match tables. You need redundant-feature clustering based on RT and correlation — that is Gravity's role, not Eclipse's subalignment matching You need drift correction of pooled technical replicates and internal standards — that is Blueshift's DriftCorrection step Datasets were produced by different LC-MS methods — Eclipse is scoped to align same-method nontargeted LCMS datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3369 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Cross-dataset nontargeted LC-MS feature alignment via Eclipse (bmxp): scale the Source dataset to the Target with survey-based LOWESS RT/m-z scalers, retain candidate matches within ±6 RSE on RT, m/z and Intensity, and assign one-to-one best matches by penalty-score ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf290
skills.summary: Cross-dataset nontargeted LC-MS feature alignment via Eclipse (bmxp): scale the Source dataset to the Target with survey-based LOWESS RT/m-z scalers, retain candidate matches within ±6 RSE on RT, m/z and Intensity, and assign one-to-one best matches by penalty-score ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need redundant-feature clustering based on RT and correlation — that is Gravity's role, not Eclipse's subalignment matching You need drift correction of pooled technical replicates and internal standards — that is Blueshift's DriftCorrection step Datasets were produced by different LC-MS methods — Eclipse is scoped to align same-method nontargeted LCMS datasets

skills.description: Use when a Thermo .raw or .mzML LC-MS data file needs to be loaded into lcmsWorld for 3D visualization, especially as the first load of a file that has no cached .lcms conversion yet.
skills.name: lcms-data-ingestion
skills.search_text: lcms-data-ingestion Use when a Thermo .raw or .mzML LC-MS data file needs to be loaded into lcmsWorld for 3D visualization, especially as the first load of a file that has no cached .lcms conversion yet. The data is already in .lcms format — load it directly to start viewing instantly instead of re-ingesting the .raw/.mzml. The input is a peptide identification file (.csv or tab-separated text with m/z, rt, intensity columns) — these are loaded via the identification/Annotations pathway, not the LC-MS ingestion pathway. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Ingests LC-MS data into lcmsWorld by loading Thermo .raw or .mzML files through Thermo RawFileReader (a 64-bit .NET application), which triggers automatic conversion to a .lcms file for fast streaming during visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00618
skills.summary: Ingests LC-MS data into lcmsWorld by loading Thermo .raw or .mzML files through Thermo RawFileReader (a 64-bit .NET application), which triggers automatic conversion to a .lcms file for fast streaming during visualization.

skills.description: Use when running or monitoring large LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics analyses (e.g. Thermo Orbitrap acquisition sequences) and you need per-specimen QC status (Pass/Fail/Warn) for internal standards within minutes of each raw file being written.
skills.name: lcms-data-quality-control-assessment
skills.search_text: lcms-data-quality-control-assessment Use when running or monitoring large LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics analyses (e.g. Thermo Orbitrap acquisition sequences) and you need per-specimen QC status (Pass/Fail/Warn) for internal standards within minutes of each raw file being written. The data are from Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, or Waters acquisition sequences and vendor formats — the tool has only been tested extensively on Thermo Fisher mass spectrometers, Thermo acquisition sequences, and Thermo RAW files. The analysis is post-hoc batch QC with no need for real-time, in-run monitoring — Rapid QC-MS is designed for synchronous assessment during data acquisition, not retrospective reprocessing. The environment is MacOS-only — MSConvert and MS-DIAL dependencies are Windows-oriented, and MacOS users can only use Rapid QC-MS to monitor/view instrument run data, not run the full QC pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Automated, real-time LC-MS/MS data quality assessment using Rapid QC-MS, which converts Thermo RAW files to mzML via MSConvert, processes them with MS-DIAL against an .msp library, and surfaces internal standard retention time, m/z, and intensity QC results on a browser dashboard with Slack/email alerts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Automated, real-time LC-MS/MS data quality assessment using Rapid QC-MS, which converts Thermo RAW files to mzML via MSConvert, processes them with MS-DIAL against an .msp library, and surfaces internal standard retention time, m/z, and intensity QC results on a browser dashboard with Slack/email alerts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are from Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, or Waters acquisition sequences and vendor formats — the tool has only been tested extensively on Thermo Fisher mass spectrometers, Thermo acquisition sequences, and Thermo RAW files. The analysis is post-hoc batch QC with no need for real-time, in-run monitoring — Rapid QC-MS is designed for synchronous assessment during data acquisition, not retrospective reprocessing. The environment is MacOS-only — MSConvert and MS-DIAL dependencies are Windows-oriented, and MacOS users can only use Rapid QC-MS to monitor/view instrument run data, not run the full QC pipeline.

skills.description: Use when building an in-house LC-MS metabolite standard reference library from mzML files and per-adduct EICs must be generated at expected m/z values before peak finding, peak-quality filtering, or RT assignment.
skills.name: lcms-eic-extraction
skills.search_text: lcms-eic-extraction Use when building an in-house LC-MS metabolite standard reference library from mzML files and per-adduct EICs must be generated at expected m/z values before peak finding, peak-quality filtering, or RT assignment. skills.search_text: lcms-feature-grouping-retention-time-coelution Use when processing raw LC/MS feature lists (e.g. from XCMS) where multiple m/z features originate from a single metabolite and you need to reduce feature-list redundancy before adduct or isotope annotation. skills.summary: Group LC/MS features derived from the same analyte into pseudo-spectra ('compound spectra') by co-elution using Gaussian retention-time peak-shape similarity and EIC intensity correlation across samples, as implemented in CAMERA's groupFWHM and groupCorr functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table with per-analyte grouping (e.g. annotated by hand or from a reference library). skills.search_text: lcms-feature-matching Use when integrating two similar untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables (e.g. two batches or two cohorts peak-picked with XCMS) that need feature-level correspondence based solely on RT, MZ, and FI values. skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS mass spectra must be converted into a fixed-dimension 2D feature matrix (m/z bins × RT windows) for feeding CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers, and spectrum_dim differs per dataset (e.g. 12000 NSCLC/CRLM, 9900 RCC, 15000 Canine Sarcoma).

skills.name: lcms-feature-quantification-peak-area-extraction
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-quantification-peak-area-extraction Use when LC-MS data contain a dilution/mixing series with known composition ratios (e.g. BM21 plasma–vegetable juice dilutions) and you need to compare peak-area quantification quality across processing tools like asari vs XCMS. Input is already a feature table from a single tool with no competing quantification to benchmark, and no dilution/mixing series exists to define expected abundance gradients Data are low-resolution LC-MS or non-Orbitrap platforms, since asari does not work with low-resolution data and its settings are mostly tested on Orbitrap platforms MS/MS-centric analyses, because MS/MS spectra are ignored by asari's default LC-MS workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Extract peak-area feature tables from LC-MS metabolomics data using asari and XCMS, then evaluate quantification quality by correlating feature peak areas against known sample mixing ratios in a dilution series (BM21). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Extract peak-area feature tables from LC-MS metabolomics data using asari and XCMS, then evaluate quantification quality by correlating feature peak areas against known sample mixing ratios in a dilution series (BM21).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table from a single tool with no competing quantification to benchmark, and no dilution/mixing series exists to define expected abundance gradients Data are low-resolution LC-MS or non-Orbitrap platforms, since asari does not work with low-resolution data and its settings are mostly tested on Orbitrap platforms MS/MS-centric analyses, because MS/MS spectra are ignored by asari's default LC-MS workflow

skills.description: Use when DIA (SWATH) feature tables of individual biological samples lack metabolic features that were confidently detected in the pooled-QC DDA run, and their intensities must be recovered from the DIA raw data.
skills.name: lcms-feature-rescue-from-dda-in-dia
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-rescue-from-dda-in-dia Use when DIA (SWATH) feature tables of individual biological samples lack metabolic features that were confidently detected in the pooled-QC DDA run, and their intensities must be recovered from the DIA raw data. The feature is already detected with an intensity in the DIA feature table of the individual sample — no rescue is needed. Input files are not paired DDA/DIA mzXML acquisitions (e.g. only DIA or only DDA data exist), since EIC matching requires the DIA raw chromatogram at the DDA feature's m/z and retention time. The goal is MS2 spectral annotation rather than intensity recovery — use the DaDIA.R annotation step with the MoNA spectral library instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Rescue metabolic features that were detected in the pooled-QC DDA run but are missing from the individual-sample DIA feature tables by matching extracted-ion chromatograms (EICs) in the DIA raw data, as implemented in the DaDIA.R workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c05022
skills.summary: Rescue metabolic features that were detected in the pooled-QC DDA run but are missing from the individual-sample DIA feature tables by matching extracted-ion chromatograms (EICs) in the DIA raw data, as implemented in the DaDIA.R workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature is already detected with an intensity in the DIA feature table of the individual sample — no rescue is needed. Input files are not paired DDA/DIA mzXML acquisitions (e.g. only DIA or only DDA data exist), since EIC matching requires the DIA raw chromatogram at the DDA feature's m/z and retention time. The goal is MS2 spectral annotation rather than intensity recovery — use the DaDIA.R annotation step with the MoNA spectral library instead.

skills.description: Use when processing LC/MS feature tables from untargeted metabolomics where features must be grouped into compound spectra and annotated with ion species to cut feature count before statistical analysis or compound identification.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-analysis
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-analysis Use when processing LC/MS feature tables from untargeted metabolomics where features must be grouped into compound spectra and annotated with ion species to cut feature count before statistical analysis or compound identification. When the input is already a feature table annotated at the compound level (no need to re-derive grouping rules) When only MS/MS spectral matching is needed and no LC feature grouping is required When the user has a single-polarity dataset and cannot tolerate the added complexity of cross-polarity rule overrides http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Group LC/MS features derived from the same analyte and annotate ion species (adducts, isotopes, neutral losses) in feature tables using CAMERA's dynamic rule set, reducing feature-list redundancy and revealing quasi-molecular ions for downstream identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Group LC/MS features derived from the same analyte and annotate ion species (adducts, isotopes, neutral losses) in feature tables using CAMERA's dynamic rule set, reducing feature-list redundancy and revealing quasi-molecular ions for downstream identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a feature table annotated at the compound level (no need to re-derive grouping rules) When only MS/MS spectral matching is needed and no LC feature grouping is required When the user has a single-polarity dataset and cannot tolerate the added complexity of cross-polarity rule overrides

skills.description: Use when you have a tab-delimited feature table (feature ID, m/z, rtime, intensities) from LC-MS data — e.g. from asari v1.9.2 — and need to group degenerate ions into empirical compounds and infer neutral masses before database annotation, including stable isotope tracing.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-annotation
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-annotation Use when you have a tab-delimited feature table (feature ID, m/z, rtime, intensities) from LC-MS data — e.g. from asari v1.9.2 — and need to group degenerate ions into empirical compounds and infer neutral masses before database annotation, including stable isotope tracing. You need complete annotation including metabolite names — khipu is pre-annotation only; full annotation still requires contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS data You only have raw LC-MS files — preprocessing (e.g. asari v1.9.2) must run first to produce the feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Pre-annotation of LC-MS feature tables into khipu trees ('empirical compounds') by connecting isotope and adduct edges into a mass distance network, converting it to a directed acyclic graph, and inferring the M0 neutral mass by regression — the generalized tree structure of Li and Zheng (2023). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Pre-annotation of LC-MS feature tables into khipu trees ('empirical compounds') by connecting isotope and adduct edges into a mass distance network, converting it to a directed acyclic graph, and inferring the M0 neutral mass by regression — the generalized tree structure of Li and Zheng (2023).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need complete annotation including metabolite names — khipu is pre-annotation only; full annotation still requires contaminants, authentic libraries, and tandem MS data You only have raw LC-MS files — preprocessing (e.g. asari v1.9.2) must run first to produce the feature table

skills.description: Use when apLCMS- or XCMS-generated feature tables (m/z, RT, intensity columns) from LC/MS metabolomics data acquired in negative ion mode need KEGG metabolite annotation via adduct matching, e.g. to compare annotation/matching rates across preprocessing methods.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-annotation
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-annotation Use when apLCMS- or XCMS-generated feature tables (m/z, RT, intensity columns) from LC/MS metabolomics data acquired in negative ion mode need KEGG metabolite annotation via adduct matching, e.g. to compare annotation/matching rates across preprocessing methods. Input is raw LC/MS profiles (NetCDF/CDF files) rather than a processed feature table — first run apLCMS cdf.to.ftr/proc.cdf preprocessing The data were acquired in positive ion mode — the adduct list in this workflow is negative-mode specific ([M-H]- etc.) The goal is correcting between-batch intensity differences post hoc — the paper notes such methods 'can only adjust signal intensity' and cannot fix misalignment or incomplete weak signal recovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate LC/MS feature tables (m/z, retention time, intensity) against the KEGG metabolite database via xMSAnnotator using the paper's nine negative-mode adduct ions, to compute per-method m/z matching rates as in Fig. 3b of the ST000868 batch-effect study. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: Annotate LC/MS feature tables (m/z, retention time, intensity) against the KEGG metabolite database via xMSAnnotator using the paper's nine negative-mode adduct ions, to compute per-method m/z matching rates as in Fig. 3b of the ST000868 batch-effect study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC/MS profiles (NetCDF/CDF files) rather than a processed feature table — first run apLCMS cdf.to.ftr/proc.cdf preprocessing The data were acquired in positive ion mode — the adduct list in this workflow is negative-mode specific ([M-H]- etc.) The goal is correcting between-batch intensity differences post hoc — the paper notes such methods 'can only adjust signal intensity' and cannot fix misalignment or incomplete weak signal recovery

skills.description: Use when an LC/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table must be turned into the two input lists (significant m/z features and reference list of all detected features) that mummichog requires for pathway/network activity prediction.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-filtering
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-filtering Use when an LC/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table must be turned into the two input lists (significant m/z features and reference list of all detected features) that mummichog requires for pathway/network activity prediction. Input is already a cleaned feature table or annotation file (e.g. JMS empirical-compound JSON); the skill targets raw feature-table QC and significance filtering Data are tandem-MS spectra intended for metabolite identification; the article states mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification The analysis goal is targeted quantification of known metabolites rather than untargeted pathway/network activity prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Prepares the m/z feature tables (significant list and reference list) that mummichog consumes by applying QC-driven intensity, CV, imputation, and significance filters to LC/MS metabolomics data from untargeted profiling experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: Prepares the m/z feature tables (significant list and reference list) that mummichog consumes by applying QC-driven intensity, CV, imputation, and significance filters to LC/MS metabolomics data from untargeted profiling experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned feature table or annotation file (e.g. JMS empirical-compound JSON); the skill targets raw feature-table QC and significance filtering Data are tandem-MS spectra intended for metabolite identification; the article states mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification The analysis goal is targeted quantification of known metabolites rather than untargeted pathway/network activity prediction

skills.description: Use when a feature table with mz, rt, and group-defined intensity columns is available and features enriched between two conditions (e.g. hacl-1 vs WT) must be isolated with intensity, significance, and fold-change cutoffs.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-filtering
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-filtering Use when a feature table with mz, rt, and group-defined intensity columns is available and features enriched between two conditions (e.g. hacl-1 vs WT) must be isolated with intensity, significance, and fold-change cutoffs. Input is raw vendor LC/MS data that has not yet undergone xcms feature detection and alignment — use the xcms module first The analysis goal is molecular formula or fragment-annotation work (e.g. SIRIUS prediction, Find Patterns GLEA motif search) rather than abundance-based feature enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Filter xcms/Metaboseek-derived LC/MS molecular feature tables by intensity percentile, unadjusted p-value, and genotype fold-change thresholds to isolate metabolites enriched in a mutant condition, as done in the hacl-1 vs WT C. elegans exo-metabolome comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: Filter xcms/Metaboseek-derived LC/MS molecular feature tables by intensity percentile, unadjusted p-value, and genotype fold-change thresholds to isolate metabolites enriched in a mutant condition, as done in the hacl-1 vs WT C. elegans exo-metabolome comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor LC/MS data that has not yet undergone xcms feature detection and alignment — use the xcms module first The analysis goal is molecular formula or fragment-annotation work (e.g. SIRIUS prediction, Find Patterns GLEA motif search) rather than abundance-based feature enrichment

skills.description: Use when you have raw mzML files plus an mzMine- or XCMS-derived feature table CSV/TSV and need to bring both into a single NeatMS Experiment for downstream peak labelling.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-import
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-import Use when you have raw mzML files plus an mzMine- or XCMS-derived feature table CSV/TSV and need to bring both into a single NeatMS Experiment for downstream peak labelling. Input is only an already-predicted or annotation-labelled peak table that skips the curation step. The raw LC-MS data folder is unavailable or unreadable — the Experiment constructor loads both raw data and features, so one cannot be supplied without the other. The feature table comes from a pipeline other than mzMine or XCMS (no parser is documented in this context). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Load raw LC-MS data files and a processed feature table (e.g. mzMine or XCMS CSV output) into a NeatMS Experiment object, which builds per-sample peak/feature collections ready for neural-network peak curation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02220
skills.summary: Load raw LC-MS data files and a processed feature table (e.g. mzMine or XCMS CSV output) into a NeatMS Experiment object, which builds per-sample peak/feature collections ready for neural-network peak curation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only an already-predicted or annotation-labelled peak table that skips the curation step. The raw LC-MS data folder is unavailable or unreadable — the Experiment constructor loads both raw data and features, so one cannot be supplied without the other. The feature table comes from a pipeline other than mzMine or XCMS (no parser is documented in this context).

skills.description: Use when you have an LC-MS feature table (from XCMS mzXML extraction or a custom csv from MS-DIAL/MZmine2) and need to identify which features are in-source fragments of which precursor ions.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-interpretation
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-interpretation Use when you have an LC-MS feature table (from XCMS mzXML extraction or a custom csv from MS-DIAL/MZmine2) and need to identify which features are in-source fragments of which precursor ions. When you already have an ISF-annotated results object and only need the relationship-tree visualization (Part 5.2) or the exported ISF result feature table (Part 5.1) rather than feature-table interpretation itself When your input is raw chromatographic data and you need peak alignment/filling across samples — use XCMS directly; ISFrag only operates on the resulting feature table When you need CAMERA adduct and isotope annotation but your feature table comes from a non-XCMS source, since CAMERA annotation is limited to XCMS-only analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Interpret an LC-MS/MS metabolite feature table by recognizing in-source fragments (ISF) with the ISFrag R package, running level 3→2→1 relationship detection and summarizing precursor–fragment relationships. This converts a raw peak table (m/z, rt, rtmin, rtmax, intensities) into annotated ISF relationships usable for results export and tree visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01644
skills.summary: Interpret an LC-MS/MS metabolite feature table by recognizing in-source fragments (ISF) with the ISFrag R package, running level 3→2→1 relationship detection and summarizing precursor–fragment relationships. This converts a raw peak table (m/z, rt, rtmin, rtmax, intensities) into annotated ISF relationships usable for results export and tree visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you already have an ISF-annotated results object and only need the relationship-tree visualization (Part 5.2) or the exported ISF result feature table (Part 5.1) rather than feature-table interpretation itself When your input is raw chromatographic data and you need peak alignment/filling across samples — use XCMS directly; ISFrag only operates on the resulting feature table When you need CAMERA adduct and isotope annotation but your feature table comes from a non-XCMS source, since CAMERA annotation is limited to XCMS-only analysis

skills.description: Use when feature tables from multiple LC-MS processing tools must be parsed and unified for cross-tool comparison or per-feature rescoring, e.g. recomputing peak-shape fitness scores on the Yeast2021 dataset.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-parsing
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-parsing Use when feature tables from multiple LC-MS processing tools must be parsed and unified for cross-tool comparison or per-feature rescoring, e.g. recomputing peak-shape fitness scores on the Yeast2021 dataset. The analysis goal is annotation or pathway analysis on an already-curated feature table rather than cross-tool quality rescoring of raw tool outputs Input is raw (profile-mode or centroided-only) spectra without any tool-produced feature table to parse Data are low-resolution LC-MS, for which the asari-based scoring approach is not designed Loads and normalizes LC-MS feature tables produced by different processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine wavelet and MZmine local minimum) into a common per-feature structure so downstream per-feature quality metrics, such as Gaussian peak-shape fitness on Yeast2021, can be recomputed and compared across tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Loads and normalizes LC-MS feature tables produced by different processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine wavelet and MZmine local minimum) into a common per-feature structure so downstream per-feature quality metrics, such as Gaussian peak-shape fitness on Yeast2021, can be recomputed and compared across tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is annotation or pathway analysis on an already-curated feature table rather than cross-tool quality rescoring of raw tool outputs Input is raw (profile-mode or centroided-only) spectra without any tool-produced feature table to parse Data are low-resolution LC-MS, for which the asari-based scoring approach is not designed

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS(/MS) files from a serially diluted sample set must be preprocessed in MZmine into aligned full-scan feature tables (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak areas) suitable for downstream regression-based feature selection.
skills.name: lcms-feature-table-processing
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-table-processing Use when raw LC-MS(/MS) files from a serially diluted sample set must be preprocessed in MZmine into aligned full-scan feature tables (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak areas) suitable for downstream regression-based feature selection. The input is already an aligned MZmine .csv feature table — skip preprocessing and proceed directly to the RegFilter filtering step The data are targeted MS/MS acquisitions with no serial dilution series, so linear-regression filtering across dilution points is not meaningful Only DDA-mode data without a full-scan feature table are available, since the filtering pool requires the full-scan features detected in full scan mode http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Converts raw LC-MS files to .mzXML, preprocesses full-scan and MS/MS data in MZmine 2.53 (mass detection, ADAP chromatogram building, deconvolution, isotopic grouping, join alignment, gap filling), and exports aligned feature tables (.csv) that feed the RegFilter dilution-series filter. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Converts raw LC-MS files to .mzXML, preprocesses full-scan and MS/MS data in MZmine 2.53 (mass detection, ADAP chromatogram building, deconvolution, isotopic grouping, join alignment, gap filling), and exports aligned feature tables (.csv) that feed the RegFilter dilution-series filter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an aligned MZmine .csv feature table — skip preprocessing and proceed directly to the RegFilter filtering step The data are targeted MS/MS acquisitions with no serial dilution series, so linear-regression filtering across dilution points is not meaningful Only DDA-mode data without a full-scan feature table are available, since the filtering pool requires the full-scan features detected in full scan mode

skills.description: Reference for grouping LC/MS peaks detected by XCMS into per-analyte compound spectra when you need to de-redundant a feature list and know which features co-elute with a compound.
skills.name: lcms-feature-to-compound-spectrum-assignment
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-to-compound-spectrum-assignment Reference for grouping LC/MS peaks detected by XCMS into per-analyte compound spectra when you need to de-redundant a feature list and know which features co-elute with a compound. The input is already a dereplicated compound spectrum or a list of per-analyte spectra — groupFWHM would re-split already-grouped features. Retention-time windows are unreliable because chromatographic peak shapes are saturated; the authors note that saturation 'is known to cause shifts of m/z and retention time centroids of the features'. The goal is peak detection rather than feature grouping — use the upstream XCMS feature-detection step instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Assigns LC/MS features from an XCMS feature table into compound spectra (pseudospectra) using CAMERA's retention-time/FWHM-based grouping, with subsequent m/z and correlation-based refinement, to recover the features derived from a single analyte. Grounded in CAMERA's evaluation against the MM39 mixture of 39 known compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Assigns LC/MS features from an XCMS feature table into compound spectra (pseudospectra) using CAMERA's retention-time/FWHM-based grouping, with subsequent m/z and correlation-based refinement, to recover the features derived from a single analyte. Grounded in CAMERA's evaluation against the MM39 mixture of 39 known compounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a dereplicated compound spectrum or a list of per-analyte spectra — groupFWHM would re-split already-grouped features. Retention-time windows are unreliable because chromatographic peak shapes are saturated; the authors note that saturation 'is known to cause shifts of m/z and retention time centroids of the features'. The goal is peak detection rather than feature grouping — use the upstream XCMS feature-detection step instead.

skills.description: Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table (mass_dataset object) needs metabolite annotations, and database-level identifications (MSI level 2) must be produced by matching m/z and retention time.
skills.name: lcms-feature-to-metabolite-mapping
skills.search_text: lcms-feature-to-metabolite-mapping Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table (mass_dataset object) needs metabolite annotations, and database-level identifications (MSI level 2) must be produced by matching m/z and retention time. Input is raw LC-MS data that has not been peak-picked and cleaned — run the tidyMass raw data processing and data cleaning steps first You require MSI level 1 identifications or MS/MS spectral verification — this skill only guarantees annotations up to MSI level 2 You need to annotate GC-MS or MS/MS data — the skill is grounded in LC-MS feature tables only http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates LC-MS peak features to putative metabolites using metID within tidyMass, matching accurate m/z and retention time against in-house HILIC (71 metabolites) and RPLC (55 metabolites) databases plus public databases, then deduplicates annotations by annotation score and retains MSI level 2 identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: Annotates LC-MS peak features to putative metabolites using metID within tidyMass, matching accurate m/z and retention time against in-house HILIC (71 metabolites) and RPLC (55 metabolites) databases plus public databases, then deduplicates annotations by annotation score and retains MSI level 2 identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data that has not been peak-picked and cleaned — run the tidyMass raw data processing and data cleaning steps first You require MSI level 1 identifications or MS/MS spectral verification — this skill only guarantees annotations up to MSI level 2 You need to annotate GC-MS or MS/MS data — the skill is grounded in LC-MS feature tables only

skills.description: Use when building training corpora from repository-scale LC-MS/MS deposits (e.g. MassIVE GNPS .mzML/.mzXML experiments) and you need to drop low-quality files before spectrum-level QC.

skills.search_text: lcms-file-level-quality-filtering Use when building training corpora from repository-scale LC-MS/MS deposits (e.g. MassIVE GNPS .mzML/.mzXML experiments) and you need to drop low-quality files before spectrum-level QC. Input is already a curated spectral library such as MoNA or NIST20 rather than raw mined repository experiments You need spectrum-level filtering (peak count, precursor charge, m/z range, centroid-consistency checks) — this skill covers only file-level checks (Algorithm 1), not Algorithm 2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filter LC-MS/MS experiment files mined from MassIVE GNPS by file-level quality checks before spectrum-level filtering into GeMS-A/B/C subsets, using retention-time/MS-level ordering checks and an XIC-based instrument m/z-accuracy filter (Algorithm 1). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Filter LC-MS/MS experiment files mined from MassIVE GNPS by file-level quality checks before spectrum-level filtering into GeMS-A/B/C subsets, using retention-time/MS-level ordering checks and an XIC-based instrument m/z-accuracy filter (Algorithm 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated spectral library such as MoNA or NIST20 rather than raw mined repository experiments You need spectrum-level filtering (peak count, precursor charge, m/z range, centroid-consistency checks) — this skill covers only file-level checks (Algorithm 1), not Algorithm 2

skills.description: Use when the goal is to identify fluorescently labeled N-linked glycans from LC-MS/MS data acquired on an Orbitrap (or MALDI-TOF) instrument, replacing manual analyst peak picking with automated MS1/MS2 searching and Excel reporting.
skills.name: lcms-glycan-identification-reporting
skills.search_text: lcms-glycan-identification-reporting Use when the goal is to identify fluorescently labeled N-linked glycans from LC-MS/MS data acquired on an Orbitrap (or MALDI-TOF) instrument, replacing manual analyst peak picking with automated MS1/MS2 searching and Excel reporting. The input data are O-linked glycans or the analysis requires de novo glycan identification for structures not in the database — the app is limited to N-linked glycans present in its database You need to process multiple mzXML files simultaneously — batch processing is a planned future improvement, not implemented You need a customizable isomer retention-time window — the ±1.75 min isomer RT range is fixed and cannot be adjusted http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Automate N-linked glycan identification from Orbitrap LC–MS/MS data with GlyKAn AZ: run the MS1 peak search over an mzXML file and MS1 glycan database, detect same-m/z isomer peaks within a ±1.75 min window, confirm candidates by annotated MS2 fragmentation spectra, and report the results in Excel. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Automate N-linked glycan identification from Orbitrap LC–MS/MS data with GlyKAn AZ: run the MS1 peak search over an mzXML file and MS1 glycan database, detect same-m/z isomer peaks within a ±1.75 min window, confirm candidates by annotated MS2 fragmentation spectra, and report the results in Excel.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are O-linked glycans or the analysis requires de novo glycan identification for structures not in the database — the app is limited to N-linked glycans present in its database You need to process multiple mzXML files simultaneously — batch processing is a planned future improvement, not implemented You need a customizable isomer retention-time window — the ±1.75 min isomer RT range is fixed and cannot be adjusted

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed LC-MS peak table (m/z, rt, intensity columns, e.g. the mtbls1358 dataset) should be annotated with homologue series IDs — e.g. to find polymer/PEG-like repeating-unit ladders or compare targeted vs untargeted detection runs.
skills.name: lcms-homologue-series-detection
skills.search_text: lcms-homologue-series-detection Use when a pre-processed LC-MS peak table (m/z, rt, intensity columns, e.g. the mtbls1358 dataset) should be annotated with homologue series IDs — e.g. to find polymer/PEG-like repeating-unit ladders or compare targeted vs untargeted detection runs. Input is raw LC-MS vendor data or an mzML file — the package operates on an already-peak-picked table with mz/rt/intensity columns The goal is general feature detection or peak picking rather than detecting repeating homologue-series ladders at a specific m/z increment Series of interest are shorter than min_series_length (e.g. < 5 members) or fall outside the supplied rt window (e.g. rt ≤ 500 s of the filtered mtbls1358 table) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Detect homologue series in LC-MS metabolomics peak tables using the homologueDiscoverer R package, in either targeted mode (fixed m/z increment, e.g. 44.02628 Da) or untargeted mode (m/z increment window, e.g. 10–20), and manage/merge the resulting annotated series with a local series database. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac647
skills.summary: Detect homologue series in LC-MS metabolomics peak tables using the homologueDiscoverer R package, in either targeted mode (fixed m/z increment, e.g. 44.02628 Da) or untargeted mode (m/z increment window, e.g. 10–20), and manage/merge the resulting annotated series with a local series database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS vendor data or an mzML file — the package operates on an already-peak-picked table with mz/rt/intensity columns The goal is general feature detection or peak picking rather than detecting repeating homologue-series ladders at a specific m/z increment Series of interest are shorter than min_series_length (e.g. < 5 members) or fall outside the supplied rt window (e.g. rt ≤ 500 s of the filtered mtbls1358 table)

skills.description: Use when an LC/MS ion-feature matrix (>150 samples) has QC injections that can be withheld, and the goal is to test whether data-driven synthetic-QC drift correction matches experimental-QC normalization.
skills.name: lcms-intensity-normalization-comparison
skills.search_text: lcms-intensity-normalization-comparison Use when an LC/MS ion-feature matrix (>150 samples) has QC injections that can be withheld, and the goal is to test whether data-driven synthetic-QC drift correction matches experimental-QC normalization. The dataset contains no QC injections (experimental or identifiable run-order QC) whose RSD can serve as the drift-correction benchmark Input is raw mzML spectra rather than a processed ion-feature matrix — peak detection/alignment via mzLearn must run first before this comparison is meaningful The task requires MS/MS identification or de-isotoping — mzLearn output is at the ion MS1 level only and this skill evaluates normalization, not compound annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmarks four LC/MS intensity normalization treatments — mzLearn's synthetic-QC drift correction, withheld experimental-QC correction, total-ion-current (TIC) normalization, and no normalization — by computing relative standard deviation (RSD/CV×100) of feature intensities across hidden QC injections on each normalization-evaluation dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Benchmarks four LC/MS intensity normalization treatments — mzLearn's synthetic-QC drift correction, withheld experimental-QC correction, total-ion-current (TIC) normalization, and no normalization — by computing relative standard deviation (RSD/CV×100) of feature intensities across hidden QC injections on each normalization-evaluation dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no QC injections (experimental or identifiable run-order QC) whose RSD can serve as the drift-correction benchmark Input is raw mzML spectra rather than a processed ion-feature matrix — peak detection/alignment via mzLearn must run first before this comparison is meaningful The task requires MS/MS identification or de-isotoping — mzLearn output is at the ion MS1 level only and this skill evaluates normalization, not compound annotation

skills.search_text: lcms-intensity-rank-sorting Use when processing raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data in R to derive universal feature-extraction parameters via rank-ordered intensity profiles and zone-of-interest structures, prior to tools like MS-DIAL or XCMS CentWave. Input is already a processed feature table or peak list — rank sorting and zone-of-interest derivation apply to raw LC-MS intensity profiles only. Dereplication of features is not needed — mzdiff should be set to a negative value instead of relying on this skill's parameter tuning. Goal is downstream statistical analysis of metabolites — this skill only measures universal parameters prior to feature extraction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs Paramounter's rank-based intensity sorting and zone-of-interest mechanism, which underlies its automatic measurement of universal LC-MS parameters (mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, instrumental shift) from raw metabolomics data in R. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c04758
skills.summary: Reconstructs Paramounter's rank-based intensity sorting and zone-of-interest mechanism, which underlies its automatic measurement of universal LC-MS parameters (mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, instrumental shift) from raw metabolomics data in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or peak list — rank sorting and zone-of-interest derivation apply to raw LC-MS intensity profiles only. Dereplication of features is not needed — mzdiff should be set to a negative value instead of relying on this skill's parameter tuning. Goal is downstream statistical analysis of metabolites — this skill only measures universal parameters prior to feature extraction.

skills.description: Use when you have XCMS-processed untargeted LC/MS feature data from paired unlabeled vs. labeled samples (e.g. CELL_Glc12 vs CELL_Glc13) and need to flag isotopically enriched features and their base-peak isotope assignments.
skills.name: lcms-isotope-label-detection
skills.search_text: lcms-isotope-label-detection Use when you have XCMS-processed untargeted LC/MS feature data from paired unlabeled vs. labeled samples (e.g. CELL_Glc12 vs CELL_Glc13) and need to flag isotopically enriched features and their base-peak isotope assignments. Input is raw vendor LC/MS data rather than an XCMS-processed feature/peak table — run XCMS peak picking, alignment and grouping first. You need isotope tracing of elements whose mass shift differs from 13C (L.atomM must be set to the labeled atom's exact mass; the example workflow is parameterized for 12C/13C). There are no biologically equivalent unlabeled control samples to compare against — geoRge's core logic compares isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Detect stable isotope labeling in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics by comparing isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples using geoRge on XCMS feature output, then assign monoisotopic base peaks to putatively labeled features (e.g. 13C glucose-labeled ARPE-19 cells, MTBLS213). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: Detect stable isotope labeling in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics by comparing isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples using geoRge on XCMS feature output, then assign monoisotopic base peaks to putatively labeled features (e.g. 13C glucose-labeled ARPE-19 cells, MTBLS213).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor LC/MS data rather than an XCMS-processed feature/peak table — run XCMS peak picking, alignment and grouping first. You need isotope tracing of elements whose mass shift differs from 13C (L.atomM must be set to the labeled atom's exact mass; the example workflow is parameterized for 12C/13C). There are no biologically equivalent unlabeled control samples to compare against — geoRge's core logic compares isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled samples.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS untargeted feature table (ids, rel.ids, mzs, RTs, Ints) has been feature-clustered and isotope peaks must be grouped into isotope-pattern units before IPA annotation.

skills.search_text: lcms-isotope-pattern-mapping Use when an LC-MS untargeted feature table (ids, rel.ids, mzs, RTs, Ints) has been feature-clustered and isotope peaks must be grouped into isotope-pattern units before IPA annotation. Input is an unclustered feature table — run clusterFeatures() first, since map_isotope_patterns() assumes already-clustered MS1 features. The goal is adduct enumeration or annotation — map_isotope_patterns() is only the first step; use compute_all_adducts() and MS1annotation()/MSMSannotation() instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Maps MS1 isotope peaks into per-metabolite isotope fingerprints using ipaPy2's map_isotope_patterns(), reducing the combinatorial burden of adduct/isotope enumeration downstream in the IPA Bayesian annotation pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad455
skills.summary: Maps MS1 isotope peaks into per-metabolite isotope fingerprints using ipaPy2's map_isotope_patterns(), reducing the combinatorial burden of adduct/isotope enumeration downstream in the IPA Bayesian annotation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unclustered feature table — run clusterFeatures() first, since map_isotope_patterns() assumes already-clustered MS1 features. The goal is adduct enumeration or annotation — map_isotope_patterns() is only the first step; use compute_all_adducts() and MS1annotation()/MSMSannotation() instead.

skills.description: Use when you have a table of significant features whose column headers encode AssayName_RTsec_m/z, and you need to group isotopologues and adducts into structural clusters across multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics data.
skills.name: lcms-isotopologue-pattern-detection
skills.search_text: lcms-isotopologue-pattern-detection Use when you have a table of significant features whose column headers encode AssayName_RTsec_m/z, and you need to group isotopologues and adducts into structural clusters across multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics data. The feature columns do not encode retention time and m/z in the AssayName_RTsec_m/z header format, so load_lcms() cannot parse the structural metadata Features have not yet been filtered by statistical significance (e.g. MB-VIP permutation p-values < 0.01), since the structural search is designed to operate on the selected significant-feature subset The data are not untargeted LC-MS metabolomics features with electrospray-ionisation adduct behaviour (the framework was tested on metabolomics phenotyping data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Detects isotopologue signatures among statistically significant LC-MS features by searching for 1.00335 Da mass differences between m/z values within 5-second retention-time windows, as implemented in MAMSI's MamsiStructSearch. This groups features that plausibly derive from the same metabolite and underpins subsequent adduct and structural-cluster merging. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01327
skills.summary: Detects isotopologue signatures among statistically significant LC-MS features by searching for 1.00335 Da mass differences between m/z values within 5-second retention-time windows, as implemented in MAMSI's MamsiStructSearch. This groups features that plausibly derive from the same metabolite and underpins subsequent adduct and structural-cluster merging.

skills.search_text: lcms-lipidomics-data-reprocessing Use when reprocessing publicly deposited LC-MS lipidomics raw files (Thermo .raw, e.g. MSV000091033 Nile rat plasma) to reproduce or re-annotate reported lipid feature counts and identifications. skills.description: Use when centroided mzML LC-MS files must be converted into per-sample mass tracks (full-RT intensity vectors per unique m/z) and aligned into a MassGrid before peak picking or annotation.
skills.name: lcms-mass-track-extraction-from-mzml
skills.search_text: lcms-mass-track-extraction-from-mzml Use when centroided mzML LC-MS files must be converted into per-sample mass tracks (full-RT intensity vectors per unique m/z) and aligned into a MassGrid before peak picking or annotation. Input data are low-resolution mass spectra — the paper states 'The software does not work with low resolution data' since 0.001 amu binning requires high mass resolution You already have a feature table or composite mass tracks — this skill covers the upstream track-extraction/alignment stage only Data are MS/MS spectra — 'MS/MS spectra are ignored by asari' in the default LC-MS workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extracts per-sample mass tracks (EICs of unique m/z values over the full RT range) from centroided mzML files by binning m/z into 0.001 amu bins and NN-clustering bins with seeds, then aligns the tracks into a MassGrid. This mass-first alignment is asari's core strategy for trackable feature detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Extracts per-sample mass tracks (EICs of unique m/z values over the full RT range) from centroided mzML files by binning m/z into 0.001 amu bins and NN-clustering bins with seeds, then aligns the tracks into a MassGrid. This mass-first alignment is asari's core strategy for trackable feature detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are low-resolution mass spectra — the paper states 'The software does not work with low resolution data' since 0.001 amu binning requires high mass resolution You already have a feature table or composite mass tracks — this skill covers the upstream track-extraction/alignment stage only Data are MS/MS spectra — 'MS/MS spectra are ignored by asari' in the default LC-MS workflow

skills.description: Use when a study has a list of predicted metabolites from a tool like BioTransformer and an LC-HRMS detection list from postincubation samples, and the goal is to compute the number (or percentage) of predictions that were actually observed.
skills.name: lcms-metabolite-detection-counting
skills.search_text: lcms-metabolite-detection-counting Use when a study has a list of predicted metabolites from a tool like BioTransformer and an LC-HRMS detection list from postincubation samples, and the goal is to compute the number (or percentage) of predictions that were actually observed. When the analysis goal is structural elucidation or annotation of novel (unpredicted) metabolites rather than counting predictions that were observed. When the input is already a summary table of detected versus predicted metabolites — this skill computes the counts and rate, not the summary itself. When the metabolites of interest come from extrahepatic compartments or enzymes not active in the liver S9 fraction, as these are expected to be absent from PharmMet DB. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Skill for quantifying how many of the in silico-predicted drug metabolites (e.g. BioTransformer 3.0 predictions) were experimentally detected by LC-HRMS after S9 fraction incubation, yielding counts and a detection-rate percentage such as 59,869 of 130,464 (45.89%). metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.dmd.2025.100183
skills.summary: Skill for quantifying how many of the in silico-predicted drug metabolites (e.g. BioTransformer 3.0 predictions) were experimentally detected by LC-HRMS after S9 fraction incubation, yielding counts and a detection-rate percentage such as 59,869 of 130,464 (45.89%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is structural elucidation or annotation of novel (unpredicted) metabolites rather than counting predictions that were observed. When the metabolites of interest come from extrahepatic compartments or enzymes not active in the liver S9 fraction, as these are expected to be absent from PharmMet DB.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS metabolomics feature table (XCMS/MZmine2/SIEVE/Skyline output) with pooled QC samples injected at fixed intervals shows injection-order signal drift and needs drift correction before statistical analysis.
skills.name: lcms-metabolomics-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: lcms-metabolomics-data-preprocessing Use when an LC-MS metabolomics feature table (XCMS/MZmine2/SIEVE/Skyline output) with pooled QC samples injected at fixed intervals shows injection-order signal drift and needs drift correction before statistical analysis. The dataset has no repeated pooled-QC injections in the run order — use shiftCor_dQC with Combat instead, which statTarget provides for QC-free datasets. Data are label-free proteomics SRM transition tables rather than metabolomics profiles, where the paper's proteomics workflow (Dataset 3, 174 transitions, 69 proteins) and its own QC spacing apply. Input is already a drift-corrected, quality-filtered feature table; only statAnalysis (glog/Pareto, imputation) is needed, not shiftCor. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Preprocesses and drift-corrects quantitative LC-MS metabolomics feature tables using the statTarget R package (shiftCor with QC-RFSC / QC-RLSC random forest or LOESS correction), turning raw peak-abundance files into precise, batch-corrected data ready for statistical analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Preprocesses and drift-corrects quantitative LC-MS metabolomics feature tables using the statTarget R package (shiftCor with QC-RFSC / QC-RLSC random forest or LOESS correction), turning raw peak-abundance files into precise, batch-corrected data ready for statistical analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no repeated pooled-QC injections in the run order — use shiftCor_dQC with Combat instead, which statTarget provides for QC-free datasets. Data are label-free proteomics SRM transition tables rather than metabolomics profiles, where the paper's proteomics workflow (Dataset 3, 174 transitions, 69 proteins) and its own QC spacing apply. Input is already a drift-corrected, quality-filtered feature table; only statAnalysis (glog/Pareto, imputation) is needed, not shiftCor.

skills.description: Use when a non-targeted LC-MS peak table stored as a notame MetaboSet still contains NA values in its exprs matrix after drift correction, quality flagging, and QC removal, and those gaps must be filled before statistical analysis.
skills.name: lcms-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: lcms-missing-value-imputation Use when a non-targeted LC-MS peak table stored as a notame MetaboSet still contains NA values in its exprs matrix after drift correction, quality flagging, and QC removal, and those gaps must be filled before statistical analysis. When QC samples are still present in the object — remove them with drop_qcs first, since imputation should be based on biological samples only. When the data is not preprocessed LC-MS peak data (e.g. raw instrument files) — notame's imputation operates on MetaboSet abundance matrices, not raw LC-MS files. When you intend to leave missing values as NA for methods that tolerate them — notame treats NA as the missing-value representation and imputation is a preprocessing step before its statistical tests. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Imputes remaining missing values (NAs) in a notame MetaboSet feature-abundance matrix using random forest imputation via missForest, after QC samples have been dropped and low-quality features flagged. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135
skills.summary: Imputes remaining missing values (NAs) in a notame MetaboSet feature-abundance matrix using random forest imputation via missForest, after QC samples have been dropped and low-quality features flagged.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When QC samples are still present in the object — remove them with drop_qcs first, since imputation should be based on biological samples only. When the data is not preprocessed LC-MS peak data (e.g. raw instrument files) — notame's imputation operates on MetaboSet abundance matrices, not raw LC-MS files. When you intend to leave missing values as NA for methods that tolerate them — notame treats NA as the missing-value representation and imputation is a preprocessing step before its statistical tests.

Input is raw mzML or other instrument output that has not yet been peak-picked and clustered (the 'clusterFeatures()' step) — pre-process with mzMatch/CAMERA-compatible pipelines first The dataset contains no MS2 spectra and you want fragmentation-evidence-based scores — MSMSannotation requires an MS2 database (e.g. DBMS2_test_pos.csv) and only adds accuracy when such data exist A customised compound database is inappropriate for the instrument setup and sample types — users are strongly advised to build their own ad-hoc database; off-the-shelf DB/IPA_MS1.csv may not match http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Statistically rigorous Bayesian annotation of LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics features via ipaPy2, integrating isotope patterns, adduct formation, biochemical relations, and tandem MS fragmentation to yield per-annotation prior and posterior probabilities. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad455
skills.summary: Statistically rigorous Bayesian annotation of LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics features via ipaPy2, integrating isotope patterns, adduct formation, biochemical relations, and tandem MS fragmentation to yield per-annotation prior and posterior probabilities.
