skills.description: Use when a metabolomics data matrix contains missing values that arise from a known limit of detection (MNAR below-LOD missingness) combined with random missingness, and downstream statistical testing requires accurate imputation.
skills.name: limit-of-detection-data-handling
skills.search_text: limit-of-detection-data-handling Use when a metabolomics data matrix contains missing values that arise from a known limit of detection (MNAR below-LOD missingness) combined with random missingness, and downstream statistical testing requires accurate imputation. The dataset has no limit of detection — the article reports that on the African Race data set there was no significant difference between any of the KNN imputation algorithms and mean imputation, so simple imputation suffices Metabolite distributions are strongly non-normal and cannot be made approximately normal by log transformation, since KNN-TN relies on the normality assumption for estimating the truncated mean and standard deviation Missingness is extremely high or samples are very small — estimation of the truncated normal mean and variance is unstable in these settings, giving higher RMSE variability than simpler methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Handles metabolomics missing values caused by a limit of detection (LOD) by treating the observed data as a left-truncated normal distribution, estimating truncated means/SDs via maximum likelihood, and imputing with a distribution-based KNN (KNN-TN) instead of substituting minimum/zero/mean values. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: Handles metabolomics missing values caused by a limit of detection (LOD) by treating the observed data as a left-truncated normal distribution, estimating truncated means/SDs via maximum likelihood, and imputing with a distribution-based KNN (KNN-TN) instead of substituting minimum/zero/mean values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no limit of detection — the article reports that on the African Race data set there was no significant difference between any of the KNN imputation algorithms and mean imputation, so simple imputation suffices Metabolite distributions are strongly non-normal and cannot be made approximately normal by log transformation, since KNN-TN relies on the normality assumption for estimating the truncated mean and standard deviation Missingness is extremely high or samples are very small — estimation of the truncated normal mean and variance is unstable in these settings, giving higher RMSE variability than simpler methods

skills.description: Use when a wide-format feature intensity table includes blank samples in its companion design file and features must be flagged/filtered against a blank-derived limit of detection before downstream statistics.
skills.name: limit-of-detection-estimation
skills.search_text: limit-of-detection-estimation Use when a wide-format feature intensity table includes blank samples in its companion design file and features must be flagged/filtered against a blank-derived limit of detection before downstream statistics. The dataset contains no blank samples in the design file, so no blank-based limit of detection can be computed; a threshold-based criterion such as the Threshold Based Flags tool (features below a user-specified threshold in >50% of samples within a group) is the alternative. The feature table has already been blank-filtered and the goal is downstream statistical analysis (ANOVA, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis, PLS-DA) or visualization (PCA, hierarchical cluster heatmap). The goal is feature annotation or peak picking rather than post-acquisition quality control; SECIMTools complements tools like Galaxy-M (peak-picking/feature identification) and Workflow4Metabolomics (feature annotation). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimates a per-feature limit of detection (limit of blank) from blank-sample intensities, as implemented in SECIMTools' Blank Feature Filtering (BFF) tool, and uses it to flag and remove metabolomic features at or below blank-level signal. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Estimates a per-feature limit of detection (limit of blank) from blank-sample intensities, as implemented in SECIMTools' Blank Feature Filtering (BFF) tool, and uses it to flag and remove metabolomic features at or below blank-level signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no blank samples in the design file, so no blank-based limit of detection can be computed; a threshold-based criterion such as the Threshold Based Flags tool (features below a user-specified threshold in >50% of samples within a group) is the alternative. The feature table has already been blank-filtered and the goal is downstream statistical analysis (ANOVA, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis, PLS-DA) or visualization (PCA, hierarchical cluster heatmap). The goal is feature annotation or peak picking rather than post-acquisition quality control; SECIMTools complements tools like Galaxy-M (peak-picking/feature identification) and Workflow4Metabolomics (feature annotation).

skills.description: Use when reproducing single-dataset imputation comparisons (e.g., Figure 6-style plots) where missing values are partly MNAR below a detection limit and below-LOD imputation accuracy must be inspected visually.
skills.name: limit-of-detection-region-shading
skills.search_text: limit-of-detection-region-shading Use when reproducing single-dataset imputation comparisons (e.g., Figure 6-style plots) where missing values are partly MNAR below a detection limit and below-LOD imputation accuracy must be inspected visually. The dataset has purely MAR/MCAR missingness with no detection limit, so there is no below-LOD region to shade and no MNAR regime to inspect The goal is a quantitative multi-dataset comparison (RMSE or MLCI tables) rather than visual inspection of imputations for a single dataset Missing values are substituted by simple constant imputation (minimum value, zero, metabolite mean) where no per-entry imputed values exist to overlay against the LOD http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A visualization skill from Shah et al. (2017, BMC Bioinformatics) that shades the below-limit-of-detection region in light red on an imputation-comparison plot, so that MNAR imputed values from KNN-TN, KNN-CR, and KNN-EU can be visually inspected against the LOD threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: A visualization skill from Shah et al. (2017, BMC Bioinformatics) that shades the below-limit-of-detection region in light red on an imputation-comparison plot, so that MNAR imputed values from KNN-TN, KNN-CR, and KNN-EU can be visually inspected against the LOD threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has purely MAR/MCAR missingness with no detection limit, so there is no below-LOD region to shade and no MNAR regime to inspect The goal is a quantitative multi-dataset comparison (RMSE or MLCI tables) rather than visual inspection of imputations for a single dataset Missing values are substituted by simple constant imputation (minimum value, zero, metabolite mean) where no per-entry imputed values exist to overlay against the LOD

skills.description: Use when comparing a pathway/hyperlink prediction model against a baseline (e.g. CHESHIRE) under artificially limited labeled-pathway conditions on metabolite correlation networks, to mimic organisms with sparse pathway knowledge.
skills.name: limited-labeled-pathway-evaluation
skills.search_text: limited-labeled-pathway-evaluation Use when comparing a pathway/hyperlink prediction model against a baseline (e.g. CHESHIRE) under artificially limited labeled-pathway conditions on metabolite correlation networks, to mimic organisms with sparse pathway knowledge. When labeled pathways are abundant and the goal is standard model selection — the paper's main evaluation uses 10-fold cross-validation instead of the limited-label holdout When the aim is threshold tuning or score computation for NetAurHPD itself (that is handled by Youden's J statistic in the NetAurHPD pipeline, not by the CHESHIRE baseline protocol) When the input network is not a metabolite correlation network (e.g. the Enron or NDC hyperlink datasets used in the NetAurHPD repository examples), since the pathway labels and central-pathway metrics are tomato-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 A benchmarking protocol that stresses hyperlink/pathway prediction models by holding out pathways around minimally-annotated metabolites, then compares a baseline (CHESHIRE) against NetAurHPD per year and per training fraction on tomato pericarp metabolite correlation networks. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that stresses hyperlink/pathway prediction models by holding out pathways around minimally-annotated metabolites, then compares a baseline (CHESHIRE) against NetAurHPD per year and per training fraction on tomato pericarp metabolite correlation networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When labeled pathways are abundant and the goal is standard model selection — the paper's main evaluation uses 10-fold cross-validation instead of the limited-label holdout When the aim is threshold tuning or score computation for NetAurHPD itself (that is handled by Youden's J statistic in the NetAurHPD pipeline, not by the CHESHIRE baseline protocol) When the input network is not a metabolite correlation network (e.g. the Enron or NDC hyperlink datasets used in the NetAurHPD repository examples), since the pathway labels and central-pathway metrics are tomato-specific

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics/proteomics feature table (e.g. ST000284) has study covariates (batch, sex, age, etc.) that may confound group comparisons, and you need covariate-adjusted differential abundance results to compare against unadjusted t-test/ANOVA calls.
skills.name: limma-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: limma-differential-abundance-analysis Use when a metabolomics/proteomics feature table (e.g. ST000284) has study covariates (batch, sex, age, etc.) that may confound group comparisons, and you need covariate-adjusted differential abundance results to compare against unadjusted t-test/ANOVA calls. The design has no meaningful covariates beyond the group variable — a plain t-test/ANOVA already captures the model, and adding an aliased covariate term is redundant The data have not passed through preprocessing (missing-value imputation, e.g. 20% per-group feature removal threshold, normalization) — the linear models assume a cleaned, imputed feature table The covariate is perfectly confounded with the group label, making the design matrix rank-deficient http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Fit covariate-adjusted linear models (limma/ANCOVA) for each feature of a metabolomics or proteomics feature table, as an alternative to plain t-test/ANOVA group comparisons, and compare the resulting significant feature sets. In the POMAShiny/POMA context, this tests whether covariate adjustment changes which features are called significant. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009148
skills.summary: Fit covariate-adjusted linear models (limma/ANCOVA) for each feature of a metabolomics or proteomics feature table, as an alternative to plain t-test/ANOVA group comparisons, and compare the resulting significant feature sets. In the POMAShiny/POMA context, this tests whether covariate adjustment changes which features are called significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The design has no meaningful covariates beyond the group variable — a plain t-test/ANOVA already captures the model, and adding an aliased covariate term is redundant The data have not passed through preprocessing (missing-value imputation, e.g. 20% per-group feature removal threshold, normalization) — the linear models assume a cleaned, imputed feature table The covariate is perfectly confounded with the group label, making the design matrix rank-deficient

skills.description: Use when a normalized MultiABLER feature table plus sample metadata are available and the goal is group-level differential expression of lipids or metabolites, such as genotype contrasts in mouse arterial tissue.
skills.name: limma-differential-abundance-modeling
skills.search_text: limma-differential-abundance-modeling Use when a normalized MultiABLER feature table plus sample metadata are available and the goal is group-level differential expression of lipids or metabolites, such as genotype contrasts in mouse arterial tissue. The input has not been processed by tbManipulate and normalized with normEigenMS (EigenMS) — MultiABLER does not implement kNN imputation, mean normalization, or quantile normalization, so running limma on un-normalized tables violates the reference workflow. The data are proteomic — MultiABLER currently does not provide functions to analyze proteomic data, and proteomic integration is planned only for future development. The analysis goal is multivariate integration (sPLS or rCCA) rather than univariate group-contrast differential expression testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Fit a limma linear model on MultiABLER-processed metabolite/lipid feature tables to call differentially expressed features between biological groups (e.g. Apoe+/+ vs Apoe−/− mice) at adjusted p < 0.05. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106881
skills.summary: Fit a limma linear model on MultiABLER-processed metabolite/lipid feature tables to call differentially expressed features between biological groups (e.g. Apoe+/+ vs Apoe−/− mice) at adjusted p < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input has not been processed by tbManipulate and normalized with normEigenMS (EigenMS) — MultiABLER does not implement kNN imputation, mean normalization, or quantile normalization, so running limma on un-normalized tables violates the reference workflow. The data are proteomic — MultiABLER currently does not provide functions to analyze proteomic data, and proteomic integration is planned only for future development. The analysis goal is multivariate integration (sPLS or rCCA) rather than univariate group-contrast differential expression testing.

skills.description: Use when a normalised metabolite abundance matrix (metabolites × samples) is paired with a sample-level binary phenotype such as hypertension status, and per-metabolite differential-abundance hits with adjusted p-values are required.
skills.name: limma-linear-model-fitting
skills.search_text: limma-linear-model-fitting Use when a normalised metabolite abundance matrix (metabolites × samples) is paired with a sample-level binary phenotype such as hypertension status, and per-metabolite differential-abundance hits with adjusted p-values are required. Input is raw or un-normalised metabolite abundance data — the hypertension associations were recoverable only from hRUV-normalised data, so normalise first (e.g. with the hRUV package) The analysis goal is batch/drift correction itself rather than downstream phenotype testing — use the hRUV hierarchical normalisation workflow instead of a limma model The input has missing values and no completed imputation/normalisation step has been applied, since the upstream hRUV algorithm expects data without missing values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential-abundance testing of metabolomics data by fitting a per-metabolite limma linear model (with empirical Bayes moderation and Benjamini-Hochberg correction) against a clinical covariate such as hypertension status, applied to hRUV-normalised metabolite abundance matrices from large-scale plasma studies. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Differential-abundance testing of metabolomics data by fitting a per-metabolite limma linear model (with empirical Bayes moderation and Benjamini-Hochberg correction) against a clinical covariate such as hypertension status, applied to hRUV-normalised metabolite abundance matrices from large-scale plasma studies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or un-normalised metabolite abundance data — the hypertension associations were recoverable only from hRUV-normalised data, so normalise first (e.g. with the hRUV package) The analysis goal is batch/drift correction itself rather than downstream phenotype testing — use the hRUV hierarchical normalisation workflow instead of a limma model The input has missing values and no completed imputation/normalisation step has been applied, since the upstream hRUV algorithm expects data without missing values

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (samples × features, e.g. the imputed cancerCell demo table from MetaboReport) shows sample-to-sample variation that should be reduced by per-sample scaling, and a simple mean- or median-intensity baseline is acceptable.
skills.name: linear-baseline-scaling-mean-median
skills.search_text: linear-baseline-scaling-mean-median Use when a metabolomics feature table (samples × features, e.g. the imputed cancerCell demo table from MetaboReport) shows sample-to-sample variation that should be reduced by per-sample scaling, and a simple mean- or median-intensity baseline is acceptable. The table is raw and not yet imputed — MetaboReport applies normalization during preprocessing after imputation A distribution-based correction is needed rather than a per-sample scalar scaling (use quantile or probabilistic quotient normalization instead) Normalization should be driven by specific reference signals (use internal standard-based normalization instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A sample-wise normalization method in MetaboReport's preprocessing suite that reduces sample-to-sample variation by linearly scaling each sample's feature intensities against a per-sample baseline computed as either the mean or the median intensity across all features in that sample. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: A sample-wise normalization method in MetaboReport's preprocessing suite that reduces sample-to-sample variation by linearly scaling each sample's feature intensities against a per-sample baseline computed as either the mean or the median intensity across all features in that sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The table is raw and not yet imputed — MetaboReport applies normalization during preprocessing after imputation A distribution-based correction is needed rather than a per-sample scalar scaling (use quantile or probabilistic quotient normalization instead) Normalization should be driven by specific reference signals (use internal standard-based normalization instead)

skills.description: Use when SWATH-MS-based untargeted metabolomics data contain coeluted, unresolved chromatographic peaks of fragment ions in multiplexed MS/MS spectra that must be separated into metabolite-specific MS2 spectra.
skills.name: linear-combination-decomposition-of-fragment-ion-peaks
skills.search_text: linear-combination-decomposition-of-fragment-ion-peaks Use when SWATH-MS-based untargeted metabolomics data contain coeluted, unresolved chromatographic peaks of fragment ions in multiplexed MS/MS spectra that must be separated into metabolite-specific MS2 spectra. Input MS2 spectra are already resolved by data-dependent acquisition (DDA), so no multiplexed deconvolution is needed — direct DDA spectra comparison suffices. The task is annotating already-deconvolved MS2 spectra, which is the downstream job of MetDNA or Sirius rather than this skill. Input is non-SWATH metabolomics data outside the scope of tools developed 'to process SWATH-MS based data for metabolomics'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Deconvolves multiplexed SWATH-MS MS/MS spectra by selecting multiple model chromatographic peaks that model coeluted, unresolved fragment-ion peaks, then decomposing each multiplexed spectrum as a linear combination of those model peaks to recover metabolite-specific MS2 spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b02655
skills.summary: Deconvolves multiplexed SWATH-MS MS/MS spectra by selecting multiple model chromatographic peaks that model coeluted, unresolved fragment-ion peaks, then decomposing each multiplexed spectrum as a linear combination of those model peaks to recover metabolite-specific MS2 spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input MS2 spectra are already resolved by data-dependent acquisition (DDA), so no multiplexed deconvolution is needed — direct DDA spectra comparison suffices. The task is annotating already-deconvolved MS2 spectra, which is the downstream job of MetDNA or Sirius rather than this skill. Input is non-SWATH metabolomics data outside the scope of tools developed 'to process SWATH-MS based data for metabolomics'.

skills.description: Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) contains single-cell metabolite intensities plus fluorescence channels for two or more morphologically distinguishable cell types, and the goal is to test whether metabolic profiles alone predict cell type.
skills.name: linear-discriminant-analysis-classification
skills.search_text: linear-discriminant-analysis-classification Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) contains single-cell metabolite intensities plus fluorescence channels for two or more morphologically distinguishable cell types, and the goal is to test whether metabolic profiles alone predict cell type. Input is raw MALDI-imaging data (.RAW/.imzML/.ibd microscopy tiles) that has not yet been processed by SpaceM into a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix — run the SpaceM pipeline first. Cells cannot be assigned ground-truth labels by an independent modality (e.g. no fluorescence channels or marker decision boundary), making supervised classification unverifiable. Classes are defined by the same features used for prediction, which would inflate accuracy and not validate single-cell metabolic resolution. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Classify cell types in co-culture solely from SpaceM single-cell metabolic profiles using Linear Discriminant Analysis on metabolite intensity columns of the spatio-molecular matrix, validating single-cell resolution of the method. In the SpaceM HeLa/NIH3T3 benchmark this reached 91.3% accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Classify cell types in co-culture solely from SpaceM single-cell metabolic profiles using Linear Discriminant Analysis on metabolite intensity columns of the spatio-molecular matrix, validating single-cell resolution of the method. In the SpaceM HeLa/NIH3T3 benchmark this reached 91.3% accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MALDI-imaging data (.RAW/.imzML/.ibd microscopy tiles) that has not yet been processed by SpaceM into a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix — run the SpaceM pipeline first. Cells cannot be assigned ground-truth labels by an independent modality (e.g. no fluorescence channels or marker decision boundary), making supervised classification unverifiable. Classes are defined by the same features used for prediction, which would inflate accuracy and not validate single-cell metabolic resolution.

skills.description: Use when processing lipidomics peak tables (e.g., LipiDex 2 Peak Finder/Spectral Searcher results) where quantitation confidence must be validated against a dilution-series-derived linear dynamic range before downstream statistics.
skills.name: linear-dynamic-range-validation
skills.search_text: linear-dynamic-range-validation Use when processing lipidomics peak tables (e.g., LipiDex 2 Peak Finder/Spectral Searcher results) where quantitation confidence must be validated against a dilution-series-derived linear dynamic range before downstream statistics. Input is already a fully QC-filtered feature table that has passed Degreaser's 7 filtering criteria Analysis uses raw MS data without peak tables or spectral matches from the LipiDex 2 pipeline — Degreaser takes in results from the peak identification and spectral matching steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A QC filter within the LipiDex 2 Degreaser module that models linear dynamic range from a dilution series and removes lipid quantitations falling outside the established linear range, improving identification-rate confidence in LC-MS lipidomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: A QC filter within the LipiDex 2 Degreaser module that models linear dynamic range from a dilution series and removes lipid quantitations falling outside the established linear range, improving identification-rate confidence in LC-MS lipidomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fully QC-filtered feature table that has passed Degreaser's 7 filtering criteria Analysis uses raw MS data without peak tables or spectral matches from the LipiDex 2 pipeline — Degreaser takes in results from the peak identification and spectral matching steps

skills.description: Use when paired or repeated clinical metabolomics samples (e.g. VAT/SAT tissue pairs from 59 CRC patients) contain subject-specific variation that confounds metabolite signals and you need to readjust per-metabolite abundances before PCA or PLS-DA.
skills.name: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting
skills.search_text: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting Use when paired or repeated clinical metabolomics samples (e.g. VAT/SAT tissue pairs from 59 CRC patients) contain subject-specific variation that confounds metabolite signals and you need to readjust per-metabolite abundances before PCA or PLS-DA. The data are untransformed or not pre-processed — signals must already be pre-processed (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) and log2-transformed before LMM fitting Samples lack patient metadata (no fixed-effect covariates such as Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) and have no repeated measures or patient Id for a random intercept The goal is classification-model evaluation rather than signal readjustment — the article evaluates predictions separately with caret under repeated 4-fold cross validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits a per-metabolite linear mixed-effects model (via lmm2met, built on lme4) in which patient metadata (e.g. Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) are fixed effects and a patient random intercept '(1|Id)' captures subject-specific variation, producing a readjusted metabolite matrix with reduced per-metabolite variance prior to multivariate analyses. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: Fits a per-metabolite linear mixed-effects model (via lmm2met, built on lme4) in which patient metadata (e.g. Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) are fixed effects and a patient random intercept '(1|Id)' captures subject-specific variation, producing a readjusted metabolite matrix with reduced per-metabolite variance prior to multivariate analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are untransformed or not pre-processed — signals must already be pre-processed (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) and log2-transformed before LMM fitting Samples lack patient metadata (no fixed-effect covariates such as Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) and have no repeated measures or patient Id for a random intercept The goal is classification-model evaluation rather than signal readjustment — the article evaluates predictions separately with caret under repeated 4-fold cross validation

skills.description: Use when NMR metabolomics concentrations are available for blood samples exposed to varying pre-/postcentrifugation delays across tube types and you must quantify how fast each metabolite changes (time to 20% concentration change).
skills.name: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting-for-metabolite-stability
skills.search_text: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting-for-metabolite-stability Use when NMR metabolomics concentrations are available for blood samples exposed to varying pre-/postcentrifugation delays across tube types and you must quantify how fast each metabolite changes (time to 20% concentration change). The goal is a pass/fail quality flag for an uploaded sample cohort — use the PRIMA Panel performance-report workflow instead of refitting models Samples were not collected in peripheral-blood tubes (plasma/serum) with recorded pre-/postcentrifugation delays, so delay effects cannot be modeled No repeated measures per donor exist, so a random-intercept structure (donor) is not identifiable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fits linear mixed models to NMR-quantified metabolite concentrations measured after controlled pre- and postcentrifugation delays, with donor as random intercept and cell count as random slope, to derive each parameter's 20% 'stability time point' per tube type (EDTA plasma, LiHep plasma, serum). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c04938
skills.summary: Fits linear mixed models to NMR-quantified metabolite concentrations measured after controlled pre- and postcentrifugation delays, with donor as random intercept and cell count as random slope, to derive each parameter's 20% 'stability time point' per tube type (EDTA plasma, LiHep plasma, serum).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a pass/fail quality flag for an uploaded sample cohort — use the PRIMA Panel performance-report workflow instead of refitting models Samples were not collected in peripheral-blood tubes (plasma/serum) with recorded pre-/postcentrifugation delays, so delay effects cannot be modeled No repeated measures per donor exist, so a random-intercept structure (donor) is not identifiable

skills.description: Use when protein-level abundance matrices from twin/pair-related or longitudinally repeated DIA (SWATH) measurements must be decomposed into heritable, environmental, and longitudinal variance components.
skills.name: linear-mixed-effects-modeling-of-protein-abundances
skills.search_text: linear-mixed-effects-modeling-of-protein-abundances Use when protein-level abundance matrices from twin/pair-related or longitudinally repeated DIA (SWATH) measurements must be decomposed into heritable, environmental, and longitudinal variance components. Input is already a variance-components table or the per-protein abundance matrix has not been produced from OpenSWATH targeted analysis of the DIA maps The data are not twin/pair-related or longitudinally repeated measurements, so heritable vs environmental vs longitudinal components cannot be distinguished Absolute protein abundance quantification is the goal rather than decomposition of variance in already-quantified abundances http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fits a per-protein linear mixed-effects model to SWATH-MS plasma protein abundances, partitioning observed variance into heritable (shared between co-twins), common/individual environmental, and longitudinal (time) components, as demonstrated in the Liu et al. twin-cohort analysis with OpenMS/OpenSWATH-derived quantities. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nmeth.3959
skills.summary: Fits a per-protein linear mixed-effects model to SWATH-MS plasma protein abundances, partitioning observed variance into heritable (shared between co-twins), common/individual environmental, and longitudinal (time) components, as demonstrated in the Liu et al. twin-cohort analysis with OpenMS/OpenSWATH-derived quantities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a variance-components table or the per-protein abundance matrix has not been produced from OpenSWATH targeted analysis of the DIA maps The data are not twin/pair-related or longitudinally repeated measurements, so heritable vs environmental vs longitudinal components cannot be distinguished Absolute protein abundance quantification is the goal rather than decomposition of variance in already-quantified abundances

skills.description: Use when NMR-quantified plasma/serum metabolite concentrations are available at multiple controlled pre- or postcentrifugation delay time points (e.g. 2, 4, 6, 8 h) and per-parameter concentration changes must be predicted or a stability time point (20% change) must be located.
skills.name: linear-mixed-model-prediction
skills.search_text: linear-mixed-model-prediction Use when NMR-quantified plasma/serum metabolite concentrations are available at multiple controlled pre- or postcentrifugation delay time points (e.g. 2, 4, 6, 8 h) and per-parameter concentration changes must be predicted or a stability time point (20% change) must be located. The input is not peripheral-blood plasma/serum NMR data with known collection, centrifugation, and freezing timestamps — the models were trained only on this preanalytical design. The metabolite of interest does not follow the linear response captured by the models, e.g. glucose in EDTA and LiHep plasma, which showed unexpectedly large MPE at later (6 and 8 h) time points. http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Fits and applies linear mixed models to NMR-quantified metabolite concentrations measured across controlled pre- and postcentrifugation delays, so that concentration changes for each metabolic parameter can be predicted and quantified at arbitrary processing times. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c04938
skills.summary: Fits and applies linear mixed models to NMR-quantified metabolite concentrations measured across controlled pre- and postcentrifugation delays, so that concentration changes for each metabolic parameter can be predicted and quantified at arbitrary processing times.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not peripheral-blood plasma/serum NMR data with known collection, centrifugation, and freezing timestamps — the models were trained only on this preanalytical design. skills.description: Use when candidate peak boundaries from a sliding-window TIC/chromatogram peak detection must be sharpened before downstream parameter estimation, and per-peak scan bounds with an explicit fit-quality criterion (R2 >= 0.8) are needed.
skills.name: linear-model-bound-fitting
skills.search_text: linear-model-bound-fitting Use when candidate peak boundaries from a sliding-window TIC/chromatogram peak detection must be sharpened before downstream parameter estimation, and per-peak scan bounds with an explicit fit-quality criterion (R2 >= 0.8) are needed. Input is already a processed feature table — boundary refinement operates on raw chromatograms, not feature tables The goal is optimizing the non-automatable Group difference parameter or the remaining centWave parameters via parameter sweeping — those are separate later stages of AutoTuner Peak detection quality is sufficient from the sliding-window stage alone and user inspection has already accepted the coarse bounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Refines the retention-time/scan boundaries of peaks detected by a sliding-window analysis (e.g., AutoTuner's ThresholdingAlgo over a total ion chromatogram) by iteratively fitting a linear model to the first and last three points bounding each candidate peak, expanding the ending bound by one scan until the fit's R2 reaches 0.8 and the bound is a local maximum. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/812370
skills.summary: Refines the retention-time/scan boundaries of peaks detected by a sliding-window analysis (e.g., AutoTuner's ThresholdingAlgo over a total ion chromatogram) by iteratively fitting a linear model to the first and last three points bounding each candidate peak, expanding the ending bound by one scan until the fit's R2 reaches 0.8 and the bound is a local maximum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table — boundary refinement operates on raw chromatograms, not feature tables The goal is optimizing the non-automatable Group difference parameter or the remaining centWave parameters via parameter sweeping — those are separate later stages of AutoTuner Peak detection quality is sufficient from the sliding-window stage alone and user inspection has already accepted the coarse bounds

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics dataset has grouped samples plus a potential confounding clinical variable (e.g. Race, batch, age) and you need a covariate-adjusted group contrast rather than a plain two-group comparison.

skills.search_text: linear-model-design-matrix-specification Use when a lipidomics dataset has grouped samples plus a potential confounding clinical variable (e.g. Race, batch, age) and you need a covariate-adjusted group contrast rather than a plain two-group comparison. When there is no confounding variable and a simple two-group contrast suffices — the unadjusted comparison is appropriate and the design matrix adds a covariate term unnecessarily When the clinical variables of interest have not been added to the object via add_sample_annotation — de_design cannot build the design matrix from unloaded annotations When the analysis target is lipid set enrichment (LSEA) or multivariate ordination (PCA/OPLS-DA) rather than a linear-model contrast http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Specify covariate-adjusted linear models for lipidomics differential analysis using lipidr's de_design, which builds design matrices over loaded clinical variables so a coefficient of interest (e.g. SampleTypeCancer) is estimated while controlling for confounders such as Race, with statistical power borrowed from the limma framework. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00082
skills.summary: Specify covariate-adjusted linear models for lipidomics differential analysis using lipidr's de_design, which builds design matrices over loaded clinical variables so a coefficient of interest (e.g. SampleTypeCancer) is estimated while controlling for confounders such as Race, with statistical power borrowed from the limma framework.

skills.description: Use when a series of Thermo .raw system-suitability or QC files (e.g. the ~12 h longitudinal FGCZ Orbitrap series) contains an iRT peptide mix (Biognosys) and you need to verify that retention times remain highly linear and comparable across instruments and time.
skills.name: linear-model-diagnostic-assessment
skills.search_text: linear-model-diagnostic-assessment Use when a series of Thermo .raw system-suitability or QC files (e.g. the ~12 h longitudinal FGCZ Orbitrap series) contains an iRT peptide mix (Biognosys) and you need to verify that retention times remain highly linear and comparable across instruments and time. The input data are already aggregated/feature tables (e.g. MaxQuant or Skyline outputs) rather than raw .raw files with iRT spectra — the workflow here reads raw vendor files via rawrr The raw files do not contain the iRT peptide mix or MS2 spectra of the iRT peptides, so no observed-vs-indexed RT pairs can be regressed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits a per-file linear regression of observed iRT peptide retention times against indexed iRT values and inspects slope, intercept, and R squared to judge LC-RT linearity and instrument stability across Thermo Orbitrap system suitability runs. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.10.30.362533
skills.summary: Fits a per-file linear regression of observed iRT peptide retention times against indexed iRT values and inspects slope, intercept, and R squared to judge LC-RT linearity and instrument stability across Thermo Orbitrap system suitability runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are already aggregated/feature tables (e.g. MaxQuant or Skyline outputs) rather than raw .raw files with iRT spectra — the workflow here reads raw vendor files via rawrr The raw files do not contain the iRT peptide mix or MS2 spectra of the iRT peptides, so no observed-vs-indexed RT pairs can be regressed

skills.description: Use when a peak-value feature matrix (samples x features) from 1D NMR spectra must be tested for features associated with a continuous dose, ordinal diet level, or multi-group factor, with multiple-testing correction.
skills.name: linear-model-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: linear-model-differential-abundance-analysis Use when a peak-value feature matrix (samples x features) from 1D NMR spectra must be tested for features associated with a continuous dose, ordinal diet level, or multi-group factor, with multiple-testing correction. Input is already a processed feature table from a different tool whose peak lists are intended for MetaboAnalyst or muma-R rather than the speaq 2.0 statistical tools The goal is raw spectra alignment or quantitation (speaq <= 1.2.3 CluPA/BW-ratio functionality) rather than peak-based differential analysis The spectra are severely shifted and only an alignment step (not peak-based modeling) is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Fit a linear model of each peak-value feature against a continuous or multi-group design variable (e.g., increasing onion diet percentage) using the speaq 2.0 feature matrix, and call significant peaks after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. Applied in the paper to a 31-sample x 677-feature urine 1D NMR matrix, yielding 9 significant peaks queryable against HMDB. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Fit a linear model of each peak-value feature against a continuous or multi-group design variable (e.g., increasing onion diet percentage) using the speaq 2.0 feature matrix, and call significant peaks after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. Applied in the paper to a 31-sample x 677-feature urine 1D NMR matrix, yielding 9 significant peaks queryable against HMDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table from a different tool whose peak lists are intended for MetaboAnalyst or muma-R rather than the speaq 2.0 statistical tools The goal is raw spectra alignment or quantitation (speaq <= 1.2.3 CluPA/BW-ratio functionality) rather than peak-based differential analysis The spectra are severely shifted and only an alignment step (not peak-based modeling) is required

skills.description: Use when you have a peak-based feature/sample matrix from speaq 2.0 (e.g. from BuildFeatureMatrix on Winedata) plus class metadata and need a per-feature significance test between two groups.
skills.name: linear-model-group-comparison
skills.search_text: linear-model-group-comparison Use when you have a peak-based feature/sample matrix from speaq 2.0 (e.g. from BuildFeatureMatrix on Winedata) plus class metadata and need a per-feature significance test between two groups. The input is already a list of significant features or a finished differential-analysis results table rather than a feature matrix to be tested The comparison involves more than the two designated groups without adjusting the linear model design (though speaq 2.0's differential analysis does also support more than 2 groups) The data are raw 1D spectra that have not been peak-picked, grouped and filled into a feature matrix — run the speaq 2.0 peak-based workflow first http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Per-feature univariate differential analysis of a speaq 2.0-derived NMR feature matrix using linear models on a class factor, with Bonferroni correction of p-values, to identify features that significantly discriminate between groups (e.g. 33 significant red-vs-white wine features). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Per-feature univariate differential analysis of a speaq 2.0-derived NMR feature matrix using linear models on a class factor, with Bonferroni correction of p-values, to identify features that significantly discriminate between groups (e.g. 33 significant red-vs-white wine features).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a list of significant features or a finished differential-analysis results table rather than a feature matrix to be tested The comparison involves more than the two designated groups without adjusting the linear model design (though speaq 2.0's differential analysis does also support more than 2 groups) The data are raw 1D spectra that have not been peak-picked, grouped and filled into a feature matrix — run the speaq 2.0 peak-based workflow first

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table spans several dose levels of a compound (e.g. four etomoxir doses on BT549 cells) and the goal is fitted dose-response curves plus per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values for risk assessment.
skills.name: linear-nonlinear-model-comparison
skills.search_text: linear-nonlinear-model-comparison Use when a metabolomics feature table spans several dose levels of a compound (e.g. four etomoxir doses on BT549 cells) and the goal is fitted dose-response curves plus per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values for risk assessment. The study has only two conditions or a single dose with control — use standard differential/uni-variate statistical analysis instead of dose-response fitting Input is still raw LC-MS spectra — run the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 Spectra Processing module (MS1/MS2 peak detection, asari algorithm) first to obtain a feature table The aim is risk assessment of chemical exposures from animal-model data at dose levels incompatible with the module's in vitro-cell-line-style design (the case study is demonstrated on four etomoxir doses in BT549 cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits metabolomics features measured across multiple dose levels to both linear and non-linear dose-response models and derives per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values, as implemented in the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 Dose-Response Analysis module and demonstrated on the published etomoxir BT549 breast cancer cell dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Fits metabolomics features measured across multiple dose levels to both linear and non-linear dose-response models and derives per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values, as implemented in the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 Dose-Response Analysis module and demonstrated on the published etomoxir BT549 breast cancer cell dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study has only two conditions or a single dose with control — use standard differential/uni-variate statistical analysis instead of dose-response fitting Input is still raw LC-MS spectra — run the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 Spectra Processing module (MS1/MS2 peak detection, asari algorithm) first to obtain a feature table The aim is risk assessment of chemical exposures from animal-model data at dose levels incompatible with the module's in vitro-cell-line-style design (the case study is demonstrated on four etomoxir doses in BT549 cells)

skills.description: Use when a target HSQC NMR spectrum must be reconstructed as a union of library compound spectra scaled by concentration factors, with joint capacity constraints preventing over-assignment of shared peaks.
skills.name: linear-program-formulation-with-capacity-constraints
skills.search_text: linear-program-formulation-with-capacity-constraints Use when a target HSQC NMR spectrum must be reconstructed as a union of library compound spectra scaled by concentration factors, with joint capacity constraints preventing over-assignment of shared peaks. When the mixture contains compounds whose spectral peak pattern is not represented in the library — the method cannot complete the reconstruction for unknown constituents. When spectra have strong peak shifts between library and target: the method is explicitly noted as sensitive toward peak shifts, which the local assignment radius only partially compensates. When the input is already a fully deconvolved list of compound concentrations — the LP reconstruction would be redundant. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Formulate NMR mixture reconstruction as a minimum-cost-flow linear program over a network of compound hub nodes, compound-peak nodes, capacity-limited mixture nodes, and an absorption sink, then solve it with the HiGHS solver via the SciPy interface. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01652
skills.summary: Formulate NMR mixture reconstruction as a minimum-cost-flow linear program over a network of compound hub nodes, compound-peak nodes, capacity-limited mixture nodes, and an absorption sink, then solve it with the HiGHS solver via the SciPy interface.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the mixture contains compounds whose spectral peak pattern is not represented in the library — the method cannot complete the reconstruction for unknown constituents. When spectra have strong peak shifts between library and target: the method is explicitly noted as sensitive toward peak shifts, which the local assignment radius only partially compensates. When the input is already a fully deconvolved list of compound concentrations — the LP reconstruction would be redundant.

skills.description: Use when you have a concentration-series calibration data set (e.g., narcotics standards) plus a test sample of unknown concentration, and need fitted linear/quadratic calibration curves with adjusted R2 and per-analyte relative errors.
skills.name: linear-quadratic-regression-model-fitting
skills.search_text: linear-quadratic-regression-model-fitting Use when you have a concentration-series calibration data set (e.g., narcotics standards) plus a test sample of unknown concentration, and need fitted linear/quadratic calibration curves with adjusted R2 and per-analyte relative errors. The task is untargeted metabolomics preprocessing or peak annotation rather than targeted concentration quantification — use SMART's untargeted modules instead. Calibration standards were not acquired under consistent LC-MS experimental conditions; the article states consistency is crucial for constructing a reliable calibration curve and accurate quantification. The analyte cannot be detected at all (e.g., SMART 2.0 could not detect heroin and nimetazepam in the narcotics data), leaving no peak response to regress against concentration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits weighted linear and quadratic calibration curves to concentration-series data, removes outliers via Cook's distance and confidence intervals, refits, and uses the models to estimate unknown-sample concentrations with relative errors, as implemented in SMART 2.0's concentration calibration module for the 12-narcotics data set. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: Fits weighted linear and quadratic calibration curves to concentration-series data, removes outliers via Cook's distance and confidence intervals, refits, and uses the models to estimate unknown-sample concentrations with relative errors, as implemented in SMART 2.0's concentration calibration module for the 12-narcotics data set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is untargeted metabolomics preprocessing or peak annotation rather than targeted concentration quantification — use SMART's untargeted modules instead. Calibration standards were not acquired under consistent LC-MS experimental conditions; the article states consistency is crucial for constructing a reliable calibration curve and accurate quantification. The analyte cannot be detected at all (e.g., SMART 2.0 could not detect heroin and nimetazepam in the narcotics data), leaving no peak response to regress against concentration.

skills.description: Use when validating a learned predictor for an auxiliary molecular property (RT or CCS) by demonstrating it beats a trivial univariate regression baseline on identical data splits, e.g. reproducing Fig. 5-style parity plots.
skills.name: linear-regression-baseline-benchmarking
skills.search_text: linear-regression-baseline-benchmarking Use when validating a learned predictor for an auxiliary molecular property (RT or CCS) by demonstrating it beats a trivial univariate regression baseline on identical data splits, e.g. reproducing Fig. 5-style parity plots. When benchmarking spectral intensity prediction against ICEBERG or CFM-ID — this skill covers only the auxiliary RT and CCS property tasks, not MS/MS spectra similarity When no retention time or CCS annotations exist for the compounds (e.g. NIST'17 does not provide RT and CCS values), since neither the model nor the linear baselines can be trained or evaluated When a tuned baseline is required — hyperparameters were not specifically tuned for the RT and CCS task and the feature is still in prototype stage Fits simple property-specific linear regression baselines (logP-based for retention time, precursor-m/z-based for CCS) on the same train/val/test splits used for the neural model, so that FIORA's RT and CCS submodules can be judged by R² deltas rather than absolute values. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Fits simple property-specific linear regression baselines (logP-based for retention time, precursor-m/z-based for CCS) on the same train/val/test splits used for the neural model, so that FIORA's RT and CCS submodules can be judged by R² deltas rather than absolute values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When benchmarking spectral intensity prediction against ICEBERG or CFM-ID — this skill covers only the auxiliary RT and CCS property tasks, not MS/MS spectra similarity When no retention time or CCS annotations exist for the compounds (e.g. NIST'17 does not provide RT and CCS values), since neither the model nor the linear baselines can be trained or evaluated When a tuned baseline is required — hyperparameters were not specifically tuned for the RT and CCS task and the feature is still in prototype stage

skills.description: Use when TIM-MS or DTIM-MS lipidomics CCS values show class-specific bias against a DTCCSN2 reference library and at least 3 U13C-labeled lipids per lipid class-adduct combination are available for regression.
skills.name: linear-regression-ccs-correction-fitting
skills.search_text: linear-regression-ccs-correction-fitting Use when TIM-MS or DTIM-MS lipidomics CCS values show class-specific bias against a DTCCSN2 reference library and at least 3 U13C-labeled lipids per lipid class-adduct combination are available for regression. Fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids exist for a lipid class-adduct combination, since linear regression requires a minimum of 3 lipids per function (correction restricted to Cer, DG, HexCer, LPC, PA, PC, PE, PI, PS, TG) Input measured values are already corrected CCS values — this skill fits functions from uncorrected measured CCS vs library pairs and should not be reapplied to corrected output Fits lipid class- and adduct-specific CCS correction functions by resampling 3–6 U13C-labeled lipids per combination and regressing measured CCS values against DTCCSN2 library values, then applying the functions to correct all measured CCS values. Enables MobiLipid's internal CCS quality control without external calibrant measurements. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: Fits lipid class- and adduct-specific CCS correction functions by resampling 3–6 U13C-labeled lipids per combination and regressing measured CCS values against DTCCSN2 library values, then applying the functions to correct all measured CCS values. Enables MobiLipid's internal CCS quality control without external calibrant measurements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids exist for a lipid class-adduct combination, since linear regression requires a minimum of 3 lipids per function (correction restricted to Cer, DG, HexCer, LPC, PA, PC, PE, PI, PS, TG) Input measured values are already corrected CCS values — this skill fits functions from uncorrected measured CCS vs library pairs and should not be reapplied to corrected output

skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature table (m/z rows, samples as columns) must be screened for features significantly altered by a binary condition, with batch-corrected vs raw comparisons.
skills.name: linear-regression-feature-screening
skills.search_text: linear-regression-feature-screening Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature table (m/z rows, samples as columns) must be screened for features significantly altered by a binary condition, with batch-corrected vs raw comparisons. Data has not yet been corrected for drift across batches — the article's workflow applies this screening AFTER dbnorm batch-effect correction (ber, ComBat, lowess), not on unprocessed intensities. The experiment has more than two conditions or a continuous covariate design where a simple two-group linear regression does not capture the biological contrast of interest. The goal is to select the batch-correction model itself rather than find differential features — use dbnormSCORE / adj-R2 scoring instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Per-feature linear regression of metabolomics intensities against a biological condition (e.g., HFD vs control) to estimate Log2 fold-change and p-values, followed by BH adjustment and screening with Log2FC > 1.5 and adjusted p < 0.05 to define a volcano-plot-highlighted differential feature list. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Per-feature linear regression of metabolomics intensities against a biological condition (e.g., HFD vs control) to estimate Log2 fold-change and p-values, followed by BH adjustment and screening with Log2FC > 1.5 and adjusted p < 0.05 to define a volcano-plot-highlighted differential feature list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not yet been corrected for drift across batches — the article's workflow applies this screening AFTER dbnorm batch-effect correction (ber, ComBat, lowess), not on unprocessed intensities. The experiment has more than two conditions or a continuous covariate design where a simple two-group linear regression does not capture the biological contrast of interest. The goal is to select the batch-correction model itself rather than find differential features — use dbnormSCORE / adj-R2 scoring instead.

skills.description: Use when benchmark timing measurements exist for a tool's runtime across varying input file sizes or parameter counts, and you must verify a claimed linear scaling relationship quantitatively.

skills.search_text: linear-regression-fitting-of-computational-scaling Use when benchmark timing measurements exist for a tool's runtime across varying input file sizes or parameter counts, and you must verify a claimed linear scaling relationship quantitatively. skills.description: Use when a series of spectra contains compounds spiked at known graded amounts (e.g., 0/20/40/60/80 uL) and you must confirm linear amplitude response plus a nonzero intercept from endogenous matrix content.
skills.name: linear-regression-intercept-verification
skills.search_text: linear-regression-intercept-verification Use when a series of spectra contains compounds spiked at known graded amounts (e.g., 0/20/40/60/80 uL) and you must confirm linear amplitude response plus a nonzero intercept from endogenous matrix content. The input spectra are not high-resolution 1D metabolomics NMR — the article states the current SAND version is tuned for high-resolution metabolomics spectra. You need exact quantitative concentrations rather than linearity/intercept verification — SAND's accuracy is a ~0.9 correlation with ground truth, not exact quantitation. The amplitude-vs-volume relationship is expected to be nonlinear (e.g., saturation or matrix depletion), making a straight-line intercept test inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Verifies that SAND-quantified 1D NMR peak amplitudes rise linearly with spike-in volume and that the fitted regression Y-intercept is clearly nonzero, exposing an endogenous analyte (e.g., glucose) already present in the unspiked matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03078
skills.summary: Verifies that SAND-quantified 1D NMR peak amplitudes rise linearly with spike-in volume and that the fitted regression Y-intercept is clearly nonzero, exposing an endogenous analyte (e.g., glucose) already present in the unspiked matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra are not high-resolution 1D metabolomics NMR — the article states the current SAND version is tuned for high-resolution metabolomics spectra. You need exact quantitative concentrations rather than linearity/intercept verification — SAND's accuracy is a ~0.9 correlation with ground truth, not exact quantitation. The amplitude-vs-volume relationship is expected to be nonlinear (e.g., saturation or matrix depletion), making a straight-line intercept test inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics data (e.g., TIMCCSN2 values from a Bruker timsTOF Pro) are spiked with U13C-labeled lipids and a DTCCSN2 reference library exists, and CCS biases must be corrected per lipid class-adduct combination via linear regression.
skills.name: linear-regression-model-fitting
skills.search_text: linear-regression-model-fitting Use when IM-MS lipidomics data (e.g., TIMCCSN2 values from a Bruker timsTOF Pro) are spiked with U13C-labeled lipids and a DTCCSN2 reference library exists, and CCS biases must be corrected per lipid class-adduct combination via linear regression. skills.summary: Fits lipid class- and adduct-specific linear CCS correction functions (y = m*x + b) by regressing measured TIMCCSN2 values of U13C-labeled yeast lipids against DTCCSN2 library values, enabling internal standardization-based CCS bias correction in IM-MS lipidomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids detected — regression cannot be fit and CCS correction is restricted to Cer, DG, HexCer, LPC, PA, PC, PE, PI, PS, and TG only The data are not spiked with U13C-labeled internal standards (fully labeled yeast extract) or no DTCCSN2 library values are available — the x and y regression inputs do not exist The goal is only CCS bias monitoring without correction — use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the correction workflow

skills.name: linear-regression-model-fitting
skills.search_text: linear-regression-model-fitting Use when calibrating single-field DTIMS-MS data with external calibrants (e.g. Agilent tune-mix): feature tables provide measured arrival times and a reference CCS list (TuneMix-CCS.txt) provides known CCS values, and a linear Ω″-vs-time calibration curve is needed. Stepped-field DTIMS data, where CCS is determined directly from multiple field strengths and no calibration curve is required Traveling-wave data (Waters Synapt, SLIM, Bruker timsTOF) where AutoCCS uses non-linear (polynomial or linearized power function) calibration instead of a degree-1 linear fit Data with no calibrant CCS reference file (e.g. TuneMix-CCS.txt), since external calibration requires known calibrant CCS values http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fits a degree-1 least-squares calibration line (numpy.polyfit) relating P/T-adjusted reduced CCS values (Ω″) to corrected arrival times from single-field DTIMS calibrant runs, as AutoCCS does for its enhanced single-field method (Eq. 4). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: Fits a degree-1 least-squares calibration line (numpy.polyfit) relating P/T-adjusted reduced CCS values (Ω″) to corrected arrival times from single-field DTIMS calibrant runs, as AutoCCS does for its enhanced single-field method (Eq. 4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Stepped-field DTIMS data, where CCS is determined directly from multiple field strengths and no calibration curve is required Traveling-wave data (Waters Synapt, SLIM, Bruker timsTOF) where AutoCCS uses non-linear (polynomial or linearized power function) calibration instead of a degree-1 linear fit Data with no calibrant CCS reference file (e.g. TuneMix-CCS.txt), since external calibration requires known calibrant CCS values

skills.description: Use when two GC–MS preprocessing tools have produced per-sample compound/feature quantification tables for the same samples and compounds, and you need a numeric per-compound agreement metric (R²) to validate that a new method (e.g., eRah) reproduces established quantification.
skills.name: linear-regression-r2-computation
skills.search_text: linear-regression-r2-computation Use when two GC–MS preprocessing tools have produced per-sample compound/feature quantification tables for the same samples and compounds, and you need a numeric per-compound agreement metric (R²) to validate that a new method (e.g., eRah) reproduces established quantification. Input is a single preprocessing tool's feature table with no second platform's quantification for the same samples/compounds — there is nothing to correlate against. The compounds in the two tables cannot be matched by name or identifier (e.g., eRah AlignID vs XCMS mzRT features have no crosswalk), since per-compound pairing is required before regression. The goal is peak picking or deconvolution itself rather than post-hoc quantification comparison; use eRah's deconvolveComp/alignComp pipeline or XCMS centWave first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute per-compound coefficients of determination (R²) by linearly regressing one platform's quantitative metabolite values (e.g., eRah's integrated deconvolved elution-profile areas) against another's (e.g., XCMS centWave or MetAlign ion-feature areas) across matched serum samples, to quantify cross-tool quantification agreement. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.6b02927
skills.summary: Compute per-compound coefficients of determination (R²) by linearly regressing one platform's quantitative metabolite values (e.g., eRah's integrated deconvolved elution-profile areas) against another's (e.g., XCMS centWave or MetAlign ion-feature areas) across matched serum samples, to quantify cross-tool quantification agreement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single preprocessing tool's feature table with no second platform's quantification for the same samples/compounds — there is nothing to correlate against. The compounds in the two tables cannot be matched by name or identifier (e.g., eRah AlignID vs XCMS mzRT features have no crosswalk), since per-compound pairing is required before regression. The goal is peak picking or deconvolution itself rather than post-hoc quantification comparison; use eRah's deconvolveComp/alignComp pipeline or XCMS centWave first.

skills.search_text: linear-regression-two-stage-batch-fitting Use when a log2-scaled LC-MS metabolomics matrix (.csv, samples in rows, features in columns, batch levels in the first column) shows across-batch signal drift — e. skills.name: linearized-power-function-ccs-regression
skills.search_text: linearized-power-function-ccs-regression Use when converting arrival-time measurements from single-field DTIMS or traveling-wave/SLIM IMS-MS into CCS values and the calibrant-to-analyte relationship is non-linear — e.g. SLIM helium data calibrated with TAA/tune-mix references where a quadratic poly fit underperforms. Data are stepped-field DTIMS-MS measurements — AutoCCS handles these in multi-field mode where calibration functions are not applied this way Input is raw UIMF or MS frames rather than extracted feature tables — AutoCCS expects Features_csv files, not UIMF-Library output Analyte arrival times lie outside the calibrant range (e.g. Pterin outside the TAA calibrant range), where extrapolation error dominates the choice of calibration function http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Calibrates single-field or traveling-wave IMS-MS arrival times to collision cross-section (CCS) values in AutoCCS using the linearized power regression function (Ruotolo et al., 2008), as an alternative to linear or polynomial (quadratic/cubic) calibration functions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: Calibrates single-field or traveling-wave IMS-MS arrival times to collision cross-section (CCS) values in AutoCCS using the linearized power regression function (Ruotolo et al., 2008), as an alternative to linear or polynomial (quadratic/cubic) calibration functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are stepped-field DTIMS-MS measurements — AutoCCS handles these in multi-field mode where calibration functions are not applied this way Input is raw UIMF or MS frames rather than extracted feature tables — AutoCCS expects Features_csv files, not UIMF-Library output Analyte arrival times lie outside the calibrant range (e.g. Pterin outside the TAA calibrant range), where extrapolation error dominates the choice of calibration function

skills.description: Use when calibrating TWIMS-MS arrival times to CCS (e.g. SLIM-based IMS or Waters Synapt) using reference calibrants such as Agilent tune-mix, and a power-law relationship (rather than polynomial) is desired for the calibration function.
skills.name: linearized-power-function-fitting
skills.search_text: linearized-power-function-fitting Use when calibrating TWIMS-MS arrival times to CCS (e.g. SLIM-based IMS or Waters Synapt) using reference calibrants such as Agilent tune-mix, and a power-law relationship (rather than polynomial) is desired for the calibration function. The data are stepped-field or single-field DTIMS, where CCS can be computed directly from the fundamental low-field ion mobility equation and no TWIMS calibration function is needed. A polynomial (quadratic/cubic) calibration function is preferred — use --calib_method poly instead of the power method. Input is a Bruker timsTOF dataset, which AutoCCS handles with linear calibration rather than the traveling-wave power function. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Fits AutoCCS's linearized power (TWIMS) calibration function — log-log regression of known calibrant CCS values against arrival-time terms per Ruotolo et al. 2008 — for traveling-wave IMS platforms (Waters Synapt, SLIM) where CCS cannot be computed directly from the low-field mobility equation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: Fits AutoCCS's linearized power (TWIMS) calibration function — log-log regression of known calibrant CCS values against arrival-time terms per Ruotolo et al. 2008 — for traveling-wave IMS platforms (Waters Synapt, SLIM) where CCS cannot be computed directly from the low-field mobility equation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are stepped-field or single-field DTIMS, where CCS can be computed directly from the fundamental low-field ion mobility equation and no TWIMS calibration function is needed. A polynomial (quadratic/cubic) calibration function is preferred — use --calib_method poly instead of the power method. Input is a Bruker timsTOF dataset, which AutoCCS handles with linear calibration rather than the traveling-wave power function.

skills.description: Use when NPOmix candidate BGC-GCF/MS-MS links exist for paired genome-MS/MS samples and you need to quantify precision against validated PoDP links, optionally filtered by a Jaccard co-occurrence threshold.
skills.name: link-prediction-precision-evaluation
skills.search_text: link-prediction-precision-evaluation Use when NPOmix candidate BGC-GCF/MS-MS links exist for paired genome-MS/MS samples and you need to quantify precision against validated PoDP links, optionally filtered by a Jaccard co-occurrence threshold. The query organism (e.g., a fungal species) has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset — output will contain no answer to evaluate Links involve RiPP-class metabolites — none of the currently validated metabolites in the PoDP database belong to the RiPP class, so precision cannot be grounded The goal is confirming novel (non-PoDP) links as final metabolite structures — these require proper elucidation (planar 2D and absolute 3D), not just classifier precision http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Evaluates NPOmix BGC-to-MS/MS candidate link precision by applying a Jaccard co-occurrence threshold (0.7) between BGC and MS/MS fingerprint vectors, then scoring filtered predictions against PoDP-validated gene-metabolite links. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Evaluates NPOmix BGC-to-MS/MS candidate link precision by applying a Jaccard co-occurrence threshold (0.7) between BGC and MS/MS fingerprint vectors, then scoring filtered predictions against PoDP-validated gene-metabolite links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query organism (e.g., a fungal species) has no BGC similar to any BGC in the NPOmix training dataset — output will contain no answer to evaluate Links involve RiPP-class metabolites — none of the currently validated metabolites in the PoDP database belong to the RiPP class, so precision cannot be grounded The goal is confirming novel (non-PoDP) links as final metabolite structures — these require proper elucidation (planar 2D and absolute 3D), not just classifier precision

skills.name: link-rank-comparison-table-reproduction
skills.search_text: link-rank-comparison-table-reproduction Use when benchmarking a BGC–MS/MS linking method (e.g. NPClassScore vs Metcalf-only) against a set of experimentally validated links from the PoDP, and you must report per-link retention and rank changes at a fixed score cut-off. When no experimentally validated links are available for the paired dataset — the article notes 'the lack of verified genome-metabolome links remains one of the current bottlenecks to validate new integrative omics mining methods' When the metabolites of interest exceed the ~850 Da CANOPUS mass cut-off or lack any CANOPUS/MolNetEnhancer class prediction, since such links are discarded by the filter_missing_scores toggle When the goal is de novo link discovery rather than benchmarking retention/rank against known validated links http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces the ranked-position comparison table (Table 1) showing where experimentally validated BGC–MS/MS links sit before and after NPClassScore filtering in NPLinker, quantifying retention (23/24 detectable links, 96%) and rank improvements such as staurosporine and rosamicin moving to rank 1. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the pruning effect of NPClassScore class matching on candidate BGC-MS/MS links per GCF in paired genome-metabolome datasets after Metcalf scoring, and to validate reported reduction percentages.
skills.name: link-reduction-percentage-calculation
skills.search_text: link-reduction-percentage-calculation Use when you need to quantify the pruning effect of NPClassScore class matching on candidate BGC-MS/MS links per GCF in paired genome-metabolome datasets after Metcalf scoring, and to validate reported reduction percentages. The goal is absolute prioritisation performance rather than reduction accounting: without discarding links that lack structure-based classes, the average decrease is only 49%, so mixing filter_missing_scores settings makes the percentage incomparable to the reported 63%. The Nocardia dataset is analysed without adjusting the Metcalf threshold: validated links there scored below the standard cut-off of 2.5, so the threshold must be lowered to 2 to include them before counting reductions. No structure-based class predictions exist (no CANOPUS/MolNetEnhancer output): NPClassScore filtering will discard nearly all links and the reduction percentages are not meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies how much NPClassScore chemical-class filtering (cut-off 0.25) reduces candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links per GCF relative to standardised Metcalf co-occurrence scoring alone, across the three PoDP paired omics datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Quantifies how much NPClassScore chemical-class filtering (cut-off 0.25) reduces candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links per GCF relative to standardised Metcalf co-occurrence scoring alone, across the three PoDP paired omics datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is absolute prioritisation performance rather than reduction accounting: without discarding links that lack structure-based classes, the average decrease is only 49%, so mixing filter_missing_scores settings makes the percentage incomparable to the reported 63%. The Nocardia dataset is analysed without adjusting the Metcalf threshold: validated links there scored below the standard cut-off of 2.5, so the threshold must be lowered to 2 to include them before counting reductions. No structure-based class predictions exist (no CANOPUS/MolNetEnhancer output): NPClassScore filtering will discard nearly all links and the reduction percentages are not meaningful.

skills.name: lipid-acyl-chain-labeling-analysis
skills.search_text: lipid-acyl-chain-labeling-analysis Use when HRMS lipidomics data from a 13C labeling time course contains a resolved lipid molecular species (e.g., PC(36:4)) whose precursor isotopologue distribution must be decomposed into per-acyl-chain (18:1, 18:2, 18:3) labeling using MS2 fragment spectra. Input is raw LC-MS vendor files that have not been pre-processed with XCMS into a feature table with isotopologue-level resolution MS2 spectra are nominal-resolution only and cannot distinguish resolved isotopologues (e.g., M0 vs M6) of the lipid species Goal is precursor-level (whole-lipid) isotopologue distribution without per-acyl-chain decomposition http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A SIMPEL-based procedure for reconstructing how 13C labeling is distributed among the individual fatty acyl chains of a phospholipid molecular species, using high-resolution MS2 spectra of resolved isotopologues (e.g., unlabeled M0 vs labeled M6 of PC(36:4)) to attribute precursor enrichment to acyl-chain combinations such as 18:1/18:2/18:3 pair-summed weights. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42003-024-05844-z
