skills.description: Use when a MALDI-MSI peak list (e.g. imzML or exported intensity CSV from SCiLS/MSiReader) contains unassigned high-abundance ions whose pairwise mass differences match known matrix adducts, and you need to flag them as matrix-adduct duplicates rather than distinct metabolite signals.
skills.name: lipid-adduct-annotation-maldi-msi
skills.search_text: lipid-adduct-annotation-maldi-msi Use when a MALDI-MSI peak list (e.g. imzML or exported intensity CSV from SCiLS/MSiReader) contains unassigned high-abundance ions whose pairwise mass differences match known matrix adducts, and you need to flag them as matrix-adduct duplicates rather than distinct metabolite signals. The ion of interest is a true metabolite signal whose mass difference to a neighbor is coincidental — mass-difference matching alone is insufficient; require the spatial-correlation and/or MS2 fragment confirmation step before labeling as adduct. Input is raw, unbinned imzML without preprocessing: mass2adduct needs a peak-binned intensity matrix (`peakBin()` must be run in Cardinal first; it does not process centroid-free profiles). You only have a simple list of masses and no pixel data — `corrPairsMSI` spatial validation is impossible; the workflow reduces to mass-difference screening only. The adduct of interest is not in the `adducts`/`adducts2` reference tables and no custom data.frame (name, formula, mass) is supplied. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates lipid/metabolite ion peaks in MALDI-MSI data as matrix adducts (e.g. [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+) by combining mass-difference matching against a reference adduct table with spatial co-localization of parent and adduct ion maps, using the R package mass2adduct. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: Annotates lipid/metabolite ion peaks in MALDI-MSI data as matrix adducts (e.g. [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+) by combining mass-difference matching against a reference adduct table with spatial co-localization of parent and adduct ion maps, using the R package mass2adduct.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ion of interest is a true metabolite signal whose mass difference to a neighbor is coincidental — mass-difference matching alone is insufficient; require the spatial-correlation and/or MS2 fragment confirmation step before labeling as adduct. Input is raw, unbinned imzML without preprocessing: mass2adduct needs a peak-binned intensity matrix (`peakBin()` must be run in Cardinal first; it does not process centroid-free profiles). You only have a simple list of masses and no pixel data — `corrPairsMSI` spatial validation is impossible; the workflow reduces to mass-difference screening only. The adduct of interest is not in the `adducts`/`adducts2` reference tables and no custom data.frame (name, formula, mass) is supplied.

skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-agreement-disagreement-analysis Use when aligning lipid annotations between two spectral libraries (e.g., CalicoLipids and MS-DIAL) and a per-library score cutoff is needed to separate authentic from spurious identifications. skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-candidate-filtering Use when you must narrow a LipidBlast-style candidate list from precursor m/z matches for lipidomics queries and want multidimensional (RT, CCS) re-ranking with recall metrics. Your molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se — SigmaCCS cannot predict CCS for them Your ion adduct is not one of the three encoded types ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-) — SigmaCCS only handles these adduct ion types You already have a fully resolved identification table with no candidate ambiguity — filtering would add no ranking benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A staged candidate-filtering workflow for lipid identification that progressively combines precursor m/z matching, GNN-RT-predicted retention times, and SigmaCCS-predicted CCS values to re-rank candidate annotations and improve Recall@1/Recall@30. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00939-w

skills.name: lipid-annotation-conversion
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-conversion Use when lipid shorthand annotations from heterogeneous software (e.g. MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, MZmine2) or databases (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, HMDB, RefMet) must be unified, level-equalized, or linked to LION/KEGG/ChEBI/Rhea/UniProtKB identifiers. The input lipids are plant or bacterial classes outside the current mammalian coverage (25 classes across five categories: fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) and no new JSON configuration entry has been added yet The annotations are already in canonical LipidLynxX ID form and only raw identifier strings are needed with no cross-mapping or level equalization The molecules are non-lipid metabolites needing general ID conversion outside LipidLynxX's lipid-focused vocabulary Convert heterogeneous lipid annotations (26 input styles from 5 databases and 17 lipidomics programs) into unified LipidLynxX IDs and cross-mapped LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, and PubChem identifiers, then translate them into ontology/pathway/network identifiers (LION, KEGG, ChEBI, Rhea, UniProtKB) via LipidLynxX's Converter, Equalizer, and Linker modules. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Convert heterogeneous lipid annotations (26 input styles from 5 databases and 17 lipidomics programs) into unified LipidLynxX IDs and cross-mapped LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, and PubChem identifiers, then translate them into ontology/pathway/network identifiers (LION, KEGG, ChEBI, Rhea, UniProtKB) via LipidLynxX's Converter, Equalizer, and Linker modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lipids are plant or bacterial classes outside the current mammalian coverage (25 classes across five categories: fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) and no new JSON configuration entry has been added yet The annotations are already in canonical LipidLynxX ID form and only raw identifier strings are needed with no cross-mapping or level equalization The molecules are non-lipid metabolites needing general ID conversion outside LipidLynxX's lipid-focused vocabulary

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether PNNL PreProcessor preprocessing improves lipid annotation yield in a replicate LC-DT IM-MS lipidomics workflow, or when reproducing a reported annotation-count improvement between two processing conditions on the same deposited MSV000087295 lists.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-count-comparison
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-count-comparison Use when evaluating whether PNNL PreProcessor preprocessing improves lipid annotation yield in a replicate LC-DT IM-MS lipidomics workflow, or when reproducing a reported annotation-count improvement between two processing conditions on the same deposited MSV000087295 lists. When the input is already an aggregated feature table without replicate-level annotation lists — the consensus rule requires per-file annotation lists to recompute the ≥2-replicate counts When the comparison basis differs from MS1-level lipid annotations in Agilent .d files processed by Lipid Annotator (e.g., proteomics feature counts or MS2-level identifications) — the counting rule and tool consensus logic would not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A method for recomputing the change in lipid annotation yield attributable to PNNL PreProcessor preprocessing by counting lipid annotations present in at least 2 of 3 replicates, as generated by Lipid Annotator from Agilent .d LC-DT IM-MS files, and comparing original versus preprocessed annotation totals. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: A method for recomputing the change in lipid annotation yield attributable to PNNL PreProcessor preprocessing by counting lipid annotations present in at least 2 of 3 replicates, as generated by Lipid Annotator from Agilent .d LC-DT IM-MS files, and comparing original versus preprocessed annotation totals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already an aggregated feature table without replicate-level annotation lists — the consensus rule requires per-file annotation lists to recompute the ≥2-replicate counts When the comparison basis differs from MS1-level lipid annotations in Agilent .d files processed by Lipid Annotator (e.g., proteomics feature counts or MS2-level identifications) — the counting rule and tool consensus logic would not apply

skills.description: Use when auditing or reproducing published lipidomics annotation counts from a supplemental annotation workbook — e.g., recounting LipidMatch negative-mode identifications on Red Cross plasma (210 lipid ions, 159 features, 15 lipid types) from Additional file 3 Table S4.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-count-reconciliation
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-count-reconciliation Use when auditing or reproducing published lipidomics annotation counts from a supplemental annotation workbook — e.g., recounting LipidMatch negative-mode identifications on Red Cross plasma (210 lipid ions, 159 features, 15 lipid types) from Additional file 3 Table S4. Feature tables and MS/MS spectra are raw and unannotated — run the full LipidMatch pipeline first (peak picking with MZmine/XCMS/MS-DIAL, MSConvert conversion to .ms2, then LipidMatch matching) rather than recounting annotations The annotation table contains no LipidMatch annotation column/entries (e.g., only MS-DIAL or Greazy output) — this skill specifically isolates and recounts LipidMatch identifications Fresh identifications are requested using current LipidMatch libraries (over 500,000 species across over 60 lipid types per README) and compared against 2017 published counts (250,000 species, 56 types) — library drift makes such counts non-comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Recounts distinct lipid ions, features (unique m/z + retention time pairs), and lipid types among LipidMatch annotations in a published annotation table (e.g., the negative-polarity worksheet of Additional file 3, Table S4) and reconciles the recounted figures against published counts. It verifies the reproducibility of negative-mode Red Cross plasma annotation counts (210 lipid ions, 159 features, 15 lipid types) that underpin cross-software corroboration claims. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Recounts distinct lipid ions, features (unique m/z + retention time pairs), and lipid types among LipidMatch annotations in a published annotation table (e.g., the negative-polarity worksheet of Additional file 3, Table S4) and reconciles the recounted figures against published counts. It verifies the reproducibility of negative-mode Red Cross plasma annotation counts (210 lipid ions, 159 features, 15 lipid types) that underpin cross-software corroboration claims.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Feature tables and MS/MS spectra are raw and unannotated — run the full LipidMatch pipeline first (peak picking with MZmine/XCMS/MS-DIAL, MSConvert conversion to .ms2, then LipidMatch matching) rather than recounting annotations The annotation table contains no LipidMatch annotation column/entries (e.g., only MS-DIAL or Greazy output) — this skill specifically isolates and recounts LipidMatch identifications Fresh identifications are requested using current LipidMatch libraries (over 500,000 species across over 60 lipid types per README) and compared against 2017 published counts (250,000 species, 56 types) — library drift makes such counts non-comparable

skills.description: Use when reproducing published lipidomics annotation counts from a LipidMatch/MS-DIAL/Greazy annotation workbook (e.g. Additional file 3) or validating counts of unique lipid ions, features, and lipid types per polarity.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-counting
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-counting Use when reproducing published lipidomics annotation counts from a LipidMatch/MS-DIAL/Greazy annotation workbook (e.g. Additional file 3) or validating counts of unique lipid ions, features, and lipid types per polarity. Input is already a validated count table rather than raw annotation rows Annotations come from a tool other than LipidMatch (e.g. only MS-DIAL or Greazy) and the counting convention differs The workbook is a fragmentation library (e.g. LipidMatch in silico libraries) rather than feature-level annotation output http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Recount and cross-check lipid annotation counts (unique lipid ions, distinct features, and lipid types) from LipidMatch output spreadsheets in a given ionization mode, using pandas/openpyxl over the paper's Additional file 3 worksheets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Recount and cross-check lipid annotation counts (unique lipid ions, distinct features, and lipid types) from LipidMatch output spreadsheets in a given ionization mode, using pandas/openpyxl over the paper's Additional file 3 worksheets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated count table rather than raw annotation rows Annotations come from a tool other than LipidMatch (e.g. only MS-DIAL or Greazy) and the counting convention differs The workbook is a fragmentation library (e.g. LipidMatch in silico libraries) rather than feature-level annotation output

skills.description: Use when you have MS/MS feature tables from LC-MS lipidomics (e.g., RBL-2H3, mixture, human sera, zebrafish) and need to quantify annotation confidence via an estimated FDR against the LipidIN theoretical library.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-fdr-estimation Use when you have MS/MS feature tables from LC-MS lipidomics (e.g., RBL-2H3, mixture, human sera, zebrafish) and need to quantify annotation confidence via an estimated FDR against the LipidIN theoretical library. Your goal is downstream quantification, differential analysis, or pathway enrichment rather than annotation confidence estimation Your data requires Paternò–Büchi double-bond localization rather than standard chain-composition annotation scoring Input is already a finalized annotation table without the raw MS/MS features needed to re-score EQ+LCI hits at the 2.4 cutoff http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Estimate the false discovery rate of LipidIN EQ+LCI lipid annotations on LC-MS/MS feature tables by combining MS2 library search, LCI relative-RT-rule filtering, and strict ECN-rule/feature-peak criteria; the reference benchmark achieves ~5.7% average FDR across 8,923 annotated lipids in four datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Estimate the false discovery rate of LipidIN EQ+LCI lipid annotations on LC-MS/MS feature tables by combining MS2 library search, LCI relative-RT-rule filtering, and strict ECN-rule/feature-peak criteria; the reference benchmark achieves ~5.7% average FDR across 8,923 annotated lipids in four datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is downstream quantification, differential analysis, or pathway enrichment rather than annotation confidence estimation Your data requires Paternò–Büchi double-bond localization rather than standard chain-composition annotation scoring Input is already a finalized annotation table without the raw MS/MS features needed to re-score EQ+LCI hits at the 2.4 cutoff

skills.description: Use when two or more lipidomics annotation lists report lipids at mixed structural levels (e.g. PC 38:4 vs PC 16:0_20:4 vs PC(16:0/20:4)) and you need to cross-match or merge them at a shared level.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-level-equalization
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-level-equalization Use when two or more lipidomics annotation lists report lipids at mixed structural levels (e.g. PC 38:4 vs PC 16:0_20:4 vs PC(16:0/20:4)) and you need to cross-match or merge them at a shared level. Input lipids are plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, and sterols The goal is identifier conversion to LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or PubChem accessions rather than cross-level cross-matching — use the LipidLynxX Converter module instead Annotations are already reported at a single uniform structural level in both datasets, so no level equalization is needed before comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 LipidLynxX Equalizer reduces heterogeneous lipid identifiers (species, molecular species, sn-position, DB-position, full-structure) to a single common structural annotation level via an annotation-level matrix, so lipidomics datasets annotated at different levels can be cross-compared and compiled for meta-analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: LipidLynxX Equalizer reduces heterogeneous lipid identifiers (species, molecular species, sn-position, DB-position, full-structure) to a single common structural annotation level via an annotation-level matrix, so lipidomics datasets annotated at different levels can be cross-compared and compiled for meta-analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lipids are plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, and sterols The goal is identifier conversion to LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or PubChem accessions rather than cross-level cross-matching — use the LipidLynxX Converter module instead Annotations are already reported at a single uniform structural level in both datasets, so no level equalization is needed before comparison

skills.description: Use when you have a TIC-normalized peak list of m/z values from MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data and need to assign putative lipid identities before regional or differential analysis.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-lipid-maps-search
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-lipid-maps-search Use when you have a TIC-normalized peak list of m/z values from MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data and need to assign putative lipid identities before regional or differential analysis. Annotating image-guided single-cell (SCMS) spectra lacking spatial information, where FDR-controlled annotation methods are difficult to apply per the article's discussion When m/z values have not been peak-binned/aligned across sections, causing mass shifts that would inflate false matches http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates MSI lipid features by matching detected m/z values against the LIPID MAPS experimental and virtual databases with a ±0.005 m/z threshold, prioritizing experimentally validated lipids sorted by ppm error. This converts a peak list into named lipid species (e.g., HexCer, Cer, SM) that can then be linked to anatomical regions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Annotates MSI lipid features by matching detected m/z values against the LIPID MAPS experimental and virtual databases with a ±0.005 m/z threshold, prioritizing experimentally validated lipids sorted by ppm error. This converts a peak list into named lipid species (e.g., HexCer, Cer, SM) that can then be linked to anatomical regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotating image-guided single-cell (SCMS) spectra lacking spatial information, where FDR-controlled annotation methods are difficult to apply per the article's discussion When m/z values have not been peak-binned/aligned across sections, causing mass shifts that would inflate false matches

skills.description: Use when lipid structure records (e.g., LIPID MAPS or SwissLipids exports at the highest structural resolution level) must be checked for correct double bond position encoding, or when the plausibility of double bond annotations in a lipid database must be quantified.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-qc-evaluation
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-qc-evaluation Use when lipid structure records (e.g., LIPID MAPS or SwissLipids exports at the highest structural resolution level) must be checked for correct double bond position encoding, or when the plausibility of double bond annotations in a lipid database must be quantified. Input lipid species lack explicit double bond positions (only summary notation like PC 38:4 is available) — no positional sets can be computed The goal is lipidome-level quantitative comparison or feature analysis rather than structural annotation correctness — use LipidSpace's MCS/Jaccard structural comparison or statistics module instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Quality-control evaluation of lipid structural annotations by extracting double bond positions from fatty acyl chains (forward from the carbonyl carbon and backward in ω-notation) and computing the probability of complete double bond mismatch between chain pairs, validated against the ~73% threshold reported for LIPID MAPS. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Quality-control evaluation of lipid structural annotations by extracting double bond positions from fatty acyl chains (forward from the carbonyl carbon and backward in ω-notation) and computing the probability of complete double bond mismatch between chain pairs, validated against the ~73% threshold reported for LIPID MAPS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lipid species lack explicit double bond positions (only summary notation like PC 38:4 is available) — no positional sets can be computed The goal is lipidome-level quantitative comparison or feature analysis rather than structural annotation correctness — use LipidSpace's MCS/Jaccard structural comparison or statistics module instead

skills.description: Use when a task requires enumerating which lipid identification software or lipid databases have predefined annotation input styles, or when building/validating a converter's style catalog from JSON rule configurations.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-style-curation
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-style-curation Use when a task requires enumerating which lipid identification software or lipid databases have predefined annotation input styles, or when building/validating a converter's style catalog from JSON rule configurations. The goal is to convert lipid abbreviations between styles (use the LipidLynxX Converter/Equalizer modules directly instead of re-curating the style list) The target database/program has no configuration file in lynx/configurations/rules/input and is not covered by the 26 pre-defined styles You need lipid annotation coverage for plant or bacterial lipids, which LipidLynxX does not currently cover http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Compiles the full set of predefined lipid annotation input styles (17 lipid identification programs plus 5 lipid-oriented databases = 26 styles) from the LipidLynxX JSON configuration files, producing a cross-checked CSV catalog of style-to-source mappings. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Compiles the full set of predefined lipid annotation input styles (17 lipid identification programs plus 5 lipid-oriented databases = 26 styles) from the LipidLynxX JSON configuration files, producing a cross-checked CSV catalog of style-to-source mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to convert lipid abbreviations between styles (use the LipidLynxX Converter/Equalizer modules directly instead of re-curating the style list) The target database/program has no configuration file in lynx/configurations/rules/input and is not covered by the 26 pre-defined styles You need lipid annotation coverage for plant or bacterial lipids, which LipidLynxX does not currently cover

skills.description: Use when you have annotation lists from Lipid Annotator for original vs. preprocessed LC-IM-MS replicates and need per-replicate detection/annotation counts for a specific lipid feature.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-table-querying
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-table-querying Use when you have annotation lists from Lipid Annotator for original vs. preprocessed LC-IM-MS replicates and need per-replicate detection/annotation counts for a specific lipid feature. You already have a single consolidated feature table and only need downstream statistics (e.g. fold change, p-values), not per-replicate presence/absence tallies. The data are not LC-IM-MS lipidomics replicates and the tool used is not Lipid Annotator or a compatible annotation table producer. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Query and tally lipid annotation records across replicate LC-IM-MS feature lists, e.g. to determine in which of the 3 replicates a low-abundance feature such as Sphingomyelin d34:5 (m/z 695.5088, RT 6.2 min, AT 36.7 ms) is annotated after PNNL PreProcessor smoothing versus in the original data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: Query and tally lipid annotation records across replicate LC-IM-MS feature lists, e.g. to determine in which of the 3 replicates a low-abundance feature such as Sphingomyelin d34:5 (m/z 695.5088, RT 6.2 min, AT 36.7 ms) is annotated after PNNL PreProcessor smoothing versus in the original data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a single consolidated feature table and only need downstream statistics (e.g. fold change, p-values), not per-replicate presence/absence tallies. The data are not LC-IM-MS lipidomics replicates and the tool used is not Lipid Annotator or a compatible annotation table producer.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature annotations must be filtered by RBP score thresholds and compared between two fragmentation libraries to reproduce annotation counts and agreement statistics.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-threshold-filtering Use when raw LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature annotations must be filtered by RBP score thresholds and compared between two fragmentation libraries to reproduce annotation counts and agreement statistics. Input is already a filtered annotation table with no raw scores available to re-apply RBP thresholds The task concerns a single library search rather than a dual-library (CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) comparison, since library-specific thresholds and overlap statistics are not applicable Data are untargeted metabolomics (non-lipid) features outside the lipid classes covered by the in-silico libraries Filters lipidomics compound annotations from dual in-silico library searches (CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) using library-specific Retention Balance Point (RBP) score thresholds in MAVEN2, then quantifies annotation overlap and library agreement at lipid-class and full-structure level. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12080684
skills.summary: Filters lipidomics compound annotations from dual in-silico library searches (CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) using library-specific Retention Balance Point (RBP) score thresholds in MAVEN2, then quantifies annotation overlap and library agreement at lipid-class and full-structure level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered annotation table with no raw scores available to re-apply RBP thresholds The task concerns a single library search rather than a dual-library (CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) comparison, since library-specific thresholds and overlap statistics are not applicable Data are untargeted metabolomics (non-lipid) features outside the lipid classes covered by the in-silico libraries

skills.description: Use when LC/MS feature tables contain enriched lipid features with tentative acyl-chain annotations whose biosynthetic origin is unknown and isotope-labeled precursor (e.g., 13C6-leucine) versus unlabeled control data are available to test incorporation.
skills.name: lipid-annotation-verification
skills.search_text: lipid-annotation-verification Use when LC/MS feature tables contain enriched lipid features with tentative acyl-chain annotations whose biosynthetic origin is unknown and isotope-labeled precursor (e.g., 13C6-leucine) versus unlabeled control data are available to test incorporation. The candidate lipids already have confident Level 1/2 annotations with authentic standards, so isotope tracing adds no annotation evidence Only unlabeled samples exist — no labeled-supplement feature table is available for pairwise Label Finder comparison The analysis goal is raw feature detection from profiles rather than testing annotations of already-detected features (use the xcms module first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Verification of putative lipid annotations by isotope tracing in Metaboseek's Label Finder, testing whether candidate lipids (e.g., odd-chain 13:1 and 15:1 monounsaturated species) derive from a proposed biosynthetic route such as branched-chain fatty acid (BCFA) metabolism via 13C6-leucine incorporation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: Verification of putative lipid annotations by isotope tracing in Metaboseek's Label Finder, testing whether candidate lipids (e.g., odd-chain 13:1 and 15:1 monounsaturated species) derive from a proposed biosynthetic route such as branched-chain fatty acid (BCFA) metabolism via 13C6-leucine incorporation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate lipids already have confident Level 1/2 annotations with authentic standards, so isotope tracing adds no annotation evidence Only unlabeled samples exist — no labeled-supplement feature table is available for pairwise Label Finder comparison The analysis goal is raw feature detection from profiles rather than testing annotations of already-detected features (use the xcms module first)

skills.description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic data matrix is at the molecular-species level (e.g., 'PC 16:0_18:1') and a chain-level (lipid building block) sub-matrix is required for downstream analysis.
skills.name: lipid-building-block-submatrix-generation
skills.search_text: lipid-building-block-submatrix-generation Use when an uploaded lipidomic data matrix is at the molecular-species level (e.g., 'PC 16:0_18:1') and a chain-level (lipid building block) sub-matrix is required for downstream analysis. The input matrix is already at the lipid class (LCL) level, so no chain decomposition is possible The input is already a chain-level/building-block matrix — re-splitting would divide values by chain counts a second time Row identifiers do not follow lipid shorthand notation with class prefix and colon-separated chain annotations, so chains cannot be parsed http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Automatically derives the lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix from a molecular-species (LMS-level) intensity matrix by splitting each lipid species row into its constituent acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chain rows, conserving total signal, and aggregating chains shared across species into pseudo-lipid rows. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Automatically derives the lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix from a molecular-species (LMS-level) intensity matrix by splitting each lipid species row into its constituent acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chain rows, conserving total signal, and aggregating chains shared across species into pseudo-lipid rows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already at the lipid class (LCL) level, so no chain decomposition is possible The input is already a chain-level/building-block matrix — re-splitting would divide values by chain counts a second time Row identifiers do not follow lipid shorthand notation with class prefix and colon-separated chain annotations, so chains cannot be parsed

skills.description: Reference for building or auditing an experimental lipid CCS/m/z reference database from cleaned per-instrument CCS collections (DTIM, TWIM, TIMS) when per-field totals must be verified against reported row counts.
skills.name: lipid-ccs-database-assembly
skills.search_text: lipid-ccs-database-assembly Reference for building or auditing an experimental lipid CCS/m/z reference database from cleaned per-instrument CCS collections (DTIM, TWIM, TIMS) when per-field totals must be verified against reported row counts. The goal is CCS prediction for lipids absent from experimental collections — use the trained machine-learning prediction models and the predicted database (145,388 entries) instead of re-assembling the experimental database. The analysis target is lipidomics data analysis (statistics, plotting, identification) on an IM-MS dataset — use the lipydomics stats/plotting/identification modules on a Dataset instance rather than rebuilding the reference database. Input collections are not cleaned or lack per-entry ionization-mode/drift-tube-type annotations, so per-field totals cannot be validated. Assemble a combined experimental lipid reference database by aggregating cleaned per-dataset JSON CCS collections (DTIM, TWIM, TIMS) into a single SQLite file with m/z, CCS, lipid class, ionization mode, and drift-tube-type fields, then verify per-field totals. This provides the verifiable experimental backbone that LiPydomics uses for lipid identification and for training CCS/retention-time prediction models. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560
skills.summary: Assemble a combined experimental lipid reference database by aggregating cleaned per-dataset JSON CCS collections (DTIM, TWIM, TIMS) into a single SQLite file with m/z, CCS, lipid class, ionization mode, and drift-tube-type fields, then verify per-field totals. This provides the verifiable experimental backbone that LiPydomics uses for lipid identification and for training CCS/retention-time prediction models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is CCS prediction for lipids absent from experimental collections — use the trained machine-learning prediction models and the predicted database (145,388 entries) instead of re-assembling the experimental database. The analysis target is lipidomics data analysis (statistics, plotting, identification) on an IM-MS dataset — use the lipydomics stats/plotting/identification modules on a Dataset instance rather than rebuilding the reference database. Input collections are not cleaned or lack per-entry ionization-mode/drift-tube-type annotations, so per-field totals cannot be validated.

skills.description: Use when annotating lipid metabolites from ion-mobility MS data where candidate structures from PubChem must be ranked or filtered using measured/predicted CCS values, and a lipid-superclass [M−H]− training set is available or desired.
skills.name: lipid-ccs-prediction
skills.search_text: lipid-ccs-prediction Use when annotating lipid metabolites from ion-mobility MS data where candidate structures from PubChem must be ranked or filtered using measured/predicted CCS values, and a lipid-superclass [M−H]− training set is available or desired. The analyte is outside the lipid/lipid-like superclass or uses adduct types not covered by the training set (e.g., dimers such as [2M+H]+ or [2M−H]−, other less common adducts, or in-source fragments) No CCS measurements are available to curate a superclass-matched training set and only generic all-class prediction is needed — consider broader models (MetCCS, AllCCS) instead of tailored training Very large prediction jobs where the 12-hour/20-minute-idle limits of Google Colab would be hit — use the locally hosted Jupyter Lab notebook instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Train and apply a superclass-matched linear support vector regression model in CCSP 2.0 (a Jupyter notebook using 1613 Mordred molecular descriptors) to predict collision cross sections for lipid [M−H]− ions and filter false-positive annotation candidates at a ΔCCS threshold of 2.8%. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c03491
skills.summary: Train and apply a superclass-matched linear support vector regression model in CCSP 2.0 (a Jupyter notebook using 1613 Mordred molecular descriptors) to predict collision cross sections for lipid [M−H]− ions and filter false-positive annotation candidates at a ΔCCS threshold of 2.8%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte is outside the lipid/lipid-like superclass or uses adduct types not covered by the training set (e.g., dimers such as [2M+H]+ or [2M−H]−, other less common adducts, or in-source fragments) No CCS measurements are available to curate a superclass-matched training set and only generic all-class prediction is needed — consider broader models (MetCCS, AllCCS) instead of tailored training Very large prediction jobs where the 12-hour/20-minute-idle limits of Google Colab would be hit — use the locally hosted Jupyter Lab notebook instead

skills.description: Use when a curated lipid CCS training table (e.g., the 6394-measurement LiPydomics dataset) with one-hot lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and adduct features plus sum composition and m/z must be used to fit and evaluate an SVR CCS predictor.
skills.name: lipid-ccs-prediction-model-training
skills.search_text: lipid-ccs-prediction-model-training Use when a curated lipid CCS training table (e.g., the 6394-measurement LiPydomics dataset) with one-hot lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and adduct features plus sum composition and m/z must be used to fit and evaluate an SVR CCS predictor. The input is already a trained model or a serialized prediction artifact — this skill only covers fitting and evaluating the SVR from the encoded measurement table. The task is HILIC retention time prediction rather than CCS prediction — the paper trains those models separately (23 lipid classes for RT vs 22 for CCS). The lipid class of interest is not among the 22 lipid classes covered by the paper's trained CCS prediction models, so no published reference metrics exist to validate against. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Train a support vector regression model with an RBF kernel that predicts lipid collision cross sections (CCS, in Å²) from 39-feature lipid encodings, replicating the LiPydomics CCS prediction approach. The skill exists to reproduce the published model's error profile and serialize it for downstream CCS prediction in HILIC-IM-MS lipidomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560
skills.summary: Train a support vector regression model with an RBF kernel that predicts lipid collision cross sections (CCS, in Å²) from 39-feature lipid encodings, replicating the LiPydomics CCS prediction approach. The skill exists to reproduce the published model's error profile and serialize it for downstream CCS prediction in HILIC-IM-MS lipidomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a trained model or a serialized prediction artifact — this skill only covers fitting and evaluating the SVR from the encoded measurement table. The task is HILIC retention time prediction rather than CCS prediction — the paper trains those models separately (23 lipid classes for RT vs 22 for CCS). The lipid class of interest is not among the 22 lipid classes covered by the paper's trained CCS prediction models, so no published reference metrics exist to validate against.

skills.description: Use when building or auditing a DTCCSN2 library of U13C-labeled lipids for internal standardization in LC-IM-MS lipidomics, or when verifying that a supplied library (e.g. U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv) meets stated quality criteria.
skills.name: lipid-ccs-reference-library-validation
skills.search_text: lipid-ccs-reference-library-validation Use when building or auditing a DTCCSN2 library of U13C-labeled lipids for internal standardization in LC-IM-MS lipidomics, or when verifying that a supplied library (e.g. U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv) meets stated quality criteria. Input data come from a TIM-MS (e.g. Bruker timsTOF Pro) or other non-DTIM platform — the library must be built from DTCCSN2 (Agilent 6560 drift-tube) measurements, not from trapped-IM values. The analytes are unlabeled ('light') lipids only — the library and validation apply specifically to U13C-labeled ('heavy') internal standards spiked into samples. A lipid class-adduct combination appears in the data but is not listed as permissible (e.g. LPC with [M-H]) — such entries must be rejected rather than added to the library. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Curation and validation of a DTCCSN2 reference library for U13C-labeled yeast lipids, generated from Agilent 6560 DTIM-MS measurements and used inside MobiLipid for internal CCS bias calculation and correction. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: Curation and validation of a DTCCSN2 reference library for U13C-labeled yeast lipids, generated from Agilent 6560 DTIM-MS measurements and used inside MobiLipid for internal CCS bias calculation and correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data come from a TIM-MS (e.g. Bruker timsTOF Pro) or other non-DTIM platform — the library must be built from DTCCSN2 (Agilent 6560 drift-tube) measurements, not from trapped-IM values. The analytes are unlabeled ('light') lipids only — the library and validation apply specifically to U13C-labeled ('heavy') internal standards spiked into samples. A lipid class-adduct combination appears in the data but is not listed as permissible (e.g. LPC with [M-H]) — such entries must be rejected rather than added to the library.

skills.description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with fully U13C-labeled yeast extract lipids, measured CCS values exist per lipid class/adduct, and TIMCCSN2-vs-DTCCSN2 bias needs correction via lipid class- and adduct-specific linear regression.
skills.name: lipid-class-adduct-ccs-regression-correction
skills.search_text: lipid-class-adduct-ccs-regression-correction Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with fully U13C-labeled yeast extract lipids, measured CCS values exist per lipid class/adduct, and TIMCCSN2-vs-DTCCSN2 bias needs correction via lipid class- and adduct-specific linear regression. The goal is only to monitor CCS bias without correction - use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the CCS-correction Rmd. A lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids - linear regression requires a minimum of 3 lipids, so correction is restricted to Cer, DG, HexCer, LPC, PA, PC, PE, PI, PS, and TG (AcCa, Co, LPE, PG, SPH are not correctable). The data are from unlabeled-only workflows without U13C yeast extract spike-in - the DTCCSN2 library values for U13C-labeled lipids are the regression targets and cannot be substituted. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A MobiLipid procedure that computes lipid class- and adduct-specific linear CCS correction functions (y = m*x + b) by regressing measured CCS of U13C-labeled lipids against their DTCCSN2 library values, then applies those functions to all measured CCS values regardless of labeling status, driving mean absolute CCSN2 bias toward 0%. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: A MobiLipid procedure that computes lipid class- and adduct-specific linear CCS correction functions (y = m*x + b) by regressing measured CCS of U13C-labeled lipids against their DTCCSN2 library values, then applies those functions to all measured CCS values regardless of labeling status, driving mean absolute CCSN2 bias toward 0%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only to monitor CCS bias without correction - use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the CCS-correction Rmd. A lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids - linear regression requires a minimum of 3 lipids, so correction is restricted to Cer, DG, HexCer, LPC, PA, PC, PE, PI, PS, and TG (AcCa, Co, LPE, PG, SPH are not correctable). The data are from unlabeled-only workflows without U13C yeast extract spike-in - the DTCCSN2 library values for U13C-labeled lipids are the regression targets and cannot be substituted.

skills.description: Use when the input is a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix (rows = lipid species in LIPID MAPS shorthand notation, columns = samples) and a lipid-class-level (LCL) matrix is needed for downstream class-level statistics.
skills.name: lipid-class-aggregation-from-molecular-species
skills.search_text: lipid-class-aggregation-from-molecular-species Use when the input is a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix (rows = lipid species in LIPID MAPS shorthand notation, columns = samples) and a lipid-class-level (LCL) matrix is needed for downstream class-level statistics. The input matrix is already at the lipid-class level (one row per class) — aggregation would double-count nothing but adds no information and class-level statistics can proceed directly. The target is building-block (LBB) level analysis of acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chains — that requires a different decomposition of species into building blocks, not class-prefix summation. Lipid shorthand notation does not follow LIPID MAPS conventions (e.g., free-text or proprietary names), so class prefixes cannot be reliably extracted without a prior nomenclature mapping step (see the article's Support Protocol on lipid nomenclature). http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates the lipid class (LCL) sub-matrix from a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix by summing, sample-by-sample, the abundances of all molecular species sharing the same LIPID MAPS shorthand lipid class prefix (e.g., PC, PE, TG). This is the aggregation step LipidOne 2.0 performs so users can analyze lipids at the class structural level without manual submatrix calculations. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Generates the lipid class (LCL) sub-matrix from a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix by summing, sample-by-sample, the abundances of all molecular species sharing the same LIPID MAPS shorthand lipid class prefix (e.g., PC, PE, TG). This is the aggregation step LipidOne 2.0 performs so users can analyze lipids at the class structural level without manual submatrix calculations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already at the lipid-class level (one row per class) — aggregation would double-count nothing but adds no information and class-level statistics can proceed directly. The target is building-block (LBB) level analysis of acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chains — that requires a different decomposition of species into building blocks, not class-prefix summation. Lipid shorthand notation does not follow LIPID MAPS conventions (e.g., free-text or proprietary names), so class prefixes cannot be reliably extracted without a prior nomenclature mapping step (see the article's Support Protocol on lipid nomenclature).
