skills.name: lipid-compound-class-annotation-from-spectral-matches
skills.search_text: lipid-compound-class-annotation-from-spectral-matches Use when MS2Query (or a similar library-matching tool) has returned per-spectrum matches for complex-mixture metabolomics data and you must check whether annotations agree with the expected compound class (e.g., lipids in plasma). Query data are not from a mixture with a known expected compound-class composition — there is no reference class expectation to validate against Input spectra have not been preprocessed: MS2Query does no peak picking or clustering, and raw files with many MS2 spectra per feature should first be reduced (e.g. MZMine FBMN output) The goal is exact structural elucidation rather than class-level consistency checking — MS2Query predicts analogues and exact matches, not de novo structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Attach compound-class annotations (lipid vs non-lipid) to MS2Query spectral matches using LIPID MAPS, HMDB, and GNPS mappings, then verify that predicted matches consistently belong to the expected compound class, as demonstrated on the NIST 1950 plasma case study where 72 of 75 matches were lipids. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: Attach compound-class annotations (lipid vs non-lipid) to MS2Query spectral matches using LIPID MAPS, HMDB, and GNPS mappings, then verify that predicted matches consistently belong to the expected compound class, as demonstrated on the NIST 1950 plasma case study where 72 of 75 matches were lipids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data are not from a mixture with a known expected compound-class composition — there is no reference class expectation to validate against Input spectra have not been preprocessed: MS2Query does no peak picking or clustering, and raw files with many MS2 spectra per feature should first be reduced (e.g. MZMine FBMN output) The goal is exact structural elucidation rather than class-level consistency checking — MS2Query predicts analogues and exact matches, not de novo structures

skills.description: Use when you have a targeted-lipidomics abundance matrix (lipid species such as PI, PC, PE, PS, PG and AA-containing species as rows; e.g. 0.01/1 U/mL thrombin, 1/5 µg/mL CRP plus unstimulated control as columns) and need to test class-level depletion claims and co-regulation structure.
skills.name: lipid-correlation-network-reconstruction
skills.search_text: lipid-correlation-network-reconstruction Use when you have a targeted-lipidomics abundance matrix (lipid species such as PI, PC, PE, PS, PG and AA-containing species as rows; e.g. 0.01/1 U/mL thrombin, 1/5 µg/mL CRP plus unstimulated control as columns) and need to test class-level depletion claims and co-regulation structure. The input is already a correlation network or edge list — no abundance matrix to re-correlate. The dataset has no unstimulated control column, so per-condition log2 fold-changes cannot be computed. Lipid identifications come from unvalidated assays in simple model systems (e.g. yeast) without multiple fragments and both polarity modes, making co-regulation signals unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reconstructs a Spearman rank-correlation network over platelet lipid species and class-level log2 fold-change summaries across thrombin/CRP stimulation conditions, to test claims about PI-cluster depletion and the PI pool as the dominant arachidonic-acid (AA) reservoir. Uses Skyline/LipidCreator-derived targeted-lipidomics quantities as input. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Reconstructs a Spearman rank-correlation network over platelet lipid species and class-level log2 fold-change summaries across thrombin/CRP stimulation conditions, to test claims about PI-cluster depletion and the PI pool as the dominant arachidonic-acid (AA) reservoir. Uses Skyline/LipidCreator-derived targeted-lipidomics quantities as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a correlation network or edge list — no abundance matrix to re-correlate. The dataset has no unstimulated control column, so per-condition log2 fold-changes cannot be computed. Lipid identifications come from unvalidated assays in simple model systems (e.g. yeast) without multiple fragments and both polarity modes, making co-regulation signals unreliable.

skills.description: Use when lipid shorthand annotations (e.g. PC 16:0_18:2, MS-DIAL/LipidSearch-style abbreviations, DHA-style aliases) must be cross-matched to LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or PubChem accession IDs for cross-database comparison or systems biology integration.
skills.name: lipid-database-accession-linking
skills.search_text: lipid-database-accession-linking Use when lipid shorthand annotations (e.g. PC 16:0_18:2, MS-DIAL/LipidSearch-style abbreviations, DHA-style aliases) must be cross-matched to LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or PubChem accession IDs for cross-database comparison or systems biology integration. Annotations are plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, and sterols Input is already a unified identifier table with LIPID MAPS/SwissLipids accessions — re-running conversion adds no annotation-level equalization value The goal is metabolic pathway/network analysis rather than identifier cross-matching — use the downstream Linker/integration tools (BioPAN, Metabolomics2Networks) directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Cross-maps lipid shorthand annotations into external accession identifiers (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, PubChem) via the LipidLynxX Converter and Linker modules, enabling experimental lipidomics tables to be linked to data integration tools. Validated on the paper's 131-lipid example dataset with zero conversion failures. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Cross-maps lipid shorthand annotations into external accession identifiers (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, PubChem) via the LipidLynxX Converter and Linker modules, enabling experimental lipidomics tables to be linked to data integration tools. Validated on the paper's 131-lipid example dataset with zero conversion failures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotations are plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, and sterols Input is already a unified identifier table with LIPID MAPS/SwissLipids accessions — re-running conversion adds no annotation-level equalization value The goal is metabolic pathway/network analysis rather than identifier cross-matching — use the downstream Linker/integration tools (BioPAN, Metabolomics2Networks) directly instead

skills.description: Use when a structural-space or structural-similarity analysis needs molecular graphs for named lipid species (e.g., PC 12:0/[12-24,26]:0 series) and only species names/SMILES-free identifiers are available.
skills.name: lipid-database-structure-retrieval
skills.search_text: lipid-database-structure-retrieval Use when a structural-space or structural-similarity analysis needs molecular graphs for named lipid species (e.g., PC 12:0/[12-24,26]:0 series) and only species names/SMILES-free identifiers are available. The analysis only needs exact species-name matching across lipidomes and no structural comparison — name normalization via Goslin alone suffices Lipid names are only at sum-composition level (e.g., PC 36:1) with no chain detail; retrieved structures cannot resolve sn-order-aware acyl comparisons accurately http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Retrieves lipid molecular structures from structure databases such as LIPID MAPS and SwissLipids at the highest structural resolution level, so that downstream graph-based comparison (e.g., LipidSpace's maximum common subgraph + Jaccard index approach) can operate on actual molecular graphs rather than parsed names alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Retrieves lipid molecular structures from structure databases such as LIPID MAPS and SwissLipids at the highest structural resolution level, so that downstream graph-based comparison (e.g., LipidSpace's maximum common subgraph + Jaccard index approach) can operate on actual molecular graphs rather than parsed names alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only needs exact species-name matching across lipidomes and no structural comparison — name normalization via Goslin alone suffices Lipid names are only at sum-composition level (e.g., PC 36:1) with no chain detail; retrieved structures cannot resolve sn-order-aware acyl comparisons accurately

skills.description: Use when lipid structure records carry explicit double bond positions on fatty acyl chains and you must quantify how often two arbitrary chains share no double bond at the same position under forward (carbonyl) and backward (omega) numbering, or need a reference-database ground truth for.
skills.name: lipid-double-bond-position-extraction
skills.search_text: lipid-double-bond-position-extraction Use when lipid structure records carry explicit double bond positions on fatty acyl chains and you must quantify how often two arbitrary chains share no double bond at the same position under forward (carbonyl) and backward (omega) numbering, or need a reference-database ground truth for. Lipid entries are only at partial structural resolution (e.g., sum-composition or DB-position-free notations) — the mismatch statistics are undefined without explicit double bond positions The goal is lipidome-level abundance analysis or PCA/dendrogram exploration in LipidSpace rather than validating structural double bond comparison correctness Input is already a lipidomics intensity table (csv/xlsx/mzTab-M) for import; this skill operates on reference structure databases, not measured abundance data http://edamontology.org/topic_3368 Extracts carbon chains with explicit double bond positions from high-resolution lipid structure records in reference databases (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids), then quantifies directional double bond mismatch probabilities between chain pairs under carbonyl-forward versus omega-backward counting conventions to ground correctness evaluation of lipid structural comparisons. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Extracts carbon chains with explicit double bond positions from high-resolution lipid structure records in reference databases (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids), then quantifies directional double bond mismatch probabilities between chain pairs under carbonyl-forward versus omega-backward counting conventions to ground correctness evaluation of lipid structural comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Lipid entries are only at partial structural resolution (e.g., sum-composition or DB-position-free notations) — the mismatch statistics are undefined without explicit double bond positions The goal is lipidome-level abundance analysis or PCA/dendrogram exploration in LipidSpace rather than validating structural double bond comparison correctness Input is already a lipidomics intensity table (csv/xlsx/mzTab-M) for import; this skill operates on reference structure databases, not measured abundance data

skills.description: Use when LC/MS feature tables from two or more biological groups (e.g., WT vs hacl-1 mutant on OP50 vs cyclopropane-deficient JW1653-1 diets) must be compared to find features enriched in one genotype that additionally depend on the bacterial diet.
skills.name: lipid-feature-abundance-comparison
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-abundance-comparison Use when LC/MS feature tables from two or more biological groups (e.g., WT vs hacl-1 mutant on OP50 vs cyclopropane-deficient JW1653-1 diets) must be compared to find features enriched in one genotype that additionally depend on the bacterial diet. Input is already a filtered, regrouped feature table with diet/genotype labels assigned and blanks removed — proceed directly to statistical comparison instead The question is structural annotation or molecular formula prediction of features rather than group-wise abundance comparison (use Metaboseek's SIRIUS/formula modules instead) Data are unprocessed profile-mode raw files with no xcms feature detection run — feature detection must precede this comparison workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 A comparative metabolomics workflow for detecting lipid-derived LC/MS molecular features whose abundance depends on both genotype and diet, exemplified by diet-dependent cyclopropane N-acyl GPEs accumulating in hacl-1 C. elegans mutants (e.g., GPE 13:1, m/z 496.2317) using Metaboseek. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: A comparative metabolomics workflow for detecting lipid-derived LC/MS molecular features whose abundance depends on both genotype and diet, exemplified by diet-dependent cyclopropane N-acyl GPEs accumulating in hacl-1 C. elegans mutants (e.g., GPE 13:1, m/z 496.2317) using Metaboseek.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered, regrouped feature table with diet/genotype labels assigned and blanks removed — proceed directly to statistical comparison instead The question is structural annotation or molecular formula prediction of features rather than group-wise abundance comparison (use Metaboseek's SIRIUS/formula modules instead) Data are unprocessed profile-mode raw files with no xcms feature detection run — feature detection must precede this comparison workflow

skills.description: Use when lipid features from traveling-wave IM-MS (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) have been class-assigned and CCS-calibrated and you need database-backed validation of exact mass and CCS against curated lipid reference values.
skills.name: lipid-feature-annotation-against-lipidpioneer
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-annotation-against-lipidpioneer Use when lipid features from traveling-wave IM-MS (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) have been class-assigned and CCS-calibrated and you need database-backed validation of exact mass and CCS against curated lipid reference values. Features have not yet been CCS-calibrated or class-assigned by MOCCal (the skill assumes a MOCCal output with class, TWCCSN2, and ΔCCS columns) Data are in negative ionization mode or from non-TWIM platforms — MOCCal and its calibrations are currently limited to small molecule, lipid, and peptide classes on TWIM-MS instruments like the Waters SYNAPT XS Validates MOCCal-classified lipid features from TWIM-MS (e.g., HILIC-IM-MS of NIST SRM 1950 plasma extract) by comparing exact masses and calibrated TWCCSN2 values against the LipidPioneer and Unified CCS Compendium databases to quantify per-feature assignment error and cross-class misassignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04290
skills.summary: Validates MOCCal-classified lipid features from TWIM-MS (e.g., HILIC-IM-MS of NIST SRM 1950 plasma extract) by comparing exact masses and calibrated TWCCSN2 values against the LipidPioneer and Unified CCS Compendium databases to quantify per-feature assignment error and cross-class misassignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features have not yet been CCS-calibrated or class-assigned by MOCCal (the skill assumes a MOCCal output with class, TWCCSN2, and ΔCCS columns) Data are in negative ionization mode or from non-TWIM platforms — MOCCal and its calibrations are currently limited to small molecule, lipid, and peptide classes on TWIM-MS instruments like the Waters SYNAPT XS

skills.description: Use when a LipiDex 2 (or similar) discovery lipidomics run has Peak Finder and Spectral Searcher outputs plus Degreaser QC filtering results, and you must report how feature counts and identification rate changed after filtering.
skills.name: lipid-feature-count-reconciliation
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-count-reconciliation Use when a LipiDex 2 (or similar) discovery lipidomics run has Peak Finder and Spectral Searcher outputs plus Degreaser QC filtering results, and you must report how feature counts and identification rate changed after filtering. Input is a single unfiltered peak table with no spectral search or QC filtering performed — there are no pre/post stages to reconcile The goal is lipid identification or spectral matching itself rather than count bookkeeping across filtering stages Data were not processed through a LipiDex 2-style pipeline with identifiable filtering criteria (e.g., adduct/dimer removal, RT modeling, %RSD), so per-filter attribution is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconciles lipid feature and identification counts across pre- and post-QC-filter stages of the LipiDex 2 Degreaser pipeline, quantifying how many identified lipids, identifications, and unidentified features survive each filtering criterion and the resulting change in identification rate. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Reconciles lipid feature and identification counts across pre- and post-QC-filter stages of the LipiDex 2 Degreaser pipeline, quantifying how many identified lipids, identifications, and unidentified features survive each filtering criterion and the resulting change in identification rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single unfiltered peak table with no spectral search or QC filtering performed — there are no pre/post stages to reconcile The goal is lipid identification or spectral matching itself rather than count bookkeeping across filtering stages Data were not processed through a LipiDex 2-style pipeline with identifiable filtering criteria (e.g., adduct/dimer removal, RT modeling, %RSD), so per-filter attribution is undefined

skills.description: Use when you have MALDI MSI peak data co-registered with an IFM segmentation mask (e.g. thresholded Ly6G marker) and need to rank which lipids (m/z features) classify marker-positive vs marker-negative pixels.
skills.name: lipid-feature-importance-ranking
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-importance-ranking Use when you have MALDI MSI peak data co-registered with an IFM segmentation mask (e.g. thresholded Ly6G marker) and need to rank which lipids (m/z features) classify marker-positive vs marker-negative pixels. Your goal is lipid annotation/interpretation rather than candidate discovery — msiFlow explicitly does not include an annotation or interpretation step (use databases such as LipidMaps separately) Your labels come from manual ROI drawing rather than a thresholded IFM marker segmentation, so the binary pixel-binning premise (marker-positive vs marker-negative classes) does not apply Your data are single-modality MSI without co-registered microscopy, leaving no IFM-derived class labels to train on Identifies the spatial lipidomic signature of an image-derived cell population (e.g. Ly6G+ neutrophils) by training a tree-based XGBoost classifier on co-registered MALDI MSI pixel spectra and ranking lipid features by classifier feature importance and Pearson correlation with the marker-positive class, as implemented in msiFlow's molecular_signatures_flow. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Identifies the spatial lipidomic signature of an image-derived cell population (e.g. Ly6G+ neutrophils) by training a tree-based XGBoost classifier on co-registered MALDI MSI pixel spectra and ranking lipid features by classifier feature importance and Pearson correlation with the marker-positive class, as implemented in msiFlow's molecular_signatures_flow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is lipid annotation/interpretation rather than candidate discovery — msiFlow explicitly does not include an annotation or interpretation step (use databases such as LipidMaps separately) Your labels come from manual ROI drawing rather than a thresholded IFM marker segmentation, so the binary pixel-binning premise (marker-positive vs marker-negative classes) does not apply Your data are single-modality MSI without co-registered microscopy, leaving no IFM-derived class labels to train on

skills.description: Use when LipidIN-annotated lipid feature tables from patient cohorts (e.g., breast cancer vs. healthy plasma LC-MS lipidomics, Supplementary Data 9) are available and a small diagnostic panel with cross-cohort generalization is needed.
skills.name: lipid-feature-importance-selection
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-importance-selection Use when LipidIN-annotated lipid feature tables from patient cohorts (e.g., breast cancer vs. healthy plasma LC-MS lipidomics, Supplementary Data 9) are available and a small diagnostic panel with cross-cohort generalization is needed. Input is raw LC-MS/MS data not yet processed by LipidIN annotation/quantification/QC (CV / PCA / PLS-DA); feature importance selection requires an annotated feature table first Only one cohort is available and the goal includes estimating cross-cohort generalization, which this skill's two-cohort validation design addresses The task is lipid annotation itself (MS2 library search against the 168.6-million-entry theoretical library) rather than downstream biomarker modeling http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects a compact disease-discriminating lipid biomarker panel by ranking LipidIN-annotated lipid features with random-forest Gini importance, then validates discrimination with a LightGBM classifier across independent clinical cohorts. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Selects a compact disease-discriminating lipid biomarker panel by ranking LipidIN-annotated lipid features with random-forest Gini importance, then validates discrimination with a LightGBM classifier across independent clinical cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS/MS data not yet processed by LipidIN annotation/quantification/QC (CV / PCA / PLS-DA); feature importance selection requires an annotated feature table first Only one cohort is available and the goal includes estimating cross-cohort generalization, which this skill's two-cohort validation design addresses The task is lipid annotation itself (MS2 library search against the 168.6-million-entry theoretical library) rather than downstream biomarker modeling

skills.description: Use when a lipid feature/abundance matrix plus a phenotype file must be normalized (mstus) and decomposed via lipidr into lipid class, chain length, and saturation features before differential lipid analysis in MOI.
skills.name: lipid-feature-normalization
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-normalization Use when a lipid feature/abundance matrix plus a phenotype file must be normalized (mstus) and decomposed via lipidr into lipid class, chain length, and saturation features before differential lipid analysis in MOI. Input is transcriptomics data (mRNA, miRNA, isoform count matrices) — use MOI's RNA-seq modules (filterByExp, quantile normalization, edgeR/DESeq2/RankProduct) instead. Input is already a normalized, lipidr-annotated feature table with no phenotype file — differential contrasts against phenotype groups cannot be defined, so skip to downstream visualization only. The analysis target is multi-omics integration (MCIA PCA) rather than lipid-specific normalization and differential analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Normalizes lipid abundance matrices with the mstus approach (preprocessCore), then uses lipidr to parse lipid identifiers into lipid-class, total chain length, and degree-of-saturation features for MOI's lipidomics module. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae175
skills.summary: Normalizes lipid abundance matrices with the mstus approach (preprocessCore), then uses lipidr to parse lipid identifiers into lipid-class, total chain length, and degree-of-saturation features for MOI's lipidomics module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is transcriptomics data (mRNA, miRNA, isoform count matrices) — use MOI's RNA-seq modules (filterByExp, quantile normalization, edgeR/DESeq2/RankProduct) instead. Input is already a normalized, lipidr-annotated feature table with no phenotype file — differential contrasts against phenotype groups cannot be defined, so skip to downstream visualization only. The analysis target is multi-omics integration (MCIA PCA) rather than lipid-specific normalization and differential analysis.

skills.description: Use when training or applying lipid CCS prediction models that need tabular lipid measurements (lipid class, fatty acid sum composition, adduct, m/z) converted to a fixed-width numeric feature matrix for scikit-learn estimators.
skills.name: lipid-feature-one-hot-encoding
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-one-hot-encoding Use when training or applying lipid CCS prediction models that need tabular lipid measurements (lipid class, fatty acid sum composition, adduct, m/z) converted to a fixed-width numeric feature matrix for scikit-learn estimators. Input is already an encoded numeric feature matrix or a generic descriptor table (e.g., DeepCCS-style descriptors) — re-encoding would break compatibility with the LiPydomics-trained models The target lipid class or adduct is outside the 22 CCS prediction classes trained by LiPydomics; encoding an unseen category yields an uninformative vector The goal is lipid identification or stats/plotting analysis of HILIC-IM-MS data rather than CCS prediction — use the identification or stats modules instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encodes lipid m/z and CCS measurements into fixed-width numeric feature vectors — one-hot encoded lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and adduct features plus sum composition and m/z — so machine learning models (e.g., scikit-learn SVR) can predict collision cross sections from simple but specialized lipid descriptors. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560
skills.summary: Encodes lipid m/z and CCS measurements into fixed-width numeric feature vectors — one-hot encoded lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and adduct features plus sum composition and m/z — so machine learning models (e.g., scikit-learn SVR) can predict collision cross sections from simple but specialized lipid descriptors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an encoded numeric feature matrix or a generic descriptor table (e.g., DeepCCS-style descriptors) — re-encoding would break compatibility with the LiPydomics-trained models The target lipid class or adduct is outside the 22 CCS prediction classes trained by LiPydomics; encoding an unseen category yields an uninformative vector The goal is lipid identification or stats/plotting analysis of HILIC-IM-MS data rather than CCS prediction — use the identification or stats modules instead

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics peak table (e.g. from Compound Discoverer 3.3 .cdResult) contains adduct peaks, dimers, or identifications failing QC evidence such as >30% RSD in QC samples, and must be filtered before quantitation.
skills.name: lipid-feature-qc-filtering
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-qc-filtering Use when a lipidomics peak table (e.g. from Compound Discoverer 3.3 .cdResult) contains adduct peaks, dimers, or identifications failing QC evidence such as >30% RSD in QC samples, and must be filtered before quantitation. Input is still raw MS/MS data before spectral matching and peak identification — filtering operates on post-identification results from the LipiDex 2 pipeline Peak table originates from a tool other than Compound Discoverer 3.3 — Peak Finder requires .cdResult files as input for the peak table Input is already a manually curated or previously filtered feature table where adduct/dimer removal would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Post-identification quality control for LC-MS lipidomics using LipiDex 2's Peak Finder filtering and Degreaser QC module to remove adducts, dimers, in-source fragments, and other spurious features and to downgrade identifications lacking required fragment evidence. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Post-identification quality control for LC-MS lipidomics using LipiDex 2's Peak Finder filtering and Degreaser QC module to remove adducts, dimers, in-source fragments, and other spurious features and to downgrade identifications lacking required fragment evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw MS/MS data before spectral matching and peak identification — filtering operates on post-identification results from the LipiDex 2 pipeline Peak table originates from a tool other than Compound Discoverer 3.3 — Peak Finder requires .cdResult files as input for the peak table Input is already a manually curated or previously filtered feature table where adduct/dimer removal would be redundant

skills.description: Use when raw peak lists from MSI sections or single-cell SCMS runs contain mass-shifted duplicate m/z peaks, and you need to retain only mutually observed, low-occurrence-filtered lipid features for downstream annotation or clustering.
skills.name: lipid-feature-quality-control
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-quality-control Use when raw peak lists from MSI sections or single-cell SCMS runs contain mass-shifted duplicate m/z peaks, and you need to retain only mutually observed, low-occurrence-filtered lipid features for downstream annotation or clustering. Input is already a de-duplicated, annotated feature table with no mass-shift issues to correct The goal is de novo metabolite annotation from a spectral database rather than cross-annotating SCMS peaks against a tissue MSI lipid feature list Features must be retained regardless of prevalence, e.g. when quantifying rare, region-specific lipids that appear in under 5% of cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A feature-level QC skill from the MEISTER multiscale mass-spectrometry pipeline that aligns lipid peaks by m/z binning in 3-ppm increments, then filters features and cells by a 5% prevalence threshold before cross-annotating single-cell SCMS spectra against a tissue MSI lipid feature database. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: A feature-level QC skill from the MEISTER multiscale mass-spectrometry pipeline that aligns lipid peaks by m/z binning in 3-ppm increments, then filters features and cells by a 5% prevalence threshold before cross-annotating single-cell SCMS spectra against a tissue MSI lipid feature database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a de-duplicated, annotated feature table with no mass-shift issues to correct The goal is de novo metabolite annotation from a spectral database rather than cross-annotating SCMS peaks against a tissue MSI lipid feature list Features must be retained regardless of prevalence, e.g. when quantifying rare, region-specific lipids that appear in under 5% of cells

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics abundance table is annotated with sample-associated study variables (e.g., BMI, tissue, condition) and you need the lipid subset that distinguishes each variable.
skills.name: lipid-feature-sequential-forward-selection
skills.search_text: lipid-feature-sequential-forward-selection Use when a lipidomics abundance table is annotated with sample-associated study variables (e.g., BMI, tissue, condition) and you need the lipid subset that distinguishes each variable. The dataset carries no sample-associated study variables (lipid abundances only) — there is nothing for the regression/classification models to target. The goal is lipidome-level structural similarity, PCA, dendrogram clustering, or quality control rather than identifying lipids that distinguish study variables. A complete exhaustive feature search is required — this skill is a fast heuristic SFS terminated after √n rounds, not an exhaustive subset search. LipidSpace's feature analysis and selection module applies a heuristic sequential forward selection (SFS) over lipid abundances to identify, per study variable, the lipid subset that best describes that variable, scored by AIC (and ROC accuracy for binary nominal variables). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: LipidSpace's feature analysis and selection module applies a heuristic sequential forward selection (SFS) over lipid abundances to identify, per study variable, the lipid subset that best describes that variable, scored by AIC (and ROC accuracy for binary nominal variables).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset carries no sample-associated study variables (lipid abundances only) — there is nothing for the regression/classification models to target. The goal is lipidome-level structural similarity, PCA, dendrogram clustering, or quality control rather than identifying lipids that distinguish study variables. A complete exhaustive feature search is required — this skill is a fast heuristic SFS terminated after √n rounds, not an exhaustive subset search.

skills.description: Use when MS2 library search (EQ) plus LCI filtering leaves low-confidence or unannotated LC-MS/MS lipid features that need recall boosting via regenerated fingerprint spectra from a pre-trained deep-learning model.
skills.name: lipid-fingerprint-regeneration
skills.search_text: lipid-fingerprint-regeneration Use when MS2 library search (EQ) plus LCI filtering leaves low-confidence or unannotated LC-MS/MS lipid features that need recall boosting via regenerated fingerprint spectra from a pre-trained deep-learning model. Features already annotated with high confidence by the EQ MS2 library search and LCI strict-criteria filtering — regeneration adds no value and risks false positives Non-lipid small-molecule metabolite identification where no lipid structural features (head group, chain length, unsaturation) map to retention/fingerprint models When a sample-specific experimental spectral library is already available — direct library search is preferable to model-regenerated fingerprints http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Regenerates lipid fragment fingerprint spectra using LipidIN's Wide-spectrum Modeling Yield network (WMYn) as a 'reverse lipidomics' 5th-level library, boosting annotation recall (~20% estimated) and confirming low-confidence lipids independent of sample matrix, instrument, and analytical method. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Regenerates lipid fragment fingerprint spectra using LipidIN's Wide-spectrum Modeling Yield network (WMYn) as a 'reverse lipidomics' 5th-level library, boosting annotation recall (~20% estimated) and confirming low-confidence lipids independent of sample matrix, instrument, and analytical method.

skills.description: Use when designing or auditing a targeted lipidomics PRM/MRM assay: you must decide how many MS/MS fragments (and which tolerance, e.g. ±0.5 Da vs ±2.5 ppm) are needed so that target lipids cannot be confused with decoys within the sample lipidome background.

skills.search_text: lipid-fragment-mass-probability-computation Use when designing or auditing a targeted lipidomics PRM/MRM assay: you must decide how many MS/MS fragments (and which tolerance, e.g. ±0.5 Da vs ±2.5 ppm) are needed so that target lipids cannot be confused with decoys within the sample lipidome background. You need an automated FDR scoring algorithm — LipidCreator does not provide a dedicated scoring algorithm to determine false discovery rates and intentionally does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids and peak area integration. Your analysis is untargeted lipidome-wide screening rather than targeted assay development for a defined set of lipids of interest. Your sample requires stereoisomer resolution — the article notes no large-scale methods exist to cope with stereoisomers due to lack of isotope-coded standards. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes, per fragment count (0–3) and mass tolerance (±0.5 Da vs ±2.5 ppm), the probability that a precursor–fragment pair identifies a lipid species unambiguously against a background lipidome, and validates the resulting accuracy against target-decoy PRM identification counts (e.g. ~98% for yeast with three fragments in both polarities). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z

skills.description: Use when lipid identifiers contain unresolved mass-isomer groups such as 'TAG 48:2 total (14:0/16:0/18:2)(14:0/16:1/18:1)(16:0/16:1/16:1)', and residue extraction must account for or discard isobaric uncertainty.
skills.name: lipid-isomer-ambiguity-handling
skills.search_text: lipid-isomer-ambiguity-handling Use when lipid identifiers contain unresolved mass-isomer groups such as 'TAG 48:2 total (14:0/16:0/18:2)(14:0/16:1/18:1)(16:0/16:1/16:1)', and residue extraction must account for or discard isobaric uncertainty. The lipid identifier is a single unambiguous species with no isomer group — no ambiguity policy is needed and the standard residue extraction suffices. The analysis targets the lipid class (LCL) or molecular species (LMS) level only — no chain decomposition is needed and existing sub-matrices can be used directly Row identifiers lack parsable chain annotations (e.g. only class names or non-shorthand labels), so class prefix and chain list cannot be split reliably The matrix is already a chain-level/pseudo-lipid feature table, and re-splitting would double-divide intensities http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Derives the lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix from a molecular-species (LMS) intensity matrix by parsing each species identifier into a lipid class prefix and chain list, splitting rows into per-chain pseudo-lipids with signal conservation, and aggregating duplicate chain rows. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Derives the lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix from a molecular-species (LMS) intensity matrix by parsing each species identifier into a lipid class prefix and chain list, splitting rows into per-chain pseudo-lipids with signal conservation, and aggregating duplicate chain rows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets the lipid class (LCL) or molecular species (LMS) level only — no chain decomposition is needed and existing sub-matrices can be used directly Row identifiers lack parsable chain annotations (e.g. only class names or non-shorthand labels), so class prefix and chain list cannot be split reliably The matrix is already a chain-level/pseudo-lipid feature table, and re-splitting would double-divide intensities

skills.description: Use when lipid identifiers come from mixed sources (e.g. MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids) in inconsistent notation styles and must be decomposed and cross-compared at a common structural level.
skills.name: lipid-nomenclature-parsing
skills.search_text: lipid-nomenclature-parsing Use when lipid identifiers come from mixed sources (e.g. MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids) in inconsistent notation styles and must be decomposed and cross-compared at a common structural level. The lipids of interest are plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across five categories (fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) The input identifiers are already uniform canonical LipidLynxX IDs at a single level and no cross-level comparison is needed You need ontology-structured output rather than abbreviation conversion — an ontology mapper (e.g. LION/LipidLION) may be more appropriate for that goal http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Parse heterogeneous lipid abbreviation styles (space shorthand like 'PC 16:0_18:2', bracket derivatives like 'PC(16:0_18:2)', and aliases like DHA/PLPC) into uniform, decomposed LipidLynxX identifiers so lipidomics identifiers from different tools can be compared and equalized to a shared annotation level. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Parse heterogeneous lipid abbreviation styles (space shorthand like 'PC 16:0_18:2', bracket derivatives like 'PC(16:0_18:2)', and aliases like DHA/PLPC) into uniform, decomposed LipidLynxX identifiers so lipidomics identifiers from different tools can be compared and equalized to a shared annotation level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The lipids of interest are plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across five categories (fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) The input identifiers are already uniform canonical LipidLynxX IDs at a single level and no cross-level comparison is needed You need ontology-structured output rather than abbreviation conversion — an ontology mapper (e.g. LION/LipidLION) may be more appropriate for that goal

skills.description: Use when an annotated m/z feature table contains raw lipid annotation strings (e.g. multi-isomer entries in an all_IsomerNames-style column) that must be collapsed into standard lipid categories and subclasses before downstream statistics.
skills.name: lipid-nomenclature-standardisation
skills.search_text: lipid-nomenclature-standardisation Use when an annotated m/z feature table contains raw lipid annotation strings (e.g. multi-isomer entries in an all_IsomerNames-style column) that must be collapsed into standard lipid categories and subclasses before downstream statistics. Annotations are already standardised class-level lipid identifiers, so RefineLipids would collapse information you still need The refinement goal is pathway-correlation prioritisation of annotations rather than nomenclature simplification — use SpaMTP's CalculateAnnotationStatistics / CalculateSingleAnnotationStatistics instead The annotation strings are non-lipid metabolites that rgoslin's lipid nomenclature parser cannot resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Standardises free-text lipid annotations (e.g. PC(34:1), SM(34:1)) into common lipid categories and classes using SpaMTP's RefineLipids function, which parses lipid names via rgoslin and maps them to the simplified 'lipid_info' level. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Standardises free-text lipid annotations (e.g. PC(34:1), SM(34:1)) into common lipid categories and classes using SpaMTP's RefineLipids function, which parses lipid names via rgoslin and maps them to the simplified 'lipid_info' level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotations are already standardised class-level lipid identifiers, so RefineLipids would collapse information you still need The refinement goal is pathway-correlation prioritisation of annotations rather than nomenclature simplification — use SpaMTP's CalculateAnnotationStatistics / CalculateSingleAnnotationStatistics instead The annotation strings are non-lipid metabolites that rgoslin's lipid nomenclature parser cannot resolve

skills.description: Use when the input is a set of FDR-controlled METASPACE formula-adduct annotations from imaging MS (MS1-only data where isomers/isobars cannot be resolved) and the goal is overrepresentation of lipid-ontology (LION) terms.
skills.name: lipid-ontology-enrichment
skills.search_text: lipid-ontology-enrichment Use when the input is a set of FDR-controlled METASPACE formula-adduct annotations from imaging MS (MS1-only data where isomers/isobars cannot be resolved) and the goal is overrepresentation of lipid-ontology (LION) terms. The molecular identities are unambiguous (e.g. MS/MS-validated structures), where conventional ORA without bootstrapping suffices The target biology is pathways/metabolite sets rather than lipid classes — use MSEA or non-lipid backgrounds instead of the LION lipid ontology Input is raw imaging MS data rather than FDR-controlled METASPACE annotations — annotate first (e.g. METASPACE at 10% FDR) before enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Perform overrepresentation analysis of lipid-ontology (LION) terms on METASPACE imaging-MS annotations using S2IsoMEr, with bootstrapping to propagate isomeric/isobaric ambiguity. The skill is demonstrated on the mouse brain spatial metabolomics dataset 2022-05-31_10h46m34s annotated against the CoreMetabolome database at 10% FDR. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf100
skills.summary: Perform overrepresentation analysis of lipid-ontology (LION) terms on METASPACE imaging-MS annotations using S2IsoMEr, with bootstrapping to propagate isomeric/isobaric ambiguity. The skill is demonstrated on the mouse brain spatial metabolomics dataset 2022-05-31_10h46m34s annotated against the CoreMetabolome database at 10% FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecular identities are unambiguous (e.g. MS/MS-validated structures), where conventional ORA without bootstrapping suffices The target biology is pathways/metabolite sets rather than lipid classes — use MSEA or non-lipid backgrounds instead of the LION lipid ontology Input is raw imaging MS data rather than FDR-controlled METASPACE annotations — annotate first (e.g. METASPACE at 10% FDR) before enrichment

skills.description: Use when the query set is a list of lipid species (e.g., PA(18:0/16:0), TG(16:0/16:0/16:0), GlcCer(d18:0/24:0)) rather than KEGG metabolites, and enrichment should be tested against lipid ontology terms instead of KEGG pathways.
skills.name: lipid-ontology-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: lipid-ontology-enrichment-analysis Use when the query set is a list of lipid species (e.g., PA(18:0/16:0), TG(16:0/16:0/16:0), GlcCer(d18:0/24:0)) rather than KEGG metabolites, and enrichment should be tested against lipid ontology terms instead of KEGG pathways. The query set consists of KEGG metabolites and the analysis target is KEGG pathway enrichment — use EnrichMet's standard KEGG workflow instead of substituting LION annotations. The analysis requires ranked-list enrichment (MetSEA/fgsea) or network/topology-based impact analysis rather than categorical over-representation of lipids. No lipid-ontology annotations can be retrieved and no user-supplied lipid pathway-to-lipid table is available — the package does not redistribute LION data, so ORA cannot proceed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Extends EnrichMet's Fisher's Exact Test over-representation framework beyond KEGG-based metabolomics to lipidomics by using lipid–ontology associations from the LION database as the pathway-to-lipid annotation source, as demonstrated in the lung cancer lipidomics case study (Figure S2). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Extends EnrichMet's Fisher's Exact Test over-representation framework beyond KEGG-based metabolomics to lipidomics by using lipid–ontology associations from the LION database as the pathway-to-lipid annotation source, as demonstrated in the lung cancer lipidomics case study (Figure S2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query set consists of KEGG metabolites and the analysis target is KEGG pathway enrichment — use EnrichMet's standard KEGG workflow instead of substituting LION annotations. The analysis requires ranked-list enrichment (MetSEA/fgsea) or network/topology-based impact analysis rather than categorical over-representation of lipids. No lipid-ontology annotations can be retrieved and no user-supplied lipid pathway-to-lipid table is available — the package does not redistribute LION data, so ORA cannot proceed.

skills.description: Use when a lipid annotation list (e.g. abbreviations like PC 16:0_18:2) needs identifiers for downstream ontology (LION), pathway (KEGG, Rhea), or network/interaction (UniProtKB, ChEBI) analysis.
skills.name: lipid-ontology-id-mapping
skills.search_text: lipid-ontology-id-mapping Use when a lipid annotation list (e.g. abbreviations like PC 16:0_18:2) needs identifiers for downstream ontology (LION), pathway (KEGG, Rhea), or network/interaction (UniProtKB, ChEBI) analysis. Input lipids are plant or bacterial — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes in five categories (fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) The goal is only format normalization between annotation styles (e.g. LIPID MAPS to RefMet) — the Converter/Equalizer modules suffice; the Linker is for ontology/pathway/network identifier retrieval No network access is available, since the Linker must query external databases (ChEBI, KEGG, Rhea, UniProtKB) online http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Maps experimental lipid annotations to ontology, pathway, and network identifiers (LION, KEGG compound, ChEBI, Rhea reaction, UniProtKB protein) using the LipidLynxX Linker module, closing the gap between lipidomics ID lists and systems biology tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Maps experimental lipid annotations to ontology, pathway, and network identifiers (LION, KEGG compound, ChEBI, Rhea reaction, UniProtKB protein) using the LipidLynxX Linker module, closing the gap between lipidomics ID lists and systems biology tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lipids are plant or bacterial — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes in five categories (fatty acids, glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, sterols) The goal is only format normalization between annotation styles (e.g. LIPID MAPS to RefMet) — the Converter/Equalizer modules suffice; the Linker is for ontology/pathway/network identifier retrieval No network access is available, since the Linker must query external databases (ChEBI, KEGG, Rhea, UniProtKB) online

skills.description: Use when you have a peak-picked feature table (e.g., MZmine CSV with m/z, RT, intensities) and in silico lipid precursor libraries, and need candidate lipid/adduct assignments per feature before MS/MS fragment confirmation.
skills.name: lipid-precursor-exact-mass-matching
skills.search_text: lipid-precursor-exact-mass-matching Use when you have a peak-picked feature table (e.g., MZmine CSV with m/z, RT, intensities) and in silico lipid precursor libraries, and need candidate lipid/adduct assignments per feature before MS/MS fragment confirmation. The goal is MS/MS fragment-level confirmation or identification-level assignment (LipidMatch Steps 2-7) — this skill only produces MS1-level candidate matches Input is raw vendor MS files rather than a peak-picked feature table; run MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS feature detection first Waters instrument files are involved — the README states LipidMatch does not currently support Waters files http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Links each peak-picked feature (m/z, RT, intensities) to candidate lipid species by exact mass matching the feature's m/z against in silico precursor ions from LipidMatch's fragmentation libraries at the MS1 level (Step 1 of the LipidMatch workflow), using a user-defined m/z tolerance in Da. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Links each peak-picked feature (m/z, RT, intensities) to candidate lipid species by exact mass matching the feature's m/z against in silico precursor ions from LipidMatch's fragmentation libraries at the MS1 level (Step 1 of the LipidMatch workflow), using a user-defined m/z tolerance in Da.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is MS/MS fragment-level confirmation or identification-level assignment (LipidMatch Steps 2-7) — this skill only produces MS1-level candidate matches Input is raw vendor MS files rather than a peak-picked feature table; run MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS feature detection first Waters instrument files are involved — the README states LipidMatch does not currently support Waters files

skills.description: Use when a generated lipid/precursor library from Lipid Spectrum Generator must be handed to data-dependent acquisition instrumentation (Excalibur/Orbitrap) or to Skyline as a .CSV precursor or transition list.
skills.name: lipid-precursor-list-export
skills.search_text: lipid-precursor-list-export Use when a generated lipid/precursor library from Lipid Spectrum Generator must be handed to data-dependent acquisition instrumentation (Excalibur/Orbitrap) or to Skyline as a .CSV precursor or transition list. The goal is to export an in silico spectral library itself for lipid identification — in that case export with the '.MSP' file extension selected instead. The instrument acquisition workflow is not DDA on an Orbitrap and no Skyline transition list is needed — the Excalibur-compatible precursor list convention does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Exports lipid spectral library entries from the Lipid Spectrum Generator as a .CSV file, yielding either an Excalibur-compatible precursor list for DDA analysis on the Orbitrap or a Skyline-compatible transition list. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c04518
skills.summary: Exports lipid spectral library entries from the Lipid Spectrum Generator as a .CSV file, yielding either an Excalibur-compatible precursor list for DDA analysis on the Orbitrap or a Skyline-compatible transition list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to export an in silico spectral library itself for lipid identification — in that case export with the '.MSP' file extension selected instead. The instrument acquisition workflow is not DDA on an Orbitrap and no Skyline transition list is needed — the Excalibur-compatible precursor list convention does not apply.

skills.description: Use when designing targeted lipidomics PRM/MRM assays: you need to compute monoisotopic precursor m/z and diagnostic fragment masses from lipid class definitions, fatty acyl chains, and adducts, or generate transition lists for Skyline.
skills.name: lipid-precursor-mass-computation
skills.search_text: lipid-precursor-mass-computation Use when designing targeted lipidomics PRM/MRM assays: you need to compute monoisotopic precursor m/z and diagnostic fragment masses from lipid class definitions, fatty acyl chains, and adducts, or generate transition lists for Skyline. Your input is already a validated transition list or spectral library — LipidCreator does not re-score or re-calculate existing assays. You need automated false discovery rate scoring or handling of coeluting/isobaric lipids — LipidCreator intentionally does not address this. Your targets are bacterial (e.g. E. coli acyl-PG, acyl-PE) or archaeal lipids — no standards exist and the current knowledge base is eukaryotic-focused. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reconstructs LipidCreator's knowledge-base-driven assembly of lipid building blocks (head groups, fatty acyls, adducts) into precursor and fragment masses for over 61 lipid classes, emitting targeted-assay transition lists covering ~10^12 lipid molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Reconstructs LipidCreator's knowledge-base-driven assembly of lipid building blocks (head groups, fatty acyls, adducts) into precursor and fragment masses for over 61 lipid classes, emitting targeted-assay transition lists covering ~10^12 lipid molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a validated transition list or spectral library — LipidCreator does not re-score or re-calculate existing assays. You need automated false discovery rate scoring or handling of coeluting/isobaric lipids — LipidCreator intentionally does not address this. Your targets are bacterial (e.g. E. coli acyl-PG, acyl-PE) or archaeal lipids — no standards exist and the current knowledge base is eukaryotic-focused.

skills.description: Use when a LipidCreator-generated transition list has been measured as PRM/SRM triplicate LC-MS/MS injections (e.g., 5 µL, Q-Exactive HF or QTRAP 6500) and you must quantify targeted plasma lipids, filter species by curve linearity and precision, and compare to NIST SRM 1950.
skills.name: lipid-quantification-qc-curve-validation
skills.search_text: lipid-quantification-qc-curve-validation Use when a LipidCreator-generated transition list has been measured as PRM/SRM triplicate LC-MS/MS injections (e.g., 5 µL, Q-Exactive HF or QTRAP 6500) and you must quantify targeted plasma lipids, filter species by curve linearity and precision, and compare to NIST SRM 1950. The analysis is untargeted/screening or DIA-based without a LipidCreator-designed transition list and calibration curves — LipidCreator is for targeted lipidomics assay development and intentionally does not address peak area integration or coeluting/isobaric lipids Input is already a QC-filtered feature table with no replicate injections, so per-species CV < 20% and calibration-curve R² > 0.8 cannot be computed The analytes are not lipids (e.g., lipid mediators outside the covered classes or bacterial/archaeal lipids lacking standards), since the CE models cover only a subset of lipid classes and the majority of eukaryotic lipid classes have some exceptions http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 QC-validates a LipidCreator/Skyline targeted lipidomics quantification by retaining only lipid species with linear response R² > 0.8 and triplicate CV < 20%, then benchmarking quantification against NIST SRM 1950 reference material via log-transformed Pearson correlation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: QC-validates a LipidCreator/Skyline targeted lipidomics quantification by retaining only lipid species with linear response R² > 0.8 and triplicate CV < 20%, then benchmarking quantification against NIST SRM 1950 reference material via log-transformed Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is untargeted/screening or DIA-based without a LipidCreator-designed transition list and calibration curves — LipidCreator is for targeted lipidomics assay development and intentionally does not address peak area integration or coeluting/isobaric lipids Input is already a QC-filtered feature table with no replicate injections, so per-species CV < 20% and calibration-curve R² > 0.8 cannot be computed The analytes are not lipids (e.g., lipid mediators outside the covered classes or bacterial/archaeal lipids lacking standards), since the CE models cover only a subset of lipid classes and the majority of eukaryotic lipid classes have some exceptions

skills.name: lipid-refmet-analyte-class-mapping
skills.search_text: lipid-refmet-analyte-class-mapping Use when a user-supplied analyte list or uploaded measurement table must be matched to ALISTER's stability database — e. When the user's analytes use a naming scheme that is neither lipid shorthand nomenclature (for lipids) nor RefMet nomenclature (for polar metabolites) and cannot be reconciled — the app requires names matched against its underlying database When the uploaded .csv is not in tabular form with sample names in rows and analyte names in columns, since the app requires that structure and will not alter or store the data When the goal is prospective protocol planning or retrospective stability assessment for a single, individually named analyte in Analyte search rather than class-based or bulk mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Maps lipid and polar-metabolite analyte names in user datasets to ALISTER's underlying stability database by matching against lipid shorthand nomenclature (lipids) and RefMet nomenclature (polar metabolites), so that analytes can be grouped by main class for class-based selection and stability queries. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cca.2024.117858
skills.summary: Maps lipid and polar-metabolite analyte names in user datasets to ALISTER's underlying stability database by matching against lipid shorthand nomenclature (lipids) and RefMet nomenclature (polar metabolites), so that analytes can be grouped by main class for class-based selection and stability queries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the user's analytes use a naming scheme that is neither lipid shorthand nomenclature (for lipids) nor RefMet nomenclature (for polar metabolites) and cannot be reconciled — the app requires names matched against its underlying database When the uploaded .csv is not in tabular form with sample names in rows and analyte names in columns, since the app requires that structure and will not alter or store the data When the goal is prospective protocol planning or retrospective stability assessment for a single, individually named analyte in Analyte search rather than class-based or bulk mapping

skills.description: Use when you have a processed lipidomics table (one lipid identifier per row, one sample per column, e.g. from pandas.read_excel) and need to reprocess analyte annotations into per-sample fatty acid residue abundances rather than individual molecular lipid levels.
skills.name: lipid-residue-extraction
skills.search_text: lipid-residue-extraction Use when you have a processed lipidomics table (one lipid identifier per row, one sample per column, e.g. from pandas.read_excel) and need to reprocess analyte annotations into per-sample fatty acid residue abundances rather than individual molecular lipid levels. The input is raw mass-spectrometry data (mzML, centroided peaks) rather than a processed, final lipidomic data table — liputils parses textual lipid identifiers, not spectra. The analysis goal is tracking individual molecular lipid species or ratios rather than aggregate fatty acid residue composition (residue extraction deliberately discards the lipid class context). Lipid identifiers cannot be interpreted by the parser (neither generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M' format, isomer groups, nor RefMet names) and cannot be batch-translated with RefMet's online translator — residues may be silently wrong or dropped. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extract individual fatty acid residues (e.g. 18:1, 20:4, 26:0) from processed lipidomic data tables using the liputils Python module, which parses lipid string identifiers from RefMet-compliant or generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M/...' formats into residue counts in submolar fractions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70259-9
skills.summary: Extract individual fatty acid residues (e.g. 18:1, 20:4, 26:0) from processed lipidomic data tables using the liputils Python module, which parses lipid string identifiers from RefMet-compliant or generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M/...' formats into residue counts in submolar fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw mass-spectrometry data (mzML, centroided peaks) rather than a processed, final lipidomic data table — liputils parses textual lipid identifiers, not spectra. The analysis goal is tracking individual molecular lipid species or ratios rather than aggregate fatty acid residue composition (residue extraction deliberately discards the lipid class context). Lipid identifiers cannot be interpreted by the parser (neither generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M' format, isomer groups, nor RefMet names) and cannot be batch-translated with RefMet's online translator — residues may be silently wrong or dropped.

skills.description: Use when you have annotated lipid identities paired with LC-MS retention times in one or more datasets and want to quantify conformity of the ECN/IUP/ESCN relative RT ordering rules.
skills.name: lipid-retention-time-rule-implementation
skills.search_text: lipid-retention-time-rule-implementation Use when you have annotated lipid identities paired with LC-MS retention times in one or more datasets and want to quantify conformity of the ECN/IUP/ESCN relative RT ordering rules. Do not use for direct MS/MS spectral annotation or false-positive removal — that is the province of LipidIN's annotation pipeline, not the RT rule benchmark Do not use when only raw MS data without lipid annotation (subclass, chain length, double-bond counts) is available; the rules require already-annotated lipid identities Do not use for absolute RT prediction from chemical structure alone (e.g., for de novo retention modelling) — this skill evaluates relative ordering consistency, not absolute RT prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A benchmark skill for evaluating how consistently the three relative retention-time rules (ECN, IUP, ESCN) hold across lipid subclasses in LC-MS/MS datasets, computing per-dataset conformity fractions and average absolute RT deviation rates (1.44% for ECN, 1.28% for ESCN). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: A benchmark skill for evaluating how consistently the three relative retention-time rules (ECN, IUP, ESCN) hold across lipid subclasses in LC-MS/MS datasets, computing per-dataset conformity fractions and average absolute RT deviation rates (1.44% for ECN, 1.28% for ESCN).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use for direct MS/MS spectral annotation or false-positive removal — that is the province of LipidIN's annotation pipeline, not the RT rule benchmark Do not use when only raw MS data without lipid annotation (subclass, chain length, double-bond counts) is available; the rules require already-annotated lipid identities Do not use for absolute RT prediction from chemical structure alone (e.g., for de novo retention modelling) — this skill evaluates relative ordering consistency, not absolute RT prediction

skills.description: Use when a lipid feature table with identifications, retention times, and fatty acyl compositions needs per-class RT plausibility checks or filtering of likely incorrect identifications.
skills.name: lipid-rt-ecn-regression-modeling
skills.search_text: lipid-rt-ecn-regression-modeling Use when a lipid feature table with identifications, retention times, and fatty acyl compositions needs per-class RT plausibility checks or filtering of likely incorrect identifications. Input is a raw MS file or unannotated peak table with no lipid identifications and fatty acyl compositions — the regression needs parsed FA carbon counts and unsaturations per class The goal is generic chromatographic peak detection or alignment rather than lipid-identification plausibility QC A lipid class has fewer than the minimum examples (default 5), making a per-class regression unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Per-lipid-class regression of retention time against fatty acyl composition (RT ~ FA carbons + alkene unsaturations, i.e., effective carbon number vs. RT modeling) as implemented in the LipiDex 2 Degreaser QC module to flag identifications with large deviation from predicted RT. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Per-lipid-class regression of retention time against fatty acyl composition (RT ~ FA carbons + alkene unsaturations, i.e., effective carbon number vs. RT modeling) as implemented in the LipiDex 2 Degreaser QC module to flag identifications with large deviation from predicted RT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw MS file or unannotated peak table with no lipid identifications and fatty acyl compositions — the regression needs parsed FA carbon counts and unsaturations per class The goal is generic chromatographic peak detection or alignment rather than lipid-identification plausibility QC A lipid class has fewer than the minimum examples (default 5), making a per-class regression unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have a LipidSigR differential-expression output table of lipid species and want to test whether a priori-defined lipid sets (e.g., lipid classes like Cer, TAG, PC O-) show statistically significant, concordant differences between two biological states (e.g., phenotypes).
skills.name: lipid-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: lipid-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a LipidSigR differential-expression output table of lipid species and want to test whether a priori-defined lipid sets (e.g., lipid classes like Cer, TAG, PC O-) show statistically significant, concordant differences between two biological states (e.g., phenotypes). The analysis goal is testing over-representation of a pre-selected significant lipid list rather than a ranked full lipidome — use LipidSigR's ORA approach instead The input is raw lipidomics intensity data that has not yet been processed through the Differential Expression workflow — LSEA requires differential-expression results as input The data are multi-group: enrichment interpretation in the surfaced case study is case-versus-control, and Network/Machine-learning-style two-group constraints signal this package's two-group orientation http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Run Lipid Set Enrichment Analysis (LSEA) with LipidSigR to rank differential-expression results (e.g., by p-value) and identify lipid classes — such as TAGs, PC O-, or Ceramides — enriched among up- or down-regulated lipid species, then visualize the results with dedicated LSEA plots. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf047
skills.summary: Run Lipid Set Enrichment Analysis (LSEA) with LipidSigR to rank differential-expression results (e.g., by p-value) and identify lipid classes — such as TAGs, PC O-, or Ceramides — enriched among up- or down-regulated lipid species, then visualize the results with dedicated LSEA plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is testing over-representation of a pre-selected significant lipid list rather than a ranked full lipidome — use LipidSigR's ORA approach instead The input is raw lipidomics intensity data that has not yet been processed through the Differential Expression workflow — LSEA requires differential-expression results as input The data are multi-group: enrichment interpretation in the surfaced case study is case-versus-control, and Network/Machine-learning-style two-group constraints signal this package's two-group orientation

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics dataset (Skyline export, numerical matrix, or Metabolomics Workbench file) has been differentially analyzed with lipidr and you need to know which lipid classes or chain characteristics are enriched in the regulated lipids.
skills.name: lipid-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: lipid-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a lipidomics dataset (Skyline export, numerical matrix, or Metabolomics Workbench file) has been differentially analyzed with lipidr and you need to know which lipid classes or chain characteristics are enriched in the regulated lipids. Input lipids are not annotated with class/chain information — LSEA depends on lipidr automatically inferring lipid class and chain information from lipid names The goal is gene/protein set enrichment rather than lipid-annotation-set enrichment — LSEA tests lipid classes, chain lengths or unsaturation patterns, not gene sets No differential or ranking statistics exist yet — lsea requires ranked lipids (e.g. by logFC) from a prior differential analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Run lipidr's novel Lipid Set Enrichment Analysis (LSEA) to detect preferential enrichment of lipid classes, total chain lengths or unsaturation patterns among ranked differentially expressed lipids, and visualize the enrichment results. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00082
skills.summary: Run lipidr's novel Lipid Set Enrichment Analysis (LSEA) to detect preferential enrichment of lipid classes, total chain lengths or unsaturation patterns among ranked differentially expressed lipids, and visualize the enrichment results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lipids are not annotated with class/chain information — LSEA depends on lipidr automatically inferring lipid class and chain information from lipid names The goal is gene/protein set enrichment rather than lipid-annotation-set enrichment — LSEA tests lipid classes, chain lengths or unsaturation patterns, not gene sets No differential or ranking statistics exist yet — lsea requires ranked lipids (e.g. by logFC) from a prior differential analysis

skills.description: Use when lipid identifiers arrive as heterogeneous shorthand names (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or search-engine dialects from LipidXplorer, LDA, MS-DIAL) and must be converted to a canonical, machine-comparable structure before distance computation or structural comparison.
skills.name: lipid-shorthand-name-parsing
skills.search_text: lipid-shorthand-name-parsing Use when lipid identifiers arrive as heterogeneous shorthand names (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or search-engine dialects from LipidXplorer, LDA, MS-DIAL) and must be converted to a canonical, machine-comparable structure before distance computation or structural comparison. Input is already a canonical structural representation (e.g., SMILES or atom/bond graphs) rather than a shorthand lipid name The lipid names are free-text descriptions or non-standard abbreviations that Goslin's grammars cannot tokenize — the parser will fail rather than produce a reliable structure The analysis only requires exact name matching between lipidomes and no structural comparison, in which case parsing to structures is unnecessary overhead Parses and standardizes lipid shorthand names (e.g., FA 18:2(9Z,12Z), PC 18:0_16:1) into structured components — headgroup, fatty acyl chains, DB positions and sn-positions — using the Goslin grammar implementation (cppgoslin), which LipidSpace embeds as the first step of every analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Parses and standardizes lipid shorthand names (e.g., FA 18:2(9Z,12Z), PC 18:0_16:1) into structured components — headgroup, fatty acyl chains, DB positions and sn-positions — using the Goslin grammar implementation (cppgoslin), which LipidSpace embeds as the first step of every analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a canonical structural representation (e.g., SMILES or atom/bond graphs) rather than a shorthand lipid name The lipid names are free-text descriptions or non-standard abbreviations that Goslin's grammars cannot tokenize — the parser will fail rather than produce a reliable structure The analysis only requires exact name matching between lipidomes and no structural comparison, in which case parsing to structures is unnecessary overhead

skills.name: lipid-shorthand-nomenclature-tokenization
skills.search_text: lipid-shorthand-nomenclature-tokenization Use when labeled lipid species strings (e.g. from HDF5 'lipid_species' attributes) must be decomposed into headgroup/fatty-acyl/adduct tokens for seq2seq training, per-component accuracy scoring, or token-level prediction comparison. Input is raw profile spectra (mzML) without lipid species labels — tokenization only applies to named lipid species, not unlabeled prediction-mode files Species names use legacy or divergent nomenclatures that have not been reconciled to the updated lipid shorthand notation, since token boundaries will not align with the training vocabulary The goal is spectral preprocessing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, m/z 50–1600 trimming) rather than label/prediction handling Splits molecular lipid species names in updated lipid shorthand notation into discrete tokens — headgroup, fatty acid side chains, and adduct — so each token can be embedded as a transformer decoder label (and parsed back from predictions) in LipiDetective. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.07.617094
skills.summary: Splits molecular lipid species names in updated lipid shorthand notation into discrete tokens — headgroup, fatty acid side chains, and adduct — so each token can be embedded as a transformer decoder label (and parsed back from predictions) in LipiDetective.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw profile spectra (mzML) without lipid species labels — tokenization only applies to named lipid species, not unlabeled prediction-mode files Species names use legacy or divergent nomenclatures that have not been reconciled to the updated lipid shorthand notation, since token boundaries will not align with the training vocabulary The goal is spectral preprocessing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, m/z 50–1600 trimming) rather than label/prediction handling
