skills.description: Use when running LipiDetective prediction on MS2 spectra and you have raw decoded token sequences (headgroup, fatty-acid chain, adduct, end-of-sequence tokens from the 1,032-token vocabulary) that must be converted to lipid shorthand notation strings with confidence values.
skills.name: lipid-shorthand-token-reassembly
skills.search_text: lipid-shorthand-token-reassembly Use when running LipiDetective prediction on MS2 spectra and you have raw decoded token sequences (headgroup, fatty-acid chain, adduct, end-of-sequence tokens from the 1,032-token vocabulary) that must be converted to lipid shorthand notation strings with confidence values. Input is already a complete, human-readable lipid annotation string or a database entry (e.g. from LipiDex or Compound Discoverer 3.1) — no token reassembly is needed. The task is raw spectra preprocessing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, m/z 50–1600 trimming, base peak normalization) rather than post-decoding formatting. Working with the training/HDF5 pipeline where spectra are stored as arrays rather than decoded predictions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Reassemble the token-by-token output of LipiDetective's transformer decoder into the lipid shorthand notation string (e.g. 'PC 16:0_18:1 [M+HCOO]-') and attach a confidence score, applying the 0.98 threshold before exporting results as CSV. This is the final formatting/validation layer of the autoregressive decoding pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.07.617094
skills.summary: Reassemble the token-by-token output of LipiDetective's transformer decoder into the lipid shorthand notation string (e.g. 'PC 16:0_18:1 [M+HCOO]-') and attach a confidence score, applying the 0.98 threshold before exporting results as CSV. This is the final formatting/validation layer of the autoregressive decoding pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a complete, human-readable lipid annotation string or a database entry (e.g. from LipiDex or Compound Discoverer 3.1) — no token reassembly is needed. The task is raw spectra preprocessing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, m/z 50–1600 trimming, base peak normalization) rather than post-decoding formatting. Working with the training/HDF5 pipeline where spectra are stored as arrays rather than decoded predictions.

skills.description: Use when raw lipid identification/quantification files from LipidSearch or LIQUID (or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment) must be converted into a structured table of lipid class, chain length, and double-bond strata before normalization or differential analysis.
skills.name: lipid-species-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: lipid-species-annotation-parsing Use when raw lipid identification/quantification files from LipidSearch or LIQUID (or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment) must be converted into a structured table of lipid class, chain length, and double-bond strata before normalization or differential analysis. Input is already a parsed, boundary-filtered abundance/concentration matrix rather than raw vendor (LipidSearch/LIQUID) identification and quantification output The experiment data are not in a format ADViSELipidomics handles (LipidSearch, LIQUID, or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment retrievable via the metabolomicsWorkbenchR do_query() function) The goal is purely statistical analysis of an existing parsed table with no need to re-stratify species into class/chain/double-bond fields http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses lipid species identifiers from vendor lipidomics outputs (LipidSearch, LIQUID, Metabolomics Workbench) using the LIPID MAPS classification, stratifying each species into class, chain length/carbon-atom count, and double-bond count, and pre-filters species against internal reference boundaries before downstream normalization. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac706
skills.summary: Parses lipid species identifiers from vendor lipidomics outputs (LipidSearch, LIQUID, Metabolomics Workbench) using the LIPID MAPS classification, stratifying each species into class, chain length/carbon-atom count, and double-bond count, and pre-filters species against internal reference boundaries before downstream normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a parsed, boundary-filtered abundance/concentration matrix rather than raw vendor (LipidSearch/LIQUID) identification and quantification output The experiment data are not in a format ADViSELipidomics handles (LipidSearch, LIQUID, or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment retrievable via the metabolomicsWorkbenchR do_query() function) The goal is purely statistical analysis of an existing parsed table with no need to re-stratify species into class/chain/double-bond fields

skills.description: Use when preprocessing vendor lipidomics output (e.g., LipidSearch or LIQUID tables) whose lipid species names must be validated against class-specific carbon-atom and double-bond limits before downstream normalization or statistical analysis.
skills.name: lipid-species-boundary-filtering
skills.search_text: lipid-species-boundary-filtering Use when preprocessing vendor lipidomics output (e.g., LipidSearch or LIQUID tables) whose lipid species names must be validated against class-specific carbon-atom and double-bond limits before downstream normalization or statistical analysis. Input data comes directly from the Metabolomics Workbench rather than LipidSearch/LIQUID vendor outputs whose species names need boundary validation. The lipid matrix is already a validated feature table — re-running boundary filtering could remove legitimate species. The analysis goal is differential abundance testing or batch effect correction, which presuppose that boundary filtering has already been applied. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A preprocessing step in ADViSELipidomics that parses lipid species identifiers using LIPID MAPS classification (class, total carbons, double-bond count) and removes species violating double-bond or carbon-atom boundaries defined in an internal reference file, duplicating entries, or having odd-chain structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac706
skills.summary: A preprocessing step in ADViSELipidomics that parses lipid species identifiers using LIPID MAPS classification (class, total carbons, double-bond count) and removes species violating double-bond or carbon-atom boundaries defined in an internal reference file, duplicating entries, or having odd-chain structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data comes directly from the Metabolomics Workbench rather than LipidSearch/LIQUID vendor outputs whose species names need boundary validation. The lipid matrix is already a validated feature table — re-running boundary filtering could remove legitimate species. The analysis goal is differential abundance testing or batch effect correction, which presuppose that boundary filtering has already been applied.

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics identification module needs a comprehensive predicted lipid database spanning class and composition space beyond available experimental CCS/RT collections, especially for HILIC-IM-MS workflows.
skills.name: lipid-species-enumeration-fatty-acyl-chain-space
skills.search_text: lipid-species-enumeration-fatty-acyl-chain-space Use when a lipidomics identification module needs a comprehensive predicted lipid database spanning class and composition space beyond available experimental CCS/RT collections, especially for HILIC-IM-MS workflows. The analysis only needs identifications against experimentally measured values — the experimental database of m/z and CCS of 45 lipid classes (23 with HILIC retention times) already covers the query, and predicted entries would be unnecessary. The lipid space of interest falls outside the enumeration grid — e.g., acyl chains shorter than 10 or longer than 30 carbons, more than 6 degrees of unsaturation, or lipid classes not defined in the LipidMass-based 31-class set. The input is already an observed feature list (m/z, CCS, RT) requiring lipid identification at different confidence levels rather than generation of a theoretical species database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Systematically enumerates lipid species for LipidMass-defined lipid classes by combining fatty acyl chain lengths (10–30 carbons, even and odd) and degrees of unsaturation (0–6), then attaches theoretical m/z values (ESI adducts such as [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-), predicted CCS values (22 classes) and predicted HILIC retention times (23 classes) to build a broad predicted lipid database of 145,388 entries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560
skills.summary: Systematically enumerates lipid species for LipidMass-defined lipid classes by combining fatty acyl chain lengths (10–30 carbons, even and odd) and degrees of unsaturation (0–6), then attaches theoretical m/z values (ESI adducts such as [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-), predicted CCS values (22 classes) and predicted HILIC retention times (23 classes) to build a broad predicted lipid database of 145,388 entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only needs identifications against experimentally measured values — the experimental database of m/z and CCS of 45 lipid classes (23 with HILIC retention times) already covers the query, and predicted entries would be unnecessary. The lipid space of interest falls outside the enumeration grid — e.g., acyl chains shorter than 10 or longer than 30 carbons, more than 6 degrees of unsaturation, or lipid classes not defined in the LipidMass-based 31-class set. The input is already an observed feature list (m/z, CCS, RT) requiring lipid identification at different confidence levels rather than generation of a theoretical species database.

skills.description: Use when a completed Lipid Spectrum Generator run (lipids enumerated by class and fatty-acid composition, spectra per adduct) must be written out as a '.MSP' spectral library for downstream LC-MS/MS lipid identification.
skills.name: lipid-spectra-library-formatting
skills.search_text: lipid-spectra-library-formatting Use when a completed Lipid Spectrum Generator run (lipids enumerated by class and fatty-acid composition, spectra per adduct) must be written out as a '.MSP' spectral library for downstream LC-MS/MS lipid identification. The goal is an Excalibur-compatible precursor list for Orbitrap DDA analysis or a Skyline-compatible transition list — in that case select '.CSV' instead of '.MSP'. Only experimental (non-in-silico) spectra are involved and no on-demand spectral library generation by lipid class, fatty acid composition, or adduct is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Export the lipid spectra generated by the Lipid Spectrum Generator as a spectral-library file using the '.MSP' extension, the format consumed by LC-MS/MS lipid identification search engines. Alternatives (.CSV precursor/transition lists) are handled separately. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c04518
skills.summary: Export the lipid spectra generated by the Lipid Spectrum Generator as a spectral-library file using the '.MSP' extension, the format consumed by LC-MS/MS lipid identification search engines. Alternatives (.CSV precursor/transition lists) are handled separately.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is an Excalibur-compatible precursor list for Orbitrap DDA analysis or a Skyline-compatible transition list — in that case select '.CSV' instead of '.MSP'. Only experimental (non-in-silico) spectra are involved and no on-demand spectral library generation by lipid class, fatty acid composition, or adduct is needed.

skills.description: Use when constructing a reference spectral library for lipid identification in liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and experimental library entries are missing or need custom lipid classes/adducts.
skills.name: lipid-spectral-library-generation
skills.search_text: lipid-spectral-library-generation Use when constructing a reference spectral library for lipid identification in liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and experimental library entries are missing or need custom lipid classes/adducts. An experimental, curated spectral library already covers the lipid classes and adducts of interest — enumerating additional in silico species is unnecessary and may introduce false identifications. The analysis goal is small-molecule (non-lipid) metabolite identification; LSG's fragmentation patterns are built specifically for lipid classes and their fatty acid compositions. Downstream software cannot read '.MSP' or '.CSV' precursor/transition lists — verify import compatibility before generating a large library. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generate on-demand in silico lipid (mass)spectral libraries using the open-source Lipid Spectrum Generator (LSG), which enumerates lipid species by lipid class and fatty acid composition and then computes fragmentation spectra per lipid adduct, exporting them as .MSP libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c04518
skills.summary: Generate on-demand in silico lipid (mass)spectral libraries using the open-source Lipid Spectrum Generator (LSG), which enumerates lipid species by lipid class and fatty acid composition and then computes fragmentation spectra per lipid adduct, exporting them as .MSP libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: An experimental, curated spectral library already covers the lipid classes and adducts of interest — enumerating additional in silico species is unnecessary and may introduce false identifications. The analysis goal is small-molecule (non-lipid) metabolite identification; LSG's fragmentation patterns are built specifically for lipid classes and their fatty acid compositions. Downstream software cannot read '.MSP' or '.CSV' precursor/transition lists — verify import compatibility before generating a large library.

skills.description: Use when a downstream acquisition or analysis workflow (e.g. Skyline transition lists for targeted MS, or Excalibur precursor lists for Orbitrap DDA) needs lipid species generated by class, fatty-acid composition, and adduct in an importable file format.
skills.name: lipid-spectrum-generator-export-configuration
skills.search_text: lipid-spectrum-generator-export-configuration Use when a downstream acquisition or analysis workflow (e.g. Skyline transition lists for targeted MS, or Excalibur precursor lists for Orbitrap DDA) needs lipid species generated by class, fatty-acid composition, and adduct in an importable file format. The downstream tool expects a spectral-library file rather than a transition/precursor list — export with the default '.MSP' extension instead of '.CSV'. The lipid class, fatty-acid composition, or adduct combination has not yet been generated in LSG — export configuration cannot proceed without generated spectra. The consuming software requires a format other than Skyline transitions, Excalibur precursor lists, or '.MSP' libraries, since LSG only documents these export options. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Configures the Lipid Spectrum Generator (LSG) to export its in silico lipid spectral libraries in the right file format: '.MSP' for spectral-library output, or '.CSV' for a Skyline-compatible transition list or Excalibur-compatible precursor list for DDA analysis on an Orbitrap. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c04518
skills.summary: Configures the Lipid Spectrum Generator (LSG) to export its in silico lipid spectral libraries in the right file format: '.MSP' for spectral-library output, or '.CSV' for a Skyline-compatible transition list or Excalibur-compatible precursor list for DDA analysis on an Orbitrap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream tool expects a spectral-library file rather than a transition/precursor list — export with the default '.MSP' extension instead of '.CSV'. The lipid class, fatty-acid composition, or adduct combination has not yet been generated in LSG — export configuration cannot proceed without generated spectra. The consuming software requires a format other than Skyline transitions, Excalibur precursor lists, or '.MSP' libraries, since LSG only documents these export options.

skills.description: Use when comparing flux distributions between host-optimal and virus-optimal objectives in an integrated host–virus genome-scale metabolic model, especially to quantify pathway-level (lipid, sphingolipid, fatty acid) flux perturbations caused by maximal viral growth.
skills.name: lipid-sphingolipid-fatty-acid-pathway-flux-analysis
skills.search_text: lipid-sphingolipid-fatty-acid-pathway-flux-analysis Use when comparing flux distributions between host-optimal and virus-optimal objectives in an integrated host–virus genome-scale metabolic model, especially to quantify pathway-level (lipid, sphingolipid, fatty acid) flux perturbations caused by maximal viral growth. The analysis goal is chokepoint/essential-reaction drug-target identification rather than comparing flux distributions between two objective-function optima (use findCPcli bottleneck analysis instead) The model is not an integrated host–virus model with a distinct viral biomass objective, so no virus-optimum condition can be defined Only a single objective (host-only or virus-only) is of interest and no host-vs-virus flux comparison is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how host-cell metabolic fluxes in lipid, sphingolipid, and fatty-acid biosynthesis pathways shift when the SARS-CoV-2 virus is run at its optimum versus the host-optimum condition in the integrated iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 model, using FVA in COBRApy with the GLPK solver. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Quantifies how host-cell metabolic fluxes in lipid, sphingolipid, and fatty-acid biosynthesis pathways shift when the SARS-CoV-2 virus is run at its optimum versus the host-optimum condition in the integrated iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 model, using FVA in COBRApy with the GLPK solver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is chokepoint/essential-reaction drug-target identification rather than comparing flux distributions between two objective-function optima (use findCPcli bottleneck analysis instead) The model is not an integrated host–virus model with a distinct viral biomass objective, so no virus-optimum condition can be defined Only a single objective (host-only or virus-only) is of interest and no host-vs-virus flux comparison is needed

skills.description: Use when lipid species names have been parsed/standardized (e.g., via Goslin) and a pairwise structural distance/similarity matrix between all distinct lipid species is required for downstream PCA, lipidome comparison, or dendrogram clustering.
skills.name: lipid-structural-distance-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: lipid-structural-distance-matrix-computation Use when lipid species names have been parsed/standardized (e.g., via Goslin) and a pairwise structural distance/similarity matrix between all distinct lipid species is required for downstream PCA, lipidome comparison, or dendrogram clustering. The input is already a quantitative feature matrix and the goal is sample-level statistics — quantitative information is deliberately not added to this structural comparison model (abundances are only added downstream, normalized to the variance of the first PC) Lipid names are non-standardized or from heterogeneous dialects — running structural comparison without prior Goslin parsing/standardization yields invalid FA-chain comparisons Only exact species-name matching across lipidomes is needed — the article positions this skill precisely for the case where exact-name matching is insufficient, e.g., heterogeneous lipidomes Computes a pairwise structural distance matrix between lipid species by combining the maximum common subgraph (LaWeCSE) approach with the Jaccard index, forming the basis for LipidSpace's structural space models and lipidome similarity computations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes a pairwise structural distance matrix between lipid species by combining the maximum common subgraph (LaWeCSE) approach with the Jaccard index, forming the basis for LipidSpace's structural space models and lipidome similarity computations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a quantitative feature matrix and the goal is sample-level statistics — quantitative information is deliberately not added to this structural comparison model (abundances are only added downstream, normalized to the variance of the first PC) Lipid names are non-standardized or from heterogeneous dialects — running structural comparison without prior Goslin parsing/standardization yields invalid FA-chain comparisons Only exact species-name matching across lipidomes is needed — the article positions this skill precisely for the case where exact-name matching is insufficient, e.g., heterogeneous lipidomes

skills.description: Use when preparing structured inputs for the WMYn reverse-lipidomics model: lipid annotations (head group, chain length, degree of unsaturation per fatty acyl chain) must be converted into the feature representation the network consumes before MS2 fingerprint regeneration.
skills.name: lipid-structural-feature-encoding
skills.search_text: lipid-structural-feature-encoding Use when preparing structured inputs for the WMYn reverse-lipidomics model: lipid annotations (head group, chain length, degree of unsaturation per fatty acyl chain) must be converted into the feature representation the network consumes before MS2 fingerprint regeneration. When the goal is annotating already-acquired MS2 spectra by similarity search against an existing library — use Flash Entropy Search / MS-DIAL style search instead of reverse-lipidomics encoding. When the task is double-bond localization via Paternò–Büchi derivatization, which relies on PB reaction spectra rather than structural-feature encoding. When input lipids lack resolvable chain composition/unsaturation information, since the encoding is defined over head group, chain length, and per-chain degree of unsaturation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Encodes lipid structural features — head group, fatty-acyl chain length, and degree of unsaturation of each chain — into the numeric input representation required by the WMYn (Wide-spectrum Modeling Yield network) for reverse-lipidomics fingerprint regeneration in LipidIN. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Encodes lipid structural features — head group, fatty-acyl chain length, and degree of unsaturation of each chain — into the numeric input representation required by the WMYn (Wide-spectrum Modeling Yield network) for reverse-lipidomics fingerprint regeneration in LipidIN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotating already-acquired MS2 spectra by similarity search against an existing library — use Flash Entropy Search / MS-DIAL style search instead of reverse-lipidomics encoding. When the task is double-bond localization via Paternò–Büchi derivatization, which relies on PB reaction spectra rather than structural-feature encoding. When input lipids lack resolvable chain composition/unsaturation information, since the encoding is defined over head group, chain length, and per-chain degree of unsaturation.

skills.description: Use when pairwise structural distances or similarities between lipid species must be derived from their molecular structures (e.g., to build a structural space PCA model, an arc-shaped lipid ordering, or lipidome-level similarity), rather than from exact name matches or abundances.
skills.name: lipid-structure-distance-computation-mcs-jaccard
skills.search_text: lipid-structure-distance-computation-mcs-jaccard Use when pairwise structural distances or similarities between lipid species must be derived from their molecular structures (e.g., to build a structural space PCA model, an arc-shaped lipid ordering, or lipidome-level similarity), rather than from exact name matches or abundances. The analysis only needs comparisons of lipid species by exact name/identifier matches across homogeneous lipidomes — structural distance computation is unnecessary overhead. Quantitative abundance patterns, not molecular structure, should drive the comparison — note that quantitative information is not added to the structural comparison models, which can be influenced by low-abundance lipid species. Only one fatty acyl chain class or single-chain lipids without headgroup/FA comparison semantics are involved, where LaWeCSE headgroup and sn-order-aware FA comparison rules do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes pairwise structural distances between lipid species by combining the maximum common subgraph (MCS/LaWeCSE) approach with the Jaccard index, yielding a distance = 1 - similarity in [0, 1] that underlies LipidSpace's structural space PCA models and lipidome similarity computations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes pairwise structural distances between lipid species by combining the maximum common subgraph (MCS/LaWeCSE) approach with the Jaccard index, yielding a distance = 1 - similarity in [0, 1] that underlies LipidSpace's structural space PCA models and lipidome similarity computations.

skills.search_text: lipid-structure-maximum-common-subgraph-comparison Use when pairwise structural similarity between lipid species must be quantified from molecular graphs — e.g. building a lipid distance matrix, constructing a lipid space model, or testing whether counting double-bond positions changes the overlap between two fatty acids. The task requires combining lipid abundances with structural similarity — the raw MCS comparison is purely structural and does not add quantitative information, which the article notes makes models heavily influenced by low-abundant species. Lipid species are only compared by exact name/identifier matches and no molecular structures are available, so no molecular graph can be built. An unbounded (0-to-infinity) distance is required for downstream visualization; the default bound metric ranges 0–1 and switching modes trades lipid space visibility for accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes pairwise structural similarity between lipid species by representing each lipid as a molecular graph (atoms and bonds as components) and applying a LaWeCSE-based maximum common subgraph (MCS) approach scored with the Jaccard index. Used to build the structural distance matrix underlying LipidSpace's lipid space model and to verify that double-bond (DB) position comparisons are handled correctly. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes pairwise structural similarity between lipid species by representing each lipid as a molecular graph (atoms and bonds as components) and applying a LaWeCSE-based maximum common subgraph (MCS) approach scored with the Jaccard index. Used to build the structural distance matrix underlying LipidSpace's lipid space model and to verify that double-bond (DB) position comparisons are handled correctly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires combining lipid abundances with structural similarity — the raw MCS comparison is purely structural and does not add quantitative information, which the article notes makes models heavily influenced by low-abundant species. Lipid species are only compared by exact name/identifier matches and no molecular structures are available, so no molecular graph can be built. An unbounded (0-to-infinity) distance is required for downstream visualization; the default bound metric ranges 0–1 and switching modes trades lipid space visibility for accuracy.

skills.description: Use when a published lipidomics dataset reports a known set of lipids (e.g. 2704 lipids in the mouse aging-associated lipidome atlas) and you must quantify how many are recovered by a spectral-library search.
skills.name: lipid-subclass-recall-benchmarking
skills.search_text: lipid-subclass-recall-benchmarking Use when a published lipidomics dataset reports a known set of lipids (e.g. 2704 lipids in the mouse aging-associated lipidome atlas) and you must quantify how many are recovered by a spectral-library search. The goal is discovery of novel/unannotated lipids rather than quantitative benchmarking against a known reference lipid list. The dataset lacks MS/MS spectra or retention-time information, so neither the EQ MS2 library search nor the LCI relative-RT filtering can be applied. The task is Paternò–Büchi double-bond localization, which uses LipidIN's separate PB library module rather than the general hierarchical library recall workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks lipid annotation recall of a spectral library against a reference list of reported lipids from a published dataset, comparing library variants (e.g. hierarchical level 1–4 vs 1–5) and a public-database baseline at overall and per-subclass granularity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks lipid annotation recall of a spectral library against a reference list of reported lipids from a published dataset, comparing library variants (e.g. hierarchical level 1–4 vs 1–5) and a public-database baseline at overall and per-subclass granularity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discovery of novel/unannotated lipids rather than quantitative benchmarking against a known reference lipid list. skills.description: Use when you have two or more lipidomes (e.g., csv/xlsx or mzTab-M tables with lipid species abundances) and need a global structural comparison relating all lipidomes, rather than only exact lipid-name matching.
skills.name: lipidome-hausdorff-distance-computation
skills.search_text: lipidome-hausdorff-distance-computation Use when you have two or more lipidomes (e.g., csv/xlsx or mzTab-M tables with lipid species abundances) and need a global structural comparison relating all lipidomes, rather than only exact lipid-name matching. When you only need quantitative differential-abundance statistics between sample groups rather than structural comparison across whole lipidomes — use the statistics/feature-analysis modules instead. When lipid species lists cannot be parsed into structures (e.g., shorthand names unsupported by Goslin grammars), since structural distances depend on graph comparison of lipid structures. When a single lipidome is analyzed — Hausdorff distances require at least two lipidomes to relate to each other. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes a global lipidome distance model in LipidSpace by embedding all lipids of multiple lipidomes in a graph-based structural space (MCS + Jaccard via LaWeCSE, PCA via Lanczos), then measuring pairwise Hausdorff distances between the m lipidomes over the union lipid set and clustering them hierarchically. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Computes a global lipidome distance model in LipidSpace by embedding all lipids of multiple lipidomes in a graph-based structural space (MCS + Jaccard via LaWeCSE, PCA via Lanczos), then measuring pairwise Hausdorff distances between the m lipidomes over the union lipid set and clustering them hierarchically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need quantitative differential-abundance statistics between sample groups rather than structural comparison across whole lipidomes — use the statistics/feature-analysis modules instead. When lipid species lists cannot be parsed into structures (e.g., shorthand names unsupported by Goslin grammars), since structural distances depend on graph comparison of lipid structures. When a single lipidome is analyzed — Hausdorff distances require at least two lipidomes to relate to each other.

skills.summary: Project lipidomes into the global lipid space model by running PCA on the pairwise lipid-structure distance matrix with the lambda-lanczos implementation, then deliver PC1/PC2 coordinates and ready-to-use result figures (Figure 1F) as exportable output.

skills.description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic matrix is at molecular-species level (rows like PC, PE, TG species) but the target analysis is at the lipid class (LCL) or building block (LBB) structural level.
skills.name: lipidomic-data-matrix-reshaping
skills.search_text: lipidomic-data-matrix-reshaping Use when an uploaded lipidomic matrix is at molecular-species level (rows like PC, PE, TG species) but the target analysis is at the lipid class (LCL) or building block (LBB) structural level. The input matrix is already at the lipid-class (LCL) level — aggregation would double-count rows that are already class sums The matrix contains duplicate lipid names or all-zero/zero-variance rows within a group — LipidOne 2.0 rejects the upload with an error listing the offending names, so clean the data first Row names do not follow LIPID MAPS shorthand notation, so class prefixes cannot be reliably extracted http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Reshapes a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix into lipid-class (LCL) or building-block (LBB) sub-matrices by aggregating rows that share a LIPID MAPS shorthand class prefix, sample-by-sample, so that class- and block-level analyses can run without manual submatrix calculation. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Reshapes a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix into lipid-class (LCL) or building-block (LBB) sub-matrices by aggregating rows that share a LIPID MAPS shorthand class prefix, sample-by-sample, so that class- and block-level analyses can run without manual submatrix calculation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already at the lipid-class (LCL) level — aggregation would double-count rows that are already class sums The matrix contains duplicate lipid names or all-zero/zero-variance rows within a group — LipidOne 2.0 rejects the upload with an error listing the offending names, so clean the data first Row names do not follow LIPID MAPS shorthand notation, so class prefixes cannot be reliably extracted

skills.description: Use when a lipidomic data matrix with experimental group assignments must be tested per lipid feature (class, molecular species, or building-block level) to flag significant group differences with significance asterisks.

skills.search_text: lipidomic-feature-group-statistics Use when a lipidomic data matrix with experimental group assignments must be tested per lipid feature (class, molecular species, or building-block level) to flag significant group differences with significance asterisks. When the goal is multivariate analysis (e.g., heatmaps via pheatmap or lipid pathway/network analysis via igraph) rather than per-feature univariate group comparisons When the study design violates the tool's assumptions — the bar-chart statistics use two-tailed Student's t-tests assuming equal variances, so paired designs or unequal-variance comparisons need a different approach When the data matrix has not been prepared and nomenclature-standardized per LipidOne 2.0's dataset-preparation and lipid-nomenclature protocols (Basic Protocol 1 / Support Protocol) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reproduce the LipidOne 2.0 bar-chart group-comparison statistics: per-lipid-feature two-tailed Student's t-tests (equal variance) or one-way ANOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, Tukey post hoc, and p-value-to-asterisk annotation (< .05, < .01, < .001). metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Reproduce the LipidOne 2.0 bar-chart group-comparison statistics: per-lipid-feature two-tailed Student's t-tests (equal variance) or one-way ANOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, Tukey post hoc, and p-value-to-asterisk annotation (< .05, < .01, < .001).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is multivariate analysis (e.g., heatmaps via pheatmap or lipid pathway/network analysis via igraph) rather than per-feature univariate group comparisons When the study design violates the tool's assumptions — the bar-chart statistics use two-tailed Student's t-tests assuming equal variances, so paired designs or unequal-variance comparisons need a different approach When the data matrix has not been prepared and nomenclature-standardized per LipidOne 2.0's dataset-preparation and lipid-nomenclature protocols (Basic Protocol 1 / Support Protocol)

skills.description: Use when raw lipidomic or metabolomic peak-intensity feature tables (e.g. MetaboLights S-BSST1038/S-BSST1039 exports) need filtering, imputation, log-transformation, and EigenMS normalization before downstream limma or ClassifyR analysis.
skills.name: lipidomic-feature-table-preprocessing
skills.search_text: lipidomic-feature-table-preprocessing Use when raw lipidomic or metabolomic peak-intensity feature tables (e.g. MetaboLights S-BSST1038/S-BSST1039 exports) need filtering, imputation, log-transformation, and EigenMS normalization before downstream limma or ClassifyR analysis. Input is proteomic data — MultiABLER currently does not provide functions to analyze proteomic data, which is another output of the Multi-ABLE extraction method. The table has already been filtered, imputed, and normalized (e.g. by TidyMass or a prior MultiABLER run) — re-running tbManipulate/normEigenMS would double-process the data. The required normalization mode is kNN imputation, mean, or quantile normalization — these were not implemented in MultiABLER. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Preprocess lipidomic and metabolomic peak-intensity feature tables with MultiABLER's tbManipulate (filtering, imputation, log transformation) and EigenMS normalization, producing a clean feature table ready for differential-expression or classification analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106881
skills.summary: Preprocess lipidomic and metabolomic peak-intensity feature tables with MultiABLER's tbManipulate (filtering, imputation, log transformation) and EigenMS normalization, producing a clean feature table ready for differential-expression or classification analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is proteomic data — MultiABLER currently does not provide functions to analyze proteomic data, which is another output of the Multi-ABLE extraction method. The table has already been filtered, imputed, and normalized (e.g. by TidyMass or a prior MultiABLER run) — re-running tbManipulate/normEigenMS would double-process the data. The required normalization mode is kNN imputation, mean, or quantile normalization — these were not implemented in MultiABLER.

skills.search_text: lipidomics-batch-effect-correction Use when a lipidomics abundance matrix (LipidSearch/LIQUID output or Metabolomics Workbench data) spans multiple acquisition batches and the user wants corrected values feeding the differential lipid abundance analysis (MA/volcano plots). skills.when_to_use_negative: The experiment contains no batch structure (single acquisition batch), since the correction is an optional step applied only when batch effects are present in the design metadata. skills.search_text: lipidomics-dimensionality-reduction Use when a preprocessed lipidomics data matrix (from LipidSearch/LIQUID outputs or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment) is loaded in the ADViSELipidomics Shiny app and you need unsupervised/supervised dimension reduction, sample clustering, or interactive exploratory visualizations. The goal is differential abundance testing, internal-standard-based normalization to absolute concentrations, or batch effect correction — these are separate ADViSELipidomics capabilities, not the exploratory dimension-reduction stage The input is raw LipidSearch/LIQUID identification output that has not yet been preprocessed into a lipid-by-sample abundance matrix Applies the exploratory-analysis layer of ADViSELipidomics — PCA (unsupervised) and PLS-DA (supervised) dimension reduction plus clustering algorithms — to a preprocessed lipid abundance matrix, and generates interactive, customizable plots on lipids and samples (density, spider, scatter, heatmaps). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac706

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential abundance testing, internal-standard-based normalization to absolute concentrations, or batch effect correction — these are separate ADViSELipidomics capabilities, not the exploratory dimension-reduction stage The input is raw LipidSearch/LIQUID identification output that has not yet been preprocessed into a lipid-by-sample abundance matrix

Input is a raw vendor file or an unannotated peak table — annotations from all tools must already be appended before benchmarking Comparing tools that annotate different lipid structural levels — corroboration is defined on fatty acyl constituent composition, not just class-level matches Waters vendor files, which LipidMatch does not currently support http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks lipid identification software (e.g., LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) by counting annotated features per tool per ion polarity and computing the percentage of one tool's fatty acyl constituent identifications corroborated by the others on shared features. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Benchmarks lipid identification software (e.g., LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) by counting annotated features per tool per ion polarity and computing the percentage of one tool's fatty acyl constituent identifications corroborated by the others on shared features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw vendor file or an unannotated peak table — annotations from all tools must already be appended before benchmarking Comparing tools that annotate different lipid structural levels — corroboration is defined on fatty acyl constituent composition, not just class-level matches Waters vendor files, which LipidMatch does not currently support

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics abundance table (csv/xlsx, flat or pivot, or mzTab-M) with attached study variables must be reduced to the lipid subset that explains each variable.
skills.name: lipidomics-feature-importance-analysis
skills.search_text: lipidomics-feature-importance-analysis Use when a lipidomics abundance table (csv/xlsx, flat or pivot, or mzTab-M) with attached study variables must be reduced to the lipid subset that explains each variable. The goal is structural comparison, lipidome similarity, dendrogram/clustering, or quality control — those are separate LipidSpace modules (MCS/Jaccard distances, QC workflow), not feature analysis. The imported data contains no study variables attached to the samples — the regression/classification models are built per study variable, so SFS has no targets to explain. Only a single study variable is present and a full cross-variable dependency analysis is desired — LipidSpace's 'Complete feature analysis' requires at least two study variables. A feature analysis and selection method from LipidSpace that identifies, per study variable, the subset of lipids that best describes it via heuristic sequential forward selection (SFS) scored by AIC, with ROC accuracy for binary nominal variables. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: A feature analysis and selection method from LipidSpace that identifies, per study variable, the subset of lipids that best describes it via heuristic sequential forward selection (SFS) scored by AIC, with ROC accuracy for binary nominal variables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is structural comparison, lipidome similarity, dendrogram/clustering, or quality control — those are separate LipidSpace modules (MCS/Jaccard distances, QC workflow), not feature analysis. The imported data contains no study variables attached to the samples — the regression/classification models are built per study variable, so SFS has no targets to explain. Only a single study variable is present and a full cross-variable dependency analysis is desired — LipidSpace's 'Complete feature analysis' requires at least two study variables.

skills.description: Use when you have LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature annotations from two spectral libraries and need to quantify annotation overlap, library agreement on lipid class/composition/adduct, or reproduce per-instrument identification counts.
skills.name: lipidomics-feature-set-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: lipidomics-feature-set-overlap-analysis Use when you have LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature annotations from two spectral libraries and need to quantify annotation overlap, library agreement on lipid class/composition/adduct, or reproduce per-instrument identification counts. You have only a single library's annotations and no second library to compare against — there is no overlap or agreement to quantify Your annotations were produced without RBP-score filtering (unthresholded matches), since the counts being reproduced depend specifically on the thresholded dual-library search The task is de novo lipid identification or spectral library construction rather than comparison of existing annotation results Reproduces the dual-library (CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) lipidomics annotation comparison described in the MAVEN2 paper by applying Retention Balance Point (RBP) score thresholds, partitioning annotated features into library-specific and shared sets, and computing class-level and full-structure agreement statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12080684
skills.summary: Reproduces the dual-library (CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) lipidomics annotation comparison described in the MAVEN2 paper by applying Retention Balance Point (RBP) score thresholds, partitioning annotated features into library-specific and shared sets, and computing class-level and full-structure agreement statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single library's annotations and no second library to compare against — there is no overlap or agreement to quantify Your annotations were produced without RBP-score filtering (unthresholded matches), since the counts being reproduced depend specifically on the thresholded dual-library search The task is de novo lipid identification or spectral library construction rather than comparison of existing annotation results

skills.search_text: lipidomics-feature-table-prefiltering Use when raw vendor lipidomics identification/quantification tables (LipidSearch or LIQUID outputs) or Metabolomics Workbench experiments must be imported, pre-filtered, and lipid species decomposed into class/chain/double-bond strata. Input is already a parsed feature table with lipid class/chain/double-bond annotations — proceed directly to normalization or differential analysis instead Data are not lipid identification/quantification outputs from LipidSearch, LIQUID, or the Metabolomics Workbench (ADViSELipidomics only copes with these sources) The goal is normalization to absolute concentrations via internal standards — that is a downstream step that assumes the import/parsing stage is already done http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Data-import stage of ADViSELipidomics in which lipid identification/quantification outputs (e.g. LipidSearch files) are loaded, pre-filtered to retain features of interest, and each lipid species identifier is parsed using LIPID MAPS classification into lipid class, chain length and double-bond count. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac706
skills.summary: Data-import stage of ADViSELipidomics in which lipid identification/quantification outputs (e.g. LipidSearch files) are loaded, pre-filtered to retain features of interest, and each lipid species identifier is parsed using LIPID MAPS classification into lipid class, chain length and double-bond count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a parsed feature table with lipid class/chain/double-bond annotations — proceed directly to normalization or differential analysis instead Data are not lipid identification/quantification outputs from LipidSearch, LIQUID, or the Metabolomics Workbench (ADViSELipidomics only copes with these sources) The goal is normalization to absolute concentrations via internal standards — that is a downstream step that assumes the import/parsing stage is already done

Input is already a concentration matrix (peak-area-to-concentration conversion would double-transform the data) No internal standards are present or standard.txt lacks a Conc. value for a class, so no class-specific conversion factor can be built The analysis goal is annotation or pathway interpretation at class/molecular-species/building-block level rather than producing quantified concentrations http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the Lipid Data Quantification utility of LipidOne 2.0, converting peak-area or peak-height values into concentrations using class-specific internal standards (e.g., SPLASH Lipidomix species), then removes standard rows and consolidates duplicate molecular species entries. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Reconstructs the Lipid Data Quantification utility of LipidOne 2.0, converting peak-area or peak-height values into concentrations using class-specific internal standards (e.g., SPLASH Lipidomix species), then removes standard rows and consolidates duplicate molecular species entries.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or verifying library-composition claims for a lipid identification tool, or comparing the number of lipid types/species covered across open-source lipidomics software.
skills.name: lipidomics-library-coverage-benchmarking
skills.search_text: lipidomics-library-coverage-benchmarking Use when reproducing or verifying library-composition claims for a lipid identification tool, or comparing the number of lipid types/species covered across open-source lipidomics software. The goal is validating identification accuracy on experimental MS/MS data rather than enumerating library composition — use the rule-based identification filter steps instead The README reports a newer distribution with different totals (over 500,000 species across over 60 lipid types), so the 2017 paper's exact-match counts (250,000+ species, 56 types) should not be expected against the current GitHub release http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies the compositional coverage of a lipidomics software's in silico fragmentation libraries — total lipid species, distinct lipid types, and fatty acid combination lists — and benchmarks coverage against comparable open-source tools. skills.search_text: lipidomics-metadata-annotation Use when a lipidomics matrix (numerical matrix, Skyline CSV export, or Metabolomics Workbench file) contains lipid molecule name strings that need class, chain-length, and double-bond annotations, or when some names fail pattern matching. The input is not a lipidomics dataset with lipid name strings (lipidr's automatic class/chain inference depends on parseable lipid names). Molecule names are already standardized shorthand with class/chain/unsaturation encoded and no re-annotation is needed. The analysis goal is generic metabolite identification from spectra rather than annotation of lipid molecule names. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Parses lipid molecule name strings with lipidr's lipidnames_pattern rules to derive lipid class, total chain length, and unsaturation annotations, flagging unparseable names and renaming full-chemical-name entries (e.g. ceramides) via RegEx so annotations are correctly inferred. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00082
skills.summary: Parses lipid molecule name strings with lipidr's lipidnames_pattern rules to derive lipid class, total chain length, and unsaturation annotations, flagging unparseable names and renaming full-chemical-name entries (e.g. ceramides) via RegEx so annotations are correctly inferred.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a lipidomics dataset with lipid name strings (lipidr's automatic class/chain inference depends on parseable lipid names). Molecule names are already standardized shorthand with class/chain/unsaturation encoded and no re-annotation is needed. The analysis goal is generic metabolite identification from spectra rather than annotation of lipid molecule names.

skills.description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS lipidomics or metabolomics mzML data where MS/MS scans must be linked to quantified MS1 peak groups across multiple samples.
skills.name: lipidomics-msms-slice-formation-in-mz-rt-space
skills.search_text: lipidomics-msms-slice-formation-in-mz-rt-space Use when processing LC-MS/MS lipidomics or metabolomics mzML data where MS/MS scans must be linked to quantified MS1 peak groups across multiple samples. Input is MS1-only LC-MS data with no fragmentation scans — grouping reduces to standard MAVEN peak detection with no slices to merge Input is already a finalized feature/peak table rather than raw mzML scans, since slices must be formed from raw fragmentation scans http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 MAVEN2's MS/MS-aware peak grouping pipeline: fragmentation scans are grouped into slices of (m/z, RT) space around precursor isolation windows, merged progressively across samples, then peak groups are formed and MS/MS scans are attached to finalized groups by retention time proximity. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12080684
skills.summary: MAVEN2's MS/MS-aware peak grouping pipeline: fragmentation scans are grouped into slices of (m/z, RT) space around precursor isolation windows, merged progressively across samples, then peak groups are formed and MS/MS scans are attached to finalized groups by retention time proximity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is MS1-only LC-MS data with no fragmentation scans — grouping reduces to standard MAVEN peak detection with no slices to merge Input is already a finalized feature/peak table rather than raw mzML scans, since slices must be formed from raw fragmentation scans

skills.summary: Search LC-MS/MS lipidomics features in MAVEN2 against in-silico spectral libraries (CalicoLipids and MS-DIAL) and score spectral matches with the hypergeometric score, yielding per-feature lipid annotations.

skills.description: Use when you have a chromatographic peak table from Compound Discoverer (v3.3 .cdResult or .csv) plus lipid identifications and want to remove adduct peaks, in-source fragments, dimers, and redundant unidentified features correlated with identified lipids before downstream statistics.
skills.name: lipidomics-peak-table-filtering
skills.search_text: lipidomics-peak-table-filtering Use when you have a chromatographic peak table from Compound Discoverer (v3.3 .cdResult or .csv) plus lipid identifications and want to remove adduct peaks, in-source fragments, dimers, and redundant unidentified features correlated with identified lipids before downstream statistics. Input is a raw spectral file (.mgf, .mzXML, .raw) rather than a chromatographic peak table — use Spectrum Searcher for spectral matching instead of peak-table filtering. You need in-silico spectral library generation or fragment annotation — those are Library Generator and Lipid Spectral Annotator roles, not peak-table filtering. The dataset lacks QC replicates or a sufficient number of non-QC, non-blank samples (the correlation filter requires features quantified in ≥10 such samples), so the ≥0.99 correlation and %RSD criteria cannot be evaluated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filter LC-MS lipidomics peak tables with LipiDex 2's Peak Finder correlation-based filtering and post-processing criteria to remove adducts, dimers, in-source fragments, and spurious co-eluting features, boosting confidence in remaining lipid identifications and quantitation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Filter LC-MS lipidomics peak tables with LipiDex 2's Peak Finder correlation-based filtering and post-processing criteria to remove adducts, dimers, in-source fragments, and spurious co-eluting features, boosting confidence in remaining lipid identifications and quantitation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw spectral file (.mgf, .mzXML, .raw) rather than a chromatographic peak table — use Spectrum Searcher for spectral matching instead of peak-table filtering. You need in-silico spectral library generation or fragment annotation — those are Library Generator and Lipid Spectral Annotator roles, not peak-table filtering. The dataset lacks QC replicates or a sufficient number of non-QC, non-blank samples (the correlation filter requires features quantified in ≥10 such samples), so the ≥0.99 correlation and %RSD criteria cannot be evaluated.

skills.description: Use when specific lipid species must be confirmed or quantified as precursor-ion targets in HRMS full-scan lipidomics data (e.g., Waters Synapt G2 HDMS runs of FASN-inhibitor treated vs. control cells) rather than discovered by untargeted feature finding.

skills.search_text: lipidomics-precursor-ion-targeting Use when specific lipid species must be confirmed or quantified as precursor-ion targets in HRMS full-scan lipidomics data (e.g., Waters Synapt G2 HDMS runs of FASN-inhibitor treated vs. control cells) rather than discovered by untargeted feature finding. skills.summary: Targeted extraction and quantification of specific lipid species (e.g., diacylglycerols DAG 30:0 and DAG 32:0) as precursor-ion targets from high-resolution MS full-scan lipidomics data using Skyline's small-molecule mode, enabling differential expression testing between treatment groups without fragment transitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is untargeted lipid discovery (MS1 feature-finding, alignment, identification) — use XCMS, MZmine, or MS-DIAL instead of targeted precursor extraction When fragment/transition-based quantification (e.g., SRM/MRM with product ions) is required — this skill is precursor-only extraction from full-scan HRMS data When the instrument data is GC-MS or ion-mobility small molecule data, where the article notes Skyline support is still ongoing and no single tool is best for all workflows

skills.search_text: lipidomics-qc-filtering Use when downstream of LipiDex 2 Peak Finder and Spectrum Searcher results you need to remove spurious/redundant lipid identifications and unidentified features using automated lipid-specific QC thresholds before statistical analysis. skills.summary: Apply LipiDex 2's Degreaser QC module to automatically validate and filter lipid identifications and features from LC-MS lipidomics peak tables, using seven criteria (ECN-vs-RT modeling, linear dynamic range, %RSD in QC samples, spectral match validation, PQF) to boost identification confidence.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or verifying claims that spectral-library query time is independent of library size, or when benchmarking MS/MS search engines (LipidIN EQ vs Flash Entropy Search) for per-query latency.
skills.name: lipidomics-query-throughput-reproduction
skills.search_text: lipidomics-query-throughput-reproduction Use when reproducing or verifying claims that spectral-library query time is independent of library size, or when benchmarking MS/MS search engines (LipidIN EQ vs Flash Entropy Search) for per-query latency. The goal is annotation accuracy, lipid coverage, or false-discovery rate of LipidIN rather than raw query throughput/speed benchmarking. Queries will be run multi-threaded or against libraries smaller than the reported size variants, so results are not comparable to the single-thread 2.3 µs / 0.14 s figures. The task requires Flash Entropy Search's other search modes (hybrid, neutral loss, open search) rather than timing the search itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Benchmark the LipidIN EQ module's library-size-independent query speed (hash-table/bisection linear-time data structure) against Flash Entropy Search by timing per-query wall-clock latency of MassBank library searches on a single-thread, low-memory CPU. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Benchmark the LipidIN EQ module's library-size-independent query speed (hash-table/bisection linear-time data structure) against Flash Entropy Search by timing per-query wall-clock latency of MassBank library searches on a single-thread, low-memory CPU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation accuracy, lipid coverage, or false-discovery rate of LipidIN rather than raw query throughput/speed benchmarking. Queries will be run multi-threaded or against libraries smaller than the reported size variants, so results are not comparable to the single-thread 2.3 µs / 0.14 s figures. The task requires Flash Entropy Search's other search modes (hybrid, neutral loss, open search) rather than timing the search itself.

skills.search_text: lipidomics-spectrum-classification Use when you have raw untargeted LC-MS lipidomics spectra (mzML or npy per sample) with class labels (e.g. 928 CCLE cell lines across 23 cancer types) and need end-to-end disease-type classification without peak picking or annotation. skills.description: Use when raw lipid MS2 spectra (e.g. from phospholipid standard measurements or profile-mode mzML) must be cleaned, normalized, and filtered before deep-learning training or downstream identification in tools like LipiDetective.
skills.name: lipidomics-spectrum-quality-control
skills.search_text: lipidomics-spectrum-quality-control Use when raw lipid MS2 spectra (e.g. from phospholipid standard measurements or profile-mode mzML) must be cleaned, normalized, and filtered before deep-learning training or downstream identification in tools like LipiDetective. Input spectra have already been smoothed, peak-picked, normalized, and stored in HDF5 — re-running this skill would discard spectra a second time or distort intensities. The analysis target is MS1 precursor survey data or raw chromatographic peak detection rather than MS2 fragment spectra for lipid species identification. Spectra were acquired on instruments/modes outside the scope of lipid tandem-MS (e.g. small-molecule metabolomics spectra not using shorthand lipid nomenclature), where the 50–1600 m/z window and lipid-fragment assumptions do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A preprocessing-and-filtering skill that converts raw (including profile-mode) lipid MS2 spectra into a high-quality, normalized peak list — via pyOpenMS smoothing/baseline-correction/peak-picking, base peak normalization, m/z trimming to 50–1600, and exclusion of noisy spectra above a 0.01 median-intensity threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.07.617094
skills.summary: A preprocessing-and-filtering skill that converts raw (including profile-mode) lipid MS2 spectra into a high-quality, normalized peak list — via pyOpenMS smoothing/baseline-correction/peak-picking, base peak normalization, m/z trimming to 50–1600, and exclusion of noisy spectra above a 0.01 median-intensity threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra have already been smoothed, peak-picked, normalized, and stored in HDF5 — re-running this skill would discard spectra a second time or distort intensities. The analysis target is MS1 precursor survey data or raw chromatographic peak detection rather than MS2 fragment spectra for lipid species identification. Spectra were acquired on instruments/modes outside the scope of lipid tandem-MS (e.g. small-molecule metabolomics spectra not using shorthand lipid nomenclature), where the 50–1600 m/z window and lipid-fragment assumptions do not apply.

skills.description: Use when a background-corrected two-color (e.g. CFP/YFP) live-cell time-lapse confocal series is available and you need time-resolved colocalization proportions plus a fitted dissociation rate after a perturbation such as LMB.
skills.name: live-cell-time-lapse-kinetics-fitting
skills.search_text: live-cell-time-lapse-kinetics-fitting Use when a background-corrected two-color (e.g. CFP/YFP) live-cell time-lapse confocal series is available and you need time-resolved colocalization proportions plus a fitted dissociation rate after a perturbation such as LMB. The question requires direct measurement of physical binding distance rather than colocalization dynamics — FRET was negative for the Rev-CRM1 complex because CRM1 is 130 kDa, and FRET alone only detects interaction when the average distance is <10, so neither approach alone substitutes for the other. The input is a static single-time-point image with no temporal dimension — the kinetics-fitting step requires a time series spanning before and after perturbation. Images cannot be background-corrected or lack independent red/green channels, since thresholding relies on scrambling blocks of a two-color image to build the random-overlap distribution. Quantifies how a perturbation (e.g. leptomycin B) changes the nucleolar colocalization proportions of two fluorescently tagged proteins across a live-cell confocal time-lapse, then fits the decay of colocalization to extract a protein-protein interaction dissociation rate. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422

skills.search_text: log-likelihood-ratio-spectrum-scoring Use when tandem mass spectra must be matched to candidate molecules from a structure database (e.g., PubChem, DNP) with calibrated FDR, rather than heuristic peak-count scores like MetFrag or EPIC. You need a spectral library search rather than in silico database search — direct spectral library search remains the most reliable annotation method when reference spectra exist for the molecule. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Score candidate molecule–spectrum pairs with a probabilistic log-likelihood ratio and estimate false discovery rates via target–decoy shuffling, as implemented in molDiscovery for small molecule identification from tandem mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0

skills.description: Use when applying notame's correct_drift() to LC-MS feature abundances: you log-transform the exprs matrix, fit a smooth.spline to QC samples across injection order, correct in log space, then must convert the corrected matrix back to linear intensities for output.
skills.name: log-space-abundance-back-transformation
skills.search_text: log-space-abundance-back-transformation Use when applying notame's correct_drift() to LC-MS feature abundances: you log-transform the exprs matrix, fit a smooth.spline to QC samples across injection order, correct in log space, then must convert the corrected matrix back to linear intensities for output. The abundance data have already been back-transformed to linear scale — exponentiating again would distort values Drift correction is being skipped (e.g. the dataset has too few QC samples, fewer than 4, and correct_drift() records Missing_QCs) — there is no log-space corrected matrix to transform back The data are not log-transformed LC-MS feature abundances (e.g. peak areas on another scale) and the additive log-space correction model does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 The back-transformation step of notame's drift correction: after fitting a cubic spline to log-transformed QC abundances versus injection order, corrected log-space values are exponentiated to return the feature abundance matrix to linear scale, satisfying the spline model's assumptions while delivering results in the original measurement units. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135
skills.summary: The back-transformation step of notame's drift correction: after fitting a cubic spline to log-transformed QC abundances versus injection order, corrected log-space values are exponentiated to return the feature abundance matrix to linear scale, satisfying the spline model's assumptions while delivering results in the original measurement units.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance data have already been back-transformed to linear scale — exponentiating again would distort values Drift correction is being skipped (e.g. the dataset has too few QC samples, fewer than 4, and correct_drift() records Missing_QCs) — there is no log-space corrected matrix to transform back The data are not log-transformed LC-MS feature abundances (e.g. peak areas on another scale) and the additive log-space correction model does not apply

skills.search_text: log-transformation-for-normality Use when metabolomics abundance data (e.g. myocardial infarction, atherothrombotic, or African Race metabolite matrices) are skewed before KNN-TN imputation or distribution-based simulation of missing values. Metabolite values include zeros or negatives on the raw scale, so the logarithm is undefined unless an offset is first justified — the article does not describe an offset convention The downstream imputation method does not rely on a normality assumption (e.g. pure KNN-EU on Euclidean distance without truncated-normal standardization), where the transform is not required by the method Data are already approximately normal (e.g. previously log-processed intensities), where re-transforming adds no benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Log-transform metabolite abundance matrices so their distributions approximately satisfy normality before truncated-normal standardization and imputation (KNN-TN), since the KNN-TN likelihood and the gene-expression distribution simulation assume normal data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: Log-transform metabolite abundance matrices so their distributions approximately satisfy normality before truncated-normal standardization and imputation (KNN-TN), since the KNN-TN likelihood and the gene-expression distribution simulation assume normal data.

The goal is a normalization method comparison on raw-scale data where log transformation would confound the evaluation criteria. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Log-transforms a metabolomics featuredata matrix (metabolite peak intensities/concentrations) using the NormalizeMets LogTransform function, either as a standalone step or as the lg=TRUE log stage applied after normalization (e.g. QC-RLSC signal correction via NormQcsamples). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Log-transforms a metabolomics featuredata matrix (metabolite peak intensities/concentrations) using the NormalizeMets LogTransform function, either as a standalone step or as the lg=TRUE log stage applied after normalization (e.g. QC-RLSC signal correction via NormQcsamples).

skills.name: log2-intensity-transformation
skills.search_text: log2-intensity-transformation Use when a raw metabolite abundance matrix (e.g. AUC peak areas integrated in MultiQuant from LC-MS/MS runs) must be placed on an additive scale before within-batch signal-drift correction or RUV-III batch adjustment in the hRUV pipeline. The input matrix is already on a log2 (or otherwise additive/log-scale) basis — re-transforming would distort the intensities. The matrix still contains zeros, negative values, or unresolved missing entries that have not been imputed; log2 is undefined there and hRUV's authors note that 'hRUV algorithm expects data without missing values'. The goal is analysis of raw vendor peak tables rather than normalization downstream — the transformation alone removes no drift; it only prepares data for the loess/rlm smoother and RUV-III steps. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Log2-transformation of raw metabolite abundance intensities as the preprocessing step of the hRUV workflow, converting multiplicative signal drift and ion-suppression effects into an additive scale so that per-batch robust smoothers (loess/rlm) against run order can be fitted and subtracted. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Log2-transformation of raw metabolite abundance intensities as the preprocessing step of the hRUV workflow, converting multiplicative signal drift and ion-suppression effects into an additive scale so that per-batch robust smoothers (loess/rlm) against run order can be fitted and subtracted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already on a log2 (or otherwise additive/log-scale) basis — re-transforming would distort the intensities. The matrix still contains zeros, negative values, or unresolved missing entries that have not been imputed; log2 is undefined there and hRUV's authors note that 'hRUV algorithm expects data without missing values'. The goal is analysis of raw vendor peak tables rather than normalization downstream — the transformation alone removes no drift; it only prepares data for the loess/rlm smoother and RUV-III steps.

skills.description: Use when you have a batch-corrected LC-MS feature table from a two-group dietary/condition contrast and need a statistically defensible list of differentially abundant metabolites with a volcano plot.
skills.name: log2fold-change-thresholding
skills.search_text: log2fold-change-thresholding Use when you have a batch-corrected LC-MS feature table from a two-group dietary/condition contrast and need a statistically defensible list of differentially abundant metabolites with a volcano plot. skills.search_text: longitudinal-gradient-normalization Use when 2D DESI-MSI ion-intensity images of a linear developmental axis (e.g., maize root tip-to-mature gradient) must be projected to normalized 1D linescans and clustered by enrichment pattern. The tissue or gradient has no linear developmental axis — DIMPLE is explicitly designed to 'leverage the linear developmental axis', so radial or non-polarized spatial structures are the wrong input. The input is already a matrix of 1D enrichment profiles or a feature table; then only the Ward clustering step, not the 2D-to-1D projection and normalization, is needed. The goal is metabolite annotation of individual m/z peaks (e.g. via METASPACE, Metlin Classic, or LOTUS) rather than grouping signatures by developmental enrichment pattern. DIMPLE's normalization scheme that reduces 2D DESI-MSI spatial ion-intensity images to 1D longitudinal linescans along the root developmental axis, normalizes them (unit-sum/TIC), smooths with a 10-pixel running median, and feeds the resulting feature matrix into Ward hierarchical clustering to recover developmental enrichment patterns in maize roots. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw intensities that have not been cleaned/transformed or QC-filtered — GetFeatistics expects pre-processed feature tables (e.g. pooled-QC filtered) The analysis is a single fixed-effect model with no longitudinal structure and no censoring — a plain lm outside this multi-mode mechanism is simpler The goal is untargeted feature extraction or annotation rather than statistical association testing (use patRoon/MS-DIAL import and QC-filtering functions instead)

skills.description: Use when feature abundance data (KO table or compound table with KEGG C numbers) are paired with a continuous or time-point metadata variable and you need threshold-free pathway-level enrichment along that variable.

skills.search_text: longitudinal-omics-regression-testing Use when feature abundance data (KO table or compound table with KEGG C numbers) are paired with a continuous or time-point metadata variable and you need threshold-free pathway-level enrichment along that variable. The abundance table has been prefiltered to a small background feature set — GRSA is threshold-free and considers all KOs in a pathway, so prefiltering biases the reporter scores The design is a simple binary comparison that only needs a hypergeometric over-representation test on a pre-defined significant list (KO_enrich/KO_fisher) rather than threshold-free pathway aggregation Feature IDs are not standardized (e.g., metabolite names not converted to KEGG C numbers) — ko.test/reporter_score cannot map compounds to the pathway database http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) from the ReporterScore R package to test feature (KO or KEGG compound) abundance against a continuous longitudinal variable (e.g., gestational age), aggregating per-feature statistics into pathway-level reporter scores without predefined thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Applies Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) from the ReporterScore R package to test feature (KO or KEGG compound) abundance against a continuous longitudinal variable (e.g., gestational age), aggregating per-feature statistics into pathway-level reporter scores without predefined thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance table has been prefiltered to a small background feature set — GRSA is threshold-free and considers all KOs in a pathway, so prefiltering biases the reporter scores The design is a simple binary comparison that only needs a hypergeometric over-representation test on a pre-defined significant list (KO_enrich/KO_fisher) rather than threshold-free pathway aggregation Feature IDs are not standardized (e.g., metabolite names not converted to KEGG C numbers) — ko.test/reporter_score cannot map compounds to the pathway database
