skills.description: Use when you have two non-overlapping (by inchi_key) spectral libraries — a query library and a main library with (mass, intensity) spectra — and need top-k lookup error/recall metrics for predicted versus experimental EI-MS spectra.
skills.name: lookup-rank-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: lookup-rank-metrics-computation Use when you have two non-overlapping (by inchi_key) spectral libraries — a query library and a main library with (mass, intensity) spectra — and need top-k lookup error/recall metrics for predicted versus experimental EI-MS spectra. The query and main library share molecules (overlapping inchi_keys) — the pipeline asserts strict non-overlap, and leakage would inflate recall. You need forward-prediction quality metrics (Stein dot product between predicted and experimental spectra of the same molecule) rather than retrieval metrics — use `analysis_pipeline.py`/results.metrics instead. Input molecules fall outside the models' supported scope — FormulaNet handles mols ≤ 48 atoms and only HCONFSPCl elements, so lookup evaluation of such molecules with these pretrained models is out of scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes spectral library-matching (database lookup) metrics by ranking a main library's spectra by decreasing weighted Stein dot product (SDP) against each query spectrum and converting the true match's rank into error rates at 1 and 10. This is the RASSP paper's evaluation of how well predicted EI–MS spectra retrieve the correct compound from a spectral database. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Computes spectral library-matching (database lookup) metrics by ranking a main library's spectra by decreasing weighted Stein dot product (SDP) against each query spectrum and converting the true match's rank into error rates at 1 and 10. This is the RASSP paper's evaluation of how well predicted EI–MS spectra retrieve the correct compound from a spectral database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query and main library share molecules (overlapping inchi_keys) — the pipeline asserts strict non-overlap, and leakage would inflate recall. You need forward-prediction quality metrics (Stein dot product between predicted and experimental spectra of the same molecule) rather than retrieval metrics — use `analysis_pipeline.py`/results.metrics instead. Input molecules fall outside the models' supported scope — FormulaNet handles mols ≤ 48 atoms and only HCONFSPCl elements, so lookup evaluation of such molecules with these pretrained models is out of scope.

skills.description: Use when a molecular network already has Louvain community labels (e.g., from a spectral-similarity edge list) and you need interpretable, cycle-free per-cluster subnetworks that preserve connectivity of every assigned metabolite.
skills.name: louvain-partition-consumption
skills.search_text: louvain-partition-consumption Use when a molecular network already has Louvain community labels (e.g., from a spectral-similarity edge list) and you need interpretable, cycle-free per-cluster subnetworks that preserve connectivity of every assigned metabolite. The analysis goal is conventional threshold-based molecular networking, where edges below an arbitrary similarity cutoff are simply removed rather than replaced by a spanning-tree backbone. The network has no precomputed Louvain partition, so there is no community structure to consume and per-community subgraphs cannot be formed. Retaining cycles within communities is essential (e.g., for downstream loop/alternating-path analyses), since spanning trees are by definition cycle-free. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Consumes the Louvain community assignment of a spectral-similarity-weighted molecular network by splitting it into per-community subgraphs and pruning each to its maximum-weight spanning tree, retaining the strongest similarity edges while keeping every community node connected. This avoids the arbitrary similarity-threshold pruning that the MCN paper argues fractures natural metabolite families. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Consumes the Louvain community assignment of a spectral-similarity-weighted molecular network by splitting it into per-community subgraphs and pruning each to its maximum-weight spanning tree, retaining the strongest similarity edges while keeping every community node connected. This avoids the arbitrary similarity-threshold pruning that the MCN paper argues fractures natural metabolite families.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is conventional threshold-based molecular networking, where edges below an arbitrary similarity cutoff are simply removed rather than replaced by a spanning-tree backbone. The network has no precomputed Louvain partition, so there is no community structure to consume and per-community subgraphs cannot be formed. Retaining cycles within communities is essential (e.g., for downstream loop/alternating-path analyses), since spanning trees are by definition cycle-free.

skills.description: Use when the urine feature table contains low-abundance peaks lacking MS/MS fragmentation but with accurate mass and retention time that fall within condition-matched in-house library tolerance windows for m/z and RT.
skills.name: low-abundance-compound-annotation
skills.search_text: low-abundance-compound-annotation Use when the urine feature table contains low-abundance peaks lacking MS/MS fragmentation but with accurate mass and retention time that fall within condition-matched in-house library tolerance windows for m/z and RT. When the feature has an MS/MS spectrum, use precursor accurate mass plus MS/MS matching (MSI level 2 with spectral evidence) or CSI:FingerID/NIST hybrid search for MSI level 3 instead of m/z+RT-only annotation. When the in-house m/z/RT library was acquired on different chromatography or instrument conditions, RT-matching windows are not valid and this skill should not be applied. When the goal is highest-confidence MSI level 1 identification, authentic standards with precursor mass, RT, and MS/MS matching are required; m/z+RT matching alone cannot reach level 1. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Annotates low-abundance metabolite signals in untargeted LC-HRMS urine data by matching accurate precursor m/z and retention time against in-house m/z/RT libraries acquired under identical chromatographic and instrument conditions (HILIC-Q Exactive HF and CSH-Q Exactive HF), without requiring MS/MS spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Annotates low-abundance metabolite signals in untargeted LC-HRMS urine data by matching accurate precursor m/z and retention time against in-house m/z/RT libraries acquired under identical chromatographic and instrument conditions (HILIC-Q Exactive HF and CSH-Q Exactive HF), without requiring MS/MS spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the feature has an MS/MS spectrum, use precursor accurate mass plus MS/MS matching (MSI level 2 with spectral evidence) or CSI:FingerID/NIST hybrid search for MSI level 3 instead of m/z+RT-only annotation. When the in-house m/z/RT library was acquired on different chromatography or instrument conditions, RT-matching windows are not valid and this skill should not be applied. When the goal is highest-confidence MSI level 1 identification, authentic standards with precursor mass, RT, and MS/MS matching are required; m/z+RT matching alone cannot reach level 1.

skills.description: Use when a mixture spectrum comes from a low-field benchtop 1H NMR spectrometer (e.g. Magritek 43 MHz) with nearly complete peak overlap, or when peak-picking quantification has failed on overlapping signals.
skills.name: low-field-benchtop-nmr-mixture-quantification
skills.search_text: low-field-benchtop-nmr-mixture-quantification Use when a mixture spectrum comes from a low-field benchtop 1H NMR spectrometer (e.g. Magritek 43 MHz) with nearly complete peak overlap, or when peak-picking quantification has failed on overlapping signals. Spectra where peaks are well resolved and peak-picking tools (ACD/TP, MANIQ) suffice — Magnetstein's transport-based deconvolution is aimed at overlapped, low-resolution, distorted, or shifted spectra. Mass spectrometry data — the sibling tool Masserstein/MasserFront covers mass-spectrometry result analysis, not NMR mixture quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Quantifies mixture-component proportions from low-resolution benchtop 1H NMR spectra (e.g. Magritek 43 MHz) by applying Magnetstein's optimal-transport deconvolution, a regime where peak-picking tools like ACD/TP and MANIQ fail because peaks overlap almost completely. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03594
skills.summary: Quantifies mixture-component proportions from low-resolution benchtop 1H NMR spectra (e.g. Magritek 43 MHz) by applying Magnetstein's optimal-transport deconvolution, a regime where peak-picking tools like ACD/TP and MANIQ fail because peaks overlap almost completely.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra where peaks are well resolved and peak-picking tools (ACD/TP, MANIQ) suffice — Magnetstein's transport-based deconvolution is aimed at overlapped, low-resolution, distorted, or shifted spectra. skills.description: Use when enhancing an MLP or GNN spectral predictor so co-occurring spectral-peak dependencies are learned, by adding a rank-limited (e.g. correlation_mat_rank=100) mixing matrix and an auxiliary LDA topic-distribution head.

skills.search_text: low-rank-matrix-factorization-pytorch Use when enhancing an MLP or GNN spectral predictor so co-occurring spectral-peak dependencies are learned, by adding a rank-limited (e.g. correlation_mat_rank=100) mixing matrix and an auxiliary LDA topic-distribution head. You only need the baseline MLP or GNN spectrum prediction without peak-dependency mixing or LDA topic multi-tasking — set the disable flags and skip this module. Your spectra are not discretized to the 1000-bin resolution the ESP pipeline expects (e.g. EI/GC-MS NEIMS-style data), since Ql operates on the 1000-bin predicted spectra. You cannot train ESP end-to-end because pretrained MLP and GNN checkpoints are missing — ESP training requires best_model_mlp_*.pt and best_model_gnn_*.pt first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implementation of ESP's learnable low-rank peak-dependency mixing — matrices Ql = Dl Dl^T applied to 1000-bin predicted spectra via a mixing residual weight — plus the multi-task LDA spectral-topic head, in PyTorch, to capture dependencies among co-occurring spectral peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae490

The input is high-resolution, high-accuracy mass spectrometry data — the article notes other models (SIRIUS4/CSI:FingerID, MSNovelist, MassGenie) suit those data and TeFT's advantage lies in low-resolution spectra. The spectra were recorded in negative ion mode: TeFT was only trained on positive ion mode (H+) spectra, so its applicability is restricted. The goal is identifying known compounds by library search rather than de novo annotation of unknown natural products or drug metabolites from low-resolution on-site data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocess low-resolution MSn peak lists from miniaturized mass spectrometers (average replicates, deconvolute, cap at 100 peaks by intensity, keep top 5–6 fragmentation peaks with five nearby points) so they are suitable for TeFT fragment-tree construction and SMILES similarity scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0

skills.description: Use when aligned per-sample mass tracks (from centroided mzML files) show retention time drift across samples in a study and must be mapped to a common reference sample before aggregating into composite mass tracks.
skills.name: lowess-retention-time-calibration-to-reference-sample
skills.search_text: lowess-retention-time-calibration-to-reference-sample Use when aligned per-sample mass tracks (from centroided mzML files) show retention time drift across samples in a study and must be mapped to a common reference sample before aggregating into composite mass tracks. Input data are low-resolution mass spectra — asari's mass-track framework (and its RT calibration step) is built for high-resolution data and 'does not work with low resolution data'. Data have very high noise or come from long chromatography runs — the article notes 'data of very high noise may need customized processing' and efficiency 'is not optimal on data from longer chromatography'. The goal is MS/MS-based analysis — 'MS/MS spectra are ignored by asari' in the default LC-MS workflow, so RT calibration of MS1 mass tracks alone will not serve MS/MS-centric pipelines. Calibrates retention time of each LC-MS sample to a common reference sample via LOWESS regression on matched landmark elution peaks, so per-sample mass tracks can be summed into composite mass tracks in asari. This corrects chromatographic drift before peak detection is performed once per composite track rather than per sample. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Calibrates retention time of each LC-MS sample to a common reference sample via LOWESS regression on matched landmark elution peaks, so per-sample mass tracks can be summed into composite mass tracks in asari. This corrects chromatographic drift before peak detection is performed once per composite track rather than per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are low-resolution mass spectra — asari's mass-track framework (and its RT calibration step) is built for high-resolution data and 'does not work with low resolution data'. Data have very high noise or come from long chromatography runs — the article notes 'data of very high noise may need customized processing' and efficiency 'is not optimal on data from longer chromatography'. The goal is MS/MS-based analysis — 'MS/MS spectra are ignored by asari' in the default LC-MS workflow, so RT calibration of MS1 mass tracks alone will not serve MS/MS-centric pipelines.

skills.name: lsh-hash-collision-signal-classification
skills.search_text: lsh-hash-collision-signal-classification Use when raw TimsTOF LC-IMS-MS frames (e.g., DDA-PASEF precursor frames from a .d folder) must be denoised or reduced in size while retaining true peptide signal, and intensity thresholding is inadequate. The sample is dominated by self-similar chemical noise (repeated contaminants), which the LSH approach would misclassify as 'true' signal Signals of interest have very low relative intensity to noise peaks — the similarity measure underlying the LSH drops and such signals could be lost A gold-standard peak-level ground truth is required for evaluation: no such annotation of real data was available, and vendor DDA-selected masses are a biased (high-intensity, fragmented-only) reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classifies mass spectrometry raw-data peaks as signal or noise using locality-sensitive hashing: windows of a binned mass axis are hashed, and a window is called 'signal' if any of its hash values collides in a shared occurrence map, enabling scalable denoising prefiltering of LC-IMS-MS frames. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-022-04833-5
skills.summary: Classifies mass spectrometry raw-data peaks as signal or noise using locality-sensitive hashing: windows of a binned mass axis are hashed, and a window is called 'signal' if any of its hash values collides in a shared occurrence map, enabling scalable denoising prefiltering of LC-IMS-MS frames.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is dominated by self-similar chemical noise (repeated contaminants), which the LSH approach would misclassify as 'true' signal Signals of interest have very low relative intensity to noise peaks — the similarity measure underlying the LSH drops and such signals could be lost A gold-standard peak-level ground truth is required for evaluation: no such annotation of real data was available, and vendor DDA-selected masses are a biased (high-intensity, fragmented-only) reference

skills.description: Use when tuning (m,n) AND/OR-connective settings of an LSH signal/noise classifier on TimsTOF LC-IMS-MS frames, to quantify false-positive/false-negative rates or the data-reduction vs. retained-precursor trade-off.
skills.name: lsh-parameter-sweep-evaluation
skills.search_text: lsh-parameter-sweep-evaluation Use when tuning (m,n) AND/OR-connective settings of an LSH signal/noise classifier on TimsTOF LC-IMS-MS frames, to quantify false-positive/false-negative rates or the data-reduction vs. retained-precursor trade-off. The data are chemical noise/contaminants that are self-similar — the LSH approach would misclassify them as 'true' signal regardless of (m,n). Signals have low relative intensity compared to noise peaks — the similarity measure underlying LSH drops and such signals can be lost even at permissive settings. A peak-level gold-standard ground truth is required for evaluation — none was available for real data; vendor-selected DDA peaks are a biased, high-intensity-only reference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Sweeps the augmented locality-sensitive-hashing parameters (m OR-connectives, n AND-connectives) of the mzBucket/proteolizard signal classifier and quantifies the resulting trade-off between data reduction and retention of true signal in LC-IMS-MS raw data, via Monte-Carlo collision-probability surfaces and real DDA-PASEF frame benchmarks. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-022-04833-5
skills.summary: Sweeps the augmented locality-sensitive-hashing parameters (m OR-connectives, n AND-connectives) of the mzBucket/proteolizard signal classifier and quantifies the resulting trade-off between data reduction and retention of true signal in LC-IMS-MS raw data, via Monte-Carlo collision-probability surfaces and real DDA-PASEF frame benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are chemical noise/contaminants that are self-similar — the LSH approach would misclassify them as 'true' signal regardless of (m,n). Signals have low relative intensity compared to noise peaks — the similarity measure underlying LSH drops and such signals can be lost even at permissive settings. A peak-level gold-standard ground truth is required for evaluation — none was available for real data; vendor-selected DDA peaks are a biased, high-intensity-only reference.

skills.description: Use when a large mass spectra collection (e.g., millions of LC-MS/MS spectra from GeMS/MassIVE GNPS) contains redundant similar spectra and you need near-duplicate clusters in linear time before capping or subsampling.
skills.name: lsh-random-projection-clustering
skills.search_text: lsh-random-projection-clustering Use when a large mass spectra collection (e.g., millions of LC-MS/MS spectra from GeMS/MassIVE GNPS) contains redundant similar spectra and you need near-duplicate clusters in linear time before capping or subsampling. The dataset is small enough that exact pairwise cosine similarity (e.g., spectral entropy or dot-product similarity from matchms tooling) is tractable; LSH approximation is only needed at repository scale. The goal is a k-nearest-neighbor similarity graph rather than redundancy-clustering — the article used approximate 3-NN graph construction (PyNNDescent) for the DreaMS Atlas, not LSH. Spectra are already deduplicated or are library spectra where retaining all variants of similar spectra is desired for supervised training. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Redundancy reduction for repository-scale tandem MS/MS collections by clustering spectra with random-projection locality-sensitive hashing (LSH), which approximates cosine similarity in linear time, then capping cluster sizes by random sampling to produce deduplicated dataset variants. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Redundancy reduction for repository-scale tandem MS/MS collections by clustering spectra with random-projection locality-sensitive hashing (LSH), which approximates cosine similarity in linear time, then capping cluster sizes by random sampling to produce deduplicated dataset variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that exact pairwise cosine similarity (e.g., spectral entropy or dot-product similarity from matchms tooling) is tractable; LSH approximation is only needed at repository scale. The goal is a k-nearest-neighbor similarity graph rather than redundancy-clustering — the article used approximate 3-NN graph construction (PyNNDescent) for the DreaMS Atlas, not LSH. Spectra are already deduplicated or are library spectra where retaining all variants of similar spectra is desired for supervised training.

skills.search_text: machine-learning-model-evaluation Use when you have a labeled peak-quality development set and multiple metric-set × ML-algorithm candidate classifiers, and must choose one global classifier with statistically defensible evidence before deploying it on independent datasets. Input is a preprocessed feature table without XCMS objects or EIC points, so getEvalObj() cannot extract eicPts/eicPeakData/eicNos needed for metric computation. skills.search_text: maize-root-spatial-metabolomics Use when you have DESI-MSI hyperspectral images of maize (or other linearly organized) tissue sections and need to identify mass signatures enriched at specific positions along a developmental gradient or in specific cell layers, and to annotate unknown m/z values. The data are bulk metabolomics feature tables rather than spatially resolved MSI pixels — the skill's core value is spatial localization along the developmental axis The tissue has no linear organizational axis to exploit; DIMPLE is specifically designed to 'leverage the linear developmental axis' The goal is high spatial resolution below DESI-MSI's ∼50-100 µm limit, where matrix-assisted approaches like MALDI or SIMS would be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Maps and annotates metabolites along the linear maize root developmental axis using DESI-MSI (∼50-100 µm spatial resolution) and the DIMPLE pipeline, then curates cluster-specific mass signature tables and annotates m/z values with METASPACE, Metlin Classic, and LOTUS. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Maps and annotates metabolites along the linear maize root developmental axis using DESI-MSI (∼50-100 µm spatial resolution) and the DIMPLE pipeline, then curates cluster-specific mass signature tables and annotates m/z values with METASPACE, Metlin Classic, and LOTUS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk metabolomics feature tables rather than spatially resolved MSI pixels — the skill's core value is spatial localization along the developmental axis The tissue has no linear organizational axis to exploit; DIMPLE is specifically designed to 'leverage the linear developmental axis' The goal is high spatial resolution below DESI-MSI's ∼50-100 µm limit, where matrix-assisted approaches like MALDI or SIMS would be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when DESI-MSI mass signatures from linear maize-root developmental gradients need zone-level localization labels (e.g., meristem-localized Cluster 1) or when comparing signature localization between varieties such as B73 and Oaxacan Green.
skills.name: maize-root-zone-annotation
skills.search_text: maize-root-zone-annotation Use when DESI-MSI mass signatures from linear maize-root developmental gradients need zone-level localization labels (e.g., meristem-localized Cluster 1) or when comparing signature localization between varieties such as B73 and Oaxacan Green. The tissue lacks a linear developmental axis (branched organs, arbitrary 2D sections) — DIMPLE's zone clustering is designed to leverage the linear root tip-to-base gradient. The goal is compound-identity annotation of m/z values — use database searches (METASPACE, Metlin Classic, LOTUS) instead of developmental-zone clustering. Input is a bulk metabolomics feature table without spatial coordinates — zone localization cannot be inferred, and bulk tissue-scale data masks rare cell-type signatures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assigns developmental-zone localization classes (e.g., meristem-localized Cluster 1, root-tip, EZ cortex) to DESI-MSI mass signatures from maize root longitudinal sections using DIMPLE clusters along the linear tip-to-base axis, enabling cross-variety conservation/divergence calls between B73 and Oaxacan Green. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Assigns developmental-zone localization classes (e.g., meristem-localized Cluster 1, root-tip, EZ cortex) to DESI-MSI mass signatures from maize root longitudinal sections using DIMPLE clusters along the linear tip-to-base axis, enabling cross-variety conservation/divergence calls between B73 and Oaxacan Green.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue lacks a linear developmental axis (branched organs, arbitrary 2D sections) — DIMPLE's zone clustering is designed to leverage the linear root tip-to-base gradient. The goal is compound-identity annotation of m/z values — use database searches (METASPACE, Metlin Classic, LOTUS) instead of developmental-zone clustering. Input is a bulk metabolomics feature table without spatial coordinates — zone localization cannot be inferred, and bulk tissue-scale data masks rare cell-type signatures.

skills.description: Use when several independently trained classifiers (e.g., LDA, NN, SVM across different random seeds) each produce per-spectrum MS/MS predictions that must be merged into one binary 'relevant'/'other' label.
skills.name: majority-vote-ensemble-aggregation
skills.search_text: majority-vote-ensemble-aggregation Use when several independently trained classifiers (e.g., LDA, NN, SVM across different random seeds) each produce per-spectrum MS/MS predictions that must be merged into one binary 'relevant'/'other' label. When only a single classifier (or a single random seed) is available — majority voting requires multiple independent predictions to aggregate When the training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article explicitly warns that classification will most often fail and 'The presented python package is not capable of resolving this issue' When the task requires multi-class substance-class assignment — AnnoMe's ensemble produces only a binary 'relevant' vs 'other' classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Aggregates per-classifier predictions from multiple models (LDA, NN, SVM) trained with cross-validation and different random seeds into a single final 'relevant'/'other' label per HR-MS/MS spectrum, as implemented in AnnoMe for natural product discovery. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Aggregates per-classifier predictions from multiple models (LDA, NN, SVM) trained with cross-validation and different random seeds into a single final 'relevant'/'other' label per HR-MS/MS spectrum, as implemented in AnnoMe for natural product discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single classifier (or a single random seed) is available — majority voting requires multiple independent predictions to aggregate When the training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article explicitly warns that classification will most often fail and 'The presented python package is not capable of resolving this issue' When the task requires multi-class substance-class assignment — AnnoMe's ensemble produces only a binary 'relevant' vs 'other' classification

skills.description: Use when you need to prioritize novel HR-MS/MS spectra by a compound class of interest — e.g., flagging putative prenylated flavonoids in plant extracts — using curated 'relevant'/'other' reference spectra.
skills.name: majority-vote-ensemble-classification
skills.search_text: majority-vote-ensemble-classification Use when you need to prioritize novel HR-MS/MS spectra by a compound class of interest — e.g., flagging putative prenylated flavonoids in plant extracts — using curated 'relevant'/'other' reference spectra. When the training dataset is highly imbalanced between 'relevant' and 'other' compounds — the article and README state the package is not capable of resolving this issue and classification will most often not be successful When only a single classifier or a single random seed is available — the method depends on aggregating multiple cross-validated classifiers with different random seeds by majority vote When the input is raw MS1 peak data without HR-MS/MS spectra — AnnoMe operates on MS/MS spectra (MGF inference files) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classify HR-MS/MS spectra into user-defined 'relevant' vs 'other' substance classes by combining predictions from multiple classifiers (LDA, NN, SVM, etc.) trained with cross-validation and different random seeds on MS2DeepScore embeddings, and aggregating the individual outcomes by majority vote. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Classify HR-MS/MS spectra into user-defined 'relevant' vs 'other' substance classes by combining predictions from multiple classifiers (LDA, NN, SVM, etc.) trained with cross-validation and different random seeds on MS2DeepScore embeddings, and aggregating the individual outcomes by majority vote.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the training dataset is highly imbalanced between 'relevant' and 'other' compounds — the article and README state the package is not capable of resolving this issue and classification will most often not be successful When only a single classifier or a single random seed is available — the method depends on aggregating multiple cross-validated classifiers with different random seeds by majority vote When the input is raw MS1 peak data without HR-MS/MS spectra — AnnoMe operates on MS/MS spectra (MGF inference files)

skills.description: Use when you have quantized peak m/z and intensity vectors from preprocessed MS/MS spectra and need compact binary high-dimensional representations (HVs) for fast GPU distance computation in spectral clustering pipelines like HyperSpec.
skills.name: majority-xor-binary-spectrum-encoding
skills.search_text: majority-xor-binary-spectrum-encoding Use when you have quantized peak m/z and intensity vectors from preprocessed MS/MS spectra and need compact binary high-dimensional representations (HVs) for fast GPU distance computation in spectral clustering pipelines like HyperSpec. Spectra have not been preprocessed yet — raw spectra must first go through HyperSpec's spectrum preprocessing (precursor/low-intensity peak removal, <5-peak/<250 Da range filtering, 50-peak cap, L2 normalization) and bucket division before encoding You need low-dimensional hashed spectral vectors rather than binary high-dimensional hypervectors — the article contrasts HDC encoding with hashing-based methods like msCRUSH and falcon http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Encodes preprocessed MS/MS spectra as bit-packed binary hypervectors (default D = 2048, Q = 16) using level-id HD encoding: XOR the ID hypervector of each peak m/z with the level hypervector of its intensity and bind all pairs with a pointwise majority function, then batch-encode on GPU for HyperSpec clustering. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00612
skills.summary: Encodes preprocessed MS/MS spectra as bit-packed binary hypervectors (default D = 2048, Q = 16) using level-id HD encoding: XOR the ID hypervector of each peak m/z with the level hypervector of its intensity and bind all pairs with a pointwise majority function, then batch-encode on GPU for HyperSpec clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra have not been preprocessed yet — raw spectra must first go through HyperSpec's spectrum preprocessing (precursor/low-intensity peak removal, <5-peak/<250 Da range filtering, 50-peak cap, L2 normalization) and bucket division before encoding You need low-dimensional hashed spectral vectors rather than binary high-dimensional hypervectors — the article contrasts HDC encoding with hashing-based methods like msCRUSH and falcon

skills.description: Use when processing MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry data of cultured cells where per-cell metabolite assignment requires detecting laser ablation marks in post-MALDI microscopy and linking them to segmented cells.
skills.name: maldi-ablation-mark-detection-in-post-maldi-microscopy
skills.search_text: maldi-ablation-mark-detection-in-post-maldi-microscopy Use when processing MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry data of cultured cells where per-cell metabolite assignment requires detecting laser ablation marks in post-MALDI microscopy and linking them to segmented cells. Ablation marks are overlapping or not visible in the post-MALDI microscopy (README states this is critical and invalidates the registration) Aim is single-cell metabolomics of tissue sections or non-adhered cells rather than cultured cells acquired as tiled microscopy with fiducial pen marks You already have pre-stitched microscopy images — the current SpaceM implementation requires raw tiles and out.txt coordinates (a limitation of the implementation, not the method) http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Detect MALDI laser ablation marks in post-MALDI microscopy tiles and co-register them with pre-MALDI cell segmentations at subcellular precision, so that per-mark molecular profiles from METASPACE can be assigned to individual cells in the SpaceM pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Detect MALDI laser ablation marks in post-MALDI microscopy tiles and co-register them with pre-MALDI cell segmentations at subcellular precision, so that per-mark molecular profiles from METASPACE can be assigned to individual cells in the SpaceM pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ablation marks are overlapping or not visible in the post-MALDI microscopy (README states this is critical and invalidates the registration) Aim is single-cell metabolomics of tissue sections or non-adhered cells rather than cultured cells acquired as tiled microscopy with fiducial pen marks You already have pre-stitched microscopy images — the current SpaceM implementation requires raw tiles and out.txt coordinates (a limitation of the implementation, not the method)

skills.description: Use when raw imzML/HDF5 FT-ICR MSI data (e.g., tens of thousands of m/z variables) contains a specific candidate m/z (e.g., 400.9546) whose spatial pattern must be rendered as an ion image and compared against histology-annotated tumor regions.

skills.search_text: maldi-fticr-ion-image-extraction Use when raw imzML/HDF5 FT-ICR MSI data (e.g., tens of thousands of m/z variables) contains a specific candidate m/z (e.g., 400.9546) whose spatial pattern must be rendered as an ion image and compared against histology-annotated tumor regions. The data have already been peak-picked or reduced to a feature table, since this skill depends on extracting directly from raw spectral channels without preprocessing The goal is pixel-level tissue classification rather than visualizing the spatial distribution of a single candidate m/z peak The dataset is not spatially resolved MSI (no pixel coordinates), so no ion image can be reconstructed http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Extracts and spatially reconstructs a single m/z channel from raw high-resolution MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging data into a 2D ion image, without peak picking, to visualize the spatial distribution of a candidate tumor-associated peak. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Extracts and spatially reconstructs a single m/z channel from raw high-resolution MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging data into a 2D ion image, without peak picking, to visualize the spatial distribution of a candidate tumor-associated peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have already been peak-picked or reduced to a feature table, since this skill depends on extracting directly from raw spectral channels without preprocessing The goal is pixel-level tissue classification rather than visualizing the spatial distribution of a single candidate m/z peak The dataset is not spatially resolved MSI (no pixel coordinates), so no ion image can be reconstructed

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI-imaging data (*.RAW, *.UDP, *.imzML, *.ibd) plus tiled pre-/post-MALDI microscopy tiles with out.txt coordinates must be converted into a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix via the SpaceM pipeline.
skills.name: maldi-imaging-data-processing
skills.search_text: maldi-imaging-data-processing Use when raw MALDI-imaging data (*.RAW, *.UDP, *.imzML, *.ibd) plus tiled pre-/post-MALDI microscopy tiles with out.txt coordinates must be converted into a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix via the SpaceM pipeline. Microscopy is already pre-stitched rather than supplied as tiled acquisitions with out.txt coordinates (current code requires tile stitching and is optimized for Nikon Ti-E output format) Post-MALDI microscopy lacks visible or contains overlapping ablation marks, so per-cell metabolite intensity assignment cannot be trusted Data are not MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry of cultured cells paired with light microscopy (e.g., bulk LC-MS/MS tissue measurements or scRNA-seq) Runs the SpaceM single-cell metabolomics pipeline on paired MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry files (.RAW, .UDP, .imzML, .ibd) and tiled pre-/post-MALDI microscopy, producing a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) of normalized metabolite intensities plus microscopy-derived morphometric features. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Runs the SpaceM single-cell metabolomics pipeline on paired MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry files (.RAW, .UDP, .imzML, .ibd) and tiled pre-/post-MALDI microscopy, producing a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) of normalized metabolite intensities plus microscopy-derived morphometric features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Microscopy is already pre-stitched rather than supplied as tiled acquisitions with out.txt coordinates (current code requires tile stitching and is optimized for Nikon Ti-E output format) Post-MALDI microscopy lacks visible or contains overlapping ablation marks, so per-cell metabolite intensity assignment cannot be trusted Data are not MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry of cultured cells paired with light microscopy (e.g., bulk LC-MS/MS tissue measurements or scRNA-seq)

skills.description: Use when you have MALDI-AIF imzML data (e.g. 600-1600 m/z, negative mode) from 13C-labelled tissue and need spatial isotopologue ion images for fatty acids rather than METASPACE's natural-abundance-only annotations.
skills.name: maldi-imaging-isotopologue-extraction
skills.search_text: maldi-imaging-isotopologue-extraction Use when you have MALDI-AIF imzML data (e.g. 600-1600 m/z, negative mode) from 13C-labelled tissue and need spatial isotopologue ion images for fatty acids rather than METASPACE's natural-abundance-only annotations. Your annotations already come from METASPACE and you only need natural-abundance isotopologue distributions - METASPACE output suffices and the pyimzML extraction step is unnecessary. Overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia single-cell data): fitting a binomial distribution to estimate uptake fraction becomes unreliable and was only used for ACLYkd and brain data. You need absolute quantification of substrate contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool - the method provides only relative contributions since pool size cannot be quantified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Parse MALDI-imaging imzML files with pyimzML and extract per-pixel ion images for all isotopologues (M+0 to M+16+) of labelled fatty acids, so that natural-abundance correction and binomial fitting can quantify de novo synthesis versus uptake spatially, as done in 13C-SpaceM for U-13C-glucose-labelled glioma tissue. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Parse MALDI-imaging imzML files with pyimzML and extract per-pixel ion images for all isotopologues (M+0 to M+16+) of labelled fatty acids, so that natural-abundance correction and binomial fitting can quantify de novo synthesis versus uptake spatially, as done in 13C-SpaceM for U-13C-glucose-labelled glioma tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your annotations already come from METASPACE and you only need natural-abundance isotopologue distributions - METASPACE output suffices and the pyimzML extraction step is unnecessary. Overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia single-cell data): fitting a binomial distribution to estimate uptake fraction becomes unreliable and was only used for ACLYkd and brain data. You need absolute quantification of substrate contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool - the method provides only relative contributions since pool size cannot be quantified.

skills.description: Use when MALDI imaging data from 13C6-glucose-labeled tissue must be analyzed per pixel instead of per cell, to recover spatial maps of isotopologue distributions and binomial-fitted labelling probability p for fatty acids.
skills.name: maldi-imaging-pixelwise-isotope-tracing
skills.search_text: maldi-imaging-pixelwise-isotope-tracing Use when MALDI imaging data from 13C6-glucose-labeled tissue must be analyzed per pixel instead of per cell, to recover spatial maps of isotopologue distributions and binomial-fitted labelling probability p for fatty acids. When single-cell segmentation from co-registered microscopy is available — use the SpaceM single-cell workflow instead of pixel-wise analysis. When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiments): 'it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction'. When the goal is absolute quantification of substrate contribution — the method only provides relative contribution because the size of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool cannot be quantified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Analyzes MALDI imaging isotope-tracing data (MALDI-AIF after 13C6-glucose labeling) on a per-pixel basis: natural isotope abundance correction of each ion's isotopologue distribution followed by binomial-model fitting to estimate substrate contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool, producing spatial maps of heterogeneity in fatty acid synthesis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Analyzes MALDI imaging isotope-tracing data (MALDI-AIF after 13C6-glucose labeling) on a per-pixel basis: natural isotope abundance correction of each ion's isotopologue distribution followed by binomial-model fitting to estimate substrate contribution to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool, producing spatial maps of heterogeneity in fatty acid synthesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When single-cell segmentation from co-registered microscopy is available — use the SpaceM single-cell workflow instead of pixel-wise analysis. When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiments): 'it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction'. When the goal is absolute quantification of substrate contribution — the method only provides relative contribution because the size of the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool cannot be quantified.

skills.description: Use when processing MALDI imaging mass spectrometry isotope-tracing data (imzML files, e.g. 13C6-glucose-labelled tissue) at pixel rather than single-cell level, to obtain corrected, normalized isotopologue distributions for fatty acids per pixel.
skills.name: maldi-imaging-pixelwise-isotopologue-normalization
skills.search_text: maldi-imaging-pixelwise-isotopologue-normalization Use when processing MALDI imaging mass spectrometry isotope-tracing data (imzML files, e.g. 13C6-glucose-labelled tissue) at pixel rather than single-cell level, to obtain corrected, normalized isotopologue distributions for fatty acids per pixel. When analysing single-cell (per-cell) data from SpaceM output rather than raw tissue MALDI images — use the per-cell sc_analysis.py workflow with natural abundance correction, median signal averaging per cell, and per-cell normalization instead. When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiments), where the article states it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction. When absolute substrate contributions to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool are needed — the method provides only relative contributions since the pool size cannot be quantified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Per-pixel analysis of MALDI imaging isotope-tracing data: natural isotope abundance correction and normalization of fatty acid isotopologue distributions at each pixel of an imzML image, enabling spatial comparison of 13C-glucose-derived labelling between tumour and surrounding brain tissue. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4
skills.summary: Per-pixel analysis of MALDI imaging isotope-tracing data: natural isotope abundance correction and normalization of fatty acid isotopologue distributions at each pixel of an imzML image, enabling spatial comparison of 13C-glucose-derived labelling between tumour and surrounding brain tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When analysing single-cell (per-cell) data from SpaceM output rather than raw tissue MALDI images — use the per-cell sc_analysis.py workflow with natural abundance correction, median signal averaging per cell, and per-cell normalization instead. When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiments), where the article states it becomes impossible to reliably fit a binomial distribution and estimate the uptake fraction. When absolute substrate contributions to the lipogenic acetyl-CoA pool are needed — the method provides only relative contributions since the pool size cannot be quantified.

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI-MS or ESI-MS spectra with mismatched, irregularly-spaced m/z grids must be organized into one m/z-by-replicate data frame before smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection, or normalization (e.g., rel_TIC).
skills.name: maldi-intensity-data-frame-organization
skills.search_text: maldi-intensity-data-frame-organization Use when raw MALDI-MS or ESI-MS spectra with mismatched, irregularly-spaced m/z grids must be organized into one m/z-by-replicate data frame before smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection, or normalization (e.g., rel_TIC). Data are already aligned on a common m/z grid and stored in a tidy table — re-alignment is unnecessary The workflow requires S3/S4 class-based pipelines (e.g., MSnbase or MALDIquant object models) rather than accessible data frames Data are not mass spectrometry spectra with m/z and intensity columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Organizes irregularly-spaced MALDI-MS/ESI-MS spectra into a single rectangular data frame using the subMALDI R package, with all m/z values in the first column and each spectral replicate's intensities in adjacent columns, without hiding data in S3/S4 objects. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02694
skills.summary: Organizes irregularly-spaced MALDI-MS/ESI-MS spectra into a single rectangular data frame using the subMALDI R package, with all m/z values in the first column and each spectral replicate's intensities in adjacent columns, without hiding data in S3/S4 objects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already aligned on a common m/z grid and stored in a tidy table — re-alignment is unnecessary The workflow requires S3/S4 class-based pipelines (e.g., MSnbase or MALDIquant object models) rather than accessible data frames Data are not mass spectrometry spectra with m/z and intensity columns

skills.description: Use when annotating MALDI-imaging datasets where matrix cluster ions (e.g., from 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid) may pollute annotations, and a predicted list of matrix cluster formulas is needed to match recognized off-sample signals.
skills.name: maldi-matrix-cluster-modeling
skills.search_text: maldi-matrix-cluster-modeling Use when annotating MALDI-imaging datasets where matrix cluster ions (e.g., from 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid) may pollute annotations, and a predicted list of matrix cluster formulas is needed to match recognized off-sample signals. The MALDI matrix is not DHB and no analogous cluster-generating model is available for it — the Keller and Li (2000) parameterization is specific to DHB-derived clusters The goal is detecting analyte metabolites rather than matrix/off-sample cluster ions — use the standard METASPACE annotation database instead Segmenting individual off-sample pixels is required — this skill models cluster formulas only and 'does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Enumerate candidate MALDI matrix cluster ion molecular formulas using a combinatorial cluster-generating model (Keller and Li, 2000), here applied to the DHB matrix, to build a custom molecular database for annotating matrix/off-sample signals in METASPACE MALDI-imaging data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: Enumerate candidate MALDI matrix cluster ion molecular formulas using a combinatorial cluster-generating model (Keller and Li, 2000), here applied to the DHB matrix, to build a custom molecular database for annotating matrix/off-sample signals in METASPACE MALDI-imaging data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MALDI matrix is not DHB and no analogous cluster-generating model is available for it — the Keller and Li (2000) parameterization is specific to DHB-derived clusters The goal is detecting analyte metabolites rather than matrix/off-sample cluster ions — use the standard METASPACE annotation database instead Segmenting individual off-sample pixels is required — this skill models cluster formulas only and 'does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region'

skills.search_text: maldi-msi-group-comparison-statistics Use when you have segmented, ROI-annotated MSI pixel-intensity data from two sample groups and need per-lipid fold-change/p-value statistics per tissue region with volcano plots. skills.summary: Automated registration of immunofluorescence microscopy (IFM) images to high-resolution MALDI MSI data and handling of the registered multimodal outputs via msiFlow's `msi_if_registration_flow`, enabling pixel-level mapping of spatial lipidomic signatures to specific cell populations (e.g. Ly6G+ neutrophils) in infected bladder tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MSI and IFM already share the same coordinate system or you have reliable landmark-based registration features or laser ablation marks — msiFlow's automated architecture-based registration may be less accurate than landmark-based approaches in that setting You need lipid annotation/interpretation — msiFlow explicitly does not include an annotation or interpretation step, only pattern identification and preliminary candidates Input is already a registered, segmented feature table ready for clustering — use the segmentation or molecular_heterogeneity_flow workflows instead of re-registering

skills.description: Use when a MALDI-MS data frame holds multiple replicate intensity columns (e.g. matrix blanks or technical replicates) on a shared m/z grid and you need one averaged intensity column before subtraction, normalization, or plotting.
skills.name: maldi-spectral-replicate-averaging
skills.search_text: maldi-spectral-replicate-averaging Use when a MALDI-MS data frame holds multiple replicate intensity columns (e.g. matrix blanks or technical replicates) on a shared m/z grid and you need one averaged intensity column before subtraction, normalization, or plotting. The spectra are irregularly spaced or on different m/z grids — align to a resolution-specified m/z grid first; averaging misaligned columns will mix non-corresponding m/z values You need to preserve each replicate separately (e.g. for replicate-level variability assessment or TIC/normalization per spectrum) rather than collapse them The data are wrapped in S3/S4 objects from other packages (e.g. MALDIquant, MSnbase) without first converting to the plain data-frame layout subMALDI expects http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Averaging replicate mass spectra (e.g. matrix blank replicates 'Blank1'/'Blank2', or sample replicates) into a single intensity column using subMALDI's avgSpectra with the mean method, keeping m/z in the first column and intensities in adjacent columns so downstream subSpectra can consume the averaged column. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02694
skills.summary: Averaging replicate mass spectra (e.g. matrix blank replicates 'Blank1'/'Blank2', or sample replicates) into a single intensity column using subMALDI's avgSpectra with the mean method, keeping m/z in the first column and intensities in adjacent columns so downstream subSpectra can consume the averaged column.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are irregularly spaced or on different m/z grids — align to a resolution-specified m/z grid first; averaging misaligned columns will mix non-corresponding m/z values You need to preserve each replicate separately (e.g. for replicate-level variability assessment or TIC/normalization per spectrum) rather than collapse them The data are wrapped in S3/S4 objects from other packages (e.g. MALDIquant, MSnbase) without first converting to the plain data-frame layout subMALDI expects

skills.search_text: maldi-tof-spectral-ion-count-extraction Use when MALDI-TOF spectra have been acquired over a library or array of targets (e.g., 749 yeast SSM colonies or nL droplet arrays) and per-target ion intensities at specific fatty acyl m/z values must be tabulated and ratio-ranked. skills.summary: Extract ion counts at target m/z values (e.g., C16:1 and C18:1 fatty acyl fragments) from MALDI-TOF mass spectra of hundreds of screened samples using macroMS data-analysis tools, then compute per-sample intensity ratios for screening and ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targets are smaller than 300 μm, where the article states the microscope-guided microMS suite is more effective The analysis goal is full spectrum identification or de novo peak annotation rather than targeted ion-count extraction at a few known m/z values Only a handful of samples are involved and building an optical image-guided coordinate file via macroMS would add overhead without benefit

skills.description: Use when you have a permethylated released N-glycan MALDI-TOF spectrum (e.g., Super-DHB matrix) and need to assign glycan identities to detected peaks by accurate-mass search against a glycan mass database, replacing manual peak-by-peak analysis.
skills.name: maldi-tof-spectral-peak-detection
skills.search_text: maldi-tof-spectral-peak-detection Use when you have a permethylated released N-glycan MALDI-TOF spectrum (e.g., Super-DHB matrix) and need to assign glycan identities to detected peaks by accurate-mass search against a glycan mass database, replacing manual peak-by-peak analysis. The data are LC-MS/MS Orbitrap (OrbiTrap) acquisitions of fluorescent-labeled N-glycans — use the app's MS1 and MS2 Peak Confirmation tabs instead of the MALDI Peak ID tab. The glycans of interest are O-linked, or absent from the database — the app's scope is N-linked glycans and has no de novo identification capability. The goal is MS/MS fragment annotation rather than intact-mass peak identification. Automated detection and identification of glycan peaks in permethylated N-linked glycan MALDI-TOF spectra using the GlyKAn AZ MATLAB app's MALDI Peak ID tab, which matches observed peak masses against a glycan mass database of theoretical masses (Da) and reproduces manual analyst assignments. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Automated detection and identification of glycan peaks in permethylated N-linked glycan MALDI-TOF spectra using the GlyKAn AZ MATLAB app's MALDI Peak ID tab, which matches observed peak masses against a glycan mass database of theoretical masses (Da) and reproduces manual analyst assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are LC-MS/MS Orbitrap (OrbiTrap) acquisitions of fluorescent-labeled N-glycans — use the app's MS1 and MS2 Peak Confirmation tabs instead of the MALDI Peak ID tab. The glycans of interest are O-linked, or absent from the database — the app's scope is N-linked glycans and has no de novo identification capability. The goal is MS/MS fragment annotation rather than intact-mass peak identification.

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI spectra (m/z + intensity data frames) show an irregular baseline and you need combined baseline correction plus peak detection without masking data into S3/S4 objects.
skills.name: maldim-spectral-baseline-correction
skills.search_text: maldim-spectral-baseline-correction Use when raw MALDI spectra (m/z + intensity data frames) show an irregular baseline and you need combined baseline correction plus peak detection without masking data into S3/S4 objects. Input is not raw spectral data but an already peak-picked or feature-aligned table — subMALDI's pre-processing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection) targets raw spectra The spectra are regularly spaced and already processed into another R framework's S3/S4 class objects that you do not want to unmask You only need normalization or replicate alignment to an m/z grid, not baseline correction or peak detection Corrects the irregular baseline of raw MALDI mass spectra and performs peak detection in one step by combining subMALDI's plain data-frame spectral structure with the MassSpecWavelet continuous wavelet transform (CWT) pipeline, then filtering peaks by signal-to-noise ratio. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02694
skills.summary: Corrects the irregular baseline of raw MALDI mass spectra and performs peak detection in one step by combining subMALDI's plain data-frame spectral structure with the MassSpecWavelet continuous wavelet transform (CWT) pipeline, then filtering peaks by signal-to-noise ratio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw spectral data but an already peak-picked or feature-aligned table — subMALDI's pre-processing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection) targets raw spectra The spectra are regularly spaced and already processed into another R framework's S3/S4 class objects that you do not want to unmask You only need normalization or replicate alignment to an m/z grid, not baseline correction or peak detection

skills.search_text: maml-1d-cnn-backbone-selection Use when building a MAML meta-learning classifier for single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics data and you must decide which 1D-CNN backbone to adopt before full-scale meta-training with limited cells. Input data are bulk omics profiles or already-labeled large feature matrices — the comparison targets limited-sample SCMS single-cell metabolomics where ambient methods yield relatively small cell numbers The classification goal involves cell pairs with high metabolomic similarity that PCA can discriminate easily — a simpler model comparison may suffice You need image (2D) or sequence inputs — these backbones are 1D-CNNs designed for 1D SCMS spectral signals http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark 1D-CNN backbones (Lecun, LeNet, VGG9) inside the MAML-based MetaPhenotype framework on untreated IGR39/IGR37 SCMS metabolomics data across 1-, 5-, and 10-shot meta-training settings, and select the backbone (LeNet) that best balances meta-evaluation accuracy and computational efficiency. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Benchmark 1D-CNN backbones (Lecun, LeNet, VGG9) inside the MAML-based MetaPhenotype framework on untreated IGR39/IGR37 SCMS metabolomics data across 1-, 5-, and 10-shot meta-training settings, and select the backbone (LeNet) that best balances meta-evaluation accuracy and computational efficiency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are bulk omics profiles or already-labeled large feature matrices — the comparison targets limited-sample SCMS single-cell metabolomics where ambient methods yield relatively small cell numbers The classification goal involves cell pairs with high metabolomic similarity that PCA can discriminate easily — a simpler model comparison may suffice You need image (2D) or sequence inputs — these backbones are 1D-CNNs designed for 1D SCMS spectral signals

skills.description: Decision support for quantifying spatial correlation between two LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g. 55Mn vs 66Zn) when reporting colocalisation coefficients such as Manders, Li ICQ, or Pearson R.
skills.name: manders-costes-threshold-colocalisation-analysis
skills.search_text: manders-costes-threshold-colocalisation-analysis Decision support for quantifying spatial correlation between two LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g. 55Mn vs 66Zn) when reporting colocalisation coefficients such as Manders, Li ICQ, or Pearson R. The input is a single-channel image or the two channels have mismatched pixel dimensions — coefficients require pixelwise comparison of two aligned channels You only need visual colocalisation inspection, e.g. an RGB overlay (55Mn red, 56Fe green, 66Zn blue) without quantitative coefficients The task is segmentation or ROI isolation rather than overlap quantification — use Pew2's thresholding/k-means tools instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Threshold-dependent colocalisation analysis implemented in Pew2 that computes Manders overlap coefficients via the Costes method (doi 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422) to quantify the spatial relationship between two LA-ICP-MS elemental image channels, alongside Li ICQ and Pearson R (with shuffle-based ρ probability). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Threshold-dependent colocalisation analysis implemented in Pew2 that computes Manders overlap coefficients via the Costes method (doi 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422) to quantify the spatial relationship between two LA-ICP-MS elemental image channels, alongside Li ICQ and Pearson R (with shuffle-based ρ probability).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-channel image or the two channels have mismatched pixel dimensions — coefficients require pixelwise comparison of two aligned channels You only need visual colocalisation inspection, e.g. an RGB overlay (55Mn red, 56Fe green, 66Zn blue) without quantitative coefficients The task is segmentation or ROI isolation rather than overlap quantification — use Pew2's thresholding/k-means tools instead

skills.description: Use when comparing two groups (e.g. COPD vs control, mild vs severe COVID-19) on pathway-score or molecular-level matrices to estimate what fraction of features separates groups under controlled effect sizes.
skills.name: mann-whitney-u-group-comparison
skills.search_text: mann-whitney-u-group-comparison Use when comparing two groups (e.g. COPD vs control, mild vs severe COVID-19) on pathway-score or molecular-level matrices to estimate what fraction of features separates groups under controlled effect sizes. When the goal is predictive multi-omics modelling rather than univariate power assessment — PathIntegrate Single-View or Multi-View supervised models are the appropriate framework. When molecules cannot be reliably mapped to pathways (poor pathway coverage/annotation), since the advantage of grouping molecules into pathways depends on usable pathway definitions. When comparing more than two groups or needing multivariate interaction modelling — MWU is a two-sample univariate test. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Applies Mann-Whitney-U (MWU) univariate tests to ssPA pathway-transformed multi-omics scores to quantify group-separation power, as used in PathIntegrate's semi-synthetic benchmarks where pathway transformation detected more significant signals than molecular-level Fisher-combined testing at effect sizes 0.25–0.55. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Applies Mann-Whitney-U (MWU) univariate tests to ssPA pathway-transformed multi-omics scores to quantify group-separation power, as used in PathIntegrate's semi-synthetic benchmarks where pathway transformation detected more significant signals than molecular-level Fisher-combined testing at effect sizes 0.25–0.55.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is predictive multi-omics modelling rather than univariate power assessment — PathIntegrate Single-View or Multi-View supervised models are the appropriate framework. When molecules cannot be reliably mapped to pathways (poor pathway coverage/annotation), since the advantage of grouping molecules into pathways depends on usable pathway definitions. When comparing more than two groups or needing multivariate interaction modelling — MWU is a two-sample univariate test.

skills.description: Reference for testing whether median feature intensities differ across outcome categories (correct vs incorrect vs no annotation) when you need a nonparametric, rank-based significance test rather than a parametric t-test.
skills.name: mann-whitney-u-test-statistics
skills.search_text: mann-whitney-u-test-statistics Reference for testing whether median feature intensities differ across outcome categories (correct vs incorrect vs no annotation) when you need a nonparametric, rank-based significance test rather than a parametric t-test. When the comparison groups are derived from the same feature measured under paired conditions — use a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired t-test instead When feature intensities are known to be approximately normal and equal-variance across groups, a t-test yields more power at the same sample size When the goal is to compare annotation success rates (proportions) rather than intensity distributions — use a chi-squared or Fisher's exact test http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Mann–Whitney U statistics are used to determine whether feature intensity distributions differ significantly across annotation outcome classes, with the p<0.05 significance threshold indicating where MetaboAnnotatoR's rank-1 annotations are intensity-dependent rather than class-independent. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Mann–Whitney U statistics are used to determine whether feature intensity distributions differ significantly across annotation outcome classes, with the p<0.05 significance threshold indicating where MetaboAnnotatoR's rank-1 annotations are intensity-dependent rather than class-independent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison groups are derived from the same feature measured under paired conditions — use a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired t-test instead When feature intensities are known to be approximately normal and equal-variance across groups, a t-test yields more power at the same sample size When the goal is to compare annotation success rates (proportions) rather than intensity distributions — use a chi-squared or Fisher's exact test

No manually annotated library analytes exist for the dataset — the evaluation would have no ground truth to match against The goal is de novo feature alignment or quantification rather than scoring an alignment method's accuracy against a reference Input is a single-run feature table with no multi-run alignment to evaluate http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates LC–MS feature alignment accuracy by matching algorithm-aligned consensus features against a manually annotated ground-truth dataset (m/z, RT, area of library analytes), counting accurately aligned features and analytes. Provides the ground-truth-based validation used to benchmark G-Aligner against MZmine2, OpenMS, and XCMS. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Evaluates LC–MS feature alignment accuracy by matching algorithm-aligned consensus features against a manually annotated ground-truth dataset (m/z, RT, area of library analytes), counting accurately aligned features and analytes. skills.description: Use when MSIght's automated affine registration of an MSI image to an H&E stain fails—e.g., when phase cross correlation does not minimize SSD sufficiently and tissue masks do not overlap—requiring manual landmark placement.
skills.name: manual-landmark-affine-transform-selection
skills.search_text: manual-landmark-affine-transform-selection Use when MSIght's automated affine registration of an MSI image to an H&E stain fails—e.g., when phase cross correlation does not minimize SSD sufficiently and tissue masks do not overlap—requiring manual landmark placement. When the automated phase-cross-correlation affine transform (register_he_msi) already yields a satisfactory overlap between H&E foreground and MSI tissue mask—manual landmarks are only the fallback. For non-linear distortions within the tissue (folds, tears, local warping): manual affine is coarse and should be followed by the B-spline refinement (perform_bspline), not used alone. When H&E and MSI derive from adjacent, not identical, tissue sections with grossly different morphology, since manual landmark pairing becomes unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 A fallback registration procedure within MSIght in which the analyst hand-selects paired MSI/H&E landmarks to derive a manual affine transform when automated phase-cross-correlation minimization of SSD fails to align the moving MSI image to the fixed H&E image. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: A fallback registration procedure within MSIght in which the analyst hand-selects paired MSI/H&E landmarks to derive a manual affine transform when automated phase-cross-correlation minimization of SSD fails to align the moving MSI image to the fixed H&E image.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the automated phase-cross-correlation affine transform (register_he_msi) already yields a satisfactory overlap between H&E foreground and MSI tissue mask—manual landmarks are only the fallback. For non-linear distortions within the tissue (folds, tears, local warping): manual affine is coarse and should be followed by the B-spline refinement (perform_bspline), not used alone. When H&E and MSI derive from adjacent, not identical, tissue sections with grossly different morphology, since manual landmark pairing becomes unreliable.

skills.description: Use when a matchMz()/matchSpectra() call has returned a Matched result object and the many-to-many peak-to-compound matches must be converted into a tabular annotation table (one row per match, NA for unmatched) for CSV export or downstream QC.

skills.search_text: many-to-many-match-result-extraction Use when a matchMz()/matchSpectra() call has returned a Matched result object and the many-to-many peak-to-compound matches must be converted into a tabular annotation table (one row per match, NA for unmatched) for CSV export or downstream QC. When a one-to-one best-candidate assignment per feature is required; this extraction preserves the many-to-many nature of m/z-only matching. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Extracts a flat, one-row-per-match annotation table from a MetaboAnnotation Matched result object (e.g. the many-to-many peak-to-compound mapping produced by matchMz with Mass2MzParam), using matchedData() and exporting columns such as peak_id, target_name, target_formula, adduct, score and ppm_error to CSV. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12020173
skills.summary: Extracts a flat, one-row-per-match annotation table from a MetaboAnnotation Matched result object (e.g. the many-to-many peak-to-compound mapping produced by matchMz with Mass2MzParam), using matchedData() and exporting columns such as peak_id, target_name, target_formula, adduct, score and ppm_error to CSV.

When a one-to-one best-candidate assignment per feature is required; this extraction preserves the many-to-many nature of m/z-only matching.

skills.name: map-bayesian-estimation
skills.search_text: map-bayesian-estimation Use when individual PK parameters (CL, V, etas) must be estimated from patient TDM concentrations given a user-defined population PK model, or when validating/replicating NONMEM MAP-BE results in R for MIPD workflows. The goal is population PK/PD model building or parameter estimation at the population level — use nlmixr or saemix instead, as mapbayr is dedicated to individual MAP-BE The Bayesian estimation design (residual error, sampling schedule) has not been previously validated for the intended dosing/sampling strategy Quantification of estimation uncertainty (e.g. Fisher information matrix, posterior sampling) is required — not implemented in the current mapbayr version http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 http://edamontology.org/topic_3077 Perform maximum a posteriori Bayesian estimation (MAP-BE) of individual PK parameters in R with mapbayr: code the model in mrgsolve, format dosing/observations in NM-TRAN style, and minimize the objective function over etas with L-BFGS-B, replicating NONMEM-grade estimation without external software. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/psp4.12689

skills.search_text: mapping-rate-aggregation-statistics Use when you need to measure how consistently MetaFetcheR resolves metabolite identifiers across the five supported small-compound databases, e.g. to validate a populated PostgreSQL cache or compare mapping quality per source database. The PostgreSQL cache is empty or incompletely populated (bulk_insert_hmdb, bulk_insert_chebi, bulk_insert_lipidmaps, bulk_insert_secondary_ids have not been run) — sampling random identifiers from an unpopulated database yields meaningless rates The goal is mapping metabolite identifiers for a downstream analysis (e.g. pathway enrichment) rather than benchmarking mapping quality — use the standard MetaFetcheR mapping workflow instead The identifier source is user-supplied experimental data rather than randomly sampled identifiers from the five supported databases — the test's rates only characterize the databases themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Quantifies the reliability of MetaFetcheR's cross-database identifier mapping by repeatedly resolving randomly sampled identifiers from HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG and LIPID MAPS and computing per-database consistency, ambiguity, and unresolved rates.
