skills.name: mass-spectral-binning-0-1-da
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-binning-0-1-da Use when comparing predicted tandem mass spectra (from ICEBERG or baseline simulators) against ground-truth library spectra and you need a dataset-wide average cosine similarity on a common binned representation. NPLIB1 support has been retired on the ms-pred main branch — use the iceberg_1.0 branch for NPLIB1 (CANOPUS) evaluation, or switch to NIST20/23 on main When the goal is fragment-level structural interpretation rather than scalar spectrum-level accuracy — binned cosine similarity cannot judge whether breakage-event explanations are physically correct When comparing predictors that operate on different fragmentation granularities without first mapping all outputs to a shared binned representation Bins predicted and experimental MS/MS peak lists into 0.1-Da intensity vectors and computes vectorized cosine similarity, the evaluation convention used to benchmark ICEBERG against MassFormer, FixedVocab, SCARF, NEIMS, and CFM-ID on NPLIB1 and NIST20. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Bins predicted and experimental MS/MS peak lists into 0.1-Da intensity vectors and computes vectorized cosine similarity, the evaluation convention used to benchmark ICEBERG against MassFormer, FixedVocab, SCARF, NEIMS, and CFM-ID on NPLIB1 and NIST20.
skills.when_to_use_negative: NPLIB1 support has been retired on the ms-pred main branch — use the iceberg_1.0 branch for NPLIB1 (CANOPUS) evaluation, or switch to NIST20/23 on main When the goal is fragment-level structural interpretation rather than scalar spectrum-level accuracy — binned cosine similarity cannot judge whether breakage-event explanations are physically correct When comparing predictors that operate on different fragmentation granularities without first mapping all outputs to a shared binned representation

skills.description: Use when the input is an unlabeled EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS positive-mode mass spectrum (structure unknown or 'dark' metabolome) and the goal is a bitter/non-bitter class prediction directly from spectral features.
skills.name: mass-spectral-bitterness-classification
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-bitterness-classification Use when the input is an unlabeled EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS positive-mode mass spectrum (structure unknown or 'dark' metabolome) and the goal is a bitter/non-bitter class prediction directly from spectral features. When the chemical structure is already known and descriptors can be computed — BitterPredict predicts bitterness from structure and is the appropriate tool instead When spectra are in negative ion mode — the model makes predictions based on EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS spectra obtained in positive ion mode only When training only on the EI-MS-only or ESI-MS/MS-only subset — prediction on individual sets showed poor results compared with the combined set http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 BitterMasS-style direct prediction of bitter vs non-bitter compounds from EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS (positive ion mode) mass spectra, using a Random Forest classifier trained on 5414 experimental MassBank spectra, avoiding the lossy spectrum-to-structure-to-bitterness detour. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jafc.3c09767
skills.summary: BitterMasS-style direct prediction of bitter vs non-bitter compounds from EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS (positive ion mode) mass spectra, using a Random Forest classifier trained on 5414 experimental MassBank spectra, avoiding the lossy spectrum-to-structure-to-bitterness detour.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the chemical structure is already known and descriptors can be computed — BitterPredict predicts bitterness from structure and is the appropriate tool instead When spectra are in negative ion mode — the model makes predictions based on EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS spectra obtained in positive ion mode only When training only on the EI-MS-only or ESI-MS/MS-only subset — prediction on individual sets showed poor results compared with the combined set

skills.description: Use when you have computed MS2DeepScore embeddings for annotated MS/MS spectra (e.g. a 3601-spectrum test set with InChIKeys) and need to verify or display that the embeddings group spectra by chemical superclass.
skills.name: mass-spectral-clustering-visualization
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-clustering-visualization Use when you have computed MS2DeepScore embeddings for annotated MS/MS spectra (e.g. a 3601-spectrum test set with InChIKeys) and need to verify or display that the embeddings group spectra by chemical superclass. When the goal is a similarity-score matrix between spectra pairs rather than an embedding-space visualization — use the MS2DeepScore model score computation instead When spectra lack InChIKey/structural annotations, since superclass coloring and the chemical-clustering check cannot be performed When embeddings come from a non-MS2DeepScore pipeline with different dimensionality or binning; the 200-dim cosine t-SNE setup is specific to this embedding space http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Visualize chemically meaningful structure in MS2DeepScore 200-dimensional spectrum embeddings by projecting them to 2D with t-SNE and coloring points by ClassyFire chemical superclass, to check that spectra of the same chemical (super)class cluster together. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Visualize chemically meaningful structure in MS2DeepScore 200-dimensional spectrum embeddings by projecting them to 2D with t-SNE and coloring points by ClassyFire chemical superclass, to check that spectra of the same chemical (super)class cluster together.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a similarity-score matrix between spectra pairs rather than an embedding-space visualization — use the MS2DeepScore model score computation instead When spectra lack InChIKey/structural annotations, since superclass coloring and the chemical-clustering check cannot be performed When embeddings come from a non-MS2DeepScore pipeline with different dimensionality or binning; the 200-dim cosine t-SNE setup is specific to this embedding space

skills.description: Use when you have unlabeled MS1/MS2 features from herbal or TCM plasma/tissue samples and need to bridge in vivo metabolites back to prototype components without predicting structures beforehand.
skills.name: mass-spectral-data-post-processing
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-data-post-processing Use when you have unlabeled MS1/MS2 features from herbal or TCM plasma/tissue samples and need to bridge in vivo metabolites back to prototype components without predicting structures beforehand. Input is already a curated, annotated metabolite list with established prototype-metabolite assignments — no bridging is required The MS acquisition lacks MS2 fragment data, since MDRB requires the similarity of MS2 fragments as one of its three scoring dimensions The goal is targeted quantification of known compounds rather than non-targeted identification and bridging of unknown metabolites http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Post-process LC-MS metabolomics datasets with the R-based MDRB (mass dataset relevance bridging) technique, which scores metabolite-prototype pairs by sequentially integrating m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, and MS2 fragment similarity to bridge prototypes and metabolites of TCM samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Post-process LC-MS metabolomics datasets with the R-based MDRB (mass dataset relevance bridging) technique, which scores metabolite-prototype pairs by sequentially integrating m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, and MS2 fragment similarity to bridge prototypes and metabolites of TCM samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated, annotated metabolite list with established prototype-metabolite assignments — no bridging is required The MS acquisition lacks MS2 fragment data, since MDRB requires the similarity of MS2 fragments as one of its three scoring dimensions The goal is targeted quantification of known compounds rather than non-targeted identification and bridging of unknown metabolites

skills.description: Use when you have a curated compound list with labels or properties of interest and need the corresponding experimental mass spectra (EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS, positive ion mode) to run a spectrum-based prediction model, and the compounds' spectra are known to be deposited in MassBank or DrugBank.
skills.name: mass-spectral-database-retrieval
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-database-retrieval Use when you have a curated compound list with labels or properties of interest and need the corresponding experimental mass spectra (EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS, positive ion mode) to run a spectrum-based prediction model, and the compounds' spectra are known to be deposited in MassBank or DrugBank. When the chemical structure of each compound is already known and a structure-based classifier (e.g., BitterPredict) is sufficient — the article's discussion notes the spectrum-to-structure-to-bitterness route is 'the most problematic stage' and covers fewer compounds When the compounds of interest have no deposited spectra in MassBank or DrugBank — retrieval will return nothing and the downstream spectrum-based model cannot be applied When only negative-ion-mode spectra are available — the article's BitterMasS implementation makes predictions based on spectra 'obtained in positive ion mode' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retrieve experimental positive-ion-mode EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS spectra for a curated compound list from the MassBank database (supplemented by DrugBank spectra for medication and vitamin categories), so that spectra can be fed to a downstream classifier such as BitterMasS. This is the data-acquisition step that turned sensory-labeled compounds into 759 spectra covering 106 compounds for BitterMasS external testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jafc.3c09767
skills.summary: Retrieve experimental positive-ion-mode EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS spectra for a curated compound list from the MassBank database (supplemented by DrugBank spectra for medication and vitamin categories), so that spectra can be fed to a downstream classifier such as BitterMasS. This is the data-acquisition step that turned sensory-labeled compounds into 759 spectra covering 106 compounds for BitterMasS external testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the chemical structure of each compound is already known and a structure-based classifier (e.g., BitterPredict) is sufficient — the article's discussion notes the spectrum-to-structure-to-bitterness route is 'the most problematic stage' and covers fewer compounds When the compounds of interest have no deposited spectra in MassBank or DrugBank — retrieval will return nothing and the downstream spectrum-based model cannot be applied When only negative-ion-mode spectra are available — the article's BitterMasS implementation makes predictions based on spectra 'obtained in positive ion mode'

skills.description: Use when experimental tandem MS spectra need to be matched to known molecules or previously unreported molecule variants from databases such as PubChem, COCONUT, or NPAtlas, especially at atlas scale (e.g. 483M GNPS spectra vs 87M molecules).
skills.name: mass-spectral-database-search
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-database-search Use when experimental tandem MS spectra need to be matched to known molecules or previously unreported molecule variants from databases such as PubChem, COCONUT, or NPAtlas, especially at atlas scale (e.g. 483M GNPS spectra vs 87M molecules). The spectra have already been preprocessed locally — in that case the README says the advanced peak-merging and peak-filtering settings should be changed rather than left at defaults, and blindly applying defaults may double-preprocess peaks. The goal is de novo sequencing or structural elucidation without any candidate molecule database — this skill scores spectra against a fixed candidate database and cannot produce identifications absent a molecular library. The input data kind is not mass spectra (e.g. already a feature table or metabolite intensity matrix) — VInSMoC requires MGF, mzXML, or mzML spectral inputs uploaded as 'Mass Spectrum' data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Scores query mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, mzML) against a database of candidate molecules using VInSMoC on the run.npanalysis.org server, matching precursor masses in exact mode or explaining precursor mass differences via molecule variants in variable mode, with Markov chain Monte Carlo P values to control false identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Scores query mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, mzML) against a database of candidate molecules using VInSMoC on the run.npanalysis.org server, matching precursor masses in exact mode or explaining precursor mass differences via molecule variants in variable mode, with Markov chain Monte Carlo P values to control false identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra have already been preprocessed locally — in that case the README says the advanced peak-merging and peak-filtering settings should be changed rather than left at defaults, and blindly applying defaults may double-preprocess peaks. The goal is de novo sequencing or structural elucidation without any candidate molecule database — this skill scores spectra against a fixed candidate database and cannot produce identifications absent a molecular library. The input data kind is not mass spectra (e.g. already a feature table or metabolite intensity matrix) — VInSMoC requires MGF, mzXML, or mzML spectral inputs uploaded as 'Mass Spectrum' data.

skills.description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be annotated by searching against a large molecular structure database (e.g., DNP, PubChem, MoNA) and candidate structures need probabilistic scoring plus FDR-estimated identifications.
skills.name: mass-spectral-database-search
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-database-search Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be annotated by searching against a large molecular structure database (e.g., DNP, PubChem, MoNA) and candidate structures need probabilistic scoring plus FDR-estimated identifications. A reference spectral library contains the molecule — spectral library search is the most reliable annotation method and should be preferred over in silico database search De novo structure prediction is required for molecules absent from known databases — this skill only annotates spectra against known structure databases Peptidic p-value computation or experiment-specific fragmentation modeling (instrument type, dissociation technique, collision energy) is required — molDiscovery's default model covers only a limited number of bond types and rearrangement rules and was trained on combined CID/HCD positive-mode spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Probabilistic tandem mass spectral search of small molecules against molecular structure databases using molDiscovery, which learns a fragmentation model P(logRank|bondType, logRankpa) from training molecule-spectrum pairs and scores candidates by log-likelihood ratio with target-decoy FDR estimation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Probabilistic tandem mass spectral search of small molecules against molecular structure databases using molDiscovery, which learns a fragmentation model P(logRank|bondType, logRankpa) from training molecule-spectrum pairs and scores candidates by log-likelihood ratio with target-decoy FDR estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference spectral library contains the molecule — spectral library search is the most reliable annotation method and should be preferred over in silico database search De novo structure prediction is required for molecules absent from known databases — this skill only annotates spectra against known structure databases Peptidic p-value computation or experiment-specific fragmentation modeling (instrument type, dissociation technique, collision energy) is required — molDiscovery's default model covers only a limited number of bond types and rearrangement rules and was trained on combined CID/HCD positive-mode spectra

skills.description: Use when integrating multiple OMSLs (e.g., GNPS .MGF, MoNA .MSP, MassBank, MS-Dial-VS17) and you need to measure cross-library redundancy: the fraction of unique chemicals shared between two or more libraries and per-library duplicate spectra counts.
skills.name: mass-spectral-duplicate-counting
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-duplicate-counting Use when integrating multiple OMSLs (e.g., GNPS .MGF, MoNA .MSP, MassBank, MS-Dial-VS17) and you need to measure cross-library redundancy: the fraction of unique chemicals shared between two or more libraries and per-library duplicate spectra counts. When the input is a single library with no cross-source integration question — overlap and redundancy statistics are only meaningful across multiple sources When chemical identifiers are not harmonized (raw SMILES/InChI as submitted by submitters); without RDKit-standardized InChIKeys, cross-library matching will be inflated by inconsistent identifier representations When the analysis goal is spectral similarity scoring or identification rather than library coverage/redundancy assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies chemical identifier overlap and spectral redundancy across Open Mass Spectral Libraries (OMSLs) by extracting harmonized InChIKeys from each source and tabulating how many of the integrated unique identifiers appear in one, two, three, or all four libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02219
skills.summary: Quantifies chemical identifier overlap and spectral redundancy across Open Mass Spectral Libraries (OMSLs) by extracting harmonized InChIKeys from each source and tabulating how many of the integrated unique identifiers appear in one, two, three, or all four libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is a single library with no cross-source integration question — overlap and redundancy statistics are only meaningful across multiple sources When chemical identifiers are not harmonized (raw SMILES/InChI as submitted by submitters); without RDKit-standardized InChIKeys, cross-library matching will be inflated by inconsistent identifier representations When the analysis goal is spectral similarity scoring or identification rather than library coverage/redundancy assessment

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed MS/MS spectra (mgf, msp, mzml, mzxml, json, usi) in positive and/or negative ionization mode and need a numeric representation for cross-mode similarity scoring or chemical-space visualization.
skills.name: mass-spectral-embedding-computation
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-embedding-computation Use when you have preprocessed MS/MS spectra (mgf, msp, mzml, mzxml, json, usi) in positive and/or negative ionization mode and need a numeric representation for cross-mode similarity scoring or chemical-space visualization. Training a new model from scratch on a small custom dataset without merging it with larger public libraries — pair sampling can be suboptimal if not checked for smaller training sets Spectra are low-quality with limited fragmentation, chimeric, or substantially dissimilar to training data — predictions are unreliable; use the embedding evaluator to flag these before trusting embeddings The DreaMS model is required instead (it has only been trained on positive ionization spectra, so is unsuitable for cross-mode training) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes 500-dimensional MS2DeepScore 2.0 embeddings for preprocessed tandem mass spectra using a Siamese neural network that predicts Tanimoto-based chemical similarity, serving as both an intermediate for score computation and a basis for UMAP visualization of chemical space. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Computes 500-dimensional MS2DeepScore 2.0 embeddings for preprocessed tandem mass spectra using a Siamese neural network that predicts Tanimoto-based chemical similarity, serving as both an intermediate for score computation and a basis for UMAP visualization of chemical space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training a new model from scratch on a small custom dataset without merging it with larger public libraries — pair sampling can be suboptimal if not checked for smaller training sets Spectra are low-quality with limited fragmentation, chimeric, or substantially dissimilar to training data — predictions are unreliable; use the embedding evaluator to flag these before trusting embeddings The DreaMS model is required instead (it has only been trained on positive ionization spectra, so is unsuitable for cross-mode training)

skills.description: Use when computing MS2DeepScore embeddings or cross-ionization-mode Tanimoto similarity predictions and you need to flag spectra with low information content or dissimilarity to training data before trusting the predicted similarities.
skills.name: mass-spectral-embedding-quality-estimation
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-embedding-quality-estimation Use when computing MS2DeepScore embeddings or cross-ionization-mode Tanimoto similarity predictions and you need to flag spectra with low information content or dissimilarity to training data before trusting the predicted similarities. Spectra are already annotated/validated and you only need similarity matrices — the evaluator adds no information about known-good reference spectra You are training a new MS2DeepScore model from scratch rather than assessing predictions of an existing one; pair-sampling quality checks apply instead The downstream task tolerates unreliable predictions (e.g. exploratory UMAP visualization) where filtering would discard informative low-quality spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Estimates per-spectrum MS2DeepScore embedding quality by predicting the model's mean squared error for each embedding, so spectra likely to yield unreliable similarity predictions can be flagged or filtered before downstream use. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Estimates per-spectrum MS2DeepScore embedding quality by predicting the model's mean squared error for each embedding, so spectra likely to yield unreliable similarity predictions can be flagged or filtered before downstream use.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are already annotated/validated and you only need similarity matrices — the evaluator adds no information about known-good reference spectra You are training a new MS2DeepScore model from scratch rather than assessing predictions of an existing one; pair-sampling quality checks apply instead The downstream task tolerates unreliable predictions (e.g. exploratory UMAP visualization) where filtering would discard informative low-quality spectra

skills.search_text: mass-spectral-envelope-visualization Use when simulating theoretical precursor isotopic envelopes of a defined peptide sequence at user-defined 13C enrichment levels (e.g., natural 1.07% vs 50%) for SIP proteomics validation and figure generation. The goal is de novo peptide identification or database search from raw spectra — Aerith validates/simulates envelopes of known PSMs, while identification is handled by Sipros/SiprosV4 pipelines Input is unconverted Thermo RAW files — first convert with Raxport or ThermoRawFileParser before spectral visualization The compound has no known chemical formula or peptide sequence — Aerith requires user-defined formulas or sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Simulate and visualize theoretical isotopic envelopes of SIP-labeled peptide precursors (e.g., HYAHVDCPGHADYVK) at user-defined 13C abundance levels (natural 1.07% vs 50% enriched) using Aerith's Rcpp-backed sequential-convolution algorithm, enabling validation of isotope incorporation in proteomic stable isotope probing experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Simulate and visualize theoretical isotopic envelopes of SIP-labeled peptide precursors (e.g., HYAHVDCPGHADYVK) at user-defined 13C abundance levels (natural 1.07% vs 50% enriched) using Aerith's Rcpp-backed sequential-convolution algorithm, enabling validation of isotope incorporation in proteomic stable isotope probing experiments.

skills.description: Use when investigating which LC-MS/MS features are adjacent to one selected feature in a pairwise spectral similarity matrix, and you need to expand that neighborhood interactively by adjusting similarity thresholds and connectivity limits.
skills.name: mass-spectral-feature-connectivity-analysis
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-feature-connectivity-analysis Use when investigating which LC-MS/MS features are adjacent to one selected feature in a pairwise spectral similarity matrix, and you need to expand that neighborhood interactively by adjusting similarity thresholds and connectivity limits. Input is raw vendor data without a precomputed pairwise similarity matrix — the skill requires the ms2deepscore similarity backbone from the specXplore importing pipeline, not raw spectra files Goal is a global network of the whole dataset (e.g. a full molecular network on GNPS servers) rather than a localized ego-network around one node — specXplore was created with adjustable settings for local network topology in mind, not to replace traditional molecular networking Dataset contains more than ~5000 features; the article anticipates dashboard difficulties for larger data sets and liberal settings http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Explores local connectivity around a single LC-MS/MS feature of interest by overlaying an ego-network of edges derived from a thresholded ms2deepscore pairwise similarity matrix onto a t-SNE overview, as implemented in the specXplore interactive Python dashboard. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Explores local connectivity around a single LC-MS/MS feature of interest by overlaying an ego-network of edges derived from a thresholded ms2deepscore pairwise similarity matrix onto a t-SNE overview, as implemented in the specXplore interactive Python dashboard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor data without a precomputed pairwise similarity matrix — the skill requires the ms2deepscore similarity backbone from the specXplore importing pipeline, not raw spectra files Goal is a global network of the whole dataset (e.g. a full molecular network on GNPS servers) rather than a localized ego-network around one node — specXplore was created with adjustable settings for local network topology in mind, not to replace traditional molecular networking Dataset contains more than ~5000 features; the article anticipates dashboard difficulties for larger data sets and liberal settings

skills.name: mass-spectral-intensity-binning
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-intensity-binning Use when raw GC-EI-MS peak lists (m/z / relative-intensity pairs, e.g. NIST 20 msp records) must be converted into a discrete intensity vocabulary before training or running a spectra-to-SMILES transformer, or when choosing among binning schemes. The data are MS/MS spectra rather than GC-EI-MS spectra — the binning scheme was tuned for single-precursor EI-MS peak lists A downstream model already consumes continuous intensity values (e.g. 4-decimal-place linear encoding) and you do not need the discrete-token trade-off Spectra have not yet passed the model-specific filters (max m/z 500, max 300 peaks, max SMILES length 100), so binned output would include records the model cannot process Discretizes continuous relative-intensity values of EI-MS peak lists into a fixed vocabulary of 30 logarithmically spaced bins (log base 1.28, shift 29) so spectra can be fed to a transformer (SpecTUS) as a discrete sequence alongside integer-rounded m/z tokens. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.05114
skills.summary: Discretizes continuous relative-intensity values of EI-MS peak lists into a fixed vocabulary of 30 logarithmically spaced bins (log base 1.28, shift 29) so spectra can be fed to a transformer (SpecTUS) as a discrete sequence alongside integer-rounded m/z tokens.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are MS/MS spectra rather than GC-EI-MS spectra — the binning scheme was tuned for single-precursor EI-MS peak lists A downstream model already consumes continuous intensity values (e.g. 4-decimal-place linear encoding) and you do not need the discrete-token trade-off Spectra have not yet passed the model-specific filters (max m/z 500, max 300 peaks, max SMILES length 100), so binned output would include records the model cannot process

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-QTOF-MS/MS screening data (e.g. MS-DIAL-exported feature tables and .msp/.mgf spectra) must be annotated against MS/MS libraries plus plastic-related and GC–MS-derived structure databases to yield identified compounds with library vs unknown status.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-annotation
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-annotation Use when untargeted LC-QTOF-MS/MS screening data (e.g. MS-DIAL-exported feature tables and .msp/.mgf spectra) must be annotated against MS/MS libraries plus plastic-related and GC–MS-derived structure databases to yield identified compounds with library vs unknown status. The analytes of interest are volatile/semi-volatile and already covered by EI-MS spectral matching (GC–MS), rather than non-volatile migrants needing LC-HRMS/MS annotation. Features have already been annotated — e.g. you hold a final identified-compound table — and only quantification or pseudo-MRM targeting remains. The unknowns are 'unknown unknowns' that may not be present in any existing structure database; the article notes in silico fragmentation only works for known unknowns. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotate LC-HRMS features of non-volatile migrants by matching processed MS/MS spectra against compiled in-house and public tandem libraries within MS-DIAL, falling back to in silico fragmentation (MS-FINDER) against structure databases for remaining unknowns. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05389
skills.summary: Annotate LC-HRMS features of non-volatile migrants by matching processed MS/MS spectra against compiled in-house and public tandem libraries within MS-DIAL, falling back to in silico fragmentation (MS-FINDER) against structure databases for remaining unknowns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analytes of interest are volatile/semi-volatile and already covered by EI-MS spectral matching (GC–MS), rather than non-volatile migrants needing LC-HRMS/MS annotation. Features have already been annotated — e.g. you hold a final identified-compound table — and only quantification or pseudo-MRM targeting remains. The unknowns are 'unknown unknowns' that may not be present in any existing structure database; the article notes in silico fragmentation only works for known unknowns.

skills.description: Use when you have extracted MS/MS spectra (.msp) from an untargeted metabolomics study where library search leaves many spectra unannotated and you want fingerprint-based additional annotations.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-annotation
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-annotation Use when you have extracted MS/MS spectra (.msp) from an untargeted metabolomics study where library search leaves many spectra unannotated and you want fingerprint-based additional annotations. Spectra already have library hits — this workflow targets MS/MS spectra that were not annotated by mass spectral library search Input is raw chromatography data not yet deconvolved to MS/MS spectra; run an extraction step (e.g. IDSL.CSA) producing .msp first You lack a reference structure database to search predicted fingerprints against (fingerprint Tanimoto matching needs structures, not spectra) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Annotate untargeted MS/MS features by library spectral matching (IDSL.CSA against NIST 20 and LipidBlast with spectral entropy >= 0.75), then boost annotation rate by searching IDSL_MINT-predicted molecular fingerprints against LipidMaps structures at Tanimoto >= 0.6. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00804-5
skills.summary: Annotate untargeted MS/MS features by library spectral matching (IDSL.CSA against NIST 20 and LipidBlast with spectral entropy >= 0.75), then boost annotation rate by searching IDSL_MINT-predicted molecular fingerprints against LipidMaps structures at Tanimoto >= 0.6.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra already have library hits — this workflow targets MS/MS spectra that were not annotated by mass spectral library search Input is raw chromatography data not yet deconvolved to MS/MS spectra; run an extraction step (e.g. IDSL.CSA) producing .msp first You lack a reference structure database to search predicted fingerprints against (fingerprint Tanimoto matching needs structures, not spectra)

skills.description: Use when an annotated MS/MS spectral library (GNPS, MassBank, MoNA) contains inconsistent metadata — missing SMILES, salt-formatted SMILES, parent masses computed from molar mass, mismatched adducts or annotations — and a curated subset with validated structure annotations is needed.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-cleaning
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-cleaning Use when an annotated MS/MS spectral library (GNPS, MassBank, MoNA) contains inconsistent metadata — missing SMILES, salt-formatted SMILES, parent masses computed from molar mass, mismatched adducts or annotations — and a curated subset with validated structure annotations is needed. Input spectra lack structure annotations entirely — the requirement filters (Require Valid Annotation via RDKit) will remove spectra rather than repair them, since Derive Annotation From Compound Name only succeeds when a compound name matches the given parent mass Validation of fragment peaks against the annotation is needed — the pipeline explicitly lacks fragment-matching plausibility checks, so wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass go unnoticed Standardization of instrument type or collision-energy metadata is the goal — these fields are not yet cleaned by current matchms filters http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A reproducible matchms pipeline (v0.26.4) that cleans annotated MS/MS spectral libraries such as the GNPS public library by running default metadata-harmonization filters plus repair filters (Derive Annotation From Compound Name via PubChem, Repair Smiles Of Salts, Repair Parent Mass Is Molar Mass, Repair Adduct And Parent Mass Based On Smiles, Repair Not Matching Annotation) followed by requirement filters, yielding a curated library ready for library searching and machine-learning training. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: A reproducible matchms pipeline (v0.26.4) that cleans annotated MS/MS spectral libraries such as the GNPS public library by running default metadata-harmonization filters plus repair filters (Derive Annotation From Compound Name via PubChem, Repair Smiles Of Salts, Repair Parent Mass Is Molar Mass, Repair Adduct And Parent Mass Based On Smiles, Repair Not Matching Annotation) followed by requirement filters, yielding a curated library ready for library searching and machine-learning training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack structure annotations entirely — the requirement filters (Require Valid Annotation via RDKit) will remove spectra rather than repair them, since Derive Annotation From Compound Name only succeeds when a compound name matches the given parent mass Validation of fragment peaks against the annotation is needed — the pipeline explicitly lacks fragment-matching plausibility checks, so wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass go unnoticed Standardization of instrument type or collision-energy metadata is the goal — these fields are not yet cleaned by current matchms filters

skills.description: Use when constructing a plant-specific annotation reference from public MS2 spectra and MS1 metabolite tables to feed a tidyMass/metID-based annotation workflow, and per-source metabolite counts must be tracked and validated.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-construction
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-construction Use when constructing a plant-specific annotation reference from public MS2 spectra and MS1 metabolite tables to feed a tidyMass/metID-based annotation workflow, and per-source metabolite counts must be tracked and validated. Your sample matrix is non-plant (e.g. human/metagenomic): use organism-appropriate references such as the Human Metabolome Database instead of the plant-specific PM database Your annotation pipeline is not tidyMass/metID-based and cannot load 'databaseClass' objects http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Build a plant-specific mass spectrometry (PM) database by converting public MS2 spectral libraries (MoNA, MassBank, ReSpect, PlaSMA, NIST, GNPS) and filtered MS1 tables (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) into metID 'databaseClass' objects for embedding into the MetMiner pipeline to improve metabolite annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Build a plant-specific mass spectrometry (PM) database by converting public MS2 spectral libraries (MoNA, MassBank, ReSpect, PlaSMA, NIST, GNPS) and filtered MS1 tables (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) into metID 'databaseClass' objects for embedding into the MetMiner pipeline to improve metabolite annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your sample matrix is non-plant (e.g. human/metagenomic): use organism-appropriate references such as the Human Metabolome Database instead of the plant-specific PM database Your annotation pipeline is not tidyMass/metID-based and cannot load 'databaseClass' objects

skills.description: Use when building or updating an open spectral library from a plate-based high-throughput LC-MSn acquisition, where compound metadata must be reconciled with PubChem/LOTUS/DrugBank identifiers and spectra merged into InChIKey-indexed MSn trees.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-curation
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-curation Use when building or updating an open spectral library from a plate-based high-throughput LC-MSn acquisition, where compound metadata must be reconciled with PubChem/LOTUS/DrugBank identifiers and spectra merged into InChIKey-indexed MSn trees. When the goal is standard single-stage MS/MS library building from legacy spectra without metadata reconciliation — MSnLib is designed for multi-stage MSn tree acquisition. When the source data are already vendor-converted open formats (mzML/MGF) and no metadata cleanup is needed; the Prefect cleanup flow adds no value. When none of the drug or natural product databases (LOTUS, DrugBank, Broad Hub, Dictionary of Natural Products) have been downloaded and no structure annotations are supplied — the flow will simply skip those sources. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build an open multi-stage (MSn) fragmentation spectral library by cleaning compound metadata against PubChem, LOTUS, and drug databases, then merging spectra from Orbitrap ID-X MS2/MS3 acquisitions into machine-ready MSn tree libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0
skills.summary: Build an open multi-stage (MSn) fragmentation spectral library by cleaning compound metadata against PubChem, LOTUS, and drug databases, then merging spectra from Orbitrap ID-X MS2/MS3 acquisitions into machine-ready MSn tree libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is standard single-stage MS/MS library building from legacy spectra without metadata reconciliation — MSnLib is designed for multi-stage MSn tree acquisition. When the source data are already vendor-converted open formats (mzML/MGF) and no metadata cleanup is needed; the Prefect cleanup flow adds no value. When none of the drug or natural product databases (LOTUS, DrugBank, Broad Hub, Dictionary of Natural Products) have been downloaded and no structure annotations are supplied — the flow will simply skip those sources.

The input is raw instrument data in a vendor or open raw format rather than an already-compiled text-based .msp spectral library file The task is identifier conversion or enrichment itself — parsing is only the IO prerequisite; conversion work belongs to the CIR/CTS/IDSM/PubChem/BridgeDb converters Only peak/spectrum intensities are needed and no record metadata will be read or modified http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Loading and parsing mass spectral library records from the open, text-based .msp format using matchms for data IO, so that per-record metadata fields (SMILES, InChI, CAS numbers, etc.) become available for annotation, curation, and validation. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04494

skills.description: Use when you have MS1-level LC/HRMS mzXML/mzML/netCDF data from an untargeted metabolomics study (possibly n>500) and need to build a reusable spectral library for annotating peaks, especially when MS2 data or MS2 library coverage is poor.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-generation
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-generation Use when you have MS1-level LC/HRMS mzXML/mzML/netCDF data from an untargeted metabolomics study (possibly n>500) and need to build a reusable spectral library for annotating peaks, especially when MS2 data or MS2 library coverage is poor. You already have rich MS2 fragmentation spectra for the peaks and a matching MS/MS spectral library (e.g. NIST 2020) — searching MS/MS libraries directly is more appropriate than building CSA libraries. The input is raw unprocessed MS data without IDSL.IPA peaklists/peak_alignment outputs — CSA requires IDSL.IPA-generated chromatographic information as a prerequisite. You need compound-level identification solely from accurate mass and formula without spectral similarity search — CSA libraries are designed for mass spectral similarity matching, not de novo annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Generate composite mass spectra (CSA) libraries in .msp format from correlating MS1-only LC/HRMS peaks using the IDSL.CSA R package, enabling chemical annotation of peaks that lack MS2 fragmentation data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00376
skills.summary: Generate composite mass spectra (CSA) libraries in .msp format from correlating MS1-only LC/HRMS peaks using the IDSL.CSA R package, enabling chemical annotation of peaks that lack MS2 fragmentation data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have rich MS2 fragmentation spectra for the peaks and a matching MS/MS spectral library (e.g. NIST 2020) — searching MS/MS libraries directly is more appropriate than building CSA libraries. The input is raw unprocessed MS data without IDSL.IPA peaklists/peak_alignment outputs — CSA requires IDSL.IPA-generated chromatographic information as a prerequisite. You need compound-level identification solely from accurate mass and formula without spectral similarity search — CSA libraries are designed for mass spectral similarity matching, not de novo annotation.

skills.description: Reference for ingesting MS/MS library files (msp, mzML, mzXML, MGF, JSON, metabolomics-USI) into matchms and running default-filter preprocessing with automatic YAML/report logging before library searching or ML training.

skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-import-and-preprocessing Reference for ingesting MS/MS library files (msp, mzML, mzXML, MGF, JSON, metabolomics-USI) into matchms and running default-filter preprocessing with automatic YAML/report logging before library searching or ML training. Input spectra already have complete, validated annotations and only need similarity scoring or fingerprinting rather than cleaning — the cleaning pipeline's repair/derivation filters would add unnecessary work The task requires fragment-matching plausibility checks against measured peaks: the article notes current matchms filters 'lack plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments' — such fragment-matching filters are only a possible future expansion You need to standardize instrument type or collision-energy metadata: the article states these 'could be important fields that might require additional standardization' that is not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Import public tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectral libraries (e.g. GNPS, MassBank, MoNA) into matchms, apply the default metadata filters, and automatically emit a reusable YAML workflow file plus a processing report so each cleaning run is reproducible and auditable. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra already have complete, validated annotations and only need similarity scoring or fingerprinting rather than cleaning — the cleaning pipeline's repair/derivation filters would add unnecessary work The task requires fragment-matching plausibility checks against measured peaks: the article notes current matchms filters 'lack plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments' — such fragment-matching filters are only a possible future expansion You need to standardize instrument type or collision-energy metadata: the article states these 'could be important fields that might require additional standardization' that is not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when the goal is to identify an unknown small molecule from its EI mass spectrum by ranking candidates in a spectral reference library (e.g., NIST 2017) and reporting recall@10.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-matching
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-matching Use when the goal is to identify an unknown small molecule from its EI mass spectrum by ranking candidates in a spectral reference library (e.g., NIST 2017) and reporting recall@10. The molecule of interest is absent from every external reference library and no predicted spectra are available — without augmentation, correct identification is impossible (the paper's stated coverage problem). The spectra come from an ionization method other than electron ionization and the model/library was not retrained for that method (NEIMS was trained only on EI spectra from NIST 2017). Isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments matter for the match — NEIMS currently does not model isotope peaks, so augmented-library matching can be degraded for such cases. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Identifies small molecules by comparing an observed query electron-ionization mass spectrum against a (possibly NEIMS-augmented) reference library using weighted cosine similarity with a molecular-mass filter. This is the evaluation task that the NEIMS paper uses to quantify how model-predicted spectra extend library coverage. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00085
skills.summary: Identifies small molecules by comparing an observed query electron-ionization mass spectrum against a (possibly NEIMS-augmented) reference library using weighted cosine similarity with a molecular-mass filter. This is the evaluation task that the NEIMS paper uses to quantify how model-predicted spectra extend library coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule of interest is absent from every external reference library and no predicted spectra are available — without augmentation, correct identification is impossible (the paper's stated coverage problem). The spectra come from an ionization method other than electron ionization and the model/library was not retrained for that method (NEIMS was trained only on EI spectra from NIST 2017). Isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments matter for the match — NEIMS currently does not model isotope peaks, so augmented-library matching can be degraded for such cases.

skills.description: Use when a structurally characterized Mass2Motif (or other fragment/loss set) needs putative annotation or validation against curated MS/MS spectral libraries before transferring annotations to new datasets.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-matching
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-matching Use when a structurally characterized Mass2Motif (or other fragment/loss set) needs putative annotation or validation against curated MS/MS spectral libraries before transferring annotations to new datasets. The motif set contains dominant neutral losses that are central to the annotation — these must be dropped for matching, so the pseudo-spectrum loses key diagnostic information. The dataset is not an information-rich, complex mixture with ramped or stepped collision energy fragmentation — MS2LDA decomposition quality drops and the motif pseudo-spectra may be unreliable. You need fully confirmed structural IDs rather than putative substructure annotations — matching only supports putative de novo annotation, not definitive structure assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validate Mass2Motif substructure annotations by representing each motif as a pseudo-spectrum (its fragments and losses as peaks) and matching it against external MS/MS reference libraries such as GNPS, Mass Bank, and NIST at a 90% normalized score threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Validate Mass2Motif substructure annotations by representing each motif as a pseudo-spectrum (its fragments and losses as peaks) and matching it against external MS/MS reference libraries such as GNPS, Mass Bank, and NIST at a 90% normalized score threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The motif set contains dominant neutral losses that are central to the annotation — these must be dropped for matching, so the pseudo-spectrum loses key diagnostic information. The dataset is not an information-rich, complex mixture with ramped or stepped collision energy fragmentation — MS2LDA decomposition quality drops and the motif pseudo-spectra may be unreliable. You need fully confirmed structural IDs rather than putative substructure annotations — matching only supports putative de novo annotation, not definitive structure assignment.

skills.description: Use when raw GNPS FBMN spectral match annotation tables (from MZmine2/MZmine3 feature tables of LC-HRMS/MS runs) need cleaning against defined match-quality thresholds before computing annotation rates or feeding downstream prioritization.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-matching-cleanup
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-matching-cleanup Use when raw GNPS FBMN spectral match annotation tables (from MZmine2/MZmine3 feature tables of LC-HRMS/MS runs) need cleaning against defined match-quality thresholds before computing annotation rates or feeding downstream prioritization. The input is already a cleaned/filtered annotation set — re-applying thresholds will double-filter and understate annotation rates. The primary results are SIRIUS/ISDB in-silico annotations rather than GNPS spectral library matches — those require min_ZodiacScore/min_ConfidenceScore cut-offs instead of cosine/shared-peaks thresholds. Data were acquired in negative ionisation mode and the ionisation_mode parameter cannot be adjusted from 'pos'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Post-processes GNPS feature-based molecular networking spectral library matches by applying stringency thresholds (ppm error, shared peaks, cosine, ionisation mode) to retain only valid annotations, as done for the Celastraceae UHPLC-HRMS/MS dataset where 2,494 library-annotated nodes were reduced to 1,751 valid annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Post-processes GNPS feature-based molecular networking spectral library matches by applying stringency thresholds (ppm error, shared peaks, cosine, ionisation mode) to retain only valid annotations, as done for the Celastraceae UHPLC-HRMS/MS dataset where 2,494 library-annotated nodes were reduced to 1,751 valid annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cleaned/filtered annotation set — re-applying thresholds will double-filter and understate annotation rates. The primary results are SIRIUS/ISDB in-silico annotations rather than GNPS spectral library matches — those require min_ZodiacScore/min_ConfidenceScore cut-offs instead of cosine/shared-peaks thresholds. Data were acquired in negative ionisation mode and the ionisation_mode parameter cannot be adjusted from 'pos'.

skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-msp-io Use when input is a mass spectral library file in .msp format whose records need loading into a Python tool, enrichment with metadata (SMILES, InChI, CAS), or export back to .msp after annotation. Input spectra are in a format other than .msp (e.g. raw vendor formats or mzML); MSMetaEnhancer's demonstrated IO supports the .msp format via matchms The goal is spectral processing (peak picking, similarity scoring) rather than metadata annotation and round-tripping of library records Records already contain complete, validated metadata (InChI, SMILES, formula) so no external enrichment round-trip is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reading and writing open text-based .msp mass spectral library files through matchms-backed IO in MSMetaEnhancer, so records can be loaded for metadata enrichment and the enriched library exported back to .msp. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04494
skills.summary: Reading and writing open text-based .msp mass spectral library files through matchms-backed IO in MSMetaEnhancer, so records can be loaded for metadata enrichment and the enriched library exported back to .msp.
