skills.description: Use when raw spectral library entries (e.g., GNPS JSON/MGF libraries) lack structural annotations like InChIKeys, or have inconsistent metadata (ionmode, charge, compound name, formula, parent mass), and structure-based analyses are planned.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-preprocessing
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-preprocessing Use when raw spectral library entries (e.g., GNPS JSON/MGF libraries) lack structural annotations like InChIKeys, or have inconsistent metadata (ionmode, charge, compound name, formula, parent mass), and structure-based analyses are planned. Spectra already carry complete InChIKey annotations and harmonized metadata — re-running the PubChem lookup could overwrite or mismatch existing annotations The downstream analysis is purely spectral (e.g., cosine or modified cosine scoring) and does not require structural identifiers The library metadata is unreliable to the extent that name/formula/parent-mass queries would return wrong PubChem compounds, since derived InChIKeys would be misleading http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0078 Cleans and structurally annotates mass spectral library entries (e.g., the GNPS ALL_GNPS.json library with 154,820 spectra) using matchms metadata harmonization followed by automated PubChem lookups, so that spectra lacking InChIKeys can be linked to structures for downstream analyses such as Tanimoto similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Cleans and structurally annotates mass spectral library entries (e.g., the GNPS ALL_GNPS.json library with 154,820 spectra) using matchms metadata harmonization followed by automated PubChem lookups, so that spectra lacking InChIKeys can be linked to structures for downstream analyses such as Tanimoto similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra already carry complete InChIKey annotations and harmonized metadata — re-running the PubChem lookup could overwrite or mismatch existing annotations The downstream analysis is purely spectral (e.g., cosine or modified cosine scoring) and does not require structural identifiers The library metadata is unreliable to the extent that name/formula/parent-mass queries would return wrong PubChem compounds, since derived InChIKeys would be misleading

skills.description: Use when querying mass spectra against a large spectral library (e.g. MoNA-hosted MassBank, GNPS, HMDB, ReSpect, FiehnLib entries) and you need to shrink the candidate set before running a full NIST cosine similarity search.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-retrieval
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-retrieval Use when querying mass spectra against a large spectral library (e.g. MoNA-hosted MassBank, GNPS, HMDB, ReSpect, FiehnLib entries) and you need to shrink the candidate set before running a full NIST cosine similarity search. The reference library is proprietary NIST-only and not openly deposited on MoNA (NIST entries cannot be released publicly, so the prefilter index cannot be built from public data) The task requires exact full-spectrum identification with maximal recall rather than search-space prefiltering, since the second block sacrifices ~13% recall at score 700 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Uses the SPLASH second summary block as a database-independent prefilter to reduce the mass spectral search space before full-spectrum similarity scoring, trading a small recall loss for large candidate-set reductions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3689
skills.summary: Uses the SPLASH second summary block as a database-independent prefilter to reduce the mass spectral search space before full-spectrum similarity scoring, trading a small recall loss for large candidate-set reductions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference library is proprietary NIST-only and not openly deposited on MoNA (NIST entries cannot be released publicly, so the prefilter index cannot be built from public data) The task requires exact full-spectrum identification with maximal recall rather than search-space prefiltering, since the second block sacrifices ~13% recall at score 700

skills.description: Use when comparing the query-time scaling of spectral library search modules (e.g., linear-time hash-table/bisection methods vs entropy-similarity search) across MassBank libraries of growing size.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-search-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-search-benchmarking Use when comparing the query-time scaling of spectral library search modules (e.g., linear-time hash-table/bisection methods vs entropy-similarity search) across MassBank libraries of growing size. The goal is annotation accuracy or identification quality (e.g., FDR) rather than query-time scaling — use an annotation-validation benchmark instead. Query spectra or libraries are not in comparable precursor/peak form (precursor_mz + peaks arrays required by FlashEntropySearch). Only a single fixed library size is available — scaling behavior vs library size cannot be assessed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks the wall-clock querying speed of spectral library search algorithms (LipidIN's EQ module vs Flash Entropy Search) as a function of library size on a single-thread, low-memory CPU. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock querying speed of spectral library search algorithms (LipidIN's EQ module vs Flash Entropy Search) as a function of library size on a single-thread, low-memory CPU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation accuracy or identification quality (e.g., FDR) rather than query-time scaling — use an annotation-validation benchmark instead. Query spectra or libraries are not in comparable precursor/peak form (precursor_mz + peaks arrays required by FlashEntropySearch). Only a single fixed library size is available — scaling behavior vs library size cannot be assessed.

skills.description: Use when comparing the runtime scalability of MS2 spectral library search methods (e.g., ML-based analogue search vs score-based search with precursor preselection) on a fixed query set and library.
skills.name: mass-spectral-library-search-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-library-search-benchmarking Use when comparing the runtime scalability of MS2 spectral library search methods (e.g., ML-based analogue search vs score-based search with precursor preselection) on a fixed query set and library. When the goal is to benchmark annotation accuracy or analogue-search quality rather than runtime throughput When query files contain many MS2 spectra per feature and no prior clustering/feature selection has been done — MS2Query does not do peak picking or clustering, so unprocessed files inflate runtimes and make timings non-comparable When the target library or query mode differs (e.g., negative mode) without downloading the corresponding pretrained model/library files http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark the wall-clock throughput of MS2-based library/analogue search tools (MS2Query vs matchms modified cosine) by timing full-library matching runs over a fixed query set and reporting spectra-per-minute. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock throughput of MS2-based library/analogue search tools (MS2Query vs matchms modified cosine) by timing full-library matching runs over a fixed query set and reporting spectra-per-minute.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to benchmark annotation accuracy or analogue-search quality rather than runtime throughput When query files contain many MS2 spectra per feature and no prior clustering/feature selection has been done — MS2Query does not do peak picking or clustering, so unprocessed files inflate runtimes and make timings non-comparable When the target library or query mode differs (e.g., negative mode) without downloading the corresponding pretrained model/library files

skills.description: Use when you need a coarse theoretical isotopic envelope (main peaks at integer neutron differences from the monoisotopic mass) for a metabolite with a known chemical formula or a peptide precursor, rather than the full isotopic fine structure.
skills.name: mass-spectral-main-peak-extraction
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-main-peak-extraction Use when you need a coarse theoretical isotopic envelope (main peaks at integer neutron differences from the monoisotopic mass) for a metabolite with a known chemical formula or a peptide precursor, rather than the full isotopic fine structure. You need isotopic fine structure (resolved by high-resolution MS or Aerith's Monte Carlo multinomial simulation) — the FFT method does not account for fine structure. The compound has partial isotope incorporation and you need a fully fine-structure-resolved simulator like IsoSpec2-style output. The input is raw vendor data rather than a chemical formula or peptide sequence — convert with Raxport or ThermoRawFileParser first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Extracts the main isotopic peaks (M, M+1, M+2, ...) at integer neutron offsets from a computed isotopic envelope, discarding fine-structure sub-peaks. In Aerith this is the peak-picking step after the FFT-based envelope simulation for metabolites and peptide precursors, implemented in C++ via Rcpp. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Extracts the main isotopic peaks (M, M+1, M+2, ...) at integer neutron offsets from a computed isotopic envelope, discarding fine-structure sub-peaks. In Aerith this is the peak-picking step after the FFT-based envelope simulation for metabolites and peptide precursors, implemented in C++ via Rcpp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need isotopic fine structure (resolved by high-resolution MS or Aerith's Monte Carlo multinomial simulation) — the FFT method does not account for fine structure. The compound has partial isotope incorporation and you need a fully fine-structure-resolved simulator like IsoSpec2-style output. The input is raw vendor data rather than a chemical formula or peptide sequence — convert with Raxport or ThermoRawFileParser first.

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular network already has mapped Mass2Motifs and a chemical class annotation dataframe is available, and the two annotation layers must be combined into one Cytoscape-ready network artifact.
skills.name: mass-spectral-molecular-network-annotation-merging
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-molecular-network-annotation-merging Use when a GNPS molecular network already has mapped Mass2Motifs and a chemical class annotation dataframe is available, and the two annotation layers must be combined into one Cytoscape-ready network artifact. The network has not yet had Mass2Motifs mapped to it or the chemical class annotation dataframe has not yet been produced — run the motif-mapping and chemical-class mapping steps first. Only in silico structure annotation (Network Annotation Propagation or DEREPLICATOR) output is needed — those tools are complementary to this workflow and are not merged by this skill. A standalone chemical classification (ClassyFire) result is wanted without integration into a molecular network. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Merges Mass2Motif substructure annotations and ClassyFire chemical class annotations into a single GNPS molecular network object using pyMolNetEnhancer, then exports the integrated network as a .graphml file plus tab-delimited edge/node tables for Cytoscape visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Merges Mass2Motif substructure annotations and ClassyFire chemical class annotations into a single GNPS molecular network object using pyMolNetEnhancer, then exports the integrated network as a .graphml file plus tab-delimited edge/node tables for Cytoscape visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network has not yet had Mass2Motifs mapped to it or the chemical class annotation dataframe has not yet been produced — run the motif-mapping and chemical-class mapping steps first. Only in silico structure annotation (Network Annotation Propagation or DEREPLICATOR) output is needed — those tools are complementary to this workflow and are not merged by this skill. A standalone chemical classification (ClassyFire) result is wanted without integration into a molecular network.

skills.description: Use when you have GNPS molecular network outputs (graphml, clustered MGF, edges/nodes files) plus an MS2LDA experiment and need to link substructure motifs to network nodes/edges for annotation and visualization.
skills.name: mass-spectral-molecular-network-motif-mapping
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-molecular-network-motif-mapping Use when you have GNPS molecular network outputs (graphml, clustered MGF, edges/nodes files) plus an MS2LDA experiment and need to link substructure motifs to network nodes/edges for annotation and visualization. Input is a feature-based molecular network built with MZmine rather than a classical GNPS network — use the Mass2Motifs_2_Network_FeatureBased workflow instead of the classical one No MS2LDA experiment exists yet: motifs must first be discovered on ms2lda.org from the GNPS clustered MGF before mapping is possible Goal is purely chemical class annotation without substructure motifs — the chemical-class mapping branch of MolNetEnhancer is the appropriate route, not Mass2Motif mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Maps MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructural annotations onto GNPS mass spectral molecular networks using the MolNetEnhancer/pyMolNetEnhancer workflow, enabling discovery of subtle substructural diversity within molecular families such as peptidic motifs in Xenorhabdus/Photorhabdus extracts. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Maps MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructural annotations onto GNPS mass spectral molecular networks using the MolNetEnhancer/pyMolNetEnhancer workflow, enabling discovery of subtle substructural diversity within molecular families such as peptidic motifs in Xenorhabdus/Photorhabdus extracts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature-based molecular network built with MZmine rather than a classical GNPS network — use the Mass2Motifs_2_Network_FeatureBased workflow instead of the classical one No MS2LDA experiment exists yet: motifs must first be discovered on ms2lda.org from the GNPS clustered MGF before mapping is possible Goal is purely chemical class annotation without substructure motifs — the chemical-class mapping branch of MolNetEnhancer is the appropriate route, not Mass2Motif mapping

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample DIMS peak lists (e.g. SIM-stitched FT-ICR m/z peaks from MTBLS79 cow/sheep heart samples plus QC and blank) and need a cross-sample aligned matrix before replicate/blank/sample filtering and PCA.
skills.name: mass-spectral-peak-alignment
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-peak-alignment Use when you have per-sample DIMS peak lists (e.g. SIM-stitched FT-ICR m/z peaks from MTBLS79 cow/sheep heart samples plus QC and blank) and need a cross-sample aligned matrix before replicate/blank/sample filtering and PCA. Input is already an aligned feature table or data matrix (e.g. post-filtering DSO) — alignment would be redundant Processing LC-MS data, where Galaxy-M instead uses the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe (feature detection, retention time correction and alignment via XCMS) rather than the DIMS Align Samples tool Raw unprocessed .dat transients — SIM-stitch peak picking must precede alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aligning peak lists across samples in the Galaxy-M DIMS workflow so that m/z features measured in multiple samples are matched into a single data matrix ready for filtering, imputation, and PCA. This step converts per-sample SIM-stitched peak lists into the consistent X matrix the Galaxy-M statistics tools require. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: Aligning peak lists across samples in the Galaxy-M DIMS workflow so that m/z features measured in multiple samples are matched into a single data matrix ready for filtering, imputation, and PCA. This step converts per-sample SIM-stitched peak lists into the consistent X matrix the Galaxy-M statistics tools require.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table or data matrix (e.g. post-filtering DSO) — alignment would be redundant Processing LC-MS data, where Galaxy-M instead uses the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe (feature detection, retention time correction and alignment via XCMS) rather than the DIMS Align Samples tool Raw unprocessed .dat transients — SIM-stitch peak picking must precede alignment

skills.description: Use when raw mass spectral peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature vectors for a classifier, or when spectra from different acquisition modes (EI-MS vs ESI-MS/MS) must be projected onto a common m/z scale for training or comparison.
skills.name: mass-spectral-peak-binning
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-peak-binning Use when raw mass spectral peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature vectors for a classifier, or when spectra from different acquisition modes (EI-MS vs ESI-MS/MS) must be projected onto a common m/z scale for training or comparison. The input is a chemical structure (SMILES/descriptors) rather than a spectrum — BitterPredict predicts bitterness from structure, not from spectral data Spectra were acquired in negative ion mode — BitterMasS predictions are based on EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS spectra obtained in positive ion mode only The input is already a fixed-length feature table aligned to a common m/z grid, so re-binning would discard or duplicate information http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Bins experimental EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS peak intensities onto a shared 0.1 m/z grid to build fixed-length feature matrices for machine-learning bitterness classification, as done for the BitterMasS Random Forest classifier trained on 5414 experimental mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jafc.3c09767
skills.summary: Bins experimental EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS peak intensities onto a shared 0.1 m/z grid to build fixed-length feature matrices for machine-learning bitterness classification, as done for the BitterMasS Random Forest classifier trained on 5414 experimental mass spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a chemical structure (SMILES/descriptors) rather than a spectrum — BitterPredict predicts bitterness from structure, not from spectral data Spectra were acquired in negative ion mode — BitterMasS predictions are based on EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS spectra obtained in positive ion mode only The input is already a fixed-length feature table aligned to a common m/z grid, so re-binning would discard or duplicate information

skills.description: Use when filtered MS/MS peak lists must be turned into fixed-width numeric vectors (10,000 bins over 10–1000 m/z) to feed the MS2DeepScore base network or to build 200-dimensional spectrum embeddings.
skills.name: mass-spectral-peak-binning
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-peak-binning Use when filtered MS/MS peak lists must be turned into fixed-width numeric vectors (10,000 bins over 10–1000 m/z) to feed the MS2DeepScore base network or to build 200-dimensional spectrum embeddings. Spectra have already been binned or embedded (e.g. 200-dimensional MS2DeepScore embeddings already computed) — re-binning would discard information The goal is a classical similarity measure such as (modified) cosine or Spec2Vec, which operate on peaks or learned vectors rather than the binned network input Spectra contain peaks outside the 10–1000 m/z range that are essential to the analysis, since the binning scheme discards anything outside these bounds and collapses sub-bin resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts filtered MS/MS spectra into fixed-length numeric vectors by assigning each peak to one of 10,000 equally-sized bins spanning 10–1000 m/z, keeping the highest peak intensity per bin. This binning is the first stage of input preparation for the MS2DeepScore Siamese base network and is part of the embedding creation step. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Converts filtered MS/MS spectra into fixed-length numeric vectors by assigning each peak to one of 10,000 equally-sized bins spanning 10–1000 m/z, keeping the highest peak intensity per bin. This binning is the first stage of input preparation for the MS2DeepScore Siamese base network and is part of the embedding creation step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra have already been binned or embedded (e.g. 200-dimensional MS2DeepScore embeddings already computed) — re-binning would discard information The goal is a classical similarity measure such as (modified) cosine or Spec2Vec, which operate on peaks or learned vectors rather than the binned network input Spectra contain peaks outside the 10–1000 m/z range that are essential to the analysis, since the binning scheme discards anything outside these bounds and collapses sub-bin resolution

skills.description: Use when you have tandem mass spectra (e.g., MassSpecGym or NPLIB1/CANOPUS-format entries) with a known or inferrable chemical formula and need de novo candidate molecular structures ranked by sampling frequency.
skills.name: mass-spectral-peak-embedding-with-formula-assignment
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-peak-embedding-with-formula-assignment Use when you have tandem mass spectra (e.g., MassSpecGym or NPLIB1/CANOPUS-format entries) with a known or inferrable chemical formula and need de novo candidate molecular structures ranked by sampling frequency. The chemical formula cannot be assigned from the spectrum (no high-resolution MS1/isotopic-trace support), since generation is formula-restricted by construction The goal is library/database annotation of existing reference spectra rather than de novo generation of structures absent from PubChem or HMDB The input is already a fingerprint or molecular structure table with no mass spectra — use fp2mol pretraining-style training instead of spectrum-conditioned inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Encodes tandem mass spectra into latent embeddings and formula-constrained molecular generations by combining a spectrum-to-fingerprint encoder (MIST) with a formula-restricted discrete graph diffusion decoder (DiffMS), pretrained on 2.8M fingerprint-structure pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Encodes tandem mass spectra into latent embeddings and formula-constrained molecular generations by combining a spectrum-to-fingerprint encoder (MIST) with a formula-restricted discrete graph diffusion decoder (DiffMS), pretrained on 2.8M fingerprint-structure pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chemical formula cannot be assigned from the spectrum (no high-resolution MS1/isotopic-trace support), since generation is formula-restricted by construction The goal is library/database annotation of existing reference spectra rather than de novo generation of structures absent from PubChem or HMDB The input is already a fingerprint or molecular structure table with no mass spectra — use fp2mol pretraining-style training instead of spectrum-conditioned inference

skills.description: Use when a matrix-annotation score (e.g. spectral S1 or morphological S2 in rMSIcleanup) falls below the user threshold and overlapped or isobaric peaks may share the same ion image as matrix-related ions, risking misclassification.
skills.name: mass-spectral-peak-overlap-detection
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-peak-overlap-detection Use when a matrix-annotation score (e.g. spectral S1 or morphological S2 in rMSIcleanup) falls below the user threshold and overlapped or isobaric peaks may share the same ion image as matrix-related ions, risking misclassification. Clusters whose S1 and S2 scores are already above the user-specified threshold — the paper states the overlapping detection algorithm is only executed for below-threshold clusters Data that has not been pre-processed into a centroid-mode peak matrix with rMSIproc (the module operates on peak matrices and ion images, not raw profile-mode imzML) Annotation problems where matrix chemical composition is unknown — matrix-related ions are determined from the matrix chemical formula and spatial distribution, which this module depends on http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 A bisecting k-means-based overlapping peak detection module that flags overlapped or isobaric ions inside low-scoring rMSIcleanup clusters so they are not misclassified as matrix-related peaks. It recursively splits clusters by spatial-distribution correlation and rescoring until subgroups qualify or become too small. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00449-0
skills.summary: A bisecting k-means-based overlapping peak detection module that flags overlapped or isobaric ions inside low-scoring rMSIcleanup clusters so they are not misclassified as matrix-related peaks. It recursively splits clusters by spatial-distribution correlation and rescoring until subgroups qualify or become too small.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters whose S1 and S2 scores are already above the user-specified threshold — the paper states the overlapping detection algorithm is only executed for below-threshold clusters Data that has not been pre-processed into a centroid-mode peak matrix with rMSIproc (the module operates on peak matrices and ion images, not raw profile-mode imzML) Annotation problems where matrix chemical composition is unknown — matrix-related ions are determined from the matrix chemical formula and spatial distribution, which this module depends on

skills.description: Use when raw LC-HRMS files (e.g., Thermo Orbitrap ID-X, MS1 scan range m/z 100–1000 at 60,000 resolution) must be converted into m/z and retention-time feature lists for differential comparison of preincubation and postincubation samples.
skills.name: mass-spectral-peak-picking
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-peak-picking Use when raw LC-HRMS files (e.g., Thermo Orbitrap ID-X, MS1 scan range m/z 100–1000 at 60,000 resolution) must be converted into m/z and retention-time feature lists for differential comparison of preincubation and postincubation samples. Input is already a processed feature/peak table (m/z, RT, intensities) — skip raw-file import and proceed directly to differential feature detection Targeted quantification of known metabolites with validated transitions, rather than untargeted MS1 feature detection for 0-hour vs 24-hour comparison MS2 spectra need to be interpreted or matched at this stage — peak picking here operates on MS1 spectral data; MS2 (HCD 35%) is used later for annotation/confirmation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Detect chromatographic features (m/z and retention time) from raw LC-HRMS files by importing each sample into MZmine 2.53 and building chromatograms with the ADAP chromatogram builder, producing the per-sample MS1 feature lists needed for downstream differential metabolite detection (e.g., 0-hour vs 24-hour S9 incubation comparisons). metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.dmd.2025.100183
skills.summary: Detect chromatographic features (m/z and retention time) from raw LC-HRMS files by importing each sample into MZmine 2.53 and building chromatograms with the ADAP chromatogram builder, producing the per-sample MS1 feature lists needed for downstream differential metabolite detection (e.g., 0-hour vs 24-hour S9 incubation comparisons).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature/peak table (m/z, RT, intensities) — skip raw-file import and proceed directly to differential feature detection Targeted quantification of known metabolites with validated transitions, rather than untargeted MS1 feature detection for 0-hour vs 24-hour comparison MS2 spectra need to be interpreted or matched at this stage — peak picking here operates on MS1 spectral data; MS2 (HCD 35%) is used later for annotation/confirmation

skills.description: Use when ranked candidate lists (e.g., the top-100 ranked compounds PS2MS yields per analyte) exist for the same test substances under two or more similarity metrics, and you must quantify which metric puts the true compound at rank 1.
skills.name: mass-spectral-ranking-metric-analysis
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-ranking-metric-analysis Use when ranked candidate lists (e.g., the top-100 ranked compounds PS2MS yields per analyte) exist for the same test substances under two or more similarity metrics, and you must quantify which metric puts the true compound at rank 1. The analyte mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectrum library (NIST, Wiley, or SWGDRUG), where conventional screening is sufficient and no ranking-metric comparison is needed The chemical structure of the NPS is already known, since in silico spectral prediction such as NEIMS is limited to known structures and no metric re-ranking is required The task is to build or filter the synthetic NPS database (enumeration and rule-based filtering of derivatives) rather than evaluate match metrics A benchmarking skill for comparing similarity metrics used to rank candidate compound identities in mass-spectral matching, as in PS2MS where an integrated SMSF (mass spectrum + molecular fingerprint) metric is evaluated against spectrum-only matching on GC/EI-MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing similarity metrics used to rank candidate compound identities in mass-spectral matching, as in PS2MS where an integrated SMSF (mass spectrum + molecular fingerprint) metric is evaluated against spectrum-only matching on GC/EI-MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectrum library (NIST, Wiley, or SWGDRUG), where conventional screening is sufficient and no ranking-metric comparison is needed The chemical structure of the NPS is already known, since in silico spectral prediction such as NEIMS is limited to known structures and no metric re-ranking is required The task is to build or filter the synthetic NPS database (enumeration and rule-based filtering of derivatives) rather than evaluate match metrics

skills.description: Use when you have predicted spectra and ground-truth library spectra for the same molecules and need to score similarity directly (cosine similarity ratios) or via augmented-library matching with recall@10.
skills.name: mass-spectral-similarity-metric-selection
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-similarity-metric-selection Use when you have predicted spectra and ground-truth library spectra for the same molecules and need to score similarity directly (cosine similarity ratios) or via augmented-library matching with recall@10. You need to train or tune the spectral prediction model itself rather than score prediction quality against ground truth Your spectra include isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments — NEIMS does not model them, so similarity ratios may be misleading You cannot supply a reasonable molecular mass for queries, so the 5 Da mass-filtering option cannot be applied and library matching accuracy will drop Quantify agreement between predicted and ground-truth electron-ionization mass spectra using weighted cosine similarity, both directly (predicted-vs-ground-truth similarity ratios) and indirectly via library matching (recall@10). Provides the metric and filtering conventions used to validate NEIMS spectral predictions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00085
skills.summary: Quantify agreement between predicted and ground-truth electron-ionization mass spectra using weighted cosine similarity, both directly (predicted-vs-ground-truth similarity ratios) and indirectly via library matching (recall@10). Provides the metric and filtering conventions used to validate NEIMS spectral predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to train or tune the spectral prediction model itself rather than score prediction quality against ground truth Your spectra include isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments — NEIMS does not model them, so similarity ratios may be misleading You cannot supply a reasonable molecular mass for queries, so the 5 Da mass-filtering option cannot be applied and library matching accuracy will drop

skills.description: Use when building metabolomic networks from GC-TOF-MS (or similar) feature spectra where many molecular features lack structural annotation and you want to connect unknowns to identified metabolites via spectral similarity.
skills.name: mass-spectral-similarity-network-construction
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-similarity-network-construction Use when building metabolomic networks from GC-TOF-MS (or similar) feature spectra where many molecular features lack structural annotation and you want to connect unknowns to identified metabolites via spectral similarity. Features already have structural annotations and KEGG RPAIR biochemical (substrate-product) transformations alone would connect them — biochemical/structural networks may suffice Input is empirical abundance data across samples rather than spectra — use Empirical Dependency Networks (Pearson, biweight or Spearman correlations) instead You need spectral library identification of unknowns rather than similarity-based edge construction between features http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Constructs spectral similarity networks in MetaMapR by computing pairwise cosine correlations between mass spectra encoded as m/z–intensity pairs and retaining edges above a cosine correlation threshold (>0.7 in the paper), linking structurally unknown metabolites to annotated species. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Constructs spectral similarity networks in MetaMapR by computing pairwise cosine correlations between mass spectra encoded as m/z–intensity pairs and retaining edges above a cosine correlation threshold (>0.7 in the paper), linking structurally unknown metabolites to annotated species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features already have structural annotations and KEGG RPAIR biochemical (substrate-product) transformations alone would connect them — biochemical/structural networks may suffice Input is empirical abundance data across samples rather than spectra — use Empirical Dependency Networks (Pearson, biweight or Spearman correlations) instead You need spectral library identification of unknowns rather than similarity-based edge construction between features

skills.description: Use when metabolites in a measured feature table (e.g. GC-TOF-MS metabolites with BinBase identifiers) lack structural annotation or KEGG/PubChem mappings, and you need network edges connecting them via mass spectra.
skills.name: mass-spectral-similarity-networking
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-similarity-networking Use when metabolites in a measured feature table (e.g. GC-TOF-MS metabolites with BinBase identifiers) lack structural annotation or KEGG/PubChem mappings, and you need network edges connecting them via mass spectra. The metabolites already have structural annotations and the goal is purely biochemical transformation networks based on KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs. Input data lack mass spectra (m/z:intensity pairs), so no cosine similarity can be computed — use empirical Spearman correlation networks instead. The goal is pathway-based rather than pathway-independent network mapping, where sparse disconnected graphs are acceptable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Builds mass spectral similarity edges between metabolites by computing pairwise cosine correlations between m/z:intensity spectra pairs, extending network analysis to structurally unannotated 'unknowns' (MetaMapR spectral similarity networks). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Builds mass spectral similarity edges between metabolites by computing pairwise cosine correlations between m/z:intensity spectra pairs, extending network analysis to structurally unannotated 'unknowns' (MetaMapR spectral similarity networks).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites already have structural annotations and the goal is purely biochemical transformation networks based on KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs. Input data lack mass spectra (m/z:intensity pairs), so no cosine similarity can be computed — use empirical Spearman correlation networks instead. The goal is pathway-based rather than pathway-independent network mapping, where sparse disconnected graphs are acceptable.

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra in MGF/h5py format must be scored against a spectral library (e.g., GNPS/MassBank) to retrieve structural analogues, or when similarity scores must reflect subtle structural modifications.
skills.name: mass-spectral-similarity-prediction
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-similarity-prediction Use when MS/MS spectra in MGF/h5py format must be scored against a spectral library (e.g., GNPS/MassBank) to retrieve structural analogues, or when similarity scores must reflect subtle structural modifications. When only simple heuristic comparison suffices and no analogue search or explanation is needed — the paper targets structural-analogue retrieval, where Cosine/Modified Cosine underperform When the input is not tandem MS/MS spectra (e.g., MS1 features or an already-computed feature table) When no trained model or training data (paired MS/MS spectra with structural similarity labels) is available, since TransExION is a supervised method http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Predict MS/MS spectral similarity between query and reference spectra with the Transformer-based TransExION model, whose scores correlate with structural similarity (Tanimoto), enabling spectral library search for structural analogues beyond Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, and MS2DeepScore. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Predict MS/MS spectral similarity between query and reference spectra with the Transformer-based TransExION model, whose scores correlate with structural similarity (Tanimoto), enabling spectral library search for structural analogues beyond Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, and MS2DeepScore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only simple heuristic comparison suffices and no analogue search or explanation is needed — the paper targets structural-analogue retrieval, where Cosine/Modified Cosine underperform When the input is not tandem MS/MS spectra (e.g., MS1 features or an already-computed feature table) When no trained model or training data (paired MS/MS spectra with structural similarity labels) is available, since TransExION is a supervised method

skills.description: Use when you have a query .msp spectra file (e.g. unique CSA spectra variants exported for one study) and a reference .msp library (e.g. CSA or MS/MS library from another study), and you want to annotate compounds by spectral similarity.
skills.name: mass-spectral-similarity-search
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-similarity-search Use when you have a query .msp spectra file (e.g. unique CSA spectra variants exported for one study) and a reference .msp library (e.g. CSA or MS/MS library from another study), and you want to annotate compounds by spectral similarity. The input is raw profile MS data (mzXML/mzML/netCDF) that has not yet been peak-picked — process it with IDSL.IPA and IDSL.CSA first to generate composite spectra before searching. The chemical space of interest has no representative spectra in any available reference library — available MS2 libraries poorly cover the expected chemical space, so similarity search cannot recover those compounds. You only need peak detection/chromatogram deconvolution or adduct grouping rather than library-based compound annotation. Searches .msp/.mgf mass spectra (including MS1-derived composite spectra from IDSL.CSA) against a reference spectral library using IDSL.FSA, which combines mass spectral entropy similarity, dot product (cosine) similarity, and normalized Euclidean mass error (NEME) criteria to transfer chemical annotations across untargeted metabolomics studies. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00376
skills.summary: Searches .msp/.mgf mass spectra (including MS1-derived composite spectra from IDSL.CSA) against a reference spectral library using IDSL.FSA, which combines mass spectral entropy similarity, dot product (cosine) similarity, and normalized Euclidean mass error (NEME) criteria to transfer chemical annotations across untargeted metabolomics studies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw profile MS data (mzXML/mzML/netCDF) that has not yet been peak-picked — process it with IDSL.IPA and IDSL.CSA first to generate composite spectra before searching. The chemical space of interest has no representative spectra in any available reference library — available MS2 libraries poorly cover the expected chemical space, so similarity search cannot recover those compounds. You only need peak detection/chromatogram deconvolution or adduct grouping rather than library-based compound annotation.

skills.description: Use when msp or .mgf spectra files (e.g., CSA composite spectra exported from MS1-only data, or DDA/DIA spectra) need compound-level annotations against a reference MS/MS library such as NIST 2020.
skills.name: mass-spectral-similarity-searching
skills.search_text: mass-spectral-similarity-searching Use when msp or .mgf spectra files (e.g., CSA composite spectra exported from MS1-only data, or DDA/DIA spectra) need compound-level annotations against a reference MS/MS library such as NIST 2020. Input peaks are unprocessed raw LC/HRMS files (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) — these must first be processed by IDSL.IPA and IDSL.CSA to produce composite spectra before library searching. The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than similarity-based annotation against an existing MS/MS spectral library. The query file is an aligned peak/feature table without spectra — FSA annotates .msp and .mgf spectra files, not feature tables. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates LC/HRMS spectra by searching query mass spectra (including MS1-derived composite spectra from IDSL.CSA) against reference MS/MS libraries such as NIST 2020 using the IDSL.FSA R package, scoring matches by mass spectral entropy similarity, dot-product (cosine) similarity, and normalized Euclidean mass error (NEME). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00376
skills.summary: Annotates LC/HRMS spectra by searching query mass spectra (including MS1-derived composite spectra from IDSL.CSA) against reference MS/MS libraries such as NIST 2020 using the IDSL.FSA R package, scoring matches by mass spectral entropy similarity, dot-product (cosine) similarity, and normalized Euclidean mass error (NEME).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input peaks are unprocessed raw LC/HRMS files (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) — these must first be processed by IDSL.IPA and IDSL.CSA to produce composite spectra before library searching. The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than similarity-based annotation against an existing MS/MS spectral library. The query file is an aligned peak/feature table without spectra — FSA annotates .msp and .mgf spectra files, not feature tables.

skills.description: Use when a study provides proprietary Thermo .raw files plus a sample-metadata CSV and centroided mzML inputs are required for downstream LC-MS preprocessing (e.g., Asari in pcpfm).
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-acquisition-metadata-handling
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-acquisition-metadata-handling Use when a study provides proprietary Thermo .raw files plus a sample-metadata CSV and centroided mzML inputs are required for downstream LC-MS preprocessing (e.g., Asari in pcpfm). The input data are already .mzML files — pcpfm skips this step entirely and proceeds directly to preprocessing. Acquisitions come from non-Thermo instruments, since ThermoRawFileParser targets Thermo .raw files; the README notes '.raw files but support is limited'. A feature table already exists and no raw-level reprocessing is needed — this skill only produces conversion-ready mzML inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts proprietary Thermo .raw LC-MS acquisitions into centroided .mzML files using ThermoRawFileParser, driven by an experiment metadata CSV that maps sample names to raw file paths, so the pcpfm pipeline can proceed to Asari preprocessing. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: Converts proprietary Thermo .raw LC-MS acquisitions into centroided .mzML files using ThermoRawFileParser, driven by an experiment metadata CSV that maps sample names to raw file paths, so the pcpfm pipeline can proceed to Asari preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are already .mzML files — pcpfm skips this step entirely and proceeds directly to preprocessing. Acquisitions come from non-Thermo instruments, since ThermoRawFileParser targets Thermo .raw files; the README notes '.raw files but support is limited'. A feature table already exists and no raw-level reprocessing is needed — this skill only produces conversion-ready mzML inputs.

skills.description: Use when an LC/MS feature table contains multiple features per analyte (isotope/adduct/fragment series) and you must assign quasi-molecular ion species, charge states, or neutral losses to reduce feature-list redundancy before statistical analysis or compound identification.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-adduct-annotation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-adduct-annotation Use when an LC/MS feature table contains multiple features per analyte (isotope/adduct/fragment series) and you must assign quasi-molecular ion species, charge states, or neutral losses to reduce feature-list redundancy before statistical analysis or compound identification. The input is already an annotated, de-isotoped feature list with one feature per analyte — annotation would add nothing and risk misassignment. The compound spectrum contains only the molecular ion and fragment ions with no further adducts and the neutral loss has not been added to the rule set — CAMERA cannot annotate such cases directly. The data come from a single ungrouped peak list without prior isotope/retention-time/intensity-correlation grouping; rule matching operates within compound spectra, not raw peak lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate the ion species (adducts, neutral losses, cluster ions, isotopes) underlying each LC/MS feature by matching within-compound-spectrum m/z differences against a dynamic rule set, as implemented in the CAMERA Bioconductor package for untargeted metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/ac202450g
skills.summary: Annotate the ion species (adducts, neutral losses, cluster ions, isotopes) underlying each LC/MS feature by matching within-compound-spectrum m/z differences against a dynamic rule set, as implemented in the CAMERA Bioconductor package for untargeted metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an annotated, de-isotoped feature list with one feature per analyte — annotation would add nothing and risk misassignment. The compound spectrum contains only the molecular ion and fragment ions with no further adducts and the neutral loss has not been added to the rule set — CAMERA cannot annotate such cases directly. The data come from a single ungrouped peak list without prior isotope/retention-time/intensity-correlation grouping; rule matching operates within compound spectra, not raw peak lists.

skills.description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks where suspected matrix or salt adducts (e.g., DHB) may inflate peak counts or cause false-positive metabolite identifications from exact mass alone.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-adduct-identification
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-adduct-identification Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks where suspected matrix or salt adducts (e.g., DHB) may inflate peak counts or cause false-positive metabolite identifications from exact mass alone. When the input is already a fully annotated feature table where adducts have been explicitly resolved and removed (e.g., post-annotation deconvolution), as this skill operates on raw peak m/z lists to discover adducts de novo. When the data are LC-MS/MS or non-imaging spectra without spatial/pixel information, since `corrPairsMSI()` co-localization confirmation relies on spatially resolved pixel intensities and `msimat` objects. When only exact-mass database annotation is needed and matrix/salt adducts are known to be negligible for the sample type—although the paper argues adducts are rarely negligible, the skill is not designed to replace conventional database searching itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A computational skill for identifying and quantifying metabolite adducts (e.g., DHB, salt) in MALDI-MSI data by computing all pairwise mass differences between detected m/z peaks, binning them, and matching them against a reference adduct list (e.g., DHB-H₂O at 136.016 Da) using spatial co-localization as orthogonal confirmation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: A computational skill for identifying and quantifying metabolite adducts (e.g., DHB, salt) in MALDI-MSI data by computing all pairwise mass differences between detected m/z peaks, binning them, and matching them against a reference adduct list (e.g., DHB-H₂O at 136.016 Da) using spatial co-localization as orthogonal confirmation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a fully annotated feature table where adducts have been explicitly resolved and removed (e.g., post-annotation deconvolution), as this skill operates on raw peak m/z lists to discover adducts de novo. When the data are LC-MS/MS or non-imaging spectra without spatial/pixel information, since `corrPairsMSI()` co-localization confirmation relies on spatially resolved pixel intensities and `msimat` objects. When only exact-mass database annotation is needed and matrix/salt adducts are known to be negligible for the sample type—although the paper argues adducts are rarely negligible, the skill is not designed to replace conventional database searching itself.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking annotation propagation on a molecular network: you need to quantify whether annotations reach nodes not directly connected to spectral library matches, not just first neighbours.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-annotation-evaluation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-annotation-evaluation Use when benchmarking annotation propagation on a molecular network: you need to quantify whether annotations reach nodes not directly connected to spectral library matches, not just first neighbours. Input is an unannotated molecular network with no spectral library matches — the seed set would be empty and no propagation benchmark is possible Goal is only local first-neighbour annotation (NAP-style) rather than evaluating propagation beyond direct neighbours No candidate structures available from in silico fragmentation (MetFrag), since ChemWalker propagates through candidate structures rather than raw spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Evaluates molecular-network annotation quality by testing whether random-walk propagation (ChemWalker) annotates nodes that lack any direct neighbour with a spectral library match, overcoming NAP's local first-neighbour limitation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad078
skills.summary: Evaluates molecular-network annotation quality by testing whether random-walk propagation (ChemWalker) annotates nodes that lack any direct neighbour with a spectral library match, overcoming NAP's local first-neighbour limitation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unannotated molecular network with no spectral library matches — the seed set would be empty and no propagation benchmark is possible Goal is only local first-neighbour annotation (NAP-style) rather than evaluating propagation beyond direct neighbours No candidate structures available from in silico fragmentation (MetFrag), since ChemWalker propagates through candidate structures rather than raw spectra

skills.description: Use when you have SIRIUS/ZODIAC annotation output files plus ground-truth formula lists (e.g. from MassIVE MSV000080502, MSV000081364) and need to reproduce or extend the molecular formula accuracy benchmark.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-annotation-file-parsing
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-annotation-file-parsing Use when you have SIRIUS/ZODIAC annotation output files plus ground-truth formula lists (e.g. from MassIVE MSV000080502, MSV000081364) and need to reproduce or extend the molecular formula accuracy benchmark. Raw mzML/mzXML spectra that have not yet been annotated by SIRIUS/ZODIAC — run the annotation pipeline first (including the modified OpenMS 2.4.0 workflow), not this parsing step Structure-level identification tasks (CSI:FingerID database search) — this skill only compares top-ranked molecular formulas, not structural hits Datasets lacking a manually validated ground truth — accuracy and error-rate columns cannot be computed without it http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parse deposited SIRIUS and ZODIAC molecular formula annotation result files and match top-ranked formulas against manually validated ground truth to compute per-dataset annotation accuracy and error rates across five biological LC-MS/MS datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Parse deposited SIRIUS and ZODIAC molecular formula annotation result files and match top-ranked formulas against manually validated ground truth to compute per-dataset annotation accuracy and error rates across five biological LC-MS/MS datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw mzML/mzXML spectra that have not yet been annotated by SIRIUS/ZODIAC — run the annotation pipeline first (including the modified OpenMS 2.4.0 workflow), not this parsing step Structure-level identification tasks (CSI:FingerID database search) — this skill only compares top-ranked molecular formulas, not structural hits Datasets lacking a manually validated ground truth — accuracy and error-rate columns cannot be computed without it

skills.description: Use when evaluating spectral annotation models on a candidate set and you need average rank / Rank@K metrics, or relative improvement percentages (e.g. 23.7% and 37.2%) against baselines.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-annotation-rank-metric-computation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-annotation-rank-metric-computation Use when evaluating spectral annotation models on a candidate set and you need average rank / Rank@K metrics, or relative improvement percentages (e.g. 23.7% and 37.2%) against baselines. When the models being compared were evaluated on different candidate sets or different training datasets (e.g. NPLIB1-published models vs unpublished NIST-20-trained models) — ranks are not comparable across these conditions. When only top-1 or top-5 hit rate is needed for a definitive conclusion: the paper notes 'MLP approaches remain strong contenders when considering top five ranks', so Rank@K alone can contradict average-rank conclusions. When trying to reproduce NIST-20-trained metric tables end-to-end: NIST-20 data is not published alongside the NIST-20-trained models due to NIST license regulations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes average rank and Rank@K (k=1..20) metrics for mass spectrometry metabolite annotation models (MLP, GNN, ESP) on candidate sets, and derives relative improvement percentages such as the 23.7%/37.2% average-rank gains ESP shows over MLP/GNN baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae490
skills.summary: Computes average rank and Rank@K (k=1..20) metrics for mass spectrometry metabolite annotation models (MLP, GNN, ESP) on candidate sets, and derives relative improvement percentages such as the 23.7%/37.2% average-rank gains ESP shows over MLP/GNN baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the models being compared were evaluated on different candidate sets or different training datasets (e.g. NPLIB1-published models vs unpublished NIST-20-trained models) — ranks are not comparable across these conditions. When only top-1 or top-5 hit rate is needed for a definitive conclusion: the paper notes 'MLP approaches remain strong contenders when considering top five ranks', so Rank@K alone can contradict average-rank conclusions. When trying to reproduce NIST-20-trained metric tables end-to-end: NIST-20 data is not published alongside the NIST-20-trained models due to NIST license regulations.

skills.description: Use when processing full-scan AEMS spectra (precursor ion or neutral loss modes) from 384- or 1536-well plates where persistent high-intensity baseline signals obscure weaker, less well-defined analyte peaks that need quantification.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-area-integration
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-area-integration Use when processing full-scan AEMS spectra (precursor ion or neutral loss modes) from 384- or 1536-well plates where persistent high-intensity baseline signals obscure weaker, less well-defined analyte peaks that need quantification. Data are MRM acquisitions (<5 transitions) rather than full-scan spectra — rtmsEcho handles MRM with a separate, faster path and reference-peak alignment is unnecessary Spectra lack well-defined high-mass reference peaks above the persistent baseline, so no anchor frames can be established Data are conventional chromatography-coupled LC-MS runs, not acoustic ejection plate-based acquisitions http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies analyte abundance in acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) data by baseline-correcting signal traces and integrating peak areas within time frames anchored to well-defined high-mass reference peaks, as implemented in the rtmsEcho R package. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03730
skills.summary: Quantifies analyte abundance in acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) data by baseline-correcting signal traces and integrating peak areas within time frames anchored to well-defined high-mass reference peaks, as implemented in the rtmsEcho R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are MRM acquisitions (<5 transitions) rather than full-scan spectra — rtmsEcho handles MRM with a separate, faster path and reference-peak alignment is unnecessary Spectra lack well-defined high-mass reference peaks above the persistent baseline, so no anchor frames can be established Data are conventional chromatography-coupled LC-MS runs, not acoustic ejection plate-based acquisitions

skills.description: Use when raw vendor MS files (e.g. SCIEX .wiff/.wiff.scan) contain compressed binary m/z and intensity arrays that must be decompressed and reassembled into usable spectra before peak integration or quantification.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-array-decompression
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-array-decompression Use when raw vendor MS files (e.g. SCIEX .wiff/.wiff.scan) contain compressed binary m/z and intensity arrays that must be decompressed and reassembled into usable spectra before peak integration or quantification. Input is already an open-format spectrum (e.g. mzML or an R rtms object) that needs no byte-stream decompression. Data are MRM acquisitions rather than full-scan (PI or NL) mode, where per-transition traces rather than reconstructed full spectra are needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs full m/z-intensity spectra from compressed binary byte streams embedded in vendor scan blocks (e.g. .wiff.scan blocks from SCIEX .wiff files) so that per-ejection AEMS spectra can be built in rtms-compatible R data structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03730
skills.summary: Reconstructs full m/z-intensity spectra from compressed binary byte streams embedded in vendor scan blocks (e.g. .wiff.scan blocks from SCIEX .wiff files) so that per-ejection AEMS spectra can be built in rtms-compatible R data structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an open-format spectrum (e.g. mzML or an R rtms object) that needs no byte-stream decompression. Data are MRM acquisitions rather than full-scan (PI or NL) mode, where per-transition traces rather than reconstructed full spectra are needed.

skills.description: Use when you have a set of MS/MS spectra (a .mgf file from MZmine or a list of USIs in .csv/.tsv) and need to find matching datasets and taxa in public metabolomics repositories.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-batch-search
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-batch-search Use when you have a set of MS/MS spectra (a .mgf file from MZmine or a list of USIs in .csv/.tsv) and need to find matching datasets and taxa in public metabolomics repositories. Only a single spectrum needs searching — the standalone microbeMASST web app (https://masst.gnps2.org/microbemasst/) searches one spectrum at a time Input is already a feature table or aggregated counts rather than raw MS/MS spectra/USIs The target domain is not microbial (e.g., plant metabolites) — use plantMASST or another domain-specific MASST http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Batch-search multiple MS/MS spectra (e.g., GNPS library spectra of microbial metabolites) against indexed public datasets using the microbeMASST/Fast Search API via jobs.py, to trace which taxa match each spectrum. Used to taxonomically validate molecular annotations across GNPS/MassIVE, Metabolomics Workbench, Metabolights, and NORMAN. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Batch-search multiple MS/MS spectra (e.g., GNPS library spectra of microbial metabolites) against indexed public datasets using the microbeMASST/Fast Search API via jobs.py, to trace which taxa match each spectrum. Used to taxonomically validate molecular annotations across GNPS/MassIVE, Metabolomics Workbench, Metabolights, and NORMAN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single spectrum needs searching — the standalone microbeMASST web app (https://masst.gnps2.org/microbemasst/) searches one spectrum at a time Input is already a feature table or aggregated counts rather than raw MS/MS spectra/USIs The target domain is not microbial (e.g., plant metabolites) — use plantMASST or another domain-specific MASST

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics/mass-spectrometry paper or abstract states numeric performance claims (runtimes, speedup factors, latency, accuracy, memory overhead) that must be tabulated and traced verbatim to source text.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-benchmark-claim-extraction
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-benchmark-claim-extraction Use when a metabolomics/mass-spectrometry paper or abstract states numeric performance claims (runtimes, speedup factors, latency, accuracy, memory overhead) that must be tabulated and traced verbatim to source text. The source text contains no quantitative benchmark claims (e.g. purely qualitative method descriptions), so there is nothing to parse into metric/condition/value rows Claims appear only in the discussion or supplementary text rather than the abstract, since the extraction here is grounded in verbatim abstract statements You need to reproduce the benchmark experiments themselves rather than extract the paper's reported claim values Extracts every quantitative performance claim about spectral similarity search from a mass-spectrometry methods paper (here, flash entropy search vs. full dot product/entropy similarity on ~1-billion-spectra libraries) and structures them into a machine-readable benchmark_claims.csv with metric, experimental condition, and reported value. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-023-02012-9
skills.summary: Extracts every quantitative performance claim about spectral similarity search from a mass-spectrometry methods paper (here, flash entropy search vs. full dot product/entropy similarity on ~1-billion-spectra libraries) and structures them into a machine-readable benchmark_claims.csv with metric, experimental condition, and reported value.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source text contains no quantitative benchmark claims (e.g. purely qualitative method descriptions), so there is nothing to parse into metric/condition/value rows Claims appear only in the discussion or supplementary text rather than the abstract, since the extraction here is grounded in verbatim abstract statements You need to reproduce the benchmark experiments themselves rather than extract the paper's reported claim values

skills.description: Decision support for quantifying how scaffold retrieval error limits spectra-conditioned molecular generation, when per-condition metric tables for both an oracle scaffold retriever (lookup table) and a predictive contrastive retriever are available alongside SPA values.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-benchmark-metric-tabulation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-benchmark-metric-tabulation Decision support for quantifying how scaffold retrieval error limits spectra-conditioned molecular generation, when per-condition metric tables for both an oracle scaffold retriever (lookup table) and a predictive contrastive retriever are available alongside SPA values. Only one retriever condition (oracle or predictive alone) is available — no oracle-minus-predictive gap can be computed without paired per-condition tables The goal is to evaluate a method like MSNovelist whose results are limited to accuracy metrics — Tanimoto similarity and MCES edit distance are unavailable ('-') for such methods and cannot be gap-tabulated The question is about generation quality with the oracle retriever only (e.g., attention-integration effectiveness), not about the effect of scaffold retrieval error http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Tabulates oracle-vs-predictive performance gaps for MADGEN's two-stage scaffold-based de novo generation across NIST23, CANOPUS, and MassSpecGym, joining each metric gap with the retriever's scaffold prediction accuracy (SPA) to quantify how scaffold retrieval error constrains generation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2501.01950
skills.summary: Tabulates oracle-vs-predictive performance gaps for MADGEN's two-stage scaffold-based de novo generation across NIST23, CANOPUS, and MassSpecGym, joining each metric gap with the retriever's scaffold prediction accuracy (SPA) to quantify how scaffold retrieval error constrains generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one retriever condition (oracle or predictive alone) is available — no oracle-minus-predictive gap can be computed without paired per-condition tables The goal is to evaluate a method like MSNovelist whose results are limited to accuracy metrics — Tanimoto similarity and MCES edit distance are unavailable ('-') for such methods and cannot be gap-tabulated The question is about generation quality with the oracle retriever only (e.g., attention-integration effectiveness), not about the effect of scaffold retrieval error

skills.description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Scientific raw Orbitrap file and you need to inspect or plot centroided MS/MS scans, a total ion chromatogram over MS1 scans, or extracted ion chromatograms directly from R.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-centroided-spectra-visualization
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-centroided-spectra-visualization Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Scientific raw Orbitrap file and you need to inspect or plot centroided MS/MS scans, a total ion chromatogram over MS1 scans, or extracted ion chromatograms directly from R. skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-data-compression Use when converting vendor MS files (SCIEX, Thermo, Agilent; DDA, DIA/SWATH, PRM, PASEF) into a computation-oriented format where decoding speed and m/z storage size matter, or when benchmarking ZDPD against Zlib-only compression. The data must remain strictly lossless in the original floating-point domain — ZDPD quantizes m/z floats to integers at a controllable precision The required acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility, which were under development at publication time The goal is lossless m/z-only compression of existing mzXML files without format conversion — MassComp targets that case instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compress mass spectrometry m/z arrays using Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD) scheme — quantize floats to integers, delta-code, then SIMD-accelerated FastPfor encoding wrapped in Zlib — to reach ~55% smaller m/z data than Zlib-only and ~3x faster decoding. This addresses the bottleneck that vendor formats and mzML/mgf/mz5 are slow to decode in computational workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Compress mass spectrometry m/z arrays using Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD) scheme — quantize floats to integers, delta-code, then SIMD-accelerated FastPfor encoding wrapped in Zlib — to reach ~55% smaller m/z data than Zlib-only and ~3x faster decoding. This addresses the bottleneck that vendor formats and mzML/mgf/mz5 are slow to decode in computational workflows.

skills.summary: Preprocess tandem mass spectrometry datasets for de novo chemical formula assignment by enumerating RDBE-plausible formula candidates from MS1 exact masses with SIRIUS's 'decomp' dynamic-programming module, then downselecting the (often >5,000) candidates per spectrum with the FastFilter energy model to a tractable top-256 set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are negative ion mode — MIST-CF/FastFilter models were trained only for positive-mode data, so candidate filtering would be unsupported. Candidates already come from a curated database search (e.g., NIST, GNPS, HMDB, PubChem) rather than de novo mass decomposition, so RDBE-permissive enumeration and FastFilter downselection are unnecessary. A NIST20-trained model is required for Orbitrap/high-resolution data but unavailable — the released quickstart model (public NPLIB1/CANOPUS data) may underperform on such spectra.
