skills.description: Use when evaluating small-molecule identification accuracy of a mass spectral database-search method on spectra with known true structures, such as benchmarking top-1/3/5/10 accuracy on the PNNL lipid library against LMSD compounds.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-scoring
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-scoring Use when evaluating small-molecule identification accuracy of a mass spectral database-search method on spectra with known true structures, such as benchmarking top-1/3/5/10 accuracy on the PNNL lipid library against LMSD compounds. Spectra are from molecules outside the pretrained model's scope, e.g. super small molecules (<400 Da) where existing ML methods perform poorly or heavy molecules (>1000 Da) that are computationally insufficient The goal is novel compound discovery with no candidate structure database — de novo prediction or spectral library search against GNPS reference spectra is the appropriate alternative Spectra were acquired in negative ion mode or with fragmentation conditions far outside the default model, which was trained on combined CID/HCD positive-mode spectra and does not fully model instrument type, dissociation technique, or collision energy http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Benchmark mass spectral database-search identification accuracy by scoring tandem MS spectra against candidate molecular structures with molDiscovery's learned probabilistic fragmentation model, then computing top-k accuracy against known true molecules (e.g., 15,917 PNNL lipid library [M+H]+ spectra searched against the 39,126-compound LMSD database). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Benchmark mass spectral database-search identification accuracy by scoring tandem MS spectra against candidate molecular structures with molDiscovery's learned probabilistic fragmentation model, then computing top-k accuracy against known true molecules (e.g., 15,917 PNNL lipid library [M+H]+ spectra searched against the 39,126-compound LMSD database).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are from molecules outside the pretrained model's scope, e.g. super small molecules (<400 Da) where existing ML methods perform poorly or heavy molecules (>1000 Da) that are computationally insufficient The goal is novel compound discovery with no candidate structure database — de novo prediction or spectral library search against GNPS reference spectra is the appropriate alternative Spectra were acquired in negative ion mode or with fragmentation conditions far outside the default model, which was trained on combined CID/HCD positive-mode spectra and does not fully model instrument type, dissociation technique, or collision energy

skills.description: Use when you have paired genome + LC-MS/MS samples and need to turn raw fragmentation spectra (GNPS job output or cryptic spectra) into per-sample MS/MS fingerprints for BGC linking or benchmarking.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-spectrum-processing
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-spectrum-processing Use when you have paired genome + LC-MS/MS samples and need to turn raw fragmentation spectra (GNPS job output or cryptic spectra) into per-sample MS/MS fingerprints for BGC linking or benchmarking. The query organism has no BGCs similar to the NPOmix training set (e.g., a fungal species with no BGC similar to any PoDP-derived training BGC) — output would contain no answer The goal is distinguishing isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — the correlation-based approach lacks that resolution Only raw spectra without any paired genome/metagenome data exist, since linking requires the genomic fingerprint side Processes untargeted LC-MS/MS fragmentation spectra into MS/MS similarity fingerprints for BGC–metabolite linking: GNPS-computed pairwise modified cosine scores are aggregated per sample into a testing matrix that feeds the k-nearest neighbor classifier (NPOmix) and enables benchmarking linking precision/recall against validated links. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Processes untargeted LC-MS/MS fragmentation spectra into MS/MS similarity fingerprints for BGC–metabolite linking: GNPS-computed pairwise modified cosine scores are aggregated per sample into a testing matrix that feeds the k-nearest neighbor classifier (NPOmix) and enables benchmarking linking precision/recall against validated links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query organism has no BGCs similar to the NPOmix training set (e.g., a fungal species with no BGC similar to any PoDP-derived training BGC) — output would contain no answer The goal is distinguishing isomers or regioselectivity of homologs — the correlation-based approach lacks that resolution Only raw spectra without any paired genome/metagenome data exist, since linking requires the genomic fingerprint side

skills.description: Use when you have 2D DESI-MSI hyperspectral images of a tissue with an approximate linear developmental gradient (e.g., maize root tip) and need to assign mass signatures to developmental enrichment clusters.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-image-linescan-projection
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-image-linescan-projection Use when you have 2D DESI-MSI hyperspectral images of a tissue with an approximate linear developmental gradient (e.g., maize root tip) and need to assign mass signatures to developmental enrichment clusters. The tissue lacks a linear developmental axis or the developmental positions are not aligned across samples, since projection to a single axis assumes comparable longitudinal coordinates. You already have a precomputed feature table of signals per sample (no spatial 2D ion images to project) — clustering, not linescan projection, is the relevant step. Input is raw, unprocessed MSI data; DIMPLE requires the preprocessing/harmonization stage to be completed first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Project 2D DESI-MSI ion-intensity images along a root's longitudinal (developmental) axis into 1D linescans, then cluster mass signatures with Ward hierarchical clustering so metabolites with similar developmental enrichment patterns (e.g., meristem/root-tip enrichment in B73 maize roots) group together. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Project 2D DESI-MSI ion-intensity images along a root's longitudinal (developmental) axis into 1D linescans, then cluster mass signatures with Ward hierarchical clustering so metabolites with similar developmental enrichment patterns (e.g., meristem/root-tip enrichment in B73 maize roots) group together.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue lacks a linear developmental axis or the developmental positions are not aligned across samples, since projection to a single axis assumes comparable longitudinal coordinates. You already have a precomputed feature table of signals per sample (no spatial 2D ion images to project) — clustering, not linescan projection, is the relevant step. Input is raw, unprocessed MSI data; DIMPLE requires the preprocessing/harmonization stage to be completed first.

skills.description: Use when a peak-picked MSI dataset (e.g., imzML loaded into Cardinal as a processed MSImagingExperiment) must be partitioned into chemically homogeneous tissue segments without class labels, and the expected number of segments is known from a reference figure or must be selected by scanning.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-image-segmentation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-image-segmentation Use when a peak-picked MSI dataset (e.g., imzML loaded into Cardinal as a processed MSImagingExperiment) must be partitioned into chemically homogeneous tissue segments without class labels, and the expected number of segments is known from a reference figure or must be selected by scanning. The goal is classification to pre-defined class labels rather than unsupervised segmentation — use Cardinal's image classification (which assigns locations to pre-defined classes and estimates error by cross-validation) instead. The input spectra are not yet peak-picked/pre-processed; first apply Cardinal's pre-processing pipeline (normalize, smooth, reduceBaseline, peakPick/peakAlign/peakProcess) before segmenting. Raw spectra exceed memory and the data have not been prepared with Cardinal's larger-than-memory matter backend. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Unsupervised segmentation of mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) pixels into tissue segments using Cardinal's Spatial Shrunken Centroids with a Spatially-Aware ('gaussian') distance, demonstrated on peak-picked pig fetus data (28,016 non-background pixels, 10,200 mass features, 298 detected peaks) yielding 11 tissue segments. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv146
skills.summary: Unsupervised segmentation of mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) pixels into tissue segments using Cardinal's Spatial Shrunken Centroids with a Spatially-Aware ('gaussian') distance, demonstrated on peak-picked pig fetus data (28,016 non-background pixels, 10,200 mass features, 298 detected peaks) yielding 11 tissue segments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classification to pre-defined class labels rather than unsupervised segmentation — use Cardinal's image classification (which assigns locations to pre-defined classes and estimates error by cross-validation) instead. The input spectra are not yet peak-picked/pre-processed; first apply Cardinal's pre-processing pipeline (normalize, smooth, reduceBaseline, peakPick/peakAlign/peakProcess) before segmenting. Raw spectra exceed memory and the data have not been prepared with Cardinal's larger-than-memory matter backend.

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI MSI spectra (e.g. imzML/HDF5 with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be classified into tissue classes (normal vs tumor) with per-pixel probabilities, and the probabilistic outputs must be mapped back into image space to localize classification uncertainty such as at tumor.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-classification
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-imaging-classification Use when raw MALDI MSI spectra (e.g. imzML/HDF5 with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be classified into tissue classes (normal vs tumor) with per-pixel probabilities, and the probabilistic outputs must be mapped back into image space to localize classification uncertainty such as at tumor. When a feature table or peak-picked spectra are already available and a classical ML method (e.g. SVM) with prior spectral preprocessing is preferred — massNet is designed to classify directly from raw spectra without prior preprocessing or peak picking When the task requires multi-class tissue classification — the paper demonstrates only binary class classification (normal vs tumor) and leaves multi-class extension for future development When reliable ground truth annotation is unavailable — the paper notes annotating MSI data from histology alone is an approximation, especially with intra-tumor heterogeneity http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A deep-learning skill for probabilistic pixel-based classification of MALDI mass spectrometry imaging data directly from raw mass spectra, without prior preprocessing or peak picking, and for spatially reconstructing predicted class probabilities and uncertainty to visualize tumor margins. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: A deep-learning skill for probabilistic pixel-based classification of MALDI mass spectrometry imaging data directly from raw mass spectra, without prior preprocessing or peak picking, and for spatially reconstructing predicted class probabilities and uncertainty to visualize tumor margins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a feature table or peak-picked spectra are already available and a classical ML method (e.g. SVM) with prior spectral preprocessing is preferred — massNet is designed to classify directly from raw spectra without prior preprocessing or peak picking When the task requires multi-class tissue classification — the paper demonstrates only binary class classification (normal vs tumor) and leaves multi-class extension for future development When reliable ground truth annotation is unavailable — the paper notes annotating MSI data from histology alone is an approximation, especially with intra-tumor heterogeneity

skills.description: Use when imzML MSI pixel spectra need unsupervised segmentation into tissue clusters, especially when t-SNE embedding parameters (perplexity, learning rate, iterations) must be tuned and compared via Silhouette score.

skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-imaging-clustering Use when imzML MSI pixel spectra need unsupervised segmentation into tissue clusters, especially when t-SNE embedding parameters (perplexity, learning rate, iterations) must be tuned and compared via Silhouette score. The goal is peptide identification confidence from untargeted LC-MS/MS confirmation rather than unsupervised tissue segmentation of MSI pixels Input is not spatially resolved imaging data (e.g., bulk LC-MS/MS or already-extracted feature tables), since the skill depends on per-pixel imzML spectra and ion-image context A supervised or histology-guided segmentation is required — this skill is unsupervised k-means on t-SNE embeddings and does not by itself use H&E co-registration http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3344 Unsupervised segmentation of MALDI-MSI pixel spectra by embedding preprocessed intensity data via PCA-to-t-SNE and k-means clustering, with Silhouette-score-based comparison of t-SNE hyperparameter optimization strategies (exhaustive, random, Bayesian) as implemented in MSIght. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Unsupervised segmentation of MALDI-MSI pixel spectra by embedding preprocessed intensity data via PCA-to-t-SNE and k-means clustering, with Silhouette-score-based comparison of t-SNE hyperparameter optimization strategies (exhaustive, random, Bayesian) as implemented in MSIght.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peptide identification confidence from untargeted LC-MS/MS confirmation rather than unsupervised tissue segmentation of MSI pixels Input is not spatially resolved imaging data (e.g., bulk LC-MS/MS or already-extracted feature tables), since the skill depends on per-pixel imzML spectra and ion-image context A supervised or histology-guided segmentation is required — this skill is unsupervised k-means on t-SNE embeddings and does not by itself use H&E co-registration

skills.description: Use when a trained massNet-style VAE over high-dimensional MALDI MSI spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) exists and you need to inspect its 5-D latent space or check normal-vs-tumor separability in a 2D UMAP map.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-spectra-embedding
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-imaging-spectra-embedding Use when a trained massNet-style VAE over high-dimensional MALDI MSI spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) exists and you need to inspect its 5-D latent space or check normal-vs-tumor separability in a 2D UMAP map. No trained encoder is available and you would have to run UMAP directly on the raw 85,062-dimensional spectra — the paper deliberately embeds the 5-D latent variable instead of the original MSI data to avoid the curse of dimensionality. The data are already reduced to a peak/feature table or low-dimensional representation — re-embedding with this skill is redundant. The goal is spectral preprocessing or peak picking (e.g., msiPL-based peak identification) rather than latent-space embedding — massNet consumes raw spectra without prior preprocessing and peak picking. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Embeds high-dimensional MALDI FT-ICR mass spectra into a low-dimensional latent space by forwarding them through a trained massNet variational autoencoder (5-dimensional Code layer) and then visualizes the codes with UMAP to expose normal-vs-tumor separation and inter-tumor heterogeneity. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Embeds high-dimensional MALDI FT-ICR mass spectra into a low-dimensional latent space by forwarding them through a trained massNet variational autoencoder (5-dimensional Code layer) and then visualizes the codes with UMAP to expose normal-vs-tumor separation and inter-tumor heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trained encoder is available and you would have to run UMAP directly on the raw 85,062-dimensional spectra — the paper deliberately embeds the 5-D latent variable instead of the original MSI data to avoid the curse of dimensionality. The data are already reduced to a peak/feature table or low-dimensional representation — re-embedding with this skill is redundant. The goal is spectral preprocessing or peak picking (e.g., msiPL-based peak identification) rather than latent-space embedding — massNet consumes raw spectra without prior preprocessing and peak picking.

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra contain many low-intensity noise peaks — e.g. prior to peak annotation, library comparison, or spectrum visualization — and you need to restrict peaks to a fraction of the base peak intensity and cap their number.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-intensity-filtering
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-intensity-filtering Use when MS/MS spectra contain many low-intensity noise peaks — e.g. prior to peak annotation, library comparison, or spectrum visualization — and you need to restrict peaks to a fraction of the base peak intensity and cap their number. spectrum_utils does not provide functionality to read spectral data files; do not use this skill as the file-reading step — obtain spectra from an external reader (e.g. pymzML) first. Spectra that are already denoised peak lists (few, high-quality fragment peaks) — further aggressive filtering (50-peak cap, 5% base-peak cutoff) could discard informative low-abundance fragments. skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-lipidomics-validation Use when a targeted lipidomics transition list (PRM/SRM) has been generated in silico — e.g., LipidCreator-computed fragment masses for defined fatty acyl combinations — and you must confirm the computed ion signatures yield linear instrument response before deploying the assay. The spectrum identifier is a SPLASH hash rather than a USI — SPLASH requires a complex hashing operation and is not trivially constructed, so a different retrieval path is needed The data are stored only as local raw files not deposited in a supported repository (GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, ProteomeXchange), since the resolver can only retrieve deposited spectra You need MS/MS-specific interactive figure customization beyond the resolver's plotting parameters — generic vector editors like Inkscape lack MS/MS features but offer higher customization at significant time cost http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Retrieve MS/MS spectra from heterogeneous repositories (GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, ProteomeXchange) in a unified fashion by constructing a metabolomics-extended Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) and querying the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver web service for machine-readable (/json/, /csv/) or image (/png/, /svg/) output. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Retrieve MS/MS spectra from heterogeneous repositories (GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, ProteomeXchange) in a unified fashion by constructing a metabolomics-extended Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) and querying the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver web service for machine-readable (/json/, /csv/) or image (/png/, /svg/) output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum identifier is a SPLASH hash rather than a USI — SPLASH requires a complex hashing operation and is not trivially constructed, so a different retrieval path is needed The data are stored only as local raw files not deposited in a supported repository (GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, ProteomeXchange), since the resolver can only retrieve deposited spectra You need MS/MS-specific interactive figure customization beyond the resolver's plotting parameters — generic vector editors like Inkscape lack MS/MS features but offer higher customization at significant time cost

GPU-accelerated dynamic programming (DP) algorithm against the conventional CPU DP implementation for computer-assisted mixture structure elucidation from high-resolution mass spectra, quantifying acceleration factors at up to five decimal digits of mass (D=5). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-017-0238-7
skills.summary: Benchmark the G.A.M.E. GPU-accelerated dynamic programming (DP) algorithm against the conventional CPU DP implementation for computer-assisted mixture structure elucidation from high-resolution mass spectra, quantifying acceleration factors at up to five decimal digits of mass (D=5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a computed acceleration-factor table or published timing comparison rather than raw GPU/CPU runtime measurements The analysis targets single-compound structure elucidation rather than mixture (CSCCP) elucidation from high-resolution mass spectra Mass data require more than five decimal digits, beyond G.A.M.E.'s supported range, or the DP problem size is small enough that GPU overhead negates speedup

skills.description: Use when raw mass spectra have variable total ion counts and ragged, non-uniform m/z grids, and you need a TIC-filtered, uniformly binned feature matrix (CSV) for CNN/Transformer classifiers.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-tic-filtering
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-tic-filtering Use when raw mass spectra have variable total ion counts and ragged, non-uniform m/z grids, and you need a TIC-filtered, uniformly binned feature matrix (CSV) for CNN/Transformer classifiers. Input is already a uniform feature table or is already TIC normalized, as the MSMCE repo expects ('the input of each dataset is tic normalized in this implementation') Data requiring retention-time-aware preprocessing beyond simple m/z binning (the rt_binning_window parameter targets RT data, not spectral TIC quality control) Spectra from instruments or acquisition modes where low-TIC spectra carry real biological signal and a hard 1×10^4 TIC cutoff would discard valid measurements http://edamontology.org/topic_0081 Preprocess raw SpiderMass-style mass spectra (e.g., the Canine Sarcoma dataset) by removing low-quality spectra with total ion count (TIC) below 1×10^4 and binning retained spectra along the m/z axis at 0.1 Da so every spectrum becomes a fixed-length feature vector for downstream deep-learning classifiers like MSMCE-ResNet50. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: Preprocess raw SpiderMass-style mass spectra (e.g., the Canine Sarcoma dataset) by removing low-quality spectra with total ion count (TIC) below 1×10^4 and binning retained spectra along the m/z axis at 0.1 Da so every spectrum becomes a fixed-length feature vector for downstream deep-learning classifiers like MSMCE-ResNet50.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a uniform feature table or is already TIC normalized, as the MSMCE repo expects ('the input of each dataset is tic normalized in this implementation') Data requiring retention-time-aware preprocessing beyond simple m/z binning (the rt_binning_window parameter targets RT data, not spectral TIC quality control) Spectra from instruments or acquisition modes where low-TIC spectra carry real biological signal and a hard 1×10^4 TIC cutoff would discard valid measurements

skills.description: Decision support for setting mass and RT matching tolerances when linking peak-picked features to in silico lipid precursor and fragment libraries in LipidMatch.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-tolerance-configuration
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-tolerance-configuration Decision support for setting mass and RT matching tolerances when linking peak-picked features to in silico lipid precursor and fragment libraries in LipidMatch. The data are low-resolution MS/MS spectra where ppm-level fragment matching is not meaningful and library matching relies on nominal-mass or spectral-similarity approaches instead. You need to perform the matching itself rather than configure tolerances — e.g. running the full rule-based identification workflow is a separate skill; this skill only covers choosing the tolerance parameters. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Configure the m/z (Da), ppm, and retention-time tolerances that LipidMatch uses for MS1 precursor matching and MS/MS fragment matching when annotating lipid species from UHPLC-HRMS/MS feature tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Configure the m/z (Da), ppm, and retention-time tolerances that LipidMatch uses for MS1 precursor matching and MS/MS fragment matching when annotating lipid species from UHPLC-HRMS/MS feature tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are low-resolution MS/MS spectra where ppm-level fragment matching is not meaningful and library matching relies on nominal-mass or spectral-similarity approaches instead. You need to perform the matching itself rather than configure tolerances — e.g. running the full rule-based identification workflow is a separate skill; this skill only covers choosing the tolerance parameters.

skills.description: Use when no experimentally acquired ground-truth high-resolution transients exist to benchmark reconstruction, and you need simulated MSI data with known peak centroids, adduct identities, and tissue-region assignments to quantify SNR gain and correlation fidelity.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-transient-signal-simulation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-transient-signal-simulation Use when no experimentally acquired ground-truth high-resolution transients exist to benchmark reconstruction, and you need simulated MSI data with known peak centroids, adduct identities, and tissue-region assignments to quantify SNR gain and correlation fidelity. When experimentally acquired high-resolution FT-ICR transients (e.g. the 1M-point full raw data from MassIVE) already exist as ground truth for benchmarking — use MEISTER_eval.ipynb on real data instead. When the goal is integrative tissue–single-cell analysis or 3D registration of real MSI sections, not reconstruction validation on synthetic data. When the study requires molecules beyond lipids/peptides with no defined adduct and isotope behavior, or non-brain tissue whose spatial annotations cannot be mapped to ABA-derived pseudo-regions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Generate a biochemically realistic simulated mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) dataset — building time-domain transients from a generic signal model with adducted isotopic distributions and pseudo-tissue spatial regions — so that deep-learning reconstruction can be validated against ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Generate a biochemically realistic simulated mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) dataset — building time-domain transients from a generic signal model with adducted isotopic distributions and pseudo-tissue spatial regions — so that deep-learning reconstruction can be validated against ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimentally acquired high-resolution FT-ICR transients (e.g. the 1M-point full raw data from MassIVE) already exist as ground truth for benchmarking — use MEISTER_eval.ipynb on real data instead. When the goal is integrative tissue–single-cell analysis or 3D registration of real MSI sections, not reconstruction validation on synthetic data. When the study requires molecules beyond lipids/peptides with no defined adduct and isotope behavior, or non-brain tissue whose spatial annotations cannot be mapped to ABA-derived pseudo-regions.

skills.description: Use when raw vendor MS files (e.g. SCIEX TripleTOF, Thermo Q-Exactive, Agilent) must be converted to an open format such as Aird, mzML, mgf, or mz5 before DDA or DIA/SWATH analysis, or when comparing file sizes across formats.
skills.name: mass-spectrometry-vendor-file-conversion
skills.search_text: mass-spectrometry-vendor-file-conversion Use when raw vendor MS files (e.g. SCIEX TripleTOF, Thermo Q-Exactive, Agilent) must be converted to an open format such as Aird, mzML, mgf, or mz5 before DDA or DIA/SWATH analysis, or when comparing file sizes across formats. The input is already an open format such as mzML, mzXML, mgf, or mz5 — conversion is unnecessary and may lose vendor metadata. Acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility that the current Aird version does not yet support (under development); convert to mzML instead. The analysis requires PSI-MS standard compliance or lossless vendor fidelity — Aird uses controllable (lossy) precision on the m/z dimension, so MSNumpress or mzML is more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Convert raw vendor mass spectrometry files (SCIEX WIFF, Thermo, Agilent) into open, analysis-ready formats — Aird via AirdPro and mzML/mgf/mz5 via MSConvert — for cross-platform compatibility, storage-efficiency comparison, and downstream computational workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Convert raw vendor mass spectrometry files (SCIEX WIFF, Thermo, Agilent) into open, analysis-ready formats — Aird via AirdPro and mzML/mgf/mz5 via MSConvert — for cross-platform compatibility, storage-efficiency comparison, and downstream computational workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an open format such as mzML, mzXML, mgf, or mz5 — conversion is unnecessary and may lose vendor metadata. Acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility that the current Aird version does not yet support (under development); convert to mzML instead. The analysis requires PSI-MS standard compliance or lossless vendor fidelity — Aird uses controllable (lossy) precision on the m/z dimension, so MSNumpress or mzML is more appropriate.

skills.description: Use when you have a tandem mass spectrum plus an inferred molecular formula and need candidate molecular structures ranked by top-k accuracy, MCES distance, or Tanimoto similarity against a ground-truth molecule.
skills.name: mass-spectrum-conditional-molecule-generation
skills.search_text: mass-spectrum-conditional-molecule-generation Use when you have a tandem mass spectrum plus an inferred molecular formula and need candidate molecular structures ranked by top-k accuracy, MCES distance, or Tanimoto similarity against a ground-truth molecule. You only need candidate molecular formulas rather than full structures — formula-restricted tools like SIRIUS, BUDDY, or MIST-CF address that upstream step The target structures exist in standard virtual chemical libraries (PubChem, Human Metabolome Database) where library lookup suffices You lack a reliably inferred molecular formula, since DiffMS is formula-restricted (heavy-atom-constrained) and takes the formula as given http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Formula-restricted de novo generation of molecular structures from tandem mass spectra using DiffMS, a permutation-invariant discrete graph-diffusion encoder-decoder that generates molecules as graphs (atoms, charges, and a 5-way bond-type adjacency matrix) conditioned on the spectrum and a chemical formula. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Formula-restricted de novo generation of molecular structures from tandem mass spectra using DiffMS, a permutation-invariant discrete graph-diffusion encoder-decoder that generates molecules as graphs (atoms, charges, and a 5-way bond-type adjacency matrix) conditioned on the spectrum and a chemical formula.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need candidate molecular formulas rather than full structures — formula-restricted tools like SIRIUS, BUDDY, or MIST-CF address that upstream step The target structures exist in standard virtual chemical libraries (PubChem, Human Metabolome Database) where library lookup suffices You lack a reliably inferred molecular formula, since DiffMS is formula-restricted (heavy-atom-constrained) and takes the formula as given

skills.description: Use when you need to determine which component of a spectrum-matching pipeline (embedding representation vs. approximate nearest-neighbor index) drives recall@k accuracy versus query throughput, as verifiable by testing hybrid configurations on measured spectra.
skills.name: mass-spectrum-matching-speed-profiling
skills.search_text: mass-spectrum-matching-speed-profiling Use when you need to determine which component of a spectrum-matching pipeline (embedding representation vs. approximate nearest-neighbor index) drives recall@k accuracy versus query throughput, as verifiable by testing hybrid configurations on measured spectra. You only need end-to-end FastEI identification accuracy on new compounds beyond NIST 2017 (e.g. the 10-molecule extra test set) rather than component attribution Your library is small enough that exact nearest-neighbor search is affordable — the HNSW speed dimension of the ablation is then irrelevant Your spectra are not electron-ionization spectra compatible with the Word2vec spectral embedding trained on 2,123,695 predicted spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ablation-profiling skill for EI mass spectrum matching: it runs the hybrid configurations EC (Word2vec embeddings + cosine similarity) and BH (weighted binning + HNSW) against the full FastEI pipeline and the WCS baseline to attribute FastEI's accuracy gains to embeddings and its speed gains to the HNSW graph index. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Ablation-profiling skill for EI mass spectrum matching: it runs the hybrid configurations EC (Word2vec embeddings + cosine similarity) and BH (weighted binning + HNSW) against the full FastEI pipeline and the WCS baseline to attribute FastEI's accuracy gains to embeddings and its speed gains to the HNSW graph index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need end-to-end FastEI identification accuracy on new compounds beyond NIST 2017 (e.g. the 10-molecule extra test set) rather than component attribution Your library is small enough that exact nearest-neighbor search is affordable — the HNSW speed dimension of the ablation is then irrelevant Your spectra are not electron-ionization spectra compatible with the Word2vec spectral embedding trained on 2,123,695 predicted spectra

skills.description: Use when a matrix-only template peak list has been subtracted from an MSI peak list (e.g. via mass2adduct subtractPeaks) and you must verify the resulting cleaned peak count matches the expected removal before downstream adduct identification.
skills.name: mass-spectrum-peak-count-verification
skills.search_text: mass-spectrum-peak-count-verification Use when a matrix-only template peak list has been subtracted from an MSI peak list (e.g. via mass2adduct subtractPeaks) and you must verify the resulting cleaned peak count matches the expected removal before downstream adduct identification. When the goal is adduct identification or co-localization testing rather than verifying the peak count after subtraction — use massdiff()/adductMatch()/corrPairsMSI() for those steps. When the input is an already-cleaned or feature-reduced peak table whose count is known a priori — re-running subtractPeaks just to re-verify counts is redundant. When the mass accuracy of the data does not support a 5 ppm matching tolerance (e.g. lower-resolution instruments) — bin-width/ppm choices must be adjusted and the expected removal count recalculated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Quantitative verification of the peak counts remaining after subtracting matrix-only template peaks from a MALDI-MSI peak list, confirming that the mass2adduct subtractPeaks() step removed the expected number of matrix cluster ions within a defined ppm tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: Quantitative verification of the peak counts remaining after subtracting matrix-only template peaks from a MALDI-MSI peak list, confirming that the mass2adduct subtractPeaks() step removed the expected number of matrix cluster ions within a defined ppm tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is adduct identification or co-localization testing rather than verifying the peak count after subtraction — use massdiff()/adductMatch()/corrPairsMSI() for those steps. When the input is an already-cleaned or feature-reduced peak table whose count is known a priori — re-running subtractPeaks just to re-verify counts is redundant. When the mass accuracy of the data does not support a 5 ppm matching tolerance (e.g. lower-resolution instruments) — bin-width/ppm choices must be adjusted and the expected removal count recalculated.

skills.name: mass-tolerance-based-peak-matching
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-based-peak-matching Use when ranking candidate molecular formulas for LC-MS/MS spectra by matching fragment peak masses against formula-derived masses under dataset-specific tolerances, as in the FSA pipeline across eight test datasets (HMDB_QTOF, HMDB_ITFT, HMDB_QFT, NPL_MAXIS, NPL_QTOF, NPL_OT, LIPIDS_OT, CASMI_OT). When structural information is needed to disambiguate isomeric formulas — the article notes FSA 'has not utilized structural information yet and therefore its accuracy may not be competitive with some of the state-of-the-art identification tools' When compounds contain elements beyond C, H, O, N, S, and P, since 'FSA has so far been validated on datasets containing compounds composed of C, H, O, N, S, and P' When peak-formula assignment depends on species/adduct-specific chemical rules that are not yet implemented in FSA http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Matches observed LC-MS/MS fragment peak m/z values to candidate chemical formulas by applying dataset-specific mass matching tolerances within the FSA (formula subset analysis) workflow, using only the top-30 most abundant fragments per spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-025-02379-0
skills.summary: Matches observed LC-MS/MS fragment peak m/z values to candidate chemical formulas by applying dataset-specific mass matching tolerances within the FSA (formula subset analysis) workflow, using only the top-30 most abundant fragments per spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When structural information is needed to disambiguate isomeric formulas — the article notes FSA 'has not utilized structural information yet and therefore its accuracy may not be competitive with some of the state-of-the-art identification tools' When compounds contain elements beyond C, H, O, N, S, and P, since 'FSA has so far been validated on datasets containing compounds composed of C, H, O, N, S, and P' When peak-formula assignment depends on species/adduct-specific chemical rules that are not yet implemented in FSA

skills.description: Use when assigning identities to LC-MS peaks by m/z matching against HMDB or MassBank, and you must choose a mass tolerance window; triggers on estimated m/z lists from targeted/untargeted peak analysis.
skills.name: mass-tolerance-configuration
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-configuration Use when assigning identities to LC-MS peaks by m/z matching against HMDB or MassBank, and you must choose a mass tolerance window; triggers on estimated m/z lists from targeted/untargeted peak analysis. The compound has no record in the target database — HMDB does not include heroin and nimetazepam, so those narcotics cannot be identified regardless of tolerance Direct one-to-one identification without prior drug information is required — other metabolites may share identical m/z values, so m/z matching alone cannot uniquely assign identity The goal is structural confirmation of an unknown peak — MS/MS, NMR, or standard comparison is needed instead of tolerance-based m/z matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Configures the ppm mass tolerance used by SMART 2.0's peak identification module when matching estimated m/z values against metabolite databases (HMDB, MassBank), using 2 ppm as the primary threshold and 3 ppm to capture additional matches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: Configures the ppm mass tolerance used by SMART 2.0's peak identification module when matching estimated m/z values against metabolite databases (HMDB, MassBank), using 2 ppm as the primary threshold and 3 ppm to capture additional matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound has no record in the target database — HMDB does not include heroin and nimetazepam, so those narcotics cannot be identified regardless of tolerance Direct one-to-one identification without prior drug information is required — other metabolites may share identical m/z values, so m/z matching alone cannot uniquely assign identity The goal is structural confirmation of an unknown peak — MS/MS, NMR, or standard comparison is needed instead of tolerance-based m/z matching

skills.description: Reference for setting the mzdiff mass tolerance in XCMS CentWave when features with similar m/z and retention times need dereplication, or when dereplication should be disabled.
skills.name: mass-tolerance-dereplication-configuration
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-dereplication-configuration Reference for setting the mzdiff mass tolerance in XCMS CentWave when features with similar m/z and retention times need dereplication, or when dereplication should be disabled. When the analysis does not use XCMS CentWave feature extraction, since mzdiff is specific to that program's dereplication step. When the goal is tuning peak height or other universal parameters (e.g., peak width, instrumental shift) rather than mass-tolerance dereplication. When a different dereplication strategy (not based on m/z/retention-time similarity within a mass tolerance) is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Configure the XCMS CentWave mzdiff mass-tolerance parameter that dereplicates features with similar m/z and retention times, choosing 0.001–0.01 as suggested defaults or a negative value to disable dereplication entirely. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c04758
skills.summary: Configure the XCMS CentWave mzdiff mass-tolerance parameter that dereplicates features with similar m/z and retention times, choosing 0.001–0.01 as suggested defaults or a negative value to disable dereplication entirely.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis does not use XCMS CentWave feature extraction, since mzdiff is specific to that program's dereplication step. When the goal is tuning peak height or other universal parameters (e.g., peak width, instrumental shift) rather than mass-tolerance dereplication. When a different dereplication strategy (not based on m/z/retention-time similarity within a mass tolerance) is required.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data must be processed for feature extraction and the software-specific mass tolerance (e.g., mzdiff in XCMS CentWave) needs to be measured from the data itself.
skills.name: mass-tolerance-estimation
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-estimation Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data must be processed for feature extraction and the software-specific mass tolerance (e.g., mzdiff in XCMS CentWave) needs to be measured from the data itself. The data has already been processed into a feature table — Paramounter must measure parameters from raw LC-MS data prior to feature extraction. The user wants to disable dereplication: in that case mzdiff should simply be set to any negative value rather than tuned. A retention-time/index-dependent alignment task that is not about mass-based dereplication tolerance is the actual goal. This skill measures the mass tolerance universal parameter (used for feature dereplication in LC-MS metabolomics feature extraction) automatically from raw LC-MS data, using Paramounter's rank-based intensity sorting and zone of interest concepts rather than user-supplied defaults. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c04758
skills.summary: This skill measures the mass tolerance universal parameter (used for feature dereplication in LC-MS metabolomics feature extraction) automatically from raw LC-MS data, using Paramounter's rank-based intensity sorting and zone of interest concepts rather than user-supplied defaults.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data has already been processed into a feature table — Paramounter must measure parameters from raw LC-MS data prior to feature extraction. The user wants to disable dereplication: in that case mzdiff should simply be set to any negative value rather than tuned. A retention-time/index-dependent alignment task that is not about mass-based dereplication tolerance is the actual goal.

skills.description: Use when performing library matching against an augmented spectral library where the query molecule's molecular mass is known with some accuracy, and the full library search is too large or introduces false candidates outside the plausible mass window.
skills.name: mass-tolerance-library-filtering
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-library-filtering Use when performing library matching against an augmented spectral library where the query molecule's molecular mass is known with some accuracy, and the full library search is too large or introduces false candidates outside the plausible mass window. When the molecular mass of the query sample cannot be determined with a few-Dalton accuracy — the filter depends on knowing the mass and would incorrectly exclude the true candidate When evaluating predictors or similarity metrics on a fully unfiltered search where mass information is deliberately held out, since filtering confounds the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Restrict the NEIMS library-matching candidate set to spectra whose molecular mass falls within a 5 Da tolerance of the query molecule's mass before computing weighted cosine similarity, shrinking the search space to a median of 6696 spectra per query and improving recall@10. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00085
skills.summary: Restrict the NEIMS library-matching candidate set to spectra whose molecular mass falls within a 5 Da tolerance of the query molecule's mass before computing weighted cosine similarity, shrinking the search space to a median of 6696 spectra per query and improving recall@10.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the molecular mass of the query sample cannot be determined with a few-Dalton accuracy — the filter depends on knowing the mass and would incorrectly exclude the true candidate When evaluating predictors or similarity metrics on a fully unfiltered search where mass information is deliberately held out, since filtering confounds the comparison

skills.description: Use when candidate-structure annotation leaves high-quality MS/MS peaks unexplained and you must decide whether the failure stems from a missing candidate structure or from too-restrictive mass tolerance settings.
skills.name: mass-tolerance-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-parameter-tuning Use when candidate-structure annotation leaves high-quality MS/MS peaks unexplained and you must decide whether the failure stems from a missing candidate structure or from too-restrictive mass tolerance settings. The correct candidate was verified absent from the initial PubChem candidate set — raising the mass tolerance cannot recover a missing structure Peaks remain unexplained even with relaxed tolerance because the default in silico fragmentation depth (up to 3 bond dissociations) is insufficient, as in challenge 16 where higher-energy peaks like m/z 122.0408 and 221.07309 stayed unmatched http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 A diagnostic-and-replay procedure for MAGMa candidate ranking: when MS/MS peaks remain unexplained, test whether the assumed mass deviation (default 10 ppm with an absolute minimum of 0.002 Da) was too restrictive rather than assuming the correct structure was absent from the candidate list, by reprocessing with a raised minimum mass tolerance (0.005 Da). metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033
skills.summary: A diagnostic-and-replay procedure for MAGMa candidate ranking: when MS/MS peaks remain unexplained, test whether the assumed mass deviation (default 10 ppm with an absolute minimum of 0.002 Da) was too restrictive rather than assuming the correct structure was absent from the candidate list, by reprocessing with a raised minimum mass tolerance (0.005 Da).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The correct candidate was verified absent from the initial PubChem candidate set — raising the mass tolerance cannot recover a missing structure Peaks remain unexplained even with relaxed tolerance because the default in silico fragmentation depth (up to 3 bond dissociations) is insufficient, as in challenge 16 where higher-energy peaks like m/z 122.0408 and 221.07309 stayed unmatched

skills.description: Use when constraining a Pickaxe network expansion to an unannotated metabolomics peak list and you must choose the adduct list and user-defined mass tolerance that decide which predicted compounds are retained.
skills.name: mass-tolerance-parameterization
skills.search_text: mass-tolerance-parameterization Use when constraining a Pickaxe network expansion to an unannotated metabolomics peak list and you must choose the adduct list and user-defined mass tolerance that decide which predicted compounds are retained. When the goal is annotating peaks with known database compounds rather than constraining a novel reaction network — the metabolomics filter only retains predicted compounds, it does not assign identities to peaks When no experimental peak list or adduct list is available; the filter cannot operate without user-supplied peaks, adducts, and a tolerance When filtering on other criteria such as chemical similarity to targets, thermodynamics, or reaction feasibility — Pickaxe provides separate filters for those http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parameterizes the Pickaxe metabolomics filter: for each predicted compound, adducted m/z values are computed from a user-supplied adduct list and matched against experimental unannotated peaks within a user-defined mass tolerance, so only compounds consistent with observed peaks survive network expansion. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05149-8
skills.summary: Parameterizes the Pickaxe metabolomics filter: for each predicted compound, adducted m/z values are computed from a user-supplied adduct list and matched against experimental unannotated peaks within a user-defined mass tolerance, so only compounds consistent with observed peaks survive network expansion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotating peaks with known database compounds rather than constraining a novel reaction network — the metabolomics filter only retains predicted compounds, it does not assign identities to peaks When no experimental peak list or adduct list is available; the filter cannot operate without user-supplied peaks, adducts, and a tolerance When filtering on other criteria such as chemical similarity to targets, thermodynamics, or reaction feasibility — Pickaxe provides separate filters for those

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics measurements (e.g. mzML) must be converted into feature-level intensities, especially when isotope-pattern-aware feature detection is needed before linking, alignment, or statistical analysis.
skills.name: mass-trace-feature-detection
skills.search_text: mass-trace-feature-detection Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics measurements (e.g. mzML) must be converted into feature-level intensities, especially when isotope-pattern-aware feature detection is needed before linking, alignment, or statistical analysis. Input is already a feature table or peak-picked feature list — the skill operates on raw LC-MS mass traces, not on existing quantification matrices. The analytes are intact proteins or another class outside the small-molecule scope (though the algorithm also applies to lipidomics and peptidomics, it is not built for large biomolecule deconvolution). Data are not chromatography-based (e.g. direct-infusion MS without co-elution information), since feature assembly relies on co-eluting mass traces. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Detects mass traces in LC-MS metabolomics data and assembles them into isotope-resolved features using OpenMS FeatureFinderMetabo, the basis for reliable label-free quantification. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278
skills.summary: Detects mass traces in LC-MS metabolomics data and assembles them into isotope-resolved features using OpenMS FeatureFinderMetabo, the basis for reliable label-free quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or peak-picked feature list — the skill operates on raw LC-MS mass traces, not on existing quantification matrices. The analytes are intact proteins or another class outside the small-molecule scope (though the algorithm also applies to lipidomics and peptidomics, it is not built for large biomolecule deconvolution). Data are not chromatography-based (e.g. direct-infusion MS without co-elution information), since feature assembly relies on co-eluting mass traces.

skills.description: Use when peak lists (e.g. DIMS MTBLS79 or LC-MS MTBLS146 subsets) have already been formula-assigned by Empirical Formulae Search and you must link those accurate-mass formulae to putative metabolites in compound reference databases.
skills.name: mass-transformation-mapping
skills.search_text: mass-transformation-mapping Use when peak lists (e.g. DIMS MTBLS79 or LC-MS MTBLS146 subsets) have already been formula-assigned by Empirical Formulae Search and you must link those accurate-mass formulae to putative metabolites in compound reference databases. When the peak list has not yet been processed by Empirical Formulae Search — Transformation Mapping searches empirically assigned formulae, not raw masses When no compound reference database (KEGG, HMDB, LIPID MAPS) is installed, since the search depends on these resources When the goal is raw-data processing (peak picking, alignment, filtering) rather than metabolite annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Applies MI-Pack Transformation Mapping within the Galaxy-M annotation stage to search empirically assigned elemental formulae against compound reference databases (e.g. KEGG, HMDB, LIPID MAPS), producing an SQLite annotation database that is consolidated via Combine Outputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: Applies MI-Pack Transformation Mapping within the Galaxy-M annotation stage to search empirically assigned elemental formulae against compound reference databases (e.g. KEGG, HMDB, LIPID MAPS), producing an SQLite annotation database that is consolidated via Combine Outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the peak list has not yet been processed by Empirical Formulae Search — Transformation Mapping searches empirically assigned formulae, not raw masses When no compound reference database (KEGG, HMDB, LIPID MAPS) is installed, since the search depends on these resources When the goal is raw-data processing (peak picking, alignment, filtering) rather than metabolite annotation

skills.description: Use when a large enumerated derivative database (hundreds of millions of candidates) must be pruned to plausible candidates before similarity scoring, and a reference M+ mass from a GC/EI-MS analyte spectrum is available.
skills.name: mass-weight-tolerance-filtering
skills.search_text: mass-weight-tolerance-filtering Use when a large enumerated derivative database (hundreds of millions of candidates) must be pruned to plausible candidates before similarity scoring, and a reference M+ mass from a GC/EI-MS analyte spectrum is available. The analyte's spectrum already matches an established reference spectrum (NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG) — the conventional screening path should be used instead of enumerating and mass-filtering derivatives No reliable M+ peak can be identified in the analyte spectrum, since the entire filter is anchored to that reference mass You need isomer-level discrimination — mass tolerance filtering only removes grossly different molecular masses and cannot separate isobaric candidates; use integrated spectrum/fingerprint similarity for that http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Rule-based filtering step from PS2MS that narrows an enumerated synthetic NPS database by retaining only derivatives whose molecular mass falls within a tolerance window (e.g., ±1 Da or ±5 Da) of the analyte's M+ peak reference mass. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Rule-based filtering step from PS2MS that narrows an enumerated synthetic NPS database by retaining only derivatives whose molecular mass falls within a tolerance window (e.g., ±1 Da or ±5 Da) of the analyte's M+ peak reference mass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte's spectrum already matches an established reference spectrum (NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG) — the conventional screening path should be used instead of enumerating and mass-filtering derivatives No reliable M+ peak can be identified in the analyte spectrum, since the entire filter is anchored to that reference mass You need isomer-level discrimination — mass tolerance filtering only removes grossly different molecular masses and cannot separate isobaric candidates; use integrated spectrum/fingerprint similarity for that

skills.description: Use when building annotation candidate lists at multiple parent-mass windows (down to 0 ppm isobaric) to test whether CCS filtering of false positives remains stable as mass discrimination is tightened.
skills.name: mass-window-candidate-list-generation
skills.search_text: mass-window-candidate-list-generation Use when building annotation candidate lists at multiple parent-mass windows (down to 0 ppm isobaric) to test whether CCS filtering of false positives remains stable as mass discrimination is tightened. You only need a single broad mass tolerance for one-shot annotation filtering rather than a comparison across windows — a single 10 ppm ΔCCS threshold filter (2.8%) suffices Your candidates involve dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments, which the CCSP training sets do not support The training set needed for the CCS prediction cannot be defined prior to prediction (CCSP requires a specific training set to be chosen upfront) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates metabolite annotation candidate lists at successively narrower parent-mass tolerances (10, 7, 5, 3, 1, and 0 ppm isobaric) from PubChem/Entrez, then pairs each candidate with CCSP-predicted CCS values so that CCS-based filtering efficacy can be evaluated as a function of mass-window width. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2022.08.09.503345
skills.summary: Generates metabolite annotation candidate lists at successively narrower parent-mass tolerances (10, 7, 5, 3, 1, and 0 ppm isobaric) from PubChem/Entrez, then pairs each candidate with CCSP-predicted CCS values so that CCS-based filtering efficacy can be evaluated as a function of mass-window width.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single broad mass tolerance for one-shot annotation filtering rather than a comparison across windows — a single 10 ppm ΔCCS threshold filter (2.8%) suffices Your candidates involve dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments, which the CCSP training sets do not support The training set needed for the CCS prediction cannot be defined prior to prediction (CCSP requires a specific training set to be chosen upfront)

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed MS2 spectra (~1,000 MS peaks per sample, positive and negative ionization mode) from complex mixtures and want unsupervised discovery of conserved fragmentation substructures for de novo annotation.
skills.name: mass2motif-fragmentation-pattern-extraction
skills.search_text: mass2motif-fragmentation-pattern-extraction Use when you have preprocessed MS2 spectra (~1,000 MS peaks per sample, positive and negative ionization mode) from complex mixtures and want unsupervised discovery of conserved fragmentation substructures for de novo annotation. The MS2 spectra are information-poor (e.g., not acquired with ramped or stepped collision energy) — MS2LDA works best for complex mixtures where a large number of metabolites are fragmented The goal is targeted annotation against reference libraries rather than unsupervised motif discovery (use spectral matching to Mass Bank/NIST/GNPS instead) Only a small spectral dataset is available where per-motif degree would rarely reach the >= 10 retention threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Applies latent Dirichlet allocation topic modeling (MS2LDA) to MS2 fragmentation spectra to discover recurring substructures (Mass2Motifs) as sets of co-occurring fragments and neutral losses, and decomposes each spectrum into these motifs without training data. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Applies latent Dirichlet allocation topic modeling (MS2LDA) to MS2 fragmentation spectra to discover recurring substructures (Mass2Motifs) as sets of co-occurring fragments and neutral losses, and decomposes each spectrum into these motifs without training data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MS2 spectra are information-poor (e.g., not acquired with ramped or stepped collision energy) — MS2LDA works best for complex mixtures where a large number of metabolites are fragmented The goal is targeted annotation against reference libraries rather than unsupervised motif discovery (use spectral matching to Mass Bank/NIST/GNPS instead) Only a small spectral dataset is available where per-motif degree would rarely reach the >= 10 retention threshold

skills.description: Use when you have decomposition output (motifset.json / ms2lda_viz.gz) from MS2LDA or the GNPS–MS2LDA repository, MS/MS spectra from complex mixtures, and you want motif-based annotation instead of library matching.
skills.name: mass2motif-membership-annotation
skills.search_text: mass2motif-membership-annotation Use when you have decomposition output (motifset.json / ms2lda_viz.gz) from MS2LDA or the GNPS–MS2LDA repository, MS/MS spectra from complex mixtures, and you want motif-based annotation instead of library matching. The input is already a fully annotated feature table and you only need to re-quantify peaks — motif discovery is redundant. Spectra come from DDA data where MS1-to-MS2 matching is unreliable, because motif decomposition depends on reliable MS1–MS2 peak matching. You need to compare conditions across samples with PLAGE or differential-expression analyses; this skill covers annotation only, not motif-level differential expression. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotate metabolite MS/MS spectra by their membership in Mass2Motifs — recurring fragment/neutral-loss substructures learned by LDA — rather than by whole-spectrum library matching, yielding up to three-fold more annotations in complex mixtures like beer extracts. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Annotate metabolite MS/MS spectra by their membership in Mass2Motifs — recurring fragment/neutral-loss substructures learned by LDA — rather than by whole-spectrum library matching, yielding up to three-fold more annotations in complex mixtures like beer extracts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a fully annotated feature table and you only need to re-quantify peaks — motif discovery is redundant. Spectra come from DDA data where MS1-to-MS2 matching is unreliable, because motif decomposition depends on reliable MS1–MS2 peak matching. You need to compare conditions across samples with PLAGE or differential-expression analyses; this skill covers annotation only, not motif-level differential expression.

skills.description: Use when filtering MS2LDA decomposition output where each spectrum–Mass2Motif link carries a probability and you must decide which memberships count as validated substructure annotations, e.g. before cross-library validation against GNPS or Mass Bank spectra.
skills.name: mass2motif-probability-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: mass2motif-probability-threshold-filtering Use when filtering MS2LDA decomposition output where each spectrum–Mass2Motif link carries a probability and you must decide which memberships count as validated substructure annotations, e.g. before cross-library validation against GNPS or Mass Bank spectra. Input is already a curated motif-annotation table where probabilities are no longer available The task is de novo motif discovery rather than filtering existing memberships Working with data-independent acquisition fragments that lack reliable MS1-to-MS2 matching, since Mass2Motif membership depends on that linkage http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applying the MS2LDA paper's probability threshold of 0.1 to decide which substructure annotations (Mass2Motif-to-spectrum memberships) are accepted as validated, enabling benchmarking against GNPS and Mass Bank reference spectra and selective retention of motif links. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Applying the MS2LDA paper's probability threshold of 0.1 to decide which substructure annotations (Mass2Motif-to-spectrum memberships) are accepted as validated, enabling benchmarking against GNPS and Mass Bank reference spectra and selective retention of motif links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated motif-annotation table where probabilities are no longer available The task is de novo motif discovery rather than filtering existing memberships Working with data-independent acquisition fragments that lack reliable MS1-to-MS2 matching, since Mass2Motif membership depends on that linkage

skills.description: Use when MS2LDA inference has produced Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra (fragment and neutral-loss masses with probabilities) that need automated putative substructure annotations, e.g. to label discovered motifs across beer, urine, or GNPS spectra without manual curation.
skills.name: mass2motif-spectral-matching-annotation
skills.search_text: mass2motif-spectral-matching-annotation Use when MS2LDA inference has produced Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra (fragment and neutral-loss masses with probabilities) that need automated putative substructure annotations, e.g. to label discovered motifs across beer, urine, or GNPS spectra without manual curation. The input is raw MS1/MS2 centroid data that has not yet been decomposed by MS2LDA into Mass2Motifs — run LDA inference first. Neutral-loss information is essential to the annotation and cannot be dropped, since spectral matching tools 'do not currently support' losses and they must be omitted. The mixture is simple or MS2 spectra are information-poor (no ramped/stepped collision energy), where MS2LDA motifs themselves are unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Automatically annotates MS2LDA-discovered Mass2Motifs by representing each motif as a pseudo-spectrum and subjecting it to spectral (substructure) matching, validating fragment-based substructure labels such as acetylations, nitro groups, and sugar fragments. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Automatically annotates MS2LDA-discovered Mass2Motifs by representing each motif as a pseudo-spectrum and subjecting it to spectral (substructure) matching, validating fragment-based substructure labels such as acetylations, nitro groups, and sugar fragments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw MS1/MS2 centroid data that has not yet been decomposed by MS2LDA into Mass2Motifs — run LDA inference first. Neutral-loss information is essential to the annotation and cannot be dropped, since spectral matching tools 'do not currently support' losses and they must be omitted. The mixture is simple or MS2 spectra are information-poor (no ramped/stepped collision energy), where MS2LDA motifs themselves are unreliable.

skills.description: Use when a strain collection has both genome-mined BGCs (antiSMASH) and MS/MS-derived Mass2Motifs per strain, and you need to test which sub-clusters chemically explain which molecular substructures.
skills.name: mass2motif-substructure-linking
skills.search_text: mass2motif-substructure-linking Use when a strain collection has both genome-mined BGCs (antiSMASH) and MS/MS-derived Mass2Motifs per strain, and you need to test which sub-clusters chemically explain which molecular substructures. When you only have MS/MS data (Mass2Motifs) without corresponding genome sequences / BGC annotations — no sub-clusters exist to correlate against. When the goal is de novo BGC detection rather than linking already-mined sub-clusters to molecular substructures; use iPRESTO sub-cluster prediction itself instead. When strains are few or highly redundant such that permutation testing cannot meaningfully control for related-strain co-occurrence inflation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3855 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Correlates MS/MS-derived Mass2Motif substructure patterns with iPRESTO-predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters (sub-cluster motifs and SCCs) across a paired genome-metabolome strain collection, using a Dorogui-style co-occurrence correlation score plus permutation testing to identify significant metabologenomic links. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Correlates MS/MS-derived Mass2Motif substructure patterns with iPRESTO-predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters (sub-cluster motifs and SCCs) across a paired genome-metabolome strain collection, using a Dorogui-style co-occurrence correlation score plus permutation testing to identify significant metabologenomic links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only have MS/MS data (Mass2Motifs) without corresponding genome sequences / BGC annotations — no sub-clusters exist to correlate against. When the goal is de novo BGC detection rather than linking already-mined sub-clusters to molecular substructures; use iPRESTO sub-cluster prediction itself instead. When strains are few or highly redundant such that permutation testing cannot meaningfully control for related-strain co-occurrence inflation.

skills.description: Use when an aligned HRMS feature table (m/z + retention-time pairs) exists and features must be assigned candidate formulae and compound identities via MS/MS spectral matching against MassBank/MoNA.
skills.name: massbank-database-querying
skills.search_text: massbank-database-querying Use when an aligned HRMS feature table (m/z + retention-time pairs) exists and features must be assigned candidate formulae and compound identities via MS/MS spectral matching against MassBank/MoNA. Input is still raw .mzML data that has not been peak-picked and aligned (run mssmain.peak_pick and alignment first) Features correspond to compounds above 500 Da, where MSS formula prediction is not supported The goal is feature clustering, dilution prediction, or source tracking — use the dm.ms_cluster / feature_model analysis module instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates HRMS features from the MSS pipeline by querying the MassBank of North America (MoNA endpoint) with individual or averaged MS/MS spectra, complemented by ChemCalc formula prediction and dot-product isotopic scoring, to produce a fully annotated feature table. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00741-9

skills.search_text: massspec-candidate-ranking Use when you have MS/MS spectra plus a candidate molecule list (by mass or formula) and need a ranked list of structures per spectrum, or when reproducing MVP's MassSpecGym rank@1 benchmark. skills.description: Use when you have relative-abundance time-course metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec) for a metabolic network and need to infer response factors / absolute concentrations without chemical standards via the kinetic equation (KE) approach.
skills.name: matlab-nonlinear-least-squares-scripting
skills.search_text: matlab-nonlinear-least-squares-scripting Use when you have relative-abundance time-course metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec) for a metabolic network and need to infer response factors / absolute concentrations without chemical standards via the kinetic equation (KE) approach. Data are not intracellular, single-compartment metabolomics samples from a directly connected metabolic network (MetaboPAC assumes all metabolites are connected via reactions and ignores inter-compartment transport in eukaryotes). High noise or substantial missingness (e.g. 10% values imputed) where mass balances are violated, since the optimizer's feasibility assessment depends on mass-balance consistency. Metabolites whose response factors are strongly nonlinear with concentration (ion suppression / limited linear dynamic range), since the optimization assumes constant response factors. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 MATLAB-based optimization scripting in MetaboPAC that solves for response factors (and thus absolute metabolite concentrations) from relative abundance time-course GC-MS data by minimizing penalties grounded in mass balances and known kinetic equations. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: MATLAB-based optimization scripting in MetaboPAC that solves for response factors (and thus absolute metabolite concentrations) from relative abundance time-course GC-MS data by minimizing penalties grounded in mass balances and known kinetic equations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not intracellular, single-compartment metabolomics samples from a directly connected metabolic network (MetaboPAC assumes all metabolites are connected via reactions and ignores inter-compartment transport in eukaryotes). High noise or substantial missingness (e.g. 10% values imputed) where mass balances are violated, since the optimizer's feasibility assessment depends on mass-balance consistency. Metabolites whose response factors are strongly nonlinear with concentration (ion suppression / limited linear dynamic range), since the optimization assumes constant response factors.
