skills.search_text: metabolic-network-visualization-export Use when metabolite association networks (biochemical, structural, spectral, or empirical edges) have been calculated and need interactive thresholding, node attribute mapping, or export to CSV/SVG/Cytoscape for interpretation. The metabolite table has not yet passed identifier translation (CTSgetR to KEGG/PubChem CIDs) or network calculation — there are no edges to visualize or export The analysis goal is pathway-enriched network mapping rather than pathway-independent metabolite association networks A pre-existing Cytoscape network only needs layout or styling, not re-export of MetaMapR edge lists or node-ID mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Interactive visualization and export of metabolomic networks generated by MetaMapR, covering edge-type hierarchy tuning, node-ID-to-uploaded-row mapping, and export of edge-list/node-attribute CSVs, SVG graphics, and Cytoscape-ready tables for downstream network analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Interactive visualization and export of metabolomic networks generated by MetaMapR, covering edge-type hierarchy tuning, node-ID-to-uploaded-row mapping, and export of edge-list/node-attribute CSVs, SVG graphics, and Cytoscape-ready tables for downstream network analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolite table has not yet passed identifier translation (CTSgetR to KEGG/PubChem CIDs) or network calculation — there are no edges to visualize or export The analysis goal is pathway-enriched network mapping rather than pathway-independent metabolite association networks A pre-existing Cytoscape network only needs layout or styling, not re-export of MetaMapR edge lists or node-ID mapping

skills.description: Use when you have an unfiltered KO/gene/compound abundance table plus sample metadata (categorical groups, multiple time points, or a continuous variable) and need pathway-level enrichment with high sensitivity.
skills.name: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when you have an unfiltered KO/gene/compound abundance table plus sample metadata (categorical groups, multiple time points, or a continuous variable) and need pathway-level enrichment with high sensitivity. When the abundance table has been prefiltered to significant features only — GRSA is threshold-free and relies on background information, so prefiltering invalidates the reporter score aggregation When you need a strict-specificity enrichment ranking: GRSA showed slightly lower specificity than comparator methods in the mouse knockout benchmark, so results require additional experimental validation When feature IDs are not mappable to K numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers (e.g., unstandardized metabolite compound IDs) — the README requires converting compound IDs to C numbers http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Performs threshold-free Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) on KO or compound abundance tables using the R package ReporterScore, aggregating feature-level statistics into KEGG pathway/module reporter scores for differential, multi-group, longitudinal, or continuous-variable (e.g., gestational age) designs. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Performs threshold-free Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) on KO or compound abundance tables using the R package ReporterScore, aggregating feature-level statistics into KEGG pathway/module reporter scores for differential, multi-group, longitudinal, or continuous-variable (e.g., gestational age) designs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the abundance table has been prefiltered to significant features only — GRSA is threshold-free and relies on background information, so prefiltering invalidates the reporter score aggregation When you need a strict-specificity enrichment ranking: GRSA showed slightly lower specificity than comparator methods in the mouse knockout benchmark, so results require additional experimental validation When feature IDs are not mappable to K numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers (e.g., unstandardized metabolite compound IDs) — the README requires converting compound IDs to C numbers

skills.description: Use when a list of differentially abundant metabolites must be interpreted functionally via ORA against KEGG, Reactome, or BioCyc compound sets, and background-set/parameter choices must be controlled.
skills.name: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-testing Use when a list of differentially abundant metabolites must be interpreted functionally via ORA against KEGG, Reactome, or BioCyc compound sets, and background-set/parameter choices must be controlled. The goal is an extensive comparison of pathway databases — the authors state this is beyond the scope of the paper and refer readers to dedicated comparison studies The data are not MS-based untargeted metabolomics compound lists — the study's conclusions were validated only on five MS-based untargeted metabolomics datasets No assay-specific background set can be defined — a non-assay-specific background yields large numbers of false-positive pathways, so conclusions from such a run are unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Over-representation analysis (ORA) for metabolomics: tests whether differentially abundant metabolites are over-represented in KEGG, Reactome, or BioCyc pathway compound sets using a right-tailed Fisher's exact (hypergeometric) test, with protocol choices (assay-specific background, ≥3-compound pathways) that control false positives. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Over-representation analysis (ORA) for metabolomics: tests whether differentially abundant metabolites are over-represented in KEGG, Reactome, or BioCyc pathway compound sets using a right-tailed Fisher's exact (hypergeometric) test, with protocol choices (assay-specific background, ≥3-compound pathways) that control false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is an extensive comparison of pathway databases — the authors state this is beyond the scope of the paper and refer readers to dedicated comparison studies The data are not MS-based untargeted metabolomics compound lists — the study's conclusions were validated only on five MS-based untargeted metabolomics datasets No assay-specific background set can be defined — a non-assay-specific background yields large numbers of false-positive pathways, so conclusions from such a run are unreliable

skills.description: Use when a list of significant metabolites (e.g. Log2FC > 1.5, adj-p < 0.05) from HFD or other treatment comparisons needs mapping to KEGG pathways to identify which metabolic functions are over-represented.
skills.name: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-visualization
skills.search_text: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-visualization Use when a list of significant metabolites (e.g. Log2FC > 1.5, adj-p < 0.05) from HFD or other treatment comparisons needs mapping to KEGG pathways to identify which metabolic functions are over-represented. The input is raw uncorrected metabolite intensities rather than a differential (Log2FC/adj-p) metabolite list — MSEA will under-detect pathways as seen with the raw-data metabolite list. The metabolite identifiers cannot be mapped to HMDB or KEGG compound IDs, since enrichment is performed against the predefined KEGG pathways database. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotate a differentially regulated metabolite list from a batch-corrected LC–MS metabolomics dataset to functional pathways via metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) against KEGG pathways, reporting pathways meeting an at-least-2-metabolite and q-value < 0.05 significance threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Annotate a differentially regulated metabolite list from a batch-corrected LC–MS metabolomics dataset to functional pathways via metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) against KEGG pathways, reporting pathways meeting an at-least-2-metabolite and q-value < 0.05 significance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw uncorrected metabolite intensities rather than a differential (Log2FC/adj-p) metabolite list — MSEA will under-detect pathways as seen with the raw-data metabolite list. The metabolite identifiers cannot be mapped to HMDB or KEGG compound IDs, since enrichment is performed against the predefined KEGG pathways database.

skills.description: Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset is available and the goal is unsupervised, de novo reconstruction of a specialized metabolite biosynthetic pathway without prior knowledge of a 'bait' compound or enzyme.
skills.name: metabolic-pathway-hypothesis-reconstruction
skills.search_text: metabolic-pathway-hypothesis-reconstruction Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset is available and the goal is unsupervised, de novo reconstruction of a specialized metabolite biosynthetic pathway without prior knowledge of a 'bait' compound or enzyme. The input requires reasoning over stereoisomers: mass spectrometric data does not capture stereochemistry, and RetroRules rules involving stereomeric structures are filtered, so stereo-specific steps (e.g., phenylalanine to p-coumaroyl-CoA) will be missed. The target pathway contains multi-substrate reactions (e.g., tyrosine plus p-coumaroyl-CoA to p-coumaroyltyramine), since RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions only. A supervised or bait-based co-expression analysis is desired instead; this skill is specifically the unsupervised network/DAG-based reconstruction stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reconstructs biosynthetic pathway hypotheses from paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data by building a directed reaction network of mass signatures (including unmeasured 'ghost' intermediates), converting it into per-substrate directed acyclic graphs, and extracting the longest valid reaction path from each DAG. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Reconstructs biosynthetic pathway hypotheses from paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data by building a directed reaction network of mass signatures (including unmeasured 'ghost' intermediates), converting it into per-substrate directed acyclic graphs, and extracting the longest valid reaction path from each DAG.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input requires reasoning over stereoisomers: mass spectrometric data does not capture stereochemistry, and RetroRules rules involving stereomeric structures are filtered, so stereo-specific steps (e.g., phenylalanine to p-coumaroyl-CoA) will be missed. The target pathway contains multi-substrate reactions (e.g., tyrosine plus p-coumaroyl-CoA to p-coumaroyltyramine), since RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions only. A supervised or bait-based co-expression analysis is desired instead; this skill is specifically the unsupervised network/DAG-based reconstruction stage.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify and statistically validate how much of a reference set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions a computational reaction-rule predictor (e.g., MEANtools/RetroRules rules) can anticipate.
skills.name: metabolic-pathway-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: metabolic-pathway-prediction-evaluation Use when you need to quantify and statistically validate how much of a reference set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions a computational reaction-rule predictor (e.g., MEANtools/RetroRules rules) can anticipate. The goal is de novo pathway discovery from multi-omics data rather than benchmarking predictor coverage — use the MEANtools discovery workflow (MR correlation, ClusterONE feature clusters) instead The reaction set includes multi-substrate conversions or stereoisomeric steps (e.g., phenylalanine to p-coumaroyl-CoA), since RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions and MEANtools filters stereomeric rules Only the loose RetroRules ruleset is available and spurious reaction-Pfam associations cannot be excluded — benchmark results would be inflated Benchmark a rule-based reaction-prediction engine (MEANtools reaction rules built on RetroRules) against a curated set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions, quantifying coverage (134/187, 72%) and testing significance with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test (χ2 = 35.10; DF = 1; p < 0.001). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Benchmark a rule-based reaction-prediction engine (MEANtools reaction rules built on RetroRules) against a curated set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions, quantifying coverage (134/187, 72%) and testing significance with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test (χ2 = 35.10; DF = 1; p < 0.001).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo pathway discovery from multi-omics data rather than benchmarking predictor coverage — use the MEANtools discovery workflow (MR correlation, ClusterONE feature clusters) instead The reaction set includes multi-substrate conversions or stereoisomeric steps (e.g., phenylalanine to p-coumaroyl-CoA), since RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions and MEANtools filters stereomeric rules Only the loose RetroRules ruleset is available and spurious reaction-Pfam associations cannot be excluded — benchmark results would be inflated

skills.description: Use when you have the KEGG code of one or more organisms and a pathway list (organismList.txt / pathwayList.txt) and need per-pathway reaction sets for the functional level of the network.
skills.name: metabolic-pathway-reconstruction
skills.search_text: metabolic-pathway-reconstruction Use when you have the KEGG code of one or more organisms and a pathway list (organismList.txt / pathwayList.txt) and need per-pathway reaction sets for the functional level of the network. When you need to reconstruct the metabolic network from newly annotated genomes or raw genomic data — MetNet does not accept genomic input; use AutoKEGGRec or the KBase Predictive Biology platform instead. When the source of pathway/reaction information is not the KEGG database — the reconstruction is uniquely based on KEGG, which constrains the represented information. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Automatic reconstruction of the functional (reactions-based) level of a metabolic network for a KEGG organism: retrieve each reference pathway's KGML file via KEGG's public APIs and parse it to extract the pathway's compounds and reactions. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Automatic reconstruction of the functional (reactions-based) level of a metabolic network for a KEGG organism: retrieve each reference pathway's KGML file via KEGG's public APIs and parse it to extract the pathway's compounds and reactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need to reconstruct the metabolic network from newly annotated genomes or raw genomic data — MetNet does not accept genomic input; use AutoKEGGRec or the KBase Predictive Biology platform instead. When the source of pathway/reaction information is not the KEGG database — the reconstruction is uniquely based on KEGG, which constrains the represented information.

skills.description: Use when labeled Metabolite CNs are too sparse to train a pathway predictor and only a subset of known chemical reactions (hyperlinks) is available to imitate the organism's metabolic activity and generate artificial networks.
skills.name: metabolic-reaction-iteration
skills.search_text: metabolic-reaction-iteration Use when labeled Metabolite CNs are too sparse to train a pathway predictor and only a subset of known chemical reactions (hyperlinks) is available to imitate the organism's metabolic activity and generate artificial networks. Input already consists of experimentally measured metabolomics profiles with sufficient labeled Metabolite CNs — simulation-based augmentation is meant to mitigate sparsity of labeled data The goal is graph auralization or M5 classifier training (waveform extraction and classification), which consumes the augmented networks downstream rather than producing them The available pathway pool lacks directional substrate-product information, so reactions cannot be executed as transformations http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 A data augmentation procedure that mimics metabolic activity by iteratively executing known metabolic pathways (directional reactions from a 126-pathway tomato pericarp pool), then computes Pearson Correlation Coefficients between every metabolite pair to build artificial Metabolite CNs that enrich training data for NetAurHPD. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: A data augmentation procedure that mimics metabolic activity by iteratively executing known metabolic pathways (directional reactions from a 126-pathway tomato pericarp pool), then computes Pearson Correlation Coefficients between every metabolite pair to build artificial Metabolite CNs that enrich training data for NetAurHPD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input already consists of experimentally measured metabolomics profiles with sufficient labeled Metabolite CNs — simulation-based augmentation is meant to mitigate sparsity of labeled data The goal is graph auralization or M5 classifier training (waveform extraction and classification), which consumes the augmented networks downstream rather than producing them The available pathway pool lacks directional substrate-product information, so reactions cannot be executed as transformations

skills.description: Use when building or expanding a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network from KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB records with predicted reaction pairs, or when verifying curated MRN metabolite/reaction-pair counts.
skills.name: metabolic-reaction-network-curation
skills.search_text: metabolic-reaction-network-curation Use when building or expanding a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network from KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB records with predicted reaction pairs, or when verifying curated MRN metabolite/reaction-pair counts. Input is already an annotated feature table and the goal is annotation propagation rather than network construction (use the MRN as a knowledge layer instead of re-curation) You require a validated FDR for the MRN itself — no FDR is reported because non-RPs are undefined under the screening conditions The analysis is purely statistical/clustering over features with no biochemical reaction knowledge involved http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Curates a comprehensive metabolic reaction network (MRN) by integrating seed knowledge from KEGG, MetaCyc, and HMDB with GNN-predicted and BioTransformer-generated reaction pairs, yielding the knowledge layer that MetDNA3 uses for annotation propagation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Curates a comprehensive metabolic reaction network (MRN) by integrating seed knowledge from KEGG, MetaCyc, and HMDB with GNN-predicted and BioTransformer-generated reaction pairs, yielding the knowledge layer that MetDNA3 uses for annotation propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated feature table and the goal is annotation propagation rather than network construction (use the MRN as a knowledge layer instead of re-curation) You require a validated FDR for the MRN itself — no FDR is reported because non-RPs are undefined under the screening conditions The analysis is purely statistical/clustering over features with no biochemical reaction knowledge involved

skills.description: Use when constructing the predictable-metabolite matching rule set for a mass spectrometry bridging analysis — i.e., you need to enumerate metabolic transformation products of prototypes and score m/z and MS2 similarity for each candidate metabolite-prototype pair.
skills.name: metabolic-reaction-rule-catalog-construction
skills.search_text: metabolic-reaction-rule-catalog-construction Use when constructing the predictable-metabolite matching rule set for a mass spectrometry bridging analysis — i.e., you need to enumerate metabolic transformation products of prototypes and score m/z and MS2 similarity for each candidate metabolite-prototype pair. The analysis target is non-targeted background subtraction of unassigned features rather than bridging metabolites to prototypes via reaction rules (PATBS handles that step) Only single metabolite-to-prototype MS2 spectral matching is needed and no reaction-catalog or mass-defect-based scoring is required (this was the limitation of the prior MTSF approach) The reaction space of interest is beyond two transformation steps from the prototype http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds a predictable metabolite reaction catalog by combining the known one- and two-step metabolic reactions from Metworks 1.3.0.200 with TCM-specific deglycosylation reactions, then scores candidate metabolite-prototype pairs by m/z match (±5 ppm → 70 points) and MS2 fragment similarity degree (1 → 20, ≥2 → 30, 0 → 0 points) within the MDRB post-processing workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Builds a predictable metabolite reaction catalog by combining the known one- and two-step metabolic reactions from Metworks 1.3.0.200 with TCM-specific deglycosylation reactions, then scores candidate metabolite-prototype pairs by m/z match (±5 ppm → 70 points) and MS2 fragment similarity degree (1 → 20, ≥2 → 30, 0 → 0 points) within the MDRB post-processing workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is non-targeted background subtraction of unassigned features rather than bridging metabolites to prototypes via reaction rules (PATBS handles that step) Only single metabolite-to-prototype MS2 spectral matching is needed and no reaction-catalog or mass-defect-based scoring is required (this was the limitation of the prior MTSF approach) The reaction space of interest is beyond two transformation steps from the prototype

skills.description: Use when you have a PathModel knowledge base (.lp) with molecules as atom/bond predicates and known reactions, and need reaction sites (biochemical transformations) to drive analogical inference of new reactions or metabolite structures.
skills.name: metabolic-reaction-site-extraction
skills.search_text: metabolic-reaction-site-extraction Use when you have a PathModel knowledge base (.lp) with molecules as atom/bond predicates and known reactions, and need reaction sites (biochemical transformations) to drive analogical inference of new reactions or metabolite structures. When molecules are not (and cannot be) encoded as atom/bond predicates with consistent atom numbering — the article notes manual encoding of the starting knowledge base and atom numbering during reactions cannot yet be fully automated When the goal is genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction rather than analogical inference on a manually curated pathway with a defined source and goal molecule http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Extract biochemical transformations (reaction sites before and after a reaction) from known reactions encoded as atom and bond predicates in an ASP .lp knowledge base, so that PathModel can analogically apply these transformations to infer new reactions and metabolite structures (e.g., in the MAA pathway from sedoheptulose-7-phosphate toward palythine and MAA1). metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100849
skills.summary: Extract biochemical transformations (reaction sites before and after a reaction) from known reactions encoded as atom and bond predicates in an ASP .lp knowledge base, so that PathModel can analogically apply these transformations to infer new reactions and metabolite structures (e.g., in the MAA pathway from sedoheptulose-7-phosphate toward palythine and MAA1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When molecules are not (and cannot be) encoded as atom/bond predicates with consistent atom numbering — the article notes manual encoding of the starting knowledge base and atom numbering during reactions cannot yet be fully automated When the goal is genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction rather than analogical inference on a manually curated pathway with a defined source and goal molecule

skills.description: Use when multiple automatically generated draft GEMs for the same isolates (e.g. from KBase, CarveMe, RAVEN 2.0, AuReMe) must be merged into a single consensus model and compared against curated reference models.
skills.name: metabolic-reconstruction-merging
skills.search_text: metabolic-reconstruction-merging Use when multiple automatically generated draft GEMs for the same isolates (e.g. from KBase, CarveMe, RAVEN 2.0, AuReMe) must be merged into a single consensus model and compared against curated reference models. When the goal is community-dependent gap filling rather than consensus generation — use COMMIT's gap-filling procedure instead, which considers metabolite permeability and community composition When a single curated reference model already exists for the organism and no merging across pipelines is required When reaction identifiers cannot be translated to a common namespace (comparison was hampered by lack of cross-references to other name spaces, with translations done only 'whenever possible') http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Builds consensus genome-scale metabolic reconstructions by merging per-isolate draft models from four automated pipelines (KBase, RAVEN 2.0, CarveMe, AuReMe/Pathway Tools) after translating all identifiers to the MNXref namespace, and evaluates the merged models against curated references. The consensus yields higher organism specificity and quality than any individual draft while remaining smaller than the sum of the underlying reconstructions. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: Builds consensus genome-scale metabolic reconstructions by merging per-isolate draft models from four automated pipelines (KBase, RAVEN 2.0, CarveMe, AuReMe/Pathway Tools) after translating all identifiers to the MNXref namespace, and evaluates the merged models against curated references. The consensus yields higher organism specificity and quality than any individual draft while remaining smaller than the sum of the underlying reconstructions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is community-dependent gap filling rather than consensus generation — use COMMIT's gap-filling procedure instead, which considers metabolite permeability and community composition When a single curated reference model already exists for the organism and no merging across pipelines is required When reaction identifiers cannot be translated to a common namespace (comparison was hampered by lack of cross-references to other name spaces, with translations done only 'whenever possible')

skills.description: Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) of single-cell metabolic profiles must be partitioned into unsupervised metabolic states and per-condition state proportions quantified, e.g. CTRL vs +FA vs +FA+IL17A vs +FA+IL17A+TPCA1 NAFLD/NASH cultures.
skills.name: metabolic-state-annotation-in-hepatocytes
skills.search_text: metabolic-state-annotation-in-hepatocytes Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) of single-cell metabolic profiles must be partitioned into unsupervised metabolic states and per-condition state proportions quantified, e.g. CTRL vs +FA vs +FA+IL17A vs +FA+IL17A+TPCA1 NAFLD/NASH cultures. The goal is to distinguish different cell types rather than resolve states within one isogenic population — the article addresses cell-type prediction separately (91.3% accuracy from metabolomes alone) and this state-resolution pipeline targets within-population heterogeneity. Input is raw MALDI-imaging data (.RAW/.imzML/.ibd) or microscopy tiles — SpaceM preprocessing must first be run via runAnalysis.py to produce MORPHnMOL.csv before state annotation. The population lacks detectable substructure (no fatty-acid stimulation / no metabolic perturbation), so forcing three Leiden states would be unjustified. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Resolves unsupervised metabolic states (homeostatic, intermediate, steatotic) within isogenic fatty-acid-stimulated dHepaRG hepatocytes from SpaceM spatio-molecular matrices using Scanpy graph-based clustering (neighbors + Leiden), UMAP embedding, and PAGA state-relationship inference, then tabulates per-condition state fractions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Resolves unsupervised metabolic states (homeostatic, intermediate, steatotic) within isogenic fatty-acid-stimulated dHepaRG hepatocytes from SpaceM spatio-molecular matrices using Scanpy graph-based clustering (neighbors + Leiden), UMAP embedding, and PAGA state-relationship inference, then tabulates per-condition state fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to distinguish different cell types rather than resolve states within one isogenic population — the article addresses cell-type prediction separately (91.3% accuracy from metabolomes alone) and this state-resolution pipeline targets within-population heterogeneity. Input is raw MALDI-imaging data (.RAW/.imzML/.ibd) or microscopy tiles — SpaceM preprocessing must first be run via runAnalysis.py to produce MORPHnMOL.csv before state annotation. The population lacks detectable substructure (no fatty-acid stimulation / no metabolic perturbation), so forcing three Leiden states would be unjustified.

skills.description: Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) contains ablation marks that co-sampled neighboring cells and you must quantify whether excluding them changes metabolic-state clustering, marker significance, or cell type classification accuracy.
skills.name: metabolic-state-marker-stability-assessment
skills.search_text: metabolic-state-marker-stability-assessment Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) contains ablation marks that co-sampled neighboring cells and you must quantify whether excluding them changes metabolic-state clustering, marker significance, or cell type classification accuracy. Input is not a SpaceM-derived per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) but raw MALDI imaging data (.RAW/.imzML) or pre-stitched microscopy — the skill operates downstream of SpaceM's runAnalysis.py output The question is method development of segmentation, tile stitching, or METASPACE annotation rather than robustness of downstream clustering/classification to co-sampling The dataset has no spatially-heterogeneous co-culture or neighboring-cell co-sampling, so the sampling-specificity filter has nothing to remove http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Re-runs SpaceM downstream analysis after dropping co-sampling ablation marks (and diffused metabolites) to test whether cell type classification, metabolic-state assignments, and state balance per condition are robust to ablation-mark cross-contamination in the HeLa/NIH3T3 co-culture and dHepaRG NAFLD model. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Re-runs SpaceM downstream analysis after dropping co-sampling ablation marks (and diffused metabolites) to test whether cell type classification, metabolic-state assignments, and state balance per condition are robust to ablation-mark cross-contamination in the HeLa/NIH3T3 co-culture and dHepaRG NAFLD model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a SpaceM-derived per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) but raw MALDI imaging data (.RAW/.imzML) or pre-stitched microscopy — the skill operates downstream of SpaceM's runAnalysis.py output The question is method development of segmentation, tile stitching, or METASPACE annotation rather than robustness of downstream clustering/classification to co-sampling The dataset has no spatially-heterogeneous co-culture or neighboring-cell co-sampling, so the sampling-specificity filter has nothing to remove

skills.description: Use when interpreting an LC/MS feature table (m/z, rtime, p-value) via network-level analysis: matching features to tentative metabolites and scoring metabolic subnetwork modules instead of relying on confirmed metabolite IDs.
skills.name: metabolic-subnetwork-module-detection
skills.search_text: metabolic-subnetwork-module-detection Use when interpreting an LC/MS feature table (m/z, rtime, p-value) via network-level analysis: matching features to tentative metabolites and scoring metabolic subnetwork modules instead of relying on confirmed metabolite IDs. Targeted metabolomics where metabolite identities are already confirmed — mummichog does not replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification Quantification or feature selection has not been done upstream; these steps remain problematic and mummichog expects a curated feature table In vivo multivariate studies where serum/urine mass balance is impossible because the reactions producing these metabolites occur in other tissues http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 mummichog's subnetwork module detection: from a list of significant m/z features, compute all possibly matched metabolites, extract subnetworks within one to four reactions, and identify structural modules with Newman's spectral split algorithm to predict network activity without metabolite identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: mummichog's subnetwork module detection: from a list of significant m/z features, compute all possibly matched metabolites, extract subnetworks within one to four reactions, and identify structural modules with Newman's spectral split algorithm to predict network activity without metabolite identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targeted metabolomics where metabolite identities are already confirmed — mummichog does not replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification Quantification or feature selection has not been done upstream; these steps remain problematic and mummichog expects a curated feature table In vivo multivariate studies where serum/urine mass balance is impossible because the reactions producing these metabolites occur in other tissues

skills.description: Use when you have a series of 1D NMR spectra (acquired individually or as a pseudo-2D experiment) from a metabolic time course — e.g. real-time glycolysis monitoring on 31P or 1H — and need fitted intensities, areas, chemical shifts, linewidths, and coupling constants per signal per time point.
skills.name: metabolic-time-course-quantification-from-pseudo-2d-nmr
skills.search_text: metabolic-time-course-quantification-from-pseudo-2d-nmr Use when you have a series of 1D NMR spectra (acquired individually or as a pseudo-2D experiment) from a metabolic time course — e.g. real-time glycolysis monitoring on 31P or 1H — and need fitted intensities, areas, chemical shifts, linewidths, and coupling constants per signal per time point. skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-candidate-filtering Use when a high-resolution MS metabolite annotation workflow yields too many exact-mass candidates (e.g. 43–13,984 per compound within 10 ppm) and measured or predictable ion-mobility CCS values are available to prune them. Adducts not covered by the training set — current CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments found in ESI-MS experiments No user-curated class-matched training set can be defined prior to prediction, since CCSP 2.0 requires the specific training set to be chosen before CCS prediction Candidates lack measured or predictable CCS data (e.g. no ion-mobility dimension in the acquisition) — use retention-time matching or tandem MS instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filters false-positive metabolite annotation candidates from exact-mass database searches by predicting collision cross section (CCS) values with class-matched linear support vector regression (CCSP 2.0) and rejecting structures whose ΔCCS exceeds a threshold, at a defined ppm mass tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2022.08.09.503345
skills.summary: Filters false-positive metabolite annotation candidates from exact-mass database searches by predicting collision cross section (CCS) values with class-matched linear support vector regression (CCSP 2.0) and rejecting structures whose ΔCCS exceeds a threshold, at a defined ppm mass tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Adducts not covered by the training set — current CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments found in ESI-MS experiments No user-curated class-matched training set can be defined prior to prediction, since CCSP 2.0 requires the specific training set to be chosen before CCS prediction Candidates lack measured or predictable CCS data (e.g. no ion-mobility dimension in the acquisition) — use retention-time matching or tandem MS instead

skills.description: Use when starting from a raw GCxGC-TOFMS detected-peak list (e.g. 691 peaks) and you must document exclusion criteria, missing-value replacement rules, and the annotation-class breakdown of retained metabolites.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-class-categorization
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-class-categorization Use when starting from a raw GCxGC-TOFMS detected-peak list (e.g. 691 peaks) and you must document exclusion criteria, missing-value replacement rules, and the annotation-class breakdown of retained metabolites. The peak list is already filtered and annotated (e.g. a feature table with metabolite class assignments) - the audit would be redundant. The analysis goal is downstream biomarker modeling (OPLS-DA, ROC curve analysis) rather than documenting the filtering/annotation provenance. The data are from a platform whose quality-control and annotation criteria differ fundamentally from this GCxGC-TOFMS plasma protocol (e.g. LC-MS/MS with MS/MS spectral matching). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Documents the peak-exclusion and missing-value-replacement filtering that reduces a raw GCxGC-TOFMS detected-peak list (691 peaks) to a curated metabolite set (195 metabolites), and categorizes the retained metabolites by annotation class (putative annotation, assigned class, uncertain, unknown) in a reproducible audit table. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pntd.0006215
skills.summary: Documents the peak-exclusion and missing-value-replacement filtering that reduces a raw GCxGC-TOFMS detected-peak list (691 peaks) to a curated metabolite set (195 metabolites), and categorizes the retained metabolites by annotation class (putative annotation, assigned class, uncertain, unknown) in a reproducible audit table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak list is already filtered and annotated (e.g. a feature table with metabolite class assignments) - the audit would be redundant. The analysis goal is downstream biomarker modeling (OPLS-DA, ROC curve analysis) rather than documenting the filtering/annotation provenance. The data are from a platform whose quality-control and annotation criteria differ fundamentally from this GCxGC-TOFMS plasma protocol (e.g. LC-MS/MS with MS/MS spectral matching).

skills.description: Use when assembling a curated set of known metabolites from HMDB-classified SMILES to train or evaluate a chemical language model and you need to exclude merely predicted/expected annotations and lipid-like molecules.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-class-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-class-filtering Use when assembling a curated set of known metabolites from HMDB-classified SMILES to train or evaluate a chemical language model and you need to exclude merely predicted/expected annotations and lipid-like molecules. The model is intended for human metabolites; applying it to plant or bacterial metabolism will require a bespoke model trained on a different curated set. Do not use this filter when you want to include lipids or molecules whose biosynthetic routes are divergent and undiscovered, since the curated set explicitly excludes lipid-like superclasses. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Curates a training set of known human metabolites by retaining only HMDB entries annotated in the 'detected' or 'quantified' classes and excluding entries in predicted/expected classes and lipid-like superclasses, then cleaning SMILES with RDKit before model training. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Curates a training set of known human metabolites by retaining only HMDB entries annotated in the 'detected' or 'quantified' classes and excluding entries in predicted/expected classes and lipid-like superclasses, then cleaning SMILES with RDKit before model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is intended for human metabolites; applying it to plant or bacterial metabolism will require a bespoke model trained on a different curated set. Do not use this filter when you want to include lipids or molecules whose biosynthetic routes are divergent and undiscovered, since the curated set explicitly excludes lipid-like superclasses.

skills.description: Use when an unassigned LC-HRMS signal (e.g. a recurrent m/z feature observed on multiple platforms such as Orbitrap Fusion and Q-ToF Impact II) has been characterized by HRMS/MS and needs a metabolite annotation with an explicit MSI confidence level.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-confidence-level-assignment
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-confidence-level-assignment Use when an unassigned LC-HRMS signal (e.g. a recurrent m/z feature observed on multiple platforms such as Orbitrap Fusion and Q-ToF Impact II) has been characterized by HRMS/MS and needs a metabolite annotation with an explicit MSI confidence level. The compound has been confirmed with an authentic standard analyzed under identical conditions — this would be MSI level 1, and the level-2 assignment logic does not apply Only raw unprocessed vendor files are available and no cleaned, SOP-conformant spectral metadata exist — PeakForest requires users to supply completely-cleaned data and manually entered metadata The task is storage or reprocessing of raw spectral data rather than annotation reporting — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Assign Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) confidence levels to LC-HRMS/MS metabolite annotations by cross-checking retrieved spectral and compound records (e.g. via PeakForest REST Web services) against published results, as done for the recurrent NIST plasma m/z 247.1441 signal annotated as hypaphorine at MSI level 2. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
skills.summary: Assign Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) confidence levels to LC-HRMS/MS metabolite annotations by cross-checking retrieved spectral and compound records (e.g. via PeakForest REST Web services) against published results, as done for the recurrent NIST plasma m/z 247.1441 signal annotated as hypaphorine at MSI level 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound has been confirmed with an authentic standard analyzed under identical conditions — this would be MSI level 1, and the level-2 assignment logic does not apply Only raw unprocessed vendor files are available and no cleaned, SOP-conformant spectral metadata exist — PeakForest requires users to supply completely-cleaned data and manually entered metadata The task is storage or reprocessing of raw spectral data rather than annotation reporting — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data

skills.description: Use when validating network-derived (e.g., MetDNA3 level 3) metabolite annotations by testing concordance with independent tools such as CFM-ID, MetFrag, MS-FINDER, and SIRIUS on feature-matched annotations.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-confidence-level-matching
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-confidence-level-matching Use when validating network-derived (e.g., MetDNA3 level 3) metabolite annotations by testing concordance with independent tools such as CFM-ID, MetFrag, MS-FINDER, and SIRIUS on feature-matched annotations. Annotations already confirmed by chemical standards (level 1/2 confidence) — corroboration statistics target network-propagated level 3 annotations that lack standard confirmation The goal is de novo metabolite annotation rather than validating existing network-based annotation results with independent tools Tool outputs cannot be feature-matched by m/z / retention time because they were generated on a different feature set or raw data preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Corroborates network-based metabolite annotations (e.g., MetDNA3 level 3 annotations) by matching features against independent, non-network-based annotation tools and computing multi-tool concordance statistics, as done for Fig. 4b–c of the MetDNA3 paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Corroborates network-based metabolite annotations (e.g., MetDNA3 level 3 annotations) by matching features against independent, non-network-based annotation tools and computing multi-tool concordance statistics, as done for Fig. 4b–c of the MetDNA3 paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotations already confirmed by chemical standards (level 1/2 confidence) — corroboration statistics target network-propagated level 3 annotations that lack standard confirmation The goal is de novo metabolite annotation rather than validating existing network-based annotation results with independent tools Tool outputs cannot be feature-matched by m/z / retention time because they were generated on a different feature set or raw data preprocessing

skills.description: Use when input is MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML, e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench) lacking MS/MS acquisition, and the goal is metabolite annotations at MSI level 2/3 confidence with per-mode counts.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-confidence-leveling
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-confidence-leveling Use when input is MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML, e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench) lacking MS/MS acquisition, and the goal is metabolite annotations at MSI level 2/3 confidence with per-mode counts. Input data already contains data-dependent MS/MS scans — direct MS/MS library search (e.g. MS2-id or GNPS search) is more appropriate than pseudo MS/MS reconstruction Input is MS imaging (imzML) data — use the ms1_id msi workflow with the stricter spatial-cutoff variant (minimum spectral usage 0.05, ≥50 shared pixels) instead of the LC-MS cutoffs Only molecular formula assignment is needed at MSI level 4/5 — tools such as METASPACE or formula-aware annotation are sufficient without spectral matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A skill for producing level 2/3 structural metabolite annotations from MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data by generating pseudo MS/MS spectra and matching them against MS/MS libraries with ms1-id, then counting unique annotated metabolites per analytical mode. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: A skill for producing level 2/3 structural metabolite annotations from MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data by generating pseudo MS/MS spectra and matching them against MS/MS libraries with ms1-id, then counting unique annotated metabolites per analytical mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data already contains data-dependent MS/MS scans — direct MS/MS library search (e.g. MS2-id or GNPS search) is more appropriate than pseudo MS/MS reconstruction Input is MS imaging (imzML) data — use the ms1_id msi workflow with the stricter spatial-cutoff variant (minimum spectral usage 0.05, ≥50 shared pixels) instead of the LC-MS cutoffs Only molecular formula assignment is needed at MSI level 4/5 — tools such as METASPACE or formula-aware annotation are sufficient without spectral matching

skills.description: Use when a KGMN or MetDNA2 annotation run produced putatively annotated unknown peaks (e.g. from NIST urine) that cannot be validated against spectral libraries or standards, and independent in silico MS/MS support is needed.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-corroboration
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-corroboration Use when a KGMN or MetDNA2 annotation run produced putatively annotated unknown peaks (e.g. from NIST urine) that cannot be validated against spectral libraries or standards, and independent in silico MS/MS support is needed. The metabolites of interest are knowns already present in standard spectral libraries — match MS1 m/z and MS2 spectra directly against libraries instead Structurally similar isomers must be distinguished (KGMN cannot effectively discriminate isomers such as isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers) Input is a feature table with no MS/MS spectra and no candidate structures available from HMDB or PubChem http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Corroborates KGMN/MetDNA2-putatively annotated unknown metabolites (absent from spectral databases and lacking chemical standards) using three independent in silico MS/MS fragmentation tools — MetFrag, CFM-ID, and MS-FINDER — on NIST urine LC-MS/MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Corroborates KGMN/MetDNA2-putatively annotated unknown metabolites (absent from spectral databases and lacking chemical standards) using three independent in silico MS/MS fragmentation tools — MetFrag, CFM-ID, and MS-FINDER — on NIST urine LC-MS/MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites of interest are knowns already present in standard spectral libraries — match MS1 m/z and MS2 spectra directly against libraries instead Structurally similar isomers must be distinguished (KGMN cannot effectively discriminate isomers such as isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers) Input is a feature table with no MS/MS spectra and no candidate structures available from HMDB or PubChem

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how much of a known metabolite set a network-based annotation pipeline recovers (coverage, Top 1/3/10 correct rate, Top 3 FDR) by hiding a fraction of known annotations and testing their recovery from seed metabolites.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-coverage-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-coverage-analysis Use when you need to quantify how much of a known metabolite set a network-based annotation pipeline recovers (coverage, Top 1/3/10 correct rate, Top 3 FDR) by hiding a fraction of known annotations and testing their recovery from seed metabolites. The goal is annotation of a new experimental dataset (production annotation) rather than benchmarking recovery of known annotations — use the full MetDNA3/MetDNA2 annotation workflow instead. Comparing tools whose training sets may overlap with the validation metabolites: the article notes 'these tools may have included part of validation metabolites in their training, potentially contributing to the high accuracy', so cross-tool coverage comparison may be inflated. Cross-tool concordance without chemical standards — the article warns 'cross-tool concordance may overestimate performance due to the lack of chemical standards'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark metabolite annotation coverage and correct rate by partitioning known annotations into 30% seed / 70% validation folds under 10-fold cross-validation, propagating annotations from seeds across the two-layer (knowledge + data) network with MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3, and comparing against the MetDNA2 baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Benchmark metabolite annotation coverage and correct rate by partitioning known annotations into 30% seed / 70% validation folds under 10-fold cross-validation, propagating annotations from seeds across the two-layer (knowledge + data) network with MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3, and comparing against the MetDNA2 baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation of a new experimental dataset (production annotation) rather than benchmarking recovery of known annotations — use the full MetDNA3/MetDNA2 annotation workflow instead. Comparing tools whose training sets may overlap with the validation metabolites: the article notes 'these tools may have included part of validation metabolites in their training, potentially contributing to the high accuracy', so cross-tool coverage comparison may be inflated. Cross-tool concordance without chemical standards — the article warns 'cross-tool concordance may overestimate performance due to the lack of chemical standards'.

skills.description: Use when an annotated feature table (e.g. FBMN + ChemWalker + SIRIUS output for actinomycete strains such as BRA006, BRA010, BRA177) needs KEGG compound mapping, pathway assignment, and cross-strain pathway comparison.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-cross-referencing
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-cross-referencing Use when an annotated feature table (e.g. FBMN + ChemWalker + SIRIUS output for actinomycete strains such as BRA006, BRA010, BRA177) needs KEGG compound mapping, pathway assignment, and cross-strain pathway comparison. The feature table has no structural/in silico annotations yet (no FBMN spectral pairing, ChemWalker propagation, or SIRIUS results) — cross-referencing KEGG requires annotations to map from The goal is signal detection/feature filtering of unfragmented ions (use RegFilter-based feature selection instead) Compounds of interest lack KEGG compound entries, since the skill depends entirely on KEGG cross-referencing http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Cross-references annotated molecular features from LC-MS/MS metabolomics (GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker and SIRIUS annotations) against the KEGG database (Kanehisa and Goto, 2000) to assign metabolic pathways, and compares pathway assignments across multiple strains to find shared pathways with different intermediates. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Cross-references annotated molecular features from LC-MS/MS metabolomics (GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker and SIRIUS annotations) against the KEGG database (Kanehisa and Goto, 2000) to assign metabolic pathways, and compares pathway assignments across multiple strains to find shared pathways with different intermediates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has no structural/in silico annotations yet (no FBMN spectral pairing, ChemWalker propagation, or SIRIUS results) — cross-referencing KEGG requires annotations to map from The goal is signal detection/feature filtering of unfragmented ions (use RegFilter-based feature selection instead) Compounds of interest lack KEGG compound entries, since the skill depends entirely on KEGG cross-referencing

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether generated candidate structures plus predicted MS/MS spectra improve exact-structure assignment of held-out metabolites over accurate-mass prioritization alone.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-cross-validation
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-cross-validation Use when evaluating whether generated candidate structures plus predicted MS/MS spectra improve exact-structure assignment of held-out metabolites over accurate-mass prioritization alone. Applying to plant, bacterial, or other evolutionarily distant metabolism — the language model was trained and evaluated only on human metabolite structures and would require a bespoke model When the goal is annotating metabolites from divergent, undiscovered biosynthetic routes — the model has inherent limitations anticipating these When no candidate structure set or predicted/in silico MS/MS library exists — the evaluation requires spectral matching against CFM-ID-predicted candidates http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark language-model-guided metabolite annotation by cross-validating held-out metabolites against an in silico MS/MS library built from generated candidate structures, reporting exact-structure assignment, top-k hit rates, and chemical similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Benchmark language-model-guided metabolite annotation by cross-validating held-out metabolites against an in silico MS/MS library built from generated candidate structures, reporting exact-structure assignment, top-k hit rates, and chemical similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Applying to plant, bacterial, or other evolutionarily distant metabolism — the language model was trained and evaluated only on human metabolite structures and would require a bespoke model When the goal is annotating metabolites from divergent, undiscovered biosynthetic routes — the model has inherent limitations anticipating these When no candidate structure set or predicted/in silico MS/MS library exists — the evaluation requires spectral matching against CFM-ID-predicted candidates

skills.description: Use when METASPACE-annotated spatial or single-cell metabolomics data must be linked to metabolite/lipid set terms for overrepresentation or set enrichment analysis while accounting for isomeric and isobaric candidate ambiguity.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-database-mapping
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-database-mapping Use when METASPACE-annotated spatial or single-cell metabolomics data must be linked to metabolite/lipid set terms for overrepresentation or set enrichment analysis while accounting for isomeric and isobaric candidate ambiguity. Input is already a feature table with unambiguous, structure-resolved metabolite IDs (e.g. from MS/MS spectral matching) — simple ORA/MSEA without bootstrapping suffices. The MS data are MS2-based such that isomeric/isobaric molecules are already resolved by spectra, which MS1-only imaging data do not provide. No annotation database match is available for the target chemistry (e.g. non-lipid metabolites under a lipid-only ontology such as LION). http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps MS1 imaging-MS annotations (METASPACE formula_adduct ions) onto curated metabolite-set databases (RAMP-DB 2.0 sub/main/super-classes, pathways from KEGG/Reactome/SMPDB/WikiPathways, HMDB, SwissLipids, LipidMaps, LION) within S2IsoMEr, so that isomeric/isobaric molecular ambiguity can be propagated into ORA/MSEA enrichment analyses. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf100
skills.summary: Maps MS1 imaging-MS annotations (METASPACE formula_adduct ions) onto curated metabolite-set databases (RAMP-DB 2.0 sub/main/super-classes, pathways from KEGG/Reactome/SMPDB/WikiPathways, HMDB, SwissLipids, LipidMaps, LION) within S2IsoMEr, so that isomeric/isobaric molecular ambiguity can be propagated into ORA/MSEA enrichment analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table with unambiguous, structure-resolved metabolite IDs (e.g. from MS/MS spectral matching) — simple ORA/MSEA without bootstrapping suffices. The MS data are MS2-based such that isomeric/isobaric molecules are already resolved by spectra, which MS1-only imaging data do not provide. No annotation database match is available for the target chemistry (e.g. non-lipid metabolites under a lipid-only ontology such as LION).

skills.description: Use when MALDI-imaging datasets must be re-annotated with a specific formula list (e.g., matrix clusters) against a metabolite database and a controlled FDR cutoff is needed before image classification.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-fdr-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-fdr-filtering Use when MALDI-imaging datasets must be re-annotated with a specific formula list (e.g., matrix clusters) against a metabolite database and a controlled FDR cutoff is needed before image classification. The input is raw centroided/profile imaging MS data not yet processed into METASPACE-ready imzML datasets — annotation requires the METASPACE engine pipeline first The analysis requires strict annotation confidence (e.g., FDR <= 5-10%); this skill deliberately uses the most permissive FDR <= 50% threshold to capture matrix clusters, which would inflate false positives in high-confidence workflows The matrix is not DHB (e.g., CHCA, 9-AA) — the 353 cluster formulas are specific to 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid generated per the Keller and Li (2000) model http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Re-annotate target ion sets (e.g., 353 generated DHB matrix-cluster molecular formulas) in METASPACE against the HMDB v4 database at the False Positive Rate <= 50% threshold (the most permissive METASPACE value) to obtain per-annotation FDR-filtered results for downstream off-sample classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: Re-annotate target ion sets (e.g., 353 generated DHB matrix-cluster molecular formulas) in METASPACE against the HMDB v4 database at the False Positive Rate <= 50% threshold (the most permissive METASPACE value) to obtain per-annotation FDR-filtered results for downstream off-sample classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw centroided/profile imaging MS data not yet processed into METASPACE-ready imzML datasets — annotation requires the METASPACE engine pipeline first The analysis requires strict annotation confidence (e.g., FDR <= 5-10%); this skill deliberately uses the most permissive FDR <= 50% threshold to capture matrix clusters, which would inflate false positives in high-confidence workflows The matrix is not DHB (e.g., CHCA, 9-AA) — the 353 cluster formulas are specific to 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid generated per the Keller and Li (2000) model

skills.description: Use when building marker/query and universe sets for metabolite enrichment from METASPACE annotation tables, and an FDR-controlled significance cutoff (e.g. 0.1) must be applied per annotation database before ORA or MSEA.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-fdr-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-fdr-filtering Use when building marker/query and universe sets for metabolite enrichment from METASPACE annotation tables, and an FDR-controlled significance cutoff (e.g. 0.1) must be applied per annotation database before ORA or MSEA. Input is already a curated list of confidently resolved metabolite structures (e.g. MS2-confirmed IDs) where isomeric/isobaric ambiguity propagation is unnecessary The annotation source is not METASPACE and does not provide per-annotation FDR estimates The goal is annotation quality control or calibration of the FDR itself rather than selecting significant annotations for downstream enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Filter FDR-controlled METASPACE formula-adduct annotation results (e.g. at FDR <= 0.1 against HMDB v4 or CoreMetabolome) so that only passing annotations form the ORA/MSEA query set, while all detected annotations serve as the custom universe for S2IsoMEr bootstrapping enrichment. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf100
skills.summary: Filter FDR-controlled METASPACE formula-adduct annotation results (e.g. at FDR <= 0.1 against HMDB v4 or CoreMetabolome) so that only passing annotations form the ORA/MSEA query set, while all detected annotations serve as the custom universe for S2IsoMEr bootstrapping enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated list of confidently resolved metabolite structures (e.g. MS2-confirmed IDs) where isomeric/isobaric ambiguity propagation is unnecessary The annotation source is not METASPACE and does not provide per-annotation FDR estimates The goal is annotation quality control or calibration of the FDR itself rather than selecting significant annotations for downstream enrichment

skills.description: Decision support for whether a predicted-structure library actually expands annotation coverage: you hold a large set of experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. from MetaboLights blood analyses) and want the fold-change in matched spectra versus a known-metabolite-only search.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-gain-quantification
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-gain-quantification Decision support for whether a predicted-structure library actually expands annotation coverage: you hold a large set of experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. from MetaboLights blood analyses) and want the fold-change in matched spectra versus a known-metabolite-only search. You want to annotate a single spectrum or small cohort with putative structure IDs rather than quantify library-level coverage gain — use a spectral search/annotation skill instead. Your candidate structures come from a database of confirmed metabolites only, with no predicted structures to add — there is no added-library contrast to quantify. Your MS/MS data are deconvoluted peak lists with no precursor masses or the predicted library cannot be scored with cosine similarity under consistent settings, making the two-library comparison incommensurable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Quantifies the increase in experimental MS/MS spectra that can be annotated with a chemical structure when an in silico predicted-spectrum library (e.g. from DeepMet) is added to a known-metabolite library (e.g. HMDB), using cosine-similarity spectral matching at a fixed threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Quantifies the increase in experimental MS/MS spectra that can be annotated with a chemical structure when an in silico predicted-spectrum library (e.g. from DeepMet) is added to a known-metabolite library (e.g. HMDB), using cosine-similarity spectral matching at a fixed threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to annotate a single spectrum or small cohort with putative structure IDs rather than quantify library-level coverage gain — use a spectral search/annotation skill instead. Your candidate structures come from a database of confirmed metabolites only, with no predicted structures to add — there is no added-library contrast to quantify. Your MS/MS data are deconvoluted peak lists with no precursor masses or the predicted library cannot be scored with cosine similarity under consistent settings, making the two-library comparison incommensurable.

skills.description: Use when a shortlist of tumor-co-localized m/z peaks (Pearson r ≥ 0.7 against a massNet tumor-class prediction map) needs tentative molecular formula and adduct assignment via exact-mass search of HMDB and METLIN.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-hmdb-metlin-matching
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-hmdb-metlin-matching Use when a shortlist of tumor-co-localized m/z peaks (Pearson r ≥ 0.7 against a massNet tumor-class prediction map) needs tentative molecular formula and adduct assignment via exact-mass search of HMDB and METLIN. Peaks have not passed the co-localization filter (Pearson < 0.7 vs. the tumor-class map) — annotating all 85,062 m/z variables would be untargeted and wasteful. Confirmed (not tentative) metabolite identification is required — exact-mass matching to HMDB/METLIN alone gives no structural confirmation. Data come from a lower mass-accuracy instrument where ppm errors cannot discriminate among candidate formulas and adducts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates tumor-correlated m/z peaks from MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging with tentative molecular formulas and positive-mode adducts ([M+K]+, [M+2K-H]+) by exact-mass searching the HMDB and METLIN databases and recording the ppm error of each assignment, enabling Table 2-style reporting of tumor-delineation metabolite features. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Annotates tumor-correlated m/z peaks from MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging with tentative molecular formulas and positive-mode adducts ([M+K]+, [M+2K-H]+) by exact-mass searching the HMDB and METLIN databases and recording the ppm error of each assignment, enabling Table 2-style reporting of tumor-delineation metabolite features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks have not passed the co-localization filter (Pearson < 0.7 vs. the tumor-class map) — annotating all 85,062 m/z variables would be untargeted and wasteful. Confirmed (not tentative) metabolite identification is required — exact-mass matching to HMDB/METLIN alone gives no structural confirmation. Data come from a lower mass-accuracy instrument where ppm errors cannot discriminate among candidate formulas and adducts.

skills.description: Use when a filtered/normalized margheRita mRList object derived from MS-Dial output needs feature-metabolite annotation, and MS/MS spectra for features are available for matching against the RPShort positive-mode spectral library.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-level-assignment
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-level-assignment Use when a filtered/normalized margheRita mRList object derived from MS-Dial output needs feature-metabolite annotation, and MS/MS spectra for features are available for matching against the RPShort positive-mode spectral library. When no MS/MS information for the features is present in the selected reference spectral library — margheRita identification is only possible up to level-1 provided the required MS/MS information is available in the library. skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-mapping Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS features (from MZmine2 output: feature table + MGF spectra) need molecular formulas, fingerprints, and chemical-taxonomy annotations attached to a chemical tree so annotated molecules can be traced across samples. The dataset contains only MS1 features without MS/MS spectra — fingerprints cannot be predicted and such features are filtered out. You need complete chemical characterization of a complex sample — spectral match annotation coverage is typically only 1–20% of features, too low to adequately summarize chemical content. skills.summary: Maps metabolite annotations — spectral library matches and in silico properties predicted by SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID — onto the Qemistree chemical hierarchy, assigning each MS/MS feature a ClassyFire 5-level chemical taxonomy so annotations can be interpreted in the context of sample metadata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains only MS1 features without MS/MS spectra — fingerprints cannot be predicted and such features are filtered out. You need complete chemical characterization of a complex sample — spectral match annotation coverage is typically only 1–20% of features, too low to adequately summarize chemical content. Comparison of already co-processed datasets where retention-time alignment is valid; the fingerprint-based representation is mainly advantageous when repeating feature detection/alignment is impractical.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics peak table with MS2 spectra contains annotated known metabolites (seeded from standard spectral libraries) that must be propagated to reaction-paired, spectrally similar unknown peaks via KGMN.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-network-reconstruction
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-network-reconstruction Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics peak table with MS2 spectra contains annotated known metabolites (seeded from standard spectral libraries) that must be propagated to reaction-paired, spectrally similar unknown peaks via KGMN. The input lacks seed annotations from standard spectral library matching — without known metabolite seeds the KGMN propagation has no starting points The goal is de novo structure generation from spectra without structural databases (e.g., MSNovelist-style de novo annotation), rather than propagating from knowns Samples come from non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles where human-derived reaction sets (e.g., BioTransformer reactions) may not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs the knowledge-guided multi-layer network (KGMN) for metabolite annotation from knowns to unknowns by merging three network layers — the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (KMRN), the knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network, and the global peak correlation network — using MetDNA2Vis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Reconstructs the knowledge-guided multi-layer network (KGMN) for metabolite annotation from knowns to unknowns by merging three network layers — the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (KMRN), the knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network, and the global peak correlation network — using MetDNA2Vis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks seed annotations from standard spectral library matching — without known metabolite seeds the KGMN propagation has no starting points The goal is de novo structure generation from spectra without structural databases (e.g., MSNovelist-style de novo annotation), rather than propagating from knowns Samples come from non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles where human-derived reaction sets (e.g., BioTransformer reactions) may not apply

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw imaging MS centroid or profile data that has not yet been annotated by METASPACE-ML — this skill evaluates existing annotations, not spectra Evaluating annotation quality against manually curated ground-truth databases rather than target-decoy FDR estimates Comparing METASPACE-ML against the rule-based MSM approach on precision/throughput rather than selecting a per-dataset FDR threshold

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how the connectivity/edge density of a knowledge-driven metabolite network (MRN vs SMN vs FCN) changes annotation accuracy, estimated FDR, and propagation specificity, with decoy MS2 spectra as negative controls.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-propagation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-propagation-benchmarking Use when you must quantify how the connectivity/edge density of a knowledge-driven metabolite network (MRN vs SMN vs FCN) changes annotation accuracy, estimated FDR, and propagation specificity, with decoy MS2 spectra as negative controls. Your goal is to increase annotation coverage by densifying the network — the benchmark shows added connectivity (SMN, FCN) raises estimated FDR (36.4%, 44.5%) and lowers specificity, so it is not a quality improvement Your MS2 spectra are not matched against decoy references and you lack the supplementary decoy entries (Supplementary Data 4), so FDR cannot be estimated You are annotating with a single fixed topology and need no comparative topology evaluation — use the standard MetDNA3 annotation workflow instead of this benchmarking skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark how knowledge-driven network topologies of varying connectivity (MRN, SMN, FCN) affect network-based metabolite annotation quality in MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3, using decoy-MS2 evaluation on 20 Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics datasets to measure Top-3 accuracy, estimated FDR, and same-superclass propagation specificity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Benchmark how knowledge-driven network topologies of varying connectivity (MRN, SMN, FCN) affect network-based metabolite annotation quality in MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3, using decoy-MS2 evaluation on 20 Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics datasets to measure Top-3 accuracy, estimated FDR, and same-superclass propagation specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to increase annotation coverage by densifying the network — the benchmark shows added connectivity (SMN, FCN) raises estimated FDR (36.4%, 44.5%) and lowers specificity, so it is not a quality improvement Your MS2 spectra are not matched against decoy references and you lack the supplementary decoy entries (Supplementary Data 4), so FDR cannot be estimated You are annotating with a single fixed topology and need no comparative topology evaluation — use the standard MetDNA3 annotation workflow instead of this benchmarking skill

skills.description: Use when a plant metabolomics LC-MS/MS peak needs a reproducible annotation score: e.g. a peak defined by m/z (e.g. 385.1118 in negative mode) plus RT (e.g. 1.27 min) whose MS/MS spectrum should be scored against a plant-specific metabolite database.
skills.name: metabolite-annotation-scoring
skills.search_text: metabolite-annotation-scoring Use when a plant metabolomics LC-MS/MS peak needs a reproducible annotation score: e.g. a peak defined by m/z (e.g. 385.1118 in negative mode) plus RT (e.g. 1.27 min) whose MS/MS spectrum should be scored against a plant-specific metabolite database. The input is a feature/intensity table or statistical analysis task rather than an MS/MS spectrum needing annotation scoring. No MS/MS fragment data are available, so only an MS1 precursor match at the 25 ppm cutoff can be computed and the integrated score cannot be reproduced. The metabolite of interest is unlikely to be in the plant-specific metabolite database (e.g. non-plant or uncharacterized compounds). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Reproduce metabolite annotation confidence scores with PlantMetSuite by combining MS1 precursor mass match, MS/MS fragment match (10 ppm tolerance), and retention-time scores into a single weighted integrated score (Equation (3)), as validated on the 1-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl sinapate example (final score 0.9688). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/plants12152880
skills.summary: Reproduce metabolite annotation confidence scores with PlantMetSuite by combining MS1 precursor mass match, MS/MS fragment match (10 ppm tolerance), and retention-time scores into a single weighted integrated score (Equation (3)), as validated on the 1-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl sinapate example (final score 0.9688).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a feature/intensity table or statistical analysis task rather than an MS/MS spectrum needing annotation scoring. No MS/MS fragment data are available, so only an MS1 precursor match at the 25 ppm cutoff can be computed and the integrated score cannot be reproduced. The metabolite of interest is unlikely to be in the plant-specific metabolite database (e.g. non-plant or uncharacterized compounds).
