skills.description: Use when empirical metabolomics data (time-course metabolite intensities, boundary fluxes, isotope labeling) must be placed onto KEGG-derived pathway nodes of a genome-annotated organism to infer missing or unannotated reactions.
skills.name: metabolite-node-assignment-onto-pathway-graph
skills.search_text: metabolite-node-assignment-onto-pathway-graph Use when empirical metabolomics data (time-course metabolite intensities, boundary fluxes, isotope labeling) must be placed onto KEGG-derived pathway nodes of a genome-annotated organism to infer missing or unannotated reactions. The organism or pathway of interest is not among the 66 KEGG base metabolic pathway layouts shipped with MINNO, and no KEGG ortholog layout exists The goal is quantitative stoichiometric modeling or flux balance analysis rather than visual inference of missing reactions from empirical overlays No empirical metabolomics data (intensities, boundary fluxes, isotope labeling) are available to overlay — the tool refines networks using empirical evidence, not genome annotation alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Map empirically detected metabolites (temporal intensity profiles and boundary fluxes) onto KEGG compound nodes of a species-specific metabolic network built in MINNO, so that active-but-disconnected positions flag missing or unannotated reactions without mathematical modeling. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Map empirically detected metabolites (temporal intensity profiles and boundary fluxes) onto KEGG compound nodes of a species-specific metabolic network built in MINNO, so that active-but-disconnected positions flag missing or unannotated reactions without mathematical modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism or pathway of interest is not among the 66 KEGG base metabolic pathway layouts shipped with MINNO, and no KEGG ortholog layout exists The goal is quantitative stoichiometric modeling or flux balance analysis rather than visual inference of missing reactions from empirical overlays No empirical metabolomics data (intensities, boundary fluxes, isotope labeling) are available to overlay — the tool refines networks using empirical evidence, not genome annotation alone

skills.description: Use when a merged metabolomics dataset has been assembled (e.g. via InChIKey-based MMS) and you need to audit naming consistency, count synonym-hidden merges, and report same/different-name statistics.
skills.name: metabolite-nomenclature-consistency-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-nomenclature-consistency-analysis Use when a merged metabolomics dataset has been assembled (e.g. via InChIKey-based MMS) and you need to audit naming consistency, count synonym-hidden merges, and report same/different-name statistics. Input is a raw, unmerged study table where the question is which identifiers to attach (MMS Step 2 attribute retrieval), not whether already-merged rows agree on naming Names have already been curated to RefMet/PubChem title names, so a same/different-name audit would be trivially 100%/0% and uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Quantifies how often merged metabolomics entries are reported under their canonical database title name versus a synonym, using exact string comparison of reported names against the PubChem title (and RefMet) names, and derives how many compounds would have gone unmerged without name-merging support. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13121167
skills.summary: Quantifies how often merged metabolomics entries are reported under their canonical database title name versus a synonym, using exact string comparison of reported names against the PubChem title (and RefMet) names, and derives how many compounds would have gone unmerged without name-merging support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw, unmerged study table where the question is which identifiers to attach (MMS Step 2 attribute retrieval), not whether already-merged rows agree on naming Names have already been curated to RefMet/PubChem title names, so a same/different-name audit would be trivially 100%/0% and uninformative

skills.description: Use when an input metabolomics dataset carries raw or inconsistently formatted metabolite names (e.g. from a Metabolomics Workbench study via getmwstudies) that must be mapped to RefMet standard classes before enrichment scoring.
skills.name: metabolite-nomenclature-standardization
skills.search_text: metabolite-nomenclature-standardization Use when an input metabolomics dataset carries raw or inconsistently formatted metabolite names (e.g. from a Metabolomics Workbench study via getmwstudies) that must be mapped to RefMet standard classes before enrichment scoring. When metabolites are already keyed by RefMet-standard names or existing class annotations — the mapping step would be redundant re-processing When the goal is KEGG-based pathway mapping rather than metabolite-class standardization; use map_keggid / met_pathways instead When metabolite identifiers are already structured IDs (e.g. KEGG compound IDs) rather than free-text names, since convert_refmet targets name-to-nomenclature mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Standardizes free-text metabolite names by mapping them to RefMet's hierarchical classification (main_class, sub_class, super_class) using MetENP's convert_refmet function, so downstream metabolite-class enrichment analysis operates on a consistent nomenclature. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.11.20.391912
skills.summary: Standardizes free-text metabolite names by mapping them to RefMet's hierarchical classification (main_class, sub_class, super_class) using MetENP's convert_refmet function, so downstream metabolite-class enrichment analysis operates on a consistent nomenclature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When metabolites are already keyed by RefMet-standard names or existing class annotations — the mapping step would be redundant re-processing When the goal is KEGG-based pathway mapping rather than metabolite-class standardization; use map_keggid / met_pathways instead When metabolite identifiers are already structured IDs (e.g. KEGG compound IDs) rather than free-text names, since convert_refmet targets name-to-nomenclature mapping

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature/annotation table needs compound-origin labels (e.g., nutrient, drug, MDM, plant, peptide, halogenated) to prioritize metabolites for pathway analysis.
skills.name: metabolite-origin-classification
skills.search_text: metabolite-origin-classification Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature/annotation table needs compound-origin labels (e.g., nutrient, drug, MDM, plant, peptide, halogenated) to prioritize metabolites for pathway analysis. The task is reducing redundant putative annotations rather than assigning origin labels — use REname or RowMerger modules instead The input already contains curated compound identities with known origin classes, so database matching would add no information Compounds are outside the scope of the parsed reference lists (HMDB nutrients, DrugBank/HMDB drugs, PlantCyc, LOTUS, Metabolomics Data Explorer MDMs) and fail both regex classifiers, so no label can be assigned http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Classifies compounds from untargeted metabolomics putative-annotation tables by biological/chemical origin (nutrients, drugs, microbiota-dependent metabolites, plants/natural products, peptides, halogenated molecules) using the TurboPutative Tagger module, which parses reference databases and applies halogen/peptide regex classifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.952149
skills.summary: Classifies compounds from untargeted metabolomics putative-annotation tables by biological/chemical origin (nutrients, drugs, microbiota-dependent metabolites, plants/natural products, peptides, halogenated molecules) using the TurboPutative Tagger module, which parses reference databases and applies halogen/peptide regex classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is reducing redundant putative annotations rather than assigning origin labels — use REname or RowMerger modules instead The input already contains curated compound identities with known origin classes, so database matching would add no information Compounds are outside the scope of the parsed reference lists (HMDB nutrients, DrugBank/HMDB drugs, PlantCyc, LOTUS, Metabolomics Data Explorer MDMs) and fail both regex classifiers, so no label can be assigned

skills.description: Use when you have a list of significant metabolites (e.g. absolute fold change >= 1 and adjusted p-value < 0.05 from differential metabolomics) and need to rank KEGG pathways by enrichment significance.
skills.name: metabolite-over-representation-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-over-representation-analysis Use when you have a list of significant metabolites (e.g. absolute fold change >= 1 and adjusted p-value < 0.05 from differential metabolomics) and need to rank KEGG pathways by enrichment significance. You want to rank metabolites by full distribution statistics rather than a significant-metabolite list — use MetSEA (fgsea on ranked log2 fold change / p-value lists) instead of Fisher's Exact Test ORA. You lack KEGG annotations for your metabolites and cannot supply an equivalent Pathway/Metabolites table — the Fisher's test depends on a pathway-feature mapping. You need lipid-ontology or other non-KEGG enrichment without first fetching the corresponding ontology mapping (e.g. fetch_lion_lipid_ontology()). http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Over-representation analysis of significant metabolites against KEGG pathways using Fisher's Exact Test on a 2x2 contingency table with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, implemented via the EnrichMet R package's enrichment module. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Over-representation analysis of significant metabolites against KEGG pathways using Fisher's Exact Test on a 2x2 contingency table with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, implemented via the EnrichMet R package's enrichment module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to rank metabolites by full distribution statistics rather than a significant-metabolite list — use MetSEA (fgsea on ranked log2 fold change / p-value lists) instead of Fisher's Exact Test ORA. You lack KEGG annotations for your metabolites and cannot supply an equivalent Pathway/Metabolites table — the Fisher's test depends on a pathway-feature mapping. You need lipid-ontology or other non-KEGG enrichment without first fetching the corresponding ontology mapping (e.g. fetch_lion_lipid_ontology()).

skills.description: Use when two metabolomics studies of related conditions (e.g., acute infection vs. chronic carriage) each yield significant-metabolite lists, and the goal is to classify shared metabolites by concordant/discordant direction and identify condition-only elevated metabolites.
skills.name: metabolite-overlap-comparison-across-datasets
skills.search_text: metabolite-overlap-comparison-across-datasets Use when two metabolomics studies of related conditions (e.g., acute infection vs. chronic carriage) each yield significant-metabolite lists, and the goal is to classify shared metabolites by concordant/discordant direction and identify condition-only elevated metabolites. The input is a single-study differential-expression table with no second condition/study to compare against — use a within-study differential analysis instead Metabolite identities cannot be matched across datasets (different annotation standards, no shared names or spectra/retention-index matches) — cross-referencing by identity is not feasible The goal is classifier discrimination between sample groups (OPLS-DA/ROC), not overlap characterization across studies http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Cross-dataset metabolite concordance analysis: compare significant metabolites identified in one GCxGC-TOFMS study (e.g., chronic Salmonella gallbladder carriage) against those from a related study (e.g., acute enteric fever), classifying overlap by metabolite identity and direction of change to determine whether biomarker profiles are condition-unique. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pntd.0006215
skills.summary: Cross-dataset metabolite concordance analysis: compare significant metabolites identified in one GCxGC-TOFMS study (e.g., chronic Salmonella gallbladder carriage) against those from a related study (e.g., acute enteric fever), classifying overlap by metabolite identity and direction of change to determine whether biomarker profiles are condition-unique.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-study differential-expression table with no second condition/study to compare against — use a within-study differential analysis instead Metabolite identities cannot be matched across datasets (different annotation standards, no shared names or spectra/retention-index matches) — cross-referencing by identity is not feasible The goal is classifier discrimination between sample groups (OPLS-DA/ROC), not overlap characterization across studies

skills.description: Use when raw metabolite abundance profiles (e.g., tomato pericarp metabolic profiles across biological replicates) must be converted into a nodes-and-edges correlation network for downstream network analysis or pathway prediction.
skills.name: metabolite-pairwise-correlation-computation
skills.search_text: metabolite-pairwise-correlation-computation Use when raw metabolite abundance profiles (e.g., tomato pericarp metabolic profiles across biological replicates) must be converted into a nodes-and-edges correlation network for downstream network analysis or pathway prediction. When the input is already a thresholded nodes-and-edges network rather than raw metabolite abundance profiles — reconstruction is unnecessary. When the analysis goal is pathway prediction itself (use NetAurHPD on an existing Metabolite CN) rather than building the correlation network from raw data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs metabolite correlation-based networks (Metabolite CNs) by computing pairwise Pearson Correlation Coefficients across metabolite abundance profiles and thresholding the matrices at |r| >= 0.3 and p <= 0.01 to retain significant links. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Constructs metabolite correlation-based networks (Metabolite CNs) by computing pairwise Pearson Correlation Coefficients across metabolite abundance profiles and thresholding the matrices at |r| >= 0.3 and p <= 0.01 to retain significant links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a thresholded nodes-and-edges network rather than raw metabolite abundance profiles — reconstruction is unnecessary. When the analysis goal is pathway prediction itself (use NetAurHPD on an existing Metabolite CN) rather than building the correlation network from raw data.

skills.description: Use when a supervised classifier built on the full preprocessed GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite matrix separates known clinical classes (e.
skills.name: metabolite-panel-feature-selection
skills.search_text: metabolite-panel-feature-selection Use when a supervised classifier built on the full preprocessed GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite matrix separates known clinical classes (e. The analysis goal is unsupervised exploration of group structure — use the PCA scores approach (as in S1 Fig) before any supervised panel selection. The goal is separating S. Typhi carriage from S. Paratyphi A carriage — that requires the multi-class OPLS-DA model along the second component (p = 0.0031), not the combined-carriage two-class panel. The input matrix is not preprocessed GCxGC-TOFMS plasma data or the class labels for carriage vs non-carriage are missing, so supervised OPLS-DA fitting and cross-validated ROC scoring cannot be performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Selects a minimal co-varying metabolite panel from a GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite matrix and validates it as a combined latent diagnostic pattern, using OPLS-DA rather than individual-metabolite testing. In the typhoid carriage study this yielded a five-metabolite panel (glutaric acid, hexanoic acid, Unknown_087, Unknown_118, Unknown_399) with AUC 0.935. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pntd.0006215
skills.summary: Selects a minimal co-varying metabolite panel from a GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite matrix and validates it as a combined latent diagnostic pattern, using OPLS-DA rather than individual-metabolite testing. In the typhoid carriage study this yielded a five-metabolite panel (glutaric acid, hexanoic acid, Unknown_087, Unknown_118, Unknown_399) with AUC 0.935.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is unsupervised exploration of group structure — use the PCA scores approach (as in S1 Fig) before any supervised panel selection. The goal is separating S. Typhi carriage from S. Paratyphi A carriage — that requires the multi-class OPLS-DA model along the second component (p = 0.0031), not the combined-carriage two-class panel. The input matrix is not preprocessed GCxGC-TOFMS plasma data or the class labels for carriage vs non-carriage are missing, so supervised OPLS-DA fitting and cross-validated ROC scoring cannot be performed.

skills.description: Use when analyzing standard one-dimensional 1H NMR spectra (e.
skills.name: metabolite-panel-integration-quantitation
skills.search_text: metabolite-panel-integration-quantitation Use when analyzing standard one-dimensional 1H NMR spectra (e. The input is not a standard 1D 1H NMR spectrum of serum/plasma (e.g., it is already a feature/concentration table or a 2D spectrum such as 2D-Jres, which the paper only uses for validation rather than primary assignment). The metabolites of interest are outside the 22-metabolite targeted panel, or the spectra require complex signal deconvolution or spectral baseline fitting that SMolESY-select deliberately precludes. The spectra are macromolecule-rich CPMG spectra rather than SMolESY-transformed data, since SMolESY-select relies on the SMolESY pattern within predefined spectral windows and on s/n trade-offs relative to CPMG (at most ~10% less). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A computational skill for assigning and quantifying a targeted panel of 22 metabolites in 1D 1H NMR spectra of blood serum/plasma by searching SMolESY-enhanced data for predefined spin-system patterns (bins) and directly integrating the assigned spectral components without deconvolution or baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: A computational skill for assigning and quantifying a targeted panel of 22 metabolites in 1D 1H NMR spectra of blood serum/plasma by searching SMolESY-enhanced data for predefined spin-system patterns (bins) and directly integrating the assigned spectral components without deconvolution or baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a standard 1D 1H NMR spectrum of serum/plasma (e.g., it is already a feature/concentration table or a 2D spectrum such as 2D-Jres, which the paper only uses for validation rather than primary assignment). The metabolites of interest are outside the 22-metabolite targeted panel, or the spectra require complex signal deconvolution or spectral baseline fitting that SMolESY-select deliberately precludes. The spectra are macromolecule-rich CPMG spectra rather than SMolESY-transformed data, since SMolESY-select relies on the SMolESY pattern within predefined spectral windows and on s/n trade-offs relative to CPMG (at most ~10% less).

skills.description: Use when the input is standard 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g., Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) and a targeted panel of metabolite concentrations (22 spin systems) is needed without manual peak fitting.
skills.name: metabolite-panel-quantification
skills.search_text: metabolite-panel-quantification Use when the input is standard 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g., Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) and a targeted panel of metabolite concentrations (22 spin systems) is needed without manual peak fitting. Input spectra are 2D (e.g., 2D-Jres) or non-IVDr acquisitions requiring spectral fitting — the method targets standard 1D 1H NMR only The analysis requires discovery of metabolites outside the 22 predefined spin systems, since bins are fixed from the 4023-sample cohort Baseline fitting or complex deconvolution of overlapping multiplets is explicitly desired — SMolESY-select deliberately precludes these steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Quantifies a panel of 22 serum/plasma metabolites from standard 1D 1H NMR spectra using SMolESY-select, a fully automated algorithm that assigns spin systems to predefined bins and integrates them directly, avoiding deconvolution and baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Quantifies a panel of 22 serum/plasma metabolites from standard 1D 1H NMR spectra using SMolESY-select, a fully automated algorithm that assigns spin systems to predefined bins and integrates them directly, avoiding deconvolution and baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are 2D (e.g., 2D-Jres) or non-IVDr acquisitions requiring spectral fitting — the method targets standard 1D 1H NMR only The analysis requires discovery of metabolites outside the 22 predefined spin systems, since bins are fixed from the 4023-sample cohort Baseline fitting or complex deconvolution of overlapping multiplets is explicitly desired — SMolESY-select deliberately precludes these steps

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics hit list needs biochemical pathway labels or pathway-level enrichment direction (e.g., KEGG sets, NES from single-sample GSEA) to interpret oncoprotein-driven metabolic phenotypes.
skills.name: metabolite-pathway-annotation
skills.search_text: metabolite-pathway-annotation Use when a metabolomics hit list needs biochemical pathway labels or pathway-level enrichment direction (e.g., KEGG sets, NES from single-sample GSEA) to interpret oncoprotein-driven metabolic phenotypes. Input is untargeted MS output with only spectral features and no metabolite identifiers — pathway sets like KEGG cannot be applied until metabolites are identified The goal is absolute concentration measurement itself (e.g., µg/g tissue quantitation with internal standards) rather than pathway-level annotation and enrichment interpretation The biological material lies outside the pathway set coverage (e.g., metabolites with no KEGG annotation), so enrichment scores would be undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates mass-spectrometry-detected metabolites to biochemical pathways (e.g., KEGG metabolite sets) and quantifies pathway-level enrichment direction so that metabolite classes (aerobic glycolysis intermediates, SCD1-derived fatty acids, lysine-metabolism intermediates, creatine) can be linked to oncoprotein phenotypes such as activated AKT1 or MYC overexpression. metabolomics/v3 10.1158/0008-5472.can-14-1490
skills.summary: Annotates mass-spectrometry-detected metabolites to biochemical pathways (e.g., KEGG metabolite sets) and quantifies pathway-level enrichment direction so that metabolite classes (aerobic glycolysis intermediates, SCD1-derived fatty acids, lysine-metabolism intermediates, creatine) can be linked to oncoprotein phenotypes such as activated AKT1 or MYC overexpression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is untargeted MS output with only spectral features and no metabolite identifiers — pathway sets like KEGG cannot be applied until metabolites are identified The goal is absolute concentration measurement itself (e.g., µg/g tissue quantitation with internal standards) rather than pathway-level annotation and enrichment interpretation The biological material lies outside the pathway set coverage (e.g., metabolites with no KEGG annotation), so enrichment scores would be undefined

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolite-pathway association table (e.g., MetENP's met_path output from a Metabolomics Workbench study such as ST000915) and need to recover the reactions, organism-specific gene IDs, and EC numbers behind each pathway, plus whether each metabolite is a reactant or product.
skills.name: metabolite-pathway-association-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-pathway-association-analysis Use when you have a metabolite-pathway association table (e.g., MetENP's met_path output from a Metabolomics Workbench study such as ST000915) and need to recover the reactions, organism-specific gene IDs, and EC numbers behind each pathway, plus whether each metabolite is a reactant or product. The metabolites have no available KEGG pathway entries or no KEGG compound IDs (MetENP support is limited to 'all metabolite species with available KEGG pathways'). You only need metabolite-class or pathway enrichment scores (use metclassenrichment or path_enrichmentscore instead) and do not need gene/enzyme/reaction-level annotation. Your organism is not in MetENP's korg list of KEGG-supported species, so organism-specific gene IDs cannot be resolved. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 MetENP workflow step that links significantly altered metabolites to KEGG pathways for a chosen species and then annotates each associated pathway/reaction with genes, EC enzymes, and reactant/product roles via KEGGREST queries to the KEGG REST API. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.11.20.391912
skills.summary: MetENP workflow step that links significantly altered metabolites to KEGG pathways for a chosen species and then annotates each associated pathway/reaction with genes, EC enzymes, and reactant/product roles via KEGGREST queries to the KEGG REST API.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites have no available KEGG pathway entries or no KEGG compound IDs (MetENP support is limited to 'all metabolite species with available KEGG pathways'). You only need metabolite-class or pathway enrichment scores (use metclassenrichment or path_enrichmentscore instead) and do not need gene/enzyme/reaction-level annotation. Your organism is not in MetENP's korg list of KEGG-supported species, so organism-specific gene IDs cannot be resolved.

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed peak-intensity/concentration matrix has already yielded a shortlist of significantly changed metabolites (via P/FDR/|log2FC| or PLS-DA/OPLS-DA VIP thresholds) and the goal is pathway-level biological interpretation via MSEA and MetPA.
skills.name: metabolite-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when a preprocessed peak-intensity/concentration matrix has already yielded a shortlist of significantly changed metabolites (via P/FDR/|log2FC| or PLS-DA/OPLS-DA VIP thresholds) and the goal is pathway-level biological interpretation via MSEA and MetPA. Input is raw spectral data — iMAP does not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking and annotation, so spectra must already be preprocessed into a peak table No metabolites-selection result exists yet — pathway analysis must be run on metabolites that already passed the P/FDR/|log2FC| or VIP selection thresholds The goal is purely statistical/bivariate exploration (PCA, clustering) rather than biological interpretation of a metabolite list http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 The data-interpretation step of the iMAP three-step metabolomics analysis framework (data-processing -> metabolites-selection -> data-interpretation), in which metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) and metabolic pathway analysis (MetPA) are applied to a curated list of selected metabolites to reach a biologically significant conclusion. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: The data-interpretation step of the iMAP three-step metabolomics analysis framework (data-processing -> metabolites-selection -> data-interpretation), in which metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) and metabolic pathway analysis (MetPA) are applied to a curated list of selected metabolites to reach a biologically significant conclusion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spectral data — iMAP does not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking and annotation, so spectra must already be preprocessed into a peak table No metabolites-selection result exists yet — pathway analysis must be run on metabolites that already passed the P/FDR/|log2FC| or VIP selection thresholds The goal is purely statistical/bivariate exploration (PCA, clustering) rather than biological interpretation of a metabolite list

skills.description: Use when a cluster-level marker metabolite list (e.g. from spatialmeta.pp.rank_gene_and_metabolite_groups) needs pathway-level interpretation, such as testing whether Imm_4 marker metabolites like Phosphatidylglycerol and PA (24:0/24:1(15Z)) indicate upregulated lipid metabolic pathways.
skills.name: metabolite-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when a cluster-level marker metabolite list (e.g. from spatialmeta.pp.rank_gene_and_metabolite_groups) needs pathway-level interpretation, such as testing whether Imm_4 marker metabolites like Phosphatidylglycerol and PA (24:0/24:1(15Z)) indicate upregulated lipid metabolic pathways. Input is raw SM mass-spectrometry intensity data that has not been integrated and clustered — marker metabolites must come from rank_gene_and_metabolite_groups on the joint AnnData first Metabolites cannot be matched to HMDB annotations because user-defined adducts and ppm tolerance are not specified High-resolution single-cell or subcellular data, since SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only Functional interpretation of marker metabolites identified from SpatialMETA-integrated ST-SM data by testing their over-representation in HMDB-referenced metabolic pathways with a hypergeometric distribution test, as applied to detect upregulated lipid metabolism in the ccRCC Imm_4 immune sub-cluster. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Functional interpretation of marker metabolites identified from SpatialMETA-integrated ST-SM data by testing their over-representation in HMDB-referenced metabolic pathways with a hypergeometric distribution test, as applied to detect upregulated lipid metabolism in the ccRCC Imm_4 immune sub-cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw SM mass-spectrometry intensity data that has not been integrated and clustered — marker metabolites must come from rank_gene_and_metabolite_groups on the joint AnnData first Metabolites cannot be matched to HMDB annotations because user-defined adducts and ppm tolerance are not specified High-resolution single-cell or subcellular data, since SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolite abundance matrix with metabolite names and need personalized pathway-level features for classification or survival analysis; also when you need a metabolite-pathway lookup table to select a specific pathway (e.
skills.name: metabolite-pathway-mapping
skills.search_text: metabolite-pathway-mapping Use when you have a metabolite abundance matrix with metabolite names and need personalized pathway-level features for classification or survival analysis; also when you need a metabolite-pathway lookup table to select a specific pathway (e. Input is already a pathway-level feature table or PDS matrix — re-running MetaTOpathway/PDSfun would remap features incorrectly The analysis goal is feature selection, classification, or prognosis on an existing PDSmatrix — use those skills instead of this mapping step Metabolite identifiers are not recognized names that MetaTOpathway('name') can convert to HMDB ids http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Map metabolite identifiers to their associated metabolic pathways and transform metabolite-level abundance data into pathway-level features in Lilikoi v2.0. This is the dimension-transformation core of the personalized pathway-based analysis: raw metabolite measurements (e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) become a normalized [0,1] pathway dysregulation score (PDS) matrix used for downstream classification and prognosis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Map metabolite identifiers to their associated metabolic pathways and transform metabolite-level abundance data into pathway-level features in Lilikoi v2.0. This is the dimension-transformation core of the personalized pathway-based analysis: raw metabolite measurements (e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) become a normalized [0,1] pathway dysregulation score (PDS) matrix used for downstream classification and prognosis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway-level feature table or PDS matrix — re-running MetaTOpathway/PDSfun would remap features incorrectly The analysis goal is feature selection, classification, or prognosis on an existing PDSmatrix — use those skills instead of this mapping step Metabolite identifiers are not recognized names that MetaTOpathway('name') can convert to HMDB ids

skills.description: Use when you have per-group differential metabolite tables (e.g., male vs female tumors from a massstat differential analysis) and need to know which KEGG/SMPDB biological pathways are specifically enriched in one group but not the other.
skills.name: metabolite-pathway-over-representation-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolite-pathway-over-representation-analysis Use when you have per-group differential metabolite tables (e.g., male vs female tumors from a massstat differential analysis) and need to know which KEGG/SMPDB biological pathways are specifically enriched in one group but not the other. Input is raw LC-MS data still needing peak picking, data cleaning, or metabolite annotation — pathway enrichment must be preceded by the tidyMass data-processing and differential-analysis steps that produce the differential-metabolite lists Metabolites lack pathway-compatible identifiers (annotations below level 2 or unmapped to KEGG/SMPDB sets), so the query cannot be matched to the universe background The goal is quantitative pathway/topology analysis or flux modeling rather than categorical over-representation of a differential hit list http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Runs over-representation (Hypergeometric/Fisher's exact) pathway enrichment on sex-stratified differential-metabolite lists from colorectal cancer tumors using metPath (tidyMass ecosystem) against KEGG and SMPDB metabolite sets, then partitions enriched pathways into male-only, female-only, or shared sets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: Runs over-representation (Hypergeometric/Fisher's exact) pathway enrichment on sex-stratified differential-metabolite lists from colorectal cancer tumors using metPath (tidyMass ecosystem) against KEGG and SMPDB metabolite sets, then partitions enriched pathways into male-only, female-only, or shared sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data still needing peak picking, data cleaning, or metabolite annotation — pathway enrichment must be preceded by the tidyMass data-processing and differential-analysis steps that produce the differential-metabolite lists Metabolites lack pathway-compatible identifiers (annotations below level 2 or unmapped to KEGG/SMPDB sets), so the query cannot be matched to the universe background The goal is quantitative pathway/topology analysis or flux modeling rather than categorical over-representation of a differential hit list

skills.description: Use when metabolite-level p-values (e.g. from two-tailed t-tests per compound) must be converted into a filtered list of differentially abundant metabolites for over-representation analysis.
skills.name: metabolite-pvalue-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: metabolite-pvalue-multiple-testing-correction Use when metabolite-level p-values (e.g. from two-tailed t-tests per compound) must be converted into a filtered list of differentially abundant metabolites for over-representation analysis. The input is already a filtered list of metabolite identifiers, not raw metabolite p-values — threshold selection is not the step needed. Pathway-level p-values from ORA need correction (the paper's SEP selection used p ≤ 0.1 without multiple testing correction); this skill targets metabolite-level test statistics only. Group comparisons are not simple two-group contrasts; the two-tailed Student's t-test basis for the p-values would not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Adjusts metabolite t-test p-values for multiple testing using Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR procedures to produce the differentially abundant (DA) metabolite list that serves as ORA input, and quantifies how threshold and correction choice alter downstream pathway counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Adjusts metabolite t-test p-values for multiple testing using Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR procedures to produce the differentially abundant (DA) metabolite list that serves as ORA input, and quantifies how threshold and correction choice alter downstream pathway counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered list of metabolite identifiers, not raw metabolite p-values — threshold selection is not the step needed. Pathway-level p-values from ORA need correction (the paper's SEP selection used p ≤ 0.1 without multiple testing correction); this skill targets metabolite-level test statistics only. Group comparisons are not simple two-group contrasts; the two-tailed Student's t-test basis for the p-values would not apply.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw per-sample data or standard deviations are available — then classical effect-size meta-analysis methods that model within-study variance are preferable Only qualitative trend labels (up/down-regulation) are reported and no P-values exist — use amanida_vote vote-counting instead Studies report neither a P-value nor study size n — the gamma-distribution weighting cannot be computed

skills.name: metabolite-to-som-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: metabolite-to-som-annotation-mapping Use when comparing a metabolite/Byproduct-predicting tool against SoM-only predictors on a common benchmark, so predicted products must be converted to atom-level SoM labels (e.g., TP/(TP+FN+FP) Jaccard over CYP450 isoforms). When the tool already outputs SoM atom annotations directly (e.g. FAME2, FAME3, XenoSite) — mapping products back to SoMs is unnecessary and can introduce alignment errors When the evaluation target is byproduct (product-level) accuracy rather than atom-level SoM agreement — in that case score whole metabolite structures instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0209 Maps predicted metabolite structures (byproducts) back onto the parent substrate to recover site-of-metabolism (SoM) atom annotations, enabling head-to-head Jaccard comparison between metabolite-predicting tools (CyProduct, GLORY, BioTransformer) and SoM-predicting tools (FAME2, FAME3) on CYP450 data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Maps predicted metabolite structures (byproducts) back onto the parent substrate to recover site-of-metabolism (SoM) atom annotations, enabling head-to-head Jaccard comparison between metabolite-predicting tools (CyProduct, GLORY, BioTransformer) and SoM-predicting tools (FAME2, FAME3) on CYP450 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the tool already outputs SoM atom annotations directly (e.g. FAME2, FAME3, XenoSite) — mapping products back to SoMs is unnecessary and can introduce alignment errors When the evaluation target is byproduct (product-level) accuracy rather than atom-level SoM agreement — in that case score whole metabolite structures instead

skills.description: Use when input data consist only of compound identifiers and trend/behaviour labels (up-regulated, down-regulated, or no trend) per study — i.e. studies that do not disclose p-values, fold-changes, or standard deviations — and a qualitative per-compound meta-analysis is needed.
skills.name: metabolite-trend-classification-updown-regulation
skills.search_text: metabolite-trend-classification-updown-regulation Use when input data consist only of compound identifiers and trend/behaviour labels (up-regulated, down-regulated, or no trend) per study — i.e. studies that do not disclose p-values, fold-changes, or standard deviations — and a qualitative per-compound meta-analysis is needed. The dataset includes p-values and fold-changes (with study size n) — use amanida's quantitative weighted meta-analysis (compute_amanida, mode = 'quan') instead, which combines p-values via weighted Fisher's method and fold-changes via weighted log-average. The input already contains vote-counting results rather than raw per-study trend labels. Raw data with standard deviations/variances are available, permitting standard quantitative meta-analysis methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Qualitative vote-counting meta-analysis for metabolomics compounds when studies report only the direction of change (trend) rather than p-values or fold-changes: each compound-study observation is scored +1 (up-regulated), -1 (down-regulated), or 0 (no trend), and votes are summed per compound using the amanida R package's amanida_vote function. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab591
skills.summary: Qualitative vote-counting meta-analysis for metabolomics compounds when studies report only the direction of change (trend) rather than p-values or fold-changes: each compound-study observation is scored +1 (up-regulated), -1 (down-regulated), or 0 (no trend), and votes are summed per compound using the amanida R package's amanida_vote function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset includes p-values and fold-changes (with study size n) — use amanida's quantitative weighted meta-analysis (compute_amanida, mode = 'quan') instead, which combines p-values via weighted Fisher's method and fold-changes via weighted log-average. The input already contains vote-counting results rather than raw per-study trend labels. Raw data with standard deviations/variances are available, permitting standard quantitative meta-analysis methods.

skills.description: Use when a processed LC-MS feature table (samples x metabolite features with group labels) must be tested feature-by-feature for differential abundance between two classes, producing fold change, p-value, and adjusted p-value per feature for volcano plots.
skills.name: metabolite-univariate-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: metabolite-univariate-statistical-testing Use when a processed LC-MS feature table (samples x metabolite features with group labels) must be tested feature-by-feature for differential abundance between two classes, producing fold change, p-value, and adjusted p-value per feature for volcano plots. Input is raw LC-MS vendor data still needing peak picking and grouping — that preprocessing stage belongs to tools like MZmine, MS-DIAL, or XCMS, not to statistical testing The feature table has not been quality-controlled (e.g., noisy features with >20% missing values in QC samples or >50% MVs in study groups not yet removed), which would bias univariate tests The analysis goal is multivariate modeling or biological function mining rather than per-feature two-group differential testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Per-feature univariate statistical testing of metabolomics intensity data to identify differentially expressed metabolites between two groups (e.g., tumor vs normal), using fold change, t-test/Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and multiple-testing correction within the tidyMass/massStat framework, with results compiled into volcano-plot source tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: Per-feature univariate statistical testing of metabolomics intensity data to identify differentially expressed metabolites between two groups (e.g., tumor vs normal), using fold change, t-test/Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and multiple-testing correction within the tidyMass/massStat framework, with results compiled into volcano-plot source tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS vendor data still needing peak picking and grouping — that preprocessing stage belongs to tools like MZmine, MS-DIAL, or XCMS, not to statistical testing The feature table has not been quality-controlled (e.g., noisy features with >20% missing values in QC samples or >50% MVs in study groups not yet removed), which would bias univariate tests The analysis goal is multivariate modeling or biological function mining rather than per-feature two-group differential testing

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolomics matrix and an lmm2met fit object and need to visually validate that linear mixed-effects modelling reduced per-metabolite variance, as in Figure S-1/Fig. 3a.
skills.name: metabolite-variance-boxplot-visualization
skills.search_text: metabolite-variance-boxplot-visualization Use when you have a metabolomics matrix and an lmm2met fit object and need to visually validate that linear mixed-effects modelling reduced per-metabolite variance, as in Figure S-1/Fig. 3a. Input data are raw, non-log2-transformed signals that have not gone through the LMM fitting step — the before/after comparison is only meaningful on log2-transformed data and its fitted counterpart The goal is statistical significance testing of metabolite differences rather than visual QC of variance reduction; use PLS-DA/OPLS-DA with VIP > 1 feature selection instead There is no subject metadata available to formulate the LMMs — the paper's approach requires patient metadata as rich information of subject characteristics to model metabolite abundances http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Generates before-vs-after boxplots of metabolite signals (e.g., log2-transformed lipids from SAT and VAT of 59 CRC patients) using ggplot2 via lmm2met, to demonstrate that LMM fitting reduces per-metabolite variance and corrects outliers. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: Generates before-vs-after boxplots of metabolite signals (e.g., log2-transformed lipids from SAT and VAT of 59 CRC patients) using ggplot2 via lmm2met, to demonstrate that LMM fitting reduces per-metabolite variance and corrects outliers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw, non-log2-transformed signals that have not gone through the LMM fitting step — the before/after comparison is only meaningful on log2-transformed data and its fitted counterpart The goal is statistical significance testing of metabolite differences rather than visual QC of variance reduction; use PLS-DA/OPLS-DA with VIP > 1 feature selection instead There is no subject metadata available to formulate the LMMs — the paper's approach requires patient metadata as rich information of subject characteristics to model metabolite abundances

skills.description: Use when preprocessing urine metabolite intensity tables (e.g. synthetic_metabolomics.csv) for downstream integration, where metabolites differ in variance and must be scaled before MOFA or similarity network analysis.
skills.name: metabolite-wise-pareto-scaling
skills.search_text: metabolite-wise-pareto-scaling Use when preprocessing urine metabolite intensity tables (e.g. synthetic_metabolomics.csv) for downstream integration, where metabolites differ in variance and must be scaled before MOFA or similarity network analysis. The metabolomics matrix is already creatinine-normalized and Pareto-scaled (re-scaling would alter validated downstream inputs) Data are DNA methylation probes, which undergo a different QC route (top 10% most variable autosomal probes) rather than creatinine normalization and Pareto scaling Sample-wise creatinine normalization has not yet been performed, since Pareto scaling is applied after dilution correction in this workflow A metabolomics preprocessing step in the ACTIONdemonstrator workflow that scales each urine metabolite to mean-zero with variance adjusted by the square root of its standard deviation (Pareto scaling), applied after sample-wise creatinine normalization to make metabolites comparable in downstream multi-omics integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad115
skills.summary: A metabolomics preprocessing step in the ACTIONdemonstrator workflow that scales each urine metabolite to mean-zero with variance adjusted by the square root of its standard deviation (Pareto scaling), applied after sample-wise creatinine normalization to make metabolites comparable in downstream multi-omics integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolomics matrix is already creatinine-normalized and Pareto-scaled (re-scaling would alter validated downstream inputs) Data are DNA methylation probes, which undergo a different QC route (top 10% most variable autosomal probes) rather than creatinine normalization and Pareto scaling Sample-wise creatinine normalization has not yet been performed, since Pareto scaling is applied after dilution correction in this workflow

skills.description: Use when the goal is to convert a cohort of raw 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) into an automated, per-sample quantitative table for a predefined panel of ~22 abundant metabolites.
skills.name: metabolites-assignment-table-construction
skills.search_text: metabolites-assignment-table-construction Use when the goal is to convert a cohort of raw 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) into an automated, per-sample quantitative table for a predefined panel of ~22 abundant metabolites. You need quantitation of metabolites outside the 22-metabolite panel targeted by the algorithm's defined bins Input spectra are not standard 1D 1H NMR (e.g. only 2D-Jres or CPMG-only data, or spectra lacking the glucose anomeric proton needed for 5.233 ppm calibration) The task requires deconvolving heavily overlapped regions or identifying unknown/unassigned signals rather than quantifying the predefined spin-system panel Builds a quantitative 22-metabolite × samples table from standard 1D 1H NMR blood serum/plasma spectra by automatically assigning 24 spin-system patterns in SMolESY-transformed data and directly integrating each assigned component, with no deconvolution or baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Builds a quantitative 22-metabolite × samples table from standard 1D 1H NMR blood serum/plasma spectra by automatically assigning 24 spin-system patterns in SMolESY-transformed data and directly integrating each assigned component, with no deconvolution or baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need quantitation of metabolites outside the 22-metabolite panel targeted by the algorithm's defined bins Input spectra are not standard 1D 1H NMR (e.g. only 2D-Jres or CPMG-only data, or spectra lacking the glucose anomeric proton needed for 5.233 ppm calibration) The task requires deconvolving heavily overlapped regions or identifying unknown/unassigned signals rather than quantifying the predefined spin-system panel

skills.description: Use when a strain collection has both genome-mined BGCs (with iPRESTO sub-cluster motifs or SCCs) and MS/MS data with Mass2Motifs, and the goal is to link molecular substructures to their biosynthetic sub-clusters via co-occurrence correlation.
skills.name: metabologenomic-correlation-scoring
skills.search_text: metabologenomic-correlation-scoring Use when a strain collection has both genome-mined BGCs (with iPRESTO sub-cluster motifs or SCCs) and MS/MS data with Mass2Motifs, and the goal is to link molecular substructures to their biosynthetic sub-clusters via co-occurrence correlation. The genome and metabolome samples are not strain-paired (co-occurrence correlation needs both measurements for the same strains). The MS/MS data has no Mass2Motif annotations, or the genome mining produced no sub-cluster predictions — there is nothing to correlate. You only need BGC sub-cluster prediction itself (run iPRESTO alone); this skill is specifically the downstream metabologenomic linkage step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Links MS/MS-derived Mass2Motif substructures to genome-mined BGC sub-clusters by computing Doroghazi et al. co-occurrence correlation scores across a strain collection, then applying permutation tests to separate true metabologenomic links from chance co-occurrence. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Links MS/MS-derived Mass2Motif substructures to genome-mined BGC sub-clusters by computing Doroghazi et al. co-occurrence correlation scores across a strain collection, then applying permutation tests to separate true metabologenomic links from chance co-occurrence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome and metabolome samples are not strain-paired (co-occurrence correlation needs both measurements for the same strains). The MS/MS data has no Mass2Motif annotations, or the genome mining produced no sub-cluster predictions — there is nothing to correlate. You only need BGC sub-cluster prediction itself (run iPRESTO alone); this skill is specifically the downstream metabologenomic linkage step.

skills.description: Use when you have downloaded the PoDP Zenodo JSON deposit and need to reproduce or audit the published dataset statistics (Box 1) — e.g. validating that 1,306 metagenomes, 1,268 genomes, and 42 MAGs are present.
skills.name: metabolome-genome-link-tabulation
skills.search_text: metabolome-genome-link-tabulation Use when you have downloaded the PoDP Zenodo JSON deposit and need to reproduce or audit the published dataset statistics (Box 1) — e.g. validating that 1,306 metagenomes, 1,268 genomes, and 42 MAGs are present. You need the raw metabolomics or genomics data itself — the PoDP captures only metadata defining pairs of omics datasets in existing public databases and stores no spectra or sequences You want to enumerate individual genome–metabolite link instances rather than reproduce aggregate corpus-level statistics The metadata you need lives in free-text 'Other' boxes, which is inherently not machine-readable and cannot be tabulated programmatically http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduce PoDP preliminary dataset statistics by parsing the community-curated JSON project metadata archived to Zenodo and aggregating counts of projects, MS samples, genomes, metagenomes, MAGs, metadata methods, and registered BGC–MS/MS links. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00724-z
skills.summary: Reproduce PoDP preliminary dataset statistics by parsing the community-curated JSON project metadata archived to Zenodo and aggregating counts of projects, MS samples, genomes, metagenomes, MAGs, metadata methods, and registered BGC–MS/MS links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the raw metabolomics or genomics data itself — the PoDP captures only metadata defining pairs of omics datasets in existing public databases and stores no spectra or sequences You want to enumerate individual genome–metabolite link instances rather than reproduce aggregate corpus-level statistics The metadata you need lives in free-text 'Other' boxes, which is inherently not machine-readable and cannot be tabulated programmatically

skills.description: Use when a labeled metabolomics feature table (samples × metabolite intensities with phenotype metadata, e.g. age, sex, region) is available and the goal is an automated, metabolome-informed predictive classifier.
skills.name: metabolome-informed-phenotype-prediction
skills.search_text: metabolome-informed-phenotype-prediction Use when a labeled metabolomics feature table (samples × metabolite intensities with phenotype metadata, e.g. age, sex, region) is available and the goal is an automated, metabolome-informed predictive classifier. The goal is metabolite identification or structural annotation — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification; it only supports identity- and fuzzy-search annotation Downstream biological or clinical validation of the selected metabolites' function is the goal — experiments are required to confirm biological function of selected features The data is raw LC-MS files rather than a processed, quality-controlled final data table — use MassCube's peak detection/alignment workflow first http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build a phenotype classifier (random forest) from MassCube's quality-controlled metabolomics feature table, selecting features by metadata association and importance strength to predict sample labels such as mouse age group. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Build a phenotype classifier (random forest) from MassCube's quality-controlled metabolomics feature table, selecting features by metadata association and importance strength to predict sample labels such as mouse age group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is metabolite identification or structural annotation — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification; it only supports identity- and fuzzy-search annotation Downstream biological or clinical validation of the selected metabolites' function is the goal — experiments are required to confirm biological function of selected features The data is raw LC-MS files rather than a processed, quality-controlled final data table — use MassCube's peak detection/alignment workflow first

skills.description: Use when you have MiMeNet biclustered microbe/metabolite modules and WGCNA modules for paired microbiome-metabolome data (e.g. IBD PRISM) and want to determine if module-level features match original features for predicting disease labels.
skills.name: metabolome-module-feature-aggregation
skills.search_text: metabolome-module-feature-aggregation Use when you have MiMeNet biclustered microbe/metabolite modules and WGCNA modules for paired microbiome-metabolome data (e.g. IBD PRISM) and want to determine if module-level features match original features for predicting disease labels. Input is a single feature table without paired microbiome-metabolome data — this skill requires both modalities to define biclustered microbe and metabolite modules You only want to predict the metabolomic profile from microbial taxa (use the MiMeNet prediction workflow) rather than evaluate phenotype-relevant information retained by module features No supervised sample labels (e.g. IBD diagnosis) exist — classifier training and AUC evaluation cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 Aggregates microbe and metabolite bicluster modules into per-module feature values by averaging normalized abundances, then compares their predictive power (via MLPNN classifiers on IBD data) against original features and WGCNA module features to test whether MiMeNet modules retain phenotype-relevant information. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009021
skills.summary: Aggregates microbe and metabolite bicluster modules into per-module feature values by averaging normalized abundances, then compares their predictive power (via MLPNN classifiers on IBD data) against original features and WGCNA module features to test whether MiMeNet modules retain phenotype-relevant information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single feature table without paired microbiome-metabolome data — this skill requires both modalities to define biclustered microbe and metabolite modules You only want to predict the metabolomic profile from microbial taxa (use the MiMeNet prediction workflow) rather than evaluate phenotype-relevant information retained by module features No supervised sample labels (e.g. IBD diagnosis) exist — classifier training and AUC evaluation cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when a SummarizedExperiment of metabolic feature intensities (e.g. plasma 1H NMR) plus clinical metadata (phenotype + confounders) must be screened feature-by-feature for phenotype associations with multiple-testing control.
skills.name: metabolome-wide-association-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolome-wide-association-analysis Use when a SummarizedExperiment of metabolic feature intensities (e.g. plasma 1H NMR) plus clinical metadata (phenotype + confounders) must be screened feature-by-feature for phenotype associations with multiple-testing control. The goal is multivariate modelling of metabonomic data where confounders are not handled feature-wise — the article notes multivariate packages 'do not properly account for cofounding factors (e.g. age, gender)', which is precisely why the univariate MWAS route is used instead The task is metabolite assignment, QC or network/pathway interpretation (STOCSY, biological interpretation), which are separate MWASTools functionalities rather than the association-testing step http://edamontology.org/topic_3277 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Performs metabolome-wide association studies (MWAS) by testing each metabolic feature (e.g. 1H NMR intensity) for association with a phenotype such as BMI, using univariate models — partial Spearman correlations or generalized linear models — with efficient handling of epidemiological confounders like age and gender, plus Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Performs metabolome-wide association studies (MWAS) by testing each metabolic feature (e.g. 1H NMR intensity) for association with a phenotype such as BMI, using univariate models — partial Spearman correlations or generalized linear models — with efficient handling of epidemiological confounders like age and gender, plus Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is multivariate modelling of metabonomic data where confounders are not handled feature-wise — the article notes multivariate packages 'do not properly account for cofounding factors (e.g. age, gender)', which is precisely why the univariate MWAS route is used instead The task is metabolite assignment, QC or network/pathway interpretation (STOCSY, biological interpretation), which are separate MWASTools functionalities rather than the association-testing step

skills.description: Use when a metabolomic peak table has passed filtering/imputation (S1) and QCS correction (S2) and must be nonlinearly transformed (e.g., LOG) and normalized (e.g., VAS-LIN) before performance assessment in NOREVA.
skills.name: metabolomic-data-transformation-and-normalization
skills.search_text: metabolomic-data-transformation-and-normalization Use when a metabolomic peak table has passed filtering/imputation (S1) and QCS correction (S2) and must be nonlinearly transformed (e.g., LOG) and normalized (e.g., VAS-LIN) before performance assessment in NOREVA. Input is a raw proprietary instrument file that still needs conversion and peak-table generation (use Proteowizard, nmrML, XCMS or NMRProc Flow first) The peak table has not yet been filtered/imputed (S1) or QCS-corrected (S2) — NOREVA's four processing stages are ordered S1→S2→S3→S4 and cannot be run out of sequence The goal is performance assessment itself (S5) rather than producing the normalized processing outcome that assessment consumes http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies the S3 (data transformation) and S4 (data normalization) stages of the NOREVA protocol to standardized metabolomic peak tables, correcting data heteroscedasticity and removing unwanted technical variation after the study-assumption (S4a) has been determined. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Applies the S3 (data transformation) and S4 (data normalization) stages of the NOREVA protocol to standardized metabolomic peak tables, correcting data heteroscedasticity and removing unwanted technical variation after the study-assumption (S4a) has been determined.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw proprietary instrument file that still needs conversion and peak-table generation (use Proteowizard, nmrML, XCMS or NMRProc Flow first) The peak table has not yet been filtered/imputed (S1) or QCS-corrected (S2) — NOREVA's four processing stages are ordered S1→S2→S3→S4 and cannot be run out of sequence The goal is performance assessment itself (S5) rather than producing the normalized processing outcome that assessment consumes

skills.description: Use when you have edge-list files of putative biochemical transformations from FT-ICR MS peak mass differences and need a Cytoscape network plus network statistics tables and plots.
skills.name: metabolomic-edge-list-import-processing
skills.search_text: metabolomic-edge-list-import-processing Use when you have edge-list files of putative biochemical transformations from FT-ICR MS peak mass differences and need a Cytoscape network plus network statistics tables and plots. Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra or a peak abundance table without molecular formula assignments — MetaboDirect expects formulas to be assigned before network generation You only need chemodiversity or multivariate statistics; those are separate MetaboDirect pipeline steps (chemodiversity analysis, statistical analysis) and do not involve Cytoscape Mass differences were not filtered against reference biochemical transformation keys (1 ppm max error), since unfiltered mass differences would produce spurious edges http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Import MetaboDirect-generated transformation edge lists (mass-difference links between FT-ICR MS peaks) into Cytoscape, style nodes by molecular class, and compute per-network and per-transformation-type statistics via the pipeline's network_stats.R script, exporting .csv tables and bar plots. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Import MetaboDirect-generated transformation edge lists (mass-difference links between FT-ICR MS peaks) into Cytoscape, style nodes by molecular class, and compute per-network and per-transformation-type statistics via the pipeline's network_stats.R script, exporting .csv tables and bar plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra or a peak abundance table without molecular formula assignments — MetaboDirect expects formulas to be assigned before network generation You only need chemodiversity or multivariate statistics; those are separate MetaboDirect pipeline steps (chemodiversity analysis, statistical analysis) and do not involve Cytoscape Mass differences were not filtered against reference biochemical transformation keys (1 ppm max error), since unfiltered mass differences would produce spurious edges

skills.description: Use when you have per-patient DAM lists (absolute z-score >= 2) from XCMS untargeted LC-MS output and need continuous [0,1] per-gene seed labels for metPropagate label propagation over STRING.
skills.name: metabolomic-enrichment-score-scaling
skills.search_text: metabolomic-enrichment-score-scaling Use when you have per-patient DAM lists (absolute z-score >= 2) from XCMS untargeted LC-MS output and need continuous [0,1] per-gene seed labels for metPropagate label propagation over STRING. Candidate gene ranking from propagated scores is already done — this skill only produces pre-propagation seed labels, not final Score.ID rankings. No differentially abundant metabolites exist for the patient (e.g., disease-associated metabolites like large glycosaminoglycans are not measurable by the metabolomic system), so no meaningful ME seed signal can be computed. Input is raw LC-MS feature intensities that have not yet passed XCMS peak detection, 10% sample-presence filtering, HMDB annotation, and non-base-isotope removal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME) scores from patient-specific untargeted LC-MS data — Fisher's Exact enrichment of DAMs against HMDB gene-metabolite sets, multiplied by the gene's largest metabolite z-score — and scales them to [0,1] for use as seed labels in network label propagation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Computes per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME) scores from patient-specific untargeted LC-MS data — Fisher's Exact enrichment of DAMs against HMDB gene-metabolite sets, multiplied by the gene's largest metabolite z-score — and scales them to [0,1] for use as seed labels in network label propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate gene ranking from propagated scores is already done — this skill only produces pre-propagation seed labels, not final Score.ID rankings. No differentially abundant metabolites exist for the patient (e.g., disease-associated metabolites like large glycosaminoglycans are not measurable by the metabolomic system), so no meaningful ME seed signal can be computed. Input is raw LC-MS feature intensities that have not yet passed XCMS peak detection, 10% sample-presence filtering, HMDB annotation, and non-base-isotope removal.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a hybrid DDA/DIA acquisition strategy against conventional DDA and DIA(SWATH) runs and you need reproducible feature/MS2-count tables with recomputed relative gains.

skills.summary: Compares detected-feature and MS2-feature counts across LC-MS acquisition workflows (DDA, DIA/SWATH, DaDIA) on the same samples, verifying relative percentage increases against the article's reported figures.
