skills.description: Use when comparing LC-MS acquisition workflows (DDA vs DIA vs hybrid DaDIA) and you need to measure how many DDA-derived metabolic features are recovered in the combined data and assess their peak-shape reliability.
skills.name: metabolomic-feature-recovery-quantification
skills.search_text: metabolomic-feature-recovery-quantification Use when comparing LC-MS acquisition workflows (DDA vs DIA vs hybrid DaDIA) and you need to measure how many DDA-derived metabolic features are recovered in the combined data and assess their peak-shape reliability. Input is already a final metabolite annotation table rather than raw mzXML feature extraction output — the skill requires re-running feature extraction to compare DDA vs DaDIA feature lists. Data were acquired without a pooled QC sample run in DDA mode alongside individual samples run in DIA mode; the rescue step depends on having both acquisition modes represented. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Quantifies how many metabolic features detected in DDA mode are rescued in the combined DaDIA (DDA+DIA) dataset and validates the rescued features by manual extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) inspection, yielding recovered-feature counts plus true-positive and false-positive rates. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c05022
skills.summary: Quantifies how many metabolic features detected in DDA mode are rescued in the combined DaDIA (DDA+DIA) dataset and validates the rescued features by manual extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) inspection, yielding recovered-feature counts plus true-positive and false-positive rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a final metabolite annotation table rather than raw mzXML feature extraction output — the skill requires re-running feature extraction to compare DDA vs DaDIA feature lists. Data were acquired without a pooled QC sample run in DDA mode alongside individual samples run in DIA mode; the rescue step depends on having both acquisition modes represented.

skills.description: Use when a quality-controlled metabolomic feature table plus sample metadata (e.g., age group, sex, brain region) is available and the goal is metadata-driven feature selection and phenotype prediction.
skills.name: metabolomic-feature-selection-by-metadata
skills.search_text: metabolomic-feature-selection-by-metadata Use when a quality-controlled metabolomic feature table plus sample metadata (e.g., age group, sex, brain region) is available and the goal is metadata-driven feature selection and phenotype prediction. Input is raw vendor LC-MS data rather than a processed feature table — run MassCube's peak detection, adduct/ISF grouping, alignment, and QC modules first The goal is metabolite identification/structural elucidation — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification, and downstream experiments remain necessary to confirm biological function of selected metabolites The task needs a graphical interface or time-series/statistical modules not yet implemented (no GUI, no time-series analysis, no SERRF normalization in the current version) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Select discriminative metabolomic features from a QC'd LC-MS feature table by metadata group membership and feature-importance strength, then fit a random-forest phenotype classifier (e.g., adolescent vs middle-age mouse brain) and report AUC and cross-validated accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-60640-5
skills.summary: Select discriminative metabolomic features from a QC'd LC-MS feature table by metadata group membership and feature-importance strength, then fit a random-forest phenotype classifier (e.g., adolescent vs middle-age mouse brain) and report AUC and cross-validated accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor LC-MS data rather than a processed feature table — run MassCube's peak detection, adduct/ISF grouping, alignment, and QC modules first The goal is metabolite identification/structural elucidation — MassCube does not directly perform metabolite identification, and downstream experiments remain necessary to confirm biological function of selected metabolites The task needs a graphical interface or time-series/statistical modules not yet implemented (no GUI, no time-series analysis, no SERRF normalization in the current version)

skills.description: Use when you have a paired-design LC-MS metabolomic feature table (e.g. from XCMS centWave on DDA or DaDIA data) and need to identify statistically significant metabolic features for downstream workflow comparison or metabolite annotation.
skills.name: metabolomic-feature-significance-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolomic-feature-significance-filtering Use when you have a paired-design LC-MS metabolomic feature table (e.g. from XCMS centWave on DDA or DaDIA data) and need to identify statistically significant metabolic features for downstream workflow comparison or metabolite annotation. Input is already a significance-annotated feature table or a metabolite list — the filtering step would be redundant. Data are from an unpaired study design; the paired two-tailed t-test threshold of the leukemia plasma study is not valid. Data lack method blank samples or MS2 spectra; background-noise filtering and metabolite annotation by dot-product matching cannot be performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Applies the leukemia plasma metabolomic significance criteria from the DaDIA study to pick statistically significant metabolic features in XCMS-extracted feature tables, then compares significant-feature counts, MS2 coverage, and annotated endogenous metabolites across acquisition workflows (DDA vs DaDIA). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c05022
skills.summary: Applies the leukemia plasma metabolomic significance criteria from the DaDIA study to pick statistically significant metabolic features in XCMS-extracted feature tables, then compares significant-feature counts, MS2 coverage, and annotated endogenous metabolites across acquisition workflows (DDA vs DaDIA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a significance-annotated feature table or a metabolite list — the filtering step would be redundant. Data are from an unpaired study design; the paired two-tailed t-test threshold of the leukemia plasma study is not valid. Data lack method blank samples or MS2 spectra; background-noise filtering and metabolite annotation by dot-product matching cannot be performed.

skills.description: Use when a post-formula-assignment FT-ICR MS peak table (e.g., Report.csv with peak abundances and molecular formulas) must be normalized across samples before multivariate statistics, and the normalization method itself must be selected empirically via test_normalization.
skills.name: metabolomic-intensity-normalization-handling
skills.search_text: metabolomic-intensity-normalization-handling Use when a post-formula-assignment FT-ICR MS peak table (e.g., Report.csv with peak abundances and molecular formulas) must be normalized across samples before multivariate statistics, and the normalization method itself must be selected empirically via test_normalization. The input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra that still needs molecular formula assignment — MetaboDirect requires formula assignment to be performed prior to use The peak table was already normalized upstream (e.g., the S. fallax data set was previously filtered/processed by the original authors), so re-normalization would be redundant or inappropriate The goal is cheminformatics on structural/MS2 data (e.g., molecular networking of isomer-resolved spectra) rather than direct-injection FT-ICR MS peak-intensity tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Handles the intensity-normalization stage of MetaboDirect: selecting the best normalization method with the test_normalization companion script, then applying it to FT-ICR MS peak-intensity tables so downstream dissimilarity, PERMANOVA, NMDS/PCA, and chemodiversity analyses operate on comparable per-sample abundances. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Handles the intensity-normalization stage of MetaboDirect: selecting the best normalization method with the test_normalization companion script, then applying it to FT-ICR MS peak-intensity tables so downstream dissimilarity, PERMANOVA, NMDS/PCA, and chemodiversity analyses operate on comparable per-sample abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra that still needs molecular formula assignment — MetaboDirect requires formula assignment to be performed prior to use The peak table was already normalized upstream (e.g., the S. fallax data set was previously filtered/processed by the original authors), so re-normalization would be redundant or inappropriate The goal is cheminformatics on structural/MS2 data (e.g., molecular networking of isomer-resolved spectra) rather than direct-injection FT-ICR MS peak-intensity tables

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolite abundance table (e.g., >470 plasma metabolites from GC-TOF-MS) and need to connect analytes — including unknowns — via biochemical, structural, spectral, and empirical edges rather than pathway maps.
skills.name: metabolomic-network-construction
skills.search_text: metabolomic-network-construction Use when you have a metabolite abundance table (e.g., >470 plasma metabolites from GC-TOF-MS) and need to connect analytes — including unknowns — via biochemical, structural, spectral, and empirical edges rather than pathway maps. The goal is pathway-map-based visualization (e.g., KEGG pathway overlays) rather than pathway-independent association networks. Analytes lack KEGG/PubChem identifiers, computable structures, and mass spectra, so no biochemical, structural, or spectral edge can be derived and the network would be empty or disconnected. Input is raw chromatography–mass spectrometry data not yet processed into a peak/abundance table with metabolite-level identifiers. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Construct a pathway-independent metabolomic network by integrating four orthogonal edge types — biochemical (KEGG RPAIR), structural similarity (PubChem Substructure Fingerprints, Tanimoto >0.7), mass spectral similarity (cosine >0.7), and empirical dependency (Spearman correlation, FDR p<0.05) — using MetaMapR, which connects metabolites even when biochemical annotations or structures are unknown. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Construct a pathway-independent metabolomic network by integrating four orthogonal edge types — biochemical (KEGG RPAIR), structural similarity (PubChem Substructure Fingerprints, Tanimoto >0.7), mass spectral similarity (cosine >0.7), and empirical dependency (Spearman correlation, FDR p<0.05) — using MetaMapR, which connects metabolites even when biochemical annotations or structures are unknown.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pathway-map-based visualization (e.g., KEGG pathway overlays) rather than pathway-independent association networks. Analytes lack KEGG/PubChem identifiers, computable structures, and mass spectra, so no biochemical, structural, or spectral edge can be derived and the network would be empty or disconnected. Input is raw chromatography–mass spectrometry data not yet processed into a peak/abundance table with metabolite-level identifiers.

skills.description: Use when building a MetaMapR metabolomic network from molecular feature data (identified metabolites plus structurally unknown features with mass spectra) and you need to threshold similarity edges, e.g. retaining only cosine correlation >0.7 spectral edges.
skills.name: metabolomic-network-edge-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolomic-network-edge-threshold-filtering Use when building a MetaMapR metabolomic network from molecular feature data (identified metabolites plus structurally unknown features with mass spectra) and you need to threshold similarity edges, e.g. retaining only cosine correlation >0.7 spectral edges. The input is already a filtered, edge-list network file and the goal is visualization only (export it directly to Cytoscape rather than re-thresholding) The goal is biochemical transformation networks built strictly from KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs, where no spectral or structural similarity edges are desired MetaMapR constructs metabolomic networks from four orthogonal association measures (KEGG RPAIR biochemical transformations, PubChem substructure fingerprint similarity, mass spectral cosine similarity, empirical correlations) and filters edges by tunable similarity thresholds before export. This skill applies those thresholding rules—e.g. cosine correlation >0.7 for spectral edges—to produce a controlled-density edge list. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: MetaMapR constructs metabolomic networks from four orthogonal association measures (KEGG RPAIR biochemical transformations, PubChem substructure fingerprint similarity, mass spectral cosine similarity, empirical correlations) and filters edges by tunable similarity thresholds before export. This skill applies those thresholding rules—e.g. cosine correlation >0.7 for spectral edges—to produce a controlled-density edge list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered, edge-list network file and the goal is visualization only (export it directly to Cytoscape rather than re-thresholding) The goal is biochemical transformation networks built strictly from KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs, where no spectral or structural similarity edges are desired

skills.description: Use when a MetaMapR network (edge list with source, target, edge-type columns and a node attributes table with numeric node IDs) must be handed off to downstream network tools such as Cytoscape.
skills.name: metabolomic-network-export
skills.search_text: metabolomic-network-export Use when a MetaMapR network (edge list with source, target, edge-type columns and a node attributes table with numeric node IDs) must be handed off to downstream network tools such as Cytoscape. The network has not yet been calculated in MetaMapR (no edge list or node ID mapping exists) — identifier translation or network calculation must happen first The target analysis requires the interactive Shiny/D3.js visualization rather than a static or tabular export Node IDs need to be re-derived from scratch — use MetaMapR's edge index option during calculation instead of post-hoc reassignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Exports a MetaMapR-calculated metabolic network (edge list plus node attribute table) as CSV files formatted for Cytoscape ingestion, alongside static high-quality graphics (SVG/PNG) rendered from the interactive D3.js visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Exports a MetaMapR-calculated metabolic network (edge list plus node attribute table) as CSV files formatted for Cytoscape ingestion, alongside static high-quality graphics (SVG/PNG) rendered from the interactive D3.js visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network has not yet been calculated in MetaMapR (no edge list or node ID mapping exists) — identifier translation or network calculation must happen first The target analysis requires the interactive Shiny/D3.js visualization rather than a static or tabular export Node IDs need to be re-derived from scratch — use MetaMapR's edge index option during calculation instead of post-hoc reassignment

skills.description: Use when metabolomic intensity data (rows/columns labelled with KEGG compound IDs such as 'C00042') must be converted into an inferred metabolite interaction network with topology statistics (nodes, edges, neighbours, path length, clustering coefficient, density).
skills.name: metabolomic-network-inference
skills.search_text: metabolomic-network-inference Use when metabolomic intensity data (rows/columns labelled with KEGG compound IDs such as 'C00042') must be converted into an inferred metabolite interaction network with topology statistics (nodes, edges, neighbours, path length, clustering coefficient, density). When the input is already a finished network edge list or adjacency matrix rather than raw metabolomic intensity data requiring Jacobian-based inference. When the goal is standard MetaboAnalyst pathway-enrichment or statistical testing without dynamic interaction modelling between metabolites. When the metabolite identifiers are not KEGG compound IDs present in both rows and columns of the dataset, as minfer() expects. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 An R-based skill that bridges MetaboAnalyst outputs and Jacobian analysis to infer dynamic metabolite interaction networks, using the MInfer package to prepare data, generate covariance matrices, compute Jacobian matrices, and visualise metabolite interaction networks. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cmpb.2025.108672
skills.summary: An R-based skill that bridges MetaboAnalyst outputs and Jacobian analysis to infer dynamic metabolite interaction networks, using the MInfer package to prepare data, generate covariance matrices, compute Jacobian matrices, and visualise metabolite interaction networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a finished network edge list or adjacency matrix rather than raw metabolomic intensity data requiring Jacobian-based inference. When the goal is standard MetaboAnalyst pathway-enrichment or statistical testing without dynamic interaction modelling between metabolites. When the metabolite identifiers are not KEGG compound IDs present in both rows and columns of the dataset, as minfer() expects.

skills.description: Use when a DaDIA.R run (XCMS 3.11.4+) has produced metabolite_intensity_table.csv and ms2_spectra.mgf and you must verify MGF parsability, required CSV columns, and DDA/DIA source tagging before MS2 spectral matching.
skills.name: metabolomic-output-format-validation
skills.search_text: metabolomic-output-format-validation Use when a DaDIA.R run (XCMS 3.11.4+) has produced metabolite_intensity_table.csv and ms2_spectra.mgf and you must verify MGF parsability, required CSV columns, and DDA/DIA source tagging before MS2 spectral matching. The raw DDA and DIA mzXML files have not yet been processed through DaDIA.R — there are no exported artifacts to validate The inputs are already a curated, annotated metabolite table (post dot-product > 0.7 annotation) rather than DaDIA.R's raw exports http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validates the two exported artifacts of a DaDIA.R run — metabolite_intensity_table.csv (merged DDA/DIA feature intensities) and ms2_spectra.mgf (MS2 spectra tagged with DDA/DIA origin) — so downstream metabolite annotation works on well-formed inputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c05022
skills.summary: Validates the two exported artifacts of a DaDIA.R run — metabolite_intensity_table.csv (merged DDA/DIA feature intensities) and ms2_spectra.mgf (MS2 spectra tagged with DDA/DIA origin) — so downstream metabolite annotation works on well-formed inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The raw DDA and DIA mzXML files have not yet been processed through DaDIA.R — there are no exported artifacts to validate The inputs are already a curated, annotated metabolite table (post dot-product > 0.7 annotation) rather than DaDIA.R's raw exports

skills.description: Use when you have metabolomic peak tables (e.g., MetaboLights MTBLS6, MTBLS583, MTBLS403, MTBLS370, MTBLS59, MTBLS656, MTBLS319, MTBLS1569, MTBLS665) and must run a specific method combination across the four processing stages to produce a processed output for performance assessment.
skills.name: metabolomic-peak-table-processing-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: metabolomic-peak-table-processing-workflow-execution Use when you have metabolomic peak tables (e.g., MetaboLights MTBLS6, MTBLS583, MTBLS403, MTBLS370, MTBLS59, MTBLS656, MTBLS319, MTBLS1569, MTBLS665) and must run a specific method combination across the four processing stages to produce a processed output for performance assessment. You only need to interpret existing Good/Fair/Poor rankings already reported (e.g., in NOREVA's Table 3) rather than run the processing stages yourself The dataset has fewer than 6 samples in one timepoint or class — criterion Cc is unsuitable, so the downstream assessment, not the execution itself, must be adapted The goal is raw-file conversion or peak picking (Proteowizard, nmrML, XCMS) rather than post-peak-table processing of an existing metabolite feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Executes candidate metabolomic peak-table processing workflows (e.g., MDI+NON+NON+[CON-AUT], HAM+LLR+NON+[SUM-LEV], KNN+NON+LOG+[VAS-LIN]) through the NOREVA R package, running the four ordered stages S1 filtering/imputation, S2 QCS correction, S3 transformation, and S4 normalization on standardized MetaboLights benchmark tables so their outputs can be scored in stage S5. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Executes candidate metabolomic peak-table processing workflows (e.g., MDI+NON+NON+[CON-AUT], HAM+LLR+NON+[SUM-LEV], KNN+NON+LOG+[VAS-LIN]) through the NOREVA R package, running the four ordered stages S1 filtering/imputation, S2 QCS correction, S3 transformation, and S4 normalization on standardized MetaboLights benchmark tables so their outputs can be scored in stage S5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to interpret existing Good/Fair/Poor rankings already reported (e.g., in NOREVA's Table 3) rather than run the processing stages yourself The dataset has fewer than 6 samples in one timepoint or class — criterion Cc is unsuitable, so the downstream assessment, not the execution itself, must be adapted The goal is raw-file conversion or peak picking (Proteowizard, nmrML, XCMS) rather than post-peak-table processing of an existing metabolite feature table

skills.description: Use when a raw or tool-generated metabolomic peak table (e.g., from MetaboLights MTBLS403, MTBLS6, MTBLS656) must be reshaped to NOREVA's unified format before running the R-based workflow scan and ranking.
skills.name: metabolomic-peak-table-standardization
skills.search_text: metabolomic-peak-table-standardization Use when a raw or tool-generated metabolomic peak table (e.g., from MetaboLights MTBLS403, MTBLS6, MTBLS656) must be reshaped to NOREVA's unified format before running the R-based workflow scan and ranking. The peak table already satisfies NOREVA's unified format (rows = samples by name, columns preserved), in which case it can be loaded directly without re-standardization You need raw-spectra feature detection/alignment rather than reshaping an existing peak table — use the upstream peak-table preparation tools (XCMS, NMRProc Flow) instead The goal is statistical analysis or biomarker discovery on an already-processed table (MetaboAnalyst, W4M territory) rather than NOREVA pre-processing workflow optimization http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Reformats a metabolomic peak table into NOREVA's unified input format — preserving rows as samples (by name) and columns as metabolites — so that the four-stage processing workflow scan (S1 filtering/imputation through S4 normalization) and S5 performance assessment can run on it. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Reformats a metabolomic peak table into NOREVA's unified input format — preserving rows as samples (by name) and columns as metabolites — so that the four-stage processing workflow scan (S1 filtering/imputation through S4 normalization) and S5 performance assessment can run on it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak table already satisfies NOREVA's unified format (rows = samples by name, columns preserved), in which case it can be loaded directly without re-standardization You need raw-spectra feature detection/alignment rather than reshaping an existing peak table — use the upstream peak-table preparation tools (XCMS, NMRProc Flow) instead The goal is statistical analysis or biomarker discovery on an already-processed table (MetaboAnalyst, W4M territory) rather than NOREVA pre-processing workflow optimization

skills.description: Use when a metabonomic SummarizedExperiment (metabo_SE) and its per-feature CV table (metabo_CV) need filtering of non-reproducible metabolic features prior to downstream MWAS or STOCSY analysis.
skills.name: metabolomic-qc-feature-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolomic-qc-feature-filtering Use when a metabonomic SummarizedExperiment (metabo_SE) and its per-feature CV table (metabo_CV) need filtering of non-reproducible metabolic features prior to downstream MWAS or STOCSY analysis. When the metabolomic matrix has not yet been paired with a per-feature CV table (metabo_CV) from an upstream CV-analysis step. When the goal is statistical association modelling (e.g. MWAS models, bootstrapping) rather than QC removal of non-reproducible features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 Filters non-reproducible metabolic features from a metabonomic dataset by applying a coefficient-of-variation (CV) threshold (CV_th = 0.30) via the MWASTools CV_filter mechanism, retaining only features with CV <= 0.30 in the SummarizedExperiment object metabo_SE. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Filters non-reproducible metabolic features from a metabonomic dataset by applying a coefficient-of-variation (CV) threshold (CV_th = 0.30) via the MWASTools CV_filter mechanism, retaining only features with CV <= 0.30 in the SummarizedExperiment object metabo_SE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the metabolomic matrix has not yet been paired with a per-feature CV table (metabo_CV) from an upstream CV-analysis step. When the goal is statistical association modelling (e.g. MWAS models, bootstrapping) rather than QC removal of non-reproducible features.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomic peak table (case-control, multiclass, or time-course) must be exhaustively scanned across all valid processing method combinations to find the study-specific optimal workflow before S5 multi-criteria assessment.
skills.name: metabolomic-workflow-combinatorial-enumeration
skills.search_text: metabolomic-workflow-combinatorial-enumeration Use when a metabolomic peak table (case-control, multiclass, or time-course) must be exhaustively scanned across all valid processing method combinations to find the study-specific optimal workflow before S5 multi-criteria assessment. The peak table already has a fixed, user-prescribed processing pipeline and no combinatorial optimization is intended — enumeration would only add hundreds-to-thousands of minutes of scanning time The dataset has fewer than 6 samples per class/timepoint (criterion Cc inapplicable) or lacks reference metabolites/spike-ins (criterion Ce/LogFC inapplicable), so the downstream S5 assessment that consumes the enumeration cannot be completed The data are not metabolomic peak tables in NOREVA's unified format and cannot be standardized (manual standardization step not yet performed) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Enumerates the full combinatorial space of metabolomic peak-table processing workflows by combining NOREVA's stage-specific methods (4 imputation, 3 QCS-correction, 2 transformation, 23 normalization) under scenario-specific applicability constraints, yielding 5,904 workflows for QCS data, 48 for IS data, and 1,968 for data with neither. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Enumerates the full combinatorial space of metabolomic peak-table processing workflows by combining NOREVA's stage-specific methods (4 imputation, 3 QCS-correction, 2 transformation, 23 normalization) under scenario-specific applicability constraints, yielding 5,904 workflows for QCS data, 48 for IS data, and 1,968 for data with neither.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak table already has a fixed, user-prescribed processing pipeline and no combinatorial optimization is intended — enumeration would only add hundreds-to-thousands of minutes of scanning time The dataset has fewer than 6 samples per class/timepoint (criterion Cc inapplicable) or lacks reference metabolites/spike-ins (criterion Ce/LogFC inapplicable), so the downstream S5 assessment that consumes the enumeration cannot be completed The data are not metabolomic peak tables in NOREVA's unified format and cannot be standardized (manual standardization step not yet performed)

skills.description: Use when multiple processed peak tables from candidate normalization/QCS/transformation workflows are available and each must be ranked study-specifically to pick the -performing workflow before downstream statistics or biomarker discovery.
skills.name: metabolomic-workflow-performance-scoring
skills.search_text: metabolomic-workflow-performance-scoring Use when multiple processed peak tables from candidate normalization/QCS/transformation workflows are available and each must be ranked study-specifically to pick the -performing workflow before downstream statistics or biomarker discovery. The dataset has fewer than 6 samples in one timepoint or class — criterion Cc is unsuitable and cannot be computed, so the full five-criteria assessment cannot be applied No reference metabolites (e.g., spike-ins / internal standards) are provided — criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied and only the four remaining criteria are usable The goal is raw-data processing (file conversion, peak picking) rather than evaluating already-processed peak tables — use upstream tools like Proteowizard or XCMS instead of this assessment stage http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 NOREVA's final assessment stage (S5) scores each candidate metabolomic processing workflow using five independent criteria (Ca/PMAD, Cb/purity, Cc/CWrel, Cd/AUC, Ce/LogFC) and classifies outcomes as Good/Fair/Poor, enabling study-specific selection of the optimal workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: NOREVA's final assessment stage (S5) scores each candidate metabolomic processing workflow using five independent criteria (Ca/PMAD, Cb/purity, Cc/CWrel, Cd/AUC, Ce/LogFC) and classifies outcomes as Good/Fair/Poor, enabling study-specific selection of the optimal workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has fewer than 6 samples in one timepoint or class — criterion Cc is unsuitable and cannot be computed, so the full five-criteria assessment cannot be applied No reference metabolites (e.g., spike-ins / internal standards) are provided — criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied and only the four remaining criteria are usable The goal is raw-data processing (file conversion, peak picking) rather than evaluating already-processed peak tables — use upstream tools like Proteowizard or XCMS instead of this assessment stage

skills.description: Use when a raw or unnormalized metabolomic peak table (case-control, multi-class, or time-course, e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS403) needs an objectively optimal combination of filtering, imputation, QCS correction, transformation, and normalization methods.
skills.name: metabolomic-workflow-scan-optimization
skills.search_text: metabolomic-workflow-scan-optimization Use when a raw or unnormalized metabolomic peak table (case-control, multi-class, or time-course, e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS403) needs an objectively optimal combination of filtering, imputation, QCS correction, transformation, and normalization methods. Datasets with fewer than 6 samples per class or timepoint, since criterion Cc is unsuitable Datasets with no reference metabolites (e.g. spike-ins) available, since criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied Peak tables whose columns are internal-standard/QCS columns the user cannot identify — normulticlassisall requires explicitly listing IS column numbers http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 An R-based NOREVA protocol that scans thousands of combinatorially generated metabolomic peak-table processing workflows (stages S1 data filtering/imputation, S2 QCS correction, S3 transformation, S4 normalization) and ranks them by multi-criteria performance assessment (S5), because the optimal workflow is dataset- and study-specific. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: An R-based NOREVA protocol that scans thousands of combinatorially generated metabolomic peak-table processing workflows (stages S1 data filtering/imputation, S2 QCS correction, S3 transformation, S4 normalization) and ranks them by multi-criteria performance assessment (S5), because the optimal workflow is dataset- and study-specific.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with fewer than 6 samples per class or timepoint, since criterion Cc is unsuitable Datasets with no reference metabolites (e.g. spike-ins) available, since criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied Peak tables whose columns are internal-standard/QCS columns the user cannot identify — normulticlassisall requires explicitly listing IS column numbers

skills.description: Use when a clinical metabolomics feature table (e.g. log2-transformed GC-TOF MS lipid abundances) still shows subject-specific variation/outliers after standard normalization, and patient metadata is available to model and readjust each metabolite signal before multivariate analyses.
skills.name: metabolomics-abundance-readjustment
skills.search_text: metabolomics-abundance-readjustment Use when a clinical metabolomics feature table (e.g. log2-transformed GC-TOF MS lipid abundances) still shows subject-specific variation/outliers after standard normalization, and patient metadata is available to model and readjust each metabolite signal before multivariate analyses. The input is already an LMM-processed (readjusted) feature matrix — re-fitting would remove biological signal rather than subject-specific variation. No patient/subject metadata is available to serve as fixed effects and no repeated-measures structure exists, so the LMM formulation cannot be specified. The task is raw MS data pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) — this skill is an additional post-processing step applied after normalization and log2 transformation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 An additional data-processing step that fits each metabolite in a log2-transformed clinical metabolomics matrix to a linear mixed-effects model (LMM), using patient metadata (e.g. Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) as fixed effects and a patient-level random intercept to readjust metabolite abundances prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA and OPLS-DA. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: An additional data-processing step that fits each metabolite in a log2-transformed clinical metabolomics matrix to a linear mixed-effects model (LMM), using patient metadata (e.g. Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) as fixed effects and a patient-level random intercept to readjust metabolite abundances prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA and OPLS-DA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an LMM-processed (readjusted) feature matrix — re-fitting would remove biological signal rather than subject-specific variation. No patient/subject metadata is available to serve as fixed effects and no repeated-measures structure exists, so the LMM formulation cannot be specified. The task is raw MS data pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) — this skill is an additional post-processing step applied after normalization and log2 transformation.

skills.description: Use when resolving metabolite identifiers across databases and an identifier maps to multiple candidate compounds from the same database, so ambiguity must be surfaced for user selection instead of silently forcing one mapping.
skills.name: metabolomics-annotation-ambiguity-flagging
skills.search_text: metabolomics-annotation-ambiguity-flagging Use when resolving metabolite identifiers across databases and an identifier maps to multiple candidate compounds from the same database, so ambiguity must be surfaced for user selection instead of silently forcing one mapping. The entity space is not small compounds (e.g., gene or protein identifiers) — MetaFetcheR covers only HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG and LIPID MAPS Every metabolite already has a complete, unambiguous cross-database identifier set with no multi-mapped candidates A single-database mapping (e.g., HMDB-only) is intended, which the paper warns can cause loss of information and mismatches http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Flags metabolite identifier entries that resolve to multiple candidate compounds from the same small-compound database (HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG, LIPID MAPS) during MetaFetcheR's queue-based resolution, rather than forcing a single mapping, and routes these ambiguous cases to the user for representative-identifier selection. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.02.28.433248
skills.summary: Flags metabolite identifier entries that resolve to multiple candidate compounds from the same small-compound database (HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG, LIPID MAPS) during MetaFetcheR's queue-based resolution, rather than forcing a single mapping, and routes these ambiguous cases to the user for representative-identifier selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The entity space is not small compounds (e.g., gene or protein identifiers) — MetaFetcheR covers only HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG and LIPID MAPS Every metabolite already has a complete, unambiguous cross-database identifier set with no multi-mapped candidates A single-database mapping (e.g., HMDB-only) is intended, which the paper warns can cause loss of information and mismatches

skills.summary: Verifies metabolite classification counts from the TurboPutative Tagger module by re-running classification on a putative-annotation table and reconciling per-origin category counts against published reference totals.

skills.summary: Quantify how many MS2 annotations each spectral library (GNPS, MoNA, MassBank EU, MSnLib) yields on a shared feature-based molecular networking run of a public dataset, then compute per-library and unique-match counts for direct benchmarking.

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics putative-annotation table needs each compound assigned a biological-origin label to prioritize metabolites and gain preliminary insight into the studied biological system.

skills.search_text: metabolomics-annotation-labeling Use when an untargeted metabolomics putative-annotation table needs each compound assigned a biological-origin label to prioritize metabolites and gain preliminary insight into the studied biological system. The goal is deduplication or merging of redundant annotation rows rather than origin labeling — use REname or RowMerger instead Scoring features by adduct probability and intensity correlations is needed — that is TPMetrics' role, not Tagger's http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Implements the Tagger module of TurboPutative, which classifies putative annotation entries from untargeted metabolomics datasets by compound origin (nutrient, drug, microbiota-dependent metabolite, or natural product/plant) by parsing reference databases and applying halogen/peptide regex classifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.952149
skills.summary: Implements the Tagger module of TurboPutative, which classifies putative annotation entries from untargeted metabolomics datasets by compound origin (nutrient, drug, microbiota-dependent metabolite, or natural product/plant) by parsing reference databases and applying halogen/peptide regex classifiers.

skills.description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of annotation pipelines (e.g., MetDNA3 vs MetDNA2) on the same metabolomics datasets, or when validating a claimed fold speedup from published runtime tables.
skills.name: metabolomics-annotation-pipeline-comparison
skills.search_text: metabolomics-annotation-pipeline-comparison Use when comparing computational efficiency of annotation pipelines (e.g., MetDNA3 vs MetDNA2) on the same metabolomics datasets, or when validating a claimed fold speedup from published runtime tables. When comparing annotation coverage, accuracy, or FDR of tools rather than computational efficiency — runtime benchmarks do not inform annotation quality claims When the goal is a head-to-head accuracy comparison involving tools like GNPS/FBMN, IIMN, or NetID on benchmark sets with chemical standards When only a single dataset is available and no per-dataset runtime table exists — the mean and fold speedup require the 12-dataset/3-sample structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of MetDNA3's recursive annotation propagation against MetDNA2 across biological metabolomics datasets, quantifying the reported >14-fold per-dataset speedup (mean 77 min vs 1082 min) using the Source Data for Fig. 2g. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of MetDNA3's recursive annotation propagation against MetDNA2 across biological metabolomics datasets, quantifying the reported >14-fold per-dataset speedup (mean 77 min vs 1082 min) using the Source Data for Fig. 2g.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing annotation coverage, accuracy, or FDR of tools rather than computational efficiency — runtime benchmarks do not inform annotation quality claims When the goal is a head-to-head accuracy comparison involving tools like GNPS/FBMN, IIMN, or NetID on benchmark sets with chemical standards When only a single dataset is available and no per-dataset runtime table exists — the mean and fold speedup require the 12-dataset/3-sample structure

skills.description: Use when you have annotation counts per MSI confidence level plus a total count of acquired/merged MS/MS spectra, and need to report annotation coverage and the unannotated residual.
skills.name: metabolomics-annotation-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: metabolomics-annotation-summary-statistics Use when you have annotation counts per MSI confidence level plus a total count of acquired/merged MS/MS spectra, and need to report annotation coverage and the unannotated residual. The goal is to assign new annotations to unannotated spectra (use SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID and NIST hybrid search for level 3 annotation) rather than to summarize coverage of existing annotations Input is raw LC-MS/MS signal data or a feature table rather than counts of merged spectra and their MSI-level annotations The annotation set includes MSI level 3 (in-silico) assignments but you intend to report only high-confidence coverage; mixing levels inflates the numerator inconsistently http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Computes the fraction of acquired MS/MS spectra covered by MSI confidence-level annotations (e.g. 753 MSI level 1+2 annotated spectra out of 3,894 merged urinary MS/MS spectra = 19.3%) and quantifies the residual unannotated fraction, exposing the size of the uncharted metabolome. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Computes the fraction of acquired MS/MS spectra covered by MSI confidence-level annotations (e.g. 753 MSI level 1+2 annotated spectra out of 3,894 merged urinary MS/MS spectra = 19.3%) and quantifies the residual unannotated fraction, exposing the size of the uncharted metabolome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to assign new annotations to unannotated spectra (use SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID and NIST hybrid search for level 3 annotation) rather than to summarize coverage of existing annotations Input is raw LC-MS/MS signal data or a feature table rather than counts of merged spectra and their MSI-level annotations The annotation set includes MSI level 3 (in-silico) assignments but you intend to report only high-confidence coverage; mixing levels inflates the numerator inconsistently

skills.description: Use when a KGMN/MetDNA2Vis unknown-annotation table is available and you must prepare MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites for GNPS MASST searches to test recurrence across public metabolomics data.
skills.name: metabolomics-annotation-table-preparation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-annotation-table-preparation Use when a KGMN/MetDNA2Vis unknown-annotation table is available and you must prepare MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites for GNPS MASST searches to test recurrence across public metabolomics data. The metabolites are known compounds already present in common MS/MS libraries — repository mining is intended for unknowns absent from spectral databases You only need the three-layer KGMN networks (KMRN, MS2 similarity network, peak correlation network) themselves rather than spectra prepared for external repository search The input is raw metabolomics data not yet processed through KGMN/MetDNA2 annotation — no unknown annotation table exists to prepare http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extracts the putatively annotated unknown metabolite list and their MS/MS spectra from KGMN/MetDNA2Vis annotation results (e.g., Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos) and reformats each spectrum (precursor m/z plus fragment peaks) for submission to GNPS MASST repository mining against MassIVE. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Extracts the putatively annotated unknown metabolite list and their MS/MS spectra from KGMN/MetDNA2Vis annotation results (e.g., Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos) and reformats each spectrum (precursor m/z plus fragment peaks) for submission to GNPS MASST repository mining against MassIVE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites are known compounds already present in common MS/MS libraries — repository mining is intended for unknowns absent from spectral databases You only need the three-layer KGMN networks (KMRN, MS2 similarity network, peak correlation network) themselves rather than spectra prepared for external repository search The input is raw metabolomics data not yet processed through KGMN/MetDNA2 annotation — no unknown annotation table exists to prepare

skills.description: Use when untargeted metabolomics peak lists (e.g., XCMS centWave output from mzML files) need curation to remove EIC artifacts, or when quantifying what fraction of detected features are artifacts.
skills.name: metabolomics-artifact-classification
skills.search_text: metabolomics-artifact-classification Use when untargeted metabolomics peak lists (e.g., XCMS centWave output from mzML files) need curation to remove EIC artifacts, or when quantifying what fraction of detected features are artifacts. Input is already a manually curated or validated feature table with trusted annotations — classification would add little and risk discarding true peaks Data are not LC/MS untargeted metabolomics profiles; PeakDetective was tailored to LC/MS methods and must be retrained per sample type You only need peak detection without curation — running XCMS alone suffices and avoids the active-learning labeling burden http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Classify XCMS-detected LC/MS peaks as artifacts or true peaks using PeakDetective's semisupervised autoencoder-plus-classifier workflow with active learning, and quantify artifact fractions in peak lists. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00764
skills.summary: Classify XCMS-detected LC/MS peaks as artifacts or true peaks using PeakDetective's semisupervised autoencoder-plus-classifier workflow with active learning, and quantify artifact fractions in peak lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a manually curated or validated feature table with trusted annotations — classification would add little and risk discarding true peaks Data are not LC/MS untargeted metabolomics profiles; PeakDetective was tailored to LC/MS methods and must be retrained per sample type You only need peak detection without curation — running XCMS alone suffices and avoids the active-learning labeling burden

skills.description: Use when evaluating a response-factor inference method for relative-abundance metabolomics where no external published competitor exists, and negative-control baselines must substitute for published-method comparison.
skills.name: metabolomics-baseline-comparator-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metabolomics-baseline-comparator-benchmarking Use when evaluating a response-factor inference method for relative-abundance metabolomics where no external published competitor exists, and negative-control baselines must substitute for published-method comparison. A published competitor method for response-factor inference exists — head-to-head comparison against that method should be used instead of negative controls The metabolomics dataset is not time-course relative-abundance GC-MS data with an associated kinetic model, so mass-balance-based inference (and its comparison to random/constant baselines) is inapplicable The evaluation target is metabolite concentration accuracy rather than response-factor accuracy — the log2-fold tolerance metric must be recomputed on inferred concentrations, not response factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A benchmarking skill for MetaboPAC response-factor inference: construct negative-control baselines (random response factors sampled uniformly from 1–1000, and a constant response factor of 500) and compare prediction accuracy against the inferred response factors at fixed error tolerances. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for MetaboPAC response-factor inference: construct negative-control baselines (random response factors sampled uniformly from 1–1000, and a constant response factor of 500) and compare prediction accuracy against the inferred response factors at fixed error tolerances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A published competitor method for response-factor inference exists — head-to-head comparison against that method should be used instead of negative controls The metabolomics dataset is not time-course relative-abundance GC-MS data with an associated kinetic model, so mass-balance-based inference (and its comparison to random/constant baselines) is inapplicable The evaluation target is metabolite concentration accuracy rather than response-factor accuracy — the log2-fold tolerance metric must be recomputed on inferred concentrations, not response factors

skills.description: Use when an uncorrected LC-MS metabolomics feature table with QC injections at fixed intervals (e.g., every 5–6 samples) shows high RSDs and scattered QC samples in PCA, and you need drift/batch correction plus visual validation.
skills.name: metabolomics-batch-correction-pca-visualization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-batch-correction-pca-visualization Use when an uncorrected LC-MS metabolomics feature table with QC injections at fixed intervals (e.g., every 5–6 samples) shows high RSDs and scattered QC samples in PCA, and you need drift/batch correction plus visual validation. The dataset has no repeated QC injections and cannot support QC-based correction — use statTarget's shiftCor_dQC with MLmethod='Combat' instead Input is already batch-corrected or you only need univariate statistics without PCA visualization The data are label-free LC-MS proteomics rather than metabolomics and the task targets proteomics-specific preprocessing (though QC-RFSC is also applicable there) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Corrects signal drift and batch effects in LC-MS metabolomics feature tables using the statTarget QC-RFSC random forest algorithm, then visualizes the impact via Pareto-scaled, glog-transformed PCA score plots comparing raw vs. corrected QC clustering and biological group separation. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Corrects signal drift and batch effects in LC-MS metabolomics feature tables using the statTarget QC-RFSC random forest algorithm, then visualizes the impact via Pareto-scaled, glog-transformed PCA score plots comparing raw vs. corrected QC clustering and biological group separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no repeated QC injections and cannot support QC-based correction — use statTarget's shiftCor_dQC with MLmethod='Combat' instead Input is already batch-corrected or you only need univariate statistics without PCA visualization The data are label-free LC-MS proteomics rather than metabolomics and the task targets proteomics-specific preprocessing (though QC-RFSC is also applicable there)

skills.description: Use when raw targeted or untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data must be checked for analytical batch effects before choosing a correction model, e.g. samples appear grouped by run order.
skills.name: metabolomics-batch-diagnostics-pca-plotting
skills.search_text: metabolomics-batch-diagnostics-pca-plotting Use when raw targeted or untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data must be checked for analytical batch effects before choosing a correction model, e.g. samples appear grouped by run order. Data have already been batch-corrected and you need to compare correction models via adjusted-R2 scoring rather than raw-data diagnostics Dataset has more than ~2000 features, where dbnorm functions are not suggested for computational speed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 An unsupervised diagnostic step from the dbnorm R package that runs PCA on raw log2-scaled metabolomics data and plots sample scores colored by analytical batch to expose across-batch signal drift. In the SKIPOGH dataset (1079 samples, 239 metabolites, 11 batches) it revealed samples clustered by batch order. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: An unsupervised diagnostic step from the dbnorm R package that runs PCA on raw log2-scaled metabolomics data and plots sample scores colored by analytical batch to expose across-batch signal drift. In the SKIPOGH dataset (1079 samples, 239 metabolites, 11 batches) it revealed samples clustered by batch order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data have already been batch-corrected and you need to compare correction models via adjusted-R2 scoring rather than raw-data diagnostics Dataset has more than ~2000 features, where dbnorm functions are not suggested for computational speed

skills.description: Use when a log2-transformed LC–MS metabolomics matrix (.csv, samples in rows, batch labels in column 1) shows batch-dependent clustering (e.g., PCA grouping by batch order) and you need to compare batch-correction models quantitatively.
skills.name: metabolomics-batch-effect-correction
skills.search_text: metabolomics-batch-effect-correction Use when a log2-transformed LC–MS metabolomics matrix (.csv, samples in rows, batch labels in column 1) shows batch-dependent clustering (e.g., PCA grouping by batch order) and you need to compare batch-correction models quantitatively. Datasets with more than ~2000 features — dbnormSCORE and Visodbnorm are explicitly suggested for fewer than 2000 variables for computational speed Input is not a batch-annotated metabolomics matrix (no batch levels in the first column) or is not yet log2-scaled, violating dbnorm's stated input requirements Goal is QC-sample-injection-based drift correction or biological differential analysis (volcano plots, MSEA) rather than statistical-model batch adjustment and model selection http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Correct drift-across-batch in large metabolomics matrices with the dbnorm R package — ber/bagging-ber, parametric and nonparametric ComBat, and lowess — then score each correction with dbnormSCORE via the maximum metabolite-vs-batch adjusted-R² (0–1) to select the best-fitting model. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Correct drift-across-batch in large metabolomics matrices with the dbnorm R package — ber/bagging-ber, parametric and nonparametric ComBat, and lowess — then score each correction with dbnormSCORE via the maximum metabolite-vs-batch adjusted-R² (0–1) to select the best-fitting model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with more than ~2000 features — dbnormSCORE and Visodbnorm are explicitly suggested for fewer than 2000 variables for computational speed Input is not a batch-annotated metabolomics matrix (no batch levels in the first column) or is not yet log2-scaled, violating dbnorm's stated input requirements Goal is QC-sample-injection-based drift correction or biological differential analysis (volcano plots, MSEA) rather than statistical-model batch adjustment and model selection

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS peak intensity matrix (e.g., XCMS/CAMERA output) with a per-sample injection order vector, but batch labels are missing or there is only one batch, and batch/drift effects must be removed.
skills.name: metabolomics-batch-effect-removal
skills.search_text: metabolomics-batch-effect-removal Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS peak intensity matrix (e.g., XCMS/CAMERA output) with a per-sample injection order vector, but batch labels are missing or there is only one batch, and batch/drift effects must be removed. Input is raw LC-MS data (.d, mzXML) rather than an XCMS/CAMERA-preprocessed peak intensity matrix — peak detection, 80%-detection filtering, and annotation must happen first Injection order metadata is unavailable, since WaveICA 2.0 uses only injection order information for batch effect removal The data already consists of only QC samples or has no injection-order-dependent structure to model http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Removes inter-batch and intra-batch (run order) effects from untargeted metabolomics peak intensity matrices without batch labels, using WaveICA 2.0: MODWT decomposition, ICA, GAM-based screening against injection order, and inverse MODWT reconstruction. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01839-7
skills.summary: Removes inter-batch and intra-batch (run order) effects from untargeted metabolomics peak intensity matrices without batch labels, using WaveICA 2.0: MODWT decomposition, ICA, GAM-based screening against injection order, and inverse MODWT reconstruction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data (.d, mzXML) rather than an XCMS/CAMERA-preprocessed peak intensity matrix — peak detection, 80%-detection filtering, and annotation must happen first Injection order metadata is unavailable, since WaveICA 2.0 uses only injection order information for batch effect removal The data already consists of only QC samples or has no injection-order-dependent structure to model

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking peak-detection/quality-filtering outputs from competing LC-MS metabolomics tools on the same public dataset, and when validating that repeated executions produce identical counts.

skills.description: Use when comparing LC-MS metabolomics feature-extraction/annotation software head-to-head on the same raw or pre-processed data with pre-optimized parameters, e.g. urine RP(+) feature counts across JPA vs MZmine 2, XCMS, MS-DIAL.
skills.name: metabolomics-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: metabolomics-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing LC-MS metabolomics feature-extraction/annotation software head-to-head on the same raw or pre-processed data with pre-optimized parameters, e.g. urine RP(+) feature counts across JPA vs MZmine 2, XCMS, MS-DIAL. The input is a single pre-existing aligned feature table and no raw mzXML data or competing tools are involved — JPA requires per-file unaligned CSV tables and this skill is specifically a multi-tool benchmark. The data are full-scan or DIA acquisitions — the README warns not to use the MS2-recognition (MR) extraction step in that case, which is part of the benchmarked JPA workflow. The goal is quantitative validation (LOD, accuracy, precision) rather than sensitivity/coverage comparison of feature and annotation counts. Benchmark the JPA joint feature-extraction and annotation workflow against MZmine 2, XCMS, and MS-DIAL on pre-optimized LC-MS data by tabulating extracted features (PP, MR, target levels) and annotated metabolites per tool. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212
skills.summary: Benchmark the JPA joint feature-extraction and annotation workflow against MZmine 2, XCMS, and MS-DIAL on pre-optimized LC-MS data by tabulating extracted features (PP, MR, target levels) and annotated metabolites per tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single pre-existing aligned feature table and no raw mzXML data or competing tools are involved — JPA requires per-file unaligned CSV tables and this skill is specifically a multi-tool benchmark. The data are full-scan or DIA acquisitions — the README warns not to use the MS2-recognition (MR) extraction step in that case, which is part of the benchmarked JPA workflow. The goal is quantitative validation (LOD, accuracy, precision) rather than sensitivity/coverage comparison of feature and annotation counts.

skills.search_text: metabolomics-benchmark-count-reproduction Use when validating or reproducing quantitative claims from a metabolomics methods paper — e.g., '105 of 177 compounds yielded CSA spectra, 25,351 total spectra' — using the authors' own public dataset and toolchain. skills.search_text: metabolomics-feature-table-matching Use when you have a RegFilter-exported scheduled precursor list (.csv) and MZmine MS1 feature tables and need to compute per-strain overlap percentages and common-feature counts between SPL and DDA precursors. Input is still raw LC-MS/MS data (mzXML) — MZmine preprocessing (mass detection, ADAP chromatogram building, Join aligner) must run first to obtain feature tables No RegFilter-generated scheduled precursor list exists — this skill quantifies SPL-vs-DDA overlap only, not general feature table alignment between unrelated experiments The goal is MS2-level comparison (spectral pairing, molecular networking) rather than MS1 precursor presence/absence matching Matches RegFilter-generated scheduled precursor list (SPL) ions against MZmine-exported DDA MS1 feature tables to quantify precursor overlap and count features shared between SPL and DDA fragmented precursors, per strain (BRA006, BRA010, BRA177). It validates that statistically selected ions for targeted fragmentation are actually observable in untargeted DDA full-scan data. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Matches RegFilter-generated scheduled precursor list (SPL) ions against MZmine-exported DDA MS1 feature tables to quantify precursor overlap and count features shared between SPL and DDA fragmented precursors, per strain (BRA006, BRA010, BRA177). It validates that statistically selected ions for targeted fragmentation are actually observable in untargeted DDA full-scan data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw LC-MS/MS data (mzXML) — MZmine preprocessing (mass detection, ADAP chromatogram building, Join aligner) must run first to obtain feature tables No RegFilter-generated scheduled precursor list exists — this skill quantifies SPL-vs-DDA overlap only, not general feature table alignment between unrelated experiments The goal is MS2-level comparison (spectral pairing, molecular networking) rather than MS1 precursor presence/absence matching

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS outputs (feature/quant tables plus MGF MS/MS spectra) must be turned into a chemical hierarchy for sample-level chemical comparison — e.g., weighted UniFrac on Qemistree trees vs Bray-Curtis on food metabolomics data.
skills.name: metabolomics-feature-table-processing
skills.search_text: metabolomics-feature-table-processing Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS outputs (feature/quant tables plus MGF MS/MS spectra) must be turned into a chemical hierarchy for sample-level chemical comparison — e.g., weighted UniFrac on Qemistree trees vs Bray-Curtis on food metabolomics data. Features lack MS/MS spectra (MS1-only): fingerprints cannot be predicted and such features are explicitly excluded, so the hierarchy will not represent the full table. Goal is high-confidence identification of individual metabolites by library matching — spectral match coverage (typically 1-20% of features) is too low to summarize the chemical content of complex samples. A chemical hierarchy already exists (e.g., GNPS cosine-score hierarchy imported as FeatureData[Molecules]) and only downstream UniFrac/ordination is needed — no table-to-tree fingerprint processing required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Converts untargeted LC-MS/MS feature tables (MZmine2 quant tables plus MGF fragmentation spectra) into predicted molecular fingerprints (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, 2936 properties) and Qemistree chemical hierarchies, enabling chemically informed sample dissimilarity (weighted UniFrac) benchmarked against tree-agnostic metrics (Bray-Curtis, CSCS). It is the data-processing backbone for tree-based metabolomics analysis in QIIME 2. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00677-3
skills.summary: Converts untargeted LC-MS/MS feature tables (MZmine2 quant tables plus MGF fragmentation spectra) into predicted molecular fingerprints (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, 2936 properties) and Qemistree chemical hierarchies, enabling chemically informed sample dissimilarity (weighted UniFrac) benchmarked against tree-agnostic metrics (Bray-Curtis, CSCS). It is the data-processing backbone for tree-based metabolomics analysis in QIIME 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features lack MS/MS spectra (MS1-only): fingerprints cannot be predicted and such features are explicitly excluded, so the hierarchy will not represent the full table. Goal is high-confidence identification of individual metabolites by library matching — spectral match coverage (typically 1-20% of features) is too low to summarize the chemical content of complex samples. A chemical hierarchy already exists (e.g., GNPS cosine-score hierarchy imported as FeatureData[Molecules]) and only downstream UniFrac/ordination is needed — no table-to-tree fingerprint processing required.

skills.search_text: metabolomics-feature-table-wrangling Use when a pcpfm/Asari feature table (preferred_drop_missing.tsv or full_feature_table.tsv) still contains missing values, infrequent features, or failed-injection samples, and you need a curated, ready-for-statistics table. The input is raw mzML or .raw data that has not yet been preprocessed by Asari into a feature table The table is already complete (no missing values, no infrequent features, no outlier samples) so re-running imputation would alter valid zeros or low signals You need de novo MS2 annotation or empirical-compound (khipu) grouping rather than table curation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 A skill for curating Asari/pcpfm feature tables (TSV) through operations like normalization, blank masking, batch correction, removal of uncommon features, outlier sample dropping (|Z|>2.5 on feature-count Z-score), and missing value imputation via per-feature minimum × interpolation_ratio (default 0.5). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: A skill for curating Asari/pcpfm feature tables (TSV) through operations like normalization, blank masking, batch correction, removal of uncommon features, outlier sample dropping (|Z|>2.5 on feature-count Z-score), and missing value imputation via per-feature minimum × interpolation_ratio (default 0.5).

skills.search_text: metabolomics-figure-s10-reproduction Use when evaluating whether artifact-aware peak reintegration improves LC/MS peak boundary definition — i.e., when comparing pre- vs post-reintegration peak-area CV distributions for feature lists scored by a trained PeakDetective classifier. When the goal is peak detection or artifact classification itself (training the autoencoder/classifier via active learning) rather than reintegration-based CV evaluation of an already-scored peak list When raw mzML files are unavailable — reintegration requires extracting EICs from raw data, so a peak-intensity table alone is insufficient When peak boundaries are already well-defined (e.g., peaks flagged as true peaks at cutoff 0.8, which are not re-integrated) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduces the PeakDetective artifact-aware peak reintegration analysis: artifact peaks from an XCMS peak list are re-integrated from raw mzML data using mean peak boundaries learned from non-artifact samples, and the resulting reduction in peak-area coefficient of variation (CV) across Datasets 1–3 is quantified and plotted as Figure S10. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00764

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (CSV/XLSX, samples as rows, metabolite columns, a group/factor column) has two or more sample groups and you need per-metabolite significance plus pairwise inter-group p-values.
skills.name: metabolomics-group-comparison-statistics
skills.search_text: metabolomics-group-comparison-statistics Use when a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (CSV/XLSX, samples as rows, metabolite columns, a group/factor column) has two or more sample groups and you need per-metabolite significance plus pairwise inter-group p-values. The dataset has not yet passed Viime's upstream treatment pipeline (error correction, imputation of MCAR/MNAR blocks, normalization, log/square-root/cube-root transformation, autoscaling/Pareto/range/vast/level scaling) — run those steps first. You need univariate two-group testing only on data with a single group — Viime applies Wilcoxon and ANOVA on data with two or more groups. You expect significance-adjusted (e.g. FDR/Bonferroni) values rather than raw p-values — the article reports Wilcoxon rank sum and Tukey post-hoc p-values only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Performs univariate and multivariate group-comparison statistics on metabolomics concentration tables: Wilcoxon rank sum tests per metabolite plus a multivariate ANOVA with an automatic post-hoc Tukey HSD test that yields pairwise p-values for every inter-group comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Performs univariate and multivariate group-comparison statistics on metabolomics concentration tables: Wilcoxon rank sum tests per metabolite plus a multivariate ANOVA with an automatic post-hoc Tukey HSD test that yields pairwise p-values for every inter-group comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has not yet passed Viime's upstream treatment pipeline (error correction, imputation of MCAR/MNAR blocks, normalization, log/square-root/cube-root transformation, autoscaling/Pareto/range/vast/level scaling) — run those steps first. You need univariate two-group testing only on data with a single group — Viime applies Wilcoxon and ANOVA on data with two or more groups. You expect significance-adjusted (e.g. FDR/Bonferroni) values rather than raw p-values — the article reports Wilcoxon rank sum and Tukey post-hoc p-values only.

skills.description: Use when a samples-by-metabolites high-dimensional feature matrix requires an M-by-M dependency matrix for eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation, and Pearson correlation is suspected of missing non-linear dependence among metabolite features.
skills.name: metabolomics-high-dimensional-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolomics-high-dimensional-correlation-analysis Use when a samples-by-metabolites high-dimensional feature matrix requires an M-by-M dependency matrix for eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation, and Pearson correlation is suspected of missing non-linear dependence among metabolite features. The goal is standard Pearson-correlation-based Meff correction (plain GWAS-style eigen-analysis), not the distance-correlation-based DisCo P-ad modification. The input is already a validated non-negative-definite DisCo matrix (disco_pad_matrix.csv) awaiting Meff estimation — proceed directly to the eigen-analysis step. The feature matrix is not high-dimensional omics-style data (samples by features) from which an M-by-M pairwise dependency matrix is required. Computes an M-by-M empirical distance-correlation (DisCo) matrix from a metabolite feature matrix using MATLAB's fastDcov, projects it onto the nearest non-negative-definite matrix with nearestSPD, and feeds the result to eigen-analysis-based Meff estimators for DisCo P-ad multiple-testing correction. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Computes an M-by-M empirical distance-correlation (DisCo) matrix from a metabolite feature matrix using MATLAB's fastDcov, projects it onto the nearest non-negative-definite matrix with nearestSPD, and feeds the result to eigen-analysis-based Meff estimators for DisCo P-ad multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standard Pearson-correlation-based Meff correction (plain GWAS-style eigen-analysis), not the distance-correlation-based DisCo P-ad modification. The input is already a validated non-negative-definite DisCo matrix (disco_pad_matrix.csv) awaiting Meff estimation — proceed directly to the eigen-analysis step. The feature matrix is not high-dimensional omics-style data (samples by features) from which an M-by-M pairwise dependency matrix is required.

skills.description: Use when targeted metabolomics (FFA/BA LC-MS) matrices contain LOD/LOQ-driven MNAR gaps and you must objectively choose an imputation method rather than substituting a single value blindly.
skills.name: metabolomics-imputation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metabolomics-imputation-benchmarking Use when targeted metabolomics (FFA/BA LC-MS) matrices contain LOD/LOQ-driven MNAR gaps and you must objectively choose an imputation method rather than substituting a single value blindly. Input is already a non-targeted GC/MS dataset where the majority of missing values are MCAR/MAR before manual missing retrieval — the article states GSimp's default left-censored settings were only evaluated for that case after missing retrieval, not as a general benchmarking target. Missing values are informative deletions from a design (e.g. QC-flagged compounds) rather than LOD/LOQ-driven left-censoring; MNAR simulation would not reflect the actual mechanism. You need runtime or convergence benchmarks for large-scale data — the article defers these to supplementary S1 Table and S2 Fig rather than the benchmarking pipeline itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark left-censored MNAR imputation methods (GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN, HM) on targeted metabolomics data by generating graded missingness, running per-method imputation wrappers, and scoring accuracy, distribution preservation, and downstream statistical sensitivity against the original complete data. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Benchmark left-censored MNAR imputation methods (GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN, HM) on targeted metabolomics data by generating graded missingness, running per-method imputation wrappers, and scoring accuracy, distribution preservation, and downstream statistical sensitivity against the original complete data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a non-targeted GC/MS dataset where the majority of missing values are MCAR/MAR before manual missing retrieval — the article states GSimp's default left-censored settings were only evaluated for that case after missing retrieval, not as a general benchmarking target. Missing values are informative deletions from a design (e.g. QC-flagged compounds) rather than LOD/LOQ-driven left-censoring; MNAR simulation would not reflect the actual mechanism. You need runtime or convergence benchmarks for large-scale data — the article defers these to supplementary S1 Table and S2 Fig rather than the benchmarking pipeline itself.
