skills.name: metabolomics-intensity-log-transformation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-intensity-log-transformation Use when raw (untransformed) metabolomics feature intensities (e.g., a compounds x samples matrix such as the 393-run, 269-metabolite ENVIRONAGE urine dataset) feed into Metanorm normalization (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC) or downstream DAM testing. The input matrix is already on a log scale (e.g., the Metanorm example rawdata values are ~16.1–16.8, consistent with log-transformed intensities) — re-transforming would double-transform and distort the drift fits The matrix contains zero or negative intensities, for which the base-e logarithm is undefined and requires prior imputation or a different handling step The data are count-based (e.g., sequencing counts) rather than continuous LC-MS/MS intensity measurements, where other variance-stabilizing transforms are appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Log-transforms (base e) raw metabolomics intensity matrices before normalization and differential abundance testing, as done in the Metanorm/ENVIRONAGE workflow so that intensity values are on an additive scale suitable for drift/batch normalization and Wilcoxon DAM testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06841
skills.summary: Log-transforms (base e) raw metabolomics intensity matrices before normalization and differential abundance testing, as done in the Metanorm/ENVIRONAGE workflow so that intensity values are on an additive scale suitable for drift/batch normalization and Wilcoxon DAM testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already on a log scale (e.g., the Metanorm example rawdata values are ~16.1–16.8, consistent with log-transformed intensities) — re-transforming would double-transform and distort the drift fits The matrix contains zero or negative intensities, for which the base-e logarithm is undefined and requires prior imputation or a different handling step The data are count-based (e.g., sequencing counts) rather than continuous LC-MS/MS intensity measurements, where other variance-stabilizing transforms are appropriate

skills.description: Use when raw metabolite-by-sample intensity data (e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) requires normalization or imputation prior to pathway scoring or classification.
skills.name: metabolomics-intensity-normalization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-intensity-normalization Use when raw metabolite-by-sample intensity data (e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) requires normalization or imputation prior to pathway scoring or classification. Input is already a pathway-level feature matrix (PDSmatrix) rather than raw metabolite intensities — use pathway transformation instead. The goal is disease classification or prognosis modeling on already-normalized data rather than preparing intensities for downstream analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Normalizes metabolomics intensity matrices using Lilikoi v2.0's lilikoi.preproc_norm, which offers standard, quantile, and median-fold normalization for metabolite-by-sample data, plus optional knn imputation via lilikoi.preproc_knn. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Normalizes metabolomics intensity matrices using Lilikoi v2.0's lilikoi.preproc_norm, which offers standard, quantile, and median-fold normalization for metabolite-by-sample data, plus optional knn imputation via lilikoi.preproc_knn.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway-level feature matrix (PDSmatrix) rather than raw metabolite intensities — use pathway transformation instead. The goal is disease classification or prognosis modeling on already-normalized data rather than preparing intensities for downstream analysis.

skills.description: Use when raw targeted or untargeted feature tables contain missing intensity values and non-normal, heteroscedastic intensities that must be transformed before running t-tests, fold-change, ANOVA, or regression in GetFeatistics.
skills.name: metabolomics-intensity-transformation-and-scaling
skills.search_text: metabolomics-intensity-transformation-and-scaling Use when raw targeted or untargeted feature tables contain missing intensity values and non-normal, heteroscedastic intensities that must be transformed before running t-tests, fold-change, ANOVA, or regression in GetFeatistics. Input is already a processed feature table that has been filtered against pooled QC criteria and normalized — re-applying transf_data would double-transform intensities. Raw vendor MS files that still need feature extraction with XCMS or patRoon — this skill operates on extracted feature tables, not chromatograms. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Prepares metabolomics intensity matrices for univariate statistics by replacing missing values, log-transforming raw feature intensities, and applying pareto scaling, as implemented in the GetFeatistics transf_data function. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Prepares metabolomics intensity matrices for univariate statistics by replacing missing values, log-transforming raw feature intensities, and applying pareto scaling, as implemented in the GetFeatistics transf_data function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table that has been filtered against pooled QC criteria and normalized — re-applying transf_data would double-transform intensities. Raw vendor MS files that still need feature extraction with XCMS or patRoon — this skill operates on extracted feature tables, not chromatograms.

skills.description: Use when pipeline stages (Asari feature tables → khipu pre-annotation → MS1/MS2 annotation) must persist intermediate results in an interoperable, JSON-compatible data model such as empCpd.json or experiment.json.
skills.name: metabolomics-json-data-serialization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-json-data-serialization Use when pipeline stages (Asari feature tables → khipu pre-annotation → MS1/MS2 annotation) must persist intermediate results in an interoperable, JSON-compatible data model such as empCpd.json or experiment.json. Input is already a fully annotated, pipeline-issued JSON artifact (e.g. an existing empCpd.json) that only needs downstream statistical analysis rather than re-serialization. The target downstream tool requires tabular formats rather than the JSON-compatible MetDataModel structures (pcpfm also emits standardized .txt feature tables for that case). The data model must deviate from the minimal MetDataModel core classes; internal structures are explicitly not meant to be final and interoperability depends on adhering to the core concepts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Serializes metabolomics processing artifacts (empirical compounds, feature tables, experiments) into JSON using the MetDataModel data models, so that empCpds, annotations, and experiment state persist as chainable, interoperable JSON files between pcpfm pipeline steps. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: Serializes metabolomics processing artifacts (empirical compounds, feature tables, experiments) into JSON using the MetDataModel data models, so that empCpds, annotations, and experiment state persist as chainable, interoperable JSON files between pcpfm pipeline steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fully annotated, pipeline-issued JSON artifact (e.g. an existing empCpd.json) that only needs downstream statistical analysis rather than re-serialization. The target downstream tool requires tabular formats rather than the JSON-compatible MetDataModel structures (pcpfm also emits standardized .txt feature tables for that case). The data model must deviate from the minimal MetDataModel core classes; internal structures are explicitly not meant to be final and interoperability depends on adhering to the core concepts.

skills.description: Use when you have large-scale population NMR metabolomics profiles (e.g., UK Biobank plasma NMR panels with ~249 metabolite features) and need a pre-trained foundation model for downstream multi-disease prediction or risk stratification.
skills.name: metabolomics-language-model-pretraining
skills.search_text: metabolomics-language-model-pretraining Use when you have large-scale population NMR metabolomics profiles (e.g., UK Biobank plasma NMR panels with ~249 metabolite features) and need a pre-trained foundation model for downstream multi-disease prediction or risk stratification. Input is not NMR-platform plasma metabolomics (e.g., mass-spectrometry metabolomics) — the article notes NMR-based metabolomics may miss metabolites detectable by other analytical methods Input features are not the 249 metabolite columns expected by the pretrained asset (e.g., a generic feature table from a different cohort/platform) The goal is single-disease clinical risk scoring with validated equations (e.g., ASCVD) rather than metabolomics-based multi-disease prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Pre-train a transformer-based metabolomic language model (MetaboLM) on NMR plasma metabolomics data from 83,744 relatively healthy UK Biobank participants to capture normative metabolite expression and interaction patterns, then fine-tune the checkpoint on chronic-disease prediction tasks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66163-3
skills.summary: Pre-train a transformer-based metabolomic language model (MetaboLM) on NMR plasma metabolomics data from 83,744 relatively healthy UK Biobank participants to capture normative metabolite expression and interaction patterns, then fine-tune the checkpoint on chronic-disease prediction tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not NMR-platform plasma metabolomics (e.g., mass-spectrometry metabolomics) — the article notes NMR-based metabolomics may miss metabolites detectable by other analytical methods Input features are not the 249 metabolite columns expected by the pretrained asset (e.g., a generic feature table from a different cohort/platform) The goal is single-disease clinical risk scoring with validated equations (e.g., ASCVD) rather than metabolomics-based multi-disease prediction

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics dataset (e.g. a MetaboLights accession such as MTBLS1) has been loaded and preprocessed in an R/SummarizedExperiment container and per-metabolite association testing (linear models, statistical analysis) is the next analytical step.
skills.name: metabolomics-linear-model-statistics
skills.search_text: metabolomics-linear-model-statistics Use when a metabolomics dataset (e.g. a MetaboLights accession such as MTBLS1) has been loaded and preprocessed in an R/SummarizedExperiment container and per-metabolite association testing (linear models, statistical analysis) is the next analytical step. Input is raw instrument data (e.g. unprocessed vendor files) — maplet expects data to first be loaded, annotated and preprocessed into the SummarizedExperiment container before statistics are applied The analysis is not in R (e.g. a Python/Scikit-learn workflow) — maplet is an R package built on the Bioconductor SummarizedExperiment structure Only a single descriptive summary is needed with no statistical testing — maplet's value is in recording fitted models and parameters, which is overhead for one-off summaries http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits linear models and other statistical tests on metabolomics feature tables using maplet's R functions, embedding each fitted model, its parameters and results into the SummarizedExperiment pipeline container so every statistical step is retraced and reproducible. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab741
skills.summary: Fits linear models and other statistical tests on metabolomics feature tables using maplet's R functions, embedding each fitted model, its parameters and results into the SummarizedExperiment pipeline container so every statistical step is retraced and reproducible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw instrument data (e.g. unprocessed vendor files) — maplet expects data to first be loaded, annotated and preprocessed into the SummarizedExperiment container before statistics are applied The analysis is not in R (e.g. a Python/Scikit-learn workflow) — maplet is an R package built on the Bioconductor SummarizedExperiment structure Only a single descriptive summary is needed with no statistical testing — maplet's value is in recording fitted models and parameters, which is overhead for one-off summaries

skills.description: Use when a plasma/serum NMR metabolomics matrix contains zero values (below detection limit) that must be shifted, log-transformed, and z-scaled per cohort before survival or association modeling.
skills.name: metabolomics-log-transformation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-log-transformation Use when a plasma/serum NMR metabolomics matrix contains zero values (below detection limit) that must be shifted, log-transformed, and z-scaled per cohort before survival or association modeling. The goal is a clinically deployable score in absolute concentration units — the article notes the per-cohort scaled score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic' The biomarker matrix contains no zero/below-detection-limit values and is already on a comparable scale across cohorts The downstream analysis requires raw concentration units rather than per-study standardized values http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Cohort-level preprocessing of Nightingale Health NMR metabolic biomarker matrices: shift below-detection-limit zeros by +1, log-transform, and scale to standard deviation units separately per study, yielding the analysis-ready biomarker matrix for Cox proportional hazards modeling. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: Cohort-level preprocessing of Nightingale Health NMR metabolic biomarker matrices: shift below-detection-limit zeros by +1, log-transform, and scale to standard deviation units separately per study, yielding the analysis-ready biomarker matrix for Cox proportional hazards modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a clinically deployable score in absolute concentration units — the article notes the per-cohort scaled score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic' The biomarker matrix contains no zero/below-detection-limit values and is already on a comparable scale across cohorts The downstream analysis requires raw concentration units rather than per-study standardized values

skills.description: Use when preparing targeted LC/MS or GC/MS metabolomics matrices (e.g., real_data.csv, targeted_data.csv) with non-normal variable distributions and missing values, before running GS_impute or comparable imputation methods.
skills.name: metabolomics-log-transformation-scaling
skills.search_text: metabolomics-log-transformation-scaling Use when preparing targeted LC/MS or GC/MS metabolomics matrices (e.g., real_data.csv, targeted_data.csv) with non-normal variable distributions and missing values, before running GS_impute or comparable imputation methods. When variables are already approximately normal on the raw scale, log-transformation (applied 'for non-normal data') may be unnecessary and could distort the distribution. When the goal is imputation of right-censored missing values, the pipeline should use 'rsym' initialization with an informative lower truncation point instead of the QRILC-initialized left-censored setup. When the data are not a metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., already a feature table or sample metadata), scaling/recovery semantics of the wrapper do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Pre-processing pipeline for targeted metabolomics data prior to GSimp imputation: log-transformation of non-normal data, QRILC initialization of missing values, centralization/scaling for elastic-net prediction, followed by scaling and exponential recovery of the imputed matrix. It is wrapped in the pre_processing_GS_wrapper function for one-step processing and imputation. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Pre-processing pipeline for targeted metabolomics data prior to GSimp imputation: log-transformation of non-normal data, QRILC initialization of missing values, centralization/scaling for elastic-net prediction, followed by scaling and exponential recovery of the imputed matrix. It is wrapped in the pre_processing_GS_wrapper function for one-step processing and imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When variables are already approximately normal on the raw scale, log-transformation (applied 'for non-normal data') may be unnecessary and could distort the distribution. When the goal is imputation of right-censored missing values, the pipeline should use 'rsym' initialization with an informative lower truncation point instead of the QRILC-initialized left-censored setup. When the data are not a metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., already a feature table or sample metadata), scaling/recovery semantics of the wrapper do not apply.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics analysis step needs its input read from or written to CSV as a metabolite x sample matrix — e.g. before lilikoi.preproc_norm/preproc_knn or after producing normalized/imputed tables.
skills.name: metabolomics-matrix-csv-io
skills.search_text: metabolomics-matrix-csv-io Use when a metabolomics analysis step needs its input read from or written to CSV as a metabolite x sample matrix — e.g. before lilikoi.preproc_norm/preproc_knn or after producing normalized/imputed tables. The data is already an in-memory R matrix/data.frame from a prior Lilikoi step and only needs to be passed directly to the next module — re-reading CSV adds no value. The file is raw mass-spectrometry output (e.g. mzML, NetCDF) rather than a pre-tabulated metabolite x sample CSV; Lilikoi v2.0's CSV I/O does not parse spectral files. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Load and round-trip metabolite-by-sample intensity matrices to/from CSV within the Lilikoi v2.0 R environment, using lilikoi.Loaddata to split a plasma_breast_cancer.csv-style file into a dataSet (metabolite rows, sample columns) and Metadata (labels/covariates), so downstream normalization, imputation, and pathway modules receive a consistent matrix structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Load and round-trip metabolite-by-sample intensity matrices to/from CSV within the Lilikoi v2.0 R environment, using lilikoi.Loaddata to split a plasma_breast_cancer.csv-style file into a dataSet (metabolite rows, sample columns) and Metadata (labels/covariates), so downstream normalization, imputation, and pathway modules receive a consistent matrix structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is already an in-memory R matrix/data.frame from a prior Lilikoi step and only needs to be passed directly to the next module — re-reading CSV adds no value. The file is raw mass-spectrometry output (e.g. mzML, NetCDF) rather than a pre-tabulated metabolite x sample CSV; Lilikoi v2.0's CSV I/O does not parse spectral files.

skills.description: Use when a log-transformed, missing-value-imputed metabolomics peak-intensity matrix (featuredata format) needs sample-wise scaling normalization, or when comparing sum/median/mean/reference scaling variants before downstream differential or classification analysis.
skills.name: metabolomics-matrix-normalization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-matrix-normalization Use when a log-transformed, missing-value-imputed metabolomics peak-intensity matrix (featuredata format) needs sample-wise scaling normalization, or when comparing sum/median/mean/reference scaling variants before downstream differential or classification analysis. The data are raw and not yet log-transformed and imputed — apply LogTransform and MissingValues first, since the package workflow requires an analysis-ready matrix The unwanted variation is driven by batch/matrix effects or QC drift better addressed by the package's other functions (NormQcmets using internal/external standards, or NormQcsamples QC-RLSC signal correction) rather than simple per-sample scaling A combined sequential normalization is needed — use NormCombined instead of a single scaling method http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Apply scaling normalization to a metabolomics featuredata matrix (metabolites in columns, unique sample names as rows) using the NormalizeMets package's NormScaling function, which offers sum, median, mean, and reference-vector scaling. Preprocessing via LogTransform(zerotona=TRUE) and MissingValues(method="knn") is required first to obtain an analysis-ready matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Apply scaling normalization to a metabolomics featuredata matrix (metabolites in columns, unique sample names as rows) using the NormalizeMets package's NormScaling function, which offers sum, median, mean, and reference-vector scaling. Preprocessing via LogTransform(zerotona=TRUE) and MissingValues(method="knn") is required first to obtain an analysis-ready matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw and not yet log-transformed and imputed — apply LogTransform and MissingValues first, since the package workflow requires an analysis-ready matrix The unwanted variation is driven by batch/matrix effects or QC drift better addressed by the package's other functions (NormQcmets using internal/external standards, or NormQcsamples QC-RLSC signal correction) rather than simple per-sample scaling A combined sequential normalization is needed — use NormCombined instead of a single scaling method

skills.description: Use when metabolomics studies report only overall statistical parameters (P-value, fold-change, study size n) without raw data or standard deviations, and per-compound combined P-values are needed for meta-analysis.
skills.name: metabolomics-meta-analysis-pvalue-aggregation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-meta-analysis-pvalue-aggregation Use when metabolomics studies report only overall statistical parameters (P-value, fold-change, study size n) without raw data or standard deviations, and per-compound combined P-values are needed for meta-analysis. Raw data or per-study standard deviations/variances are available — then standard inverse-variance meta-analysis methods are appropriate instead. Only qualitative trend labels (up/down-regulation) are available with no P-values — use amanida's vote-counting (amanida_vote) rather than weighted P-value combination. Studies report effect sizes with full statistical detail beyond P-value and fold-change. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Combine per-study P-values into a single combined P-value per compound in metabolomics meta-analysis using a weighted Fisher's method with non-integral weights (via a gamma distribution) proportional to study size (n), applicable when only overall P-values and fold-changes are reported. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab591
skills.summary: Combine per-study P-values into a single combined P-value per compound in metabolomics meta-analysis using a weighted Fisher's method with non-integral weights (via a gamma distribution) proportional to study size (n), applicable when only overall P-values and fold-changes are reported.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw data or per-study standard deviations/variances are available — then standard inverse-variance meta-analysis methods are appropriate instead. Only qualitative trend labels (up/down-regulation) are available with no P-values — use amanida's vote-counting (amanida_vote) rather than weighted P-value combination. Studies report effect sizes with full statistical detail beyond P-value and fold-change.

skills.description: Use when preparing spectral metadata records (e.g. LC-MS/MS spectra from a urine analytical matrix) for import into PeakForest, where users must supply completely-cleaned data from an Excel-like template.
skills.name: metabolomics-metadata-curation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-metadata-curation Use when preparing spectral metadata records (e.g. LC-MS/MS spectra from a urine analytical matrix) for import into PeakForest, where users must supply completely-cleaned data from an Excel-like template. You need data clean-up, extraction, or processing of raw spectral files — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data Metadata is incomplete or noisy and cannot be fully cleaned before import, since PeakForest requires completely-cleaned data and offers no clean-up tools The task is browsing/querying existing spectra (use PeakForest's filter/search Web service with column characteristics or AND/OR logic instead of re-curating records) http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Curates and validates metabolite spectral metadata (compound metadata, MS-MS spectral metadata, biological-matrix annotations) for ingestion into the PeakForest database, which stores metadata about raw data rather than the raw spectra themselves. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
skills.summary: Curates and validates metabolite spectral metadata (compound metadata, MS-MS spectral metadata, biological-matrix annotations) for ingestion into the PeakForest database, which stores metadata about raw data rather than the raw spectra themselves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need data clean-up, extraction, or processing of raw spectral files — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data Metadata is incomplete or noisy and cannot be fully cleaned before import, since PeakForest requires completely-cleaned data and offers no clean-up tools The task is browsing/querying existing spectra (use PeakForest's filter/search Web service with column characteristics or AND/OR logic instead of re-curating records)

skills.search_text: metabolomics-metadata-parsing Use when raw inputs are a metabolomics study's processed data matrix plus repository metadata (MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench accession) that must be converted into a SummarizedExperiment before running maplet pipelines. skills.summary: Parse metabolomics repository metadata (from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench) and assemble a processed intensity matrix together with structured sample and metabolite annotations into a SummarizedExperiment container, the central data structure maplet pipelines operate on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already stored in a SummarizedExperiment container with populated rowData/colData — maplet pipelines can proceed directly without re-loading from the repository. Only a single committed, untagged version of maplet is available — commits without a release tag are not guaranteed to be stable, so repository loader behavior may not match v1.2.1.

skills.search_text: metabolomics-metadata-quality-checking Use when you have downloaded JSON project documents from the PoDP Zenodo archive and need to verify, per project, that each document conforms to the community-defined project format before downstream data mining or linking analysis. The input is raw metabolomics or genomics data (mzML, FASTA, genome accessions) rather than a curated PoDP project JSON document — the PoDP 'does not store any metabolomics or genomics datasets' itself You need to validate submitted data against MassIVE or MetaboLights, not against the PoDP project schema — this skill only checks the paired-data-form project JSON format The goal is content/semantic quality of free-text 'Other' fields, which by design are not machine-readable and cannot be schema-checked http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Validates PoDP paired-omics project documents — JSON files archived monthly to Zenodo by the paired-data-form platform — against the published JSON schema at app/public/schema.json in the iomega/paired-data-form repository, flagging structural or field-constraint violations per project. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00724-z

skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-data-handling Use when a metabolomics or lipidomics feature table contains widespread missing intensities and the analysis must decide, per feature, whether gaps reflect measurement dropout to impute or genuine absence to zero-fill — e.g. heterogeneous datasets mixing endogenous metabolites and xenobiotics. skills.summary: A QComics-derived skill for distinguishing missing values (imputable signal dropout) from truly absent metabolites (genuine real zeros) in MS-based metabolomics data, so that appropriate statistical treatment preserves biological information rather than discarding it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a clean feature table with no missing or zero intensity entries — there is nothing to classify The dataset is not MS-based metabolomics (e.g. transcriptomics without analogous intensity-missingness semantics) — QComics was initially designed for MS-based metabolomics, though the authors note it may extend to other omics/MS data You need a fully automated, scriptable batch QC pipeline — QComics runs as a Shiny app (QComics::run_app()) and is intended for interactive use without advanced programming skills

skills.description: Use when a targeted metabolomics data matrix (e.g., LC/MS FFA/BA data) contains left-censored MNAR missing values caused by LOD/LOQ and a complete matrix is needed before PLS-DA or other analyses.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-data-preprocessing Use when a targeted metabolomics data matrix (e.g., LC/MS FFA/BA data) contains left-censored MNAR missing values caused by LOD/LOQ and a complete matrix is needed before PLS-DA or other analyses. The input matrix has no missing values — the pre-processing/Gibbs chain is unnecessary and QRILC initialization would fabricate nothing meaningful Missingness is MCAR/MAR (e.g., non-targeted GC/MS data before missing retrieval) and left-censored truncation hi='min' is inappropriate, unless non-informative bounds (+Inf/-Inf) are deliberately supplied Missing values are right-censored rather than left-censored — the 'rsym' initialization path exists, but the default lo=-Inf, hi='min' bounds target left-censoring http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A left-censored missing value imputation workflow for targeted metabolomics that embeds a glmnet elastic net prediction model in an iterative Gibbs sampler (GSimp), preceded by log-transformation, QRILC initialization, and scaling, and followed by scaling/exponential recovery. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: A left-censored missing value imputation workflow for targeted metabolomics that embeds a glmnet elastic net prediction model in an iterative Gibbs sampler (GSimp), preceded by log-transformation, QRILC initialization, and scaling, and followed by scaling/exponential recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix has no missing values — the pre-processing/Gibbs chain is unnecessary and QRILC initialization would fabricate nothing meaningful Missingness is MCAR/MAR (e.g., non-targeted GC/MS data before missing retrieval) and left-censored truncation hi='min' is inappropriate, unless non-informative bounds (+Inf/-Inf) are deliberately supplied Missing values are right-censored rather than left-censored — the 'rsym' initialization path exists, but the default lo=-Inf, hi='min' bounds target left-censoring

skills.description: Use when evaluating the stability of a pathway ranking method on metabolomics peak data where missing peaks and noise are prevalent, and you need a quantitative robustness comparison against alternative methods.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-feature-subsampling
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-feature-subsampling Use when evaluating the stability of a pathway ranking method on metabolomics peak data where missing peaks and noise are prevalent, and you need a quantitative robustness comparison against alternative methods. Input data has no missing features and the question is about pathway ranking accuracy rather than robustness to missingness — full-data ranking alone suffices. Peak features lack compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs), since unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis and the subsampling comparison would not be meaningful. The goal is transcriptomics/proteomics pathway ranking with gene-level databases (UniProt/ENSEMBL); this skill targets metabolomics peak data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Benchmark strategy that quantifies how robust pathway ranking methods (mPLAGE, ORA, GSEA) are when a large share of metabolomic peak features is randomly removed, by comparing subsampled rankings against full-data reference rankings using precision, recall, and F1 over hundreds of repetitions. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Benchmark strategy that quantifies how robust pathway ranking methods (mPLAGE, ORA, GSEA) are when a large share of metabolomic peak features is randomly removed, by comparing subsampled rankings against full-data reference rankings using precision, recall, and F1 over hundreds of repetitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has no missing features and the question is about pathway ranking accuracy rather than robustness to missingness — full-data ranking alone suffices. Peak features lack compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs), since unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis and the subsampling comparison would not be meaningful. The goal is transcriptomics/proteomics pathway ranking with gene-level databases (UniProt/ENSEMBL); this skill targets metabolomics peak data.

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset (tab-delimited peak areas with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) contains NA values or samples flagged as statistical outliers in QC samples, and downstream calculations must exclude them.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-and-outlier-exclusion
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-and-outlier-exclusion Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset (tab-delimited peak areas with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) contains NA values or samples flagged as statistical outliers in QC samples, and downstream calculations must exclude them. Input is not peak-integrated targeted metabolomics data (e.g. already a processed feature table from untargeted tools like OpenMS or MZmine) — mzQuality expects vendor-integrated peak areas from dMRM/polarity-switching LC-MS. A compound is entirely absent from LQC and SQC samples — mzQuality assumes it is not present and does not report it, so exclusion logic should not be applied to it. The goal is de novo statistical outlier detection on raw peak areas without QC sample context — the Rosner Test in mzQuality operates on QC samples specifically, not arbitrary study samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Excludes statistical outliers flagged by the Rosner test on QC samples and treats NA values as absent data points before downstream calculations in mzQuality-based targeted metabolomics QC, so that unreliable samples and missing signals do not bias metrics such as RSDQC and batch correction. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Excludes statistical outliers flagged by the Rosner test on QC samples and treats NA values as absent data points before downstream calculations in mzQuality-based targeted metabolomics QC, so that unreliable samples and missing signals do not bias metrics such as RSDQC and batch correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not peak-integrated targeted metabolomics data (e.g. already a processed feature table from untargeted tools like OpenMS or MZmine) — mzQuality expects vendor-integrated peak areas from dMRM/polarity-switching LC-MS. A compound is entirely absent from LQC and SQC samples — mzQuality assumes it is not present and does not report it, so exclusion logic should not be applied to it. The goal is de novo statistical outlier detection on raw peak areas without QC sample context — the Rosner Test in mzQuality operates on QC samples specifically, not arbitrary study samples.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing heterogeneous metabolomics/xenobiotics feature-intensity tables where some variables show high missingness and you must decide per variable whether missingness means absence (zero) or data loss, and filter variables excessively missing across every study group.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-filtering
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-filtering Use when preprocessing heterogeneous metabolomics/xenobiotics feature-intensity tables where some variables show high missingness and you must decide per variable whether missingness means absence (zero) or data loss, and filter variables excessively missing across every study group. The dataset is untargeted MS data without pooled QC samples or study-group structure, since thresholds are computed per study group Missingness has already been resolved (features categorized as absent vs missing and filtered), so re-applying the 20%/70% rules would double-filter The goal is general QC (signal drift, carryover, outlier removal) rather than specifically missing-data handling — use the full QComics sequential workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 QComics-based missing-data handling for targeted metabolomics that distinguishes truly absent data (features with >70% missingness treated as real zeros) from genuinely missing values, and removes variables whose missing rate exceeds 20% in all study groups before imputing the remainder. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: QComics-based missing-data handling for targeted metabolomics that distinguishes truly absent data (features with >70% missingness treated as real zeros) from genuinely missing values, and removes variables whose missing rate exceeds 20% in all study groups before imputing the remainder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is untargeted MS data without pooled QC samples or study-group structure, since thresholds are computed per study group Missingness has already been resolved (features categorized as absent vs missing and filtered), so re-applying the 20%/70% rules would double-filter The goal is general QC (signal drift, carryover, outlier removal) rather than specifically missing-data handling — use the full QComics sequential workflow instead

skills.description: Use when raw metabolomics peak-intensity tables (e.g., TEDDY ST001386/ST001636 from Metabolomics Workbench) contain missing values and must be made complete before building DNEA partial correlation networks or comparing against marginal-correlation tools like MetaBox2.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-filtering-and-imputation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-filtering-and-imputation Use when raw metabolomics peak-intensity tables (e.g., TEDDY ST001386/ST001636 from Metabolomics Workbench) contain missing values and must be made complete before building DNEA partial correlation networks or comparing against marginal-correlation tools like MetaBox2. Data has already been normalized/log-transformed by another pipeline — re-imputing median values on transformed data is not the paper's recipe (imputation is done on raw peak intensities before DNEA's own log-transform and auto-scaling) The analysis is pathway enrichment (e.g., FELLA/KEGG mapping) rather than network construction — missing-value handling does not address the KEGG annotation bottleneck (only 19 of 174 TEDDY metabolites were mappable) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Pre-processing step in the DNEA metabolomics workflow that drops metabolites missing in more than 30% of samples and median-imputes the remaining missing values, yielding a complete peak-intensity matrix suitable for GLASSO-based partial correlation network estimation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Pre-processing step in the DNEA metabolomics workflow that drops metabolites missing in more than 30% of samples and median-imputes the remaining missing values, yielding a complete peak-intensity matrix suitable for GLASSO-based partial correlation network estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has already been normalized/log-transformed by another pipeline — re-imputing median values on transformed data is not the paper's recipe (imputation is done on raw peak intensities before DNEA's own log-transform and auto-scaling) The analysis is pathway enrichment (e.g., FELLA/KEGG mapping) rather than network construction — missing-value handling does not address the KEGG annotation bottleneck (only 19 of 174 TEDDY metabolites were mappable)

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) contains missing values that must be filled before downstream statistics such as ANOVA, PLS-DA, or random forest classification.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-imputation Use when a metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) contains missing values that must be filled before downstream statistics such as ANOVA, PLS-DA, or random forest classification. The table has no missing values — running imputation would alter complete data unnecessarily Features have not yet passed upstream QC (e.g. Blank Feature Filtering, Threshold Based Flags, CV Flags) — the SECIMTools workflow places filtering and diagnostics before imputation The goal is peak picking or feature identification rather than post-preprocessing gap filling — that is handled by Galaxy-M or Workflow4Metabolomics upstream http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fills missing entries in wide-format metabolomics feature tables using the SECIMTools Imputation tool, which substitutes the group mean, group median, or K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) estimates, and emits a flag column marking imputed features per the SECIMTools flag-file convention. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Fills missing entries in wide-format metabolomics feature tables using the SECIMTools Imputation tool, which substitutes the group mean, group median, or K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) estimates, and emits a flag column marking imputed features per the SECIMTools flag-file convention.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The table has no missing values — running imputation would alter complete data unnecessarily Features have not yet passed upstream QC (e.g. Blank Feature Filtering, Threshold Based Flags, CV Flags) — the SECIMTools workflow places filtering and diagnostics before imputation The goal is peak picking or feature identification rather than post-preprocessing gap filling — that is handled by Galaxy-M or Workflow4Metabolomics upstream

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC/MS metabolomics data matrix contains left-censored missing values caused by LOD/LOQ (MNAR) and imputation quality must be evaluated before univariate or multivariate analysis such as PLS-DA.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-imputation Use when a targeted LC/MS metabolomics data matrix contains left-censored missing values caused by LOD/LOQ (MNAR) and imputation quality must be evaluated before univariate or multivariate analysis such as PLS-DA. Missing values are mostly MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored LOD/LOQ — the authors state that non-informative bounds (+Inf/-Inf) would be needed, i.e., GSimp's default left-censored setup is the wrong choice The dataset is a non-targeted GC/MS profile with heavy missingness before manual missing retrieval — the authors recommend missing retrieval from raw spectral data first, and note the majority of such missing values are MCAR/MAR The task is feature selection or peak annotation rather than filling a missing-value matrix in an existing metabolomics sample x variable table http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Iterative Gibbs-sampler based imputation (GSimp) of left-censored (MNAR) missing values in MS-based targeted metabolomics matrices, benchmarked against QRILC and kNN-TN on imputation accuracy, distribution preservation, and downstream statistical sensitivity. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Iterative Gibbs-sampler based imputation (GSimp) of left-censored (MNAR) missing values in MS-based targeted metabolomics matrices, benchmarked against QRILC and kNN-TN on imputation accuracy, distribution preservation, and downstream statistical sensitivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Missing values are mostly MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored LOD/LOQ — the authors state that non-informative bounds (+Inf/-Inf) would be needed, i.e., GSimp's default left-censored setup is the wrong choice The dataset is a non-targeted GC/MS profile with heavy missingness before manual missing retrieval — the authors recommend missing retrieval from raw spectral data first, and note the majority of such missing values are MCAR/MAR The task is feature selection or peak annotation rather than filling a missing-value matrix in an existing metabolomics sample x variable table

skills.description: Use when a metabolite abundance matrix has missing values generated by MNAR (metabolite below the LOD) combined with MAR dropout, and imputation quality must preserve both RMSE accuracy and downstream significance-testing metabolite lists.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-imputation Use when a metabolite abundance matrix has missing values generated by MNAR (metabolite below the LOD) combined with MAR dropout, and imputation quality must preserve both RMSE accuracy and downstream significance-testing metabolite lists. Missingness is purely MAR/MCAR with no limit-of-detection truncation — the truncated-normal standardization step of KNN-TN offers no advantage, and KNN-CR, KNN-EU or mean imputation suffice. A metabolite's sample mean lies far above the LOD (> 3 SD away) or missingness below the LOD is excessive — Newton-Raphon truncated-normal estimation may fail to converge or yield unstable, high-variance RMSE for that metabolite. Metabolite distributions are strongly non-normal and cannot be log-transformed to approximate normality — the normality assumption underlying the truncated mean and variance estimation is a stated limitation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A nearest-neighbor imputation skill for metabolomics matrices in which missing values arise from both MAR technical dropout and MNAR censoring at the limit of detection (LOD); it centers on KNN-TN, which standardizes metabolites using truncated-normal maximum-likelihood means and SDs (LOD as the truncation point) before correlation-based KNN imputation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: A nearest-neighbor imputation skill for metabolomics matrices in which missing values arise from both MAR technical dropout and MNAR censoring at the limit of detection (LOD); it centers on KNN-TN, which standardizes metabolites using truncated-normal maximum-likelihood means and SDs (LOD as the truncation point) before correlation-based KNN imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Missingness is purely MAR/MCAR with no limit-of-detection truncation — the truncated-normal standardization step of KNN-TN offers no advantage, and KNN-CR, KNN-EU or mean imputation suffice. A metabolite's sample mean lies far above the LOD (> 3 SD away) or missingness below the LOD is excessive — Newton-Raphon truncated-normal estimation may fail to converge or yield unstable, high-variance RMSE for that metabolite. Metabolite distributions are strongly non-normal and cannot be log-transformed to approximate normality — the normality assumption underlying the truncated mean and variance estimation is a stated limitation.

skills.description: Use when a feature count matrix destined for RALPS normalization contains missing values, or when stress-testing normalization robustness by randomly replacing matrix values with the 1000-count minimum.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-masking
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-masking Use when a feature count matrix destined for RALPS normalization contains missing values, or when stress-testing normalization robustness by randomly replacing matrix values with the 1000-count minimum. The input matrix is complete (no missing values) and the task is batch-effect harmonization only, so threshold replacement/masking adds nothing on its own Missing values require feature-aware or model-based imputation rather than RALPS's flat 1000-count minimum replacement True low-abundance signals below 1000 counts must be preserved after normalization instead of being zero-masked http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Missing-value handling for RALPS normalization of multi-batch untargeted metabolomics matrices: missing values are replaced with min_relevant_intensity (default 1000 counts) before training, sub-threshold values are zero-masked in the normalized output, and RALPS tolerates up to 30% randomly replaced values with only marginal loss of replicate cross-correlation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096
skills.summary: Missing-value handling for RALPS normalization of multi-batch untargeted metabolomics matrices: missing values are replaced with min_relevant_intensity (default 1000 counts) before training, sub-threshold values are zero-masked in the normalized output, and RALPS tolerates up to 30% randomly replaced values with only marginal loss of replicate cross-correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is complete (no missing values) and the task is batch-effect harmonization only, so threshold replacement/masking adds nothing on its own Missing values require feature-aware or model-based imputation rather than RALPS's flat 1000-count minimum replacement True low-abundance signals below 1000 counts must be preserved after normalization instead of being zero-masked

skills.description: Use when a Nightingale 1H-NMR metabolomics matrix (CSV/TSV) contains missing or zero metabolite values that must be QC-filtered and imputed before computing metaboAge, surrogate, or published clinical scores in MiMIR.
skills.name: metabolomics-missing-value-qc-and-imputation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missing-value-qc-and-imputation Use when a Nightingale 1H-NMR metabolomics matrix (CSV/TSV) contains missing or zero metabolite values that must be QC-filtered and imputed before computing metaboAge, surrogate, or published clinical scores in MiMIR. The input is phenotypic data or a non-Nightingale metabolomics platform, where Nightingale-specific column names, plus-one offsets, and MEAN/SD scaling parameters do not apply. You only need to binarize phenotypes or calibrate already-computed surrogate scores (e.g. via binarize_all_pheno or plattCalibration), which operate downstream of metabolite QC. A single global QC/imputation is desired across all 24 models; MiMIR instead runs per-model QC in parallel with model-specific parameters. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A sample-level QC and imputation procedure for Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics matrices, implemented in MiMIR, that removes samples exceeding missing/zero-value thresholds and SD-based outliers before scaling with bundled MEAN/SD parameters and imputing residual missing values, so pre-trained scores can be projected onto complete data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac388
skills.summary: A sample-level QC and imputation procedure for Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics matrices, implemented in MiMIR, that removes samples exceeding missing/zero-value thresholds and SD-based outliers before scaling with bundled MEAN/SD parameters and imputing residual missing values, so pre-trained scores can be projected onto complete data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is phenotypic data or a non-Nightingale metabolomics platform, where Nightingale-specific column names, plus-one offsets, and MEAN/SD scaling parameters do not apply. You only need to binarize phenotypes or calibrate already-computed surrogate scores (e.g. via binarize_all_pheno or plattCalibration), which operate downstream of metabolite QC. A single global QC/imputation is desired across all 24 models; MiMIR instead runs per-model QC in parallel with model-specific parameters.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metabolite imputation algorithms on real metabolomics data where missingness combines MNAR (below limit of detection) and MAR mechanisms, and averaged RMSE comparisons across missingness levels are needed.
skills.name: metabolomics-missingness-simulation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-missingness-simulation Use when benchmarking metabolite imputation algorithms on real metabolomics data where missingness combines MNAR (below limit of detection) and MAR mechanisms, and averaged RMSE comparisons across missingness levels are needed. The dataset contains essentially no values below the limit of detection, so missingness is purely MAR/MCAR and the truncated-normal KNN-TN machinery adds no benefit. The evaluation dataset behaves like the African Race data set, where the paper found 'no significant difference between any of the KNN imputation algorithms and mean imputation'. Sample sizes are under 20 or missing percentages fall below those evaluated in the study (9%, 15%, 30%) — the paper reports such cases only as 'data not shown'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces the paper's real-data missingness simulation: 100 replicate datasets generated from three real metabolomics matrices (myocardial infarction, atherothrombotic, African Race) with imposed MNAR+MAR missingness at 9%, 15%, and 30%, to benchmark KNN-TN vs KNN-CR vs KNN-EU imputation by averaged RMSE. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: Reproduces the paper's real-data missingness simulation: 100 replicate datasets generated from three real metabolomics matrices (myocardial infarction, atherothrombotic, African Race) with imposed MNAR+MAR missingness at 9%, 15%, and 30%, to benchmark KNN-TN vs KNN-CR vs KNN-EU imputation by averaged RMSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains essentially no values below the limit of detection, so missingness is purely MAR/MCAR and the truncated-normal KNN-TN machinery adds no benefit. The evaluation dataset behaves like the African Race data set, where the paper found 'no significant difference between any of the KNN imputation algorithms and mean imputation'. Sample sizes are under 20 or missing percentages fall below those evaluated in the study (9%, 15%, 30%) — the paper reports such cases only as 'data not shown'.

skills.description: Use when annotating LC-MS metabolite features from a tidyMass mass_dataset object against a reference library, and you must assign MSI annotation levels from m/z, RT, and MS2 evidence.
skills.name: metabolomics-ms2-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: metabolomics-ms2-spectral-matching Use when annotating LC-MS metabolite features from a tidyMass mass_dataset object against a reference library, and you must assign MSI annotation levels from m/z, RT, and MS2 evidence. When only MS1 m/z data are available with no MS2 spectra for any features — the best assignable level is 3, so spectral matching adds no discrimination beyond m/z lookup. When the goal is removing in-source fragmentation products misannotated as genuine metabolites — the article states there is currently no satisfactory solution for this, deferred to a future MetMiner version. When a non-plant organism is studied, since the integrated database is specifically plant-oriented; use a database matched to the sample's taxonomy instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Annotates metabolite features by matching MS1 m/z and MS2 spectra against MetMiner's integrated plant-specific mass spectrometry database, assigning Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) annotation levels 1–3 based on whether m/z, retention time, and MS2 spectral evidence all match. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Annotates metabolite features by matching MS1 m/z and MS2 spectra against MetMiner's integrated plant-specific mass spectrometry database, assigning Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) annotation levels 1–3 based on whether m/z, retention time, and MS2 spectral evidence all match.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only MS1 m/z data are available with no MS2 spectra for any features — the best assignable level is 3, so spectral matching adds no discrimination beyond m/z lookup. When the goal is removing in-source fragmentation products misannotated as genuine metabolites — the article states there is currently no satisfactory solution for this, deferred to a future MetMiner version. When a non-plant organism is studied, since the integrated database is specifically plant-oriented; use a database matched to the sample's taxonomy instead.

skills.description: Use when a feature-count matrix (e.g. 170 metabolites x 2856 samples) spans multiple LC-MS batches with reference samples (pooled/NIST 1950 SRM) present in each batch and interbatch differences must be removed before analysis.
skills.name: metabolomics-multi-batch-normalization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-multi-batch-normalization Use when a feature-count matrix (e.g. 170 metabolites x 2856 samples) spans multiple LC-MS batches with reference samples (pooled/NIST 1950 SRM) present in each batch and interbatch differences must be removed before analysis. Data contains only a single batch — RALPS is designed to harmonize multi-batch measurements, not intrabatch drift correction (normalize each batch individually first) No reference/replicate samples (e.g. pooled QC or NIST 1950 SRM) are present in the batches to define group/batch info for training The dataset has been pre-normalized so interbatch differences are already removed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Normalize multi-batch untargeted metabolomics data with RALPS (Regularized Adversarial Learning Preserving Similarity), a PyTorch adversarial autoencoder with a three-term loss that removes interbatch differences while preserving biological identity, spectral properties and coefficients of variation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096
skills.summary: Normalize multi-batch untargeted metabolomics data with RALPS (Regularized Adversarial Learning Preserving Similarity), a PyTorch adversarial autoencoder with a three-term loss that removes interbatch differences while preserving biological identity, spectral properties and coefficients of variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contains only a single batch — RALPS is designed to harmonize multi-batch measurements, not intrabatch drift correction (normalize each batch individually first) No reference/replicate samples (e.g. pooled QC or NIST 1950 SRM) are present in the batches to define group/batch info for training The dataset has been pre-normalized so interbatch differences are already removed

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics pipeline needs to control false discoveries: selecting differentially abundant metabolites from two-tailed t-tests, or converting raw ORA pathway p-values into q-values before declaring significant enriched pathways (SEPs).
skills.name: metabolomics-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: metabolomics-multiple-testing-correction Use when a metabolomics pipeline needs to control false discoveries: selecting differentially abundant metabolites from two-tailed t-tests, or converting raw ORA pathway p-values into q-values before declaring significant enriched pathways (SEPs). When reporting exploratory results without correction is explicitly intended — the article flags that 'a p-value threshold of P <= 0.1 was used without multiple testing correction to select SEPs' as a limitation, not a recommended default When the goal is a single pre-specified pathway hypothesis test rather than simultaneous testing of a full KEGG/Reactome/BioCyc pathway set When the input is already a table of adjusted q-values — re-applying BH correction would double-adjust and over-conservatively shrink the SEP list http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (BH FDR) correction to metabolomics p-values — both for selecting differentially abundant metabolites prior to ORA (q ≤ 0.05) and for calling significantly enriched pathways from right-tailed Fisher's exact test pathway p-values (q ≤ 0.1). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (BH FDR) correction to metabolomics p-values — both for selecting differentially abundant metabolites prior to ORA (q ≤ 0.05) and for calling significantly enriched pathways from right-tailed Fisher's exact test pathway p-values (q ≤ 0.1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reporting exploratory results without correction is explicitly intended — the article flags that 'a p-value threshold of P <= 0.1 was used without multiple testing correction to select SEPs' as a limitation, not a recommended default When the goal is a single pre-specified pathway hypothesis test rather than simultaneous testing of a full KEGG/Reactome/BioCyc pathway set When the input is already a table of adjusted q-values — re-applying BH correction would double-adjust and over-conservatively shrink the SEP list

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics/proteomics feature table (samples x metabolites, e.g. from ST000284-style targeted studies) must be reduced or classified, and per-sample PCA/PLS-DA scores plus a discriminative metabolite list are the required deliverables.
skills.name: metabolomics-multivariate-score-extraction
skills.search_text: metabolomics-multivariate-score-extraction Use when a preprocessed metabolomics/proteomics feature table (samples x metabolites, e.g. from ST000284-style targeted studies) must be reduced or classified, and per-sample PCA/PLS-DA scores plus a discriminative metabolite list are the required deliverables. Input is still raw spectral data (mzML/NetCDF or similar) that has not yet been imputed, normalized or scaled — POMAShiny's preprocessing panel (20% missing-value threshold, one of six imputation and six normalization methods, outlier removal) must run first. The analysis goal is purely univariate (e.g. fold-change or t-test per metabolite) with no need for dimension reduction or classification. Only two-group comparison without any interest in feature selection is required — simpler POMA tests may suffice and sPLS-DA tuning overhead is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Run PCA, PLS-DA and sPLS-DA on a preprocessed metabolomics/proteomics feature matrix via the POMA R/Bioconductor package (as used by POMAShiny), and export per-sample scores on the first two components plus the sPLS-DA selected-feature list. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009148
skills.summary: Run PCA, PLS-DA and sPLS-DA on a preprocessed metabolomics/proteomics feature matrix via the POMA R/Bioconductor package (as used by POMAShiny), and export per-sample scores on the first two components plus the sPLS-DA selected-feature list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw spectral data (mzML/NetCDF or similar) that has not yet been imputed, normalized or scaled — POMAShiny's preprocessing panel (20% missing-value threshold, one of six imputation and six normalization methods, outlier removal) must run first. The analysis goal is purely univariate (e.g. fold-change or t-test per metabolite) with no need for dimension reduction or classification. Only two-group comparison without any interest in feature selection is required — simpler POMA tests may suffice and sPLS-DA tuning overhead is unnecessary.
