skills.description: Use when a tab-delimited feature abundance table (e.g. MS-DIAL output) has matched sample annotations with class labels distinguishing QC from biological samples, and low-quality features must be filtered before imputation, normalization, or statistics.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-based-feature-retention
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-based-feature-retention Use when a tab-delimited feature abundance table (e.g. MS-DIAL output) has matched sample annotations with class labels distinguishing QC from biological samples, and low-quality features must be filtered before imputation, normalization, or statistics. The input is not a preprocessed feature abundance table but raw instrument data — margheRita expects MS-Dial-generated tab-delimited output, not vendor files No QC injections are present in the sample annotation, since the CV ratio is defined as CV(no-QC samples) divided by CV(QC samples) and cannot be computed The goal is drift correction or imputation rather than quality-based feature removal — margheRita provides separate imputation (NA replacement with 10%–25% of the feature minimum) and normalization steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retain LC-MS/MS metabolomic features by computing the coefficient-of-variation ratio between biological samples and QC samples and keeping features whose CV ratio exceeds a threshold (default 1), as implemented in the margheRita R package. This removes low-quality signals whose technical variability is not lower than biological variability. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.06.20.599545
skills.summary: Retain LC-MS/MS metabolomic features by computing the coefficient-of-variation ratio between biological samples and QC samples and keeping features whose CV ratio exceeds a threshold (default 1), as implemented in the margheRita R package. This removes low-quality signals whose technical variability is not lower than biological variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a preprocessed feature abundance table but raw instrument data — margheRita expects MS-Dial-generated tab-delimited output, not vendor files No QC injections are present in the sample annotation, since the CV ratio is defined as CV(no-QC samples) divided by CV(QC samples) and cannot be computed The goal is drift correction or imputation rather than quality-based feature removal — margheRita provides separate imputation (NA replacement with 10%–25% of the feature minimum) and normalization steps

skills.description: Use when monitoring untargeted MS-based metabolomics acquisitions — e.g. pooled QC injections every 5–10 injections — and you need to visualize RT/m/z deviation, intensity drift, or contaminant levels per batch to catch analytical problems.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-data-visualization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-data-visualization Use when monitoring untargeted MS-based metabolomics acquisitions — e.g. pooled QC injections every 5–10 injections — and you need to visualize RT/m/z deviation, intensity drift, or contaminant levels per batch to catch analytical problems. Input is already a processed feature table or post-corrected intensities (e.g. from QC-MXP) rather than raw vendor files needing real-time tracking. The goal is postanalysis intensity drift correction rather than monitoring/visualization — QC4Metabolomics tracks and visualizes QC parameters, it does not itself correct drifts. No pooled QC samples or user-defined m/z/RT pairs exist, so module_TrackCmp has no targets to monitor. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Presents QC4Metabolomics extraction and quality-control results (observed m/z, retention time, intensity, peak shape, and contaminant levels) on an interactive web dashboard so that drifts, calibration offsets, and instrument problems can be spotted in real time or retrospectively. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: Presents QC4Metabolomics extraction and quality-control results (observed m/z, retention time, intensity, peak shape, and contaminant levels) on an interactive web dashboard so that drifts, calibration offsets, and instrument problems can be spotted in real time or retrospectively.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or post-corrected intensities (e.g. from QC-MXP) rather than raw vendor files needing real-time tracking. The goal is postanalysis intensity drift correction rather than monitoring/visualization — QC4Metabolomics tracks and visualizes QC parameters, it does not itself correct drifts. No pooled QC samples or user-defined m/z/RT pairs exist, so module_TrackCmp has no targets to monitor.

skills.description: Use when raw peak-picked feature tables from two LC–MS metabolomics datasets must be QC-filtered and summarized (RT, m/z, FI medians) before feature correspondence matching.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-feature-table-handling
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-feature-table-handling Use when raw peak-picked feature tables from two LC–MS metabolomics datasets must be QC-filtered and summarized (RT, m/z, FI medians) before feature correspondence matching. Input is already a post-QC feature table of RT/mz/FI medians ready for M2S matching The goal is metabolite annotation or database searching (LIPID MAPS, METLIN, HMDB, GNPS, MassBank) rather than preparing features for correspondence matching Datasets were not peak-picked separately with XCMS and lack per-sample feature intensities needed for QC and median computation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Prepares post-XCMS untargeted LC–MS feature tables for inter-dataset matching by applying QC dilution-series filtering (R² < 0.7), retention-time trimming, and per-feature median characterization of RT, m/z, and FI so that only well-behaved features enter correspondence matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03592
skills.summary: Prepares post-XCMS untargeted LC–MS feature tables for inter-dataset matching by applying QC dilution-series filtering (R² < 0.7), retention-time trimming, and per-feature median characterization of RT, m/z, and FI so that only well-behaved features enter correspondence matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a post-QC feature table of RT/mz/FI medians ready for M2S matching The goal is metabolite annotation or database searching (LIPID MAPS, METLIN, HMDB, GNPS, MassBank) rather than preparing features for correspondence matching Datasets were not peak-picked separately with XCMS and lack per-sample feature intensities needed for QC and median computation

skills.description: Use when a pooled-QC-injected targeted metabolomics/lipidomics sequence (Sciex MultiQuant txt exports) needs outlying samples flagged before statistical analysis, and you need defensible, reportable outlier criteria based on PCA scores.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-outlier-flagging
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-outlier-flagging Use when a pooled-QC-injected targeted metabolomics/lipidomics sequence (Sciex MultiQuant txt exports) needs outlying samples flagged before statistical analysis, and you need defensible, reportable outlier criteria based on PCA scores. Data is unprocessed raw signal: QComics outlier removal is step (iii) of the sequential workflow, which should first correct for background noise and carryover and detect signal drifts (steps i–ii) Data contains missing values and truly absent features that have not yet been separated, since QComics requires separately handling missing values and truly absent data to avoid losing relevant biological information The dataset lacks regularly injected pooled QC (QCpool) samples, which the QComics package requires as its monitoring basis http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Flags outlying samples in metabolomics QC data by fitting a PCA model to the processed QC data and identifying samples outside the 95% Hotelling T2 confidence ellipse, complemented by DmodX residual-distance screening, as step (iii) 'removal of outlying samples' of the QComics sequential QC workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: Flags outlying samples in metabolomics QC data by fitting a PCA model to the processed QC data and identifying samples outside the 95% Hotelling T2 confidence ellipse, complemented by DmodX residual-distance screening, as step (iii) 'removal of outlying samples' of the QComics sequential QC workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is unprocessed raw signal: QComics outlier removal is step (iii) of the sequential workflow, which should first correct for background noise and carryover and detect signal drifts (steps i–ii) Data contains missing values and truly absent features that have not yet been separated, since QComics requires separately handling missing values and truly absent data to avoid losing relevant biological information The dataset lacks regularly injected pooled QC (QCpool) samples, which the QComics package requires as its monitoring basis

skills.description: Use when raw LC–MS injections (mzML from Waters RAW converted with msconvert) plus a batch sequence mapping SSS and pooled/intrastudy QC injections must be assessed for platform conditioning and system suitability with TidyMS.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-pipeline-execution Use when raw LC–MS injections (mzML from Waters RAW converted with msconvert) plus a batch sequence mapping SSS and pooled/intrastudy QC injections must be assessed for platform conditioning and system suitability with TidyMS. Input is already a feature table or extracted data matrix — this skill operates on raw mzML injections through TidyMS's reader and processor pipeline The goal is downstream feature annotation or statistical modeling of curated features — TidyMS explicitly lacks feature annotation capability, and data curation/signal-drift pipelines are separate skills Data are not QC-oriented injections (no SSS or pooled/intrastudy QC samples in the batch) — the conditioning assessment depends on those injection types http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Executes the TidyMS system-conditioning and LC–MS system suitability pipelines on raw metabolomics injections (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS1919 plasma RM data) to regenerate QC assessment tables and figures, as demonstrated in the Riquelme et al. 2020 TidyMS paper on NIST candidate RM 8231 and SRM 1950. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Executes the TidyMS system-conditioning and LC–MS system suitability pipelines on raw metabolomics injections (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS1919 plasma RM data) to regenerate QC assessment tables and figures, as demonstrated in the Riquelme et al. 2020 TidyMS paper on NIST candidate RM 8231 and SRM 1950.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or extracted data matrix — this skill operates on raw mzML injections through TidyMS's reader and processor pipeline The goal is downstream feature annotation or statistical modeling of curated features — TidyMS explicitly lacks feature annotation capability, and data curation/signal-drift pipelines are separate skills Data are not QC-oriented injections (no SSS or pooled/intrastudy QC samples in the batch) — the conditioning assessment depends on those injection types

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics sequence contains repeated pooled QC (QCpool) injections and you need to quantitatively assess overall data quality in terms of precision and accuracy per chemical descriptor before reporting the study.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-rsd-calculation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-rsd-calculation Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics sequence contains repeated pooled QC (QCpool) injections and you need to quantitatively assess overall data quality in terms of precision and accuracy per chemical descriptor before reporting the study. The sequence lacks repeated pooled QC (QCpool) injections — precision and accuracy cannot be estimated without them You are performing earlier QComics steps (background/carryover correction, drift detection, missing-value handling, outlier removal) rather than the final overall data-quality assessment Data are non-MS omics outputs where intensity/RT/peak-width descriptors and ppm m/z error do not apply without redefining criteria http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes per-descriptor precision (%RSD of peak intensity, retention time, and peak width) and mass accuracy (ppm m/z error) across repeated pooled-QC injections, then applies the QComics acceptance criteria (RSD < 30% intensity, RSD < 2% RT, RSD < 15% peak width, m/z error < 10 ppm for HRMS) to flag each descriptor pass/fail as the final overall data-quality assessment. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: Computes per-descriptor precision (%RSD of peak intensity, retention time, and peak width) and mass accuracy (ppm m/z error) across repeated pooled-QC injections, then applies the QComics acceptance criteria (RSD < 30% intensity, RSD < 2% RT, RSD < 15% peak width, m/z error < 10 ppm for HRMS) to flag each descriptor pass/fail as the final overall data-quality assessment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequence lacks repeated pooled QC (QCpool) injections — precision and accuracy cannot be estimated without them You are performing earlier QComics steps (background/carryover correction, drift detection, missing-value handling, outlier removal) rather than the final overall data-quality assessment Data are non-MS omics outputs where intensity/RT/peak-width descriptors and ppm m/z error do not apply without redefining criteria

skills.description: Use when a post-data-curation LC–MS feature matrix (e.g. from MetaboLights MTBLS1919) with pooled/intrastudy QC injections is available and you need to check QC clustering, sample outliers, or drift-correlated variance via PCA scores.
skills.name: metabolomics-qc-sample-clustering
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-sample-clustering Use when a post-data-curation LC–MS feature matrix (e.g. from MetaboLights MTBLS1919) with pooled/intrastudy QC injections is available and you need to check QC clustering, sample outliers, or drift-correlated variance via PCA scores. Input is raw centroided/vendor LC–MS data rather than an extracted, curated feature matrix — run the TidyMS data-curation filters (Rt > 90 s, blank 10-fold, RSD 20%, D-ratio) first The goal is feature annotation or compound identification — the article notes TidyMS lacks feature annotation capability, and PCA scores do not provide it Study design has no pooled/intrastudy QC injections, so QC-based drift evaluation and the LOESS batch-correction precondition cannot be met http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assesses LC–MS untargeted metabolomics data quality by fitting PCA models (scikit-learn) on the curated feature matrix from the NIST candidate RM 8231 / SRM 1950 study and inspecting score plots of pooled/intrastudy QC injections versus study samples, mirroring the paper's Figure 4 and Figure S3 before/after-curation comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Assesses LC–MS untargeted metabolomics data quality by fitting PCA models (scikit-learn) on the curated feature matrix from the NIST candidate RM 8231 / SRM 1950 study and inspecting score plots of pooled/intrastudy QC injections versus study samples, mirroring the paper's Figure 4 and Figure S3 before/after-curation comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw centroided/vendor LC–MS data rather than an extracted, curated feature matrix — run the TidyMS data-curation filters (Rt > 90 s, blank 10-fold, RSD 20%, D-ratio) first The goal is feature annotation or compound identification — the article notes TidyMS lacks feature annotation capability, and PCA scores do not provide it Study design has no pooled/intrastudy QC injections, so QC-based drift evaluation and the LOESS batch-correction precondition cannot be met

skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-threshold-configuration Use when a raw metabolomics feature table (e.g. Nightingale NMR, Metabolon xlsx, Olink txt, SomaLogic adat) must be quality-controlled and filtered with explicit, reproducible sample/feature exclusion thresholds. skills.search_text: metabolomics-qc-workflow-design Use when you must evaluate or correct time-related signal drift in untargeted LC–MS batches that include pooled/intrastudy QC samples acquired in order (e.g., mzML runs from MetaboLights MTBLS1919). Input is already a curated feature table without raw mzML data or injection-order metadata, so drift cannot be evaluated on QC injections in acquisition order The batch contains no pooled/intrastudy QC samples — LOESS batch correction and drift evaluation require features present in pooled QC injections The goal is metabolite/feature annotation — the paper explicitly notes TidyMS lacks feature annotation capability http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Designs and executes the LC–MS quality-control workflow demonstrated in the TidyMS 2020 paper: system suitability check, system conditioning, signal drift evaluation on pooled/intrastudy QC injections, and QC-driven data curation with LOESS batch correction. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Designs and executes the LC–MS quality-control workflow demonstrated in the TidyMS 2020 paper: system suitability check, system conditioning, signal drift evaluation on pooled/intrastudy QC injections, and QC-driven data curation with LOESS batch correction.

skills.description: Use when a targeted metabolomics or lipidomics study has pooled QC samples (QCpool) measured at regular intervals across one or more sequences, and you need to detect signal drift, background/carryover effects or out-of-control injections before downstream missing-value handling and outlier removal.
skills.name: metabolomics-qcpool-series-monitoring
skills.search_text: metabolomics-qcpool-series-monitoring Use when a targeted metabolomics or lipidomics study has pooled QC samples (QCpool) measured at regular intervals across one or more sequences, and you need to detect signal drift, background/carryover effects or out-of-control injections before downstream missing-value handling and outlier removal. The dataset lacks pooled QC samples injected at regular intervals — QComics' QCpool-based monitoring cannot be performed and preanalytical quality markers should be used instead. The analysis goal is handling missing values versus truly absent data, removing outlying samples, or monitoring preanalytical quality markers — these are later steps of the QComics workflow, not the run-sequence control-chart step. Data are not from MS-based metabolomics/lipidomics injections exported via Sciex MultiQuant and you cannot reformat them as the QCpool descriptor txt table expected by the R app. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Monitors pooled QC (QCpool) metabolomics series by plotting each chemical descriptor over run order with Shewhart control limits at ±1SD, ±2SD and ±3SD, then applying Westgard decision rules to flag out-of-control injections and decide whether a sequence is acceptable. This is the drift/contamination detection stage of the QComics protocol (Anal. Chem. 2024). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: Monitors pooled QC (QCpool) metabolomics series by plotting each chemical descriptor over run order with Shewhart control limits at ±1SD, ±2SD and ±3SD, then applying Westgard decision rules to flag out-of-control injections and decide whether a sequence is acceptable. This is the drift/contamination detection stage of the QComics protocol (Anal. Chem. 2024).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks pooled QC samples injected at regular intervals — QComics' QCpool-based monitoring cannot be performed and preanalytical quality markers should be used instead. The analysis goal is handling missing values versus truly absent data, removing outlying samples, or monitoring preanalytical quality markers — these are later steps of the QComics workflow, not the run-sequence control-chart step. Data are not from MS-based metabolomics/lipidomics injections exported via Sciex MultiQuant and you cannot reformat them as the QCpool descriptor txt table expected by the R app.

skills.description: Use when a MetaboDiff MultiAssayExperiment object (Metabolon®-style metabolite measurements) has been imputed and vsn-normalized and you must visually verify near-constant variance and comparable per-sample distributions before differential analysis.
skills.name: metabolomics-quality-control-boxplot-visualization
skills.search_text: metabolomics-quality-control-boxplot-visualization Use when a MetaboDiff MultiAssayExperiment object (Metabolon®-style metabolite measurements) has been imputed and vsn-normalized and you must visually verify near-constant variance and comparable per-sample distributions before differential analysis. The MultiAssayExperiment object lacks the 'norm' and 'norm_imputed' slots because normalize_met has not yet been run — run normalization first, the boxplot comparison is meaningless without the vsn-normalized panel. The goal is differential testing (Student's T-Test, ANOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg correction) or metabolic correlation network analysis rather than QC of the normalization step. Input is a raw vendor metabolite measurement table that has not passed the knn_impute 40% cutoff and outlier-cluster removal QC chain. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Renders per-sample boxplots of raw, imputed, normalized, and imputed+normalized metabolomic measurements with MetaboDiff's quality_plot to visually confirm that variance stabilizing normalization (vsn) has made the variance nearly constant across the measurement spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty344
skills.summary: Renders per-sample boxplots of raw, imputed, normalized, and imputed+normalized metabolomic measurements with MetaboDiff's quality_plot to visually confirm that variance stabilizing normalization (vsn) has made the variance nearly constant across the measurement spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MultiAssayExperiment object lacks the 'norm' and 'norm_imputed' slots because normalize_met has not yet been run — run normalization first, the boxplot comparison is meaningless without the vsn-normalized panel. The goal is differential testing (Student's T-Test, ANOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg correction) or metabolic correlation network analysis rather than QC of the normalization step. Input is a raw vendor metabolite measurement table that has not passed the knn_impute 40% cutoff and outlier-cluster removal QC chain.

skills.description: Use when a 1H-NMR or metabonomic dataset contains QC replicate samples and you must quantify analytical reproducibility per metabolic feature, or decide which features to retain via CV < 0.30 / CV < 0.15 filtering.

skills.search_text: metabolomics-quality-control-cv-analysis Use when a 1H-NMR or metabonomic dataset contains QC replicate samples and you must quantify analytical reproducibility per metabolic feature, or decide which features to retain via CV < 0.30 / CV < 0.15 filtering. The dataset lacks QC replicate samples, so no across-QC coefficient of variation can be computed The goal is a downstream metabolite-phenotype association model (partial correlations or generalized linear models) rather than analytical reproducibility assessment Quality-control analysis of metabolic features by computing per-feature coefficients of variation (CV) across QC replicate samples and applying FDA-established reproducibility thresholds of 0.30 (biomarker discovery) and 0.15 (quantification), as supported by the MWASTools R/Bioconductor package for metabonomic data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Quality-control analysis of metabolic features by computing per-feature coefficients of variation (CV) across QC replicate samples and applying FDA-established reproducibility thresholds of 0.30 (biomarker discovery) and 0.15 (quantification), as supported by the MWASTools R/Bioconductor package for metabonomic data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks QC replicate samples, so no across-QC coefficient of variation can be computed The goal is a downstream metabolite-phenotype association model (partial correlations or generalized linear models) rather than analytical reproducibility assessment

skills.description: Use when raw platform-exported metabolomics data (e.g. Metabolon OrigScale xlsx, Nightingale NMR, Olink, SomaLogic adat) must be QC'd, filtered on missingness/outlier thresholds, and summarized before association analysis.
skills.name: metabolomics-quality-control-filtering

Input is already a QC-filtered feature table with no sample metadata — the package expects preformed worksheets with features/samples annotations Analysis requires statistical testing or association modeling; metaboprep is explicitly a preanalysis data description and processing tool Non-metabolomics omics data outside the supported platform formats (Metabolon, Nightingale, Olink, SomaLogic, dummy CSV) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Standardized preanalysis quality-control and filtering of (un)targeted metabolomics datasets using the metaboprep R package, which reads preformed worksheets, computes sample/feature quality summaries, excludes samples and metabolites against user-defined thresholds, and emits tab-delimited summaries plus an HTML report. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac059
skills.summary: Standardized preanalysis quality-control and filtering of (un)targeted metabolomics datasets using the metaboprep R package, which reads preformed worksheets, computes sample/feature quality summaries, excludes samples and metabolites against user-defined thresholds, and emits tab-delimited summaries plus an HTML report.

skills.description: Use when untargeted MS-based metabolomics files (mzML, mzXML, mzData) are being acquired or already acquired and you need to monitor QC parameters such as m/z deviation, retention time deviation, intensity drift, calibration offset, or contaminant levels in (near) real time or retrospectively.
skills.name: metabolomics-quality-control-monitoring
skills.search_text: metabolomics-quality-control-monitoring Use when untargeted MS-based metabolomics files (mzML, mzXML, mzData) are being acquired or already acquired and you need to monitor QC parameters such as m/z deviation, retention time deviation, intensity drift, calibration offset, or contaminant levels in (near) real time or retrospectively. Input is already a processed feature table or corrected intensity matrix — QC4Metabolomics expects vendor raw or mzML-format untargeted MS files acquired during or after an LC-MS run, not ready-made downstream results. You need targeted quantitation of a small panel of analytes with a validated calibration curve — this skill is for untargeted metabolomics QC monitoring, not targeted assay validation. Data are not mass-spectrometry-based (e.g. NMR spectra, imaging data) or lack the pooled-QC injection cadence needed to anchor intensity-drift and calibration monitoring. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Real-time and retrospective quality control of untargeted mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data using QC4Metabolomics, a Shiny web application and R package that tracks user-defined compounds and contaminants across acquired mzML files. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: Real-time and retrospective quality control of untargeted mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data using QC4Metabolomics, a Shiny web application and R package that tracks user-defined compounds and contaminants across acquired mzML files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or corrected intensity matrix — QC4Metabolomics expects vendor raw or mzML-format untargeted MS files acquired during or after an LC-MS run, not ready-made downstream results. You need targeted quantitation of a small panel of analytes with a validated calibration curve — this skill is for untargeted metabolomics QC monitoring, not targeted assay validation. Data are not mass-spectrometry-based (e.g. NMR spectra, imaging data) or lack the pooled-QC injection cadence needed to anchor intensity-drift and calibration monitoring.

skills.description: Use when an Asari preferred_Feature_table.tsv from a pcpfm experiment shows per-sample TIC differences driven by feature counts, or samples span multiple batches, and the table must be normalized/batch-corrected before downstream analysis.
skills.name: metabolomics-quality-correction-workflow
skills.search_text: metabolomics-quality-correction-workflow Use when an Asari preferred_Feature_table.tsv from a pcpfm experiment shows per-sample TIC differences driven by feature counts, or samples span multiple batches, and the table must be normalized/batch-corrected before downstream analysis. Input is raw .mzML or .raw data — preprocessing via Asari must run first to produce the feature table. The table has already been TIC-normalized; re-normalization would double-scale the intensities. Only a small fraction of features are shared across samples, so the TIC_normalization_percentile filter would leave too few conserved features to compute robust factors. Applies pcpfm's data-quality correction operations — TIC-based normalization (one-pass or batch-aware two-pass), blank masking, batch correction, removal of uncommon/rare features, and missing value imputation — to Asari feature tables so they are fit for downstream statistical analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: Applies pcpfm's data-quality correction operations — TIC-based normalization (one-pass or batch-aware two-pass), blank masking, batch correction, removal of uncommon/rare features, and missing value imputation — to Asari feature tables so they are fit for downstream statistical analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw .mzML or .raw data — preprocessing via Asari must run first to produce the feature table. The table has already been TIC-normalized; re-normalization would double-scale the intensities. Only a small fraction of features are shared across samples, so the TIC_normalization_percentile filter would leave too few conserved features to compute robust factors.

skills.name: metabolomics-quality-parameter-extraction
skills.search_text: metabolomics-quality-parameter-extraction Use when acquired or archived untargeted MS metabolomics files (mzML, mzXML, mzData) must be summarized into per-file quality metrics — RT and m/z deviations, intensity drift, peak shape — for real-time or retrospective QC. The goal is postanalysis intensity-drift correction rather than per-file QC parameter extraction — use tools like QC-MXP instead. The analysis is a targeted assay with no pooled QC samples injected at regular intervals (every 5–10 injections) — the tracked-compound approach presumes such QC samples exist. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extract per-file quality parameters from untargeted metabolomics mzML data by tracking user-defined compounds (observed m/z, retention time, intensity, peak shape) and metadata, as implemented in QC4Metabolomics's module_File_info and module_TrackCmp. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: Extract per-file quality parameters from untargeted metabolomics mzML data by tracking user-defined compounds (observed m/z, retention time, intensity, peak shape) and metadata, as implemented in QC4Metabolomics's module_File_info and module_TrackCmp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated feature table or processed peak matrix — this skill operates on raw mzML/mzXML/mzData acquisition files. The goal is postanalysis intensity-drift correction rather than per-file QC parameter extraction — use tools like QC-MXP instead. The analysis is a targeted assay with no pooled QC samples injected at regular intervals (every 5–10 injections) — the tracked-compound approach presumes such QC samples exist.

skills.description: Use when a MetaPro run-1 quantification export (.xlsx) is available for a benchmark mixture design with known SB:SA dilution ratios (1/16 to 16/1) and you need to verify that observed log2 fold changes track the designed values before manual peak inspection.
skills.name: metabolomics-quantification-report-processing
skills.search_text: metabolomics-quantification-report-processing Use when a MetaPro run-1 quantification export (.xlsx) is available for a benchmark mixture design with known SB:SA dilution ratios (1/16 to 16/1) and you need to verify that observed log2 fold changes track the designed values before manual peak inspection. The data are still vendor instrument files (e.g., unconverted .raw/.wiff2) that have not been processed by AirdPro conversion and MetaPro Target Search, so no quantification report exists yet. The study has no designed dilution standards or control groups, so there is no ground-truth fold change to validate quantification against. The goal is interactive peak-shape QC (manual integration, Reset TargetRT) rather than numerical validation of run-1 quantification accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Validates the quantification accuracy of a first-run (raw, uninspected) MetaPro LC-MS semi-targeted analysis by comparing log2-transformed relative quantification fold changes against a benchmark standard-mixture design (Gm controls plus 130 compounds at designed SB:SA ratios) on both TripleTOF 6600 and QE HF platforms. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-023-02018-6
skills.summary: Validates the quantification accuracy of a first-run (raw, uninspected) MetaPro LC-MS semi-targeted analysis by comparing log2-transformed relative quantification fold changes against a benchmark standard-mixture design (Gm controls plus 130 compounds at designed SB:SA ratios) on both TripleTOF 6600 and QE HF platforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are still vendor instrument files (e.g., unconverted .raw/.wiff2) that have not been processed by AirdPro conversion and MetaPro Target Search, so no quantification report exists yet. The study has no designed dilution standards or control groups, so there is no ground-truth fold change to validate quantification against. The goal is interactive peak-shape QC (manual integration, Reset TargetRT) rather than numerical validation of run-1 quantification accuracy.

skills.name: metabolomics-quantitative-results-extraction
skills.search_text: metabolomics-quantitative-results-extraction Use when a source card asks to reproduce reported metabolomics counts (peaks/identifications per ionisation mode) from a paper's Results text and supplementary figures, and the deliverable is a validated summary table rather than re-processed spectra. The feature table has not been through JPA's peak.alignment step (unaligned per-sample tables lack a common feature index and 'level' column) The dataset has no replicate samples, so RSD% cannot be computed You need to evaluate LOD, peak shape, or feature-rescue rate rather than replicate precision — use the paper's dilution-series or LOD workflows instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Computes replicate relative standard deviation (RSD%) of aligned LC-MS metabolic features, stratified by JPA extraction level (PP vs MR), to verify that rescued features meet the precision threshold (<15% RSD) required for downstream statistical analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS spectra from a serial dilution series (known dilution design, replicate tubes) are available and you need to validate that a spectra-processing workflow quantifies features proportionally to concentration.
skills.name: metabolomics-replicate-qc-evaluation
skills.search_text: metabolomics-replicate-qc-evaluation Use when raw LC-MS spectra from a serial dilution series (known dilution design, replicate tubes) are available and you need to validate that a spectra-processing workflow quantifies features proportionally to concentration. The input is already a processed feature table with no linked raw dilution-series spectra and no known dilution ratios, so correlations against expected concentrations cannot be computed. The dataset is a single-condition or case-control study with no dilution/concentration gradient — replicate QC by correlation to dilution ratio is undefined. The goal is MS2 compound-identification QC (e.g. DDA/DIA deconvolution or spectral library matching accuracy) rather than MS1 quantification accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Evaluates LC-MS1 feature quantification accuracy by computing Pearson correlations between measured feature intensities and known dilution ratios across a serial dilution series, then judging the processing workflow by the fraction of features exceeding a correlation threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-48009-6
skills.summary: Evaluates LC-MS1 feature quantification accuracy by computing Pearson correlations between measured feature intensities and known dilution ratios across a serial dilution series, then judging the processing workflow by the fraction of features exceeding a correlation threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table with no linked raw dilution-series spectra and no known dilution ratios, so correlations against expected concentrations cannot be computed. The dataset is a single-condition or case-control study with no dilution/concentration gradient — replicate QC by correlation to dilution ratio is undefined. The goal is MS2 compound-identification QC (e.g. DDA/DIA deconvolution or spectral library matching accuracy) rather than MS1 quantification accuracy.

skills.summary: Quantify reproducibility of metabolites per sample pair and sample pairs per metabolite in MS-Metabolomics replicate experiments using the nonparametric MaRR (Maximum Rank Reproducibility) maximal rank statistic, implemented in the R/Bioconductor marr package.

skills.search_text: metabolomics-sample-fingerprint-generation Use when you have LC-MS/MS samples (e.g. an MZmine-exported aligned feature table plus a GNPS FBMN-exported .mgf spectra file) and need a retention-time-agnostic sample-vs-sample comparison matrix built from MS2 peak/loss occurrence counts. Analysis requires quantitative use of MS1 feature intensities — MEMO fingerprints record only peak/loss occurrence (presence/absence), ignoring intensities. Comparison depends on retention-time behavior (e.g. detecting RT shifts) — MEMO is deliberately retention-time agnostic. Samples were compared where a well-behaved feature overlap exists and standard feature-table metrics suffice — MEMO targets chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap. Generates MS2-based sample fingerprints by counting the occurrence of MS2 peaks and neutral losses (to the precursor) per sample, then aligns them into a shared sample-by-feature MEMO matrix. This provides a retention-time-agnostic vectorization of LC-MS/MS samples that works without a prior feature alignment step. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964

skills.search_text: metabolomics-spectra-matrix-export Use when a set of calibrated 1D 1H NMR spectra (Bruker/Agilent FID, Bruker 1r files, or nmrML) has been baseline-corrected and realigned across selected ppm areas in NMRProcFlow and a spectral data matrix must be produced for statistical analysis. skills.search_text: metabolomics-statistics-subsetting Use when a metabolomics data frame with KEGG compound IDs has been statistically tested (e.g. omu_summary student's t-test with BH adjustment) and only metabolites of interest (e.g. adjusted p <= 0.05) should be carried into KEGG enzyme/gene annotation. The input is a raw untested metabolomics count table that has not yet been analyzed with omu_summary or omu_anova — run the statistical tests first. Compounds lacking KEGG numbers are the target of interest; keep_unknowns/KEGG annotation paths handle those separately and subsetting on adjusted p values will not add identifiers. The goal is compound hierarchy classification alone without enzyme/gene annotation — assign_hierarchy with a KEGG identifier suffices without the KEGG_gather subsetting pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A workflow for reducing an omu metabolomics count data frame (with KEGG compound identifiers) to statistically significant metabolites of interest, so that downstream KEGG orthology and gene annotation via KEGG_gather/assign_hierarchy is performed only on biologically relevant compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00129-19

skills.name: metabolomics-supervised-modeling-reporting
skills.search_text: metabolomics-supervised-modeling-reporting Use when GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite feature tables (e.g. 195 metabolites from plasma) carry sample-class labels such as S. Typhi carriage, S. Paratyphi A carriage, and non-carriage controls, and the goal is supervised discrimination with significance testing and ROC-validated latent biomarkers. The question is purely exploratory structure discovery with no class labels or discrimination hypothesis — plain PCA suffices and supervised OPLS-DA would overfit. skills.summary: Builds and reports supervised chemometric models (PCA for unsupervised overview, OPLS-DA for class discrimination) on GCxGC-TOFMS plasma metabolite profiles, extracting model significance p-values and ROC-validated biomarker panels (e.g. a five-metabolite carriage signature) into structured records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is purely exploratory structure discovery with no class labels or discrimination hypothesis — plain PCA suffices and supervised OPLS-DA would overfit. The comparison targets acute enteric fever signatures rather than chronic carriage — the article notes substantial heterogeneity between these profiles, so carriage-model p-values should not be reused.

skills.search_text: metadata-curation-for-spectra Use when a .msp mass spectral library file has records missing metadata such as SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, formula, or CAS number, and those identifiers must be fetched or derived before downstream annotation. The spectral records already contain complete, correctly formed metadata (SMILES, InChI, CAS number) and no post-processing enrichment is needed. You need offline annotation with no network access — the web converters (CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) query external services over HTTP, so only computed converters like RDKit would work. The input is not a mass spectral library in .msp (or supported) format but an unrelated feature table or raw instrument file. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Annotate mass spectral library records in .msp files with missing metadata (InChI, IUPAC name, canonical SMILES, formula, CAS number) by querying external identifier-conversion services (CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) through MSMetaEnhancer's asynchronous workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04494
skills.summary: Annotate mass spectral library records in .msp files with missing metadata (InChI, IUPAC name, canonical SMILES, formula, CAS number) by querying external identifier-conversion services (CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) through MSMetaEnhancer's asynchronous workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectral records already contain complete, correctly formed metadata (SMILES, InChI, CAS number) and no post-processing enrichment is needed. You need offline annotation with no network access — the web converters (CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) query external services over HTTP, so only computed converters like RDKit would work. The input is not a mass spectral library in .msp (or supported) format but an unrelated feature table or raw instrument file.

skills.description: Use when a QIIME PCoA plot of beta-diversity ordination must be recolored or its points shown/hidden per arbitrary metadata column (categorical, gradient, or MIxS standard) for exploratory visual analysis of large microbial community datasets.
skills.name: metadata-driven-point-recoloring
skills.search_text: metadata-driven-point-recoloring Use when a QIIME PCoA plot of beta-diversity ordination must be recolored or its points shown/hidden per arbitrary metadata column (categorical, gradient, or MIxS standard) for exploratory visual analysis of large microbial community datasets. Input is not a PCoA/beta-diversity ordination paired with a metadata mapping file, e.g. raw sequencing reads or a 2D heatmap where ordination-based recoloring does not apply. The task requires heavy custom computation inside the visualization (EMPeror is an exploratory WebGL viewer in Chrome, not a statistics engine for post-hoc analysis). A reproducible static figure for publication is needed rather than an interactive browser-based exploration; generic plotting packages like MATLAB, R, Excel, or Matplotlib would be more suitable. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Recolor and toggle visibility of 3D principal-coordinates plot points as a function of per-sample metadata categories (including MIxS-family GSC fields), using EMPeror's decoupled coloring and visibility controllers embedded in a standalone HTML5/WebGL page. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/2047-217x-2-16
skills.summary: Recolor and toggle visibility of 3D principal-coordinates plot points as a function of per-sample metadata categories (including MIxS-family GSC fields), using EMPeror's decoupled coloring and visibility controllers embedded in a standalone HTML5/WebGL page.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a PCoA/beta-diversity ordination paired with a metadata mapping file, e.g. raw sequencing reads or a 2D heatmap where ordination-based recoloring does not apply. The task requires heavy custom computation inside the visualization (EMPeror is an exploratory WebGL viewer in Chrome, not a statistics engine for post-hoc analysis). skills.description: Use when an expression dataset carries sample metadata (organ, tumor/non-tumor status, disease stage) and analyses — correlation QC, Mann–Whitney U tests, outlier screening — must be stratified by biological condition rather than run across all samples pooled.
skills.name: metadata-driven-sample-grouping
skills.search_text: metadata-driven-sample-grouping Use when an expression dataset carries sample metadata (organ, tumor/non-tumor status, disease stage) and analyses — correlation QC, Mann–Whitney U tests, outlier screening — must be stratified by biological condition rather than run across all samples pooled. The dataset lacks sample metadata or metadata cannot be integrated into the project, so groups cannot be defined by organ/tumor status The goal is a pooled, whole-dataset analysis (e.g. globally consistent DE genes across all cancers) where condition-level separation would change the question Input is single-condition data with no tumor/non-tumor or stage contrast to stratify http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Group expression-dataset samples by biological condition using integrated sample metadata (e.g. organ/cancer type and tumor status in the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset) before downstream QC and statistical tests in MetaOmGraph (MOG). Metadata-driven grouping underpins pairwise sample-correlation QC, outlier detection, and group-wise differential expression analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Group expression-dataset samples by biological condition using integrated sample metadata (e.g. organ/cancer type and tumor status in the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset) before downstream QC and statistical tests in MetaOmGraph (MOG). Metadata-driven grouping underpins pairwise sample-correlation QC, outlier detection, and group-wise differential expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks sample metadata or metadata cannot be integrated into the project, so groups cannot be defined by organ/tumor status The goal is a pooled, whole-dataset analysis (e.g. globally consistent DE genes across all cancers) where condition-level separation would change the question Input is single-condition data with no tumor/non-tumor or stage contrast to stratify

skills.description: Use when you have a large phylogeny (thousands of leaf taxa, e.g., a 3,737-taxon PhyloPhlAn tree in PhyloXML format) plus per-leaf genome metadata (module presence/absence, continuous values like genome size) that must be overlaid as external rings on a circular cladogram.
skills.name: metadata-ring-annotation
skills.search_text: metadata-ring-annotation Use when you have a large phylogeny (thousands of leaf taxa, e.g., a 3,737-taxon PhyloPhlAn tree in PhyloXML format) plus per-leaf genome metadata (module presence/absence, continuous values like genome size) that must be overlaid as external rings on a circular cladogram. Your goal is interactive exploration of a moderate-size tree with metadata overlays — iTOL or Krona target that interactive use case; GraPhlAn ring annotation is command-driven and aimed at static publication figures Your input is a taxonomic/metagenomic abundance table rather than a phylogeny — convert profile data via export2graphlan/hclust2 workflows first, or use a heatmap tool like hclust2 instead of tree ring annotation Your metadata must be attached to internal clade highlights, backgrounds, or biomarker shading from LEfSe rather than per-leaf external rings http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Annotate a large phylogenetic tree with genome-specific metadata (e.g., KEGG functional modules and genome size) as concentric external rings using GraPhlAn's annotation mechanism, rendering a compact circular cladogram with matplotlib. This enables visualizing thousands of taxa together with per-genome functional or phenotypic metadata in a single publication-quality figure. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Annotate a large phylogenetic tree with genome-specific metadata (e.g., KEGG functional modules and genome size) as concentric external rings using GraPhlAn's annotation mechanism, rendering a compact circular cladogram with matplotlib. This enables visualizing thousands of taxa together with per-genome functional or phenotypic metadata in a single publication-quality figure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is interactive exploration of a moderate-size tree with metadata overlays — iTOL or Krona target that interactive use case; GraPhlAn ring annotation is command-driven and aimed at static publication figures Your input is a taxonomic/metagenomic abundance table rather than a phylogeny — convert profile data via export2graphlan/hclust2 workflows first, or use a heatmap tool like hclust2 instead of tree ring annotation Your metadata must be attached to internal clade highlights, backgrounds, or biomarker shading from LEfSe rather than per-leaf external rings

skills.name: metadata-stratified-sample-clustering
skills.search_text: metadata-stratified-sample-clustering Use when a multi-batch untargeted metabolomics peak-area table (e.g., brain, serum, liver, cecal content, feces from 3xTg and 5xFAD mouse cohorts) must be checked for batch/cohort clustering before differential analysis is pooled across studies. Data are already a normalized, compositional feature table that has been stratified and does not require a batch/clustering check. The analysis goal is a targeted quantification of a single metabolite rather than an exploratory clustering assessment of an untargeted peak-area matrix.

skills.description: Use when you have mzmine feature lists from .raw/.mzML flow injection acquisitions plus a cleaned metadata sheet and need to map each feature to its compound ID (e.g. to reproduce coverage counts like 30,008 unique molecules across ionization modes).
skills.name: metadata-to-feature-mapping
skills.search_text: metadata-to-feature-mapping Use when you have mzmine feature lists from .raw/.mzML flow injection acquisitions plus a cleaned metadata sheet and need to map each feature to its compound ID (e.g. to reproduce coverage counts like 30,008 unique molecules across ionization modes). Input is already a compound-level feature table with assigned compound identifiers — re-running the metadata join would duplicate mappings Metadata has not passed through the metadata cleanup flow and lacks the template columns (unique sample id, plate_id, well location) — the join keys will not match The goal is spectral library generation (MSn tree building) rather than compound coverage/detection statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Joins mzmine-extracted per-file feature lists from flow injection Orbitrap MSn acquisitions against the cleaned metadata table so every detected feature is assigned to a unique compound identifier, enabling per-ionization-mode compound counts and positive/negative mode set intersections. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0
skills.summary: Joins mzmine-extracted per-file feature lists from flow injection Orbitrap MSn acquisitions against the cleaned metadata table so every detected feature is assigned to a unique compound identifier, enabling per-ionization-mode compound counts and positive/negative mode set intersections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a compound-level feature table with assigned compound identifiers — re-running the metadata join would duplicate mappings Metadata has not passed through the metadata cleanup flow and lacks the template columns (unique sample id, plate_id, well location) — the join keys will not match The goal is spectral library generation (MSn tree building) rather than compound coverage/detection statistics

skills.description: Use when running a matchms SpectrumProcessor library-cleaning pipeline (e.g. on the GNPS public library) and you need a per-filter breakdown of how many spectra were deleted, had metadata changed, or had peak information changed.
skills.name: metadata-versus-peak-change-differentiation
skills.search_text: metadata-versus-peak-change-differentiation Use when running a matchms SpectrumProcessor library-cleaning pipeline (e.g. on the GNPS public library) and you need a per-filter breakdown of how many spectra were deleted, had metadata changed, or had peak information changed. When you only need a cleaned library without auditing which filter changed what — the three-class breakdown is a reporting artifact, not a cleaning step itself. When spectra carry no annotations at all (e.g. unannotated MGF peaks lists): the metadata-change column relies on annotation fields (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, adduct, precursor m/z) that may be absent. When you need plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments — the article notes wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass go unnoticed, and fragment-matching filters are only a possible future expansion. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Interpret matchms library-cleaning processing reports by classifying each filter's effect on spectra into three distinct change classes: complete spectrum removal, metadata-only changes, and peak-information changes. This differentiation is the reporting backbone of the reproducible MS/MS library cleaning pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: Interpret matchms library-cleaning processing reports by classifying each filter's effect on spectra into three distinct change classes: complete spectrum removal, metadata-only changes, and peak-information changes. This differentiation is the reporting backbone of the reproducible MS/MS library cleaning pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need a cleaned library without auditing which filter changed what — the three-class breakdown is a reporting artifact, not a cleaning step itself. When spectra carry no annotations at all (e.g. unannotated MGF peaks lists): the metadata-change column relies on annotation fields (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, adduct, precursor m/z) that may be absent. When you need plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments — the article notes wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass go unnoticed, and fragment-matching filters are only a possible future expansion.

skills.search_text: metadata-vocabulary-extension Use when a user has confirmed a freetext sample-metadata term that is absent from an existing SMetaS vocabulary and the tf-idf/nearest-neighbors matching models must be rebuilt to recognize it. The freetext terms already exist in the target vocabulary — use SMetaS's normal synonym-matching/typo-fixing standardization instead of extending it New terms are not user-confirmed and would only be guessed additions to the vocabulary The task is bulk standardization of an existing metadata table rather than maintenance of the vocabulary/models themselves Extends SMetaS sample-metadata vocabularies with user-confirmed freetext terms (e.g., 'allergen exposure', 'ozone', 'hours/day') and retracts/retrains the n-grams/tf-idf/nearest-neighbors models so future mappings resolve to the new entries. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941
skills.summary: Extends SMetaS sample-metadata vocabularies with user-confirmed freetext terms (e.g., 'allergen exposure', 'ozone', 'hours/day') and retracts/retrains the n-grams/tf-idf/nearest-neighbors models so future mappings resolve to the new entries.

skills.description: Use when sample metadata records contain inconsistent, freetext descriptor terms that must be mapped to fixed vocabularies before database integration, cross-study comparison, or ontological parent aggregation.
skills.name: metadata-vocabulary-standardization
skills.search_text: metadata-vocabulary-standardization Use when sample metadata records contain inconsistent, freetext descriptor terms that must be mapped to fixed vocabularies before database integration, cross-study comparison, or ontological parent aggregation. Input metadata already consist of terms from fixed vocabularies with no freetext variants — standardization would only risk remapping correct terms. The goal is capturing relationships beyond simple 'is a' links (e.g. co-cultures) — the fixed tabular representation cannot hold these; extend to a node/edge graph representation instead. Cross-study statistical meta-analysis on raw metabolomics data is needed — SMetaS standardizes metadata only, not metabolomics measurements. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Standardize freetext metabolomics sample metadata by replacing freetext terms with terms from fixed vocabularies, using synonym matching and typographical fixing in an n-grams/nearest neighbors model approach (SMetaS/MetaS). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941
skills.summary: Standardize freetext metabolomics sample metadata by replacing freetext terms with terms from fixed vocabularies, using synonym matching and typographical fixing in an n-grams/nearest neighbors model approach (SMetaS/MetaS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metadata already consist of terms from fixed vocabularies with no freetext variants — standardization would only risk remapping correct terms. The goal is capturing relationships beyond simple 'is a' links (e.g. co-cultures) — the fixed tabular representation cannot hold these; extend to a node/edge graph representation instead. Cross-study statistical meta-analysis on raw metabolomics data is needed — SMetaS standardizes metadata only, not metabolomics measurements.

skills.summary: A three-pass curation procedure, implemented in the containerized SMetaS/MetaS application, that transforms freetext sample metadata strings into ontology-derived vocabulary terms via tf-idf n-grams/nearest-neighbor matching, substring search over fixed vocabularies, and user-confirmed creation of genuinely new terms.

skills.name: metagenomic-abundance-table-conversion
skills.search_text: metagenomic-abundance-table-conversion Use when you have a taxonomy- or function-annotated abundance table (MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN text output or BIOM v1/v2 file, e.g. from QIIME or mothur 16S studies) and need GraPhlAn input files for circular visualization. skills.summary: Convert metagenomic/metataxonomic abundance tables — including MetaPhlAn, LEfSe, HUMAnN outputs and BIOM-format files (e.g. 16S rRNA profiles such as vaginal microbiota data) — into the GraPhlAn tree.txt and annot.txt files using export2graphlan, for rendering circular phylogenetic visualizations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a GraPhlAn tree/annotation pair or raw phylogenetic tree without abundance data — export2graphlan is a converter for abundance/biomarker tables. The goal is interactive exploration rather than a publication-quality static circular figure — tools like iTOL or Krona target that use case. The abundance table is unclassified at any taxonomic level and --internal_levels cannot reconcile hierarchy, so leaf-to-root summation is undefined.

skills.description: Use when you have assembled genomes or metagenomes (e.g., 40 cyanobacterial samples from the PoDP) and need annotated BGC GenBank files plus a BGC-BGC similarity matrix to link metabolites to gene clusters.
skills.name: metagenomic-bgc-annotation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-bgc-annotation Use when you have assembled genomes or metagenomes (e.g., 40 cyanobacterial samples from the PoDP) and need annotated BGC GenBank files plus a BGC-BGC similarity matrix to link metabolites to gene clusters. Input is MS/MS spectral data only with no genome or metagenome to mine for BGCs — the annotation step requires assembled nucleotide sequence The target organism has no BGCs similar to the training set (e.g., a fungal species dissimilar to the PoDP-derived training BGCs), so downstream fingerprint matching yields no answer The goal is de novo metabolite structure elucidation rather than BGC-metabolite linking — NPOmix-style correlation cannot confirm 2D/3D structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_3370 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Annotates biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) in cyanobacterial genomes and metagenomes with antiSMASH and computes pairwise BGC similarity networks with BiG-SCAPE, producing the similarity tables and fingerprints that downstream NPOmix-style KNN classifiers consume. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Annotates biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) in cyanobacterial genomes and metagenomes with antiSMASH and computes pairwise BGC similarity networks with BiG-SCAPE, producing the similarity tables and fingerprints that downstream NPOmix-style KNN classifiers consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is MS/MS spectral data only with no genome or metagenome to mine for BGCs — the annotation step requires assembled nucleotide sequence The target organism has no BGCs similar to the training set (e.g., a fungal species dissimilar to the PoDP-derived training BGCs), so downstream fingerprint matching yields no answer The goal is de novo metabolite structure elucidation rather than BGC-metabolite linking — NPOmix-style correlation cannot confirm 2D/3D structures

skills.description: Use when you have LEfSe biomarker results and a MetaPhlAn (or HUMAnN) abundance profile and need a publication-quality circular cladogram highlighting discriminatory taxa with metadata overlays.
skills.name: metagenomic-biomarker-visualization
skills.search_text: metagenomic-biomarker-visualization Use when you have LEfSe biomarker results and a MetaPhlAn (or HUMAnN) abundance profile and need a publication-quality circular cladogram highlighting discriminatory taxa with metadata overlays. Input is already a GraPhlAn tree/annotation pair — use GraPhlAn directly instead of re-converting. Interactive exploration of large phylogenies is the goal (iTOL/Krona are the comparison points in the paper), not reproducible pipeline rendering. skills.summary: Automatically converts MetaPhlAn, LEfSe, and/or HUMAnN outputs into GraPhlAn tree and annotation files, then renders high-quality circular phylogenies (e.g., the HMP aerobiosis cladogram, Fig. S1) with LEfSe biomarker LDA scores mapped to clade sizes and class assignments to shaded backgrounds.

skills.description: Use when you have shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ from fecal samples) and need functional pathway enrichment comparisons between groups rather than only taxonomic composition.
skills.name: metagenomic-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-functional-annotation Use when you have shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ from fecal samples) and need functional pathway enrichment comparisons between groups rather than only taxonomic composition. Input is already a pathway abundance or functional table — skip read-level annotation and go straight to differential testing. The goal is taxonomic (species-level) profiling only; use the taxonomic profiler instead of aggregating to KEGG pathways. http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Annotates metagenomic sequencing reads to functional gene families or orthologs (e.g. KEGG orthologs) and aggregates them into pathway abundance profiles so that functional, rather than only taxonomic, differences between host genotypes can be tested and visualized. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Annotates metagenomic sequencing reads to functional gene families or orthologs (e.g. KEGG orthologs) and aggregates them into pathway abundance profiles so that functional, rather than only taxonomic, differences between host genotypes can be tested and visualized.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway abundance or functional table — skip read-level annotation and go straight to differential testing. The goal is taxonomic (species-level) profiling only; use the taxonomic profiler instead of aggregating to KEGG pathways.

skills.description: Use when starting from microbial genome assemblies and needing predicted MGCs/BGCs reduced to representative GCFs as mapping targets for metagenomic or metatranscriptomic abundance analysis.
skills.name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-mining
skills.search_text: metagenomic-gene-cluster-mining Use when starting from microbial genome assemblies and needing predicted MGCs/BGCs reduced to representative GCFs as mapping targets for metagenomic or metatranscriptomic abundance analysis. The gene clusters are already predicted and dereplicated and you only need read mapping/abundance — use bigmap-map/bigmap-download directly instead. The dataset is already an abundance/feature table (e.g., RPKM per sample per cluster); mining genomes again would not apply. You need pathway-level functional profiling from reads alone without reference genomes (tools like HUMAnN2, MetaPath, FMAP, Metatrans are the alternatives the paper contrasts against). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Predict metabolic gene clusters (MGCs) from microbial reference genomes with gutSMASH/antiSMASH and group them into non-redundant gene cluster families (GCFs) with BiG-MAP's MinHash and BiG-SCAPE filtering, so metagenomic reads can be mapped to distinct cluster representatives for abundance profiling. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Predict metabolic gene clusters (MGCs) from microbial reference genomes with gutSMASH/antiSMASH and group them into non-redundant gene cluster families (GCFs) with BiG-MAP's MinHash and BiG-SCAPE filtering, so metagenomic reads can be mapped to distinct cluster representatives for abundance profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene clusters are already predicted and dereplicated and you only need read mapping/abundance — use bigmap-map/bigmap-download directly instead. The dataset is already an abundance/feature table (e.g., RPKM per sample per cluster); mining genomes again would not apply. You need pathway-level functional profiling from reads alone without reference genomes (tools like HUMAnN2, MetaPath, FMAP, Metatrans are the alternatives the paper contrasts against).

skills.summary: Predicts protein-coding genes on de novo-assembled metagenomic scaftigs using Prodigal (or MetaGeneMark) as implemented in MetaRon, providing the gene coordinates needed for downstream proximon and operon prediction without functional or experimental information.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic profiler against a known ground truth (e.g. CAMI marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and you need clade-level presence/absence discordance beyond F1 or UniFrac scores.

skills.summary: Run TAMPA in contrast mode to compare a taxonomic profiler's output against a gold-standard CAMI2 marine profile at a fixed taxonomic rank (e.g. class/phylum), flagging clades unique to one profile as false positives or false negatives — differences that single-valued metrics such as the F1 score miss.

skills.description: Use when analyzing metaproteomics tandem MS/MS spectra against metagenome-derived protein databases (metapeptide or non-redundant environmental FASTA), or when benchmarking database search vs de novo peptide-detection counts.
skills.name: metagenomic-protein-database-construction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-protein-database-construction Use when analyzing metaproteomics tandem MS/MS spectra against metagenome-derived protein databases (metapeptide or non-redundant environmental FASTA), or when benchmarking database search vs de novo peptide-detection counts. The sample's protein complement is known in advance (e.g. a single organism) — sequence database searching against a standard reference database suffices and metagenome-informed database construction is unnecessary The goal is assigning de novo peptides to foreign spectra beyond target-decoy matching — the target-decoy matching approach 'misses out on the power of de novo sequencing to assign peptides to foreign spectra' The data are not bottom-up DDA tandem MS/MS spectra suitable for Casanovo or Tide http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Constructs and applies sample-specific protein search databases for metaproteomics — a metagenome-derived metapeptide database and a non-redundant environmental protein database — so that database-search (Tide+Percolator) and de novo (Casanovo) peptide detection can be compared against the same matched peptide space. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-49731-x
skills.summary: Constructs and applies sample-specific protein search databases for metaproteomics — a metagenome-derived metapeptide database and a non-redundant environmental protein database — so that database-search (Tide+Percolator) and de novo (Casanovo) peptide detection can be compared against the same matched peptide space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample's protein complement is known in advance (e.g. a single organism) — sequence database searching against a standard reference database suffices and metagenome-informed database construction is unnecessary The goal is assigning de novo peptides to foreign spectra beyond target-decoy matching — the target-decoy matching approach 'misses out on the power of de novo sequencing to assign peptides to foreign spectra' The data are not bottom-up DDA tandem MS/MS spectra suitable for Casanovo or Tide

skills.description: Use when you have predicted operon sequences from metagenomic shotgun samples and raw paired-end reads, and need per-sample pathway/KO abundances to compare disease versus control groups.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-operons
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-operons Use when you have predicted operon sequences from metagenomic shotgun samples and raw paired-end reads, and need per-sample pathway/KO abundances to compare disease versus control groups. skills.description: Use when a Qiita-deposited fecal shotgun metagenomics feature table (n=666 paired SPF fecal samples) with metadata fields genotype/study/sex/cohort must be subset (e.g., Sacrifice cohort, per-study) before PERMANOVA or beta-diversity testing.

skills.search_text: metagenomic-sample-metadata-stratification Use when a Qiita-deposited fecal shotgun metagenomics feature table (n=666 paired SPF fecal samples) with metadata fields genotype/study/sex/cohort must be subset (e.g., Sacrifice cohort, per-study) before PERMANOVA or beta-diversity testing. The analysis targets Longitudinal-cohort fecal samples: they were collected randomly per cage without animal IDs, so single-animal metadata linkage (and genotype-stratified testing) is not possible. The question concerns untargeted metabolomics feature abundance (e.g., serum carnitines) rather than metagenomic community composition tested via beta diversity/PERMANOVA. skills.description: Use when molecular networks contain ion variants annotated as [M+Na]+ (or other metal adducts) that fail to link to their [M+H]+ counterparts under conventional similarity-threshold networks, and you need to verify whether the connectivity method recovers the true metabolite relationship.
skills.name: metal-adduct-fragmentation-analysis
skills.search_text: metal-adduct-fragmentation-analysis Use when molecular networks contain ion variants annotated as [M+Na]+ (or other metal adducts) that fail to link to their [M+H]+ counterparts under conventional similarity-threshold networks, and you need to verify whether the connectivity method recovers the true metabolite relationship. Input is already a feature table with adduct relationships resolved (e.g. via CAMERA-style annotation) — no network connectivity check is needed Spectra are compared within the same adduct class (e.g. [M+H]+ vs [M+H]+ only), where conventional cosine thresholds already suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Identifies and links metal-adducted ion variants (e.g. [M+Na]+) to their protonated ([M+H]+) precursors in molecular networks, where metal adduction shifts fragmentation patterns and breaks conventional cosine-similarity links. Grounded in the molecular community networking (MCN) workflow that recovers these otherwise-hidden metabolite connections. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Identifies and links metal-adducted ion variants (e.g. [M+Na]+) to their protonated ([M+H]+) precursors in molecular networks, where metal adduction shifts fragmentation patterns and breaks conventional cosine-similarity links. Grounded in the molecular community networking (MCN) workflow that recovers these otherwise-hidden metabolite connections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table with adduct relationships resolved (e.g. via CAMERA-style annotation) — no network connectivity check is needed Spectra are compared within the same adduct class (e.g. [M+H]+ vs [M+H]+ only), where conventional cosine thresholds already suffice

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is chemical-class-based filtering rather than co-occurrence ranking — NPClassScore (0.25 cut-off) complements rather than replaces the Metcalf step and must be applied to surviving links afterwards The dataset's validated links show low standardised Metcalf scores at the default 2.5 cut-off, as happened for the Nocardia dataset, and no threshold adjustment is acceptable for the analysis No paired genome–metabolome data are available; Metcalf scoring requires strain-level co-occurrence across both omics layers

skills.name: metcalf-co-occurrence-scoring
skills.search_text: metcalf-co-occurrence-scoring Use when generating an initial set of candidate gene cluster family (GCF) to MS/MS spectrum links from paired genome–metabolome data before applying class-based filtering such as NPClassScore. When the goal is already class-matched, prioritised links — apply NPClassScore filtering (cut-off 0.25) on top of the Metcalf results instead of stopping at co-occurrence When no strain-level mapping between genomes and metabolomics samples is available, since co-occurrence scoring requires paired occurrence profiles When validated links are known to have low standardised Metcalf scores (e.g. the Nocardia dataset, where the threshold had to be lowered from 2.5 to 2) http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Standardised Metcalf co-occurrence scoring within NPLinker generates the initial candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links by correlating GCF occurrence across strains with spectrum presence, using a cut-off of 2.5.
