skills.description: Use when a PCoA/beta-diversity visualization of thousands of microbiome samples loads too slowly or produces unwieldy plot files, and you need quantitative load-time and file-size evidence to choose between visualization tools such as EMPeror and KiNG.
skills.name: microbiome-visualization-load-benchmarking
skills.search_text: microbiome-visualization-load-benchmarking Use when a PCoA/beta-diversity visualization of thousands of microbiome samples loads too slowly or produces unwieldy plot files, and you need quantitative load-time and file-size evidence to choose between visualization tools such as EMPeror and KiNG. The input is not PCoA/ordination data derived from a beta diversity distance matrix — EMPeror and KiNG both consume principal coordinates and mapping files, not raw feature tables or reads. The dataset is small (few dozen samples) with sparse metadata, where coordinate duplication per category in KiNG does not inflate files enough for load-time differences to be meaningful. You need a browser-independent GUI: EMPeror's GUI lists only Chrome as a requirement, so the benchmark result does not transfer to other browsers without retesting. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarking procedure for comparing browser-based 3D ordination visualization tools by loading time and output file size, validated on EMPeror versus KiNG using a 5,740-sample PCoA dataset with 120 metadata columns. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/2047-217x-2-16
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure for comparing browser-based 3D ordination visualization tools by loading time and output file size, validated on EMPeror versus KiNG using a 5,740-sample PCoA dataset with 120 metadata columns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not PCoA/ordination data derived from a beta diversity distance matrix — EMPeror and KiNG both consume principal coordinates and mapping files, not raw feature tables or reads. The dataset is small (few dozen samples) with sparse metadata, where coordinate duplication per category in KiNG does not inflate files enough for load-time differences to be meaningful. You need a browser-independent GUI: EMPeror's GUI lists only Chrome as a requirement, so the benchmark result does not transfer to other browsers without retesting.

skills.description: Use when a human GEM (e.g. RECON3D in SBML/cobrapy format) must be conditioned on gut microbiota metabolism — i.e. when studying metabolic interaction between gut microbes and human cells and exchange-reaction lower bounds need updating from microbial fluxes.
skills.name: microbiota-flux-aggregation
skills.search_text: microbiota-flux-aggregation Use when a human GEM (e.g. RECON3D in SBML/cobrapy format) must be conditioned on gut microbiota metabolism — i.e. when studying metabolic interaction between gut microbes and human cells and exchange-reaction lower bounds need updating from microbial fluxes. The model of interest is not a human GEM whose exchange reactions should be conditioned on gut microbial metabolism — M2R targets human GEMs like RECON3D. You need de novo simulation of microbiota community flux rather than modifying an existing human GEM's exchange bounds from selected microbes. No gut microbiota metabolic models are available as input — the aggregation step has nothing to incorporate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3895 Aggregate in- and out-fluxes from user-selected gut microbiota GEMs and apply them to modify the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D), using the M2R add-on to cobrapy. This changes the pool of metabolites entering and leaving the human GEM to reflect gut microbial metabolism. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: Aggregate in- and out-fluxes from user-selected gut microbiota GEMs and apply them to modify the lower bounds of exchange reactions in a human genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D), using the M2R add-on to cobrapy. This changes the pool of metabolites entering and leaving the human GEM to reflect gut microbial metabolism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model of interest is not a human GEM whose exchange reactions should be conditioned on gut microbial metabolism — M2R targets human GEMs like RECON3D. You need de novo simulation of microbiota community flux rather than modifying an existing human GEM's exchange bounds from selected microbes. No gut microbiota metabolic models are available as input — the aggregation step has nothing to incorporate.

skills.description: Use when you have a gut microbiota metabolic model (SBML) and need its per-metabolite boundary fluxes aggregated and normalized (scaled to e.g. 1000) to modify exchange-reaction lower bounds in a human GEM like RECON3D.
skills.name: microbiota-metabolic-model-parsing
skills.search_text: microbiota-metabolic-model-parsing Use when you have a gut microbiota metabolic model (SBML) and need its per-metabolite boundary fluxes aggregated and normalized (scaled to e.g. 1000) to modify exchange-reaction lower bounds in a human GEM like RECON3D. You need to run FBA on the human GEM itself (e.g. RECON3D) rather than extract boundary fluxes from a microbiota model — this skill only processes the microbe's model. Your microbiota model has no external (boundary) reactions to aggregate — the aggregation/normalization step is undefined in that case. You want to modify the human GEM directly without microbe-derived fluxes — plain cobrapy editing, not this skill, is the right approach. http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Parse a gut microbiota genome-scale metabolic model (SBML) with cobrapy, run FBA, and aggregate/normalize the in- and out-fluxes of every metabolite participating in the microbe's external (boundary) reactions so they can be used to modify a human GEM such as RECON3D via M2R. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: Parse a gut microbiota genome-scale metabolic model (SBML) with cobrapy, run FBA, and aggregate/normalize the in- and out-fluxes of every metabolite participating in the microbe's external (boundary) reactions so they can be used to modify a human GEM such as RECON3D via M2R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to run FBA on the human GEM itself (e.g. RECON3D) rather than extract boundary fluxes from a microbiota model — this skill only processes the microbe's model. Your microbiota model has no external (boundary) reactions to aggregate — the aggregation/normalization step is undefined in that case. You want to modify the human GEM directly without microbe-derived fluxes — plain cobrapy editing, not this skill, is the right approach.

skills.description: Use when a human GEM (e.g., RECON3D) must be modified with flux information from gut microbiota models, updating exchange-reaction lower bounds of reactions that contain metabolites present in the microbiota model.
skills.name: microbiota-metabolite-mapping-to-host-gem
skills.search_text: microbiota-metabolite-mapping-to-host-gem Use when a human GEM (e.g., RECON3D) must be modified with flux information from gut microbiota models, updating exchange-reaction lower bounds of reactions that contain metabolites present in the microbiota model. The microbiota model shares no metabolite identifiers with the host GEM, so no reactions can be matched and no bounds can be updated. The goal is to add reactions or modify upper bounds of the host GEM rather than adjust the lower bounds of exchange reactions. The task is simulation of the gut microbiota model alone, without integration into a human GEM like RECON3D. http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Applies M2R (a Python add-on to cobrapy) to incorporate gut microbiota metabolic models into a human genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) such as RECON3D by rewriting exchange-reaction lower bounds with aggregated microbiota in/out-fluxes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab060
skills.summary: Applies M2R (a Python add-on to cobrapy) to incorporate gut microbiota metabolic models into a human genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) such as RECON3D by rewriting exchange-reaction lower bounds with aggregated microbiota in/out-fluxes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The microbiota model shares no metabolite identifiers with the host GEM, so no reactions can be matched and no bounds can be updated. The goal is to add reactions or modify upper bounds of the host GEM rather than adjust the lower bounds of exchange reactions. The task is simulation of the gut microbiota model alone, without integration into a human GEM like RECON3D.

skills.description: Use when input microscopy consists of multiple tiles (e.g., tile_1.tif, tile_2.tif) accompanied by an out.txt coordinate file, and the tiles must be reassembled into a stitched pre- or post-MALDI image for ablation-mark-to-cell co-registration.
skills.name: microscopy-tile-stitching-from-coordinate-files
skills.search_text: microscopy-tile-stitching-from-coordinate-files Use when input microscopy consists of multiple tiles (e.g., tile_1.tif, tile_2.tif) accompanied by an out.txt coordinate file, and the tiles must be reassembled into a stitched pre- or post-MALDI image for ablation-mark-to-cell co-registration. The microscopy images are already pre-stitched — the README notes a future implementation 'will also be accepting pre-stitched images', so this tile-stitching step is unnecessary then The microscope output format is not Nikon Ti-E — the stitching code is explicitly optimized for that format and may not parse other coordinate files Ablation marks are overlapping or not visible in the post-MALDI microscopy — stitching alone cannot rescue the co-registration requirement http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3385 Stitches tiled pre- and post-MALDI microscopy acquisitions of a cell culture into whole-field images using the upper-left pixel x-y coordinates (in um) recorded in each tile's out.txt file, enabling co-registration of cells with MALDI laser ablation marks in SpaceM. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Stitches tiled pre- and post-MALDI microscopy acquisitions of a cell culture into whole-field images using the upper-left pixel x-y coordinates (in um) recorded in each tile's out.txt file, enabling co-registration of cells with MALDI laser ablation marks in SpaceM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The microscopy images are already pre-stitched — the README notes a future implementation 'will also be accepting pre-stitched images', so this tile-stitching step is unnecessary then The microscope output format is not Nikon Ti-E — the stitching code is explicitly optimized for that format and may not parse other coordinate files Ablation marks are overlapping or not visible in the post-MALDI microscopy — stitching alone cannot rescue the co-registration requirement

skills.description: Use when SpaceM input contains tiled microscopy acquisitions (tile_1.tif, tile_2.tif, ...) each paired with an out.txt coordinate file, and tiles must be merged before cell segmentation and MALDI-ablation co-registration.
skills.name: microscopy-tile-stitching-with-coordinates
skills.search_text: microscopy-tile-stitching-with-coordinates Use when SpaceM input contains tiled microscopy acquisitions (tile_1.tif, tile_2.tif, ...) each paired with an out.txt coordinate file, and tiles must be merged before cell segmentation and MALDI-ablation co-registration. Images are already pre-stitched — the README notes the next implementation version will accept pre-stitched images, but the current pipeline expects tiles plus out.txt coordinates Tile coordinate format does not match Nikon Ti-E microscope output — this code is explicitly optimized only for that format Post-MALDI microscopy lacks visible or has overlapping ablation marks — co-registration of metabolite intensities to cells will be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Stitch tiled pre- and post-MALDI microscopy images using per-tile upper-left pixel x-y coordinates from out.txt files, enabling SpaceM's subcellular co-registration of cells with MALDI laser ablation marks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Stitch tiled pre- and post-MALDI microscopy images using per-tile upper-left pixel x-y coordinates from out.txt files, enabling SpaceM's subcellular co-registration of cells with MALDI laser ablation marks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Images are already pre-stitched — the README notes the next implementation version will accept pre-stitched images, but the current pipeline expects tiles plus out.txt coordinates Tile coordinate format does not match Nikon Ti-E microscope output — this code is explicitly optimized only for that format Post-MALDI microscopy lacks visible or has overlapping ablation marks — co-registration of metabolite intensities to cells will be unreliable

skills.description: Use when untargeted metabolomics feature tables from different separation platforms (e.g., HILIC-Orbitrap MS ESI+/- and CE-Orbitrap MS) must be combined into one augmented dataset for joint statistical evaluation.
skills.name: mid-level-data-fusion-across-separation-techniques
skills.search_text: mid-level-data-fusion-across-separation-techniques Use when untargeted metabolomics feature tables from different separation platforms (e.g., HILIC-Orbitrap MS ESI+/- and CE-Orbitrap MS) must be combined into one augmented dataset for joint statistical evaluation. Data are single-platform only — existing tools like XCMS Online, MetaboAnalyst, MetaboAnalystR or MZmine handle single-platform analysis, and augmentation of different separation techniques adds no value. Features have not yet passed the upstream false-positive filter, since the augmentation step expects the filtered per-group data cubes as input. Features from two or more methods need to be connected precisely and autonomously via MS/MS spectra — AriumMS does not implement MS/MS spectral networking (listed as future development). http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 AriumMS's mid-level data fusion links per-separation-method feature data cubes (e.g., HILIC-MS and CE-MS) along the m/z dimension into a single augmented feature space, collapsing cross-group features with identical mass and occurrence count so multi-platform data can be evaluated with one chemometric result. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: AriumMS's mid-level data fusion links per-separation-method feature data cubes (e.g., HILIC-MS and CE-MS) along the m/z dimension into a single augmented feature space, collapsing cross-group features with identical mass and occurrence count so multi-platform data can be evaluated with one chemometric result.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-platform only — existing tools like XCMS Online, MetaboAnalyst, MetaboAnalystR or MZmine handle single-platform analysis, and augmentation of different separation techniques adds no value. Features have not yet passed the upstream false-positive filter, since the augmentation step expects the filtered per-group data cubes as input. Features from two or more methods need to be connected precisely and autonomously via MS/MS spectra — AriumMS does not implement MS/MS spectral networking (listed as future development).

skills.description: Use when combining untargeted MS datasets from different separation techniques (e.g., CE-MS and HILIC-MS in ESI+ and ESI−) into one augmented feature table to increase metabolome coverage beyond any single method.
skills.name: mid-level-data-fusion-evaluation
skills.search_text: mid-level-data-fusion-evaluation Use when combining untargeted MS datasets from different separation techniques (e.g., CE-MS and HILIC-MS in ESI+ and ESI−) into one augmented feature table to increase metabolome coverage beyond any single method. The analysis is single-platform only — tools like XCMS Online, MetaboAnalyst, MetaboAnalystR, or MZmine handle single-platform processing without augmentation The datasets cannot be processed with method-specific parameters because different separation techniques need individual settings (AriumMS exists precisely because standard tools do not support per-method preprocessing in one run) MS/MS spectral networking or coupling of spectroscopic data with chromatographic/electrophoretic data is required — these are not implemented in AriumMS http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Performs mid-level data fusion (augmentation) of multi-platform untargeted metabolomics datasets — here three CE-Orbitrap MS and two HILIC-Orbitrap MS methods — using AriumMS's ROI-based workflow, yielding a single fused feature table for chemometric evaluation and target/suspect coverage counting. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Performs mid-level data fusion (augmentation) of multi-platform untargeted metabolomics datasets — here three CE-Orbitrap MS and two HILIC-Orbitrap MS methods — using AriumMS's ROI-based workflow, yielding a single fused feature table for chemometric evaluation and target/suspect coverage counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is single-platform only — tools like XCMS Online, MetaboAnalyst, MetaboAnalystR, or MZmine handle single-platform processing without augmentation The datasets cannot be processed with method-specific parameters because different separation techniques need individual settings (AriumMS exists precisely because standard tools do not support per-method preprocessing in one run) MS/MS spectral networking or coupling of spectroscopic data with chromatographic/electrophoretic data is required — these are not implemented in AriumMS

skills.description: Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS mzML data where migration times vary substantially across runs or batches (e.g. nonlinear electroosmotic flow changes) and analyte peaks must be annotated and integrated without manual realignment.
skills.name: migration-index-based-migration-time-prediction
skills.search_text: migration-index-based-migration-time-prediction Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS mzML data where migration times vary substantially across runs or batches (e.g. nonlinear electroosmotic flow changes) and analyte peaks must be annotated and integrated without manual realignment. Data are already aligned or come from a separation technique with stable migration times where simple retention-time matching suffices (the MTI machinery is specific to MSI-CE-MS variability). The analysis is untargeted feature discovery rather than targeted annotation of a known analyte mass list — PeakMeister requires a targeted mass list with known m/z values. Late-migrating metabolites lack two flanking or a stable-isotope internal standard — the article warns these are prone to peak misannotation and should not be trusted without extra validation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Predict analyte migration times in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs using migration time indices (MTI) computed from a panel of internal standards, avoiding computationally intensive dynamic time warping or effective mobility transformations. Implemented in PeakMeister to enable reliable peak annotation across batches despite large migration time fluctuations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03513
skills.summary: Predict analyte migration times in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs using migration time indices (MTI) computed from a panel of internal standards, avoiding computationally intensive dynamic time warping or effective mobility transformations. Implemented in PeakMeister to enable reliable peak annotation across batches despite large migration time fluctuations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already aligned or come from a separation technique with stable migration times where simple retention-time matching suffices (the MTI machinery is specific to MSI-CE-MS variability). The analysis is untargeted feature discovery rather than targeted annotation of a known analyte mass list — PeakMeister requires a targeted mass list with known m/z values. Late-migrating metabolites lack two flanking or a stable-isotope internal standard — the article warns these are prone to peak misannotation and should not be trusted without extra validation.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS data with large, nonlinear migration time fluctuations across batches, where peak alignment and metabolite annotation must be automated at scale (e.g., thousands of serum samples).
skills.name: migration-index-based-peak-annotation
skills.search_text: migration-index-based-peak-annotation Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS data with large, nonlinear migration time fluctuations across batches, where peak alignment and metabolite annotation must be automated at scale (e.g., thousands of serum samples). Input data are already preprocessed feature/peak-area tables rather than raw MSI-CE-MS mzML files Analytes are late-migrating serum metabolites lacking two flanking or a stable-isotope internal standard — these are prone to peak misannotation and need manual review Sample matrices other than serum (e.g., urine, saliva, stool) — PeakMeister has not yet been validated for these matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotate and integrate metabolite peaks in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS electropherograms by computing migration time indices (MTI) from a panel of 11 internal standards, rather than time-warping or effective-mobility transformations. This is the core algorithm implemented in PeakMeister for high-fidelity automated peak annotation of serum metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03513
skills.summary: Annotate and integrate metabolite peaks in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS electropherograms by computing migration time indices (MTI) from a panel of 11 internal standards, rather than time-warping or effective-mobility transformations. This is the core algorithm implemented in PeakMeister for high-fidelity automated peak annotation of serum metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already preprocessed feature/peak-area tables rather than raw MSI-CE-MS mzML files Analytes are late-migrating serum metabolites lacking two flanking or a stable-isotope internal standard — these are prone to peak misannotation and need manual review Sample matrices other than serum (e.g., urine, saliva, stool) — PeakMeister has not yet been validated for these matrices

skills.description: Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS mzML data where migration time drift (~105 s uncorrected) breaks peak alignment, and internal standards flank the analytes so MTIs can predict elution times.
skills.name: migration-time-index-calibration
skills.search_text: migration-time-index-calibration Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS mzML data where migration time drift (~105 s uncorrected) breaks peak alignment, and internal standards flank the analytes so MTIs can predict elution times. Input data are not multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs — the inter-peak spacing confirmation and sample position assignment (1-13) assume serial injections within each run Sample matrices other than serum (e.g., urine, saliva, stool), for which PeakMeister is not yet validated Untargeted metabolomics where no targeted mass list or internal-standard reference migration times are available http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Calibrates metabolite migration times in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs using migration time indexes (MTIs) computed from a panel of internal standards, replacing time-warping or effective-mobility alignment with a computationally simple interpolation between each analyte's flanking standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03513
skills.summary: Calibrates metabolite migration times in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs using migration time indexes (MTIs) computed from a panel of internal standards, replacing time-warping or effective-mobility alignment with a computationally simple interpolation between each analyte's flanking standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not multiplexed MSI-CE-MS runs — the inter-peak spacing confirmation and sample position assignment (1-13) assume serial injections within each run Sample matrices other than serum (e.g., urine, saliva, stool), for which PeakMeister is not yet validated Untargeted metabolomics where no targeted mass list or internal-standard reference migration times are available

skills.description: Use when a metabolite concentration table (CSV/XLSX) has columns designated as metabolite concentrations in Viime and per-sample values need range rescaling so all metabolites share a comparable scale prior to transformation, scaling, or PCA inspection.
skills.name: min-max-concentration-normalization
skills.search_text: min-max-concentration-normalization Use when a metabolite concentration table (CSV/XLSX) has columns designated as metabolite concentrations in Viime and per-sample values need range rescaling so all metabolites share a comparable scale prior to transformation, scaling, or PCA inspection. The table still contains uncorrected errors or missing values — Viime performs error detection and automatic imputation before normalization, so normalize only after imputation. The intended normalization is reference-sample-sum, fixed-sum (default 100), or weight/volume based — pick that specific method instead; Viime lets the user select among them. The goal is post-normalization treatment (Log10/Log2/square-root/cube-root transformation or autoscaling/Pareto/range/vast/level scaling) — those are distinct downstream steps, not this one. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Rescales each metabolite concentration column of a sample-by-metabolite table (CSV/XLSX) to a common [0,1] range via min-max normalization, one of the user-selectable normalization options in Viime's data-treatment pipeline, applied before transformation and scaling. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Rescales each metabolite concentration column of a sample-by-metabolite table (CSV/XLSX) to a common [0,1] range via min-max normalization, one of the user-selectable normalization options in Viime's data-treatment pipeline, applied before transformation and scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The table still contains uncorrected errors or missing values — Viime performs error detection and automatic imputation before normalization, so normalize only after imputation. The intended normalization is reference-sample-sum, fixed-sum (default 100), or weight/volume based — pick that specific method instead; Viime lets the user select among them. The goal is post-normalization treatment (Log10/Log2/square-root/cube-root transformation or autoscaling/Pareto/range/vast/level scaling) — those are distinct downstream steps, not this one.

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS molecular network (components of similar MS/MS spectra) plus a set of mineMS2-mined fragmentation patterns, and need to identify which patterns explain each network component using recall/precision/size metrics.
skills.name: minems2-component-pattern-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: minems2-component-pattern-metrics-computation Use when you have a GNPS molecular network (components of similar MS/MS spectra) plus a set of mineMS2-mined fragmentation patterns, and need to identify which patterns explain each network component using recall/precision/size metrics. You only need to mine patterns de novo from spectra — use the mineMS2 pattern-mining workflow instead; this skill assumes patterns and network components already exist You want to annotate patterns with chemical concepts (ChemOnt terms) rather than rank patterns against network components — that is a different mineMS2 use case The spectra have not been organized into a molecular network (no GNPS components), since there are no components to explain http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Ranks mined mineMS2 fragmentation patterns by how specifically they explain each component of a GNPS molecular network, computing recall, precision, and size metrics per pattern-component pair. This reproduces the paper's analysis of the P. nordicum dataset where, e.g., pattern P70 uniquely explains component 8 with F1-score 1. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-01051-y
skills.summary: Ranks mined mineMS2 fragmentation patterns by how specifically they explain each component of a GNPS molecular network, computing recall, precision, and size metrics per pattern-component pair. This reproduces the paper's analysis of the P. nordicum dataset where, e.g., pattern P70 uniquely explains component 8 with F1-score 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to mine patterns de novo from spectra — use the mineMS2 pattern-mining workflow instead; this skill assumes patterns and network components already exist You want to annotate patterns with chemical concepts (ChemOnt terms) rather than rank patterns against network components — that is a different mineMS2 use case The spectra have not been organized into a molecular network (no GNPS components), since there are no components to explain

skills.description: Use when many antiSMASH or gutSMASH-predicted gene clusters (e.g., 1,849 BGCs from 170 S. mutans genomes) must be reduced to a nonredundant representative set before metagenomic read mapping.
skills.name: minhash-gene-cluster-family-redundancy-filtering
skills.search_text: minhash-gene-cluster-family-redundancy-filtering Use when many antiSMASH or gutSMASH-predicted gene clusters (e.g., 1,849 BGCs from 170 S. mutans genomes) must be reduced to a nonredundant representative set before metagenomic read mapping. The anti- or gutSMASH output folders for the genomes have not yet been generated — bigmap-family requires these pre-computed predictions as input and cannot mine genomes itself The gene clusters have already been reduced to a nonredundant GCF set and per-sample mapping with bigmap-map is the next step, so a second filtering pass would be redundant The analysis does not involve mapping metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads to gene clusters (e.g., the goal is only to enumerate BGCs per genome), in which case the redundancy collapse for unambiguous mapping is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A redundancy-filtering step in the BiG-MAP pipeline that collapses many antiSMASH/gutSMASH-predicted biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into nonredundant representatives and gene cluster families (GCFs) using MinHash (MASH) sequence similarity, optionally refined with BiG-SCAPE. It is essential to avoid ambiguous mapping of metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads to overlapping cluster sequences downstream. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: A redundancy-filtering step in the BiG-MAP pipeline that collapses many antiSMASH/gutSMASH-predicted biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into nonredundant representatives and gene cluster families (GCFs) using MinHash (MASH) sequence similarity, optionally refined with BiG-SCAPE. It is essential to avoid ambiguous mapping of metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads to overlapping cluster sequences downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The anti- or gutSMASH output folders for the genomes have not yet been generated — bigmap-family requires these pre-computed predictions as input and cannot mine genomes itself The gene clusters have already been reduced to a nonredundant GCF set and per-sample mapping with bigmap-map is the next step, so a second filtering pass would be redundant The analysis does not involve mapping metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads to gene clusters (e.g., the goal is only to enumerate BGCs per genome), in which case the redundancy collapse for unambiguous mapping is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic/metatranscriptomic profiling pipeline receives multiple predicted gene clusters (antiSMASH/gutSMASH GenBank output dirs) that must be deduplicated to avoid ambiguous read mapping downstream.
skills.name: minhash-sketching-of-gene-clusters
skills.search_text: minhash-sketching-of-gene-clusters Use when a metagenomic/metatranscriptomic profiling pipeline receives multiple predicted gene clusters (antiSMASH/gutSMASH GenBank output dirs) that must be deduplicated to avoid ambiguous read mapping downstream. Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/SRA accessions) — that belongs to the bigmap-download module, not the redundancy-filtering step The goal is abundance/expression quantification or differential analysis of already-filtered representatives — use bigmap-map and bigmap-analyse instead Input gene clusters are not in antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directory format (the module expects their GenBank output folders, produced beforehand) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Redundancy-filtering of antiSMASH/gutSMASH-predicted gene clusters by sketching their protein sequences with MASH MinHash, clustering at a similarity cutoff, and selecting the medoid as each cluster's nonredundant representative before metagenomic read mapping. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Redundancy-filtering of antiSMASH/gutSMASH-predicted gene clusters by sketching their protein sequences with MASH MinHash, clustering at a similarity cutoff, and selecting the medoid as each cluster's nonredundant representative before metagenomic read mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/SRA accessions) — that belongs to the bigmap-download module, not the redundancy-filtering step The goal is abundance/expression quantification or differential analysis of already-filtered representatives — use bigmap-map and bigmap-analyse instead Input gene clusters are not in antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directory format (the module expects their GenBank output folders, produced beforehand)

skills.description: Use when reconstructing a target 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR mixture spectrum as a weighted union of library compound spectra, especially when peak overlaps and inter-compound dependencies must be handled jointly rather than fitted per compound.
skills.name: minimum-cost-flow-network-construction
skills.search_text: minimum-cost-flow-network-construction Use when reconstructing a target 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR mixture spectrum as a weighted union of library compound spectra, especially when peak overlaps and inter-compound dependencies must be handled jointly rather than fitted per compound. The mixture may contain compounds whose spectral peak pattern is not known — a complete reconstruction requires knowledge of every constituent's peak pattern Peak shifts between library and target are large relative to the assignment radius r, since the method is explicitly noted as sensitive toward peak shifts The task requires a definitive protocol for choosing r, c_phi, or theta — the paper states there is 'no definite answer or protocol to choose these values' http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 Constructs a minimum cost flow network over library compound HSQC peaks and mixture target peaks to identify and quantify compounds in an NMR mixture via the Earth Mover's Distance analogue, solved as a linear program with HiGHS. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01652
skills.summary: Constructs a minimum cost flow network over library compound HSQC peaks and mixture target peaks to identify and quantify compounds in an NMR mixture via the Earth Mover's Distance analogue, solved as a linear program with HiGHS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mixture may contain compounds whose spectral peak pattern is not known — a complete reconstruction requires knowledge of every constituent's peak pattern Peak shifts between library and target are large relative to the assignment radius r, since the method is explicitly noted as sensitive toward peak shifts The task requires a definitive protocol for choosing r, c_phi, or theta — the paper states there is 'no definite answer or protocol to choose these values'

skills.description: Use when you have 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR spectra of a mixture (grid data or peak lists) and a compound library, and need to identify/quantify constituents without peak-picking the mixture spectrum.
skills.name: minimum-cost-flow-optimization
skills.search_text: minimum-cost-flow-optimization Use when you have 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR spectra of a mixture (grid data or peak lists) and a compound library, and need to identify/quantify constituents without peak-picking the mixture spectrum. Mixture constituents whose peak pattern is unknown, so no library spectra exist to fit (the article notes 'the mixture may contain compounds whose spectral peak pattern is not known'). Samples where a peak-picking preprocessing step is already required by the downstream pipeline (the MCF approach can 'be used without peak-picking the mixture spectrum'). Extremely complex mixtures with severe peak overlap where the article reports 'diminishing performance for mixtures of increasing complexity' and 'limited quantification accuracy'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Fit compound spectra to an NMR mixture spectrum by casting peak-to-peak intensity matching as a minimum cost flow problem on a network whose nodes represent spectral peaks of library compounds and the mixture, solved with a linear optimizer. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01652
skills.summary: Fit compound spectra to an NMR mixture spectrum by casting peak-to-peak intensity matching as a minimum cost flow problem on a network whose nodes represent spectral peaks of library compounds and the mixture, solved with a linear optimizer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mixture constituents whose peak pattern is unknown, so no library spectra exist to fit (the article notes 'the mixture may contain compounds whose spectral peak pattern is not known'). Samples where a peak-picking preprocessing step is already required by the downstream pipeline (the MCF approach can 'be used without peak-picking the mixture spectrum'). Extremely complex mixtures with severe peak overlap where the article reports 'diminishing performance for mixtures of increasing complexity' and 'limited quantification accuracy'.

skills.description: Use when you need to identify and quantify compounds in 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR mixture spectra against a compound library, especially when peak-picking the mixture is undesirable or peaks overlap/shift due to sample-matrix effects.
skills.name: minimum-cost-flow-spectral-fitting
skills.search_text: minimum-cost-flow-spectral-fitting Use when you need to identify and quantify compounds in 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR mixture spectra against a compound library, especially when peak-picking the mixture is undesirable or peaks overlap/shift due to sample-matrix effects. The compound's peak pattern is absent from the library — reconstruction is incomplete because no source node exists for its peaks You need exact quantitative concentrations rather than semiquantitative estimates (limited quantification accuracy is a stated limitation) The sample has severe peak shifts or very high-complexity mixtures where MCF performance diminishes and the assignment radius/variant choice cannot compensate http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Fits 2D 1H,13C HSQC mixture spectra by solving a minimum cost flow (MCF) problem on a network of library- and target-spectrum peaks, enabling simultaneous compound identification and semiquantitative concentration reconstruction via the Earth Mover's Distance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01652
skills.summary: Fits 2D 1H,13C HSQC mixture spectra by solving a minimum cost flow (MCF) problem on a network of library- and target-spectrum peaks, enabling simultaneous compound identification and semiquantitative concentration reconstruction via the Earth Mover's Distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound's peak pattern is absent from the library — reconstruction is incomplete because no source node exists for its peaks You need exact quantitative concentrations rather than semiquantitative estimates (limited quantification accuracy is a stated limitation) The sample has severe peak shifts or very high-complexity mixtures where MCF performance diminishes and the assignment radius/variant choice cannot compensate
