skills.name: minimum-fraction-single-value-imputation
skills.search_text: minimum-fraction-single-value-imputation Use when a metabolomics feature table (e.g., the cancerCell demo dataset) contains NA/NaN intensities and simple single-value replacement — constant 1, 1/5 of the feature minimum, or column mean/median — is acceptable before downstream statistics. The feature table already contains zero NA/NaN entries — imputation would be a no-op and adds no value Missingness is missing-at-random and sample-profile similarity is preferred over a single constant — use the KNN variant (VIM kNN) instead of single-value replacement The task is general web-app reporting or visualization with MetaboReport rather than filling missing values in a feature table Applies MetaboReport's single-value missing-data imputation for metabolomics feature tables — constant 1, one-fifth-of-feature-minimum, column-wise mean, and median — to fill gaps arising from missing-not-at-random (below-detection-limit) and missing-at-random mechanisms before statistical analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Applies MetaboReport's single-value missing-data imputation for metabolomics feature tables — constant 1, one-fifth-of-feature-minimum, column-wise mean, and median — to fill gaps arising from missing-not-at-random (below-detection-limit) and missing-at-random mechanisms before statistical analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table already contains zero NA/NaN entries — imputation would be a no-op and adds no value Missingness is missing-at-random and sample-profile similarity is preferred over a single constant — use the KNN variant (VIM kNN) instead of single-value replacement The task is general web-app reporting or visualization with MetaboReport rather than filling missing values in a feature table

skills.description: Use when a pcpfm/Asari feature table (e.g. preferred_drop_missing TSV) contains missing entries after removal of uncommon features and the table must be complete for downstream statistical analysis.
skills.name: minimum-intensity-scalar-imputation
skills.search_text: minimum-intensity-scalar-imputation Use when a pcpfm/Asari feature table (e.g. preferred_drop_missing TSV) contains missing entries after removal of uncommon features and the table must be complete for downstream statistical analysis. The input table is already complete with no missing entries, since imputation would only scale existing values. The analysis requires a globally constant imputation value or model-based imputation; this method only implements per-feature minimum-scalar imputation. The table is not a feature-by-sample intensity table (e.g. it is an empirical compound JSON or annotation table), since the per-feature minimum logic assumes feature columns of intensities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Imputes missing entries in an LC-MS feature table by replacing each missing value with a scalar fraction (default 0.5) of that feature's minimum observed non-zero intensity, as implemented in the pcpfm pipeline. This keeps imputation intensity-scaled per feature rather than using a global constant. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: Imputes missing entries in an LC-MS feature table by replacing each missing value with a scalar fraction (default 0.5) of that feature's minimum observed non-zero intensity, as implemented in the pcpfm pipeline. This keeps imputation intensity-scaled per feature rather than using a global constant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table is already complete with no missing entries, since imputation would only scale existing values. The analysis requires a globally constant imputation value or model-based imputation; this method only implements per-feature minimum-scalar imputation. The table is not a feature-by-sample intensity table (e.g. it is an empirical compound JSON or annotation table), since the per-feature minimum logic assumes feature columns of intensities.

skills.description: Use when implementing or modifying the SAND adaptive binning stage on 1D high-resolution metabolomics NMR spectra and each binned region (nominal 0.002 ppm buckets) needs intensity offsets removed before raised-cosine banding and inverse Fourier processing.
skills.name: minimum-shift-baseline-removal-implementation
skills.search_text: minimum-shift-baseline-removal-implementation Use when implementing or modifying the SAND adaptive binning stage on 1D high-resolution metabolomics NMR spectra and each binned region (nominal 0.002 ppm buckets) needs intensity offsets removed before raised-cosine banding and inverse Fourier processing. The input is already a feature/peak table produced by SAND decomposition — baseline handling at the spectrum level no longer applies The spectrum has not yet been adaptively partitioned and you need a global whole-spectrum baseline correction rather than per-binned-region offset removal The data are not high-resolution metabolomics NMR spectra — SAND's current version is tuned for that case and other NMR data types are not yet accommodated http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Implements the minimum-shift baseline-correction step inside SAND's adaptive frequency-binning preprocessing: within each binned region of a 1D metabolomics NMR spectrum, intensity offsets are corrected before raised-cosine apodization and Hilbert/inverse-FT conversion to per-bin FIDs. It is a prerequisite step because bin-to-FID modeling assumes each bin's intensities are referenced to a corrected baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03078
skills.summary: Implements the minimum-shift baseline-correction step inside SAND's adaptive frequency-binning preprocessing: within each binned region of a 1D metabolomics NMR spectrum, intensity offsets are corrected before raised-cosine apodization and Hilbert/inverse-FT conversion to per-bin FIDs. It is a prerequisite step because bin-to-FID modeling assumes each bin's intensities are referenced to a corrected baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/peak table produced by SAND decomposition — baseline handling at the spectrum level no longer applies The spectrum has not yet been adaptively partitioned and you need a global whole-spectrum baseline correction rather than per-binned-region offset removal The data are not high-resolution metabolomics NMR spectra — SAND's current version is tuned for that case and other NMR data types are not yet accommodated

skills.description: Reference for constructing an MST over MS/MS spectra whose pairwise modified cosine similarity scores are known, when a deterministic ordering of spectra is needed for transitive peak alignment within a molecular network component.
skills.name: minimum-spanning-tree-construction-over-spectra
skills.search_text: minimum-spanning-tree-construction-over-spectra Reference for constructing an MST over MS/MS spectra whose pairwise modified cosine similarity scores are known, when a deterministic ordering of spectra is needed for transitive peak alignment within a molecular network component. Input is already a single pairwise spectrum-spectrum alignment result and no multi-spectrum consensus is needed Spectra lack precursor metadata or peak filtering context (±25 m/z window, ±17 m/z precursor exclusion), so the modified cosine similarity matrix cannot be produced http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds a minimum spanning tree (MST) over MS/MS spectra within a molecular network component, using NetworkX 3.3 and greedy spanning tree logic with edges weighted by modified cosine similarity subtracted from 1, to drive the transitive spectral alignment in MMSA. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Builds a minimum spanning tree (MST) over MS/MS spectra within a molecular network component, using NetworkX 3.3 and greedy spanning tree logic with edges weighted by modified cosine similarity subtracted from 1, to drive the transitive spectral alignment in MMSA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single pairwise spectrum-spectrum alignment result and no multi-spectrum consensus is needed Spectra lack precursor metadata or peak filtering context (±25 m/z window, ±17 m/z precursor exclusion), so the modified cosine similarity matrix cannot be produced

skills.description: Use when you have a molecular network component's MS/MS spectra (GNPS2 task/component or USIs) and need a deterministic ordering for transitive multiple-spectrum alignment in MMSA.
skills.name: minimum-spanning-tree-spectra-ordering
skills.search_text: minimum-spanning-tree-spectra-ordering Use when you have a molecular network component's MS/MS spectra (GNPS2 task/component or USIs) and need a deterministic ordering for transitive multiple-spectrum alignment in MMSA. You only need pairwise spectrum comparison or standard GNPS molecular networking without multiple-spectrum consensus alignment Input is already a consensus or aligned peak set rather than raw component MS/MS spectra The component has fewer than two spectra so no MST ordering is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Orders MS/MS spectra within a molecular-networking component by building a minimum spanning tree (MST) with NetworkX 3.3, weighting edges as 1 minus pairwise modified cosine similarity, then topologically sorting nodes to fix the processing order for MMSA spectral alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Orders MS/MS spectra within a molecular-networking component by building a minimum spanning tree (MST) with NetworkX 3.3, weighting edges as 1 minus pairwise modified cosine similarity, then topologically sorting nodes to fix the processing order for MMSA spectral alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need pairwise spectrum comparison or standard GNPS molecular networking without multiple-spectrum consensus alignment Input is already a consensus or aligned peak set rather than raw component MS/MS spectra The component has fewer than two spectra so no MST ordering is required

skills.description: Use when a molecular networking component (a molecular family of related MS/MS spectra, e.g. ~80 rhamnolipid spectra or an albicidin analog family) needs its common fragments and modification-site shifts aligned across all members, beyond pairwise spectral comparison.
skills.name: minimum-spanning-tree-spectral-alignment
skills.search_text: minimum-spanning-tree-spectral-alignment Use when a molecular networking component (a molecular family of related MS/MS spectra, e.g. ~80 rhamnolipid spectra or an albicidin analog family) needs its common fragments and modification-site shifts aligned across all members, beyond pairwise spectral comparison. The question is standard molecular network construction (FBNM cosine edges) rather than explaining commonalities of fragmentation within an already-networked molecular family. Only pairwise spectral comparison is needed — MMSA is designed for multiple alignment of an entire molecular family, not two-spectrum matching. The user needs to capture every shifted fragment peak: the greedy alignment is known to miss smaller peak alignments (e.g. y2 peaks in the albicidin family and C12-HAA shifts in the rhamnolipid family), so site localization may need supplemental inspection. http://edamontology.org/topic_0081 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A greedy multiple alignment of MS/MS spectra within a molecular networking component: build a minimum spanning tree over spectra weighted by modified cosine similarity, align transitively along the tree, then compute non-transitive consensus peak sets that reveal shared fragments and modification-driven shifts across a molecular family. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: A greedy multiple alignment of MS/MS spectra within a molecular networking component: build a minimum spanning tree over spectra weighted by modified cosine similarity, align transitively along the tree, then compute non-transitive consensus peak sets that reveal shared fragments and modification-driven shifts across a molecular family.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is standard molecular network construction (FBNM cosine edges) rather than explaining commonalities of fragmentation within an already-networked molecular family. Only pairwise spectral comparison is needed — MMSA is designed for multiple alignment of an entire molecular family, not two-spectrum matching. The user needs to capture every shifted fragment peak: the greedy alignment is known to miss smaller peak alignments (e.g. y2 peaks in the albicidin family and C12-HAA shifts in the rhamnolipid family), so site localization may need supplemental inspection.

skills.description: Use when a processed, aligned peak list from the Galaxy-M DIMS SIM-stitch pipeline (calibrated m/z values with blank/replicate filtering already applied) needs metabolite annotation as the final analysis step of the workflow.
skills.name: mipack-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: mipack-metabolite-annotation Use when a processed, aligned peak list from the Galaxy-M DIMS SIM-stitch pipeline (calibrated m/z values with blank/replicate filtering already applied) needs metabolite annotation as the final analysis step of the workflow. Input is still raw instrument data (.dat transient files) rather than a processed, calibrated peak list — the SimStitch/alignment/filtering steps must run first The task requires statistical testing (t-test p-values, PCA Scores Test) rather than annotation — Galaxy-M's PLS-Toolbox/PCA tools cover that, and no univariate statistics tools are included in the current implementation Peak detection itself is needed — MI-Pack annotates already-detected peaks; peak picking is done upstream by SIM-stitching (DIMS) or XCMS (LC-MS) http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 MI-Pack annotates peaks detected by the Galaxy-M DIMS/LC-MS processing pipelines against compound reference databases (KEGG, HMDB, LIPID MAPS) by integrating accurate masses and metabolic pathways, exporting the results as a tab-delimited annotation table. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: MI-Pack annotates peaks detected by the Galaxy-M DIMS/LC-MS processing pipelines against compound reference databases (KEGG, HMDB, LIPID MAPS) by integrating accurate masses and metabolic pathways, exporting the results as a tab-delimited annotation table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw instrument data (.dat transient files) rather than a processed, calibrated peak list — the SimStitch/alignment/filtering steps must run first The task requires statistical testing (t-test p-values, PCA Scores Test) rather than annotation — Galaxy-M's PLS-Toolbox/PCA tools cover that, and no univariate statistics tools are included in the current implementation Peak detection itself is needed — MI-Pack annotates already-detected peaks; peak picking is done upstream by SIM-stitching (DIMS) or XCMS (LC-MS)

skills.description: Use when integrating miRNA data with other omics (genes, isoforms, proteins, lipids) in MOI and you need to annotate putative miRNA-mRNA regulatory connections among the loaded feature matrices before downstream analysis.
skills.name: mirna-target-interaction-retrieval
skills.search_text: mirna-target-interaction-retrieval Use when integrating miRNA data with other omics (genes, isoforms, proteins, lipids) in MOI and you need to annotate putative miRNA-mRNA regulatory connections among the loaded feature matrices before downstream analysis. The input data contain no miRNA layer (e.g. mRNA-only RNA-seq or proteomics-only runs), since there are no miRNA features to query against targets You already possess a curated, validated miRNA-target annotation for your features and only need correlation or MCIA integration The goal is standalone pathway enrichment on a single omics dataset without integration or regulatory-edge annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieves putative miRNA-mRNA regulatory interactions (via multiMiR) to annotate connections among features loaded into the MOI multi-omics integration module, prior to correlation-based filtering and pathway enrichment. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae175
skills.summary: Retrieves putative miRNA-mRNA regulatory interactions (via multiMiR) to annotate connections among features loaded into the MOI multi-omics integration module, prior to correlation-based filtering and pathway enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data contain no miRNA layer (e.g. mRNA-only RNA-seq or proteomics-only runs), since there are no miRNA features to query against targets You already possess a curated, validated miRNA-target annotation for your features and only need correlation or MCIA integration The goal is standalone pathway enrichment on a single omics dataset without integration or regulatory-edge annotation

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS feature annotated against the GNPS Drug Library must be linked across sample contexts — e.g. confirming that an incubation-derived drug analog matches a fecal-sample feature — and when distinguishing true microbial transformation products from abiotic or ion-form artifacts.
skills.name: mirror-match-spectral-comparison
skills.search_text: mirror-match-spectral-comparison Use when an LC-MS/MS feature annotated against the GNPS Drug Library must be linked across sample contexts — e.g. confirming that an incubation-derived drug analog matches a fecal-sample feature — and when distinguishing true microbial transformation products from abiotic or ion-form artifacts. The feature is only the parent drug with no analog/metabolite candidate to cross-confirm — annotation against the GNPS Drug Library alone suffices The candidate analog is already established as abiotic (present in drug-only controls at t=0, absent from drug-free controls) — it should be excluded rather than mirror-matched as a microbial product Only extracted-ion chromatographic retention-time overlap is available without MS/MS spectra — mirror matching cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Confirms that an annotated drug analog detected in one sample context (e.g. an hCom gut-microbe incubation) is the same molecular species as a feature observed elsewhere (e.g. a fecal sample) by GNPS-based mirror-match comparison of their MS/MS spectra using cosine similarity scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5
skills.summary: Confirms that an annotated drug analog detected in one sample context (e.g. an hCom gut-microbe incubation) is the same molecular species as a feature observed elsewhere (e.g. a fecal sample) by GNPS-based mirror-match comparison of their MS/MS spectra using cosine similarity scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature is only the parent drug with no analog/metabolite candidate to cross-confirm — annotation against the GNPS Drug Library alone suffices The candidate analog is already established as abiotic (present in drug-only controls at t=0, absent from drug-free controls) — it should be excluded rather than mirror-matched as a microbial product Only extracted-ion chromatographic retention-time overlap is available without MS/MS spectra — mirror matching cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when an experimental MS/MS spectrum must be compared against a spectral library match (or another dataset spectrum) and the deliverable is a publication-ready mirror plot with a quantified cosine similarity and highlighted matching peaks.
skills.name: mirror-plot-cosine-similarity-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: mirror-plot-cosine-similarity-spectral-matching Use when an experimental MS/MS spectrum must be compared against a spectral library match (or another dataset spectrum) and the deliverable is a publication-ready mirror plot with a quantified cosine similarity and highlighted matching peaks. Only a single spectrum needs to be visualized — use the plain /png/ or /svg/ rendering endpoints instead of /mirror A machine-readable peak list or metadata export is needed rather than a figure — use the /json/, /csv/, or /proxi/v0.1/spectra endpoints The spectra cannot be addressed by a supported USI construct (the resolver supports specific draft-USI formats for GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA, MassIVE, MetaboLights, and Metabolomics Workbench sources) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Render two tandem MS spectra as a mirror plot via the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver's /mirror endpoints by supplying their USIs, quantifying the match with standard cosine similarity and highlighting shared fragments between the top and bottom spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Render two tandem MS spectra as a mirror plot via the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver's /mirror endpoints by supplying their USIs, quantifying the match with standard cosine similarity and highlighting shared fragments between the top and bottom spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single spectrum needs to be visualized — use the plain /png/ or /svg/ rendering endpoints instead of /mirror A machine-readable peak list or metadata export is needed rather than a figure — use the /json/, /csv/, or /proxi/v0.1/spectra endpoints The spectra cannot be addressed by a supported USI construct (the resolver supports specific draft-USI formats for GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA, MassIVE, MetaboLights, and Metabolomics Workbench sources)

skills.description: Use when two USI-resolvable tandem MS spectra (e.g. GNPS/MassBank/MassIVE library or task spectra) must be compared side-by-side, with matched peaks highlighted and a cosine similarity score for the pair.
skills.name: mirror-plot-spectrum-comparison
skills.search_text: mirror-plot-spectrum-comparison Use when two USI-resolvable tandem MS spectra (e.g. GNPS/MassBank/MassIVE library or task spectra) must be compared side-by-side, with matched peaks highlighted and a cosine similarity score for the pair. Comparing more than two spectra — the /mirror/ endpoint supports only a pair of spectra (usi1 and usi2) The input is a single spectrum to visualize alone — use the /spectrum/ or /svg/ single-spectrum endpoints instead of /mirror/ You need proteomics peptide-spectrum match scoring rather than metabolomics spectral cosine comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute and visually compare two tandem MS spectra as a mirror plot using the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver, including an optional shifted cosine similarity that also matches fragment peaks differing by the precursor mass difference between the spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Compute and visually compare two tandem MS spectra as a mirror plot using the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver, including an optional shifted cosine similarity that also matches fragment peaks differing by the precursor mass difference between the spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing more than two spectra — the /mirror/ endpoint supports only a pair of spectra (usi1 and usi2) The input is a single spectrum to visualize alone — use the /spectrum/ or /svg/ single-spectrum endpoints instead of /mirror/ You need proteomics peptide-spectrum match scoring rather than metabolomics spectral cosine comparison

skills.description: Use when consensus/deconvolved MS2 spectra have been searched against reference databases and you need visual verification of top-scoring compound matches, or when compiling annotated features for a QC case study.
skills.name: mirror-plot-spectrum-visualization
skills.search_text: mirror-plot-spectrum-visualization Use when consensus/deconvolved MS2 spectra have been searched against reference databases and you need visual verification of top-scoring compound matches, or when compiling annotated features for a QC case study. Input is raw MS1 spectra or a pre-built feature/peak table rather than deconvolved MS2 spectra with precursor m/z and retention time — the skill presupposes the MS2 Peak Annotation search step has already been run. Only one spectrum or one compound needs to be visualized with no reference library to match against — there is nothing to overlay in a mirror plot. The goal is statistical analysis, pathway analysis, or mGWAS/dose-response modeling — this skill is purely for MS2 peak annotation verification, not downstream analysis modules. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates mirror plots that overlay each deconvolved query MS2 spectrum against its best-matching reference spectrum from MetaboAnalyst 6.0's MS2 Peak Annotation module, providing visual verification of compound identifications produced by the spectral search. It pairs a compound identification table with inspection-ready overlay figures. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Generates mirror plots that overlay each deconvolved query MS2 spectrum against its best-matching reference spectrum from MetaboAnalyst 6.0's MS2 Peak Annotation module, providing visual verification of compound identifications produced by the spectral search. It pairs a compound identification table with inspection-ready overlay figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS1 spectra or a pre-built feature/peak table rather than deconvolved MS2 spectra with precursor m/z and retention time — the skill presupposes the MS2 Peak Annotation search step has already been run. Only one spectrum or one compound needs to be visualized with no reference library to match against — there is nothing to overlay in a mirror plot. The goal is statistical analysis, pathway analysis, or mGWAS/dose-response modeling — this skill is purely for MS2 peak annotation verification, not downstream analysis modules.

skills.description: Use when two MS/MS spectra need to be compared visually (e.g. a library spectrum vs. an unknown query spectrum from GNPS), to assess peak-by-peak similarity, including annotated peptide fragment ions (a/b/y).
skills.name: mirror-spectrum-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: mirror-spectrum-plot-visualization Use when two MS/MS spectra need to be compared visually (e.g. a library spectrum vs. an unknown query spectrum from GNPS), to assess peak-by-peak similarity, including annotated peptide fragment ions (a/b/y). You only need to inspect a single spectrum — use the regular static or interactive spectrum plot rather than a mirror plot You need to read raw spectral data files (e.g. mzML) directly — spectrum_utils does not provide file reading; use pymzML or another external tool first and supply data as MsmsSpectrum objects The spectra have not been noise-filtered and low-intensity peaks would overwhelm the fragment-ion comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Render a mirror plot with spectrum_utils to compare two MS/MS spectra: the top spectrum is plotted normally and the comparison spectrum is inverted below it, making matched (and unmatched) peaks between the two spectra visually apparent. This is the standard way to show spectral similarity, e.g. library-versus-query spectrum matches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b04884
skills.summary: Render a mirror plot with spectrum_utils to compare two MS/MS spectra: the top spectrum is plotted normally and the comparison spectrum is inverted below it, making matched (and unmatched) peaks between the two spectra visually apparent. This is the standard way to show spectral similarity, e.g. library-versus-query spectrum matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to inspect a single spectrum — use the regular static or interactive spectrum plot rather than a mirror plot You need to read raw spectral data files (e.g. mzML) directly — spectrum_utils does not provide file reading; use pymzML or another external tool first and supply data as MsmsSpectrum objects The spectra have not been noise-filtered and low-intensity peaks would overwhelm the fragment-ion comparison

skills.description: Use when reviewing targeted LC-MS metabolomics data from multiple batches and study samples must be screened for mis-injections or low/high total IS-area outliers before compound-level reporting and batch correction, with flagged samples excluded from further calculations.
skills.name: mis-injection-detection-from-is-areas
skills.search_text: mis-injection-detection-from-is-areas Use when reviewing targeted LC-MS metabolomics data from multiple batches and study samples must be screened for mis-injections or low/high total IS-area outliers before compound-level reporting and batch correction, with flagged samples excluded from further calculations. Screening pooled SQC samples for outliers — those are assumed identical and should instead be flagged via Compound/IS ratio deviations (Rosner's test), not IS areas. The input is not peak-integrated targeted metabolomics data with the mandatory columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch); mzQuality will not accept it. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Flag study-sample outliers such as probable mis-injections by inspecting Internal Standard (IS) areas across batches, following mzQuality's approach that distinguishes study samples from pooled QC samples. Because pooled SQC samples are assumed identical, QC outliers are instead detected from Compound/IS ratio deviations (via Rosner's test), whereas study samples cannot be compared against a known composition and rely on IS-area aberrations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Flag study-sample outliers such as probable mis-injections by inspecting Internal Standard (IS) areas across batches, following mzQuality's approach that distinguishes study samples from pooled QC samples. Because pooled SQC samples are assumed identical, QC outliers are instead detected from Compound/IS ratio deviations (via Rosner's test), whereas study samples cannot be compared against a known composition and rely on IS-area aberrations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Screening pooled SQC samples for outliers — those are assumed identical and should instead be flagged via Compound/IS ratio deviations (Rosner's test), not IS areas. The input is not peak-integrated targeted metabolomics data with the mandatory columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch); mzQuality will not accept it.

skills.description: Use when ncGTW has flagged potentially misaligned feature groups from XCMS output and you must decide which flagged features are genuine misalignments worth keeping, using CV improvement from ncGTW-guided peak-filling as the truth signal.
skills.name: misaligned-feature-truth-label-interpretation
skills.search_text: misaligned-feature-truth-label-interpretation Use when ncGTW has flagged potentially misaligned feature groups from XCMS output and you must decide which flagged features are genuine misalignments worth keeping, using CV improvement from ncGTW-guided peak-filling as the truth signal. When the goal is only to detect misalignment, not to judge which detected features are real — use the ncGTW misalignment-detection module alone instead When no paired before/after peak-filling comparison can be computed (e.g., raw profiles or XCMS output are unavailable), since truth labels hinge on CV improvement When working with features already confirmed well-aligned by the single XCMS warping function, which would not enter this labeling workflow Interprets features flagged by the ncGTW misalignment-detection module by labeling each as a true positive (circle) or false positive (cross) based on whether substituting the ncGTW per-sample warping functions into XCMS peak-filling actually lowers the coefficient of variation (compCV) for that feature. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa037
skills.summary: Interprets features flagged by the ncGTW misalignment-detection module by labeling each as a true positive (circle) or false positive (cross) based on whether substituting the ncGTW per-sample warping functions into XCMS peak-filling actually lowers the coefficient of variation (compCV) for that feature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only to detect misalignment, not to judge which detected features are real — use the ncGTW misalignment-detection module alone instead When no paired before/after peak-filling comparison can be computed (e.g., raw profiles or XCMS output are unavailable), since truth labels hinge on CV improvement When working with features already confirmed well-aligned by the single XCMS warping function, which would not enter this labeling workflow

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS profiles (e.g. mzXML) must be preprocessed by XCMS into two grouping objects — one at large bw, one near RT sampling resolution — so ncGTW can detect misaligned features.
skills.name: misalignment-detection-input-preparation
skills.search_text: misalignment-detection-input-preparation Use when raw LC-MS profiles (e.g. mzXML) must be preprocessed by XCMS into two grouping objects — one at large bw, one near RT sampling resolution — so ncGTW can detect misaligned features. Input is already a peak/feature table with no raw chromatographic profiles, so centWave/retcor cannot be run and the profile-level grouping objects cannot be formed The downstream plan does not use ncGTW (e.g. another alignment tool that does not require paired low/high-resolution grouping results) Only one grouping granularity is needed because no misalignment detection is planned http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Prepares the XCMS preprocessing outputs (centWave peak detection, retcor RT correction, and two group() results at different bw values) that the ncGTW misalignment-detection module consumes before it can flag and realign misaligned LC-MS feature groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa037
skills.summary: Prepares the XCMS preprocessing outputs (centWave peak detection, retcor RT correction, and two group() results at different bw values) that the ncGTW misalignment-detection module consumes before it can flag and realign misaligned LC-MS feature groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak/feature table with no raw chromatographic profiles, so centWave/retcor cannot be run and the profile-level grouping objects cannot be formed The downstream plan does not use ncGTW (e.g. another alignment tool that does not require paired low/high-resolution grouping results) Only one grouping granularity is needed because no misalignment detection is planned

skills.description: Use when a Progenesis-format peak table from LC-MS/MS pre-processing shows split isotope/adduct features, and you need to identify or merge mispicked ions before downstream blank/replicate filtering.
skills.name: mispicked-ion-peak-merging
skills.search_text: mispicked-ion-peak-merging Use when a Progenesis-format peak table from LC-MS/MS pre-processing shows split isotope/adduct features, and you need to identify or merge mispicked ions before downstream blank/replicate filtering. Input is raw vendor LC-MS/MS data not yet pre-processed into a Progenesis-format feature table — import_data() expects a peak table plus metadata. The goal is removing solvent blank carryover or non-reproducible features — those are handled by filter_group() and filter_cv(), not this filter. The target issue is in-source fragmentation rather than split isotopic patterns — use filter_insource_ions() instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Detects and optionally merges mispicked MS1 features — isotopic patterns incorrectly split during pre-processing of tandem MS/MS data — using the mpactr filter_mispicked_ions() filter, and reports per-ion outcomes via qc_summary(). metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00997-24
skills.summary: Detects and optionally merges mispicked MS1 features — isotopic patterns incorrectly split during pre-processing of tandem MS/MS data — using the mpactr filter_mispicked_ions() filter, and reports per-ion outcomes via qc_summary().
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor LC-MS/MS data not yet pre-processed into a Progenesis-format feature table — import_data() expects a peak table plus metadata. The goal is removing solvent blank carryover or non-reproducible features — those are handled by filter_group() and filter_cv(), not this filter. The target issue is in-source fragmentation rather than split isotopic patterns — use filter_insource_ions() instead.

skills.description: Use when comparing whether a formula-identification model trained on one instrument type (Q-TOF vs Orbitrap) generalizes to the other, using identical compound sets and per-formula missed-atom counts as the error metric.
skills.name: missed-atom-error-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: missed-atom-error-matrix-analysis Use when comparing whether a formula-identification model trained on one instrument type (Q-TOF vs Orbitrap) generalizes to the other, using identical compound sets and per-formula missed-atom counts as the error metric. When the goal is formula identification accuracy (top-1/top-5) rather than instrument-generalization error analysis When no matched compound sets exist across Q-TOF and Orbitrap sources, so cross-instrument comparisons would be confounded by compound differences When spectra fall outside the paper's data space, e.g. fewer than five peaks, m/z above 1500, or molecules with atom counts above 300 or non-frequent atoms http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Quantifies cross-instrument generalization of FIDDLE formula predictors by evaluating a Q-TOF-trained and an Orbitrap-trained TCN model on matched spectra of both instrument types, assembling a 2x2 matrix of missed atoms per predicted formula (reproducing Fig. 4j). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Quantifies cross-instrument generalization of FIDDLE formula predictors by evaluating a Q-TOF-trained and an Orbitrap-trained TCN model on matched spectra of both instrument types, assembling a 2x2 matrix of missed atoms per predicted formula (reproducing Fig. 4j).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is formula identification accuracy (top-1/top-5) rather than instrument-generalization error analysis When no matched compound sets exist across Q-TOF and Orbitrap sources, so cross-instrument comparisons would be confounded by compound differences When spectra fall outside the paper's data space, e.g. fewer than five peaks, m/z above 1500, or molecules with atom counts above 300 or non-frequent atoms

skills.description: Use when annotating validated peptide-spectrum matches (e.g. MGF spectra from PRIDE/MassIVE with pseudo-ground-truth PSMs filtered at 1% FDR) to quantify missing fragment ions before evaluating de novo sequencing recall.
skills.name: missing-cleavage-site-detection
skills.search_text: missing-cleavage-site-detection Use when annotating validated peptide-spectrum matches (e.g. MGF spectra from PRIDE/MassIVE with pseudo-ground-truth PSMs filtered at 1% FDR) to quantify missing fragment ions before evaluating de novo sequencing recall. Input is raw vendor raw files not yet converted to MGF — convert with ProteoWizard first. PSMs have not been validated (no database-search result filtered at 1% FDR) — no ground-truth peptide sequence is available to compute theoretical fragment ions. Goal is to evaluate noise peaks rather than missing fragmentation: use the noise-peak labeling skill instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Detects which peptide bond cleavage sites in a peptide-spectrum match lack any supporting fragment ion, using theoretical b/y ion-type m/z matching against the observed MS/MS peaks via Pyteomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Detects which peptide bond cleavage sites in a peptide-spectrum match lack any supporting fragment ion, using theoretical b/y ion-type m/z matching against the observed MS/MS peaks via Pyteomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor raw files not yet converted to MGF — convert with ProteoWizard first. PSMs have not been validated (no database-search result filtered at 1% FDR) — no ground-truth peptide sequence is available to compute theoretical fragment ions. Goal is to evaluate noise peaks rather than missing fragmentation: use the noise-peak labeling skill instead.

skills.description: Use when combining published fold-changes and P-values across metabolomics studies that report only overall statistics (no raw data, error, or variance), with incomplete/missing values per compound.
skills.name: missing-data-tolerant-meta-analysis-computation
skills.search_text: missing-data-tolerant-meta-analysis-computation Use when combining published fold-changes and P-values across metabolomics studies that report only overall statistics (no raw data, error, or variance), with incomplete/missing values per compound. Raw data or per-study standard deviations/variances are available — standard meta-analysis methods using effect sizes with error estimates are preferable, since amanida targets overall results without standard deviation Studies report only trend labels (up-/down-regulation) without fold-changes or P-values — use amanida's qualitative vote-counting mode instead Identifiers are uncurated (mixed chemical names, InChI, InChIKey, SMILES) and harmonization to PubChem is not possible — identifier curation is required before reliable per-compound combination http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Combines per-study fold-changes (and P-values) from metabolomics systematic reviews into per-compound estimates using amanida's weighted, non-integral meta-analysis, which works without standard deviations and ignores missing entries. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab591
skills.summary: Combines per-study fold-changes (and P-values) from metabolomics systematic reviews into per-compound estimates using amanida's weighted, non-integral meta-analysis, which works without standard deviations and ignores missing entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw data or per-study standard deviations/variances are available — standard meta-analysis methods using effect sizes with error estimates are preferable, since amanida targets overall results without standard deviation Studies report only trend labels (up-/down-regulation) without fold-changes or P-values — use amanida's qualitative vote-counting mode instead Identifiers are uncurated (mixed chemical names, InChI, InChIKey, SMILES) and harmonization to PubChem is not possible — identifier curation is required before reliable per-compound combination

skills.description: Use when comparing pathway-ranking methods (PLAGE/mPLAGE, ORA, GSEA) for robustness to missing peaks in metabolomics feature tables, by synthetically injecting known missingness levels (20/40/60/80%) over many seeded replicates.
skills.name: missing-feature-perturbation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: missing-feature-perturbation-benchmarking Use when comparing pathway-ranking methods (PLAGE/mPLAGE, ORA, GSEA) for robustness to missing peaks in metabolomics feature tables, by synthetically injecting known missingness levels (20/40/60/80%) over many seeded replicates. The goal is a single one-shot pathway ranking on an existing dataset, not a robustness comparison — plain PALS (PLAGE/ORA/GSEA) output suffices without perturbation replicates. Missing features arise naturally in the measured data and only imputation is needed — the PALS loading-time imputation (min_replace / mean-of-non-zero) handles this without the synthetic removal loop. Peak features lack compound annotations entirely — peaks without annotations are excluded from pathway analysis, so the perturbation benchmark would have no annotated features to remove. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A controlled perturbation benchmark that randomly removes 20–80% of annotated peak features from a metabolomics intensity matrix across hundreds of seeded replicates to quantify the robustness of pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE/PLAGE vs ORA vs GSEA) by aggregated p-value distributions and F1 scores. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: A controlled perturbation benchmark that randomly removes 20–80% of annotated peak features from a metabolomics intensity matrix across hundreds of seeded replicates to quantify the robustness of pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE/PLAGE vs ORA vs GSEA) by aggregated p-value distributions and F1 scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single one-shot pathway ranking on an existing dataset, not a robustness comparison — plain PALS (PLAGE/ORA/GSEA) output suffices without perturbation replicates. Missing features arise naturally in the measured data and only imputation is needed — the PALS loading-time imputation (min_replace / mean-of-non-zero) handles this without the synthetic removal loop. Peak features lack compound annotations entirely — peaks without annotations are excluded from pathway analysis, so the perturbation benchmark would have no annotated features to remove.

skills.description: Use when mapping metabolite identifiers to model identifiers (e.g. via metsEngroVsMetabolomics.csv) before computing mass-action-law substrate-product propensity scores, and you must decide which reactions can be scored given missing abundance measurements.
skills.name: missing-metabolite-abundance-filtering
skills.search_text: missing-metabolite-abundance-filtering Use when mapping metabolite identifiers to model identifiers (e.g. via metsEngroVsMetabolomics.csv) before computing mass-action-law substrate-product propensity scores, and you must decide which reactions can be scored given missing abundance measurements. When the analysis targets transcriptomics-derived Reaction Activity Scores (RAS) from GPR rules, where no metabolite abundance completeness check applies. When at least one substrate of the reaction of interest has no abundance measurement in metabolomics_LM.csv — that reaction must be omitted rather than imputed or scored. When extracellular exo-metabolomics ratios (ysi_ratio.csv) are being used to constrain uptake/secretion bounds instead of intracellular substrate-based propensity scoring. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Filters reactions for the Reaction Propensity Score (RPS) computation so that only reactions whose substrates are all quantified in the intracellular metabolomics dataset (metabolomics_LM.csv) are retained, dropping any reaction with at least one missing substrate concentration. This is the completeness gate applied by INTEGRATE's createMetabolicDataset step before mass-action-law scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009337
skills.summary: Filters reactions for the Reaction Propensity Score (RPS) computation so that only reactions whose substrates are all quantified in the intracellular metabolomics dataset (metabolomics_LM.csv) are retained, dropping any reaction with at least one missing substrate concentration. This is the completeness gate applied by INTEGRATE's createMetabolicDataset step before mass-action-law scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis targets transcriptomics-derived Reaction Activity Scores (RAS) from GPR rules, where no metabolite abundance completeness check applies. When at least one substrate of the reaction of interest has no abundance measurement in metabolomics_LM.csv — that reaction must be omitted rather than imputed or scored. When extracellular exo-metabolomics ratios (ysi_ratio.csv) are being used to constrain uptake/secretion bounds instead of intracellular substrate-based propensity scoring.

skills.description: Use when per-dataset clusterings (label vectors c_m with K_m clusters each) cover different subsets of N observations and must be stacked into a single binary K̄×N matrix before Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis.
skills.name: missing-observation-zero-padding
skills.search_text: missing-observation-zero-padding Use when per-dataset clusterings (label vectors c_m with K_m clusters each) cover different subsets of N observations and must be stacked into a single binary K̄×N matrix before Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis. Input clusterings already share the same fully observed sample set and a similarity/kernel-based integrative method such as KLIC is preferred, since KLIC down-weights noisy datasets instead of zero-padding missing entries The per-dataset outputs are continuous (e.g. kernel/similarity matrices from consensus clustering) rather than discrete cluster labels — the MOC encoding requires binary membership vectors http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Encodes per-dataset cluster assignments of partially observed samples into COCA's binary Matrix Of Clusters (MOC) of size K̄×N, entering zeros for observations missing from a dataset so that consensus clustering can proceed on the union of all samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Encodes per-dataset cluster assignments of partially observed samples into COCA's binary Matrix Of Clusters (MOC) of size K̄×N, entering zeros for observations missing from a dataset so that consensus clustering can proceed on the union of all samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input clusterings already share the same fully observed sample set and a similarity/kernel-based integrative method such as KLIC is preferred, since KLIC down-weights noisy datasets instead of zero-padding missing entries The per-dataset outputs are continuous (e.g. kernel/similarity matrices from consensus clustering) rather than discrete cluster labels — the MOC encoding requires binary membership vectors

skills.description: Use when XCMS peak-filling left a flagged feature undetected in one or more samples and the ncGTW realignment warping functions must supply an apex position and rigidly aligned peak boundaries for those missing peaks before results are handed back to XCMS.
skills.name: missing-peak-apex-estimation
skills.search_text: missing-peak-apex-estimation Use when XCMS peak-filling left a flagged feature undetected in one or more samples and the ncGTW realignment warping functions must supply an apex position and rigidly aligned peak boundaries for those missing peaks before results are handed back to XCMS. Feature apices are already co-aligned across samples and peak shapes (width/height profiles) are preserved — no distortion correction is needed. Misaligned features have not yet been detected/flagged; run the ncGTW misalignment detection module first. No XCMS peak table or peak start/end/width information exists, so there is no apex constraint or median peak width to align missing peaks against. Recovers apex positions and peak boundaries for features that XCMS peak detection/peak-filling missed in some samples, using the ncGTW realignment output: the apex is located on the virtual reference profile aggregated from the other samples and mapped through the per-sample warping function, so the whole missing peak can be aligned and returned to XCMS. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa037
skills.summary: Recovers apex positions and peak boundaries for features that XCMS peak detection/peak-filling missed in some samples, using the ncGTW realignment output: the apex is located on the virtual reference profile aggregated from the other samples and mapped through the per-sample warping function, so the whole missing peak can be aligned and returned to XCMS.

skills.description: Use when KEGG+RefSeq-derived organism-specific networks (e.g. Borrelia) leave activity without an annotated reaction — boundary fluxes indicate flux through a node pair absent from KEGG.
skills.name: missing-reaction-gap-flagging
skills.search_text: missing-reaction-gap-flagging Use when KEGG+RefSeq-derived organism-specific networks (e.g. Borrelia) leave activity without an annotated reaction — boundary fluxes indicate flux through a node pair absent from KEGG. Input is a fully reconstructed FBA model with all reactions already annotated — boundary-flux gap flagging is for refining KEGG/RefSeq-derived networks, not re-validating curated models. No empirical metabolomics data (temporal intensities or boundary fluxes) is available — without flux/intensity evidence, flagging relies purely on annotations and cannot infer missing reactions. The target organism is not present in KEGG (e.g. a truly novel isolate with no ortholog layout) — MINNO's base pathways would not map. If the goal is functional pathway enrichment or differential metabolite analysis rather than structural gap detection, use pathway-activity tools instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Flags missing or unannotated reactions in a KEGG-derived metabolic network by overlaying empirical, time-resolved metabolite intensity profiles and boundary fluxes onto the species-specific pathway graph, exposing disconnected nodes and light-gray edges that represent candidate gaps. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Flags missing or unannotated reactions in a KEGG-derived metabolic network by overlaying empirical, time-resolved metabolite intensity profiles and boundary fluxes onto the species-specific pathway graph, exposing disconnected nodes and light-gray edges that represent candidate gaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a fully reconstructed FBA model with all reactions already annotated — boundary-flux gap flagging is for refining KEGG/RefSeq-derived networks, not re-validating curated models. The target organism is not present in KEGG (e.g. a truly novel isolate with no ortholog layout) — MINNO's base pathways would not map. If the goal is functional pathway enrichment or differential metabolite analysis rather than structural gap detection, use pathway-activity tools instead.

skills.description: Use when MINNO's boundary-flux analysis has produced a set of candidate missing reactions from KEGG and each candidate must be triaged into 'literature-supported' versus 'NCBI-RefSeq homology' evidence categories before network refinement.
skills.name: missing-reaction-table-annotation
skills.search_text: missing-reaction-table-annotation Use when MINNO's boundary-flux analysis has produced a set of candidate missing reactions from KEGG and each candidate must be triaged into 'literature-supported' versus 'NCBI-RefSeq homology' evidence categories before network refinement. The reaction set already carries curated evidence labels (e.g. a previously annotated gap-filling result), so re-triaging literature vs RefSeq homology would be redundant. The goal is to detect missing reactions de novo from metabolomics boundary fluxes rather than to categorize an already-identified list. The candidate reactions come from a pathway database other than KEGG (e.g. BiGG) where the article's literature/RefSeq triage workflow was not applied. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotates the set of reactions MINNO identifies as missing from the KEGG database by assigning each one an evidence-source label — primary-literature support or NCBI-RefSeq homology — and writing the categorized reaction table (with reaction identifiers and evidence-source labels) to a CSV file. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501

skills.when_to_use_negative: The reaction set already carries curated evidence labels (e.g. a previously annotated gap-filling result), so re-triaging literature vs RefSeq homology would be redundant. The candidate reactions come from a pathway database other than KEGG (e.g. BiGG) where the article's literature/RefSeq triage workflow was not applied.

skills.description: Use when you have one or more fully observed datasets (continuous, categorical, or mixed-type) and need controlled artificial missingness benchmarks to evaluate imputation methods against known ground truth.

skills.search_text: missing-value-artificial-mask-generation Use when you have one or more fully observed datasets (continuous, categorical, or mixed-type) and need controlled artificial missingness benchmarks to evaluate imputation methods against known ground truth. The data already contain genuinely missing values — artificial masking assumes a complete ground-truth matrix as the starting point Missingness is expected to be MNAR or MAR rather than MCAR — this mask generator removes values completely at random and will not reflect structured missingness mechanisms The goal is a real imputation application rather than a benchmark — masking destroys observed data and is only useful when ground-truth error evaluation (NRMSE/PFC) is the objective http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Generates benchmark matrices for imputation evaluation by removing values completely at random (MCAR) at 10%, 20% or 30% from complete source datasets, producing 50 independent masked replicates paired with their ground-truth complete matrices for NRMSE/PFC error computation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btr597
skills.summary: Generates benchmark matrices for imputation evaluation by removing values completely at random (MCAR) at 10%, 20% or 30% from complete source datasets, producing 50 independent masked replicates paired with their ground-truth complete matrices for NRMSE/PFC error computation.

skills.search_text: missing-value-filtering-qc-thresholds Use when a processed LC-MS feature table contains missing values and you must decide which features to drop before statistical analysis, following the tidyMass CRC case-study criteria. The input is already a cleaned feature table with no missing values, so filtering would remove nothing and imputation/normalization would be redundant. skills.search_text: missing-value-imputation-and-normalization Use when a preprocessed metabolomics peak-intensity/concentration matrix (CSV with a SampleID/group sample table) still contains missing values or batch/intensity artifacts and needs cleaning before statistical metabolite selection. skills.description: Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix (log-transformed peak intensities) still contains missing values that must be filled before normalization functions such as NormScaling can be run.

skills.search_text: missing-value-imputation-knn Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix (log-transformed peak intensities) still contains missing values that must be filled before normalization functions such as NormScaling can be run. The input is already a complete, imputed feature matrix ready for normalization (proceed directly to NormScaling or NormQcmets). Zeros represent true below-detection-limit observations to be converted to NA by LogTransform(zerotona=TRUE) — that conversion belongs to the LogTransform step, not to imputation. skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a complete, imputed feature matrix ready for normalization (proceed directly to NormScaling or NormQcmets).
