skills.description: Use when a metabolomics metabolite-by-sample matrix (e.g., plasma_breast_cancer.csv from Lilikoi) contains missing intensity values that must be filled before pathway transformation, feature selection, or machine learning classification.
skills.name: missing-value-knn-imputation
skills.search_text: missing-value-knn-imputation Use when a metabolomics metabolite-by-sample matrix (e.g., plasma_breast_cancer.csv from Lilikoi) contains missing intensity values that must be filled before pathway transformation, feature selection, or machine learning classification. Input matrix already contains complete data with no missing values — imputation is unnecessary and adds noise Analysis goal is something other than preprocessing a metabolomics matrix, e.g., prognosis modeling (lilikoi.prognosis) or KEGG visualization (lilikoi.KEGGplot), which are separate Lilikoi v2.0 modules http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Imputes missing metabolite intensities in metabolomics matrices using k-nearest neighbors (impute.knn) via Lilikoi v2.0's lilikoi.preproc_knn function, a preprocessing capability added in Lilikoi v2.0 to ready metabolite-sample matrices for downstream classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Imputes missing metabolite intensities in metabolomics matrices using k-nearest neighbors (impute.knn) via Lilikoi v2.0's lilikoi.preproc_knn function, a preprocessing capability added in Lilikoi v2.0 to ready metabolite-sample matrices for downstream classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrix already contains complete data with no missing values — imputation is unnecessary and adds noise Analysis goal is something other than preprocessing a metabolomics matrix, e.g., prognosis modeling (lilikoi.prognosis) or KEGG visualization (lilikoi.KEGGplot), which are separate Lilikoi v2.0 modules

skills.description: Use when augmenting MSI ion images for contrastive/self-supervised training and you need augmented views that mimic the missing-value artifacts of MS ion detection, as in DeepION's T_COL or T_ISO transforms.
skills.name: missing-value-pattern-simulation
skills.search_text: missing-value-pattern-simulation Use when augmenting MSI ion images for contrastive/self-supervised training and you need augmented views that mimic the missing-value artifacts of MS ion detection, as in DeepION's T_COL or T_ISO transforms. Augmenting for the ISO mode of DeepION: the intensity-dependent missing-value transform must be added there, so the COL-only recipe is the wrong choice Input is already an augmented view or a downstream representation vector (e.g. the 20-dimensional UMAP output) — augmentation applies only to original ion images before encoding The task is standard natural-image contrastive learning where MSI-specific artifacts (Poisson noise, missing values) are not present in the data modality http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Stochastically masks pixel values in ion images to simulate the random missing-value pattern characteristic of mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data, used as part of DeepION's T_COL data augmentation (with an intensity-dependent variant reserved for T_ISO). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Stochastically masks pixel values in ion images to simulate the random missing-value pattern characteristic of mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data, used as part of DeepION's T_COL data augmentation (with an intensity-dependent variant reserved for T_ISO).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Augmenting for the ISO mode of DeepION: the intensity-dependent missing-value transform must be added there, so the COL-only recipe is the wrong choice Input is already an augmented view or a downstream representation vector (e.g. the 20-dimensional UMAP output) — augmentation applies only to original ion images before encoding The task is standard natural-image contrastive learning where MSI-specific artifacts (Poisson noise, missing values) are not present in the data modality

skills.description: Use when dispatching a statistical activity (t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) or other computation onto a chart/column in Instant Clue and the underlying dataset may contain missing values that the activity cannot handle.
skills.name: missing-value-prefiltering-before-statistical-activities
skills.search_text: missing-value-prefiltering-before-statistical-activities Use when dispatching a statistical activity (t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) or other computation onto a chart/column in Instant Clue and the underlying dataset may contain missing values that the activity cannot handle. When the activity you dispatch explicitly handles missing values — pre-filtering is only applied automatically if the activity cannot handle them When you intentionally need to impute or otherwise repair missing entries rather than drop rows — use the column-based imputation activity instead http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 In Instant Clue, before any statistical test (each test is an activity, e.g. t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) is executed, rows containing missing values are automatically filtered out for the scope of that activity only, leaving the source data unchanged. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6
skills.summary: In Instant Clue, before any statistical test (each test is an activity, e.g. t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) is executed, rows containing missing values are automatically filtered out for the scope of that activity only, leaving the source data unchanged.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the activity you dispatch explicitly handles missing values — pre-filtering is only applied automatically if the activity cannot handle them When you intentionally need to impute or otherwise repair missing entries rather than drop rows — use the column-based imputation activity instead

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g., tomato pericarp metabolic profiles from seasons 2001, 2003, 2004) contains missing metabolite measurements that would corrupt downstream pairwise Pearson correlation computation.
skills.name: missing-value-probabilistic-pca-imputation
skills.search_text: missing-value-probabilistic-pca-imputation Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g., tomato pericarp metabolic profiles from seasons 2001, 2003, 2004) contains missing metabolite measurements that would corrupt downstream pairwise Pearson correlation computation. The abundance matrix is already complete — imputation would only distort measured values before correlation thresholding The downstream analysis is not correlation-network construction (e.g., differential abundance testing where missingness should be modeled explicitly instead) Fills missing entries in metabolite abundance matrices by fitting a probabilistic PCA model with the pcaMethods package in Rstudio, as a prerequisite step before computing Pearson-correlation metabolite networks. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Fills missing entries in metabolite abundance matrices by fitting a probabilistic PCA model with the pcaMethods package in Rstudio, as a prerequisite step before computing Pearson-correlation metabolite networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance matrix is already complete — imputation would only distort measured values before correlation thresholding The downstream analysis is not correlation-network construction (e.g., differential abundance testing where missingness should be modeled explicitly instead)

skills.description: Use when a peak table matrix (pixels x m/z ion columns with X/Y coordinates) must be checked for missing/undetected signals before noise ion filtering or clustering, e.g. to validate a preprocessed AFADESI dataset's quality.
skills.name: missing-value-quantification-spatial-metabolomics
skills.search_text: missing-value-quantification-spatial-metabolomics Use when a peak table matrix (pixels x m/z ion columns with X/Y coordinates) must be checked for missing/undetected signals before noise ion filtering or clustering, e.g. to validate a preprocessed AFADESI dataset's quality. Input is raw MS imaging data (e.g. imzML) rather than an already-built peak table matrix — SMQVP expects a pixel x ion intensity matrix with X/Y coordinate columns The analysis goal is to impute or fill missing values rather than quantify and visualize their distribution The question concerns background consistency, noise ion filtering, isotopic/adduct identification, or other SMQVP quality visualization points unrelated to missingness http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantify and visualize missing-value distributions at both pixel and ion levels in a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix, using SMQVP's Missing Value Distribution quality visualization point on AFADESI-acquired mouse brain data. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Quantify and visualize missing-value distributions at both pixel and ion levels in a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix, using SMQVP's Missing Value Distribution quality visualization point on AFADESI-acquired mouse brain data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS imaging data (e.g. imzML) rather than an already-built peak table matrix — SMQVP expects a pixel x ion intensity matrix with X/Y coordinate columns The analysis goal is to impute or fill missing values rather than quantify and visualize their distribution The question concerns background consistency, noise ion filtering, isotopic/adduct identification, or other SMQVP quality visualization points unrelated to missingness

skills.description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion intensities, e.g. 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ions) needs quality assessment of detection completeness, or when deciding which pixels/ions to retain before preprocessing.
skills.name: missing-value-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: missing-value-ratio-computation Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion intensities, e.g. 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ions) needs quality assessment of detection completeness, or when deciding which pixels/ions to retain before preprocessing. Input is raw mass-spectrometry imaging data (e.g. imzML vendor files) rather than an already-picked feature matrix of m/z intensities per pixel — SMAnalyst QC operates on the uploaded feature table only The goal is peak picking or ion feature detection from spectra; missing-value ratios presuppose a completed peak-picking step with pixels × ions dimensions Assessing background signal spatial consistency (QC1) or median intensity distributions (QC2) — those use correlation and intensity metrics, not missing-value counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computation of missing-value rates in spatial metabolomics feature matrices as part of SMAnalyst's QC assessment: per-pixel missing ratios (proportion of undetected ions per pixel) and per-ion missing ratios (proportion of pixels where each ion was undetected), used to judge data completeness before and after noise-ion filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Computation of missing-value rates in spatial metabolomics feature matrices as part of SMAnalyst's QC assessment: per-pixel missing ratios (proportion of undetected ions per pixel) and per-ion missing ratios (proportion of pixels where each ion was undetected), used to judge data completeness before and after noise-ion filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mass-spectrometry imaging data (e.g. imzML vendor files) rather than an already-picked feature matrix of m/z intensities per pixel — SMAnalyst QC operates on the uploaded feature table only The goal is peak picking or ion feature detection from spectra; missing-value ratios presuppose a completed peak-picking step with pixels × ions dimensions Assessing background signal spatial consistency (QC1) or median intensity distributions (QC2) — those use correlation and intensity metrics, not missing-value counts

skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS pre-processing consensus map contains consensus features with missing intensity values in some sample files, and complete quantification is needed for statistical analysis.
skills.name: missing-value-requantification-of-consensus-features
skills.search_text: missing-value-requantification-of-consensus-features Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS pre-processing consensus map contains consensus features with missing intensity values in some sample files, and complete quantification is needed for statistical analysis. The feature matrix is already complete — no consensus features have missing intensity values, so targeted re-extraction offers no benefit. You want to keep original untargeted intensities untouched and only impute a few cells; UmetaFlow replaces all intensity values with targeted extraction results. Input is raw vendor data not yet pre-processed — re-quantification operates on the pre-processing consensus map, not raw files. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 UmetaFlow's optional re-quantification step fills missing intensities arising from untargeted pre-processing by running targeted extraction (FeatureFinderMetaboIdent) against a target library of consensus features that have at least one missing value across samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: UmetaFlow's optional re-quantification step fills missing intensities arising from untargeted pre-processing by running targeted extraction (FeatureFinderMetaboIdent) against a target library of consensus features that have at least one missing value across samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature matrix is already complete — no consensus features have missing intensity values, so targeted re-extraction offers no benefit. You want to keep original untargeted intensities untouched and only impute a few cells; UmetaFlow replaces all intensity values with targeted extraction results. Input is raw vendor data not yet pre-processed — re-quantification operates on the pre-processing consensus map, not raw files.

skills.description: Use when a targeted MS-based metabolomics or lipidomics QCpool data set (Sciex MultiQuant txt exports) contains features that are absent in some QCpool injections, and you must decide whether to impute, flag, or drop them without losing relevant biological information.
skills.name: missing-value-versus-absent-data-handling
skills.search_text: missing-value-versus-absent-data-handling Use when a targeted MS-based metabolomics or lipidomics QCpool data set (Sciex MultiQuant txt exports) contains features that are absent in some QCpool injections, and you must decide whether to impute, flag, or drop them without losing relevant biological information. When the input is already a cleaned feature table with no missing/absent entries and QCpool data are not involved — the QComics workflow is specific to QCpool-based QC of targeted MS metabolomics data. When analysing untargeted data where absence cannot be reliably distinguished from noise, as QComics was designed for targeted (Sciex MultiQuant) outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A QComics QC workflow stage that distinguishes 'missing' values (features below detection in a run but potentially detectable elsewhere) from 'truly absent' data (features genuinely not present in the sample matrix), so that imputation or exclusion decisions do not discard biologically meaningful information. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: A QComics QC workflow stage that distinguishes 'missing' values (features below detection in a run but potentially detectable elsewhere) from 'truly absent' data (features genuinely not present in the sample matrix), so that imputation or exclusion decisions do not discard biologically meaningful information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a cleaned feature table with no missing/absent entries and QCpool data are not involved — the QComics workflow is specific to QCpool-based QC of targeted MS metabolomics data. When analysing untargeted data where absence cannot be reliably distinguished from noise, as QComics was designed for targeted (Sciex MultiQuant) outputs.

skills.description: Use when an LC/MS feature table (e.g. apLCMS or XCMS output on a dataset like ST000868) contains missing/zero values and a two-group comparison (e.g. cell-type t-test at FDR <= 0.2) requires removing sparse features before testing.
skills.name: missing-value-zero-fraction-filtering
skills.search_text: missing-value-zero-fraction-filtering Use when an LC/MS feature table (e.g. apLCMS or XCMS output on a dataset like ST000868) contains missing/zero values and a two-group comparison (e.g. cell-type t-test at FDR <= 0.2) requires removing sparse features before testing. The input is already a cleaned feature table with missing values imputed or previously filtered — re-filtering would double-remove features The analysis goal is batch effect correction of raw preprocessing output rather than pre-statistical feature filtering (use the two-stage preprocessing skill instead) The feature table comes from a single-group design with no subgroup labels, since the <= 33% zero criterion is computed within each biological group http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A pre-statistical filter for LC/MS metabolomics feature tables that retains only features with <= 33% zero (missing) intensity values within at least one biological group, so that group-comparison tests like the oak vs. wine yeast t-test are performed only on features with usable signal in at least one condition. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: A pre-statistical filter for LC/MS metabolomics feature tables that retains only features with <= 33% zero (missing) intensity values within at least one biological group, so that group-comparison tests like the oak vs. wine yeast t-test are performed only on features with usable signal in at least one condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cleaned feature table with missing values imputed or previously filtered — re-filtering would double-remove features The analysis goal is batch effect correction of raw preprocessing output rather than pre-statistical feature filtering (use the two-stage preprocessing skill instead) The feature table comes from a single-group design with no subgroup labels, since the <= 33% zero criterion is computed within each biological group

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics intensity table contains features with intermittent missing signals and you must decide which are real zeros versus missing data before imputation or filtering.
skills.name: missing-versus-absent-data-discrimination
skills.search_text: missing-versus-absent-data-discrimination Use when a metabolomics intensity table contains features with intermittent missing signals and you must decide which are real zeros versus missing data before imputation or filtering. When the data are not MS-based metabolomics/lipidomics intensities with pooled QC (QCpool) samples measured at regular intervals — the QComics workflow assumes this design When missingness is purely random (MCAR) and no distinction between absent compounds and failed measurements is needed — a simple global imputation suffices When data are heterogeneous omics types other than MS-based metabolomics without adaptation — although QComics is extendable to other omics/MS data, thresholds were designed for metabolomics http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 QComics-based missing-data handling that distinguishes truly absent features (treated as real zeros) from genuine missing values, then filters variables with excessive missingness per study group. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: QComics-based missing-data handling that distinguishes truly absent features (treated as real zeros) from genuine missing values, then filters variables with excessive missingness per study group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data are not MS-based metabolomics/lipidomics intensities with pooled QC (QCpool) samples measured at regular intervals — the QComics workflow assumes this design When missingness is purely random (MCAR) and no distinction between absent compounds and failed measurements is needed — a simple global imputation suffices When data are heterogeneous omics types other than MS-based metabolomics without adaptation — although QComics is extendable to other omics/MS data, thresholds were designed for metabolomics

skills.description: Use when raw un/targeted metabolomics sample-by-feature matrices (e.g. Metabolon or Nightingale exports) need preanalysis cleaning by dropping samples and metabolites above missingness thresholds before downstream analysis.
skills.name: missingness-based-sample-feature-exclusion
skills.search_text: missingness-based-sample-feature-exclusion Use when raw un/targeted metabolomics sample-by-feature matrices (e.g. Metabolon or Nightingale exports) need preanalysis cleaning by dropping samples and metabolites above missingness thresholds before downstream analysis. Data has already passed missingness QC or is a curated feature table — re-running would drop nothing or re-filter inappropriately The goal is exploratory visualization or report generation rather than deciding which samples/metabolites to exclude Non-metabolomics omics data (e.g. gene expression) where metaboprep's missingness and peak-area QC semantics do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A quality-control filtering step from the metaboprep R package that excludes samples and metabolites (features) whose missingness exceeds user-defined thresholds (e.g. 0.2 at the user-defined level, >=80% at the extreme level), yielding a high-quality preanalysis dataset for metabolomics platforms such as Metabolon UPLC-MS/MS and Nightingale NMR. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac059
skills.summary: A quality-control filtering step from the metaboprep R package that excludes samples and metabolites (features) whose missingness exceeds user-defined thresholds (e.g. 0.2 at the user-defined level, >=80% at the extreme level), yielding a high-quality preanalysis dataset for metabolomics platforms such as Metabolon UPLC-MS/MS and Nightingale NMR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has already passed missingness QC or is a curated feature table — re-running would drop nothing or re-filter inappropriately The goal is exploratory visualization or report generation rather than deciding which samples/metabolites to exclude Non-metabolomics omics data (e.g. gene expression) where metaboprep's missingness and peak-area QC semantics do not apply

skills.description: Use when clinical metabolomics data (e.g. GC-TOF MS or UPLC-QTOF MS feature tables, log2-transformed) contain subject-specific biological variation that should be modeled and removed prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA/OPLS-DA.
skills.name: mixed-effects-metabolomics-data-processing
skills.search_text: mixed-effects-metabolomics-data-processing Use when clinical metabolomics data (e.g. GC-TOF MS or UPLC-QTOF MS feature tables, log2-transformed) contain subject-specific biological variation that should be modeled and removed prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA/OPLS-DA. The data matrix has not been pre-processed and log2-transformed as described (raw MS signals still requiring noise reduction, peak matching and retention time correction). There is no subject-level metadata available to formulate the random-effects structure of the LMMs. The goal is per-metabolite differential abundance testing rather than readjusting signals to improve multivariate classification; note the potential introduction of false positives due to increased sensitivity and the article's recommendation of further experimental validation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 An additional data processing step that fits a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to each metabolite signal using patient metadata (e.g. a random-intercept term (1|Id)) to readjust individual metabolite abundances in clinical metabolomics matrices, improving downstream PLS classification performance. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: An additional data processing step that fits a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to each metabolite signal using patient metadata (e.g. a random-intercept term (1|Id)) to readjust individual metabolite abundances in clinical metabolomics matrices, improving downstream PLS classification performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data matrix has not been pre-processed and log2-transformed as described (raw MS signals still requiring noise reduction, peak matching and retention time correction). There is no subject-level metadata available to formulate the random-effects structure of the LMMs. The goal is per-metabolite differential abundance testing rather than readjusting signals to improve multivariate classification; note the potential introduction of false positives due to increased sensitivity and the article's recommendation of further experimental validation.

skills.description: Use when quantitative parameters (intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, J coupling constants) must be extracted from 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra of multiplets whose lineshape is neither purely Gaussian nor purely Lorentzian.
skills.name: mixed-gaussian-lorentzian-lineshape-fitting
skills.search_text: mixed-gaussian-lorentzian-lineshape-fitting Use when quantitative parameters (intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, J coupling constants) must be extracted from 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra of multiplets whose lineshape is neither purely Gaussian nor purely Lorentzian. The spectrum is 2D (not 1D or pseudo-2D) — MultiNMRFit is designed for series of 1D spectra Only peak positions are needed without quantitative intensity/area/coupling estimation A lineshape model outside the built-in singlet–quadruplet multiplets is required and no user-defined model has been implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Fit 1D/pseudo-2D NMR multiplet signals (singlet through quadruplet) with MultiNMRFit's built-in mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian signal models to recover intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, and coupling constants with estimated standard deviations. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Fit 1D/pseudo-2D NMR multiplet signals (singlet through quadruplet) with MultiNMRFit's built-in mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian signal models to recover intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, and coupling constants with estimated standard deviations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum is 2D (not 1D or pseudo-2D) — MultiNMRFit is designed for series of 1D spectra Only peak positions are needed without quantitative intensity/area/coupling estimation A lineshape model outside the built-in singlet–quadruplet multiplets is required and no user-defined model has been implemented

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics meta-analysis input table mixes identifier types (common name, InChIKey, SMILES) for the same compounds, inflating unique-ID counts and masking duplicate votes across studies.
skills.name: mixed-identifier-type-mapping
skills.search_text: mixed-identifier-type-mapping Use when a metabolomics meta-analysis input table mixes identifier types (common name, InChIKey, SMILES) for the same compounds, inflating unique-ID counts and masking duplicate votes across studies. The input compound list already uses a single consistent identifier type (e.g. all InChIKeys), so harmonization adds no resolution of synonyms The analysis goal is raw spectral processing or feature detection rather than meta-analysis of already-aggregated statistics (p-value, fold-change) Compounds lack resolvable machine-readable IDs (InChIKey/SMILES) that webchem can map to common nomenclature http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Harmonizes heterogeneous compound identifiers (common names, InChIKeys, SMILES) onto a single common chemical nomenclature using Easy-Amanida's 'Include compounds IDs' option, which drives the amanida and webchem back-end, before running aggregate-statistics meta-analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jrsm.1713
skills.summary: Harmonizes heterogeneous compound identifiers (common names, InChIKeys, SMILES) onto a single common chemical nomenclature using Easy-Amanida's 'Include compounds IDs' option, which drives the amanida and webchem back-end, before running aggregate-statistics meta-analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input compound list already uses a single consistent identifier type (e.g. all InChIKeys), so harmonization adds no resolution of synonyms The analysis goal is raw spectral processing or feature detection rather than meta-analysis of already-aggregated statistics (p-value, fold-change) Compounds lack resolvable machine-readable IDs (InChIKey/SMILES) that webchem can map to common nomenclature

skills.description: Use when HRMS data were acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes and the goal is a single aligned feature table combining both polarities, rather than processing each mode independently.
skills.name: mixed-ionization-mode-feature-set-combination
skills.search_text: mixed-ionization-mode-feature-set-combination Use when HRMS data were acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes and the goal is a single aligned feature table combining both polarities, rather than processing each mode independently. Only one ionization mode was acquired — a classical single-polarity patRoon workflow suffices Features have already been aligned into a combined feature table — re-running makeSet on an aligned table is unnecessary The analysis goal is transformation product screening on a single polarity rather than cross-polarity feature alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A patRoon 2.0 sets workflow that separately detects features in positive and negative ionization LC-HRMS analyses, combines them into a single set via makeSet with default adducts ([M+H]+ and [M-H]-), converts m/z to neutral masses, and aligns/groups features across polarities into one mixed-polarity featureGroupsSet. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04029
skills.summary: A patRoon 2.0 sets workflow that separately detects features in positive and negative ionization LC-HRMS analyses, combines them into a single set via makeSet with default adducts ([M+H]+ and [M-H]-), converts m/z to neutral masses, and aligns/groups features across polarities into one mixed-polarity featureGroupsSet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one ionization mode was acquired — a classical single-polarity patRoon workflow suffices Features have already been aligned into a combined feature table — re-running makeSet on an aligned table is unnecessary The analysis goal is transformation product screening on a single polarity rather than cross-polarity feature alignment

skills.description: Use when sample cohorts carry variable pre- and postcentrifugation processing delays and you need to predict, per metabolite (NMR-quantified serum/plasma), which concentrations shift and by how much before running downstream analyses.
skills.name: mixed-model-based-delay-impact-prediction
skills.search_text: mixed-model-based-delay-impact-prediction Use when sample cohorts carry variable pre- and postcentrifugation processing delays and you need to predict, per metabolite (NMR-quantified serum/plasma), which concentrations shift and by how much before running downstream analyses. Samples are not peripheral blood plasma/serum or were not NMR-quantified — the models predict changes only for these metabolic parameters under pre-/postcentrifugation delay The pre-analytical table lacks date+time stamps from which pre- and post-centrifugation delays can be computed — the panel's Tools tab expects date+time stamp differences You only need Bruker BiobankQC-style basic pass/fail output without per-metabolite delay-effect quantification — PRIMA was developed to enhance that basic pass/fail output, so a simple QC call may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3339 Fit linear mixed models to predict and quantify how each NMR-quantified metabolic parameter in plasma/serum changes with pre- and postcentrifugation delays, then combine both delay types to flag metabolites undergoing minor vs. major change at a chosen tolerable-error threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c04938
skills.summary: Fit linear mixed models to predict and quantify how each NMR-quantified metabolic parameter in plasma/serum changes with pre- and postcentrifugation delays, then combine both delay types to flag metabolites undergoing minor vs. major change at a chosen tolerable-error threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are not peripheral blood plasma/serum or were not NMR-quantified — the models predict changes only for these metabolic parameters under pre-/postcentrifugation delay The pre-analytical table lacks date+time stamps from which pre- and post-centrifugation delays can be computed — the panel's Tools tab expects date+time stamp differences You only need Bruker BiobankQC-style basic pass/fail output without per-metabolite delay-effect quantification — PRIMA was developed to enhance that basic pass/fail output, so a simple QC call may suffice

skills.description: Use when benchmarking imputation methods on mixed-type or categorical-only data (e.g. the Children's Hospital data with 48 continuous and 76 categorical variables) and a numeric-only baseline such as KNNimpute must also handle categorical entries.
skills.name: mixed-type-categorical-dummy-coding
skills.search_text: mixed-type-categorical-dummy-coding Use when benchmarking imputation methods on mixed-type or categorical-only data (e.g. the Children's Hospital data with 48 continuous and 76 categorical variables) and a numeric-only baseline such as KNNimpute must also handle categorical entries. When the target method is missForest itself — it handles mixed-type data natively without dummy coding; the {-1,1} encoding is specific to the numeric-only KNNimpute baseline. When the dataset is purely continuous — the continuous pipeline (NRMSE, cross-validated KNNimpute/MissPALasso on standardized data) applies instead, with no dummy coding or PFC step. When the categorical data contain ill-distributed or nearly dependent variables for MICE, as on the Children's Hospital data, where results must be treated cautiously and significance statements cannot be reported. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encodes categorical variables of a mixed-type dataset into {-1,1} dichotomous dummy variables so that a purely numeric imputer (cross-validated KNNimpute, Algorithm 2) can be run as a baseline, then decodes the imputed dummy matrix back to the original categorical labels for PFC-based error evaluation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btr597
skills.summary: Encodes categorical variables of a mixed-type dataset into {-1,1} dichotomous dummy variables so that a purely numeric imputer (cross-validated KNNimpute, Algorithm 2) can be run as a baseline, then decodes the imputed dummy matrix back to the original categorical labels for PFC-based error evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target method is missForest itself — it handles mixed-type data natively without dummy coding; the {-1,1} encoding is specific to the numeric-only KNNimpute baseline. When the dataset is purely continuous — the continuous pipeline (NRMSE, cross-validated KNNimpute/MissPALasso on standardized data) applies instead, with no dummy coding or PFC step. When the categorical data contain ill-distributed or nearly dependent variables for MICE, as on the Children's Hospital data, where results must be treated cautiously and significance statements cannot be reported.

skills.name: mixture-component-identification
skills.search_text: mixture-component-identification Use when given one or more 1H NMR spectra of flavor mixtures (known or undisclosed compositions) and a pretrained FlavorFormer model, to produce per-spectrum component predictions and compute ACC, TPR, and FPR against a ground-truth formulation or standards library. The input consists of spectra of pure, single compounds rather than multi-component flavor mixtures — FlavorFormer's fusion pooling and weighted loss are designed for mixture identification, and the reported TPR/FPR gains are specific to complex mixtures. You need novel model training from scratch rather than reload-and-predict — use the training path of demo.ipynb instead of treating this as an inference-only skill. The spectral data are not 1H NMR (e.g. 13C, MS, or IR) — the paper's model, metrics, and reported accuracies are specific to 1H NMR spectra of flavor mixtures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Identify the chemical components of a flavor mixture from its 1H NMR spectrum using FlavorFormer, a hybrid CNN and Transformer model that combines a bi-encoder and cross-encoder with fusion pooling and a weighted loss function to predict the compound list. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2025.115372

skills.description: Use when you have an XCMS-derived feature table of extracted ion chromatogram peaks with expert Pass/Fail quality labels and need to select and benchmark a machine learning classifier that flags low-quality peak integrations.
skills.name: ml-classification-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: ml-classification-metric-evaluation Use when you have an XCMS-derived feature table of extracted ion chromatogram peaks with expert Pass/Fail quality labels and need to select and benchmark a machine learning classifier that flags low-quality peak integrations. Input is a vendor-processed output (e.g. MassHunter Profinder, Progenesis QI, Compound Discoverer) that is not an XCMS object — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input and cannot consume uniquely formatted vendor outputs in its current form. The dataset contains many low-abundance Pass peaks but few labeled examples of that class — the development dataset did not contain many such examples, and the classifier is conservative and performs worse for the low-quality (Fail) class than the high-quality one on Tests 1 and 2. The task is peak detection or alignment parameter optimization rather than quality classification of already-detected peaks — IPO or warpgroup are the appropriate tools for pre-filtering peak integration quality before classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates supervised peak-quality classifiers for untargeted LC–MS metabolomics by pairing three peak-quality metric sets (Zhang M4, TargetedMSQC-derived M7, and combined M11) with eight ML algorithms, using fivefold cross-validation on the expert-labeled development dataset (MW id ST000726) and selecting the best classifier via Friedman/Nemenyi statistical tests on Accuracy, F-measure, Pass/Fail F-measure and AUC. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Evaluates supervised peak-quality classifiers for untargeted LC–MS metabolomics by pairing three peak-quality metric sets (Zhang M4, TargetedMSQC-derived M7, and combined M11) with eight ML algorithms, using fivefold cross-validation on the expert-labeled development dataset (MW id ST000726) and selecting the best classifier via Friedman/Nemenyi statistical tests on Accuracy, F-measure, Pass/Fail F-measure and AUC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a vendor-processed output (e.g. MassHunter Profinder, Progenesis QI, Compound Discoverer) that is not an XCMS object — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input and cannot consume uniquely formatted vendor outputs in its current form. The dataset contains many low-abundance Pass peaks but few labeled examples of that class — the development dataset did not contain many such examples, and the classifier is conservative and performs worse for the low-quality (Fail) class than the high-quality one on Tests 1 and 2. The task is peak detection or alignment parameter optimization rather than quality classification of already-detected peaks — IPO or warpgroup are the appropriate tools for pre-filtering peak integration quality before classification.

skills.description: Decision support for benchmarking imputation methods on complete metabolomics matrices when you need missing values reflecting both MNAR (below-LOD) and MAR mechanisms, e.g. 15% missingness with more MNAR than MAR.
skills.name: mnar-mar-missingness-injection
skills.search_text: mnar-mar-missingness-injection Decision support for benchmarking imputation methods on complete metabolomics matrices when you need missing values reflecting both MNAR (below-LOD) and MAR mechanisms, e.g. 15% missingness with more MNAR than MAR. The input matrix already contains missing values — the skill assumes a complete matrix so deletions create known ground truth; imputing an already-incomplete dataset needs a different workflow. Missingness in your data is entirely below-LOD (pure MNAR) or entirely random (pure MCAR) with no mixture — a single-mechanism mask is then more appropriate than the combined MNAR+MAR scheme. The goal is to impute real incomplete clinical/pre-clinical metabolomics data for downstream analysis rather than to evaluate an imputer against simulated ground truth. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Injects controlled missingness into complete metabolomics data by combining below-limit-of-detection (MNAR) deletions and random (MAR/MCAR) deletions, so that imputation algorithms such as KNN-TN, KNN-CR, and KNN-EU can be benchmarked against known ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: Injects controlled missingness into complete metabolomics data by combining below-limit-of-detection (MNAR) deletions and random (MAR/MCAR) deletions, so that imputation algorithms such as KNN-TN, KNN-CR, and KNN-EU can be benchmarked against known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix already contains missing values — the skill assumes a complete matrix so deletions create known ground truth; imputing an already-incomplete dataset needs a different workflow. Missingness in your data is entirely below-LOD (pure MNAR) or entirely random (pure MCAR) with no mixture — a single-mechanism mask is then more appropriate than the combined MNAR+MAR scheme. The goal is to impute real incomplete clinical/pre-clinical metabolomics data for downstream analysis rather than to evaluate an imputer against simulated ground truth.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data with genuine missing values and no complete reference matrix — the evaluation requires an original complete data matrix as ground truth. Unsupervised evaluation goals (e.g., PCA-based structure preservation) — this skill is specifically group-label-informed (t-tests and PLS-DA supervised ordination). Missing values in non-targeted GC/MS data assumed to be MCAR/MAR before missing retrieval — GSimp's left-censored defaults (lo=-Inf, hi='min') target MNAR, and non-informative bounds should be used instead.

skills.description: Use when you have a complete (or near-complete) metabolomics data matrix, e.g. data_sim.csv or real_data.csv, and need to simulate left-censored MNAR missingness to evaluate imputation accuracy, distribution preservation, or statistical sensitivity.
skills.name: mnar-missing-data-simulation
skills.search_text: mnar-missing-data-simulation Use when you have a complete (or near-complete) metabolomics data matrix, e.g. data_sim.csv or real_data.csv, and need to simulate left-censored MNAR missingness to evaluate imputation accuracy, distribution preservation, or statistical sensitivity. When the dataset's missingness is MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored MNAR — the paper states the majority of missing values in non-targeted GC/MS data were assumed MCAR/MAR before manual missing retrieval, and non-informative bounds (lo=-Inf, hi=Inf) apply there instead When the data already contain real missing values and no complete reference exists — degradation simulation requires a complete matrix to compute NRMSE, Procrustes SSE, and TPR against ground truth When evaluating right-censored missing values — use 'rsym' initialization with an informative lower truncation point rather than the left-censored cut-off mechanism http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates MNAR-degraded versions of complete metabolomics matrices using MNAR_gen_imp, introducing left-censored missingness at controlled proportions of missing variables and per-variable cut-offs, to benchmark imputation methods (GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN, HM) against a known complete reference. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Generates MNAR-degraded versions of complete metabolomics matrices using MNAR_gen_imp, introducing left-censored missingness at controlled proportions of missing variables and per-variable cut-offs, to benchmark imputation methods (GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN, HM) against a known complete reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset's missingness is MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored MNAR — the paper states the majority of missing values in non-targeted GC/MS data were assumed MCAR/MAR before manual missing retrieval, and non-informative bounds (lo=-Inf, hi=Inf) apply there instead When the data already contain real missing values and no complete reference exists — degradation simulation requires a complete matrix to compute NRMSE, Procrustes SSE, and TPR against ground truth When evaluating right-censored missing values — use 'rsym' initialization with an informative lower truncation point rather than the left-censored cut-off mechanism

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains missing intensity values and you need to classify the missingness mechanism (MNAR vs MAR) and apply an imputation method before downstream statistical analysis.
skills.name: mnar-vs-mar-missingness-classification
skills.search_text: mnar-vs-mar-missingness-classification Use when a metabolomics feature table contains missing intensity values and you need to classify the missingness mechanism (MNAR vs MAR) and apply an imputation method before downstream statistical analysis. Input is already fully imputed or contains zero NA/NaN entries — no imputation is needed Data are raw instrument files (e.g. mzML/NetCDF) rather than a processed feature intensity table — peak detection/alignment must precede imputation The goal is reporting/visualization of completed analyses rather than preprocessing feature tables — use MetaboReport's other modules instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs MetaboReport's missing value imputation strategy for metabolomics feature tables, covering single-value imputation (constant 1, one-fifth-minimum, mean, median) and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) imputation, chosen according to whether gaps arise from missing-not-at-random (MNAR, e.g. below-detection-limit signals) or missing-at-random (MAR) mechanisms. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Reconstructs MetaboReport's missing value imputation strategy for metabolomics feature tables, covering single-value imputation (constant 1, one-fifth-minimum, mean, median) and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) imputation, chosen according to whether gaps arise from missing-not-at-random (MNAR, e.g. below-detection-limit signals) or missing-at-random (MAR) mechanisms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already fully imputed or contains zero NA/NaN entries — no imputation is needed Data are raw instrument files (e.g. mzML/NetCDF) rather than a processed feature intensity table — peak detection/alignment must precede imputation The goal is reporting/visualization of completed analyses rather than preprocessing feature tables — use MetaboReport's other modules instead

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single tool's annotation with no cross-tool or ClinVar comparison — normalization for concordance benchmarking adds no value All variants are already normalized against a common transcript set (e.g., MANE) with no repeat-region or MNV content to shift The analysis targets non-coding or structural annotation tasks rather than HGVS nomenclature and coding-impact concordance

skills.description: Use when draft reconstructions from different pipelines (KBase, RAVEN 2.0, CarveMe, AuReMe/Pathway Tools) use incompatible identifier namespaces, or when molecular properties must be pulled from PubChem for MNXref metabolites.
skills.name: mnxref-identifier-cross-referencing
skills.search_text: mnxref-identifier-cross-referencing Use when draft reconstructions from different pipelines (KBase, RAVEN 2.0, CarveMe, AuReMe/Pathway Tools) use incompatible identifier namespaces, or when molecular properties must be pulled from PubChem for MNXref metabolites. When reconstructions already share a common identifier namespace (e.g., all models are already MNXref-consistent) and no external molecular properties are needed When the analysis requires full compound coverage — only ~26% of InChI keys translate to PubChem CIDs, so properties will be missing for most metabolites http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Translates metabolite and reaction identifiers to MNXref using the MetaNetX translation tables (chem_prop.tsv, chem_xref.tsv) and maps MNXref entries to PubChem CIDs via InChI keys, enabling retrieval of molecular properties (MW, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RB, XLogP3) for downstream permeability classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: Translates metabolite and reaction identifiers to MNXref using the MetaNetX translation tables (chem_prop.tsv, chem_xref.tsv) and maps MNXref entries to PubChem CIDs via InChI keys, enabling retrieval of molecular properties (MW, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RB, XLogP3) for downstream permeability classification.

skills.search_text: mnxref-identifier-matching Use when merging or comparing draft genome-scale metabolic reconstructions from different tools (KBase, CarveMe, RAVEN 2.0, AuReMe) whose self-defined identifiers differ, before consensus generation or MNXref-based gap filling. Reconstructions whose entries already come from the MetaNetX database and are already structurally matched between various databases — re-translation adds no information Cross-reference-based model comparison when source models lack reaction cross-references to namespaces other than self-defined identifiers (translations only possible 'whenever possible') http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Translates metabolite, reaction, and gene identifiers from draft metabolic reconstructions (generated by tools such as KBase, RAVEN 2.0, CarveMe, AuReMe/Pathway Tools) into MNXref identifiers via the MNXref reference files, so that models can be merged into a consensus and compared against a common gap-filling database (Universal-model-MNXref-balanced.mat). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906

skills.search_text: mobile-phase-constraint-validation Use when enumerating candidate LC gradients (p-dimensional mobile-phase percentage vectors over gradient time points) for BAGO's gpModel.genSearchSpace and you must filter out gradients that are not physically executable. When the goal is scoring gradients after experimentation (separation efficiency from retention times via sepEfficiency) rather than defining the pre-experimental search space When optimizing isocratic or non-monotonic gradient programs that intentionally violate the monotonic strong-mobile-phase assumption When the objective is selecting the next gradient to run (computeNextGradient with an acquisition function such as EI), which operates on the already-constrained space http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A validation step in the BAGO gradient search-space generator that enforces two physical plausibility constraints — monotonically increasing strong mobile phase percentage and total eluting power within a reasonable range — on every enumerated LC gradient before it enters the Bayesian optimization search space. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.09.08.556930
skills.summary: A validation step in the BAGO gradient search-space generator that enforces two physical plausibility constraints — monotonically increasing strong mobile phase percentage and total eluting power within a reasonable range — on every enumerated LC gradient before it enters the Bayesian optimization search space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is scoring gradients after experimentation (separation efficiency from retention times via sepEfficiency) rather than defining the pre-experimental search space When optimizing isocratic or non-monotonic gradient programs that intentionally violate the monotonic strong-mobile-phase assumption When the objective is selecting the next gradient to run (computeNextGradient with an acquisition function such as EI), which operates on the already-constrained space

skills.search_text: modality-contribution-angular-similarity-analysis Use when a fused ST-SM latent embedding has been trained with SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM and you need to quantify each modality's contribution to the shared representation, e.g. during the Fig. 4d ccRCC IM2 integration benchmark. The embedding was produced by a baseline method (Seurat RPCA/CCA, scVI, scANVI, totalVI, scPoli, spaVAE, PCA) that does not expose separate ST and SM modality embeddings — use scIB metrics instead The data are single-cell or subcellular resolution ST/SM — SpatialMETA's angular-similarity interpretability is designed for low-resolution spot-level ST and SM data More than two modalities are being integrated — SpatialMETA currently supports only two modalities (ST and SM) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Quantifies how much the spatial transcriptomics (ST) versus spatial metabolomics (SM) modalities contribute to SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM fused latent embedding by computing angular similarity between modality-specific embeddings, improving interpretability of the cross-modal integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Quantifies how much the spatial transcriptomics (ST) versus spatial metabolomics (SM) modalities contribute to SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM fused latent embedding by computing angular similarity between modality-specific embeddings, improving interpretability of the cross-modal integration.

skills.description: Use when you have colocalised SM ('SPM' assay) and ST ('SPT' assay) data on shared spatial units — e.g. MALDI pixels binned into Visium spots — and need integrated spot-level clusters that a single modality alone cannot resolve.
skills.name: modality-weighted-spatial-clustering
skills.search_text: modality-weighted-spatial-clustering Use when you have colocalised SM ('SPM' assay) and ST ('SPT' assay) data on shared spatial units — e.g. MALDI pixels binned into Visium spots — and need integrated spot-level clusters that a single modality alone cannot resolve. You hold only one modality (SM-only or ST-only): run standard Seurat FindNeighbors/FindClusters on the single assay instead — MultiOmicIntegration requires both 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays on shared coordinates. The spatial units of the two modalities do not colocalise and cannot be binned (e.g. unpaired tissue sections or incompatible resolutions): MapSpatialOmics spot-binning must be feasible first, otherwise integration is built on misaligned measurements. Modality-specific quality checks fail (e.g. spot-binned metabolic signal diverges from raw-pixel signal for key metabolites like dopamine): fix the mapping before clustering, since WNN clusters will inherit binning artefacts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 SpaMTP's MultiOmicIntegration performs Seurat-based weighted-nearest-neighbour (WNN) integration of spatial metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics assays so that per-spot clusters reflect combined metabolite and gene expression, recovering spot populations (e.g. opposing striatal metabolic activity) that single-modality clustering misses. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: SpaMTP's MultiOmicIntegration performs Seurat-based weighted-nearest-neighbour (WNN) integration of spatial metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics assays so that per-spot clusters reflect combined metabolite and gene expression, recovering spot populations (e.g. opposing striatal metabolic activity) that single-modality clustering misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You hold only one modality (SM-only or ST-only): run standard Seurat FindNeighbors/FindClusters on the single assay instead — MultiOmicIntegration requires both 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays on shared coordinates. The spatial units of the two modalities do not colocalise and cannot be binned (e.g. unpaired tissue sections or incompatible resolutions): MapSpatialOmics spot-binning must be feasible first, otherwise integration is built on misaligned measurements. Modality-specific quality checks fail (e.g. spot-binned metabolic signal diverges from raw-pixel signal for key metabolites like dopamine): fix the mapping before clustering, since WNN clusters will inherit binning artefacts.

skills.description: Use when you have predicted spectra (mgf/msp) from a FIORA checkpoint and paired reference spectra, and need CLI-driven cosine-similarity metrics per test split (NIST/MS-DIAL test split, MSnLib, CASMI 16/22) to benchmark prediction quality.
skills.name: model-checkpoint-evaluation-via-cli
skills.search_text: model-checkpoint-evaluation-via-cli Use when you have predicted spectra (mgf/msp) from a FIORA checkpoint and paired reference spectra, and need CLI-driven cosine-similarity metrics per test split (NIST/MS-DIAL test split, MSnLib, CASMI 16/22) to benchmark prediction quality. You need retention time or CCS accuracy metrics rather than spectral cosine similarity — those are separate prediction outputs not covered by the spectral evaluation workflow described here Spectra were acquired with multi-step (MSn, n>2) fragmentation — FIORA lacks multi-step fragmentation support, so its evaluations are limited to single-step MS/MS Predictions come from CFM-ID trained on METLIN17 where train/test compound separation cannot be guaranteed — interpret such comparisons with the paper's stated caveat rather than as a clean generalization test http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluate a trained FIORA spectral-prediction checkpoint against reference spectra through the packaged command-line evaluation tool, computing the square-root-transformed spectral cosine similarity (spectral_sqrt_cosine) and writing per-split result CSVs for downstream aggregation (e.g., Table 1 benchmarks vs. CFM-ID and ICEBERG). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Evaluate a trained FIORA spectral-prediction checkpoint against reference spectra through the packaged command-line evaluation tool, computing the square-root-transformed spectral cosine similarity (spectral_sqrt_cosine) and writing per-split result CSVs for downstream aggregation (e.g., Table 1 benchmarks vs. CFM-ID and ICEBERG).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need retention time or CCS accuracy metrics rather than spectral cosine similarity — those are separate prediction outputs not covered by the spectral evaluation workflow described here Spectra were acquired with multi-step (MSn, n>2) fragmentation — FIORA lacks multi-step fragmentation support, so its evaluations are limited to single-step MS/MS Predictions come from CFM-ID trained on METLIN17 where train/test compound separation cannot be guaranteed — interpret such comparisons with the paper's stated caveat rather than as a clean generalization test

skills.description: Use when a trained GNN reaction-pair classifier has finished training on 14,974 RP / 14,974 non-RP pairs (8:1:1 split) and its checkpoint, prediction scores, and evaluation artifacts must be saved for reproducibility.
skills.name: model-checkpoint-persistence
skills.search_text: model-checkpoint-persistence Use when a trained GNN reaction-pair classifier has finished training on 14,974 RP / 14,974 non-RP pairs (8:1:1 split) and its checkpoint, prediction scores, and evaluation artifacts must be saved for reproducibility. The task is only threshold selection or ROC computation on already-saved scores — no checkpoint needs to be written. The model architecture or feature pipeline (graph convolutional + fingerprint + reaction-class features) has changed, making an existing checkpoint incompatible and misleading on reload. The classifier is being applied through the full MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3 annotation pipeline rather than being trained/evaluated standalone. Persist the trained GNN reaction-pair classifier (built with PyTorch/PyTorch Geometric for MetDNA3's metabolic reaction network curation) as a serialized checkpoint alongside its test-set prediction scores and ROC curve figure, so the reaction-relationship prediction can be reloaded, audited, and reproduced without retraining. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Persist the trained GNN reaction-pair classifier (built with PyTorch/PyTorch Geometric for MetDNA3's metabolic reaction network curation) as a serialized checkpoint alongside its test-set prediction scores and ROC curve figure, so the reaction-relationship prediction can be reloaded, audited, and reproduced without retraining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is only threshold selection or ROC computation on already-saved scores — no checkpoint needs to be written. The model architecture or feature pipeline (graph convolutional + fingerprint + reaction-class features) has changed, making an existing checkpoint incompatible and misleading on reload. The classifier is being applied through the full MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3 annotation pipeline rather than being trained/evaluated standalone.

skills.description: Use when a CNN takes fixed-size grayscale images as input and you must choose among several candidate image resolutions to maximize validation accuracy while controlling training/inference cost.
skills.name: model-efficiency-tradeoff-analysis
skills.search_text: model-efficiency-tradeoff-analysis Use when a CNN takes fixed-size grayscale images as input and you must choose among several candidate image resolutions to maximize validation accuracy while controlling training/inference cost. Input is an aligned feature table (tabular MS features) rather than rendered grayscale fingerprint images — this skill ablates the resolution of MS2toImg image inputs specifically Samples cannot be assigned to high/low activity groups (no normalized bioactivity values relative to the 0.4/0.6 thresholds), since stratified labeling is prerequisite to the cross-validated comparison Deployment fixes a single image size with no efficiency–accuracy tradeoff to evaluate, making the multi-resolution sweep unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains an identical CNN on grayscale 'molecular fingerprint' images rendered at multiple input resolutions (75×70, 150×140, 300×280) and compares accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 to select the resolution that balances predictive performance against computational efficiency. For the MS2toImg framework, the medium 150×140 resolution hit peak validation accuracy while 300×280 overfit and 75×70 underperformed. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Trains an identical CNN on grayscale 'molecular fingerprint' images rendered at multiple input resolutions (75×70, 150×140, 300×280) and compares accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 to select the resolution that balances predictive performance against computational efficiency. For the MS2toImg framework, the medium 150×140 resolution hit peak validation accuracy while 300×280 overfit and 75×70 underperformed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an aligned feature table (tabular MS features) rather than rendered grayscale fingerprint images — this skill ablates the resolution of MS2toImg image inputs specifically Samples cannot be assigned to high/low activity groups (no normalized bioactivity values relative to the 0.4/0.6 thresholds), since stratified labeling is prerequisite to the cross-validated comparison Deployment fixes a single image size with no efficiency–accuracy tradeoff to evaluate, making the multi-resolution sweep unnecessary
