skills.name: model-quality-evaluation-sensitivity-precision
skills.search_text: model-quality-evaluation-sensitivity-precision Use when assessing how faithful draft or consensus genome-scale metabolic reconstructions are to curated reference models, and when true negatives cannot be defined so only sensitivity and precision are reportable. When no curated reference model exists for the organism — sensitivity/precision against a reference cannot be computed When full model quality assessment is needed (e.g. via memote test suite) rather than content-accuracy against a reference When true negatives are determinable and full confusion-matrix metrics are wanted http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Evaluate automatically generated metabolic reconstructions by comparing them to curated reference models (e.g. iMZ1055 for B. megaterium and iRP911 for M. extorquens), computing sensitivity and precision as the only quality metrics because true negatives cannot be determined. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
skills.summary: Evaluate automatically generated metabolic reconstructions by comparing them to curated reference models (e.g. iMZ1055 for B. megaterium and iRP911 for M. extorquens), computing sensitivity and precision as the only quality metrics because true negatives cannot be determined.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no curated reference model exists for the organism — sensitivity/precision against a reference cannot be computed When full model quality assessment is needed (e.g. via memote test suite) rather than content-accuracy against a reference When true negatives are determinable and full confusion-matrix metrics are wanted

skills.description: Use when a multi-step statistical pipeline (e.g. mean centring followed by PCA) must be built from struct/structToolbox model objects and applied to a DatasetExperiment to obtain predicted outputs such as PCA scores.
skills.name: model-sequence-composition-with-plus-operator
skills.search_text: model-sequence-composition-with-plus-operator Use when a multi-step statistical pipeline (e.g. mean centring followed by PCA) must be built from struct/structToolbox model objects and applied to a DatasetExperiment to obtain predicted outputs such as PCA scores. When a single model step suffices — composition with '+' is only needed to chain methods (e.g. mean centring before PCA); a lone model object can be trained and applied directly. When the input is not a struct DatasetExperiment — model_train/model_apply expect DatasetExperiment objects in struct format, not plain data frames or matrices. When methods are not implemented as struct template objects (e.g. ad hoc R functions without struct classes) — they cannot be combined with the '+' operator into a model_seq. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compose struct model objects (e.g. mean_centre and PCA from structToolbox) into a model_seq using the '+' operator, train and apply the sequence to a DatasetExperiment, and extract the default predicted output (two-component PCA scores). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa1031
skills.summary: Compose struct model objects (e.g. mean_centre and PCA from structToolbox) into a model_seq using the '+' operator, train and apply the sequence to a DatasetExperiment, and extract the default predicted output (two-component PCA scores).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single model step suffices — composition with '+' is only needed to chain methods (e.g. mean centring before PCA); a lone model object can be trained and applied directly. When the input is not a struct DatasetExperiment — model_train/model_apply expect DatasetExperiment objects in struct format, not plain data frames or matrices. When methods are not implemented as struct template objects (e.g. ad hoc R functions without struct classes) — they cannot be combined with the '+' operator into a model_seq.

skills.description: Use when re-implementing or adapting a published CCS prediction architecture (e.g., extending SigmaCCS with fingerprints, descriptors, molecule type, or instrument type features) and you must confirm the assembled modules execute on real molecular graphs before training.
skills.name: model-structure-verification
skills.search_text: model-structure-verification Use when re-implementing or adapting a published CCS prediction architecture (e.g., extending SigmaCCS with fingerprints, descriptors, molecule type, or instrument type features) and you must confirm the assembled modules execute on real molecular graphs before training. You only need to benchmark pre-existing published models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) rather than reconstruct or modify an architecture — train and evaluate them as-is instead. Input is already trained model weights or prediction outputs (e.g., Zenodo prediction archives) rather than SMILES/features to build a network from. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs and sanity-checks a GNN-based CCS prediction architecture (Mol2CCS as an extension of SigmaCCS) by wiring the three ECC graph layers of SigmaCCS in parallel with a four-layer fully connected module (256/512/512/256 neurons, dropout 0.1) for seven extra features, concatenating them, and confirming the assembled network executes a correct forward pass on sample molecular graphs. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs and sanity-checks a GNN-based CCS prediction architecture (Mol2CCS as an extension of SigmaCCS) by wiring the three ECC graph layers of SigmaCCS in parallel with a four-layer fully connected module (256/512/512/256 neurons, dropout 0.1) for seven extra features, concatenating them, and confirming the assembled network executes a correct forward pass on sample molecular graphs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to benchmark pre-existing published models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) rather than reconstruct or modify an architecture — train and evaluate them as-is instead. Input is already trained model weights or prediction outputs (e.g., Zenodo prediction archives) rather than SMILES/features to build a network from.

skills.description: Use when deciding whether to merge multi-collision-energy MS/MS spectra before CNN training, by comparing wall-clock epoch times between spectral-representation variants.
skills.name: model-training-time-benchmarking
skills.search_text: model-training-time-benchmarking Use when deciding whether to merge multi-collision-energy MS/MS spectra before CNN training, by comparing wall-clock epoch times between spectral-representation variants. The goal is measuring annotation accuracy or embedding quality (Euclidean distance, cosine similarity) rather than training cost — use the spectral-representation ablation skill instead. Inputs are already merged spectra and the only remaining variant is merged-plus-neutral-loss; epoch-time differences then reflect neutral-loss processing, not the merge decision itself. Training on external benchmarks (CASMI 2016/2022, ARUS) where the original timing claim on the paper's test split does not directly apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark computational cost of CNN training under different spectral-representation schemes by timing one full epoch with merged spectra versus individual collision-energy spectra, quantifying the ~17x speed-up from merged inputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Benchmark computational cost of CNN training under different spectral-representation schemes by timing one full epoch with merged spectra versus individual collision-energy spectra, quantifying the ~17x speed-up from merged inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is measuring annotation accuracy or embedding quality (Euclidean distance, cosine similarity) rather than training cost — use the spectral-representation ablation skill instead. Inputs are already merged spectra and the only remaining variant is merged-plus-neutral-loss; epoch-time differences then reflect neutral-loss processing, not the merge decision itself. Training on external benchmarks (CASMI 2016/2022, ARUS) where the original timing claim on the paper's test split does not directly apply.

skills.description: Use when building a benchmark of structurally related compound pairs from reference MS/MS libraries where each pair must differ by exactly one modification site, and you need to verify single-edge boundaries with RDKit substructure matching.
skills.name: modification-site-edge-counting
skills.search_text: modification-site-edge-counting Use when building a benchmark of structurally related compound pairs from reference MS/MS libraries where each pair must differ by exactly one modification site, and you need to verify single-edge boundaries with RDKit substructure matching. When compound pairs differ by more than one edge between the matched substructure and the remainder, i.e. multiple simultaneous modification sites When precursor mass exceeds 2000 Da or the mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller compound's precursor mass When the two compounds do not share the same M+H adduct or were acquired under non-matched instrument conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Enumerate candidate analog pairs from public MS/MS libraries and count the graph edges between the matched substructure and the remainder of the heavier compound, retaining only pairs with exactly one such edge so that a single structural modification site is defined. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Enumerate candidate analog pairs from public MS/MS libraries and count the graph edges between the matched substructure and the remainder of the heavier compound, retaining only pairs with exactly one such edge so that a single structural modification site is defined.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When compound pairs differ by more than one edge between the matched substructure and the remainder, i.e. multiple simultaneous modification sites When precursor mass exceeds 2000 Da or the mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller compound's precursor mass When the two compounds do not share the same M+H adduct or were acquired under non-matched instrument conditions

skills.description: Use when a ModiFinder prediction has produced a per-atom likelihood array Ω for the known compound and you need to collapse it into a single evaluation score that rewards peaked, site-concentrated distributions over diffuse, ambiguous ones.
skills.name: modification-site-likelihood-distribution-interpretation
skills.search_text: modification-site-likelihood-distribution-interpretation Use when a ModiFinder prediction has produced a per-atom likelihood array Ω for the known compound and you need to collapse it into a single evaluation score that rewards peaked, site-concentrated distributions over diffuse, ambiguous ones. You only need ModiFinder's qualitative top-ranked modification-site prediction, not a quantitative evaluation of the likelihood distribution Input peaks have not yet passed ModiFinder's pipeline (intensity filtering <1% base peak, Euclidean-norm-1 normalization, 40 ppm substructure assignment), so no valid Ω exists yet The structure has no calculable 2D graph diameter Φ (e.g., disconnected or trivial graph), making normalized distances undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Interprets ModiFinder's per-atom modification-site likelihood array Ω by post-processing it (threshold 0.5, power of 4, renormalization) and scoring it with the Average-distance metric, which balances proximity cover (high-scoring atoms near the true site) against ambiguity cover (informativeness of a diffuse likelihood array). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Interprets ModiFinder's per-atom modification-site likelihood array Ω by post-processing it (threshold 0.5, power of 4, renormalization) and scoring it with the Average-distance metric, which balances proximity cover (high-scoring atoms near the true site) against ambiguity cover (informativeness of a diffuse likelihood array).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need ModiFinder's qualitative top-ranked modification-site prediction, not a quantitative evaluation of the likelihood distribution Input peaks have not yet passed ModiFinder's pipeline (intensity filtering <1% base peak, Euclidean-norm-1 normalization, 40 ppm substructure assignment), so no valid Ω exists yet The structure has no calculable 2D graph diameter Φ (e.g., disconnected or trivial graph), making normalized distances undefined

skills.description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra of a structurally related known-unknown compound pair and need to score each atom of the known compound for being the modification site.
skills.name: modification-site-likelihood-scoring
skills.search_text: modification-site-likelihood-scoring Use when you have MS/MS spectra of a structurally related known-unknown compound pair and need to score each atom of the known compound for being the modification site. The known and unknown spectra are not structurally related analogs (no MS/MS analog-search relationship or shared molecular-network edge) The pair has more than one modification site (benchmark eligibility requires exactly one modification site determined by RDKit GetSubstructMatch edge count) or precursor mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller compound The goal is full de novo structure elucidation rather than localizing a modification on a known scaffold (use MetFrag, MAGMa, MIDAS, or MS-Finder for general fragmentation analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 ModiFinder-style per-atom likelihood scoring that localizes structural modification sites by combining MS/MS spectral alignment (shifted vs. unshifted peaks) with MAGMa combinatorial-fragmentation substructure annotations on the known compound's 2D graph. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: ModiFinder-style per-atom likelihood scoring that localizes structural modification sites by combining MS/MS spectral alignment (shifted vs. unshifted peaks) with MAGMa combinatorial-fragmentation substructure annotations on the known compound's 2D graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The known and unknown spectra are not structurally related analogs (no MS/MS analog-search relationship or shared molecular-network edge) The pair has more than one modification site (benchmark eligibility requires exactly one modification site determined by RDKit GetSubstructMatch edge count) or precursor mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller compound The goal is full de novo structure elucidation rather than localizing a modification on a known scaffold (use MetFrag, MAGMa, MIDAS, or MS-Finder for general fragmentation analysis)

skills.description: Use when query MS/MS spectra resemble but do not exactly match library spectra, and the goal is to detect putative analogs via mass shifts (e.g., the −41 Da stenothricin analog class consistent with a lysine-to-serine substitution).
skills.name: modification-tolerant-spectral-library-search
skills.search_text: modification-tolerant-spectral-library-search Use when query MS/MS spectra resemble but do not exactly match library spectra, and the goal is to detect putative analogs via mass shifts (e.g., the −41 Da stenothricin analog class consistent with a lysine-to-serine substitution). When the goal is an exact library identification (no expected analog mass shift) — use GNPS exact spectral library search instead, which is scored by normalized dot product without delta edges When query and library spectra should be related de novo without any reference spectra — use molecular networking instead When a strict FDR-validated identification is required — chemistry-level analog assignments from variable dereplication are subject to expert review http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 GNPS variable dereplication extends exact spectral library search by adding bipartite matching edges between library and query peaks that differ by the precursor mass difference delta ± the user-defined fragment mass tolerance, enabling detection of putative analogs of known compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3597
skills.summary: GNPS variable dereplication extends exact spectral library search by adding bipartite matching edges between library and query peaks that differ by the precursor mass difference delta ± the user-defined fragment mass tolerance, enabling detection of putative analogs of known compounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is an exact library identification (no expected analog mass shift) — use GNPS exact spectral library search instead, which is scored by normalized dot product without delta edges When query and library spectra should be related de novo without any reference spectra — use molecular networking instead When a strict FDR-validated identification is required — chemistry-level analog assignments from variable dereplication are subject to expert review

skills.description: Use when annotating natural-products MS/MS spectra against reference libraries or comparing spectra pairwise where modifications cause mass shifts: peaks differ by a consistent delta equal to the precursor mass difference.
skills.name: modification-tolerant-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: modification-tolerant-spectral-matching Use when annotating natural-products MS/MS spectra against reference libraries or comparing spectra pairwise where modifications cause mass shifts: peaks differ by a consistent delta equal to the precursor mass difference. When the query is expected to exactly match a library spectrum with no mass shift — the plain exact spectral search with a normalized dot product is sufficient and avoids delta-mismatched peak assignments When the goal is clustering raw spectra into consensus spectra (use MSCluster first) rather than scoring spectrum pairs When applying the mutual top-K edge-retention rule to build the final molecular network — this skill only produces candidate edges above the minimum match score http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 GNPS-style modification-tolerant matching of query/consensus MS/MS spectra against library spectra or each other, scoring with a normalized dot product computed via maximum bipartite peak matching, with edges added between peaks differing by the precursor mass difference delta plus/minus a user-defined fragment mass tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3597
skills.summary: GNPS-style modification-tolerant matching of query/consensus MS/MS spectra against library spectra or each other, scoring with a normalized dot product computed via maximum bipartite peak matching, with edges added between peaks differing by the precursor mass difference delta plus/minus a user-defined fragment mass tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query is expected to exactly match a library spectrum with no mass shift — the plain exact spectral search with a normalized dot product is sufficient and avoids delta-mismatched peak assignments When the goal is clustering raw spectra into consensus spectra (use MSCluster first) rather than scoring spectrum pairs When applying the mutual top-K edge-retention rule to build the final molecular network — this skill only produces candidate edges above the minimum match score

skills.description: Use when a molecular networking or dereplication job returns unannotated nodes whose spectra resemble a known compound library hit but whose precursor masses differ by a consistent delta, suggesting analogs or modifications.
skills.name: modification-tolerant-variable-dereplication
skills.search_text: modification-tolerant-variable-dereplication Use when a molecular networking or dereplication job returns unannotated nodes whose spectra resemble a known compound library hit but whose precursor masses differ by a consistent delta, suggesting analogs or modifications. A query spectrum is expected to match the library entry exactly (no modification) — use GNPS exact spectral library search with normalized dot product instead MS/MS spectra have MS1 precursor intensity <1E4 or precursor m/z ppm error >=50 relative to theoretical mass — these are ignored by the dereplication workflow The goal is de novo structural elucidation rather than annotation against existing reference libraries — variable dereplication only matches known library spectra plus a mass delta A GNPS dereplication mode that annotates MS/MS spectra against reference libraries while allowing a systematic mass shift, so that modified analogs (e.g., stenothricin analogs shifted by -41 Da) are flagged instead of left unannotated. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3597
skills.summary: A GNPS dereplication mode that annotates MS/MS spectra against reference libraries while allowing a systematic mass shift, so that modified analogs (e.g., stenothricin analogs shifted by -41 Da) are flagged instead of left unannotated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A query spectrum is expected to match the library entry exactly (no modification) — use GNPS exact spectral library search with normalized dot product instead MS/MS spectra have MS1 precursor intensity <1E4 or precursor m/z ppm error >=50 relative to theoretical mass — these are ignored by the dereplication workflow The goal is de novo structural elucidation rather than annotation against existing reference libraries — variable dereplication only matches known library spectra plus a mass delta

skills.description: Use when validating or re-implementing GNPS molecular networking edge scores: you have consensus .mgf spectra, precursor masses, and a GNPS edge table and must reproduce cosine_score per node pair.
skills.name: modified-cosine-fragment-ion-matching
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-fragment-ion-matching Use when validating or re-implementing GNPS molecular networking edge scores: you have consensus .mgf spectra, precursor masses, and a GNPS edge table and must reproduce cosine_score per node pair. The goal is library spectral matching / dereplication of a single spectrum against reference libraries, not pairwise consensus-vs-consensus edge scoring The input is already a feature abundance table (quantitative data) — classic molecular networking with modified cosine provides only qualitative information from MS2 scans, not calibrated quantitation Spectra were not pre-clustered into consensus spectra / nodes (e.g., raw per-scan MS2 without GNPS consensus clustering), since the score is defined on GNPS-style consensus spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs GNPS's modified cosine pairwise MS2 spectral alignment, in which fragment ions are matched both at identical m/z and at m/z shifts equal to the precursor ion mass difference, to independently verify the cosine_score edges of a GNPS molecular networking job. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-020-0317-5
skills.summary: Reconstructs GNPS's modified cosine pairwise MS2 spectral alignment, in which fragment ions are matched both at identical m/z and at m/z shifts equal to the precursor ion mass difference, to independently verify the cosine_score edges of a GNPS molecular networking job.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is library spectral matching / dereplication of a single spectrum against reference libraries, not pairwise consensus-vs-consensus edge scoring The input is already a feature abundance table (quantitative data) — classic molecular networking with modified cosine provides only qualitative information from MS2 scans, not calibrated quantitation Spectra were not pre-clustered into consensus spectra / nodes (e.g., raw per-scan MS2 without GNPS consensus clustering), since the score is defined on GNPS-style consensus spectra

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a learned spectral similarity score (e.g. Spec2Vec) against a classical peak-matching score, or when building molecular networks that account for neutral-loss shifts between fragment peaks of related molecules.
skills.name: modified-cosine-score-computation
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-score-computation Use when benchmarking a learned spectral similarity score (e.g. Spec2Vec) against a classical peak-matching score, or when building molecular networks that account for neutral-loss shifts between fragment peaks of related molecules. When a trained embedding model is available and the goal is structural-analogue search — Spec2Vec scores correlate better with structural similarity than cosine-based scores When peak shifts between compared spectra do not correspond to chemically meaningful neutral losses (plain cosine is then the simpler baseline) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes all-pairs modified cosine similarity scores between MS/MS spectra as a baseline spectral similarity measure, used in the Spec2Vec paper to benchmark embedding-based scoring for molecular networking clustering quality. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Computes all-pairs modified cosine similarity scores between MS/MS spectra as a baseline spectral similarity measure, used in the Spec2Vec paper to benchmark embedding-based scoring for molecular networking clustering quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a trained embedding model is available and the goal is structural-analogue search — Spec2Vec scores correlate better with structural similarity than cosine-based scores When peak shifts between compared spectra do not correspond to chemically meaningful neutral losses (plain cosine is then the simpler baseline)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking library-search throughput or computing modified cosine analogue matches between MS2 query spectra and a large GNPS library (~302,514 spectra) with precursor m/z preselection.
skills.name: modified-cosine-score-computation
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-score-computation Use when benchmarking library-search throughput or computing modified cosine analogue matches between MS2 query spectra and a large GNPS library (~302,514 spectra) with precursor m/z preselection. When search speed at library scale is the priority: the 100 Da precursor preselection plus modified cosine scoring took 9 h 24 min for 5987 spectra versus 1 h 14 min for MS2Query on the same laptop hardware When analogues beyond a 100 Da precursor m/z difference must be found, since this method's analogue search is defined by that preselection, whereas MS2Query performs no precursor m/z preselection http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes modified cosine scores between positive-mode MS2 query spectra and a GNPS spectral library using the matchms implementation, with a 100 Da precursor m/z preselection, serving as the classical analogue-search baseline in the MS2Query benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: Computes modified cosine scores between positive-mode MS2 query spectra and a GNPS spectral library using the matchms implementation, with a 100 Da precursor m/z preselection, serving as the classical analogue-search baseline in the MS2Query benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When search speed at library scale is the priority: the 100 Da precursor preselection plus modified cosine scoring took 9 h 24 min for 5987 spectra versus 1 h 14 min for MS2Query on the same laptop hardware When analogues beyond a 100 Da precursor m/z difference must be found, since this method's analogue search is defined by that preselection, whereas MS2Query performs no precursor m/z preselection

skills.description: Use when comparing spectral similarity measures on annotated MS/MS data (e.g. a 3601-spectrum test set of 500 unique InChIKey compounds from GNPS) to quantify which measure retrieves high-Tanimoto (Tanimoto > 0.6) compound pairs via precision/recall curves.
skills.name: modified-cosine-similarity-comparison
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-similarity-comparison Use when comparing spectral similarity measures on annotated MS/MS data (e.g. a 3601-spectrum test set of 500 unique InChIKey compounds from GNPS) to quantify which measure retrieves high-Tanimoto (Tanimoto > 0.6) compound pairs via precision/recall curves. The spectra lack InChIKey/SMILES annotations, so no RDKit fingerprint ground-truth Tanimoto similarities can be computed for labelling positive pairs The goal is compound identification (near-complete chemical match) rather than retrieval of chemically related pairs — the paper notes it is difficult to discriminate Tanimoto 0.8–0.9 from a near-complete chemical match Applying MS2DeepScore scores trained on GNPS library biases to experimental data from compound classes poorly represented in spectral libraries Benchmark spectral similarity measures (MS2DeepScore, modified Cosine, Spec2Vec) by their ability to retrieve chemically related MS/MS spectrum pairs, using RDKit-derived Tanimoto similarity > 0.6 as ground truth over a swept score threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Benchmark spectral similarity measures (MS2DeepScore, modified Cosine, Spec2Vec) by their ability to retrieve chemically related MS/MS spectrum pairs, using RDKit-derived Tanimoto similarity > 0.6 as ground truth over a swept score threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra lack InChIKey/SMILES annotations, so no RDKit fingerprint ground-truth Tanimoto similarities can be computed for labelling positive pairs The goal is compound identification (near-complete chemical match) rather than retrieval of chemically related pairs — the paper notes it is difficult to discriminate Tanimoto 0.8–0.9 from a near-complete chemical match Applying MS2DeepScore scores trained on GNPS library biases to experimental data from compound classes poorly represented in spectral libraries

skills.description: Use when you have pseudo MS/MS spectra (MGF) derived from MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data and need a molecular network whose edges link features by modified cosine similarity, enabling annotation propagation across related metabolites.
skills.name: modified-cosine-similarity-networking
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-similarity-networking Use when you have pseudo MS/MS spectra (MGF) derived from MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data and need a molecular network whose edges link features by modified cosine similarity, enabling annotation propagation across related metabolites. Input is real acquired MS/MS data rather than pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only full-scan files — standard GNPS networking without the ion-cleaning step is the appropriate path. The goal is single-feature library annotation rather than network construction — use ms1-id's reverse spectral matching directly (min_score 0.7, min_matched_peak 3) instead of networking. Peaks above the precursor m/z cannot be removed (e.g. multimer/adduct ions must be retained), since modified cosine calculations will not be possible on the uncleaned spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds molecular networks from pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra generated by ms1-id by submitting cleaned MGF files to GNPS2 classical molecular networking, where edges are formed under modified cosine similarity so that structurally related metabolites (e.g. N-acyl amides) cluster into biologically coherent subnetworks with propagated annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Builds molecular networks from pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra generated by ms1-id by submitting cleaned MGF files to GNPS2 classical molecular networking, where edges are formed under modified cosine similarity so that structurally related metabolites (e.g. N-acyl amides) cluster into biologically coherent subnetworks with propagated annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real acquired MS/MS data rather than pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only full-scan files — standard GNPS networking without the ion-cleaning step is the appropriate path. The goal is single-feature library annotation rather than network construction — use ms1-id's reverse spectral matching directly (min_score 0.7, min_matched_peak 3) instead of networking. Peaks above the precursor m/z cannot be removed (e.g. multimer/adduct ions must be retained), since modified cosine calculations will not be possible on the uncleaned spectra.

skills.description: Use when propagating MS/MS library annotations (e.g., drugs and their metabolites/analogs from the GNPS Drug Library) into untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics datasets, where peaks may have different precursor m/z than the reference but share fragment and neutral-loss structure.
skills.name: modified-cosine-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-spectral-matching Use when propagating MS/MS library annotations (e.g., drugs and their metabolites/analogs from the GNPS Drug Library) into untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics datasets, where peaks may have different precursor m/z than the reference but share fragment and neutral-loss structure. When spectra are expected to share an identical precursor m/z and full fragment pattern (e.g., direct library identification rather than analog/metabolite propagation) — plain cosine scoring suffices and modified cosine's mass-shift tolerance is unnecessary. When the reference library does not contain pharmacologic metadata needed to propagate a meaningful annotation (e.g., a drug library lacking drug class or indication fields), as matches cannot be interpreted beyond spectral identity. When input spectra are not LC-MS/MS fragmentation data (e.g., GC-EI-MS or MS1-only data), as the modified cosine score depends on paired MS/MS fragment ion lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Alignment of MS/MS reference spectra against untargeted metabolomics peaks using modified cosine scoring (accounting for neutral-loss differences between precursor masses) to propagate drug metabolite and analog annotations from a curated drug spectral library into public datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5
skills.summary: Alignment of MS/MS reference spectra against untargeted metabolomics peaks using modified cosine scoring (accounting for neutral-loss differences between precursor masses) to propagate drug metabolite and analog annotations from a curated drug spectral library into public datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When spectra are expected to share an identical precursor m/z and full fragment pattern (e.g., direct library identification rather than analog/metabolite propagation) — plain cosine scoring suffices and modified cosine's mass-shift tolerance is unnecessary. When the reference library does not contain pharmacologic metadata needed to propagate a meaningful annotation (e.g., a drug library lacking drug class or indication fields), as matches cannot be interpreted beyond spectral identity. When input spectra are not LC-MS/MS fragmentation data (e.g., GC-EI-MS or MS1-only data), as the modified cosine score depends on paired MS/MS fragment ion lists.

skills.description: Use when LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data include MS/MS peak lists and the goal is to group features that are structurally similar before feature group-wise statistical testing in msFeaST.
skills.name: modified-cosine-spectral-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: modified-cosine-spectral-similarity-scoring Use when LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data include MS/MS peak lists and the goal is to group features that are structurally similar before feature group-wise statistical testing in msFeaST. The dataset lacks MS/MS fragment spectra (only MS1 feature tables are available), so no spectral similarity can be computed. You already have a structurally informed feature grouping (e.g. from molecular networking or annotation) and only need statistical testing — globaltest can be run on that grouping directly without re-scoring spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute pairwise modified-cosine spectral similarity scores between LC-MS/MS features so that structurally similar metabolites can be grouped (via k-medoids) and statistically tested with globaltest in the msFeaST pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae584
skills.summary: Compute pairwise modified-cosine spectral similarity scores between LC-MS/MS features so that structurally similar metabolites can be grouped (via k-medoids) and statistically tested with globaltest in the msFeaST pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks MS/MS fragment spectra (only MS1 feature tables are available), so no spectral similarity can be computed. You already have a structurally informed feature grouping (e.g. from molecular networking or annotation) and only need statistical testing — globaltest can be run on that grouping directly without re-scoring spectra.

skills.description: Use when annotating MS/MS spectra of suspected modified metabolites that fail exact library matching, and you need to associate them with parent-compound library entries via mass-shift-consistent fragment correspondences (NIST17 hybrid search logic).
skills.name: modified-metabolite-fragmentation-pattern-analysis
skills.search_text: modified-metabolite-fragmentation-pattern-analysis Use when annotating MS/MS spectra of suspected modified metabolites that fail exact library matching, and you need to associate them with parent-compound library entries via mass-shift-consistent fragment correspondences (NIST17 hybrid search logic). Spectra already identified at MSI level 1 or 2 with exact precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching against authentic standards — direct library matching, not hybrid search, is appropriate. Compounds lacking any related library entry or suspected parent (e.g., fully novel structures) — use in silico fragmentation (CSI:FingerID/SIRIUS) instead, as the hybrid search requires a parent library spectrum for head-to-tail comparison. MS1-only signals that did not trigger MS/MS fragmentation — no fragment shifts can be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs the NIST hybrid search mechanism by comparing MS/MS spectra of chemically modified metabolites (methylated, acetylated, phosphorylated, hydroxylated forms) against library spectra of their non-modified parents, using precursor and fragment mass shifts to link modified compounds to their best-scoring related library entries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Reconstructs the NIST hybrid search mechanism by comparing MS/MS spectra of chemically modified metabolites (methylated, acetylated, phosphorylated, hydroxylated forms) against library spectra of their non-modified parents, using precursor and fragment mass shifts to link modified compounds to their best-scoring related library entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra already identified at MSI level 1 or 2 with exact precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching against authentic standards — direct library matching, not hybrid search, is appropriate. Compounds lacking any related library entry or suspected parent (e.g., fully novel structures) — use in silico fragmentation (CSI:FingerID/SIRIUS) instead, as the hybrid search requires a parent library spectrum for head-to-tail comparison. MS1-only signals that did not trigger MS/MS fragmentation — no fragment shifts can be computed.

Only single-omics data are available — use BiomiX's single-omics pipelines (DESeq2/Limma, ChAMP, TidyMass/Wilcoxon) instead of MOFA integration The goal is supervised prediction of class labels rather than latent-factor exploration — MOFA is a middle-integration, unsupervised factor model Proteomics or genomics data are the primary inputs — BiomiX does not yet support these omics types http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (MOFA) via BiomiX to integrate omics matrices (e.g. transcriptomics, methylomics, metabolomics), tune the total number of factors, identify cohort-discriminant factors, and interpret them through clinical correlation, EnrichR/GSEA pathway analysis, and PubMed bibliography mining. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y

This underpins isotopologue deconvolution for single- and multi-tracer (13C, 18O) SIRM MS data.

skills.description: Use when preparing Mol2CCS input records: you have SMILES and an adduct label per measurement and must build the additional 1-D feature vectors (fingerprints, descriptors, encodings) the model consumes alongside the graph.
skills.name: mol2ccs-feature-vector-construction
skills.search_text: mol2ccs-feature-vector-construction Use when preparing Mol2CCS input records: you have SMILES and an adduct label per measurement and must build the additional 1-D feature vectors (fingerprints, descriptors, encodings) the model consumes alongside the graph. You are training SigmaCCS or GraphCCS directly from SMILES and adduct only — those models consume the graph (node/adjacency/edge feature matrices from 3D conformers) rather than the concatenated 1-D feature vector. The input is already a formatted Mol2CCS parquet produced by the data_processing notebooks — re-extracting features would duplicate work; instead go straight to the training split or prediction step. Your molecules have no valid SMILES representation (RDKit cannot parse them) — fingerprint and descriptor extraction will fail before the graph is built. http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Construction of the seven one-dimensional feature vectors Mol2CCS appends to the molecular graph representation for CCS prediction, combining Morgan fingerprints, molecular weight, Drug Tax class counts, adduct/instrument one-hot encodings, and monomer/dimer flags, written as a parquet feature matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Construction of the seven one-dimensional feature vectors Mol2CCS appends to the molecular graph representation for CCS prediction, combining Morgan fingerprints, molecular weight, Drug Tax class counts, adduct/instrument one-hot encodings, and monomer/dimer flags, written as a parquet feature matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are training SigmaCCS or GraphCCS directly from SMILES and adduct only — those models consume the graph (node/adjacency/edge feature matrices from 3D conformers) rather than the concatenated 1-D feature vector. skills.description: Use when cleaning an annotated MS/MS library where stored parent masses are systematically offset from the monoisotopic mass implied by the SMILES/InChI annotation, a common annotation error in public libraries.
skills.name: molar-vs-monoisotopic-mass-correction
skills.search_text: molar-vs-monoisotopic-mass-correction Use when cleaning an annotated MS/MS library where stored parent masses are systematically offset from the monoisotopic mass implied by the SMILES/InChI annotation, a common annotation error in public libraries. The spectrum is unannotated or lacks SMILES/InChI/InChIKey, so there is no structure from which a monoisotopic mass can be recomputed. The parent mass is already monoisotopic and consistent with the annotation — no correction is warranted, and the spectrum should instead be routed to other filters (e.g. adduct/precursor or annotation-match repair). A matchms metadata-repair filter that detects and corrects spectra whose stored parent mass was computed from the average molar mass instead of the monoisotopic mass, recomputing it from the annotated structure so the spectrum can be retained and further validated rather than discarded. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: A matchms metadata-repair filter that detects and corrects spectra whose stored parent mass was computed from the average molar mass instead of the monoisotopic mass, recomputing it from the annotated structure so the spectrum can be retained and further validated rather than discarded.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum is unannotated or lacks SMILES/InChI/InChIKey, so there is no structure from which a monoisotopic mass can be recomputed. The parent mass is already monoisotopic and consistent with the annotation — no correction is warranted, and the spectrum should instead be routed to other filters (e.g. adduct/precursor or annotation-match repair).

skills.description: Use when a chemical formula (heavy-atom composition) is known and a molecular graph must be generated conditionally from a latent structural signal such as a spectrum embedding or 4,096-bit Morgan fingerprint.
skills.name: molecular-adjacency-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: molecular-adjacency-matrix-generation Use when a chemical formula (heavy-atom composition) is known and a molecular graph must be generated conditionally from a latent structural signal such as a spectrum embedding or 4,096-bit Morgan fingerprint. The chemical formula is unknown or unreliable — the pipeline takes the formula as given and cannot recover node counts/types; use formula-inference tools (SIRIUS, BUDDY, MIST-CF) first. The task is unconditional molecule generation or graph sizes exceed ~100-200 nodes, where the dense Graph Transformer diffusion formulation becomes impractical. The goal is property regression or spectrum fingerprint prediction rather than generating a molecular structure graph. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generate a molecular adjacency matrix (bond-type graph) via discrete denoising diffusion conditioned on a fixed heavy-atom composition and a structural condition (spectrum embedding or molecular fingerprint), following the DiGress formulation as adapted by DiffMS. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Generate a molecular adjacency matrix (bond-type graph) via discrete denoising diffusion conditioned on a fixed heavy-atom composition and a structural condition (spectrum embedding or molecular fingerprint), following the DiGress formulation as adapted by DiffMS.

The task is unconditional molecule generation or graph sizes exceed ~100-200 nodes, where the dense Graph Transformer diffusion formulation becomes impractical. The goal is property regression or spectrum fingerprint prediction rather than generating a molecular structure graph.

skills.description: Use when untargeted metabolomics MS/MS spectra (reference or experimental) must be grouped into molecular communities and conventional threshold-based molecular networking risks fracturing natural metabolite families.
skills.name: molecular-community-detection
skills.search_text: molecular-community-detection Use when untargeted metabolomics MS/MS spectra (reference or experimental) must be grouped into molecular communities and conventional threshold-based molecular networking risks fracturing natural metabolite families. When a conventional fixed-threshold molecular network is explicitly required for comparability — MCN's per-metabolite connectivity optimization will merge or rescue connections that a single arbitrary similarity threshold would exclude. When the input is already a feature table or annotated metabolite list rather than spectra from which pairwise spectral similarity can be computed. When a quantitative structural-annotation result is needed — the reference-set validation here is a qualitative correspondence check of clusters against structural classes, not per-molecule identification. Molecular community networking (MCN) groups MS/MS spectra into molecular communities by optimizing connectivity for each metabolite individually, instead of cutting a spectral-similarity network at a single arbitrary threshold. This rescues metabolite relationships that fixed-threshold molecular networking fractures, as validated on a reference spectra library (Figures 1g-i, S2-11). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Molecular community networking (MCN) groups MS/MS spectra into molecular communities by optimizing connectivity for each metabolite individually, instead of cutting a spectral-similarity network at a single arbitrary threshold. This rescues metabolite relationships that fixed-threshold molecular networking fractures, as validated on a reference spectra library (Figures 1g-i, S2-11).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a conventional fixed-threshold molecular network is explicitly required for comparability — MCN's per-metabolite connectivity optimization will merge or rescue connections that a single arbitrary similarity threshold would exclude. When the input is already a feature table or annotated metabolite list rather than spectra from which pairwise spectral similarity can be computed. When a quantitative structural-annotation result is needed — the reference-set validation here is a qualitative correspondence check of clusters against structural classes, not per-molecule identification.

skills.description: Use when analyzing untargeted metabolomics MS/MS spectra where cosine-threshold molecular networks fracture metabolite families, and you want community structure (e.g. community assignments for every node) to emerge from modularity optimization on the unpruned similarity network.
skills.name: molecular-community-networking
skills.search_text: molecular-community-networking Use when analyzing untargeted metabolomics MS/MS spectra where cosine-threshold molecular networks fracture metabolite families, and you want community structure (e.g. community assignments for every node) to emerge from modularity optimization on the unpruned similarity network. When a predefined number or size of metabolite communities is required — MCN specifically lets the Louvain modularity optimization determine community structure rather than fixing it. When the goal is a conventional cosine-threshold molecular network (e.g. cosine similarity > 0.7 edges only) — pruning is exactly what MCN avoids, as it can fracture natural metabolite families. When the input is already a pruned/thresholded molecular network with most edges removed — running Louvain on the pruned graph would not recover the full-connectivity structure MCN relies on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Molecular community networking (MCN) partitions untargeted metabolomics MS/MS similarity networks by optimizing connectivity for each metabolite via modularity-based community detection (Louvain) on the full-connectivity network, instead of pruning edges with an arbitrary cosine-similarity threshold. It rescues 'hidden' metabolite relationships that conventional molecular networking loses, as demonstrated by the discovery of novel dipeptide-conjugated bile acids linked to Bifidobacterium. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Molecular community networking (MCN) partitions untargeted metabolomics MS/MS similarity networks by optimizing connectivity for each metabolite via modularity-based community detection (Louvain) on the full-connectivity network, instead of pruning edges with an arbitrary cosine-similarity threshold. It rescues 'hidden' metabolite relationships that conventional molecular networking loses, as demonstrated by the discovery of novel dipeptide-conjugated bile acids linked to Bifidobacterium.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a predefined number or size of metabolite communities is required — MCN specifically lets the Louvain modularity optimization determine community structure rather than fixing it. When the goal is a conventional cosine-threshold molecular network (e.g. cosine similarity > 0.7 edges only) — pruning is exactly what MCN avoids, as it can fracture natural metabolite families. When the input is already a pruned/thresholded molecular network with most edges removed — running Louvain on the pruned graph would not recover the full-connectivity structure MCN relies on.

skills.search_text: molecular-conformer-geometry-feature-extraction Use when 3D molecular conformations (e.g. [max_atom_num, 21] arrays of xyz + 18 one-hot atom features with a covalent bond graph) must be turned into pose-independent encoder inputs, or when verifying E(3)/SE(3) invariance of a molecular geometry layer. skills.summary: Extracts pose-independent geometric features from 3D molecular conformations using the 3DMolMS MolConv elemental operation, which aggregates k-nearest-neighbor distances and inner-product angle terms over relative displacements rather than absolute coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input molecules have no 3D conformations and only 2D structures are available (generate ETKDGv3 conformers first, e.g. via molecules_to_records, or the geometry channels are undefined). skills.description: Use when you need to convert molecular structures from a training or target set into a large numerical descriptor matrix (e.g. 1613 Mordred descriptors) before feature selection and machine learning regression.
skills.name: molecular-descriptor-computation
skills.search_text: molecular-descriptor-computation Use when you need to convert molecular structures from a training or target set into a large numerical descriptor matrix (e.g. 1613 Mordred descriptors) before feature selection and machine learning regression. You already have a final feature table or curated descriptor set — recomputing all 1613 Mordred descriptors is unnecessary. You need CCS predictions for dimers such as [2 M + H]+ or [2 M − H]−, or other less common adducts or in-source fragments — current training sets and their descriptor pipeline do not support these. You lack structures for the target compounds — Mordred descriptors cannot be computed without molecular input structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Compute the 1613-entry Mordred molecular descriptor library from compound structures to serve as regression features for machine learning models such as CCSP 2.0's linear-kernel SVR CCS predictors. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c03491
skills.summary: Compute the 1613-entry Mordred molecular descriptor library from compound structures to serve as regression features for machine learning models such as CCSP 2.0's linear-kernel SVR CCS predictors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a final feature table or curated descriptor set — recomputing all 1613 Mordred descriptors is unnecessary. You need CCS predictions for dimers such as [2 M + H]+ or [2 M − H]−, or other less common adducts or in-source fragments — current training sets and their descriptor pipeline do not support these. You lack structures for the target compounds — Mordred descriptors cannot be computed without molecular input structures.
