skills.search_text: molecular-diagram-clash-resolution Use when rendering spaghetti diagrams of modular PKS/NRPS clusters whose bonds or labels overlap, or when reproducing RAIChU's drawing engine layout rules for vertically aligned backbones in SVG output. The task is structure or product prediction rather than visualisation — use antiSMASH/PRISM prediction or PIKAChU chemical-correctness checking instead The target is non-modular chemistry (e.g. RiPP or terpene tailoring pathways) where the modular vertical-backbone spaghetti layout rules do not directly apply The diagram is for a summarized pathway view (initial and final intermediates only), which uses a different simplified representation http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Applies RAIChU's clash-resolution finetuning to spaghetti-diagram layouts of modular PKS/NRPS biosynthetic gene clusters, removing overlaps by constraining central-chain bond angles to alternating 60/-60 degrees, cyclic bonds to 90 degrees, and side-chain bonds to 0/180 degrees so diagrams meet the paper's readability criteria. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00898-x
skills.summary: Applies RAIChU's clash-resolution finetuning to spaghetti-diagram layouts of modular PKS/NRPS biosynthetic gene clusters, removing overlaps by constraining central-chain bond angles to alternating 60/-60 degrees, cyclic bonds to 90 degrees, and side-chain bonds to 0/180 degrees so diagrams meet the paper's readability criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is structure or product prediction rather than visualisation — use antiSMASH/PRISM prediction or PIKAChU chemical-correctness checking instead The target is non-modular chemistry (e.g. RiPP or terpene tailoring pathways) where the modular vertical-backbone spaghetti layout rules do not directly apply The diagram is for a summarized pathway view (initial and final intermediates only), which uses a different simplified representation

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-trained ROASMI checkpoint and a new user-defined retention reference set, and need to retrain the model and evaluate how far its rank-score gains transfer to new chemical and chromatographic spaces.
skills.name: molecular-embedding-finetuning
skills.search_text: molecular-embedding-finetuning Use when you have a pre-trained ROASMI checkpoint and a new user-defined retention reference set, and need to retrain the model and evaluate how far its rank-score gains transfer to new chemical and chromatographic spaces. The candidate molecules fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S or lie in a chemical space far from the retraining reference set — ChemSS is low and gains will be negligible. The chromatographic system is HILIC or otherwise outside the RPLC/pH ~2.7 space the initial models were trained for, with no matching user-defined reference set available. You only need retention scores from the existing pre-trained ensemble without adapting to a new reference set — the base prediction workflow (ROASMI_predict.py alone) suffices. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fine-tune the pre-trained ROASMI model's D-MPNN molecular embedding module and RankNet retention prediction module using a user-defined retraining reference set, and quantify rank-score improvement transferability via chemical-space (ChemSS) and chromatographic-space (ChrSS) similarity between reference and prediction sets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Fine-tune the pre-trained ROASMI model's D-MPNN molecular embedding module and RankNet retention prediction module using a user-defined retraining reference set, and quantify rank-score improvement transferability via chemical-space (ChemSS) and chromatographic-space (ChrSS) similarity between reference and prediction sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate molecules fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S or lie in a chemical space far from the retraining reference set — ChemSS is low and gains will be negligible. The chromatographic system is HILIC or otherwise outside the RPLC/pH ~2.7 space the initial models were trained for, with no matching user-defined reference set available. You only need retention scores from the existing pre-trained ensemble without adapting to a new reference set — the base prediction workflow (ROASMI_predict.py alone) suffices.

skills.description: Use when you have MSP-format MS/MS spectra (positive or negative ionization) and need to convert them into molecular embeddings to rank candidate structures, e.g. for metabolite identification or annotation of unannotated spectra.
skills.name: molecular-embedding-prediction
skills.search_text: molecular-embedding-prediction Use when you have MSP-format MS/MS spectra (positive or negative ionization) and need to convert them into molecular embeddings to rank candidate structures, e.g. for metabolite identification or annotation of unannotated spectra. Your target compounds may lie outside the 520,083-compound reference database — ChemEmbed cannot identify structures absent from it regardless of spectral quality You need to compare results against a differently sized reference database — results obtained with a smaller or larger reference are not directly comparable You have raw mzML/centroided profile data rather than MSP peak lists — ChemEmbed's preprocessing expects MSP files converted to structured DataFrames http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs ChemEmbed's pre-trained CNN to predict 300-dimensional Mol2vec embeddings from enhanced (merged, neutral-loss-enriched) MS/MS spectra and ranks candidate metabolites by cosine similarity against a 520,083-compound reference database. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Runs ChemEmbed's pre-trained CNN to predict 300-dimensional Mol2vec embeddings from enhanced (merged, neutral-loss-enriched) MS/MS spectra and ranks candidate metabolites by cosine similarity against a 520,083-compound reference database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your target compounds may lie outside the 520,083-compound reference database — ChemEmbed cannot identify structures absent from it regardless of spectral quality You need to compare results against a differently sized reference database — results obtained with a smaller or larger reference are not directly comparable You have raw mzML/centroided profile data rather than MSP peak lists — ChemEmbed's preprocessing expects MSP files converted to structured DataFrames

skills.description: Use when you have GNPS molecular-family groupings of (possibly unknown) metabolites and want to identify whole MFs significantly changing (e.g. p<=0.05, >=10 molecules) between defined case/control sample groups.
skills.name: molecular-family-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: molecular-family-activity-scoring Use when you have GNPS molecular-family groupings of (possibly unknown) metabolites and want to identify whole MFs significantly changing (e.g. p<=0.05, >=10 molecules) between defined case/control sample groups. Your peaks have database annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) and you want pathway-level rather than fragmentation-grouped analysis — use the standard Reactome/KEGG pathway mode of PALS instead Your data has no defined case/control comparison (e.g. only one experimental group) — PLAGE scoring in PALS is defined in terms of a case vs control design You need per-molecule differential analysis rather than activity levels of grouped metabolite sets — MF scoring ranks sets, not individual features Ranks GNPS Molecular Families (MFs) — groups of metabolites sharing fragmentation patterns — by their differential activity between case and control groups using the PLAGE decomposition implemented in PALS, yielding p-values per molecular family instead of per individual peak. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Ranks GNPS Molecular Families (MFs) — groups of metabolites sharing fragmentation patterns — by their differential activity between case and control groups using the PLAGE decomposition implemented in PALS, yielding p-values per molecular family instead of per individual peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your peaks have database annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) and you want pathway-level rather than fragmentation-grouped analysis — use the standard Reactome/KEGG pathway mode of PALS instead Your data has no defined case/control comparison (e.g. only one experimental group) — PLAGE scoring in PALS is defined in terms of a case vs control design You need per-molecule differential analysis rather than activity levels of grouped metabolite sets — MF scoring ranks sets, not individual features

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS molecular network contains unannotated connected components whose members should be tied to known natural product classes via MIBiG reference accessions (e.g. BGC0001840, BGC0001878, BGC0001841) and strain-level co-occurrence.
skills.name: molecular-family-annotation-against-mibig
skills.search_text: molecular-family-annotation-against-mibig Use when an LC-MS/MS molecular network contains unannotated connected components whose members should be tied to known natural product classes via MIBiG reference accessions (e.g. BGC0001840, BGC0001878, BGC0001841) and strain-level co-occurrence. Input is already an annotated feature table with identified compounds — no spectral networking or MIBiG cross-referencing is needed The goal is de novo compound structure elucidation; this skill only relates mass features to known MIBiG reference BGCs and flags putative analogues Only a single strain or no strain-level replicate data is available, since correlatable GCFs required representatives in two or more strains http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates molecular families from LC-MS/MS molecular networking by linking uncharacterized mass features to known biosynthetic gene clusters via MIBiG reference compounds and metabologenomic correlation, as demonstrated for the detoxin/rimosamide family in a 363-strain actinomycete study. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Annotates molecular families from LC-MS/MS molecular networking by linking uncharacterized mass features to known biosynthetic gene clusters via MIBiG reference compounds and metabologenomic correlation, as demonstrated for the detoxin/rimosamide family in a 363-strain actinomycete study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated feature table with identified compounds — no spectral networking or MIBiG cross-referencing is needed The goal is de novo compound structure elucidation; this skill only relates mass features to known MIBiG reference BGCs and flags putative analogues Only a single strain or no strain-level replicate data is available, since correlatable GCFs required representatives in two or more strains

skills.description: Use when a feature quantification table plus MGF MS/MS spectra must be grouped into molecular families (e.g. GNPS FBMN) and scored per phenotype to identify differentially enriched, annotated families.
skills.name: molecular-family-annotation-interpretation
skills.search_text: molecular-family-annotation-interpretation Use when a feature quantification table plus MGF MS/MS spectra must be grouped into molecular families (e.g. GNPS FBMN) and scored per phenotype to identify differentially enriched, annotated families. The input is gene cluster abundance/expression data from metagenomes or metatranscriptomes rather than metabolomics feature tables — use BiG-MAP's abundance/expression profiling modules instead. Only a feature table is available without MS/MS fragmentation spectra (no MGF), so molecular families cannot be built by fragmentation similarity. Molecular families have already been clustered and activity-scored and only a phenotype-annotation narrative is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Clusters metabolomics features into molecular families from MS/MS fragmentation similarity and interprets which families are enriched in a phenotype, connecting metabolite-level signals (e.g. (poly)acrolein-like fragmentation) to gene-cluster-level findings such as reuterin MGC enrichment. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21
skills.summary: Clusters metabolomics features into molecular families from MS/MS fragmentation similarity and interprets which families are enriched in a phenotype, connecting metabolite-level signals (e.g. (poly)acrolein-like fragmentation) to gene-cluster-level findings such as reuterin MGC enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is gene cluster abundance/expression data from metagenomes or metatranscriptomes rather than metabolomics feature tables — use BiG-MAP's abundance/expression profiling modules instead. Only a feature table is available without MS/MS fragmentation spectra (no MGF), so molecular families cannot be built by fragmentation similarity. Molecular families have already been clustered and activity-scored and only a phenotype-annotation narrative is required.

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking spectra.mgf file and molecular_families.tsv are available and per-spectrum CANOPUS ClassyFire/NPClassifier predictions must be aggregated into MF-level class annotations for NPClassScore linking.
skills.name: molecular-family-class-aggregation
skills.search_text: molecular-family-class-aggregation Use when a GNPS molecular networking spectra.mgf file and molecular_families.tsv are available and per-spectrum CANOPUS ClassyFire/NPClassifier predictions must be aggregated into MF-level class annotations for NPClassScore linking. Spectra or metabolites above 850 Da — CANOPUS is only applied with --maxmz 850 because fragmentation tree calculation becomes too time-consuming; larger metabolites are better handled by methods like Spec2Vec or MS2DeepScore When network-level class propagation is required via MolNetEnhancer — this cannot be run within NPLinker and must be run externally, e.g. on the GNPS platform When the goal is BGC-side (genome-based) class assignment rather than structure-based metabolite classes — that uses MIBiG-derived classifications instead of CANOPUS predictions Pools per-spectrum CANOPUS-predicted ClassyFire and NPClassifier chemical classes (super-, class-, and subclass-level) into molecular family (MF)-level annotations within the NPLinker NPClassScore workflow, so that structure-based class information can be matched against BGC classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Pools per-spectrum CANOPUS-predicted ClassyFire and NPClassifier chemical classes (super-, class-, and subclass-level) into molecular family (MF)-level annotations within the NPLinker NPClassScore workflow, so that structure-based class information can be matched against BGC classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra or metabolites above 850 Da — CANOPUS is only applied with --maxmz 850 because fragmentation tree calculation becomes too time-consuming; larger metabolites are better handled by methods like Spec2Vec or MS2DeepScore When network-level class propagation is required via MolNetEnhancer — this cannot be run within NPLinker and must be run externally, e.g. on the GNPS platform When the goal is BGC-side (genome-based) class assignment rather than structure-based metabolite classes — that uses MIBiG-derived classifications instead of CANOPUS predictions

skills.description: Use when peak intensity data from an untargeted metabolomics experiment must be ranked as grouped metabolite sets (Molecular Families, Mass2Motifs) by differential activity between experimental factors, e.g. Rhamnus vs Ziziphus.
skills.name: molecular-family-metabolite-set-analysis
skills.search_text: molecular-family-metabolite-set-analysis Use when peak intensity data from an untargeted metabolomics experiment must be ranked as grouped metabolite sets (Molecular Families, Mass2Motifs) by differential activity between experimental factors, e.g. Rhamnus vs Ziziphus. The task is single-peak differential testing rather than ranking metabolite sets as a whole Peaks cannot be assigned to any metabolite set (no Molecular Family/Mass2Motif grouping or compound annotations), since unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis The goal is Reactome pathway queries for transcriptomics/proteomics data (UniProt/ENSEMBL databases) rather than metabolite-set ranking from fragmentation-spectrum groupings http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Ranks user-defined metabolite sets — GNPS Molecular Families and MS2LDA Mass2Motifs — by activity level using the PALS PLAGE decomposition on LC-MS peak intensity matrices, e.g. detecting that flavonoid-related Mass2Motifs (rhamnocitrin, kaempferol, flavonoid core, emodin) are overrepresented in Rhamnus versus Ziziphus. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Ranks user-defined metabolite sets — GNPS Molecular Families and MS2LDA Mass2Motifs — by activity level using the PALS PLAGE decomposition on LC-MS peak intensity matrices, e.g. detecting that flavonoid-related Mass2Motifs (rhamnocitrin, kaempferol, flavonoid core, emodin) are overrepresented in Rhamnus versus Ziziphus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-peak differential testing rather than ranking metabolite sets as a whole Peaks cannot be assigned to any metabolite set (no Molecular Family/Mass2Motif grouping or compound annotations), since unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis The goal is Reactome pathway queries for transcriptomics/proteomics data (UniProt/ENSEMBL databases) rather than metabolite-set ranking from fragmentation-spectrum groupings

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS classical or feature-based molecular network plus MS2LDA Mass2Motifs and want to know which motifs dominate each molecular family.
skills.name: molecular-family-motif-mapping
skills.search_text: molecular-family-motif-mapping Use when you have a GNPS classical or feature-based molecular network plus MS2LDA Mass2Motifs and want to know which motifs dominate each molecular family. When the analysis goal is chemical class annotation (khipu/MetFrag ClassyFire output) rather than MS2LDA substructure motifs — use the ChemClasses_to_Network workflow instead. When molecular families are already fully structurally annotated (e.g. DEREPLICATOR output is sufficient) and no substructural diversity discovery is needed. When input data are not mass spectrometry fragmentation spectra in GNPS-clustered MGF format, since MS2LDA and the motif-mapping pipeline operate on that representation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Maps MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructural annotations onto GNPS molecular-network molecular families (network component indices) using pyMolNetEnhancer or RMolNetEnhancer, so each family can be inspected for shared substructures such as amino sugar motifs. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Maps MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructural annotations onto GNPS molecular-network molecular families (network component indices) using pyMolNetEnhancer or RMolNetEnhancer, so each family can be inspected for shared substructures such as amino sugar motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is chemical class annotation (khipu/MetFrag ClassyFire output) rather than MS2LDA substructure motifs — use the ChemClasses_to_Network workflow instead. When molecular families are already fully structurally annotated (e.g. DEREPLICATOR output is sufficient) and no substructural diversity discovery is needed. When input data are not mass spectrometry fragmentation spectra in GNPS-clustered MGF format, since MS2LDA and the motif-mapping pipeline operate on that representation.

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists (e.g., from a GNPS2/FBMN task's specs_ms.mgf, keyed by scan number) must be cleaned and reduced before computing a global multiple-spectrum alignment of a molecular family.
skills.name: molecular-family-spectra-preprocessing
skills.search_text: molecular-family-spectra-preprocessing Use when raw MS/MS peak lists (e.g., from a GNPS2/FBMN task's specs_ms.mgf, keyed by scan number) must be cleaned and reduced before computing a global multiple-spectrum alignment of a molecular family. Input is already a preprocessed or aligned peak-set JSON from the MMSA sets-creation step (preprocessing has already been applied) Goal is display-side analysis (custom spectrum ordering, m/z range filtering, top-10 intensity analysis, X-axis limits) rather than preparing spectra for alignment Analysis targets pairwise spectrum comparison or molecular network graph construction rather than multi-spectrum alignment within a family http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocess raw MS/MS peak sets from a molecular network component before MMSA spectral alignment: filter each spectrum to its top 6 most intense peaks within a ±25 m/z range, exclude peaks within ±17 m/z of the precursor ion, apply square-root intensity transformation, and normalize peak intensities so downstream consensus-peak alignment is not dominated by outliers or precursor-region peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Preprocess raw MS/MS peak sets from a molecular network component before MMSA spectral alignment: filter each spectrum to its top 6 most intense peaks within a ±25 m/z range, exclude peaks within ±17 m/z of the precursor ion, apply square-root intensity transformation, and normalize peak intensities so downstream consensus-peak alignment is not dominated by outliers or precursor-region peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed or aligned peak-set JSON from the MMSA sets-creation step (preprocessing has already been applied) Goal is display-side analysis (custom spectrum ordering, m/z range filtering, top-10 intensity analysis, X-axis limits) rather than preparing spectra for alignment Analysis targets pairwise spectrum comparison or molecular network graph construction rather than multi-spectrum alignment within a family

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular network family has mapped MS2LDA Mass2Motifs (e.g., xenoamicin ring A, putative ring B, peptidic tail motifs) and you must verify substructure-membership breakdown and >75% fragment consistency against DEREPLICATOR annotations.
skills.name: molecular-family-substructure-consistency-evaluation
skills.search_text: molecular-family-substructure-consistency-evaluation Use when a GNPS molecular network family has mapped MS2LDA Mass2Motifs (e.g., xenoamicin ring A, putative ring B, peptidic tail motifs) and you must verify substructure-membership breakdown and >75% fragment consistency against DEREPLICATOR annotations. The molecular family has no MS2LDA Mass2Motif assignments (only ClassyFire chemical-class annotation is desired — use chemical-class mapping instead of substructure-consistency evaluation) The network was not created through the GNPS platform (classical or feature-based workflow), so GNPS edge tables and MS2LDA job summaries cannot be matched You need novel substructure discovery rather than validation of already-annotated motifs — create a new LDA experiment on ms2lda.org instead of evaluating consistency Evaluates the consistency of MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructure assignments (e.g., ring and peptidic tail motifs) across all members of a molecular family in a GNPS molecular network, by verifying the motif-membership breakdown and cross-checking motif presence against in silico fragment annotations from DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Evaluates the consistency of MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructure assignments (e.g., ring and peptidic tail motifs) across all members of a molecular family in a GNPS molecular network, by verifying the motif-membership breakdown and cross-checking motif presence against in silico fragment annotations from DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecular family has no MS2LDA Mass2Motif assignments (only ClassyFire chemical-class annotation is desired — use chemical-class mapping instead of substructure-consistency evaluation) The network was not created through the GNPS platform (classical or feature-based workflow), so GNPS edge tables and MS2LDA job summaries cannot be matched You need novel substructure discovery rather than validation of already-annotated motifs — create a new LDA experiment on ms2lda.org instead of evaluating consistency

skills.description: Use when a bioassay-annotated feature quantification table (row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area, plus bioassay values per sample) exported from MZmine2/Optimus is available and each feature's abundance across fractions must be correlated with per-fraction bioassay results.
skills.name: molecular-feature-abundance-profiling-across-fractions
skills.search_text: molecular-feature-abundance-profiling-across-fractions Use when a bioassay-annotated feature quantification table (row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area, plus bioassay values per sample) exported from MZmine2/Optimus is available and each feature's abundance across fractions must be correlated with per-fraction bioassay results. The input is not yet a bioassay-annotated feature quantification table — Step 1 (MZmine2/Optimus processing with the required 'Export row ID', 'Export row m/z', 'Export row retention time', 'Peak area' CSV export and addition of bioassay values) must be completed first The analysis goal is the GNPS feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) job itself (Step 3) rather than computing per-feature bioactivity correlations There are too few bioassayed fractions to support meaningful Pearson correlation significance against the bioassay result vector http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Correlates the relative abundance profile of every LC-MS/MS-detected feature across bioassay-guided fractions with each fraction's bioassay result, using Pearson correlation and p-value significance computed in R inside the Bioactive Molecular Networks Jupyter notebook. This converts feature abundance patterns into bioactivity scores that can be mapped onto molecular networks. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.7b00737
skills.summary: Correlates the relative abundance profile of every LC-MS/MS-detected feature across bioassay-guided fractions with each fraction's bioassay result, using Pearson correlation and p-value significance computed in R inside the Bioactive Molecular Networks Jupyter notebook. This converts feature abundance patterns into bioactivity scores that can be mapped onto molecular networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not yet a bioassay-annotated feature quantification table — Step 1 (MZmine2/Optimus processing with the required 'Export row ID', 'Export row m/z', 'Export row retention time', 'Peak area' CSV export and addition of bioassay values) must be completed first The analysis goal is the GNPS feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) job itself (Step 3) rather than computing per-feature bioactivity correlations There are too few bioassayed fractions to support meaningful Pearson correlation significance against the bioassay result vector

skills.description: Use when a differentially abundant molecular feature from a mouse-model untargeted metabolomics study (e.g. a microbially-modulated carnitine in AD serum) needs to be matched to public human or animal metabolomics datasets to assess tissue, organism, and disease associations.
skills.name: molecular-feature-tracking-across-studies
skills.search_text: molecular-feature-tracking-across-studies Use when a differentially abundant molecular feature from a mouse-model untargeted metabolomics study (e.g. a microbially-modulated carnitine in AD serum) needs to be matched to public human or animal metabolomics datasets to assess tissue, organism, and disease associations. When the query feature already has a fully validated structural annotation from a reference library (Level 1 MSI annotation); tissueMASST complements rather than replaces library-based annotation. When the analysis goal is de novo structure elucidation of a completely unknown feature with no MS/MS fragmentation data; tissueMASST requires an MS/MS spectrum to search. When the feature is expected to be absent from public repositories because of study-specific extraction methods, workflows, or instrumentation; lack of detection in tissueMASST does not necessarily mean the feature is absent in tissue. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Bridges animal-model metabolomics findings to human data by searching known or unknown MS/MS spectra (e.g. microbially-modulated carnitines like phenylacetyl-carnitine) against a reference database of public MS/MS files organized by tissue, organism, and disease metadata via the tissueMASST search tool. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Bridges animal-model metabolomics findings to human data by searching known or unknown MS/MS spectra (e.g. microbially-modulated carnitines like phenylacetyl-carnitine) against a reference database of public MS/MS files organized by tissue, organism, and disease metadata via the tissueMASST search tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query feature already has a fully validated structural annotation from a reference library (Level 1 MSI annotation); tissueMASST complements rather than replaces library-based annotation. When the analysis goal is de novo structure elucidation of a completely unknown feature with no MS/MS fragmentation data; tissueMASST requires an MS/MS spectrum to search. When the feature is expected to be absent from public repositories because of study-specific extraction methods, workflows, or instrumentation; lack of detection in tissueMASST does not necessarily mean the feature is absent in tissue.

skills.description: Use when a new feature set for metabolite-protein interaction prediction (e.g., shadow prices) must be benchmarked against a molecular-structure baseline under identical classifier, sampling, and cross-validation settings.
skills.name: molecular-fingerprint-baseline-benchmarking
skills.search_text: molecular-fingerprint-baseline-benchmarking Use when a new feature set for metabolite-protein interaction prediction (e.g., shadow prices) must be benchmarked against a molecular-structure baseline under identical classifier, sampling, and cross-validation settings. The goal is standalone MPI prediction from structure only — this skill is a benchmark control, not the primary prediction method The comparison should isolate constraint-based (shadow price) information: using fingerprints alongside shadow prices as combined features would defeat the controlled comparison Gold standard metabolites lack structures retrievable via Bio.Entrez/PubChem, so 128-bit RDKit fingerprints cannot be generated http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Establishes a molecular-structure-only baseline for metabolite-protein interaction prediction by training the same random forest classifier on 128-bit RDKit fingerprints and comparing accuracy, AUC, and F1 against SARTRE's constraint-based shadow price features (e.g., on the Piazza E. coli gold standard). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad098
skills.summary: Establishes a molecular-structure-only baseline for metabolite-protein interaction prediction by training the same random forest classifier on 128-bit RDKit fingerprints and comparing accuracy, AUC, and F1 against SARTRE's constraint-based shadow price features (e.g., on the Piazza E. coli gold standard).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standalone MPI prediction from structure only — this skill is a benchmark control, not the primary prediction method The comparison should isolate constraint-based (shadow price) information: using fingerprints alongside shadow prices as combined features would defeat the controlled comparison Gold standard metabolites lack structures retrievable via Bio.Entrez/PubChem, so 128-bit RDKit fingerprints cannot be generated

skills.description: Use when an unidentified analyte's GC/EI-MS spectrum matches no known reference (NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG) and a structural representation must be derived from the spectrum alone to rank enumerated derivative candidates.
skills.name: molecular-fingerprint-bitvector-representation
skills.search_text: molecular-fingerprint-bitvector-representation Use when an unidentified analyte's GC/EI-MS spectrum matches no known reference (NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG) and a structural representation must be derived from the spectrum alone to rank enumerated derivative candidates. The analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectrum in the NIST, Wiley, or SWGDRUG libraries — conventional library screening suffices and the fingerprint prediction step is unnecessary. The chemical structure of the target compound is already known — in that case NEIMS-style spectrum prediction from structure (ECFP input) applies, not spectrum-to-fingerprint inference, since existing prediction methods 'are limited to cases where the chemical structure of NPS is already known.' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Convert an analyte's EI mass spectrum into its structural molecular fingerprint (binary 0/1 bit vector) using the DeepEI deep learning model, without needing to know the analyte's structure. This predicted fingerprint is the structural half of PS2MS's integrated SMSF similarity metric for ranking candidate NPS identities. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Convert an analyte's EI mass spectrum into its structural molecular fingerprint (binary 0/1 bit vector) using the DeepEI deep learning model, without needing to know the analyte's structure. This predicted fingerprint is the structural half of PS2MS's integrated SMSF similarity metric for ranking candidate NPS identities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte's mass spectrum already matches an established reference spectrum in the NIST, Wiley, or SWGDRUG libraries — conventional library screening suffices and the fingerprint prediction step is unnecessary. The chemical structure of the target compound is already known — in that case NEIMS-style spectrum prediction from structure (ECFP input) applies, not spectrum-to-fingerprint inference, since existing prediction methods 'are limited to cases where the chemical structure of NPS is already known.'

skills.description: Use when candidate compounds have been retrieved (e.g. via PubChem or MetaboQuest queries) and each candidate needs a fixed-length molecular fingerprint vector to compare with a predicted fingerprint.
skills.name: molecular-fingerprint-calculation-with-openbabel
skills.search_text: molecular-fingerprint-calculation-with-openbabel Use when candidate compounds have been retrieved (e.g. via PubChem or MetaboQuest queries) and each candidate needs a fixed-length molecular fingerprint vector to compare with a predicted fingerprint. Input data is not from the 3,965-compound evaluation dataset or lacks both SIRIUS version outputs, so the reported deltas (+26.6 pp, +6.3 pp) cannot be validated. Only a single SIRIUS setting (e.g. isotope pattern alone) is available, making the combined MS1+MS/MS comparison and wrong-formula reduction impossible to compute. Reproduces and verifies the SIRIUS 3.0 vs SIRIUS 4 molecular formula identification benchmark on the 3,965-compound evaluation dataset (Supplementary Fig. 6a / Supplementary Table 3), quantifying percentage-point gains in top-1 formula assignment and the drop in wrongly assigned formulas across isotope-pattern-only and MS1+MS/MS settings. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8

skills.description: Use when you have SIRIUS formula candidate scores (top ~50 per compound) for a whole LC-MS/MS sample and need de novo, database-independent formula reranking, especially for high-mass compounds (>500 Da).
skills.name: molecular-formula-gibbs-sampling
skills.search_text: molecular-formula-gibbs-sampling Use when you have SIRIUS formula candidate scores (top ~50 per compound) for a whole LC-MS/MS sample and need de novo, database-independent formula reranking, especially for high-mass compounds (>500 Da). Input lacks SIRIUS fragmentation tree candidates — ZODIAC builds upon SIRIUS and reranks its top candidates, so it cannot run de novo from raw spectra alone. Analyzing isolated single-compound spectra with no sample context — the network-based model's power comes from pairwise similarities across compounds in a dataset. Adduct information is needed but unreliable: deduce high-quality adduct annotations during preprocessing, since adducts cannot be reliably inferred from isotope pattern and MS/MS data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Rerank SIRIUS molecular formula candidates using ZODIAC's network-based Gibbs sampler, which combines fragmentation tree scores with Bayesian statistics over pairwise similarity potentials across compounds in an LC-MS/MS sample. This addresses SIRIUS 4's performance drop for compounds above 500 Da. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Rerank SIRIUS molecular formula candidates using ZODIAC's network-based Gibbs sampler, which combines fragmentation tree scores with Bayesian statistics over pairwise similarity potentials across compounds in an LC-MS/MS sample. This addresses SIRIUS 4's performance drop for compounds above 500 Da.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks SIRIUS fragmentation tree candidates — ZODIAC builds upon SIRIUS and reranks its top candidates, so it cannot run de novo from raw spectra alone. skills.search_text: molecular-formula-hill-notation-normalization Use when a list of de novo molecular formula annotations (e.g. from ZODIAC on LC-MS/MS data) must be checked against a structure database and formula strings may come in inconsistent element orderings. Input formulas are already guaranteed to be in Hill notation and only a database lookup is needed — normalization adds no value and risks transcription errors. skills.description: Use when a feature's formula annotation (e.g., a novel ZODIAC/SIRIUS formula like C24H47BrNO8P at m/z 588.230) needs independent confirmation from its MS1 isotope envelope, especially for halogen-containing formulas.
skills.name: molecular-formula-isotope-matching
skills.search_text: molecular-formula-isotope-matching Use when a feature's formula annotation (e.g., a novel ZODIAC/SIRIUS formula like C24H47BrNO8P at m/z 588.230) needs independent confirmation from its MS1 isotope envelope, especially for halogen-containing formulas. The input is already a numeric element-count or atom table — parsing formula strings again would be redundant. Peak lists are raw, un-annotated IDSL.IPA peaklists without molecular formula annotations — there is nothing to parse until UFA annotation runs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses molecular formula strings from an IDSL.UFA-annotated aligned peak table into per-element atom counts, enabling downstream formula-class detection such as ΔH/ΔC chain progressions and fixed-carbon halogenated classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00563

skills.summary: Aggregate per-sample molecular formula annotation lists from IDSL.UFA into an aligned annotated peak table using detection frequency and median rank statistics, then rank formula hits per peak (e.g. median rank ≤ 5, top rank ≤ 30) across individual samples in population-scale LC/HRMS studies.

skills.description: Use when features from an untargeted LC-MS/MS run have candidate formulas ranked by SIRIUS fragmentation trees but top-ranked candidates may be wrong due to interference, and before fingerprint prediction via CSI:FingerID.

When the dataset has very few features or no correlated MS/MS patterns — ZODIAC's joint re-scoring relies on cross-feature evidence and may not improve on SIRIUS-only rankings. When you only need a first-pass formula candidate and plan no downstream fingerprint prediction or tree-based analysis. skills.summary: Reranks candidate molecular formulas for MS/MS features using ZODIAC (SIRIUS 4), correcting SIRIUS per-feature fragmentation-tree scores by exploiting correlation of fragmentation patterns across features in the same dataset to select the most probable formula.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset has very few features or no correlated MS/MS patterns — ZODIAC's joint re-scoring relies on cross-feature evidence and may not improve on SIRIUS-only rankings. When you only need a first-pass formula candidate and plan no downstream fingerprint prediction or tree-based analysis. When you want per-feature structural class only from spectral library matches (ClassyFire) without molecular formula assignment.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input peaks have not been processed by IDSL.IPA (no per-sample peak lists or isotopic-profile peak properties) — IDSL.UFA requires IDSL.IPA chromatographic information as input MS2-only or DDA/DIA fragmentation data is the sole evidence source — this skill is an MS1-only isotopic profile matching approach The formula space needed exceeds the supplied IPDB (e.g. exhaustive enumeration across C, B, Br, Cl, K, S, Si, N, H, As, F, I, Na, O, P is required) — use IDSL.UFAx instead

skills.name: molecular-formula-subset-search
skills.search_text: molecular-formula-subset-search Use when assigning candidate molecular formulas to LC-MS/MS metabolite spectra (e.g., mzML from QTOF/ITFT/QFT/Orbitrap datasets) without spectral-library matches, or as a fast prescreening step before SIRIUS/Buddy-style identification. When accurate structural-level identification is required: FSA does not utilize structural information, so accuracy may not be competitive with state-of-the-art tools such as Buddy and SIRIUS When compounds contain elements beyond C, H, O, N, S, and P, or form diverse adduct types: FSA has so far been validated only on CHONSP-containing compounds When extensive chemical-rule filtering of formula candidates is essential: FSA implements only few chemical rules to rank or filter out unfeasible formulas http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Runs FSA (Formula Subset Analysis), a training-free MS/MS molecular formula ranking algorithm that scores candidate chemical formulas from fragment peaks without requiring MS/MS databases, achieving 85.28% rank-1 accuracy at 0.024 s per spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-025-02379-0
skills.summary: Runs FSA (Formula Subset Analysis), a training-free MS/MS molecular formula ranking algorithm that scores candidate chemical formulas from fragment peaks without requiring MS/MS databases, achieving 85.28% rank-1 accuracy at 0.024 s per spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When accurate structural-level identification is required: FSA does not utilize structural information, so accuracy may not be competitive with state-of-the-art tools such as Buddy and SIRIUS When compounds contain elements beyond C, H, O, N, S, and P, or form diverse adduct types: FSA has so far been validated only on CHONSP-containing compounds When extensive chemical-rule filtering of formula candidates is essential: FSA implements only few chemical rules to rank or filter out unfeasible formulas

skills.description: Use when a model outputs a probability distribution over molecular fragments (atom subsets or chemical subformulae) with known exact masses and you need to convert those into a final mass spectrum at 1 Da or 0.1 Da resolution.
skills.name: molecular-fragment-annotation
skills.search_text: molecular-fragment-annotation Use when a model outputs a probability distribution over molecular fragments (atom subsets or chemical subformulae) with known exact masses and you need to convert those into a final mass spectrum at 1 Da or 0.1 Da resolution. The target spectrum is already directly predicted peak-by-peak from a fingerprint or molecular structure (e.g. NEIMS-style direct regression) rather than via a fragment probability distribution The molecule contains atoms outside HCONFSPCl, has > 48 atoms (FormulaNet) or > 64 atoms (SubsetNet), or would yield > 4096 unique fragment formulae Collision-induced-dissociation MS2 or sub-Dalton high-resolution regimes where exotic fragmentation schemes ignored by this enumeration would dominate http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates the fragments underlying a predicted or observed EI mass spectrum by enumerating a molecule's vertex (atom) subsets and chemical subformulae — via recursive bond-breaking and hydrogen rearrangements — then weighting each fragment's exactly computed isotope-aware spectrum by the model's predicted probability and summing them into a final spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Annotates the fragments underlying a predicted or observed EI mass spectrum by enumerating a molecule's vertex (atom) subsets and chemical subformulae — via recursive bond-breaking and hydrogen rearrangements — then weighting each fragment's exactly computed isotope-aware spectrum by the model's predicted probability and summing them into a final spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target spectrum is already directly predicted peak-by-peak from a fingerprint or molecular structure (e.g. NEIMS-style direct regression) rather than via a fragment probability distribution The molecule contains atoms outside HCONFSPCl, has > 48 atoms (FormulaNet) or > 64 atoms (SubsetNet), or would yield > 4096 unique fragment formulae Collision-induced-dissociation MS2 or sub-Dalton high-resolution regimes where exotic fragmentation schemes ignored by this enumeration would dominate

skills.description: Use when raw natural-product structure tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz from LOTUS sources) contain salts, charged species or dimeric SMILES entries that must be reduced to single, neutral, parent molecules before structure deduplication or standardization to InChI.
skills.name: molecular-fragment-removal-and-uncharging
skills.search_text: molecular-fragment-removal-and-uncharging Use when raw natural-product structure tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz from LOTUS sources) contain salts, charged species or dimeric SMILES entries that must be reduced to single, neutral, parent molecules before structure deduplication or standardization to InChI. Input structures are already single-component neutral SMILES with no salts, charges, or dimers — applying MolVS sanitization can still degrade them ('correct salts, charged or dimeric molecules in the input data will suffer an unwanted sanitization step'), so skipping the step preserves fidelity. The goal is name-to-structure conversion of chemical names rather than cleaning existing SMILES; in LOTUS that is handled separately by translating names to InChI with OPSIN before/independent of sanitization. You need a broad alternative natural-product cleaning pipeline rather than the LOTUS three-stage MolVS approach; the article notes 'the current processing pipeline still removes a lot of correct entries and misses or induces some incorrect ones', so results are not interchangeable with other curation workflows. http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A chemical sanitization sub-step of the LOTUS processing pipeline in which SMILES-derived molecule objects are standardized, stripped of salts/fragments, and uncharged via the MolVS package before being written into the cleaned structure table with standardized InChI identifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: A chemical sanitization sub-step of the LOTUS processing pipeline in which SMILES-derived molecule objects are standardized, stripped of salts/fragments, and uncharged via the MolVS package before being written into the cleaned structure table with standardized InChI identifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input structures are already single-component neutral SMILES with no salts, charges, or dimers — applying MolVS sanitization can still degrade them ('correct salts, charged or dimeric molecules in the input data will suffer an unwanted sanitization step'), so skipping the step preserves fidelity. The goal is name-to-structure conversion of chemical names rather than cleaning existing SMILES; in LOTUS that is handled separately by translating names to InChI with OPSIN before/independent of sanitization. You need a broad alternative natural-product cleaning pipeline rather than the LOTUS three-stage MolVS approach; the article notes 'the current processing pipeline still removes a lot of correct entries and misses or induces some incorrect ones', so results are not interchangeable with other curation workflows.

skills.description: Use when simulating MS/MS spectra directly from a molecular structure, when you need fragment-level (not formula-level) peak attribution with hydrogen-shift annotations, or when building fragmentation-tree training labels with MAGMa.
skills.name: molecular-fragmentation-graph-generation
skills.search_text: molecular-fragmentation-graph-generation Use when simulating MS/MS spectra directly from a molecular structure, when you need fragment-level (not formula-level) peak attribution with hydrogen-shift annotations, or when building fragmentation-tree training labels with MAGMa. A formula-level (not fragment-level) prediction is sufficient — SCARF predicts spectra at the level of chemical formula and is ~10x faster (~1 CPU second per molecule for ICEBERG). Single-stage, maximum-speed simulation is the priority — GLACIER in the same ms-pred repo is described as an even faster and more accurate single-stage MS/MS simulator. You need guaranteed correct physical explanations: there are no guarantees that generated fragment attributions are the correct physical explanations due to equivalent-mass atom and bond rearrangements and the cosine-similarity training objective. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Implements ICEBERG, a two-stage Generate-then-Score MS/MS spectrum predictor: a gated-GNN predicts atom-wise bond breakage probabilities to reconstruct a molecular fragmentation graph, then a Set Transformer assigns intensities to each generated fragment-hydrogen-shift pair. It lifts the combinatorial MAGMa fragmentation approach into a fast neural model trained on experimental MS/MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Implements ICEBERG, a two-stage Generate-then-Score MS/MS spectrum predictor: a gated-GNN predicts atom-wise bond breakage probabilities to reconstruct a molecular fragmentation graph, then a Set Transformer assigns intensities to each generated fragment-hydrogen-shift pair. It lifts the combinatorial MAGMa fragmentation approach into a fast neural model trained on experimental MS/MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A formula-level (not fragment-level) prediction is sufficient — SCARF predicts spectra at the level of chemical formula and is ~10x faster (~1 CPU second per molecule for ICEBERG). Single-stage, maximum-speed simulation is the priority — GLACIER in the same ms-pred repo is described as an even faster and more accurate single-stage MS/MS simulator. You need guaranteed correct physical explanations: there are no guarantees that generated fragment attributions are the correct physical explanations due to equivalent-mass atom and bond rearrangements and the cosine-similarity training objective.

skills.description: Use when building MS-relevant topological feature vectors from rooted fragment graphs — i.e., you need a canonical, index-invariant ordering of fragment atoms (nearest to the cleaved-bond root) before constructing an adjacency-tensor representation.
skills.name: molecular-graph-breadth-first-traversal
skills.search_text: molecular-graph-breadth-first-traversal Use when building MS-relevant topological feature vectors from rooted fragment graphs — i.e., you need a canonical, index-invariant ordering of fragment atoms (nearest to the cleaved-bond root) before constructing an adjacency-tensor representation. The input is already a flat feature table or fingerprint (e.g. CSI:FingerID-style 1415-bit fingerprint) rather than a rooted fragment graph You need whole-molecule descriptors rather than fragment-local topology relative to a cleaved-bond root — the N=10 nearest-vertex selection deliberately restricts context to atoms within ~2 bonds of the root Bonds or atom types fall outside the encoded vocabularies (single/double/triple/higher/aromatic/conjugated; C, N, O, P, S, other), since these map to zero vectors or the 'other' bucket http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Canonical two-pass breadth-first traversal of a rooted fragment graph that assigns root-distance-based vertex indices, enabling CFM-ID 4.0's adjacency-matrix connectivity-matrix feature representation for learning ESI-MS/MS fragmentation transition probabilities. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Canonical two-pass breadth-first traversal of a rooted fragment graph that assigns root-distance-based vertex indices, enabling CFM-ID 4.0's adjacency-matrix connectivity-matrix feature representation for learning ESI-MS/MS fragmentation transition probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a flat feature table or fingerprint (e.g. CSI:FingerID-style 1415-bit fingerprint) rather than a rooted fragment graph You need whole-molecule descriptors rather than fragment-local topology relative to a cleaved-bond root — the N=10 nearest-vertex selection deliberately restricts context to atoms within ~2 bonds of the root Bonds or atom types fall outside the encoded vocabularies (single/double/triple/higher/aromatic/conjugated; C, N, O, P, S, other), since these map to zero vectors or the 'other' bucket

skills.description: Use when validating that a molecular-graph similarity method correctly treats double-bond positions, e.g. checking MCS overlaps between structurally similar FAs like FA 18:2(9Z,12Z) and FA 18:1(9Z).
skills.name: molecular-graph-component-verification
skills.search_text: molecular-graph-component-verification Use when validating that a molecular-graph similarity method correctly treats double-bond positions, e.g. checking MCS overlaps between structurally similar FAs like FA 18:2(9Z,12Z) and FA 18:1(9Z). Input lipid names or structures lack double-bond position annotations (e.g. only FA 18:2 without 9Z,12Z), so the DB-position-aware mode cannot be meaningfully exercised The goal is lipidome-level comparison of many lipids with abundances (Hausdorff distances on the lipid space model) rather than pairwise structural verification of single species Lipid sn-positions are unspecified in a way that requires the 'Ignore lipid sn-positions' all-combinations mode, since that changes which fatty acyl chains are paired and compared http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A verification procedure for LipidSpace's graph-based lipid structure comparison that checks whether counting double-bond (DB) positions in the maximum-common-subgraph (MCS) computation changes pairwise similarity between fatty acids such as FA 18:2(9Z,12Z) and FA 18:1(9Z). It validates the tool's 'Correctness of Double Bond Comparisons' claim by comparing DB-position-aware vs DB-agnostic intersection/union component counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: A verification procedure for LipidSpace's graph-based lipid structure comparison that checks whether counting double-bond (DB) positions in the maximum-common-subgraph (MCS) computation changes pairwise similarity between fatty acids such as FA 18:2(9Z,12Z) and FA 18:1(9Z). It validates the tool's 'Correctness of Double Bond Comparisons' claim by comparing DB-position-aware vs DB-agnostic intersection/union component counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lipid names or structures lack double-bond position annotations (e.g. only FA 18:2 without 9Z,12Z), so the DB-position-aware mode cannot be meaningfully exercised The goal is lipidome-level comparison of many lipids with abundances (Hausdorff distances on the lipid space model) rather than pairwise structural verification of single species Lipid sn-positions are unspecified in a way that requires the 'Ignore lipid sn-positions' all-combinations mode, since that changes which fatty acyl chains are paired and compared

skills.description: Use when you need to generate candidate fragment ions (m/z values) from a molecular structure (SMILES/SDF) for in silico spectral matching against tandem mass spectra, e.g. molecules from PubChem or DNP up to 2000 Da.

skills.search_text: molecular-graph-fragment-generation Use when you need to generate candidate fragment ions (m/z values) from a molecular structure (SMILES/SDF) for in silico spectral matching against tandem mass spectra, e.g. molecules from PubChem or DNP up to 2000 Da. skills.summary: Efficiently enumerate mass-spectrometry fragments of a small molecule by representing it as a molecular graph, disconnecting only N-C, O-C, and C-C candidate bonds, and using a Hopcroft-Tarjan bridges-and-2-cuts algorithm to yield single- and double-bond-cut fragments as in molDiscovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to explain peaks caused by rearrangement rules or moieties — molDiscovery ignores local/global structural features and covers only a limited number of bond types and rearrangement rules The structure contains benzene rings or large resonant systems where correct bond order matters — molDiscovery naively treats them as alternating single/double bonds You require quantum-chemical or learned fragmentation spectra prediction rather than efficient graph-cut enumeration

skills.description: Use when you need to generate a full molecular graph from an MS/MS spectrum given a known or retrieved Murcko scaffold, e.g. as the second stage of MADGEN's scaffold-conditioned de novo generation pipeline.
skills.name: molecular-graph-generative-modeling
skills.search_text: molecular-graph-generative-modeling Use when you need to generate a full molecular graph from an MS/MS spectrum given a known or retrieved Murcko scaffold, e.g. as the second stage of MADGEN's scaffold-conditioned de novo generation pipeline. You do not have a scaffold — MADGEN's generator requires a Murcko scaffold as the starting graph; for scaffold-free generation use a different model class. Your spectra are raw, un-normalized, and noisy — MADGEN preprocessing first normalizes intensities and removes low-intensity peaks below a predefined threshold; skip that preprocessing at your own risk. You only need scaffold retrieval/ranking, not molecule generation — use the contrastive retrieval module instead of the graph generator. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate a target molecule as a graph by adapting an absorbing-state Markov bridge model (RetroBridge-style) that starts from a fixed Murcko scaffold and fills in edges connecting scaffold atoms to free atoms, guided by MS/MS spectra via cross-attention. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2501.01950
skills.summary: Generate a target molecule as a graph by adapting an absorbing-state Markov bridge model (RetroBridge-style) that starts from a fixed Murcko scaffold and fills in edges connecting scaffold atoms to free atoms, guided by MS/MS spectra via cross-attention.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You do not have a scaffold — MADGEN's generator requires a Murcko scaffold as the starting graph; for scaffold-free generation use a different model class. Your spectra are raw, un-normalized, and noisy — MADGEN preprocessing first normalizes intensities and removes low-intensity peaks below a predefined threshold; skip that preprocessing at your own risk. You only need scaffold retrieval/ranking, not molecule generation — use the contrastive retrieval module instead of the graph generator.

skills.name: molecular-graph-neural-network-implementation
skills.search_text: molecular-graph-neural-network-implementation Use when building a compound-to-spectrum (C2MS) model from a molecular structure and a precomputed fragmentation DAG, where per-fragment formula probabilities must be learned by message-passing over molecular graphs. skills.summary: Implement FraGNNet's two-stage GNN: a Molecule GNN (GINE in PyTorch Geometric) that embeds the RDKit-featurized input molecular graph, and a Fragment GNN (node-wise MLP variant) over the fragmentation DAG whose per-node output MLPs produce a distribution over formulae, which maps to monoisotopic peak masses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an unknown MS/MS spectrum with no candidate molecular structure — the Molecule GNN requires a molecular graph G and is for the compound-to-spectrum (C2MS) direction, not MS2C retrieval alone Fragments require complex chemistry such as cyclizations, which dramatically expands the fragment search space beyond the recursive edge-removal DAG and the GNN's support The task is a fixed formula-set predictor (e.g. GrAFF-MS-style top-10,000 product/neutral-loss formula classification) rather than a per-fragment probabilistic distribution over formulae

skills.description: Use when sampling candidate molecular structures from a conditional graph diffusion decoder and you must filter invalid/disconnected molecules and select top-k hits by frequency.

skills.search_text: molecular-graph-sampling-and-validation Use when sampling candidate molecular structures from a conditional graph diffusion decoder and you must filter invalid/disconnected molecules and select top-k hits by frequency. When the chemical formula is unknown — DiffMS is formula-restricted (heavy atom-constrained) and requires composition to be given by tools like SIRIUS or MIST-CF When the goal is de novo generation of the exact molecular structure with guaranteed correctness — the paper notes structurally close matches, not exact structures, are what the method delivers When ranking MSNovelist-style outputs — that baseline uses beam search (width 100) with log-likelihood ranking, not diffusion sampling with frequency-based top-k selection http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates candidate molecular graphs from a trained diffusion decoder (DiffMS/DiGress formulation), then post-filters them with RDKit for chemical validity, connectedness, and formula-consistent atom composition before ranking candidates by frequency. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Generates candidate molecular graphs from a trained diffusion decoder (DiffMS/DiGress formulation), then post-filters them with RDKit for chemical validity, connectedness, and formula-consistent atom composition before ranking candidates by frequency.

skills.description: Use when scoring a set of candidate molecules generated per spectrum (or per query) against a known reference molecule, e.g. after sampling 100 structures per spectrum from a generative model and ranking by frequency.
skills.name: molecular-graph-similarity-evaluation
skills.search_text: molecular-graph-similarity-evaluation Use when scoring a set of candidate molecules generated per spectrum (or per query) against a known reference molecule, e.g. after sampling 100 structures per spectrum from a generative model and ranking by frequency. Input is already an aggregated metrics table rather than per-spectrum ranked candidate lists — no re-ranking or metric computation is possible The task is spectral matching against a spectral library (retrieval/identification) rather than de novo structure generation, where MCES/Tanimoto against a single ground-truth structure is not defined Candidate molecules cannot be sanitized by RDKit (invalid or disconnected) and have not yet passed the invalid/disconnected filter step — including them corrupts the top-k ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Evaluates de novo generated molecular structures against ground-truth molecules using Top-1/Top-10 accuracy plus two structure-aware graph similarity metrics: minimum MCES distance and maximum Tanimoto similarity. This is the standard evaluation protocol DiffMS applies after frequency-ranking sampled molecules on NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571

skills.search_text: molecular-graph-validity-filtering Use when a generative model (e.g., DiffMS discrete graph diffusion) has produced a pool of ~100 sampled molecules per mass spectrum and you need chemically valid, connected, frequency-ranked candidate structures for top-k evaluation (k=1, 10). skills.name: molecular-hierarchy-annotation
skills.search_text: molecular-hierarchy-annotation Use when a merged chemical hierarchy (e.g., qemistree.qza from make-hierarchy) and its merged feature data exist and you need ClassyFire taxonomy labels (e.g., acyl-carnitines, flavonoids) to interpret chemical-class subtrees across sample types. Features are MS1-only without MS/MS data or resolved structures — they cannot be assigned ClassyFire taxonomy and are not the target of this annotation step The goal is to build or prune the chemical hierarchy itself (use make-hierarchy or prune-hierarchy) rather than label existing features with chemical ontology terms You need a complete chemical summary of a complex sample from spectral matches alone — spectral-match coverage is typically only 1–20% of features and too low to summarize chemical content Input is a raw feature table before fingerprint prediction/hierarchy construction — taxonomy annotation presumes structures already exist Annotates each chemical feature in a Qemistree-built molecular hierarchy with the ClassyFire 5-level chemical taxonomy (kingdom, superclass, class, subclass, direct parent), enabling class-level subtree interpretation of the chemical tree against sample metadata. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00677-3

The goal is site-of-metabolism prediction (atom-level which-site output) rather than molecule-level reactant classification — SMARTCyp addresses the site question, CypReact addresses the reactant question The input is not molecular structural data (SMILES/SDF) — e.g. omics or spectral data unrelated to reactant prediction No binary reactant labels and no cross-validation protocol are available, so AUROC cannot be computed to judge correct application Loads and standardizes molecular inputs for CYP450 reactant prediction: molecules supplied as SMILES strings or SDF records are paired with binary reactant labels for the nine major human CYP450 enzymes (CYP1A2, CYP2A6, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, CYP3A4) so they can be scored by CypReact and evaluated by AUROC. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.8b00035

skills.description: Use when training a pairwise RankSVM on molecular structures for LC retention-order prediction: structures are given as InChI/MACCS representations and a kernel matrix between training molecules is required.
skills.name: molecular-kernel-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: molecular-kernel-matrix-construction Use when training a pairwise RankSVM on molecular structures for LC retention-order prediction: structures are given as InChI/MACCS representations and a kernel matrix between training molecules is required. The goal is predicting absolute retention times rather than pairwise elution order — the paper uses SVR with per-system RT calibration for that, which cannot leverage heterogeneous LC systems the way the kernelized RankSVM can. The prediction task operates on MS/MS spectra rather than molecular structures — molecular candidate scoring is handled by IOKR, not by the molecular kernel matrix. Molecule representations are already provided as explicit feature vectors and a linear kernel suffices; building a MinMax/Tanimoto molecular kernel is unnecessary overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Constructs the molecular kernel matrix K_m with entries [K_m]_ij = phi(m_i)^T phi(m_j) from MACCS fingerprints, using the MinMax kernel for counting fingerprints and the Tanimoto kernel for binary fingerprints. This kernel is the molecular side of the RankSVM retention-order pipeline and is decomposed as Q = A K_m A^T so the full pairwise kernel never needs materializing. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty590
skills.summary: Constructs the molecular kernel matrix K_m with entries [K_m]_ij = phi(m_i)^T phi(m_j) from MACCS fingerprints, using the MinMax kernel for counting fingerprints and the Tanimoto kernel for binary fingerprints. This kernel is the molecular side of the RankSVM retention-order pipeline and is decomposed as Q = A K_m A^T so the full pairwise kernel never needs materializing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is predicting absolute retention times rather than pairwise elution order — the paper uses SVR with per-system RT calibration for that, which cannot leverage heterogeneous LC systems the way the kernelized RankSVM can. The prediction task operates on MS/MS spectra rather than molecular structures — molecular candidate scoring is handled by IOKR, not by the molecular kernel matrix. Molecule representations are already provided as explicit feature vectors and a linear kernel suffices; building a MinMax/Tanimoto molecular kernel is unnecessary overhead.

skills.description: Use when feature intensities with sample x/y/z coordinates and spot radii (e.g. Optimus 'ili_input.csv) must be overlaid on a 2D image or 3D STL model, and the resulting molecular map view should be tuned, saved, and reproducibly shared.
skills.name: molecular-map-spatial-visualization
skills.search_text: molecular-map-spatial-visualization Use when feature intensities with sample x/y/z coordinates and spot radii (e.g. Optimus 'ili_input.csv) must be overlaid on a 2D image or 3D STL model, and the resulting molecular map view should be tuned, saved, and reproducibly shared. The data are direct-infusion or non-spatial LC-MS runs with no x/y/z coordinates and no 2D/3D model to map onto. The input is a raw feature quantification matrix that first requires Optimus feature detection, alignment, filtering, and 'Save 'ili input file' node execution — visualization in 'ili is premature.
