skills.description: Use when you have a table of canonical SMILES (e.g. DeepMet-generated candidate metabolites) and need per-molecule calculated molecular mass and formula to enable m/z-based filtering or annotation of metabolomics peaks.
skills.name: molecular-mass-and-formula-calculation
skills.search_text: molecular-mass-and-formula-calculation Use when you have a table of canonical SMILES (e.g. DeepMet-generated candidate metabolites) and need per-molecule calculated molecular mass and formula to enable m/z-based filtering or annotation of metabolomics peaks. Input SMILES have not yet been parsed/validated with RDKit and may include invalid structures — validate first, then annotate mass/formula You need experimental MS/MS spectra or retention times rather than calculated properties — the article notes predicting MS/MS spectra or retention times from chemical structures remain open problems Structures are already annotated with masses/formulas in the source table (e.g. the released 34.4-million-structure resource) — reuse rather than recompute http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Compute the calculated molecular mass and molecular formula for each canonicalized SMILES so that generated candidate metabolites can be filtered and prioritized by mass-to-charge ratio against MS/MS signals. In the DeepMet workflow this step converts a table of valid canonical structures into a mass/formula-annotated structure-frequency resource. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Compute the calculated molecular mass and molecular formula for each canonicalized SMILES so that generated candidate metabolites can be filtered and prioritized by mass-to-charge ratio against MS/MS signals. In the DeepMet workflow this step converts a table of valid canonical structures into a mass/formula-annotated structure-frequency resource.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input SMILES have not yet been parsed/validated with RDKit and may include invalid structures — validate first, then annotate mass/formula You need experimental MS/MS spectra or retention times rather than calculated properties — the article notes predicting MS/MS spectra or retention times from chemical structures remain open problems Structures are already annotated with masses/formulas in the source table (e.g. the released 34.4-million-structure resource) — reuse rather than recompute

skills.description: Use when performing library matching against an augmented NEIMS spectral library and you know the molecular mass of the query molecule with reasonable accuracy, so candidates can be restricted to spectra within a few Daltons of the query mass.
skills.name: molecular-mass-computation
skills.search_text: molecular-mass-computation Use when performing library matching against an augmented NEIMS spectral library and you know the molecular mass of the query molecule with reasonable accuracy, so candidates can be restricted to spectra within a few Daltons of the query mass. Molecular mass of the sample molecule is unknown or inaccurate — the article states the filter applies only 'for experimental setups where it is possible to know the molecular mass of the sample with some accuracy'. Molecule candidates span isotopic species that shift nominal mass by more than the tolerance, since NEIMS currently does not model isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments. The query is already restricted to a library whose spectra are all mass-compatible, making filtering a no-op. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the molecular mass of each query molecule from its structure so that the spectral reference library can be filtered to candidates within a 5 Da tolerance before library matching. This mass filter is the NEIMS library-matching step that reduces candidate libraries to a median of 6696 spectra per query and improves recall-at-10. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00085
skills.summary: Computes the molecular mass of each query molecule from its structure so that the spectral reference library can be filtered to candidates within a 5 Da tolerance before library matching. This mass filter is the NEIMS library-matching step that reduces candidate libraries to a median of 6696 spectra per query and improves recall-at-10.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Molecular mass of the sample molecule is unknown or inaccurate — the article states the filter applies only 'for experimental setups where it is possible to know the molecular mass of the sample with some accuracy'. Molecule candidates span isotopic species that shift nominal mass by more than the tolerance, since NEIMS currently does not model isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments. The query is already restricted to a library whose spectra are all mass-compatible, making filtering a no-op.

skills.description: Use when performing library matching of an EI mass spectrum against a large reference library (e.g., the NIST 2017 library) and the molecular mass of the query sample is known with reasonable accuracy.
skills.name: molecular-mass-filtering
skills.search_text: molecular-mass-filtering Use when performing library matching of an EI mass spectrum against a large reference library (e.g., the NIST 2017 library) and the molecular mass of the query sample is known with reasonable accuracy. The molecular mass of the query sample cannot be estimated with some accuracy, so the filter cannot prune candidates reliably The reference library is already small enough that filtering adds no benefit or risks excluding the true candidate beyond the tolerance window http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Restricts the spectral reference library to candidates whose molecular mass is within a tolerance (5 Da) of the query molecule's mass before cosine-similarity library matching, as used in NEIMS library matching. This shrinks the candidate space (median 6696 spectra per query) and improves recall@10. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00085
skills.summary: Restricts the spectral reference library to candidates whose molecular mass is within a tolerance (5 Da) of the query molecule's mass before cosine-similarity library matching, as used in NEIMS library matching. This shrinks the candidate space (median 6696 spectra per query) and improves recall@10.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecular mass of the query sample cannot be estimated with some accuracy, so the filter cannot prune candidates reliably The reference library is already small enough that filtering adds no benefit or risks excluding the true candidate beyond the tolerance window

skills.description: Use when curating a CCS or metabolomics reference table where each row carries a structure identifier (InChI/SMILES), an adduct type, a listed theoretical m/z, and an m/z tolerance window for structural validation.
skills.name: molecular-mass-mz-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: molecular-mass-mz-consistency-checking Use when curating a CCS or metabolomics reference table where each row carries a structure identifier (InChI/SMILES), an adduct type, a listed theoretical m/z, and an m/z tolerance window for structural validation. Input entries lack a structure representation (InChI/SMILES) from which m/z can be recomputed — only the listed m/z is available, so no independent consistency check is possible The goal is CCS prediction or annotation filtering (ΔCCS threshold of 2.8% and 10 ppm mass error), not training-data scrubbing — use CCSP 2.0 prediction instead Target adducts are dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments, which the CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validates that theoretical m/z values listed for database entries match m/z recomputed from the entry's structure and ionic species, flagging mismatches beyond a small tolerance (e.g. >1 mDa) so corrupt or mislabelled records can be excluded before modeling. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2022.08.09.503345
skills.summary: Validates that theoretical m/z values listed for database entries match m/z recomputed from the entry's structure and ionic species, flagging mismatches beyond a small tolerance (e.g. >1 mDa) so corrupt or mislabelled records can be excluded before modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input entries lack a structure representation (InChI/SMILES) from which m/z can be recomputed — only the listed m/z is available, so no independent consistency check is possible The goal is CCS prediction or annotation filtering (ΔCCS threshold of 2.8% and 10 ppm mass error), not training-data scrubbing — use CCSP 2.0 prediction instead Target adducts are dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments, which the CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support

skills.description: Use when a molecular network (e.g., GNPS) contains an unannotated node adjacent to library hits of a related metabolite, and the structural site of modification between the analogs must be localized from MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: molecular-network-analog-prioritization
skills.search_text: molecular-network-analog-prioritization Use when a molecular network (e.g., GNPS) contains an unannotated node adjacent to library hits of a related metabolite, and the structural site of modification between the analogs must be localized from MS/MS spectra. The unknown compound can be directly reidentified by standard MS/MS library search against GNPS libraries (no analog step is needed) No library-hit analog is adjacent in the molecular network — ModiFinder requires a structurally related known molecule as reference Precursor masses differ by more than 50% or exceed 2000 Da (benchmark eligibility checks i–ii), making analog alignment unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Localizes the modification site of an unknown analog within a molecular network family by aligning its MS/MS spectrum against a structurally related library-hit analog using ModiFinder, which scores the likelihood of each atom in the known analog being the modification site. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Localizes the modification site of an unknown analog within a molecular network family by aligning its MS/MS spectrum against a structurally related library-hit analog using ModiFinder, which scores the likelihood of each atom in the known analog being the modification site.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unknown compound can be directly reidentified by standard MS/MS library search against GNPS libraries (no analog step is needed) No library-hit analog is adjacent in the molecular network — ModiFinder requires a structurally related known molecule as reference Precursor masses differ by more than 50% or exceed 2000 Da (benchmark eligibility checks i–ii), making analog alignment unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have GNPS molecular networking outputs (edges and annotated spectra/MGF tables) and want to label nodes and edges with chemical class or MS2LDA Mass2Motif information to interpret network organization.
skills.name: molecular-network-annotation-propagation
skills.search_text: molecular-network-annotation-propagation Use when you have GNPS molecular networking outputs (edges and annotated spectra/MGF tables) and want to label nodes and edges with chemical class or MS2LDA Mass2Motif information to interpret network organization. The input is raw GC-MS data that has not yet been deconvolved and networked through MSHub/GNPS — spectral deconvolution must precede annotation propagation You only have standalone library-matched spectra with no molecular network edges, since propagation relies on network connectivity The goal is de novo spectral annotation rather than transferring existing chemical class labels across a network http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Propagate chemical class and substructural annotations across GNPS molecular network edges using pyMolNetEnhancer, so that structurally related consensus spectra in a network inherit consistent chemical class labels. Applied here to EI-based GC-MS molecular networks to show that cosine-similarity edges are driven by structural (chemical class) similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Propagate chemical class and substructural annotations across GNPS molecular network edges using pyMolNetEnhancer, so that structurally related consensus spectra in a network inherit consistent chemical class labels. Applied here to EI-based GC-MS molecular networks to show that cosine-similarity edges are driven by structural (chemical class) similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw GC-MS data that has not yet been deconvolved and networked through MSHub/GNPS — spectral deconvolution must precede annotation propagation You only have standalone library-matched spectra with no molecular network edges, since propagation relies on network connectivity The goal is de novo spectral annotation rather than transferring existing chemical class labels across a network

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS-style molecular network with per-spectrum candidate annotations and sparse spectral library matches (e.g. only ~10% seed nodes) and need annotations on nodes without any library match.
skills.name: molecular-network-annotation-propagation
skills.search_text: molecular-network-annotation-propagation Use when you have a GNPS-style molecular network with per-spectrum candidate annotations and sparse spectral library matches (e.g. only ~10% seed nodes) and need annotations on nodes without any library match. When the goal is direct spectral library matching of individual spectra rather than propagation of library identities across a network. When NAP's local first-neighbour propagation is sufficient and a standalone Java/NAP pipeline is preferred over a Python package — though ChemWalker is the better choice for running time, scalability and maintainability. When the graph contains non-positive edge weights: pyrwr's RWR is defined only on positively weighted networks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Propagate spectral library match identities through candidate structures on a molecular network using a random walk (ChemWalker), overcoming NAP's limitation of propagating only to the first neighbour of a spectral match. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad078
skills.summary: Propagate spectral library match identities through candidate structures on a molecular network using a random walk (ChemWalker), overcoming NAP's limitation of propagating only to the first neighbour of a spectral match.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct spectral library matching of individual spectra rather than propagation of library identities across a network. When NAP's local first-neighbour propagation is sufficient and a standalone Java/NAP pipeline is preferred over a Python package — though ChemWalker is the better choice for running time, scalability and maintainability. When the graph contains non-positive edge weights: pyrwr's RWR is defined only on positively weighted networks.

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS molecular networking output (classical or feature-based) plus SMILES annotations (library hits, NAP, DEREPLICATOR) and want ClassyFire chemical class labels mapped onto the network graph.
skills.name: molecular-network-chemical-class-annotation
skills.search_text: molecular-network-chemical-class-annotation Use when you have a GNPS molecular networking output (classical or feature-based) plus SMILES annotations (library hits, NAP, DEREPLICATOR) and want ClassyFire chemical class labels mapped onto the network graph. The dataset has no SMILES annotations (no GNPS library hits, NAP or DEREPLICATOR results) — ClassyFire cannot be queried without structures You only want structural motif substructure info without chemical taxonomy — the standalone MS2LDA-to-network mapping workflow suffices Input is not a GNPS molecular network (e.g. an already-aggregated feature table with no graph or scan IDs to join on) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotate GNPS molecular network nodes with hierarchical chemical taxonomy (ClassyFire superclass/class/subclass) by combining in silico annotation outputs (NAP, DEREPLICATOR, GNPS library hits) and optionally MS2LDA Mass2Motifs, using pyMolNetEnhancer or RMolNetEnhancer, and export annotated .graphml/.tsv files for Cytoscape visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Annotate GNPS molecular network nodes with hierarchical chemical taxonomy (ClassyFire superclass/class/subclass) by combining in silico annotation outputs (NAP, DEREPLICATOR, GNPS library hits) and optionally MS2LDA Mass2Motifs, using pyMolNetEnhancer or RMolNetEnhancer, and export annotated .graphml/.tsv files for Cytoscape visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no SMILES annotations (no GNPS library hits, NAP or DEREPLICATOR results) — ClassyFire cannot be queried without structures You only want structural motif substructure info without chemical taxonomy — the standalone MS2LDA-to-network mapping workflow suffices Input is not a GNPS molecular network (e.g. an already-aggregated feature table with no graph or scan IDs to join on)

skills.description: Use when candidate MS2 annotation lists (e.g., ISDB-LOTUS spectral matches) need to be reweighted using the chemical consistency of the molecular-network cluster a feature belongs to.
skills.name: molecular-network-cluster-consistency-reweighting
skills.search_text: molecular-network-cluster-consistency-reweighting Use when candidate MS2 annotation lists (e.g., ISDB-LOTUS spectral matches) need to be reweighted using the chemical consistency of the molecular-network cluster a feature belongs to. Features lack associated MS2 scans or have no molecular-network edges, so no cluster consistency signal exists (the ENPKG feature filtering keeps only features with an associated MS2 scan) The goal is reranking by taxonomic distance of the producing organism rather than chemical cluster consistency — that is a separate reranking mechanism in the same workflow Only a single annotation method is desired without cross-validation, e.g., when combining ISDB and SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID annotations for confidence is the actual goal http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reranks candidate structural annotations by propagating annotation confidence across a feature-based molecular network: features connected by high modified-cosine edges inherit support from the annotations of their spectral neighbors, following the Network Annotation Propagation principle. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Reranks candidate structural annotations by propagating annotation confidence across a feature-based molecular network: features connected by high modified-cosine edges inherit support from the annotations of their spectral neighbors, following the Network Annotation Propagation principle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features lack associated MS2 scans or have no molecular-network edges, so no cluster consistency signal exists (the ENPKG feature filtering keeps only features with an associated MS2 scan) The goal is reranking by taxonomic distance of the producing organism rather than chemical cluster consistency — that is a separate reranking mechanism in the same workflow Only a single annotation method is desired without cross-validation, e.g., when combining ISDB and SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID annotations for confidence is the actual goal

skills.description: Use when a set of identified spectra (PSMs/compound–spectrum matches) must be expanded to related spectra via GNPS molecular network clusters, with variants grouped into families and rendered as network graphs.
skills.name: molecular-network-cluster-visualization
skills.search_text: molecular-network-cluster-visualization Use when a set of identified spectra (PSMs/compound–spectrum matches) must be expanded to related spectra via GNPS molecular network clusters, with variants grouped into families and rendered as network graphs. Spectra are not organized into GNPS molecular network clusters (e.g., isolated spectra with no spectral network output), so no propagation across network distance 1–2 is possible The query metabolite class is outside the tool's scope — the article notes DEREPLICATOR+ 'is not applicable to all the classes of compounds' Only a visualization of raw (unidentified) clusters is needed with no identified spectra to seed families — components without at least one identified spectrum are not treated as metabolite families http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Propagates database-search identifications (e.g., DEREPLICATOR+ PSMs at FDR 0%) across GNPS molecular network clusters and renders each connected component — a metabolite family — as a network graph, enumerating spectral variants of the identified seed metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-018-06082-8
skills.summary: Propagates database-search identifications (e.g., DEREPLICATOR+ PSMs at FDR 0%) across GNPS molecular network clusters and renders each connected component — a metabolite family — as a network graph, enumerating spectral variants of the identified seed metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are not organized into GNPS molecular network clusters (e.g., isolated spectra with no spectral network output), so no propagation across network distance 1–2 is possible The query metabolite class is outside the tool's scope — the article notes DEREPLICATOR+ 'is not applicable to all the classes of compounds' Only a visualization of raw (unidentified) clusters is needed with no identified spectra to seed families — components without at least one identified spectrum are not treated as metabolite families

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular network component (e.g. a 21-spectra cluster) contains unknown spectra that pairwise similarity alone cannot structurally explain, and you want the mined fragmentation pattern with highest support and precision over that component.
skills.name: molecular-network-component-analysis
skills.search_text: molecular-network-component-analysis Use when a GNPS molecular network component (e.g. a 21-spectra cluster) contains unknown spectra that pairwise similarity alone cannot structurally explain, and you want the mined fragmentation pattern with highest support and precision over that component. The goal is to extract common structures shared by only two spectra — GNPS pairwise edges already propagate those annotations and mineMS2 pattern mining is unnecessary The spectra have not been processed by mineMS2 pattern mining (discretizeMzDifferences binning at 15 ppm and graph building), so no candidate patterns exist to score against the component Probabilistic substructure topics are preferred over exact graph-structured patterns — MS2LDA/MolNetEnhancer is the alternative pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Couples mineMS2-extracted exact fragmentation patterns to GNPS molecular network components to identify the pattern that best explains a component (support/precision over its spectra) and annotate its unknown members, e.g. the 99.0683 m/z difference (C5H9ON, valine loss) explaining the 21-spectra P. nordicum fungisporin component. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-01051-y
skills.summary: Couples mineMS2-extracted exact fragmentation patterns to GNPS molecular network components to identify the pattern that best explains a component (support/precision over its spectra) and annotate its unknown members, e.g. the 99.0683 m/z difference (C5H9ON, valine loss) explaining the 21-spectra P. nordicum fungisporin component.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to extract common structures shared by only two spectra — GNPS pairwise edges already propagate those annotations and mineMS2 pattern mining is unnecessary The spectra have not been processed by mineMS2 pattern mining (discretizeMzDifferences binning at 15 ppm and graph building), so no candidate patterns exist to score against the component Probabilistic substructure topics are preferred over exact graph-structured patterns — MS2LDA/MolNetEnhancer is the alternative pipeline

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (mzXML/mzML) must be organized into a molecular network to group related spectra, detect analog mass shifts (e.g. -41 Da stenothricin analogs), or dereplicate known metabolites.
skills.name: molecular-network-construction
skills.search_text: molecular-network-construction Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (mzXML/mzML) must be organized into a molecular network to group related spectra, detect analog mass shifts (e.g. -41 Da stenothricin analogs), or dereplicate known metabolites. Input is already a processed feature table or abundance matrix with no MS/MS spectra to cluster The goal is library search of individual query spectra against reference spectra (spectral library searching), not inter-sample spectrum-to-spectrum networking Only a few individual spectra or a single LC-MS file need matching to databases such as Massbank, Metlin, mzCloud, or ReSpect http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 GNPS molecular networking: MS/MS spectra are clustered into consensus spectra with MSCluster, consensus spectra are compared with modification-tolerant spectral matching, and edges are retained only under a mutual top-K neighbor rule to produce a node/edge network of related molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3597
skills.summary: GNPS molecular networking: MS/MS spectra are clustered into consensus spectra with MSCluster, consensus spectra are compared with modification-tolerant spectral matching, and edges are retained only under a mutual top-K neighbor rule to produce a node/edge network of related molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or abundance matrix with no MS/MS spectra to cluster The goal is library search of individual query spectra against reference spectra (spectral library searching), not inter-sample spectrum-to-spectrum networking Only a few individual spectra or a single LC-MS file need matching to databases such as Massbank, Metlin, mzCloud, or ReSpect

skills.description: Use when building molecular networks from clustered LC–MS/MS consensus spectra (per-sample MGF files) to represent ionization variants of the same precursor as one [M+H]+ ion entity for dereplication and bioactivity ranking.
skills.name: molecular-network-construction
skills.search_text: molecular-network-construction Use when building molecular networks from clustered LC–MS/MS consensus spectra (per-sample MGF files) to represent ionization variants of the same precursor as one [M+H]+ ion entity for dereplication and bioactivity ranking. Input is already a quantification/feature table without MS2 consensus spectra — network construction requires per-sample MGF clean consensus spectra The goal is spectral library identification (step 6, Tremolo search against GNPS/ISDB libraries) rather than network-based grouping of ionization variants http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Construction of spectral similarity molecular networks (SSMN) and ionization variant annotation molecular networks (IVAMN) from clean consensus MS2 spectra in NP3 MS Workflow, grouping in-source/adduct ionization variants of the same precursor under a single PageRank-selected [M + H]+ representative ion. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Construction of spectral similarity molecular networks (SSMN) and ionization variant annotation molecular networks (IVAMN) from clean consensus MS2 spectra in NP3 MS Workflow, grouping in-source/adduct ionization variants of the same precursor under a single PageRank-selected [M + H]+ representative ion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantification/feature table without MS2 consensus spectra — network construction requires per-sample MGF clean consensus spectra The goal is spectral library identification (step 6, Tremolo search against GNPS/ISDB libraries) rather than network-based grouping of ionization variants

skills.description: Use when you have a large extract library (e.g., thousands of MGF MS/MS spectra) and want to cluster spectra into molecular families using a learned spectral similarity (TransExION) instead of GNPS cosine networking.
skills.name: molecular-network-construction
skills.search_text: molecular-network-construction Use when you have a large extract library (e.g., thousands of MGF MS/MS spectra) and want to cluster spectra into molecular families using a learned spectral similarity (TransExION) instead of GNPS cosine networking. Input is raw LC-MS/MS vendor files or a feature table rather than MGF/h5py MS/MS spectra — peak picking and MGF export must happen first. The goal is de novo structural elucidation of a single unknown spectrum rather than network-level compound-family organization. A strict peak-matched cosine network (GNPS classical networking) is required for comparability with legacy workflows; TransExION edges do not require a minimum matched peak count. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Constructs a molecular network of MS/MS spectra by computing all pairwise spectral similarities with TransExION, filtering edges (score > 0.6, no minimum matched-peak requirement), and importing the similarity matrix into meRgeION to recover compound-family sub-networks such as those originally derived with SNAP-MS/GNPS. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Constructs a molecular network of MS/MS spectra by computing all pairwise spectral similarities with TransExION, filtering edges (score > 0.6, no minimum matched-peak requirement), and importing the similarity matrix into meRgeION to recover compound-family sub-networks such as those originally derived with SNAP-MS/GNPS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS/MS vendor files or a feature table rather than MGF/h5py MS/MS spectra — peak picking and MGF export must happen first. The goal is de novo structural elucidation of a single unknown spectrum rather than network-level compound-family organization. A strict peak-matched cosine network (GNPS classical networking) is required for comparability with legacy workflows; TransExION edges do not require a minimum matched peak count.

skills.description: Use when you have all-pairs spectral similarity scores (Spec2Vec, cosine, or modified cosine) over a positive-ionization MS/MS dataset and want to cluster spectra into molecular networks whose edges reflect structural (Tanimoto) similarity.
skills.name: molecular-network-construction-from-similarity-scores
skills.search_text: molecular-network-construction-from-similarity-scores Use when you have all-pairs spectral similarity scores (Spec2Vec, cosine, or modified cosine) over a positive-ionization MS/MS dataset and want to cluster spectra into molecular networks whose edges reflect structural (Tanimoto) similarity. When your training set does not include a large fraction of the fragment ions and losses present in the query data — Spec2Vec needs training data and its missing-word issue becomes relevant on smaller datasets or with more m/z decimals in peak words For GC-MS data — the paper only demonstrated performance on LC-MS data When you only need pairwise library matching of a few query spectra rather than all-pairs network construction over a large dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Builds molecular networks from all-pairs MS/MS spectral similarity scores (e.g. Spec2Vec vs modified cosine) by retaining top-k links per node, splitting large poorly connected clusters with the Louvain algorithm, and scoring clusters by Tanimoto structural similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Builds molecular networks from all-pairs MS/MS spectral similarity scores (e.g. Spec2Vec vs modified cosine) by retaining top-k links per node, splitting large poorly connected clusters with the Louvain algorithm, and scoring clusters by Tanimoto structural similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When your training set does not include a large fraction of the fragment ions and losses present in the query data — Spec2Vec needs training data and its missing-word issue becomes relevant on smaller datasets or with more m/z decimals in peak words For GC-MS data — the paper only demonstrated performance on LC-MS data When you only need pairwise library matching of a few query spectra rather than all-pairs network construction over a large dataset

skills.description: Use when a differential LC/MS feature table plus centroided MS/MS raw data are available and structurally related differential features need to be grouped by MS2 spectral similarity into subnetworks for class-level annotation.
skills.name: molecular-network-construction-ms2-spectra
skills.search_text: molecular-network-construction-ms2-spectra Use when a differential LC/MS feature table plus centroided MS/MS raw data are available and structurally related differential features need to be grouped by MS2 spectral similarity into subnetworks for class-level annotation.
