skills.description: Use when you have MZmine-exported feature quantification tables (.csv) and .mgf fragmentation spectra — especially ions present only in a scheduled precursor list and never fragmented by DDA — that need multi-level annotation.
skills.name: molecular-networking-fbmn-annotation
skills.search_text: molecular-networking-fbmn-annotation Use when you have MZmine-exported feature quantification tables (.csv) and .mgf fragmentation spectra — especially ions present only in a scheduled precursor list and never fragmented by DDA — that need multi-level annotation. Nodes that already have a direct spectral library match from the FBMN/GNPS2 spectral pairing step — no propagation or in silico layer is needed for them List-only ions for which no fragmentation spectrum (.mgf entry) exists, since FBMN, ChemWalker, and SIRIUS all require MS/MS spectra Data acquired or preprocessed outside MZmine without a GNPS-FBMN-compatible export (row ID, m/z, retention time, and MS2-filtered rows) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Three-level annotation of fragmentation spectra — GNPS2 FBMN spectral pairing, ChemWalker annotation propagation over the molecular network, and SIRIUS 5.8.5 in silico annotation — used here to annotate list-only precursor ions from RegFilter scheduled precursor lists that DDA mode missed, recovering 43 (BRA006), 46 (BRA010), and 47 (BRA177) annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Three-level annotation of fragmentation spectra — GNPS2 FBMN spectral pairing, ChemWalker annotation propagation over the molecular network, and SIRIUS 5.8.5 in silico annotation — used here to annotate list-only precursor ions from RegFilter scheduled precursor lists that DDA mode missed, recovering 43 (BRA006), 46 (BRA010), and 47 (BRA177) annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Nodes that already have a direct spectral library match from the FBMN/GNPS2 spectral pairing step — no propagation or in silico layer is needed for them List-only ions for which no fragmentation spectrum (.mgf entry) exists, since FBMN, ChemWalker, and SIRIUS all require MS/MS spectra Data acquired or preprocessed outside MZmine without a GNPS-FBMN-compatible export (row ID, m/z, retention time, and MS2-filtered rows)

skills.description: Use when validated BGC–metabolite links must be scored or benchmarked — e.g. PoDP JSON metadata with MIBiG IDs, MS/MS URLs (GNPS-MassIVE or MetaboLights), and genome labels are available and a candidate link ranking is needed.
skills.name: molecular-networking-genome-mining-integration
skills.search_text: molecular-networking-genome-mining-integration Use when validated BGC–metabolite links must be scored or benchmarked — e.g. PoDP JSON metadata with MIBiG IDs, MS/MS URLs (GNPS-MassIVE or MetaboLights), and genome labels are available and a candidate link ranking is needed. Your data is unpaired/unannotated omics data with no BGC–metabolite links — the PoDP does not store metabolomics or genomics datasets themselves, only metadata defining pairs, so raw unpaired inputs cannot be scored You need to discover BGC–MS/MS links de novo — this skill scores and ranks already validated or candidate links documented in PoDP metadata, it does not create the links Input metadata relies heavily on free text in 'Other' boxes, which is 'inherently not machine-readable' and cannot be reliably parsed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Score and rank BGC–metabolite links by loading PoDP community-curated paired datasets (MIBiG identifiers linked to MS/MS URLs with scan numbers and genome labels) into the NPLinker framework and computing the newly proposed scoring system on validated links. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00724-z
skills.summary: Score and rank BGC–metabolite links by loading PoDP community-curated paired datasets (MIBiG identifiers linked to MS/MS URLs with scan numbers and genome labels) into the NPLinker framework and computing the newly proposed scoring system on validated links.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data is unpaired/unannotated omics data with no BGC–metabolite links — the PoDP does not store metabolomics or genomics datasets themselves, only metadata defining pairs, so raw unpaired inputs cannot be scored You need to discover BGC–MS/MS links de novo — this skill scores and ranks already validated or candidate links documented in PoDP metadata, it does not create the links Input metadata relies heavily on free text in 'Other' boxes, which is 'inherently not machine-readable' and cannot be reliably parsed

skills.description: Use when MSHub deconvolution output (per-compound fragmentation/abundance table) must be annotated with balance scores and filtered before being used as GNPS molecular networking input.
skills.name: molecular-networking-input-preparation
skills.search_text: molecular-networking-input-preparation Use when MSHub deconvolution output (per-compound fragmentation/abundance table) must be annotated with balance scores and filtered before being used as GNPS molecular networking input. The table is already the balance-score-filtered output (filtered_annotations.csv); re-filtering would compound the thresholds. The GC-MS data are still raw and have not been auto-deconvoluted by MSHub, so no per-compound balance score exists yet. The analysis is LC-MS/MS feature-based molecular networking (e.g., MZmine/GNPS feature tables) rather than MSHub GC-MS deconvolution output. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Prepares MSHub/GNPS deconvoluted GC-MS compound tables for molecular networking by annotating each deconvoluted compound with its balance score — a metric of fragmentation-pattern reproducibility across all samples — and filtering annotations at a balance-score threshold applied jointly with the cosine match score. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3
skills.summary: Prepares MSHub/GNPS deconvoluted GC-MS compound tables for molecular networking by annotating each deconvoluted compound with its balance score — a metric of fragmentation-pattern reproducibility across all samples — and filtering annotations at a balance-score threshold applied jointly with the cosine match score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The table is already the balance-score-filtered output (filtered_annotations.csv); re-filtering would compound the thresholds. The GC-MS data are still raw and have not been auto-deconvoluted by MSHub, so no per-compound balance score exists yet. The analysis is LC-MS/MS feature-based molecular networking (e.g., MZmine/GNPS feature tables) rather than MSHub GC-MS deconvolution output.

skills.description: Use when validating an MCN molecular network against a conventional similarity-threshold network by checking whether specific ion pairs (e.g. [M+Na]+/[M+H]+ adduct variants of the same metabolite) are connected only in the MCN graph.
skills.name: molecular-networking-link-verification
skills.search_text: molecular-networking-link-verification Use when validating an MCN molecular network against a conventional similarity-threshold network by checking whether specific ion pairs (e.g. [M+Na]+/[M+H]+ adduct variants of the same metabolite) are connected only in the MCN graph. The network under test is already an MCN graph and you only need descriptive statistics rather than a link-verification comparison against a conventional network. The ion pairs of interest are not adduct variants of the same metabolite (e.g. unrelated metabolites); the skill is specifically scoped to sodiated–protonated adduct pairs. No conventional similarity-threshold network is available for comparison — the verification depends on contrasting MCN links with conventional-network absence. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Verification workflow for molecular community networking (MCN) that tests whether adduct variants (e.g. sodiated [M+Na]+ ions) are linked to their protonated [M+H]+ precursors in MCN output but remain disconnected in conventional threshold-based molecular networks. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Verification workflow for molecular community networking (MCN) that tests whether adduct variants (e.g. sodiated [M+Na]+ ions) are linked to their protonated [M+H]+ precursors in MCN output but remain disconnected in conventional threshold-based molecular networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network under test is already an MCN graph and you only need descriptive statistics rather than a link-verification comparison against a conventional network. The ion pairs of interest are not adduct variants of the same metabolite (e.g. unrelated metabolites); the skill is specifically scoped to sodiated–protonated adduct pairs. No conventional similarity-threshold network is available for comparison — the verification depends on contrasting MCN links with conventional-network absence.

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS feature-based molecular networking job (Node_info.tsv), CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv), and spectral library match data, and need consensus chemical class annotations for ion features across subnetworks.
skills.name: molecular-networking-node-classification
skills.search_text: molecular-networking-node-classification Use when you have a GNPS feature-based molecular networking job (Node_info.tsv), CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv), and spectral library match data, and need consensus chemical class annotations for ion features across subnetworks. When no molecular network or spectral library matches are available — ConCISE fuses molecular networking, spectral library matching and in silico class predictions, and cannot propagate consensus without a subnetwork structure. When you need exact structure elucidation rather than chemical-class annotation — ConCISE yields putative classifications at the ChemOnt superclass/class/subclass levels, not identified metabolite structures. When annotation confidence requirements cannot tolerate consensus thresholds — propagation is limited to structural classes identical for the majority of ion features within a subnetwork, so low-redundancy subnetworks with few class predictions will yield few consensus annotations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Annotates ion features in GNPS feature-based molecular networking by fusing spectral library matches with SIRIUS/CANOPUS in silico class predictions into consensus ClassyFire ChemOnt classifications (superclass, class, subclass) per subnetwork, propagating annotations only where a structural class is shared by the majority of ion features. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: Annotates ion features in GNPS feature-based molecular networking by fusing spectral library matches with SIRIUS/CANOPUS in silico class predictions into consensus ClassyFire ChemOnt classifications (superclass, class, subclass) per subnetwork, propagating annotations only where a structural class is shared by the majority of ion features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no molecular network or spectral library matches are available — ConCISE fuses molecular networking, spectral library matching and in silico class predictions, and cannot propagate consensus without a subnetwork structure. When you need exact structure elucidation rather than chemical-class annotation — ConCISE yields putative classifications at the ChemOnt superclass/class/subclass levels, not identified metabolite structures. When annotation confidence requirements cannot tolerate consensus thresholds — propagation is limited to structural classes identical for the majority of ion features within a subnetwork, so low-redundancy subnetworks with few class predictions will yield few consensus annotations.

skills.description: Use when you have GNPS feature-based molecular networking output plus a CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv and node info with library spectral matches, and need to propagate chemical class annotations to unannotated subnetwork members.
skills.name: molecular-networking-subnetwork-propagation
skills.search_text: molecular-networking-subnetwork-propagation Use when you have GNPS feature-based molecular networking output plus a CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv and node info with library spectral matches, and need to propagate chemical class annotations to unannotated subnetwork members. Subnetworks (or singletons) contain no library spectral match — ConCISE discards these nodes and assigns no in silico annotation, so propagation cannot help. GNPS has not supplied ClassyFire ontology columns for your library matches and you have not applied a workaround (NPClassifier or manual Fiehn classyfire Batch lookup) — the consensus tally cannot be computed without superclass/class/subclass annotations. You need structural (SMILES/InChI) annotations rather than hierarchical class labels — ConCISE only propagates ChemOnt (or NPClassifier) classification levels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 ConCISE propagates consensus ClassyFire ChemOnt classifications from library-matched and CANOPUS in-silico-annotated nodes to unannotated ion features within GNPS molecular networking subnetworks, using percent-consensus cutoffs (superclass >= 50%, class/subclass >= 70%). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: ConCISE propagates consensus ClassyFire ChemOnt classifications from library-matched and CANOPUS in-silico-annotated nodes to unannotated ion features within GNPS molecular networking subnetworks, using percent-consensus cutoffs (superclass >= 50%, class/subclass >= 70%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Subnetworks (or singletons) contain no library spectral match — ConCISE discards these nodes and assigns no in silico annotation, so propagation cannot help. GNPS has not supplied ClassyFire ontology columns for your library matches and you have not applied a workaround (NPClassifier or manual Fiehn classyfire Batch lookup) — the consensus tally cannot be computed without superclass/class/subclass annotations. You need structural (SMILES/InChI) annotations rather than hierarchical class labels — ConCISE only propagates ChemOnt (or NPClassifier) classification levels.

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists must be converted to continuous molecular property values (e.g. QED, synthetic accessibility, Bertz complexity) and spectrum-to-structure reference libraries are unavailable.
skills.name: molecular-property-regression-from-spectra
skills.search_text: molecular-property-regression-from-spectra Use when raw MS/MS peak lists must be converted to continuous molecular property values (e.g. QED, synthetic accessibility, Bertz complexity) and spectrum-to-structure reference libraries are unavailable. The goal is molecular-structure retrieval by fingerprint search in PubChem — that is a separate fingerprint-prediction and accuracy@k retrieval task, not property regression Spectra are outside the training distribution the article covers, e.g. negative ionization mode or multiply charged precursor ions, which the authors explicitly note were not incorporated A production-ready property predictor is required — the authors state this fine-tuning 'should be understood as a proof of concept that our approach can achieve competitive performance with MIST' http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fine-tunes the pre-trained 116M-parameter DreaMS transformer on MS/MS spectra paired with molecular structures so a regression head predicts chemical properties (QED, synthetic accessibility, Bertz complexity, among 11 total) directly from raw tandem mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Fine-tunes the pre-trained 116M-parameter DreaMS transformer on MS/MS spectra paired with molecular structures so a regression head predicts chemical properties (QED, synthetic accessibility, Bertz complexity, among 11 total) directly from raw tandem mass spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is molecular-structure retrieval by fingerprint search in PubChem — that is a separate fingerprint-prediction and accuracy@k retrieval task, not property regression Spectra are outside the training distribution the article covers, e.g. negative ionization mode or multiply charged precursor ions, which the authors explicitly note were not incorporated A production-ready property predictor is required — the authors state this fine-tuning 'should be understood as a proof of concept that our approach can achieve competitive performance with MIST'

skills.description: Use when comparing candidate molecular representations (RDKit-normalized descriptors, Morgan counts, D-MPNN, hybrid embeddings) for retention-order prediction, via 5-fold cross-validation on a reference training set followed by independent-dataset generalizability testing.
skills.name: molecular-representation-training-cross-validation
skills.search_text: molecular-representation-training-cross-validation Use when comparing candidate molecular representations (RDKit-normalized descriptors, Morgan counts, D-MPNN, hybrid embeddings) for retention-order prediction, via 5-fold cross-validation on a reference training set followed by independent-dataset generalizability testing. Retention data from HILIC chromatographic systems — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems, and HILIC model construction with generalizability is stated as future work Compounds outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S — the broader chemical space is unexplored The goal is already-decided retention scoring with a trained model rather than representation comparison — use ROASMI_predict.py instead of retraining http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains the ROASMI RankNet retention-order model on the dataset_87 reference set under 5-fold cross-validation using five candidate molecular representations (Rdkit_norm, Morgan_count, D-MPNN, Hybrid_1, Hybrid_2), then evaluates the top two on independent test datasets to select the best-generalizing representation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Trains the ROASMI RankNet retention-order model on the dataset_87 reference set under 5-fold cross-validation using five candidate molecular representations (Rdkit_norm, Morgan_count, D-MPNN, Hybrid_1, Hybrid_2), then evaluates the top two on independent test datasets to select the best-generalizing representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Retention data from HILIC chromatographic systems — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems, and HILIC model construction with generalizability is stated as future work Compounds outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S — the broader chemical space is unexplored The goal is already-decided retention scoring with a trained model rather than representation comparison — use ROASMI_predict.py instead of retraining

skills.description: Use when raw SMILES strings and adduct labels ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-) must be transformed into graph representations (node, adjacency, edge matrices or adduct graphs) with 3D coordinates before training or evaluating GNN CCS prediction models.
skills.name: molecular-smiles-feature-preparation
skills.search_text: molecular-smiles-feature-preparation Use when raw SMILES strings and adduct labels ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-) must be transformed into graph representations (node, adjacency, edge matrices or adduct graphs) with 3D coordinates before training or evaluating GNN CCS prediction models. Input is already a featurized graph dataset (MyDataset/DGL graphs) — re-running conformer generation wastes compute and may change predictions via different random conformers The goal is cross-database generalization testing on already-trained models — only the prepared test parquet is needed, not re-featurization logic Molecules cannot be embedded or lack valid SMILES; ETKDGv3 embedding failures will silently degrade coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Converts SMILES strings plus adduct annotations into GNN-ready molecular graph inputs — 3D conformers (ETKDGv3/MMFF via RDKit v2023.09.5), node/adjacency/edge feature matrices or DGL adduct graphs — for CCS prediction models such as SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, and Mol2CCS. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Converts SMILES strings plus adduct annotations into GNN-ready molecular graph inputs — 3D conformers (ETKDGv3/MMFF via RDKit v2023.09.5), node/adjacency/edge feature matrices or DGL adduct graphs — for CCS prediction models such as SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, and Mol2CCS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a featurized graph dataset (MyDataset/DGL graphs) — re-running conformer generation wastes compute and may change predictions via different random conformers The goal is cross-database generalization testing on already-trained models — only the prepared test parquet is needed, not re-featurization logic Molecules cannot be embedded or lack valid SMILES; ETKDGv3 embedding failures will silently degrade coverage

skills.description: Use when a lipidomic intensity matrix needs to be reduced to the molecular-species (LMS) level before LipidOne 2.0 statistical or pathway analysis and it still contains missing or '0' entries that must be imputed per-row.
skills.name: molecular-species-submatrix-extraction
skills.search_text: molecular-species-submatrix-extraction Use when a lipidomic intensity matrix needs to be reduced to the molecular-species (LMS) level before LipidOne 2.0 statistical or pathway analysis and it still contains missing or '0' entries that must be imputed per-row. The matrix already contains no missing or zero values — imputation would needlessly replace nothing or alter real measurements. The analysis targets the lipid class (LCL) or building block (LBB) level, where sub-matrix derivation follows different rules than the LMS level. Zeros represent genuine below-limit measurements the analyst wants to keep as such rather than substitute with small random values. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extracts the lipid molecular species (LMS) sub-matrix from an uploaded lipidomic data matrix and imputes missing or zero intensity values by sampling uniformly between one-twentieth and one-tenth of each row's minimum valid value, as implemented in LipidOne 2.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Extracts the lipid molecular species (LMS) sub-matrix from an uploaded lipidomic data matrix and imputes missing or zero intensity values by sampling uniformly between one-twentieth and one-tenth of each row's minimum valid value, as implemented in LipidOne 2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix already contains no missing or zero values — imputation would needlessly replace nothing or alter real measurements. The analysis targets the lipid class (LCL) or building block (LBB) level, where sub-matrix derivation follows different rules than the LMS level. Zeros represent genuine below-limit measurements the analyst wants to keep as such rather than substitute with small random values.

skills.description: Use when a molecular-species intensity matrix (row IDs like 'PC 16:0_18:1') must be converted to chain-level building-block rows for statistical or pathway analysis at the LBB level.
skills.name: molecular-species-to-chain-decomposition
skills.search_text: molecular-species-to-chain-decomposition Use when a molecular-species intensity matrix (row IDs like 'PC 16:0_18:1') must be converted to chain-level building-block rows for statistical or pathway analysis at the LBB level. The input is already a chain-level or lipid-class (LCL) sub-matrix rather than a molecular-species matrix Row identifiers lack parseable lipid class prefixes and chain annotations (e.g., trivial names or non-shorthand labels), so rows cannot be split into class + chain components http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Decomposes an LMS-level (molecular species) lipid intensity matrix into a lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix, splitting each species row into its constituent acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chains as 'pseudo-lipid' rows while conserving total signal. This supports the third structural level (classes, molecular species, building blocks) explored by LipidOne 2.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Decomposes an LMS-level (molecular species) lipid intensity matrix into a lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix, splitting each species row into its constituent acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chains as 'pseudo-lipid' rows while conserving total signal. This supports the third structural level (classes, molecular species, building blocks) explored by LipidOne 2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a chain-level or lipid-class (LCL) sub-matrix rather than a molecular-species matrix Row identifiers lack parseable lipid class prefixes and chain annotations (e.g., trivial names or non-shorthand labels), so rows cannot be split into class + chain components

skills.description: Use when a metabolomic dataset (e.g. GC-TOF-MS feature table with BinBase identifiers) contains metabolites with no known biochemical intermediates or missing KEGG annotations, producing sparse disconnected biochemical networks that need structural edges.
skills.name: molecular-structural-similarity-networking
skills.search_text: molecular-structural-similarity-networking Use when a metabolomic dataset (e.g. GC-TOF-MS feature table with BinBase identifiers) contains metabolites with no known biochemical intermediates or missing KEGG annotations, producing sparse disconnected biochemical networks that need structural edges. All analytes lack structural annotations (no translatable PubChem CID), e.g. fully unknown features — use mass spectral (cosine) similarity to relate them instead The goal is evidence of direct enzymatic transformation between metabolites — use KEGG RPAIR Biochemical Reaction Networks, since structural similarity does not imply a substrate-product relationship A precomputed structural similarity matrix already exists — recomputing fingerprints and Tanimoto scores in MetaMapR is redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Builds pathway-independent molecular networks by linking metabolites via pairwise Tanimoto similarity of PubChem Substructure Fingerprints, filling gaps between metabolites that lack direct KEGG RPAIR biochemical transformations. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Builds pathway-independent molecular networks by linking metabolites via pairwise Tanimoto similarity of PubChem Substructure Fingerprints, filling gaps between metabolites that lack direct KEGG RPAIR biochemical transformations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All analytes lack structural annotations (no translatable PubChem CID), e.g. fully unknown features — use mass spectral (cosine) similarity to relate them instead The goal is evidence of direct enzymatic transformation between metabolites — use KEGG RPAIR Biochemical Reaction Networks, since structural similarity does not imply a substrate-product relationship A precomputed structural similarity matrix already exists — recomputing fingerprints and Tanimoto scores in MetaMapR is redundant

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed low-resolution GC-EI-MS spectrum (intensity-binned, threshold-filtered, m/z ≤ 500, ≤ 300 peaks) must be translated de novo into a ranked list of candidate SMILES structures without a reference database.
skills.name: molecular-structure-candidate-ranking
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-candidate-ranking Use when a preprocessed low-resolution GC-EI-MS spectrum (intensity-binned, threshold-filtered, m/z ≤ 500, ≤ 300 peaks) must be translated de novo into a ranked list of candidate SMILES structures without a reference database. Input is an MS/MS (tandem) spectrum rather than a GC-EI-MS spectrum — the model was trained specifically on EI-MS data and comparisons in the paper note other de novo models were built for MS/MS Spectra violate model constraints (m/z > 500, more than 300 peaks, deuterium-containing compounds, expected SMILES longer than 100 characters) A rigorously curated reference library (e.g. NIST or SWGDRUG) is available and a database search would suffice — SpecTUS is aimed at novel compounds absent from spectral libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Rank candidate molecular structures for an EI-MS spectrum using SpecTUS, a transformer encoder-decoder that de novo translates GC-EI-MS spectra into SMILES and orders candidates by the model's inherent certainty, enabling annotation of compounds absent from spectral libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.05114
skills.summary: Rank candidate molecular structures for an EI-MS spectrum using SpecTUS, a transformer encoder-decoder that de novo translates GC-EI-MS spectra into SMILES and orders candidates by the model's inherent certainty, enabling annotation of compounds absent from spectral libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an MS/MS (tandem) spectrum rather than a GC-EI-MS spectrum — the model was trained specifically on EI-MS data and comparisons in the paper note other de novo models were built for MS/MS Spectra violate model constraints (m/z > 500, more than 300 peaks, deuterium-containing compounds, expected SMILES longer than 100 characters) A rigorously curated reference library (e.g. NIST or SWGDRUG) is available and a database search would suffice — SpecTUS is aimed at novel compounds absent from spectral libraries

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate that graph-neural-network-learned molecular representations (e.g., 16-dim pooled node attributes) reflect chemical structure, by visualizing their 2D UMAP embedding colored by ring number or molecular class.
skills.name: molecular-structure-clustering-visualization
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-clustering-visualization Use when you need to demonstrate that graph-neural-network-learned molecular representations (e.g., 16-dim pooled node attributes) reflect chemical structure, by visualizing their 2D UMAP embedding colored by ring number or molecular class. The model output you want to inspect is the predicted CCS value or attention/interpretation map rather than the pooled intermediate representation — use the model-agnostic interpretation method instead. Your molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, Se, since SigmaCCS cannot encode them and the ECC-layer forward pass will not be meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Extracts pooled GNN node representations from a trained model (e.g., SigmaCCS 16-dimensional molecular vectors after ECC layers and global sum pooling) and projects them to 2D with UMAP to test whether the learned embeddings are chemically meaningful, i.e., cluster by ring content, structural similarity, and molecular class. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00939-w
skills.summary: Extracts pooled GNN node representations from a trained model (e.g., SigmaCCS 16-dimensional molecular vectors after ECC layers and global sum pooling) and projects them to 2D with UMAP to test whether the learned embeddings are chemically meaningful, i.e., cluster by ring content, structural similarity, and molecular class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model output you want to inspect is the predicted CCS value or attention/interpretation map rather than the pooled intermediate representation — use the model-agnostic interpretation method instead. Your molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, Se, since SigmaCCS cannot encode them and the ECC-layer forward pass will not be meaningful.

skills.description: Use when you have tandem mass spectra (e.g., positive-mode [M+H]+) whose true structures are absent from spectral libraries and you must search them against a large molecular structure database (LMSD, PubChem, DNP).
skills.name: molecular-structure-database-search
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-database-search Use when you have tandem mass spectra (e.g., positive-mode [M+H]+) whose true structures are absent from spectral libraries and you must search them against a large molecular structure database (LMSD, PubChem, DNP). The spectrum has an exact reference in a spectral library — spectral library search is the most reliable annotation method and should be preferred You need de novo structure prediction for unknown compounds absent from any known database, due to low signal-to-noise spectra and structural complexity Molecules are very small (<400 Da) or very heavy (>1000 Da), where the model performs poorly or is computationally insufficient You need statistical significance (p-values) for non-peptidic molecules — the MCMC p-value approach exists only for peptidic molecules http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Score experimental tandem MS/MS spectra against molecular structure databases (e.g., LMSD, PubChem) using molDiscovery's probabilistic fragmentation model, then rank candidates by matching score to identify small molecules without spectral library coverage. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Score experimental tandem MS/MS spectra against molecular structure databases (e.g., LMSD, PubChem) using molDiscovery's probabilistic fragmentation model, then rank candidates by matching score to identify small molecules without spectral library coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum has an exact reference in a spectral library — spectral library search is the most reliable annotation method and should be preferred You need de novo structure prediction for unknown compounds absent from any known database, due to low signal-to-noise spectra and structural complexity Molecules are very small (<400 Da) or very heavy (>1000 Da), where the model performs poorly or is computationally insufficient You need statistical significance (p-values) for non-peptidic molecules — the MCMC p-value approach exists only for peptidic molecules

skills.description: Use when a per-MZ-position peak classifier built on 2D-only molecular embeddings (mol2vec or graph features) underperforms and you want to test whether 3D conformer-derived structure features lift per-bin F1.
skills.name: molecular-structure-feature-augmentation
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-feature-augmentation Use when a per-MZ-position peak classifier built on 2D-only molecular embeddings (mol2vec or graph features) underperforms and you want to test whether 3D conformer-derived structure features lift per-bin F1. Your goal is full-spectrum intensity regression rather than per-fragment peak-presence classification — SingleFrag deliberately focuses on presence/absence per peak, not intensities. Your molecules cannot be embedded into 3D conformations (e.g., unsupported atom types or >300 atoms), which is outside 3DMolMS's supported input space. You only need annotation of experimental spectra against an existing library, not improved in silico fragment prediction models. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Augments existing molecular input representations (e.g., 300-dim mol2vec embeddings or molecular graphs) with 3D atom-location structural features derived from computed conformers, as used by 3DMolMS, to improve per-fragment MS/MS peak-presence classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Augments existing molecular input representations (e.g., 300-dim mol2vec embeddings or molecular graphs) with 3D atom-location structural features derived from computed conformers, as used by 3DMolMS, to improve per-fragment MS/MS peak-presence classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is full-spectrum intensity regression rather than per-fragment peak-presence classification — SingleFrag deliberately focuses on presence/absence per peak, not intensities. Your molecules cannot be embedded into 3D conformations (e.g., unsupported atom types or >300 atoms), which is outside 3DMolMS's supported input space. You only need annotation of experimental spectra against an existing library, not improved in silico fragment prediction models.

skills.description: Use when preparing large molecular structure databases (SDF/SMILES) as inputs for in-silico EI-MS spectrum prediction, and unreasonable molecules (heavy, exotic-element, ionic, high-LogP, or duplicate structures) must be excluded first.
skills.name: molecular-structure-filtering-by-mass-and-elements
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-filtering-by-mass-and-elements Use when preparing large molecular structure databases (SDF/SMILES) as inputs for in-silico EI-MS spectrum prediction, and unreasonable molecules (heavy, exotic-element, ionic, high-LogP, or duplicate structures) must be excluded first. When the target structures fall outside GC-MS scope, e.g. metal-organics or molecules with elements beyond H, C, O, N, P, S, Cl, F, Br, I, Si — rule (2) will wrongly exclude them by design. When you need the raw, unfiltered NIST/ChEMBL/HMDB contents for library building or benchmarking without the five-rule preprocessing. When ionic compounds, salts, or molecules over 1000 Da are explicitly of analytical interest — all are deliberately excluded by this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Applies five filter rules (mass < 1000 Da, 11 allowed elements, no ionic compounds, LogP -12 to 24, within- and cross-dataset deduplication) with RDKit to convert NIST 2017, ChEMBL 28, and HMDB 5.0 into the f-NIST, f-ChEMBL, and f-HMDB molecule sets used to build the million-scale in-silico EI-MS library. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Applies five filter rules (mass < 1000 Da, 11 allowed elements, no ionic compounds, LogP -12 to 24, within- and cross-dataset deduplication) with RDKit to convert NIST 2017, ChEMBL 28, and HMDB 5.0 into the f-NIST, f-ChEMBL, and f-HMDB molecule sets used to build the million-scale in-silico EI-MS library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target structures fall outside GC-MS scope, e.g. metal-organics or molecules with elements beyond H, C, O, N, P, S, Cl, F, Br, I, Si — rule (2) will wrongly exclude them by design. When you need the raw, unfiltered NIST/ChEMBL/HMDB contents for library building or benchmarking without the five-rule preprocessing. When ionic compounds, salts, or molecules over 1000 Da are explicitly of analytical interest — all are deliberately excluded by this skill.

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether per-compound spectral prediction accuracy depends on how structurally similar each test compound is to the training set, e.g. via maximum Bulk Tanimoto similarity on RDKit fingerprints.
skills.name: molecular-structure-fingerprinting
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-fingerprinting Use when you need to test whether per-compound spectral prediction accuracy depends on how structurally similar each test compound is to the training set, e.g. via maximum Bulk Tanimoto similarity on RDKit fingerprints. Input is already a feature/embedding table (e.g. 3DMolMS molecular embeddings from molnet_engine.save_features()) rather than raw structures needing fingerprint-based similarity The question is cross-instrument generalization after fine-tuning on a small set of spectra, not the dependence of accuracy on training-set chemical similarity Compounds contain atom types outside the supported set (C, O, N, H, P, S, F, Cl, B, Br, I) or exceed 300 atoms, so RDKit-fingerprintable structures cannot be assumed comparable Computes structural (chemical) similarity between test and training compounds using RDKit fingerprints and Bulk Tanimoto scores, then correlates per-compound 3DMolMS MS/MS prediction accuracy (cosine similarity) with maximum training-set similarity (Supplementary Fig. S3 of the qtof evaluation). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad354
skills.summary: Computes structural (chemical) similarity between test and training compounds using RDKit fingerprints and Bulk Tanimoto scores, then correlates per-compound 3DMolMS MS/MS prediction accuracy (cosine similarity) with maximum training-set similarity (Supplementary Fig. S3 of the qtof evaluation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/embedding table (e.g. 3DMolMS molecular embeddings from molnet_engine.save_features()) rather than raw structures needing fingerprint-based similarity The question is cross-instrument generalization after fine-tuning on a small set of spectra, not the dependence of accuracy on training-set chemical similarity Compounds contain atom types outside the supported set (C, O, N, H, P, S, F, Cl, B, Br, I) or exceed 300 atoms, so RDKit-fingerprintable structures cannot be assumed comparable

skills.description: Use when you need de novo small-molecule structure candidates from unannotated tandem mass spectra, conditioned on chemical formula metadata, without a reference spectral library — e.g. MassSpecGym or NPLIB1-style test folds.
skills.name: molecular-structure-generation-from-spectra
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-generation-from-spectra Use when you need de novo small-molecule structure candidates from unannotated tandem mass spectra, conditioned on chemical formula metadata, without a reference spectral library — e.g. MassSpecGym or NPLIB1-style test folds. When a reference spectral library exists and library-search retrieval is sufficient (retrieval-based pipelines are cheaper and more reliable for known compounds) When the adduct is not [M+H]+ (e.g. [M+Na]+) — the model was fine-tuned and aligned only on the dominant [M+H]+ data When exact structure is required without candidate re-ranking — molecular hallucination remains possible and Top-1 accuracy on MassSpecGym is still below diffusion baselines for some metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate candidate molecular structures from MS/MS spectra by representing each spectrum as a tokenized Morgan fingerprint intermediate, using a finetuned BART language model (MS-BART) for fingerprint-to-SELFIES translation, and re-ranking beam candidates against predicted fingerprints — the paper's fastest de novo elucidation approach (~3 s/spectrum vs ~160 s for diffusion). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Generate candidate molecular structures from MS/MS spectra by representing each spectrum as a tokenized Morgan fingerprint intermediate, using a finetuned BART language model (MS-BART) for fingerprint-to-SELFIES translation, and re-ranking beam candidates against predicted fingerprints — the paper's fastest de novo elucidation approach (~3 s/spectrum vs ~160 s for diffusion).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a reference spectral library exists and library-search retrieval is sufficient (retrieval-based pipelines are cheaper and more reliable for known compounds) When the adduct is not [M+H]+ (e.g. [M+Na]+) — the model was fine-tuned and aligned only on the dominant [M+H]+ data When exact structure is required without candidate re-ranking — molecular hallucination remains possible and Top-1 accuracy on MassSpecGym is still below diffusion baselines for some metrics

skills.description: Use when you have four MS/MS spectra files ([M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE) with spectra embeddings and need de-novo SMILES structures reconstructed by a pre-trained decoder.
skills.name: molecular-structure-representation-translation
skills.search_text: molecular-structure-representation-translation Use when you have four MS/MS spectra files ([M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE) with spectra embeddings and need de-novo SMILES structures reconstructed by a pre-trained decoder. Input is a single spectrum CSV or spectra in other precursor/energy conditions than [M+H]+/[M-H]- at 35% or 130% NCE — the decoder expects the four specific input spectra files You only need spectra embeddings (encoder output) without molecular structure prediction — use the encoder filter stage instead SMILES structures already exist and you only need to compare against known reference structures rather than generate de-novo molecules http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Decodes spectra embeddings produced by the Spec2Mol encoder into candidate SMILES strings of molecular structures using a decoder pre-trained on a massive corpus of chemical structures, with RDKit validation of the reconstructed molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00932-3
skills.summary: Decodes spectra embeddings produced by the Spec2Mol encoder into candidate SMILES strings of molecular structures using a decoder pre-trained on a massive corpus of chemical structures, with RDKit validation of the reconstructed molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single spectrum CSV or spectra in other precursor/energy conditions than [M+H]+/[M-H]- at 35% or 130% NCE — the decoder expects the four specific input spectra files You only need spectra embeddings (encoder output) without molecular structure prediction — use the encoder filter stage instead SMILES structures already exist and you only need to compare against known reference structures rather than generate de-novo molecules

skills.description: Use when you have generated candidate molecules (2D topology from a diffusion or generative model) paired with known reference structures and need to quantify exact-match and similarity-based elucidation accuracy.
skills.name: molecular-topology-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: molecular-topology-accuracy-evaluation Use when you have generated candidate molecules (2D topology from a diffusion or generative model) paired with known reference structures and need to quantify exact-match and similarity-based elucidation accuracy. When the goal is 3D conformational fidelity rather than 2D topology — use RMSD-based evaluation (eval_sampled_mols/rmsd.py) instead. When evaluating unconditional generation quality (validity, uniqueness, novelty) rather than recovering a specific target molecule from spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates whether spectra-conditioned diffusion samples (e.g., DiffSpectra on QM9S) reproduce the ground-truth molecule's atom types and bond types, reporting top-1/top-10 accuracy plus similarity metrics such as MCES. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Evaluates whether spectra-conditioned diffusion samples (e.g., DiffSpectra on QM9S) reproduce the ground-truth molecule's atom types and bond types, reporting top-1/top-10 accuracy plus similarity metrics such as MCES.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is 3D conformational fidelity rather than 2D topology — use RMSD-based evaluation (eval_sampled_mols/rmsd.py) instead. When evaluating unconditional generation quality (validity, uniqueness, novelty) rather than recovering a specific target molecule from spectra.

skills.description: Use when a sum-normalized FT-ICR MS peak table with assigned molecular formulas must be summarized as per-sample functional diversity (Rao's Q) grouped by experimental conditions such as phage treatment or incubation condition.
skills.name: molecular-trait-functional-diversity-calculation
skills.search_text: molecular-trait-functional-diversity-calculation Use when a sum-normalized FT-ICR MS peak table with assigned molecular formulas must be summarized as per-sample functional diversity (Rao's Q) grouped by experimental conditions such as phage treatment or incubation condition. The input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra that has not yet undergone molecular formula assignment — MetaboDirect accepts peak abundance and formula data only after initial processing The peak table has not been normalized — run the test_normalization/SPANS companion script first to select the best normalization method The goal is taxonomic or sequence-based diversity rather than molecular-trait-based chemodiversity of metabolomic peaks Computes functional (trait-based) chemodiversity from FT-ICR MS metabolomic data by deriving molecular-level trait vectors from assigned elemental formulas (elemental ratios, double-bond equivalents/AI_mod aromaticity, reactivity proxies) and calculating Rao's quadratic entropy per sample, alongside abundance-based indices (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1), in the MetaboDirect pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Computes functional (trait-based) chemodiversity from FT-ICR MS metabolomic data by deriving molecular-level trait vectors from assigned elemental formulas (elemental ratios, double-bond equivalents/AI_mod aromaticity, reactivity proxies) and calculating Rao's quadratic entropy per sample, alongside abundance-based indices (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1), in the MetaboDirect pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra that has not yet undergone molecular formula assignment — MetaboDirect accepts peak abundance and formula data only after initial processing The peak table has not been normalized — run the test_normalization/SPANS companion script first to select the best normalization method The goal is taxonomic or sequence-based diversity rather than molecular-trait-based chemodiversity of metabolomic peaks

skills.description: Use when a GNPS-format mass spectral dataset (MGF/mzXML/mzML) has been searched with VInSMoC variable mode and the goal is to explain precursor-vs-molecule mass differences as known chemical mass shifts and quantify FDR across score thresholds.
skills.name: molecular-variant-mass-shift-annotation
skills.search_text: molecular-variant-mass-shift-annotation Use when a GNPS-format mass spectral dataset (MGF/mzXML/mzML) has been searched with VInSMoC variable mode and the goal is to explain precursor-vs-molecule mass differences as known chemical mass shifts and quantify FDR across score thresholds. When only exact-match identifications of known molecules are needed — use VInSMoC exact mode, which matches spectra to molecules whose masses match the precursor m/z rather than explaining a mass difference When the input spectra have already been pre-processed locally — the README says advanced preprocessing settings 'should be left unchanged unless you have already down some preprocessing on your input spectra before uploading to our server' When the analysis requires biosynthesis pathway reconstruction (e.g. promothiocin B / depsidomycin in Streptomyces) rather than mass-shift annotation of variable-mode hits http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Run VInSMoC in variable mode against a chemical database (e.g. COCONUT) on the run.npanalysis.org server, collect the mass difference between each hit and its parent molecule, and interpret high-frequency shifts as known chemical transformations (oxidation +15.9949 Da, methylation +14.0157 Da, deoxygenation -15.9949 Da) while sweeping score/P-value cutoffs to build false discovery rate curves. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Run VInSMoC in variable mode against a chemical database (e.g. COCONUT) on the run.npanalysis.org server, collect the mass difference between each hit and its parent molecule, and interpret high-frequency shifts as known chemical transformations (oxidation +15.9949 Da, methylation +14.0157 Da, deoxygenation -15.9949 Da) while sweeping score/P-value cutoffs to build false discovery rate curves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only exact-match identifications of known molecules are needed — use VInSMoC exact mode, which matches spectra to molecules whose masses match the precursor m/z rather than explaining a mass difference When the input spectra have already been pre-processed locally — the README says advanced preprocessing settings 'should be left unchanged unless you have already down some preprocessing on your input spectra before uploading to our server' When the analysis requires biosynthesis pathway reconstruction (e.g. promothiocin B / depsidomycin in Streptomyces) rather than mass-shift annotation of variable-mode hits

skills.description: Use when you must decide whether pathway transformation before multi-omics integration (ssPA + MB-PLS) degrades predictive performance relative to modelling raw molecule abundances, e.g. on COPDgene plasma metabolomics/proteomics/transcriptomics.
skills.name: molecular-vs-pathway-level-model-comparison
skills.search_text: molecular-vs-pathway-level-model-comparison Use when you must decide whether pathway transformation before multi-omics integration (ssPA + MB-PLS) degrades predictive performance relative to modelling raw molecule abundances, e.g. on COPDgene plasma metabolomics/proteomics/transcriptomics. Samples from individuals without data on all omics views are present — PathIntegrate requires all input omics measured on the same individuals and discards incomplete samples, so the comparison cannot be run fairly The goal is pathway-level interpretation of associated biological processes rather than an explicit predictive-performance comparison of the two modelling levels The question calls for comparison against conventional pathway analysis (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) — the authors state no direct comparison to these was performed as it was beyond the scope of the work A benchmarking skill for quantifying whether pathway-based multi-omics modelling (ssPA-transformed MB-PLS in PathIntegrate Multi-View) trades off predictive performance against a molecular-level MB-PLS model fitted on raw molecule abundances, using COPDgene plasma multi-omics as the reference experiment. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for quantifying whether pathway-based multi-omics modelling (ssPA-transformed MB-PLS in PathIntegrate Multi-View) trades off predictive performance against a molecular-level MB-PLS model fitted on raw molecule abundances, using COPDgene plasma multi-omics as the reference experiment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples from individuals without data on all omics views are present — PathIntegrate requires all input omics measured on the same individuals and discards incomplete samples, so the comparison cannot be run fairly The goal is pathway-level interpretation of associated biological processes rather than an explicit predictive-performance comparison of the two modelling levels The question calls for comparison against conventional pathway analysis (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) — the authors state no direct comparison to these was performed as it was beyond the scope of the work

skills.description: Use when a chemical list is about to be processed with fragment- or descriptor-based QSAR models (e.g., IFS biotransformation half-life prediction) and must first be screened for metals or MW > 1,000.
skills.name: molecular-weight-and-metal-atom-filtering
skills.search_text: molecular-weight-and-metal-atom-filtering Use when a chemical list is about to be processed with fragment- or descriptor-based QSAR models (e.g., IFS biotransformation half-life prediction) and must first be screened for metals or MW > 1,000. The downstream QSAR model handles metal-containing or very large (MW > 1,000) molecules, so removing them would needlessly shrink coverage The goal is exposure or toxicity prioritization (e.g., SEEM/TEST/ToxPi ranking) rather than biotransformation half-life prediction — the filter is specific to the IFS applicability domain Input chemicals lack structures or molecular formulas, so metal content and molecular weight cannot be determined http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0209 Pre-filters chemical inventories by excluding compounds containing a metal atom or exceeding a molecular weight of 1,000 before running the Iterative Fragment Selection (IFS) QSAR for biotransformation half-life (HLB) prediction, since the IFS approach cannot handle such structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Pre-filters chemical inventories by excluding compounds containing a metal atom or exceeding a molecular weight of 1,000 before running the Iterative Fragment Selection (IFS) QSAR for biotransformation half-life (HLB) prediction, since the IFS approach cannot handle such structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream QSAR model handles metal-containing or very large (MW > 1,000) molecules, so removing them would needlessly shrink coverage The goal is exposure or toxicity prioritization (e.g., SEEM/TEST/ToxPi ranking) rather than biotransformation half-life prediction — the filter is specific to the IFS applicability domain Input chemicals lack structures or molecular formulas, so metal content and molecular weight cannot be determined

skills.description: Reference for building the seven one-dimensional feature vectors that Mol2CCS feeds alongside the 3-D molecular graph, when SMILES, adduct and instrument metadata are available per record.
skills.name: molecular-weight-descriptor-calculation
skills.search_text: molecular-weight-descriptor-calculation Reference for building the seven one-dimensional feature vectors that Mol2CCS feeds alongside the 3-D molecular graph, when SMILES, adduct and instrument metadata are available per record. The downstream model is vanilla SigmaCCS or GraphCCS, which consumes only the molecular graph and adduct — the extra 1-D features are an Mol2CCS extension and are ignored by those architectures. Input records lack instrument type or molecule-type metadata, so the one-hot encodings and monomer/dimer flag cannot be populated without imputation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Computes molecular weight and related 1-D molecular descriptors (e.g. 35-dimensional Drug Tax structural class counts, one-hot adduct/instrument/type encodings) from SMILES with RDKit, producing the flat feature vector Mol2CCS concatenates with the molecular graph and Morgan fingerprint for CCS prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: Computes molecular weight and related 1-D molecular descriptors (e.g. 35-dimensional Drug Tax structural class counts, one-hot adduct/instrument/type encodings) from SMILES with RDKit, producing the flat feature vector Mol2CCS concatenates with the molecular graph and Morgan fingerprint for CCS prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream model is vanilla SigmaCCS or GraphCCS, which consumes only the molecular graph and adduct — the extra 1-D features are an Mol2CCS extension and are ignored by those architectures. Input records lack instrument type or molecule-type metadata, so the one-hot encodings and monomer/dimer flag cannot be populated without imputation.

skills.description: Reference for quantifying whether two molecular benchmark sets differ in structural complexity via the Ertl-Schuffenhauer synthetic accessibility score and molecular weight.
skills.name: molecular-weight-descriptor-calculation
skills.search_text: molecular-weight-descriptor-calculation Reference for quantifying whether two molecular benchmark sets differ in structural complexity via the Ertl-Schuffenhauer synthetic accessibility score and molecular weight. When you need fragmentation-aware or spectral descriptors (e.g. predicted mass spectra, fragmentation graphs) rather than simple molecular complexity metrics — use ICEBERG or SCARF instead. When the dataset is not one of NPLIB1/NIST20 (or a similar SMILES-labeled benchmark) and the goal is only retrieval or elucidation accuracy, not complexity comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute synthetic accessibility (SA) scores and molecular weights for molecules across two datasets (e.g. NPLIB1 vs NIST20) to quantify dataset-level molecular complexity and explain performance differences between spectrum prediction approaches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Compute synthetic accessibility (SA) scores and molecular weights for molecules across two datasets (e.g. NPLIB1 vs NIST20) to quantify dataset-level molecular complexity and explain performance differences between spectrum prediction approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need fragmentation-aware or spectral descriptors (e.g. predicted mass spectra, fragmentation graphs) rather than simple molecular complexity metrics — use ICEBERG or SCARF instead. When the dataset is not one of NPLIB1/NIST20 (or a similar SMILES-labeled benchmark) and the goal is only retrieval or elucidation accuracy, not complexity comparison.

skills.description: Use when a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (normal or multiplicity-edited) must yield a predicted molecular weight via DeepSAT's pretrained CNN regression head, and the result must be validated against the paper's R-squared benchmarks.
skills.name: molecular-weight-regression-scoring
skills.search_text: molecular-weight-regression-scoring Use when a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (normal or multiplicity-edited) must yield a predicted molecular weight via DeepSAT's pretrained CNN regression head, and the result must be validated against the paper's R-squared benchmarks. The input is not a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (e.g., MS/MS fragmentation spectra, 1D proton/carbon NMR) — DeepSAT consumes only HSQC data The goal is compound class or fingerprint prediction scoring (use class-accuracy or cosine-similarity skills) rather than molecular weight regression No trained model weights or matching TensorFlow Serving model metadata are available; the README warns that model input names must match between the serving endpoint and the code http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Runs DeepSAT's multi-task CNN molecular weight regression head on 1H-13C HSQC spectra (128x128x1 normal or 128x128x2 multiplicity-edited tensors) and scores predictions with mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and R-squared against reported values (R² = 0.9183 normal / 0.9336 edited). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Runs DeepSAT's multi-task CNN molecular weight regression head on 1H-13C HSQC spectra (128x128x1 normal or 128x128x2 multiplicity-edited tensors) and scores predictions with mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and R-squared against reported values (R² = 0.9183 normal / 0.9336 edited).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (e.g., MS/MS fragmentation spectra, 1D proton/carbon NMR) — DeepSAT consumes only HSQC data The goal is compound class or fingerprint prediction scoring (use class-accuracy or cosine-similarity skills) rather than molecular weight regression No trained model weights or matching TensorFlow Serving model metadata are available; the README warns that model input names must match between the serving endpoint and the code

skills.description: Use when a generative model (e.g. DiffMS's graph diffusion decoder) outputs many sampled molecular structures per mass spectrum and you need a deterministic ranked candidate list for top-k (k=1,10) elucidation evaluation.
skills.name: molecule-frequency-ranking
skills.search_text: molecule-frequency-ranking Use when a generative model (e.g. DiffMS's graph diffusion decoder) outputs many sampled molecular structures per mass spectrum and you need a deterministic ranked candidate list for top-k (k=1,10) elucidation evaluation. When ranking an MSNovelist baseline, whose candidates are instead produced by beam search with width 100 and ranked by computed log-likelihoods rather than generation frequency When only a single generated structure per spectrum exists (frequency counting is meaningless without repeated samples) http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Post-processing filter for diffusion-based de novo structure generation: validate sampled molecules with RDKit, drop invalid/disconnected structures, rank distinct candidates by generation frequency per spectrum, and select the top-k to form the per-spectrum candidate pool. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Post-processing filter for diffusion-based de novo structure generation: validate sampled molecules with RDKit, drop invalid/disconnected structures, rank distinct candidates by generation frequency per spectrum, and select the top-k to form the per-spectrum candidate pool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ranking an MSNovelist baseline, whose candidates are instead produced by beam search with width 100 and ranked by computed log-likelihoods rather than generation frequency When only a single generated structure per spectrum exists (frequency counting is meaningless without repeated samples)

skills.description: Use when binary presence/absence GCF and ion tables from 363 strains have been correlated and you must validate that known molecule–GCF pairs (e.g. 9 detoxin/rimosamide-type pairs) rank in the rightmost tail, or choose between BiG-SCAPE mode/cutoff settings.
skills.name: molecule-gcf-pair-tail-validation
skills.search_text: molecule-gcf-pair-tail-validation Use when binary presence/absence GCF and ion tables from 363 strains have been correlated and you must validate that known molecule–GCF pairs (e.g. 9 detoxin/rimosamide-type pairs) rank in the rightmost tail, or choose between BiG-SCAPE mode/cutoff settings. The ion identity table has not been built yet — ions must already satisfy mass within 4 ppm and fragmentation cosine similarity above 0.75 before correlating A GCF of interest has representative gene clusters in only a single strain — such GCFs were not considered correlatable and cannot be tail-validated The goal is de novo molecule-GCF linking without any known pairs to anchor tail validation — molecular network family identification in this study was performed manually against known detoxins and rimosamides, not automatically inferred http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validates metabologenomic correlation output by checking whether known molecule–GCF pairs fall in the rightmost tail of the binary correlation score distribution, and selects the BiG-SCAPE alignment mode/cutoff combination (glocal, 0.30) that best recovers these known connections. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9

skills.description: Use when molecular abundance matrices (e.g. metabolite names, ChEBI, UniProt or ENSEMBL columns) must be converted to the identifier vocabulary of a pathway database (Reactome, KEGG, PathBank) before ssPA scoring or any pathway-based multi-omics integration.

skills.search_text: molecule-identifier-mapping-to-pathway-databases Use when molecular abundance matrices (e.g. metabolite names, ChEBI, UniProt or ENSEMBL columns) must be converted to the identifier vocabulary of a pathway database (Reactome, KEGG, PathBank) before ssPA scoring or any pathway-based multi-omics integration. The abundance matrix columns already carry the database's own identifiers (e.g. ChEBI columns for Reactome) — mapping is unnecessary and re-running it risks losing valid IDs. The analysis does not require pathway transformation, e.g. purely molecular-level modelling or ORA/GSEA workflows that take a differential-abundance list and can accept the original IDs. The molecule cannot be annotated to any pathway in the database — un-annotated molecules cannot be incorporated into pathway-based models and will be dropped, so an alternative non-pathway approach is preferable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Harmonise metabolite and protein identifiers (metabolite names, KEGG compounds, ChEBI, UniProt, ENSEMBL) so each molecular abundance matrix matches the ID scheme of the chosen pathway database (Reactome/PathBank use ChEBI + UniProt; KEGG uses KEGG compound/gene IDs), a prerequisite for pathway transformation in PathIntegrate. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Harmonise metabolite and protein identifiers (metabolite names, KEGG compounds, ChEBI, UniProt, ENSEMBL) so each molecular abundance matrix matches the ID scheme of the chosen pathway database (Reactome/PathBank use ChEBI + UniProt; KEGG uses KEGG compound/gene IDs), a prerequisite for pathway transformation in PathIntegrate.

skills.name: molecule-structure-decoding-selfies
skills.search_text: molecule-structure-decoding-selfies Use when a generative model outputs molecule representations as SELFIES token sequences (possibly beam-sampled) and you must convert them to valid SMILES, then score Top-1/Top-10 accuracy by InChIKey, minimum MCES distance, and maximum Tanimoto similarity. Only spectrum-level metadata (e.g., formula, adduct) needs to be predicted without generating any molecular structure candidates — this skill presupposes a generative molecule decoder. Evaluating retrieval-based methods that return database compounds directly rather than de novo generated token sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Decode generated molecular SELFIES token sequences into SMILES molecules and compute identity and structural similarity metrics (exact InChIKey match, MCES distance, Tanimoto similarity) using RDKit, as done in MS-BART for evaluating structure elucidation from mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Decode generated molecular SELFIES token sequences into SMILES molecules and compute identity and structural similarity metrics (exact InChIKey match, MCES distance, Tanimoto similarity) using RDKit, as done in MS-BART for evaluating structure elucidation from mass spectra.

When the goal is similarity rather than exact substructure search — COCONUT handles that separately with an LSH-based similarity search in MongoDB and should not reuse the $allBitsSet screen. When a dedicated cheminformatics search engine (e.g. a cartridge with native substructure indexing) is available; the MongoDB $allBitsSet screen is a workaround for chemical search being uncommon with MongoDB. skills.search_text: mongodb-reaction-network-querying Reference for practitioners whose Pickaxe network-expansion run has written results into a MongoDB collection and who need to load, query, or iterate those reactions/compounds in Python for downstream analysis or filtering. Run output was written to .tsv files only — parse those directly instead of standing up a MongoDB instance. You need only a single-generation, small network where an in-memory list of reactions from a Pickaxe script would be simpler than a database round-trip. The downstream task is rule construction or starting-compound selection, which occurs before any results exist in the database. http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Store and query Pickaxe-generated novel compounds and reactions in a MongoDB instance via PyMongo, enabling downstream filtering and analysis workflows (e.g. metabolomics-peak annotation, target-compound expansion) that read generation results back from a persistent database. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05149-8
skills.summary: Store and query Pickaxe-generated novel compounds and reactions in a MongoDB instance via PyMongo, enabling downstream filtering and analysis workflows (e.g. metabolomics-peak annotation, target-compound expansion) that read generation results back from a persistent database.

The downstream task is rule construction or starting-compound selection, which occurs before any results exist in the database.

skills.search_text: monoisotopic-basepeak-assignment Use when an XCMS-derived feature table already contains putatively labeled features (PuInc_seeker output) and each labeled feature needs a monoisotopic base peak assigned before adduct/database queries. Upstream PuInc_seeker has not been run — basepeak_finder requires the PuIncR object with flagged labeled features, not a raw XCMS peak table The goal is de novo isotope annotation from theoretical mass differences over all MS signals rather than comparing unlabeled vs labeled biologically equivalent samples (geoRge's design premise) Data were not processed by XCMS, since geoRge 'runs on the output structure of the XCMS package' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 geoRge's basepeak_finder step matches each putatively labeled feature (from PuInc_seeker output) to its monoisotopic base peak in the XCMS feature set, using the exact masses of the unlabeled (12.0) and labeled (13.003355) atoms and a ppm tolerance, enabling isotope-envelope annotation in untargeted LC/MS stable-isotope-labeling experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628

skills.description: Use when you need theoretical monoisotopic masses or isotope distributions (M, M+1, M+2) for element-count molecular formulas (e.g., C3H8O2) in MS method development or adduct m/z prediction.
skills.name: monoisotopic-exact-mass-calculation
skills.search_text: monoisotopic-exact-mass-calculation Use when you need theoretical monoisotopic masses or isotope distributions (M, M+1, M+2) for element-count molecular formulas (e.g., C3H8O2) in MS method development or adduct m/z prediction. Input is raw MS data (MZA/HDF5 spectra) needing extraction or peak finding rather than theoretical isotope calculations Formulas require full isotope envelopes beyond M+2 or isotope-resolved simulation of complex mixtures, since predict_m_m1_m2 covers only M, M+1, M+2 The input already contains measured monoisotopic masses (e.g., PrecursorMonoisotopicMz from MZA metadata) that need no theoretical prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Compute monoisotopic exact masses and M/M+1/M+2 isotopologue masses and abundances for molecular formulas using mzapy.isotopes, which bases its calculations on a most-abundant-isotope exact-mass element table sourced from unimod.org. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c01653
skills.summary: Compute monoisotopic exact masses and M/M+1/M+2 isotopologue masses and abundances for molecular formulas using mzapy.isotopes, which bases its calculations on a most-abundant-isotope exact-mass element table sourced from unimod.org.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS data (MZA/HDF5 spectra) needing extraction or peak finding rather than theoretical isotope calculations Formulas require full isotope envelopes beyond M+2 or isotope-resolved simulation of complex mixtures, since predict_m_m1_m2 covers only M, M+1, M+2 The input already contains measured monoisotopic masses (e.g., PrecursorMonoisotopicMz from MZA metadata) that need no theoretical prediction

skills.description: Use when enumerating formula candidates from elemental compositions (e.g., a 16-element ECS of C, H, As, B, Br, Cl, F, I, K, N, Na, O, P, S, Se, Si) and monoisotopic masses must be recorded per candidate to build or reuse an IPDB for LC/HRMS formula annotation.

skills.search_text: monoisotopic-mass-calculation Use when enumerating formula candidates from elemental compositions (e.g., a 16-element ECS of C, H, As, B, Br, Cl, F, I, K, N, Na, O, P, S, Se, Si) and monoisotopic masses must be recorded per candidate to build or reuse an IPDB for LC/HRMS formula annotation. Input is raw LC/HRMS data (mzXML/mzML/netCDF) that has not been peak-picked — IDSL.IPA must first extract peaks; this skill assumes peaklists exist. A pre-calculated IPDB already covers the chemical space (e.g., RefMetDB positive/negative-mode IPDBs from Zenodo) — reload it via PARAM0004 instead of re-enumerating formulas and recomputing masses. The target chemical space requires elements outside the ECS element list (e.g., metals outside K/Na) — the enumeration and mass tables do not cover them. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Computes exact monoisotopic masses (and records element counts) for enumerated molecular formula candidates over a defined elemental chemical space (ECS), so that candidates can feed theoretical isotopic-profile database (IPDB) generation and MS1 matching in IDSL.UFA. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00563
skills.summary: Computes exact monoisotopic masses (and records element counts) for enumerated molecular formula candidates over a defined elemental chemical space (ECS), so that candidates can feed theoretical isotopic-profile database (IPDB) generation and MS1 matching in IDSL.UFA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC/HRMS data (mzXML/mzML/netCDF) that has not been peak-picked — IDSL.IPA must first extract peaks; this skill assumes peaklists exist. A pre-calculated IPDB already covers the chemical space (e.g., RefMetDB positive/negative-mode IPDBs from Zenodo) — reload it via PARAM0004 instead of re-enumerating formulas and recomputing masses. The target chemical space requires elements outside the ECS element list (e.g., metals outside K/Na) — the enumeration and mass tables do not cover them.

skills.description: Use when a fragment set from a bond-breaking DAG must be converted to predicted peak masses — enumerate formulae {f_n^{-j},...,f_n^{j}} per fragment and compute exact monoisotopic masses for spectrum construction or formula annotation.

skills.search_text: monoisotopic-mass-calculation Use when a fragment set from a bond-breaking DAG must be converted to predicted peak masses — enumerate formulae {f_n^{-j},...,f_n^{j}} per fragment and compute exact monoisotopic masses for spectrum construction or formula annotation. The candidate formulae do not originate from a bond-breaking fragment DAG — e.g. GrAFF-MS instead selects the top 10,000 product and neutral loss formulae by total intensity across the dataset. The task is fragment identity prediction or peak explanation for chemistry outside the model's scope (e.g. cyclizations), where unexplained OS peaks arise that the mass set cannot account for. The analysis targets glycan or peptide spectra, which the paper explicitly excluded from its formula annotation analysis to focus on small molecules. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Compute monoisotopic masses for fragment formulae (and hydrogen-tolerant formula variants) generated by combinatorial bond breaking, so that predicted fragment distributions can be converted into an MS/MS spectrum by matching formula masses to peak m/z values. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2404.02360
skills.summary: Compute monoisotopic masses for fragment formulae (and hydrogen-tolerant formula variants) generated by combinatorial bond breaking, so that predicted fragment distributions can be converted into an MS/MS spectrum by matching formula masses to peak m/z values.
