The task is fragment identity prediction or peak explanation for chemistry outside the model's scope (e.g. cyclizations), where unexplained OS peaks arise that the mass set cannot account for. The analysis targets glycan or peptide spectra, which the paper explicitly excluded from its formula annotation analysis to focus on small molecules.

skills.description: Use when you need theoretical monoisotopic masses for B/Y/internal glycan fragments of a new N-linked glycan not already in a database, to support MS1/MS2 peak identification from LC-MS/MS data.
skills.name: monoisotopic-mass-calculation
skills.search_text: monoisotopic-mass-calculation Use when you need theoretical monoisotopic masses for B/Y/internal glycan fragments of a new N-linked glycan not already in a database, to support MS1/MS2 peak identification from LC-MS/MS data. The glycan is an O-linked glycan — the app's scope is explicitly limited to N-linked glycans The glycan is already present in the MS1/MS2 databases — the Fragment Generator is intended for new glycans not already located in the database A de novo glycan identification from spectra is required — the app explicitly lacks de novo identification capability and relies on database masses http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes theoretical monoisotopic fragment masses for glycan structures by summing residue masses from a monosaccharide mass table (e.g. Hex 180.0634, HexNAc 221.0899, Fuc 164.0685) with terminal-group corrections, as implemented in the GlyKAn AZ Fragment Generator for expanding glycan databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Computes theoretical monoisotopic fragment masses for glycan structures by summing residue masses from a monosaccharide mass table (e.g. Hex 180.0634, HexNAc 221.0899, Fuc 164.0685) with terminal-group corrections, as implemented in the GlyKAn AZ Fragment Generator for expanding glycan databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The glycan is an O-linked glycan — the app's scope is explicitly limited to N-linked glycans The glycan is already present in the MS1/MS2 databases — the Fragment Generator is intended for new glycans not already located in the database A de novo glycan identification from spectra is required — the app explicitly lacks de novo identification capability and relies on database masses

skills.description: Use when a differential MS1 feature table contains dysregulated m/z peaks, no reference-standard spectra are available, and a library of parent structures plus biotransformation reaction rules can be exploited to compute theoretical candidate masses for preannotation.
skills.name: monoisotopic-mass-computation-for-metabolites
skills.search_text: monoisotopic-mass-computation-for-metabolites Use when a differential MS1 feature table contains dysregulated m/z peaks, no reference-standard spectra are available, and a library of parent structures plus biotransformation reaction rules can be exploited to compute theoretical candidate masses for preannotation. MS2 spectra match a reference library or authentic standard is available — traditional bottom-up library-based annotation is more direct and should be preferred No reaction rules or parent structures exist for the analyte class, so theoretical monoisotopic masses cannot be enumerated The feature table has not been filtered for dysregulated features (no DMS layer), making an omics-scale candidate-vs-feature cross-reference uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Enumerates theoretical biotransformed metabolites by applying reaction rules in silico to parent xenobiotics (here 1,021 pesticides), computes their monoisotopic m/z values to form a pseudo-MS1 candidature space, and preannotates them against dysregulated MS1 features by accurate-mass matching at ≤ 5 ppm. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: Enumerates theoretical biotransformed metabolites by applying reaction rules in silico to parent xenobiotics (here 1,021 pesticides), computes their monoisotopic m/z values to form a pseudo-MS1 candidature space, and preannotates them against dysregulated MS1 features by accurate-mass matching at ≤ 5 ppm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MS2 spectra match a reference library or authentic standard is available — traditional bottom-up library-based annotation is more direct and should be preferred No reaction rules or parent structures exist for the analyte class, so theoretical monoisotopic masses cannot be enumerated The feature table has not been filtered for dysregulated features (no DMS layer), making an omics-scale candidate-vs-feature cross-reference uninformative

skills.search_text: monoisotopic-mass-computation-from-structure Use when you need to verify or predict the theoretical m/z of a derivatized metabolite from its chemical structure — e.g., confirming that Met-ID hits for FMP-10-derivatized dopamine (1A, 2A, 2B) correspond to expected [M+H]+ ions within a 5 ppm mass-error window. skills.summary: Computes the neutral monoisotopic mass of a metabolite from its structure (via RDKit) and derives theoretical [M+H]+ m/z values for single and double FMP-10 derivatization states, enabling validation of Met-ID annotations such as dopamine peaks at m/z 421.1911, 674.2802, and 688.2959.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotation of observed m/z features from MALDI-MSI data rather than computing theoretical masses from a known structure — use metid.identify() directly instead When discrimination between derivatized forms relies on MS2 fragmentation patterns (e.g., distinguishing dopamine derivatives that retain vs. lose a methyl group) — mass computation alone cannot resolve this When the metabolite has no structure/name entry in the HMDB- or LIPID MAPS-derived Met-ID database

skills.search_text: monoisotopic-peak-identification-by-intensity-stepping Use when a target feature in an AIF LC-MS feature table may be an isotopologue rather than the monoisotopic mass, i.e. before running the fragment-library candidate search on m/z that must first be corrected to M+0. skills.description: Use when testing whether the Pearson correlation between two fluorescence channels (e.g., CFP/YFP or red/green from a Zeiss LSM 510) exceeds random overlap, and adjacent pixel intensities are spatially correlated by texture or the PSF so pixel-level scrambling would be invalid.

skills.search_text: monte-carlo-null-distribution-sampling Use when testing whether the Pearson correlation between two fluorescence channels (e.g., CFP/YFP or red/green from a Zeiss LSM 510) exceeds random overlap, and adjacent pixel intensities are spatially correlated by texture or the PSF so pixel-level scrambling would be invalid. Input is a single-channel image or lacks a paired second-channel image, so no two-color overlap null distribution can be constructed. The goal is measuring physical interaction distance between proteins (e.g., FRET, which detects interaction only if average binding distance is <10 nm) rather than colocalization significance. The question is colocalization extent from the 2D histogram's diagonal-selection approach, where assuming selected pixels are entirely colocalized can overpredict the amount of colocalization. Monte Carlo block-scrambling significance test for two-color colocalization: after background correction, blocks of image (sized by the texture/PSF autocorrelation width rather than single pixels) are randomized 200 times per region to build a null distribution of random overlap from which the colocalization significance threshold is derived. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422

skills.description: Use when a targeted MRM dataset contains QC samples per batch and you need to reduce systematic injection-order drift in compound abundances, e.g. before downstream statistical or pathway analysis.
skills.name: mrm-abundance-table-manipulation
skills.search_text: mrm-abundance-table-manipulation Use when a targeted MRM dataset contains QC samples per batch and you need to reduce systematic injection-order drift in compound abundances, e.g. before downstream statistical or pathway analysis. The dataset contains no QC samples in the sample files (MRMQuant skips batch-effect correction when no QCs are present). The input is raw vendor MRM data rather than a quantitated abundance matrix — first run MRMQuant quantitation to produce abundances before applying this correction. The analysis goal is deconvolution of coeluted peaks or absolute quantitation via standard curves, which are separate MRMQuant features rather than abundance-table drift correction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Manipulate the MRMQuant-quantitated abundance matrix (from the MAT-file or xlsx output) to fit LOESS curves on QC samples, interpolate QC trends via cubic splines across injection order, and rescale non-QC abundances to restore the reference sample's magnitude. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Manipulate the MRMQuant-quantitated abundance matrix (from the MAT-file or xlsx output) to fit LOESS curves on QC samples, interpolate QC trends via cubic splines across injection order, and rescale non-QC abundances to restore the reference sample's magnitude.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no QC samples in the sample files (MRMQuant skips batch-effect correction when no QCs are present). The input is raw vendor MRM data rather than a quantitated abundance matrix — first run MRMQuant quantitation to produce abundances before applying this correction. The analysis goal is deconvolution of coeluted peaks or absolute quantitation via standard curves, which are separate MRMQuant features rather than abundance-table drift correction.

skills.search_text: mrm-ion-chromatogram-smoothing Use when MRM sample files (mzML, MRM) must be preprocessed so that each ion chromatogram's peaks are detectable and traceable before peak detection, coelution deconvolution, and absolute quantitation in MRMQuant. The workflow step needed is batch-effect correction across BQCs (the later pipeline stage); smoothing is a per-sample preprocessing step, not a cross-sample normalisation method.

The task is pure MS/MS spectral intensity prediction from MSnLib, which has its own download/preprocess scripts (download_msnlib.py, preprocess_msnlib.py) and does not need MS-DIAL RT/CCS mining.

skills.description: Use when you have processed MS feature data (MZmine 2 or GNPS outputs, mzML-derived peak lists) for an extract library plus bioassay results, and need to score which features match the biological profile for prioritization or dereplication.
skills.name: ms-feature-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: ms-feature-activity-scoring Use when you have processed MS feature data (MZmine 2 or GNPS outputs, mzML-derived peak lists) for an extract library plus bioassay results, and need to score which features match the biological profile for prioritization or dereplication. Input MS data are raw peak lists without preprocessing (replicate comparison, basketing, intensity cutoff) — raw mass lists add junk features and inflate candidate bioactive features Bioassay columns are not normalized to a common scale — the Activity Score sums squared values across assays and unscaled columns would dominate the score The goal is de novo MS/MS spectrum identification rather than linking features to bioactivity profiles — NP Analyst is a target-agnostic activity-mapping tool, not a spectral annotation engine http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Computes NP Analyst Activity Scores and Cluster Scores for each mass spectrometry feature by integrating a basketed MS feature table (features x samples with m/z and retention time) with normalized bioassay data (samples x bioassay columns), to prioritize which metabolites in an extract library best explain the observed bioactivity. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Computes NP Analyst Activity Scores and Cluster Scores for each mass spectrometry feature by integrating a basketed MS feature table (features x samples with m/z and retention time) with normalized bioassay data (samples x bioassay columns), to prioritize which metabolites in an extract library best explain the observed bioactivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input MS data are raw peak lists without preprocessing (replicate comparison, basketing, intensity cutoff) — raw mass lists add junk features and inflate candidate bioactive features Bioassay columns are not normalized to a common scale — the Activity Score sums squared values across assays and unscaled columns would dominate the score The goal is de novo MS/MS spectrum identification rather than linking features to bioactivity profiles — NP Analyst is a target-agnostic activity-mapping tool, not a spectral annotation engine

skills.description: Use when NP Analyst (or equivalent Compound Activity Mapping) output shows several distinct m/z features with similar Activity and Cluster Scores sharing one retention time, indicating adduct/fragment/multiply-charged stripes of one molecule.
skills.name: ms-feature-adduct-fragment-interpretaion
skills.search_text: ms-feature-adduct-fragment-interpretaion Use when NP Analyst (or equivalent Compound Activity Mapping) output shows several distinct m/z features with similar Activity and Cluster Scores sharing one retention time, indicating adduct/fragment/multiply-charged stripes of one molecule. Input is already a basketed/replicate-merged feature table where adducts and fragments have been collapsed into single entries The goal is computing Activity Scores or Cluster Scores themselves — NP Analyst performs that computation; this skill only interprets its per-feature output Bioactivity scores are absent (e.g., raw unprocessed mass lists with no bioassay association), so stripes cannot be distinguished from noise features http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Manual interpretation step that groups independently scored NP Analyst MS features belonging to the same metabolite (adducts, in-source fragments, multiply-charged species) by co-located retention time and shared Activity/Cluster Scores, so a single bioactive molecule (e.g., [M+H]+ 753.3243 and its 623.2319 fragment for amychelin C) is treated as one prioritization target rather than separate features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Manual interpretation step that groups independently scored NP Analyst MS features belonging to the same metabolite (adducts, in-source fragments, multiply-charged species) by co-located retention time and shared Activity/Cluster Scores, so a single bioactive molecule (e.g., [M+H]+ 753.3243 and its 623.2319 fragment for amychelin C) is treated as one prioritization target rather than separate features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a basketed/replicate-merged feature table where adducts and fragments have been collapsed into single entries The goal is computing Activity Scores or Cluster Scores themselves — NP Analyst performs that computation; this skill only interprets its per-feature output Bioactivity scores are absent (e.g., raw unprocessed mass lists with no bioassay association), so stripes cannot be distinguished from noise features

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS feature-based molecular networking task with CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv) and node/library-match info (Node_info.tsv), and need per-feature chemical consensus annotations.
skills.name: ms-feature-annotation-table-generation
skills.search_text: ms-feature-annotation-table-generation Use when you have a GNPS feature-based molecular networking task with CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv) and node/library-match info (Node_info.tsv), and need per-feature chemical consensus annotations. The question is about compound-level structural elucidation or MS/MS spectrum identification rather than propagating class-level annotations across a molecular network — ConCISE annotates subnetworks with ChemOnt classes, not individual structures. Subnetworks contain no GNPS library spectral matches — propagation is restricted to subnetworks with at least one library match, and singleton nodes without library matches receive no in silico annotation. You require NPClassifier-based natural-product ontologies only for in silico matches but ClassyFire for library matches — the NPC flag applies NPClassifier ontologies to BOTH library matches and in silico matches. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates a consensus chemical-annotation table for ion features in untargeted tandem MS by fusing GNPS molecular networking, spectral library matching, and CANOPUS in silico class predictions across the ClassyFire ChemOnt hierarchy (superclass/class/subclass). Rationale: propagating only annotations that a majority of a subnetwork agrees on yields reliable class assignments (TPR > 95%) and expands consistent feature annotation up to 76%. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12121275
skills.summary: Generates a consensus chemical-annotation table for ion features in untargeted tandem MS by fusing GNPS molecular networking, spectral library matching, and CANOPUS in silico class predictions across the ClassyFire ChemOnt hierarchy (superclass/class/subclass). Rationale: propagating only annotations that a majority of a subnetwork agrees on yields reliable class assignments (TPR > 95%) and expands consistent feature annotation up to 76%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about compound-level structural elucidation or MS/MS spectrum identification rather than propagating class-level annotations across a molecular network — ConCISE annotates subnetworks with ChemOnt classes, not individual structures. Subnetworks contain no GNPS library spectral matches — propagation is restricted to subnetworks with at least one library match, and singleton nodes without library matches receive no in silico annotation. You require NPClassifier-based natural-product ontologies only for in silico matches but ClassyFire for library matches — the NPC flag applies NPClassifier ontologies to BOTH library matches and in silico matches.

skills.description: Use when a direct-injection MS dataset lacks chromatographic separation and features must be grouped as adducts/in-source fragments of one analyte via time-profile correlation plus exact mass differences.
skills.name: ms-feature-metadata-annotation
skills.search_text: ms-feature-metadata-annotation Use when a direct-injection MS dataset lacks chromatographic separation and features must be grouped as adducts/in-source fragments of one analyte via time-profile correlation plus exact mass differences. Input is already a curated feature table from LC-MS with chromatographic separation — retention-time-based coelution methods are more appropriate than time-profile correlation of direct-injection XICs. The goal is definitive molecular identification rather than putative adduct/in-source fragment annotation — correlation plus mass difference only yields putative assignments. MS1 data cannot be loaded via matchms-supported formats (.mgf/.mzML/.mzXML) and cannot first be exported with DBDIpy's export_to_spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Putative annotation of MS1 features as adducts or in-source fragments (e.g. [M+H]+, [M-H2O+H]+, [M+nO+H]+) arising from the same analyte, using pointwise XIC correlation combined with exact mass-difference analysis in direct-injection, chromatography-free plasma ionization (DBDI) datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad088
skills.summary: Putative annotation of MS1 features as adducts or in-source fragments (e.g. [M+H]+, [M-H2O+H]+, [M+nO+H]+) arising from the same analyte, using pointwise XIC correlation combined with exact mass-difference analysis in direct-injection, chromatography-free plasma ionization (DBDI) datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table from LC-MS with chromatographic separation — retention-time-based coelution methods are more appropriate than time-profile correlation of direct-injection XICs. The goal is definitive molecular identification rather than putative adduct/in-source fragment annotation — correlation plus mass difference only yields putative assignments. MS1 data cannot be loaded via matchms-supported formats (.mgf/.mzML/.mzXML) and cannot first be exported with DBDIpy's export_to_spectra.

skills.description: Use when you have extract/fraction-level bioassay results (e.g., BioMAP inhibition profiles) plus replicate LC-MS feature lists and need to map which MS features drive activity and which prefractions cluster together.
skills.name: ms-feature-network-community-analysis
skills.search_text: ms-feature-network-community-analysis Use when you have extract/fraction-level bioassay results (e.g., BioMAP inhibition profiles) plus replicate LC-MS feature lists and need to map which MS features drive activity and which prefractions cluster together. The MS data have no technical replicates, so replicate comparison ('strongly recommended where possible') cannot be applied and raw mass lists will inflate the number of candidate bioactive MS features with junk peaks A very low signal intensity cutoff is chosen relative to the bioassay's limit of detection, which 'may dramatically increase the complexity of the resulting networks without including any additional biologically informative MS features' The goal is clustering samples by their activity profiles rather than by bioactive MS feature distribution — NP Analyst communities are built on feature distribution, not sample activity profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Build and interpret NP Analyst compound activity mapping networks that relate MS features (from mzML/MZmine 2/GNPS peak lists) to normalized bioassay profiles, then use the scatter, network, and community views to prioritize bioactive metabolites such as micromonolactam, collismycin A/SF2738D, and amychelin C. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Build and interpret NP Analyst compound activity mapping networks that relate MS features (from mzML/MZmine 2/GNPS peak lists) to normalized bioassay profiles, then use the scatter, network, and community views to prioritize bioactive metabolites such as micromonolactam, collismycin A/SF2738D, and amychelin C.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MS data have no technical replicates, so replicate comparison ('strongly recommended where possible') cannot be applied and raw mass lists will inflate the number of candidate bioactive MS features with junk peaks A very low signal intensity cutoff is chosen relative to the bioassay's limit of detection, which 'may dramatically increase the complexity of the resulting networks without including any additional biologically informative MS features' The goal is clustering samples by their activity profiles rather than by bioactive MS feature distribution — NP Analyst communities are built on feature distribution, not sample activity profiles

skills.description: Use when an NP Analyst community contains multiple strong-Activity-Score MS features that cluster at the same retention time in the community view's RT vs m/z plot, suggesting adducts/fragments of one molecule rather than distinct compounds.
skills.name: ms-feature-retention-time-stripe-grouping
skills.search_text: ms-feature-retention-time-stripe-grouping Use when an NP Analyst community contains multiple strong-Activity-Score MS features that cluster at the same retention time in the community view's RT vs m/z plot, suggesting adducts/fragments of one molecule rather than distinct compounds. Input is raw unprocessed LC-MS data rather than a processed, replicate-compared feature table from MZmine 2 or GNPS — unpreprocessed runs increase candidate bioactive MS features with junk peaks The community has a single clear individual bioactive MS feature — direct feature prioritization is more appropriate than stripe grouping No bioactivity scores are available, so Activity/Cluster Score similarity cannot be used to decide whether co-retaining features belong to one molecule http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A dereplication step for NP Analyst communities: group co-eluting high-Activity-Score MS features into retention-time 'stripes' and interpret each stripe as adducts, fragments, or isotopes of a single parent molecule. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: A dereplication step for NP Analyst communities: group co-eluting high-Activity-Score MS features into retention-time 'stripes' and interpret each stripe as adducts, fragments, or isotopes of a single parent molecule.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unprocessed LC-MS data rather than a processed, replicate-compared feature table from MZmine 2 or GNPS — unpreprocessed runs increase candidate bioactive MS features with junk peaks The community has a single clear individual bioactive MS feature — direct feature prioritization is more appropriate than stripe grouping No bioactivity scores are available, so Activity/Cluster Score similarity cannot be used to decide whether co-retaining features belong to one molecule

skills.description: Use when an aligned feature quantification matrix (features_quantification_matrix.csv from MZmine2 or Optimus) contains many features lacking MS/MS scans and must be reduced to MS/MS-backed rows before GNPS FBMN or bioactivity correlation.
skills.name: ms-feature-table-filtering
skills.search_text: ms-feature-table-filtering Use when an aligned feature quantification matrix (features_quantification_matrix.csv from MZmine2 or Optimus) contains many features lacking MS/MS scans and must be reduced to MS/MS-backed rows before GNPS FBMN or bioactivity correlation. The input table is already the edited bioactivity-annotated file (features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.csv) with MS/MS filtering completed upstream. The dataset consists of direct-infusion data acquired without MS/MS scans, so the MS/MS row filter would empty the table. The analysis targets spatial mapping in Optimus rather than GNPS feature-based molecular networking, where MS/MS presence is not required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filter the aligned LC-MS/MS feature quantification table produced by MZmine2 or Optimus so that only features with an acquired MS/MS scan survive for downstream bioactive molecular networking and Pearson-correlation scoring against bioassay values. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.7b00737
skills.summary: Filter the aligned LC-MS/MS feature quantification table produced by MZmine2 or Optimus so that only features with an acquired MS/MS scan survive for downstream bioactive molecular networking and Pearson-correlation scoring against bioassay values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table is already the edited bioactivity-annotated file (features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.csv) with MS/MS filtering completed upstream. The dataset consists of direct-infusion data acquired without MS/MS scans, so the MS/MS row filter would empty the table. The analysis targets spatial mapping in Optimus rather than GNPS feature-based molecular networking, where MS/MS presence is not required.

skills.name: ms-file-analysis-table-parsing
skills.search_text: ms-file-analysis-table-parsing Use when per-file analysis rows for transferred MS data (e.g. task_001/per_file_analysis_table) need to be rolled up into a QC summary of PSM, peptide and protein group counts at a given FDR filter, posted to a dashboard. Input is raw MS data (e.g. Thermo RAW or mzML) rather than an already-produced per-file analysis table — conversion and parsing are upstream steps A full third-party search/analysis engine run is required — MSConnect is a wrapper/interface and 'does not come with any data processor or analysis software/license' Quantitative downstream analysis (imputing missing values, normalization, differential expression) is the goal rather than identification-count QC summarization http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Aggregates per-file MS analysis results into a tabulated QC summary of basic spectrum identification information — PSMs, peptides and protein groups passing a given FDR filter — mirroring the automated QC artifact MSConnect generates after raw files are transferred to storage. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c00854

skills.description: Use when choosing an open mass spectrometry file format for storing converted vendor raw data and you need an empirical file-size comparison across formats like MZA, mz5, mzXML, mzML and mzMLb.
skills.name: ms-file-size-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: ms-file-size-benchmark-comparison Use when choosing an open mass spectrometry file format for storing converted vendor raw data and you need an empirical file-size comparison across formats like MZA, mz5, mzXML, mzML and mzMLb. You need speed/parse-time benchmarks rather than storage footprint - the article reports improvements in speed are still needed for MZA and does not provide runtime benchmarks for this comparison. Your comparison requires identical conversion parameters across formats that you cannot reproduce (e.g. no ProteoWizard version control), since the size ordering depends on equivalent lossless settings. You are converting only a single small file; the benchmark's discriminative signal comes from datasets with large numbers of spectra such as the LC-SLIM-MS file. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks the storage footprint of MZA's HDF5-based MS data format against competing open formats (mz5, mzXML, mzML, mzMLb) by converting identical vendor raw files under lossless, zero-intensity-omitted settings and recording the resulting byte sizes. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00313
skills.summary: Benchmarks the storage footprint of MZA's HDF5-based MS data format against competing open formats (mz5, mzXML, mzML, mzMLb) by converting identical vendor raw files under lossless, zero-intensity-omitted settings and recording the resulting byte sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need speed/parse-time benchmarks rather than storage footprint - the article reports improvements in speed are still needed for MZA and does not provide runtime benchmarks for this comparison. Your comparison requires identical conversion parameters across formats that you cannot reproduce (e.g. no ProteoWizard version control), since the size ordering depends on equivalent lossless settings. You are converting only a single small file; the benchmark's discriminative signal comes from datasets with large numbers of spectra such as the LC-SLIM-MS file.

skills.description: Use when both original raw MS-files and preprocessed counterparts of the same dataset exist in a deposit (e.g. MassIVE MSV000087295) and the goal is to numerically verify a claim that preprocessing reduces file size.

skills.search_text: ms-file-storage-size-quantification Use when both original raw MS-files and preprocessed counterparts of the same dataset exist in a deposit (e.g. MassIVE MSV000087295) and the goal is to numerically verify a claim that preprocessing reduces file size. Input is a single MS-file without a matched preprocessed counterpart, so no paired size comparison can be made The analysis goal is signal-quality improvement (e.g. lipid annotation counts, mass error), not storage-size quantification File listings cannot be matched one-to-one between original and preprocessed versions, making the paired ratio undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies the storage-size benefit of MS-file preprocessing by comparing byte sizes of original raw LC-IM-MS files against PreProcessor-generated files (e.g. the "_MA-d3-c3-Min20_SR" lipid extract files in MassIVE MSV000087295) and expressing the result as a size-reduction ratio that must lie strictly between 0 and 1. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single MS-file without a matched preprocessed counterpart, so no paired size comparison can be made The analysis goal is signal-quality improvement (e.g. lipid annotation counts, mass error), not storage-size quantification File listings cannot be matched one-to-one between original and preprocessed versions, making the paired ratio undefined

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectral matching or in silico MS/MS annotation leaves many isomeric structure candidates and predicted LC retention times (from Retip) are available to rank or exclude candidates in MS-FINDER 3.30+.
skills.name: ms-finder-rt-similarity-filtering
skills.search_text: ms-finder-rt-similarity-filtering Use when MS/MS spectral matching or in silico MS/MS annotation leaves many isomeric structure candidates and predicted LC retention times (from Retip) are available to rank or exclude candidates in MS-FINDER 3.30+. Predicting/annotating compounds outside the chemical landscape of the Retip training set (e.g., complex high molecular weight lipids such as triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines were largely excluded from training), where predictions may be more erroneous Trying to discriminate closely eluting positional isomers in typical 12 min UPLC methods — 1 min prediction errors preclude narrow retention-time search windows When no measured retention time exists for the query feature, since the filter compares predicted RT against observed RT http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Filters and re-ranks MS-FINDER structure/isomer candidates using predicted retention times exported from Retip, applying Gaussian RT similarity scoring and RT tolerance windows (about ±1 min) to remove false-positive annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Filters and re-ranks MS-FINDER structure/isomer candidates using predicted retention times exported from Retip, applying Gaussian RT similarity scoring and RT tolerance windows (about ±1 min) to remove false-positive annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting/annotating compounds outside the chemical landscape of the Retip training set (e.g., complex high molecular weight lipids such as triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines were largely excluded from training), where predictions may be more erroneous Trying to discriminate closely eluting positional isomers in typical 12 min UPLC methods — 1 min prediction errors preclude narrow retention-time search windows When no measured retention time exists for the query feature, since the filter compares predicted RT against observed RT

skills.description: Use when building an RT-annotated structure library for MS-FINDER ≥3.24 to rank/exclude isomer candidates in untargeted MS/MS annotation, starting from SMILES sets from HMDB, DrugBank, FooDB, STOFF-IDENT and other Retiplib databases.
skills.name: ms-finder-spectral-library-format-preparation
skills.search_text: ms-finder-spectral-library-format-preparation Use when building an RT-annotated structure library for MS-FINDER ≥3.24 to rank/exclude isomer candidates in untargeted MS/MS annotation, starting from SMILES sets from HMDB, DrugBank, FooDB, STOFF-IDENT and other Retiplib databases. The compounds are complex high-molecular-weight lipids (e.g. triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines) that were largely excluded from the Retip training sets — predictions outside the training chemical landscape may be more erroneous The goal is discriminating closely eluting compounds with narrow retention time search windows (e.g. 12 min UPLC methods), since ~1 min prediction errors are not adequate for that Retention times must be adjusted for small changes in a specific chromatographic method — this was beyond the scope of the Retip study http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Prepares RT-annotated compound library files for MS-FINDER (v3.24+/3.30) by batch-predicting HILIC and reversed-phase LC retention times for large small-molecule structure sets (e.g. 320,919 compounds from Retip's bundled databases) with Retip's pre-trained Keras neural-network models, so predicted RTs can rank or exclude candidate structures during untargeted metabolomics annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Prepares RT-annotated compound library files for MS-FINDER (v3.24+/3.30) by batch-predicting HILIC and reversed-phase LC retention times for large small-molecule structure sets (e.g. 320,919 compounds from Retip's bundled databases) with Retip's pre-trained Keras neural-network models, so predicted RTs can rank or exclude candidate structures during untargeted metabolomics annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compounds are complex high-molecular-weight lipids (e.g. triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines) that were largely excluded from the Retip training sets — predictions outside the training chemical landscape may be more erroneous The goal is discriminating closely eluting compounds with narrow retention time search windows (e.g. 12 min UPLC methods), since ~1 min prediction errors are not adequate for that Retention times must be adjusted for small changes in a specific chromatographic method — this was beyond the scope of the Retip study

The data contain true MS/MS scans (MS2 spectra are available) — use conventional MS/MS library search instead of pseudo MS/MS generation The input is LC-MS mzML/mzXML data where correlation should be done on XICs in the retention-time domain, not on spatial ion images The target analytes produce too few in-source fragments above m/z 100 (e.g., guanine m/z 150.0421 and glutamic acid m/z 146.0459 failed for lack of sufficient in-source fragments) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Extract ion images from MS1-only imaging MS data (imzML/ibd) and spatially correlate them to assemble pseudo MS/MS spectra, enabling MS/MS library-based structural annotation of MALDI-imaging datasets with ms1-id. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269

skills.when_to_use_negative: The data contain true MS/MS scans (MS2 spectra are available) — use conventional MS/MS library search instead of pseudo MS/MS generation The input is LC-MS mzML/mzXML data where correlation should be done on XICs in the retention-time domain, not on spatial ion images The target analytes produce too few in-source fragments above m/z 100 (e.g., guanine m/z 150.0421 and glutamic acid m/z 146.0459 failed for lack of sufficient in-source fragments)

skills.search_text: ms-instrument-type-comparison Use when comparing a predictor's per-spectrum accuracy across MS/MS instrument types (Q-TOF vs. Orbitrap) or strata such as LogP polarity, precursor mass bins, or chemical superclass, to locate where a model underperforms. The input is raw vendor MS/MS data before any model inference has produced per-spectrum candidate formulas — run the FIDDLE evaluation pipeline first The goal is benchmarking a model against baselines (SIRIUS, BUDDY) on overall accuracy rather than dissecting accuracy across molecular strata and instruments Spectra come from instrument types or precursor types outside the evaluated scope (e.g., non-Q-TOF/Orbitrap data or rare precursor types excluded by the training filters) Stratified evaluation of a formula-identification model's accuracy by instrument type (Q-TOF vs. Orbitrap) and by molecular strata (LogP polarity bins, precursor mass bins, ClassyFire superclass), as used to characterize FIDDLE's top-5 accuracy trends on the NIST23 test set. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9

skills.description: Use when raw LC-IM-MS or LC-DT IM-MS TOF profile-mode data (Agilent .d or UIMF) contains a large background of low-count points that inflate file size and degrade downstream feature finding or lipid annotation.
skills.name: ms-low-intensity-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: ms-low-intensity-threshold-filtering Use when raw LC-IM-MS or LC-DT IM-MS TOF profile-mode data (Agilent .d or UIMF) contains a large background of low-count points that inflate file size and degrade downstream feature finding or lipid annotation. Input is already centroided or a peak/feature list rather than raw profile-mode IM-MS data points — the threshold operates on raw counts of individual points The downstream tool requires the original unfiltered file, e.g., when saturation repair or smoothing must be applied to the full dynamic range before thresholding MS-files where the threshold would remove true low-abundance analyte signals the user intends to retain, since the filter deletes all points not exceeding the specified count value http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 The PNNL PreProcessor's low intensity threshold filter removes raw LC-IM-MS data points that do not exceed a user-specified count value (e.g., 20 counts in the lipid workflow), reducing file size and cleaning background before spike removal and downstream IM-MS processing. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: The PNNL PreProcessor's low intensity threshold filter removes raw LC-IM-MS data points that do not exceed a user-specified count value (e.g., 20 counts in the lipid workflow), reducing file size and cleaning background before spike removal and downstream IM-MS processing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already centroided or a peak/feature list rather than raw profile-mode IM-MS data points — the threshold operates on raw counts of individual points The downstream tool requires the original unfiltered file, e.g., when saturation repair or smoothing must be applied to the full dynamic range before thresholding MS-files where the threshold would remove true low-abundance analyte signals the user intends to retain, since the filter deletes all points not exceeding the specified count value

skills.search_text: ms-marker-feature-visualization Use when a GC–MS run has been processed with NPFimg (2D m/z–retention-time map, no conventional peak picking) and the identified multivariate marker features for analytes such as aroma odor or human breath metabolites need to be rendered on the original MS map for inspection or reporting. The goal is de novo metabolite identification rather than visualizing marker features already identified by NPFimg's machine-learning stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Visualize multivariate chemo-/biomarker features identified by NPFimg on a two-dimensional GC–MS map (m/z vs retention time), rendering the peak-picking-free marker calls produced by its image-processing and machine-learning stages as an interpretable map image. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03163
skills.summary: Visualize multivariate chemo-/biomarker features identified by NPFimg on a two-dimensional GC–MS map (m/z vs retention time), rendering the peak-picking-free marker calls produced by its image-processing and machine-learning stages as an interpretable map image.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated peak/feature table from conventional peak picking rather than a 2D m/z–retention-time MS map processed by NPFimg — NPFimg's visualization is tied to its peak-picking-free map representation. skills.search_text: ms-ms-spectra-alignment-shifted-unshifted-peak-matching Use when you have MS/MS spectra of a known compound and a structural analog (same adduct, one modification site) and need to classify matching/shifted/unshifted fragment peaks to localize where the structural modification occurs. The pair has no shifted peak explainable by a substructure of the parent compound — after this filter only 62% of benchmark pairs (8033) remain, so pairs failing it cannot be localized this way The compounds differ at more than one modification site or use different adducts (benchmark eligibility requires exactly one modification site via RDKit GetSubstructMatch edge count and identical M+H adduct) Precursor mass exceeds 2000 Da or the precursor mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller compound (benchmark eligibility checks i–iv) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Aligns MS/MS spectra of a structurally related known and unknown compound pair by greedy bipartite-graph matching, classifying peak matches as shifted or unshifted; shifted peaks mark substructures of the known molecule that putatively contain the modification site, which is the core signal ModiFinder exploits for modification site localization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Aligns MS/MS spectra of a structurally related known and unknown compound pair by greedy bipartite-graph matching, classifying peak matches as shifted or unshifted; shifted peaks mark substructures of the known molecule that putatively contain the modification site, which is the core signal ModiFinder exploits for modification site localization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pair has no shifted peak explainable by a substructure of the parent compound — after this filter only 62% of benchmark pairs (8033) remain, so pairs failing it cannot be localized this way The compounds differ at more than one modification site or use different adducts (benchmark eligibility requires exactly one modification site via RDKit GetSubstructMatch edge count and identical M+H adduct) Precursor mass exceeds 2000 Da or the precursor mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller compound (benchmark eligibility checks i–iv)

skills.name: ms-rt-purity-scoring
skills.search_text: ms-rt-purity-scoring Use when clustering tandem mass spectra (e.g. from PXD023047 with MS-Cluster, Falcon, or MaRaCluster) and you need a per-cluster purity score that does not depend on FDR-controlled database-search identifications, or when validating an MS-RT purity score against a DB-Search reference. skills.description: Use when raw 2D chromatography–MS data (GC–MS or LC–MS maps of m/z vs retention time) must be comprehensively characterized and marker features identified and visualized, and conventional peak picking is either unavailable, unreliable (prone to false peak detections), or undesired — e.
skills.name: ms-signal-characterization-without-peak-picking
skills.search_text: ms-signal-characterization-without-peak-picking Use when raw 2D chromatography–MS data (GC–MS or LC–MS maps of m/z vs retention time) must be comprehensively characterized and marker features identified and visualized, and conventional peak picking is either unavailable, unreliable (prone to false peak detections), or undesired — e. Input is already a peak-picked feature table or a processed analyte list — this skill specifically operates on the raw two-dimensional MS map without peak picking, so applying it to already-reduced feature data is inappropriate. The analysis goal is conventional peak picking / peak detection itself rather than marker-feature identification from image-domain signal characterization — this skill's rationale explicitly replaces the peak-picking process. The target is not a chromatography–MS map (e.g., single-dimension MS-only spectra without a retention-time dimension, or non-chromatographic spectroscopy) — NPFimg is designed for GC–MS and LC–MS data with m/z vs retention time structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Skill for automatically identifying and visualizing multivariate chemo-/biomarker features of analytes in chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS or LC–MS) data by combining image processing and machine learning on a two-dimensional MS map (m/z vs retention time), explicitly bypassing the conventional peak-picking process that suffers from false peak detections. Implemented by the open-source tool NPFimg. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03163
skills.summary: Skill for automatically identifying and visualizing multivariate chemo-/biomarker features of analytes in chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS or LC–MS) data by combining image processing and machine learning on a two-dimensional MS map (m/z vs retention time), explicitly bypassing the conventional peak-picking process that suffers from false peak detections. Implemented by the open-source tool NPFimg.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-picked feature table or a processed analyte list — this skill specifically operates on the raw two-dimensional MS map without peak picking, so applying it to already-reduced feature data is inappropriate. The analysis goal is conventional peak picking / peak detection itself rather than marker-feature identification from image-domain signal characterization — this skill's rationale explicitly replaces the peak-picking process. The target is not a chromatography–MS map (e.g., single-dimension MS-only spectra without a retention-time dimension, or non-chromatographic spectroscopy) — NPFimg is designed for GC–MS and LC–MS data with m/z vs retention time structure.

skills.description: Decision support for profiling spectrum preprocessing as a runtime bottleneck before choosing or optimizing an MS/MS spectral clustering tool; triggered when MGF-converted PRIDE data are available and per-stage timings are needed.
skills.name: ms-spectra-clustering-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: ms-spectra-clustering-runtime-profiling Decision support for profiling spectrum preprocessing as a runtime bottleneck before choosing or optimizing an MS/MS spectral clustering tool; triggered when MGF-converted PRIDE data are available and per-stage timings are needed. Input data are already preprocessed or stored in a format other than raw PRIDE files (e.g., vendor MGF ready for clustering), so no raw-to-MGF conversion or preprocessing share measurement is applicable. The goal is to profile a GPU-accelerated tool such as HyperSpec rather than the CPU-only reference tools; HyperSpec's optimized preprocessing module makes it a different runtime profile. Only a single clustering tool is of interest and cross-tool runtime comparison is not needed, so the three-tool profiling workflow is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Profiles the stage-wise runtime of state-of-the-art CPU spectral clustering tools (MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, MaRaCluster) by converting PRIDE raw files to MGF with ThermoRawFileParser, timing preprocessing versus total wall clock, and reporting the preprocessing share as a fraction of overall runtime (reported range: 20–90%). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00612
skills.summary: Profiles the stage-wise runtime of state-of-the-art CPU spectral clustering tools (MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, MaRaCluster) by converting PRIDE raw files to MGF with ThermoRawFileParser, timing preprocessing versus total wall clock, and reporting the preprocessing share as a fraction of overall runtime (reported range: 20–90%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already preprocessed or stored in a format other than raw PRIDE files (e.g., vendor MGF ready for clustering), so no raw-to-MGF conversion or preprocessing share measurement is applicable. The goal is to profile a GPU-accelerated tool such as HyperSpec rather than the CPU-only reference tools; HyperSpec's optimized preprocessing module makes it a different runtime profile. Only a single clustering tool is of interest and cross-tool runtime comparison is not needed, so the three-tool profiling workflow is unnecessary.

skills.search_text: ms1-feature-metabolite-mass-matching Use when starting MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3 annotation: you have a curated MRN (igraph), an MS1 feature table, and seed metabolite annotations, and must constrain the network before reaction mapping and MS2-similarity propagation. skills.search_text: ms1-scan-filtering Use when the goal is to restrict spectral access to MS1-level scans of a Thermo Fisher .raw file (e.g. building a base-peak table, TIC, or XIC) and the input is a proprietary Orbitrap raw file readable by rawR. The analysis needs fragment-ion spectra (MS2/HCD scans); the 'ms' filter excludes them, so use a scan filter string like 'FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00 [100.0000-1015.0000]' instead. The raw file is not from Thermo Fisher Scientific or lacks the .raw format that rawR/RawFileReader can read. Input data are already in an open format such as mzML handled by other backends and direct proprietary raw access is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filters Thermo raw file scans to the MS1 (survey) level by passing filter='ms' to rawrr's reader functions, enabling per-scan extraction of base peak m/z, base peak intensity, and scan start time for QC tables such as basepeak_ms1.csv. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00866
skills.summary: Filters Thermo raw file scans to the MS1 (survey) level by passing filter='ms' to rawrr's reader functions, enabling per-scan extraction of base peak m/z, base peak intensity, and scan start time for QC tables such as basepeak_ms1.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis needs fragment-ion spectra (MS2/HCD scans); the 'ms' filter excludes them, so use a scan filter string like 'FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00 [100.0000-1015.0000]' instead. The raw file is not from Thermo Fisher Scientific or lacks the .raw format that rawR/RawFileReader can read. Input data are already in an open format such as mzML handled by other backends and direct proprietary raw access is unnecessary.

skills.summary: Execute the mzLearn MS1 signal-detection and alignment pipeline: run raw LC/MS mzML files through the zero-parameter mzLearn algorithm to produce a feature table of median rt/m/z with normalized intensities, then benchmark outputs against XCMS and ASARI. skills.description: Use when metabolomics samples cannot be compared by RT-aligned features — chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, different LC gradients, or different MS instruments (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) — and a sample-level MS2 fingerprint matrix is needed.
skills.name: ms2-fingerprint-vectorization
skills.search_text: ms2-fingerprint-vectorization Use when metabolomics samples cannot be compared by RT-aligned features — chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, different LC gradients, or different MS instruments (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) — and a sample-level MS2 fingerprint matrix is needed. Samples already align well by retention time and share substantial feature overlap, where standard RT-based feature alignment and ordination suffice — MEMO is stated to suit particularly well to chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap or strong RT shifts. The analysis requires structurally annotated, compound-level chemical similarity (e.g. cosine-score-based metrics like CSCS) rather than raw occurrence counts of MS2 peaks and neutral losses. Spectra contain too few peaks to be informative — the document encoding requires min_peaks_required=10, so sparse MS2 files yield weak fingerprints. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Vectorizes LC-MS/MS samples by counting occurrences of MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor as peak@mz / loss@mz word tokens, producing retention-time-agnostic MEMO sample vectors that are aligned into a sample-by-word matrix without prior feature alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Vectorizes LC-MS/MS samples by counting occurrences of MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor as peak@mz / loss@mz word tokens, producing retention-time-agnostic MEMO sample vectors that are aligned into a sample-by-word matrix without prior feature alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples already align well by retention time and share substantial feature overlap, where standard RT-based feature alignment and ordination suffice — MEMO is stated to suit particularly well to chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap or strong RT shifts. The analysis requires structurally annotated, compound-level chemical similarity (e.g. cosine-score-based metrics like CSCS) rather than raw occurrence counts of MS2 peaks and neutral losses. Spectra contain too few peaks to be informative — the document encoding requires min_peaks_required=10, so sparse MS2 files yield weak fingerprints.
