Input spectra lack an associated MS2 scan or isotopic pattern (the upstream feature filtering module is what guarantees every kept feature carries an MS2 scan) — rerun feature detection/filtering first The goal is spectral library matching (e.g. GNPS/ISDB-LOTUS search) rather than in-silico formula/structure elucidation — ENPKG handles that in a separate ISDB step (03_enpkg_mn_isdb_isdb_taxo) and the two are meant to be compared, not substituted Features have m/z above 800 or adducts outside the configured lists ([M + H]+, [M + NH4]+, [M + K]+, [M + Na]+ in PI; [M – H]−, [M + K-2H]−, [M + Na-2H]− in NI) — they fall outside this SIRIUS configuration http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 In the ENPKG workflow, MZmine-exported per-feature MS1 isotopic patterns and MS2 spectra are elucidated into molecular formula and 2D structure candidates with SIRIUS (ZODIAC re-ranking) and CSI:FingerID, complemented by CANOPUS class predictions and NPClassifier natural-product taxonomy, as a per-sample step before knowledge-graph integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: In the ENPKG workflow, MZmine-exported per-feature MS1 isotopic patterns and MS2 spectra are elucidated into molecular formula and 2D structure candidates with SIRIUS (ZODIAC re-ranking) and CSI:FingerID, complemented by CANOPUS class predictions and NPClassifier natural-product taxonomy, as a per-sample step before knowledge-graph integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack an associated MS2 scan or isotopic pattern (the upstream feature filtering module is what guarantees every kept feature carries an MS2 scan) — rerun feature detection/filtering first The goal is spectral library matching (e.g. GNPS/ISDB-LOTUS search) rather than in-silico formula/structure elucidation — ENPKG handles that in a separate ISDB step (03_enpkg_mn_isdb_isdb_taxo) and the two are meant to be compared, not substituted Features have m/z above 800 or adducts outside the configured lists ([M + H]+, [M + NH4]+, [M + K]+, [M + Na]+ in PI; [M – H]−, [M + K-2H]−, [M + Na-2H]− in NI) — they fall outside this SIRIUS configuration

skills.description: Use when you have LC-MS2 peak lists from a fractionated natural product extract and need to prioritize fractions for isolation or compare unknowns against reference compounds (e.g., swinholide A) via spectral similarity networks.
skills.name: ms2-molecular-networking-annotation
skills.search_text: ms2-molecular-networking-annotation Use when you have LC-MS2 peak lists from a fractionated natural product extract and need to prioritize fractions for isolation or compare unknowns against reference compounds (e.g., swinholide A) via spectral similarity networks. Input is a purified single-compound spectrum — spectral library matching alone suffices and networking adds nothing Data lacks MS2 fragmentation (e.g., 1D NMR or MS1-only data) — use SMART 2.0 NMR-based mixture analysis instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 MS2-based molecular networking for prioritizing and annotating natural products in LC-MS2 data of crude/fractionated extracts, used here alongside cytotoxicity and SMART 2.0 NMR analysis to guide isolation from an environmental Symploca extract. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jacs.9b13786
skills.summary: MS2-based molecular networking for prioritizing and annotating natural products in LC-MS2 data of crude/fractionated extracts, used here alongside cytotoxicity and SMART 2.0 NMR analysis to guide isolation from an environmental Symploca extract.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a purified single-compound spectrum — spectral library matching alone suffices and networking adds nothing Data lacks MS2 fragmentation (e.g., 1D NMR or MS1-only data) — use SMART 2.0 NMR-based mixture analysis instead

skills.description: Use when a LC-MS lipidomics pipeline has already produced MS2 and MS3+ spectral matches (e.g. from LipiDex 2 Spectrum Searcher) and fragment-level peak assignments are needed to validate or annotate chromatographic features.
skills.name: ms2-ms3-fragment-peak-annotation
skills.search_text: ms2-ms3-fragment-peak-annotation Use when a LC-MS lipidomics pipeline has already produced MS2 and MS3+ spectral matches (e.g. from LipiDex 2 Spectrum Searcher) and fragment-level peak assignments are needed to validate or annotate chromatographic features. Input spectra have not yet been assigned spectral matches by Spectrum Searcher — the Annotator requires existing MS2/MS3+ matches as its input The goal is lipid identification from raw spectra rather than fragment-level annotation of already-identified features; use Spectrum Searcher first The peak table originates from a tool other than the LipiDex 2 pipeline's CSV format, since the Annotator consumes LipiDex 2's inter-module CSV results http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate fragment peaks on chromatographic lipid features using MS2 and MS3+ spectral matches, as implemented in the LipiDex 2 Lipid Spectral Annotator module. This turns raw Spectrum Searcher spectral matches into per-fragment peak assignments that support downstream purity and quality-control evaluation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Annotate fragment peaks on chromatographic lipid features using MS2 and MS3+ spectral matches, as implemented in the LipiDex 2 Lipid Spectral Annotator module. This turns raw Spectrum Searcher spectral matches into per-fragment peak assignments that support downstream purity and quality-control evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra have not yet been assigned spectral matches by Spectrum Searcher — the Annotator requires existing MS2/MS3+ matches as its input The goal is lipid identification from raw spectra rather than fragment-level annotation of already-identified features; use Spectrum Searcher first The peak table originates from a tool other than the LipiDex 2 pipeline's CSV format, since the Annotator consumes LipiDex 2's inter-module CSV results

skills.description: Use when replicate-grouped, deconvolved MS2 spectra (e.g., DDA or SWATH-DIA output) must be merged into one consensus spectrum per MS1 peak and fragment intensities need normalization before MSP export.
skills.name: ms2-peak-intensity-normalization
skills.search_text: ms2-peak-intensity-normalization Use when replicate-grouped, deconvolved MS2 spectra (e.g., DDA or SWATH-DIA output) must be merged into one consensus spectrum per MS1 peak and fragment intensities need normalization before MSP export. Input is already a merged/consensus spectrum or a clean feature abundance table — normalization for statistical analysis is a separate MetaboAnalystR module MS2 spectra come from a single replicate (no replicate group) — the frequency-based filtering rationale does not apply Only MS1 peak-picking/quantification is needed; this skill belongs to the MS2 deconvolution-to-annotation pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3395 Normalizes the fragment-ion intensities of replicate MS2 spectra within MetaboAnalystR 4.0's spectrum-consensus step, after frequency-based fragment filtering, so that all replicate MS2 spectra of an MS1 feature can be merged into a single consensus spectrum. It reduces noise and errors in downstream MS2-based compound identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-48009-6
skills.summary: Normalizes the fragment-ion intensities of replicate MS2 spectra within MetaboAnalystR 4.0's spectrum-consensus step, after frequency-based fragment filtering, so that all replicate MS2 spectra of an MS1 feature can be merged into a single consensus spectrum. It reduces noise and errors in downstream MS2-based compound identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a merged/consensus spectrum or a clean feature abundance table — normalization for statistical analysis is a separate MetaboAnalystR module MS2 spectra come from a single replicate (no replicate group) — the frequency-based filtering rationale does not apply Only MS1 peak-picking/quantification is needed; this skill belongs to the MS2 deconvolution-to-annotation pipeline

skills.description: Use when annotating MS2 fragment peaks with chemical subformulae for a candidate precursor formula and you want to avoid costly fragmentation tree computation (e.g. as input features for formula scoring models like MIST-CF).
skills.name: ms2-peak-mass-decomposition
skills.search_text: ms2-peak-mass-decomposition Use when annotating MS2 fragment peaks with chemical subformulae for a candidate precursor formula and you want to avoid costly fragmentation tree computation (e.g. as input features for formula scoring models like MIST-CF). When a full fragmentation tree with fragmentation-event edges is explicitly required (e.g. SIRIUS-style tree scoring) — this routine deliberately circumvents tree construction For negative-mode data or adduct-switching scenarios: MIST-CF models were trained only for positive-mode data and adduct switching in MS2 subformula assignment is not considered When the candidate precursor formula is unknown — the routine enumerates subformulae of a given formula and cannot proceed without one http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A lightweight MS2 peak subformula assignment routine from MIST-CF that replaces fragmentation tree construction: subtract the precursor adduct mass, enumerate candidate subformulae of the precursor formula, and match each peak to its nearest subformula within an instrument-specific ppm tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: A lightweight MS2 peak subformula assignment routine from MIST-CF that replaces fragmentation tree construction: subtract the precursor adduct mass, enumerate candidate subformulae of the precursor formula, and match each peak to its nearest subformula within an instrument-specific ppm tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a full fragmentation tree with fragmentation-event edges is explicitly required (e.g. SIRIUS-style tree scoring) — this routine deliberately circumvents tree construction For negative-mode data or adduct-switching scenarios: MIST-CF models were trained only for positive-mode data and adduct switching in MS2 subformula assignment is not considered When the candidate precursor formula is unknown — the routine enumerates subformulae of a given formula and cannot proceed without one

skills.description: Use when you have LC-MS/MS peak lists (e.g. .mgf) and need to vectorize samples without feature alignment — especially for chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap or strong RT shifts.
skills.name: ms2-peak-neutral-loss-counting
skills.search_text: ms2-peak-neutral-loss-counting Use when you have LC-MS/MS peak lists (e.g. .mgf) and need to vectorize samples without feature alignment — especially for chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap or strong RT shifts. When intensities matter to your analysis: MEMO discards MS1 feature intensity and uses only presence/absence of peaks and losses When you need retention-time-aware sample comparison — MEMO is deliberately RT agnostic and will not preserve RT information When features are already aligned across samples and an intensity-based distance (e.g. Bray-Curtis on the feature table) is the intended metric http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generates an MS2 fingerprint for each metabolomics sample by counting the occurrence of MS2 fragment peaks and neutral losses (relative to the precursor), as implemented in the memo-ms package, then aligns these fingerprints into a sample-by-feature MEMO matrix for retention-time-agnostic sample comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Generates an MS2 fingerprint for each metabolomics sample by counting the occurrence of MS2 fragment peaks and neutral losses (relative to the precursor), as implemented in the memo-ms package, then aligns these fingerprints into a sample-by-feature MEMO matrix for retention-time-agnostic sample comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When intensities matter to your analysis: MEMO discards MS1 feature intensity and uses only presence/absence of peaks and losses When you need retention-time-aware sample comparison — MEMO is deliberately RT agnostic and will not preserve RT information When features are already aligned across samples and an intensity-based distance (e.g. Bray-Curtis on the feature table) is the intended metric

skills.description: Use when you have a simulated (e.g., SMITER-generated mzML) or real complex-mixture dataset and must estimate how many distinct peptides co-fragment within each MS2 spectrum before committing to a real MS experiment.
skills.name: ms2-precursor-coisolation-analysis
skills.search_text: ms2-precursor-coisolation-analysis Use when you have a simulated (e.g., SMITER-generated mzML) or real complex-mixture dataset and must estimate how many distinct peptides co-fragment within each MS2 spectrum before committing to a real MS experiment. The input is a single-peptide or well-separated dataset with no overlapping retention times, where chimericity cannot arise and the analysis adds no information. The goal is de novo peptide identification from real spectra rather than quantifying co-fragmentation prevalence in a ground-truth (gold-standard) simulation. The data are not LC-MS/MS tandem spectra in a parseable format such as mzML with known precursor candidates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Quantify co-fragmentation (chimeric MS2 spectra) in a simulated or measured LC-MS/MS run by annotating each MS2 spectrum's peaks against theoretical fragment ions from all co-eluting precursor peptides, yielding per-spectrum peptide multiplicity statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/genes12030396
skills.summary: Quantify co-fragmentation (chimeric MS2 spectra) in a simulated or measured LC-MS/MS run by annotating each MS2 spectrum's peaks against theoretical fragment ions from all co-eluting precursor peptides, yielding per-spectrum peptide multiplicity statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-peptide or well-separated dataset with no overlapping retention times, where chimericity cannot arise and the analysis adds no information. The goal is de novo peptide identification from real spectra rather than quantifying co-fragmentation prevalence in a ground-truth (gold-standard) simulation. The data are not LC-MS/MS tandem spectra in a parseable format such as mzML with known precursor candidates.

skills.description: Use when comparing a query MS/MS spectrum against reference library spectra to find structural analogues, and you need to explain which query–reference product-ion pairs (including mass-shifted ones like +15.99 Da) drive the similarity score.
skills.name: ms2-product-ion-mass-difference-alignment
skills.search_text: ms2-product-ion-mass-difference-alignment Use when comparing a query MS/MS spectrum against reference library spectra to find structural analogues, and you need to explain which query–reference product-ion pairs (including mass-shifted ones like +15.99 Da) drive the similarity score. You only need a simple heuristic alignment score without interpretability — plain Cosine or Modified Cosine suffices and needs no trained model No trained TransExION model or structural-similarity reference files are available and training data (GNPS_MassBank_train/val MGF) cannot be obtained The spectra are not tandem MS/MS product-ion spectra convertible to the MGF/h5py format the TransExION scripts expect http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aligns MS/MS product ions between a query spectrum and a reference spectrum not only by co-occurring fragments and neutral losses but also through their mass difference, using a Transformer-based model (TransExION) with a post-hoc layer-wise relevance propagation explanation rendered as a query-vs-reference product-ion heatmap. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Aligns MS/MS product ions between a query spectrum and a reference spectrum not only by co-occurring fragments and neutral losses but also through their mass difference, using a Transformer-based model (TransExION) with a post-hoc layer-wise relevance propagation explanation rendered as a query-vs-reference product-ion heatmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a simple heuristic alignment score without interpretability — plain Cosine or Modified Cosine suffices and needs no trained model No trained TransExION model or structural-similarity reference files are available and training data (GNPS_MassBank_train/val MGF) cannot be obtained The spectra are not tandem MS/MS product-ion spectra convertible to the MGF/h5py format the TransExION scripts expect

skills.description: Use when processing DDA LC-MS mzXML data in which conventional peak picking (XCMS.featureTable with snthresh=6, prefilter=c(3,100)) has already run but low-intensity or poorly shaped peaks with detectable MS2 spectra were missed.
skills.name: ms2-recognition-feature-rescue
skills.search_text: ms2-recognition-feature-rescue Use when processing DDA LC-MS mzXML data in which conventional peak picking (XCMS.featureTable with snthresh=6, prefilter=c(3,100)) has already run but low-intensity or poorly shaped peaks with detectable MS2 spectra were missed. Do not use when processing full-scan or DIA data — the README explicitly warns 'Please do not use this function when processing full-scan or DIA data set!' because MR recognition depends on DDA MS2 spectra. Do not use when the input is already an aligned feature table rather than per-file mzXML/raw data with associated MS2 spectra. Do not use before any PP feature extraction — MR features are found on top of an existing peak-picked feature table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Rescues metabolic features that XCMS peak picking missed by recognizing features with bad chromatographic peak shapes that nevertheless have tandem MS2 spectra, labeling them as 'MR' level features via JPA's find.level3features(). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12030212
skills.summary: Rescues metabolic features that XCMS peak picking missed by recognizing features with bad chromatographic peak shapes that nevertheless have tandem MS2 spectra, labeling them as 'MR' level features via JPA's find.level3features().
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use when processing full-scan or DIA data — the README explicitly warns 'Please do not use this function when processing full-scan or DIA data set!' because MR recognition depends on DDA MS2 spectra. Do not use when the input is already an aligned feature table rather than per-file mzXML/raw data with associated MS2 spectra. Do not use before any PP feature extraction — MR features are found on top of an existing peak-picked feature table.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS mzML files contain multiple MS2 scans per chromatographic feature and you need one representative MS2 spectrum per feature (m/z, RT) to feed formula assignment or ML-based annotation.
skills.name: ms2-representative-spectra-selection
skills.search_text: ms2-representative-spectra-selection Use when raw LC-MS/MS mzML files contain multiple MS2 scans per chromatographic feature and you need one representative MS2 spectrum per feature (m/z, RT) to feed formula assignment or ML-based annotation. Input is already a processed feature table with per-feature MS2 spectra — the original meat study case where processed spectra were missing required full replication, but a ready feature list makes this skill redundant Data are in negative ion mode or a non-LC-MS/MS acquisition, since the demonstrated evaluation focuses on positive ion mode LC–MS/MS data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Selects a single representative MS2 spectrum for each chromatographic feature detected from LC-MS/MS mzML files using MZmine3, so downstream formula/adduct assignment (SIRIUS v6.1.0) and metabolite annotation operate on one canonical spectrum per feature. Validated on the cultured-vs-conventional meat Metabolomics Workbench deposit, where ~900 features were detected. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.688047
skills.summary: Selects a single representative MS2 spectrum for each chromatographic feature detected from LC-MS/MS mzML files using MZmine3, so downstream formula/adduct assignment (SIRIUS v6.1.0) and metabolite annotation operate on one canonical spectrum per feature. Validated on the cultured-vs-conventional meat Metabolomics Workbench deposit, where ~900 features were detected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table with per-feature MS2 spectra — the original meat study case where processed spectra were missing required full replication, but a ready feature list makes this skill redundant Data are in negative ion mode or a non-LC-MS/MS acquisition, since the demonstrated evaluation focuses on positive ion mode LC–MS/MS data

skills.description: Use when a vendor-format raw LC-MS/MS file (e.g., from GNPS-MassIVE dataset MSV000083437) has been converted to .mzXML or .mzML and must be confirmed readable and MS2-scan-containing before molecular networking upload.
skills.name: ms2-scan-content-quality-checking
skills.search_text: ms2-scan-content-quality-checking Use when a vendor-format raw LC-MS/MS file (e.g., from GNPS-MassIVE dataset MSV000083437) has been converted to .mzXML or .mzML and must be confirmed readable and MS2-scan-containing before molecular networking upload. Input is still an unconverted vendor raw file — run the MSConvert conversion step first before quality-checking scan content Analysis requires calibrated quantitative information rather than qualitative MS2-based networking, since classic molecular networking uses only MS2 scans Input is already a processed feature table (e.g., MZmine2 output) rather than a spectrum-level converted data file Validates that vendor-raw LC-MS/MS data converted to open formats (.mzXML, .mzML, .mgf) via ProteoWizard MSConvert actually contain readable MS2-level scans, which are the required input for downstream GNPS molecular networking. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-020-0317-5
skills.summary: Validates that vendor-raw LC-MS/MS data converted to open formats (.mzXML, .mzML, .mgf) via ProteoWizard MSConvert actually contain readable MS2-level scans, which are the required input for downstream GNPS molecular networking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still an unconverted vendor raw file — run the MSConvert conversion step first before quality-checking scan content Analysis requires calibrated quantitative information rather than qualitative MS2-based networking, since classic molecular networking uses only MS2 scans Input is already a processed feature table (e.g., MZmine2 output) rather than a spectrum-level converted data file

skills.description: Use when you need to simulate or prototype a Top-N DDA acquisition method in ViMMS 2.0 — i.e. you have simulated chemicals or mzML-derived ROIs and must decide which MS1 precursors get fragmented in which MS2 scans at each point in the run.
skills.name: ms2-scan-parameter-scheduling
skills.search_text: ms2-scan-parameter-scheduling Use when you need to simulate or prototype a Top-N DDA acquisition method in ViMMS 2.0 — i.e. you have simulated chemicals or mzML-derived ROIs and must decide which MS1 precursors get fragmented in which MS2 scans at each point in the run. You want a data-independent acquisition (DIA) method such as All-ion-fragmentation or SWATH-MS — those are separate filter steps/controllers in ViMMS, not Top-N DDA scheduling. You need an adaptive/exclusion-weighted variant — use the provided SmartROIController or WeightedDEWController rather than writing a plain Top-N loop. You only need to replay existing acquisitions without changing the fragmentation strategy — ViMMS can virtually replay a previous LC-MS/MS analysis without implementing a new controller. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implements a Top-N DDA fragmentation strategy as a ViMMS 2.0 controller: subclass the base Controller class, override _process_scan to select the N most intense MS1 peaks (honouring dynamic exclusion, mz_tol/rt_tol and min_ms1_intensity), and return scheduled MS2 tasks as Scan Parameters that the Environment executes on an IndependentMassSpectrometer. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Implements a Top-N DDA fragmentation strategy as a ViMMS 2.0 controller: subclass the base Controller class, override _process_scan to select the N most intense MS1 peaks (honouring dynamic exclusion, mz_tol/rt_tol and min_ms1_intensity), and return scheduled MS2 tasks as Scan Parameters that the Environment executes on an IndependentMassSpectrometer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want a data-independent acquisition (DIA) method such as All-ion-fragmentation or SWATH-MS — those are separate filter steps/controllers in ViMMS, not Top-N DDA scheduling. You need an adaptive/exclusion-weighted variant — use the provided SmartROIController or WeightedDEWController rather than writing a plain Top-N loop. You only need to replay existing acquisitions without changing the fragmentation strategy — ViMMS can virtually replay a previous LC-MS/MS analysis without implementing a new controller.

skills.description: Use when QC-comparing the MS1/MS2 acquisition balance across Thermo RAW runs — e.g., diagnosing underperforming HeLa QC runs from MetaXtract scan-header CSVs where only the Scan Mode column is required.
skills.name: ms2-scan-proportion-computation
skills.search_text: ms2-scan-proportion-computation Use when QC-comparing the MS1/MS2 acquisition balance across Thermo RAW runs — e.g., diagnosing underperforming HeLa QC runs from MetaXtract scan-header CSVs where only the Scan Mode column is required. Identification-based QC is needed — this skill uses only acquisition-side scan headers and involves no database search results (unlike MSQC-style metrics). Input RAW files are not Thermo Fisher format — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW files. Only a single run is available with no comparison runs — the paper presents MS2 proportion as a comparative indicator between reference and underperforming runs, not an absolute pass/fail threshold. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes the percentage of MS2 scans relative to total scans per Thermo RAW run from MetaXtract scan-header exports (Scan Mode column) using pandas, providing a search-free acquisition-quality indicator that separated the paper's reference HeLa QC runs (60%, 62%) from underperforming runs (56%, 59%). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.687968
skills.summary: Computes the percentage of MS2 scans relative to total scans per Thermo RAW run from MetaXtract scan-header exports (Scan Mode column) using pandas, providing a search-free acquisition-quality indicator that separated the paper's reference HeLa QC runs (60%, 62%) from underperforming runs (56%, 59%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Identification-based QC is needed — this skill uses only acquisition-side scan headers and involves no database search results (unlike MSQC-style metrics). Input RAW files are not Thermo Fisher format — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW files. Only a single run is available with no comparison runs — the paper presents MS2 proportion as a comparative indicator between reference and underperforming runs, not an absolute pass/fail threshold.

skills.description: Use when you have LC/MS data with detected molecular features (feature table from xcms) plus centroided MS/MS scans, and you need to associate each MS2 spectrum with the correct feature to enable MS/MS spectral similarity or networking.
skills.name: ms2-scan-to-feature-association
skills.search_text: ms2-scan-to-feature-association Use when you have LC/MS data with detected molecular features (feature table from xcms) plus centroided MS/MS scans, and you need to associate each MS2 spectrum with the correct feature to enable MS/MS spectral similarity or networking. Input MS data has not yet been processed into a molecular feature table (no xcms feature detection has been run) The analysis goal is purely MS1-level statistical comparison of features without any fragmentation-based annotation Data are profile-mode and not centroided, so MS2 peaks cannot be matched at ppm-level tolerance http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Links centroided MS/MS (MS2) scans to molecular features from an xcms-generated feature table in Metaboseek (FindMS2ScansModule), so that averaged fragmentation spectra can be used for downstream molecular networking of differential metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: Links centroided MS/MS (MS2) scans to molecular features from an xcms-generated feature table in Metaboseek (FindMS2ScansModule), so that averaged fragmentation spectra can be used for downstream molecular networking of differential metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input MS data has not yet been processed into a molecular feature table (no xcms feature detection has been run) The analysis goal is purely MS1-level statistical comparison of features without any fragmentation-based annotation Data are profile-mode and not centroided, so MS2 peaks cannot be matched at ppm-level tolerance

skills.description: Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS/MS features beyond spectral-library hits by propagating annotations through a knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network connecting reaction-paired metabolites with similar MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: ms2-similarity-network-annotation
skills.search_text: ms2-similarity-network-annotation Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS/MS features beyond spectral-library hits by propagating annotations through a knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network connecting reaction-paired metabolites with similar MS/MS spectra. The goal is purely data-driven molecular networking (e.g., GNPS-style MS/MS similarity networks) — KGMN deliberately removes spectrally similar but hard-to-interpret connections Applying to non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples, since the predefined reaction sets (e.g., BioTransformer) mainly originate from human metabolic reactions and the article advises caution Distinguishing structurally similar isomers of an unknown (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which the MS2 similarity layer cannot effectively separate http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Builds the knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network — layer 2 of the KGMN workflow — which links peaks whose MS/MS spectra are similar and whose putative metabolites are reaction-paired, so that metabolite annotations propagate from library-matched knowns to unknown peaks in untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Builds the knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network — layer 2 of the KGMN workflow — which links peaks whose MS/MS spectra are similar and whose putative metabolites are reaction-paired, so that metabolite annotations propagate from library-matched knowns to unknown peaks in untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is purely data-driven molecular networking (e.g., GNPS-style MS/MS similarity networks) — KGMN deliberately removes spectrally similar but hard-to-interpret connections Applying to non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples, since the predefined reaction sets (e.g., BioTransformer) mainly originate from human metabolic reactions and the article advises caution Distinguishing structurally similar isomers of an unknown (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which the MS2 similarity layer cannot effectively separate

skills.description: Use when a feature table carries network-propagated level 3 annotations (e.g. MetDNA3 output on Orbitrap data) and you need to quantify how many annotations independent in-silico tools support.
skills.name: ms2-similarity-network-tool-comparison
skills.search_text: ms2-similarity-network-tool-comparison Use when a feature table carries network-propagated level 3 annotations (e.g. MetDNA3 output on Orbitrap data) and you need to quantify how many annotations independent in-silico tools support. Annotations are already level 1/2 confirmed with chemical standards — concordance testing adds no orthogonal information and cross-tool agreement would be circular Input features come from non-Orbitrap instruments not represented in the 20-dataset benchmark, so the 4,302-feature denominator and reported fractions do not apply You need de novo annotation rather than validation of existing network-based level 3 annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Cross-validates network-based (MetDNA3) level 3 metabolite annotations against four independent, non-network annotation tools (CFM-ID, MetFrag, MS-FINDER, SIRIUS) by matching features and counting consistent candidate metabolite/molecular formula assignments, reproducing the corroboration statistics of Fig. 4b–c. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6

skills.description: Use when you have positive-mode MS2 spectra (MGF or SIRIUS .ms) with no library match, need de novo candidate structures, or want to evaluate whether de novo candidates rival database-search annotations.

skills.search_text: ms2-spectra-de-novo-structure-generation Use when you have positive-mode MS2 spectra (MGF or SIRIUS .ms) with no library match, need de novo candidate structures, or want to evaluate whether de novo candidates rival database-search annotations. Input spectra are negative-mode MS2 — the model is only trained for positive-mode data, so performance is expected to be lower You only need formula annotation or compound-class level insight — SIRIUS/CANOPUS alone suffice and formula errors can exceed 50% for individual spectra up to m/z 800 Spectra have fewer than three fragment ions or isomers fragment indistinguishably, making structural elucidation not possible in all cases http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 De novo molecular structure identification from tandem MS (MS2) spectra: SIRIUS predicts the molecular formula, CSI:FingerID predicts a structural fingerprint, and an encoder–decoder RNN (MSNovelist) generates candidate SMILES constrained by formula, re-ranked by fingerprint match using the modified Platt score. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01486-3
skills.summary: De novo molecular structure identification from tandem MS (MS2) spectra: SIRIUS predicts the molecular formula, CSI:FingerID predicts a structural fingerprint, and an encoder–decoder RNN (MSNovelist) generates candidate SMILES constrained by formula, re-ranked by fingerprint match using the modified Platt score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are negative-mode MS2 — the model is only trained for positive-mode data, so performance is expected to be lower You only need formula annotation or compound-class level insight — SIRIUS/CANOPUS alone suffice and formula errors can exceed 50% for individual spectra up to m/z 800 Spectra have fewer than three fragment ions or isomers fragment indistinguishably, making structural elucidation not possible in all cases

skills.description: Use when tens of millions of MS/MS spectra (tens to hundreds of GB) must be merged into consensus spectra before peptide identification and CPU-only clustering tools like MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, or MaRaCluster are too slow.
skills.name: ms2-spectral-clustering
skills.search_text: ms2-spectral-clustering Use when tens of millions of MS/MS spectra (tens to hundreds of GB) must be merged into consensus spectra before peptide identification and CPU-only clustering tools like MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, or MaRaCluster are too slow. The data set is small enough that CPU-only tools (MaRaCluster, spectra-cluster) finish in acceptable time — HyperSpec's GPU requirement (CUDA, GTX 1080Ti/3090) is unnecessary overhead. No CUDA-capable GPU is available and the full PXD000561-scale clustering is needed, since the README states clustering PXD000561 'requires GTX 3090 with larger memory'. Precise peptide-level clustering quality is the sole priority and the trade-offs of fast tools (e.g., reduced quality seen for falcon and ClusterSheep) are unacceptable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Cluster large-scale MS/MS spectra (e.g., >21M spectra from PXD000561) by encoding them as binary hypervectors via hyperdimensional computing and clustering buckets on GPU with HyperSpec, cutting runtime from hours (~4 h with MaRaCluster) to ~24 min. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00612
skills.summary: Cluster large-scale MS/MS spectra (e.g., >21M spectra from PXD000561) by encoding them as binary hypervectors via hyperdimensional computing and clustering buckets on GPU with HyperSpec, cutting runtime from hours (~4 h with MaRaCluster) to ~24 min.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data set is small enough that CPU-only tools (MaRaCluster, spectra-cluster) finish in acceptable time — HyperSpec's GPU requirement (CUDA, GTX 1080Ti/3090) is unnecessary overhead. skills.description: Use when you need to compare metabolomics samples by their overall MS2 fragmentation content rather than aligned features — e.g. chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, or different LC/MS methods — or to flag spectrally dissimilar extracts for novelty prioritization.
skills.name: ms2-spectral-vectorization-memo
skills.search_text: ms2-spectral-vectorization-memo Use when you need to compare metabolomics samples by their overall MS2 fragmentation content rather than aligned features — e.g. chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, or different LC/MS methods — or to flag spectrally dissimilar extracts for novelty prioritization. Your samples have rich feature overlap and standard retention-time alignment suffices — MEMO suits chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap or strong RT shifts, so applying it there adds complexity without benefit. You need per-feature or annotated-structure comparison (e.g. FC based on non-annotated features) rather than a whole-sample MS2-spectrum-level comparison; the SC operates on unannotated peaks/neutral losses and does not use the feature alignment table. Your data are MS1-only with no MS2 fragmentation spectra — MEMO requires fragment spectra (MS2 peaks and precursor neutral losses) to build fingerprints. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Vectorizes metabolomics samples into MS2-based fingerprints using the MEMO metric — counting MS2 peaks and neutral losses per sample — then compares samples via an RT-agnostic dissimilarity matrix to detect spectrally dissimilar extracts (outliers) feeding the Inventa Similarity Component (SC). metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Vectorizes metabolomics samples into MS2-based fingerprints using the MEMO metric — counting MS2 peaks and neutral losses per sample — then compares samples via an RT-agnostic dissimilarity matrix to detect spectrally dissimilar extracts (outliers) feeding the Inventa Similarity Component (SC).

Your data are MS1-only with no MS2 fragmentation spectra — MEMO requires fragment spectra (MS2 peaks and precursor neutral losses) to build fingerprints.

skills.search_text: ms2-spectrum-clustering Use when processing raw MS2 peak lists (e.g. .mzXML) for classic molecular networking and a reduced set of representative consensus spectra is needed instead of redundant duplicate scans. skills.summary: Reconstructs the MS-Cluster consensus-clustering step of GNPS classic molecular networking, in which nearly identical MS2 spectra are collapsed into a single consensus spectrum (node) that becomes the input for network construction and spectral library searching.

Running Feature-Based Molecular Networking, where features rather than MS-Cluster consensus spectra define the nodes.

skills.search_text: ms2-spectrum-count-normalization Use when comparing untargeted metabolomics feature tables produced with different centWave parameter sets (AutoTuner- vs IPO-derived) and you need to test whether a feature subset is depleted for MS2 spectra after controlling for subset size. skills.name: msi-ion-image-augmentation
skills.search_text: msi-ion-image-augmentation Use when training a contrastive encoder on MSI ion images and you need augmentation pairs that reflect MSI priors — Poisson ion counts, missing values, or isotope-ion relationships — rather than generic image transforms. When the goal is identifying colocalized ions but the augmentation objective is not specifically isotope-ion contrastive training — the intensity-dependent missing-value step belongs to T_ISO only, so applying the full T_ISO pipeline in COL mode would contaminate the training distribution. When augmenting natural images (e.g. for standard SimSiam on photographs) — MSI-specific transforms like Poisson noise and missing-value masking are inappropriate there. When the input is already an embedding or feature table (e.g. after UMAP reduction to 20 dimensions) — augmentation must be applied to raw ion images before encoder training. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Applies DeepION's modality-specific augmentation pipelines T_COL and T_ISO to ion images from mass spectrometry imaging data, generating augmented views for contrastive training by simulating MSI characteristics (Poisson-distributed ion abundance, random and intensity-dependent missing patterns) rather than natural-image transforms alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Applies DeepION's modality-specific augmentation pipelines T_COL and T_ISO to ion images from mass spectrometry imaging data, generating augmented views for contrastive training by simulating MSI characteristics (Poisson-distributed ion abundance, random and intensity-dependent missing patterns) rather than natural-image transforms alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is identifying colocalized ions but the augmentation objective is not specifically isotope-ion contrastive training — the intensity-dependent missing-value step belongs to T_ISO only, so applying the full T_ISO pipeline in COL mode would contaminate the training distribution. When augmenting natural images (e.g. for standard SimSiam on photographs) — MSI-specific transforms like Poisson noise and missing-value masking are inappropriate there. When the input is already an embedding or feature table (e.g. after UMAP reduction to 20 dimensions) — augmentation must be applied to raw ion images before encoder training.

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed imzML dataset and need to extract an ion image at a specific m/z, or to overlay that ion image on a co-registered H&E stain for spatial localization review.
skills.name: msi-ion-image-extraction-and-overlay-visualization
skills.search_text: msi-ion-image-extraction-and-overlay-visualization Use when you have a preprocessed imzML dataset and need to extract an ion image at a specific m/z, or to overlay that ion image on a co-registered H&E stain for spatial localization review. Before the affine and B-spline registration of MSI to H&E has been applied — overlaying unregistered MSI on histology produces misleading spatial correspondence. When the MSI data has not been preprocessed (loaded via load_and_preprocess_imzml with create_intensity_matrix) — the extraction functions assume an intensity matrix input. For co-registration itself: this skill only extracts and overlays images; the actual alignment is done by register_he_msi and perform_bspline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Extract representative ion images from preprocessed MALDI-MSI data (imzML) and visualize them as single-panel images or as co-registered overlays on H&E histology using MSIght's mz-image extraction and overlay functions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Extract representative ion images from preprocessed MALDI-MSI data (imzML) and visualize them as single-panel images or as co-registered overlays on H&E histology using MSIght's mz-image extraction and overlay functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Before the affine and B-spline registration of MSI to H&E has been applied — overlaying unregistered MSI on histology produces misleading spatial correspondence. When the MSI data has not been preprocessed (loaded via load_and_preprocess_imzml with create_intensity_matrix) — the extraction functions assume an intensity matrix input. For co-registration itself: this skill only extracts and overlays images; the actual alignment is done by register_he_msi and perform_bspline.

skills.description: Use when you have MSI level 1 authentic-standard MS/MS identifications and need to quantify how accurately an in silico annotation tool (e.g., CSI:FingerID) ranks the true structure among its candidates.
skills.name: msi-level1-authentic-standard-validation
skills.search_text: msi-level1-authentic-standard-validation Use when you have MSI level 1 authentic-standard MS/MS identifications and need to quantify how accurately an in silico annotation tool (e.g., CSI:FingerID) ranks the true structure among its candidates. Spectra are not backed by authentic standards (e.g., MSI level 2 or level 3 annotations) — there is no ground-truth identity to validate against You need a confidence estimate for individual unknown spectra rather than a global accuracy benchmark of the annotation tool The acquisition platform, collision energies, or precursor mass tolerance differ substantially from the 5 ppm HILIC-Q Exactive HF conditions the benchmark was computed under http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates in silico structure annotations (e.g., CSI:FingerID top-ranked hits) by benchmarking them against MSI confidence level 1 identifications established with authentic standards using precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching. This yields a concrete top-hit accuracy figure for untargeted metabolomics annotation workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Validates in silico structure annotations (e.g., CSI:FingerID top-ranked hits) by benchmarking them against MSI confidence level 1 identifications established with authentic standards using precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching. This yields a concrete top-hit accuracy figure for untargeted metabolomics annotation workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are not backed by authentic standards (e.g., MSI level 2 or level 3 annotations) — there is no ground-truth identity to validate against You need a confidence estimate for individual unknown spectra rather than a global accuracy benchmark of the annotation tool The acquisition platform, collision energies, or precursor mass tolerance differ substantially from the 5 ppm HILIC-Q Exactive HF conditions the benchmark was computed under

skills.search_text: msi-matrix-reshaping-and-shape-validation Use when raw MSI matrices must be exported as a two-dimensional pixel-by-ion matrix plus a one-dimensional peak list and the horizontal/vertical pixel shape passed to DeepION's --input_shape must be verified. skills.summary: Reshape preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data into the [X*Y, P] pixel-by-ion matrix and [P,1] peak list that DeepION requires, then validate the grid dimensions (e.g. 198×422 positive-mode, 192×425 negative-mode rat brain sections) before running the model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated [X*Y, P] matrix with matching --input_shape dimensions — reshaping again is redundant and may corrupt the grid. Data are single spectra or profiles (not ion images); no pixel grid exists to validate.

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed MSI data with a measured m/z column and need to assign metabolite names and adduct forms by matching against an organ- and ion-mode-specific metabolite database.
skills.name: msi-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: msi-metabolite-annotation Use when you have preprocessed MSI data with a measured m/z column and need to assign metabolite names and adduct forms by matching against an organ- and ion-mode-specific metabolite database. The input is raw, unprocessed MSI data — the tool annotates processed MSI data only The metabolite database's organ or ion mode does not match the MSI dataset to be annotated (e.g., a liver positive-mode database against kidney negative-mode data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Annotate metabolites and adduct forms in preprocessed ambient mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data using the MATLAB script MSIannotator.m, which matches measured m/z values against an organ-specific, mode-specific metabolite database within a default 10 ppm m/z error range. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Annotate metabolites and adduct forms in preprocessed ambient mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data using the MATLAB script MSIannotator.m, which matches measured m/z values against an organ-specific, mode-specific metabolite database within a default 10 ppm m/z error range.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unprocessed MSI data — the tool annotates processed MSI data only The metabolite database's organ or ion mode does not match the MSI dataset to be annotated (e.g., a liver positive-mode database against kidney negative-mode data)

skills.description: Use when metabolite annotations from ambient MSI (e.g., AFADESI-MSI of mouse body sections) must be organized into per-organ membership/enrichment sets and compared across organs, ionization modes, or mouse strains.
skills.name: msi-metabolite-database-interpretation
skills.search_text: msi-metabolite-database-interpretation Use when metabolite annotations from ambient MSI (e.g., AFADESI-MSI of mouse body sections) must be organized into per-organ membership/enrichment sets and compared across organs, ionization modes, or mouse strains. Input is raw, unannotated MSI peak data — run MSIannotator.m first to obtain metabolite/adduct annotations before set-based organ comparison. The metabolite list comes from a single organ or tissue with no multi-organ panel — per-organ set-difference/intersection analysis needs the nine organ/serum sheets. You need m/z-level peak matching rather than interpreting already-annotated metabolite names — that is MSIannotator's 10 ppm matching step, not this interpretation skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Interprets organ-specific metabolite databases (1298 positive-mode and 515 negative-mode metabolites, Sheets 1–11 of 'Organ specific metabolite database.xlsx') using MATLAB set operations to determine whether metabolites are distributed organ-specifically across the whole mouse body and whether that pattern is conserved across mouse strains. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Interprets organ-specific metabolite databases (1298 positive-mode and 515 negative-mode metabolites, Sheets 1–11 of 'Organ specific metabolite database.xlsx') using MATLAB set operations to determine whether metabolites are distributed organ-specifically across the whole mouse body and whether that pattern is conserved across mouse strains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unannotated MSI peak data — run MSIannotator.m first to obtain metabolite/adduct annotations before set-based organ comparison. The metabolite list comes from a single organ or tissue with no multi-organ panel — per-organ set-difference/intersection analysis needs the nine organ/serum sheets. You need m/z-level peak matching rather than interpreting already-annotated metabolite names — that is MSIannotator's 10 ppm matching step, not this interpretation skill.

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed MSI feature list (measured m/z in column 1) must be annotated against an organ-specific metabolite database (metabolite name + theoretical m/z in specified adduct columns) with a controlled ppm tolerance.
skills.name: msi-mz-matching
skills.search_text: msi-mz-matching Use when a preprocessed MSI feature list (measured m/z in column 1) must be annotated against an organ-specific metabolite database (metabolite name + theoretical m/z in specified adduct columns) with a controlled ppm tolerance. Input is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed feature list whose first column already contains measured m/z — the script expects MSIdata already preprocessed. The organ sheet or detection mode of the supplied Database does not match the MSIdata to be annotated (e.g. a liver positive-mode database against a negative-mode dataset); the README explicitly requires checking this consistency before running. No user-supplied or built-in metabolite database with theoretical m/z in the required adduct forms exists for the target organ and ionization mode. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Matches measured m/z features in a preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) dataset against an organ-specific metabolite database using a ppm-based mass-error window, assigning each feature an annotated metabolite name and adduct form. Implemented as the MSIannotator.m MATLAB script, it underpins the AFADESI-MSI annotation workflow of Zhu et al. (Anal. Chem. 2022). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Matches measured m/z features in a preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) dataset against an organ-specific metabolite database using a ppm-based mass-error window, assigning each feature an annotated metabolite name and adduct form. Implemented as the MSIannotator.m MATLAB script, it underpins the AFADESI-MSI annotation workflow of Zhu et al. (Anal. Chem. 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed feature list whose first column already contains measured m/z — the script expects MSIdata already preprocessed. The organ sheet or detection mode of the supplied Database does not match the MSIdata to be annotated (e.g. a liver positive-mode database against a negative-mode dataset); the README explicitly requires checking this consistency before running. No user-supplied or built-in metabolite database with theoretical m/z in the required adduct forms exists for the target organ and ionization mode.

skills.search_text: msi-pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have a centroid-mode MSI peak matrix (e.g. rMSIproc .zip format) and need dimensionality reduction to visually compare data quality before and after a peak-removal step such as matrix-related signal removal. Input is already a processed feature table with non-MSI features whose physical relationships would justify unit-variance scaling (scaling was deliberately omitted here) The dataset is profile-mode raw spectra in imzML rather than a centroid-mode peak matrix; rMSIproc processing (smoothing, calibration, peak-picking) must be applied first http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply PCA (e.g. stats::prcomp) to mass spectrometry imaging peak matrices, centring data without scaling or normalization, and render the first three principal component scores per pixel as spatial RGB ion images to qualitatively assess spectral post-processing quality. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00449-0

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI section data (e.g. rat brain, positive or negative ion mode) must be converted into a validated pixel-by-ion intensity matrix with a paired peak list before running DeepION COL/ISO or similar ion-image representation models.
skills.name: msi-peak-filtering-pooling
skills.search_text: msi-peak-filtering-pooling Use when raw MALDI-MSI section data (e.g. rat brain, positive or negative ion mode) must be converted into a validated pixel-by-ion intensity matrix with a paired peak list before running DeepION COL/ISO or similar ion-image representation models. Input is already a preprocessed pixel-by-ion matrix with hotspot truncation and [0, 1] normalization applied (e.g. the DATASET/Pos_brain_data_matrix.txt DeepION expects) — re-filtering would distort intensities. The data are non-MSI spectral data or already-processed feature tables (e.g. labelled feature matrices for supervised classifiers) where SCiLS Lab peak picking and peak pooling have no meaning. Only a single ion image or sub-region is of interest without a full pixel-by-peak matrix; peak pooling across the section requires the complete SCiLS peak list. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Preprocess raw rat-brain MALDI mass spectrometry imaging data into a clean pixel-by-ion matrix: pick and align m/z peaks across pixels (SCiLS Lab), filter and pool spurious peaks with Python scripts, truncate hotspot pixels at 99% of each ion's maximum intensity, and min–max normalize each ion image to [0, 1]. This yields exactly the [X*Y, P] matrices DeepION consumes (2165 ions, 192×425 negative mode; 2263 ions, 198×422 positive mode). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Preprocess raw rat-brain MALDI mass spectrometry imaging data into a clean pixel-by-ion matrix: pick and align m/z peaks across pixels (SCiLS Lab), filter and pool spurious peaks with Python scripts, truncate hotspot pixels at 99% of each ion's maximum intensity, and min–max normalize each ion image to [0, 1]. This yields exactly the [X*Y, P] matrices DeepION consumes (2165 ions, 192×425 negative mode; 2263 ions, 198×422 positive mode).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed pixel-by-ion matrix with hotspot truncation and [0, 1] normalization applied (e.g. the DATASET/Pos_brain_data_matrix.txt DeepION expects) — re-filtering would distort intensities. The data are non-MSI spectral data or already-processed feature tables (e.g. labelled feature matrices for supervised classifiers) where SCiLS Lab peak picking and peak pooling have no meaning. Only a single ion image or sub-region is of interest without a full pixel-by-peak matrix; peak pooling across the section requires the complete SCiLS peak list.

skills.description: Use when raw MSI spectral data (imzML in profile mode) must be converted into a centroid-mode peak matrix and processed dataset suitable for matrix-related peak annotation.
skills.name: msi-peak-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: msi-peak-matrix-processing Use when raw MSI spectral data (imzML in profile mode) must be converted into a centroid-mode peak matrix and processed dataset suitable for matrix-related peak annotation. Input is already a rMSIproc-format peak matrix (.zip) and processed file (.tar) — e.g. the rMSIcleanup Sample Data Ag_Pancreas_TOF_2015_Dataset2 — which can be loaded directly. The goal is only to annotate or remove matrix-related peaks on an existing processed peak matrix; use rMSIcleanup's annotate_matrix / remove_matrix instead of re-processing spectra. Data normalization is required before downstream analysis — the paper's pipeline explicitly performs no normalization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Process raw MSI spectral data into a centroid-mode peak matrix using the rMSIproc pipeline, so that downstream annotation tools such as rMSIcleanup can consume a peak matrix (.zip) alongside processed spectra (.tar). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00449-0
skills.summary: Process raw MSI spectral data into a centroid-mode peak matrix using the rMSIproc pipeline, so that downstream annotation tools such as rMSIcleanup can consume a peak matrix (.zip) alongside processed spectra (.tar).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a rMSIproc-format peak matrix (.zip) and processed file (.tar) — e.g. the rMSIcleanup Sample Data Ag_Pancreas_TOF_2015_Dataset2 — which can be loaded directly. The goal is only to annotate or remove matrix-related peaks on an existing processed peak matrix; use rMSIcleanup's annotate_matrix / remove_matrix instead of re-processing spectra. Data normalization is required before downstream analysis — the paper's pipeline explicitly performs no normalization.

skills.description: Use when you have binned MSI peak data (CSV from SCiLS/MSiReader or an msimat object) and need to enumerate candidate adduct ion pairs by mass difference before adduct annotation and spatial correlation.
skills.name: msi-peak-pair-mass-difference-calculation
skills.search_text: msi-peak-pair-mass-difference-calculation Use when you have binned MSI peak data (CSV from SCiLS/MSiReader or an msimat object) and need to enumerate candidate adduct ion pairs by mass difference before adduct annotation and spatial correlation. Data are raw, unbinned spectra — peaks must already be binned (e.g. with Cardinal's peakBin()) before pairwise differences are meaningful You need statistical evidence of adduct identity rather than candidate enumeration — massdiff alone gives mass differences; follow with corrPairsMSI() spatial correlation Memory-constrained sessions with multi-Gb CSV matrices — use the msimunging.pl triplet-format reformatting or corrPairsMSIchunks instead of loading the full matrix directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Tabulate all pairwise mass differences between peaks in a MALDI-MSI peak table with mass2adduct's massdiff(), treating each difference as a candidate molecular adduct (e.g. metabolite–matrix adducts such as [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+) for downstream annotation and correlation testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: Tabulate all pairwise mass differences between peaks in a MALDI-MSI peak table with mass2adduct's massdiff(), treating each difference as a candidate molecular adduct (e.g. metabolite–matrix adducts such as [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+) for downstream annotation and correlation testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw, unbinned spectra — peaks must already be binned (e.g. with Cardinal's peakBin()) before pairwise differences are meaningful You need statistical evidence of adduct identity rather than candidate enumeration — massdiff alone gives mass differences; follow with corrPairsMSI() spatial correlation Memory-constrained sessions with multi-Gb CSV matrices — use the msimunging.pl triplet-format reformatting or corrPairsMSIchunks instead of loading the full matrix directly

skills.description: Use when segmenting peak-picked MSI pixel-by-feature intensity data (e.g. processed imzML loaded into Cardinal) into spatially coherent tissue regions and selecting the number of segments by scanning a regularization parameter.
skills.name: msi-peak-picked-intensity-analysis
skills.search_text: msi-peak-picked-intensity-analysis Use when segmenting peak-picked MSI pixel-by-feature intensity data (e.g. processed imzML loaded into Cardinal) into spatially coherent tissue regions and selecting the number of segments by scanning a regularization parameter. Locations must be assigned to pre-defined classes — this is unsupervised segmentation, not image classification; use Cardinal's supervised classification workflow instead Input is raw, unbinned spectra that still require normalization, smoothing, baseline reduction (reduceBaseline), or peak picking (peakPick) before intensities are peak-picked Input is already a feature table or per-segment summary — segmentation operates on pixel-level peak-picked intensities http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Unsupervised image segmentation of peak-picked mass spectrometry imaging data using Cardinal's spatialShrunkenCentroids with Spatially-Aware (gaussian) distance, which partitions tissue into homogeneous chemical segments without pre-defined class labels. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv146
skills.summary: Unsupervised image segmentation of peak-picked mass spectrometry imaging data using Cardinal's spatialShrunkenCentroids with Spatially-Aware (gaussian) distance, which partitions tissue into homogeneous chemical segments without pre-defined class labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Locations must be assigned to pre-defined classes — this is unsupervised segmentation, not image classification; use Cardinal's supervised classification workflow instead Input is raw, unbinned spectra that still require normalization, smoothing, baseline reduction (reduceBaseline), or peak picking (peakPick) before intensities are peak-picked Input is already a feature table or per-segment summary — segmentation operates on pixel-level peak-picked intensities

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI MSI sections must be converted into a common peak list and a [X*Y,P] ion-intensity matrix with normalized intensities before a representation model such as DeepION is trained.
skills.name: msi-peak-picking-alignment
skills.search_text: msi-peak-picking-alignment Use when raw MALDI MSI sections must be converted into a common peak list and a [X*Y,P] ion-intensity matrix with normalized intensities before a representation model such as DeepION is trained. Input is already a preprocessed [X*Y,P] matrix with a [P,1] peak list (DeepION-ready) — re-running peak picking/alignment would double-filter and alter expected ion counts. skills.summary: Preprocess raw rat brain mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data by peak picking with m/z alignment in SCiLS Lab, then filtering/pooling peaks in Python, hotspot truncation at 99% max intensity, and min–max normalization to [0,1] to yield a pixel-by-ion matrix plus peak list ready for DeepION.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed [X*Y,P] matrix with a [P,1] peak list (DeepION-ready) — re-running peak picking/alignment would double-filter and alter expected ion counts. Data are not raw MSI ion images (e.g. bulk spectra, LC-MS feature tables) — the SCiLS Lab peak-picking and pixel-grid reshaping steps assume spatial pixel coordinates.

skills.description: Use when co-registered MALDI MSI and immunofluorescence microscopy data are available and you need to assign lipids to marker-defined cell populations (e.g. Ly6G+ neutrophils in UPEC-infected bladder) via supervised pixel classification.
skills.name: msi-pixel-classification-by-ifm-marker
skills.search_text: msi-pixel-classification-by-ifm-marker Use when co-registered MALDI MSI and immunofluorescence microscopy data are available and you need to assign lipids to marker-defined cell populations (e.g. Ly6G+ neutrophils in UPEC-infected bladder) via supervised pixel classification. mziFlow does not include lipid annotation or interpretation — do not use this skill alone to assign identities to the ranked m/z features (use databases such as LipidMaps separately) Input data lacks co-registered IFM marker segmentation, so no pixel-level labels can be derived The goal is unsupervised spatial segmentation or molecular heterogeneity analysis — use msi_segmentation_flow or the UMAP-based workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Trains a tree-based (XGBoost) classifier on pixel-wise MALDI MSI mass spectra using binary labels derived from thresholded IFM marker segmentation (e.g. Ly6G for neutrophils), to identify lipid signatures such as ether-linked PCs that mark specific cell populations in tissue. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Trains a tree-based (XGBoost) classifier on pixel-wise MALDI MSI mass spectra using binary labels derived from thresholded IFM marker segmentation (e.g. Ly6G for neutrophils), to identify lipid signatures such as ether-linked PCs that mark specific cell populations in tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: mziFlow does not include lipid annotation or interpretation — do not use this skill alone to assign identities to the ranked m/z features (use databases such as LipidMaps separately) Input data lacks co-registered IFM marker segmentation, so no pixel-level labels can be derived The goal is unsupervised spatial segmentation or molecular heterogeneity analysis — use msi_segmentation_flow or the UMAP-based workflow instead

skills.description: Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (pixels x m/z ion columns) contains off-tissue/background pixels that must be removed before downstream clustering, e.g. when an intensity image shows clearly separable background signal.
skills.name: msi-pixel-filtering
skills.search_text: msi-pixel-filtering Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (pixels x m/z ion columns) contains off-tissue/background pixels that must be removed before downstream clustering, e.g. when an intensity image shows clearly separable background signal. Input is not a peak table matrix (first two columns X/Y coordinates followed by m/z intensity columns) — SMQVP's documented input format The goal is to filter noise IONS rather than background PIXELS — that is a separate SMQVP module (noise ion filtering) No tissue and background regions can be delineated, so tissue-enriched ions cannot be identified via the Wilcoxon rank-sum comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Background pixel removal for spatial metabolomics (SMQVP Process 2): construct a total-intensity image from tissue-enriched ions and apply a fixed total-intensity threshold (107.37 in the AFADESI mouse brain example) to remove background pixels from the peak table matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Background pixel removal for spatial metabolomics (SMQVP Process 2): construct a total-intensity image from tissue-enriched ions and apply a fixed total-intensity threshold (107.37 in the AFADESI mouse brain example) to remove background pixels from the peak table matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a peak table matrix (first two columns X/Y coordinates followed by m/z intensity columns) — SMQVP's documented input format The goal is to filter noise IONS rather than background PIXELS — that is a separate SMQVP module (noise ion filtering) No tissue and background regions can be delineated, so tissue-enriched ions cannot be identified via the Wilcoxon rank-sum comparison
