skills.name: msi-pixel-to-spot-binning
skills.search_text: msi-pixel-to-spot-binning Use when pairing pixel-resolution MALDI imaging mass spectrometry data with spot-based ST data (e.g. Visium) from the same tissue section, and a shared spot-level object is needed for multi-omic integration. When the SM and ST data are already at matching resolution (no pixel-to-spot aggregation needed) When analysing spatial metabolomics alone without any paired spatial-omics modality — SpaMTP still supports SM-only workflows, but binning is only needed for integration When working with single-cell-resolution SM data exported from METASPACE, where spot binning to 55 µm Visium geometry does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aligns an MALDI-TOF spatial metabolomics image (pixel-level imzML) onto paired spatial transcriptomics capture spots (e.g. 55 µm 10X Visium) and bins MALDI pixels into colocalised spots, producing a single Seurat object holding both 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays for integrative analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Aligns an MALDI-TOF spatial metabolomics image (pixel-level imzML) onto paired spatial transcriptomics capture spots (e.g. 55 µm 10X Visium) and bins MALDI pixels into colocalised spots, producing a single Seurat object holding both 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays for integrative analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the SM and ST data are already at matching resolution (no pixel-to-spot aggregation needed) When analysing spatial metabolomics alone without any paired spatial-omics modality — SpaMTP still supports SM-only workflows, but binning is only needed for integration When working with single-cell-resolution SM data exported from METASPACE, where spot binning to 55 µm Visium geometry does not apply

skills.description: Use when the input is an MSI dataset (imzML or Analyze 7.5) and the goal is unsupervised exploratory analysis to discover regions of interest, or when benchmarking the runtime cost of PCA on raw versus pre-processed/peak-picked spectra.
skills.name: msi-principal-component-analysis
skills.search_text: msi-principal-component-analysis Use when the input is an MSI dataset (imzML or Analyze 7.5) and the goal is unsupervised exploratory analysis to discover regions of interest, or when benchmarking the runtime cost of PCA on raw versus pre-processed/peak-picked spectra. The goal is supervised image classification or segmentation with predefined classes — Cardinal offers dedicated classification/segmentation methods based on nearest shrunken centroids and mixture modeling instead. Spectra have not undergone any pre-processing but a fully processed feature matrix is required downstream and peak picking has not yet been run — apply peakPick/peakProcess first for the runtime benefit. The data are not mass spectrometry imaging spectra (e.g. already a generic feature table unrelated to MSI). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Runs PCA on mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) spectra using Cardinal in R, computing the first N principal components (e.g. ncomp=20) on either raw or peak-picked spectra. Peak picking before PCA yields large speedups (reported ~4.3 s on picked peaks vs ~86.9 s raw for 20 components). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv146
skills.summary: Runs PCA on mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) spectra using Cardinal in R, computing the first N principal components (e.g. ncomp=20) on either raw or peak-picked spectra. Peak picking before PCA yields large speedups (reported ~4.3 s on picked peaks vs ~86.9 s raw for 20 components).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is supervised image classification or segmentation with predefined classes — Cardinal offers dedicated classification/segmentation methods based on nearest shrunken centroids and mixture modeling instead. Spectra have not undergone any pre-processing but a fully processed feature matrix is required downstream and peak picking has not yet been run — apply peakPick/peakProcess first for the runtime benefit. The data are not mass spectrometry imaging spectra (e.g. already a generic feature table unrelated to MSI).

skills.description: Use when an imzML/Analyze 7.5 MSI dataset has already been segmented (e.g. pig fetus liver/heart sections) and you need the per-segment enriched/absent peak counts and ranked peak tables.
skills.name: msi-segment-topfeatures-ranking
skills.search_text: msi-segment-topfeatures-ranking Use when an imzML/Analyze 7.5 MSI dataset has already been segmented (e.g. pig fetus liver/heart sections) and you need the per-segment enriched/absent peak counts and ranked peak tables. Input is raw spectra or a pre-processed imzML/Analyze 7.5 file that has not yet been segmented — run Cardinal image segmentation first, since topFeatures() operates on a fitted segmentation The goal is assigning pixels to pre-defined classes (image classification) rather than characterizing which ions distinguish segments of an unsupervised/supervised segmentation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Rank m/z peaks within each tissue segment of a fitted Cardinal spatial-shrunken-centroids segmentation by per-segment t-statistics from topFeatures(), labeling peaks as enriched (positive t) or absent (negative t) relative to the mean spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv146
skills.summary: Rank m/z peaks within each tissue segment of a fitted Cardinal spatial-shrunken-centroids segmentation by per-segment t-statistics from topFeatures(), labeling peaks as enriched (positive t) or absent (negative t) relative to the mean spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spectra or a pre-processed imzML/Analyze 7.5 file that has not yet been segmented — run Cardinal image segmentation first, since topFeatures() operates on a fitted segmentation The goal is assigning pixels to pre-defined classes (image classification) rather than characterizing which ions distinguish segments of an unsupervised/supervised segmentation

skills.description: Use when you have MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra (e.g. HDF5 with ~85,062 m/z variables) plus a pixel-level tumor-class prediction map, and you need to find and annotate the m/z peaks most co-localized with tumor tissue.
skills.name: msi-spatial-colocalization-analysis
skills.search_text: msi-spatial-colocalization-analysis Use when you have MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra (e.g. HDF5 with ~85,062 m/z variables) plus a pixel-level tumor-class prediction map, and you need to find and annotate the m/z peaks most co-localized with tumor tissue. Input is already a curated peak/feature table without spatial pixel-level ion images — Pearson colocalization with a class-prediction map requires reconstructed spatial patterns per peak. The classification task is multi-class or involves tissue types where ground-truth histology annotation is unreliable (the article demonstrates binary tumor/normal classification and notes intra-tumor heterogeneity limits ground-truth quality). You need absolute metabolite quantification — this skill yields tentative formula/adduct annotations with ppm error, not verified identifications. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Identifies tumor-associated m/z features in mass spectrometry imaging data by reconstructing spatial ion images from a VAE decoder and selecting peaks whose spatial patterns correlate with the predicted tumor-class map (Pearson correlation ≥ 0.7), followed by database annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Identifies tumor-associated m/z features in mass spectrometry imaging data by reconstructing spatial ion images from a VAE decoder and selecting peaks whose spatial patterns correlate with the predicted tumor-class map (Pearson correlation ≥ 0.7), followed by database annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated peak/feature table without spatial pixel-level ion images — Pearson colocalization with a class-prediction map requires reconstructed spatial patterns per peak. The classification task is multi-class or involves tissue types where ground-truth histology annotation is unreliable (the article demonstrates binary tumor/normal classification and notes intra-tumor heterogeneity limits ground-truth quality). You need absolute metabolite quantification — this skill yields tentative formula/adduct annotations with ppm error, not verified identifications.

skills.description: Use when you have a pixel-by-ion peak table (e.g., 53,812 pixels x 2,654 ions with X/Y coordinates in the first two columns) and need to visualize graph-based clustering (Louvain) results as spatial maps to validate preprocessing quality against tissue morphology.
skills.name: msi-spatial-visualization
skills.search_text: msi-spatial-visualization Use when you have a pixel-by-ion peak table (e.g., 53,812 pixels x 2,654 ions with X/Y coordinates in the first two columns) and need to visualize graph-based clustering (Louvain) results as spatial maps to validate preprocessing quality against tissue morphology. The peak table has already been spatially clustered and rendered — re-running adds no information The goal is quality assessment/preprocessing of raw MSI data itself (use SMQVP's quality visualization modules) rather than visualizing downstream clustering results The data lacks pixel X/Y coordinates, so cluster labels cannot be mapped back to spatial positions http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Render spatially resolved visualizations of mass-spec imaging clustering results by mapping pixel cluster labels back to X/Y coordinates, so that spatial regions (e.g., mouse brain neuroanatomy) can be compared against H&E-stained morphology as a quality check on preprocessing. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Render spatially resolved visualizations of mass-spec imaging clustering results by mapping pixel cluster labels back to X/Y coordinates, so that spatial regions (e.g., mouse brain neuroanatomy) can be compared against H&E-stained morphology as a quality check on preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak table has already been spatially clustered and rendered — re-running adds no information The goal is quality assessment/preprocessing of raw MSI data itself (use SMQVP's quality visualization modules) rather than visualizing downstream clustering results The data lacks pixel X/Y coordinates, so cluster labels cannot be mapped back to spatial positions

skills.description: Use when training a self-supervised contrastive encoder (e.g., SimSiam with ResNet18 backbone) on MSI ion images and you must generate augmented view pairs whose noise model matches the Poisson-distributed ion abundance and random/intensity-dependent missing patterns of MSI data.
skills.name: msi-specific-data-augmentation-design
skills.search_text: msi-specific-data-augmentation-design Use when training a self-supervised contrastive encoder (e.g., SimSiam with ResNet18 backbone) on MSI ion images and you must generate augmented view pairs whose noise model matches the Poisson-distributed ion abundance and random/intensity-dependent missing patterns of MSI data. When the input is a single image per sample and generic computer-vision augmentation suffices — this skill's T_COL/T_ISO exist specifically to mirror MSI's Poisson-distributed ion abundance and random/intensity-dependent missing values. When the goal is downstream similarity scoring rather than representation learning: augmentation feeds encoder training, but the identification step itself runs on the UMAP-reduced 20-dimensional vectors, not on the augmented images. When the input is raw (unpreprocessed) MSI data: the augmentation module expects the preprocessed MSI matrix [X*Y, P] and peak list [P, 1] already prepared by preprocessing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Design modality-specific data augmentation for contrastive learning on mass spectrometry imaging ion images: T_COL (color jitter, filtering, Poisson noise, random missing value) for colocalized-ion mode and T_ISO (adding intensity-dependent missing value) for isotope mode, so the SimSiam encoder learns meaningful ion-image representations without manual annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Design modality-specific data augmentation for contrastive learning on mass spectrometry imaging ion images: T_COL (color jitter, filtering, Poisson noise, random missing value) for colocalized-ion mode and T_ISO (adding intensity-dependent missing value) for isotope mode, so the SimSiam encoder learns meaningful ion-image representations without manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is a single image per sample and generic computer-vision augmentation suffices — this skill's T_COL/T_ISO exist specifically to mirror MSI's Poisson-distributed ion abundance and random/intensity-dependent missing values. When the goal is downstream similarity scoring rather than representation learning: augmentation feeds encoder training, but the identification step itself runs on the UMAP-reduced 20-dimensional vectors, not on the augmented images. When the input is raw (unpreprocessed) MSI data: the augmentation module expects the preprocessed MSI matrix [X*Y, P] and peak list [P, 1] already prepared by preprocessing.

skills.description: Use when you have raw MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) with ground-truth normal/tumor labels and a trained massNet model, and need probabilistic binary pixel-level classification plus ROC AUC, accuracy, confusion matrix, and runtime.
skills.name: msi-spectrum-binary-classification-inference
skills.search_text: msi-spectrum-binary-classification-inference Use when you have raw MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) with ground-truth normal/tumor labels and a trained massNet model, and need probabilistic binary pixel-level classification plus ROC AUC, accuracy, confusion matrix, and runtime. The task requires multi-class tissue classification — the article demonstrates only binary (normal/tumor) classification and explicitly leaves multi-class extension to future development The input is already a preprocessed, peak-picked feature table — massNet's core advantage is probabilistic pixel-based classification directly from raw high-dimensional mass spectral data without prior peak picking No trained massNet model or reproducible ground-truth annotation is available — the article notes ground-truth annotation of MSI data is a challenging task for other tissues and tumor types http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs the trained massNet deep learning model (VAE encoder plus sigmoid-activated classifier on a 5-dimensional latent variable) directly on raw MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra to obtain normal/tumor class probabilities without any prior preprocessing or peak picking, then evaluates robustness with standard classification metrics and runtime benchmarks. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Runs the trained massNet deep learning model (VAE encoder plus sigmoid-activated classifier on a 5-dimensional latent variable) directly on raw MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra to obtain normal/tumor class probabilities without any prior preprocessing or peak picking, then evaluates robustness with standard classification metrics and runtime benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires multi-class tissue classification — the article demonstrates only binary (normal/tumor) classification and explicitly leaves multi-class extension to future development The input is already a preprocessed, peak-picked feature table — massNet's core advantage is probabilistic pixel-based classification directly from raw high-dimensional mass spectral data without prior peak picking No trained massNet model or reproducible ground-truth annotation is available — the article notes ground-truth annotation of MSI data is a challenging task for other tissues and tumor types

skills.description: Use when many misaligned serial MSI tissue sections (e.g., H5-serialized 3D MSI like coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) must be aligned to a reference MRI/atlas for volumetric reconstruction and per-brain-region profiling.
skills.name: msi-to-mri-multimodal-image-registration
skills.search_text: msi-to-mri-multimodal-image-registration Use when many misaligned serial MSI tissue sections (e.g., H5-serialized 3D MSI like coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) must be aligned to a reference MRI/atlas for volumetric reconstruction and per-brain-region profiling. Input is a single already-aligned 2D MSI section with no serial-section misalignment to correct — the multimodal registration pipeline addresses incoherent registration across serial sections in large 3D MSI datasets Reference modality is not an anatomical MRI/atlas (e.g., single-cell or tissue-only analysis such as SCMS cross-annotation does not require MRI registration) Modalities cannot yield mutually informative feature images (e.g., no parametric UMAP embedding can produce grayscale anatomical contrast between MSI and MRI) http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Registers serial 2D mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) sections of a reconstructed 3D rat brain volume to T2*-weighted MRI slices from the Waxholm Space atlas via affine plus cubic B-spline registration, enabling coherent volumetric reconstruction and quantitative regional chemical profiling. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Registers serial 2D mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) sections of a reconstructed 3D rat brain volume to T2*-weighted MRI slices from the Waxholm Space atlas via affine plus cubic B-spline registration, enabling coherent volumetric reconstruction and quantitative regional chemical profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single already-aligned 2D MSI section with no serial-section misalignment to correct — the multimodal registration pipeline addresses incoherent registration across serial sections in large 3D MSI datasets Reference modality is not an anatomical MRI/atlas (e.g., single-cell or tissue-only analysis such as SCMS cross-annotation does not require MRI registration) Modalities cannot yield mutually informative feature images (e.g., no parametric UMAP embedding can produce grayscale anatomical contrast between MSI and MRI)

skills.description: Use when an integrated spatial transcriptome/MALDI-MSI object (haCCA b_predict with X feature matrix and D spatial matrix) is available and the goal is to test whether a gene's spatial expression distribution overlaps a specific metabolite's intensity distribution.
skills.name: msi-transcriptome-integrated-data-interpretation
skills.search_text: msi-transcriptome-integrated-data-interpretation Use when an integrated spatial transcriptome/MALDI-MSI object (haCCA b_predict with X feature matrix and D spatial matrix) is available and the goal is to test whether a gene's spatial expression distribution overlaps a specific metabolite's intensity distribution. The transcriptome and MALDI-MSI sections have not yet been aligned/integrated by haCCA (no b_predict) — interpretability of spot-to-spot overlap is not meaningful before integration The metabolite of interest has no intensity features represented in the aligned MALDI-MSI matrix (no shared features to map onto spots) The analysis target is cross-modality integration/alignment itself rather than downstream biological interpretation of an already-integrated object http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Interpret haCCA-integrated mouse-brain data (b_predict), in which MALDI-MSI metabolite intensities (e.g. dopamine, 3-MT) are mapped onto 10X Visium transcriptome spot coordinates, by rendering spatial metabolite maps and quantifying co-localization with candidate genes (e.g. Th) to nominate gene–metabolite associations. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: Interpret haCCA-integrated mouse-brain data (b_predict), in which MALDI-MSI metabolite intensities (e.g. dopamine, 3-MT) are mapped onto 10X Visium transcriptome spot coordinates, by rendering spatial metabolite maps and quantifying co-localization with candidate genes (e.g. Th) to nominate gene–metabolite associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The transcriptome and MALDI-MSI sections have not yet been aligned/integrated by haCCA (no b_predict) — interpretability of spot-to-spot overlap is not meaningful before integration The metabolite of interest has no intensity features represented in the aligned MALDI-MSI matrix (no shared features to map onto spots) The analysis target is cross-modality integration/alignment itself rather than downstream biological interpretation of an already-integrated object

skills.description: Use when a matrix-related peak-annotation method for AgLDI/silver-nanolayer MSI needs a ground-truth list to validate classification performance, or when Table 2-style theoretical Ag peak masses must be reproduced.
skills.name: msi-validation-list-curation
skills.search_text: msi-validation-list-curation Use when a matrix-related peak-annotation method for AgLDI/silver-nanolayer MSI needs a ground-truth list to validate classification performance, or when Table 2-style theoretical Ag peak masses must be reproduced. The goal is to annotate/remove matrix peaks in an already-processed peak matrix — that is rMSIcleanup's annotate_matrix/remove_matrix workflow, not list curation The MSI dataset was acquired without a silver-sputtered nanolayer, so silver-cluster and silver-adduct peaks are not the relevant chemical space A different LDI-promoting material (not silver) is used; the positive/negative class definitions are silver-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Curates a ground-truth validation list of possible and not-possible silver-related peaks (positive class: Ag clusters; negative class: silver salts, diatomic salts and silver adducts of lipids/waxes) for benchmarking AgLDI MSI peak-classification algorithms such as rMSIcleanup. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00449-0
skills.summary: Curates a ground-truth validation list of possible and not-possible silver-related peaks (positive class: Ag clusters; negative class: silver salts, diatomic salts and silver adducts of lipids/waxes) for benchmarking AgLDI MSI peak-classification algorithms such as rMSIcleanup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to annotate/remove matrix peaks in an already-processed peak matrix — that is rMSIcleanup's annotate_matrix/remove_matrix workflow, not list curation The MSI dataset was acquired without a silver-sputtered nanolayer, so silver-cluster and silver-adduct peaks are not the relevant chemical space A different LDI-promoting material (not silver) is used; the positive/negative class definitions are silver-specific

skills.description: Use when MALDI MSI (optionally multimodal with IFM) data must be processed through an automated, reproducible workflow — e.g. pixel-wise statistical comparison of lipid intensities between infected and control groups within tissue ROIs.
skills.name: msiflow-workflow-configuration-and-execution
skills.search_text: msiflow-workflow-configuration-and-execution Use when MALDI MSI (optionally multimodal with IFM) data must be processed through an automated, reproducible workflow — e.g. pixel-wise statistical comparison of lipid intensities between infected and control groups within tissue ROIs. msiFlow does not include an annotation or interpretation step — do not expect lipid ID annotation (beyond preliminary mass matching, e.g. LipidMaps) from these workflows Scaling to other MSI modalities such as metabolomics and proteomics is anticipated but not demonstrated — avoid assuming out-of-the-box support If the analysis requires the exact landmark-based registration accuracy of laser ablation marks, the automated registration approach may be less accurate than desired http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Configure and run msiFlow's Snakemake workflows (e.g. msi_preprocessing_flow, msi_segmentation_flow, region_group_analysis_flow) to carry out end-to-end, reproducible MALDI MSI analysis from raw data import to statistical comparison of ROIs between sample groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Configure and run msiFlow's Snakemake workflows (e.g. msi_preprocessing_flow, msi_segmentation_flow, region_group_analysis_flow) to carry out end-to-end, reproducible MALDI MSI analysis from raw data import to statistical comparison of ROIs between sample groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: msiFlow does not include an annotation or interpretation step — do not expect lipid ID annotation (beyond preliminary mass matching, e.g. LipidMaps) from these workflows Scaling to other MSI modalities such as metabolomics and proteomics is anticipated but not demonstrated — avoid assuming out-of-the-box support If the analysis requires the exact landmark-based registration accuracy of laser ablation marks, the automated registration approach may be less accurate than desired

skills.search_text: mslevel-collision-energy-annotation Use when converting Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE or mzML profile-mode data to Parquet/HDF5 with arcMS and you need to preserve and exploit the low vs high collision energy (MS1/MS2) distinction for filtering and chromatogram/spectrum queries. Input data are centroided feature tables or peak lists where MS level is already resolved — arcMS conversion operates on profile-mode mzML or raw UNIFI data The target format is HDF5 and you only need one energy level — reading the ms1 or ms2 dataset directly is simpler than filtering a combined table http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Annotates each spectral datapoint in converted HRMS data with an mslevel discriminator separating low collision energy (MS1) from high collision energy (MS2) scans, so downstream Arrow/dplyr filtering (e.g. TIC, EIC) can operate on the correct energy level in Parquet files produced by arcMS. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae160

skills.description: Use when training CFM-ID 4.0's learned (MSML) predictor on QTOF ESI-MS/MS spectra at 10/20/40 eV, or when benchmarking in silico compound identification (MS2C) on CASMI 2016 category-3 Orbitrap/QTOF data.
skills.name: msml-model-training-on-qtof-spectra
skills.search_text: msml-model-training-on-qtof-spectra Use when training CFM-ID 4.0's learned (MSML) predictor on QTOF ESI-MS/MS spectra at 10/20/40 eV, or when benchmarking in silico compound identification (MS2C) on CASMI 2016 category-3 Orbitrap/QTOF data. Input spectra were collected on instruments other than QTOF instruments — the authors note they plan to adapt CFM-ID to handle other instruments, so Orbitrap/QQQ data must first be converted or handled differently The task is EI-MS/MS (electron ionization) spectral prediction — the MSML/QTOF training pipeline described here covers ESI-MS/MS, not EI Only a handful of training spectra are available for the compound classes of interest — the learned predictor needs large Metlin-scale training sets; hand-written rule-based prediction may be the better route http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Train CFM-ID 4.0's MSML machine-learning spectral predictor on QTOF ESI-MS/MS data (Metlin 2019 [M+H]+ and [M-H]- sets) using an adjacency/connectivity-matrix molecular representation, then use the trained models to predict spectra and rank candidate compounds for identification benchmarks such as CASMI 2016. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Train CFM-ID 4.0's MSML machine-learning spectral predictor on QTOF ESI-MS/MS data (Metlin 2019 [M+H]+ and [M-H]- sets) using an adjacency/connectivity-matrix molecular representation, then use the trained models to predict spectra and rank candidate compounds for identification benchmarks such as CASMI 2016.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra were collected on instruments other than QTOF instruments — the authors note they plan to adapt CFM-ID to handle other instruments, so Orbitrap/QQQ data must first be converted or handled differently The task is EI-MS/MS (electron ionization) spectral prediction — the MSML/QTOF training pipeline described here covers ESI-MS/MS, not EI Only a handful of training spectra are available for the compound classes of interest — the learned predictor needs large Metlin-scale training sets; hand-written rule-based prediction may be the better route

skills.search_text: msml-neural-network-retraining Use when observed MS/MS spectra come from a non-QTOF instrument (e.g. Orbitrap HCD) and the stock CFM-ID 4.0 QTOF-trained MSML model must be recalibrated before in silico spectral prediction and candidate ranking. skills.description: Use when PeakBot has annotated walls/background signals in blank or background LC-HRMS samples and you need a targeted DDA exclusion list to boost MS/MS coverage of true chromatographic peaks in subsequent runs.
skills.name: msms-exclusion-list-generation
skills.search_text: msms-exclusion-list-generation Use when PeakBot has annotated walls/background signals in blank or background LC-HRMS samples and you need a targeted DDA exclusion list to boost MS/MS coverage of true chromatographic peaks in subsequent runs. The task is standard peak picking/feature detection only and no MS/MS acquisition is planned — use PeakBot's detection/grouping workflow (detect.py, group.py) without compiling an exclusion list. Chromatograms are already reduced to a feature table or peak list without profile-mode data — PeakBot operates on profile-mode LC-HRMS data (rt × m/z local maxima), so no wall annotations can be extracted. No blank/background samples are available, or walls are absent from the sample background — the exclusion list is derived from PeakBot's wall-type background annotations, so it cannot be built. If you need MS/MS exclusion lists from sources other than PeakBot wall annotations (e.g. in-source ions, reporter ions), this workflow is not designed for that. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Generates an MS/MS exclusion list (msms_exclusion_list.tsv) from PeakBot's CNN-detected wall/background annotations of LC-HRMS blank samples, so that co-eluting background signals are excluded from fragmentation and MS/MS coverage of true chromatographic peaks increases. The workflow was validated against the paper's Supplementary Table S2, where coverage rose from 1356 to 1605 (negative mode) and 855 to 1810 (positive mode). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Generates an MS/MS exclusion list (msms_exclusion_list.tsv) from PeakBot's CNN-detected wall/background annotations of LC-HRMS blank samples, so that co-eluting background signals are excluded from fragmentation and MS/MS coverage of true chromatographic peaks increases. The workflow was validated against the paper's Supplementary Table S2, where coverage rose from 1356 to 1605 (negative mode) and 855 to 1810 (positive mode).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is standard peak picking/feature detection only and no MS/MS acquisition is planned — use PeakBot's detection/grouping workflow (detect.py, group.py) without compiling an exclusion list. Chromatograms are already reduced to a feature table or peak list without profile-mode data — PeakBot operates on profile-mode LC-HRMS data (rt × m/z local maxima), so no wall annotations can be extracted. No blank/background samples are available, or walls are absent from the sample background — the exclusion list is derived from PeakBot's wall-type background annotations, so it cannot be built. If you need MS/MS exclusion lists from sources other than PeakBot wall annotations (e.g. in-source ions, reporter ions), this workflow is not designed for that.

skills.name: msms-fingerprint-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: msms-fingerprint-prediction-evaluation Use when a study has MS/MS spectra left unannotated by spectral library search (e.g. IDSL.CSA vs NIST 20/LipidBlast) and you need to quantify annotation gains from predicted-fingerprint structure matching. The spectra are already annotated by library search — this skill targets MS/MS spectra with no hit in existing mass spectral libraries (>80% of spectra typically lack library hits) You need de novo structure elucidation rather than ranking against a fixed reference database (LipidMaps); the method can only annotate compounds represented in the searched database No reference structure database or its SMILES/InChI entries are available to compute Tanimoto similarity against http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluate a deep-learning MS/MS-to-fingerprint model (e.g. IDSL_MINT) by predicting molecular fingerprint descriptors from unannotated MS/MS spectra, searching them against a reference structure database (LipidMaps) via Tanimoto similarity, and tabulating how many new annotations are added beyond spectral library search. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00804-5
skills.summary: Evaluate a deep-learning MS/MS-to-fingerprint model (e.g. IDSL_MINT) by predicting molecular fingerprint descriptors from unannotated MS/MS spectra, searching them against a reference structure database (LipidMaps) via Tanimoto similarity, and tabulating how many new annotations are added beyond spectral library search.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are already annotated by library search — this skill targets MS/MS spectra with no hit in existing mass spectral libraries (>80% of spectra typically lack library hits) You need de novo structure elucidation rather than ranking against a fixed reference database (LipidMaps); the method can only annotate compounds represented in the searched database No reference structure database or its SMILES/InChI entries are available to compute Tanimoto similarity against

skills.description: Use when you have ranked candidate molecular formulas per MS/MS spectrum (from FSA or a comparable ranker) and need to quantify rank#1 accuracy, top-5 accuracy, and per-spectrum runtime against known metabolite ground truth.
skills.name: msms-formula-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: msms-formula-accuracy-benchmarking Use when you have ranked candidate molecular formulas per MS/MS spectrum (from FSA or a comparable ranker) and need to quantify rank#1 accuracy, top-5 accuracy, and per-spectrum runtime against known metabolite ground truth. When the input spectra are already converted to a feature table or have known formulas for all peaks — this skill only evaluates candidate-formula ranking, it does not extract features or confirm formulas structurally. When the goal is to identify compounds by MS/MS spectral library match or in-silico structure prediction (e.g. using CFM-ID 4.0 or SIRIUS spectra) — this skill benchmarks formula-ranking accuracy, not structural identification. When compound scope includes elements outside C, H, O, N, S, P, or F, Cl, Br, I (e.g. metals, organometallics) — the reference formula list and the paper's validation did not cover such compositions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark metabolite molecular-formula ranking accuracy and runtime for FSA against a published reference (85.28% rank#1, 97.35% top-5, 0.024 s/spectrum over 30,690 MS/MS spectra), including stress-test variants such as expanding the PubChem reference list with halogen elements (F, Cl, Br, I). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-025-02379-0
skills.summary: Benchmark metabolite molecular-formula ranking accuracy and runtime for FSA against a published reference (85.28% rank#1, 97.35% top-5, 0.024 s/spectrum over 30,690 MS/MS spectra), including stress-test variants such as expanding the PubChem reference list with halogen elements (F, Cl, Br, I).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input spectra are already converted to a feature table or have known formulas for all peaks — this skill only evaluates candidate-formula ranking, it does not extract features or confirm formulas structurally. When the goal is to identify compounds by MS/MS spectral library match or in-silico structure prediction (e.g. using CFM-ID 4.0 or SIRIUS spectra) — this skill benchmarks formula-ranking accuracy, not structural identification. When compound scope includes elements outside C, H, O, N, S, P, or F, Cl, Br, I (e.g. metals, organometallics) — the reference formula list and the paper's validation did not cover such compositions.

skills.description: Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for derivatized unsaturated sterols (or other C=C-containing molecules) to support matching of LC-IM-MS/MS features against a reference lipid database.
skills.name: msms-fragment-annotation
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-annotation Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for derivatized unsaturated sterols (or other C=C-containing molecules) to support matching of LC-IM-MS/MS features against a reference lipid database. Molecules lacking C=C double bonds, since the script recognizes double bond positions and only sterol lipids have been tested Spectra matching against an already-built fragment database — use the downstream 4D data-processing/identification workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Generates theoretical MS/MS fragment patterns for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids by recognizing C=C double bond positions and applying N-Me fragmentation rules, providing the fragment-ion dimension of the 4D sterol lipid database used for isomer-level identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/anie.202507483
skills.summary: Generates theoretical MS/MS fragment patterns for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids by recognizing C=C double bond positions and applying N-Me fragmentation rules, providing the fragment-ion dimension of the 4D sterol lipid database used for isomer-level identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Molecules lacking C=C double bonds, since the script recognizes double bond positions and only sterol lipids have been tested Spectra matching against an already-built fragment database — use the downstream 4D data-processing/identification workflow instead

skills.description: Use when raw MS2 spectra (e.g. from beer-extract or other complex-mixture LC-MS/MS runs) must be converted into the fragment-and-neutral-loss bag-of-words documents that LDA/MS2LDA topic modeling consumes.
skills.name: msms-fragment-bag-of-words-corpus-construction
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-bag-of-words-corpus-construction Use when raw MS2 spectra (e.g. from beer-extract or other complex-mixture LC-MS/MS runs) must be converted into the fragment-and-neutral-loss bag-of-words documents that LDA/MS2LDA topic modeling consumes. Input data is already a processed peak/feature table or motif-decomposed spectra (no LDA corpus construction needed). Only a single simple-mixture MS2 spectrum with sparse fragments is available; MS2LDA works best for complex mixtures with information-rich MS2 spectra such as ramped or stepped collision energy data, not low-fragmentation single-spectrum input. Downstream analysis requires neutral-loss information via spectral-matching tools that do not support losses; corpus construction with losses is fine, but if the pipeline target is pure spectral matching (no topic modeling), omitting the corpus step is more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Constructs an LDA-ready corpus from MS2 spectra by representing each MS1 peak's fragmentation spectrum as a bag of words built from m/z-binned fragments and derived neutral losses, the preprocessing step that MS2LDA requires before topic-model inference. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Constructs an LDA-ready corpus from MS2 spectra by representing each MS1 peak's fragmentation spectrum as a bag of words built from m/z-binned fragments and derived neutral losses, the preprocessing step that MS2LDA requires before topic-model inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is already a processed peak/feature table or motif-decomposed spectra (no LDA corpus construction needed). Only a single simple-mixture MS2 spectrum with sparse fragments is available; MS2LDA works best for complex mixtures with information-rich MS2 spectra such as ramped or stepped collision energy data, not low-fragmentation single-spectrum input. Downstream analysis requires neutral-loss information via spectral-matching tools that do not support losses; corpus construction with losses is fine, but if the pipeline target is pure spectral matching (no topic modeling), omitting the corpus step is more appropriate.

skills.description: Use when comparing MS/MS spectra of several features from an .mgf file to see which fragment m/z values and neutral losses they share in one heatmap view.
skills.name: msms-fragment-binning-and-factorization
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-binning-and-factorization Use when comparing MS/MS spectra of several features from an .mgf file to see which fragment m/z values and neutral losses they share in one heatmap view. You only need pairwise similarity scores (ms2deepscore, modified cosine, spec2vec) rather than a fragment-level overlap view — those are computed separately in the importing pipeline. Input spectra are not in .mgf format; specXplore currently requires .mgf-formatted MS/MS data (convert e.g. via MZmine3 export first). Only one spectrum is of interest — with a single spectrum there is no cross-spectral overlap to display and a fragmap adds nothing over a plain spectrum plot. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Bins the mass-to-charge ratios of MS/MS fragments from multiple spectra, sorts the bins ascending, and factorizes them so crowded m/z regions are split and empty space between distant fragments is removed — the data-preparation step behind specXplore's fragmentation overview (fragmap) heatmap. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Bins the mass-to-charge ratios of MS/MS fragments from multiple spectra, sorts the bins ascending, and factorizes them so crowded m/z regions are split and empty space between distant fragments is removed — the data-preparation step behind specXplore's fragmentation overview (fragmap) heatmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need pairwise similarity scores (ms2deepscore, modified cosine, spec2vec) rather than a fragment-level overlap view — those are computed separately in the importing pipeline. Input spectra are not in .mgf format; specXplore currently requires .mgf-formatted MS/MS data (convert e.g. via MZmine3 export first). Only one spectrum is of interest — with a single spectrum there is no cross-spectral overlap to display and a fragmap adds nothing over a plain spectrum plot.

skills.description: Use when UNIFI-exported .xlsx MS/MS spectra of reference standards need to be converted into a fragment datatable stratified by standard and collision energy (20/40/60 eV).
skills.name: msms-fragment-data-extraction
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-data-extraction Use when UNIFI-exported .xlsx MS/MS spectra of reference standards need to be converted into a fragment datatable stratified by standard and collision energy (20/40/60 eV). Input is in silico predicted fragment data (CFM-ID predictions) rather than experimentally acquired MS/MS spectra — those belong in the predicted-fragments datatable Spectra were not acquired at the three specified collision energies (20, 40, 60 eV), so entries cannot align with the deposited datatable's energy stratification The goal is de novo spectrum interpretation rather than reproducing/curating the reference-standard fragment library Extracts fragment-ion entries from UNIFI-exported .xlsx MS/MS spectra files of 15 DNA adduct reference standards, acquired at three collision energies (20, 40, 60 eV), and reorganizes them into one searchable datatable row per fragment ion for a DNA adductomics spectral library. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Extracts fragment-ion entries from UNIFI-exported .xlsx MS/MS spectra files of 15 DNA adduct reference standards, acquired at three collision energies (20, 40, 60 eV), and reorganizes them into one searchable datatable row per fragment ion for a DNA adductomics spectral library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is in silico predicted fragment data (CFM-ID predictions) rather than experimentally acquired MS/MS spectra — those belong in the predicted-fragments datatable Spectra were not acquired at the three specified collision energies (20, 40, 60 eV), so entries cannot align with the deposited datatable's energy stratification The goal is de novo spectrum interpretation rather than reproducing/curating the reference-standard fragment library

skills.description: Use when LC–MS/MS spectra (.mgf) are embedded via an ms2deepscore similarity matrix and you need to characterize how much of the fragmentation signal is shared among spectra in a dense local neighborhood around a feature of interest.
skills.name: msms-fragment-ion-overlap-quantification
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-ion-overlap-quantification Use when LC–MS/MS spectra (.mgf) are embedded via an ms2deepscore similarity matrix and you need to characterize how much of the fragmentation signal is shared among spectra in a dense local neighborhood around a feature of interest. The dataset exceeds ~5000 features after preprocessing — the article reports the dashboard is only expected to scale to 5000 features and is untested beyond that The goal is fully automated annotation rather than manual fragmentation-overlap-driven structural hypothesis generation — the article frames overlap analysis as a starting point for manual annotation efforts ms2deepscore scores are needed but the underlying compound class is poorly covered by or unrelated to the ms2deepscore training data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies pairwise MS/MS fragment-ion overlap within a densely connected similarity neighborhood (e.g., around a reference-standard feature such as Procyanidin-A2), exposing shared fragmentation patterns that, together with local topology and metadata, seed structural hypothesis generation and manual annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Quantifies pairwise MS/MS fragment-ion overlap within a densely connected similarity neighborhood (e.g., around a reference-standard feature such as Procyanidin-A2), exposing shared fragmentation patterns that, together with local topology and metadata, seed structural hypothesis generation and manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset exceeds ~5000 features after preprocessing — the article reports the dashboard is only expected to scale to 5000 features and is untested beyond that The goal is fully automated annotation rather than manual fragmentation-overlap-driven structural hypothesis generation — the article frames overlap analysis as a starting point for manual annotation efforts ms2deepscore scores are needed but the underlying compound class is poorly covered by or unrelated to the ms2deepscore training data

skills.description: Use when public/commercial MS/MS libraries lack spectra for a compound class (e.g., <50 acylcarnitine structures) and MSI level 2 annotation requires predicted fragment ions.
skills.name: msms-fragment-ion-prediction
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-ion-prediction Use when public/commercial MS/MS libraries lack spectra for a compound class (e.g., <50 acylcarnitine structures) and MSI level 2 annotation requires predicted fragment ions. Compound class is already covered by experimental spectra and authentic standards are available for MSI level 1 identification (precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching) Input is a single unknown spectrum without any template class or formula constraint — use de novo fragmentation-tree tools rather than a template-derived library Goal is confirmation of already-annotated metabolites rather than annotation of the previously unannotated spectral space Predict tandem MS/MS fragment ions from chemical structure templates to build spectral libraries (CarniBlast-style for acylcarnitines, LipidBlast-style rules) or run in silico fragmentation (CSI:FingerID), enabling structure annotation where experimental libraries are sparse. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Predict tandem MS/MS fragment ions from chemical structure templates to build spectral libraries (CarniBlast-style for acylcarnitines, LipidBlast-style rules) or run in silico fragmentation (CSI:FingerID), enabling structure annotation where experimental libraries are sparse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compound class is already covered by experimental spectra and authentic standards are available for MSI level 1 identification (precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS matching) Input is a single unknown spectrum without any template class or formula constraint — use de novo fragmentation-tree tools rather than a template-derived library Goal is confirmation of already-annotated metabolites rather than annotation of the previously unannotated spectral space

skills.description: Use when you have chained MS/MS fragment ion-intensity profiles of two (or more) isomeric compounds across multiple collision energies and need per-fragment similarity scores to distinguish them.
skills.name: msms-fragment-lfp-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-lfp-similarity-scoring Use when you have chained MS/MS fragment ion-intensity profiles of two (or more) isomeric compounds across multiple collision energies and need per-fragment similarity scores to distinguish them. Only a single MS/MS spectrum per compound is available (no multi-collision-energy profiles) — cross-sectional algorithms like entropy similarity or dot product are the appropriate choice instead The goal is general metabolite identification against a spectral library rather than pairwise isomer differentiation — the full identification pipeline (ROC-derived criteria, CQMU database) is needed, not just pairwise LFP scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes longitudinal Jaccard similarity between fragment ion-intensity profiles (LFPs) of compound pairs measured across 13 collision energies plus the stepped NCE 20/40/60% combined spectrum, to differentiate isomers such as leucine/isoleucine that cross-sectional spectral matching cannot separate. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: Computes longitudinal Jaccard similarity between fragment ion-intensity profiles (LFPs) of compound pairs measured across 13 collision energies plus the stepped NCE 20/40/60% combined spectrum, to differentiate isomers such as leucine/isoleucine that cross-sectional spectral matching cannot separate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single MS/MS spectrum per compound is available (no multi-collision-energy profiles) — cross-sectional algorithms like entropy similarity or dot product are the appropriate choice instead The goal is general metabolite identification against a spectral library rather than pairwise isomer differentiation — the full identification pipeline (ROC-derived criteria, CQMU database) is needed, not just pairwise LFP scoring

skills.description: Reference for building or extending metabolite fragment libraries when new experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. MassBank records such as MSBNK-RIKEN-PR100295 for Pantothenic acid [M+H]+) must be converted into scored .csv entries for MetaboAnnotatoR.
skills.name: msms-fragment-library-generation
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-library-generation Reference for building or extending metabolite fragment libraries when new experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. MassBank records such as MSBNK-RIKEN-PR100295 for Pantothenic acid [M+H]+) must be converted into scored .csv entries for MetaboAnnotatoR. The goal is annotating features from AIF LC–MS chromatograms rather than building the fragment library itself — that is the separate MetaboAnnotatoR annotation workflow, not library generation. Input spectra are in formats other than .msp and not raw experimental MS/MS peak lists supported by genFragEntry (the README lists only experimental spectra and .msp conversion as supported entry-generation paths). Target data were acquired on a different DIA scheme such as SWATH — the article notes only AIF is currently supported, so library entries tuned for AIF annotation may not transfer directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates MetaboAnnotatoR metabolite fragment-library entries from experimental MS/MS spectra — either raw centroid spectra or MassBank-style .msp records — by attributing occurrence scores to marker (fragment) peaks and writing scored .csv library entries used for AIF LC–MS feature annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Generates MetaboAnnotatoR metabolite fragment-library entries from experimental MS/MS spectra — either raw centroid spectra or MassBank-style .msp records — by attributing occurrence scores to marker (fragment) peaks and writing scored .csv library entries used for AIF LC–MS feature annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating features from AIF LC–MS chromatograms rather than building the fragment library itself — that is the separate MetaboAnnotatoR annotation workflow, not library generation. Input spectra are in formats other than .msp and not raw experimental MS/MS peak lists supported by genFragEntry (the README lists only experimental spectra and .msp conversion as supported entry-generation paths). Target data were acquired on a different DIA scheme such as SWATH — the article notes only AIF is currently supported, so library entries tuned for AIF annotation may not transfer directly.

skills.description: Use when an aligned feature table contains m/z and retention-time pairs whose monoisotopic precursor masses need compound-level annotation via MS/MS spectral matching against an online MassBank library.
skills.name: msms-fragment-library-searching
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-library-searching Use when an aligned feature table contains m/z and retention-time pairs whose monoisotopic precursor masses need compound-level annotation via MS/MS spectral matching against an online MassBank library. Input is raw .mzML data that has not yet gone through MSS peak picking (mssmain.peak_pick) and alignment — fragment matching expects an aligned feature table No MS/MS spectra are available for the features (the workflow relies on MS/MS fragment spectra uploaded to MoNA) Candidate formula prediction is needed for molecules above 500 Da — MSS formula prediction supports small molecules under 500 Da http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compound identification by uploading individual or averaged MS/MS spectra through the MSS fragment module (frag.py) to the MassBank of North America (MoNA) online database and retrieving matches following MassBank search criteria, as a stage of MSS's HRMS non-targeted analysis workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00741-9
skills.summary: Compound identification by uploading individual or averaged MS/MS spectra through the MSS fragment module (frag.py) to the MassBank of North America (MoNA) online database and retrieving matches following MassBank search criteria, as a stage of MSS's HRMS non-targeted analysis workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw .mzML data that has not yet gone through MSS peak picking (mssmain.peak_pick) and alignment — fragment matching expects an aligned feature table No MS/MS spectra are available for the features (the workflow relies on MS/MS fragment spectra uploaded to MoNA) Candidate formula prediction is needed for molecules above 500 Da — MSS formula prediction supports small molecules under 500 Da

skills.description: Use when building targeted PRM/MRM or DIA assays for lipids and you must enumerate precursor-to-fragment transitions (m/z, adduct, charge) for lipid classes rather than measuring them experimentally.
skills.name: msms-fragment-mass-enumeration
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-mass-enumeration Use when building targeted PRM/MRM or DIA assays for lipids and you must enumerate precursor-to-fragment transitions (m/z, adduct, charge) for lipid classes rather than measuring them experimentally. The goal is untargeted lipid discovery or de novo identification — LipidCreator intentionally does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids, peak area integration, or false discovery rate scoring, offering only knowledge-based transition list selection. Target lipids are from bacteria such as E. coli (acyl-PG, acyl-PE) or archaea, where explicit lack of standards means the eukaryotic-focused knowledge base is not covered. The task requires stereoisomer-resolved quantification — no large-scale methods exist to cope with stereoisomers due to lack of isotope-coded standards. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Enumerate targeted lipidomics precursor and MS/MS fragment transition lists by assembling head groups, fatty acyl chains/long chain bases, and adducts per lipid class, computing monoisotopic masses and class-specific fragment ions — the core computation performed by LipidCreator's knowledge-base for over 61 lipid classes spanning 10^12 lipid molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Enumerate targeted lipidomics precursor and MS/MS fragment transition lists by assembling head groups, fatty acyl chains/long chain bases, and adducts per lipid class, computing monoisotopic masses and class-specific fragment ions — the core computation performed by LipidCreator's knowledge-base for over 61 lipid classes spanning 10^12 lipid molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is untargeted lipid discovery or de novo identification — LipidCreator intentionally does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids, peak area integration, or false discovery rate scoring, offering only knowledge-based transition list selection. Target lipids are from bacteria such as E. coli (acyl-PG, acyl-PE) or archaea, where explicit lack of standards means the eukaryotic-focused knowledge base is not covered. The task requires stereoisomer-resolved quantification — no large-scale methods exist to cope with stereoisomers due to lack of isotope-coded standards.

skills.description: Decision support for whether CFM-ID predicted fragments can back annotation of DNA adducts in HRMS adductomics when experimental MS/MS spectra exist only for a subset (e.g. 15 of 582) of database entries.
skills.name: msms-fragment-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-overlap-analysis Decision support for whether CFM-ID predicted fragments can back annotation of DNA adducts in HRMS adductomics when experimental MS/MS spectra exist only for a subset (e.g. 15 of 582) of database entries. No experimental MS/MS spectra exist for the adducts of interest — the comparison degenerates and overlap cannot be computed. The spectra were acquired on a low-resolution instrument whose mass accuracy cannot support the high-resolution tolerance assumed for qTOF fragment matching. A preliminary spectral library already exists for the adducts; annotation should then rely on measured spectra rather than predicted-fragment overlap. Assess agreement between CFM-ID in-silico MS/MS fragment predictions and experimental tandem HRMS/MS spectra of DNA adduct reference standards, quantifying fragment overlap to validate using predicted fragments for DNA adduct annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2022.908572
skills.summary: Assess agreement between CFM-ID in-silico MS/MS fragment predictions and experimental tandem HRMS/MS spectra of DNA adduct reference standards, quantifying fragment overlap to validate using predicted fragments for DNA adduct annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No experimental MS/MS spectra exist for the adducts of interest — the comparison degenerates and overlap cannot be computed. The spectra were acquired on a low-resolution instrument whose mass accuracy cannot support the high-resolution tolerance assumed for qTOF fragment matching. A preliminary spectral library already exists for the adducts; annotation should then rely on measured spectra rather than predicted-fragment overlap.

skills.description: Use when you have centroided LC/MS data (mzML) with a feature table and MS2 scans, and a known diagnostic product ion (e.g., m/z 333.0592) to screen for structurally related features across many spectra.
skills.name: msms-fragment-pattern-search
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-pattern-search Use when you have centroided LC/MS data (mzML) with a feature table and MS2 scans, and a known diagnostic product ion (e.g., m/z 333.0592) to screen for structurally related features across many spectra. You need confident (Level 1/2) compound identifications — this pattern search supports only tentative annotations; the article notes Metaboseek facilitates metabolite annotation only up to confidence Level 3. You only have MS1 data with no associated MS2 scans — the MS2 Browser linkage and pattern search require fragmentation spectra. Your goal is de novo formula prediction or spectral library matching rather than screening for a known diagnostic fragment motif. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Search MS2 spectra of LC/MS molecular features in Metaboseek's Find Patterns module (FindPatternsModule) for a diagnostic fragment-ion pattern, exemplified by the GLEA-characteristic product ion at m/z 333.0592 plus phosphoglycerol- and glucose-derived fragments, to rapidly flag structurally related metabolites across molecular subnetworks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-28391-9
skills.summary: Search MS2 spectra of LC/MS molecular features in Metaboseek's Find Patterns module (FindPatternsModule) for a diagnostic fragment-ion pattern, exemplified by the GLEA-characteristic product ion at m/z 333.0592 plus phosphoglycerol- and glucose-derived fragments, to rapidly flag structurally related metabolites across molecular subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need confident (Level 1/2) compound identifications — this pattern search supports only tentative annotations; the article notes Metaboseek facilitates metabolite annotation only up to confidence Level 3. You only have MS1 data with no associated MS2 scans — the MS2 Browser linkage and pattern search require fragmentation spectra. Your goal is de novo formula prediction or spectral library matching rather than screening for a known diagnostic fragment motif.

skills.description: Use when annotating an LC-MS/MS peak (e.g. negative-mode peak M386T77, m/z 385.1118, RT 1.27 min) by matching its fragment peaks to a candidate metabolite's reference fragments within a 10 ppm tolerance to obtain an MS/MS score.
skills.name: msms-fragment-peak-matching
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-peak-matching Use when annotating an LC-MS/MS peak (e.g. negative-mode peak M386T77, m/z 385.1118, RT 1.27 min) by matching its fragment peaks to a candidate metabolite's reference fragments within a 10 ppm tolerance to obtain an MS/MS score. The input is already a quantified feature table or downstream statistical result — this skill only scores spectral annotation evidence for raw peaks No reference fragment spectra or candidate annotation database is available for the metabolite, so fragment matching cannot be performed The analysis is not plant metabolomics and requires a non-plant metabolite reference space beyond what PlantMetSuite's plant-specific database covers http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Matches acquired MS/MS fragment peaks against a candidate metabolite's reference fragments to compute a fragment-match score that feeds PlantMetSuite's integrated metabolite annotation scoring (Equation (3)). Rationale: reproducible fragment-level matching with explicit ppm tolerances is the core evidence component for assigning a metabolite identity to an LC-MS/MS peak. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/plants12152880
skills.summary: Matches acquired MS/MS fragment peaks against a candidate metabolite's reference fragments to compute a fragment-match score that feeds PlantMetSuite's integrated metabolite annotation scoring (Equation (3)). Rationale: reproducible fragment-level matching with explicit ppm tolerances is the core evidence component for assigning a metabolite identity to an LC-MS/MS peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a quantified feature table or downstream statistical result — this skill only scores spectral annotation evidence for raw peaks No reference fragment spectra or candidate annotation database is available for the metabolite, so fragment matching cannot be performed The analysis is not plant metabolomics and requires a non-plant metabolite reference space beyond what PlantMetSuite's plant-specific database covers

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data are acquired at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and isomers with similar substructures must be distinguished, so a single cross-sectional spectrum match is insufficient.
skills.name: msms-fragment-profile-matching
skills.search_text: msms-fragment-profile-matching Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data are acquired at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and isomers with similar substructures must be distinguished, so a single cross-sectional spectrum match is insufficient. skills.search_text: msms-fragmentation-candidate-ranking Use when a challenge provides MS/MS peak lists (possibly merged across collision energies) with a known elemental composition, and candidate structures must be retrieved from PubChem and ranked without reference spectra. The unknown's high-energy fragment peaks require more than 3 bond dissociations to explain (as in challenge 16, where peaks such as m/z=122.0408 and m/z=221.07309 remained unexplained) — extend the fragmentation level instead of ranking with defaults. A reference spectral library is available and library matching is sufficient; MAGMa's substructure annotation is designed for the absence of informative reference spectra. The correct compound is likely to carry a very low PubChem refscore — stepwise refscore filtering can eliminate it, as happened for challenge 3's N2-acetyl glutaminyl leucinamide (refscore 1) once lists dropped below 200 molecules. Rank candidate chemical structures for an unknown MS/MS spectrum by matching observed peaks against in silico generated substructures (up to 3 bond dissociations) of PubChem candidates, yielding intensity-weighted penalty scores, with PubChem refscore used to break score ties and to stepwise filter oversized candidate lists. metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033

skills.search_text: msms-noise-denoising Use when raw MS/MS query spectra (e.g., AD plasma from Orbitrap Astral or Exploris 240) contain electronic and chemical noise ions, and the goal is higher-confidence compound annotation via spectral library matching with entropy similarity. Mass analyzer is not an Orbitrap instrument — the method is optimized for Orbitrap and adapting it requires retuning and validating parameters The analysis goal requires differentiating isomeric compounds or in-source fragments, or compound confirmation via retention time / cross-section / biological metadata — MS/MS-only matching after denoising cannot resolve these Reference spectra or query spectra have inherently low spectral entropy (e.g., <0.5, fewer than two fragment ions) — such spectra are vulnerable to noise ions and prone to false negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Two-stage MS/MS spectrum cleaning — electronic denoising (removing 'grass' noise ions) and chemical denoising (removing ions not explainable by plausible subformula losses) — plus Denoising Search, which pseudo-denoises query spectra against reference library candidates to boost compound annotations in plasma metabolomics/exposomics on Orbitrap instruments. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x

skills.search_text: msms-noise-filtering Use when raw MS2 fragmentation spectra paired to MS1 peaks contain noisy fragment or neutral-loss entries that must be removed before building a bag-of-fragments matrix or running topic-model inference. Input is already a cleaned, aligned feature table or count matrix — re-filtering would discard valid features. The goal is library spectral matching against MassBank or NIST: the 90% normalized-score matching path does not consume the noise-filtered motif vocabulary, and neutral losses are not supported by spectral matching tools. Data are information-poor MS2 spectra (few metabolites fragmented, single fixed collision energy) where the MS2LDA preprocessing and inference chain underperforms. Cleans paired MS1–MS2 fragmentation spectra by removing noise entries from fragment and neutral-loss lists using the MS2LDA preprocessing module (load_and_clean), so that only reliable MS2 features feed downstream corpus generation and LDA inference. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Cleans paired MS1–MS2 fragmentation spectra by removing noise entries from fragment and neutral-loss lists using the MS2LDA preprocessing module (load_and_clean), so that only reliable MS2 features feed downstream corpus generation and LDA inference.

skills.name: msms-noise-ion-simulation
skills.search_text: msms-noise-ion-simulation Use when benchmarking MS/MS library-matching similarity scores for robustness: you have cleaned, centroided reference spectra and need to quantify score degradation as artificial noise ions are added at graded levels. When the goal is library search accuracy or false discovery rate benchmarking against NIST20 (434,287 spectra) rather than noise-robustness characterization of a similarity score When noise in the real data is chemical/matrix interference or signal-dependent noise rather than randomly added ions with uniformly sampled m/z and Poisson (lambda=1) intensity contributions When input spectra are profile-mode or lack precursor m/z metadata, since the workflow requires centroided peaks and precursor-ion removal above precursor_mz - 1.6 Da Simulates graded artificial noise-ion contamination on centroided NIST20 MS/MS reference spectra (m/z uniformly sampled, Poisson-distributed intensities) and quantifies how entropy similarity degrades versus dot product (cosine) similarity as noise levels increase. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01331-z

skills.name: msms-pairwise-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: msms-pairwise-similarity-computation Use when you have MS/MS spectra (MGF files) from a spectral library or extract library and need pairwise similarity scores that reflect structural relatedness, e.g., to build a molecular network or find structural analogues beyond cosine-based matching. When a conventional, heuristic similarity is sufficient and fully interpretable by construction (e.g., Cosine or Modified Cosine for simple aligned-peak comparisons) — TransExION is a deep-learning model whose scores require the trained model checkpoint When you do not have a trained TransExION model and cannot train one: training additionally requires structural (Tanimoto) similarity matrices computed with ms_compute_structural_similarity.py from known structures When inputs are not MS/MS peak lists (e.g., raw LC-MS/MS instrument files) — MGF conversion must happen first http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute all-pairs spectral similarity between MS/MS spectra using the pre-trained TransExION Transformer model, whose scores correlate with structural similarity and can feed downstream molecular networking (e.g., meRgeION) or spectral library analogue search. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Compute all-pairs spectral similarity between MS/MS spectra using the pre-trained TransExION Transformer model, whose scores correlate with structural similarity and can feed downstream molecular networking (e.g., meRgeION) or spectral library analogue search.

skills.search_text: msms-peak-filtering Use when raw MS/MS peak sets from spectra in a molecular network component must be preprocessed before MMSA multiple spectral alignment, e.g. to reduce noise and outlier intensity effects prior to consensus peak identification. The input is already an aligned consensus peak set or alignment JSON from a completed MMSA run — filtering at that stage would discard aligned signal. skills.name: msms-peak-fragment-matching
skills.search_text: msms-peak-fragment-matching Use when you have a measured HR-MS/MS peak list and a set of candidate structures, and need to rank candidates by how well their in silico fragments explain the product ions. skills.search_text: msms-peak-post-processing-filtering Use when a predicted ESI-MS/MS peak list (CFM-ID 4.0/3.0/2.0 output at 10, 20, 40 eV) must be trimmed to a canonical form before comparing against experimental Metlin QTOF spectra with peak-match metrics. skills.summary: Rank candidate precursor molecular formulas for LC-MS/MS metabolites using the Formula Subset Analysis (FSA) algorithm, which scores formulas from mass-difference relationships (MDRs) among fragment formulas — no training data or MS/MS spectral databases required.

skills.description: Use when processing high-dimensional LC-IMS-MS/MS data where MS2 fragment ions must be attributed to MS1 precursors, especially when retention time alone is insufficient to separate coeluting species and drift time must be jointly considered.
skills.name: msms-precursor-fragment-association
skills.search_text: msms-precursor-fragment-association Use when processing high-dimensional LC-IMS-MS/MS data where MS2 fragment ions must be attributed to MS1 precursors, especially when retention time alone is insufficient to separate coeluting species and drift time must be jointly considered. When the data are low-dimensional (only m/z and retention time, no drift time) — the paper shows that m/z versus RT followed by DT yields poor agreement and that retention time alone produces false assignments between 77 and 83 Da attributed to the m/z 212 precursor. When MS2 fragments have already been extracted and deconvolved — re-running association on an already deconvolved spectrum would double-count convolution artifacts rather than mitigate them. When the goal is feature detection or CCS calibration rather than fragment-to-precursor attribution — those are separate DEIMoS workflow steps. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Associates MS2 fragment ions with their MS1 precursor ions by computing multidimensional cosine similarity scores across the non-m/z separation dimensions (drift time and retention time) of LC-IMS-MS/MS data, using DEIMoS deconvolution to mitigate convolution artifacts in tandem mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Associates MS2 fragment ions with their MS1 precursor ions by computing multidimensional cosine similarity scores across the non-m/z separation dimensions (drift time and retention time) of LC-IMS-MS/MS data, using DEIMoS deconvolution to mitigate convolution artifacts in tandem mass spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data are low-dimensional (only m/z and retention time, no drift time) — the paper shows that m/z versus RT followed by DT yields poor agreement and that retention time alone produces false assignments between 77 and 83 Da attributed to the m/z 212 precursor. When MS2 fragments have already been extracted and deconvolved — re-running association on an already deconvolved spectrum would double-count convolution artifacts rather than mitigate them. skills.description: Use when cleaning raw MS/MS spectra prior to formula identification — e.g., converting m/z to monoisotopic Da via adduct correction and removing spurious precursor-adjacent and contamination peaks.

skills.search_text: msms-precursor-mass-filtering Use when cleaning raw MS/MS spectra prior to formula identification — e.g., converting m/z to monoisotopic Da via adduct correction and removing spurious precursor-adjacent and contamination peaks. skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra from untargeted metabolomics have no level 1 hit from an authentic-standard library and you need MSI level 2 annotations from public or in-silico spectral libraries without retention time confirmation.

skills.search_text: msms-precursor-mass-matching Use when MS/MS spectra from untargeted metabolomics have no level 1 hit from an authentic-standard library and you need MSI level 2 annotations from public or in-silico spectral libraries without retention time confirmation. When authentic standards exist for a spectrum: precursor mass + retention time + MS/MS matching against the in-house standard library must be used first (MSI level 1), not mass-only level 2 matching. skills.summary: Annotate MS/MS spectra at MSI level 2 by matching precursor accurate mass and MS/MS fragment ions against MoNA, NIST17, NIST hybrid search, and the CarniBlast acylcarnitine library, yielding 578 level 2 annotations for urine metabolomics data acquired on HILIC- and CSH-Q Exactive HF instruments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When authentic standards exist for a spectrum: precursor mass + retention time + MS/MS matching against the in-house standard library must be used first (MSI level 1), not mass-only level 2 matching. skills.description: Use when assessing day-to-day MS/MS product ion consistency from DDA-acquired system suitability (SST) data where stochastic precursor triggering makes raw product ion intensities incomparable across scans and acquisitions.

skills.search_text: msms-product-ion-intensity-normalization Use when assessing day-to-day MS/MS product ion consistency from DDA-acquired system suitability (SST) data where stochastic precursor triggering makes raw product ion intensities incomparable across scans and acquisitions. skills.when_to_use_negative: When only MS1-level metrics (retention time, extracted ion chromatogram peak areas) are needed — MS1 queries suffice without product-ion normalization When MS/MS scans are triggered deterministically (e.g. targeted PRM/SRM) rather than stochastically by DDA, since the normalization rationale targets DDA triggering variability When the goal is absolute quantification of fragment ion intensities — normalization to total scan signal deliberately discards absolute intensity information
