skills.search_text: msms-query-spectrum-processing Use when MS/MS query spectra from an annotated molecular network (GNPS/MassIVE) need per-spectrum molecular formula and structure identification, or when benchmarking a new annotation method against SIRIUS. Input is raw LC-MS/MS acquisition data rather than deconvoluted, library-annotated query spectra from an annotated molecular network node The query compound is not represented in the structural database (bioDB), since annotation is only evaluated for compounds present there The goal is de novo biotransformation-based annotation of unknown suspects (use BAM instead) rather than database-restricted formula/structure identification http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Prepare MS/MS query spectra from a global molecular network anchor–suspect data set and run SIRIUS 5.6.3 molecular formula and structure annotation against bioDB, establishing a baseline annotation rate (4756 correct formulas / 4560 correct structures out of 38,368 queries). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01565
skills.summary: Prepare MS/MS query spectra from a global molecular network anchor–suspect data set and run SIRIUS 5.6.3 molecular formula and structure annotation against bioDB, establishing a baseline annotation rate (4756 correct formulas / 4560 correct structures out of 38,368 queries).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS/MS acquisition data rather than deconvoluted, library-annotated query spectra from an annotated molecular network node The query compound is not represented in the structural database (bioDB), since annotation is only evaluated for compounds present there The goal is de novo biotransformation-based annotation of unknown suspects (use BAM instead) rather than database-restricted formula/structure identification

skills.description: Use when candidate lists from MS/MS tools (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) for LC-MS peaks in an RPLC run need re-ranking with predicted retention-order scores, or when peaks lack usable MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: msms-retention-score-integration
skills.search_text: msms-retention-score-integration Use when candidate lists from MS/MS tools (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) for LC-MS peaks in an RPLC run need re-ranking with predicted retention-order scores, or when peaks lack usable MS/MS spectra. The chromatography is HILIC or another non-RPLC system — ROASMI applies only to RPLC and retraining HILIC models with generalizability remains future work Compounds fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S — the trained models do not cover the broader chemical space Candidate pairs are indistinguishable by the retention model (e.g. 4-hydroxybenzoic acid vs 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, close retention with high prediction variance) — such pairs should be excluded rather than resolved by retention ordering http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 A probabilistic integration of ROASMI-predicted retention-order scores with MS/MS scores (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) to re-rank candidate structures, improving candidate ranking and top-k identification accuracy over MS/MS tools alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: A probabilistic integration of ROASMI-predicted retention-order scores with MS/MS scores (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) to re-rank candidate structures, improving candidate ranking and top-k identification accuracy over MS/MS tools alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chromatography is HILIC or another non-RPLC system — ROASMI applies only to RPLC and retraining HILIC models with generalizability remains future work Compounds fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S — the trained models do not cover the broader chemical space Candidate pairs are indistinguishable by the retention model (e.g. 4-hydroxybenzoic acid vs 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, close retention with high prediction variance) — such pairs should be excluded rather than resolved by retention ordering

skills.description: Use when processing ddMS2-topN or AIF UHPLC-HRMS/MS .ms2 files after MS1 exact-mass matching: you need to isolate the tandem-MS scans co-eluting with each feature before matching experimental fragments against in silico library m/z values.
skills.name: msms-scan-retention-time-filtering
skills.search_text: msms-scan-retention-time-filtering Use when processing ddMS2-topN or AIF UHPLC-HRMS/MS .ms2 files after MS1 exact-mass matching: you need to isolate the tandem-MS scans co-eluting with each feature before matching experimental fragments against in silico library m/z values. Input MS/MS data is still in vendor raw format — LipidMatch requires .ms2 files, so MSConvert peak picking and conversion must happen first Data comes from Waters files, which LipidMatch does not currently support You only have MS1 full-scan data with no ddMS2-topN or AIF spectra acquired from pooled/representative samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Selects, for each feature–lipid candidate pair, the MS/MS scans from .ms2 files that fall within a user-defined retention-time and m/z tolerance of the feature, where the m/z tolerance equals the isolation window used for ion selection. This is Step 2 of the LipidMatch identification workflow and defines the fragment pool for subsequent ppm-level fragment matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Selects, for each feature–lipid candidate pair, the MS/MS scans from .ms2 files that fall within a user-defined retention-time and m/z tolerance of the feature, where the m/z tolerance equals the isolation window used for ion selection. This is Step 2 of the LipidMatch identification workflow and defines the fragment pool for subsequent ppm-level fragment matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input MS/MS data is still in vendor raw format — LipidMatch requires .ms2 files, so MSConvert peak picking and conversion must happen first Data comes from Waters files, which LipidMatch does not currently support You only have MS1 full-scan data with no ddMS2-topN or AIF spectra acquired from pooled/representative samples

skills.description: Use when a feature table row has multiple lipid candidates passing rule-based identification (same or similar m/z, co-eluting) and you must rank them by summed fragment intensity across MS/MS scans spanning the feature peak.
skills.name: msms-scan-statistics-aggregation
skills.search_text: msms-scan-statistics-aggregation Use when a feature table row has multiple lipid candidates passing rule-based identification (same or similar m/z, co-eluting) and you must rank them by summed fragment intensity across MS/MS scans spanning the feature peak. A feature has only one candidate lipid passing confirmatory fragment requirements — ranking adds no information You need identification confirmation itself (required-fragment/scan-count binarization, Steps 4–5) rather than candidate ordering Waters vendor files are the input, since LipidMatch does not currently support Waters files http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Aggregates per-scan fragment match statistics into a summed fragment intensity score that ranks multiple lipid candidates co-eluting within a single feature (defined by m/z and retention time). This is LipidMatch's unique disambiguation mechanism for features containing multiple co-eluting molecules with similar m/z values. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Aggregates per-scan fragment match statistics into a summed fragment intensity score that ranks multiple lipid candidates co-eluting within a single feature (defined by m/z and retention time). This is LipidMatch's unique disambiguation mechanism for features containing multiple co-eluting molecules with similar m/z values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A feature has only one candidate lipid passing confirmatory fragment requirements — ranking adds no information You need identification confirmation itself (required-fragment/scan-count binarization, Steps 4–5) rather than candidate ordering Waters vendor files are the input, since LipidMatch does not currently support Waters files

skills.description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS metabolomics or lipidomics mzML samples where fragmentation scans must be grouped into precursor-defined (m/z, RT) slices and attached to finalized peak groups rather than analyzed per-scan.
skills.name: msms-scan-to-peak-group-assignment
skills.search_text: msms-scan-to-peak-group-assignment Use when processing LC-MS/MS metabolomics or lipidomics mzML samples where fragmentation scans must be grouped into precursor-defined (m/z, RT) slices and attached to finalized peak groups rather than analyzed per-scan. Input data is MS1-only LC-MS metabolomics with no MS/MS fragmentation scans, where prior-MAVEN peak grouping alone suffices You need MS/MS spectral library matching or in-silico lipidomics library search rather than peak grouping (those are separate MAVEN2 capabilities) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces the MAVEN2 MS/MS-based peak grouping pipeline: MS/MS fragmentation scans are grouped into (m/z, retention time) slices, slices are progressively merged across samples, peak groups are formed with prior-MAVEN peak-grouping logic, and pre-merged slice scans are attached to finalized peak groups by retention time proximity. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12080684
skills.summary: Reproduces the MAVEN2 MS/MS-based peak grouping pipeline: MS/MS fragmentation scans are grouped into (m/z, retention time) slices, slices are progressively merged across samples, peak groups are formed with prior-MAVEN peak-grouping logic, and pre-merged slice scans are attached to finalized peak groups by retention time proximity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is MS1-only LC-MS metabolomics with no MS/MS fragmentation scans, where prior-MAVEN peak grouping alone suffices You need MS/MS spectral library matching or in-silico lipidomics library search rather than peak grouping (those are separate MAVEN2 capabilities)

skills.description: Use when two structurally related MS/MS spectra (MS2-known and MS2-unknown) are available with a 2D structure of the known compound, and the goal is to localize where the structural modification occurs on the known molecule.
skills.name: msms-shifted-peak-alignment-analysis
skills.search_text: msms-shifted-peak-alignment-analysis Use when two structurally related MS/MS spectra (MS2-known and MS2-unknown) are available with a 2D structure of the known compound, and the goal is to localize where the structural modification occurs on the known molecule. The unknown compound has no structurally related known compound with matching MS/MS spectra — analog library search or molecular networking identification alone is the appropriate choice No 2D structure is available for the known compound, since combinatorial fragmentation requires the initial structure S-known Precursor mass difference exceeds the benchmark eligibility criteria (e.g. difference in precursor masses >= 50% or precursor mass above 2000 Da) http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 A ModiFinder-based analysis skill that aligns MS/MS peaks between a known compound and a structural analog to score every atom of the known molecule for its likelihood of being the modification site, optionally refined by expert peak-to-fragment mapping edits. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: A ModiFinder-based analysis skill that aligns MS/MS peaks between a known compound and a structural analog to score every atom of the known molecule for its likelihood of being the modification site, optionally refined by expert peak-to-fragment mapping edits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unknown compound has no structurally related known compound with matching MS/MS spectra — analog library search or molecular networking identification alone is the appropriate choice No 2D structure is available for the known compound, since combinatorial fragmentation requires the initial structure S-known Precursor mass difference exceeds the benchmark eligibility criteria (e.g. difference in precursor masses >= 50% or precursor mass above 2000 Da)

skills.description: Use when exploring LC-MS/MS .mgf feature spectra with specXplore and you want cluster groupings (at several k values) of features based on ms2deepscore similarities, not edge-threshold-driven partial networks.
skills.name: msms-similarity-network-cluster-visualization
skills.search_text: msms-similarity-network-cluster-visualization Use when exploring LC-MS/MS .mgf feature spectra with specXplore and you want cluster groupings (at several k values) of features based on ms2deepscore similarities, not edge-threshold-driven partial networks. The goal is edge-level connectivity analysis driven by similarity thresholds and top-K neighbor limits, not feature groupings independent of edge filtering. The dataset exceeds roughly 5000 features or very liberal settings are used, since the paper only anticipates (not tests) scaling beyond that point. The spectra fall outside or far from ms2deepscore's training data domain, where similarity scores are expected to be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Groups MS/MS features by k-medoid clustering over the ms2deepscore pairwise similarity matrix and overlays the resulting cluster labels on the specXplore t-SNE overview, complementing local connectivity views with cluster-level structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Groups MS/MS features by k-medoid clustering over the ms2deepscore pairwise similarity matrix and overlays the resulting cluster labels on the specXplore t-SNE overview, complementing local connectivity views with cluster-level structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is edge-level connectivity analysis driven by similarity thresholds and top-K neighbor limits, not feature groupings independent of edge filtering. The dataset exceeds roughly 5000 features or very liberal settings are used, since the paper only anticipates (not tests) scaling beyond that point. The spectra fall outside or far from ms2deepscore's training data domain, where similarity scores are expected to be unreliable.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS peak table and MS2 spectra contain library-confirmed known metabolites and reaction-paired unknown peaks that must be annotated by propagating known seeds across spectrally similar, knowledge-guided network edges.
skills.name: msms-similarity-network-propagation
skills.search_text: msms-similarity-network-propagation Use when an LC-MS/MS peak table and MS2 spectra contain library-confirmed known metabolites and reaction-paired unknown peaks that must be annotated by propagating known seeds across spectrally similar, knowledge-guided network edges. When the peak table has no library-confirmed known seed metabolites (network 2 propagates only from knowns found after reconstructNetwork1) When peaks of interest are not reaction-paired: the article notes ~40% of reaction-paired metabolites have low MS/MS similarity scores despite high structural similarity, and KGMN removes spectrally similar but hard-to-interpret connections When the goal is to discriminate structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively distinguish http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Constructs the knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network layer of the KGMN workflow (MetDNA2Vis reconstructNetwork2), propagating metabolite annotations from library-confirmed 'known' seed peaks to reaction-paired 'unknown' peaks that show high MS/MS spectral similarity, thereby extending annotation from knowns to unknowns in LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Constructs the knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network layer of the KGMN workflow (MetDNA2Vis reconstructNetwork2), propagating metabolite annotations from library-confirmed 'known' seed peaks to reaction-paired 'unknown' peaks that show high MS/MS spectral similarity, thereby extending annotation from knowns to unknowns in LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the peak table has no library-confirmed known seed metabolites (network 2 propagates only from knowns found after reconstructNetwork1) When peaks of interest are not reaction-paired: the article notes ~40% of reaction-paired metabolites have low MS/MS similarity scores despite high structural similarity, and KGMN removes spectrally similar but hard-to-interpret connections When the goal is to discriminate structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively distinguish

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample MS-DIAL feature lists (precursor MS1 m/z, RT, MS/MS spectra) from many samples (e.g. 545 wild soybean accessions) and need to align and merge equivalent features into one table.
skills.name: msms-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: msms-similarity-scoring Use when you have per-sample MS-DIAL feature lists (precursor MS1 m/z, RT, MS/MS spectra) from many samples (e.g. 545 wild soybean accessions) and need to align and merge equivalent features into one table. Your downstream model consumes raw fragmentation patterns directly (e.g. the MS2toImg image encoding), which is explicitly less sensitive to alignment errors and does not rely on precise feature matching You already have an aligned, non-redundant feature table and only need preprocessing steps like TIC normalization or adduct filtering Features lack MS/MS spectra or retention time information, making the three-score average impossible to compute http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Merge equivalent per-sample LC-MS/MS features into a unified feature table by computing similarity scores for MS1 m/z, retention time, and MS/MS spectra, and consolidating features when the average of the three similarity scores exceeds 0.8. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Merge equivalent per-sample LC-MS/MS features into a unified feature table by computing similarity scores for MS1 m/z, retention time, and MS/MS spectra, and consolidating features when the average of the three similarity scores exceeds 0.8.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your downstream model consumes raw fragmentation patterns directly (e.g. the MS2toImg image encoding), which is explicitly less sensitive to alignment errors and does not rely on precise feature matching You already have an aligned, non-redundant feature table and only need preprocessing steps like TIC normalization or adduct filtering Features lack MS/MS spectra or retention time information, making the three-score average impossible to compute

skills.description: Use when experimental HR-MS/MS spectra (MGF) must be classified into user-defined substance classes, e.g. prioritizing putative (prenylated) flavonoids in natural product discovery.
skills.name: msms-spectra-annotation
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-annotation Use when experimental HR-MS/MS spectra (MGF) must be classified into user-defined substance classes, e.g. prioritizing putative (prenylated) flavonoids in natural product discovery. The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the paper explicitly states classification will most often fail in that case and the package cannot resolve it The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than binary 'relevant'/'other' prioritization of spectra against user-defined substance classes Input spectra are already labeled with trusted class annotations, making substructure filtering and classifier training unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Train user-defined 'relevant'/'other' classifiers for HR-MS/MS spectra using AnnoMe: substructure (SMARTS) filtering of MGF spectral libraries to build training classes, MS2DeepScore embeddings, and a majority vote over LDA/NN/SVM classifiers to assign novel spectra to substance classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Train user-defined 'relevant'/'other' classifiers for HR-MS/MS spectra using AnnoMe: substructure (SMARTS) filtering of MGF spectral libraries to build training classes, MS2DeepScore embeddings, and a majority vote over LDA/NN/SVM classifiers to assign novel spectra to substance classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the paper explicitly states classification will most often fail in that case and the package cannot resolve it The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than binary 'relevant'/'other' prioritization of spectra against user-defined substance classes Input spectra are already labeled with trusted class annotations, making substructure filtering and classifier training unnecessary

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (MoNA or NIST 17, positive mode, HCD/QqQ/Q-TOF or IT) must be preprocessed into binned, denoised feature vectors to train a multi-class multi-label ANN like MetFID.
skills.name: msms-spectra-binning-and-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-binning-and-feature-extraction Use when raw MS/MS spectra (MoNA or NIST 17, positive mode, HCD/QqQ/Q-TOF or IT) must be preprocessed into binned, denoised feature vectors to train a multi-class multi-label ANN like MetFID. Spectra were already converted to a fixed-length fingerprint or feature table by another pipeline — re-binning would destroy bin metadata. Only negative-mode or in-source-fragmentation spectra are available, since the method filters to positive-mode collision-cell or ion-trap data. Candidate ranking via spectral library matching rather than ANN fingerprint prediction is the goal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Converts raw MS/MS spectra into fixed-length feature vectors for ANN fingerprint prediction by binning the m/z axis, computing loss features from precursor-ion m/z differences, and scaling/filtering peak intensities. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Converts raw MS/MS spectra into fixed-length feature vectors for ANN fingerprint prediction by binning the m/z axis, computing loss features from precursor-ion m/z differences, and scaling/filtering peak intensities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra were already converted to a fixed-length fingerprint or feature table by another pipeline — re-binning would destroy bin metadata. Only negative-mode or in-source-fragmentation spectra are available, since the method filters to positive-mode collision-cell or ion-trap data. Candidate ranking via spectral library matching rather than ANN fingerprint prediction is the goal.

skills.description: Use when per-spectrum or molecular-family-level chemical class annotations (ClassyFire/NPClassifier at super-, class-, and subclass-levels) are needed from MS/MS spectra in an NPLinker workflow and compounds are below 850 Da.
skills.name: msms-spectra-canopus-class-prediction
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-canopus-class-prediction Use when per-spectrum or molecular-family-level chemical class annotations (ClassyFire/NPClassifier at super-, class-, and subclass-levels) are needed from MS/MS spectra in an NPLinker workflow and compounds are below 850 Da. Compounds above 850 Da: the 850 Da mass cut-off limits CANOPUS coverage, and larger metabolites are not well handled — mass-spectral embeddings such as Spec2Vec and MS2DeepScore may be better suited When a network-level (rather than spectrum-level) class propagation is acceptable and per-spectrum structure-based prediction is unnecessary — MolNetEnhancer run externally on the GNPS platform may suffice Spectra for which CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer yields no structure-based class prediction — links relying on these spectra were discarded under the filter_missing_scores toggle rather than forced through this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Run CANOPUS through SIRIUS v4.9.3 directly on the GNPS molecular networking spectra.mgf file within NPLinker to obtain structure-based ClassyFire and NPClassifier class predictions, restricted to spectra below 850 Da because fragmentation-tree calculation is time-consuming. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Run CANOPUS through SIRIUS v4.9.3 directly on the GNPS molecular networking spectra.mgf file within NPLinker to obtain structure-based ClassyFire and NPClassifier class predictions, restricted to spectra below 850 Da because fragmentation-tree calculation is time-consuming.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds above 850 Da: the 850 Da mass cut-off limits CANOPUS coverage, and larger metabolites are not well handled — mass-spectral embeddings such as Spec2Vec and MS2DeepScore may be better suited When a network-level (rather than spectrum-level) class propagation is acceptable and per-spectrum structure-based prediction is unnecessary — MolNetEnhancer run externally on the GNPS platform may suffice Spectra for which CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer yields no structure-based class prediction — links relying on these spectra were discarded under the filter_missing_scores toggle rather than forced through this skill

skills.description: Use when experimental HR-MS/MS spectra (MGF files) must be screened against a user-defined 'relevant' substance class (e.g. prenylated flavonoids) for prioritization, and you have curated 'relevant' and 'other' reference spectra to train classifiers.
skills.name: msms-spectra-compound-class-prediction
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-compound-class-prediction Use when experimental HR-MS/MS spectra (MGF files) must be screened against a user-defined 'relevant' substance class (e.g. prenylated flavonoids) for prioritization, and you have curated 'relevant' and 'other' reference spectra to train classifiers. The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article states classification of MS/MS spectra into substance classes 'most often will not be successful' in this case and the package 'is not capable of resolving this issue' The goal is general-purpose compound-class ontology assignment (e.g. full ClassyFire hierarchy) or molecular formula/structure elucidation rather than screening against one user-defined 'relevant' class The input is already a labeled feature table or classified result rather than raw MS/MS spectra needing class assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Classifies experimental HR-MS/MS spectra into a user-defined substance class of interest ('relevant', e.g. prenylated flavonoids) versus 'other' using MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings and custom-trained classifiers (LDA, NN, SVM) aggregated by majority vote. Serves as a user-targeted alternative/complement to generic compound-class predictors such as SIRIUS with ClassyFire. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Classifies experimental HR-MS/MS spectra into a user-defined substance class of interest ('relevant', e.g. prenylated flavonoids) versus 'other' using MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings and custom-trained classifiers (LDA, NN, SVM) aggregated by majority vote. Serves as a user-targeted alternative/complement to generic compound-class predictors such as SIRIUS with ClassyFire.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article states classification of MS/MS spectra into substance classes 'most often will not be successful' in this case and the package 'is not capable of resolving this issue' The goal is general-purpose compound-class ontology assignment (e.g. full ClassyFire hierarchy) or molecular formula/structure elucidation rather than screening against one user-defined 'relevant' class The input is already a labeled feature table or classified result rather than raw MS/MS spectra needing class assignment

skills.description: Use when you have four comma-separated CSV peak lists of MS/MS spectra — [M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE, with m/z in column 1 and intensity in column 2 — and need spectra embeddings for downstream structure decoding.
skills.name: msms-spectra-csv-ingestion
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-csv-ingestion Use when you have four comma-separated CSV peak lists of MS/MS spectra — [M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE, with m/z in column 1 and intensity in column 2 — and need spectra embeddings for downstream structure decoding. Input spectra come from a single collision energy or a single polarity only, so the four-file (pos/neg, low/high NCE) interface cannot be filled Peak lists are in a vendor or open instrument format (e.g. mzML) rather than the required two-column m/z,intensity CSV layout The goal is decoding embeddings into SMILES structures rather than producing the embeddings themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Ingest four MS/MS peak-list CSV files (positive/negative mode, low/high collision energy) and encode them into spectra embeddings using the Spec2Mol spectra encoder trained on the NIST Tandem Mass Spectral Library 2020. The resulting embeddings are the decoder-facing representation of the input spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00932-3
skills.summary: Ingest four MS/MS peak-list CSV files (positive/negative mode, low/high collision energy) and encode them into spectra embeddings using the Spec2Mol spectra encoder trained on the NIST Tandem Mass Spectral Library 2020. The resulting embeddings are the decoder-facing representation of the input spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra come from a single collision energy or a single polarity only, so the four-file (pos/neg, low/high NCE) interface cannot be filled Peak lists are in a vendor or open instrument format (e.g. mzML) rather than the required two-column m/z,intensity CSV layout The goal is decoding embeddings into SMILES structures rather than producing the embeddings themselves

skills.description: Use when LC-MS/MS spectra of metabolites or other small molecules must be identified at the structure level by searching a molecular structure database such as PubChem, and measured spectral-library matching (e.g. GNPS library cosine search) is insufficient or unavailable.
skills.name: msms-spectra-database-searching
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-database-searching Use when LC-MS/MS spectra of metabolites or other small molecules must be identified at the structure level by searching a molecular structure database such as PubChem, and measured spectral-library matching (e.g. GNPS library cosine search) is insufficient or unavailable. The goal is de novo molecular formula determination only — SIRIUS isotope pattern analysis / fragmentation tree computation alone suffices without CSI:FingerID structure search. Input spectra are MS1-only (no tandem MS peaks); CSI:FingerID requires MS/MS fragmentation information. A curated experimental MS/MS spectral library (e.g. GNPS library search) confidently matches the spectra, making fingerprint-based database search unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Searches tandem MS/MS spectra of small molecules against molecular structure databases (e.g. PubChem) via SIRIUS + CSI:FingerID, which predicts structural fingerprints from fragmentation trees and ranks candidate structures. Enables structure identification even when no measured MS/MS reference spectra exist in a spectral library. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8
skills.summary: Searches tandem MS/MS spectra of small molecules against molecular structure databases (e.g. PubChem) via SIRIUS + CSI:FingerID, which predicts structural fingerprints from fragmentation trees and ranks candidate structures. Enables structure identification even when no measured MS/MS reference spectra exist in a spectral library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo molecular formula determination only — SIRIUS isotope pattern analysis / fragmentation tree computation alone suffices without CSI:FingerID structure search. Input spectra are MS1-only (no tandem MS peaks); CSI:FingerID requires MS/MS fragmentation information. A curated experimental MS/MS spectral library (e.g. GNPS library search) confidently matches the spectra, making fingerprint-based database search unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when detected LC-MS features have associated MS/MS spectra and you need portable spectral files (MGF/MAT) for GNPS spectral-library dereplication, MS-FINDER, or Sirius annotation.
skills.name: msms-spectra-export-mgf-mat
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-export-mgf-mat Use when detected LC-MS features have associated MS/MS spectra and you need portable spectral files (MGF/MAT) for GNPS spectral-library dereplication, MS-FINDER, or Sirius annotation. Features lack acquired MS/MS spectra — apply the optional 'Exclusion of features for which MS/MS spectra were not acquired' filter first, since only features with MS/MS can be exported for library matching You already have a GNPS dereplication result — proceed directly to building the mz-RT annotation list rather than re-exporting spectra The goal is only intensity quantification/normalization or spatial mapping in 'ili, which does not require spectral export http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Exports MS/MS spectra of LC-MS features detected with the Optimus KNIME workflow into MGF (for GNPS dereplication or Sirius) and MAT (for MS-FINDER) formats so spectra can be matched against public spectral libraries and used for downstream in-silico annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nprot.2017.122
skills.summary: Exports MS/MS spectra of LC-MS features detected with the Optimus KNIME workflow into MGF (for GNPS dereplication or Sirius) and MAT (for MS-FINDER) formats so spectra can be matched against public spectral libraries and used for downstream in-silico annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features lack acquired MS/MS spectra — apply the optional 'Exclusion of features for which MS/MS spectra were not acquired' filter first, since only features with MS/MS can be exported for library matching You already have a GNPS dereplication result — proceed directly to building the mz-RT annotation list rather than re-exporting spectra The goal is only intensity quantification/normalization or spatial mapping in 'ili, which does not require spectral export

skills.description: Use when a local, self-contained reference compound/MS2 spectral database (e.g. SQLite CompDb) must be created from a public resource like HMDB so experimental fragment spectra can later be compared against a curated library.

skills.search_text: msms-spectra-merging Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be converted into merged training feature vectors for per-bit libSVM fingerprint prediction, and candidate compounds must be ranked by Jaccard similarity of predicted vs. reference fingerprints from chemdb. Input spectra are not in ChemDistiller's internal hierarchical format — format conversion was not yet available and other formats require prior conversion. Only 1D MS1 peak detection is needed without tandem MS/MS annotation — the FingerScorer depends on MS/MS spectra as feature vectors. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs ChemDistiller's FingerScorer pipeline: merge tandem MS/MS spectra into training feature vectors, train one libSVM model per occupied CDK fingerprint bit to predict molecular fingerprints from experimental MS/MS data, then rank candidate compounds by Jaccard similarity between predicted and pre-calculated reference fingerprints. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: Reconstructs ChemDistiller's FingerScorer pipeline: merge tandem MS/MS spectra into training feature vectors, train one libSVM model per occupied CDK fingerprint bit to predict molecular fingerprints from experimental MS/MS data, then rank candidate compounds by Jaccard similarity between predicted and pre-calculated reference fingerprints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not in ChemDistiller's internal hierarchical format — format conversion was not yet available and other formats require prior conversion. skills.description: Use when two centroided MS/MS peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be combined into a merged spectrum AB to compute spectral entropy similarity, e.g. for library matching or compound identification scoring.
skills.name: msms-spectra-merging-and-renormalization
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-merging-and-renormalization Use when two centroided MS/MS peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be combined into a merged spectrum AB to compute spectral entropy similarity, e.g. for library matching or compound identification scoring. Spectra have not been centroided and entropy-normalized first (intensities do not sum to 1) — merge before normalization invalidates the entropy calculation The goal is weighted (entropy-weighted) similarity rather than unweighted similarity — then apply_weight_to_intensity or calculate_entropy_similarity should be used instead High-abundance noise or precursor ions are still present — clean_spectrum preprocessing (including removal of peaks above precursor_mz - precursor_ions_removal_da) should be run upstream first http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Builds the 1:1 merged, weighted spectrum AB from two entropy-normalized MS/MS spectra by matching ions within 0.05 Da tolerance and renormalizing merged intensities to sum = 1, enabling computation of unweighted entropy similarity per equation (2). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01331-z
skills.summary: Builds the 1:1 merged, weighted spectrum AB from two entropy-normalized MS/MS spectra by matching ions within 0.05 Da tolerance and renormalizing merged intensities to sum = 1, enabling computation of unweighted entropy similarity per equation (2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra have not been centroided and entropy-normalized first (intensities do not sum to 1) — merge before normalization invalidates the entropy calculation The goal is weighted (entropy-weighted) similarity rather than unweighted similarity — then apply_weight_to_intensity or calculate_entropy_similarity should be used instead High-abundance noise or precursor ions are still present — clean_spectrum preprocessing (including removal of peaks above precursor_mz - precursor_ions_removal_da) should be run upstream first

skills.search_text: msms-spectra-merging-by-inchikey Use when building a training set from MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g. NIST 17, MoNA) where the same compound appears in multiple spectra at different collision energies or instrument types, and a single unified input vector per compound is needed. When the goal is collision-energy-specific prediction: the article showed a combined model has slightly lower accuracy and F1 than a low-energy-only model on low-energy test spectra, so use separate models instead of merging When the spectra are already deduplicated per compound (e.g. a single reference spectrum per InChIKey) and no peak-consolidation step is needed When the unknown analyte's candidate pool includes compounds whose spectra were acquired under drastically different conditions that the ANN was never trained to merge across http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Aggregates multiple MS/MS spectra of the same compound — acquired at different collision energies (low ≤30 eV vs. high ≥30 eV) or on different instruments (HCD, QqQ, Q-TOF, IT) — into a single merged training spectrum keyed on the compound's first InChIKey block, to build collision-energy- and instrument-agnostic ANN inputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Aggregates multiple MS/MS spectra of the same compound — acquired at different collision energies (low ≤30 eV vs. high ≥30 eV) or on different instruments (HCD, QqQ, Q-TOF, IT) — into a single merged training spectrum keyed on the compound's first InChIKey block, to build collision-energy- and instrument-agnostic ANN inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is collision-energy-specific prediction: the article showed a combined model has slightly lower accuracy and F1 than a low-energy-only model on low-energy test spectra, so use separate models instead of merging When the spectra are already deduplicated per compound (e.g. a single reference spectrum per InChIKey) and no peak-consolidation step is needed When the unknown analyte's candidate pool includes compounds whose spectra were acquired under drastically different conditions that the ANN was never trained to merge across

skills.search_text: msms-spectra-preprocessing Use when input is raw MSP files of tandem MS spectra (possibly split across multiple collision energies) and you need model-ready spectra arrays for CNN-based metabolite identification with ChemEmbed. The spectra are already merged, binarized model inputs — re-binning or re-binarizing could destroy peak information You need to adjust candidate retrieval parameters — precursor filtering is controlled by --precursor_tolerance_ppm, not by the spectral preprocessing parameters You are reproducing legacy pre-1.1.1 results where the exact 3-decimal precursor bucket was used — in that case use --precursor_tolerance_ppm 0 rather than altering preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Preprocess MS/MS spectra for ChemEmbed's CNN by merging multi-collision-energy MS2 scans, binarizing intensities, applying peak binning, and converting MSP files into model-ready arrays. This enhanced-spectrum format is what the pretrained CNN expects before predicting 300-dimensional Mol2vec embeddings. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Preprocess MS/MS spectra for ChemEmbed's CNN by merging multi-collision-energy MS2 scans, binarizing intensities, applying peak binning, and converting MSP files into model-ready arrays. This enhanced-spectrum format is what the pretrained CNN expects before predicting 300-dimensional Mol2vec embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are already merged, binarized model inputs — re-binning or re-binarizing could destroy peak information You need to adjust candidate retrieval parameters — precursor filtering is controlled by --precursor_tolerance_ppm, not by the spectral preprocessing parameters You are reproducing legacy pre-1.1.1 results where the exact 3-decimal precursor bucket was used — in that case use --precursor_tolerance_ppm 0 rather than altering preprocessing

skills.description: Use when preparing raw MGF spectra from PRIDE-style datasets (e.g., PXD000561 charge 2/3 MS/MS) for spectral clustering and you need reproducible peak filtering, intensity normalization, and low-quality spectrum removal.
skills.name: msms-spectra-preprocessing
skills.search_text: msms-spectra-preprocessing Use when preparing raw MGF spectra from PRIDE-style datasets (e.g., PXD000561 charge 2/3 MS/MS) for spectral clustering and you need reproducible peak filtering, intensity normalization, and low-quality spectrum removal. Input is already preprocessed consensus spectra or a spectral library — re-filtering would strip valid low-intensity peaks and distort normalized intensities. You need exhaustive fragment-peak information for de novo sequencing; the <1% base-peak intensity cutoff and 50-peak cap discard most peaks by design for clustering, not identification. Spectra are charge states other than 2/3 or below the 5-peak/250 Da quality gates — they are removed rather than clustered. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocess MGF-format MS/MS spectra into clean, L2-normalized, ≤50-peak inputs before hypervector encoding and clustering, using HyperSpec's hybrid C++-Python parser and Numba/CUDA-parallelized preprocessor to cut the preprocessing bottleneck that consumes 20-90% of runtime in state-of-the-art clustering tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00612
skills.summary: Preprocess MGF-format MS/MS spectra into clean, L2-normalized, ≤50-peak inputs before hypervector encoding and clustering, using HyperSpec's hybrid C++-Python parser and Numba/CUDA-parallelized preprocessor to cut the preprocessing bottleneck that consumes 20-90% of runtime in state-of-the-art clustering tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already preprocessed consensus spectra or a spectral library — re-filtering would strip valid low-intensity peaks and distort normalized intensities. You need exhaustive fragment-peak information for de novo sequencing; the <1% base-peak intensity cutoff and 50-peak cap discard most peaks by design for clustering, not identification. Spectra are charge states other than 2/3 or below the 5-peak/250 Da quality gates — they are removed rather than clustered.

skills.search_text: msms-spectra-retrieval-from-mona Use when a standards dataframe row contains an inchiKey (linking to MassBank of North America) and you want to enrich an exported LC-MS reference library with MoNA MS/MS spectra alongside the adduct RT/m/z and quality fields. skills.name: msms-spectral-binning-feature-engineering
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-binning-feature-engineering Use when preparing MS/MS spectra (MoNA, NIST 17, HCD/QqQ/Q-TOF or IT, positive mode) as neural-network input vectors for fingerprint prediction, and a uniform binning/scaling representation is needed. Input is already a binned, normalized feature matrix (e.g. a saved .h5 model input) — re-binning would destroy the trained model's bin alignment Spectra are in negative ionization mode or acquired on non-collision-cell, non-IT instruments, which fall outside MetFID's training scope Spectra contain fewer than five peaks above 2% relative intensity — they should be removed rather than binned http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Convert raw MS/MS spectra into fixed-length binned feature vectors (m/z integer bins, intensities scaled 0–100) plus loss features, so they can serve as ANN inputs for compound fingerprint prediction in MetFID. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Convert raw MS/MS spectra into fixed-length binned feature vectors (m/z integer bins, intensities scaled 0–100) plus loss features, so they can serve as ANN inputs for compound fingerprint prediction in MetFID.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a binned, normalized feature matrix (e.g. a saved .h5 model input) — re-binning would destroy the trained model's bin alignment Spectra are in negative ionization mode or acquired on non-collision-cell, non-IT instruments, which fall outside MetFID's training scope Spectra contain fewer than five peaks above 2% relative intensity — they should be removed rather than binned

skills.description: Use when ranking candidate metabolite annotations from predicted vs. experimental tandem mass spectra, or when judging whether the top-ranked annotation is trustworthy via the Δcos gap between top-1 and top-2 candidates.
skills.name: msms-spectral-cosine-scoring
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-cosine-scoring Use when ranking candidate metabolite annotations from predicted vs. experimental tandem mass spectra, or when judging whether the top-ranked annotation is trustworthy via the Δcos gap between top-1 and top-2 candidates. When experimental spectra are already available in a curated reference library and a direct library match suffices — the paper notes SingleFrag is intended to overcome the lack of comprehensive reference spectral libraries, not to replace curated empirical matching. When the question is peak-intensity prediction rather than presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately focuses on predicting the presence or absence of each peak, and intensity-based scoring is out of scope for this skill. When spectra were acquired at a single collision energy without multi-collision-energy context — the paper warns that public libraries (GNPS, MSDial, MassBank) often contain only one or a few collision energies per compound, limiting the reliability of cosine-based ranking against such spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Scores in silico predicted MS/MS spectra against experimental spectra and ranks candidate metabolites by cosine similarity, using the cosine-similarity gap between the top and second candidate (Δcos > 0.2) as a reliability signal for top-ranked annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Scores in silico predicted MS/MS spectra against experimental spectra and ranks candidate metabolites by cosine similarity, using the cosine-similarity gap between the top and second candidate (Δcos > 0.2) as a reliability signal for top-ranked annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimental spectra are already available in a curated reference library and a direct library match suffices — the paper notes SingleFrag is intended to overcome the lack of comprehensive reference spectral libraries, not to replace curated empirical matching. When the question is peak-intensity prediction rather than presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately focuses on predicting the presence or absence of each peak, and intensity-based scoring is out of scope for this skill. When spectra were acquired at a single collision energy without multi-collision-energy context — the paper warns that public libraries (GNPS, MSDial, MassBank) often contain only one or a few collision energies per compound, limiting the reliability of cosine-based ranking against such spectra.

skills.description: Use when deconvoluted MS/MS spectra have been exported to .msp format from raw LC-MS/MS data and you must validate that the number of unique spectra per ionization mode matches reported/published counts before downstream modeling.
skills.name: msms-spectral-count-verification
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-count-verification Use when deconvoluted MS/MS spectra have been exported to .msp format from raw LC-MS/MS data and you must validate that the number of unique spectra per ionization mode matches reported/published counts before downstream modeling. Input is already a feature table, annotation matrix, or predicted-fingerprint output — counts of MS/MS blocks in .msp format are not applicable at that stage Spectra have not been deduplicated within an ionization mode, since duplicated blocks will inflate counts and produce spurious mismatches The comparison target is annotation coverage (e.g. 638/3,386 and 299/1,901 library hits) rather than the total unique-spectrum inventory http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Verifies that deconvoluted MS/MS spectra extracted from raw LC-MS/MS data (via IDSL.IPA + IDSL.CSA) match the expected unique-spectrum counts per ionization mode by counting spectrum blocks in NIST .msp files — here 3,386 in ESI+ and 1,901 in ESI− for Metabolomics WorkBench study ST002044. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00804-5
skills.summary: Verifies that deconvoluted MS/MS spectra extracted from raw LC-MS/MS data (via IDSL.IPA + IDSL.CSA) match the expected unique-spectrum counts per ionization mode by counting spectrum blocks in NIST .msp files — here 3,386 in ESI+ and 1,901 in ESI− for Metabolomics WorkBench study ST002044.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table, annotation matrix, or predicted-fingerprint output — counts of MS/MS blocks in .msp format are not applicable at that stage Spectra have not been deduplicated within an ionization mode, since duplicated blocks will inflate counts and produce spurious mismatches The comparison target is annotation coverage (e.g. 638/3,386 and 299/1,901 library hits) rather than the total unique-spectrum inventory

skills.description: Use when raw benchmark MS/MS files must be converted to mgf with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type and collision_energy fields so FIDDLE (or SIRIUS/BUDDY baselines) can consume them for formula-identification evaluation.
skills.name: msms-spectral-data-format-conversion
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-data-format-conversion Use when raw benchmark MS/MS files must be converted to mgf with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type and collision_energy fields so FIDDLE (or SIRIUS/BUDDY baselines) can consume them for formula-identification evaluation. Input spectra are already in mgf format with all required fields — rerunning conversion only risks corrupting metadata The task is internal FIDDLE training on NIST20/NIST23/MoNA/GNPS data rather than external CASMI/EMBL-MCF benchmark evaluation Spectra fall outside the small-molecule scope (precursor m/z > 1500 or fewer than five peaks), which the pipeline explicitly excludes http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts external benchmark tandem MS spectra (CASMI 2016/2017, EMBL-MCF 2.0) into MGF format with the metadata fields FIDDLE's run_fiddle.py pipeline requires, and applies the article's spectrum-level filters before evaluation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Converts external benchmark tandem MS spectra (CASMI 2016/2017, EMBL-MCF 2.0) into MGF format with the metadata fields FIDDLE's run_fiddle.py pipeline requires, and applies the article's spectrum-level filters before evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are already in mgf format with all required fields — rerunning conversion only risks corrupting metadata The task is internal FIDDLE training on NIST20/NIST23/MoNA/GNPS data rather than external CASMI/EMBL-MCF benchmark evaluation Spectra fall outside the small-molecule scope (precursor m/z > 1500 or fewer than five peaks), which the pipeline explicitly excludes

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzML, msp, JSON from GNPS or similar libraries) must be cleaned and harmonized before training spectral embeddings, computing cosine/modified-cosine similarities, or building molecular networks.
skills.name: msms-spectral-dataset-preprocessing
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-dataset-preprocessing Use when raw MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzML, msp, JSON from GNPS or similar libraries) must be cleaned and harmonized before training spectral embeddings, computing cosine/modified-cosine similarities, or building molecular networks. Input is already a cleaned, feature-annotated spectrum collection that matches the downstream model's training distribution — re-filtering with different thresholds (e.g., a new minimum-peak count) would break comparability with the published model. The task is single-pair spectral comparison of already-curated library entries rather than corpus-level preparation — the corpus filters (m/z [0,1000], >=10 peaks) add nothing there. Data is GC-MS, which the study explicitly did not assess ('In the present work, we have only demonstrated performance on LC-MS data'). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Clean and filter MS/MS spectra collections with matchms before spectral-similarity modeling or networking: remove peaks outside a defined m/z range, discard low-peak spectra, correct metadata, and optionally derive InChIKey-annotated subsets so downstream models (e.g., Spec2Vec Word2Vec training) operate on a consistent corpus. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Clean and filter MS/MS spectra collections with matchms before spectral-similarity modeling or networking: remove peaks outside a defined m/z range, discard low-peak spectra, correct metadata, and optionally derive InChIKey-annotated subsets so downstream models (e.g., Spec2Vec Word2Vec training) operate on a consistent corpus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned, feature-annotated spectrum collection that matches the downstream model's training distribution — re-filtering with different thresholds (e.g., a new minimum-peak count) would break comparability with the published model. The task is single-pair spectral comparison of already-curated library entries rather than corpus-level preparation — the corpus filters (m/z [0,1000], >=10 peaks) add nothing there. Data is GC-MS, which the study explicitly did not assess ('In the present work, we have only demonstrated performance on LC-MS data').

skills.description: Use when MS/MS query spectra were acquired on a non-Orbitrap high-resolution analyzer and the NIST23-derived electronic denoising threshold and mass tolerances must be re-derived and validated before applying Spectral Denoising.
skills.name: msms-spectral-denoising-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-denoising-parameter-tuning Use when MS/MS query spectra were acquired on a non-Orbitrap high-resolution analyzer and the NIST23-derived electronic denoising threshold and mass tolerances must be re-derived and validated before applying Spectral Denoising. Query spectra were acquired on an Orbitrap instrument, where the existing NIST23-calibrated parameters (identical-intensity cutoff >4, 10-mDa threshold) are already valid Spectra are low-resolution or lack accurate precursor masses, since formula denoising requires chemically plausible subformula losses within a tight precursor mass window The goal is plain spectral cleaning without validation — parameter retuning is only justified when the analyzer-specific threshold must be re-derived and benchmarked http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Retunes and validates Spectral Denoising parameters (electronic-noise threshold and formula-denoising mass tolerance) when adapting the Orbitrap-optimized denoising method to a different high-resolution mass analyzer, using entropy similarity against reference spectra as the acceptance metric. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Retunes and validates Spectral Denoising parameters (electronic-noise threshold and formula-denoising mass tolerance) when adapting the Orbitrap-optimized denoising method to a different high-resolution mass analyzer, using entropy similarity against reference spectra as the acceptance metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query spectra were acquired on an Orbitrap instrument, where the existing NIST23-calibrated parameters (identical-intensity cutoff >4, 10-mDa threshold) are already valid Spectra are low-resolution or lack accurate precursor masses, since formula denoising requires chemically plausible subformula losses within a tight precursor mass window The goal is plain spectral cleaning without validation — parameter retuning is only justified when the analyzer-specific threshold must be re-derived and benchmarked

skills.description: Use when experimental MS/MS peak lists from small-molecule metabolomics must be matched against candidate chemical structures to produce ranked, calibrated exact-structure assignments.
skills.name: msms-spectral-dot-product-scoring
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-dot-product-scoring Use when experimental MS/MS peak lists from small-molecule metabolomics must be matched against candidate chemical structures to produce ranked, calibrated exact-structure assignments. When only accurate mass is available and no tandem-MS spectra were acquired — mass-to-charge-based prioritization alone is the applicable route When the true metabolite originates from divergent, undiscovered biosynthetic routes outside the human metabolome the DeepMet model was trained on — candidates will be absent from the library When candidates are drawn from arbitrary chemical space rather than the DeepMet-generated metabolite candidate resource, since the meta-learning combiner is calibrated to sampling-frequency confidence from that resource http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Score experimental tandem-MS spectra against a library of CFM-ID-predicted in silico spectra using spectral dot-product matching, then integrate the match score with DeepMet sampling-frequency confidence via a meta-learning combiner to rank exact-structure annotations of unknown metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Score experimental tandem-MS spectra against a library of CFM-ID-predicted in silico spectra using spectral dot-product matching, then integrate the match score with DeepMet sampling-frequency confidence via a meta-learning combiner to rank exact-structure annotations of unknown metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only accurate mass is available and no tandem-MS spectra were acquired — mass-to-charge-based prioritization alone is the applicable route When the true metabolite originates from divergent, undiscovered biosynthetic routes outside the human metabolome the DeepMet model was trained on — candidates will be absent from the library When candidates are drawn from arbitrary chemical space rather than the DeepMet-generated metabolite candidate resource, since the meta-learning combiner is calibrated to sampling-frequency confidence from that resource

skills.description: Use when HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g., MGF-format annotated spectra from MSnLib or in-house libraries) must be converted into MS2DeepScore feature vectors before training or applying spectra classifiers.
skills.name: msms-spectral-embedding-generation
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-embedding-generation Use when HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g., MGF-format annotated spectra from MSnLib or in-house libraries) must be converted into MS2DeepScore feature vectors before training or applying spectra classifiers. The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article states classification into substance classes will most often fail in that case and AnnoMe cannot resolve it Embeddings have already been computed and cached for the same spectra — regenerate only for new/changed spectra, not as a routine re-run The task is spectral filtering or classification itself rather than feature preparation — use the AnnoMe filtering GUI or classification GUI instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute structure-informed MS2DeepScore embeddings for HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g., filtered annotated MSnLib spectra) so that spectra can be represented as fixed-length vectors for downstream training of 'relevant' vs 'other' classifiers within the AnnoMe workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Compute structure-informed MS2DeepScore embeddings for HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g., filtered annotated MSnLib spectra) so that spectra can be represented as fixed-length vectors for downstream training of 'relevant' vs 'other' classifiers within the AnnoMe workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article states classification into substance classes will most often fail in that case and AnnoMe cannot resolve it Embeddings have already been computed and cached for the same spectra — regenerate only for new/changed spectra, not as a routine re-run The task is spectral filtering or classification itself rather than feature preparation — use the AnnoMe filtering GUI or classification GUI instead

skills.description: Use when query MS/MS spectra (validated reference spectra or cryptic spectra without GNPS library matches) must be converted into per-sample similarity vectors over paired genome-MS/MS samples so a KNN classifier can assign gene cluster family (GCF) labels.
skills.name: msms-spectral-fingerprint-construction
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-fingerprint-construction Use when query MS/MS spectra (validated reference spectra or cryptic spectra without GNPS library matches) must be converted into per-sample similarity vectors over paired genome-MS/MS samples so a KNN classifier can assign gene cluster family (GCF) labels. The goal is metabolite identification against a spectral library rather than linking spectra to biosynthetic gene clusters via paired data. The dataset lacks paired genome-MS/MS samples (e.g., a fungal species with no paired data or no BGCs similar to the PoDP training set), so fingerprints have no meaningful training counterpart. The analysis requires distinguishing isomers or regioselectivity of homologs; the correlation-based fingerprinting cannot resolve these. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Construction of MS/MS similarity fingerprints for the NPOmix KNN classifier: each query spectrum (GNPS reference or cryptic) is represented as a vector of maximum modified cosine scores against the pooled experimental spectra of every paired genome-MS/MS sample. This testing matrix is the metabolomic analogue of the BGC fingerprint training matrix and is required for linking spectra to gene cluster families. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac257
skills.summary: Construction of MS/MS similarity fingerprints for the NPOmix KNN classifier: each query spectrum (GNPS reference or cryptic) is represented as a vector of maximum modified cosine scores against the pooled experimental spectra of every paired genome-MS/MS sample. This testing matrix is the metabolomic analogue of the BGC fingerprint training matrix and is required for linking spectra to gene cluster families.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is metabolite identification against a spectral library rather than linking spectra to biosynthetic gene clusters via paired data. The dataset lacks paired genome-MS/MS samples (e.g., a fungal species with no paired data or no BGCs similar to the PoDP training set), so fingerprints have no meaningful training counterpart. The analysis requires distinguishing isomers or regioselectivity of homologs; the correlation-based fingerprinting cannot resolve these.

skills.description: Use when you have cleaned positive- or negative-mode MS2 query spectra (mzML, MGF, msp, mzXML, json, USI, or pickled matchms) and need reliable library matches and analogues beyond modified cosine search.
skills.name: msms-spectral-library-analogue-search
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-analogue-search Use when you have cleaned positive- or negative-mode MS2 query spectra (mzML, MGF, msp, mzXML, json, USI, or pickled matchms) and need reliable library matches and analogues beyond modified cosine search. Input is raw LC-MS data that still needs peak picking or MS2 clustering — MS2Query does no peak picking, so preprocess with e.g. MZMine FBMN first The spectra mix multiple ionization modes in one run — MS2Query requires a single --ionmode (positive or negative) per run with the matching library http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Run MS2Query to search MS2 query spectra against a preprocessed GNPS mass spectral library in one run, finding both exact matches and analogues by combining MS2Deepscore preselection with a random-forest re-ranking of 5 features. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: Run MS2Query to search MS2 query spectra against a preprocessed GNPS mass spectral library in one run, finding both exact matches and analogues by combining MS2Deepscore preselection with a random-forest re-ranking of 5 features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data that still needs peak picking or MS2 clustering — MS2Query does no peak picking, so preprocess with e.g. MZMine FBMN first The spectra mix multiple ionization modes in one run — MS2Query requires a single --ionmode (positive or negative) per run with the matching library

skills.description: Use when batch QC inspection of LC-MS DDA data (e.g., TripleTOF or QE HF converted Aird files) has produced checked analysis overviews and you need to build a homemade MS/MS spectral library from inspected-and-passed compounds.
skills.name: msms-spectral-library-curation
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-curation Use when batch QC inspection of LC-MS DDA data (e.g., TripleTOF or QE HF converted Aird files) has produced checked analysis overviews and you need to build a homemade MS/MS spectral library from inspected-and-passed compounds. Input is raw vendor instrument data (e.g., .raw, .wiff2, .d) that still needs conversion to Aird format via AirdPro and targeted search — curation requires already-inspected, user-approved spectra from batch QC. The goal is comparing spectra against existing curated databases such as HMDB or METLIN rather than building a homemade library. QC overview records are still unchecked or manually unreviewed — curation should only collect inspected-and-passed (Success) compounds, so starting from unverified peaks defeats the review-based curation rationale. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Curate a homemade MS/MS spectral library by accumulating user-approved spectra grouped by metabolite, with recorded instrument type, collision energy, ionization mode, and source file metadata, using MetaPro's library curation module backed by MongoDB. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-023-02018-6
skills.summary: Curate a homemade MS/MS spectral library by accumulating user-approved spectra grouped by metabolite, with recorded instrument type, collision energy, ionization mode, and source file metadata, using MetaPro's library curation module backed by MongoDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor instrument data (e.g., .raw, .wiff2, .d) that still needs conversion to Aird format via AirdPro and targeted search — curation requires already-inspected, user-approved spectra from batch QC. The goal is comparing spectra against existing curated databases such as HMDB or METLIN rather than building a homemade library. QC overview records are still unchecked or manually unreviewed — curation should only collect inspected-and-passed (Success) compounds, so starting from unverified peaks defeats the review-based curation rationale.

skills.description: Use when building training data for MS/MS spectrum classification: you have MGF spectral library files and SMARTS structure queries for a compound class of interest and need to label spectra as 'relevant' or 'other'.
skills.name: msms-spectral-library-filtering
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-filtering Use when building training data for MS/MS spectrum classification: you have MGF spectral library files and SMARTS structure queries for a compound class of interest and need to label spectra as 'relevant' or 'other'. When the goal is direct spectral library search/annotation of unknown spectra rather than assembling labeled training data for a custom classifier When the training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article explicitly warns that classification will most often not succeed in that case and AnnoMe cannot resolve this issue When your compound class cannot be expressed as a SMARTS structure query over library structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Filter large public HR-MS/MS spectral libraries (MGF format, e.g. MSnLib v6) down to spectra of a user-defined substance class by applying SMARTS structure queries to library structures, using the AnnoMe filtering GUI. This creates labeled 'relevant'/'other' training sets for spectral classification, split per polarity and collision-energy subset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Filter large public HR-MS/MS spectral libraries (MGF format, e.g. MSnLib v6) down to spectra of a user-defined substance class by applying SMARTS structure queries to library structures, using the AnnoMe filtering GUI. This creates labeled 'relevant'/'other' training sets for spectral classification, split per polarity and collision-energy subset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct spectral library search/annotation of unknown spectra rather than assembling labeled training data for a custom classifier When the training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article explicitly warns that classification will most often not succeed in that case and AnnoMe cannot resolve this issue When your compound class cannot be expressed as a SMARTS structure query over library structures

skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-matching Use when detected LC-MS features with acquired MS/MS spectra (mzML runs processed in Optimus) need putative molecular annotations via MS/MS library matching on GNPS, or mz-RT matching to a GNPS-exported molecule list. When you need Metabolomics Standards Initiative level-1 or validated identifications — Optimus only provides level-2 putative annotations via mz-RT matching and MS/MS validation is not provided in the workflow When the input is already a fully annotated feature table or the annotation list comes from an in-house library unrelated to GNPS spectral-library matching output When features have no acquired MS/MS spectra — such features are typically excluded upstream (step 6 of the Optimus workflow) and cannot be dereplicated on GNPS http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Attaches level-2 'putatively annotated compound' metabolite identifications to LC-MS features by exporting feature MS/MS spectra (MGF/MAT) from Optimus, matching them against GNPS public spectral libraries, and feeding the filtered mz-RT list back into Optimus annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nprot.2017.122

skills.description: Use when chemical annotations must be assigned to MS/MS spectra in public MassIVE files or one's own data by spectral reference matching (GNPS library search), or when building a binary annotation-by-file matrix from ReDU's pre-computed results.

skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-matching Use when chemical annotations must be assigned to MS/MS spectra in public MassIVE files or one's own data by spectral reference matching (GNPS library search), or when building a binary annotation-by-file matrix from ReDU's pre-computed results. Input is already a annotated feature table or the goal is de novo / molecular-networking based annotation — molecular networking is a separate GNPS workflow with its own 3000-file limit, not library search Spectra are in proprietary vendor formats that have not been converted to .mzXML/.mzML, since the annotation workflow requires open-format converted data uploaded to GNPS/MassIVE Level 1 confirmed identifications (e.g. authentic standard verification) are required — spectral reference matching only reaches level 2 or level 3 confidence http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotate compounds in tandem MS data by matching MS/MS (product ion) spectra against curated reference spectral libraries in GNPS, as pre-computed at repository scale in ReDU. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-020-0916-7
skills.summary: Annotate compounds in tandem MS data by matching MS/MS (product ion) spectra against curated reference spectral libraries in GNPS, as pre-computed at repository scale in ReDU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a annotated feature table or the goal is de novo / molecular-networking based annotation — molecular networking is a separate GNPS workflow with its own 3000-file limit, not library search Spectra are in proprietary vendor formats that have not been converted to .mzXML/.mzML, since the annotation workflow requires open-format converted data uploaded to GNPS/MassIVE Level 1 confirmed identifications (e.g. authentic standard verification) are required — spectral reference matching only reaches level 2 or level 3 confidence

skills.summary: Search LC-MS/MS spectra (mzML) against a metabolite spectral library in MAVEN2, computing multiple match scores (dot product, fraction matched, fraction of TIC matched, HGS, MVH) to separate authentic from spurious metabolite identifications.
