skills.description: Use when a large set of experimental MS/MS spectra needs structural annotation via cosine spectral matching against an in silico predicted library (e.g. HMDB + DeepMet candidates) rather than direct formula assignment.
skills.name: msms-spectral-library-searching
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-searching Use when a large set of experimental MS/MS spectra needs structural annotation via cosine spectral matching against an in silico predicted library (e.g. HMDB + DeepMet candidates) rather than direct formula assignment. Input is a raw metabolomics feature table without MS/MS peak lists — spectral matching requires tandem MS data with fragment ions. The candidate structure library is empty or contains only structures with no predicted MS/MS spectra — cosine matching cannot score against missing spectra. The goal is de novo metabolite identification without any candidate structures — this skill matches spectra to existing predicted libraries, not to novel structures generated on the fly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Cosine-similarity matching of experimental tandem mass spectra against in silico predicted MS/MS libraries to annotate unknown peaks with chemical structures, as demonstrated by searching 29.1 million human blood spectra against HMDB and HMDB+DeepMet predicted libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Cosine-similarity matching of experimental tandem mass spectra against in silico predicted MS/MS libraries to annotate unknown peaks with chemical structures, as demonstrated by searching 29.1 million human blood spectra against HMDB and HMDB+DeepMet predicted libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw metabolomics feature table without MS/MS peak lists — spectral matching requires tandem MS data with fragment ions. The candidate structure library is empty or contains only structures with no predicted MS/MS spectra — cosine matching cannot score against missing spectra. The goal is de novo metabolite identification without any candidate structures — this skill matches spectra to existing predicted libraries, not to novel structures generated on the fly.

skills.description: Use when consensus MS2 spectra already associated with precursor m/z and retention time (e.g. deconvolved DIA data or DDA pooled QC spectra) must be annotated with named chemical identities via spectral library matching.
skills.name: msms-spectral-library-searching
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-library-searching Use when consensus MS2 spectra already associated with precursor m/z and retention time (e.g. deconvolved DIA data or DDA pooled QC spectra) must be annotated with named chemical identities via spectral library matching. Input is raw MS1 spectra still needing peak detection/quantification — use the MetaboAnalyst spectra processing module (asari/OptiLCMS) first, not library searching MS2 spectra from DIA data have not yet been deconvolved to reconstruct precursor ion associations — deconvolution must precede library searching The goal is fragment-level structural annotation without requiring whole-spectrum library matches to named compounds — the MS2 Peak Annotation module's scoring is designed for library matches http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Search deconvolved/consensus MS2 spectra (from DDA or DIA pooled QC acquisitions) against MetaboAnalyst 6.0's comprehensive MS2 reference databases (~1.5 million MS2 spectra) to produce named compound identifications with similarity scores and mirror plots. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Search deconvolved/consensus MS2 spectra (from DDA or DIA pooled QC acquisitions) against MetaboAnalyst 6.0's comprehensive MS2 reference databases (~1.5 million MS2 spectra) to produce named compound identifications with similarity scores and mirror plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS1 spectra still needing peak detection/quantification — use the MetaboAnalyst spectra processing module (asari/OptiLCMS) first, not library searching MS2 spectra from DIA data have not yet been deconvolved to reconstruct precursor ion associations — deconvolution must precede library searching The goal is fragment-level structural annotation without requiring whole-spectrum library matches to named compounds — the MS2 Peak Annotation module's scoring is designed for library matches

skills.description: Use when MS/MS peak lists (.mgf) from natural product extracts must be annotated against a spectral database, or when establishing a pre-taxonomic baseline of rank-1 correct annotations for tools like ISDB-DNP, Sirius, or MS-Finder.
skills.name: msms-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-matching Use when MS/MS peak lists (.mgf) from natural product extracts must be annotated against a spectral database, or when establishing a pre-taxonomic baseline of rank-1 correct annotations for tools like ISDB-DNP, Sirius, or MS-Finder. The benchmarking set compounds are all in the DNP, so ISDB-DNP is favored and tool comparison on such a set is not fair — avoid using ISDB-DNP-only matching performance to rank tools against each other. Spectra have fewer than 6 fragments or lack MS2 scans (features without MS2 scans are removed by the peak-list rows filter). Your goal is taxonomically informed re-ranking of existing candidate lists rather than the initial spectral library search. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Query filtered MS/MS spectra against experimental or theoretical spectral databases (e.g., the ISDB-DNP library backed by Dictionary of Natural Products v27.1) to obtain rank-ordered metabolite candidate annotations, establishing the baseline spectral-matching score before taxonomically informed re-ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Query filtered MS/MS spectra against experimental or theoretical spectral databases (e.g., the ISDB-DNP library backed by Dictionary of Natural Products v27.1) to obtain rank-ordered metabolite candidate annotations, establishing the baseline spectral-matching score before taxonomically informed re-ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmarking set compounds are all in the DNP, so ISDB-DNP is favored and tool comparison on such a set is not fair — avoid using ISDB-DNP-only matching performance to rank tools against each other. Spectra have fewer than 6 fragments or lack MS2 scans (features without MS2 scans are removed by the peak-list rows filter). Your goal is taxonomically informed re-ranking of existing candidate lists rather than the initial spectral library search.

skills.description: Use when a molecular networking component contains multiple tandem mass spectra (e.g., adducts or in-source fragments of one metabolite) and you need to identify which consensus peaks drive the family's shared fragmentation beyond pairwise spectral comparison.
skills.name: msms-spectral-mst-based-multiple-alignment
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-mst-based-multiple-alignment Use when a molecular networking component contains multiple tandem mass spectra (e.g., adducts or in-source fragments of one metabolite) and you need to identify which consensus peaks drive the family's shared fragmentation beyond pairwise spectral comparison. The goal is pairwise spectral comparison of only two spectra (e.g., a single mirror plot or modified cosine score) rather than alignment of an entire molecular family You expect fine-grained shifted-peak detail below what greedy multiple alignment resolves — e.g., small shifted peaks like C12 HAA (m/z 239.162) or y2 ions may not be fully captured Input is already a feature table or quantified metabolite matrix; MMSA operates on raw MS/MS peak lists within network components Multiple Mass Spectral Alignment (MMSA) computes a global alignment of all peaks across MS/MS spectra within a molecular network component, revealing consensus peak sets that explain shared fragmentation chemistry across adducts and in-source fragments. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Multiple Mass Spectral Alignment (MMSA) computes a global alignment of all peaks across MS/MS spectra within a molecular network component, revealing consensus peak sets that explain shared fragmentation chemistry across adducts and in-source fragments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pairwise spectral comparison of only two spectra (e.g., a single mirror plot or modified cosine score) rather than alignment of an entire molecular family You expect fine-grained shifted-peak detail below what greedy multiple alignment resolves — e.g., small shifted peaks like C12 HAA (m/z 239.162) or y2 ions may not be fully captured Input is already a feature table or quantified metabolite matrix; MMSA operates on raw MS/MS peak lists within network components

skills.description: Use when evaluating robustness of formula-identification methods on MS/MS spectra (MGF format) by systematically injecting intensity noise and comparing top-k accuracy degradation across instruments.
skills.name: msms-spectral-noise-perturbation
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-noise-perturbation Use when evaluating robustness of formula-identification methods on MS/MS spectra (MGF format) by systematically injecting intensity noise and comparing top-k accuracy degradation across instruments. The input is unlabeled spectra with no known ground-truth formulas — accuracy against reference formulas cannot be computed The goal is to augment training data rather than evaluate robustness — note the paper found noise augmentation helped Q-TOF but was not applied for Orbitrap training because it lowered similarity The spectra are chimeric/co-eluting — that robustness axis (spectral mixing) is a separate evaluation, not noise perturbation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Perturbs MS/MS spectra with additive Gaussian noise (mean 0, standard deviation 0.1 intensity units) at increasing levels to benchmark how robust molecular formula identification tools (FIDDLE, BUDDY, SIRIUS) are to spectral noise across Q-TOF and Orbitrap instruments. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Perturbs MS/MS spectra with additive Gaussian noise (mean 0, standard deviation 0.1 intensity units) at increasing levels to benchmark how robust molecular formula identification tools (FIDDLE, BUDDY, SIRIUS) are to spectral noise across Q-TOF and Orbitrap instruments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is unlabeled spectra with no known ground-truth formulas — accuracy against reference formulas cannot be computed The goal is to augment training data rather than evaluate robustness — note the paper found noise augmentation helped Q-TOF but was not applied for Orbitrap training because it lowered similarity The spectra are chimeric/co-eluting — that robustness axis (spectral mixing) is a separate evaluation, not noise perturbation

skills.description: Use when a pair of tandem MS spectra from structurally related analogs must be peak-aligned to identify which fragment peaks are shifted between the MS2-known and MS2-unknown spectra, prior to modification-site localization or analog-pair filtering.
skills.name: msms-spectral-pair-alignment
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-pair-alignment Use when a pair of tandem MS spectra from structurally related analogs must be peak-aligned to identify which fragment peaks are shifted between the MS2-known and MS2-unknown spectra, prior to modification-site localization or analog-pair filtering. You have only a single MS/MS spectrum with no structurally related analog partner — alignment requires two spectra from a known-unknown analog pair The two spectra come from compounds with the same precursor mass (no mass difference), so no shifted peaks can exist to inform localization You need library identification of a single compound against a reference database — use MS/MS library search or molecular networking instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aligns MS2 peaks between a structurally related known-unknown analog pair (MS2-known vs MS2-unknown) using a bipartite-graph greedy matching at 40 ppm m/z tolerance, producing matched shifted and unshifted peak sets that are the prerequisite input for ModiFinder's modification-site localization scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Aligns MS2 peaks between a structurally related known-unknown analog pair (MS2-known vs MS2-unknown) using a bipartite-graph greedy matching at 40 ppm m/z tolerance, producing matched shifted and unshifted peak sets that are the prerequisite input for ModiFinder's modification-site localization scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single MS/MS spectrum with no structurally related analog partner — alignment requires two spectra from a known-unknown analog pair The two spectra come from compounds with the same precursor mass (no mass difference), so no shifted peaks can exist to inform localization You need library identification of a single compound against a reference database — use MS/MS library search or molecular networking instead

skills.description: Use when you need in silico MS/MS spectra for metabolites lacking empirical library entries, or when predicting binary peak presence at specific m/z bins (2-decimal resolution) is preferred over intensity regression across collision energies.
skills.name: msms-spectral-peak-presence-prediction
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-peak-presence-prediction Use when you need in silico MS/MS spectra for metabolites lacking empirical library entries, or when predicting binary peak presence at specific m/z bins (2-decimal resolution) is preferred over intensity regression across collision energies. When you need calibrated peak intensities rather than binary presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately predicts presence, not intensity When the molecule exceeds the representable chemistry of the bundled Mol2vec/threshold assets — only the most frequented 1,000 MZ positions in the training set have thresholds and models When you require curation-verified multi-collision-energy reference spectra — the paper notes GNPS, MSDial, and MassBank typically contain spectra at only one or a few collision energies per compound http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Predict the presence or absence of each MS/MS peak at individual MZ positions using SingleFrag's per-bin deep learning classifiers (ANN/GNN/COM), which train a separate model per fragment ion rather than one model for the whole spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Predict the presence or absence of each MS/MS peak at individual MZ positions using SingleFrag's per-bin deep learning classifiers (ANN/GNN/COM), which train a separate model per fragment ion rather than one model for the whole spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need calibrated peak intensities rather than binary presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately predicts presence, not intensity When the molecule exceeds the representable chemistry of the bundled Mol2vec/threshold assets — only the most frequented 1,000 MZ positions in the training set have thresholds and models When you require curation-verified multi-collision-energy reference spectra — the paper notes GNPS, MSDial, and MassBank typically contain spectra at only one or a few collision energies per compound

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra from spectral libraries (e.g., MoNA or NIST 17) need to be cleaned, merged per compound, and converted into integer m/z bin feature vectors before training or applying a machine-learning metabolite annotation model.
skills.name: msms-spectral-preprocessing
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-preprocessing Use when raw MS/MS spectra from spectral libraries (e.g., MoNA or NIST 17) need to be cleaned, merged per compound, and converted into integer m/z bin feature vectors before training or applying a machine-learning metabolite annotation model. When spectra are already peak-binned or preprocessed feature vectors, applying this skill again would re-denose and re-bin them incorrectly When spectra are from negative ion mode or use adducts other than H+ or NH4+, since the paper's homogeneity selection criteria exclude them When the goal is de novo spectral library matching (not ANN fingerprint prediction), since these steps are tailored to the MetFID feature-extraction pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A set of steps described in the MetFID paper for converting raw MS/MS spectra (from MoNA and NIST 17 libraries) into merged, denoised, and binned feature vectors suitable for ANN-based fingerprint prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: A set of steps described in the MetFID paper for converting raw MS/MS spectra (from MoNA and NIST 17 libraries) into merged, denoised, and binned feature vectors suitable for ANN-based fingerprint prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When spectra are already peak-binned or preprocessed feature vectors, applying this skill again would re-denose and re-bin them incorrectly When spectra are from negative ion mode or use adducts other than H+ or NH4+, since the paper's homogeneity selection criteria exclude them When the goal is de novo spectral library matching (not ANN fingerprint prediction), since these steps are tailored to the MetFID feature-extraction pipeline

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra acquired across multiple collision energies must be cleaned (noise peak removal, invalid fragment removal) before computing per-fragment LFP intensity vectors.
skills.name: msms-spectral-preprocessing-filtering
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-preprocessing-filtering Use when raw MS/MS spectra acquired across multiple collision energies must be cleaned (noise peak removal, invalid fragment removal) before computing per-fragment LFP intensity vectors. Input is a single-collision-energy spectrum — longitudinal filtering presumes an acquired CE series across which fragment RII behavior can be assessed The spectra are already filtered (i.e., an existing lfp_profiles.csv or cleaned spectral table is available) — re-running would drop valid fragments against the 2% RII criterion redundantly The task is downstream similarity scoring or metabolite identification — this skill only covers the preprocessing stages, not isomer similarity calculations or identification http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filters and cleans multi-collision-energy MS/MS spectra (13 NCEs plus stepped NCE 20/40/60%) prior to longitudinal fragment profile (LFP) construction, removing noise peaks and invalid fragments so only fragments with meaningful longitudinal behavior are retained. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: Filters and cleans multi-collision-energy MS/MS spectra (13 NCEs plus stepped NCE 20/40/60%) prior to longitudinal fragment profile (LFP) construction, removing noise peaks and invalid fragments so only fragments with meaningful longitudinal behavior are retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-collision-energy spectrum — longitudinal filtering presumes an acquired CE series across which fragment RII behavior can be assessed The spectra are already filtered (i.e., an existing lfp_profiles.csv or cleaned spectral table is available) — re-running would drop valid fragments against the 2% RII criterion redundantly The task is downstream similarity scoring or metabolite identification — this skill only covers the preprocessing stages, not isomer similarity calculations or identification

skills.description: Use when preparing MS/MS spectra for MMSA or multiple spectral alignment in a molecular family — before building the minimum spanning tree, topological sorting, and transitive alignment steps.
skills.name: msms-spectral-preprocessing-filtering
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-preprocessing-filtering Use when preparing MS/MS spectra for MMSA or multiple spectral alignment in a molecular family — before building the minimum spanning tree, topological sorting, and transitive alignment steps. When the goal is pairwise-only spectral comparison without any multiple-alignment step, since the MMSA preprocessing pipeline is designed for the multiple spectral alignment workflow When spectra are already preprocessed by the molecular networking task (e.g. FBMN output) and the user only wants to visualize existing alignment sets rather than recompute them http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Preprocess tandem mass spectra before multiple spectral alignment by filtering peaks, applying square-root intensity transformation, and normalizing peak intensities, so that subsequent consensus peak set computation in MMSA is not dominated by high-intensity outliers or peaks near the precursor ion. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Preprocess tandem mass spectra before multiple spectral alignment by filtering peaks, applying square-root intensity transformation, and normalizing peak intensities, so that subsequent consensus peak set computation in MMSA is not dominated by high-intensity outliers or peaks near the precursor ion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pairwise-only spectral comparison without any multiple-alignment step, since the MMSA preprocessing pipeline is designed for the multiple spectral alignment workflow When spectra are already preprocessed by the molecular networking task (e.g. FBMN output) and the user only wants to visualize existing alignment sets rather than recompute them

skills.description: Use when a molecular feature of interest from an untargeted metabolomics dataset is unannotated or only Level 2/3 annotated, and you want to map it to prior public MS/MS data from specific tissues, organisms, or disease cohorts.
skills.name: msms-spectral-search
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-search Use when a molecular feature of interest from an untargeted metabolomics dataset is unannotated or only Level 2/3 annotated, and you want to map it to prior public MS/MS data from specific tissues, organisms, or disease cohorts. The feature is already annotated to MSI Level 1 via an authentic standard — a tissue search adds no structural certainty The goal is de novo structure elucidation of a novel molecule with no prior MS/MS detection in any public repository The input is raw LC-MS/MS data requiring peak detection and feature quantification first; run a metabolomics processing pipeline before spectral search http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Search unknown MS/MS spectra against public metabolomics repository reference databases (e.g. via tissueMASST) to identify where a feature has been detected before, linking animal-model findings to human cohorts and assigning tissue, organism, and disease metadata to molecular features. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Search unknown MS/MS spectra against public metabolomics repository reference databases (e.g. via tissueMASST) to identify where a feature has been detected before, linking animal-model findings to human cohorts and assigning tissue, organism, and disease metadata to molecular features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature is already annotated to MSI Level 1 via an authentic standard — a tissue search adds no structural certainty The goal is de novo structure elucidation of a novel molecule with no prior MS/MS detection in any public repository The input is raw LC-MS/MS data requiring peak detection and feature quantification first; run a metabolomics processing pipeline before spectral search

skills.description: Use when you have a processed LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table with associated MS/MS spectra and need to quantify structural similarity between every feature pair before clustering.
skills.name: msms-spectral-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-similarity-computation Use when you have a processed LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table with associated MS/MS spectra and need to quantify structural similarity between every feature pair before clustering. Input is already a pairwise similarity/distance matrix or pre-clustered feature groups — re-computation is redundant. You only have MS1 quantification without MS/MS spectra; the skill requires per-feature MS/MS spectra as input. You want feature-set statistical testing directly on raw intensities without spectral structural grouping — use globaltest on feature groups instead of recomputing similarity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Compute all pairwise similarity scores between LC-MS/MS feature MS/MS spectra using a user-selected spectral similarity score within the msFeaST workflow, assembling the results into a symmetric distance matrix used for downstream k-medoids feature grouping and t-SNE embedding. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae584
skills.summary: Compute all pairwise similarity scores between LC-MS/MS feature MS/MS spectra using a user-selected spectral similarity score within the msFeaST workflow, assembling the results into a symmetric distance matrix used for downstream k-medoids feature grouping and t-SNE embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pairwise similarity/distance matrix or pre-clustered feature groups — re-computation is redundant. You only have MS1 quantification without MS/MS spectra; the skill requires per-feature MS/MS spectra as input. You want feature-set statistical testing directly on raw intensities without spectral structural grouping — use globaltest on feature groups instead of recomputing similarity.

skills.description: Use when you have untargeted LC-MS/MS data (converted to open formats like .mzXML/.mzML/.mgf) and want to group related molecules, dereplicate knowns via library matching, and propagate annotations across a spectral network.
skills.name: msms-spectral-similarity-molecular-networking
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-similarity-molecular-networking Use when you have untargeted LC-MS/MS data (converted to open formats like .mzXML/.mzML/.mgf) and want to group related molecules, dereplicate knowns via library matching, and propagate annotations across a spectral network. You need calibrated quantitative results — classic molecular networking can provide only qualitative information about the experiment because only MS2 scans are considered; targeted follow-up LC-MS is required You need to differentiate regio- or stereoisomers — MS2 spectra typically cannot differentiate them You need comprehensive compound identification — only ~5–6% of MS2 spectra in untargeted metabolomics get annotated and most remain unannotated 'dark matter'; in silico annotation tools are beyond the scope of this networking protocol http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Clusters consensus MS2 spectra into molecular-network nodes connected by cosine spectral similarity, then annotates nodes by GNPS spectral-library search — the core GNPS molecular networking analysis that organizes tandem MS data to reveal structurally related molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-020-0317-5
skills.summary: Clusters consensus MS2 spectra into molecular-network nodes connected by cosine spectral similarity, then annotates nodes by GNPS spectral-library search — the core GNPS molecular networking analysis that organizes tandem MS data to reveal structurally related molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need calibrated quantitative results — classic molecular networking can provide only qualitative information about the experiment because only MS2 scans are considered; targeted follow-up LC-MS is required You need to differentiate regio- or stereoisomers — MS2 spectra typically cannot differentiate them You need comprehensive compound identification — only ~5–6% of MS2 spectra in untargeted metabolomics get annotated and most remain unannotated 'dark matter'; in silico annotation tools are beyond the scope of this networking protocol

skills.description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra of an unknown metabolite (e.g. from Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) and need to identify it against a database whose entries may only be structurally related, not identical, compounds.
skills.name: msms-spectral-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-similarity-scoring Use when you have MS/MS spectra of an unknown metabolite (e.g. from Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) and need to identify it against a database whose entries may only be structurally related, not identical, compounds. The experimental spectra dataset has been removed from the repository, so the package cannot be run directly out of the box; do not attempt direct reproduction without the original MetDNA dataset or your own in-house database spectra. Use when the goal is scoring structural similarity from MS/MS spectra — if you only need exact spectrum match against a database without deep-learning similarity transfer, this skill is the wrong choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 DeepMASS scores structural similarity between an unknown metabolite and every metabolite in a database from their MS/MS spectra, using a deep neural network plus a candidate-ranking step to identify unknowns even when only structure-related metabolites are in the database. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05405
skills.summary: DeepMASS scores structural similarity between an unknown metabolite and every metabolite in a database from their MS/MS spectra, using a deep neural network plus a candidate-ranking step to identify unknowns even when only structure-related metabolites are in the database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental spectra dataset has been removed from the repository, so the package cannot be run directly out of the box; do not attempt direct reproduction without the original MetDNA dataset or your own in-house database spectra. Use when the goal is scoring structural similarity from MS/MS spectra — if you only need exact spectrum match against a database without deep-learning similarity transfer, this skill is the wrong choice.

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra in .msp format must be converted into transformer-ready token sequences (m/z binned into tokens, intensities normalized) for training or inference with IDSL_MINT-style encoder-decoder models.
skills.name: msms-spectral-tokenization
skills.search_text: msms-spectral-tokenization Use when raw MS/MS spectra in .msp format must be converted into transformer-ready token sequences (m/z binned into tokens, intensities normalized) for training or inference with IDSL_MINT-style encoder-decoder models. The goal is traditional library matching (e.g. spectral entropy score ≥ 0.75 against NIST 20 or LipidBlast) rather than deep-learning translation of spectra into descriptors The .msp blocks lack PrecursorMZ row entries or any SMILES/InChI/fingerprint labels, since IDSL_MINT requires PrecursorMZ and identifies structures via SMILES/InChI labels Input is already a fingerprint-bit vector or descriptor table (tokenization applies to raw peak lists, not to precomputed descriptors) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Tokenize MS/MS peak lists from NIST .msp spectra into discrete m/z-interval tokens paired with normalized intensities, so a transformer (IDSL_MINT) can treat spectra-to-fingerprint or spectra-to-SMILES prediction as a language translation problem. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00804-5

skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-peak-filtering Use when raw GNPS or other MS/MS library spectra (e.g. ALL_GNPS.json) must be peak-filtered before spectral similarity scoring, model training, or building annotated training subsets like AllPositive/UniqueInchikey. skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-peak-normalization Use when an experimental MS/MS spectrum (peak m/z and intensity pairs) must be scored against theoretical fragment peak lists from candidate molecules, and intensity-scale differences between spectra would bias the match score. When only precursor/MS1 peak m/z values are needed (candidate retrieval there uses the --delta_mz ppm tolerance, not MS/MS intensity normalization) When the spectrum has already been normalized or the downstream scorer expects raw intensities (re-normalizing would double-scale the intensity weights) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Normalizes an experimental tandem MS spectrum's peak intensities so they sum to 1.0, mirroring the ChemDistiller msspectra spectrum handling, so that candidate-scoring against pre-calculated fragmentation patterns is intensity-weighted and comparable across spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: Normalizes an experimental tandem MS spectrum's peak intensities so they sum to 1.0, mirroring the ChemDistiller msspectra spectrum handling, so that candidate-scoring against pre-calculated fragmentation patterns is intensity-weighted and comparable across spectra.

skills.description: Use when you need in silico MS/MS spectra for compounds with known SMILES (e.g., CASMI challenge sets, [M+H]+/[M-H]- precursors) and must quantify prediction quality via cosine similarity versus annotated peak-intensity coverage.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-prediction
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-prediction Use when you need in silico MS/MS spectra for compounds with known SMILES (e.g., CASMI challenge sets, [M+H]+/[M-H]- precursors) and must quantify prediction quality via cosine similarity versus annotated peak-intensity coverage. Compounds require multi-step (MSn) fragmentation prediction — the article states 'the lack of multi-step fragmentation is currently the biggest limitation' of FIORA Predictions need RT or CCS values tuned for production use — RT/CCS prediction is a prototype stage with untuned hyperparameters Spectra have missing collision energies or unclear formats — these were explicitly excluded from FIORA's training/evaluation data http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Predict tandem MS/MS spectra from molecular structures using FIORA, a graph neural network that models each bond cleavage via its local molecular neighborhood, and evaluate prediction quality against observed challenge spectra (e.g., CASMI 2016/2022) using intensity coverage and square-root cosine similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Predict tandem MS/MS spectra from molecular structures using FIORA, a graph neural network that models each bond cleavage via its local molecular neighborhood, and evaluate prediction quality against observed challenge spectra (e.g., CASMI 2016/2022) using intensity coverage and square-root cosine similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds require multi-step (MSn) fragmentation prediction — the article states 'the lack of multi-step fragmentation is currently the biggest limitation' of FIORA Predictions need RT or CCS values tuned for production use — RT/CCS prediction is a prototype stage with untuned hyperparameters Spectra have missing collision energies or unclear formats — these were explicitly excluded from FIORA's training/evaluation data

skills.description: Use when you have molecule SMILES but no experimental MS/MS reference spectrum, and you need predicted spectra for library generation, metabolite annotation, or benchmarking against tools like CFM-ID and 3DMolMS.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-prediction
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-prediction Use when you have molecule SMILES but no experimental MS/MS reference spectrum, and you need predicted spectra for library generation, metabolite annotation, or benchmarking against tools like CFM-ID and 3DMolMS. A curated experimental MS/MS spectrum already exists for the compound at the relevant collision energy — an empirical library match is preferable, since NIST MS/MS provides systematically curated multi-collision-energy spectra The target is peak intensity prediction rather than peak presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately focuses on presence/absence and does not model intensities The molecule falls outside 3DMolMS's supported atom-type set (C, O, N, H, P, S, F, Cl, B, Br, I) or exceeds 300 atoms if using the 3D-conformation-based alternative http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Predict MS/MS spectra of small molecules in silico by training/running per-MZ-position deep learning models (SingleFrag ANN/GNN/COM) that call peak presence or absence, enabling spectral prediction for compounds lacking empirical reference spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Predict MS/MS spectra of small molecules in silico by training/running per-MZ-position deep learning models (SingleFrag ANN/GNN/COM) that call peak presence or absence, enabling spectral prediction for compounds lacking empirical reference spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A curated experimental MS/MS spectrum already exists for the compound at the relevant collision energy — an empirical library match is preferable, since NIST MS/MS provides systematically curated multi-collision-energy spectra The target is peak intensity prediction rather than peak presence/absence — SingleFrag deliberately focuses on presence/absence and does not model intensities The molecule falls outside 3DMolMS's supported atom-type set (C, O, N, H, P, S, F, Cl, B, Br, I) or exceeds 300 atoms if using the 3D-conformation-based alternative

skills.description: Use when a trained C2MS model must convert a molecular structure into a predicted tandem MS/MS spectrum — e.g. to predict spectra for PubChem molecules absent from NIST20 so they can be ranked against an unknown spectrum.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-prediction-inference
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-prediction-inference Use when a trained C2MS model must convert a molecular structure into a predicted tandem MS/MS spectrum — e.g. to predict spectra for PubChem molecules absent from NIST20 so they can be ranked against an unknown spectrum. When an experimental MS/MS spectrum is already available in a spectral library such as NIST20 — retrieval against real spectra is the baseline and predicted spectra should augment, not replace, it When the target chemistry involves complex rearrangements (e.g. cyclizations) that the recursive edge-removal algorithm cannot account for, as these produce unexplained Outside-of-Support (OS) peaks When evaluating spectra from unmerged data or experimental conditions beyond the training scope (different instrument platforms, non-[M+H]+ precursor adducts), where performance has not been established http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Runs the FraGNNet two-stage probabilistic GNN (Molecule GNN + Fragment GNN) to predict an MS/MS spectrum from a molecular structure via its fragmentation DAG, producing a table of monoisotopic-mass peaks with intensities and formula/fragment annotations. This is the C2MS inference step used both for prediction-error benchmarking and to generate candidate spectra for retrieval-based MS2C. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2404.02360
skills.summary: Runs the FraGNNet two-stage probabilistic GNN (Molecule GNN + Fragment GNN) to predict an MS/MS spectrum from a molecular structure via its fragmentation DAG, producing a table of monoisotopic-mass peaks with intensities and formula/fragment annotations. This is the C2MS inference step used both for prediction-error benchmarking and to generate candidate spectra for retrieval-based MS2C.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When an experimental MS/MS spectrum is already available in a spectral library such as NIST20 — retrieval against real spectra is the baseline and predicted spectra should augment, not replace, it When the target chemistry involves complex rearrangements (e.g. cyclizations) that the recursive edge-removal algorithm cannot account for, as these produce unexplained Outside-of-Support (OS) peaks When evaluating spectra from unmerged data or experimental conditions beyond the training scope (different instrument platforms, non-[M+H]+ precursor adducts), where performance has not been established

skills.description: Use when a task requires simulating MS/MS spectra from a molecular structure — e.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-prediction-training
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-prediction-training Use when a task requires simulating MS/MS spectra from a molecular structure — e. The goal is formula-level rather than fragment-level prediction — SCARF (also in ms-pred) predicts spectra at the level of chemical formula and may be the more appropriate comparator Only a small NPLIB1/CANOPUS-style dataset is needed, since main-branch support for NPLIB1 is retired and requires the legacy iceberg_1.0 branch Throughput matters more than interpretability: ICEBERG costs roughly 1 CPU second per molecule, nearly an order of magnitude slower than SCARF http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Trains and applies ICEBERG, a two-stage Generate-then-Score MS/MS spectrum predictor that simulates bond breakage events with a gated GNN and scores fragments/hydrogen shifts with a Set Transformer, yielding interpretable, physically grounded predicted spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Trains and applies ICEBERG, a two-stage Generate-then-Score MS/MS spectrum predictor that simulates bond breakage events with a gated GNN and scores fragments/hydrogen shifts with a Set Transformer, yielding interpretable, physically grounded predicted spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is formula-level rather than fragment-level prediction — SCARF (also in ms-pred) predicts spectra at the level of chemical formula and may be the more appropriate comparator Only a small NPLIB1/CANOPUS-style dataset is needed, since main-branch support for NPLIB1 is retired and requires the legacy iceberg_1.0 branch Throughput matters more than interpretability: ICEBERG costs roughly 1 CPU second per molecule, nearly an order of magnitude slower than SCARF

skills.description: Use when preparing raw or centroided query spectra and spectral library spectra (e.g. iPRG2012 TripleTOF data, NIST/Selevsek libraries) as input to ANN-SoLo or SpectraST-style library searching.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-preprocessing
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-preprocessing Use when preparing raw or centroided query spectra and spectral library spectra (e.g. iPRG2012 TripleTOF data, NIST/Selevsek libraries) as input to ANN-SoLo or SpectraST-style library searching. Spectra have already been preprocessed with different, incompatible peak-count or intensity-normalization conventions — reapplying could double-filter or distort the remaining peaks The downstream tool expects raw intensities or its own internal preprocessing (e.g. MSFragger fragment-index database search, which is not spectral-library based) Spectra intentionally kept with few peaks or narrow mass ranges for targeted diagnostics, since the <10-peak / <250 Da discard rule will silently remove them http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocess query and spectral-library MS/MS spectra identically before open spectral library searching: remove the precursor peak, strip low-intensity noise, cap peak counts, discard poor spectra, and rank-transform intensities so similarity scores (dot product / shifted dot product) behave consistently. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: Preprocess query and spectral-library MS/MS spectra identically before open spectral library searching: remove the precursor peak, strip low-intensity noise, cap peak counts, discard poor spectra, and rank-transform intensities so similarity scores (dot product / shifted dot product) behave consistently.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra have already been preprocessed with different, incompatible peak-count or intensity-normalization conventions — reapplying could double-filter or distort the remaining peaks The downstream tool expects raw intensities or its own internal preprocessing (e.g. MSFragger fragment-index database search, which is not spectral-library based) Spectra intentionally kept with few peaks or narrow mass ranges for targeted diagnostics, since the <10-peak / <250 Da discard rule will silently remove them

skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-preprocessing Use when input is a raw MSP file of MS/MS peak lists (e.g. Orbitrap or QTOF scans at several collision energies) that must be turned into fixed-width model inputs for embedding prediction or candidate matching. Input is already preprocessed model input (e.g. a binned spectrum array or embedding) — re-binning or re-merging would discard information. Only a single collision-energy spectrum exists per feature and no merging is intended; the preprocessing step still applies (thresholding/binning) but the merged-spectrum rationale does not. Candidate retrieval stage is the target — precursor tolerance (--precursor_tolerance_ppm), not --tolerance, governs filtering there; this skill does not change retrieval. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Convert raw MSP peak lists into model-ready spectra by merging scans across collision energies, binarizing intensities above a threshold, binning peaks at a fixed m/z resolution, and appending calculated neutral losses — the featurization ChemEmbed's CNN consumes. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Convert raw MSP peak lists into model-ready spectra by merging scans across collision energies, binarizing intensities above a threshold, binning peaks at a fixed m/z resolution, and appending calculated neutral losses — the featurization ChemEmbed's CNN consumes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already preprocessed model input (e.g. a binned spectrum array or embedding) — re-binning or re-merging would discard information. Only a single collision-energy spectrum exists per feature and no merging is intended; the preprocessing step still applies (thresholding/binning) but the merged-spectrum rationale does not. Candidate retrieval stage is the target — precursor tolerance (--precursor_tolerance_ppm), not --tolerance, governs filtering there; this skill does not change retrieval.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (or MZmine output) must be converted to .mzXML, MS2 centroided, exported as MS2-only .csv plus .mgf spectra, and library-matched in GNPS2 FBMN to reproduce cosine/paired-peak annotations.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-preprocessing
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-preprocessing Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (or MZmine output) must be converted to .mzXML, MS2 centroided, exported as MS2-only .csv plus .mgf spectra, and library-matched in GNPS2 FBMN to reproduce cosine/paired-peak annotations. The task is feature filtering or scheduled precursor list (SPL) construction from a full-scan .csv — that upstream step is RegFilter's job (npts-based filtering); this skill starts from already-acquired MS/MS data. Input is raw vendor data not yet converted to .mzXML — MSConvert conversion must precede MZmine 2.53 preprocessing in this workflow. The goal is purely in silico annotation (e.g., the SIRIUS 5.8.5 layer) rather than spectral pairing against a curated in-house/GNPS2 library — no .mgf library match is produced in that case. http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Preprocesses SPL- and DDA-acquired LC-MS/MS data of actinomycete extracts by converting raw files to .mzXML (MSConvert), centroiding MS2 in MZmine 2.53 (Centroid detector, noise 1E2), exporting MS2-only .csv feature tables and .mgf paired fragmentation spectra, and searching them in the GNPS2 FBMN workflow against curated in-house/GNPS2 libraries for cosine scores and paired-peak counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Preprocesses SPL- and DDA-acquired LC-MS/MS data of actinomycete extracts by converting raw files to .mzXML (MSConvert), centroiding MS2 in MZmine 2.53 (Centroid detector, noise 1E2), exporting MS2-only .csv feature tables and .mgf paired fragmentation spectra, and searching them in the GNPS2 FBMN workflow against curated in-house/GNPS2 libraries for cosine scores and paired-peak counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is feature filtering or scheduled precursor list (SPL) construction from a full-scan .csv — that upstream step is RegFilter's job (npts-based filtering); this skill starts from already-acquired MS/MS data. skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-preprocessing-binning Use when raw MS/MS peak lists (precursor m/z, ionization mode, m/z-intensity pairs) must be converted into MetFID's fixed-length binned feature vectors before loading them into the fingerprint-prediction ANN. The input is already a binned, scaled feature matrix or the spectra are being submitted directly to the pre-trained .h5 model after prior preprocessing The task requires merging across collision energies for testing spectra — MetFID's testing workflow applies preprocessing but without merging across collision energies The data are chromatographic peak tables or other non-MS/MS feature lists rather than per-analyte peak lists with precursor mass and ionization mode http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Preprocessing workflow from MetFID that converts raw MS/MS peak lists into fixed-length numeric feature vectors via intensity scaling (0–100), denoising (remove peaks with intensity < 10), neutral-loss feature calculation, and integer-bin m/z binning so spectra can be fed to the fingerprint-predicting ANN. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Preprocessing workflow from MetFID that converts raw MS/MS peak lists into fixed-length numeric feature vectors via intensity scaling (0–100), denoising (remove peaks with intensity < 10), neutral-loss feature calculation, and integer-bin m/z binning so spectra can be fed to the fingerprint-predicting ANN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a binned, scaled feature matrix or the spectra are being submitted directly to the pre-trained .h5 model after prior preprocessing The task requires merging across collision energies for testing spectra — MetFID's testing workflow applies preprocessing but without merging across collision energies The data are chromatographic peak tables or other non-MS/MS feature lists rather than per-analyte peak lists with precursor mass and ionization mode

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS peak files (mzML, mzXML, or MGF) must be cleaned before spectrum similarity computation, feature hashing, or clustering — e.g. precursor peaks and noise dominate the spectrum and would distort cosine similarity.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-preprocessing-peak-filtering
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-preprocessing-peak-filtering Use when raw MS/MS peak files (mzML, mzXML, or MGF) must be cleaned before spectrum similarity computation, feature hashing, or clustering — e.g. precursor peaks and noise dominate the spectrum and would distort cosine similarity. Input spectra are metabolomics or top-down data with few, widely spaced peaks — the default min_peaks=5 and 250 m/z range filters would incorrectly discard valid spectra Input is already a processed/consensus spectrum (e.g. cluster representative from a prior falcon run) where re-filtering would remove informative peaks The downstream similarity measure requires raw untransformed intensities and you have not adjusted the eps cosine threshold for the scaling method http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocess high-resolution MS/MS spectra prior to clustering or similarity search by removing precursor-ion and low-intensity noise peaks, restricting to the most intense peaks, discarding low-quality spectra, and applying a square-root intensity transformation to de-emphasize dominant peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Preprocess high-resolution MS/MS spectra prior to clustering or similarity search by removing precursor-ion and low-intensity noise peaks, restricting to the most intense peaks, discarding low-quality spectra, and applying a square-root intensity transformation to de-emphasize dominant peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are metabolomics or top-down data with few, widely spaced peaks — the default min_peaks=5 and 250 m/z range filters would incorrectly discard valid spectra Input is already a processed/consensus spectrum (e.g. cluster representative from a prior falcon run) where re-filtering would remove informative peaks The downstream similarity measure requires raw untransformed intensities and you have not adjusted the eps cosine threshold for the scaling method

skills.description: Use when antibody MGF spectra plus a database-search pseudo-ground truth (MS-GF+/X!Tandem, 1% FDR) are available and you need to quantify missing fragment ions or noise-peak fractions to interpret de novo sequencing errors.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-quality-metrics
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-quality-metrics Use when antibody MGF spectra plus a database-search pseudo-ground truth (MS-GF+/X!Tandem, 1% FDR) are available and you need to quantify missing fragment ions or noise-peak fractions to interpret de novo sequencing errors. Input spectra lack a validated database-search ground truth (e.g. purely de novo predictions with no MS-GF+/X!Tandem PSMs at 1% FDR), so fragment ion completeness cannot be assessed against known sequences. Spectra are already pre-annotated with ion assignments or the analysis goal is de novo prediction itself rather than spectrum quality characterization. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates antibody MS/MS spectra for fragment ion completeness and noise by matching the eight b/y ion types to observed peaks with Pyteomics at 0.5 Da tolerance, then computes per-dataset noise factors. This quantifies the spectral quality limitations (missing fragmentation sites and noisy peaks) that constrain de novo peptide sequencing tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Annotates antibody MS/MS spectra for fragment ion completeness and noise by matching the eight b/y ion types to observed peaks with Pyteomics at 0.5 Da tolerance, then computes per-dataset noise factors. This quantifies the spectral quality limitations (missing fragmentation sites and noisy peaks) that constrain de novo peptide sequencing tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack a validated database-search ground truth (e.g. purely de novo predictions with no MS-GF+/X!Tandem PSMs at 1% FDR), so fragment ion completeness cannot be assessed against known sequences. Spectra are already pre-annotated with ion assignments or the analysis goal is de novo prediction itself rather than spectrum quality characterization.

skills.description: Use when HR-MS/MS spectra of novel compounds must be labeled 'relevant' vs 'other' for a user-defined substance class (e.g., prenylated (iso-)flavonoids) from annotated training spectra and MS2DeepScore embeddings.
skills.name: msms-spectrum-relevant-other-labeling
skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-relevant-other-labeling Use when HR-MS/MS spectra of novel compounds must be labeled 'relevant' vs 'other' for a user-defined substance class (e.g., prenylated (iso-)flavonoids) from annotated training spectra and MS2DeepScore embeddings. The training set of 'relevant' reference spectra is highly imbalanced versus 'other' spectra — the authors state classification will most often not succeed in this case and AnnoMe cannot resolve it. Compute is too limited to generate and cache MS2DeepScore embeddings (the ~4-hour step could not be processed on a 16GB MacBook Air with passive cooling) and no cached embeddings exist. The task needs multi-class substance-class assignment rather than the binary 'relevant'/'other' decision AnnoMe's classifiers produce. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Labels HR-MS/MS spectra of novel compounds as 'relevant' or 'other' by training LDA, NN, and SVM classifiers on MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings of user-curated reference spectra and taking a majority vote, enabling prioritization of e.g. prenylated (iso-)flavonoids in natural product discovery. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Labels HR-MS/MS spectra of novel compounds as 'relevant' or 'other' by training LDA, NN, and SVM classifiers on MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings of user-curated reference spectra and taking a majority vote, enabling prioritization of e.g. prenylated (iso-)flavonoids in natural product discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training set of 'relevant' reference spectra is highly imbalanced versus 'other' spectra — the authors state classification will most often not succeed in this case and AnnoMe cannot resolve it. Compute is too limited to generate and cache MS2DeepScore embeddings (the ~4-hour step could not be processed on a 16GB MacBook Air with passive cooling) and no cached embeddings exist. The task needs multi-class substance-class assignment rather than the binary 'relevant'/'other' decision AnnoMe's classifiers produce.

skills.search_text: msms-spectrum-vectorization Use when filtered MS/MS spectra (matchms Spectrum objects or m/z + intensity arrays) must be turned into fixed-width numerical vectors — e.g., to feed a Siamese neural network for embedding creation or pairwise similarity scoring. Spectra have not yet been filtered (peak removal, 1000-peak cap, square-root intensity transform must happen first per the paper's preprocessing) The analysis needs the original discrete peak list rather than a quantized vector — e.g., classical peak-matching measures like modified Cosine that align individual peaks Peaks lie outside the 10–1000 m/z binning window and must be retained, since binning is restricted to that range http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts MS/MS peak lists into fixed-length 10,000-element numerical vectors by binning peaks into equal-width bins spanning 10–1000 m/z, keeping the highest peak intensity per bin. skills.name: msms-synthetic-noise-simulation
skills.search_text: msms-synthetic-noise-simulation Use when validating a denoising pipeline on clean query MS/MS spectra: synthetic chemical noise (from formula_db) and electronic noise must be injected before running spectral_denoising and scoring recovery.
