Only a single assay feature table is available — fit a single-block PLS model instead of an MB-PLS integration The goal is structural clustering or annotation of already-selected significant features — use MamsiStructSearch rather than re-running the MB-PLS integration Data are raw LC-MS instrument files (mzML/NetCDF) rather than preprocessed feature tables — feature extraction must occur first http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates multiple multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics feature tables into a single multiblock partial least-squares (MB-PLS) model using the MAMSI Python framework, enabling prediction of a phenotypic outcome and quantification of each data block's contribution. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01327
skills.summary: Integrates multiple multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics feature tables into a single multiblock partial least-squares (MB-PLS) model using the MAMSI Python framework, enabling prediction of a phenotypic outcome and quantification of each data block's contribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single assay feature table is available — fit a single-block PLS model instead of an MB-PLS integration The goal is structural clustering or annotation of already-selected significant features — use MamsiStructSearch rather than re-running the MB-PLS integration Data are raw LC-MS instrument files (mzML/NetCDF) rather than preprocessed feature tables — feature extraction must occur first

skills.description: Use when feature-intensity tables exported from XCMS, MZmine2, SIEVE, or Skyline span multiple or long LC/GC-MS batches and show injection-order signal drift (QC RSD rising over time) that must be corrected before statistical analysis.
skills.name: multi-batch-metabolomics-data-integration
skills.search_text: multi-batch-metabolomics-data-integration Use when feature-intensity tables exported from XCMS, MZmine2, SIEVE, or Skyline span multiple or long LC/GC-MS batches and show injection-order signal drift (QC RSD rising over time) that must be corrected before statistical analysis. No QC samples are available in the batches — shiftCor requires named 'QC' injections; use the QC-free Combat alternative (shiftCor_dQC) instead. The goal is ready-to-submit feature peak areas from raw mass-spectrometric files rather than batch correction of an existing intensity table. A single short batch already meets precision criteria (e.g. most QC peaks already < 15% RSD), where correction would add no benefit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Integrate multi-batch LC/GC-MS-based metabolomics or label-free proteomics datasets by applying QC-based random forest signal correction (QC-RFSC) with the statTarget shiftCor function, which corrects feature-level inter- and intra-batch signal drift using pooled QC injection-order trends. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Integrate multi-batch LC/GC-MS-based metabolomics or label-free proteomics datasets by applying QC-based random forest signal correction (QC-RFSC) with the statTarget shiftCor function, which corrects feature-level inter- and intra-batch signal drift using pooled QC injection-order trends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No QC samples are available in the batches — shiftCor requires named 'QC' injections; use the QC-free Combat alternative (shiftCor_dQC) instead. The goal is ready-to-submit feature peak areas from raw mass-spectrometric files rather than batch correction of an existing intensity table. A single short batch already meets precision criteria (e.g. most QC peaks already < 15% RSD), where correction would add no benefit.

skills.description: Use when merging two or more platform-specific metabolomics tables (e.g., MS and NMR) whose rows cover the same biological samples, and simple concatenation or mid-level PCA-score fusion would let a high-variance platform dominate the integrated table.
skills.name: multi-block-data-fusion-scaling
skills.search_text: multi-block-data-fusion-scaling Use when merging two or more platform-specific metabolomics tables (e.g., MS and NMR) whose rows cover the same biological samples, and simple concatenation or mid-level PCA-score fusion would let a high-variance platform dominate the integrated table. There is only a single platform/table to analyze — no second block exists to fuse; run Viime's normalization/transformation/scaling pipeline instead. Raw per-metabolite concentration columns must be preserved unscaled in the merged table — Viime's simple (i.e., concatenative) merge algorithm is the right choice, not multi-block scaling. The datasets share no overlapping samples — multi-block fusion requires rows to be aligned to the same biological samples across blocks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Viime's multi-block data fusion scaling normalizes each platform-specific metabolomics table (e.g., MS and NMR blocks) by dividing it by its first singular value, so every block's first principal component has the same length before the blocks are combined into one fused dataset. It is one of three integration algorithms — with simple (concatenative) and mid-level PCA-score fusion — offered by Viime's dataset merge operation. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Viime's multi-block data fusion scaling normalizes each platform-specific metabolomics table (e.g., MS and NMR blocks) by dividing it by its first singular value, so every block's first principal component has the same length before the blocks are combined into one fused dataset. It is one of three integration algorithms — with simple (concatenative) and mid-level PCA-score fusion — offered by Viime's dataset merge operation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is only a single platform/table to analyze — no second block exists to fuse; run Viime's normalization/transformation/scaling pipeline instead. Raw per-metabolite concentration columns must be preserved unscaled in the merged table — Viime's simple (i.e., concatenative) merge algorithm is the right choice, not multi-block scaling. The datasets share no overlapping samples — multi-block fusion requires rows to be aligned to the same biological samples across blocks.

skills.description: Use when integrating two or more pathway-transformed omics matrices (samples as rows, pathway scores as columns) to predict a binary outcome and rank pathways with block-specific importances.
skills.name: multi-block-partial-least-squares-modeling
skills.search_text: multi-block-partial-least-squares-modeling Use when integrating two or more pathway-transformed omics matrices (samples as rows, pathway scores as columns) to predict a binary outcome and rank pathways with block-specific importances. Input data is raw molecular abundances and you want to include molecules not annotated to any pathway — a molecular-level MB-PLS (skipping ssPA) achieved the same AUC 0.70 but needed more latent variables (6 vs 4) Samples lack measurements across all omics views — PathIntegrate requires all input omics measured on the same individuals and discards incomplete samples You only need unsupervised pathway enrichment without outcome prediction — conventional approaches (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) serve that purpose and were not benchmarked here http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits a multi-block partial least squares (MB-PLS) model on pathway-transformed multi-omics views to integrate them in a shared latent space, producing block-wise MB-VIP pathway importances and outcome prediction. Used in PathIntegrate Multi-View to associate pathways with outcomes across omics layers. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Fits a multi-block partial least squares (MB-PLS) model on pathway-transformed multi-omics views to integrate them in a shared latent space, producing block-wise MB-VIP pathway importances and outcome prediction. Used in PathIntegrate Multi-View to associate pathways with outcomes across omics layers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw molecular abundances and you want to include molecules not annotated to any pathway — a molecular-level MB-PLS (skipping ssPA) achieved the same AUC 0.70 but needed more latent variables (6 vs 4) Samples lack measurements across all omics views — PathIntegrate requires all input omics measured on the same individuals and discards incomplete samples You only need unsupervised pathway enrichment without outcome prediction — conventional approaches (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) serve that purpose and were not benchmarked here

skills.description: Use when raw, TIC-normalized, m/z-binned (0.1 Da) 1D MS vectors must be transformed into multi-channel embedded representations to feed CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers instead of single-channel inputs.
skills.name: multi-channel-embedding-module-implementation
skills.search_text: multi-channel-embedding-module-implementation Use when raw, TIC-normalized, m/z-binned (0.1 Da) 1D MS vectors must be transformed into multi-channel embedded representations to feed CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers instead of single-channel inputs. Input is already a multi-channel or image-structured representation (the module targets raw single-channel 1D MS vectors, in_channels=1) The task requires biological/clinical interpretation of which m/z regions contribute to classification — the article states the biological interpretation of learned features was not investigated Sample size is too small or classes are severely imbalanced — the article notes deep models may fail to learn embedding representations in these extreme cases http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Implements the MSMCE (Multi-Channel Embedding) representation module for raw 1D mass spectrometry vectors in PyTorch: a two-layer fully connected encoder (D→2048→d=1024 with LayerNorm/ReLU/Dropout) followed by two 1D convolutional channel-embedding layers (out_channels=256, kernel_size=3, padding 1), whose outputs are concatenated along the channel dimension to form a fused B×257×1024 tensor for downstream classifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: Implements the MSMCE (Multi-Channel Embedding) representation module for raw 1D mass spectrometry vectors in PyTorch: a two-layer fully connected encoder (D→2048→d=1024 with LayerNorm/ReLU/Dropout) followed by two 1D convolutional channel-embedding layers (out_channels=256, kernel_size=3, padding 1), whose outputs are concatenated along the channel dimension to form a fused B×257×1024 tensor for downstream classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a multi-channel or image-structured representation (the module targets raw single-channel 1D MS vectors, in_channels=1) The task requires biological/clinical interpretation of which m/z regions contribute to classification — the article states the biological interpretation of learned features was not investigated Sample size is too small or classes are severely imbalanced — the article notes deep models may fail to learn embedding representations in these extreme cases

skills.description: Use when classifying raw, TIC-normalized 1D mass spectrometry spectra (e.g., NSCLC, CRLM, RCC, or Canine Sarcoma feature matrices) and single-channel CNN/sequence baselines underperform;
skills.name: multi-channel-embedding-representation-learning
skills.search_text: multi-channel-embedding-representation-learning Use when classifying raw, TIC-normalized 1D mass spectrometry spectra (e.g., NSCLC, CRLM, RCC, or Canine Sarcoma feature matrices) and single-channel CNN/sequence baselines underperform; The input is already a curated feature table or a non-MS data modality — MSMCE is designed for raw/TIC-normalized 1D MS vectors, and embedding dimensions require dataset-specific tuning for new domains The dataset is severely class-imbalanced or has very few samples — the paper notes performance may be limited in such extreme cases and deep models may fail to learn embeddings The goal is transfer learning across datasets/tasks — the article states transferability of the module has not yet been evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Applies the MSMCE (Multi-Channel Embedding Representation Module) to one-dimensional raw mass spectrometry vectors, learning inter-channel dependencies to produce multi-channel embedded representations that are fused with an initial encoded representation and fed to classifiers such as ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, LSTM, or Transformer. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: Applies the MSMCE (Multi-Channel Embedding Representation Module) to one-dimensional raw mass spectrometry vectors, learning inter-channel dependencies to produce multi-channel embedded representations that are fused with an initial encoded representation and fed to classifiers such as ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, LSTM, or Transformer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated feature table or a non-MS data modality — MSMCE is designed for raw/TIC-normalized 1D MS vectors, and embedding dimensions require dataset-specific tuning for new domains The dataset is severely class-imbalanced or has very few samples — the paper notes performance may be limited in such extreme cases and deep models may fail to learn embeddings The goal is transfer learning across datasets/tasks — the article states transferability of the module has not yet been evaluated

skills.description: Use when a trained Keras/TensorFlow classifier has a sigmoid output layer with two classes (e.g. massNet's normal/tumor head) but the training label vector contains K > 2 class labels, and a probabilistic multi-class output is required.
skills.name: multi-class-classification-loss-selection
skills.search_text: multi-class-classification-loss-selection Use when a trained Keras/TensorFlow classifier has a sigmoid output layer with two classes (e.g. massNet's normal/tumor head) but the training label vector contains K > 2 class labels, and a probabilistic multi-class output is required. The task remains the paper's binary normal/tumor delineation problem — the original sigmoid + binary cross-entropy configuration is already adequate and should not be changed. The classifier consumes raw m/z spectra directly rather than the VAE 5-dimensional Code layer — this skill modifies only the output head, not the feature representation. There is no multi-class ground-truth annotation available; the article notes that annotating MSI data from histology alone is an approximation and that ground-truth establishment is the challenging task for other tissue and tumor types. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Adapts the massNet classifier — originally a Keras/TensorFlow model with two fully connected hidden layers and a 2-class sigmoid output — to multi-class probabilistic classification by switching the output layer to a K-unit softmax and replacing binary cross-entropy with categorical cross-entropy. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Adapts the massNet classifier — originally a Keras/TensorFlow model with two fully connected hidden layers and a 2-class sigmoid output — to multi-class probabilistic classification by switching the output layer to a K-unit softmax and replacing binary cross-entropy with categorical cross-entropy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task remains the paper's binary normal/tumor delineation problem — the original sigmoid + binary cross-entropy configuration is already adequate and should not be changed. The classifier consumes raw m/z spectra directly rather than the VAE 5-dimensional Code layer — this skill modifies only the output head, not the feature representation. There is no multi-class ground-truth annotation available; the article notes that annotating MSI data from histology alone is an approximation and that ground-truth establishment is the challenging task for other tissue and tumor types.

skills.description: Use when pooling metabolomics matrices from multiple cohorts (e.g., 226 Nightingale NMR biomarkers across 12 studies, N=44,168) that contain below-detection-limit zeros and need per-cohort transformation before joint survival modeling or meta-analysis.
skills.name: multi-cohort-harmonization-of-metabolomics-data
skills.search_text: multi-cohort-harmonization-of-metabolomics-data Use when pooling metabolomics matrices from multiple cohorts (e.g., 226 Nightingale NMR biomarkers across 12 studies, N=44,168) that contain below-detection-limit zeros and need per-cohort transformation before joint survival modeling or meta-analysis. A score in absolute concentration units is required (e.g., for clinical patient classification), since per-cohort scaled values are explicitly not suitable for this purpose in the article The input is already an analysis-ready, transformed biomarker matrix — re-applying the x+1 shift, log transform, and z-scaling would distort values The biomarkers come from a different metabolomics platform without zero-valued detection-limit entries, where the x+1 censoring correction is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Harmonizes metabolic biomarker measurements across multiple cohorts by handling below-detection-limit values (x+1 shift), log-transforming, and z-scaling each biomarker separately per study, producing an analysis-ready biomarker matrix suitable for joint Cox survival modeling and meta-analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: Harmonizes metabolic biomarker measurements across multiple cohorts by handling below-detection-limit values (x+1 shift), log-transforming, and z-scaling each biomarker separately per study, producing an analysis-ready biomarker matrix suitable for joint Cox survival modeling and meta-analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A score in absolute concentration units is required (e.g., for clinical patient classification), since per-cohort scaled values are explicitly not suitable for this purpose in the article The input is already an analysis-ready, transformed biomarker matrix — re-applying the x+1 shift, log transform, and z-scaling would distort values The biomarkers come from a different metabolomics platform without zero-valued detection-limit entries, where the x+1 censoring correction is not applicable

skills.description: Use when reproducing or reporting gene-set enrichment results (ES plus permutation p-values) for specific pathways across multiple pairwise comparisons of microarray groups, e.g. DM2 vs NGT and smoker vs never-smoker.
skills.name: multi-comparison-pathway-result-tabulation
skills.search_text: multi-comparison-pathway-result-tabulation Use when reproducing or reporting gene-set enrichment results (ES plus permutation p-values) for specific pathways across multiple pairwise comparisons of microarray groups, e.g. DM2 vs NGT and smoker vs never-smoker. The goal is to compute pathway activity levels via SVD (the PLAGE approach) rather than to reproduce GSEA-style ES and permutation p-values for named gene-sets Only a single comparison is of interest with no need to cross-compare pathway ES/p-values across groups The gene-set collection or expression dataset differs from the KEGG/Biocarta ~400 pathway sets and the diabetes/smoking microarray datasets, so the published ES values are no longer valid reproduction targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tabulates gene-set enrichment scores (ES) and permutation-based p-values for target pathways (e.g., KEGG ribosome, KEGG oxidative phosphorylation, Biocarta Lectin Induced Complement Pathway) across several pairwise group comparisons of expression data, following the GSEA-style procedure compared against PLAGE in Tomfohr et al. 2005. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Tabulates gene-set enrichment scores (ES) and permutation-based p-values for target pathways (e.g., KEGG ribosome, KEGG oxidative phosphorylation, Biocarta Lectin Induced Complement Pathway) across several pairwise group comparisons of expression data, following the GSEA-style procedure compared against PLAGE in Tomfohr et al. 2005.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compute pathway activity levels via SVD (the PLAGE approach) rather than to reproduce GSEA-style ES and permutation p-values for named gene-sets Only a single comparison is of interest with no need to cross-compare pathway ES/p-values across groups The gene-set collection or expression dataset differs from the KEGG/Biocarta ~400 pathway sets and the diabetes/smoking microarray datasets, so the published ES values are no longer valid reproduction targets

skills.description: Use when a metabolomic peak table has been processed by multiple candidate workflows (filtering/imputation, QCS correction, transformation, normalization combinations) and you must rank or grade which workflow performs for that specific study.
skills.name: multi-criteria-workflow-performance-assessment
skills.search_text: multi-criteria-workflow-performance-assessment Use when a metabolomic peak table has been processed by multiple candidate workflows (filtering/imputation, QCS correction, transformation, normalization combinations) and you must rank or grade which workflow performs for that specific study. The dataset has fewer than 6 samples in one timepoint or class — criterion Cc is unsuitable for such small-sample data No reference metabolites (e.g., spike-ins) are provided — criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied, so the full five-criteria evaluation is impossible The goal is raw-file conversion or peak-table generation rather than judging already-processed workflows — use Proteowizard/XCMS-type preparation tools instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assess candidate metabolomic peak-table processing workflows (e.g., MDI+NON+NON+[CON-AUT], HAM+LLR+NON+[SUM-LEV]) against five independent performance criteria (Ca–Cd plus LogFC) in stage S5 of NOREVA, converting numeric scores into Good/Fair/Poor classifications so the best workflow for a specific study can be identified among thousands of combinatorial candidates. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Assess candidate metabolomic peak-table processing workflows (e.g., MDI+NON+NON+[CON-AUT], HAM+LLR+NON+[SUM-LEV]) against five independent performance criteria (Ca–Cd plus LogFC) in stage S5 of NOREVA, converting numeric scores into Good/Fair/Poor classifications so the best workflow for a specific study can be identified among thousands of combinatorial candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has fewer than 6 samples in one timepoint or class — criterion Cc is unsuitable for such small-sample data No reference metabolites (e.g., spike-ins) are provided — criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied, so the full five-criteria evaluation is impossible The goal is raw-file conversion or peak-table generation rather than judging already-processed workflows — use Proteowizard/XCMS-type preparation tools instead

skills.description: Use when training a structure-generative model (e.g. MSNovelist RNN) that must consume a large merged chemical-structure corpus independent of spectral libraries.
skills.name: multi-database-chemical-structure-training-set-staging
skills.search_text: multi-database-chemical-structure-training-set-staging Use when training a structure-generative model (e.g. MSNovelist RNN) that must consume a large merged chemical-structure corpus independent of spectral libraries. The input is already a processed spectral library (e.g. GNPS or MoNA spectra) rather than a chemical-structure corpus — MSNovelist training is deliberately independent of spectral libraries You only need to run inference/prediction on new MS2 spectra with the released SIRIUS 6 GUI or the prebuilt Docker container, not retrain the RNN Working on the login node only: the Singularity build and AWS dataset download 'freak out on login node' and must run on job nodes http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Stages the 1,232,184-structure training corpus for the MSNovelist encoder–decoder RNN by compiling chemical structures from HMDB 4.0, COCONUT and DSSTox plus 14,047 predicted fingerprints, via an AWS S3 dataset and Singularity workflow on an Euler HPC cluster. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01486-3
skills.summary: Stages the 1,232,184-structure training corpus for the MSNovelist encoder–decoder RNN by compiling chemical structures from HMDB 4.0, COCONUT and DSSTox plus 14,047 predicted fingerprints, via an AWS S3 dataset and Singularity workflow on an Euler HPC cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed spectral library (e.g. GNPS or MoNA spectra) rather than a chemical-structure corpus — MSNovelist training is deliberately independent of spectral libraries You only need to run inference/prediction on new MS2 spectra with the released SIRIUS 6 GUI or the prebuilt Docker container, not retrain the RNN Working on the login node only: the Singularity build and AWS dataset download 'freak out on login node' and must run on job nodes

skills.description: Use when a metadata sheet (unique sample id, plate_id, well_location, compound name, structure fields) for compound libraries lacks standardized structure information or descriptor fields and needs enrichment from PubChem plus optional DNP/LOTUS/DrugBank/DrugCentral/Broad-Hub lookups.
skills.name: multi-database-metadata-enrichment
skills.search_text: multi-database-metadata-enrichment Use when a metadata sheet (unique sample id, plate_id, well_location, compound name, structure fields) for compound libraries lacks standardized structure information or descriptor fields and needs enrichment from PubChem plus optional DNP/LOTUS/DrugBank/DrugCentral/Broad-Hub lookups. When the metadata sheet already contains validated, standardized structures and all descriptor fields (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey/logP/monoisotopic mass) populated — re-running the cleanup adds no information When the goal is MS data acquisition or spectral library building (e.g. Orbitrap ID-X sequence creation or mzmine processing) rather than compound metadata/structure harmonization When a database requires a local file and/or special access that is unavailable and you cannot set it to False in jobs.py — the flow will not correctly skip that source http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Harmonizes a shared-template metadata sheet for compound libraries and enriches each row with standardized structures and descriptors (canonical/isomeric SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, logP, monoisotopic mass) by querying PubChem and optional natural-product/drug databases, orchestrated as a Prefect 2 flow with per-database toggles in jobs.py. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0
skills.summary: Harmonizes a shared-template metadata sheet for compound libraries and enriches each row with standardized structures and descriptors (canonical/isomeric SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, logP, monoisotopic mass) by querying PubChem and optional natural-product/drug databases, orchestrated as a Prefect 2 flow with per-database toggles in jobs.py.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the metadata sheet already contains validated, standardized structures and all descriptor fields (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey/logP/monoisotopic mass) populated — re-running the cleanup adds no information When the goal is MS data acquisition or spectral library building (e.g. Orbitrap ID-X sequence creation or mzmine processing) rather than compound metadata/structure harmonization When a database requires a local file and/or special access that is unavailable and you cannot set it to False in jobs.py — the flow will not correctly skip that source

skills.description: Use when you have raw MS/MS feature tables from multiple LC-MS/MS lipidomics datasets and need standardized lipid annotations with estimated FDR aggregated across datasets.
skills.name: multi-dataset-annotation-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-dataset-annotation-aggregation Use when you have raw MS/MS feature tables from multiple LC-MS/MS lipidomics datasets and need standardized lipid annotations with estimated FDR aggregated across datasets. Input is already a curated, filtered annotation table — re-running EQ+LCI library search and ECN filtering would duplicate existing work Target analytes are non-lipid metabolites — the LCI retention-time rules and LipidIN library are lipid-specific (121 subclasses) The task requires double-bond localization via Paternò–Büchi derivatization — use the separate PB spectral library workflow, not the general EQ+LCI pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Runs the LipidIN EQ+LCI annotation workflow across four LC-MS/MS datasets (RBL-2H3 cells, lipid mixture, human sera, zebrafish tissue), computes per-dataset false discovery rates, and aggregates them to a reported average FDR of 5.69% at the cutoff threshold of 2.4. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Runs the LipidIN EQ+LCI annotation workflow across four LC-MS/MS datasets (RBL-2H3 cells, lipid mixture, human sera, zebrafish tissue), computes per-dataset false discovery rates, and aggregates them to a reported average FDR of 5.69% at the cutoff threshold of 2.4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated, filtered annotation table — re-running EQ+LCI library search and ECN filtering would duplicate existing work Target analytes are non-lipid metabolites — the LCI retention-time rules and LipidIN library are lipid-specific (121 subclasses) The task requires double-bond localization via Paternò–Büchi derivatization — use the separate PB spectral library workflow, not the general EQ+LCI pipeline

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether MetaboAnnotatoR's fragment matching outperforms tools on diverse LC–MS AIF datasets, or when deciding whether a precision (82–92%) and recall (82–85%) at rank 1–5 is acceptable for a given biological matrix.
skills.name: multi-dataset-annotation-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-dataset-annotation-performance-comparison Use when evaluating whether MetaboAnnotatoR's fragment matching outperforms tools on diverse LC–MS AIF datasets, or when deciding whether a precision (82–92%) and recall (82–85%) at rank 1–5 is acceptable for a given biological matrix. The dataset is a single matrix or already has ground-truth annotations for all features — this skill is specifically for comparing across multiple datasets/matrices. You need annotations for Orbitrap-acquired or SWATH data — the article explicitly states these were not tested and future work is needed. Your fragment library is very small for nonlipid metabolites — recall will be misleadingly low; use a different evaluation approach. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 This skill is used to compare annotation performance between MetaboAnnotatoR and MS-DIAL across multiple datasets and matrices, using precision and recall as metrics. It helps understand when high-rank scores (1–5) are reliable and when they fail for datasets dominated by nonlipid metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: This skill is used to compare annotation performance between MetaboAnnotatoR and MS-DIAL across multiple datasets and matrices, using precision and recall as metrics. It helps understand when high-rank scores (1–5) are reliable and when they fail for datasets dominated by nonlipid metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a single matrix or already has ground-truth annotations for all features — this skill is specifically for comparing across multiple datasets/matrices. You need annotations for Orbitrap-acquired or SWATH data — the article explicitly states these were not tested and future work is needed. Your fragment library is very small for nonlipid metabolites — recall will be misleadingly low; use a different evaluation approach.

skills.description: Use when a collection of raw LC-MS metabolomics datasets (e.g., 11 validation datasets spanning different sample types, data acquisition modes, and MS vendors) must be processed with automatically tuned, dataset-specific feature-extraction parameters rather than one-size-fits-all defaults.
skills.name: multi-dataset-batch-processing
skills.search_text: multi-dataset-batch-processing Use when a collection of raw LC-MS metabolomics datasets (e.g., 11 validation datasets spanning different sample types, data acquisition modes, and MS vendors) must be processed with automatically tuned, dataset-specific feature-extraction parameters rather than one-size-fits-all defaults. The input is already a processed feature table rather than raw LC-MS data — Paramounter measures parameters directly from raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data prior to feature extraction. Only a single dataset with known-good manually tuned parameters is available and no cross-dataset robustness or parameter automation is needed. The target feature-extraction program is not among the programs Paramounter translates parameters for (e.g., MS-DIAL-based or XCMS CentWave pipelines). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Batch-process multiple LC-MS metabolomics datasets through Paramounter, which automatically measures universal parameters (mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, instrumental shift) from raw data and translates them into software-specific parameters for feature extraction, validating that the tuning is robust across sample types, acquisition modes, and MS vendors. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c04758
skills.summary: Batch-process multiple LC-MS metabolomics datasets through Paramounter, which automatically measures universal parameters (mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, instrumental shift) from raw data and translates them into software-specific parameters for feature extraction, validating that the tuning is robust across sample types, acquisition modes, and MS vendors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table rather than raw LC-MS data — Paramounter measures parameters directly from raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data prior to feature extraction. Only a single dataset with known-good manually tuned parameters is available and no cross-dataset robustness or parameter automation is needed. skills.description: Use when evaluating whether combining link-scoring functions (e.g. IOKR and standardised Metcalf-style strain correlation) yields a higher proportion of validated links than individual scores, using percentile thresholds over per-pair link scores.

skills.search_text: multi-dataset-link-enrichment-analysis Use when evaluating whether combining link-scoring functions (e.g. IOKR and standardised Metcalf-style strain correlation) yields a higher proportion of validated links than individual scores, using percentile thresholds over per-pair link scores. When no ground-truth validated-link labels exist for the data sets, since enrichment proportions cannot be computed When the goal is ranking or generating links themselves (use NPLinker's get_links scoring) rather than statistically evaluating score enrichment When scores are not comparable on a common percentile basis across data sets, since the 90th-percentile threshold is defined per data set per scoring method http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Reproduces the 90th-percentile enrichment analysis showing that metabolomic–genomic links scoring above the 90th percentile on both IOKR and standardised strain correlation scores are significantly enriched for validated links compared to either score alone across the Crüsemann, Gross, and Leão data sets (Table 2). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Reproduces the 90th-percentile enrichment analysis showing that metabolomic–genomic links scoring above the 90th percentile on both IOKR and standardised strain correlation scores are significantly enriched for validated links compared to either score alone across the Crüsemann, Gross, and Leão data sets (Table 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth validated-link labels exist for the data sets, since enrichment proportions cannot be computed When the goal is ranking or generating links themselves (use NPLinker's get_links scoring) rather than statistically evaluating score enrichment When scores are not comparable on a common percentile basis across data sets, since the 90th-percentile threshold is defined per data set per scoring method

skills.description: Use when you have multiple annotated lipidomics datasets with retention times and need to quantify how consistently a relative retention-time ordering rule holds across all of them, rather than within a single dataset.
skills.name: multi-dataset-median-conformity-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-dataset-median-conformity-aggregation Use when you have multiple annotated lipidomics datasets with retention times and need to quantify how consistently a relative retention-time ordering rule holds across all of them, rather than within a single dataset. You have only a single dataset and want a per-dataset RT ordering check — this skill aggregates medians across many datasets. Lipids lack subclass/chain-composition annotations, so ECN or ESCN scores cannot be computed and the ordering predicates are undefined. The input is raw MS spectra rather than already-annotated lipids with retention times — annotation must precede this aggregation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aggregates per-dataset conformity statistics for lipid retention-time rules (ECN, intra-subclass unsaturation parallelism, ESCN) across >100 published LC-MS datasets to obtain a median conformity value and average absolute RT deviation rates. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Aggregates per-dataset conformity statistics for lipid retention-time rules (ECN, intra-subclass unsaturation parallelism, ESCN) across >100 published LC-MS datasets to obtain a median conformity value and average absolute RT deviation rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single dataset and want a per-dataset RT ordering check — this skill aggregates medians across many datasets. Lipids lack subclass/chain-composition annotations, so ECN or ESCN scores cannot be computed and the ordering predicates are undefined. The input is raw MS spectra rather than already-annotated lipids with retention times — annotation must precede this aggregation.

skills.summary: Aggregates per-dataset evaluation metrics (F_ACC, A_ACC, solver running time) across the three benchmark datasets (TripleTOF 6600, QE HF, MTBLS562) into a single solver-comparison table, so accuracy–runtime trade-offs of G-Aligner's Greedy, Gurobi and VLSNS solvers can be jointly verified.

skills.description: Use when a sample cohort table carries 2–3 categorical metadata dimensions (e.g., two-category treatment, three-category gender, four-category age group) that must be balanced across batches and randomized within a plate before LC/GC-MS injection to avoid drift and batch effects.
skills.name: multi-dimensional-stratified-sample-metadata-handling
skills.search_text: multi-dimensional-stratified-sample-metadata-handling Use when a sample cohort table carries 2–3 categorical metadata dimensions (e.g., two-category treatment, three-category gender, four-category age group) that must be balanced across batches and randomized within a plate before LC/GC-MS injection to avoid drift and batch effects. You need to preserve the natural numerical characteristics of the sample feature distribution — block randomization completely averages out the distribution, and complete randomization is explicitly not a perfect substitute A dimension has too many groups under special numerical distributions — the optimized block randomization's averaging-step calculation can lead to local aggregation Samples have no categorical metadata dimensions at all and only require QC placement (use the Predefined QC Location / Pre-Interpolation of QC workflow instead) Import, balance, and randomize a sample cohort across multiple metadata classification dimensions (e.g., treatment/placebo, gender, age group) using InjectionDesign's inter-batch balancing and intra-batch stratified block randomization for LC/GC-MS plate and injection-sequence design. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.02.26.530140
skills.summary: Import, balance, and randomize a sample cohort across multiple metadata classification dimensions (e.g., treatment/placebo, gender, age group) using InjectionDesign's inter-batch balancing and intra-batch stratified block randomization for LC/GC-MS plate and injection-sequence design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to preserve the natural numerical characteristics of the sample feature distribution — block randomization completely averages out the distribution, and complete randomization is explicitly not a perfect substitute A dimension has too many groups under special numerical distributions — the optimized block randomization's averaging-step calculation can lead to local aggregation Samples have no categorical metadata dimensions at all and only require QC placement (use the Predefined QC Location / Pre-Interpolation of QC workflow instead)

skills.description: Use when multiple random forest models (one per metabolite per feature set) have been trained and their feature importances must be ranked, tallied across control runs, and merged into a network table with confidence scores.
skills.name: multi-feature-set-model-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-feature-set-model-aggregation Use when multiple random forest models (one per metabolite per feature set) have been trained and their feature importances must be ranked, tallied across control runs, and merged into a network table with confidence scores. You need causal/mechanistic relationships — the 'guilt by association' strategy used by network inference methods may not identify causative mechanisms Input is already an aggregated network table or only a single feature set without the 8 control experiments, so no 0–8 confidence tally can be computed You want to transfer the trained models to predict metabolomics from in vivo or other non-CCLE sources — models are not directly transferrable due to in vitro vs in vivo differences and limited feature overlap http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates per-metabolite, per-feature-set random forest regression models into a single regulome network table (Metab8D_network.xlsx) by extracting each model's top 20 features and assigning a 0–8 confidence score based on how many of 8 control experiments a feature appears in. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Aggregates per-metabolite, per-feature-set random forest regression models into a single regulome network table (Metab8D_network.xlsx) by extracting each model's top 20 features and assigning a 0–8 confidence score based on how many of 8 control experiments a feature appears in.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need causal/mechanistic relationships — the 'guilt by association' strategy used by network inference methods may not identify causative mechanisms Input is already an aggregated network table or only a single feature set without the 8 control experiments, so no 0–8 confidence tally can be computed You want to transfer the trained models to predict metabolomics from in vivo or other non-CCLE sources — models are not directly transferrable due to in vitro vs in vivo differences and limited feature overlap

skills.description: Use when ingesting mass spectral library records from multiple OMSL sources in differing file formats (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV, .XML) whose field names and values must be harmonized before integration or annotation workflows.
skills.name: multi-format-ms-file-parsing-msp-mgf-json-csv
skills.search_text: multi-format-ms-file-parsing-msp-mgf-json-csv Use when ingesting mass spectral library records from multiple OMSL sources in differing file formats (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV, .XML) whose field names and values must be harmonized before integration or annotation workflows. The input is already a unified, FragHub-processed library whose fields are already in the harmonized schema — re-parsing would risk breaking the naming. The goal is processing raw instrument acquisition files (e.g. mzML/Thermo raw) rather than spectral library records — FragHub handles OMSL library formats, not raw data. The source file encodes only what FragHub cannot use: spectra lacking both SMILES and InChI, precursor m/z and adduct information are removed during processing anyway. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Parse heterogeneous open mass spectral library (OMSL) files in .MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV and .XML formats (e.g. GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial exports) and map their field names/values to a unified, GNPS-compatible naming scheme so downstream tools like MS-Dial, MZmine and Flash Entropy Search can consume the result. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02219
skills.summary: Parse heterogeneous open mass spectral library (OMSL) files in .MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV and .XML formats (e.g. GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial exports) and map their field names/values to a unified, GNPS-compatible naming scheme so downstream tools like MS-Dial, MZmine and Flash Entropy Search can consume the result.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a unified, FragHub-processed library whose fields are already in the harmonized schema — re-parsing would risk breaking the naming. The goal is processing raw instrument acquisition files (e.g. mzML/Thermo raw) rather than spectral library records — FragHub handles OMSL library formats, not raw data. The source file encodes only what FragHub cannot use: spectra lacking both SMILES and InChI, precursor m/z and adduct information are removed during processing anyway.

skills.description: Use when input is an unfiltered KO (or gene/compound) abundance table with metadata containing ≥2 groups, time points, or a continuous variable, and pathway/module-level enrichment is the goal.
skills.name: multi-group-microbiome-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-group-microbiome-enrichment-analysis Use when input is an unfiltered KO (or gene/compound) abundance table with metadata containing ≥2 groups, time points, or a continuous variable, and pathway/module-level enrichment is the goal. The abundance table has been prefiltered to a background gene list — GRSA is threshold-free and requires all background features retained The design is a simple two-condition set-based test where a standard hypergeometric/GSEA tool is adequate and multi-group compatibility is not needed The features are not mappable to the built-in KEGG pathway/module, compound, or GO databases and no custom modulelist can be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) via the R package ReporterScore to detect KEGG pathway/module enrichment in KO abundance tables under multi-group, longitudinal, or correlation designs, e.g. re-analyzing skin microbiota (IHSMGC) functional shifts across five aging groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Applies Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) via the R package ReporterScore to detect KEGG pathway/module enrichment in KO abundance tables under multi-group, longitudinal, or correlation designs, e.g. re-analyzing skin microbiota (IHSMGC) functional shifts across five aging groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance table has been prefiltered to a background gene list — GRSA is threshold-free and requires all background features retained The design is a simple two-condition set-based test where a standard hypergeometric/GSEA tool is adequate and multi-group compatibility is not needed The features are not mappable to the built-in KEGG pathway/module, compound, or GO databases and no custom modulelist can be constructed

skills.description: Use when the input is a targeted serum metabolic profiling matrix with more than two phenotype groups plus a sample-information table (SampleID, group), and the goal is to feed iMAP's data-processing and metabolite-selection modules.
skills.name: multi-group-serum-metabolomics-data-handling
skills.search_text: multi-group-serum-metabolomics-data-handling Use when the input is a targeted serum metabolic profiling matrix with more than two phenotype groups plus a sample-information table (SampleID, group), and the goal is to feed iMAP's data-processing and metabolite-selection modules. Input is raw mass-spectrometry data requiring peak picking and annotation — iMAP explicitly did not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking/annotation modules Data has already passed missing-value handling, normalization, and scaling and only feature selection is needed The task is correlation-based network construction rather than feature selection / predictive modeling http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Handles multi-group targeted serum metabolomics data matrices (e.g. 113 metabolites x 234 samples across CRC, polyp, and healthy-control groups) within iMAP/IP4M, preparing them for downstream feature selection and predictive modeling with SVM, RF, or Boruta. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: Handles multi-group targeted serum metabolomics data matrices (e.g. 113 metabolites x 234 samples across CRC, polyp, and healthy-control groups) within iMAP/IP4M, preparing them for downstream feature selection and predictive modeling with SVM, RF, or Boruta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mass-spectrometry data requiring peak picking and annotation — iMAP explicitly did not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking/annotation modules Data has already passed missing-value handling, normalization, and scaling and only feature selection is needed The task is correlation-based network construction rather than feature selection / predictive modeling

skills.description: Use when an annotated spatial metabolomics m/z table contains multiple isomer-level lipid annotation strings per peak (e.g. PC(34:1)/PC(30:2)) that need collapsing into standard lipid classes (DG, TG, PA, PC, PE, SM) before downstream statistics.
skills.name: multi-isomer-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: multi-isomer-annotation-parsing Use when an annotated spatial metabolomics m/z table contains multiple isomer-level lipid annotation strings per peak (e.g. PC(34:1)/PC(30:2)) that need collapsing into standard lipid classes (DG, TG, PA, PC, PE, SM) before downstream statistics. When the annotation data are not lipid names (RefineLipids specialises in lipid nomenclature simplification, not small-molecule or peptide annotation). When annotations are already collapsed to a single standardised identifier per m/z — re-running adds parsing overhead without reducing multiplicity. When lipid names do not conform to a nomenclature rgoslin can parse (e.g. free-text or vendor-specific labels). http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses and simplifies multi-isomer lipid metabolite annotations from spatial metabolomics m/z feature tables into common lipid nomenclature using SpaMTP's RefineLipids function, which converts lipid names into standardised lipid categories and classes via rgoslin parsing. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Parses and simplifies multi-isomer lipid metabolite annotations from spatial metabolomics m/z feature tables into common lipid nomenclature using SpaMTP's RefineLipids function, which converts lipid names into standardised lipid categories and classes via rgoslin parsing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the annotation data are not lipid names (RefineLipids specialises in lipid nomenclature simplification, not small-molecule or peptide annotation). When annotations are already collapsed to a single standardised identifier per m/z — re-running adds parsing overhead without reducing multiplicity. When lipid names do not conform to a nomenclature rgoslin can parse (e.g. free-text or vendor-specific labels).

skills.description: Use when you have completed all three KGMN network reconstructions in MetDNA2Vis and need to visualize or reproduce how a specific unknown peak (e.g., M182T541) is connected to a known metabolite (e.g., C00082) across the layered networks.
skills.name: multi-layer-subnetwork-merging
skills.search_text: multi-layer-subnetwork-merging Use when you have completed all three KGMN network reconstructions in MetDNA2Vis and need to visualize or reproduce how a specific unknown peak (e.g., M182T541) is connected to a known metabolite (e.g., C00082) across the layered networks. The three layer networks have not yet been reconstructed with reconstructNetwork1/2/3 — retrieval and merging require those outputs on disk You only need global network statistics rather than a peak-anchored annotation path; the whole-network reconstruction steps alone suffice Peaks of interest are not connected through the KGMN layers (e.g., unknowns outside the KMRN/BioTransformer reaction space or in non-model organisms not covered by organism-specific reaction databases) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extracts per-layer subnetworks anchored on a pair of peaks (e.g., M182T541 and M262T526) from the three KGMN layers — knowledge-based metabolic reaction network, knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network, and global peak correlation network — and merges them with MetDNA2Vis to visualize the annotation path from a known metabolite (C00082) to an unknown peak. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Extracts per-layer subnetworks anchored on a pair of peaks (e.g., M182T541 and M262T526) from the three KGMN layers — knowledge-based metabolic reaction network, knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network, and global peak correlation network — and merges them with MetDNA2Vis to visualize the annotation path from a known metabolite (C00082) to an unknown peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The three layer networks have not yet been reconstructed with reconstructNetwork1/2/3 — retrieval and merging require those outputs on disk You only need global network statistics rather than a peak-anchored annotation path; the whole-network reconstruction steps alone suffice Peaks of interest are not connected through the KGMN layers (e.g., unknowns outside the KMRN/BioTransformer reaction space or in non-model organisms not covered by organism-specific reaction databases)

skills.description: Use when labeled peak-quality data from multiple biofluid matrices (stool, saliva, urine) is available and a single classifier is needed that reliably flags 'Bad' targeted LC–MS peaks across matrices.
skills.name: multi-matrix-model-training
skills.search_text: multi-matrix-model-training Use when labeled peak-quality data from multiple biofluid matrices (stool, saliva, urine) is available and a single classifier is needed that reliably flags 'Bad' targeted LC–MS peaks across matrices. Data are unlabeled — the classifier is supervised and requires peaks already annotated as 'Good'/'Bad' quality Only a single biofluid matrix is in scope — the article also trains single-matrix RF classifiers per matrix, which may be the better fit The task is untargeted LC–MS preprocessing (e.g. xcms, MZmine, OpenMS) rather than targeted peak integration and quality classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a pooled (multimatrix) random-forest classifier on TARDIS peak-quality metrics (AUC, maximum intensity, points over the peak, custom SNR, bell-curve similarity) to identify 'Bad' chromatographic peaks across stool, saliva and urine matrices in FGFP LC–MS metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00567
skills.summary: Trains a pooled (multimatrix) random-forest classifier on TARDIS peak-quality metrics (AUC, maximum intensity, points over the peak, custom SNR, bell-curve similarity) to identify 'Bad' chromatographic peaks across stool, saliva and urine matrices in FGFP LC–MS metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unlabeled — the classifier is supervised and requires peaks already annotated as 'Good'/'Bad' quality Only a single biofluid matrix is in scope — the article also trains single-matrix RF classifiers per matrix, which may be the better fit The task is untargeted LC–MS preprocessing (e.g. xcms, MZmine, OpenMS) rather than targeted peak integration and quality classification

skills.description: Use when you need to isolate the contribution of each spectral modality (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) to a conditional generative model's structure-elucidation accuracy, e.g. to reproduce or extend the DiffSpectra modality ablation table.
skills.name: multi-modal-spectra-ablation-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-modal-spectra-ablation-analysis Use when you need to isolate the contribution of each spectral modality (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) to a conditional generative model's structure-elucidation accuracy, e.g. to reproduce or extend the DiffSpectra modality ablation table. The question is about 3D structural fidelity rather than conditioning-modality effects — use the RMSD/Hungarian-atom-mapping evaluation path (eval_sampled_mols/rmsd.py) instead of the accuracy ablation. skills.summary: Runs a controlled conditioning-modality ablation for a spectra-conditioned diffusion generator (DiffSpectra/DMT), comparing IR-only, Raman-only, UV-Vis-only and joint 'allspectra' conditioning on the QM9S test set to quantify how much multi-modal spectral input improves structure elucidation accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about 3D structural fidelity rather than conditioning-modality effects — use the RMSD/Hungarian-atom-mapping evaluation path (eval_sampled_mols/rmsd.py) instead of the accuracy ablation. The spectral modalities of interest are NMR or mass spectrometry — the article states DiffSpectra 'currently focuses on three spectral types—UV-Vis, IR, and Raman' and applicability to other modalities remains unexplored. You want general unconditional molecular-generation metrics (e.g. comparison against CDGS or JODO baselines) rather than spectrum-conditioned structure elucidation accuracy.

skills.description: Use when conditioning a 2D/3D molecular generative model on multi-modal spectral inputs (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) and you need fixed-dimensional spectral embeddings rather than point-wise encodings.
skills.name: multi-modal-spectra-encoding
skills.search_text: multi-modal-spectra-encoding Use when conditioning a 2D/3D molecular generative model on multi-modal spectral inputs (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) and you need fixed-dimensional spectral embeddings rather than point-wise encodings. When the task only requires a single spectral modality in isolation and a simple per-frequency-point encoder suffices — the article notes existing methods are 'limited to processing a single type of spectrum in isolation', which is the baseline this skill supersedes. When the downstream generative model does not accept fixed-dimensional conditioning vectors and expects raw spectra, e.g. retrieval-based approaches on finite molecular libraries. When the spectral modality of interest is NMR or mass spectrometry — the discussion states DiffSpectra 'currently focuses on three spectral types—UV-Vis, IR, and Raman' and other modalities 'remain to be' explored. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Segment IR, Raman, and UV-Vis spectra into overlapping patches, project them with learnable linear transforms plus positional encodings into a unified sequence, and encode with a Transformer (SpecFormer) pre-trained via masked patch reconstruction and spectrum-structure contrastive alignment to yield spectral embeddings for conditioning molecular generation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Segment IR, Raman, and UV-Vis spectra into overlapping patches, project them with learnable linear transforms plus positional encodings into a unified sequence, and encode with a Transformer (SpecFormer) pre-trained via masked patch reconstruction and spectrum-structure contrastive alignment to yield spectral embeddings for conditioning molecular generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task only requires a single spectral modality in isolation and a simple per-frequency-point encoder suffices — the article notes existing methods are 'limited to processing a single type of spectrum in isolation', which is the baseline this skill supersedes. When the downstream generative model does not accept fixed-dimensional conditioning vectors and expects raw spectra, e.g. retrieval-based approaches on finite molecular libraries. When the spectral modality of interest is NMR or mass spectrometry — the discussion states DiffSpectra 'currently focuses on three spectral types—UV-Vis, IR, and Raman' and other modalities 'remain to be' explored.

skills.description: Use when a dataset provides multiple spectrum types per molecule (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) and the goal is to condition structure elucidation or generation on all modalities jointly rather than a single spectrum type.
skills.name: multi-modal-spectral-data-handling
skills.search_text: multi-modal-spectral-data-handling Use when a dataset provides multiple spectrum types per molecule (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) and the goal is to condition structure elucidation or generation on all modalities jointly rather than a single spectrum type. The target data contains spectral modalities outside the supported set — DiffSpectra currently handles only UV-Vis, IR, and Raman, and applicability to NMR or mass spectrometry remains unexplored. Only one spectrum type is available and a joint multi-modal run is not needed — in that case use spectra_version ir, raman, or uv instead of allspectra. skills.summary: Benchmark multiple MS/MS spectrum-prediction models (ICEBERG vs. MassFormer, FixedVocab, SCARF, NEIMS, CFM-ID, etc.) on the same test splits (NPLIB1, NIST20) by generating predicted spectra from each model and computing vectorized cosine similarity against true 0.1-Da binned spectra.

skills.description: Use when you must select a regression model for retention time prediction from several candidates and need quantitative comparison of training/test/validation errors and true-positive coverage within ±1 min windows to justify the choice.
skills.name: multi-model-machine-learning-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-model-machine-learning-comparison Use when you must select a regression model for retention time prediction from several candidates and need quantitative comparison of training/test/validation errors and true-positive coverage within ±1 min windows to justify the choice. You need predictions for compound classes absent from training data, e.g. complex high molecular weight lipids such as triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines, which were largely excluded from Retip models. You require narrow retention time search windows finer than ±1 min, e.g. to discriminate closely eluting isomers in typical 12 min UPLC methods. Your chromatographic method differs from the trained HILIC/RPLC setup and you have no matching training data to refit models. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmarks five machine learning regressors (random forest, Bayesian-regularized neural network, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras) side by side for retention time prediction on the HILIC (981 compounds) and RPLC data sets, selecting Keras for lowest overfitting and mean absolute errors of 0.78 min (HILIC) and 0.57 min (RPLC). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Benchmarks five machine learning regressors (random forest, Bayesian-regularized neural network, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras) side by side for retention time prediction on the HILIC (981 compounds) and RPLC data sets, selecting Keras for lowest overfitting and mean absolute errors of 0.78 min (HILIC) and 0.57 min (RPLC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need predictions for compound classes absent from training data, e.g. complex high molecular weight lipids such as triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines, which were largely excluded from Retip models. You require narrow retention time search windows finer than ±1 min, e.g. to discriminate closely eluting isomers in typical 12 min UPLC methods. Your chromatographic method differs from the trained HILIC/RPLC setup and you have no matching training data to refit models.

skills.description: Use when you have spot-level multi-module spatial data (transcript, metabolite, morphology) integrated by haCCA and need to demonstrate that the integrated view captures more heterogeneity than any single modality.

skills.search_text: multi-module-heterogeneity-quantification Use when you have spot-level multi-module spatial data (transcript, metabolite, morphology) integrated by haCCA and need to demonstrate that the integrated view captures more heterogeneity than any single modality. skills.summary: Quantifies spatial heterogeneity by comparing cluster counts and heterogeneity metrics across transcript-only, metabolite-only, and integrated multi-module (morphology + transcript + metabolite) WNN embeddings built with Scanpy on haCCA-integrated 10X Visium and MALDI-MSI mouse brain data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single spatial modality (e.g. transcript-only) is available and no integrated multi-module embedding exists to compare against.
