skills.description: Use when a paired spatial metabolomics + transcriptomics dataset (e.g. integrated Seurat object with MALDI and Visium assays) has per-cluster differential metabolite and gene results and you need regional pathway enrichment.
skills.name: multi-omic-pathway-database-querying
skills.search_text: multi-omic-pathway-database-querying Use when a paired spatial metabolomics + transcriptomics dataset (e.g. integrated Seurat object with MALDI and Visium assays) has per-cluster differential metabolite and gene results and you need regional pathway enrichment. The m/z values have not yet been annotated to metabolite and gene identifiers — pathway overlap tests require annotated feature sets, so run the SpaMTP annotation pipeline first The dataset is metabolomics-only with no transcriptomic modality, since the pipeline is built around metabolite-gene based downstream statistical analyses on integrated Seurat objects You only need single-m/z annotation statistics (use CalculateSingleAnnotationStatistics / CalculateAnnotationStatistics instead of pathway enrichment) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3388 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Joint metabolite- and gene-level pathway enrichment within SpaMTP's downstream statistical pipeline, using Fisher's exact over-representation and GSEA-like rank-based tests against RaMP-DB pathway sets, followed by Graphite-topology Enrichment Map network construction. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Joint metabolite- and gene-level pathway enrichment within SpaMTP's downstream statistical pipeline, using Fisher's exact over-representation and GSEA-like rank-based tests against RaMP-DB pathway sets, followed by Graphite-topology Enrichment Map network construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The m/z values have not yet been annotated to metabolite and gene identifiers — pathway overlap tests require annotated feature sets, so run the SpaMTP annotation pipeline first The dataset is metabolomics-only with no transcriptomic modality, since the pipeline is built around metabolite-gene based downstream statistical analyses on integrated Seurat objects You only need single-m/z annotation statistics (use CalculateSingleAnnotationStatistics / CalculateAnnotationStatistics instead of pathway enrichment)

skills.description: Use when a paired SM (e.g. MALDI-TOF imzML) and ST (e.g. 10X Visium) dataset has been mapped onto common spatial units (spots/pixels) and unimodal clustering of one assay misses metabolically defined populations.
skills.name: multi-omic-wnn-integration
skills.search_text: multi-omic-wnn-integration Use when a paired SM (e.g. MALDI-TOF imzML) and ST (e.g. 10X Visium) dataset has been mapped onto common spatial units (spots/pixels) and unimodal clustering of one assay misses metabolically defined populations. Only one modality is present (SM-only or ST-only) — run Seurat FindNeighbors/FindClusters on the single assay instead; WNN requires co-localised 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays. The SM and ST measurements come from different, unaligned tissue sections — AlignSpatialOmics/MapSpatialOmics binning cannot produce valid colocalised spots, so integration weights would be meaningless. SM pixels have not yet been binned to the transcriptomic spot grid and the question concerns pixel-level (sub-spot) metabolic structure — spot binning deliberately sacrifices pixel resolution. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Weighted-nearest-neighbour (WNN) integration of spatial metabolomics (SM) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data into a single clustering solution, as implemented by SpaMTP's MultiOmicIntegration on a Seurat-class object holding co-registered 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Weighted-nearest-neighbour (WNN) integration of spatial metabolomics (SM) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data into a single clustering solution, as implemented by SpaMTP's MultiOmicIntegration on a Seurat-class object holding co-registered 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one modality is present (SM-only or ST-only) — run Seurat FindNeighbors/FindClusters on the single assay instead; WNN requires co-localised 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays. The SM and ST measurements come from different, unaligned tissue sections — AlignSpatialOmics/MapSpatialOmics binning cannot produce valid colocalised spots, so integration weights would be meaningless. SM pixels have not yet been binned to the transcriptomic spot grid and the question concerns pixel-level (sub-spot) metabolic structure — spot binning deliberately sacrifices pixel resolution.

skills.description: Use when you have >=2 molecular abundance matrices measured on the same individuals and need a predictive, pathway-level multi-omics model that ranks pathways and quantifies each omics layer's contribution.
skills.name: multi-omics-data-integration
skills.search_text: multi-omics-data-integration Use when you have >=2 molecular abundance matrices measured on the same individuals and need a predictive, pathway-level multi-omics model that ranks pathways and quantifies each omics layer's contribution. Input is already a pathway-level or feature table rather than molecular abundance matrices requiring ssPA transformation Omics views are not measured on the same individuals, since PathIntegrate discards samples without data on all omics Goal is conventional per-omics hypothesis testing (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) rather than predictive, pathway-level multivariate integration http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Integrates two or more molecular abundance matrices (e.g. metabolomics, proteomics, transcriptomics) by transforming them to Reactome pathway-level scores with single-sample pathway analysis (kPCA) and fitting a multi-block PLS (MB-PLS) model, yielding pathways ranked by MB-VIP with omics-layer attribution. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Integrates two or more molecular abundance matrices (e.g. metabolomics, proteomics, transcriptomics) by transforming them to Reactome pathway-level scores with single-sample pathway analysis (kPCA) and fitting a multi-block PLS (MB-PLS) model, yielding pathways ranked by MB-VIP with omics-layer attribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway-level or feature table rather than molecular abundance matrices requiring ssPA transformation Omics views are not measured on the same individuals, since PathIntegrate discards samples without data on all omics Goal is conventional per-omics hypothesis testing (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) rather than predictive, pathway-level multivariate integration

skills.description: Use when raw DepMap/CCLE omics feature tables (CNV, mutations, methylation, histone PTMs, RNA, miRNA, lncRNA, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) must be cleaned and normalized before training per-metabolite ML models.
skills.name: multi-omics-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: multi-omics-data-preprocessing Use when raw DepMap/CCLE omics feature tables (CNV, mutations, methylation, histone PTMs, RNA, miRNA, lncRNA, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) must be cleaned and normalized before training per-metabolite ML models. Input is already a clean, Z-scored feature table — re-applying median collapsing or zero-variance removal would be redundant. When the goal is prediction on non-CCLE (e.g. in vivo or other cell-line-panel) data, where the article notes models are not directly transferrable due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions and limited feature overlap. http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Preprocesses raw CCLE omics feature matrices for the ten feature sets of Metab8D by imputing NaNs with zeros, collapsing repeated observations via medians, removing zero-variance features, and Z-score normalizing within each 5-fold CV split so random forest metabolite predictors can be trained. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Preprocesses raw CCLE omics feature matrices for the ten feature sets of Metab8D by imputing NaNs with zeros, collapsing repeated observations via medians, removing zero-variance features, and Z-score normalizing within each 5-fold CV split so random forest metabolite predictors can be trained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a clean, Z-scored feature table — re-applying median collapsing or zero-variance removal would be redundant. When the goal is prediction on non-CCLE (e.g. in vivo or other cell-line-panel) data, where the article notes models are not directly transferrable due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions and limited feature overlap.

skills.description: Use when two or more omics abundance matrices must be harmonized before cross-omics correlation or network analysis, and raw matrices contain many zero (unmeasured) entries that would distort Spearman correlations.
skills.name: multi-omics-data-zero-filtering
skills.search_text: multi-omics-data-zero-filtering Use when two or more omics abundance matrices must be harmonized before cross-omics correlation or network analysis, and raw matrices contain many zero (unmeasured) entries that would distort Spearman correlations. Input is already a processed feature table with no systematic zero padding — re-filtering would silently discard valid samples/variables. Analysis targets a single omics layer with its own domain-specific filtering rules (e.g. raw spectra peak picking), which iMAP deliberately does not implement. The omics matrices measure different cohorts with no shared samples — intersecting would produce an empty table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Pre-processing step for paired multi-omics abundance matrices (e.g. metabolomics and proteomics) that removes high-sparsity samples and variables by zero-fraction thresholds (samples >90% zeros, variables >40% zeros) before normalization, so that downstream correlation/network analysis is computed on matched, adequately-measured features. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: Pre-processing step for paired multi-omics abundance matrices (e.g. metabolomics and proteomics) that removes high-sparsity samples and variables by zero-fraction thresholds (samples >90% zeros, variables >40% zeros) before normalization, so that downstream correlation/network analysis is computed on matched, adequately-measured features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table with no systematic zero padding — re-filtering would silently discard valid samples/variables. Analysis targets a single omics layer with its own domain-specific filtering rules (e.g. raw spectra peak picking), which iMAP deliberately does not implement. The omics matrices measure different cohorts with no shared samples — intersecting would produce an empty table.

skills.description: Use when processing concurrently generated untargeted metabolomic and lipidomic LC-MS/MS feature tables (e.g. from the Multi-ABLE method) through filtering, imputation, EigenMS normalization, and limma differential expression, then verifying reported DE feature counts at adjusted p < 0.05.
skills.name: multi-omics-de-count-validation
skills.search_text: multi-omics-de-count-validation Use when processing concurrently generated untargeted metabolomic and lipidomic LC-MS/MS feature tables (e.g. from the Multi-ABLE method) through filtering, imputation, EigenMS normalization, and limma differential expression, then verifying reported DE feature counts at adjusted p < 0.05. Input is already a filtered, normalized feature table — tbManipulate and EigenMS reprocessing would distort the data The data are proteomic: MultiABLER does not yet provide functions to analyze proteomic data, which is an output of the MultiABLER extraction method Only a single omics layer is present and no joint metabolite/lipid downstream analysis is planned, so the integrative MultiABLER pipeline adds little value http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Runs the MultiABLER pipeline (filter, impute, EigenMS-normalize, limma) on Multi-ABLE-derived metabolomic and lipidomic feature tables and validates the resulting differential-expression counts, as benchmarked on the Apoe+/+ vs Apoe−/− arterial-tissue comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106881
skills.summary: Runs the MultiABLER pipeline (filter, impute, EigenMS-normalize, limma) on Multi-ABLE-derived metabolomic and lipidomic feature tables and validates the resulting differential-expression counts, as benchmarked on the Apoe+/+ vs Apoe−/− arterial-tissue comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered, normalized feature table — tbManipulate and EigenMS reprocessing would distort the data The data are proteomic: MultiABLER does not yet provide functions to analyze proteomic data, which is an output of the MultiABLER extraction method Only a single omics layer is present and no joint metabolite/lipid downstream analysis is planned, so the integrative MultiABLER pipeline adds little value

skills.description: Use when two or more standardized omics matrices (e.g. top-10%-most-variable DNAm beta values and creatinine-normalized urine metabolite intensities) need to be integrated into shared latent factors without a priori labels.
skills.name: multi-omics-factor-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-omics-factor-analysis Use when two or more standardized omics matrices (e.g. top-10%-most-variable DNAm beta values and creatinine-normalized urine metabolite intensities) need to be integrated into shared latent factors without a priori labels. Input matrices have not been preprocessed (DNAm not restricted to top 10% most variable autosomal probes, or metabolomics not creatinine-normalized and missing-value filtered) The goal is dimensionality reduction of categorical behavioral data — the paper uses MCA (FactoMineR 2.4) for behavioral data, not MOFA Only a single omics view is available; MOFA2 here is trained on two views (DNAm and metabolomics) http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3339 Trains a multi-view unsupervised factor model with R/Bioconductor MOFA2 (v1.3.4), executed via the Nextflow module action.nf in a Docker container, to obtain 10 latent factors that jointly describe buccal DNA methylation and creatinine-normalized urine metabolomics data per cohort. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad115
skills.summary: Trains a multi-view unsupervised factor model with R/Bioconductor MOFA2 (v1.3.4), executed via the Nextflow module action.nf in a Docker container, to obtain 10 latent factors that jointly describe buccal DNA methylation and creatinine-normalized urine metabolomics data per cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices have not been preprocessed (DNAm not restricted to top 10% most variable autosomal probes, or metabolomics not creatinine-normalized and missing-value filtered) The goal is dimensionality reduction of categorical behavioral data — the paper uses MCA (FactoMineR 2.4) for behavioral data, not MOFA Only a single omics view is available; MOFA2 here is trained on two views (DNAm and metabolomics)

skills.description: Use when a discriminant MOFA/DIABLO factor from BiomiX needs biological interpretation and you want literature-grounded annotation of its multi-omics contributor features via PubMed abstracts.
skills.name: multi-omics-factor-literature-annotation
skills.search_text: multi-omics-factor-literature-annotation Use when a discriminant MOFA/DIABLO factor from BiomiX needs biological interpretation and you want literature-grounded annotation of its multi-omics contributor features via PubMed abstracts. The factor is not discriminant (not separating cohorts/conditions) — BiomiX's bibliography search is designed for discriminative factor interpretation No known contributor feature names exist for the factor, so no keyword lists can be compiled for the three-level PubMed search Interpretation via clinical-data correlation or pathway analysis (EnrichR/GSEA) alone is sufficient and literature mining is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Annotates discriminant MOFA (or DIABLO) factor contributors by mining PubMed: a three-level contributor-keyword literature search retrieves abstracts, then litsearchR text mining reduces abstract-derived keywords to non-redundant 2–4-word terms mapped to GO-BP and HPO vocabularies for biological interpretation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Annotates discriminant MOFA (or DIABLO) factor contributors by mining PubMed: a three-level contributor-keyword literature search retrieves abstracts, then litsearchR text mining reduces abstract-derived keywords to non-redundant 2–4-word terms mapped to GO-BP and HPO vocabularies for biological interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The factor is not discriminant (not separating cohorts/conditions) — BiomiX's bibliography search is designed for discriminative factor interpretation No known contributor feature names exist for the factor, so no keyword lists can be compiled for the three-level PubMed search Interpretation via clinical-data correlation or pathway analysis (EnrichR/GSEA) alone is sufficient and literature mining is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when per-metabolite model feature importances exist across multiple omics feature sets (e.g., 9 feature sets x 225 metabolites) and the goal is a global, cross-omics top-regulator ranking.
skills.name: multi-omics-feature-importance-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-omics-feature-importance-aggregation Use when per-metabolite model feature importances exist across multiple omics feature sets (e.g., 9 feature sets x 225 metabolites) and the goal is a global, cross-omics top-regulator ranking. When the goal is mechanistic/causal regulation: the 'guilt by association' aggregation is descriptive and not necessarily mechanistic. When applying to a single metabolite model or a single omics class — the aggregation is only meaningful across all 225 metabolite models and multiple feature sets. When the trained models come from non-CCLE sources: the models are not directly transferrable due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions and limited feature overlap. http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Aggregates per-metabolite random-forest feature importances across the 225 metabolite models and all omics feature sets (transcriptomics, proteomics, methylation, phosphoproteomics, CNV, etc.) into a normalized global top-regulator ranking, revealing cross-omics consistent regulators such as YAP1. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Aggregates per-metabolite random-forest feature importances across the 225 metabolite models and all omics feature sets (transcriptomics, proteomics, methylation, phosphoproteomics, CNV, etc.) into a normalized global top-regulator ranking, revealing cross-omics consistent regulators such as YAP1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is mechanistic/causal regulation: the 'guilt by association' aggregation is descriptive and not necessarily mechanistic. When applying to a single metabolite model or a single omics class — the aggregation is only meaningful across all 225 metabolite models and multiple feature sets. When the trained models come from non-CCLE sources: the models are not directly transferrable due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions and limited feature overlap.

skills.search_text: multi-omics-integration-baseline-comparison Use when a new multi-modal integration embedding (e.g., fused spatial transcriptomics + spatial metabolomics latent space) must be fairly ranked against published integration methods on the same AnnData inputs. skills.summary: Benchmark a novel joint ST-SM integration model (SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM) against vertical (Seurat RPCA/CCA, totalVI, Stabmap) and horizontal (scVI, scANVI, scPoli, spaVAE, PCA) baselines on identical inputs, scoring batch correction vs biological conservation with scIB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell or subcellular resolution ST/SM — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data More than two modalities must be integrated — SpatialMETA currently only supports integration of two modalities An independent gold-standard label set is required — the article's labels were manually annotated from H&E histological features, not an external ground truth

skills.description: Use when comparing integration methods (e.g., SpatialMETA, totalVI, SpatialGLUE, MISO, Seurat v5 BNN, Stabmap, spaMultiVAE) on paired ST-SM samples and you need quantitative, ranked evidence of which method's joint embedding preserves spatial biology.
skills.name: multi-omics-integration-embedding-quality-metrics
skills.search_text: multi-omics-integration-embedding-quality-metrics Use when comparing integration methods (e.g., SpatialMETA, totalVI, SpatialGLUE, MISO, Seurat v5 BNN, Stabmap, spaMultiVAE) on paired ST-SM samples and you need quantitative, ranked evidence of which method's joint embedding preserves spatial biology. When the task is horizontal (cross-sample) integration rather than vertical (cross-modal ST-SM) integration — the metric families and ranking here benchmark vertical integration performance When ground-truth labels are unavailable or the tissue cannot be manually annotated from H&E — the biological conservation metrics depend on the manually annotated label key, not an independent gold standard When data are at single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA and this benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark framework for scoring joint embeddings from vertical integration of spatial transcriptomics (ST) and spatial metabolomics (SM) data using four scIB-style metric families — reconstruction accuracy, continuity, marker, and biological conservation — aggregated into an overall score to rank integration methods. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Benchmark framework for scoring joint embeddings from vertical integration of spatial transcriptomics (ST) and spatial metabolomics (SM) data using four scIB-style metric families — reconstruction accuracy, continuity, marker, and biological conservation — aggregated into an overall score to rank integration methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is horizontal (cross-sample) integration rather than vertical (cross-modal ST-SM) integration — the metric families and ranking here benchmark vertical integration performance When ground-truth labels are unavailable or the tissue cannot be manually annotated from H&E — the biological conservation metrics depend on the manually annotated label key, not an independent gold standard When data are at single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA and this benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data

skills.description: Use when you have independent clusterings (or per-dataset kernels) over the same set of observations from M omic platforms and need a single global clustering that down-weights noisy datasets, e.g. pan-cancer subtyping or transcriptional module discovery.
skills.name: multi-omics-integrative-clustering
skills.search_text: multi-omics-integrative-clustering Use when you have independent clusterings (or per-dataset kernels) over the same set of observations from M omic platforms and need a single global clustering that down-weights noisy datasets, e.g. pan-cancer subtyping or transcriptional module discovery. You only have a single omic layer and no per-dataset clusterings or kernels — integrative consensus clustering has nothing to combine You need raw feature-level integration (e.g. regression or classifier features) rather than integration of precomputed cluster structures; KLIC and COCA operate on kernels/clusterings, not raw feature tables Datasets cover non-overlapping sets of observations, since the MOC is N-column binary over a shared observation set and kernels must be defined on the same samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Integrative clustering of multiple omic datasets via Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering (KLIC), which frames consensus clustering as a multiple kernel learning problem with learned per-dataset weights, and its COCA alternative for combining per-dataset clusterings. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Integrative clustering of multiple omic datasets via Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering (KLIC), which frames consensus clustering as a multiple kernel learning problem with learned per-dataset weights, and its COCA alternative for combining per-dataset clusterings.

skills.summary: PathIntegrate Single-View supervised classification on ssPA pathway-transformed multi-omics data: combine all omics layers into one multi-omics pathway-score matrix and fit any SciKitLearn-compatible predictive model (demonstrated with a random forest achieving test AUC 0.95 on COVID-19 data from Su et al. 2020).

skills.description: Use when you have two or more omics data matrices measured on the same individuals (e.g. COPDgene plasma proteomics/metabolomics or the Su et al. 2020 COVID-19 data) and need supervised prediction plus pathway-level interpretation of the outcome.

skills.search_text: multi-omics-predictive-modelling Use when you have two or more omics data matrices measured on the same individuals (e.g. COPDgene plasma proteomics/metabolomics or the Su et al. 2020 COVID-19 data) and need supervised prediction plus pathway-level interpretation of the outcome. Many molecules of interest are un-annotated to pathways — un-annotated molecules cannot currently be incorporated into pathway-based models, causing information loss (a molecular-level MB-PLS on raw abundances should be compared instead) Input omics are not measured on the same individuals — PathIntegrate does not support entire rows of missing data, so samples without all omics must be discarded The goal is conventional differential-enrichment analysis (ORA/GSEA/MultiGSEA/IMPaLA) rather than predictive modelling; no direct comparison to these was performed in the article http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Predictive multi-omics integration at the pathway level using the PathIntegrate framework: molecules are transformed to pathway scores via single-sample pathway analysis (ssPA), then classified/regressed with a Single-View (SKlearn-compatible) or Multi-View multi-block PLS model. It provides outcome prediction, model performance evaluation, and pathway-ranked interpretation, unlike molecule-list-based pathway analysis tools. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Predictive multi-omics integration at the pathway level using the PathIntegrate framework: molecules are transformed to pathway scores via single-sample pathway analysis (ssPA), then classified/regressed with a Single-View (SKlearn-compatible) or Multi-View multi-block PLS model. skills.description: Use when you have paired transcriptomics and intracellular metabolomics data mapped onto a stoichiometric model and want to determine, per reaction, whether flux variation follows substrate abundance (metabolic), enzyme expression (transcriptional), both, or neither.
skills.name: multi-omics-regulation-classification
skills.search_text: multi-omics-regulation-classification Use when you have paired transcriptomics and intracellular metabolomics data mapped onto a stoichiometric model and want to determine, per reaction, whether flux variation follows substrate abundance (metabolic), enzyme expression (transcriptional), both, or neither. The omics data are already integrated and only a single regulation layer is of interest — the intersection step adds no value. No constraint-based model covering the measured reactions is available; concordance analysis requires reaction-level GPRs and flux sampling on the model. Only extracellular metabolomics is measured; the paper's mass-action RPS derivation requires intracellular substrate abundances. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Classifies each metabolic reaction as regulated at the metabolic level, the transcriptional level, both, or neither, by intersecting RPS-vs-RAS and RPS-vs-FFD concordance scores computed from metabolomics and transcriptomics data on a constraint-based model. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009337
skills.summary: Classifies each metabolic reaction as regulated at the metabolic level, the transcriptional level, both, or neither, by intersecting RPS-vs-RAS and RPS-vs-FFD concordance scores computed from metabolomics and transcriptomics data on a constraint-based model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The omics data are already integrated and only a single regulation layer is of interest — the intersection step adds no value. No constraint-based model covering the measured reactions is available; concordance analysis requires reaction-level GPRs and flux sampling on the model. Only extracellular metabolomics is measured; the paper's mass-action RPS derivation requires intracellular substrate abundances.

skills.search_text: multi-platform-data-augmentation Use when you have feature tables from multiple separation methods (e.g., HILIC-Orbitrap MS in ESI+ and ESI− plus CE-Orbitrap MS) that need to be combined into one augmented multi-platform dataset for joint target/suspect counting or chemometric evaluation. You only have a single separation platform (single-method data does not need augmentation; process it directly with the single-platform pipeline) You need MS/MS spectral networking to autonomously connect features detected by two or more methods — this is not implemented in AriumMS and is listed as future development Your input is already a fused/augmented feature table — augmentation would re-link already-merged entries http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Mid-level data fusion of untargeted metabolomics feature tables from different separation platforms (e.g., HILIC-MS and CE-MS) using AriumMS's augmentation step, which links per-method data cubes along the m/z dimension so multi-platform data can be processed and evaluated as a single augmented dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6

skills.description: Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to automatically detect samples whose spectra deviate from the spectral similarity expected across samples before downstream analysis.
skills.name: multi-sample-outlier-detection-via-spectral-similarity
skills.search_text: multi-sample-outlier-detection-via-spectral-similarity Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to automatically detect samples whose spectra deviate from the spectral similarity expected across samples before downstream analysis. Single-sample datasets: the method relies on spectral similarity across multiple samples, so with one sample there is no cross-sample reference to define sample-specific clusters. Datasets where a manual or landmark-based QC approach is already available and preferred over automated outlier flagging. Non-MSI imaging data (e.g. IFM) without pixel-wise spectral peak features, since the embedding requires peak features comparable across samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Automated identification of outlier samples in multi-sample MALDI MSI datasets by jointly embedding all pixels from every sample in a shared 2D UMAP space, clustering with HDBSCAN, and flagging samples whose pixels are dominated by sample-specific clusters (SSC). This is the outlier-detection principle used in msiFlow's pre-processing workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Automated identification of outlier samples in multi-sample MALDI MSI datasets by jointly embedding all pixels from every sample in a shared 2D UMAP space, clustering with HDBSCAN, and flagging samples whose pixels are dominated by sample-specific clusters (SSC). This is the outlier-detection principle used in msiFlow's pre-processing workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-sample datasets: the method relies on spectral similarity across multiple samples, so with one sample there is no cross-sample reference to define sample-specific clusters. Datasets where a manual or landmark-based QC approach is already available and preferred over automated outlier flagging. Non-MSI imaging data (e.g. IFM) without pixel-wise spectral peak features, since the embedding requires peak features comparable across samples.

skills.name: multi-seed-ensemble-variance-estimation
skills.search_text: multi-seed-ensemble-variance-estimation Use when training a RankNet-type pairwise retention-order model where single-seed predictions are noisy, and you need an interpretable uncertainty estimate (prediction variance) to mark distinguishable vs indistinguishable molecular pairs. When only a single deterministic retention-time prediction is needed rather than an uncertainty-aware pairwise order (e.g. the RT outliers the paper says require in-depth mechanistic study). When the chromatographic system is HILIC — the article states ROASMI applies only to RPLC and that constructing HILIC models with generalizability is future work. When the molecular pair falls outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S, since ROASMI's learned embeddings have not been validated on a broader chemical space. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Train the ROASMI RankNet retention model five times from different random seeds to produce ROASMI_1–ROASMI_5, and use the cross-seed variance of predicted pairwise elution probabilities as an uncertainty signal that flags molecular pairs whose retention order is not reliably determined. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Train the ROASMI RankNet retention model five times from different random seeds to produce ROASMI_1–ROASMI_5, and use the cross-seed variance of predicted pairwise elution probabilities as an uncertainty signal that flags molecular pairs whose retention order is not reliably determined.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single deterministic retention-time prediction is needed rather than an uncertainty-aware pairwise order (e.g. the RT outliers the paper says require in-depth mechanistic study). When the chromatographic system is HILIC — the article states ROASMI applies only to RPLC and that constructing HILIC models with generalizability is future work. When the molecular pair falls outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S, since ROASMI's learned embeddings have not been validated on a broader chemical space.

skills.description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks from a derivatizing matrix (e.g. FMP-10) and the analyte has multiple taggable functional groups, so single- and double-derivatized species (forms A and B) must be mass-predicted separately.
skills.name: multi-site-derivatization-mass-accounting
skills.search_text: multi-site-derivatization-mass-accounting Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks from a derivatizing matrix (e.g. FMP-10) and the analyte has multiple taggable functional groups, so single- and double-derivatized species (forms A and B) must be mass-predicted separately. The analyte has only one taggable functional group, so only the singly derivatized species exists and multi-site mass accounting adds no variants The data were acquired with a conventional (non-derivatizing) matrix, where ions follow standard [M+H]+/[M-H]- rules and no derivatization increments apply Input is already a list of Met-ID annotation results; this skill predicts masses rather than annotating them http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes theoretical [M+H]+ m/z values for metabolites derivatized one or more times by a reactive matrix such as FMP-10, accounting for the two double-derivatization variants (demethylated form A via methyl loss and dehydrogenated form B via hydrogen loss). Rationale: FMP-10 can tag multiple functional groups on one molecule, so predicted masses must be generated per derivatization count and variant before checking against observed peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00633
skills.summary: Computes theoretical [M+H]+ m/z values for metabolites derivatized one or more times by a reactive matrix such as FMP-10, accounting for the two double-derivatization variants (demethylated form A via methyl loss and dehydrogenated form B via hydrogen loss). Rationale: FMP-10 can tag multiple functional groups on one molecule, so predicted masses must be generated per derivatization count and variant before checking against observed peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte has only one taggable functional group, so only the singly derivatized species exists and multi-site mass accounting adds no variants The data were acquired with a conventional (non-derivatizing) matrix, where ions follow standard [M+H]+/[M-H]- rules and no derivatization increments apply Input is already a list of Met-ID annotation results; this skill predicts masses rather than annotating them

skills.description: Use when a MZmine feature table has been annotated by multiple lipid identification tools (e.g., LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) and you need to measure cross-software agreement of fatty acyl constituent assignments per polarity.
skills.name: multi-software-lipid-annotation-corroboration-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-software-lipid-annotation-corroboration-analysis Use when a MZmine feature table has been annotated by multiple lipid identification tools (e.g., LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) and you need to measure cross-software agreement of fatty acyl constituent assignments per polarity. You have only a single software's annotations — corroboration cannot be assessed without at least two independent identification sources. Feature annotations from different software have not been aligned to a common feature table (m/z/RT alignment must precede comparison). The goal is de novo lipid identification rather than benchmarking agreement between existing annotation sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Quantifies agreement between lipid annotations from independent software (LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) by appending all identifications to a shared MZmine feature table via CombineSoftwareIDs.R and computing how often each LipidMatch fatty acyl assignment is corroborated by at least one other tool per ion polarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between lipid annotations from independent software (LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) by appending all identifications to a shared MZmine feature table via CombineSoftwareIDs.R and computing how often each LipidMatch fatty acyl assignment is corroborated by at least one other tool per ion polarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single software's annotations — corroboration cannot be assessed without at least two independent identification sources. Feature annotations from different software have not been aligned to a common feature table (m/z/RT alignment must precede comparison). The goal is de novo lipid identification rather than benchmarking agreement between existing annotation sets.

skills.description: Use when you have per-feature candidate lists from several spectral/compound annotation sources and must reduce them to a single, source-supported chemical structure (SMILES) per feature for downstream network or reporting steps.
skills.name: multi-source-annotation-fusion
skills.search_text: multi-source-annotation-fusion Use when you have per-feature candidate lists from several spectral/compound annotation sources and must reduce them to a single, source-supported chemical structure (SMILES) per feature for downstream network or reporting steps. Input is raw MS2 mzML data still needing preprocessing and spectral dereplication — that belongs to the upstream MAW-R segment (Spectra, SIRIUS), not final candidate selection. Only one annotation source is available, so cross-source candidate fusion and source-priority ranking provide no added discrimination. SIRIUS CLI output with no deterministic probability score is the only compound annotation and you need score-based ranking thresholds — the article notes such thresholds were discarded as case-dependent. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Final-stage candidate fusion in the MAW workflow: merge and rank top-scoring annotation candidates from multiple dereplication sources (GNPS, HMDB, MassBank, SIRIUS/MetFrag) using RDKit structural similarity, and select exactly one final candidate chemical structure per MS2 feature. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00695-y
skills.summary: Final-stage candidate fusion in the MAW workflow: merge and rank top-scoring annotation candidates from multiple dereplication sources (GNPS, HMDB, MassBank, SIRIUS/MetFrag) using RDKit structural similarity, and select exactly one final candidate chemical structure per MS2 feature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS2 mzML data still needing preprocessing and spectral dereplication — that belongs to the upstream MAW-R segment (Spectra, SIRIUS), not final candidate selection. Only one annotation source is available, so cross-source candidate fusion and source-priority ranking provide no added discrimination. SIRIUS CLI output with no deterministic probability score is the only compound annotation and you need score-based ranking thresholds — the article notes such thresholds were discarded as case-dependent.

skills.description: Use when several spectral libraries (e.g., .MGF, .MSP files from GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial) have been harmonized and you need to know what fraction of unique compounds is shared vs. exclusive to each source.
skills.name: multi-source-chemical-set-intersection
skills.search_text: multi-source-chemical-set-intersection Use when several spectral libraries (e.g., .MGF, .MSP files from GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial) have been harmonized and you need to know what fraction of unique compounds is shared vs. exclusive to each source. Input spectra lack recalcuable SMILES/InChI and precursor/adduct metadata, so no reliable InChIKey can be derived for set membership You need collision-energy or peak-level spectral deduplication rather than compound-level identifier overlap (SPLASH keys, not InChIKeys, are the appropriate unit there) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Quantifies overlap of unique chemical identifiers (harmonized InChIKeys) across multiple open mass spectral libraries (OMSLs) by building an identifier-to-library membership mapping and tabulating identifiers found in exactly one, two, three, or all sources. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02219
skills.summary: Quantifies overlap of unique chemical identifiers (harmonized InChIKeys) across multiple open mass spectral libraries (OMSLs) by building an identifier-to-library membership mapping and tabulating identifiers found in exactly one, two, three, or all sources.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack recalcuable SMILES/InChI and precursor/adduct metadata, so no reliable InChIKey can be derived for set membership You need collision-energy or peak-level spectral deduplication rather than compound-level identifier overlap (SPLASH keys, not InChIKeys, are the appropriate unit there)

skills.description: Use when several MS/MS spectra from an .mgf file (e.g. a feature group of interest) must be compared for shared fragment m/z bins and neutral losses, beyond what a single mirror plot or pairwise similarity score can reveal.
skills.name: multi-spectrum-fragmentation-overlap-assessment
skills.search_text: multi-spectrum-fragmentation-overlap-assessment Use when several MS/MS spectra from an .mgf file (e.g. a feature group of interest) must be compared for shared fragment m/z bins and neutral losses, beyond what a single mirror plot or pairwise similarity score can reveal. You only need a single pairwise spectrum comparison or a mirror plot for one pair of spectra — the fragmap is for multi-spectrum overlap inspection. You are inspecting the global similarity structure; the t-SNE overview network or pairwise similarity matrix views are the intended entry points for that. The .mgf file lacks the 'feature_id' metadata key specXplore expects, and no matchms-based renaming has been done. Your data exceeds roughly 5000 features, where dashboard scaling is untested and performance difficulties are anticipated. Builds a 2D fragmap heatmap in specXplore that aligns all MS/MS spectra of a selected feature group along the y-axis against factorized fragment m/z bins on the x-axis, filling cells with fragment intensities and overlaying neutral losses so spectral overlaps (or their absence) become visible in a single overview. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Builds a 2D fragmap heatmap in specXplore that aligns all MS/MS spectra of a selected feature group along the y-axis against factorized fragment m/z bins on the x-axis, filling cells with fragment intensities and overlaying neutral losses so spectral overlaps (or their absence) become visible in a single overview.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single pairwise spectrum comparison or a mirror plot for one pair of spectra — the fragmap is for multi-spectrum overlap inspection. You are inspecting the global similarity structure; the t-SNE overview network or pairwise similarity matrix views are the intended entry points for that. The .mgf file lacks the 'feature_id' metadata key specXplore expects, and no matchms-based renaming has been done. Your data exceeds roughly 5000 features, where dashboard scaling is untested and performance difficulties are anticipated.

skills.description: Use when training or restoring ESP MLP/GNN models with multi-task LDA topic prediction and peak-correlation label mixing enabled, and forward/backward passes or output shapes must be validated.
skills.name: multi-task-loss-debugging
skills.search_text: multi-task-loss-debugging Use when training or restoring ESP MLP/GNN models with multi-task LDA topic prediction and peak-correlation label mixing enabled, and forward/backward passes or output shapes must be validated. Only evaluating a pretrained model on a test candidate set (e.g. torch_tecand_1000bin_te_cand100) with no multi-task heads active — the loss-debugging path does not apply Reproducing EI/GC-MS NEIMS-style spectra — the ESP setup is ESI/LC-MS and the code cannot redistribute NIST-20 training data Training the ESP ensemble weighting itself (ens_train_canopus.py ranking task) rather than debugging the per-base-model multi-task heads http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Debugs the ESP multi-task/peak-dependency extensions by enabling the LDA-topic auxiliary head and the rank-limited label-mixing matrix (Q_l = D_l D_l^T) in the MLP/GNN predictors, then verifying forward/backward passes produce 1000-bin spectra and T-topic distributions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae490
skills.summary: Debugs the ESP multi-task/peak-dependency extensions by enabling the LDA-topic auxiliary head and the rank-limited label-mixing matrix (Q_l = D_l D_l^T) in the MLP/GNN predictors, then verifying forward/backward passes produce 1000-bin spectra and T-topic distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only evaluating a pretrained model on a test candidate set (e.g. torch_tecand_1000bin_te_cand100) with no multi-task heads active — the loss-debugging path does not apply Reproducing EI/GC-MS NEIMS-style spectra — the ESP setup is ESI/LC-MS and the code cannot redistribute NIST-20 training data Training the ESP ensemble weighting itself (ens_train_canopus.py ranking task) rather than debugging the per-base-model multi-task heads

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table has many biological groups (e.g. 14 tissues) and the goal is to identify features dramatically enriched in one group versus all others at a strict FDR threshold (e.g. P<0.001, >1000-fold change).
skills.name: multi-tissue-metabolomics-group-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-tissue-metabolomics-group-comparison Use when a metabolomics feature table has many biological groups (e.g. 14 tissues) and the goal is to identify features dramatically enriched in one group versus all others at a strict FDR threshold (e.g. P<0.001, >1000-fold change). The dataset has only two groups or no single tissue/group expected to dominate abundance — a standard pairwise comparison without the >1000-fold filter is more appropriate The data are positive-ion-mode or already normalized/summarized to identified metabolites rather than raw mass features — the thresholds and row-count validation are specific to negative-ion-mode mass-feature tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A statistical differential-abundance workflow for multi-tissue LC-MS metabolomics feature tables, exemplified by comparing one tissue group (buccal gland) against the pooled remaining 13 tissue groups in negative-ion-mode data, using MetaboReport's analysis functions with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and fold-change filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: A statistical differential-abundance workflow for multi-tissue LC-MS metabolomics feature tables, exemplified by comparing one tissue group (buccal gland) against the pooled remaining 13 tissue groups in negative-ion-mode data, using MetaboReport's analysis functions with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and fold-change filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has only two groups or no single tissue/group expected to dominate abundance — a standard pairwise comparison without the >1000-fold filter is more appropriate The data are positive-ion-mode or already normalized/summarized to identified metabolites rather than raw mass features — the thresholds and row-count validation are specific to negative-ion-mode mass-feature tables

skills.description: Use when two or more annotation tools (e.g. mWISE and xMSannotator) must be compared on identical LC-MS peak lists with known compound ground truth, to rank tools by sensitivity, F1, and structural closeness of proposals.
skills.name: multi-tool-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-tool-annotation-comparison Use when two or more annotation tools (e.g. mWISE and xMSannotator) must be compared on identical LC-MS peak lists with known compound ground truth, to rank tools by sensitivity, F1, and structural closeness of proposals. If the datasets have no known compound annotations to serve as ground truth — sensitivity and Tanimoto-vs-original metrics cannot be computed. If you only need to annotate peaks once (no second tool to compare against); use the annotation skill directly rather than a comparison pipeline. If mWISE's KEGG-only database coverage is insufficient for the compounds of interest — the article notes this is a limitation relative to xMSannotator's KEGG, HMDB, Lipid Maps, and T3DB support. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark LC-MS feature annotation algorithms (mWISE vs xMSannotator, and optionally mummichog) side by side on the same filtered peak lists, computing sensitivity and specificity of top candidate lists plus Tanimoto structural similarity of proposed compounds against known references. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00238
skills.summary: Benchmark LC-MS feature annotation algorithms (mWISE vs xMSannotator, and optionally mummichog) side by side on the same filtered peak lists, computing sensitivity and specificity of top candidate lists plus Tanimoto structural similarity of proposed compounds against known references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the datasets have no known compound annotations to serve as ground truth — sensitivity and Tanimoto-vs-original metrics cannot be computed. If you only need to annotate peaks once (no second tool to compare against); use the annotation skill directly rather than a comparison pipeline. If mWISE's KEGG-only database coverage is insufficient for the compounds of interest — the article notes this is a limitation relative to xMSannotator's KEGG, HMDB, Lipid Maps, and T3DB support.

skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single tool's annotations, so pairwise cross-tool Tanimoto indicators (t_gs, t_gi, t_si) cannot be computed Feature candidates lack machine-readable structures (InChI/SMILES), making Morgan fingerprints impossible — first recover empty annotations (e.g. GNPS iterative search produces empty.tsv for missing InChIs/SMILES) You only need a ranked MS2DECIDE output and already possess a complete indicators table — go directly to K-value estimation

skills.description: Use when comparing computational efficiency (runtime, memory) of network-construction implementations across R packages on identical inputs, or when validating performance claims for a new package against established baselines.

skills.search_text: multi-tool-performance-comparison Use when comparing computational efficiency (runtime, memory) of network-construction implementations across R packages on identical inputs, or when validating performance claims for a new package against established baselines. The goal is accuracy or topological correctness of constructed networks rather than computational efficiency — this skill only measures time and memory Datasets exceed the benchmarked scale (>1,000 features in the source protocol); the article's headline numbers (<0.2 s, <100 MB) are calibrated to the 50–1,000-feature range, though MetaNet claims scalability past 10,000 features Comparing tools whose correlation methods or significance thresholds differ, since the benchmark's validity depends on identical inputs and parameters across packages http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_1317 Benchmarks MetaNet's c_net_calculate correlation-network construction against WGCNA, microeco, ggClusterNet, and NetCoMi on identical synthetic omics matrices of increasing size (50–1,000 features), quantifying elapsed time and memory with bench::mark to verify reported up-to-100-fold speed and 50-fold memory advantages. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.06.26.661636
skills.summary: Benchmarks MetaNet's c_net_calculate correlation-network construction against WGCNA, microeco, ggClusterNet, and NetCoMi on identical synthetic omics matrices of increasing size (50–1,000 features), quantifying elapsed time and memory with bench::mark to verify reported up-to-100-fold speed and 50-fold memory advantages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy or topological correctness of constructed networks rather than computational efficiency — this skill only measures time and memory Datasets exceed the benchmarked scale (>1,000 features in the source protocol); the article's headline numbers (<0.2 s, <100 MB) are calibrated to the 50–1,000-feature range, though MetaNet claims scalability past 10,000 features Comparing tools whose correlation methods or significance thresholds differ, since the benchmark's validity depends on identical inputs and parameters across packages

skills.description: Use when starting from a raw table of metabolite measurements plus metabolite (rowData) and sample (colData) metadata, and you need a clean, normalized MultiAssayExperiment object before differential metabolomic testing.
skills.name: multiassayexperiment-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: multiassayexperiment-data-preprocessing Use when starting from a raw table of metabolite measurements plus metabolite (rowData) and sample (colData) metadata, and you need a clean, normalized MultiAssayExperiment object before differential metabolomic testing. Input is already a preprocessed MultiAssayExperiment object (annotated, imputed, and vsn-normalized) — re-running kNN imputation or vsn would distort the data. Your metabolite annotations do not come from or map to the Small Molecular Pathway Database (SMPDB); get_SMPDBanno expects SMPDB identifiers. You are past preprocessing and only need group-wise statistical testing — use diff_test (Student's T-Test/ANOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg correction) on the prepared object instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build and preprocess a MultiAssayExperiment object for MetaboDiff by merging the metabolite measurement table with rowData and colData, then annotating against SMPDB, imputing missing values with kNN at a 0.4 cutoff, removing outlier clusters, and applying variance stabilizing normalization (vsn). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty344
skills.summary: Build and preprocess a MultiAssayExperiment object for MetaboDiff by merging the metabolite measurement table with rowData and colData, then annotating against SMPDB, imputing missing values with kNN at a 0.4 cutoff, removing outlier clusters, and applying variance stabilizing normalization (vsn).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed MultiAssayExperiment object (annotated, imputed, and vsn-normalized) — re-running kNN imputation or vsn would distort the data. skills.search_text: multiblock-pls-regression-modeling Use when you have two or more sample-aligned LC-MS feature-intensity tables (e.g. HPOS/LPOS/LNEG or multi-assay serum assays) and a numeric outcome (continuous bilirubin levels or encoded biological sex) to predict jointly across blocks. You have only a single assay block and no interblock structure to model — a single-block PLS or standard regression suffices The assay blocks are not sample-aligned (features from different assays cannot be indexed onto a common sample order), which breaks block-wise NIPALS fitting The goal is annotation or structural clustering of already-selected features rather than outcome modeling — use MamsiStructSearch instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Fit a multi-block partial least-squares (MB-PLS) model to integrate multiple LC-MS metabolomics assay blocks against a continuous or binary phenotypic outcome, selecting latent variables by cross-validation (estimate_lv) and evaluating performance with k-fold or Monte Carlo cross-validation. This is the core modeling step of the MAMSI workflow and outperforms single-assay models by modeling interblock relationships. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01327

This is the core modeling step of the MAMSI workflow and outperforms single-assay models by modeling interblock relationships.

skills.description: Use when aligning untargeted LC-MS feature lists (m/z, RT, area CSVs) across multiple runs with nonlinear RT drift, where nearest-neighbor or bipartite matching yields ambiguous or inaccurate consensus features and a global non-centric optimum is needed.
skills.name: multidimensional-assignment-optimization
skills.search_text: multidimensional-assignment-optimization Use when aligning untargeted LC-MS feature lists (m/z, RT, area CSVs) across multiple runs with nonlinear RT drift, where nearest-neighbor or bipartite matching yields ambiguous or inaccurate consensus features and a global non-centric optimum is needed. When the input is already a consensus feature map or when pairwise correspondence is sufficient — G-Aligner's graph construction and MAP solving are designed for multi-run, non-centric matching where local pairwise methods underperform. When computing speed is the binding constraint: the multidimensional assignment problem is NP-Hard and G-Aligner's main limitation is 'lack of computing speed'; simple nearest-neighbour or greedy-only pipelines may be preferable for very large datasets. When the feature extraction step itself is the bottleneck — this skill addresses only the feature alignment (matching) stage, not raw peak detection or quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Formulates multi-run LC-MS feature matching as an unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem (MAP) over a multipartite graph of features and potential correspondences, solved with three combinatorial optimization algorithms (Gurobi, Greedy, VLSNS_MSR, VLSNS_MSG variants as surfaced in G-Aligner) to produce optimal consensus feature groups without ambiguous matched groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Formulates multi-run LC-MS feature matching as an unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem (MAP) over a multipartite graph of features and potential correspondences, solved with three combinatorial optimization algorithms (Gurobi, Greedy, VLSNS_MSR, VLSNS_MSG variants as surfaced in G-Aligner) to produce optimal consensus feature groups without ambiguous matched groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a consensus feature map or when pairwise correspondence is sufficient — G-Aligner's graph construction and MAP solving are designed for multi-run, non-centric matching where local pairwise methods underperform. When computing speed is the binding constraint: the multidimensional assignment problem is NP-Hard and G-Aligner's main limitation is 'lack of computing speed'; simple nearest-neighbour or greedy-only pipelines may be preferable for very large datasets. When the feature extraction step itself is the bottleneck — this skill addresses only the feature alignment (matching) stage, not raw peak detection or quantification.

skills.description: Use when aligning detected features across LC-IMS-MS/MS samples where m/z, drift time, and retention time must all be matched to achieve high-confidence feature correspondence between samples.
skills.name: multidimensional-feature-matching
skills.search_text: multidimensional-feature-matching Use when aligning detected features across LC-IMS-MS/MS samples where m/z, drift time, and retention time must all be matched to achieve high-confidence feature correspondence between samples. Input data are 1D or 2D only (e.g., simple LC-MS without ion mobility), where DEIMoS's multidimensional matching offers no advantage over standard m/z-versus-RT alignment Features have already been aligned and only coordinate correction is needed; in that case the SVR-fitting sub-step applies but the matching step is redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Matches features across study samples by simultaneously considering all acquired dimensions (m/z, drift time, retention time) rather than pairwise 2D comparisons, increasing cross-sample alignment/feature matching confidence in DEIMoS workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Matches features across study samples by simultaneously considering all acquired dimensions (m/z, drift time, retention time) rather than pairwise 2D comparisons, increasing cross-sample alignment/feature matching confidence in DEIMoS workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are 1D or 2D only (e.g., simple LC-MS without ion mobility), where DEIMoS's multidimensional matching offers no advantage over standard m/z-versus-RT alignment Features have already been aligned and only coordinate correction is needed; in that case the SVR-fitting sub-step applies but the matching step is redundant

skills.description: Use when raw LC-IMS-MS/MS data (mzML) has been loaded into a common m/z, drift time, retention time, intensity grid and you need to locate ion peaks in 3D without sequential 1D/2D processing that would yield only ~13% cross-sample intersection.
skills.name: multidimensional-local-maximum-peak-picking
skills.search_text: multidimensional-local-maximum-peak-picking Use when raw LC-IMS-MS/MS data (mzML) has been loaded into a common m/z, drift time, retention time, intensity grid and you need to locate ion peaks in 3D without sequential 1D/2D processing that would yield only ~13% cross-sample intersection. Input is already a detected feature table rather than raw high-dimensional MS data — peak picking on pre-partitioned peaks would double-count ions. Data are low-dimensional (e.g. conventional LC-MS without ion mobility), where DEIMoS's 3D simultaneous filtering has no advantage over m/z versus RT processing followed by drift time. You need only a coarse peak list without replicate validation; skipping the analytical-triplicate confirmation discards the article's confidence criterion. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A feature-detection method from DEIMoS that applies a local-maximum filter (scipy.ndimage maximum_filter) simultaneously across m/z, drift time, and retention time of LC-IMS-MS/MS data, then partitions peaks around maxima and thresholds them to produce per-mode feature coordinate tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: A feature-detection method from DEIMoS that applies a local-maximum filter (scipy.ndimage maximum_filter) simultaneously across m/z, drift time, and retention time of LC-IMS-MS/MS data, then partitions peaks around maxima and thresholds them to produce per-mode feature coordinate tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a detected feature table rather than raw high-dimensional MS data — peak picking on pre-partitioned peaks would double-count ions. Data are low-dimensional (e.g. conventional LC-MS without ion mobility), where DEIMoS's 3D simultaneous filtering has no advantage over m/z versus RT processing followed by drift time. You need only a coarse peak list without replicate validation; skipping the analytical-triplicate confirmation discards the article's confidence criterion.

skills.description: Use when input is a time-domain multi-dimensional NMR FID dataset (possibly NUS-sampled, e.g. an NUScon Protein A HNCACB with 8.8% sampling schedule) and the goal is a processed, reconstructed 3D spectrum in NV format.
skills.name: multidimensional-nmr-processing
skills.search_text: multidimensional-nmr-processing Use when input is a time-domain multi-dimensional NMR FID dataset (possibly NUS-sampled, e.g. an NUScon Protein A HNCACB with 8.8% sampling schedule) and the goal is a processed, reconstructed 3D spectrum in NV format. Input is already a processed/frequency-domain spectrum needing only peak picking, assignment, chemical shift prediction, or structure calculation — use the corresponding NMRFx tools instead Data are uniformly (fully) sampled — GRINS NUS reconstruction is unnecessary; only apodization, zero-fill, FT, and phasing apply Data are 1D or other non-NMR formats not readable as NV files (magic value 874032077 check will fail) http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Process multi-dimensional (e.g., 3D) biomolecular NMR datasets — including non-uniformly sampled ones — with NMRFx Processor, applying apodization, zero-fill, Fourier transform, and NUS reconstruction (GRINS) to produce NV-format spectra inspectable in NMRViewJ. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-025-01812-8
skills.summary: Process multi-dimensional (e.g., 3D) biomolecular NMR datasets — including non-uniformly sampled ones — with NMRFx Processor, applying apodization, zero-fill, Fourier transform, and NUS reconstruction (GRINS) to produce NV-format spectra inspectable in NMRViewJ.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed/frequency-domain spectrum needing only peak picking, assignment, chemical shift prediction, or structure calculation — use the corresponding NMRFx tools instead Data are uniformly (fully) sampled — GRINS NUS reconstruction is unnecessary; only apodization, zero-fill, FT, and phasing apply Data are 1D or other non-NMR formats not readable as NV files (magic value 874032077 check will fail)

skills.description: Use when a numerical measurement column has more than two groups (e.g. a 'Condition' column) and the goal is a multi-group comparison — either ANOVA (parametric) or Kruskal-Wallis (non-parametric) — with the p-value annotated on the chart.
skills.name: multigroup-anova-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: multigroup-anova-hypothesis-testing Use when a numerical measurement column has more than two groups (e.g. a 'Condition' column) and the goal is a multi-group comparison — either ANOVA (parametric) or Kruskal-Wallis (non-parametric) — with the p-value annotated on the chart. The numerical column contains exactly two groups — use the t-test (parametric) or U-test (non-parametric Mann-Whitney) two-group activities instead. The activity cannot handle missing values and you need the raw source rows retained — the automatic pre-filtering step removes rows with missing values before submission, so raw data should not be required unchanged downstream. The goal is supervised prediction or feature selection (scikit-learn estimators with grid search), not group-comparison hypothesis testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies parametric (ANOVA) and non-parametric (Kruskal-Wallis) multi-group comparison tests inside Instant Clue's drag & drop Analysis toolbox, annotating the resulting p-value directly on the chart. The skill covers dispatching tests onto a base chart, automatic missing-value pre-filtering, and collecting per-column statistics for export. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6

The skill covers dispatching tests onto a base chart, automatic missing-value pre-filtering, and collecting per-column statistics for export.

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra (binned peak vectors) must be mapped to a full compound fingerprint vector simultaneously, or when a per-digit/per-block multi-model setup is undesirable.
skills.name: multilabel-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: multilabel-neural-network-training Use when MS/MS spectra (binned peak vectors) must be mapped to a full compound fingerprint vector simultaneously, or when a per-digit/per-block multi-model setup is undesirable. The task only requires single-label classification of one fingerprint digit or a small fingerprint block, where a softmax/categorical cross-entropy setup is sufficient. Spectra cannot be binned or lack the metadata (precursor mass, collision energy, InChIKey) needed for the merging, filtering, and loss-feature preprocessing steps. Only fingerprints not covered by MACCS, FP3, or FP4 are needed; the article notes further investigation is needed to evaluate other fingerprint sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a single multi-label ANN (Keras/TensorFlow) that maps binned MS/MS peak vectors to an entire 528-bit MACCS+FP3+FP4 fingerprint in one pass, using sigmoid + binary cross-entropy so latent relationships between fingerprint digits are learned jointly rather than through per-digit or per-block models. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Train a single multi-label ANN (Keras/TensorFlow) that maps binned MS/MS peak vectors to an entire 528-bit MACCS+FP3+FP4 fingerprint in one pass, using sigmoid + binary cross-entropy so latent relationships between fingerprint digits are learned jointly rather than through per-digit or per-block models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task only requires single-label classification of one fingerprint digit or a small fingerprint block, where a softmax/categorical cross-entropy setup is sufficient. Spectra cannot be binned or lack the metadata (precursor mass, collision energy, InChIKey) needed for the merging, filtering, and loss-feature preprocessing steps. Only fingerprints not covered by MACCS, FP3, or FP4 are needed; the article notes further investigation is needed to evaluate other fingerprint sets.

skills.description: Use when you have completed KGMN network reconstruction (reconstructNetwork1/2/3) on MetDNA2 output and need to extract, inspect, or merge the three-layer subnetwork for a specific peak pair or centric metabolite (e.g. M182T541–M262T526).
skills.name: multilayer-metabolic-subnetwork-retrieval
skills.search_text: multilayer-metabolic-subnetwork-retrieval Use when you have completed KGMN network reconstruction (reconstructNetwork1/2/3) on MetDNA2 output and need to extract, inspect, or merge the three-layer subnetwork for a specific peak pair or centric metabolite (e.g. M182T541–M262T526). Global networks have not yet been reconstructed — reconstructNetwork1/2/3 (with reformatTable1 for the annotation table) must run first The analysis targets non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples where organism-specific reaction databases are not yet incorporated into KGMN The goal is to distinguish structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites — KGMN cannot effectively discriminate such isomers (e.g. isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Extract and consolidate layer-specific subnetworks from the KGMN global networks (metabolic reaction network, peak-to-peak correlation network, MS/MS similarity network) around specific peaks/metabolites using the MetDNA2Vis R package, then merge them into a single resolved subnetwork with conflicting base peaks optimized away. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Extract and consolidate layer-specific subnetworks from the KGMN global networks (metabolic reaction network, peak-to-peak correlation network, MS/MS similarity network) around specific peaks/metabolites using the MetDNA2Vis R package, then merge them into a single resolved subnetwork with conflicting base peaks optimized away.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Global networks have not yet been reconstructed — reconstructNetwork1/2/3 (with reformatTable1 for the annotation table) must run first The analysis targets non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples where organism-specific reaction databases are not yet incorporated into KGMN The goal is to distinguish structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites — KGMN cannot effectively discriminate such isomers (e.g. isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers)

skills.description: Use when a set of natural extracts needs prioritization for spectral dissimilarity: a MEMO vectorized dissimilarity matrix (e.g. Celastraceae_memomatrix.csv) is available and the Similarity Component of Inventa's priority rank must be computed from MS2 spectral fingerprints.
skills.name: multimatrix-outlier-detection-machine-learning
skills.search_text: multimatrix-outlier-detection-machine-learning Use when a set of natural extracts needs prioritization for spectral dissimilarity: a MEMO vectorized dissimilarity matrix (e.g. Celastraceae_memomatrix.csv) is available and the Similarity Component of Inventa's priority rank must be computed from MS2 spectral fingerprints. When the goal is to score extract novelty from annotated features — that is the Feature Component (FC), which uses the MZmine quantification table and GNPS/ISDB/SIRIUS annotations, not the MEMO matrix When the goal is chemical-class novelty against literature reports — use the Class Component (CC, CANOPUS-based) or Literature Component (LC) instead When no MEMO vectorized dissimilarity matrix exists — MEMO is an optional input; without it Inventa will run only the Feature Component http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Computes Inventa's Similarity Component (SC) by mining a MEMO vectorized MS2 dissimilarity matrix with multiple unsupervised outlier-detection machine-learning algorithms (LOF, One-Class SVM, Isolation Forest) to flag spectrally dissimilar extracts as outliers (SC = 1). metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Computes Inventa's Similarity Component (SC) by mining a MEMO vectorized MS2 dissimilarity matrix with multiple unsupervised outlier-detection machine-learning algorithms (LOF, One-Class SVM, Isolation Forest) to flag spectrally dissimilar extracts as outliers (SC = 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to score extract novelty from annotated features — that is the Feature Component (FC), which uses the MZmine quantification table and GNPS/ISDB/SIRIUS annotations, not the MEMO matrix When the goal is chemical-class novelty against literature reports — use the Class Component (CC, CANOPUS-based) or Literature Component (LC) instead When no MEMO vectorized dissimilarity matrix exists — MEMO is an optional input; without it Inventa will run only the Feature Component

skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need pattern frequency/support across the whole spectral collection rather than component-specific explanation (rank by frequency instead) When no molecular network components exist (e.g. singletons or an unconnected set of spectra) — findPatternsExplainingComponents requires components to score against When a scoring system or prior annotation (e.g. MS2LDA motifs from MotifDB) is available, since mineMS2 itself currently lacks a pattern scoring system per the discussion

skills.description: Use when an MSI composite/cluster image must be upscaled to match the pixel dimensions of a co-registered H&E stain for side-by-side or overlay visualization, and an interpolation method must be chosen.
skills.name: multimodal-image-overlay-visualization
