skills.description: Use when you have a reconstructed multi-section 3D MSI dataset whose serial sections are misaligned and you need contrast-rich 'feature' images to register them to an MRI/atlas (e.g. rat brain coronal/sagittal sections).
skills.name: multimodal-registration-preprocessing-of-3d-msi
skills.search_text: multimodal-registration-preprocessing-of-3d-msi Use when you have a reconstructed multi-section 3D MSI dataset whose serial sections are misaligned and you need contrast-rich 'feature' images to register them to an MRI/atlas (e.g. rat brain coronal/sagittal sections). When the MSI sections are already registered or you only need ion-image visualization without multimodal co-registration — this skill exists to produce registration-ready feature images, not final ion maps. When only a single 2D section is available and there is no volumetric reconstruction or atlas/MRI target, since the embedding is trained on pixels pooled across all serial sections to form a single shared embedding space. When the input is raw low-resolution transient data (e.g. 64k-point FT-ICR transients) — reconstruction/processing (deep-learning decode, m/z binning, TIC normalization) must be completed first, since this skill expects processed peak data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 MEISTER preprocessing step that converts the reconstructed 3D MSI data cube (m/z-binned 3 ppm, TIC-normalized serial-section peak data, e.g. coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) into parametric-UMAP grayscale feature images with MRI-like anatomical contrast so the 2D serial sections can be registered to a rat brain MRI atlas. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: MEISTER preprocessing step that converts the reconstructed 3D MSI data cube (m/z-binned 3 ppm, TIC-normalized serial-section peak data, e.g. coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) into parametric-UMAP grayscale feature images with MRI-like anatomical contrast so the 2D serial sections can be registered to a rat brain MRI atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the MSI sections are already registered or you only need ion-image visualization without multimodal co-registration — this skill exists to produce registration-ready feature images, not final ion maps. When only a single 2D section is available and there is no volumetric reconstruction or atlas/MRI target, since the embedding is trained on pixels pooled across all serial sections to form a single shared embedding space. When the input is raw low-resolution transient data (e.g. 64k-point FT-ICR transients) — reconstruction/processing (deep-learning decode, m/z binning, TIC normalization) must be completed first, since this skill expects processed peak data.

skills.description: Use when an already-processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum needs interactive contour visualization, a pseudo-3D surface-mesh rendering, or exported publication-style images of both without any local software installation.
skills.name: multimodal-spectra-image-rendering
skills.search_text: multimodal-spectra-image-rendering Use when an already-processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum needs interactive contour visualization, a pseudo-3D surface-mesh rendering, or exported publication-style images of both without any local software installation. The spectrum is raw time-domain data (Bruker fid/ser) that still needs zero-filling, apodization, Fourier transformation, or phase correction — use the client-side WebAssembly processing workflow first. The target is quantitative peak deconvolution/line-shape fitting rather than visual inspection — use DEEP Picker / Voigt Fitter or Simple Picker instead. A non-browser, natively installed visualization program is required (e.g. in an environment without WebGL or a recent browser). http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Render processed 2D and pseudo-3D NMR spectra as WebGL contour plots and 3D surface meshes directly in a web browser using COLMARvista, whose JavaScript/WebGL graphics are architecture- and OS-independent, and export the resulting contour and mesh images. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s10858-025-00465-y
skills.summary: Render processed 2D and pseudo-3D NMR spectra as WebGL contour plots and 3D surface meshes directly in a web browser using COLMARvista, whose JavaScript/WebGL graphics are architecture- and OS-independent, and export the resulting contour and mesh images.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum is raw time-domain data (Bruker fid/ser) that still needs zero-filling, apodization, Fourier transformation, or phase correction — use the client-side WebAssembly processing workflow first. The target is quantitative peak deconvolution/line-shape fitting rather than visual inspection — use DEEP Picker / Voigt Fitter or Simple Picker instead. A non-browser, natively installed visualization program is required (e.g. in an environment without WebGL or a recent browser).

skills.description: Use when a pre-trained MMST model fails to correctly predict structures for a set of molecules (out-of-distribution chemical space, e.g. PubChem sets) and analogues plus simulated spectra can be generated to recover predictions.
skills.name: multimodal-transformer-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: multimodal-transformer-fine-tuning Use when a pre-trained MMST model fails to correctly predict structures for a set of molecules (out-of-distribution chemical space, e.g. PubChem sets) and analogues plus simulated spectra can be generated to recover predictions. The molecule set is already in-distribution and the pre-trained MMST achieves the expected 72% top-1 accuracy without fine-tuning No spectral simulation pipeline (SGNN / Chemprop-IR) or GPU resources are available to generate training data for analogues The task is training MMST from scratch on a new dataset (e.g. the Alberts benchmark) rather than fine-tuning a pre-trained checkpoint http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Fine-tune the MultiModalSpectralTransformer (MMST) on newly simulated multi-spectral data (NMR, HSQC, COSY, IR) generated for out-of-distribution molecules, as part of the active learning improvement cycle that adapts the model to new chemical spaces. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/ange.202517611

skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule set is already in-distribution and the pre-trained MMST achieves the expected 72% top-1 accuracy without fine-tuning No spectral simulation pipeline (SGNN / Chemprop-IR) or GPU resources are available to generate training data for analogues The task is training MMST from scratch on a new dataset (e.g. the Alberts benchmark) rather than fine-tuning a pre-trained checkpoint

skills.description: Use when processing a batch of GC×GC–MS samples in GcDUO where a feature's retention-2 elution profile shifts between samples and you need per-sample peak areas/intensities without forcing rigid tri-linearity.
skills.name: multimode-elution-profile-alignment
skills.search_text: multimode-elution-profile-alignment Use when processing a batch of GC×GC–MS samples in GcDUO where a feature's retention-2 elution profile shifts between samples and you need per-sample peak areas/intensities without forcing rigid tri-linearity. The feature is detected in only one sample — GcDUO skips Module V evaluation for such features and preserves their data from module III instead You need a rigid tri-linear decomposition where all modes must be identical across samples — plain PARAFAC, not PARAFAC2, is the appropriate model http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aligns GC×GC–MS features across a batch by refitting PARAFAC2 models per feature with the second-dimension elution-profile mode free to vary between samples, while imposing the annotated library mass spectrum as a constraint, yielding comparable peak areas and intensities per sample. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbaf080
skills.summary: Aligns GC×GC–MS features across a batch by refitting PARAFAC2 models per feature with the second-dimension elution-profile mode free to vary between samples, while imposing the annotated library mass spectrum as a constraint, yielding comparable peak areas and intensities per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature is detected in only one sample — GcDUO skips Module V evaluation for such features and preserves their data from module III instead You need a rigid tri-linear decomposition where all modes must be identical across samples — plain PARAFAC, not PARAFAC2, is the appropriate model

skills.description: Use when a user-defined chemical formula (e.g., glucose, penicillin) needs theoretical isotopic fine structures at a specified SIP atom% enrichment, especially where FFT-based envelope methods miss fine structure.
skills.name: multinomial-distribution-isotopologue-sampling
skills.search_text: multinomial-distribution-isotopologue-sampling Use when a user-defined chemical formula (e.g., glucose, penicillin) needs theoretical isotopic fine structures at a specified SIP atom% enrichment, especially where FFT-based envelope methods miss fine structure. The target output is a whole isotopic envelope rather than high-resolution fine structure — Aerith computes metabolite envelopes with an FFT-based algorithm, which is faster (though it does not account for fine structure) The compound is a peptide whose isotope distribution can be modeled by sequentially convoluting monomeric-unit isotopic envelopes instead of formula-level Monte Carlo sampling The analysis requires isotopic fine structures only under natural abundance with no SIP enrichment — IsoSpec2 already provides rapid natural-abundance fine-structure simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs Aerith's Monte Carlo fine-structure simulator, which draws isotopologue compositions from a multinomial distribution to capture low-abundance isotopic fine-structure variants of user-defined chemical formulas at any user-specified stable-isotope enrichment level (0–100%). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Reconstructs Aerith's Monte Carlo fine-structure simulator, which draws isotopologue compositions from a multinomial distribution to capture low-abundance isotopic fine-structure variants of user-defined chemical formulas at any user-specified stable-isotope enrichment level (0–100%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target output is a whole isotopic envelope rather than high-resolution fine structure — Aerith computes metabolite envelopes with an FFT-based algorithm, which is faster (though it does not account for fine structure) The compound is a peptide whose isotope distribution can be modeled by sequentially convoluting monomeric-unit isotopic envelopes instead of formula-level Monte Carlo sampling The analysis requires isotopic fine structures only under natural abundance with no SIP enrichment — IsoSpec2 already provides rapid natural-abundance fine-structure simulation

skills.description: Use when correcting measured fractional abundances of isotopologs (FAM) to mass distribution vectors (MDV) and you need the theoretical natural-abundance + isotopic-impurity correction matrix for a compound of known formula and a specified tracer (e.g., U-13C6 glucose).
skills.name: multinomial-isotopologue-distribution-computation
skills.search_text: multinomial-isotopologue-distribution-computation Use when correcting measured fractional abundances of isotopologs (FAM) to mass distribution vectors (MDV) and you need the theoretical natural-abundance + isotopic-impurity correction matrix for a compound of known formula and a specified tracer (e.g., U-13C6 glucose). On high-resolving-power mass spectrometers (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000–280,000 nominal resolution) that can resolve isotopologs of the same nominal mass — the NRE matrix is significantly less accurate than resolution-dependent corrections (MDT/ULS). When the selected tracer element is not present in the compound's formula — ElemCor's algorithm reports an error (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N data). When the goal is tracer-analysis correction on unlabeled samples for resolution-effect estimation rather than theoretical matrix construction (use ULS deconvolution instead). Constructs the theoretical (non-resolution-effect, NRE) isotope correction matrix C1·C2·C3 for stable-isotope labeling LC-MS data by multinomial convolution of natural-abundance isotope distributions over non-tracer atoms, combinatorics over the Nt tracer positions, and the tracer's nutrient isotopic purity — the combinatorial baseline used by IsoCor and as the NRE comparator in ElemCor. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Constructs the theoretical (non-resolution-effect, NRE) isotope correction matrix C1·C2·C3 for stable-isotope labeling LC-MS data by multinomial convolution of natural-abundance isotope distributions over non-tracer atoms, combinatorics over the Nt tracer positions, and the tracer's nutrient isotopic purity — the combinatorial baseline used by IsoCor and as the NRE comparator in ElemCor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: On high-resolving-power mass spectrometers (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000–280,000 nominal resolution) that can resolve isotopologs of the same nominal mass — the NRE matrix is significantly less accurate than resolution-dependent corrections (MDT/ULS). When the selected tracer element is not present in the compound's formula — ElemCor's algorithm reports an error (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N data). When the goal is tracer-analysis correction on unlabeled samples for resolution-effect estimation rather than theoretical matrix construction (use ULS deconvolution instead).

skills.summary: Evaluates how well MOCCal assigns unknown TWIM-MS features to their correct biomolecular class (small molecules, lipids, peptides) by benchmarking class-assignment accuracy under simulated calibration errors and against IMSCal and single power law baselines.

skills.description: Use when a traveling-wave IM-MS feature table (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) contains unidentified small-molecule, lipid, and peptide features from a mixed multiomic mixture and class-specific TWCCSN2 values are needed without prior identification.
skills.name: multiomic-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: multiomic-feature-annotation Use when a traveling-wave IM-MS feature table (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) contains unidentified small-molecule, lipid, and peptide features from a mixed multiomic mixture and class-specific TWCCSN2 values are needed without prior identification. The data are already identified feature annotations (e.g. named lipids/peptides) — use direct CCS comparison rather than class-assignment-by-ΔCCS Only one biomolecular class is present and a single power law calibration suffices; MOCCal's multi-class machinery adds no value Negative ionization mode data or chemical classes outside small molecules, lipids, and peptides — the article notes MOCCal is currently limited to these classes and positive-mode datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Biomolecular-class annotation of unknown TWIM-MS features by calibrating each arrival time with up to three class-specific power law equations (small molecule, lipid, peptide) and selecting the class whose calibrated TWCCSN2 value sits closest to its DTCCSN2-vs-m/z regression trendline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04290
skills.summary: Biomolecular-class annotation of unknown TWIM-MS features by calibrating each arrival time with up to three class-specific power law equations (small molecule, lipid, peptide) and selecting the class whose calibrated TWCCSN2 value sits closest to its DTCCSN2-vs-m/z regression trendline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already identified feature annotations (e.g. named lipids/peptides) — use direct CCS comparison rather than class-assignment-by-ΔCCS Only one biomolecular class is present and a single power law calibration suffices; MOCCal's multi-class machinery adds no value Negative ionization mode data or chemical classes outside small molecules, lipids, and peptides — the article notes MOCCal is currently limited to these classes and positive-mode datasets

skills.search_text: multiomic-feature-classification Use when you have singly charged feature arrival times from TWIM-MS (e.g., Waters SYNAPT XS) with computed class-specific TWCCSN2 calibration parameters, and you must assign each unknown feature to a biomolecular class without prior identification. skills.summary: MOCCal's biomolecular class assignment step assigns unidentifiable TWIM-MS features to small molecule, lipid, or peptide classes by calibrating each arrival time with up to three class-specific power law curves and selecting the class whose ΔCCS to the DTCCSN2 vs m/z trendline is smallest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are multiply charged — these receive a default score of 0 and are outside the core ΔCCS assignment logic calibrated for singly charged species Data were acquired in negative ionization mode — MOCCal is not yet extended to negative ionization mode data sets Features belong to chemical classes outside small molecules, lipids, and peptides (e.g., other endogenous or xenobiotic classes) — MOCCal is currently scoped to these three calibrations

skills.search_text: multiomic-feature-table-processing Use when you have singly charged features from Waters SYNAPT XS traveling-wave IM-MS data spanning small molecules, lipids, and peptides, and need class-assigned calibrated CCS values without prior identification. skills.summary: Prepare a multiomic TWIM-MS feature table (feature IDs, m/z, charge state, retention time, arrival time) and run it through MOCCal's class-specific power law CCS calibrations to assign biomolecular class and calibrated TWCCSN2 values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from drift-tube IM-MS or non-traveling-wave IM platforms — MOCCal's power law calibrations are TWIM-specific. Features are multiply charged (charge > 1) — class assignment and ΔCCS-based selection operate on singly charged features; multiply charged assignments default to score 0. skills.description: Use when processing multiomic TWIM-MS data on Waters instruments where unknown features must be assigned to small molecule, lipid, or peptide calibrations and calibrated CCS values computed without prior identification.
skills.name: multiomic-power-law-curve-selection
skills.search_text: multiomic-power-law-curve-selection Use when processing multiomic TWIM-MS data on Waters instruments where unknown features must be assigned to small molecule, lipid, or peptide calibrations and calibrated CCS values computed without prior identification. The data set is already a fully annotated feature table where features are identified and class assignment by ΔCCS is unnecessary Data were acquired in negative ionization mode or from chemical classes outside small molecule, lipid, and peptide scope (MOCCal does not yet calibrate these) The instrument is not a traveling wave ion mobility platform (e.g. drift tube IM-MS where DTCCSN2 is measured directly rather than calibrated) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Automates selecting the class-specific power law calibration (small molecule, lipid, or peptide) that yields the most accurate TWCCSN2 value for each unknown feature in traveling wave ion mobility MS data. Uses ΔCCS-to-trendline selection without prior feature identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04290
skills.summary: Automates selecting the class-specific power law calibration (small molecule, lipid, or peptide) that yields the most accurate TWCCSN2 value for each unknown feature in traveling wave ion mobility MS data. Uses ΔCCS-to-trendline selection without prior feature identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data set is already a fully annotated feature table where features are identified and class assignment by ΔCCS is unnecessary Data were acquired in negative ionization mode or from chemical classes outside small molecule, lipid, and peptide scope (MOCCal does not yet calibrate these) The instrument is not a traveling wave ion mobility platform (e.g. drift tube IM-MS where DTCCSN2 is measured directly rather than calibrated)

skills.description: Use when a study has matched multiomic feature tables and a metabolite abundance matrix for the same samples (e.g. CCLE cell lines), and the goal is to determine which omics class most accurately predicts metabolomic variation.
skills.name: multiomics-feature-set-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multiomics-feature-set-benchmarking Use when a study has matched multiomic feature tables and a metabolite abundance matrix for the same samples (e.g. CCLE cell lines), and the goal is to determine which omics class most accurately predicts metabolomic variation. When the omics input has no matched metabolite abundance measurements for the same samples (models are not directly transferrable to other sources due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions, cell line panels, and limited feature overlap). When the objective is causal mechanism discovery rather than predictive feature benchmarking: the 'guilt by association' strategy may not identify causative mechanisms and network associations from systems-level data are descriptive. When only a small set of omics classes is available and the comparison across classes is not the goal — the benchmarking loses its discriminating purpose. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_3337 Benchmark omics feature sets from eight biomolecular classes (CNV, methylation, histone PTMs, coding/non-coding transcriptomics, miRNA/lncRNA, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) for their ability to predict metabolite abundance across matched cancer cell lines using per-metabolite random forest regression with 5-fold cross-validation and Pearson's correlation as the accuracy metric. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.17.608400
skills.summary: Benchmark omics feature sets from eight biomolecular classes (CNV, methylation, histone PTMs, coding/non-coding transcriptomics, miRNA/lncRNA, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) for their ability to predict metabolite abundance across matched cancer cell lines using per-metabolite random forest regression with 5-fold cross-validation and Pearson's correlation as the accuracy metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the omics input has no matched metabolite abundance measurements for the same samples (models are not directly transferrable to other sources due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions, cell line panels, and limited feature overlap). When the objective is causal mechanism discovery rather than predictive feature benchmarking: the 'guilt by association' strategy may not identify causative mechanisms and network associations from systems-level data are descriptive. When only a small set of omics classes is available and the comparison across classes is not the goal — the benchmarking loses its discriminating purpose.

skills.description: Use when aligning features across multiple LC-MS runs from CSV feature tables (m/z, RT, area columns) where nearest-neighbor matching is insufficient and all potential inter-run correspondences must be jointly considered in a graph structure.
skills.name: multipartite-graph-construction-from-feature-lists
skills.search_text: multipartite-graph-construction-from-feature-lists Use when aligning features across multiple LC-MS runs from CSV feature tables (m/z, RT, area columns) where nearest-neighbor matching is insufficient and all potential inter-run correspondences must be jointly considered in a graph structure. The input is raw LC-MS data (mzML) rather than already-extracted feature lists — feature detection/quantification must be done first by tools like MZmine2, OpenMS or XCMS A simple reference-run pairwise nearest matching suffices and computational speed matters more than accuracy — G-Aligner's main limitation is lack of computing speed since the assignment problem is NP-Hard Only two runs need pairwise alignment via bipartite matching (e.g. LWBmatch-style); the multipartite graph targets non-centric matching across all runs http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds an undirected multipartite relation graph in which features from all LC-MS runs are nodes and potential feature correspondences (within user-specified m/z and RT tolerances after coarse RT registration) are edges, enabling non-centric multi-run feature matching. This graph representation is the core data structure G-Aligner uses before solving alignment as an unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Builds an undirected multipartite relation graph in which features from all LC-MS runs are nodes and potential feature correspondences (within user-specified m/z and RT tolerances after coarse RT registration) are edges, enabling non-centric multi-run feature matching. This graph representation is the core data structure G-Aligner uses before solving alignment as an unbalanced multidimensional assignment problem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-MS data (mzML) rather than already-extracted feature lists — feature detection/quantification must be done first by tools like MZmine2, OpenMS or XCMS A simple reference-run pairwise nearest matching suffices and computational speed matters more than accuracy — G-Aligner's main limitation is lack of computing speed since the assignment problem is NP-Hard Only two runs need pairwise alignment via bipartite matching (e.g. LWBmatch-style); the multipartite graph targets non-centric matching across all runs

skills.description: Use when you have a binary presence/absence detection matrix across cohort samples and need to identify statistically significant co-detection pairs (e.g., parent compounds vs. their CMDN-annotated metabolites) among many tested pairs.
skills.name: multiple-comparison-significance-filtering
skills.search_text: multiple-comparison-significance-filtering Use when you have a binary presence/absence detection matrix across cohort samples and need to identify statistically significant co-detection pairs (e.g., parent compounds vs. their CMDN-annotated metabolites) among many tested pairs. Input data are continuous abundance/intensity values rather than binary detection calls — the 2x2 contingency-table construction requires qualitative presence/absence coding The goal is quantitative correlation of exposure levels rather than qualitative co-occurrence of detection events Testing a single pre-specified pair only, where multiple-comparison filtering across a large pair space is not the concern http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies Chi-squared tests of independence to 2x2 contingency tables built from binary detection/non-detection data, flagging parent pesticide–metabolite co-occurrence pairs at p < 0.05 to control which exposure linkages are reported from a large pairwise testing space. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: Applies Chi-squared tests of independence to 2x2 contingency tables built from binary detection/non-detection data, flagging parent pesticide–metabolite co-occurrence pairs at p < 0.05 to control which exposure linkages are reported from a large pairwise testing space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are continuous abundance/intensity values rather than binary detection calls — the 2x2 contingency-table construction requires qualitative presence/absence coding The goal is quantitative correlation of exposure levels rather than qualitative co-occurrence of detection events Testing a single pre-specified pair only, where multiple-comparison filtering across a large pair space is not the concern

skills.description: Use when behavioral questionnaire items are categorical (e.g., CBCL item scores) and you need to reduce them to a few underlying dimensions and quantify per-dimension explained variance.
skills.name: multiple-correspondence-analysis
skills.search_text: multiple-correspondence-analysis Use when behavioral questionnaire items are categorical (e.g., CBCL item scores) and you need to reduce them to a few underlying dimensions and quantify per-dimension explained variance. The behavioral data are continuous rather than categorical item scores — MCA is designed for categorical variables; use a method suited to continuous data (e.g., PCA/MOFA as used for the omics blocks) The goal is integrating multi-omics (methylation/metabolomics) data blocks — the workflow used MOFA2 for those, MCA only for the behavioral CBCL items You need significance testing between groups — the workflow ran downstream Mann–Whitney U / Kruskal–Wallis / GEE tests on the MCA dimension scores as a separate step http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Apply multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) with the R library FactoMineR (v2.4) to categorical parent-rated ASEBA CBCL externalizing behavior items to obtain behavioral dimensions and their explained variance fractions in the ACTION cohorts (NTR and LUMC-Curium). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad115
skills.summary: Apply multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) with the R library FactoMineR (v2.4) to categorical parent-rated ASEBA CBCL externalizing behavior items to obtain behavioral dimensions and their explained variance fractions in the ACTION cohorts (NTR and LUMC-Curium).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The behavioral data are continuous rather than categorical item scores — MCA is designed for categorical variables; use a method suited to continuous data (e.g., PCA/MOFA as used for the omics blocks) The goal is integrating multi-omics (methylation/metabolomics) data blocks — the workflow used MOFA2 for those, MCA only for the behavioral CBCL items You need significance testing between groups — the workflow ran downstream Mann–Whitney U / Kruskal–Wallis / GEE tests on the MCA dimension scores as a separate step

skills.description: Use when several omic data layers over the same N samples have been converted to per-layer N x N kernel/consensus matrices and you need an integrative clustering whose per-dataset weights reveal which layers carry the cluster structure.
skills.name: multiple-kernel-learning-clustering
skills.search_text: multiple-kernel-learning-clustering Use when several omic data layers over the same N samples have been converted to per-layer N x N kernel/consensus matrices and you need an integrative clustering whose per-dataset weights reveal which layers carry the cluster structure. Input is a raw feature/data matrix rather than per-layer kernel or consensus matrices — first run the Kernel step (Consensus Clustering per layer) before applying KLIC. Only one dataset/layer is available — combining kernels is unnecessary; run plain kernel k-means on the single consensus matrix instead. Samples are not matched across the layers (each layer must be an N x N kernel over the same N samples) or the layers do not share a common clustering structure. Integrative clustering via Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering (KLIC): combine per-dataset kernel (consensus) matrices by learning sample-specific convex kernel weights with localized multiple kernel k-means, so that noisy datasets are down-weighted relative to more informative ones. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Integrative clustering via Kernel Learning Integrative Clustering (KLIC): combine per-dataset kernel (consensus) matrices by learning sample-specific convex kernel weights with localized multiple kernel k-means, so that noisy datasets are down-weighted relative to more informative ones.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw feature/data matrix rather than per-layer kernel or consensus matrices — first run the Kernel step (Consensus Clustering per layer) before applying KLIC. Only one dataset/layer is available — combining kernels is unnecessary; run plain kernel k-means on the single consensus matrix instead. Samples are not matched across the layers (each layer must be an N x N kernel over the same N samples) or the layers do not share a common clustering structure.

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics feature (e.g. creatinine) must be validated against an external clinical trait (CKD-EPI/eGFR, clinical routine creatinine) to check whether batch correction improves the biological signal.
skills.name: multiple-regression-egfr-creatinine-association
skills.search_text: multiple-regression-egfr-creatinine-association Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics feature (e.g. creatinine) must be validated against an external clinical trait (CKD-EPI/eGFR, clinical routine creatinine) to check whether batch correction improves the biological signal. No paired clinical outcome (CKD-EPI or clinical creatinine) is available for the metabolomics participants, so the association model cannot be fit The goal is batch correction/model selection itself rather than post-correction validation — use Visodbnorm or dbnormSCORE instead Dataset has more than 2000 features, where dbnorm's Visodbnorm/dbnormSCORE functions are not recommended for computational speed http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Validate batch-effect correction in LC-MS metabolomics by regressing a clinical renal outcome (CKD-EPI) on the LC-MS creatinine feature adjusted for age and sex, comparing raw vs. dbnorm-corrected SKIPOGH datasets. It tests whether statistical batch correction restores a biologically expected metabolite–clinical association that is masked in raw data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Validate batch-effect correction in LC-MS metabolomics by regressing a clinical renal outcome (CKD-EPI) on the LC-MS creatinine feature adjusted for age and sex, comparing raw vs. dbnorm-corrected SKIPOGH datasets. It tests whether statistical batch correction restores a biologically expected metabolite–clinical association that is masked in raw data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No paired clinical outcome (CKD-EPI or clinical creatinine) is available for the metabolomics participants, so the association model cannot be fit The goal is batch correction/model selection itself rather than post-correction validation — use Visodbnorm or dbnormSCORE instead Dataset has more than 2000 features, where dbnorm's Visodbnorm/dbnormSCORE functions are not recommended for computational speed

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites x samples, control vs mutant groups) yields per-metabolite p-values, or when Fisher's Exact Test pathway hits must be judged against an adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05.
skills.name: multiple-testing-adjustment-metabolomics
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-adjustment-metabolomics Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites x samples, control vs mutant groups) yields per-metabolite p-values, or when Fisher's Exact Test pathway hits must be judged against an adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05. Input is already a pre-filtered list of significant metabolites with no raw per-metabolite p-values to adjust The analysis performs a single pre-registered hypothesis test rather than many simultaneous metabolite/pathway tests, so multiplicity correction is unwarranted The goal is a ranked-list GSEA-style scan where no fold-change/p-value cutoff filtering is desired before enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction to metabolomics group-comparison p-values and to Fisher's Exact Test pathway p-values, defining significance via adjusted p-value < 0.05. This controls false positives before selecting the significant-metabolite query set and before declaring enriched pathways. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction to metabolomics group-comparison p-values and to Fisher's Exact Test pathway p-values, defining significance via adjusted p-value < 0.05. This controls false positives before selecting the significant-metabolite query set and before declaring enriched pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pre-filtered list of significant metabolites with no raw per-metabolite p-values to adjust The analysis performs a single pre-registered hypothesis test rather than many simultaneous metabolite/pathway tests, so multiplicity correction is unwarranted The goal is a ranked-list GSEA-style scan where no fold-change/p-value cutoff filtering is desired before enrichment

skills.description: Use when thousands of genes are tested simultaneously for differential expression between sample groups (e.g. tumor vs non-tumor) and raw Mann–Whitney U or other per-gene P-values must be corrected for multiple testing before filtering.
skills.name: multiple-testing-bh-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-bh-correction Use when thousands of genes are tested simultaneously for differential expression between sample groups (e.g. tumor vs non-tumor) and raw Mann–Whitney U or other per-gene P-values must be corrected for multiple testing before filtering. Only a handful of pre-defined genes are tested with no simultaneous-testing inflation — a raw P-value suffices and BH correction would over-penalize The comparison is not gene-wise hypothesis testing (e.g. sample-level batch-effect checks by pairwise Pearson correlation), which MOG performs without a correction step Expression values are not comparable across groups (no log2 transform applied), since the paper's test and correction are defined on log2-transformed data http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to per-gene P-values from differential expression tests (e.g. Mann–Whitney U tests on log2-transformed RNA-Seq data), so that gene-level calls are evaluated against a strict BH-corrected P-value threshold (<10^-3) rather than raw P-values. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to per-gene P-values from differential expression tests (e.g. Mann–Whitney U tests on log2-transformed RNA-Seq data), so that gene-level calls are evaluated against a strict BH-corrected P-value threshold (<10^-3) rather than raw P-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a handful of pre-defined genes are tested with no simultaneous-testing inflation — a raw P-value suffices and BH correction would over-penalize The comparison is not gene-wise hypothesis testing (e.g. sample-level batch-effect checks by pairwise Pearson correlation), which MOG performs without a correction step Expression values are not comparable across groups (no log2 transform applied), since the paper's test and correction are defined on log2-transformed data

skills.description: Use when calling significant parent–adduct ion pairs from massdiff/corrPairsMSI output — i.e. when each candidate pair's Pearson p-value must be judged against a family-wise threshold to avoid false adduct calls.
skills.name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction Use when calling significant parent–adduct ion pairs from massdiff/corrPairsMSI output — i.e. when each candidate pair's Pearson p-value must be judged against a family-wise threshold to avoid false adduct calls. Input is already a filtered list of few ion pairs where the multiplicity correction would be overly conservative (Bonferroni's family-wise threshold assumes many simultaneous tests). The analysis goal is adduct discovery by mass-difference histogram matching (adductMatch/topAdducts), not statistical validation of spatial co-localization. Testing non-pairwise metabolite correlations where a less conservative FDR-based approach is expected rather than family-wise error control. http://edamontology.org/topic_3179 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Bonferroni correction applied within mass2adduct to control false positives when testing spatial correlations of putative parent–adduct ion pairs in MALDI-MSI peak-intensity data. It sets a family-wise significance threshold over the many ion pairs tested, so only confidently co-localized adduct pairs are retained. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c04720
skills.summary: Bonferroni correction applied within mass2adduct to control false positives when testing spatial correlations of putative parent–adduct ion pairs in MALDI-MSI peak-intensity data. It sets a family-wise significance threshold over the many ion pairs tested, so only confidently co-localized adduct pairs are retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered list of few ion pairs where the multiplicity correction would be overly conservative (Bonferroni's family-wise threshold assumes many simultaneous tests). The analysis goal is adduct discovery by mass-difference histogram matching (adductMatch/topAdducts), not statistical validation of spatial co-localization. Testing non-pairwise metabolite correlations where a less conservative FDR-based approach is expected rather than family-wise error control.

skills.description: Use when a feature-by-feature univariate test (e.g. t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum between tumor and normal groups) has been run on many metabolomics features and p-values must be adjusted before reporting differential metabolites or rendering volcano plots.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction Use when a feature-by-feature univariate test (e.g. t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum between tumor and normal groups) has been run on many metabolomics features and p-values must be adjusted before reporting differential metabolites or rendering volcano plots. Input is raw LC-MS data rather than a processed feature table — peak picking and data cleaning (e.g. via xcms or tidyMass processing) must happen first Features have not been filtered for missing values (noisy features with >20% MV in QC or >50% MV in study groups should be removed before testing) Only a single pre-specified hypothesis is being tested, so multiplicity correction is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Adjust per-feature p-values from univariate metabolomics comparisons for the multiplicity incurred when testing thousands of LC-MS features, as done in the tidyMass/massStat CRC case study to generate volcano-plot statistics for sex-stratified tumor-vs-normal differential metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: Adjust per-feature p-values from univariate metabolomics comparisons for the multiplicity incurred when testing thousands of LC-MS features, as done in the tidyMass/massStat CRC case study to generate volcano-plot statistics for sex-stratified tumor-vs-normal differential metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data rather than a processed feature table — peak picking and data cleaning (e.g. via xcms or tidyMass processing) must happen first Features have not been filtered for missing values (noisy features with >20% MV in QC or >50% MV in study groups should be removed before testing) Only a single pre-specified hypothesis is being tested, so multiplicity correction is not applicable

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics feature table (CSV) has been tested feature-by-feature (t-test/ANOVA, or covariate-adjusted limma/ANCOVA models) and the resulting raw p-values must be FDR-corrected to define significant feature sets.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction-fdr
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction-fdr Use when a metabolomics or proteomics feature table (CSV) has been tested feature-by-feature (t-test/ANOVA, or covariate-adjusted limma/ANCOVA models) and the resulting raw p-values must be FDR-corrected to define significant feature sets. The feature table has not yet passed POMAShiny preprocessing — features with more than 20% missing values per study group should be removed and missing values imputed before testing, not after correction The goal is exploratory data analysis (EDA) rather than hypothesis testing — the workflow recommends EDA first, and FDR correction is not part of the EDA panel Only a single pre-specified comparison is tested, so no multiplicity correction across features is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies multiple-testing (FDR) correction to per-feature univariate p-values from metabolomics/proteomics data analyzed with POMA/POMAShiny, defining significant feature sets at a chosen FDR threshold and enabling comparison of unadjusted versus covariate-adjusted (ANCOVA/limma) significance results. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009148
skills.summary: Applies multiple-testing (FDR) correction to per-feature univariate p-values from metabolomics/proteomics data analyzed with POMA/POMAShiny, defining significant feature sets at a chosen FDR threshold and enabling comparison of unadjusted versus covariate-adjusted (ANCOVA/limma) significance results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has not yet passed POMAShiny preprocessing — features with more than 20% missing values per study group should be removed and missing values imputed before testing, not after correction The goal is exploratory data analysis (EDA) rather than hypothesis testing — the workflow recommends EDA first, and FDR correction is not part of the EDA panel Only a single pre-specified comparison is tested, so no multiplicity correction across features is required

skills.description: Use when you need Meff estimates for eigen-analysis-based multiple testing correction: you have M correlated tests (e.g., metabolites) and a Pearson correlation matrix, and must compute effective numbers of tests for p-value adjustment as in DisCo P-ad.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction-function-implementation
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction-function-implementation Use when you need Meff estimates for eigen-analysis-based multiple testing correction: you have M correlated tests (e.g., metabolites) and a Pearson correlation matrix, and must compute effective numbers of tests for p-value adjustment as in DisCo P-ad. You only need the Meff value itself and no implementation — use the paper's reported results or the DisCoPad repository scripts instead of re-coding. Your multiple testing correction does not rely on eigen-analysis of a correlation matrix (e.g., simple FDR without Meff) — the seven estimators are specific to this family of procedures. The number of tests M is trivially small or features are uncorrelated — setting Meff = M (Bonferroni/Šidák) suffices and eigen-analysis adds no value. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implement the seven effective-number-of-tests (Meff) estimators used for multiple testing correction in metabolomics/GWAS contexts — Bonferroni, Šidák, Nyholt, Li and Ji, Gao, Galwey, and Peluso — as callable R or MATLAB functions built on eigen-analysis of the features' M-by-M Pearson correlation matrix (Equations 1–4e of the DisCo P-ad paper). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Implement the seven effective-number-of-tests (Meff) estimators used for multiple testing correction in metabolomics/GWAS contexts — Bonferroni, Šidák, Nyholt, Li and Ji, Gao, Galwey, and Peluso — as callable R or MATLAB functions built on eigen-analysis of the features' M-by-M Pearson correlation matrix (Equations 1–4e of the DisCo P-ad paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the Meff value itself and no implementation — use the paper's reported results or the DisCoPad repository scripts instead of re-coding. Your multiple testing correction does not rely on eigen-analysis of a correlation matrix (e.g., simple FDR without Meff) — the seven estimators are specific to this family of procedures. The number of tests M is trivially small or features are uncorrelated — setting Meff = M (Bonferroni/Šidák) suffices and eigen-analysis adds no value.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an alternative correlation matrix (e.g., Spearman's rank correlation) improves or matches eigen-analysis-based Meff estimates in a simulation scenario such as a small sample size (n=100).
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction-simulation
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction-simulation Use when evaluating whether an alternative correlation matrix (e.g., Spearman's rank correlation) improves or matches eigen-analysis-based Meff estimates in a simulation scenario such as a small sample size (n=100). The goal is a single real metabolomics dataset analysis rather than a simulation benchmark across replicates with a known true Meff The multiple testing correction procedure in use does not rely on eigen-analysis of a correlation matrix (e.g., Bonferroni-type corrections independent of correlation structure) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A simulation-based skill for benchmarking effective-number-of-tests (Meff) estimators: substitute alternative correlation matrices (Spearman, DisCo, PrsCo) into eigen-analysis-based multiple testing correction procedures and compare RMSE against the true effective number of tests, as done in the DisCo P-ad metabolomics study. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: A simulation-based skill for benchmarking effective-number-of-tests (Meff) estimators: substitute alternative correlation matrices (Spearman, DisCo, PrsCo) into eigen-analysis-based multiple testing correction procedures and compare RMSE against the true effective number of tests, as done in the DisCo P-ad metabolomics study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single real metabolomics dataset analysis rather than a simulation benchmark across replicates with a known true Meff The multiple testing correction procedure in use does not rely on eigen-analysis of a correlation matrix (e.g., Bonferroni-type corrections independent of correlation structure)

skills.description: Use when comparing two cell groups (e.g. +FA benign vs +FA+IL17A inflammatory steatotic hepatocytes) across hundreds of metabolites in a per-cell matrix and uncorrected p-values would inflate false positives.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction-statistics
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction-statistics Use when comparing two cell groups (e.g. +FA benign vs +FA+IL17A inflammatory steatotic hepatocytes) across hundreds of metabolites in a per-cell matrix and uncorrected p-values would inflate false positives. Input is already a differential table with adjusted p-values (correction already applied) The comparison is a single hypothesis with one p-value, where no family-wise correction across features is needed Cells have not been assigned to the states/conditions being compared (grouping must precede the per-feature tests) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Statistical skill for applying multiple-testing correction to per-feature p-values from non-parametric group comparisons — here, Wilcoxon rank-sum differential abundance of metabolites between single-cell metabolic states in SpaceM spatio-molecular data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Statistical skill for applying multiple-testing correction to per-feature p-values from non-parametric group comparisons — here, Wilcoxon rank-sum differential abundance of metabolites between single-cell metabolic states in SpaceM spatio-molecular data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a differential table with adjusted p-values (correction already applied) The comparison is a single hypothesis with one p-value, where no family-wise correction across features is needed Cells have not been assigned to the states/conditions being compared (grouping must precede the per-feature tests)

skills.description: Use when a pathway-level test yields one p-value per pathway across many tested pathways (e.g., NetGSA, DEGraph, CAMERA, Pathway-Express) and you must adjust for multiplicity with FDR q-values before calling pathways dysregulated.
skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-control
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-control Use when a pathway-level test yields one p-value per pathway across many tested pathways (e.g., NetGSA, DEGraph, CAMERA, Pathway-Express) and you must adjust for multiplicity with FDR q-values before calling pathways dysregulated.
