skills.search_text: multivariate-anova-across-metabolite-columns Use when the input is a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (samples as rows, metabolite columns, a group/factor column) and per-metabolite significance testing across two or more sample groups is the goal. The data have only two groups and a univariate non-parametric comparison is wanted — Viime pairs the Wilcoxon rank sum test with two-group univariate analysis, and ANOVA is designated for two or more groups The table is raw instrument output (e.g. unnormalized NMR/MS intensities) that has not passed Viime's normalization, transformation, and scaling steps The concentration columns contain non-numeric data or missing values exceeding the default threshold, which Viime flags as errors that must be corrected (or imputed via its MCAR/MNAR strategy) before analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs a multivariate ANOVA over metabolite concentration columns in a group-factored dataset and, when two or more groups are present, automatically applies a post-hoc Tukey HSD test yielding per-metabolite p-values for every inter-group comparison, as implemented in Viime via its R/OpenCPU processing backend. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Runs a multivariate ANOVA over metabolite concentration columns in a group-factored dataset and, when two or more groups are present, automatically applies a post-hoc Tukey HSD test yielding per-metabolite p-values for every inter-group comparison, as implemented in Viime via its R/OpenCPU processing backend.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have only two groups and a univariate non-parametric comparison is wanted — Viime pairs the Wilcoxon rank sum test with two-group univariate analysis, and ANOVA is designated for two or more groups The table is raw instrument output (e.g. unnormalized NMR/MS intensities) that has not passed Viime's normalization, transformation, and scaling steps The concentration columns contain non-numeric data or missing values exceeding the default threshold, which Viime flags as errors that must be corrected (or imputed via its MCAR/MNAR strategy) before analysis

skills.description: Use when input is two-dimensional MS map data (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS and the goal is to identify and visualize multivariate marker features without conventional peak picking, e.g. untargeted metabolomics of aroma odor or human breath.
skills.name: multivariate-biomarker-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: multivariate-biomarker-feature-extraction Use when input is two-dimensional MS map data (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS and the goal is to identify and visualize multivariate marker features without conventional peak picking, e.g. untargeted metabolomics of aroma odor or human breath. Input is already a peak-picked feature table — NPFimg's value is working directly on the 2D MS map image, bypassing peak picking. The task requires a long-established, widely supported peak picking workflow — the article itself benchmarks against 'the widely used XCMS', implying XCMS is the conventional alternative. The data is not a two-dimensional m/z vs retention-time MS map (e.g. no chromatographic dimension or non-MS modality) — NPFimg is defined for chromatography–MS data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 NPFimg automatically identifies multivariate chemo-/biomarker features of analytes in chromatography–mass spectrometry data by combining image processing and machine learning on two-dimensional MS maps (m/z vs retention time), bypassing the conventional peak picking process that suffers from false peak detections. Validated on GC–MS aroma odor and human breath data (down to the parts per billion level) and shown to have lower signal-acquisition and marker-identification error rates than XCMS. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03163
skills.summary: NPFimg automatically identifies multivariate chemo-/biomarker features of analytes in chromatography–mass spectrometry data by combining image processing and machine learning on two-dimensional MS maps (m/z vs retention time), bypassing the conventional peak picking process that suffers from false peak detections. Validated on GC–MS aroma odor and human breath data (down to the parts per billion level) and shown to have lower signal-acquisition and marker-identification error rates than XCMS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-picked feature table — NPFimg's value is working directly on the 2D MS map image, bypassing peak picking. The task requires a long-established, widely supported peak picking workflow — the article itself benchmarks against 'the widely used XCMS', implying XCMS is the conventional alternative. The data is not a two-dimensional m/z vs retention-time MS map (e.g. no chromatographic dimension or non-MS modality) — NPFimg is defined for chromatography–MS data.

skills.description: Use when raw two-dimensional MS maps (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS must be characterized, analytes discriminated, and multivariate chemo-/biomarker features identified and visualized without a peak picking stage.
skills.name: multivariate-chemomarker-feature-identification
skills.search_text: multivariate-chemomarker-feature-identification Use when raw two-dimensional MS maps (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS must be characterized, analytes discriminated, and multivariate chemo-/biomarker features identified and visualized without a peak picking stage. The pipeline output is already a peak-picked feature table (e.g. XCMS output) — NPFimg's design deliberately replaces the conventional peak picking process, so feeding it pre-picked features defeats its purpose. The data are not a two-dimensional chromatography–MS map arranged as m/z versus retention time (e.g. standalone direct-injection MS or non-chromatographic spectra), which the article does not claim NPFimg handles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Identifies and visualizes multivariate chemo-/biomarker features of analytes in chromatography–MS data (e.g. GC–MS m/z vs retention time maps) using the NPFimg combination of image processing and machine learning, avoiding the false peak detections of conventional peak picking. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03163
skills.summary: Identifies and visualizes multivariate chemo-/biomarker features of analytes in chromatography–MS data (e.g. GC–MS m/z vs retention time maps) using the NPFimg combination of image processing and machine learning, avoiding the false peak detections of conventional peak picking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline output is already a peak-picked feature table (e.g. XCMS output) — NPFimg's design deliberately replaces the conventional peak picking process, so feeding it pre-picked features defeats its purpose. The data are not a two-dimensional chromatography–MS map arranged as m/z versus retention time (e.g. standalone direct-injection MS or non-chromatographic spectra), which the article does not claim NPFimg handles.

skills.description: Use when a numerical feature matrix has columns on heterogeneous scales (e.g. iris-like morphological measurements) and PCA, clustering or another scikit-learn-based activity is about to be run on the raw columns.
skills.name: multivariate-feature-standardization
skills.search_text: multivariate-feature-standardization Use when a numerical feature matrix has columns on heterogeneous scales (e.g. iris-like morphological measurements) and PCA, clustering or another scikit-learn-based activity is about to be run on the raw columns. Columns are already on a common scale or the analysis is scale-invariant (e.g. rank-based or correlation-based methods), so z-scoring would add no benefit The table still contains missing values that you intend to impute first — the automatic pre-filter would silently drop rows before standardization The goal is batch-effect correction of expression data rather than plain per-feature scaling — use ComBat/pyComBat (bundled via the combat package) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Standardizes each numerical feature of a multivariate table (e.g. z-score per column) so that variables measured on different scales contribute equally to downstream decomposition methods such as principal component analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6
skills.summary: Standardizes each numerical feature of a multivariate table (e.g. z-score per column) so that variables measured on different scales contribute equally to downstream decomposition methods such as principal component analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Columns are already on a common scale or the analysis is scale-invariant (e.g. rank-based or correlation-based methods), so z-scoring would add no benefit The table still contains missing values that you intend to impute first — the automatic pre-filter would silently drop rows before standardization The goal is batch-effect correction of expression data rather than plain per-feature scaling — use ComBat/pyComBat (bundled via the combat package) instead

skills.description: Use when you need controlled simulated data that preserves the empirical multivariate correlation structure of a real metabolite abundance matrix (e.g., to compute permutation-based effective number of tests, Meff0, across sample sizes n=100/500/1000).
skills.name: multivariate-gaussian-simulation
skills.search_text: multivariate-gaussian-simulation Use when you need controlled simulated data that preserves the empirical multivariate correlation structure of a real metabolite abundance matrix (e.g., to compute permutation-based effective number of tests, Meff0, across sample sizes n=100/500/1000). When the analysis goal is to evaluate a correction on real (observed) data rather than on controlled simulated null scenarios When the outcome is binary/categorical and the correlation-structure-preserving Gaussian simulation design from the paper (continuous logit(FEV1/FVC) response) is not adapted appropriately http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Simulate multivariate-Gaussian feature sets whose correlation structure matches that estimated from real metabolomics data (e.g., COPDGene ST001443, 761 metabolites x 1054 subjects), enabling controlled simulation studies of multiple-testing correction procedures such as the permutation-based gold-standard Meff0. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Simulate multivariate-Gaussian feature sets whose correlation structure matches that estimated from real metabolomics data (e.g., COPDGene ST001443, 761 metabolites x 1054 subjects), enabling controlled simulation studies of multiple-testing correction procedures such as the permutation-based gold-standard Meff0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is to evaluate a correction on real (observed) data rather than on controlled simulated null scenarios When the outcome is binary/categorical and the correlation-structure-preserving Gaussian simulation design from the paper (continuous logit(FEV1/FVC) response) is not adapted appropriately

skills.description: Use when you have an assembled experimental lipid database (e.g., m/z, CCS, HILIC retention time entries across lipid classes) with gaps in chemical space and need to train regression models to predict CCS or HILIC retention times for unseen lipid species.
skills.name: multivariate-linear-regression-model-training
skills.search_text: multivariate-linear-regression-model-training Use when you have an assembled experimental lipid database (e.g., m/z, CCS, HILIC retention time entries across lipid classes) with gaps in chemical space and need to train regression models to predict CCS or HILIC retention times for unseen lipid species. When the lipid classes of interest already have comprehensive experimental CCS or retention time coverage — the models exist to fill gaps, not to re-predict known values. When input is raw MS/IM-MS data rather than a curated lipid database with measured retention times/CCS — use the stats/plotting/identification modules instead. When lipid species lack representation in the 45-lipid-class experimental database (e.g., unannotated bacterial lipid subclasses) — feature encoding and model transfer will be invalid. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains multivariate linear regression models (e.g., via scikit-learn) on specialized lipid feature sets — covering lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and sum composition — to predict HILIC retention times or CCS values, and evaluates them on held-out test data with MAE, MDAE, and RMSE metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560
skills.summary: Trains multivariate linear regression models (e.g., via scikit-learn) on specialized lipid feature sets — covering lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and sum composition — to predict HILIC retention times or CCS values, and evaluates them on held-out test data with MAE, MDAE, and RMSE metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the lipid classes of interest already have comprehensive experimental CCS or retention time coverage — the models exist to fill gaps, not to re-predict known values. When input is raw MS/IM-MS data rather than a curated lipid database with measured retention times/CCS — use the stats/plotting/identification modules instead. When lipid species lack representation in the 45-lipid-class experimental database (e.g., unannotated bacterial lipid subclasses) — feature encoding and model transfer will be invalid.

skills.description: Use when both feature-wise tests (with FDR-adjusted q-values) and a multivariate importance model (e.g., MUVR RF ranks) have already been produced for the same feature table, and the goal is to prioritize features for metabolite identification.
skills.name: multivariate-metabolomics-feature-prioritization
skills.search_text: multivariate-metabolomics-feature-prioritization Use when both feature-wise tests (with FDR-adjusted q-values) and a multivariate importance model (e.g., MUVR RF ranks) have already been produced for the same feature table, and the goal is to prioritize features for metabolite identification. Input data has not yet passed notame preprocessing/QC (drift correction, flagging of low-quality features, random forest imputation, batch effect correction) — rank aggregation assumes a cleaned, analyzed feature table No multivariate model importance ranks exist yet (e.g., MUVR was not run); summing ranks is then impossible and univariate FDR ranking alone should be used instead The goal is exploratory interpretation or visualization of statistical results rather than producing a prioritized selection list for metabolite identification http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Combines per-feature univariate statistical evidence (FDR-adjusted p-values/q-values) with multivariate model importance ranks (e.g., MUVR random forest 'mid' model) into a single 'Final Ranks' ordering used to select the most robust metabolic features for downstream identification. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135
skills.summary: Combines per-feature univariate statistical evidence (FDR-adjusted p-values/q-values) with multivariate model importance ranks (e.g., MUVR random forest 'mid' model) into a single 'Final Ranks' ordering used to select the most robust metabolic features for downstream identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not yet passed notame preprocessing/QC (drift correction, flagging of low-quality features, random forest imputation, batch effect correction) — rank aggregation assumes a cleaned, analyzed feature table No multivariate model importance ranks exist yet (e.g., MUVR was not run); summing ranks is then impossible and univariate FDR ranking alone should be used instead The goal is exploratory interpretation or visualization of statistical results rather than producing a prioritized selection list for metabolite identification

skills.description: Use when a supervised multivariate model (e.g. OPLS-DA) has separated sample classes (carriage vs controls) and you must quantify its diagnostic performance with ROC AUC values and confidence intervals.
skills.name: multivariate-model-validation
skills.search_text: multivariate-model-validation Use when a supervised multivariate model (e.g. OPLS-DA) has separated sample classes (carriage vs controls) and you must quantify its diagnostic performance with ROC AUC values and confidence intervals. Input is a single-metabolite feature list rather than cross-validated scores from a supervised pattern-recognition model — the skill evaluates the multivariate latent biomarker pattern, not individual metabolites. The goal is unsupervised exploration of sample-group distribution — PCA is used for that; this skill only evaluates class-separating supervised models. Comparing carriage profiles against acute enteric fever profiles — the paper treats that as a separate heterogeneity question, not a ROC-validated diagnostic model. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Validates supervised chemometric models (OPLS-DA on GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite data) by converting cross-validated scores into ROC curves, computing AUCs, and reporting 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 bootstrap resamples to quantify diagnostic performance of latent metabolite patterns. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pntd.0006215
skills.summary: Validates supervised chemometric models (OPLS-DA on GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite data) by converting cross-validated scores into ROC curves, computing AUCs, and reporting 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 bootstrap resamples to quantify diagnostic performance of latent metabolite patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-metabolite feature list rather than cross-validated scores from a supervised pattern-recognition model — the skill evaluates the multivariate latent biomarker pattern, not individual metabolites. The goal is unsupervised exploration of sample-group distribution — PCA is used for that; this skill only evaluates class-separating supervised models. Comparing carriage profiles against acute enteric fever profiles — the paper treats that as a separate heterogeneity question, not a ROC-validated diagnostic model.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking missing-value imputation methods on high-dimensional metabolomics-like matrices and you need replicated simulated data with known true values, specified correlation structure, and controlled MNAR/MAR missingness for RMSE evaluation.
skills.name: multivariate-normal-data-simulation
skills.search_text: multivariate-normal-data-simulation Use when benchmarking missing-value imputation methods on high-dimensional metabolomics-like matrices and you need replicated simulated data with known true values, specified correlation structure, and controlled MNAR/MAR missingness for RMSE evaluation. Input is real observed metabolomics data where the goal is imputation on actual measurements rather than simulation with known ground truth The analysis goal is downstream statistical-testing concordance (e.g., MLCI on real datasets) rather than RMSE-based simulation benchmarking You need realistic non-normal metabolite distributions — this simulation relies on the multivariate normal assumption, which the paper itself flags as a limitation of KNN-TN http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generates synthetic high-dimensional metabolomics-like datasets by drawing samples from an M-dimensional multivariate normal with controlled correlation structures, so that imputation methods (KNN-TN, KNN-CR, KNN-EU) can be benchmarked against known ground-truth values under controlled MNAR/MAR missingness. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: Generates synthetic high-dimensional metabolomics-like datasets by drawing samples from an M-dimensional multivariate normal with controlled correlation structures, so that imputation methods (KNN-TN, KNN-CR, KNN-EU) can be benchmarked against known ground-truth values under controlled MNAR/MAR missingness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real observed metabolomics data where the goal is imputation on actual measurements rather than simulation with known ground truth The analysis goal is downstream statistical-testing concordance (e.g., MLCI on real datasets) rather than RMSE-based simulation benchmarking You need realistic non-normal metabolite distributions — this simulation relies on the multivariate normal assumption, which the paper itself flags as a limitation of KNN-TN

skills.description: Use when a benchmark needs a fully-observed synthetic data matrix with realistic covariance and group structure, e.g., to evaluate imputation methods under controlled MNAR masking before injecting missing values.
skills.name: multivariate-normal-sampling
skills.search_text: multivariate-normal-sampling Use when a benchmark needs a fully-observed synthetic data matrix with realistic covariance and group structure, e.g., to evaluate imputation methods under controlled MNAR masking before injecting missing values. The goal is to impute an already-missing real dataset (e.g., targeted_data.csv or untargeted_data.csv) rather than to generate synthetic fully-observed benchmark data The data are non-normal and cannot be reasonably modeled by a multivariate normal without prior log-transformation A benchmark requires real missingness patterns (LOD/LOQ-driven MNAR from actual MS acquisition) instead of simulated group structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates a simulated metabolomics dataset by drawing two 80-observation groups from a multivariate normal distribution whose covariance matrix Cov is estimated from a real targeted metabolomics dataset (the diabetes dataset with P=76 FFAs and BAs), preserving realistic covariance structure and between-group differences for imputation benchmarking. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Generates a simulated metabolomics dataset by drawing two 80-observation groups from a multivariate normal distribution whose covariance matrix Cov is estimated from a real targeted metabolomics dataset (the diabetes dataset with P=76 FFAs and BAs), preserving realistic covariance structure and between-group differences for imputation benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to impute an already-missing real dataset (e.g., targeted_data.csv or untargeted_data.csv) rather than to generate synthetic fully-observed benchmark data The data are non-normal and cannot be reasonably modeled by a multivariate normal without prior log-transformation A benchmark requires real missingness patterns (LOD/LOQ-driven MNAR from actual MS acquisition) instead of simulated group structure

skills.description: Use when you have an aggregated peak-area table from GC-MS library hits (e.g. mzExacto output) and need standardized, statistically comparable component areas for downstream ordination or modeling.
skills.name: multivariate-ordination-input-preparation
skills.search_text: multivariate-ordination-input-preparation Use when you have an aggregated peak-area table from GC-MS library hits (e.g. mzExacto output) and need standardized, statistically comparable component areas for downstream ordination or modeling. Input is already a standardized or normalized feature table ready for ordination Data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 spectra — uafR's algorithms depend on published fragmentation data and do not yet apply The goal is chemical annotation or compound selection (use categorate()/exactoThese()) rather than abundance standardization http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Standardizes GC-MS component areas of tentatively identified chemicals relative to known internal or external standards and formats the result as an ordination-ready table for PCA, NMDS, or machine-learning analyses in the uafR workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0306202
skills.summary: Standardizes GC-MS component areas of tentatively identified chemicals relative to known internal or external standards and formats the result as an ordination-ready table for PCA, NMDS, or machine-learning analyses in the uafR workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a standardized or normalized feature table ready for ordination Data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 spectra — uafR's algorithms depend on published fragmentation data and do not yet apply The goal is chemical annotation or compound selection (use categorate()/exactoThese()) rather than abundance standardization

skills.description: Use when a standardized GC-MS compound-area matrix (areas relative to internal/external standards) must be ordinated with NMDS and the between-treatment significance pattern checked against a published manual-peak-annotation analysis.
skills.name: multivariate-ordination-visualization
skills.search_text: multivariate-ordination-visualization Use when a standardized GC-MS compound-area matrix (areas relative to internal/external standards) must be ordinated with NMDS and the between-treatment significance pattern checked against a published manual-peak-annotation analysis. The input data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 spectra — uafR's algorithms do not apply to these data types The data are from untested instrument/data contexts such as LC-MS, Q-TOF, Orbitrap, TimsTOF HT, or Astral The goal is de novo peak deconvolution or library matching — use Agilent Unknowns Analysis (deconvolution algorithm) upstream of this skill instead Runs non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ordination on standardized GC-MS compound-area tables via uafR's downstream statistical pathway, then tests between-treatment differences and audits the result against the originally published significance pattern (Ponce et al. 2022). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0306202
skills.summary: Runs non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ordination on standardized GC-MS compound-area tables via uafR's downstream statistical pathway, then tests between-treatment differences and audits the result against the originally published significance pattern (Ponce et al. 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are MS2, MS3, or ion mobility + MS2 spectra — uafR's algorithms do not apply to these data types The data are from untested instrument/data contexts such as LC-MS, Q-TOF, Orbitrap, TimsTOF HT, or Astral The goal is de novo peak deconvolution or library matching — use Agilent Unknowns Analysis (deconvolution algorithm) upstream of this skill instead

skills.description: Use when a post-curation feature data matrix plus pooled/intrastudy QC injections are available and you need to verify curation quality, spot outliers, QC clustering, or time-related signal drift before statistical analysis.
skills.name: multivariate-outlier-detection
skills.search_text: multivariate-outlier-detection Use when a post-curation feature data matrix plus pooled/intrastudy QC injections are available and you need to verify curation quality, spot outliers, QC clustering, or time-related signal drift before statistical analysis. Input is still the raw extracted matrix before the TidyMS curation filters (Rt filter, blank filter, RSD filter, prevalence filter, D-ratio filter) have been applied, when the goal is to judge curation outcome rather than raw-data condition The dataset lacks pooled/intrastudy QC injections, so no QC-referenced quality or drift assessment can be anchored in score space The goal is feature annotation or biological group-difference testing rather than QC/outlier inspection of the data matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build PCA models with scikit-learn on raw and curated LC-MS feature matrices (NIST candidate RM 8231 and SRM 1950 plasma, MetaboLights MTBLS1919) and inspect score plots of pooled/intrastudy QC injections to visually assess data quality, outliers, and drift at each step of the TidyMS data-curation pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Build PCA models with scikit-learn on raw and curated LC-MS feature matrices (NIST candidate RM 8231 and SRM 1950 plasma, MetaboLights MTBLS1919) and inspect score plots of pooled/intrastudy QC injections to visually assess data quality, outliers, and drift at each step of the TidyMS data-curation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still the raw extracted matrix before the TidyMS curation filters (Rt filter, blank filter, RSD filter, prevalence filter, D-ratio filter) have been applied, when the goal is to judge curation outcome rather than raw-data condition The dataset lacks pooled/intrastudy QC injections, so no QC-referenced quality or drift assessment can be anchored in score space The goal is feature annotation or biological group-difference testing rather than QC/outlier inspection of the data matrix

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics sequence contains regularly injected QCpool samples and you must identify outlying or out-of-control samples that univariate plots miss, before outlier removal in the QComics sequential workflow.
skills.name: multivariate-qc-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: multivariate-qc-plot-visualization Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics sequence contains regularly injected QCpool samples and you must identify outlying or out-of-control samples that univariate plots miss, before outlier removal in the QComics sequential workflow. The study has no QCpool samples measured at regular intervals during the sequence(s) — the package requires pooled samples injected regularly to monitor quality The QC data were not exported from Sciex MultiQuant (> v3.0.3) to txt format, so the QComics app cannot parse the input The goal is correction of background noise/carryover, missing-data handling, or quality-marker monitoring — those are earlier/later steps in the QComics sequential workflow, not multivariate outlier visualization http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Multivariate quality-control visualization from the QComics protocol: fit a PCA model to processed metabolomics QC data and render Hotelling T2 (95% confidence ellipse) and DmodX residual plots via make_qc_graph to flag 'out-of-control' samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660
skills.summary: Multivariate quality-control visualization from the QComics protocol: fit a PCA model to processed metabolomics QC data and render Hotelling T2 (95% confidence ellipse) and DmodX residual plots via make_qc_graph to flag 'out-of-control' samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study has no QCpool samples measured at regular intervals during the sequence(s) — the package requires pooled samples injected regularly to monitor quality The QC data were not exported from Sciex MultiQuant (> v3.0.3) to txt format, so the QComics app cannot parse the input The goal is correction of background noise/carryover, missing-data handling, or quality-marker monitoring — those are earlier/later steps in the QComics sequential workflow, not multivariate outlier visualization

skills.description: Use when a feature table has vastly more features than samples and you need to assess whether a supervised classifier (OPLS-DA) overfits by comparing in-sample R²Y against cross-validated Q²Y with a scores plot.
skills.name: multivariate-scores-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: multivariate-scores-plot-visualization Use when a feature table has vastly more features than samples and you need to assess whether a supervised classifier (OPLS-DA) overfits by comparing in-sample R²Y against cross-validated Q²Y with a scores plot. skills.summary: Fit a supervised OPLS-DA discriminant model (ropls in R) on the merged wild soybean feature table with DPPH High/Low labels, render a two-component scores plot, and record R²Y, cross-validated Q²Y, and permutation-test results to diagnose overfitting in high-dimensional untargeted metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS/MS data rather than an aligned feature table — use the MS2toImg image-encoding route instead, which bypasses feature alignment entirely The goal is accurate bioactivity prediction rather than diagnosing overfitting of classical multivariate statistics; the article shows OPLS-DA generalizes poorly (Q²Y ≈ 0.287) despite high fit Samples cannot be split into labeled classes (e.g., DPPH High/Low groups) since OPLS-DA is a supervised discriminant method

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed (batch-corrected, log-transformed, standardised) ICP-MS ionome table of ion concentrations needs exploratory multivariate analysis: variance decomposition, element-element correlation networks, or clustered correlation heat maps.
skills.name: multivariate-statistical-analysis
skills.search_text: multivariate-statistical-analysis Use when a pre-processed (batch-corrected, log-transformed, standardised) ICP-MS ionome table of ion concentrations needs exploratory multivariate analysis: variance decomposition, element-element correlation networks, or clustered correlation heat maps. Data have not passed through the PreProcessing section — the pipeline requires the cleaned dataset from PreProcessing before exploratory analysis, so raw, outlier-laden concentration tables should not be fed directly to these analysis steps The goal is metabolomics feature or spectral analysis rather than ion-concentration (ionomics) profiles — although the authors note applicability may extend to metabolomics, the tool was designed and benchmarked on ICP-MS ionome data Only a single-variable summary or univariate group comparison is needed — the suite is built for multivariate variance structure, correlation, and network inference across many ions http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies the multivariate statistics suite of the IonFlow R package — PCA, element-element correlation analysis, Ward-based hierarchical clustering, relevance network extraction, and correlation heat-mapping — to ICP-MS ionome profiles from ionomics experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01841-z

The task is de novo molecule generation or spectrum simulation (the other MassSpecGym challenges) — MVP only ranks a provided set of candidate structures given a query spectrum. You need a training objective that directly optimizes candidate ranking — the paper notes losses that prioritize ranking molecular candidates are not currently included in MVP. No candidate structure list exists for the query spectra — MVP annotates by ranking provided candidates (candidates_pth), not by generating structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and apply MVP (MultiView Projection), a contrastive framework that jointly aligns four views — molecular graph (Zmol), Morgan fingerprint (Zfp), spectrum (Zs), and consensus spectrum (Zcs) — in one joint embedding space to rank molecular candidates for MS/MS spectra on MassSpecGym. Joint multi-view learning improves candidate ranking over approaches that concatenate views or use them as auxiliary-task targets. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.688047
skills.summary: Train and apply MVP (MultiView Projection), a contrastive framework that jointly aligns four views — molecular graph (Zmol), Morgan fingerprint (Zfp), spectrum (Zs), and consensus spectrum (Zcs) — in one joint embedding space to rank molecular candidates for MS/MS spectra on MassSpecGym. Joint multi-view learning improves candidate ranking over approaches that concatenate views or use them as auxiliary-task targets.

skills.name: munkres-optimal-domain-matching
skills.search_text: munkres-optimal-domain-matching Use when computing pairwise distances between biosynthetic gene clusters with differing numbers of Pfam domains per type, and you need an optimal, non-quadratic one-to-one domain assignment to score sequence similarity and copy-number differences. When the goal is full evolutionary reconstruction of a gene cluster family — CORASON's multi-locus core phylogeny, not Munkres matching, is the appropriate mechanism When comparing clusters with largely non-overlapping domain-type inventories — with few or no shared domain types the assignment is uninformative and the Jaccard index alone will dominate the distance When BGCs are not closely related enough for hmmalign-based profile alignments to be informative; alternative alignment backends (Muscle, MAFFT via --mix) should be benchmarked instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 A pairwise BGC comparison strategy that uses the Munkres (Hungarian) assignment algorithm to find the optimal one-to-one matching between domains of the same Pfam type in two gene clusters, so that copy-number differences and domain sequence identity (Domain Sequence Similarity, DSS) can be scored efficiently instead of relying on slow all-versus-all sequence alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: A pairwise BGC comparison strategy that uses the Munkres (Hungarian) assignment algorithm to find the optimal one-to-one matching between domains of the same Pfam type in two gene clusters, so that copy-number differences and domain sequence identity (Domain Sequence Similarity, DSS) can be scored efficiently instead of relying on slow all-versus-all sequence alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is full evolutionary reconstruction of a gene cluster family — CORASON's multi-locus core phylogeny, not Munkres matching, is the appropriate mechanism When comparing clusters with largely non-overlapping domain-type inventories — with few or no shared domain types the assignment is uninformative and the Jaccard index alone will dominate the distance When BGCs are not closely related enough for hmmalign-based profile alignments to be informative; alternative alignment backends (Muscle, MAFFT via --mix) should be benchmarked instead

Query spectra are already available as an xcms result object in R, where MS2 can be extracted directly with chromPeakSpectra() instead of importing an external MGF The reference database provides precursor m/z values and a precursor-m/z prefilter is desired, so requirePrecursor = TRUE (default) in CompareSpectraParam is appropriate The goal is MS1-level annotation by m/z and retention time, which matchMz with Mass2MzParam or MzRtParam handles http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Imports MZmine-exported GNPS MGF files into R as Spectra objects via MsBackendMgf so that externally generated MS2 feature spectra can serve as the query in matchSpectra()-based annotation against a CompoundDb reference such as HMDB 5.0. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12020173
skills.summary: Imports MZmine-exported GNPS MGF files into R as Spectra objects via MsBackendMgf so that externally generated MS2 feature spectra can serve as the query in matchSpectra()-based annotation against a CompoundDb reference such as HMDB 5.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query spectra are already available as an xcms result object in R, where MS2 can be extracted directly with chromPeakSpectra() instead of importing an external MGF The reference database provides precursor m/z values and a precursor-m/z prefilter is desired, so requirePrecursor = TRUE (default) in CompareSpectraParam is appropriate The goal is MS1-level annotation by m/z and retention time, which matchMz with Mass2MzParam or MzRtParam handles

skills.description: Use when the input is a MZmine join-aligned feature table (.csv, produced with m/z tolerance 40 ppm and RT tolerance 0.2 min) plus its corresponding GNPS FBMN .mgf spectra file, and the goal is to build a MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrix from the aligned samples (e.g. MSV000083306 demo data).
skills.name: mzmine-feature-table-import
skills.search_text: mzmine-feature-table-import Use when the input is a MZmine join-aligned feature table (.csv, produced with m/z tolerance 40 ppm and RT tolerance 0.2 min) plus its corresponding GNPS FBMN .mgf spectra file, and the goal is to build a MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrix from the aligned samples (e.g. MSV000083306 demo data). When quantification depends on MS1 feature intensities — MEMO's aligned-sample workflow uses only a presence/absence matrix and ignores MS1 intensity values. When the spectra are not MZmine/GNPS FBMN exports or the table is not an aligned feature quantification .csv, since this import path assumes the MZmine join-aligner output format. When a MEMO matrix is already built — this skill is the import/front-end step, not the fingerprint-alignment or downstream filtering/visualization step. Loads an MZmine-exported aligned feature quantification table (.csv) together with its GNPS FBMN-exported .mgf MS2 spectra file into the memo_ms package (import_data), providing the aligned-sample entry point for MS2-based sample vectorization where only feature presence/absence — not MS1 intensity — is used. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Loads an MZmine-exported aligned feature quantification table (.csv) together with its GNPS FBMN-exported .mgf MS2 spectra file into the memo_ms package (import_data), providing the aligned-sample entry point for MS2-based sample vectorization where only feature presence/absence — not MS1 intensity — is used.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When quantification depends on MS1 feature intensities — MEMO's aligned-sample workflow uses only a presence/absence matrix and ignores MS1 intensity values. When the spectra are not MZmine/GNPS FBMN exports or the table is not an aligned feature quantification .csv, since this import path assumes the MZmine join-aligner output format. When a MEMO matrix is already built — this skill is the import/front-end step, not the fingerprint-alignment or downstream filtering/visualization step.

skills.description: Use when the input is an MZmine 2/3-exported quantitative feature table and sample metadata and you need to load, normalize, and reduce the feature set (e.g., 727 → 104 → 26 for Pristimera indica roots) prior to computing Inventa components.
skills.name: mzmine-feature-table-processing
skills.search_text: mzmine-feature-table-processing Use when the input is an MZmine 2/3-exported quantitative feature table and sample metadata and you need to load, normalize, and reduce the feature set (e.g., 727 → 104 → 26 for Pristimera indica roots) prior to computing Inventa components. The input is already a curated/filtered feature list rather than a raw MZmine quantitative export, so re-filtering would double-reduce features The analysis does not require feature-count reduction, e.g., when only the Literature Component (LC), which is independent of spectral data, is needed The feature table was exported with columns other than Peak area/row m/z/row retention time and cannot be reconciled by dropping columns in quant_table() http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Load and curate MZmine quantitative feature tables (peak area, row m/z, row retention time columns) with GNPS-format metadata inside the Inventa pipeline, then apply intensity-based and quantile-based filtering to reduce features before scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Load and curate MZmine quantitative feature tables (peak area, row m/z, row retention time columns) with GNPS-format metadata inside the Inventa pipeline, then apply intensity-based and quantile-based filtering to reduce features before scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated/filtered feature list rather than a raw MZmine quantitative export, so re-filtering would double-reduce features The analysis does not require feature-count reduction, e.g., when only the Literature Component (LC), which is independent of spectral data, is needed The feature table was exported with columns other than Peak area/row m/z/row retention time and cannot be reconciled by dropping columns in quant_table()

skills.description: Use when the input is an MZmine 2 aligned peak list (from 'More Restrictive' or 'Less Restrictive' extraction) that must be decomposed into candidate peak groups with sample-level intensity profiles and RT window boundaries before filtering or classification.
skills.name: mzmine-peak-list-parsing
skills.search_text: mzmine-peak-list-parsing Use when the input is an MZmine 2 aligned peak list (from 'More Restrictive' or 'Less Restrictive' extraction) that must be decomposed into candidate peak groups with sample-level intensity profiles and RT window boundaries before filtering or classification. Input is already a filtered feature table of peak-group summary parameters with no per-sample intensity shapes — use the peak-group parameter logistic regression filtering path instead Peak lists were produced by a tool other than MZmine 2 (e.g., XCMS centWave output without MZmine-style aligned peak groups and grouped peak windows), since the parsing logic assumes MZmine 2 peak-list structure The goal is spectral identification or annotation of metabolites rather than peak quality classification of extracted LC-MS features http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Load MZmine 2-aligned peak lists extracted from non-targeted HILIC LC-MS plasma data and extract per-peak-group m/z and retention-time windows, selecting the 63 samples in which each candidate peak was most intense as the basis for downstream image-raster construction and true/false peak classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b02983
skills.summary: Load MZmine 2-aligned peak lists extracted from non-targeted HILIC LC-MS plasma data and extract per-peak-group m/z and retention-time windows, selecting the 63 samples in which each candidate peak was most intense as the basis for downstream image-raster construction and true/false peak classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature table of peak-group summary parameters with no per-sample intensity shapes — use the peak-group parameter logistic regression filtering path instead Peak lists were produced by a tool other than MZmine 2 (e.g., XCMS centWave output without MZmine-style aligned peak groups and grouped peak windows), since the parsing logic assumes MZmine 2 peak-list structure The goal is spectral identification or annotation of metabolites rather than peak quality classification of extracted LC-MS features

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS challenge or study data arrives as mzML files and you need discrete, exported MS/MS spectra (e.g., an MGF-style set) as input for formula or structure annotation tools like MIST-CF or SIRIUS.
skills.name: mzmine-peak-picking-and-msms-extraction
skills.search_text: mzmine-peak-picking-and-msms-extraction Use when raw LC-MS/MS challenge or study data arrives as mzML files and you need discrete, exported MS/MS spectra (e.g., an MGF-style set) as input for formula or structure annotation tools like MIST-CF or SIRIUS. Input is already exported, preprocessed spectra (e.g., the demo_specs.mgf MGF shipped in the mist-cf repo or a feature table) — re-running MZmine would be redundant The downstream task is negative-mode formula annotation — the released MIST-CF pipeline targets positive mode only, so positive-mode extraction assumptions apply You need MS1 isotopic-pattern scoring — MIST-CF uses zero MS1 isotopic information, so isotope-focused peak picking is out of scope for this pipeline Extract per-feature MS/MS spectra from raw challenge mzML files using MZmine 3 feature detection/export, as done to prepare the 304 positive-mode CASMI 2022 challenge spectra for downstream chemical formula benchmarking with MIST-CF and SIRIUS. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Extract per-feature MS/MS spectra from raw challenge mzML files using MZmine 3 feature detection/export, as done to prepare the 304 positive-mode CASMI 2022 challenge spectra for downstream chemical formula benchmarking with MIST-CF and SIRIUS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already exported, preprocessed spectra (e.g., the demo_specs.mgf MGF shipped in the mist-cf repo or a feature table) — re-running MZmine would be redundant The downstream task is negative-mode formula annotation — the released MIST-CF pipeline targets positive mode only, so positive-mode extraction assumptions apply You need MS1 isotopic-pattern scoring — MIST-CF uses zero MS1 isotopic information, so isotope-focused peak picking is out of scope for this pipeline

skills.description: Use when building a sample-centric LC-HRMS2 feature detection pipeline on UHPLC-MS2 DDA data (mzML/mzXML inputs) that must yield a per-sample feature table and MS2 .mgf export for FBMN, ISDB, or KG integration.
skills.name: mzmine-workflow-configuration
skills.search_text: mzmine-workflow-configuration Use when building a sample-centric LC-HRMS2 feature detection pipeline on UHPLC-MS2 DDA data (mzML/mzXML inputs) that must yield a per-sample feature table and MS2 .mgf export for FBMN, ISDB, or KG integration. When the input is already an aligned N x M feature quantification table — the ENPKG workflow's motivation is precisely to avoid retention-time-based feature alignment across batches. When processing data other than LC-HRMS2 DDA metabolomics (e.g., proteomics LC-MS/MS or GC-MS EI data), since the ADAP/wavelet parameters and 12 ppm tolerance were tuned for this instrumental setup. When a downstream tool requires a merged, batch-aligned dataset rather than per-sample MZmine output. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Configure the MZmine stage of the ENPKG pipeline: convert Thermo RAW to mzXML, centroid mass detection, ADAP chromatogram building and wavelet deconvolution, isotope grouping, MS2/RT feature filtering, and export of the feature quantification table plus per-feature MS2 .mgf spectra for downstream annotation and molecular networking. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Configure the MZmine stage of the ENPKG pipeline: convert Thermo RAW to mzXML, centroid mass detection, ADAP chromatogram building and wavelet deconvolution, isotope grouping, MS2/RT feature filtering, and export of the feature quantification table plus per-feature MS2 .mgf spectra for downstream annotation and molecular networking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already an aligned N x M feature quantification table — the ENPKG workflow's motivation is precisely to avoid retention-time-based feature alignment across batches. When processing data other than LC-HRMS2 DDA metabolomics (e.g., proteomics LC-MS/MS or GC-MS EI data), since the ADAP/wavelet parameters and 12 ppm tolerance were tuned for this instrumental setup. When a downstream tool requires a merged, batch-aligned dataset rather than per-sample MZmine output.

skills.description: Use when raw LC–MS/MS mzML files need feature extraction and per-feature representative MS2 spectra before formula/adduct assignment and molecular candidate ranking.
skills.name: mzmine3-workflow-configuration
skills.search_text: mzmine3-workflow-configuration Use when raw LC–MS/MS mzML files need feature extraction and per-feature representative MS2 spectra before formula/adduct assignment and molecular candidate ranking. Input is already a processed feature table with per-feature m/z and MS2 spectra — rerunning MZmine3 extraction is unnecessary. The goal is to skip feature extraction entirely and only rank molecular candidates from preprocessed spectra; the MVP pretrained model (test.py) consumes already-prepped spectra files, not raw mzML. Data are negative ion mode spectra when the analysis scope targets only positive ion mode data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Configures MZmine3 to perform feature extraction (mass detection, chromatogram building, feature deconvolution) and representative spectra selection on LC–MS/MS mzML files, producing a feature table of m/z, retention time, and representative MS2 spectra for downstream annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.688047
skills.summary: Configures MZmine3 to perform feature extraction (mass detection, chromatogram building, feature deconvolution) and representative spectra selection on LC–MS/MS mzML files, producing a feature table of m/z, retention time, and representative MS2 spectra for downstream annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table with per-feature m/z and MS2 spectra — rerunning MZmine3 extraction is unnecessary. The goal is to skip feature extraction entirely and only rank molecular candidates from preprocessed spectra; the MVP pretrained model (test.py) consumes already-prepped spectra files, not raw mzML. Data are negative ion mode spectra when the analysis scope targets only positive ion mode data.

skills.description: Use when raw metabolomics data are supplied as individual centroided mzML files (or per-replicate peak-list CSVs) and a deduplicated list of unique MS features is needed for downstream Compound Activity Mapping or bioactivity integration.
skills.name: mzml-centroided-peak-import
skills.search_text: mzml-centroided-peak-import Use when raw metabolomics data are supplied as individual centroided mzML files (or per-replicate peak-list CSVs) and a deduplicated list of unique MS features is needed for downstream Compound Activity Mapping or bioactivity integration. Input is already an MZmine 2 output peak list or a GNPS network (.graphml) file — use the GNPS/MZmine import type instead of the mzML replicate pipeline Replicate injections are not available — replicate comparison requires n replicates and the paper notes it is only possible 'where possible' Data have not been peak-picked/centroided — the pipeline expects centroided peak lists, not profile-mode spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Imports peak-picked centroided mzML-derived peak lists into the NP Analyst tool-chain and reduces them to a single list of unique MS features via replicate comparison (present in n−1 of n replicates) followed by R-tree based basketing of overlapping m/z and retention-time error ranges. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Imports peak-picked centroided mzML-derived peak lists into the NP Analyst tool-chain and reduces them to a single list of unique MS features via replicate comparison (present in n−1 of n replicates) followed by R-tree based basketing of overlapping m/z and retention-time error ranges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an MZmine 2 output peak list or a GNPS network (.graphml) file — use the GNPS/MZmine import type instead of the mzML replicate pipeline Replicate injections are not available — replicate comparison requires n replicates and the paper notes it is only possible 'where possible' Data have not been peak-picked/centroided — the pipeline expects centroided peak lists, not profile-mode spectra

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the computational performance or scalability of LC-MS metabolomics data processing tools, and you need study-size-varied inputs from a fixed centroided mzML corpus rather than a single fixed-size run.
skills.name: mzml-dataset-subset-sampling
skills.search_text: mzml-dataset-subset-sampling Use when benchmarking the computational performance or scalability of LC-MS metabolomics data processing tools, and you need study-size-varied inputs from a fixed centroided mzML corpus rather than a single fixed-size run. The goal is feature-detection or quantification accuracy comparison (e.g. feature counts vs XCMS/MZmine), not runtime/memory scaling The input data are low-resolution or non-Orbitrap profiles without optimization, since asari's benchmark performance was established on high-resolution Orbitrap centroided mzML data Only one dataset size is needed and no scaling characterization is intended — a single timed run suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Systematically varies LC-MS metabolomics study size by selecting nested subsets of centroided mzML files (e.g. 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 samples) from a public dataset, so that computational tools such as asari and XCMS can be benchmarked for CPU time, wall-clock time, and peak memory scaling. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Systematically varies LC-MS metabolomics study size by selecting nested subsets of centroided mzML files (e.g. 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 samples) from a public dataset, so that computational tools such as asari and XCMS can be benchmarked for CPU time, wall-clock time, and peak memory scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is feature-detection or quantification accuracy comparison (e.g. feature counts vs XCMS/MZmine), not runtime/memory scaling The input data are low-resolution or non-Orbitrap profiles without optimization, since asari's benchmark performance was established on high-resolution Orbitrap centroided mzML data Only one dataset size is needed and no scaling characterization is intended — a single timed run suffices

skills.description: Use when mzML lipidomics runs need per-feature MS/MS-based lipid identifications, especially when comparing candidate annotations from multiple in-silico fragmentation libraries.
skills.name: mzml-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: mzml-feature-annotation Use when mzML lipidomics runs need per-feature MS/MS-based lipid identifications, especially when comparing candidate annotations from multiple in-silico fragmentation libraries. Input is already a scored feature annotation table and no MS/MS spectral search is required. The samples lack MS/MS fragmentation data — MAVEN2's spectral-matching search depends on fragmentation spectra. The goal is compound annotation outside the lipid classes covered by the available in-silico lipid libraries (e.g., general metabolite spectra without a suitable fragmentation library). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotate LC-MS/MS features from lipidomics mzML samples by running MAVEN2's MS/MS spectral-matching search against two in-silico lipid libraries (CalicoLipids and MS-DIAL), scoring every match with the hypergeometric score. This yields per-feature proposed lipid annotations from each library for downstream thresholding and comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12080684
skills.summary: Annotate LC-MS/MS features from lipidomics mzML samples by running MAVEN2's MS/MS spectral-matching search against two in-silico lipid libraries (CalicoLipids and MS-DIAL), scoring every match with the hypergeometric score. This yields per-feature proposed lipid annotations from each library for downstream thresholding and comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a scored feature annotation table and no MS/MS spectral search is required. The samples lack MS/MS fragmentation data — MAVEN2's spectral-matching search depends on fragmentation spectra. The goal is compound annotation outside the lipid classes covered by the available in-silico lipid libraries (e.g., general metabolite spectra without a suitable fragmentation library).

skills.description: Use when raw LC–MS data in mzML format must be turned into extracted feature lists (m/z, RT, area CSV per run) so that feature alignment tools like G-Aligner, or its evaluation against manual annotations, can be run.
skills.name: mzml-feature-extraction-parsing
skills.search_text: mzml-feature-extraction-parsing Use when raw LC–MS data in mzML format must be turned into extracted feature lists (m/z, RT, area CSV per run) so that feature alignment tools like G-Aligner, or its evaluation against manual annotations, can be run. Feature lists are already extracted as CSV with m/z, RT, area columns (e.g. provided in the G-Aligner repository's data folders) — skip extraction and go straight to alignment You need de novo feature detection performed by G-Aligner itself — G-Aligner does not detect features from raw mzML; extraction must be done by MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS or MetaPro Your data are not LC–MS metabolomics runs (e.g. proteomics or non-MS data) where m/z/RT/area feature lists are not the target representation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Converts raw mzML LC–MS runs from public metabolomics benchmark datasets (e.g. MTBLS562, QE_HF, TripleTOF_6600) into software-extracted feature lists in CSV format with m/z, RT and area columns, the only input format G-Aligner accepts for downstream multipartite-graph feature alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Converts raw mzML LC–MS runs from public metabolomics benchmark datasets (e.g. MTBLS562, QE_HF, TripleTOF_6600) into software-extracted feature lists in CSV format with m/z, RT and area columns, the only input format G-Aligner accepts for downstream multipartite-graph feature alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Feature lists are already extracted as CSV with m/z, RT, area columns (e.g. provided in the G-Aligner repository's data folders) — skip extraction and go straight to alignment You need de novo feature detection performed by G-Aligner itself — G-Aligner does not detect features from raw mzML; extraction must be done by MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS or MetaPro Your data are not LC–MS metabolomics runs (e.g. proteomics or non-MS data) where m/z/RT/area feature lists are not the target representation

skills.description: Use when you have raw LC-MS mzML files plus an aligned or unaligned feature table CSV (from mzMine2, XCMS, etc.) and need to load both into NeatMS before peak prediction or filtering.
skills.name: mzml-feature-table-ingestion
skills.search_text: mzml-feature-table-ingestion Use when you have raw LC-MS mzML files plus an aligned or unaligned feature table CSV (from mzMine2, XCMS, etc.) and need to load both into NeatMS before peak prediction or filtering. If you already have a labelled/filtered peak table and only need to re-export it — ingestion into a new Experiment would duplicate work rather than relabel peaks. If your feature table comes from a pipeline whose column schema NeatMS does not recognise (e.g. a custom exporter not matching mzMine2 or XCMS formats) — the Experiment constructor will not map the properties correctly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Ingest raw mzML files and a commonly produced feature table (e.g. from mzMine2 or XCMS) into a NeatMS Experiment object, so neural-network peak labelling and filtering can be applied downstream. This is the data-loading step that maps aligned/unaligned feature CSVs onto the raw spectral data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02220
skills.summary: Ingest raw mzML files and a commonly produced feature table (e.g. from mzMine2 or XCMS) into a NeatMS Experiment object, so neural-network peak labelling and filtering can be applied downstream. This is the data-loading step that maps aligned/unaligned feature CSVs onto the raw spectral data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you already have a labelled/filtered peak table and only need to re-export it — ingestion into a new Experiment would duplicate work rather than relabel peaks. If your feature table comes from a pipeline whose column schema NeatMS does not recognise (e.g. a custom exporter not matching mzMine2 or XCMS formats) — the Experiment constructor will not map the properties correctly.

skills.description: Use when a ground-truth LC-MS/MS dataset with known molecule identities, abundances, and retention times is needed to benchmark quantification or identification algorithms before running real MS experiments.
skills.name: mzml-file-generation
skills.search_text: mzml-file-generation Use when a ground-truth LC-MS/MS dataset with known molecule identities, abundances, and retention times is needed to benchmark quantification or identification algorithms before running real MS experiments. The input is already measured LC-MS/MS data and the goal is analysis or identification rather than creation of a synthetic ground-truth benchmark The molecules of interest cannot be represented as chemical formulas, so SMITER's formula-based isotope-pattern and fragmentation calculations do not apply A realistic noise/contaminant profile identical to a specific instrument is required — simulated runs exhibit lower noise than real measurements and lack unidentified contaminant peaks (e.g. the ~15 min peak in the real nucleoside measurement) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate synthetic LC-MS/MS mzML files with SMITER by simulating chromatographic peaks, isotope patterns, MS2 fragmentation, and noise from chemical formulas, producing gold-standard datasets with known ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/genes12030396
skills.summary: Generate synthetic LC-MS/MS mzML files with SMITER by simulating chromatographic peaks, isotope patterns, MS2 fragmentation, and noise from chemical formulas, producing gold-standard datasets with known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already measured LC-MS/MS data and the goal is analysis or identification rather than creation of a synthetic ground-truth benchmark The molecules of interest cannot be represented as chemical formulas, so SMITER's formula-based isotope-pattern and fragmentation calculations do not apply A realistic noise/contaminant profile identical to a specific instrument is required — simulated runs exhibit lower noise than real measurements and lack unidentified contaminant peaks (e.g. the ~15 min peak in the real nucleoside measurement)

skills.description: Use when an instrument PC writes vendor raw files that must be automatically converted to mzML, picked up by a monitoring daemon, and queued for QC processing without manual intervention.
skills.name: mzml-file-ingestion-and-scheduling
skills.search_text: mzml-file-ingestion-and-scheduling Use when an instrument PC writes vendor raw files that must be automatically converted to mzML, picked up by a monitoring daemon, and queued for QC processing without manual intervention. Input files are already processed feature tables or already converted, registered mzML files that QC4Metabolomics has previously ingested — ingestion and scheduling would duplicate records. The analysis goal is retrospective postanalysis correction of intensity drifts rather than real-time detection of newly acquired files. Data are not MS-based untargeted metabolomics acquisitions (e.g. non-MS omics or NMR data); the pipeline's modules assume chromatographic MS files. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Continuously detect newly acquired metabolomics data files (mzML, mzXML, mzData), register them in a database, and schedule them for downstream quality-parameter extraction within the QC4Metabolomics processing loop. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: Continuously detect newly acquired metabolomics data files (mzML, mzXML, mzData), register them in a database, and schedule them for downstream quality-parameter extraction within the QC4Metabolomics processing loop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are already processed feature tables or already converted, registered mzML files that QC4Metabolomics has previously ingested — ingestion and scheduling would duplicate records. The analysis goal is retrospective postanalysis correction of intensity drifts rather than real-time detection of newly acquired files. Data are not MS-based untargeted metabolomics acquisitions (e.g. non-MS omics or NMR data); the pipeline's modules assume chromatographic MS files.

skills.description: Use when raw LC-IMS-MS/MS acquisitions in mzML(.gz) format (e.g. Agilent 6560 Ion Mobility LC/Q-TOF deposits such as MSV000091746) must be converted into DEIMoS's common N-dimensional grid before peak detection or other downstream steps.
skills.name: mzml-file-loading-and-grid-construction
skills.search_text: mzml-file-loading-and-grid-construction Use when raw LC-IMS-MS/MS acquisitions in mzML(.gz) format (e.g. Agilent 6560 Ion Mobility LC/Q-TOF deposits such as MSV000091746) must be converted into DEIMoS's common N-dimensional grid before peak detection or other downstream steps. Input is already a processed feature coordinate table (e.g. example_data_peaks.h5) rather than raw mzML; downstream alignment or CCS calibration tools are the right choice instead Data are not multidimensional (no drift time / ion mobility dimension), since DEIMoS's grid-and-multidimensional-algorithm approach offers no advantage over single-dimension processing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Skill for loading mzML(.gz) mass spectrometry files into a common m/z, drift time, retention time, intensity grid as the first DEIMoS processing step, providing the N-dimensional data structure on which all downstream feature detection, alignment, CCS calibration, isotope detection and MS/MS deconvolution operate. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Skill for loading mzML(.gz) mass spectrometry files into a common m/z, drift time, retention time, intensity grid as the first DEIMoS processing step, providing the N-dimensional data structure on which all downstream feature detection, alignment, CCS calibration, isotope detection and MS/MS deconvolution operate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature coordinate table (e.g. example_data_peaks.h5) rather than raw mzML; downstream alignment or CCS calibration tools are the right choice instead Data are not multidimensional (no drift time / ion mobility dimension), since DEIMoS's grid-and-multidimensional-algorithm approach offers no advantage over single-dimension processing

skills.description: Use when raw acquisition output from DDA controllers (full-scan, TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) is available as mzML files and scan counts, precursor events, or inter-scan timing metrics must be extracted before efficiency or timing analysis.
skills.name: mzml-file-parsing
skills.search_text: mzml-file-parsing Use when raw acquisition output from DDA controllers (full-scan, TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) is available as mzML files and scan counts, precursor events, or inter-scan timing metrics must be extracted before efficiency or timing analysis. Input is already an aggregated metrics table (e.g. acquisition_scan_metrics.csv) — no mzML parsing needed Goal is peak picking or fragmentation coverage itself (MZmine2 bounding boxes matched to MS2 precursor events) rather than scan-level extraction Data are not in mzML (e.g. raw vendor formats) and no mzML conversion step is available Parse raw LC-MS/MS acquisition files in mzML format (produced by ViMMS simulations or real instruments via IAPI) to enumerate MS1/MS2 scans, extract precursor and start-time metadata, and derive per-controller acquisition metrics such as scan counts and MS1 scan-plus-processing timings. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Parse raw LC-MS/MS acquisition files in mzML format (produced by ViMMS simulations or real instruments via IAPI) to enumerate MS1/MS2 scans, extract precursor and start-time metadata, and derive per-controller acquisition metrics such as scan counts and MS1 scan-plus-processing timings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated metrics table (e.g. acquisition_scan_metrics.csv) — no mzML parsing needed Goal is peak picking or fragmentation coverage itself (MZmine2 bounding boxes matched to MS2 precursor events) rather than scan-level extraction Data are not in mzML (e.g. raw vendor formats) and no mzML conversion step is available

skills.description: Use when raw HRMS instrument files in mzML format must be extracted against a compound or mass list with configured m/z/RT tolerances and MS1/MS2 intensity thresholds, especially when serial vs parallel wall-clock timing must be compared.
skills.name: mzml-file-processing-pipeline-configuration
skills.search_text: mzml-file-processing-pipeline-configuration Use when raw HRMS instrument files in mzML format must be extracted against a compound or mass list with configured m/z/RT tolerances and MS1/MS2 intensity thresholds, especially when serial vs parallel wall-clock timing must be compared. The data is already a processed feature table (e.g. from xcms or RforMassSpectrometry) rather than raw mzML files requiring extraction The goal is interactive low-level access to individual spectra or peaks without a compound/mass list — low-level packages such as mzR are the article-cited fit for that case Compound identification downstream of prescreening is the goal — use Shinyscreen's MetFrag integration rather than bare extraction configuration Configure and execute Shinyscreen's initialisation → extraction/prescreening pipeline over raw high-resolution MS data in mzML format, setting m/z and retention-time error tolerances, MS1/MS2 intensity thresholds and retention-time shifts, and optionally parallelising the identical extraction run with the R future package. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-01044-x
skills.summary: Configure and execute Shinyscreen's initialisation → extraction/prescreening pipeline over raw high-resolution MS data in mzML format, setting m/z and retention-time error tolerances, MS1/MS2 intensity thresholds and retention-time shifts, and optionally parallelising the identical extraction run with the R future package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is already a processed feature table (e.g. from xcms or RforMassSpectrometry) rather than raw mzML files requiring extraction The goal is interactive low-level access to individual spectra or peaks without a compound/mass list — low-level packages such as mzR are the article-cited fit for that case Compound identification downstream of prescreening is the goal — use Shinyscreen's MetFrag integration rather than bare extraction configuration

skills.search_text: mzml-jcamp-dx-data-interpretation Use when the input is an mzML (MS) file that must be brought into JCAMP-DX form so it can undergo the ChemSpectra standardized processing, editing, and peak-output workflow. Input is already a JCAMP-DX (IR, MS, NMR) file — no non-JCAMP-DX conversion step is needed before processing Input is a proprietary RAW (MS) file and the msConvert (ProteoWizard) docker conversion to mzML has not yet been performed The goal is viewing or analysis of 2D NMR data — the article lists 2D data functions as missing, planned future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Interprets mass spectrometry data held in mzML by leveraging the ChemSpectra chem-spectra-app backend, which converts non-JCAMP-DX files (mzML) to standardized JCAMP-DX using pymzML before any downstream spectral processing. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00481-0
skills.summary: Interprets mass spectrometry data held in mzML by leveraging the ChemSpectra chem-spectra-app backend, which converts non-JCAMP-DX files (mzML) to standardized JCAMP-DX using pymzML before any downstream spectral processing.
