skills.description: Use when you need a synthetic mzML gold-standard for benchmarking MS algorithms, predicting co-elution/co-fragmentation, or simulating runs for arbitrary biomolecules given only chemical formulas.
skills.name: mzml-output-generation
skills.search_text: mzml-output-generation Use when you need a synthetic mzML gold-standard for benchmarking MS algorithms, predicting co-elution/co-fragmentation, or simulating runs for arbitrary biomolecules given only chemical formulas. Input analytes are not representable as chemical formulas, so isotope-pattern-based simulation is impossible The goal is to process or search real experimental spectra rather than create ground-truth simulated data A fragmentation or noise behavior is required that is not implemented and cannot be adapted within SMITER's modular noise/fragmentation interfaces http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generate synthetic LC-MS/MS mzML files with SMITER by building a peak-properties dict from a peptide CSV, choosing a fragmentor and noise injector, and writing the simulated run via smiter.synthetic_mzml.write_mzml. This produces gold-standard datasets where ground truth is known for benchmarking computational MS algorithms. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/genes12030396
skills.summary: Generate synthetic LC-MS/MS mzML files with SMITER by building a peak-properties dict from a peptide CSV, choosing a fragmentor and noise injector, and writing the simulated run via smiter.synthetic_mzml.write_mzml. This produces gold-standard datasets where ground truth is known for benchmarking computational MS algorithms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input analytes are not representable as chemical formulas, so isotope-pattern-based simulation is impossible The goal is to process or search real experimental spectra rather than create ground-truth simulated data A fragmentation or noise behavior is required that is not implemented and cannot be adapted within SMITER's modular noise/fragmentation interfaces

skills.description: Use when you have a profile-mode mzML file from LC-DTIM-MS plus a list of molecular formulae and want to target their predicted ion species for peak picking, isotopologue confirmation, and CCS database entry building.
skills.name: mzml-parsing-for-targeted-lc-im-ms-analysis
skills.search_text: mzml-parsing-for-targeted-lc-im-ms-analysis Use when you have a profile-mode mzML file from LC-DTIM-MS plus a list of molecular formulae and want to target their predicted ion species for peak picking, isotopologue confirmation, and CCS database entry building. Input is centroided rather than profile data mzML, or is not from LC-IM-MS at all — CCSfind is built for drift tube IM-MS profile mzML files You lack the single-field CCS calibration coefficients (Tfix and Beta) or drift gas identity for the data file, which are compulsory inputs You need de novo feature finding across all detectable ions; CCSfind only targets ion species predicted for user-supplied molecular formulae http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Parsing open-source mzML profile data from LC-DTIM-MS runs so that predicted ion species of input molecular formulae can be targeted in a single, unified CCSfind processing step. This is the foundational data-loading step of chemically informed LC-IM-MS database building. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040
skills.summary: Parsing open-source mzML profile data from LC-DTIM-MS runs so that predicted ion species of input molecular formulae can be targeted in a single, unified CCSfind processing step. This is the foundational data-loading step of chemically informed LC-IM-MS database building.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is centroided rather than profile data mzML, or is not from LC-IM-MS at all — CCSfind is built for drift tube IM-MS profile mzML files You lack the single-field CCS calibration coefficients (Tfix and Beta) or drift gas identity for the data file, which are compulsory inputs You need de novo feature finding across all detectable ions; CCSfind only targets ion species predicted for user-supplied molecular formulae

skills.description: Use when parsing mzML files of authentic metabolite standards for in-house RT/m/z library construction and you need to determine and apply a background noise level before extracting adduct EICs.
skills.name: mzml-parsing-noise-filtering
skills.search_text: mzml-parsing-noise-filtering Use when parsing mzML files of authentic metabolite standards for in-house RT/m/z library construction and you need to determine and apply a background noise level before extracting adduct EICs. Input is already a feature table or peak list — noise filtering at the mzML observation level has no raw signal left to threshold. The analysis depends on MS/MS spectra — metScribeR focuses library building on MS1 & RT data and MS2 data is not used or required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Removes MS observations below a user-defined background noise threshold (mzML_parsing_noise_level) when parsing positive- and negative-mode mzML files, so that subsequent adduct EIC construction in metScribeR is not cluttered by low-intensity noise. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Removes MS observations below a user-defined background noise threshold (mzML_parsing_noise_level) when parsing positive- and negative-mode mzML files, so that subsequent adduct EIC construction in metScribeR is not cluttered by low-intensity noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or peak list — noise filtering at the mzML observation level has no raw signal left to threshold. The analysis depends on MS/MS spectra — metScribeR focuses library building on MS1 & RT data and MS2 data is not used or required.

skills.description: Use when vendor .raw files need to be converted to mzML and matched against a .msp library to tabulate internal standard RT, intensity, and mass-accuracy metrics per specimen during QC.
skills.name: mzml-peak-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: mzml-peak-feature-annotation Use when vendor .raw files need to be converted to mzML and matched against a .msp library to tabulate internal standard RT, intensity, and mass-accuracy metrics per specimen during QC. Input is already a processed feature table or mzML — annotation via MSConvert raw conversion is unnecessary The goal is de novo feature detection without a .msp spectral library of internal standard targets Non-Thermo vendor sequences (.raw from Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, Waters) where support is explicitly untested and bugs are expected http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts vendor raw LC-MS/MS files into open mzML format with MSConvert and annotates peaks against a spectral library (.msp) with MS-DIAL, yielding per-specimen internal standard retention time, intensity, and Δm/z metrics for drift monitoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Converts vendor raw LC-MS/MS files into open mzML format with MSConvert and annotates peaks against a spectral library (.msp) with MS-DIAL, yielding per-specimen internal standard retention time, intensity, and Δm/z metrics for drift monitoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or mzML — annotation via MSConvert raw conversion is unnecessary The goal is de novo feature detection without a .msp spectral library of internal standard targets Non-Thermo vendor sequences (.raw from Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, Waters) where support is explicitly untested and bugs are expected

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a tool that parses LC-IM-MS mzML files: you have runtime measurements at multiple file sizes (e.g. 460–1083 MB) or formula counts (e.g. 15–38 s per added formula) and need to verify linear scaling and absolute runtime criteria.
skills.name: mzml-processing-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mzml-processing-runtime-benchmarking Use when benchmarking a tool that parses LC-IM-MS mzML files: you have runtime measurements at multiple file sizes (e.g. 460–1083 MB) or formula counts (e.g. 15–38 s per added formula) and need to verify linear scaling and absolute runtime criteria. The goal is analytical result quality (peak picking, isotopologue matching confirmation, CCS calibration) rather than computational performance characterization The scaling is suspected to be non-linear or the tool processes multiple files in batch, so a single-file linear time-vs-size model would be invalid Input is already a processed feature/result table rather than raw profile mzML data, so no mzML parsing stage exists to benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark and model the computational runtime of mzML-processing tools such as CCSfind by fitting linear regressions of total processing time versus input mzML file size (460–1083 MB) and versus number of targeted molecular formulae, verifying performance claims like sub-2-minute processing of 1 GB files. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040
skills.summary: Benchmark and model the computational runtime of mzML-processing tools such as CCSfind by fitting linear regressions of total processing time versus input mzML file size (460–1083 MB) and versus number of targeted molecular formulae, verifying performance claims like sub-2-minute processing of 1 GB files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is analytical result quality (peak picking, isotopologue matching confirmation, CCS calibration) rather than computational performance characterization The scaling is suspected to be non-linear or the tool processes multiple files in batch, so a single-file linear time-vs-size model would be invalid Input is already a processed feature/result table rather than raw profile mzML data, so no mzML parsing stage exists to benchmark

skills.description: Use when raw LC/GC-HRMS data must be read from vendor-independent mzML files (centroided, DDA/ddMS2) into Python via pyOpenMS as the entry point for feature finding or feature prioritization workflows.
skills.name: mzml-raw-data-parsing
skills.search_text: mzml-raw-data-parsing Use when raw LC/GC-HRMS data must be read from vendor-independent mzML files (centroided, DDA/ddMS2) into Python via pyOpenMS as the entry point for feature finding or feature prioritization workflows. Input is already a processed feature list without the corresponding mzML files — MS2 data would be missing, and data evaluation only works when the mzML files are also provided Raw data are profile-mode or were acquired without data-dependent ddMS2 acquisition — PFΔScreen expects centroided spectra with DDA Data are in a vendor-specific raw format (.d, .raw, etc.) that has not first been converted to mzML via MSConvert http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Loads and parses vendor-independent, centroided mzML raw MS data (data-dependent ddMS2 acquisition) into pyOpenMS so that downstream PFΔScreen feature detection, MS2-to-precursor assignment, and blank correction can operate on MS1 and MS2 spectra from any instrument vendor. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-05070-2
skills.summary: Loads and parses vendor-independent, centroided mzML raw MS data (data-dependent ddMS2 acquisition) into pyOpenMS so that downstream PFΔScreen feature detection, MS2-to-precursor assignment, and blank correction can operate on MS1 and MS2 spectra from any instrument vendor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature list without the corresponding mzML files — MS2 data would be missing, and data evaluation only works when the mzML files are also provided Raw data are profile-mode or were acquired without data-dependent ddMS2 acquisition — PFΔScreen expects centroided spectra with DDA Data are in a vendor-specific raw format (.d, .raw, etc.) that has not first been converted to mzML via MSConvert

skills.name: mzml-scan-event-parsing
skills.search_text: mzml-scan-event-parsing Use when you need to quantify what fraction of picked peaks a DDA controller actually fragmented: i.e. when you have mzML files from TopN injections and peak bounding boxes (min/max RT and m/z) from MZmine2-style peak picking. You only have the picked-peak feature table and no instrument-generated mzML from the controller injection — no MS2 events can be extracted or matched The data are DIA or simulated-only (no real TopN controller injections), since this skill measures coverage of a specific DDA controller's decisions against peak bounding boxes You need spectral identification rather than acquisition-coverage measurement — identification tools like SIRIUS4, CFM-ID or MS2LDA operate on the resulting MS2 spectra, not on scan-event coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses mzML files produced by a TopN DDA controller injection to extract MS2 fragmentation events (with RT and precursor m/z), then matches them against picked-peak bounding boxes to measure DDA coverage and efficiency on samples like serum (QCA) and beer (QCB) extracts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Parses mzML files produced by a TopN DDA controller injection to extract MS2 fragmentation events (with RT and precursor m/z), then matches them against picked-peak bounding boxes to measure DDA coverage and efficiency on samples like serum (QCA) and beer (QCB) extracts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have the picked-peak feature table and no instrument-generated mzML from the controller injection — no MS2 events can be extracted or matched The data are DIA or simulated-only (no real TopN controller injections), since this skill measures coverage of a specific DDA controller's decisions against peak bounding boxes You need spectral identification rather than acquisition-coverage measurement — identification tools like SIRIUS4, CFM-ID or MS2LDA operate on the resulting MS2 spectra, not on scan-event coverage

skills.search_text: mzml-scan-import-parsing Use when starting an HRMS non-targeted analysis from vendor-neutral raw files (.mzML) in Python and you need scan-level metadata (m/z–intensity scans) before chromatographic peak detection with mssmain.peak_pick. skills.summary: Import and parse HRMS raw data in .mzML format into Python-compatible scan metadata using pymzML via the Mass-Suite (MSS) function mssmain.get_scans, with optional baseline subtraction prior to peak picking. skills.summary: Parse mzML files to extract per-scan metadata (MS1 survey scans and MS2 fragmentation events with retention times and precursor m/z) so that downstream DDA-coverage and ion-prioritization analyses in ViMMS/IAPI workflows can operate on acquisition data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a picked-peak bounding-box table or a coverage flag table rather than raw mzML acquisition data The goal is peak picking itself — that is done in MZmine 2 (Supporting Information Table SI-1 parameters) before the parsed MS2 events are matched to boxes The data are not mzML scan-level acquisitions, e.g. structural comparison tasks handled by SIRIUS4/CFM-ID or substructure discovery with MS2LDA

skills.description: Use when raw tandem mass spectra are stored in mzML, mzXML, or MGF files and must be ingested into the npanalysis.org platform as parsed 'Mass Spectrum' data before running VInSMoC search tasks.
skills.name: mzml-spectrum-upload-and-parsing
skills.search_text: mzml-spectrum-upload-and-parsing Use when raw tandem mass spectra are stored in mzML, mzXML, or MGF files and must be ingested into the npanalysis.org platform as parsed 'Mass Spectrum' data before running VInSMoC search tasks. The spectrum has already been uploaded and successfully parsed on the server (skip re-upload and associate it to the project instead). The input is a chemical database rather than a mass spectrum file — databases like NPAtlas are instead made available through the project data table. The file extension does not match the actual data format (e.g. an mzXML payload declared as .mzML); the parse will fail, and the format declaration must be corrected first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Upload an mzML (or MGF/mzXML) mass spectrum file to the run.npanalysis.org server, select 'Mass Spectrum' as the data kind, and wait for the server to parse it into a representation usable by downstream tools such as VInSMoC. This is the prerequisite data-ingestion step before any VInSMoC database search task can be launched. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Upload an mzML (or MGF/mzXML) mass spectrum file to the run.npanalysis.org server, select 'Mass Spectrum' as the data kind, and wait for the server to parse it into a representation usable by downstream tools such as VInSMoC. This is the prerequisite data-ingestion step before any VInSMoC database search task can be launched.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum has already been uploaded and successfully parsed on the server (skip re-upload and associate it to the project instead). The input is a chemical database rather than a mass spectrum file — databases like NPAtlas are instead made available through the project data table. skills.description: Use when retention times of features measured in one lab must be matched to reference compounds annotated in another (e.g. HPLC vs UHPLC), so annotation should rely on m/z plus retention index rather than raw RT.
skills.name: nalkylpyridinium-sulfonate-ri-calibration
skills.search_text: nalkylpyridinium-sulfonate-ri-calibration Use when retention times of features measured in one lab must be matched to reference compounds annotated in another (e.g. HPLC vs UHPLC), so annotation should rely on m/z plus retention index rather than raw RT. skills.description: Use when comparing GPU vs CPU runtimes of the CSCCP dynamic-programming solver across natural-product mixture datasets, or when reproducing the reported ~20.72 s vs 324.16 s runtime at D=5 mass precision.
skills.name: natural-product-dataset-benchmarking
skills.search_text: natural-product-dataset-benchmarking Use when comparing GPU vs CPU runtimes of the CSCCP dynamic-programming solver across natural-product mixture datasets, or when reproducing the reported ~20.72 s vs 324.16 s runtime at D=5 mass precision. The goal is structure elucidation accuracy of unknown mixtures rather than runtime benchmarking — use the full G.A.M.E. prediction workflow instead Mass precision other than D=1–5 is required; the DP algorithm's runtime grows by orders of magnitude as decimal digits increase, so D far above 5 is impractical for the CPU reference No CUDA-capable GPU is available — G.A.M.E.'s acceleration depends on GPU parallelization over w values http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Benchmark the GPU-accelerated DP solver (G.A.M.E.) against the CPU DP reference on four natural-product testing datasets at five decimal digits of mass precision, measuring wall-clock runtimes and computing speed-up factors into a CSV table. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-017-0238-7
skills.summary: Benchmark the GPU-accelerated DP solver (G.A.M.E.) against the CPU DP reference on four natural-product testing datasets at five decimal digits of mass precision, measuring wall-clock runtimes and computing speed-up factors into a CSV table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is structure elucidation accuracy of unknown mixtures rather than runtime benchmarking — use the full G.A.M.E. prediction workflow instead Mass precision other than D=1–5 is required; the DP algorithm's runtime grows by orders of magnitude as decimal digits increase, so D far above 5 is impractical for the CPU reference No CUDA-capable GPU is available — G.A.M.E.'s acceleration depends on GPU parallelization over w values

skills.description: Reference for evaluating NMR-based structure annotation tools on measured natural product HSQC spectra, especially when testing performance under changed solvent conditions (methanol-d4 vs chloroform-d) or comparing against NMRshiftDB shift-search baselines.
skills.name: natural-product-identification-benchmarking
skills.search_text: natural-product-identification-benchmarking Reference for evaluating NMR-based structure annotation tools on measured natural product HSQC spectra, especially when testing performance under changed solvent conditions (methanol-d4 vs chloroform-d) or comparing against NMRshiftDB shift-search baselines. When the query is not an HSQC spectrum but a full 1D proton/carbon NMR spectrum processed by reference-search tools like MetaboMiner or COLMAR — the article reports those achieved under 3% correct identification via NMRshiftDB shift search, so a shift-matching baseline is the wrong frame for DeepSAT-style fingerprint prediction. When the goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than identification of related known compounds or similar-structure retrieval. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Benchmark DeepSAT, a CNN multi-task model trained on 143,467 1H-13C HSQC spectra, for natural product structure identification by scoring predicted Morgan fingerprints, molecular weights, and structure classes against known small molecules using a cosine-score threshold of 0.8, including cross-solvent robustness testing in methanol-d4 vs chloroform-d. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Benchmark DeepSAT, a CNN multi-task model trained on 143,467 1H-13C HSQC spectra, for natural product structure identification by scoring predicted Morgan fingerprints, molecular weights, and structure classes against known small molecules using a cosine-score threshold of 0.8, including cross-solvent robustness testing in methanol-d4 vs chloroform-d.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query is not an HSQC spectrum but a full 1D proton/carbon NMR spectrum processed by reference-search tools like MetaboMiner or COLMAR — the article reports those achieved under 3% correct identification via NMRshiftDB shift search, so a shift-matching baseline is the wrong frame for DeepSAT-style fingerprint prediction. When the goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than identification of related known compounds or similar-structure retrieval.

skills.description: Use when a crude natural product extract (e.g., marine cyanobacterial LC-MS2 data) must be fractionated and you need to decide which fractions to pursue based on MS2 molecular networking, cytotoxicity, and NMR mixture analysis signals.
skills.name: natural-product-isolation-prioritization
skills.search_text: natural-product-isolation-prioritization Use when a crude natural product extract (e.g., marine cyanobacterial LC-MS2 data) must be fractionated and you need to decide which fractions to pursue based on MS2 molecular networking, cytotoxicity, and NMR mixture analysis signals. When the extract is already resolved into a purified compound — this skill targets prioritization of rough fractionation of crude mixtures When no MS2 or cytotoxicity data can be acquired, since prioritization relies on the combination of MS2-based molecular networking, cancer cell cytotoxicity, and SMART 2.0 When the goal is purely computational dereplication of a spectral library without any follow-up isolation work http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Prioritizes and guides fractionation of a crude natural product extract by combining MS2-based molecular networking (GNPS cosine-similarity edges), cancer cell cytotoxicity screening, and NMR-based SMART 2.0, so that isolation effort is concentrated on chemically and biologically interesting fractions. Applied to an environmental Symploca extract this workflow yielded symplocolide A and annotations of swinholide A, samholides A–I, and new derivatives. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jacs.9b13786

Applied to an environmental Symploca extract this workflow yielded symplocolide A and annotations of swinholide A, samholides A–I, and new derivatives.

skills.description: Use when curating a natural products collection that includes predicted NPs from SuperNatural II and you must decide which SuperNatural II-only molecules qualify as genuine or plausible predicted NPs before adding them to the database.
skills.name: natural-product-likeness-score-filtering
skills.search_text: natural-product-likeness-score-filtering Use when curating a natural products collection that includes predicted NPs from SuperNatural II and you must decide which SuperNatural II-only molecules qualify as genuine or plausible predicted NPs before adding them to the database. The molecule already originates from a curated source (e.g. ChEBI NPs, AfroDB, BitterDB) — this additional QC applies only to molecules found exclusively in SuperNatural II You are running the general COCONUT structure QC (heavy-atom size 5–210, connectivity, pseudo-atoms, hydrogens, valences) rather than deciding NP-likeness of SuperNatural II-only entries The goal is removing polyfluorinated compounds (64 total) or structures unparseable by the ChEMBL curation pipeline (113 total) — those are separate filter steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 An OR-based quality-control filter for predicted natural products sourced only from SuperNatural II: molecules must have a strictly positive NP-likeness score, OR an NPclassifier NP classification, OR a sugar moiety to be retained in COCONUT; all others are removed. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00478-9
skills.summary: An OR-based quality-control filter for predicted natural products sourced only from SuperNatural II: molecules must have a strictly positive NP-likeness score, OR an NPclassifier NP classification, OR a sugar moiety to be retained in COCONUT; all others are removed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule already originates from a curated source (e.g. ChEBI NPs, AfroDB, BitterDB) — this additional QC applies only to molecules found exclusively in SuperNatural II You are running the general COCONUT structure QC (heavy-atom size 5–210, connectivity, pseudo-atoms, hydrogens, valences) rather than deciding NP-likeness of SuperNatural II-only entries The goal is removing polyfluorinated compounds (64 total) or structures unparseable by the ChEMBL curation pipeline (113 total) — those are separate filter steps

skills.name: natural-product-msms-data-processing
skills.search_text: natural-product-msms-data-processing Use when given MS/MS spectra of two structurally related natural products (known + unknown analog) with 2D structures, and the goal is to localize the modification site on the known molecule or reproduce benchmark analog-pair analyses. Input is de novo structure elucidation with no structurally related known analog — ModiFinder requires an MS2-known/MS2-unknown pair with a known structure Spectra have unmatched precursor masses or violate benchmark eligibility (precursor > 2000 Da, precursor mass difference > 50%) The goal is compound identification by library matching alone rather than localization of the modification site on a known structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Load and preprocess natural-product MS/MS spectra (e.g., Kirromycin/Goldinodox, Naphthomycin A/B from GNPS/TUEBINGEN libraries), then run ModiFinder's MF-R workflow to localize structural modification sites between compound analog pairs, refining peak-to-fragment maps with domain knowledge. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Load and preprocess natural-product MS/MS spectra (e.g., Kirromycin/Goldinodox, Naphthomycin A/B from GNPS/TUEBINGEN libraries), then run ModiFinder's MF-R workflow to localize structural modification sites between compound analog pairs, refining peak-to-fragment maps with domain knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is de novo structure elucidation with no structurally related known analog — ModiFinder requires an MS2-known/MS2-unknown pair with a known structure Spectra have unmatched precursor masses or violate benchmark eligibility (precursor > 2000 Da, precursor mass difference > 50%) The goal is compound identification by library matching alone rather than localization of the modification site on a known structure

skills.description: Use when query tandem MS/MS spectra from natural-product extracts (e.g., MassIVE deposits of S. roseosporus or Streptomyces sp. DSM5940) must be matched against reference MS/MS library spectra, especially to find analogs whose peaks are shifted by a constant mass delta.
skills.name: natural-product-msms-dereplication
skills.search_text: natural-product-msms-dereplication Use when query tandem MS/MS spectra from natural-product extracts (e.g., MassIVE deposits of S. roseosporus or Streptomyces sp. DSM5940) must be matched against reference MS/MS library spectra, especially to find analogs whose peaks are shifted by a constant mass delta. The goal is clustering and relating unknown spectra with no library analog — molecular networking (MSCluster consensus spectra with mutual top-K neighbor edges) is the appropriate GNPS workflow, not library search Data are raw non-MS/MS or MS1-only, or the library spectra needed are not in any community library (only ~1.01% of spectra in public GNPS datasets matched to third-party reference libraries) An exact, modification-free spectral library search is sufficient and the extra delta edges would only add false analog matches http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Dereplication of natural-product MS/MS spectra by spectral library search in GNPS, including the modification-tolerant 'variable dereplication' mode that adds bipartite matching edges for peak pairs offset by the precursor mass difference delta, enabling detection of putative analogs such as the -41 Da stenothricin analogs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3597
skills.summary: Dereplication of natural-product MS/MS spectra by spectral library search in GNPS, including the modification-tolerant 'variable dereplication' mode that adds bipartite matching edges for peak pairs offset by the precursor mass difference delta, enabling detection of putative analogs such as the -41 Da stenothricin analogs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering and relating unknown spectra with no library analog — molecular networking (MSCluster consensus spectra with mutual top-K neighbor edges) is the appropriate GNPS workflow, not library search Data are raw non-MS/MS or MS1-only, or the library spectra needed are not in any community library (only ~1.01% of spectra in public GNPS datasets matched to third-party reference libraries) An exact, modification-free spectral library search is sufficient and the extra delta edges would only add false analog matches

skills.description: Use when you have 1D NMR spectra of crude extracts, fractions, or purified natural products (e.g., Symploca fractions, cyclic-peptide case-study spectra) and need rapid NP class-level annotation, prioritization, or benchmarking against the 'atomic sort' method.
skills.name: natural-product-nmr-spectral-classification
skills.search_text: natural-product-nmr-spectral-classification Use when you have 1D NMR spectra of crude extracts, fractions, or purified natural products (e.g., Symploca fractions, cyclic-peptide case-study spectra) and need rapid NP class-level annotation, prioritization, or benchmarking against the 'atomic sort' method. skills.description: Use when you have 1H, TOCSY and HSQC spectra for a panel of reference natural products or extract fractions and need to determine which compounds share structural scaffolds versus remain unconnected singletons in a chemical similarity network.
skills.name: natural-product-scaffold-clustering
skills.search_text: natural-product-scaffold-clustering Use when you have 1H, TOCSY and HSQC spectra for a panel of reference natural products or extract fractions and need to determine which compounds share structural scaffolds versus remain unconnected singletons in a chemical similarity network. Compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals — sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes — are precluded from analysis by the shielded-quadrant exclusion You have a single spectrum with no panel to compare against; MADByTE's network formation requires matching spin system features between multiple samples The goal is dereplication against a known-compound library rather than unsupervised scaffold grouping; use MADByTE's dereplication module instead of relying on network clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Clusters structurally related natural product compounds into sub-networks by matching TOCSY/HSQC spin system features across a sample panel with MADByTE, then visualizing the chemical similarity network in Gephi (Force Atlas 2) to verify scaffold groupings and singletons. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Clusters structurally related natural product compounds into sub-networks by matching TOCSY/HSQC spin system features across a sample panel with MADByTE, then visualizing the chemical similarity network in Gephi (Force Atlas 2) to verify scaffold groupings and singletons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals — sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes — are precluded from analysis by the shielded-quadrant exclusion You have a single spectrum with no panel to compare against; MADByTE's network formation requires matching spin system features between multiple samples The goal is dereplication against a known-compound library rather than unsupervised scaffold grouping; use MADByTE's dereplication module instead of relying on network clustering

skills.search_text: natural-product-structure-annotation Use when molecular networking or analog library search (GNPS) surfaces an unknown MS/MS spectrum with a structurally related library hit, and the modification site on the known structure must be localized to annotate the new natural product. No structurally related known compound (library hit or analog) exists for the unknown — ModiFinder requires a known reference structure for spectral alignment The goal is de novo molecular formula or structure elucidation from fragmentation trees alone (use SIRIUS directly) rather than localizing a modification between two related structures The unknown and known differ by more than the benchmark-supported regime (precursor mass > 2000 Da or precursor mass difference > 50%) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Localize the structural modification site of an unknown natural product analog relative to a known library hit by aligning their MS/MS spectra with ModiFinder, which scores the likelihood of each atom in the known molecule as the modification site. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061

skills.description: Use when you have SMILES strings for natural products (e.g. NP Atlas entries tagged bacterial vs fungal) and need pathway/superclass/class labels to aggregate counts or compare biosynthetic distributions across organism groups.
skills.name: natural-product-structure-classification
skills.search_text: natural-product-structure-classification Use when you have SMILES strings for natural products (e.g. NP Atlas entries tagged bacterial vs fungal) and need pathway/superclass/class labels to aggregate counts or compare biosynthetic distributions across organism groups. The input is not a chemical structure (no SMILES) — NPClassifier requires a counted Morgan fingerprint derived from a SMILES string and cannot classify textual organism or activity metadata directly. You need consistent cross-platform chemical ontology classes for compounds outside natural product space — the article benchmarked against ClassyFire using Dictionary of Natural Products classes, and NPClassifier's ontology is natural-product specific. You cannot run docker/docker-compose or install tensorflow 2.3.0 — model conversion to HDF5 TF2 and the serving stack depend on those exact versions per the README. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classify natural product structures hierarchically (Pathway, Superclass, Class) from SMILES using NPClassifier's three feed-forward DNNs over counted Morgan fingerprints, served locally via a dockerized TensorFlow-Serving API. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.1c00399
skills.summary: Classify natural product structures hierarchically (Pathway, Superclass, Class) from SMILES using NPClassifier's three feed-forward DNNs over counted Morgan fingerprints, served locally via a dockerized TensorFlow-Serving API.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a chemical structure (no SMILES) — NPClassifier requires a counted Morgan fingerprint derived from a SMILES string and cannot classify textual organism or activity metadata directly. You need consistent cross-platform chemical ontology classes for compounds outside natural product space — the article benchmarked against ClassyFire using Dictionary of Natural Products classes, and NPClassifier's ontology is natural-product specific. You cannot run docker/docker-compose or install tensorflow 2.3.0 — model conversion to HDF5 TF2 and the serving stack depend on those exact versions per the README.

skills.search_text: natural-product-structure-comparison Use when you have antiSMASH annotations of PKS, NRPS, or NRPS/PKS hybrid BGCs and need to validate RAIChU-predicted product structures against characterised natural product structures, classifying any mismatches. You need automatic fingerprinting-based validation across all MIBiG BGCs — the article notes fingerprinting was considered but not implemented and that RAIChU generates scaffolds, not mature natural products, so predicted and real-world structures may not show high fingerprinting similarity Your BGCs are RiPP, terpene, or other classes outside the cis-AT PKS/NRPS/hybrid modular scope of this comparison workflow Regio- and stereochemistry of tailoring enzymes must be predicted automatically — RAIChU requires users to specify reaction targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Compares RAIChU-rendered biosynthetic product structures against experimentally characterised natural products (SMILES from MIBiG, PubChem, or NP Atlas) to identify and classify discrepancies between predicted and real-world biosynthetic scaffolds. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00898-x

skills.search_text: natural-product-structure-informatics Use when you need ground-truth linkages between gene clusters and MS2 spectra for evaluating linking algorithms, and both MIBiG BGC annotations and GNPS library InChIKeys are available but the two databases contain no direct cross-references. MS2 spectra or reference annotations already contain full stereochemical InChIKeys with a reliable link table — first-block truncation would needlessly discard chirality information The goal is scoring candidate GCF–molecular-family links (e.g. metcalf scoring via npl.get_links), not constructing the ground-truth pair table itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Builds a validated set of known BGC–spectrum pairs by joining MIBiG 2.0 biosynthetic gene cluster metadata (compound names and InChIKeys) against GNPS library spectrum annotations, using first-block InChIKey matching so stereoisomers collapse onto the same chemical skeleton. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Builds a validated set of known BGC–spectrum pairs by joining MIBiG 2.0 biosynthetic gene cluster metadata (compound names and InChIKeys) against GNPS library spectrum annotations, using first-block InChIKey matching so stereoisomers collapse onto the same chemical skeleton.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MS2 spectra or reference annotations already contain full stereochemical InChIKeys with a reliable link table — first-block truncation would needlessly discard chirality information The goal is scoring candidate GCF–molecular-family links (e.g. metcalf scoring via npl.get_links), not constructing the ground-truth pair table itself

skills.description: Use when benchmarking or running spectral library searches against natural product structures and you must merge community structure databases (DNP, GNPS) into one searchable reference set with ground-truth annotations.
skills.name: natural-product-structure-library-curation
skills.search_text: natural-product-structure-library-curation Use when benchmarking or running spectral library searches against natural product structures and you must merge community structure databases (DNP, GNPS) into one searchable reference set with ground-truth annotations. Input is already a single well-defined community database such as PubChem (83M compounds) and no benchmark ground truth is needed - this skill is specifically for merging curated natural product sources with known annotations. You are dereplicating purely peptidic natural products with DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest on a single-structure-source database rather than building a merged multi-class reference set. The target metabolites fall outside natural product classes (polyketides, terpenes, benzenoids, alkaloids, flavonoids, etc.) covered by these community databases. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Build a combined reference library of known natural product chemical structures (e.g. DNP plus GNPS library structures, ~86,665 compounds) so dereplication searches can match MS/MS spectra against candidate metabolites across multiple chemical classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-018-06082-8
skills.summary: Build a combined reference library of known natural product chemical structures (e.g. DNP plus GNPS library structures, ~86,665 compounds) so dereplication searches can match MS/MS spectra against candidate metabolites across multiple chemical classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single well-defined community database such as PubChem (83M compounds) and no benchmark ground truth is needed - this skill is specifically for merging curated natural product sources with known annotations. You are dereplicating purely peptidic natural products with DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest on a single-structure-source database rather than building a merged multi-class reference set. The target metabolites fall outside natural product classes (polyketides, terpenes, benzenoids, alkaloids, flavonoids, etc.) covered by these community databases.

skills.description: Use when annotated MIBiG BGC entries need cross-references to chemical structure/spectral databases (Natural Products Atlas, GNPS, PubChem) based on matching compound names and structures.
skills.name: natural-products-atlas-identifier-matching
skills.search_text: natural-products-atlas-identifier-matching Use when annotated MIBiG BGC entries need cross-references to chemical structure/spectral databases (Natural Products Atlas, GNPS, PubChem) based on matching compound names and structures. The task is de novo identification of compounds from spectra or sequences — this skill only cross-references already-annotated MIBiG compound names/structures against existing databases. The target clusters are unannotated candidate BGCs (e.g. from IMG-ABC or antiSMASH-DB) without compound name or structure fields to match on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Matches compound names and chemical structures annotated in MIBiG BGC records against the Natural Products Atlas (with GNPS and PubChem as companion targets) to establish cross-links and produce a per-entry linkage inventory. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz882
skills.summary: Matches compound names and chemical structures annotated in MIBiG BGC records against the Natural Products Atlas (with GNPS and PubChem as companion targets) to establish cross-links and produce a per-entry linkage inventory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is de novo identification of compounds from spectra or sequences — this skill only cross-references already-annotated MIBiG compound names/structures against existing databases. The target clusters are unannotated candidate BGCs (e.g. from IMG-ABC or antiSMASH-DB) without compound name or structure fields to match on.

skills.description: Use when filtered MS/MS spectra ([M+H]+ adducts, >=6 fragments, 500 most intense peaks, parent masses 100-1,500 Da) from specialized metabolites need annotation against a natural products structural database before any taxonomic re-ranking.
skills.name: natural-products-database-dereplication
skills.search_text: natural-products-database-dereplication Use when filtered MS/MS spectra ([M+H]+ adducts, >=6 fragments, 500 most intense peaks, parent masses 100-1,500 Da) from specialized metabolites need annotation against a natural products structural database before any taxonomic re-ranking. When the goal is to re-rank or score existing candidate annotations using organism taxonomy - use the taxonomically informed scoring step (taxo_scorer) instead of a fresh database lookup When the benchmark aim is a fair cross-tool comparison, since all compounds in the benchmarking dataset are present in the DNP and ISDB-DNP is by definition backed by the same DB and thus favored When spectra target ubiquitous/primary metabolites rather than specialized metabolites, which is the scope the ISDB-DNP database and taxonomic scoring are designed for http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Dereplication of MS/MS spectra from natural product extracts by querying them against a specialized-metabolite spectral library such as ISDB-DNP (backed by the Dictionary of Natural Products v 27.1), producing ranked candidate annotations whose rank-1 correctness can be evaluated against reference identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Dereplication of MS/MS spectra from natural product extracts by querying them against a specialized-metabolite spectral library such as ISDB-DNP (backed by the Dictionary of Natural Products v 27.1), producing ranked candidate annotations whose rank-1 correctness can be evaluated against reference identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to re-rank or score existing candidate annotations using organism taxonomy - use the taxonomically informed scoring step (taxo_scorer) instead of a fresh database lookup When the benchmark aim is a fair cross-tool comparison, since all compounds in the benchmarking dataset are present in the DNP and ISDB-DNP is by definition backed by the same DB and thus favored When spectra target ubiquitous/primary metabolites rather than specialized metabolites, which is the scope the ISDB-DNP database and taxonomic scoring are designed for

skills.description: Use when merging structure-organism pair records from multiple NP electronic resources (e.g. KNApSAcK, NAPRALERT, NPAtlas, PubChem, GBIF) and you need standardized chemical, biological and reference levels plus validated retention before open release.
skills.name: natural-products-database-harmonization
skills.search_text: natural-products-database-harmonization Use when merging structure-organism pair records from multiple NP electronic resources (e.g. KNApSAcK, NAPRALERT, NPAtlas, PubChem, GBIF) and you need standardized chemical, biological and reference levels plus validated retention before open release. The input is a single already-curated NP database that does not need cross-source harmonization or validation filtering. The goal is structural or spectral searching over the dataset rather than curation — Wikidata hosting does not provide these search modes; use the parallel lotus-web hosting instead. The candidate resources are commercial or not publicly disseminable (e.g. DNP, FooDB), which LOTUS used only for comparison/curation, not as open harmonization input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates and harmonizes structure-organism occurrence pairs from 40+ heterogeneous natural product (NP) electronic resources into a standardized, validated open dataset, following the LOTUS three-stage curation pipeline (harmonization, processing, validation) and dissemination via Wikidata. It converts scattered, inconsistent NP records into a FAIR/TRUST-compliant resource released under CC0. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Aggregates and harmonizes structure-organism occurrence pairs from 40+ heterogeneous natural product (NP) electronic resources into a standardized, validated open dataset, following the LOTUS three-stage curation pipeline (harmonization, processing, validation) and dissemination via Wikidata. It converts scattered, inconsistent NP records into a FAIR/TRUST-compliant resource released under CC0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single already-curated NP database that does not need cross-source harmonization or validation filtering. The goal is structural or spectral searching over the dataset rather than curation — Wikidata hosting does not provide these search modes; use the parallel lotus-web hosting instead. The candidate resources are commercial or not publicly disseminable (e.g. DNP, FooDB), which LOTUS used only for comparison/curation, not as open harmonization input.

skills.description: Use when a published database paper reports aggregate counts (e.g. retained structure-organism pairs, unique structures, organisms) and the deposited dataset (Zenodo deposit, TSV table) is available to reproduce them.
skills.name: natural-products-database-quality-verification
skills.search_text: natural-products-database-quality-verification Use when a published database paper reports aggregate counts (e.g. retained structure-organism pairs, unique structures, organisms) and the deposited dataset (Zenodo deposit, TSV table) is available to reproduce them. The goal is to re-run the LOTUS processing/filtering pipeline itself (filter_dirty.R, MolVS sanitization) rather than verify counts on an already-curated table The deposited table is raw/uncurated, so counts would not correspond to the paper's reported curated totals The claim to verify is not a countable aggregate (e.g. qualitative validation rules or translation-quality judgments), which require manual expert review instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3489 Verifies reported quality/coverage figures of a curated natural-products database by independently recomputing record counts from the deposited dataset table, as done for LOTUS's 750,000+ referenced structure-organism pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Verifies reported quality/coverage figures of a curated natural-products database by independently recomputing record counts from the deposited dataset table, as done for LOTUS's 750,000+ referenced structure-organism pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to re-run the LOTUS processing/filtering pipeline itself (filter_dirty.R, MolVS sanitization) rather than verify counts on an already-curated table The deposited table is raw/uncurated, so counts would not correspond to the paper's reported curated totals The claim to verify is not a countable aggregate (e.g. qualitative validation rules or translation-quality judgments), which require manual expert review instead

skills.description: Use when a research question requires counts or inventories of reported natural products per taxon (family/genus/species) from a structured NP database dump, or when chemical-class coverage of a clade must be benchmarked against a larger kingdom-wide set.
skills.name: natural-products-database-querying
skills.search_text: natural-products-database-querying Use when a research question requires counts or inventories of reported natural products per taxon (family/genus/species) from a structured NP database dump, or when chemical-class coverage of a clade must be benchmarked against a larger kingdom-wide set. The goal is prioritizing extracts for novelty from untargeted MS data (use Inventa's FC/LC/CC/SC scoring instead of a database census) The database does not provide organism taxonomy or chemical ontology columns, so family-level filtering and NPClassifier class mapping cannot be performed Only literature-reported compounds per single species are needed for Inventa's Literature Component, not a database-wide clade census http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Queries curated natural-product databases such as LOTUS to extract compound–organism pairs, then filters them by taxonomic rank (e.g. family=Celastraceae), deduplicates compounds by canonical structure identifiers (SMILES/InChI), and aggregates chemotaxonomic censuses of unique NPs, genera, species, and NPClassifier chemical classes. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Queries curated natural-product databases such as LOTUS to extract compound–organism pairs, then filters them by taxonomic rank (e.g. family=Celastraceae), deduplicates compounds by canonical structure identifiers (SMILES/InChI), and aggregates chemotaxonomic censuses of unique NPs, genera, species, and NPClassifier chemical classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is prioritizing extracts for novelty from untargeted MS data (use Inventa's FC/LC/CC/SC scoring instead of a database census) The database does not provide organism taxonomy or chemical ontology columns, so family-level filtering and NPClassifier class mapping cannot be performed Only literature-reported compounds per single species are needed for Inventa's Literature Component, not a database-wide clade census

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or audit COCONUT's dataset statistics for a specific release — i.e., reconstruct Table 1 per-source counts and verify them against reported totals of unique flat and stereochemistry-preserving NPs.
skills.name: natural-products-source-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: natural-products-source-count-aggregation Use when you need to reproduce or audit COCONUT's dataset statistics for a specific release — i.e., reconstruct Table 1 per-source counts and verify them against reported totals of unique flat and stereochemistry-preserving NPs. The target release is not the October 2020 COCONUT release — later releases have different provenance (e.g., 63 sources as of September 2024) and different totals (695,133 molecules with 89,593 non-stereo and 555,897 stereo), so Oct-2020 reference totals will not reconcile The goal is per-molecule provenance tracing (which source/organism a specific NP came from) rather than aggregate per-source counts The source datasets still need structure curation or quality control (e.g., removal of the 24,880 SuperNatural II molecules, 64 polyfluorinated compounds, or 113 unparsable structures) — this skill assumes post-curation counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs COCONUT's provenance accounting by assembling the per-source entry counts of its public datasets (e.g., AfroDB 874, BitterDB 625, ChEBI NPs 14,603) plus manual literature selections into a single table, and reconciles the summed totals against the release-level unique counts obtained by merging duplicates via stereo-less InChIKey. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00478-9
skills.summary: Reconstructs COCONUT's provenance accounting by assembling the per-source entry counts of its public datasets (e.g., AfroDB 874, BitterDB 625, ChEBI NPs 14,603) plus manual literature selections into a single table, and reconciles the summed totals against the release-level unique counts obtained by merging duplicates via stereo-less InChIKey.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target release is not the October 2020 COCONUT release — later releases have different provenance (e.g., 63 sources as of September 2024) and different totals (695,133 molecules with 89,593 non-stereo and 555,897 stereo), so Oct-2020 reference totals will not reconcile The goal is per-molecule provenance tracing (which source/organism a specific NP came from) rather than aggregate per-source counts The source datasets still need structure curation or quality control (e.g., removal of the 24,880 SuperNatural II molecules, 64 polyfluorinated compounds, or 113 unparsable structures) — this skill assumes post-curation counts

skills.description: Use when you need predicted 1H chemical shifts for a batch of known natural product structures (e.g. Natural Products Atlas SMILES/MOL files) to compute shielded/deshielded signal statistics or build an in silico reference spectral library.
skills.name: natural-products-structure-dataset-processing
skills.search_text: natural-products-structure-dataset-processing Use when you need predicted 1H chemical shifts for a batch of known natural product structures (e.g. Natural Products Atlas SMILES/MOL files) to compute shielded/deshielded signal statistics or build an in silico reference spectral library. When only experimental NMR spectra (raw FID/processed 1D or 2D data) are available and no structures need in silico prediction When the goal is dereplicating compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes), which are precluded from analysis by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Predicts in silico 1H NMR spectra for a large natural product structure set (e.g. 27,844 microbial NPAtlas compounds) using the stereo-aware HOSE code model from NMRShiftDB2, then tallies shielded vs deshielded signal fractions to characterize the chemical-shift coverage of a dereplication library. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Predicts in silico 1H NMR spectra for a large natural product structure set (e.g. 27,844 microbial NPAtlas compounds) using the stereo-aware HOSE code model from NMRShiftDB2, then tallies shielded vs deshielded signal fractions to characterize the chemical-shift coverage of a dereplication library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only experimental NMR spectra (raw FID/processed 1D or 2D data) are available and no structures need in silico prediction When the goal is dereplicating compound classes with exclusively shielded 1H signals (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes), which are precluded from analysis by design

skills.description: Use when MINNO or a similar flux-based workflow flags reactions as absent from the KEGG database and each candidate must be classified as literature-supported or RefSeq-homology-supported before being added to the network.
skills.name: ncbi-refseq-homology-verification
skills.search_text: ncbi-refseq-homology-verification Use when MINNO or a similar flux-based workflow flags reactions as absent from the KEGG database and each candidate must be classified as literature-supported or RefSeq-homology-supported before being added to the network. The reaction is already present in the KEGG base network that MINNO loads — no verification is needed because it is annotated, not inferred. The goal is de novo pathway reconstruction from raw sequencing reads rather than triage of a small set of flux-inferred candidate reactions. Neither literature nor RefSeq homology is available for the organism in question; the reaction remains unverified and should be flagged as hypothetical rather than forced into either category. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Verify that metabolic reactions inferred as missing from a KEGG-derived network (e.g. via MINNO boundary-flux analysis) are supported by primary literature or by homology to annotated genes in the NCBI-RefSeq database, producing a categorized table of evidence sources for each reaction. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Verify that metabolic reactions inferred as missing from a KEGG-derived network (e.g. via MINNO boundary-flux analysis) are supported by primary literature or by homology to annotated genes in the NCBI-RefSeq database, producing a categorized table of evidence sources for each reaction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reaction is already present in the KEGG base network that MINNO loads — no verification is needed because it is annotated, not inferred. The goal is de novo pathway reconstruction from raw sequencing reads rather than triage of a small set of flux-inferred candidate reactions. Neither literature nor RefSeq homology is available for the organism in question; the reaction remains unverified and should be flagged as hypothetical rather than forced into either category.

skills.description: Use when a CAMI-format taxonomic profile contains taxIDs that must be attached to an NCBI taxonomy tree (e.g., to annotate nodes with percentage abundances or emit a Newick tree for downstream plotting).
skills.name: ncbi-taxonomy-resolution
skills.search_text: ncbi-taxonomy-resolution Use when a CAMI-format taxonomic profile contains taxIDs that must be attached to an NCBI taxonomy tree (e.g., to annotate nodes with percentage abundances or emit a Newick tree for downstream plotting). Input is an amplicon dataset — metacoder-style tools, not TAMPA's NCBI taxdump resolution, are the article's stated wrong fit, and TAMPA is not designed for amplicon data You only need a single-value benchmarking metric (e.g., F1 score or UniFrac) — taxonomy-tree construction is unnecessary No NCBI taxdump database is available and none can be supplied via -d, since taxa cannot be attached without it http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Resolves taxIDs from a CAMI-format taxonomic profile against the NCBI taxdump database using the ete3 toolkit's NCBI taxonomy interface, so that per-taxon percentage abundances can be placed on the correct nodes of the taxonomy tree used by TAMPA for visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Resolves taxIDs from a CAMI-format taxonomic profile against the NCBI taxdump database using the ete3 toolkit's NCBI taxonomy interface, so that per-taxon percentage abundances can be placed on the correct nodes of the taxonomy tree used by TAMPA for visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an amplicon dataset — metacoder-style tools, not TAMPA's NCBI taxdump resolution, are the article's stated wrong fit, and TAMPA is not designed for amplicon data You only need a single-value benchmarking metric (e.g., F1 score or UniFrac) — taxonomy-tree construction is unnecessary No NCBI taxdump database is available and none can be supplied via -d, since taxa cannot be attached without it

skills.description: Use when curating or benchmarking an MS/MS spectral library (e.g. an MGF file) and you need to quantify or remove spectra that are near-duplicates of another spectrum of the same compound, as a data-quality or train/test-leakage check.
skills.name: near-duplicate-spectra-detection
skills.search_text: near-duplicate-spectra-detection Use when curating or benchmarking an MS/MS spectral library (e.g. an MGF file) and you need to quantify or remove spectra that are near-duplicates of another spectrum of the same compound, as a data-quality or train/test-leakage check. Input spectra lack InChIKey annotations or ion-polarity metadata, so same-compound groups cannot be formed. You need de-duplication for Spectraverse itself; the article only reports near-duplicate removal counts in comparison to MassSpecGym and does not state completeness of de-duplication for Spectraverse. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Detects near-duplicate MS/MS spectra by grouping spectra from the same compound (first 14 InChIKey characters plus ion polarity) and flagging pairs with cosine similarity ≥ 0.99 using the SpectralEntropy cosine implementation, as used to quantify the 77,774 near-duplicate spectra in MassSpecGym. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06256
skills.summary: Detects near-duplicate MS/MS spectra by grouping spectra from the same compound (first 14 InChIKey characters plus ion polarity) and flagging pairs with cosine similarity ≥ 0.99 using the SpectralEntropy cosine implementation, as used to quantify the 77,774 near-duplicate spectra in MassSpecGym.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack InChIKey annotations or ion-polarity metadata, so same-compound groups cannot be formed. You need de-duplication for Spectraverse itself; the article only reports near-duplicate removal counts in comparison to MassSpecGym and does not state completeness of de-duplication for Spectraverse.

skills.description: Use when a trained protein/domain embedding must be validated for functional coherence, e.g. checking that pfam2vec vectors place domains with related Pfam descriptions close together in cosine space.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-description-similarity-analysis
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-description-similarity-analysis Use when a trained protein/domain embedding must be validated for functional coherence, e.g. checking that pfam2vec vectors place domains with related Pfam descriptions close together in cosine space. The embedding has not yet been trained — validate clustering (intra-clan cosine similarity, MIBiG t-SNE) only after pfam2vec vectors exist The goal is BGC detection in a genome rather than embedding validation — use the deepbgc pipeline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Validates a learned domain-embedding (pfam2vec) by retrieving each Pfam domain's nearest neighbors in the 100-dimensional embedding space and checking that neighbors share functional description terms, providing evidence the embedding captures biological meaning. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz654
skills.summary: Validates a learned domain-embedding (pfam2vec) by retrieving each Pfam domain's nearest neighbors in the 100-dimensional embedding space and checking that neighbors share functional description terms, providing evidence the embedding captures biological meaning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The embedding has not yet been trained — validate clustering (intra-clan cosine similarity, MIBiG t-SNE) only after pfam2vec vectors exist The goal is BGC detection in a genome rather than embedding validation — use the deepbgc pipeline instead

skills.description: Use when freetext sample metadata strings must be coerced into a fixed, pre-determined vocabulary via synonym matching and typographical fixing, e.g. curating metabolomics metadata headers.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-freetext-term-mapping
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-freetext-term-mapping Use when freetext sample metadata strings must be coerced into a fixed, pre-determined vocabulary via synonym matching and typographical fixing, e.g. curating metabolomics metadata headers. When metadata strings already conform to the constrained vocabulary and need no term mapping When the target vocabularies differ from MeSH, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus, NCIT or FDA and cannot be built by the SMetaS vocabulary-generation pipeline Maps user-submitted freetext sample metadata strings onto constrained vocabulary terms (MeSH, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus, NCIT, FDA) using a character-trigram tf-idf vector space and nearest-neighbors matching, as implemented in SMetaS for metabolomics metadata standardization. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941
skills.summary: Maps user-submitted freetext sample metadata strings onto constrained vocabulary terms (MeSH, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus, NCIT, FDA) using a character-trigram tf-idf vector space and nearest-neighbors matching, as implemented in SMetaS for metabolomics metadata standardization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When metadata strings already conform to the constrained vocabulary and need no term mapping When the target vocabularies differ from MeSH, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus, NCIT or FDA and cannot be built by the SMetaS vocabulary-generation pipeline

skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-outlier-alignment Use when two adjacent spatial sections (e.g. 10X Visium spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI) have already undergone manual gross and ICP alignment, but residual spot-to-spot distances must be minimized before feature-based integration. When the sections have not yet undergone gross affine and ICP alignment — direct_alignment is the third stage of haCCA's modified morphological alignment pipeline, applied to (_a, _b_prime) When modalities other than spatial transcriptome and spatial metabolome data are involved — the article notes only these two have been used so far haCCA's direct_alignment step: after gross affine and ICP-based registration, it further aligns a MALDI-MSI section to a spatial transcriptome section by minimizing the distances between outlier spots lacking a MSI neighbor and their nearest-neighbor spots, yielding spot-to-spot aligned data (b_predict). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
