skills.when_to_use_negative: When the sections have not yet undergone gross affine and ICP alignment — direct_alignment is the third stage of haCCA's modified morphological alignment pipeline, applied to (_a, _b_prime) When modalities other than spatial transcriptome and spatial metabolome data are involved — the article notes only these two have been used so far

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether ANN indexing (feature hashing + Voronoi inverted index) avoids exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison at scale, e.g. on millions of MS/MS spectra from proteomics PRIDE datasets.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-search-comparison-profiling
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-search-comparison-profiling Use when benchmarking whether ANN indexing (feature hashing + Voronoi inverted index) avoids exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison at scale, e.g. on millions of MS/MS spectra from proteomics PRIDE datasets. When the goal is clustering quality assessment rather than profiling the computational cost of nearest neighbor searching (use falcon_notebooks' tool-comparison notebooks instead). When clustering metabolomics or top-down data: falcon's default preprocessing (min_peaks 5, min_mz_range 250 m/z, min_mz 101, max_mz 500 m/z) must first be adjusted, invalidating cost comparability with the proteomics benchmark. When the dataset is too small for ANN to matter — exhaustive pairwise comparison within the precursor tolerance may be feasible and the ~47 comparisons/spectrum benchmark would not be meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Profiles the computational cost of falcon's approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searching by instrumenting a clustering run to count spectrum–spectrum comparisons per spectrum, contrasting it with exhaustive pairwise comparison within the 20 ppm precursor tolerance and with msCRUSH's runtime as a baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Profiles the computational cost of falcon's approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searching by instrumenting a clustering run to count spectrum–spectrum comparisons per spectrum, contrasting it with exhaustive pairwise comparison within the 20 ppm precursor tolerance and with msCRUSH's runtime as a baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is clustering quality assessment rather than profiling the computational cost of nearest neighbor searching (use falcon_notebooks' tool-comparison notebooks instead). When clustering metabolomics or top-down data: falcon's default preprocessing (min_peaks 5, min_mz_range 250 m/z, min_mz 101, max_mz 500 m/z) must first be adjusted, invalidating cost comparability with the proteomics benchmark. When the dataset is too small for ANN to matter — exhaustive pairwise comparison within the precursor tolerance may be feasible and the ~47 comparisons/spectrum benchmark would not be meaningful.

skills.description: Use when clustering very large tandem MS/MS datasets (e.g. 25 million spectra from a human draft proteome) where exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison is quadratically expensive and an approximate sparse distance matrix suffices.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-spectrum-similarity-searching
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-spectrum-similarity-searching Use when clustering very large tandem MS/MS datasets (e.g. 25 million spectra from a human draft proteome) where exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison is quadratically expensive and an approximate sparse distance matrix suffices. When the dataset is small enough that exhaustive pairwise comparison is tractable and exact similarities are required, since approximate nearest neighbor searching can slightly miss neighbors When data are metabolomics or top-down spectra, because default preprocessing (min_peaks 5, min_mz 101, max_mz 500, mass range 250 Da) is intended for bottom-up proteomics and would discard valid spectra When a similarity measure other than cosine distance is needed (e.g. probabilistic scores or fragment rarity metrics), as the hashing and inverted index conserves cosine similarity specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Efficiently computes spectrum similarities for millions of MS/MS spectra by converting high-resolution spectra to low-dimensional vectors via feature hashing, building nearest neighbor indexes (Voronoi diagram inverted indexes), and computing a sparse pairwise cosine distance matrix instead of exhaustive pairwise comparisons, as implemented in falcon. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Efficiently computes spectrum similarities for millions of MS/MS spectra by converting high-resolution spectra to low-dimensional vectors via feature hashing, building nearest neighbor indexes (Voronoi diagram inverted indexes), and computing a sparse pairwise cosine distance matrix instead of exhaustive pairwise comparisons, as implemented in falcon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset is small enough that exhaustive pairwise comparison is tractable and exact similarities are required, since approximate nearest neighbor searching can slightly miss neighbors When data are metabolomics or top-down spectra, because default preprocessing (min_peaks 5, min_mz 101, max_mz 500, mass range 250 Da) is intended for bottom-up proteomics and would discard valid spectra When a similarity measure other than cosine distance is needed (e.g. probabilistic scores or fragment rarity metrics), as the hashing and inverted index conserves cosine similarity specifically

skills.description: Use when an empirical M-by-M pairwise distance-correlation matrix of metabolite features must be made non-negative-definite before eigen-analysis-based effective-number-of-tests (Meff) correction in a MWAS multiple-testing pipeline.
skills.name: nearest-spd-matrix-projection
skills.search_text: nearest-spd-matrix-projection Use when an empirical M-by-M pairwise distance-correlation matrix of metabolite features must be made non-negative-definite before eigen-analysis-based effective-number-of-tests (Meff) correction in a MWAS multiple-testing pipeline. The input matrix is already verified non-negative definite (e.g., a Pearson correlation matrix known to be PSD) — projection would be redundant The downstream correction does not rely on eigen-analysis of the correlation matrix, so PSD-ness is not required The input is a raw samples-by-metabolites feature table rather than a square pairwise distance-correlation matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Projects an empirical distance-correlation (DisCo) matrix onto the nearest non-negative-definite matrix in the Frobenius norm using the MATLAB nearestSPD() routine, so that eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation in the DisCo P-ad pipeline is mathematically valid. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Projects an empirical distance-correlation (DisCo) matrix onto the nearest non-negative-definite matrix in the Frobenius norm using the MATLAB nearestSPD() routine, so that eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation in the DisCo P-ad pipeline is mathematically valid.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already verified non-negative definite (e.g., a Pearson correlation matrix known to be PSD) — projection would be redundant The downstream correction does not rely on eigen-analysis of the correlation matrix, so PSD-ness is not required The input is a raw samples-by-metabolites feature table rather than a square pairwise distance-correlation matrix

skills.description: Use when you have a NEF-format constraint file (deposited chemical shifts, distance/dihedral restraints) for a protein or nucleic acid and need to run or reproduce an NMR structure calculation in NMRFx without a pre-existing project.
skills.name: nef-constraint-file-processing
skills.search_text: nef-constraint-file-processing Use when you have a NEF-format constraint file (deposited chemical shifts, distance/dihedral restraints) for a protein or nucleic acid and need to run or reproduce an NMR structure calculation in NMRFx without a pre-existing project. You already have an NMRFx (or NMRViewJ) project with constraints loaded and simply want interactive peak picking, assignment, or chemical shift prediction rather than a batch structure calculation. You only need spectrum processing (FID to processed NUS/non-NUS spectra); the NEF batch route addresses structure calculation, not data processing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_1317 Load NMR constraint data in NEF (NMR Exchange Format) files into NMRFx's batch structure-calculation engine, so that torsion-angle geometry can be generated from deposited chemical shifts, NOEs, J-couplings, RDCs and other restraints rather than from native NMRFx project files. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-025-01812-8
skills.summary: Load NMR constraint data in NEF (NMR Exchange Format) files into NMRFx's batch structure-calculation engine, so that torsion-angle geometry can be generated from deposited chemical shifts, NOEs, J-couplings, RDCs and other restraints rather than from native NMRFx project files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have an NMRFx (or NMRViewJ) project with constraints loaded and simply want interactive peak picking, assignment, or chemical shift prediction rather than a batch structure calculation. You only need spectrum processing (FID to processed NUS/non-NUS spectra); the NEF batch route addresses structure calculation, not data processing.

skills.description: Use when an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry must be syntax-validated and its chemical shift loop and restraint saveframes (NOE distances, dihedral angles) converted to the NEF interchange format for OneDep/wwPDB deposition with IUPAC atom nomenclature preserved.
skills.name: nef-format-conversion
skills.search_text: nef-format-conversion Use when an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry must be syntax-validated and its chemical shift loop and restraint saveframes (NOE distances, dihedral angles) converted to the NEF interchange format for OneDep/wwPDB deposition with IUPAC atom nomenclature preserved. The shift and restraint data are already in NEF or NMR-STAR format accepted by OneDep — no format conversion is needed. The actual problem is atom-nomenclature remapping itself: STARch converts table formats but not atom nomenclature, so a format converter will not fix inconsistent names. The goal is visualizing or exploring chemical shift distributions rather than producing a depositable NEF file (analysis/visualization libraries such as PyBMRB are the better fit). http://edamontology.org/topic_1317 Validates archival BMRB NMR-STAR entries with PyNMR-STAR against the BMRB NMR-STAR 3.2 schema, then converts their chemical shift loop and restraint saveframes (NOE distance, dihedral angle) into the NEF interchange format that OneDep accepts. Rationale: deposition requires restraints in NEF or NMR-STAR format, and mismatched atom nomenclature tables are rejected. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/978-1-0716-0270-6_14
skills.summary: Validates archival BMRB NMR-STAR entries with PyNMR-STAR against the BMRB NMR-STAR 3.2 schema, then converts their chemical shift loop and restraint saveframes (NOE distance, dihedral angle) into the NEF interchange format that OneDep accepts. Rationale: deposition requires restraints in NEF or NMR-STAR format, and mismatched atom nomenclature tables are rejected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The shift and restraint data are already in NEF or NMR-STAR format accepted by OneDep — no format conversion is needed. The actual problem is atom-nomenclature remapping itself: STARch converts table formats but not atom nomenclature, so a format converter will not fix inconsistent names. The goal is visualizing or exploring chemical shift distributions rather than producing a depositable NEF file (analysis/visualization libraries such as PyBMRB are the better fit).

skills.description: Use when a trained MS/MS classifier's false-positive rate must be quantified: i.e., when a curated ground-truth set of known non-target (negative-control) compound spectra is available and the fraction correctly assigned to the 'other' class needs to be reported per ion mode.
skills.name: negative-control-classification-evaluation
skills.search_text: negative-control-classification-evaluation Use when a trained MS/MS classifier's false-positive rate must be quantified: i.e., when a curated ground-truth set of known non-target (negative-control) compound spectra is available and the fraction correctly assigned to the 'other' class needs to be reported per ion mode. The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article states classification into substance classes will often not be successful and the package cannot resolve this failure mode The goal is compound identification or dereplication of individual spectra rather than binary 'relevant'/'other' class-assignment evaluation of a user-defined substance class No curated ground-truth negative-control spectra (verified non-prenylated compounds) exist, so the correct-'other' rejection rate cannot be measured http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates custom-trained HR-MS/MS classifiers by classifying a ground-truth set of known non-target compounds and measuring how often they are correctly rejected to the 'other' class. For the AnnoMe prenylated flavonoid model, this quantifies false-positive propensity of the LDA/NN/SVM majority-vote ensemble per ion mode. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Evaluates custom-trained HR-MS/MS classifiers by classifying a ground-truth set of known non-target compounds and measuring how often they are correctly rejected to the 'other' class. For the AnnoMe prenylated flavonoid model, this quantifies false-positive propensity of the LDA/NN/SVM majority-vote ensemble per ion mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article states classification into substance classes will often not be successful and the package cannot resolve this failure mode The goal is compound identification or dereplication of individual spectra rather than binary 'relevant'/'other' class-assignment evaluation of a user-defined substance class No curated ground-truth negative-control spectra (verified non-prenylated compounds) exist, so the correct-'other' rejection rate cannot be measured

skills.description: Use when applying hRUV/RUV-III normalisation to large-scale metabolomics data and you must decide which metabolites serve as negative controls — e.g. selecting all metabolites vs. ranking non-differentially expressed metabolites by p-values per batch for a response variable such as hypertension.
skills.name: negative-control-metabolite-selection
skills.search_text: negative-control-metabolite-selection Use when applying hRUV/RUV-III normalisation to large-scale metabolomics data and you must decide which metabolites serve as negative controls — e.g. selecting all metabolites vs. ranking non-differentially expressed metabolites by p-values per batch for a response variable such as hypertension. When the study is small-scale or has no signal drift/batch structure — the assumption that pooled QC samples are identical over extended periods may hold, and negative-control sensitivity analysis adds no value. When the response variable and batch boundaries differ from a large-scale, multi-day design (e.g. a single short-run LC-MS/MS batch) — the p-value-per-batch ranking of non-differentially expressed metabolites cannot be estimated meaningfully. When metabolite data contain missing values that cannot be imputed — hRUV expects data without missing values, which is often not possible in large-scale metabolomics; the imputation workaround must be resolved first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Selects metabolite negative controls for RUV-III-based hRUV batch correction, comparing a data-driven iterative selection of stable (non-differentially expressed, p-value-ranked) metabolites against the default of using all metabolites, so the analyst can decide whether control-choice materially changes the normalized BioHEART-CT plasma metabolomics output. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Selects metabolite negative controls for RUV-III-based hRUV batch correction, comparing a data-driven iterative selection of stable (non-differentially expressed, p-value-ranked) metabolites against the default of using all metabolites, so the analyst can decide whether control-choice materially changes the normalized BioHEART-CT plasma metabolomics output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the study is small-scale or has no signal drift/batch structure — the assumption that pooled QC samples are identical over extended periods may hold, and negative-control sensitivity analysis adds no value. When the response variable and batch boundaries differ from a large-scale, multi-day design (e.g. a single short-run LC-MS/MS batch) — the p-value-per-batch ranking of non-differentially expressed metabolites cannot be estimated meaningfully. When metabolite data contain missing values that cannot be imputed — hRUV expects data without missing values, which is often not possible in large-scale metabolomics; the imputation workaround must be resolved first.

skills.description: Use when you must show that a computational inference method (e.g., MetaboPAC's heuristic penalty-function optimization of response factors) significantly outperforms negative control methods across graded conditions such as percKnownKinetics = [0 20 40 60 80 100].
skills.name: negative-control-statistical-comparison
skills.search_text: negative-control-statistical-comparison Use when you must show that a computational inference method (e.g., MetaboPAC's heuristic penalty-function optimization of response factors) significantly outperforms negative control methods across graded conditions such as percKnownKinetics = [0 20 40 60 80 100]. Data are noisy or sampled at low frequency (timepoints [50 15], CoV [5 15]) — the noise-add workflow MetaboPAC_*_noisy.m is the appropriate comparator setting, not the noiseless benchmark Response factors were sampled from a log-uniform distribution — use MetaboPAC_*_log.m at percKnownKinetics = 100 instead of the uniform noiseless protocol The goal is calibration/validation of a single method's absolute accuracy rather than a head-to-head significance comparison against negative controls http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark an inference method's output against negative control comparator methods using predefined error-tolerance bins and per-condition statistical tests, as done for MetaboPAC's response-factor inference on noiseless GC-MS-derived in silico data. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Benchmark an inference method's output against negative control comparator methods using predefined error-tolerance bins and per-condition statistical tests, as done for MetaboPAC's response-factor inference on noiseless GC-MS-derived in silico data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are noisy or sampled at low frequency (timepoints [50 15], CoV [5 15]) — the noise-add workflow MetaboPAC_*_noisy.m is the appropriate comparator setting, not the noiseless benchmark Response factors were sampled from a log-uniform distribution — use MetaboPAC_*_log.m at percKnownKinetics = 100 instead of the uniform noiseless protocol The goal is calibration/validation of a single method's absolute accuracy rather than a head-to-head significance comparison against negative controls

skills.description: Use when a correlation network built from abundance data carries both positive and negative edges, and the analysis goal (e.g., sample-specific subnetworks or topological comparison) requires retaining only co-occurrence (positive) edges.
skills.name: negative-correlation-filtering
skills.search_text: negative-correlation-filtering Use when a correlation network built from abundance data carries both positive and negative edges, and the analysis goal (e.g., sample-specific subnetworks or topological comparison) requires retaining only co-occurrence (positive) edges. The metric matrix is non-negative by construction (e.g., similarity or Jaccard), so there are no negative edges to remove — filtering is a no-op. Negative (mutual-exclusion) edges are themselves the biological object of study and must be preserved in the topology. The goal is a full multi-omics cross-layer network where inhibitory cross-layer relationships are of interest. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Filters signed correlation-based co-occurrence networks to retain only positive edges (remove_negative=TRUE) before subnetwork extraction and topological computation, so downstream indices are not distorted by indirect/antagonistic associations. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.06.26.661636
skills.summary: Filters signed correlation-based co-occurrence networks to retain only positive edges (remove_negative=TRUE) before subnetwork extraction and topological computation, so downstream indices are not distorted by indirect/antagonistic associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metric matrix is non-negative by construction (e.g., similarity or Jaccard), so there are no negative edges to remove — filtering is a no-op. Negative (mutual-exclusion) edges are themselves the biological object of study and must be preserved in the topology. The goal is a full multi-omics cross-layer network where inhibitory cross-layer relationships are of interest.

skills.description: Use when you have a negative-ion-mode LC-MS feature table with tissue/group labels (e.g. 94 samples across 14 tissues) and need to determine whether a specific tissue separates from the others in PCA space.
skills.name: negative-ion-mode-lc-ms-data-interpretation
skills.search_text: negative-ion-mode-lc-ms-data-interpretation Use when you have a negative-ion-mode LC-MS feature table with tissue/group labels (e.g. 94 samples across 14 tissues) and need to determine whether a specific tissue separates from the others in PCA space. The data is raw instrument output (e.g. vendor RAW or mzML spectra) rather than a processed feature/intensity table with sample-by-tissue metadata The analysis goal is feature annotation or metabolite identification rather than exploratory tissue-separation assessment by PCA Only two groups are being compared and a univariate test is sufficient — multivariate PCA separation is designed for many-group exploration (e.g. 14 tissues) Interpret negative-ion-mode LC-MS spatial metabolomics feature tables by applying variance-stabilizing transformation and autoscaling, then running PCA (PC1–PC2) to reveal tissue-level metabolic separation, as demonstrated for the lamprey buccal gland dataset (94 samples, 14 tissues) analyzed with MetaboReport. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Interpret negative-ion-mode LC-MS spatial metabolomics feature tables by applying variance-stabilizing transformation and autoscaling, then running PCA (PC1–PC2) to reveal tissue-level metabolic separation, as demonstrated for the lamprey buccal gland dataset (94 samples, 14 tissues) analyzed with MetaboReport.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is raw instrument output (e.g. vendor RAW or mzML spectra) rather than a processed feature/intensity table with sample-by-tissue metadata The analysis goal is feature annotation or metabolite identification rather than exploratory tissue-separation assessment by PCA Only two groups are being compared and a univariate test is sufficient — multivariate PCA separation is designed for many-group exploration (e.g. 14 tissues)

skills.description: Use when running mummichog on negative-ion-mode LC/MS feature tables (e.g. mzXML-derived yeast mutant vs wild-type data) and the predicted metabolites must be constrained to deprotonated M−H[−] species.
skills.name: negative-mode-adduct-enforcement
skills.search_text: negative-mode-adduct-enforcement Use when running mummichog on negative-ion-mode LC/MS feature tables (e.g. mzXML-derived yeast mutant vs wild-type data) and the predicted metabolites must be constrained to deprotonated M−H[−] species. Positive-ion-mode data — use the M+H[+] enforcement option instead of M−H[−] The goal is definitive metabolite identification — mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification The metabolic model compounds lack correct neutral masses (salt formats present) — fix formulas first or look them up via compound identifiers before running http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Enforces the M−H[−] adduct form in mummichog's metabolite prediction when the input LC/MS feature table comes from negative-ion-mode acquisition, so that m/z-to-compound matching is restricted to chemically consistent deprotonated forms built from correct neutral formulas. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: Enforces the M−H[−] adduct form in mummichog's metabolite prediction when the input LC/MS feature table comes from negative-ion-mode acquisition, so that m/z-to-compound matching is restricted to chemically consistent deprotonated forms built from correct neutral formulas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Positive-ion-mode data — use the M+H[+] enforcement option instead of M−H[−] The goal is definitive metabolite identification — mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification The metabolic model compounds lack correct neutral masses (salt formats present) — fix formulas first or look them up via compound identifiers before running

skills.description: Use when converting a catalogued SMILES list (e.g., the EPA CompTox PFAS list) into a predicted MS/MS fragment library for negative-mode PFAS annotation and you must drop structures incapable of forming [M−H]−.
skills.name: negative-mode-ionization-rule-filtering
skills.search_text: negative-mode-ionization-rule-filtering Use when converting a catalogued SMILES list (e.g., the EPA CompTox PFAS list) into a predicted MS/MS fragment library for negative-mode PFAS annotation and you must drop structures incapable of forming [M−H]−. Compounds with measured MS/MS spectra already available — the original FluoroMatch suspect-screening workflow targets those, so predicted-fragment generation is redundant Positive-mode acquisition campaigns — the MZedDB rule set applied here is specific to [M−H]− precursor formation and would wrongly discard structures ionizable only in positive mode Input is already a feature table or peak list without SMILES structures — ionization rules cannot be evaluated without structural records http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Restricts a candidate PFAS structure list to SMILES that can form the [M−H]− precursor ion per MZedDB ionisation rules, so that predicted-MS/MS fragment libraries generated downstream (via RCDK substructure matching) are physically ionizable in negative-mode LC–HRMS experiments used by FluoroMatch 2.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Restricts a candidate PFAS structure list to SMILES that can form the [M−H]− precursor ion per MZedDB ionisation rules, so that predicted-MS/MS fragment libraries generated downstream (via RCDK substructure matching) are physically ionizable in negative-mode LC–HRMS experiments used by FluoroMatch 2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds with measured MS/MS spectra already available — the original FluoroMatch suspect-screening workflow targets those, so predicted-fragment generation is redundant Positive-mode acquisition campaigns — the MZedDB rule set applied here is specific to [M−H]− precursor formation and would wrongly discard structures ionizable only in positive mode Input is already a feature table or peak list without SMILES structures — ionization rules cannot be evaluated without structural records

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a small molecule database search tool (e.g., molDiscovery) on negative-ion-mode tandem mass spectra against a structure database such as DNP, especially to quantify the penalty of using a positive-mode-trained fragmentation model.
skills.name: negative-mode-tandem-ms-evaluation
skills.search_text: negative-mode-tandem-ms-evaluation Use when benchmarking a small molecule database search tool (e.g., molDiscovery) on negative-ion-mode tandem mass spectra against a structure database such as DNP, especially to quantify the penalty of using a positive-mode-trained fragmentation model. Evaluating positive-mode spectra or a model retrained on negative-mode spectra — the ~36% figure applies only to the unretrained default model on negative-mode spectra Spectral library search (searching against reference spectra) rather than in silico search against molecular structure databases like DNP Comparing against baselines on datasets where molDiscovery's reported advantage (e.g., 3,185 unique molecules at 0% FDR on 8 million GNPS spectra) was established in positive mode http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark protocol for evaluating how well a mass spectral database search tool identifies small molecules from negatively charged tandem MS spectra without retraining its fragmentation model. Grounded in molDiscovery's evaluation on 3,964 negative-mode GNPS spectral library spectra searched against the non-redundant Dictionary of Natural Products (DNP), which yielded ~36% top-1 accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for evaluating how well a mass spectral database search tool identifies small molecules from negatively charged tandem MS spectra without retraining its fragmentation model. Grounded in molDiscovery's evaluation on 3,964 negative-mode GNPS spectral library spectra searched against the non-redundant Dictionary of Natural Products (DNP), which yielded ~36% top-1 accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating positive-mode spectra or a model retrained on negative-mode spectra — the ~36% figure applies only to the unretrained default model on negative-mode spectra Spectral library search (searching against reference spectra) rather than in silico search against molecular structure databases like DNP Comparing against baselines on datasets where molDiscovery's reported advantage (e.g., 3,185 unique molecules at 0% FDR on 8 million GNPS spectra) was established in positive mode

skills.description: Use when two peak-picked LC–MS feature tables (RT, m/z, FI per feature) must be matched across datasets and you need a robustly determined expected shift at each reference feature's RT before applying residual-threshold matching.
skills.name: neighbor-definition-shift-modeling
skills.search_text: neighbor-definition-shift-modeling Use when two peak-picked LC–MS feature tables (RT, m/z, FI per feature) must be matched across datasets and you need a robustly determined expected shift at each reference feature's RT before applying residual-threshold matching. When only a single retention-time drift function is expected across the whole m/z range and no co-eluting features with divergent drift exist — a simple global RT alignment suffices, e.g. metabCombiner's robust RT shift model. When candidate matches have not yet been generated by threshold-based RT/MZ/FI screening — applying neighbor modeling directly to raw peak lists without prior candidate filtering will be dominated by spurious neighbors. When features lack reliable retention-time information (e.g. direct-infusion MS), since both 'cross' and 'circle' definitions key on RTref neighborhoods. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Defines k nearest neighbors among candidate matched feature pairs to model the expected inter-dataset shift in retention time (and optionally m/z and feature intensity) between two LC–MS metabolomics feature tables, distinguishing the 'cross' (per-dimension neighbors, one shift per RTref) and 'circle' (normalized Euclidean RT+MZ distance, multiple shifts at the same RTref) mechanisms. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03592
skills.summary: Defines k nearest neighbors among candidate matched feature pairs to model the expected inter-dataset shift in retention time (and optionally m/z and feature intensity) between two LC–MS metabolomics feature tables, distinguishing the 'cross' (per-dimension neighbors, one shift per RTref) and 'circle' (normalized Euclidean RT+MZ distance, multiple shifts at the same RTref) mechanisms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single retention-time drift function is expected across the whole m/z range and no co-eluting features with divergent drift exist — a simple global RT alignment suffices, e.g. metabCombiner's robust RT shift model. When candidate matches have not yet been generated by threshold-based RT/MZ/FI screening — applying neighbor modeling directly to raw peak lists without prior candidate filtering will be dominated by spurious neighbors. When features lack reliable retention-time information (e.g. direct-infusion MS), since both 'cross' and 'circle' definitions key on RTref neighborhoods.

skills.description: Use when creating pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome / MALDI-MSI benchmark datasets from spatial transcriptome matrices, so that spot-to-spot integration methods can be evaluated under realistic neighbor-section morphological disagreement.
skills.name: neighbor-section-morphological-disagreement-modeling
skills.search_text: neighbor-section-morphological-disagreement-modeling Use when creating pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome / MALDI-MSI benchmark datasets from spatial transcriptome matrices, so that spot-to-spot integration methods can be evaluated under realistic neighbor-section morphological disagreement. Input is real-world paired spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data with its own tissue sections rather than pseudo-pairs needing synthetic morphological disagreement The spatial coordinates are already aligned between the two sections, so no Gaussian translation perturbation should be injected Data is non-spatial (bulk or single-cell without coordinates), since the perturbation acts on the spatial matrix D rather than only the feature matrix A pseudo-MALDI-MSI benchmark data generator that mimics the morphological disagreement between neighboring tissue sections by randomly splitting a spatial transcriptome's gene set into two disjoint pseudo-sections and applying Gaussian translation to the spatial coordinates of one of them. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: A pseudo-MALDI-MSI benchmark data generator that mimics the morphological disagreement between neighboring tissue sections by randomly splitting a spatial transcriptome's gene set into two disjoint pseudo-sections and applying Gaussian translation to the spatial coordinates of one of them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real-world paired spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data with its own tissue sections rather than pseudo-pairs needing synthetic morphological disagreement The spatial coordinates are already aligned between the two sections, so no Gaussian translation perturbation should be injected Data is non-spatial (bulk or single-cell without coordinates), since the perturbation acts on the spatial matrix D rather than only the feature matrix

skills.description: Use when you need EI mass spectra for molecules lacking measured spectra — e.g., building an in-silico library from SMILES/SDF sets like f-NIST (255,821) and ChEMBL 28 to expand coverage beyond the 0.27M compounds in NIST 2017.
skills.name: neims-spectrum-prediction
skills.search_text: neims-spectrum-prediction Use when you need EI mass spectra for molecules lacking measured spectra — e.g., building an in-silico library from SMILES/SDF sets like f-NIST (255,821) and ChEMBL 28 to expand coverage beyond the 0.27M compounds in NIST 2017. When you only need to search/match query spectra against a library — use FastEI (Word2vec embedding + HNSW) instead of re-predicting spectra When the ready-made IN_SILICO_LIBRARY.db (Zenodo record 7293922) suffices, avoiding redundant prediction of 2,146,690 spectra When molecules fall outside the article's filter scope (mass ≥ 1000 Da, ionic compounds, elements beyond the 11 common ones) since NEIMS predictions are not validated there http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Predict electron-ionization mass spectra for arbitrary molecules by feeding RDKit-generated ECFP fingerprints into the pre-trained NEIMS fully connected neural network, enabling construction of million-scale in-silico libraries without any experimental measurement or re-training. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Predict electron-ionization mass spectra for arbitrary molecules by feeding RDKit-generated ECFP fingerprints into the pre-trained NEIMS fully connected neural network, enabling construction of million-scale in-silico libraries without any experimental measurement or re-training.

skills.description: Use when validating molecular formula annotations from IDSL.UFA (or any MS1 isotopic-profile matching tool) by quantifying monoisotopic mass error in mDa against authentic reference standards.
skills.name: neme-mass-error-statistics

skills.search_text: nested-cross-validation-benchmarking Use when you must compare several hyperparameter-tuned regressors on one labeled dataset (e.g. 80,038 SMRT retention times with alvaDesc descriptors/fingerprints) and need an unbiased error estimate without validation-set leakage. You only need to train and deploy a single model, not compare several regressors — nested CV adds large compute cost for no comparison benefit. Your dataset is too small to afford 5x7 cross-validation folds (the paper relies on 80,038 labeled molecules). skills.search_text: netgsa-subnetwork-enrichment-testing Use when two-condition metabolomics networks have been estimated with DNEA (glasso partial correlations + clusterNet consensus clustering) and you need to determine which metabolic subnetworks are differentially enriched between groups. When all metabolites can be confidently mapped to well-annotated KEGG pathways and standard reference-based pathway enrichment is sufficient — data-driven module testing is designed for datasets containing exogenous, secondary, and unknown metabolites. When the network has not yet been clustered into subnetworks (no clusterNet output) — NetGSA enrichment requires defined metabolic modules with >= 5 metabolites. When analyzing a single experimental group with no case/control contrast — NetGSA here tests differential enrichment between two conditions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Tests data-driven metabolic subnetworks (modules) identified by DNEA consensus clustering for differential enrichment between two experimental groups using the NetGSA algorithm, as implemented in the DNEA R package's runNetGSA() function. This replaces reference-based pathway analysis when metabolites (e.g., exogenous, lipid, or unknown compounds) cannot be mapped to pathway databases like KEGG. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Tests data-driven metabolic subnetworks (modules) identified by DNEA consensus clustering for differential enrichment between two experimental groups using the NetGSA algorithm, as implemented in the DNEA R package's runNetGSA() function. This replaces reference-based pathway analysis when metabolites (e.g., exogenous, lipid, or unknown compounds) cannot be mapped to pathway databases like KEGG.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When all metabolites can be confidently mapped to well-annotated KEGG pathways and standard reference-based pathway enrichment is sufficient — data-driven module testing is designed for datasets containing exogenous, secondary, and unknown metabolites. When analyzing a single experimental group with no case/control contrast — NetGSA here tests differential enrichment between two conditions.

The input adjacency matrices are already provided — NetGSA's main function accepts a user-supplied A (list of adjacency matrices across tested groups), so retrieval is unnecessary The goal is pathway enrichment scoring rather than network construction — use the NetGSA main function instead of edge-list retrieval http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Retrieves gene-gene interaction (edge) information for user-specified pathway databases (e.g. KEGG, Reactome) via graphite and exports them as a standardized edge list, replacing the manual curation that previously made topology-based pathway analysis an expert task in netgsa. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Retrieves gene-gene interaction (edge) information for user-specified pathway databases (e.g. KEGG, Reactome) via graphite and exports them as a standardized edge list, replacing the manual curation that previously made topology-based pathway analysis an expert task in netgsa.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input adjacency matrices are already provided — NetGSA's main function accepts a user-supplied A (list of adjacency matrices across tested groups), so retrieval is unnecessary The goal is pathway enrichment scoring rather than network construction — use the NetGSA main function instead of edge-list retrieval

skills.description: Use when MetaMapR network calculations (KEGG RPAIR, Tanimoto >0.7 structural, cosine >0.7 spectral, or Spearman/FDR <0.05 correlation edges) must be persisted as .csv edge lists and node attributes for downstream network analysis.
skills.name: network-edge-list-export
skills.search_text: network-edge-list-export Use when MetaMapR network calculations (KEGG RPAIR, Tanimoto >0.7 structural, cosine >0.7 spectral, or Spearman/FDR <0.05 correlation edges) must be persisted as .csv edge lists and node attributes for downstream network analysis. The metabolite identifiers have not yet been translated to KEGG compound IDs or PubChem CIDs via CTSgetR — run identifier translation first The analysis goal is a canonical pathway-based network map; MetaMapR is explicitly pathway independent and its biochemical layer derives only KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs Raw mass spectral or chromatographic data still require preprocessing — this skill operates on already-computed similarity/correlation edge tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Export MetaMapR-calculated metabolic networks (biochemical, structural, spectral, empirical correlation, or combined) as comma-separated value edge lists plus node-attribute tables mapping numeric node IDs to uploaded analytes, ready for import into Cytoscape. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Export MetaMapR-calculated metabolic networks (biochemical, structural, spectral, empirical correlation, or combined) as comma-separated value edge lists plus node-attribute tables mapping numeric node IDs to uploaded analytes, ready for import into Cytoscape.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolite identifiers have not yet been translated to KEGG compound IDs or PubChem CIDs via CTSgetR — run identifier translation first The analysis goal is a canonical pathway-based network map; MetaMapR is explicitly pathway independent and its biochemical layer derives only KEGG RPAIR substrate-product pairs Raw mass spectral or chromatographic data still require preprocessing — this skill operates on already-computed similarity/correlation edge tables

skills.description: Use when merging multiple MetaMapR edge lists (KEGG RPAIR biochemical, PubChem Tanimoto structural, mass spectral cosine, empirical Spearman) into one network and duplicate node pairs carry more than one edge type.
skills.name: network-edge-priority-resolution
skills.search_text: network-edge-priority-resolution Use when merging multiple MetaMapR edge lists (KEGG RPAIR biochemical, PubChem Tanimoto structural, mass spectral cosine, empirical Spearman) into one network and duplicate node pairs carry more than one edge type. The analysis needs all association types represented per metabolite pair (e.g. to study edge-type overlap itself) — leave the 'unique edges' checkbox unchecked instead. Edge lists come from a single association type only, so no duplicate node-pair edges exist to resolve. Edges lack the four MetaMapR association types (e.g. arbitrary custom relations with no defined priority), making the Biochemical > Structural > Mass Spectral > Correlation hierarchy inapplicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Resolves overlapping multi-type edges (biochemical, structural, mass spectral, correlation) between the same metabolite pairs in MetaMapR by returning only the edge from the highest-priority association type, using the fixed hierarchy Biochemical > Structural > Mass Spectral > Correlation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Resolves overlapping multi-type edges (biochemical, structural, mass spectral, correlation) between the same metabolite pairs in MetaMapR by returning only the edge from the highest-priority association type, using the fixed hierarchy Biochemical > Structural > Mass Spectral > Correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis needs all association types represented per metabolite pair (e.g. to study edge-type overlap itself) — leave the 'unique edges' checkbox unchecked instead. Edge lists come from a single association type only, so no duplicate node-pair edges exist to resolve. Edges lack the four MetaMapR association types (e.g. arbitrary custom relations with no defined priority), making the Biochemical > Structural > Mass Spectral > Correlation hierarchy inapplicable.

skills.description: Use when a GGM/marginal-correlation network over metabolomics data is too dense to interpret, and edges must be filtered by an absolute correlation cutoff (e.g., |r| or |pcor| >= 0.2).
skills.name: network-edge-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: network-edge-threshold-filtering Use when a GGM/marginal-correlation network over metabolomics data is too dense to interpret, and edges must be filtered by an absolute correlation cutoff (e.g., |r| or |pcor| >= 0.2). When the input is raw peak-intensity data rather than an already-estimated network — data preprocessing (excluding metabolites missing in >30% of samples, median imputation) and network estimation must precede filtering When the dataset has fewer than ~500 samples per group and the lambda approximation (Eq. 3) rather than BIC tuning is used — the resulting unfiltered networks may not be comparable to paper edge counts When filtering is desired by statistical significance rather than edge strength — filterNetworks() supports only percentile or correlation-threshold based filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Prune estimated metabolite-metabolite networks by thresholding edge strength (absolute partial or marginal correlation coefficient), using the DNEA package's filterNetworks() function to control network density and retain the most biologically relevant connections. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Prune estimated metabolite-metabolite networks by thresholding edge strength (absolute partial or marginal correlation coefficient), using the DNEA package's filterNetworks() function to control network density and retain the most biologically relevant connections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw peak-intensity data rather than an already-estimated network — data preprocessing (excluding metabolites missing in >30% of samples, median imputation) and network estimation must precede filtering When the dataset has fewer than ~500 samples per group and the lambda approximation (Eq. 3) rather than BIC tuning is used — the resulting unfiltered networks may not be comparable to paper edge counts When filtering is desired by statistical significance rather than edge strength — filterNetworks() supports only percentile or correlation-threshold based filtering

skills.description: Use when a Cytoscape network (e.g. a stringApp Disease Query PPI) needs to be enriched with compound-target, gene-disease, gene-pathway, or transcription-factor interactions from pre-built XGMML linksets, reproducibly via command line or R/Python.
skills.name: network-extension-with-linksets
skills.search_text: network-extension-with-linksets Use when a Cytoscape network (e.g. a stringApp Disease Query PPI) needs to be enriched with compound-target, gene-disease, gene-pathway, or transcription-factor interactions from pre-built XGMML linksets, reproducibly via command line or R/Python. You only need to visualize interactions supported by multiple resources rather than extend the network — use the 'filterOverlap' function instead of a fresh extension. The seed network's node identifiers cannot be matched by any linkset identifier mapping (e.g. a failed BridgeDb mapper leaves nodes with only their input id, making extension useless). The task is linkset creation itself rather than network extension; use the linkset-automation LinksetCreator workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Extend a Cytoscape network (e.g. a stringApp PPI network) with prior-knowledge edges from XGMML linksets (ChEMBL compound-target, OMIM gene-disease, WikiPathways, TFLink, etc.) via the CyTargetLinker 'extend' automation command, enabling repeatable, scriptable workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.12688/f1000research.14613.2
skills.summary: Extend a Cytoscape network (e.g. a stringApp PPI network) with prior-knowledge edges from XGMML linksets (ChEMBL compound-target, OMIM gene-disease, WikiPathways, TFLink, etc.) via the CyTargetLinker 'extend' automation command, enabling repeatable, scriptable workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to visualize interactions supported by multiple resources rather than extend the network — use the 'filterOverlap' function instead of a fresh extension. The seed network's node identifiers cannot be matched by any linkset identifier mapping (e.g. a failed BridgeDb mapper leaves nodes with only their input id, making extension useless). The task is linkset creation itself rather than network extension; use the linkset-automation LinksetCreator workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when ICP-MS ion-concentration data (e.g. haploid S. cerevisiae deletion-mutant ionomes) have been normalised/symbolised and you need element-element or mutant-mutant network extraction plus correlation analysis.
skills.name: network-inference
skills.search_text: network-inference Use when ICP-MS ion-concentration data (e.g. haploid S. cerevisiae deletion-mutant ionomes) have been normalised/symbolised and you need element-element or mutant-mutant network extraction plus correlation analysis. The input is raw, uncorrected ICP-MS output that has not passed through IonFlow's pre-processing (outlier removal and median batch correction) — network edges would reflect batch effects The analysis goal is purely exploratory dimensionality reduction with no relational/network question (PCA or hierarchical clustering alone suffices) The data are not elemental-concentration profiles (IonFlow's applicability to metabolomics is stated as only potential, not demonstrated) http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Extract and analyse relevance networks from ionome profiles measured by ICP-MS, using ion-profile-specific similarity measures to link mutants or elements, as implemented in the IonFlow R/Galaxy pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01841-z
skills.summary: Extract and analyse relevance networks from ionome profiles measured by ICP-MS, using ion-profile-specific similarity measures to link mutants or elements, as implemented in the IonFlow R/Galaxy pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, uncorrected ICP-MS output that has not passed through IonFlow's pre-processing (outlier removal and median batch correction) — network edges would reflect batch effects The analysis goal is purely exploratory dimensionality reduction with no relational/network question (PCA or hierarchical clustering alone suffices) The data are not elemental-concentration profiles (IonFlow's applicability to metabolomics is stated as only potential, not demonstrated)

skills.description: Use when a patient-level per-gene score vector (e.g., metabolomic enrichment) needs to be smoothed/ranked over a protein interaction network so that neighborhood signal can implicate genes lacking direct annotation.
skills.name: network-label-propagation
skills.search_text: network-label-propagation Use when a patient-level per-gene score vector (e.g., metabolomic enrichment) needs to be smoothed/ranked over a protein interaction network so that neighborhood signal can implicate genes lacking direct annotation. When the analysis goal is ranking genes by direct gene-metabolite annotation alone — the ME score alone prioritized 31% fewer Miller patients than propagation across the STRING network When the candidate list must be restricted to physically interacting proteins only — the physical-only STRING subset ranked causative genes worse for ~90% of cases and omitted several causative genes entirely When no gene-metabolite association database (HMDB) or patient-vs-control metabolomic intensity matrix exists to construct the initial label vector http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Seed a protein functional linkage network (STRING) with per-gene metabolomic enrichment (ME/DME) scores and propagate the labels with the Zhou et al. label-propagation formulation to rank candidate disease genes per patient, as implemented in metPropagate. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Seed a protein functional linkage network (STRING) with per-gene metabolomic enrichment (ME/DME) scores and propagate the labels with the Zhou et al. label-propagation formulation to rank candidate disease genes per patient, as implemented in metPropagate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is ranking genes by direct gene-metabolite annotation alone — the ME score alone prioritized 31% fewer Miller patients than propagation across the STRING network When the candidate list must be restricted to physically interacting proteins only — the physical-only STRING subset ranked causative genes worse for ~90% of cases and omitted several causative genes entirely When no gene-metabolite association database (HMDB) or patient-vs-control metabolomic intensity matrix exists to construct the initial label vector

skills.description: Use when two ICA decompositions (metagene/sk weight vectors) from different transcriptomic datasets must be matched to assess reproducibility of independent components via a graph of 'orthologous' metagenes.
skills.name: network-modularity-and-clustering-analysis
skills.search_text: network-modularity-and-clustering-analysis Use when two ICA decompositions (metagene/sk weight vectors) from different transcriptomic datasets must be matched to assess reproducibility of independent components via a graph of 'orthologous' metagenes. You need quantitative agreement thresholds between components — the section provides no numeric cutoff, so reproducibility is judged only by qualitative/expert comparison with Sections 2.4 and 3.6. The decomposition outputs are sample-weight (dr) vectors or single-dataset components with no second decomposition to match against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstruct a reciprocal best hit (RBH) graph linking metagenes (sk vectors) from two ICA decompositions of cancer transcriptomic datasets, then quantify component reproducibility via modularity, average clustering coefficient, and community structure computed with networkx. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414
skills.summary: Reconstruct a reciprocal best hit (RBH) graph linking metagenes (sk vectors) from two ICA decompositions of cancer transcriptomic datasets, then quantify component reproducibility via modularity, average clustering coefficient, and community structure computed with networkx.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need quantitative agreement thresholds between components — the section provides no numeric cutoff, so reproducibility is judged only by qualitative/expert comparison with Sections 2.4 and 3.6. The decomposition outputs are sample-weight (dr) vectors or single-dataset components with no second decomposition to match against.

skills.description: Use when a co-occurrence network (e.g. MetaNet c_net_build output at r_threshold=0.6, p=0.05) needs community decomposition and hub/connector classification, such as microbial species networks from abundance tables.
skills.name: network-module-detection-keystone-classification
skills.search_text: network-module-detection-keystone-classification Use when a co-occurrence network (e.g. MetaNet c_net_build output at r_threshold=0.6, p=0.05) needs community decomposition and hub/connector classification, such as microbial species networks from abundance tables. The network was built with a different similarity metric or threshold, so Zi/P keystone cutoffs and module stability are not comparable to the article's Spearman |ρ|>0.6 standard The graph is too small or too sparse (e.g. the singletons already pruned by delete_single=TRUE) to support meaningful community detection or keystone-role statistics The goal is differential or cross-condition network comparison (c_net_union/intersect/difference) rather than within-network module and keystone analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0611 http://edamontology.org/topic_3300 Detects densely connected modules in an omics co-occurrence network built with MetaNet (c_net_module/get_module) and classifies keystone taxa by within-module (Zi) and among-module (P) connectivity, using Spearman-|ρ|>0.6 networks as the substrate. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.06.26.661636
skills.summary: Detects densely connected modules in an omics co-occurrence network built with MetaNet (c_net_module/get_module) and classifies keystone taxa by within-module (Zi) and among-module (P) connectivity, using Spearman-|ρ|>0.6 networks as the substrate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network was built with a different similarity metric or threshold, so Zi/P keystone cutoffs and module stability are not comparable to the article's Spearman |ρ|>0.6 standard The graph is too small or too sparse (e.g. the singletons already pruned by delete_single=TRUE) to support meaningful community detection or keystone-role statistics The goal is differential or cross-condition network comparison (c_net_union/intersect/difference) rather than within-network module and keystone analysis

skills.description: Use when per-patient metPropagate LPA propagated scores and Exomiser-Phenotype candidate scores (Exomiser-filtered lists of ~281-609 genes) must be merged to boost causative-gene ranks for suspected IEM patients.
skills.name: network-neighborhood-metabolic-annotation
skills.search_text: network-neighborhood-metabolic-annotation Use when per-patient metPropagate LPA propagated scores and Exomiser-Phenotype candidate scores (Exomiser-filtered lists of ~281-609 genes) must be merged to boost causative-gene ranks for suspected IEM patients. No protein functional linkage network or gene-metabolite annotations are available (e.g., non-human organism or no STRING/HMDB coverage), so the per-gene p weight cannot be computed Input is raw LC/MS feature data requiring the XCMS/metabolomic-processing pipeline rather than already-prioritized candidate gene lists from Exomiser filtering Candidate lists are already very short (e.g., trio WES with parental data), so the top-20th-percentile binning and reweighting add little value http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A re-ranking skill that quantifies each STRING gene's percentage of first-degree neighbors annotated in HMDB and converts it into a per-gene weight p, producing the combined score C = p*Exomiser + (1-p)*metPropagate that corrects metPropagate's bias toward genes embedded in metabolic neighborhoods. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: A re-ranking skill that quantifies each STRING gene's percentage of first-degree neighbors annotated in HMDB and converts it into a per-gene weight p, producing the combined score C = p*Exomiser + (1-p)*metPropagate that corrects metPropagate's bias toward genes embedded in metabolic neighborhoods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No protein functional linkage network or gene-metabolite annotations are available (e.g., non-human organism or no STRING/HMDB coverage), so the per-gene p weight cannot be computed Input is raw LC/MS feature data requiring the XCMS/metabolomic-processing pipeline rather than already-prioritized candidate gene lists from Exomiser filtering Candidate lists are already very short (e.g., trio WES with parental data), so the top-20th-percentile binning and reweighting add little value

skills.description: Use when the intersecting genes from a hypergeometric metabolic/GWAS comparison need to be attributed to primary keyword nodes versus first-neighbour nodes of a GWAS Catalog network to interpret where the signal arises.
skills.name: network-neighbourhood-tracing
skills.search_text: network-neighbourhood-tracing Use when the intersecting genes from a hypergeometric metabolic/GWAS comparison need to be attributed to primary keyword nodes versus first-neighbour nodes of a GWAS Catalog network to interpret where the signal arises. When running the over-representation analysis itself — this skill is post-hoc node attribution, not the hypergeometric comparison step. When paired metabolomics-GWAS data are available, since direct SNP-metabolite associations bypass the network neighbourhood of the GWAS Catalog. When the GWAS Catalog network object GWASnetwork_discoverableGenesOnly_2021_10_14.RData has not been downloaded, as it is not bundled in the supplementary material. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Traces each gene in the metGWAS 1.0 metabolic/GWAS intersection back to its position in the GWAS Catalog subnetwork, labelling it as a primary keyword node or a first-neighbour node. This reveals whether metabolite-gene associations originate from keyword-matched GWAS studies or from their immediate network neighbours. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Traces each gene in the metGWAS 1.0 metabolic/GWAS intersection back to its position in the GWAS Catalog subnetwork, labelling it as a primary keyword node or a first-neighbour node. This reveals whether metabolite-gene associations originate from keyword-matched GWAS studies or from their immediate network neighbours.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When running the over-representation analysis itself — this skill is post-hoc node attribution, not the hypergeometric comparison step. When paired metabolomics-GWAS data are available, since direct SNP-metabolite associations bypass the network neighbourhood of the GWAS Catalog. When the GWAS Catalog network object GWASnetwork_discoverableGenesOnly_2021_10_14.RData has not been downloaded, as it is not bundled in the supplementary material.

skills.description: Use when a motif-mapped molecular network (.graphml or Mass2Motifs_Nodes/Edges TSVs from pyMolNetEnhancer) is available and you need per-motif node frequencies and counts of annotated motifs across the network.
skills.name: network-node-motif-frequency-counting
skills.search_text: network-node-motif-frequency-counting Use when a motif-mapped molecular network (.graphml or Mass2Motifs_Nodes/Edges TSVs from pyMolNetEnhancer) is available and you need per-motif node frequencies and counts of annotated motifs across the network. Input is a raw spectral file with no GNPS molecular network or MS2LDA motif output — frequency counting requires a motif-mapped network first You need motif discovery rather than counting — run MS2LDA on the clustered MGF instead; this skill only quantifies already-mapped motifs The summary table was exported from ms2lda.org with different prob/overlap thresholds than the ones used downstream — the table contains filtered motif-document relations using thresholds set in the web app, so mixed thresholds will skew counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Counts how often Mass2Motifs mapped by MolNetEnhancer/pyMolNetEnhancer occur across all nodes of a GNPS molecular network and tallies how many motifs could be annotated (e.g. peptidic motifs linked to known peptides via DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest), as demonstrated on the 6228-node Xenorhabdus/Photorhabdus network (MSV000081063). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Counts how often Mass2Motifs mapped by MolNetEnhancer/pyMolNetEnhancer occur across all nodes of a GNPS molecular network and tallies how many motifs could be annotated (e.g. peptidic motifs linked to known peptides via DEREPLICATOR/VarQuest), as demonstrated on the 6228-node Xenorhabdus/Photorhabdus network (MSV000081063).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw spectral file with no GNPS molecular network or MS2LDA motif output — frequency counting requires a motif-mapped network first You need motif discovery rather than counting — run MS2LDA on the clustered MGF instead; this skill only quantifies already-mapped motifs The summary table was exported from ms2lda.org with different prob/overlap thresholds than the ones used downstream — the table contains filtered motif-document relations using thresholds set in the web app, so mixed thresholds will skew counts

skills.description: Use when a full-connectivity metabolite similarity network (all pairwise cosine edges retained, no threshold) needs to be partitioned into molecular communities without a predefined community count.
skills.name: network-partition-export
skills.search_text: network-partition-export Use when a full-connectivity metabolite similarity network (all pairwise cosine edges retained, no threshold) needs to be partitioned into molecular communities without a predefined community count. Input network has already been pruned with an arbitrary cosine similarity threshold — MCN's premise is that such thresholds fracture natural metabolite families The number or sizes of communities is predefined by the analysis — this skill requires modularity optimization to determine community structure from the data http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Runs modularity-based community detection (Louvain) on an unpruned, full-connectivity metabolite similarity network and exports the node-to-community partition as a structured communities.csv table. It lets community structure emerge from the data rather than imposing a preset number of clusters. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Runs modularity-based community detection (Louvain) on an unpruned, full-connectivity metabolite similarity network and exports the node-to-community partition as a structured communities.csv table. It lets community structure emerge from the data rather than imposing a preset number of clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input network has already been pruned with an arbitrary cosine similarity threshold — MCN's premise is that such thresholds fracture natural metabolite families The number or sizes of communities is predefined by the analysis — this skill requires modularity optimization to determine community structure from the data

skills.description: Use when a single patient's untargeted metabolomics yields DAMs (|z| >= 2) plus an Exomiser-filtered candidate gene list, and genes must be ranked by metabolomics-derived scores propagated across a STRING protein interaction network.
skills.name: network-propagation-score-ranking
skills.search_text: network-propagation-score-ranking Use when a single patient's untargeted metabolomics yields DAMs (|z| >= 2) plus an Exomiser-filtered candidate gene list, and genes must be ranked by metabolomics-derived scores propagated across a STRING protein interaction network. Input is still raw LC/MS feature tables (negative/positive intensity matrices, peakTables) — these must first pass through METABOLOMIC_PROCESSING_PIPELINE (median-scaling, min-intensity imputation, HMDB annotation) to produce per-gene enrichment scores. The disease's diagnostic metabolites are outside the platform's measurable space or HMDB annotation (e.g. large glycosaminoglycans for the IDS patient; acyl glycines/acyl carnitines not annotated to IEM genes) — propagation cannot recover absent signal. No patient metabolomics exists and only HPO phenotype terms are available — Exomiser's hiPHIVE phenotype-driven ranking is the appropriate tool instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 metPropagate's core ranking skill: per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME/DME) scores derived from a patient's untargeted metabolomics are label-propagated across the STRING v11 protein functional linkage network, and Exomiser-filtered candidate genes are ranked by the post-propagation score (Score.ID) to prioritize metabolic disease genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: metPropagate's core ranking skill: per-gene metabolic enrichment (ME/DME) scores derived from a patient's untargeted metabolomics are label-propagated across the STRING v11 protein functional linkage network, and Exomiser-filtered candidate genes are ranked by the post-propagation score (Score.ID) to prioritize metabolic disease genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw LC/MS feature tables (negative/positive intensity matrices, peakTables) — these must first pass through METABOLOMIC_PROCESSING_PIPELINE (median-scaling, min-intensity imputation, HMDB annotation) to produce per-gene enrichment scores. The disease's diagnostic metabolites are outside the platform's measurable space or HMDB annotation (e.g. large glycosaminoglycans for the IDS patient; acyl glycines/acyl carnitines not annotated to IEM genes) — propagation cannot recover absent signal. No patient metabolomics exists and only HPO phenotype terms are available — Exomiser's hiPHIVE phenotype-driven ranking is the appropriate tool instead.

skills.search_text: network-scale-verification Use when a KGMN-style analysis requires rebuilding network layer 1 (KMRN) from KEGG and BioTransformer and you must confirm the reconstruction matches the published network scale before downstream subnetwork retrieval. skills.summary: Reconstruct the KGMN knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (KMRN) from KEGG RCLASS reactant pairs plus BioTransformer in silico biotransformations, then verify the reconstructed network reproduces the reported scale (34,858 unknown metabolites, 52,137 edges, 1504 biotransformation types) before using it for annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need downstream visualization or subnetwork retrieval from an already-validated KGMN result folder — use retrieveSubNetwork1/2/3 and mergeSubnetwork instead of rebuilding network 1 Your study targets non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics samples where the human-centric BioTransformer reaction sets are inappropriate without organism-specific database extension The input is a feature/peak table without any KGMN result directory — the reconstruction functions depend on KGMN-generated files

skills.description: Use when you have FT-ICR MS peak abundance data with assigned molecular formulas and need to construct transformation networks from mass differences and summarize network metrics.
skills.name: network-statistics-computation
skills.search_text: network-statistics-computation Use when you have FT-ICR MS peak abundance data with assigned molecular formulas and need to construct transformation networks from mass differences and summarize network metrics. Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must be performed before using MetaboDirect You need chemical isomer separation or LC-MS-level structural connectivity — DI-MS mass-difference networks cannot separate chemical isomers The goal is pathway-level annotation rather than ab initio mass-difference connectivity — use the KEGGREST query step instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds mass-difference transformation networks from FT-ICR MS peak pairs in Cytoscape (nodes = detected peaks colored by molecular class, edges = putative biochemical transformations) and computes per-network and per-transformation-type statistics exported as .csv tables and bar plots. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Builds mass-difference transformation networks from FT-ICR MS peak pairs in Cytoscape (nodes = detected peaks colored by molecular class, edges = putative biochemical transformations) and computes per-network and per-transformation-type statistics exported as .csv tables and bar plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must be performed before using MetaboDirect You need chemical isomer separation or LC-MS-level structural connectivity — DI-MS mass-difference networks cannot separate chemical isomers The goal is pathway-level annotation rather than ab initio mass-difference connectivity — use the KEGGREST query step instead

skills.summary: Assembles top-ranked ML feature–metabolite pairs into an Excel network table (Metab8_network.xlsx) where each pair carries a 0–8 confidence score counting how many of the 8 control experiments the feature appeared in for that metabolite.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mutations are excluded from random forest model results due to their binary structure, so mutation-derived features should not be tabulated into the network The trained models are not directly transferrable to predicting metabolomics from other sources due to differences between in vitro and in vivo conditions, so confidence scores should not be applied to out-of-panel datasets

skills.description: Use when per-condition or per-sample subnetworks have been extracted from a co-occurrence network and you need global topological indices compared against a baseline to detect fragmentation or restructuring under exposure or other treatments.
skills.name: network-topological-index-computation
skills.search_text: network-topological-index-computation Use when per-condition or per-sample subnetworks have been extracted from a co-occurrence network and you need global topological indices compared against a baseline to detect fragmentation or restructuring under exposure or other treatments. The input is still a raw abundance table with no constructed network — build the co-occurrence network first (c_net_calculate/c_net_build) before computing topology. The goal is module/community detection or visualization of a single network rather than global index computation and cross-network comparison. The question concerns differential edges between two specific networks (intersection/union/difference) rather than per-sample topological index trajectories. Computes global topological indices (modularity, average path length, global efficiency, clustering coefficient, natural connectivity) on omics co-occurrence networks and sample-specific subnetworks using MetaNet, to quantify shifts such as community fragmentation across experimental conditions. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.06.26.661636
skills.summary: Computes global topological indices (modularity, average path length, global efficiency, clustering coefficient, natural connectivity) on omics co-occurrence networks and sample-specific subnetworks using MetaNet, to quantify shifts such as community fragmentation across experimental conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is still a raw abundance table with no constructed network — build the co-occurrence network first (c_net_calculate/c_net_build) before computing topology. The goal is module/community detection or visualization of a single network rather than global index computation and cross-network comparison. The question concerns differential edges between two specific networks (intersection/union/difference) rather than per-sample topological index trajectories.

skills.description: Use when an FBMN molecular network has spectral pairing (GNPS/GNPS2 library) matches for only a subset of nodes and the remaining MS/MS spectra still need chemical annotations.
skills.name: network-topology-annotation-propagation
skills.search_text: network-topology-annotation-propagation Use when an FBMN molecular network has spectral pairing (GNPS/GNPS2 library) matches for only a subset of nodes and the remaining MS/MS spectra still need chemical annotations. When the node already has a direct spectral library match in the GNPS2 library — propagation adds nothing beyond the first-level annotation When the input is raw vendor data or unprocessed MS1/MS2 centroids rather than an MZmine-preprocessed feature table and .mgf MS/MS spectra When the analysis goal is discovering entirely novel spectra without structural analogs in the network — propagation requires connected annotated neighbors http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotate spectral-library-unmatched nodes in a Feature Based Molecular Network by propagating known annotations along the molecular network topology, then filling remaining gaps with SIRIUS in silico annotation — the second and third annotation layers in this RegFilter LC-MS/MS workflow for actinomycete extracts. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Annotate spectral-library-unmatched nodes in a Feature Based Molecular Network by propagating known annotations along the molecular network topology, then filling remaining gaps with SIRIUS in silico annotation — the second and third annotation layers in this RegFilter LC-MS/MS workflow for actinomycete extracts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the node already has a direct spectral library match in the GNPS2 library — propagation adds nothing beyond the first-level annotation When the input is raw vendor data or unprocessed MS1/MS2 centroids rather than an MZmine-preprocessed feature table and .mgf MS/MS spectra When the analysis goal is discovering entirely novel spectra without structural analogs in the network — propagation requires connected annotated neighbors

skills.summary: Builds a molecular network from TransExION pairwise MS/MS spectral similarities using meRgeION and compares its sub-network topology against a reference (SNAP-MS/GNPS) network to confirm that confidently-assigned compound families are recovered.
