skills.description: Use when you must decide which knowledge-driven network topology (metabolic reaction network vs. spectral or fully connected network) to adopt for MS2-based annotation propagation, by quantifying accuracy, FDR, and specificity trade-offs.
skills.name: network-topology-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: network-topology-comparison-analysis Use when you must decide which knowledge-driven network topology (metabolic reaction network vs. spectral or fully connected network) to adopt for MS2-based annotation propagation, by quantifying accuracy, FDR, and specificity trade-offs. When the input is already a single-feature annotation result and no topology choice is being made — this skill benchmarks topologies, it does not annotate features directly. When the dataset is not LC-MS/MS Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics with MS2 spectra available, since decoy-MS2 evaluation and propagation specificity depend on MS2 spectral data. When you need a single annotation result for downstream analysis rather than a comparative evaluation across network connectivities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark different knowledge-driven network topologies (MRN, SMN, FCN) for network-based metabolite annotation by computing same-superclass propagation specificity, decoy-MS2 Top-3 accuracy, and estimated FDR per topology, revealing that sparser networks (MRN) outperform denser ones. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Benchmark different knowledge-driven network topologies (MRN, SMN, FCN) for network-based metabolite annotation by computing same-superclass propagation specificity, decoy-MS2 Top-3 accuracy, and estimated FDR per topology, revealing that sparser networks (MRN) outperform denser ones.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a single-feature annotation result and no topology choice is being made — this skill benchmarks topologies, it does not annotate features directly. When the dataset is not LC-MS/MS Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics with MS2 spectra available, since decoy-MS2 evaluation and propagation specificity depend on MS2 spectral data. When you need a single annotation result for downstream analysis rather than a comparative evaluation across network connectivities.

The goal is pathway over-representation or MetSEA on KEGG pathways rather than chemical-chemical interaction topology — use EnrichMet's Fisher's exact test or fgsea modules instead Interaction data comes from Reactome reaction mappings rather than STITCH chemical-chemical relationships, since the combined score >= 100 filter is STITCH-specific Metabolites cannot be mapped to STITCH compound identifiers, so the interaction query would return an empty or unrepresentative network http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Builds a metabolite-metabolite interaction network from STITCH chemical-chemical relationships (combined score >= 100) and computes node degree/betweenness centrality to rank hub metabolites, as demonstrated by identifying Xanthine as a hub in the lung cancer control-vs-mutant case study. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Builds a metabolite-metabolite interaction network from STITCH chemical-chemical relationships (combined score >= 100) and computes node degree/betweenness centrality to rank hub metabolites, as demonstrated by identifying Xanthine as a hub in the lung cancer control-vs-mutant case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pathway over-representation or MetSEA on KEGG pathways rather than chemical-chemical interaction topology — use EnrichMet's Fisher's exact test or fgsea modules instead Interaction data comes from Reactome reaction mappings rather than STITCH chemical-chemical relationships, since the combined score >= 100 filter is STITCH-specific Metabolites cannot be mapped to STITCH compound identifiers, so the interaction query would return an empty or unrepresentative network

skills.search_text: network-topology-validation Use when building or filtering MetDNA3 feature/metadata reaction networks and you must verify intermediate graph sizes (node/edge counts) against published reference values before recursive annotation propagation. skills.summary: Validate network topology counts at each stage of MetDNA3's two-layer annotation pipeline, e.g. checking that the data-constrained MRN for NIST urine HILIC-MS(+) contains exactly 2,993 metabolites and 55,674 reaction pairs before annotation propagation proceeds.

skills.search_text: networking-parameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when re-running or reproducing a GNPS METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 molecular networking job on a public dataset (e.g. MassIVE MSV000083381) and you need to characterize how clustering or tolerance parameters alter node counts and library annotations. Input is already a processed feature table or quantified molecular network output — this skill concerns the networking job parameters themselves The goal is calibrated quantitative analysis — classic molecular networking provides only qualitative information because only MS2 scans are considered Application of in silico annotation tools (e.g. structure prediction beyond library matching) is required — this is beyond the scope of the networking protocol A systematic sweep of GNPS molecular networking parameters (Minimum Consensus Cluster Size, PIMT/FIMT precursor/fragment mass tolerances, and spectrum filtering options) on a fixed LC-MS/MS dataset to quantify how each setting changes subnetwork size and annotation yield. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-020-0317-5
skills.summary: A systematic sweep of GNPS molecular networking parameters (Minimum Consensus Cluster Size, PIMT/FIMT precursor/fragment mass tolerances, and spectrum filtering options) on a fixed LC-MS/MS dataset to quantify how each setting changes subnetwork size and annotation yield.

skills.description: Use when you need to predict EI mass spectra from molecular structures (SMILES/SDF/InChI) or augment a spectral reference library (e.g., NIST, MassBank, Wiley) with predicted spectra for molecules absent from the library.
skills.name: neural-mass-spectrum-prediction
skills.search_text: neural-mass-spectrum-prediction Use when you need to predict EI mass spectra from molecular structures (SMILES/SDF/InChI) or augment a spectral reference library (e.g., NIST, MassBank, Wiley) with predicted spectra for molecules absent from the library. The molecule is already present in the reference library — direct observed-spectrum matching is preferable to replacing observed spectra with predictions Accurate isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments are required — the article notes 'NEIMS currently does not have a method to model intensity peaks corresponding to isotopes in ion fragments' The ionization method is not electron ionization without retraining — the model was trained on EI spectra from NIST 2017 and would need retraining for other ionization methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Predict electron-ionization mass spectra for small molecules with a bidirectional MLP (NEIMS) over additive ECFP fingerprints, then use the predicted spectra to augment mass spectral reference libraries for library matching (~5 ms per molecule, 91.8% recall@10). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.9b00085
skills.summary: Predict electron-ionization mass spectra for small molecules with a bidirectional MLP (NEIMS) over additive ECFP fingerprints, then use the predicted spectra to augment mass spectral reference libraries for library matching (~5 ms per molecule, 91.8% recall@10).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule is already present in the reference library — direct observed-spectrum matching is preferable to replacing observed spectra with predictions Accurate isotope intensity peaks in ion fragments are required — the article notes 'NEIMS currently does not have a method to model intensity peaks corresponding to isotopes in ion fragments' The ionization method is not electron ionization without retraining — the model was trained on EI spectra from NIST 2017 and would need retraining for other ionization methods

skills.description: Use when comparing annotation models (e.g. ESP vs MLP/GNN baselines) on mass spectra candidate sets and you must reproduce or verify reported average-rank improvements such as 23.7%/37.2%.

skills.search_text: neural-network-annotation-evaluation Use when comparing annotation models (e.g. ESP vs MLP/GNN baselines) on mass spectra candidate sets and you must reproduce or verify reported average-rank improvements such as 23.7%/37.2%. Comparing models on top-five hit rate only, where the paper notes MLP approaches remain strong contenders and average rank may mislead Evaluating on NIST-20-trained models where the data cannot be published due to NIST license regulations and cannot be retrained locally Candidate sets whose size or candidate-similarity-to-target differs from the evaluation configuration, since annotation performance depends on these factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluate neural-network metabolite annotation models (MLP, GNN, ensemble ESP) using average rank and Rank@K metrics on candidate sets, and compute relative percentage improvements between models to verify claimed performance gains. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae490
skills.summary: Evaluate neural-network metabolite annotation models (MLP, GNN, ensemble ESP) using average rank and Rank@K metrics on candidate sets, and compute relative percentage improvements between models to verify claimed performance gains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing models on top-five hit rate only, where the paper notes MLP approaches remain strong contenders and average rank may mislead Evaluating on NIST-20-trained models where the data cannot be published due to NIST license regulations and cannot be retrained locally Candidate sets whose size or candidate-similarity-to-target differs from the evaluation configuration, since annotation performance depends on these factors

skills.description: Use when a paper describes a network's architecture concretely (layer count, hidden dimensions, output activation) and the goal is to reimplement, train, and validate it from the described spec and released codebase.
skills.name: neural-network-architecture-reconstruction
skills.search_text: neural-network-architecture-reconstruction Use when a paper describes a network's architecture concretely (layer count, hidden dimensions, output activation) and the goal is to reimplement, train, and validate it from the described spec and released codebase. Input is raw centroided spectra needing the main formula prediction model — this skill only reconstructs the auxiliary rescore/ranking network, not the dilated-convolution formula identifier. Working with FIDDLE v2.0.0, where the rescore model was redesigned as a Siamese architecture and the five-layer 416-208-104-26-13 spec no longer applies. Data lacking instrument labels or candidate formula lists, since the model is trained separately for Orbitrap vs. Q-TOF and requires per-candidate feature vectors. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstruct a published deep learning module from its paper-specified architecture and training protocol — here, FIDDLE's rescore network that estimates confidence scores for candidate formulas. It converts textual architecture descriptions (layer stack, hidden dimensions, activation, output) into working PyTorch code plus a reproducible training/scoring pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Reconstruct a published deep learning module from its paper-specified architecture and training protocol — here, FIDDLE's rescore network that estimates confidence scores for candidate formulas. It converts textual architecture descriptions (layer stack, hidden dimensions, activation, output) into working PyTorch code plus a reproducible training/scoring pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw centroided spectra needing the main formula prediction model — this skill only reconstructs the auxiliary rescore/ranking network, not the dilated-convolution formula identifier. Working with FIDDLE v2.0.0, where the rescore model was redesigned as a Siamese architecture and the five-layer 416-208-104-26-13 spec no longer applies. Data lacking instrument labels or candidate formula lists, since the model is trained separately for Orbitrap vs. Q-TOF and requires per-candidate feature vectors.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell count matrix (genes x cells, raw or normalized counts) needs cell-wise reaction-rate (fluxome) prediction and metabolite-variation estimates, e.g., comparing glucose-glutamine flux among cancer, myeloid, and T cells in tumor microenvironment data.

skills.search_text: neural-network-flux-balance-modeling Use when a single-cell count matrix (genes x cells, raw or normalized counts) needs cell-wise reaction-rate (fluxome) prediction and metabolite-variation estimates, e.g., comparing glucose-glutamine flux among cancer, myeloid, and T cells in tumor microenvironment data. Input is already a flux or feature table (e.g., pre-computed ssGSEA module scores) rather than a gene-by-cell count matrix. skills.summary: Estimates cell-wise metabolic flux and metabolite balance (stress) from scRNA-seq or bulk transcriptomics using scFEA/FLUXestimator, a graph neural network solver that enforces flux balance constraints over a curated human metabolic module map (e.g., M171 modules), enabling analysis of metabolic heterogeneity across cell types.

skills.description: Use when single-cell (or bulk) transcriptomics data must be converted to cell-wise metabolic flux estimates using a flux-balance-constrained neural network, e.g. rebuilding the scFEA factor-graph solver or reproducing its loss convergence.

skills.search_text: neural-network-flux-estimation Use when single-cell (or bulk) transcriptomics data must be converted to cell-wise metabolic flux estimates using a flux-balance-constrained neural network, e.g. rebuilding the scFEA factor-graph solver or reproducing its loss convergence. When working with formula-level predictors such as SCARF, which predict spectra at the subformula level rather than on molecular fragment graphs Before peaks have been assigned to fragment nodes within the 20 ppm tolerance — neutral-loss nodes depend on those assignments When only predicted spectra are available and no observed neutral losses can be grounded in experimental peak differences Augments per-molecule fragmentation DAGs—built by MAGMa-style substructure enumeration for ICEBERG training data—with neutral-loss nodes that connect fragment nodes to their observed neutral losses, completing the explanatory graph structure exported for model training. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Augments per-molecule fragmentation DAGs—built by MAGMa-style substructure enumeration for ICEBERG training data—with neutral-loss nodes that connect fragment nodes to their observed neutral losses, completing the explanatory graph structure exported for model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When working with formula-level predictors such as SCARF, which predict spectra at the subformula level rather than on molecular fragment graphs Before peaks have been assigned to fragment nodes within the 20 ppm tolerance — neutral-loss nodes depend on those assignments When only predicted spectra are available and no observed neutral losses can be grounded in experimental peak differences

skills.description: Use when decomposing external reference MS2 spectra (Mass Bank, GNPS) with pre-characterized Mass2Motifs and running motif-based spectral library matching, since loss fields are unsupported by matching tools.
skills.name: neutral-loss-omission-in-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: neutral-loss-omission-in-spectral-matching Use when decomposing external reference MS2 spectra (Mass Bank, GNPS) with pre-characterized Mass2Motifs and running motif-based spectral library matching, since loss fields are unsupported by matching tools. A spectral matching tool that natively supports neutral losses is available — the omission is a workaround, not a principled choice The goal is de novo substructure discovery on your own complex-mixture data rather than validating already-characterized motifs against reference libraries The MS2 spectra are information-poor (single collision energy, few fragments per metabolite) where MS2LDA itself works poorly http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 When validating MS2LDA Mass2Motifs against external spectral libraries such as Mass Bank and GNPS, co-occurring fragments of a motif are used as peaks but the motif's neutral losses are omitted, because spectral matching tools do not support losses. This skill prescribes that omission plus the 90% normalized-score acceptance threshold and the 0.1 probability cutoff used to validate transferred substructure annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: When validating MS2LDA Mass2Motifs against external spectral libraries such as Mass Bank and GNPS, co-occurring fragments of a motif are used as peaks but the motif's neutral losses are omitted, because spectral matching tools do not support losses. This skill prescribes that omission plus the 90% normalized-score acceptance threshold and the 0.1 probability cutoff used to validate transferred substructure annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A spectral matching tool that natively supports neutral losses is available — the omission is a workaround, not a principled choice The goal is de novo substructure discovery on your own complex-mixture data rather than validating already-characterized motifs against reference libraries The MS2 spectra are information-poor (single collision energy, few fragments per metabolite) where MS2LDA itself works poorly

skills.description: Use when per-compound MS/MS spectra spanning multiple collision energies (from MSP-derived data) must be transformed into a single enhanced spectrum containing fragment ions plus neutral-loss peaks in binarized (0/1) form before CNN-based metabolite identification.
skills.name: neutral-loss-peak-calculation
skills.search_text: neutral-loss-peak-calculation Use when per-compound MS/MS spectra spanning multiple collision energies (from MSP-derived data) must be transformed into a single enhanced spectrum containing fragment ions plus neutral-loss peaks in binarized (0/1) form before CNN-based metabolite identification. Spectra are already merged and intensity-binarized — re-applying the collapse would discard real collision-energy-specific structure. Intensity quantitation is the goal — binarization to 0/1 deliberately discards relative intensity information to reduce overfitting. The peak list should feed tools that require raw intensity values (e.g. library dot-product scoring against intensity-weighted reference spectra) rather than ChemEmbed's binarized CNN input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Enriches merged MS/MS spectra with calculated neutral-loss peaks (precursor m/z minus fragment m/z) and binarizes intensities, producing the enhanced spectral input used by ChemEmbed for metabolite identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: Enriches merged MS/MS spectra with calculated neutral-loss peaks (precursor m/z minus fragment m/z) and binarizes intensities, producing the enhanced spectral input used by ChemEmbed for metabolite identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are already merged and intensity-binarized — re-applying the collapse would discard real collision-energy-specific structure. Intensity quantitation is the goal — binarization to 0/1 deliberately discards relative intensity information to reduce overfitting. The peak list should feed tools that require raw intensity values (e.g. library dot-product scoring against intensity-weighted reference spectra) rather than ChemEmbed's binarized CNN input.

skills.description: Use when Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra containing both fragment and neutral-loss entries must be fed to a spectral-matching-based annotation tool (e.g. MS2Analyzer-style matching) that only accepts fragments.
skills.name: neutral-loss-removal-from-pseudo-spectra
skills.search_text: neutral-loss-removal-from-pseudo-spectra Use when Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra containing both fragment and neutral-loss entries must be fed to a spectral-matching-based annotation tool (e.g. MS2Analyzer-style matching) that only accepts fragments. When the annotation tool natively supports neutral losses — the removal is a workaround because 'losses are not currently supported by spectral matching tools', not an inherent requirement When the goal is motif discovery itself (unsupervised LDA extraction of fragments and neutral losses) rather than automated annotation of already-characterized motifs When pseudo-spectra are already fragment-only or come from negative-ionization-mode or non-beer matrices, which were not part of the reported validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Removes neutral-loss entries from Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra so they can be subjected to spectral matching for automated substructure annotation, because spectral matching tools do not support losses. This adaptation is what enabled 19 of the structurally characterized positive-mode beer Mass2Motifs to be correctly annotated. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Removes neutral-loss entries from Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra so they can be subjected to spectral matching for automated substructure annotation, because spectral matching tools do not support losses. This adaptation is what enabled 19 of the structurally characterized positive-mode beer Mass2Motifs to be correctly annotated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the annotation tool natively supports neutral losses — the removal is a workaround because 'losses are not currently supported by spectral matching tools', not an inherent requirement When the goal is motif discovery itself (unsupervised LDA extraction of fragments and neutral losses) rather than automated annotation of already-characterized motifs When pseudo-spectra are already fragment-only or come from negative-ionization-mode or non-beer matrices, which were not part of the reported validation

skills.description: Use when comparing parent and TP MS/MS fragment spectra (m/z–intensity peak lists) to score similarity for TP componentization, and equal neutral losses or a constant mass shift between fragments should contribute to the score.
skills.name: neutral-loss-spectrum-combination
skills.search_text: neutral-loss-spectrum-combination Use when comparing parent and TP MS/MS fragment spectra (m/z–intensity peak lists) to score similarity for TP componentization, and equal neutral losses or a constant mass shift between fragments should contribute to the score. Input is only MS1 feature data with no MS/MS fragment peak lists — spectral matching requires fragment spectra Candidate TPs are isomers that cannot be distinguished by MS (patRoon instead provides a 'Remove isomers' filter for this case) The goal is to prioritize candidate structures for a single feature — compound annotation (MetFrag, SIRIUS) rather than spectrum comparison is the appropriate step http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes MS/MS spectral similarity between parent and transformation-product (TP) fragment spectra in patRoon, combining matched fragments with neutral losses so that fragments related by a constant mass shift also contribute to cosine and Jaccard similarity scores. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04029
skills.summary: Computes MS/MS spectral similarity between parent and transformation-product (TP) fragment spectra in patRoon, combining matched fragments with neutral losses so that fragments related by a constant mass shift also contribute to cosine and Jaccard similarity scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only MS1 feature data with no MS/MS fragment peak lists — spectral matching requires fragment spectra Candidate TPs are isomers that cannot be distinguished by MS (patRoon instead provides a 'Remove isomers' filter for this case) The goal is to prioritize candidate structures for a single feature — compound annotation (MetFrag, SIRIUS) rather than spectrum comparison is the appropriate step

skills.search_text: neutral-loss-spectrum-derivation Use when preparing paired query-reference MS/MS inputs for TransExION: neutral-loss representations must be built alongside original-spectrum representations from MGF/h5py peak lists. When processing a single isolated spectrum with no reference partner — the neutral-loss MDM/aligned matrix is defined per (query, reference) pair, not per spectrum When the goal is classic peak matching only (cosine/modified cosine), where neutral-loss and mass-difference features are not part of the representation http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Converts each MS/MS spectrum into a hypothetical neutral-loss spectrum (precursor m/z minus fragment ion m/z) and then builds the neutral-loss mass difference matrix (MDM) and aligned matrix that serve as Transformer inputs for TransExION spectral similarity prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Converts each MS/MS spectrum into a hypothetical neutral-loss spectrum (precursor m/z minus fragment ion m/z) and then builds the neutral-loss mass difference matrix (MDM) and aligned matrix that serve as Transformer inputs for TransExION spectral similarity prediction.

skills.description: Use when cleaning MS/MS spectral libraries (MGF format) where adduct metadata must yield chemically coherent neutral masses, especially when [M]+ or [M]− adducts are annotated with a reported charge of zero.
skills.name: neutral-mass-derivation-from-adduct-annotations
skills.search_text: neutral-mass-derivation-from-adduct-annotations Use when cleaning MS/MS spectral libraries (MGF format) where adduct metadata must yield chemically coherent neutral masses, especially when [M]+ or [M]− adducts are annotated with a reported charge of zero. Input spectra lack adduct annotations entirely (or lack precursor m/z and ionization mode), since round 2 REQUIRE_COMPLETE_METADATA filters would simply discard them The target library contains non-small-molecule spectra outside the Spectraverse small-molecule curation scope You need the unmodified upstream matchms behavior for a non-Spectraverse pipeline — the required matchms.zip patch changes _get_neutral_mass semantics Derives and validates compound neutral masses from adduct annotations (e.g., [M]+, [M]−, [M+H]+) during matchms-based MS/MS library curation, using a patched matchms whose _get_neutral_mass function excludes [M]+/[M]− spectra that report a net charge of zero. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06256
skills.summary: Derives and validates compound neutral masses from adduct annotations (e.g., [M]+, [M]−, [M+H]+) during matchms-based MS/MS library curation, using a patched matchms whose _get_neutral_mass function excludes [M]+/[M]− spectra that report a net charge of zero.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack adduct annotations entirely (or lack precursor m/z and ionization mode), since round 2 REQUIRE_COMPLETE_METADATA filters would simply discard them The target library contains non-small-molecule spectra outside the Spectraverse small-molecule curation scope You need the unmodified upstream matchms behavior for a non-Spectraverse pipeline — the required matchms.zip patch changes _get_neutral_mass semantics

skills.description: Use when a mass distance network of LC-MS features (e.g. from asari-preprocessed feature tables like ecoli_pos.tsv) has been converted into a 2-tier adduct/isotope tree and the neutral M0 mass of each empirical compound must be recovered.
skills.name: neutral-mass-regression-inference
skills.search_text: neutral-mass-regression-inference Use when a mass distance network of LC-MS features (e.g. from asari-preprocessed feature tables like ecoli_pos.tsv) has been converted into a 2-tier adduct/isotope tree and the neutral M0 mass of each empirical compound must be recovered. Input is a raw centroided or profile mass spectrum rather than a preprocessed feature table — khipu expects a tab-delimited feature table with feature ID, m/z, rtime and intensities columns, typically from asari Annotation already requires chromatographic or tandem-MS confirmation of isomers — regression infers a neutral mass but cannot resolve N1- vs N8-acetylspermidine-like isomer mixtures; LC-MS/MS with authentic standards is needed Only a subset of ions is matched to neither trunk nor branch — the regression depends on matched m/z values; singleton features that failed the DAG/tree conversion carry no usable ion-to-grid match http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Infers the neutral mass of the M0 original compound from an annotated khipu tree by linear regression of matched m/z values against the theoretical khipu grid of isotope/adduct patterns, as implemented in the khipu Python package for LC-MS metabolomics and isotope tracing data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05810
skills.summary: Infers the neutral mass of the M0 original compound from an annotated khipu tree by linear regression of matched m/z values against the theoretical khipu grid of isotope/adduct patterns, as implemented in the khipu Python package for LC-MS metabolomics and isotope tracing data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw centroided or profile mass spectrum rather than a preprocessed feature table — khipu expects a tab-delimited feature table with feature ID, m/z, rtime and intensities columns, typically from asari Annotation already requires chromatographic or tandem-MS confirmation of isomers — regression infers a neutral mass but cannot resolve N1- vs N8-acetylspermidine-like isomer mixtures; LC-MS/MS with authentic standards is needed Only a subset of ions is matched to neither trunk nor branch — the regression depends on matched m/z values; singleton features that failed the DAG/tree conversion carry no usable ion-to-grid match

skills.description: Use when you have microbeMASST/microbeMASST-style batch search outputs (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) plus NCBI lineage Newick/JSON taxon data and need a lineage-consistent taxonomic tree showing which microbes may produce a queried metabolite.
skills.name: newick-tree-filtering-and-pruning
skills.search_text: newick-tree-filtering-and-pruning Use when you have microbeMASST/microbeMASST-style batch search outputs (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) plus NCBI lineage Newick/JSON taxon data and need a lineage-consistent taxonomic tree showing which microbes may produce a queried metabolite. Input is a per-scan search result alone (_matches.tsv, _library.tsv, _datasets.tsv) with no taxonomic lineage data — the tree cannot be built without NCBI lineage information. You only need library hits for MSI Level 2 annotation; use _library.tsv output rather than taxonomic tree pruning. The batch search output has not been re-run to convergence (skip_existing=True) — incomplete matches would produce a tree missing taxa. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Filters an NCBI lineage taxonomy tree to only taxa whose spectra matched in a domainMASST batch search, aggregates match counts and proportions across ranks, and converts the result into a D3-consumable JSON hierarchy for rendering an interactive taxonomic HTML tree. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Filters an NCBI lineage taxonomy tree to only taxa whose spectra matched in a domainMASST batch search, aggregates match counts and proportions across ranks, and converts the result into a D3-consumable JSON hierarchy for rendering an interactive taxonomic HTML tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a per-scan search result alone (_matches.tsv, _library.tsv, _datasets.tsv) with no taxonomic lineage data — the tree cannot be built without NCBI lineage information. You only need library hits for MSI Level 2 annotation; use _library.tsv output rather than taxonomic tree pruning. The batch search output has not been re-run to convergence (skip_existing=True) — incomplete matches would produce a tree missing taxa.

skills.description: Use when a phylogenetic analysis has produced a species-level distance matrix (e.g. from averaged compareMS2 pairwise spectra comparisons) and the reconstructed topology must be exported as a Newick (.nwk) file for downstream inspection or validation.
skills.name: newick-tree-format-serialization
skills.search_text: newick-tree-format-serialization Use when a phylogenetic analysis has produced a species-level distance matrix (e.g. from averaged compareMS2 pairwise spectra comparisons) and the reconstructed topology must be exported as a Newick (.nwk) file for downstream inspection or validation. The input is raw spectral data and no pairwise compareMS2 distance matrix has yet been computed — tree serialization presupposes distances are already available The goal is peptide/protein identification by database search rather than distance-based phylogenetic comparison — compareMS2 deliberately does not use sequence databases or spectral libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Serialize a distance-based phylogenetic tree (e.g. UPGMA or neighbor-joining over compareMS2 spectra dot-product distances, averaged across individuals per species) into the Newick text format so the reconstructed primate topology can be stored, shared, and validated against the published unique correct tree. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.6162
skills.summary: Serialize a distance-based phylogenetic tree (e.g. UPGMA or neighbor-joining over compareMS2 spectra dot-product distances, averaged across individuals per species) into the Newick text format so the reconstructed primate topology can be stored, shared, and validated against the published unique correct tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw spectral data and no pairwise compareMS2 distance matrix has yet been computed — tree serialization presupposes distances are already available The goal is peptide/protein identification by database search rather than distance-based phylogenetic comparison — compareMS2 deliberately does not use sequence databases or spectral libraries

skills.description: Use when a symmetric pairwise distance matrix over tandem MS datasets has been computed (e.g., by compareMS2) and a rooted, ultrametric tree in Newick format is the required output for phylogenetic display or downstream tooling.
skills.name: newick-tree-serialization
skills.search_text: newick-tree-serialization Use when a symmetric pairwise distance matrix over tandem MS datasets has been computed (e.g., by compareMS2) and a rooted, ultrametric tree in Newick format is the required output for phylogenetic display or downstream tooling. Input is raw tandem MS spectra or MGF files rather than an already-computed distance matrix — the pairwise comparison phase must run first A non-ultrametric or bootstrapped tree is required (e.g., neighbor-joining with support values); UPGMA assumes a constant rate and produces a rooted ultrametric tree without replicate support http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Converts a pairwise distance matrix from tandem MS dataset comparisons into a rooted Newick-format phylogenetic tree using UPGMA (implemented in JavaScript in compareMS2 2.0), so that molecular-phylogenetic relationships between LC-MS/MS datasets can be serialized and rendered. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00457
skills.summary: Converts a pairwise distance matrix from tandem MS dataset comparisons into a rooted Newick-format phylogenetic tree using UPGMA (implemented in JavaScript in compareMS2 2.0), so that molecular-phylogenetic relationships between LC-MS/MS datasets can be serialized and rendered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw tandem MS spectra or MGF files rather than an already-computed distance matrix — the pairwise comparison phase must run first A non-ultrametric or bootstrapped tree is required (e.g., neighbor-joining with support values); UPGMA assumes a constant rate and produces a rooted ultrametric tree without replicate support

skills.description: Use when running mummichog module analysis on a significant m/z feature list and you need to partition the matched-metabolite subnetworks into structural modules for activity scoring against a permuted null.
skills.name: newman-spectral-split-subnetwork-identification
skills.search_text: newman-spectral-split-subnetwork-identification Use when running mummichog module analysis on a significant m/z feature list and you need to partition the matched-metabolite subnetworks into structural modules for activity scoring against a permuted null. When the goal is definitive metabolite identification — mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification When mass balance across reactions is required — mass balance is almost impossible within serum or urine samples because producing reactions occur in other tissues http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Within mummichog's module analysis, tentatively matched metabolites are grouped into subnetworks of one to four reactions, and structural modules are identified using Newman's spectral split algorithm to score pathway/network activity from untargeted LC/MS feature tables without prior metabolite identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: Within mummichog's module analysis, tentatively matched metabolites are grouped into subnetworks of one to four reactions, and structural modules are identified using Newman's spectral split algorithm to score pathway/network activity from untargeted LC/MS feature tables without prior metabolite identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is definitive metabolite identification — mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification When mass balance across reactions is required — mass balance is almost impossible within serum or urine samples because producing reactions occur in other tissues

skills.description: Use when estimating parameters (e.g. mean and SD) of a truncated normal distribution via maximum likelihood on left-truncated metabolomics data, where missing values below the LOD require iterative numeric optimization.
skills.name: newton-raphson-numeric-optimization
skills.search_text: newton-raphson-numeric-optimization Use when estimating parameters (e.g. mean and SD) of a truncated normal distribution via maximum likelihood on left-truncated metabolomics data, where missing values below the LOD require iterative numeric optimization. Metabolite data are heavily non-normal, since the likelihood relies on a normality assumption for the truncated distribution (noted as a limitation in the paper) Missingness below the LOD is excessive or the sample is very small, making truncated-likelihood estimation unstable (higher RMSE variability observed for KNN-TN) The full likelihood including the missing-data mechanism is needed — the KNN-TN likelihood is based solely on observed data and does not model MNAR/MAR/MCAR explicitly http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Newton-Raphson iterative root-finding/maximum-likelihood optimization, as applied in KNN-TN to estimate truncated-normal metabolite means and standard deviations from metabolomics data with missing values below the limit of detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6
skills.summary: Newton-Raphson iterative root-finding/maximum-likelihood optimization, as applied in KNN-TN to estimate truncated-normal metabolite means and standard deviations from metabolomics data with missing values below the limit of detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metabolite data are heavily non-normal, since the likelihood relies on a normality assumption for the truncated distribution (noted as a limitation in the paper) Missingness below the LOD is excessive or the sample is very small, making truncated-likelihood estimation unstable (higher RMSE variability observed for KNN-TN) The full likelihood including the missing-data mechanism is needed — the KNN-TN likelihood is based solely on observed data and does not model MNAR/MAR/MCAR explicitly

skills.description: Use when a Nextflow workflow (e.g., LC-MS metabolomics processing) has finished or failed and you must audit what ran, with which container/parameters, on which resources, or verify cross-platform reproducibility.
skills.name: nextflow-execution-report-interpretation
skills.search_text: nextflow-execution-report-interpretation Use when a Nextflow workflow (e.g., LC-MS metabolomics processing) has finished or failed and you must audit what ran, with which container/parameters, on which resources, or verify cross-platform reproducibility. When the goal is scientific provenance of the data analysis itself (parameters, peak tables) rather than execution metadata — the reports capture retrospective provenance, not MS-DIAL/MS-FLO parameter semantics When auditing a non-Nextflow pipeline (e.g., CWL, Snakemake), which will not emit these report artifacts http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Interprets Nextflow retrospective provenance artifacts — execution_report.html, execution_timeline.html, and the execution log — from an LC-MS metabolomics workflow run to audit runtime, resource usage, versions, parameters, and container metadata, and to verify reproducibility claims. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00364
skills.summary: Interprets Nextflow retrospective provenance artifacts — execution_report.html, execution_timeline.html, and the execution log — from an LC-MS metabolomics workflow run to audit runtime, resource usage, versions, parameters, and container metadata, and to verify reproducibility claims.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify a Nextflow workflow's structural complexity — enumerate every process in main.nf and count user-facing parameters in conf/*.config to compare pipelines' complexity.
skills.name: nextflow-pipeline-structure-analysis
skills.search_text: nextflow-pipeline-structure-analysis Use when you need to quantify a Nextflow workflow's structural complexity — enumerate every process in main.nf and count user-facing parameters in conf/*.config to compare pipelines' complexity. The goal is to execute the pipeline and reproduce results (e.g. run nextflow run main.nf -profile docker) rather than characterize its structure. The workflow under analysis is not a Nextflow workflow, so process enumeration from main.nf and conf/*.config does not apply. You need runtime metrics (CPU, memory, wall time) rather than static structural counts — use the execution_report.html and execution_timeline.html logs instead. Enumerates the processes and counts the user-facing configuration parameters of a Nextflow workflow by parsing its main.nf and conf/ files, so structural complexity can be quantified and compared across pipelines (here, Nextflow4MS-DIAL's two-process MS-DIAL→MS-FLO design versus Metaboigniter's 20+ processes and 200+ parameters). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00364
skills.summary: Enumerates the processes and counts the user-facing configuration parameters of a Nextflow workflow by parsing its main.nf and conf/ files, so structural complexity can be quantified and compared across pipelines (here, Nextflow4MS-DIAL's two-process MS-DIAL→MS-FLO design versus Metaboigniter's 20+ processes and 200+ parameters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to execute the pipeline and reproduce results (e.g. run nextflow run main.nf -profile docker) rather than characterize its structure. skills.description: Use when a Nextflow workflow run (e.g. containerized MS-DIAL/MS-FLO processing of .mzML LC-MS data) must yield retrospective provenance artifacts — execution reports, timeline, and logs — documenting runtime, resources, and data derivation.
skills.name: nextflow-provenance-capture
skills.search_text: nextflow-provenance-capture Use when a Nextflow workflow run (e.g. containerized MS-DIAL/MS-FLO processing of .mzML LC-MS data) must yield retrospective provenance artifacts — execution reports, timeline, and logs — documenting runtime, resources, and data derivation. You need prospective/FAIR-compliant provenance (e.g. workflow deposit to WorkflowHub) — the paper states this is not yet done and is future work. Input is not a Nextflow-executed workflow (e.g. a manual MS-DIAL GUI run) — there is no Nextflow provenance machinery to capture. You need quantitative scalability or reproducibility metrics — the authors note these were not quantitatively measured. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Captures retrospective provenance of a Nextflow workflow execution by collecting Nextflow's task execution reports, intermediate results, and data files stored in each task's working directory, as demonstrated by the Nextflow4MS-DIAL LC-MS metabolomics pipeline (MS-DIAL -> MS-FLO). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00364

skills.search_text: nist-cosine-similarity-scoring Use when a reduced candidate set of mass spectra (e.g. grouped by SPLASH second-block value) must be scored and ranked against a query spectrum to quantify search-space reduction versus similarity-based recall. Spectra are not represented as peak-intensity vectors suitable for cosine scoring (e.g. raw profile-mode data not yet peak-picked) The goal is identity assignment via the full SPLASH hash block rather than similarity-based recall over a prefiltered candidate set The reference library is the NIST 14 library itself, which cannot be released publicly and is excluded from the open MoNA deposit http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Scores query-reference mass spectrum pairs with the NIST cosine similarity computed on peak-intensity vectors, then ranks candidates and evaluates recall at a fixed score threshold. skills.search_text: nist-spectral-library-annotation-processing Reference for exporting spectra from the NIST20 MS/MS spectral library and cleaning expert-curated formula annotations (10 ppm mass consistency, glycan/peptide removal) before evaluating formula-annotation precision/recall or retrieval. skills.search_text: nist-srm-1950-plasma-qc-pool-handling Decision support for organizing NIST SRM 1950 plasma QC-pool sample sets — 112 specimens, 40 QC pools, 10 blanks — prior to DEIMoS feature detection and cross-sample alignment. The input corpus is not the NIST SRM 1950 plasma study (e.g. Bruker or Waters datasets with 9 or 6 study samples in triplicate) — the 112/40/10 sample structure and QC-pool alignment anchors are specific to this study. No analytical replicate structure exists (single-run acquisition), since the QC-pool handling relies on 3 replicates per sample class for cross-sample alignment. Blank samples were not acquired, since blank exclusion across all blanks is a prerequisite filtering step in this workflow. skills.search_text: nmr-baseline-correction Use when a raw 1D NMR spectrum (ppm scale and intensity array) shows a curved or offset baseline that must be subtracted prior to multivariate statistical analysis, and dense peak regions risk being over-corrected by a naive spline fit. Input is already a baseline-corrected or variance-stabilised spectrum destined directly for multivariate analysis Task is 2D NMR processing, segmental alignment, spectral scaling, or automated phase correction rather than baseline flattening The goal is isotopomer distribution derivation from NMR multiplet and GC-MS data (metabolabpytools scope) http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Reconstructs MetaboLabPy's SplineBaseline approach: anchor a cubic spline on sparse signal-free baseline points, then apply a 'linear-spline' fallback that inserts intermediate baseline points along straight lines between adjacent anchors separated by more than a set maximum number of data points, preventing over-correction in dense spectral regions of 1D NMR spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Reconstructs MetaboLabPy's SplineBaseline approach: anchor a cubic spline on sparse signal-free baseline points, then apply a 'linear-spline' fallback that inserts intermediate baseline points along straight lines between adjacent anchors separated by more than a set maximum number of data points, preventing over-correction in dense spectral regions of 1D NMR spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a baseline-corrected or variance-stabilised spectrum destined directly for multivariate analysis Task is 2D NMR processing, segmental alignment, spectral scaling, or automated phase correction rather than baseline flattening The goal is isotopomer distribution derivation from NMR multiplet and GC-MS data (metabolabpytools scope)

skills.description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra (Bruker or Agilent/Varian FID, or Bruker 1r files) show baseline distortion from macromolecules in extracts or an intense peak dominating less intense neighboring ones, before alignment or binning.
skills.name: nmr-baseline-correction
skills.search_text: nmr-baseline-correction Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra (Bruker or Agilent/Varian FID, or Bruker 1r files) show baseline distortion from macromolecules in extracts or an intense peak dominating less intense neighboring ones, before alignment or binning. Input is already a bucket/intensity matrix (post-binning) — baseline correction operates on spectra, and buckets failing the signal-to-noise filter are handled at the output step instead Data are 2D NMR spectra — NMRProcFlow is dedicated to 1D (1H & 13C) spectra processing The processing need is deconvolution-based quantification in crowded regions with heavy peak overlap — that method is only planned in a future version of NMRProcFlow http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Apply baseline correction to 1D NMR metabolomics spectra (1H & 13C) within NMRProcFlow's processing chain, choosing either a 'locally' scoped correction on selected ppm zones or a 'fully' scoped correction across the whole ppm scale. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Apply baseline correction to 1D NMR metabolomics spectra (1H & 13C) within NMRProcFlow's processing chain, choosing either a 'locally' scoped correction on selected ppm zones or a 'fully' scoped correction across the whole ppm scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a bucket/intensity matrix (post-binning) — baseline correction operates on spectra, and buckets failing the signal-to-noise filter are handled at the output step instead Data are 2D NMR spectra — NMRProcFlow is dedicated to 1D (1H & 13C) spectra processing The processing need is deconvolution-based quantification in crowded regions with heavy peak overlap — that method is only planned in a future version of NMRProcFlow

skills.description: Use when automatically phasing a series of 1D-NMR spectra and a phase-corrected reference spectrum exists: baseline-only edge regions (>10.0 ppm and <−0.5 ppm) can be used to define an optimisation objective for zero/first-order phase (ph0/ph1).
skills.name: nmr-baseline-region-objective-definition
skills.search_text: nmr-baseline-region-objective-definition Use when automatically phasing a series of 1D-NMR spectra and a phase-corrected reference spectrum exists: baseline-only edge regions (>10.0 ppm and <−0.5 ppm) can be used to define an optimisation objective for zero/first-order phase (ph0/ph1). Edge regions (>10.0 ppm, <−0.5 ppm) are not baseline-only — e.g. broad water/DCM resonances or buffer peaks contaminate them, making the left–right difference meaningless as a phasing objective No phase-corrected reference spectrum is available, since ph0/ph1 initialisation for the series is taken from it Task is 2D-NMR processing or isotopomer/tracer analysis rather than phasing of 1D-NMR spectra series http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Defines the objective function used by MetaboLabPy's reference-spectrum-based automatic phase correction: the absolute difference between the baseline signal in the left (>10.0 ppm) and right (<−0.5 ppm) edge regions of a series of 1D-NMR spectra, minimised with Powell's conjugate direction method to derive per-spectrum ph0/ph1 values. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Defines the objective function used by MetaboLabPy's reference-spectrum-based automatic phase correction: the absolute difference between the baseline signal in the left (>10.0 ppm) and right (<−0.5 ppm) edge regions of a series of 1D-NMR spectra, minimised with Powell's conjugate direction method to derive per-spectrum ph0/ph1 values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Edge regions (>10.0 ppm, <−0.5 ppm) are not baseline-only — e.g. broad water/DCM resonances or buffer peaks contaminate them, making the left–right difference meaningless as a phasing objective No phase-corrected reference spectrum is available, since ph0/ph1 initialisation for the series is taken from it Task is 2D-NMR processing or isotopomer/tracer analysis rather than phasing of 1D-NMR spectra series

skills.summary: Reshape the binned NMR data matrix produced by upstream bucketing into the exact input formats required by MetaboAnalyst (samples-by-variables CSV) and Workflows4Metabolomics (three .TABULAR files), so repository data can be analyzed without manual reformatting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not NMR-based metabolomics data from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench (CloMet's harmonization focuses on NMR-based metabolomics) The data are already in a MetaboAnalyst CSV or W4M dataMatrix/sampleMetadata/variableMetadata layout, so reshaping would be redundant The goal is to apply data processing algorithms rather than convert file formats — CloMet explicitly leaves processing out of scope

skills.search_text: nmr-biomarker-hazard-ratio-estimation Use when UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations (original or ukbnmr remove_technical_variation output) must be tested for association with incident disease endpoints via per-SD Cox models adjusted for age and sex. The data have not yet passed through remove_technical_variation and the goal is QC itself — no prefiltering or downstream modelling should precede that function The analysis targets genetic associations (GWAS) rather than epidemiological incident-disease Cox models The endpoint is a continuous trait rather than incident CAD/stroke requiring survival analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3335 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A skill for running epidemiological biomarker association scans: per-biomarker Cox proportional hazards models over the 249 UK Biobank NMR metabolic biomarkers for incident coronary artery disease and stroke, computed on both original and ukbnmr QC-corrected concentrations to quantify how removing technical variation changes hazard ratios. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: A skill for running epidemiological biomarker association scans: per-biomarker Cox proportional hazards models over the 249 UK Biobank NMR metabolic biomarkers for incident coronary artery disease and stroke, computed on both original and ukbnmr QC-corrected concentrations to quantify how removing technical variation changes hazard ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have not yet passed through remove_technical_variation and the goal is QC itself — no prefiltering or downstream modelling should precede that function The analysis targets genetic associations (GWAS) rather than epidemiological incident-disease Cox models The endpoint is a continuous trait rather than incident CAD/stroke requiring survival analysis

skills.description: Use when preparing the 107 non-derived UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations for robust regression-based removal of technical variation and some biomarkers contain exact 0 values.
skills.name: nmr-biomarker-log-transformation-with-zero-offset
skills.search_text: nmr-biomarker-log-transformation-with-zero-offset Use when preparing the 107 non-derived UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations for robust regression-based removal of technical variation and some biomarkers contain exact 0 values. Biomarker data that are already log-transformed or already processed via remove_technical_variation() — applying the offset twice would distort concentrations Analysis of derived biomarkers and ratios — the procedure is recommended only for the 107 non-derived biomarkers, with composites re-derived afterwards via recompute_derived_biomarkers() Datasets with samples or biomarker columns pre-filtered before calling remove_technical_variation(), since the algorithms expect all data present http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Log-transforms absolute NMR biomarker concentrations from UK Biobank Nightingale measurements, adding a small offset (half the minimum non-zero value) to biomarkers that contain zeros so the log transform is defined prior to sequential regression of technical covariates. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: Log-transforms absolute NMR biomarker concentrations from UK Biobank Nightingale measurements, adding a small offset (half the minimum non-zero value) to biomarkers that contain zeros so the log transform is defined prior to sequential regression of technical covariates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Biomarker data that are already log-transformed or already processed via remove_technical_variation() — applying the offset twice would distort concentrations Analysis of derived biomarkers and ratios — the procedure is recommended only for the 107 non-derived biomarkers, with composites re-derived afterwards via recompute_derived_biomarkers() Datasets with samples or biomarker columns pre-filtered before calling remove_technical_variation(), since the algorithms expect all data present

skills.description: Use when raw NMR metabolomics biomarker concentrations (e.g., 226 Nightingale Health platform measures in EDTA plasma/serum) contain zeroes marking values below the detection limit and must be made analysis-ready for per-cohort Cox survival models.
skills.name: nmr-biomarker-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: nmr-biomarker-matrix-preprocessing Use when raw NMR metabolomics biomarker concentrations (e.g., 226 Nightingale Health platform measures in EDTA plasma/serum) contain zeroes marking values below the detection limit and must be made analysis-ready for per-cohort Cox survival models. The biomarker matrix contains no zeroes/below-detection-limit entries and values are already on the log scale needed for modeling — the x+1 offset would distort genuine low concentrations. The goal is a clinically deployable mortality risk score in concentration units; the paper explicitly states the score built on per-cohort scaled biomarker values 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic' and that concentration-unit scores still need to be created. The data come from a different metabolomics platform or untargeted assay for which per-study z-scaling of 226 Nightingale biomarkers is not the appropriate normalization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Per-cohort preprocessing of Nightingale Health NMR metabolic biomarker measurements: adds 1 to biomarker values below the detection limit (zeroes), log-transforms all biomarkers, and scales them to standard deviation units within each study, yielding an analysis-ready biomarker matrix for Cox proportional hazards survival modeling. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: Per-cohort preprocessing of Nightingale Health NMR metabolic biomarker measurements: adds 1 to biomarker values below the detection limit (zeroes), log-transforms all biomarkers, and scales them to standard deviation units within each study, yielding an analysis-ready biomarker matrix for Cox proportional hazards survival modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biomarker matrix contains no zeroes/below-detection-limit entries and values are already on the log scale needed for modeling — the x+1 offset would distort genuine low concentrations. The goal is a clinically deployable mortality risk score in concentration units; the paper explicitly states the score built on per-cohort scaled biomarker values 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic' and that concentration-unit scores still need to be created. The data come from a different metabolomics platform or untargeted assay for which per-study z-scaling of 226 Nightingale biomarkers is not the appropriate normalization.

skills.description: Use when you have post-QC UK Biobank NMR biomarker data produced by remove_technical_variation() and need the derived composites (61), original ratios (81), or extended ratios (76) recomputed from adjusted non-derived biomarkers rather than directly adjusted.
skills.name: nmr-biomarker-ratio-recomputation
skills.search_text: nmr-biomarker-ratio-recomputation Use when you have post-QC UK Biobank NMR biomarker data produced by remove_technical_variation() and need the derived composites (61), original ratios (81), or extended ratios (76) recomputed from adjusted non-derived biomarkers rather than directly adjusted. The input is raw UK Biobank field export data that has not yet been processed with remove_technical_variation() — no prefiltering of samples or columns should be done before technical variation removal You only need the 107 non-derived biomarkers and have no use for composites, ratios, or the extended Nightingale panel You intend to directly adjust the original composite biomarkers and ratios in your own model instead of re-deriving them from adjusted parts — the article warns this can introduce new unwanted variation into ratios and percentages http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Recomputes the 61 composite biomarkers and 81 biomarker ratios of the UK Biobank NMR metabolomics panel from the 107 non-derived biomarkers after removal of technical variation, optionally extending with 76 additional biologically motivated ratios, because adjusting component biomarkers independently would otherwise introduce new unwanted variation into ratios and composites. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: Recomputes the 61 composite biomarkers and 81 biomarker ratios of the UK Biobank NMR metabolomics panel from the 107 non-derived biomarkers after removal of technical variation, optionally extending with 76 additional biologically motivated ratios, because adjusting component biomarkers independently would otherwise introduce new unwanted variation into ratios and composites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw UK Biobank field export data that has not yet been processed with remove_technical_variation() — no prefiltering of samples or columns should be done before technical variation removal You only need the 107 non-derived biomarkers and have no use for composites, ratios, or the extended Nightingale panel You intend to directly adjust the original composite biomarkers and ratios in your own model instead of re-deriving them from adjusted parts — the article warns this can introduce new unwanted variation into ratios and percentages

skills.description: Use when a 1D 1H/13C NMR spectra processing pipeline has produced a bucket table (ppm intervals × per-spectrum intensities) and noisy, low-intensity buckets must be removed before statistical analysis.
skills.name: nmr-bucket-snr-filtering
skills.search_text: nmr-bucket-snr-filtering Use when a 1D 1H/13C NMR spectra processing pipeline has produced a bucket table (ppm intervals × per-spectrum intensities) and noisy, low-intensity buckets must be removed before statistical analysis. Input is raw FID or unprocessed spectra — binning must be done first so a bucket table exists to filter The analysis goal is peak deconvolution or quantification of crowded, heavily overlapping regions, which NMRProcFlow planned as a future feature rather than SNR-based bucket filtering Only baseline correction, ppm calibration, or alignment is needed — these are separate upstream processing steps, not bucket filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Retain or discard buckets from an NMR bucket table according to their signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), as implemented in NMRProcFlow, which permits this filtering either during the computing process or at the output step. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Retain or discard buckets from an NMR bucket table according to their signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), as implemented in NMRProcFlow, which permits this filtering either during the computing process or at the output step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FID or unprocessed spectra — binning must be done first so a bucket table exists to filter The analysis goal is peak deconvolution or quantification of crowded, heavily overlapping regions, which NMRProcFlow planned as a future feature rather than SNR-based bucket filtering Only baseline correction, ppm calibration, or alignment is needed — these are separate upstream processing steps, not bucket filtering

skills.description: Use when a processed 1D NMR bucket table (ppm-interval buckets per spectrum) must be handed off, without intermediate file conversions, to online statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow.
skills.name: nmr-bucket-table-export
skills.search_text: nmr-bucket-table-export Use when a processed 1D NMR bucket table (ppm-interval buckets per spectrum) must be handed off, without intermediate file conversions, to online statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow. The input is raw FID data from Bruker or Agilent (Varian) instruments — spectra processing (calibration, baseline correction, realignment, binning) must run in NMRProcFlow first; this skill only exports the already-processed bucket table. The bucket table is already in a statistical-tools-ready matrix format with class labels — re-exporting adds no value. The goal is to perform the downstream statistical analysis itself (e.g. PCA, clustering) rather than producing the import-compatible data matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 Reshapes NMRProcFlow's SNR-filtered bucket table into a samples-by-buckets data matrix with experimental-factor class-label columns, exported in the format NMRProcFlow documents as compatible with MetaboAnalyst 3.0 and BioStatFlow, so processed spectral data reaches downstream statistics without file conversions. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Reshapes NMRProcFlow's SNR-filtered bucket table into a samples-by-buckets data matrix with experimental-factor class-label columns, exported in the format NMRProcFlow documents as compatible with MetaboAnalyst 3.0 and BioStatFlow, so processed spectral data reaches downstream statistics without file conversions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FID data from Bruker or Agilent (Varian) instruments — spectra processing (calibration, baseline correction, realignment, binning) must run in NMRProcFlow first; this skill only exports the already-processed bucket table. The bucket table is already in a statistical-tools-ready matrix format with class labels — re-exporting adds no value. The goal is to perform the downstream statistical analysis itself (e.g. PCA, clustering) rather than producing the import-compatible data matrix.

skills.description: Use when MWAS results from 1H NMR metabonomic data need to be visualized as a skyline plot against chemical shift (ppm), e.g. reproducing paper figures like the BMI association plot over the δ 0.80–1.60 ppm lipid region.
skills.name: nmr-chemical-shift-axis-plotting
skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-axis-plotting Use when MWAS results from 1H NMR metabonomic data need to be visualized as a skyline plot against chemical shift (ppm), e.g. reproducing paper figures like the BMI association plot over the δ 0.80–1.60 ppm lipid region. Input data are mass spectrometry or other non-spectral metabolomics results — the skyline is indexed by 1H NMR chemical shift (ppm), not m/z or retention time The analysis goal is statistical association modeling itself (partial correlations / generalized linear models with confounder adjustment) rather than visualization of already-computed MWAS results A tabular or Manhattan-style summary of associations is needed rather than a spectrum-anchored skyline over a specific ppm region http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Renders metabolome-wide association (MWAS) results along the 1H NMR chemical shift axis as a skyline plot, using MWASTools' MWAS_skylineNMR on a SummarizedExperiment of NMR spectra plus an association results matrix. It maps statistical signal (sign-adjusted -log10 p-values) to spectral position (ppm) so metabolite regions of association are visually interpretable. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Renders metabolome-wide association (MWAS) results along the 1H NMR chemical shift axis as a skyline plot, using MWASTools' MWAS_skylineNMR on a SummarizedExperiment of NMR spectra plus an association results matrix. It maps statistical signal (sign-adjusted -log10 p-values) to spectral position (ppm) so metabolite regions of association are visually interpretable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are mass spectrometry or other non-spectral metabolomics results — the skyline is indexed by 1H NMR chemical shift (ppm), not m/z or retention time The analysis goal is statistical association modeling itself (partial correlations / generalized linear models with confounder adjustment) rather than visualization of already-computed MWAS results A tabular or Manhattan-style summary of associations is needed rather than a spectrum-anchored skyline over a specific ppm region

skills.description: Use when preparing a 13C NMR peak list (comma-separated carbon ppm shifts) as model input for the NMR2Struct multitask spectrum-to-structure CNN/transformer pipeline.
skills.name: nmr-chemical-shift-binning
skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-binning Use when preparing a 13C NMR peak list (comma-separated carbon ppm shifts) as model input for the NMR2Struct multitask spectrum-to-structure CNN/transformer pipeline. The input is a full 1H NMR spectrum (ppm, intensity pairs) — that channel requires linear interpolation to a 28000-point grid and normalization by highest intensity, not shift binning The 13C data is a continuous spectrum/FID rather than a peak-position list — the model was trained on simulated MestreNova-derived chemical shift lists, so raw unprocessed spectra are out of scope The target molecule falls outside the model's demonstrated scope (more than 19 heavy atoms) http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Extracts 13C chemical shift peak positions from a carbon NMR spectrum and bins them into an 80-bin binary vector spanning 3.42 to 231.3 ppm, producing the 13C component of the concatenated input representation for the NMR2Struct multitask spectrum-to-structure model. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.4c01132
skills.summary: Extracts 13C chemical shift peak positions from a carbon NMR spectrum and bins them into an 80-bin binary vector spanning 3.42 to 231.3 ppm, producing the 13C component of the concatenated input representation for the NMR2Struct multitask spectrum-to-structure model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a full 1H NMR spectrum (ppm, intensity pairs) — that channel requires linear interpolation to a 28000-point grid and normalization by highest intensity, not shift binning The 13C data is a continuous spectrum/FID rather than a peak-position list — the model was trained on simulated MestreNova-derived chemical shift lists, so raw unprocessed spectra are out of scope The target molecule falls outside the model's demonstrated scope (more than 19 heavy atoms)

skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-curation Use when building or extending a metabolite NMR chemical-shift reference library for ROI-based metabolite identification, e.g., swapping the HMDB source for BMRB assignments to drop into ROIAL-NMR. The goal is identifying ROIs automatically from raw spectra — the paper states automated ROI identification is beyond the current scope; ROIs must be user-defined first The goal is absolute quantification of metabolite concentrations — the program's primary aim is identification/categorization, not quantification The input is already a validated ROIAL-NMR-format database workbook (re-curation is unnecessary) http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Curate a metabolite proton NMR assignment library from a biological NMR reference database (e.g., BMRB as an alternative to the HMDB) and format it as the two-table Excel workbook (chemical-shift values plus SRRM multiplets) that ROIAL-NMR consumes as a user-selected metabolic database. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/nbm.70131

skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-database-construction Use when a ROI-based NMR metabolite identification tool needs reference chemical shift and J-coupling (SRRM) libraries, and you must derive them from HMDB records and organize them by biological sample type. skills.summary: Construct program-specific metabolic reference databases — one holding 1H chemical shift values and one holding spectral region resonance multiplets (SRRMs) — by parsing Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) NMR records with Python, and split them into biosample-specific tables (serum, saliva, sweat, urine, CSF, tissues) so that tools like ROIAL-NMR can match user-defined ROIs to candidate metabolites.
