skills.description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. a Daphnia magna extract series) shows chemical-shift drift between spectra and you need to quantify misalignment against a user-selected reference within a chosen spectral region before and after segmental alignment.
skills.name: nmr-chemical-shift-drift-assessment
skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-drift-assessment Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. a Daphnia magna extract series) shows chemical-shift drift between spectra and you need to quantify misalignment against a user-selected reference within a chosen spectral region before and after segmental alignment. The spectra series is already aligned or shows no chemical-shift drift relative to the chosen reference, so pre-alignment correlations would not be in the low (<0.3) regime this assessment expects. The input is 2D-NMR or tracer/GC-MS isotopomer data rather than a 1D-NMR spectra series for multivariate pre-processing. No spectrum in the series has sufficient signal-to-noise to serve as a trustworthy alignment reference for the selected region. Quantifies chemical-shift drift in a series of 1D-NMR spectra by computing Pearson correlation coefficients of each spectrum against a high-SNR reference spectrum before and after MetaboLabPy segmental alignment, with the drift-removal outcome judged by a rise from generally <0.3 to >0.95. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Quantifies chemical-shift drift in a series of 1D-NMR spectra by computing Pearson correlation coefficients of each spectrum against a high-SNR reference spectrum before and after MetaboLabPy segmental alignment, with the drift-removal outcome judged by a rise from generally <0.3 to >0.95.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra series is already aligned or shows no chemical-shift drift relative to the chosen reference, so pre-alignment correlations would not be in the low (<0.3) regime this assessment expects. The input is 2D-NMR or tracer/GC-MS isotopomer data rather than a 1D-NMR spectra series for multivariate pre-processing. No spectrum in the series has sufficient signal-to-noise to serve as a trustworthy alignment reference for the selected region.

skills.description: Use when a query HSQC spectrum (list of 1H/13C shift pairs) must be identified or annotated by peak-shift matching against a reference library, or when reproducing the SMART 2.0 / NMRShiftDB baseline of a DeepSAT benchmark.
skills.name: nmr-chemical-shift-library-searching
skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-library-searching Use when a query HSQC spectrum (list of 1H/13C shift pairs) must be identified or annotated by peak-shift matching against a reference library, or when reproducing the SMART 2.0 / NMRShiftDB baseline of a DeepSAT benchmark. Query spectra are 1D NMR or non-HSQC data — the in-house library and thresholds here are specific to 1H-13C HSQC peak shifts The goal is annotation of compounds absent from any reference spectral library — pure shift searching cannot go beyond library coverage, which is why DeepSAT searches structural databases via predicted fingerprints instead Baseline small-molecule identification by directly matching query 1H-13C HSQC proton/carbon chemical shifts against reference spectral libraries (in-house HSQC library via SMART 2.0, n=143,467; NMRShiftDB, n=53,954), serving as the comparator against DeepSAT fingerprint-based retrieval. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Baseline small-molecule identification by directly matching query 1H-13C HSQC proton/carbon chemical shifts against reference spectral libraries (in-house HSQC library via SMART 2.0, n=143,467; NMRShiftDB, n=53,954), serving as the comparator against DeepSAT fingerprint-based retrieval.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query spectra are 1D NMR or non-HSQC data — the in-house library and thresholds here are specific to 1H-13C HSQC peak shifts The goal is annotation of compounds absent from any reference spectral library — pure shift searching cannot go beyond library coverage, which is why DeepSAT searches structural databases via predicted fingerprints instead

skills.description: Use when simulating 1D or 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectra at a target pH different from the standard pH0 (usually 7.4) and you must reposition peaks that shift with pH.
skills.name: nmr-chemical-shift-ph-dependence-modeling
skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-ph-dependence-modeling Use when simulating 1D or 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectra at a target pH different from the standard pH0 (usually 7.4) and you must reposition peaks that shift with pH. The metabolite's peaks do not shift with pH in the region of interest (Δδ effectively zero between pH0 and pH1) — applying the transform adds no realism You only need the standard spectrum at pH0 itself; no shift correction is required Target peaks are 13C or non-exchangeable nuclei without an ionizable group modelled by δL/δHL and a pKa in HMDB 5.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Quantifies pH-dependent chemical-shift changes of metabolite peaks using a Henderson-Hasselbalch-derived transformation (equation 3), computing Δδ in ppm from δL, δHL, pH0 and pH1, for both 1D 1H peaks and projected 2D J-Res/COSY peak clusters in MetAssimulo 2.0 spectral simulation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf045
skills.summary: Quantifies pH-dependent chemical-shift changes of metabolite peaks using a Henderson-Hasselbalch-derived transformation (equation 3), computing Δδ in ppm from δL, δHL, pH0 and pH1, for both 1D 1H peaks and projected 2D J-Res/COSY peak clusters in MetAssimulo 2.0 spectral simulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolite's peaks do not shift with pH in the region of interest (Δδ effectively zero between pH0 and pH1) — applying the transform adds no realism You only need the standard spectrum at pH0 itself; no shift correction is required Target peaks are 13C or non-exchangeable nuclei without an ionizable group modelled by δL/δHL and a pKa in HMDB 5.0

skills.description: Use when you need predicted 1H NMR shifts across a compound structure library (e.g., SMILES/SDF from the Natural Products Atlas) to assess dereplication coverage or classify shielded vs. deshielded resonances.
skills.name: nmr-chemical-shift-prediction
skills.search_text: nmr-chemical-shift-prediction Use when you need predicted 1H NMR shifts across a compound structure library (e.g., SMILES/SDF from the Natural Products Atlas) to assess dereplication coverage or classify shielded vs. deshielded resonances. When accurate structure dereplication against reference spectra is required — the authors state 'lightweight' NMR predictors do not have sufficient accuracy for that task When compounds belong to specialist classes (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) whose exclusively shielded 1H signals fall outside the analysis scope Predict in silico 1H NMR chemical shifts for a large natural product structure set using the stereo-aware HOSE code model from NMRShiftDB2, enabling shielded/deshielded signal statistics (e.g., 94.9% of 27,844 Natural Products Atlas microbial NPs possess at least 10% deshielded signals; 0.4% exclusively shielded). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Predict in silico 1H NMR chemical shifts for a large natural product structure set using the stereo-aware HOSE code model from NMRShiftDB2, enabling shielded/deshielded signal statistics (e.g., 94.9% of 27,844 Natural Products Atlas microbial NPs possess at least 10% deshielded signals; 0.4% exclusively shielded).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When accurate structure dereplication against reference spectra is required — the authors state 'lightweight' NMR predictors do not have sufficient accuracy for that task When compounds belong to specialist classes (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) whose exclusively shielded 1H signals fall outside the analysis scope

skills.description: Use when a series of 1D NMR spectra (individual, pseudo-2D, or tabulated text files) has been fitted and fitted signal areas must be converted to mM concentrations and time courses with uncertainties.
skills.name: nmr-concentration-calibration
skills.search_text: nmr-concentration-calibration Use when a series of 1D NMR spectra (individual, pseudo-2D, or tabulated text files) has been fitted and fitted signal areas must be converted to mM concentrations and time courses with uncertainties. Input is raw or unfitted spectra — spectral fitting (peak picking, multiplet model fitting) must precede the calibration step Data are 2D NMR experiments rather than 1D spectra or pseudo-2D series, which is MultiNMRFit's stated scope No calibration is available to relate fitted signal areas to concentrations, so absolute mM values cannot be derived http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A skill for converting fitted NMR signal areas into absolute millimolar concentrations by applying a calibration, with parameter uncertainties (standard deviations) propagated from the spectral fitting. It relies on MultiNMRFit's ability to estimate signal areas from 1D and pseudo-2D spectra using multiplet signal models. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: A skill for converting fitted NMR signal areas into absolute millimolar concentrations by applying a calibration, with parameter uncertainties (standard deviations) propagated from the spectral fitting. It relies on MultiNMRFit's ability to estimate signal areas from 1D and pseudo-2D spectra using multiplet signal models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or unfitted spectra — spectral fitting (peak picking, multiplet model fitting) must precede the calibration step Data are 2D NMR experiments rather than 1D spectra or pseudo-2D series, which is MultiNMRFit's stated scope No calibration is available to relate fitted signal areas to concentrations, so absolute mM values cannot be derived

skills.description: Use when a one-dimensional 1H NMR spectrum (JCAMP-DX) has been loaded and peak-picked, and per-peak coupling constants and multiplicity labels must be derived automatically from the splitting pattern.
skills.name: nmr-coupling-constant-calculation
skills.search_text: nmr-coupling-constant-calculation Use when a one-dimensional 1H NMR spectrum (JCAMP-DX) has been loaded and peak-picked, and per-peak coupling constants and multiplicity labels must be derived automatically from the splitting pattern. The input spectrum is 13C NMR (typically decoupled, no interpretable splitting), IR, or MS data rather than 1H NMR — ChemSpectra treats these types separately and coupling/multiplicity logic is 1H-specific. The data are 2D NMR spectra — the paper explicitly lists 2D viewing and analysis as a missing feature for future improvement. Multiplicities have already been manually assigned by the user and only display/integration is needed (react-spectra-editor supports manual editing without recalculation). http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Automatic calculation of 1H NMR coupling constants and assignment of multiplicity labels (s, d, t, q, quint, m) from picked peak splitting patterns, as implemented in ChemSpectra's NMR analysis workflow, where multiplicities are inferred from known libraries and validated by additional rules. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00481-0
skills.summary: Automatic calculation of 1H NMR coupling constants and assignment of multiplicity labels (s, d, t, q, quint, m) from picked peak splitting patterns, as implemented in ChemSpectra's NMR analysis workflow, where multiplicities are inferred from known libraries and validated by additional rules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectrum is 13C NMR (typically decoupled, no interpretable splitting), IR, or MS data rather than 1H NMR — ChemSpectra treats these types separately and coupling/multiplicity logic is 1H-specific. The data are 2D NMR spectra — the paper explicitly lists 2D viewing and analysis as a missing feature for future improvement. Multiplicities have already been manually assigned by the user and only display/integration is needed (react-spectra-editor supports manual editing without recalculation).

skills.search_text: nmr-cross-peak-overlap-resolution Use when a processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum contains significantly overlapped cross-peaks that prevent straightforward peak picking, and quantitatively analyzable individual components (positions, line shapes, intensities) are needed. skills.summary: Resolves overlapping 2D NMR cross-peaks into individually quantifiable components by feeding processed 2D spectra through COLMARvista's integrated DEEP Picker deep-neural-network peak picker and Voigt Fitter line-shape deconvolution, enabling quantitative analysis such as compound concentration determination and cross-peak-specific relaxation parameter extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum is 1D or the goal is raw FID processing (phase correction, apodization, Fourier transformation) rather than 2D cross-peak deconvolution The spectrum is already fully deconvoluted with a clean, non-overlapping peak list — Simple Picker local-maxima picking suffices Data must not leave the local machine and the browser cannot run WebWorker/WebAssembly locally without the documented browser flag changes

skills.search_text: nmr-dataset-retrieval-from-metabolomics-repositories Use when a task requires acquiring public NMR metabolomics data sets from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench, or when raw repository file-system formats must be converted into analysis-ready formats for MetaboAnalyst or Workflows4Metabolomics. skills.description: Use when 1H NMR plasma spectra (e.g. FGENTCARD metabo_SE SummarizedExperiment) contain unassigned peaks linked to a phenotype and you need a metabolite assignment via driver-signal correlation.
skills.name: nmr-doublet-signal-interpretation
skills.search_text: nmr-doublet-signal-interpretation Use when 1H NMR plasma spectra (e.g. FGENTCARD metabo_SE SummarizedExperiment) contain unassigned peaks linked to a phenotype and you need a metabolite assignment via driver-signal correlation. Input is already a validated metabolite table or annotated feature list — STOCSY adds no assignment value there. The driver ppm corresponds to a broad/solvent-suppressed region with no distinct doublet to anchor the correlation. Data are LC-MS or other non-NMR feature intensities where STOCSY's NMR spin-system logic does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3337 http://edamontology.org/topic_0003 A skill for metabolite assignment in 1H NMR metabonomic data using STOCSY (Statistical Total Correlation Spectroscopy): a driver signal (e.g. a doublet at δ 1.04 ppm) is correlated across samples to surface co-correlating peaks, letting unknown BMI-associated signals be mapped to a metabolite (here valine). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: A skill for metabolite assignment in 1H NMR metabonomic data using STOCSY (Statistical Total Correlation Spectroscopy): a driver signal (e.g. a doublet at δ 1.04 ppm) is correlated across samples to surface co-correlating peaks, letting unknown BMI-associated signals be mapped to a metabolite (here valine).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated metabolite table or annotated feature list — STOCSY adds no assignment value there. The driver ppm corresponds to a broad/solvent-suppressed region with no distinct doublet to anchor the correlation. Data are LC-MS or other non-NMR feature intensities where STOCSY's NMR spin-system logic does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you have a speaq 2.0 peak-picked/grouped feature matrix (samples x features) plus class metadata for 1D NMR spectra, and you need to find features that significantly differ between two classes (e.g. red vs white wines).
skills.name: nmr-feature-differential-analysis
skills.search_text: nmr-feature-differential-analysis Use when you have a speaq 2.0 peak-picked/grouped feature matrix (samples x features) plus class metadata for 1D NMR spectra, and you need to find features that significantly differ between two classes (e.g. red vs white wines). Input is already a summarized/binned feature table not produced by speaq 2.0's peak-picking-and-grouping pipeline (the method avoids binning, so binned inputs change feature semantics) Raw unprocessed spectra without prior peak picking, grouping, and feature-matrix construction — run getWaveletPeaks/PeakGrouper/BuildFeatureMatrix first Analysis goal requiring multivariate modelling (e.g. PCA, supervised classification) rather than per-feature univariate class comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Univariate differential analysis of a speaq 2.0-derived NMR peak-based feature matrix (e.g. red vs white wine classes) using linear models per feature with Bonferroni correction, as implemented in the speaq R package. It identifies the spectral features that significantly discriminate predefined sample classes after Pareto scaling. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Univariate differential analysis of a speaq 2.0-derived NMR peak-based feature matrix (e.g. red vs white wine classes) using linear models per feature with Bonferroni correction, as implemented in the speaq R package. It identifies the spectral features that significantly discriminate predefined sample classes after Pareto scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a summarized/binned feature table not produced by speaq 2.0's peak-picking-and-grouping pipeline (the method avoids binning, so binned inputs change feature semantics) Raw unprocessed spectra without prior peak picking, grouping, and feature-matrix construction — run getWaveletPeaks/PeakGrouper/BuildFeatureMatrix first Analysis goal requiring multivariate modelling (e.g. PCA, supervised classification) rather than per-feature univariate class comparison

skills.description: Use when raw 1D NMR spectra must be reduced to a feature matrix of peak groups for downstream statistics (PCA, differential analysis), and binning would lose information.
skills.name: nmr-feature-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: nmr-feature-matrix-construction Use when raw 1D NMR spectra must be reduced to a feature matrix of peak groups for downstream statistics (PCA, differential analysis), and binning would lose information. Input is already a feature table or peak-value matrix (e.g. post-binning data) rather than raw spectra Severely shifted spectra where alignment-based approaches are the explicit target — the supplementary notes spectral alignment algorithms 'is not always optimal when dealing with severely shifted spectra', so peak-based processing should not be conflated with alignment methods Targeted quantification of known metabolite concentrations, where tools like BATMAN (aimed at concentration estimates for known metabolites) are the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Constructs a feature/sample/peak-value matrix from raw 1D NMR spectra using the speaq 2.0 wavelet-based pipeline (peak picking with the Mexican hat CWT, peak grouping, and peak filling), replacing binning to avoid information loss. Applied to raw spectral matrices (e.g. 40 wines x 8712 points, 31 urine spectra) it reduces them to compact peak-group feature tables (e.g. 40 x 207, 31 x 677). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Constructs a feature/sample/peak-value matrix from raw 1D NMR spectra using the speaq 2.0 wavelet-based pipeline (peak picking with the Mexican hat CWT, peak grouping, and peak filling), replacing binning to avoid information loss. Applied to raw spectral matrices (e.g. 40 wines x 8712 points, 31 urine spectra) it reduces them to compact peak-group feature tables (e.g. 40 x 207, 31 x 677).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or peak-value matrix (e.g. post-binning data) rather than raw spectra Severely shifted spectra where alignment-based approaches are the explicit target — the supplementary notes spectral alignment algorithms 'is not always optimal when dealing with severely shifted spectra', so peak-based processing should not be conflated with alignment methods Targeted quantification of known metabolite concentrations, where tools like BATMAN (aimed at concentration estimates for known metabolites) are the appropriate choice

skills.description: Use when comparing processing speed of NMR software on a batch of 1D 1H-NMR FIDs requiring identical parameters (e.g., zero-filling to 131072 points, 0.3 Hz exponential line broadening, FT, automated phase correction), or when scripting batch NMR pre-processing in Python.
skills.name: nmr-fid-batch-processing
skills.search_text: nmr-fid-batch-processing Use when comparing processing speed of NMR software on a batch of 1D 1H-NMR FIDs requiring identical parameters (e.g., zero-filling to 131072 points, 0.3 Hz exponential line broadening, FT, automated phase correction), or when scripting batch NMR pre-processing in Python. The task is isotopomer/tracer analysis or HSQC+GC-MS based isotopomer prediction — that belongs to metabolabpytools, not batch 1D processing speed benchmarking. The input data is 2D NMR or already fully processed spectra that do not require FID-level zero-filling, apodization, and phase correction. Only one spectrum or a small non-uniform batch is being processed, where the 100-spectra batch benchmark design (identical parameters across all spectra) does not apply. Benchmarks how quickly different software (MetaboLabPy, MNova, TopSpin, MetaboLab) processes a batch of 100 1H-NMR spectra through zero-filling, line broadening, Fourier transform, and automatic phase correction. Grounded in the MetaboLabPy paper's timing comparison, where MetaboLabPy's reference-spectrum baseline-based phase correction processed all 100 Daphnia extract spectra in 28 s. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Benchmarks how quickly different software (MetaboLabPy, MNova, TopSpin, MetaboLab) processes a batch of 100 1H-NMR spectra through zero-filling, line broadening, Fourier transform, and automatic phase correction. Grounded in the MetaboLabPy paper's timing comparison, where MetaboLabPy's reference-spectrum baseline-based phase correction processed all 100 Daphnia extract spectra in 28 s.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is isotopomer/tracer analysis or HSQC+GC-MS based isotopomer prediction — that belongs to metabolabpytools, not batch 1D processing speed benchmarking. The input data is 2D NMR or already fully processed spectra that do not require FID-level zero-filling, apodization, and phase correction. Only one spectrum or a small non-uniform batch is being processed, where the 100-spectra batch benchmark design (identical parameters across all spectra) does not apply.

skills.description: Use when raw Bruker FIDs (time-domain, complex) carry a DSP digital-filter group delay recorded in the acqus parameters and you need phase-corrected FIDs prior to apodization, zero filling, and Fourier transform.
skills.name: nmr-fid-group-delay-correction
skills.search_text: nmr-fid-group-delay-correction Use when raw Bruker FIDs (time-domain, complex) carry a DSP digital-filter group delay recorded in the acqus parameters and you need phase-corrected FIDs prior to apodization, zero filling, and Fourier transform. Input data is already frequency-domain spectra (post fourier_transform) — group delay is a time-domain point-offset artifact and must be corrected on the FID before Fourier transform. The Bruker dataset lacks the acqus DSP group-delay parameter (acqus_df has no group-delay entry), in which case there is no defined number of leading points to delete. FIDs were acquired on a non-Bruker instrument without a digital-filter group delay, so no first-order phase error from the 'death time' artifact exists. Removes the Bruker digital-filter group-delay ('death time') artifact from each 1H-NMR FID by deleting exactly the acqus-specified number of leading data points, correcting the first-order phase error before further Protomix preprocessing. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Removes the Bruker digital-filter group-delay ('death time') artifact from each 1H-NMR FID by deleting exactly the acqus-specified number of leading data points, correcting the first-order phase error before further Protomix preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is already frequency-domain spectra (post fourier_transform) — group delay is a time-domain point-offset artifact and must be corrected on the FID before Fourier transform. The Bruker dataset lacks the acqus DSP group-delay parameter (acqus_df has no group-delay entry), in which case there is no defined number of leading points to delete. FIDs were acquired on a non-Bruker instrument without a digital-filter group delay, so no first-order phase error from the 'death time' artifact exists.

skills.description: Use when raw Bruker time-domain 2D NMR FID data (`fid` or `ser`) must be converted to a phased 2D spectrum via the automated chain: zero-filling, apodization, water suppression, Fourier transformation, phase correction.
skills.name: nmr-fourier-transform-processing
skills.search_text: nmr-fourier-transform-processing Use when raw Bruker time-domain 2D NMR FID data (`fid` or `ser`) must be converted to a phased 2D spectrum via the automated chain: zero-filling, apodization, water suppression, Fourier transformation, phase correction. The data are already frequency-domain (processed) spectra that only need viewing, peak picking, or 2D line-shape fitting rather than time-domain reconstruction. The experiment is NUS and the goal is iterative SMILE reconstruction of pseudo-3D/3D data, which is a different branch of COLMARvista functionality than the conventional autonomous chain. Interactive, user-guided manual processing is required — this chain is defined by COLMARvista's fully autonomous (no user intervention) behavior. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Reconstructs the autonomous 2D NMR spectral processing chain used by COLMARvista — zero-filling → apodization → water (solvent) suppression → Fourier transformation → automated phase correction — as standalone inspectable steps applied to raw Bruker time-domain FID data. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s10858-025-00465-y
skills.summary: Reconstructs the autonomous 2D NMR spectral processing chain used by COLMARvista — zero-filling → apodization → water (solvent) suppression → Fourier transformation → automated phase correction — as standalone inspectable steps applied to raw Bruker time-domain FID data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already frequency-domain (processed) spectra that only need viewing, peak picking, or 2D line-shape fitting rather than time-domain reconstruction. The experiment is NUS and the goal is iterative SMILE reconstruction of pseudo-3D/3D data, which is a different branch of COLMARvista functionality than the conventional autonomous chain. Interactive, user-guided manual processing is required — this chain is defined by COLMARvista's fully autonomous (no user intervention) behavior.

skills.description: Use when the input is a pseudo-3D NMR series (e.g., pulsed-field-gradient DOSY, or T1/T2/titration/kinetics series of 2D planes) and per-component parameters such as diffusion coefficient D must be extracted, especially when peaks overlap.
skills.name: nmr-gradient-decay-curve-fitting
skills.search_text: nmr-gradient-decay-curve-fitting Use when the input is a pseudo-3D NMR series (e.g., pulsed-field-gradient DOSY, or T1/T2/titration/kinetics series of 2D planes) and per-component parameters such as diffusion coefficient D must be extracted, especially when peaks overlap. The input is a single 2D spectrum rather than a multi-plane series — there is no gradient/relaxation dimension from which to extract decay curves. The analysis goal is CEST dip analysis or exchange-active residue filtering ('Show ≥2 Peaks Only') rather than series fitting — COLMARvista provides a separate CEST/ChemEx workflow for that. Only processing/visualization of one plane is needed; the WebAssembly pipeline (phase correction, apodization, zero filling, solvent suppression, baseline correction) alone suffices without the sequential fitting step. Extracts per-cross-peak diffusion coefficients (D) from a pseudo-3D DOSY dataset — a series of 2D spectra acquired at increasing pulsed-field-gradient strengths — by multi-plane sequential peak fitting in COLMARvista and fitting each component's intensity decay to the Stejskal-Tanner relation. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s10858-025-00465-y
skills.summary: Extracts per-cross-peak diffusion coefficients (D) from a pseudo-3D DOSY dataset — a series of 2D spectra acquired at increasing pulsed-field-gradient strengths — by multi-plane sequential peak fitting in COLMARvista and fitting each component's intensity decay to the Stejskal-Tanner relation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single 2D spectrum rather than a multi-plane series — there is no gradient/relaxation dimension from which to extract decay curves. The analysis goal is CEST dip analysis or exchange-active residue filtering ('Show ≥2 Peaks Only') rather than series fitting — COLMARvista provides a separate CEST/ChemEx workflow for that. Only processing/visualization of one plane is needed; the WebAssembly pipeline (phase correction, apodization, zero filling, solvent suppression, baseline correction) alone suffices without the sequential fitting step.

skills.description: Use when a mixture 1H NMR spectrum must be deconvolved against reference component spectra and peaks overlap almost completely, lineshapes are distorted, or peaks are shifted — e.g., low-field benchtop (Magritek 43 MHz) data where peak-picking tools fail.
skills.name: nmr-library-component-matching
skills.search_text: nmr-library-component-matching Use when a mixture 1H NMR spectrum must be deconvolved against reference component spectra and peaks overlap almost completely, lineshapes are distorted, or peaks are shifted — e.g., low-field benchtop (Magritek 43 MHz) data where peak-picking tools fail. The spectrum is mass-spectrometry data: the related MasserFront/Masserstein tooling targets mass spectrometry result analysis, not NMR library matching Peaks are well separated and a peak-picking/deconvolution-by-integration method (e.g., ACD/TP, MANIQ) already gives acceptable errors Absolute concentrations are required but no quantitative reference spectrum can be added to the library (the external-standard approach requires a known-concentration substance spectrum algebraically added to the mixture spectrum) Quantify components in 1H NMR mixtures by treating mixture and reference-library spectra as probability distributions of signal intensity and running an optimal-transport deconvolution (Magnetstein), which works where peak-picking fails (e.g., low-resolution benchtop spectra with near-complete peak overlap). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03594
skills.summary: Quantify components in 1H NMR mixtures by treating mixture and reference-library spectra as probability distributions of signal intensity and running an optimal-transport deconvolution (Magnetstein), which works where peak-picking fails (e.g., low-resolution benchtop spectra with near-complete peak overlap).

skills.summary: Assigns resonances in 1H-NMR metabonomic spectra to metabolites using Statistical Total Correlation Spectroscopy (STOCSY): a highly correlated ppm signal is chosen as driver and the covariance/correlation pseudo-spectrum reveals co-varying peaks of the same molecule.

skills.description: Use when you hold a pandas DataFrame of FIDs (grpd_df) that has already been through group-delay correction, and dominant residual solvent decays must be removed before apodization and Fourier transform in a 1H-NMR metabolomics pipeline.
skills.name: nmr-solvent-residual-signal-removal
skills.search_text: nmr-solvent-residual-signal-removal Use when you hold a pandas DataFrame of FIDs (grpd_df) that has already been through group-delay correction, and dominant residual solvent decays must be removed before apodization and Fourier transform in a 1H-NMR metabolomics pipeline. Input is already frequency-domain spectra (spectra_df); this skill operates on time-domain FIDs after group-delay removal and before apodization/zero_filling/fourier_transform. FIDs have not yet been group-delay corrected (still fids_df straight from px.extract_fids), since the first points of the FID would distort the smoother's solvent estimate. The goal is peak alignment or binning of spectra (px.Icoshift, px.binning), which are later-stage steps in the Protomix workflow, not solvent removal. Removes residual solvent (e.g., water) signals from group-delay-corrected 1H-NMR FID data using Protomix's solvent_residuals_removal, which fits the solvent component via discrete penalized least squares with second-order differences (Whitaker/Whittaker smoother, Whittaker 1922; Eilers 2003) and subtracts it from each FID. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Removes residual solvent (e.g., water) signals from group-delay-corrected 1H-NMR FID data using Protomix's solvent_residuals_removal, which fits the solvent component via discrete penalized least squares with second-order differences (Whitaker/Whittaker smoother, Whittaker 1922; Eilers 2003) and subtracts it from each FID.

The goal is peak alignment or binning of spectra (px.Icoshift, px.binning), which are later-stage steps in the Protomix workflow, not solvent removal.

When the compound of interest is outside the closed library of 24 flavor standards and no retraining with that standard added is possible. skills.search_text: nmr-spectra-dataframe-processing Use when Fourier-transformed 1H-NMR spectra are held as a pandas DataFrame (samples × ppm) and need per-spectrum phase correction or further Protomix preprocessing before statistical analysis. Input is still raw FID/free-induction-decay data rather than a Fourier-transformed spectra DataFrame — apply group_delay_removal, apodization, zero_filling, and fourier_transform first. Task is peak alignment across spectra — use Protomix's Icoshift/pyicoshift rather than phase correction. The DataFrame already contains referenced, baseline-corrected spectra (e.g. output of baseline_correction) — further phase correction is unnecessary. Processes 1H-NMR spectra represented as a pandas DataFrame (rows = samples, columns = chemical shift in ppm) through Protomix's Fourier-domain preprocessing steps, most notably automatic per-spectrum phase correction that optimizes the RMS of positive peaks. This yields pure absorption lineshapes ready for referencing, baseline correction, and downstream metabolomics analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Processes 1H-NMR spectra represented as a pandas DataFrame (rows = samples, columns = chemical shift in ppm) through Protomix's Fourier-domain preprocessing steps, most notably automatic per-spectrum phase correction that optimizes the RMS of positive peaks. skills.search_text: nmr-spectra-integral-binning Use when a preprocessed, window-selected NMR spectra matrix (spectra_df, samples x chemical shift points) is still too high-dimensional for multivariate statistics and you need a bucketed feature table with one integrated intensity per fixed ppm bin, while coarsely tolerating residual peak shifts. High spectral resolution must be preserved for peak-level interpretation — binning deliberately reduces dimensionality and cannot recover per-peak information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Equidistant spectral binning for 1H-NMR metabolomics: partition the chemical shift axis into fixed-width bins (e.g. 0.1 ppm) and integrate the spectral area under the curve within each bin using Protomix's binning function, producing a reduced-dimension bucketed matrix for multivariate analysis such as PCA. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192

You need to train the model from scratch or re-run full training rather than reload and predict — that is the separate training path also run through demo.ipynb, not the inference-only reproduction of unknown-mixture identification. Input spectra are not 1H NMR (e.g. 13C or other nuclei), which is outside the article's stated scope.

Analysis tasks requiring quantified concentrations rather than binary presence/absence identification of compounds. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A synthetic data-augmentation strategy for 1H NMR mixture identification that builds simulated mixture spectra by weighted-summing 1–7 of 24 flavor-standard spectra with coefficients in [0.2, 1.0], perturbing them with Gaussian chemical-shift deviations and random noise, and assigning binary per-compound labels to form positive/negative spectral pairs for training FlavorFormer. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2025.115372

skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluation on real experimental mixtures where synthetic weighted-sum spectra with Gaussian shift/noise would not match true measurement conditions — use the two experimental flavor-mixture datasets for that purpose. skills.description: Use when a raw 1D NMR spectrum (ppm scale plus intensity array) has a distorted baseline and you need baseline points selected only in signal-free regions before spline fitting and subtraction.

skills.search_text: nmr-spectral-noise-region-selection Use when a raw 1D NMR spectrum (ppm scale plus intensity array) has a distorted baseline and you need baseline points selected only in signal-free regions before spline fitting and subtraction. The spectrum already has a flat baseline oscillating around zero in signal-free regions, so re-fitting a spline risks removing real signal The baseline anchors cannot be placed in signal-free regions because peaks span the whole spectral width — sparse anchors would sit on resonances and bias the spline The task is phase correction, segmental alignment, spectral scaling, or variance stabilisation rather than baseline removal http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Selects sparse anchor points in signal-free (noise) regions of a 1D NMR spectrum and fits a cubic-spline baseline through them, with a linear-spline fallback that inserts intermediate points between widely spaced anchors to avoid over-correcting dense spectral regions. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Selects sparse anchor points in signal-free (noise) regions of a 1D NMR spectrum and fits a cubic-spline baseline through them, with a linear-spline fallback that inserts intermediate points between widely spaced anchors to avoid over-correcting dense spectral regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum already has a flat baseline oscillating around zero in signal-free regions, so re-fitting a spline risks removing real signal The baseline anchors cannot be placed in signal-free regions because peaks span the whole spectral width — sparse anchors would sit on resonances and bias the spline The task is phase correction, segmental alignment, spectral scaling, or variance stabilisation rather than baseline removal

skills.search_text: nmr-spectral-realignment Use when overlaid/stacked 1D 1H NMR spectra show uncontrolled chemical shift variations between spectra after ppm-scale calibration, i.e. peaks of the same metabolite drift across the spectral dimension. The goal is ppm-scale calibration, baseline correction (locally or fully), or binning (Intelligent, variable size or fixed width) rather than correcting chemical shift variations between spectra — these are separate NMRProcFlow processing stages. skills.name: nmr-spectral-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: nmr-spectral-runtime-benchmarking Use when you need to verify that a fully automated NMR metabolite-assignment pipeline (SMolESY-select) is fast enough for high-throughput processing of standard 1D 1H NMR serum spectra, e.g. an external cohort like MTBLS395. The input is not a standard one-dimensional 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. 2D-Jres or pre-processed CPMG data), since SMolESY-select requires only standard 1D 1H NMR spectra by design The goal is to validate assignment accuracy or metabolite quantitation (>99.5% accuracy across 22 metabolites), not computational efficiency The input is already an aggregated timing table — you only need statistics, not re-benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Benchmarks the wall-clock per-spectrum runtime of SMolESY-select on standard 1D 1H NMR serum spectra to verify the algorithm's claim of computational lightness (<15 s per spectrum on a conventional laptop) versus minutes-long fitting/deconvolution approaches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock per-spectrum runtime of SMolESY-select on standard 1D 1H NMR serum spectra to verify the algorithm's claim of computational lightness (<15 s per spectrum on a conventional laptop) versus minutes-long fitting/deconvolution approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a standard one-dimensional 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. 2D-Jres or pre-processed CPMG data), since SMolESY-select requires only standard 1D 1H NMR spectra by design The goal is to validate assignment accuracy or metabolite quantitation (>99.5% accuracy across 22 metabolites), not computational efficiency The input is already an aggregated timing table — you only need statistics, not re-benchmarking

skills.description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. a metabolomics sample set) shows chemical-shift drift within a spectral region and peaks must be aligned to a reference spectrum before multivariate statistical analysis.
skills.name: nmr-spectral-segmental-alignment
skills.search_text: nmr-spectral-segmental-alignment Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. a metabolomics sample set) shows chemical-shift drift within a spectral region and peaks must be aligned to a reference spectrum before multivariate statistical analysis. Spectra already show high correlation with the reference (>0.95) in the selected region, i.e. there is no chemical-shift drift to correct The candidate reference spectrum lacks sufficient signal in the selected region — segmental alignment will not occur and a different reference must be chosen The analysis goal is isotopomer distribution derivation from NMR multiplet and GC-MS data — use the metabolabpytools isotopomer routines instead Removes chemical-shift drift across a series of 1D-NMR spectra by computing, for each spectrum in a user-selected region, the spectral shift that maximizes simple Pearson correlation with a chosen reference spectrum, as implemented in MetaboLabPy's segmental alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Removes chemical-shift drift across a series of 1D-NMR spectra by computing, for each spectrum in a user-selected region, the spectral shift that maximizes simple Pearson correlation with a chosen reference spectrum, as implemented in MetaboLabPy's segmental alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra already show high correlation with the reference (>0.95) in the selected region, i.e. there is no chemical-shift drift to correct The candidate reference spectrum lacks sufficient signal in the selected region — segmental alignment will not occur and a different reference must be chosen The analysis goal is isotopomer distribution derivation from NMR multiplet and GC-MS data — use the metabolabpytools isotopomer routines instead

skills.description: Use when starting from raw Bruker time-domain FID files (fid or ser) and an unprocessed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum is needed; triggers include 'free induction decay' input and no phased spectrum yet.
skills.name: nmr-spectral-zero-filling-apodization
skills.search_text: nmr-spectral-zero-filling-apodization Use when starting from raw Bruker time-domain FID files (fid or ser) and an unprocessed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum is needed; triggers include 'free induction decay' input and no phased spectrum yet. Input is already a processed, phased 2D spectrum rather than raw time-domain fid/ser data Input is non-uniformly sampled (NUS) data requiring direct-FT or iterative SMILE reconstruction instead of the conventional processing chain The goal is peak deconvolution or line-shape fitting (DEEP Picker / Voigt Fitter) rather than producing a phased spectrum http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 A skill for autonomously processing raw Bruker 2D time-domain NMR FID data (fid/ser) through the COLMARvista chain of zero-filling, apodization, water suppression, Fourier transformation, and phase correction, producing a phased 2D spectrum without user intervention. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s10858-025-00465-y
skills.summary: A skill for autonomously processing raw Bruker 2D time-domain NMR FID data (fid/ser) through the COLMARvista chain of zero-filling, apodization, water suppression, Fourier transformation, and phase correction, producing a phased 2D spectrum without user intervention.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed, phased 2D spectrum rather than raw time-domain fid/ser data Input is non-uniformly sampled (NUS) data requiring direct-FT or iterative SMILE reconstruction instead of the conventional processing chain The goal is peak deconvolution or line-shape fitting (DEEP Picker / Voigt Fitter) rather than producing a phased spectrum

skills.description: Use when you have a trained multitask spectrum-to-structure checkpoint and simulated 1H/13C NMR spectra (concatenated 28000-point 1H grid plus 80-bin 13C shifts) and need SMILES structure predictions without molecular formula input.
skills.name: nmr-spectrum-inference-decoding
skills.search_text: nmr-spectrum-inference-decoding Use when you have a trained multitask spectrum-to-structure checkpoint and simulated 1H/13C NMR spectra (concatenated 28000-point 1H grid plus 80-bin 13C shifts) and need SMILES structure predictions without molecular formula input. You only need substructure predictions, not full SMILES structures — use pred_gen_fn 'infer_multitask_model_substructures' instead of SMILES generation You are running the substructure-to-structure transformer alone (no spectral input); that model uses a different source representation (957 substructure indices) and its own token conventions Input is experimental (not simulated) NMR spectra — the model was trained on MestreNova-simulated SpectraBase spectra and does not yet capture nuances of real spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Run inference with the NMR2Struct spectrum-to-structure multitask model to decode 1D 1H/13C NMR spectra into SMILES structure predictions, using the correct alphabet/token conventions and top-k sampling, then canonicalize outputs for downstream accuracy analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.4c01132
skills.summary: Run inference with the NMR2Struct spectrum-to-structure multitask model to decode 1D 1H/13C NMR spectra into SMILES structure predictions, using the correct alphabet/token conventions and top-k sampling, then canonicalize outputs for downstream accuracy analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need substructure predictions, not full SMILES structures — use pred_gen_fn 'infer_multitask_model_substructures' instead of SMILES generation You are running the substructure-to-structure transformer alone (no spectral input); that model uses a different source representation (957 substructure indices) and its own token conventions Input is experimental (not simulated) NMR spectra — the model was trained on MestreNova-simulated SpectraBase spectra and does not yet capture nuances of real spectra

skills.description: Use when you have Fourier-transformed 1H-NMR spectra (e.g. Protomix spectra_df from 10000-point zero-filled FIDs) that still show phase errors and baseline offsets before referencing, binning, or normalization.
skills.name: nmr-spectrum-phase-and-baseline-correction
skills.search_text: nmr-spectrum-phase-and-baseline-correction Use when you have Fourier-transformed 1H-NMR spectra (e.g. Protomix spectra_df from 10000-point zero-filled FIDs) that still show phase errors and baseline offsets before referencing, binning, or normalization. Input is still raw FID data — phase and baseline correction act on frequency-domain spectra, not on time-domain signals (use group_delay_removal/solvent_residuals_removal instead). Spectra are already binned into a feature table — correction must precede binning (bin_size=0.1) and normalization (method='TotalArea'), not follow it. Analysis only needs peak alignment (Icoshift) on already-corrected spectra — re-correcting can distort previously aligned peaks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Correct phase distortions and remove baseline drift from 1H-NMR spectra after Fourier transform, using Protomix's phase_correction and baseline_correction (airPLS) functions on a spectra DataFrame. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Correct phase distortions and remove baseline drift from 1H-NMR spectra after Fourier transform, using Protomix's phase_correction and baseline_correction (airPLS) functions on a spectra DataFrame.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FID data — phase and baseline correction act on frequency-domain spectra, not on time-domain signals (use group_delay_removal/solvent_residuals_removal instead). Spectra are already binned into a feature table — correction must precede binning (bin_size=0.1) and normalization (method='TotalArea'), not follow it. Analysis only needs peak alignment (Icoshift) on already-corrected spectra — re-correcting can distort previously aligned peaks.

skills.description: Use when quantifying components of 1H NMR mixture spectra that suffer from overlapping peaks, shifted resonances, low resolution, or distorted lineshapes where peak-based deconvolution methods fail.
skills.name: nmr-spectrum-probability-measure-representation
skills.search_text: nmr-spectrum-probability-measure-representation Use when quantifying components of 1H NMR mixture spectra that suffer from overlapping peaks, shifted resonances, low resolution, or distorted lineshapes where peak-based deconvolution methods fail. When the mixture spectrum contains no overlapping or shifted peaks and a peak-based method such as MANIQ or ACD/TP would suffice When the goal is absolute quantification without a reference spectrum in the library — the external-standard workflow requires algebraically adding a known-concentration substance spectrum to the mixture When spectra come from a different modality without adaptation — multidimensional generalizations (sliced Wasserstein, graph-flow representations) are listed as future work only http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Represents 1H NMR mixture and library spectra as discrete probability measures of signal intensity over the chemical-shift axis so that component quantification can be cast as a Wasserstein-distance optimal-transport problem, as implemented in Magnetstein. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03594
skills.summary: Represents 1H NMR mixture and library spectra as discrete probability measures of signal intensity over the chemical-shift axis so that component quantification can be cast as a Wasserstein-distance optimal-transport problem, as implemented in Magnetstein.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the mixture spectrum contains no overlapping or shifted peaks and a peak-based method such as MANIQ or ACD/TP would suffice When the goal is absolute quantification without a reference spectrum in the library — the external-standard workflow requires algebraically adding a known-concentration substance spectrum to the mixture When spectra come from a different modality without adaptation — multidimensional generalizations (sliced Wasserstein, graph-flow representations) are listed as future work only

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic metabolomic 1H NMR spectra (1D, 2D J-Res, or 2D COSY) of urine, blood, or CSF mixtures — e.g. for benchmarking spectral processing algorithms or reproducing paper comparisons against real spectra.
skills.name: nmr-spectrum-simulation
skills.search_text: nmr-spectrum-simulation Use when you need synthetic metabolomic 1H NMR spectra (1D, 2D J-Res, or 2D COSY) of urine, blood, or CSF mixtures — e.g. for benchmarking spectral processing algorithms or reproducing paper comparisons against real spectra. You need simulation of NMR modalities outside 1D 1H, 2D J-Res, and 2D COSY (e.g. HSQC, NOESY) — MetAssimulo 2.0's scope is 1D and 2D J-Res/COSY metabolomic 1H spectra You need spectra of biofluids other than urine, blood, or cerebral spinal fluid You already have real experimental NMR spectra and only need processing/statistical analysis rather than synthetic data generation http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Simulates realistic 1D and 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectra (J-Res and COSY) of urine, blood, and CSF using MetAssimulo 2.0, a Python-based Dash web app, to generate synthetic spectral data for algorithm development and method validation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf045
skills.summary: Simulates realistic 1D and 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectra (J-Res and COSY) of urine, blood, and CSF using MetAssimulo 2.0, a Python-based Dash web app, to generate synthetic spectral data for algorithm development and method validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need simulation of NMR modalities outside 1D 1H, 2D J-Res, and 2D COSY (e.g. HSQC, NOESY) — MetAssimulo 2.0's scope is 1D and 2D J-Res/COSY metabolomic 1H spectra You need spectra of biofluids other than urine, blood, or cerebral spinal fluid You already have real experimental NMR spectra and only need processing/statistical analysis rather than synthetic data generation

skills.description: Use when you have 2D NMR (TOCSY + HSQC) peak data from complex natural product mixtures and need discrete, comparable spin system features to drive sample-to-sample similarity networks.
skills.name: nmr-spin-system-feature-construction
skills.search_text: nmr-spin-system-feature-construction Use when you have 2D NMR (TOCSY + HSQC) peak data from complex natural product mixtures and need discrete, comparable spin system features to drive sample-to-sample similarity networks. Compounds with exclusively shielded 1H signals (e.g. sterols, low-MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) — the <2.5 ppm TOCSY quadrant is excluded and 1H < 2.5 ppm cross-peaks are removed You already have a processed feature/similarity table and only need network generation — go straight to correlation_matrix_generation/generate_network instead Absolute-value (non-phase-sensitive) HSQC data is the only option and SNR trade-offs of phase-sensitive acquisition were not planned for http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Constructs spin system features from paired TOCSY and HSQC spectra by generating a directed graph from each TOCSY peak table (nodes = 1H signals) and annotating nodes with 13C shifts from HSQC cross-peaks, producing the feature objects MADByTE uses for chemical similarity networking. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Constructs spin system features from paired TOCSY and HSQC spectra by generating a directed graph from each TOCSY peak table (nodes = 1H signals) and annotating nodes with 13C shifts from HSQC cross-peaks, producing the feature objects MADByTE uses for chemical similarity networking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Compounds with exclusively shielded 1H signals (e.g. sterols, low-MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) — the <2.5 ppm TOCSY quadrant is excluded and 1H < 2.5 ppm cross-peaks are removed You already have a processed feature/similarity table and only need network generation — go straight to correlation_matrix_generation/generate_network instead Absolute-value (non-phase-sensitive) HSQC data is the only option and SNR trade-offs of phase-sensitive acquisition were not planned for

skills.description: Use when you need to assign metabolite signals in calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra to a curated metabolite panel by matching spin-system patterns inside spectral windows derived from a large cohort.
skills.name: nmr-spin-system-pattern-search
skills.search_text: nmr-spin-system-pattern-search Use when you need to assign metabolite signals in calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra to a curated metabolite panel by matching spin-system patterns inside spectral windows derived from a large cohort. The spectrum is a 2D NMR acquisition (e.g. 2D-Jres) rather than the standard one-dimensional 1H NMR data the algorithm requires The spectrum has not been baseline-corrected by SMolESY or calibrated to the glucose anomeric proton at 5.233 ppm — the pattern search operates on SMolESY-processed data The metabolite of interest lies outside the 22-metabolite panel for which bins were defined using the 4023-sample cohort http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Searches SMolESY-processed 1D 1H NMR blood serum/plasma spectra for each metabolite spin system's pattern within predefined spectral windows (bins), producing per-bin assignments that feed direct integration without deconvolution or baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Searches SMolESY-processed 1D 1H NMR blood serum/plasma spectra for each metabolite spin system's pattern within predefined spectral windows (bins), producing per-bin assignments that feed direct integration without deconvolution or baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum is a 2D NMR acquisition (e.g. 2D-Jres) rather than the standard one-dimensional 1H NMR data the algorithm requires The spectrum has not been baseline-corrected by SMolESY or calibrated to the glucose anomeric proton at 5.233 ppm — the pattern search operates on SMolESY-processed data The metabolite of interest lies outside the 22-metabolite panel for which bins were defined using the 4023-sample cohort

skills.description: Use when starting from a BMRB accession (or a local NMR-STAR entry) and you need the protein entity sequence in FASTA format to run BLAST-based cross-linking of BMRB archive data to external public databases.
skills.name: nmr-star-entry-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: nmr-star-entry-sequence-extraction Use when starting from a BMRB accession (or a local NMR-STAR entry) and you need the protein entity sequence in FASTA format to run BLAST-based cross-linking of BMRB archive data to external public databases. The sequence already exists in FASTA or the entry is from a non-BMRB archive (fetch directly from UniProt/PDB instead of parsing NMR-STAR). You need chemical shifts, restraints, or spectra rather than the entity sequence — use PyBMRB/RBMRB visualization or the BMRB query grid instead. The BMRB entry is one of the ~25 older-format entries excluded from current query grids; verify entry availability via /list_entries or /status first. Retrieves a BMRB entry's entity amino-acid sequence via the BMRB RESTful API and/or PyNMR-STAR parsing of the NMR-STAR file, emitting it in FASTA format as the query for downstream sequence-homology searches (e.g., NCBI blastp against UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/978-1-0716-0270-6_14
skills.summary: Retrieves a BMRB entry's entity amino-acid sequence via the BMRB RESTful API and/or PyNMR-STAR parsing of the NMR-STAR file, emitting it in FASTA format as the query for downstream sequence-homology searches (e.g., NCBI blastp against UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequence already exists in FASTA or the entry is from a non-BMRB archive (fetch directly from UniProt/PDB instead of parsing NMR-STAR). You need chemical shifts, restraints, or spectra rather than the entity sequence — use PyBMRB/RBMRB visualization or the BMRB query grid instead. The BMRB entry is one of the ~25 older-format entries excluded from current query grids; verify entry availability via /list_entries or /status first.

skills.description: Use when a task requires reading, validating, or extracting saveframes and loops (e.g., the assigned Atom_chem_shift chemical shift loop, NOE/dihedral restraint saveframes) from a BMRB entry in NMR-STAR format.
skills.name: nmr-star-file-parsing
skills.search_text: nmr-star-file-parsing Use when a task requires reading, validating, or extracting saveframes and loops (e.g., the assigned Atom_chem_shift chemical shift loop, NOE/dihedral restraint saveframes) from a BMRB entry in NMR-STAR format. The chemical shift table only needs format conversion between table formats — use the STARch converter, which converts table formats but not atom nomenclature. Input is already NEF or a plain tab-delimited/CSV shift table — there is no NMR-STAR to parse. Goal is visualization of chemical shift lists as spectra or shift-distribution histograms — use PyBMRB, which fetches and parses the data for you. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_1317 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Parses and syntax-validates BMRB entries in the NMR-STAR data format using PyNMR-STAR, exposing saveframes/loops such as the Atom_chem_shift chemical shift loop for downstream extraction, conversion, and analysis. This is the core handling step for any BMRB archival data, since BMRB archives spectral and derived data in NMR-STAR. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/978-1-0716-0270-6_14
skills.summary: Parses and syntax-validates BMRB entries in the NMR-STAR data format using PyNMR-STAR, exposing saveframes/loops such as the Atom_chem_shift chemical shift loop for downstream extraction, conversion, and analysis. This is the core handling step for any BMRB archival data, since BMRB archives spectral and derived data in NMR-STAR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chemical shift table only needs format conversion between table formats — use the STARch converter, which converts table formats but not atom nomenclature. Input is already NEF or a plain tab-delimited/CSV shift table — there is no NMR-STAR to parse. Goal is visualization of chemical shift lists as spectra or shift-distribution histograms — use PyBMRB, which fetches and parses the data for you.

skills.description: Use when input is an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry file that must be parsed, validated against the NMR-STAR 3.2 schema, or converted (e.g., to NEF) before deposition or downstream analysis.
skills.name: nmr-star-schema-validation
skills.search_text: nmr-star-schema-validation Use when input is an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry file that must be parsed, validated against the NMR-STAR 3.2 schema, or converted (e.g., to NEF) before deposition or downstream analysis. The data is raw time-domain or processed spectra not represented in NMR-STAR format — BMRB accepts these as separate uploaded data files, not via schema-parsed STAR entries Only the atom nomenclature needs remapping (e.g., to ALATIS identifiers) — STARch converts table formats but not atom nomenclature, so a different tool/step is required The goal is querying or visualizing existing BMRB chemical shift data rather than validating/converting a specific entry — the BMRB REST API or PyBMRB/RBMRB is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Parse and syntax-validate NMR-STAR files (the data format BMRB uses to archive NMR experiments, spectral and derived data, and supporting metadata) against the BMRB NMR-STAR 3.2 schema using the PyNMR-STAR library, as a prerequisite for converting entries to NEF for deposition. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/978-1-0716-0270-6_14
skills.summary: Parse and syntax-validate NMR-STAR files (the data format BMRB uses to archive NMR experiments, spectral and derived data, and supporting metadata) against the BMRB NMR-STAR 3.2 schema using the PyNMR-STAR library, as a prerequisite for converting entries to NEF for deposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is raw time-domain or processed spectra not represented in NMR-STAR format — BMRB accepts these as separate uploaded data files, not via schema-parsed STAR entries Only the atom nomenclature needs remapping (e.g., to ALATIS identifiers) — STARch converts table formats but not atom nomenclature, so a different tool/step is required The goal is querying or visualizing existing BMRB chemical shift data rather than validating/converting a specific entry — the BMRB REST API or PyBMRB/RBMRB is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when you have 1H-13C HSQC (optionally multiplicity edited) NMR peak lists from a small natural product or metabolite and need to retrieve candidate structures or nearest known compounds from large chemical databases rather than limited NMR spectral libraries.
skills.name: nmr-structure-annotation
skills.search_text: nmr-structure-annotation Use when you have 1H-13C HSQC (optionally multiplicity edited) NMR peak lists from a small natural product or metabolite and need to retrieve candidate structures or nearest known compounds from large chemical databases rather than limited NMR spectral libraries. Input is a raw FID or 2D matrix rather than an HSQC-derived peak list with 1H and 13C chemical shifts — DeepSAT consumes peak lists, not processed images of full spectra Query spectra are 1D proton/carbon chemical-shift tables from reference libraries such as NMRShiftDB — the article reports searching NMRshiftDB by proton and carbon shifts achieved under 3% correct identifications, so classical library matching is the wrong tool here The target is a protein/oligomer or other macromolecule outside the small-molecule metabolite scope the model was trained on http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Annotate and identify small-molecule structures from a single 1H-13C HSQC spectrum by running it through the DeepSAT CNN multi-task model, which predicts chemical fingerprint bit strings, molecular weights, and structure classes, then matches predictions against known-molecule fingerprints via cosine similarity to search chemical databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Annotate and identify small-molecule structures from a single 1H-13C HSQC spectrum by running it through the DeepSAT CNN multi-task model, which predicts chemical fingerprint bit strings, molecular weights, and structure classes, then matches predictions against known-molecule fingerprints via cosine similarity to search chemical databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw FID or 2D matrix rather than an HSQC-derived peak list with 1H and 13C chemical shifts — DeepSAT consumes peak lists, not processed images of full spectra Query spectra are 1D proton/carbon chemical-shift tables from reference libraries such as NMRShiftDB — the article reports searching NMRshiftDB by proton and carbon shifts achieved under 3% correct identifications, so classical library matching is the wrong tool here The target is a protein/oligomer or other macromolecule outside the small-molecule metabolite scope the model was trained on

skills.description: Use when you have NEF files containing NMR constraints for proteins and need to generate an ensemble of ranked structural conformers via torsion-angle dynamics.
skills.name: nmr-structure-calculation
skills.search_text: nmr-structure-calculation Use when you have NEF files containing NMR constraints for proteins and need to generate an ensemble of ranked structural conformers via torsion-angle dynamics. Input is already a set of PDB structures without NMR restraints (e.g. pure homology models) You need full Cartesian-space molecular dynamics rather than torsion-angle dynamics Processing raw FIDs for spectra rather than performing a structure calculation http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Computes protein NMR solution structures from deposited NEF constraint files using NMRFx's torsion-angle structure generator, producing ensembles of ranked conformers that can be superimposed onto reference PDB structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-025-01812-8
skills.summary: Computes protein NMR solution structures from deposited NEF constraint files using NMRFx's torsion-angle structure generator, producing ensembles of ranked conformers that can be superimposed onto reference PDB structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of PDB structures without NMR restraints (e.g. pure homology models) You need full Cartesian-space molecular dynamics rather than torsion-angle dynamics Processing raw FIDs for spectra rather than performing a structure calculation

skills.name: nmr-study-file-validation
skills.search_text: nmr-study-file-validation Use when a study downloaded from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench has been converted to CloMet's internal standard (a_ / i_ / m_ / s_ / audit metadata files with per-sample experiment directories holding acqu, acqus, fid) and you must decide whether it is usable downstream. skills.description: Use when raw Bruker time-domain FID files (`fid` or `ser`) must be turned into inspectable, phased 2D spectra and no manually tuned processing parameters are available or desired.
skills.name: nmr-time-domain-fid-processing
skills.search_text: nmr-time-domain-fid-processing Use when raw Bruker time-domain FID files (`fid` or `ser`) must be turned into inspectable, phased 2D spectra and no manually tuned processing parameters are available or desired. Input is already frequency-domain / processed 2D data that only needs viewing or peak picking — use the viewing and DEEP Picker/Voigt Fitter functions instead Input is non-uniformly sampled (NUS) data requiring direct-FT or iterative SMILE reconstruction — that is a separate reconstruction workflow, not this autonomous FID chain The goal is quantitative deconvolution (concentrations, cross-peak relaxation parameters) — this skill only produces the phased spectrum that feeds DEEP Picker and Voigt Fitter Autonomous conversion of raw Bruker time-domain FID data (`fid`, `ser`) into phased 2D NMR spectra by executing COLMARvista's client-side WebAssembly chain: zero-filling → apodization → solvent/water suppression → Fourier transformation → automated phase correction, without user intervention. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s10858-025-00465-y
skills.summary: Autonomous conversion of raw Bruker time-domain FID data (`fid`, `ser`) into phased 2D NMR spectra by executing COLMARvista's client-side WebAssembly chain: zero-filling → apodization → solvent/water suppression → Fourier transformation → automated phase correction, without user intervention.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already frequency-domain / processed 2D data that only needs viewing or peak picking — use the viewing and DEEP Picker/Voigt Fitter functions instead Input is non-uniformly sampled (NUS) data requiring direct-FT or iterative SMILE reconstruction — that is a separate reconstruction workflow, not this autonomous FID chain The goal is quantitative deconvolution (concentrations, cross-peak relaxation parameters) — this skill only produces the phased spectrum that feeds DEEP Picker and Voigt Fitter

skills.description: Use when you have paired TOCSY and HSQC spectra for multiple complex natural products extract/prefraction samples and need shared spin system features to cluster samples or dereplicate known scaffolds.
skills.name: nmr-tocsy-hsqc-spin-system-construction
skills.search_text: nmr-tocsy-hsqc-spin-system-construction Use when you have paired TOCSY and HSQC spectra for multiple complex natural products extract/prefraction samples and need shared spin system features to cluster samples or dereplicate known scaffolds. The compound class of interest (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) has exclusively shielded 1H signals — 0.4% of predicted molecules are entirely shielded and the <2.5 ppm TOCSY quadrant is excluded You expect to capture every spin system in the mixture — MADByTE will not identify every spin system, and peak picking performs poorly in the crowded shielded region Input is already a processed feature table or you need atom-accurate structure prediction — lightweight NMR predictors lack sufficient accuracy for dereplication at scale http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 MADByTE skill for constructing spin system features from paired 2D TOCSY/HSQC NMR spectra of complex mixtures, then matching features across samples to build chemical similarity networks for dereplication and spiked-compound detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: MADByTE skill for constructing spin system features from paired 2D TOCSY/HSQC NMR spectra of complex mixtures, then matching features across samples to build chemical similarity networks for dereplication and spiked-compound detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound class of interest (sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) has exclusively shielded 1H signals — 0.4% of predicted molecules are entirely shielded and the <2.5 ppm TOCSY quadrant is excluded You expect to capture every spin system in the mixture — MADByTE will not identify every spin system, and peak picking performs poorly in the crowded shielded region Input is already a processed feature table or you need atom-accurate structure prediction — lightweight NMR predictors lack sufficient accuracy for dereplication at scale
