You only have a feature table without parent suspect screening results or TP predictions — componentization requires confirmed parent/TP feature pairs to link The goal is plain compound annotation or adduct/isotope componentization rather than transformation-product parent/TP grouping This tutorial-level NTA is not meant as a detailed overview; do not use it as a production TP screening protocol without tuning filters for your matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Links each confirmed parent feature with its corresponding transformation-product features and groups them into TP components using patRoon 2.0's TP componentization, the final linking step of the automated TP screening workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04029
skills.summary: Links each confirmed parent feature with its corresponding transformation-product features and groups them into TP components using patRoon 2.0's TP componentization, the final linking step of the automated TP screening workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a feature table without parent suspect screening results or TP predictions — componentization requires confirmed parent/TP feature pairs to link The goal is plain compound annotation or adduct/isotope componentization rather than transformation-product parent/TP grouping This tutorial-level NTA is not meant as a detailed overview; do not use it as a production TP screening protocol without tuning filters for your matrix

skills.description: Use when imzML-derived pixel-by-m/z data (e.g. image.norm.csv with lipid annotations, m/z and TIC-normalised intensities) must be classified into tissue regions such as cerebellum white matter, granular and molecular layers.
skills.name: pareto-scaled-multivariate-image-analysis
skills.search_text: pareto-scaled-multivariate-image-analysis Use when imzML-derived pixel-by-m/z data (e.g. image.norm.csv with lipid annotations, m/z and TIC-normalised intensities) must be classified into tissue regions such as cerebellum white matter, granular and molecular layers. Input is raw vendor data not yet parsed and pre-processed by massPix (mzextractor, peakpicker.bin, deisotoping, annotate, normalise) — the skill expects the image.norm.csv feature table, not spectra The goal is putative lipid annotation by accurate mass matching against the generated lipid library — that is handled by makelibrary/annotate, not clustering You need spatially-aware clustering (e.g. as in Cardinal) — massPix clustering is non-spatial and currently supports only k-means http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates multivariate statistical tissue images from mass spectrometry imaging data by centering and Pareto scaling TIC-normalised pixel intensities and applying k-means clustering (or PCA) with massPix, so tissue regions with high spectral similarity are classified as spatially coherent clusters with cluster-center spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1252-5
skills.summary: Generates multivariate statistical tissue images from mass spectrometry imaging data by centering and Pareto scaling TIC-normalised pixel intensities and applying k-means clustering (or PCA) with massPix, so tissue regions with high spectral similarity are classified as spatially coherent clusters with cluster-center spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor data not yet parsed and pre-processed by massPix (mzextractor, peakpicker.bin, deisotoping, annotate, normalise) — the skill expects the image.norm.csv feature table, not spectra The goal is putative lipid annotation by accurate mass matching against the generated lipid library — that is handled by makelibrary/annotate, not clustering You need spatially-aware clustering (e.g. as in Cardinal) — massPix clustering is non-spatial and currently supports only k-means

skills.description: Use when you have a peak-based feature/sample/peak-value matrix from NMR spectra (e.g. speaq 2.0 output) and need to equalize variable influence before PCA or multivariate statistics.
skills.name: pareto-scaling-data-normalization
skills.search_text: pareto-scaling-data-normalization Use when you have a peak-based feature/sample/peak-value matrix from NMR spectra (e.g. speaq 2.0 output) and need to equalize variable influence before PCA or multivariate statistics. The input is raw spectra rather than a peak-picked, grouped feature matrix — run getWaveletPeaks, PeakGrouper and BuildFeatureMatrix first The downstream method already performs internal scaling (e.g. prcomp with scale.=TRUE gives unit-variance scaling, not Pareto scaling) The goal is quantitation or spectral alignment rather than statistical analysis of the feature matrix Pareto scaling (dividing each variable by the square root of its standard deviation) with mean centering of a peak-based feature matrix, preparing NMR metabolomics data for PCA and other downstream statistical analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Pareto scaling (dividing each variable by the square root of its standard deviation) with mean centering of a peak-based feature matrix, preparing NMR metabolomics data for PCA and other downstream statistical analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw spectra rather than a peak-picked, grouped feature matrix — run getWaveletPeaks, PeakGrouper and BuildFeatureMatrix first The downstream method already performs internal scaling (e.g. prcomp with scale.=TRUE gives unit-variance scaling, not Pareto scaling) The goal is quantitation or spectral alignment rather than statistical analysis of the feature matrix

skills.description: Use when a peak-based feature matrix has been built with speaq 2.0 (BuildFeatureMatrix) and a univariate test such as red-vs-white linear-model differential analysis requires column scaling as a pre-statistics step.
skills.name: pareto-scaling-metabolomics-matrix
skills.search_text: pareto-scaling-metabolomics-matrix Use when a peak-based feature matrix has been built with speaq 2.0 (BuildFeatureMatrix) and a univariate test such as red-vs-white linear-model differential analysis requires column scaling as a pre-statistics step. The input is already a scaled feature table or you plan a method that handles scaling internally — re-scaling can double-transform the data. Raw 1D NMR spectra rather than a peak-picked/grouped feature matrix — run the speaq 2.0 peak picking and grouping workflow first. Binned/bucketed data from other NMR frameworks — speaq 2.0's paradigm avoids the binning step, and its scaling is designed for the peak-value matrix it produces. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Apply Pareto scaling to a speaq 2.0-derived NMR feature/sample/peak-value matrix (e.g. the wine NMR feature matrix) so that downstream univariate statistics such as linear-model differential analysis compare features on a common scale while partially preserving large peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Apply Pareto scaling to a speaq 2.0-derived NMR feature/sample/peak-value matrix (e.g. the wine NMR feature matrix) so that downstream univariate statistics such as linear-model differential analysis compare features on a common scale while partially preserving large peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a scaled feature table or you plan a method that handles scaling internally — re-scaling can double-transform the data. Raw 1D NMR spectra rather than a peak-picked/grouped feature matrix — run the speaq 2.0 peak picking and grouping workflow first. Binned/bucketed data from other NMR frameworks — speaq 2.0's paradigm avoids the binning step, and its scaling is designed for the peak-value matrix it produces.

skills.description: Use when a trained FIORA model checkpoint and annotated compound sets (RT and CCS labels) are available and you need to quantify/visualize regression accuracy of RT/CCS predictions against simple baselines on held-out splits.
skills.name: parity-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: parity-plot-visualization Use when a trained FIORA model checkpoint and annotated compound sets (RT and CCS labels) are available and you need to quantify/visualize regression accuracy of RT/CCS predictions against simple baselines on held-out splits. Using NIST'17 as the annotation source for this task — it does not provide RT and CCS values of the measured compounds Evaluating spectral (peak-intensity) prediction quality rather than the auxiliary scalar properties RT and CCS Applying to compounds outside the trained ionization modes ([M+H]+ and [M-H]-) or outside the dataset's weight/energy constraints (max 1000 Da, max 100 eV) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reproduce predicted-versus-observed parity plots for FIORA's auxiliary property predictions — retention time (RT) and collision cross section (CCS) — annotated with R² values against baseline linear regressions (Fig. 5 of the FIORA paper). This validates that FIORA's modular graph architecture generalizes beyond spectra to orthogonal identification dimensions. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Reproduce predicted-versus-observed parity plots for FIORA's auxiliary property predictions — retention time (RT) and collision cross section (CCS) — annotated with R² values against baseline linear regressions (Fig. 5 of the FIORA paper). This validates that FIORA's modular graph architecture generalizes beyond spectra to orthogonal identification dimensions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Using NIST'17 as the annotation source for this task — it does not provide RT and CCS values of the measured compounds Evaluating spectral (peak-intensity) prediction quality rather than the auxiliary scalar properties RT and CCS Applying to compounds outside the trained ionization modes ([M+H]+ and [M-H]-) or outside the dataset's weight/energy constraints (max 1000 Da, max 100 eV)

skills.description: Use when proprietary vendor HRMS data (Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE, or Thermo RAW converted to mzML) must be stored compactly, queried fast, or shared across R and Python.
skills.name: parquet-columnar-spectra-conversion
skills.search_text: parquet-columnar-spectra-conversion Use when proprietary vendor HRMS data (Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE, or Thermo RAW converted to mzML) must be stored compactly, queried fast, or shared across R and Python. The data is already a processed feature table or peak list rather than raw/profile HRMS spectra Only a single chromatogram or spectrum plot is needed — the arcms-dataviz Shiny app can visualize existing Parquet files without re-conversion The source is not UNIFI-accessible data nor a format convertible to mzML (arcMS's documented ingestion paths) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3077 Convert high-resolution mass spectrometry data — Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE or vendor RAW files intermediated as mzML (e.g. Thermo) — into a long-format Apache Parquet columnar table with columns rt, scanid, mslevel, mz and intensity (plus bin/dt for ion mobility), for compact storage and fast Arrow-based access. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae160
skills.summary: Convert high-resolution mass spectrometry data — Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE or vendor RAW files intermediated as mzML (e.g. Thermo) — into a long-format Apache Parquet columnar table with columns rt, scanid, mslevel, mz and intensity (plus bin/dt for ion mobility), for compact storage and fast Arrow-based access.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is already a processed feature table or peak list rather than raw/profile HRMS spectra Only a single chromatogram or spectrum plot is needed — the arcms-dataviz Shiny app can visualize existing Parquet files without re-conversion The source is not UNIFI-accessible data nor a format convertible to mzML (arcMS's documented ingestion paths)

skills.description: Use when Thermo RAW spectral peak data must be converted to scalable, analysis-ready arrays for downstream ML/QC workflows, joining per-scan spectra to scan-header metadata via scan numbers.
skills.name: parquet-columnar-spectral-storage
skills.search_text: parquet-columnar-spectral-storage Use when Thermo RAW spectral peak data must be converted to scalable, analysis-ready arrays for downstream ML/QC workflows, joining per-scan spectra to scan-header metadata via scan numbers. Input is not a Thermo Fisher RAW file — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW files and additional vendor formats are not yet supported Only scan-header metadata is needed (retention time, TIC, injection time) — the plain metadata/TSV export path suffices without peak-list Parquet export Running on Linux containers for MS-method/LC-method extraction — those Thermo method-reading calls are unsupported on Linux (peak-list export itself still works in containers) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Exports Thermo RAW-file MS1 and MS2 peak lists as indexed, columnar Parquet files — one row per scan holding NumPy-style arrays (m/z, intensity, and for MS2 also resolution, noise, baseline, and charge) — so spectra join to scan-header metadata by scan number and can be read memory-efficiently without loading whole RAW files. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.687968
skills.summary: Exports Thermo RAW-file MS1 and MS2 peak lists as indexed, columnar Parquet files — one row per scan holding NumPy-style arrays (m/z, intensity, and for MS2 also resolution, noise, baseline, and charge) — so spectra join to scan-header metadata by scan number and can be read memory-efficiently without loading whole RAW files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a Thermo Fisher RAW file — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW files and additional vendor formats are not yet supported Only scan-header metadata is needed (retention time, TIC, injection time) — the plain metadata/TSV export path suffices without peak-list Parquet export Running on Linux containers for MS-method/LC-method extraction — those Thermo method-reading calls are unsupported on Linux (peak-list export itself still works in containers)

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark read/query performance of Parquet-stored HRMS (MSE/HDMSE) data against other formats (mzML, mz5, mzMLb), measuring query wall time and output data volume from on-disk Arrow datasets.
skills.name: parquet-on-disk-query-timing-measurement
skills.search_text: parquet-on-disk-query-timing-measurement Use when you need to benchmark read/query performance of Parquet-stored HRMS (MSE/HDMSE) data against other formats (mzML, mz5, mzMLb), measuring query wall time and output data volume from on-disk Arrow datasets. Input data is not in Parquet columnar format (e.g. proprietary UNIFI raw data not yet converted with arcMS, or mzML/HDF5 files) — convert first or use format-specific readers The goal is conversion-speed benchmarking of MSConvertGUI vs arcMS rather than on-disk query/read timing of already-converted files The query fully loads the file into memory via read_parquet(), since then no on-disk lazy evaluation is being measured http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking procedure for quantifying how fast HRMS data stored in Apache Parquet can be queried on disk (TIC, binned rt/mz aggregation) using Arrow and DuckDB, contrasting in-memory footprint with lazy query time and output size. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae160
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure for quantifying how fast HRMS data stored in Apache Parquet can be queried on disk (TIC, binned rt/mz aggregation) using Arrow and DuckDB, contrasting in-memory footprint with lazy query time and output size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not in Parquet columnar format (e.g. proprietary UNIFI raw data not yet converted with arcMS, or mzML/HDF5 files) — convert first or use format-specific readers The goal is conversion-speed benchmarking of MSConvertGUI vs arcMS rather than on-disk query/read timing of already-converted files The query fully loads the file into memory via read_parquet(), since then no on-disk lazy evaluation is being measured

skills.description: Use when a draft SBML GENRE fails to produce biomass under defined media conditions and reactions must be added from a universal reaction database (universal.pickle) to restore growth.
skills.name: parsimonious-flux-balance-analysis-gap-filling
skills.search_text: parsimonious-flux-balance-analysis-gap-filling Use when a draft SBML GENRE fails to produce biomass under defined media conditions and reactions must be added from a universal reaction database (universal.pickle) to restore growth. The input is a .fasta or BLASTp output file requiring de novo reconstruction — use Reconstructor type 1 or type 2 inputs instead of type 3 gap-filling The draft model already achieves the required biomass objective under the media conditions and no reactions need to be added http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Gap-filling of draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) using parsimonious flux balance analysis (pFBA), as implemented in the COBRApy-compatible Reconstructor package. It minimizes total flux through candidate reactions from the universal ModelSEED-derived database rather than minimizing the number of reactions added. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Gap-filling of draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) using parsimonious flux balance analysis (pFBA), as implemented in the COBRApy-compatible Reconstructor package. It minimizes total flux through candidate reactions from the universal ModelSEED-derived database rather than minimizing the number of reactions added.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a .fasta or BLASTp output file requiring de novo reconstruction — use Reconstructor type 1 or type 2 inputs instead of type 3 gap-filling The draft model already achieves the required biomass objective under the media conditions and no reactions need to be added

skills.description: Use when testing whether a metabolic biomarker panel adds predictive value beyond conventional risk factors, or when the question is whether risk-factor information is already captured by correlated metabolites (e.g. lipids measured by both clinical chemistry and NMR).
skills.name: partial-correlation-analysis-of-biomarkers
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-analysis-of-biomarkers Use when testing whether a metabolic biomarker panel adds predictive value beyond conventional risk factors, or when the question is whether risk-factor information is already captured by correlated metabolites (e.g. lipids measured by both clinical chemistry and NMR). When the goal is a clinically deployable classification score in concentration units — the article explicitly states the constructed metabolic biomarker score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic, since it is based on scaled biomarker values created separately for each cohort' When adding lipid-based conventional risk factors (total cholesterol, HDL, triglycerides) as if they were independent information — these are already captured by the Nightingale NMR platform and must be excluded from the combined score When the prediction target is a disease-specific endpoint rather than 5–10 year all-cause mortality, since biomarker weights and score design are mortality-specific Quantifies the partial correlation structure between Nightingale NMR metabolic biomarkers and conventional risk factors, and tests whether adding conventional risk factors (sex, BMI, systolic blood pressure, cholesterol fractions, smoking, etc.) to a biomarker-only Cox risk score further improves 5- and 10-year all-cause mortality prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: Quantifies the partial correlation structure between Nightingale NMR metabolic biomarkers and conventional risk factors, and tests whether adding conventional risk factors (sex, BMI, systolic blood pressure, cholesterol fractions, smoking, etc.) to a biomarker-only Cox risk score further improves 5- and 10-year all-cause mortality prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a clinically deployable classification score in concentration units — the article explicitly states the constructed metabolic biomarker score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic, since it is based on scaled biomarker values created separately for each cohort' When adding lipid-based conventional risk factors (total cholesterol, HDL, triglycerides) as if they were independent information — these are already captured by the Nightingale NMR platform and must be excluded from the combined score When the prediction target is a disease-specific endpoint rather than 5–10 year all-cause mortality, since biomarker weights and score design are mortality-specific

skills.description: Use when testing metabolite–phenotype associations in a metabolomics dataset (e.g. plasma 1H NMR features vs BMI) while adjusting for epidemiological confounders such as age, gender or disease status, and a rank-based univariate model with pFDR control is needed.
skills.name: partial-correlation-confounder-adjustment
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-confounder-adjustment Use when testing metabolite–phenotype associations in a metabolomics dataset (e.g. plasma 1H NMR features vs BMI) while adjusting for epidemiological confounders such as age, gender or disease status, and a rank-based univariate model with pFDR control is needed. When the analysis goal is multivariate modelling without explicit confounder adjustment — the article states existing multivariate packages fail to properly account for confounding factors such as age and gender, which is exactly what this univariate partial-correlation approach addresses. When the data container is not a SummarizedExperiment/MultiAssayExperiment object with matched phenotype metadata (BMI, confounder columns); MWAS_stats expects this structure. When per-feature stability of estimates is not needed and bootstrapping would add unnecessary compute — bootstrap CIs only validate, they do not replace the BH-corrected association test. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Perform metabolome-wide association studies (MWAS) of a phenotype such as BMI using partial Spearman correlations that partial out epidemiological confounders (e.g. Age, Gender, T2D) with BH multiple-testing correction, as implemented in MWASTools::MWAS_stats on a SummarizedExperiment metabolomics container. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx477
skills.summary: Perform metabolome-wide association studies (MWAS) of a phenotype such as BMI using partial Spearman correlations that partial out epidemiological confounders (e.g. Age, Gender, T2D) with BH multiple-testing correction, as implemented in MWASTools::MWAS_stats on a SummarizedExperiment metabolomics container.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is multivariate modelling without explicit confounder adjustment — the article states existing multivariate packages fail to properly account for confounding factors such as age and gender, which is exactly what this univariate partial-correlation approach addresses. When the data container is not a SummarizedExperiment/MultiAssayExperiment object with matched phenotype metadata (BMI, confounder columns); MWAS_stats expects this structure. When per-feature stability of estimates is not needed and bootstrapping would add unnecessary compute — bootstrap CIs only validate, they do not replace the BH-corrected association test.

skills.description: Use when testing whether a specific metabolite feature (e.g. a Level 1-annotated carnitine peak from untargeted metabolomics) is associated with a continuous clinical biomarker in a human cohort subset, and demographic covariates (age, sex, BMI) must be held constant.
skills.name: partial-correlation-covariate-adjustment
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-covariate-adjustment Use when testing whether a specific metabolite feature (e.g. a Level 1-annotated carnitine peak from untargeted metabolomics) is associated with a continuous clinical biomarker in a human cohort subset, and demographic covariates (age, sex, BMI) must be held constant. When the metabolite of interest is not Level 1 or Level 2 annotated (e.g. only a putative MSI Level 3 assignment) — the directional validation against a named metabolite would be uninterpretable. When covariates are collinear with the biomarker itself (e.g. age is part of the diagnostic definition rather than a confounder), partialling it out may remove signal rather than confounding. When the sample size after subsetting is too small to support a partial correlation with the chosen covariate set (the method assumes sufficient residual degrees of freedom). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Computes partial correlations between a single metabolite feature (e.g. phenylacetyl-carnitine peak areas from untargeted LC-MS/MS) and clinical/biomarker outcomes (CSF p-tau, α-synuclein, Aβ42/Aβ40) while adjusting for confounders such as age, sex, and BMI. Used to separate metabolite-biomarker associations from demographic confounding in cohort subsets. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Computes partial correlations between a single metabolite feature (e.g. phenylacetyl-carnitine peak areas from untargeted LC-MS/MS) and clinical/biomarker outcomes (CSF p-tau, α-synuclein, Aβ42/Aβ40) while adjusting for confounders such as age, sex, and BMI. Used to separate metabolite-biomarker associations from demographic confounding in cohort subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the metabolite of interest is not Level 1 or Level 2 annotated (e.g. only a putative MSI Level 3 assignment) — the directional validation against a named metabolite would be uninterpretable. When covariates are collinear with the biomarker itself (e.g. age is part of the diagnostic definition rather than a confounder), partialling it out may remove signal rather than confounding. When the sample size after subsetting is too small to support a partial correlation with the chosen covariate set (the method assumes sufficient residual degrees of freedom).

skills.description: Use when a fitted GLASSO/GraphLassoCV precision matrix is available and you need an edge list of partial correlations to build a sparse metabolite network.
skills.name: partial-correlation-edge-extraction
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-edge-extraction Use when a fitted GLASSO/GraphLassoCV precision matrix is available and you need an edge list of partial correlations to build a sparse metabolite network. When the goal is cell-type-specific pathway discovery rather than a full-dataset network — MetaboLINK applies GLASSO agnostic of cell type for this step, and stage-specific sub-networks come from the later PCA overlay When the input is an unnormalized concentration table — the mean- and stddev-normalization from the MetaboLINK pipeline must be applied before fitting GLASSO When you need raw covariance rather than conditional dependence — partial correlations from the precision matrix are not plain Pearson correlations http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Derives network edges from a GLASSO sparse precision (inverse covariance) matrix by converting nonzero precision entries into partial correlations, retaining both positive and negative conditional-dependence edges between metabolite features. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fnins.2024.1520982
skills.summary: Derives network edges from a GLASSO sparse precision (inverse covariance) matrix by converting nonzero precision entries into partial correlations, retaining both positive and negative conditional-dependence edges between metabolite features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cell-type-specific pathway discovery rather than a full-dataset network — MetaboLINK applies GLASSO agnostic of cell type for this step, and stage-specific sub-networks come from the later PCA overlay When the input is an unnormalized concentration table — the mean- and stddev-normalization from the MetaboLINK pipeline must be applied before fitting GLASSO When you need raw covariance rather than conditional dependence — partial correlations from the precision matrix are not plain Pearson correlations

skills.description: Use when a DNEA (or Filigree) GLASSO network has been estimated for two experimental groups and the raw edge list is too dense for interpretation — edges must be filtered by partial correlation strength or percentile.
skills.name: partial-correlation-edge-filtering
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-edge-filtering Use when a DNEA (or Filigree) GLASSO network has been estimated for two experimental groups and the raw edge list is too dense for interpretation — edges must be filtered by partial correlation strength or percentile. The input is a raw peak-intensity feature table that has not yet been through BICtune/stabilitySelection/getNetworks — there are no edges to filter yet. Pathway-database enrichment (e.g. FELLA/KEGG) is the goal — FELLA required KEGG IDs and covered only 19 of 174 TEDDY metabolites; data-driven network filtering is not a substitute for pathway mapping. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Filtering GLASSO-estimated differential metabolite networks with DNEA's filterNetworks() to retain only edges meeting a partial correlation strength threshold (e.g. |pcor| >= 0.2), controlling network density before counting or enrichment analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Filtering GLASSO-estimated differential metabolite networks with DNEA's filterNetworks() to retain only edges meeting a partial correlation strength threshold (e.g. |pcor| >= 0.2), controlling network density before counting or enrichment analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw peak-intensity feature table that has not yet been through BICtune/stabilitySelection/getNetworks — there are no edges to filter yet. Pathway-database enrichment (e.g. FELLA/KEGG) is the goal — FELLA required KEGG IDs and covered only 19 of 174 TEDDY metabolites; data-driven network filtering is not a substitute for pathway mapping.

skills.description: Use when a small labeled cohort (e.g. CheckMate025 ccRCC baseline serum metabolomics, 543/149/149 split) must be fine-tuned from the mzLearn 2,736-feature pre-trained VAE and naive full retraining would overfit or destroy pre-trained representations.
skills.name: partial-layer-freezing-transfer-learning
skills.search_text: partial-layer-freezing-transfer-learning Use when a small labeled cohort (e.g. CheckMate025 ccRCC baseline serum metabolomics, 543/149/149 split) must be fine-tuned from the mzLearn 2,736-feature pre-trained VAE and naive full retraining would overfit or destroy pre-trained representations. No relevant pre-trained checkpoint exists (pretrained_dir=None) — the mzEmbed finetune entry point then randomly initializes weights, which is the control condition, not transfer learning Input is raw LC/MS mzML data rather than an mzLearn-derived feature matrix — signal detection/alignment must happen first Data are outside HILIC positive mode metabolomics — the current pre-trained model is specific to HILIC positive mode and other LC modes are not covered http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Fine-tune a pre-trained metabolomics VAE by freezing all weights except the final encoder layer (and the task/prediction head), preserving the representations learned from ~20,548 public blood-sample spectra while adapting to a small unseen cohort. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Fine-tune a pre-trained metabolomics VAE by freezing all weights except the final encoder layer (and the task/prediction head), preserving the representations learned from ~20,548 public blood-sample spectra while adapting to a small unseen cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No relevant pre-trained checkpoint exists (pretrained_dir=None) — the mzEmbed finetune entry point then randomly initializes weights, which is the control condition, not transfer learning Input is raw LC/MS mzML data rather than an mzLearn-derived feature matrix — signal detection/alignment must happen first Data are outside HILIC positive mode metabolomics — the current pre-trained model is specific to HILIC positive mode and other LC modes are not covered

skills.description: Use when a QSAR half-life prediction step (e.g., IFS per Arnot et al. 2014) requires log Kow and log Koa inputs for a chemical list, and descriptors must be fetched before filtering and prediction.
skills.name: partition-coefficient-descriptor-retrieval
skills.search_text: partition-coefficient-descriptor-retrieval Use when a QSAR half-life prediction step (e.g., IFS per Arnot et al. 2014) requires log Kow and log Koa inputs for a chemical list, and descriptors must be fetched before filtering and prediction. The chemical contains a metal atom or has molecular weight > 1,000, which the IFS approach cannot handle — such chemicals should be excluded rather than queried The downstream analysis does not require partition-coefficient descriptors (e.g., purely experimental half-life compilation or BioTransformer metabolite prediction, which does not consume log Kow/log Koa) http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Retrieves log Kow and log Koa partition-coefficient descriptors for each chemical in a compiled exposome database from the UFZ-LSER database (v3.2.1), producing the descriptor table required by the Iterative Fragment Selection (IFS) QSAR to predict human biotransformation half-lives (HLBs). metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Retrieves log Kow and log Koa partition-coefficient descriptors for each chemical in a compiled exposome database from the UFZ-LSER database (v3.2.1), producing the descriptor table required by the Iterative Fragment Selection (IFS) QSAR to predict human biotransformation half-lives (HLBs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chemical contains a metal atom or has molecular weight > 1,000, which the IFS approach cannot handle — such chemicals should be excluded rather than queried The downstream analysis does not require partition-coefficient descriptors (e.g., purely experimental half-life compilation or BioTransformer metabolite prediction, which does not consume log Kow/log Koa)

skills.description: Use when raw UPLC-HRMS peak lists in positive and negative ESI modes contain background/blank ions that must be removed to enumerate genuine in vitro sample components (prototypes) before annotating identities and ranking abundances.
skills.name: patbs-background-subtraction
skills.search_text: patbs-background-subtraction Use when raw UPLC-HRMS peak lists in positive and negative ESI modes contain background/blank ions that must be removed to enumerate genuine in vitro sample components (prototypes) before annotating identities and ranking abundances. Input is already a cleaned, background-subtracted feature table — applying PATBS again would strip genuine sample components. The task is matching single metabolites against a prototype database using only secondary mass-spectrometry map similarity — the article notes this MTSF-style approach is narrower than the PATBS+MDRB strategy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A non-targeted, R-based background-subtraction workflow (PATBS, precise-and-thorough background-subtraction) that strips background/blank ions from UPLC-HRMS peak lists in positive and negative ESI modes to build a genuine in vitro component (prototype) list for a TCM herb without requiring prior prediction of component structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: A non-targeted, R-based background-subtraction workflow (PATBS, precise-and-thorough background-subtraction) that strips background/blank ions from UPLC-HRMS peak lists in positive and negative ESI modes to build a genuine in vitro component (prototype) list for a TCM herb without requiring prior prediction of component structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cleaned, background-subtracted feature table — applying PATBS again would strip genuine sample components. The goal is characterizing in vivo metabolites and bridging them to prototypes via mass defect and MS2 fragment matching — that is the role of the MDRB scoring approach, not PATBS. The task is matching single metabolites against a prototype database using only secondary mass-spectrometry map similarity — the article notes this MTSF-style approach is narrower than the PATBS+MDRB strategy.

skills.description: Use when gene expression data (e.g., 43 type 2 diabetes samples) must be converted into per-sample activity levels for ~400 predefined KEGG/Biocarta pathways and correlated with a continuous phenotype such as OGTT glucose.
skills.name: pathway-activity-level-computation-via-svd
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-level-computation-via-svd Use when gene expression data (e.g., 43 type 2 diabetes samples) must be converted into per-sample activity levels for ~400 predefined KEGG/Biocarta pathways and correlated with a continuous phenotype such as OGTT glucose. The analysis goal is a pairwise two-group comparison (e.g., diabetic vs non-diabetic mean activity differences via t statistics), not correlation of pathway activity with a continuous phenotype variable The input expression data are not gene-level and cannot be standardized per gene to zero mean and unit variance across samples No predefined pathway gene sets (KEGG/Biocarta) exist for the organism or genes in the expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 PLAGE-style computation of per-sample pathway 'activity' levels by singular value decomposition (SVD) of standardized, pathway-restricted expression matrices, followed by correlation of activity levels with a quantitative phenotype (e.g., 1-hour OGTT blood glucose) and permutation-based significance testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: PLAGE-style computation of per-sample pathway 'activity' levels by singular value decomposition (SVD) of standardized, pathway-restricted expression matrices, followed by correlation of activity levels with a quantitative phenotype (e.g., 1-hour OGTT blood glucose) and permutation-based significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a pairwise two-group comparison (e.g., diabetic vs non-diabetic mean activity differences via t statistics), not correlation of pathway activity with a continuous phenotype variable The input expression data are not gene-level and cannot be standardized per gene to zero mean and unit variance across samples No predefined pathway gene sets (KEGG/Biocarta) exist for the organism or genes in the expression matrix

skills.name: pathway-activity-level-scoring
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-level-scoring Use when you have a peak-intensity matrix plus peak-to-compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) or fragmentation-based metabolite sets (GNPS Molecular Families, Mass2Motifs) and need to rank metabolite sets by activity between a case and control group. skills.summary: Rank significantly changing metabolite sets (KEGG pathways, GNPS Molecular Families, or MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) using PALS, which decomposes pathway activity levels via the PLAGE method and is more robust to missing peaks and noise than ORA or GSEA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a ranked or normalised pathway-level table rather than raw peak intensities needing decomposition Peak features carry no compound annotations and no fragmentation-based groupings (Molecular Families/Mass2Motifs) exist — unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis The goal is transcriptomics/proteomics pathway queries without the matching database: UniProt/ENSEMBL Reactome databases, not the metabolomics PiMP_KEGG/ChEBI options, must be selected

skills.description: Use when you have one or more standardised, log-transformed molecular abundance matrices (metabolomics with ChEBI/KEGG IDs, proteomics or RNA-seq with UniProt/ENSEMBL or gene symbols) and need per-sample pathway-level feature scores to feed supervised multi-omics integration models.
skills.name: pathway-activity-score-computation-kernel-pca
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-score-computation-kernel-pca Use when you have one or more standardised, log-transformed molecular abundance matrices (metabolomics with ChEBI/KEGG IDs, proteomics or RNA-seq with UniProt/ENSEMBL or gene symbols) and need per-sample pathway-level feature scores to feed supervised multi-omics integration models. Input matrix has not been log-transformed and z-score standardised per molecule; kPCA scores are unreliable on raw or unnormalised abundance values Molecule identifiers do not match the pathway database (e.g. metabolite names against Reactome ChEBI IDs without prior sspa.identifier_conversion and sspa.map_identifiers harmonisation) The goal is conventional differential-molecule pathway testing (ORA or GSEA), not per-sample pathway scoring for supervised prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Computes per-sample pathway activity-score matrices from standardised molecular abundance data using the kernel PCA (sspa_kpca) implementation in the sspa package, converting an N-by-M molecule matrix into an N-by-P pathway matrix for PathIntegrate Single-View and Multi-View models. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Computes per-sample pathway activity-score matrices from standardised molecular abundance data using the kernel PCA (sspa_kpca) implementation in the sspa package, converting an N-by-M molecule matrix into an N-by-P pathway matrix for PathIntegrate Single-View and Multi-View models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrix has not been log-transformed and z-score standardised per molecule; kPCA scores are unreliable on raw or unnormalised abundance values Molecule identifiers do not match the pathway database (e.g. metabolite names against Reactome ChEBI IDs without prior sspa.identifier_conversion and sspa.map_identifiers harmonisation) The goal is conventional differential-molecule pathway testing (ORA or GSEA), not per-sample pathway scoring for supervised prediction

skills.description: Use when a peak-feature intensity matrix (samples as columns, group row) plus a peak-to-compound annotation table is available and pathway-level ranking of significantly changing metabolite sets is the analysis goal.

skills.summary: Rank metabolite sets (KEGG/Reactome pathways, GNPS Molecular Families, MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) by pathway activity level using the PLAGE decomposition in the PALS library, which is more robust to missing peaks and noise than overrepresentation analysis (ORA) or GSEA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Many peak features lack compound annotations — unannotated peaks are simply not used for pathway analysis, degrading coverage Goal is all Reactome pathways in offline mode — offline mode provides only metabolic pathways; full-pathway or up-to-date queries need an online Neo4j Reactome instance Input is raw spectra needing feature detection first — PALS expects a processed peak-intensity matrix, not centroided/profile MS data

skills.description: Use when a metabolite set enrichment analysis (MetSEA/GSEA) step requires pathway-to-metabolite annotations in a specific file format and the source annotations are only available as a table, KEGG dump, or API response.
skills.name: pathway-annotation-gmt-formatting
skills.search_text: pathway-annotation-gmt-formatting Use when a metabolite set enrichment analysis (MetSEA/GSEA) step requires pathway-to-metabolite annotations in a specific file format and the source annotations are only available as a table, KEGG dump, or API response. The input is already in GMT format or the downstream tool consumes pathway-metabolite mappings natively (e.g. a custom `Pathway`/`Metabolites` table is accepted directly), so reformatting would be redundant. Annotations are for a non-metabolite feature type (e.g. genes) that requires a different identifier namespace than KEGG compound IDs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Converts curated pathway-metabolite associations (e.g. from KEGG) into Gene Matrix Transposed (GMT) format so ranked metabolite lists can be enriched with fgsea in the MetSEA module of EnrichMet. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Converts curated pathway-metabolite associations (e.g. from KEGG) into Gene Matrix Transposed (GMT) format so ranked metabolite lists can be enriched with fgsea in the MetSEA module of EnrichMet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already in GMT format or the downstream tool consumes pathway-metabolite mappings natively (e.g. a custom `Pathway`/`Metabolites` table is accepted directly), so reformatting would be redundant. The analysis goal is Fisher's exact-test over-representation on a metabolite set without ranked statistics; GMT conversion is not needed for that module. Annotations are for a non-metabolite feature type (e.g. genes) that requires a different identifier namespace than KEGG compound IDs.

skills.description: Use when you must annotate host metabolic reactions — identified as viral-PPI, chokepoint/bottleneck, or essential-reaction intersections — with their metabolic pathway membership in iHsaEC21 to catalogue SARS-CoV-2-hijacked pathways.
skills.name: pathway-annotation-of-hijacked-metabolic-pathways
skills.search_text: pathway-annotation-of-hijacked-metabolic-pathways Use when you must annotate host metabolic reactions — identified as viral-PPI, chokepoint/bottleneck, or essential-reaction intersections — with their metabolic pathway membership in iHsaEC21 to catalogue SARS-CoV-2-hijacked pathways. The input is a raw PPI table alone without an integrated host/virus genome-scale metabolic model and findCPcli chokepoint/essential-reaction results — no intersection can be defined The goal is generic pathway-enrichment statistics on a gene list rather than annotating specific bottleneck/essential reaction nodes with viral partners The metabolic model lacks GPR associations, so PPI-mapped human proteins cannot be traced to catalysed reactions http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 A procedure for labelling reactions at PPi (protein–protein-interaction/pathway) intersection nodes with their iHsaEC21 pathway membership, viral interaction partner, and catalysing enzyme, yielding the set of metabolic pathways hijacked by SARS-CoV-2 (48 of 334 human metabolic pathways). It links experimental PPI data (Gordon et al, 2020) to the in silico integrated host/virus genome-scale metabolic models. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: A procedure for labelling reactions at PPi (protein–protein-interaction/pathway) intersection nodes with their iHsaEC21 pathway membership, viral interaction partner, and catalysing enzyme, yielding the set of metabolic pathways hijacked by SARS-CoV-2 (48 of 334 human metabolic pathways). It links experimental PPI data (Gordon et al, 2020) to the in silico integrated host/virus genome-scale metabolic models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw PPI table alone without an integrated host/virus genome-scale metabolic model and findCPcli chokepoint/essential-reaction results — no intersection can be defined The goal is generic pathway-enrichment statistics on a gene list rather than annotating specific bottleneck/essential reaction nodes with viral partners The metabolic model lacks GPR associations, so PPI-mapped human proteins cannot be traced to catalysed reactions

skills.description: Use when per-metabolite partial residuals from null covariate regressions and a regularized graph kernel matrix (τ = 1) are available and pathway-level association p-values against a phenotype are required.
skills.name: pathway-association-pvalue-calculation
skills.search_text: pathway-association-pvalue-calculation Use when per-metabolite partial residuals from null covariate regressions and a regularized graph kernel matrix (τ = 1) are available and pathway-level association p-values against a phenotype are required. When the pathway graph is disconnected and no regularization step has been applied — the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered testing performance on disconnected graphs When the goal is omnibus multi-pathway or genome-wide association rather than testing individual pathway–phenotype associations within PaIRKAT's semi-parametric kernel framework http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Computes pathway-level p-values for phenotype association in PaIRKAT by forming a kernel-weighted quadratic-form score statistic from covariate-adjusted partial residuals and the regularized graph kernel, then approximating its null distribution with Satterthwaite's moment-matched scaled chi-square. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Computes pathway-level p-values for phenotype association in PaIRKAT by forming a kernel-weighted quadratic-form score statistic from covariate-adjusted partial residuals and the regularized graph kernel, then approximating its null distribution with Satterthwaite's moment-matched scaled chi-square.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the pathway graph is disconnected and no regularization step has been applied — the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered testing performance on disconnected graphs When the goal is omnibus multi-pathway or genome-wide association rather than testing individual pathway–phenotype associations within PaIRKAT's semi-parametric kernel framework

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare pathway databases (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) or other ORA parameters rather than the effect of the background set Only one background set is available for the dataset, so no nonspecific-vs-assay-specific pairing can be constructed Ground-truth identities of enriched pathways are required for validating ORA output — the study notes no such ground-truth dataset exists

skills.search_text: pathway-coexpression-coordination-quantification Use when you have expression profiles plus predefined KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets and need to measure pathway-wide expression coordination, or to test whether GSEA's top-ranked sets are merely coordinately expressed rather than differentially active between groups. When the goal is to test whether a pathway's mean activity level differs between groups (the PLAGE pairwise-comparison use case with permuted t-statistics) rather than to quantify how coordinately the pathway's genes are expressed When genes are not organized into predefined gene-sets (no KEGG/Biocarta membership lists available), since each score requires a restricted gene-by-sample matrix per named pathway http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how strongly a predefined pathway's genes are coordinately expressed by computing the fraction of total variation captured by the first singular value (λ²/(ng·ns)) of the restricted gene-by-sample matrix, and relates this coordination score to gene-set enrichment (GSEA) rankings. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to test whether a pathway's mean activity level differs between groups (the PLAGE pairwise-comparison use case with permuted t-statistics) rather than to quantify how coordinately the pathway's genes are expressed When genes are not organized into predefined gene-sets (no KEGG/Biocarta membership lists available), since each score requires a restricted gene-by-sample matrix per named pathway

skills.description: Use when you need to assess whether ORA conclusions on metabolomics datasets are robust to the choice of pathway database, e.g. comparing KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc significantly enriched pathway (SEP) sets.

skills.search_text: pathway-database-concordance-analysis Use when you need to assess whether ORA conclusions on metabolomics datasets are robust to the choice of pathway database, e.g. comparing KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc significantly enriched pathway (SEP) sets. skills.summary: Quantifies how much over-representation analysis (ORA) results agree when the same metabolomics datasets are analysed against different pathway databases (KEGG, Reactome, BioCyc/HumanCyc), by pooling metabolites underlying significantly enriched pathways and computing overlap coefficients.

skills.description: Use when a topology-based pathway analysis needs gene-gene interaction (edge) lists pulled from pathway databases like KEGG or Reactome for a user-supplied gene identifier set, instead of hand-curated network files.
skills.name: pathway-database-interaction-retrieval
skills.search_text: pathway-database-interaction-retrieval Use when a topology-based pathway analysis needs gene-gene interaction (edge) lists pulled from pathway databases like KEGG or Reactome for a user-supplied gene identifier set, instead of hand-curated network files. skills.search_text: pathway-database-redundancy-analysis Use when you need to measure the extent of shared metabolite content between pathways drawn from multiple source databases (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways) hosted in a RaMP MySQL instance, e.g. to assess cross-database pathway redundancy. skills.summary: Quantifies metabolite-content redundancy between biochemical pathways integrated from KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways in RaMP by computing pairwise Jaccard overlap matrices, identifying which database pairs contain the most overlapping pathways.

The pathways of interest are not integrated into RaMP (e.g. pathways from a source outside KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, HMDB).

skills.summary: Per-sample dimension transformation in Lilikoi v2.0 that projects metabolite-level intensities onto pathway-level features by computing a pathway dysregulation score (PDS) between 0 and 1 for every sample-pathway pair, producing a samples x pathways PDS matrix.

skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) plus a significant-vs-reference feature split needs pathway-level interpretation, and metabolite identification is not yet available.

skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) plus a significant-vs-reference feature split needs pathway-level interpretation, and metabolite identification is not yet available. The goal is definitive metabolite identification — 'Mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification.' The analysis requires mass flow balance of metabolic reactions in samples like serum or urine, where producing reactions occur in other tissues and mass balance is infeasible. The study requires validated multivariate (in vivo) activity calls that mummichog's single-feature significant-list input cannot directly support. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Pathway and network module enrichment for untargeted LC/MS metabolomics using mummichog, which maps significant m/z features to tentative metabolites against a genome-scale metabolic model and tests pathway activity without prior metabolite identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: Pathway and network module enrichment for untargeted LC/MS metabolomics using mummichog, which maps significant m/z features to tentative metabolites against a genome-scale metabolic model and tests pathway activity without prior metabolite identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is definitive metabolite identification — 'Mummichog is not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification.' The analysis requires mass flow balance of metabolic reactions in samples like serum or urine, where producing reactions occur in other tissues and mass balance is infeasible. The study requires validated multivariate (in vivo) activity calls that mummichog's single-feature significant-list input cannot directly support.

The input is a targeted panel of pre-identified metabolites where feature-level ambiguity is absent. skills.summary: Pathway-level enrichment testing of LC/MS spectral features against genome-scale metabolic models using Fisher's exact test with an EASE-score correction and a Gamma-modeled permutation null for adjusted p-values, as implemented in mummichog for untargeted metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A metabolite-identity table is already available and standard over-representation tools (GO/KEGG ORA) suffice — this skill is specifically for feature-level (pre-identification) enrichment. skills.description: Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table already carries level-2 metabolite annotations and the goal is to identify enriched metabolic pathways from differential-metabolite lists in the tidyMass pipeline.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-of-annotated-metabolites
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-of-annotated-metabolites Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table already carries level-2 metabolite annotations and the goal is to identify enriched metabolic pathways from differential-metabolite lists in the tidyMass pipeline. The input is raw LC-MS data or an unannotated feature table — annotations must exist at level 2 before pathway mapping is meaningful. skills.summary: Maps metabolites annotated at Metabolomics Standards Initiative level 2 (after redundant-annotation removal) onto metabolic pathways and computes pathway enrichment with the metpath package, as the biological-function-mining step of the tidyMass LC-MS untargeted metabolomics workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-MS data or an unannotated feature table — annotations must exist at level 2 before pathway mapping is meaningful. skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (DDA or SWATH-DIA, e.g. mzML from Metabolomics Workbench ST002796/ST002798) has been processed to MS1 features plus MS2 compound IDs and the goal is to test whether MS2 filtering yields more significant mummichog pathways than MS1 alone.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-result-comparison
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-result-comparison Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (DDA or SWATH-DIA, e.g. mzML from Metabolomics Workbench ST002796/ST002798) has been processed to MS1 features plus MS2 compound IDs and the goal is to test whether MS2 filtering yields more significant mummichog pathways than MS1 alone. Input is already a curated list of identified metabolites with no unannotated MS1 features — traditional enrichment on confirmed compounds does not need the MS2-filtering-vs-unfiltered comparison No MS2 spectra or compound identification results are available (e.g. MS1-only acquisition), since the second arm of the comparison cannot be built The data are not LC-MS metabolomics (e.g. proteomics or transcriptomics), since mummichog empirical-compound permutation is designed for metabolomic feature tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Compares mummichog pathway enrichment results from MetaboAnalystR 4.0 run twice on the same MS1 feature table — once unfiltered and once filtered by MS2-based compound identifications — to quantify how spectral annotation improves functional interpretation on clinical LC-MS metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-48009-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated list of identified metabolites with no unannotated MS1 features — traditional enrichment on confirmed compounds does not need the MS2-filtering-vs-unfiltered comparison No MS2 spectra or compound identification results are available (e.g. MS1-only acquisition), since the second arm of the comparison cannot be built The data are not LC-MS metabolomics (e.g. proteomics or transcriptomics), since mummichog empirical-compound permutation is designed for metabolomic feature tables

skills.description: Use when you have sex-specific (or group-specific) differential metabolite tables from a massstat differential-analysis step and need to identify which KEGG/SMPDB pathways are enriched in one group but not another.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-results-visualization
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-results-visualization Use when you have sex-specific (or group-specific) differential metabolite tables from a massstat differential-analysis step and need to identify which KEGG/SMPDB pathways are enriched in one group but not another. skills.summary: Run over-representation pathway enrichment (metPath) on sex-stratified differential metabolite lists from LC-MS colorectal-cancer data and render a per-sex summary figure. It implements the tidyMass 'biological function mining' step, converting differential-metabolite tables into KEGG/SMPDB pathway-level findings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data or a peak/feature table that has not yet passed differential analysis — use the tidyMass raw-data-processing and statistical-analysis packages first. You need pathway mapping from annotated (level-2) metabolite IDs but only have unannotated features — metabolite annotation must precede biological function mining. skills.description: Use when testing whether entire pathways are enriched/dysregulated from gene expression data by incorporating pathway topology (gene-gene interactions), or when benchmarking enrichment methods' statistical power and type-I error in simulations.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-testing Use when testing whether entire pathways are enriched/dysregulated from gene expression data by incorporating pathway topology (gene-gene interactions), or when benchmarking enrichment methods' statistical power and type-I error in simulations. Genes are treated as independent (over-representation/gene-set methods without topology) and pathway structure should not be modeled Only a list of pre-identified differentially expressed genes is available and topology-based approaches like SPIA/PRS that require detected DE genes are being considered instead Input variables include genes that belong to no tested pathway — the README says to filter the data matrix to keep only genes in at least one tested pathway before running NetGSA http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Topology-based pathway enrichment testing using the overhauled NetGSA/netgsa R package, which evaluates gene-gene interaction structure within pathways (KEGG, Reactome, PantherDB) via variance-component estimation with REHE, with optional clustering of genes into subnetworks, and benchmarking power against DEGraph, CAMERA, Pathway-Express, SPIA, PRS, and topologyGSA. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Topology-based pathway enrichment testing using the overhauled NetGSA/netgsa R package, which evaluates gene-gene interaction structure within pathways (KEGG, Reactome, PantherDB) via variance-component estimation with REHE, with optional clustering of genes into subnetworks, and benchmarking power against DEGraph, CAMERA, Pathway-Express, SPIA, PRS, and topologyGSA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes are treated as independent (over-representation/gene-set methods without topology) and pathway structure should not be modeled Only a list of pre-identified differentially expressed genes is available and topology-based approaches like SPIA/PRS that require detected DE genes are being considered instead Input variables include genes that belong to no tested pathway — the README says to filter the data matrix to keep only genes in at least one tested pathway before running NetGSA

skills.description: Use when metabolite pathway over-representation output (e.g. MetaboAnalyst 'pathway_results.csv') must be reduced to significant pathways and their constituent metabolites converted from KEGG IDs to HMDB IDs.
skills.name: pathway-fdr-significance-filtering
skills.search_text: pathway-fdr-significance-filtering Use when metabolite pathway over-representation output (e.g. MetaboAnalyst 'pathway_results.csv') must be reduced to significant pathways and their constituent metabolites converted from KEGG IDs to HMDB IDs. skills.summary: Filters MetaboAnalyst over-representation pathway results to statistically significant pathways (FDR q-value ≤ 0.05, computed via the qvalue package) and annotates each retained pathway's metabolites by mapping KEGG entries to HMDB IDs for downstream metGWAS 1.0 gene-set construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not MetaboAnalyst over-representation output (e.g. raw metabolite abundance tables or GWAS summary statistics) — this skill expects pathway_results.csv and name_map.csv. skills.description: Use when metabolomics or multiomics feature tables carry KEGG IDs and you need to place features on KEGG pathway gene/compound nodes (with topology) before ORA or perturbation impact analysis such as eSPIA.
skills.name: pathway-feature-mapping-kegg-ids
skills.search_text: pathway-feature-mapping-kegg-ids Use when metabolomics or multiomics feature tables carry KEGG IDs and you need to place features on KEGG pathway gene/compound nodes (with topology) before ORA or perturbation impact analysis such as eSPIA. skills.search_text: pathway-gene-set-mapping-kegg-biocarta Use when a genes-by-samples expression matrix (e.g., microarray) must be decomposed into predefined KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene sets (~400 pathways and complexes) as input to SVD-based pathway activity analysis. skills.description: Use when a gene expression analysis needs a predefined gene-set universe (KEGG, Biocarta pathways and complexes) to quantify pathway activity or compute enrichment scores from gene rankings.

skills.search_text: pathway-geneset-curation-kegg-biocarta Use when a gene expression analysis needs a predefined gene-set universe (KEGG, Biocarta pathways and complexes) to quantify pathway activity or compute enrichment scores from gene rankings. skills.summary: Curate the collection of ~400 predefined KEGG and Biocarta pathways and complexes that serve as the gene-set universe for pathway-level gene expression analysis (e.g. PLAGE, GSEA), making each set available as a list of member genes for ranking-based enrichment or SVD activity computation.
