skills.description: Use when metabolites map onto a pathway graph (e.g., KEGG edges from the KEGG reaction database) that is sparse or disconnected, and you want to incorporate that graph topology into a kernel machine association test via a regularized normalized Laplacian.
skills.name: pathway-graph-kernel-smoothing
skills.search_text: pathway-graph-kernel-smoothing Use when metabolites map onto a pathway graph (e.g., KEGG edges from the KEGG reaction database) that is sparse or disconnected, and you want to incorporate that graph topology into a kernel machine association test via a regularized normalized Laplacian. When the pathway graph is well-connected and dense — regularization targets sparsity and disconnected components, and the article notes it is important to examine graph structure before applying a regularization step When you have no metabolite-to-pathway mapping (e.g., metabolites lack KEGG/HMDB identifiers), since the Laplacian cannot be constructed When the goal is standard per-metabolite differential analysis rather than pathway-level kernel association testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Graph kernel regularization in the PaIRKAT sense: eigendecompose a pathway's normalized Laplacian, apply the linear regularization r(λ)=1+τλ with τ=1 to its eigenvalues, and pass the reconstructed regularized Laplacian into the kernel function of a semi-parametric kernel machine score test, dampening noisy graph components while preserving biologically relevant structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Graph kernel regularization in the PaIRKAT sense: eigendecompose a pathway's normalized Laplacian, apply the linear regularization r(λ)=1+τλ with τ=1 to its eigenvalues, and pass the reconstructed regularized Laplacian into the kernel function of a semi-parametric kernel machine score test, dampening noisy graph components while preserving biologically relevant structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the pathway graph is well-connected and dense — regularization targets sparsity and disconnected components, and the article notes it is important to examine graph structure before applying a regularization step When you have no metabolite-to-pathway mapping (e.g., metabolites lack KEGG/HMDB identifiers), since the Laplacian cannot be constructed When the goal is standard per-metabolite differential analysis rather than pathway-level kernel association testing

skills.description: Use when you need to evaluate robustness or statistical power of pathway-structured association tests (e.g. kernel machine tests on Laplacian-derived pathway kernels) under controlled amounts of incorrect or incomplete pathway graph knowledge.
skills.name: pathway-graph-simulation-edge-permutation
skills.search_text: pathway-graph-simulation-edge-permutation Use when you need to evaluate robustness or statistical power of pathway-structured association tests (e.g. kernel machine tests on Laplacian-derived pathway kernels) under controlled amounts of incorrect or incomplete pathway graph knowledge. The goal is a real-data pathway analysis on measured (not simulated) pathway knowledge — this skill fabricates synthetic graphs for benchmarking, not for biological inference. Pathway graphs are already correct and only incomplete coverage (missing metabolites/edges) is of interest rather than incorrectly rewired edges; a different incompleteness simulation would be appropriate. The analysis pipeline does not consume a graph or pathway structure at all (e.g. univariate metabolite association testing); permuting edges has no target to perturb. Generate Barabasi-Albert random pathway graphs with igraph and permute a controlled fraction of their edges (keeping edge count fixed) to simulate incorrect pathway knowledge, so that power of graph-regularized tests like PaIRKAT can be measured as a function of pathway mismatch. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Generate Barabasi-Albert random pathway graphs with igraph and permute a controlled fraction of their edges (keeping edge count fixed) to simulate incorrect pathway knowledge, so that power of graph-regularized tests like PaIRKAT can be measured as a function of pathway mismatch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a real-data pathway analysis on measured (not simulated) pathway knowledge — this skill fabricates synthetic graphs for benchmarking, not for biological inference. Pathway graphs are already correct and only incomplete coverage (missing metabolites/edges) is of interest rather than incorrectly rewired edges; a different incompleteness simulation would be appropriate. The analysis pipeline does not consume a graph or pathway structure at all (e.g. univariate metabolite association testing); permuting edges has no target to perturb.

skills.description: Use when testing phenotype–pathway associations from metabolomics data where metabolites can be mapped to a pathway graph (e.g., KEGG reaction edges) and the graph's topography should inform the kernel.
skills.name: pathway-graph-topology-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-graph-topology-analysis Use when testing phenotype–pathway associations from metabolomics data where metabolites can be mapped to a pathway graph (e.g., KEGG reaction edges) and the graph's topography should inform the kernel. There is no pathway/graph annotation linking metabolites — PaIRKAT requires a pathway adjacency matrix such as KEGG reaction-derived edges; without it the kernel cannot incorporate topography. The pathway graph structure has not been inspected first — the authors state it is important to examine graph structure before applying regularization, and sparse or poorly characterized graphs can hinder performance. The cohort is large (>1,000 observations) and the goal is to distinguish between competing methods — p-values from compared methods were indistinguishable at that sample size. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 PaIRKAT incorporates pathway graph topography into semiparametric kernel machine regression by feeding the regularized (smoothed) normalized Laplacian of the pathway graph into the kernel function, yielding more powerful score tests of phenotype–pathway associations in metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: PaIRKAT incorporates pathway graph topography into semiparametric kernel machine regression by feeding the regularized (smoothed) normalized Laplacian of the pathway graph into the kernel function, yielding more powerful score tests of phenotype–pathway associations in metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no pathway/graph annotation linking metabolites — PaIRKAT requires a pathway adjacency matrix such as KEGG reaction-derived edges; without it the kernel cannot incorporate topography. The pathway graph structure has not been inspected first — the authors state it is important to examine graph structure before applying regularization, and sparse or poorly characterized graphs can hinder performance. The cohort is large (>1,000 observations) and the goal is to distinguish between competing methods — p-values from compared methods were indistinguishable at that sample size.

skills.description: Use when labeled pathway sets (positives from TomatoCyc, negatives from MetaCyc plus random sampling) must be classified from metabolite correlation network waveforms, or when reproducing NetAurHPD-style AUC benchmarks.
skills.name: pathway-hyperlink-classification-training
skills.search_text: pathway-hyperlink-classification-training Use when labeled pathway sets (positives from TomatoCyc, negatives from MetaCyc plus random sampling) must be classified from metabolite correlation network waveforms, or when reproducing NetAurHPD-style AUC benchmarks. Input is raw metabolomics intensity data rather than already-auralized pathway signals — imputation (probabilistic PCA via pcaMethods in Rstudio), Metabolite CN construction (Pearson |r| >= 0.3, p <= 0.01), and auralization must happen first The network is a generic centrality-estimation task rather than hyperlink/pathway classification — use the centrality-learning auralization pipelines instead of the M5 classifier Only two compounds per pathway are observed in the Metabolite CN, since the dataset keeps only pathways with more than two compounds present http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Trains the M5 deep convolutional classifier on auralized pathway signals (averaged metabolite waveforms from Metabolite CNs) to predict presence/absence of metabolic pathways, then optimizes the decision threshold via Youden's J statistic and computes micro-average AUC under 10-fold cross-validation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Trains the M5 deep convolutional classifier on auralized pathway signals (averaged metabolite waveforms from Metabolite CNs) to predict presence/absence of metabolic pathways, then optimizes the decision threshold via Youden's J statistic and computes micro-average AUC under 10-fold cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metabolomics intensity data rather than already-auralized pathway signals — imputation (probabilistic PCA via pcaMethods in Rstudio), Metabolite CN construction (Pearson |r| >= 0.3, p <= 0.01), and auralization must happen first The network is a generic centrality-estimation task rather than hyperlink/pathway classification — use the centrality-learning auralization pipelines instead of the M5 classifier Only two compounds per pathway are observed in the Metabolite CN, since the dataset keeps only pathways with more than two compounds present

skills.description: Use when you have ORA enrichment results (adjusted Fisher's exact-test p-values on KEGG pathways) plus a significant metabolite list, and need to prioritize pathways by network topology impact rather than p-value rank alone.
skills.name: pathway-impact-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: pathway-impact-plot-visualization Use when you have ORA enrichment results (adjusted Fisher's exact-test p-values on KEGG pathways) plus a significant metabolite list, and need to prioritize pathways by network topology impact rather than p-value rank alone. When only a ranked metabolite list is available (no significant-metabolite set for contingency-table testing) — MetSEA via fgsea is the appropriate module instead When analyzing lipidomics or non-KEGG feature types without a pathway-feature mapping — supply a custom Pathway/Metabolites table or use the LION-based lipidomics workflow rather than the KEGG impact plot When the input is a raw metabolomics intensity matrix — differential analysis (run_de with fc_threshold=1, pval_threshold=0.05) must be performed first to obtain significant metabolites http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Renders the EnrichMet pathway impact plot, which combines -log10(BH-adjusted p-values) from Fisher's exact-test over-representation analysis with a topology-based pathway impact score derived from betweenness centrality on a STITCH metabolite-metabolite interaction network. This surfaces pathways (e.g., caffeine metabolism) that statistical significance alone would rank below top hits (e.g., pyrimidine metabolism). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Renders the EnrichMet pathway impact plot, which combines -log10(BH-adjusted p-values) from Fisher's exact-test over-representation analysis with a topology-based pathway impact score derived from betweenness centrality on a STITCH metabolite-metabolite interaction network. This surfaces pathways (e.g., caffeine metabolism) that statistical significance alone would rank below top hits (e.g., pyrimidine metabolism).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a ranked metabolite list is available (no significant-metabolite set for contingency-table testing) — MetSEA via fgsea is the appropriate module instead When analyzing lipidomics or non-KEGG feature types without a pathway-feature mapping — supply a custom Pathway/Metabolites table or use the LION-based lipidomics workflow rather than the KEGG impact plot When the input is a raw metabolomics intensity matrix — differential analysis (run_de with fc_threshold=1, pval_threshold=0.05) must be performed first to obtain significant metabolites

skills.description: Use when you have fitted a pathway-level multi-omics model (PathIntegrate MB-PLS/Single-View or DIABLO on ssPA-transformed data) and need ranked pathway importance statistics with permutation-tested significance or detection AUCs.
skills.name: pathway-importance-scoring
skills.search_text: pathway-importance-scoring Use when you have fitted a pathway-level multi-omics model (PathIntegrate MB-PLS/Single-View or DIABLO on ssPA-transformed data) and need ranked pathway importance statistics with permutation-tested significance or detection AUCs. When you need molecule-level (not pathway-level) feature importance — this skill ranks multi-omics pathways, not individual molecules When the pathway coverage of your omics data is too low for a pathway-level analysis (a stated bottleneck, particularly for metabolomics) When samples lack measurements across all omics views — PathIntegrate requires all input omics measured on the same individuals, so such samples must be discarded http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes and validates pathway-level importance statistics from fitted multi-omics predictive models (MB-VIP/VIP for PathIntegrate MB-PLS/Single-View, RGCCA loadings and bootstrap non-zero loadings for DIABLO), using permutation-based null distributions to score pathway detection by confusion-matrix AUC. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Computes and validates pathway-level importance statistics from fitted multi-omics predictive models (MB-VIP/VIP for PathIntegrate MB-PLS/Single-View, RGCCA loadings and bootstrap non-zero loadings for DIABLO), using permutation-based null distributions to score pathway detection by confusion-matrix AUC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need molecule-level (not pathway-level) feature importance — this skill ranks multi-omics pathways, not individual molecules When the pathway coverage of your omics data is too low for a pathway-level analysis (a stated bottleneck, particularly for metabolomics) When samples lack measurements across all omics views — PathIntegrate requires all input omics measured on the same individuals, so such samples must be discarded

skills.description: Use when you have a PDS score matrix (0–1 pathway deregulation scores) restricted to Lilikoi-selected pathway features and want to check whether pathway-level profiles visually separate phenotype classes before or after classification modeling.
skills.name: pathway-level-clustering
skills.search_text: pathway-level-clustering Use when you have a PDS score matrix (0–1 pathway deregulation scores) restricted to Lilikoi-selected pathway features and want to check whether pathway-level profiles visually separate phenotype classes before or after classification modeling. Input is raw metabolite measurements rather than a pathway-level PDS matrix — run metab_to_pathway and get_pd_scores first No phenotype labels are available, so cluster separation relative to classes cannot be validated The goal is group-level pathway enrichment (e.g. MetPA/IMPaLA/MPEA) rather than personalized, sample-level pathway representation and classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cluster samples on Lilikoi's personalized pathway deregulation score (PDS) matrix — e.g. hierarchical clustering on the selected pathway features — to verify that the pathway-level representation separates disease phenotypes such as ER+ vs ER− breast cancer tissue samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giy136
skills.summary: Cluster samples on Lilikoi's personalized pathway deregulation score (PDS) matrix — e.g. hierarchical clustering on the selected pathway features — to verify that the pathway-level representation separates disease phenotypes such as ER+ vs ER− breast cancer tissue samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metabolite measurements rather than a pathway-level PDS matrix — run metab_to_pathway and get_pd_scores first No phenotype labels are available, so cluster separation relative to classes cannot be validated The goal is group-level pathway enrichment (e.g. MetPA/IMPaLA/MPEA) rather than personalized, sample-level pathway representation and classification

skills.description: Use when you have a per-sample pathway score matrix (e.g., Lilikoi PDS matrix built by lilikoi.PDSfun) and need to pick the most significant pathway features before running a classification or prognosis model in Lilikoi v2.0.
skills.name: pathway-level-feature-selection
skills.search_text: pathway-level-feature-selection Use when you have a per-sample pathway score matrix (e.g., Lilikoi PDS matrix built by lilikoi.PDSfun) and need to pick the most significant pathway features before running a classification or prognosis model in Lilikoi v2.0. Input is still raw metabolite intensities rather than a pathway-level (PDS) score matrix — run lilikoi.MetaTOpathway and lilikoi.PDSfun first, since featuresSelection expects pathway-level features. You want a survival-feature selection step for the Cox-PH / Cox-nnet prognosis module instead of the disease-classification pathway filter — the article describes featuresSelection in the classification workflow, not for prognosis feature picking. The sample labels are unavailable or unreliable — information-gain selection is supervised and needs phenotype labels to rank pathways. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects the phenotype-informative pathways from a metabolite-derived pathway dysregulation score (PDS) matrix using information gain ranking with a 0.50 threshold, as implemented in Lilikoi v2.0's lilikoi.featuresSelection, so that downstream classification/regression operates on a reduced set of significant pathways. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Selects the phenotype-informative pathways from a metabolite-derived pathway dysregulation score (PDS) matrix using information gain ranking with a 0.50 threshold, as implemented in Lilikoi v2.0's lilikoi.featuresSelection, so that downstream classification/regression operates on a reduced set of significant pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw metabolite intensities rather than a pathway-level (PDS) score matrix — run lilikoi.MetaTOpathway and lilikoi.PDSfun first, since featuresSelection expects pathway-level features. You want a survival-feature selection step for the Cox-PH / Cox-nnet prognosis module instead of the disease-classification pathway filter — the article describes featuresSelection in the classification workflow, not for prognosis feature picking. The sample labels are unavailable or unreliable — information-gain selection is supervised and needs phenotype labels to rank pathways.

skills.description: Use when you need to empirically justify a pathway-transformation step by comparing pathway-level versus molecular-level univariate detection power on injected-signal simulations spanning effect sizes 0–1.
skills.name: pathway-level-vs-molecular-level-signal-detection-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pathway-level-vs-molecular-level-signal-detection-benchmarking Use when you need to empirically justify a pathway-transformation step by comparing pathway-level versus molecular-level univariate detection power on injected-signal simulations spanning effect sizes 0–1. Your goal is a full comparison of PathIntegrate to conventional pathway analysis approaches (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) — the authors explicitly state this was beyond the scope of their work You need a benchmarking dataset with known validated molecular/pathway-level signals and n ≥ 1000 — the authors note such an ideal benchmarking dataset was not available, so semi-synthetic injection is a proxy rather than a validation of real biological signals Your comparison depends on exact pathway definitions and sizes — the authors warn these vary between databases, making molecular vs. pathway-level model comparison a challenge http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A semi-synthetic benchmarking skill that quantifies whether single-sample pathway analysis (ssPA) transformation of multi-omics abundance matrices increases univariate Mann-Whitney-U detection power versus Fisher-combined molecular-level tests in low signal-to-noise scenarios. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: A semi-synthetic benchmarking skill that quantifies whether single-sample pathway analysis (ssPA) transformation of multi-omics abundance matrices increases univariate Mann-Whitney-U detection power versus Fisher-combined molecular-level tests in low signal-to-noise scenarios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is a full comparison of PathIntegrate to conventional pathway analysis approaches (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) — the authors explicitly state this was beyond the scope of their work You need a benchmarking dataset with known validated molecular/pathway-level signals and n ≥ 1000 — the authors note such an ideal benchmarking dataset was not available, so semi-synthetic injection is a proxy rather than a validation of real biological signals Your comparison depends on exact pathway definitions and sizes — the authors warn these vary between databases, making molecular vs. pathway-level model comparison a challenge

skills.description: Use when you need to stress-test the stability of an ORA-derived list of significantly enriched metabolomics pathways against compound annotation errors, e.g. measuring how many baseline pathways (p <= 0.1) are lost or falsely gained at a given simulated misidentification rate.
skills.name: pathway-loss-gain-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: pathway-loss-gain-rate-quantification Use when you need to stress-test the stability of an ORA-derived list of significantly enriched metabolomics pathways against compound annotation errors, e.g. measuring how many baseline pathways (p <= 0.1) are lost or falsely gained at a given simulated misidentification rate. The goal is a comparison of pathway databases (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) — the authors state an extensive comparison of pathway databases is beyond the scope of this work The task is identifying truly affected pathways in a real perturbation experiment — the study notes no ground-truth dataset exists where the identities of enriched pathways are known, and this skill only measures stability under simulated annotation error The pathway significance list was selected with multiple-testing correction (e.g. q <= 0.05 BH FDR) — this skill's loss/gain metric is defined on SEPs at p <= 0.1 without correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies the sensitivity of over-representation analysis (ORA) to metabolite misidentification by simulating replacement of compounds with approximately isobaric (±20 ppm) or identical-chemical-formula counterparts and computing pathway loss and gain rates against a 0% misidentification baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Quantifies the sensitivity of over-representation analysis (ORA) to metabolite misidentification by simulating replacement of compounds with approximately isobaric (±20 ppm) or identical-chemical-formula counterparts and computing pathway loss and gain rates against a 0% misidentification baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a comparison of pathway databases (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) — the authors state an extensive comparison of pathway databases is beyond the scope of this work The task is identifying truly affected pathways in a real perturbation experiment — the study notes no ground-truth dataset exists where the identities of enriched pathways are known, and this skill only measures stability under simulated annotation error The pathway significance list was selected with multiple-testing correction (e.g. q <= 0.05 BH FDR) — this skill's loss/gain metric is defined on SEPs at p <= 0.1 without correction

skills.description: Use when annotating m/z features from preprocessed organ-specific MSI data (e.g. AFADESI-MSI in positive/negative mode) and tracing which metabolic pathways are altered across multiple organs, such as liver, brain, and kidney.
skills.name: pathway-metabolite-mapping
skills.search_text: pathway-metabolite-mapping Use when annotating m/z features from preprocessed organ-specific MSI data (e.g. AFADESI-MSI in positive/negative mode) and tracing which metabolic pathways are altered across multiple organs, such as liver, brain, and kidney. The input is unprocessed or non-imaging data: MSIannotator expects a preprocessed MSI dataset with measured m/z in the first column, not raw spectral files. The database organ or detection mode does not match the MSI data being annotated (e.g. a liver positive-mode database paired with brain negative-mode MSIdata). The goal is LC-MS/MS compound identification rather than MSI metabolite annotation: the workflow was built around the adduct form differences between LC-MS and AFADESI-MSI. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Maps organ-specific metabolite annotations from ambient mass spectrometry imaging (AFADESI-MSI) data onto shared metabolic pathways to reveal spatial metabolic alterations across organs, e.g. identifying the alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism pathway as simultaneously altered in the liver, brain, and kidney of diabetic mice. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Maps organ-specific metabolite annotations from ambient mass spectrometry imaging (AFADESI-MSI) data onto shared metabolic pathways to reveal spatial metabolic alterations across organs, e.g. identifying the alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism pathway as simultaneously altered in the liver, brain, and kidney of diabetic mice.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is unprocessed or non-imaging data: MSIannotator expects a preprocessed MSI dataset with measured m/z in the first column, not raw spectral files. The database organ or detection mode does not match the MSI data being annotated (e.g. a liver positive-mode database paired with brain negative-mode MSIdata). The goal is LC-MS/MS compound identification rather than MSI metabolite annotation: the workflow was built around the adduct form differences between LC-MS and AFADESI-MSI.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature list must be mapped to pathway database identifiers (KEGG compound IDs) to enable pathway-based network construction or enrichment, and when you need to quantify how many features are actually annotatable.
skills.name: pathway-network-construction
skills.search_text: pathway-network-construction Use when a metabolomics feature list must be mapped to pathway database identifiers (KEGG compound IDs) to enable pathway-based network construction or enrichment, and when you need to quantify how many features are actually annotatable. The dataset contains many exogenous, secondary-metabolism, or unknown metabolites and the goal is unbiased network analysis — use a data-driven approach such as the DNEA R package (GLASSO partial correlation networks) instead The metabolite list is already a set of KEGG compound IDs requiring no name-to-ID mapping step http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Construction of pathway-database-dependent biological networks requires mapping metabolite features to reference identifiers (e.g., KEGG compound IDs) before tools like FELLA can build networks from pathway definitions; this skill covers the ID-mapping step and quantifying the resulting pathway-coverage gap. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Construction of pathway-database-dependent biological networks requires mapping metabolite features to reference identifiers (e.g., KEGG compound IDs) before tools like FELLA can build networks from pathway definitions; this skill covers the ID-mapping step and quantifying the resulting pathway-coverage gap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains many exogenous, secondary-metabolism, or unknown metabolites and the goal is unbiased network analysis — use a data-driven approach such as the DNEA R package (GLASSO partial correlation networks) instead The metabolite list is already a set of KEGG compound IDs requiring no name-to-ID mapping step

skills.description: Use when interpreting metabolomics data with ORA and you need to know how sensitive the significant-pathway result is to the background set, the DA-metabolite list construction (e.g. BH FDR q <= 0.05 vs p-value ordering), or the pathway database (KEGG, Reactome, BioCyc).
skills.name: pathway-ora-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-ora-sensitivity-analysis Use when interpreting metabolomics data with ORA and you need to know how sensitive the significant-pathway result is to the background set, the DA-metabolite list construction (e.g. BH FDR q <= 0.05 vs p-value ordering), or the pathway database (KEGG, Reactome, BioCyc). Input is already a validated ground-truth set of enriched pathways — the authors note this study is limited by the lack of availability of a ground-truth dataset where the identities of enriched pathways are known You need a definitive single answer for which pathway database is best — an extensive comparison of pathway databases is beyond the scope of this work and readers are referred to other studies Your data come from a platform without a chromatographic separation step (e.g. Quiros et al. 2017, Fuhrer et al. 2017) and metabolite identifications carry high uncertainty, since the sensitivity conclusions assume reasonably confident compound assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Systematically varies over-representation analysis (ORA) inputs — background set, differential metabolite selection threshold, pathway database, misidentification rate, and assay-specific mapping — to quantify how each choice changes the list of significantly enriched pathways (SEPs), using five MS-based untargeted metabolomics datasets and right-tailed Fisher's exact (hypergeometric) tests in Python. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Systematically varies over-representation analysis (ORA) inputs — background set, differential metabolite selection threshold, pathway database, misidentification rate, and assay-specific mapping — to quantify how each choice changes the list of significantly enriched pathways (SEPs), using five MS-based untargeted metabolomics datasets and right-tailed Fisher's exact (hypergeometric) tests in Python.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated ground-truth set of enriched pathways — the authors note this study is limited by the lack of availability of a ground-truth dataset where the identities of enriched pathways are known You need a definitive single answer for which pathway database is best — an extensive comparison of pathway databases is beyond the scope of this work and readers are referred to other studies Your data come from a platform without a chromatographic separation step (e.g. Quiros et al. 2017, Fuhrer et al. 2017) and metabolite identifications carry high uncertainty, since the sensitivity conclusions assume reasonably confident compound assignments

skills.description: Use when a standalone metabolomics dataset (e.g., a table of 56 named urine metabolites) needs pathway-level interpretation via over-representation testing before downstream metabolite-gene set comparison.
skills.name: pathway-over-representation-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-over-representation-analysis Use when a standalone metabolomics dataset (e.g., a table of 56 named urine metabolites) needs pathway-level interpretation via over-representation testing before downstream metabolite-gene set comparison. Input is paired metabolomics-GWAS data — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for standalone, unpaired datasets and is limited to genes with known metabolite interactions. The metabolite list has not been mapped to HMDB identifiers yet — run the name-mapping step first, since over-representation testing operates on mapped identifiers. You need user-adjustable normalization or scaling — the MetaboAnalyst-based preprocessing in this workflow is fixed/hard-coded in the Section 2.1 script. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Hypergeometric over-representation testing of mapped metabolites against KEGG pathway gene sets, as implemented in the MetaboAnalyst-based first step of the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow, to identify pathways enriched in a standalone metabolomics dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Hypergeometric over-representation testing of mapped metabolites against KEGG pathway gene sets, as implemented in the MetaboAnalyst-based first step of the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow, to identify pathways enriched in a standalone metabolomics dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is paired metabolomics-GWAS data — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for standalone, unpaired datasets and is limited to genes with known metabolite interactions. The metabolite list has not been mapped to HMDB identifiers yet — run the name-mapping step first, since over-representation testing operates on mapped identifiers. You need user-adjustable normalization or scaling — the MetaboAnalyst-based preprocessing in this workflow is fixed/hard-coded in the Section 2.1 script.

skills.description: Use when you have a curated list of dysregulated metabolites (e.g., Log2FC > 1.5, BH-adj p < 0.05) from LC–MS metabolomics and want to identify over-represented biological pathways such as lipid or amino-acid metabolism.
skills.name: pathway-over-representation-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-over-representation-analysis Use when you have a curated list of dysregulated metabolites (e.g., Log2FC > 1.5, BH-adj p < 0.05) from LC–MS metabolomics and want to identify over-represented biological pathways such as lipid or amino-acid metabolism. The metabolite list is from raw, uncorrected data and may be too sparse or contaminated with batch drift — the article noted the raw-data list contained too few metabolites from these pathways to trigger enrichment. You need pathway-level abundance changes rather than presence/absence over-representation; this method tests whether a pre-defined pathway's compounds are over-represented, not whether pathway activity changed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Over-representation (MSEA) analysis of a differential metabolite list against the KEGG compound pathway database using ConsensusPathDB's hypergeometric test with FDR correction, to identify biological pathways enriched among dysregulated metabolites (e.g., alpha-Linolenic acid metabolism, fatty acid biosynthesis). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Over-representation (MSEA) analysis of a differential metabolite list against the KEGG compound pathway database using ConsensusPathDB's hypergeometric test with FDR correction, to identify biological pathways enriched among dysregulated metabolites (e.g., alpha-Linolenic acid metabolism, fatty acid biosynthesis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolite list is from raw, uncorrected data and may be too sparse or contaminated with batch drift — the article noted the raw-data list contained too few metabolites from these pathways to trigger enrichment. You need pathway-level abundance changes rather than presence/absence over-representation; this method tests whether a pre-defined pathway's compounds are over-represented, not whether pathway activity changed.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of metabolites and/or genes of interest and need statistically adjusted pathway overrepresentation p-values from the RaMP relational database (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, HMDB annotations).
skills.name: pathway-overrepresentation-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-overrepresentation-analysis Use when you have a list of metabolites and/or genes of interest and need statistically adjusted pathway overrepresentation p-values from the RaMP relational database (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, HMDB annotations). Your analyte list is already a scored/continuous feature table rather than a discrete list of identifiers — Fisher's exact test contingency tables require membership counts, not fold changes or intensities You need pathway enrichment across non-RaMP sources (e.g. GO-only or MSigDB-only gene sets) or species lacking KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways/HMDB annotation coverage You only want raw pathway membership lookups without statistical overrepresentation testing — use RaMP's batch query functions (e.g. rampFastCata, getPathwayFromAnalyte alone) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Runs RaMP's pathway overrepresentation analysis on user-supplied gene and/or metabolite lists, using Fisher's exact test per pathway and Fisher's combined-probability test to merge metabolite- and gene-side p-values, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg and Holm multiple-testing adjustment. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo8010016
skills.summary: Runs RaMP's pathway overrepresentation analysis on user-supplied gene and/or metabolite lists, using Fisher's exact test per pathway and Fisher's combined-probability test to merge metabolite- and gene-side p-values, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg and Holm multiple-testing adjustment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analyte list is already a scored/continuous feature table rather than a discrete list of identifiers — Fisher's exact test contingency tables require membership counts, not fold changes or intensities You need pathway enrichment across non-RaMP sources (e.g. GO-only or MSigDB-only gene sets) or species lacking KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways/HMDB annotation coverage You only want raw pathway membership lookups without statistical overrepresentation testing — use RaMP's batch query functions (e.g. rampFastCata, getPathwayFromAnalyte alone) instead

skills.description: Use when a Fisher's enrichment result table (fishers_df) contains many overlapping significant pathways across KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB, and you need to reduce redundancy into non-overlapping pathway clusters.
skills.name: pathway-overrepresentation-clustering
skills.search_text: pathway-overrepresentation-clustering Use when a Fisher's enrichment result table (fishers_df) contains many overlapping significant pathways across KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB, and you need to reduce redundancy into non-overlapping pathway clusters. Input is a raw analyte list rather than a filtered Fisher's enrichment results table — run runFisherTest and FilterFishersResults first The goal is building or updating the RaMP MySQL backend database itself (use Mathelab/RaMP-BackEnd scripts instead of findCluster) Only a single pathway or a small non-overlapping set of enriched pathways is under review, where clustering by overlap adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Groups significantly enriched pathways from a Fisher's overrepresentation test into redundant-reducing clusters using RaMP's DAVID-style heuristic fuzzy multiple-linkage partitioning: Jaccard analyte-overlap seeds, threshold-based assignment, and iterative agglomerative cluster merging. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo8010016
skills.summary: Groups significantly enriched pathways from a Fisher's overrepresentation test into redundant-reducing clusters using RaMP's DAVID-style heuristic fuzzy multiple-linkage partitioning: Jaccard analyte-overlap seeds, threshold-based assignment, and iterative agglomerative cluster merging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw analyte list rather than a filtered Fisher's enrichment results table — run runFisherTest and FilterFishersResults first The goal is building or updating the RaMP MySQL backend database itself (use Mathelab/RaMP-BackEnd scripts instead of findCluster) Only a single pathway or a small non-overlapping set of enriched pathways is under review, where clustering by overlap adds no value

skills.description: Use when evaluating how stable pathway rankings from a metabolomics tool remain when a large fraction of peak features is randomly removed, and you need a quantitative robustness metric (F1) to compare competing ranking methods.
skills.name: pathway-ranking-robustness-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pathway-ranking-robustness-benchmarking Use when evaluating how stable pathway rankings from a metabolomics tool remain when a large fraction of peak features is randomly removed, and you need a quantitative robustness metric (F1) to compare competing ranking methods. The dataset is complete (no missing peaks) and the goal is simply to rank pathways, not to compare method robustness — run the ranking method directly instead. Peak features lack compound annotations (unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis), so subsampling of annotated features would not reflect pathway coverage. The pathway database or annotations cannot be mapped to a supported ID space (KEGG/ChEBI), as ORA/GSEA/PLAGE in PALS require compound-level ID matching. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Benchmarks pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE/PLAGE, ORA, GSEA) under data loss by comparing top-ranked pathway sets from subsampled data against full-data reference rankings, using precision/recall/F1 to quantify which method is most robust to missing features. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Benchmarks pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE/PLAGE, ORA, GSEA) under data loss by comparing top-ranked pathway sets from subsampled data against full-data reference rankings, using precision/recall/F1 to quantify which method is most robust to missing features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is complete (no missing peaks) and the goal is simply to rank pathways, not to compare method robustness — run the ranking method directly instead. Peak features lack compound annotations (unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis), so subsampling of annotated features would not reflect pathway coverage. The pathway database or annotations cannot be mapped to a supported ID space (KEGG/ChEBI), as ORA/GSEA/PLAGE in PALS require compound-level ID matching.

skills.description: Use when you have a feature abundance table (KO numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers) with sample metadata and need threshold-free, pathway/module-level enrichment with directionality across two-group, multi-group, or longitudinal designs.
skills.name: pathway-reporter-score-aggregation
skills.search_text: pathway-reporter-score-aggregation Use when you have a feature abundance table (KO numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers) with sample metadata and need threshold-free, pathway/module-level enrichment with directionality across two-group, multi-group, or longitudinal designs. The input abundance table has been prefiltered to significant features — GRSA is threshold-free and requires background information The analysis requires per-feature significance testing only, without pathway-level aggregation (use ko.test alone) A hypergeometric-style over-representation analysis of a pre-defined significant list is specifically required (GRSA instead considers all KOs in a pathway for increased sensitivity) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aggregate per-feature (KO/gene/compound) differential statistics into pathway- or module-level reporter scores using the Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) implemented in the R package ReporterScore, a threshold-free method supporting multi-group and longitudinal omics designs. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Aggregate per-feature (KO/gene/compound) differential statistics into pathway- or module-level reporter scores using the Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) implemented in the R package ReporterScore, a threshold-free method supporting multi-group and longitudinal omics designs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input abundance table has been prefiltered to significant features — GRSA is threshold-free and requires background information The analysis requires per-feature significance testing only, without pathway-level aggregation (use ko.test alone) A hypergeometric-style over-representation analysis of a pre-defined significant list is specifically required (GRSA instead considers all KOs in a pathway for increased sensitivity)

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics dataset contains multiple analytical assays (e.
skills.name: pathway-set-intersection-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-set-intersection-analysis Use when a metabolomics dataset contains multiple analytical assays (e. The dataset comes from a single analytical assay, so no cross-assay chemical-bias comparison is possible. The goal is to compare pathway databases (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) rather than assay-derived pathway accessibility within one database. The objective is quantifying metabolite misidentification effects rather than assay-specific pathway coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies the chemical bias of an analytical assay on over-representation analysis by partitioning a metabolomics dataset (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS136, 667 controls and 332 estrogen users) by assay type, converting each assay's compounds to KEGG IDs via MetaboAnalyst 4.0, and intersecting the pathway sets each assay can reach among the 256 KEGG human pathways. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Quantifies the chemical bias of an analytical assay on over-representation analysis by partitioning a metabolomics dataset (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS136, 667 controls and 332 estrogen users) by assay type, converting each assay's compounds to KEGG IDs via MetaboAnalyst 4.0, and intersecting the pathway sets each assay can reach among the 256 KEGG human pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset comes from a single analytical assay, so no cross-assay chemical-bias comparison is possible. The goal is to compare pathway databases (KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc) rather than assay-derived pathway accessibility within one database. The objective is quantifying metabolite misidentification effects rather than assay-specific pathway coverage.

skills.description: Use when choosing between candidate pathway databases or pathway sets for ORA and you need to know whether differing enrichment counts stem from genuinely different biology or merely from set size/overlap differences.
skills.name: pathway-set-overlap-coefficient-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-set-overlap-coefficient-analysis Use when choosing between candidate pathway databases or pathway sets for ORA and you need to know whether differing enrichment counts stem from genuinely different biology or merely from set size/overlap differences. When comparing pathway databases that do not share compound identifiers (e.g. KEGG IDs vs BioCyc IDs) without prior identifier harmonisation — OC is undefined on non-overlapping identifier spaces. When the goal is simply to run ORA and report significant pathways; this skill is a diagnostic step before or alongside ORA, not a replacement for it. When pathway sets are already known to be identical (OC would be trivially 1) and the analysis goal lies elsewhere, such as background set selection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies how similar two metabolite pathway sets (e.g. organism-specific KEGG human vs KEGG reference) are, pathway by pathway, using the overlap coefficient on shared compound identifiers, to contextualise differences in ORA results across pathway databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Quantifies how similar two metabolite pathway sets (e.g. organism-specific KEGG human vs KEGG reference) are, pathway by pathway, using the overlap coefficient on shared compound identifiers, to contextualise differences in ORA results across pathway databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing pathway databases that do not share compound identifiers (e.g. KEGG IDs vs BioCyc IDs) without prior identifier harmonisation — OC is undefined on non-overlapping identifier spaces. When the goal is simply to run ORA and report significant pathways; this skill is a diagnostic step before or alongside ORA, not a replacement for it. When pathway sets are already known to be identical (OC would be trivially 1) and the analysis goal lies elsewhere, such as background set selection.

skills.description: Use when a pathway-prediction run (e.g., MEANtools reaction anticipation on the Jeon 2020 tomato paired-omics dataset) must be scored against published pathway steps.
skills.name: pathway-step-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: pathway-step-benchmark-comparison Use when a pathway-prediction run (e.g., MEANtools reaction anticipation on the Jeon 2020 tomato paired-omics dataset) must be scored against published pathway steps. The benchmark pathway contains multi-substrate conversions (e.g., p-coumaroyltyramine formation from tyrosine and p-coumaroyl-CoA), since RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions only The published steps hinge on stereoisomeric conversions (e.g., phenylalanine to p-coumaroyl-CoA), which are not captured by the mass spectrometric data and are filtered by MEANtools The run used the loose RetroRules dataset, where spurious reaction-Pfam links (e.g., AminoTran_1_2, Glyco_transf_20) survive the Pfam cutoff of 6 and can inflate the match count http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Benchmarks computationally anticipated biosynthetic reaction steps against a published, experimentally characterized pathway (e.g., the 7-step tomato falcarindiol pathway of Jeon and colleagues, 2020), tabulating which steps are predicted or missed. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Benchmarks computationally anticipated biosynthetic reaction steps against a published, experimentally characterized pathway (e.g., the 7-step tomato falcarindiol pathway of Jeon and colleagues, 2020), tabulating which steps are predicted or missed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmark pathway contains multi-substrate conversions (e.g., p-coumaroyltyramine formation from tyrosine and p-coumaroyl-CoA), since RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions only The published steps hinge on stereoisomeric conversions (e.g., phenylalanine to p-coumaroyl-CoA), which are not captured by the mass spectrometric data and are filtered by MEANtools The run used the loose RetroRules dataset, where spurious reaction-Pfam links (e.g., AminoTran_1_2, Glyco_transf_20) survive the Pfam cutoff of 6 and can inflate the match count

skills.description: Use when a multiomics (gene expression + metabolomics) study needs pathway-level significance that accounts for pathway topology over KEGG, beyond simple over-representation of differentially abundant features.
skills.name: pathway-topology-analysis-espia
skills.search_text: pathway-topology-analysis-espia Use when a multiomics (gene expression + metabolomics) study needs pathway-level significance that accounts for pathway topology over KEGG, beyond simple over-representation of differentially abundant features. The analysis targets only narcotics identification or concentration calibration (SMART 2.0 peak identification and calibration modules), not pathway significance. Only one omics layer is available (metabolites alone or genes alone) and no topology-informed multiomics comparison is intended — plain ORA is the appropriate choice. The pathway database of interest is not KEGG (e.g., Reactome or WikiPathways); the demonstrated eSPIA workflow is over KEGG pathways. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Extended significance analysis of pathway networks (eSPIA) within the SMART 2.0 integrative omics pathway analysis (IOPA) module, which tests KEGG pathway topology using combined gene-expression and metabolite evidence. In the SMART 2.0 breast cancer demonstration it detected two significant pathways where ORA alone detected 51. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: Extended significance analysis of pathway networks (eSPIA) within the SMART 2.0 integrative omics pathway analysis (IOPA) module, which tests KEGG pathway topology using combined gene-expression and metabolite evidence. In the SMART 2.0 breast cancer demonstration it detected two significant pathways where ORA alone detected 51.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets only narcotics identification or concentration calibration (SMART 2.0 peak identification and calibration modules), not pathway significance. Only one omics layer is available (metabolites alone or genes alone) and no topology-informed multiomics comparison is intended — plain ORA is the appropriate choice. The pathway database of interest is not KEGG (e.g., Reactome or WikiPathways); the demonstrated eSPIA workflow is over KEGG pathways.

skills.description: Use when you have a standalone list of metabolite names (e.g. 56 urine metabolites from a metabolomics-GWAS case study) and need KEGG pathway over-representation P-values, FDR, and pathway-impact scores to connect them to disease GWAS genes.
skills.name: pathway-topology-betweenness-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-topology-betweenness-analysis Use when you have a standalone list of metabolite names (e.g. 56 urine metabolites from a metabolomics-GWAS case study) and need KEGG pathway over-representation P-values, FDR, and pathway-impact scores to connect them to disease GWAS genes. You have paired metabolomics-GWAS data with individual-level SNP–metabolite associations — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for standalone, unpaired datasets where associations are limited to genes with known metabolite interactions Your metabolite names cannot be mapped to HMDB identifiers, so the metabolite-to-interacting-protein (gene) crosswalk cannot be built Your question is purely about SNPs/genomic gene sets with no metabolite input — the GWAS-network step alone suffices and the MetaboAnalyst pathway-impact step is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Maps a standalone metabolite list to HMDB identifiers and runs MetaboAnalyst-style over-representation analysis (hypergeometric test) plus betweenness-centrality-based pathway impact against KEGG pathway gene sets, as implemented inside the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Maps a standalone metabolite list to HMDB identifiers and runs MetaboAnalyst-style over-representation analysis (hypergeometric test) plus betweenness-centrality-based pathway impact against KEGG pathway gene sets, as implemented inside the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have paired metabolomics-GWAS data with individual-level SNP–metabolite associations — metGWAS 1.0 is designed for standalone, unpaired datasets where associations are limited to genes with known metabolite interactions Your metabolite names cannot be mapped to HMDB identifiers, so the metabolite-to-interacting-protein (gene) crosswalk cannot be built Your question is purely about SNPs/genomic gene sets with no metabolite input — the GWAS-network step alone suffices and the MetaboAnalyst pathway-impact step is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you have a two-condition gene expression matrix (e.g., breastcancer2012: 520 subjects × 2784 genes) and need topology-aware pathway enrichment against KEGG/Reactome interaction networks on ordinary hardware.
skills.name: pathway-topology-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-topology-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a two-condition gene expression matrix (e.g., breastcancer2012: 520 subjects × 2784 genes) and need topology-aware pathway enrichment against KEGG/Reactome interaction networks on ordinary hardware. Your analysis only needs a list of differentially expressed genes fed into a fast method — SPIA and PRS are computationally efficient but require differentially expressed genes, whereas NetGSA does not. Your input genes are not covered by any interaction database in KEGG/Reactome/PantherDB, so obtainEdgeList cannot curate edges. You need a method with specific simple input requirements rather than network estimation (e.g., topologyGSA or Pathway-Express inputs). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Topology-based, third-generation pathway enrichment using the overhauled netgsa R package: curate gene-gene interactions from KEGG/Reactome, build clustered pathway adjacency matrices, and run NetGSA with REHE variance-component estimation and sampling so thousands of genes can be tested in minutes on a personal computer without sacrificing statistical power. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Topology-based, third-generation pathway enrichment using the overhauled netgsa R package: curate gene-gene interactions from KEGG/Reactome, build clustered pathway adjacency matrices, and run NetGSA with REHE variance-component estimation and sampling so thousands of genes can be tested in minutes on a personal computer without sacrificing statistical power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analysis only needs a list of differentially expressed genes fed into a fast method — SPIA and PRS are computationally efficient but require differentially expressed genes, whereas NetGSA does not. Your input genes are not covered by any interaction database in KEGG/Reactome/PantherDB, so obtainEdgeList cannot curate edges. You need a method with specific simple input requirements rather than network estimation (e.g., topologyGSA or Pathway-Express inputs).

skills.description: Use when you have node-level waveforms from network auralization of a metabolite correlation network and need one representative signal per metabolic pathway (hyperlink) before training the M5 classifier.
skills.name: pathway-waveform-aggregation-from-metabolite-signals
skills.search_text: pathway-waveform-aggregation-from-metabolite-signals Use when you have node-level waveforms from network auralization of a metabolite correlation network and need one representative signal per metabolic pathway (hyperlink) before training the M5 classifier. Input is already aggregated pathway-level signals — re-averaging would double-aggregate and corrupt the representation You only need node-level centrality scores rather than hyperlink (pathway) predictions — use the centrality-learning auralization tooling instead The graph is not a metabolite correlation network with pathways defined over metabolite participants (e.g., generic social-network hyperlink data lacks the pathway-participant structure) Aggregates per-metabolite waveforms produced by Network Auralization of a Metabolite CN into per-pathway (hyperlink) signals by averaging participant waveforms by index, producing the fixed-length 1-channel inputs that the M5 classifier consumes for pathway presence/absence prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Aggregates per-metabolite waveforms produced by Network Auralization of a Metabolite CN into per-pathway (hyperlink) signals by averaging participant waveforms by index, producing the fixed-length 1-channel inputs that the M5 classifier consumes for pathway presence/absence prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aggregated pathway-level signals — re-averaging would double-aggregate and corrupt the representation You only need node-level centrality scores rather than hyperlink (pathway) predictions — use the centrality-learning auralization tooling instead The graph is not a metabolite correlation network with pathways defined over metabolite participants (e.g., generic social-network hyperlink data lacks the pathway-participant structure)

skills.description: Use when you have a full (unprefiltered) KO, gene, or compound abundance table plus sample metadata and need threshold-free pathway enrichment with permutation-calibrated reporter scores.
skills.name: pathway-zscore-aggregation
skills.search_text: pathway-zscore-aggregation Use when you have a full (unprefiltered) KO, gene, or compound abundance table plus sample metadata and need threshold-free pathway enrichment with permutation-calibrated reporter scores. Input has been prefiltered to a list of 'significant' features, discarding background information — GRSA is threshold-free and requires the full background table Features cannot be mapped to any pathway database and no custom_modulelist can be constructed (e.g. unmapped compound IDs not standardized to KEGG C numbers) The goal is to enumerate only a small pre-defined significant list via hypergeometric overlap rather than aggregate Z-scores over all pathway members http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes pathway-level reporter scores by converting per-feature differential P-values into (signed or unsigned) Z-scores, aggregating them over KEGG pathway/module members, and standardizing against a permutation-derived null distribution, as implemented in the GRSA method of the R package ReporterScore. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Computes pathway-level reporter scores by converting per-feature differential P-values into (signed or unsigned) Z-scores, aggregating them over KEGG pathway/module members, and standardizing against a permutation-derived null distribution, as implemented in the GRSA method of the R package ReporterScore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has been prefiltered to a list of 'significant' features, discarding background information — GRSA is threshold-free and requires the full background table Features cannot be mapped to any pathway database and no custom_modulelist can be constructed (e.g. unmapped compound IDs not standardized to KEGG C numbers) The goal is to enumerate only a small pre-defined significant list via hypergeometric overlap rather than aggregate Z-scores over all pathway members

skills.description: Use when clinical metabolomics data (e.g., GC-TOF MS lipid profiles) contain patient metadata and subject-specific biological variation should be readjusted before multivariate analyses like PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, or PCA.
skills.name: patient-metadata-driven-metabolite-modeling
skills.search_text: patient-metadata-driven-metabolite-modeling Use when clinical metabolomics data (e.g., GC-TOF MS lipid profiles) contain patient metadata and subject-specific biological variation should be readjusted before multivariate analyses like PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, or PCA. Data are raw MS signals that still require pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) or have not yet been normalized, scaled, centered and log2-transformed No patient/subject metadata (tissue type, age, BMI, sex, tumor location and stage) is available to enter as fixed effects, so the LMM cannot be formulated The goal is raw-signal quality control rather than an additional data-processing step to readjust individual metabolite signals prior to multivariate analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits each log2-transformed metabolite signal to a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) in which patient metadata (Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) are fixed effects and patient ID is a random intercept, using the lmm2met R package built on lme4. The fitted model readjusts metabolite abundances to reduce subject-specific variation prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: Fits each log2-transformed metabolite signal to a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) in which patient metadata (Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) are fixed effects and patient ID is a random intercept, using the lmm2met R package built on lme4. The fitted model readjusts metabolite abundances to reduce subject-specific variation prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw MS signals that still require pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) or have not yet been normalized, scaled, centered and log2-transformed No patient/subject metadata (tissue type, age, BMI, sex, tumor location and stage) is available to enter as fixed effects, so the LMM cannot be formulated The goal is raw-signal quality control rather than an additional data-processing step to readjust individual metabolite signals prior to multivariate analyses

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature matrix has paired or repeated measurements per patient plus subject metadata, and residual inter-individual variation masks biological group separation (e.g. SAT vs VAT) prior to PCA or PLS-DA.
skills.name: patient-metadata-fixed-effects-modeling
skills.search_text: patient-metadata-fixed-effects-modeling Use when a metabolomics feature matrix has paired or repeated measurements per patient plus subject metadata, and residual inter-individual variation masks biological group separation (e.g. SAT vs VAT) prior to PCA or PLS-DA. The data lack patient metadata or repeated/paired measurements per subject, so no random intercept '(1|Id)' can be defined A downstream classifier evaluation pipeline requires untouched raw intensities rather than model-readjusted signals The matrix is already processed by an equivalent normalization that accounts for subject-specific covariates http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to each metabolite in a clinical metabolomics matrix, using patient metadata (Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) as fixed effects and a per-patient random intercept, via the lmm2met R package. This readjusts individual metabolite signals to reduce subject-specific variation before multivariate analyses such as PCA or PLS-DA. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: Fit a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to each metabolite in a clinical metabolomics matrix, using patient metadata (Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue) as fixed effects and a per-patient random intercept, via the lmm2met R package. This readjusts individual metabolite signals to reduce subject-specific variation before multivariate analyses such as PCA or PLS-DA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack patient metadata or repeated/paired measurements per subject, so no random intercept '(1|Id)' can be defined A downstream classifier evaluation pipeline requires untouched raw intensities rather than model-readjusted signals The matrix is already processed by an equivalent normalization that accounts for subject-specific covariates

skills.description: Use when patRoon featureGroups and MFsummary outputs must be brought into GetFeatistics as featTable/featINFO data frames for pooled-QC filtering, annotation grading, regression modelling, or plotting.
skills.name: patroon-feature-table-import
skills.search_text: patroon-feature-table-import Use when patRoon featureGroups and MFsummary outputs must be brought into GetFeatistics as featTable/featINFO data frames for pooled-QC filtering, annotation grading, regression modelling, or plotting. The input is an MS-DIAL area export rather than patRoon output — use get_feat_table_from_MSDial / get_feat_info_from_MSDial, which apply dot-product and fragment-presence cut-offs instead of MoNAScore Raw MS data still needs feature extraction — patRoon (or XCMS) must first process the raw data files before tables exist to import A targeted study requiring calibration curve-based quantification with weighted regressions is the goal rather than untargeted feature-table elaboration http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Import patRoon feature-group results (featureGroups and MFsummary objects) into the GetFeatistics R environment using get_feat_table_from_patRoon and get_feat_info_from_patRoon, structuring intensities and metadata into the featTable and featINFO data frames that all downstream GetFeatistics processing expects. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Import patRoon feature-group results (featureGroups and MFsummary objects) into the GetFeatistics R environment using get_feat_table_from_patRoon and get_feat_info_from_patRoon, structuring intensities and metadata into the featTable and featINFO data frames that all downstream GetFeatistics processing expects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an MS-DIAL area export rather than patRoon output — use get_feat_table_from_MSDial / get_feat_info_from_MSDial, which apply dot-product and fragment-presence cut-offs instead of MoNAScore Raw MS data still needs feature extraction — patRoon (or XCMS) must first process the raw data files before tables exist to import A targeted study requiring calibration curve-based quantification with weighted regressions is the goal rather than untargeted feature-table elaboration

skills.description: Use when starting an untargeted metabolomics analysis whose features were extracted and annotated with patRoon, and the data must be converted into GetFeatistics' featTable/featINFO structures before pooled-QC filtration or regression modelling.
skills.name: patroon-featuregroups-import
skills.search_text: patroon-featuregroups-import Use when starting an untargeted metabolomics analysis whose features were extracted and annotated with patRoon, and the data must be converted into GetFeatistics' featTable/featINFO structures before pooled-QC filtration or regression modelling. skills.search_text: pca-based-drift-diagnostics Use when a feature matrix contains ordered pooled/intrastudy QC injections and you need to quantify or visually assess signal drift, or to verify that LOESS batch correction reduced time-related systematic variance. The dataset contains no pooled/intrastudy QC injections ordered by acquisition time — drift cannot be separated from sample composition effects. When the comparison depends on retention-time behavior — MEMO is explicitly a retention time (RT) agnostic alignment, so PCoA on MEMO distances will not resolve RT differences When samples have strong feature overlap and a conventional RT-aligned feature table analysis is appropriate rather than MS2-fingerprint vectorization When the input is raw chromatographic (MS1) data without MS2 fragmentation spectra, since the fingerprints require MS2 peaks and neutral losses http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Ordinate metabolomics samples in PCoA space from an aligned MS2-fingerprint (MEMO) distance matrix and quantify group separation (e.g., MS platform vs sample composition) with scikit-bio PERMANOVA pseudo-F statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Ordinate metabolomics samples in PCoA space from an aligned MS2-fingerprint (MEMO) distance matrix and quantify group separation (e.g., MS platform vs sample composition) with scikit-bio PERMANOVA pseudo-F statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison depends on retention-time behavior — MEMO is explicitly a retention time (RT) agnostic alignment, so PCoA on MEMO distances will not resolve RT differences When samples have strong feature overlap and a conventional RT-aligned feature table analysis is appropriate rather than MS2-fingerprint vectorization When the input is raw chromatographic (MS1) data without MS2 fragmentation spectra, since the fingerprints require MS2 peaks and neutral losses

skills.description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates (PCoA) file and a metadata mapping file and need an interactive, shareable 3D ordination of thousands of microbial community samples, optionally overlaid with biplot or procrustes layers.
skills.name: pcoa-ordination-plot-generation
skills.search_text: pcoa-ordination-plot-generation Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates (PCoA) file and a metadata mapping file and need an interactive, shareable 3D ordination of thousands of microbial community samples, optionally overlaid with biplot or procrustes layers. The input is raw high-throughput sequencing data or a beta diversity distance matrix that has not yet been ordinated — perform PCoA dimensionality reduction first, then plot. The goal is a generic 3D plot unrelated to microbial community metadata-driven coloring/controls (e.g. a plain scatter from a generic package like MATLAB, R, or Matplotlib may suffice instead). You require a commercial interactive analytics environment or need a command line interface on Windows — the EMPeror CLI is stated to run on OS X (10.6 and higher) and Linux only. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates interactive 3D principal coordinates visualizations of microbial community samples from a QIIME PCoA file plus metadata mapping file, with optional auxiliary layers (taxon biplots, procrustes comparisons, jackknifed beta diversity) rendered as a standalone WebGL web page via EMPeror. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/2047-217x-2-16
skills.summary: Generates interactive 3D principal coordinates visualizations of microbial community samples from a QIIME PCoA file plus metadata mapping file, with optional auxiliary layers (taxon biplots, procrustes comparisons, jackknifed beta diversity) rendered as a standalone WebGL web page via EMPeror.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw high-throughput sequencing data or a beta diversity distance matrix that has not yet been ordinated — perform PCoA dimensionality reduction first, then plot. The goal is a generic 3D plot unrelated to microbial community metadata-driven coloring/controls (e.g. a plain scatter from a generic package like MATLAB, R, or Matplotlib may suffice instead). You require a commercial interactive analytics environment or need a command line interface on Windows — the EMPeror CLI is stated to run on OS X (10.6 and higher) and Linux only.

skills.description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file and a metadata mapping file (e.g. thousands of samples, many metadata columns) and need an exploratory 3D ordination visualization colored by sample metadata.
skills.name: pcoa-ordination-visualization
skills.search_text: pcoa-ordination-visualization Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file and a metadata mapping file (e.g. thousands of samples, many metadata columns) and need an exploratory 3D ordination visualization colored by sample metadata. You need upstream analysis (e.g. generating the beta diversity distance matrix or the PCoA coordinates themselves) — QIIME handles the upstream analysis and EMPeror only visualizes the resulting coordinates. The dataset is small and a generic 3D plotting package (R, MATLAB, Matplotlib, SpotFire, KiNG) already meets your needs without metadata-integrated recoloring of thousands of points. You require a Windows-supported CLI or a browser other than Chrome — the EMPeror command line interface is stated as OS X (10.6+) and Linux only, and the GUI requires Chrome. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Visualize high-throughput microbial community beta diversity as an interactive 3D PCoA plot with EMPeror, recoloring points dynamically as a function of metadata gradients (e.g. age) or discrete categories so that patterns such as infant-versus-adult separation become directly viewable. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/2047-217x-2-16
skills.summary: Visualize high-throughput microbial community beta diversity as an interactive 3D PCoA plot with EMPeror, recoloring points dynamically as a function of metadata gradients (e.g. age) or discrete categories so that patterns such as infant-versus-adult separation become directly viewable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need upstream analysis (e.g. generating the beta diversity distance matrix or the PCoA coordinates themselves) — QIIME handles the upstream analysis and EMPeror only visualizes the resulting coordinates. The dataset is small and a generic 3D plotting package (R, MATLAB, Matplotlib, SpotFire, KiNG) already meets your needs without metadata-integrated recoloring of thousands of points. skills.search_text: pcoa-plot-reproduction-from-deposited-files Use when you have a deposited QIIME principal coordinates file and mapping file (e.g. the 5,740-sample, 120-column combined dataset) and need to rebuild a PCoA 3D plot or benchmark visualization loading performance. skills.summary: Reproduce published PCoA visualizations by regenerating EMPeror plots from the deposited QIIME principal coordinates and metadata mapping files, comparing load-time and file-size performance against the legacy KiNG QIIME export path.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You do not have the original deposited principal coordinates file or mapping file — the skill regenerates plots from these exact artifacts, not from raw sequence data. You need statistical analysis of the ordination itself rather than plot reproduction or loading benchmarking. skills.description: Use when two reproducibility methods disagree on top-k gene sets for SEQC RNA-seq replicate comparisons and an independent qPCR/Taqman gold standard is available to judge which method's sets are more biologically relevant.
skills.name: pcr-gold-standard-external-validation
skills.search_text: pcr-gold-standard-external-validation Use when two reproducibility methods disagree on top-k gene sets for SEQC RNA-seq replicate comparisons and an independent qPCR/Taqman gold standard is available to judge which method's sets are more biologically relevant. No independent gold-standard measurements (e.g., Taqman PCR) exist for the ranked transcripts, so external validation cannot arbitrate between methods and only cross-method agreement could be assessed The transcript sets being compared are already known to be identical (no method disagreement to adjudicate), making the method-specific rank comparison moot The data are not SEQC-style replicate rank lists with a matched-k top-k set per method, so the k values and alpha = 0.01 thresholds from this workflow do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Externally validates a reproducibility method (e.g., MaRR vs. the copula mixture model) by intersecting each method's declared top-k reproducible transcript sets with an independent Taqman qPCR gold standard from the SEQC project, then comparing PCR-measurement ranks of method-specific genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1080/01621459.2017.1397521
skills.summary: Externally validates a reproducibility method (e.g., MaRR vs. the copula mixture model) by intersecting each method's declared top-k reproducible transcript sets with an independent Taqman qPCR gold standard from the SEQC project, then comparing PCR-measurement ranks of method-specific genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent gold-standard measurements (e.g., Taqman PCR) exist for the ranked transcripts, so external validation cannot arbitrate between methods and only cross-method agreement could be assessed The transcript sets being compared are already known to be identical (no method disagreement to adjudicate), making the method-specific rank comparison moot The data are not SEQC-style replicate rank lists with a matched-k top-k set per method, so the k values and alpha = 0.01 thresholds from this workflow do not apply
