skills.name: peak-abundance-table-preparation
skills.search_text: peak-abundance-table-preparation Use when direct-injection FT-ICR MS data have already been formula-assigned but still need peak filtering and a normalization-method choice before running the MetaboDirect pipeline on datasets like the bacterium-phage (36 samples) or S. fallax (4 samples) examples. skills.search_text: peak-area-correlation-analysis Use when a matched feature table with peak areas from PeakBot and XCMS (e.g. from a PHM tool comparison) must be compared: regression R2, trimming of dissimilar features, and derivation of the profile-to-centroid median area factor. Input is raw LC-HRMS profile-mode data that has not yet been peak-picked and grouped into a feature table — peak detection with PeakBot must run first The two peak-area sets are not matched feature-by-feature (e.g. unaligned peak lists), since correlation requires per-feature pairing The goal is training or applying a PeakBot CNN model rather than post-hoc comparison of two peak-area tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies agreement between peak areas from two peak-picking approaches (PeakBot profile-mode vs XCMS centroid-mode) on matched LC-HRMS features via linear regression, symmetric 5%/5% outlier trimming, and a profile-versus-centroid area-factor statistic. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between peak areas from two peak-picking approaches (PeakBot profile-mode vs XCMS centroid-mode) on matched LC-HRMS features via linear regression, symmetric 5%/5% outlier trimming, and a profile-versus-centroid area-factor statistic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-HRMS profile-mode data that has not yet been peak-picked and grouped into a feature table — peak detection with PeakBot must run first The two peak-area sets are not matched feature-by-feature (e.g. unaligned peak lists), since correlation requires per-feature pairing The goal is training or applying a PeakBot CNN model rather than post-hoc comparison of two peak-area tables

skills.description: Use when GC × GC–MS deconvoluted features must be quantified across all samples — the annotated peaks from GcDUO's module III need area/intensity values, not just detection and annotation.
skills.name: peak-area-integration
skills.search_text: peak-area-integration Use when GC × GC–MS deconvoluted features must be quantified across all samples — the annotated peaks from GcDUO's module III need area/intensity values, not just detection and annotation. Input data has not yet been peak-picked and annotated (module I–III incomplete) — running module V on raw GcDuoObject alone is invalid. Only a single-sample chromatogram must be quantified — GcDUO's batch-constrained PARAFAC2 re-evaluation is designed for features detected across multiple samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0078 Computes per-feature peak areas and maximum intensities for each sample in a batch GC × GC–MS run by re-fitting PARAFAC2 models constrained by library spectra, and assembles them into summary tables (CSV). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbaf080
skills.summary: Computes per-feature peak areas and maximum intensities for each sample in a batch GC × GC–MS run by re-fitting PARAFAC2 models constrained by library spectra, and assembles them into summary tables (CSV).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not yet been peak-picked and annotated (module I–III incomplete) — running module V on raw GcDuoObject alone is invalid. Only a single-sample chromatogram must be quantified — GcDUO's batch-constrained PARAFAC2 re-evaluation is designed for features detected across multiple samples.

skills.description: Use when processing AEMS MRM raw data (XIC points per mass transition and ejection/well) to produce a baseline-corrected area table, e.g. mrm_areas.csv, for shot-to-peak quantification.
skills.name: peak-area-integration
skills.search_text: peak-area-integration Use when processing AEMS MRM raw data (XIC points per mass transition and ejection/well) to produce a baseline-corrected area table, e.g. mrm_areas.csv, for shot-to-peak quantification. Input is already a peak-area table (mrm_areas.csv) rather than raw AEMS XIC data — the areas have already been computed. Data are conventional LC-MS chromatograms with retained chromatographic separation rather than AEMS ejection windows. The acquisition is full-scan AEMS (precursor ion or neutral loss mode) rather than targeted MRM transitions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes per-ejection, per-transition MRM peak areas from acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) raw data by baseline-correcting extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) within each detection window and summing intensity, reproducing rtmsEcho's automated area-quantification behavior. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03730
skills.summary: Computes per-ejection, per-transition MRM peak areas from acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) raw data by baseline-correcting extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) within each detection window and summing intensity, reproducing rtmsEcho's automated area-quantification behavior.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-area table (mrm_areas.csv) rather than raw AEMS XIC data — the areas have already been computed. Data are conventional LC-MS chromatograms with retained chromatographic separation rather than AEMS ejection windows. The acquisition is full-scan AEMS (precursor ion or neutral loss mode) rather than targeted MRM transitions.

skills.description: Use when you have a referenced 2D 13C INADEQUATE spectrum and need to detect peaks and quantify their areas with a multi-threshold sweep, before network filtering and metabolite matching.
skills.name: peak-area-quantification
skills.search_text: peak-area-quantification Use when you have a referenced 2D 13C INADEQUATE spectrum and need to detect peaks and quantify their areas with a multi-threshold sweep, before network filtering and metabolite matching. Input is already a picked peak list — this skill covers threshold-sweep picking; use PyINETA's cluster/find/match steps instead for network filtering and database matching. Query spectra are not 2D INADEQUATE with a direct and double-quantum dimension — the PPCS/PPDQ center-of-mass merging assumes that dimensional structure. Raw input files exceed 100 Mb (as in the README's example2), which the repository does not ship — you must contact the Edison lab for those raw files rather than expecting local example data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Slice-wise peak picking for 2D INADEQUATE NMR spectra in PyINETA: sweeps an intensity threshold from PPmax down to PPmin to define peaks and their areas, then merges nearby picks via center-of-mass tolerances (PPCS, PPDQ) into a picked_peaks.csv for downstream network filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c03966
skills.summary: Slice-wise peak picking for 2D INADEQUATE NMR spectra in PyINETA: sweeps an intensity threshold from PPmax down to PPmin to define peaks and their areas, then merges nearby picks via center-of-mass tolerances (PPCS, PPDQ) into a picked_peaks.csv for downstream network filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a picked peak list — this skill covers threshold-sweep picking; use PyINETA's cluster/find/match steps instead for network filtering and database matching. Query spectra are not 2D INADEQUATE with a direct and double-quantum dimension — the PPCS/PPDQ center-of-mass merging assumes that dimensional structure. Raw input files exceed 100 Mb (as in the README's example2), which the repository does not ship — you must contact the Edison lab for those raw files rather than expecting local example data.

skills.description: Use when the input is a lipidomic peak-area/peak-height matrix whose rows include internal standard species and a companion standards table (Standard/Class/Conc.) exists, and the goal is a per-species concentration matrix.
skills.name: peak-area-to-concentration-conversion
skills.search_text: peak-area-to-concentration-conversion Use when the input is a lipidomic peak-area/peak-height matrix whose rows include internal standard species and a companion standards table (Standard/Class/Conc.) exists, and the goal is a per-species concentration matrix. Input data are already concentration values rather than raw peak areas/heights — re-applying conversion factors would double-normalize The dataset lacks internal standard rows or a standards table (no Standard/Class/Conc. mapping), so class-specific conversion factors cannot be constructed The goal is downstream statistical analysis (mono-/multivariate tests, biomarker identification) on already-quantified data — use LipidOne 2.0's data-mining functions instead of the quantification utility http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts MS-derived peak area (or peak height) values into concentration values for lipid molecular species using class-specific internal standards (e.g., SPLASH Lipidomix species) with known concentrations, as implemented in the Lipid Data Quantification utility of LipidOne 2.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Converts MS-derived peak area (or peak height) values into concentration values for lipid molecular species using class-specific internal standards (e.g., SPLASH Lipidomix species) with known concentrations, as implemented in the Lipid Data Quantification utility of LipidOne 2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already concentration values rather than raw peak areas/heights — re-applying conversion factors would double-normalize The dataset lacks internal standard rows or a standards table (no Standard/Class/Conc. mapping), so class-specific conversion factors cannot be constructed The goal is downstream statistical analysis (mono-/multivariate tests, biomarker identification) on already-quantified data — use LipidOne 2.0's data-mining functions instead of the quantification utility

skills.description: Use when you have raw mzML files plus a detected peak list (mz, rt columns, e.g. from XCMS) and need to separate genuine metabolite peaks from artifacts without large manually annotated training sets.
skills.name: peak-artifact-classification
skills.search_text: peak-artifact-classification Use when you have raw mzML files plus a detected peak list (mz, rt columns, e.g. from XCMS) and need to separate genuine metabolite peaks from artifacts without large manually annotated training sets. Input is already a curated, manually annotated feature table where peak labels are known — supervised training or direct filtering is more appropriate than active learning. Data lacks raw mzML scans (only processed peak intensities are available), since EIC extraction from raw data is required to build the n x 60 input matrix. Only a very small peak list is available (far below the min_peaks=100000 used to train the smoother autoencoder), which undermines unsupervised latent-space learning. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Classifies LC/MS peaks from an XCMS-style peak list as artifacts or true peaks using a semisupervised deep-learning pipeline: an autoencoding CNN compresses n x 60 EIC matrices into an n x 5 latent space, and an active-learning classifier scores peaks using fewer than 100 user-labeled peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00764
skills.summary: Classifies LC/MS peaks from an XCMS-style peak list as artifacts or true peaks using a semisupervised deep-learning pipeline: an autoencoding CNN compresses n x 60 EIC matrices into an n x 5 latent space, and an active-learning classifier scores peaks using fewer than 100 user-labeled peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated, manually annotated feature table where peak labels are known — supervised training or direct filtering is more appropriate than active learning. Data lacks raw mzML scans (only processed peak intensities are available), since EIC extraction from raw data is required to build the n x 60 input matrix. Only a very small peak list is available (far below the min_peaks=100000 used to train the smoother autoencoder), which undermines unsupervised latent-space learning.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw untargeted metabolomics data (.mzML, .mzXML, or .CDF from qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR instruments) and needing dataset-specific centWave peak-picking and XCMS grouping parameters before feature-table generation.
skills.name: peak-based-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: peak-based-parameter-estimation Use when starting from raw untargeted metabolomics data (.mzML, .mzXML, or .CDF from qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR instruments) and needing dataset-specific centWave peak-picking and XCMS grouping parameters before feature-table generation. Input is already a processed feature table — parameters must be estimated from raw data prior to peak picking, not retrofitted You need retention-time correction parameter estimation — the divide-and-conquer approach does not compare EIC peaks across samples for that purpose Full automation is required with no user interaction — the sliding window analysis in the first portion of AutoTuner requires user input, and the Group difference estimate is non-automatable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimate dataset-specific peak-picking parameters for untargeted metabolomics directly from raw data by detecting TIC peaks and statistically aggregating per-peak estimates into the eight centWave/grouping parameters used by XCMS and MZmine2, replacing slow iterative parameter sweeping. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/812370
skills.summary: Estimate dataset-specific peak-picking parameters for untargeted metabolomics directly from raw data by detecting TIC peaks and statistically aggregating per-peak estimates into the eight centWave/grouping parameters used by XCMS and MZmine2, replacing slow iterative parameter sweeping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table — parameters must be estimated from raw data prior to peak picking, not retrofitted You need retention-time correction parameter estimation — the divide-and-conquer approach does not compare EIC peaks across samples for that purpose Full automation is required with no user interaction — the sliding window analysis in the first portion of AutoTuner requires user input, and the Group difference estimate is non-automatable

skills.description: Use when comparing feature tables from LC-MS processing tools and you must judge whether extra reported features are genuine or low-quality, by recomputing a shape-fitness score on the EIC around each reported peak boundary.
skills.name: peak-boundary-eic-extraction
skills.search_text: peak-boundary-eic-extraction Use when comparing feature tables from LC-MS processing tools and you must judge whether extra reported features are genuine or low-quality, by recomputing a shape-fitness score on the EIC around each reported peak boundary. The goal is de novo peak detection rather than scoring the quality of already-reported peak boundaries Data are low-resolution or from very high-noise acquisitions — the asari framework does not work with low-resolution data and high-noise data may need customized processing You need MS/MS handling — the default LC-MS workflow in asari ignores MS/MS spectra, so shape scoring applies only to MS1 features http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts EIC intensity lists over reported LC-MS peak boundaries (padded by 3 s on each side) and fits a Gaussian to compute a peak-shape fitness score, used to separate good-quality from bad-quality features across processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Extracts EIC intensity lists over reported LC-MS peak boundaries (padded by 3 s on each side) and fits a Gaussian to compute a peak-shape fitness score, used to separate good-quality from bad-quality features across processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo peak detection rather than scoring the quality of already-reported peak boundaries Data are low-resolution or from very high-noise acquisitions — the asari framework does not work with low-resolution data and high-noise data may need customized processing You need MS/MS handling — the default LC-MS workflow in asari ignores MS/MS spectra, so shape scoring applies only to MS1 features

skills.description: Use when an acquisition controller's simulated or real MS2 scan schedule (mzML with MS1/MS2 events) must be scored by how many chromatographic peaks it actually fragmented, rather than counting MS2 scans.
skills.name: peak-bounding-box-coverage-evaluation
skills.search_text: peak-bounding-box-coverage-evaluation Use when an acquisition controller's simulated or real MS2 scan schedule (mzML with MS1/MS2 events) must be scored by how many chromatographic peaks it actually fragmented, rather than counting MS2 scans. Input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw MS1/MS2 scan data — peak picking with MZmine 2 bounding boxes cannot be re-done The goal is comparing MS2-level identifications (spectral matches, SIRIUS4/CFM-ID scores) rather than fragmentation coverage of MS1-detected peaks The schedule is DIA-based, where the notion of targeting specific MS1 ions with MS2 events does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluates an MS2 acquisition schedule by picking peaks as MZmine 2 bounding boxes on full-scan data and computing coverage — the fraction of picked peaks whose RT/mz region contains at least one fragmentation event — against a TopN baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Evaluates an MS2 acquisition schedule by picking peaks as MZmine 2 bounding boxes on full-scan data and computing coverage — the fraction of picked peaks whose RT/mz region contains at least one fragmentation event — against a TopN baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw MS1/MS2 scan data — peak picking with MZmine 2 bounding boxes cannot be re-done The goal is comparing MS2-level identifications (spectral matches, SIRIUS4/CFM-ID scores) rather than fragmentation coverage of MS1-detected peaks The schedule is DIA-based, where the notion of targeting specific MS1 ions with MS2 events does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have an mzML run containing MS2 fragmentation events plus an exported MZmine2 picked-peak bounding-box list for a corresponding full-scan run, and need per-peak coverage flags to score a fragmentation controller.
skills.name: peak-bounding-box-matching
skills.search_text: peak-bounding-box-matching Use when you have an mzML run containing MS2 fragmentation events plus an exported MZmine2 picked-peak bounding-box list for a corresponding full-scan run, and need per-peak coverage flags to score a fragmentation controller. Input is a raw centroided MS1-only run with no MS2 fragmentation events and no MZmine2 bounding boxes — there is nothing to match against. You already hold a computed feature-abundance/coverage table; re-matching boxes would double-count peaks rather than add information. Comparing controllers by MS1/MS2 scan counts or per-cycle timings only — coverage matching is unnecessary for timing-based benchmarks like the SmartROI 0.68 s vs full-scan 0.54 s comparison. Assigns MS2 fragmentation events extracted from mzML files to MZmine2-picked peak bounding boxes (RT and m/z min/max) to compute the fragmentation coverage of a DDA controller — the proportion of picked peaks that contain at least one fragmentation event. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Assigns MS2 fragmentation events extracted from mzML files to MZmine2-picked peak bounding boxes (RT and m/z min/max) to compute the fragmentation coverage of a DDA controller — the proportion of picked peaks that contain at least one fragmentation event.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw centroided MS1-only run with no MS2 fragmentation events and no MZmine2 bounding boxes — there is nothing to match against. You already hold a computed feature-abundance/coverage table; re-matching boxes would double-count peaks rather than add information. Comparing controllers by MS1/MS2 scan counts or per-cycle timings only — coverage matching is unnecessary for timing-based benchmarks like the SmartROI 0.68 s vs full-scan 0.54 s comparison.

skills.description: Use when annotating ion forms and relationships among untargeted LC-MS metabolic features (e.g., NIST urine positive-mode peak tables) where conventional isotope/adduct rule grouping (CAMERA) misses in-source fragments and neutral losses.
skills.name: peak-correlation-network-analysis
skills.search_text: peak-correlation-network-analysis Use when annotating ion forms and relationships among untargeted LC-MS metabolic features (e.g., NIST urine positive-mode peak tables) where conventional isotope/adduct rule grouping (CAMERA) misses in-source fragments and neutral losses. Applying to non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles — the article advises caution because organism-specific databases are not yet incorporated The goal is distinguishing structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively discriminate The input is raw chromatographic data rather than a peak table with MS2 spectra; the workflow expects pre-extracted metabolic features http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Builds the KGMN global peak correlation network (layer 3 of the knowledge-guided multilayer network) with MetDNA2Vis to assign ion forms — including in-source fragmentation ions and neutral losses — to LC-MS metabolic features, benchmarked against CAMERA-style isotope/adduct annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Builds the KGMN global peak correlation network (layer 3 of the knowledge-guided multilayer network) with MetDNA2Vis to assign ion forms — including in-source fragmentation ions and neutral losses — to LC-MS metabolic features, benchmarked against CAMERA-style isotope/adduct annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Applying to non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles — the article advises caution because organism-specific databases are not yet incorporated The goal is distinguishing structurally similar isomers of unknown metabolites (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot effectively discriminate The input is raw chromatographic data rather than a peak table with MS2 spectra; the workflow expects pre-extracted metabolic features

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a Sample Filtering percentage in Galaxy-M: re-run the DIMS (100% threshold) and LC-MS (80% threshold) pipelines over MTBLS79 and MTBLS146 data, and record per-step peak removals before deciding whether Missing Values Imputation (e.g. KNN) is required.
skills.name: peak-count-accounting-across-filter-steps
skills.search_text: peak-count-accounting-across-filter-steps Decision support for choosing a Sample Filtering percentage in Galaxy-M: re-run the DIMS (100% threshold) and LC-MS (80% threshold) pipelines over MTBLS79 and MTBLS146 data, and record per-step peak removals before deciding whether Missing Values Imputation (e.g. KNN) is required. The pipeline's Sample Filtering threshold is already fixed and the downstream imputation decision has been made — there is nothing to re-run or compare. Peak counts are needed from XCMS feature detection or SIM-stitching itself rather than from the Replicate/Blank/Sample Filtering stages. Data contains no blank or replicate metadata (class labels for biological vs blank samples), so the DSO-based filter chain cannot be evaluated meaningfully. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Tracks how many peaks enter and leave each Galaxy-M filtering stage (Replicate Filtering, Blank Filtering, Sample Filtering) for the DIMS and LC-MS case studies, so that the imputation requirement at the end of the pipeline can be attributed to a specific Sample Filtering threshold (100% vs 80%). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: Tracks how many peaks enter and leave each Galaxy-M filtering stage (Replicate Filtering, Blank Filtering, Sample Filtering) for the DIMS and LC-MS case studies, so that the imputation requirement at the end of the pipeline can be attributed to a specific Sample Filtering threshold (100% vs 80%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline's Sample Filtering threshold is already fixed and the downstream imputation decision has been made — there is nothing to re-run or compare. Peak counts are needed from XCMS feature detection or SIM-stitching itself rather than from the Replicate/Blank/Sample Filtering stages. Data contains no blank or replicate metadata (class labels for biological vs blank samples), so the DSO-based filter chain cannot be evaluated meaningfully.

skills.description: Use when GC-MS peak picking has been run with multiple embedded algorithms (e.g. centWave and matchedFilter) via WiPP and you need to quantify whether the integrated result set yields larger high-quality peak coverage than either algorithm alone.
skills.name: peak-count-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: peak-count-comparison-analysis Use when GC-MS peak picking has been run with multiple embedded algorithms (e.g. centWave and matchedFilter) via WiPP and you need to quantify whether the integrated result set yields larger high-quality peak coverage than either algorithm alone. Only a single peak-picking algorithm was enabled in the WiPP config.yaml (e.g. the example project defaults to one algorithm), so there is no second algorithm's output to compare against. Input is a raw GC-MS data file (mzML, mzData, NetCDF) that has not yet been through WiPP's peak picking, classification, and result-integration stages. The goal is parameter optimisation or classifier training rather than evaluating high-quality peak coverage of the integrated result set. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compares the number of high-quality peaks (as assigned by WiPP's seven-class SVM peak quality classifier) produced by the merged/integrated result set versus each individual peak-picking algorithm (e.g. centWave and matchedFilter), to quantify the coverage gain from result integration across algorithms. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9090171
skills.summary: Compares the number of high-quality peaks (as assigned by WiPP's seven-class SVM peak quality classifier) produced by the merged/integrated result set versus each individual peak-picking algorithm (e.g. centWave and matchedFilter), to quantify the coverage gain from result integration across algorithms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single peak-picking algorithm was enabled in the WiPP config.yaml (e.g. the example project defaults to one algorithm), so there is no second algorithm's output to compare against. Input is a raw GC-MS data file (mzML, mzData, NetCDF) that has not yet been through WiPP's peak picking, classification, and result-integration stages. The goal is parameter optimisation or classifier training rather than evaluating high-quality peak coverage of the integrated result set.

skills.description: Use when re-running or validating DIMPLE preprocessing under altered parameters (e.g., ppm mass tolerance or background-enrichment threshold) and you need average peak counts per root plus percent-change metrics versus defaults.
skills.name: peak-count-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: peak-count-metrics-computation Use when re-running or validating DIMPLE preprocessing under altered parameters (e.g., ppm mass tolerance or background-enrichment threshold) and you need average peak counts per root plus percent-change metrics versus defaults. The MSI data are not along a linear developmental axis — DIMPLE is designed specifically for linear gradients, so peak-count comparisons on non-linear tissue geometry are out of scope The goal is annotating mass signatures (use METASPACE, Metlin Classic, or LOTUS instead of re-tuning DIMPLE's peak-detection thresholds) The data are not DESI-MSI root acquisitions in cdf/Matlab-workspace format compatible with batchcdfread Quantifies how many m/z signatures DIMPLE identifies per maize root under different parameter settings, expressing each relaxed-parameter run as an average peaks-per-root value and percent change relative to the default-parameter baseline (~196 peaks per root on B73). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Quantifies how many m/z signatures DIMPLE identifies per maize root under different parameter settings, expressing each relaxed-parameter run as an average peaks-per-root value and percent change relative to the default-parameter baseline (~196 peaks per root on B73).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MSI data are not along a linear developmental axis — DIMPLE is designed specifically for linear gradients, so peak-count comparisons on non-linear tissue geometry are out of scope The goal is annotating mass signatures (use METASPACE, Metlin Classic, or LOTUS instead of re-tuning DIMPLE's peak-detection thresholds) The data are not DESI-MSI root acquisitions in cdf/Matlab-workspace format compatible with batchcdfread

skills.description: Use when scoring query mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) against candidate molecules in VInSMoC and you need the raw peak count score that determines which spectrum-molecule couples exceed the minimum score reporting threshold.
skills.name: peak-count-scoring-of-spectrum-molecule-matches
skills.search_text: peak-count-scoring-of-spectrum-molecule-matches Use when scoring query mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) against candidate molecules in VInSMoC and you need the raw peak count score that determines which spectrum-molecule couples exceed the minimum score reporting threshold. You need statistically calibrated significance rather than a raw ranking score — peak count scores are biased (e.g. cyclic compounds can out-score correct linear matches at equal peak counts), so use the MCMC P value strategy instead. Your spectra have already been peak-merged or peak-filtered upstream — the default Peak Merge Threshold / Peaks Per Window preprocessing would double-process them; adjust advanced settings accordingly. The candidate molecule's precursor mass cannot be matched and no molecular variant can explain the mass difference Δ — no peak count score will be produced for that couple. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Compute the peak count score that VInSMoC uses to rank spectrum-molecule matches: count experimental peaks that align to theoretical fragments of a candidate molecule after the standard peak-merge and peak-filter preprocessing. This score is the raw ranking signal whose bias (e.g. toward cyclic topologies) is later corrected by MCMC P values. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Compute the peak count score that VInSMoC uses to rank spectrum-molecule matches: count experimental peaks that align to theoretical fragments of a candidate molecule after the standard peak-merge and peak-filter preprocessing. This score is the raw ranking signal whose bias (e.g. toward cyclic topologies) is later corrected by MCMC P values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need statistically calibrated significance rather than a raw ranking score — peak count scores are biased (e.g. cyclic compounds can out-score correct linear matches at equal peak counts), so use the MCMC P value strategy instead. Your spectra have already been peak-merged or peak-filtered upstream — the default Peak Merge Threshold / Peaks Per Window preprocessing would double-process them; adjust advanced settings accordingly. The candidate molecule's precursor mass cannot be matched and no molecular variant can explain the mass difference Δ — no peak count score will be produced for that couple.

skills.description: Use when validating or re-implementing asari peak quality metrics on extracted ion chromatograms, or when assessing whether a chromatographic peak in a composite mass track is selective (cSelectivity up to 1.0) versus contaminated by co-eluting signal.
skills.name: peak-cselectivity-fraction-calculation
skills.search_text: peak-cselectivity-fraction-calculation Use when validating or re-implementing asari peak quality metrics on extracted ion chromatograms, or when assessing whether a chromatographic peak in a composite mass track is selective (cSelectivity up to 1.0) versus contaminated by co-eluting signal. Input is a low-resolution or very high noise LC-MS dataset — asari is mostly tested on high-resolution Orbitrap platforms and does not work with low resolution data You only need the exported quality values — cSelectivity and snr are already carried in full_Feature_table.tsv and can be filtered directly (snr > 2, peakshape > 0.5) Analysis targets MS/MS spectra — these are ignored by asari's default LC-MS workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Implements asari's chromatographic peak selectivity (cSelectivity) quality metric on mass track (EIC) data: the fraction of data points above half the peak height that belong to the evaluated peak. It enables programmatic peak-quality assessment that reproduces the values exported with asari feature tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Implements asari's chromatographic peak selectivity (cSelectivity) quality metric on mass track (EIC) data: the fraction of data points above half the peak height that belong to the evaluated peak. The query spectra are true MS/MS spectra acquired at matching collision energies — scaling is designed for low-energy in-source fragments in MS1-only pseudo MS/MS data You are annotating MS/MS (MS2) data directly — the README specifies the gnps.pkl (unscaled) library is used for MS/MS annotation, while k10-scaled libraries are for MS1 annotation The compound class does not produce in-source fragments in the collected m/z range (e.g., guanine m/z 150.0421 and glutamic acid m/z 146.0459 failed for lack of sufficient in-source fragments above m/z 100) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A mass-dependent reference MS/MS peak intensity scaling approach (scale each fragment intensity by alpha_i = fragment m/z / precursor m/z raised to k=10, then square-root transform both spectra) that enables matching of low-energy in-source fragments in pseudo MS/MS spectra against reference libraries collected at medium-to-high collision energies. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: A mass-dependent reference MS/MS peak intensity scaling approach (scale each fragment intensity by alpha_i = fragment m/z / precursor m/z raised to k=10, then square-root transform both spectra) that enables matching of low-energy in-source fragments in pseudo MS/MS spectra against reference libraries collected at medium-to-high collision energies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectra are true MS/MS spectra acquired at matching collision energies — scaling is designed for low-energy in-source fragments in MS1-only pseudo MS/MS data You are annotating MS/MS (MS2) data directly — the README specifies the gnps.pkl (unscaled) library is used for MS/MS annotation, while k10-scaled libraries are for MS1 annotation The compound class does not produce in-source fragments in the collected m/z range (e.g., guanine m/z 150.0421 and glutamic acid m/z 146.0459 failed for lack of sufficient in-source fragments above m/z 100)

skills.name: peak-intensity-sqrt-transformation
skills.search_text: peak-intensity-sqrt-transformation Use when preprocessing MS/MS spectra (from mzML, mzXML, or MGF peak files) for cosine-similarity comparison or clustering, and dominant high-intensity peaks would otherwise skew the similarity measure. When clustering metabolomics or top-down data where the bottom-up proteomics preprocessing defaults (including this scaling and the 5-peak/250 m/z-range filters) likely need adjustment When a downstream similarity measure other than cosine similarity is used, since the scaling method's benefit (de-emphasizing dominant peaks) is tied to cosine-based comparison and influences the eps threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Square-root transform MS/MS peak intensities during spectrum preprocessing to de-emphasize overly dominant peaks before vectorization and cosine-similarity-based clustering, as done in the falcon spectrum clustering pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Square-root transform MS/MS peak intensities during spectrum preprocessing to de-emphasize overly dominant peaks before vectorization and cosine-similarity-based clustering, as done in the falcon spectrum clustering pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When clustering metabolomics or top-down data where the bottom-up proteomics preprocessing defaults (including this scaling and the 5-peak/250 m/z-range filters) likely need adjustment When a downstream similarity measure other than cosine similarity is used, since the scaling method's benefit (de-emphasizing dominant peaks) is tied to cosine-based comparison and influences the eps threshold

skills.description: Use when curating a mass spectral library (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON) in FragHub and you need to drop sparse or low-intensity spectra before writing the final unified library.
skills.name: peak-intensity-thresholding
skills.search_text: peak-intensity-thresholding Use when curating a mass spectral library (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON) in FragHub and you need to drop sparse or low-intensity spectra before writing the final unified library. The input is raw untargeted MS/MS data from an instrument rather than an already integrated open mass spectral library, since FragHub's filtering stage assumes parsed, standardized spectra. The library is already split by ionization mode and chromatography method and requires metadata harmonization (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey recalculation) rather than peak-list quality filtering. The goal is to filter by precursor m/z, peak count beyond three, or entropy score, where other FragHub filters like remove_peak_above_precursormz, reduce_peak_list, or remove_spectrum_under_entropy_score are the appropriate choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies FragHub's two-part spectral quality gate: retain only mass spectra containing at least three peaks and at least two peaks whose intensity is at least 5% of the maximum intensity, removing low-information spectra from integrated OMSL libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02219
skills.summary: Applies FragHub's two-part spectral quality gate: retain only mass spectra containing at least three peaks and at least two peaks whose intensity is at least 5% of the maximum intensity, removing low-information spectra from integrated OMSL libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw untargeted MS/MS data from an instrument rather than an already integrated open mass spectral library, since FragHub's filtering stage assumes parsed, standardized spectra. The library is already split by ionization mode and chromatography method and requires metadata harmonization (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey recalculation) rather than peak-list quality filtering. The goal is to filter by precursor m/z, peak count beyond three, or entropy score, where other FragHub filters like remove_peak_above_precursormz, reduce_peak_list, or remove_spectrum_under_entropy_score are the appropriate choice.

skills.description: Use when scoring similarity between two ESI-MS2 peak lists (m/z, intensity pairs) for compound identification against MassBank-style reference spectra, or when comparing exponent choices (m=0.5/n=2 vs m=0.6/n=3) at a 0.6 score threshold.
skills.name: peak-intensity-weighting
skills.search_text: peak-intensity-weighting Use when scoring similarity between two ESI-MS2 peak lists (m/z, intensity pairs) for compound identification against MassBank-style reference spectra, or when comparing exponent choices (m=0.5/n=2 vs m=0.6/n=3) at a 0.6 score threshold. Input spectra are EI-MS data — Stein and Scott's exponents (m=0.6, n=3) were derived for EI and the ESI-MS2-optimized m=0.5, n=2 may not transfer Input is already a similarity matrix or identification result table — the weighting step is redundant You need the merged-record identification precision gains: those require merging ESI-MS2 records across collision-induced dissociation conditions, not just re-weighting peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Implements MassBank's spectral-search similarity score: a weighted cosine correlation in which each peak i is weighted by W_i = [Intensity_i]^m * [m/z_i]^n, using the ESI-MS2-optimized exponents m = 0.5 and n = 2. These exponents differ from Stein and Scott's EI-MS values (m = 0.6, n = 3) and were tuned on 8785 ESI-MS2 spectra of ~700 authentic primary metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.1777
skills.summary: Implements MassBank's spectral-search similarity score: a weighted cosine correlation in which each peak i is weighted by W_i = [Intensity_i]^m * [m/z_i]^n, using the ESI-MS2-optimized exponents m = 0.5 and n = 2. These exponents differ from Stein and Scott's EI-MS values (m = 0.6, n = 3) and were tuned on 8785 ESI-MS2 spectra of ~700 authentic primary metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are EI-MS data — Stein and Scott's exponents (m=0.6, n=3) were derived for EI and the ESI-MS2-optimized m=0.5, n=2 may not transfer Input is already a similarity matrix or identification result table — the weighting step is redundant You need the merged-record identification precision gains: those require merging ESI-MS2 records across collision-induced dissociation conditions, not just re-weighting peaks

skills.description: Use when reconstructing Spec2Vec similarity scores from a trained Word2Vec model: processed MS/MS spectra must be converted into peak/loss word documents and embedded into fixed-length vectors via intensity-weighted summation.
skills.name: peak-intensity-weighting-of-spectral-tokens
skills.search_text: peak-intensity-weighting-of-spectral-tokens Use when reconstructing Spec2Vec similarity scores from a trained Word2Vec model: processed MS/MS spectra must be converted into peak/loss word documents and embedded into fixed-length vectors via intensity-weighted summation. No trained Word2Vec model is available — unlike cosine scores, Spec2Vec requires training data to learn fragment peak relationships Query spectra are far outside the training vocabulary (missing fraction exceeds the <0.05 threshold) — returned scores would be unreliable Input is raw, unprocessed spectra without peak filtering (m/z range [0,1000], >=10 peaks) and metadata cleaning via matchms http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Compute a Spec2Vec spectrum embedding as the peak-intensity-weighted sum of its fragment and neutral-loss word vectors from a trained gensim Word2Vec model, so that spectral similarity reduces to a cosine between two fixed-length vectors. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Compute a Spec2Vec spectrum embedding as the peak-intensity-weighted sum of its fragment and neutral-loss word vectors from a trained gensim Word2Vec model, so that spectral similarity reduces to a cosine between two fixed-length vectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trained Word2Vec model is available — unlike cosine scores, Spec2Vec requires training data to learn fragment peak relationships Query spectra are far outside the training vocabulary (missing fraction exceeds the <0.05 threshold) — returned scores would be unreliable Input is raw, unprocessed spectra without peak filtering (m/z range [0,1000], >=10 peaks) and metadata cleaning via matchms

skills.name: peak-label-csv-export
skills.search_text: peak-label-csv-export Use when an aligned or unaligned MZmine/XCMS feature table must be labelled as High_quality, Low_quality, or Noise by the pretrained NeatMS model and exported to CSV for downstream use. Goal is peak identification or reproducibility assessment — NeatMS gives no information on peak identity and cannot remove non-lipid metabolite peaks without a curated library panel. Input is already a labelled/curated table and you only need group filtering, not NN classification. Peak quality depends on properties other than MS2-derived feature quality (e.g. non-lipid metabolites) that the pretrained model was not trained on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Loads the pretrained NeatMS neural network into an NN_handler, labels every LC-MS MS1 peak at the 0.22 threshold, and writes a CSV whose columns (rt, mz, height, area, label) are controlled by export_properties. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02220
skills.summary: Loads the pretrained NeatMS neural network into an NN_handler, labels every LC-MS MS1 peak at the 0.22 threshold, and writes a CSV whose columns (rt, mz, height, area, label) are controlled by export_properties.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is peak identification or reproducibility assessment — NeatMS gives no information on peak identity and cannot remove non-lipid metabolite peaks without a curated library panel. Input is already a labelled/curated table and you only need group filtering, not NN classification. Peak quality depends on properties other than MS2-derived feature quality (e.g. non-lipid metabolites) that the pretrained model was not trained on.

Input is raw spectra rather than peak lists — alignment modules consume peak lists produced after peak picking and peak list deisotoping Only a single sample's peak list exists, so there is nothing to align across samples Non-LC-MS data types (e.g., GC-MS) — the paper notes the developed modules were tested mainly on LC-MS data http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Aligns per-sample LC-MS peak lists into a single master peak list in MZmine 2, either with the Join aligner's fixed 2D m/z–RT window or with the RANSAC-based aligner that fits a LOESS-smoothed retention-time correspondence model to handle non-linear RT shifts; performance is judged by precision/recall against ground-truth alignments. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-11-395

skills.search_text: peak-list-alignment-precision-recall-analysis Use when comparing peak list alignment algorithms on LC-MS feature tables where a 'ground truth' alignment table exists, and you need precision/recall metrics to decide which aligner (e.g., RANSAC vs Join) performs better on specific dataset fractions. skills.description: Use when Thermo .RAW files must be converted into columnar (Parquet) spectral peak lists for downstream machine learning, secondary analysis, or QC — e.g. when per-scan m/z, intensity, noise, baseline and charge arrays are needed.
skills.name: peak-list-parquet-export
skills.search_text: peak-list-parquet-export Use when Thermo .RAW files must be converted into columnar (Parquet) spectral peak lists for downstream machine learning, secondary analysis, or QC — e.g. when per-scan m/z, intensity, noise, baseline and charge arrays are needed. Input files are not Thermo Fisher RAW format — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW; additional vendor formats are not yet supported The goal is database-search-dependent QC metrics — this skill is search-free and acquisition-side only, so it cannot substitute for tools like MSQC that compute metrics from identified spectra ms_method/lc_method extraction on Linux containers is needed — those Thermo method-reading calls are not supported on Linux (peak-list export itself is unaffected) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Exports MS1 and MS2 spectral peak lists from Thermo RAW files as Parquet files: MS2 as indexed extended peak lists (mz_array, intensity_array, resolution_array, noises_array, baselines_array, charges_array) linked to scan-level metadata via scan numbers, and MS1 as m/z/intensity arrays with a centroid/profile flag. This makes raw spectra available for data-driven modelling such as spectral quality assessment, retention-time prediction, or anomaly detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.687968
skills.summary: Exports MS1 and MS2 spectral peak lists from Thermo RAW files as Parquet files: MS2 as indexed extended peak lists (mz_array, intensity_array, resolution_array, noises_array, baselines_array, charges_array) linked to scan-level metadata via scan numbers, and MS1 as m/z/intensity arrays with a centroid/profile flag. This makes raw spectra available for data-driven modelling such as spectral quality assessment, retention-time prediction, or anomaly detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are not Thermo Fisher RAW format — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW; additional vendor formats are not yet supported The goal is database-search-dependent QC metrics — this skill is search-free and acquisition-side only, so it cannot substitute for tools like MSQC that compute metrics from identified spectra ms_method/lc_method extraction on Linux containers is needed — those Thermo method-reading calls are not supported on Linux (peak-list export itself is unaffected)

You only need simple reproducibility-based noise removal rather than integration-quality assessment — a direct RSD < 30% cut-off in pooled QC samples may suffice without computing metric features. Your data have not yet been through XCMS peak-picking, retention time correction, and grouping — the metrics require the integrated EICs and grouped peak information an XCMS object provides.

skills.search_text: peak-quality-score-feature-engineering Use when building or retraining ML models for peak picking/peak reporting on LC-QQQ-MS MRM data (mzML) and you need the quality-score features that automRm derives from quantifier and qualifier traces. Excessively dirty samples, very-low-input samples, or newly established LC methods, where the article advises retreating to manual peak review Acquisition methods lacking any qualifier transition, since automRm requires at least one qualifier in addition to the quantifier for optimal performance Rule-based (non-ML) peak reporting is desired, since the quality-score feature engineering exists specifically to power ML-based decisions that surpass classical rule-based approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Engineering of ML feature vectors (quality scores) from LC-QQQ MRM chromatograms in automRm: local maxima in smoothed quantifier traces, cross-correlation-based RT shifts fitted as a quadratic function of RT, and prototype chromatogram construction. skills.description: Use when comparing feature tables from multiple LC-MS processing tools (e.g. asari, XCMS, MZmine) on the same raw data and you need to determine whether differences in reported feature counts reflect genuine coverage or low-quality peaks.
skills.name: peak-quality-threshold-counting
skills.search_text: peak-quality-threshold-counting Use when comparing feature tables from multiple LC-MS processing tools (e.g. asari, XCMS, MZmine) on the same raw data and you need to determine whether differences in reported feature counts reflect genuine coverage or low-quality peaks. The goal is metabolite annotation or identification — this skill only quantifies peak-shape quality and does not assign compounds Data are low-resolution MS: asari's mass-track-based processing and this quality metric assume high-resolution data A single tool's feature table is being validated with the tool's own internal QC rather than a cross-tool feature-count comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Counts good- vs bad-quality LC-MS features by fitting a Gaussian to each extracted ion chromatogram (EIC, padded 3 s on both sides of the reported peak boundary) and thresholding the peak-shape fitness score at 0.5. Used to show that inflated feature counts from tools like XCMS and MZmine arise mostly from low-quality, non-reproducible peaks rather than better coverage. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: Counts good- vs bad-quality LC-MS features by fitting a Gaussian to each extracted ion chromatogram (EIC, padded 3 s on both sides of the reported peak boundary) and thresholding the peak-shape fitness score at 0.5. Used to show that inflated feature counts from tools like XCMS and MZmine arise mostly from low-quality, non-reproducible peaks rather than better coverage.

skills.search_text: peak-record-unique-identifier-assignment Use when a raw Agilent Unknowns Analysis CSV (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) must be expanded into one uniquely-identified record per datapoint before compound extraction or annotation. skills.description: Use when processing high-resolution GC-CI-MS stable-isotope labeling data and you need to know which isotopologue m/z values of a derivatized formula can be distinguished at the instrument's resolution setting before quantifying them.
skills.name: peak-resolvability-assessment-at-given-resolution
skills.search_text: peak-resolvability-assessment-at-given-resolution Use when processing high-resolution GC-CI-MS stable-isotope labeling data and you need to know which isotopologue m/z values of a derivatized formula can be distinguished at the instrument's resolution setting before quantifying them. Input is low-resolution GC-CI-MS data (e.g. from an Agilent 7000 QqQ in SIM or narrow-window scan mode), where isoSCAN does not use enviPat-based envelope prediction and resolvability is not assessed from the formula. The analyte's derivatized formula is unknown or incomplete — enviPat cannot predict the isotopologue envelope without the full elemental composition including derivatization atoms (Si, etc.). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Predicts the theoretical isotopologue envelope of a derivatized formula using enviPat in R, computing each isotopologue's exact m/z and flagging whether neighboring isotopologue peaks (e.g. the M+0 through M+11 13C series of [M+H]+ ions) are resolved at the mass analyzer's configured resolving power (e.g. 60,000 at 200 m/z on a GC-Orbitrap). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02998
skills.summary: Predicts the theoretical isotopologue envelope of a derivatized formula using enviPat in R, computing each isotopologue's exact m/z and flagging whether neighboring isotopologue peaks (e.g. the M+0 through M+11 13C series of [M+H]+ ions) are resolved at the mass analyzer's configured resolving power (e.g. 60,000 at 200 m/z on a GC-Orbitrap).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is low-resolution GC-CI-MS data (e.g. from an Agilent 7000 QqQ in SIM or narrow-window scan mode), where isoSCAN does not use enviPat-based envelope prediction and resolvability is not assessed from the formula. The analyte's derivatized formula is unknown or incomplete — enviPat cannot predict the isotopologue envelope without the full elemental composition including derivatization atoms (Si, etc.).

skills.search_text: peak-shape-manual-annotation Use when an automated feature-detection output (mzLearn, XCMS, ASARI) must be scored for accuracy and you need peak-shape-based ground-truth labels for true-positive and false-positive rates. skills.description: Use when a targeted MRM workflow (e.g. SmartPeak/OpenMS) has produced a FeatureDB CSV of sample types and meta-values such as peak_area, logSN, and RT and you need per-compound internal-standard quality scores before quantitative reporting.
skills.name: peak-shape-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: peak-shape-quality-assessment Use when a targeted MRM workflow (e.g. SmartPeak/OpenMS) has produced a FeatureDB CSV of sample types and meta-values such as peak_area, logSN, and RT and you need per-compound internal-standard quality scores before quantitative reporting. skills.summary: Optional internal-standard scoring module in the SmartPeak targeted-quantitation workflow that computes per-compound IS metrics (peak tailing, asymmetry, analyte-to-IS height ratio) from a FeatureDB export and emits a per-compound score table (is_scores.csv).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a SmartPeak/OpenMS FeatureDB export (e.g. already aggregated peak-area tables without transition-level meta-values such as tailing or asymmetry). skills.description: Use when you have MZmine 2-extracted LC-MS peak groups (e.g., from human plasma HILIC LC-MS data) and need to represent each peak's shape across samples as a raster image for image-based deep learning peak classification.

skills.search_text: peak-shape-raster-image-generation Use when you have MZmine 2-extracted LC-MS peak groups (e.g., from human plasma HILIC LC-MS data) and need to represent each peak's shape across samples as a raster image for image-based deep learning peak classification. skills.summary: Converts LC-MS peak shape information from MZmine 2 peak lists into raster images (rows = samples, columns = scan points, pixel values = intensity) so that an image-based deep neural network can classify peak groups as true or false peaks.

skills.name: peak-table-matrix-parsing
skills.search_text: peak-table-matrix-parsing Use when input is a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (e.g. the AFADESI mouse brain table with 53,812 pixels x 2,654 ion peaks) that must be loaded and split into pixel coordinates and ion intensity columns before SMQVP analysis. Input is raw instrument data (e.g. imaging MS raw files) rather than an already-constructed peak table matrix — SMQVP's input requirement is specifically a peak table with X/Y coordinates plus m/z intensity columns The table lacks the first-two-column X/Y coordinate layout, e.g. it is a plain feature-by-sample intensity table without spatial pixel indices The goal is metabolite annotation or identification rather than quality visualization and preprocessing of pixel-level spatial data http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parse spatial metabolomics peak table matrices in the SMQVP-defined layout — first two columns are pixel X/Y coordinates and remaining columns are m/z ion intensities — so downstream quality visualization and preprocessing modules receive a correctly shaped pixel-by-ion matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Parse spatial metabolomics peak table matrices in the SMQVP-defined layout — first two columns are pixel X/Y coordinates and remaining columns are m/z ion intensities — so downstream quality visualization and preprocessing modules receive a correctly shaped pixel-by-ion matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw instrument data (e.g. imaging MS raw files) rather than an already-constructed peak table matrix — SMQVP's input requirement is specifically a peak table with X/Y coordinates plus m/z intensity columns The table lacks the first-two-column X/Y coordinate layout, e.g. it is a plain feature-by-sample intensity table without spatial pixel indices The goal is metabolite annotation or identification rather than quality visualization and preprocessing of pixel-level spatial data

skills.description: Use when benchmarking peak-picking/alignment pipelines on identical mzML/mzXML cohorts and you need defensible sensitivity, specificity, speed, and overlap numbers, such as IPA vs MS-DIAL on 499-sample studies.
skills.name: peak-table-metrics-comparison-across-pipelines
skills.search_text: peak-table-metrics-comparison-across-pipelines Use when benchmarking peak-picking/alignment pipelines on identical mzML/mzXML cohorts and you need defensible sensitivity, specificity, speed, and overlap numbers, such as IPA vs MS-DIAL on 499-sample studies. When only one pipeline's aligned feature table is already available and no raw data exists to rerun a second tool — comparison requires processing the same raw files through both pipelines. When the goal is formula annotation or MS2 deconvolution rather than peak-picking benchmarking — those tasks belong to IDSL.UFA, IDSL.UFAx, or IDSL.CSA, not this skill. When the two pipelines differ in upstream peak-detection logic (e.g. MZmine 2/xcms-CAMERA chromatographic ROI methods) and no shared-peak overlap metric is planned — raw count deltas alone do not distinguish m/z-binning differences from true detection differences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Run two LC/HRMS peak-picking pipelines (e.g. IDSL.IPA and MS-DIAL) on the same raw cohort, then quantify cross-tool agreement by the number of aligned peaks, processing time, and shared-peak coverage. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: Run two LC/HRMS peak-picking pipelines (e.g. IDSL.IPA and MS-DIAL) on the same raw cohort, then quantify cross-tool agreement by the number of aligned peaks, processing time, and shared-peak coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one pipeline's aligned feature table is already available and no raw data exists to rerun a second tool — comparison requires processing the same raw files through both pipelines. When the goal is formula annotation or MS2 deconvolution rather than peak-picking benchmarking — those tasks belong to IDSL.UFA, IDSL.UFAx, or IDSL.CSA, not this skill. When the two pipelines differ in upstream peak-detection logic (e.g. MZmine 2/xcms-CAMERA chromatographic ROI methods) and no shared-peak overlap metric is planned — raw count deltas alone do not distinguish m/z-binning differences from true detection differences.

skills.search_text: peak-table-processing-stage-modeling Use when a metabolomic peak table must be processed and you need to enumerate or reason about which ordered combinations of imputation, QCS-correction, transformation and normalization methods are applicable to the data scenario (with QCSs, with ISs, or neither). Input is not a peak table but raw instrument data — conversion/peak picking (Proteowizard, nmrML, XCMS, NMRProc Flow) must happen before stage modeling The study already prescribes a single fixed processing pipeline and no comparative workflow optimization is intended Data come from emerging techniques (e.g. pseudotargeted or spatial metabolomics) whose systematic bias structure the staged model has not been validated for http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Models metabolomic peak-table processing as an ordered sequence of method stages (S1 data filtering/imputation, S2 QCS correction, S3 transformation, S4 normalization) whose combinations are enumerated to expose the thousands of candidate workflows NOREVA scans before S5 multi-criterion assessment. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Models metabolomic peak-table processing as an ordered sequence of method stages (S1 data filtering/imputation, S2 QCS correction, S3 transformation, S4 normalization) whose combinations are enumerated to expose the thousands of candidate workflows NOREVA scans before S5 multi-criterion assessment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a peak table but raw instrument data — conversion/peak picking (Proteowizard, nmrML, XCMS, NMRProc Flow) must happen before stage modeling The study already prescribes a single fixed processing pipeline and no comparative workflow optimization is intended Data come from emerging techniques (e.g. pseudotargeted or spatial metabolomics) whose systematic bias structure the staged model has not been validated for

skills.search_text: peak-table-quality-checking Use when you have an integrated, time-aligned, imputed peak table from untargeted LC-MS metabolomics and need to filter peaks for quality checking and account for technical variation prior to downstream grouping or statistics. Input is a raw vendor file (e.g. .CDF) or MS2 mzXML spectra rather than an imputed peak table — run integration and imputation first Data have not yet been processed for missing values and artifacts; filtering on a peak table with remaining missing values will misjudge feature quality You need annotation or tentative identification by database search — that is the separate OUKS '5. skills.summary: Quality-checking and filtering of an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics peak table using the OUKS '6. Filtering.R' script, which removes poor-quality features and accounts for technical variation before statistical analysis.

Annotation.R' step, not quality filtering

skills.description: Use when a tab-delimited peak-integrated table (columns aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) from targeted LC-MS dMRM measurements must be split by sample type (QC, blank, study) so that per-compound RSD of QC area ratios and blank-derived background signal (e-score) can be.
skills.name: peak-table-sample-type-partitioning
skills.search_text: peak-table-sample-type-partitioning Use when a tab-delimited peak-integrated table (columns aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) from targeted LC-MS dMRM measurements must be split by sample type (QC, blank, study) so that per-compound RSD of QC area ratios and blank-derived background signal (e-score) can be. The input is not a peak-integrated table with the mandatory mzQuality columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) — readData will reject it The dataset is untargeted/feature-based (e.g. mzML features from OpenMS or MZmine) rather than peak-integrated targeted LC-MS dMRM output; mzQuality processes peak-integrated data independently of vendor software and is not a peak-picking tool The goal is batch correction or outlier detection rather than compound confidence-tier classification; those are separate mzQuality workflow steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Partition a tab-delimited peak-integrated metabolomics table into QC (LQC/SQC), blank, and study sample groups using the mzQuality `type` column, then compute per-compound RSDQC and background e-score metrics and classify each compound into High Confidence, Caution, or Low SNR tiers using the RSDQC <15%, 15–30%, and RSDQC >30% / e-score >40% thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Partition a tab-delimited peak-integrated metabolomics table into QC (LQC/SQC), blank, and study sample groups using the mzQuality `type` column, then compute per-compound RSDQC and background e-score metrics and classify each compound into High Confidence, Caution, or Low SNR tiers using the RSDQC <15%, 15–30%, and RSDQC >30% / e-score >40% thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a peak-integrated table with the mandatory mzQuality columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) — readData will reject it The dataset is untargeted/feature-based (e.g. mzML features from OpenMS or MZmine) rather than peak-integrated targeted LC-MS dMRM output; mzQuality processes peak-integrated data independently of vendor software and is not a peak-picking tool The goal is batch correction or outlier detection rather than compound confidence-tier classification; those are separate mzQuality workflow steps

skills.description: Use when an HRMS feature list from .mzML data of mixed chemical standards with known composition needs reliability validation by matching detected peaks to the spiked standard list and computing extraction accuracy.
skills.name: peak-to-known-standard-matching
skills.search_text: peak-to-known-standard-matching Use when an HRMS feature list from .mzML data of mixed chemical standards with known composition needs reliability validation by matching detected peaks to the spiked standard list and computing extraction accuracy. Input is already a curated feature table from a tool other than the extraction pipeline under test — cross-tool agreement should instead be measured as overlap (e.g., the ~52% MSS vs. MSDIAL/XCMS comparison), not standard-matching accuracy Samples are real environmental or unknown-composition matrices with no spiked standard list, so no ground-truth peak inventory exists to match against The goal is identification/annotation of unknown features (e.g., MS/MS fragment matching against MoNA MassBank), not extraction reliability assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validates an HRMS feature-extraction workflow by matching every extracted chromatographic peak against a curated list of chemicals of known composition (e.g., the 398 MS-amenable chemicals spiked into EPA ENTACT mixtures #505, #506, #508) and reporting accuracy as the fraction of known peaks recovered, which for Mass-Suite (MSS) was 99.5% (2 of 398 unmatched). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00741-9
skills.summary: Validates an HRMS feature-extraction workflow by matching every extracted chromatographic peak against a curated list of chemicals of known composition (e.g., the 398 MS-amenable chemicals spiked into EPA ENTACT mixtures #505, #506, #508) and reporting accuracy as the fraction of known peaks recovered, which for Mass-Suite (MSS) was 99.5% (2 of 398 unmatched).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table from a tool other than the extraction pipeline under test — cross-tool agreement should instead be measured as overlap (e.g., the ~52% MSS vs. MSDIAL/XCMS comparison), not standard-matching accuracy Samples are real environmental or unknown-composition matrices with no spiked standard list, so no ground-truth peak inventory exists to match against The goal is identification/annotation of unknown features (e.g., MS/MS fragment matching against MoNA MassBank), not extraction reliability assessment

skills.description: Use when a 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. JCAMP-DX) has been loaded and peak-picked with a threshold, and you need per-peak coupling constants and multiplicity labels assembled into a structured CSV table.
skills.name: peak-to-multiplicity-table-assembly
skills.search_text: peak-to-multiplicity-table-assembly Use when a 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. JCAMP-DX) has been loaded and peak-picked with a threshold, and you need per-peak coupling constants and multiplicity labels assembled into a structured CSV table. The input is 2D NMR data — the article lists viewing and analysis of 2D data as a future improvement not yet supported by ChemSpectra The input is a raw Bruker FID file requiring advanced phase correction and baseline correction — the article notes FID file processing still has to be improved The goal is IR or MS analysis — coupling constant calculation and multiplicity assignment are NMR-specific functions http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Assembles a peak-to-multiplicity assignment table for a 1H NMR spectrum: picked peaks with positions (x) and intensities (y) are annotated with coupling constants computed from the splitting pattern of neighbouring lines and multiplicity labels (s, d, t, q, quint, m) inferred by known libraries and checked by additional rules, following the ChemSpectra workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00481-0
skills.summary: Assembles a peak-to-multiplicity assignment table for a 1H NMR spectrum: picked peaks with positions (x) and intensities (y) are annotated with coupling constants computed from the splitting pattern of neighbouring lines and multiplicity labels (s, d, t, q, quint, m) inferred by known libraries and checked by additional rules, following the ChemSpectra workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is 2D NMR data — the article lists viewing and analysis of 2D data as a future improvement not yet supported by ChemSpectra The input is a raw Bruker FID file requiring advanced phase correction and baseline correction — the article notes FID file processing still has to be improved The goal is IR or MS analysis — coupling constant calculation and multiplicity assignment are NMR-specific functions

skills.search_text: peakforest-data-model-entity-mapping Use when a batch compound list must be loaded into a local PeakForest database and each template row's metadata (common name, InChI, InChIKey, etc.) must be mapped to the chemical compound entity before validation and database ingestion. PeakForest does not include data clean-up or extraction tools, so do not use this mapping to clean or normalize dirty spectra/metadata — users must supply completely-cleaned data following the PeakForest team's SOPs The goal is storing raw spectral data rather than metabolite annotation report data and compound metadata; PeakForest is designed for the latter, not raw spectral data storage Only a handful of ad hoc compounds need manual entry — the manual 'Import compounds and spectral data' workflow via the Web interface is simpler than building a template-based batch import http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps columns of a supplementary compound-import template (e.g. Online Resource 2 XLSX) onto the chemical compound entity fields of the PeakForest data model, so batch-imported compound lists can be validated and serialized for ingestion into the PeakForest MySQL-backed webapp. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
