skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw spectra whose molecular formula assignment and peak filtering (m/z, 13C isotopes, 0.5 ppm error, minimum sample count) have not yet been done — MetaboDirect requires pre-processed formula-assigned data Situations where a single significant PERMANOVA result will be over-interpreted as visible group separation — the paper shows significant p-values can occur when NMDS/PCA ordination fails to discriminate groups Data lacking sample grouping metadata, since PERMANOVA tests dissimilarity against a grouping factor

skills.description: Use when testing whether compositional (beta-diversity) distances separate predefined sample groups — e.g. genotype or sex in SPF mouse metagenomics — and you need a per-factor pseudo-F and p-value rather than abundance-level tests.
skills.name: permanova-group-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permanova-group-significance-testing Use when testing whether compositional (beta-diversity) distances separate predefined sample groups — e.g. genotype or sex in SPF mouse metagenomics — and you need a per-factor pseudo-F and p-value rather than abundance-level tests. The question concerns alpha diversity or differential abundance of individual taxa/features rather than community-composition (beta-diversity) separation between groups. You intend to pool 3xTg and 5xFAD samples into a single PERMANOVA — the genotype effect was observed only in the 3xTg Sacrifice cohort, so per-study stratification is required. The data are from the Longitudinal cohort, whose fecal samples lack animal IDs and differ in collection method (fresh fecal vs. colon after sacrifice) from the Sacrifice cohort. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Runs PERMANOVA on beta-diversity distances (here phylo-RPCA distances from fecal shotgun metagenomics) to test whether predefined groups such as genotype or sex differ significantly in community composition, reporting pseudo-F and p-value per factor and study. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Runs PERMANOVA on beta-diversity distances (here phylo-RPCA distances from fecal shotgun metagenomics) to test whether predefined groups such as genotype or sex differ significantly in community composition, reporting pseudo-F and p-value per factor and study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns alpha diversity or differential abundance of individual taxa/features rather than community-composition (beta-diversity) separation between groups. You intend to pool 3xTg and 5xFAD samples into a single PERMANOVA — the genotype effect was observed only in the 3xTg Sacrifice cohort, so per-study stratification is required. The data are from the Longitudinal cohort, whose fecal samples lack animal IDs and differ in collection method (fresh fecal vs. colon after sacrifice) from the Sacrifice cohort.

skills.description: Use when a sample metadata column (e.g., chromatographic batch) must be tested against beta diversity of a metabolomics feature table, especially to quantify how much a Qemistree chemical hierarchy attenuates batch-driven separation.
skills.name: permanova-group-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permanova-group-significance-testing Use when a sample metadata column (e.g., chromatographic batch) must be tested against beta diversity of a metabolomics feature table, especially to quantify how much a Qemistree chemical hierarchy attenuates batch-driven separation. No chemical hierarchy is available (features lack MS/MS data or SIRUS/CSI:FingerID fingerprints), so a tree-informed UniFrac metric cannot be computed and only tree-agnostic distances apply. The metadata column has fewer than two groups or highly unbalanced group sizes, making PERMANOVA pseudo-F interpretation unreliable. The goal is within-sample (alpha) diversity such as Faith's Phylogenetic Diversity rather than between-sample group separation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Tests whether sample grouping (e.g., chromatographic batch) explains significant variation in beta-diversity by running one-sided PERMANOVA (999 permutations) on distance matrices, comparing tree-agnostic (Bray-Curtis) vs tree-informed (weighted UniFrac on a Qemistree chemical hierarchy) metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00677-3
skills.summary: Tests whether sample grouping (e.g., chromatographic batch) explains significant variation in beta-diversity by running one-sided PERMANOVA (999 permutations) on distance matrices, comparing tree-agnostic (Bray-Curtis) vs tree-informed (weighted UniFrac on a Qemistree chemical hierarchy) metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No chemical hierarchy is available (features lack MS/MS data or SIRUS/CSI:FingerID fingerprints), so a tree-informed UniFrac metric cannot be computed and only tree-agnostic distances apply. The metadata column has fewer than two groups or highly unbalanced group sizes, making PERMANOVA pseudo-F interpretation unreliable. The goal is within-sample (alpha) diversity such as Faith's Phylogenetic Diversity rather than between-sample group separation.

skills.description: Use when a precomputed sample-sample distance matrix (MEMO, Qemistree UniFrac, CSCS, or feature-table Bray-Curtis) must be tested for group effects — e.g. 'experiment' (C18 vs C18 RT-shift, Q-Exactive vs Maxis II Q-TOF) vs 'composition' — via PERMANOVA pseudo-F.
skills.name: permanova-pseudo-f-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: permanova-pseudo-f-hypothesis-testing Use when a precomputed sample-sample distance matrix (MEMO, Qemistree UniFrac, CSCS, or feature-table Bray-Curtis) must be tested for group effects — e.g. 'experiment' (C18 vs C18 RT-shift, Q-Exactive vs Maxis II Q-TOF) vs 'composition' — via PERMANOVA pseudo-F. No distance matrix and no sample metadata factor with replicate groups exist yet — PERMANOVA operates on precomputed distance matrices plus categorical groupings, not raw spectra or per-feature tables The question is feature-level (which peaks/losses differ) rather than sample-level group separation — PERMANOVA pseudo-F tests factors over samples only A parametric effect-size estimate or per-feature significance testing is required — PERMANOVA is a non-parametric pseudo-F permutation test, not a differential-abundance method http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Non-parametric PERMANOVA hypothesis testing of sample-level distance matrices using scikit-bio, reporting pseudo-F statistics and p-values (999 permutations) for factors such as LC method, MS platform, or sample composition. In the MEMO workflow it is the benchmark metric quantifying how well each clustering method (MEMO, Qemistree UniFrac, CSCS, feature-table Bray-Curtis) mitigates the artificial retention-time batch effect. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Non-parametric PERMANOVA hypothesis testing of sample-level distance matrices using scikit-bio, reporting pseudo-F statistics and p-values (999 permutations) for factors such as LC method, MS platform, or sample composition. In the MEMO workflow it is the benchmark metric quantifying how well each clustering method (MEMO, Qemistree UniFrac, CSCS, feature-table Bray-Curtis) mitigates the artificial retention-time batch effect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No distance matrix and no sample metadata factor with replicate groups exist yet — PERMANOVA operates on precomputed distance matrices plus categorical groupings, not raw spectra or per-feature tables The question is feature-level (which peaks/losses differ) rather than sample-level group separation — PERMANOVA pseudo-F tests factors over samples only A parametric effect-size estimate or per-feature significance testing is required — PERMANOVA is a non-parametric pseudo-F permutation test, not a differential-abundance method

skills.description: Use when you have a permethylated N-glycan MALDI-TOF spectrum (e.g., PNGase-F released, HILIC SPE enriched, permethylated with DMSO/NaOH/CH3I, mixed with Super-DHB matrix) and a glycan name/theoretical-mass (Da) database, and need to call which glycans are present by accurate mass matching.
skills.name: permethylated-n-glycan-mass-assignment
skills.search_text: permethylated-n-glycan-mass-assignment Use when you have a permethylated N-glycan MALDI-TOF spectrum (e.g., PNGase-F released, HILIC SPE enriched, permethylated with DMSO/NaOH/CH3I, mixed with Super-DHB matrix) and a glycan name/theoretical-mass (Da) database, and need to call which glycans are present by accurate mass matching. The data are LC-MS/MS Orbitrap runs of fluorescently labeled (2-AB or ProCA) N-glycans — use the app's MS1/MS2 tabs instead of the MALDI Peak ID tab Glycans of interest are not in the database — the app performs mass search only and has no de novo glycan identification capability The analytes are O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assign permethylated N-glycan species in MALDI-TOF mass spectra by searching observed peak masses against a theoretical glycan mass database using the MALDI Peak ID tab of the GlyKAn AZ MATLAB app. The skill replaces manual peak-by-mass glycan calling and was validated by reproducing a full manual analysis (49 confirmed glycans plus one unassigned peak). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: Assign permethylated N-glycan species in MALDI-TOF mass spectra by searching observed peak masses against a theoretical glycan mass database using the MALDI Peak ID tab of the GlyKAn AZ MATLAB app. The skill replaces manual peak-by-mass glycan calling and was validated by reproducing a full manual analysis (49 confirmed glycans plus one unassigned peak).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are LC-MS/MS Orbitrap runs of fluorescently labeled (2-AB or ProCA) N-glycans — use the app's MS1/MS2 tabs instead of the MALDI Peak ID tab Glycans of interest are not in the database — the app performs mass search only and has no de novo glycan identification capability The analytes are O-linked glycans — the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans

skills.description: Use when you need a gold-standard family-wise error rate benchmark (Meff0 = alpha / alpha_f0) to calibrate or validate eigen-analysis or distance-correlation-based p-value adjustment procedures for high-dimensional metabolomics association testing.
skills.name: permutation-based-family-wise-error-estimation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-family-wise-error-estimation Use when you need a gold-standard family-wise error rate benchmark (Meff0 = alpha / alpha_f0) to calibrate or validate eigen-analysis or distance-correlation-based p-value adjustment procedures for high-dimensional metabolomics association testing. The goal is a fast p-value adjustment on the observed data itself — this skill is a computationally heavy gold-standard benchmark (10,000 permutations with full re-testing), not a practical correction procedure like DisCo P-ad The response is not a continuous outcome or the features are not well approximated by a multivariate-Gaussian with an estimable correlation structure Only a small sub-sample of the real data is available, so the empirical correlation structure of the 761 metabolites cannot be reliably estimated http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates the gold-standard effective number of tests (Meff0 = alpha / alpha_f0) by running K=10,000 label permutations with full re-testing of all marginal metabolite-outcome associations per permutation, establishing an empirical family-wise Type-I error benchmark for multiple-testing correction methods in MWAS. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Estimates the gold-standard effective number of tests (Meff0 = alpha / alpha_f0) by running K=10,000 label permutations with full re-testing of all marginal metabolite-outcome associations per permutation, establishing an empirical family-wise Type-I error benchmark for multiple-testing correction methods in MWAS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a fast p-value adjustment on the observed data itself — this skill is a computationally heavy gold-standard benchmark (10,000 permutations with full re-testing), not a practical correction procedure like DisCo P-ad The response is not a continuous outcome or the features are not well approximated by a multivariate-Gaussian with an estimable correlation structure Only a small sub-sample of the real data is available, so the empirical correlation structure of the 761 metabolites cannot be reliably estimated

skills.name: permutation-based-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: permutation-based-multiple-testing-correction Use when comparing pathway activity levels between two sample groups with per-pathway t statistics and a family-wise error correction is needed for many correlated pathway tests. Testing a single pre-specified pathway hypothesis where no family-wise correction across pathways is needed A one-way or multi-factor analysis where a two-group t statistic on mean activity is not the test statistic being calibrated http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Empirical multiple-testing correction that converts per-pathway t statistics to p-values by comparing each observed statistic against the maximum t statistic recorded across all ~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathways in 10,000 sample-label permutations, as used by the PLAGE pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Empirical multiple-testing correction that converts per-pathway t statistics to p-values by comparing each observed statistic against the maximum t statistic recorded across all ~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathways in 10,000 sample-label permutations, as used by the PLAGE pipeline.

skills.description: Use when a gene-by-sample matrix has been converted to pathway activity levels for ~400 KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets and you need empirical p-values for phenotype associations without parametric distributional assumptions.
skills.name: permutation-based-pathway-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-based-pathway-significance-testing Use when a gene-by-sample matrix has been converted to pathway activity levels for ~400 KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets and you need empirical p-values for phenotype associations without parametric distributional assumptions. You have no predefined pathway gene-set definitions (KEGG/Biocarta) for your genes — there is nothing to build pathway activity levels or their null distribution on. The analysis goal is to yield gene rankings (e.g., signal-to-noise ordered gene lists) rather than pathway-level p-values — use gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) instead, as in the article's companion comparison. The phenotype association is at the individual-gene level with no interest in group-defined pathway features — the paper argues individual-gene analyses are complementary, not substitutes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Empirical significance assessment for pathway activity levels (PLAGE-style SVD first-row coefficients) by randomly permuting sample labels or continuous phenotypes 10,000 times and comparing each pathway's observed statistic against the extremal (maximum t-statistic or minimum/maximum correlation) statistic from permuted data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Empirical significance assessment for pathway activity levels (PLAGE-style SVD first-row coefficients) by randomly permuting sample labels or continuous phenotypes 10,000 times and comparing each pathway's observed statistic against the extremal (maximum t-statistic or minimum/maximum correlation) statistic from permuted data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no predefined pathway gene-set definitions (KEGG/Biocarta) for your genes — there is nothing to build pathway activity levels or their null distribution on. The analysis goal is to yield gene rankings (e.g., signal-to-noise ordered gene lists) rather than pathway-level p-values — use gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) instead, as in the article's companion comparison. The phenotype association is at the individual-gene level with no interest in group-defined pathway features — the paper argues individual-gene analyses are complementary, not substitutes.

skills.name: permutation-based-prioritization-benchmarking
skills.search_text: permutation-based-prioritization-benchmarking Use when you have a ranked per-patient candidate gene list with a known causative gene and need to quantify whether the prioritization rate exceeds chance, e.g. reproducing metPropagate's 92% top-20th-percentile rate. When no known causative gene exists for a case (e.g. novel discovery patients like TIDEX), since the permutation requires seeding the causative gene in each random list When candidate lists are much smaller than the fixed 300-gene design (e.g. trio WES lists), where the top-20th-percentile cutoff of rank <= 60 no longer matches the article's 55-115 gene range per patient Benchmark a gene-prioritization method by generating random candidate gene lists that include the known causative gene, ranking it against random genes, and scoring how often it lands in the top 20th percentile — as done for metPropagate on the Miller 107-patient IEM dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Benchmark a gene-prioritization method by generating random candidate gene lists that include the known causative gene, ranking it against random genes, and scoring how often it lands in the top 20th percentile — as done for metPropagate on the Miller 107-patient IEM dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no known causative gene exists for a case (e.g. novel discovery patients like TIDEX), since the permutation requires seeding the causative gene in each random list When candidate lists are much smaller than the fixed 300-gene design (e.g. trio WES lists), where the top-20th-percentile cutoff of rank <= 60 no longer matches the article's 55-115 gene range per patient

skills.description: Use when testing many predefined gene-sets (~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathways) for differential activity between two sample groups and you need a multiple-testing-aware empirical p-value without parametric assumptions on small microarray cohorts.
skills.name: permutation-based-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-pvalue-estimation Use when testing many predefined gene-sets (~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathways) for differential activity between two sample groups and you need a multiple-testing-aware empirical p-value without parametric assumptions on small microarray cohorts. When the number of possible distinct sample-label permutations is too small to support the permutation count (e.g. very few samples per group), since the empirical p-value resolution is bounded by the permutation space When testing a single pre-specified hypothesis rather than the full ~400-pathway collection — the max-statistic null would needlessly apply a collection-wide multiple-testing correction When a validated parametric correction (e.g. FDR over computed statistics) is explicitly required by the analysis plan http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates pathway-level significance by randomly permuting sample labels many times (10,000 in the PLAGE article; 1,000 for the GSEA-style ES workflow) and building a null distribution from the most extreme statistic (max t-statistic or max enrichment score) across all ~400 KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets, so that p-values account for testing hundreds of pathways simultaneously. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Estimates pathway-level significance by randomly permuting sample labels many times (10,000 in the PLAGE article; 1,000 for the GSEA-style ES workflow) and building a null distribution from the most extreme statistic (max t-statistic or max enrichment score) across all ~400 KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets, so that p-values account for testing hundreds of pathways simultaneously.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the number of possible distinct sample-label permutations is too small to support the permutation count (e.g. very few samples per group), since the empirical p-value resolution is bounded by the permutation space When testing a single pre-specified hypothesis rather than the full ~400-pathway collection — the max-statistic null would needlessly apply a collection-wide multiple-testing correction When a validated parametric correction (e.g. FDR over computed statistics) is explicitly required by the analysis plan

skills.description: Use when a pathway-level importance statistic (MB-VIP, VIP, RGCCA loading relevance, bootstrap non-zero-loading count) needs a p-value, and no closed-form null exists because the statistic comes from a fitted multivariate model (MB-PLS, PLS, DIABLO).
skills.name: permutation-based-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-based-significance-testing Use when a pathway-level importance statistic (MB-VIP, VIP, RGCCA loading relevance, bootstrap non-zero-loading count) needs a p-value, and no closed-form null exists because the statistic comes from a fitted multivariate model (MB-PLS, PLS, DIABLO). The goal is differential-abundance testing of individual molecules, where standard statistical tests (e.g. t-tests used in sspa ORA) provide the null directly and permutation of model statistics is unnecessary. Samples are not measured across all omics views — PathIntegrate requires complete multi-omics data, so individuals missing an omics layer must be excluded before model fitting and permutation. The analysis targets conventional pathway analysis (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) rather than pathway importance statistics from a predictive model; the paper notes no direct comparison to these approaches was performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assess significance of pathway importance statistics (MB-VIP, VIP, DIABLO loading relevance) by building empirical null distributions through repeated label permutation and model refitting, then applying Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. This is how PathIntegrate attaches p-values to multi-omics pathway rankings. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Assess significance of pathway importance statistics (MB-VIP, VIP, DIABLO loading relevance) by building empirical null distributions through repeated label permutation and model refitting, then applying Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. This is how PathIntegrate attaches p-values to multi-omics pathway rankings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential-abundance testing of individual molecules, where standard statistical tests (e.g. t-tests used in sspa ORA) provide the null directly and permutation of model statistics is unnecessary. Samples are not measured across all omics views — PathIntegrate requires complete multi-omics data, so individuals missing an omics layer must be excluded before model fitting and permutation. The analysis targets conventional pathway analysis (ORA, GSEA, MultiGSEA, IMPaLA) rather than pathway importance statistics from a predictive model; the paper notes no direct comparison to these approaches was performed.

skills.description: Use when correlating metabolomics-derived substructure motifs (Mass2Motifs) with genome-mined sub-cluster features across a paired genome-metabolome strain panel, and you need p-values that account for non-independence of closely related strains.

skills.search_text: permutation-significance-testing Use when correlating metabolomics-derived substructure motifs (Mass2Motifs) with genome-mined sub-cluster features across a paired genome-metabolome strain panel, and you need p-values that account for non-independence of closely related strains. The input is a single BGC–molecule pair without a replicated strain panel — permutation of co-occurrence across strains requires multiple genomes and metabolomes. Correlations are between variables expected to be independent (e.g. two mass motifs); the null here is specifically about BGC-required-but-possibly-cryptic co-occurrence. Your strain panel contains only highly clonal isolates and you cannot correct for shared-BGC inflation — the p-values would be spuriously small. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assess whether observed co-occurrence correlation scores between MS/MS-derived Mass2Motifs and genome-mined biosynthetic sub-clusters (iPRESTO sub-cluster motifs and sub-cluster clans/SCCs) exceed chance, by permutation testing that explicitly controls for inflation from highly related strains sharing many BGCs and compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462

Your strain panel contains only highly clonal isolates and you cannot correct for shared-BGC inflation — the p-values would be spuriously small.

skills.description: Use when non-target HRMS data (mzML, ddMS2, centroided, ESI/APCI) yields thousands of features and you need to separate PFAS analytes from matrix components using mass-defect, KMD, MS2-fragment, and suspect-list criteria.

skills.search_text: pfas-mass-defect-prioritization Use when non-target HRMS data (mzML, ddMS2, centroided, ESI/APCI) yields thousands of features and you need to separate PFAS analytes from matrix components using mass-defect, KMD, MS2-fragment, and suspect-list criteria. skills.summary: Classifies HRMS features as potentially fluorinated (PFAS) vs hydrocarbon matrix components using the CH2-scaled Kendrick mass defect framework: per-feature carbon number, mass per carbon (m/C), and mass defect per carbon (MD/C), visualized as a 2D density histogram and applied as a data-reduction filter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not HRMS feature-level measurements (e.g., already confirmed PFAS identities or raw spectra without feature finding) — use suspect screening or MS2 fragment matching instead The goal is to assign PFAS classes or confirm structures; MD/C-m/C is a prioritization/data-reduction step, not an identification method Sample matrix is not dominated by hydrocarbon components whose m/C/MD/C separation (m/C < ~25, positive MD/C) underlies the cutoff rationale

skills.name: pfas-msms-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: pfas-msms-feature-annotation Use when processing LC-HRMS/MS acquisitions of PFAS-containing samples (e.g. AFFF, serum) where you need per-feature PFAS MS/MS evidence flags and per-round confidence-scored (score A) annotation counts. The input is already a curated, confidence-scored feature table with per-feature PFAS annotations — re-running annotation would duplicate the scoring step. Only MS1 data without tandem MS/MS spectra are available, since class-based MS/MS screening and fragment screening require MS/MS evidence. Targeted quantification of a short list of certified PFAS standards (e.g. PFOA/PFOS-only assays) rather than non-targeted annotation of known, uncommon, and unknown PFAS. http://edamontology.org/topic_3368 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates PFAS features from LC-HRMS/MS acquisitions by running FluoroMatch Modular's non-targeted pipeline (feature detection, blank filtering, class-based MS/MS and fragment screening) and assigning confidence scores, so PFAS MS/MS evidence counts and score A annotations can be tracked across injection rounds (e.g. iterative-exclusion rounds of an AFFF sample). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Annotates PFAS features from LC-HRMS/MS acquisitions by running FluoroMatch Modular's non-targeted pipeline (feature detection, blank filtering, class-based MS/MS and fragment screening) and assigning confidence scores, so PFAS MS/MS evidence counts and score A annotations can be tracked across injection rounds (e.g. iterative-exclusion rounds of an AFFF sample).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated, confidence-scored feature table with per-feature PFAS annotations — re-running annotation would duplicate the scoring step. skills.search_text: pfas-nontargeted-screening Use when processing LC-HRMS/MS feature tables from PFAS discovery samples (e.g., AFFF or environmental extracts) and blanks, needing to separate true PFAS features from background and annotate known, uncommon, and unknown PFAS non-targeted. You already have a curated target list and MS/MS spectra — the original FluoroMatch release's suspect screening approach, not the 2.0 non-targeted workflow, fits that case Your analysis is lipidomics or Tween-related rather than PFAS — toggle Lipid <- TRUE is required for those applications and defaults otherwise to PFAS analysis You need quantification rather than annotation/discovery — the skill covers annotation and filtering, not quantitative calibration Automates the non-targeted PFAS annotation pipeline in FluoroMatch 2.0, from vendor feature-table detection through blank filtering, exact mass matching, mass defect and homologous series filtering, to MS/MS-based annotation with a confidence-level scoring framework. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Automates the non-targeted PFAS annotation pipeline in FluoroMatch 2.0, from vendor feature-table detection through blank filtering, exact mass matching, mass defect and homologous series filtering, to MS/MS-based annotation with a confidence-level scoring framework.

skills.description: Use when fitting PLS/PLS-DA or another supervised classifier on a high-dimensional omics table (e.g., 20,254 genes plus 504 metabolites) and you need a defensible, two-stage significance-plus-influence cutoff to shrink the feature space before refitting.
skills.name: pfdr-multiple-testing-thresholding
skills.search_text: pfdr-multiple-testing-thresholding Use when fitting PLS/PLS-DA or another supervised classifier on a high-dimensional omics table (e.g., 20,254 genes plus 504 metabolites) and you need a defensible, two-stage significance-plus-influence cutoff to shrink the feature space before refitting. When the goal is per-feature hypothesis testing or p-value combination (e.g., multi-study meta-analysis via Pbine) rather than building a predictive classifier When the feature table is already small or pre-filtered, where a pFDR-plus-top-10-VIP cutoff would discard informative variables unnecessarily When the task is untargeted peak detection, annotation, or concentration calibration — these belong to SMART 2.0's other modules, not the classification module http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A two-stage feature-reduction strategy for supervised omics modeling in SMART 2.0: first threshold features by pFDR < 0.05, then retain only the top 10 VIP-ranked variables before refitting a covariate-adjusted PLS/PLS-DA model, which lifted cross-validated Q2Y from 0.55 to 0.701 on the breast cancer gene-expression and metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: A two-stage feature-reduction strategy for supervised omics modeling in SMART 2.0: first threshold features by pFDR < 0.05, then retain only the top 10 VIP-ranked variables before refitting a covariate-adjusted PLS/PLS-DA model, which lifted cross-validated Q2Y from 0.55 to 0.701 on the breast cancer gene-expression and metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is per-feature hypothesis testing or p-value combination (e.g., multi-study meta-analysis via Pbine) rather than building a predictive classifier When the feature table is already small or pre-filtered, where a pFDR-plus-top-10-VIP cutoff would discard informative variables unnecessarily When the task is untargeted peak detection, annotation, or concentration calibration — these belong to SMART 2.0's other modules, not the classification module

skills.description: Use when generating simulated 1D or 2D 1H NMR spectra (e.g. urine J-Res) whose peak positions must track pH variation, or when diagnosing why simulated metabolite peaks misalign with real reference spectra.
skills.name: ph-based-chemical-shift-perturbation
skills.search_text: ph-based-chemical-shift-perturbation Use when generating simulated 1D or 2D 1H NMR spectra (e.g. urine J-Res) whose peak positions must track pH variation, or when diagnosing why simulated metabolite peaks misalign with real reference spectra. You already have real experimental NMR spectra and only need processing/quantification — the perturbation only applies to simulated spectra produced by MetAssimulo 2.0. The matrix of interest is not urine, blood, or cerebral spinal fluid — MetAssimulo 2.0's pH perturbation models these three biological matrices. pH is unknown or poorly constrained for the sample; shifting resonance positions to an arbitrary pH would degrade, not improve, realism. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 A simulation step within MetAssimulo 2.0 in which each metabolite's 1H resonance positions are adjusted according to the sample matrix's pH before synthesising the NMR spectrum, so that simulated urine, blood, or CSF spectra reflect the pH-dependent chemical-shift behaviour observed in real spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf045
skills.summary: A simulation step within MetAssimulo 2.0 in which each metabolite's 1H resonance positions are adjusted according to the sample matrix's pH before synthesising the NMR spectrum, so that simulated urine, blood, or CSF spectra reflect the pH-dependent chemical-shift behaviour observed in real spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have real experimental NMR spectra and only need processing/quantification — the perturbation only applies to simulated spectra produced by MetAssimulo 2.0. The goal is immediate clinical decision-making — the article explicitly states the GNPS Drug Library is 'not intended for immediate clinical decision-making' and only lays groundwork for precision medicine Reliable self-reported medication records already exist and no empirical cross-check or exposure stratification of unannotated metabolites (e.g., N-acyl lipids) is needed Input is still raw LC-MS/MS spectra with no MZmine feature extraction or GNPS Drug Library annotation performed — run feature detection and spectral matching first http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Aggregate GNPS Drug Library spectral-matching drug annotations across individuals in an untargeted metabolomics cohort, tally pharmacologic class frequencies, and test demographic associations (e.g., age and sex) with chi-square tests to empirically establish drug exposure patterns. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5

skills.description: Use when mapbayr and NONMEM produce discordant individual eta estimates (e.g., Runs 3, 4, 6 with lag-time/infusion-duration estimation, large IIV, or dose-related parameters) and you need to determine which estimates have lower OFV.
skills.name: pharmacometric-model-validation
skills.search_text: pharmacometric-model-validation Use when mapbayr and NONMEM produce discordant individual eta estimates (e.g., Runs 3, 4, 6 with lag-time/infusion-duration estimation, large IIV, or dose-related parameters) and you need to determine which estimates have lower OFV. When mapbayr and NONMEM estimates are concordant (98% of test-model estimations were identical), there are no discordant etas to adjudicate via OFV comparison When the goal is to return the true individual parameter value (ηi) — MAP estimation cannot assess this, only likelihood of estimates When a proper run-time or estimation-uncertainty comparison is needed — neither was performed, and current mapbayr versions provide no Fisher-information or posterior-sampling uncertainty quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Validates MAP-Bayesian estimation of pharmacokinetic parameters by comparing mapbayr and NONMEM estimates across simulated profiles, and adjudicates discordant cases by recomputing individual objective function values (OFVi,NM-like) from NONMEM's eta estimates using mapbayr's compute_ofv machinery. This determines which tool found the more likely eta estimates when point estimates diverge. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/psp4.12689
skills.summary: Validates MAP-Bayesian estimation of pharmacokinetic parameters by comparing mapbayr and NONMEM estimates across simulated profiles, and adjudicates discordant cases by recomputing individual objective function values (OFVi,NM-like) from NONMEM's eta estimates using mapbayr's compute_ofv machinery. This determines which tool found the more likely eta estimates when point estimates diverge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When mapbayr and NONMEM estimates are concordant (98% of test-model estimations were identical), there are no discordant etas to adjudicate via OFV comparison When the goal is to return the true individual parameter value (ηi) — MAP estimation cannot assess this, only likelihood of estimates When a proper run-time or estimation-uncertainty comparison is needed — neither was performed, and current mapbayr versions provide no Fisher-information or posterior-sampling uncertainty quantification

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing the per-reaction-type metabolite tally from the PharmMet DB human liver S9 study (ST003991) — e.g. 30,752 oxidations, 6311 glucuronidations — against BioTransformer 3.0 predictions.
skills.name: pharmmet-db-count-validation
skills.search_text: pharmmet-db-count-validation Use when reproducing or auditing the per-reaction-type metabolite tally from the PharmMet DB human liver S9 study (ST003991) — e.g. 30,752 oxidations, 6311 glucuronidations — against BioTransformer 3.0 predictions. The input is raw LC-HRMS mass spectral data rather than curated annotation tables — feature detection (MZmine 2.53, 0-hour vs 24-hour comparison) must run first. The goal is structural elucidation or isolation of novel metabolites; the article notes novel metabolites from nearly 1000 drugs require considerable research beyond the database. The metabolites of interest form in extrahepatic compartments (intestine, kidney) or via enzymes not abundant or active in human liver S9 — PharmMet DB is expected to lack them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Tallies experimentally detected drug metabolites by biotransformation reaction type (oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis, glucuronidation, etc.) from the PharmMet DB human liver S9 annotations (Metabolomics Workbench Study ST003991) and validates each count against the BioTransformer 3.0 predictions reported in the source paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.dmd.2025.100183
skills.summary: Tallies experimentally detected drug metabolites by biotransformation reaction type (oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis, glucuronidation, etc.) from the PharmMet DB human liver S9 annotations (Metabolomics Workbench Study ST003991) and validates each count against the BioTransformer 3.0 predictions reported in the source paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-HRMS mass spectral data rather than curated annotation tables — feature detection (MZmine 2.53, 0-hour vs 24-hour comparison) must run first. skills.description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra requires automated zero- and first-order phase correction and a phase-corrected reference spectrum is available to initialise ph0/ph1.
skills.name: phase-parameter-initialization-from-reference-spectrum
skills.search_text: phase-parameter-initialization-from-reference-spectrum Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra requires automated zero- and first-order phase correction and a phase-corrected reference spectrum is available to initialise ph0/ph1. The reference spectrum itself is not phase-corrected — seeded ph0/ph1 would start the Powell optimisation from a misleading point Spectra lack signal-free baseline regions beyond 10.0 ppm or below −0.5 ppm (e.g. resonances or truncation at the spectral edges), so the baseline-difference objective is meaningless Manual interactive phasing of a single 2D spectrum is needed rather than automated correction of a 1D series Seeds automated phase correction of a 1D-NMR spectral series with zero-order (ph0) and first-order (ph1) values taken from a phase-corrected reference spectrum, then optimises them per spectrum via MetaboLabPy's baseline-minimisation algorithm. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Seeds automated phase correction of a 1D-NMR spectral series with zero-order (ph0) and first-order (ph1) values taken from a phase-corrected reference spectrum, then optimises them per spectrum via MetaboLabPy's baseline-minimisation algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference spectrum itself is not phase-corrected — seeded ph0/ph1 would start the Powell optimisation from a misleading point Spectra lack signal-free baseline regions beyond 10.0 ppm or below −0.5 ppm (e.g. resonances or truncation at the spectral edges), so the baseline-difference objective is meaningless Manual interactive phasing of a single 2D spectrum is needed rather than automated correction of a 1D series

skills.description: Use when a cohort of patients has both an Exomiser-filtered candidate gene list with hiPHIVE phenotype scores and an alternative (e.g., metabolomics-driven) per-gene score, and you need to compare causative-gene ranks per patient.
skills.name: phenotype-based-gene-prioritization-interpretation
skills.search_text: phenotype-based-gene-prioritization-interpretation Use when a cohort of patients has both an Exomiser-filtered candidate gene list with hiPHIVE phenotype scores and an alternative (e.g., metabolomics-driven) per-gene score, and you need to compare causative-gene ranks per patient. The patient has no known/previously diagnosed causative gene — rank comparison against ground truth is not possible (the analysis needs a confirmed diagnosis, as in the 11 TIDEX patients) The candidate list lacks Exomiser hiPHIVE phenotype scores (e.g., only variant-effect/frequency-filtered genes with no phenotype ranking), so the Exomiser-Phenotype rank cannot be computed Feature-to-metabolite mapping is unavailable for the metabolomic system (as for the TIDEX metabolomic platform), which limits interpreting the metabolomics-driven side of the comparison at the metabolite level Per-patient, head-to-head interpretation of Exomiser's hiPHIVE phenotype-driven (Exomiser-Phenotype) candidate gene rankings against a metabolomics-driven ranking such as metPropagate's propagated scores, recording the rank of each patient's known causative gene under both schemes and flagging which tool ranked it higher. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5

skills.description: Use when you have a feature quantification table plus phenotype metadata (e.g. 25 healthy vs 24 caries samples) and need to identify which molecular families or gene clusters are differentially abundant between the two conditions.
skills.name: phenotype-differential-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: phenotype-differential-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a feature quantification table plus phenotype metadata (e.g. 25 healthy vs 24 caries samples) and need to identify which molecular families or gene clusters are differentially abundant between the two conditions. Input is already a single-family or single-metabolite table with no phenotype grouping — set-based enrichment scoring is unnecessary; use per-feature differential testing instead Samples lack phenotype/condition metadata — PALS scoring requires phenotype labels to compute set activity per condition The goal is BGC discovery from genomes rather than differential abundance profiling across metagenomic samples — use antiSMASH/gutSMASH directly instead of the enrichment workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A set-based differential enrichment workflow that tests whether molecular families (from Feature-Based Molecular Networking) or metabolic gene clusters are enriched in one phenotype versus another, e.g. healthy vs caries-associated oral samples, using PALS activity scoring and BiG-MAP differential abundance testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single-family or single-metabolite table with no phenotype grouping — set-based enrichment scoring is unnecessary; use per-feature differential testing instead Samples lack phenotype/condition metadata — PALS scoring requires phenotype labels to compute set activity per condition The goal is BGC discovery from genomes rather than differential abundance profiling across metagenomic samples — use antiSMASH/gutSMASH directly instead of the enrichment workflow

skills.description: Use when a chemical hierarchy (Qemistree Newick/Phylogeny[Rooted]) exists for the MS1 features and the goal is to quantify sample dissimilarity in a way that accounts for chemical relatedness of features, e.g., batch-effect mitigation or food-ontology clustering.
skills.name: phylogenetic-beta-diversity-computation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-beta-diversity-computation Use when a chemical hierarchy (Qemistree Newick/Phylogeny[Rooted]) exists for the MS1 features and the goal is to quantify sample dissimilarity in a way that accounts for chemical relatedness of features, e.g., batch-effect mitigation or food-ontology clustering. skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature set contains only MS1 features without predicted fingerprints — MS1-only features are filtered out and cannot be placed on the hierarchy No chemical hierarchy tree has been built (use qiime qemistree make-hierarchy from fingerprint predictions first) The goal is spectral-library annotation coverage rather than sample-level dissimilarity — annotations from spectral matches alone cover typically 1-20% of features, too low to summarize sample chemistry

skills.description: Use when GCF clustering (e.g., BiG-SCAPE) may have omitted or misassigned related BGCs due to fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters, and you need a query-gene-rooted phylogeny to recover them.
skills.name: phylogenetic-clade-resolution-validation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-clade-resolution-validation Use when GCF clustering (e.g., BiG-SCAPE) may have omitted or misassigned related BGCs due to fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters, and you need a query-gene-rooted phylogeny to recover them. BGCs are so divergent that the conserved core collapses to only the query gene — without a multi-locus alignment the output BGCs are drawn but not sorted, so clade validation is meaningless The goal is global GCF/GCC assignment by pairwise domain-content distance rather than evolutionary resolution within one family — BiG-SCAPE (Jaccard/domain-sequence/adjacency distances, Affinity Propagation) is the appropriate tool The alignment comes out empty and reducing the hmmer score cutoff or taxonomic scope of the genomic database is not acceptable for the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Builds a high-resolution multi-locus phylogeny of BGCs sharing a query gene with CORASON (all-vs-all best bidirectional hits → hmmalign domain alignment → FastTree) and validates the result by qualitative clade resolution rather than numeric cutoffs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Builds a high-resolution multi-locus phylogeny of BGCs sharing a query gene with CORASON (all-vs-all best bidirectional hits → hmmalign domain alignment → FastTree) and validates the result by qualitative clade resolution rather than numeric cutoffs.

skills.search_text: phylum-level-taxonomic-clade-inspection Use when comparing a taxonomic profiler's output against a ground-truth CAMI profile and you need to identify which specific clades (e.g., at class/phylum rank) are discordantly present or absent between the two profiles. Input is a single profiler profile with no gold-standard comparison available — contrast mode and false-positive/false-negative calling require a ground-truth profile The analysis goal is a global single-value benchmark score (e.g., F1, UniFrac) rather than clade-level biological interpretation — use a benchmarking platform like OPAL instead Amplicon (16S) microbial data — TAMPA's WGS metagenomic profile visualization is not designed for amplicon analyses (cf. metacoder's limitation) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Inspect phylum/class-level clades in a taxonomic profiler output versus a gold-standard CAMI2 marine profile using TAMPA's contrast mode, to surface biological divergences (e.g., missed Planctomycetes and Tenericutes) that single-value metrics such as the F1 score cannot reveal. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008

skills.description: Use when computing per-pathway functional similarity (SimPi) for two KEGG organisms and a reference pathway is missing from one organism or has no reactions in either, requiring special-case values instead of a Jaccard ratio.
skills.name: physical-vs-reaction-pathway-case-handling
skills.search_text: physical-vs-reaction-pathway-case-handling Use when computing per-pathway functional similarity (SimPi) for two KEGG organisms and a reference pathway is missing from one organism or has no reactions in either, requiring special-case values instead of a Jaccard ratio. The pathway is present in both organisms and contains reactions — then the plain Jaccard index |Ri∩Ri′|/|Ri∪Ri′| applies and no special case is triggered Computing the structural-level index SimSi — it has a different case rule set (1/(1+k) for isolated-vs-connected nodes) and must not reuse SimPi's 0/1 defaults Input networks were not reconstructed from KEGG KGML data — the reference-pathway decomposition underpinning the case handling is KEGG-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Handles the degenerate pathway cases MetNet's functional similarity index SimPi must distinguish — pathways present in only one organism, and pathways present in both but containing no reactions ('physical' pathways) — assigning SimPi=0 and SimPi=1 respectively before Jaccard computation on reaction sets/multisets. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Handles the degenerate pathway cases MetNet's functional similarity index SimPi must distinguish — pathways present in only one organism, and pathways present in both but containing no reactions ('physical' pathways) — assigning SimPi=0 and SimPi=1 respectively before Jaccard computation on reaction sets/multisets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway is present in both organisms and contains reactions — then the plain Jaccard index |Ri∩Ri′|/|Ri∪Ri′| applies and no special case is triggered Computing the structural-level index SimSi — it has a different case rule set (1/(1+k) for isolated-vs-connected nodes) and must not reuse SimPi's 0/1 defaults Input networks were not reconstructed from KEGG KGML data — the reference-pathway decomposition underpinning the case handling is KEGG-specific

skills.description: Use when a generated reaction network (e.g. from Pickaxe) must be pruned by thermodynamic feasibility before downstream pathway design or metabolomics annotation, so likely-impossible reactions are excluded on a per-reaction basis.
skills.name: physiological-gibbs-free-energy-computation
skills.search_text: physiological-gibbs-free-energy-computation Use when a generated reaction network (e.g. from Pickaxe) must be pruned by thermodynamic feasibility before downstream pathway design or metabolomics annotation, so likely-impossible reactions are excluded on a per-reaction basis. If the reaction network is already filtered by DeepRFC or another feasibility method and thermodynamic pruning is not required. If the input reactions fall outside eQuilibrator's prediction scope so no ΔG can be computed and the filter cannot comment on their feasibility. If the reaction set has not been generated by Pickaxe or stored in a MongoDB database the workflow can query. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Computes the physiological Gibbs free energy (ΔG) of each generated reaction using eQuilibrator-api, flagging reactions whose ΔG exceeds 50 kJ/mol as thermodynamically infeasible; un-computable ΔG values are recorded and the corresponding reactions retained. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05149-8
skills.summary: Computes the physiological Gibbs free energy (ΔG) of each generated reaction using eQuilibrator-api, flagging reactions whose ΔG exceeds 50 kJ/mol as thermodynamically infeasible; un-computable ΔG values are recorded and the corresponding reactions retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the reaction network is already filtered by DeepRFC or another feasibility method and thermodynamic pruning is not required. If the reaction set has not been generated by Pickaxe or stored in a MongoDB database the workflow can query.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or re-implementing the coarse RT correction of DeepRTAlign — piecewise per-1-min-window shift estimation against an anchor sample — before deep-learning direct matching of LC-MS features.
skills.name: piecewise-rt-shift-correction
skills.search_text: piecewise-rt-shift-correction Use when reproducing or re-implementing the coarse RT correction of DeepRTAlign — piecewise per-1-min-window shift estimation against an anchor sample — before deep-learning direct matching of LC-MS features. Input is raw LC-MS data (e.g. mzML or Thermo RAW) rather than a feature list — the coarse alignment consumes feature lists from Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder or TXT/CSV, so run feature extraction first You need final aligned feature groups with QC scores — the coarse step alone produces no group names or alignment scores; run the full DeepRTAlign pipeline (steps 3-6 including direct matching and FDR QC) Single-run data with no RT shifts across samples — piecewise shift estimation against an anchor sample is meaningless without multiple samples, since correspondence mapping applies to experiments involving multiple samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs DeepRTAlign's coarse alignment step (step 2 of 6, the 'pseudo warping function'): every sample is compared piecewise against a designated anchor sample and the average RT shift per time-window piece is added to each feature in that piece, correcting RT shifts before the deep-learning-based direct matching model. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Reconstructs DeepRTAlign's coarse alignment step (step 2 of 6, the 'pseudo warping function'): every sample is compared piecewise against a designated anchor sample and the average RT shift per time-window piece is added to each feature in that piece, correcting RT shifts before the deep-learning-based direct matching model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data (e.g. mzML or Thermo RAW) rather than a feature list — the coarse alignment consumes feature lists from Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder or TXT/CSV, so run feature extraction first You need final aligned feature groups with QC scores — the coarse step alone produces no group names or alignment scores; run the full DeepRTAlign pipeline (steps 3-6 including direct matching and FDR QC) Single-run data with no RT shifts across samples — piecewise shift estimation against an anchor sample is meaningless without multiple samples, since correspondence mapping applies to experiments involving multiple samples

Input data lacks pixel X/Y coordinates (e.g., bulk LC-MS feature tables) — the quadrat test on spatial intensity patterns cannot be computed The goal is removing background pixels rather than noise ions — SMQVP's Background Noise Removal module is the appropriate step Very few pixels per ion or already cluster-validated ion lists — the CSR test is designed to flag randomly distributed signals and may not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A noise-ion filtering method for spatial metabolomics that scores each ion's spatial pattern across pixels using the spatstat quadrat test for Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR), converts the p-value to a noise score (-log10), and removes ions with scores below a threshold (90 in the SMQVP mouse-brain example). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354

skills.search_text: poisson-noise-modeling Use when generating augmented views of MSI ion images for self-supervised/contrastive training and you need the augmentation to reflect the Poisson distribution of ion counts; also relevant when simulating count-noise on ion images. The input is not MSI ion-image data with count-like (non-negative integer-scale) abundances — Poisson noise assumes count-based ion detection. You are building the ISO-mode T_ISO pipeline and need the intensity-dependent missing-value step — that operation is additive to, not a replacement for, Poisson noise and belongs to a different modality. The goal is general natural-image augmentation without MSI-specific priors — plain color jitter/filtering suffices and Poisson noise would be unmotivated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Applies Poisson-distributed noise to ion images from mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data, as used in DeepION's data augmentation module to emulate the count-based, Poisson-distributed nature of ion abundance detection before contrastive training. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002

The goal is general natural-image augmentation without MSI-specific priors — plain color jitter/filtering suffices and Poisson noise would be unmotivated.

skills.description: Use when you need a labeled synthetic mass-spectrometry benchmark with controlled noise density (e.g. to compute ROC curves for signal-vs-noise classifiers like LSH vs. intensity thresholding) and no real-data peak-level ground truth exists.
skills.name: poisson-noise-peak-sampling
skills.search_text: poisson-noise-peak-sampling Use when you need a labeled synthetic mass-spectrometry benchmark with controlled noise density (e.g. to compute ROC curves for signal-vs-noise classifiers like LSH vs. intensity thresholding) and no real-data peak-level ground truth exists. The goal is to evaluate classification on real timsTOF raw data — the article notes synthetic data cannot fully reflect real-data behavior and no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real data was available. The downstream task requires removing peaks inside signal windows: the synthetic noise_2 class (noise within signal windows) is explicitly not removed by the LSH approach and was excluded from classification-rate computation. You need to model chemical/contaminant noise that is self-similar across windows — such noise would be misclassified as true signal by the LSH method and is not captured by this stochastic noise model. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Stochastic generation of synthetic background-noise peaks for a timsTOF-style benchmark: per-window peak counts are drawn from a Poisson(4)+1 distribution and intensities from an exponential distribution with parameter 15, then labeled noise_1/noise_2 alongside averagine-modeled signal peaks so LSH classification can be evaluated against ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-022-04833-5
skills.summary: Stochastic generation of synthetic background-noise peaks for a timsTOF-style benchmark: per-window peak counts are drawn from a Poisson(4)+1 distribution and intensities from an exponential distribution with parameter 15, then labeled noise_1/noise_2 alongside averagine-modeled signal peaks so LSH classification can be evaluated against ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate classification on real timsTOF raw data — the article notes synthetic data cannot fully reflect real-data behavior and no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real data was available. The downstream task requires removing peaks inside signal windows: the synthetic noise_2 class (noise within signal windows) is explicitly not removed by the LSH approach and was excluded from classification-rate computation. You need to model chemical/contaminant noise that is self-similar across windows — such noise would be misclassified as true signal by the LSH method and is not captured by this stochastic noise model.

Data acquisition is already complete — this skill designs the experimental run order before acquisition and cannot retrofit replicates onto existing runs The downstream normalization does not rely on embedded sample replicates (e.g. methods that assume pooled QCs are identical over extended periods without inter-batch replicates) Plate format or run length differs substantially from 96-well/10-run spacing without re-deriving QC spacing and replicate counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Generates the hRUV replicate arrangement for a 96-well plate batch layout: three pooled QC samples in the first wells, one pooled QC after every 10 runs, one short replicate per row, and 5 batch replicates from the previous plate — enabling within- and between-batch unwanted variation estimation for large-scale metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Generates the hRUV replicate arrangement for a 96-well plate batch layout: three pooled QC samples in the first wells, one pooled QC after every 10 runs, one short replicate per row, and 5 batch replicates from the previous plate — enabling within- and between-batch unwanted variation estimation for large-scale metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data acquisition is already complete — this skill designs the experimental run order before acquisition and cannot retrofit replicates onto existing runs The downstream normalization does not rely on embedded sample replicates (e.g. methods that assume pooled QCs are identical over extended periods without inter-batch replicates) Plate format or run length differs substantially from 96-well/10-run spacing without re-deriving QC spacing and replicate counts

skills.description: Use when a post-extraction untargeted metabolomics feature table (e.g. from XCMS, patRoon or MS-DIAL) contains blank, pooled QC and diluted-QC (QC_half) sample groups and unreliable features must be removed before statistics.
skills.name: pooled-qc-feature-filtration
skills.search_text: pooled-qc-feature-filtration Use when a post-extraction untargeted metabolomics feature table (e.g. from XCMS, patRoon or MS-DIAL) contains blank, pooled QC and diluted-QC (QC_half) sample groups and unreliable features must be removed before statistics. Input is raw mass-spectrometry data — feature extraction must be done first with tools such as XCMS (or patRoon/MS-DIAL feature-table export) before QC filtration Targeted metabolomics quantification requiring calibration curves — this skill only covers pooled-QC-based feature filtration for untargeted feature tables The dataset contains no pooled QC, blank and diluted-QC (QC_half) injections, so the four QC criteria cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Filter untargeted metabolomics features using pooled quality control criteria via the GetFeatistics QCs_process function, which removes features failing QC reproducibility (CV%), detection frequency, blank/QC intensity ratio, and dilution-response (QC vs QC_half) checks, optionally per sample-group QC pool. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Filter untargeted metabolomics features using pooled quality control criteria via the GetFeatistics QCs_process function, which removes features failing QC reproducibility (CV%), detection frequency, blank/QC intensity ratio, and dilution-response (QC vs QC_half) checks, optionally per sample-group QC pool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mass-spectrometry data — feature extraction must be done first with tools such as XCMS (or patRoon/MS-DIAL feature-table export) before QC filtration Targeted metabolomics quantification requiring calibration curves — this skill only covers pooled-QC-based feature filtration for untargeted feature tables The dataset contains no pooled QC, blank and diluted-QC (QC_half) injections, so the four QC criteria cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when an LC–MS feature table (e.g. CSV from TidyMS or MZmine2/XCMS/MSDIAL) contains time-ordered pooled/intrastudy QC injections and study samples whose intensities show signal drift that must be corrected before statistical analysis.
skills.name: pooled-qc-signal-drift-correction
skills.search_text: pooled-qc-signal-drift-correction Use when an LC–MS feature table (e.g. CSV from TidyMS or MZmine2/XCMS/MSDIAL) contains time-ordered pooled/intrastudy QC injections and study samples whose intensities show signal drift that must be corrected before statistical analysis. The feature table has not yet passed the upstream filters (Rt filter ≥ 90 s, presence in pooled/intrastudy QC, 10-fold blank-based area filter, RSD ≤ 20% in pooled/intrastudy QC, 100% intraclass prevalence with area threshold 5, D-ratio < 10%) — correction on unfiltered data reintroduces non-robust features. There are no pooled/intrastudy QC injections in the run, so no time-ordered reference series exists to fit the LOESS smoother. The goal is feature annotation or de novo peak picking rather than post-extraction data curation — TidyMS is noted as lacking feature annotation capability. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Applies a LOESS smoother fitted on pooled/intrastudy QC sample injections (via TidyMS + statsmodels) to remove time-related systematic variance (signal drift) from LC–MS feature intensities in study samples, outputting a batch-corrected data matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Applies a LOESS smoother fitted on pooled/intrastudy QC sample injections (via TidyMS + statsmodels) to remove time-related systematic variance (signal drift) from LC–MS feature intensities in study samples, outputting a batch-corrected data matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has not yet passed the upstream filters (Rt filter ≥ 90 s, presence in pooled/intrastudy QC, 10-fold blank-based area filter, RSD ≤ 20% in pooled/intrastudy QC, 100% intraclass prevalence with area threshold 5, D-ratio < 10%) — correction on unfiltered data reintroduces non-robust features. There are no pooled/intrastudy QC injections in the run, so no time-ordered reference series exists to fit the LOESS smoother. The goal is feature annotation or de novo peak picking rather than post-extraction data curation — TidyMS is noted as lacking feature annotation capability.

skills.description: Use when processing untargeted LC-MS/MS raw spectral data (e.g. mzML/mzData) that includes pooled-QC MS2 acquisitions — especially SWATH-DIA runs — and you need to verify MS2 spectral quality and assign compound identities.
skills.name: pooled-qc-spectral-quality-check
skills.search_text: pooled-qc-spectral-quality-check Use when processing untargeted LC-MS/MS raw spectral data (e.g. mzML/mzData) that includes pooled-QC MS2 acquisitions — especially SWATH-DIA runs — and you need to verify MS2 spectral quality and assign compound identities. Input is already a processed feature table — this skill operates on raw MS/MS spectra and pooled-QC acquisitions, not on quantified peak tables The dataset contains no pooled-QC (or other) MS2 spectra, so no spectral quality check or MS2-based identification is possible Targeted metabolomics where identities and transitions are predefined and MS2 database deconvolution adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Leverages tandem MS (MS2) spectra acquired on pooled QC samples to check spectral quality and support compound identification in untargeted LC-MS metabolomics, using MetaboAnalyst 6.0/MetaboAnalystR 4.0's MS/MS deconvolution and annotation module against a ~1.5 million MS2 spectra database. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Leverages tandem MS (MS2) spectra acquired on pooled QC samples to check spectral quality and support compound identification in untargeted LC-MS metabolomics, using MetaboAnalyst 6.0/MetaboAnalystR 4.0's MS/MS deconvolution and annotation module against a ~1.5 million MS2 spectra database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table — this skill operates on raw MS/MS spectra and pooled-QC acquisitions, not on quantified peak tables The dataset contains no pooled-QC (or other) MS2 spectra, so no spectral quality check or MS2-based identification is possible Targeted metabolomics where identities and transitions are predefined and MS2 database deconvolution adds no value

skills.description: Use when you need simulated concentration-time profiles from a population PK model (e.g. 4000 profiles per model combining single/multiple dosing and rich/sparse sampling) to validate estimation tools or explore dosing scenarios.
skills.name: population-pk-model-simulation
skills.search_text: population-pk-model-simulation Use when you need simulated concentration-time profiles from a population PK model (e.g. 4000 profiles per model combining single/multiple dosing and rich/sparse sampling) to validate estimation tools or explore dosing scenarios. When the goal is estimating individual parameters from observed concentrations — use MAP-Bayesian estimation (mapbayest()) instead, simulation only supports it When model-based design optimality is required — the article points to dedicated software (PFIM or PopED), not plain mrgsolve simulation When the model cannot be expressed in mrgsolve's ODE framework (the README notes C++ compilers/Rtools are required) http://edamontology.org/topic_3390 http://edamontology.org/topic_3070 Simulate PK profiles from user-defined population pharmacokinetic models coded in mrgsolve, optionally using MAP-Bayesian-estimated individual parameters (ETA) to generate concentration-time predictions for validation or MIPD scenarios. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/psp4.12689
skills.summary: Simulate PK profiles from user-defined population pharmacokinetic models coded in mrgsolve, optionally using MAP-Bayesian-estimated individual parameters (ETA) to generate concentration-time predictions for validation or MIPD scenarios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is estimating individual parameters from observed concentrations — use MAP-Bayesian estimation (mapbayest()) instead, simulation only supports it When model-based design optimality is required — the article points to dedicated software (PFIM or PopED), not plain mrgsolve simulation When the model cannot be expressed in mrgsolve's ODE framework (the README notes C++ compilers/Rtools are required)

skills.description: Use when re-analyzing positive ion mode LC–MS/MS metabolomics data and you need MZmine3 feature tables plus SIRIUS formula/adduct assignments (e.g., replicating the cultured-vs-conventional meat study).
skills.name: positive-ion-mode-spectra-handling
skills.search_text: positive-ion-mode-spectra-handling Use when re-analyzing positive ion mode LC–MS/MS metabolomics data and you need MZmine3 feature tables plus SIRIUS formula/adduct assignments (e.g., replicating the cultured-vs-conventional meat study). The acquisition or evaluation concerns negative ion mode data — the article's meat-study evaluation explicitly focuses on the positive ion mode data only. The feature table already carries SIRIUS formula/adduct assignments; re-running assignment would be redundant and could shift the expected 866/900 count. The goal is ranking candidate structures for individual or consensus spectra (MVP/MassSpecGym retrieval) rather than producing feature-level formula/adduct assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Skill for the article's positive ion mode LC–MS/MS handling chain: MZmine3 feature extraction and representative spectra selection, followed by SIRIUS v6.1.0 formula and adduct assignment, turning raw mzML into a per-feature assignment table (866 of 900 meat-study features assigned). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.688047
skills.summary: Skill for the article's positive ion mode LC–MS/MS handling chain: MZmine3 feature extraction and representative spectra selection, followed by SIRIUS v6.1.0 formula and adduct assignment, turning raw mzML into a per-feature assignment table (866 of 900 meat-study features assigned).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The acquisition or evaluation concerns negative ion mode data — the article's meat-study evaluation explicitly focuses on the positive ion mode data only. The feature table already carries SIRIUS formula/adduct assignments; re-running assignment would be redundant and could shift the expected 866/900 count. The goal is ranking candidate structures for individual or consensus spectra (MVP/MassSpecGym retrieval) rather than producing feature-level formula/adduct assignments.

skills.description: Use when constructing an augmented training corpus for a Siamese/CNN compound-identification model from a library of pure-component spectra: pairs of spectra with matching vs. differing compound compositions must be synthesized before training pSCNN.
skills.name: positive-negative-pair-generation
skills.search_text: positive-negative-pair-generation Use when constructing an augmented training corpus for a Siamese/CNN compound-identification model from a library of pure-component spectra: pairs of spectra with matching vs. differing compound compositions must be synthesized before training pSCNN. The goal is benchmarking pSCNN on real experimental data (flavor mixtures or additional flavor mixture datasets) rather than synthesizing training pairs — use the experimental datasets directly instead. Input spectra are already paired or labeled training examples; regeneration of synthetic pairs would duplicate existing augmentation. A target compound's pure-standard spectrum is absent from the database, since negative pairs are defined by omitting that compound's spectrum. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates the positive and negative NMR spectral pairs used to train, validate and test the pSCNN model by superposing flavor-standard database spectra at random mixing ratios (0.2–1.0) with random noise, so that the Siamese network can learn compound identification despite chemical shift variation and peak overlap. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Generates the positive and negative NMR spectral pairs used to train, validate and test the pSCNN model by superposing flavor-standard database spectra at random mixing ratios (0.2–1.0) with random noise, so that the Siamese network can learn compound identification despite chemical shift variation and peak overlap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is benchmarking pSCNN on real experimental data (flavor mixtures or additional flavor mixture datasets) rather than synthesizing training pairs — use the experimental datasets directly instead. Input spectra are already paired or labeled training examples; regeneration of synthetic pairs would duplicate existing augmentation. A target compound's pure-standard spectrum is absent from the database, since negative pairs are defined by omitting that compound's spectrum.

skills.description: Use when ZODIAC Gibbs sampling (ten parallel chains, 1,000 burn-in + 2,000 sampling epochs) has run on a compound–candidate formula similarity graph and you need per-compound posterior probabilities for every SIRIUS formula candidate.
skills.name: posterior-marginal-aggregation
skills.search_text: posterior-marginal-aggregation Use when ZODIAC Gibbs sampling (ten parallel chains, 1,000 burn-in + 2,000 sampling epochs) has run on a compound–candidate formula similarity graph and you need per-compound posterior probabilities for every SIRIUS formula candidate. You only need SIRIUS's own top-1 formula annotation and are not doing network-based reranking of the top 50 candidates Compounds are isolated in the ZODIAC similarity network (no pairwise-score edges), so Gibbs marginals would largely mirror the raw SIRIUS candidate scores You are analyzing raw mzML/mzXML spectra or computing fragmentation trees — this skill operates downstream, on ZODIAC's Gibbs samples, not on spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates thinned Gibbs-sampler states from ZODIAC's parallel Markov chains into per-compound posterior marginals over SIRIUS molecular formula candidates, so reranked formula probabilities (not just a top-1 pick) can be inspected, thresholded, or propagated downstream. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Aggregates thinned Gibbs-sampler states from ZODIAC's parallel Markov chains into per-compound posterior marginals over SIRIUS molecular formula candidates, so reranked formula probabilities (not just a top-1 pick) can be inspected, thresholded, or propagated downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need SIRIUS's own top-1 formula annotation and are not doing network-based reranking of the top 50 candidates Compounds are isolated in the ZODIAC similarity network (no pairwise-score edges), so Gibbs marginals would largely mirror the raw SIRIUS candidate scores You are analyzing raw mzML/mzXML spectra or computing fragmentation trees — this skill operates downstream, on ZODIAC's Gibbs samples, not on spectra
