skills.search_text: posterior-probability-confidence-ranking Use when merged GCxGC/TOF-MS peak lists (e.g. 76 merged peaks per replicate run) must be assigned to reference-library metabolites and ranked by posterior confidence to produce an identification table. The goal is biomarker discovery with fdr2d control rather than metabolite identification — MetPC treats these as separate pipeline stages Input data has not yet been preprocessed and peaks have not been merged across the replicate runs No reference metabolite library is available to provide candidate spectra for matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Ranks candidate metabolite assignments by the posterior confidence measure computed from a hierarchical statistical model fitted with the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, so that the metabolites most likely to exist in a sample (e.g. the top-20 of a 35-compound GCxGC/TOF-MS mixture) can be reported with per-metabolite confidence values. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9050103
skills.summary: Ranks candidate metabolite assignments by the posterior confidence measure computed from a hierarchical statistical model fitted with the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, so that the metabolites most likely to exist in a sample (e.g. the top-20 of a 35-compound GCxGC/TOF-MS mixture) can be reported with per-metabolite confidence values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biomarker discovery with fdr2d control rather than metabolite identification — MetPC treats these as separate pipeline stages Input data has not yet been preprocessed and peaks have not been merged across the replicate runs No reference metabolite library is available to provide candidate spectra for matching

skills.description: Use when an identifier-mapping workflow repeatedly resolves metabolite identifiers across HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem and LIPID MAPS and needs a local cache to avoid redundant HTTP fetches.
skills.name: postgresql-cache-database-querying
skills.search_text: postgresql-cache-database-querying Use when an identifier-mapping workflow repeatedly resolves metabolite identifiers across HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem and LIPID MAPS and needs a local cache to avoid redundant HTTP fetches. The task only needs a single one-off identifier lookup and no repeated resolution — direct API calls to KEGG/PubChem may suffice without building the cache The metabolites of interest lie outside the five supported small compound databases (HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG, LIPID MAPS), e.g. METLIN-only identifiers http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Construct and query a local PostgreSQL cache database that underlies MetaFetcheR, storing HMDB, ChEBI and LIPID MAPS records from downloaded dump files via bulk insertion and accumulating KEGG and PubChem instances cached on the fly through HTTP calls. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.02.28.433248
skills.summary: Construct and query a local PostgreSQL cache database that underlies MetaFetcheR, storing HMDB, ChEBI and LIPID MAPS records from downloaded dump files via bulk insertion and accumulating KEGG and PubChem instances cached on the fly through HTTP calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task only needs a single one-off identifier lookup and no repeated resolution — direct API calls to KEGG/PubChem may suffice without building the cache The metabolites of interest lie outside the five supported small compound databases (HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, KEGG, LIPID MAPS), e.g. METLIN-only identifiers

skills.description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra needs automated ph0/ph1 phase correction and a phase-corrected reference spectrum is available to seed the optimisation.
skills.name: powell-conjugate-direction-optimization
skills.search_text: powell-conjugate-direction-optimization Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra needs automated ph0/ph1 phase correction and a phase-corrected reference spectrum is available to seed the optimisation. Input is 2D-NMR or GC-MS / isotopomer data, which is handled by other MetaboLabPy/metabolabpytools routines (e.g. isotopomer analysis from HSQC multiplet and GC-MS data) A phase-corrected reference spectrum is not available, so initial ph0/ph1 values cannot be seeded from it Manual/interactive phase correction by visual inspection is required instead of automated correction Automatic phase correction of 1D-NMR spectra series in MetaboLabPy: zero- and first-order phases are optimised per spectrum by minimising the absolute difference between baseline edge regions (>10.0 ppm and <−0.5 ppm) using Powell's conjugate direction method from scipy.optimize. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Automatic phase correction of 1D-NMR spectra series in MetaboLabPy: zero- and first-order phases are optimised per spectrum by minimising the absolute difference between baseline edge regions (>10.0 ppm and <−0.5 ppm) using Powell's conjugate direction method from scipy.optimize.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 2D-NMR or GC-MS / isotopomer data, which is handled by other MetaboLabPy/metabolabpytools routines (e.g. isotopomer analysis from HSQC multiplet and GC-MS data) A phase-corrected reference spectrum is not available, so initial ph0/ph1 values cannot be seeded from it Manual/interactive phase correction by visual inspection is required instead of automated correction

skills.description: Use when you have TWIM-MS arrival times from calibrant mixtures (e.g., Waters Major Mix IMS/Tof Calibration Kit, Agilent ESI-L Tune Mix) plus reference DTCCSN2 values, and need accurate CCS calibration of unknown features without prior identification.
skills.name: power-law-calibration-curve-fitting
skills.search_text: power-law-calibration-curve-fitting Use when you have TWIM-MS arrival times from calibrant mixtures (e.g., Waters Major Mix IMS/Tof Calibration Kit, Agilent ESI-L Tune Mix) plus reference DTCCSN2 values, and need accurate CCS calibration of unknown features without prior identification. Data acquired in negative ionization mode — MOCCal is not yet extended to negative ionization mode data sets Chemical classes outside small molecules, lipids, and peptides (e.g., other endogenous or xenobiotic classes) on TWIM-MS platforms Drift-tube or trapped IM instruments — the power law formulation and arrival-time terminology are specific to traveling wave IM-MS http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fits class-specific power law calibration curves (small molecule, lipid, peptide) relating TWIM arrival times to drift-tube DTCCSN2 reference values, as implemented in MOCCal, so that each unknown feature on a Waters SYNAPT XS-type TWIM-MS platform can be calibrated with the structurally matched equation rather than a single global curve. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04290
skills.summary: Fits class-specific power law calibration curves (small molecule, lipid, peptide) relating TWIM arrival times to drift-tube DTCCSN2 reference values, as implemented in MOCCal, so that each unknown feature on a Waters SYNAPT XS-type TWIM-MS platform can be calibrated with the structurally matched equation rather than a single global curve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data acquired in negative ionization mode — MOCCal is not yet extended to negative ionization mode data sets Chemical classes outside small molecules, lipids, and peptides (e.g., other endogenous or xenobiotic classes) on TWIM-MS platforms Drift-tube or trapped IM instruments — the power law formulation and arrival-time terminology are specific to traveling wave IM-MS

skills.description: Use when a built microbial or multi-omics co-occurrence network (e.g., Spearman |ρ|>0.6, BH-adjusted edges) must be checked for scale-free topology by fitting its degree distribution to a power law.
skills.name: power-law-degree-distribution-fitting
skills.search_text: power-law-degree-distribution-fitting Use when a built microbial or multi-omics co-occurrence network (e.g., Spearman |ρ|>0.6, BH-adjusted edges) must be checked for scale-free topology by fitting its degree distribution to a power law. Networks built from curated reference databases (e.g., STRING, KEGG hybrid networks) rather than correlation-based construction, where a scale-free degree assumption may not hold Datasets too small or over-filtered, where the degree distribution after thresholding (e.g., >10% prevalence plus |ρ|>0.6) is too sparse to support a meaningful power-law fit When the goal is module/hub role classification (zp_analyse/zp_plot) rather than verifying global topology http://edamontology.org/topic_1317 Verify that a constructed omics co-occurrence network is scale-free by fitting a power law to its degree distribution with MetaNet's fit_power, alongside global topological indices computed via net_par. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.06.26.661636
skills.summary: Verify that a constructed omics co-occurrence network is scale-free by fitting a power law to its degree distribution with MetaNet's fit_power, alongside global topological indices computed via net_par.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Networks built from curated reference databases (e.g., STRING, KEGG hybrid networks) rather than correlation-based construction, where a scale-free degree assumption may not hold Datasets too small or over-filtered, where the degree distribution after thresholding (e.g., >10% prevalence plus |ρ|>0.6) is too sparse to support a meaningful power-law fit When the goal is module/hub role classification (zp_analyse/zp_plot) rather than verifying global topology

skills.description: Use when reimplementing or refactoring SMITER noise injection (e.g. UniformNoiseInjector-style injectors) and you need to verify that an intensity-dependent noise sigma (power-law m*i^{-y} or saturating form) reproduces published parameters and behaves monotonically.
skills.name: power-law-parameter-unit-testing
skills.search_text: power-law-parameter-unit-testing Use when reimplementing or refactoring SMITER noise injection (e.g. UniformNoiseInjector-style injectors) and you need to verify that an intensity-dependent noise sigma (power-law m*i^{-y} or saturating form) reproduces published parameters and behaves monotonically. The goal is to run an end-to-end SMITER LC-MS/MS simulation and write mzML output via smiter.synthetic_mzml.write_mzml rather than to validate noise-model parameters in isolation. The target noise model is intensity-independent (e.g. pure uniform noise injection), where sigma bounds and monotonic intensity dependence do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Implement SMITER's intensity-specific noise models as a standalone Python module and validate their parameters with pytest unit tests, asserting the bounds and monotonic behavior of sigma vs. intensity. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/genes12030396
skills.summary: Implement SMITER's intensity-specific noise models as a standalone Python module and validate their parameters with pytest unit tests, asserting the bounds and monotonic behavior of sigma vs. intensity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to run an end-to-end SMITER LC-MS/MS simulation and write mzML output via smiter.synthetic_mzml.write_mzml rather than to validate noise-model parameters in isolation. The target noise model is intensity-independent (e.g. pure uniform noise injection), where sigma bounds and monotonic intensity dependence do not apply.

skills.search_text: power-law-regression-fit-assessment Use when drift time data from IMS calibrants with known CCS values (e.g. Agilent 6560 tune mix in positive/negative ESI mode) must be regressed to obtain beta and tfix and the fit must be quantified. Fit quality is quantified per ionization mode with a correlation coefficient and sum of residuals. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Fit and assess the quality of a power-law collision cross section (CCS) calibration that yields beta and tfix coefficients from drift-tube/trapped IMS data, using known-CCS calibrants such as the Agilent tune mix. Fit quality is quantified per ionization mode with a correlation coefficient and sum of residuals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw (non-peak-picked) IMS file — the tune mix calibrants must first be processed via peak detection or manual exploration of the data The instrument's calibrants lack known reference CCS values, so no calibrant-to-CCS pairing can be built The task is generic feature detection, alignment, or MS/MS deconvolution rather than CCS calibration fit assessment

skills.search_text: power-law-regression-parameter-selection Use when processing Waters SYNAPT XS TWIM calibration data — e.g. Major Mix, SPLASH Lipidomix, or Agilent Tune Mix — to derive class-specific calibration parameters for later CCS assignment. skills.summary: Fit class-specific power law CCS calibration curves (small molecule, lipid, peptide) by regressing calibrant arrival time against reference DTCCSN2 values, yielding the parameters used by MOCCal to convert TWIM arrival times into calibrated TWCCSN2 values.

skills.description: Use when you have an experimentally derived host–pathogen PPI dataset and a genome-scale metabolic model with GPR rules, and you need to identify which model reactions are catalysed by enzymes that physically interact with viral proteins.
skills.name: ppi-data-mapping-onto-metabolic-model-enzymes
skills.search_text: ppi-data-mapping-onto-metabolic-model-enzymes Use when you have an experimentally derived host–pathogen PPI dataset and a genome-scale metabolic model with GPR rules, and you need to identify which model reactions are catalysed by enzymes that physically interact with viral proteins. The PPI data are predicted/computational rather than experimentally characterized (e.g. Yeast-two-hybrid-free in silico predictions), since the method anchors on the Gordon et al (2020) experimental interactions The metabolic model lacks gene–reaction (GPR) associations, so viral-interacting human proteins cannot be linked to catalysed reactions The goal is to compute chokepoints or essential reactions themselves rather than to intersect them with PPI-mapped enzymes — use findCPcli's own computations directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0736 Maps experimentally characterized human/SARS-CoV-2 protein–protein interaction data (Gordon et al, 2020) onto the enzymes of an integrated genome-scale metabolic model (iHsaEC21 + SARS-CoV-2, BioModels MODEL2007210001) via gene–reaction (GPR) associations, to label reactions at PPi-pathway intersection nodes as candidate drug targets. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Maps experimentally characterized human/SARS-CoV-2 protein–protein interaction data (Gordon et al, 2020) onto the enzymes of an integrated genome-scale metabolic model (iHsaEC21 + SARS-CoV-2, BioModels MODEL2007210001) via gene–reaction (GPR) associations, to label reactions at PPi-pathway intersection nodes as candidate drug targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The PPI data are predicted/computational rather than experimentally characterized (e.g. Yeast-two-hybrid-free in silico predictions), since the method anchors on the Gordon et al (2020) experimental interactions The metabolic model lacks gene–reaction (GPR) associations, so viral-interacting human proteins cannot be linked to catalysed reactions The goal is to compute chokepoints or essential reactions themselves rather than to intersect them with PPI-mapped enzymes — use findCPcli's own computations directly instead

skills.description: Use when the analysis goal is to generate a PPI network for a specific disease in Cytoscape as a seed network for later linkset-based extension (e.g. compound-target or gene-disease annotation).
skills.name: ppi-network-construction-from-disease-query
skills.search_text: ppi-network-construction-from-disease-query Use when the analysis goal is to generate a PPI network for a specific disease in Cytoscape as a seed network for later linkset-based extension (e.g. compound-target or gene-disease annotation). The network already exists (e.g. a differentially expressed gene list is the input) — use gene-pathway extension workflows instead of a disease query The goal is a non-biological network such as the author-article-journal network built via the two-step Wikidata linkset extension The target interaction data is not protein-protein associations (e.g. only pathway membership is needed) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Builds a disease-focused protein-protein interaction network in Cytoscape using stringApp's Disease Query (e.g. query="Rett syndrome", cutoff=0.4, limit=20), producing a seed network that can subsequently be extended with external linksets such as ChEMBL and OMIM via CyTargetLinker. metabolomics/v3 10.12688/f1000research.14613.2
skills.summary: Builds a disease-focused protein-protein interaction network in Cytoscape using stringApp's Disease Query (e.g. query="Rett syndrome", cutoff=0.4, limit=20), producing a seed network that can subsequently be extended with external linksets such as ChEMBL and OMIM via CyTargetLinker.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network already exists (e.g. a differentially expressed gene list is the input) — use gene-pathway extension workflows instead of a disease query The goal is a non-biological network such as the author-article-journal network built via the two-step Wikidata linkset extension The target interaction data is not protein-protein associations (e.g. only pathway membership is needed)

skills.description: Use when raw 1D NMR spectra (Bruker or Agilent/Varian FID, or Bruker 1r files) show uncontrolled chemical shift offsets and a reference resonance must be pinned to its target ppm value prior to baseline correction, alignment, or binning.
skills.name: ppm-axis-chemical-shift-calibration
skills.search_text: ppm-axis-chemical-shift-calibration Use when raw 1D NMR spectra (Bruker or Agilent/Varian FID, or Bruker 1r files) show uncontrolled chemical shift offsets and a reference resonance must be pinned to its target ppm value prior to baseline correction, alignment, or binning. Input is already a processed bucket/intensity data matrix — calibration operates on raw spectra, not on post-binning tables Spectra need only binning or baseline correction and already share a correct ppm axis — calibration would add no value Fully automated batch processing without expert visual inspection is mandatory and no reference resonance can be identified interactively — the article notes batch-mode workflows usable by non-experts have not reached full maturity http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Interactive chemical shift calibration of the ppm scale for 1D 1H (and 13C) NMR spectra using NMRProcFlow's NMRspec GUI, so a reference resonance is set to its target ppm position across a spectra set before further processing. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Interactive chemical shift calibration of the ppm scale for 1D 1H (and 13C) NMR spectra using NMRProcFlow's NMRspec GUI, so a reference resonance is set to its target ppm position across a spectra set before further processing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed bucket/intensity data matrix — calibration operates on raw spectra, not on post-binning tables Spectra need only binning or baseline correction and already share a correct ppm axis — calibration would add no value Fully automated batch processing without expert visual inspection is mandatory and no reference resonance can be identified interactively — the article notes batch-mode workflows usable by non-experts have not reached full maturity

skills.description: Use when you have XCMS feature pairs flagged as putatively labeled and need to assign each labeled feature its monoisotopic base peak within a defined ppm mass tolerance.
skills.name: ppm-based-mass-matching
skills.search_text: ppm-based-mass-matching Use when you have XCMS feature pairs flagged as putatively labeled and need to assign each labeled feature its monoisotopic base peak within a defined ppm mass tolerance. The input is raw mzXML/mzML data that has not been peak-picked, aligned and grouped by XCMS — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure only. Upstream putative labeling pairs have not been detected yet; basepeak_finder requires the PuInc_seeker result as its PuIncR argument. The goal is isotopologue annotation against a metabolite database rather than monoisotopic base peak assignment — use geoRge's database_query step instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Matches each putatively labeled LC/MS feature to its monoisotopic base peak by searching for the unlabeled (12C-based) isotopologue within a parts-per-million mass tolerance, using exact atomic mass differences (12.0 vs 13.003355) as implemented in geoRge's basepeak_finder. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: Matches each putatively labeled LC/MS feature to its monoisotopic base peak by searching for the unlabeled (12C-based) isotopologue within a parts-per-million mass tolerance, using exact atomic mass differences (12.0 vs 13.003355) as implemented in geoRge's basepeak_finder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw mzXML/mzML data that has not been peak-picked, aligned and grouped by XCMS — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure only. Upstream putative labeling pairs have not been detected yet; basepeak_finder requires the PuInc_seeker result as its PuIncR argument. The goal is isotopologue annotation against a metabolite database rather than monoisotopic base peak assignment — use geoRge's database_query step instead.

skills.description: Use when high-resolution (FT-ICR) MSI peaks already filtered for tumor co-localization must be annotated with candidate formulas/adducts from HMDB/METLIN, with ppm errors recorded per assignment.
skills.name: ppm-error-calculation-for-mz-assignment
skills.search_text: ppm-error-calculation-for-mz-assignment Use when high-resolution (FT-ICR) MSI peaks already filtered for tumor co-localization must be annotated with candidate formulas/adducts from HMDB/METLIN, with ppm errors recorded per assignment. When the m/z list has not yet been co-localization filtered — annotating all 85,062 raw m/z variables would produce mostly spurious assignments; filter at Pearson T ≥ 0.7 first When the data come from a low-mass-accuracy instrument where ppm-level formula assignment is not meaningful (this skill is grounded in 9.4 Tesla FT-ICR data) When the goal is peak picking or tissue classification itself — those are handled upstream by massNet/msiPL without prior preprocessing or peak picking http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assigns tentative molecular formulas and adducts ([M+K]+, [M+2K-H]+) to tumor-co-localized m/z peaks by searching the HMDB and METLIN databases, and quantifies assignment quality as a ppm error between observed and theoretical exact masses, as in massNet's Table 2. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Assigns tentative molecular formulas and adducts ([M+K]+, [M+2K-H]+) to tumor-co-localized m/z peaks by searching the HMDB and METLIN databases, and quantifies assignment quality as a ppm error between observed and theoretical exact masses, as in massNet's Table 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the m/z list has not yet been co-localization filtered — annotating all 85,062 raw m/z variables would produce mostly spurious assignments; filter at Pearson T ≥ 0.7 first When the data come from a low-mass-accuracy instrument where ppm-level formula assignment is not meaningful (this skill is grounded in 9.4 Tesla FT-ICR data) When the goal is peak picking or tissue classification itself — those are handled upstream by massNet/msiPL without prior preprocessing or peak picking

skills.description: Use when building mass-difference transformation networks from direct-injection FT-ICR MS peak tables and you must decide which pairwise m/z differences match predefined biochemical transformation keys within a ppm error threshold.
skills.name: ppm-error-tolerance-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-error-tolerance-filtering Use when building mass-difference transformation networks from direct-injection FT-ICR MS peak tables and you must decide which pairwise m/z differences match predefined biochemical transformation keys within a ppm error threshold. Input is raw unprocessed FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must already have been performed before this skill applies The task is formula assignment itself (e.g., using MFAssignR) rather than matching already-assigned mass differences to transformation keys The analysis requires chromatographic separation of isomers — direct injection FT-ICR MS cannot separate chemical isomers and suffers signal suppression/enhancement http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies parts-per-million (ppm) error tolerances to decide which FT-ICR MS mass differences count as putative biochemical transformations (max 1 ppm) and which peaks/formula assignments survive pre-processing (0.5 ppm formula error) in MetaboDirect's transformation network workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-023-01476-3
skills.summary: Applies parts-per-million (ppm) error tolerances to decide which FT-ICR MS mass differences count as putative biochemical transformations (max 1 ppm) and which peaks/formula assignments survive pre-processing (0.5 ppm formula error) in MetaboDirect's transformation network workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unprocessed FT-ICR MS spectra — molecular formula assignment must already have been performed before this skill applies The task is formula assignment itself (e.g., using MFAssignR) rather than matching already-assigned mass differences to transformation keys The analysis requires chromatographic separation of isomers — direct injection FT-ICR MS cannot separate chemical isomers and suffers signal suppression/enhancement

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging dataset (e.g. MSIdata.xlsx with measured m/z in the first column) must be annotated against a metabolite database by an m/z error tolerance expressed in ppm.
skills.name: ppm-error-tolerance-matching
skills.search_text: ppm-error-tolerance-matching Use when a preprocessed mass spectrometry imaging dataset (e.g. MSIdata.xlsx with measured m/z in the first column) must be annotated against a metabolite database by an m/z error tolerance expressed in ppm. The dataset is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed m/z feature list with a measured m/z column. The database organ or detection mode does not match the MSIdata being annotated — the README explicitly requires consistency before running the tolerance match. The input already contains metabolite annotations; the skill is only for m/z-to-metabolite/adduct matching, not for validating or re-annotating existing labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Matches measured m/z features in a preprocessed MSI dataset against theoretical m/z values from an organ-specific metabolite database using a relative-error criterion (default 10 ppm, configurable to e.g. 5 ppm by editing the MATLAB tolerance line), producing an annotated metabolite list with adduct forms. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Matches measured m/z features in a preprocessed MSI dataset against theoretical m/z values from an organ-specific metabolite database using a relative-error criterion (default 10 ppm, configurable to e.g. 5 ppm by editing the MATLAB tolerance line), producing an annotated metabolite list with adduct forms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed m/z feature list with a measured m/z column. The database organ or detection mode does not match the MSIdata being annotated — the README explicitly requires consistency before running the tolerance match. The input already contains metabolite annotations; the skill is only for m/z-to-metabolite/adduct matching, not for validating or re-annotating existing labels.

skills.description: Use when you have a matrix of aligned, baseline-corrected 1D 1H NMR spectra (ppm scale x samples) from metabolic fingerprinting and need to reduce them to a samples x buckets intensity table while keeping peaks with uncontrolled chemical-shift variations inside single buckets.
skills.name: ppm-interval-intensity-summarization
skills.search_text: ppm-interval-intensity-summarization Use when you have a matrix of aligned, baseline-corrected 1D 1H NMR spectra (ppm scale x samples) from metabolic fingerprinting and need to reduce them to a samples x buckets intensity table while keeping peaks with uncontrolled chemical-shift variations inside single buckets. The input is already a bucket/feature table — this skill operates on raw aligned spectral matrices, not on pre-binned intensities Targeted metabolomics requiring per-resonance quantification of crowded, heavily overlapped regions — NMRProcFlow's local signal deconvolution quantification method is only planned in a future version and not available here Spectra have not yet undergone ppm-scale calibration, baseline correction and realignment — bucketing shifted, uncorrected spectra would reintroduce the peak-shift artifacts this skill exists to avoid Summarizes aligned, baseline-corrected 1D 1H NMR spectra into a bucket table by summing intensities over ppm intervals, using the Adaptive Intelligent Binning algorithm (De Meyer et al. 2008) to avoid the information loss and peak-shift artifacts of equally sized bins. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Summarizes aligned, baseline-corrected 1D 1H NMR spectra into a bucket table by summing intensities over ppm intervals, using the Adaptive Intelligent Binning algorithm (De Meyer et al. 2008) to avoid the information loss and peak-shift artifacts of equally sized bins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a bucket/feature table — this skill operates on raw aligned spectral matrices, not on pre-binned intensities Targeted metabolomics requiring per-resonance quantification of crowded, heavily overlapped regions — NMRProcFlow's local signal deconvolution quantification method is only planned in a future version and not available here Spectra have not yet undergone ppm-scale calibration, baseline correction and realignment — bucketing shifted, uncorrected spectra would reintroduce the peak-shift artifacts this skill exists to avoid

skills.description: Use when raw mzML/mzXML LC-MS/MS files must be preprocessed into feature tables with clean, merged MS/MS fragment peak lists (e.g., before computing fragmentation trees with SIRIUS or reranking with ZODIAC).
skills.name: ppm-mass-accuracy-peak-merging
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-accuracy-peak-merging Use when raw mzML/mzXML LC-MS/MS files must be preprocessed into feature tables with clean, merged MS/MS fragment peak lists (e.g., before computing fragmentation trees with SIRIUS or reranking with ZODIAC). Input is already a filtered feature table — the before/after counting logic expects pre-filter feature counts (e.g., dendroides 1,078 to 784) Goal is reranking SIRIUS molecular formula candidates with ZODIAC's Gibbs sampling rather than the preprocessing/peak-merging stage itself Goal is ZODIAC post-hoc filters such as minimum ZODIAC score 0.999 or 95% explained MS/MS intensity, which operate on ZODIAC output, not on raw spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Merges fragment peaks belonging to the same feature within a 10 ppm / 0.0025 m/z mass-accuracy window as part of the OpenMS-based preprocessing that discards low-quality MS/MS spectra before SIRIUS/ZODIAC molecular formula annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Merges fragment peaks belonging to the same feature within a 10 ppm / 0.0025 m/z mass-accuracy window as part of the OpenMS-based preprocessing that discards low-quality MS/MS spectra before SIRIUS/ZODIAC molecular formula annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature table — the before/after counting logic expects pre-filter feature counts (e.g., dendroides 1,078 to 784) Goal is reranking SIRIUS molecular formula candidates with ZODIAC's Gibbs sampling rather than the preprocessing/peak-merging stage itself Goal is ZODIAC post-hoc filters such as minimum ZODIAC score 0.999 or 95% explained MS/MS intensity, which operate on ZODIAC output, not on raw spectra

skills.description: Use when raw MZA spectra contain known calibrant peaks and you need to quantify mass error in ppm, fit a calibration against a reference list, and report residual tables for accuracy assessment.
skills.name: ppm-mass-accuracy-residual-analysis
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-accuracy-residual-analysis Use when raw MZA spectra contain known calibrant peaks and you need to quantify mass error in ppm, fit a calibration against a reference list, and report residual tables for accuracy assessment. When the goal is extracting spectra/XICs/ATDs from MZA files rather than calibrating m/z values — use mzapy's raw extraction and collect_xic_arrays_by_mz utilities instead When calibrating collision cross section rather than m/z — mzapy's CCS calibration for single-field DTIMS is a separate routine When raw data have not been converted to the MZA format; vendor files (.d, .raw, mzML) must first be converted with the mza executable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Fits a mass calibration model (mzapy.calibration.MassCalibration) that maps measured m/z values onto reference calibrant masses, then quantifies mass accuracy as ppm residuals before and after calibration. It leverages mzapy's supporting utilities beyond raw data extraction to validate instrument mass accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c01653
skills.summary: Fits a mass calibration model (mzapy.calibration.MassCalibration) that maps measured m/z values onto reference calibrant masses, then quantifies mass accuracy as ppm residuals before and after calibration. It leverages mzapy's supporting utilities beyond raw data extraction to validate instrument mass accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is extracting spectra/XICs/ATDs from MZA files rather than calibrating m/z values — use mzapy's raw extraction and collect_xic_arrays_by_mz utilities instead When calibrating collision cross section rather than m/z — mzapy's CCS calibration for single-field DTIMS is a separate routine When raw data have not been converted to the MZA format; vendor files (.d, .raw, mzML) must first be converted with the mza executable

skills.description: Use when tracking known compounds in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics mzML files (e.g. Waters Synapt) and you need to detect mass-accuracy drift or calibration failure from long-term QC pool data.
skills.name: ppm-mass-accuracy-threshold-evaluation
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-accuracy-threshold-evaluation Use when tracking known compounds in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics mzML files (e.g. Waters Synapt) and you need to detect mass-accuracy drift or calibration failure from long-term QC pool data. Input is already a processed feature table or peak-picked data rather than raw vendor files / mzML that can be peak-detected against m/z–RT pairs The goal is intensity-drift correction rather than mass-accuracy monitoring (QC-MXP handles intensity drifts) Calibration is known to be accurate and there is no need to monitor m/z stability; the skill adds no value if deviation checks are redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A QC skill that computes per-injection m/z deviations (in ppm) from a user-defined list of target m/z–retention time pairs and flags deviations exceeding a 20 ppm threshold, indicating serious analytical problems that should be addressed promptly. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: A QC skill that computes per-injection m/z deviations (in ppm) from a user-defined list of target m/z–retention time pairs and flags deviations exceeding a 20 ppm threshold, indicating serious analytical problems that should be addressed promptly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table or peak-picked data rather than raw vendor files / mzML that can be peak-detected against m/z–RT pairs The goal is intensity-drift correction rather than mass-accuracy monitoring (QC-MXP handles intensity drifts) Calibration is known to be accurate and there is no need to monitor m/z stability; the skill adds no value if deviation checks are redundant

skills.description: Use when chromatographic peaks (m/z, rt) from xcms peak detection must be assigned candidate compounds from a reference database using only MS1 m/z, and mass error should be tolerated relative to each target's mass (ppm-based) rather than as an absolute Da window.
skills.name: ppm-mass-accuracy-thresholding
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-accuracy-thresholding Use when chromatographic peaks (m/z, rt) from xcms peak detection must be assigned candidate compounds from a reference database using only MS1 m/z, and mass error should be tolerated relative to each target's mass (ppm-based) rather than as an absolute Da window. You need unambiguous compound IDs from MS1 m/z alone — most peaks match several compounds, so m/z-only annotation cannot resolve identity without additional evidence (RT, retention index, or MS2 spectra). The query data already carries reference m/z and retention time annotations to match directly — use MzRtParam-style matching instead of recomputing target m/z from exact masses. MS2 fragment spectra are available against a reference library — use matchSpectra-based MS2 annotation, which provides higher-confidence identifications. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates LC-MS chromatographic peaks with candidate metabolites by matching query feature m/z values against target m/z values computed from compound exact masses for specified adducts, using a relative mass-error threshold expressed in ppm (here 10 ppm) rather than an absolute m/z tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo12020173
skills.summary: Annotates LC-MS chromatographic peaks with candidate metabolites by matching query feature m/z values against target m/z values computed from compound exact masses for specified adducts, using a relative mass-error threshold expressed in ppm (here 10 ppm) rather than an absolute m/z tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need unambiguous compound IDs from MS1 m/z alone — most peaks match several compounds, so m/z-only annotation cannot resolve identity without additional evidence (RT, retention index, or MS2 spectra). The query data already carries reference m/z and retention time annotations to match directly — use MzRtParam-style matching instead of recomputing target m/z from exact masses. MS2 fragment spectra are available against a reference library — use matchSpectra-based MS2 annotation, which provides higher-confidence identifications.

skills.description: Use when aligning processed LC-HRMS feature lists (m/z, retention time) across batches and a systematic ppm-level mass shift (e.g. -3.4 ppm) plus non-linear retention-time shifts (e.g. 7-52 s) must be corrected against a reference chromatogram before feature matching.
skills.name: ppm-mass-deviation-evaluation
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-deviation-evaluation Use when aligning processed LC-HRMS feature lists (m/z, retention time) across batches and a systematic ppm-level mass shift (e.g. -3.4 ppm) plus non-linear retention-time shifts (e.g. 7-52 s) must be corrected against a reference chromatogram before feature matching. Input is raw LC-HRMS vendor data that has not yet been processed into a feature list with m/z values and retention times; MetMatch aligns pre-processed feature lists The metabolite experiment does not exhibit m/z or retention-time shifts relative to a reference chromatogram, so correction and ppm-deviation evaluation are unnecessary Differently formed ion adducts are not expected or the reference list already collapses adducts, in which case adduct-aware matching changes little (though note the 42 vs 92 match difference observed in the wheat case) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A skill for evaluating and correcting ppm-scale systematic m/z deviations (e.g. the -3.4 ppm average shift observed in the wheat phenylalanine-derived metabolite experiment) when aligning LC-HRMS feature lists across measurement batches using MetMatch. Accurate m/z-deviation handling, combined with adduct-aware matching, directly determines how many metabolite features can be matched across experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: A skill for evaluating and correcting ppm-scale systematic m/z deviations (e.g. the -3.4 ppm average shift observed in the wheat phenylalanine-derived metabolite experiment) when aligning LC-HRMS feature lists across measurement batches using MetMatch. Accurate m/z-deviation handling, combined with adduct-aware matching, directly determines how many metabolite features can be matched across experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-HRMS vendor data that has not yet been processed into a feature list with m/z values and retention times; MetMatch aligns pre-processed feature lists The metabolite experiment does not exhibit m/z or retention-time shifts relative to a reference chromatogram, so correction and ppm-deviation evaluation are unnecessary Differently formed ion adducts are not expected or the reference list already collapses adducts, in which case adduct-aware matching changes little (though note the 42 vs 92 match difference observed in the wheat case)

skills.description: Use when annotating preprocessed MSI features against a metabolite database and you need a confidence criterion for m/z-based metabolite/adduct matches, e.g. deciding which theoretical adduct ions match a measured peak.
skills.name: ppm-mass-error-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-error-filtering Use when annotating preprocessed MSI features against a metabolite database and you need a confidence criterion for m/z-based metabolite/adduct matches, e.g. deciding which theoretical adduct ions match a measured peak. The input is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed peak/m/z table with measured m/z in the first column. The task requires LC-MS/MS-level identification or MS/MS spectral matching — this filter relies solely on precursor m/z agreement against a database of 27,407 adduct ions and does not use product-ion evidence. The database organ or ionization mode does not match the MSI data (e.g. a negative-mode database sheet against positive-mode liver data); the ppm filter cannot compensate for a mismatched Database. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Relative m/z error filtering criterion used by MSIannotator.m to accept or reject metabolite/adduct matches between measured m/z from AFADESI-MSI data and theoretical adduct m/z in an organ-specific metabolite database; default threshold is 10 ppm, adjustable at line 25. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c00557
skills.summary: Relative m/z error filtering criterion used by MSIannotator.m to accept or reject metabolite/adduct matches between measured m/z from AFADESI-MSI data and theoretical adduct m/z in an organ-specific metabolite database; default threshold is 10 ppm, adjustable at line 25.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unprocessed MSI data rather than a preprocessed peak/m/z table with measured m/z in the first column. The task requires LC-MS/MS-level identification or MS/MS spectral matching — this filter relies solely on precursor m/z agreement against a database of 27,407 adduct ions and does not use product-ion evidence. The database organ or ionization mode does not match the MSI data (e.g. a negative-mode database sheet against positive-mode liver data); the ppm filter cannot compensate for a mismatched Database.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of theoretical metabolite m/z values from in-silico reaction-rule expansion and a feature table of dysregulated peaks, and need to flag which features correspond to which reaction-derived candidates.
skills.name: ppm-mass-error-preannotation
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-error-preannotation Use when you have a list of theoretical metabolite m/z values from in-silico reaction-rule expansion and a feature table of dysregulated peaks, and need to flag which features correspond to which reaction-derived candidates. Input is already a validated, standard-confirmed annotation set — 5 ppm preannotation is only a first-pass cross-reference, not confirmation Only MS2 spectra are available without accurate MS1 m/z values, since the matching operates entirely on monoisotopic precursor masses The goal is discovery of intact (non-biotransformed) parent chemicals against a reference library, where traditional bottom-up library search is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Preannotates theoretical biotransformed metabolite candidates against dysregulated LC-HRMS features by accurate-mass matching within a tight m/z error tolerance (≤5 ppm), as implemented in the RCS layer of CMDN. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: Preannotates theoretical biotransformed metabolite candidates against dysregulated LC-HRMS features by accurate-mass matching within a tight m/z error tolerance (≤5 ppm), as implemented in the RCS layer of CMDN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated, standard-confirmed annotation set — 5 ppm preannotation is only a first-pass cross-reference, not confirmation Only MS2 spectra are available without accurate MS1 m/z values, since the matching operates entirely on monoisotopic precursor masses The goal is discovery of intact (non-biotransformed) parent chemicals against a reference library, where traditional bottom-up library search is appropriate

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that a computed theoretical m/z for a derivatized or adducted species matches a reported/observed peak within a defined ppm tolerance, or to derive expected m/z values for single- and multi-site derivatization products.
skills.name: ppm-mass-error-tolerance-comparison
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-error-tolerance-comparison Use when you need to verify that a computed theoretical m/z for a derivatized or adducted species matches a reported/observed peak within a defined ppm tolerance, or to derive expected m/z values for single- and multi-site derivatization products. Input is already a confirmed identification from Met-ID's MS2 spectral database rather than a theoretical m/z that needs verification The analyte is underivatized and detected as a conventional [M+H]+/[M-H]- ion, so no derivatization increments need to be modeled Observed peaks have mass errors exceeding the configured tolerance (e.g., >5 ppm), which the Met-ID mass-match filter would reject as false positives http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes theoretical m/z values for derivatized metabolites (e.g., FMP-10-tagged dopamine) and compares them against reported or observed values as ppm differences, validating agreement within a user-specified mass error (e.g., 5 ppm) used by Met-ID identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00633
skills.summary: Computes theoretical m/z values for derivatized metabolites (e.g., FMP-10-tagged dopamine) and compares them against reported or observed values as ppm differences, validating agreement within a user-specified mass error (e.g., 5 ppm) used by Met-ID identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a confirmed identification from Met-ID's MS2 spectral database rather than a theoretical m/z that needs verification The analyte is underivatized and detected as a conventional [M+H]+/[M-H]- ion, so no derivatization increments need to be modeled Observed peaks have mass errors exceeding the configured tolerance (e.g., >5 ppm), which the Met-ID mass-match filter would reject as false positives

skills.description: Use when you have a list of significant/up-regulated ion m/z values from an rMSIKeyIon TestIonSelect comparison and need putative metabolite IDs via ppm-tolerant database matching with adduct consideration.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-annotation
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-annotation Use when you have a list of significant/up-regulated ion m/z values from an rMSIKeyIon TestIonSelect comparison and need putative metabolite IDs via ppm-tolerant database matching with adduct consideration. Input is already an annotated feature table with metabolite names — re-annotation at 20 ppm would add nothing The ion list has not been filtered by TestIonSelect; matching unfiltered peak matrices will flood results with spurious candidates The analysis targets negative-mode or unusual adduct chemistry not covered by the H/Na/K/NH4 positive-mode adduct set http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotate putative metabolite identities for up-regulated MSI ion m/z lists by matching against a metabolite database (e.g. HMDB 4.0) within a fixed ppm mass tolerance, enumerating candidate adducts. This converts statistically filtered ion lists from rMSIKeyIon into named metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9080162
skills.summary: Annotate putative metabolite identities for up-regulated MSI ion m/z lists by matching against a metabolite database (e.g. HMDB 4.0) within a fixed ppm mass tolerance, enumerating candidate adducts. This converts statistically filtered ion lists from rMSIKeyIon into named metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated feature table with metabolite names — re-annotation at 20 ppm would add nothing The ion list has not been filtered by TestIonSelect; matching unfiltered peak matrices will flood results with spurious candidates The analysis targets negative-mode or unusual adduct chemistry not covered by the H/Na/K/NH4 positive-mode adduct set

skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-annotation-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-annotation-filtering Use when processing .imzML mass spectrometry imaging data in massPix and you need putative lipid annotations for deisotoped ion features based on accurate mass within a defined ppm tolerance. The input is already a feature table with confirmed lipid annotations requiring no mass matching Only a database hit is insufficient for the analysis goal — accurate-mass matches must be confirmed by MS/MS, so this skill alone cannot provide definitive metabolite identification The analytes of interest are lipid classes outside those searched by massPix (e.g. not among DAG, TAG, PC, PE, PS, LysoPC, CE, SM, Cer, PA, PG, PI, FFA), since the generated library is restricted to common lipid classes http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates deisotoped mass spectrometry imaging ion features with putative lipid identities by accurate-mass matching against a generated lipid m/z library, retaining only matches whose |observed m/z - theoretical m/z| falls below a ppm threshold (e.g. 10 ppm). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1252-5
skills.summary: Annotates deisotoped mass spectrometry imaging ion features with putative lipid identities by accurate-mass matching against a generated lipid m/z library, retaining only matches whose |observed m/z - theoretical m/z| falls below a ppm threshold (e.g. 10 ppm).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature table with confirmed lipid annotations requiring no mass matching Only a database hit is insufficient for the analysis goal — accurate-mass matches must be confirmed by MS/MS, so this skill alone cannot provide definitive metabolite identification The analytes of interest are lipid classes outside those searched by massPix (e.g. not among DAG, TAG, PC, PE, PS, LysoPC, CE, SM, Cer, PA, PG, PI, FFA), since the generated library is restricted to common lipid classes

skills.description: Use when benchmarking formula ranking tools (SIRIUS, Buddy, FSA) on shared MS/MS datasets and each tool's mass tolerance must be set to its documented optimum (e.g., SIRIUS 5.8.6 with the paper's optimal ppm tolerance, Buddy 0.3.8 with 10-20 ppm).
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-configuration
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-configuration Use when benchmarking formula ranking tools (SIRIUS, Buddy, FSA) on shared MS/MS datasets and each tool's mass tolerance must be set to its documented optimum (e.g., SIRIUS 5.8.6 with the paper's optimal ppm tolerance, Buddy 0.3.8 with 10-20 ppm). When the goal is de novo method development rather than head-to-head tool benchmarking under published tolerance settings (e.g., FSA's own development, which tested additional scoring terms via a genetic algorithm rather than fixed tolerance configurations). When only one tool is being run without a comparative accuracy/runtime claim, since the tolerance-configuration skill exists to make cross-tool Table 3 comparisons reproducible. Configures per-tool mass tolerance (ppm) settings when benchmarking formula assignment tools such as SIRIUS, Buddy, and FSA on the same LC-MS/MS datasets, so that rank-1/top-3/top-5 accuracy and wall-clock runtime comparisons are run under each tool's documented optimal tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-025-02379-0
skills.summary: Configures per-tool mass tolerance (ppm) settings when benchmarking formula assignment tools such as SIRIUS, Buddy, and FSA on the same LC-MS/MS datasets, so that rank-1/top-3/top-5 accuracy and wall-clock runtime comparisons are run under each tool's documented optimal tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo method development rather than head-to-head tool benchmarking under published tolerance settings (e.g., FSA's own development, which tested additional scoring terms via a genetic algorithm rather than fixed tolerance configurations).
