skills.description: Use when annotating precursor m/z values from an MS-DIAL peak list (e.g. CSH-Q Exactive HF positive-ion lipidomics) against an in-silico library such as LipidBlast and you need a fixed mass-tolerance window to accept matches as MSI level 3 annotations.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-filtering Use when annotating precursor m/z values from an MS-DIAL peak list (e.g. CSH-Q Exactive HF positive-ion lipidomics) against an in-silico library such as LipidBlast and you need a fixed mass-tolerance window to accept matches as MSI level 3 annotations. The precursor already has an MS/MS match at MSI level 1 or 2 (authentic standard or precursor + MS/MS matching) — accurate-mass-only lookup would lower confidence. The instrument mass accuracy is unknown or substantially worse than the 5 mDa window — filtering at a fixed tolerance without verified calibration can produce false annotations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Applies precursor accurate-mass tolerance filters (millidalton or ppm windows, e.g. 5 mDa for LipidBlast v49 lipid library matching) to accept MSI level 2/3 structure annotations in the CSH-Q Exactive HF urinary lipidomics workflow, using the LipidBlast v49 m/z lookup macro for MS-DIAL precursor masses. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Applies precursor accurate-mass tolerance filters (millidalton or ppm windows, e.g. 5 mDa for LipidBlast v49 lipid library matching) to accept MSI level 2/3 structure annotations in the CSH-Q Exactive HF urinary lipidomics workflow, using the LipidBlast v49 m/z lookup macro for MS-DIAL precursor masses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The precursor already has an MS/MS match at MSI level 1 or 2 (authentic standard or precursor + MS/MS matching) — accurate-mass-only lookup would lower confidence. The instrument mass accuracy is unknown or substantially worse than the 5 mDa window — filtering at a fixed tolerance without verified calibration can produce false annotations.

skills.description: Use when you have MS1 precursor m/z values and a pre-calculated compound database (HDF5 with fingerprints/fragmentation patterns), and need to bound the candidate set by a ppm m/z tolerance before annotation.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-filtering Use when you have MS1 precursor m/z values and a pre-calculated compound database (HDF5 with fingerprints/fragmentation patterns), and need to bound the candidate set by a ppm m/z tolerance before annotation. You need molecular formula-level candidate enumeration from elemental compositions rather than retrieval from a pre-built exact-mass compound database (use chemdistiller.filters.formula/element for that) Spectra are not yet converted to the ChemDistiller internal hierarchical format — the engine currently requires that format for input spectra You are doing MS2-only or fragmentation-pattern comparison without an MS1 precursor m/z to constrain the search http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 First-stage candidate generation in ChemDistiller: retrieve all compounds from a pre-built HDF5 database whose exact masses fall within a ppm tolerance window of the MS1 precursor m/z. This prunes the compound search space before fragmentation-based scoring (e.g. ~24 candidates per MS1 peak from a ~130k-compound small database at 20 ppm). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: First-stage candidate generation in ChemDistiller: retrieve all compounds from a pre-built HDF5 database whose exact masses fall within a ppm tolerance window of the MS1 precursor m/z. This prunes the compound search space before fragmentation-based scoring (e.g. ~24 candidates per MS1 peak from a ~130k-compound small database at 20 ppm).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need molecular formula-level candidate enumeration from elemental compositions rather than retrieval from a pre-built exact-mass compound database (use chemdistiller.filters.formula/element for that) Spectra are not yet converted to the ChemDistiller internal hierarchical format — the engine currently requires that format for input spectra You are doing MS2-only or fragmentation-pattern comparison without an MS1 precursor m/z to constrain the search

skills.description: Use when annotating deisotoped MSI ions by accurate mass in massPix and you need to choose or justify an annotation ppm tolerance, or reproduce the paper's 5 ppm vs 50 ppm comparison (~200 extra annotations) on lipidomics imzML data.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-matching
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-matching Use when annotating deisotoped MSI ions by accurate mass in massPix and you need to choose or justify an annotation ppm tolerance, or reproduce the paper's 5 ppm vs 50 ppm comparison (~200 extra annotations) on lipidomics imzML data. Input is raw spectra not yet preprocessed — ions must first be extracted, binned, filtered and deisotoped (mzextractor, peakpicker.bin, filter, deisotope) before tolerance-based matching You need confident metabolite identification rather than putative annotation — accurate-mass matching is only the first step and requires MS/MS confirmation Your goal is false-discovery-rate-controlled annotation; the article points to METASPACE as the framework for FDR-controlled metabolite annotation in MSI http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies the effect of the accurate-mass matching tolerance (ppm.annotate) on putative lipid annotations in massPix, e.g. comparing 5 ppm vs 50 ppm on the MTBLS487 test_POS.imzML data where the looser tolerance yields roughly 200 additional annotations. The skill grounds annotation in deisotoped ion m/z searched against a generated lipid library of fatty acid, head-group and adduct combinations. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1252-5
skills.summary: Quantifies the effect of the accurate-mass matching tolerance (ppm.annotate) on putative lipid annotations in massPix, e.g. comparing 5 ppm vs 50 ppm on the MTBLS487 test_POS.imzML data where the looser tolerance yields roughly 200 additional annotations. The skill grounds annotation in deisotoped ion m/z searched against a generated lipid library of fatty acid, head-group and adduct combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spectra not yet preprocessed — ions must first be extracted, binned, filtered and deisotoped (mzextractor, peakpicker.bin, filter, deisotope) before tolerance-based matching You need confident metabolite identification rather than putative annotation — accurate-mass matching is only the first step and requires MS/MS confirmation Your goal is false-discovery-rate-controlled annotation; the article points to METASPACE as the framework for FDR-controlled metabolite annotation in MSI

skills.description: Use when running DIMPLE preprocessing on DESI-MSI root data and you need to choose or justify the 2.5 ppm mass tolerance (default) versus 5 ppm, or the 1.5 versus 1.1 background-enrichment threshold, based on peak-count sensitivity.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-parameter-tuning Use when running DIMPLE preprocessing on DESI-MSI root data and you need to choose or justify the 2.5 ppm mass tolerance (default) versus 5 ppm, or the 1.5 versus 1.1 background-enrichment threshold, based on peak-count sensitivity. Data are not DESI-MSI root sections analyzed along a linear developmental gradient by DIMPLE You need absolute metabolite annotation confidence rather than relative peak-count sensitivity; relaxed tolerance inflates candidate mass signatures without validating them Input is already a peak table and only annotation or statistics are required — no preprocessing re-run is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Tuning procedure for the DIMPLE preprocessing mass tolerance (ppm) and background-enrichment thresholds, quantifying how relaxing them changes the average number of m/z signatures detected per DESI-MSI maize root. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Tuning procedure for the DIMPLE preprocessing mass tolerance (ppm) and background-enrichment thresholds, quantifying how relaxing them changes the average number of m/z signatures detected per DESI-MSI maize root.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not DESI-MSI root sections analyzed along a linear developmental gradient by DIMPLE You need absolute metabolite annotation confidence rather than relative peak-count sensitivity; relaxed tolerance inflates candidate mass signatures without validating them Input is already a peak table and only annotation or statistics are required — no preprocessing re-run is possible

skills.description: Use when comparing predicted spectra from C2MS models (FraGNNet, GrAFF-MS, ICEBERG) against real NIST20 MS/MS spectra and you need peak-level or formula-annotation-level agreement metrics under a ppm mass-accuracy tolerance.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-peak-matching
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-peak-matching Use when comparing predicted spectra from C2MS models (FraGNNet, GrAFF-MS, ICEBERG) against real NIST20 MS/MS spectra and you need peak-level or formula-annotation-level agreement metrics under a ppm mass-accuracy tolerance. Input spectra are glycan or peptide spectra — these were explicitly excluded from the formula annotation analysis to focus on small molecules You need absolute peak-intensity error or spectral similarity metrics (e.g. cosine) rather than mass-matched annotation overlap Formula annotations with masses more than 10 ppm from their associated peak mass have not been filtered — leaving them in corrupts the precision/recall denominators http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Matches predicted MS/MS peaks to real peaks using a relative mass tolerance of 10 ppm (epsilon = 1e-5, scaled by max(m, 200)) to enable formula annotation recall/precision (AR/AP/AWR/AWP) comparison of C2MS models on NIST20 scaffold-split spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2404.02360
skills.summary: Matches predicted MS/MS peaks to real peaks using a relative mass tolerance of 10 ppm (epsilon = 1e-5, scaled by max(m, 200)) to enable formula annotation recall/precision (AR/AP/AWR/AWP) comparison of C2MS models on NIST20 scaffold-split spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are glycan or peptide spectra — these were explicitly excluded from the formula annotation analysis to focus on small molecules You need absolute peak-intensity error or spectral similarity metrics (e.g. cosine) rather than mass-matched annotation overlap Formula annotations with masses more than 10 ppm from their associated peak mass have not been filtered — leaving them in corrupts the precision/recall denominators

skills.description: Use when you need chromatograms for known precursor m/z values (e.g., iRT peptides) directly from a Thermo Fisher .raw file with a ppm mass tolerance, without converting to mzML or using vendor GUI software.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-precursor-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-precursor-filtering Use when you need chromatograms for known precursor m/z values (e.g., iRT peptides) directly from a Thermo Fisher .raw file with a ppm mass tolerance, without converting to mzML or using vendor GUI software. When extracting fragment-ion signal from MS2 scans — use the scan-filter form of readChromatogram with a filter string like 'FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00 [100.0000-1015.0000]' instead of the MS1-only 'ms' filter. When the input is already converted/centroided open-format data (mzML) or a feature/quantification table — no raw-file access is needed. When the data are not from Thermo Fisher Scientific instruments, since rawrr wraps the vendor-provided RawFileReader API for Thermo .raw files only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Extract precursor-level chromatographic signal from Thermo raw files by computing extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) around expected precursor m/z values with a ppm-based mass tolerance, restricted to MS1-level scans via rawrr::readChromatogram. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00866
skills.summary: Extract precursor-level chromatographic signal from Thermo raw files by computing extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) around expected precursor m/z values with a ppm-based mass tolerance, restricted to MS1-level scans via rawrr::readChromatogram.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When extracting fragment-ion signal from MS2 scans — use the scan-filter form of readChromatogram with a filter string like 'FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00 [100.0000-1015.0000]' instead of the MS1-only 'ms' filter. When the input is already converted/centroided open-format data (mzML) or a feature/quantification table — no raw-file access is needed. When the data are not from Thermo Fisher Scientific instruments, since rawrr wraps the vendor-provided RawFileReader API for Thermo .raw files only.

skills.description: Use when searching experimental high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of NRP/PK compounds against a custom building-block/sequence database (e.g. MassSpecBlocks-exported) and benchmarking top-1/top-10 retrieval accuracy with strict mass-accuracy configurations.
skills.name: ppm-mass-tolerance-search-configuration
skills.search_text: ppm-mass-tolerance-search-configuration Use when searching experimental high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of NRP/PK compounds against a custom building-block/sequence database (e.g. MassSpecBlocks-exported) and benchmarking top-1/top-10 retrieval accuracy with strict mass-accuracy configurations. When running Dereplicator or Dereplicator+, which are configured with absolute tolerances of 0.005 Da rather than ppm values — transplanting the 5 ppm configuration would be wrong When the goal is de novo spectral annotation in CycloBranch rather than database search/dereplication against a sequence database When a custom building-block/sequence database must be constructed in NRPro — NRPro users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Configures CycloBranch (and comparably NRPro) dereplication/database searches of high-resolution tandem mass spectra of NRPs and polyketides using 5 ppm precursor and fragment ion m/z tolerances, zero relative peak intensity threshold, and restriction to b-ions and a-ions with at most one neutral loss of H2O or NH3. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00530-2
skills.summary: Configures CycloBranch (and comparably NRPro) dereplication/database searches of high-resolution tandem mass spectra of NRPs and polyketides using 5 ppm precursor and fragment ion m/z tolerances, zero relative peak intensity threshold, and restriction to b-ions and a-ions with at most one neutral loss of H2O or NH3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When running Dereplicator or Dereplicator+, which are configured with absolute tolerances of 0.005 Da rather than ppm values — transplanting the 5 ppm configuration would be wrong When the goal is de novo spectral annotation in CycloBranch rather than database search/dereplication against a sequence database When a custom building-block/sequence database must be constructed in NRPro — NRPro users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences

skills.description: Use when comparing two NMR spectral reconstruction/quantification methods and whole-spectrum RMSE alone does not explain where errors concentrate — e.g. when ASICS-like linear-combination fits fail in specific ppm windows of plasma 1H NMR data.
skills.name: ppm-region-restricted-error-analysis
skills.search_text: ppm-region-restricted-error-analysis Use when comparing two NMR spectral reconstruction/quantification methods and whole-spectrum RMSE alone does not explain where errors concentrate — e.g. when ASICS-like linear-combination fits fail in specific ppm windows of plasma 1H NMR data. The goal is quantification accuracy of metabolite concentrations rather than spectral reconstruction quality — RMSE on spectra does not directly validate fitted concentrations The spectra have different chemical-shift axes or preprocessing across methods, so window subsetting (3–4 ppm) would not be comparable between the two reconstructions The comparison target is metabolite biomarker discovery via estimated relative concentrations, not whole-spectrum fitting fidelity http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A reconstruction-error localization technique for 1H NMR spectra: in addition to whole-spectrum RMSE, RMSE is recomputed within a narrow chemical-shift window (3–4 ppm) to pinpoint the region where a fitting method fails, as done when comparing NMRQNet against ASICS on EDTA plasma spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.03.01.530642
skills.summary: A reconstruction-error localization technique for 1H NMR spectra: in addition to whole-spectrum RMSE, RMSE is recomputed within a narrow chemical-shift window (3–4 ppm) to pinpoint the region where a fitting method fails, as done when comparing NMRQNet against ASICS on EDTA plasma spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantification accuracy of metabolite concentrations rather than spectral reconstruction quality — RMSE on spectra does not directly validate fitted concentrations The spectra have different chemical-shift axes or preprocessing across methods, so window subsetting (3–4 ppm) would not be comparable between the two reconstructions The comparison target is metabolite biomarker discovery via estimated relative concentrations, not whole-spectrum fitting fidelity

skills.description: Use when processing 1D 1H NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. Bruker/Varian FID-derived) in NMRProcFlow and overlaid spectra show resonance shifts within specific ppm areas that baseline correction and ppm-scale calibration cannot fix.
skills.name: ppm-region-selection-for-shift-correction
skills.search_text: ppm-region-selection-for-shift-correction Use when processing 1D 1H NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. Bruker/Varian FID-derived) in NMRProcFlow and overlaid spectra show resonance shifts within specific ppm areas that baseline correction and ppm-scale calibration cannot fix. The spectra are raw, uncalibrated FIDs — ppm-scale calibration and baseline correction must be done first, since realignment assumes calibrated spectra The chemical shift differences are not uncontrolled drift between spectra but a uniform offset that a single ppm-scale calibration step can fix A region has different numbers of peaks across spectra — Parametric Time Warping there violates its assumption and will not produce a better result http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Interactive selection of ppm areas in 1D 1H NMR spectra whose resonances show uncontrolled chemical shift variations between samples, followed by realignment of each selected area using NMRProcFlow's Least-Square algorithm or Parametric Time Warping. It corrects peak drift prior to binning so that metabolite signals line up across the spectra matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Interactive selection of ppm areas in 1D 1H NMR spectra whose resonances show uncontrolled chemical shift variations between samples, followed by realignment of each selected area using NMRProcFlow's Least-Square algorithm or Parametric Time Warping. It corrects peak drift prior to binning so that metabolite signals line up across the spectra matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are raw, uncalibrated FIDs — ppm-scale calibration and baseline correction must be done first, since realignment assumes calibrated spectra The chemical shift differences are not uncontrolled drift between spectra but a uniform offset that a single ppm-scale calibration step can fix A region has different numbers of peaks across spectra — Parametric Time Warping there violates its assumption and will not produce a better result

skills.description: Use when setting precursor-mass search tolerances for tandem MS annotation (e.g. ChemDistiller's --delta_mz) or when quantifying how much a high-accuracy ppm window narrows database candidate lists.
skills.name: ppm-to-dalton-mass-tolerance-conversion
skills.search_text: ppm-to-dalton-mass-tolerance-conversion Use when setting precursor-mass search tolerances for tandem MS annotation (e.g. ChemDistiller's --delta_mz) or when quantifying how much a high-accuracy ppm window narrows database candidate lists. The analysis requires MS2-level discrimination (fragmentation patterns, fingerprints, FingerScorer SVM scoring) rather than precursor-mass pre-filtering of candidates The MS1 data are low-resolution so that a 20 ppm window is unrealistic; the delta_mz tolerance should be set to match the instrument's actual mass accuracy The comparison database differs fundamentally in composition from PubChem, so the absolute counts (250,079 / 3,229) and the ~77.5x ratio would not transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Converts an MS1 m/z tolerance expressed in ppm (e.g. 20 ppm) into an absolute Dalton window (e.g. +/-0.008 Da at 400 Da) and quantifies the resulting candidate-molecule search-space reduction against a 1 Da window in a compound database such as PubChem. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: Converts an MS1 m/z tolerance expressed in ppm (e.g. 20 ppm) into an absolute Dalton window (e.g. +/-0.008 Da at 400 Da) and quantifies the resulting candidate-molecule search-space reduction against a 1 Da window in a compound database such as PubChem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires MS2-level discrimination (fragmentation patterns, fingerprints, FingerScorer SVM scoring) rather than precursor-mass pre-filtering of candidates The MS1 data are low-resolution so that a 20 ppm window is unrealistic; the delta_mz tolerance should be set to match the instrument's actual mass accuracy The comparison database differs fundamentally in composition from PubChem, so the absolute counts (250,079 / 3,229) and the ~77.5x ratio would not transfer

skills.description: Use when comparing feature tables produced by different LC-MS preprocessing tools and you need to quantify whether reported m/z values are distinguishable at a stated instrument mass resolution (ppm tolerance), e.g. auditing XCMS/MZmine output against asari's mass-track granularity.
skills.name: ppm-tolerance-feature-comparison
skills.search_text: ppm-tolerance-feature-comparison Use when comparing feature tables produced by different LC-MS preprocessing tools and you need to quantify whether reported m/z values are distinguishable at a stated instrument mass resolution (ppm tolerance), e.g. auditing XCMS/MZmine output against asari's mass-track granularity. Input is raw centroided mzML data rather than an already-produced feature table — feature detection/processing must happen first Data are low-resolution or from non-Orbitrap platforms where asari's mass-track settings are not optimized and ppm-based distinctness is not meaningful Goal is comparing annotation or quantification accuracy rather than m/z distinguishability at instrument resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking method that scores m/z features from different LC-MS processing tools (XCMS, MZmine, asari) by mSelectivity — the distinctness of each feature's m/z relative to nearest neighbors within the instrument's ppm resolution (e.g. 5 ppm on HZV029) — after rounding m/z to the 3rd decimal place, to expose mass-alignment deficiencies. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: A benchmarking method that scores m/z features from different LC-MS processing tools (XCMS, MZmine, asari) by mSelectivity — the distinctness of each feature's m/z relative to nearest neighbors within the instrument's ppm resolution (e.g. 5 ppm on HZV029) — after rounding m/z to the 3rd decimal place, to expose mass-alignment deficiencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw centroided mzML data rather than an already-produced feature table — feature detection/processing must happen first Data are low-resolution or from non-Orbitrap platforms where asari's mass-track settings are not optimized and ppm-based distinctness is not meaningful Goal is comparing annotation or quantification accuracy rather than m/z distinguishability at instrument resolution

skills.description: Use when candidate metabolites of a TCM prototype must be assigned a bridging score via exact-mass matching (±5 ppm) and MS2 fragment similarity, using a one-/two-step predictable reaction catalog.
skills.name: ppm-tolerance-mass-matching
skills.search_text: ppm-tolerance-mass-matching Use when candidate metabolites of a TCM prototype must be assigned a bridging score via exact-mass matching (±5 ppm) and MS2 fragment similarity, using a one-/two-step predictable reaction catalog. The candidate metabolite cannot be reached by one- or two-step Metworks 1.3.0.200 reactions plus TCM deglycosylation, so it falls outside the predictable reaction catalog (unpredictable metabolites need the separate mass-defect/scoring branch of MDRB) Only MS1 data are available with no MS2 fragment spectra, since the MS2 similarity component (20/30/0 points) cannot be scored The metabolite list has not yet been produced by the PATBS non-targeted background-subtraction pipeline, so no candidate metabolites or fragment matches exist to score http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Scores predictable TCM metabolite–prototype pairs by combining an m/z match score (70 points when matched within ±5 ppm) with an MS2 fragment-similarity score (20/30/0 points by match degree 1/≥2/0), over a predictable reaction catalog built from Metworks 1.3.0.200 one- and two-step reactions plus TCM deglycosylation. It is the scoring core of the MDRB bridging strategy for relating in vivo metabolites back to in vitro prototypes. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Scores predictable TCM metabolite–prototype pairs by combining an m/z match score (70 points when matched within ±5 ppm) with an MS2 fragment-similarity score (20/30/0 points by match degree 1/≥2/0), over a predictable reaction catalog built from Metworks 1.3.0.200 one- and two-step reactions plus TCM deglycosylation. It is the scoring core of the MDRB bridging strategy for relating in vivo metabolites back to in vitro prototypes.

skills.search_text: ppm-tolerance-mass-search Use when detected m/z values from an SM dataset (e.g. imzML read via Cardinal) need metabolite identities without MS/MS, and the platform is not supported by high-resolution-only tools like METASPACE or pySM. skills.description: Decision support for testing whether restricting end-to-end LC-MS deep-learning classification to published biomarker m/z windows reduces accuracy versus training on complete raw metabolomic data.
skills.name: ppm-tolerance-mz-filtering
skills.search_text: ppm-tolerance-mz-filtering Decision support for testing whether restricting end-to-end LC-MS deep-learning classification to published biomarker m/z windows reduces accuracy versus training on complete raw metabolomic data. When the goal is maximum-accuracy disease classification rather than testing the contribution of known biomarker signals — full raw data gives the baseline accuracy (AUC 0.99). When input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw LC-MS data, since DeepMSProfiler operates end-to-end on raw signals converted to .npy. When biomarker m/z values or publication counts for the disease of interest are unavailable, since the filtering depends entirely on the curated PC-annotated biomarker list. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Filters raw LC-MS metabolomic signals to only those m/z values within a 3 ppm tolerance of curated biomarker m/z values (retained at publication-count thresholds PC>1, PC>3, PC>8), enabling ablation of DeepMSProfiler against the full-data baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-51433-3
skills.summary: Filters raw LC-MS metabolomic signals to only those m/z values within a 3 ppm tolerance of curated biomarker m/z values (retained at publication-count thresholds PC>1, PC>3, PC>8), enabling ablation of DeepMSProfiler against the full-data baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is maximum-accuracy disease classification rather than testing the contribution of known biomarker signals — full raw data gives the baseline accuracy (AUC 0.99). When input is already a peak/feature table rather than raw LC-MS data, since DeepMSProfiler operates end-to-end on raw signals converted to .npy. When biomarker m/z values or publication counts for the disease of interest are unavailable, since the filtering depends entirely on the curated PC-annotated biomarker list.

skills.summary: Matches measured MS2 peak m/z values against theoretical fragment m/z values from a candidate lipid within a stated ppm mass tolerance, using hash-table/bisection lookup as in the LipidIN expeditious querying (EQ) module, to compute Score_matched and Score_ratio per candidate.

skills.name: ppm-tolerance-peak-matching
skills.search_text: ppm-tolerance-peak-matching Use when you have two peak lists from MALDI FT-ICR MS runs — e.g. peak_data_sc_regional_decode.imzML (13,566 single-cell SCMS spectra) and coronal3D_slide3_5_R00_propagated_decoded. skills.summary: A m/z feature-matching strategy for cross-annotating single-cell SCMS peak lists against a tissue MSI lipid feature database, using 3-ppm mass windows to absorb inter-run mass shifts and enable multiscale lipid-level integration of the two measurement types.

When the two datasets come from different ionization modes or mass spectrometers with incompatible m/z ranges — the 3-ppm window cannot bridge gross m/z discrepancies; only small mass shifts between runs are assumed.

skills.description: Use when evaluating how many fragments per lipid species are needed for unambiguous identification in a background lipidome (e.g. yeast) and you need to compare loose Da-level versus tight ppm-level matching tolerances.
skills.name: ppm-vs-da-tolerance-comparison
skills.search_text: ppm-vs-da-tolerance-comparison Use when evaluating how many fragments per lipid species are needed for unambiguous identification in a background lipidome (e.g. yeast) and you need to compare loose Da-level versus tight ppm-level matching tolerances. The background lipidome is bacterial or archaeal (e.g. E. coli acyl-PG/acyl-PE), since the article notes a lack of standards and the knowledge-base does not cover these classes. A dedicated FDR scoring algorithm is required — LipidCreator intentionally does not provide one and does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids or peak-area integration. Stereoisomer discrimination is the goal, because the article states there are currently no large-scale methods available to cope with occurring stereoisomers. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Recomputes the false-match probability of precursor–fragment lipid identifications at coarse ±0.5 Da versus high-resolution ±2.5 ppm tolerances to quantify how mass-accuracy filtering controls target–decoy discrimination in targeted lipidomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Recomputes the false-match probability of precursor–fragment lipid identifications at coarse ±0.5 Da versus high-resolution ±2.5 ppm tolerances to quantify how mass-accuracy filtering controls target–decoy discrimination in targeted lipidomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The background lipidome is bacterial or archaeal (e.g. E. coli acyl-PG/acyl-PE), since the article notes a lack of standards and the knowledge-base does not cover these classes. A dedicated FDR scoring algorithm is required — LipidCreator intentionally does not provide one and does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids or peak-area integration. Stereoisomer discrimination is the goal, because the article states there are currently no large-scale methods available to cope with occurring stereoisomers.

skills.description: Use when raw 1D NMR metabolomics spectra (Bruker FID, Varian/Agilent FID, or nmrML) show baseline distortion or macromolecule residuals and you must delimit ppm areas for local baseline correction or realignment in NMRProcFlow.
skills.name: ppm-zone-delimitation
skills.search_text: ppm-zone-delimitation Use when raw 1D NMR metabolomics spectra (Bruker FID, Varian/Agilent FID, or nmrML) show baseline distortion or macromolecule residuals and you must delimit ppm areas for local baseline correction or realignment in NMRProcFlow. Spectra already carry a flat baseline and only need downstream steps such as ppm-scale calibration, realignment, or binning — apply those steps directly instead The user wants a fully automated batch-mode black-box workflow without interactive inspection; NMRProcFlow's delimitation is deliberately interactive GUI-driven The data are not 1D NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. feature tables or 2D NMR); NMRProcFlow's viewer and processing stages target 1D spectra Delimiting specific ppm zones in 1D NMR metabolomics spectra within NMRProcFlow's interactive viewer so that scoped processing steps—especially local baseline correction and realignment of ppm areas—can be applied only where needed, e.g. to eliminate residual macromolecule effects without distorting peaks elsewhere. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-017-1178-y
skills.summary: Delimiting specific ppm zones in 1D NMR metabolomics spectra within NMRProcFlow's interactive viewer so that scoped processing steps—especially local baseline correction and realignment of ppm areas—can be applied only where needed, e.g. to eliminate residual macromolecule effects without distorting peaks elsewhere.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra already carry a flat baseline and only need downstream steps such as ppm-scale calibration, realignment, or binning — apply those steps directly instead The user wants a fully automated batch-mode black-box workflow without interactive inspection; NMRProcFlow's delimitation is deliberately interactive GUI-driven The data are not 1D NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. feature tables or 2D NMR); NMRProcFlow's viewer and processing stages target 1D spectra

skills.name: pqn-normalization-of-metabolomics-data
skills.search_text: pqn-normalization-of-metabolomics-data Use when a peak-aligned X matrix (peaks × samples) with biological/blank class labels still shows dilution-driven intensity variation across biological samples and must be normalized before KNN imputation and G-log transformation in the Galaxy-M DIMS pipeline. The input is raw unaligned mass-spectral data (transient/.dat or centroided peaks) rather than an aligned X matrix — peak picking, calibration, SIM-stitching and Align Samples must run first. The matrix has not yet been through Blank Filtering and Sample Filtering, since PQN sits mid-way in the documented Galaxy-M DIMS cleansing sequence and its input should be the filtered peak table. The data are LC-MS features already processed by the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe rather than the DIMS workflow data considered here. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) to a peak-aligned DIMS feature matrix inside the Galaxy-M data-cleansing workflow, correcting for sample dilution differences before missing-value imputation and G-log variance stabilization. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: Applies probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) to a peak-aligned DIMS feature matrix inside the Galaxy-M data-cleansing workflow, correcting for sample dilution differences before missing-value imputation and G-log variance stabilization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw unaligned mass-spectral data (transient/.dat or centroided peaks) rather than an aligned X matrix — peak picking, calibration, SIM-stitching and Align Samples must run first. The matrix has not yet been through Blank Filtering and Sample Filtering, since PQN sits mid-way in the documented Galaxy-M DIMS cleansing sequence and its input should be the filtered peak table. The data are LC-MS features already processed by the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe rather than the DIMS workflow data considered here.

skills.description: Use when plasma/serum samples carry time-stamp-derived pre- and post-centrifugation delay metadata and you need to model or validate metabolite stability, or generate performance reports per delay type.
skills.name: pre-post-centrifugation-delay-stratification
skills.search_text: pre-post-centrifugation-delay-stratification Use when plasma/serum samples carry time-stamp-derived pre- and post-centrifugation delay metadata and you need to model or validate metabolite stability, or generate performance reports per delay type. Samples lack time-stamp-derived pre- or post-centrifugation delay information — the stratification and PRIMA performance report cannot be computed Analytes are known not to follow the linear mixed-model response (e.g. glucose in EDTA and LiHep plasma showed unexpectedly large MPE at later time points), so model-based stability claims would be misleading The goal is pass/fail sample QC only (Bruker BiobankQC provides that basic output); PRIMA stratification is for exploring delay effects and delay-specific modeling http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 http://edamontology.org/topic_3337 Stratifies NMR-metabolomics blood samples by pre- vs post-centrifugation processing delay so that linear mixed models can be fitted (or applied) separately for each delay type, quantifying how each metabolite's concentration drifts with prolonged handling. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c04938
skills.summary: Stratifies NMR-metabolomics blood samples by pre- vs post-centrifugation processing delay so that linear mixed models can be fitted (or applied) separately for each delay type, quantifying how each metabolite's concentration drifts with prolonged handling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack time-stamp-derived pre- or post-centrifugation delay information — the stratification and PRIMA performance report cannot be computed Analytes are known not to follow the linear mixed-model response (e.g. glucose in EDTA and LiHep plasma showed unexpectedly large MPE at later time points), so model-based stability claims would be misleading The goal is pass/fail sample QC only (Bruker BiobankQC provides that basic output); PRIMA stratification is for exploring delay effects and delay-specific modeling

skills.description: Use when paired LC-MS/MS feature lists exist for pre-dosing (blank) and post-dosing biological matrices (e.g., plasma, lung, urine, feces) and the goal is non-targeted isolation of dosage-related exogenous components for prototype/metabolite annotation.
skills.name: pre-post-dosing-feature-comparison
skills.search_text: pre-post-dosing-feature-comparison Use when paired LC-MS/MS feature lists exist for pre-dosing (blank) and post-dosing biological matrices (e.g., plasma, lung, urine, feces) and the goal is non-targeted isolation of dosage-related exogenous components for prototype/metabolite annotation. When no matched pre-dosing (blank) matrix is available for the post-dosing sample, since background subtraction requires the blank comparison. When the goal is targeted, structure-predicted quantification of a predefined metabolite panel rather than non-targeted discovery of exogenous components. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A non-targeted LC-MS/MS background-subtraction workflow (PATBS) that compares post-dosing sample feature lists against matched pre-dosing (blank) matrices to retain exogenous, dosage-related components, then labels them as prototypes or metabolites of a model herb (here, semen Armeniacae Amarum, CKXR). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: A non-targeted LC-MS/MS background-subtraction workflow (PATBS) that compares post-dosing sample feature lists against matched pre-dosing (blank) matrices to retain exogenous, dosage-related components, then labels them as prototypes or metabolites of a model herb (here, semen Armeniacae Amarum, CKXR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no matched pre-dosing (blank) matrix is available for the post-dosing sample, since background subtraction requires the blank comparison. When the goal is targeted, structure-predicted quantification of a predefined metabolite panel rather than non-targeted discovery of exogenous components.

skills.search_text: preanalytical-delay-count-tabulation-by-sample-type Use when you have PRIMA Panel stability time point data (minutes, annotated by sample type and pre-/postcentrifugation delay) and need per-sample-type counts of parameters stable within a fixed delay threshold. skills.summary: Tabulates, per sample type (EDTA plasma, serum, LiHep plasma), the number of metabolic parameters whose stability time points fall within a chosen pre- or postcentrifugation delay window (e.g. 4 h), using the PRIMA Panel's SPREC-sorted stability time point data.

skills.description: Use when blood samples collected in EDTA/LiHep/serum tubes carry recorded pre- and postcentrifugation delay times and you need to predict metabolite concentration changes or compute 20% stability time points per tube type.
skills.name: preanalytical-delay-effect-quantification-across-tube-types

skills.description: Use when evaluating spectral-search identification performance: you have query and reference peak lists (e.g. QqQ vs QqTOF ESI-MS2 spectra), per-pair similarity scores, and need precision/recall/F at a fixed score cutoff such as 0.6.

skills.search_text: precision-recall-metric-computation Use when evaluating spectral-search identification performance: you have query and reference peak lists (e.g. QqQ vs QqTOF ESI-MS2 spectra), per-pair similarity scores, and need precision/recall/F at a fixed score cutoff such as 0.6. The reference spectra are already merged across collision-induced dissociation conditions — the merged search is a separate analysis (paper reports merged data improves precision by 21-23% at score 0.6), so unmerged-baseline metrics would not apply directly. The input is EI mass spectra intended for the Stein-Scott regime; the ESI-MS2-optimized exponents m=0.5/n=2 are not the appropriate weights there. Computes precision, recall, and F-value for MassBank-style spectral searches by classifying top-hit identifications against a similarity-score threshold (0.6 in the paper), using a weighted cosine correlation with ESI-MS2-optimized exponents (m=0.5 on peak intensity, n=2 on m/z). This quantifies how well unmerged versus merged ESI-MS2 reference data identify compounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.1777

This quantifies how well unmerged versus merged ESI-MS2 reference data identify compounds.

Input spectra have already been pre-processed off-server (Peak Merge Threshold / Peak Filtering) and the goal is scoring accuracy rather than runtime benchmarking The goal is molecule identification output itself rather than measuring runtime scaling across precursor tolerance thresholds http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks VInSMoC runtime in exact and variable search modes by sweeping precursor ion tolerance values over one mass spectral search task per tolerance, comparing against other search engines such as Dereplicator+ on a fixed spectrum/database pair. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks VInSMoC runtime in exact and variable search modes by sweeping precursor ion tolerance values over one mass spectral search task per tolerance, comparing against other search engines such as Dereplicator+ on a fixed spectrum/database pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra have already been pre-processed off-server (Peak Merge Threshold / Peak Filtering) and the goal is scoring accuracy rather than runtime benchmarking The goal is molecule identification output itself rather than measuring runtime scaling across precursor tolerance thresholds

skills.description: Use when you hold a list of precursor accurate masses (e.g., oxPC precursor m/z values in a CSV) and need compound-level annotations — species name, molecular formula, expert-system score — from CMM 3.0.
skills.name: precursor-mass-annotation
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-annotation Use when you hold a list of precursor accurate masses (e.g., oxPC precursor m/z values in a CSV) and need compound-level annotations — species name, molecular formula, expert-system score — from CMM 3.0. Input is already an annotated feature table — re-annotating peaks that already carry formula/annotation fields adds nothing. The goal is MS2 spectral comparison or spectral quality assessment; CMM 3.0 provides separate dedicated services for those, not the oxPC annotation service. The search must span the full CMM experimental (332,665) or predicted (681,198) metabolite space rather than the specialized in-house oxidized lipid library. http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Batch-annotation of precursor accurate masses — specifically oxidized glycerophosphocholine (oxPC) m/z values — against the CMM 3.0 dedicated oxidized-lipid annotation service, returning species names, molecular formulas, and expert-system-scored annotation labels. The CMM 3.0 in-house oxidized lipid library covers oxidized lipids not present in other databases. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00720
skills.summary: Batch-annotation of precursor accurate masses — specifically oxidized glycerophosphocholine (oxPC) m/z values — against the CMM 3.0 dedicated oxidized-lipid annotation service, returning species names, molecular formulas, and expert-system-scored annotation labels. The CMM 3.0 in-house oxidized lipid library covers oxidized lipids not present in other databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated feature table — re-annotating peaks that already carry formula/annotation fields adds nothing. The goal is MS2 spectral comparison or spectral quality assessment; CMM 3.0 provides separate dedicated services for those, not the oxPC annotation service. The search must span the full CMM experimental (332,665) or predicted (681,198) metabolite space rather than the specialized in-house oxidized lipid library.

skills.description: Use when searching query tandem mass spectra against large structure databases (e.g., PubChem, DNP) and you must first restrict candidate molecules by observed precursor mass before running fragment-matching scores.
skills.name: precursor-mass-candidate-filtering
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-candidate-filtering Use when searching query tandem mass spectra against large structure databases (e.g., PubChem, DNP) and you must first restrict candidate molecules by observed precursor mass before running fragment-matching scores. The query spectra are in negative ionization mode or from instruments/techniques not represented in the combined CID/HCD positive-mode training data The structure database contains very small molecules (<400 Da) or very heavy molecules (>1000 Da), where molDiscovery's fragmentation approach performs poorly or is computationally insufficient You need statistical significance for non-peptidic molecules — no p-value computation exists for general molecules, only an MCMC approach for peptidic ones http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Narrows the molecular structure database for molDiscovery spectral search by retrieving only candidate molecules whose precursor mass falls within 0.02 Da of the observed precursor mass of each query tandem mass spectrum, before probabilistic fragmentation scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Narrows the molecular structure database for molDiscovery spectral search by retrieving only candidate molecules whose precursor mass falls within 0.02 Da of the observed precursor mass of each query tandem mass spectrum, before probabilistic fragmentation scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectra are in negative ionization mode or from instruments/techniques not represented in the combined CID/HCD positive-mode training data The structure database contains very small molecules (<400 Da) or very heavy molecules (>1000 Da), where molDiscovery's fragmentation approach performs poorly or is computationally insufficient You need statistical significance for non-peptidic molecules — no p-value computation exists for general molecules, only an MCMC approach for peptidic ones

skills.description: Use when a set of LC-MS precursor queries (measured m/z, optional RT) needs candidate structures from a database narrowed down, and orthogonal predicted properties (RT, CCS) are available to re-rank candidates.
skills.name: precursor-mass-candidate-screening
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-candidate-screening Use when a set of LC-MS precursor queries (measured m/z, optional RT) needs candidate structures from a database narrowed down, and orthogonal predicted properties (RT, CCS) are available to re-rank candidates. Molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se, since SigmaCCS cannot predict them The adduct is not one of the three encoded ion types ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-), because SigmaCCS handles only these three adduct ion types Input is already a single confident identification per query with no candidate ambiguity, so multi-stage candidate re-ranking adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A candidate-filtering workflow that screens lipid/small-molecule identification candidates by precursor m/z matching and then progressively re-ranks them with predicted retention time (GNN-RT) and predicted CCS (SigmaCCS), improving correct-identification recall in LC-MS lipidomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-023-00939-w
skills.summary: A candidate-filtering workflow that screens lipid/small-molecule identification candidates by precursor m/z matching and then progressively re-ranks them with predicted retention time (GNN-RT) and predicted CCS (SigmaCCS), improving correct-identification recall in LC-MS lipidomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Molecules contain elements outside C, H, O, N, P, S, F, Cl, Br, I, Co, As, and Se, since SigmaCCS cannot predict them The adduct is not one of the three encoded ion types ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-), because SigmaCCS handles only these three adduct ion types Input is already a single confident identification per query with no candidate ambiguity, so multi-stage candidate re-ranking adds no value

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how often adduct annotations in a mass spectral library (e.g., GNPS MGF spectra with SMILES) are wrong or can be corrected from SMILES plus precursor m/z alone.
skills.name: precursor-mass-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-consistency-checking Use when you need to quantify how often adduct annotations in a mass spectral library (e.g., GNPS MGF spectra with SMILES) are wrong or can be corrected from SMILES plus precursor m/z alone. You need plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments — the article states current filters lack such checks and wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass will go unnoticed. The spectra lack valid SMILES annotations, so repair_adduct_based_on_smiles cannot derive a neutral monoisotopic mass. You are repairing parent mass errors where the parent mass was calculated from the molar mass instead of the monoisotopic mass — that is the separate Repair Parent Mass Is Molar Mass filter. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 This skill reproduces the error-rate estimation workflow for the 'repair adduct and parent mass based on SMILES' filter in the matchms library-cleaning pipeline, which corrects a spectrum's adduct by testing candidate adducts against the SMILES-derived neutral monoisotopic mass and the observed precursor m/z. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: This skill reproduces the error-rate estimation workflow for the 'repair adduct and parent mass based on SMILES' filter in the matchms library-cleaning pipeline, which corrects a spectrum's adduct by testing candidate adducts against the SMILES-derived neutral monoisotopic mass and the observed precursor m/z.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments — the article states current filters lack such checks and wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass will go unnoticed. The spectra lack valid SMILES annotations, so repair_adduct_based_on_smiles cannot derive a neutral monoisotopic mass. You are repairing parent mass errors where the parent mass was calculated from the molar mass instead of the monoisotopic mass — that is the separate Repair Parent Mass Is Molar Mass filter.

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra of suspected chemically modified metabolites (methylation, acetylation, phosphorylation, hydroxylation) must be associated with library spectra of their non-modified parent compounds by measuring precursor and fragment mass shifts.
skills.name: precursor-mass-defect-computation
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-defect-computation Use when MS/MS spectra of suspected chemically modified metabolites (methylation, acetylation, phosphorylation, hydroxylation) must be associated with library spectra of their non-modified parent compounds by measuring precursor and fragment mass shifts. The spectrum already matches a library entry directly at MSI level 2 by precursor accurate mass and MS/MS matching — no hybrid head-to-tail comparison is needed The input is MS1-only data with no MS/MS fragmentation, since fragment mass shifts cannot be computed No plausible non-modified parent compound exists in the spectral library, leaving no parent spectrum to compare head-to-tail http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes precursor mass shifts (and consistent fragment mass shifts) between experimental modified-metabolite MS/MS spectra and their non-modified parent library entries, so that modified compounds (e.g., methyladenosine vs adenosine) can be linked to library spectra via the NIST17 hybrid search head-to-tail comparison mechanism. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Computes precursor mass shifts (and consistent fragment mass shifts) between experimental modified-metabolite MS/MS spectra and their non-modified parent library entries, so that modified compounds (e.g., methyladenosine vs adenosine) can be linked to library spectra via the NIST17 hybrid search head-to-tail comparison mechanism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum already matches a library entry directly at MSI level 2 by precursor accurate mass and MS/MS matching — no hybrid head-to-tail comparison is needed The input is MS1-only data with no MS/MS fragmentation, since fragment mass shifts cannot be computed No plausible non-modified parent compound exists in the spectral library, leaving no parent spectrum to compare head-to-tail

skills.description: Use when comparing two tandem MS spectra (e.g. a library spectrum vs. a query spectrum of a related molecule) and you need to score match quality including peaks shifted by the precursor mass difference.
skills.name: precursor-mass-difference-alignment
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-difference-alignment Use when comparing two tandem MS spectra (e.g. a library spectrum vs. a query spectrum of a related molecule) and you need to score match quality including peaks shifted by the precursor mass difference. Only a single spectrum is available and no pairwise comparison is requested The goal is peptide/proteomics spectral identification against ProteomeXchange data rather than metabolomics mirror-match quality assessment The comparison requires full peak-by-peak fragment assignment rather than an aggregate similarity score Computes standard and shifted cosine similarity scores for a pair of MS/MS spectra, where the shifted variant additionally matches fragment peaks offset by the precursor mass difference between the spectra, as exposed by the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver's mirror plots. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Computes standard and shifted cosine similarity scores for a pair of MS/MS spectra, where the shifted variant additionally matches fragment peaks offset by the precursor mass difference between the spectra, as exposed by the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver's mirror plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single spectrum is available and no pairwise comparison is requested The goal is peptide/proteomics spectral identification against ProteomeXchange data rather than metabolomics mirror-match quality assessment The comparison requires full peak-by-peak fragment assignment rather than an aggregate similarity score

skills.description: Use when a large corpus of unidentified spectra has been clustered (e.g., GLEAMS clusters with medoid indexes) and you need to annotate representative spectra via open modification search and derive the mass-difference profile.
skills.name: precursor-mass-difference-analysis
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-difference-analysis Use when a large corpus of unidentified spectra has been clustered (e.g., GLEAMS clusters with medoid indexes) and you need to annotate representative spectra via open modification search and derive the mass-difference profile. The spectra already have confident database-search identifications (no unidentified-cluster annotation is needed) The dataset is small and not clustered — direct closed or open searching of individual spectra is more appropriate than medoid-search-plus-propagation The target library lacks the organism/instrument type of the query spectra (e.g., non-Human HCD data against the Human HCD library) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate previously unidentified MS/MS spectra via open modification searching of spectrum-cluster medoids, then catalog the precursor mass differences of the resulting PSMs to characterize post-translational modifications and other mass shifts. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Annotate previously unidentified MS/MS spectra via open modification searching of spectrum-cluster medoids, then catalog the precursor mass differences of the resulting PSMs to characterize post-translational modifications and other mass shifts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra already have confident database-search identifications (no unidentified-cluster annotation is needed) The dataset is small and not clustered — direct closed or open searching of individual spectra is more appropriate than medoid-search-plus-propagation The target library lacks the organism/instrument type of the query spectra (e.g., non-Human HCD data against the Human HCD library)

skills.description: Use when assembling analog compound-pair benchmarks from MS/MS libraries — you have enumerated pairs and must enforce precursor mass and adduct eligibility before substructure matching.
skills.name: precursor-mass-eligibility-filtering
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-eligibility-filtering Use when assembling analog compound-pair benchmarks from MS/MS libraries — you have enumerated pairs and must enforce precursor mass and adduct eligibility before substructure matching. Your goal is to filter spectral peaks within a single spectrum (e.g. removing peaks <1% of base peak intensity) — that is peak preprocessing, not pair eligibility screening. You have already identified modification sites via RDKit GetSubstructMatch and edge counting; this filter runs earlier, before structural matching. Precursor masses exceed 2000 Da or the mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller precursor — such pairs are excluded by design, not candidates for further processing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Filters within-library compound pairs by precursor mass constraints (mass < 2000 Da, mass difference < 50% of the smaller precursor mass, and matching M+H adducts) to define an analog benchmark of single-modification pairs, yielding 12,909 pairs from four reference MS/MS libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Filters within-library compound pairs by precursor mass constraints (mass < 2000 Da, mass difference < 50% of the smaller precursor mass, and matching M+H adducts) to define an analog benchmark of single-modification pairs, yielding 12,909 pairs from four reference MS/MS libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to filter spectral peaks within a single spectrum (e.g. removing peaks <1% of base peak intensity) — that is peak preprocessing, not pair eligibility screening. You have already identified modification sites via RDKit GetSubstructMatch and edge counting; this filter runs earlier, before structural matching. Precursor masses exceed 2000 Da or the mass difference exceeds 50% of the smaller precursor — such pairs are excluded by design, not candidates for further processing.

skills.description: Use when an unannotated molecular feature defined by precursor m/z (e.g., m/z 266.138, 280.153, 294.169) or an MS/MS spectrum must be searched across tissues or mapped from an animal model into public human metabolomics studies.
skills.name: precursor-mass-feature-tracking
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-feature-tracking Use when an unannotated molecular feature defined by precursor m/z (e.g., m/z 266.138, 280.153, 294.169) or an MS/MS spectrum must be searched across tissues or mapped from an animal model into public human metabolomics studies. The input is a processed feature table with no MS/MS peak lists — tissueMASST requires precursor mass plus fragment spectra to search. A fully validated (MSI Level 1) structural identification is required; spectral matching yields Level 2 or 3 annotations only. The spectrum was acquired with poor fragmentation or missing fragments, so reliable network edges and library matches cannot be formed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Tracks an unknown or annotated molecular feature by its precursor m/z and MS/MS spectrum across tissues and public metabolomics repositories using tissueMASST, bridging mouse-model findings (e.g., microbially-modulated carnitines in the 3xTg atlas) to human AD datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Tracks an unknown or annotated molecular feature by its precursor m/z and MS/MS spectrum across tissues and public metabolomics repositories using tissueMASST, bridging mouse-model findings (e.g., microbially-modulated carnitines in the 3xTg atlas) to human AD datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a processed feature table with no MS/MS peak lists — tissueMASST requires precursor mass plus fragment spectra to search. A fully validated (MSI Level 1) structural identification is required; spectral matching yields Level 2 or 3 annotations only. The spectrum was acquired with poor fragmentation or missing fragments, so reliable network edges and library matches cannot be formed.

skills.description: Use when matching EI-MS query spectra against a million-scale in-silico library and the query's molecular mass is known or estimable, so candidates can be restricted to a ±5 Da mass window to improve recall@1/recall@10.
skills.name: precursor-mass-filtering-spectrum-search
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-filtering-spectrum-search Use when matching EI-MS query spectra against a million-scale in-silico library and the query's molecular mass is known or estimable, so candidates can be restricted to a ±5 Da mass window to improve recall@1/recall@10. The query spectrum has no reliable molecular mass estimate, so a 5 Da window cannot be constructed The candidate library is small enough that exhaustive exact search (e.g., brute-force WCS) is already tractable and the filter's speed benefit is moot The query molecules are outside the library's chemical scope (e.g., mass ≥ 1000 Da, ionic compounds, or elements beyond H, C, O, N, P, S, Cl, F, Br, I, Si), which the library filtering steps already excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Restricts spectrum-matching candidates in the FastEI pipeline to in-silico library entries whose molecular mass is within 5 Da of the query's molecular mass, before or after approximate nearest-neighbor search with the HNSW index. This raises identification accuracy (e.g., recall@10 from 80.4% to 88.3%) at little additional cost. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Restricts spectrum-matching candidates in the FastEI pipeline to in-silico library entries whose molecular mass is within 5 Da of the query's molecular mass, before or after approximate nearest-neighbor search with the HNSW index. This raises identification accuracy (e.g., recall@10 from 80.4% to 88.3%) at little additional cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectrum has no reliable molecular mass estimate, so a 5 Da window cannot be constructed The candidate library is small enough that exhaustive exact search (e.g., brute-force WCS) is already tractable and the filter's speed benefit is moot The query molecules are outside the library's chemical scope (e.g., mass ≥ 1000 Da, ionic compounds, or elements beyond H, C, O, N, P, S, Cl, F, Br, I, Si), which the library filtering steps already excluded

skills.description: Use when dereplicating untargeted LC-MS2 features (.mzML input) against public spectral libraries (GNPS, HMDB, MassBank) inside MAW-R and you need reproducible precursor-ppm and similarity-score filtering of candidates.
skills.name: precursor-mass-ppm-filtering
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-ppm-filtering Use when dereplicating untargeted LC-MS2 features (.mzML input) against public spectral libraries (GNPS, HMDB, MassBank) inside MAW-R and you need reproducible precursor-ppm and similarity-score filtering of candidates. You are doing compound-structure candidate selection or chemical classification (MAW-Py/RDKit, SIRIUS, Tanimoto similarity), not spectral library dereplication. Input is not tandem MS2 data in .mzML format (e.g., already a feature table or MS1-only peaks). You need annotation against compound structure databases such as PubChem/COCONUT via MetFrag — MAW v1 integrates only SIRIUS for compound databases and spectral dereplication covers GNPS/HMDB/MassBank. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 MAW's spectral database dereplication step: it matches MS2 query spectra (from .mzML) against GNPS, HMDB, and MassBank spectral libraries in R/Spectra, gating candidate matches by precursor m/z at 15 ppm and similarity thresholds (GNPS 0.85, HMDB/MassBank cosine 0.70, MAW metrics ≥ 0.50). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00695-y
skills.summary: MAW's spectral database dereplication step: it matches MS2 query spectra (from .mzML) against GNPS, HMDB, and MassBank spectral libraries in R/Spectra, gating candidate matches by precursor m/z at 15 ppm and similarity thresholds (GNPS 0.85, HMDB/MassBank cosine 0.70, MAW metrics ≥ 0.50).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are doing compound-structure candidate selection or chemical classification (MAW-Py/RDKit, SIRIUS, Tanimoto similarity), not spectral library dereplication. Input is not tandem MS2 data in .mzML format (e.g., already a feature table or MS1-only peaks). skills.description: Use when running modified cosine (or similar score-based) analogue searching against a large library (e.g., 302,514 GNPS spectra) and you need to bound pairwise score computations by precursor m/z proximity, or when benchmarking the runtime cost of such preselection.
skills.name: precursor-mass-preselection-filtering
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-preselection-filtering Use when running modified cosine (or similar score-based) analogue searching against a large library (e.g., 302,514 GNPS spectra) and you need to bound pairwise score computations by precursor m/z proximity, or when benchmarking the runtime cost of such preselection. When running MS2Query-style embedding-based search (MS2Deepscore + random forest re-ranking), which deliberately performs no precursor m/z preselection When the goal is exact library matching with a tight mass tolerance (e.g., 0.25 Da), which is a different filtering regime When candidate analogues are expected to lie outside the chosen precursor m/z window, since preselection will discard them before scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A library-spectra preselection filter that restricts candidate matches to those within a maximum precursor m/z difference (e.g., 100 Da) before spectral similarity score computation, as used for the matchms modified cosine analogue search benchmarked against MS2Query. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-37446-4
skills.summary: A library-spectra preselection filter that restricts candidate matches to those within a maximum precursor m/z difference (e.g., 100 Da) before spectral similarity score computation, as used for the matchms modified cosine analogue search benchmarked against MS2Query.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When running MS2Query-style embedding-based search (MS2Deepscore + random forest re-ranking), which deliberately performs no precursor m/z preselection When the goal is exact library matching with a tight mass tolerance (e.g., 0.25 Da), which is a different filtering regime When candidate analogues are expected to lie outside the chosen precursor m/z window, since preselection will discard them before scoring

skills.description: Use when query MS/MS spectra from molecular networking or dereplication jobs show putative analogs of known compounds: the goal is to find library hits whose fragment peaks are systematically shifted by the precursor mass difference δ ± the user-defined fragment mass tolerance, rather than.
skills.name: precursor-mass-shift-analog-detection
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-shift-analog-detection Use when query MS/MS spectra from molecular networking or dereplication jobs show putative analogs of known compounds: the goal is to find library hits whose fragment peaks are systematically shifted by the precursor mass difference δ ± the user-defined fragment mass tolerance, rather than. When the goal is exact compound identification against known library spectra — use the standard GNPS exact spectral library search instead; variable dereplication intentionally relaxes fragment matching by δ ± tolerance and may produce false analog assignments. When the input is already a dereplication result table or a molecular network graph — this skill operates on query MS/MS spectra against reference library spectra, not on downstream network annotations. When δ is unknown or cannot be computed from the precursor masses (e.g. no precursor m/z information for either spectrum) — the method fundamentally depends on δ as determined by the precursor mass difference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 A modification-tolerant spectral library search (GNPS variable dereplication) that matches a query MS/MS spectrum to a library compound whose peaks differ from the query peaks by the precursor mass difference δ ± fragment mass tolerance, enabling detection of putative analogs rather than exact known compound identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nbt.3597
skills.summary: A modification-tolerant spectral library search (GNPS variable dereplication) that matches a query MS/MS spectrum to a library compound whose peaks differ from the query peaks by the precursor mass difference δ ± fragment mass tolerance, enabling detection of putative analogs rather than exact known compound identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is exact compound identification against known library spectra — use the standard GNPS exact spectral library search instead; variable dereplication intentionally relaxes fragment matching by δ ± tolerance and may produce false analog assignments. When the input is already a dereplication result table or a molecular network graph — this skill operates on query MS/MS spectra against reference library spectra, not on downstream network annotations. When δ is unknown or cannot be computed from the precursor masses (e.g. no precursor m/z information for either spectrum) — the method fundamentally depends on δ as determined by the precursor mass difference.

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-HRMS feature tables from a sample (e.g., AFFF) must be aligned to solvent-blank feature tables by precursor m/z to distinguish real sample features from background contamination.
skills.name: precursor-mass-tolerance-alignment
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-tolerance-alignment Use when untargeted LC-HRMS feature tables from a sample (e.g., AFFF) must be aligned to solvent-blank feature tables by precursor m/z to distinguish real sample features from background contamination. Input is already a blank-filtered feature list or the downstream annotation does not require background subtraction. The blank files are not from the same LC-HRMS acquisition batch, since the ±0.005 Da precursor alignment assumes identical ion detection across sample and blank runs. You are processing lipids with LipidMatch rather than PFAS: the README notes the Lipid/TWeen flags must be toggled, otherwise Modular 'defaults to PFAS analysis'. Aligns sample and blank vendor feature tables by precursor mass (±0.005 Da) in FluoroMatch Modular so blank-derived features can be matched and removed as background before downstream PFAS annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Aligns sample and blank vendor feature tables by precursor mass (±0.005 Da) in FluoroMatch Modular so blank-derived features can be matched and removed as background before downstream PFAS annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a blank-filtered feature list or the downstream annotation does not require background subtraction. The blank files are not from the same LC-HRMS acquisition batch, since the ±0.005 Da precursor alignment assumes identical ion detection across sample and blank runs. You are processing lipids with LipidMatch rather than PFAS: the README notes the Lipid/TWeen flags must be toggled, otherwise Modular 'defaults to PFAS analysis'.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking dereplication tools (DEREPLICATOR+, DEREPLICATOR-G, DEREPLICATOR) on spectra with known metabolite annotations and you need to measure how precursor mass tolerance settings (e.g. 0.5 Da vs 0.02 Da) change top-rank identification rates.
skills.name: precursor-mass-tolerance-benchmarking
skills.search_text: precursor-mass-tolerance-benchmarking Use when benchmarking dereplication tools (DEREPLICATOR+, DEREPLICATOR-G, DEREPLICATOR) on spectra with known metabolite annotations and you need to measure how precursor mass tolerance settings (e.g. 0.5 Da vs 0.02 Da) change top-rank identification rates.
