skills.summary: Automated, omics-agnostic extraction and inspection of precursor-ion peak metrics (errors in mass, retention time, arrival time) from raw MS data using PeakQC, which auto-tracks the topmost abundant MS1 ions or uses user-specified reference ions and flags outliers with Isolation Forest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw MS data but already identified spectral matches — the article notes identification-based QC tools 'do little to pinpoint the specific causes of performance deterioration', so this skill is not for scoring identification outputs The task is interactive visualization or export of individual chromatograms/MS2 mirror plots rather than batch QC — the Mirador tool in IonToolPack is the appropriate choice The goal is unattended, command-line QC across batches over months and years — per the discussion this is planned functionality, not yet delivered by the GUI workflow

skills.description: Use when a USI-loaded or MGF-loaded MS/MS spectrum (e.g. mzspec:PXD004732:...:scan:41840 or iPRG2012.mgf) still contains the precursor ion peak and must be cleaned before fragment annotation, noise filtering, or plotting.
skills.name: precursor-peak-removal
skills.search_text: precursor-peak-removal Use when a USI-loaded or MGF-loaded MS/MS spectrum (e.g. mzspec:PXD004732:...:scan:41840 or iPRG2012.mgf) still contains the precursor ion peak and must be cleaned before fragment annotation, noise filtering, or plotting. Input is raw spectral data still in file form (mzML/MGF) — spectrum_utils does not provide functionality to read spectral data files and relies on external tools such as pymzML or Pyteomics for this task The precursor ion signal itself is the target of the analysis (e.g. intact precursor characterization) rather than the fragment peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Removes the precursor ion peak from an MS/MS spectrum loaded into spectrum_utils, so that downstream processing, fragment annotation (a/b/y ions), and visualization focus on fragment peaks rather than the intact precursor. It is one of the standard spectrum processing operations the package provides. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b04884
skills.summary: Removes the precursor ion peak from an MS/MS spectrum loaded into spectrum_utils, so that downstream processing, fragment annotation (a/b/y ions), and visualization focus on fragment peaks rather than the intact precursor. It is one of the standard spectrum processing operations the package provides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spectral data still in file form (mzML/MGF) — spectrum_utils does not provide functionality to read spectral data files and relies on external tools such as pymzML or Pyteomics for this task The precursor ion signal itself is the target of the analysis (e.g. intact precursor characterization) rather than the fragment peaks

skills.description: Use when MS-DIAL result tables contain raw precursor and fragment ion intensities that must be converted to comparable 0–1 scales before rendering MS1×MS2 grayscale fingerprint images for CNN input.
skills.name: precursor-product-ion-intensity-normalization
skills.search_text: precursor-product-ion-intensity-normalization Use when MS-DIAL result tables contain raw precursor and fragment ion intensities that must be converted to comparable 0–1 scales before rendering MS1×MS2 grayscale fingerprint images for CNN input. Input is already an aligned feature table destined for PCA, OPLS-DA, or Random Forest — those baselines consume the feature matrix directly, not the 0–1 normalized image-encoding values Data comes from a non-MS-DIAL preprocessing pipeline where product-ion intensities are not grouped by precursor ion, since the 0–1 product scaling is defined relative to product ions of the same precursor http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Normalizes MS-DIAL-extracted precursor (MS1) ion intensities to a 0–1 global range and product-ion (MS2) intensities to a 0–1 range relative to product ions of the same precursor, so they can be encoded as size and grayscale intensity in the MS2toImg molecular fingerprint scatter image. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Normalizes MS-DIAL-extracted precursor (MS1) ion intensities to a 0–1 global range and product-ion (MS2) intensities to a 0–1 range relative to product ions of the same precursor, so they can be encoded as size and grayscale intensity in the MS2toImg molecular fingerprint scatter image.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned feature table destined for PCA, OPLS-DA, or Random Forest — those baselines consume the feature matrix directly, not the 0–1 normalized image-encoding values Data comes from a non-MS-DIAL preprocessing pipeline where product-ion intensities are not grouped by precursor ion, since the 0–1 product scaling is defined relative to product ions of the same precursor

skills.description: Use when annotating pseudo MS/MS spectra (MGF) reconstructed from MS1-only LC-MS or imaging MS data, where each spectrum contains multiple ion forms (e.g. [M+H]+, adducts, multimers) rather than a single true precursor.
skills.name: precursor-tolerant-open-search
skills.search_text: precursor-tolerant-open-search Use when annotating pseudo MS/MS spectra (MGF) reconstructed from MS1-only LC-MS or imaging MS data, where each spectrum contains multiple ion forms (e.g. [M+H]+, adducts, multimers) rather than a single true precursor. When the query spectra are genuine MS/MS with a single predefined precursor — the precursor-tolerant reverse search is designed for pseudo MS/MS with multiple ion forms, not standard MS/MS library matching When only molecular formula annotation (MSI level 4) is needed and no structural (level 2/3) annotation via MS/MS library matching is required When the reference library was acquired exclusively at high collision energies without low-energy spectra — peak scaling was validated on low-energy in-source fragments and may not align well with hard fragmentation patterns http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 An asymmetric reverse spectral search against an indexed MS/MS library that does not assume a single predefined precursor; every ion in the pseudo MS/MS spectrum is treated as a potential precursor, and unmatched query peaks are discarded when computing scores. It enables structural annotation of MS1-only LC-MS and imaging data whose pseudo MS/MS spectra carry adducts, multimers, and co-eluting contaminants absent from reference spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: An asymmetric reverse spectral search against an indexed MS/MS library that does not assume a single predefined precursor; every ion in the pseudo MS/MS spectrum is treated as a potential precursor, and unmatched query peaks are discarded when computing scores. It enables structural annotation of MS1-only LC-MS and imaging data whose pseudo MS/MS spectra carry adducts, multimers, and co-eluting contaminants absent from reference spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query spectra are genuine MS/MS with a single predefined precursor — the precursor-tolerant reverse search is designed for pseudo MS/MS with multiple ion forms, not standard MS/MS library matching When only molecular formula annotation (MSI level 4) is needed and no structural (level 2/3) annotation via MS/MS library matching is required When the reference library was acquired exclusively at high collision energies without low-energy spectra — peak scaling was validated on low-energy in-source fragments and may not align well with hard fragmentation patterns

skills.description: Use when annotating full-scan MS data (MS1-only mzML/mzXML/imzML or pseudo MS/MS mgf) against a reference MS/MS library, especially when the true precursor m/z is unknown or multiple adducts/multimers must be matched at once.
skills.name: precursor-tolerant-reverse-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: precursor-tolerant-reverse-spectral-matching Use when annotating full-scan MS data (MS1-only mzML/mzXML/imzML or pseudo MS/MS mgf) against a reference MS/MS library, especially when the true precursor m/z is unknown or multiple adducts/multimers must be matched at once. The data already contain true MS/MS scans — use conventional MS/MS library search (forward cosine/modified cosine) instead of pseudo MS/MS reverse matching You need strict isomeric-level annotation with a confirmed precursor mass rather than precursor-tolerant level 2/3 annotation of MS1-only features For molecular networking, where modified cosine (>= 0.8, >= 6 matched peaks) with ions larger than the feature m/z removed is required instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reverse spectral matching of deconvolved MS1 pseudo MS/MS spectra (from in-source fragments) against peak scale-adjusted MS/MS libraries such as GNPS, using a precursor-tolerant (open) search that accommodates multiple ion forms simultaneously to achieve level 2/3 structural annotation of MS1-only LC-MS and MS imaging data. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Reverse spectral matching of deconvolved MS1 pseudo MS/MS spectra (from in-source fragments) against peak scale-adjusted MS/MS libraries such as GNPS, using a precursor-tolerant (open) search that accommodates multiple ion forms simultaneously to achieve level 2/3 structural annotation of MS1-only LC-MS and MS imaging data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data already contain true MS/MS scans — use conventional MS/MS library search (forward cosine/modified cosine) instead of pseudo MS/MS reverse matching You need strict isomeric-level annotation with a confirmed precursor mass rather than precursor-tolerant level 2/3 annotation of MS1-only features For molecular networking, where modified cosine (>= 0.8, >= 6 matched peaks) with ions larger than the feature m/z removed is required instead

skills.description: Use when a liputils-produced residue count table (residues as DataFrame index, samples as columns) must be subset by chain-length and unsaturation, e.g. restricting to residues ≤30 carbons because low-resolution compounds like PE(P-40:6)/PE(O-40:7) are ambiguous.
skills.name: predicate-based-residue-index-filtering
skills.search_text: predicate-based-residue-index-filtering Use when a liputils-produced residue count table (residues as DataFrame index, samples as columns) must be subset by chain-length and unsaturation, e.g. restricting to residues ≤30 carbons because low-resolution compounds like PE(P-40:6)/PE(O-40:7) are ambiguous. The input is still a raw lipidomics table of lipid identifiers rather than a residues table — run make_residues_table() first You need to remove ambiguous/isobaric lipids themselves rather than filter residue chain properties — use residues(drop_ambiguous=True) instead All residues should be kept, e.g. when the dataset contains only high-resolution, unambiguous annotations and no long-chain cutoff is warranted http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies liputils' saturated() and max_carbon() predicates to filter the fatty-acyl residue index of a residues-count table, keeping e.g. only unsaturated residues up to a chosen carbon cutoff (C-30 in the ST000668 dietary intervention reanalysis). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70259-9
skills.summary: Applies liputils' saturated() and max_carbon() predicates to filter the fatty-acyl residue index of a residues-count table, keeping e.g. only unsaturated residues up to a chosen carbon cutoff (C-30 in the ST000668 dietary intervention reanalysis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is still a raw lipidomics table of lipid identifiers rather than a residues table — run make_residues_table() first You need to remove ambiguous/isobaric lipids themselves rather than filter residue chain properties — use residues(drop_ambiguous=True) instead All residues should be kept, e.g. when the dataset contains only high-resolution, unambiguous annotations and no long-chain cutoff is warranted

skills.description: Use when aligned, peak-picked HILIC-IM-MS feature tables (positive and/or negative ESI) must be annotated with lipid identities at graded confidence levels using m/z, retention time, and CCS matching.
skills.name: predicted-lipid-database-matching
skills.search_text: predicted-lipid-database-matching Use when aligned, peak-picked HILIC-IM-MS feature tables (positive and/or negative ESI) must be annotated with lipid identities at graded confidence levels using m/z, retention time, and CCS matching. Data lacks ion-mobility CCS values or HILIC retention times, so the higher-confidence tiers (m/z + RT + CCS) cannot be evaluated and only m/z-only matching is possible Input is raw vendor spectra rather than an aligned, peak-picked feature table suitable for loading as a lipydomics Dataset Analytes are non-lipid metabolites outside the 45 lipid classes covered by LiPydomics' experimental and predicted databases Tiered lipid identification by matching HILIC-IM-MS features against LiPydomics' predicted lipid database (145,388 entries) and its experimental m/z-RT-CCS database, annotating each feature at the highest confidence level (m/z, RT, CCS) supported by the data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02560
skills.summary: Tiered lipid identification by matching HILIC-IM-MS features against LiPydomics' predicted lipid database (145,388 entries) and its experimental m/z-RT-CCS database, annotating each feature at the highest confidence level (m/z, RT, CCS) supported by the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks ion-mobility CCS values or HILIC retention times, so the higher-confidence tiers (m/z + RT + CCS) cannot be evaluated and only m/z-only matching is possible Input is raw vendor spectra rather than an aligned, peak-picked feature table suitable for loading as a lipydomics Dataset Analytes are non-lipid metabolites outside the 45 lipid classes covered by LiPydomics' experimental and predicted databases

skills.description: Use when a structure-based metabolism predictor (e.g. CyProduct, GLORY, BioTransformer, ADMET Predictor) has produced predicted metabolite lists and you need a quantitative comparison against known true metabolites.
skills.name: predicted-metabolite-set-matching
skills.search_text: predicted-metabolite-set-matching Use when a structure-based metabolism predictor (e.g. CyProduct, GLORY, BioTransformer, ADMET Predictor) has produced predicted metabolite lists and you need a quantitative comparison against known true metabolites. When the evaluation target is site-of-metabolism (SoM) prediction rather than whole-molecule byproducts — the paper used a separate Jaccard evaluation for SoMs (CypBoM vs FAME2/FAME3). When no curated reference metabolite set exists for the input substrates, since the Jaccard score requires a complete true-metabolite list to compute FN. When evaluating a tool on non-CYP450 biotransformations — CyProduct and its benchmark cover only the nine major human CYP450 enzymes (1A2, 2A6, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 2E1, 3A4). http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0209 Evaluates a metabolite-prediction tool's output by matching its predicted metabolite set against a reference set of true metabolites using the Jaccard score (TP/(TP+FN+FP)), as done to benchmark CyProduct against ADMET Predictor, BioTransformer and GLORY. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Evaluates a metabolite-prediction tool's output by matching its predicted metabolite set against a reference set of true metabolites using the Jaccard score (TP/(TP+FN+FP)), as done to benchmark CyProduct against ADMET Predictor, BioTransformer and GLORY.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the evaluation target is site-of-metabolism (SoM) prediction rather than whole-molecule byproducts — the paper used a separate Jaccard evaluation for SoMs (CypBoM vs FAME2/FAME3). When no curated reference metabolite set exists for the input substrates, since the Jaccard score requires a complete true-metabolite list to compute FN. When evaluating a tool on non-CYP450 biotransformations — CyProduct and its benchmark cover only the nine major human CYP450 enzymes (1A2, 2A6, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 2E1, 3A4).

skills.description: Use when you have mummichog's two input lists (significant m/z features selected by a cutoff and the full reference feature list) and need to know whether the predicted activity network is robust to the cutoff choice, e.g. for sensitivity analysis of the ~60-metabolite moDC prediction.
skills.name: predicted-metabolite-set-stability-assessment
skills.search_text: predicted-metabolite-set-stability-assessment Use when you have mummichog's two input lists (significant m/z features selected by a cutoff and the full reference feature list) and need to know whether the predicted activity network is robust to the cutoff choice, e.g. for sensitivity analysis of the ~60-metabolite moDC prediction. You want to validate metabolite identity rather than prediction stability — mummichog is explicitly not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry for identification The feature-selection cutoff is fixed by the experimental design and there is no need to test its sensitivity; a single mummichog run suffices Input is not an untargeted LC/MS feature table (e.g. targeted assays or pre-annotated compounds), where mummichog's pathway/module approach on unassigned m/z features does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Sweeps the m/z feature-selection p-value cutoff across the range shown in Figure S7, rerunning mummichog's pathway and network module pipeline at each cutoff to quantify how stable the predicted metabolite set is on a given LC/MS dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: Sweeps the m/z feature-selection p-value cutoff across the range shown in Figure S7, rerunning mummichog's pathway and network module pipeline at each cutoff to quantify how stable the predicted metabolite set is on a given LC/MS dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to validate metabolite identity rather than prediction stability — mummichog is explicitly not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry for identification The feature-selection cutoff is fixed by the experimental design and there is no need to test its sensitivity; a single mummichog run suffices Input is not an untargeted LC/MS feature table (e.g. targeted assays or pre-annotated compounds), where mummichog's pathway/module approach on unassigned m/z features does not apply

skills.description: Use when benchmarking mummichog metabolite prediction against a published, experimentally annotated metabolite list for the same MS dataset, e.g. the human urine set of Roux et al. 2012 with a BioCyc model.
skills.name: predicted-vs-annotated-metabolite-validation
skills.search_text: predicted-vs-annotated-metabolite-validation Use when benchmarking mummichog metabolite prediction against a published, experimentally annotated metabolite list for the same MS dataset, e.g. the human urine set of Roux et al. 2012 with a BioCyc model. When no published annotation list exists for the dataset — mummichog is 'not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification', so this validation cannot stand in for MS/MS-level confirmation. When the input is raw spectra rather than a processed feature table — mummichog requires two lists of m/z features (significant list and reference list), not spectral peaks. When a negative-mode dataset is being evaluated without switching the enforcement to the M−H[−] option, since the M+H[+] enforcement is specific to positive mode. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A validation skill that reruns mummichog metabolite prediction on a published urine metabolomics feature table (Roux et al. 2012) with the M+H[+] ion-form enforcement enabled, then compares the predicted metabolites against the paper's original annotation to quantify agreement (41/41, 100%). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003123
skills.summary: A validation skill that reruns mummichog metabolite prediction on a published urine metabolomics feature table (Roux et al. 2012) with the M+H[+] ion-form enforcement enabled, then compares the predicted metabolites against the paper's original annotation to quantify agreement (41/41, 100%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no published annotation list exists for the dataset — mummichog is 'not designed to replace tandem mass spectrometry in metabolite identification', so this validation cannot stand in for MS/MS-level confirmation. When the input is raw spectra rather than a processed feature table — mummichog requires two lists of m/z features (significant list and reference list), not spectral peaks. When a negative-mode dataset is being evaluated without switching the enforcement to the M−H[−] option, since the M+H[+] enforcement is specific to positive mode.

skills.description: Use when a supervised or heuristic spectral similarity metric must be visually benchmarked against a structural ground truth (Daylight Tanimoto) on MS/MS query–reference pairs, and a scatter point cloud plus Pearson r are the reporting format.
skills.name: predicted-vs-groundtruth-scatter-visualization
skills.search_text: predicted-vs-groundtruth-scatter-visualization Use when a supervised or heuristic spectral similarity metric must be visually benchmarked against a structural ground truth (Daylight Tanimoto) on MS/MS query–reference pairs, and a scatter point cloud plus Pearson r are the reporting format. The input pairs lack any structural ground truth (e.g., unknown or non-molecular spectra), so no Tanimoto score can anchor the scatter plot The task is evaluating retrieval/analogue search performance or molecular networking rather than correlation of a similarity score with structural similarity Only a single method's scores exist without the baselines (Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) needed for the comparative scatter benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates predicted-vs-Tanimoto scatter plots for spectral similarity methods (e.g., TransExION, Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) on the mergedGNPS testing pairs, using binned pair sampling and Pearson correlation to visualize how well each predicted score tracks structural similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Generates predicted-vs-Tanimoto scatter plots for spectral similarity methods (e.g., TransExION, Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) on the mergedGNPS testing pairs, using binned pair sampling and Pearson correlation to visualize how well each predicted score tracks structural similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input pairs lack any structural ground truth (e.g., unknown or non-molecular spectra), so no Tanimoto score can anchor the scatter plot The task is evaluating retrieval/analogue search performance or molecular networking rather than correlation of a similarity score with structural similarity Only a single method's scores exist without the baselines (Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) needed for the comparative scatter benchmark

skills.description: Use when a compound isolated via NP Analyst-guided mass-guided fractionation must be confirmed as the predominant active component by comparing its measured bioassay (BioMAP) profile against the aggregated activity profile of the bioactive community's member prefractions.
skills.name: predicted-vs-purified-bioactivity-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: predicted-vs-purified-bioactivity-concordance-analysis Use when a compound isolated via NP Analyst-guided mass-guided fractionation must be confirmed as the predominant active component by comparing its measured bioassay (BioMAP) profile against the aggregated activity profile of the bioactive community's member prefractions. The purified compound's bioassay data exist but no community-level predicted profile was ever computed — there is no NP Analyst community to compare against; run the compound activity mapping stage first. Bioassay columns are not normalized to a common scale — per the article, such data are unsuitable for assembly into biological profiles for NP Analyst, so any concordance comparison would be invalid. The goal is dereplication of known compounds from the MS features alone rather than validating an isolation lead against its predicted community activity. Validates that the bioactivity profile NP Analyst's Compound Activity Mapping predicts for a bioactive MS-feature community is recapitulated by the measured BioMAP profile of the compound subsequently purified from that community's prefractions — the confirmation step of mass-guided isolation (e.g., amychelin C from community 16). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Validates that the bioactivity profile NP Analyst's Compound Activity Mapping predicts for a bioactive MS-feature community is recapitulated by the measured BioMAP profile of the compound subsequently purified from that community's prefractions — the confirmation step of mass-guided isolation (e.g., amychelin C from community 16).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The purified compound's bioassay data exist but no community-level predicted profile was ever computed — there is no NP Analyst community to compare against; run the compound activity mapping stage first. Bioassay columns are not normalized to a common scale — per the article, such data are unsuitable for assembly into biological profiles for NP Analyst, so any concordance comparison would be invalid. The goal is dereplication of known compounds from the MS features alone rather than validating an isolation lead against its predicted community activity.

skills.description: Use when a trained MS2DeepScore model must be validated on held-out test pairs, especially to check whether cross-ionization-mode Tanimoto predictions correlate with ground-truth structural similarity.
skills.name: predicted-vs-true-similarity-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: predicted-vs-true-similarity-correlation-analysis Use when a trained MS2DeepScore model must be validated on held-out test pairs, especially to check whether cross-ionization-mode Tanimoto predictions correlate with ground-truth structural similarity. Spectra that are low-quality, chimeric, or have limited fragmentation — filter these with the embedding evaluator first, since poor predictions are expected and will depress the correlation Training-data construction rather than validation: pair sampling for training is a separate step (pair_sampling_tutorial) and this skill only scores held-out pairs Datasets restricted to MS1 or lacking annotated structures, since ground-truth Tanimoto labels cannot be derived and MS1 data was not included in training http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates a trained MS2DeepScore 2.0 model by predicting Tanimoto similarity for held-out test spectrum pairs — including cross-ionization-mode (positive vs. negative) pairs — and comparing predicted vs. true chemical similarity with Pearson correlation and RMSE, as in Figure 2b of the paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Evaluates a trained MS2DeepScore 2.0 model by predicting Tanimoto similarity for held-out test spectrum pairs — including cross-ionization-mode (positive vs. negative) pairs — and comparing predicted vs. true chemical similarity with Pearson correlation and RMSE, as in Figure 2b of the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra that are low-quality, chimeric, or have limited fragmentation — filter these with the embedding evaluator first, since poor predictions are expected and will depress the correlation Training-data construction rather than validation: pair sampling for training is a separate step (pair_sampling_tutorial) and this skill only scores held-out pairs Datasets restricted to MS1 or lacking annotated structures, since ground-truth Tanimoto labels cannot be derived and MS1 data was not included in training

skills.description: Use when you have per-spectrum embedding-quality estimates (predicted MSE from an embedding evaluator) and a similarity prediction error metric, and want to quantify how much accuracy improves as the highest-uncertainty spectra are removed.
skills.name: prediction-accuracy-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: prediction-accuracy-curve-analysis Use when you have per-spectrum embedding-quality estimates (predicted MSE from an embedding evaluator) and a similarity prediction error metric, and want to quantify how much accuracy improves as the highest-uncertainty spectra are removed. Spectra have no per-spectrum uncertainty estimates (no embedding evaluator trained alongside the model), so there is no predicted MSE to rank by Reference Tanimoto similarities are unavailable for the test spectra, so accuracy cannot be recomputed after each removal step The goal is a single similarity matrix for molecular networking rather than diagnosing how accuracy depends on spectrum quality http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds a prediction-accuracy curve for MS2DeepScore 2.0 by iteratively removing test spectra with the highest predicted MSE from the InceptionTime embedding evaluator and recomputing prediction accuracy (e.g., RMSE between predicted and true Tanimoto similarity) on the remaining spectra, demonstrating that overall accuracy rises as unreliable spectra are filtered out (Figure 4c). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Builds a prediction-accuracy curve for MS2DeepScore 2.0 by iteratively removing test spectra with the highest predicted MSE from the InceptionTime embedding evaluator and recomputing prediction accuracy (e.g., RMSE between predicted and true Tanimoto similarity) on the remaining spectra, demonstrating that overall accuracy rises as unreliable spectra are filtered out (Figure 4c).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra have no per-spectrum uncertainty estimates (no embedding evaluator trained alongside the model), so there is no predicted MSE to rank by Reference Tanimoto similarities are unavailable for the test spectra, so accuracy cannot be recomputed after each removal step The goal is a single similarity matrix for molecular networking rather than diagnosing how accuracy depends on spectrum quality

skills.description: Decision support for judging whether computationally predicted collision cross sections agree with experimental TWIMS CCS values within ±3%, per metabolite or per adduct state.
skills.name: prediction-accuracy-statistics
skills.search_text: prediction-accuracy-statistics Decision support for judging whether computationally predicted collision cross sections agree with experimental TWIMS CCS values within ±3%, per metabolite or per adduct state. Input is raw MS peak list data rather than already-computed CCS values needing accuracy assessment against a reference. The user wants to compare a molecular ML model (e.g. MI-CCS-style pre-trained models) to the QM workflow, rather than evaluate the snakemake_ccs workflow's own predictions. The metabolite set falls outside the benchmark scope of atom counts 10–40 with protonated/deprotonated adduct states explored here. Quantify the accuracy of in silico CCS predictions from the snakemake_ccs workflow by computing percent errors of Boltzmann-averaged and single-conformer CCS values against experimental TWIMS reference values, using the paper's ±3% agreement criterion. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.1c00315
skills.summary: Quantify the accuracy of in silico CCS predictions from the snakemake_ccs workflow by computing percent errors of Boltzmann-averaged and single-conformer CCS values against experimental TWIMS reference values, using the paper's ±3% agreement criterion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS peak list data rather than already-computed CCS values needing accuracy assessment against a reference. The user wants to compare a molecular ML model (e.g. MI-CCS-style pre-trained models) to the QM workflow, rather than evaluate the snakemake_ccs workflow's own predictions. The metabolite set falls outside the benchmark scope of atom counts 10–40 with protonated/deprotonated adduct states explored here.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking normalization methods on in-silico metabolomics data with known ground-truth drift and injected outliers, and per-run squared prediction errors must be aggregated into median estimates.
skills.name: prediction-error-aggregation-across-simulation-runs
skills.search_text: prediction-error-aggregation-across-simulation-runs Use when benchmarking normalization methods on in-silico metabolomics data with known ground-truth drift and injected outliers, and per-run squared prediction errors must be aggregated into median estimates. The data are real experimental metabolomics measurements without a known drift-free ground truth — squared prediction error against truth cannot be computed, and the paper instead uses replicate concordance, drift and batch-effect reduction on such data. The goal is to proxy normalization quality by reduction of the relative standard deviation of QC samples or increased numbers of differentially abundant metabolites — the paper explicitly flags these as common benchmarking pitfalls. Only a single method or a single outlier setting is being evaluated — cross-method comparison of degradation with increasing outlier count (e.g. QC-RLSC deteriorating while robust methods degrade gracefully) is the point of the aggregation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates per-run squared prediction errors of normalized metabolomics signals against a known drift-free ground truth into median estimates across 200 simulated runs, benchmarking QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM and tGAM under varying outlier counts and QC densities. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Aggregates per-run squared prediction errors of normalized metabolomics signals against a known drift-free ground truth into median estimates across 200 simulated runs, benchmarking QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM and tGAM under varying outlier counts and QC densities.

skills.search_text: prediction-error-metric-aggregation Use when a benchmark produces per-split error metrics (e.g. MRE and RMSE over 101 random 70:30 splits) and you need robust median-based rankings of multiple prediction tools per adduct class. When the goal is annotation filtering with a ΔCCS threshold (e.g. 2.8% with 10 ppm mass error) rather than cross-tool benchmark ranking. skills.summary: Aggregates per-split regression error metrics (MRE, RMSE) computed over many random train/test splits into robust medians per method per adduct, then ranks competing predictors (e.g. CCSP 2.0 vs CCSbase vs AllCCS vs DeepCCS).

RT prediction within the SMRT chromatographic method itself — no projection is needed; use the DLM predicted RT directly Candidate ranking/filtering tasks where predicted RT is used to rank accurate-mass-search candidates rather than to quantify cross-method transfer error ECMs for which fewer than ~50 molecules have experimental RT in both the SMRT method and the target method, where the polynomial fit cannot be reliably estimated http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Projects retention times predicted by the METLIN SMRT deep-learning model (DLM) onto independent experimental chromatographic methods (ECMs) from PredRet, then quantifies transfer error as the median absolute difference in seconds between projected predicted RT and experimental RT per ECM. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7

skills.search_text: prediction-error-threshold-coverage-evaluation Use when you have paired true vs. predicted retention times for a held-out test set and need to quantify model coverage at error cutoffs and the FDR impact of an RT-based candidate filter. skills.search_text: prediction-pipeline-grid-search-tuning Use when a labeled data set (e.g. a quality rating treated as a categorical class label) must be turned into a class-prediction estimator whose pre-processing, feature selection and estimator settings need joint optimization. skills.description: Use when rescoring immunopeptidomics or other PSMs with predicted fragment-ion intensities and you need to detect sequences whose spectral-angle fit is unstable under adjacent-residue swaps, as in inSPIRE-style rescoring.
skills.name: prediction-stability-delta-scoring
skills.search_text: prediction-stability-delta-scoring Use when rescoring immunopeptidomics or other PSMs with predicted fragment-ion intensities and you need to detect sequences whose spectral-angle fit is unstable under adjacent-residue swaps, as in inSPIRE-style rescoring. Input PSMs lack predicted fragment-ion intensities (no Prosit predictions available), since both the SA and the swapped-sequence SA require predicted intensity vectors The goal is generic PSM feature generation or semi-supervised rescoring (e.g. MS²Rescore's ms2pip/deeplc/ristretto pipeline) rather than specifically assessing sequence-assignment stability via spectral-angle deltas Peptides have no adjacent residue pairs worth swapping (e.g. very short sequences), making the stability delta uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes the Prosit-delta score: the stability of the normalized spectral contrast angle (SA) between observed and Prosit-predicted fragment-ion intensity vectors when adjacent amino-acid positions in a peptide are swapped. Low Prosit-delta flags peptide-spectrum matches likely misassigned to similar, though incorrect, peptide sequences. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/pmic.202300336
skills.summary: Computes the Prosit-delta score: the stability of the normalized spectral contrast angle (SA) between observed and Prosit-predicted fragment-ion intensity vectors when adjacent amino-acid positions in a peptide are swapped. Low Prosit-delta flags peptide-spectrum matches likely misassigned to similar, though incorrect, peptide sequences.

skills.description: Use when predicted RTs from a DNN (e.g. trained on SMRT) must be projected onto a target chromatographic method with few (~10) identified molecules and probabilistic intervals are needed to score candidate metabolites.
skills.name: predictive-interval-quantification-for-rt-projections
skills.search_text: predictive-interval-quantification-for-rt-projections Use when predicted RTs from a DNN (e.g. trained on SMRT) must be projected onto a target chromatographic method with few (~10) identified molecules and probabilistic intervals are needed to score candidate metabolites. The target chromatographic method has abundant identified molecules — a directly trained projection (non-meta-learned GP) may suffice and the meta-learned prior is unnecessary. Molecules are non-retained (RT < 5 min) and were not excluded; they distort the log-transformed, robustly scaled training pairs. Only point RT estimates are needed with no uncertainty requirement and no candidate ranking by z-score is planned. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify uncertainty in retention-time projections between chromatographic methods using a Bayesian meta-learned Gaussian Process that yields a posterior predictive mean with 95% credible intervals, not just point estimates, from as few as 10 identified molecules. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8
skills.summary: Quantify uncertainty in retention-time projections between chromatographic methods using a Bayesian meta-learned Gaussian Process that yields a posterior predictive mean with 95% credible intervals, not just point estimates, from as few as 10 identified molecules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target chromatographic method has abundant identified molecules — a directly trained projection (non-meta-learned GP) may suffice and the meta-learned prior is unnecessary. Molecules are non-retained (RT < 5 min) and were not excluded; they distort the log-transformed, robustly scaled training pairs. Only point RT estimates are needed with no uncertainty requirement and no candidate ranking by z-score is planned.

skills.description: Use when a tuned supervised classifier (e.g. SKlearn random forest on pathway scores) has been trained with nested cross-validation and you must quantify held-out predictive performance as AUC, especially to compare against a molecular-level concatenated baseline.
skills.name: predictive-model-auc-evaluation
skills.search_text: predictive-model-auc-evaluation Use when a tuned supervised classifier (e.g. SKlearn random forest on pathway scores) has been trained with nested cross-validation and you must quantify held-out predictive performance as AUC, especially to compare against a molecular-level concatenated baseline. The analysis goal is unsupervised pathway ranking or conventional ORA/GSEA rather than outcome prediction — PathIntegrate's predictive AUC evaluation does not apply to MultiGSEA, IMPaLA, or ActivePathways-style hypothesis-generation workflows. Input omics are not measured on the same individuals (samples with missing entire omics views must be discarded, since PathIntegrate requires all input omics on the same individuals). The comparison is against methods like DIABLO operating at the molecular level without pathway transformation — a different benchmarking protocol than this pathway-level AUC evaluation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Evaluate a pathway-level (or molecular-level baseline) supervised classification model on a held-out test set using AUC, benchmarking multi-omics pathway-transformed predictions against concatenated molecular data as done in the PathIntegrate Su et al. 2020 COVID-19 severity case study. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Evaluate a pathway-level (or molecular-level baseline) supervised classification model on a held-out test set using AUC, benchmarking multi-omics pathway-transformed predictions against concatenated molecular data as done in the PathIntegrate Su et al. 2020 COVID-19 severity case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is unsupervised pathway ranking or conventional ORA/GSEA rather than outcome prediction — PathIntegrate's predictive AUC evaluation does not apply to MultiGSEA, IMPaLA, or ActivePathways-style hypothesis-generation workflows. Input omics are not measured on the same individuals (samples with missing entire omics views must be discarded, since PathIntegrate requires all input omics on the same individuals). The comparison is against methods like DIABLO operating at the molecular level without pathway transformation — a different benchmarking protocol than this pathway-level AUC evaluation.

skills.search_text: predret-dataset-preprocessing Use when loading PredRet retention time data from multiple LC systems via a config.json file and you need per-system cleaning (duplicate RTs, small-RT noise, >5% spread outliers) before order prediction or cross-system comparison. skills.description: Use when a prefractionated extract library has per-prefraction bioassay results plus processed MS feature data (GNPS graphML or MZmine 2 peak lists), and the goal is to identify which MS feature drives the activity of a bioactive community and dereplicate it against known compound profiles.
skills.name: prefraction-activity-community-prioritization
skills.search_text: prefraction-activity-community-prioritization Use when a prefractionated extract library has per-prefraction bioassay results plus processed MS feature data (GNPS graphML or MZmine 2 peak lists), and the goal is to identify which MS feature drives the activity of a bioactive community and dereplicate it against known compound profiles. Input MS data are raw/unprocessed mass lists — NP Analyst run without preprocessing typically increases the number of candidate bioactive MS features with junk peaks; preprocess via MZmine 2/GNPS with replicate comparison and an intensity cutoff first. Only one MS feature is present per sample with no prefractionation or bioassay matrix — feature distribution scoring and community formation require feature-by-prefraction activity data. The goal is de novo structure elucidation of the bioactive compound — this skill maps activity to MS features and dereplicates against known profiles; it does not determine structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Prioritizes the MS feature(s) responsible for a prefractionated extract library's bioactivity by relating metabolite MS feature distributions with bioassay results, using NP Analyst's Activity Score and Cluster Score computations on feature-by-prefraction baskets. Rationale: communities are built from bioactive MS feature distribution rather than sample activity profiles, so the prioritized feature is the one whose presence pattern matches the community's activity profile. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.1c01108
skills.summary: Prioritizes the MS feature(s) responsible for a prefractionated extract library's bioactivity by relating metabolite MS feature distributions with bioassay results, using NP Analyst's Activity Score and Cluster Score computations on feature-by-prefraction baskets. Rationale: communities are built from bioactive MS feature distribution rather than sample activity profiles, so the prioritized feature is the one whose presence pattern matches the community's activity profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input MS data are raw/unprocessed mass lists — NP Analyst run without preprocessing typically increases the number of candidate bioactive MS features with junk peaks; preprocess via MZmine 2/GNPS with replicate comparison and an intensity cutoff first. Only one MS feature is present per sample with no prefractionation or bioassay matrix — feature distribution scoring and community formation require feature-by-prefraction activity data. The goal is de novo structure elucidation of the bioactive compound — this skill maps activity to MS features and dereplicates against known profiles; it does not determine structures.

skills.description: Use when validating that a specXplore preprocessing run of .mgf MS/MS data (e.g. wheat or urine datasets) completes within the published runtime envelope and yields the expected number of features after processing.
skills.name: preprocessing-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: preprocessing-benchmark-comparison Use when validating that a specXplore preprocessing run of .mgf MS/MS data (e.g. wheat or urine datasets) completes within the published runtime envelope and yields the expected number of features after processing. Input is raw LC–MS/MS vendor data rather than a pre-extracted .mgf file with a 'feature_id' key — specXplore requires .mgf output from MZmine3 or equivalent preprocessing first. The task is visual dashboard exploration (t-SNE, network views, heatmaps) rather than measuring importing-pipeline preprocessing time and feature counts. Operating on Windows — the README states the current version of specXplore works on macOS and Linux but fails on Windows, so benchmark numbers on Windows are not comparable to the paper's reported system. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark the specXplore importing pipeline's preprocessing runtime and feature counts on real LC–MS/MS datasets (wheat and urine .mgf files) by timing the full run — MS2Query library search and pairwise spectral similarity computations — and comparing measured values against the paper's reported ranges (<15 min wheat, <75 min urine). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Benchmark the specXplore importing pipeline's preprocessing runtime and feature counts on real LC–MS/MS datasets (wheat and urine .mgf files) by timing the full run — MS2Query library search and pairwise spectral similarity computations — and comparing measured values against the paper's reported ranges (<15 min wheat, <75 min urine).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC–MS/MS vendor data rather than a pre-extracted .mgf file with a 'feature_id' key — specXplore requires .mgf output from MZmine3 or equivalent preprocessing first. The deposit holds only original raw files with no PreProcessor-generated counterparts, so no 1:1 size pairing or ratio can be computed. The goal is signal-quality evaluation (lipid annotation counts, mass error, feature detection speed) rather than quantifying storage-size reduction. skills.description: Use when a notame preprocessing pipeline has produced a feature-by-sample abundance matrix and you must capture the exact transformation, PQN and center/scale settings before writing the transformed matrix onward.
skills.name: preprocessing-parameter-recording
skills.search_text: preprocessing-parameter-recording Use when a notame preprocessing pipeline has produced a feature-by-sample abundance matrix and you must capture the exact transformation, PQN and center/scale settings before writing the transformed matrix onward. Input is raw instrument data (e.g. mzML or MS-DIAL peak tables) that has not yet been through notame's peak-picking, drift correction, flagging and imputation — parameter recording is only meaningful for a matrix that already has preprocessing parameters to describe. The analysis is purely exploratory visualization on an already-normalized matrix where no new transformation parameters were chosen — no parameter record needs to be written. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Records the transformation, normalization and scaling parameters applied to a MetaboSet LC-MS feature matrix (e.g. log transformation, PQN reference/method, autoscaling center/scale flags) so that downstream multivariate analyses remain reproducible and auditable. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135

The analysis is purely exploratory visualization on an already-normalized matrix where no new transformation parameters were chosen — no parameter record needs to be written.

skills.description: Use when you have a large set of predicted statistical sub-clusters (e.g. PRESTO-STAT output from antiSMASH-DB BGCs) and need to organise related ones into hierarchical families/clans via a binary gene-content representation.
skills.name: presence-absence-matrix-construction-from-tokenised-genes
skills.search_text: presence-absence-matrix-construction-from-tokenised-genes Use when you have a large set of predicted statistical sub-clusters (e.g. PRESTO-STAT output from antiSMASH-DB BGCs) and need to organise related ones into hierarchical families/clans via a binary gene-content representation. Input is raw antiSMASH BGCs that have not yet been tokenised and processed by PRESTO-STAT — run BGC tokenisation and sub-cluster prediction first. The analysis requires gene-order information — a presence/absence matrix is a bag-of-genes representation (like the LDA 'bag of words' model) and discards original gene order that the statistical (Stat) method preserves. The data is already grouped into SCFs/SCCs and only needs annotation or query against sub-cluster families/clans. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Represents PRESTO-STAT-predicted statistical sub-clusters as a presence/absence matrix over tokenised genes (domain combinations/subPfams) so that two rounds of K-means clustering can group 108,085 sub-clusters into 10,000 sub-cluster families (SCFs) and 2,000 sub-cluster clans (SCCs). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Represents PRESTO-STAT-predicted statistical sub-clusters as a presence/absence matrix over tokenised genes (domain combinations/subPfams) so that two rounds of K-means clustering can group 108,085 sub-clusters into 10,000 sub-cluster families (SCFs) and 2,000 sub-cluster clans (SCCs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw antiSMASH BGCs that have not yet been tokenised and processed by PRESTO-STAT — run BGC tokenisation and sub-cluster prediction first. The analysis requires gene-order information — a presence/absence matrix is a bag-of-genes representation (like the LDA 'bag of words' model) and discards original gene order that the statistical (Stat) method preserves. The data is already grouped into SCFs/SCCs and only needs annotation or query against sub-cluster families/clans.

skills.description: Use when a vendor-, sequence-, and field-strength-specific (3T PRESS) metabolite basis set must be simulated in MATLAB, or when validating simulated basis functions against release FID-A or phantom-measured (LCModel) basis sets.
skills.name: press-localization-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: press-localization-parameter-configuration Use when a vendor-, sequence-, and field-strength-specific (3T PRESS) metabolite basis set must be simulated in MATLAB, or when validating simulated basis functions against release FID-A or phantom-measured (LCModel) basis sets. The experiment requires STEAM or SPECIAL localization — MRSCloud does not implement these sequences. The target field strength is not 3T — the existing MRSCloud version only supports 3T basis-set generation. The sequence requires product-specific RF waveforms or replicating all disseminated vendor versions (e.g., MEGA-PRESS variants) — product sequences and RF waveforms are not shared in the GitHub repo and simulations cannot capture all such differences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Configure and run density-matrix basis-set simulations for 1H MRS with PRESS localization (e.g., TE 30/68 ms) using MRSCloud's MATLAB code (built on FID-A), tuning parameters such as simMRS. fields, spatial_points (41 acceptable, 101 ideal), and output directories before executing run_simulations_cloud.m. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: Configure and run density-matrix basis-set simulations for 1H MRS with PRESS localization (e.g., TE 30/68 ms) using MRSCloud's MATLAB code (built on FID-A), tuning parameters such as simMRS. fields, spatial_points (41 acceptable, 101 ideal), and output directories before executing run_simulations_cloud.m.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experiment requires STEAM or SPECIAL localization — MRSCloud does not implement these sequences. The target field strength is not 3T — the existing MRSCloud version only supports 3T basis-set generation. The sequence requires product-specific RF waveforms or replicating all disseminated vendor versions (e.g., MEGA-PRESS variants) — product sequences and RF waveforms are not shared in the GitHub repo and simulations cannot capture all such differences.

skills.description: Use when single-field DTIMS CCS values for the same ion vary across many runs (e.g. large RapidFire SPE-IMS-MS batches) and per-run pressure/temperature fluctuations are suspected of inflating %RSD.
skills.name: pressure-temperature-corrected-ccs-calibration
skills.search_text: pressure-temperature-corrected-ccs-calibration Use when single-field DTIMS CCS values for the same ion vary across many runs (e.g. large RapidFire SPE-IMS-MS batches) and per-run pressure/temperature fluctuations are suspected of inflating %RSD. Data were acquired with stepped-field DTIMS, where CCS is derived directly from multi-field measurements (--mode multi) rather than calibrated single-field drift times The platform is TWIMS/SLIM and requires traveling-wave calibration (e.g. linearized power function) rather than single-field drift-time calibration Only a single run is available, so per-run pressure/temperature correction cannot reduce run-to-run variance http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 An enhanced single-field DTIMS calibration implemented in AutoCCS that incorporates per-run pressure and temperature from IMS frame metadata into the CCS calculation, reducing calibrated CCS variance caused by instrument condition fluctuations in large-scale RapidFire SPE-IMS-MS runs. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: An enhanced single-field DTIMS calibration implemented in AutoCCS that incorporates per-run pressure and temperature from IMS frame metadata into the CCS calculation, reducing calibrated CCS variance caused by instrument condition fluctuations in large-scale RapidFire SPE-IMS-MS runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were acquired with stepped-field DTIMS, where CCS is derived directly from multi-field measurements (--mode multi) rather than calibrated single-field drift times The platform is TWIMS/SLIM and requires traveling-wave calibration (e.g. linearized power function) rather than single-field drift-time calibration Only a single run is available, so per-run pressure/temperature correction cannot reduce run-to-run variance

skills.description: Use when a biosynthetic gene cluster dataset (e.g. tokenised antiSMASH BGCs) needs statistical sub-cluster prediction whose performance must be benchmarked against experimentally verified SubClusterBlast sub-clusters using an overlap-fraction criterion.
skills.name: presto-stat-subcluster-detection
skills.search_text: presto-stat-subcluster-detection Use when a biosynthetic gene cluster dataset (e.g. tokenised antiSMASH BGCs) needs statistical sub-cluster prediction whose performance must be benchmarked against experimentally verified SubClusterBlast sub-clusters using an overlap-fraction criterion. The goal is topic-model-based sub-cluster discovery rather than validating the statistical co-occurrence method — use PRESTO-TOP (LDA, bag-of-words, gene order ignored) instead of the order-aware PRESTO-STAT approach. The BGCs have not been tokenised into (sub)Pfams with non-biosynthetic Pfams removed, so no comparable gene-token representation exists for overlap computation. No experimentally verified reference sub-clusters (e.g. SubClusterBlast or MIBiG-annotated sub-clusters) are available to compute overlap against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Validate PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-cluster predictions from iPRESTO by computing gene-overlap fractions against experimentally verified SubClusterBlast sub-clusters, using a 0.6 overlap cut-off to declare detection. Confirms the statistical co-occurrence method recovers most known sub-clusters and is largely consistent with PRESTO-TOP topic-model motifs. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Validate PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-cluster predictions from iPRESTO by computing gene-overlap fractions against experimentally verified SubClusterBlast sub-clusters, using a 0.6 overlap cut-off to declare detection. Confirms the statistical co-occurrence method recovers most known sub-clusters and is largely consistent with PRESTO-TOP topic-model motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is topic-model-based sub-cluster discovery rather than validating the statistical co-occurrence method — use PRESTO-TOP (LDA, bag-of-words, gene order ignored) instead of the order-aware PRESTO-STAT approach. The BGCs have not been tokenised into (sub)Pfams with non-biosynthetic Pfams removed, so no comparable gene-token representation exists for overlap computation. No experimentally verified reference sub-clusters (e.g. SubClusterBlast or MIBiG-annotated sub-clusters) are available to compute overlap against.

skills.description: Use when tokenised BGCs (antiSMASH-predicted clusters with detected (sub)Pfams) need unsupervised sub-cluster motif discovery, or when validating predicted sub-clusters against curated SubClusterBlast/MIBiG references via overlap fractions.
skills.name: presto-top-motif-matching
skills.search_text: presto-top-motif-matching Use when tokenised BGCs (antiSMASH-predicted clusters with detected (sub)Pfams) need unsupervised sub-cluster motif discovery, or when validating predicted sub-clusters against curated SubClusterBlast/MIBiG references via overlap fractions. When gene order within the BGC matters for the sub-cluster signal — PRESTO-TOP uses a bag-of-words model that discards original gene order; use PRESTO-STAT instead When BGCs have not been tokenised (sub)Pfam-annotated — raw GenBank/antiSMASH output without Pfam detection cannot be fed to the topic model http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply iPRESTO's PRESTO-TOP Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic-modelling approach to match sub-cluster motifs (bag-of-(sub)Pfam-words) across BGCs, and validate detected sub-clusters against experimentally verified antiSMASH SubClusterBlast sub-clusters using a 0.6 overlap cut-off. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Apply iPRESTO's PRESTO-TOP Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic-modelling approach to match sub-cluster motifs (bag-of-(sub)Pfam-words) across BGCs, and validate detected sub-clusters against experimentally verified antiSMASH SubClusterBlast sub-clusters using a 0.6 overlap cut-off.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene order within the BGC matters for the sub-cluster signal — PRESTO-TOP uses a bag-of-words model that discards original gene order; use PRESTO-STAT instead When BGCs have not been tokenised (sub)Pfam-annotated — raw GenBank/antiSMASH output without Pfam detection cannot be fed to the topic model

skills.name: pretrained-resnet-backbone-adaptation
skills.search_text: pretrained-resnet-backbone-adaptation Use when building a self-supervised representation model for ion images (MSI) where a pretrained CNN backbone must be converted into a twin shared-parameter encoder feeding projection/prediction MLPs and a SimSiam-style contrastive loss with stop-gradient. The downstream goal is supervised classification with labeled ion images rather than self-supervised representation learning without manual annotation. Input data are not ion images from MSI (e.g. spectra-only profiles without spatial X*Y pixel structure), since the ResNet18 encoder expects 2D image-like inputs. skills.summary: Adapts a pretrained ResNet18 backbone as the twin parameter-sharing encoder of a self-supervised contrastive model (DeepION, built on SimSiam), so each ion image is transformed into a 512-dimensional representation vector without manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream goal is supervised classification with labeled ion images rather than self-supervised representation learning without manual annotation. Only a single (non-paired) view per ion image is available, because the twin encoder and SimSiam contrastive loss require two augmented views of the same image.

skills.search_text: pretraining-dataset-scaling-ablation Use when you must quantify whether scaling a decoder pretraining corpus (fingerprint-to-molecule pairs) improves downstream de novo structure generation, and you can pretrain/finetune at multiple corpus sizes on a held-out benchmark. You want to ablate the spectrum-encoder pretraining corpus (spectrum-to-fingerprint prediction) rather than the fingerprint-to-molecule decoder corpus — this skill only varies decoder pretraining size. skills.summary: An ablation protocol that quantifies how the size of the fingerprint-to-molecule pretraining corpus for a diffusion decoder (0, 0.2M, 0.8M, 1.2M, 2.8M pairs) affects downstream spectra-to-molecule generation accuracy after end-to-end finetuning, as done for DiffMS on NPLIB1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to ablate the spectrum-encoder pretraining corpus (spectrum-to-fingerprint prediction) rather than the fingerprint-to-molecule decoder corpus — this skill only varies decoder pretraining size. skills.description: Use when a metabolic network reconstruction (e.g. from KEGG/NCBI-RefSeq mapping in MINNO) has yielded predicted missing reactions and each candidate needs an evidence label — primary-literature confirmation vs homology support — before downstream use.
skills.name: primary-literature-confirmation-mapping
skills.search_text: primary-literature-confirmation-mapping Use when a metabolic network reconstruction (e.g. from KEGG/NCBI-RefSeq mapping in MINNO) has yielded predicted missing reactions and each candidate needs an evidence label — primary-literature confirmation vs homology support — before downstream use. Reactions already present in the reference database (e.g. annotated in KEGG) — confirmation mapping only applies to predicted-missing candidates. No literature or homology evidence is available for a candidate, in which case it should remain flagged as unsupported rather than forced into a category. The goal is purely visual network exploration in MINNO without curation intent — boundary-flux inspection alone does not require literature confirmation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Verifies whether computationally predicted (e.g. MINNO-inferred) missing metabolic reactions are supported by published experiments or by sequence homology in a reference database such as NCBI-RefSeq, producing an evidence-categorized reaction table. This step grounds boundary-flux-based network refinements in independently validated sources before they are accepted as real biology. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Verifies whether computationally predicted (e.g. MINNO-inferred) missing metabolic reactions are supported by published experiments or by sequence homology in a reference database such as NCBI-RefSeq, producing an evidence-categorized reaction table. This step grounds boundary-flux-based network refinements in independently validated sources before they are accepted as real biology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reactions already present in the reference database (e.g. annotated in KEGG) — confirmation mapping only applies to predicted-missing candidates. No literature or homology evidence is available for a candidate, in which case it should remain flagged as unsupported rather than forced into a category. skills.description: Use when you have a metabolite abundance matrix (e.g., metabolite names or HMDB ids × samples) and need to reduce it to pathway-level features via PDS projection before feature selection or ML classification.

skills.search_text: principal-curve-projection Use when you have a metabolite abundance matrix (e.g., metabolite names or HMDB ids × samples) and need to reduce it to pathway-level features via PDS projection before feature selection or ML classification. Input is already a pathway-level or PDS feature matrix — re-running this skill would double-transform and misalign dimensions. You need to classify using raw metabolite intensities without pathway-based feature engineering; Lilikoi's classifier can take the original measurement matrix. The metabolites cannot be mapped to any pathway (MetaTOpathway returns an empty table), leaving no pathway to compute PDS over. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes a pathway dysregulation score (PDS) for each sample-pathway pair in Lilikoi v2.0 by projecting metabolite intensities onto principal curves within each pathway, converting a raw metabolite abundance matrix into a normalized pathway-level feature matrix. This is the dimension-transformer step that turns metabolite-level measurements into personalized, pathway-based features for downstream feature selection and classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Computes a pathway dysregulation score (PDS) for each sample-pathway pair in Lilikoi v2.0 by projecting metabolite intensities onto principal curves within each pathway, converting a raw metabolite abundance matrix into a normalized pathway-level feature matrix. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway-level or PDS feature matrix — re-running this skill would double-transform and misalign dimensions.
