skills.description: Use when designing or auditing a targeted lipidomics PRM/SRM assay and you must decide how many MS/MS fragments per lipid are needed for unambiguous identification within a background lipidome.
skills.name: prm-assay-validation-verification
skills.search_text: prm-assay-validation-verification Use when designing or auditing a targeted lipidomics PRM/SRM assay and you must decide how many MS/MS fragments per lipid are needed for unambiguous identification within a background lipidome. LipidCreator intentionally does not address false discovery rate scoring, coeluting/isobaric lipids, or peak area integration — do not use this skill as a replacement for a dedicated FDR scoring algorithm on raw LC-MS data. The assay targets organisms lacking lipid standards (e.g., E. coli or archaea) where LipidCreator's eukaryote-focused coverage and the background matrix are incomplete. Input is untargeted/shotgun screening data rather than a LipidCreator-designed PRM or MRM transition list. Stereoisomer differentiation is required — no large-scale methods exist due to lack of isotope-coded standards. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates LipidCreator-generated target-decoy PRM/MRM lipidomics assays by computing fragment-count-dependent match probabilities and comparing computed accuracy ratios against reported target-decoy identification counts. Ensures that a chosen number of fragments (and polarity modes) yields unambiguous lipid species identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Validates LipidCreator-generated target-decoy PRM/MRM lipidomics assays by computing fragment-count-dependent match probabilities and comparing computed accuracy ratios against reported target-decoy identification counts. Ensures that a chosen number of fragments (and polarity modes) yields unambiguous lipid species identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: LipidCreator intentionally does not address false discovery rate scoring, coeluting/isobaric lipids, or peak area integration — do not use this skill as a replacement for a dedicated FDR scoring algorithm on raw LC-MS data. The assay targets organisms lacking lipid standards (e.g., E. coli or archaea) where LipidCreator's eukaryote-focused coverage and the background matrix are incomplete. Input is untargeted/shotgun screening data rather than a LipidCreator-designed PRM or MRM transition list. Stereoisomer differentiation is required — no large-scale methods exist due to lack of isotope-coded standards.

skills.description: Use when a Thermo .raw file is claimed to be PRM/targeted and you must confirm regularly spaced MS2 scans for a precursor (e.g. FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00) via scan-index deltas.
skills.name: prm-targeted-scan-interval-verification
skills.search_text: prm-targeted-scan-interval-verification Use when a Thermo .raw file is claimed to be PRM/targeted and you must confirm regularly spaced MS2 scans for a precursor (e.g. FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00) via scan-index deltas. The acquisition is conventional DDA shotgun LC-MS/MS, where irregular MS2 spacing is expected and a constant delta would not be meaningful The data has already been converted to an exchange format like mzML via ProteoWizard/MSconvert, so rawrr's RawFileReader access is unnecessary The analysis goal is quantification or XIC extraction around the target mass at 10 ppm using MS1-level scans rather than verifying the acquisition schedule http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Verifies parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) acquisition by extracting the scan index of a Thermo Fisher .raw file with rawrr::readIndex and showing that consecutive targeted MS2 scans are separated by a constant scan delta (e.g. 22 scans for the 487.2567 iRT precursor), confirming a regular PRM cycle. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.10.30.362533
skills.summary: Verifies parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) acquisition by extracting the scan index of a Thermo Fisher .raw file with rawrr::readIndex and showing that consecutive targeted MS2 scans are separated by a constant scan delta (e.g. 22 scans for the 487.2567 iRT precursor), confirming a regular PRM cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The acquisition is conventional DDA shotgun LC-MS/MS, where irregular MS2 spacing is expected and a constant delta would not be meaningful The data has already been converted to an exchange format like mzML via ProteoWizard/MSconvert, so rawrr's RawFileReader access is unnecessary The analysis goal is quantification or XIC extraction around the target mass at 10 ppm using MS1-level scans rather than verifying the acquisition schedule

skills.description: Use when predicting an MS/MS spectrum from a known molecular structure (C2MS), especially when high mass accuracy, formula annotations, and fragment-level interpretability matter for library augmentation.
skills.name: probabilistic-fragment-distribution-modeling
skills.search_text: probabilistic-fragment-distribution-modeling Use when predicting an MS/MS spectrum from a known molecular structure (C2MS), especially when high mass accuracy, formula annotations, and fragment-level interpretability matter for library augmentation. The goal is formula annotation of glycan or peptide spectra, which the paper excluded to focus on small molecules No candidate molecular structure is available (the skill predicts spectra from a known structure G; it does not solve structure elucidation from the spectrum alone) Prediction is needed on unmerged spectra or under instrument platforms/adducts beyond the Orbitrap HCD [M+H]+ setting validated in the paper http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Reconstruct FraGNNet's two-stage probabilistic GNN that formulates C2MS prediction as learning a distribution over molecule fragments: a Molecule GNN embeds the input graph, a Fragment GNN over the fragmentation DAG predicts P(n), P(f|n), P(f), and P(m), which are converted to an MS/MS spectrum via formula masses. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2404.02360
skills.summary: Reconstruct FraGNNet's two-stage probabilistic GNN that formulates C2MS prediction as learning a distribution over molecule fragments: a Molecule GNN embeds the input graph, a Fragment GNN over the fragmentation DAG predicts P(n), P(f|n), P(f), and P(m), which are converted to an MS/MS spectrum via formula masses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is formula annotation of glycan or peptide spectra, which the paper excluded to focus on small molecules No candidate molecular structure is available (the skill predicts spectra from a known structure G; it does not solve structure elucidation from the spectrum alone) Prediction is needed on unmerged spectra or under instrument platforms/adducts beyond the Orbitrap HCD [M+H]+ setting validated in the paper

skills.description: Use when training or retraining a learned fragmentation model for tandem mass spectral database search, or when scoring candidate molecule-spectrum pairs and estimating target-decoy FDR for small molecule identification.
skills.name: probabilistic-fragmentation-model-training
skills.search_text: probabilistic-fragmentation-model-training Use when training or retraining a learned fragmentation model for tandem mass spectral database search, or when scoring candidate molecule-spectrum pairs and estimating target-decoy FDR for small molecule identification. The task is de novo structure prediction or pure spectral library search rather than in silico search against a molecular structure database Accurate modeling of low-mass molecules (<600 Da) is critical, since fewer fragments are generated for molecules in this range and accuracy is lower Experimental conditions (instrument type, dissociation technique, ionization mode, collision energy) differ substantially from the default model, which was trained on combined CID/HCD positive-mode spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Train the molDiscovery probabilistic fragment-matching model, P(logRank|bondType, logRankpa), by counting observed fragment bondType/logRank pairs in matched molecule-spectrum training pairs and normalizing the count matrix, then use it for log-likelihood-ratio scoring with target-decoy FDR estimation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Train the molDiscovery probabilistic fragment-matching model, P(logRank|bondType, logRankpa), by counting observed fragment bondType/logRank pairs in matched molecule-spectrum training pairs and normalizing the count matrix, then use it for log-likelihood-ratio scoring with target-decoy FDR estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is de novo structure prediction or pure spectral library search rather than in silico search against a molecular structure database Accurate modeling of low-mass molecules (<600 Da) is critical, since fewer fragments are generated for molecules in this range and accuracy is lower Experimental conditions (instrument type, dissociation technique, ionization mode, collision energy) differ substantially from the default model, which was trained on combined CID/HCD positive-mode spectra

skills.description: Use when you have per-peak MS/MS candidate scores and pairwise ROASMI P_ij retention-order probabilities and need to rank candidate structures for each detected peak, e.g. to distinguish isomers or annotate peaks lacking usable MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: probabilistic-graph-integration-of-retention-order-and-msms-scores
skills.search_text: probabilistic-graph-integration-of-retention-order-and-msms-scores Use when you have per-peak MS/MS candidate scores and pairwise ROASMI P_ij retention-order probabilities and need to rank candidate structures for each detected peak, e.g. to distinguish isomers or annotate peaks lacking usable MS/MS spectra. When your data is on HILIC chromatography — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems, so retention scores would be invalid for this integration. When candidate pairs fall outside the C, H, N, O, P, and S elemental restrictions of ROASMI — retention predictions are out of domain. When a candidate pair's chromatographic peaks are too close for consistent retention order across experiments (ROASMI marks them indistinguishable); including them in ranking is unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Combines ROASMI-predicted retention-order probabilities P_ij with per-peak MS/MS spectral scores by modeling score integration as inference on a fully connected graph over candidate structures, using random spanning-tree ensembles to infer maximum-marginal top-k rankings. This lets ROASMI's RankNet retention scores refine annotations for peaks lacking usable MS/MS spectra or with coexisting isomers. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Combines ROASMI-predicted retention-order probabilities P_ij with per-peak MS/MS spectral scores by modeling score integration as inference on a fully connected graph over candidate structures, using random spanning-tree ensembles to infer maximum-marginal top-k rankings. This lets ROASMI's RankNet retention scores refine annotations for peaks lacking usable MS/MS spectra or with coexisting isomers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When your data is on HILIC chromatography — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems, so retention scores would be invalid for this integration. When candidate pairs fall outside the C, H, N, O, P, and S elemental restrictions of ROASMI — retention predictions are out of domain. When a candidate pair's chromatographic peaks are too close for consistent retention order across experiments (ROASMI marks them indistinguishable); including them in ranking is unreliable.

skills.description: Use when you have molDiscovery fragment-peak matches on training molecules with reference spectra and want to learn or visualize how fragment log-ranks depend on bond type and parent-molecule log rank.
skills.name: probabilistic-log-rank-model-fitting
skills.search_text: probabilistic-log-rank-model-fitting Use when you have molDiscovery fragment-peak matches on training molecules with reference spectra and want to learn or visualize how fragment log-ranks depend on bond type and parent-molecule log rank. Your goal is de novo structure prediction or spectral library search of unknown sample spectra rather than learning fragmentation preferences from reference-spectrum training data The molecules of interest rely on structural features molDiscovery does not model, e.g. benzene rings or large resonant structures, which are 'naively treated as alternate single bonds and double bonds' Fragmentation depends strongly on experimental conditions (instrument type, dissociation technique, ionization mode, collision energy) that differ from the combined CID/HCD positive-mode training spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Fit the conditional probability model P(logRank | bondType, logRankpa) learned by molDiscovery from fragment-peak matches on GNPS spectral library reference spectra, to characterize which bond types (CC, NC, OC single bonds, bridges, 2-cuts) are preferentially broken during mass spectrometry fragmentation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Fit the conditional probability model P(logRank | bondType, logRankpa) learned by molDiscovery from fragment-peak matches on GNPS spectral library reference spectra, to characterize which bond types (CC, NC, OC single bonds, bridges, 2-cuts) are preferentially broken during mass spectrometry fragmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is de novo structure prediction or spectral library search of unknown sample spectra rather than learning fragmentation preferences from reference-spectrum training data The molecules of interest rely on structural features molDiscovery does not model, e.g. benzene rings or large resonant structures, which are 'naively treated as alternate single bonds and double bonds' Fragmentation depends strongly on experimental conditions (instrument type, dissociation technique, ionization mode, collision energy) that differ from the combined CID/HCD positive-mode training spectra

skills.description: Use when a metabolite profiles matrix (e.g. tomato pericarp metabolic profiles for the 2001, 2003 and 2004 harvesting seasons) contains missing values that must be completed before downstream correlation-network construction or other pairwise analyses.
skills.name: probabilistic-pca-data-completion
skills.search_text: probabilistic-pca-data-completion Use when a metabolite profiles matrix (e.g. tomato pericarp metabolic profiles for the 2001, 2003 and 2004 harvesting seasons) contains missing values that must be completed before downstream correlation-network construction or other pairwise analyses. The input matrix already contains no missing values — imputation is unnecessary and would only add noise before correlation-network construction. The downstream analysis is not a pairwise correlation or similar method that requires a complete matrix; other analyses may tolerate missing entries directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Impute missing values in a metabolite profiles matrix using the probabilistic PCA method from the pcaMethods package in R (RStudio), as a preliminary step before constructing metabolite correlation networks. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Impute missing values in a metabolite profiles matrix using the probabilistic PCA method from the pcaMethods package in R (RStudio), as a preliminary step before constructing metabolite correlation networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix already contains no missing values — imputation is unnecessary and would only add noise before correlation-network construction. The downstream analysis is not a pairwise correlation or similar method that requires a complete matrix; other analyses may tolerate missing entries directly.

skills.description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI pixel spectra (e.g. HDF5-format FT-ICR MSI with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be classified normal vs tumor per pixel with probabilistic scores, and spatially mapped uncertainty at tumor margins is the target output.
skills.name: probabilistic-pixel-classification
skills.search_text: probabilistic-pixel-classification Use when raw MALDI-MSI pixel spectra (e.g. HDF5-format FT-ICR MSI with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be classified normal vs tumor per pixel with probabilistic scores, and spatially mapped uncertainty at tumor margins is the target output. Multi-class tissue classification is required — the demonstrated model is binary (normal vs tumor); multi-class is left for future development Input is already a reduced peak/feature table or requires interpretable picked peaks — massNet operates on full raw spectra without prior preprocessing and peak picking Ground-truth annotation cannot be established from annotated histology — for other tissues/tumor types the bottleneck becomes establishing ground truth annotation of the MSI data http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3444 A deep learning skill (massNet) that performs probabilistic pixel-based classification directly from raw, high-dimensional mass spectrometry imaging spectra — no prior preprocessing or peak picking — yielding per-pixel normal/tumor probabilities and spatial uncertainty maps for tumor delineation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: A deep learning skill (massNet) that performs probabilistic pixel-based classification directly from raw, high-dimensional mass spectrometry imaging spectra — no prior preprocessing or peak picking — yielding per-pixel normal/tumor probabilities and spatial uncertainty maps for tumor delineation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Multi-class tissue classification is required — the demonstrated model is binary (normal vs tumor); multi-class is left for future development Input is already a reduced peak/feature table or requires interpretable picked peaks — massNet operates on full raw spectra without prior preprocessing and peak picking Ground-truth annotation cannot be established from annotated histology — for other tissues/tumor types the bottleneck becomes establishing ground truth annotation of the MSI data

skills.description: Use when an mRList of MS-Dial-derived Urine or similar LC-MS/MS feature abundances has been filtered (m/z, NA, CV vs QC) and needs PQN, but mRList$metab_ann lacks the 'reference' column.
skills.name: probabilistic-quotient-normalization
skills.search_text: probabilistic-quotient-normalization Use when an mRList of MS-Dial-derived Urine or similar LC-MS/MS feature abundances has been filtered (m/z, NA, CV vs QC) and needs PQN, but mRList$metab_ann lacks the 'reference' column. Profiles that have already been normalized (e.g. by log or reference-sample normalization) would be distorted by a second PQN pass Data has not been filtered/imputed first (m_z_filtering, filter_NA, CV vs QC, imputation) — PQN quotients would be computed on low-quality or NA-containing features The task is peak picking or drift correction in a different pipeline (e.g. notame's cubic spline drift correction) rather than margheRita-based normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Apply probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) to filtered LC-MS/MS metabolomic profiles with the margheRita function normalize_profiles(method = 'pqn'), generating the required reference profile via calc_reference() when no 'reference' column exists in mRList$metab_ann. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.06.20.599545
skills.summary: Apply probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) to filtered LC-MS/MS metabolomic profiles with the margheRita function normalize_profiles(method = 'pqn'), generating the required reference profile via calc_reference() when no 'reference' column exists in mRList$metab_ann.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Profiles that have already been normalized (e.g. by log or reference-sample normalization) would be distorted by a second PQN pass Data has not been filtered/imputed first (m_z_filtering, filter_NA, CV vs QC, imputation) — PQN quotients would be computed on low-quality or NA-containing features The task is peak picking or drift correction in a different pipeline (e.g. notame's cubic spline drift correction) rather than margheRita-based normalization

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table shows unwanted sample-to-sample variation (e.g. dilution or total-signal differences) and a normalization robust to a few dominant metabolite changes is needed before statistical analysis.
skills.name: probabilistic-quotient-normalization
skills.search_text: probabilistic-quotient-normalization Use when a metabolomics feature table shows unwanted sample-to-sample variation (e.g. dilution or total-signal differences) and a normalization robust to a few dominant metabolite changes is needed before statistical analysis. The feature table has not yet been imputed / cleaned (PQN should be applied during preprocessing on a completed feature table) A normalization tied to measured concentration is required, e.g. when internal standard signals measured in the same sample are available and preferred A distribution-shape correction across samples is the goal rather than a global per-sample scaling factor — quantile normalization, which forces identical empirical distributions, is the better choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) is one of the five sample-to-sample normalization methods implemented in MetaboReport for metabolomics feature tables; each sample is scaled by the median of its feature-wise quotient ratios relative to a reference sample, making it robust to large concentration changes in a few metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) is one of the five sample-to-sample normalization methods implemented in MetaboReport for metabolomics feature tables; each sample is scaled by the median of its feature-wise quotient ratios relative to a reference sample, making it robust to large concentration changes in a few metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table has not yet been imputed / cleaned (PQN should be applied during preprocessing on a completed feature table) A normalization tied to measured concentration is required, e.g. when internal standard signals measured in the same sample are available and preferred A distribution-shape correction across samples is the goal rather than a global per-sample scaling factor — quantile normalization, which forces identical empirical distributions, is the better choice

skills.description: Use when preprocessing a feature-abundance matrix from non-targeted LC-MS metabolomics and samples need to be normalized against a reference (e.g. QC pool) before multivariate analysis.
skills.name: probabilistic-quotient-normalization
skills.search_text: probabilistic-quotient-normalization Use when preprocessing a feature-abundance matrix from non-targeted LC-MS metabolomics and samples need to be normalized against a reference (e.g. QC pool) before multivariate analysis. The matrix is already a peak table straight from MS-DIAL peak picking — mark missing values, correct drift, flag low-quality features and impute missing values first. The dataset is going into batch effect correction with normalize_batches/dobc/ruvs_qc — those operate on their own reference criteria (QC or sample mean/median differences based on feature reproducibility). The analysis is feature-wise statistical testing rather than multivariate analysis where autoscaling after PQN matters. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) in the notame LC–MS metabolomics workflow: scales each sample's feature abundances against a reference (e.g. pooled QC) before autoscaling for multivariate analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135
skills.summary: Probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) in the notame LC–MS metabolomics workflow: scales each sample's feature abundances against a reference (e.g. pooled QC) before autoscaling for multivariate analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix is already a peak table straight from MS-DIAL peak picking — mark missing values, correct drift, flag low-quality features and impute missing values first. The dataset is going into batch effect correction with normalize_batches/dobc/ruvs_qc — those operate on their own reference criteria (QC or sample mean/median differences based on feature reproducibility). The analysis is feature-wise statistical testing rather than multivariate analysis where autoscaling after PQN matters.

skills.description: Use when a trained pSCNN model has produced inclusion probabilities for N mixture–compound spectral pairs and you must convert these probabilities into a thresholded, descending-rank list of candidate components of an NMR mixture.
skills.name: probability-thresholding-and-component-ranking
skills.search_text: probability-thresholding-and-component-ranking Use when a trained pSCNN model has produced inclusion probabilities for N mixture–compound spectral pairs and you must convert these probabilities into a thresholded, descending-rank list of candidate components of an NMR mixture. You have raw NMR spectra but no trained pSCNN model or database compound spectra to form the mixture–compound spectral pairs — training and data augmentation come first The task is training or validating the pSCNN model itself (e.g., splitting the augmented dataset into training, validation and test sets) rather than predicting components of an unknown mixture Compounds in the mixture are not represented in the spectral database, since identification is restricted to database compounds scored by the model http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Ranks candidate mixture components by thresholding the per-pair inclusion probabilities that the pSCNN pseudo-Siamese CNN outputs for each mixture–database compound spectral pair, converting soft predictions into a ranked compound list (e.g., the U1 mixture's β-Ionone → 2-Methylbutyric acid ordering). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Ranks candidate mixture components by thresholding the per-pair inclusion probabilities that the pSCNN pseudo-Siamese CNN outputs for each mixture–database compound spectral pair, converting soft predictions into a ranked compound list (e.g., the U1 mixture's β-Ionone → 2-Methylbutyric acid ordering).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have raw NMR spectra but no trained pSCNN model or database compound spectra to form the mixture–compound spectral pairs — training and data augmentation come first The task is training or validating the pSCNN model itself (e.g., splitting the augmented dataset into training, validation and test sets) rather than predicting components of an unknown mixture Compounds in the mixture are not represented in the spectral database, since identification is restricted to database compounds scored by the model

skills.description: Use when you have a per-fragment probability distribution (atom subsets or chemical subformulae) with exact atomic-composition masses and need to render it as a summed mass spectrum at a specified bin resolution.
skills.name: probability-weighted-fragment-spectral-aggregation
skills.search_text: probability-weighted-fragment-spectral-aggregation Use when you have a per-fragment probability distribution (atom subsets or chemical subformulae) with exact atomic-composition masses and need to render it as a summed mass spectrum at a specified bin resolution. You only need a per-fragment spectrum and not the final summed model prediction — stop at the per-fragment observed-spectrum step instead of aggregating. The fragment distribution carries no probability weights or the weights do not sum to 1; the aggregation relies on the model output probabilities from FormulaNet/SubsetNet. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts a model's predicted probability distribution over molecular fragments into a final mass spectrum by computing an isotope- and mass-defect-aware observed spectrum per fragment, weighting it by the fragment probability, and summing at the desired integer or sub-Dalton bin resolution. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Converts a model's predicted probability distribution over molecular fragments into a final mass spectrum by computing an isotope- and mass-defect-aware observed spectrum per fragment, weighting it by the fragment probability, and summing at the desired integer or sub-Dalton bin resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a per-fragment spectrum and not the final summed model prediction — stop at the per-fragment observed-spectrum step instead of aggregating. The fragment distribution carries no probability weights or the weights do not sum to 1; the aggregation relies on the model output probabilities from FormulaNet/SubsetNet.

skills.search_text: processing-report-generation Use when a matchms library-cleaning pipeline has been run (e.g. on the GNPS public library of 500,569 spectra) and you need a per-filter accounting of removals/repairs to quantify repair-function impact or audit the cleaning run. skills.summary: Auto-generation of a processing report that tallies, per matchms library-cleaning filter, how many spectra were removed, had metadata changed, or had peaks changed, alongside a YAML record of all settings and filters used for reproducibility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to detect wrong chemical annotations that are consistent with the measured mass — the report only counts filter effects and the pipeline lacks plausibility checks that consider both metadata and measured fragments You need standardized instrument type or collision-energy metadata — these fields are not yet cleaned or reported by current matchms filters You need curation during library upload rather than a post-hoc batch cleaning report — a fast validator tool for upload-time curation is only proposed as future work

skills.summary: Automatic emission of two logging artifacts by the matchms library cleaning pipeline (matchms 0.26.4): a YAML file recording all pipeline settings and filters, and a processing report (processing_report.csv) quantifying how many spectra each filter removed, metadata-changed, or peak-changed — the mechanism that makes each GNPS-style cleaning run reproducible and transparent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You expect the report to catch wrong chemical annotations consistent with the measured mass — the pipeline lacks plausibility checks over both metadata and measured fragments; fragment-matching filters are only future work You need standardized instrument type or collision energy fields — current matchms filters do not clean/standardize these metadata Your goal is peak picking or raw-data preprocessing — that is handled by tools like MZMine, MSDial, or OpenMS, not this reporting step

skills.search_text: processing-report-interpreting-per-filter-spectrum-changes Use when auditing or reproducing a matchms SpectrumProcessor/Pipeline cleaning run (e.g. on GNPS, MassBank, or MoNA libraries): you need to verify which filters ran in the fixed global order and how many spectra each filter removed or modified. skills.summary: Interprets the automatically generated matchms processing report, which tabulates per-filter counts of spectra removed, metadata fields changed, and peaks changed during a library-cleaning run, alongside the auto-created YAML workflow file that fixes all settings for reproducibility.

Your processing was not run through the matchms SpectrumProcessor/Pipeline machinery, so no auto-generated report or YAML file exists to interpret. skills.description: Use when raw LC–MS mzML files must be curated into a quality-controlled feature matrix and you need a reusable, versioned sequence of filtering/correction processors rather than ad-hoc scripts.
skills.name: processor-pipeline-architecture-design
skills.search_text: processor-pipeline-architecture-design Use when raw LC–MS mzML files must be curated into a quality-controlled feature matrix and you need a reusable, versioned sequence of filtering/correction processors rather than ad-hoc scripts. Feature detection/annotation, not matrix curation: TidyMS is explicitly noted as lacking feature annotation capability, so this skill is wrong for annotating putative metabolites Peak picking itself: if the input is still raw vendor data and the goal is only retention-time alignment, deisotoping, or grouping adducts, use the extraction stage rather than building the curation Pipeline Datasets without quality-control samples (pooled/intrastudy QCs, blanks): most processors (RSD, D-ratio, blank, prevalence) cannot be computed and the pipeline should not be assembled http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3372 Architectural skill derived from TidyMS: model an LC–MS data-curation strategy as a fixed Pipeline of Processor objects (feature Filters and Correctors) that operate on a DataContainer holding the extracted feature matrix and its sample/feature descriptors as Pandas DataFrames. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Architectural skill derived from TidyMS: model an LC–MS data-curation strategy as a fixed Pipeline of Processor objects (feature Filters and Correctors) that operate on a DataContainer holding the extracted feature matrix and its sample/feature descriptors as Pandas DataFrames.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Feature detection/annotation, not matrix curation: TidyMS is explicitly noted as lacking feature annotation capability, so this skill is wrong for annotating putative metabolites Peak picking itself: if the input is still raw vendor data and the goal is only retention-time alignment, deisotoping, or grouping adducts, use the extraction stage rather than building the curation Pipeline Datasets without quality-control samples (pooled/intrastudy QCs, blanks): most processors (RSD, D-ratio, blank, prevalence) cannot be computed and the pipeline should not be assembled

skills.name: procrustes-coordinate-comparison-visualization
skills.search_text: procrustes-coordinate-comparison-visualization Use when two principal coordinates ordinations of the same samples (e.g., QIIME PCoA files from a procrustes comparison) must be visualized together, or when biplot taxa arrows/jackknifed beta diversity layers should be overlaid on a 3D PCoA plot. The input ordination is not a principal coordinates plot derived from a beta diversity distance matrix — EMPeror is tailored to PCoA of distance matrices as generated by QIIME Running on Windows or without Chrome — the command line interface supports OS X (10.6 and higher) and Linux only, and the graphical user interface requires Chrome Working outside the Python 2.7 environment with QIIME (python libraries only), NumPy, BIOM 1.1.0 and PyCogent installed — these are stated requirements http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Overlay a second ordination onto a 3D principal coordinates scatter so corresponding samples from two PCoA coordinate files are compared/connected as a procrustes analysis plot, using EMPeror's auxiliary-data display alongside biplot and jackknifed beta diversity layers. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/2047-217x-2-16

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input ordination is not a principal coordinates plot derived from a beta diversity distance matrix — EMPeror is tailored to PCoA of distance matrices as generated by QIIME Running on Windows or without Chrome — the command line interface supports OS X (10.6 and higher) and Linux only, and the graphical user interface requires Chrome Working outside the Python 2.7 environment with QIIME (python libraries only), NumPy, BIOM 1.1.0 and PyCogent installed — these are stated requirements

skills.description: Use when comparing imputed vs. original metabolomics data matrices to verify that supervised group-separation structure (e.g., case/control labels like rep(c(0,1), each=80)) was preserved after missing-value imputation.
skills.name: procrustes-sample-distribution-comparison
skills.search_text: procrustes-sample-distribution-comparison Use when comparing imputed vs. original metabolomics data matrices to verify that supervised group-separation structure (e.g., case/control labels like rep(c(0,1), each=80)) was preserved after missing-value imputation. The task concerns unsupervised data structure (PCA-type ordination); the pipeline supports DR='PCA' but group-label fidelity assessment requires supervised PLS with the outcome supplied The imputed dataset lacks matched group labels or a complete original reference matrix, since Procrustes SSE is computed between paired original and imputed ordinations of the same samples Data are non-targeted GC/MS profiles assumed MCAR/MAR after missing retrieval, where default GSimp truncation settings rather than group-difference evaluation drive the choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A supervised multivariate evaluation step from the GSimp imputation pipeline: fit PLS-DA (ropls, nPCs=2) to original and imputed matrices using binary group labels, then quantify divergence of sample distributions via vegan's Procrustes sum of squared errors to test whether an imputation method preserved group-separation structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: A supervised multivariate evaluation step from the GSimp imputation pipeline: fit PLS-DA (ropls, nPCs=2) to original and imputed matrices using binary group labels, then quantify divergence of sample distributions via vegan's Procrustes sum of squared errors to test whether an imputation method preserved group-separation structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task concerns unsupervised data structure (PCA-type ordination); the pipeline supports DR='PCA' but group-label fidelity assessment requires supervised PLS with the outcome supplied The imputed dataset lacks matched group labels or a complete original reference matrix, since Procrustes SSE is computed between paired original and imputed ordinations of the same samples Data are non-targeted GC/MS profiles assumed MCAR/MAR after missing retrieval, where default GSimp truncation settings rather than group-difference evaluation drive the choice

skills.description: Use when XCMS preprocessing leaves suspected misaligned feature groups whose RT drift differs across m/z bins or samples, and single per-sample warping functions cannot correct them.
skills.name: profile-based-graphical-time-warping
skills.search_text: profile-based-graphical-time-warping Use when XCMS preprocessing leaves suspected misaligned feature groups whose RT drift differs across m/z bins or samples, and single per-sample warping functions cannot correct them. The input is already a feature table without raw extracted-ion profiles — ncGTW realignment operates on profile-level data, not peak tables alone Features are well aligned: XCMS's single per-sample warping function already suffices, and ncGTW's false positive rate may be higher than its theoretical 0.05 threshold (as reported for the Rotterdam dataset) Peak-shape distortion after realignment is unacceptable and cannot be handled — apply ncGTW's post-processing module or consider that parameter tuning may be needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Realignment of misaligned LC-MS extracted-ion profile features via ncGTW, a reference-free two-stage graphical time warping (combinatorial pairwise warpings aggregated onto a pseudo-reference), used as a plug-in to replace XCMS corrected retention times. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa037
skills.summary: Realignment of misaligned LC-MS extracted-ion profile features via ncGTW, a reference-free two-stage graphical time warping (combinatorial pairwise warpings aggregated onto a pseudo-reference), used as a plug-in to replace XCMS corrected retention times.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature table without raw extracted-ion profiles — ncGTW realignment operates on profile-level data, not peak tables alone Features are well aligned: XCMS's single per-sample warping function already suffices, and ncGTW's false positive rate may be higher than its theoretical 0.05 threshold (as reported for the Rotterdam dataset) Peak-shape distortion after realignment is unacceptable and cannot be handled — apply ncGTW's post-processing module or consider that parameter tuning may be needed

skills.description: Use when computing BiG-SCAPE's Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index, or when many antiSMASH-predicted domain sequences must be aligned per Pfam domain type against profile HMMs instead of running all-versus-all sequence alignment between BGC pairs.
skills.name: profile-hmm-domain-alignment
skills.search_text: profile-hmm-domain-alignment Use when computing BiG-SCAPE's Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index, or when many antiSMASH-predicted domain sequences must be aligned per Pfam domain type against profile HMMs instead of running all-versus-all sequence alignment between BGC pairs. Goal is evolutionary relationships between clusters (multi-locus phylogenies, genomic context) — that is CORASON's phylogenomic approach, not the profile-HMM DSS alignment Input is raw genome contigs without antiSMASH domain predictions — there are no domain sequences to align; run antiSMASH v4 first Pairwise BGC distances are already computed and only downstream GCF/network clustering is needed Align antiSMASH-predicted BGC domain sequences to their Pfam profile HMMs using hmmalign (HMMER 3.1b2) so that BiG-SCAPE can compute its Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index — copy-number differences plus sequence identity — without quadratic all-versus-all sequence comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Align antiSMASH-predicted BGC domain sequences to their Pfam profile HMMs using hmmalign (HMMER 3.1b2) so that BiG-SCAPE can compute its Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index — copy-number differences plus sequence identity — without quadratic all-versus-all sequence comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is evolutionary relationships between clusters (multi-locus phylogenies, genomic context) — that is CORASON's phylogenomic approach, not the profile-HMM DSS alignment Input is raw genome contigs without antiSMASH domain predictions — there are no domain sequences to align; run antiSMASH v4 first Pairwise BGC distances are already computed and only downstream GCF/network clustering is needed

skills.description: Use when raw profile-mode HRMS files (Waters UNIFI MSE/HDMSE exports or mzML) must be converted to a compact columnar format while retaining ion-mobility dimensions, and later queried, filtered or aggregated with Apache Arrow.
skills.name: profile-mode-hrms-data-handling
skills.search_text: profile-mode-hrms-data-handling Use when raw profile-mode HRMS files (Waters UNIFI MSE/HDMSE exports or mzML) must be converted to a compact columnar format while retaining ion-mobility dimensions, and later queried, filtered or aggregated with Apache Arrow. The data are already stored as an arcMS-created Parquet file and the goal is visualization or filtering — use the Arrow/duckdb query pipeline or the arcms-dataviz Shiny app instead of re-converting. The source data are not Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE exports or mzML files — arcMS collects MSE from UNIFI and supports mzML conversion, not other vendor formats. Only the HDF5 layout (ms1/ms2/metadata datasets in one .h5 file) is required and Parquet is not acceptable — although arcMS supports format="hdf5", this skill targets the Parquet/Arrow columnar workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Convert and handle multi-dimensional profile-mode HRMS data (MSE/HDMSE from Waters UNIFI, or mzML) into columnar Apache Parquet files with arcMS, preserving long-format spectra (rt, scanid, mslevel, mz, intensity, bin, dt) plus metadata, for compact storage and fast Arrow-based access in R or Python. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae160
skills.summary: Convert and handle multi-dimensional profile-mode HRMS data (MSE/HDMSE from Waters UNIFI, or mzML) into columnar Apache Parquet files with arcMS, preserving long-format spectra (rt, scanid, mslevel, mz, intensity, bin, dt) plus metadata, for compact storage and fast Arrow-based access in R or Python.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already stored as an arcMS-created Parquet file and the goal is visualization or filtering — use the Arrow/duckdb query pipeline or the arcms-dataviz Shiny app instead of re-converting. The source data are not Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE exports or mzML files — arcMS collects MSE from UNIFI and supports mzML conversion, not other vendor formats. Only the HDF5 layout (ms1/ms2/metadata datasets in one .h5 file) is required and Parquet is not acceptable — although arcMS supports format="hdf5", this skill targets the Parquet/Arrow columnar workflow.

skills.description: Use when raw mzXML/mzML LC-HRMS profile-mode data must be converted into fixed-size (32 scans x 128 m/z) standardized areas around every local maximum, prior to CNN peak classification.
skills.name: profile-mode-lc-hrms-data-processing
skills.search_text: profile-mode-lc-hrms-data-processing Use when raw mzXML/mzML LC-HRMS profile-mode data must be converted into fixed-size (32 scans x 128 m/z) standardized areas around every local maximum, prior to CNN peak classification. Input is already a centroided peak list or a feature table (e.g. RT/m/z/intensity matrix) — PeakBot requires profile-mode data to extract local-maxima neighborhoods. The goal is feature alignment/grouping of already-detected peaks (use peakbot.cuda.KNNalignFeatures / groupFeatures instead). No CUDA-enabled GPU is available and very large batches must be exported quickly, or GPU memory is below 4 GB without lowering exportBatchSize. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Preprocess raw profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms by detecting all local signal maxima and exporting each as a super-sampled, intensity-scaled standardized area ready for CNN-based peak-apex classification with PeakBot. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Preprocess raw profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms by detecting all local signal maxima and exporting each as a super-sampled, intensity-scaled standardized area ready for CNN-based peak-apex classification with PeakBot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a centroided peak list or a feature table (e.g. RT/m/z/intensity matrix) — PeakBot requires profile-mode data to extract local-maxima neighborhoods. The goal is feature alignment/grouping of already-detected peaks (use peakbot.cuda.KNNalignFeatures / groupFeatures instead). No CUDA-enabled GPU is available and very large batches must be exported quickly, or GPU memory is below 4 GB without lowering exportBatchSize.

skills.description: Use when a matched feature table with peak areas from two peak-picking tools (e.g. PeakBot and XCMS) is available and the goal is to quantify correlation (R2) and the systematic profile-versus-centroid area scaling factor.
skills.name: profile-versus-centroid-mode-area-comparison
skills.search_text: profile-versus-centroid-mode-area-comparison Use when a matched feature table with peak areas from two peak-picking tools (e.g. PeakBot and XCMS) is available and the goal is to quantify correlation (R2) and the systematic profile-versus-centroid area scaling factor. The input is raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms rather than a matched feature peak-area table — peak detection/grouping must be run first (e.g. peakbot.cuda.groupFeatures or XCMS). Features are not matched across the two tools; unmatched feature lists cannot yield per-feature area ratios or a meaningful regression. Only centroid-mode data is available, since the skill quantifies the profile-versus-centroid-mode area scaling between PeakBot (profile) and XCMS (centroid). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantitative comparison of matched feature peak areas from PeakBot (profile-mode LC-HRMS peak-picking) and XCMS via linear regression and robust trimming, plus estimation of the profile-versus-centroid-mode area factor. It verifies how closely PeakBot-derived peak areas agree with XCMS and quantifies the systematic area scaling between the two acquisition modes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac344
skills.summary: Quantitative comparison of matched feature peak areas from PeakBot (profile-mode LC-HRMS peak-picking) and XCMS via linear regression and robust trimming, plus estimation of the profile-versus-centroid-mode area factor. It verifies how closely PeakBot-derived peak areas agree with XCMS and quantifies the systematic area scaling between the two acquisition modes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms rather than a matched feature peak-area table — peak detection/grouping must be run first (e.g. peakbot.cuda.groupFeatures or XCMS). Features are not matched across the two tools; unmatched feature lists cannot yield per-feature area ratios or a meaningful regression. Only centroid-mode data is available, since the skill quantifies the profile-versus-centroid-mode area scaling between PeakBot (profile) and XCMS (centroid).

skills.description: Use when two or more taxonomic profilers report an identical benchmarking score (e.g., UniFrac) on a sample and you need to determine whether the underlying taxonomic profiles actually differ at specific clades.
skills.name: profiler-metric-tie-verification
skills.search_text: profiler-metric-tie-verification Use when two or more taxonomic profilers report an identical benchmarking score (e.g., UniFrac) on a sample and you need to determine whether the underlying taxonomic profiles actually differ at specific clades. When a ground truth (gold standard) profile is not available — TAMPA's tie/difference verification against a reference requires one; it can only suggest appropriate profilers otherwise When you need a binning (not profiling) assessment — use AMBER for binning; this skill targets taxonomic profile comparisons When the profilers' scores are not tied and single-value metrics already separate them — a full TAMPA-style clade-level diff may be unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Verifies whether taxonomic profilers with identical single-value metric scores (e.g., tied UniFrac or F1 scores on a CAMI sample) truly produce identical taxonomic profiles, by computing per-taxon percentage relative abundances and revealing clade-level differences that single-value metrics miss. Grounded in the TAMPA case study where Taxy-Pro and MetaPhyler tied on UniFrac for CAMI_HIGH_S001. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Verifies whether taxonomic profilers with identical single-value metric scores (e.g., tied UniFrac or F1 scores on a CAMI sample) truly produce identical taxonomic profiles, by computing per-taxon percentage relative abundances and revealing clade-level differences that single-value metrics miss. Grounded in the TAMPA case study where Taxy-Pro and MetaPhyler tied on UniFrac for CAMI_HIGH_S001.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a ground truth (gold standard) profile is not available — TAMPA's tie/difference verification against a reference requires one; it can only suggest appropriate profilers otherwise When you need a binning (not profiling) assessment — use AMBER for binning; this skill targets taxonomic profile comparisons When the profilers' scores are not tied and single-value metrics already separate them — a full TAMPA-style clade-level diff may be unnecessary

skills.description: Use when an MS/MS spectrum corresponds to a known peptide sequence and peaks must be labeled as fragment ions (e.g. a, b, y series, including modified residues such as oxidized methionine) for publication-quality figures.
skills.name: proforma-peptide-spectrum-annotation
skills.search_text: proforma-peptide-spectrum-annotation Use when an MS/MS spectrum corresponds to a known peptide sequence and peaks must be labeled as fragment ions (e.g. a, b, y series, including modified residues such as oxidized methionine) for publication-quality figures. Spectra have not yet been converted, centroided, and database-searched — inference/FDR is a downstream step and cannot be applied to raw profile-mode spectra The goal is peptide-only identification without protein-level grouping or false discovery rate assessment Data comes from metabolomics or non-proteomics LC-MS workflows for which protein inference is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 OpenMS-based skill for inferring proteins from identified peptides and applying statistical error control (FDR) after database searching, as used in the GENCODE proteogenomics re-annotation workflow that processed over 55 million public tandem mass spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nmeth.3959
skills.summary: OpenMS-based skill for inferring proteins from identified peptides and applying statistical error control (FDR) after database searching, as used in the GENCODE proteogenomics re-annotation workflow that processed over 55 million public tandem mass spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra have not yet been converted, centroided, and database-searched — inference/FDR is a downstream step and cannot be applied to raw profile-mode spectra The goal is peptide-only identification without protein-level grouping or false discovery rate assessment Data comes from metabolomics or non-proteomics LC-MS workflows for which protein inference is not applicable

skills.description: Use when the research question asks whether two specific proteins physically interact and the source text describes named assays (e.g. yeast two-hybrid, co-IP) with figure/supplement locators that must be tabulated per assay.
skills.name: protein-interaction-evidence-extraction
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-evidence-extraction Use when the research question asks whether two specific proteins physically interact and the source text describes named assays (e.g. yeast two-hybrid, co-IP) with figure/supplement locators that must be tabulated per assay. The question concerns genetic cooperation or mutant phenotypes (e.g. rmh-2(jf94); top-3-ZnF::ha double-mutant phenotypes) rather than physical interaction assays The source text describes a negative interaction result without assay locators, e.g. RMH-1 pull-down experiments that did not detect interaction with RMH-2 A structured interaction table already exists and only needs reformatting rather than extraction from prose http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Extracts physical protein-interaction evidence (assay type, construct pair, outcome, and exact figure/supplement locator) from article Results text into a structured CSV. For the Dello Stritto et al. 2022 NAR TOP-3/RMH-2 study, this yields a two-row table covering the yeast two-hybrid assay (Figure 7C) and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation (Supplementary Figure S5F). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac408
skills.summary: Extracts physical protein-interaction evidence (assay type, construct pair, outcome, and exact figure/supplement locator) from article Results text into a structured CSV. For the Dello Stritto et al. 2022 NAR TOP-3/RMH-2 study, this yields a two-row table covering the yeast two-hybrid assay (Figure 7C) and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation (Supplementary Figure S5F).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns genetic cooperation or mutant phenotypes (e.g. rmh-2(jf94); top-3-ZnF::ha double-mutant phenotypes) rather than physical interaction assays The source text describes a negative interaction result without assay locators, e.g. RMH-1 pull-down experiments that did not detect interaction with RMH-2 A structured interaction table already exists and only needs reformatting rather than extraction from prose

skills.description: Use when a patient's differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) fail to directly enrich the causative gene's metabolite set, and you need network propagation over protein-protein interactions to recover candidate genes from metabolomic enrichment scores.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-seeding
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-seeding Use when a patient's differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) fail to directly enrich the causative gene's metabolite set, and you need network propagation over protein-protein interactions to recover candidate genes from metabolomic enrichment scores. The candidate gene already has direct metabolomic evidence — if the causative gene's own HMDB-annotated metabolites are differentially abundant, ME-score ranking alone may suffice without network propagation. The metabolites driving the phenotype are unmeasured or unannotated (e.g. large glycosaminoglycans in the IDS patient, or acyl glycines/acyl carnitines not annotated to IEM genes in HMDB) — propagation cannot create signal absent from the seed labels. A physical-interaction-only network is required, since functional edges (e.g. co-citation via KEGG pathway membership) carry much of the propagated signal. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Seeds a protein functional linkage network (STRING v11, 19,354 genes) with per-gene metabolomic enrichment (ME/DME) scores and propagates them via label propagation to prioritize disease genes whose own metabolites are not differentially abundant. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Seeds a protein functional linkage network (STRING v11, 19,354 genes) with per-gene metabolomic enrichment (ME/DME) scores and propagates them via label propagation to prioritize disease genes whose own metabolites are not differentially abundant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate gene already has direct metabolomic evidence — if the causative gene's own HMDB-annotated metabolites are differentially abundant, ME-score ranking alone may suffice without network propagation. The metabolites driving the phenotype are unmeasured or unannotated (e.g. large glycosaminoglycans in the IDS patient, or acyl glycines/acyl carnitines not annotated to IEM genes in HMDB) — propagation cannot create signal absent from the seed labels. A physical-interaction-only network is required, since functional edges (e.g. co-citation via KEGG pathway membership) carry much of the propagated signal.

skills.description: Use when you have a segmented single-cell feature matrix with per-cell protein marker intensities and metabolite intensities of very different dimensionality/variability (e.g., ~25 protein vs ~200 metabolic markers) and need a joint latent representation.
skills.name: protein-metabolite-integrative-embedding-analysis
skills.search_text: protein-metabolite-integrative-embedding-analysis Use when you have a segmented single-cell feature matrix with per-cell protein marker intensities and metabolite intensities of very different dimensionality/variability (e.g., ~25 protein vs ~200 metabolic markers) and need a joint latent representation. The data is already a joint embedding or an integrated multi-omics feature table — this skill trains the embedding from raw segmented intensity blocks Protein and metabolite measurements do not come from the same registered single cells (e.g., cross-modality registration via Histone 3/Intercalator and Phosphate 79 m/z channels was not performed), since branch-wise training assumes paired per-cell features The analysis goal is integration across cells/datasets of a single modality — multi-omics integrators like MNN, Scanorama, Conos, MARIO, or Seurat are the article's stated alternatives for that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a two-branch cross-modality Variational Autoencoder (scSpaMet Keras implementation) that fuses normalized single-cell protein (IMC) and metabolite (TOF-SIMS/3D-SMF) intensity blocks into a shared 16-dimensional joint latent embedding, benchmarking reconstruction MAE against single-modality baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43917-5
skills.summary: Trains a two-branch cross-modality Variational Autoencoder (scSpaMet Keras implementation) that fuses normalized single-cell protein (IMC) and metabolite (TOF-SIMS/3D-SMF) intensity blocks into a shared 16-dimensional joint latent embedding, benchmarking reconstruction MAE against single-modality baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is already a joint embedding or an integrated multi-omics feature table — this skill trains the embedding from raw segmented intensity blocks Protein and metabolite measurements do not come from the same registered single cells (e.g., cross-modality registration via Histone 3/Intercalator and Phosphate 79 m/z channels was not performed), since branch-wise training assumes paired per-cell features The analysis goal is integration across cells/datasets of a single modality — multi-omics integrators like MNN, Scanorama, Conos, MARIO, or Seurat are the article's stated alternatives for that setting

skills.name: protein-nucleolar-compartment-proportion-measurement
skills.search_text: protein-nucleolar-compartment-proportion-measurement Use when live-cell, two-color confocal time-lapse images (e.g., Rev-CFP/YFP-CRM1 in HeLa cells) must be converted into time-resolved proportions of each protein within a subnuclear compartment, or when a drug perturbation (e. Single-color images or assays where the two probes cannot be excited/detected separately (no two-dimensional red/green histogram can be built). Situations where the physical proximity of the two proteins is expected to be <10 nm and FRET is the appropriate readout — this skill measures compartment proportions, not binding distances, and the article notes FRET was negative for the large (130 kDa) CRM1. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Quantifies the proportion of a fluorescently tagged protein residing in a defined nuclear compartment (e.g., the nucleolus) over time in live-cell two-color confocal series, by automatic pixel colocalization classification in a two-dimensional intensity histogram after background correction and block-scrambled significance testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422

skills.description: Use when raw MSFragger/FragPipe PSM tables (e.g., searched against a proteome like Mus musculus at 1% protein FDR) must be filtered into a confident peptide/protein set for validating MSI peptide identifications.
skills.name: protein-peptide-mapping-confidence-scoring
skills.search_text: protein-peptide-mapping-confidence-scoring Use when raw MSFragger/FragPipe PSM tables (e.g., searched against a proteome like Mus musculus at 1% protein FDR) must be filtered into a confident peptide/protein set for validating MSI peptide identifications. The input is already a filtered, protein-level feature table rather than raw PSM-level output — the cascade assumes unfiltered MSFragger PSM identifications. The goal is MSI image processing, co-registration of H&E stains, or MSI clustering rather than LC-MS/MS peptide confirmation (those are separate MSIght modules). No monoisotopic mass information is available in the PSM table, making the mass-uniqueness filter inapplicable without re-running the search. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces MSIght's LC-MS/MS peptide confirmation cascade, applying successive filters (unique peptides, unique monoisotopic mass at 0.02 Da tolerance, >=5 peptides per protein) to MSFragger PSM output at 1% protein FDR so that MALDI-MSI peptide images are annotated with high-confidence protein-level support. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Reproduces MSIght's LC-MS/MS peptide confirmation cascade, applying successive filters (unique peptides, unique monoisotopic mass at 0.02 Da tolerance, >=5 peptides per protein) to MSFragger PSM output at 1% protein FDR so that MALDI-MSI peptide images are annotated with high-confidence protein-level support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered, protein-level feature table rather than raw PSM-level output — the cascade assumes unfiltered MSFragger PSM identifications. The goal is MSI image processing, co-registration of H&E stains, or MSI clustering rather than LC-MS/MS peptide confirmation (those are separate MSIght modules). No monoisotopic mass information is available in the PSM table, making the mass-uniqueness filter inapplicable without re-running the search.

skills.description: Use when aligning pairs of fragmentation (MS/MS) spectra that contain multiple delocalized structural differences, where cosine-based similarity fails and a biologically-meaningful alignment with p-value estimation is required.
skills.name: protein-sequence-alignment-analogy-application
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-alignment-analogy-application Use when aligning pairs of fragmentation (MS/MS) spectra that contain multiple delocalized structural differences, where cosine-based similarity fails and a biologically-meaningful alignment with p-value estimation is required. The task is compound identification where cosine-based scoring is already appropriate — the article recommends complementing SIMILE with cosine-based scoring, and notes some molecule classes may be more appropriate for cosine-based scoring. The alignment does not require statistical significance — intermediate similarity scores without p-values are to some degree uninterpretable for prioritizing metabolites. The analysis involves adducts other than protonation/deprotonation — SIMILE is currently limited to analysis of protonation/deprotonation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Applies the protein-sequence alignment framework (Needleman–Wunsch, Smith–Waterman, BLAST) by analogy to tandem mass spectrometry, substituting a pair-specific fragment ion similarity matrix for a global substitution matrix so that MS/MS spectra can be aligned with gaps, substitutions, and statistical significance. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-30118-9
skills.summary: Applies the protein-sequence alignment framework (Needleman–Wunsch, Smith–Waterman, BLAST) by analogy to tandem mass spectrometry, substituting a pair-specific fragment ion similarity matrix for a global substitution matrix so that MS/MS spectra can be aligned with gaps, substitutions, and statistical significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is compound identification where cosine-based scoring is already appropriate — the article recommends complementing SIMILE with cosine-based scoring, and notes some molecule classes may be more appropriate for cosine-based scoring. The alignment does not require statistical significance — intermediate similarity scores without p-values are to some degree uninterpretable for prioritizing metabolites. The analysis involves adducts other than protonation/deprotonation — SIMILE is currently limited to analysis of protonation/deprotonation.

skills.description: Use when the input is an annotated amino acid .fasta file (Type 1 input) and KEGG-based gene annotations are needed to seed a draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction.
skills.name: protein-sequence-alignment-diamond
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-alignment-diamond Use when the input is an annotated amino acid .fasta file (Type 1 input) and KEGG-based gene annotations are needed to seed a draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction. Input is already DIAMOND BLASTp output — use Type 2 input (--file_type 2) instead of re-aligning You already have an existing SBML GENRE needing further gap-filling — use Type 3 input rather than sequence alignment Only transcript or whole-genome nucleotide data without annotated protein sequences is available (Reconstructor expects annotated amino acid .fasta files) http://edamontology.org/topic_0176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns an annotated amino-acid FASTA against a KEGG reference database with DIAMOND BLASTp to produce gene hits that anchor a draft GENRE in Reconstructor. DIAMOND provides BLAST-level sensitivity at 100x–10,000x speed for big protein sequence data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already DIAMOND BLASTp output — use Type 2 input (--file_type 2) instead of re-aligning You already have an existing SBML GENRE needing further gap-filling — use Type 3 input rather than sequence alignment Only transcript or whole-genome nucleotide data without annotated protein sequences is available (Reconstructor expects annotated amino acid .fasta files)

skills.description: Use when you have antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directories in GenBank format and need the predicted gene-cluster protein sequences as input for MASH MinHash redundancy filtering or BiG-SCAPE GCF grouping in BiG-MAP.
skills.name: protein-sequence-extraction-from-genbank
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-extraction-from-genbank Use when you have antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directories in GenBank format and need the predicted gene-cluster protein sequences as input for MASH MinHash redundancy filtering or BiG-SCAPE GCF grouping in BiG-MAP. Input gene clusters are already nonredundant and unique representatives are already chosen — MinHash sketching and medoid selection would only add redundancy filtering overhead The goal is to map metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads or run differential abundance analysis (bigmap-map / bigmap-analyse) rather than build the nonredundant reference collection Input is raw genome FASTA rather than antiSMASH/gutSMASH output — the clusters must first be predicted (README states the module takes 'the output directories of any anti- or gutSMASH run') http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Extracts protein sequences from antiSMASH/gutSMASH GenBank gene-cluster output directories so they can be sketched with MASH and clustered into nonredundant representative gene clusters within the BiG-MAP family module. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/msystems.00937-21

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input gene clusters are already nonredundant and unique representatives are already chosen — MinHash sketching and medoid selection would only add redundancy filtering overhead The goal is to map metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads or run differential abundance analysis (bigmap-map / bigmap-analyse) rather than build the nonredundant reference collection Input is raw genome FASTA rather than antiSMASH/gutSMASH output — the clusters must first be predicted (README states the module takes 'the output directories of any anti- or gutSMASH run')

skills.description: Use when you have computed NMR structure ensembles (from NMRFx torsion-angle calculation on NEF constraint files) that need to be aligned and validated against experimentally confirmed PDB structures, or when aggregating per-protein quality statistics for comparison against published tables.
skills.name: protein-structure-superposition
skills.search_text: protein-structure-superposition Use when you have computed NMR structure ensembles (from NMRFx torsion-angle calculation on NEF constraint files) that need to be aligned and validated against experimentally confirmed PDB structures, or when aggregating per-protein quality statistics for comparison against published tables. When the input is a single unvalidated structure with no corresponding experimentally confirmed PDB reference for alignment When the goal is purely de novo structure prediction without constraint files (no NEF input for NMRFx calculation) When working with RNA or small-molecule structures rather than the protein NMR datasets the article's benchmarking covers http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Alignment and comparison of computed protein NMR structure ensembles against experimentally determined reference structures, using NMRFx's structure-calculation output (10-structure PDBx/mmCIF ensembles) superimposed onto deposited PDB coordinates to validate that the calculated structures agree with published assignments. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-025-01812-8
skills.summary: Alignment and comparison of computed protein NMR structure ensembles against experimentally determined reference structures, using NMRFx's structure-calculation output (10-structure PDBx/mmCIF ensembles) superimposed onto deposited PDB coordinates to validate that the calculated structures agree with published assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is a single unvalidated structure with no corresponding experimentally confirmed PDB reference for alignment When the goal is purely de novo structure prediction without constraint files (no NEF input for NMRFx calculation) When working with RNA or small-molecule structures rather than the protein NMR datasets the article's benchmarking covers

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered LC-MS/MS peptide list mapped to proteins and per-peptide m/z ion images from an imzML MSI dataset that must be summed gene-wise and overlaid on registered histology.
skills.name: protein-wise-peptide-image-aggregation
skills.search_text: protein-wise-peptide-image-aggregation Use when you have a filtered LC-MS/MS peptide list mapped to proteins and per-peptide m/z ion images from an imzML MSI dataset that must be summed gene-wise and overlaid on registered histology. The peptide list has not yet been filtered by LC-MS/MS confirmation — aggregating unconfirmed peptides defeats the confidence-gaining purpose of the MSIght workflow. The H&E-to-MSI registration matrix has not been computed; peptide images must be transformed into histology space before gene-wise summation. The goal is a single-m/z ion image or small-molecule MSI image rather than peptide-level images that must be summed per protein. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Aggregates transformed, per-peptide MALDI-MS ion images into a single summed image per protein (e.g., smoothelin, Col6a1, fibronectin, myosin-11) and overlays the result on the binarized H&E histology image, as implemented in MSIght for Figure 5-style biomarker panels. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Aggregates transformed, per-peptide MALDI-MS ion images into a single summed image per protein (e.g., smoothelin, Col6a1, fibronectin, myosin-11) and overlays the result on the binarized H&E histology image, as implemented in MSIght for Figure 5-style biomarker panels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peptide list has not yet been filtered by LC-MS/MS confirmation — aggregating unconfirmed peptides defeats the confidence-gaining purpose of the MSIght workflow. The H&E-to-MSI registration matrix has not been computed; peptide images must be transformed into histology space before gene-wise summation. The goal is a single-m/z ion image or small-molecule MSI image rather than peptide-level images that must be summed per protein.

skills.description: Use when you have large collections of public tandem MS spectra (e.g. tens of millions) and want to identify peptides supporting novel protein-coding gene annotations beyond an existing genome annotation such as GENCODE.
skills.name: proteogenomics-novel-annotation-discovery
skills.search_text: proteogenomics-novel-annotation-discovery Use when you have large collections of public tandem MS spectra (e.g. tens of millions) and want to identify peptides supporting novel protein-coding gene annotations beyond an existing genome annotation such as GENCODE. When the goal is routine peptide/protein identification within an already-complete annotation and no novel-annotation discovery is intended — standard database searching without the proteogenomics export step suffices. When input spectra cannot be converted to standardized open formats accepted by OpenMS file-conversion tooling. When the reference genome annotation is absent, since novel annotations are defined relative to the reference annotation and cannot be validated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 An OpenMS proteogenomics workflow that searches public tandem mass spectra against a protein reference database, controls FDR through protein inference, and exports peptides mapping outside existing annotation to discover new protein-coding gene annotations (e.g. in the GENCODE human reference genome). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nmeth.3959
skills.summary: An OpenMS proteogenomics workflow that searches public tandem mass spectra against a protein reference database, controls FDR through protein inference, and exports peptides mapping outside existing annotation to discover new protein-coding gene annotations (e.g. in the GENCODE human reference genome).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is routine peptide/protein identification within an already-complete annotation and no novel-annotation discovery is intended — standard database searching without the proteogenomics export step suffices. When input spectra cannot be converted to standardized open formats accepted by OpenMS file-conversion tooling. When the reference genome annotation is absent, since novel annotations are defined relative to the reference annotation and cannot be validated.

skills.name: proteome-first-peptide-annotation
skills.search_text: proteome-first-peptide-annotation Use when you have large collections of unidentified MS/MS spectra (e.g. GLEAMS clusters) and want proteome-anchored de novo peptide assignments plus variant-enrichment evidence for single-mismatch predictions. skills.summary: Assign previously unidentified 'dark proteome' MS/MS spectra by running Casanovo de novo sequencing on GLEAMS-clustered spectra, deriving cluster-level consensus peptides, and retaining only clusters whose consensus peptides map to predicted proteomes.

skills.search_text: proteomexchange-vendor-dataset-retrieval Use when a benchmark or conversion study needs original vendor RAW files, and the article supplies ProteomeXchange/MetaboLights accession IDs (e.g. PXD021390, PXD018139, IPX0001509000, MTBLS2119, XCMS1197236) that must be fetched. You only have the post-QC information_target.csv and no information_all.csv — decoy alignments are absent, so FDR cannot be estimated; rerun DeepRTAlign with keep_temp=1. skills.summary: Reconstructs DeepRTAlign's decoy-based quality-control module, which estimates the FDR of RT-alignment results by randomly designating one aligned group per m/z window as a target, building its decoy counterpart, and computing decoy/target alignment counts at each score cutoff against the default FDR threshold of 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have the post-QC information_target.csv and no information_all.csv — decoy alignments are absent, so FDR cannot be estimated; rerun DeepRTAlign with keep_temp=1. skills.search_text: proteomics-psm-label-pairing Use when spectra have PSM peptide identifications (e.g., Mascot or MSGF+ results at 1% FDR) and you need positive/negative spectrum pairs to train or evaluate a spectral embedding on an independent dataset such as the phosphoproteomics PXD015943 study.
