skills.description: Use when the input consists of vendor Thermo RAW LC-HRMS2 files (negative or positive ionization mode) that must be converted to open formats before MZmine processing or repository upload.
skills.name: proteowizard-msconvert-parameterization
skills.search_text: proteowizard-msconvert-parameterization Use when the input consists of vendor Thermo RAW LC-HRMS2 files (negative or positive ionization mode) that must be converted to open formats before MZmine processing or repository upload. The input files are already in an open format (mzML/mzXML) — reconversion only risks loss or duplication The goal is feature detection, alignment, or .mgf MS2 spectrum export — those are performed by the downstream MZmine step, not by MSConvert The spectra require centroiding, noise filtering, or RT-window filtering — the ENPKG pipeline applies those filters later (e.g., feature filtering to RT 0.5–8.0 min in MZmine), not during format conversion http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Parameterizes MSConvert (ProteoWizard) to convert vendor Thermo RAW LC-MS2 files from the ENPKG sample-centric workflow into open interchange formats (mzXML/mzML) that retain both MS1 and MS2 scans, so downstream MZmine feature detection and MassIVE sharing can proceed. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Parameterizes MSConvert (ProteoWizard) to convert vendor Thermo RAW LC-MS2 files from the ENPKG sample-centric workflow into open interchange formats (mzXML/mzML) that retain both MS1 and MS2 scans, so downstream MZmine feature detection and MassIVE sharing can proceed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input files are already in an open format (mzML/mzXML) — reconversion only risks loss or duplication The goal is feature detection, alignment, or .mgf MS2 spectrum export — those are performed by the downstream MZmine step, not by MSConvert The spectra require centroiding, noise filtering, or RT-window filtering — the ENPKG pipeline applies those filters later (e.g., feature filtering to RT 0.5–8.0 min in MZmine), not during format conversion

skills.description: Use when preparing a small molecule (<~205 Da in the benchmark) for CID-MS/MS spectrum prediction and all plausible protonation sites/protomers must be enumerated and optimized before running collision trajectories.
skills.name: protonated-molecular-ion-protomer-construction
skills.search_text: protonated-molecular-ion-protomer-construction Use when preparing a small molecule (<~205 Da in the benchmark) for CID-MS/MS spectrum prediction and all plausible protonation sites/protomers must be enumerated and optimized before running collision trajectories. The molecule is large (>~205 Da in this benchmark) or highly flexible, where the article notes prediction accuracy drops with increasing molecular mass and protomer/tautomer count You only need to score already-predicted spectra against experimental data — use CIDMD_compare instead You want to predict which protomer forms without running simulations; the article explicitly notes no method exists yet to predict protomer formation states prior to CIDMD http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0081 Constructs all relevant protonated molecular-ion structures (protomers and tautomers) of a target metabolite in Avogadro and geometry-optimizes them at unrestricted B3LYP/6–31G* with TeraChem, providing the input geometries that CIDMD collision simulations require. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00760
skills.summary: Constructs all relevant protonated molecular-ion structures (protomers and tautomers) of a target metabolite in Avogadro and geometry-optimizes them at unrestricted B3LYP/6–31G* with TeraChem, providing the input geometries that CIDMD collision simulations require.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecule is large (>~205 Da in this benchmark) or highly flexible, where the article notes prediction accuracy drops with increasing molecular mass and protomer/tautomer count You only need to score already-predicted spectra against experimental data — use CIDMD_compare instead You want to predict which protomer forms without running simulations; the article explicitly notes no method exists yet to predict protomer formation states prior to CIDMD

skills.description: Use when preparing a small molecule (<205 Da or larger) for CID-MS/MS spectrum prediction from structure alone, and the exact protonation site in ESI is unknown: enumerate every candidate protomer/tautomer at heteroatom sites and simulate each independently before comparing to the experimental.
skills.name: protonation-site-protomer-enumeration
skills.search_text: protonation-site-protomer-enumeration Use when preparing a small molecule (<205 Da or larger) for CID-MS/MS spectrum prediction from structure alone, and the exact protonation site in ESI is unknown: enumerate every candidate protomer/tautomer at heteroatom sites and simulate each independently before comparing to the experimental. The experimental spectrum is already known and only a single dominant protomer was confirmed by prior orthogonal evidence—enumerating all sites adds cost without improving the prediction. The molecule's protonation state under ESI is known unambiguously (e.g., permanent quaternary ammonium) and there are no alternative heteroatom sites—run a single CIDMD simulation instead. Molecules with very large numbers of protomers/tautomers where the article warns average CIDMD prediction accuracy decreases as protomer count grows, making exhaustive enumeration computationally prohibitive. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Systematically enumerate candidate protonated molecular ion (protomer/tautomer) structures at plausible protonation sites—primarily heteroatoms—before running CIDMD simulations, then evaluate each protomer's predicted spectrum against experimental MS/MS to select the most probable protomer(s). The article shows that different protomers yield markedly different fragmentation patterns, so enumeration directly controls prediction accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00760
skills.summary: Systematically enumerate candidate protonated molecular ion (protomer/tautomer) structures at plausible protonation sites—primarily heteroatoms—before running CIDMD simulations, then evaluate each protomer's predicted spectrum against experimental MS/MS to select the most probable protomer(s). The article shows that different protomers yield markedly different fragmentation patterns, so enumeration directly controls prediction accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental spectrum is already known and only a single dominant protomer was confirmed by prior orthogonal evidence—enumerating all sites adds cost without improving the prediction. The molecule's protonation state under ESI is known unambiguously (e.g., permanent quaternary ammonium) and there are no alternative heteroatom sites—run a single CIDMD simulation instead. Molecules with very large numbers of protomers/tautomers where the article warns average CIDMD prediction accuracy decreases as protomer count grows, making exhaustive enumeration computationally prohibitive.

skills.description: Use when non-targeted LC-MS/MS feature lists from dosed vs. blank biological matrices (e.g., mouse plasma, lung, urine, feces) must be annotated as prototypes or metabolites of a known herbal prototype component set.
skills.name: prototype-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: prototype-metabolite-annotation Use when non-targeted LC-MS/MS feature lists from dosed vs. blank biological matrices (e.g., mouse plasma, lung, urine, feces) must be annotated as prototypes or metabolites of a known herbal prototype component set. No prototype component database exists for the herb under study, since MDRB bridging requires prototypes as anchors for mass-defect and fragment-similarity scoring The goal is targeted quantification of known compounds rather than non-targeted annotation of exogenous components in dosed vs. blank samples Only MS2 map similarity matching to a single prototype is needed (MTSF-style), which the article notes cannot exploit mass-defect dimensions or build relationship networks http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Bridges exogenous LC-MS/MS features to herbal prototype components and their metabolites using PATBS background subtraction plus MDRB scoring over m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, and MS2 fragment similarity, as demonstrated for semen Armeniacae Amarum (CKXR) in mice. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Bridges exogenous LC-MS/MS features to herbal prototype components and their metabolites using PATBS background subtraction plus MDRB scoring over m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, and MS2 fragment similarity, as demonstrated for semen Armeniacae Amarum (CKXR) in mice.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prototype component database exists for the herb under study, since MDRB bridging requires prototypes as anchors for mass-defect and fragment-similarity scoring The goal is targeted quantification of known compounds rather than non-targeted annotation of exogenous components in dosed vs. blank samples Only MS2 map similarity matching to a single prototype is needed (MTSF-style), which the article notes cannot exploit mass-defect dimensions or build relationship networks

skills.description: Use when you have scaffold/contig-level gene predictions (from Prodigal or MetaGeneMark) and need to cluster adjacent same-strand genes into proximons based on intergenic distance before operon prediction.
skills.name: proximon-operon-prediction
skills.search_text: proximon-operon-prediction Use when you have scaffold/contig-level gene predictions (from Prodigal or MetaGeneMark) and need to cluster adjacent same-strand genes into proximons based on intergenic distance before operon prediction. Input genes come from different strands or are not adjacent along a scaffold — co-directionality and adjacency are prerequisites for proximon clustering A pre-assembled metagenome or gene predictions are unavailable and raw reads must be processed end-to-end — use the 'ago' process (assembly via IDBA, gene prediction via prodigal) instead of proximon prediction alone Operons must be predicted using functional or experimental annotations — MetaRon's proximon/operon prediction is designed to work without any functional information and cannot exploit such inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identifies proximons — clusters of adjacent co-directional genes — from a gene prediction (.tab) file using an intergenic distance (IGD) threshold of < 601 bp, as implemented in the MetaRon operon prediction pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12864-020-07357-5
skills.summary: Identifies proximons — clusters of adjacent co-directional genes — from a gene prediction (.tab) file using an intergenic distance (IGD) threshold of < 601 bp, as implemented in the MetaRon operon prediction pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genes come from different strands or are not adjacent along a scaffold — co-directionality and adjacency are prerequisites for proximon clustering A pre-assembled metagenome or gene predictions are unavailable and raw reads must be processed end-to-end — use the 'ago' process (assembly via IDBA, gene prediction via prodigal) instead of proximon prediction alone Operons must be predicted using functional or experimental annotations — MetaRon's proximon/operon prediction is designed to work without any functional information and cannot exploit such inputs

skills.description: Use when a single NMR mixture spectrum must be decomposed into its constituent compounds against a library of known compound NMR spectra, especially when chemical shift variation and peak overlapping complicate matching.
skills.name: pscnn-inclusion-probability-prediction
skills.search_text: pscnn-inclusion-probability-prediction Use when a single NMR mixture spectrum must be decomposed into its constituent compounds against a library of known compound NMR spectra, especially when chemical shift variation and peak overlapping complicate matching. You need to identify compounds in a pure (single-compound) spectrum rather than deconvolve a mixture — pSCNN was built for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures No pre-trained model or training data are available and you cannot train pSCNN — the method requires the model uploaded to Zenodo or the data-augmentation training pipeline The target spectra are not NMR (e.g. MS or IR) — the translational-invariance argument and training data are specific to NMR spectral representations http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Predicts whether each compound in an NMR spectral database is present in a mixture by feeding pseudo-Siamese CNN (pSCNN) spectral pairs of the mixture spectrum and each database compound spectrum, then thresholding the predicted inclusion probabilities at 0.5 to rank candidate components. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Predicts whether each compound in an NMR spectral database is present in a mixture by feeding pseudo-Siamese CNN (pSCNN) spectral pairs of the mixture spectrum and each database compound spectrum, then thresholding the predicted inclusion probabilities at 0.5 to rank candidate components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to identify compounds in a pure (single-compound) spectrum rather than deconvolve a mixture — pSCNN was built for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures No pre-trained model or training data are available and you cannot train pSCNN — the method requires the model uploaded to Zenodo or the data-augmentation training pipeline The target spectra are not NMR (e.g. MS or IR) — the translational-invariance argument and training data are specific to NMR spectral representations

skills.description: Use when a similarity/co-clustering matrix must be certified as a kernel: after aggregating H re-sampled co-clustering matrices into a consensus matrix, check all eigenvalues are >= 0 before kernel learning.
skills.name: psd-eigenvalue-verification
skills.search_text: psd-eigenvalue-verification Use when a similarity/co-clustering matrix must be certified as a kernel: after aggregating H re-sampled co-clustering matrices into a consensus matrix, check all eigenvalues are >= 0 before kernel learning. The input matrix is an arbitrary similarity matrix not built as a weighted sum of co-clustering matrices — PSD is not guaranteed and the check may legitimately fail You need to construct or weight kernels across datasets (multiple kernel learning) rather than certify a single consensus matrix's definiteness The matrix is not square/symmetric (e.g. a cluster label assignment or a distance matrix with asymmetric entries) Verifies that a consensus matrix — the non-negative weighted sum of re-sampled co-clustering matrices produced by Consensus Clustering in the klic workflow — is positive semi-definite via eigendecomposition, confirming it can serve as a valid kernel matrix for KLIC. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa593
skills.summary: Verifies that a consensus matrix — the non-negative weighted sum of re-sampled co-clustering matrices produced by Consensus Clustering in the klic workflow — is positive semi-definite via eigendecomposition, confirming it can serve as a valid kernel matrix for KLIC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is an arbitrary similarity matrix not built as a weighted sum of co-clustering matrices — PSD is not guaranteed and the check may legitimately fail You need to construct or weight kernels across datasets (multiple kernel learning) rather than certify a single consensus matrix's definiteness The matrix is not square/symmetric (e.g. a cluster label assignment or a distance matrix with asymmetric entries)

skills.description: Use when a pseudo-3D NMR dataset (a series of 2D planes at varying gradient strength, relaxation delay, titration point, or time point) needs per-cross-peak intensities and decay-parameter fitting, especially with overlapping peaks.
skills.name: pseudo-3d-nmr-series-peak-fitting
skills.search_text: pseudo-3d-nmr-series-peak-fitting Use when a pseudo-3D NMR dataset (a series of 2D planes at varying gradient strength, relaxation delay, titration point, or time point) needs per-cross-peak intensities and decay-parameter fitting, especially with overlapping peaks. Input is a single 1D or plain 2D spectrum with no series dimension — multi-plane sequential fitting is not applicable Cross-peaks are fully resolved, so direct integration suffices and deconvolution-based per-component fitting adds no value Analysis goal is outside the supported series types (T1/T2 relaxation, titration, kinetics, DOSY), e.g., pure CEST profiling handled by the separate CEST/ChemEx workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Per-cross-peak parameter extraction from pseudo-3D NMR series (DOSY gradient arrays, T1/T2 relaxation, titration, kinetics) by combining COLMARvista's client-side plane processing with DEEP Picker/Voigt Fitter deconvolution and multi-plane sequential peak fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s10858-025-00465-y
skills.summary: Per-cross-peak parameter extraction from pseudo-3D NMR series (DOSY gradient arrays, T1/T2 relaxation, titration, kinetics) by combining COLMARvista's client-side plane processing with DEEP Picker/Voigt Fitter deconvolution and multi-plane sequential peak fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single 1D or plain 2D spectrum with no series dimension — multi-plane sequential fitting is not applicable Cross-peaks are fully resolved, so direct integration suffices and deconvolution-based per-component fitting adds no value Analysis goal is outside the supported series types (T1/T2 relaxation, titration, kinetics, DOSY), e.g., pure CEST profiling handled by the separate CEST/ChemEx workflow

skills.name: pseudo-bulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-maldi-data
skills.search_text: pseudo-bulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-maldi-data Use when single-cell MALDI-MS isotope tracing data (e.g. 13C-SpaceM anndata objects with per-cell isotopologue fractions M+0..M+16) must be collapsed per condition to compare with bulk LC-MS or to visualize condition-level shifts. When overall substrate usage is very low (e.g. hypoxia/normoxia experiment), the binomial fit cannot reliably estimate uptake fraction — the model was only used for ACLYkd data. When per-cell heterogeneity is the target (pseudo-bulking intentionally obscures single-cell heterogeneity in acetyl-CoA labelling that bulk analysis hides). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Aggregates quality-controlled single-cell isotopologue distributions from MALDI imaging (13C-SpaceM anndata objects) into pseudo-bulk per-condition distributions by median-averaging, enabling comparison with bulk LC-MS measurements. In the ACLYkd experiment this reveals the shift of the palmitate isotopologue distribution toward lower mass isotopologues after ACLY silencing. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42255-024-01118-4

skills.name: pseudo-bulk-differential-metabolite-expression
skills.search_text: pseudo-bulk-differential-metabolite-expression Use when a MALDI/imaging-MS spatial metabolomics dataset (e.g. imzML converted to a SpaMTP Seurat object) has been segmented into clusters (e.g. urothelium, lamina propria, muscle) and you need significantly differentially expressed m/z peaks between those clusters. Input is already an aggregated/bulk feature table without spatial pixels — pseudo-bulking and spatial clustering are unnecessary The goal is m/z-to-metabolite annotation (use SpaMTP's AnnotateBigData/CalculateAnnotationStatistics pipeline instead of DEM testing) Clustering quality is unverified — DEM calls inherit any segmentation errors from the Louvain clustering step http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Identifies significantly differentially expressed metabolites (DEMs) between spatial metabolomics clusters by pseudo-bulking pixels per cluster and testing with EdgeR via SpaMTP's FindAllDEMs, yielding annotated m/z peaks that define tissue regions. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Identifies significantly differentially expressed metabolites (DEMs) between spatial metabolomics clusters by pseudo-bulking pixels per cluster and testing with EdgeR via SpaMTP's FindAllDEMs, yielding annotated m/z peaks that define tissue regions.

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated m/z intensity matrix with tissue-cluster labels (e.g. urothelium, muscle, adventitial layer) and need to identify metabolite peaks that vary between spatial regions via differential expression testing.
skills.name: pseudo-bulk-pooling-of-spatial-metabolite-intensities
skills.search_text: pseudo-bulk-pooling-of-spatial-metabolite-intensities Use when you have an annotated m/z intensity matrix with tissue-cluster labels (e.g. urothelium, muscle, adventitial layer) and need to identify metabolite peaks that vary between spatial regions via differential expression testing. When the input is already bulk or pseudo-bulked metabolomics data rather than pixel-level MALDI imaging intensities requiring aggregation. When the goal is multi-modal SM-ST integration or pathway analysis rather than region-vs-region differential peak expression testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aggregate MALDI imaging m/z intensity values per spatial region or cluster by summing relative intensities into pseudo-bulked pools, then run edgeR differential testing to identify significantly differentially expressed metabolite peaks between tissue regions. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Aggregate MALDI imaging m/z intensity values per spatial region or cluster by summing relative intensities into pseudo-bulked pools, then run edgeR differential testing to identify significantly differentially expressed metabolite peaks between tissue regions.

skills.description: Use when evaluating de novo peptide sequencing tools on antibody MS/MS data and no authoritative reference sequences exist — a database search against the known antibody sequences provides the pseudo-ground-truth PSMs needed to compute precision, recall and error-type distributions.
skills.name: pseudo-ground-truth-comparison-database-search
skills.search_text: pseudo-ground-truth-comparison-database-search Use when evaluating de novo peptide sequencing tools on antibody MS/MS data and no authoritative reference sequences exist — a database search against the known antibody sequences provides the pseudo-ground-truth PSMs needed to compute precision, recall and error-type distributions. When a true reference antibody sequence is unavailable or the protein database is too incomplete for a meaningful database search — the pseudo-ground truth would then be unreliable When the goal is to discriminate isomeric residues such as isoleucine/leucine, which the article notes cannot be resolved via MS/MS and require MS3 fragmentation http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds a pseudo-ground-truth set of peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) for antibody MS/MS data by database searching with MS-GF+ and X!Tandem via SearchGUI (v.4.1.7) and PeptideShaker (v.2.2.2) at 1% FDR, so that de novo sequencing predictions (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) can be scored against an independent reference. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Builds a pseudo-ground-truth set of peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) for antibody MS/MS data by database searching with MS-GF+ and X!Tandem via SearchGUI (v.4.1.7) and PeptideShaker (v.2.2.2) at 1% FDR, so that de novo sequencing predictions (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) can be scored against an independent reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a true reference antibody sequence is unavailable or the protein database is too incomplete for a meaningful database search — the pseudo-ground truth would then be unreliable When the goal is to discriminate isomeric residues such as isoleucine/leucine, which the article notes cannot be resolved via MS/MS and require MS3 fragmentation

skills.description: Use when de novo sequencing predictions on antibody MS/MS data must be scored for accuracy or filtered against reference peptides from database search, e.g. to set confidence thresholds at 50% AA precision before ALPS assembly.
skills.name: pseudo-ground-truth-peptide-matching
skills.search_text: pseudo-ground-truth-peptide-matching Use when de novo sequencing predictions on antibody MS/MS data must be scored for accuracy or filtered against reference peptides from database search, e.g. to set confidence thresholds at 50% AA precision before ALPS assembly. When a true reference protein or antibody sequence is available — database-search-derived pseudo-ground truth is only needed when no a priori sequence knowledge exists When full-length reconstruction rather than prediction-quality assessment is the goal — that requires the de Bruijn assembler ALPS applied to the already-filtered predictions When distinguishing isobaric residues (e.g. I/L, Q vs AG, deamidated N vs D) — the matched-amino-acid criterion cannot resolve these via MS/MS http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Matches de novo peptide sequencing predictions (e.g. from Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) against a pseudo-ground-truth peptide set derived from database search (MS-GF+ and X!Tandem combined via PeptideShaker at 1% FDR), using a matched-amino-acid criterion to compute amino-acid-level precision and calibrate per-tool confidence-score thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbac542
skills.summary: Matches de novo peptide sequencing predictions (e.g. from Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) against a pseudo-ground-truth peptide set derived from database search (MS-GF+ and X!Tandem combined via PeptideShaker at 1% FDR), using a matched-amino-acid criterion to compute amino-acid-level precision and calibrate per-tool confidence-score thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a true reference protein or antibody sequence is available — database-search-derived pseudo-ground truth is only needed when no a priori sequence knowledge exists When full-length reconstruction rather than prediction-quality assessment is the goal — that requires the de Bruijn assembler ALPS applied to the already-filtered predictions When distinguishing isobaric residues (e.g. I/L, Q vs AG, deamidated N vs D) — the matched-amino-acid criterion cannot resolve these via MS/MS

skills.description: Use when an LMS-level (molecular species) intensity matrix must be decomposed into chain-level lipid building block rows for downstream LBB-level statistics or pathway analysis, preserving total sample signal.
skills.name: pseudo-lipid-header-construction
skills.search_text: pseudo-lipid-header-construction Use when an LMS-level (molecular species) intensity matrix must be decomposed into chain-level lipid building block rows for downstream LBB-level statistics or pathway analysis, preserving total sample signal. The input matrix is already at the LBB (building block/chain) or LCL (lipid class) level and needs no species-to-chain decomposition. Row identifiers cannot be parsed into a lipid class prefix plus chain list (non-standard lipid shorthand notation), since chain count and pseudo-lipid headers depend on this parsing. The goal is class-level or molecular-species-level analysis, where splitting into chains would discard species-level information. Reconstructs LipidOne 2.0's automated generation of the lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix: each molecular-species row (e.g., 'PC 16:0_18:1') is split into chain-level pseudo-lipid rows with class-underscore-chain headers, intensities divided by chain count to conserve signal, and duplicate pseudo-lipid rows summed. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cpz1.70009
skills.summary: Reconstructs LipidOne 2.0's automated generation of the lipid building block (LBB) sub-matrix: each molecular-species row (e.g., 'PC 16:0_18:1') is split into chain-level pseudo-lipid rows with class-underscore-chain headers, intensities divided by chain count to conserve signal, and duplicate pseudo-lipid rows summed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already at the LBB (building block/chain) or LCL (lipid class) level and needs no species-to-chain decomposition. Row identifiers cannot be parsed into a lipid class prefix plus chain list (non-standard lipid shorthand notation), since chain count and pseudo-lipid headers depend on this parsing. The goal is class-level or molecular-species-level analysis, where splitting into chains would discard species-level information.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a spatial-transcriptome/MALDI-MSI integration method and no real paired metabolome data exist — split features of a 10X Visium mouse-brain section into two pseudo-sections and perturb coordinates with Gaussian translation to mimic neighboring-section morphology.
skills.name: pseudo-maldi-msi-simulation
skills.search_text: pseudo-maldi-msi-simulation Use when benchmarking a spatial-transcriptome/MALDI-MSI integration method and no real paired metabolome data exist — split features of a 10X Visium mouse-brain section into two pseudo-sections and perturb coordinates with Gaussian translation to mimic neighboring-section morphology. When real paired MALDI-MSI and spatial transcriptome data from the same tissue section exist — use actual data rather than simulated pseudo-sections. When the integration method under test requires metabolite/peak features (m/z) rather than gene features — a pseudo-MSI section built from gene splits contains no metabolomic content. When evaluating performance on higher-resolution spatial data (the article notes this behavior 'should be further explored' and is not assessed by this benchmark). http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Generates benchmark pairs of pseudo-spatial-transcriptome and pseudo-MALDI-MSI sections from public 10X Visium spatial transcriptome data by randomly splitting gene features and applying Gaussian translation to spatial coordinates, so haCCA's integration accuracy can be evaluated without real paired MSI data. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: Generates benchmark pairs of pseudo-spatial-transcriptome and pseudo-MALDI-MSI sections from public 10X Visium spatial transcriptome data by randomly splitting gene features and applying Gaussian translation to spatial coordinates, so haCCA's integration accuracy can be evaluated without real paired MSI data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When real paired MALDI-MSI and spatial transcriptome data from the same tissue section exist — use actual data rather than simulated pseudo-sections. When the integration method under test requires metabolite/peak features (m/z) rather than gene features — a pseudo-MSI section built from gene splits contains no metabolomic content. When evaluating performance on higher-resolution spatial data (the article notes this behavior 'should be further explored' and is not assessed by this benchmark).

skills.description: Use when input is centroid-mode SWATH-DIA mzML with sequential variable-size MS2 windows (e.g., 10 windows, 1.0 m/z overlap, ~0.9 s cycle time) and pseudo-MS2 spectra must be reconstructed per MS1 feature.
skills.name: pseudo-ms2-spectrum-reconstruction
skills.search_text: pseudo-ms2-spectrum-reconstruction Use when input is centroid-mode SWATH-DIA mzML with sequential variable-size MS2 windows (e.g., 10 windows, 1.0 m/z overlap, ~0.9 s cycle time) and pseudo-MS2 spectra must be reconstructed per MS1 feature. The data are DDA with chimeric spectra — use the auto-optimized DDA deconvolution workflow (PerformDDADeconvolution) instead Input is already a feature table or processed peak list with no raw SWATH MS2 windows available for EIC detection MS1-only data with no MS2 spectra, where relinking precursors to fragments is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Deconvolves SWATH-DIA MS2 spectra so that precursors are correctly relinked with their fragment ions when all ions in a wide m/z range are co-fragmented, exporting a pseudo-MS2 spectrum per target MS1 feature. Implemented in MetaboAnalystR 4.0 as a DecoMetDIA-style algorithm with an Rcpp/C++ core supporting parallel computing. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-48009-6
skills.summary: Deconvolves SWATH-DIA MS2 spectra so that precursors are correctly relinked with their fragment ions when all ions in a wide m/z range are co-fragmented, exporting a pseudo-MS2 spectrum per target MS1 feature. Implemented in MetaboAnalystR 4.0 as a DecoMetDIA-style algorithm with an Rcpp/C++ core supporting parallel computing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are DDA with chimeric spectra — use the auto-optimized DDA deconvolution workflow (PerformDDADeconvolution) instead Input is already a feature table or processed peak list with no raw SWATH MS2 windows available for EIC detection MS1-only data with no MS2 spectra, where relinking precursors to fragments is impossible

skills.description: Use when annotating features from AIF LC–MS/MS data by ranking library candidates per feature using m/z error and fragment matching against pseudo-MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: pseudo-msms-fragment-library-matching
skills.search_text: pseudo-msms-fragment-library-matching Use when annotating features from AIF LC–MS/MS data by ranking library candidates per feature using m/z error and fragment matching against pseudo-MS/MS spectra. Input is targeted MS/MS data with true precursor-selected fragmentation spectra — spectral matching to MS/MS libraries (METLIN, MassBank, GNPS) is more appropriate. Data were acquired on a DIA scheme other than AIF (e.g., SWATH), which MetaboAnnotatoR does not currently support. The feature table was already fully annotated (e.g., by MS-DIAL) and no re-ranking of library candidates is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Scores and ranks candidate metabolites per LC–MS feature by combining a bounded reciprocal m/z error term with a pseudo-MS/MS fragment-matching score, downweighting AIF-only fragments, as implemented in MetaboAnnotatoR for AIF untargeted metabolomics annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Scores and ranks candidate metabolites per LC–MS feature by combining a bounded reciprocal m/z error term with a pseudo-MS/MS fragment-matching score, downweighting AIF-only fragments, as implemented in MetaboAnnotatoR for AIF untargeted metabolomics annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is targeted MS/MS data with true precursor-selected fragmentation spectra — spectral matching to MS/MS libraries (METLIN, MassBank, GNPS) is more appropriate. Data were acquired on a DIA scheme other than AIF (e.g., SWATH), which MetaboAnnotatoR does not currently support. The feature table was already fully annotated (e.g., by MS-DIAL) and no re-ranking of library candidates is needed.

skills.description: Use when MS1-only data (mzML/mzXML/imzML or pseudo MS/MS .mgf) must be structurally annotated or annotation propagated across molecular networks via spectral similarity, as in MASST-style cross-matching.
skills.name: pseudo-msms-spectral-matching
skills.search_text: pseudo-msms-spectral-matching Use when MS1-only data (mzML/mzXML/imzML or pseudo MS/MS .mgf) must be structurally annotated or annotation propagated across molecular networks via spectral similarity, as in MASST-style cross-matching. The data already contains true MS/MS scans — standard MS/MS library searching is appropriate instead of pseudo MS/MS reconstruction from in-source fragments Only an aligned feature table without chromatographic or spatial correlation information is available, so no pseudo MS/MS spectra can be generated The metabolite class requires lipid-only tools such as rMSIfragment; ms1-id is the complementary approach providing broader coverage across metabolite classes Propagates and validates structural annotations by matching pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra generated from MS1-only data against MS/MS library or neighbor-pool spectra using flash-entropy-based cosine matching in ms1-id, enabling level 2/3 annotation of full-scan LC-MS and imaging data. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Propagates and validates structural annotations by matching pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra generated from MS1-only data against MS/MS library or neighbor-pool spectra using flash-entropy-based cosine matching in ms1-id, enabling level 2/3 annotation of full-scan LC-MS and imaging data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data already contains true MS/MS scans — standard MS/MS library searching is appropriate instead of pseudo MS/MS reconstruction from in-source fragments Only an aligned feature table without chromatographic or spatial correlation information is available, so no pseudo MS/MS spectra can be generated The metabolite class requires lipid-only tools such as rMSIfragment; ms1-id is the complementary approach providing broader coverage across metabolite classes

skills.description: Use when pseudo MS/MS spectra generated by ms1-id from MS1-only LC-MS data contain extra ion forms above the feature's precursor m/z and must be prepared for modified cosine molecular networking or library matching.
skills.name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-cleaning
skills.search_text: pseudo-msms-spectrum-cleaning Use when pseudo MS/MS spectra generated by ms1-id from MS1-only LC-MS data contain extra ion forms above the feature's precursor m/z and must be prepared for modified cosine molecular networking or library matching. When the target is ms1-id's precursor-tolerant reverse spectral search against reference MS/MS libraries — that search tolerates extra ion forms (adducts, multimers, contaminants) and discards unmatched query peaks, so aggressive cleaning is unnecessary When input is real MS/MS (MS2) spectra, whose fragments are inherently below the precursor and need no precursor-m/z filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Cleans pseudo MS/MS spectra reconstructed from MS1-only data by removing all fragment ions with m/z larger than the metabolic feature's precursor m/z, so that modified cosine-based spectral similarity calculations (e.g. GNPS2 molecular networking) become possible. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Cleans pseudo MS/MS spectra reconstructed from MS1-only data by removing all fragment ions with m/z larger than the metabolic feature's precursor m/z, so that modified cosine-based spectral similarity calculations (e.g. GNPS2 molecular networking) become possible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target is ms1-id's precursor-tolerant reverse spectral search against reference MS/MS libraries — that search tolerates extra ion forms (adducts, multimers, contaminants) and discards unmatched query peaks, so aggressive cleaning is unnecessary When input is real MS/MS (MS2) spectra, whose fragments are inherently below the precursor and need no precursor-m/z filtering

skills.description: Use when input is MS1-only data — mzML/mzXML LC-MS runs or imzML imaging acquisitions — and structural (level 2/3) annotation requires pseudo MS/MS spectra built from correlated in-source fragments.
skills.name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-generation
skills.search_text: pseudo-msms-spectrum-generation Use when input is MS1-only data — mzML/mzXML LC-MS runs or imzML imaging acquisitions — and structural (level 2/3) annotation requires pseudo MS/MS spectra built from correlated in-source fragments. Data already contains true MS/MS scans (DDA MS/MS spectra) — use direct MS/MS library matching instead of pseudo-spectrum reconstruction. Input is already a pseudo_msms.mgf file — proceed directly to annotation rather than regenerating spectra. The target features' co-eluting ions do not share ≥ 4 consecutive MS1 scans (LC-MS) or ≥ 50 non-zero shared pixels (imaging), so no correlated cluster can be formed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generate pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only LC-MS or MS imaging data by clustering in/post-source fragment ions that correlate with a target feature across the chromatographic (XIC) or spatial (ion-image) domain, then write them as MGF for downstream spectral-library annotation with ms1-id. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Generate pseudo MS/MS spectra from MS1-only LC-MS or MS imaging data by clustering in/post-source fragment ions that correlate with a target feature across the chromatographic (XIC) or spatial (ion-image) domain, then write them as MGF for downstream spectral-library annotation with ms1-id.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data already contains true MS/MS scans (DDA MS/MS spectra) — use direct MS/MS library matching instead of pseudo-spectrum reconstruction. Input is already a pseudo_msms.mgf file — proceed directly to annotation rather than regenerating spectra. The target features' co-eluting ions do not share ≥ 4 consecutive MS1 scans (LC-MS) or ≥ 50 non-zero shared pixels (imaging), so no correlated cluster can be formed.

skills.description: Use when input is MS1-only full-scan data (mzML, mzXML, or imzML) containing in-source fragments and the goal is structural (level 2/3) annotation without real MS/MS spectra — e.g. reanalysis of public repository LC-MS or MS imaging files.
skills.name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-generation-from-in-source-fragments
skills.search_text: pseudo-msms-spectrum-generation-from-in-source-fragments Use when input is MS1-only full-scan data (mzML, mzXML, or imzML) containing in-source fragments and the goal is structural (level 2/3) annotation without real MS/MS spectra — e.g. reanalysis of public repository LC-MS or MS imaging files. The data already contain genuine MS/MS scans — standard MS/MS library search (e.g. the ms2_id branch of the ms1-id lcms workflow) is the appropriate route Data were acquired with deliberate extra in-source fragmentation (isCID) designs — enhanced in-source fragmentation methods such as IDSL.CSA, eISA, or EISA-EXPOSOME are designed for that scenario instead The annotation target is lipid-only, where specialized tools like rMSIfragment or HERMES (in-source fragment annotation) may be preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Generates pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra from MS1-only full-scan LC-MS or imaging MS data by clustering in/post-source fragment ions with correlation analysis, enabling level 2/3 structural annotation via reverse spectral search against reference MS/MS libraries. This addresses the gap that over 40% of public LC-MS files contain only MS1 scans. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.14.618269
skills.summary: Generates pseudo MS/MS (composite) spectra from MS1-only full-scan LC-MS or imaging MS data by clustering in/post-source fragment ions with correlation analysis, enabling level 2/3 structural annotation via reverse spectral search against reference MS/MS libraries. This addresses the gap that over 40% of public LC-MS files contain only MS1 scans.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data already contain genuine MS/MS scans — standard MS/MS library search (e.g. the ms2_id branch of the ms1-id lcms workflow) is the appropriate route Data were acquired with deliberate extra in-source fragmentation (isCID) designs — enhanced in-source fragmentation methods such as IDSL.CSA, eISA, or EISA-EXPOSOME are designed for that scenario instead The annotation target is lipid-only, where specialized tools like rMSIfragment or HERMES (in-source fragment annotation) may be preferred

skills.description: Use when processing centroid-mode LC-MS AIF (DIA) chromatograms where the analyst needs a pseudo-MS/MS spectrum for a subset of features of interest, e.g. features reaching statistical significance in an untargeted metabolomics experiment.
skills.name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-reconstruction-from-aif
skills.search_text: pseudo-msms-spectrum-reconstruction-from-aif Use when processing centroid-mode LC-MS AIF (DIA) chromatograms where the analyst needs a pseudo-MS/MS spectrum for a subset of features of interest, e.g. features reaching statistical significance in an untargeted metabolomics experiment. Input data were acquired with a DIA scheme other than plain AIF (e.g. SWATH-MS, SONAR) — MetaboAnnotatoR currently supports only AIF and the article flags this as future work. The analyst needs annotated spectra for all detected features in an untargeted manner — MS-DIAL performs untargeted annotation, whereas this workflow is intentionally restricted to a user-selected feature subset. The target compound's fragments are poorly detected or the feature co-elutes with compounds sharing similar chemical groups — the article warns this can yield incomplete pseudo-MS/MS spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstruct an in-source pseudo-MS/MS spectrum for a target LC-MS feature from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) data by correlating its MS1 extracted ion chromatogram (EIC) with high-collision-energy AIF EICs (MetaboAnnotatoR step 2, using xcmsSpec/RCspec/getPseudoMSMS), retaining co-eluting fragment peaks above a correlation threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03032
skills.summary: Reconstruct an in-source pseudo-MS/MS spectrum for a target LC-MS feature from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) data by correlating its MS1 extracted ion chromatogram (EIC) with high-collision-energy AIF EICs (MetaboAnnotatoR step 2, using xcmsSpec/RCspec/getPseudoMSMS), retaining co-eluting fragment peaks above a correlation threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data were acquired with a DIA scheme other than plain AIF (e.g. SWATH-MS, SONAR) — MetaboAnnotatoR currently supports only AIF and the article flags this as future work. The analyst needs annotated spectra for all detected features in an untargeted manner — MS-DIAL performs untargeted annotation, whereas this workflow is intentionally restricted to a user-selected feature subset. The target compound's fragments are poorly detected or the feature co-elutes with compounds sharing similar chemical groups — the article warns this can yield incomplete pseudo-MS/MS spectra.

skills.description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a spatial omics integration method (e.g. haCCA) that claims to outperform morphological alignment (STUtility, ICP) on data where no true shared spots exist, by building a pseudo-paired dataset with a known ground truth for label transfer.
skills.name: pseudo-paired-omics-data-evaluation
skills.search_text: pseudo-paired-omics-data-evaluation Use when evaluating or benchmarking a spatial omics integration method (e.g. haCCA) that claims to outperform morphological alignment (STUtility, ICP) on data where no true shared spots exist, by building a pseudo-paired dataset with a known ground truth for label transfer. Data contains true shared spots or features between the spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI modalities, so a paired evaluation with real correspondence is possible instead of a pseudo-paired surrogate. The goal is to integrate real-world normal tissue or tumor data rather than to quantify benchmark performance against morphological alignment methods. Only a single spatial modality is available (no second spatial metabolome/MSI layer), so no cross-modality label transfer can be scored. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Creates pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome/MALDI-MSI data with known ground-truth correspondence so that haCCA's label-transfer accuracy (AC) and ARI can be benchmarked against morphological-only alternatives such as STUtility and standalone ICP. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: Creates pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome/MALDI-MSI data with known ground-truth correspondence so that haCCA's label-transfer accuracy (AC) and ARI can be benchmarked against morphological-only alternatives such as STUtility and standalone ICP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contains true shared spots or features between the spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI modalities, so a paired evaluation with real correspondence is possible instead of a pseudo-paired surrogate. The goal is to integrate real-world normal tissue or tumor data rather than to quantify benchmark performance against morphological alignment methods. Only a single spatial modality is available (no second spatial metabolome/MSI layer), so no cross-modality label transfer can be scored.

skills.description: Use when you have NMR spectral pairs of mixture components with chemical shift variation and need to identify mixture components, or to test how much ppm-level shift a trained pSCNN model tolerates.
skills.name: pseudo-siamese-cnn-inference-on-nmr-spectra
skills.search_text: pseudo-siamese-cnn-inference-on-nmr-spectra Use when you have NMR spectral pairs of mixture components with chemical shift variation and need to identify mixture components, or to test how much ppm-level shift a trained pSCNN model tolerates. Your input is a single pure-compound spectrum rather than mixture spectra / mixture-component spectral pairs — pSCNN was built for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures You need to train the pSCNN model from scratch on augmented data rather than reload the pretrained Zenodo model for prediction Your chemical shift variation exceeds the tested +/-0.052 ppm range, beyond which the paper's robustness guarantee (probabilities > 0.5 within (-0.015, 0.015) ppm) no longer applies http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reload a pretrained pseudo Siamese convolutional neural network (pSCNN) to predict which compounds are present in NMR spectra of mixtures, and quantify its robustness to chemical shift variation by feeding 980 chemically shifted spectral pairs and checking predicted probabilities stay above 0.5. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Reload a pretrained pseudo Siamese convolutional neural network (pSCNN) to predict which compounds are present in NMR spectra of mixtures, and quantify its robustness to chemical shift variation by feeding 980 chemically shifted spectral pairs and checking predicted probabilities stay above 0.5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is a single pure-compound spectrum rather than mixture spectra / mixture-component spectral pairs — pSCNN was built for compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures You need to train the pSCNN model from scratch on augmented data rather than reload the pretrained Zenodo model for prediction Your chemical shift variation exceeds the tested +/-0.052 ppm range, beyond which the paper's robustness guarantee (probabilities > 0.5 within (-0.015, 0.015) ppm) no longer applies

skills.description: Use when analyzing MSI data with hundreds-to-thousands of peaks per pixel, where untargeted analysis of the full pixel-level mass spectrum is intractable and a per-pixel pooled spectrum is needed.
skills.name: pseudobulk-spectrum-construction
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-spectrum-construction Use when analyzing MSI data with hundreds-to-thousands of peaks per pixel, where untargeted analysis of the full pixel-level mass spectrum is intractable and a per-pixel pooled spectrum is needed. Input is already a per-sample pooled spectrum or a peak table — summation would be redundant. Targeted analysis of a known m/z where a per-pixel spatial map is required — summation destroys the spatial dimension needed for localization. Data from a non-linear developmental axis where linear gradient assumptions of DIMPLE do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sum DESI-MSI pixel intensities across a spatial dataset into a single pseudobulk mass spectrum per root, providing the m/z intensity profile from which consensus peaks are extracted in the DIMPLE pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.22.677919
skills.summary: Sum DESI-MSI pixel intensities across a spatial dataset into a single pseudobulk mass spectrum per root, providing the m/z intensity profile from which consensus peaks are extracted in the DIMPLE pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-sample pooled spectrum or a peak table — summation would be redundant. Targeted analysis of a known m/z where a per-pixel spatial map is required — summation destroys the spatial dimension needed for localization. Data from a non-linear developmental axis where linear gradient assumptions of DIMPLE do not apply.

skills.description: Use when time-course relative-abundance metabolomics data must be converted into flux profiles for penalty calculation, and the stoichiometric system S·v = dx/dt is underdetermined without fluxomics measurements.
skills.name: pseudoinverse-underdetermined-system-computation
skills.search_text: pseudoinverse-underdetermined-system-computation Use when time-course relative-abundance metabolomics data must be converted into flux profiles for penalty calculation, and the stoichiometric system S·v = dx/dt is underdetermined without fluxomics measurements. Data are from eukaryotic systems where inter-compartment transport reactions matter — MetaboPAC does not take transport reactions across intracellular compartments into consideration Samples are extracellular or multi-compartment — the approach applies only to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment Flux profiles are already available from fluxomics measurements, making inference from concentration derivatives unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Solves the stoichiometric mass-balance system S·v = dx/dt to infer metabolic flux profiles needed by MetaboPAC's penalty calculation: exactly for determined systems and via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse (with known kinetic terms constraining the system) for underdetermined models. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c

skills.search_text: psm-false-discovery-rate-control Use when PSMs from a spectral library or database search (e.g., ANN-SoLo, MS-GF+) must be filtered to a 1% FDR before counting identifications, propagating peptide labels, or building training resources. Identifications are already provided with FDR-controlled q-values in the source dataset (e.g., MassIVE-KB metadata TSV), so re-filtering would be redundant The downstream analysis requires sensitivity over specificity, since 1% FDR deliberately discards lower-confidence matches The search results are de novo sequences or spectral embeddings (e.g., GLEAMS 32-dimensional vectors) that lack target-decoy PSM scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies 1% false discovery rate (FDR) control to peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) from database and spectral library searching so that only confident identifications are counted, propagated, or used for downstream annotation. In this workflow, FDR-controlled PSMs underpin both GLEAMS training data compilation and validation of ANN-SoLo open modification search results. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Applies 1% false discovery rate (FDR) control to peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) from database and spectral library searching so that only confident identifications are counted, propagated, or used for downstream annotation. skills.description: Use when evaluating the purity of spectrum clustering results: you have per-spectrum cluster labels from a clustering tool and need to attach 1%-FDR PSM peptide identifications (e.g., from MS-GF+ via MassIVE RMSV000000091.3) to compute the fraction of incorrectly clustered spectra.
skills.name: psm-fdr-identification-mapping
skills.search_text: psm-fdr-identification-mapping Use when evaluating the purity of spectrum clustering results: you have per-spectrum cluster labels from a clustering tool and need to attach 1%-FDR PSM peptide identifications (e.g., from MS-GF+ via MassIVE RMSV000000091.3) to compute the fraction of incorrectly clustered spectra. The input identifications are not filtered at a controlled FDR (e.g., unfiltered PSMs), since the ~1% incorrectly-clustered operating points of the five tools are only comparable at the 1% FDR identification level. You need absolute clustering completeness or downstream identification sensitivity rather than cluster purity — this skill only labels spectra within clusters as correct/incorrect relative to the majority peptide. Clusters contain only unidentified spectra or singletons: the method explicitly ignores unidentified spectra and treats singletons as noise, so no purity signal can be computed for them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Maps peptide-spectrum match (PSM) identifications, filtered at 1% FDR, onto spectrum clustering results so that each cluster can be assigned a majority peptide label and member spectra with deviating labels can be counted as incorrectly clustered. This is the identification-mapping step underlying the cluster purity and cluster-size-distribution comparisons of falcon, MaRaCluster, MS-Cluster, msCRUSH, and spectra-cluster. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Maps peptide-spectrum match (PSM) identifications, filtered at 1% FDR, onto spectrum clustering results so that each cluster can be assigned a majority peptide label and member spectra with deviating labels can be counted as incorrectly clustered. This is the identification-mapping step underlying the cluster purity and cluster-size-distribution comparisons of falcon, MaRaCluster, MS-Cluster, msCRUSH, and spectra-cluster.

skills.search_text: pubchem-compound-database-processing Use when you need to measure or justify database pruning for MS1 candidate retrieval in PubChem, e.g. comparing ppm-scale mass tolerances (--delta_mz) against absolute Da windows before annotation. Input is already an annotated tandem MS spectrum or feature table — use the full ChemDistiller annotation pipeline (annotate.py) with scoring/SVM fingerprint scoring instead of raw mass-window counting. The instrument's MS1 accuracy is too low for ppm-scale tolerance (poor calibration), where a wide 1 Da window is the realistic operating point and the 'reduction' is not meaningful. You need formula-level or element-level candidate filtering beyond mass (chemdistiller.filters.formula / filters.element), which this mass-window skill does not perform. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Loads a PubChem compound monoisotopic-mass dump with NumPy and quantifies how much a high-accuracy 20 ppm m/z window (+/-0.008 Da at 400 Da) shrinks the candidate compound search space versus a 1 Da window, as used upstream of ChemDistiller's tandem-MS annotation engine. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: Loads a PubChem compound monoisotopic-mass dump with NumPy and quantifies how much a high-accuracy 20 ppm m/z window (+/-0.008 Da at 400 Da) shrinks the candidate compound search space versus a 1 Da window, as used upstream of ChemDistiller's tandem-MS annotation engine.

skills.description: Use when ranking unknowns from HR-MS/MS spectra requires candidate structures from a large open compound database: you have a precursor m/z (e.g. 199.0428) and need PubChem candidates for fragmentation-based scoring.
skills.name: pubchem-database-candidate-retrieval
skills.search_text: pubchem-database-candidate-retrieval Use when ranking unknowns from HR-MS/MS spectra requires candidate structures from a large open compound database: you have a precursor m/z (e.g. 199.0428) and need PubChem candidates for fragmentation-based scoring. The unknown is already covered by a small, specific database — the article stresses that smaller, specific databases (KEGG, HMDB, STOFF-IDENT, NORMAN suspects, MassBank) greatly improve the chance of ranking the correct answer highly, so prefer those over full PubChem when available. You need retention-time-aware ranking from the start — PubChem retrieval alone supplies structures; RT–logP weighting and user-defined scores must be added afterwards in MetFrag2.2. The input is a reference-spectrum library match (e.g. MassBank) rather than an unknown requiring de novo candidate retrieval. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Retrieves candidate structures from the PubChem compound database by precursor formula mass (e.g. ppm-mass windows around 199.04284) and optionally applies InChIKey first-block filtering to collapse stereoisomers, supplying a reduced SDF candidate set to downstream in silico fragmenters such as MetFrag2.2 and CFM-ID. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: Retrieves candidate structures from the PubChem compound database by precursor formula mass (e.g. ppm-mass windows around 199.04284) and optionally applies InChIKey first-block filtering to collapse stereoisomers, supplying a reduced SDF candidate set to downstream in silico fragmenters such as MetFrag2.2 and CFM-ID.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unknown is already covered by a small, specific database — the article stresses that smaller, specific databases (KEGG, HMDB, STOFF-IDENT, NORMAN suspects, MassBank) greatly improve the chance of ranking the correct answer highly, so prefer those over full PubChem when available. You need retention-time-aware ranking from the start — PubChem retrieval alone supplies structures; RT–logP weighting and user-defined scores must be added afterwards in MetFrag2.2. skills.search_text: pubchem-entrez-candidate-querying Use when building an annotation-candidate list for a target analyte of known exact mass — e.g. gathering PubChem structures for downstream CCS prediction and ΔCCS filtering. If the target compounds already have curated candidate lists or if only the true-annotation CCS prediction is needed (no competitor-structure enumeration) — skip the broad Entrez query. When the target compound has no exact PubChem match; in the article 9 such compounds were excluded, so a missing record means the query step will return nothing useful. When the analysis requires dimers ([2M+H]+, [2M-H]-), less common adducts, or in-source fragments — CCSP 2.0 training sets do not support these, so candidate enumeration for them is out of scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 http://edamontology.org/topic_3335 Query PubChem via the Entrez Global Query Cross-Database Search System (Biopython) to enumerate all candidate annotations whose exact mass falls within a specified ppm tolerance of a target compound's exact mass, producing the candidate lists that feed downstream CCS-based filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2022.08.09.503345
skills.summary: Query PubChem via the Entrez Global Query Cross-Database Search System (Biopython) to enumerate all candidate annotations whose exact mass falls within a specified ppm tolerance of a target compound's exact mass, producing the candidate lists that feed downstream CCS-based filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the target compounds already have curated candidate lists or if only the true-annotation CCS prediction is needed (no competitor-structure enumeration) — skip the broad Entrez query. skills.description: Use when you have a measured precursor molecular formula plus an observed LC retention time and need to enumerate and prune isomeric candidate structures to reduce metabolite-annotation ambiguity.
skills.name: pubchem-formula-based-candidate-retrieval
skills.search_text: pubchem-formula-based-candidate-retrieval Use when you have a measured precursor molecular formula plus an observed LC retention time and need to enumerate and prune isomeric candidate structures to reduce metabolite-annotation ambiguity. The unknown has no reliable observed retention time under the chromatographic method the RT model was trained/fine-tuned for — RT pruning is then uninformative. Formula-matched isomers are indistinguishable by RT-Transformer (near-identical predicted RTs), e.g. positional isomers with similar chromatographic behavior. You need structural ranking (MS/MS similarity) rather than chromatographic plausibility — this skill only eliminates formula-matched candidates by RT. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Retrieves all isomeric candidate structures from PubChem (PUG REST) by exact molecular formula for each unknown metabolite, then uses the RT-Transformer retention-time predictor to eliminate formula-matched candidates whose predicted RT is inconsistent with the observed chromatographic RT. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Retrieves all isomeric candidate structures from PubChem (PUG REST) by exact molecular formula for each unknown metabolite, then uses the RT-Transformer retention-time predictor to eliminate formula-matched candidates whose predicted RT is inconsistent with the observed chromatographic RT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unknown has no reliable observed retention time under the chromatographic method the RT model was trained/fine-tuned for — RT pruning is then uninformative. Formula-matched isomers are indistinguishable by RT-Transformer (near-identical predicted RTs), e.g. positional isomers with similar chromatographic behavior. You need structural ranking (MS/MS similarity) rather than chromatographic plausibility — this skill only eliminates formula-matched candidates by RT.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking candidate ranking on a fixed compound dataset against historical database snapshots, e.g. quantifying how PubChem growth (338 vs 2508 average candidates per compound) degrades MetFrag ranks.
skills.name: pubchem-snapshot-candidate-list-processing
skills.search_text: pubchem-snapshot-candidate-list-processing Use when reproducing or benchmarking candidate ranking on a fixed compound dataset against historical database snapshots, e.g. quantifying how PubChem growth (338 vs 2508 average candidates per compound) degrades MetFrag ranks. When the goal is MetFrag2.2 evaluation with reference-count or retention-time (RT–log P) scoring — the 2006-vs-2009 snapshot comparison must use fragment-explanation scoring only to isolate the database-size effect When candidate lists are drawn from a current database download or ChemSpider/KEGG rather than the fixed historical PubChem snapshots — ranks are then not comparable to the published benchmarks When the dataset is not a fixed compound list (e.g. EA, UF, EQEx datasets) without per-snapshot candidate files, since the comparison depends on identical spectra against differing candidate pools http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Prepares and compares versioned PubChem candidate-structure snapshots (e.g. Feb. 2006 vs 2009) for a fixed compound set, so that database-growth effects on in silico fragmentation ranking (MetFrag2010) can be quantified per snapshot. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: Prepares and compares versioned PubChem candidate-structure snapshots (e.g. Feb. 2006 vs 2009) for a fixed compound set, so that database-growth effects on in silico fragmentation ranking (MetFrag2010) can be quantified per snapshot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is MetFrag2.2 evaluation with reference-count or retention-time (RT–log P) scoring — the 2006-vs-2009 snapshot comparison must use fragment-explanation scoring only to isolate the database-size effect When candidate lists are drawn from a current database download or ChemSpider/KEGG rather than the fixed historical PubChem snapshots — ranks are then not comparable to the published benchmarks When the dataset is not a fixed compound list (e.g. EA, UF, EQEx datasets) without per-snapshot candidate files, since the comparison depends on identical spectra against differing candidate pools

skills.search_text: pubchem-structure-lookup-validation Use when library spectra carry only a compound name (no SMILES), or when validating existing SMILES/InChI/InChIKey annotations against each other in a mass spectral library cleaning pipeline. The spectrum already has a complete, validated SMILES, InChI, and InChIKey that were all derived from the same original structure — the lookup adds nothing and could overwrite a good annotation The compound name is missing, empty, or so generic (e.g. a trivial abbreviation) that a unique PubChem hit cannot be expected; then the filter would yield no candidate or a wrong one You need to check whether measured fragments actually match the annotation — the article notes such plausibility checks over both metadata and fragments are not yet implemented in matchms http://edamontology.org/topic_3418 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Derives canonical SMILES, InChI, and InChIKey from PubChem using the compound name in spectrum metadata, accepting a candidate only when its PubChem mass matches the spectrum's parent mass, then validates the recovered structures by loading them with RDKit and cross-comparing the three identifier forms. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: Derives canonical SMILES, InChI, and InChIKey from PubChem using the compound name in spectrum metadata, accepting a candidate only when its PubChem mass matches the spectrum's parent mass, then validates the recovered structures by loading them with RDKit and cross-comparing the three identifier forms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum already has a complete, validated SMILES, InChI, and InChIKey that were all derived from the same original structure — the lookup adds nothing and could overwrite a good annotation The compound name is missing, empty, or so generic (e.g. a trivial abbreviation) that a unique PubChem hit cannot be expected; then the filter would yield no candidate or a wrong one You need to check whether measured fragments actually match the annotation — the article notes such plausibility checks over both metadata and fragments are not yet implemented in matchms

skills.search_text: pubchem-title-name-matching Use when a merged metabolomics dataset (e.g., 391 urinary asthma metabolites) has been assembled via InChIKeys and you must quantify name consistency against PubChem title names or estimate name-only merge failures. The goal is to perform the merge itself via InChIKeys (MMS Step 1) rather than audit name consistency of an already-merged dataset The dataset has no PubChem title names or no retrieved name attributes from MMS Step 2, so exact string comparison against a reference name is impossible You need fuzzy/synonym-aware matching; this audit intentionally uses exact string matching so synonyms fall into the different-name group http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A post-merge name-consistency audit that labels each metabolite in a merged dataset as carrying its PubChem 'title' name or a different (synonym/acronym) name, and quantifies how many compounds would have gone unmerged without the Metabolites Merging Strategy (MMS). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13121167
skills.summary: A post-merge name-consistency audit that labels each metabolite in a merged dataset as carrying its PubChem 'title' name or a different (synonym/acronym) name, and quantifies how many compounds would have gone unmerged without the Metabolites Merging Strategy (MMS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to perform the merge itself via InChIKeys (MMS Step 1) rather than audit name consistency of an already-merged dataset The dataset has no PubChem title names or no retrieved name attributes from MMS Step 2, so exact string comparison against a reference name is impossible You need fuzzy/synonym-aware matching; this audit intentionally uses exact string matching so synonyms fall into the different-name group

skills.description: Use when a question asks how many PoDP projects match a List-tab keyword query (e.g., 'Streptomyces | Salinispora' → 18 projects) and you must retrieve the archived Zenodo JSON snapshot and filter it locally.
skills.name: public-data-deposit-retrieval
skills.search_text: public-data-deposit-retrieval Use when a question asks how many PoDP projects match a List-tab keyword query (e.g., 'Streptomyces | Salinispora' → 18 projects) and you must retrieve the archived Zenodo JSON snapshot and filter it locally. You need the actual raw metabolomics or genomics data files — the PoDP does not store datasets, it only captures metadata linking to public repositories (MassIVE, MetaboLights, NCBI GenBank) You need reproducible ontology-based metadata selection across arbitrary fields with guaranteed machine-readable semantics — free text entered in 'Other' boxes is inherently not machine-readable You expect the current live count to equal a historical figure — keyword counts (e.g., 'currently 18') change as the Zenodo archive is re-uploaded monthly Retrieves the community-curated Paired Omics Data Platform (PoDP) project archive from its regularly published Zenodo dataset (JSON format) and applies the platform's List-tab keyword search semantics (e.g., 'Streptomyces | Salinispora') offline to reproduce project counts and retrieve matching project records. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00724-z
skills.summary: Retrieves the community-curated Paired Omics Data Platform (PoDP) project archive from its regularly published Zenodo dataset (JSON format) and applies the platform's List-tab keyword search semantics (e.g., 'Streptomyces | Salinispora') offline to reproduce project counts and retrieve matching project records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the actual raw metabolomics or genomics data files — the PoDP does not store datasets, it only captures metadata linking to public repositories (MassIVE, MetaboLights, NCBI GenBank) You need reproducible ontology-based metadata selection across arbitrary fields with guaranteed machine-readable semantics — free text entered in 'Other' boxes is inherently not machine-readable You expect the current live count to equal a historical figure — keyword counts (e.g., 'currently 18') change as the Zenodo archive is re-uploaded monthly

skills.description: Use when curating propagated drug-analog MS/MS matches and needing to remove signals whose detection is too widespread across public metabolomics data to plausibly reflect real drug exposure.
skills.name: public-dataset-overdetection-screening
skills.search_text: public-dataset-overdetection-screening Use when curating propagated drug-analog MS/MS matches and needing to remove signals whose detection is too widespread across public metabolomics data to plausibly reflect real drug exposure. The analog spectrum already receives a full library match in the GNPS library — these are direct spectral hits, not propagated analogs, and are removed by the library-match filter before dataset testing. The parent drug carries an endogenous or dietary-source exposure annotation — such analogs are excluded by the source filter regardless of detection prevalence. The analog's mass offset is not among the 156 curated, chemically explained mass offsets — dataset testing cannot rescue chemically unexplained offsets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 The fourth curation filter of the GNPS Drug Library propagated-analog workflow: analog spectra surviving the endogenous/food-source, mass-offset, and library-match filters are searched against 20 public test metabolomics datasets, and analogs detected too ubiquitously to indicate true drug exposure are excluded before propagating the final library. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-65993-5
skills.summary: The fourth curation filter of the GNPS Drug Library propagated-analog workflow: analog spectra surviving the endogenous/food-source, mass-offset, and library-match filters are searched against 20 public test metabolomics datasets, and analogs detected too ubiquitously to indicate true drug exposure are excluded before propagating the final library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analog spectrum already receives a full library match in the GNPS library — these are direct spectral hits, not propagated analogs, and are removed by the library-match filter before dataset testing. The parent drug carries an endogenous or dietary-source exposure annotation — such analogs are excluded by the source filter regardless of detection prevalence. The analog's mass offset is not among the 156 curated, chemically explained mass offsets — dataset testing cannot rescue chemically unexplained offsets.

skills.description: Use when you have an MS/MS feature from an animal model (e.g. phenylacetyl-carnitine at m/z 280.153) and want to find which public human/mouse/rat datasets detect it, across which tissues and disease states.
skills.name: public-metabolomics-repository-querying
skills.search_text: public-metabolomics-repository-querying Use when you have an MS/MS feature from an animal model (e.g. phenylacetyl-carnitine at m/z 280.153) and want to find which public human/mouse/rat datasets detect it, across which tissues and disease states. Input is already a feature-abundance table or you only need a spectral library annotation — this skill returns tissue/disease provenance, not identifications, and annotations from spectral matching are only Level 2/3 (MSI), not fully validated structures. Absence of a query in reference datasets is used to conclude the feature is not present in a tissue — detection across reference datasets is confounded by study-specific extraction methods, workflows and instrumentation. The task is de novo annotation of unknowns with no public reference spectra available, or you need quantitative abundance estimates from the repositories rather than presence/absence provenance. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Search query MS/MS spectra against reference libraries assembled from public metabolomics repositories (GNPS/MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench) using tissueMASST-style cosine-similarity matching, to map animal-model features onto human tissues and disease cohorts. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Search query MS/MS spectra against reference libraries assembled from public metabolomics repositories (GNPS/MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench) using tissueMASST-style cosine-similarity matching, to map animal-model features onto human tissues and disease cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature-abundance table or you only need a spectral library annotation — this skill returns tissue/disease provenance, not identifications, and annotations from spectral matching are only Level 2/3 (MSI), not fully validated structures. Absence of a query in reference datasets is used to conclude the feature is not present in a tissue — detection across reference datasets is confounded by study-specific extraction methods, workflows and instrumentation. The task is de novo annotation of unknowns with no public reference spectra available, or you need quantitative abundance estimates from the repositories rather than presence/absence provenance.
