skills.description: Use when a repository-scale chemical annotation table over public tandem MS files is needed, i.e., when a downstream analysis requires a compound-by-file binary matrix rather than running new GNPS library search jobs.
skills.name: public-repository-data-harvesting-massive
skills.search_text: public-repository-data-harvesting-massive Use when a repository-scale chemical annotation table over public tandem MS files is needed, i.e., when a downstream analysis requires a compound-by-file binary matrix rather than running new GNPS library search jobs. When the goal is novel chemical annotation of a private dataset not yet deposited in MassIVE — run your own GNPS spectral library search instead of harvesting ReDU's pre-computed results When a finer-grained quantity is needed than binary detection (e.g., precursor intensities or cosine scores) — the ReDU matrix only encodes annotated/not-annotated per compound per file When molecular networking co-analysis is intended — that is a separate ReDU/GNPS analysis with its own 3000-file recommended limit, not the library-search harvest http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Harvests ReDU's pre-computed GNPS spectral library search annotations for all public MassIVE files and encodes them as a binary chemical-annotation-by-file matrix (1 = detected, 0 = not detected), preserving multiple GNPS annotations per chemical. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-020-0916-7
skills.summary: Harvests ReDU's pre-computed GNPS spectral library search annotations for all public MassIVE files and encodes them as a binary chemical-annotation-by-file matrix (1 = detected, 0 = not detected), preserving multiple GNPS annotations per chemical.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is novel chemical annotation of a private dataset not yet deposited in MassIVE — run your own GNPS spectral library search instead of harvesting ReDU's pre-computed results When a finer-grained quantity is needed than binary detection (e.g., precursor intensities or cosine scores) — the ReDU matrix only encodes annotated/not-annotated per compound per file When molecular networking co-analysis is intended — that is a separate ReDU/GNPS analysis with its own 3000-file recommended limit, not the library-search harvest

skills.description: Use when a figure produced by a GraphBio module (heatmap, volcano, MA, ROC, chord, network, etc.) needs to be saved in a downloadable image format with publication-appropriate dimensions and resolution rather than only viewed on screen.
skills.name: publication-ready-figure-export
skills.search_text: publication-ready-figure-export Use when a figure produced by a GraphBio module (heatmap, volcano, MA, ROC, chord, network, etc.) needs to be saved in a downloadable image format with publication-appropriate dimensions and resolution rather than only viewed on screen. skills.description: Use when an XCMS feature table has biologically equivalent unlabeled vs stable-isotope-labeled LC/MS sample classes (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and you must flag features that are new or higher-intensity in labeled samples.
skills.name: putative-incorporation-feature-detection
skills.search_text: putative-incorporation-feature-detection Use when an XCMS feature table has biologically equivalent unlabeled vs stable-isotope-labeled LC/MS sample classes (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and you must flag features that are new or higher-intensity in labeled samples. Input is raw mzXML/NetCDF not yet processed by XCMS — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure, so peak picking, alignment and grouping must happen first. There are no biologically equivalent unlabeled/labeled sample pairs to contrast; geoRge compares paired isotopic distributions rather than iterating over all MS signals using theoretical mass differences. Expected labeled features fall below the intensity gates (PuInc.int.lim=4000, Basepeak.minInt=2000) or the basepeak match exceeds the 6.5 ppm tolerance, so the incorporation signal cannot be detected. http://edamontology.org/topic_3344 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 geoRge-based detection of putative stable-isotope (13C) incorporation in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics: PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder compare isotopic distributions between biologically equivalent unlabeled and labeled samples on an XCMS feature table to flag features with new or higher-intensity m/z peaks in the labeled condition. On MTBLS213 (ARPE-19 cells grown on normal vs high glucose), this enumerates the features whose isotopic distribution shifts per glucose condition. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: geoRge-based detection of putative stable-isotope (13C) incorporation in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics: PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder compare isotopic distributions between biologically equivalent unlabeled and labeled samples on an XCMS feature table to flag features with new or higher-intensity m/z peaks in the labeled condition. On MTBLS213 (ARPE-19 cells grown on normal vs high glucose), this enumerates the features whose isotopic distribution shifts per glucose condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzXML/NetCDF not yet processed by XCMS — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure, so peak picking, alignment and grouping must happen first. Expected labeled features fall below the intensity gates (PuInc.int.lim=4000, Basepeak.minInt=2000) or the basepeak match exceeds the 6.5 ppm tolerance, so the incorporation signal cannot be detected.

skills.search_text: putative-label-flagging-statistics Use when you have paired unlabeled/labeled replicate sample classes (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) in an XCMS xcmsSet and need to identify which features show isotopic enrichment before basepeak assignment or database querying. The spectral data is real experimental NMR rather than MetAssimulo-simulated spectra — the modules are built around the paper's simulated spectral data structures and its HMDB 5.0 parameter tables, not raw instrument output. skills.description: Use when a large-scale tabular omics matrix (e.g., 168-dim NMR metabolomics per participant) must be pre-trained into a foundation model via masked-feature reconstruction before downstream fine-tuning.
skills.name: pytorch-transformer-model-training
skills.search_text: pytorch-transformer-model-training Use when a large-scale tabular omics matrix (e.g., 168-dim NMR metabolomics per participant) must be pre-trained into a foundation model via masked-feature reconstruction before downstream fine-tuning. The input already contains disease labels and the goal is supervised prediction — use fine-tuning (e.g., the repo's train-binary CLI for current/future disease prediction) instead of masked pre-training. The metabolite panel differs from the 168 NMR biomarkers the pre-trained model expects (the companion repo lists expected columns in assets/pretrained/metabolite_columns.txt); retraining from scratch would be needed. Only a handful of samples are available — transformer pre-training on 83,744 individuals relies on large-scale population data to capture normative metabolite patterns. http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Train a BERT-style transformer encoder in PyTorch on tabular biomarker data using masked-feature reconstruction: here, Hadamard-product embedding of 168 NMR metabolite biomarkers from 83,744 UK Biobank individuals with a [CLS] token and 10% random metabolite masking, optimized with AdamW for 200 epochs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66163-3
skills.summary: Train a BERT-style transformer encoder in PyTorch on tabular biomarker data using masked-feature reconstruction: here, Hadamard-product embedding of 168 NMR metabolite biomarkers from 83,744 UK Biobank individuals with a [CLS] token and 10% random metabolite masking, optimized with AdamW for 200 epochs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input already contains disease labels and the goal is supervised prediction — use fine-tuning (e.g., the repo's train-binary CLI for current/future disease prediction) instead of masked pre-training. The metabolite panel differs from the 168 NMR biomarkers the pre-trained model expects (the companion repo lists expected columns in assets/pretrained/metabolite_columns.txt); retraining from scratch would be needed. Only a handful of samples are available — transformer pre-training on 83,744 individuals relies on large-scale population data to capture normative metabolite patterns.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics intensity matrix (compounds × runs) spans multiple acquisition batches, QC samples are interspersed in the run order, and signal drift/batch effects must be removed before differential abundance testing.
skills.name: qc-based-batch-correction
skills.search_text: qc-based-batch-correction Use when a metabolomics intensity matrix (compounds × runs) spans multiple acquisition batches, QC samples are interspersed in the run order, and signal drift/batch effects must be removed before differential abundance testing. The matrix contains no interspersed QC samples — QC-RLSC/QC-RSC are unusable and the QC-vs-biological fit checks cannot run Multivariate (cross-metabolite) outlier detection is required — the article notes treatment is currently feature-level, and multivariate methods like SERFF and TIGER were not benchmarked within Metanorm Data are already normalized or the goal is only statistical inference — applying batch correction would alter p-values without addressing a drift problem (note multiple testing correction was explicitly out of scope here) Batchwise metabolomics normalization that fits intensity-vs-run-order curves (QC-based signal-drift correction) per compound, implemented in the Metanorm R package as QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, and the outlier-robust variants rLOESS, rGAM, and tGAM. The skill exists because QC-sample outliers deteriorate classical correction and inflate/deflate downstream differential abundance calls. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06841
skills.summary: Batchwise metabolomics normalization that fits intensity-vs-run-order curves (QC-based signal-drift correction) per compound, implemented in the Metanorm R package as QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, and the outlier-robust variants rLOESS, rGAM, and tGAM. The skill exists because QC-sample outliers deteriorate classical correction and inflate/deflate downstream differential abundance calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix contains no interspersed QC samples — QC-RLSC/QC-RSC are unusable and the QC-vs-biological fit checks cannot run Multivariate (cross-metabolite) outlier detection is required — the article notes treatment is currently feature-level, and multivariate methods like SERFF and TIGER were not benchmarked within Metanorm Data are already normalized or the goal is only statistical inference — applying batch correction would alter p-values without addressing a drift problem (note multiple testing correction was explicitly out of scope here)

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature matrix includes pooled QC samples injected across batches and you must correct across-batch signal drift while identifying features (e.g. xanthosine 5'-monophosphate) absent from QCs.
skills.name: qc-based-lowess-drift-correction
skills.search_text: qc-based-lowess-drift-correction Use when a metabolomics feature matrix includes pooled QC samples injected across batches and you must correct across-batch signal drift while identifying features (e.g. xanthosine 5'-monophosphate) absent from QCs. A feature is undetected (zero/NA) in all pooled-QC injections — it cannot be drift-corrected by a QC-based model and must be excluded a priori; use statistical models such as ber or ComBat implemented in dbnorm instead The dataset lacks periodically injected QC samples — QC-based lowess requires repeated QC measurements to model the drift The goal is comparing multiple correction models rather than applying the QC-based lowess method — dbnorm's dbnormSCORE/Visodbnorm functions are designed for model comparison and selection http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Applies QC sample-based lowess drift correction to log2-transformed untargeted metabolomics feature matrices with pooled-tissue surrogate QCs, and compiles the a-priori excluded-feature list of metabolites that are undetected (zero/NA) in all QC injections and therefore cannot be drift-corrected by a QC-based model. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Applies QC sample-based lowess drift correction to log2-transformed untargeted metabolomics feature matrices with pooled-tissue surrogate QCs, and compiles the a-priori excluded-feature list of metabolites that are undetected (zero/NA) in all QC injections and therefore cannot be drift-corrected by a QC-based model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A feature is undetected (zero/NA) in all pooled-QC injections — it cannot be drift-corrected by a QC-based model and must be excluded a priori; use statistical models such as ber or ComBat implemented in dbnorm instead The dataset lacks periodically injected QC samples — QC-based lowess requires repeated QC measurements to model the drift The goal is comparing multiple correction models rather than applying the QC-based lowess method — dbnorm's dbnormSCORE/Visodbnorm functions are designed for model comparison and selection

skills.description: Use when selecting among QC-based drift-normalization methods (QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) and outlier robustness must be quantified on simulated data with known ground-truth drift.
skills.name: qc-based-normalization-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: qc-based-normalization-method-benchmarking Use when selecting among QC-based drift-normalization methods (QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) and outlier robustness must be quantified on simulated data with known ground-truth drift. Benchmark quality would be judged by reduction of the QC relative standard deviation (RSD) or by an increased number of differentially abundant metabolites — the article names both as benchmarking pitfalls rather than valid benchmarks. You only have real experimental data without a known drift ground truth — the median squared prediction error requires in-silico data where ground truth is known; experimental datasets need the separate data-driven evaluation approach. The simulation would be generated from a fitted model of one of the benchmarked methods — this breaks the neutrality the article demands and can favor that method. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark QC-based LC-MS metabolomics normalization methods (QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) on in-silico data with known sine-based drift and injected outliers, scoring each method by median squared prediction error over 200 simulated runs to quantify outlier robustness. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Benchmark QC-based LC-MS metabolomics normalization methods (QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) on in-silico data with known sine-based drift and injected outliers, scoring each method by median squared prediction error over 200 simulated runs to quantify outlier robustness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmark quality would be judged by reduction of the QC relative standard deviation (RSD) or by an increased number of differentially abundant metabolites — the article names both as benchmarking pitfalls rather than valid benchmarks. You only have real experimental data without a known drift ground truth — the median squared prediction error requires in-silico data where ground truth is known; experimental datasets need the separate data-driven evaluation approach. The simulation would be generated from a fitted model of one of the benchmarked methods — this breaks the neutrality the article demands and can favor that method.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics peak-intensity matrix has repeatedly injected pooled QCSs interspersed with subject samples and intensities drift with injection order or batch, and a batch label is available.
skills.name: qc-based-signal-correction
skills.search_text: qc-based-signal-correction Use when a metabolomics peak-intensity matrix has repeatedly injected pooled QCSs interspersed with subject samples and intensities drift with injection order or batch, and a batch label is available. There is only one batch of data or the batch label is unknown — the article shows QC-RLSC and QC-SVRC failed to increase QCS similarity on single-batch data while WaveICA 2.0 (injection-order-only) succeeded. No repeatedly injected pooled QCSs are present in the run — these regression correctors require QCSs to fit the drift curves/models. The input is already batch-corrected or you need within-batch drift removal without batch information, where the article's own comparisons favor WaveICA 2.0. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Corrects intensity drift and run-order/batch effects in untargeted metabolomics peak tables by fitting regression models to repeated quality control samples (QCSs) and applying the fitted curves/models to subject samples. This card covers the loess-style QC-RLSC and SVM-based QC-SVRC variants benchmarked against WaveICA 2.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01839-7
skills.summary: Corrects intensity drift and run-order/batch effects in untargeted metabolomics peak tables by fitting regression models to repeated quality control samples (QCSs) and applying the fitted curves/models to subject samples. This card covers the loess-style QC-RLSC and SVM-based QC-SVRC variants benchmarked against WaveICA 2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is only one batch of data or the batch label is unknown — the article shows QC-RLSC and QC-SVRC failed to increase QCS similarity on single-batch data while WaveICA 2.0 (injection-order-only) succeeded. No repeatedly injected pooled QCSs are present in the run — these regression correctors require QCSs to fit the drift curves/models. The input is already batch-corrected or you need within-batch drift removal without batch information, where the article's own comparisons favor WaveICA 2.0.

skills.description: Use when a large-scale metabolomics or proteomics intensity matrix contains pooled QC samples injected repeatedly across the run and cumulative RSD plots show signal drift or batch effects that must be removed at the feature level before statistical analysis.
skills.name: qc-based-signal-drift-correction
skills.search_text: qc-based-signal-drift-correction Use when a large-scale metabolomics or proteomics intensity matrix contains pooled QC samples injected repeatedly across the run and cumulative RSD plots show signal drift or batch effects that must be removed at the feature level before statistical analysis. Dataset contains no pooled QC injections across the run — use statTarget's shiftCor_dQC with Combat instead. Data have not yet been peak-picked (still raw instrument files); conversion and peak extraction must happen first via transX/XCMS/Skyline. Only single-batch data with no observable inter-batch variation — the batch-integration output of shiftCor is unnecessary overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Removes inter- and intra-batch signal drift at the feature level in LC-MS/GC-MS metabolomics and label-free proteomics by fitting a QC-based random forest signal correction (QC-RFSC) to pooled QC injections and dividing each feature by its per-sample correction factor, as implemented in the statTarget shiftCor function. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Removes inter- and intra-batch signal drift at the feature level in LC-MS/GC-MS metabolomics and label-free proteomics by fitting a QC-based random forest signal correction (QC-RFSC) to pooled QC injections and dividing each feature by its per-sample correction factor, as implemented in the statTarget shiftCor function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset contains no pooled QC injections across the run — use statTarget's shiftCor_dQC with Combat instead. Data have not yet been peak-picked (still raw instrument files); conversion and peak extraction must happen first via transX/XCMS/Skyline. Only single-batch data with no observable inter-batch variation — the batch-integration output of shiftCor is unnecessary overhead.

skills.description: Use when unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics data (compound x sample intensity matrix) show signal drift, batch effects, or outliers that degrade replicate concordance and downstream differential-abundance power.
skills.name: qc-based-signal-drift-normalization
skills.search_text: qc-based-signal-drift-normalization Use when unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics data (compound x sample intensity matrix) show signal drift, batch effects, or outliers that degrade replicate concordance and downstream differential-abundance power. QC samples are not representative of the biological samples (QCcheck fails) — QC-based drift correction will be invalid You need to remove outliers manually first — the article notes automated outlier detection is non-trivial and manual identification is subjective and labor-intensive for large feature counts Downstream multiple-testing-corrected inference is the goal itself — normalization is a prerequisite, not a substitute http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Normalizes LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices against signal drift and batch effects using QC-sample-based models (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC) implemented in the Metanorm R package, with tGAM as the recommended default because of its outlier robustness. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.09.30.679445
skills.summary: Normalizes LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices against signal drift and batch effects using QC-sample-based models (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC) implemented in the Metanorm R package, with tGAM as the recommended default because of its outlier robustness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: QC samples are not representative of the biological samples (QCcheck fails) — QC-based drift correction will be invalid You need to remove outliers manually first — the article notes automated outlier detection is non-trivial and manual identification is subjective and labor-intensive for large feature counts Downstream multiple-testing-corrected inference is the goal itself — normalization is a prerequisite, not a substitute

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table (e.g. exported from patRoon or MS-DIAL) contains blank, pooled QC, and diluted-QC (QC_half) sample groups and low-quality features must be removed before statistical analysis.
skills.name: qc-coefficient-of-variation-thresholding
skills.search_text: qc-coefficient-of-variation-thresholding Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table (e.g. exported from patRoon or MS-DIAL) contains blank, pooled QC, and diluted-QC (QC_half) sample groups and low-quality features must be removed before statistical analysis. The study is targeted with calibration-curve-based quantification, which GetFeatistics handles through a different quantification pathway rather than pooled-QC feature filtering. The feature table does not contain blank, pooled QC, or diluted-QC (QC_half) sample groups, so the four QC criteria cannot be computed. Features have already been filtered by pooled QC criteria upstream and only downstream steps (intensity pre-processing, regression modelling) remain. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Filter untargeted metabolomics features using pooled quality control criteria as implemented in the GetFeatistics R-package's QCs_process function: QC reproducibility (CV%), QC detection frequency, blank contribution, and diluted-QC response, with an optional per-sample-group separated pooled-QC variant. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Filter untargeted metabolomics features using pooled quality control criteria as implemented in the GetFeatistics R-package's QCs_process function: QC reproducibility (CV%), QC detection frequency, blank contribution, and diluted-QC response, with an optional per-sample-group separated pooled-QC variant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study is targeted with calibration-curve-based quantification, which GetFeatistics handles through a different quantification pathway rather than pooled-QC feature filtering. The feature table does not contain blank, pooled QC, or diluted-QC (QC_half) sample groups, so the four QC criteria cannot be computed. Features have already been filtered by pooled QC criteria upstream and only downstream steps (intensity pre-processing, regression modelling) remain.

skills.description: Use when LC-IM-MS derived CCS values for known benchmark/QC compounds (e.g., Quad LCMS QC mixture) need to be validated against external reference databases such as the CCS Compendium.
skills.name: qc-compound-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: qc-compound-annotation-matching Use when LC-IM-MS derived CCS values for known benchmark/QC compounds (e.g., Quad LCMS QC mixture) need to be validated against external reference databases such as the CCS Compendium. The compounds of interest are not part of an external reference database (e.g., no CCS Compendium entries exist), so no bias benchmarking is possible CCS values come from a different IM-MS technique (e.g., TWIM-MS rather than drift tube IM-MS with nitrogen drift gas), making direct DTCCS N2 comparison against Compendium values inappropriate Input is raw mzML profile data requiring CCSfind processing itself rather than already-determined CCS values ready for benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks experimentally determined drift-tube CCS values (DTCCS N2) from CCSfind against published CCS Compendium reference entries for the same small-molecule QC compounds, computing per-compound and mean absolute percent bias to validate standardized DTIM-MS calibration. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040
skills.summary: Benchmarks experimentally determined drift-tube CCS values (DTCCS N2) from CCSfind against published CCS Compendium reference entries for the same small-molecule QC compounds, computing per-compound and mean absolute percent bias to validate standardized DTIM-MS calibration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compounds of interest are not part of an external reference database (e.g., no CCS Compendium entries exist), so no bias benchmarking is possible CCS values come from a different IM-MS technique (e.g., TWIM-MS rather than drift tube IM-MS with nitrogen drift gas), making direct DTCCS N2 comparison against Compendium values inappropriate Input is raw mzML profile data requiring CCSfind processing itself rather than already-determined CCS values ready for benchmarking

skills.description: Use when untargeted MS-based metabolomics mzML files (including pooled QC injections) must be monitored for a defined compound list — e.g. tracking the MetNexs long-term QC pool to compute m/z/RT deviation timelines and flag deviations > 20 ppm.
skills.name: qc-compound-peak-detection
skills.search_text: qc-compound-peak-detection Use when untargeted MS-based metabolomics mzML files (including pooled QC injections) must be monitored for a defined compound list — e.g. tracking the MetNexs long-term QC pool to compute m/z/RT deviation timelines and flag deviations > 20 ppm. You need drift correction or intensity-drift modeling rather than compound tracking — QC-MXP-style postanalysis corrections are a different module The input is a processed peak/feature table rather than vendor-raw or mzML files obtained directly from the instrument Your goal is contaminant screening across ~800 known ions — use module_Contaminants instead of a bespoke target list http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Detects and extracts chromatographic peaks for user-specified target compounds (m/z + RT pairs) from mzML injections, producing per-injection diagnostics (observed m/z, RT, intensity, peak shape) used to track instrument quality over time in QC4Metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: Detects and extracts chromatographic peaks for user-specified target compounds (m/z + RT pairs) from mzML injections, producing per-injection diagnostics (observed m/z, RT, intensity, peak shape) used to track instrument quality over time in QC4Metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need drift correction or intensity-drift modeling rather than compound tracking — QC-MXP-style postanalysis corrections are a different module The input is a processed peak/feature table rather than vendor-raw or mzML files obtained directly from the instrument Your goal is contaminant screening across ~800 known ions — use module_Contaminants instead of a bespoke target list

skills.description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS specimen files from a monitored analysis need their internal standard RT, intensity, and Δm/z values tabulated in acquisition order to expose gradual drift.
skills.name: qc-dashboard-metric-tabulation
skills.search_text: qc-dashboard-metric-tabulation Use when raw LC-MS/MS specimen files from a monitored analysis need their internal standard RT, intensity, and Δm/z values tabulated in acquisition order to expose gradual drift. Data is already a processed feature table or QC report — this skill is for deriving IS QC metrics from raw acquisition files, not re-summarizing existing results Acquisition uses Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, or Waters sequences — Rapid QC-MS has only been tested extensively on Thermo acquisition sequences and Thermo RAW files, so IS tabulation for those vendors may fail The goal is acute failure alerting rather than gradual drift analysis — use Rapid QC-MS's messaging-app alerts instead of the tabulation workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Tabulate per-specimen internal standard retention time, intensity, and Δm/z values in acquisition order from Rapid QC-MS processing, so that gradual drifts in instrument sensitivity, in-run retention time shifts, and mass accuracy become visible in the interactive dashboard. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Tabulate per-specimen internal standard retention time, intensity, and Δm/z values in acquisition order from Rapid QC-MS processing, so that gradual drifts in instrument sensitivity, in-run retention time shifts, and mass accuracy become visible in the interactive dashboard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already a processed feature table or QC report — this skill is for deriving IS QC metrics from raw acquisition files, not re-summarizing existing results Acquisition uses Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, or Waters sequences — Rapid QC-MS has only been tested extensively on Thermo acquisition sequences and Thermo RAW files, so IS tabulation for those vendors may fail The goal is acute failure alerting rather than gradual drift analysis — use Rapid QC-MS's messaging-app alerts instead of the tabulation workflow

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS peak table (e.g. MS-DIAL Excel export) must be quality-filtered before statistics, and pooled QC samples are available to compute detection rates and Broadhurst RSD/D-ratio metrics.
skills.name: qc-detection-rate-filtering
skills.search_text: qc-detection-rate-filtering Use when a preprocessed LC-MS peak table (e.g. MS-DIAL Excel export) must be quality-filtered before statistics, and pooled QC samples are available to compute detection rates and Broadhurst RSD/D-ratio metrics. The input is raw LC-MS data that has not yet been peak-picked into a feature table (notame expects preprocessed LC-MS data). The dataset has no pooled QC samples, so QC detection rate and QC-based RSD/D-ratio cannot be computed. The goal is hard removal of features rather than flagging — notame's design flags low-quality features because they may aid metabolite identification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Flags low-quality molecular features in a MetaboSet (notame) based on QC-sample detection rate and Broadhurst quality metrics (RSD, D-ratio), so only reproducible features proceed to downstream analysis while flagged features are retained for metabolite identification. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135
skills.summary: Flags low-quality molecular features in a MetaboSet (notame) based on QC-sample detection rate and Broadhurst quality metrics (RSD, D-ratio), so only reproducible features proceed to downstream analysis while flagged features are retained for metabolite identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-MS data that has not yet been peak-picked into a feature table (notame expects preprocessed LC-MS data). The dataset has no pooled QC samples, so QC detection rate and QC-based RSD/D-ratio cannot be computed. The goal is hard removal of features rather than flagging — notame's design flags low-quality features because they may aid metabolite identification.

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table contains pooled QC and diluted-QC (QC_half) injections and features must be removed whose dilution behaviour does not follow the expected fold-change, or when pooled-QC-based filtering more broadly is needed.
skills.name: qc-dilution-response-checking
skills.search_text: qc-dilution-response-checking Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table contains pooled QC and diluted-QC (QC_half) injections and features must be removed whose dilution behaviour does not follow the expected fold-change, or when pooled-QC-based filtering more broadly is needed. Targeted analyses, where GetFeatistics instead supports calibration curve-based quantification with different data weighting options Feature tables lacking diluted-QC (QC_half) injections, since the dilution-response criterion requires a QC vs QC_half intensity comparison Raw MS data files that still require feature extraction (e.g. with XCMS) before QC cut-off filtering can be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Filters untargeted metabolomics features by checking dilution response in pooled quality-control samples — the QC vs diluted-QC (QC_half) mean-intensity ratio criterion (step IIII of GetFeatistics' four-step QCs_process) — alongside the companion QC criteria (CV% reproducibility, QC detection frequency, blank/QC ratio). metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Filters untargeted metabolomics features by checking dilution response in pooled quality-control samples — the QC vs diluted-QC (QC_half) mean-intensity ratio criterion (step IIII of GetFeatistics' four-step QCs_process) — alongside the companion QC criteria (CV% reproducibility, QC detection frequency, blank/QC ratio).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targeted analyses, where GetFeatistics instead supports calibration curve-based quantification with different data weighting options Feature tables lacking diluted-QC (QC_half) injections, since the dilution-response criterion requires a QC vs QC_half intensity comparison Raw MS data files that still require feature extraction (e.g. with XCMS) before QC cut-off filtering can be applied

skills.description: Use when you have a QC-labeled LC-MS feature table (e.g. statTarget input from XCMS/Skyline peak abundances) and need to quantify precision by computing RSD% per feature across QC injections and plotting cumulative RSD distributions.
skills.name: qc-feature-rsd-computation
skills.search_text: qc-feature-rsd-computation Use when you have a QC-labeled LC-MS feature table (e.g. statTarget input from XCMS/Skyline peak abundances) and need to quantify precision by computing RSD% per feature across QC injections and plotting cumulative RSD distributions. Datasets without repeated pooled QC injections interleaved with real samples (e.g. QC-free designs); use Combat via shiftCor_dQC instead, since no QC RSDs can be computed Peak tables not yet formatted to statTarget input layout (XCMS/MZmine/SIEVE/Skyline output must first be converted with the transX function) When the goal is drift correction itself rather than precision assessment — RSD computation only evaluates correction quality, it does not correct signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Computes the relative standard deviation (RSD/CV%) of every feature across pooled QC injections in LC-MS metabolomics peak tables, then bins features into cumulative RSD intervals to quantify data precision before and after signal-drift correction (e.g. QC-RFSC vs QC-RLSC vs QC-SVR). metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Computes the relative standard deviation (RSD/CV%) of every feature across pooled QC injections in LC-MS metabolomics peak tables, then bins features into cumulative RSD intervals to quantify data precision before and after signal-drift correction (e.g. QC-RFSC vs QC-RLSC vs QC-SVR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets without repeated pooled QC injections interleaved with real samples (e.g. QC-free designs); use Combat via shiftCor_dQC instead, since no QC RSDs can be computed Peak tables not yet formatted to statTarget input layout (XCMS/MZmine/SIEVE/Skyline output must first be converted with the transX function) When the goal is drift correction itself rather than precision assessment — RSD computation only evaluates correction quality, it does not correct signal

skills.description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature intensity table (features as rows, samples as columns) includes blank samples, and features must be flagged and filtered against a blank-derived limit of detection.
skills.name: qc-flag-based-feature-filtering
skills.search_text: qc-flag-based-feature-filtering Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature intensity table (features as rows, samples as columns) includes blank samples, and features must be flagged and filtered against a blank-derived limit of detection. The input has no blank samples (or no design-file annotations distinguishing blanks), so no blank-based limit of detection can be computed — use the Threshold Based Flags tool instead, which identifies features below a user-specified threshold in more than 50% of samples within a given group. The goal is to evaluate features by retention-time variability, run order, or coefficient of variation rather than blank contamination — use the RT Flags, Run Order Regression, or CV Flags tools instead. The data are raw instrument files (e.g. pre-peak-picking) rather than a preprocessed wide-format feature table, since BFF starts from feature identification output. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 The Blank Feature Filtering (BFF) quality-control tool from SECIMTools computes a per-feature limit of detection from blank-sample intensity values and removes features that do not exceed that blank-derived threshold in a wide-format metabolomics feature table. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: The Blank Feature Filtering (BFF) quality-control tool from SECIMTools computes a per-feature limit of detection from blank-sample intensity values and removes features that do not exceed that blank-derived threshold in a wide-format metabolomics feature table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input has no blank samples (or no design-file annotations distinguishing blanks), so no blank-based limit of detection can be computed — use the Threshold Based Flags tool instead, which identifies features below a user-specified threshold in more than 50% of samples within a given group. The goal is to evaluate features by retention-time variability, run order, or coefficient of variation rather than blank contamination — use the RT Flags, Run Order Regression, or CV Flags tools instead. The data are raw instrument files (e.g. pre-peak-picking) rather than a preprocessed wide-format feature table, since BFF starts from feature identification output.

skills.search_text: qc-sample-rlsc-signal-correction Use when metabolomics peak-intensity matrices (featuredata) show drift with run order and QC samples were injected periodically, so a QC-sample-based LOESS signal correction (rlsc) is needed before scaling or comparison. Normalization should be driven by internal/external standard metabolites or QC metabolites rather than QC samples — use NormQcmets (methods 'nomis', 'ccmn', 'is', 'ruv2') instead Only sample-wise median/mean/sum/reference scaling is needed with no run-order drift — use NormScaling rather than rlsc The dataset has no periodically injected QC samples, so QC-RLSC signal correction cannot be fit Corrects run-order drift in metabolomics feature data by applying the QC-RLSC (quality control sample based robust LOESS signal correction) method via NormalizeMets' NormQcsamples function, using QC samples analysed periodically throughout the batch. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Corrects run-order drift in metabolomics feature data by applying the QC-RLSC (quality control sample based robust LOESS signal correction) method via NormalizeMets' NormQcsamples function, using QC samples analysed periodically throughout the batch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Normalization should be driven by internal/external standard metabolites or QC metabolites rather than QC samples — use NormQcmets (methods 'nomis', 'ccmn', 'is', 'ruv2') instead Only sample-wise median/mean/sum/reference scaling is needed with no run-order drift — use NormScaling rather than rlsc The dataset has no periodically injected QC samples, so QC-RLSC signal correction cannot be fit

skills.description: Use when a peak-integrated targeted LC-MS table (with aliquot, compound, area, type, batch columns) has been batch-corrected via pooled SQC samples and you must decide which compounds are reliable enough to report.
skills.name: qc-threshold-based-compound-flagging
skills.search_text: qc-threshold-based-compound-flagging Use when a peak-integrated targeted LC-MS table (with aliquot, compound, area, type, batch columns) has been batch-corrected via pooled SQC samples and you must decide which compounds are reliable enough to report. Input is raw LC-MS vendor peak data that has not yet been peak-integrated to a compound x sample table (mzQuality does not process raw peaks; OpenMS/MZmine handle that step). The dataset has no QC or blank sample type annotations, since RSDqc and background e-score cannot be computed without pooled QC and blank samples. Compounds lack stable-isotope internal standard assignments and calibration concentrations, since ratio-based RSD and e-score are meaningless in that configuration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classifies targeted metabolomics compounds into quality tiers (High confidence, Caution, Low Signal-to-Noise) using mzQuality thresholds on QC-sample relative standard deviation (RSDqc) and blank-sample background e-score, so unreliable compounds are excluded from reporting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Classifies targeted metabolomics compounds into quality tiers (High confidence, Caution, Low Signal-to-Noise) using mzQuality thresholds on QC-sample relative standard deviation (RSDqc) and blank-sample background e-score, so unreliable compounds are excluded from reporting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS vendor peak data that has not yet been peak-integrated to a compound x sample table (mzQuality does not process raw peaks; OpenMS/MZmine handle that step). The dataset has no QC or blank sample type annotations, since RSDqc and background e-score cannot be computed without pooled QC and blank samples. Compounds lack stable-isotope internal standard assignments and calibration concentrations, since ratio-based RSD and e-score are meaningless in that configuration.

skills.summary: Stage S2 of the NOREVA metabolomic peak-table processing pipeline: correct instrumental signal drift using repeatedly measured quality control samples (QCS) before transformation (S3) and normalization (S4), as part of a combinatorial workflow scan whose results are ranked by multiple criteria in S5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks quality control samples (QCS) — use the no-QCS variants (normulticlassnoall / nortimecoursenoall) instead of the qcall functions Classes or time points contain fewer than 6 samples, since criterion Cc is unsuitable for small-sample datasets and will distort S5 ranking The goal is exploratory statistics or biomarker discovery rather than optimizing the peak-table processing workflow itself (NOREVA does not replace MetaboAnalyst/W4M-style downstream analysis)

skills.search_text: qemistree-cscs-metric-evaluation Use when comparing how well MS2-based sample clustering metrics (MEMO, Qemistree UniFrac, CSCS) versus feature-table Bray-Curtis suppress a retention-time batch effect, quantified by PERMANOVA pseudo-F. skills.summary: Benchmark of six clustering distance metrics (MEMO aligned/unaligned, Qemistree weighted/unweighted UniFrac, CSCS weighted/unweighted, feature-table Bray-Curtis) on the 27-sample Qemistree evaluation dataset, scoring how well each mitigates the artificial C18 RT-shift batch effect using PERMANOVA pseudo-F for 'experiment' and 'composition' factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks MS/MS fragmentation spectra (feature table only), so MS2 fingerprints and cosine-score edges for MEMO/CSCS cannot be computed. skills.description: Use when validating a spectral-structure generative model on QM9S simulated IR/Raman/UV-Vis spectra, or when comparing a new elucidation model against DiffSpectra's 40.76% top-1 / 99.49% top-10 baseline.
skills.name: qm9s-benchmark-reproduction
skills.search_text: qm9s-benchmark-reproduction Use when validating a spectral-structure generative model on QM9S simulated IR/Raman/UV-Vis spectra, or when comparing a new elucidation model against DiffSpectra's 40.76% top-1 / 99.49% top-10 baseline. Input spectra are experimental NMR or mass spectrometry data — the paper explicitly limits the framework to IR, Raman, and UV-Vis modalities, so extension to NMR/MS remains unexplored. The goal is unconditional de novo molecule generation rather than spectra-conditioned elucidation — the eval pipeline conditions every sample on a QM9S spectrum and scores against a ground-truth reference structure. Only a single spectrum type is available and you still expect the 40.76% headline number — that figure corresponds to the all-spectra (IR + Raman + UV-Vis) configuration with pretrained SpecFormer; single-modality runs (ir, raman, uv) yield lower accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduce the DiffSpectra benchmark on the QM9S test set: run the spectra-conditioned diffusion sampler (DMT + SpecFormer) for a fixed number of samples per spectrum, then compute top-1/top-10 accuracy, similarity, and 3D RMSD metrics exactly as defined in the paper. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Reproduce the DiffSpectra benchmark on the QM9S test set: run the spectra-conditioned diffusion sampler (DMT + SpecFormer) for a fixed number of samples per spectrum, then compute top-1/top-10 accuracy, similarity, and 3D RMSD metrics exactly as defined in the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are experimental NMR or mass spectrometry data — the paper explicitly limits the framework to IR, Raman, and UV-Vis modalities, so extension to NMR/MS remains unexplored. The goal is unconditional de novo molecule generation rather than spectra-conditioned elucidation — the eval pipeline conditions every sample on a QM9S spectrum and scores against a ground-truth reference structure. skills.description: Use when a chemical inventory (with QSAR-ready SMILES, e.g. from HExpMetDB) lacks experimental toxicity values and predicted rat oral LD50 endpoints are needed for hazard or ToxPi-style risk ranking.
skills.name: qsar-smiles-batch-submission
skills.search_text: qsar-smiles-batch-submission Use when a chemical inventory (with QSAR-ready SMILES, e.g. from HExpMetDB) lacks experimental toxicity values and predicted rat oral LD50 endpoints are needed for hazard or ToxPi-style risk ranking. The substance contains a metal atom or has molecular weight >1,000 — the article notes such chemicals fall outside prediction coverage (stated for the IFS HLB approach); TEST predictions may likewise be unavailable. Experimental in vivo LD50 or chronic/subchronic toxicity data are already available for the chemicals — measured values should be preferred, since the article notes the LD50 approach may underestimate chronic and subchronic toxicity risk. The endpoint needed is chronic toxicity or internal exposure (IVIVE) rather than acute rat oral LD50. http://edamontology.org/topic_2815 Batch-submits QSAR-ready SMILES for a compiled chemical list to U.S. EPA TEST (v4.2.1) to obtain predicted rat oral LD50 values, producing a CASRN-to-LD50 mapping used for risk-based prioritization of human exposome chemicals. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Batch-submits QSAR-ready SMILES for a compiled chemical list to U.S. EPA TEST (v4.2.1) to obtain predicted rat oral LD50 values, producing a CASRN-to-LD50 mapping used for risk-based prioritization of human exposome chemicals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The substance contains a metal atom or has molecular weight >1,000 — the article notes such chemicals fall outside prediction coverage (stated for the IFS HLB approach); TEST predictions may likewise be unavailable. Experimental in vivo LD50 or chronic/subchronic toxicity data are already available for the chemicals — measured values should be preferred, since the article notes the LD50 approach may underestimate chronic and subchronic toxicity risk. The endpoint needed is chronic toxicity or internal exposure (IVIVE) rather than acute rat oral LD50.

skills.description: Use when you have sentinel variants (e.g. 227 mQTLs or 562 cis-pQTLs) with GRCh37 coordinates, proxy LD data, and VEP output, and need to prioritize causal candidate genes per locus.
skills.name: qtl-causal-gene-prioritization
skills.search_text: qtl-causal-gene-prioritization Use when you have sentinel variants (e.g. 227 mQTLs or 562 cis-pQTLs) with GRCh37 coordinates, proxy LD data, and VEP output, and need to prioritize causal candidate genes per locus. Prioritizing causal genes at trans-pQTLs: the article notes 'the prioritization of candidate causal genes at trans-pQTLs would call for a different top-down strategy to the one adopted here' (the top-down logic relies on local metabolic gene annotations) Your input is not GRCh37-anchored sentinel/proxy coordinates or you lack a VEP output covering sentinel-proxy combinations Your molecular phenotype is not metabolic-related and you have not prepared an equivalent .RData gene list for the top-down component (the bundled annotated_metabolic_genes.RData only covers metabolic phenotypes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 ProGeM is a configurable R-script framework that prioritizes candidate causal genes at molecular QTLs by combining a bottom-up component (nearest genes, LD-overlapping genes, GTEx cis-eQTL targets, VEP HIGH/MODERATE IMPACT annotation) with a top-down component (metabolic gene databases scored 0-5), and flagging cooccurring candidates as primary causal candidates. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gky837
skills.summary: ProGeM is a configurable R-script framework that prioritizes candidate causal genes at molecular QTLs by combining a bottom-up component (nearest genes, LD-overlapping genes, GTEx cis-eQTL targets, VEP HIGH/MODERATE IMPACT annotation) with a top-down component (metabolic gene databases scored 0-5), and flagging cooccurring candidates as primary causal candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Prioritizing causal genes at trans-pQTLs: the article notes 'the prioritization of candidate causal genes at trans-pQTLs would call for a different top-down strategy to the one adopted here' (the top-down logic relies on local metabolic gene annotations) Your input is not GRCh37-anchored sentinel/proxy coordinates or you lack a VEP output covering sentinel-proxy combinations Your molecular phenotype is not metabolic-related and you have not prepared an equivalent .RData gene list for the top-down component (the bundled annotated_metabolic_genes.RData only covers metabolic phenotypes)

skills.summary: Parse the three ProGeM summary outputs (OUTPUT_bottom_up_summary.txt, OUTPUT_top_down_scores.txt, OUTPUT_cooccurring_candidates.txt) in R, map candidate genes to sentinel loci, and benchmark each component's sensitivity and specificity against a curated reference set of 227 metabolite QTL causal gene assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw ProGeM settings or VEP output rather than the completed OUTPUT_* summary tables — parsing benchmarks require the final gene lists per sentinel locus When the reference causal gene set has not been curated (e.g. no Supplementary Table S1-equivalent assignments); sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed without a high-confidence reference For trans-pQTL loci — the article notes the top-down strategy is not directly applicable to trans-pQTLs, so benchmarking those components there would be misleading

skills.name: qtof-collision-energy-intensity-scaling
skills.search_text: qtof-collision-energy-intensity-scaling Use when building or validating a hand-written SMIRKS rule library (MSRB) whose relative-intensity parameters must be sourced from QTOF spectra at 10/20/40 eV, e.g. compiling msrb_rules_table.csv for CFM-ID 4.0-class predictors. Input spectra were collected on instruments other than QTOF — CFM-ID 4.0 explicitly notes the intent to later adapt to non-QTOF instruments, so scaled intensities from this library may not transfer The prediction task is purely combinatorial/learned (C2MS bond-topology model) rather than rule-based MSRB, since ClassyFire routing and SMIRKS rules only apply to classes suitable for MSRB fragmentation Curates and intensity-scales hand-written SMIRKS-based (MSRB) fragmentation rules so that each rule carries average scaled relative intensities derived from experimental QTOF ESI-MS/MS spectra acquired at 10, 20, and 40 eV collision energies, as implemented in CFM-ID 4.0's expanded rule library of 313 rules covering 11 chemical classes and 3 adduct types. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Curates and intensity-scales hand-written SMIRKS-based (MSRB) fragmentation rules so that each rule carries average scaled relative intensities derived from experimental QTOF ESI-MS/MS spectra acquired at 10, 20, and 40 eV collision energies, as implemented in CFM-ID 4.0's expanded rule library of 313 rules covering 11 chemical classes and 3 adduct types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra were collected on instruments other than QTOF — CFM-ID 4.0 explicitly notes the intent to later adapt to non-QTOF instruments, so scaled intensities from this library may not transfer The prediction task is purely combinatorial/learned (C2MS bond-topology model) rather than rule-based MSRB, since ClassyFire routing and SMIRKS rules only apply to classes suitable for MSRB fragmentation

skills.search_text: qtof-msms-cosine-similarity-scoring Use when comparing in-silico structure annotation (COSMIC/CSI:FingerID) against spectral library search on independent QTOF MS/MS query spectra, with correct-hit counts at FDR 5%. The goal is novel annotation of structures absent from spectral libraries — COSMIC is the appropriate primary method, and spectral library search matches only a small fraction of spectra De-replication where reference spectra for the target compounds are unavailable — the article notes COSMIC outperformed spectral library search for de-replication despite not being designed for it Query compounds whose own reference spectra must remain in the library — this skill requires the spectrum-disjoint evaluation setup http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Builds spectral-library-search baselines for QTOF tandem MS/MS data using normalized dot-product cosine similarity (plus a square-root-intensity-transformed variant), benchmarked against COSMIC at FDR 5% under a spectrum-disjoint evaluation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Builds spectral-library-search baselines for QTOF tandem MS/MS data using normalized dot-product cosine similarity (plus a square-root-intensity-transformed variant), benchmarked against COSMIC at FDR 5% under a spectrum-disjoint evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is novel annotation of structures absent from spectral libraries — COSMIC is the appropriate primary method, and spectral library search matches only a small fraction of spectra De-replication where reference spectra for the target compounds are unavailable — the article notes COSMIC outperformed spectral library search for de-replication despite not being designed for it Query compounds whose own reference spectra must remain in the library — this skill requires the spectrum-disjoint evaluation setup

skills.description: Use when LC-MS/MS samples were acquired on different mass spectrometers (e.g., Q-Exactive Orbitrap vs Maxis II Q-TOF) or with strong RT shifts, and you need to compare samples without prior feature alignment.
skills.name: qtof-orbitrap-cross-platform-sample-comparison
skills.search_text: qtof-orbitrap-cross-platform-sample-comparison Use when LC-MS/MS samples were acquired on different mass spectrometers (e.g., Q-Exactive Orbitrap vs Maxis II Q-TOF) or with strong RT shifts, and you need to compare samples without prior feature alignment. The samples were all acquired on a single platform with well-aligned features — a standard feature-table-based ordination suffices and MEMO's cross-platform advantage is unneeded You need to compare samples using a feature table with prior alignment (e.g., GNPS bucket table + CSCS edges); MEMO is specifically designed to avoid the prior feature alignment step Only MS1-level feature data are available without MS2 fragmentation spectra, since MS2 fingerprints are built from MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Vectorizes metabolomics samples acquired on different MS platforms (Maxis II Q-TOF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) using MEMO MS2 fingerprints, enabling retention-time-agnostic, cross-platform sample comparison via PCoA and PERMANOVA. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Vectorizes metabolomics samples acquired on different MS platforms (Maxis II Q-TOF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) using MEMO MS2 fingerprints, enabling retention-time-agnostic, cross-platform sample comparison via PCoA and PERMANOVA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples were all acquired on a single platform with well-aligned features — a standard feature-table-based ordination suffices and MEMO's cross-platform advantage is unneeded You need to compare samples using a feature table with prior alignment (e.g., GNPS bucket table + CSCS edges); MEMO is specifically designed to avoid the prior feature alignment step Only MS1-level feature data are available without MS2 fragmentation spectra, since MS2 fingerprints are built from MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor

skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS run (e.g. Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) yields MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites that must be matched to database compounds via structural-similarity ranking, not exact spectral library hits.
skills.name: qtof-spectra-compound-identification
skills.search_text: qtof-spectra-compound-identification Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS run (e.g. Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) yields MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites that must be matched to database compounds via structural-similarity ranking, not exact spectral library hits. When the unknown compound's exact spectrum already exists in a public spectral library, a direct library search gives a definitive annotation and DeepMASS's structural-similarity route is unnecessary. When the query metabolite has no structure-related metabolite in the reference database, DeepMASS identification is not valid by the paper's own criterion and other methods should be sought. When the analysis goal is quantification or feature detection rather than structural annotation of unknowns. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 DeepMASS structural-similarity scoring identifies unknown metabolites from QTOF MS/MS spectra (e.g. male-infertility biomarkers on a Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) by ranking database metabolites with a deep neural network, remaining valid when a structure-related metabolite exists in the database (KEGG). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05405
skills.summary: DeepMASS structural-similarity scoring identifies unknown metabolites from QTOF MS/MS spectra (e.g. male-infertility biomarkers on a Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) by ranking database metabolites with a deep neural network, remaining valid when a structure-related metabolite exists in the database (KEGG).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the unknown compound's exact spectrum already exists in a public spectral library, a direct library search gives a definitive annotation and DeepMASS's structural-similarity route is unnecessary. When the query metabolite has no structure-related metabolite in the reference database, DeepMASS identification is not valid by the paper's own criterion and other methods should be sought. When the analysis goal is quantification or feature detection rather than structural annotation of unknowns.

skills.description: Use when input is Q-TOF MS/MS spectra (MGF with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type, collision_energy) and the goal is top-k chemical formula identification, optionally ablation of augmentation/contrastive loss/post-processing.
skills.name: qtof-spectrum-formula-prediction
skills.search_text: qtof-spectrum-formula-prediction Use when input is Q-TOF MS/MS spectra (MGF with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type, collision_energy) and the goal is top-k chemical formula identification, optionally ablation of augmentation/contrastive loss/post-processing. Spectra come from Orbitrap instruments — no data augmentation was applied there (noise addition lowered similarity), and the 5 ppm tolerance applies instead of 10 ppm Spectra have fewer than five peaks or m/z above 1500 — these are excluded as unreliable or rare by the pipeline filters The task is structural elucidation rather than formula prediction — FIDDLE only provides the initial formula constraint step http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Predict molecular formulas from Q-TOF tandem mass spectra using FIDDLE, a deep learning pipeline that encodes MS/MS with dilated convolutions, refines predictions via breadth-first search against the precursor mass with SENIOR-rule filtering, and ranks candidates with a secondary confidence-scoring model. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Predict molecular formulas from Q-TOF tandem mass spectra using FIDDLE, a deep learning pipeline that encodes MS/MS with dilated convolutions, refines predictions via breadth-first search against the precursor mass with SENIOR-rule filtering, and ranks candidates with a secondary confidence-scoring model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra come from Orbitrap instruments — no data augmentation was applied there (noise addition lowered similarity), and the 5 ppm tolerance applies instead of 10 ppm Spectra have fewer than five peaks or m/z above 1500 — these are excluded as unreliable or rare by the pipeline filters The task is structural elucidation rather than formula prediction — FIDDLE only provides the initial formula constraint step

skills.search_text: qtof-vs-orbitrap-fragmentation-behavior-analysis Use when evaluating or retraining CFM-ID 4.0 on Orbitrap (or other non-QTOF) MS/MS data, or when benchmarking in silico MS-to-compound identification on the CASMI 2016 category 3 Orbitrap dataset. The input spectra were already collected on a QTOF instrument, where the paper's own QTOF-trained CFM-ID 4.0 model and its 147/208 baseline apply directly The analysis targets EI-MS/MS spectral prediction rather than ESI-MS/MS (the paper reports EI improvements separately, and this skill concerns ESI-QTOF/Orbitrap transfer) No candidate structure database is available, since identification requires scoring predicted spectra against candidates from CFM-ID's spectral database A benchmarking skill for testing whether CFM-ID 4.0's MS/MS spectral prediction generalizes across instrument types: retrain the MSML model on Orbitrap HCD MS/MS data instead of the QTOF Metlin data used in the paper, then evaluate compound identification on the CASMI 2016 category 3 benchmark against the reported QTOF-trained baseline of 147/208. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for testing whether CFM-ID 4.0's MS/MS spectral prediction generalizes across instrument types: retrain the MSML model on Orbitrap HCD MS/MS data instead of the QTOF Metlin data used in the paper, then evaluate compound identification on the CASMI 2016 category 3 benchmark against the reported QTOF-trained baseline of 147/208.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra were already collected on a QTOF instrument, where the paper's own QTOF-trained CFM-ID 4.0 model and its 147/208 baseline apply directly The analysis targets EI-MS/MS spectral prediction rather than ESI-MS/MS (the paper reports EI improvements separately, and this skill concerns ESI-QTOF/Orbitrap transfer) No candidate structure database is available, since identification requires scoring predicted spectra against candidates from CFM-ID's spectral database

skills.description: Use when predicting cell-/sample-wise metabolic flux from scRNA-seq or bulk transcriptomics data by training the scFEA factor-graph neural network under flux balance constraints, or when reproducing/evaluating its convergence behavior.
skills.name: quadratic-flux-balance-loss-optimization
skills.search_text: quadratic-flux-balance-loss-optimization Use when predicting cell-/sample-wise metabolic flux from scRNA-seq or bulk transcriptomics data by training the scFEA factor-graph neural network under flux balance constraints, or when reproducing/evaluating its convergence behavior. The goal is reconstruction of context-specific (disease, tissue, or cell type specific) metabolic networks and modules — the article lists this as not yet implemented Additional biochemical constraints such as redox balance, pH balance, or energy balance are required — these are described as future directions, not implemented The data are proteomics or metabolomics rather than transcriptomics — flux estimation for other omics types is listed as not yet available http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reconstructs the scFEA/FLUXestimator optimization solver: per-module multi-layer neural networks map gene expression to reaction fluxes, and a quadratic mass-balance loss on intermediate metabolite in-/out-flux plus a non-negativity penalty is minimized with Adam in PyTorch to estimate a cell-wise fluxome. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkad444
skills.summary: Reconstructs the scFEA/FLUXestimator optimization solver: per-module multi-layer neural networks map gene expression to reaction fluxes, and a quadratic mass-balance loss on intermediate metabolite in-/out-flux plus a non-negativity penalty is minimized with Adam in PyTorch to estimate a cell-wise fluxome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is reconstruction of context-specific (disease, tissue, or cell type specific) metabolic networks and modules — the article lists this as not yet implemented Additional biochemical constraints such as redox balance, pH balance, or energy balance are required — these are described as future directions, not implemented The data are proteomics or metabolomics rather than transcriptomics — flux estimation for other omics types is listed as not yet available

skills.description: Use when per-metabolite RT shifts obtained by cross-correlation of quantifier/qualifier MRM chromatograms against a reference sample show implausibly pronounced, non-smooth deviations across the chromatogram and must be regularized before peak picking or reporting.
skills.name: quadratic-regression-fitting-of-retention-time-shifts
skills.search_text: quadratic-regression-fitting-of-retention-time-shifts Use when per-metabolite RT shifts obtained by cross-correlation of quantifier/qualifier MRM chromatograms against a reference sample show implausibly pronounced, non-smooth deviations across the chromatogram and must be regularized before peak picking or reporting. Data are not MRM-mode LC-MS chromatograms (e.g. DDA/DIA or GC-MS runs without quantifier/qualifier traces), since the fitting relies on per-metabolite cross-correlation of quantifier and qualifier chromatograms The batch has only a quantifier and no qualifier transitions, since automRm requires at least one qualifier for optimal performance You need an absolute RT standardization across heterogeneous methods rather than smoothing sample-specific shifts within one batch http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Smooths per-metabolite cross-correlation retention time shifts across an LC-MS MRM chromatogram by fitting the RT shifts of all metabolites in a sample as a quadratic function of RT, eliminating artifacts from improbably pronounced individual shifts before peak picking/reporting in automRm. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05224
skills.summary: Smooths per-metabolite cross-correlation retention time shifts across an LC-MS MRM chromatogram by fitting the RT shifts of all metabolites in a sample as a quadratic function of RT, eliminating artifacts from improbably pronounced individual shifts before peak picking/reporting in automRm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not MRM-mode LC-MS chromatograms (e.g. DDA/DIA or GC-MS runs without quantifier/qualifier traces), since the fitting relies on per-metabolite cross-correlation of quantifier and qualifier chromatograms The batch has only a quantifier and no qualifier transitions, since automRm requires at least one qualifier for optimal performance You need an absolute RT standardization across heterogeneous methods rather than smoothing sample-specific shifts within one batch

skills.description: Use when acquiring low-resolution GC-CI-MS isotopologue data on a QqQ instrument and you must choose between SIM and narrow-window (~10 Da) scan acquisition, or need to select isobutane vs methane/EI ionization for [M+H]+ isotope envelope quantification.
skills.name: quadrupole-sim-mode-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: quadrupole-sim-mode-parameter-tuning Use when acquiring low-resolution GC-CI-MS isotopologue data on a QqQ instrument and you must choose between SIM and narrow-window (~10 Da) scan acquisition, or need to select isobutane vs methane/EI ionization for [M+H]+ isotope envelope quantification. The instrument is a high-resolution GC-(q)TOF or GC-Orbitrap acquiring full scan — those configurations capture isotope clusters without SIM window tuning. The goal is EI-based metabolite identification rather than isotope-envelope quantification; CI-isobutane SIM tuning is optimized for [M+H]+ isotopologue coverage, not EI spectral libraries. Samples are unlabeled and no isotopologue enrichment needs to be resolved — standard metabolite quantification methods suffice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Configures a triple quadrupole (QqQ) GC-CI-MS instrument to acquire isotopologue data in selected ion monitoring (SIM) and narrow-window scan (NS) modes, balancing sensitivity against isotope-envelope coverage for stable isotope labeling metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02998
skills.summary: Configures a triple quadrupole (QqQ) GC-CI-MS instrument to acquire isotopologue data in selected ion monitoring (SIM) and narrow-window scan (NS) modes, balancing sensitivity against isotope-envelope coverage for stable isotope labeling metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The instrument is a high-resolution GC-(q)TOF or GC-Orbitrap acquiring full scan — those configurations capture isotope clusters without SIM window tuning. The goal is EI-based metabolite identification rather than isotope-envelope quantification; CI-isobutane SIM tuning is optimized for [M+H]+ isotopologue coverage, not EI spectral libraries. Samples are unlabeled and no isotopologue enrichment needs to be resolved — standard metabolite quantification methods suffice.

skills.search_text: qualitative-finding-tabulation-from-article-text Use when an article's Results section compares multiple methods or conditions (e.g. CI-isobutane vs CI-methane vs EI at 70/15 eV) and you need a structured per-method table with quantitative metrics and figure provenance. The article reports only aggregated conclusions without per-condition statements, figures, or quantitative metrics to trace rows against The comparison data are already available as a structured table or supplementary file that can be used directly instead of re-extracted from prose The task requires quantitative re-analysis of raw spectra (e.g. isotopologue quantification with isoSCAN) rather than tabulating reported findings http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Extracts per-condition qualitative and quantitative findings from an article's Results text and assembles them into a traced comparison table (e.g. ionization_method_comparison.csv) where every row cites an explicit statement, figure, or supplementary figure. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02998
skills.summary: Extracts per-condition qualitative and quantitative findings from an article's Results text and assembles them into a traced comparison table (e.g. ionization_method_comparison.csv) where every row cites an explicit statement, figure, or supplementary figure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article reports only aggregated conclusions without per-condition statements, figures, or quantitative metrics to trace rows against The comparison data are already available as a structured table or supplementary file that can be used directly instead of re-extracted from prose The task requires quantitative re-analysis of raw spectra (e.g. isotopologue quantification with isoSCAN) rather than tabulating reported findings

skills.description: Use when input studies disclose only compound identifiers and trend labels (up-/down-regulated, no change) with no p-values, fold-changes or standard deviations, and a per-compound qualitative summary across studies is needed.
skills.name: qualitative-vote-counting-meta-analysis
skills.search_text: qualitative-vote-counting-meta-analysis Use when input studies disclose only compound identifiers and trend labels (up-/down-regulated, no change) with no p-values, fold-changes or standard deviations, and a per-compound qualitative summary across studies is needed. Studies disclose full statistical parameters (p-value, fold-change, n) — use amanida's quantitative weighted meta-analysis (mode = "quan" with compute_amanida) instead, which combines p-values via weighted Fisher's method and fold-changes via study-size-weighted averaging Input data has not been curated: identifiers are inconsistent chemical names/InChI/InChIKey/SMILES and check_names harmonization has not been run, so votes for the same compound would be split across duplicate IDs The goal is a weighted or significance-based effect-size estimate rather than a direction-of-change tally — vote-counting ignores study size and magnitudes entirely http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Performs a qualitative meta-analysis of metabolomics compounds via vote-counting when studies report only the trend (up-/down-regulation) of a compound rather than p-values or fold-changes; each compound-study observation contributes +1, -1 or 0 and votes are summed per compound. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab591
skills.summary: Performs a qualitative meta-analysis of metabolomics compounds via vote-counting when studies report only the trend (up-/down-regulation) of a compound rather than p-values or fold-changes; each compound-study observation contributes +1, -1 or 0 and votes are summed per compound.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Studies disclose full statistical parameters (p-value, fold-change, n) — use amanida's quantitative weighted meta-analysis (mode = "quan" with compute_amanida) instead, which combines p-values via weighted Fisher's method and fold-changes via study-size-weighted averaging Input data has not been curated: identifiers are inconsistent chemical names/InChI/InChIKey/SMILES and check_names harmonization has not been run, so votes for the same compound would be split across duplicate IDs The goal is a weighted or significance-based effect-size estimate rather than a direction-of-change tally — vote-counting ignores study size and magnitudes entirely
