skills.name: reduced-collision-cross-section-correction
skills.search_text: reduced-collision-cross-section-correction Use when calibrating single-field DTIMS-MS arrival times to CCS and calibrant and sample runs differ in pressure/temperature, requiring charge-state, reduced-mass, and P/T correction before linear fitting. Data are stepped-field DTIMS measurements — use AutoCCS's stepped-field method (Stow et al., 2017, --mode multi) rather than the enhanced single-field calibration Traveling-wave IMS data (Bruker timsTOF, Waters Synapt, SLIM) — these require linear timsTOF calibration, polynomial functions, or the linearized power function (Ruotolo et al., 2008), not the single-field P/T correction Input values are already reduced/P-T-adjusted CCS values rather than raw arrival-time feature tables needing calibration Applies AutoCCS's enhanced single-field DTIMS calibration, which converts calibrant arrival times to a reduced CCS (Ω' = (1/z)·sqrt(mI/(mI+mB))·Ω) and a pressure/temperature-adjusted CCS (Ω″ = (P/T)·Ω'), then fits a degree-1 linear calibration function to assign CCS to unknown analyte ions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: Applies AutoCCS's enhanced single-field DTIMS calibration, which converts calibrant arrival times to a reduced CCS (Ω' = (1/z)·sqrt(mI/(mI+mB))·Ω) and a pressure/temperature-adjusted CCS (Ω″ = (P/T)·Ω'), then fits a degree-1 linear calibration function to assign CCS to unknown analyte ions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are stepped-field DTIMS measurements — use AutoCCS's stepped-field method (Stow et al., 2017, --mode multi) rather than the enhanced single-field calibration Traveling-wave IMS data (Bruker timsTOF, Waters Synapt, SLIM) — these require linear timsTOF calibration, polynomial functions, or the linearized power function (Ruotolo et al., 2008), not the single-field P/T correction Input values are already reduced/P-T-adjusted CCS values rather than raw arrival-time feature tables needing calibration

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains many putative annotation rows per feature (e.g., the abbreviated table output by TurboPutative REname) and rows must be consolidated before manual comparison or pathway-level prioritization of metabolites.
skills.name: redundant-annotation-collapsing
skills.search_text: redundant-annotation-collapsing Use when a metabolomics feature table contains many putative annotation rows per feature (e.g., the abbreviated table output by TurboPutative REname) and rows must be consolidated before manual comparison or pathway-level prioritization of metabolites. Input is a raw feature-intensity table or metadata table rather than an REname-processed putative annotation table Rows differ in experimental neutral mass, m/z, adduct, or mass error — these are not redundant and must not be merged The goal is scoring/prioritization by adduct probability and feature correlations, which is the TPMetrics module's role, not RowMerger's http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 RowMerger-style collapsing of redundant putative annotation rows in untargeted metabolomics tables: entries sharing the same experimental neutral mass, m/z, adduct, and mass error are merged into a single row with abbreviated metabolite names joined by the '//' delimiter, reducing dataset size by up to 80%-90%. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.952149
skills.summary: RowMerger-style collapsing of redundant putative annotation rows in untargeted metabolomics tables: entries sharing the same experimental neutral mass, m/z, adduct, and mass error are merged into a single row with abbreviated metabolite names joined by the '//' delimiter, reducing dataset size by up to 80%-90%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw feature-intensity table or metadata table rather than an REname-processed putative annotation table Rows differ in experimental neutral mass, m/z, adduct, or mass error — these are not redundant and must not be merged The goal is scoring/prioritization by adduct probability and feature correlations, which is the TPMetrics module's role, not RowMerger's

skills.description: Use when a feature table has been annotated against multiple metabolite databases in tidyMass/metID and duplicate or conflicting compound assignments must be reconciled before downstream statistical analysis.
skills.name: redundant-annotation-filtering-by-score
skills.search_text: redundant-annotation-filtering-by-score Use when a feature table has been annotated against multiple metabolite databases in tidyMass/metID and duplicate or conflicting compound assignments must be reconciled before downstream statistical analysis. When features have not yet been annotated by metID against at least one database — there are no redundant annotations to reconcile When the analysis requires MSI level 1 (authentic standard) identifications — this workflow explicitly keeps only level 2 annotations When working outside the tidyMass/mass_dataset ecosystem and no annotation score is available to rank duplicate assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Merges metabolite annotations obtained from multiple databases (in-house HILIC/RPLC and public) within the tidyMass/metID workflow and removes redundant annotations based on the annotation score, keeping only MSI level 2 identifications (74 metabolites in the CRC case study). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-32155-w
skills.summary: Merges metabolite annotations obtained from multiple databases (in-house HILIC/RPLC and public) within the tidyMass/metID workflow and removes redundant annotations based on the annotation score, keeping only MSI level 2 identifications (74 metabolites in the CRC case study).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When features have not yet been annotated by metID against at least one database — there are no redundant annotations to reconcile When the analysis requires MSI level 1 (authentic standard) identifications — this workflow explicitly keeps only level 2 annotations When working outside the tidyMass/mass_dataset ecosystem and no annotation score is available to rank duplicate assignments

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics annotation table contains many putative compound name variants for the same metabolite and redundant entries must be collapsed for downstream pathway analysis.
skills.name: redundant-annotation-grouping-by-abbreviated-name-and-mass
skills.search_text: redundant-annotation-grouping-by-abbreviated-name-and-mass Use when an untargeted metabolomics annotation table contains many putative compound name variants for the same metabolite and redundant entries must be collapsed for downstream pathway analysis. Input is already a deduplicated feature-intensity table; use TPMetrics instead, which combines datasets with feature intensity and metadata and calculates an adduct-probability/correlation score The goal is metabolite classification rather than annotation cleanup — Tagger is the module that classifies the different compounds The goal is merging rows to reduce dataset size for manual comparison of annotations — RowMerger is designed for that purpose http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 TurboPutative's REname mechanism abbreviates putative metabolite annotation names (lipids via LMSD/Goslin dictionaries, non-lipids via fallback regexes) and collapses entries sharing the same abbreviated name and accurate mass, removing redundant rows from untargeted metabolomics datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.952149
skills.summary: TurboPutative's REname mechanism abbreviates putative metabolite annotation names (lipids via LMSD/Goslin dictionaries, non-lipids via fallback regexes) and collapses entries sharing the same abbreviated name and accurate mass, removing redundant rows from untargeted metabolomics datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a deduplicated feature-intensity table; use TPMetrics instead, which combines datasets with feature intensity and metadata and calculates an adduct-probability/correlation score The goal is metabolite classification rather than annotation cleanup — Tagger is the module that classifies the different compounds The goal is merging rows to reduce dataset size for manual comparison of annotations — RowMerger is designed for that purpose

skills.description: Use when a large collection of PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-clusters (e.g. 108,085 from 60,028 non-redundant antiSMASH-DB BGCs) must be de-replicated and organised into hierarchical sub-cluster families and clans.
skills.name: redundant-subcluster-removal
skills.search_text: redundant-subcluster-removal Use when a large collection of PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-clusters (e.g. 108,085 from 60,028 non-redundant antiSMASH-DB BGCs) must be de-replicated and organised into hierarchical sub-cluster families and clans. Input consists of PRESTO-TOP topic-modelled sub-clusters, whose native representation is a bag-of-words LDA model rather than the presence/absence matrix of tokenised genes used here Input is a single BGC or a small BGC set — K-means grouping into SCFs/SCCs requires a large corpus of predicted sub-clusters to be meaningful The goal is clustering whole BGCs by gene content; this skill operates at the sub-cluster level within BGCs http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Groups related PRESTO-STAT-predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters into sub-cluster families (SCFs) and clans (SCCs) with K-means on a presence/absence matrix of tokenised genes, removing redundant sub-clusters during grouping. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Groups related PRESTO-STAT-predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters into sub-cluster families (SCFs) and clans (SCCs) with K-means on a presence/absence matrix of tokenised genes, removing redundant sub-clusters during grouping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of PRESTO-TOP topic-modelled sub-clusters, whose native representation is a bag-of-words LDA model rather than the presence/absence matrix of tokenised genes used here Input is a single BGC or a small BGC set — K-means grouping into SCFs/SCCs requires a large corpus of predicted sub-clusters to be meaningful The goal is clustering whole BGCs by gene content; this skill operates at the sub-cluster level within BGCs

skills.description: Use when per-sample detected feature tables (e.g., key 'A' from example_alignment.h5) show coordinate drift between LC-IMS-MS/MS samples and features must be matched across samples before downstream quantification.
skills.name: reference-based-feature-alignment
skills.search_text: reference-based-feature-alignment Use when per-sample detected feature tables (e.g., key 'A' from example_alignment.h5) show coordinate drift between LC-IMS-MS/MS samples and features must be matched across samples before downstream quantification. Input is already an aligned, cross-sample feature table — re-alignment would distort quantified intensities. The study lacks a stable in-study reference sample (e.g., only a single sample is available), since SVR fitting requires matched pairs against a reference. The data are not multi-dimensional (e.g., m/z versus RT only with no drift time), where the RBF-kernel SVR gains described in the paper's 3D processing would not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Corrects cross-sample feature coordinate drift in high-dimensional mass spectrometry data by matching each sample's features to an in-study reference and fitting support vector regression (SVR) per dimension (m/z, drift time, retention time), as implemented in DEIMoS. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Corrects cross-sample feature coordinate drift in high-dimensional mass spectrometry data by matching each sample's features to an in-study reference and fitting support vector regression (SVR) per dimension (m/z, drift time, retention time), as implemented in DEIMoS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned, cross-sample feature table — re-alignment would distort quantified intensities. The study lacks a stable in-study reference sample (e.g., only a single sample is available), since SVR fitting requires matched pairs against a reference. The data are not multi-dimensional (e.g., m/z versus RT only with no drift time), where the RBF-kernel SVR gains described in the paper's 3D processing would not apply.

skills.description: Use when processing a series of 1D-NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. replicate mixtures or extract series in MetaboLabPy 0.9.66) where within-series phase consistency across replicates matters, or when comparing against apk0.noe/apk5/MNova phasing.
skills.name: reference-baseline-based-phase-correction
skills.search_text: reference-baseline-based-phase-correction Use when processing a series of 1D-NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. replicate mixtures or extract series in MetaboLabPy 0.9.66) where within-series phase consistency across replicates matters, or when comparing against apk0.noe/apk5/MNova phasing. When the goal is isotopomer/tracer analysis (metabolabpytools HSQC + GC-MS neural-network workflow) rather than 1D-NMR phasing When only a single spectrum needs phasing with no replicate series — the consistency advantage over per-spectrum correction is not the deciding factor When the input is 2D-NMR data or raw instrument formats unsupported by MetaboLabPy's NMR import http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Applies MetaboLabPy's reference/baseline-based automated phase correction, which uses baseline information rather than purely per-spectrum optimization to phase 1D-NMR spectra. In the benchmark of automatic phase correction algorithms, this baseline-based algorithm gave the most consistent (lowest-dispersion) phases across metabolite mix replicate series and Daphnia extract CryoProbe spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Applies MetaboLabPy's reference/baseline-based automated phase correction, which uses baseline information rather than purely per-spectrum optimization to phase 1D-NMR spectra. In the benchmark of automatic phase correction algorithms, this baseline-based algorithm gave the most consistent (lowest-dispersion) phases across metabolite mix replicate series and Daphnia extract CryoProbe spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is isotopomer/tracer analysis (metabolabpytools HSQC + GC-MS neural-network workflow) rather than 1D-NMR phasing When only a single spectrum needs phasing with no replicate series — the consistency advantage over per-spectrum correction is not the deciding factor When the input is 2D-NMR data or raw instrument formats unsupported by MetaboLabPy's NMR import

skills.description: Use when constructing BGC sequence similarity networks from genome-mining output and you need experimentally characterized reference clusters (e.g. MIBiG) mixed into the same clustering run to assign functions to novel GCFs.
skills.name: reference-bgc-dataset-integration
skills.search_text: reference-bgc-dataset-integration Use when constructing BGC sequence similarity networks from genome-mining output and you need experimentally characterized reference clusters (e.g. MIBiG) mixed into the same clustering run to assign functions to novel GCFs. When the goal is only to count or cluster the study's own BGCs without functional anchoring — adding references changes family counts and network topology When the study BGCs were predicted with an antiSMASH version or parameters incompatible with the MIBiG GenBank format expected by BiG-SCAPE When comparing against a newer MIBiG release than the one the original analysis used (release 1.3, August 2016), as counts will not be comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Augments a study's antiSMASH-predicted BGC set with curated reference biosynthetic gene clusters from the MIBiG database (release 1.3, 1,393 BGCs in this study) before BiG-SCAPE network construction, so that newly identified GCFs can be anchored to biochemically characterized clusters. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-019-0400-9
skills.summary: Augments a study's antiSMASH-predicted BGC set with curated reference biosynthetic gene clusters from the MIBiG database (release 1.3, 1,393 BGCs in this study) before BiG-SCAPE network construction, so that newly identified GCFs can be anchored to biochemically characterized clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only to count or cluster the study's own BGCs without functional anchoring — adding references changes family counts and network topology When the study BGCs were predicted with an antiSMASH version or parameters incompatible with the MIBiG GenBank format expected by BiG-SCAPE When comparing against a newer MIBiG release than the one the original analysis used (release 1.3, August 2016), as counts will not be comparable

skills.search_text: reference-causal-gene-set-matching Use when you have prioritized candidate causal gene lists per sentinel variant and a curated reference set of true positive causal genes, and need per-component sensitivity (fraction of reference loci recovered) and specificity (true positives per candidate assignment). skills.summary: Benchmark the sensitivity and specificity of causal gene prioritization outputs (ProGeM bottom-up, top-down, and co-occurring candidates) by matching them against a curated reference set of 227 metabolite QTL causal gene assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No curated reference causal gene set exists for your QTL dataset — sensitivity cannot be computed without high-confidence true positive assignments Evaluating trans-pQTL causal gene prioritization, where the article states ProGeM's top-down strategy is not directly applicable and 'would call for a different top-down strategy' Inputs are raw QTL summary statistics or sentinel variant lists rather than prioritized candidate gene lists per locus

skills.description: Use when constructing or validating the compound input for HRMS prescreening: mapping compound names, formulas or SMILES (or precursor m/z for non-targets) to adduct-specific precursor ion masses and confirming identifiers against PubChemLite.
skills.name: reference-database-compound-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: reference-database-compound-identifier-mapping Use when constructing or validating the compound input for HRMS prescreening: mapping compound names, formulas or SMILES (or precursor m/z for non-targets) to adduct-specific precursor ion masses and confirming identifiers against PubChemLite. Input is already a validated compound_table.csv with identifier, structural fields and precursor masses present. The analysis goal is de novo annotation of unknowns without any preselected compound or mass list — Shinyscreen's focus is exclusively on a preselected list of compounds or masses of interest. Raw vendor files (e.g. Thermo Xcalibur data) need conversion or feature detection rather than compound-table preparation; Shinyscreen starts from compounds/masses, not vendor acquisition files. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Builds the validated compound table that drives Shinyscreen's list-based HRMS prescreening: parsing the YAML config and compound-list CSV, splitting target/suspect vs non-target entries, computing adduct-specific precursor masses with enviPat, and cross-checking compound identifiers against a local reference database (PubChemLite). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-01044-x
skills.summary: Builds the validated compound table that drives Shinyscreen's list-based HRMS prescreening: parsing the YAML config and compound-list CSV, splitting target/suspect vs non-target entries, computing adduct-specific precursor masses with enviPat, and cross-checking compound identifiers against a local reference database (PubChemLite).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated compound_table.csv with identifier, structural fields and precursor masses present. The analysis goal is de novo annotation of unknowns without any preselected compound or mass list — Shinyscreen's focus is exclusively on a preselected list of compounds or masses of interest. Raw vendor files (e.g. Thermo Xcalibur data) need conversion or feature detection rather than compound-table preparation; Shinyscreen starts from compounds/masses, not vendor acquisition files.

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics compound/annotation list needs biological-origin labels (nutrient, drug, microbiota-dependent metabolite, natural product/plant, halogenated, peptide-like) derived purely from compound names and synonyms rather than from spectra or structures.
skills.name: reference-database-name-matching
skills.search_text: reference-database-name-matching Use when an untargeted metabolomics compound/annotation list needs biological-origin labels (nutrient, drug, microbiota-dependent metabolite, natural product/plant, halogenated, peptide-like) derived purely from compound names and synonyms rather than from spectra or structures. The input dataset already contains compound origin/class annotations and only needs reformatting or deduplication (use REname/RowMerger instead). The goal is structural or spectral metabolite confirmation (e.g., MS/MS-based identification) rather than name-based classification. The input is a feature-intensity/metadata table for scoring (TPMetrics handles adduct-probability scoring), not a compound name list. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Classifies compounds from untargeted metabolomics annotation tables by matching compound names/synonyms against curated reference lists (HMDB nutrients, DrugBank/HMDB drugs, PlantCyc, LOTUS, Metabolomics Data Explorer MDMs), as implemented in the Tagger module of TurboPutative to add biological-origin context to putative annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.952149
skills.summary: Classifies compounds from untargeted metabolomics annotation tables by matching compound names/synonyms against curated reference lists (HMDB nutrients, DrugBank/HMDB drugs, PlantCyc, LOTUS, Metabolomics Data Explorer MDMs), as implemented in the Tagger module of TurboPutative to add biological-origin context to putative annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input dataset already contains compound origin/class annotations and only needs reformatting or deduplication (use REname/RowMerger instead). The goal is structural or spectral metabolite confirmation (e.g., MS/MS-based identification) rather than name-based classification. The input is a feature-intensity/metadata table for scoring (TPMetrics handles adduct-probability scoring), not a compound name list.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing the assembled experimental lipid CCS reference database (SQLite) and its row counts — per-mode (positive/negative), per-drift-tube-type (DTIM/TWIM/TIMS), and per-lipid-class coverage.

skills.search_text: reference-database-row-count-validation Use when reproducing or auditing the assembled experimental lipid CCS reference database (SQLite) and its row counts — per-mode (positive/negative), per-drift-tube-type (DTIM/TWIM/TIMS), and per-lipid-class coverage. skills.summary: Reproduces and validates the LiPydomics experimental reference lipid database by building a SQLite store from the cleaned per-dataset JSON CCS collections and verifying row and per-field totals (7907 CCS values across 45 lipid classes) against published figures.

When the input is an unnormalized or raw IM-MS feature list rather than the cleaned per-dataset JSON CCS collections the build scripts expect. skills.description: Use when a locally regenerated preprocessed MS-file (e.g., a '_SR' saturation-repair output in Agilent .d profile mode) must be validated against the authors' deposited preprocessed file in a public deposit such as MassIVE MSV000087295.
skills.name: reference-deposit-comparison
skills.search_text: reference-deposit-comparison Use when a locally regenerated preprocessed MS-file (e.g., a '_SR' saturation-repair output in Agilent .d profile mode) must be validated against the authors' deposited preprocessed file in a public deposit such as MassIVE MSV000087295. No deposited reference preprocessed file exists for the dataset — without an accession like MSV000087295 there is no comparison target for output_matches_reference. The goal is new discovery (e.g., counting lipid annotations) rather than verifying that a reproduced preprocessing run matches published output. Data are already reduced to peak lists or feature tables, so instrument-format/profile-mode structural equivalence with the deposit cannot be assessed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates a reproduced preprocessing output (e.g., PNNL PreProcessor saturation repair on Agilent .d LC-DT IM-MS lipid files) via direct checks — file existence, instrument format, structural match — against the authors' deposited preprocessed file in the MassIVE deposit MSV000087295, optionally augmented by an R/ChemCalc isotopic Pearson-correlation score. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: Validates a reproduced preprocessing output (e.g., PNNL PreProcessor saturation repair on Agilent .d LC-DT IM-MS lipid files) via direct checks — file existence, instrument format, structural match — against the authors' deposited preprocessed file in the MassIVE deposit MSV000087295, optionally augmented by an R/ChemCalc isotopic Pearson-correlation score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No deposited reference preprocessed file exists for the dataset — without an accession like MSV000087295 there is no comparison target for output_matches_reference. The goal is new discovery (e.g., counting lipid annotations) rather than verifying that a reproduced preprocessing run matches published output. Data are already reduced to peak lists or feature tables, so instrument-format/profile-mode structural equivalence with the deposit cannot be assessed.

skills.description: Use when multiple LC-HRMS data files from different metabolomics experiments must be matched to a reference feature list so corresponding ions across batches can be compared, e.g. after XCMS feature extraction with observed m/z and retention time shifts.
skills.name: reference-feature-list-matching
skills.search_text: reference-feature-list-matching Use when multiple LC-HRMS data files from different metabolomics experiments must be matched to a reference feature list so corresponding ions across batches can be compared, e.g. after XCMS feature extraction with observed m/z and retention time shifts. Input is already an aligned combined feature matrix — MetMatch is for matching target chromatograms against a reference feature list, not for further statistical analysis of aligned data Only a single chromatogram exists with no separate reference feature list from a prior experiment — no reference to match against Data are not LC-HRMS chromatograms with m/z and retention time values (e.g. GC-MS or direct-infusion spectra without retention time dimension) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Semi-automated alignment of LC-HRMS target chromatograms against a processed reference feature list (m/z and retention time) using MetMatch, which corrects m/z offsets and non-linear retention time shifts and combines matched chromatographic peak areas, m/z values and retention times into a single data matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: Semi-automated alignment of LC-HRMS target chromatograms against a processed reference feature list (m/z and retention time) using MetMatch, which corrects m/z offsets and non-linear retention time shifts and combines matched chromatographic peak areas, m/z values and retention times into a single data matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned combined feature matrix — MetMatch is for matching target chromatograms against a reference feature list, not for further statistical analysis of aligned data Only a single chromatogram exists with no separate reference feature list from a prior experiment — no reference to match against Data are not LC-HRMS chromatograms with m/z and retention time values (e.g. GC-MS or direct-infusion spectra without retention time dimension)

skills.description: Use when XCMS peak grouping has flagged feature groups as misaligned (features whose RT drift differs across m/z bins or with run-order-dependent drift) and the per-sample corrected RTs must be replaced with compound-specific warping functions before re-grouping or peak-filling.
skills.name: reference-free-multiple-profile-alignment
skills.search_text: reference-free-multiple-profile-alignment Use when XCMS peak grouping has flagged feature groups as misaligned (features whose RT drift differs across m/z bins or with run-order-dependent drift) and the per-sample corrected RTs must be replaced with compound-specific warping functions before re-grouping or peak-filling. Features are already well-aligned by XCMS's single per-sample warping function and were not flagged by ncGTW's misalignment detection module You need a global whole-dataset re-alignment rather than targeted realignment of specific detected feature groups — ncGTW is a targeted post-XCMS plug-in, not a full preprocessing pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Realign misaligned LC-MS feature profiles using ncGTW's two-stage, reference-free algorithm: combinatorial pairwise warpings between all sample pairs (with neighboring-sample structural constraints solved as maximum-flow problems) are coordinately aggregated onto a pseudo-reference to yield sample-specific RT warping functions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa037
skills.summary: Realign misaligned LC-MS feature profiles using ncGTW's two-stage, reference-free algorithm: combinatorial pairwise warpings between all sample pairs (with neighboring-sample structural constraints solved as maximum-flow problems) are coordinately aggregated onto a pseudo-reference to yield sample-specific RT warping functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are already well-aligned by XCMS's single per-sample warping function and were not flagged by ncGTW's misalignment detection module You need a global whole-dataset re-alignment rather than targeted realignment of specific detected feature groups — ncGTW is a targeted post-XCMS plug-in, not a full preprocessing pipeline

skills.search_text: reference-library-spectrum-matching Use when a 1H NMR mixture spectrum must be decomposed into molar proportions of known library components (e.g., BCAAs leucine/isoleucine/valine), especially with overlapping, shifted, or distorted peaks. The components of the mixture are unknown and no reference library spectra are available — Magnetstein requires candidate component spectra in the library. Absolute (not relative) concentrations are needed and no quantitative external-standard spectrum is available to add algebraically to the mixture spectrum. The spectrum is a clean, well-separated 1:10 two-component mixture where simpler peak-based tools suffice (though Magnetstein still achieves AvRE 0.0% there). http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Quantify the molar composition of a 1H NMR mixture by matching the sample spectrum against reference library spectra of known components using Magnetstein, which treats spectra as probability distributions and solves quantification via optimal transport theory. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03594
skills.summary: Quantify the molar composition of a 1H NMR mixture by matching the sample spectrum against reference library spectra of known components using Magnetstein, which treats spectra as probability distributions and solves quantification via optimal transport theory.

skills.search_text: reference-vector-normalization Use when metabolomics samples differ in total abundance due to physical quantity differences (e.g., tissue mass, sample volume) and a per-sample reference vector such as weight or volume is available to normalize against. No meaningful per-sample reference vector (weight/volume) exists — use the sum, median, or mean NormScaling variants instead Unwanted variation is batch/matrix related rather than a total-abundance scaling issue — the package routes those cases to NormQcmets, NormQcsamples (QC-RLSC), or NormCombined Input is raw peak intensities with missing values or zeros not yet handled — pre-process with LogTransform(zerotona=TRUE) and MissingValues first http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A scaling normalization from the NormalizeMets package's NormScaling function in which metabolite abundances in each sample are scaled against a user-supplied reference vector, such as sample weight or volume. It is one of four NormScaling methods (sum, median, mean, ref) for correcting sample-specific total abundance differences in metabolomics featuredata. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: A scaling normalization from the NormalizeMets package's NormScaling function in which metabolite abundances in each sample are scaled against a user-supplied reference vector, such as sample weight or volume. It is one of four NormScaling methods (sum, median, mean, ref) for correcting sample-specific total abundance differences in metabolomics featuredata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No meaningful per-sample reference vector (weight/volume) exists — use the sum, median, or mean NormScaling variants instead Unwanted variation is batch/matrix related rather than a total-abundance scaling issue — the package routes those cases to NormQcmets, NormQcsamples (QC-RLSC), or NormCombined Input is raw peak intensities with missing values or zeros not yet handled — pre-process with LogTransform(zerotona=TRUE) and MissingValues first

skills.search_text: reference-vs-target-ion-list-preparation Use when aligning untargeted LC-HRMS metabolomics batches where the same metabolites may be detected as different ion species (e.g., A1 vs. A2 adducts) and features must be matched across m/z and retention time shifts. skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference and target data were measured under identical ion-species conditions and no adduct transformation is needed — use plain benchmark alignment instead Input is already an aligned combined data matrix rather than raw per-batch feature lists

skills.summary: Tabulates significantly altered metabolites and all detected metabolites by RefMet metabolite class (main_class, sub_class, super_class) and computes a per-class hypergeometric enrichment p-value and enrichment score, as implemented in MetENP's metclassenrichment step.

skills.description: Use when lipid identifiers in a processed lipidomic table are RefMet-compliant textual names (e.g. 'FA(18:3)', 'octadecatrienoic acid') rather than the generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M' format, and you need per-residue carbon:double-bond strings.
skills.name: refmet-nomenclature-mapping
skills.search_text: refmet-nomenclature-mapping Use when lipid identifiers in a processed lipidomic table are RefMet-compliant textual names (e.g. 'FA(18:3)', 'octadecatrienoic acid') rather than the generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M' format, and you need per-residue carbon:double-bond strings. Identifiers already follow the generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M/../..' or 'CLASS(...)(...)' isomer-group format — use the standard Lipid.residues() parser instead of refmet_residues(). You need to reject isobarically ambiguous lipids outright (drop_ambiguous=True on make_residues_table) rather than decode RefMet common names. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Decodes RefMet-compliant lipid identifiers, including standardized common names like 'linolenic acid' and composite compounds like 'linoleyl palmitate', into their fatty acid residue lists with ambiguity counts using liputils' Lipid.refmet_residues() method. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70259-9
skills.summary: Decodes RefMet-compliant lipid identifiers, including standardized common names like 'linolenic acid' and composite compounds like 'linoleyl palmitate', into their fatty acid residue lists with ambiguity counts using liputils' Lipid.refmet_residues() method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Identifiers already follow the generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M/../..' or 'CLASS(...)(...)' isomer-group format — use the standard Lipid.residues() parser instead of refmet_residues(). You need to reject isobarically ambiguous lipids outright (drop_ambiguous=True on make_residues_table) rather than decode RefMet common names.

skills.description: Use when metabolite identifiers in a study's metabolite table are non-standard (free-text names) and must be harmonized to RefMet and KEGG compound IDs before counting significant metabolites or mapping to KEGG pathways.
skills.name: refmet-nomenclature-mapping
skills.search_text: refmet-nomenclature-mapping Use when metabolite identifiers in a study's metabolite table are non-standard (free-text names) and must be harmonized to RefMet and KEGG compound IDs before counting significant metabolites or mapping to KEGG pathways. Input metabolite identifiers are already RefMet-standard names and KEGG IDs are already attached — re-running convert_refmet() adds no information The target database is not KEGG (e.g., analysis targets Reactome or MetaCyc pathways), since map_keggid()/compoundinfo() produces KEGG compound IDs Working with MetENPweb only and no command-line/custom dataset processing is needed, since the web interface handles standardization internally http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Standardizes metabolite names from a metabolomics dataset (e.g., Metabolomics Workbench study tables) to RefMet nomenclature using MetENP's convert_refmet(), then maps standardized names to species-specific KEGG compound IDs via map_keggid()/compoundinfo() so downstream enrichment and pathway analysis can proceed. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.11.20.391912
skills.summary: Standardizes metabolite names from a metabolomics dataset (e.g., Metabolomics Workbench study tables) to RefMet nomenclature using MetENP's convert_refmet(), then maps standardized names to species-specific KEGG compound IDs via map_keggid()/compoundinfo() so downstream enrichment and pathway analysis can proceed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metabolite identifiers are already RefMet-standard names and KEGG IDs are already attached — re-running convert_refmet() adds no information The target database is not KEGG (e.g., analysis targets Reactome or MetaCyc pathways), since map_keggid()/compoundinfo() produces KEGG compound IDs Working with MetENPweb only and no command-line/custom dataset processing is needed, since the web interface handles standardization internally

skills.description: Use when a mass deviation query against PubChem (e.g., 10 ppm with 0.002 Da absolute minimum) returns very large candidate sets (challenges 1, 2, and 14) for MAGMa penalty-score ranking, and candidate-list reduction by compound reliability is desired.
skills.name: refscore-based-candidate-filtering
skills.search_text: refscore-based-candidate-filtering Use when a mass deviation query against PubChem (e.g., 10 ppm with 0.002 Da absolute minimum) returns very large candidate sets (challenges 1, 2, and 14) for MAGMa penalty-score ranking, and candidate-list reduction by compound reliability is desired. When the correct compound is known to have a very low PubChem refscore (like challenge 3's N2-acetyl glutaminyl leucinamide, refscore 1) — aggressive thresholds (<200) will remove it from the candidate set entirely. When the initial candidate list is already small (few candidates), filtering provides no ranking benefit and only risks excluding the true structure. When candidates must be retrieved without a refscore field (e.g., sources other than the local PubChem snapshot), since the threshold cannot be applied. Prunes large PubChem-derived candidate molecule lists using the PubChem refscore (a database quality/reliability score), either at a fixed threshold (e.g., 5) or stepwise (<1000, <500, <200 candidates) to improve MAGMa structure-ranking results. metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033
skills.summary: Prunes large PubChem-derived candidate molecule lists using the PubChem refscore (a database quality/reliability score), either at a fixed threshold (e.g., 5) or stepwise (<1000, <500, <200 candidates) to improve MAGMa structure-ranking results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the correct compound is known to have a very low PubChem refscore (like challenge 3's N2-acetyl glutaminyl leucinamide, refscore 1) — aggressive thresholds (<200) will remove it from the candidate set entirely. When the initial candidate list is already small (few candidates), filtering provides no ranking benefit and only risks excluding the true structure. When candidates must be retrieved without a refscore field (e.g., sources other than the local PubChem snapshot), since the threshold cannot be applied.

skills.description: Decision support for choosing annotation tools or transcript sources: when you must know which transcripts ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP actually cover on RefSeq vs Ensembl, and how much their transcript identifier sets overlap.
skills.name: refseq-ensembl-transcript-set-concordance
skills.search_text: refseq-ensembl-transcript-set-concordance Decision support for choosing annotation tools or transcript sources: when you must know which transcripts ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP actually cover on RefSeq vs Ensembl, and how much their transcript identifier sets overlap. You need variant-level annotation agreement (HGVSc/HGVSp/coding impact concordance) rather than transcript-set overlap — that is a different comparison performed on annotated variants, not identifier sets. Your annotation tools were run against the same standardized transcript reference, so their identifier sets are expected to be identical by construction and the concordance statistic carries no signal. Input annotation outputs do not record transcript accessions at all (e.g. gene-level-only annotations), making identifier-set intersection impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Quantifies how many NM/NR (RefSeq) and ENST (Ensembl) transcript accessions each variant annotation tool exposes, then computes pairwise concordance across ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP for the same reference database. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Quantifies how many NM/NR (RefSeq) and ENST (Ensembl) transcript accessions each variant annotation tool exposes, then computes pairwise concordance across ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP for the same reference database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need variant-level annotation agreement (HGVSc/HGVSp/coding impact concordance) rather than transcript-set overlap — that is a different comparison performed on annotated variants, not identifier sets. Your annotation tools were run against the same standardized transcript reference, so their identifier sets are expected to be identical by construction and the concordance statistic carries no signal. Input annotation outputs do not record transcript accessions at all (e.g. gene-level-only annotations), making identifier-set intersection impossible.

skills.description: Use when building a species-specific metabolic network for an organism whose KEGG map lacks complete reaction coverage, by combining NCBI-RefSeq gene annotations with the 66 base KEGG pathway layouts shipped in MINNO.
skills.name: refseq-gene-annotation-integration
skills.search_text: refseq-gene-annotation-integration Use when building a species-specific metabolic network for an organism whose KEGG map lacks complete reaction coverage, by combining NCBI-RefSeq gene annotations with the 66 base KEGG pathway layouts shipped in MINNO. When the target organism already has a fully populated, literature-curated genome-scale metabolic model (e.g., a BiGG model) that requires no further gap-filling When the goal is pure genome annotation rather than metabolic network refinement, since MINNO is specifically designed for metabolomics-driven network editing http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Integrate NCBI-RefSeq genetic annotation data with KEGG base metabolic pathway layouts inside the MINNO visualization tool to generate organism-specific metabolic networks whose annotated reactions appear as dark nodes/edges and unannotated or missing ones as light gray nodes/edges, enabling flagging of missing reactions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Integrate NCBI-RefSeq genetic annotation data with KEGG base metabolic pathway layouts inside the MINNO visualization tool to generate organism-specific metabolic networks whose annotated reactions appear as dark nodes/edges and unannotated or missing ones as light gray nodes/edges, enabling flagging of missing reactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target organism already has a fully populated, literature-curated genome-scale metabolic model (e.g., a BiGG model) that requires no further gap-filling When the goal is pure genome annotation rather than metabolic network refinement, since MINNO is specifically designed for metabolomics-driven network editing

skills.search_text: regex-based-non-lipid-name-normalization Use when a putative metabolite annotation table contains compound names that fail lipid parsing (Goslin) but still need standardized abbreviations so that redundant or equivalent entries can be collapsed. The compound name is a lipid that Goslin can parse — use the LMSD/Goslin abbreviation dictionary route instead of the fallback regexes The task is metabolite classification or adduct/feature scoring (Tagger or TPMetrics responsibilities), not annotation renaming and deduplication Annotations are already in standardized abbreviated form and the goal is only downstream pathway analysis on a cleaned table http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Applies REname's fallback regular expressions to derive well-formed abbreviated names for non-lipid compound annotations that the Goslin parser cannot handle, enabling grouping of isomers/equivalent compounds and redundant data removal in untargeted metabolomics annotation tables. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.952149

skills.description: Use when you have a registered 3D MSI volume with propagated anatomical atlas labels and need region-specific lipid enrichment tables (e.g. myelin lipids elevated in corpus callosum) from mass-spectrometry imaging data.
skills.name: region-specific-lipid-differential-analysis
skills.search_text: region-specific-lipid-differential-analysis Use when you have a registered 3D MSI volume with propagated anatomical atlas labels and need region-specific lipid enrichment tables (e.g. myelin lipids elevated in corpus callosum) from mass-spectrometry imaging data. Input is a single-cell (SCMS) dataset rather than a registered 3D tissue MSI volume — cross-annotation and regional differential analysis are designed for tissue-level spatial data. Data have not been registered to the atlas (e.g. raw reconstructed sections without propagated region labels) — regional pixel extraction and differential testing require anatomical labels. Goal is single-cell-to-tissue chemical mapping (cross-annotation) rather than region-level lipid enrichment testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Extracts lipid features from atlas-defined rat brain regions in the registered 3D MSI volume, annotates them via LIPID MAPS (±0.005 m/z), and performs log2 fold-change with FDR-adjusted Wilcoxon rank-sum testing to identify region-specific lipid enrichments. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Extracts lipid features from atlas-defined rat brain regions in the registered 3D MSI volume, annotates them via LIPID MAPS (±0.005 m/z), and performs log2 fold-change with FDR-adjusted Wilcoxon rank-sum testing to identify region-specific lipid enrichments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-cell (SCMS) dataset rather than a registered 3D tissue MSI volume — cross-annotation and regional differential analysis are designed for tissue-level spatial data. Data have not been registered to the atlas (e.g. raw reconstructed sections without propagated region labels) — regional pixel extraction and differential testing require anatomical labels. Goal is single-cell-to-tissue chemical mapping (cross-annotation) rather than region-level lipid enrichment testing.

skills.description: Use when an MSI composite/cluster image must be resampled to H&E image dimensions for co-registration and the interpolation algorithm choice (nearest, bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos) must be evaluated or justified.
skills.name: registration-resolution-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: registration-resolution-comparison-analysis Use when an MSI composite/cluster image must be resampled to H&E image dimensions for co-registration and the interpolation algorithm choice (nearest, bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos) must be evaluated or justified. The MSI image and H&E image already share the same dimensions, so no upsampling/resampling is needed before registration. The task is MSI pre-processing (peak picking, spectral normalization) rather than image-resolution alignment with histology. Registration quality is dominated by linear/non-linear transform estimation (Figure S7 workflow) rather than by the interpolation kernel choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Systematic comparison of the four image interpolation algorithms supported by MSIght (bilinear, bicubic, nearest neighbor, and Lanczos) for upscaling a low-resolution MSI composite cluster image to match H&E image dimensions before co-registration, reproducing the quality/speed ordering shown in Figure S5. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Systematic comparison of the four image interpolation algorithms supported by MSIght (bilinear, bicubic, nearest neighbor, and Lanczos) for upscaling a low-resolution MSI composite cluster image to match H&E image dimensions before co-registration, reproducing the quality/speed ordering shown in Figure S5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MSI image and H&E image already share the same dimensions, so no upsampling/resampling is needed before registration. The task is MSI pre-processing (peak picking, spectral normalization) rather than image-resolution alignment with histology. Registration quality is dominated by linear/non-linear transform estimation (Figure S7 workflow) rather than by the interpolation kernel choice.

skills.description: Use when a log2-scaled metabolomics matrix (samples as rows, batch labels in the first column) has been corrected by multiple batch-effect models and you need a quantitative, comparable metric of residual metabolite-vs-batch association to select the model.
skills.name: regression-adjusted-r2-batch-association-scoring
skills.search_text: regression-adjusted-r2-batch-association-scoring Use when a log2-scaled metabolomics matrix (samples as rows, batch labels in the first column) has been corrected by multiple batch-effect models and you need a quantitative, comparable metric of residual metabolite-vs-batch association to select the model. Datasets with more than ~2000 features (variables) — dbnormSCORE is suggested for less than 2000 features for better computational speed Input data are not normalized/log2-scaled — the README requires data to be scaled on log2 before upload The goal is exploratory visualization (PCA, PDF/violin plots per metabolite) rather than quantitative model comparison — use Visodbnorm or ProfPlot* functions instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Scores batch-effect correction performance by regressing each metabolite's intensity on batch level and taking the maximum adjusted-R² (dbnormSCORE, 0–1 scale), enabling direct comparison of lowess, ber, bagging ber, and parametric/nonparametric ComBat on log2-transformed metabolomics matrices. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-021-84824-3
skills.summary: Scores batch-effect correction performance by regressing each metabolite's intensity on batch level and taking the maximum adjusted-R² (dbnormSCORE, 0–1 scale), enabling direct comparison of lowess, ber, bagging ber, and parametric/nonparametric ComBat on log2-transformed metabolomics matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with more than ~2000 features (variables) — dbnormSCORE is suggested for less than 2000 features for better computational speed Input data are not normalized/log2-scaled — the README requires data to be scaled on log2 before upload The goal is exploratory visualization (PCA, PDF/violin plots per metabolite) rather than quantitative model comparison — use Visodbnorm or ProfPlot* functions instead

skills.summary: Simulates pooled-QC sample data for a feature/sample intensity matrix (metabolomics or proteomics) using pseudoQC's four machine learning-based regression methods, then uses the simulated QC data to drive correction and normalization of the original dataset. Motivated by pseudoQC's finding that nonlinear regression methods outperform linear ones for this correction/normalization task.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already contains actual pooled-QC samples, so QC data need not be simulated The input is raw instrument output rather than a feature/sample intensity matrix (pseudoQC takes actual metabolomics and proteomics datasets as feature/sample matrices) The analysis goal does not involve correction or normalization driven by QC sample data

skills.description: Use when you have an MZmine full-scan MS1 feature table (.
skills.name: regression-based-ion-filtering
skills.search_text: regression-based-ion-filtering Use when you have an MZmine full-scan MS1 feature table (. Input is already an MS/MS-only feature table or spectra list rather than a full-scan MS1 feature table exported from MZmine - RegFilter filters full-scan-mode feature tables. You need unsupervised statistical filtering of multiple sample groups/conditions rather than ion selection for targeted re-injection; RegFilter is a semi-automated linear-regression filter over XIC points, not a general feature-differential-analysis tool. Data have not been preprocessed by MZmine (or an equivalent aligner exporting the expected CSV columns), so no aligned feature table with row ID/m/z/RT/peak area exists to filter. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 RegFilter is a semi-automated feature selection package that runs a linear regression filter over MZmine-derived full-scan MS1 feature tables, selecting ions with R2 >= 0.9 and a negative slope so that biological signals missed in DDA fragmentation can be rationally targeted. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: RegFilter is a semi-automated feature selection package that runs a linear regression filter over MZmine-derived full-scan MS1 feature tables, selecting ions with R2 >= 0.9 and a negative slope so that biological signals missed in DDA fragmentation can be rationally targeted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an MS/MS-only feature table or spectra list rather than a full-scan MS1 feature table exported from MZmine - RegFilter filters full-scan-mode feature tables. You need unsupervised statistical filtering of multiple sample groups/conditions rather than ion selection for targeted re-injection; RegFilter is a semi-automated linear-regression filter over XIC points, not a general feature-differential-analysis tool. Data have not been preprocessed by MZmine (or an equivalent aligner exporting the expected CSV columns), so no aligned feature table with row ID/m/z/RT/peak area exists to filter.

skills.description: Use when a fitted metabolite-pathway regression in Lilikoi v2.0 must be documented as a coefficient table with significance calls (P < 0.05) for metabolites mapped to a selected pathway.
skills.name: regression-coefficient-reporting
skills.search_text: regression-coefficient-reporting Use when a fitted metabolite-pathway regression in Lilikoi v2.0 must be documented as a coefficient table with significance calls (P < 0.05) for metabolites mapped to a selected pathway. The goal is disease classification or feature selection — use Lilikoi's classification predictor or featuresSelection modules instead, since regression reporting assumes a pathway set has already been selected. The goal is prognosis modeling — Lilikoi v2.0 handles survival via the Cox-PH and Cox-nnet models (lilikoi.prognosis), not the metabolite-pathway regression module. skills.description: Use when you need to attribute normalization performance to individual components of a multi-term adversarial loss (e.g. RALPS's d_lambda, g_lambda, v_lambda) via scenario-based ablation with fixed shared hyperparameters.
skills.name: regularization-coefficient-ablation-study
skills.search_text: regularization-coefficient-ablation-study Use when you need to attribute normalization performance to individual components of a multi-term adversarial loss (e.g. RALPS's d_lambda, g_lambda, v_lambda) via scenario-based ablation with fixed shared hyperparameters. The goal is to compare RALPS against other batch-correction methods rather than dissect its internal loss terms The dataset is single-batch, so no interbatch harmonization or reference-sample-based ablation is meaningful You only need a final normalized table and cannot afford the 4x randomized grid search training cost (~5.82 minutes per 30-epoch run per scenario) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the RALPS loss-term ablation (Figure 4a) by running the normalization pipeline in four configurations that vary d_lambda, g_lambda and v_lambda from all-zero to all-active, then comparing clustering, replicate cross-correlation and batch VC criteria to show the three terms act synergistically. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096

skills.description: Use when estimating a DNEA partial-correlation network for two experimental metabolomics groups and you need per-edge regularization weighting derived from stability-selection probabilities rather than a single global lambda.
skills.name: regularization-parameter-edge-weighting
skills.search_text: regularization-parameter-edge-weighting Use when estimating a DNEA partial-correlation network for two experimental metabolomics groups and you need per-edge regularization weighting derived from stability-selection probabilities rather than a single global lambda. When stability selection was run without subsampling on severely unbalanced groups — the Filigree subsampling protocol is required to equalize group representation (e.g. 50 DM:case vs 272 DM:control samples) When lambda has not yet been tuned — the weighting multiplies the BIC-optimized lambda, so it cannot replace the BICtune() tuning step, which itself requires ~500 or more samples per group When analyzing a single group — DNEA performs joint network estimation across two experimental conditions, and this weighting scheme is defined in that two-group workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Computes per-edge selection probabilities via stability selection in the DNEA R package and converts them into an edge-specific regularization weight rho = lambda * (1/(1e-04 + selection.probability)) for final GGM network estimation. This suppresses unstable metabolite-metabolite interactions when features outnumber samples (p >> n). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Computes per-edge selection probabilities via stability selection in the DNEA R package and converts them into an edge-specific regularization weight rho = lambda * (1/(1e-04 + selection.probability)) for final GGM network estimation. This suppresses unstable metabolite-metabolite interactions when features outnumber samples (p >> n).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When stability selection was run without subsampling on severely unbalanced groups — the Filigree subsampling protocol is required to equalize group representation (e.g. 50 DM:case vs 272 DM:control samples) When lambda has not yet been tuned — the weighting multiplies the BIC-optimized lambda, so it cannot replace the BICtune() tuning step, which itself requires ~500 or more samples per group When analyzing a single group — DNEA performs joint network estimation across two experimental conditions, and this weighting scheme is defined in that two-group workflow

skills.description: Use when a pathway's connectivity is sparse or disjoint and you need a regularized graph representation for a kernel machine score test on metabolomics associations.
skills.name: regularized-normalized-laplacian-standardization
skills.search_text: regularized-normalized-laplacian-standardization Use when a pathway's connectivity is sparse or disjoint and you need a regularized graph representation for a kernel machine score test on metabolomics associations. The pathway graph is already dense and well-connected (the regularization targets sparse connectivity and disjoint pathways; in simulations the plain normalized Laplacian actually hindered performance on disconnected graphs compared with PaIRKAT or ignoring pathway information). You have not examined the graph structure yet — the paper explicitly says it is important to examine the structure of a graph before applying a regularization step. The study cohort is large enough that p-values are indistinguishable between methods (the paper notes differences were only demonstrable on random subsets of 100–500 subjects from datasets with over 1,000 observations). http://edamontology.org/topic_3396 http://edamontology.org/topic_0611 PaIRKAT's graph-kernel regularization step: form the normalized graph Laplacian from a pathway's adjacency matrix and apply a regularization kernel that dampens noisy graph components while preserving biologically relevant structure for pathway association tests. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: PaIRKAT's graph-kernel regularization step: form the normalized graph Laplacian from a pathway's adjacency matrix and apply a regularization kernel that dampens noisy graph components while preserving biologically relevant structure for pathway association tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway graph is already dense and well-connected (the regularization targets sparse connectivity and disjoint pathways; in simulations the plain normalized Laplacian actually hindered performance on disconnected graphs compared with PaIRKAT or ignoring pathway information). You have not examined the graph structure yet — the paper explicitly says it is important to examine the structure of a graph before applying a regularization step. The study cohort is large enough that p-values are indistinguishable between methods (the paper notes differences were only demonstrable on random subsets of 100–500 subjects from datasets with over 1,000 observations).

skills.description: Use when benchmarking CAMI-style taxonomic profiles where single-value metrics (F1 score, L1 norm, UniFrac) look equivalent across profilers, and you need to see which clades at class/phylum rank drive abundance differences versus ground truth.
skills.name: relative-abundance-comparison-across-profilers
skills.search_text: relative-abundance-comparison-across-profilers Use when benchmarking CAMI-style taxonomic profiles where single-value metrics (F1 score, L1 norm, UniFrac) look equivalent across profilers, and you need to see which clades at class/phylum rank drive abundance differences versus ground truth. Input is raw reads or assemblies rather than standardized taxonomic profile files — TAMPA consumes profiler profiles plus the NCBI taxdump, not sequencing data. The analysis targets amplicon microbial datasets; the paper notes metacoder serves amplicon data, while TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles. Only an overall accuracy ranking is needed (e.g., a single F1 score) with no need to inspect which clades contribute to the metric values. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Compares percentage relative abundances of taxonomic profiler outputs (e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample) against a gold-standard profile using TAMPA, which renders the comparison on an ete3 taxonomic tree so clade-level differences missed by single-value metrics like the F1 score become visible. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Compares percentage relative abundances of taxonomic profiler outputs (e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample) against a gold-standard profile using TAMPA, which renders the comparison on an ete3 taxonomic tree so clade-level differences missed by single-value metrics like the F1 score become visible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or assemblies rather than standardized taxonomic profile files — TAMPA consumes profiler profiles plus the NCBI taxdump, not sequencing data. The analysis targets amplicon microbial datasets; the paper notes metacoder serves amplicon data, while TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles. Only an overall accuracy ranking is needed (e.g., a single F1 score) with no need to inspect which clades contribute to the metric values.

skills.search_text: relative-abundance-normalization Use when comparing raw taxonomic profiler profile files (e.g., CAMI profile_submissions and gold-standard profiles) whose relative abundances must be recomputed against the NCBI taxdump before ranking tools by error metrics like the L1 norm. Data is amplicon-based rather than WGS metagenomic — the article notes metacoder 'is not designed for WGS metagenomic analyses', and TAMPA targets WGS profiler outputs Profiles are already normalized percentages summing to one, so the -n flag would be redundant or distort comparison Only a single profiler's output exists with no ground-truth or second profile to compare abundances against http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Normalizes taxonomic profiler outputs into percentage relative abundances per taxon using TAMPA, so that node weights across MetaPhyler, mOTU, Taxy-Pro and ground-truth CAMI profiles are comparable and sum to one before metric computation (e.g., L1 error). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Normalizes taxonomic profiler outputs into percentage relative abundances per taxon using TAMPA, so that node weights across MetaPhyler, mOTU, Taxy-Pro and ground-truth CAMI profiles are comparable and sum to one before metric computation (e.g., L1 error).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is amplicon-based rather than WGS metagenomic — the article notes metacoder 'is not designed for WGS metagenomic analyses', and TAMPA targets WGS profiler outputs Profiles are already normalized percentages summing to one, so the -n flag would be redundant or distort comparison Only a single profiler's output exists with no ground-truth or second profile to compare abundances against

skills.description: Use when a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table includes solvent blank or media blank sample groups and features overrepresented in those blanks (e.g. carryover) must be identified and removed before downstream analysis.
skills.name: relative-abundance-threshold-background-removal
skills.search_text: relative-abundance-threshold-background-removal Use when a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table includes solvent blank or media blank sample groups and features overrepresented in those blanks (e.g. carryover) must be identified and removed before downstream analysis. The samples lack blank/background control groups (e.g. no solvent blanks or media blanks), so there is no group against which to threshold abundance. The goal is a different QC issue mpactr handles with its own filters: mispicked isotopic patterns (filter_mispicked_ions), non-reproducible features across technical replicates (filter_cv), or in-source fragment ions (filter_insource_ions). Input is raw tandem MS/MS data rather than a pre-processed peak table importable via import_data(). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies mpactr's filter_group() to identify background components — features whose abundance exceeds a user-defined relative-abundance threshold in a specified sample group — and remove them, e.g. solvent blank impurities causing carryover and contamination in LC-MS/MS peak tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00997-24
skills.summary: Applies mpactr's filter_group() to identify background components — features whose abundance exceeds a user-defined relative-abundance threshold in a specified sample group — and remove them, e.g. solvent blank impurities causing carryover and contamination in LC-MS/MS peak tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples lack blank/background control groups (e.g. no solvent blanks or media blanks), so there is no group against which to threshold abundance. The goal is a different QC issue mpactr handles with its own filters: mispicked isotopic patterns (filter_mispicked_ions), non-reproducible features across technical replicates (filter_cv), or in-source fragment ions (filter_insource_ions). Input is raw tandem MS/MS data rather than a pre-processed peak table importable via import_data().

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an inference method like MetaboPAC that needs ground-truth absolute concentrations — simulate relative-abundance time-course GC-MS-style data from a known metabolic model with controlled noise, sampling frequency, and response-factor distributions.
skills.name: relative-abundance-time-course-data-simulation
skills.search_text: relative-abundance-time-course-data-simulation Use when benchmarking an inference method like MetaboPAC that needs ground-truth absolute concentrations — simulate relative-abundance time-course GC-MS-style data from a known metabolic model with controlled noise, sampling frequency, and response-factor distributions. MetaboPAC's own scope is intracellular, single-compartment systems with all metabolites connected via reactions — eukaryotic transport reactions across intracellular compartments are not modeled, so such systems should not be simulated with these scripts Do not use these simulation scripts when the goal is processing real experimental GC-MS/LC-MS data rather than in silico benchmarking with known ground truth Assumes response factors constant with concentration; if the target system exhibits nonlinear response or ion suppression effects, simulated data will not capture that behavior http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates in silico noiseless and noise-added relative-abundance time-course metabolomics datasets from known metabolic systems with randomly sampled true response factors, providing ground truth to benchmark MetaboPAC's standard-free absolute-concentration inference. README-based: MATLAB scripts and generated .mat datasets. All steps, files, and parameters are grounded in the README and article methods; EDAM operation inferred conservatively from simulation context. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Generates in silico noiseless and noise-added relative-abundance time-course metabolomics datasets from known metabolic systems with randomly sampled true response factors, providing ground truth to benchmark MetaboPAC's standard-free absolute-concentration inference. README-based: MATLAB scripts and generated .mat datasets. All steps, files, and parameters are grounded in the README and article methods; EDAM operation inferred conservatively from simulation context.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MetaboPAC's own scope is intracellular, single-compartment systems with all metabolites connected via reactions — eukaryotic transport reactions across intracellular compartments are not modeled, so such systems should not be simulated with these scripts Do not use these simulation scripts when the goal is processing real experimental GC-MS/LC-MS data rather than in silico benchmarking with known ground truth Assumes response factors constant with concentration; if the target system exhibits nonlinear response or ion suppression effects, simulated data will not capture that behavior

skills.description: Use when building a pathway-metabolite interaction network from significant metabolites and you need to rank hub metabolites (e.g. pyruvate, pyruvic acid, arachidonic acid) by normalized centrality rather than raw betweenness values.
skills.name: relative-betweenness-normalization
skills.search_text: relative-betweenness-normalization Use when building a pathway-metabolite interaction network from significant metabolites and you need to rank hub metabolites (e.g. pyruvate, pyruvic acid, arachidonic acid) by normalized centrality rather than raw betweenness values. The task is raw pathway over-representation significance (Fisher's exact test / Enrichment_Ratio) rather than hub identification - centrality normalization is not part of that statistic. The network topology itself is not built yet and no betweenness values exist; this skill assumes a precomputed igraph metabolite-pathway network. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Normalizes igraph betweenness centrality of metabolite nodes to Relative Betweenness Centrality (RBC) by dividing each metabolite's betweenness by the maximum betweenness in the network, so hub metabolites in a KEGG pathway-metabolite network can be ranked on a comparable 0-1 scale. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Normalizes igraph betweenness centrality of metabolite nodes to Relative Betweenness Centrality (RBC) by dividing each metabolite's betweenness by the maximum betweenness in the network, so hub metabolites in a KEGG pathway-metabolite network can be ranked on a comparable 0-1 scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is raw pathway over-representation significance (Fisher's exact test / Enrichment_Ratio) rather than hub identification - centrality normalization is not part of that statistic. The network topology itself is not built yet and no betweenness values exist; this skill assumes a precomputed igraph metabolite-pathway network.
