skills.name: relative-intensity-noise-thresholding
skills.search_text: relative-intensity-noise-thresholding Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum (e.g. from an Orbitrap instrument, .msp format) contains co-occurring 'grass' electronic noise ions that must be removed before precursor-formula-dependent chemical denoising or spectral matching. The noise is chemical rather than electronic — fragments whose masses cannot be explained by chemically plausible subformula losses from the precursor require the formula_denoising step and precursor molecular-formula information, not this intensity-based rule The spectrum was acquired on a non-Orbitrap mass analyzer — the threshold was empirically derived from NIST23 Orbitrap MS/MS spectra and adapting it to other mass analyzers requires retuning and validating parameters The noise pattern is not characterized by more than four co-occurring near-identical-intensity ions (e.g. sparse isolated noise peaks), which this rule will not flag An empirical, intensity-independent rule for removing electronic ('grass') noise ions from raw MS/MS spectra: any group of more than four ions with nearly identical relative intensities (within ±0.1%) is flagged as electronic noise and removed. This is the electronic_denoising step of the Spectral Denoising algorithm, derived by probing 230,000 Orbitrap MS/MS spectra in the NIST23 library. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: An empirical, intensity-independent rule for removing electronic ('grass') noise ions from raw MS/MS spectra: any group of more than four ions with nearly identical relative intensities (within ±0.1%) is flagged as electronic noise and removed. This is the electronic_denoising step of the Spectral Denoising algorithm, derived by probing 230,000 Orbitrap MS/MS spectra in the NIST23 library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The noise is chemical rather than electronic — fragments whose masses cannot be explained by chemically plausible subformula losses from the precursor require the formula_denoising step and precursor molecular-formula information, not this intensity-based rule The spectrum was acquired on a non-Orbitrap mass analyzer — the threshold was empirically derived from NIST23 Orbitrap MS/MS spectra and adapting it to other mass analyzers requires retuning and validating parameters The noise pattern is not characterized by more than four co-occurring near-identical-intensity ions (e.g. sparse isolated noise peaks), which this rule will not flag

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra from MSP files must be de-noised before model input, e.g. dropping peaks with intensity below 1% of the base peak while retaining precursor-mass-window consistency.
skills.name: relative-intensity-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: relative-intensity-threshold-filtering Use when raw MS/MS spectra from MSP files must be de-noised before model input, e.g. dropping peaks with intensity below 1% of the base peak while retaining precursor-mass-window consistency. Input spectra are already binarized/merged (ChemEmbed's merged collision-energy spectra binarize intensities, so a relative-intensity ranking no longer exists) Input is already a filtered peak list or model-ready tensor produced by a previous preprocessing run The goal is candidate retrieval rather than noise removal — precursor tolerance filtering (--precursor_tolerance_ppm) is the relevant mechanism there http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A per-spectrum noise-filtering step for raw MS/MS spectra that drops any fragment peak whose intensity is below 1% of the spectrum's most intense (base) peak, keeping only signals above the noise floor before model input. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.02.07.637102
skills.summary: A per-spectrum noise-filtering step for raw MS/MS spectra that drops any fragment peak whose intensity is below 1% of the spectrum's most intense (base) peak, keeping only signals above the noise floor before model input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are already binarized/merged (ChemEmbed's merged collision-energy spectra binarize intensities, so a relative-intensity ranking no longer exists) Input is already a filtered peak list or model-ready tensor produced by a previous preprocessing run The goal is candidate retrieval rather than noise removal — precursor tolerance filtering (--precursor_tolerance_ppm) is the relevant mechanism there

skills.description: Use when you have per-simulation NRMSE or PFC error tables for missForest and compared imputation methods across datasets that differ in variable-type composition (continuous-only, categorical-only, mixed) and in artificially introduced missingness, and you need to locate where the largest.
skills.name: relative-performance-stratification-by-variable-type
skills.search_text: relative-performance-stratification-by-variable-type Use when you have per-simulation NRMSE or PFC error tables for missForest and compared imputation methods across datasets that differ in variable-type composition (continuous-only, categorical-only, mixed) and in artificially introduced missingness, and you need to locate where the largest. The comparison is a single dataset with only one variable type and one missingness level — no stratification by variable-type composition is possible Only missForest's own out-of-bag error estimates are available; the skill requires per-simulation error rates from at least one compared baseline method Missing values are not MCAR (the article's evaluation introduced 10–30% of values completely at random), so relative gains may not transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmark-analysis skill that computes missForest's relative imputation-error reduction over the strongest baseline (KNNimpute/MissPALasso for continuous data; MICE/dummy-coded KNNimpute for categorical and mixed data) and stratifies those gains by variable-type composition and missingness proportion (10–30% MCAR). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btr597
skills.summary: A benchmark-analysis skill that computes missForest's relative imputation-error reduction over the strongest baseline (KNNimpute/MissPALasso for continuous data; MICE/dummy-coded KNNimpute for categorical and mixed data) and stratifies those gains by variable-type composition and missingness proportion (10–30% MCAR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison is a single dataset with only one variable type and one missingness level — no stratification by variable-type composition is possible Only missForest's own out-of-bag error estimates are available; the skill requires per-simulation error rates from at least one compared baseline method Missing values are not MCAR (the article's evaluation introduced 10–30% of values completely at random), so relative gains may not transfer

skills.description: Use when LC-MS/MS lipidomics annotations from MS2 library search contain false positives, and chromatographic retention-order information (relative RT across lipid subclasses) is available to filter or extend them.
skills.name: relative-retention-time-classification
skills.search_text: relative-retention-time-classification Use when LC-MS/MS lipidomics annotations from MS2 library search contain false positives, and chromatographic retention-order information (relative RT across lipid subclasses) is available to filter or extend them. Direct-infusion or non-chromatographic MS/MS data — relative retention time rules require aligned LC retention orders and cannot be applied Raw spectra not yet searched against a library — RT classification is a downstream filter/predictor, not an MS2 search step (run EQ/MS2 library search first) Tasks needing exact C=C positional isomer localization by orthogonal chemistry — that requires Paternò–Büchi (PB) derivatization and the PB spectral library, not LCI RT rules http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Applies LipidIN's LCI (lipid categories intelligence) module — three relative retention time rules driven by a best-first search heuristic over predicted lipid subclasses — to remove false positive MS2 annotations and predict unannotated lipids, achieving an estimated ~5.7% false discovery rate across 8,923 lipids. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Applies LipidIN's LCI (lipid categories intelligence) module — three relative retention time rules driven by a best-first search heuristic over predicted lipid subclasses — to remove false positive MS2 annotations and predict unannotated lipids, achieving an estimated ~5.7% false discovery rate across 8,923 lipids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Direct-infusion or non-chromatographic MS/MS data — relative retention time rules require aligned LC retention orders and cannot be applied Raw spectra not yet searched against a library — RT classification is a downstream filter/predictor, not an MS2 search step (run EQ/MS2 library search first) Tasks needing exact C=C positional isomer localization by orthogonal chemistry — that requires Paternò–Büchi (PB) derivatization and the PB spectral library, not LCI RT rules

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify residual intensity drift in LC/MS untargeted metabolomics after normalization, by computing per-feature RSD across withheld QC sample injections on a multi-sample feature matrix.
skills.name: relative-standard-deviation-qc-metrics
skills.search_text: relative-standard-deviation-qc-metrics Use when you need to quantify residual intensity drift in LC/MS untargeted metabolomics after normalization, by computing per-feature RSD across withheld QC sample injections on a multi-sample feature matrix. Your dataset already has a standardized QC sample scheme that normalizes drift correction internally (i.e., the paper notes public repositories often lack standardized QC samples, so this comparison only makes sense when QC samples are absent or withheld) You want to evaluate signal detection (TP/FP rates) rather than post-normalization intensity stability — use mzLearn detection benchmarks instead The input is already a pre-normalized, low-RSD feature table and you are not comparing multiple normalization treatments http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes relative standard deviation (RSD/CV×100) of ion-feature intensities across hidden QC injections to benchmark drift-correction quality of normalization treatments such as synthetic QC, experimental QC, TIC, and raw intensities on mzLearn feature matrices. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Computes relative standard deviation (RSD/CV×100) of ion-feature intensities across hidden QC injections to benchmark drift-correction quality of normalization treatments such as synthetic QC, experimental QC, TIC, and raw intensities on mzLearn feature matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your dataset already has a standardized QC sample scheme that normalizes drift correction internally (i.e., the paper notes public repositories often lack standardized QC samples, so this comparison only makes sense when QC samples are absent or withheld) You want to evaluate signal detection (TP/FP rates) rather than post-normalization intensity stability — use mzLearn detection benchmarks instead The input is already a pre-normalized, low-RSD feature table and you are not comparing multiple normalization treatments

skills.description: Use when you have raw or signal-drift-corrected LC/GC-MS metabolomics or proteomics feature tables with repeated pooled QC injections and need a quantitative precision metric (e.g. % peaks within 15% or 30% RSD) to judge correction performance.
skills.name: relative-standard-deviation-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: relative-standard-deviation-quality-assessment Use when you have raw or signal-drift-corrected LC/GC-MS metabolomics or proteomics feature tables with repeated pooled QC injections and need a quantitative precision metric (e.g. % peaks within 15% or 30% RSD) to judge correction performance. Datasets without repeated pooled QC injections throughout the batch — RSD across QCs is undefined and other QC-free assessment (e.g. statTarget shiftCor_dQC with Combat) is required instead. When the goal is differential-abundance or biological interpretation rather than quantifying technical precision — RSD on pooled QCs measures drift correction quality, not biological effect. Single-batch data where drift is negligible; the metric adds little value when raw QC RSD is already low. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes relative standard deviation (RSD) distributions of pooled-QC peak intensities across a batch to quantify drift-correction quality in LC/GC-MS metabolomics and proteomics feature tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Computes relative standard deviation (RSD) distributions of pooled-QC peak intensities across a batch to quantify drift-correction quality in LC/GC-MS metabolomics and proteomics feature tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets without repeated pooled QC injections throughout the batch — RSD across QCs is undefined and other QC-free assessment (e.g. statTarget shiftCor_dQC with Combat) is required instead. When the goal is differential-abundance or biological interpretation rather than quantifying technical precision — RSD on pooled QCs measures drift correction quality, not biological effect. Single-batch data where drift is negligible; the metric adds little value when raw QC RSD is already low.

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed ionome dataset (line-aggregated z-score ion profiles from ICP-MS, e.g. 14 ions across yeast knockout mutants) needs element-element correlation network analysis.
skills.name: relevance-network-extraction
skills.search_text: relevance-network-extraction Use when a pre-processed ionome dataset (line-aggregated z-score ion profiles from ICP-MS, e.g. 14 ions across yeast knockout mutants) needs element-element correlation network analysis. Input is raw ICP-MS concentration data that has not passed the IonFlow pre-processing section (outlier detection, log transform, median batch correction) — the README states pre-processing 'produces in output the cleaned dataset to be used in the other sections' The analysis goal is gene set enrichment / GO Slim annotation rather than element-element correlation network structure The data are not element (or analogous metabolite) concentration profiles, since IonFlow's relevance network is defined over measured ions in an ionome dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Extracts an element-element relevance network from a pre-processed ionome dataset by correlating ion profiles and linking pairs whose correlation exceeds a user-specified threshold, as implemented in the IonAnalysis section of the IonFlow Galaxy/R tool. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-021-01841-z
skills.summary: Extracts an element-element relevance network from a pre-processed ionome dataset by correlating ion profiles and linking pairs whose correlation exceeds a user-specified threshold, as implemented in the IonAnalysis section of the IonFlow Galaxy/R tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ICP-MS concentration data that has not passed the IonFlow pre-processing section (outlier detection, log transform, median batch correction) — the README states pre-processing 'produces in output the cleaned dataset to be used in the other sections' The analysis goal is gene set enrichment / GO Slim annotation rather than element-element correlation network structure The data are not element (or analogous metabolite) concentration profiles, since IonFlow's relevance network is defined over measured ions in an ionome dataset

skills.description: Use when projected surrogate scores (e.g. 'high hscrp') from Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics must be checked for calibration against binarized phenotypes, using reliability diagrams plus ECE/MCE and log-loss deltas.
skills.name: reliability-diagram-construction
skills.search_text: reliability-diagram-construction Use when projected surrogate scores (e.g. 'high hscrp') from Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics must be checked for calibration against binarized phenotypes, using reliability diagrams plus ECE/MCE and log-loss deltas. The dataset lacks the required Nightingale metabolite columns — the surrogate scores (and hence calibration curves) cannot be computed until the upload passes the metabolite-presence check No binarized phenotype ground truth is available for the surrogate of interest, since Platt calibration and reliability diagrams require actual 0/1 labels The goal is regression calibration of continuous outcomes (e.g. MetaboAge), not calibration of probabilistic surrogate scores http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Construction of reliability diagrams to visually assess calibration of MiMIR metabolic surrogate scores, paired with ECE/MCE/log-loss statistics computed on a 20% holdout after fitting Platt calibration on an 80% calibration subset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac388
skills.summary: Construction of reliability diagrams to visually assess calibration of MiMIR metabolic surrogate scores, paired with ECE/MCE/log-loss statistics computed on a 20% holdout after fitting Platt calibration on an 80% calibration subset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks the required Nightingale metabolite columns — the surrogate scores (and hence calibration curves) cannot be computed until the upload passes the metabolite-presence check No binarized phenotype ground truth is available for the surrogate of interest, since Platt calibration and reliability diagrams require actual 0/1 labels The goal is regression calibration of continuous outcomes (e.g. MetaboAge), not calibration of probabilistic surrogate scores

skills.description: Use when comparing normalization methods on metabolomics abundance data by supervised classification performance — e.g. predicting hypertension status from BioHEART-CT plasma metabolite abundances — where a repeated, averaged CV accuracy estimate is needed per method.
skills.name: repeated-cross-validation-accuracy-estimation
skills.search_text: repeated-cross-validation-accuracy-estimation Use when comparing normalization methods on metabolomics abundance data by supervised classification performance — e.g. predicting hypertension status from BioHEART-CT plasma metabolite abundances — where a repeated, averaged CV accuracy estimate is needed per method. Data have not yet been normalized — this skill evaluates normalized matrices, so normalization (e.g. hRUV variants) must be applied first The outcome variable is not a binary clinical label such as hypertension status — other endpoints need their own classifier and validation design The goal is assessing replicate variability or signal-drift removal itself rather than retention of biological signal via classification Estimates supervised classification accuracy of normalized metabolomics abundance matrices by training an SVM to predict hypertension status over 30 repeats of 10-fold cross-validation, used to benchmark normalization methods (e.g. hRUV variants vs ratio, SVR, SERRF, RLSC) on retention of biological signal. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Estimates supervised classification accuracy of normalized metabolomics abundance matrices by training an SVM to predict hypertension status over 30 repeats of 10-fold cross-validation, used to benchmark normalization methods (e.g. hRUV variants vs ratio, SVR, SERRF, RLSC) on retention of biological signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data have not yet been normalized — this skill evaluates normalized matrices, so normalization (e.g. hRUV variants) must be applied first The outcome variable is not a binary clinical label such as hypertension status — other endpoints need their own classifier and validation design The goal is assessing replicate variability or signal-drift removal itself rather than retention of biological signal via classification

skills.description: Use when a labeled metabolomics or other small-n feature matrix must be benchmarked across several classifiers, and a stable estimate of held-out performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1) under repeated k-fold cross-validation is needed.
skills.name: repeated-cross-validation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: repeated-cross-validation-benchmarking Use when a labeled metabolomics or other small-n feature matrix must be benchmarked across several classifiers, and a stable estimate of held-out performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1) under repeated k-fold cross-validation is needed. Input is unlabeled — no class labels exist, so a supervised 4:1 split with cross-validated classification benchmark cannot be performed (use the prognosis/Cox-nnet module instead) The dataset is too small to sustain a 20% held-out test set with 10-fold CV repeated 10 times without unstable metric estimates The goal is pathway analysis or metabolite-pathway regression rather than comparing classifier performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark multiple classifiers (deep learning plus LDA, SVM, RF, RPART, LOG, GBM) on a metabolomics dataset using a 4:1 train/test split with 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, and compare held-out accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1. This mirrors the Lilikoi v2.0 ER status classification benchmark on the Charité breast cancer metabolomics dataset (204 ER+ vs 67 ER−, 271 samples × 162 metabolites). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa162
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple classifiers (deep learning plus LDA, SVM, RF, RPART, LOG, GBM) on a metabolomics dataset using a 4:1 train/test split with 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, and compare held-out accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1. This mirrors the Lilikoi v2.0 ER status classification benchmark on the Charité breast cancer metabolomics dataset (204 ER+ vs 67 ER−, 271 samples × 162 metabolites).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unlabeled — no class labels exist, so a supervised 4:1 split with cross-validated classification benchmark cannot be performed (use the prognosis/Cox-nnet module instead) The dataset is too small to sustain a 20% held-out test set with 10-fold CV repeated 10 times without unstable metric estimates The goal is pathway analysis or metabolite-pathway regression rather than comparing classifier performance

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed, imputed LC-MS metabolomics feature table (MetaboSet object) with a known class label (e.g. a 'group' column) is available and the goal is supervised ranking of molecular features into minimal-optimal vs. all-relevant subsets.
skills.name: repeated-double-cross-validation-variable-selection
skills.search_text: repeated-double-cross-validation-variable-selection Use when a preprocessed, imputed LC-MS metabolomics feature table (MetaboSet object) with a known class label (e.g. a 'group' column) is available and the goal is supervised ranking of molecular features into minimal-optimal vs. all-relevant subsets. The data are raw LC-MS files or an unprocessed peak table — notame's preprocessing (mark_nas, correct_drift, flagging, imputation) must run first No class label exists and the goal is unsupervised exploration rather than supervised variable selection You need only feature-wise univariate tests rather than multivariate prediction/variable-selection models http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Applies MUVR's repeated double cross-validation with random forest (RF) and PLS(-DA) models to a preprocessed, imputed MetaboSet object from the notame LC-MS workflow, yielding nested 'min', 'mid' and 'max' variable-selection sets that distinguish minimal-optimal from all-relevant molecular features. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135
skills.summary: Applies MUVR's repeated double cross-validation with random forest (RF) and PLS(-DA) models to a preprocessed, imputed MetaboSet object from the notame LC-MS workflow, yielding nested 'min', 'mid' and 'max' variable-selection sets that distinguish minimal-optimal from all-relevant molecular features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw LC-MS files or an unprocessed peak table — notame's preprocessing (mark_nas, correct_drift, flagging, imputation) must run first No class label exists and the goal is unsupervised exploration rather than supervised variable selection You need only feature-wise univariate tests rather than multivariate prediction/variable-selection models

skills.description: Use when a log2-transformed metabolomics data matrix must be split into paired training/test sets so prediction performance (accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity) can be estimated and averaged over multiple resampled partitions.
skills.name: repeated-kfold-cross-validation-splitting
skills.search_text: repeated-kfold-cross-validation-splitting Use when a log2-transformed metabolomics data matrix must be split into paired training/test sets so prediction performance (accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity) can be estimated and averaged over multiple resampled partitions. Input is raw MS data requiring pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) — split only after log2 transformation of the processed feature table A single hold-out split or leave-one-out design is specified by the study protocol instead of repeated k-fold resampling The dataset is being used only for unsupervised exploration (e.g., PCA separation of SAT and VAT), where train/test splitting is not needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Partitions a metabolomics dataset into training and test sets using repeated k-fold cross-validation (k = 4, repeated five times) via the R caret package, yielding 20 train/test groups at roughly 75%/25% splitting so that downstream PLS-DA model performance can be averaged over many partitions. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: Partitions a metabolomics dataset into training and test sets using repeated k-fold cross-validation (k = 4, repeated five times) via the R caret package, yielding 20 train/test groups at roughly 75%/25% splitting so that downstream PLS-DA model performance can be averaged over many partitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS data requiring pre-processing (noise reduction, peak matching, retention time correction) — split only after log2 transformation of the processed feature table A single hold-out split or leave-one-out design is specified by the study protocol instead of repeated k-fold resampling The dataset is being used only for unsupervised exploration (e.g., PCA separation of SAT and VAT), where train/test splitting is not needed

skills.description: Use when metabolomics values are measured repeatedly within the same subjects (e.g., venous vs arterial conditions or multiple time points) and the goal is to rank metabolites by ANOVA significance for feature selection.
skills.name: repeated-measures-anova-on-longitudinal-metabolomics
skills.search_text: repeated-measures-anova-on-longitudinal-metabolomics Use when metabolomics values are measured repeatedly within the same subjects (e.g., venous vs arterial conditions or multiple time points) and the goal is to rank metabolites by ANOVA significance for feature selection. Measurements are independent across groups rather than repeated within the same subjects — MeTEor also offers Mixed ANOVA, Linear Mixed Models, and the Friedman test for other designs The data is still in wide format with unaddressed missing values — first impute and convert to long format before running the ANOVA module The goal is binary classification rather than feature ranking — use MeTEor's prediction module (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs MeTEor's Repeated Measures ANOVA module to rank metabolites by significance for feature selection in longitudinal metabolomics data with within-subject measurements (e.g., venous vs arterial samples across COVID-19 time points), and compares the top hits against prior reported biomarkers. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae178
skills.summary: Runs MeTEor's Repeated Measures ANOVA module to rank metabolites by significance for feature selection in longitudinal metabolomics data with within-subject measurements (e.g., venous vs arterial samples across COVID-19 time points), and compares the top hits against prior reported biomarkers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Measurements are independent across groups rather than repeated within the same subjects — MeTEor also offers Mixed ANOVA, Linear Mixed Models, and the Friedman test for other designs The data is still in wide format with unaddressed missing values — first impute and convert to long format before running the ANOVA module The goal is binary classification rather than feature ranking — use MeTEor's prediction module (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost) instead

skills.description: Use when a labeled single-cell feature matrix (e.g., the SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv spatio-molecular matrix with 88 metabolite intensity columns and fluorescence-derived cell-type labels) must be scored with an honest accuracy estimate before claiming a prediction benchmark.
skills.name: repeated-stratified-cross-validation-evaluation
skills.search_text: repeated-stratified-cross-validation-evaluation Use when a labeled single-cell feature matrix (e.g., the SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv spatio-molecular matrix with 88 metabolite intensity columns and fluorescence-derived cell-type labels) must be scored with an honest accuracy estimate before claiming a prediction benchmark. The input is already a scored prediction or a per-fold metric table — no further model fitting or cross-validation is needed. The task is unsupervised (e.g., discovering metabolic states in dHepaRG hepatocytes by clustering), where no ground-truth labels exist for stratified evaluation. Labels cannot be derived from fluorescence channels (no mCherry/GFP distinction), so stratification would be meaningless. Evaluates a supervised classifier (e.g., LinearDiscriminantAnalysis on SpaceM single-cell metabolite intensities) using repeated stratified k-fold cross-validation with scikit-learn's RepeatedStratifiedKFold, to obtain a robust accuracy estimate such as the 91.3% HeLa vs NIH3T3 cell-type prediction reported for SpaceM. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: Evaluates a supervised classifier (e.g., LinearDiscriminantAnalysis on SpaceM single-cell metabolite intensities) using repeated stratified k-fold cross-validation with scikit-learn's RepeatedStratifiedKFold, to obtain a robust accuracy estimate such as the 91.3% HeLa vs NIH3T3 cell-type prediction reported for SpaceM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a scored prediction or a per-fold metric table — no further model fitting or cross-validation is needed. The task is unsupervised (e.g., discovering metabolic states in dHepaRG hepatocytes by clustering), where no ground-truth labels exist for stratified evaluation. Labels cannot be derived from fluorescence channels (no mCherry/GFP distinction), so stratification would be meaningless.

skills.description: Use when you must determine the minimum reference feature-list size (e.g. common feature groups between reference and target chromatograms) needed for reliable retention-time alignment, requiring systematic repetition of an alignment workflow across subsampled inputs.
skills.name: repetitive-alignment-batch-orchestration
skills.search_text: repetitive-alignment-batch-orchestration Use when you must determine the minimum reference feature-list size (e.g. common feature groups between reference and target chromatograms) needed for reliable retention-time alignment, requiring systematic repetition of an alignment workflow across subsampled inputs. You already know the reference feature list is complete and representative — a single alignment run suffices; subsampling orchestration would add cost without new information The target data are not processed LC-HRMS feature chromatograms with m/z and retention times, since MetMatch operates on such feature lists rather than raw spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Orchestrates many repeated MetMatch alignment runs over progressively subsampled reference feature lists (e.g. 20 list sizes × 10 repetitions = 200 runs) against LC-HRMS datafiles to quantify how reference-list size affects alignment robustness, aggregating per-run accuracy and F-measure into statistics like Figure 10. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo6040039
skills.summary: Orchestrates many repeated MetMatch alignment runs over progressively subsampled reference feature lists (e.g. 20 list sizes × 10 repetitions = 200 runs) against LC-HRMS datafiles to quantify how reference-list size affects alignment robustness, aggregating per-run accuracy and F-measure into statistics like Figure 10.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already know the reference feature list is complete and representative — a single alignment run suffices; subsampling orchestration would add cost without new information The target data are not processed LC-HRMS feature chromatograms with m/z and retention times, since MetMatch operates on such feature lists rather than raw spectra

skills.description: Use when replicate rank lists (e.g., the six SEQC RNA-seq replicate comparisons) must be reduced to per-gene average scores and ranks to test whether a reproducibility method's top-k sets are enriched for gold-standard genes such as the 1129 SEQC Taqman PCR transcripts.
skills.name: replicate-averaging-and-ranking-of-expression-measurements
skills.search_text: replicate-averaging-and-ranking-of-expression-measurements Use when replicate rank lists (e.g., the six SEQC RNA-seq replicate comparisons) must be reduced to per-gene average scores and ranks to test whether a reproducibility method's top-k sets are enriched for gold-standard genes such as the 1129 SEQC Taqman PCR transcripts. Input is raw sequencing data or un-ranked expression intensities rather than per-transcript replicate measurements that can be averaged and ranked There is only a single experiment (no replicate comparisons), since the skill evaluates overlap between replicate-derived top-k sets against PCR ranks The analysis goal is parametric modeling of between-replicate dependence; the MaRR framework is explicitly nonparametric and makes no parametric assumptions on dependence structures http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A validation workflow for the MaRR reproducibility procedure: technical replicates of expression measurements (e.g., four SEQC Taqman PCR replicates over 1129 transcripts) are averaged, converted to transcript ranks, and used to score the biological relevance of the top-k reproducible sets returned by MaRR versus the copula mixture model. metabolomics/v3 10.1080/01621459.2017.1397521
skills.summary: A validation workflow for the MaRR reproducibility procedure: technical replicates of expression measurements (e.g., four SEQC Taqman PCR replicates over 1129 transcripts) are averaged, converted to transcript ranks, and used to score the biological relevance of the top-k reproducible sets returned by MaRR versus the copula mixture model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or un-ranked expression intensities rather than per-transcript replicate measurements that can be averaged and ranked There is only a single experiment (no replicate comparisons), since the skill evaluates overlap between replicate-derived top-k sets against PCR ranks The analysis goal is parametric modeling of between-replicate dependence; the MaRR framework is explicitly nonparametric and makes no parametric assumptions on dependence structures

skills.description: Use when large-scale metabolomics batches contain embedded sample replicates (pooled QC, short replicates, batch replicates) and unwanted variation within and between batches must be estimated with RUV-III.
skills.name: replicate-based-unwanted-variation-estimation
skills.search_text: replicate-based-unwanted-variation-estimation Use when large-scale metabolomics batches contain embedded sample replicates (pooled QC, short replicates, batch replicates) and unwanted variation within and between batches must be estimated with RUV-III. Data contain missing values that cannot be imputed — hRUV expects data without missing values, which is often not possible in large-scale metabolomics data No inter-batch sample replicates are embedded, so between-batch variation cannot be estimated from replicate pairs Input is raw/unfiltered data — metabolites not present in at least 50% of samples must first be filtered out http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Estimates and removes unwanted variation in large-scale metabolomics data by embedding biological sample replicates (pooled QC, short within-row replicates, inter-batch replicates) and applying RUV-III hierarchically across batches (hRUV). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Estimates and removes unwanted variation in large-scale metabolomics data by embedding biological sample replicates (pooled QC, short within-row replicates, inter-batch replicates) and applying RUV-III hierarchically across batches (hRUV).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain missing values that cannot be imputed — hRUV expects data without missing values, which is often not possible in large-scale metabolomics data No inter-batch sample replicates are embedded, so between-batch variation cannot be estimated from replicate pairs Input is raw/unfiltered data — metabolites not present in at least 50% of samples must first be filtered out

skills.description: Use when comparing annotation counts between two LC-IM-MS replicate groups (e.g. original vs preprocessed MS-files) and you need a per-replicate consensus cutoff instead of per-file totals.
skills.name: replicate-consensus-annotation-filtering
skills.search_text: replicate-consensus-annotation-filtering Use when comparing annotation counts between two LC-IM-MS replicate groups (e.g. original vs preprocessed MS-files) and you need a per-replicate consensus cutoff instead of per-file totals. When the downstream tool already outputs a consensus feature table across replicates and per-file lists must not be re-filtered When the goal is a per-file (individual) annotation gain — that figure (41% ± 7%) is computed without the replicate-consensus cutoff and mixing the two bases invalidates the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Counts lipid annotations in consensus across replicates, using the Lipid Annotator rule that an MS1-level feature must be present in at least half the analyzed MS-files, and quantifies the annotation gain attributable to a preprocessing step. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: Counts lipid annotations in consensus across replicates, using the Lipid Annotator rule that an MS1-level feature must be present in at least half the analyzed MS-files, and quantifies the annotation gain attributable to a preprocessing step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the downstream tool already outputs a consensus feature table across replicates and per-file lists must not be re-filtered When the goal is a per-file (individual) annotation gain — that figure (41% ± 7%) is computed without the replicate-consensus cutoff and mixing the two bases invalidates the comparison

skills.description: Use when replicate DDA or SWATH-DIA MS2 spectral files have been deconvoluted (DecoID-style regression for DDA, DecoMetDIA-style C++/Rcpp for DIA) and must be consolidated into per-feature consensus spectra with precursor-fragment associations and compound annotations.
skills.name: replicate-consensus-spectrum-assembly
skills.search_text: replicate-consensus-spectrum-assembly Use when replicate DDA or SWATH-DIA MS2 spectral files have been deconvoluted (DecoID-style regression for DDA, DecoMetDIA-style C++/Rcpp for DIA) and must be consolidated into per-feature consensus spectra with precursor-fragment associations and compound annotations. Input is already an MS1 feature/peak-abundance table (e.g. asari output) with no MS2 spectra to consolidate Only a single MS2 injection exists, so replicate-level clustering and intensity averaging across injections cannot be performed The goal is deconvolution of chimeric spectra itself rather than consolidation of already-deconvoluted replicate spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Merges deconvoluted MS2 spectra from replicate injections into consensus spectra by clustering fragments on m/z and retention time and averaging intensities, then annotates fragments against the MetaboAnalystR MS2 reference library (~1.5 million spectra) as implemented in the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 / MetaboAnalystR 4.0 Spectra Processing module. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Merges deconvoluted MS2 spectra from replicate injections into consensus spectra by clustering fragments on m/z and retention time and averaging intensities, then annotates fragments against the MetaboAnalystR MS2 reference library (~1.5 million spectra) as implemented in the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 / MetaboAnalystR 4.0 Spectra Processing module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an MS1 feature/peak-abundance table (e.g. asari output) with no MS2 spectra to consolidate Only a single MS2 injection exists, so replicate-level clustering and intensity averaging across injections cannot be performed The goal is deconvolution of chimeric spectra itself rather than consolidation of already-deconvoluted replicate spectra

skills.description: Use when triplicate LC-IM-MS replicate annotation lists must be cross-checked to verify that smoothing/preprocessing improves consistent detection of low-abundance annotated features.
skills.name: replicate-consistency-annotation-checking
skills.search_text: replicate-consistency-annotation-checking Use when triplicate LC-IM-MS replicate annotation lists must be cross-checked to verify that smoothing/preprocessing improves consistent detection of low-abundance annotated features. Data are not from a replicate set (n<3) — replicate-consistency tallies require at least 3 LC-IM-MS replicates of the same sample (e.g. the human plasma lipid extract analyzed in triplicate). No lipid annotation lists are available (e.g. only raw MS1 spectra without downstream Lipid Annotator output) — the skill operates on annotation tables, not raw spectra. The feature of interest is a high-abundance ion that is already consistently detected in all original replicates — the skill's value is showing where smoothing rescues low-abundance features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A QC skill that compares per-replicate lipid annotation lists (original vs. preprocessed LC-IM-MS data) to determine whether low-abundance features — e.g. Sphingomyelin d34:5 — become consistently detectable and annotatable across all replicates only after PNNL PreProcessor smoothing. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: A QC skill that compares per-replicate lipid annotation lists (original vs. preprocessed LC-IM-MS data) to determine whether low-abundance features — e.g. Sphingomyelin d34:5 — become consistently detectable and annotatable across all replicates only after PNNL PreProcessor smoothing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not from a replicate set (n<3) — replicate-consistency tallies require at least 3 LC-IM-MS replicates of the same sample (e.g. the human plasma lipid extract analyzed in triplicate). No lipid annotation lists are available (e.g. only raw MS1 spectra without downstream Lipid Annotator output) — the skill operates on annotation tables, not raw spectra. The feature of interest is a high-abundance ion that is already consistently detected in all original replicates — the skill's value is showing where smoothing rescues low-abundance features.

skills.description: Use when you have a multi-batch metabolomics feature matrix with replicate reference samples (e.g. pooled or NIST 1950 SRM samples) present in each batch and need to quantify whether a normalization removed batch effects.
skills.name: replicate-cross-correlation-evaluation
skills.search_text: replicate-cross-correlation-evaluation Use when you have a multi-batch metabolomics feature matrix with replicate reference samples (e.g. pooled or NIST 1950 SRM samples) present in each batch and need to quantify whether a normalization removed batch effects. The dataset has no replicate reference samples (e.g. pooled QC or NIST 1950 SRM) present across batches, so no cross-batch replicate pairs can be matched via the 'group' column You need sample-level biological discrimination rather than batch-effect assessment — benchmark groups are excluded from regularization and only support model evaluation Evaluating spectral preservation or variance inflation, where batch-wise VC and fraction of features with VC inflated by >=5% are the appropriate criteria instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Evaluates multi-batch metabolomics normalization (e.g. by RALPS) by computing mean Pearson cross-correlations among reference/replicate samples across batches, matched via the 'group' column of the batch info file. Higher replicate cross-correlation indicates successful suppression of interbatch differences while preserving biological identity. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096
skills.summary: Evaluates multi-batch metabolomics normalization (e.g. by RALPS) by computing mean Pearson cross-correlations among reference/replicate samples across batches, matched via the 'group' column of the batch info file. Higher replicate cross-correlation indicates successful suppression of interbatch differences while preserving biological identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no replicate reference samples (e.g. pooled QC or NIST 1950 SRM) present across batches, so no cross-batch replicate pairs can be matched via the 'group' column You need sample-level biological discrimination rather than batch-effect assessment — benchmark groups are excluded from regularization and only support model evaluation Evaluating spectral preservation or variance inflation, where batch-wise VC and fraction of features with VC inflated by >=5% are the appropriate criteria instead

skills.description: Use when planning a multi-plate, multi-day targeted metabolomics run (e.g., >1,000 plasma samples over 44 days) where signal drift and inter-plate batch effects must be estimable from embedded replicates before normalisation.
skills.name: replicate-design-construction-for-metabolomics
skills.search_text: replicate-design-construction-for-metabolomics Use when planning a multi-plate, multi-day targeted metabolomics run (e.g., >1,000 plasma samples over 44 days) where signal drift and inter-plate batch effects must be estimable from embedded replicates before normalisation. Data have already been acquired without embedded sample replicates — the design must be specified before the run, since RUV-III estimation depends on the physical replicate positions. Small single-batch/single-plate studies where signal drift over months and inter-plate variation are not the dominant unwanted variation. The user only needs downstream normalisation of an existing matrix and already possesses a replicate design table (use hRUV normalisation directly instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Constructs an experimental plate/run layout that embeds biological and technical sample replicates (pooled QCs, short within-row replicates, and inter-plate batch replicates) throughout a large-scale metabolomics acquisition so that within- and between-batch unwanted variation can later be estimated with RUV-III/hRUV. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Constructs an experimental plate/run layout that embeds biological and technical sample replicates (pooled QCs, short within-row replicates, and inter-plate batch replicates) throughout a large-scale metabolomics acquisition so that within- and between-batch unwanted variation can later be estimated with RUV-III/hRUV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data have already been acquired without embedded sample replicates — the design must be specified before the run, since RUV-III estimation depends on the physical replicate positions. Small single-batch/single-plate studies where signal drift over months and inter-plate variation are not the dominant unwanted variation. The user only needs downstream normalisation of an existing matrix and already possesses a replicate design table (use hRUV normalisation directly instead).

skills.description: Use when features have been detected per-sample (e.g. in positive and negative ionization mode LC-IMS-MS/MS data) from study samples acquired in triplicate and you need to downselect only those features reproducibly observed in all replicate injections.
skills.name: replicate-feature-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: replicate-feature-consistency-checking Use when features have been detected per-sample (e.g. in positive and negative ionization mode LC-IMS-MS/MS data) from study samples acquired in triplicate and you need to downselect only those features reproducibly observed in all replicate injections. Study samples were acquired as single injections rather than analytical triplicates — there is no replicate set to check consistency against. Input is already an aligned cross-sample feature table rather than per-sample detected feature coordinates. The goal is exploratory peak picking on blanks or QC samples rather than confident feature calls in study samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A validation practice from the DEIMoS LC-IMS-MS/MS workflow in which detected features are required to be observed across analytical triplicate injections of study samples, providing additional confidence in detected features beyond local-maximum detection and intensity thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: A validation practice from the DEIMoS LC-IMS-MS/MS workflow in which detected features are required to be observed across analytical triplicate injections of study samples, providing additional confidence in detected features beyond local-maximum detection and intensity thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Study samples were acquired as single injections rather than analytical triplicates — there is no replicate set to check consistency against. Input is already an aligned cross-sample feature table rather than per-sample detected feature coordinates. The goal is exploratory peak picking on blanks or QC samples rather than confident feature calls in study samples.

skills.description: Use when normalizing multi-batch untargeted metabolomics data (e.g. flow-injection MS) where reference samples such as pooled study samples or NIST 1950 SRM are present in every batch and their biological similarity must be preserved during batch-effect removal.
skills.name: replicate-group-clustering-regularization
skills.search_text: replicate-group-clustering-regularization Use when normalizing multi-batch untargeted metabolomics data (e.g. flow-injection MS) where reference samples such as pooled study samples or NIST 1950 SRM are present in every batch and their biological similarity must be preserved during batch-effect removal. Data has not been normalized per batch first — RALPS is designed as a second step after intrabatch correction of temporal LC-MS drifts No replicate/reference samples are present across batches, so there is no basis for the clustering regularization term A single-batch dataset with no interbatch differences to harmonize http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A regularization term (g_lambda) added to the RALPS autoencoder loss that rewards tight clustering of reference/replicate samples in the embedded space, preserving biological identity while the adversarial classifier removes batch effects. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad096
skills.summary: A regularization term (g_lambda) added to the RALPS autoencoder loss that rewards tight clustering of reference/replicate samples in the embedded space, preserving biological identity while the adversarial classifier removes batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been normalized per batch first — RALPS is designed as a second step after intrabatch correction of temporal LC-MS drifts No replicate/reference samples are present across batches, so there is no basis for the clustering regularization term A single-batch dataset with no interbatch differences to harmonize

skills.description: Use when MS-metabolomics data contain biological or technical replicate samples and you need a nonparametric, FDR-controlled measure of which metabolites and sample pairs are reproducible, or when comparing pre-processing pipelines.
skills.name: replicate-reproducibility-estimation-mass-spectrometry
skills.search_text: replicate-reproducibility-estimation-mass-spectrometry Use when MS-metabolomics data contain biological or technical replicate samples and you need a nonparametric, FDR-controlled measure of which metabolites and sample pairs are reproducible, or when comparing pre-processing pipelines. The goal is a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps — the paper states the goal was not comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing, but to show the measure can be used as a benchmark for comparison The data have no biological or technical replicate structure, since MaRR assesses reproducibility across replicate pairs Separation between reproducible and irreproducible components is known to be poor — true signals may fall in undetectable regions due to overlap between components Applies the nonparametric Maximum Rank Reproducibility (MaRR) procedure, via the R/Bioconductor marr package, to estimate the percentage of reproducible metabolites per sample pair and reproducible sample pairs per metabolite in mass spectrometry metabolomics replicate experiments, including benchmarking of imputation-normalization pipelines. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04336-9
skills.summary: Applies the nonparametric Maximum Rank Reproducibility (MaRR) procedure, via the R/Bioconductor marr package, to estimate the percentage of reproducible metabolites per sample pair and reproducible sample pairs per metabolite in mass spectrometry metabolomics replicate experiments, including benchmarking of imputation-normalization pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps — the paper states the goal was not comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing, but to show the measure can be used as a benchmark for comparison The data have no biological or technical replicate structure, since MaRR assesses reproducibility across replicate pairs Separation between reproducible and irreproducible components is known to be poor — true signals may fall in undetectable regions due to overlap between components

skills.description: Use when building or validating a retention-time reference library from chemical-standard mixtures measured in replicate LC-MS (e.g. three HILIC injections per mixture), and you must decide which analytes' retention times are reproducible enough to record.
skills.name: replicate-retention-time-rsd-assessment
skills.search_text: replicate-retention-time-rsd-assessment Use when building or validating a retention-time reference library from chemical-standard mixtures measured in replicate LC-MS (e.g. three HILIC injections per mixture), and you must decide which analytes' retention times are reproducible enough to record. You only need to rank mobile phases, not validate retention times — use the MetaMOPE mobile-phase scoring step (peak quality score = Sp + Saf) instead. Retention times come from a single injection per standard — with no three replicates, retention-time RSD across replicates cannot be computed and thresholds c/r/I cannot be jointly applied. Input is already a validated feature/retention-time table; this skill generates validation flags, it does not re-validate annotated libraries. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assesses reproducibility of analyte retention times across replicate LC-MS injections by computing the retention-time RSD per standard peak and applying user-specified thresholds (RSD < c, Std/Blk ratio > r, intensity > I) to validate metabolites before building a retention-time reference library. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad061
skills.summary: Assesses reproducibility of analyte retention times across replicate LC-MS injections by computing the retention-time RSD per standard peak and applying user-specified thresholds (RSD < c, Std/Blk ratio > r, intensity > I) to validate metabolites before building a retention-time reference library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to rank mobile phases, not validate retention times — use the MetaMOPE mobile-phase scoring step (peak quality score = Sp + Saf) instead. Retention times come from a single injection per standard — with no three replicates, retention-time RSD across replicates cannot be computed and thresholds c/r/I cannot be jointly applied. Input is already a validated feature/retention-time table; this skill generates validation flags, it does not re-validate annotated libraries.

skills.description: Use when QC filtering lipidomics feature tables (e.g. LipiDex 2 Peak Finder/Spectrum Searcher results) where replicate quality control samples were injected and features with >30% RSD should be flagged for removal.
skills.name: replicate-rsd-quality-control
skills.search_text: replicate-rsd-quality-control Use when QC filtering lipidomics feature tables (e.g. LipiDex 2 Peak Finder/Spectrum Searcher results) where replicate quality control samples were injected and features with >30% RSD should be flagged for removal. The dataset lacks replicate quality control sample injections, so RSD across replicates cannot be computed. The task is upstream peak detection or spectral matching rather than post-identification QC filtering of a feature table. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies replicate quality control sample percent relative standard deviation (%RSD) analysis, with run-order tracking, to flag lipid features with excessive quantitation variability for removal, as implemented in the LipiDex 2 Degreaser QC module. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Applies replicate quality control sample percent relative standard deviation (%RSD) analysis, with run-order tracking, to flag lipid features with excessive quantitation variability for removal, as implemented in the LipiDex 2 Degreaser QC module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks replicate quality control sample injections, so RSD across replicates cannot be computed. The task is upstream peak detection or spectral matching rather than post-identification QC filtering of a feature table.

skills.description: Use when you have merged peak lists from replicate GCxGC/TOF-MS runs (e.g. two runs of a 35-compound mixture) and need metabolite identification with a posterior confidence measure per metabolite, ranked by posterior probability.
skills.name: replicate-run-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: replicate-run-metabolite-annotation Use when you have merged peak lists from replicate GCxGC/TOF-MS runs (e.g. two runs of a 35-compound mixture) and need metabolite identification with a posterior confidence measure per metabolite, ranked by posterior probability. The goal is biomarker discovery rather than identification — MetPC's biomarker step controls the two-dimensional false discovery rate (fdr2d) in multiple hypothesis testing and is a separate stage of the pipeline Raw (unmerged) peak data is provided instead of merged peak lists; the model assigns peaks from merged peak lists, so preprocessing/peak merging must be done first No replicate spectra are available in the reference library to compute the cosine similarity candidate matches required by the model http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates metabolites in GCxGC/TOF-MS replicate runs by scoring merged-peak spectra against a reference metabolite library (cosine similarity) and assigning peaks to metabolites with a hierarchical statistical model fitted by an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, yielding per-metabolite posterior confidence measures. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9050103
skills.summary: Annotates metabolites in GCxGC/TOF-MS replicate runs by scoring merged-peak spectra against a reference metabolite library (cosine similarity) and assigning peaks to metabolites with a hierarchical statistical model fitted by an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, yielding per-metabolite posterior confidence measures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biomarker discovery rather than identification — MetPC's biomarker step controls the two-dimensional false discovery rate (fdr2d) in multiple hypothesis testing and is a separate stage of the pipeline Raw (unmerged) peak data is provided instead of merged peak lists; the model assigns peaks from merged peak lists, so preprocessing/peak merging must be done first No replicate spectra are available in the reference library to compute the cosine similarity candidate matches required by the model

skills.description: Use when a series of replicate 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. metabolite mix replicates or Daphnia extract CryoProbe spectra) must be phased automatically and you need to compare which algorithm gives the most reproducible phases.
skills.name: replicate-series-phase-consistency-analysis
skills.search_text: replicate-series-phase-consistency-analysis Use when a series of replicate 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. metabolite mix replicates or Daphnia extract CryoProbe spectra) must be phased automatically and you need to compare which algorithm gives the most reproducible phases. Spectra that will be phased manually rather than by automatic phase correction algorithms — the benchmark compares automated algorithms (apk5, apk0.noe, MetaboLabPy) only A single spectrum rather than a replicate series — within-series phase dispersion cannot be computed without multiple replicates 2D-NMR series or tracer/isotopomer analysis — this skill covers 1D-NMR phase consistency only, not the metabolabpytools isotopomer workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Benchmark within-series phase consistency of automatic phase correction algorithms (MetaboLabPy baseline-based and per-spectrum, MetaboLab apk5, TopSpin apk0.noe, MNova) across replicate 1D-NMR spectra series by extracting per-spectrum phase angles and comparing within-series dispersion. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048
skills.summary: Benchmark within-series phase consistency of automatic phase correction algorithms (MetaboLabPy baseline-based and per-spectrum, MetaboLab apk5, TopSpin apk0.noe, MNova) across replicate 1D-NMR spectra series by extracting per-spectrum phase angles and comparing within-series dispersion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra that will be phased manually rather than by automatic phase correction algorithms — the benchmark compares automated algorithms (apk5, apk0.noe, MetaboLabPy) only A single spectrum rather than a replicate series — within-series phase dispersion cannot be computed without multiple replicates 2D-NMR series or tracer/isotopomer analysis — this skill covers 1D-NMR phase consistency only, not the metabolabpytools isotopomer workflow

skills.description: Use when a paper reports aggregate counts for a curated resource (e.g. total entries, novel additions, taxonomic coverage) and you must verify them directly from the released data files rather than trusting the text.
skills.name: reported-count-reconciliation
skills.search_text: reported-count-reconciliation Use when a paper reports aggregate counts for a curated resource (e.g. total entries, novel additions, taxonomic coverage) and you must verify them directly from the released data files rather than trusting the text. The paper's claims are about per-entry annotations (e.g. 1188 chemical structures, 1002 bioactivities, 2020 NRPS A-domain substrates) rather than whole-database entry counts that a file-level parse can reproduce. The resource data is not versioned/tracked in a public repository, so released files matching the paper's snapshot cannot be obtained. http://edamontology.org/topic_3071 Reproduces database-level summary statistics (total entries, newly added BGCs, phylum/kingdom counts) by parsing a database release's JSON files and reconciling computed counts against values reported in the publication (e.g. MIBiG 3.0's 2502 entries, 661 new BGCs, 16 phyla, 5 kingdoms). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Reproduces database-level summary statistics (total entries, newly added BGCs, phylum/kingdom counts) by parsing a database release's JSON files and reconciling computed counts against values reported in the publication (e.g. MIBiG 3.0's 2502 entries, 661 new BGCs, 16 phyla, 5 kingdoms).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The paper's claims are about per-entry annotations (e.g. 1188 chemical structures, 1002 bioactivities, 2020 NRPS A-domain substrates) rather than whole-database entry counts that a file-level parse can reproduce. The resource data is not versioned/tracked in a public repository, so released files matching the paper's snapshot cannot be obtained.

skills.description: Use when a paper reports a database-overlap count and a significance test (e.g., 132 of 374 structures in LOTUS, chi-square 32.353) backed by a deposited dataset, and you must verify it independently.
skills.name: reported-count-reproduction-from-deposited-data
skills.search_text: reported-count-reproduction-from-deposited-data Use when a paper reports a database-overlap count and a significance test (e.g., 132 of 374 structures in LOTUS, chi-square 32.353) backed by a deposited dataset, and you must verify it independently. The target statistic is a model prediction or a result of the multi-omics MEANtools workflow itself rather than a database-overlap count reproducible from deposited tables. The structures are not available as a deposited CSV with per-structure IDs, so per-structure matched/unmatched bookkeeping cannot be performed. A different metabolite reference database is required instead of LOTUS as downloaded on 10/10/2023, changing the reference set that defines the overlap. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces a reported statistic from a paper by re-running the matching and significance computation on the deposited source data — here, the 132-of-374 LOTUS structure overlap with chi-square 32.353 (DF=1, p<0.001) — verifying the count and the contingency-table test rather than accepting the reported number. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Reproduces a reported statistic from a paper by re-running the matching and significance computation on the deposited source data — here, the 132-of-374 LOTUS structure overlap with chi-square 32.353 (DF=1, p<0.001) — verifying the count and the contingency-table test rather than accepting the reported number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target statistic is a model prediction or a result of the multi-omics MEANtools workflow itself rather than a database-overlap count reproducible from deposited tables. The structures are not available as a deposited CSV with per-structure IDs, so per-structure matched/unmatched bookkeeping cannot be performed. A different metabolite reference database is required instead of LOTUS as downloaded on 10/10/2023, changing the reference set that defines the overlap.

skills.description: Use when a reported finding is a count of parameters grouped by sample type (EDTA plasma, serum, LiHep plasma) and delay type (pre- vs postcentrifugation) and you need to verify it against the PRIMA Panel stability time point data.
skills.name: reported-count-verification-against-reference-values
skills.search_text: reported-count-verification-against-reference-values Use when a reported finding is a count of parameters grouped by sample type (EDTA plasma, serum, LiHep plasma) and delay type (pre- vs postcentrifugation) and you need to verify it against the PRIMA Panel stability time point data. When the reported claim is a qualitative finding (e.g., 'lactic acid was significantly affected by short delays') rather than a discrete count per sample type — use a per-parameter stability inspection instead. When raw NMR spectra or Bruker IVDr outputs are the only available input and stability time points have not yet been recomputed — the 240 min threshold cannot be applied without the stability time point table. Recompute tabular counts (e.g., number of metabolic parameters within a stability threshold per sample type and delay type) from the PRIMA Panel recomputed stability time point table and check each cell against reported reference values, accepting only when all cells match exactly. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c04938
skills.summary: Recompute tabular counts (e.g., number of metabolic parameters within a stability threshold per sample type and delay type) from the PRIMA Panel recomputed stability time point table and check each cell against reported reference values, accepting only when all cells match exactly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the reported claim is a qualitative finding (e.g., 'lactic acid was significantly affected by short delays') rather than a discrete count per sample type — use a per-parameter stability inspection instead. When raw NMR spectra or Bruker IVDr outputs are the only available input and stability time points have not yet been recomputed — the 240 min threshold cannot be applied without the stability time point table.

skills.description: Use when a paper reports aggregate counts (e.g., 5159 unique lipid ions, 1401 features, 26 lipid types) that must be verified by recounting them from the underlying per-feature annotation workbook in its supplementary files.
skills.name: reported-metric-verification
skills.search_text: reported-metric-verification Use when a paper reports aggregate counts (e.g., 5159 unique lipid ions, 1401 features, 26 lipid types) that must be verified by recounting them from the underlying per-feature annotation workbook in its supplementary files. The input is raw vendor data or .ms2 files rather than an already-annotated feature table workbook — run the LipidMatch identification workflow (peak picking, MSConvert, identification) first The metric to verify is a software-performance comparison across tools rather than a recountable count from a supplementary workbook The workbook mixes polarities or tools in a single sheet without polarity/annotation-source labels that allow isolating LipidMatch positive-mode columns http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Independently recounts summary statistics reported in a publication (here, LipidMatch annotation counts for positive-mode IE-ddMS2-top5 Red Cross plasma) directly from the authors' supplementary annotation workbook, accepting the recount only when it exactly matches the reported values. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1744-3
skills.summary: Independently recounts summary statistics reported in a publication (here, LipidMatch annotation counts for positive-mode IE-ddMS2-top5 Red Cross plasma) directly from the authors' supplementary annotation workbook, accepting the recount only when it exactly matches the reported values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw vendor data or .ms2 files rather than an already-annotated feature table workbook — run the LipidMatch identification workflow (peak picking, MSConvert, identification) first The metric to verify is a software-performance comparison across tools rather than a recountable count from a supplementary workbook The workbook mixes polarities or tools in a single sheet without polarity/annotation-source labels that allow isolating LipidMatch positive-mode columns

skills.description: Use when a manuscript reports paired before/after optimization metrics across multiple biological studies (e.g. GSI, feature counts, annotations) and you need a machine-readable, arithmetic-consistency-checked results table.
