skills.search_text: reported-results-extraction-from-manuscript Use when a manuscript reports paired before/after optimization metrics across multiple biological studies (e.g. GSI, feature counts, annotations) and you need a machine-readable, arithmetic-consistency-checked results table. Raw LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML) rather than published metric values is the only input — use the BAGO optimization pipeline (getBPCData, findTopSignals, sepEfficiency) instead Only one condition or study is available, so no paired before/after comparison across studies can be assembled The manuscript reports only qualitative claims (e.g. 'improved performance') without absolute before/after counts needed for arithmetic verification http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extracts before/after gradient-optimization metrics (GSI, feature counts, MS/MS spectra, annotated compounds) for all six BAGO validation studies from the manuscript text, re-derives the reported percentage gains, and assembles them into a single consolidated results table. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.09.08.556930
skills.summary: Extracts before/after gradient-optimization metrics (GSI, feature counts, MS/MS spectra, annotated compounds) for all six BAGO validation studies from the manuscript text, re-derives the reported percentage gains, and assembles them into a single consolidated results table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML) rather than published metric values is the only input — use the BAGO optimization pipeline (getBPCData, findTopSignals, sepEfficiency) instead Only one condition or study is available, so no paired before/after comparison across studies can be assembled The manuscript reports only qualitative claims (e.g. 'improved performance') without absolute before/after counts needed for arithmetic verification

skills.description: Use when a paper reports exact per-method counts of significant features (e.g., significant metabolites at FWER alpha=0.05 in Table 3/Table S1) and you must verify those counts by re-executing the analysis from the released data and code.
skills.name: reported-table-count-reproduction
skills.search_text: reported-table-count-reproduction Use when a paper reports exact per-method counts of significant features (e.g., significant metabolites at FWER alpha=0.05 in Table 3/Table S1) and you must verify those counts by re-executing the analysis from the released data and code. The target result is a continuous statistic, effect size, or figure rather than an exact integer count of significant features that can be matched to a table The analysis uses grouped metabolites or a different test than Welch's two-sample t-test, since the reported counts being reproduced apply to 761 ungrouped metabolites tested against sex http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces published significance-count tables (e.g., Table 3/Table S1) by re-running the paper's statistical pipeline — here Welch's two-sample t-tests of sex against 761 log-transformed metabolite abundances with eigen-analysis-based FWER corrections (PrsCo, Gao, Galwey, and DisCo P-ad variants) — and validating that per-method significant metabolite counts match the reported numbers exactly. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010028
skills.summary: Reproduces published significance-count tables (e.g., Table 3/Table S1) by re-running the paper's statistical pipeline — here Welch's two-sample t-tests of sex against 761 log-transformed metabolite abundances with eigen-analysis-based FWER corrections (PrsCo, Gao, Galwey, and DisCo P-ad variants) — and validating that per-method significant metabolite counts match the reported numbers exactly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target result is a continuous statistic, effect size, or figure rather than an exact integer count of significant features that can be matched to a table The analysis uses grouped metabolites or a different test than Welch's two-sample t-test, since the reported counts being reproduced apply to 761 ungrouped metabolites tested against sex

skills.description: Use when a paper reports exact counts of workflow/method combinations (e.g., 5,904/48/1,968 NOREVA workflows under QCS, IS, and neither conditions) and you must reproduce them by re-enumerating the underlying combinatorial space.
skills.name: reported-total-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: reported-total-consistency-checking Use when a paper reports exact counts of workflow/method combinations (e.g., 5,904/48/1,968 NOREVA workflows under QCS, IS, and neither conditions) and you must reproduce them by re-enumerating the underlying combinatorial space. The goal is performance assessment (S5) of the enumerated workflows against the five criteria rather than verifying that the combinatorial count itself is reproducible. The published method counts per stage are not available or have changed (NOREVA's method set cannot be extended automatically and must be manually updated by bioinformaticians). The target counts come from a study whose original processing was never described, so even NOREVA had to infer outcomes 'across all possible workflows' rather than against a stated total. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A validation skill that independently recomputes combinatorial enumerations (here, NOREVA's 4 imputation × 3 QCS-correction × 2 transformation × 23 normalization method combinations) and accepts the result only when computed scenario totals exactly match published values (5,904 QCS, 48 IS, 1,968 without both). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: A validation skill that independently recomputes combinatorial enumerations (here, NOREVA's 4 imputation × 3 QCS-correction × 2 transformation × 23 normalization method combinations) and accepts the result only when computed scenario totals exactly match published values (5,904 QCS, 48 IS, 1,968 without both).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is performance assessment (S5) of the enumerated workflows against the five criteria rather than verifying that the combinatorial count itself is reproducible. The published method counts per stage are not available or have changed (NOREVA's method set cannot be extended automatically and must be manually updated by bioinformaticians). The target counts come from a study whose original processing was never described, so even NOREVA had to infer outcomes 'across all possible workflows' rather than against a stated total.

skills.description: Use when a KO/gene/compound abundance table plus metadata (two-group, multi-group, continuous covariate, or longitudinal) needs pathway-level enrichment, and threshold-free aggregation with reporter scores is preferred over cutoff-based hypergeometric-style tests.
skills.name: reporter-score-statistics
skills.search_text: reporter-score-statistics Use when a KO/gene/compound abundance table plus metadata (two-group, multi-group, continuous covariate, or longitudinal) needs pathway-level enrichment, and threshold-free aggregation with reporter scores is preferred over cutoff-based hypergeometric-style tests. The abundance table has already been prefiltered to significant/background features — GRSA is threshold-free and requires the full background Only a pre-defined hit list without full feature abundances and metadata is available — hypergeometric-style KO_enrich/KO_fisher on ko_stat may be the appropriate fallback instead of the reporter-score aggregation Specificity must be strictly guaranteed — the article notes GRSA exhibits slightly lower specificity and that true negatives are difficult to define due to incomplete databases http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA), implemented in the R package ReporterScore, aggregates threshold-free feature-level statistics (KOs, genes, compounds) into pathway/module-level reporter scores for multi-group, longitudinal, and correlation omics designs, and benchmarks sensitivity against KO_enrich, KO_fisher, KO_gsea, KO_gsva, KO_padog, KO_safe, and KO_sea. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA), implemented in the R package ReporterScore, aggregates threshold-free feature-level statistics (KOs, genes, compounds) into pathway/module-level reporter scores for multi-group, longitudinal, and correlation omics designs, and benchmarks sensitivity against KO_enrich, KO_fisher, KO_gsea, KO_gsva, KO_padog, KO_safe, and KO_sea.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance table has already been prefiltered to significant/background features — GRSA is threshold-free and requires the full background Only a pre-defined hit list without full feature abundances and metadata is available — hypergeometric-style KO_enrich/KO_fisher on ko_stat may be the appropriate fallback instead of the reporter-score aggregation Specificity must be strictly guaranteed — the article notes GRSA exhibits slightly lower specificity and that true negatives are difficult to define due to incomplete databases

skills.description: Use when you have a species-level microbial abundance table plus sample metadata and want threshold-free, hierarchical enrichment of taxa (e.g., genera) across group contrasts instead of pathway/KO enrichment.
skills.name: reporter-score-taxonomic-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: reporter-score-taxonomic-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a species-level microbial abundance table plus sample metadata and want threshold-free, hierarchical enrichment of taxa (e.g., genera) across group contrasts instead of pathway/KO enrichment. Input is already a KO/gene/compound abundance table — use the built-in KEGG pathway, module, or GO databases (load_KOlist, load_GOlist, custom_modulelist_from_org) instead of a custom taxonomy module list You need differential abundance of individual species rather than hierarchical enrichment of higher taxa — ko.test() per-species statistics alone suffice The abundance table has been prefiltered to significant features — GRSA is threshold-free and the README warns input tables should retain background information http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extends Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) from functional to taxonomy-level enrichment by supplying a custom hierarchical genus-to-species module list to the ReporterScore package, aggregating species-level statistics into genus-level reporter scores. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Extends Generalized Reporter Score-based Analysis (GRSA) from functional to taxonomy-level enrichment by supplying a custom hierarchical genus-to-species module list to the ReporterScore package, aggregating species-level statistics into genus-level reporter scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a KO/gene/compound abundance table — use the built-in KEGG pathway, module, or GO databases (load_KOlist, load_GOlist, custom_modulelist_from_org) instead of a custom taxonomy module list You need differential abundance of individual species rather than hierarchical enrichment of higher taxa — ko.test() per-species statistics alone suffice The abundance table has been prefiltered to significant features — GRSA is threshold-free and the README warns input tables should retain background information

skills.description: Use when a curated reference database (e.g. MIBiG) has released a new version and you must report how many entries were added, how they distribute across predefined classes (including hybrids and 'Other'), and the proportional share of dominant classes.
skills.name: repository-composition-statistics
skills.search_text: repository-composition-statistics Use when a curated reference database (e.g. MIBiG) has released a new version and you must report how many entries were added, how they distribute across predefined classes (including hybrids and 'Other'), and the proportional share of dominant classes. Input is raw candidate BGC predictions from genome mining (e.g. thousands of candidates from antiSMASH or IMG-ABC/antiSMASH-DB) rather than curated BGCs of known function — MIBiG counts only validated, literature-backed entries The goal is to submit or deposit a new BGC entry to MIBiG (accession request, entry form, Annotathon curation) rather than to compute repository-level statistics You need per-entry annotation curation (fixing mistyped info, removing duplicates, adding chemical structures) rather than aggregate composition metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Quantifies the composition and growth of the MIBiG 2.0 repository by counting curated biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) per structure-based class and computing growth relative to a baseline release. It turns repository metadata into per-class counts and percentage-increase figures suitable for reporting database expansion. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz882
skills.summary: Quantifies the composition and growth of the MIBiG 2.0 repository by counting curated biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) per structure-based class and computing growth relative to a baseline release. It turns repository metadata into per-class counts and percentage-increase figures suitable for reporting database expansion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw candidate BGC predictions from genome mining (e.g. thousands of candidates from antiSMASH or IMG-ABC/antiSMASH-DB) rather than curated BGCs of known function — MIBiG counts only validated, literature-backed entries The goal is to submit or deposit a new BGC entry to MIBiG (accession request, entry form, Annotathon curation) rather than to compute repository-level statistics You need per-entry annotation curation (fixing mistyped info, removing duplicates, adding chemical structures) rather than aggregate composition metrics

skills.description: Use when a paper reports aggregate statistics about a curated database release (total entries, newly added entries, phyla/kingdom coverage) and the underlying versioned data are available in a public repository, so the numbers can be recomputed and checked.
skills.name: repository-dataset-aggregation
skills.search_text: repository-dataset-aggregation Use when a paper reports aggregate statistics about a curated database release (total entries, newly added entries, phyla/kingdom coverage) and the underlying versioned data are available in a public repository, so the numbers can be recomputed and checked. The repository does not provide per-entry machine-readable files (e.g. only a web interface or PDF tables), so counts cannot be recomputed independently The goal is to extract or score individual cluster annotations (compounds, bioactivities, A-domain substrates) rather than aggregate database-level counts Entries from multiple releases or mixed provenance are combined in one directory, making the novelty delta ambiguous without per-entry version metadata http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Download a released dataset from its versioned GitHub repository (e.g. mibig-secmet/mibig-json), parse every entry file, and aggregate database-level statistics (entry counts, novelty counts, taxonomy coverage) to independently verify figures reported in a publication's Results/Discussion and tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Download a released dataset from its versioned GitHub repository (e.g. mibig-secmet/mibig-json), parse every entry file, and aggregate database-level statistics (entry counts, novelty counts, taxonomy coverage) to independently verify figures reported in a publication's Results/Discussion and tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The repository does not provide per-entry machine-readable files (e.g. only a web interface or PDF tables), so counts cannot be recomputed independently The goal is to extract or score individual cluster annotations (compounds, bioactivities, A-domain substrates) rather than aggregate database-level counts Entries from multiple releases or mixed provenance are combined in one directory, making the novelty delta ambiguous without per-entry version metadata

skills.description: Use when a database-release paper reports divergent growth numbers per contribution channel (e.g. submission forms vs. curated events vs. classrooms) and these need to be reconciled into a verifiable per-channel table.
skills.name: repository-growth-metric-verification
skills.search_text: repository-growth-metric-verification Use when a database-release paper reports divergent growth numbers per contribution channel (e.g. submission forms vs. curated events vs. classrooms) and these need to be reconciled into a verifiable per-channel table. The repository provides a changelog or per-entry provenance fields and exact counts can be computed directly from entry metadata rather than extracted from prose The article reports only a single undifferentiated growth figure with no per-channel breakdown to verify Growth metrics concern automated pipeline deposits (e.g. antiSMASH-DB or IMG-ABC bulk entries) rather than manual curation channels http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Extracts and cross-verifies quantitative growth metrics (entry counts per curation channel) reported in a database-release article against the repository itself, producing a structured contribution table such as MIBiG's crowdsourcing (140), Annotathon (702) and classroom (10) channel counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz882
skills.summary: Extracts and cross-verifies quantitative growth metrics (entry counts per curation channel) reported in a database-release article against the repository itself, producing a structured contribution table such as MIBiG's crowdsourcing (140), Annotathon (702) and classroom (10) channel counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The repository provides a changelog or per-entry provenance fields and exact counts can be computed directly from entry metadata rather than extracted from prose The article reports only a single undifferentiated growth figure with no per-channel breakdown to verify Growth metrics concern automated pipeline deposits (e.g. antiSMASH-DB or IMG-ABC bulk entries) rather than manual curation channels

skills.description: Use when a dependency edge list or package list of metabolomics R software lacks per-package repository labels and the analysis goal requires comparing CRAN-, Bioconductor-, and GitHub-hosted packages.

skills.search_text: repository-package-classification Use when a dependency edge list or package list of metabolomics R software lacks per-package repository labels and the analysis goal requires comparing CRAN-, Bioconductor-, and GitHub-hosted packages. The input already carries a per-package repository annotation and the goal is only to compute connectivity metrics. The package set is not metabolomics-specific R software (e.g., general CRAN packages outside the review's scope). http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates metabolomics R packages with their hosting repository (CRAN, Bioconductor, or GitHub), as catalogued in the metaRbolomics review, so that downstream network analyses can compare packages across repositories. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9100200
skills.summary: Annotates metabolomics R packages with their hosting repository (CRAN, Bioconductor, or GitHub), as catalogued in the metaRbolomics review, so that downstream network analyses can compare packages across repositories.

skills.description: Use when you need to reanalyze public tandem MS (MS/MS) files at repository scale as cohorts — e.g. compute PCA of per-file GNPS chemical annotations from the ReDU/MSV000084206 identification database — rather than analyzing one dataset in isolation.
skills.name: repository-scale-tandem-ms-cohort-analysis
skills.search_text: repository-scale-tandem-ms-cohort-analysis Use when you need to reanalyze public tandem MS (MS/MS) files at repository scale as cohorts — e.g. compute PCA of per-file GNPS chemical annotations from the ReDU/MSV000084206 identification database — rather than analyzing one dataset in isolation. The goal is supervised group comparison or metadata association testing — use ReDU's Group Comparator or Sample Information Associations (View Associations button) instead of unsupervised PCA. You need to assemble cohorts of files by metadata filters — use the ReDU File Selector with the Attribute Filters Panel rather than recomputing the global PCA. Input is raw or converted mzXML/mzML data not yet annotated — GNPS spectral library search must produce chemical annotations before PCA can be run. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reproduce ReDU's unsupervised PCA over the repository-wide chemical-annotation matrix (GNPS spectral-library annotations per MassIVE file) and export per-file principal-component coordinates for interactive 3D exploration in Emperor. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-020-0916-7
skills.summary: Reproduce ReDU's unsupervised PCA over the repository-wide chemical-annotation matrix (GNPS spectral-library annotations per MassIVE file) and export per-file principal-component coordinates for interactive 3D exploration in Emperor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is supervised group comparison or metadata association testing — use ReDU's Group Comparator or Sample Information Associations (View Associations button) instead of unsupervised PCA. You need to assemble cohorts of files by metadata filters — use the ReDU File Selector with the Attribute Filters Panel rather than recomputing the global PCA. Input is raw or converted mzXML/mzML data not yet annotated — GNPS spectral library search must produce chemical annotations before PCA can be run.

skills.description: Use when you need to quality-control a whole repository's holdings rather than one file — e.g. counting how many Metabolomics Workbench analyses fail to download or fail mwTab/JSON parsing at a given snapshot date.
skills.name: repository-wide-data-corpus-auditing
skills.search_text: repository-wide-data-corpus-auditing Use when you need to quality-control a whole repository's holdings rather than one file — e.g. counting how many Metabolomics Workbench analyses fail to download or fail mwTab/JSON parsing at a given snapshot date. You only need to read or convert a handful of known analysis IDs — use mwtab's normal read_files/conversion path instead of a corpus-wide audit. The target repository exposes neither a REST enumeration endpoint nor bulk download in multiple formats — the sweep design depends on both. Your goal is content-level validation of metabolite metadata columns (e.g. NameMatcher/ValueMatcher dict_match/series_match checks) rather than downloadability and parseability of the whole corpus. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3071 Systematically enumerate and download an entire data-repository corpus (all 1891 Metabolomics Workbench analyses) in multiple formats (mwTab and JSONized) via the REST interface, then attempt to parse every file to quantify download and parse failures for repository curation and FAIRness assessment. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11030163
skills.summary: Systematically enumerate and download an entire data-repository corpus (all 1891 Metabolomics Workbench analyses) in multiple formats (mwTab and JSONized) via the REST interface, then attempt to parse every file to quantify download and parse failures for repository curation and FAIRness assessment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to read or convert a handful of known analysis IDs — use mwtab's normal read_files/conversion path instead of a corpus-wide audit. The target repository exposes neither a REST enumeration endpoint nor bulk download in multiple formats — the sweep design depends on both. Your goal is content-level validation of metabolite metadata columns (e.g. NameMatcher/ValueMatcher dict_match/series_match checks) rather than downloadability and parseability of the whole corpus.

skills.description: Use when you have gene rank lists (e.g., from RNA-seq SEQC-style replicate experiments) from three replicates and need to quantify reproducibility, estimate pi1, and call reproducible genes with FDR control.
skills.name: reproducibility-assessment-high-throughput-rank-lists
skills.search_text: reproducibility-assessment-high-throughput-rank-lists Use when you have gene rank lists (e.g., from RNA-seq SEQC-style replicate experiments) from three replicates and need to quantify reproducibility, estimate pi1, and call reproducible genes with FDR control. Input consists of raw expression measurements rather than gene rank lists — MaRR operates on ranks and does not make parametric assumptions on distributions, so ranks must be formed first Only one replicate is available — reproducibility assessment requires at least two rank lists (original MaRR) and this extension requires three A parametric, model-based dependence analysis of replicate signal intensities is explicitly preferred over the nonparametric rank-based procedure http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A nonparametric MaRR-based procedure for assessing reproducibility of gene rank lists across replicate high-throughput experiments, extended to three replicates via the maximum order statistic Mg(3)=max{Rgx,Rgy,Rgz}. It estimates the reproducible signal proportion pi1 and controls marginal FDR without tuning parameters. metabolomics/v3 10.1080/01621459.2017.1397521
skills.summary: A nonparametric MaRR-based procedure for assessing reproducibility of gene rank lists across replicate high-throughput experiments, extended to three replicates via the maximum order statistic Mg(3)=max{Rgx,Rgy,Rgz}. It estimates the reproducible signal proportion pi1 and controls marginal FDR without tuning parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of raw expression measurements rather than gene rank lists — MaRR operates on ranks and does not make parametric assumptions on distributions, so ranks must be formed first Only one replicate is available — reproducibility assessment requires at least two rank lists (original MaRR) and this extension requires three A parametric, model-based dependence analysis of replicate signal intensities is explicitly preferred over the nonparametric rank-based procedure

skills.description: Use when you need to characterize how reproducible and how complex a pipeline is (process count, parameter count, containerization) and compare it against a published baseline such as Metaboigniter's 20+ processes and 200+ parameters.
skills.name: reproducibility-feature-documentation
skills.search_text: reproducibility-feature-documentation Use when you need to characterize how reproducible and how complex a pipeline is (process count, parameter count, containerization) and compare it against a published baseline such as Metaboigniter's 20+ processes and 200+ parameters. The comparator workflow's process/parameter counts are not published or independently verifiable, so the baseline figures cannot be grounded The workflow source code (main.nf, conf/ files) is not available, so process and parameter enumeration would be guesswork The goal is algorithm performance benchmarking (peak detection accuracy, runtime scaling) rather than complexity/reproducibility documentation — the authors explicitly did not quantitatively measure scalability http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Documents a workflow's reproducibility posture by enumerating its process/parameter complexity against a published comparator and verifying that repeated executions with identical parameters and the same container yield identical outputs. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00364
skills.summary: Documents a workflow's reproducibility posture by enumerating its process/parameter complexity against a published comparator and verifying that repeated executions with identical parameters and the same container yield identical outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparator workflow's process/parameter counts are not published or independently verifiable, so the baseline figures cannot be grounded The workflow source code (main.nf, conf/ files) is not available, so process and parameter enumeration would be guesswork The goal is algorithm performance benchmarking (peak detection accuracy, runtime scaling) rather than complexity/reproducibility documentation — the authors explicitly did not quantitatively measure scalability

skills.description: Use when you have MaRR-classified reproducible/irreproducible metabolites and per-metabolite RSD values and need to show graphically whether a conventional CV/RSD cutoff (e.g., 25%) separates the two classes.
skills.name: reproducibility-scatter-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: reproducibility-scatter-plot-visualization Use when you have MaRR-classified reproducible/irreproducible metabolites and per-metabolite RSD values and need to show graphically whether a conventional CV/RSD cutoff (e.g., 25%) separates the two classes. When the goal is a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps rather than a benchmark comparison — the paper states 'our goal was not to do a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps, but instead to show how this measure can be used as a benchmark for comparison.' When reproducible and irreproducible components overlap heavily and fall in undetectable regions, making MaRR labels unreliable for the comparison. When data have not been pre-processed (e.g., missing value imputation and normalization such as BPCA/kNN imputation and quantile/median/RUV normalization) — MaRR is applied after data processing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate scatter plots of MaRR reproducibility versus relative standard deviation (RSD) for biological and technical replicates, overlaying a 25% RSD filtering cutoff, to visually demonstrate whether conventional RSD filtering removes MaRR-identified irreproducible metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04336-9
skills.summary: Generate scatter plots of MaRR reproducibility versus relative standard deviation (RSD) for biological and technical replicates, overlaying a 25% RSD filtering cutoff, to visually demonstrate whether conventional RSD filtering removes MaRR-identified irreproducible metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps rather than a benchmark comparison — the paper states 'our goal was not to do a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps, but instead to show how this measure can be used as a benchmark for comparison.' When reproducible and irreproducible components overlap heavily and fall in undetectable regions, making MaRR labels unreliable for the comparison. When data have not been pre-processed (e.g., missing value imputation and normalization such as BPCA/kNN imputation and quantile/median/RUV normalization) — MaRR is applied after data processing.

skills.description: Use when assessing reproducibility of high-dimensional replicate experiments (e.g., MS-metabolomics feature tables with metabolites x replicate sample pairs) where replicate correlation decays with rank, and FDR-controlled, power-assessed detection of reproducible signals is needed.
skills.name: reproducibility-signal-detection-under-decaying-correlation
skills.search_text: reproducibility-signal-detection-under-decaying-correlation Use when assessing reproducibility of high-dimensional replicate experiments (e.g., MS-metabolomics feature tables with metabolites x replicate sample pairs) where replicate correlation decays with rank, and FDR-controlled, power-assessed detection of reproducible signals is needed. When a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps (imputation/normalization) is the goal — the article states the goal was only to benchmark comparisons, not comprehensive pre-processing evaluation When reproducible and irreproducible components lack separation — true signals may fall in undetectable regions due to overlap between components When the input is not replicate data amenable to pairwise rank-based comparison (e.g., a single-sample feature table with no replicates) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies the nonparametric MaRR (Maximum Rank Reproducibility) maximal rank statistic to estimate the proportion of reproducible signals and detect reproducible features when correlation between replicate pairs decreases gradually with rank, without parametric assumptions on distributions or dependence structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04336-9
skills.summary: Applies the nonparametric MaRR (Maximum Rank Reproducibility) maximal rank statistic to estimate the proportion of reproducible signals and detect reproducible features when correlation between replicate pairs decreases gradually with rank, without parametric assumptions on distributions or dependence structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a comprehensive evaluation of pre-processing steps (imputation/normalization) is the goal — the article states the goal was only to benchmark comparisons, not comprehensive pre-processing evaluation When reproducible and irreproducible components lack separation — true signals may fall in undetectable regions due to overlap between components When the input is not replicate data amenable to pairwise rank-based comparison (e.g., a single-sample feature table with no replicates)

skills.description: Use when reproducing cross-laboratory lipid identification overlap statistics from a lab-by-lipid identification matrix, e.g. counting how many of 31 laboratories reported each SRM 1950 lipid and validating the ≥5-lab subset against a published value.
skills.name: reproducibility-statistic-comparison
skills.search_text: reproducibility-statistic-comparison Use when reproducing cross-laboratory lipid identification overlap statistics from a lab-by-lipid identification matrix, e.g. counting how many of 31 laboratories reported each SRM 1950 lipid and validating the ≥5-lab subset against a published value. Input is raw MS/MS data or individual spectra requiring lipid identification (use a spectrum-to-lipid identification method such as LipiDetective instead of overlap statistics) The identifications come from a single laboratory or single software run, so no cross-laboratory overlap statistic can be computed The lipid names are already harmonized and only downstream statistics other than lab-coverage overlap (e.g. quantification agreement) are needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces cross-laboratory reproducibility statistics for lipid identifications by computing per-lipid reporting-laboratory counts from a lab-by-lipid identification matrix and validating the overlap against a published reference figure (e.g. 339 of 1527 SRM 1950 sum-composition lipids reported by ≥5 of 31 laboratories). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.07.617094

skills.description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics CCS values need class- and adduct-specific correction and ≥3 U13C-labeled lipids of a lipid class-adduct combination (e.g., PC [M+H]+) are detected in measured data.
skills.name: resampling-based-correction-function-generation
skills.search_text: resampling-based-correction-function-generation Use when IM-MS lipidomics CCS values need class- and adduct-specific correction and ≥3 U13C-labeled lipids of a lipid class-adduct combination (e.g., PC [M+H]+) are detected in measured data. Fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids are detected for a lipid class-adduct combination — linear regression correction is not possible and CCS correction is skipped Only CCS bias monitoring (no correction) is needed — use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the CCS-correction workflow Lipid class-adduct combination is outside the supported set (e.g., LPE with [M+HCOO]) — MobiLipid restricts correction to specific class-adduct pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates up to 100 lipid class- and adduct-specific CCS correction functions in MobiLipid by resampling 3–6 U13C-labeled lipids per combination into linear regressions (y = m*x + b) mapping measured CCS to DTCCSN2 library values, enabling robust internal CCS correction without external calibrants. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: Generates up to 100 lipid class- and adduct-specific CCS correction functions in MobiLipid by resampling 3–6 U13C-labeled lipids per combination into linear regressions (y = m*x + b) mapping measured CCS to DTCCSN2 library values, enabling robust internal CCS correction without external calibrants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fewer than 3 U13C-labeled lipids are detected for a lipid class-adduct combination — linear regression correction is not possible and CCS correction is skipped Only CCS bias monitoring (no correction) is needed — use MobiLipid_CCS-bias-calculation.Rmd instead of the CCS-correction workflow Lipid class-adduct combination is outside the supported set (e.g., LPE with [M+HCOO]) — MobiLipid restricts correction to specific class-adduct pairs

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metabolomics normalization methods on replicate runs (especially between-batch replicates) and you need a robust concordance metric that avoids favoring any method, as an alternative to QC-sample RSD or differential-abundance-count benchmarks.
skills.name: rescaled-intensity-difference-computation
skills.search_text: rescaled-intensity-difference-computation Use when benchmarking metabolomics normalization methods on replicate runs (especially between-batch replicates) and you need a robust concordance metric that avoids favoring any method, as an alternative to QC-sample RSD or differential-abundance-count benchmarks. When there are no replicate pairs (e.g., only QC samples and single biological samples) — the metric is defined on between-replicate intensity differences and cannot be computed. When intensities are on the raw (non-log) scale — rescaled differences on raw intensities are not comparable to the log-transformed, base e intensities used in the article's computation. As a sole benchmark when multivariate methods (SERFF, TIGER) or a broader set of normalizations are of interest but the replicate structure is absent — the article flags that such benchmarking requires additional strategies. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies between-replicate concordance after normalization by computing, per replicate pair and compound, the difference between the two observed intensities rescaled by their mean intensity, then aggregating these into a MAD per normalization approach (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, SERFF, TIGER, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, unnormalized). Lower MAD indicates better correspondence of intensities across batches; this is the metric that showed the robust methods reducing MAD by 49–52% versus unnormalized data on BioH metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06841
skills.summary: Quantifies between-replicate concordance after normalization by computing, per replicate pair and compound, the difference between the two observed intensities rescaled by their mean intensity, then aggregating these into a MAD per normalization approach (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, SERFF, TIGER, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, unnormalized). Lower MAD indicates better correspondence of intensities across batches; this is the metric that showed the robust methods reducing MAD by 49–52% versus unnormalized data on BioH
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there are no replicate pairs (e.g., only QC samples and single biological samples) — the metric is defined on between-replicate intensity differences and cannot be computed. When intensities are on the raw (non-log) scale — rescaled differences on raw intensities are not comparable to the log-transformed, base e intensities used in the article's computation. As a sole benchmark when multivariate methods (SERFF, TIGER) or a broader set of normalizations are of interest but the replicate structure is absent — the article flags that such benchmarking requires additional strategies.

skills.description: Use when a review or paper reports multiple PSM rescoring benchmark results that must be reconciled into a structured comparison, especially when findings appear contradictory across tools or acquisition conditions (DDA vs timsTOF, RNN vs transformer predictors).
skills.name: rescoring-tool-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: rescoring-tool-benchmark-comparison Use when a review or paper reports multiple PSM rescoring benchmark results that must be reconciled into a structured comparison, especially when findings appear contradictory across tools or acquisition conditions (DDA vs timsTOF, RNN vs transformer predictors). When the goal is to actually execute PSM rescoring on spectra (feature generation with MS²PIP/DeepLC and ristretto SVM/LDA rescoring) rather than comparing published benchmark findings. When the source text reports only one tool's result with no cross-tool comparison to reconcile. When the article contains no methods/discussion sections reporting empirical results (e.g. a changelog-style document with no evaluation data). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts and cross-compares empirical PSM-rescoring benchmark findings reported across tools (DeepRescore, inSPIRE, MHCquant, MSBooster, Prosit, Percolator) into a structured finding–tool–condition table, so contradictory results (e.g. ΔRT judged ineffective by MHCquant but a top feature in DeepRescore) can be traced to their experimental conditions. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/pmic.202300336
skills.summary: Extracts and cross-compares empirical PSM-rescoring benchmark findings reported across tools (DeepRescore, inSPIRE, MHCquant, MSBooster, Prosit, Percolator) into a structured finding–tool–condition table, so contradictory results (e.g. ΔRT judged ineffective by MHCquant but a top feature in DeepRescore) can be traced to their experimental conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to actually execute PSM rescoring on spectra (feature generation with MS²PIP/DeepLC and ristretto SVM/LDA rescoring) rather than comparing published benchmark findings. When the source text reports only one tool's result with no cross-tool comparison to reconcile. When the article contains no methods/discussion sections reporting empirical results (e.g. a changelog-style document with no evaluation data).

skills.description: Use when a pathway-level kernel association test (PaIRKAT) must be run on metabolomics data that are confounded by clinical covariates, so covariate effects must be removed from each metabolite before computing kernel quadratic-form statistics.
skills.name: residual-based-covariate-adjustment
skills.search_text: residual-based-covariate-adjustment Use when a pathway-level kernel association test (PaIRKAT) must be run on metabolomics data that are confounded by clinical covariates, so covariate effects must be removed from each metabolite before computing kernel quadratic-form statistics. When covariates are themselves the target of inference — partial residuals remove covariate variation, so their effects cannot be tested downstream. When the association method already adjusts for covariates internally in a single joint regression rather than via a two-stage residual approach. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Adjusts metabolomic feature intensities for clinical confounders by fitting one linear regression per metabolite on the covariate set and carrying the partial residuals forward as the 'observed' metabolomics data for PaIRKAT's kernel score test. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Adjusts metabolomic feature intensities for clinical confounders by fitting one linear regression per metabolite on the covariate set and carrying the partial residuals forward as the 'observed' metabolomics data for PaIRKAT's kernel score test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When covariates are themselves the target of inference — partial residuals remove covariate variation, so their effects cannot be tested downstream. When the association method already adjusts for covariates internally in a single joint regression rather than via a two-stage residual approach.

skills.search_text: residual-discordance-fraction-derivation Use when comparing binary molecular subgroups (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high or MYC-high from k-means clustering) against SNP-array alteration calls (10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) and you need the fraction of altered cases within each subgroup denominator. skills.description: Use when matching two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables: residuals from an estimated inter-dataset RT/mz/FI shift must be normalized robustly (median + F×MAD) before scoring or threshold tightening.
skills.name: residual-mad-normalization
skills.search_text: residual-mad-normalization Use when matching two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables: residuals from an estimated inter-dataset RT/mz/FI shift must be normalized robustly (median + F×MAD) before scoring or threshold tightening. The datasets are already harmonized or the shift is known a priori — residual normalization would add noise rather than adapt thresholds. The comparison is between a feature table and a database annotation (e.g. LIPID MAPS, HMDB, METLIN) rather than two experimental LC–MS feature lists; M2S matching is designed for dataset-to-dataset correspondence. Feature intensities are absent or unreliable and you cannot compute log10FI residuals, yet FI-domain thresholds are required — MAD normalization of FI residuals needs valid FI medians. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Robustly normalizes the residuals of each candidate feature match (in RT, m/z, and log10FI) relative to the expected inter-dataset shift, using median + F×MAD scaling, so that a weighted penalization score can select unique correspondences and flag poor matches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03592
skills.summary: Robustly normalizes the residuals of each candidate feature match (in RT, m/z, and log10FI) relative to the expected inter-dataset shift, using median + F×MAD scaling, so that a weighted penalization score can select unique correspondences and flag poor matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets are already harmonized or the shift is known a priori — residual normalization would add noise rather than adapt thresholds. The comparison is between a feature table and a database annotation (e.g. LIPID MAPS, HMDB, METLIN) rather than two experimental LC–MS feature lists; M2S matching is designed for dataset-to-dataset correspondence. skills.name: residue-abundance-rank-verification
skills.search_text: residue-abundance-rank-verification Use when lipidomic abundance tables from hepatocyte cell models (PHH, HLC, HepG2 and their media) must be converted to fatty acid residue counts and checked for cell-type-specific rank patterns. Input identifiers are not parseable as 'CLASS N:N/M:M' or RefMet-compliant names and cannot be batch-translated with RefMet's online translator — liputils residue extraction will fail The question concerns individual molecular lipid species rather than aggregate fatty acid residue patterns (e.g. a PCA on individual molecular lipids was also performed in the paper) The table contains non-numerical columns or total lipid class counts and you are not using make_residues_table()'s cleanup/unwanted handling http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reprocesses cultured-cell lipidomic data with liputils to extract fatty acid residue abundances, then verifies cell-type residue patterns: that 18:1, 16:0, 18:2 and 20:4 rank highest in HepG2 culture medium and that HLC 16:0/18:1 levels sit closer to PHHs than to HepG2. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70259-9
skills.summary: Reprocesses cultured-cell lipidomic data with liputils to extract fatty acid residue abundances, then verifies cell-type residue patterns: that 18:1, 16:0, 18:2 and 20:4 rank highest in HepG2 culture medium and that HLC 16:0/18:1 levels sit closer to PHHs than to HepG2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input identifiers are not parseable as 'CLASS N:N/M:M' or RefMet-compliant names and cannot be batch-translated with RefMet's online translator — liputils residue extraction will fail The question concerns individual molecular lipid species rather than aggregate fatty acid residue patterns (e.g. a PCA on individual molecular lipids was also performed in the paper) The table contains non-numerical columns or total lipid class counts and you are not using make_residues_table()'s cleanup/unwanted handling

skills.description: Use when converting a SMILES structure into building-block sequences and each residue's formula/mass is needed for CycloBranch export, especially when blocks like Put (amine-terminated, oxygen-free) break the standard water-elimination convention.
skills.name: residue-formula-monoisotopic-mass-calculation
skills.search_text: residue-formula-monoisotopic-mass-calculation Use when converting a SMILES structure into building-block sequences and each residue's formula/mass is needed for CycloBranch export, especially when blocks like Put (amine-terminated, oxygen-free) break the standard water-elimination convention. The input is already a building-block database with residue formulas (e.g. an existing CycloBranch or Norine export) — no recomputation is needed The target tool cannot accept custom building-block databases (e.g. NRPro, where users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences) The structure is a simple peptide composed solely of canonical amino acids whose residue formulas are already known Computes residue molecular formulas and monoisotopic masses for nonribosomal peptide/polyketide building blocks during SMILES-to-sequence decomposition, applying water elimination by default and a two-hydrogen elimination for oxygen-free diamine blocks such as putrescine (Put: C4H12N2 -> C4H10N2). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00530-2
skills.summary: Computes residue molecular formulas and monoisotopic masses for nonribosomal peptide/polyketide building blocks during SMILES-to-sequence decomposition, applying water elimination by default and a two-hydrogen elimination for oxygen-free diamine blocks such as putrescine (Put: C4H12N2 -> C4H10N2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a building-block database with residue formulas (e.g. an existing CycloBranch or Norine export) — no recomputation is needed The target tool cannot accept custom building-block databases (e.g. NRPro, where users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences) The structure is a simple peptide composed solely of canonical amino acids whose residue formulas are already known

skills.description: Use when ion images from METASPACE-style imaging MS datasets must be classified as off-sample vs on-sample with a pretrained ResNet-50, or when reproducing the paper's off-sample frequency counts over DESI datasets.
skills.name: resnet-transfer-learning-inference
skills.search_text: resnet-transfer-learning-inference Use when ion images from METASPACE-style imaging MS datasets must be classified as off-sample vs on-sample with a pretrained ResNet-50, or when reproducing the paper's off-sample frequency counts over DESI datasets. The goal is per-pixel localization of the off-sample region — the authors state 'our approach does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region' Input is raw imaging MS data (e.g. imzML/mzML) rather than pre-generated ion images — the model operates on rendered ion images, not raw spectra Labelled training data is absent and only unsupervised/semi-automated approaches are acceptable — biclustering (F1 0.96) or molecular co-localization (F1 0.90) are the paper's alternatives, but this skill specifically requires a trained supervised model http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Apply the ResNet-50 CNN (pretrained on ImageNet) via the fastai/PyTorch stack to classify MALDI imaging MS ion images as off-sample or on-sample, reproducing the OffsampleAI deep learning approach that reached F1-score 0.97 on the 23,238-image gold standard. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-020-3425-x
skills.summary: Apply the ResNet-50 CNN (pretrained on ImageNet) via the fastai/PyTorch stack to classify MALDI imaging MS ion images as off-sample or on-sample, reproducing the OffsampleAI deep learning approach that reached F1-score 0.97 on the 23,238-image gold standard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-pixel localization of the off-sample region — the authors state 'our approach does not solve the segmentation problem of finding pixels which are in the off-sample region' Input is raw imaging MS data (e.g. imzML/mzML) rather than pre-generated ion images — the model operates on rendered ion images, not raw spectra Labelled training data is absent and only unsupervised/semi-automated approaches are acceptable — biclustering (F1 0.96) or molecular co-localization (F1 0.90) are the paper's alternatives, but this skill specifically requires a trained supervised model

skills.description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope labeling data (13C, 2H, 15N, 18O, or 34S tracers) acquired on Orbitrap-class analyzers where resolution-dependent isotopolog overlap makes combinatorial correction (IsoCor-style NRE) inaccurate.
skills.name: resolution-dependent-isotope-correction
skills.search_text: resolution-dependent-isotope-correction Use when correcting LC-MS isotope labeling data (13C, 2H, 15N, 18O, or 34S tracers) acquired on Orbitrap-class analyzers where resolution-dependent isotopolog overlap makes combinatorial correction (IsoCor-style NRE) inaccurate. The tracer element is not present in some compounds' formulas (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N-only data) — the algorithm will report an error and the software will not run properly Instrument resolution is extremely low, where ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor's combinatorial correction and the resolution-aware machinery adds no value Only FAM-to-MDV conversion without correction is needed — this skill is specifically the natural-abundance/impurity correction step, not downstream flux fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Apply ElemCor's modified mass difference theory (MDT) and unlabeled-sample (ULS) corrections to convert measured fractional abundances of isotopologs (FAM) into mass distribution vectors (MDV) and isotopic enrichment, explicitly accounting for instrument resolution effects on high-resolving-power LC-MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Apply ElemCor's modified mass difference theory (MDT) and unlabeled-sample (ULS) corrections to convert measured fractional abundances of isotopologs (FAM) into mass distribution vectors (MDV) and isotopic enrichment, explicitly accounting for instrument resolution effects on high-resolving-power LC-MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tracer element is not present in some compounds' formulas (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N-only data) — the algorithm will report an error and the software will not run properly Instrument resolution is extremely low, where ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor's combinatorial correction and the resolution-aware machinery adds no value Only FAM-to-MDV conversion without correction is needed — this skill is specifically the natural-abundance/impurity correction step, not downstream flux fitting

skills.description: Use when a paper claims a dataset was harmonized from a numeric minimum of source resources (e.g. 'over 40 electronic resources') and you must audit that claim by enumerating the resources into an inventory.
skills.name: resource-count-verification
skills.search_text: resource-count-verification Use when a paper claims a dataset was harmonized from a numeric minimum of source resources (e.g. 'over 40 electronic resources') and you must audit that claim by enumerating the resources into an inventory. When the paper does not state a numeric threshold for resource count — extraction would produce an unverifiable list When the goal is to use the resources themselves rather than audit the count — this skill inventories names only, it does not harvest data from them http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_3077 Extracts the named electronic natural-product resources that LOTUS harmonized from the article text and tabulates them into a structured inventory, verifying that the count meets the paper's stated threshold of over 40 electronic resources. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Extracts the named electronic natural-product resources that LOTUS harmonized from the article text and tabulates them into a structured inventory, verifying that the count meets the paper's stated threshold of over 40 electronic resources.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the paper does not state a numeric threshold for resource count — extraction would produce an unverifiable list When the goal is to use the resources themselves rather than audit the count — this skill inventories names only, it does not harvest data from them

skills.description: Use when evaluating accuracy of inferred absolute concentration scaling factors (response factors) from relative abundance GC-MS time-course data, by binning per-metabolite errors against known ground truth and comparing to negative controls.
skills.name: response-factor-error-binning-analysis
skills.search_text: response-factor-error-binning-analysis Use when evaluating accuracy of inferred absolute concentration scaling factors (response factors) from relative abundance GC-MS time-course data, by binning per-metabolite errors against known ground truth and comparing to negative controls. Data are noisy real measurements without simulated ground-truth response factors — no true RF reference exists to bin errors against. The goal is de novo inference on a new metabolic system rather than benchmarking MetaboPAC against negative controls on simulated data. Assessing noisy-data performance across sampling frequencies/CoV requires the MetaboPAC_*_noisy.m variant workflow, not the noiseless error-binning setup. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarking analysis that compares MetaboPAC-inferred response factors to true simulated response factors by computing the fraction falling within error tolerance bins of log2(1.1), log2(1.3), and log2(1.5), then statistically testing against negative-control methods. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Benchmarking analysis that compares MetaboPAC-inferred response factors to true simulated response factors by computing the fraction falling within error tolerance bins of log2(1.1), log2(1.3), and log2(1.5), then statistically testing against negative-control methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are noisy real measurements without simulated ground-truth response factors — no true RF reference exists to bin errors against. The goal is de novo inference on a new metabolic system rather than benchmarking MetaboPAC against negative controls on simulated data. Assessing noisy-data performance across sampling frequencies/CoV requires the MetaboPAC_*_noisy.m variant workflow, not the noiseless error-binning setup.

skills.description: Decision support for validating response factor inference on GC-MS relative abundance data when no published comparator method exists, by simulating random and constant response factor baselines.
skills.name: response-factor-negative-control-simulation
skills.search_text: response-factor-negative-control-simulation Decision support for validating response factor inference on GC-MS relative abundance data when no published comparator method exists, by simulating random and constant response factor baselines. MetaboPAC has already been shown to outperform these baselines in the manuscript — the comparison only serves as validation, not as a primary analysis of absolute concentration inference. The dataset contains known kinetic equations for all metabolites; negative controls are only needed when no a priori kinetic information exists (percKnownKinetics = 0). http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates negative-control baselines for MetaboPAC's response factor inference — random response factors sampled uniformly between 1 and 1000, and a constant response factor of 500 — so that MetaboPAC's accuracy can be judged against naive baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Generates negative-control baselines for MetaboPAC's response factor inference — random response factors sampled uniformly between 1 and 1000, and a constant response factor of 500 — so that MetaboPAC's accuracy can be judged against naive baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MetaboPAC has already been shown to outperform these baselines in the manuscript — the comparison only serves as validation, not as a primary analysis of absolute concentration inference. The dataset contains known kinetic equations for all metabolites; negative controls are only needed when no a priori kinetic information exists (percKnownKinetics = 0).

skills.description: Use when time-course metabolomics data provide only relative abundances (no fluxomics measurements) but a stoichiometric matrix and time vector exist, and flux profiles are needed for MetaboPAC's penalty calculation.
skills.name: response-factor-normalization-of-abundances
skills.search_text: response-factor-normalization-of-abundances Use when time-course metabolomics data provide only relative abundances (no fluxomics measurements) but a stoichiometric matrix and time vector exist, and flux profiles are needed for MetaboPAC's penalty calculation. Eukaryotic multi-compartment systems: MetaboPAC does not take into consideration transport reactions across different intracellular compartments and only applies to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment Datasets with high noise or heavy missingness that violate mass balances — high noise levels complicate assessment of biological feasibility and 10% missingness with imputation reduces inferred-concentration accuracy Cases where response factors are known to be strongly concentration-dependent (nonlinear ionization/suppression), since MetaboPAC assumes constant response factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A MetaboPAC sub-procedure that infers metabolic flux profiles from time-course relative-abundance GC-MS data by converting smoothed rates of change of relative abundance into rates of change of absolute concentration via response factors, then solving the stoichiometric mass-balance system S·v = dx/dt. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: A MetaboPAC sub-procedure that infers metabolic flux profiles from time-course relative-abundance GC-MS data by converting smoothed rates of change of relative abundance into rates of change of absolute concentration via response factors, then solving the stoichiometric mass-balance system S·v = dx/dt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Eukaryotic multi-compartment systems: MetaboPAC does not take into consideration transport reactions across different intracellular compartments and only applies to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment Datasets with high noise or heavy missingness that violate mass balances — high noise levels complicate assessment of biological feasibility and 10% missingness with imputation reduces inferred-concentration accuracy Cases where response factors are known to be strongly concentration-dependent (nonlinear ionization/suppression), since MetaboPAC assumes constant response factors

skills.description: Use when metabolomics time-course data are relative abundances only, a stoichiometric model with known kinetic equations for some metabolites is available, and absolute concentrations must be inferred standard-free.
skills.name: response-factor-optimization-with-known-kinetics
skills.search_text: response-factor-optimization-with-known-kinetics Use when metabolomics time-course data are relative abundances only, a stoichiometric model with known kinetic equations for some metabolites is available, and absolute concentrations must be inferred standard-free. The metabolomics sample spans multiple compartments or includes transport reactions — MetaboPAC does not consider transport across intracellular compartments in eukaryotic systems No kinetic equations or biological penalty information exist for any metabolite, leaving the kinetic-equation step with nothing to fix Response factors are strongly concentration-dependent (nonlinear ion suppression), since RFs are assumed constant with concentration http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A MetaboPAC strategy that fixes the response factors of metabolites whose kinetic equations are fully known (via the kinetic-equations approach) and then heuristically optimizes the remaining response factors against mass balances and biological penalty functions, improving absolute-concentration inference from relative-abundance GC-MS time-course data. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: A MetaboPAC strategy that fixes the response factors of metabolites whose kinetic equations are fully known (via the kinetic-equations approach) and then heuristically optimizes the remaining response factors against mass balances and biological penalty functions, improving absolute-concentration inference from relative-abundance GC-MS time-course data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolomics sample spans multiple compartments or includes transport reactions — MetaboPAC does not consider transport across intracellular compartments in eukaryotic systems No kinetic equations or biological penalty information exist for any metabolite, leaving the kinetic-equation step with nothing to fix Response factors are strongly concentration-dependent (nonlinear ion suppression), since RFs are assumed constant with concentration

skills.description: Use when a scientific database exposes REST Web services with an OpenAPI (v3.0) spec and you need programmatic, filterable retrieval of records (compounds, spectra) into a tabular dataset.
skills.name: rest-api-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: rest-api-data-retrieval Use when a scientific database exposes REST Web services with an OpenAPI (v3.0) spec and you need programmatic, filterable retrieval of records (compounds, spectra) into a tabular dataset. You need raw spectral data storage or retrieval — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data The data need cleaning or extraction before retrieval — PeakForest does not include data clean-up or extraction tools and requires metadata to be manually entered/curated upstream A one-off interactive browse through the Web interface suffices; scripted REST retrieval adds unnecessary setup Retrieve structured records (e.g. the 96-compound PeakForest demonstrator collection) from a scientific Web service over REST, using its OpenAPI (v3.0) specification to generate a typed client and its built-in filter system (column characteristics, AND/OR logic gates) to scope queries. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-022-01899-3
skills.summary: Retrieve structured records (e.g. the 96-compound PeakForest demonstrator collection) from a scientific Web service over REST, using its OpenAPI (v3.0) specification to generate a typed client and its built-in filter system (column characteristics, AND/OR logic gates) to scope queries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need raw spectral data storage or retrieval — PeakForest is designed for metabolite annotation report data rather than storage of raw spectral data The data need cleaning or extraction before retrieval — PeakForest does not include data clean-up or extraction tools and requires metadata to be manually entered/curated upstream A one-off interactive browse through the Web interface suffices; scripted REST retrieval adds unnecessary setup

skills.description: Use when standardized sample metadata produced by the SMetaS freetext-transformation pipeline must be consumed programmatically by downstream pipelines or database frontends, in parallel with a standardized CSV export.

skills.search_text: rest-api-endpoint-exposure Use when standardized sample metadata produced by the SMetaS freetext-transformation pipeline must be consumed programmatically by downstream pipelines or database frontends, in parallel with a standardized CSV export. The metadata are already standardized against the fixed vocabularies and only need redistribution, not re-exposure via the API. Only a file-based handoff is needed and no pipeline integration or programmatic query of submitted studies/authors is required. skills.search_text: rest-api-json-response-handling Use when a downstream analysis consumes data retrieved from a REST-style endpoint that returns JSON documents — e.g. chemical annotation records from PUG-View, whose response follows the PUG-View annotation content model (the same model as the ASNT/ASNB formats). When multiple record identifiers must be queried in a single call, since a PUG-View request cannot take multiple input record identifiers. Handles parsing and validating JSON response payloads returned by REST-style web service interfaces, exemplified here by PubChem's PUG-View service, ensuring programmatic access to structured annotation data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-019-0375-2
skills.summary: Handles parsing and validating JSON response payloads returned by REST-style web service interfaces, exemplified here by PubChem's PUG-View service, ensuring programmatic access to structured annotation data.

skills.summary: Computation of metabolite annotation confidence errors during margheRita metabolite_identification(), where each feature-metabolite match is reported with a mass-accuracy error in ppm, a retention-time error, and a retention-index error against the in-house spectral library of reference standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features lack MS/MS information or the reference standard is absent from the selected library — level-1 confidence cannot be achieved, only lower-level annotation Data were acquired on a chromatographic column or polarity not covered by the margheRita libraries (HILIC, LipC8, pZIC, RPLong, RPShort in positive/negative modes) Input is raw instrument data rather than an mRList processed by upstream margheRita pre-processing (quality control, filtering, normalization)

skills.description: Use when aligned per-sample peaklists (m/z–RT pairs) from multiple LC/HRMS samples or batches show systematic RT drift, and no external RT standard ladder is available — indigenous recurring peaks serve as the reference markers.
skills.name: retention-index-log-interpolation
skills.search_text: retention-index-log-interpolation Use when aligned per-sample peaklists (m/z–RT pairs) from multiple LC/HRMS samples or batches show systematic RT drift, and no external RT standard ladder is available — indigenous recurring peaks serve as the reference markers. Only a single HRMS data file is being processed (no cross-sample/batch drift to correct — the article's peak-picking results for MTBLS1684 file 003.d were computed without this step being the goal) The input is already an aligned, drift-corrected feature table (e.g. from MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA or MS-DIAL) — applying equation 5 again would double-correct RTs The sample has too few indigenous reference markers bracketing a peak and the median-drift fallback is unacceptable for the downstream statistical analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies the IDSL.IPA retention index approach (equation 5) to correct systematic retention time drift in untargeted LC/HRMS peaklists by interpolating RT shifts against a dynamic pool of indigenous (endogenous) reference peak markers that bracket each peak in time. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: Applies the IDSL.IPA retention index approach (equation 5) to correct systematic retention time drift in untargeted LC/HRMS peaklists by interpolating RT shifts against a dynamic pool of indigenous (endogenous) reference peak markers that bracket each peak in time.

skills.description: Use when metabolite features are named by retention-index codes (RI<value> format) from GC-based metabolomics and standard identifiers are required before KEGG pathway enrichment or compound mapping.
skills.name: retention-index-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: retention-index-metabolite-annotation Use when metabolite features are named by retention-index codes (RI<value> format) from GC-based metabolomics and standard identifiers are required before KEGG pathway enrichment or compound mapping. Metabolite names are already standard database identifiers (e.g., KEGG compound IDs, HMDB) — conversion is redundant before KEGGREST pathway mapping. The analysis goal is pathway enrichment itself rather than identifier resolution — use MeTEor's KEGGREST-based 'Map to KEGG Pathways' step once valid IDs exist. The workflow requires fully automated, API-driven ID conversion — this skill is explicitly a manual workaround while the MetaboAnalyst API is unavailable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Resolves retention-index-coded metabolite names (e.g., RI1150.81, RI1532.53, RI1557.73) into standard database identifiers via the MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion service so they can be mapped to KEGG pathways. Because the MetaboAnalyst API is unavailable, the resolution is a documented manual submission workaround. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae178
skills.summary: Resolves retention-index-coded metabolite names (e.g., RI1150.81, RI1532.53, RI1557.73) into standard database identifiers via the MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion service so they can be mapped to KEGG pathways. Because the MetaboAnalyst API is unavailable, the resolution is a documented manual submission workaround.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metabolite names are already standard database identifiers (e.g., KEGG compound IDs, HMDB) — conversion is redundant before KEGGREST pathway mapping. The analysis goal is pathway enrichment itself rather than identifier resolution — use MeTEor's KEGGREST-based 'Map to KEGG Pathways' step once valid IDs exist. The workflow requires fully automated, API-driven ID conversion — this skill is explicitly a manual workaround while the MetaboAnalyst API is unavailable.
