skills.search_text: retention-migration-time-transcription Use when a supplementary DOCX table reports per-method RT/MT ± sd and checkmark/cross detection flags for standard analytes and these must be converted into a machine-readable coverage matrix for verifying multi-platform metabolite coverage claims. The goal is feature detection or augmentation from raw mzML/mzXML MS data — use the AriumMS ROI/augmentation pipeline instead, which this table merely summarizes The analyte data are already available as a structured feature table or CSV — re-transcribing the DOCX adds no information Only single-platform (e.g. HILIC-MS alone) coverage is of interest — the value of this skill lies in cross-method (CE-MS vs HILIC-MS) coverage comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Transcribes the retention time (RT, LC-MS) and migration time (MT, CE-MS) values with standard deviations plus per-platform detection flags from the standard-analyte table (Table 1) of the AriumMS electronic supplementary file into a structured CSV, and recomputes multi-platform coverage counts (HILIC 30/36, CE 32/36, all five methods 36/36). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Transcribes the retention time (RT, LC-MS) and migration time (MT, CE-MS) values with standard deviations plus per-platform detection flags from the standard-analyte table (Table 1) of the AriumMS electronic supplementary file into a structured CSV, and recomputes multi-platform coverage counts (HILIC 30/36, CE 32/36, all five methods 36/36).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is feature detection or augmentation from raw mzML/mzXML MS data — use the AriumMS ROI/augmentation pipeline instead, which this table merely summarizes The analyte data are already available as a structured feature table or CSV — re-transcribing the DOCX adds no information Only single-platform (e.g. HILIC-MS alone) coverage is of interest — the value of this skill lies in cross-method (CE-MS vs HILIC-MS) coverage comparison

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether molecular fingerprint representation (counting vs binary, Min-Max vs Tanimoto kernel) affects pairwise retention order accuracy in a single-system RankSVM setting.
skills.name: retention-order-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: retention-order-accuracy-comparison Use when evaluating whether molecular fingerprint representation (counting vs binary, Min-Max vs Tanimoto kernel) affects pairwise retention order accuracy in a single-system RankSVM setting. The goal is the multi-system training setting (Tables 4 or Figures 4) — use the all_on_one or *_perc scenarios instead, not baseline_single. Retention time prediction rather than retention order prediction is needed — use the SVR estimator rather than RankSVM. The binary/counting MACCS fingerprints have not yet been computed in data/processed; fingerprint calculation with rcdk/rcdkTools must be run first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Reproduces the Table 3 (first two columns) comparison showing that counting MACCS fingerprints with the Min-Max kernel outperform binary MACCS fingerprints with the Tanimoto kernel for RankSVM retention order prediction when a single PredRet system is used for both training and testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty590
skills.summary: Reproduces the Table 3 (first two columns) comparison showing that counting MACCS fingerprints with the Min-Max kernel outperform binary MACCS fingerprints with the Tanimoto kernel for RankSVM retention order prediction when a single PredRet system is used for both training and testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is the multi-system training setting (Tables 4 or Figures 4) — use the all_on_one or *_perc scenarios instead, not baseline_single. Retention time prediction rather than retention order prediction is needed — use the SVR estimator rather than RankSVM. The binary/counting MACCS fingerprints have not yet been computed in data/processed; fingerprint calculation with rcdk/rcdkTools must be run first.

skills.description: Use when multiple paired RPLC retention datasets (e.g., from RepoRT, PredRet, Metabolome Workbench, MetaboLights) share compounds and you need to test whether eluent pH or other configuration attributes explain retention-order replicability.
skills.name: retention-order-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: retention-order-correlation-analysis Use when multiple paired RPLC retention datasets (e.g., from RepoRT, PredRet, Metabolome Workbench, MetaboLights) share compounds and you need to test whether eluent pH or other configuration attributes explain retention-order replicability. You need to predict retention orders for candidate molecules rather than measure replicability across existing datasets — use ROASMI (RankNet/D-MPNN model) instead. The datasets are HILIC or unpaired single-run data with no shared compounds between runs — CCRS between paired retention orders cannot be computed. You are scoring MS/MS spectra or integrating spectral scores; this skill analyzes only retention-order agreement, not MS/MS evidence. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies how well compound elution order replicates between paired RPLC datasets using CCRS (correlation coefficient of retention sequences), then relates CCRS to chromatographic configuration differences (ΔpH, ΔF, Δtemperature) to identify which factor drives retention-order replicability. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Quantifies how well compound elution order replicates between paired RPLC datasets using CCRS (correlation coefficient of retention sequences), then relates CCRS to chromatographic configuration differences (ΔpH, ΔF, Δtemperature) to identify which factor drives retention-order replicability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to predict retention orders for candidate molecules rather than measure replicability across existing datasets — use ROASMI (RankNet/D-MPNN model) instead. The datasets are HILIC or unpaired single-run data with no shared compounds between runs — CCRS between paired retention orders cannot be computed. You are scoring MS/MS spectra or integrating spectral scores; this skill analyzes only retention-order agreement, not MS/MS evidence.

skills.description: Use when you already have per-spectrum scored candidate molecule lists from an MS/MS predictor (e.g. IOKR) plus retention times for a complete LC-MS/MS run, and want to jointly identify the whole metabolite set using retention order constraints.
skills.name: retention-order-integrated-metabolite-identification
skills.search_text: retention-order-integrated-metabolite-identification Use when you already have per-spectrum scored candidate molecule lists from an MS/MS predictor (e.g. IOKR) plus retention times for a complete LC-MS/MS run, and want to jointly identify the whole metabolite set using retention order constraints. You only have a single MS/MS spectrum to identify (no retention-time ordering information across the run) — the layered graph and rank-conflict penalty are undefined without ordered layers Retention times are unavailable for the target chromatographic system and no measurements from other LC systems exist to train the RankSVM order predictor You want standalone retention-time prediction rather than retention-order-based joint identification — the paper notes SVR-based retention time prediction is limited in its capacity to use data from other chromatographic systems, unlike RankSVM http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Combines IOKR MS/MS-based candidate scores with RankSVM-predicted retention orders by solving a shortest-path problem over a layered directed graph of candidate structures, improving metabolite identification accuracy across a complete LC-MS/MS run (up to 24.8% at D=0.0075 in the PredRet LTSO setting). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty590
skills.summary: Combines IOKR MS/MS-based candidate scores with RankSVM-predicted retention orders by solving a shortest-path problem over a layered directed graph of candidate structures, improving metabolite identification accuracy across a complete LC-MS/MS run (up to 24.8% at D=0.0075 in the PredRet LTSO setting).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single MS/MS spectrum to identify (no retention-time ordering information across the run) — the layered graph and rank-conflict penalty are undefined without ordered layers Retention times are unavailable for the target chromatographic system and no measurements from other LC systems exist to train the RankSVM order predictor You want standalone retention-time prediction rather than retention-order-based joint identification — the paper notes SVR-based retention time prediction is limited in its capacity to use data from other chromatographic systems, unlike RankSVM

skills.description: Use when you need to train or fine-tune a retention-order prediction model from RT data of a reference compound set (e.g. dataset_87), producing pairwise P_ij elution probabilities for candidate small molecules in an RPLC system with eluent pH ~2.7.
skills.name: retention-order-model-training
skills.search_text: retention-order-model-training Use when you need to train or fine-tune a retention-order prediction model from RT data of a reference compound set (e.g. dataset_87), producing pairwise P_ij elution probabilities for candidate small molecules in an RPLC system with eluent pH ~2.7. The compounds fall outside conventional elemental restrictions (C, H, N, O, P, S) — ROASMI's scope is limited to these elements You are working in a HILIC chromatographic system: ROASMI's initial models are specific to RPLC at eluent pH ~2.7; HILIC retraining is possible (dataset_83/dataset_84) but constructing generalizable HILIC models is explicitly described as future work You need absolute RT predictions rather than retention-order probabilities — the model outputs pairwise order probabilities, not RT values http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a RankNet-based retention-order model (ROASMI) that couples chemprop D-MPNN molecular embeddings with pairwise elution-order probabilities, enabling retention-score prediction across new chemical and chromatographic spaces. The core insight is predicting retention order rather than absolute RT, which sidesteps the poor replicability of RTs across chromatographic methods. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Trains a RankNet-based retention-order model (ROASMI) that couples chemprop D-MPNN molecular embeddings with pairwise elution-order probabilities, enabling retention-score prediction across new chemical and chromatographic spaces. The core insight is predicting retention order rather than absolute RT, which sidesteps the poor replicability of RTs across chromatographic methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compounds fall outside conventional elemental restrictions (C, H, N, O, P, S) — ROASMI's scope is limited to these elements You are working in a HILIC chromatographic system: ROASMI's initial models are specific to RPLC at eluent pH ~2.7; HILIC retraining is possible (dataset_83/dataset_84) but constructing generalizable HILIC models is explicitly described as future work You need absolute RT predictions rather than retention-order probabilities — the model outputs pairwise order probabilities, not RT values

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how accurately a retention-order model ranks pairs of molecules for specific chromatographic systems (e.g. Eawag_XBridgeC18, FEM_long, RIKEN), and compare single-system versus pooled multi-system training regimes.
skills.name: retention-order-pairwise-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: retention-order-pairwise-accuracy-evaluation Use when you must quantify how accurately a retention-order model ranks pairs of molecules for specific chromatographic systems (e.g. Eawag_XBridgeC18, FEM_long, RIKEN), and compare single-system versus pooled multi-system training regimes. When the goal is metabolite identification performance (MS/MS + retention-order integration with IOKR and dynamic programming, scenario met_ident_perf_GS_BS) rather than pairwise-order accuracy on PredRet systems When predicting absolute retention times is the end goal — SVR is the wrong tool for cross-system pooling because 'The SVR retention time baseline does not benefit from retention time data that comes from different chromatographic systems' When the input is already aggregated per-system results; this skill runs the scenario estimation itself, not re-analysis of finished accuracy tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates retention-order predictors (RankSVM, or SVR mapped to pairwise orders) by pairwise accuracy over molecule pairs across evaluation scenarios (baseline_single, all_on_one with LTSO True/False) on the PredRet dataset, enabling comparison against the paper's Table 3/4 and Figure 4. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty590
skills.summary: Evaluates retention-order predictors (RankSVM, or SVR mapped to pairwise orders) by pairwise accuracy over molecule pairs across evaluation scenarios (baseline_single, all_on_one with LTSO True/False) on the PredRet dataset, enabling comparison against the paper's Table 3/4 and Figure 4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is metabolite identification performance (MS/MS + retention-order integration with IOKR and dynamic programming, scenario met_ident_perf_GS_BS) rather than pairwise-order accuracy on PredRet systems When predicting absolute retention times is the end goal — SVR is the wrong tool for cross-system pooling because 'The SVR retention time baseline does not benefit from retention time data that comes from different chromatographic systems' When the input is already aggregated per-system results; this skill runs the scenario estimation itself, not re-analysis of finished accuracy tables

skills.description: Use when training MS/MS spectral encoders on large unannotated LC-MS/MS collections (e.g., GeMS mined from MassIVE GNPS) and you want representations that cluster by molecular structure without supervised labels.
skills.name: retention-order-prediction-selfsupervision
skills.search_text: retention-order-prediction-selfsupervision Use when training MS/MS spectral encoders on large unannotated LC-MS/MS collections (e.g., GeMS mined from MassIVE GNPS) and you want representations that cluster by molecular structure without supervised labels. When you have a labeled spectral library (MoNA, NIST20) and a supervised prediction objective — fine-tuned DreaMS or MIST-style supervised models are the appropriate choice there When your spectra are outside the training distribution, e.g., negative ionization mode or multiply charged precursor ions, which the current model does not incorporate When the analysis requires MS1 isotopic patterns or adduct distributions — this method focuses solely on tandem mass spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A self-supervised pre-training scheme in which a 116-million-parameter transformer (DreaMS) is trained on unannotated tandem mass spectra from the GeMS dataset using masked m/z-bin peak prediction and chromatographic retention order prediction as auxiliary tasks. This induces 1,024-dimensional embeddings organized by molecular structural similarity without requiring labeled spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: A self-supervised pre-training scheme in which a 116-million-parameter transformer (DreaMS) is trained on unannotated tandem mass spectra from the GeMS dataset using masked m/z-bin peak prediction and chromatographic retention order prediction as auxiliary tasks. This induces 1,024-dimensional embeddings organized by molecular structural similarity without requiring labeled spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you have a labeled spectral library (MoNA, NIST20) and a supervised prediction objective — fine-tuned DreaMS or MIST-style supervised models are the appropriate choice there When your spectra are outside the training distribution, e.g., negative ionization mode or multiply charged precursor ions, which the current model does not incorporate When the analysis requires MS1 isotopic patterns or adduct distributions — this method focuses solely on tandem mass spectra

skills.description: Use when ready-to-identify datasets carry candidate molecular pairs with ROASMI retention scores and you must exclude indistinguishable pairs or infer elution order for identification.
skills.name: retention-order-probability-sourcing-from-roasmi-predictions
skills.search_text: retention-order-probability-sourcing-from-roasmi-predictions Use when ready-to-identify datasets carry candidate molecular pairs with ROASMI retention scores and you must exclude indistinguishable pairs or infer elution order for identification. A single trained model is available without the full ensemble, since variance-based uncertainty quantification requires the multi-model ensemble. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Converts ROASMI-predicted retention-order probabilities P_ij and variances between candidate compound pairs into filtered, distinguishable pairwise constraints used to resolve peak identity in untargeted metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Converts ROASMI-predicted retention-order probabilities P_ij and variances between candidate compound pairs into filtered, distinguishable pairwise constraints used to resolve peak identity in untargeted metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Chromatographic system is HILIC rather than RPLC — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems. Candidate compounds fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S. A single trained model is available without the full ensemble, since variance-based uncertainty quantification requires the multi-model ensemble.

skills.search_text: retention-score-integrated-candidate-reranking Use when ready-to-identify candidate lists from MS/MS tools (e.g. SIRIUS or MS-DIAL outputs as CSV) exist for RPLC-MS/MS peaks and retention-order scores should be integrated to improve top-k accuracy. The chromatography is HILIC — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems and HILIC models with generalizability are future work Candidates fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S or otherwise leave ROASMI's application domain A peak's candidate pairs are retention-indistinguishable (chromatographic peaks close enough that order is inconsistent across experiments) — such pairs should be excluded rather than ranked http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Re-ranks candidate lists produced by MS/MS identification tools (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) by combining ROASMI-predicted retention-order scores with MS/MS scores using the probabilistic integration framework of msms_rt_score_integration, improving top-k identification accuracy on RPLC metabolomics peaks. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Re-ranks candidate lists produced by MS/MS identification tools (SIRIUS, MS-DIAL) by combining ROASMI-predicted retention-order scores with MS/MS scores using the probabilistic integration framework of msms_rt_score_integration, improving top-k identification accuracy on RPLC metabolomics peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chromatography is HILIC — ROASMI currently applies only to RPLC systems and HILIC models with generalizability are future work Candidates fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S or otherwise leave ROASMI's application domain A peak's candidate pairs are retention-indistinguishable (chromatographic peaks close enough that order is inconsistent across experiments) — such pairs should be excluded rather than ranked

skills.search_text: retention-time-agnostic-memo-matrix-merging Use when new LC-MS/MS samples must be added to an existing metabolomics sample-comparison matrix despite different LC gradients (e.g. 40 min vs 8 min) or different MS instruments (QE-Plus vs QE-Focus). When samples were acquired on the same LC gradient and instrument and a standard feature-alignment-based comparison (e.g. feature-table ordination) is sufficient — MEMO's RT-agnostic fingerprint counting is designed for chemodiverse or platform-shifted data When only MS1 feature intensities (no MS2 fragmentation spectra) are available, since MEMO fingerprints are built by counting MS2 peaks and neutral losses When the goal is chemical structural similarity from molecular networking cosine scores (e.g. the CSCS metric of q2-cscs) rather than MS2-profile sample vectorization http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Append new samples' MS2-based MEMO fingerprints (e.g. Waltheria indica profiles from different LC gradients and MS instruments) to an existing MemoMatrix without any prior feature alignment, then re-project to check co-clustering with reference samples. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Append new samples' MS2-based MEMO fingerprints (e.g. Waltheria indica profiles from different LC gradients and MS instruments) to an existing MemoMatrix without any prior feature alignment, then re-project to check co-clustering with reference samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When samples were acquired on the same LC gradient and instrument and a standard feature-alignment-based comparison (e.g. feature-table ordination) is sufficient — MEMO's RT-agnostic fingerprint counting is designed for chemodiverse or platform-shifted data When only MS1 feature intensities (no MS2 fragmentation spectra) are available, since MEMO fingerprints are built by counting MS2 peaks and neutral losses When the goal is chemical structural similarity from molecular networking cosine scores (e.g. the CSCS metric of q2-cscs) rather than MS2-profile sample vectorization

skills.description: Use when comparing LC-MS/MS samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, samples acquired on different LC methods or MS platforms (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap), or over long time periods where feature-table metrics inherit acquisition-batch artifacts.
skills.name: retention-time-agnostic-sample-comparison
skills.search_text: retention-time-agnostic-sample-comparison Use when comparing LC-MS/MS samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, samples acquired on different LC methods or MS platforms (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap), or over long time periods where feature-table metrics inherit acquisition-batch artifacts. When the scientific question requires retention-time-resolved feature positions — MEMO deliberately discards RT information to be RT agnostic. When samples have good feature overlap, no RT shift, and were acquired on the same platform in one batch — a standard feature-table metric suffices and avoids the fingerprinting overhead. When quantitative intensities matter — the MEMO matrix uses only presence/absence counts of peaks and losses; the MS1 feature intensity is not used. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Vectorize metabolomics samples into MS2 fingerprints (counts of MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor) and align them to compare samples retention-time-agnostically, mitigating batch effects such as RT shifts and MS sensitivity drift that dominate feature-table based ordinations. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Vectorize metabolomics samples into MS2 fingerprints (counts of MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor) and align them to compare samples retention-time-agnostically, mitigating batch effects such as RT shifts and MS sensitivity drift that dominate feature-table based ordinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the scientific question requires retention-time-resolved feature positions — MEMO deliberately discards RT information to be RT agnostic. When samples have good feature overlap, no RT shift, and were acquired on the same platform in one batch — a standard feature-table metric suffices and avoids the fingerprinting overhead. When quantitative intensities matter — the MEMO matrix uses only presence/absence counts of peaks and losses; the MS1 feature intensity is not used.

skills.description: Use when processing a batch of MRM mzML files (e.g. HILIC 1a/1b, MTBLS429, MTBLS897) whose metabolite peaks shift in RT between samples, and peak boundaries must be aligned before peak picking and ML-based peak reporting.
skills.name: retention-time-alignment
skills.search_text: retention-time-alignment Use when processing a batch of MRM mzML files (e.g. HILIC 1a/1b, MTBLS429, MTBLS897) whose metabolite peaks shift in RT between samples, and peak boundaries must be aligned before peak picking and ML-based peak reporting. The data are not MRM/LC-QQQ-MS chromatograms with known expected RTs (automRm needs quantifier/qualifier transitions and expected RTs per analyte in metabdb.xlsx). Only a single sample is available and no reference sample exists for cross-correlation-based shift estimation. The LC method is brand new or the samples are excessively dirty/very-low-input, where the authors state they retreat to manual peak review instead of automatic processing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Corrects per-metabolite retention-time (RT) drift across an MRM LC-QQQ-MS batch by cross-correlating each sample's chromatograms against a reference sample, fitting the shifts as a quadratic function of RT, and summing RT-shifted chromatograms into a prototype for robust peak detection. This is the alignment stage inside automRm's process_batch() pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05224
skills.summary: Corrects per-metabolite retention-time (RT) drift across an MRM LC-QQQ-MS batch by cross-correlating each sample's chromatograms against a reference sample, fitting the shifts as a quadratic function of RT, and summing RT-shifted chromatograms into a prototype for robust peak detection. This is the alignment stage inside automRm's process_batch() pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not MRM/LC-QQQ-MS chromatograms with known expected RTs (automRm needs quantifier/qualifier transitions and expected RTs per analyte in metabdb.xlsx). Only a single sample is available and no reference sample exists for cross-correlation-based shift estimation. The LC method is brand new or the samples are excessively dirty/very-low-input, where the authors state they retreat to manual peak review instead of automatic processing.

skills.search_text: retention-time-alignment Use when two LC-MS feature lists — an in vitro prototype list and an in vivo metabolite list, each with retention time and accurate m/z per component — must be bridged by RT and m/z matching. When only MS2 spectral-similarity matching against a prototype database is needed without in vitro/in vivo bridging — the article notes that technique 'only enables matching between single metabolite and the prototype database, and only utilizes similarity of the secondary mass spectrometry maps'. When the input is a single feature table already aligned across samples rather than two separate lists (in vitro prototypes vs. in vivo metabolites) requiring cross-list matching. When no retention-time information is available and only accurate-mass defect or MS2 fragment matching can be used. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 An RT/m/z window-based matching step in the MDRB pipeline (R) that bridges in vitro prototype components to in vivo mouse metabolite features using a retention-time tolerance of ±25 s and an accurate-mass tolerance of ±5 ppm, flagging RT-shifted m/z-matched components as isomers. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: An RT/m/z window-based matching step in the MDRB pipeline (R) that bridges in vitro prototype components to in vivo mouse metabolite features using a retention-time tolerance of ±25 s and an accurate-mass tolerance of ±5 ppm, flagging RT-shifted m/z-matched components as isomers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only MS2 spectral-similarity matching against a prototype database is needed without in vitro/in vivo bridging — the article notes that technique 'only enables matching between single metabolite and the prototype database, and only utilizes similarity of the secondary mass spectrometry maps'. When the input is a single feature table already aligned across samples rather than two separate lists (in vitro prototypes vs. in vivo metabolites) requiring cross-list matching. When no retention-time information is available and only accurate-mass defect or MS2 fragment matching can be used.

skills.description: Use when LC-MS targeted metabolomics EICs show retention-time drift between samples or replicate groups and the same isotopologue peak must be matched across samples before peak-area integration.

skills.search_text: retention-time-alignment Use when LC-MS targeted metabolomics EICs show retention-time drift between samples or replicate groups and the same isotopologue peak must be matched across samples before peak-area integration. Input is already an aligned, row-per-feature peak table from XCMS/centWave feature matching rather than raw per-sample EICs Data are MS/MS or data-independent acquisition spectra, which TarMet does not yet support (listed as future work in the article intro) No retention-time shift exists between samples, e.g. a single-sample run where alignment has no reference to correct against http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Aligns retention-time shifts of extracted-ion chromatograms (EICs) across samples using the PAFFT cross-correlation method so that the same targeted isotopologue can be matched and quantified consistently in every sample within TarMet. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Aligns retention-time shifts of extracted-ion chromatograms (EICs) across samples using the PAFFT cross-correlation method so that the same targeted isotopologue can be matched and quantified consistently in every sample within TarMet.

Input is already a feature/peak-intensity table with no raw chromatographic data — alignment of EICs is not applicable Only a single mzML file is analyzed and no cross-run RT drift correction is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Within the PeakDetective peak-curation pipeline, retention-time alignment is toggled when building the EIC data matrix so that each peak's extracted ion chromatogram is aligned across raw mzML files before autoencoder compression and classification. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c00764

skills.description: Use when multiple LC-MS/MS or DIA/SWATH maps must be made comparable — after feature detection and database searching, before protein inference — so peptide quantities refer to the same molecular feature in every run.
skills.name: retention-time-alignment-and-feature-linking
skills.search_text: retention-time-alignment-and-feature-linking Use when multiple LC-MS/MS or DIA/SWATH maps must be made comparable — after feature detection and database searching, before protein inference — so peptide quantities refer to the same molecular feature in every run. Data has not yet been centroided and searched — alignment on raw profile spectra will link noise instead of peptide features A single-run experiment with no cross-run comparison — linking is unnecessary and can merge distinct co-eluting isobaric peptides http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Align LC-MS/MS retention times across acquisition runs with OpenMS and link the same peptide features between maps so quantities are comparable run-to-run, as used in the OpenSWATH plasma twin-cohort quantification and the GENCODE proteogenomics re-annotation workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nmeth.3959
skills.summary: Align LC-MS/MS retention times across acquisition runs with OpenMS and link the same peptide features between maps so quantities are comparable run-to-run, as used in the OpenSWATH plasma twin-cohort quantification and the GENCODE proteogenomics re-annotation workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not yet been centroided and searched — alignment on raw profile spectra will link noise instead of peptide features A single-run experiment with no cross-run comparison — linking is unnecessary and can merge distinct co-eluting isobaric peptides

skills.description: Use when you have an MZmine-exported full-scan (MS1) feature table and a RegFilter-generated SPL .csv for the same LC-MS run and need to quantify what fraction of targeted precursor ions exist as DDA MS1 features or were actually fragmented in DDA.
skills.name: retention-time-alignment-comparison
skills.search_text: retention-time-alignment-comparison Use when you have an MZmine-exported full-scan (MS1) feature table and a RegFilter-generated SPL .csv for the same LC-MS run and need to quantify what fraction of targeted precursor ions exist as DDA MS1 features or were actually fragmented in DDA. Input is already a DDA MS2 peak list with no RegFilter SPL — there is nothing to align against and the overlap metric is undefined The full-scan and DDA runs were not processed with the same MZmine parameters (m/z 0.001 m/z or 15 ppm; RT 0.2), since the Join aligner tolerances are what make the overlap match valid You need to assess spectral identity of fragments, not precursor-level presence/absence — this skill only compares m/z and RT coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Matches RegFilter-selected scheduled precursor list (SPL) ions against DDA MS1 feature tables using MZmine's Join aligner tolerances (m/z 0.001 or 15 ppm; RT 0.2 min) to quantify overlap and common-feature counts per strain, verifying that RegFilter covers chromatographic signals missed by DDA. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Matches RegFilter-selected scheduled precursor list (SPL) ions against DDA MS1 feature tables using MZmine's Join aligner tolerances (m/z 0.001 or 15 ppm; RT 0.2 min) to quantify overlap and common-feature counts per strain, verifying that RegFilter covers chromatographic signals missed by DDA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a DDA MS2 peak list with no RegFilter SPL — there is nothing to align against and the overlap metric is undefined The full-scan and DDA runs were not processed with the same MZmine parameters (m/z 0.001 m/z or 15 ppm; RT 0.2), since the Join aligner tolerances are what make the overlap match valid You need to assess spectral identity of fragments, not precursor-level presence/absence — this skill only compares m/z and RT coordinates

In the Kenar et al. 2014 label-free metabolomics workflow, this is done with OpenMS's MapAlignmentPoseClustering between feature detection (FeatureFinderMetabo) and feature linking (FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT). metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278

skills.search_text: retention-time-alignment-parameters Use when preparing raw LC/MS mzXML data (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS213) as an XCMS xcmsSet for isotopologue-pair detection with geoRge, where feature quality is determined by peak picking, alignment and grouping parameters. The input is already a grouped XCMS feature table or a pre-built xcmsSet (e.g. the mtbls213 object shipped with geoRge) — proceed directly to PuInc_seeker/basepeak_finder The downstream tool does not consume XCMS output structures (e.g. peak-picking tools with their own preprocessing), since geoRge specifically 'runs on the output structure of the XCMS package' Targeted isotope analysis where theoretical mass-difference scanning over all MS signals is appropriate rather than labeled-vs-unlabeled sample comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Guidance for configuring XCMS peak picking, alignment and grouping (including retention-time correction) so that the resulting XCMS feature table is a valid input to downstream stable-isotope-labelling tools such as geoRge, whose results depend entirely on these preprocessing parameters. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628

skills.description: Use when a metabolite standard or adduct in a metScribeR EIC review shows more than one manually labeled 'good' peak at different retention times, and ambiguous entries must be flagged or removed from the final RT/m/z library.
skills.name: retention-time-ambiguity-analysis
skills.search_text: retention-time-ambiguity-analysis Use when a metabolite standard or adduct in a metScribeR EIC review shows more than one manually labeled 'good' peak at different retention times, and ambiguous entries must be flagged or removed from the final RT/m/z library. Peaks have not yet been manually reviewed — the conflict check relies on the Good Peak / Bad Peak / Multimodal/Indeterminate labels assigned on the Review Results tab Each standard/adduct has only a single 'good' peak, so no competing RT assignment exists The goal is MS/MS-based identification — this skill operates on MS1 and RT data only, since metScribeR 'does not require MS/MS spectral information' for library construction Identifies and removes 'crossed adducts' — metabolite standard adducts with multiple manually labeled 'good' peaks at divergent retention times — during metScribeR in-house LC-MS library construction, so that RT assignments retained in the final .csv library are unambiguous. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Identifies and removes 'crossed adducts' — metabolite standard adducts with multiple manually labeled 'good' peaks at divergent retention times — during metScribeR in-house LC-MS library construction, so that RT assignments retained in the final .csv library are unambiguous.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks have not yet been manually reviewed — the conflict check relies on the Good Peak / Bad Peak / Multimodal/Indeterminate labels assigned on the Review Results tab Each standard/adduct has only a single 'good' peak, so no competing RT assignment exists The goal is MS/MS-based identification — this skill operates on MS1 and RT data only, since metScribeR 'does not require MS/MS spectral information' for library construction

skills.description: Use when raw GCxGC-MS acquisition data arrives as a NetCDF (.cdf) file and you must build the two-dimensional retention-time axis (first dimension vs modulation-period second dimension) before smoothing, baseline correction, alignment, or MPCA.
skills.name: retention-time-axis-construction
skills.search_text: retention-time-axis-construction Use when raw GCxGC-MS acquisition data arrives as a NetCDF (.cdf) file and you must build the two-dimensional retention-time axis (first dimension vs modulation-period second dimension) before smoothing, baseline correction, alignment, or MPCA. Input is already a folded 2D chromatogram or preprocessed RGCxGC S4 object rather than a raw NetCDF file — re-reading would discard prior folding/preprocessing. Data are 1D GC-MS runs without modulation, where a second retention-time axis cannot be constructed. You need unfolded matrices for supervised modeling — use unfold_chrom downstream instead of re-importing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3388 Import a raw GCxGC-MS chromatogram from a NetCDF file with RGCxGC's read_chrom and fold the 1D signal into the two-dimensional Total Intensity Chromatogram (2D-TIC) using the modulation time, producing an S4 chromatogram object with retention-time axes ready for preprocessing. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2020.104830
skills.summary: Import a raw GCxGC-MS chromatogram from a NetCDF file with RGCxGC's read_chrom and fold the 1D signal into the two-dimensional Total Intensity Chromatogram (2D-TIC) using the modulation time, producing an S4 chromatogram object with retention-time axes ready for preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a folded 2D chromatogram or preprocessed RGCxGC S4 object rather than a raw NetCDF file — re-reading would discard prior folding/preprocessing. Data are 1D GC-MS runs without modulation, where a second retention-time axis cannot be constructed. You need unfolded matrices for supervised modeling — use unfold_chrom downstream instead of re-importing.

skills.description: Use when you need to assess how well a tool clusters MS/MS spectra from metabolomics datasets (qToF or Orbitrap, e.g. MSV000081981 or MSV000093033) without ground-truth identifications, or when benchmarking clustering purity against a database-search-based evaluation.
skills.name: retention-time-based-cluster-purity-evaluation
skills.search_text: retention-time-based-cluster-purity-evaluation Use when you need to assess how well a tool clusters MS/MS spectra from metabolomics datasets (qToF or Orbitrap, e.g. MSV000081981 or MSV000093033) without ground-truth identifications, or when benchmarking clustering purity against a database-search-based evaluation. When proteomics database search identifications with FDR control are already available and DB-Search-based evaluation can be run directly (e.g. PXD021518 proteomics data), DB-Search is the established evaluation method When the input is not MS/MS spectra (e.g. already a feature table or consensus spectra with no per-scan retention time), MS-RT purity scoring is not applicable When the clustering tool output cannot be mapped to per-scan precursor m/z and retention time (missing #ParentMass or #RetTime columns), the method cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 MS-RT evaluates MS/MS clustering purity in metabolomics by exploiting the observation that MS/MS spectra of the same molecule share MS1 precursor m/z and retention time, avoiding the need for FDR-controlled identifications. It is validated against database-search-based evaluation on proteomics data and applied to benchmark MS-Cluster, Falcon, and MaRaCluster on metabolomics datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c00881
skills.summary: MS-RT evaluates MS/MS clustering purity in metabolomics by exploiting the observation that MS/MS spectra of the same molecule share MS1 precursor m/z and retention time, avoiding the need for FDR-controlled identifications. It is validated against database-search-based evaluation on proteomics data and applied to benchmark MS-Cluster, Falcon, and MaRaCluster on metabolomics datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When proteomics database search identifications with FDR control are already available and DB-Search-based evaluation can be run directly (e.g. PXD021518 proteomics data), DB-Search is the established evaluation method When the input is not MS/MS spectra (e.g. already a feature table or consensus spectra with no per-scan retention time), MS-RT purity scoring is not applicable When the clustering tool output cannot be mapped to per-scan precursor m/z and retention time (missing #ParentMass or #RetTime columns), the method cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when a formula-based database retrieval (e.g. PubChem isomeric candidates by exact molecular formula, or MS-Finder candidate lists) must be narrowed using a measured liquid-chromatography retention time for the unknown molecule.
skills.name: retention-time-candidate-filtering
skills.search_text: retention-time-candidate-filtering Use when a formula-based database retrieval (e.g. PubChem isomeric candidates by exact molecular formula, or MS-Finder candidate lists) must be narrowed using a measured liquid-chromatography retention time for the unknown molecule. No measured retention time is available for the unknown metabolite — the filter compares predicted RT against the observed RT and cannot run without it No pre-trained or transfer-learned model exists for the chromatographic method used, since different chromatographic conditions yield different RTs for the same metabolite; first run transfer learning on your method's data The goal is gas-phase or non-chromatographic compound identification — the article's scope is predicting retention times for liquid chromatography http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Filters molecular candidate lists for an unknown metabolite by predicting each candidate's retention time with RT-Transformer (graph attention network + 1D-Transformer) and discarding candidates whose predicted RT is inconsistent with the observed RT, improving annotation ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Filters molecular candidate lists for an unknown metabolite by predicting each candidate's retention time with RT-Transformer (graph attention network + 1D-Transformer) and discarding candidates whose predicted RT is inconsistent with the observed RT, improving annotation ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No measured retention time is available for the unknown metabolite — the filter compares predicted RT against the observed RT and cannot run without it No pre-trained or transfer-learned model exists for the chromatographic method used, since different chromatographic conditions yield different RTs for the same metabolite; first run transfer learning on your method's data The goal is gas-phase or non-chromatographic compound identification — the article's scope is predicting retention times for liquid chromatography

skills.description: Use when MS-FINDER compound identification returns many isomeric candidate structures per formula and you have predicted RTs (Retip) plus experimental RTs to exclude candidates that are chromatographically implausible.
skills.name: retention-time-candidate-filtering-msfinder
skills.search_text: retention-time-candidate-filtering-msfinder Use when MS-FINDER compound identification returns many isomeric candidate structures per formula and you have predicted RTs (Retip) plus experimental RTs to exclude candidates that are chromatographically implausible. skills.search_text: retention-time-drift-correction Use when MRM chromatographic peak lists from multiple samples show retention time shifts that must be corrected before peak alignment or EIC grouping, and per-sample RT drift values need to be estimated from chromatogram shapes. Input data is not MRM chromatographic (EIC) data — the algorithm assumes per-sample EIC peak lists with retention times and intensities Peaks are already aligned or drift values are already known (e.g. from internal standards), making chromatogram-similarity drift estimation redundant The goal is raw file format conversion or compression rather than drift estimation (use AirdPro/Aird SDK instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimates retention time (RT) drifts between MRM samples by aligning each extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) to a reference EIC using combined grid search and gradient descent to maximize cosine similarity. The resulting drift estimates feed MRMPro's peak alignment and automatic EIC grouping. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05685-x
skills.summary: Estimates retention time (RT) drifts between MRM samples by aligning each extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) to a reference EIC using combined grid search and gradient descent to maximize cosine similarity. The resulting drift estimates feed MRMPro's peak alignment and automatic EIC grouping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not MRM chromatographic (EIC) data — the algorithm assumes per-sample EIC peak lists with retention times and intensities Peaks are already aligned or drift values are already known (e.g. from internal standards), making chromatogram-similarity drift estimation redundant The goal is raw file format conversion or compression rather than drift estimation (use AirdPro/Aird SDK instead)

skills.search_text: retention-time-drift-correction-benchmarking Use when evaluating or comparing LC–MS feature alignment algorithms (e.g. G-Aligner, MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS, local bipartite matching) on datasets with nonlinear RT drift, especially when a manually annotated feature list is available as ground truth. The task is de novo identification or annotation of metabolites rather than benchmarking the alignment step of an untargeted LC–MS metabolomics workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Benchmark feature alignment methods that must cope with nonlinear retention time (RT) drift between LC–MS runs, by evaluating them against manually annotated feature lists and reporting precision, recall, F1, F_ACC and A_ACC on benchmark datasets such as TripleTOF_6600, QE_HF and MTBLS562. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05525-4
skills.summary: Benchmark feature alignment methods that must cope with nonlinear retention time (RT) drift between LC–MS runs, by evaluating them against manually annotated feature lists and reporting precision, recall, F1, F_ACC and A_ACC on benchmark datasets such as TripleTOF_6600, QE_HF and MTBLS562.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single LC–MS run with no multi-run correspondence problem — the skill addresses aligning features across multiple related runs, not within-run peak picking. skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-feature-evaluation Decision support for choosing or validating a retention time predictor (e.g. DeepLC, Prosit-derived RT, RTPredict) whose ΔRT error will serve as a rescoring feature in Percolator-style PSM rescoring. The analysis goal is evaluating spectral (MS²PIP/Prosit fragment-intensity) or binding-affinity features rather than retention time features Retention times of the input PSMs are unavailable or cannot be calibrated per raw file, so ΔRT cannot be computed reliably Input is already a final scored PSM table with no access to the underlying predictor, making feature-weight attribution impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark the accuracy of a retention time predictor and its ΔRT feature weight before adopting ΔRT as a PSM rescoring feature, because predictor quality — not the feature concept — determines whether ΔRT improves immunopeptide identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/pmic.202300336
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy of a retention time predictor and its ΔRT feature weight before adopting ΔRT as a PSM rescoring feature, because predictor quality — not the feature concept — determines whether ΔRT improves immunopeptide identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is evaluating spectral (MS²PIP/Prosit fragment-intensity) or binding-affinity features rather than retention time features Retention times of the input PSMs are unavailable or cannot be calibrated per raw file, so ΔRT cannot be computed reliably Input is already a final scored PSM table with no access to the underlying predictor, making feature-weight attribution impossible

skills.description: Use when predicting liquid chromatography retention times for a new chromatographic method from molecular structures (InChI/SMILES), especially with limited labeled data where training a retention-time model from scratch is infeasible.
skills.name: retention-time-prediction-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-fine-tuning Use when predicting liquid chromatography retention times for a new chromatographic method from molecular structures (InChI/SMILES), especially with limited labeled data where training a retention-time model from scratch is infeasible. When no pre-trained checkpoint applies and you have a large labeled dataset for the target method — retrain from scratch with train.py instead When the input lacks structural identifiers (InChI/SMILES) convertible to molecular graphs and fingerprints — the model requires graph and fingerprint inputs, not tabular metadata When the target task is not liquid chromatography retention time prediction (e.g. mass spectra prediction or general property regression) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Transfer a pre-trained RT-Transformer (graph attention network + 1D-Transformer trained on the 80,038-molecule SMRT dataset) to a new chromatographic method by freezing the encoders and fine-tuning a re-initialized output block on a small PredRet-style retention time dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Transfer a pre-trained RT-Transformer (graph attention network + 1D-Transformer trained on the 80,038-molecule SMRT dataset) to a new chromatographic method by freezing the encoders and fine-tuning a re-initialized output block on a small PredRet-style retention time dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no pre-trained checkpoint applies and you have a large labeled dataset for the target method — retrain from scratch with train.py instead When the input lacks structural identifiers (InChI/SMILES) convertible to molecular graphs and fingerprints — the model requires graph and fingerprint inputs, not tabular metadata When the target task is not liquid chromatography retention time prediction (e.g. mass spectra prediction or general property regression)

skills.description: Use when SMILES structures need predicted retention times (HILIC or RPLC) to rank or filter candidate structures in untargeted metabolomics, or when batch-predicting RTs for a large compound database.
skills.name: retention-time-prediction-from-chemical-descriptors
skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-from-chemical-descriptors Use when SMILES structures need predicted retention times (HILIC or RPLC) to rank or filter candidate structures in untargeted metabolomics, or when batch-predicting RTs for a large compound database. Predicting RTs for complex, high molecular weight lipids such as triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines, which were largely excluded from the training set — results may be more erroneous outside the training chemical landscape Needing narrow retention time search windows to discriminate closely eluting compounds in typical 12 min UPLC methods, where 1 min prediction errors preclude such discrimination Adjusting retention time predictions for small changes in chromatographic methods, which was explicitly beyond the scope of the Retip study Predict HILIC and reversed-phase LC retention times for small molecules from SMILES structures using the Retip R package's machine learning models (Keras neural network performed best), with RT predictions used to rank or exclude structure candidates in untargeted metabolomics annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Predict HILIC and reversed-phase LC retention times for small molecules from SMILES structures using the Retip R package's machine learning models (Keras neural network performed best), with RT predictions used to rank or exclude structure candidates in untargeted metabolomics annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting RTs for complex, high molecular weight lipids such as triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines, which were largely excluded from the training set — results may be more erroneous outside the training chemical landscape Needing narrow retention time search windows to discriminate closely eluting compounds in typical 12 min UPLC methods, where 1 min prediction errors preclude such discrimination Adjusting retention time predictions for small changes in chromatographic methods, which was explicitly beyond the scope of the Retip study

skills.description: Use when you have a molecular formula (e.g. from PubChem PUG REST) with multiple isomeric candidate SMILES and one observed retention time under an SMRT-type chromatographic method, and need to prune inconsistent candidates.
skills.name: retention-time-prediction-inference
skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-inference Use when you have a molecular formula (e.g. from PubChem PUG REST) with multiple isomeric candidate SMILES and one observed retention time under an SMRT-type chromatographic method, and need to prune inconsistent candidates. The observed retention time is already known for every candidate structure, so RT-based filtering would remove nothing The chromatographic method differs from the SMRT conditions the pre-trained model was trained on and no InChI/RT dataset is available to fine-tune via transfer.py Only a bare molecular formula is available with no candidate SMILES/InChI structures, since the model requires molecular graph and fingerprint input http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Uses RT-Transformer, a graph attention network + 1D-Transformer model that combines molecular fingerprint and molecular graph features, to predict LC retention times under a given chromatographic method and thereby eliminate candidate metabolite structures whose predicted RT is inconsistent with the observed RT. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Uses RT-Transformer, a graph attention network + 1D-Transformer model that combines molecular fingerprint and molecular graph features, to predict LC retention times under a given chromatographic method and thereby eliminate candidate metabolite structures whose predicted RT is inconsistent with the observed RT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The observed retention time is already known for every candidate structure, so RT-based filtering would remove nothing The chromatographic method differs from the SMRT conditions the pre-trained model was trained on and no InChI/RT dataset is available to fine-tune via transfer.py Only a bare molecular formula is available with no candidate SMILES/InChI structures, since the model requires molecular graph and fingerprint input

skills.description: Use when building multidimensional (4D) LC-IM-MS/MS identification databases where computationally predicted retention times must be supplied for candidate molecules lacking experimental RT measurements, e.g. derivatized sterol lipid entries.
skills.name: retention-time-prediction-integration
skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-integration Use when building multidimensional (4D) LC-IM-MS/MS identification databases where computationally predicted retention times must be supplied for candidate molecules lacking experimental RT measurements, e.g. derivatized sterol lipid entries. When experimental retention times are already available for the analytes — measured RT should be preferred over GNN predictions. When the analysis concerns non-sterol metabolites without C=C bonds, since the N-Me derivatization and fragmentation logic in the accompanying workflow was only tested on sterol lipids. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates chromatographic retention time predictions for N-Me derivatized sterol lipids using a pretrained graph neural network (GNN) approach, and integrates the RT values as one of the four 4D fields (m/z, RT, CCS, fragment ions) in the derivatized sterol lipid database. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/anie.202507483
skills.summary: Generates chromatographic retention time predictions for N-Me derivatized sterol lipids using a pretrained graph neural network (GNN) approach, and integrates the RT values as one of the four 4D fields (m/z, RT, CCS, fragment ions) in the derivatized sterol lipid database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimental retention times are already available for the analytes — measured RT should be preferred over GNN predictions. When the analysis concerns non-sterol metabolites without C=C bonds, since the N-Me derivatization and fragmentation logic in the accompanying workflow was only tested on sterol lipids.

skills.description: Use when you have SMILES/InChI structures or a compound descriptor table and need predicted retention times for HILIC or reversed-phase LC-MS runs to filter isomer candidates, rank unknowns, or remove unlikely annotations in metabolomics workflows.
skills.name: retention-time-prediction-model-inference
skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-model-inference Use when you have SMILES/InChI structures or a compound descriptor table and need predicted retention times for HILIC or reversed-phase LC-MS runs to filter isomer candidates, rank unknowns, or remove unlikely annotations in metabolomics workflows. When the target compounds fall outside the chemical landscape of the training set — predictions may be more erroneous if Retip is applied to complex high molecular weight lipids (e.g., triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines) that were largely excluded from training. When very narrow retention time search windows are required — the paper notes that for typical UPLC methods with 12 min run times, 1 min prediction errors preclude discriminating closely eluting compounds. When the analysis involves small changes in chromatographic methods — the study explicitly did not test whether retention time predictions can be adjusted for such changes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Apply trained Retip machine learning models (Random Forest, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras, or H2O autoML) to predict retention times for small molecules in HPLC-MS, enabling retention-time-based filtering of false positive annotations in untargeted metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765
skills.summary: Apply trained Retip machine learning models (Random Forest, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras, or H2O autoML) to predict retention times for small molecules in HPLC-MS, enabling retention-time-based filtering of false positive annotations in untargeted metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target compounds fall outside the chemical landscape of the training set — predictions may be more erroneous if Retip is applied to complex high molecular weight lipids (e.g., triacylglycerols or phosphatidylcholines) that were largely excluded from training. When very narrow retention time search windows are required — the paper notes that for typical UPLC methods with 12 min run times, 1 min prediction errors preclude discriminating closely eluting compounds. When the analysis involves small changes in chromatographic methods — the study explicitly did not test whether retention time predictions can be adjusted for such changes.

skills.description: Use when you need to predict retention times for compounds from SMILES/structures to complement MS/MS spectral matching, or to benchmark a learned RT predictor against a logP-based linear regression baseline.
skills.name: retention-time-prediction-modeling
skills.search_text: retention-time-prediction-modeling Use when you need to predict retention times for compounds from SMILES/structures to complement MS/MS spectral matching, or to benchmark a learned RT predictor against a logP-based linear regression baseline. Your reference library is NIST'17 — it does not provide RT (or CCS) values for measured compounds, so no RT training labels are available You need spectrally annotated RT on chromatographically incompatible setups — the RT model's hyperparameters were not tuned for this task and the feature is prototype-stage http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Train and apply FIORA's RT prediction submodule to estimate LC retention times from molecular structure, alongside CCS prediction, as additional dimensions for MS-based compound identification beyond spectral similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Train and apply FIORA's RT prediction submodule to estimate LC retention times from molecular structure, alongside CCS prediction, as additional dimensions for MS-based compound identification beyond spectral similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your reference library is NIST'17 — it does not provide RT (or CCS) values for measured compounds, so no RT training labels are available You need spectrally annotated RT on chromatographically incompatible setups — the RT model's hyperparameters were not tuned for this task and the feature is prototype-stage

skills.description: Use when the MS1 database contains RT entries (e.g. '30;60' elution ranges) for compounds, and LC-MS feature annotations must be filtered or reweighted by whether the feature's measured retention time falls within that expected range.
skills.name: retention-time-prior-integration
skills.search_text: retention-time-prior-integration Use when the MS1 database contains RT entries (e.g. '30;60' elution ranges) for compounds, and LC-MS feature annotations must be filtered or reweighted by whether the feature's measured retention time falls within that expected range. When the compound database has no 'RT' information — the RT prior cannot be applied and annotations are scored on mass accuracy, isotope pattern and prior knowledge alone. When the LC method or column is drastically different from the one used to build the database RT entries — the '30;60'-style elution ranges will be invalid and may incorrectly penalise true annotations. When hard filtering of annotations by RT is desired — ipaPy2 treats RT as a Bayesian prior with soft probabilities (pRTNone=0.8, pRTout=0.4), not a cutoff. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Integrates known retention time (RT) ranges from a compound database into the IPA Bayesian annotation of LC-MS untargeted metabolomics features, adjusting the posterior annotation probabilities of each candidate. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad455
skills.summary: Integrates known retention time (RT) ranges from a compound database into the IPA Bayesian annotation of LC-MS untargeted metabolomics features, adjusting the posterior annotation probabilities of each candidate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compound database has no 'RT' information — the RT prior cannot be applied and annotations are scored on mass accuracy, isotope pattern and prior knowledge alone. When the LC method or column is drastically different from the one used to build the database RT entries — the '30;60'-style elution ranges will be invalid and may incorrectly penalise true annotations. When hard filtering of annotations by RT is desired — ipaPy2 treats RT as a Bayesian prior with soft probabilities (pRTNone=0.8, pRTout=0.4), not a cutoff.

skills.description: Use when you have deep-learning-predicted RTs on one chromatographic method and need them transformed onto the time scale of other experimental reverse-phase methods (ECMs) to compute projection errors or rank candidates.
skills.name: retention-time-projection-across-chromatographic-methods
skills.search_text: retention-time-projection-across-chromatographic-methods Use when you have deep-learning-predicted RTs on one chromatographic method and need them transformed onto the time scale of other experimental reverse-phase methods (ECMs) to compute projection errors or rank candidates. The target chromatographic method is not reverse-phase LC (the SMRT dataset is an experimentally acquired reverse-phase chromatography retention time dataset, so projections to normal-phase or HILIC methods are out of scope). No partially identified calibration set exists — i.e. fewer than the ~50 shared molecules with RT in both the SMRT method and the target ECM are available to fit the projection. The goal is de novo RT prediction from molecular structure rather than projecting existing SMRT-predicted RTs onto another method's time scale. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Projects retention times predicted by the SMRT deep-learning model (trained on the METLIN SMRT reverse-phase dataset) onto independent experimental chromatographic methods (ECMs) using a robust least-squares four-degree polynomial fit, so predicted RTs become comparable with RTs measured under other methods. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Projects retention times predicted by the SMRT deep-learning model (trained on the METLIN SMRT reverse-phase dataset) onto independent experimental chromatographic methods (ECMs) using a robust least-squares four-degree polynomial fit, so predicted RTs become comparable with RTs measured under other methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target chromatographic method is not reverse-phase LC (the SMRT dataset is an experimentally acquired reverse-phase chromatography retention time dataset, so projections to normal-phase or HILIC methods are out of scope). No partially identified calibration set exists — i.e. fewer than the ~50 shared molecules with RT in both the SMRT method and the target ECM are available to fit the projection. The goal is de novo RT prediction from molecular structure rather than projecting existing SMRT-predicted RTs onto another method's time scale.

skills.description: Use when predicted RTs from a machine learning model must be projected to a specific chromatographic method for which only ~10 experimentally identified molecules (predicted-vs-experimental RT pairs) are available, and confidence intervals on the projections are needed.
skills.name: retention-time-projection-between-chromatographic-methods
skills.search_text: retention-time-projection-between-chromatographic-methods Use when predicted RTs from a machine learning model must be projected to a specific chromatographic method for which only ~10 experimentally identified molecules (predicted-vs-experimental RT pairs) are available, and confidence intervals on the projections are needed. The target chromatographic method has no identified molecules at all — the GP prior must be updated with target-task training points to fit the projection. The goal is RT prediction itself from molecular structure; use the SMRT-trained DNN predictor skill instead of the projection module. Non-retained molecules (RT < 5 minutes) are part of the target-task data and must be modeled — these are excluded from the projection meta-tasks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 A Bayesian meta-learning approach that maps predicted retention times (from a DNN trained on the SMRT dataset) to a target chromatographic method's experimental RT scale using as few as 10 identified molecules, via a meta-learned GP prior over projection functions that also yields 95% credible intervals. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8
skills.summary: A Bayesian meta-learning approach that maps predicted retention times (from a DNN trained on the SMRT dataset) to a target chromatographic method's experimental RT scale using as few as 10 identified molecules, via a meta-learned GP prior over projection functions that also yields 95% credible intervals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target chromatographic method has no identified molecules at all — the GP prior must be updated with target-task training points to fit the projection. The goal is RT prediction itself from molecular structure; use the SMRT-trained DNN predictor skill instead of the projection module. Non-retained molecules (RT < 5 minutes) are part of the target-task data and must be modeled — these are excluded from the projection meta-tasks.

skills.description: Use when you have a small set (10–50 molecules) of paired predicted/experimental RTs for a target chromatographic method and need to map DNN-predicted RTs onto that method's scale with 95% prediction intervals.
skills.name: retention-time-projection-meta-learning
skills.search_text: retention-time-projection-meta-learning Use when you have a small set (10–50 molecules) of paired predicted/experimental RTs for a target chromatographic method and need to map DNN-predicted RTs onto that method's scale with 95% prediction intervals. The task is training the RT predictor itself on the SMRT dataset from fingerprints/descriptors — use the predictor-training workflow (make train_predictor), not projection. No predicted RTs from the SMRT-trained DNN exist for the compounds and no experimental RTs for a few known molecules are available — the projection needs paired predicted/experimental values. Fragmentation spectra are available for candidate metabolites — standard annotation with spectral matching is preferable; this skill targets the case where annotation must rely on just m/z ratios and RTs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 A Bayesian meta-learning approach that projects DNN-predicted retention times (from a fingerprint model trained on the 80,038-experiment SMRT dataset) onto a specific chromatographic method's experimental RT scale using as few as 10 identified molecules, with calibrated confidence intervals. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8
skills.summary: A Bayesian meta-learning approach that projects DNN-predicted retention times (from a fingerprint model trained on the 80,038-experiment SMRT dataset) onto a specific chromatographic method's experimental RT scale using as few as 10 identified molecules, with calibrated confidence intervals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is training the RT predictor itself on the SMRT dataset from fingerprints/descriptors — use the predictor-training workflow (make train_predictor), not projection. No predicted RTs from the SMRT-trained DNN exist for the compounds and no experimental RTs for a few known molecules are available — the projection needs paired predicted/experimental values. Fragmentation spectra are available for candidate metabolites — standard annotation with spectral matching is preferable; this skill targets the case where annotation must rely on just m/z ratios and RTs.

skills.description: Use when you have DLM-predicted RTs, a molecule library with accurate masses (e.g. HMDB), and experimental RTs from a target chromatographic method, and you need to rank/filter candidate identities from 10 ppm accurate-mass search results.
skills.name: retention-time-projection-regression
skills.search_text: retention-time-projection-regression Use when you have DLM-predicted RTs, a molecule library with accurate masses (e.g. HMDB), and experimental RTs from a target chromatographic method, and you need to rank/filter candidate identities from 10 ppm accurate-mass search results. The target chromatographic method is not reverse-phase LC (the SMRT dataset and DLM predictions cover experimentally acquired reverse-phase RTs only). Experimental RTs are already available for the query compounds in the target method, making projected predicted RTs unnecessary. You need identity confirmation rather than candidate ranking — an RT-error rank alone cannot uniquely identify a molecule when mass-search candidates share similar RTs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Projects deep-learning-predicted reverse-phase retention times (RTs) onto other chromatographic methods via quartic polynomial regression, then uses the projected RT plus accurate-mass search to rank candidate molecular identities from real metabolomics experiments. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Projects deep-learning-predicted reverse-phase retention times (RTs) onto other chromatographic methods via quartic polynomial regression, then uses the projected RT plus accurate-mass search to rank candidate molecular identities from real metabolomics experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target chromatographic method is not reverse-phase LC (the SMRT dataset and DLM predictions cover experimentally acquired reverse-phase RTs only). Experimental RTs are already available for the query compounds in the target method, making projected predicted RTs unnecessary. You need identity confirmation rather than candidate ranking — an RT-error rank alone cannot uniquely identify a molecule when mass-search candidates share similar RTs.

skills.description: Use when executing a simulated LC-MS/MS acquisition in ViMMS 2.0 and you must bind the mass spectrometer and controller in an Environment and define the simulated RT window before env.run().
skills.name: retention-time-range-configuration-for-virtual-runs
skills.search_text: retention-time-range-configuration-for-virtual-runs Use when executing a simulated LC-MS/MS acquisition in ViMMS 2.0 and you must bind the mass spectrometer and controller in an Environment and define the simulated RT window before env.run(). The goal is to define or change the fragmentation strategy parameters themselves (N, isolation window, tolerances) — those belong to controller configuration, not Environment RT-range setup Acquisition is to be run on an actual Thermo Tribrid Fusion instrument via Thermo Fisher IAPI bridging rather than in simulation Only exporting or evaluating scans from an already-completed simulated run — use write_mzML or the evaluation methods directly instead of re-running the Environment http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Configures the ViMMS 2.0 Environment object that binds a simulated mass spectrometer and a fragmentation controller, setting the simulated retention-time window (e.g. 0–1440 minutes) before executing env.run() for an in-silico LC-MS/MS acquisition. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Configures the ViMMS 2.0 Environment object that binds a simulated mass spectrometer and a fragmentation controller, setting the simulated retention-time window (e.g. 0–1440 minutes) before executing env.run() for an in-silico LC-MS/MS acquisition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to define or change the fragmentation strategy parameters themselves (N, isolation window, tolerances) — those belong to controller configuration, not Environment RT-range setup Acquisition is to be run on an actual Thermo Tribrid Fusion instrument via Thermo Fisher IAPI bridging rather than in simulation Only exporting or evaluating scans from an already-completed simulated run — use write_mzML or the evaluation methods directly instead of re-running the Environment

skills.description: Use when building a metabolite reference library from chemical standard injections in LC-MS: replicate mzXML/mzML files of standard mixtures are available and validated retention times per analyte must be extracted and tabulated.
skills.name: retention-time-reference-library-construction
skills.search_text: retention-time-reference-library-construction Use when building a metabolite reference library from chemical standard injections in LC-MS: replicate mzXML/mzML files of standard mixtures are available and validated retention times per analyte must be extracted and tabulated. The goal is mobile phase optimization rather than retention-time library building — instead select the mobile phase with the highest peak quality score (sum of detected-peaks score Sp and asymmetry factor score Saf). Retention times already exist in a validated reference table and no new standard injections need evaluating. Data are not replicate LC/MS runs of chemical standards with matching blank injections, so the Std/Blk ratio and triplicate retention-time RSD cannot be computed. Constructs a retention-time reference library of chemical standards for HILIC LC-MS metabolomics by evaluating each standard mixture in triplicate with MetaMOPE and recording retention times only for peaks passing Std/Blk intensity ratio, retention-time RSD, and peak-intensity thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad061
skills.summary: Constructs a retention-time reference library of chemical standards for HILIC LC-MS metabolomics by evaluating each standard mixture in triplicate with MetaMOPE and recording retention times only for peaks passing Std/Blk intensity ratio, retention-time RSD, and peak-intensity thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is mobile phase optimization rather than retention-time library building — instead select the mobile phase with the highest peak quality score (sum of detected-peaks score Sp and asymmetry factor score Saf). Retention times already exist in a validated reference table and no new standard injections need evaluating. Data are not replicate LC/MS runs of chemical standards with matching blank injections, so the Std/Blk ratio and triplicate retention-time RSD cannot be computed.
