skills.search_text: rsd-repeatability-assessment-in-qc-samples Use when curating an untargeted LC–MS feature table where pooled/intrastudy QC injections are available and features with poor analytical repeatability (RSD > 20%) must be removed before statistical analysis. The dataset has no pooled/intrastudy QC injections or reference-material samples to serve as repeated measurements — RSD cannot be estimated without replicate QC data You are evaluating inter-batch/inter-laboratory robustness rather than within-run repeatability; the D-ratio filter (MAD of QC vs. MAD of study samples) targets that complementary question The input is already a fully curated matrix where low-RSD filtering was previously applied; reapplying would not change the result and would lose provenance of earlier filter steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluate repeatability of metabolic features by computing the relative standard deviation (RSD) of peak areas across pooled/intrastudy QC sample injections, and eliminate features with RSD larger than 20% in the LC–MS data curation pipeline demonstrated with NIST candidate RM 8231 and SRM 1950 plasma reference materials. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10100416
skills.summary: Evaluate repeatability of metabolic features by computing the relative standard deviation (RSD) of peak areas across pooled/intrastudy QC sample injections, and eliminate features with RSD larger than 20% in the LC–MS data curation pipeline demonstrated with NIST candidate RM 8231 and SRM 1950 plasma reference materials.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no pooled/intrastudy QC injections or reference-material samples to serve as repeated measurements — RSD cannot be estimated without replicate QC data You are evaluating inter-batch/inter-laboratory robustness rather than within-run repeatability; the D-ratio filter (MAD of QC vs. MAD of study samples) targets that complementary question The input is already a fully curated matrix where low-RSD filtering was previously applied; reapplying would not change the result and would lose provenance of earlier filter steps

skills.description: Use when pooled QC samples were injected periodically (e.g. every 5–8 samples) during an LC-MS metabolomics or SRM proteomics run and you need to quantify precision gains of a drift-correction method via QC RSD distributions.

skills.search_text: rsd-variation-quality-assessment-of-qc-samples Use when pooled QC samples were injected periodically (e.g. every 5–8 samples) during an LC-MS metabolomics or SRM proteomics run and you need to quantify precision gains of a drift-correction method via QC RSD distributions. Data contain no repeated pooled-QC injections (QC-free design); use shiftCor_dQC with Combat instead of QC-RFSC and QC-RSD assessment. Feature intensities have already been filtered/normalized downstream (e.g. via statAnalysis Pareto scaling and glog) — RSDs computed there no longer reflect raw instrument precision. Assessing biological group separation rather than measurement precision; RSD of QC samples is not the appropriate metric. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluates the relative standard deviation (RSD/CV) distribution of pooled-QC peak intensities before and after signal drift correction, using the shift in the fraction of QC features below a 30 % (or 15 %) RSD cutoff to judge whether statTarget's QC-RFSC correction improved data precision. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Evaluates the relative standard deviation (RSD/CV) distribution of pooled-QC peak intensities before and after signal drift correction, using the shift in the fraction of QC features below a 30 % (or 15 %) RSD cutoff to judge whether statTarget's QC-RFSC correction improved data precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain no repeated pooled-QC injections (QC-free design); use shiftCor_dQC with Combat instead of QC-RFSC and QC-RSD assessment. Feature intensities have already been filtered/normalized downstream (e.g. via statAnalysis Pareto scaling and glog) — RSDs computed there no longer reflect raw instrument precision. Assessing biological group separation rather than measurement precision; RSD of QC samples is not the appropriate metric.

skills.search_text: rt-based-spectrum-indexing Use when converting vendor MS data to the Aird format and you need fast random access to spectra by retention time, i.e. when building the .json metadata alongside the .aird data file. The target acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility — per the paper these formats were still under development and lack index support. The output format is mzML, mgf, or mz5 — this index is specific to the Aird format's JSON metadata layer, not these formats. You only need generic text-file conversion with no random-access readback; without an Aird reader the extra index building is wasted effort. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds the RT-MS index in Aird's JSON metadata layer so MS data are arranged linearly by retention time and each spectrum's RT and start position are recorded, letting programs read the .aird data file quickly during analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Builds the RT-MS index in Aird's JSON metadata layer so MS data are arranged linearly by retention time and each spectrum's RT and start position are recorded, letting programs read the .aird data file quickly during analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target acquisition mode is ScanningSWATH or Ion Mobility — per the paper these formats were still under development and lack index support. The output format is mzML, mgf, or mz5 — this index is specific to the Aird format's JSON metadata layer, not these formats. You only need generic text-file conversion with no random-access readback; without an Aird reader the extra index building is wasted effort.

skills.description: Use when building an in-house RT/m/z metabolite standard library from authentic-standard LC-MS mzML files, or when benchmarking that library-construction effort (per-standard time, total minutes, fold reduction) against a manual peak-picking baseline.
skills.name: rt-library-construction-workflow-analysis
skills.search_text: rt-library-construction-workflow-analysis Use when building an in-house RT/m/z metabolite standard library from authentic-standard LC-MS mzML files, or when benchmarking that library-construction effort (per-standard time, total minutes, fold reduction) against a manual peak-picking baseline. The goal is untargeted feature detection or peak picking on biological samples rather than authentic-standard library construction; tools such as MZmine, El-MAVEN, or MS-DIAL are better suited (metScribeR integrates with these downstream) The goal is MS/MS spectral library building — metScribeR focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use or require MS/MS for library construction (MS/MS retrieval from MoNA is optional and slow) Retention times must transfer across different laboratory-specific or method-specific LC-MS conditions — the article notes RT is not yet consistently transferable or predictable across methods, so in-house libraries apply within a single laboratory http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Semiautomated construction of in-house LC-MS metabolite retention-time (RT) and m/z reference libraries using metScribeR, an R package with a Shiny app that processes authentic-standard mzML files (MS1/RT only, no MS/MS required) and includes peak-quality filtering, manual review, and MoNA MS/MS lookup. Includes benchmarking the workflow's processing time against a manual MassHunter-style baseline (reported 26-fold reduction). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.5c00548
skills.summary: Semiautomated construction of in-house LC-MS metabolite retention-time (RT) and m/z reference libraries using metScribeR, an R package with a Shiny app that processes authentic-standard mzML files (MS1/RT only, no MS/MS required) and includes peak-quality filtering, manual review, and MoNA MS/MS lookup. Includes benchmarking the workflow's processing time against a manual MassHunter-style baseline (reported 26-fold reduction).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is untargeted feature detection or peak picking on biological samples rather than authentic-standard library construction; tools such as MZmine, El-MAVEN, or MS-DIAL are better suited (metScribeR integrates with these downstream) The goal is MS/MS spectral library building — metScribeR focuses on MS1 and RT data and does not use or require MS/MS for library construction (MS/MS retrieval from MoNA is optional and slow) Retention times must transfer across different laboratory-specific or method-specific LC-MS conditions — the article notes RT is not yet consistently transferable or predictable across methods, so in-house libraries apply within a single laboratory

Training the RT prediction regressors themselves (DNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) on SMRT, where a quantile transformation is applied to RTs before fitting instead of log + IQR scaling When RTs are already on the target chromatographic method's experimental scale and no cross-method projection is needed When the molecule set includes non-retained compounds that have not yet been filtered out, since they distort the learned scaling statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A preprocessing step of the Bayesian meta-learning RT projection module: retention times are compressed with log(1+x) and then robustly scaled using the median and 0.741*IQR so that the Gaussian Process can model residuals on a stable, roughly Gaussian scale. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8

skills.description: Use when a public or parameter-free LC/MS dataset lacks experimental QC injections but raw mzML-derived MS1 ion-feature matrices still show run-order/batch intensity drift that must be normalized before downstream modeling.
skills.name: rt-mz-drift-map-interpolation
skills.search_text: rt-mz-drift-map-interpolation Use when a public or parameter-free LC/MS dataset lacks experimental QC injections but raw mzML-derived MS1 ion-feature matrices still show run-order/batch intensity drift that must be normalized before downstream modeling. The input is already a normalized feature table or the drift correction was already applied — re-running would double-correct intensities Experimental QC samples with standardized injections are actually available, in which case conventional QC-based drift estimation can be used directly The analysis requires MS/MS-level de-isotoping, annotation, or compound identification — mzLearn results are at the ion MS1 level and do not perform these steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs synthetic QC samples and per-feature intensity drift maps in mzLearn when experimental QC samples are absent, by clustering run-order-consecutive samples and interpolating drift between neighboring pins in rt and m/z space. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Reconstructs synthetic QC samples and per-feature intensity drift maps in mzLearn when experimental QC samples are absent, by clustering run-order-consecutive samples and interpolating drift between neighboring pins in rt and m/z space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a normalized feature table or the drift correction was already applied — re-running would double-correct intensities Experimental QC samples with standardized injections are actually available, in which case conventional QC-based drift estimation can be used directly The analysis requires MS/MS-level de-isotoping, annotation, or compound identification — mzLearn results are at the ion MS1 level and do not perform these steps

skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples were all acquired under identical chromatographic conditions with good feature overlap, where a simple feature-table Bray-Curtis dissimilarity suffices Only MS1 feature tables are available and no MS2 fragmentation spectra were recorded (MEMO fingerprints require MS2 peaks and neutral losses) The goal is feature/compound-level annotation or molecular networking rather than sample-level clustering and batch-effect assessment

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated/annotated metabolite list or feature table rather than raw MS1 incubation data — use downstream CMDN layers (RCS/SSN) instead. Input is already a processed feature table or identification-based QC metrics (e.g., spectral match counts) rather than raw MS1 data — PeakQC's image-based PCA requires raw runs to build time-vs-m/z images The task is pinpointing the specific root cause of performance deterioration (chromatography, sensitivity, mass calibration); the PCA view flags compromised runs but identification-based metrics do little to pinpoint causes and detailed peak-metric extraction is needed Data are not mass spectrometry runs (e.g., NMR or sequencing data) — the skill is grounded in MS1 time-vs-m/z representations http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs PeakQC's PCA-based batch quality assessment: each MS run in a batch is represented by a time-versus-m/z image generated from MS1 data, and samples are projected onto leading principal components and colored by sample group so compromised or outlier MS runs are quickly spotted. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00146
skills.summary: Reconstructs PeakQC's PCA-based batch quality assessment: each MS run in a batch is represented by a time-versus-m/z image generated from MS1 data, and samples are projected onto leading principal components and colored by sample group so compromised or outlier MS runs are quickly spotted.

skills.description: Use when sample metadata records from SMetaS/MetaS need relationships beyond tabular columns — e.g. co-culture links — that a fixed 'is a' table cannot express as first-class relations.
skills.name: sample-metadata-graph-storage
skills.search_text: sample-metadata-graph-storage Use when sample metadata records from SMetaS/MetaS need relationships beyond tabular columns — e.g. co-culture links — that a fixed 'is a' table cannot express as first-class relations. The metadata relationships are adequately expressed by the existing fixed table of unique 'is a' links and no richer relations (e.g. co-cultures) are needed. Input data is raw, unstandardized freetext metadata that has not yet passed through SMetaS's vocabulary standardization step. The task is to run the standardization itself (n-grams/nearest-neighbors synonym fixing) rather than to restructure already-standardized records. Replaces SMetaS's fixed tabular representation of sample metadata with a node/edge graph in which samples and standardized descriptor terms are nodes and relationships (including 'is a' and co-culture links) are first-class typed edges, serialized to graph_storage.json. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941
skills.summary: Replaces SMetaS's fixed tabular representation of sample metadata with a node/edge graph in which samples and standardized descriptor terms are nodes and relationships (including 'is a' and co-culture links) are first-class typed edges, serialized to graph_storage.json.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metadata relationships are adequately expressed by the existing fixed table of unique 'is a' links and no richer relations (e.g. co-cultures) are needed. Input data is raw, unstandardized freetext metadata that has not yet passed through SMetaS's vocabulary standardization step. The task is to run the standardization itself (n-grams/nearest-neighbors synonym fixing) rather than to restructure already-standardized records.

skills.name: sample-metadata-standardization
skills.search_text: sample-metadata-standardization Use when a metabolomics study's sample metadata is freetext (e.g. zeroTimeEvent, drugName, drugDoseUnit columns) and terms must be mapped to fixed vocabularies, with the output feeding a study submission, repository deposit, or downstream pipeline. Metadata fields are numeric — SMetaS curation passes target non-numeric freetext strings only Input metadata already conforms to the target fixed vocabularies (e.g. controlled-terminology submissions), leaving nothing to standardize The task is general ontology building rather than mapping study metadata to a fixed vocabulary Standardize freetext metabolomics sample metadata by replacing freetext strings with terms from fixed vocabularies via SMetaS's n-grams/nearest-neighbors model (synonym matching and typographical fixing), then export the curated matrix as a standardized CSV and expose it through an API for pipeline integration. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941

skills.description: Use when you have a GNPS molecular networking job (spectra .mgf plus edges file) with sample metadata distinguishing treatment groups and need to retain spectra from one group while removing spectra network-connected to another.
skills.name: sample-metadata-stratification-gf-vs-spf
skills.search_text: sample-metadata-stratification-gf-vs-spf Use when you have a GNPS molecular networking job (spectra .mgf plus edges file) with sample metadata distinguishing treatment groups and need to retain spectra from one group while removing spectra network-connected to another. Input is already a feature table or consensus .mgf without accompanying edge table and group metadata — the cosine/±0.02 Da network filter cannot be applied The analysis goal is to search ALL spectra from a job rather than spectra unique to one sample-metadata group Sample groups cannot be distinguished from the metadata (no GF/SPF or equivalent treatment labels), making stratification impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Stratifies MS/MS spectra from a molecular networking job by sample metadata (germ-free vs SPF mouse groups) to isolate SPF-present spectra, then uses the networking edge table (cosine > 0.7, delta m/z within 0.02 Da) to remove spectra connected to GF-only spectra, producing the SPF-unique consensus set. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Stratifies MS/MS spectra from a molecular networking job by sample metadata (germ-free vs SPF mouse groups) to isolate SPF-present spectra, then uses the networking edge table (cosine > 0.7, delta m/z within 0.02 Da) to remove spectra connected to GF-only spectra, producing the SPF-unique consensus set.

When the user already supplies a finished GNPS metadata CSV exported from another pipeline and only needs to re-run networking, not rebuild the table. skills.name: sample-metadata-template-generation
skills.search_text: sample-metadata-template-generation Use when a metabolomics submission workflow needs a blank sample-metadata template (one row per sample, one column per selected attribute) for users to fill with freetext terms prior to vocabulary standardization. The user already has a completed sample-metadata CSV — route it to SMetaS's second component for vocabulary standardization instead of generating a new template. skills.summary: Generates a downloadable CSV sample-metadata matrix from a user's selections of core sample types and additional metadata attributes via the SMetaS frontend/API, providing an empty one-row-per-sample template that users complete locally with natural-language terms before resubmission to the standardization component.

skills.description: Use when a raw metabolomics data matrix (e.g. Metabolon OrigScale sheet or dummy_data.csv) needs sample-level outlier detection before analysis, and PCA-based SD-threshold flagging of samples on top PCs is desired.
skills.name: sample-outlier-flagging-sd-threshold
skills.search_text: sample-outlier-flagging-sd-threshold Use when a raw metabolomics data matrix (e.g. Metabolon OrigScale sheet or dummy_data.csv) needs sample-level outlier detection before analysis, and PCA-based SD-threshold flagging of samples on top PCs is desired. Data is already a feature-level summary or sample table with no metabolite intensity matrix — PCA outlier flagging requires the raw sample x feature data layer You only need feature (metabolite) QC rather than sample outlier identification — use feature_summary/feature_missingness instead The dataset has fewer informative PCs than the requested max_num_pcs and you cannot accept the automatic truncation with warning (README case: max_num_pcs=10 vs informative PCs=2) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Flags outlying samples in a metabolomics data matrix by running PCA on the median-imputed, z-standardized data and marking samples that deviate more than a user-defined number of standard deviations (e.g. pc_outlier_sd = 5) from the mean on the top informative PCs. Part of metaboprep's standardized preanalysis QC workflow for untargeted metabolite data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac059
skills.summary: Flags outlying samples in a metabolomics data matrix by running PCA on the median-imputed, z-standardized data and marking samples that deviate more than a user-defined number of standard deviations (e.g. pc_outlier_sd = 5) from the mean on the top informative PCs. Part of metaboprep's standardized preanalysis QC workflow for untargeted metabolite data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already a feature-level summary or sample table with no metabolite intensity matrix — PCA outlier flagging requires the raw sample x feature data layer You only need feature (metabolite) QC rather than sample outlier identification — use feature_summary/feature_missingness instead The dataset has fewer informative PCs than the requested max_num_pcs and you cannot accept the automatic truncation with warning (README case: max_num_pcs=10 vs informative PCs=2)

skills.description: Use when a lipidomics experiment (e.g. a LipidomicsExperiment from Metabolomics Workbench or Skyline export) needs QC screening before downstream analysis and suspect samples must be identified and removed.
skills.name: sample-quality-control-outlier-detection
skills.search_text: sample-quality-control-outlier-detection Use when a lipidomics experiment (e.g. a LipidomicsExperiment from Metabolomics Workbench or Skyline export) needs QC screening before downstream analysis and suspect samples must be identified and removed. The dataset is not a lipidomics experiment (lipidr's mva/PCA operates on lipid peak-area data, not general omics matrices). Outlier status must be determined from %CV of measured lipids rather than sample dispersion — lipidr supports filtering lipids by %CV, which is a different QC operation. You need lipid-level outlier detection rather than sample-level outlier detection; the workflow here identifies and removes whole samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Detect and remove outlier samples in lipidomics datasets by running PCA via lipidr's multivariate analysis and inspecting the interactive scores plot for samples with significantly large dispersion, as demonstrated on Metabolomics Workbench study ST001111. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00082
skills.summary: Detect and remove outlier samples in lipidomics datasets by running PCA via lipidr's multivariate analysis and inspecting the interactive scores plot for samples with significantly large dispersion, as demonstrated on Metabolomics Workbench study ST001111.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not a lipidomics experiment (lipidr's mva/PCA operates on lipid peak-area data, not general omics matrices). Outlier status must be determined from %CV of measured lipids rather than sample dispersion — lipidr supports filtering lipids by %CV, which is a different QC operation. You need lipid-level outlier detection rather than sample-level outlier detection; the workflow here identifies and removes whole samples.

skills.description: Use when raw (un)targeted metabolomics data (e.g. Nightingale NMR or Metabolon exports) must be characterized with sample- and feature-level QC metrics before applying user-defined exclusion thresholds.
skills.name: sample-quality-metric-computation
skills.search_text: sample-quality-metric-computation Use when raw (un)targeted metabolomics data (e.g. Nightingale NMR or Metabolon exports) must be characterized with sample- and feature-level QC metrics before applying user-defined exclusion thresholds. The data are already a filtered/QC-passed feature table and no preanalysis quality description is needed The goal is downstream statistical modelling (e.g. association testing) rather than data description and sample/metabolite exclusion The input is not a supported metabolomics platform format (Metabolon, Nightingale, Olink, SomaLogic) or generic data/features/samples tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes per-sample and per-metabolite quality-control summary statistics (missingness, total peak area, PCA-derived outliers, distributional metrics) on metabolomics data using the metaboprep R package, to support transparent, threshold-based sample and metabolite filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac059
skills.summary: Computes per-sample and per-metabolite quality-control summary statistics (missingness, total peak area, PCA-derived outliers, distributional metrics) on metabolomics data using the metaboprep R package, to support transparent, threshold-based sample and metabolite filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already a filtered/QC-passed feature table and no preanalysis quality description is needed The goal is downstream statistical modelling (e.g. association testing) rather than data description and sample/metabolite exclusion The input is not a supported metabolomics platform format (Metabolon, Nightingale, Olink, SomaLogic) or generic data/features/samples tables

skills.description: Use when two or more normalized, transformed, and scaled metabolomics tables — one per analytical platform — must be merged into a single integrated dataset in Viime and the sample rows need to correspond to the same biological samples across the merged blocks.
skills.name: sample-row-alignment-across-datasets
skills.search_text: sample-row-alignment-across-datasets Use when two or more normalized, transformed, and scaled metabolomics tables — one per analytical platform — must be merged into a single integrated dataset in Viime and the sample rows need to correspond to the same biological samples across the merged blocks. Only a single platform dataset is present — merging/alignment is unnecessary; proceed directly to normalization, transformation, scaling, and PCA analysis The workflow is still at preprocessing/annotation stage; Viime's intent is to pick up after preprocessing and annotation, and annotation is not required Samples in the platform tables do not correspond to the same biological samples — row alignment would force incorrect correspondences http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Align sample rows across platform-specific metabolomics tables (e.g. MS and NMR feature tables exported as .csv/.xlsx) so that rows correspond to the same biological samples before applying Viime's simple (concatenative), mid-level (PCA score fusion), or multi-block (first-singular-value normalization) data fusion algorithms. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Align sample rows across platform-specific metabolomics tables (e.g. MS and NMR feature tables exported as .csv/.xlsx) so that rows correspond to the same biological samples before applying Viime's simple (concatenative), mid-level (PCA score fusion), or multi-block (first-singular-value normalization) data fusion algorithms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single platform dataset is present — merging/alignment is unnecessary; proceed directly to normalization, transformation, scaling, and PCA analysis The workflow is still at preprocessing/annotation stage; Viime's intent is to pick up after preprocessing and annotation, and annotation is not required Samples in the platform tables do not correspond to the same biological samples — row alignment would force incorrect correspondences

skills.description: Use when an intra-batch randomized injection sequence has just been generated (block randomization or optimized block randomization) and must be checked for consecutive same-group runs and even group distribution before LC/GC-MS injection.
skills.name: sample-sequence-distribution-verification
skills.search_text: sample-sequence-distribution-verification Use when an intra-batch randomized injection sequence has just been generated (block randomization or optimized block randomization) and must be checked for consecutive same-group runs and even group distribution before LC/GC-MS injection. The sequence was produced by a completely random algorithm rather than block randomization — the paper notes complete randomization 'is not a perfect solution' and triple-run counts are not theoretically bounded to zero, so the zero-violation criterion does not apply The samples are still unbalanced across batches (inter-batch balancing on dimensions like age and gender has not been done), since this skill assumes the balanced assignment table from task-level balancing output Optimized block randomization was applied to a dimension with too many groups, where the paper warns local aggregation can occur under some special numerical distributions and the zero-triple expectation may not hold Validates an intra-batch randomized injection-order sequence (e.g., from block randomization with block size 2 in InjectionDesign) by scanning for runs of three consecutive samples from the same treatment/placebo group and confirming the sample distribution remains even. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.02.26.530140
skills.summary: Validates an intra-batch randomized injection-order sequence (e.g., from block randomization with block size 2 in InjectionDesign) by scanning for runs of three consecutive samples from the same treatment/placebo group and confirming the sample distribution remains even.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequence was produced by a completely random algorithm rather than block randomization — the paper notes complete randomization 'is not a perfect solution' and triple-run counts are not theoretically bounded to zero, so the zero-violation criterion does not apply The samples are still unbalanced across batches (inter-batch balancing on dimensions like age and gender has not been done), since this skill assumes the balanced assignment table from task-level balancing output Optimized block randomization was applied to a dimension with too many groups, where the paper warns local aggregation can occur under some special numerical distributions and the zero-triple expectation may not hold

skills.description: Use when multi-omics feature tables for the same samples (e.g., methylation betas and metabolite intensities) must be integrated into a single sample-by-sample similarity network to identify subject subgroups via clustering.
skills.name: sample-similarity-network-construction
skills.search_text: sample-similarity-network-construction Use when multi-omics feature tables for the same samples (e.g., methylation betas and metabolite intensities) must be integrated into a single sample-by-sample similarity network to identify subject subgroups via clustering. The goal is latent-factor extraction (e.g., MOFA2 factors) rather than discrete sample subgrouping via network fusion The data types describe different sample sets that cannot be aligned sample-by-sample per cohort Raw data are not yet standardized/preprocessed (standardization and QC are handled upstream in the ACTIONdemonstrator preprocessing workflow) Fuses standardized per-data-type sample similarity networks (DNA methylation and urine metabolomics) into one integrated similarity network with Similarity Network Fusion (SNF) and partitions samples into k=2 and k=4 clusters, as implemented in the ACTIONdemonstrator workflow for the NTR and LUMC-Curium cohorts. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad115
skills.summary: Fuses standardized per-data-type sample similarity networks (DNA methylation and urine metabolomics) into one integrated similarity network with Similarity Network Fusion (SNF) and partitions samples into k=2 and k=4 clusters, as implemented in the ACTIONdemonstrator workflow for the NTR and LUMC-Curium cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is latent-factor extraction (e.g., MOFA2 factors) rather than discrete sample subgrouping via network fusion The data types describe different sample sets that cannot be aligned sample-by-sample per cohort Raw data are not yet standardized/preprocessed (standardization and QC are handled upstream in the ACTIONdemonstrator preprocessing workflow)

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how a data-processing tool's CPU time and memory scale with sample number, or to benchmark one metabolomics pipeline against another (e.g. asari vs XCMS) on identical subsets of a public dataset.
skills.name: sample-size-scaling-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: sample-size-scaling-curve-analysis Use when you need to quantify how a data-processing tool's CPU time and memory scale with sample number, or to benchmark one metabolomics pipeline against another (e.g. asari vs XCMS) on identical subsets of a public dataset. The input is already a processed feature table — scaling analysis requires running the tools end-to-end on raw centroided mzML files The question is feature-detection accuracy or annotation quality rather than computational performance; this skill measures only CPU time, wall time, and memory The data are low-resolution or from platforms asari was not tuned for, since absolute runtimes would not generalize (asari was mostly tested on Orbitrap platforms) http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking method that varies the number of input samples (e.g. 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 centroided mzML files) and measures CPU time, wall-clock time, and peak memory for competing tools to quantify absolute performance gaps and scaling behavior. In the source work it was used to show asari's 1-2 orders-of-magnitude CPU-time improvement over XCMS and its near-linear scaling. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39889-1
skills.summary: A benchmarking method that varies the number of input samples (e.g. 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 centroided mzML files) and measures CPU time, wall-clock time, and peak memory for competing tools to quantify absolute performance gaps and scaling behavior. In the source work it was used to show asari's 1-2 orders-of-magnitude CPU-time improvement over XCMS and its near-linear scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table — scaling analysis requires running the tools end-to-end on raw centroided mzML files The question is feature-detection accuracy or annotation quality rather than computational performance; this skill measures only CPU time, wall time, and memory The data are low-resolution or from platforms asari was not tuned for, since absolute runtimes would not generalize (asari was mostly tested on Orbitrap platforms)

skills.description: Use when the same feature pairs have Pearson correlation coefficients measured in multiple studies, each with its own sample size, and a single combined fixed/random-effects estimate per pair is needed.
skills.name: sample-size-weighted-effect-combination
skills.search_text: sample-size-weighted-effect-combination Use when the same feature pairs have Pearson correlation coefficients measured in multiple studies, each with its own sample size, and a single combined fixed/random-effects estimate per pair is needed. Effect sizes are measured on different scales (e.g. mixing correlation coefficients with fold-changes or P-values) and cannot be averaged as correlations The question is simply computing per-sample Pearson correlations within one dataset — use MOG's pairwise correlation analysis instead of meta-analysis Only a single study is available, so there is nothing to combine across studies http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combines per-study Pearson correlation coefficients for the same feature (gene) pair across multiple studies using weights proportional to each study's sample size, under either a fixed effects or a random effects (e.g. DerSimonian-Laird) model, as implemented in MetaOmGraph. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Combines per-study Pearson correlation coefficients for the same feature (gene) pair across multiple studies using weights proportional to each study's sample size, under either a fixed effects or a random effects (e.g. DerSimonian-Laird) model, as implemented in MetaOmGraph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Effect sizes are measured on different scales (e.g. mixing correlation coefficients with fold-changes or P-values) and cannot be averaged as correlations The question is simply computing per-sample Pearson correlations within one dataset — use MOG's pairwise correlation analysis instead of meta-analysis Only a single study is available, so there is nothing to combine across studies

skills.description: Use when contributing studies report only aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change, sample size) per compound and you need to combine them into a single combined p-value, fold-change, and regulation direction per compound.
skills.name: sample-size-weighted-meta-analysis
skills.search_text: sample-size-weighted-meta-analysis Use when contributing studies report only aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change, sample size) per compound and you need to combine them into a single combined p-value, fold-change, and regulation direction per compound. Input studies provide individual-level (raw) data rather than aggregate statistics such as p-value and fold-change Studies report effect sizes other than p-value and fold-change (e.g. only qualitative direction calls) Compound names cannot be harmonized because no identifier mapping or naming-combination step can resolve synonyms across studies http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Combines per-study aggregate statistics (p-values and log2 fold-changes) across studies of the same compound using Amanida's weighted Fisher's method with non-integral gamma-distributed weights and sample-size-weighted averaging of fold-changes, as implemented in the amanida R package and Easy-Amanida Shiny app. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jrsm.1713
skills.summary: Combines per-study aggregate statistics (p-values and log2 fold-changes) across studies of the same compound using Amanida's weighted Fisher's method with non-integral gamma-distributed weights and sample-size-weighted averaging of fold-changes, as implemented in the amanida R package and Easy-Amanida Shiny app.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input studies provide individual-level (raw) data rather than aggregate statistics such as p-value and fold-change Studies report effect sizes other than p-value and fold-change (e.g. only qualitative direction calls) Compound names cannot be harmonized because no identifier mapping or naming-combination step can resolve synonyms across studies

skills.description: Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to automatically flag samples whose spectra deviate from the multi-sample spectral similarity structure, without manual inspection.
skills.name: sample-specific-cluster-identification-msi
skills.search_text: sample-specific-cluster-identification-msi Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to automatically flag samples whose spectra deviate from the multi-sample spectral similarity structure, without manual inspection. Single-sample datasets — the outlier detection relies on spectral similarity across multiple samples and cannot identify deviation without a cohort Analyses where pixel features have not yet been peak-picked/filtered — run the msi_preprocessing_flow peak list generation and peak filtering first Cases where you only need spatial tissue segmentation per sample (msi_segmentation_flow) rather than cross-sample outlier identification http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Automated multi-sample outlier detection for MALDI MSI pre-processing: pixel-wise peak features from all samples are jointly reduced to two dimensions with UMAP, clustered with HDBSCAN, and clusters in which ≥70% of pixels originate from one sample are labelled sample-specific clusters (SSC); samples whose pixels are dominated by SSCs are flagged as outliers. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Automated multi-sample outlier detection for MALDI MSI pre-processing: pixel-wise peak features from all samples are jointly reduced to two dimensions with UMAP, clustered with HDBSCAN, and clusters in which ≥70% of pixels originate from one sample are labelled sample-specific clusters (SSC); samples whose pixels are dominated by SSCs are flagged as outliers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-sample datasets — the outlier detection relies on spectral similarity across multiple samples and cannot identify deviation without a cohort Analyses where pixel features have not yet been peak-picked/filtered — run the msi_preprocessing_flow peak list generation and peak filtering first Cases where you only need spatial tissue segmentation per sample (msi_segmentation_flow) rather than cross-sample outlier identification

skills.description: Use when MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrices built from different MS platforms or acquisition batches must be made comparable prior to distance computation, PCoA ordination, or PERMANOVA testing.
skills.name: sample-wise-matrix-normalization
skills.search_text: sample-wise-matrix-normalization Use when MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrices built from different MS platforms or acquisition batches must be made comparable prior to distance computation, PCoA ordination, or PERMANOVA testing. Input is a raw MGF or feature quantification table that has not yet been converted into MS2 fingerprints and aligned on shared peak/loss keys — build the MemoMatrix first. Comparison requires retention-time-dependent or feature-alignment-based metrics rather than retention time agnostic MS2 fingerprint counts. The dataset consists of a single platform with no cross-platform or cross-batch comparability requirement, where simpler within-platform normalization may suffice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Sample-wise normalization scales aligned MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrices (counts of MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor per sample) so each sample contributes comparable signal. This is essential when comparing samples acquired on different MS platforms (Q-Exactive Orbitrap vs Maxis II Q-TOF) before computing MEMO distances for PCoA and PERMANOVA. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Sample-wise normalization scales aligned MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrices (counts of MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor per sample) so each sample contributes comparable signal. This is essential when comparing samples acquired on different MS platforms (Q-Exactive Orbitrap vs Maxis II Q-TOF) before computing MEMO distances for PCoA and PERMANOVA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw MGF or feature quantification table that has not yet been converted into MS2 fingerprints and aligned on shared peak/loss keys — build the MemoMatrix first. Comparison requires retention-time-dependent or feature-alignment-based metrics rather than retention time agnostic MS2 fingerprint counts. The dataset consists of a single platform with no cross-platform or cross-batch comparability requirement, where simpler within-platform normalization may suffice.

skills.description: Use when ingesting an externally published LC-MS2 dataset (e.g., MSV000093464 from MassIVE) whose .mzML, .mgf, feature quantification tables, and metadata must be organized per sample before ENPKG graph building.
skills.name: sample-wise-metabolomics-data-organization
skills.search_text: sample-wise-metabolomics-data-organization Use when ingesting an externally published LC-MS2 dataset (e.g., MSV000093464 from MassIVE) whose .mzML, .mgf, feature quantification tables, and metadata must be organized per sample before ENPKG graph building. The dataset is already a single consolidated feature table or aligned feature matrix across samples — the sample-centric organization would be redundant and the sample-level metadata mapping unavailable. The input is LC-MS data lacking per-sample taxonomic metadata (originating taxon), since the downstream Open Tree of Life (ott3.5) taxonomic enhancer cannot resolve sample identities. The goal is classical RT/m/z feature alignment across a single homogeneous batch — use a dataset-centric metabolomics workflow instead of reorganizing into a knowledge graph structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Restructures an external LC-MS/MS metabolomics dataset (e.g., .mzML and deconvoluted .mgf files retrieved from MassIVE) into a sample-wise folder architecture using the ENPKG data-organization scripts (01_enpkg_data_organization), so each sample can be processed individually and later integrated into the ENPKG knowledge graph. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Restructures an external LC-MS/MS metabolomics dataset (e.g., .mzML and deconvoluted .mgf files retrieved from MassIVE) into a sample-wise folder architecture using the ENPKG data-organization scripts (01_enpkg_data_organization), so each sample can be processed individually and later integrated into the ENPKG knowledge graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is already a single consolidated feature table or aligned feature matrix across samples — the sample-centric organization would be redundant and the sample-level metadata mapping unavailable. The input is LC-MS data lacking per-sample taxonomic metadata (originating taxon), since the downstream Open Tree of Life (ott3.5) taxonomic enhancer cannot resolve sample identities. The goal is classical RT/m/z feature alignment across a single homogeneous batch — use a dataset-centric metabolomics workflow instead of reorganizing into a knowledge graph structure.

skills.description: Use when a task requires regenerating or validating the ENPKG knowledge graph from deposited LC-MS/MS DDA data (e.g. MassIVE MSV000087728), or when reproducing sample-level feature detection, annotation, and RDF integration figures.
skills.name: sample-wise-metabolomics-workflow-reproducibility
skills.search_text: sample-wise-metabolomics-workflow-reproducibility Use when a task requires regenerating or validating the ENPKG knowledge graph from deposited LC-MS/MS DDA data (e.g. MassIVE MSV000087728), or when reproducing sample-level feature detection, annotation, and RDF integration figures. When the input is already an aligned feature quantification table or processed feature list rather than raw LC-MS2 DDA files — the workflow expects raw vendor/mzML data organized sample-wise. When the goal is batch-level feature alignment across samples via retention time; ENPKG is explicitly designed to avoid RT-based alignment, processing each sample individually. When working with non-LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics data or datasets whose folder structure differs from the expected sample-wise MassIVE organization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces the ENPKG sample-centric LC-HRMS2 workflow end-to-end, processing each sample individually (taxonomic resolution, MZmine feature detection, ISDB-LOTUS spectral matching, SIRIUS/CANOPUS annotation) and rebuilding the RDF knowledge graph from the 1,600 plant extracts dataset (MSV000087728) instead of relying on batch-wise feature alignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Reproduces the ENPKG sample-centric LC-HRMS2 workflow end-to-end, processing each sample individually (taxonomic resolution, MZmine feature detection, ISDB-LOTUS spectral matching, SIRIUS/CANOPUS annotation) and rebuilding the RDF knowledge graph from the 1,600 plant extracts dataset (MSV000087728) instead of relying on batch-wise feature alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already an aligned feature quantification table or processed feature list rather than raw LC-MS2 DDA files — the workflow expects raw vendor/mzML data organized sample-wise. When the goal is batch-level feature alignment across samples via retention time; ENPKG is explicitly designed to avoid RT-based alignment, processing each sample individually. When working with non-LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics data or datasets whose folder structure differs from the expected sample-wise MassIVE organization.

skills.description: Use when a log-transformed, missing-value-imputed metabolomics featuredata matrix (samples as rows, metabolites as columns) needs sample-wise scaling normalization, or when one of sum, median, mean, or reference-vector normalization is required.
skills.name: sample-wise-scaling-normalization
skills.search_text: sample-wise-scaling-normalization Use when a log-transformed, missing-value-imputed metabolomics featuredata matrix (samples as rows, metabolites as columns) needs sample-wise scaling normalization, or when one of sum, median, mean, or reference-vector normalization is required. When QC-sample-based signal correction is needed instead of simple scaling — use NormQcsamples (QC-RLSC) rather than NormScaling. When normalization should exploit internal/external standards or quality control metabolites — use NormQcmets methods (is, nomis, ccmn, ruv2, ruvrand, ruvrandclust). When a sequential combination of normalizations is the goal, call NormCombined directly rather than chaining NormScaling manually (though NormCombined itself chains median scaling after rlsc by default). http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scaling normalization of metabolomics feature data via the NormalizeMets NormScaling function, which normalizes each sample by its total sum, median, or mean peak intensity (or concentration), or to a user-supplied reference vector such as sample weight or volume. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1347-7
skills.summary: Scaling normalization of metabolomics feature data via the NormalizeMets NormScaling function, which normalizes each sample by its total sum, median, or mean peak intensity (or concentration), or to a user-supplied reference vector such as sample weight or volume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When QC-sample-based signal correction is needed instead of simple scaling — use NormQcsamples (QC-RLSC) rather than NormScaling. When normalization should exploit internal/external standards or quality control metabolites — use NormQcmets methods (is, nomis, ccmn, ruv2, ruvrand, ruvrandclust). When a sequential combination of normalizations is the goal, call NormCombined directly rather than chaining NormScaling manually (though NormCombined itself chains median scaling after rlsc by default).

skills.description: Use when MALDI-imaging MS data (.imzML/.ibd/.RAW/.UDP) from a laser-ablation experiment on cultured cells must be converted into per-cell molecular profiles, i.e. when ablation marks must be linked to segmented cells to build a spatio-molecular matrix.
skills.name: sampling-area-overlap-normalization-to-per-cell-molecular-assignment
skills.search_text: sampling-area-overlap-normalization-to-per-cell-molecular-assignment Use when MALDI-imaging MS data (.imzML/.ibd/.RAW/.UDP) from a laser-ablation experiment on cultured cells must be converted into per-cell molecular profiles, i.e. when ablation marks must be linked to segmented cells to build a spatio-molecular matrix. Ablation marks are overlapping or not visible in the post-MALDI microscopy — mark segmentation and per-cell assignment are unreliable Input is already a per-cell feature/molecular table (e.g. scRNA-seq or a finished MORPHnMOL.csv) — this skill addresses the raw-image-to-cell intensity assignment step only Tissue-section rather than cultured-cell MALDI-IMS experiments, where tiled cell-culture microscopy and cell segmentation do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 SpaceM assigns MALDI-IMS metabolite intensities to individual cultured cells by co-registering laser-ablation marks detected in post-MALDI microscopy with CellProfiler-segmented cells from pre-MALDI microscopy, and normalizing per-mark intensities by the 45% sampling-area overlap so each cell receives only the fraction of signal from the cell area actually ablated. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-021-01198-0
skills.summary: SpaceM assigns MALDI-IMS metabolite intensities to individual cultured cells by co-registering laser-ablation marks detected in post-MALDI microscopy with CellProfiler-segmented cells from pre-MALDI microscopy, and normalizing per-mark intensities by the 45% sampling-area overlap so each cell receives only the fraction of signal from the cell area actually ablated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ablation marks are overlapping or not visible in the post-MALDI microscopy — mark segmentation and per-cell assignment are unreliable Input is already a per-cell feature/molecular table (e.g. scRNA-seq or a finished MORPHnMOL.csv) — this skill addresses the raw-image-to-cell intensity assignment step only Tissue-section rather than cultured-cell MALDI-IMS experiments, where tiled cell-culture microscopy and cell segmentation do not apply

skills.description: Use when a concentration-inference method validated on dense, noiseless time-course metabolomics data must be stress-tested against realistic acquisition conditions — i.e., fewer sampled timepoints and noisy relative-abundance measurements with defined CoV.
skills.name: sampling-frequency-perturbation-testing
skills.search_text: sampling-frequency-perturbation-testing Use when a concentration-inference method validated on dense, noiseless time-course metabolomics data must be stress-tested against realistic acquisition conditions — i.e., fewer sampled timepoints and noisy relative-abundance measurements with defined CoV. The goal is to evaluate inference on noiseless, densely sampled data — use the plain MetaboPAC_*.m workflow instead of the _noisy variant The metabolomics data are from eukaryotic multi-compartment systems with transport reactions across intracellular compartments, which MetaboPAC does not model Only a single noise level or sampling rate is of interest and no head-to-head comparison of the two perturbations is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A robustness-testing protocol that regenerates synthetic time-course GC-MS metabolomics datasets with reduced sampling frequency (50 to 15 timepoints) and added noise (coefficient of variation 5% and 15%), then re-runs MetaboPAC to quantify how both perturbations degrade inference of absolute concentrations from relative abundance data. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: A robustness-testing protocol that regenerates synthetic time-course GC-MS metabolomics datasets with reduced sampling frequency (50 to 15 timepoints) and added noise (coefficient of variation 5% and 15%), then re-runs MetaboPAC to quantify how both perturbations degrade inference of absolute concentrations from relative abundance data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate inference on noiseless, densely sampled data — use the plain MetaboPAC_*.m workflow instead of the _noisy variant The metabolomics data are from eukaryotic multi-compartment systems with transport reactions across intracellular compartments, which MetaboPAC does not model Only a single noise level or sampling rate is of interest and no head-to-head comparison of the two perturbations is needed

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether a generative molecular-structure decoder's reported benchmark metrics depend on the sampling temperature hyperparameter, e.g. reproducing Table 8 of the MS-BART paper.
skills.name: sampling-temperature-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: sampling-temperature-sensitivity-analysis Use when you need to test whether a generative molecular-structure decoder's reported benchmark metrics depend on the sampling temperature hyperparameter, e.g. reproducing Table 8 of the MS-BART paper. Evaluating a deterministic (greedy/beam-only) decoding configuration where no sampling temperature is involved — the ablation has no varying knob. Running on the restricted NIST23 dataset, which the paper excludes due to commercial licensing. Assessing sensitivity to a non-decoding hyperparameter (e.g. fingerprint bit threshold epsilon or adduct filtering), which needs a different ablation protocol. http://edamontology.org/topic_3418 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A robustness-ablation skill that decodes a generative structure-elucidation model (e.g. MS-Bart on MassSpecGym) at several sampling temperatures and checks whether Top-1/Top-10 accuracy, MCES distance and Tanimoto similarity metrics remain stable across temperatures. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: A robustness-ablation skill that decodes a generative structure-elucidation model (e.g. MS-Bart on MassSpecGym) at several sampling temperatures and checks whether Top-1/Top-10 accuracy, MCES distance and Tanimoto similarity metrics remain stable across temperatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating a deterministic (greedy/beam-only) decoding configuration where no sampling temperature is involved — the ablation has no varying knob. Running on the restricted NIST23 dataset, which the paper excludes due to commercial licensing. Assessing sensitivity to a non-decoding hyperparameter (e.g. fingerprint bit threshold epsilon or adduct filtering), which needs a different ablation protocol.

skills.description: Use when a kernel machine score test needs a null p-value: the quadratic-form statistic Q's null distribution must be approximated by Satterthwaite moment-matching as a scaled chi-square c·χ²_ν.
skills.name: satterthwaite-moment-matching
skills.search_text: satterthwaite-moment-matching Use when a kernel machine score test needs a null p-value: the quadratic-form statistic Q's null distribution must be approximated by Satterthwaite moment-matching as a scaled chi-square c·χ²_ν. The input is raw metabolite intensities rather than partial residuals from the covariate-adjusted null regression — preprocessing (run-day median normalization, kNN imputation with k = 10, log transform, standardization) must be done first. The graph's connectivity structure has not been examined: the article notes it is important to examine graph structure before regularization, and the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered testing performance on disconnected graphs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes pathway-level significance in PaIRKAT by evaluating the quadratic-form kernel score statistic Q and approximating its null distribution with Satterthwaite's moment-matching scaled chi-square (c·χ²_ν) to obtain the p-value for H0: τ=0. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Computes pathway-level significance in PaIRKAT by evaluating the quadratic-form kernel score statistic Q and approximating its null distribution with Satterthwaite's moment-matching scaled chi-square (c·χ²_ν) to obtain the p-value for H0: τ=0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw metabolite intensities rather than partial residuals from the covariate-adjusted null regression — preprocessing (run-day median normalization, kNN imputation with k = 10, log transform, standardization) must be done first. The graph's connectivity structure has not been examined: the article notes it is important to examine graph structure before regularization, and the unregularized normalized Laplacian hindered testing performance on disconnected graphs.

skills.name: saturated-peak-exclusion
skills.search_text: saturated-peak-exclusion Use when fitting standard-curve regressions (constant/linear/quadratic) or QC-RLSC batch-effect corrections in MRMQuant, and some calibration points or BQC peaks may be saturated with unreliable abundances. Input is already a computed concentration/feature table rather than raw MRM peak abundances needing regression No calibration points or QC samples are present and no regression is being fitted (e.g. constant-abundance mode for compounds run without standards) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Automatically removes saturated calibration/QC peaks from regression in MRMQuant before fitting standard curves or QC-RLSC batch-effect correction, because saturated abundances are unreliable and would bias least-squares fits. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Automatically removes saturated calibration/QC peaks from regression in MRMQuant before fitting standard curves or QC-RLSC batch-effect correction, because saturated abundances are unreliable and would bias least-squares fits.

skills.description: Use when LC-IM-MS raw/profile-level data (e.g. Agilent .d TOF files) contain high-abundance ions with truncated intensity profiles due to detector saturation, and accurate isotopic distributions or monoisotopic peak heights are needed downstream.
skills.name: saturation-repair-peak-reconstruction
skills.search_text: saturation-repair-peak-reconstruction Use when LC-IM-MS raw/profile-level data (e.g. Agilent .d TOF files) contain high-abundance ions with truncated intensity profiles due to detector saturation, and accurate isotopic distributions or monoisotopic peak heights are needed downstream. Data are already centroided or processed to a peak/feature table, since the algorithm operates on raw/profile-level spectra and needs the full intensity profile to reconstruct saturated peaks Input is low-abundance data with no ions near detector saturation — the smoothing step (not saturation repair) is the module that addresses poorly defined low-abundance signals A theoretical isotopic distribution is already available and the user only wants to fit a model rather than recover the observed undistorted distribution from the same run http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 The PNNL PreProcessor saturation repair module reconstructs the distorted LC and IM intensity profiles of high-abundance ions whose peaks are truncated by detector saturation in LC-IM-MS data, recovering the undistorted isotopic distribution from later, unsaturated portions of the run. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00425
skills.summary: The PNNL PreProcessor saturation repair module reconstructs the distorted LC and IM intensity profiles of high-abundance ions whose peaks are truncated by detector saturation in LC-IM-MS data, recovering the undistorted isotopic distribution from later, unsaturated portions of the run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already centroided or processed to a peak/feature table, since the algorithm operates on raw/profile-level spectra and needs the full intensity profile to reconstruct saturated peaks Input is low-abundance data with no ions near detector saturation — the smoothing step (not saturation repair) is the module that addresses poorly defined low-abundance signals A theoretical isotopic distribution is already available and the user only wants to fit a model rather than recover the observed undistorted distribution from the same run

skills.description: Use when targeted LC–MS ion chromatograms (RT and intensity vectors) are noisy and peak borders must be located reliably before integration, as in TARDIS's targeted peak border detection workflow.
skills.name: savitzky-golay-chromatogram-smoothing
skills.search_text: savitzky-golay-chromatogram-smoothing Use when targeted LC–MS ion chromatograms (RT and intensity vectors) are noisy and peak borders must be located reliably before integration, as in TARDIS's targeted peak border detection workflow. The goal is untargeted feature finding across full profiles — TARDIS and this smoothing/border-detection step are for targeted peak extraction, not untargeted peak searching (xcms, MZmine, OpenMS). Peaks are already integrated and only downstream statistics or feature-table manipulation is needed — no chromatogram smoothing is required. The input is already a QC feature table of per-target average metrics rather than raw chromatographic intensity vectors. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Savitzky-Golay smoothing of chromatographic intensity vectors, as used inside the TARDIS R package (via sgolayfilt() from the signal package) to stabilize targeted LC–MS ion chromatograms before apex selection, peak border definition, and trapezoidal AUC integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00567
skills.summary: Savitzky-Golay smoothing of chromatographic intensity vectors, as used inside the TARDIS R package (via sgolayfilt() from the signal package) to stabilize targeted LC–MS ion chromatograms before apex selection, peak border definition, and trapezoidal AUC integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is untargeted feature finding across full profiles — TARDIS and this smoothing/border-detection step are for targeted peak extraction, not untargeted peak searching (xcms, MZmine, OpenMS). Peaks are already integrated and only downstream statistics or feature-table manipulation is needed — no chromatogram smoothing is required. The input is already a QC feature table of per-target average metrics rather than raw chromatographic intensity vectors.

skills.description: Use when you need to smooth noisy extracted ion chromatograms from mzXML/mzML LC-MS metabolomics data before peak detection and per-peak quality metrics (MCQ, asymmetry factor, FWHM) are computed.

skills.search_text: savitzky-golay-peak-smoothing Use when you need to smooth noisy extracted ion chromatograms from mzXML/mzML LC-MS metabolomics data before peak detection and per-peak quality metrics (MCQ, asymmetry factor, FWHM) are computed. Raw chromatograms that have not undergone IRLS baseline correction — the workflow smooths the baseline-corrected EIC, not the raw signal Data analysis aimed at quality-control filtering of already-scored peaks (e.g. applying Std/Blk > r, RSD < c, intensity > I thresholds) rather than peak-profile smoothing Smoothing of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) with a Savitzky-Golay filter after IRLS baseline correction, as implemented in the MetaMOPE workflow for fast LC-MS chromatographic peak evaluation in metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad061
skills.summary: Smoothing of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) with a Savitzky-Golay filter after IRLS baseline correction, as implemented in the MetaMOPE workflow for fast LC-MS chromatographic peak evaluation in metabolomics.

Input is already a table of derived peak metrics (MCQ, intensity, Std/Blk) — smoothing applies to raw EIC intensity traces, not to downstream metric tables Goal is mobile-phase comparison/selection from metric summaries rather than per-peak signal preprocessing of individual chromatograms Data are direct-infusion MS or non-chromatographic spectra where no retention-time axis exists to define an EIC http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Preprocesses extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) from mzML/mzXML LC-MS metabolomics runs by IRLS baseline correction followed by Savitzky-Golay smoothing, as implemented in the MetaMOPE workflow, so that per-peak metrics (MCQ, maximum intensity, asymmetry factor, FWHM, Std/Blk ratio) are computed on a clean signal. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbad061
