skills.description: Use when input is an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (possibly virus-integrated) and the goal is structural/dynamical analysis — chokepoints, bottlenecks, essential reactions, FVA flux bounds, or PPI-to-enzyme mapping for drug-target prediction.
skills.name: sbml-genome-scale-model-interrogation
skills.search_text: sbml-genome-scale-model-interrogation Use when input is an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (possibly virus-integrated) and the goal is structural/dynamical analysis — chokepoints, bottlenecks, essential reactions, FVA flux bounds, or PPI-to-enzyme mapping for drug-target prediction. The input is not an SBML constraint-based metabolic model (e.g. it is a pathway graph, PPI network alone, or expression matrix without a GEM) — chokepoint/bottleneck topology reasoning requires the reaction network. The aim is kinetic or dynamic simulation of metabolism rather than constraint-based (FBA/FVA) structural analysis, which is what COBRApy/findCPcli provide. You lack solver support (GLPK) or the model cannot be instantiated — e.g. the study validated instantiation specifically on COBRA 0.16.0. http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Load and interrogate an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. the iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 model, BioModels MODEL2007210001) with COBRApy/GLPK and compute chokepoint, essential-reaction, dead-end-metabolite, and FVA-refined analyses with findCPcli to identify host-dependency factors and drug targets. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Load and interrogate an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. the iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 model, BioModels MODEL2007210001) with COBRApy/GLPK and compute chokepoint, essential-reaction, dead-end-metabolite, and FVA-refined analyses with findCPcli to identify host-dependency factors and drug targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not an SBML constraint-based metabolic model (e.g. it is a pathway graph, PPI network alone, or expression matrix without a GEM) — chokepoint/bottleneck topology reasoning requires the reaction network. The aim is kinetic or dynamic simulation of metabolism rather than constraint-based (FBA/FVA) structural analysis, which is what COBRApy/findCPcli provide. You lack solver support (GLPK) or the model cannot be instantiated — e.g. the study validated instantiation specifically on COBRA 0.16.0.

skills.description: Use when the input is an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21 or the macrophage iAB-AMØ-1410 SARS-CoV-2 integrated models) that must be parsed and instantiated in Python before FBA/FVA/bottleneck analyses.
skills.name: sbml-metabolic-model-loading
skills.search_text: sbml-metabolic-model-loading Use when the input is an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21 or the macrophage iAB-AMØ-1410 SARS-CoV-2 integrated models) that must be parsed and instantiated in Python before FBA/FVA/bottleneck analyses. The input is not an SBML genome-scale model (e.g. gene expression tables or protein–protein interaction data), which are added only after model instantiation The analysis only requires model quality scoring rather than simulation — use MEMOTE checks instead of loading into a solver-driven pipeline A non-Python constraint-based framework is mandated, since the paper's workflow depends on the COBRApy toolbox with GLPK Load genome-scale metabolic models in SBML format into COBRApy (backed by the GLPK LP solver) so they can be instantiated without error for downstream constraint-based analyses such as FBA, FVA, chokepoint and essential-reaction computations. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Load genome-scale metabolic models in SBML format into COBRApy (backed by the GLPK LP solver) so they can be instantiated without error for downstream constraint-based analyses such as FBA, FVA, chokepoint and essential-reaction computations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not an SBML genome-scale model (e.g. gene expression tables or protein–protein interaction data), which are added only after model instantiation The analysis only requires model quality scoring rather than simulation — use MEMOTE checks instead of loading into a solver-driven pipeline A non-Python constraint-based framework is mandated, since the paper's workflow depends on the COBRApy toolbox with GLPK

skills.description: Use when member models carry fixed lower/upper flux bounds that must scale with community member abundance, or when a COBRApy community model must be saved/loaded as SBML and remain fully reusable.
skills.name: sbml-model-conversion-and-validation
skills.search_text: sbml-model-conversion-and-validation Use when member models carry fixed lower/upper flux bounds that must scale with community member abundance, or when a COBRApy community model must be saved/loaded as SBML and remain fully reusable. The member model contains no fixed flux bounds that need to become abundance-dependent — the bound-free transformation adds unnecessary dummy metabolites The target workflow requires a community model with fixed abundance profile and variable growth rate rather than variable abundance — PyCoMo's structure switching supports this without re-encoding bounds The file must remain a plain member model, not a community model with memberId_-prefixed metabolite and compartment IDs as required for ScyNet/PyCoMo community models http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Convert genome-scale member metabolic models into a bound-free, SBML-compliant community form with PyCoMo, where fixed flux bounds become stoichiometric coefficients of dummy metabolites scaled by member abundance, then validate round-trip via SBML export/load in COBRApy. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: Convert genome-scale member metabolic models into a bound-free, SBML-compliant community form with PyCoMo, where fixed flux bounds become stoichiometric coefficients of dummy metabolites scaled by member abundance, then validate round-trip via SBML export/load in COBRApy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The member model contains no fixed flux bounds that need to become abundance-dependent — the bound-free transformation adds unnecessary dummy metabolites The target workflow requires a community model with fixed abundance profile and variable growth rate rather than variable abundance — PyCoMo's structure switching supports this without re-encoding bounds The file must remain a plain member model, not a community model with memberId_-prefixed metabolite and compartment IDs as required for ScyNet/PyCoMo community models

skills.description: Use when a Reconstructor reconstruction (from FASTA, BLASTp hits, or an existing SBML) is complete or gap-filled and needs to be written out as a portable SBML GENRE for benchmarking or downstream COBRApy analysis.
skills.name: sbml-model-export
skills.search_text: sbml-model-export Use when a Reconstructor reconstruction (from FASTA, BLASTp hits, or an existing SBML) is complete or gap-filled and needs to be written out as a portable SBML GENRE for benchmarking or downstream COBRApy analysis. The input is raw sequence data needing annotation or BLASTp alignment first — SBML export assumes a draft or completed COBRApy model The target pipeline requires formats other than SBML or non-ModelSEED identifier namespaces, since Reconstructor's naming follows the ModelSEED biochemistry database You only need gap-filling statistics without a portable exported model file http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Export Reconstructor-built genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) as SBML files with reaction and metabolite naming consistent with the ModelSEED biochemistry database, so models are portable into COBRApy, MEMOTE, and other COBRA tooling. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad367
skills.summary: Export Reconstructor-built genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions (GENREs) as SBML files with reaction and metabolite naming consistent with the ModelSEED biochemistry database, so models are portable into COBRApy, MEMOTE, and other COBRA tooling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequence data needing annotation or BLASTp alignment first — SBML export assumes a draft or completed COBRApy model The target pipeline requires formats other than SBML or non-ModelSEED identifier namespaces, since Reconstructor's naming follows the ModelSEED biochemistry database You only need gap-filling statistics without a portable exported model file

skills.description: Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model has default or inconsistent reaction bounds and downstream analyses (chokepoints, reversibility, bottlenecks) require bounds updated to steady-state FVA-computed ranges.
skills.name: sbml-model-flux-bound-refinement
skills.search_text: sbml-model-flux-bound-refinement Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model has default or inconsistent reaction bounds and downstream analyses (chokepoints, reversibility, bottlenecks) require bounds updated to steady-state FVA-computed ranges. The task requires raw FVA flux ranges as a report/spreadsheet rather than an updated model file — use the default output spreadsheet (-o) instead of model refinement The downstream analysis does not depend on reaction reversibility or flux bounds (e.g. purely topological or gene-level analyses) You intend to alter the model's stoichiometry or network structure — FVA refinement only updates reaction bounds, it does not add or remove reactions (dead-end metabolite removal is a separate option) http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Refine a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format by replacing every reaction's flux bounds with the min/max flux ranges computed via Flux Variability Analysis, producing an FVA-refined model (e.g. model_fva.xml) that supports reliable reversibility determination and flux-dependent chokepoint analyses with findCPcli. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Refine a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format by replacing every reaction's flux bounds with the min/max flux ranges computed via Flux Variability Analysis, producing an FVA-refined model (e.g. model_fva.xml) that supports reliable reversibility determination and flux-dependent chokepoint analyses with findCPcli.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires raw FVA flux ranges as a report/spreadsheet rather than an updated model file — use the default output spreadsheet (-o) instead of model refinement The downstream analysis does not depend on reaction reversibility or flux bounds (e.g. purely topological or gene-level analyses) You intend to alter the model's stoichiometry or network structure — FVA refinement only updates reaction bounds, it does not add or remove reactions (dead-end metabolite removal is a separate option)

skills.description: Use when a genome-scale community metabolic model built with PyCoMo (e.g. the three-species biogas model of D. vulgaris, M. hungatei, M. barkeri) must be persisted to, or reloaded from, an SBML file for sharing, reuse, or downstream COBRA analysis.
skills.name: sbml-model-input-output
skills.search_text: sbml-model-input-output Use when a genome-scale community metabolic model built with PyCoMo (e.g. the three-species biogas model of D. vulgaris, M. hungatei, M. barkeri) must be persisted to, or reloaded from, an SBML file for sharing, reuse, or downstream COBRA analysis. The goal is analysis (exchange metabolite/cross-feeding prediction, max growth rate, FVA) rather than persisting or reusing the model — use PyCoMo's analysis workflows instead. The input is a single-organism metabolic model with no community structure — there is no shared exchange compartment or member-prefixed IDs for this skill to preserve. The model was not generated with PyCoMo and lacks the expected SBML conventions (shared exchange compartment named 'medium' or a shared_compartment_id parameter) required by downstream consumers such as ScyNet. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Saving and reloading PyCoMo-generated compartmentalized community metabolic models in SBML format so they remain COBRApy-compatible, fully reusable, and retain member-of-origin attribution and original reaction bounds. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: Saving and reloading PyCoMo-generated compartmentalized community metabolic models in SBML format so they remain COBRApy-compatible, fully reusable, and retain member-of-origin attribution and original reaction bounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is analysis (exchange metabolite/cross-feeding prediction, max growth rate, FVA) rather than persisting or reusing the model — use PyCoMo's analysis workflows instead. The input is a single-organism metabolic model with no community structure — there is no shared exchange compartment or member-prefixed IDs for this skill to preserve. The model was not generated with PyCoMo and lacks the expected SBML conventions (shared exchange compartment named 'medium' or a shared_compartment_id parameter) required by downstream consumers such as ScyNet.

skills.name: sbml-model-io-with-cobrapy
skills.search_text: sbml-model-io-with-cobrapy Use when you need to turn an annotated amino acid .fasta (or BLASTp output) into an SBML metabolic model and immediately interrogate it with COBRApy tools such as FBA or single_gene_deletion. skills.description: Use when a compartmentalized community metabolic model (SBML from PyCoMo, e.g. the biogas community of D. vulgaris, M. hungatei, M. barkeri) must be reloaded and analysed for exchange fluxes or cross-feeding via COBRApy.
skills.name: sbml-model-loading-and-analysis
skills.search_text: sbml-model-loading-and-analysis Use when a compartmentalized community metabolic model (SBML from PyCoMo, e.g. the biogas community of D. vulgaris, M. hungatei, M. barkeri) must be reloaded and analysed for exchange fluxes or cross-feeding via COBRApy. The goal is a single optimal flux distribution for a fixed abundance profile (FBA), not the full space of feasible exchange metabolites and cross-feeding interactions The input is raw member genome-scale models not yet combined — use PyCoMo model creation first, then load the resulting SBML Only visual exploration of the community network is needed (use ScyNet on the SBML instead of scripting FVA) http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Load a PyCoMo-generated, COBRApy-compatible community metabolic model from SBML and analyse it with COBRApy methods (e.g. FVA) to enumerate feasible exchange metabolites and cross-feeding interactions independent of the abundance profile. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: Load a PyCoMo-generated, COBRApy-compatible community metabolic model from SBML and analyse it with COBRApy methods (e.g. FVA) to enumerate feasible exchange metabolites and cross-feeding interactions independent of the abundance profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single optimal flux distribution for a fixed abundance profile (FBA), not the full space of feasible exchange metabolites and cross-feeding interactions The input is raw member genome-scale models not yet combined — use PyCoMo model creation first, then load the resulting SBML Only visual exploration of the community network is needed (use ScyNet on the SBML instead of scripting FVA)

skills.description: Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. from BioModels) must be assessed against community standards for annotation completeness, GPR coverage, and stoichiometric consistency before publication or reuse.
skills.name: sbml-model-validation
skills.search_text: sbml-model-validation Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. from BioModels) must be assessed against community standards for annotation completeness, GPR coverage, and stoichiometric consistency before publication or reuse. The model is not in SBML format or is not a constraint-based metabolic model (MEMOTE's test battery targets GEM content) The goal is functional simulation (e.g. FBA/FVA growth or chokepoint analysis) rather than structural/annotation quality assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Standardised quality-control of a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format using MEMOTE (which reads the model via COBRApy), covering annotation consistency, GPR coverage, stoichiometric consistency, and model metadata, benchmarked against community standards. metabolomics/v3 10.26508/lsa.202000954
skills.summary: Standardised quality-control of a genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format using MEMOTE (which reads the model via COBRApy), covering annotation consistency, GPR coverage, stoichiometric consistency, and model metadata, benchmarked against community standards.

skills.description: Use when evaluating MS/MS spectral-prediction or retrieval models on NIST20-like datasets and you need a split that prevents highly similar scaffold-mates from leaking into the test set, making generalization across chemical classes a fair test.
skills.name: scaffold-based-dataset-splitting
skills.search_text: scaffold-based-dataset-splitting Use when evaluating MS/MS spectral-prediction or retrieval models on NIST20-like datasets and you need a split that prevents highly similar scaffold-mates from leaking into the test set, making generalization across chemical classes a fair test. When the goal is a permissive random-split benchmark and scaffold leakage is acceptable — the stricter scaffold split will understate model performance. When the dataset lacks molecular structures from which Murcko scaffolds can be derived, since the split cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Split a mass spectrometry / machine-learning benchmark dataset so that test-set molecules belong to smaller Murcko scaffold clusters held out from training, exposing whether a spectral-prediction model generalizes across chemical scaffolds rather than memorizing scaffold-mates. Used in the ICEBERG work to compare ICEBERG, MassFormer, and SCARF under a stricter split than random. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Split a mass spectrometry / machine-learning benchmark dataset so that test-set molecules belong to smaller Murcko scaffold clusters held out from training, exposing whether a spectral-prediction model generalizes across chemical scaffolds rather than memorizing scaffold-mates. Used in the ICEBERG work to compare ICEBERG, MassFormer, and SCARF under a stricter split than random.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a permissive random-split benchmark and scaffold leakage is acceptable — the stricter scaffold split will understate model performance. When the dataset lacks molecular structures from which Murcko scaffolds can be derived, since the split cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when you have an MS/MS spectrum plus a candidate scaffold (predicted or oracle) and need to generate full candidate molecular structures for top-k accuracy or Tanimoto-based evaluation.
skills.name: scaffold-conditioned-de-novo-graph-generation
skills.search_text: scaffold-conditioned-de-novo-graph-generation Use when you have an MS/MS spectrum plus a candidate scaffold (predicted or oracle) and need to generate full candidate molecular structures for top-k accuracy or Tanimoto-based evaluation. You do not have a scaffold (predicted or oracle) and cannot run scaffold retrieval first — the generator is scaffold-conditioned and requires a starting scaffold. Your spectra are not MS/MS tandem spectra preprocessed with intensity normalization and low-intensity peak removal; MADGEN was built for NIST23, CANOPUS, and MassSpecGym-style MS/MS data. NIST23 data is needed but not separately licensed — the NIST dataset is commercially available and cannot be pulled from the public Zenodo records. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate de novo molecular structures from MS/MS spectra by starting from a retrieved scaffold and using spectrum-guided attention to complete the molecule (MADGEN's Markov bridge generation with classifier-free spectral guidance). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2501.01950
skills.summary: Generate de novo molecular structures from MS/MS spectra by starting from a retrieved scaffold and using spectrum-guided attention to complete the molecule (MADGEN's Markov bridge generation with classifier-free spectral guidance).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You do not have a scaffold (predicted or oracle) and cannot run scaffold retrieval first — the generator is scaffold-conditioned and requires a starting scaffold. Your spectra are not MS/MS tandem spectra preprocessed with intensity normalization and low-intensity peak removal; MADGEN was built for NIST23, CANOPUS, and MassSpecGym-style MS/MS data. NIST23 data is needed but not separately licensed — the NIST dataset is commercially available and cannot be pulled from the public Zenodo records.

skills.description: Use when building a spectra-conditioned de novo molecule generator whose output must contain a fixed Murcko scaffold subgraph, e.g. training on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym-style pickles of canonical SMILES and normalized MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: scaffold-conditioned-markov-bridge-training
skills.search_text: scaffold-conditioned-markov-bridge-training Use when building a spectra-conditioned de novo molecule generator whose output must contain a fixed Murcko scaffold subgraph, e.g. training on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym-style pickles of canonical SMILES and normalized MS/MS spectra. When the task is retrieving or ranking scaffolds from spectra rather than generating molecules — that is the separate scaffold_retrieval contrastive-learning stage (cand_rank_msg.py, cand_rank_canopus.py). When the target molecule is already known and only spectrum-to-structure lookup is needed; MADGEN's oracle retriever plus generation is for de novo generation, not annotation lookup. When no scaffold constraint is desired (unconstrained de novo generation); the whole rationale is that constraining the generation search space via the scaffold reduces complexity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3418 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains MADGEN's second-stage generator, an absorbing-state Markov bridge model that turns a Murcko scaffold graph plus an MS/MS spectrum into the target molecule, using endpoint-prediction ELBO loss and classifier-free guidance from the spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2501.01950
skills.summary: Trains MADGEN's second-stage generator, an absorbing-state Markov bridge model that turns a Murcko scaffold graph plus an MS/MS spectrum into the target molecule, using endpoint-prediction ELBO loss and classifier-free guidance from the spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is retrieving or ranking scaffolds from spectra rather than generating molecules — that is the separate scaffold_retrieval contrastive-learning stage (cand_rank_msg.py, cand_rank_canopus.py). When the target molecule is already known and only spectrum-to-structure lookup is needed; MADGEN's oracle retriever plus generation is for de novo generation, not annotation lookup. When no scaffold constraint is desired (unconstrained de novo generation); the whole rationale is that constraining the generation search space via the scaffold reduces complexity.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a mass-spectrometry scaffold retriever (e.g., contrastive-ranking models on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym pkl datasets) and you need a per-dataset accuracy for how often the true core scaffold is retrieved from ranked candidates.
skills.name: scaffold-prediction-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: scaffold-prediction-accuracy-evaluation Use when evaluating a mass-spectrometry scaffold retriever (e.g., contrastive-ranking models on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym pkl datasets) and you need a per-dataset accuracy for how often the true core scaffold is retrieved from ranked candidates. The goal is end-to-end generation accuracy (Top-1/Tanimoto/MCES) rather than the retrieval stage — use generation-evaluation workflows instead Only an oracle scaffold lookup table is used (correct scaffold always provided), so retrieval accuracy is not the measured quantity Spectra are not preprocessed (intensities not normalized, low-intensity peaks not removed), which the retriever rankings assume http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes Scaffold Prediction Accuracy (SPA) of MADGEN's first-stage contrastive scaffold retriever on MS/MS datasets, using frequency-based aggregation of top-k ranked candidate scaffolds and RDKit-extracted ground-truth scaffolds. It quantifies how well the retriever stage constrains the subsequent de novo generation stage. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2501.01950
skills.summary: Computes Scaffold Prediction Accuracy (SPA) of MADGEN's first-stage contrastive scaffold retriever on MS/MS datasets, using frequency-based aggregation of top-k ranked candidate scaffolds and RDKit-extracted ground-truth scaffolds. It quantifies how well the retriever stage constrains the subsequent de novo generation stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is end-to-end generation accuracy (Top-1/Tanimoto/MCES) rather than the retrieval stage — use generation-evaluation workflows instead Only an oracle scaffold lookup table is used (correct scaffold always provided), so retrieval accuracy is not the measured quantity Spectra are not preprocessed (intensities not normalized, low-intensity peaks not removed), which the retriever rankings assume

skills.description: Use when you have a target molecular weight (up to five decimal digits) from a mass spectrum of an unknown natural-product mixture and a scaffold database with sidechain probabilities, and need ranked candidate structures.
skills.name: scaffold-sidechain-combinatorial-search
skills.search_text: scaffold-sidechain-combinatorial-search Use when you have a target molecular weight (up to five decimal digits) from a mass spectrum of an unknown natural-product mixture and a scaffold database with sidechain probabilities, and need ranked candidate structures. Mass precision beyond five decimal digits is required, or hardware lacks a CUDA-capable GPU for the idp kernel The query is a single pure compound rather than an unknown mixture whose constituents must be combinatorially assembled from scaffolds plus side chains http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Solves the chemical substituent core combinatorial problem (CSCCP) by extending seed scaffold files (*.cIdx) with probabilistic side chains to match a high-resolution target mass, using the GPU-accelerated dynamic programming solver (G.A.M.E., idp kernel) to rank top candidate structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-017-0238-7
skills.summary: Solves the chemical substituent core combinatorial problem (CSCCP) by extending seed scaffold files (*.cIdx) with probabilistic side chains to match a high-resolution target mass, using the GPU-accelerated dynamic programming solver (G.A.M.E., idp kernel) to rank top candidate structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mass precision beyond five decimal digits is required, or hardware lacks a CUDA-capable GPU for the idp kernel The query is a single pure compound rather than an unknown mixture whose constituents must be combinatorially assembled from scaffolds plus side chains

skills.description: Use when running MetaRon's 'ago' mode after IDBA assembly of paired-end shotgun reads, to discard scaftigs ≤ 500 bp prior to prodigal/MetaGeneMark gene prediction and proximon/operon identification.
skills.name: scaftig-length-filtering
skills.search_text: scaftig-length-filtering Use when running MetaRon's 'ago' mode after IDBA assembly of paired-end shotgun reads, to discard scaftigs ≤ 500 bp prior to prodigal/MetaGeneMark gene prediction and proximon/operon identification. Input consists of pre-assembled metagenomic scaftigs and gene predictions supplied directly to MetaRon's 'op' process that have already been length-filtered upstream The analysis is whole-genome operon prediction on a complete reference genome (e.g. E. coli MG1655 NC_000913.3), where no de novo scaftig assembly occurs Scaftigs must be preserved regardless of length for a separate purpose (e.g. short-contig binning), since this filter permanently discards contigs ≤ 500 bp http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 A quality-control filter step in the MetaRon metagenomic operon pipeline that discards de novo assembled scaftigs of length ≤ 500 bp before gene and operon prediction, keeping only sufficiently long contigs to support reliable gene calls. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12864-020-07357-5
skills.summary: A quality-control filter step in the MetaRon metagenomic operon pipeline that discards de novo assembled scaftigs of length ≤ 500 bp before gene and operon prediction, keeping only sufficiently long contigs to support reliable gene calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of pre-assembled metagenomic scaftigs and gene predictions supplied directly to MetaRon's 'op' process that have already been length-filtered upstream The analysis is whole-genome operon prediction on a complete reference genome (e.g. E. coli MG1655 NC_000913.3), where no de novo scaftig assembly occurs Scaftigs must be preserved regardless of length for a separate purpose (e.g. short-contig binning), since this filter permanently discards contigs ≤ 500 bp

skills.description: Use when metabolomics intensities show run-order signal drift plus occasional extreme high/low outliers that would corrupt QC-sample-based normalization, or when pooled QC samples may be unrepresentative of biological samples.
skills.name: scaled-t-likelihood-outlier-accommodation
skills.search_text: scaled-t-likelihood-outlier-accommodation Use when metabolomics intensities show run-order signal drift plus occasional extreme high/low outliers that would corrupt QC-sample-based normalization, or when pooled QC samples may be unrepresentative of biological samples. Runtime-constrained high-throughput normalization where rGAM or rLOESS are explicitly noted as faster alternatives to the recommended-but-heavier tGAM Data with no injection-order structure or expected signal drift (e.g. already normalized or randomized-acquisition data), where fitting an order GAM adds no correction Analyses aiming to treat outliers multivariate or detect them in a dedicated preprocessing pipeline — the article notes the current treatment is feature-level and automated outlier detection prior to normalization is nontrivial and not provided http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 The tGAM normalization approach from the Metanorm R package: per-compound generalized additive models of metabolite intensity on injection order, fitted with a scaled-t error distribution via mgcv so occasional disproportionately high or low intensity outliers are downweighted by the heavy-tailed likelihood rather than distorting the drift estimate. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06841
skills.summary: The tGAM normalization approach from the Metanorm R package: per-compound generalized additive models of metabolite intensity on injection order, fitted with a scaled-t error distribution via mgcv so occasional disproportionately high or low intensity outliers are downweighted by the heavy-tailed likelihood rather than distorting the drift estimate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Runtime-constrained high-throughput normalization where rGAM or rLOESS are explicitly noted as faster alternatives to the recommended-but-heavier tGAM Data with no injection-order structure or expected signal drift (e.g. already normalized or randomized-acquisition data), where fitting an order GAM adds no correction Analyses aiming to treat outliers multivariate or detect them in a dedicated preprocessing pipeline — the article notes the current treatment is feature-level and automated outlier detection prior to normalization is nontrivial and not provided

skills.description: Use when fitting a multivariate discriminant model (e.g., KODAMA-based PLS-DA) on a lipidomic intensity matrix at the lipid molecular species (LMS) level and a scaling scheme among Autoscaling, Pareto, or None must be chosen before validation.
skills.name: scaling-method-selection-multivariate-data
skills.search_text: scaling-method-selection-multivariate-data Use when fitting a multivariate discriminant model (e.g., KODAMA-based PLS-DA) on a lipidomic intensity matrix at the lipid molecular species (LMS) level and a scaling scheme among Autoscaling, Pareto, or None must be chosen before validation. skills.search_text: scatter-plot-confidence-interval-estimation Use when you have paired chromatographic datasets with a per-pair agreement score (e.g. CCRS) and a continuous per-pair difference attribute (ΔpH, ΔF, Δtemperature), and you need to test and visualize whether that attribute explains replicability. The grouping variable is categorical (organic-phase modifier, polarity, column type) rather than a continuous difference — a grouped violin plot of CCRS (Fig. 4d-f style) is the appropriate comparison, not a Pearson correlation. This is how the ROASMI paper established that eluent pH is the main driver of retention order replicability. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8

When the only available article content describes repository-contribution mechanics (opening issues, pull requests) rather than a scientific analysis — these are excluded as non-scientific setup per the source card.

skills.description: Use when a research question about feature co-association (e.g., CLR scoring of MI networks to discount promiscuous features) must be formulated as a bounded, computable procedure with defined inputs, tools, and outputs before implementation.
skills.name: scientific-task-formulation
skills.search_text: scientific-task-formulation Use when a research question about feature co-association (e.g., CLR scoring of MI networks to discount promiscuous features) must be formulated as a bounded, computable procedure with defined inputs, tools, and outputs before implementation. The analysis goal is simple pairwise similarity (e.g., Spearman/Pearson co-expression cutoffs such as Spearman ≥ 0.60) that MOG already supports natively without CLR normalization. No bounded computable operation can be specified — as the source card found for the article section itself: no CLR computation, MI background-distribution procedure, or output table is described — and no external CLR reference (e.g., Daub et al.) is available. The dataset lacks enough samples to estimate MI background distributions reliably for each feature. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts a research question about feature co-association — here, MetaOmGraph's context likelihood of relatedness (CLR) scoring on mutual-information (MI) values — into a bounded, computable operation specifying inputs, tool steps, parameters, and an output table. It exists because the article's text alone did not yield a bounded CLR computation, so the method must be reconstructed from the MI/CLR description and external references. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209

skills.description: Use when SCMS metabolomics data (e.g., Single-probe profiles of melanoma cell pairs) are too limited for conventional deep learning and the goal is few-shot primary/metastatic cell phenotype classification via meta-learning.
skills.name: scms-cell-phenotype-meta-learning-training
skills.search_text: scms-cell-phenotype-meta-learning-training Use when SCMS metabolomics data (e.g., Single-probe profiles of melanoma cell pairs) are too limited for conventional deep learning and the goal is few-shot primary/metastatic cell phenotype classification via meta-learning. The input is already bulk omics data or cell populations rather than single-cell SCMS profiles — bulk analysis cannot evaluate cell heterogeneity, which is the motivation for this skill. A large SCMS training dataset is available and standard supervised deep learning or transfer learning would not suffer from overfitting. The goal is unsupervised exploratory separation of metabolomic profiles (e.g., PCA on MetaboAnalyst 6.0) rather than supervised phenotype classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains the MAML-based MetaPhenotype model with a 1D-CNN backbone (LeNet) on limited single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics data (1/5/10-shot tasks) to classify cell phenotypes such as primary vs metastatic melanoma, achieving >90% accuracy with few new training samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Trains the MAML-based MetaPhenotype model with a 1D-CNN backbone (LeNet) on limited single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics data (1/5/10-shot tasks) to classify cell phenotypes such as primary vs metastatic melanoma, achieving >90% accuracy with few new training samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already bulk omics data or cell populations rather than single-cell SCMS profiles — bulk analysis cannot evaluate cell heterogeneity, which is the motivation for this skill. A large SCMS training dataset is available and standard supervised deep learning or transfer learning would not suffer from overfitting. The goal is unsupervised exploratory separation of metabolomic profiles (e.g., PCA on MetaboAnalyst 6.0) rather than supervised phenotype classification.

skills.description: Use when raw single-probe SCMS spectra from cell experiments must be converted into a cleaned, normalized, aligned feature table (e.g., dataset.csv with cells × metabolite species) before machine learning classification or meta-learning.
skills.name: scms-feature-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: scms-feature-matrix-construction Use when raw single-probe SCMS spectra from cell experiments must be converted into a cleaned, normalized, aligned feature table (e.g., dataset.csv with cells × metabolite species) before machine learning classification or meta-learning. Input is already a pretreated, peak-aligned feature table (e.g., an existing dataset.csv) — rerunning pretreatment would double-normalize or drop valid species. The goal is bulk metabolomics feature construction; conventional bulk analysis cannot evaluate cell heterogeneity, so single-cell-specific pretreatment is the wrong frame. Samples come from an ambient SCMS protocol with different acquisition parameters; the 10 ppm Geena2 tolerance and established protocol were validated for this Single-probe setup. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Builds the pretreated, peak-aligned single-cell mass spectrometry feature matrix (dataset.csv) that serves as the training input for MetaPhenotype and baseline classifiers, using the established SCMS pretreatment protocol on Single-probe-derived spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Builds the pretreated, peak-aligned single-cell mass spectrometry feature matrix (dataset.csv) that serves as the training input for MetaPhenotype and baseline classifiers, using the established SCMS pretreatment protocol on Single-probe-derived spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pretreated, peak-aligned feature table (e.g., an existing dataset.csv) — rerunning pretreatment would double-normalize or drop valid species. The goal is bulk metabolomics feature construction; conventional bulk analysis cannot evaluate cell heterogeneity, so single-cell-specific pretreatment is the wrong frame. Samples come from an ambient SCMS protocol with different acquisition parameters; the 10 ppm Geena2 tolerance and established protocol were validated for this Single-probe setup.

skills.description: Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized SCMS lipid/metabolomics feature table must be screened for species differing between two cell phenotypes (e.g., primary vs metastatic) under control and drug-treated conditions to nominate biomarker candidates.
skills.name: scms-lipidomics-fold-change-analysis
skills.search_text: scms-lipidomics-fold-change-analysis Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized SCMS lipid/metabolomics feature table must be screened for species differing between two cell phenotypes (e.g., primary vs metastatic) under control and drug-treated conditions to nominate biomarker candidates. The input is raw, unprocessed single-cell spectra rather than a pretreated feature table — the established pretreatment protocol (Geena2 alignment at 10 ppm, TIC normalization) must run first. The goal is phenotype classification rather than differential abundance screening — use the MetaPhenotype meta-learning classifier, since PCA cannot effectively discriminate closely similar phenotypes such as IGR39/IGR37. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Volcano-plot differential abundance analysis of Single-probe SCMS metabolomics feature tables to prioritize lipid biomarker candidates between primary and metastatic melanoma cells, applying fold change ≥ 2.0 and FDR-adjusted p ≤ 0.05 thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Volcano-plot differential abundance analysis of Single-probe SCMS metabolomics feature tables to prioritize lipid biomarker candidates between primary and metastatic melanoma cells, applying fold change ≥ 2.0 and FDR-adjusted p ≤ 0.05 thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unprocessed single-cell spectra rather than a pretreated feature table — the established pretreatment protocol (Geena2 alignment at 10 ppm, TIC normalization) must run first. The goal is phenotype classification rather than differential abundance screening — use the MetaPhenotype meta-learning classifier, since PCA cannot effectively discriminate closely similar phenotypes such as IGR39/IGR37.

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell peak lists exported from Thermo Xcalibur must be denoised, debackgrounded, and TIC-normalized before peak alignment or PCA/machine-learning analysis of SCMS data.
skills.name: scms-noise-background-subtraction
skills.search_text: scms-noise-background-subtraction Use when raw single-cell peak lists exported from Thermo Xcalibur must be denoised, debackgrounded, and TIC-normalized before peak alignment or PCA/machine-learning analysis of SCMS data. Input is already a pretreated, aligned peak-intensity matrix (e.g. the dataset.csv used by MetaPhenotype) — reapplying subtraction would remove valid signals. Data are bulk metabolomics measurements rather than single-probe SCMS single-cell peak lists; the 3×10^3 relative-intensity noise cutoff is calibrated for single-cell spectra. Goal is peak alignment itself (Geena2, 10 ppm, 150–1500 m/z) rather than upstream noise/background removal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Pretreat raw Single-probe SCMS peak lists by removing low-intensity noise species (relative intensity < 3×10^3), subtracting background species with an in-house R script, and TIC-normalizing each cell's intensities before downstream phenotype-classification modeling. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Pretreat raw Single-probe SCMS peak lists by removing low-intensity noise species (relative intensity < 3×10^3), subtracting background species with an in-house R script, and TIC-normalizing each cell's intensities before downstream phenotype-classification modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pretreated, aligned peak-intensity matrix (e.g. the dataset.csv used by MetaPhenotype) — reapplying subtraction would remove valid signals. Data are bulk metabolomics measurements rather than single-probe SCMS single-cell peak lists; the 3×10^3 relative-intensity noise cutoff is calibrated for single-cell spectra. Goal is peak alignment itself (Geena2, 10 ppm, 150–1500 m/z) rather than upstream noise/background removal.

skills.description: Use when you have a trained meta-learning classifier (MetaPhenotype) on pretreated SCMS feature tables and need to select the small number of m/z species critical for phenotype classification, e.g. to overlay as bold dots on volcano plots.
skills.name: scms-peak-ablation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: scms-peak-ablation-significance-testing Use when you have a trained meta-learning classifier (MetaPhenotype) on pretreated SCMS feature tables and need to select the small number of m/z species critical for phenotype classification, e.g. to overlay as bold dots on volcano plots. You only need unsupervised exploration of metabolomic differences — the article notes PCA cannot effectively discriminate highly similar cells like IGR39/IGR37, but peak ablation requires a trained supervised classifier and labeled evaluation data. Input is raw, unaligned SCMS spectra — ablation must be run on the pretreated, TIC-normalized, Geena2-aligned peak table, not on exported raw peaks. You have no trained MetaPhenotype checkpoint for the target condition — significance is defined relative to that specific adapted model's classification accuracy, not a generic feature-importance metric. Identifies m/z species essential for cell-phenotype discrimination in single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) data by iteratively removing one peak at a time and flagging peaks whose removal drops MetaPhenotype classification accuracy by ≥1%. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02038
skills.summary: Identifies m/z species essential for cell-phenotype discrimination in single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) data by iteratively removing one peak at a time and flagging peaks whose removal drops MetaPhenotype classification accuracy by ≥1%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need unsupervised exploration of metabolomic differences — the article notes PCA cannot effectively discriminate highly similar cells like IGR39/IGR37, but peak ablation requires a trained supervised classifier and labeled evaluation data. Input is raw, unaligned SCMS spectra — ablation must be run on the pretreated, TIC-normalized, Geena2-aligned peak table, not on exported raw peaks. You have no trained MetaPhenotype checkpoint for the target condition — significance is defined relative to that specific adapted model's classification accuracy, not a generic feature-importance metric.

skills.search_text: score-distribution-visualization Use when validating PSMs from proteomic SIP database search outputs (e.g., Sipros searches of .FT2 spectra) by comparing experimental and theoretical isotope envelopes, or when selecting a scoring function for partially 13C-labeled PSMs. When the goal is isotope fine-structure simulation alone — Aerith's FFT-based envelope method does not account for isotopic fine structure, which requires Monte Carlo simulation or high-resolution (HRMS) data instead When converting Thermo RAW files before scoring — use Raxport or ThermoRawFileParser rather than this skill When peptides lack user-defined amino acid sequences or user-defined isotopic abundances are not needed for the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Score and visualize peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) in Aerith using MVH, Xcorr, weighted dot product (WDP), and spectral entropy similarity functions, and plot score distributions across 13C enrichment levels (0–100%) to identify which scoring function best separates true from false SIP-labeled matches. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Score and visualize peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) in Aerith using MVH, Xcorr, weighted dot product (WDP), and spectral entropy similarity functions, and plot score distributions across 13C enrichment levels (0–100%) to identify which scoring function best separates true from false SIP-labeled matches.

skills.description: Use when an MPCA model has been fitted with m_prcomp on preprocessed two-dimensional chromatogram data and the score matrix or principal-component loading values must be exported as numeric CSVs rather than viewed as plots.
skills.name: scores-and-loadings-matrix-extraction
skills.search_text: scores-and-loadings-matrix-extraction Use when an MPCA model has been fitted with m_prcomp on preprocessed two-dimensional chromatogram data and the score matrix or principal-component loading values must be exported as numeric CSVs rather than viewed as plots. The goal is to inspect loadings visually only — plot_loading with type = 'n' or 'p' already renders negative/positive loading values without exporting numerics. The chromatograms have not been preprocessed (smoothing, baseline correction via baseline_corr, and 2D-COW alignment) — MPCA on raw noisy 2D-TIC data will not yield meaningful scores/loadings. A supervised model is needed instead of unsupervised MPCA — unfold_chrom exports chromatograms for mixOmics supervised models, which is a different analysis path. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Extract the numerical results of a multiway principal component analysis (MPCA) fitted on GCxGC-MS 2D-TIC chromatograms with RGCxGC: retrieve the score matrix via scores() and export PC loadings underlying plot_loading renderings, as demonstrated on the bundled MTBLS579 dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2020.104830
skills.summary: Extract the numerical results of a multiway principal component analysis (MPCA) fitted on GCxGC-MS 2D-TIC chromatograms with RGCxGC: retrieve the score matrix via scores() and export PC loadings underlying plot_loading renderings, as demonstrated on the bundled MTBLS579 dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to inspect loadings visually only — plot_loading with type = 'n' or 'p' already renders negative/positive loading values without exporting numerics. skills.description: Use when a candidate list retrieved from PubChem/ChemSpider must be ranked with reference and patent information, i.e. when S_C_PCR and S_C_CCR scoring terms must be computed, max-normalized, and exported as a TSV for MetFrag scoring.
skills.name: scoring-term-table-export
skills.search_text: scoring-term-table-export Use when a candidate list retrieved from PubChem/ChemSpider must be ranked with reference and patent information, i.e. when S_C_PCR and S_C_CCR scoring terms must be computed, max-normalized, and exported as a TSV for MetFrag scoring. The candidate list comes from a user-supplied SDF or a local database with no patent/PubMed or ChemSpider reference counts retrievable via web services — the terms cannot be computed. The analysis goal is purely fragment-based ranking from HR-MS/MS peak matching (MetFrag in silico fragmentation alone) with no reference/retention information included. Only a single candidate is under evaluation — max-normalization over the candidate list is undefined/trivial and the terms lose their comparative meaning. Computes MetFrag2.2's combined reference scoring terms for each candidate structure — the PubChem patent/PubMed score S_C_PCR and the ChemSpider five-count score S_C_CCR — normalizes both across the candidate list, and writes per-candidate scores plus contributing counts to a tab-separated results table. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: Computes MetFrag2.2's combined reference scoring terms for each candidate structure — the PubChem patent/PubMed score S_C_PCR and the ChemSpider five-count score S_C_CCR — normalizes both across the candidate list, and writes per-candidate scores plus contributing counts to a tab-separated results table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate list comes from a user-supplied SDF or a local database with no patent/PubMed or ChemSpider reference counts retrievable via web services — the terms cannot be computed. The analysis goal is purely fragment-based ranking from HR-MS/MS peak matching (MetFrag in silico fragmentation alone) with no reference/retention information included. skills.description: Use when tuning metabCombiner's similarity-scoring weights (A for m/z, B for mapped retention time, C for abundance) before finalizing the combined feature table, using a training table of identified compounds shared between two datasets.
skills.name: scoring-weight-parameter-optimization
skills.search_text: scoring-weight-parameter-optimization Use when tuning metabCombiner's similarity-scoring weights (A for m/z, B for mapped retention time, C for abundance) before finalizing the combined feature table, using a training table of identified compounds shared between two datasets. Input is already an integrated peak/feature table — this skill operates on raw ROI intensity-vs-RT traces before feature detection and integration Analytical peaks are broad LC-MS-style profiles rather than the narrow peaks typical of CE-MS, where the Mexican hat CWT is best suited The goal is downstream chemometrics (scaling, transformation, augmentation) rather than per-ROI peak detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Automatic peak detection within chromatographic/electrophoretic region-of-interest traces by taking the second derivative of the smoothed signal and locating peak centers with continuous wavelet transform (CWT) using the Mexican hat mother wavelet, then integrating apex RT, area, and height. Suited to the narrow peaks typical of CE-MS separations, as implemented in the AriumMSEval evaluation app of the AriumMS toolbox. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Automatic peak detection within chromatographic/electrophoretic region-of-interest traces by taking the second derivative of the smoothed signal and locating peak centers with continuous wavelet transform (CWT) using the Mexican hat mother wavelet, then integrating apex RT, area, and height. Suited to the narrow peaks typical of CE-MS separations, as implemented in the AriumMSEval evaluation app of the AriumMS toolbox.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an integrated peak/feature table — this skill operates on raw ROI intensity-vs-RT traces before feature detection and integration Analytical peaks are broad LC-MS-style profiles rather than the narrow peaks typical of CE-MS, where the Mexican hat CWT is best suited The goal is downstream chemometrics (scaling, transformation, augmentation) rather than per-ROI peak detection

skills.name: secondary-metabolite-novelty-assessment
skills.search_text: secondary-metabolite-novelty-assessment Use when a BiG-SLiCE output database (SQLite3) of clustered GCFs is available and you must rank GCFs/taxa by novelty, or when a new antiSMASH BGC must be placed against precomputed GCF models to judge novelty. When the dataset is small enough that pairwise comparison tools like BiG-SCAPE can run in reasonable time — the Euclidean-space GCF pipeline is aimed at the massive datasets (~1.2M BGCs) where pairwise methods are infeasible When no BiG-SLiCE clustering run (and its SQLite3 output) exists for the BGCs of interest — the skill operates on precomputed GCF centroid features, not raw genomes When the goal is functional annotation of a BGC already matching a known MIBiG family closely — novelty assessment adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies how far predicted BGCs or BiG-SLiCE gene cluster family (GCF) models lie from experimentally verified reference BGCs (MIBiG v2.0), flagging 'uncharted biosynthetic potential' in a dataset or taxon. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa154
skills.summary: Quantifies how far predicted BGCs or BiG-SLiCE gene cluster family (GCF) models lie from experimentally verified reference BGCs (MIBiG v2.0), flagging 'uncharted biosynthetic potential' in a dataset or taxon.

skills.description: Use when smoothing MRM ion chromatograms that contain dynamic dwell time and varying signal/noise levels, where a fixed-size smoothing window would either leave noise in low-signal sections or clip true peaks in high-signal sections.
skills.name: section-adaptive-signal-smoothing
skills.search_text: section-adaptive-signal-smoothing Use when smoothing MRM ion chromatograms that contain dynamic dwell time and varying signal/noise levels, where a fixed-size smoothing window would either leave noise in low-signal sections or clip true peaks in high-signal sections. Input is not raw MRM ion chromatogram signal but already a peak table or quantitation result — smoothing is not meaningful there. The chromatogram has uniform dwell time and homogeneous noise so a fixed-window smoother suffices and the section-adaptive background rule adds no value. You are quantitating coeluted or saturated peaks — MRMQuant's separate deconvolution and regression steps handle those cases, not the smoothing step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Partitions an MRM ion chromatogram into sections, estimates each section's background as its 30th-percentile intensity, and adapts the smoothing window so each section starts and ends at a signal not higher than 1.2 times its estimated background — the dynamic smoothing step used by MRMQuant before peak detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Partitions an MRM ion chromatogram into sections, estimates each section's background as its 30th-percentile intensity, and adapts the smoothing window so each section starts and ends at a signal not higher than 1.2 times its estimated background — the dynamic smoothing step used by MRMQuant before peak detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw MRM ion chromatogram signal but already a peak table or quantitation result — smoothing is not meaningful there. The chromatogram has uniform dwell time and homogeneous noise so a fixed-window smoother suffices and the section-adaptive background rule adds no value. You are quantitating coeluted or saturated peaks — MRMQuant's separate deconvolution and regression steps handle those cases, not the smoothing step.

The input is raw mass spectrometry data or unfragmented spectra — in silico annotation with MetFrag and graph construction must happen first Spectral library matches cover more than 10% of network nodes, violating the seed sparsity constraint the method was designed under You need to propagate annotations only to first neighbors of spectral matches — NAP already does this without a random walk http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Selects seed nodes for ChemWalker's random-walk annotation propagation by marking spectral library match nodes within each molecular network component, with the constraint that seeds constitute at most 10% of all nodes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad078
skills.summary: Selects seed nodes for ChemWalker's random-walk annotation propagation by marking spectral library match nodes within each molecular network component, with the constraint that seeds constitute at most 10% of all nodes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw mass spectrometry data or unfragmented spectra — in silico annotation with MetFrag and graph construction must happen first Spectral library matches cover more than 10% of network nodes, violating the seed sparsity constraint the method was designed under You need to propagate annotations only to first neighbors of spectral matches — NAP already does this without a random walk

skills.description: Use when a chemical inventory needs risk-based prioritization by combining modeled external exposure (SEEM/EHE) with LD50-based probabilistic toxicity, as in ranking the >20,000-chemical human exposome database.
skills.name: seem-exposure-data-integration
skills.search_text: seem-exposure-data-integration Use when a chemical inventory needs risk-based prioritization by combining modeled external exposure (SEEM/EHE) with LD50-based probabilistic toxicity, as in ranking the >20,000-chemical human exposome database. Chemicals not covered by the SEEM database — the study notes 'the SEEM database was unable to cover all the compounds summarized in the present study', so no EHE means no PrHQ Assessment of chronic or subchronic toxicity risk — the LD50-based approach may underestimate risk for chronic/subchronic endpoints Chemicals lacking a CASRN, since the HTS pipeline built on the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard only retrieved data for chemicals with CASRN Integrates SEEM (Systematic Empirical Evaluation of Models) external exposure estimates with LD50-derived probabilistic reference doses (HDMI, computed from TEST-predicted oral rat LD50 values and uncertainty factors in Equations (1)–(3)) to compute a probabilistic hazard quotient (PrHQ = EHE/HDMI) for risk-based ranking of human exposome chemicals. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Integrates SEEM (Systematic Empirical Evaluation of Models) external exposure estimates with LD50-derived probabilistic reference doses (HDMI, computed from TEST-predicted oral rat LD50 values and uncertainty factors in Equations (1)–(3)) to compute a probabilistic hazard quotient (PrHQ = EHE/HDMI) for risk-based ranking of human exposome chemicals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Chemicals not covered by the SEEM database — the study notes 'the SEEM database was unable to cover all the compounds summarized in the present study', so no EHE means no PrHQ Assessment of chronic or subchronic toxicity risk — the LD50-based approach may underestimate risk for chronic/subchronic endpoints Chemicals lacking a CASRN, since the HTS pipeline built on the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard only retrieved data for chemicals with CASRN

skills.description: Use when a compiled chemical list (e.g. CASRN-annotated exposome substances) needs predicted population exposure/intake rates to support risk-based ranking or coverage assessment against a consensus exposure model.
skills.name: seem-exposure-model-prediction
skills.search_text: seem-exposure-model-prediction Use when a compiled chemical list (e.g. CASRN-annotated exposome substances) needs predicted population exposure/intake rates to support risk-based ranking or coverage assessment against a consensus exposure model. Chemicals lacking a CASRN — the Dashboard-based HTS retrieval only succeeds for chemicals with CASRN The goal is measured internal exposure or biomarker concentrations rather than model-predicted external intake rates A compound-level exposure estimate is required for every substance — the SEEM database was unable to cover all compounds in the study http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Applies the SEEM (Systematic Empirical Evaluation of Models) consensus exposure model (Ring et al. 2019, R2 ≈ 0.8) to assign predicted median intake rates (mg/kg BW per day) with 95% confidence intervals to human exposome chemicals, enabling exposure-based prioritization in HExpMetDB. metabolomics/v3 10.1289/ehp7722
skills.summary: Applies the SEEM (Systematic Empirical Evaluation of Models) consensus exposure model (Ring et al. 2019, R2 ≈ 0.8) to assign predicted median intake rates (mg/kg BW per day) with 95% confidence intervals to human exposome chemicals, enabling exposure-based prioritization in HExpMetDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Chemicals lacking a CASRN — the Dashboard-based HTS retrieval only succeeds for chemicals with CASRN The goal is measured internal exposure or biomarker concentrations rather than model-predicted external intake rates A compound-level exposure estimate is required for every substance — the SEEM database was unable to cover all compounds in the study

skills.search_text: segment-count-selection-and-evaluation Use when a peak-picked MSI dataset (e.g., imzML loaded as a processed MSImagingExperiment) must be partitioned into chemically homogeneous tissue segments and the number of segments must be selected by scanning regularization rather than fixed a priori. When class labels are already known and the task is image classification (assigning pixels to pre-defined classes with cross-validated error) rather than unsupervised segmentation When input is raw, non-peak-picked spectra — Cardinal's low-level processing (normalize, smooth, reduceBaseline, peakPick/peakAlign) must be run first via the queued process() workflow When a fixed, externally imposed segment count is required without regularization-based selection, since this skill's segment count emerges from scanning the regularization parameter http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects and evaluates the number of tissue segments in mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) segmentation by applying Cardinal's spatialShrunkenCentroids() with a Spatially-Aware (method='gaussian') distance and scanning the regularization parameter until the solution matching a reference segmentation (e.g., 11 segments for the peak-picked pig fetus dataset) is found. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv146

skills.name: segmentation-and-colocalisation-feature-comparison
skills.search_text: segmentation-and-colocalisation-feature-comparison Use when you must decide which LA-ICP-MS imaging software to adopt for vendor-native import, or when you need to segment element images and quantify Mn/Zn-type spatial colocalisation. Your data is already a calibrated feature/colocalisation table and only needs visualisation, not import or segmentation. You need native import of a vendor format other than Agilent, Perkin Elmer, Thermo, or Nu Instruments and cannot convert to delimited text first — the article notes most open-source alternatives require preformatted data. The element of interest is absent from most of the sample, breaking the marker-element peak integration requirement for spot-wise data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds a feature-by-software capability matrix for LA-ICP-MS imaging programs and then applies Pew2's built-in segmentation (k-means, mean/Otsu thresholding) and RGB colocalisation (Pearson/Li-ICQ) to element images such as 55Mn, 56Fe and 66Zn. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Builds a feature-by-software capability matrix for LA-ICP-MS imaging programs and then applies Pew2's built-in segmentation (k-means, mean/Otsu thresholding) and RGB colocalisation (Pearson/Li-ICQ) to element images such as 55Mn, 56Fe and 66Zn.

skills.search_text: self-attention-over-variable-length-peak-sequences Use when MS/MS peak lists {P_k = (M_k, I_k)} must be encoded as one token per peak for downstream cross-attention conditioning of a scaffold-conditioned molecular graph generator, rather than pooled into a fixed-length spectrum vector. When the downstream model requires a single fixed-length spectrum embedding (e.g. contrastive scaffold retrieval alignment) rather than per-peak tokens queried individually by graph nodes and edges When spectra have not been preprocessed — intensities not normalized and low-intensity peaks not removed below the predefined threshold — since the tokenization assumes MADGEN's noise-reduced peak sets When the target generator conditions via concatenation or FiLM rather than cross-attention over individual peak tokens http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Tokenizes an MS/MS spectrum into per-peak embeddings — separate MLP encoders for m/z (M_k) and intensity (I_k) concatenated per peak (Eq. 8) — then applies multi-head self-attention over the variable-length peak sequence to produce the spectrum token set H_X used by MADGEN's cross-attention-conditioned graph generator. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2501.01950

skills.search_text: self-supervised-ion-image-representation-learning Use when raw preprocessed MSI matrices (shape [X*Y, P], e. Input is raw, unpreprocessed mass-spectrometry imaging data rather than a preprocessed [X*Y, P] intensity matrix with a matching peak list — the model expects pixel-summed ion intensities, not vendor spectra or imaging files. The goal is general image classification or supervised annotation rather than self-supervised ion-image representation: DeepION requires no manual annotation, and its contrastive objective is not designed to learn labeled class boundaries. skills.search_text: selfies-candidate-sequence-generation Use when training the alignment stage of MS-BART: after fingerprint->molecule finetuning (Pretrain-FT), you need a pool of sampled SELFIES candidates per fingerprint input to score preferences against the ground-truth structure. No fine-tuned fingerprint->molecule checkpoint exists yet — candidates sampled from the raw pretrained model will not reflect experimental-spectrum adaptation; run the Pretrain-FT stage first No ground-truth structure or fingerprint prediction is available (e.g., purely de novo generation without MIST fingerprint conditioning) — preference scoring Ps(Si) requires a reference structure to compute Tanimoto similarity Input spectra contain [M+Na]+ adducts or collision-energy/adduct variability that was not thresholded and filtered as in finetuning — candidate quality will degrade on out-of-distribution conditioning tokens http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Generate n candidate molecular structures as SELFIES sequences from a fingerprint-conditioned seq2seq model (MS-BART on a BART-Base backbone), producing a candidate pool with sequence log-probabilities that feeds chemical-feedback alignment via Tanimoto/formula-distance preference scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615

skills.name: selfies-token-masking-denoising
skills.search_text: selfies-token-masking-denoising Use when pretraining a seq2seq molecular model on unlabeled SELFIES corpora and you need a denoising objective, or when reconstructing/reproducing MS-BART-style multi-task pretraining from fingerprint–molecule pairs. Finetuning or inference on experimental mass spectra — that stage conditions on MIST-predicted fingerprints (with [M+Na]+ adducts filtered out) rather than applying token masking You need actual structure elucidation from spectra — this objective only teaches SELFIES token grammar on unlabeled molecules and produces no spectra-to-structure capability by itself Your corpus is already label-rich with spectra–structure pairs; supervised translation/finetuning objectives are then more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 A self-supervised pretraining objective for molecular language models: randomly mask 30% of tokens in SELFIES sequences and train the model to recover the originals. It is one of three multi-task objectives (alongside fingerprint-to-molecule translation and hybrid denoising) used to pretrain MS-Bart on a corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615

skills.when_to_use_negative: Finetuning or inference on experimental mass spectra — that stage conditions on MIST-predicted fingerprints (with [M+Na]+ adducts filtered out) rather than applying token masking You need actual structure elucidation from spectra — this objective only teaches SELFIES token grammar on unlabeled molecules and produces no spectra-to-structure capability by itself Your corpus is already label-rich with spectra–structure pairs; supervised translation/finetuning objectives are then more appropriate

skills.description: Use when adapting a pretrained fingerprint-to-molecule model to noisy experimental spectra (e.g. MassSpecGym or NPLIB1/CANOPUS splits) without simulated spectra, using predicted fingerprints as input.
skills.name: selfies-tokenized-cross-entropy-finetuning
skills.search_text: selfies-tokenized-cross-entropy-finetuning Use when adapting a pretrained fingerprint-to-molecule model to noisy experimental spectra (e.g. MassSpecGym or NPLIB1/CANOPUS splits) without simulated spectra, using predicted fingerprints as input. The task is pretraining on unlabeled fingerprint–molecule pairs rather than transfer to experimental spectra — use the multi-task pretraining objectives (SELFIES denoising, fingerprint-to-molecule translation, hybrid denoising) instead. Data are simulated spectra under diverse conditions — the skill exists specifically to avoid requiring simulated spectra. The dataset contains mostly non-[M+H]+ adducts that must be retained for training — this pipeline filters to [M+H]+ in the training split. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Finetunes the MS-Bart BART-Base model (185-token SELFIES vocabulary) on experimental mass spectra by feeding MIST-predicted 4096-bit fingerprints binarized into <fp{i:04d}> tokens, using cross-entropy loss between target and predicted SELFIES tokens. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.20615
skills.summary: Finetunes the MS-Bart BART-Base model (185-token SELFIES vocabulary) on experimental mass spectra by feeding MIST-predicted 4096-bit fingerprints binarized into <fp{i:04d}> tokens, using cross-entropy loss between target and predicted SELFIES tokens.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is pretraining on unlabeled fingerprint–molecule pairs rather than transfer to experimental spectra — use the multi-task pretraining objectives (SELFIES denoising, fingerprint-to-molecule translation, hybrid denoising) instead. skills.description: Use when cross-validated per-metabolite SCCs are available (e.g., from 10 iterations of 10-fold CV with MiMeNet) and you need a statistically grounded count of well-predicted metabolites rather than a fixed correlation threshold.
skills.name: shuffled-background-thresholding
skills.search_text: shuffled-background-thresholding Use when cross-validated per-metabolite SCCs are available (e.g., from 10 iterations of 10-fold CV with MiMeNet) and you need a statistically grounded count of well-predicted metabolites rather than a fixed correlation threshold. You need metabolite-level significance for a single model's associations (e.g., microbe-metabolite correlation testing) rather than counting predictably well-modeled metabolites across CV folds. The metabolite set is so small or SCC distributions are so degenerate that a 95th-percentile empirical background is unstable (e.g., few-fold CV with very few metabolites). You are comparing methods using mean SCC alone (the article reports both mean SCC and well-predicted counts separately); the background threshold is only needed for the count metric. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Defines 'well-predicted' metabolites by comparing each metabolite's cross-validated Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC) against an empirical background of SCCs from shuffled samples, flagging metabolites whose SCC exceeds the 95th percentile of that background. This avoids arbitrary correlation cutoffs when counting how many metabolites the MiMeNet model predicts well. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009021
skills.summary: Defines 'well-predicted' metabolites by comparing each metabolite's cross-validated Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC) against an empirical background of SCCs from shuffled samples, flagging metabolites whose SCC exceeds the 95th percentile of that background.
