skills.search_text: significant-enriched-pathway-quantification Use when running ORA perturbation simulations (background-set reduction, metabolite misidentification, DA-list changes) and you need a robust metric of how many enriched pathways are gained or lost across datasets. You need a statistically calibrated significance call for a single analysis — p <= 0.1 without multiple-testing correction is only for sensitivity comparison, not reporting final enrichment results You need ground-truth-validated pathway enrichment — the authors note no dataset exists where the identities of enriched pathways are known, so SEP counts measure sensitivity, not accuracy The input is an unprocessed abundance matrix — DA metabolites must first be derived via two-tailed t-tests with BH FDR q <= 0.05 before SEP counting http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies significantly enriched pathways (SEPs) from over-representation analysis by counting pathways passing p <= 0.1 (without multiple testing correction) after each perturbation, expressed as a retained proportion relative to the unperturbed run, with mean and standard error over 100 randomised repetitions. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Quantifies significantly enriched pathways (SEPs) from over-representation analysis by counting pathways passing p <= 0.1 (without multiple testing correction) after each perturbation, expressed as a retained proportion relative to the unperturbed run, with mean and standard error over 100 randomised repetitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a statistically calibrated significance call for a single analysis — p <= 0.1 without multiple-testing correction is only for sensitivity comparison, not reporting final enrichment results You need ground-truth-validated pathway enrichment — the authors note no dataset exists where the identities of enriched pathways are known, so SEP counts measure sensitivity, not accuracy The input is an unprocessed abundance matrix — DA metabolites must first be derived via two-tailed t-tests with BH FDR q <= 0.05 before SEP counting

skills.description: Use when running right-tailed Fisher's exact ORA (scipy.stats.fisher_exact) on multiple candidate metabolite-of-interest lists or correction/alpha settings and you need to tabulate SEP counts to show how those choices affect enrichment outcomes.
skills.name: significant-pathway-count-tabulation
skills.search_text: significant-pathway-count-tabulation Use when running right-tailed Fisher's exact ORA (scipy.stats.fisher_exact) on multiple candidate metabolite-of-interest lists or correction/alpha settings and you need to tabulate SEP counts to show how those choices affect enrichment outcomes. When a single DA-metabolite list and single correction/alpha setting is analysed and no sensitivity comparison is needed — the tabulation is only meaningful across multiple candidate parameterisations. When ORA output is already a final list of significantly enriched pathways with BH FDR-adjusted q-values and you only need to report that list, not compare counts across settings. When pathway p-values have not been computed (e.g. input is a raw feature-abundance matrix that has not yet gone through imputation, log2 transformation, auto-scaling, t-testing, and Fisher's exact ORA). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Tabulate counts of significantly enriched pathways (SEPs) across candidate DA-metabolite lists, correction methods, and alpha thresholds for ORA sensitivity analysis. This skill quantifies how parameter choices — the metabolite-of-interest list, BH FDR vs Bonferroni adjustment, and the p <= 0.1 SEP cutoff — drive the number of detected pathways, and is implemented in the reproducible_simulations.ipynb notebook of the metabolomics-ORA repository. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009105
skills.summary: Tabulate counts of significantly enriched pathways (SEPs) across candidate DA-metabolite lists, correction methods, and alpha thresholds for ORA sensitivity analysis. This skill quantifies how parameter choices — the metabolite-of-interest list, BH FDR vs Bonferroni adjustment, and the p <= 0.1 SEP cutoff — drive the number of detected pathways, and is implemented in the reproducible_simulations.ipynb notebook of the metabolomics-ORA repository.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single DA-metabolite list and single correction/alpha setting is analysed and no sensitivity comparison is needed — the tabulation is only meaningful across multiple candidate parameterisations. When ORA output is already a final list of significantly enriched pathways with BH FDR-adjusted q-values and you only need to report that list, not compare counts across settings. When pathway p-values have not been computed (e.g. input is a raw feature-abundance matrix that has not yet gone through imputation, log2 transformation, auto-scaling, t-testing, and Fisher's exact ORA).

skills.description: Use when a table of statistically significant features (e.g. MB-VIP permutation p-value < 0.01) must be partitioned into correlation-based clusters and the cluster count k is unknown and must be chosen objectively.
skills.name: silhouette-based-optimal-cluster-count-selection
skills.search_text: silhouette-based-optimal-cluster-count-selection Use when a table of statistically significant features (e.g. MB-VIP permutation p-value < 0.01) must be partitioned into correlation-based clusters and the cluster count k is unknown and must be chosen objectively. Features are already grouped by structural properties (RT windows, isotopologue/adduct signatures) via MamsiStructSearch.get_structural_clusters — correlation clustering is a complementary, not replacement, grouping. The dataset contains fewer informative features or samples than needed to support up to 11 candidate cluster counts; silhouette scores over too few samples will be unstable. The goal is a fixed, predefined number of clusters (k known a priori) rather than objective selection of k. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Selects the number of clusters for hierarchical clustering of significant LC-MS features by flattening a complete-linkage dendrogram with the mean silhouette criterion, as implemented in MAMSI's MamsiStructSearch.get_correlation_clusters. Features are grouped by |1−r_ij| correlation-based dissimilarity rather than m/z/RT alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01327
skills.summary: Selects the number of clusters for hierarchical clustering of significant LC-MS features by flattening a complete-linkage dendrogram with the mean silhouette criterion, as implemented in MAMSI's MamsiStructSearch.get_correlation_clusters. Features are grouped by |1−r_ij| correlation-based dissimilarity rather than m/z/RT alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are already grouped by structural properties (RT windows, isotopologue/adduct signatures) via MamsiStructSearch.get_structural_clusters — correlation clustering is a complementary, not replacement, grouping. The dataset contains fewer informative features or samples than needed to support up to 11 candidate cluster counts; silhouette scores over too few samples will be unstable. skills.description: Use when a pairwise spectral similarity/distance matrix exists (e.g. from MS2DeepScore or MS2/MS similarity) and you must choose how many k-medoids clusters to group LC-MS/MS features into, with no prior label or target K.
skills.name: silhouette-cluster-validation
skills.search_text: silhouette-cluster-validation Use when a pairwise spectral similarity/distance matrix exists (e.g. from MS2DeepScore or MS2/MS similarity) and you must choose how many k-medoids clusters to group LC-MS/MS features into, with no prior label or target K. When a prior label or number of feature groups is already fixed by the experimental design — the grid sweep over K and Silhouette comparison is unnecessary. When the input is already a feature-cluster assignment table rather than a distance matrix; Silhouette scoring requires the underlying pairwise spectral distances. When data are feature-set testing targets rather than an ungrouped feature set — msFeaST downstream globaltest applies to the resulting clusters, not to raw features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Selects the number of clusters K for k-medoids feature grouping by sweeping a grid of candidate K values over a precomputed spectral (dis)similarity distance matrix and scoring each partition with Silhouette scores, as done in the msFeaST LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics workflow. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae584
skills.summary: Selects the number of clusters K for k-medoids feature grouping by sweeping a grid of candidate K values over a precomputed spectral (dis)similarity distance matrix and scoring each partition with Silhouette scores, as done in the msFeaST LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a prior label or number of feature groups is already fixed by the experimental design — the grid sweep over K and Silhouette comparison is unnecessary. When the input is already a feature-cluster assignment table rather than a distance matrix; Silhouette scoring requires the underlying pairwise spectral distances. When data are feature-set testing targets rather than an ungrouped feature set — msFeaST downstream globaltest applies to the resulting clusters, not to raw features.

skills.description: Use when selecting unsupervised segmentation parameters (e.g., t-SNE perplexity, learning rate, iteration count) or comparing search strategies, and an internal cluster-quality metric is needed to rank k-means segmentations of MSI pixel data.
skills.name: silhouette-score-cluster-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-score-cluster-evaluation Use when selecting unsupervised segmentation parameters (e.g., t-SNE perplexity, learning rate, iteration count) or comparing search strategies, and an internal cluster-quality metric is needed to rank k-means segmentations of MSI pixel data. The goal is peptide identification confirmation or histology co-registration rather than segmentation quality tuning — MSIght's core integration workflow (LC-MS/MS confirmation, H&E registration) does not require Silhouette scoring. Ground-truth spatial annotations are available, making supervised segmentation metrics more appropriate than the unsupervised Silhouette score. The clustering labels already exist and only need visualization; the skill's value is in scoring candidate segmentations, not rendering final images. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates MSI segmentation clusterings by computing Silhouette scores for each parameter combination, using the score to compare hyperparameter search strategies (exhaustive grid, random, Bayesian) for tuning t-SNE embeddings of imzML mass spectrometry imaging data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Evaluates MSI segmentation clusterings by computing Silhouette scores for each parameter combination, using the score to compare hyperparameter search strategies (exhaustive grid, random, Bayesian) for tuning t-SNE embeddings of imzML mass spectrometry imaging data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peptide identification confirmation or histology co-registration rather than segmentation quality tuning — MSIght's core integration workflow (LC-MS/MS confirmation, H&E registration) does not require Silhouette scoring. Ground-truth spatial annotations are available, making supervised segmentation metrics more appropriate than the unsupervised Silhouette score. The clustering labels already exist and only need visualization; the skill's value is in scoring candidate segmentations, not rendering final images.

skills.description: Use when an unannotated empirical tandem MS spectrum must be matched against candidate molecules whose predicted spectra are available, and ranking accuracy (Top-1/Top-5/Top-10) or annotation confidence is the goal.
skills.name: silico-spectral-library-matching
skills.search_text: silico-spectral-library-matching Use when an unannotated empirical tandem MS spectrum must be matched against candidate molecules whose predicted spectra are available, and ranking accuracy (Top-1/Top-5/Top-10) or annotation confidence is the goal. The query spectrum already has a confident empirical library match — curated empirical libraries like NIST MS/MS outperform in silico matching when coverage exists No precursor mass information is available to filter candidates, since candidate-list assembly relies on 1 ppm / 10 ppm precursor mass accuracy tolerances The molecule class falls outside the ANN model's trained domain (e.g., needs 3D structure; CFM-ID or 3DMolMS may be alternatives) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotate unannotated empirical MS/MS spectra by ranking candidate molecules with cosine similarity between the experimental spectrum and SingleFrag's in silico predicted spectra from a ~1.9M-molecule library. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Annotate unannotated empirical MS/MS spectra by ranking candidate molecules with cosine similarity between the experimental spectrum and SingleFrag's in silico predicted spectra from a ~1.9M-molecule library.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query spectrum already has a confident empirical library match — curated empirical libraries like NIST MS/MS outperform in silico matching when coverage exists No precursor mass information is available to filter candidates, since candidate-list assembly relies on 1 ppm / 10 ppm precursor mass accuracy tolerances The molecule class falls outside the ANN model's trained domain (e.g., needs 3D structure; CFM-ID or 3DMolMS may be alternatives)

skills.description: Use when an Ag-sputtered AgLDI mass spectrometry imaging peak matrix contains unassigned low-m/z peaks that must be classified as matrix-related (Ag clusters/adducts) versus endogenous signals via isotopic-pattern matching.
skills.name: silver-isotope-pattern-matching
skills.search_text: silver-isotope-pattern-matching Use when an Ag-sputtered AgLDI mass spectrometry imaging peak matrix contains unassigned low-m/z peaks that must be classified as matrix-related (Ag clusters/adducts) versus endogenous signals via isotopic-pattern matching. The dataset was not acquired with a silver-sputtered nanolayer (e.g. conventional organic MALDI matrix such as CHCA or DHB), since the algorithm relies on the specific isotopic pattern of the LDI-promoting material Only a peak matrix is available without the processed full spectral data (.tar), as annotate_matrix requires both pks and full rMSI data Peaks appear in fewer than 5% of pixels or below SNR 5 — such low-quality peaks are filtered out during rMSIproc pre-processing and should not be fed to isotope-pattern matching http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute theoretical isotope fine-structure patterns for silver clusters (Ag_n+) and silver-adduct species with enviPat, then match them against experimental AgLDI MSI peak matrices using rMSIcleanup's annotate_matrix to obtain per-peak similarity scores (spectral S1 and intra-cluster morphological S2) for matrix-related peak annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-020-00449-0
skills.summary: Compute theoretical isotope fine-structure patterns for silver clusters (Ag_n+) and silver-adduct species with enviPat, then match them against experimental AgLDI MSI peak matrices using rMSIcleanup's annotate_matrix to obtain per-peak similarity scores (spectral S1 and intra-cluster morphological S2) for matrix-related peak annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset was not acquired with a silver-sputtered nanolayer (e.g. conventional organic MALDI matrix such as CHCA or DHB), since the algorithm relies on the specific isotopic pattern of the LDI-promoting material Only a peak matrix is available without the processed full spectral data (.tar), as annotate_matrix requires both pks and full rMSI data Peaks appear in fewer than 5% of pixels or below SNR 5 — such low-quality peaks are filtered out during rMSIproc pre-processing and should not be fed to isotope-pattern matching

skills.description: Use when you need to validate or contextualize isotope-pair identifications in MSI by comparing them against PCC and R2 SIM-based baselines from METASPACE and the rMSI package, including cases where baselines fail.
skills.name: sim-based-isotope-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: sim-based-isotope-baseline-comparison Use when you need to validate or contextualize isotope-pair identifications in MSI by comparing them against PCC and R2 SIM-based baselines from METASPACE and the rMSI package, including cases where baselines fail. The task is colocalized-ion identification from different molecules (DeepION COL mode), not isotope ions from the same molecule — the SIM baselines here target isotope discovery specifically. The MSI data have not been preprocessed into the [X*Y,P] matrix and [P,1] peak-list format required by the pipeline. You need generic spectral-similarity scoring outside isotope-pair validation; PCC/R2 here are used only as METASPACE/rMSI-style isotope-identification baselines. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks monoisotope–isotope pair identifications from a learned representation method (DeepION ISO mode) against the similarity-matrix (SIM) baselines PCC and R2, which are the isotope-identification approaches used in METASPACE and the rMSI package, on rat brain tissue MSI data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Benchmarks monoisotope–isotope pair identifications from a learned representation method (DeepION ISO mode) against the similarity-matrix (SIM) baselines PCC and R2, which are the isotope-identification approaches used in METASPACE and the rMSI package, on rat brain tissue MSI data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is colocalized-ion identification from different molecules (DeepION COL mode), not isotope ions from the same molecule — the SIM baselines here target isotope discovery specifically. The MSI data have not been preprocessed into the [X*Y,P] matrix and [P,1] peak-list format required by the pipeline. You need generic spectral-similarity scoring outside isotope-pair validation; PCC/R2 here are used only as METASPACE/rMSI-style isotope-identification baselines.

skills.description: Use when processing direct infusion mass spectrometry (DIMS) FT-ICR data stored as .dat transient files organized in SIM windows (e.g. MTBLS79 DIMS_DATA) and you need a calibrated, stitched peak list across samples.
skills.name: sim-stitch-direct-infusion-peak-picking
skills.search_text: sim-stitch-direct-infusion-peak-picking Use when processing direct infusion mass spectrometry (DIMS) FT-ICR data stored as .dat transient files organized in SIM windows (e.g. MTBLS79 DIMS_DATA) and you need a calibrated, stitched peak list across samples. The input is LC-MS data — use the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe route (feature detection, retention time correction and alignment) instead of SIM-stitching The data are already peak-picked and aligned (a feature/peak table) — start at Replicate Filtering, Blank Filtering and Sample Filtering The .dat transient files are unavailable — they are not included in the MetaboLights MTBLS79 accession and must be obtained from the original authors http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 DIMS peak-picking pipeline (SimStitch tools in Galaxy-M) that converts averaged FT-ICR transients per SIM window into a single calibrated, stitched peak list per sample, providing increased metabolome coverage and very high mass accuracy at ~2 min 15 s analysis time per sample. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: DIMS peak-picking pipeline (SimStitch tools in Galaxy-M) that converts averaged FT-ICR transients per SIM window into a single calibrated, stitched peak list per sample, providing increased metabolome coverage and very high mass accuracy at ~2 min 15 s analysis time per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is LC-MS data — use the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe route (feature detection, retention time correction and alignment) instead of SIM-stitching The data are already peak-picked and aligned (a feature/peak table) — start at Replicate Filtering, Blank Filtering and Sample Filtering The .dat transient files are unavailable — they are not included in the MetaboLights MTBLS79 accession and must be obtained from the original authors

skills.description: Use when processing FT-ICR direct infusion MS transients stored as Thermo .RAW/.dat files that have already been summed and apodized per SIM window, and the next step is calibrated m/z peak lists across all windows.
skills.name: sim-window-mass-calibration-and-stitching
skills.search_text: sim-window-mass-calibration-and-stitching Use when processing FT-ICR direct infusion MS transients stored as Thermo .RAW/.dat files that have already been summed and apodized per SIM window, and the next step is calibrated m/z peak lists across all windows. The input is LC-MS data (use the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe feature detection / alignment path instead, not SIM-stitching). The FT-ICR transients have not yet been summed and processed (apodization / Fourier transform / baseline correction) — run Sum Transients and Process Transients first. You only need raw frequency-domain spectra or have not set up WINE with WINEARCH=win32 and MSFileReader; the tools cannot open Thermo data without that environment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 In the Galaxy-M DIMS pipeline, Mass Calibration and SIM-stitching converts each FT-ICR SIM window's frequency-domain spectra to m/z measurements, peak picks with an SNR threshold, and stitches all SIM windows into a single peak list. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13742-016-0115-8
skills.summary: In the Galaxy-M DIMS pipeline, Mass Calibration and SIM-stitching converts each FT-ICR SIM window's frequency-domain spectra to m/z measurements, peak picks with an SNR threshold, and stitches all SIM windows into a single peak list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is LC-MS data (use the XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe feature detection / alignment path instead, not SIM-stitching). The FT-ICR transients have not yet been summed and processed (apodization / Fourier transform / baseline correction) — run Sum Transients and Process Transients first. You only need raw frequency-domain spectra or have not set up WINE with WINEARCH=win32 and MSFileReader; the tools cannot open Thermo data without that environment.

skills.description: Use when compressing ordered, near-uniformly spaced numeric arrays (e.g. m/z values from MS spectra in mzML/vendor-converted data) where controllable precision (e.g. 3 dp for 10 ppm, 5 dp for 0.1 ppm) is acceptable and both size and decode speed matter.
skills.name: simd-accelerated-integer-compression
skills.search_text: simd-accelerated-integer-compression Use when compressing ordered, near-uniformly spaced numeric arrays (e.g. m/z values from MS spectra in mzML/vendor-converted data) where controllable precision (e.g. 3 dp for 10 ppm, 5 dp for 0.1 ppm) is acceptable and both size and decode speed matter. The data are intensity arrays or other slowly varying values where the small-delta integer assumption does not hold — Aird applies distinct compressors (e.g. Log10 Compressor) to intensity data Lossless m/z values are required with no quantization — ZDPD depends on converting the floating-point m/z array to an integer array after determining the required precision Random access with flexible indexing is the primary goal rather than compression ratio — a general-purpose format like mzML converted with MSConvert may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reproduces Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD) compressor: quantize a sorted floating-point m/z array to integers at a chosen decimal precision, delta-code adjacent integers, compress with the SIMD-accelerated FastPfor library, then wrap the output in Zlib to achieve ~55% smaller m/z data and ~3x faster decoding than Zlib alone. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-021-04490-0
skills.summary: Reproduces Aird's Zlib-Diff-PforDelta (ZDPD) compressor: quantize a sorted floating-point m/z array to integers at a chosen decimal precision, delta-code adjacent integers, compress with the SIMD-accelerated FastPfor library, then wrap the output in Zlib to achieve ~55% smaller m/z data and ~3x faster decoding than Zlib alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are intensity arrays or other slowly varying values where the small-delta integer assumption does not hold — Aird applies distinct compressors (e.g. Log10 Compressor) to intensity data Lossless m/z values are required with no quantization — ZDPD depends on converting the floating-point m/z array to an integer array after determining the required precision Random access with flexible indexing is the primary goal rather than compression ratio — a general-purpose format like mzML converted with MSConvert may be more appropriate

skills.summary: Classifies MSI m/z peaks as matrix-related (e.g., Agn+ silver clusters) vs. endogenous by thresholding per-cluster similarity scores: spectral similarity S1 and intra-cluster morphology similarity S2 computed by rMSIcleanup against theoretical isotope patterns.

skills.description: Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC-based predictor must be compared against fingerprints of candidate structures from chemical databases such as PubChem to produce ranked, thresholded annotation results.
skills.name: similarity-threshold-annotation-classification
skills.search_text: similarity-threshold-annotation-classification Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC-based predictor must be compared against fingerprints of candidate structures from chemical databases such as PubChem to produce ranked, thresholded annotation results. The query is a raw 1H/13C chemical shift list to be searched against a spectral reference library by ppm matching (use the baseline shift-search workflow with 0.5 ppm carbon / 0.05 ppm proton thresholds instead) Ground-truth fingerprints are unavailable or candidate structures cannot be converted to Morgan fingerprints (cosine similarity is undefined in that case) The goal is compound class (scaffold) prediction accuracy rather than per-structure annotation — DeepSAT's multi-task model already outputs class predictions separately http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Ranks candidate molecular structures by cosine similarity between DeepSAT-predicted Morgan fingerprints and fingerprints generated from known small molecules, then labels candidates as identical (cosine score 1.0) or similar (cosine score over 0.8). This thresholding step converts fingerprint predictions into concrete structure annotation results. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Ranks candidate molecular structures by cosine similarity between DeepSAT-predicted Morgan fingerprints and fingerprints generated from known small molecules, then labels candidates as identical (cosine score 1.0) or similar (cosine score over 0.8). This thresholding step converts fingerprint predictions into concrete structure annotation results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is a raw 1H/13C chemical shift list to be searched against a spectral reference library by ppm matching (use the baseline shift-search workflow with 0.5 ppm carbon / 0.05 ppm proton thresholds instead) Ground-truth fingerprints are unavailable or candidate structures cannot be converted to Morgan fingerprints (cosine similarity is undefined in that case) The goal is compound class (scaffold) prediction accuracy rather than per-structure annotation — DeepSAT's multi-task model already outputs class predictions separately

skills.description: Use when you need low-dimensional, annotation-free representations of ion images from an MSI matrix for downstream colocalized-ion or isotope-ion identification tasks.
skills.name: simsiam-based-self-supervised-pipeline-integration
skills.search_text: simsiam-based-self-supervised-pipeline-integration Use when you need low-dimensional, annotation-free representations of ion images from an MSI matrix for downstream colocalized-ion or isotope-ion identification tasks. Data are raw, unpreprocessed MSI spectra rather than a preprocessed [X*Y, P] matrix and a [P,1] peak list — the pipeline expects preprocessed matrix/peak inputs. Labels or annotated pairs are already available and a supervised model is preferred — DeepION is designed for self-supervised representation without manual annotation. The task is general image representation outside MSI, where MSI-specific augmentation (Poisson noise, random/intensity-dependent missing value) is not appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Builds a SimSiam-style self-supervised contrastive pipeline for ion-image representation learning in mass spectrometry imaging, using paired augmentations of the same ion image and a stop-gradient loss to produce 512-dimensional representation vectors without manual annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Builds a SimSiam-style self-supervised contrastive pipeline for ion-image representation learning in mass spectrometry imaging, using paired augmentations of the same ion image and a stop-gradient loss to produce 512-dimensional representation vectors without manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw, unpreprocessed MSI spectra rather than a preprocessed [X*Y, P] matrix and a [P,1] peak list — the pipeline expects preprocessed matrix/peak inputs. Labels or annotated pairs are already available and a supervised model is preferred — DeepION is designed for self-supervised representation without manual annotation. The task is general image representation outside MSI, where MSI-specific augmentation (Poisson noise, random/intensity-dependent missing value) is not appropriate.

skills.description: Use when training a self-supervised encoder on ion images from mass spectrometry imaging, where two augmented views of each ion image must be mapped to representation vectors and collapse must be prevented via a stop-gradient contrastive loss.
skills.name: simsiam-contrastive-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: simsiam-contrastive-loss-implementation Use when training a self-supervised encoder on ion images from mass spectrometry imaging, where two augmented views of each ion image must be mapped to representation vectors and collapse must be prevented via a stop-gradient contrastive loss. When the downstream task needs only the final 20-dimensional dense vectors for similarity measurement — the dimensionality reduction module (UMAP), not the SimSiam loss itself, is the right stage. When augmentations for the two views come from different ion images rather than two augmented views of a same image; the contrastive loss assumes a positive pair from one image. When the goal is supervised ion classification with manual annotations — DeepION is explicitly designed to generate representations self-supervised without manual annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implement the SimSiam-style stop-gradient contrastive loss used in DeepION to train ResNet18-based twin encoders that produce 512-dimensional ion image representations without manual annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Implement the SimSiam-style stop-gradient contrastive loss used in DeepION to train ResNet18-based twin encoders that produce 512-dimensional ion image representations without manual annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the downstream task needs only the final 20-dimensional dense vectors for similarity measurement — the dimensionality reduction module (UMAP), not the SimSiam loss itself, is the right stage. When augmentations for the two views come from different ion images rather than two augmented views of a same image; the contrastive loss assumes a positive pair from one image. When the goal is supervised ion classification with manual annotations — DeepION is explicitly designed to generate representations self-supervised without manual annotation.

skills.description: Use when you need an annotation-free accuracy estimate of a feature-matching method: simulate two LC–MS feature tables with known true pairs, run matching, and score match correctness, retention (e.g. 2682/2728), and precision (99.6%).
skills.name: simulated-data-validation
skills.search_text: simulated-data-validation Use when you need an annotation-free accuracy estimate of a feature-matching method: simulate two LC–MS feature tables with known true pairs, run matching, and score match correctness, retention (e.g. 2682/2728), and precision (99.6%). The task is annotation-based validation on real biological datasets where manual or database annotations (confidence level 2 per Metabolomics Standards Initiative) already provide ground truth — simulated data adds little. Feature tables lack FI (intensity) values or the m/z/RT structure needed to embed realistic shift trends. The goal is annotation-coverage assessment (e.g. how many features can be annotated to LIPID MAPS, METLIN, HMDB, GNPS, or MassBank) rather than matching-accuracy estimation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates synthetic paired LC–MS feature lists (4755 features per dataset) whose true correspondences are known, to quantify matching accuracy (99.6% correct) of M2S without relying on metabolite annotations. It also validates published-match-count ratios such as 2682/2717 = 98.71% after Step 3 poor-match filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c03592
skills.summary: Generates synthetic paired LC–MS feature lists (4755 features per dataset) whose true correspondences are known, to quantify matching accuracy (99.6% correct) of M2S without relying on metabolite annotations. It also validates published-match-count ratios such as 2682/2717 = 98.71% after Step 3 poor-match filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is annotation-based validation on real biological datasets where manual or database annotations (confidence level 2 per Metabolomics Standards Initiative) already provide ground truth — simulated data adds little. Feature tables lack FI (intensity) values or the m/z/RT structure needed to embed realistic shift trends. The goal is annotation-coverage assessment (e.g. how many features can be annotated to LIPID MAPS, METLIN, HMDB, GNPS, or MassBank) rather than matching-accuracy estimation.

skills.search_text: simulated-isotopologue-fam-generation Use when benchmarking isotopic-enrichment correction methods (MDT, ULS, NRE/IsoCor, FAM-only) against a known ground-truth enrichment, requiring simulated labeled and unlabeled FAM inputs at a specified nominal resolution (e.g., 140,000). skills.name: simulated-metabolomics-data-generation
skills.search_text: simulated-metabolomics-data-generation Use when benchmarking or validating imputation algorithms on metabolomics data and ground-truth values are needed to compute RMSE/MLCI, or when a controlled MNAR+LOD/MAR missingness setting must be reproduced. The input is real experimental metabolomics data where true missing values are unknown and RMSE against ground truth cannot be computed The target data are strongly non-normal, since the downstream KNN-TN likelihood relies on a normality assumption for the truncated mean and SD The goal is to study the full missing-data likelihood including the (unknown) missingness mechanism, which the truncated-observation likelihood does not model http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Generates synthetic metabolomics matrices from a multivariate normal distribution with controlled correlation structures and controlled missingness (MNAR below an LOD plus MAR), so that imputation methods such as KNN-TN, KNN-CR, and KNN-EU can be benchmarked against known true values. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-017-1547-6

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires realistic paired-end shotgun reads from known reference genomes so pipeline outputs (e.g., operons) can be scored against curated per-genome truth annotations.
skills.name: simulated-metagenome-read-generation
skills.search_text: simulated-metagenome-read-generation Use when a benchmark requires realistic paired-end shotgun reads from known reference genomes so pipeline outputs (e.g., operons) can be scored against curated per-genome truth annotations. Real metagenomic samples are the input and the goal is biological discovery rather than controlled benchmarking against known truth The target genomes lack curated operon annotations (e.g., DOOR), so simulated reads cannot be scored against ground truth Pre-assembled scaffolds and gene predictions are already available, in which case MetaRon's 'op' mode operates directly on scaftigs and gene predictions without simulated reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generate in silico shotgun metagenome reads from reference genomes using NeSSM so that operon prediction pipelines like MetaRon can be benchmarked against curated ground-truth annotations (e.g., DOOR). In the source work, two million Illumina reads at 15X depth were simulated from a three-genome mixture of E. coli MG1655, M. tuberculosis H37Rv and B. subtilis 168. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12864-020-07357-5
skills.summary: Generate in silico shotgun metagenome reads from reference genomes using NeSSM so that operon prediction pipelines like MetaRon can be benchmarked against curated ground-truth annotations (e.g., DOOR). skills.when_to_use_negative: Real metagenomic samples are the input and the goal is biological discovery rather than controlled benchmarking against known truth The target genomes lack curated operon annotations (e.g., DOOR), so simulated reads cannot be scored against ground truth Pre-assembled scaffolds and gene predictions are already available, in which case MetaRon's 'op' mode operates directly on scaftigs and gene predictions without simulated reads

skills.search_text: simulation-runtime-benchmarking Use when you must quantify how fast SMITER can synthesize a proteome-scale synthetic mzML (tens of thousands of peptides, thousands of MS2 scans) or verify that a simulated run meets a runtime and scan-count budget. The goal is to analyze or re-process an already-acquired real mzML file — SMITER only writes synthetic mzML from chemical formulas, it does not parse experimental runs. skills.search_text: single-cell-feature-prevalence-filtering Use when a single-cell SCMS peak matrix (e.g. imzML-derived peak lists of thousands of cells) contains sparse or noise-only m/z features, and you need prevalence-based pruning before clustering or cross-annotation. Downstream analysis requires all detected features regardless of sparsity (e.g. metabolite coverage audits) since filtering discards genuine but rare signals. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 A sparsity-based QC filter for single-cell mass-spectrometry peak matrices: discard m/z features observed in <5% of cells and remove cells carrying fewer than 5% of retained features, applied after cross-annotation against tissue MSI lipid features. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: A sparsity-based QC filter for single-cell mass-spectrometry peak matrices: discard m/z features observed in <5% of cells and remove cells carrying fewer than 5% of retained features, applied after cross-annotation against tissue MSI lipid features.

skills.search_text: single-field-ccs-calibration Use when you have single-field RapidFire-DTIMS-MS (or similar DTIMS) feature files plus IMS frame-metadata from many runs and need calibrated per-run CCS values, e.g. tracking CCS variance of a compound like protonated rotenone across thousands of SPE-IMS-MS plant-extract runs. skills.search_text: single-field-dtims-arrival-time-calibration Use when calibrating single-field DTIMS arrival/drift times to CCS via external calibrants (Agilent tune-mix with known CCS values), especially when calibrant and sample runs differ in pressure/temperature. Stepped-field DTIMS data — use AutoCCS's stepped-field method (--threshold_n_fields 5, --mode multi) instead, which determines CCS directly without a calibration curve Traveling wave-based IMS (TWIMS/SLIM) data — these require polynomial or linearized power calibration functions rather than the single-field linear (degree 1) function Feature tables without an accompanying calibrant CCS reference file (e.g., TuneMix-CCS.txt), since external calibration depends on known calibrant CCS values Builds a linear arrival-time-to-CCS calibration curve for single-field DTIMS-MS using known calibrant ions (e.g., Agilent tune-mix), correcting the measured drift time for charge and reduced mass and applying a pressure/temperature (P/T) adjustment before least-squares fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: Builds a linear arrival-time-to-CCS calibration curve for single-field DTIMS-MS using known calibrant ions (e.g., Agilent tune-mix), correcting the measured drift time for charge and reduced mass and applying a pressure/temperature (P/T) adjustment before least-squares fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Stepped-field DTIMS data — use AutoCCS's stepped-field method (--threshold_n_fields 5, --mode multi) instead, which determines CCS directly without a calibration curve Traveling wave-based IMS (TWIMS/SLIM) data — these require polynomial or linearized power calibration functions rather than the single-field linear (degree 1) function Feature tables without an accompanying calibrant CCS reference file (e.g., TuneMix-CCS.txt), since external calibration depends on known calibrant CCS values

skills.description: Use when molecular-level omics matrices need a common, interpretable scale for supervised integration — e.g. before fitting MB-PLS or a sklearn classifier on multi-omics COPDgene or COVID-19 data — to exploit coordinated pathway-level signals in low signal-to-noise scenarios.
skills.name: single-sample-pathway-analysis-scoring
skills.search_text: single-sample-pathway-analysis-scoring Use when molecular-level omics matrices need a common, interpretable scale for supervised integration — e.g. before fitting MB-PLS or a sklearn classifier on multi-omics COPDgene or COVID-19 data — to exploit coordinated pathway-level signals in low signal-to-noise scenarios. Input is already a pathway-level score matrix — re-scoring would be redundant; the skill applies to molecular-level abundance data PathIntegrate requires all input omics to be measured on the same individuals — samples with missing entire omics rows must be excluded before scoring, as the tool does not support rows of missing data Molecules lacking valid ChEBI/UniProt/ENSEMBL annotations cannot be included in pathway scoring, so un-annotated molecule lists cause information loss rather than pathway scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Transforms an N-by-M molecular abundance matrix (metabolites, proteins, or transcripts with ChEBI/UniProt/ENSEMBL or KEGG IDs) into an N-by-P pathway activity-score matrix using kPCA or SVD/PLAGE scoring from the sspa Python package, the pathway-transformation step that underpins PathIntegrate Single-View and Multi-View models. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011814
skills.summary: Transforms an N-by-M molecular abundance matrix (metabolites, proteins, or transcripts with ChEBI/UniProt/ENSEMBL or KEGG IDs) into an N-by-P pathway activity-score matrix using kPCA or SVD/PLAGE scoring from the sspa Python package, the pathway-transformation step that underpins PathIntegrate Single-View and Multi-View models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway-level score matrix — re-scoring would be redundant; the skill applies to molecular-level abundance data PathIntegrate requires all input omics to be measured on the same individuals — samples with missing entire omics rows must be excluded before scoring, as the tool does not support rows of missing data Molecules lacking valid ChEBI/UniProt/ENSEMBL annotations cannot be included in pathway scoring, so un-annotated molecule lists cause information loss rather than pathway scores

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g. BioHEART-CT targeted metabolomics) contains embedded intra-batch and inter-batch replicates and you need a baseline batch-correction with RUV-III, or to benchmark against hierarchical normalisation.
skills.name: single-step-ruv-batch-correction
skills.search_text: single-step-ruv-batch-correction Use when a multi-batch metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g. BioHEART-CT targeted metabolomics) contains embedded intra-batch and inter-batch replicates and you need a baseline batch-correction with RUV-III, or to benchmark against hierarchical normalisation. When the goal is the paper's improved batch correction itself — hRUV hierarchically merges adjustments of neighbouring batches and achieves lower replicate SD than single-step RUV (Fig. 3b) When data contain missing values that cannot be imputed — the algorithm expects complete data, which is often not possible in large-scale metabolomics When replicates were placed fully at random rather than in the systematic embedding arrangement — the authors state systematic arrangements perform better with hRUV/RUV normalisation than fully random ones http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies single-step RUV-III normalisation to large-scale metabolomics data using embedded sample replicates (pooled QC, short replicates, batch replicates) to remove unwanted variation across all batches in one pass, serving as the non-hierarchical baseline for comparison against hRUV. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.12.21.423723
skills.summary: Applies single-step RUV-III normalisation to large-scale metabolomics data using embedded sample replicates (pooled QC, short replicates, batch replicates) to remove unwanted variation across all batches in one pass, serving as the non-hierarchical baseline for comparison against hRUV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is the paper's improved batch correction itself — hRUV hierarchically merges adjustments of neighbouring batches and achieves lower replicate SD than single-step RUV (Fig. 3b) When data contain missing values that cannot be imputed — the algorithm expects complete data, which is often not possible in large-scale metabolomics When replicates were placed fully at random rather than in the systematic embedding arrangement — the authors state systematic arrangements perform better with hRUV/RUV normalisation than fully random ones

skills.description: Use when comparing query speed of spectral-search modules across libraries of varying size, or when reproducing the LipidIN EQ (~2.3 µs/query, 10M-spectrum library) vs Flash Entropy (0.14 s/MS2, 1M library) timing claims under controlled single-thread CPU conditions.
skills.name: single-thread-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: single-thread-runtime-profiling Use when comparing query speed of spectral-search modules across libraries of varying size, or when reproducing the LipidIN EQ (~2.3 µs/query, 10M-spectrum library) vs Flash Entropy (0.14 s/MS2, 1M library) timing claims under controlled single-thread CPU conditions. The goal is annotation accuracy or false discovery rate (e.g., LipidIN's 5.7% FDR over 8,923 lipids) rather than runtime — this skill measures speed only. The runtime environment is multi-threaded or GPU-accelerated, since the benchmark's validity depends on single-thread, low-memory (≥16 GB RAM) conditions. The task is small-molecule MS/MS similarity itself (spectral entropy or dot-product) rather than timing the search implementations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks spectral-library query time as a function of library size by pinning search implementations (LipidIN EQ vs Flash Entropy Search) to a single CPU thread on a low-memory machine and recording per-query wall-clock timings. This isolates algorithmic complexity (linear hash-table/bisection vs squared-time search) from parallel-hardware effects. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks spectral-library query time as a function of library size by pinning search implementations (LipidIN EQ vs Flash Entropy Search) to a single CPU thread on a low-memory machine and recording per-query wall-clock timings. This isolates algorithmic complexity (linear hash-table/bisection vs squared-time search) from parallel-hardware effects.

skills.search_text: single-tracer-13c-model-implementation Use when reconstructing or replicating how the moiety_modeling package computes calculated relative isotopologue intensities (Ix,calc) from moiety state fractional abundances for a 13C single-tracer isotopologue profile. The dataset is a multi-tracer 13C/18O experiment where carbon and oxygen moiety states must combine — use the multi-tracer extension of the same Eq. 1 product-summation scheme instead The goal is metabolic flux analysis over a curated metabolic network (EMU-framework style) rather than deconvolution of a single metabolite's MS isotopologue profile You only need to run the published package's optimization/ranking (analyze optimizations, analyze rank --rankCriteria=AICc) rather than re-implement its forward calculation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Implements the forward isotopologue-intensity calculation (Eq. 1) of the moiety modeling framework: for a single-tracer 13C model, each isotopologue's calculated relative intensity Ix,calc is the sum over isotopologue components whose isotope content equals x, each component being the product of moiety state fractional abundances across all moieties. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: Implements the forward isotopologue-intensity calculation (Eq. 1) of the moiety modeling framework: for a single-tracer 13C model, each isotopologue's calculated relative intensity Ix,calc is the sum over isotopologue components whose isotope content equals x, each component being the product of moiety state fractional abundances across all moieties.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a multi-tracer 13C/18O experiment where carbon and oxygen moiety states must combine — use the multi-tracer extension of the same Eq. 1 product-summation scheme instead The goal is metabolic flux analysis over a curated metabolic network (EMU-framework style) rather than deconvolution of a single metabolite's MS isotopologue profile You only need to run the published package's optimization/ranking (analyze optimizations, analyze rank --rankCriteria=AICc) rather than re-implement its forward calculation

skills.name: single-versus-multi-tracer-deconvolution-comparison
skills.search_text: single-versus-multi-tracer-deconvolution-comparison Decision support for choosing between single- and multi-tracer SIRM isotopologue designs: when you need to know at what added-error standard deviation (σ) model selection via AICc ranking breaks down, or must assess data-quality requirements before measuring multi-tracer datasets. Data are real measured isotopologue profiles rather than simulated timecourses — this skill evaluates data-quality requirements on simulated data, not deconvolution of experimental measurements The metabolic system involves only 13C single-tracer data with an already-settled model — the comparison of single- vs multi-tracer robustness is not informative Flux analysis requires well-curated metabolic networks (e.g., EMU-based 13C MFA) — moiety modeling is designed for cases where network models are incomplete or multiple deconvolution models are plausible http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A simulation-based robustness evaluation that compares how well the moiety_modeling framework selects the correct generating model from single-tracer versus multi-tracer simulated isotopologue timecourses as added-error magnitude (σ) increases, quantifying error propagation through thresholding and renormalization. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-3096-7
skills.summary: A simulation-based robustness evaluation that compares how well the moiety_modeling framework selects the correct generating model from single-tracer versus multi-tracer simulated isotopologue timecourses as added-error magnitude (σ) increases, quantifying error propagation through thresholding and renormalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real measured isotopologue profiles rather than simulated timecourses — this skill evaluates data-quality requirements on simulated data, not deconvolution of experimental measurements The metabolic system involves only 13C single-tracer data with an already-settled model — the comparison of single- vs multi-tracer robustness is not informative Flux analysis requires well-curated metabolic networks (e.g., EMU-based 13C MFA) — moiety modeling is designed for cases where network models are incomplete or multiple deconvolution models are plausible

skills.description: Use when featurizing integer element counts of a chemical formula candidate into a fixed-length, non-negative vector for a neural scorer — e.g., before the Formula Transformer in MIST-CF or when replicating SCARF-style sinusoidal formula embeddings.
skills.name: sinusoidal-feature-embedding-implementation
skills.search_text: sinusoidal-feature-embedding-implementation Use when featurizing integer element counts of a chemical formula candidate into a fixed-length, non-negative vector for a neural scorer — e.g., before the Formula Transformer in MIST-CF or when replicating SCARF-style sinusoidal formula embeddings. Input is already a learned or precomputed feature vector rather than raw element counts — sinusoidal encoding would discard existing structure Formulas contain elements outside the 18-element set supported by MIST-CF's counts-based encoder The target model expects a different encoder (e.g., learned embeddings); MIST-CF models were trained only for positive-mode data, so this encoder also presumes positive-mode formula candidates http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Implements MIST-CF's counts-based formula encoder (Equation 5): integer element counts are converted via sinusoidal features at powers-of-two periods (up to 256) into 8-dimensional non-negative embeddings per element, concatenated across 18 elements into a 144-dimensional vector Enc(F) fed to the Formula Transformer. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Implements MIST-CF's counts-based formula encoder (Equation 5): integer element counts are converted via sinusoidal features at powers-of-two periods (up to 256) into 8-dimensional non-negative embeddings per element, concatenated across 18 elements into a 144-dimensional vector Enc(F) fed to the Formula Transformer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a learned or precomputed feature vector rather than raw element counts — sinusoidal encoding would discard existing structure Formulas contain elements outside the 18-element set supported by MIST-CF's counts-based encoder The target model expects a different encoder (e.g., learned embeddings); MIST-CF models were trained only for positive-mode data, so this encoder also presumes positive-mode formula candidates

skills.search_text: sirius-baseline-comparison-evaluation Use when a new MS/MS annotation or property-prediction model (e.g. fingerprint retrieval, fluorine detection, similarity) must be evaluated head-to-head against the established SIRIUS-based method on the same labeled test spectra. The task is training or fine-tuning the model itself rather than evaluating it against an existing baseline (use the fine-tuning skill instead). Only a single method is of interest and no baseline (SIRIUS, MIST, MIST-CF) is available or applicable to the same spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks a spectral-property or annotation model against the SIRIUS pipeline by running both on a held-out test set of MS/MS spectra and reporting precision/recall (or equivalent) per method so the new model's advantage is quantified, e.g. DreaMS reaching precision 0.91 at recall 0.57 for fluorine detection versus SIRIUS not exceeding 0.51. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3

skills.name: sirius-formula-candidate-enumeration
skills.search_text: sirius-formula-candidate-enumeration Use when you have an exact precursor mass from MS/MS data and need a database-independent candidate formula set (RDBE-plausible, C/H/N/O/P/S/Cl/Br/F elemental space) to score and re-rank with a downstream model. When you already have a small candidate set from a spectral database match (e.g. NIST, GNPS, HMDB, PubChem) — enumeration is for de novo, database-independent settings. skills.search_text: skewness-based-sign-detection Use when independent component analysis (e.g. sklearn FastICA or fastICA with icasso stabilisation) has been run on a samples x genes expression matrix and component signs must be fixed so each source's heaviest distribution tail is positive. The decomposition is not sign-ambiguous or an orientation convention has already been fixed by another method — flipping again would destroy comparability The source distributions are expected to be symmetric, so skewness carries no tail-direction information and the flip decision becomes arbitrary The task is deconvolution with a reference-based orientation (e.g. DeconICA-style immune deconvolution with known signatures) rather than unsupervised skewness-based orientation Fixes the sign ambiguity inherent in ICA decompositions (e.g. fastICA) by checking the skewness of each independent component's source distribution and flipping the component (S -> -S, A -> -A) so that the heaviest tail is positive. This makes components from an icasso-stabilized ICA comparable and interpretable as oriented metagenes on transcriptomic data. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414

Input is already a SmartPeak feature table or a SmartPeak report CSV — use downstream post-processing (e.g. BFAIR) instead. The workflow must be interactive, with per-peak manual review in the chromatogram viewer; use the SmartPeak GUI, not the CLI. The analysis is untargeted LC-MS/MS feature-based metabolomics not requiring SmartPeak's targeted/semi-targeted quantitation steps — OpenMS or another tool may be more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Running a SmartPeak workflow through the SmartPeak CLI (an equivalent of the SmartPeak GUI), including Docker-containerized execution and workflow step cherry-picking, so that capillary-, GC-, and LC-MS(/MS) metabolomics data are processed from raw mzML to quality-controlled quantitation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03421
skills.summary: Running a SmartPeak workflow through the SmartPeak CLI (an equivalent of the SmartPeak GUI), including Docker-containerized execution and workflow step cherry-picking, so that capillary-, GC-, and LC-MS(/MS) metabolomics data are processed from raw mzML to quality-controlled quantitation.

skills.description: Use when developing or tuning DDA acquisition-controller parameters in silico before spending instrument time — specifically when maximizing fragmentation coverage of ions in complex metabolite mixtures via ViMMS virtual injections.
skills.name: smartroi-parameter-tuning-coverage-maximization
skills.search_text: smartroi-parameter-tuning-coverage-maximization Use when developing or tuning DDA acquisition-controller parameters in silico before spending instrument time — specifically when maximizing fragmentation coverage of ions in complex metabolite mixtures via ViMMS virtual injections. When validating the optimized controllers on real hardware rather than in silico — that step uses the Instrument Application Programming Interface (IAPI), not the ViMMS grid search. When the goal is a single-injection theoretical optimum rather than practical controller tuning — the article computes theoretically optimal DDA performance separately from controller parameter selection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Grid-search optimization of SmartROI (alpha, beta) and WeightedDEW (t0, t1) controller parameters in ViMMS to maximize simulated DDA fragmentation coverage, selecting the settings (alpha=1000, beta=0.1; t0=15 s, t1=120 s) that performed best on both serum and beer extracts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03895
skills.summary: Grid-search optimization of SmartROI (alpha, beta) and WeightedDEW (t0, t1) controller parameters in ViMMS to maximize simulated DDA fragmentation coverage, selecting the settings (alpha=1000, beta=0.1; t0=15 s, t1=120 s) that performed best on both serum and beer extracts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When validating the optimized controllers on real hardware rather than in silico — that step uses the Instrument Application Programming Interface (IAPI), not the ViMMS grid search. When the goal is a single-injection theoretical optimum rather than practical controller tuning — the article computes theoretically optimal DDA performance separately from controller parameter selection.

skills.description: Use when assigning chemical compounds to taxonomic categories based on computed structural features, or when building/interpreting computable chemical ontologies (e.g. ChemOnt) where category definitions rely on SMARTS-pattern substructure matching.
skills.name: smarts-pattern-interpretation
skills.search_text: smarts-pattern-interpretation Use when assigning chemical compounds to taxonomic categories based on computed structural features, or when building/interpreting computable chemical ontologies (e.g. ChemOnt) where category definitions rely on SMARTS-pattern substructure matching. When the input is a textual/keyword-based chemical description (e.g. a plain English paragraph) rather than an explicit molecular structure — ClassyFire's structural matching cannot operate on it. When classifying compounds that undergo reactions (e.g. loss of oxygen, substitutions) that fall outside the constraints of the current category definitions, as the article notes these 'might not match the constraints described in a category description'. When only a partial IUPAC name is available and parsing rules cannot resolve it to a full structure — the article notes that 'creating more rules for IUPAC name parsing could help to assign some classes more accurately' but currently the rules are insufficient in some cases. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Interprets SMARTS (SMILES ARbitrary Target Specification) patterns and other structural descriptors as the defining features that drive automated rule-based chemical classification, as implemented in ClassyFire for the ChemOnt taxonomy. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Interprets SMARTS (SMILES ARbitrary Target Specification) patterns and other structural descriptors as the defining features that drive automated rule-based chemical classification, as implemented in ClassyFire for the ChemOnt taxonomy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is a textual/keyword-based chemical description (e.g. a plain English paragraph) rather than an explicit molecular structure — ClassyFire's structural matching cannot operate on it. When classifying compounds that undergo reactions (e.g. loss of oxygen, substitutions) that fall outside the constraints of the current category definitions, as the article notes these 'might not match the constraints described in a category description'. When only a partial IUPAC name is available and parsing rules cannot resolve it to a full structure — the article notes that 'creating more rules for IUPAC name parsing could help to assign some classes more accurately' but currently the rules are insufficient in some cases.

skills.description: Use when building a structure-based chemical taxonomy or classifier where each node/category must be matched to compounds by computable structural rules (e.g. SMARTS, Markush, or feature-logic) rather than expert curation alone.
skills.name: smarts-structural-rule-encoding
skills.search_text: smarts-structural-rule-encoding Use when building a structure-based chemical taxonomy or classifier where each node/category must be matched to compounds by computable structural rules (e.g. SMARTS, Markush, or feature-logic) rather than expert curation alone. The task requires classifying compounds by biological activity, use, or MeSH-style semantic terms rather than purely structural features — ClassyFire's rules use 'only chemical structures and structural features' Structures cannot be standardized (e.g. mixtures or ill-defined polymers) where normalization/aromatization cannot produce a consistent match target You need per-class quantitative performance metrics not yet published for a specific category set — the paper notes IUPAC-name parsing rules may be insufficient for some classes http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0081 Encodes each category of a structural chemical taxonomy as a computable rule — a SMARTS string (>9000 generated), a Markush pattern, or a logical expression over structural features — so that compounds can be matched to categories purely from structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Encodes each category of a structural chemical taxonomy as a computable rule — a SMARTS string (>9000 generated), a Markush pattern, or a logical expression over structural features — so that compounds can be matched to categories purely from structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires classifying compounds by biological activity, use, or MeSH-style semantic terms rather than purely structural features — ClassyFire's rules use 'only chemical structures and structural features' Structures cannot be standardized (e.g. mixtures or ill-defined polymers) where normalization/aromatization cannot produce a consistent match target You need per-class quantitative performance metrics not yet published for a specific category set — the paper notes IUPAC-name parsing rules may be insufficient for some classes

skills.description: Use when training-set curation for spectral classification needs labeled 'relevant'/'other' classes, and structures in an MGF spectral library can be separated by SMARTS substructure definitions of a substance class.
skills.name: smarts-substructure-filtering
skills.search_text: smarts-substructure-filtering Use when training-set curation for spectral classification needs labeled 'relevant'/'other' classes, and structures in an MGF spectral library can be separated by SMARTS substructure definitions of a substance class. When you already have a curated, labeled set of 'relevant' and 'other' reference MS/MS spectra (e.g., from reference standards) and do not need structure-based filtering to generate it. When the target training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article notes classification often fails in this case and AnnoMe cannot resolve it. When the structures behind the spectra are unknown or cannot be matched by SMARTS queries, since filtering relies on substructure matching of library structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Build user-defined 'relevant'/'other' training sets for MS/MS spectral classification by applying SMARTS substructure queries to the structures behind an MGF spectral library, using AnnoMe's filtering GUI. This step produced the 655 (iso-)flavonoid 'relevant' vs 10 000 'other' spectra used to train AnnoMe classifiers on MSnLib v6. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Build user-defined 'relevant'/'other' training sets for MS/MS spectral classification by applying SMARTS substructure queries to the structures behind an MGF spectral library, using AnnoMe's filtering GUI. This step produced the 655 (iso-)flavonoid 'relevant' vs 10 000 'other' spectra used to train AnnoMe classifiers on MSnLib v6.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you already have a curated, labeled set of 'relevant' and 'other' reference MS/MS spectra (e.g., from reference standards) and do not need structure-based filtering to generate it. When the target training dataset is highly imbalanced — the article notes classification often fails in this case and AnnoMe cannot resolve it. When the structures behind the spectra are unknown or cannot be matched by SMARTS queries, since filtering relies on substructure matching of library structures.

skills.description: Use when tandem-MS candidate lists from PubChem/ChemSpider retrieval or user-supplied SDFs contain stereoisomeric redundancy, when isotope signals reveal required elements (e.g. C, S), or when known substructures (e.g. sulfonate SMARTS) should bias candidate ranking.
skills.name: smarts-substructure-scoring
skills.search_text: smarts-substructure-scoring Use when tandem-MS candidate lists from PubChem/ChemSpider retrieval or user-supplied SDFs contain stereoisomeric redundancy, when isotope signals reveal required elements (e.g. C, S), or when known substructures (e.g. sulfonate SMARTS) should bias candidate ranking. When the measured mass spectrum is dominated by one or a few fragments (e.g. a water loss) explainable by most candidates — substructure scoring cannot compensate for uninformative spectra When candidates should be restricted by spectral-library membership rather than structure rules — use suspect lists (e.g. STOFF-IDENT InChIKeys) instead When stereochemistry itself must be resolved — the InChIKey filter intentionally discards stereoisomeric distinctions by keeping only the best-scored candidate per first block http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 MetFrag2.2's candidate filtering/scoring modules that (a) reduce stereoisomer redundancy via first-InChIKey-block filtering, (b) restrict candidates by element include/require/exclude lists, and (c) score or filter candidates by SMARTS substructure inclusion/exclusion matches computed with the Chemistry Development Kit (Eqs. 3-4, W_include = W_exclude = 0.5). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: MetFrag2.2's candidate filtering/scoring modules that (a) reduce stereoisomer redundancy via first-InChIKey-block filtering, (b) restrict candidates by element include/require/exclude lists, and (c) score or filter candidates by SMARTS substructure inclusion/exclusion matches computed with the Chemistry Development Kit (Eqs. 3-4, W_include = W_exclude = 0.5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the measured mass spectrum is dominated by one or a few fragments (e.g. a water loss) explainable by most candidates — substructure scoring cannot compensate for uninformative spectra When candidates should be restricted by spectral-library membership rather than structure rules — use suspect lists (e.g. STOFF-IDENT InChIKeys) instead When stereochemistry itself must be resolved — the InChIKey filter intentionally discards stereoisomeric distinctions by keeping only the best-scored candidate per first block

skills.search_text: smarts-substructure-structure-querying Use when you need to convert a large public MS/MS spectral repository (e.g. MSnLib v6 MGF files) into labeled 'relevant'/'other' training subsets for a substance class of interest defined by SMARTS structural queries. skills.search_text: smarts-superstructure-pattern-matching Use when a chemical structure (SMILES/SDF/InChI) needs structural-feature detection to drive ChemOnt category assignment, i.e. ClassyFire's Feature Extraction step prior to rule-based category assignment. skills.description: Use when a raw CCS database export (e.g., ccsbase.net or metlin.scripps.edu excel/csv dumps) contains repeated SMILES-adduct pairs or unparseable SMILES, and you need a single cleaned value per pair before model training or splitting.
skills.name: smiles-adduct-deduplication-with-mean-ccs-averaging
skills.search_text: smiles-adduct-deduplication-with-mean-ccs-averaging Use when a raw CCS database export (e.g., ccsbase.net or metlin.scripps.edu excel/csv dumps) contains repeated SMILES-adduct pairs or unparseable SMILES, and you need a single cleaned value per pair before model training or splitting. The input already contains one row per unique SMILES-adduct pair with a single CCS value — deduplication would be a no-op and averaging could silently alter curated values You need to preserve individual replicate CCS measurements (e.g., to study inter-instrument variability across the three CCSBase instruments) rather than collapse them to means The target model schema requires raw multi-instance training data rather than Mol2CCS's smiles/adduct/ccs/coordinates parquet format http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 A data-standardization step that cleans raw CCS database dumps (CCSBase, METLIN-CCS) by dropping rows with missing or disconnected SMILES and collapsing duplicate SMILES-adduct pairs into a single record assigned the mean of the measured CCS values. Applying it to CCSBase v1.3 reduces 16,989 raw CCS values to 13,617 cleaned data points. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00899-w
skills.summary: A data-standardization step that cleans raw CCS database dumps (CCSBase, METLIN-CCS) by dropping rows with missing or disconnected SMILES and collapsing duplicate SMILES-adduct pairs into a single record assigned the mean of the measured CCS values. Applying it to CCSBase v1.3 reduces 16,989 raw CCS values to 13,617 cleaned data points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input already contains one row per unique SMILES-adduct pair with a single CCS value — deduplication would be a no-op and averaging could silently alter curated values You need to preserve individual replicate CCS measurements (e.g., to study inter-instrument variability across the three CCSBase instruments) rather than collapse them to means The target model schema requires raw multi-instance training data rather than Mol2CCS's smiles/adduct/ccs/coordinates parquet format

skills.description: Use when you need to annotate the fragment peaks of a small-molecule MS/MS spectrum (e.g. a GNPS library entry loaded by USI) using a SMILES string for the (sub)structure, before producing a static annotated figure.
skills.name: smiles-based-small-molecule-fragment-annotation
skills.search_text: smiles-based-small-molecule-fragment-annotation Use when you need to annotate the fragment peaks of a small-molecule MS/MS spectrum (e.g. a GNPS library entry loaded by USI) using a SMILES string for the (sub)structure, before producing a static annotated figure. The input is a peptide MS/MS spectrum where fragment annotations come from a ProForma 2.0 peptide string (a, b, y ions) rather than a small-molecule SMILES structure. You need to read spectral data files directly — spectrum_utils does not provide file-reading functionality and relies on external tools for that task. The molecule of interest has no SMILES representation available, so structure-based fragment annotation cannot be performed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates fragment peaks in a metabolomics MS/MS spectrum using an in-silico fragmentation of a small molecule encoded as a SMILES string, enabling colored, labeled fragment peaks in a rendered static spectrum figure (e.g. for a GNPS library entry such as CCMSLIB00000840351). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b04884
skills.summary: Annotates fragment peaks in a metabolomics MS/MS spectrum using an in-silico fragmentation of a small molecule encoded as a SMILES string, enabling colored, labeled fragment peaks in a rendered static spectrum figure (e.g. for a GNPS library entry such as CCMSLIB00000840351).

skills.description: Use when scoring SMILES strings generated by the substructure-to-structure transformer or multitask model — deduplicating/canonicalizing predictions, deciding exact-match hits, or measuring near-miss similarity for molecules the model missed.

skills.search_text: smiles-canonicalization-and-tanimoto-matching Use when scoring SMILES strings generated by the substructure-to-structure transformer or multitask model — deduplicating/canonicalizing predictions, deciding exact-match hits, or measuring near-miss similarity for molecules the model missed. skills.description: Use when preparing held-out test sets (e.g. NIST 20 test split, SWGDRUG, Cayman, MONA) for a spectral-annotation model and you must guarantee no compound overlaps the synthetic or experimental training data before evaluation.
skills.name: smiles-canonicalization-deduplication
skills.search_text: smiles-canonicalization-deduplication Use when preparing held-out test sets (e.g. NIST 20 test split, SWGDRUG, Cayman, MONA) for a spectral-annotation model and you must guarantee no compound overlaps the synthetic or experimental training data before evaluation. Input is already a set of chemical structures or SMILES strings rather than spectra embeddings — the decoder consumes encoder embeddings, not raw molecules. skills.search_text: smiles-structure-sanitization Use when a natural-products or compound table mixes SMILES strings, InChIs, and compound names, and you need sanitized structures and standardized InChIs before joining or publishing structure-organism pairs. Input structures are already canonical, salt-stripped InChIs or standardized SMILES that you must preserve verbatim — the systematic sanitization step can degrade correct salts, charged, or dimeric molecules ('correct salts, charged or dimeric molecules in the input data will suffer an unwanted sanitization step'). The goal is name-to-structure translation only, with structures already present — OPSIN name translation is only invoked when no InChI or SMILES is available. You need structural or spectral search over the cleaned structures — the LOTUS pipeline itself delegates indexing/search to Wikidata SPARQL, IDSM, and the Sachem PostgreSQL cartridge rather than this cleaning step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Standardize heterogeneous chemical structure inputs from natural-products tables into sanitized, non-dimeric SMILES with a standardized InChI representation, using RDKit parsing and the MolVS package as implemented in the lotus-processor pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Standardize heterogeneous chemical structure inputs from natural-products tables into sanitized, non-dimeric SMILES with a standardized InChI representation, using RDKit parsing and the MolVS package as implemented in the lotus-processor pipeline.

The goal is name-to-structure translation only, with structures already present — OPSIN name translation is only invoked when no InChI or SMILES is available. You need structural or spectral search over the cleaned structures — the LOTUS pipeline itself delegates indexing/search to Wikidata SPARQL, IDSM, and the Sachem PostgreSQL cartridge rather than this cleaning step.
