skills.description: Use when you have a catalogued SMILES structure list (e.g., the EPA CompTox PFAS list of 8000+ structures) and need predicted fragment ions, including F-containing fragments, to drive fragment screening without experimental MS/MS spectra.
skills.name: smiles-substructure-fragment-matching
skills.search_text: smiles-substructure-fragment-matching Use when you have a catalogued SMILES structure list (e.g., the EPA CompTox PFAS list of 8000+ structures) and need predicted fragment ions, including F-containing fragments, to drive fragment screening without experimental MS/MS spectra. Experimental MS/MS spectra already exist for the suspect list — the original FluoroMatch suspect screening approach targeting compounds with available MS/MS spectra is the right path instead Input is a feature table or raw LC-HRMS/MS data rather than a SMILES structure list — feature detection and blank filtering come first, and this skill operates purely on chemical structures Analytes ionize in positive mode or outside the MZedDB [M−H]− rules, since the library is built by restricting to SMILES forming the [M−H]− precursor ion http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generate a predicted MS/MS fragment library for PFAS by decomposing a list of SMILES structures into substructures, matching fragments to molecule SMILES with the RCDK 'match' function, and emitting a fragment–substructure table (SMILES2MS2_PFAS_fragment_library.csv) that plugs into FluoroMatch 2.0's predicted-MS/MS-from-SMILES step. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-021-03392-7
skills.summary: Generate a predicted MS/MS fragment library for PFAS by decomposing a list of SMILES structures into substructures, matching fragments to molecule SMILES with the RCDK 'match' function, and emitting a fragment–substructure table (SMILES2MS2_PFAS_fragment_library.csv) that plugs into FluoroMatch 2.0's predicted-MS/MS-from-SMILES step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Experimental MS/MS spectra already exist for the suspect list — the original FluoroMatch suspect screening approach targeting compounds with available MS/MS spectra is the right path instead Input is a feature table or raw LC-HRMS/MS data rather than a SMILES structure list — feature detection and blank filtering come first, and this skill operates purely on chemical structures Analytes ionize in positive mode or outside the MZedDB [M−H]− rules, since the library is built by restricting to SMILES forming the [M−H]− precursor ion

skills.description: Use when decoding or simulating fragment trees from candidate SMILES or MSn peak lists and you must enforce TeFT's MW, element-set, and SMILES-tree node-count limits before similarity scoring.
skills.name: smiles-tree-node-constraint-validation
skills.search_text: smiles-tree-node-constraint-validation Use when decoding or simulating fragment trees from candidate SMILES or MSn peak lists and you must enforce TeFT's MW, element-set, and SMILES-tree node-count limits before similarity scoring. Input spectra come from instruments with high mass resolution and accuracy (e.g. Orbitrap) where the TeFT low-resolution constraint set does not apply. The molecule under test contains elements outside C,H,O,N,P,S,Cl,Br,I,F or exceeds 500 Da — the constraint check would systematically exclude it rather than help. Only fingerprint prediction or formula search is needed, with no fragment tree construction — MetFrag-style database search or SIRIUS is a better fit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3421 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Validates that simulated or predicted SMILES fragment trees in the TeFT de novo structure pipeline respect the stated chemical constraints (MW < 500 Da, only C,H,O,N,P,S,Cl,Br,I,F, at most 1500 tree nodes) before downstream fragment-tree similarity scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0
skills.summary: Validates that simulated or predicted SMILES fragment trees in the TeFT de novo structure pipeline respect the stated chemical constraints (MW < 500 Da, only C,H,O,N,P,S,Cl,Br,I,F, at most 1500 tree nodes) before downstream fragment-tree similarity scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra come from instruments with high mass resolution and accuracy (e.g. Orbitrap) where the TeFT low-resolution constraint set does not apply. The molecule under test contains elements outside C,H,O,N,P,S,Cl,Br,I,F or exceeds 500 Da — the constraint check would systematically exclude it rather than help. Only fingerprint prediction or formula search is needed, with no fragment tree construction — MetFrag-style database search or SIRIUS is a better fit.

skills.name: smiles-validation-and-canonicalization
skills.search_text: smiles-validation-and-canonicalization Use when a molecular generator (e.g., DeepMet RNN sampling) emits millions of raw SMILES strings that must be validity-checked, deduplicated by canonical form, and annotated with mass and formula before frequency tabulation. Input structures are already canonicalized and validated (e.g., a published 34.4-million-structure resource with sampling frequencies already provided) — re-running would be redundant The analysis is on preprocessed training-set SMILES rather than newly generated molecules; the preprocessing pipeline (removing light fragments, neutralizing charges, filtering for valid elements, removing rare vocabulary tokens) already handles those You need de novo structure prioritization by mass-to-charge ratio or MS/MS spectral matching rather than validity checking and frequency tabulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Parse every structure produced by a generative chemical language model with RDKit, discard chemically invalid SMILES, and canonicalize the remainder so that frequency counting and InChIKey-based de-duplication are applied to a single, well-defined representation of each molecule. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Parse every structure produced by a generative chemical language model with RDKit, discard chemically invalid SMILES, and canonicalize the remainder so that frequency counting and InChIKey-based de-duplication are applied to a single, well-defined representation of each molecule.

skills.description: Use when curating a SMILES training set for a chemical language model (e.g., DeepMet/CLM) and you need to eliminate molecules whose strings contain tokens too rare to learn reliably.
skills.name: smiles-vocabulary-token-filtering
skills.search_text: smiles-vocabulary-token-filtering Use when curating a SMILES training set for a chemical language model (e.g., DeepMet/CLM) and you need to eliminate molecules whose strings contain tokens too rare to learn reliably. Input is already a canonical, pre-filtered SMILES table that passed preprocessing — re-running the rare-token filter adds no value and may drop additional valid rows. You are evaluating a model on an external dataset (e.g., PubChem for model evaluation) where the vocabulary was fixed at training time; new rare tokens there reflect the test distribution, not a training-set cleaning need. You are tokenizing a different chemical representation (e.g., SELFIES) where the rare-token criterion does not apply as designed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A molecular preprocessing filter that removes molecules containing very rare SMILES tokens from a training corpus, so that the chemical language model's vocabulary is not polluted by infrequent, poorly learned character sequences. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458

skills.description: Use when building or auditing an ESI-MS/MS in-silico rule-based predictor that needs SMIRKS fragmentation rules with chemical-class routing and relative intensities, e.g. reproducing CFM-ID 4.0's extended MSRB rule set.
skills.name: smirks-fragmentation-rule-parsing
skills.search_text: smirks-fragmentation-rule-parsing Use when building or auditing an ESI-MS/MS in-silico rule-based predictor that needs SMIRKS fragmentation rules with chemical-class routing and relative intensities, e.g. reproducing CFM-ID 4.0's extended MSRB rule set. Predicting spectra for compounds outside the covered chemical classes — CFM-ID's MSRB rules target specific ClassyFire classes (acylcarnitines, acylcholines, flavonoids, lipids); generic bond-topology (C2MS) prediction should be used instead. The input spectra were collected on non-QTOF instruments — the rules encode average scaled intensities from QTOF data at 10, 20, and 40 eV. You need machine-learned fragmentation parameters rather than hand-written rules — CFM-ID 4.0's main accuracy gains come from topology-learned parameters, not the MSRB library. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extract, annotate, and verify CFM-ID 4.0's hand-made SMIRKS-based fragmentation (MSRB) rule library — 313 rules covering 11 chemical classes and 3 adduct types — attaching average scaled relative intensities and ClassyFire class routing for each rule. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Extract, annotate, and verify CFM-ID 4.0's hand-made SMIRKS-based fragmentation (MSRB) rule library — 313 rules covering 11 chemical classes and 3 adduct types — attaching average scaled relative intensities and ClassyFire class routing for each rule.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting spectra for compounds outside the covered chemical classes — CFM-ID's MSRB rules target specific ClassyFire classes (acylcarnitines, acylcholines, flavonoids, lipids); generic bond-topology (C2MS) prediction should be used instead. The input spectra were collected on non-QTOF instruments — the rules encode average scaled intensities from QTOF data at 10, 20, and 40 eV. You need machine-learned fragmentation parameters rather than hand-written rules — CFM-ID 4.0's main accuracy gains come from topology-learned parameters, not the MSRB library.

skills.description: Use when you have a substrate structure plus a set of predicted reactive η-η / η-H bond pairs for a CYP450 isoform and need to transform the matching substructures into metabolite structures.
skills.name: smirks-reaction-transformation
skills.search_text: smirks-reaction-transformation Use when you have a substrate structure plus a set of predicted reactive η-η / η-H bond pairs for a CYP450 isoform and need to transform the matching substructures into metabolite structures. The compound has not been classified as a reactant by CypReact — CyProduct proceeds only if CypReact returns R (reactant). No reactive bonds have been predicted (e.g. CypBoM found no 〈η-η〉 or 〈η-H〉 BoM above threshold), so there is no subset S' to transform. The task is reactant/substrate classification rather than metabolite generation — use CypReact instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3370 Applies SMIRKS reaction transformation strings to the reactive bond-of-metabolism (BoM) atom pairs predicted by CypBoM, generating the structure of each CYP450 metabolite as MetaboGen does in CyProduct. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Applies SMIRKS reaction transformation strings to the reactive bond-of-metabolism (BoM) atom pairs predicted by CypBoM, generating the structure of each CYP450 metabolite as MetaboGen does in CyProduct.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound has not been classified as a reactant by CypReact — CyProduct proceeds only if CypReact returns R (reactant). No reactive bonds have been predicted (e.g. CypBoM found no 〈η-η〉 or 〈η-H〉 BoM above threshold), so there is no subset S' to transform. The task is reactant/substrate classification rather than metabolite generation — use CypReact instead.

skills.description: Use when you have standard 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma from a Bruker IVDr 600 MHz instrument and need fast, reliable assignment and integration of a small targeted metabolite panel (e.g. 22 metabolites) without sample preprocessing, deconvolution, or baseline fitting.
skills.name: smolesy-select-spin-system-pattern-search
skills.search_text: smolesy-select-spin-system-pattern-search Use when you have standard 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma from a Bruker IVDr 600 MHz instrument and need fast, reliable assignment and integration of a small targeted metabolite panel (e.g. 22 metabolites) without sample preprocessing, deconvolution, or baseline fitting. Input spectra are 2D NMR or not 1D 1H NMR (e.g. 2D-Jres is used only for validation, not as the primary input). The analysis requires full untargeted metabolite profiling or deconvolution of heavily overlapped low-abundance signals beyond the 22 targeted spin systems; SMolESY-select is designed for a targeted panel with predefined bins. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 SMolESY-select is a fully automated, computationally lightweight algorithm that assigns and integrates 22 targeted metabolites in 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma by searching SMolESY-enhanced spectra for each spin-system pattern within predefined spectral windows (bins), avoiding complex deconvolution or baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: SMolESY-select is a fully automated, computationally lightweight algorithm that assigns and integrates 22 targeted metabolites in 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma by searching SMolESY-enhanced spectra for each spin-system pattern within predefined spectral windows (bins), avoiding complex deconvolution or baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are 2D NMR or not 1D 1H NMR (e.g. 2D-Jres is used only for validation, not as the primary input). The analysis requires full untargeted metabolite profiling or deconvolution of heavily overlapped low-abundance signals beyond the 22 targeted spin systems; SMolESY-select is designed for a targeted panel with predefined bins.

skills.description: Use when a SMolESY-enhanced 1D ¹H NMR spectrum has been processed and specific spectral windows (e.g. tyrosine, phenylalanine, histidine, creatinine, choline) still show low s/n signals from low-abundance metabolites that need denoising before integration.
skills.name: smolesy-spectrum-smoothing
skills.search_text: smolesy-spectrum-smoothing Use when a SMolESY-enhanced 1D ¹H NMR spectrum has been processed and specific spectral windows (e.g. tyrosine, phenylalanine, histidine, creatinine, choline) still show low s/n signals from low-abundance metabolites that need denoising before integration. The spectrum has not been SMolESY-enhanced (e.g. it is a raw or standard 1D ¹H NMR spectrum); smoothing without prior resolution enhancement would broaden Δν1/2 toward the standard line width and lose the s/n benefit The target metabolite's signals lie outside the predefined spectral windows and require full-spectrum processing or complex deconvolution instead The sample data are CPMG spectra with adequate s/n, since the smoothing filter trades up to ∼10% s/n loss relative to CPMG and offers no advantage there http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Applies an 11-point moving average smoothing filter across the high-resolution data of selected NMR spectral windows in SMolESY-enhanced 1D ¹H NMR spectra, to denoise those windows and recover signals of frequently low-abundance metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Applies an 11-point moving average smoothing filter across the high-resolution data of selected NMR spectral windows in SMolESY-enhanced 1D ¹H NMR spectra, to denoise those windows and recover signals of frequently low-abundance metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum has not been SMolESY-enhanced (e.g. it is a raw or standard 1D ¹H NMR spectrum); smoothing without prior resolution enhancement would broaden Δν1/2 toward the standard line width and lose the s/n benefit The target metabolite's signals lie outside the predefined spectral windows and require full-spectrum processing or complex deconvolution instead The sample data are CPMG spectra with adequate s/n, since the smoothing filter trades up to ∼10% s/n loss relative to CPMG and offers no advantage there

skills.description: Use when you have calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz, MTBLS395) and need to assign 24 predefined 1H NMR spin systems to specific spectral windows (bins) so metabolite signals can be integrated without deconvolution.
skills.name: smolsesy-spectral-window-matching
skills.search_text: smolsesy-spectral-window-matching Use when you have calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz, MTBLS395) and need to assign 24 predefined 1H NMR spin systems to specific spectral windows (bins) so metabolite signals can be integrated without deconvolution. Input is already a processed metabolite concentration table or the spectrum has not been SMolESY-processed — this skill operates on SMolESY data, not raw or differently preprocessed spectra The analysis requires deconvolution or baseline fitting of complex spectral mixtures — SMolESY-select explicitly avoids these steps Metabolite is outside the predefined 22-metabolite panel / 24 spin-system bins http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assigns 1H NMR spin-system patterns of 22 serum/plasma metabolites to their spectral positions in SMolESY-processed spectra by searching each predefined spectral window (bin) for its expected pattern, producing per-bin assignments and direct integration without deconvolution or baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Assigns 1H NMR spin-system patterns of 22 serum/plasma metabolites to their spectral positions in SMolESY-processed spectra by searching each predefined spectral window (bin) for its expected pattern, producing per-bin assignments and direct integration without deconvolution or baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed metabolite concentration table or the spectrum has not been SMolESY-processed — this skill operates on SMolESY data, not raw or differently preprocessed spectra The analysis requires deconvolution or baseline fitting of complex spectral mixtures — SMolESY-select explicitly avoids these steps Metabolite is outside the predefined 22-metabolite panel / 24 spin-system bins

skills.description: Use when preprocessing LC-QQQ-MS MRM raw data (mzML) and candidate chromatographic peaks must be detected and scored before ML-based or averaged peak classification, e.g. inside automRm's process_batch() workflow.
skills.name: smoothed-trace-local-maxima-peak-candidate-detection
skills.search_text: smoothed-trace-local-maxima-peak-candidate-detection Use when preprocessing LC-QQQ-MS MRM raw data (mzML) and candidate chromatographic peaks must be detected and scored before ML-based or averaged peak classification, e.g. inside automRm's process_batch() workflow. The data are not MRM mode LC-MS (e.g. full-scan/DDA) — automRm's peak picking operates on quantifier/qualifier MRM traces and for optimal performance requires at least one qualifier in addition to the quantifier A validated peak table already exists and only the ML peak-reporting step is needed — this skill covers candidate generation, not the reporting model Samples are excessively dirty, very-low-input, or from a new LC method, where the authors retreat to manual peak review for selected metabolites automRm's peak-picking stage: local maxima are detected in a smoothed version of the quantifier MRM trace, candidate peaks are ranked by peak height, and each candidate is described by 20 quality scores (peak shape, quantifier/qualifier agreement, RT deviation) for downstream ML evaluation or averaging. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05224
skills.summary: automRm's peak-picking stage: local maxima are detected in a smoothed version of the quantifier MRM trace, candidate peaks are ranked by peak height, and each candidate is described by 20 quality scores (peak shape, quantifier/qualifier agreement, RT deviation) for downstream ML evaluation or averaging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not MRM mode LC-MS (e.g. full-scan/DDA) — automRm's peak picking operates on quantifier/qualifier MRM traces and for optimal performance requires at least one qualifier in addition to the quantifier A validated peak table already exists and only the ML peak-reporting step is needed — this skill covers candidate generation, not the reporting model Samples are excessively dirty, very-low-input, or from a new LC method, where the authors retreat to manual peak review for selected metabolites

skills.description: Use when a harmonized (or unharmonized) urinary/clinical metabolite compound list needs pathway over-representation analysis, especially to compare enrichment outcomes with vs without a merging/harmonization strategy.
skills.name: smpdb-pathway-mapping
skills.search_text: smpdb-pathway-mapping Use when a harmonized (or unharmonized) urinary/clinical metabolite compound list needs pathway over-representation analysis, especially to compare enrichment outcomes with vs without a merging/harmonization strategy. The input is raw spectral data (e.g. mzML) rather than a curated, identifier-resolved compound list — MMS harmonization must be completed first. The goal is pathway analysis on gene/protein lists rather than metabolite compound identifiers. A different pathway database than SMPDB is required, since the article's reproducible result (two pathways at FDR < 0.05) is specific to MetaboAnalyst 5.0 with SMPDB. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Runs over-representation pathway enrichment on a curated metabolite compound list using MetaboAnalyst 5.0 with the Small Molecule Pathway Database (SMPDB), and contrasts results before and after Metabolites Merging Strategy (MMS) harmonization to expose pathways hidden by identifier fragmentation. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13121167
skills.summary: Runs over-representation pathway enrichment on a curated metabolite compound list using MetaboAnalyst 5.0 with the Small Molecule Pathway Database (SMPDB), and contrasts results before and after Metabolites Merging Strategy (MMS) harmonization to expose pathways hidden by identifier fragmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw spectral data (e.g. mzML) rather than a curated, identifier-resolved compound list — MMS harmonization must be completed first. The goal is pathway analysis on gene/protein lists rather than metabolite compound identifiers. A different pathway database than SMPDB is required, since the article's reproducible result (two pathways at FDR < 0.05) is specific to MetaboAnalyst 5.0 with SMPDB.

skills.description: Use when a task needs the METLIN SMRT retention time table with ECFP fingerprints loaded and randomly split 75% training / 25% validation before training or benchmarking an RT prediction model.
skills.name: smrt-fingerprint-data-loading
skills.search_text: smrt-fingerprint-data-loading Use when a task needs the METLIN SMRT retention time table with ECFP fingerprints loaded and randomly split 75% training / 25% validation before training or benchmarking an RT prediction model. The data are already loaded as a disjoint train/validation feature matrix — re-splitting would break comparability with the published 75/25 evaluation The task is a downstream comparison (e.g., Tanimoto-thresholded k-NN vs. DLM error testing), which consumes the outputs of this skill rather than performing the loading itself The input dataset is not the METLIN SMRT RT dataset (e.g., MS/MS spectra or other chromatographic modalities), since SMRT covers reverse-phase chromatography retention times specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ingests the METLIN SMRT dataset — experimentally acquired reverse-phase chromatography retention times (in seconds) for up to 80,038 small molecules paired with ECFP fingerprints — and randomly partitions molecules into a 75% training / 25% validation split for downstream RT-prediction modeling. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Ingests the METLIN SMRT dataset — experimentally acquired reverse-phase chromatography retention times (in seconds) for up to 80,038 small molecules paired with ECFP fingerprints — and randomly partitions molecules into a 75% training / 25% validation split for downstream RT-prediction modeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already loaded as a disjoint train/validation feature matrix — re-splitting would break comparability with the published 75/25 evaluation The task is a downstream comparison (e.g., Tanimoto-thresholded k-NN vs. DLM error testing), which consumes the outputs of this skill rather than performing the loading itself The input dataset is not the METLIN SMRT RT dataset (e.g., MS/MS spectra or other chromatographic modalities), since SMRT covers reverse-phase chromatography retention times specifically

skills.description: Use when evaluating RT-Transformer (or similar RT predictors) on the SMRT retained test set to check error coverage (<60 s, <120 s) and the false negative rate of a ±2 SD RT filter before using the filter for metabolite identification.
skills.name: smrt-test-set-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: smrt-test-set-quality-assessment Use when evaluating RT-Transformer (or similar RT predictors) on the SMRT retained test set to check error coverage (<60 s, <120 s) and the false negative rate of a ±2 SD RT filter before using the filter for metabolite identification. Input is the full SMRT dataset including not-retained molecules — the paper reports a much larger average absolute error of 33.41 when no samples are removed versus 27.30 after removing not-retained molecules, so error/coverage statistics are not comparable Evaluating on a transfer-learning dataset from PredRet under a different chromatographic method — the ±2 SD threshold of 52.80 s was calibrated on the SMRT retained test set and should not be assumed transferable The goal is to run the model on new molecules to obtain predictions (use the QuickStart notebook / HuggingFace web server) rather than to audit test-set prediction quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Quality-assessment workflow that computes the absolute RT prediction error distribution of RT-Transformer on the SMRT retained-molecule test set (7,790 molecules) and quantifies the false negative rate induced by the ±2 SD (52.80 s) retention-time filter, written to smrt_retained_test_error_stats.csv. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Quality-assessment workflow that computes the absolute RT prediction error distribution of RT-Transformer on the SMRT retained-molecule test set (7,790 molecules) and quantifies the false negative rate induced by the ±2 SD (52.80 s) retention-time filter, written to smrt_retained_test_error_stats.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is the full SMRT dataset including not-retained molecules — the paper reports a much larger average absolute error of 33.41 when no samples are removed versus 27.30 after removing not-retained molecules, so error/coverage statistics are not comparable Evaluating on a transfer-learning dataset from PredRet under a different chromatographic method — the ±2 SD threshold of 52.80 s was calibrated on the SMRT retained test set and should not be assumed transferable The goal is to run the model on new molecules to obtain predictions (use the QuickStart notebook / HuggingFace web server) rather than to audit test-set prediction quality

skills.description: Use when comparing fatty acyl chains by double bond position, when numbering direction (carbonyl-forward vs ω/methyl-end) affects the comparison outcome, or when sn-positions are unspecified in lipid names such as PC 18:0_16:1.
skills.name: sn-position-vs-omega-position-counting
skills.search_text: sn-position-vs-omega-position-counting Use when comparing fatty acyl chains by double bond position, when numbering direction (carbonyl-forward vs ω/methyl-end) affects the comparison outcome, or when sn-positions are unspecified in lipid names such as PC 18:0_16:1. Lipid records are not at the highest structural resolution level (no explicit double bond positions on the chains), so forward/backward position sets cannot be constructed The goal is quantitative lipidome comparison (abundances, study variables, PCA/dendrograms) rather than structural double bond correctness checks Only a single counting direction is needed and sn-positions are fully specified, making the all-combination FA mode an unnecessary performance cost http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 A method for comparing fatty acyl chains by their double bond positions while accounting for the two counting directions — forward from the carbonyl carbon and backward from the methyl end (ω-notation) — and for unspecified sn-positions, used to verify the correctness of structural double bond comparisons against the ≥73% complete-mismatch probability reported for LIPID MAPS. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: A method for comparing fatty acyl chains by their double bond positions while accounting for the two counting directions — forward from the carbonyl carbon and backward from the methyl end (ω-notation) — and for unspecified sn-positions, used to verify the correctness of structural double bond comparisons against the ≥73% complete-mismatch probability reported for LIPID MAPS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Lipid records are not at the highest structural resolution level (no explicit double bond positions on the chains), so forward/backward position sets cannot be constructed The goal is quantitative lipidome comparison (abundances, study variables, PCA/dendrograms) rather than structural double bond correctness checks Only a single counting direction is needed and sn-positions are fully specified, making the all-combination FA mode an unnecessary performance cost

skills.description: Use when starting an untargeted LC-MS/MS analysis with UmetaFlow: you have Thermo raw files or mzMLs, need to set TRUE/FALSE step flags, ionisation mode, minfrac thresholds and sample/blank tables in the config/ folder.
skills.name: snakemake-workflow-configuration
skills.search_text: snakemake-workflow-configuration Use when starting an untargeted LC-MS/MS analysis with UmetaFlow: you have Thermo raw files or mzMLs, need to set TRUE/FALSE step flags, ionisation mode, minfrac thresholds and sample/blank tables in the config/ folder. Input data are already processed feature tables (e.g. a pre-computed feature quantification matrix) rather than raw or mzML files — configuration of the detection/conversion pipeline is unnecessary. The user needs a single ad-hoc algorithm run (e.g. only FeatureFinderMetaboIdent) rather than the full chained workflow; the pyOpenMS notebooks alone may suffice. Running on Windows: the Snakemake implementation targets Linux and MacOS systems, so use the pyOpenMS Jupyter implementation instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Configure the UmetaFlow Snakemake workflow (or its pyOpenMS Jupyter equivalent) for a specific untargeted metabolomics dataset by editing config.yaml step flags and parameters and generating dataset.tsv, blanks.tsv and samples.tsv, so that feature detection, re-quantification, annotation and benchmarking steps run reproducibly. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: Configure the UmetaFlow Snakemake workflow (or its pyOpenMS Jupyter equivalent) for a specific untargeted metabolomics dataset by editing config.yaml step flags and parameters and generating dataset.tsv, blanks.tsv and samples.tsv, so that feature detection, re-quantification, annotation and benchmarking steps run reproducibly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already processed feature tables (e.g. a pre-computed feature quantification matrix) rather than raw or mzML files — configuration of the detection/conversion pipeline is unnecessary. The user needs a single ad-hoc algorithm run (e.g. only FeatureFinderMetaboIdent) rather than the full chained workflow; the pyOpenMS notebooks alone may suffice. Running on Windows: the Snakemake implementation targets Linux and MacOS systems, so use the pyOpenMS Jupyter implementation instead.

skills.description: Use when a task requires automated, reproducible downloading of deposited Thermo RAW files from PRIDE accessions and their annotation with instrument-, run-, and scan-level metadata via MetaXtract in a batch workflow.
skills.name: snakemake-workflow-configuration
skills.search_text: snakemake-workflow-configuration Use when a task requires automated, reproducible downloading of deposited Thermo RAW files from PRIDE accessions and their annotation with instrument-, run-, and scan-level metadata via MetaXtract in a batch workflow. Input files are not Thermo Fisher RAW files — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW and additional vendor formats are not yet supported The goal is extracting Thermo MS method or LC method files on Linux containers — ms_method and lc_method exports are not supported on Linux Interactive, single-file inspection with a GUI is needed rather than automated batch processing — the container workflow is CLI/config-only and excludes the GUI http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A Snakemake-based, open-source workflow shipped with MetaXtract that automatically downloads RAW files from PRIDE (by year and file count) and runs end-to-end metadata annotation, producing structured TSV/CSV metadata (file-based details plus MS1/MS2 scan-header tables) for FAIR, reproducible batch annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.687968
skills.summary: A Snakemake-based, open-source workflow shipped with MetaXtract that automatically downloads RAW files from PRIDE (by year and file count) and runs end-to-end metadata annotation, producing structured TSV/CSV metadata (file-based details plus MS1/MS2 scan-header tables) for FAIR, reproducible batch annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files are not Thermo Fisher RAW files — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo RAW and additional vendor formats are not yet supported The goal is extracting Thermo MS method or LC method files on Linux containers — ms_method and lc_method exports are not supported on Linux Interactive, single-file inspection with a GUI is needed rather than automated batch processing — the container workflow is CLI/config-only and excludes the GUI

skills.description: Use when SNP-array alteration calls (e.g. 10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) must be reconciled against protein-level tumor subgroups (phosphoAKT1/MYC k-means classes) to compute per-subgroup concordance and residual discordance in a cohort.
skills.name: snp-array-genomic-alteration-tabulation
skills.search_text: snp-array-genomic-alteration-tabulation Use when SNP-array alteration calls (e.g. 10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) must be reconciled against protein-level tumor subgroups (phosphoAKT1/MYC k-means classes) to compute per-subgroup concordance and residual discordance in a cohort. The input is raw SNP-array intensity/CN data not yet reduced to alteration calls (10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) — segmentation and calling must happen first. Tumor subgroups have not been defined: this skill requires the k-means phosphoAKT1/MYC classification (6+21=27 phosphoAKT1-high; 6+9=15 MYC-high), not just raw densitometry. The goal is metabolomic pathway enrichment (GSEA over KEGG metabolite sets) rather than genomic–proteomic concordance accounting. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Tabulates how often SNP-array genomic alterations (10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) coincide with immunoblot-defined phosphoAKT1-high or MYC-high tumor subgroups, converting raw case counts into concordance fractions and residual-discordance fractions. It quantifies how much of oncoprotein activation the underlying copy-number changes can actually explain. metabolomics/v3 10.1158/0008-5472.can-14-1490
skills.summary: Tabulates how often SNP-array genomic alterations (10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) coincide with immunoblot-defined phosphoAKT1-high or MYC-high tumor subgroups, converting raw case counts into concordance fractions and residual-discordance fractions. It quantifies how much of oncoprotein activation the underlying copy-number changes can actually explain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw SNP-array intensity/CN data not yet reduced to alteration calls (10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) — segmentation and calling must happen first. Tumor subgroups have not been defined: this skill requires the k-means phosphoAKT1/MYC classification (6+21=27 phosphoAKT1-high; 6+9=15 MYC-high), not just raw densitometry. The goal is metabolomic pathway enrichment (GSEA over KEGG metabolite sets) rather than genomic–proteomic concordance accounting.

skills.description: Use when GWAS summary statistics (here 114 published traits/diseases) must be tested for SNP-heritability enrichment in predefined gene sets — e.g., tissue-specific DE genes from exercise training — via LD score regression rather than simple overlap tests.
skills.name: snp-heritability-partitioning-ldsc
skills.search_text: snp-heritability-partitioning-ldsc Use when GWAS summary statistics (here 114 published traits/diseases) must be tested for SNP-heritability enrichment in predefined gene sets — e.g., tissue-specific DE genes from exercise training — via LD score regression rather than simple overlap tests. The goal is expression-mediated heritability (proportion of hSNP2 mediated by gene expression) — use MESC with GWAS + eQTL summary statistics instead of LDSC enrichment The question is gene-level trait association with direction of effect rather than heritability enrichment — S-PrediXcan/TWAS is the appropriate approach Gene sets are not tissue/gene-set stratified annotations of common variants with appropriate LD Scores (e.g., rare-variant or sequencing-based signals), which LD score regression does not accommodate http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Estimate SNP-heritability (hSNP2) enrichment of trait GWAS signal in gene sets (e.g., sex-consistent 8-week exercise DE genes per tissue) using LDSC partitioned/cell-type-specific heritability regression, with a random-gene-set simulation as negative control. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-45966-w
skills.summary: Estimate SNP-heritability (hSNP2) enrichment of trait GWAS signal in gene sets (e.g., sex-consistent 8-week exercise DE genes per tissue) using LDSC partitioned/cell-type-specific heritability regression, with a random-gene-set simulation as negative control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is expression-mediated heritability (proportion of hSNP2 mediated by gene expression) — use MESC with GWAS + eQTL summary statistics instead of LDSC enrichment The question is gene-level trait association with direction of effect rather than heritability enrichment — S-PrediXcan/TWAS is the appropriate approach Gene sets are not tissue/gene-set stratified annotations of common variants with appropriate LD Scores (e.g., rare-variant or sequencing-based signals), which LD score regression does not accommodate

skills.description: Use when peak-picked and grouped 1D NMR spectra show suspicious peak groups (e.g., peaks from different metabolites merged), and you need to detect misgrouping via silhouette values plus SNR before regrouping.
skills.name: snr-based-peak-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: snr-based-peak-quality-evaluation Use when peak-picked and grouped 1D NMR spectra show suspicious peak groups (e.g., peaks from different metabolites merged), and you need to detect misgrouping via silhouette values plus SNR before regrouping. Input is raw spectra that have not yet been peak-picked and grouped by getWaveletPeaks/PeakGrouper — silhouette evaluation operates on peak groups, not raw spectra Groups already show high mean silhouette values — regrouping is unnecessary and the peak-filling step alone may mitigate the issue Evaluate peak-group quality in speaq 2.0 by computing per-group mean silhouette values with SilhouetR and cross-checking them against peak signal-to-noise ratios, so that grouping errors (low silhouette despite high SNR) can be flagged and then fixed with regroupR. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Evaluate peak-group quality in speaq 2.0 by computing per-group mean silhouette values with SilhouetR and cross-checking them against peak signal-to-noise ratios, so that grouping errors (low silhouette despite high SNR) can be flagged and then fixed with regroupR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spectra that have not yet been peak-picked and grouped by getWaveletPeaks/PeakGrouper — silhouette evaluation operates on peak groups, not raw spectra Groups already show high mean silhouette values — regrouping is unnecessary and the peak-filling step alone may mitigate the issue

skills.description: Use when validating a deep-learning spectral reconstruction on simulated or experimental MSI/SCMS data where the ground-truth or high-resolution spectra are available, and the accepted criterion is a reported SNR gain in dB over the noisy reference using a small fraction of the acquisition time.
skills.name: snr-gain-quantification
skills.search_text: snr-gain-quantification Use when validating a deep-learning spectral reconstruction on simulated or experimental MSI/SCMS data where the ground-truth or high-resolution spectra are available, and the accepted criterion is a reported SNR gain in dB over the noisy reference using a small fraction of the acquisition time. When no ground-truth (simulated) or high-resolution reference spectra exist — e.g. purely exploratory single-cell runs with no paired clean acquisition — since the SNR gain cannot be referenced against a known signal baseline. When the goal is already to reconstruct the spectra (train the autoencoder/regressor); this skill is a downstream evaluation step, not the reconstruction training itself. For non-MS imaging modalities or non-transient raw data (e.g. HPLC-MS centroids) where the transient-based SNR definition used by MEISTER does not directly apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantify the signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) improvement delivered by the MEISTER deep-learning spectral reconstruction by comparing reconstructed versus noisy/short-transient mass spectra, expressed as a decibel gain. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-024-02171-3
skills.summary: Quantify the signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) improvement delivered by the MEISTER deep-learning spectral reconstruction by comparing reconstructed versus noisy/short-transient mass spectra, expressed as a decibel gain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth (simulated) or high-resolution reference spectra exist — e.g. purely exploratory single-cell runs with no paired clean acquisition — since the SNR gain cannot be referenced against a known signal baseline. When the goal is already to reconstruct the spectra (train the autoencoder/regressor); this skill is a downstream evaluation step, not the reconstruction training itself. For non-MS imaging modalities or non-transient raw data (e.g. HPLC-MS centroids) where the transient-based SNR definition used by MEISTER does not directly apply.

skills.description: Use when a raw MALDI mass spectrum has been peak-detected (e.g. via CWT ridges from MassSpecWavelet) and the resulting peak list contains noise-level peaks that must be dropped before writing a final filtered peak table.
skills.name: snr-threshold-peak-filtering
skills.search_text: snr-threshold-peak-filtering Use when a raw MALDI mass spectrum has been peak-detected (e.g. via CWT ridges from MassSpecWavelet) and the resulting peak list contains noise-level peaks that must be dropped before writing a final filtered peak table. The input is raw, unprocessed spectral intensity data rather than an already peak-detected list — filtering should follow peak detection, not replace it. The spectrum has been processed with subMALDI's own peak detection algorithms rather than MassSpecWavelet CWT ridges, where no SNR.Th flags are produced. The goal is peak alignment or normalization of replicate spectra to an m/z grid rather than noise-peak removal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A fine-grained filtering step that removes noise-level peaks from a mass-spectrometry peak list by retaining only peaks whose signal-to-noise ratio exceeds a threshold (SNR.Th = 3 in the subMALDI/MassSpecWavelet vignette workflow), applied after CWT-based peak detection on raw MALDI spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02694
skills.summary: A fine-grained filtering step that removes noise-level peaks from a mass-spectrometry peak list by retaining only peaks whose signal-to-noise ratio exceeds a threshold (SNR.Th = 3 in the subMALDI/MassSpecWavelet vignette workflow), applied after CWT-based peak detection on raw MALDI spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unprocessed spectral intensity data rather than an already peak-detected list — filtering should follow peak detection, not replace it. The spectrum has been processed with subMALDI's own peak detection algorithms rather than MassSpecWavelet CWT ridges, where no SNR.Th flags are produced. The goal is peak alignment or normalization of replicate spectra to an m/z grid rather than noise-peak removal.

skills.description: Use when positive-mode qMSI lipid images contain [M+H]+ adducts isobarically overlapped by [M+Na]+ species of the same lipid class that cannot be mass-resolved (Δm/z 0.0025), especially in datasets with prevalent M+Na adducts.
skills.name: sodium-protonated-adduct-ratio-correction
skills.search_text: sodium-protonated-adduct-ratio-correction Use when positive-mode qMSI lipid images contain [M+H]+ adducts isobarically overlapped by [M+Na]+ species of the same lipid class that cannot be mass-resolved (Δm/z 0.0025), especially in datasets with prevalent M+Na adducts. Datasets acquired with sufficient resolving power to mass-resolve the [M+H]+/[M+Na]+ pair directly — the Δm/z of 0.0025 requires a minimum resolution of 600,000, so if the instrument achieves this the signals need no ratio-based deconvolution Lipid classes flagged as unsupported by the H/Na overlap correction — the images must be passed through unchanged rather than corrected Datasets with no prevalent [M+Na]+ adducts, where the optional Na/H overlap correction adds no value over raw or Type II-corrected images LipidQMap's pixel-wise correction that removes the isobaric contribution of [M+Na]+ lipid ions (Δm/z 0.0025 from [M+H]+, requiring ~600,000 resolution to separate) from protonated-channel ion images using sodiated-to-protonated adduct ratios measured from co-sprayed lipid class-specific standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.10.15.682422
skills.summary: LipidQMap's pixel-wise correction that removes the isobaric contribution of [M+Na]+ lipid ions (Δm/z 0.0025 from [M+H]+, requiring ~600,000 resolution to separate) from protonated-channel ion images using sodiated-to-protonated adduct ratios measured from co-sprayed lipid class-specific standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets acquired with sufficient resolving power to mass-resolve the [M+H]+/[M+Na]+ pair directly — the Δm/z of 0.0025 requires a minimum resolution of 600,000, so if the instrument achieves this the signals need no ratio-based deconvolution Lipid classes flagged as unsupported by the H/Na overlap correction — the images must be passed through unchanged rather than corrected Datasets with no prevalent [M+Na]+ adducts, where the optional Na/H overlap correction adds no value over raw or Type II-corrected images

skills.description: Use when building a weighted co-accumulation/co-expression network (e.g., WGCNA) from a metabolite peak-area or expression matrix and a scale-free topology fit must be used to pick the soft-thresholding power before dynamic tree cutting.
skills.name: soft-threshold-power-selection
skills.search_text: soft-threshold-power-selection Use when building a weighted co-accumulation/co-expression network (e.g., WGCNA) from a metabolite peak-area or expression matrix and a scale-free topology fit must be used to pick the soft-thresholding power before dynamic tree cutting. Input is already a module assignment or module eigengene table — the power has already been chosen and no network needs to be built. Only two-group differential abundance testing is needed (use MetMiner's statistical-analysis/MDAtoolkits tools instead of WGCNA). The data are raw RNA-seq read counts that first require vst normalization and noise filtering per the WGCNA FAQ; power selection should follow that preprocessing, not precede it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selection of the WGCNA soft-thresholding power from the scale-free topology fit prior to module detection in the MetMiner iterative WGCNA strategy, which is used to screen biomarker metabolites from plant metabolomics peak-area matrices. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Selection of the WGCNA soft-thresholding power from the scale-free topology fit prior to module detection in the MetMiner iterative WGCNA strategy, which is used to screen biomarker metabolites from plant metabolomics peak-area matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a module assignment or module eigengene table — the power has already been chosen and no network needs to be built. Only two-group differential abundance testing is needed (use MetMiner's statistical-analysis/MDAtoolkits tools instead of WGCNA). The data are raw RNA-seq read counts that first require vst normalization and noise filtering per the WGCNA FAQ; power selection should follow that preprocessing, not precede it.

skills.description: Use when you have SIRIUS top-50 formula candidates for multiple related compounds in an LC-MS/MS dataset and need to build the node/edge graph (softmax likelihoods, tree-similarity edges, anchor bonuses) that ZODIAC's Bayesian model requires.
skills.name: softmax-candidate-likelihood-modeling
skills.search_text: softmax-candidate-likelihood-modeling Use when you have SIRIUS top-50 formula candidates for multiple related compounds in an LC-MS/MS dataset and need to build the node/edge graph (softmax likelihoods, tree-similarity edges, anchor bonuses) that ZODIAC's Bayesian model requires. Isolated single-compound formula annotation with no related compounds in the dataset — ZODIAC's prior derives from reciprocal plausibility (tree similarity) within an LC-MS/MS dataset, so there are no informative edges Precursor data lacking high-quality adduct annotations established during preprocessing, since adduct information cannot be reliably deduced from isotope pattern and MS/MS data alone Workflows locked to stock OpenMS — reproducibility requires the modified OpenMS 2.4.0 plus a separate patch file from bio.informatik.uni-jena.de/data/ http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Constructs ZODIAC's weighted assignment graph by assigning each SIRIUS top-50 molecular formula candidate (plus a dummy node) a softmax likelihood over candidate scores, and weighting edges with fragmentation-tree similarity scores and spectral-library anchor bonuses for downstream Gibbs-sampling reranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: Constructs ZODIAC's weighted assignment graph by assigning each SIRIUS top-50 molecular formula candidate (plus a dummy node) a softmax likelihood over candidate scores, and weighting edges with fragmentation-tree similarity scores and spectral-library anchor bonuses for downstream Gibbs-sampling reranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Isolated single-compound formula annotation with no related compounds in the dataset — ZODIAC's prior derives from reciprocal plausibility (tree similarity) within an LC-MS/MS dataset, so there are no informative edges Precursor data lacking high-quality adduct annotations established during preprocessing, since adduct information cannot be reliably deduced from isotope pattern and MS/MS data alone Workflows locked to stock OpenMS — reproducibility requires the modified OpenMS 2.4.0 plus a separate patch file from bio.informatik.uni-jena.de/data/

skills.description: Use when a paper claims a quantitative quality threshold for a package's test suite (e.g. 'code coverage above 90%') and the claim must be independently reproduced by executing the tests and measuring coverage.
skills.name: software-quality-metric-comparison
skills.search_text: software-quality-metric-comparison Use when a paper claims a quantitative quality threshold for a package's test suite (e.g. 'code coverage above 90%') and the claim must be independently reproduced by executing the tests and measuring coverage. The paper reports no quantitative quality metric (e.g. only qualitative claims about functionality) — there is no threshold to reproduce. The quality metric concerns runtime performance or accuracy of data conversion results rather than test-suite code coverage. The package cannot be installed or its test suite is not shipped/published, making coverage measurement impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3377 Verifies a software package's reported software-quality metric — here, unit-test code coverage above 90% — by running the full automated test suite under coverage.py and comparing the measured total against the published figure. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13070842
skills.summary: Verifies a software package's reported software-quality metric — here, unit-test code coverage above 90% — by running the full automated test suite under coverage.py and comparing the measured total against the published figure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The paper reports no quantitative quality metric (e.g. only qualitative claims about functionality) — there is no threshold to reproduce. The quality metric concerns runtime performance or accuracy of data conversion results rather than test-suite code coverage. The package cannot be installed or its test suite is not shipped/published, making coverage measurement impossible.

skills.search_text: soil-metagenome-bgc-novelty-assessment Use when metagenomic or uncultivated-bacterial BGC predictions need to be compared against a curated reference set of known-function BGCs (MIBiG 2.0) to quantify novelty or correlate BGC abundance with other genomic features. When the goal is de novo BGC detection rather than novelty assessment against known clusters — use antiSMASH/ClusterFinder mining directly instead of the MIBiG homology baseline When the query BGCs are already annotated with known function and deposited in MIBiG; the novelty comparison is circular for curated entries When comparing against general-purpose candidate-BGC databases such as IMG-ABC or antiSMASH-DB, which store many thousands of unvalidated candidate BGCs rather than BGCs of known function http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A method for assessing how novel soil-metagenome-derived Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs) are by using MIBiG as the homology baseline, as demonstrated by Crits-Cristoph et al. (uncultivated soil bacteria) and Bahram et al. (fungal antibacterial BGCs). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz882
skills.summary: A method for assessing how novel soil-metagenome-derived Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs) are by using MIBiG as the homology baseline, as demonstrated by Crits-Cristoph et al. (uncultivated soil bacteria) and Bahram et al. (fungal antibacterial BGCs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo BGC detection rather than novelty assessment against known clusters — use antiSMASH/ClusterFinder mining directly instead of the MIBiG homology baseline When the query BGCs are already annotated with known function and deposited in MIBiG; the novelty comparison is circular for curated entries When comparing against general-purpose candidate-BGC databases such as IMG-ABC or antiSMASH-DB, which store many thousands of unvalidated candidate BGCs rather than BGCs of known function

skills.description: Use when a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table includes blank control groups (e.g., solvent blanks, media blanks) and experimental samples may carry contamination or carryover that must be removed before downstream analysis.
skills.name: solvent-blank-contamination-filtering
skills.search_text: solvent-blank-contamination-filtering Use when a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table includes blank control groups (e.g., solvent blanks, media blanks) and experimental samples may carry contamination or carryover that must be removed before downstream analysis. The input is raw MS/MS spectra rather than a pre-processed Progenesis peak table with sample-group metadata. The dataset has no blank or control group to compare against, so no group is overrepresented by carryover. The quality issue is mispicked isotopic peaks or non-reproducible features across technical replicates, which mpactr addresses with filter_mispicked_ions() and filter_cv() instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Identifies and removes background components—such as solvent-blank carryover and media-blank contaminants—from LC-MS/MS peak tables using mpactr's filter_group(), which flags features whose abundance exceeds a user-defined threshold in a specified sample group. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00997-24
skills.summary: Identifies and removes background components—such as solvent-blank carryover and media-blank contaminants—from LC-MS/MS peak tables using mpactr's filter_group(), which flags features whose abundance exceeds a user-defined threshold in a specified sample group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw MS/MS spectra rather than a pre-processed Progenesis peak table with sample-group metadata. The dataset has no blank or control group to compare against, so no group is overrepresented by carryover. The quality issue is mispicked isotopic peaks or non-reproducible features across technical replicates, which mpactr addresses with filter_mispicked_ions() and filter_cv() instead.

skills.description: Use when comparing experimental NMR mixture spectra against pure-component reference spectra in DMSO-d6 and you need chemical shift deviations free of active-hydrogen and residual solvent (DMSO-d6/HDO) contamination.
skills.name: solvent-signal-exclusion-dmso-d6-hdo
skills.search_text: solvent-signal-exclusion-dmso-d6-hdo Use when comparing experimental NMR mixture spectra against pure-component reference spectra in DMSO-d6 and you need chemical shift deviations free of active-hydrogen and residual solvent (DMSO-d6/HDO) contamination. Spectra recorded in a deuterated solvent other than DMSO-d6 — the specific exclusion of DMSO-d6/HDO residual signals will not match the artifact peaks present The goal is pure compound identification/prediction with the trained pSCNN model rather than quantifying chemical shift deviation statistics Only synthetic/augmented training spectra are being processed, where no real residual solvent peaks exist to exclude http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 A peak-pair filtering step that removes active-hydrogen signals and residual solvent peaks (DMSO-d6/HDO) from mixture-vs-reference NMR spectra before quantifying chemical shift deviations. This ensures the deviation statistics (mean −0.0016 ppm, SD 0.0077 ppm, mean ± 1.5 × SD interval of (−0.013, 0.010) ppm) reflect genuine chemical shift variation rather than solvent artifacts. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: A peak-pair filtering step that removes active-hydrogen signals and residual solvent peaks (DMSO-d6/HDO) from mixture-vs-reference NMR spectra before quantifying chemical shift deviations. This ensures the deviation statistics (mean −0.0016 ppm, SD 0.0077 ppm, mean ± 1.5 × SD interval of (−0.013, 0.010) ppm) reflect genuine chemical shift variation rather than solvent artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra recorded in a deuterated solvent other than DMSO-d6 — the specific exclusion of DMSO-d6/HDO residual signals will not match the artifact peaks present The goal is pure compound identification/prediction with the trained pSCNN model rather than quantifying chemical shift deviation statistics Only synthetic/augmented training spectra are being processed, where no real residual solvent peaks exist to exclude

skills.description: Use when candidate structures for a detected peak already have both MS/MS spectral scores and ROASMI retention-order probabilities P_ij, and you need a posterior-ranked top-k annotation list per peak.
skills.name: spanning-tree-ensemble-posterior-computation
skills.search_text: spanning-tree-ensemble-posterior-computation Use when candidate structures for a detected peak already have both MS/MS spectral scores and ROASMI retention-order probabilities P_ij, and you need a posterior-ranked top-k annotation list per peak. skills.description: Use when Gibbs sampling must be run over a large weighted similarity graph (e.g., compounds × candidate molecular formulas with pairwise ZODIAC scores) and a full conditional recomputation over all nodes is too slow; the sparse conditional update touches only flipped-node neighborhoods.
skills.name: sparse-graph-conditional-probability-update
skills.search_text: sparse-graph-conditional-probability-update Use when Gibbs sampling must be run over a large weighted similarity graph (e.g., compounds × candidate molecular formulas with pairwise ZODIAC scores) and a full conditional recomputation over all nodes is too slow; the sparse conditional update touches only flipped-node neighborhoods. The similarity graph is dense — the O(|V(c)| + deg(u) + deg(v)) conditional update degenerates toward a full-graph recomputation and the sparsity-based speedup vanishes. No pairwise scores exist between compounds' candidate formulas (e.g., only isolated per-compound SIRIUS candidate lists), so the network-based conditional structure that Lemma 2 exploits is absent. An exact (non-sampled) posterior or MAP assignment is required — this skill implements stochastic Gibbs sampling, not deterministic optimization. ZODIAC's engineered Gibbs sampler updates each compound's molecular formula assignment using only the pairwise potentials incident to the flipped compound and its neighbors, computed in O(|V(c)| + deg(u) + deg(v)) time per conditional (Lemma 2). This exploits the sparsity of the formula-similarity network to make Gibbs sampling very swift in practice. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42256-020-00234-6
skills.summary: ZODIAC's engineered Gibbs sampler updates each compound's molecular formula assignment using only the pairwise potentials incident to the flipped compound and its neighbors, computed in O(|V(c)| + deg(u) + deg(v)) time per conditional (Lemma 2). This exploits the sparsity of the formula-similarity network to make Gibbs sampling very swift in practice.
