skills.name: spatial-metabolomics-pixel-clustering
skills.search_text: spatial-metabolomics-pixel-clustering Use when you have a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (rows = pixels with X/Y coordinates, columns = m/z ion intensities) and need to segment the tissue section into spatial regions or compare them to anatomical references. Input is raw IMS spectral data rather than an already-extracted feature matrix of X/Y coordinates and m/z intensities (SMAnalyst requires the feature matrix CSV format) The goal is metabolite-level (ion co-expression) clustering or marker ion discovery rather than pixel-level tissue segmentation The tissue is expected to have far fewer anatomical domains than the default demonstration (k=25 was tuned to mouse brain divisions); an inappropriate k can force spurious spatial categories http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Pixel-level clustering of imaging-MS spatial metabolomics feature matrices (e.g., via SMAnalyst's Seurat-based or UMAP-kmeans algorithms) to segment tissue into anatomical regions, as demonstrated by reproducing 25 spatially heterogeneous clusters on a mouse brain coronal section concordant with the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Pixel-level clustering of imaging-MS spatial metabolomics feature matrices (e.g., via SMAnalyst's Seurat-based or UMAP-kmeans algorithms) to segment tissue into anatomical regions, as demonstrated by reproducing 25 spatially heterogeneous clusters on a mouse brain coronal section concordant with the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw IMS spectral data rather than an already-extracted feature matrix of X/Y coordinates and m/z intensities (SMAnalyst requires the feature matrix CSV format) The goal is metabolite-level (ion co-expression) clustering or marker ion discovery rather than pixel-level tissue segmentation The tissue is expected to have far fewer anatomical domains than the default demonstration (k=25 was tuned to mouse brain divisions); an inappropriate k can force spurious spatial categories

skills.description: Use when working with an AFADESI- or MALDI-style spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels x m/z ions) and you need to partition pixels into user-defined tissue vs. background regions to assess acquisition quality or tissue-enriched ion expression.
skills.name: spatial-metabolomics-pixel-region-classification
skills.search_text: spatial-metabolomics-pixel-region-classification Use when working with an AFADESI- or MALDI-style spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels x m/z ions) and you need to partition pixels into user-defined tissue vs. background regions to assess acquisition quality or tissue-enriched ion expression. Input is raw MS imaging data (e.g., imzML) that has not yet been peak-picked into a pixel-by-ion peak table matrix The acquisition has no background pixels outside the tissue (e.g., tightly cropped datasets), so background regions cannot be delineated The goal is ion identity annotation rather than pixel/region quality assessment — region classification does not assign m/z identities http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classify pixels of a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix into tissue and background regions by lasso-based delineation on the median pixel intensity image, enabling downstream background-consistency (QVP2) and tissue-enriched ion (QVP3) quality checks in SMQVP. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Classify pixels of a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix into tissue and background regions by lasso-based delineation on the median pixel intensity image, enabling downstream background-consistency (QVP2) and tissue-enriched ion (QVP3) quality checks in SMQVP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS imaging data (e.g., imzML) that has not yet been peak-picked into a pixel-by-ion peak table matrix The acquisition has no background pixels outside the tissue (e.g., tightly cropped datasets), so background regions cannot be delineated The goal is ion identity annotation rather than pixel/region quality assessment — region classification does not assign m/z identities

skills.description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion intensities, e.g., MALDI/DESI imaging MS) must be QC-assessed and noise-filtered before annotation, clustering, or differential analysis.
skills.name: spatial-metabolomics-quality-control
skills.search_text: spatial-metabolomics-quality-control Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion intensities, e.g., MALDI/DESI imaging MS) must be QC-assessed and noise-filtered before annotation, clustering, or differential analysis. Input is raw vendor imaging-MS data (e.g., imzML/RAW) that has not yet been peak-picked into a feature matrix — the skill expects an already-processed pixels × ions CSV The matrix has already passed noise filtering at threshold ≥30 and background removal; re-running would double-filter ions Analysis goal is metabolite annotation or differential analysis rather than pre-analysis quality assessment — use SMAnalyst's annotation or spatial/differential modules instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 SMAnalyst's four-module quality-control workflow for spatial metabolomics feature matrices: background consistency evaluation (QC1), noise ion filtering via a spatstat quadrat-test noise score with default threshold ≥30 (QC2), intensity distribution analysis (QC3), and missing value assessment (QC4). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: SMAnalyst's four-module quality-control workflow for spatial metabolomics feature matrices: background consistency evaluation (QC1), noise ion filtering via a spatstat quadrat-test noise score with default threshold ≥30 (QC2), intensity distribution analysis (QC3), and missing value assessment (QC4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vendor imaging-MS data (e.g., imzML/RAW) that has not yet been peak-picked into a feature matrix — the skill expects an already-processed pixels × ions CSV The matrix has already passed noise filtering at threshold ≥30 and background removal; re-running would double-filter ions Analysis goal is metabolite annotation or differential analysis rather than pre-analysis quality assessment — use SMAnalyst's annotation or spatial/differential modules instead

skills.description: Use when you hold paired SM (imzML, e.g. MALDI-TOF) and ST (e.g. 10X Visium) measurements from the same or adjacent tissue section and need metabolite signals mapped onto ST spots for joint clustering or WNN integration.
skills.name: spatial-metabolomics-transcriptomics-alignment
skills.search_text: spatial-metabolomics-transcriptomics-alignment Use when you hold paired SM (imzML, e.g. MALDI-TOF) and ST (e.g. 10X Visium) measurements from the same or adjacent tissue section and need metabolite signals mapped onto ST spots for joint clustering or WNN integration. Input is a single modality only (SM or ST alone) — use Cardinal/Seurat modality-specific workflows instead of cross-omic alignment SM data are single-cell resolution and you want sub-spot analysis — SpaMTP bins pixels into capture spots (e.g. 55 µm Visium), so pixel-level spatial detail is lost Data were generated on high-resolution instruments where METASPACE/pySM-style annotation is expected; SpaMTP's spot-mapping pipeline targets TOF-style SM data that those tools do not cover http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Spatial co-registration and spot-binning of MALDI-TOF spatial metabolomics (SM) pixels onto paired spatial transcriptomics (ST) capture areas — e.g. 55 µm 10X Visium spots — using SpaMTP to build a single Seurat object holding both 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays for downstream multi-omic integration. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Spatial co-registration and spot-binning of MALDI-TOF spatial metabolomics (SM) pixels onto paired spatial transcriptomics (ST) capture areas — e.g. 55 µm 10X Visium spots — using SpaMTP to build a single Seurat object holding both 'SPM' and 'SPT' assays for downstream multi-omic integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single modality only (SM or ST alone) — use Cardinal/Seurat modality-specific workflows instead of cross-omic alignment SM data are single-cell resolution and you want sub-spot analysis — SpaMTP bins pixels into capture spots (e.g. 55 µm Visium), so pixel-level spatial detail is lost Data were generated on high-resolution instruments where METASPACE/pySM-style annotation is expected; SpaMTP's spot-mapping pipeline targets TOF-style SM data that those tools do not cover

skills.description: Use when LC–MS runs were acquired across spatially arranged samples (e.g. swabs of a 96-well plate, plant surfaces, keypads) and the goal is a molecular intensity map localized onto an image or 3D model of the sampled surface.
skills.name: spatial-molecular-cartography-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-molecular-cartography-visualization Use when LC–MS runs were acquired across spatially arranged samples (e.g. swabs of a 96-well plate, plant surfaces, keypads) and the goal is a molecular intensity map localized onto an image or 3D model of the sampled surface. Input is already a feature quantification table from another metabolomics tool (Optimus expects raw mzML/mzXML runs and its own OpenMS-based detection) Data are direct-infusion or non-spatial batch LC–MS runs with no spatial mapping goal — Optimus supports such data but 'ili mapping and this skill are unnecessary Definitive (MSI level-1) molecular identification is required — the workflow only provides putative mz-RT level-2 annotation and MS/MS validation is not provided in Optimus http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reproduce spatial molecular maps from spatially sampled LC–MS untargeted metabolomics data by running the Optimus KNIME/OpenMS workflow for feature detection, alignment and mz-RT annotation, then visualizing feature intensities in 2D/3D with the 'ili app (and inspecting features with OptimusViewer). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nprot.2017.122
skills.summary: Reproduce spatial molecular maps from spatially sampled LC–MS untargeted metabolomics data by running the Optimus KNIME/OpenMS workflow for feature detection, alignment and mz-RT annotation, then visualizing feature intensities in 2D/3D with the 'ili app (and inspecting features with OptimusViewer).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature quantification table from another metabolomics tool (Optimus expects raw mzML/mzXML runs and its own OpenMS-based detection) Data are direct-infusion or non-spatial batch LC–MS runs with no spatial mapping goal — Optimus supports such data but 'ili mapping and this skill are unnecessary Definitive (MSI level-1) molecular identification is required — the workflow only provides putative mz-RT level-2 annotation and MS/MS validation is not provided in Optimus

skills.description: Use when per-cell intensity tables and centroid coordinates are available and the goal is to quantify neighborhood-dependent behavior (e.g., metabolite competition between tumor cells and T-cells) as a function of proximity to CD31+ endothelial cells or cell-cell contact.
skills.name: spatial-neighborhood-computation-from-cell-centroids
skills.search_text: spatial-neighborhood-computation-from-cell-centroids Use when per-cell intensity tables and centroid coordinates are available and the goal is to quantify neighborhood-dependent behavior (e.g., metabolite competition between tumor cells and T-cells) as a function of proximity to CD31+ endothelial cells or cell-cell contact. Single-cell segmentation or intensity extraction has not yet been performed — the skill requires per-cell intensity tables and centroids as input, not raw TOF-SIMS/IMC images IMC and SIMS modalities are not yet registered to a common coordinate frame (notebook 02 registration must precede spatial neighborhood computation) The analysis goal is cell-type clustering or VAE joint embedding rather than spatial neighbor-dependent metabolite competition http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Builds per-cell spatial neighbor sets from single-cell centroid coordinates extracted from joint TOF-SIMS/IMC imaging, enabling local metabolite competition analysis (own intensity / mean neighbor intensity) between cell types such as CD68+/T-cells and tumor cells in lung tumor tissue. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43917-5
skills.summary: Builds per-cell spatial neighbor sets from single-cell centroid coordinates extracted from joint TOF-SIMS/IMC imaging, enabling local metabolite competition analysis (own intensity / mean neighbor intensity) between cell types such as CD68+/T-cells and tumor cells in lung tumor tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell segmentation or intensity extraction has not yet been performed — the skill requires per-cell intensity tables and centroids as input, not raw TOF-SIMS/IMC images IMC and SIMS modalities are not yet registered to a common coordinate frame (notebook 02 registration must precede spatial neighborhood computation) The analysis goal is cell-type clustering or VAE joint embedding rather than spatial neighbor-dependent metabolite competition

skills.description: Use when a joint spatial transcriptomics-metabolomics embedding must be quantitatively compared against competing integration tools, requiring metric computation and a ranked overall-score table.
skills.name: spatial-omics-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: spatial-omics-benchmark-evaluation Use when a joint spatial transcriptomics-metabolomics embedding must be quantitatively compared against competing integration tools, requiring metric computation and a ranked overall-score table. Input data is at single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data Integration involves more than two modalities — SpatialMETA currently only supports integration of two modalities No ground-truth labels are available for biological conservation scoring, since evaluation depends on manually annotated H&E histological labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Benchmark a joint ST-SM integration embedding (e.g. SpatialMETA) against vertical-integration baselines by computing four scIB-style metric families — reconstruction accuracy, continuity, marker, and biological conservation — on the same eleven ccRCC, GBM, and mouse brain samples, then ranking methods by an aggregated overall score. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a joint ST-SM integration embedding (e.g. SpatialMETA) against vertical-integration baselines by computing four scIB-style metric families — reconstruction accuracy, continuity, marker, and biological conservation — on the same eleven ccRCC, GBM, and mouse brain samples, then ranking methods by an aggregated overall score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is at single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data Integration involves more than two modalities — SpatialMETA currently only supports integration of two modalities No ground-truth labels are available for biological conservation scoring, since evaluation depends on manually annotated H&E histological labels

skills.description: Use when no real paired spatial-omics sections exist but a ground-truth reference is needed to evaluate spot-to-spot integration or label transfer methods such as haCCA against morphological alignment baselines like STUtility.
skills.name: spatial-omics-benchmark-generation
skills.search_text: spatial-omics-benchmark-generation Use when no real paired spatial-omics sections exist but a ground-truth reference is needed to evaluate spot-to-spot integration or label transfer methods such as haCCA against morphological alignment baselines like STUtility. When a real paired spatial transcriptome + MALDI-MSI dataset from the same or neighboring tissue sections is already available — use the real data instead of synthesising pseudo-pairs. When the downstream integration method relies on true shared genes or shared spots rather than high-correlated feature pairs across modalities. When higher-resolution spatial data (e.g. sub-cellular or single-cell resolution) is required, since haCCA and this pseudo-pair generation have not been evaluated on higher resolution data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Generates pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome / MALDI-MSI benchmark data by splitting gene features into disjoint pseudo-spatial-transcriptome and pseudo-MALDI-MSI sections and applying Gaussian translation to coordinates of one section, mimicking the morphological disagreement observed between neighboring tissue sections. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.20.608773
skills.summary: Generates pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome / MALDI-MSI benchmark data by splitting gene features into disjoint pseudo-spatial-transcriptome and pseudo-MALDI-MSI sections and applying Gaussian translation to coordinates of one section, mimicking the morphological disagreement observed between neighboring tissue sections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a real paired spatial transcriptome + MALDI-MSI dataset from the same or neighboring tissue sections is already available — use the real data instead of synthesising pseudo-pairs. When the downstream integration method relies on true shared genes or shared spots rather than high-correlated feature pairs across modalities. When higher-resolution spatial data (e.g. sub-cellular or single-cell resolution) is required, since haCCA and this pseudo-pair generation have not been evaluated on higher resolution data.

skills.description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixel × ion intensities, e.g. AFAD-ESI+ 100 um mouse brain section) has been ion-clustered and clusters must be labeled/validated against anatomical regions like cortex or tissue edges.
skills.name: spatial-pattern-annotation-against-brain-anatomy
skills.search_text: spatial-pattern-annotation-against-brain-anatomy Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixel × ion intensities, e.g. AFAD-ESI+ 100 um mouse brain section) has been ion-clustered and clusters must be labeled/validated against anatomical regions like cortex or tissue edges. The goal is pixel-level tissue region clustering rather than metabolite-level co-expression annotation — SMAnalyst provides separate pixel clustering algorithms (Seurat-LV, Seurat-LM, Seurat-SLM, UMAP-kmeans) for that purpose Input is raw spectra or peak-picked data rather than the required SMAnalyst feature matrix format (pixel coordinates + ion intensity columns) The goal is metabolite identity annotation against databases (HMDB/KEGG/LIPIDMAPS) via mass accuracy/isotope/adduct scoring — that is SMAnalyst's annotation scoring module, not spatial pattern annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Annotates metabolite-level spatial co-expression clusters (SpaGene within SMAnalyst) of a mouse brain MSI feature matrix against gross tissue anatomy — verifying that resolved spatial expression patterns match anatomical regions such as cerebral cortex (high-expression) and tissue edge regions. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Annotates metabolite-level spatial co-expression clusters (SpaGene within SMAnalyst) of a mouse brain MSI feature matrix against gross tissue anatomy — verifying that resolved spatial expression patterns match anatomical regions such as cerebral cortex (high-expression) and tissue edge regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pixel-level tissue region clustering rather than metabolite-level co-expression annotation — SMAnalyst provides separate pixel clustering algorithms (Seurat-LV, Seurat-LM, Seurat-SLM, UMAP-kmeans) for that purpose Input is raw spectra or peak-picked data rather than the required SMAnalyst feature matrix format (pixel coordinates + ion intensity columns) The goal is metabolite identity annotation against databases (HMDB/KEGG/LIPIDMAPS) via mass accuracy/isotope/adduct scoring — that is SMAnalyst's annotation scoring module, not spatial pattern annotation

skills.description: Use when a peak table from spatial metabolomics data (pixels x m/z) contains mass-difference pairs matching known adducts (M+H, M+K, M+Na) and you must confirm which pairs co-localize spatially before assigning adduct annotations.
skills.name: spatial-pearson-correlation-of-ion-images
skills.search_text: spatial-pearson-correlation-of-ion-images Use when a peak table from spatial metabolomics data (pixels x m/z) contains mass-difference pairs matching known adducts (M+H, M+K, M+Na) and you must confirm which pairs co-localize spatially before assigning adduct annotations. Input is raw MS imaging data (e.g., imzML) rather than a preprocessed peak table matrix — SMQVP requires the peak table as input You need to distinguish isotopic peaks rather than adduct pairs — SMQVP provides a separate isotopic peak ratio module for that task Peaks lack meaningful spatial co-structure (e.g., merged or pooled samples with no pixel-level coordinates), making spatial correlation uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Pearson correlation between the spatial intensity profiles (ion images) of pairs of m/z peaks to confirm candidate adduct relationships, as implemented in SMQVP's adduct ion ratio module (QVP8) on AFADESI mouse brain data. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Computes Pearson correlation between the spatial intensity profiles (ion images) of pairs of m/z peaks to confirm candidate adduct relationships, as implemented in SMQVP's adduct ion ratio module (QVP8) on AFADESI mouse brain data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS imaging data (e.g., imzML) rather than a preprocessed peak table matrix — SMQVP requires the peak table as input You need to distinguish isotopic peaks rather than adduct pairs — SMQVP provides a separate isotopic peak ratio module for that task Peaks lack meaningful spatial co-structure (e.g., merged or pooled samples with no pixel-level coordinates), making spatial correlation uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when you have per-pixel probabilistic class scores from a trained classifier applied to mass spectrometry imaging data and need to map predicted labels and classification uncertainty back into image space to inspect tumor-margin heterogeneity.
skills.name: spatial-prediction-map-reconstruction
skills.search_text: spatial-prediction-map-reconstruction Use when you have per-pixel probabilistic class scores from a trained classifier applied to mass spectrometry imaging data and need to map predicted labels and classification uncertainty back into image space to inspect tumor-margin heterogeneity. When the input data has not yet been classified by massNet and only raw spectra are available — run the classifier first to obtain per-spectrum probabilities. When the goal is peak identification or m/z annotation rather than spatial visualization of predictions — use the msiPL/VAE pipeline instead. When the MSI data is not spatially rastered (e.g., single-spectrum or bulk measurements) — there is no image space to reconstruct into. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3444 Reconstructs massNet's per-spectrum probabilistic class predictions (normal vs. tumor) back into the original image space of MALDI FT-ICR MSI data, producing spatially resolved prediction maps and per-pixel classification uncertainty maps that reveal elevated uncertainty at the tumor margin. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Reconstructs massNet's per-spectrum probabilistic class predictions (normal vs. tumor) back into the original image space of MALDI FT-ICR MSI data, producing spatially resolved prediction maps and per-pixel classification uncertainty maps that reveal elevated uncertainty at the tumor margin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input data has not yet been classified by massNet and only raw spectra are available — run the classifier first to obtain per-spectrum probabilities. When the goal is peak identification or m/z annotation rather than spatial visualization of predictions — use the msiPL/VAE pipeline instead. When the MSI data is not spatially rastered (e.g., single-spectrum or bulk measurements) — there is no image space to reconstruct into.

skills.description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixel X/Y coordinates + per-pixel ion intensities, e.g. 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions from an AFAD-ESI(+) mouse brain IMS section) must be QC-filtered of noise ions before annotation or spatial pattern analysis.
skills.name: spatial-randomness-quadrat-testing
skills.search_text: spatial-randomness-quadrat-testing Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixel X/Y coordinates + per-pixel ion intensities, e.g. 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions from an AFAD-ESI(+) mouse brain IMS section) must be QC-filtered of noise ions before annotation or spatial pattern analysis. The dataset is already QC-filtered or the user's goal is metabolite annotation, clustering, or differential analysis rather than the QC2 noise-ion filtering step The input lacks spatial pixel coordinates (columns 1-2 X/Y), so no spatial point pattern exists for a quadrat/CSR test The user wants background-consistency evaluation (QC1), intensity distribution (QC3), or missing-value assessment (QC4) instead of noise-ion filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Noise-ion QC step from SMAnalyst that scores each ion's spatial distribution against Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR) using the spatstat quadrat test, converts p-values to -log10 noise scores, and filters ions with scores below the default threshold of 30. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Noise-ion QC step from SMAnalyst that scores each ion's spatial distribution against Complete Spatial Randomness (CSR) using the spatstat quadrat test, converts p-values to -log10 noise scores, and filters ions with scores below the default threshold of 30.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is already QC-filtered or the user's goal is metabolite annotation, clustering, or differential analysis rather than the QC2 noise-ion filtering step The input lacks spatial pixel coordinates (columns 1-2 X/Y), so no spatial point pattern exists for a quadrat/CSR test The user wants background-consistency evaluation (QC1), intensity distribution (QC3), or missing-value assessment (QC4) instead of noise-ion filtering

skills.description: Use when an integrated SpaMTP Seurat object (paired SM/ST assays) already has per-cluster differential metabolites and genes, and the goal is region-level pathway enrichment or pathway-network interpretation across spatial regions.
skills.name: spatial-region-differential-analyte-interpretation
skills.search_text: spatial-region-differential-analyte-interpretation Use when an integrated SpaMTP Seurat object (paired SM/ST assays) already has per-cluster differential metabolites and genes, and the goal is region-level pathway enrichment or pathway-network interpretation across spatial regions. The input is raw m/z data without metabolite annotations or differential metabolite/gene results per cluster — the annotation and FindAllDEMs steps must precede pathway interpretation The goal is metabolite annotation refinement (e.g. CalculateAnnotationStatistics, RefineLipids) rather than downstream regional pathway-level interpretation The dataset has no spatial region/cluster structure to contrast (e.g. a single bulk ROI), so regional enrichment between lesioned and intact areas cannot be defined Regional interpretation of spatial metabolomics/transcriptomics differences in SpaMTP: over-representation (Fisher's exact) and rank-based (GSEA-like) pathway enrichment plus Enrichment Map network construction on integrated SM-ST data, as demonstrated on the Parkinson's mouse brain case study. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Regional interpretation of spatial metabolomics/transcriptomics differences in SpaMTP: over-representation (Fisher's exact) and rank-based (GSEA-like) pathway enrichment plus Enrichment Map network construction on integrated SM-ST data, as demonstrated on the Parkinson's mouse brain case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw m/z data without metabolite annotations or differential metabolite/gene results per cluster — the annotation and FindAllDEMs steps must precede pathway interpretation The goal is metabolite annotation refinement (e.g. CalculateAnnotationStatistics, RefineLipids) rather than downstream regional pathway-level interpretation The dataset has no spatial region/cluster structure to contrast (e.g. a single bulk ROI), so regional enrichment between lesioned and intact areas cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted Cardinal segmentation of an MSI tissue section (e.g. imzML-derived peak data from pig fetus liver/heart sections) and need ranked lists of peaks enriched or absent in each spatial segment.
skills.name: spatial-segment-tstatistic-extraction
skills.search_text: spatial-segment-tstatistic-extraction Use when you have a fitted Cardinal segmentation of an MSI tissue section (e.g. imzML-derived peak data from pig fetus liver/heart sections) and need ranked lists of peaks enriched or absent in each spatial segment. The goal is supervised image classification into pre-defined classes with cross-validated error estimation rather than characterizing segments of an unsupervised segmentation. Input is raw or unprocessed spectra — Cardinal's pre-processing (normalize, smooth, reduceBaseline, peakPick/peakAlign) must be run first so topFeatures() operates on aligned peak features. No fitted segmentation exists yet; topFeatures() requires the fitted segmentation object as input. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Extracts per-segment differential ion statistics from a fitted Cardinal spatial segmentation by applying topFeatures() to compute t-statistics for every m/z feature, then labeling each peak per segment as enriched (positive t) or absent (negative t) relative to the mean spectrum. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv146
skills.summary: Extracts per-segment differential ion statistics from a fitted Cardinal spatial segmentation by applying topFeatures() to compute t-statistics for every m/z feature, then labeling each peak per segment as enriched (positive t) or absent (negative t) relative to the mean spectrum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is supervised image classification into pre-defined classes with cross-validated error estimation rather than characterizing segments of an unsupervised segmentation. Input is raw or unprocessed spectra — Cardinal's pre-processing (normalize, smooth, reduceBaseline, peakPick/peakAlign) must be run first so topFeatures() operates on aligned peak features. No fitted segmentation exists yet; topFeatures() requires the fitted segmentation object as input.

skills.description: Use when you have a pixel-by-ion feature matrix from imaging MS (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ion peaks) and need anatomically meaningful pixel clusters or region-of-interest definitions to benchmark or replace web-tool clustering.
skills.name: spatial-shrunken-centroids-pixel-clustering
skills.search_text: spatial-shrunken-centroids-pixel-clustering Use when you have a pixel-by-ion feature matrix from imaging MS (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ion peaks) and need anatomically meaningful pixel clusters or region-of-interest definitions to benchmark or replace web-tool clustering. You are already working inside SMAnalyst and can use its built-in pixel clustering algorithms (Seurat-LV, Seurat-LM, Seurat-SLM, UMAP-kmeans) instead of switching to R/Cardinal The input is raw imaging MS data rather than a preprocessed feature matrix — Cardinal shrunken centroids in this workflow expects the pixel-by-ion intensity table http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Apply Cardinal's spatial shrunken centroids method in R to assign pixels of a spatial metabolomics feature matrix into spatially coherent clusters that map to anatomical regions (e.g., 25 categories on a mouse brain section), providing cluster-defined ROIs for downstream differential analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Apply Cardinal's spatial shrunken centroids method in R to assign pixels of a spatial metabolomics feature matrix into spatially coherent clusters that map to anatomical regions (e.g., 25 categories on a mouse brain section), providing cluster-defined ROIs for downstream differential analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are already working inside SMAnalyst and can use its built-in pixel clustering algorithms (Seurat-LV, Seurat-LM, Seurat-SLM, UMAP-kmeans) instead of switching to R/Cardinal The input is raw imaging MS data rather than a preprocessed feature matrix — Cardinal shrunken centroids in this workflow expects the pixel-by-ion intensity table

skills.description: Use when haCCA integration has produced a b_predict object whose MALDI-MSI metabolite features sit on transcriptome spot coordinates and you need to visualise a metabolite against the spot background to co-localise it with a gene.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptome-background-plotting
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptome-background-plotting Use when haCCA integration has produced a b_predict object whose MALDI-MSI metabolite features sit on transcriptome spot coordinates and you need to visualise a metabolite against the spot background to co-localise it with a gene. skills.description: Use when building omics co-occurrence or multi-omics networks from a feature (species/metabolite/gene) abundance table in MetaNet, and you need defensible correlation thresholds instead of an arbitrary similarity cutoff before downstream topology, module, or keystone analyses.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-edge-filtering
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-edge-filtering Use when building omics co-occurrence or multi-omics networks from a feature (species/metabolite/gene) abundance table in MetaNet, and you need defensible correlation thresholds instead of an arbitrary similarity cutoff before downstream topology, module, or keystone analyses. You only want raw pairwise similarity for exploratory heatmaps or clustering without building a filtered graph — c_net_calculate alone suffices and c_net_build's pruning is unnecessary. The relationship of interest is non-linear or indirect; the article's discussion notes correlation-based network construction may overlook such associations. skills.summary: Prunes a MetaNet co-occurrence network to statistically robust edges by keeping only Spearman correlations with |ρ| above a chosen cutoff (e.g. 0.6–0.65) and Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p-values below 0.05, so the retained graph reflects strong, significant co-occurrence rather than arbitrary similarity.

skills.description: Use when several normalization variants (e.g., tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) have been applied to the same dataset and you need to visualize how similarly they rank metabolites by differential abundance signal.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-heatmap-clustering
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-heatmap-clustering Use when several normalization variants (e.g., tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) have been applied to the same dataset and you need to visualize how similarly they rank metabolites by differential abundance signal. skills.description: Use when you must rank candidate molecular structures for tandem mass spectra from a structure prediction model and compare that ranking against established tools (SIRIUS4, MetFrag) with statistical significance testing.
skills.name: spectra-candidate-ranking-evaluation
skills.search_text: spectra-candidate-ranking-evaluation Use when you must rank candidate molecular structures for tandem mass spectra from a structure prediction model and compare that ranking against established tools (SIRIUS4, MetFrag) with statistical significance testing. When the query spectra are high-resolution from instruments like Orbitrap or FT-ICR — the article notes TeFT is not compared favourably there and models like MassGenie or MSNovelist are geared to high mass accuracy. When the spectra are recorded in negative ion mode — TeFT was trained only on positive-mode (H+) spectra, restricting its applicability. When candidate structures need not be ranked because the identity is already known — the ranking step requires an unresolved candidate list under the MW/element constraints. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark and statistically compare spectral structure-annotation tools — e.g. TeFT against SIRIUS4 (CSI:FingerID) and MetFrag — on identical MS/MS spectrum sets under matched database constraints, reporting correct-structure and top-ranked similarity percentages plus Wilcoxon signed-rank significance. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0
skills.summary: Benchmark and statistically compare spectral structure-annotation tools — e.g. TeFT against SIRIUS4 (CSI:FingerID) and MetFrag — on identical MS/MS spectrum sets under matched database constraints, reporting correct-structure and top-ranked similarity percentages plus Wilcoxon signed-rank significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query spectra are high-resolution from instruments like Orbitrap or FT-ICR — the article notes TeFT is not compared favourably there and models like MassGenie or MSNovelist are geared to high mass accuracy. When the spectra are recorded in negative ion mode — TeFT was trained only on positive-mode (H+) spectra, restricting its applicability. When candidate structures need not be ranked because the identity is already known — the ranking step requires an unresolved candidate list under the MW/element constraints.

skills.description: Use when two MRS basis sets (e.g., an MRSCloud-simulated set and a reference set such as MARSS or LCModel) must be compared metabolite-by-metabolite and their basis functions first need to be placed on a shared spectral grid.
skills.name: spectral-basis-function-grid-alignment
skills.search_text: spectral-basis-function-grid-alignment Use when two MRS basis sets (e.g., an MRSCloud-simulated set and a reference set such as MARSS or LCModel) must be compared metabolite-by-metabolite and their basis functions first need to be placed on a shared spectral grid. Comparing MRSCloud output against the LCModel phantom-measured basis set (press_te30_3t_01a.basis) — waveforms and timings of that vendor-provided set are not well documented, making grid-aligned comparison of limited interpretability The target sequence is STEAM or SPECIAL localization — these are not implemented in MRSCloud, so no MRSCloud basis functions exist to align Field strengths other than 3T — the current MRSCloud version only supports 3T basis set generation http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Aligns simulated MRS metabolite basis functions from different sources (e.g., MRSCloud density-matrix simulations vs. MARSS-generated basis sets) onto a common spectral grid so per-metabolite agreement can be quantified with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and normalized root-mean-square differences (NRMS). metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: Aligns simulated MRS metabolite basis functions from different sources (e.g., MRSCloud density-matrix simulations vs. MARSS-generated basis sets) onto a common spectral grid so per-metabolite agreement can be quantified with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and normalized root-mean-square differences (NRMS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing MRSCloud output against the LCModel phantom-measured basis set (press_te30_3t_01a.basis) — waveforms and timings of that vendor-provided set are not well documented, making grid-aligned comparison of limited interpretability The target sequence is STEAM or SPECIAL localization — these are not implemented in MRSCloud, so no MRSCloud basis functions exist to align Field strengths other than 3T — the current MRSCloud version only supports 3T basis set generation

skills.description: Use when you have a simulated MRS basis set and a phantom-acquired or vendor-provided basis set for the same sequence/field (e.g., 3T PRESS TE 30 ms) and need per-metabolite agreement metrics such as ICCs.
skills.name: spectral-basis-set-comparison
skills.search_text: spectral-basis-set-comparison Use when you have a simulated MRS basis set and a phantom-acquired or vendor-provided basis set for the same sequence/field (e.g., 3T PRESS TE 30 ms) and need per-metabolite agreement metrics such as ICCs. When comparing two simulated basis sets (e.g., MRSCloud vs FID-A or MARSS) where no line broadening to match a phantom-measured set is needed — the article handles those as separate comparisons with ICCs >= 0.98 and >= 0.96 respectively When the vendor/sequence parameters do not match — the existing MRSCloud version only supports 3T basis sets, and the comparison assumes unedited PRESS TE 30 ms When you need a rigorous validation of simulated vs measured basis sets — the article notes the comparison is challenging because limited information is available about the LCModel basis set acquisition and its waveforms/timings likely differ from the simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies agreement between density-matrix-simulated MRS metabolite basis functions (e.g., MRSCloud unedited PRESS TE 30 ms at 3T) and an experimentally acquired basis set (LCModel phantom-measured press_te30_3t_01a.basis) by computing per-metabolite intraclass correlation coefficients in R/RStudio. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/mrm.29370
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between density-matrix-simulated MRS metabolite basis functions (e.g., MRSCloud unedited PRESS TE 30 ms at 3T) and an experimentally acquired basis set (LCModel phantom-measured press_te30_3t_01a.basis) by computing per-metabolite intraclass correlation coefficients in R/RStudio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing two simulated basis sets (e.g., MRSCloud vs FID-A or MARSS) where no line broadening to match a phantom-measured set is needed — the article handles those as separate comparisons with ICCs >= 0.98 and >= 0.96 respectively When the vendor/sequence parameters do not match — the existing MRSCloud version only supports 3T basis sets, and the comparison assumes unedited PRESS TE 30 ms When you need a rigorous validation of simulated vs measured basis sets — the article notes the comparison is challenging because limited information is available about the LCModel basis set acquisition and its waveforms/timings likely differ from the simulation

skills.name: spectral-bin-assignment-mapping
skills.search_text: spectral-bin-assignment-mapping Use when you have calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra from a Bruker IVDr 600 MHz spectrometer and need to map 24 predefined spin-system bins to metabolite signals in a 22-metabolite panel. Input spectra are not calibrated 1D 1H NMR data from a Bruker IVDr 600 MHz instrument (e.g. 2D-Jres or CPMG-only datasets without SMolESY preprocessing). The target metabolite list extends beyond the 22 metabolites validated in this algorithm, since bins were defined for exactly 24 spin systems from a plasma/serum cohort. You already have a feature/intensity table and need statistical modelling (e.g. PCA of relative concentration values) rather than per-spectrum spin-system assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0003 Assigns 1H NMR spin-system patterns to metabolite signals by searching the SMolESY-processed spectrum within predefined spectral windows (bins) for 24 1H NMR spin systems, enabling direct integration of assigned components without complex deconvolution or baseline fitting. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00113
skills.summary: Assigns 1H NMR spin-system patterns to metabolite signals by searching the SMolESY-processed spectrum within predefined spectral windows (bins) for 24 1H NMR spin systems, enabling direct integration of assigned components without complex deconvolution or baseline fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not calibrated 1D 1H NMR data from a Bruker IVDr 600 MHz instrument (e.g. 2D-Jres or CPMG-only datasets without SMolESY preprocessing). The target metabolite list extends beyond the 22 metabolites validated in this algorithm, since bins were defined for exactly 24 spin systems from a plasma/serum cohort. You already have a feature/intensity table and need statistical modelling (e.g. PCA of relative concentration values) rather than per-spectrum spin-system assignment.

skills.search_text: spectral-binning-and-totalarea-normalization Use when aligned, window-selected spectra (spectra_df rows indexed by ppm) must be converted to a fixed feature table for statistical analysis or classification, e.g. after Icoshift alignment in a Protomix 1H-NMR metabolomics pipeline. skills.summary: Reduce preprocessed 1H-NMR spectra (after window_selection and peak alignment) into a compact binned feature table and scale intensities with TotalArea normalization, using Protomix's binning and normalization functions on a 70-sample prostate cancer/BPH urine dataset.

skills.description: Use when a curated set of annotated and labeled HR-MS/MS spectra of compounds of interest ('relevant') and others ('other') is available and you need a trained ensemble that classifies new MGF spectra into 'relevant' vs 'other' for natural-product prioritization.
skills.name: spectral-classifier-ensemble-training
skills.search_text: spectral-classifier-ensemble-training Use when a curated set of annotated and labeled HR-MS/MS spectra of compounds of interest ('relevant') and others ('other') is available and you need a trained ensemble that classifies new MGF spectra into 'relevant' vs 'other' for natural-product prioritization. The training dataset is highly imbalanced between 'relevant' and 'other' spectra — the AnnoMe package explicitly cannot resolve this failure mode and classification will most often not be successful. You have no annotated, labeled training spectra of compounds of interest and others — the classifiers must first be trained on a large set of labeled MS/MS spectra. You only have few 'relevant'-class spectra (well below the ~1000-spectra regime the paper derived) and expect stable recall across training-set reductions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Train an ensemble of MS/MS spectrum classifiers (LDA, NN, SVM) with cross-validation and multiple random seeds on MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings, then aggregate per-classifier outputs into a majority vote that labels each HR-MS/MS spectrum as 'relevant' or 'other'. This is the core model-training step of the AnnoMe workflow for user-defined substance-class prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbag111
skills.summary: Train an ensemble of MS/MS spectrum classifiers (LDA, NN, SVM) with cross-validation and multiple random seeds on MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings, then aggregate per-classifier outputs into a majority vote that labels each HR-MS/MS spectrum as 'relevant' or 'other'. This is the core model-training step of the AnnoMe workflow for user-defined substance-class prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training dataset is highly imbalanced between 'relevant' and 'other' spectra — the AnnoMe package explicitly cannot resolve this failure mode and classification will most often not be successful. You only want to inspect ready-made example data in the browser dashboard — then only msFeaST_Dashboard_bundle.html and an existing .json are needed and no integration is performed. skills.description: Use when reconstructing or validating peak-detection code for simulated 1D 1H, 2D J-Res or COSY metabolomic NMR spectra where peaks must be localized as clusters above a user-defined intensity threshold before downstream spectral simulation.
skills.name: spectral-cluster-marking-and-filtering
skills.search_text: spectral-cluster-marking-and-filtering Use when reconstructing or validating peak-detection code for simulated 1D 1H, 2D J-Res or COSY metabolomic NMR spectra where peaks must be localized as clusters above a user-defined intensity threshold before downstream spectral simulation. Input is raw unprocessed spectra where no user-defined intensity threshold has been specified — the method requires a threshold value to locate maxima. The goal is de novo 2D peak picking on the full 2D matrix (J-Res or COSY) rather than 1D-projected cluster localization via skyline or diagonal projection. Spectra are real experimental data where protein background or other artefacts dominate; MetAssimulo 2.0's cluster localization is designed for its simulated spectral structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Locates peaks in simulated NMR spectra by grouping adjacent points above a user-defined intensity threshold into clusters and filtering clusters that fail criteria, applying the same cluster-localization pathway to 1D 1H, J-Res (skyline projection) and COSY (diagonal projection) spectra in MetAssimulo 2.0. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf045
skills.summary: Locates peaks in simulated NMR spectra by grouping adjacent points above a user-defined intensity threshold into clusters and filtering clusters that fail criteria, applying the same cluster-localization pathway to 1D 1H, J-Res (skyline projection) and COSY (diagonal projection) spectra in MetAssimulo 2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unprocessed spectra where no user-defined intensity threshold has been specified — the method requires a threshold value to locate maxima. The goal is de novo 2D peak picking on the full 2D matrix (J-Res or COSY) rather than 1D-projected cluster localization via skyline or diagonal projection. Spectra are real experimental data where protein background or other artefacts dominate; MetAssimulo 2.0's cluster localization is designed for its simulated spectral structures.

skills.search_text: spectral-cluster-medoid-selection Use when you have GLEAMS cluster assignments (GLEAMS_cluster.npy) and medoid indexes (GLEAMS_cluster_medoids.npy) and need to pick one representative spectrum per cluster of previously unidentified spectra for downstream search/annotation. Input spectra are already individually identified by a database search (e.g., the 185 million PSMs at 1% FDR obtained using MSGF+), so clustering/medoid propagation adds no annotations. You have fewer spectra than the minimum cluster size (2) or no precomputed GLEAMS embeddings/clusters — you must first run 'gleams embed' and 'gleams cluster' before medoids exist. You need per-spectrum modifications rather than a single representative identification per cluster; medoid propagation assigns one peptide label to all members. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Select representative (medoid) spectra from MS/MS spectral clusters — produced by GLEAMS embedding-based clustering — so that a single spectrum search per cluster (e.g., ANN-SoLo open modification search) can annotate all member spectra at once. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Select representative (medoid) spectra from MS/MS spectral clusters — produced by GLEAMS embedding-based clustering — so that a single spectrum search per cluster (e.g., ANN-SoLo open modification search) can annotate all member spectra at once.

skills.description: Use when comparing spectral clustering outputs of MS/MS spectra (e.g., MGF-derived clusters with charge 2-3 precursors) against peptide assignments to quantify completeness, incorrect clustering ratio, and clustered spectra ratio.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-quality-evaluation Use when comparing spectral clustering outputs of MS/MS spectra (e.g., MGF-derived clusters with charge 2-3 precursors) against peptide assignments to quantify completeness, incorrect clustering ratio, and clustered spectra ratio. Input is a single clustering result with no peptide identifications available — entropy-based completeness cannot be computed without peptide labels. The goal is runtime/speed benchmarking rather than clustering quality (HyperSpec's speedup claims, e.g., 21 million spectra in 24 min vs. 4 h, are measured separately). Spectra have not been preprocessed consistently across tools (e.g., differing precursor-peak removal or peak-count limits), which invalidates cross-tool quality comparisons. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Evaluates MS/MS spectral clustering quality using clustered spectra ratio, incorrect clustering ratio, and entropy-based completeness against peptide identifications, as done for HyperSpec on the draft human proteome Data set-E (PXD000561). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00612
skills.summary: Evaluates MS/MS spectral clustering quality using clustered spectra ratio, incorrect clustering ratio, and entropy-based completeness against peptide identifications, as done for HyperSpec on the draft human proteome Data set-E (PXD000561).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single clustering result with no peptide identifications available — entropy-based completeness cannot be computed without peptide labels. The goal is runtime/speed benchmarking rather than clustering quality (HyperSpec's speedup claims, e.g., 21 million spectra in 24 min vs. 4 h, are measured separately). Spectra have not been preprocessed consistently across tools (e.g., differing precursor-peak removal or peak-count limits), which invalidates cross-tool quality comparisons.

skills.description: Use when profiling the runtime breakdown of CPU-only spectral clustering tools on large MS/MS data sets (e.g. PXD000561 MGF files) to quantify the preprocessing bottleneck before benchmarking a faster method such as HyperSpec.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-tool-configuration
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-tool-configuration Use when profiling the runtime breakdown of CPU-only spectral clustering tools on large MS/MS data sets (e.g. PXD000561 MGF files) to quantify the preprocessing bottleneck before benchmarking a faster method such as HyperSpec. Input spectra are already preprocessed consensus spectra rather than raw MGF peak files — the bottleneck being profiled exists in raw-file preprocessing, not consensus handling. The goal is clustering quality comparison rather than stage-wise runtime profiling — this skill measures time distribution, not incorrect clustering ratio or completeness. The target tool is GPU-accelerated (e.g. HyperSpec) — its preprocessing modules are optimized to bypass the CPU preprocessing bottleneck being benchmarked here. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Configure and run state-of-the-art spectral clustering tools (MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, MaRaCluster) on MGF-formatted MS/MS data to measure stage-wise runtime profiles, with spectrum preprocessing benchmarked against its 20-90% share of overall runtime. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00612
skills.summary: Configure and run state-of-the-art spectral clustering tools (MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, MaRaCluster) on MGF-formatted MS/MS data to measure stage-wise runtime profiles, with spectrum preprocessing benchmarked against its 20-90% share of overall runtime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are already preprocessed consensus spectra rather than raw MGF peak files — the bottleneck being profiled exists in raw-file preprocessing, not consensus handling. The goal is clustering quality comparison rather than stage-wise runtime profiling — this skill measures time distribution, not incorrect clustering ratio or completeness. The target tool is GPU-accelerated (e.g. HyperSpec) — its preprocessing modules are optimized to bypass the CPU preprocessing bottleneck being benchmarked here.

skills.search_text: spectral-conditional-molecule-generation Use when you have simulated or measured molecular spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis, or all jointly) and need de novo molecular structure elucidation evaluated by top-1/top-10 exact match rather than retrieval from a fixed library. skills.description: Use when a batch of GC×GC–MS samples has already been peak-picked and annotated (consensus spectra available from GcDUO module III) and you need sample-wise peak areas/intensities that account for between-sample retention-time shifts, i.e. module V data integration.
skills.name: spectral-constraint-optimization
skills.search_text: spectral-constraint-optimization Use when a batch of GC×GC–MS samples has already been peak-picked and annotated (consensus spectra available from GcDUO module III) and you need sample-wise peak areas/intensities that account for between-sample retention-time shifts, i.e. module V data integration. skills.summary: Refine GC×GC–MS peak quantification by re-fitting PARAFAC2 models for each annotated feature across all samples, constraining the mass-spectrum mode to the consensus/library spectrum while allowing the elution profile to vary between samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature was detected in only one sample — module V does not evaluate such features (their data stay in module III results). No annotation/consensus spectrum is available for the feature, so no library spectrum can be imposed as the spectral-mode constraint. The extracted components do not conform to a Gaussian form, which the blind PARAFAC requires.

You only have search-engine scores or no predicted fragment-ion intensity vectors from Prosit — the SA and Prosit-delta require paired observed/predicted intensity vectors The goal is generic PSM rescoring from an existing feature table without spectrum-level similarity features — use ristretto, Percolator, or MS2Rescore directly instead The input is already an FDR-filtered final identification list with no raw spectra or prediction vectors available for recomputation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes the normalized spectral contrast angle (SA) between observed and Prosit-predicted fragment-ion intensity vectors, and derives the inSPIRE Prosit-delta stability score by swapping adjacent residues and recomputing the SA. Low Prosit-delta flags candidate peptide-spectrum matches at risk of being misassigned to similar but incorrect peptide sequences. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/pmic.202300336
