Input is already an annotated lipid feature table without raw MS2/MS3+ spectra — use Peak Finder (from .cdResult peak tables) or Degreaser QC instead Spectra are not lipidomics MSn data or no in silico library exists for the lipid classes of interest — generate a library with the Library Generator first Legacy workflows requiring LipiDex 1 Java-based matching on .mgf/.mzXML without Thermo .raw support — LipiDex 1 is no longer supported http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Spectral library matching for LC-MS/MS lipidomics using LipiDex 2 Spectrum Searcher, which scores experimental MS2 and MS3+ spectra against in silico lipid libraries using dot-product/reverse dot-product scores and spectral purity to assign high-confidence lipid identifications to chromatographic features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Spectral library matching for LC-MS/MS lipidomics using LipiDex 2 Spectrum Searcher, which scores experimental MS2 and MS3+ spectra against in silico lipid libraries using dot-product/reverse dot-product scores and spectral purity to assign high-confidence lipid identifications to chromatographic features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated lipid feature table without raw MS2/MS3+ spectra — use Peak Finder (from .cdResult peak tables) or Degreaser QC instead Spectra are not lipidomics MSn data or no in silico library exists for the lipid classes of interest — generate a library with the Library Generator first Legacy workflows requiring LipiDex 1 Java-based matching on .mgf/.mzXML without Thermo .raw support — LipiDex 1 is no longer supported

skills.description: Use when you have cleaned MGF (or mzML/mzXML/msp/USI) spectra and need all-pairs similarity scores, e.g. cosine or modified cosine, plus matching-peak counts to flag related spectra pairs.
skills.name: spectral-library-matching
skills.search_text: spectral-library-matching Use when you have cleaned MGF (or mzML/mzXML/msp/USI) spectra and need all-pairs similarity scores, e.g. cosine or modified cosine, plus matching-peak counts to flag related spectra pairs. The input spectra have not yet passed metadata cleaning and peak filters (e.g. require_minimum_number_of_peaks, normalize_intensities) — raw noisy spectra will yield unreliable cosine scores You need a fingerprint-informed or retention-time-informed comparison rather than pure peak-list cosine scoring — Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore, or RIAssigner-style methods from the matchms ecosystem are the intended route You want library annotation of a single unknown against a database entry with structure identification, rather than an all-pairs similarity scan within one collection http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Pairwise MS/MS spectral similarity scoring across a reference and query spectrum collection using matchms, e.g. comparing all spectra to all spectra with the cosine-based CosineGreedy score and counting matching peaks per pair. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02411
skills.summary: Pairwise MS/MS spectral similarity scoring across a reference and query spectrum collection using matchms, e.g. comparing all spectra to all spectra with the cosine-based CosineGreedy score and counting matching peaks per pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra have not yet passed metadata cleaning and peak filters (e.g. require_minimum_number_of_peaks, normalize_intensities) — raw noisy spectra will yield unreliable cosine scores You need a fingerprint-informed or retention-time-informed comparison rather than pure peak-list cosine scoring — Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore, or RIAssigner-style methods from the matchms ecosystem are the intended route You want library annotation of a single unknown against a database entry with structure identification, rather than an all-pairs similarity scan within one collection

skills.description: Use when consensus spectra from GC×GC–TOFMS peak picking (e.g. GcDUO $cor_spectra) must be assigned compound identities against an MSP library, with a cosine-similarity cutoff and optional RI window.
skills.name: spectral-library-matching-cosine-similarity
skills.search_text: spectral-library-matching-cosine-similarity Use when consensus spectra from GC×GC–TOFMS peak picking (e.g. GcDUO $cor_spectra) must be assigned compound identities against an MSP library, with a cosine-similarity cutoff and optional RI window. The goal is peak detection or deconvolution — annotation requires already-extracted consensus spectra from procesData; raw 4D arrays must go through ROI selection first. No suitable spectral library exists for the sample matrix (e.g. a compound missing from the in-house library, as with one fruitybeer compound) — matching cannot recover identities absent from the reference. The data are LC-MS or other non-GC×GC–MS acquisitions whose spectra and RI semantics do not match the MSP/EI-fragment assumptions of this workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotate GC × GC–MS features by cosine-similarity matching of consensus spectra against an in-house MSP spectral library, optionally constrained by retention-index tolerance, as implemented in GcDUO's duoID module. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbaf080
skills.summary: Annotate GC × GC–MS features by cosine-similarity matching of consensus spectra against an in-house MSP spectral library, optionally constrained by retention-index tolerance, as implemented in GcDUO's duoID module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peak detection or deconvolution — annotation requires already-extracted consensus spectra from procesData; raw 4D arrays must go through ROI selection first. No suitable spectral library exists for the sample matrix (e.g. a compound missing from the in-house library, as with one fruitybeer compound) — matching cannot recover identities absent from the reference. The data are LC-MS or other non-GC×GC–MS acquisitions whose spectra and RI semantics do not match the MSP/EI-fragment assumptions of this workflow.

skills.description: Use when MZmine-processed LC-HRMS2 DDA features need structural annotation against a natural-products library, especially when taxonomic metadata (e.g., Open Tree of Life ottIDs) can be exploited to reweight spectral matches.
skills.name: spectral-library-matching-isdb-lotus
skills.search_text: spectral-library-matching-isdb-lotus Use when MZmine-processed LC-HRMS2 DDA features need structural annotation against a natural-products library, especially when taxonomic metadata (e.g., Open Tree of Life ottIDs) can be exploited to reweight spectral matches. Input features lack associated MS2 scans (the ENPKG feature filtering keeps only features with an MS2 scan and RT 0.5–8.0 min), so there is nothing to match Samples have no resolvable taxonomic origin, defeating the taxonomic-distance reranking that distinguishes this matching from plain spectral search The data are not LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics spectra (e.g., already-aligned feature tables without spectra, or MS1-only acquisitions) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate MS2 fragmentation spectra from sample-wise LC-HRMS2 metabolomics runs by spectral matching against the ISDB-LOTUS in silico database of natural products, reranking candidate structures by taxonomic proximity and molecular-network annotation propagation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Annotate MS2 fragmentation spectra from sample-wise LC-HRMS2 metabolomics runs by spectral matching against the ISDB-LOTUS in silico database of natural products, reranking candidate structures by taxonomic proximity and molecular-network annotation propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features lack associated MS2 scans (the ENPKG feature filtering keeps only features with an MS2 scan and RT 0.5–8.0 min), so there is nothing to match Samples have no resolvable taxonomic origin, defeating the taxonomic-distance reranking that distinguishes this matching from plain spectral search The data are not LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics spectra (e.g., already-aligned feature tables without spectra, or MS1-only acquisitions)

skills.description: Use when quantifying how many spectra in an MS/MS dataset (e.g., four beer extracts in positive and negative ionization mode) can be identified by library matching, to benchmark novel annotation methods.
skills.name: spectral-library-matching-massbank-nist
skills.search_text: spectral-library-matching-massbank-nist Use when quantifying how many spectra in an MS/MS dataset (e.g., four beer extracts in positive and negative ionization mode) can be identified by library matching, to benchmark novel annotation methods. When the analysis goal is discovering novel or unknown substructures not represented in reference libraries — spectral matching can only recover spectra of previously characterized compounds When neutral-loss information is central to the annotation strategy, since losses are not supported by spectral matching tools and must be omitted http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Benchmark metabolite annotation coverage by matching MS/MS spectra as pseudo-spectra against the Mass Bank and NIST reference libraries, serving as the classical baseline that MS2LDA's motif-based annotation (~3x more annotations) was measured against. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Benchmark metabolite annotation coverage by matching MS/MS spectra as pseudo-spectra against the Mass Bank and NIST reference libraries, serving as the classical baseline that MS2LDA's motif-based annotation (~3x more annotations) was measured against.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is discovering novel or unknown substructures not represented in reference libraries — spectral matching can only recover spectra of previously characterized compounds When neutral-loss information is central to the annotation strategy, since losses are not supported by spectral matching tools and must be omitted

skills.description: Use when an .msp mass spectral library file contains records lacking metadata such as SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, CAS numbers, chemical formula, or molecular weight, and the records need post-processing to enrich them.
skills.name: spectral-library-metadata-annotation
skills.search_text: spectral-library-metadata-annotation Use when an .msp mass spectral library file contains records lacking metadata such as SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, CAS numbers, chemical formula, or molecular weight, and the records need post-processing to enrich them. Records already carry complete, validated metadata — re-annotation will only re-query or duplicate existing fields. The target attribute cannot be derived from any available source attribute or supported service (e.g. no SMILES present for RDKit-based molecular weight computation). The input is not a mass spectral library file in a supported format (MSMetaEnhancer's IO is matchms-based .msp). http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotate mass spectral library records in .msp format by adding missing metadata (SMILES, InChI, CAS numbers, molecular weight) using MSMetaEnhancer, which fetches identifiers from external services (CIR, CTS, PubChem, IDSM, BridgeDb) or computes them locally (e.g., molecular weight from SMILES via RDKit). metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04494
skills.summary: Annotate mass spectral library records in .msp format by adding missing metadata (SMILES, InChI, CAS numbers, molecular weight) using MSMetaEnhancer, which fetches identifiers from external services (CIR, CTS, PubChem, IDSM, BridgeDb) or computes them locally (e.g., molecular weight from SMILES via RDKit).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Records already carry complete, validated metadata — re-annotation will only re-query or duplicate existing fields. The target attribute cannot be derived from any available source attribute or supported service (e.g. no SMILES present for RDKit-based molecular weight computation). The input is not a mass spectral library file in a supported format (MSMetaEnhancer's IO is matchms-based .msp).

skills.description: Use when building a benchmarking or reference set of experimental MS/MS spectra from public spectral libraries (e.g. GNPS) and library entries need filtering, metadata cleaning, and structural ID standardization.
skills.name: spectral-library-metadata-curation
skills.search_text: spectral-library-metadata-curation Use when building a benchmarking or reference set of experimental MS/MS spectra from public spectral libraries (e.g. GNPS) and library entries need filtering, metadata cleaning, and structural ID standardization. When the input is already a curated, single-instrument feature table or a local proprietary spectral library whose entries have already been structurally resolved When the target analysis concerns ubiquitous (primary) metabolites rather than specialized metabolites, since the curated library is biased toward entries with structural identifiers and taxonomy-resolvable sources When spectra were acquired with non-protonated adducts ([M-H]-, [M+Na]+, etc.) that are not part of the [M+H]+ selection applied here http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assemble a clean, structurally resolvable benchmarking set from GNPS public spectral libraries by filtering .mgf entries, cleaning metadata, converting structures to InChIKeys, and removing duplicates/stereoisomers. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Assemble a clean, structurally resolvable benchmarking set from GNPS public spectral libraries by filtering .mgf entries, cleaning metadata, converting structures to InChIKeys, and removing duplicates/stereoisomers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a curated, single-instrument feature table or a local proprietary spectral library whose entries have already been structurally resolved When the target analysis concerns ubiquitous (primary) metabolites rather than specialized metabolites, since the curated library is biased toward entries with structural identifiers and taxonomy-resolvable sources When spectra were acquired with non-protonated adducts ([M-H]-, [M+Na]+, etc.) that are not part of the [M+H]+ selection applied here

skills.description: Use when integrating OMSLs such as GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, or MS-Dial-VS17 and you need to extract harmonized InChIKeys per spectrum to quantify identifier overlap, per-library compound counts, and spectral redundancy.
skills.name: spectral-library-metadata-parsing
skills.search_text: spectral-library-metadata-parsing Use when integrating OMSLs such as GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, or MS-Dial-VS17 and you need to extract harmonized InChIKeys per spectrum to quantify identifier overlap, per-library compound counts, and spectral redundancy. Input is already a single harmonized library in unified format — no cross-library parsing or identifier mapping is needed Spectra lack SMILES and InChI, precursor m/z, and adduct information: FragHub removes such inconsistent spectra, so overlap counts will be biased toward the refined set The goal is collision-energy harmonization — the FragHub workflow explicitly does not address it because of around 70 different nonstandardized formats http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses open mass spectral library files (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV, .XML), extracts and normalizes per-compound chemical identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) with RDKit, and builds an identifier-to-library membership map for cross-OMSL overlap analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02219
skills.summary: Parses open mass spectral library files (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV, .XML), extracts and normalizes per-compound chemical identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) with RDKit, and builds an identifier-to-library membership map for cross-OMSL overlap analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single harmonized library in unified format — no cross-library parsing or identifier mapping is needed Spectra lack SMILES and InChI, precursor m/z, and adduct information: FragHub removes such inconsistent spectra, so overlap counts will be biased toward the refined set The goal is collision-energy harmonization — the FragHub workflow explicitly does not address it because of around 70 different nonstandardized formats

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS molecular network contains an unassigned node (e.g. an unknown m/z like 328.211) sitting in a molecular family alongside library-hit analogs, and you need to reidentify known compounds or localize the modification between known and unknown analogs.
skills.name: spectral-library-node-identification
skills.search_text: spectral-library-node-identification Use when an LC-MS/MS molecular network contains an unassigned node (e.g. an unknown m/z like 328.211) sitting in a molecular family alongside library-hit analogs, and you need to reidentify known compounds or localize the modification between known and unknown analogs. The unknown has no structurally related known analog in the library or network — ModiFinder requires an MS2-known/MS2-unknown pair for spectral alignment Benchmark-style eligibility fails, e.g. precursor mass exceeds 2000 Da or the precursor mass difference between known and unknown is 50% or greater The input is already a fully annotated feature table with no raw MS/MS spectra available for alignment and substructure assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reidentifies known compounds in molecular networks by MS/MS spectral library search, then extends identification to unknown nodes via analog library search, molecular networking, and ModiFinder's MS/MS alignment to localize the structural modification site. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Reidentifies known compounds in molecular networks by MS/MS spectral library search, then extends identification to unknown nodes via analog library search, molecular networking, and ModiFinder's MS/MS alignment to localize the structural modification site.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unknown has no structurally related known analog in the library or network — ModiFinder requires an MS2-known/MS2-unknown pair for spectral alignment Benchmark-style eligibility fails, e.g. precursor mass exceeds 2000 Da or the precursor mass difference between known and unknown is 50% or greater The input is already a fully annotated feature table with no raw MS/MS spectra available for alignment and substructure assignment

skills.description: Use when you must quantify compound-level overlap between a new spectral library and reference open/commercial libraries (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA, mzCloud, NIST23) using first-InChIKey-block set differences.
skills.name: spectral-library-overlap-quantification
skills.search_text: spectral-library-overlap-quantification Use when you must quantify compound-level overlap between a new spectral library and reference open/commercial libraries (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA, mzCloud, NIST23) using first-InChIKey-block set differences. Input is already a per-compound feature/annotation table rather than raw InChIKey identity lists from spectral library records Comparison should be at full-InChIKey (stereospecific, second-block) level rather than the first-14-character skeleton level used here The task is spectral peak/matching overlap rather than compound-identity coverage comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies how many compounds in a spectral library (e.g. MSn Lib's 30,008 unique small molecules) are absent from reference libraries (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA, mzCloud, NIST23) by first-InChIKey-block set operations, and visualizes intersections with UpSet plots and TMAP chemical-space layouts. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0
skills.summary: Quantifies how many compounds in a spectral library (e.g. MSn Lib's 30,008 unique small molecules) are absent from reference libraries (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA, mzCloud, NIST23) by first-InChIKey-block set operations, and visualizes intersections with UpSet plots and TMAP chemical-space layouts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-compound feature/annotation table rather than raw InChIKey identity lists from spectral library records Comparison should be at full-InChIKey (stereospecific, second-block) level rather than the first-14-character skeleton level used here The task is spectral peak/matching overlap rather than compound-identity coverage comparison

skills.description: Use when preparing an independent evaluation set for a spectral-translation model trained on NIST 20 / synthetic ZINC spectra, to prevent train–test compound leakage before computing Acc@k or Tanimoto metrics.
skills.name: spectral-library-overlap-removal-against-training-set
skills.search_text: spectral-library-overlap-removal-against-training-set Use when preparing an independent evaluation set for a spectral-translation model trained on NIST 20 / synthetic ZINC spectra, to prevent train–test compound leakage before computing Acc@k or Tanimoto metrics. When the test library is the same curated NIST 20 experimental set used for training, since overlap removal would remove the finetuning compounds themselves When spectra are MS/MS (precursor-dependent) rather than GC-EI-MS, because the m/z ≤ 500 and ≤ 300-peak thresholds are calibrated for EI spectra When the goal is to report raw library statistics rather than a leakage-free evaluation set — the aggressive filtering (e.g. Cayman 2,262→469) distorts the library's native composition http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 De-leaks held-out EI-MS test libraries (NIST test split, SWGDRUG, Cayman, MONA) by removing compounds that overlap the experimental or synthetic training sets, deuterium-containing compounds, and spectra violating model-specific limits (m/z ≤ 500, ≤ 300 peaks, SMILES ≤ 100 chars). metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.05114
skills.summary: De-leaks held-out EI-MS test libraries (NIST test split, SWGDRUG, Cayman, MONA) by removing compounds that overlap the experimental or synthetic training sets, deuterium-containing compounds, and spectra violating model-specific limits (m/z ≤ 500, ≤ 300 peaks, SMILES ≤ 100 chars).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the test library is the same curated NIST 20 experimental set used for training, since overlap removal would remove the finetuning compounds themselves When spectra are MS/MS (precursor-dependent) rather than GC-EI-MS, because the m/z ≤ 500 and ≤ 300-peak thresholds are calibrated for EI spectra When the goal is to report raw library statistics rather than a leakage-free evaluation set — the aggressive filtering (e.g. Cayman 2,262→469) distorts the library's native composition

skills.description: Use when building an analog-pair benchmark from GNPS MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g., GNPS-MSMLS, NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY_ROUND2_POSITIVE, BERKELEY-LAB) and you need to keep only structurally related pairs with exactly one modification site.
skills.name: spectral-library-pair-eligibility-filtering
skills.search_text: spectral-library-pair-eligibility-filtering Use when building an analog-pair benchmark from GNPS MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g., GNPS-MSMLS, NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY_ROUND2_POSITIVE, BERKELEY-LAB) and you need to keep only structurally related pairs with exactly one modification site. Your data are experimental sample spectra rather than GNPS library compound pairs — the eligibility checks (identical M+H adduct, single modification site) are defined for curated library analogs You permit multiple modification sites between the known and unknown compounds — the RDKit GetSubstructMatch edge check requires exactly one You are refining substructure annotations within a single pair (e.g., MF-R helper exclusion of compounds within 0.5 precursor mass, or MF-O oracle filtering) — that is downstream substructure filtering, not pair-level eligibility screening http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Filters GNPS MS/MS library compound pairs down to structurally valid analog pairs suitable for ModiFinder modification-site evaluation, applying eligibility checks (precursor mass < 2000 Da, mass difference < 50%, identical M+H adduct, exactly one modification site) before running MF-N/MF-R/MF-O scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Filters GNPS MS/MS library compound pairs down to structurally valid analog pairs suitable for ModiFinder modification-site evaluation, applying eligibility checks (precursor mass < 2000 Da, mass difference < 50%, identical M+H adduct, exactly one modification site) before running MF-N/MF-R/MF-O scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are experimental sample spectra rather than GNPS library compound pairs — the eligibility checks (identical M+H adduct, single modification site) are defined for curated library analogs You permit multiple modification sites between the known and unknown compounds — the RDKit GetSubstructMatch edge check requires exactly one You are refining substructure annotations within a single pair (e.g., MF-R helper exclusion of compounds within 0.5 precursor mass, or MF-O oracle filtering) — that is downstream substructure filtering, not pair-level eligibility screening

skills.description: Use when you need to build a structurally grounded analog benchmark from public MS/MS library entries (spectra + SMILES) for modification-site-localization or analog-search evaluation.
skills.name: spectral-library-pair-enumeration
skills.search_text: spectral-library-pair-enumeration Use when you need to build a structurally grounded analog benchmark from public MS/MS library entries (spectra + SMILES) for modification-site-localization or analog-search evaluation. When the goal is analog search over an unknown sample rather than constructing a ground-truth benchmark of structurally related library pairs. When compound pairs lack same M+H adducts or differ by more than one structural modification — these are explicitly filtered out by the pair eligibility criteria. When the input is a single spectrum or a single compound rather than a collection of library entries that can be paired within-library. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Enumerates every within-library compound pair from public GNPS MS/MS reference libraries (GNPS-MSMLS, GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY_ROUND2_POSITIVE, GNPS-NIH-SMALLMOLECULEPHARMACOLOGICALLYACTIVE, BERKELEY-LAB) and applies structural/mass eligibility filters to assemble a benchmark of 12,909 single-modification analog pairs for evaluating ModiFinder's modification site localization. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.4c00061
skills.summary: Enumerates every within-library compound pair from public GNPS MS/MS reference libraries (GNPS-MSMLS, GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY_ROUND2_POSITIVE, GNPS-NIH-SMALLMOLECULEPHARMACOLOGICALLYACTIVE, BERKELEY-LAB) and applies structural/mass eligibility filters to assemble a benchmark of 12,909 single-modification analog pairs for evaluating ModiFinder's modification site localization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is analog search over an unknown sample rather than constructing a ground-truth benchmark of structurally related library pairs. When compound pairs lack same M+H adducts or differ by more than one structural modification — these are explicitly filtered out by the pair eligibility criteria. When the input is a single spectrum or a single compound rather than a collection of library entries that can be paired within-library.

skills.description: Use when you hold MS/MS spectra with SMILES/InChI structural annotations (e.g. a held-out GNPS-derived test set) and must compare similarity measures on retrieving structurally related pairs.
skills.name: spectral-library-pair-retrieval-benchmarking
skills.search_text: spectral-library-pair-retrieval-benchmarking Use when you hold MS/MS spectra with SMILES/InChI structural annotations (e.g. a held-out GNPS-derived test set) and must compare similarity measures on retrieving structurally related pairs. Spectra lack structural annotations (SMILES/InChI), so Tanimoto ground-truth pairs (e.g. threshold 0.6) cannot be computed You need absolute compound identification or discrimination between Tanimoto 0.8–0.9 and a near-complete chemical match, which the paper reports MS2DeepScore cannot reliably resolve Data are embeddings/clustering or uncertainty-filtering tasks rather than retrieval-benchmark comparisons across similarity measures http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks spectral similarity measures (e.g. MS2DeepScore vs. modified Cosine and Spec2Vec) by threshold-sweep precision/recall retrieval of chemically related MS/MS spectrum pairs, using structural Tanimoto similarity from fingerprints as ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks spectral similarity measures (e.g. MS2DeepScore vs. modified Cosine and Spec2Vec) by threshold-sweep precision/recall retrieval of chemically related MS/MS spectrum pairs, using structural Tanimoto similarity from fingerprints as ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra lack structural annotations (SMILES/InChI), so Tanimoto ground-truth pairs (e.g. threshold 0.6) cannot be computed You need absolute compound identification or discrimination between Tanimoto 0.8–0.9 and a near-complete chemical match, which the paper reports MS2DeepScore cannot reliably resolve Data are embeddings/clustering or uncertainty-filtering tasks rather than retrieval-benchmark comparisons across similarity measures

skills.description: Use when query tandem MS spectra must be matched to candidate molecular structures in a database (e.g., GNPS spectral library, DNP, PubChem, LMSD) to identify small molecules or lipids.
skills.name: spectral-library-search
skills.search_text: spectral-library-search Use when query tandem MS spectra must be matched to candidate molecular structures in a database (e.g., GNPS spectral library, DNP, PubChem, LMSD) to identify small molecules or lipids. The query molecules are already represented in a reference spectral library — direct spectral library search is 'the most reliable annotation method' and preferred over in silico database search The spectra require de novo structure prediction of unknown/novel molecules not present in any structure database Molecules are super small (<400 Da) or very heavy (>1000 Da), where existing machine learning scoring approaches perform poorly or are computationally insufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A mass spectral database-search skill for small molecule identification that scores query tandem MS spectra against candidate structures using molDiscovery's learned probabilistic fragmentation model, as applied to GNPS, DNP, LMSD, and PNNL lipid benchmarks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: A mass spectral database-search skill for small molecule identification that scores query tandem MS spectra against candidate structures using molDiscovery's learned probabilistic fragmentation model, as applied to GNPS, DNP, LMSD, and PNNL lipid benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query molecules are already represented in a reference spectral library — direct spectral library search is 'the most reliable annotation method' and preferred over in silico database search The spectra require de novo structure prediction of unknown/novel molecules not present in any structure database Molecules are super small (<400 Da) or very heavy (>1000 Da), where existing machine learning scoring approaches perform poorly or are computationally insufficient

skills.description: Use when query spectra (e.g., MGF files from HEK293 or iPRG2012) must be searched against a large peptide spectral library while allowing arbitrary modifications within a 500 Da precursor mass window.
skills.name: spectral-library-search
skills.search_text: spectral-library-search Use when query spectra (e.g., MGF files from HEK293 or iPRG2012) must be searched against a large peptide spectral library while allowing arbitrary modifications within a 500 Da precursor mass window. When the goal is a standard (closed) search with only unmodified peptides, since the plain dot-product search with a narrow precursor window suffices and open-search subgroup FDR is unnecessary When the intended analysis is sequence database searching rather than spectral library searching (e.g., MSFragger is used here only as a benchmark comparator) When exact (full) nearest neighbor search is required rather than approximate indexing, since ANN results only approach the full-search baseline as trees and inspected nodes increase http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Perform open modification spectral library searching with ANN-SoLo, which uses approximate nearest neighbor indexing, a two-level cascade search, and the shifted dot product to sensitively identify unmodified and modified peptide spectra while strictly controlling FDR. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: Perform open modification spectral library searching with ANN-SoLo, which uses approximate nearest neighbor indexing, a two-level cascade search, and the shifted dot product to sensitively identify unmodified and modified peptide spectra while strictly controlling FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a standard (closed) search with only unmodified peptides, since the plain dot-product search with a narrow precursor window suffices and open-search subgroup FDR is unnecessary When the intended analysis is sequence database searching rather than spectral library searching (e.g., MSFragger is used here only as a benchmark comparator) When exact (full) nearest neighbor search is required rather than approximate indexing, since ANN results only approach the full-search baseline as trees and inspected nodes increase

skills.search_text: spectral-library-search Use when you have an IDSL.IPA-aligned peak table with individual sample peak lists, a reference MS/MS spectral library (e.g. NIST 2020), and you need to quantify how often IDSL.UFA's MS1 isotope-ranked formula hits agree with MS/MS-confirmed compound formulas. skills.summary: Reproduce MS/MS-supported annotation concordance on the ST002044 study by matching aligned peak table MS/MS spectra against the NIST 2020 library, then computing the median-rank distribution of IDSL.UFA molecular formula hits across individual samples to quantify how often the MS/MS-confirmed formula ranks at or near the top (78.75% of 73 confirmed hits had median rank ≤ 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only an MS2/DDA fragmentation file without the MS1 individual and aligned peak tables from IDSL.IPA — IDSL.UFA requires MS1 chromatographic peaklists for isotopic-profile ranking No reference MS/MS library (e.g. NIST 2020) is available, so MS/MS-confirmed compound identities cannot be established to benchmark formula ranks You need structural annotation rather than formula-level concordance — IDSL.UFA does not use MS2 spectra; it annotates only molecular formulas via MS1 isotopic profiles

skills.summary: Annotate an experimental MS/MS spectrum by searching it against a reference spectral library without assuming a single precursor molecular formula: pseudo-denoise the query against every candidate formula within the precursor mass window, then score matches with entropy similarity computed on both raw and denoised spectra.

When the search goal is a standard narrow-mass database search without expected modifications, since the cascade open search and ANN indexing add overhead that a conventional sequence database search (e.g. MSFragger) handles directly When the spectral library is small enough that exhaustive pairwise scoring is tractable, as approximate ANN candidate selection sacrifices recall for speed and may miss true best matches When FDR estimation requires extremely fine-grained subgroups, because FDR filtering is only applied to subgroups containing at least 20 SSMs and small subgroups may underestimate the actual FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Open modification spectral library searching using a two-level cascade with approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexing for candidate selection, followed by scoring with the dot product and shifted dot product and target-decoy FDR filtering, as implemented in ANN-SoLo for fast and sensitive identification of modified peptides. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: Open modification spectral library searching using a two-level cascade with approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexing for candidate selection, followed by scoring with the dot product and shifted dot product and target-decoy FDR filtering, as implemented in ANN-SoLo for fast and sensitive identification of modified peptides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the search goal is a standard narrow-mass database search without expected modifications, since the cascade open search and ANN indexing add overhead that a conventional sequence database search (e.g. MSFragger) handles directly When the spectral library is small enough that exhaustive pairwise scoring is tractable, as approximate ANN candidate selection sacrifices recall for speed and may miss true best matches When FDR estimation requires extremely fine-grained subgroups, because FDR filtering is only applied to subgroups containing at least 20 SSMs and small subgroups may underestimate the actual FDR

skills.search_text: spectral-library-to-mrm-conversion Use when compounds have already been identified in untargeted LC-HRMS/DIA screening and you need to target them sensitively using a pseudo-MRM transition list derived from library MS/MS spectra. skills.description: Use when denoising selected windows of an SMolESY-enhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum whose weak metabolite signals in noisy regions must be recovered for subsequent pattern assignment and direct integration.
skills.name: spectral-moving-average-smoothing
skills.search_text: spectral-moving-average-smoothing Use when denoising selected windows of an SMolESY-enhanced 1D 1H NMR spectrum whose weak metabolite signals in noisy regions must be recovered for subsequent pattern assignment and direct integration. The input is a raw (non-SMolESY-enhanced) 1D 1H NMR or CPMG spectrum whose native line widths must be preserved without resolution enhancement or baseline suppression. The spectral region must retain full native resolution for pattern matching or quantitation that does not tolerate the ~10% s/n cost relative to CPMG. skills.description: Use when a GNPS-style molecular network has MetFrag candidate structures per node, spectral library matches are available as seeds, and you must annotate nodes beyond the first neighbors of those matches.
skills.name: spectral-network-connected-component-traversal
skills.search_text: spectral-network-connected-component-traversal Use when a GNPS-style molecular network has MetFrag candidate structures per node, spectral library matches are available as seeds, and you must annotate nodes beyond the first neighbors of those matches. No MetFrag candidate structures are available — ChemWalker's graph requires structural similarity among in silico fragmentation candidates, not just a spectral network No spectral library matches exist to serve as seed nodes — the walk departs from spectral-match seeds and cannot start without them The goal is direct spectral library matching or first-neighbor propagation (NAP-style local propagation) rather than propagation to distant nodes via random walks Propagates spectral library match annotations across molecular networks by splitting the weighted graph (spectral network + MetFusion-weighted structural similarity among MetFrag candidates) into connected components and running a random walk with restart (pyrwr) from seed nodes, so annotations reach nodes not directly connected to a spectral match — the key limitation of NAP. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad078
skills.summary: Propagates spectral library match annotations across molecular networks by splitting the weighted graph (spectral network + MetFusion-weighted structural similarity among MetFrag candidates) into connected components and running a random walk with restart (pyrwr) from seed nodes, so annotations reach nodes not directly connected to a spectral match — the key limitation of NAP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No MetFrag candidate structures are available — ChemWalker's graph requires structural similarity among in silico fragmentation candidates, not just a spectral network No spectral library matches exist to serve as seed nodes — the walk departs from spectral-match seeds and cannot start without them The goal is direct spectral library matching or first-neighbor propagation (NAP-style local propagation) rather than propagation to distant nodes via random walks

skills.description: Use when you have DEREPLICATOR+ compound–spectrum matches filtered at a score/FDR cutoff and a precomputed GNPS spectral network (clustered MGF), and you need to count metabolite families and additional variants revealed by spectral propagation.
skills.name: spectral-network-propagation-of-identified-metabolites
skills.search_text: spectral-network-propagation-of-identified-metabolites Use when you have DEREPLICATOR+ compound–spectrum matches filtered at a score/FDR cutoff and a precomputed GNPS spectral network (clustered MGF), and you need to count metabolite families and additional variants revealed by spectral propagation. Input spectra have no GNPS molecular networking clusters (no 'Clustered Spectra as MGF' output), so propagation across distance-1/2 clusters is impossible. No identifications pass the FDR = 0% cutoff, so every connected component would lack a seed and propagation would amplify false positives. The target compound classes are outside DEREPLICATOR+'s scope — the article states it 'is not applicable to all the classes of compounds.' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Propagates DEREPLICATOR+ identifications (PSMs with 0% FDR) across a GNPS molecular network (METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 clusters) to annotate structurally related variant spectra in connected components that contain at least one identified spectrum. This expands a small set of dereplicated metabolites into metabolite families and enumerates unsequenced/unnamed variants. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-018-06082-8
skills.summary: Propagates DEREPLICATOR+ identifications (PSMs with 0% FDR) across a GNPS molecular network (METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 clusters) to annotate structurally related variant spectra in connected components that contain at least one identified spectrum. skills.search_text: spectral-patch-segmentation Use when preparing simulated multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis from QM9S) for a Transformer-based spectral encoder that conditions a molecular-structure diffusion model and needs patch-level embeddings rather than point-wise encodings. The downstream model encodes each spectral frequency point individually rather than via a Transformer that consumes patch sequences — patch segmentation would be unnecessary overhead. Only a single spectral modality is available and the analysis does not require cross-spectrum (inter-modality) dependencies; a simpler point-wise encoder may suffice. The spectra are experimental/real measurements of different modality types (e.g. NMR or MS) outside the IR/Raman/UV-Vis scope that the DiffSpectra pipeline was trained on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Segments each type of multi-modal molecular spectrum (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) into patches and projects them with learnable linear transformations plus positional encodings before feeding them to the SpecFormer Transformer encoder, capturing both intra- and inter-spectrum dependencies. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Segments each type of multi-modal molecular spectrum (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) into patches and projects them with learnable linear transformations plus positional encodings before feeding them to the SpecFormer Transformer encoder, capturing both intra- and inter-spectrum dependencies.

skills.description: Use when raw merged MS/MS peak lists (m/z–intensity pairs) must be converted into a uniform binned feature matrix for machine-learning models such as the MetFID fingerprint predictor.
skills.name: spectral-peak-binning
skills.search_text: spectral-peak-binning Use when raw merged MS/MS peak lists (m/z–intensity pairs) must be converted into a uniform binned feature matrix for machine-learning models such as the MetFID fingerprint predictor. The spectra are still raw/unmerged per collision energy — MetFID merges spectra of the same compound at different collision energies first, because cluster analysis showed spectra generated using similar collision energies cluster together and 30 eV was a reasonable cutoff for high/low collision energies. The input is already a fixed-length binned feature table or a spectral_feature_table.csv — re-binning would discard the all-zero bin filtering already applied. Only a handful of spectra need simple library matching — spectral matching does not require constructing an ANN training feature table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Discretizes an MS/MS spectrum's m/z range into prespecified continuous integer bins with accumulated peak intensities as feature values, producing a fixed-length numeric feature table (spectral_feature_table.csv) used to train MetFID's ANN/CNN fingerprint predictor; all-zero bins across the training set are dropped. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Discretizes an MS/MS spectrum's m/z range into prespecified continuous integer bins with accumulated peak intensities as feature values, producing a fixed-length numeric feature table (spectral_feature_table.csv) used to train MetFID's ANN/CNN fingerprint predictor; all-zero bins across the training set are dropped.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are still raw/unmerged per collision energy — MetFID merges spectra of the same compound at different collision energies first, because cluster analysis showed spectra generated using similar collision energies cluster together and 30 eV was a reasonable cutoff for high/low collision energies. Only a handful of spectra need simple library matching — spectral matching does not require constructing an ANN training feature table.

skills.search_text: spectral-peak-binning-and-merging Use when you have per-compound MS/MS spectra (e.g. from MSP files) acquired at several collision energies and need to produce the merged, binarized, neutral-loss-enriched spectrum that ChemEmbed's CNN expects as model input. skills.description: Use when 1D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, 31P, or any nucleus) contain overlapping peaks that must be deconvolved into quantitative signal parameters, e.g. metabolomics or isotope-labeling spectra provided as tabulated text files.
skills.name: spectral-peak-deconvolution
skills.search_text: spectral-peak-deconvolution Use when 1D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, 31P, or any nucleus) contain overlapping peaks that must be deconvolved into quantitative signal parameters, e.g. metabolomics or isotope-labeling spectra provided as tabulated text files. The task is peak integration of well-separated, non-overlapping peaks where a full deconvolution fit adds unnecessary complexity The spectra are not 1D or pseudo-2D NMR (e.g. mass spectra or Raman spectra), which the MultiNMRFit signal models were not designed for A fully automated, GUI-free batch analysis is required without semi-automated peak-picking validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Fit 1D and pseudo-2D NMR spectra with MultiNMRFit to deconvolve overlapping peaks into whole multiplet signal models, extracting intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, and coupling constants with standard-deviation uncertainties. Fitting multiplets rather than individual peaks improves accuracy and precision of estimated parameters. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Fit 1D and pseudo-2D NMR spectra with MultiNMRFit to deconvolve overlapping peaks into whole multiplet signal models, extracting intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, and coupling constants with standard-deviation uncertainties. Fitting multiplets rather than individual peaks improves accuracy and precision of estimated parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is peak integration of well-separated, non-overlapping peaks where a full deconvolution fit adds unnecessary complexity The spectra are not 1D or pseudo-2D NMR (e.g. mass spectra or Raman spectra), which the MultiNMRFit signal models were not designed for A fully automated, GUI-free batch analysis is required without semi-automated peak-picking validation

skills.name: spectral-peak-detection-with-snr-thresholding
skills.search_text: spectral-peak-detection-with-snr-thresholding Use when you have a baseline-corrected spectrum (m/z and intensity columns) and need to discard noise features by flagging peaks whose intensity divided by segment-level noise falls below a user-specified SNR_thresh. Input spectrum is raw and has not yet been baseline-corrected — the SNR thresholding is designed to operate on the output of subMALDI's baseline correction step Input is already an aligned feature/intensity matrix (subMALDI's alignment step aligns processed spectra to an array of all theoretically possible m/z values at a specified resolution, which happens after peak detection) The workflow requires S3/S4 class object infrastructure, e.g. MALDIquant- or MSnbase-style containers — subMALDI intentionally keeps m/z and intensity data unmasked in plain data frames Detects peaks in mass spectrometry spectra by thresholding each candidate peak's signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where noise is estimated as the median absolute deviation (MAD) of intensity within fixed-size spectral segments, as implemented in the subMALDI R package. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02694
skills.summary: Detects peaks in mass spectrometry spectra by thresholding each candidate peak's signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), where noise is estimated as the median absolute deviation (MAD) of intensity within fixed-size spectral segments, as implemented in the subMALDI R package.

skills.search_text: spectral-peak-shift-alignment Use when an MS/MS spectrum of a putatively modified metabolite (e.g. methylated, acetylated, phosphorylated, hydroxylated) fails direct library search and you need to associate it with the -scoring parent library entry via consistent mass shifts. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not yet preprocessed (unnormalized intensities, noise peaks not thresholded) — preprocess first per the MADGEN workflow The downstream model needs a single fixed-length global spectrum vector rather than per-peak tokens queried by graph nodes and edges Working on scaffold retrieval/ranking (contrastive learning stage) rather than the spectra-conditioned generation stage of MADGEN

skills.search_text: spectral-pearson-correlation-comparison Use when you have a simulated 1D 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. MetAssimulo 2.0 blood output) and a corresponding real spectrum, and you need a single numeric similarity score to validate simulation realism. The task is simulating urine or CSF spectra — MetAssimulo's realism enhancement via protein background applies to blood spectra specifically. You need a simulation rather than a similarity assessment — this skill only scores agreement between an existing simulated and real spectrum. The spectra are on incomparable intensity scales or aligned to different chemical-shift axes without prior alignment/preprocessing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Quantifies how closely a simulated 1D 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. a MetAssimulo 2.0 blood plasma simulation with broad protein background) matches a real spectrum by computing the Pearson correlation coefficient between their spectral intensity vectors. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf045
skills.summary: Quantifies how closely a simulated 1D 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. a MetAssimulo 2.0 blood plasma simulation with broad protein background) matches a real spectrum by computing the Pearson correlation coefficient between their spectral intensity vectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is simulating urine or CSF spectra — MetAssimulo's realism enhancement via protein background applies to blood spectra specifically. You need a simulation rather than a similarity assessment — this skill only scores agreement between an existing simulated and real spectrum. The spectra are on incomparable intensity scales or aligned to different chemical-shift axes without prior alignment/preprocessing.

skills.summary: A cleaning step that removes all fragment ions with m/z larger than a metabolic feature's precursor m/z from pseudo MS/MS spectra generated by ms1-id, so that modified cosine similarity can be computed for GNPS2 molecular networking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are conventional acquired MS/MS whose peaks already lie below the precursor m/z — no filtering is needed You only want ms1-id library annotation of pseudo MS/MS spectra (reverse spectral matching), which does not require precursor-bounded peak lists The downstream networking uses a similarity measure that tolerates fragments above the precursor m/z, so modified cosine filtering is unnecessary

skills.search_text: spectral-prediction-benchmark-visualization Use when comparing multiple in silico MS/MS spectral prediction tools on a common test split and you must show how prediction quality degrades as test compounds become structurally dissimilar from training compounds. The comparison is on training-set-adjacent compounds only, not a generalizability/structural-novelty analysis — a simple overall cosine similarity table suffices The reference spectra lack annotated collision energies, so FIORA/ICEBERG/CFM-ID cannot be run under matched collision energy and instrument type The goal is compound identification (candidate ranking), not spectral prediction quality assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks predicted MS/MS spectra (FIORA vs. ICEBERG vs. CFM-ID) against reference spectra using sqrt-weighted cosine similarity, stratified by structural novelty (maximum Tanimoto similarity of each test compound to the training set), and renders the binned median similarity plot with IQR bands as in Fig. 3 of the FIORA paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-57422-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks predicted MS/MS spectra (FIORA vs. ICEBERG vs. CFM-ID) against reference spectra using sqrt-weighted cosine similarity, stratified by structural novelty (maximum Tanimoto similarity of each test compound to the training set), and renders the binned median similarity plot with IQR bands as in Fig. 3 of the FIORA paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison is on training-set-adjacent compounds only, not a generalizability/structural-novelty analysis — a simple overall cosine similarity table suffices The reference spectra lack annotated collision energies, so FIORA/ICEBERG/CFM-ID cannot be run under matched collision energy and instrument type The goal is compound identification (candidate ranking), not spectral prediction quality assessment

skills.search_text: spectral-prediction-ensemble-inference Use when you have a pretrained ESP/MLP/GNN checkpoint, preprocessed NPLIB1 test data, and PubChem-derived candidate sets and need candidate ranking or Rank@K evaluation. skills.search_text: spectral-preprocessing-for-multivariate-analysis Use when a series of raw 1D-NMR spectra (ppm scale + intensity arrays) must be cleaned of phase, baseline, and alignment artefacts before export to multivariate statistical analysis. Input is already a pre-processed spectra matrix or feature table ready for multivariate analysis Data are 2D-NMR or HSQC + GC-MS isotopomer data handled by metabolabpytools' train/predict workflow rather than 1D spectral pre-processing http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A MetaboLabPy-based workflow for pre-processing series of 1D-NMR spectra — phase correction, baseline correction (with cubic-spline and linear-spline gap filling), segmental alignment, spectral scaling, and variance stabilisation — to prepare data matrices for multivariate statistical analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15010048

skills.search_text: spectral-preprocessing-pipeline-execution Use when irregularly-spaced MALDI-MS or ESI-MS replicate spectra are stored as R data frames (m/z in the first column, replicate intensities in adjacent columns) and need averaging, blank subtraction, or full pre-processing without S3/S4 object masking. Spectra are already held in S3/S4 class objects from other R packages (e.g. MALDIquant or MSnbase workflows) and you do not need subMALDI's data-frame-native design The analysis goal is something outside subMALDI's stated scope of organization, pre-processing (smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection), and normalization — e.g. de novo spectral identification or database searching Input is not m/z/intensity spectral data (e.g. already-reduced peak tables or feature matrices), since the pipeline operates on aligned m/z-vs-intensity data frames http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Execute subMALDI's R pipeline to organize, pre-process (smooth, baseline-correct, peak-detect), normalize, average, and blank-subtract irregularly-spaced MALDI-MS/ESI-MS replicate spectra held as plain data frames, keeping m/z and intensity values accessible at every step. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02694

skills.search_text: spectral-preprocessing-qc-verification Use when a raw 1D NMR spectra matrix (samples x ppm points, e.g. 40 wines x 8712 points) has been reduced by peak-picking/grouping/peak filling and the output feature matrix must be validated before downstream statistics. skills.description: Use when MS2/MSn spectra from LC-MS lipidomics runs are being matched to an in silico lipid spectral library and you must reject matches confounded by co-eluting isobaric lipids before annotating features.
skills.name: spectral-purity-assessment-for-lipid-matches
skills.search_text: spectral-purity-assessment-for-lipid-matches Use when MS2/MSn spectra from LC-MS lipidomics runs are being matched to an in silico lipid spectral library and you must reject matches confounded by co-eluting isobaric lipids before annotating features. Input is a raw MS spectrum without any library match or candidate lipid assignment — spectral purity of a match cannot be computed without a matched reference spectrum. Analyzing untargeted metabolomics (non-lipid) features where isobaric co-elution is not the dominant confounder and lipid-specific purity thresholds do not apply. Validating features where the lipid identification comes from retention-time (ECN vs. RT) or dilution-series evidence rather than spectral matching — Degreaser QC evidence types handle those, not purity/dot-product scores. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Assess the purity of MS2/MS3+ lipid spectral matches against co-eluting isobaric species and enforce LipiDex 2 thresholds (≥75% spectral purity, dot product ≥500, reverse dot product ≥700) so that only high-confidence lipid identifications annotate chromatographic features. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Assess the purity of MS2/MS3+ lipid spectral matches against co-eluting isobaric species and enforce LipiDex 2 thresholds (≥75% spectral purity, dot product ≥500, reverse dot product ≥700) so that only high-confidence lipid identifications annotate chromatographic features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw MS spectrum without any library match or candidate lipid assignment — spectral purity of a match cannot be computed without a matched reference spectrum. Analyzing untargeted metabolomics (non-lipid) features where isobaric co-elution is not the dominant confounder and lipid-specific purity thresholds do not apply. Validating features where the lipid identification comes from retention-time (ECN vs. RT) or dilution-series evidence rather than spectral matching — Degreaser QC evidence types handle those, not purity/dot-product scores.

skills.description: Use when processing tandem mass spectra (e.g. large mzML/mzXML collections or mined GNPS data) into quality-stratified subsets—by instrument m/z accuracy, high-intensity signal counts, and redundancy—to form corpora for self-supervised ML.
skills.name: spectral-quality-control-filtering
skills.search_text: spectral-quality-control-filtering Use when processing tandem mass spectra (e.g. large mzML/mzXML collections or mined GNPS data) into quality-stratified subsets—by instrument m/z accuracy, high-intensity signal counts, and redundancy—to form corpora for self-supervised ML. Input spectra are already part of a curated paired reference library (e.g. MoNA or NIST20 with known structures) — annotation-focused training should not discard or re-tier them. The downstream task involves multiply charged precursor ions or negative ionization mode spectra that the GeMS mining scope (positive mode, singly charged precursors) does not cover. You need MS1-level features — the pipeline targets tandem MS/MS spectra and disregards MS1 isotopic patterns and adduct distributions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A QC pipeline from the DreaMS paper that filters raw MS/MS spectra mined from MassIVE GNPS into three quality tiers—GeMS-A, GeMS-B and GeMS-C—based on criteria such as instrument m/z accuracy and number of high-intensity signals, producing curated corpora suitable for deep learning. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: A QC pipeline from the DreaMS paper that filters raw MS/MS spectra mined from MassIVE GNPS into three quality tiers—GeMS-A, GeMS-B and GeMS-C—based on criteria such as instrument m/z accuracy and number of high-intensity signals, producing curated corpora suitable for deep learning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are already part of a curated paired reference library (e.g. MoNA or NIST20 with known structures) — annotation-focused training should not discard or re-tier them. The downstream task involves multiply charged precursor ions or negative ionization mode spectra that the GeMS mining scope (positive mode, singly charged precursors) does not cover. You need MS1-level features — the pipeline targets tandem MS/MS spectra and disregards MS1 isotopic patterns and adduct distributions.

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS peak files (mzML, mzXML, or MGF) must be cleaned before spectrum clustering or similarity searching, and spectra fail quality criteria such as peak count, m/z range, or dominant noise peaks.
skills.name: spectral-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: spectral-quality-filtering Use when raw MS/MS peak files (mzML, mzXML, or MGF) must be cleaned before spectrum clustering or similarity searching, and spectra fail quality criteria such as peak count, m/z range, or dominant noise peaks. Analyzing metabolomics or top-down data with bottom-up proteomics defaults — the README states the default min_peaks (5) and min_mz_range (250 m/z) 'likely need to be adjusted accordingly' and recommends reducing these values for metabolomics data Input spectra are already cluster consensus/representative spectra that have already been quality-filtered The downstream similarity measure requires untransformed absolute intensities, since square root (or other) scaling changes intensity ratios http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A spectrum preprocessing stage that removes precursor-ion and low-intensity noise peaks, restricts each MS/MS spectrum to its 50 most intense peaks, discards low-quality spectra, and transforms peak intensities prior to clustering, so that downstream similarity measures operate on clean, comparable spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: A spectrum preprocessing stage that removes precursor-ion and low-intensity noise peaks, restricts each MS/MS spectrum to its 50 most intense peaks, discards low-quality spectra, and transforms peak intensities prior to clustering, so that downstream similarity measures operate on clean, comparable spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing metabolomics or top-down data with bottom-up proteomics defaults — the README states the default min_peaks (5) and min_mz_range (250 m/z) 'likely need to be adjusted accordingly' and recommends reducing these values for metabolomics data Input spectra are already cluster consensus/representative spectra that have already been quality-filtered The downstream similarity measure requires untransformed absolute intensities, since square root (or other) scaling changes intensity ratios

skills.summary: Re-aligns selected ppm areas across a set of 1D 1H NMR metabolomics spectra to correct uncontrolled chemical-shift variations between spectra, as one stage of the NMRProcFlow interactive processing chain before binning.

skills.search_text: spectral-record-standardization-with-compound-identifier-mapping Use when raw MS2 spectra records from multiple public databases must be merged into one standardized, identifier-mapped, deduplicated reference library for compound identification. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is running MS2Query on new experimental spectra to annotate features, not benchmarking search methods against known structures The query spectra have no ground-truth structural annotations (InChIKeys), so Tanimoto scores cannot be computed Exact-match library search is the target — exact match benchmarking in this article used a 0.25 Da mass tolerance rather than the analogue-search Tanimoto/recall protocol

Input is raw GC/MS chromatograms that have not yet been deconvolved — run deconvolveComp first, since similarity is computed on reconstructed pure compound spectra, not fragment-ion peaks Only a NIST library is available for identification — it can only be read with NIST software, so export/import an MSP-format library instead Input is a peak-picking feature table (m/z value, retention-time window, fragment-ion peak area, e.g. from centWave/XCMS or MetAlign) — those quantitative variables are not compound spectra and cannot be matched by this workflow Matches deconvolved GC-EI MS compound spectra by spectral similarity, both to group the same metabolite across samples during alignment and to identify compounds by spectral library matching against reference EI spectra (e.g. MassBank, GMD). This is eRah's compound-centric alternative to fragment-ion peak picking.

When the unknown spectrum already matches an entry in the spectral library — direct library search (MS2C against NIST20) is sufficient and this skill adds unnecessary C2MS modeling overhead When the goal is de novo fragment annotation or formula annotation (classification task) rather than ranking candidates by spectral similarity When spectra come from unmerged acquisitions, different instrument platforms (not Orbitrap/HCD), or different precursor adducts than [M+H]+ — the paper notes performance has not been validated under these broader conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compares tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra from candidate spectra using spectral similarity metrics (COS, SPC, entropy-based metrics) to score candidate spectra against a reference spectrum, supporting retrieval-based compound identification (MS2C) workflows where library coverage is incomplete. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2404.02360

skills.description: Use when comparing a predicted or library MS/MS spectrum against an experimental spectrum to quantify agreement — e.g. benchmarking in silico spectral prediction or ranking candidate compound matches.
skills.name: spectral-similarity-metric-computation
skills.search_text: spectral-similarity-metric-computation Use when comparing a predicted or library MS/MS spectrum against an experimental spectrum to quantify agreement — e.g. benchmarking in silico spectral prediction or ranking candidate compound matches. The input is a single unlabeled spectrum with no reference spectrum to compare against — similarity metrics require a pair of spectra. Peaks are matched by retention-time or MS1 features only, not by m/z peak lists — this skill scores MS/MS peak agreement, not chromatographic similarity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes spectral similarity metrics (Dice coefficient, Precision, Recall, and re-weighted Stein's Dot Product) between predicted and experimental MS/MS spectra, using the CFM-ID 4.0 paper's peak-matching rule of m/z difference < 0.01 Da or 10 ppm (whichever first) to score ESI-MS/MS spectral prediction quality. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c01465
skills.summary: Computes spectral similarity metrics (Dice coefficient, Precision, Recall, and re-weighted Stein's Dot Product) between predicted and experimental MS/MS spectra, using the CFM-ID 4.0 paper's peak-matching rule of m/z difference < 0.01 Da or 10 ppm (whichever first) to score ESI-MS/MS spectral prediction quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single unlabeled spectrum with no reference spectrum to compare against — similarity metrics require a pair of spectra. When performing traditional 'bottom-up' identification against reference spectral libraries, which CMDN explicitly avoids because it restricts discovery of previously unknown xenobiotic metabolites When no MS2 spectra are available for the parent compounds — the seed-molecule assignment requires pairwise candidate-parent spectral comparison When the candidate space has not been filtered for adducts and in-source fragments (ISF), since these generate spurious high-similarity links that corrupt the network http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Constructs an MS2 spectrum similarity network (SSN) — the third layer of the CMDN framework — that links preannotated metabolite candidates to parent pesticides via entropy-based MS2 spectral similarity, designating the highest-scoring parent as the 'seed molecule'. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558

skills.description: Use when you have a collection of tandem MS spectra (e.g., a GNPS/MassIVE library or dataset edge list with cosine similarity scores) and need an unpruned weighted similarity graph as the substrate for community detection and tree-based network reconstruction.
skills.name: spectral-similarity-network-construction
skills.search_text: spectral-similarity-network-construction Use when you have a collection of tandem MS spectra (e.g., a GNPS/MassIVE library or dataset edge list with cosine similarity scores) and need an unpruned weighted similarity graph as the substrate for community detection and tree-based network reconstruction. The analysis goal is a conventional molecular network that hard-cuts edges at a cosine threshold (e.g., 0.7) — this skill deliberately retains all pairwise edges and would not reproduce that workflow The input is already a per-community subgraph of a completed MCN — the appropriate step there is maximum-weight spanning-tree pruning, not full network construction You need a predefined number of clusters; MCN/Louvain derives community structure from modularity optimization rather than preset community sizes or counts Constructs a full-connectivity molecular similarity network from pairwise spectral similarity scores (cosine between tandem MS spectra) with no arbitrary similarity threshold, so that downstream molecular community networking (MCN) can optimize connectivity for each metabolite instead of fracturing natural metabolite families at a fixed cosine cutoff. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Constructs a full-connectivity molecular similarity network from pairwise spectral similarity scores (cosine between tandem MS spectra) with no arbitrary similarity threshold, so that downstream molecular community networking (MCN) can optimize connectivity for each metabolite instead of fracturing natural metabolite families at a fixed cosine cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a conventional molecular network that hard-cuts edges at a cosine threshold (e.g., 0.7) — this skill deliberately retains all pairwise edges and would not reproduce that workflow The input is already a per-community subgraph of a completed MCN — the appropriate step there is maximum-weight spanning-tree pruning, not full network construction You need a predefined number of clusters; MCN/Louvain derives community structure from modularity optimization rather than preset community sizes or counts

skills.search_text: spectral-similarity-network-edge-filtering Use when a pairwise spectral similarity matrix (e.g. ms2deepscore scores from LC–MS/MS .mgf spectra) yields dense, heterogeneous network data and edges must be filtered to a sparse local view for exploration. Input is a raw .mgf or MZmine feature list that has not yet been processed through the specXplore importing pipeline, which computes the ms2deepscore/modified cosine/spec2vec similarities needed for edge filtering. skills.summary: Binarize a pairwise spectral-similarity matrix into a sparse feature network by applying ms2deepscore similarity thresholds, minimum fragmentation overlaps, top-K per-node neighbor limits, and maximal molecular family sizes, then render edges only on demand around a selected node.

skills.search_text: spectral-similarity-scoring Use when an unannotated MS/MS spectrum may be a modified form of a library compound — e.g. precursor/fragment shifts consistent with methylation (+14 Da), acetylation (+42 Da), hydroxylation (+16 Da), or phosphorylation (+80 Da) — and plain library matching failed to assign it. skills.description: Use when you have paired peak lists from mixture NMR spectra and their pure-component references (ppm axis) and need to quantify chemical shift deviation statistics or derive a tolerance interval for peak-pairing.
skills.name: spectral-statistics-aggregation
skills.search_text: spectral-statistics-aggregation Use when you have paired peak lists from mixture NMR spectra and their pure-component references (ppm axis) and need to quantify chemical shift deviation statistics or derive a tolerance interval for peak-pairing. Spectra were acquired in a solvent system without a well-defined residual solvent peak (DMSO-d6/HDO) or contain no active-hydrogen signals — the exclusion step does not apply as specified The goal is compound identification/classification of mixtures rather than quantifying chemical shift variability — use the pSCNN prediction workflow instead Input is already an aggregated statistics table with no raw spectral peak pairs available for recomputation http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies chemical shift variation between experimental NMR mixture spectra and their pure-component references by aggregating per-pair ppm deviations into mean, standard deviation, and a mean ± 1.5 × SD tolerance interval. This characterizes how much peak positions drift across mixtures, which is the problem pSCNN's translational invariance is meant to absorb. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Quantifies chemical shift variation between experimental NMR mixture spectra and their pure-component references by aggregating per-pair ppm deviations into mean, standard deviation, and a mean ± 1.5 × SD tolerance interval. This characterizes how much peak positions drift across mixtures, which is the problem pSCNN's translational invariance is meant to absorb.

When the training set is very small — the README warns the pair sampling 'can be suboptimal if not checked', particularly for smaller training sets, and may need re-optimization When the goal is balanced sampling of ionization-mode pair combinations — the paper explicitly states the sampling algorithm 'did not enforce balanced sampling of the different ionization mode pairs' http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A pair sampling algorithm for training MS2DeepScore 2.0 that balances selected spectrum pairs equally across 10 Tanimoto score bins while capping per-molecule sampling frequency disparity to <15%, reducing training bias. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: A pair sampling algorithm for training MS2DeepScore 2.0 that balances selected spectrum pairs equally across 10 Tanimoto score bins while capping per-molecule sampling frequency disparity to <15%, reducing training bias.

skills.description: Use when spectra must be transformed into fixed-dimensional numeric vectors (e.g. to build an ANN index or compute coarse cosine similarities) prior to spectral library candidate selection or similarity search.

skills.search_text: spectral-vector-binning Use when spectra must be transformed into fixed-dimensional numeric vectors (e.g. to build an ANN index or compute coarse cosine similarities) prior to spectral library candidate selection or similarity search. Input spectra are already processed and you only need to verify preprocessing, not re-vectorize You need fine-grained fragment-level matching rather than coarse candidate retrieval — the 1 Da binned vectors are too coarse for final SSM scoring, which requires the shifted dot product on un-binned peaks The library is small enough that exact brute-force comparison of all spectra is tractable, removing the need for an ANN vector representation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Convert peak-list spectra (query and library alike) into sparse, unit-length vectors by aggressive noise filtering, keeping only the 50 most intense peaks, and binning peaks into 1 Da mass bins with intensities summed per bin. This fixed-width sparse representation is the input format that makes approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexing of spectral libraries possible. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359

This fixed-width sparse representation is the input format that makes approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexing of spectral libraries possible.
