The query has not yet been executed in ALISTER — there is no per-analyte classification or reference set to export The user needs raw measurement data storage; ALISTER explicitly does not alter or store uploaded data, so the export cannot replace the original dataset The user wants a sampling protocol recommendation for a prospective study rather than a retrospective stability record (use Protocol search export instead of Sample search export) http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Exports a .csv file containing the user's ALISTER query, the per-analyte stability classification, and all relevant references, with a 'Variable explanation' tab that documents column meanings for downstream interpretation. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cca.2024.117858
skills.summary: Exports a .csv file containing the user's ALISTER query, the per-analyte stability classification, and all relevant references, with a 'Variable explanation' tab that documents column meanings for downstream interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query has not yet been executed in ALISTER — there is no per-analyte classification or reference set to export The user needs raw measurement data storage; ALISTER explicitly does not alter or store uploaded data, so the export cannot replace the original dataset The user wants a sampling protocol recommendation for a prospective study rather than a retrospective stability record (use Protocol search export instead of Sample search export)

skills.description: Use when building differential metabolomics/lipidomics networks (p >> n, two conditions) and you need robust edge retention before GLASSO network estimation, e.g. TEDDY case-vs-control data with 134 metabolites and unbalanced groups.
skills.name: stability-selection-edge-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: stability-selection-edge-probability-estimation Use when building differential metabolomics/lipidomics networks (p >> n, two conditions) and you need robust edge retention before GLASSO network estimation, e.g. TEDDY case-vs-control data with 134 metabolites and unbalanced groups. Single-condition network construction without a case/control contrast — use CorrelationCalculator instead, which builds a data-driven network for one group Datasets where features cannot be treated as approximately normal intensity/concentration values (the package is built for metabolomics/lipidomics or similar -omics data) Datasets lacking enough samples for either BIC tuning (~500+ per group) or the lambda approximation rationale — edge probabilities will be unstable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates metabolite–metabolite edge selection probabilities by resampling (stability selection) in the DNEA R package, so that only edges reproducibly selected under R1-regularized GLASSO survive joint network estimation of two experimental groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: Estimates metabolite–metabolite edge selection probabilities by resampling (stability selection) in the DNEA R package, so that only edges reproducibly selected under R1-regularized GLASSO survive joint network estimation of two experimental groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-condition network construction without a case/control contrast — use CorrelationCalculator instead, which builds a data-driven network for one group Datasets where features cannot be treated as approximately normal intensity/concentration values (the package is built for metabolomics/lipidomics or similar -omics data) Datasets lacking enough samples for either BIC tuning (~500+ per group) or the lambda approximation rationale — edge probabilities will be unstable

skills.description: Use when building differential metabolomics networks with DNEA/Filigree where features outnumber samples (p >> n), and only resampling-stable edges should be retained after lambda tuning or approximation.
skills.name: stability-selection-edge-resampling
skills.search_text: stability-selection-edge-resampling Use when building differential metabolomics networks with DNEA/Filigree where features outnumber samples (p >> n), and only resampling-stable edges should be retained after lambda tuning or approximation. The dataset is small (fewer than ~500 samples per group) and you still want BIC-tuned lambda rather than the Eq. 3 approximation — the BIC protocol requires large cohorts The analysis goal is pathway enrichment over curated databases (e.g. KEGG), not data-driven edge inference — DNEA's FELLA comparison showed only 19 of 174 TEDDY metabolites were KEGG-mappable You only need marginal correlations — those networks are denser and include indirect correlations that confound biologically relevant interactions http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A resampling-based stability selection step in the DNEA R package that repeatedly re-estimates GLASSO partial-correlation networks across subsampled or bootstrapped data to identify metabolite-metabolite edges that are robust, controlling false positive edge inclusion under the p >> n regime. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: A resampling-based stability selection step in the DNEA R package that repeatedly re-estimates GLASSO partial-correlation networks across subsampled or bootstrapped data to identify metabolite-metabolite edges that are robust, controlling false positive edge inclusion under the p >> n regime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small (fewer than ~500 samples per group) and you still want BIC-tuned lambda rather than the Eq. 3 approximation — the BIC protocol requires large cohorts The analysis goal is pathway enrichment over curated databases (e.g. KEGG), not data-driven edge inference — DNEA's FELLA comparison showed only 19 of 174 TEDDY metabolites were KEGG-mappable You only need marginal correlations — those networks are denser and include indirect correlations that confound biologically relevant interactions

skills.description: Use when a samples-by-features cancer omics matrix (transcriptome, methylome, proteome, or single-cell) needs to be decomposed into independent, reproducible metagene/source components, or when ICA must be compared against PCA/NMF.
skills.name: stabilized-ica-decomposition
skills.search_text: stabilized-ica-decomposition Use when a samples-by-features cancer omics matrix (transcriptome, methylome, proteome, or single-cell) needs to be decomposed into independent, reproducible metagene/source components, or when ICA must be compared against PCA/NMF. The analysis goal is supervised feature selection or predictive modeling rather than unsupervised blind source separation of omics data The data matrix is not omics-shaped (samples × features) or the goal is deconvolution of immune cell fractions only, for which DeconICA's targeted deconvolution workflow is more appropriate A decomposition must be exactly reproduced rather than statistically reproducible — ICA component order and sign vary across randomized initializations Run stabilized Independent Component Analysis (ICA) over multiple randomized initializations on a cancer omics data matrix to extract robust, non-Gaussian metagene signatures, as reviewed and demonstrated in the IJMScancer-omics ICA review and its companion Jupyter notebook. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414
skills.summary: Run stabilized Independent Component Analysis (ICA) over multiple randomized initializations on a cancer omics data matrix to extract robust, non-Gaussian metagene signatures, as reviewed and demonstrated in the IJMScancer-omics ICA review and its companion Jupyter notebook.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is supervised feature selection or predictive modeling rather than unsupervised blind source separation of omics data The data matrix is not omics-shaped (samples × features) or the goal is deconvolution of immune cell fractions only, for which DeconICA's targeted deconvolution workflow is more appropriate A decomposition must be exactly reproduced rather than statistically reproducible — ICA component order and sign vary across randomized initializations

skills.description: Use when targeted LC-SRM or HRMS chromatograms contain stable-isotope-labeled internal standards for each analyte and the goal is absolute concentration (µM, nmol/g, µmol/mmol creatinine) rather than relative peak-area comparison.
skills.name: stable-isotope-dilution-calibration
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-dilution-calibration Use when targeted LC-SRM or HRMS chromatograms contain stable-isotope-labeled internal standards for each analyte and the goal is absolute concentration (µM, nmol/g, µmol/mmol creatinine) rather than relative peak-area comparison. Input is already a feature table from untargeted profiling (XCMS/MZmine/MS-DIAL) with no stable-isotope-labeled internal standards available for each analyte — peak-area ratio calibration cannot be performed. The experiment requires relative abundance comparisons across conditions rather than absolute concentrations; unlabeled external calibration alone would suffice. GC-MS or ion-mobility small-molecule data are being analyzed; Skyline support for these is explicitly still ongoing, so isotope-dilution calibration in Skyline is not yet the right tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Calibrates LC-SRM/HRMS peak-area ratios against a ten-point 0.01–25 µM external standard curve spiked with heavy-labeled internal standards, exporting analyte concentrations as CSV from a Skyline document. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.9b00640
skills.summary: Calibrates LC-SRM/HRMS peak-area ratios against a ten-point 0.01–25 µM external standard curve spiked with heavy-labeled internal standards, exporting analyte concentrations as CSV from a Skyline document.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table from untargeted profiling (XCMS/MZmine/MS-DIAL) with no stable-isotope-labeled internal standards available for each analyte — peak-area ratio calibration cannot be performed. The experiment requires relative abundance comparisons across conditions rather than absolute concentrations; unlabeled external calibration alone would suffice. GC-MS or ion-mobility small-molecule data are being analyzed; Skyline support for these is explicitly still ongoing, so isotope-dilution calibration in Skyline is not yet the right tool.

skills.description: Use when simulating theoretical isotopic envelopes or fine structures of a user-defined peptide sequence or chemical formula under arbitrary SIP labeling percentages (partial 13C/15N incorporation), not just natural abundance.
skills.name: stable-isotope-enrichment-parameterization
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-enrichment-parameterization Use when simulating theoretical isotopic envelopes or fine structures of a user-defined peptide sequence or chemical formula under arbitrary SIP labeling percentages (partial 13C/15N incorporation), not just natural abundance. The task is identifying PSMs from experimental raw files in a SIP proteomics workflow — use Sipros/SiprosEnsemble database search instead; Aerith parameterization is for simulation and annotation, not identification. Only natural-abundance fine structures are needed — IsoSpec2 provides rapid natural-abundance fine-structure simulation, though it cannot handle partial SIP incorporation. The analysis workflow requires the isotopic envelope of a known 100%-enriched molecular tracer as input (the Miso package's assumption), rather than user-defined partial enrichment levels. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parameterize theoretical isotopic envelopes and fine structures in Aerith at user-defined stable-isotope enrichment levels (0–100%) for peptides or metabolite formulas, e.g. simulating peptide HYAHVDCPGHADYVK at natural (1.07% 13C) versus 50% 13C abundance. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Parameterize theoretical isotopic envelopes and fine structures in Aerith at user-defined stable-isotope enrichment levels (0–100%) for peptides or metabolite formulas, e.g. simulating peptide HYAHVDCPGHADYVK at natural (1.07% 13C) versus 50% 13C abundance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is identifying PSMs from experimental raw files in a SIP proteomics workflow — use Sipros/SiprosEnsemble database search instead; Aerith parameterization is for simulation and annotation, not identification. Only natural-abundance fine structures are needed — IsoSpec2 provides rapid natural-abundance fine-structure simulation, though it cannot handle partial SIP incorporation. The analysis workflow requires the isotopic envelope of a known 100%-enriched molecular tracer as input (the Miso package's assumption), rather than user-defined partial enrichment levels.

skills.description: Use when quantified 13C isotopologue peak areas from a stable isotope tracer experiment (e.g., 13C6-glucose) are available and the goal is fractional labelling per metabolite to check pathway labelling patterns across parallel samples.
skills.name: stable-isotope-fractional-labelling-calculation
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-fractional-labelling-calculation Use when quantified 13C isotopologue peak areas from a stable isotope tracer experiment (e.g., 13C6-glucose) are available and the goal is fractional labelling per metabolite to check pathway labelling patterns across parallel samples. Input is raw LC-MS data or extracted-ion chromatograms rather than already-quantified isotopologue peak areas (run TarMet's isotopologue analysis/quantification first). The analysis targets unlabelled targeted metabolite quantification where no stable isotope tracer was used, so fractional labelling is undefined. Tracer design does not produce interpretable positional labelling (e.g., metabolites outside the traced pathway), so the upstream-labelled/downstream-unlabeled check does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Compute per-metabolite fractional 13C labelling from TarMet-quantified isotopologue peak areas by normalizing each isotopologue (M+1, M+2, ...) to the summed labelled pool, enabling pathway-order verification in tracer experiments such as 13C6-glucose tracing of glycolysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-018-1363-7
skills.summary: Compute per-metabolite fractional 13C labelling from TarMet-quantified isotopologue peak areas by normalizing each isotopologue (M+1, M+2, ...) to the summed labelled pool, enabling pathway-order verification in tracer experiments such as 13C6-glucose tracing of glycolysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data or extracted-ion chromatograms rather than already-quantified isotopologue peak areas (run TarMet's isotopologue analysis/quantification first). The analysis targets unlabelled targeted metabolite quantification where no stable isotope tracer was used, so fractional labelling is undefined. Tracer design does not produce interpretable positional labelling (e.g., metabolites outside the traced pathway), so the upstream-labelled/downstream-unlabeled check does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you have an XCMS-processed XCMSet with paired unlabeled/labeled sample groups (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and need to find feature pairs showing shifted m/z and enrichment-consistent intensity changes.
skills.name: stable-isotope-label-pair-detection
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-label-pair-detection Use when you have an XCMS-processed XCMSet with paired unlabeled/labeled sample groups (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and need to find feature pairs showing shifted m/z and enrichment-consistent intensity changes. Input is raw mzXML without prior XCMS peak picking, alignment and grouping — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure, not raw spectra. No unlabeled biologically equivalent control samples exist to compare isotopic distributions against, since geoRge's contrast requires UL/L sample pairs. Labeling is with an element other than the configured atom masses (e.g., not 12C/13C at 12.0 vs 13.003355 Da) unless parameters are retuned accordingly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Detects putative isotopically-labeled feature pairs in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics by comparing isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples on an XCMS feature table (geoRge, Analytical Chemistry 2015). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: Detects putative isotopically-labeled feature pairs in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics by comparing isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples on an XCMS feature table (geoRge, Analytical Chemistry 2015).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw mzXML without prior XCMS peak picking, alignment and grouping — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure, not raw spectra. No unlabeled biologically equivalent control samples exist to compare isotopic distributions against, since geoRge's contrast requires UL/L sample pairs. Labeling is with an element other than the configured atom masses (e.g., not 12C/13C at 12.0 vs 13.003355 Da) unless parameters are retuned accordingly.

skills.description: Use when GC-CI-MS raw centroided files from a stable-isotope labelling study (e.g. 13C-glucose or 13C-arginine tracing) need automatic isotopologue quantification for derivatized central-carbon or polyamine metabolites.
skills.name: stable-isotope-labeling-data-quantification
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-labeling-data-quantification Use when GC-CI-MS raw centroided files from a stable-isotope labelling study (e.g. 13C-glucose or 13C-arginine tracing) need automatic isotopologue quantification for derivatized central-carbon or polyamine metabolites. When the acquisition is EI rather than chemical ionization: EI at 70 eV fragments compounds so the [M+H]+ envelope needed for isotopologue integration is not concentrated in a single ion. When the input is already a processed isotopologue/enrichment table rather than raw centroided mzML files. When the isotope label is not the atom specified in the formula table (e.g. labelatom must match the tracer; 15N tracing requires labelatom="15N"). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Automatically quantifies all isotopologues of derivatized metabolites in GC-CI-MS stable-isotope labelling experiments using the R package isoSCAN, handling both low-resolution (LRMS) and high-resolution (HRMS) centroided data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c02998
skills.summary: Automatically quantifies all isotopologues of derivatized metabolites in GC-CI-MS stable-isotope labelling experiments using the R package isoSCAN, handling both low-resolution (LRMS) and high-resolution (HRMS) centroided data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the acquisition is EI rather than chemical ionization: EI at 70 eV fragments compounds so the [M+H]+ envelope needed for isotopologue integration is not concentrated in a single ion. When the input is already a processed isotopologue/enrichment table rather than raw centroided mzML files. When the isotope label is not the atom specified in the formula table (e.g. labelatom must match the tracer; 15N tracing requires labelatom="15N").

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC/MS data from a stable isotope-labeling experiment (e.g. 12C vs 13C glucose) has been processed with XCMS and you need to enumerate features whose isotopic distribution shifts between unlabeled and labeled samples.
skills.name: stable-isotope-labeling-detection-in-lcms-metabolomics
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-labeling-detection-in-lcms-metabolomics Use when untargeted LC/MS data from a stable isotope-labeling experiment (e.g. 12C vs 13C glucose) has been processed with XCMS and you need to enumerate features whose isotopic distribution shifts between unlabeled and labeled samples. Data has not been processed through XCMS peak picking/alignment/grouping — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure, not raw mzXML The experiment is targeted or lacks biologically equivalent unlabeled/labeled sample pairs to compare isotopic distributions The goal is de novo isotopologue assignment from theoretical mass differences rather than sample-to-sample isotopic distribution comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 geoRge is an R tool for detecting stable isotope labeling in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics by comparing isotopic distributions between biologically equivalent unlabeled and labeled samples in an XCMS feature table, flagging features with new or higher-intensity m/z peaks in labeled samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: geoRge is an R tool for detecting stable isotope labeling in untargeted LC/MS metabolomics by comparing isotopic distributions between biologically equivalent unlabeled and labeled samples in an XCMS feature table, flagging features with new or higher-intensity m/z peaks in labeled samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been processed through XCMS peak picking/alignment/grouping — geoRge runs on the XCMS output structure, not raw mzXML The experiment is targeted or lacks biologically equivalent unlabeled/labeled sample pairs to compare isotopic distributions The goal is de novo isotopologue assignment from theoretical mass differences rather than sample-to-sample isotopic distribution comparison

skills.description: Use when analyzing untargeted LC/MS peak tables from stable isotope-labeling experiments (e.g. 12C/13C glucose pairs in XCMS output) to find putatively labeled features and annotate them against a metabolite database.
skills.name: stable-isotope-labeling-feature-detection
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-labeling-feature-detection Use when analyzing untargeted LC/MS peak tables from stable isotope-labeling experiments (e.g. 12C/13C glucose pairs in XCMS output) to find putatively labeled features and annotate them against a metabolite database. The data are not from a stable isotope-labeling experiment with paired unlabeled/labeled samples (geoRge relies on comparing isotopic distributions between biologically equivalent sample groups) Input is raw LC/MS vendor files rather than an XCMS-processed peak set — peak picking, alignment and grouping must be done with XCMS first You need targeted isotope tracing of known compounds rather than untargeted detection of putatively labeled features http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 geoRge-based R workflow that detects isotopically labeled features in untargeted LC/MS data (XCMS output) by comparing isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples, then annotates labeled base peaks with putative metabolites via a database/adduct query. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: geoRge-based R workflow that detects isotopically labeled features in untargeted LC/MS data (XCMS output) by comparing isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples, then annotates labeled base peaks with putative metabolites via a database/adduct query.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not from a stable isotope-labeling experiment with paired unlabeled/labeled samples (geoRge relies on comparing isotopic distributions between biologically equivalent sample groups) Input is raw LC/MS vendor files rather than an XCMS-processed peak set — peak picking, alignment and grouping must be done with XCMS first You need targeted isotope tracing of known compounds rather than untargeted detection of putatively labeled features

skills.description: Use when you have XCMS-processed untargeted LC/MS data from paired unlabeled/labeled tracer experiments (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and need to detect isotopically enriched features and annotate their base peaks.
skills.name: stable-isotope-lc-ms-annotation
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-lc-ms-annotation Use when you have XCMS-processed untargeted LC/MS data from paired unlabeled/labeled tracer experiments (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and need to detect isotopically enriched features and annotate their base peaks. Your data are not XCMS feature objects — geoRge runs on the output structure of the XCMS package, so raw spectra or non-XCMS peak tables are out of scope You lack biologically equivalent unlabeled and labeled sample groups — geoRge compares isotopic distributions between such pairs and cannot infer labeling from labeled samples alone You need targeted isotope-tracer quantification rather than untargeted detection of putative labeling in unannotated features http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Detects and annotates stable isotope labeling in LC/MS-based untargeted metabolomics using geoRge, an R tool that compares isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples on XCMS output, rather than scanning all MS signals for theoretical mass differences. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5b03628
skills.summary: Detects and annotates stable isotope labeling in LC/MS-based untargeted metabolomics using geoRge, an R tool that compares isotopic distributions between unlabeled and labeled biologically equivalent samples on XCMS output, rather than scanning all MS signals for theoretical mass differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are not XCMS feature objects — geoRge runs on the output structure of the XCMS package, so raw spectra or non-XCMS peak tables are out of scope You lack biologically equivalent unlabeled and labeled sample groups — geoRge compares isotopic distributions between such pairs and cannot infer labeling from labeled samples alone You need targeted isotope-tracer quantification rather than untargeted detection of putative labeling in unannotated features

skills.description: Use when LC-MS data from a stable isotope labeling experiment (13C, 2H, 15N, 18O, or 34S tracer) are given as FAM column vectors in XLSX form and must be resolution-corrected to MDV and per-compound enrichment.
skills.name: stable-isotope-lcms-labeling-data-processing
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-lcms-labeling-data-processing Use when LC-MS data from a stable isotope labeling experiment (13C, 2H, 15N, 18O, or 34S tracer) are given as FAM column vectors in XLSX form and must be resolution-corrected to MDV and per-compound enrichment. The tracer element selected is not present in some compounds' formulas — the algorithm reports an error (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S as tracer) Instrument resolution is extremely low, where ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor, or extremely high, where it performs no correction at all — the resolution-dependent correction amount may not match the experimental design The task requires cross-platform or non-MATLAB execution without the compiled runtime — ElemCor is a MATLAB stand-alone application and workflows must obtain its MATLAB functions for pipeline integration http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Corrects fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) from high-resolution LC-MS stable isotope labeling experiments for natural abundance and tracer isotopic impurity using ElemCor's mass difference theory (MDT) and/or unlabeled sample (ULS) correction matrices, then computes mass distribution vectors (MDV) and isotopic enrichment via non-negative linear regression. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Corrects fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) from high-resolution LC-MS stable isotope labeling experiments for natural abundance and tracer isotopic impurity using ElemCor's mass difference theory (MDT) and/or unlabeled sample (ULS) correction matrices, then computes mass distribution vectors (MDV) and isotopic enrichment via non-negative linear regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tracer element selected is not present in some compounds' formulas — the algorithm reports an error (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S as tracer) Instrument resolution is extremely low, where ElemCor becomes identical to IsoCor, or extremely high, where it performs no correction at all — the resolution-dependent correction amount may not match the experimental design The task requires cross-platform or non-MATLAB execution without the compiled runtime — ElemCor is a MATLAB stand-alone application and workflows must obtain its MATLAB functions for pipeline integration

skills.description: Use when HRMS lipidomics feature tables from a stable-isotope ([U-13C6] tracer) time course must be matched to lipid species and converted to isotope-corrected labeled quantities, e.g., to cluster PC/DAG species by labeling kinetics.

skills.search_text: stable-isotope-lipidomics-compound-annotation Use when HRMS lipidomics feature tables from a stable-isotope ([U-13C6] tracer) time course must be matched to lipid species and converted to isotope-corrected labeled quantities, e.g., to cluster PC/DAG species by labeling kinetics. Data are raw vendor files or mzML that have not been feature-detected — pre-process with XCMS (or MZmine2) first, since SIMPEL consumes XCMS-style feature tables The experiment is a steady-state or single-pulse endpoint metabolomics run where pool-size-normalized labeling kinetics across a time course are not of interest Targeted low-resolution MS data where isotopologues of dual-labeled tracers cannot be resolved — HRMS is required to distinguish isotopologues differing by <0.01 Da http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotate lipid compounds (e.g., PC and DAG species) in XCMS-pre-processed HRMS stable-isotope labeling data using the SIMPEL R package, matching features to a compound database by exact mass (ppm tolerance) and retention time, then generate and natural-abundance-correct isotopologue distributions so that 13C-labeled lipid abundances (nmol) can be quantified and grouped by labeling kinetics. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42003-024-05844-z
skills.summary: Annotate lipid compounds (e.g., PC and DAG species) in XCMS-pre-processed HRMS stable-isotope labeling data using the SIMPEL R package, matching features to a compound database by exact mass (ppm tolerance) and retention time, then generate and natural-abundance-correct isotopologue distributions so that 13C-labeled lipid abundances (nmol) can be quantified and grouped by labeling kinetics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw vendor files or mzML that have not been feature-detected — pre-process with XCMS (or MZmine2) first, since SIMPEL consumes XCMS-style feature tables The experiment is a steady-state or single-pulse endpoint metabolomics run where pool-size-normalized labeling kinetics across a time course are not of interest Targeted low-resolution MS data where isotopologues of dual-labeled tracers cannot be resolved — HRMS is required to distinguish isotopologues differing by <0.01 Da

skills.description: Use when analyzing proteomic stable isotope probing (SIP) data: you have peptide sequences with partially 13C-labeled spectra, need simulated isotopic envelopes at user-defined enrichment levels, or must validate database-search PSM outputs.
skills.name: stable-isotope-probing-peptide-analysis
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-probing-peptide-analysis Use when analyzing proteomic stable isotope probing (SIP) data: you have peptide sequences with partially 13C-labeled spectra, need simulated isotopic envelopes at user-defined enrichment levels, or must validate database-search PSM outputs. You only need a database search result itself, not PSM/envelope validation — Sipros (SiprosV4/Sipros 5 via Bioconda) handles identification and SIP-labeling FDR control You need isotopic fine structure of fully unlabeled compounds only under natural abundance — IsoSpec2 covers that; Aerith's FFT envelope method does not account for isotopic fine structure You need to estimate labeling percentages alone in an existing pipeline (e.g., MetaProSIP, Calisp outputs) without visualization or manual PSM validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Simulate and visualize theoretical isotopic envelopes of SIP-labeled peptides across 0–100% enrichment levels, and score/validate peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) with multiple scoring functions (MVH, Xcorr, WDP, spectral entropy) using the Aerith R package with C++/Rcpp backends. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03207
skills.summary: Simulate and visualize theoretical isotopic envelopes of SIP-labeled peptides across 0–100% enrichment levels, and score/validate peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) with multiple scoring functions (MVH, Xcorr, WDP, spectral entropy) using the Aerith R package with C++/Rcpp backends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a database search result itself, not PSM/envelope validation — Sipros (SiprosV4/Sipros 5 via Bioconda) handles identification and SIP-labeling FDR control You need isotopic fine structure of fully unlabeled compounds only under natural abundance — IsoSpec2 covers that; Aerith's FFT envelope method does not account for isotopic fine structure You need to estimate labeling percentages alone in an existing pipeline (e.g., MetaProSIP, Calisp outputs) without visualization or manual PSM validation

skills.description: Use when selecting an ionization method/reagent gas for GC-MS isotopologue detection in stable-isotope labeling experiments, or when [M+H]+ molecular ions fragment excessively under the current source settings.
skills.name: stable-isotope-tracing-spectra-evaluation
skills.search_text: stable-isotope-tracing-spectra-evaluation Use when selecting an ionization method/reagent gas for GC-MS isotopologue detection in stable-isotope labeling experiments, or when [M+H]+ molecular ions fragment excessively under the current source settings. skills.summary: A method for systematically comparing GC-MS ionization configurations (EI at 70 eV, low-energy EI at 15 eV, CI with methane, CI with isobutane) by their ability to concentrate isotopologue signal in intact [M+H]+ envelopes, to select the best ionization source for stable-isotope tracing experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is already quantifying isotopologues with a chosen source (e.g., GC-CI-MS with isobutane) rather than choosing among ionization methods — use isoSCAN processing instead When the data are from LC-MS or other non-GC separations, where the article's EI/CI-reagent-gas comparison does not apply When the analytes fall outside volatile/derivatizable GC space (the article's methoxyamination + MSTFA/TMCS silylation workflow) so no [M+H]+ envelope can be formed

skills.description: Use when non-targeted LC-MS peak lists (e.g. from MZmine 2 centWave extraction) must be transformed into image representations so a CNN can score peaks as true vs false.
skills.name: stacked-chromatogram-plotting
skills.search_text: stacked-chromatogram-plotting Use when non-targeted LC-MS peak lists (e.g. from MZmine 2 centWave extraction) must be transformed into image representations so a CNN can score peaks as true vs false. The input is already a feature/parameter table (e.g. 59 peak group parameters) destined for the multiple logistic regression or Random Forest filter models rather than the image-based DNN. Raw chromatographic peak shapes are unavailable (only summary peak quality metrics), since the raster images require per-sample intensity-vs-scan curves. The goal is peak detection itself — features must already have been extracted (e.g. MZmine 2 centWave) before stacked plots can be generated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Renders each extracted LC-MS peak group as a stacked chromatogram plot over its 63 most intense samples and converts the stack into a 64x64 raster image (pixel = intensity, row = sample, column = time/scans) suitable as input to the image-based deep neural network peak classifier. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b02983
skills.summary: Renders each extracted LC-MS peak group as a stacked chromatogram plot over its 63 most intense samples and converts the stack into a 64x64 raster image (pixel = intensity, row = sample, column = time/scans) suitable as input to the image-based deep neural network peak classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/parameter table (e.g. 59 peak group parameters) destined for the multiple logistic regression or Random Forest filter models rather than the image-based DNN. skills.description: Use when enumerating candidate metabolomic data-processing workflows and needing to constrain stage combinations to the dataset scenario (with QCSs, with ISs, or without both).
skills.name: stage-applicability-constraint-verification
skills.search_text: stage-applicability-constraint-verification Use when enumerating candidate metabolomic data-processing workflows and needing to constrain stage combinations to the dataset scenario (with QCSs, with ISs, or without both). The dataset includes quality-control samples but you intend to enumerate workflows without the S2 QCS-correction stage (or vice versa, apply S2 to data lacking QCSs). The dataset contains internal standards but S4 normalization methods not compatible with ISs are enumerated (this would break the 48-workflow IS-scenario count). The goal is already workflow ranking or performance assessment (S5, five criteria) rather than verifying which stages apply and enumerating valid combinations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Verifies that NOREVA processing stages are only applied to the data scenarios in which they are applicable — the QCS-correction stage (S2) only for data with quality-control samples and IS-compatible normalization (S4) only for data with internal standards — so that combinatorial workflow enumeration yields the correct scenario-specific workflow counts. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: Verifies that NOREVA processing stages are only applied to the data scenarios in which they are applicable — the QCS-correction stage (S2) only for data with quality-control samples and IS-compatible normalization (S4) only for data with internal standards — so that combinatorial workflow enumeration yields the correct scenario-specific workflow counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset includes quality-control samples but you intend to enumerate workflows without the S2 QCS-correction stage (or vice versa, apply S2 to data lacking QCSs). The dataset contains internal standards but S4 normalization methods not compatible with ISs are enumerated (this would break the 48-workflow IS-scenario count). The goal is already workflow ranking or performance assessment (S5, five criteria) rather than verifying which stages apply and enumerating valid combinations.

skills.description: Use when longitudinal or staged metabolomics data (e.g., NMR concentration matrices across sequential cell states) must be distilled into per-stage biomarker subnetworks, and pairwise transition-specific metabolite signatures are the goal.

skills.search_text: stage-specific-metabolic-biomarker-identification Use when longitudinal or staged metabolomics data (e.g., NMR concentration matrices across sequential cell states) must be distilled into per-stage biomarker subnetworks, and pairwise transition-specific metabolite signatures are the goal. Cross-validation (sklearn.covariance.GraphLassoCV) is infeasible because the pairwise datasets are too small for stable alpha selection Input is a static, single-population metabolomics profile rather than stage-resolved/longitudinal data — transition-specific subnetworks cannot be isolated The goal is pathway-level rather than metabolite-level biomarker discovery without network context http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Identifies stage- or transition-specific metabolic biomarkers by combining PCA loadings with sparse precision-matrix estimation (Graphical Lasso) on longitudinal NMR metabolomics data, extracting metabolite subnetworks whose hallmark metabolites (e.g., glutamate/GABA at hESC, lipids/glutathione at neuron) map to each developmental stage. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fnins.2024.1520982

skills.search_text: std-propagation-for-flux-ratios Use when you have triplicate 0 h and 72 h extracellular metabolomics intensity/concentration measurements in species and medium samples and need to assign uncertainty to per-metabolite boundary fluxes from the MINNO eq 1 estimator (e.g. purine/pyrimidine fluxes in Borrelia cultures). Input is intracellular or single-time-point data with no paired 0 h vs 72 h comparison — the STD propagation and paired t-test assume triplicate time-course pairs. Only a single replicate per metabolite is available — the replicate standard deviations required by the STD propagation rule are undefined. Metabolites are measured in batch rather than in species-plus-medium co-culture design — evaporation correction defined in eq 1 does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Propagates replicate standard deviations of 0 h vs 72 h metabolite concentrations through the MINNO metabolic boundary flux estimator (eq 1), yielding a flux uncertainty for each metabolite (e.g. extracellular metabolites measured in specific-species and medium samples over 0–72 h) that is then combined with a paired t-test (α = 0.05) and z-score screen to flag metabolites whose fluxes are statistically significant. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04501
skills.summary: Propagates replicate standard deviations of 0 h vs 72 h metabolite concentrations through the MINNO metabolic boundary flux estimator (eq 1), yielding a flux uncertainty for each metabolite (e.g. extracellular metabolites measured in specific-species and medium samples over 0–72 h) that is then combined with a paired t-test (α = 0.05) and z-score screen to flag metabolites whose fluxes are statistically significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is intracellular or single-time-point data with no paired 0 h vs 72 h comparison — the STD propagation and paired t-test assume triplicate time-course pairs. Only a single replicate per metabolite is available — the replicate standard deviations required by the STD propagation rule are undefined. Metabolites are measured in batch rather than in species-plus-medium co-culture design — evaporation correction defined in eq 1 does not apply.

skills.description: Use when computing CCS values from stepped-field DTIMS-MS acquisitions (e.g., Agilent 6560 tune-mix infusion data) where ions are measured across multiple electric fields and per-field arrival times and frame metadata are available.
skills.name: stepped-field-dtims-ccs-calculation
skills.search_text: stepped-field-dtims-ccs-calculation Use when computing CCS values from stepped-field DTIMS-MS acquisitions (e.g., Agilent 6560 tune-mix infusion data) where ions are measured across multiple electric fields and per-field arrival times and frame metadata are available. Data are single-field DTIMS or RapidFire-DTIMS acquisitions — use AutoCCS --mode single (batch) with a calibrant file (e.g., TuneMix-CCS.txt, --degree 1) instead of stepped-field regression. Data come from traveling-wave platforms (Waters Synapt, SLIM-based IMS) or Bruker timsTOF TIMS — these require TWIMS/TIMS calibration modes (--calib_method poly/power, --calibrant_file) rather than the stepped-field multi-field mode. Ions are observed in fewer than the required number of electric fields (below --threshold_n_fields 5) — stepped-field fitting cannot be applied to such targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Automated determination of collision cross-section (CCS) values from stepped-field drift-tube IMS-MS data by linear regression of arrival time versus electric field (P/V) across fields, following the Stow et al. 2017 method, implemented in AutoCCS. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab429
skills.summary: Automated determination of collision cross-section (CCS) values from stepped-field drift-tube IMS-MS data by linear regression of arrival time versus electric field (P/V) across fields, following the Stow et al. 2017 method, implemented in AutoCCS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-field DTIMS or RapidFire-DTIMS acquisitions — use AutoCCS --mode single (batch) with a calibrant file (e.g., TuneMix-CCS.txt, --degree 1) instead of stepped-field regression. Data come from traveling-wave platforms (Waters Synapt, SLIM-based IMS) or Bruker timsTOF TIMS — these require TWIMS/TIMS calibration modes (--calib_method poly/power, --calibrant_file) rather than the stepped-field multi-field mode. Ions are observed in fewer than the required number of electric fields (below --threshold_n_fields 5) — stepped-field fitting cannot be applied to such targets.

skills.description: Use when many candidate biomarkers are individually associated with survival but are highly correlated, and you must select a reduced subset that remains independently significant after mutual adjustment.
skills.name: stepwise-forward-backward-biomarker-selection
skills.search_text: stepwise-forward-backward-biomarker-selection Use when many candidate biomarkers are individually associated with survival but are highly correlated, and you must select a reduced subset that remains independently significant after mutual adjustment. When the goal is univariate ranking of all biomarkers rather than a mutually adjusted subset — run the basic per-cohort Cox meta-analysis across all 226 biomarkers instead. When biomarkers are weakly correlated and all remain significant after mutual adjustment — stepwise selection is unnecessary. When no per-cohort survival summary statistics or individual-level covariate-adjusted Cox models are available; the procedure requires successive rounds of fully adjusted meta-analyses. A multivariate biomarker selection procedure that identifies the subset of highly correlated metabolic biomarkers independently associated with a time-to-event outcome, by iterating forward-backward selection over successive rounds of fixed-effect Cox survival meta-analyses in the R-package meta. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-11311-9
skills.summary: A multivariate biomarker selection procedure that identifies the subset of highly correlated metabolic biomarkers independently associated with a time-to-event outcome, by iterating forward-backward selection over successive rounds of fixed-effect Cox survival meta-analyses in the R-package meta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is univariate ranking of all biomarkers rather than a mutually adjusted subset — run the basic per-cohort Cox meta-analysis across all 226 biomarkers instead. When biomarkers are weakly correlated and all remain significant after mutual adjustment — stepwise selection is unnecessary. When no per-cohort survival summary statistics or individual-level covariate-adjusted Cox models are available; the procedure requires successive rounds of fully adjusted meta-analyses.

skills.name: sterol-fragmentation-pattern-modeling
skills.search_text: sterol-fragmentation-pattern-modeling Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids whose C=C double bond positions are known, e.g. to build a searchable fragment ion database for isomer-level sterolomics. The target molecules lack C=C bonds, since the script's recognition and fragmentation logic is built around C═C bond-targeted N-Me derivatization and was only tested on sterol lipids You need collision cross section (CCS) prediction or retention time prediction rather than fragment ion prediction — use the QCC-assisted SVR/LASSO workflow or the GNN RT prediction workflow instead The input is raw LC-IM-MS/MS data requiring spectral processing and sterol identification rather than in silico fragment generation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 RDkit-based MS/MS calculation that recognizes C=C double bond positions in N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids and generates theoretical fragment-ion spectra (m/z and relative intensity) according to N-Me fragmentation patterns. skills.summary: RDkit-based MS/MS calculation that recognizes C=C double bond positions in N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids and generates theoretical fragment-ion spectra (m/z and relative intensity) according to N-Me fragmentation patterns. It supplies the fragment ion dimension of the 4D sterol lipid database (n = 4891) used for LC-IM-MS/MS-based sterol identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target molecules lack C=C bonds, since the script's recognition and fragmentation logic is built around C═C bond-targeted N-Me derivatization and was only tested on sterol lipids You need collision cross section (CCS) prediction or retention time prediction rather than fragment ion prediction — use the QCC-assisted SVR/LASSO workflow or the GNN RT prediction workflow instead The input is raw LC-IM-MS/MS data requiring spectral processing and sterol identification rather than in silico fragment generation

skills.description: Use when evaluating a diffusion-based molecular generator (e.g. DiffSpectra/DMT) and you need to quantify how sampling noise level affects the trade-off between structural diversity (unique atom types, bond types, SMILES) and elucidation accuracy (top-1/top-10).
skills.name: stochastic-denoising-parameter-ablation
skills.search_text: stochastic-denoising-parameter-ablation Use when evaluating a diffusion-based molecular generator (e.g. DiffSpectra/DMT) and you need to quantify how sampling noise level affects the trade-off between structural diversity (unique atom types, bond types, SMILES) and elucidation accuracy (top-1/top-10). The model output is deterministic without injected noise (τ = 0.0), which reduces accuracy and inflates MCES (4.6948); do not default to the lowest temperature for a 'safe' run. The task is training or SpecFormer pre-training rather than sampling; this skill evaluates generation-time stochasticity only. Spectra are single-modality studies outside the paper's QM9S multi-modal scope — the reported optimal τ = 1.0 was established on allspectra data and may not transfer. http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 Sweeps the sampling temperature τ of DiffSpectra's reverse-time denoising process, which scales injected Gaussian noise via Gₛ = Ḡₛ + τ·(σₛσ_t|ₛ/σ_t)G∈, to characterize the diversity/accuracy trade-off in spectra-conditioned molecular structure elucidation. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Sweeps the sampling temperature τ of DiffSpectra's reverse-time denoising process, which scales injected Gaussian noise via Gₛ = Ḡₛ + τ·(σₛσ_t|ₛ/σ_t)G∈, to characterize the diversity/accuracy trade-off in spectra-conditioned molecular structure elucidation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model output is deterministic without injected noise (τ = 0.0), which reduces accuracy and inflates MCES (4.6948); do not default to the lowest temperature for a 'safe' run. skills.description: Use when you have relative-abundance (not absolute) time-course metabolomics data for an intracellular metabolic network with a known stoichiometric matrix and need to infer response factors / absolute concentrations without chemical standards.
skills.name: stoichiometric-mass-balance-constraint-modeling
skills.search_text: stoichiometric-mass-balance-constraint-modeling Use when you have relative-abundance (not absolute) time-course metabolomics data for an intracellular metabolic network with a known stoichiometric matrix and need to infer response factors / absolute concentrations without chemical standards. When metabolites span multiple intracellular compartments (e.g. eukaryotic transport reactions) — MetaboPAC only applies to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment and does not consider transport reactions across intracellular compartments. When response factors vary with concentration — the method assumes response factors are constant with concentration, which may not hold outside the linear dynamic range or under ion suppression. When the dataset is missing many values — missing values (e.g. 10% missingness with imputation) reduce the accuracy of inferred concentrations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Uses stoichiometric mass balances of metabolic reaction networks, encoded in a stoichiometric matrix, to constrain and score candidate response-factor sets so that simulated concentrations from relative-abundance time-course GC-MS data remain biologically feasible. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Uses stoichiometric mass balances of metabolic reaction networks, encoded in a stoichiometric matrix, to constrain and score candidate response-factor sets so that simulated concentrations from relative-abundance time-course GC-MS data remain biologically feasible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When metabolites span multiple intracellular compartments (e.g. eukaryotic transport reactions) — MetaboPAC only applies to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment and does not consider transport reactions across intracellular compartments. When response factors vary with concentration — the method assumes response factors are constant with concentration, which may not hold outside the linear dynamic range or under ion suppression. When the dataset is missing many values — missing values (e.g. 10% missingness with imputation) reduce the accuracy of inferred concentrations.

skills.name: stoichiometric-mass-balance-flux-solving
skills.search_text: stoichiometric-mass-balance-flux-solving Use when time-course relative-abundance metabolomics data (concMatrix/timeVec) and a stoichiometric matrix are available but fluxomics measurements are not, and flux profiles v must be reconstructed for penalty-based optimization of response factors. Eukaryotic systems requiring transport reactions across intracellular compartments — MetaboPAC does not take these into consideration and applies only to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment Single-timepoint data with no time-course structure — concentration derivatives cannot be computed as differences between timepoints Datasets with high noise levels that violate stoichiometric mass balances, complicating assessment of biological feasibility of response factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3368 Infers metabolic flux profiles from time-course relative-abundance GC-MS metabolomics data by computing smoothed metabolite concentration derivatives and solving the stoichiometric mass balance S·v = dx/dt, exactly for determined systems and via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse with known kinetic terms for underdetermined systems. These flux profiles feed MetaboPAC's penalty calculation for inferring absolute concentrations without chemical standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1039/d2mo00168c
skills.summary: Infers metabolic flux profiles from time-course relative-abundance GC-MS metabolomics data by computing smoothed metabolite concentration derivatives and solving the stoichiometric mass balance S·v = dx/dt, exactly for determined systems and via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse with known kinetic terms for underdetermined systems. These flux profiles feed MetaboPAC's penalty calculation for inferring absolute concentrations without chemical standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Eukaryotic systems requiring transport reactions across intracellular compartments — MetaboPAC does not take these into consideration and applies only to intracellular metabolomics samples in a single compartment Single-timepoint data with no time-course structure — concentration derivatives cannot be computed as differences between timepoints Datasets with high noise levels that violate stoichiometric mass balances, complicating assessment of biological feasibility of response factors

skills.description: Use when a task requires reconstructing the structure of the scFEA human metabolic map from its CSV model files — counting reaction modules, super modules, and intermediate substrates, or tallying genes/enzymes/transporters per module.
skills.name: stoichiometry-matrix-parsing
skills.search_text: stoichiometry-matrix-parsing Use when a task requires reconstructing the structure of the scFEA human metabolic map from its CSV model files — counting reaction modules, super modules, and intermediate substrates, or tallying genes/enzymes/transporters per module. The goal is to estimate cell-wise metabolic fluxes from scRNA-seq data rather than characterize the static network structure of the metabolic map The input model is the mouse model or another non-default module-gene/stoichiometry file set (other candidate files are provided in scFEA's /data/ folder and should be used instead of the m168/m171 defaults) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Parse the scFEA stoichiometry matrix (e.g. cmMat_171.csv), module-gene table (module_gene_m168.csv), and compound-name files (e.g. cName_c70_m168.csv) with pandas to enumerate reaction modules, metabolites, and intermediate substrates, then assemble the module-to-module graph used to reproduce the M171 network composition statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkad444
skills.summary: Parse the scFEA stoichiometry matrix (e.g. cmMat_171.csv), module-gene table (module_gene_m168.csv), and compound-name files (e.g. cName_c70_m168.csv) with pandas to enumerate reaction modules, metabolites, and intermediate substrates, then assemble the module-to-module graph used to reproduce the M171 network composition statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to estimate cell-wise metabolic fluxes from scRNA-seq data rather than characterize the static network structure of the metabolic map The input model is the mouse model or another non-default module-gene/stoichiometry file set (other candidate files are provided in scFEA's /data/ folder and should be used instead of the m168/m171 defaults)

When input is already a set of extracted low-dimensional feature vectors — the encoder/projection/prediction stack is designed for raw 2D ion images. skills.summary: Trains the DeepION contrastive model with a SimSiam-style asymmetric stop-gradient loss on parameter-sharing ResNet18 encoders, preventing collapse of the 512-dimensional ion-image representations learned from augmented MSI image pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is supervised classification with annotated labels rather than self-supervised representation learning without manual annotation. When input is already a set of extracted low-dimensional feature vectors — the encoder/projection/prediction stack is designed for raw 2D ion images. When data are not mass spectrometry imaging ion images; the augmentation and Poisson-noise assumptions are MSI-specific.

skills.description: Use when GCF–spectrum link scoring requires strain co-occurrence vectors but genome/molecule objects carry heterogeneous identifiers (antiSMASH BGC ids, GNPS spectrum ids, mzXML filenames) that must first be reconciled to a shared strain namespace.
skills.name: strain-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: strain-identifier-mapping Use when GCF–spectrum link scoring requires strain co-occurrence vectors but genome/molecule objects carry heterogeneous identifiers (antiSMASH BGC ids, GNPS spectrum ids, mzXML filenames) that must first be reconciled to a shared strain namespace. Spectrum-to-strain mappings are keyed by mzXML filename and are not first passed through extract_mappings_ms_filename_spectrum_id, so filename-to-spectrum-id translation is still pending. The analysis uses a link-scoring method that does not depend on strain co-occurrence (e.g. non-strain-based scoring), in which case strain reconciliation adds nothing. No strain_mapping.json is available for the data set and no manual mapping can be supplied, since NPLinker requires this file to map strain to genomics and metabolomics data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Maps BGC and spectrum identifiers to their source microbial strain using NPLinker's strain_mapping.json file, building the strain co-occurrence vectors for GCFs and molecular families required by strain-correlation scoring (e.g. Metcalf). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Maps BGC and spectrum identifiers to their source microbial strain using NPLinker's strain_mapping.json file, building the strain co-occurrence vectors for GCFs and molecular families required by strain-correlation scoring (e.g. Metcalf).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectrum-to-strain mappings are keyed by mzXML filename and are not first passed through extract_mappings_ms_filename_spectrum_id, so filename-to-spectrum-id translation is still pending. The analysis uses a link-scoring method that does not depend on strain co-occurrence (e.g. non-strain-based scoring), in which case strain reconciliation adds nothing. No strain_mapping.json is available for the data set and no manual mapping can be supplied, since NPLinker requires this file to map strain to genomics and metabolomics data.

skills.description: Use when training a CNN classifier on grayscale molecular fingerprint images with imbalanced or skewed high/low bioactivity labels (normalized DPPH < 0.4 low, > 0.6 high) and you need stable fold-balanced metrics like AUC.
skills.name: stratified-cross-validation
skills.search_text: stratified-cross-validation Use when training a CNN classifier on grayscale molecular fingerprint images with imbalanced or skewed high/low bioactivity labels (normalized DPPH < 0.4 low, > 0.6 high) and you need stable fold-balanced metrics like AUC. Input is already a feature table from aligned peak picking where the Random Forest baseline (AUC 0.817) with standard cross-validation suffices The task is regression of continuous bioactivity values rather than high/low class discrimination Labels have not been binarized (mid-range normalized values 0.4–0.6 included), so stratified class proportions are undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Applies fivefold StratifiedKFold cross-validation (scikit-learn) to train and evaluate the MS2toImg-CNN on binarized bioactivity labels (e.g., DPPH high/low), accumulating per-fold predictions to compute ROC-AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 with confusion matrices. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2510.09716
skills.summary: Applies fivefold StratifiedKFold cross-validation (scikit-learn) to train and evaluate the MS2toImg-CNN on binarized bioactivity labels (e.g., DPPH high/low), accumulating per-fold predictions to compute ROC-AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 with confusion matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table from aligned peak picking where the Random Forest baseline (AUC 0.817) with standard cross-validation suffices The task is regression of continuous bioactivity values rather than high/low class discrimination Labels have not been binarized (mid-range normalized values 0.4–0.6 included), so stratified class proportions are undefined

skills.description: Use when comparing classifier variants (e.g., MSMCE-integrated vs. baseline ResNet50) on a labeled MS dataset and you need fair fold-shared training, fixed hold-out evaluation, and statistical significance (p < 0.05) for accuracy/F1 differences.
skills.name: stratified-cross-validation-experiment-design
skills.search_text: stratified-cross-validation-experiment-design Use when comparing classifier variants (e.g., MSMCE-integrated vs. baseline ResNet50) on a labeled MS dataset and you need fair fold-shared training, fixed hold-out evaluation, and statistical significance (p < 0.05) for accuracy/F1 differences. Ablation-study variant comparisons, where the article's protocol trains on the entire training set (not k-fold split) and evaluates only on the independent hold-out test set Datasets with severely imbalanced class distributions or very small sample sizes, where the authors warn deep models may fail to learn embedding representations Transfer-learning scenarios, which the authors explicitly note were not evaluated and are out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A rigorous benchmarking protocol for comparing deep-learning and traditional ML classifiers on raw mass spectrometry data, combining stratified k-fold cross-validation (K=6) with a fixed hold-out test set and paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank significance testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: A rigorous benchmarking protocol for comparing deep-learning and traditional ML classifiers on raw mass spectrometry data, combining stratified k-fold cross-validation (K=6) with a fixed hold-out test set and paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ablation-study variant comparisons, where the article's protocol trains on the entire training set (not k-fold split) and evaluates only on the independent hold-out test set Datasets with severely imbalanced class distributions or very small sample sizes, where the authors warn deep models may fail to learn embedding representations Transfer-learning scenarios, which the authors explicitly note were not evaluated and are out of scope

skills.description: Use when validating few-shot RT projection to a chromatographic method with limited identified molecules — e.g. testing meta-learned GP projections at 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50 training points.
skills.name: stratified-molecule-subampling-per-chromatographic-method
skills.search_text: stratified-molecule-subampling-per-chromatographic-method Use when validating few-shot RT projection to a chromatographic method with limited identified molecules — e.g. testing meta-learned GP projections at 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50 training points. The target chromatographic method has few identified molecules overall or contains non-retained molecules (RT < 5 min) that must be excluded before subsampling You need full-dataset projection accuracy rather than few-shot (10–50 molecule) evaluation Predicted and experimental RTs cannot be paired per molecule (no common compound identifiers) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds target-task training sets for RT projection evaluation by repeatedly subsampling a small, stratified set of known molecules (10–50) from a held-out chromatographic method in PredRet, so that few-shot projection performance can be averaged over subsample repeats. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8
skills.summary: Builds target-task training sets for RT projection evaluation by repeatedly subsampling a small, stratified set of known molecules (10–50) from a held-out chromatographic method in PredRet, so that few-shot projection performance can be averaged over subsample repeats.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target chromatographic method has few identified molecules overall or contains non-retained molecules (RT < 5 min) that must be excluded before subsampling You need full-dataset projection accuracy rather than few-shot (10–50 molecule) evaluation Predicted and experimental RTs cannot be paired per molecule (no common compound identifiers)

skills.description: Decision support for comparing CCS prediction algorithms on a common footing: when benchmarking CCSP 2.0, CCSbase, AllCCS or DeepCCS against the same 463 McLean CCS Compendium measurements, or designing stratified hold-out splits for IM-MS regression evaluation.
skills.name: stratified-random-test-set-sampling
skills.search_text: stratified-random-test-set-sampling Decision support for comparing CCS prediction algorithms on a common footing: when benchmarking CCSP 2.0, CCSbase, AllCCS or DeepCCS against the same 463 McLean CCS Compendium measurements, or designing stratified hold-out splits for IM-MS regression evaluation. The goal is only to train a single model on a large training set and predict CCS values for small target sets (<10,000 molecules) — no cross-algorithm benchmarking split is needed The data set is not stratified by adduct type, or dimers and less common adducts ([2M+H]+, [2M−H]−) are present — current CCSP 2.0 training sets only cover the common adduct ion types http://edamontology.org/topic_0082 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Draws per-iteration test sets by randomly sampling ~30% of annotated measurements within each adduct stratum ([M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+), holding the identical sampled test sets constant across all prediction algorithms so benchmark MRE/RMSE rankings are fair. This is how CCSP 2.0 was evaluated against CCSbase, AllCCS and DeepCCS in the McLean CCS Compendium benchmark. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c03491
skills.summary: Draws per-iteration test sets by randomly sampling ~30% of annotated measurements within each adduct stratum ([M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+), holding the identical sampled test sets constant across all prediction algorithms so benchmark MRE/RMSE rankings are fair. This is how CCSP 2.0 was evaluated against CCSbase, AllCCS and DeepCCS in the McLean CCS Compendium benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only to train a single model on a large training set and predict CCS values for small target sets (<10,000 molecules) — no cross-algorithm benchmarking split is needed The data set is not stratified by adduct type, or dimers and less common adducts ([2M+H]+, [2M−H]−) are present — current CCSP 2.0 training sets only cover the common adduct ion types

skills.description: Use when you have paired CCS (or other instrument-reported quantity) measurements from two methods/software for the same compounds and need per-stratum (mode, acquisition setting) average absolute relative bias summaries and a tabulated output.
skills.name: stratified-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: stratified-summary-statistics Use when you have paired CCS (or other instrument-reported quantity) measurements from two methods/software for the same compounds and need per-stratum (mode, acquisition setting) average absolute relative bias summaries and a tabulated output. Input is raw LC-DTIM-MS profile data in mzML that still needs CCS extraction — use the CCSfind pipeline (peak picking with isotopologue matching confirmation, single-field CCS calibration with Tfix and Beta coefficients) first, not bias statistics The two CCS value sets are not paired per compound (different compounds or no shared identifiers), making per-entry relative bias meaningless A single pooled average is requested with no stratification by ionization mode or acquisition setting — mode-specific structure (e.g., 0.35%–0.93% single-pulse bias) would be masked http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A pandas/numpy workflow for computing stratified average absolute relative bias between paired CCS values — here CCSfind (targeted) vs vendor (non-targeted) DTCCS N2 values — across ionization modes and acquisition settings, reproducing Table 1 summary statistics from the CCSfind paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040
skills.summary: A pandas/numpy workflow for computing stratified average absolute relative bias between paired CCS values — here CCSfind (targeted) vs vendor (non-targeted) DTCCS N2 values — across ionization modes and acquisition settings, reproducing Table 1 summary statistics from the CCSfind paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-DTIM-MS profile data in mzML that still needs CCS extraction — use the CCSfind pipeline (peak picking with isotopologue matching confirmation, single-field CCS calibration with Tfix and Beta coefficients) first, not bias statistics The two CCS value sets are not paired per compound (different compounds or no shared identifiers), making per-entry relative bias meaningless A single pooled average is requested with no stratification by ionization mode or acquisition setting — mode-specific structure (e.g., 0.35%–0.93% single-pulse bias) would be masked

skills.description: Use when building predictive models (e.g. RF or elastic-net classifiers) from a metabolite-by-sample intensity table with class labels, and you need class-proportioned train/test separation before feature selection and AUC evaluation.
skills.name: stratified-train-test-split-metabolomics
skills.search_text: stratified-train-test-split-metabolomics Use when building predictive models (e.g. RF or elastic-net classifiers) from a metabolite-by-sample intensity table with class labels, and you need class-proportioned train/test separation before feature selection and AUC evaluation. Raw spectra need preprocessing or peak picking/annotation — iMAP deliberately does not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking and annotation modules The task is pure statistical metabolite selection or network analysis without any prediction/validation goal — no train-test separation is needed The dataset is too small for a 20% hold-out to preserve class representation; nested cross-validation may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Splits a metabolomics intensity matrix into stratified training and held-out test sets (e.g. 8:2 ratio on the 234-sample Zhu et al. 2014 serum metabolite dataset: 66 CRC, 76 PolyP, 92 HC) as the first step of iMAP's automatic predictive-modeling pipeline, so that feature selection and model fitting can be followed by honest validation on unseen samples. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: Splits a metabolomics intensity matrix into stratified training and held-out test sets (e.g. 8:2 ratio on the 234-sample Zhu et al. 2014 serum metabolite dataset: 66 CRC, 76 PolyP, 92 HC) as the first step of iMAP's automatic predictive-modeling pipeline, so that feature selection and model fitting can be followed by honest validation on unseen samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw spectra need preprocessing or peak picking/annotation — iMAP deliberately does not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking and annotation modules The task is pure statistical metabolite selection or network analysis without any prediction/validation goal — no train-test separation is needed The dataset is too small for a 20% hold-out to preserve class representation; nested cross-validation may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when authentic analytical standards are unavailable for CMDN-annotated metabolites and chromatographic plausibility must be validated by predicting LC-HRMS retention times from molecular structure (SMILES/InChIKey).
skills.name: stratified-train-test-split-optimization
skills.search_text: stratified-train-test-split-optimization Use when authentic analytical standards are unavailable for CMDN-annotated metabolites and chromatographic plausibility must be validated by predicting LC-HRMS retention times from molecular structure (SMILES/InChIKey). Authentic analytical or stable-isotopic-labeled standards are available for the metabolites, so standard verification rather than in silico RT prediction should be used for validation The compounds of interest have no experimentally measured LC-HRMS retention times, so no labeled training set exists to fit or evaluate the regressors The goal is MS2-level annotation (spectral similarity) rather than chromatographic-behavior validation, which this RT-only regression does not address http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Builds retention-time (RT) prediction models (XGBoost, Random Forest, Bayesian regularized neural network) on the 1,021-pesticide library using RDKit molecular descriptors, and applies an 80:20 train/test split stratified on the RT distribution so that model selection is reproducible and comparable across regressors. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558
skills.summary: Builds retention-time (RT) prediction models (XGBoost, Random Forest, Bayesian regularized neural network) on the 1,021-pesticide library using RDKit molecular descriptors, and applies an 80:20 train/test split stratified on the RT distribution so that model selection is reproducible and comparable across regressors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Authentic analytical or stable-isotopic-labeled standards are available for the metabolites, so standard verification rather than in silico RT prediction should be used for validation The compounds of interest have no experimentally measured LC-HRMS retention times, so no labeled training set exists to fit or evaluate the regressors The goal is MS2-level annotation (spectral similarity) rather than chromatographic-behavior validation, which this RT-only regression does not address

skills.description: Use when you have co-registered spatial metabolomics (MALDI-TOF/imzML) and spatial transcriptomics (e.g. 10X Visium) data on the same tissue section and need to test whether multi-omic integration recovers spatial populations that unimodal clustering misses.
skills.name: striatal-cluster-map-comparison
skills.search_text: striatal-cluster-map-comparison Use when you have co-registered spatial metabolomics (MALDI-TOF/imzML) and spatial transcriptomics (e.g. 10X Visium) data on the same tissue section and need to test whether multi-omic integration recovers spatial populations that unimodal clustering misses. Only one modality is available (SM or ST alone) — integration requires paired, spatially co-registered data on the same section The MALDI and transcriptomics data have not been aligned to a shared spot grid (e.g. MALDI pixels not binned into 55 µm Visium spots) — run AlignSpatialOmics/MapSpatialOmics first The goal is metabolite m/z annotation rather than clustering — use SpaMTP's annotation pipeline (AnnotateBigData, BuildMZAnnotationIndex) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares per-spot cluster assignments from SM-only, ST-only, and WNN-integrated clustering of paired spatial metabolomics/transcriptomics data using SpaMTP's MultiOmicIntegration (Seurat-based weighted nearest neighbours), to reveal striatal spot populations that single-modality clustering misses. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Compares per-spot cluster assignments from SM-only, ST-only, and WNN-integrated clustering of paired spatial metabolomics/transcriptomics data using SpaMTP's MultiOmicIntegration (Seurat-based weighted nearest neighbours), to reveal striatal spot populations that single-modality clustering misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one modality is available (SM or ST alone) — integration requires paired, spatially co-registered data on the same section The MALDI and transcriptomics data have not been aligned to a shared spot grid (e.g. MALDI pixels not binned into 55 µm Visium spots) — run AlignSpatialOmics/MapSpatialOmics first The goal is metabolite m/z annotation rather than clustering — use SpaMTP's annotation pipeline (AnnotateBigData, BuildMZAnnotationIndex) instead
