skills.search_text: string-functional-network-mapping Use when per-gene enrichment scores (e.g., linear_msea_genebig_allpeaks_combined.csv) must be propagated over the STRING functional network to rank WES candidate genes for a single patient. When the patient's disease-associated metabolites are not measurable by the available metabolomic system (e.g., large glycosaminoglycans for the IDS patient), since ME scores for those genes will be missing or uninformative When curated metabolite identities are required rather than non-curated feature-level enrichment — TIDEX feature-to-metabolite mapping was unavailable, so exact metabolic identities cannot be determined When candidate lists are already short (trio WES with parental data), where the paper notes prioritization is already simplified and network smoothing adds less value http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Maps per-gene metabolomic perturbation scores (ME/DME from Fisher's Exact enrichment against HMDB gene-metabolite sets) onto STRING v11 functional linkage network nodes, then propagates them with label propagation so candidate genes inherit evidence from network neighbors. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Maps per-gene metabolomic perturbation scores (ME/DME from Fisher's Exact enrichment against HMDB gene-metabolite sets) onto STRING v11 functional linkage network nodes, then propagates them with label propagation so candidate genes inherit evidence from network neighbors.

skills.search_text: structural-analogue-retrieval-evaluation Use when MS/MS spectra must be searched against a spectral library to retrieve structural analogues and compared to baseline similarity measures via precision-recall curves at Tanimoto cut-offs from 0.6 to 0.9. The task is spectral similarity prediction for training a model or computing post hoc fragment-association explanations rather than benchmarking analogue-retrieval performance against baselines. Structural similarity cannot be computed (no reference structures available to derive Daylight-fingerprint Tanimoto scores), since the precision-recall evaluation depends on Tanimoto cut-offs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates how well MS/MS spectral similarity measures (TransExION vs. Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) retrieve structural analogues from a spectral library, using precision-recall analysis at Daylight-fingerprint Tanimoto cut-offs (0.6–0.9). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Evaluates how well MS/MS spectral similarity measures (TransExION vs. Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) retrieve structural analogues from a spectral library, using precision-recall analysis at Daylight-fingerprint Tanimoto cut-offs (0.6–0.9).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is spectral similarity prediction for training a model or computing post hoc fragment-association explanations rather than benchmarking analogue-retrieval performance against baselines. Structural similarity cannot be computed (no reference structures available to derive Daylight-fingerprint Tanimoto scores), since the precision-recall evaluation depends on Tanimoto cut-offs.

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics workflow has processed samples containing compounds of known identity (e.g. actinomycete extracts or commercial standards) and you must quantify how accurately formulas, structures, and spectral matches were annotated.
skills.name: structural-annotation-evaluation
skills.search_text: structural-annotation-evaluation Use when a metabolomics workflow has processed samples containing compounds of known identity (e.g. actinomycete extracts or commercial standards) and you must quantify how accurately formulas, structures, and spectral matches were annotated. Benchmarking feature detection, quantification, or marker selection on public datasets (MTBLS733/MTBLS736/MTBLS1129/MTBLS1130) — that evaluation compares ground-truth feature recovery and quantification, not annotation accuracy. Input samples lack compounds of known identity or expected features, so no ground truth exists against which to compute detection or annotation fractions. Input is already an annotated feature table where you only need downstream export (e.g. GNPS FBMN/IIMN GraphML integration) rather than accuracy assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Validates untargeted metabolomics structural and formula annotation performance by computing accuracy fractions of SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID predictions and spectral-library matches against compounds with known identities. In the UmetaFlow paper this yielded 76% formula, ~62% structure, and 65% total annotation accuracy on actinomycete and commercial-standard LC-MS/MS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w
skills.summary: Validates untargeted metabolomics structural and formula annotation performance by computing accuracy fractions of SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID predictions and spectral-library matches against compounds with known identities. In the UmetaFlow paper this yielded 76% formula, ~62% structure, and 65% total annotation accuracy on actinomycete and commercial-standard LC-MS/MS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking feature detection, quantification, or marker selection on public datasets (MTBLS733/MTBLS736/MTBLS1129/MTBLS1130) — that evaluation compares ground-truth feature recovery and quantification, not annotation accuracy. Input samples lack compounds of known identity or expected features, so no ground truth exists against which to compute detection or annotation fractions. Input is already an annotated feature table where you only need downstream export (e.g. GNPS FBMN/IIMN GraphML integration) rather than accuracy assessment.

skills.name: structural-descriptor-calculation
skills.search_text: structural-descriptor-calculation Use when a compound metadata sheet (template columns: unique sample id, plate_id, well_location, name, structure fields) must be standardized and enriched with SMILES/InChI/InChIKey/logP/monoisotopic mass before spectral library generation or database cross-referencing. skills.summary: Compute per-compound structural descriptors — canonical and isomeric SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, logP, and monoisotopic mass — from a harmonized metadata table as part of the MSnLib metadata cleanup Prefect flow, using the ChEMBL structure pipeline for standardization and PubChem name lookups when structures are missing.

skills.description: Use when building annotation records for taxonomy categories or compounds that must be defined by unambiguous, computable structural keys (elemental composition, formula, oxyanions) parsed from a ChemOnt OBO file, as ClassyFire does for its inorganic branch.
skills.name: structural-key-annotation-extraction
skills.search_text: structural-key-annotation-extraction Use when building annotation records for taxonomy categories or compounds that must be defined by unambiguous, computable structural keys (elemental composition, formula, oxyanions) parsed from a ChemOnt OBO file, as ClassyFire does for its inorganic branch. Classifying organic compounds by functional group — use the standard ClassyFire feature-extraction and rule-based category-assignment pipeline instead Compounds that undergo reactions (e.g. loss of oxygen, substitutions) may not match the constraints described in a category description, so structural-key annotation alone can mis-assign them Query compounds for which only an IUPAC name is available and the ~200 name-parsing rules are insufficient for accurate class assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Extracts computable structural keys (elemental content, molecular formula, oxyanion lists) from the ChemOnt taxonomy's category definitions — especially the inorganic branch — and writes them as parent-linked, machine-readable annotation records. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Extracts computable structural keys (elemental content, molecular formula, oxyanion lists) from the ChemOnt taxonomy's category definitions — especially the inorganic branch — and writes them as parent-linked, machine-readable annotation records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Classifying organic compounds by functional group — use the standard ClassyFire feature-extraction and rule-based category-assignment pipeline instead Compounds that undergo reactions (e.g. loss of oxygen, substitutions) may not match the constraints described in a category description, so structural-key annotation alone can mis-assign them Query compounds for which only an IUPAC name is available and the ~200 name-parsing rules are insufficient for accurate class assignment

skills.description: Use when you must confirm that relative positions of a chosen lipid series in a graph-based structural space remain stable after recomputation within a larger background lipidome, e.g. reproducing the arc-like PC ordering.
skills.name: structural-ordering-robustness-comparison-across-embeddings
skills.search_text: structural-ordering-robustness-comparison-across-embeddings Use when you must confirm that relative positions of a chosen lipid series in a graph-based structural space remain stable after recomputation within a larger background lipidome, e.g. reproducing the arc-like PC ordering. The analysis goal is quantitative (abundance-based) comparison of lipidomes — abundances are deliberately excluded from structural space models, so this skill cannot validate intensity-driven conclusions Lipid names cannot be resolved to full structures (e.g. species without defined fatty acyl composition), since MCS/Jaccard distances require structural resolution from LIPID MAPS/SwissLipids You need a standalone numeric pipeline output rather than an interactive check — LipidSpace currently cannot store or load an analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Verifies that the relative spatial ordering of a defined lipid subset in a structural space (built from maximum-common-subgraph + Jaccard distances and Lanczos PCA) is preserved when the subset is embedded in a larger background lipidome. In LipidSpace, the 14 PC 12:0/[12−24,26]:0 species retain their arc-like sequential arrangement in both the isolated and the embedded model. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c02449
skills.summary: Verifies that the relative spatial ordering of a defined lipid subset in a structural space (built from maximum-common-subgraph + Jaccard distances and Lanczos PCA) is preserved when the subset is embedded in a larger background lipidome. In LipidSpace, the 14 PC 12:0/[12−24,26]:0 species retain their arc-like sequential arrangement in both the isolated and the embedded model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is quantitative (abundance-based) comparison of lipidomes — abundances are deliberately excluded from structural space models, so this skill cannot validate intensity-driven conclusions Lipid names cannot be resolved to full structures (e.g. species without defined fatty acyl composition), since MCS/Jaccard distances require structural resolution from LIPID MAPS/SwissLipids You need a standalone numeric pipeline output rather than an interactive check — LipidSpace currently cannot store or load an analysis

skills.description: Use when a spectral similarity network (e.g., an MCN output) must be validated against reference spectra with known structural classes, to check that community/cluster assignments group structurally related molecules together.
skills.name: structural-relatedness-assessment-of-spectral-clusters
skills.search_text: structural-relatedness-assessment-of-spectral-clusters Use when a spectral similarity network (e.g., an MCN output) must be validated against reference spectra with known structural classes, to check that community/cluster assignments group structurally related molecules together. The spectra lack known structural class annotations, so cluster-to-structure correspondence cannot be checked (this skill is a reference-set validation, not a discovery workflow). The network was built with a conventional single arbitrary similarity threshold rather than MCN's per-metabolite connectivity optimization, since the validation is specific to MCN-derived communities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Validation procedure for molecular community networking (MCN) outputs in which clusters derived from a deposited reference spectra collection are compared against the known structural classes of the reference compounds, confirming that network connections reflect meaningful molecular relationships rather than arbitrary similarity-threshold artifacts. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.02.606356
skills.summary: Validation procedure for molecular community networking (MCN) outputs in which clusters derived from a deposited reference spectra collection are compared against the known structural classes of the reference compounds, confirming that network connections reflect meaningful molecular relationships rather than arbitrary similarity-threshold artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra lack known structural class annotations, so cluster-to-structure correspondence cannot be checked (this skill is a reference-set validation, not a discovery workflow). The network was built with a conventional single arbitrary similarity threshold rather than MCN's per-metabolite connectivity optimization, since the validation is specific to MCN-derived communities.

skills.description: Use when you have acquired tandem MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites (e.g. from Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) and need to identify them by ranking known database metabolites (e.g. KEGG) by structural similarity rather than exact spectral match.
skills.name: structural-similarity-metabolite-ranking
skills.search_text: structural-similarity-metabolite-ranking Use when you have acquired tandem MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites (e.g. from Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) and need to identify them by ranking known database metabolites (e.g. KEGG) by structural similarity rather than exact spectral match. When you already have a high-quality experimental MS/MS spectrum of the unknown compound in the database, an exact spectral match should be preferred over structural-similarity ranking. When your query spectra are not from the instruments/formats the trained DeepMASS model was built for (e.g. spectra outside the 40V collision-energy context or an in-house database very different from KEGG), retraining with test.py is required before ranking. When the analysis goal is de-novo structure elucidation rather than ranking known database metabolites — this skill only ranks candidates that exist in the reference database. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Rank candidate structures for an unknown metabolite by scoring structural similarity against known database metabolites from their MS/MS spectra, using the DeepMASS deep-neural-network scorer, and validate identifications via a structure-related-metabolite criterion. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05405
skills.summary: Rank candidate structures for an unknown metabolite by scoring structural similarity against known database metabolites from their MS/MS spectra, using the DeepMASS deep-neural-network scorer, and validate identifications via a structure-related-metabolite criterion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you already have a high-quality experimental MS/MS spectrum of the unknown compound in the database, an exact spectral match should be preferred over structural-similarity ranking. When your query spectra are not from the instruments/formats the trained DeepMASS model was built for (e.g. spectra outside the 40V collision-energy context or an in-house database very different from KEGG), retraining with test.py is required before ranking. When the analysis goal is de-novo structure elucidation rather than ranking known database metabolites — this skill only ranks candidates that exist in the reference database.

skills.description: Use when identifying an unknown metabolite whose MS/MS spectrum lacks an exact match in a database, but structurally related known metabolites (e.g. KEGG entries) exist whose spectra can anchor similarity scoring.
skills.name: structural-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: structural-similarity-scoring Use when identifying an unknown metabolite whose MS/MS spectrum lacks an exact match in a database, but structurally related known metabolites (e.g. KEGG entries) exist whose spectra can anchor similarity scoring. The unknown metabolite's spectrum has an exact match in the MS/MS database — direct spectral matching is faster and already sufficient No structure-related metabolite exists in the database, since the paper states identification is valid only when a structure-related metabolite is available Spectra were acquired at collision energies other than the pretrained model's (40V), and no in-house database is available to retrain (the MetDNA experimental-spectra dataset was removed from the repo, so the package cannot be run directly out of the box) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 DeepMASS uses a deep neural network trained on MS/MS spectrum pairs to output a structural-similarity score that ranks database candidates for an unknown metabolite, extending identification beyond exact spectral matches in databases like KEGG. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b05405
skills.summary: DeepMASS uses a deep neural network trained on MS/MS spectrum pairs to output a structural-similarity score that ranks database candidates for an unknown metabolite, extending identification beyond exact spectral matches in databases like KEGG.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unknown metabolite's spectrum has an exact match in the MS/MS database — direct spectral matching is faster and already sufficient No structure-related metabolite exists in the database, since the paper states identification is valid only when a structure-related metabolite is available Spectra were acquired at collision energies other than the pretrained model's (40V), and no in-house database is available to retrain (the MetDNA experimental-spectra dataset was removed from the repo, so the package cannot be run directly out of the box)

skills.description: Use when you have held-out 1H-13C HSQC query spectra (normal or multiplicity edited) with ground-truth structures and need to score/reproduce Top-1 identification rates, annotation rates at cosine > 0.8, and precision/recall/F1@k against SMART 2.0 or NMRShiftDB shift-search baselines.
skills.name: structure-annotation-benchmark-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: structure-annotation-benchmark-metrics-computation Use when you have held-out 1H-13C HSQC query spectra (normal or multiplicity edited) with ground-truth structures and need to score/reproduce Top-1 identification rates, annotation rates at cosine > 0.8, and precision/recall/F1@k against SMART 2.0 or NMRShiftDB shift-search baselines. Query spectra are MS/MS fragmentation or bioactivity/genome-mining data (AntiSMASH, BiG-SCAPE/CORASON, GNPS) rather than 1H-13C HSQC spectra The goal is training or recalibrating the DeepSAT model itself, not evaluating annotation/search performance against baselines No ground-truth structures or known Morgan fingerprints exist for the queries, so no cosine-threshold scoring at 0.8 can be computed Computes and compares benchmark metrics — Top-1 identification rates, annotation rates (cosine > 0.8 on Morgan fingerprints), and precision/recall/F1@k — for NMR-driven structure annotation systems, reproducing the DeepSAT vs SMART 2.0 vs NMRShiftDB comparison on held-out 1H-13C HSQC test spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00738-4
skills.summary: Computes and compares benchmark metrics — Top-1 identification rates, annotation rates (cosine > 0.8 on Morgan fingerprints), and precision/recall/F1@k — for NMR-driven structure annotation systems, reproducing the DeepSAT vs SMART 2.0 vs NMRShiftDB comparison on held-out 1H-13C HSQC test spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query spectra are MS/MS fragmentation or bioactivity/genome-mining data (AntiSMASH, BiG-SCAPE/CORASON, GNPS) rather than 1H-13C HSQC spectra The goal is training or recalibrating the DeepSAT model itself, not evaluating annotation/search performance against baselines No ground-truth structures or known Morgan fingerprints exist for the queries, so no cosine-threshold scoring at 0.8 can be computed

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a candidate-ranking score for MS/MS structure annotation against known-correct structures (e.g., CASMI 2016 contest data), to quantify separation via AUC, FDR-level hit counts, and mean rank of correct hits.
skills.name: structure-annotation-rank-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: structure-annotation-rank-benchmark-evaluation Use when benchmarking a candidate-ranking score for MS/MS structure annotation against known-correct structures (e.g., CASMI 2016 contest data), to quantify separation via AUC, FDR-level hit counts, and mean rank of correct hits. Input is raw LC–MS/MS data (mzML/mzXML) requiring SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID candidate generation and scoring rather than evaluation of already-published hit scores There is no known correct structure for the queries (e.g., biological datasets), since the rank benchmark requires ground truth to compute ROC, FDR-level hit counts, and mean rank The goal is de novo annotation of unseen compounds rather than quantifying how well an existing score separates correct from incorrect annotations Evaluates whether a structure-annotation score (e.g., COSMIC confidence score vs in silico tool hit scores) actually separates correct from incorrect candidate annotations, using rank-based metrics (ROC AUC, hop plots, correct-hit counts at FDR levels) on benchmark data such as CASMI 2016. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a structure-annotation score (e.g., COSMIC confidence score vs in silico tool hit scores) actually separates correct from incorrect candidate annotations, using rank-based metrics (ROC AUC, hop plots, correct-hit counts at FDR levels) on benchmark data such as CASMI 2016.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC–MS/MS data (mzML/mzXML) requiring SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID candidate generation and scoring rather than evaluation of already-published hit scores There is no known correct structure for the queries (e.g., biological datasets), since the rank benchmark requires ground truth to compute ROC, FDR-level hit counts, and mean rank The goal is de novo annotation of unseen compounds rather than quantifying how well an existing score separates correct from incorrect annotations

skills.description: Use when MS/MS library entries carry structural annotations (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey) whose consistency against adduct, precursor m/z, parent mass and ionmode must be checked or repaired before library searching or ML training.
skills.name: structure-annotation-validation
skills.search_text: structure-annotation-validation Use when MS/MS library entries carry structural annotations (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey) whose consistency against adduct, precursor m/z, parent mass and ionmode must be checked or repaired before library searching or ML training. The goal is to verify that measured fragments match the given annotation — fragment-matching plausibility filters are not implemented and wrong annotations consistent with the measured mass go unnoticed The fields needing cleanup are instrument type or collision energies — these are not yet standardized by current matchms filters Spectra lack any structure annotation or derivable compound name — validation can neither repair nor confirm them and they will be removed by Require Valid Annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validate and repair chemical structure annotations (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) of MS/MS library spectra for internal consistency with adduct, precursor m/z and parent mass, using matchms filters backed by RDKit and PubChem, removing spectra with irreparable annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00878-1
skills.summary: Validate and repair chemical structure annotations (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) of MS/MS library spectra for internal consistency with adduct, precursor m/z and parent mass, using matchms filters backed by RDKit and PubChem, removing spectra with irreparable annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to verify that measured fragments match the given annotation — fragment-matching plausibility filters are not implemented and wrong annotations consistent with the measured mass go unnoticed The fields needing cleanup are instrument type or collision energies — these are not yet standardized by current matchms filters Spectra lack any structure annotation or derivable compound name — validation can neither repair nor confirm them and they will be removed by Require Valid Annotation

skills.description: Use when untargeted metabolomics spectra (mzML/mzXML, positive ion mode) cannot be matched to spectral libraries and you need ranked, confidence-scored structure annotations from a structure database such as HMDB or a combinatorial candidate set.
skills.name: structure-candidate-ranking
skills.search_text: structure-candidate-ranking Use when untargeted metabolomics spectra (mzML/mzXML, positive ion mode) cannot be matched to spectral libraries and you need ranked, confidence-scored structure annotations from a structure database such as HMDB or a combinatorial candidate set. Reference MS/MS spectra exist in spectral libraries (MassBank, GNPS, NIST 2017) — spectral library search is the appropriate first-line de-replication method You need stereochemical assignment — the method considers only the two-dimensional structure, as stereochemistry cannot be established from fragmentation spectra Input is a peptide/protein ID problem or a processed feature table lacking fragmentation spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Rank molecular structure candidates for untargeted LC–MS/MS features by combining SIRIUS 4 de novo formula assignment, CSI:FingerID structure candidate search, and the COSMIC confidence score, so that in silico annotations absent from spectral libraries can be filtered to high confidence (~FDR 10% at score threshold 0.64). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Rank molecular structure candidates for untargeted LC–MS/MS features by combining SIRIUS 4 de novo formula assignment, CSI:FingerID structure candidate search, and the COSMIC confidence score, so that in silico annotations absent from spectral libraries can be filtered to high confidence (~FDR 10% at score threshold 0.64).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference MS/MS spectra exist in spectral libraries (MassBank, GNPS, NIST 2017) — spectral library search is the appropriate first-line de-replication method You need stereochemical assignment — the method considers only the two-dimensional structure, as stereochemistry cannot be established from fragmentation spectra Input is a peptide/protein ID problem or a processed feature table lacking fragmentation spectra

skills.description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra of compounds already assigned at MSI confidence level 1 via authentic standards and need to measure how often an in silico annotator (CSI:FingerID) ranks the true structure first or in the top 3.
skills.name: structure-candidate-ranking-comparison
skills.search_text: structure-candidate-ranking-comparison Use when you have MS/MS spectra of compounds already assigned at MSI confidence level 1 via authentic standards and need to measure how often an in silico annotator (CSI:FingerID) ranks the true structure first or in the top 3. The input spectra are not supported by authentic-standard measurements — results would only reach MSI level 2/3 confidence, not the level 1 ground truth this benchmark requires You lack a defined structure search space or mass tolerance, so candidate ranking is not reproducible against the published 40%/52% figures The goal is general chemical-class profiling of unannotated spectra (ClassyFire/ontology work), not accuracy measurement of structure ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Benchmarks in silico structure annotation (CSI:FingerID) top-ranked and top-3 candidate predictions against authentic-standard (MSI level 1) compound assignments to quantify annotation accuracy, as in the urine HILIC/CSH Q Exactive HF study where 40% of 103 MSI level 1 compounds were correctly annotated as the top hit. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.8b04698
skills.summary: Benchmarks in silico structure annotation (CSI:FingerID) top-ranked and top-3 candidate predictions against authentic-standard (MSI level 1) compound assignments to quantify annotation accuracy, as in the urine HILIC/CSH Q Exactive HF study where 40% of 103 MSI level 1 compounds were correctly annotated as the top hit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra are not supported by authentic-standard measurements — results would only reach MSI level 2/3 confidence, not the level 1 ground truth this benchmark requires You lack a defined structure search space or mass tolerance, so candidate ranking is not reproducible against the published 40%/52% figures The goal is general chemical-class profiling of unannotated spectra (ClassyFire/ontology work), not accuracy measurement of structure ranking

skills.description: Use when enumerating a combinatorial search database (e.g. amino-acid conjugates of bile acid scaffolds) and you must confirm the enumerated structure count matches the expected database size before downstream annotation.
skills.name: structure-database-size-validation
skills.search_text: structure-database-size-validation Use when enumerating a combinatorial search database (e.g. amino-acid conjugates of bile acid scaffolds) and you must confirm the enumerated structure count matches the expected database size before downstream annotation. When structures already exist in a curated database (e.g. the HMDB structure database with 113,983 compounds); no combinatorial enumeration is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Validates an in silico combinatorial structure database generation run for COSMIC by exhaustively enumerating bile acid conjugates with SmiLib v2.0 and checking that the output contains exactly 28,630 structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Validates an in silico combinatorial structure database generation run for COSMIC by exhaustively enumerating bile acid conjugates with SmiLib v2.0 and checking that the output contains exactly 28,630 structures.

skills.description: Use when building a non-redundant structural dataset from spectral library entries (e.g. GNPS .mgf) where duplicate structures and stereoisomers must be collapsed to unique first-layer InChIKeys.
skills.name: structure-deduplication-by-inchikey-layer
skills.search_text: structure-deduplication-by-inchikey-layer Use when building a non-redundant structural dataset from spectral library entries (e.g. GNPS .mgf) where duplicate structures and stereoisomers must be collapsed to unique first-layer InChIKeys. Stereochemistry must be preserved as distinct candidates (e.g. benchmarking stereospecific annotation), since deduplication by the first 14 InChIKey characters merges stereoisomers by design. Spectra are still under the mgf pre-filter (fewer than 6 fragments or >500 peaks unprocessed) — apply mgf filtering first, as this deduplication operates on the cleaned entry set. The goal is detecting (near-)duplicate molecules across databases for clustering rather than building a benchmarking set — a broader similarity search is needed, not connectivity-layer dedup. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Collapses duplicate structures and stereoisomers in a spectral library dataset by comparing the first layer (first 14 characters) of the RDKit-generated InChIKey, keeping one entry per unique structural layer. Used in the taxonomically informed annotation pipeline to build the 40,138-entry benchmarking set from 8,558 unique structures. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Collapses duplicate structures and stereoisomers in a spectral library dataset by comparing the first layer (first 14 characters) of the RDKit-generated InChIKey, keeping one entry per unique structural layer. Used in the taxonomically informed annotation pipeline to build the 40,138-entry benchmarking set from 8,558 unique structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Stereochemistry must be preserved as distinct candidates (e.g. benchmarking stereospecific annotation), since deduplication by the first 14 InChIKey characters merges stereoisomers by design. Spectra are still under the mgf pre-filter (fewer than 6 fragments or >500 peaks unprocessed) — apply mgf filtering first, as this deduplication operates on the cleaned entry set. The goal is detecting (near-)duplicate molecules across databases for clustering rather than building a benchmarking set — a broader similarity search is needed, not connectivity-layer dedup.

skills.description: Use when re-evaluating formula or structure identification tools (e.g. SIRIUS 4 / CSI:FingerID) on a public challenge dataset such as CASMI 2016 and a fair, training-independent estimate of top-1/top-k identification rates is needed.
skills.name: structure-disjoint-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: structure-disjoint-benchmark-evaluation Use when re-evaluating formula or structure identification tools (e.g. SIRIUS 4 / CSI:FingerID) on a public challenge dataset such as CASMI 2016 and a fair, training-independent estimate of top-1/top-k identification rates is needed. skills.name: subcluster-motif-probability-filtering
skills.search_text: subcluster-motif-probability-filtering Use when querying tokenised BGCs (bags of (sub)Pfam domain combinations) against trained LDA sub-cluster motifs and you must decide which gene-to-motif assignments count as real sub-cluster predictions versus noise. When gene order matters — LDA assumes a bag-of-words model where original gene order is not considered; use the PRESTO-STAT statistical method which keeps tokenised genes in their original order When the goal is de novo BGC discovery rather than sub-cluster prediction — the motifs only cover sub-clusters (e.g. methoxymalonate, AHBA motifs), not full BGC core machinery When the motif bank has not been trained — the thresholds are meaningless without per-motif and per-gene probability vectors from a fitted LDA model http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Filters PRESTO-TOP LDA sub-cluster motifs and query hits using probability thresholds: motif domain-combinations are truncated at a cumulative probability of 0.95 to remove noise, and BGC gene-to-motif matches must pass gene-level (p > 0.3), summed (Σp > 1.1), and overlap (≥ 0.15) cut-offs before a sub-cluster prediction is accepted. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Filters PRESTO-TOP LDA sub-cluster motifs and query hits using probability thresholds: motif domain-combinations are truncated at a cumulative probability of 0.95 to remove noise, and BGC gene-to-motif matches must pass gene-level (p > 0.3), summed (Σp > 1.1), and overlap (≥ 0.15) cut-offs before a sub-cluster prediction is accepted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene order matters — LDA assumes a bag-of-words model where original gene order is not considered; use the PRESTO-STAT statistical method which keeps tokenised genes in their original order When the goal is de novo BGC discovery rather than sub-cluster prediction — the motifs only cover sub-clusters (e.g. methoxymalonate, AHBA motifs), not full BGC core machinery When the motif bank has not been trained — the thresholds are meaningless without per-motif and per-gene probability vectors from a fitted LDA model

skills.description: Use when you have antiSMASH-predicted BGCs tokenised with (sub)Pfam domains and need to identify which PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster motifs they match, e.g. to nominate a candidate BGC for an orphan metabolite.
skills.name: subcluster-motif-querying
skills.search_text: subcluster-motif-querying Use when you have antiSMASH-predicted BGCs tokenised with (sub)Pfam domains and need to identify which PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster motifs they match, e.g. to nominate a candidate BGC for an orphan metabolite. The BGCs have not yet been tokenised into (sub)Pfam domain tokens — run antiSMASH and the tokenisation step first The goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery rather than querying existing motifs — use iPRESTO's PRESTO-STAT/PRESTO-TOP prediction mode instead You need to link metabolomics Mass2Motifs to sub-clusters across a strain panel — that requires the metabologenomic correlation workflow, not motif querying http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Query tokenised BGCs against a reference set of PRESTO sub-cluster motifs (e.g. the 1,000 annotated PRESTO-TOP motifs from antiSMASH-DB) to flag biosynthetic sub-structures — such as methylaminosugar or halogenated aromatic moieties — inside newly mined gene clusters, enabling genome-based structure prediction for orphan metabolites. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Query tokenised BGCs against a reference set of PRESTO sub-cluster motifs (e.g. the 1,000 annotated PRESTO-TOP motifs from antiSMASH-DB) to flag biosynthetic sub-structures — such as methylaminosugar or halogenated aromatic moieties — inside newly mined gene clusters, enabling genome-based structure prediction for orphan metabolites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BGCs have not yet been tokenised into (sub)Pfam domain tokens — run antiSMASH and the tokenisation step first The goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery rather than querying existing motifs — use iPRESTO's PRESTO-STAT/PRESTO-TOP prediction mode instead You need to link metabolomics Mass2Motifs to sub-clusters across a strain panel — that requires the metabologenomic correlation workflow, not motif querying

skills.description: Use when validating predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters against a curated set of experimentally verified sub-clusters by quantifying per-sub-cluster gene overlap fractions against a defined cut-off.
skills.name: subcluster-overlap-calculation
skills.search_text: subcluster-overlap-calculation Use when validating predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters against a curated set of experimentally verified sub-clusters by quantifying per-sub-cluster gene overlap fractions against a defined cut-off. When the goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery or tokenisation of BGCs rather than benchmarking predicted sub-clusters against known ones When comparing sub-clusters by gene order or adjacency rather than gene-set membership — the overlap metric treats sub-clusters as sets of genes and ignores the adjacency-index graph filtering used elsewhere in iPRESTO http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the fraction of genes from an experimentally verified sub-cluster (e.g. from the antiSMASH SubClusterBlast module) that are found in a predicted sub-cluster (PRESTO-STAT or PRESTO-TOP), using a 0.6 overlap cut-off to declare a validated sub-cluster as detected. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Computes the fraction of genes from an experimentally verified sub-cluster (e.g. from the antiSMASH SubClusterBlast module) that are found in a predicted sub-cluster (PRESTO-STAT or PRESTO-TOP), using a 0.6 overlap cut-off to declare a validated sub-cluster as detected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery or tokenisation of BGCs rather than benchmarking predicted sub-clusters against known ones When comparing sub-clusters by gene order or adjacency rather than gene-set membership — the overlap metric treats sub-clusters as sets of genes and ignores the adjacency-index graph filtering used elsewhere in iPRESTO

skills.description: Use when a PRESTO-STAT run on tokenised antiSMASH-DB BGCs has produced a sub-cluster table and you must verify the detection count and the size and BGC-occurrence distributions reproduce the reported benchmarks.
skills.name: subcluster-size-occurrence-distribution-validation
skills.search_text: subcluster-size-occurrence-distribution-validation Use when a PRESTO-STAT run on tokenised antiSMASH-DB BGCs has produced a sub-cluster table and you must verify the detection count and the size and BGC-occurrence distributions reproduce the reported benchmarks. Sub-clusters were produced by the PRESTO-TOP LDA topic-modelling approach rather than the PRESTO-STAT statistical method — the 108,085 count and distribution benchmarks apply to the statistical method only The input dataset is not the filtered non-redundant antiSMASH-DB set (60,028 BGCs), since count and distribution expectations are dataset-specific Sub-clusters shorter than three genes or occurring in only one BGC have not yet been filtered out, making distribution metrics incomparable to the published benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Validates output of iPRESTO's PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-cluster detection by checking the total count (108,085 sub-clusters on the filtered non-redundant antiSMASH-DB dataset of 60,028 BGCs) and the size/occurrence distributions (over 80% of sub-clusters contain fewer than ten genes; 17% occur in more than 10 BGCs). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Validates output of iPRESTO's PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-cluster detection by checking the total count (108,085 sub-clusters on the filtered non-redundant antiSMASH-DB dataset of 60,028 BGCs) and the size/occurrence distributions (over 80% of sub-clusters contain fewer than ten genes; 17% occur in more than 10 BGCs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sub-clusters were produced by the PRESTO-TOP LDA topic-modelling approach rather than the PRESTO-STAT statistical method — the 108,085 count and distribution benchmarks apply to the statistical method only The input dataset is not the filtered non-redundant antiSMASH-DB set (60,028 BGCs), since count and distribution expectations are dataset-specific Sub-clusters shorter than three genes or occurring in only one BGC have not yet been filtered out, making distribution metrics incomparable to the published benchmark

skills.description: Use when an unsupervised sub-cluster prediction model (e.g. PRESTO-TOP topics trained on tokenised BGCs) must be benchmarked against experimentally verified sub-clusters such as the 109 SubClusterBlast entries.
skills.name: subclusterblast-validation-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: subclusterblast-validation-overlap-analysis Use when an unsupervised sub-cluster prediction model (e.g. PRESTO-TOP topics trained on tokenised BGCs) must be benchmarked against experimentally verified sub-clusters such as the 109 SubClusterBlast entries. When the goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery without a benchmark: the 0.6 overlap validation only quantifies recovery of known SubClusterBlast sub-clusters and cannot assess novelty When gene order matters to the hypothesis: validation compares gene content overlaps, and the LDA bag-of-words representation ignores original gene order (unlike the PRESTO-STAT variant) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Validates predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters (e.g. PRESTO-TOP LDA motifs) against the experimentally verified sub-clusters stored in the antiSMASH SubClusterBlast module, counting a hit when at least 0.6 of the reference sub-cluster's genes are recovered in a predicted sub-cluster. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Validates predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters (e.g. PRESTO-TOP LDA motifs) against the experimentally verified sub-clusters stored in the antiSMASH SubClusterBlast module, counting a hit when at least 0.6 of the reference sub-cluster's genes are recovered in a predicted sub-cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo sub-cluster discovery without a benchmark: the 0.6 overlap validation only quantifies recovery of known SubClusterBlast sub-clusters and cannot assess novelty When gene order matters to the hypothesis: validation compares gene content overlaps, and the LDA bag-of-words representation ignores original gene order (unlike the PRESTO-STAT variant)

skills.description: Use when annotating MS2 peaks from a tandem mass spectrum against a candidate molecular formula, e.g. de novo formula ranking with MIST-CF, and no fragmentation tree is required.
skills.name: subformula-enumeration-from-precursor-formula
skills.search_text: subformula-enumeration-from-precursor-formula Use when annotating MS2 peaks from a tandem mass spectrum against a candidate molecular formula, e.g. de novo formula ranking with MIST-CF, and no fragmentation tree is required. Spectra acquired in negative ion mode — MIST-CF models were trained only on positive-mode data Analyses that require true fragmentation trees with fragmentation-event edges and neutral-loss tree structure — this protocol only does independent peak-wise subformula matching Cases involving adduct switching in MS2 subformula assignment, which the MIST-CF authors explicitly do not consider http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assigns MS2 fragment peaks to chemical subformulae of a candidate precursor formula by enumerating candidate formulae (via SIRIUS decomp), filtering with an RDBE >= 0 heuristic, and matching each peak to its nearest subformula mass within an instrument-specific ppm tolerance — replacing fragmentation tree construction in MIST-CF. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Assigns MS2 fragment peaks to chemical subformulae of a candidate precursor formula by enumerating candidate formulae (via SIRIUS decomp), filtering with an RDBE >= 0 heuristic, and matching each peak to its nearest subformula mass within an instrument-specific ppm tolerance — replacing fragmentation tree construction in MIST-CF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra acquired in negative ion mode — MIST-CF models were trained only on positive-mode data Analyses that require true fragmentation trees with fragmentation-event edges and neutral-loss tree structure — this protocol only does independent peak-wise subformula matching Cases involving adduct switching in MS2 subformula assignment, which the MIST-CF authors explicitly do not consider

skills.description: Use when a peak list has already passed electronic denoising and a precursor formula (from SMILES+adduct or formula) is known, and remaining fragment ions must be classified as plausible subformula losses vs chemical noise.
skills.name: subformula-loss-annotation
skills.search_text: subformula-loss-annotation Use when a peak list has already passed electronic denoising and a precursor formula (from SMILES+adduct or formula) is known, and remaining fragment ions must be classified as plausible subformula losses vs chemical noise. The precursor molecular formula cannot be retrieved from a reference spectral library or computed from SMILES — no master formula means no subformula enumeration The analyte may produce losses requiring molecular-connectivity knowledge (e.g. radical losses that Sirius/MS-FINDER also fail to recognize); plausibility checks here are limited to Seven Golden Rules without connectivity The input is a raw spectrum still containing electronic noise — run electronic_denoising first, since this skill assumes the fragment region is already cleaned http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Tags each fragment ion in an electronically denoised MS/MS spectrum as chemical signal or chemical noise by testing whether its exact mass corresponds to a chemically plausible subformula loss from the precursor ion, validated with the Seven Golden Rules. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Tags each fragment ion in an electronically denoised MS/MS spectrum as chemical signal or chemical noise by testing whether its exact mass corresponds to a chemically plausible subformula loss from the precursor ion, validated with the Seven Golden Rules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The precursor molecular formula cannot be retrieved from a reference spectral library or computed from SMILES — no master formula means no subformula enumeration The analyte may produce losses requiring molecular-connectivity knowledge (e.g. radical losses that Sirius/MS-FINDER also fail to recognize); plausibility checks here are limited to Seven Golden Rules without connectivity The input is a raw spectrum still containing electronic noise — run electronic_denoising first, since this skill assumes the fragment region is already cleaned

skills.description: Use when MS/MS spectra contain chemical noise ions — e.g. co-isolated contaminants or artificially generated chemical noise — and the precursor molecular formula and adduct are known, so fragments lacking chemically plausible subformula losses can be removed before spectral matching.
skills.name: subformula-loss-chemical-denoising
skills.search_text: subformula-loss-chemical-denoising Use when MS/MS spectra contain chemical noise ions — e.g. co-isolated contaminants or artificially generated chemical noise — and the precursor molecular formula and adduct are known, so fragments lacking chemically plausible subformula losses can be removed before spectral matching. The precursor molecular formula/adduct is unknown and no reference-library hit can supply it — use denoising_search, which pseudo-denoises against all molecular formulas within the precursor mass accuracy window, instead Input is a feature/peak table or chromatographic data rather than MS/MS peak arrays (m/z, intensity) from .msp files or packed numpy arrays Data were acquired on non-Orbitrap mass analyzers, where the parameters must be retuned and validated before use http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Chemical denoising of MS/MS spectra as implemented in the spectral_denoising package (formula_denoising): each fragment ion's exact mass must be explainable as a chemically plausible subformula loss from the precursor molecular ion, with candidate losses validated by the Seven Golden Rules algorithm (LEWIS and SENIOR checks ignored). It removes chemical noise ions that electronic denoising cannot touch, enabling high-confidence compound annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Chemical denoising of MS/MS spectra as implemented in the spectral_denoising package (formula_denoising): each fragment ion's exact mass must be explainable as a chemically plausible subformula loss from the precursor molecular ion, with candidate losses validated by the Seven Golden Rules algorithm (LEWIS and SENIOR checks ignored). It removes chemical noise ions that electronic denoising cannot touch, enabling high-confidence compound annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The precursor molecular formula/adduct is unknown and no reference-library hit can supply it — use denoising_search, which pseudo-denoises against all molecular formulas within the precursor mass accuracy window, instead Input is a feature/peak table or chromatographic data rather than MS/MS peak arrays (m/z, intensity) from .msp files or packed numpy arrays Data were acquired on non-Orbitrap mass analyzers, where the parameters must be retuned and validated before use

skills.description: Use when cleaning MS/MS spectra of chemical noise ions with a known or predicted precursor molecular formula (SMILES or formula) and adduct, so fragments unexplainable by plausible subformula losses can be discarded before spectral matching.
skills.name: subformula-loss-chemical-plausibility-filtering
skills.search_text: subformula-loss-chemical-plausibility-filtering Use when cleaning MS/MS spectra of chemical noise ions with a known or predicted precursor molecular formula (SMILES or formula) and adduct, so fragments unexplainable by plausible subformula losses can be discarded before spectral matching. No precursor molecular formula or SMILES is available and none can be retrieved from a reference library or cheminformatic prediction, since the filter cannot evaluate subformula losses The data come from non-Orbitrap mass analyzers, where the method's parameters must be retuned and revalidated before use Reference spectra have inherently low spectral entropy (<0.5, fewer than two fragment ions), making them vulnerable to noise-ion-driven false negatives even after filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A chemical noise removal step in MS/MS spectral denoising that keeps only fragment ions whose exact masses can be explained as chemically plausible subformula losses from the parent molecular ion, validated with the Seven Golden Rules algorithm. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: A chemical noise removal step in MS/MS spectral denoising that keeps only fragment ions whose exact masses can be explained as chemically plausible subformula losses from the parent molecular ion, validated with the Seven Golden Rules algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No precursor molecular formula or SMILES is available and none can be retrieved from a reference library or cheminformatic prediction, since the filter cannot evaluate subformula losses The data come from non-Orbitrap mass analyzers, where the method's parameters must be retuned and revalidated before use Reference spectra have inherently low spectral entropy (<0.5, fewer than two fragment ions), making them vulnerable to noise-ion-driven false negatives even after filtering

skills.description: Use when adapting the Spectral Denoising / Denoising Search pipeline to MS/MS data from a non-Orbitrap high-resolution analyzer, where the Orbitrap-calibrated electronic-noise rule (fewer than four ions at ±0.1% relative intensity) and mass tolerances may not transfer.
skills.name: subformula-loss-mass-tolerance-retuning
skills.search_text: subformula-loss-mass-tolerance-retuning Use when adapting the Spectral Denoising / Denoising Search pipeline to MS/MS data from a non-Orbitrap high-resolution analyzer, where the Orbitrap-calibrated electronic-noise rule (fewer than four ions at ±0.1% relative intensity) and mass tolerances may not transfer. Data were acquired on an Orbitrap instrument, where the NIST23-calibrated defaults (identical intensities > 4, 10 mDa threshold) already apply without retuning Spectra are low-quality references with spectral entropy <0.5 (fewer than two fragment ions), which are excluded from this kind of denoising evaluation The goal is distinguishing isomeric compounds or in-source fragments, which MS/MS spectral matching alone cannot resolve even after denoising http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retunes and validates the Spectral Denoising parameters — the electronic-noise identical-intensity cutoff and the formula-denoising mass tolerance — that were empirically calibrated on Orbitrap NIST23 data before applying the method to a non-Orbitrap high-resolution mass analyzer. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x
skills.summary: Retunes and validates the Spectral Denoising parameters — the electronic-noise identical-intensity cutoff and the formula-denoising mass tolerance — that were empirically calibrated on Orbitrap NIST23 data before applying the method to a non-Orbitrap high-resolution mass analyzer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were acquired on an Orbitrap instrument, where the NIST23-calibrated defaults (identical intensities > 4, 10 mDa threshold) already apply without retuning Spectra are low-quality references with spectral entropy <0.5 (fewer than two fragment ions), which are excluded from this kind of denoising evaluation The goal is distinguishing isomeric compounds or in-source fragments, which MS/MS spectral matching alone cannot resolve even after denoising

skills.description: Use when a user-defined gene panel (e.g., 26 IFN-induced genes) should partition samples into activity-score-positive/negative subgroups, and per-subgroup differential expression plus pathway exploration (EnrichR/GSEA) is the analysis goal.
skills.name: subgroup-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: subgroup-differential-expression-analysis Use when a user-defined gene panel (e.g., 26 IFN-induced genes) should partition samples into activity-score-positive/negative subgroups, and per-subgroup differential expression plus pathway exploration (EnrichR/GSEA) is the analysis goal. The analysis goal is whole-condition contrast (e.g., PTB vs HC) without a gene-panel-defined subpopulation — the standard BiomiX transcriptomics DESeq2 pipeline is the right path instead The omics data type has no gene-panel equivalent (e.g., metabolomics peaks), since subgrouping here depends on gene Z activity scores Samples are unannotated/unlabelled data outside the BiomiX single-omics transcriptomics pipeline scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 BiomiX-style subpopulation analysis that stratifies samples into user-defined subgroups via a gene-panel Z activity score and then runs separate differential expression and enrichment analyses per subgroup. It powers findings such as separating PTB patients with a 26 IFN-induced gene panel. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: BiomiX-style subpopulation analysis that stratifies samples into user-defined subgroups via a gene-panel Z activity score and then runs separate differential expression and enrichment analyses per subgroup. It powers findings such as separating PTB patients with a 26 IFN-induced gene panel.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is whole-condition contrast (e.g., PTB vs HC) without a gene-panel-defined subpopulation — the standard BiomiX transcriptomics DESeq2 pipeline is the right path instead The omics data type has no gene-panel equivalent (e.g., metabolomics peaks), since subgrouping here depends on gene Z activity scores Samples are unannotated/unlabelled data outside the BiomiX single-omics transcriptomics pipeline scope

skills.description: Use when filtering open-search SSMs (e.g. shifted dot product matches with large precursor mass shifts) where a single global FDR would be inflated or underpowered for modified peptides; requires target and decoy SSM counts per mass-difference group.
skills.name: subgroup-fdr-filtering
skills.search_text: subgroup-fdr-filtering Use when filtering open-search SSMs (e.g. shifted dot product matches with large precursor mass shifts) where a single global FDR would be inflated or underpowered for modified peptides; requires target and decoy SSM counts per mass-difference group. Standard closed searches (single narrow precursor mass window) where a single global target-decoy FDR suffices and no mass-difference subgroups exist Subgroups that are intentionally kept smaller than ~20 SSMs — the article warns the actual FDR may be underestimated for too-small groups, so results there are unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Subgroup FDR filtering for open modification spectral library searches: target-decoy FDR is estimated separately for SSMs grouped by charge-normalized precursor mass difference, so that modified-peptide matches at large mass shifts are not dominated by the unmodified-peptide FDR. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: Subgroup FDR filtering for open modification spectral library searches: target-decoy FDR is estimated separately for SSMs grouped by charge-normalized precursor mass difference, so that modified-peptide matches at large mass shifts are not dominated by the unmodified-peptide FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Standard closed searches (single narrow precursor mass window) where a single global target-decoy FDR suffices and no mass-difference subgroups exist Subgroups that are intentionally kept smaller than ~20 SSMs — the article warns the actual FDR may be underestimated for too-small groups, so results there are unreliable

skills.description: Reference for controlling FDR in open searches where modifications shift precursor masses and a single global target-decoy FDR would underestimate error rates.
skills.name: subgroup-fdr-stratification
skills.search_text: subgroup-fdr-stratification Reference for controlling FDR in open searches where modifications shift precursor masses and a single global target-decoy FDR would underestimate error rates. The search is a standard (narrow-window, unmodified-peptide) library search where a single global FDR is appropriate rather than mass-difference subgroups. Subgroups are too small (fewer than 20 SSMs per group), as the article warns the actual FDR may be underestimated. Only matches within a single narrow precursor mass window are analyzed, making mass-difference stratification unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A false discovery rate estimation strategy for open modification spectral library searches in which SSMs are grouped by their charge-normalized precursor mass difference between query and library spectra, and FDR is computed within each subgroup before filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: A false discovery rate estimation strategy for open modification spectral library searches in which SSMs are grouped by their charge-normalized precursor mass difference between query and library spectra, and FDR is computed within each subgroup before filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The search is a standard (narrow-window, unmodified-peptide) library search where a single global FDR is appropriate rather than mass-difference subgroups. Subgroups are too small (fewer than 20 SSMs per group), as the article warns the actual FDR may be underestimated. Only matches within a single narrow precursor mass window are analyzed, making mass-difference stratification unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when validating mwTab-format files from Metabolomics Workbench studies: run this check on every parsed MWTabFile to detect blank/missing sample IDs or factors and sample IDs in SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS that do not appear in the _DATA blocks.
skills.name: subject-sample-factor-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: subject-sample-factor-consistency-checking Use when validating mwTab-format files from Metabolomics Workbench studies: run this check on every parsed MWTabFile to detect blank/missing sample IDs or factors and sample IDs in SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS that do not appear in the _DATA blocks. The file cannot be parsed into an MWTabFile at all (unparseable remainder of the corpus) — these are skipped by read_files and cannot be block-checked The file contains no SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS or _DATA blocks (e.g. metadata-only mwTab file), leaving nothing to cross-compare The goal is schema-structural validation rather than cross-block sample consistency — use MWTabFile.validate with ms_required_schema/nmr_required_schema instead A sub-validation of mwTab-format study files that checks whether sample IDs and sample factors declared in the SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS block are consistent with the _DATA blocks — flagging blank or duplicate sample IDs and inconsistent factor headings. It was used as part of the mwtab validator that found validation errors in 1539 of 1818 parseable Metabolomics Workbench files. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11030163
skills.summary: A sub-validation of mwTab-format study files that checks whether sample IDs and sample factors declared in the SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS block are consistent with the _DATA blocks — flagging blank or duplicate sample IDs and inconsistent factor headings. It was used as part of the mwtab validator that found validation errors in 1539 of 1818 parseable Metabolomics Workbench files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The file cannot be parsed into an MWTabFile at all (unparseable remainder of the corpus) — these are skipped by read_files and cannot be block-checked The file contains no SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS or _DATA blocks (e.g. metadata-only mwTab file), leaving nothing to cross-compare The goal is schema-structural validation rather than cross-block sample consistency — use MWTabFile.validate with ms_required_schema/nmr_required_schema instead

skills.description: Use when Metabolomics Workbench analyses are available in both 'mwTab' and JSON formats and you must verify whether SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS entries (and related section/item content) agree between the two parsed representations.
skills.name: subject-sample-factors-metadata-verification
skills.search_text: subject-sample-factors-metadata-verification Use when Metabolomics Workbench analyses are available in both 'mwTab' and JSON formats and you must verify whether SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS entries (and related section/item content) agree between the two parsed representations. Only one format is available for an analysis — no paired mwTab/JSON comparison is possible. The goal is schema validation of a single mwTab file rather than cross-format consistency; use mwtab's validate/validate_file with mwschema ms/nmr required schemas instead. Input is a non-Metabolomics-Workbench metabolomics format (e.g., mzML or NetCDF); the mwTab MWTabFile parser does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Compares the SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS metadata sections of paired Metabolomics Workbench files to detect mismatches between the mwTab text representation and its JSONized counterpart, as part of cross-format consistency checking of metabolomics analyses. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11030163
skills.summary: Compares the SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS metadata sections of paired Metabolomics Workbench files to detect mismatches between the mwTab text representation and its JSONized counterpart, as part of cross-format consistency checking of metabolomics analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one format is available for an analysis — no paired mwTab/JSON comparison is possible. The goal is schema validation of a single mwTab file rather than cross-format consistency; use mwtab's validate/validate_file with mwschema ms/nmr required schemas instead. Input is a non-Metabolomics-Workbench metabolomics format (e.g., mzML or NetCDF); the mwTab MWTabFile parser does not apply.

skills.description: Use when building a BiG-SLiCE feature space that needs finer resolution than the 293 core biosynthetic pHMMs, i.e. when sub-clade-level domain fingerprinting of BGCs is required.
skills.name: sublevel-phmm-construction
skills.search_text: sublevel-phmm-construction Use when building a BiG-SLiCE feature space that needs finer resolution than the 293 core biosynthetic pHMMs, i.e. when sub-clade-level domain fingerprinting of BGCs is required. Generic chemical-class-level BGC classification suffices — the 293 biosynthetic-Pfam models already capture the domain content needed. Your goal is BGC detection/prediction rather than domain fingerprinting — use antiSMASH, DeepBGC, or ClusterFinder instead of building sublevel HMMs. A core domain resolves into fewer than 10 or more than 100 clades — it is excluded from the sub-Pfam set by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Constructs granular sub-Pfam (signature domain) pHMMs by hierarchically clustering aligned representative protein sequences from core biosynthetic domains into clades and building a sublevel HMM per clade, capturing sequence-level diversity that generic biosynthetic-Pfam models miss. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giaa154
skills.summary: Constructs granular sub-Pfam (signature domain) pHMMs by hierarchically clustering aligned representative protein sequences from core biosynthetic domains into clades and building a sublevel HMM per clade, capturing sequence-level diversity that generic biosynthetic-Pfam models miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Generic chemical-class-level BGC classification suffices — the 293 biosynthetic-Pfam models already capture the domain content needed. Your goal is BGC detection/prediction rather than domain fingerprinting — use antiSMASH, DeepBGC, or ClusterFinder instead of building sublevel HMMs. A core domain resolves into fewer than 10 or more than 100 clades — it is excluded from the sub-Pfam set by design.

skills.description: Use when a learned spectral encoder (e.g. GLEAMS) needs a small, diverse reference-spectrum set for pairwise similarity features, and the training corpus (~200,000 downsampled MS/MS spectra) is too large to compare against exhaustively.
skills.name: submodular-reference-spectra-selection
skills.search_text: submodular-reference-spectra-selection Use when a learned spectral encoder (e.g. GLEAMS) needs a small, diverse reference-spectrum set for pairwise similarity features, and the training corpus (~200,000 downsampled MS/MS spectra) is too large to compare against exhaustively. The input spectra are unidentified experimental runs rather than labeled training PSMs from a curated knowledge base like MassIVE-KB — the selection is defined on identified training data. The downstream model does not use reference-based similarity features (e.g. plain `gleams cluster` hierarchical clustering on embeddings needs no reference set). The candidate pool is already small enough to use directly as references, making submodular selection unnecessary overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Select a compact, representative set of reference MS/MS spectra (500 in the GLEAMS workflow) from a large labeled training corpus by running apricot's submodular facility-location function on a precomputed pairwise similarity matrix, so the encoder can compute similarity features against a small set of reference spectra instead of the full ~200,000-spectrum training set. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Select a compact, representative set of reference MS/MS spectra (500 in the GLEAMS workflow) from a large labeled training corpus by running apricot's submodular facility-location function on a precomputed pairwise similarity matrix, so the encoder can compute similarity features against a small set of reference spectra instead of the full ~200,000-spectrum training set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra are unidentified experimental runs rather than labeled training PSMs from a curated knowledge base like MassIVE-KB — the selection is defined on identified training data. The downstream model does not use reference-based similarity features (e.g. plain `gleams cluster` hierarchical clustering on embeddings needs no reference set). The candidate pool is already small enough to use directly as references, making submodular selection unnecessary overhead.

skills.description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking job is complete and a specific molecular family (a connected cluster of MS2 consensus spectra) must be isolated and its nodes classified by sample origin, e.g., lung tissue vs. microbial isolates in MSV000083359.
skills.name: subnetwork-extraction-and-node-coloring
skills.search_text: subnetwork-extraction-and-node-coloring Use when a GNPS molecular networking job is complete and a specific molecular family (a connected cluster of MS2 consensus spectra) must be isolated and its nodes classified by sample origin, e.g., lung tissue vs. microbial isolates in MSV000083359. The goal is calibrated quantitation of the metabolites — classic molecular networking is qualitative because only MS2 scans are considered; follow-up targeted LC-MS is required. The analysis input is already a feature table (e.g., from MZmine2 or Feature-Based Molecular Networking) rather than a finished GNPS classic molecular networking job. The question requires differentiating regio- or stereoisomers — MS2 spectra typically cannot resolve these, so node coloring cannot distinguish them. Extracts a target molecular family (e.g., the Pseudomonas quinolone subnetwork) from a GNPS METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 molecular network in Cytoscape and colors its nodes by sample origin using the standardized sample metadata table, yielding a publishable classified subnetwork node table. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-020-0317-5
skills.summary: Extracts a target molecular family (e.g., the Pseudomonas quinolone subnetwork) from a GNPS METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 molecular network in Cytoscape and colors its nodes by sample origin using the standardized sample metadata table, yielding a publishable classified subnetwork node table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calibrated quantitation of the metabolites — classic molecular networking is qualitative because only MS2 scans are considered; follow-up targeted LC-MS is required. The analysis input is already a feature table (e.g., from MZmine2 or Feature-Based Molecular Networking) rather than a finished GNPS classic molecular networking job. skills.summary: Tabulates node and consensus-spectrum counts for individual subnetworks (e.g., the stenothricin-containing subnetwork) across GNPS METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 jobs run under different parameter settings, producing a parameter-sensitivity table showing how Minimum Consensus Cluster Size, ion mass tolerances, and spectrum filters reshape network structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw instrument data or an unsubmitted dataset — conversion (mzXML/mzML/mgf), upload, and job submission must happen first; this skill only tabulates results of completed networking jobs.
