skills.description: Use when standard Pfam pHMMs are too coarse for downstream BGC tokenisation and per-clade subfamily-level pHMMs are needed from existing Pfam MSAs.
skills.name: subpfam-hmm-construction-from-msa-clades
skills.search_text: subpfam-hmm-construction-from-msa-clades Use when standard Pfam pHMMs are too coarse for downstream BGC tokenisation and per-clade subfamily-level pHMMs are needed from existing Pfam MSAs. The target Pfams are rare or already functionally specific, since subPfams were only constructed for the 112 most frequent Pfam domains in antiSMASH-DB Only raw unaligned protein sequences are available and no curated Pfam MSA exists to phylogenetically split The downstream analysis does not require subfamily-level domain tokenisation (ordinary Pfam pHMMs suffice) http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Builds finer-grained 'subPfam' pHMM models by splitting each Pfam multiple sequence alignment into phylogenetic clades and converting every clade into its own pHMM, so that overly broad Pfam domains (e.g. the 112 most abundant biosynthetic Pfams in antiSMASH-DB) can be tokenised at higher resolution with hmmscan. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Builds finer-grained 'subPfam' pHMM models by splitting each Pfam multiple sequence alignment into phylogenetic clades and converting every clade into its own pHMM, so that overly broad Pfam domains (e.g. the 112 most abundant biosynthetic Pfams in antiSMASH-DB) can be tokenised at higher resolution with hmmscan.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target Pfams are rare or already functionally specific, since subPfams were only constructed for the 112 most frequent Pfam domains in antiSMASH-DB Only raw unaligned protein sequences are available and no curated Pfam MSA exists to phylogenetically split The downstream analysis does not require subfamily-level domain tokenisation (ordinary Pfam pHMMs suffice)

skills.description: Use when comparing statistical testing methods whose p-values are indistinguishable on the full cohort (here, >1,000 complete cases), and differences in power need to be exposed by evaluating averaged p-values over random subsamples of controlled smaller sizes.
skills.name: subsample-pvalue-aggregation
skills.search_text: subsample-pvalue-aggregation Use when comparing statistical testing methods whose p-values are indistinguishable on the full cohort (here, >1,000 complete cases), and differences in power need to be exposed by evaluating averaged p-values over random subsamples of controlled smaller sizes. When the full-cohort analysis already separates the methods — the article notes p-values were indistinguishable only 'for both data sets with over 1,000 observations'; with <1,000 observations the raw p-values may differ without subsampling. When the goal is a single definitive association test on the complete cohort rather than a power comparison between competing test variants. When samples are too costly or too few to allow 100 repeated draws of sizes up to 500 without heavy overlap / duplication. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A power-revealing p-value averaging scheme that draws 100 random subject subsets of sizes 100–500 from each phenotype dataset, runs the comparison methods (PaIRKAT regularized Laplacian, unregularized normalized Laplacian, no-topography) on every subset, and averages p-values per method so that differences between kernel machine variants become visible even when full-cohort p-values are identical. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: A power-revealing p-value averaging scheme that draws 100 random subject subsets of sizes 100–500 from each phenotype dataset, runs the comparison methods (PaIRKAT regularized Laplacian, unregularized normalized Laplacian, no-topography) on every subset, and averages p-values per method so that differences between kernel machine variants become visible even when full-cohort p-values are identical.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the full-cohort analysis already separates the methods — the article notes p-values were indistinguishable only 'for both data sets with over 1,000 observations'; with <1,000 observations the raw p-values may differ without subsampling. When the goal is a single definitive association test on the complete cohort rather than a power comparison between competing test variants. When samples are too costly or too few to allow 100 repeated draws of sizes up to 500 without heavy overlap / duplication.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether multidimensional (N-dim) feature detection improves sensitivity over staged lower-dimensional processing on LC-IMS-MS/MS data, or when comparing a DEIMoS pipeline to MS-DIAL-style (m/z versus RT followed by DT) approaches.
skills.name: subspace-permutation-processing-strategies
skills.search_text: subspace-permutation-processing-strategies Use when evaluating whether multidimensional (N-dim) feature detection improves sensitivity over staged lower-dimensional processing on LC-IMS-MS/MS data, or when comparing a DEIMoS pipeline to MS-DIAL-style (m/z versus RT followed by DT) approaches. Data is 1D or 2D only (e.g. LC-MS without ion mobility) — there is no 3D native space to compare against subspace permutations. Input is already a curated feature table; this skill operates on thresholded raw/picked peak lists prior to alignment. The goal is cross-sample alignment or CCS calibration rather than comparing detection-strategy sensitivity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarks DEIMoS's native 3D peak detection (m/z–drift time–retention time simultaneously) against lower-dimensional subspace permutations (2D→1D, 1D→2D, successive 1D) on LC-IMS-MS/MS data, quantifying feature-count and coordinate-deviation differences. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c05017
skills.summary: Benchmarks DEIMoS's native 3D peak detection (m/z–drift time–retention time simultaneously) against lower-dimensional subspace permutations (2D→1D, 1D→2D, successive 1D) on LC-IMS-MS/MS data, quantifying feature-count and coordinate-deviation differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is 1D or 2D only (e.g. LC-MS without ion mobility) — there is no 3D native space to compare against subspace permutations. Input is already a curated feature table; this skill operates on thresholded raw/picked peak lists prior to alignment. The goal is cross-sample alignment or CCS calibration rather than comparing detection-strategy sensitivity.

skills.description: Use when a workflow needs the full set of third-party chemical annotations or assay descriptions for a specific PubChem SID or AID, and the required data are not exposed by other PubChem programmatic access routes.
skills.name: substance-assay-annotation-retrieval
skills.search_text: substance-assay-annotation-retrieval Use when a workflow needs the full set of third-party chemical annotations or assay descriptions for a specific PubChem SID or AID, and the required data are not exposed by other PubChem programmatic access routes. Input is a list of many record identifiers needing bulk retrieval — PUG-View cannot take multiple input record identifiers in one request. Goal is retrieving a small set of specific computed compound properties rather than full annotation content — PUG-REST is better suited for that purpose. Only a specific tabular data type is needed — some specialized (especially tabular) data come from other backend services and are not currently accessible through PUG-View. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Retrieve complete annotation data for a given substance or assay record from PubChem by issuing a PUG-View request URL against the /rest/pug_view/data/.../JSON endpoint, honoring version parameters and usage policies. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-019-0375-2
skills.summary: Retrieve complete annotation data for a given substance or assay record from PubChem by issuing a PUG-View request URL against the /rest/pug_view/data/.../JSON endpoint, honoring version parameters and usage policies.

skills.description: Use when you need to count and tabulate NRPS A-domain substrate annotations (e.g. per-substrate frequencies, unique substrate totals) from structured biosynthetic gene cluster records such as MIBiG JSON entries.
skills.name: substrate-frequency-tabulation
skills.search_text: substrate-frequency-tabulation Use when you need to count and tabulate NRPS A-domain substrate annotations (e.g. per-substrate frequencies, unique substrate totals) from structured biosynthetic gene cluster records such as MIBiG JSON entries. You need A-domain substrate *predictions* (e.g. SANDPUMA or NRPSPredictor2 outputs) rather than curated experimental annotations from validated BGC entries. You are counting PKS AT-domain substrates or other domain selectivities; this tabulation targets NRPS A-domain annotations specifically. Input records lack isomeric SMILES or have unvalidated SMILES strings, so substrate identity cannot be deduplicated reliably. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Tabulates NRPS A-domain substrate annotations from MIBiG JSON entries, deduplicating substrates by stereochemically curated isomeric SMILES and counting annotated A-domains per substrate. Produces the substrate-to-SMILES frequency table used to quantify MIBiG 3.0's A-domain annotation coverage. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Tabulates NRPS A-domain substrate annotations from MIBiG JSON entries, deduplicating substrates by stereochemically curated isomeric SMILES and counting annotated A-domains per substrate. Produces the substrate-to-SMILES frequency table used to quantify MIBiG 3.0's A-domain annotation coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need A-domain substrate *predictions* (e.g. SANDPUMA or NRPSPredictor2 outputs) rather than curated experimental annotations from validated BGC entries. You are counting PKS AT-domain substrates or other domain selectivities; this tabulation targets NRPS A-domain annotations specifically. Input records lack isomeric SMILES or have unvalidated SMILES strings, so substrate identity cannot be deduplicated reliably.

skills.description: Use when you need to convert a site-of-metabolism (SoM) dataset into atom-pair BoM annotations, or when reproducing/verifying the 2262-record EBoMD annotation counts (828 η-η, 1348 η-H, 86 η-SPN).
skills.name: substrate-metabolite-pair-annotation
skills.search_text: substrate-metabolite-pair-annotation Use when you need to convert a site-of-metabolism (SoM) dataset into atom-pair BoM annotations, or when reproducing/verifying the 2262-record EBoMD annotation counts (828 η-η, 1348 η-H, 86 η-SPN). The task is reactant-vs-nonreactant classification for a CYP450 isoform — that is CypReact's scope, not BoM annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 Curate a Bond-of-Metabolism (BoM) dataset by converting SoM annotations into explicit substrate-metabolite pair records (η-η, η-H, η-SPN categories), the data foundation used to train CypBoM and derive MetaboGen's SMIRKS rules from the EBoMD. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00144
skills.summary: Curate a Bond-of-Metabolism (BoM) dataset by converting SoM annotations into explicit substrate-metabolite pair records (η-η, η-H, η-SPN categories), the data foundation used to train CypBoM and derive MetaboGen's SMIRKS rules from the EBoMD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a BoM-annotated dataset and the goal is metabolite structure generation — use MetaboGen instead. skills.description: Use when molecular families in a GNPS molecular network have no or few spectral library matches but MS2LDA motif data, NAP/DEREPLICATOR in silico annotations, and ClassyFire classification are available, and you need level-3 class or substructure-level annotation.
skills.name: substructure-annotation-of-molecular-families
skills.search_text: substructure-annotation-of-molecular-families Use when molecular families in a GNPS molecular network have no or few spectral library matches but MS2LDA motif data, NAP/DEREPLICATOR in silico annotations, and ClassyFire classification are available, and you need level-3 class or substructure-level annotation. Input molecular family nodes already carry GNPS spectral library matches at MSI level 2 or higher, so motif-based propagation adds little over direct annotation. The analysis goal is feature-based (FBMN) rather than classical molecular networking — use Mass2Motifs_2_Network_FeatureBased instead, as the workflow and outputs differ. No MS2LDA experiment or in silico structure annotations (NAP, DEREPLICATOR, or another tool) exist for the dataset; MolNetEnhancer's integration depends on these external outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Map MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructural annotations onto GNPS molecular networks with pyMolNetEnhancer, raising annotation of molecular families that lack GNPS spectral library hits to MSI level 3 (putatively characterized compound classes), as demonstrated for two Euphorbia diterpenoid molecular families covering 73 molecular features. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9070144
skills.summary: Map MS2LDA Mass2Motif substructural annotations onto GNPS molecular networks with pyMolNetEnhancer, raising annotation of molecular families that lack GNPS spectral library hits to MSI level 3 (putatively characterized compound classes), as demonstrated for two Euphorbia diterpenoid molecular families covering 73 molecular features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input molecular family nodes already carry GNPS spectral library matches at MSI level 2 or higher, so motif-based propagation adds little over direct annotation. The analysis goal is feature-based (FBMN) rather than classical molecular networking — use Mass2Motifs_2_Network_FeatureBased instead, as the workflow and outputs differ. No MS2LDA experiment or in silico structure annotations (NAP, DEREPLICATOR, or another tool) exist for the dataset; MolNetEnhancer's integration depends on these external outputs.

skills.description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS chemical features (MGF with MS1+MS2 peaks imported as MassSpectrometryFeatures) need predicted molecular fingerprints to build a Qemistree chemical hierarchy, rather than relying on sparse spectral library matches.
skills.name: substructure-fingerprint-prediction
skills.search_text: substructure-fingerprint-prediction Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS chemical features (MGF with MS1+MS2 peaks imported as MassSpectrometryFeatures) need predicted molecular fingerprints to build a Qemistree chemical hierarchy, rather than relying on sparse spectral library matches. Features lacking MS/MS data (MS1-only features are not considered — they cannot receive fingerprints). Analysis goals relying on spectral library matches for structural annotation, when library-match coverage (typically only 1–20% of features) is instead the limiting factor and fingerprints are needed. Datasets requiring ClassyFire taxonomy assignment or hierarchy construction only — those are downstream steps (make-hierarchy, get-classyfire-taxonomy) that consume fingerprints.qza, not part of this prediction stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the SIRIUS → ZODIAC → CSI:FingerID stage of the Qemistree pipeline, in which fragmentation trees computed from MS/MS spectra are re-ranked for molecular formulas and then converted into 2936-property molecular substructure fingerprint vectors per chemical feature. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00677-3
skills.summary: Reconstructs the SIRIUS → ZODIAC → CSI:FingerID stage of the Qemistree pipeline, in which fragmentation trees computed from MS/MS spectra are re-ranked for molecular formulas and then converted into 2936-property molecular substructure fingerprint vectors per chemical feature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features lacking MS/MS data (MS1-only features are not considered — they cannot receive fingerprints). Analysis goals relying on spectral library matches for structural annotation, when library-match coverage (typically only 1–20% of features) is instead the limiting factor and fingerprints are needed. Datasets requiring ClassyFire taxonomy assignment or hierarchy construction only — those are downstream steps (make-hierarchy, get-classyfire-taxonomy) that consume fingerprints.qza, not part of this prediction stage.

skills.name: substructure-motif-frequency-analysis
skills.search_text: substructure-motif-frequency-analysis Use when you have a GNPS molecular network and MS2LDA Mass2Motifs and need to quantify motif frequency across molecular families to find substructural diversity or common substructures linking known and unknown compounds. skills.description: Use when annotating MS/MS or MSn spectra where no informative reference spectra exist and candidate structures (e.g. from PubChem) must be ranked by how well they explain observed fragment peaks.
skills.name: substructure-penalty-scoring
skills.search_text: substructure-penalty-scoring Use when annotating MS/MS or MSn spectra where no informative reference spectra exist and candidate structures (e.g. from PubChem) must be ranked by how well they explain observed fragment peaks. Informative reference spectra are available for library matching — this skill is designed for the absence of reference spectra. The candidate structure contains fragmentations requiring more than 3 bond dissociations — in challenge 16 several higher-energy peaks (e.g. m/z=122.0408, 221.07309) could not be explained with up to 3 bond dissociations. skills.summary: Ranks candidate chemical structures by matching observed MS/MS m/z values against in silico generated substructures (up to 3 bond dissociations) of each candidate, producing intensity-weighted penalty scores for candidate ranking without reference spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Informative reference spectra are available for library matching — this skill is designed for the absence of reference spectra. skills.search_text: substructure-presence-vector-construction Use when you have a molecule as a SMILES string and need the substructure presence representation (957 SMART-defined fragments) required to train or run inference with the substructure-to-structure transformer. skills.search_text: supplementary-table-data-extraction Use when a paper's main text defers quantitative results to supplementary tables (e.g., Supplementary Tables 6/7/8/11 in the GNPS SI) and the goal is to reproduce or verify a reported number from those tables. skills.summary: Combines cohort-level Cox proportional hazards estimates for circulating biomarkers into a fixed-effect survival meta-analysis (R-package meta) and reports HR, 95% CI, P, I2 and P(het) per biomarker, then feeds the pooled P values into a Bonferroni-controlled stepwise (forward-backward) selection of independently mortality-associated biomarkers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single cohort — no cross-cohort pooling or I2/P(het) assessment is possible You need an individual-level pooled analysis or a random-effects model; this skill is specific to successive rounds of fixed-effect meta-analysis on summary statistics Your goal is a clinically usable risk score in concentration units — the article states the scaled-biomarker score 'is not yet suitable for classification of patients in the clinic'

skills.description: Use when ranked candidate lists (e.g. BAM suspect rankings) must be scored for how accurately the correct structure is placed, or when a rank-distribution histogram and top-k hit rates need to be computed and visualized.
skills.name: suspect-ranking-evaluation
skills.search_text: suspect-ranking-evaluation Use when ranked candidate lists (e.g. BAM suspect rankings) must be scored for how accurately the correct structure is placed, or when a rank-distribution histogram and top-k hit rates need to be computed and visualized. Input is a set of spectral similarity scores or cosine scores rather than ordinal candidate rankings — this skill evaluates rank positions, not score distributions. The task is to evaluate molecular formula annotation accuracy (SIRIUS-based) rather than suspect structure ranking; formula annotation precedes ranking and has its own accuracy metric (24.2% correct assignments). Candidate lists are unranked (all candidates treated as equally likely); the average-rank tie rule presupposes an ordered candidate list. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Evaluates the ranking accuracy of BAM-generated derivative candidates for anchor-suspect pairs by computing average ranks and rank-distribution statistics, using the average-rank tie-resolution rule. Quantifies how often the correct suspect structure appears at the top of the ranked candidate list. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01565
skills.summary: Evaluates the ranking accuracy of BAM-generated derivative candidates for anchor-suspect pairs by computing average ranks and rank-distribution statistics, using the average-rank tie-resolution rule. Quantifies how often the correct suspect structure appears at the top of the ranked candidate list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a set of spectral similarity scores or cosine scores rather than ordinal candidate rankings — this skill evaluates rank positions, not score distributions. The task is to evaluate molecular formula annotation accuracy (SIRIUS-based) rather than suspect structure ranking; formula annotation precedes ranking and has its own accuracy metric (24.2% correct assignments). Candidate lists are unranked (all candidates treated as equally likely); the average-rank tie rule presupposes an ordered candidate list.

skills.description: Use when a raw gene/miRNA/isoform count matrix from an RNA-seq workflow (e.g. Salmon quantification) shows batch structure — samples processed in multiple batches or confounded runs — and must be batch-corrected before differential expression analysis.
skills.name: sva-combat-batch-effect-correction
skills.search_text: sva-combat-batch-effect-correction Use when a raw gene/miRNA/isoform count matrix from an RNA-seq workflow (e.g. Salmon quantification) shows batch structure — samples processed in multiple batches or confounded runs — and must be batch-corrected before differential expression analysis. The dataset consists of samples processed in a single batch with no confounding — mom_batch_method_genes should be 'none' rather than applying ComBat/SVA unnecessarily. The matrix is raw and unfiltered — correction should follow MOI's filtering (filterByExp or cutoff) and quantile normalization stages, not replace them. The goal is single-omics transcript-level analysis outside MOI (e.g. nf-core/rnaseq) where batch correction is handled by that pipeline's own modules. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Corrects batch effects in a filtered, normalized count matrix within the MultiOmicsIntegrator (MOI) Nextflow pipeline, using ComBat and/or Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) from the sva, limma, and edgeR R packages as configured by the mom_batch_method_genes parameter. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae175
skills.summary: Corrects batch effects in a filtered, normalized count matrix within the MultiOmicsIntegrator (MOI) Nextflow pipeline, using ComBat and/or Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) from the sva, limma, and edgeR R packages as configured by the mom_batch_method_genes parameter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset consists of samples processed in a single batch with no confounding — mom_batch_method_genes should be 'none' rather than applying ComBat/SVA unnecessarily. The matrix is raw and unfiltered — correction should follow MOI's filtering (filterByExp or cutoff) and quantile normalization stages, not replace them. The goal is single-omics transcript-level analysis outside MOI (e.g. nf-core/rnaseq) where batch correction is handled by that pipeline's own modules.

skills.description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature matrix (samples as columns, unique feature IDs as rows) plus a design file mapping samples to groups needs ordination, group separation assessment, or feature-weight inspection.
skills.name: svd-based-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: svd-based-dimensionality-reduction Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature matrix (samples as columns, unique feature IDs as rows) plus a design file mapping samples to groups needs ordination, group separation assessment, or feature-weight inspection. The input is already peak-picked and needs upstream quality-control filtering first — use SECIMTools QC steps (Blank Feature Filtering, CV Flags, RT Flags) before ordination The goal is supervised discrimination between known groups — PLS-DA or random forest in SECIMTools is the appropriate choice, not unsupervised PCA The data require a per-feature statistical test (ANOVA, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis) rather than sample-level ordination http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Principal component analysis of metabolomics feature tables via singular value decomposition, as implemented in the SECIMTools PCA tool: scores, loadings, and 2D/3D visual summaries colored by design-file group. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Principal component analysis of metabolomics feature tables via singular value decomposition, as implemented in the SECIMTools PCA tool: scores, loadings, and 2D/3D visual summaries colored by design-file group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already peak-picked and needs upstream quality-control filtering first — use SECIMTools QC steps (Blank Feature Filtering, CV Flags, RT Flags) before ordination The goal is supervised discrimination between known groups — PLS-DA or random forest in SECIMTools is the appropriate choice, not unsupervised PCA The data require a per-feature statistical test (ANOVA, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis) rather than sample-level ordination

skills.description: Use when converting an estimated covariance matrix of metabolite abundances into a Jacobian matrix in R and the linear system is ill-conditioned or noisy, requiring SVD-stabilized solving across replicate estimates.
skills.name: svd-based-matrix-inversion-stabilization
skills.search_text: svd-based-matrix-inversion-stabilization Use when converting an estimated covariance matrix of metabolite abundances into a Jacobian matrix in R and the linear system is ill-conditioned or noisy, requiring SVD-stabilized solving across replicate estimates. Input is still raw metabolite abundance data rather than a generated covariance matrix — run prepare_data and generate_covariance first No stoichiometry/interaction matrix (interactions_fin) is available, since calculate_jacobian requires stoi as a positional argument Goal is KEGG-ID-driven network analysis via the minfer(input_ids) entry point rather than Jacobian matrix computation from covariance data http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 SVD-based numerical stabilization inside MInfer's calculate_jacobian: the covariance-to-Jacobian inverse problem is vectorized via a Kronecker-product system matrix and solved with singular value decomposition, sampling icount stochastic replicate Jacobians and reporting median/quantile statistics. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.cmpb.2025.108672
skills.summary: SVD-based numerical stabilization inside MInfer's calculate_jacobian: the covariance-to-Jacobian inverse problem is vectorized via a Kronecker-product system matrix and solved with singular value decomposition, sampling icount stochastic replicate Jacobians and reporting median/quantile statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw metabolite abundance data rather than a generated covariance matrix — run prepare_data and generate_covariance first No stoichiometry/interaction matrix (interactions_fin) is available, since calculate_jacobian requires stoi as a positional argument Goal is KEGG-ID-driven network analysis via the minfer(input_ids) entry point rather than Jacobian matrix computation from covariance data

skills.description: Use when you have gene expression matrices over groups (e.g. 17 DM2/17 NGT/9 IGT diabetes samples or 75 airway epithelium smoker samples) and need to check whether gene-set enrichment rankings reflect coordinate expression strength rather than consistent group differences.
skills.name: svd-metagene-eigenvalue-analysis
skills.search_text: svd-metagene-eigenvalue-analysis Use when you have gene expression matrices over groups (e.g. 17 DM2/17 NGT/9 IGT diabetes samples or 75 airway epithelium smoker samples) and need to check whether gene-set enrichment rankings reflect coordinate expression strength rather than consistent group differences. Your goal is a straightforward differential pathway-activity test (permute sample labels, record the max t-statistic across pathways) rather than diagnosing whether enrichment ranks are driven by coordinate expression strength. Your pathway gene-sets are very small or near-uncorrelated by construction — the first-eigenvalue fraction will sit near the ~0.05 size-matched Gaussian noise baseline and carry little signal. You lack the raw gene expression matrix and only have precomputed enrichment scores, since the SVD must be computed on the restricted, standardized gene-by-sample matrix Y. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies how strongly each ~400-KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene-set is coordinately expressed by computing the first-eigenvalue fraction of the SVD of its standardized gene-by-sample expression matrix, and joins this metric to GSEA enrichment scores to test whether GSEA's top-ranked sets are merely the most coordinated (e.g. the ribosome set) rather than the most differentially active. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Quantifies how strongly each ~400-KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene-set is coordinately expressed by computing the first-eigenvalue fraction of the SVD of its standardized gene-by-sample expression matrix, and joins this metric to GSEA enrichment scores to test whether GSEA's top-ranked sets are merely the most coordinated (e.g. the ribosome set) rather than the most differentially active.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is a straightforward differential pathway-activity test (permute sample labels, record the max t-statistic across pathways) rather than diagnosing whether enrichment ranks are driven by coordinate expression strength. Your pathway gene-sets are very small or near-uncorrelated by construction — the first-eigenvalue fraction will sit near the ~0.05 size-matched Gaussian noise baseline and carry little signal. You lack the raw gene expression matrix and only have precomputed enrichment scores, since the SVD must be computed on the restricted, standardized gene-by-sample matrix Y.

skills.description: Use when peak-intensity matrices with compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) must be converted to pathway-level activity scores, especially when noise and missing peaks make ORA/GSEA unreliable.
skills.name: svd-pathway-activity-decomposition
skills.search_text: svd-pathway-activity-decomposition Use when peak-intensity matrices with compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) must be converted to pathway-level activity scores, especially when noise and missing peaks make ORA/GSEA unreliable. If most peak features lack compound annotations — unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis, so coverage will be too low to rank pathways meaningfully When the goal is to analyse individual metabolites rather than groups of metabolites as sets (pathways, GNPS Molecular Families, MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Decomposes per-metabolite-set intensity matrices via singular value decomposition (the PLAGE method), taking the first metacompound (leading singular vector) as the set's activity levels, then ranks metabolite sets by their activity-level change using mPLAGE p-values. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Decomposes per-metabolite-set intensity matrices via singular value decomposition (the PLAGE method), taking the first metacompound (leading singular vector) as the set's activity levels, then ranks metabolite sets by their activity-level change using mPLAGE p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If most peak features lack compound annotations — unannotated peaks are not used for pathway analysis, so coverage will be too low to rank pathways meaningfully When the goal is to analyse individual metabolites rather than groups of metabolites as sets (pathways, GNPS Molecular Families, MS2LDA Mass2Motifs)

skills.name: svg-figure-generation
skills.search_text: svg-figure-generation Use when you need to programmatically draw a biosynthetic gene cluster (e.g. a MIBiG modular PKS/NRPS entry) as a spaghetti diagram with a vertically aligned backbone, exported to an .svg file. Input is not a modular PKS/NRPS system or lacks a cluster definition (e.g. RiPP/terpene pathways needing custom user-specified enzymatic steps) The goal is predicted scaffold structures rather than diagram rendering — RAIChU cannot produce mature natural products from raw antiSMASH output without user-specified tailoring targets Regio- and stereochemistry of tailoring reactions must be predicted automatically; RAIChU requires users to specify reaction targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Reconstruct RAIChU's spaghetti-diagram drawing engine to render modular PKS/NRPS cluster visualisations as SVG files, applying its central-chain, cyclic-bond, and side-chain angle rules so diagrams meet the paper's readability criteria. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00898-x
skills.summary: Reconstruct RAIChU's spaghetti-diagram drawing engine to render modular PKS/NRPS cluster visualisations as SVG files, applying its central-chain, cyclic-bond, and side-chain angle rules so diagrams meet the paper's readability criteria.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how much biological signal a normalisation method preserves — e.g. comparing hRUV variants, ratio, SVR, SERRF, or RLSC on their cross-validated accuracy for a binary clinical outcome such as hypertension status.
skills.name: svm-classification-hypertension-status
skills.search_text: svm-classification-hypertension-status Use when you need to quantify how much biological signal a normalisation method preserves — e.g. comparing hRUV variants, ratio, SVR, SERRF, or RLSC on their cross-validated accuracy for a binary clinical outcome such as hypertension status. When the evaluation goal is unsupervised normalisation quality (e.g. variability among replicates or signal-drift removal) rather than retention of a supervised biological signal — the paper assesses normalisation on multiple criteria, and this skill covers only the supervised-accuracy criterion When hypertension (or other outcome) labels are unavailable for the samples, since the SVM cross-validation requires a supervised response variable When the study design lacks embedded biological replicates across batches, since hierarchical hRUV depends on intra- and inter-batch replicates for unwanted-variation estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks metabolomics normalisation methods by their ability to retain biological signal, using an SVM classifier to predict hypertension status from normalised metabolite abundances under 30 repeats of 10-fold cross-validation. skills.description: Use when a curated, expert-labeled set of representative good and bad chromatographic peaks exists and you want a single combined classifier for peak quality filtering instead of varying individual metric cutoff thresholds.
skills.name: svm-classifier-training
skills.search_text: svm-classifier-training Use when a curated, expert-labeled set of representative good and bad chromatographic peaks exists and you want a single combined classifier for peak quality filtering instead of varying individual metric cutoff thresholds. No curated good/bad training peak set exists — the article states machine learning-based peak identification is not yet implemented because the required training samples have not been compiled; fall back to individual metric cutoff-threshold filtering. The goal is to evaluate extracted EIC quality rather than detected peak quality — use the EIC-related global zigzag index / MCQ index evaluation path instead. The goal is to characterize individual metrics' cutoff-threshold behavior (Recall/Precision/F-score sweeps, individual and combined), not to build a supervised classifier. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a support vector machine to classify LC/MS chromatographic peaks as good or bad from six normalized quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, local zigzag index), implementing the paper's proposed but unrealized alternative to per-metric cutoff thresholds. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-15-s11-s5
skills.summary: Trains a support vector machine to classify LC/MS chromatographic peaks as good or bad from six normalized quality metrics (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, local zigzag index), implementing the paper's proposed but unrealized alternative to per-metric cutoff thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No curated good/bad training peak set exists — the article states machine learning-based peak identification is not yet implemented because the required training samples have not been compiled; fall back to individual metric cutoff-threshold filtering. The goal is to evaluate extracted EIC quality rather than detected peak quality — use the EIC-related global zigzag index / MCQ index evaluation path instead. The goal is to characterize individual metrics' cutoff-threshold behavior (Recall/Precision/F-score sweeps, individual and combined), not to build a supervised classifier.

skills.description: Use when you need a classical supervised classification baseline for raw high-dimensional mass spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables from MALDI FT-ICR MSI) with pixel-level normal/tumor labels, to benchmark against a deep learning model.
skills.name: svm-classifier-training-on-msi-spectra
skills.search_text: svm-classifier-training-on-msi-spectra Use when you need a classical supervised classification baseline for raw high-dimensional mass spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables from MALDI FT-ICR MSI) with pixel-level normal/tumor labels, to benchmark against a deep learning model. The input is already a reduced feature/peak table or dimensionality-reduced embedding (e.g., the 5-dimensional latent variable from the massNet VAE Code layer) rather than the full 85,062 m/z raw spectra. The goal is classification of more than the binary normal/tumor classes, which the source model does not support (multi-class classification is left for future development). No ground-truth pixel annotations are available; the paper notes that establishing ground truth annotation of MSI data is a challenging task requiring more pathological investigation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a support vector machine (SVM), a widely-used classical machine learning baseline, on pixel-wise normal/tumor-labeled MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra to benchmark deep learning classifiers such as massNet on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC, and runtime. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Train a support vector machine (SVM), a widely-used classical machine learning baseline, on pixel-wise normal/tumor-labeled MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra to benchmark deep learning classifiers such as massNet on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC, and runtime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a reduced feature/peak table or dimensionality-reduced embedding (e.g., the 5-dimensional latent variable from the massNet VAE Code layer) rather than the full 85,062 m/z raw spectra. skills.description: Use when calibrating in silico structure annotation scores (e.g. CSI:FingerID) from reference-spectra training sets into posterior confidence scores for FDR estimation of novel-molecule annotations.
skills.name: svm-confidence-score-training
skills.search_text: svm-confidence-score-training Use when calibrating in silico structure annotation scores (e.g. CSI:FingerID) from reference-spectra training sets into posterior confidence scores for FDR estimation of novel-molecule annotations. The input is already a set of calibrated confidence scores or posterior probabilities rather than raw candidate scores needing calibration. You need to validate known library compounds by spectral library search rather than score and rank novel in silico structure candidates. skills.summary: Trains COSMIC's confidence-score model for CSI:FingerID structure annotations: kernel density P-value estimation of proxy-decoy hit scores, per-candidate linear SVMs with enforced feature directionality, and Platt scaling to posterior probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a set of calibrated confidence scores or posterior probabilities rather than raw candidate scores needing calibration. You need to validate known library compounds by spectral library search rather than score and rank novel in silico structure candidates. The goal is establishing absolute or stereochemical structure identity — COSMIC cannot distinguish small structure modifications or stereochemistry from MS/MS alone.

skills.name: synonym-matching-vocabulary-mapping
skills.search_text: synonym-matching-vocabulary-mapping Use when a metabolomics sample-metadata matrix contains freetext field values (inconsistent synonyms, typographical errors) that must be replaced with fixed-vocabulary terms to make datasets interoperable and FAIR. Input metadata is already expressed in fixed-vocabulary terms with no synonym or typo variance — the transformation adds no value and risks unnecessary term churn. The task is general text normalization outside sample-metadata fields (e.g. free-form abstracts or prose) — the n-grams/nearest-neighbors model targets metadata vocabulary terms, not arbitrary prose. A downstream system requires the original unmodified freetext provenance — replacement by fixed-vocabulary terms discards the original strings. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 SMetaS's core transformation maps freetext sample-metadata terms in a metabolomics metadata matrix onto fixed vocabularies using synonym matching and typographical fixing in an n-grams/nearest neighbors model approach, yielding standardized metadata suitable for study submission or repository deposit. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941

skills.search_text: synthetic-gaussian-signal-generation Use when validating mzapy.peaks peak finders against signals of known composition: generate summed-Gaussian 1D signals with recorded ground-truth parameters to quantify detection and parameter-recovery error. The input is real experimental MZA/HDF5 mass spectrometry data where peaks are unknown — synthetic generation is for validation, not for analyzing actual LC-IMS-MS signals The target peaks are heavily overlapping or poorly resolved, since the documented reliability of sequential Gaussian fitting holds for clean, well-resolved signals Evaluating mzapy capabilities unrelated to 1D peak finding, e.g. MZA conversion, mass/CCS calibration, or isotopic m/z prediction Builds synthetic 1D signals as sums of Gaussian peaks with known center, height, and width (plus a controlled noise floor) on an m/z-like axis, to serve as ground-truth test inputs for validating mzapy peak-finding utilities such as find_peaks_1d_gauss and find_peaks_1d_localmax. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c01653
skills.summary: Builds synthetic 1D signals as sums of Gaussian peaks with known center, height, and width (plus a controlled noise floor) on an m/z-like axis, to serve as ground-truth test inputs for validating mzapy peak-finding utilities such as find_peaks_1d_gauss and find_peaks_1d_localmax.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real experimental MZA/HDF5 mass spectrometry data where peaks are unknown — synthetic generation is for validation, not for analyzing actual LC-IMS-MS signals The target peaks are heavily overlapping or poorly resolved, since the documented reliability of sequential Gaussian fitting holds for clean, well-resolved signals Evaluating mzapy capabilities unrelated to 1D peak finding, e.g. MZA conversion, mass/CCS calibration, or isotopic m/z prediction

skills.summary: Generate synthetic plant-metabolite LC-MS maps with MSSimulator (supplemental Table S5 configurations: 500 metabolites, 100–1000 m/z, 25 min gradient) whose simulations also yield ground-truth feature lists, enabling recall/precision/F-score benchmarking of feature detection against known truth under controlled noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental LC-MS data with no ground-truth feature annotations — matching-based precision/recall cannot be computed exactly The goal is downstream label-free quantification (retention-time correction, feature linking, export to tabular text) rather than detection-algorithm benchmarking The analytes are outside the article's scope of small molecules such as metabolites in complex backgrounds (e.g. human plasma spike-in linearity studies)

skills.description: Use when a benchmark or test needs lipid identifier pairs at known annotation levels to verify cross-dataset equalization/matching logic, and ground-truth mappings must be constructed rather than harvested from real datasets.
skills.name: synthetic-lipidomics-dataset-construction
skills.search_text: synthetic-lipidomics-dataset-construction Use when a benchmark or test needs lipid identifier pairs at known annotation levels to verify cross-dataset equalization/matching logic, and ground-truth mappings must be constructed rather than harvested from real datasets. Input datasets already report all lipid identifiers at a single, uniform annotation level — no equalization is needed and the Equalizer matrix would only truncate information The analysis targets plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across five categories The goal is ontology or pathway mapping rather than cross-level identifier matching — the Linker module or LION-style mapping tools are the appropriate route http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Constructs synthetic lipidomics annotation lists with identifiers deliberately spread across structural levels (species, molecular species, sn-position, DB-position, full structure) so that LipidLynxX Equalizer-based cross-level matching can be exercised and validated end-to-end on controlled ground truth. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.04.09.033894
skills.summary: Constructs synthetic lipidomics annotation lists with identifiers deliberately spread across structural levels (species, molecular species, sn-position, DB-position, full structure) so that LipidLynxX Equalizer-based cross-level matching can be exercised and validated end-to-end on controlled ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input datasets already report all lipid identifiers at a single, uniform annotation level — no equalization is needed and the Equalizer matrix would only truncate information The analysis targets plant or bacterial lipids — LipidLynxX currently covers mammalian lipids from 25 classes across five categories The goal is ontology or pathway mapping rather than cross-level identifier matching — the Linker module or LION-style mapping tools are the appropriate route

skills.description: Use when you need labeled synthetic mass spectrometry peak data with known signal/noise ground truth (e.g., to compute ROC curves for a classification method) because real peak-level annotations are unavailable.
skills.name: synthetic-mass-spectrometry-data-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-mass-spectrometry-data-generation Use when you need labeled synthetic mass spectrometry peak data with known signal/noise ground truth (e.g., to compute ROC curves for a classification method) because real peak-level annotations are unavailable. The input is real timsTOF raw data in Bruker .d format — access it via proteolizard-data/OpenTIMS instead of generating synthetic windows You need to model chemical/repeated-contaminant noise, which is self-similar and not captured by the Poisson noise model used here You need a validated real-data gold standard for evaluation — the paper notes no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real data was available, which is precisely why synthetics are generated http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Generates ground-truth-annotated synthetic timsTOF-style mass spectrometry windows (noise-only and signal+noise) using the createSynthetics module of the mzBucket/proteolizard framework, with Poisson-distributed noise peaks and averagine-modeled isotope patterns, to benchmark signal-classification methods such as LSH against intensity thresholding. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-022-04833-5
skills.summary: Generates ground-truth-annotated synthetic timsTOF-style mass spectrometry windows (noise-only and signal+noise) using the createSynthetics module of the mzBucket/proteolizard framework, with Poisson-distributed noise peaks and averagine-modeled isotope patterns, to benchmark signal-classification methods such as LSH against intensity thresholding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real timsTOF raw data in Bruker .d format — access it via proteolizard-data/OpenTIMS instead of generating synthetic windows You need to model chemical/repeated-contaminant noise, which is self-similar and not captured by the Poisson noise model used here You need a validated real-data gold standard for evaluation — the paper notes no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real data was available, which is precisely why synthetics are generated

skills.summary: Benchmark peak list alignment algorithms by generating synthetic metabolomic/lipidomic datasets from a seed sample with known ground-truth correspondences, then scoring precision and recall of each aligner (e.g. RANSAC vs Join aligner in MZmine 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already real experimental data with no ground-truth alignment table — the synthetic seed-expansion scheme requires known true correspondences by construction The goal is general MS data processing (peak picking, deisotoping, gap filling) rather than benchmarking of alignment algorithms specifically Only a single aligner is of interest with no comparison target — precision/recall benchmarking is only meaningful relative to the ground truth and, ideally, a competing aligner such as the Join aligner

skills.description: Use when labeled pathway data is too sparse to train a pathway-prediction model like NetAurHPD, and a subset of known chemical reactions (e.g., TomatoCyc directional pathways) is available to imitate metabolic activity.
skills.name: synthetic-metabolomics-data-augmentation
skills.search_text: synthetic-metabolomics-data-augmentation Use when labeled pathway data is too sparse to train a pathway-prediction model like NetAurHPD, and a subset of known chemical reactions (e.g., TomatoCyc directional pathways) is available to imitate metabolic activity. The goal is network auralization or waveform representation of an existing real Metabolite CN (Algorithm 1 / SignalPropagation), not synthetic network generation. You need to predict pathway presence from already-trained M5 waveforms — then only hyperlink waveform averaging and Youden-index threshold optimization are needed. The organism's pathway pool is not directional or lacks substrate/product labels, so reactions cannot be executed as substrate-to-product transformations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates artificial Metabolite CNs by simulating metabolic activity over a directional pool of known reactions (e.g., 126 tomato pericarp pathways) and computing Pearson correlations between metabolites, to mitigate the sparsity of labeled data for hyperlink prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Generates artificial Metabolite CNs by simulating metabolic activity over a directional pool of known reactions (e.g., 126 tomato pericarp pathways) and computing Pearson correlations between metabolites, to mitigate the sparsity of labeled data for hyperlink prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is network auralization or waveform representation of an existing real Metabolite CN (Algorithm 1 / SignalPropagation), not synthetic network generation. You need to predict pathway presence from already-trained M5 waveforms — then only hyperlink waveform averaging and Youden-index threshold optimization are needed. The organism's pathway pool is not directional or lacks substrate/product labels, so reactions cannot be executed as substrate-to-product transformations.

When the input is already a real, ontology-mapped dataset from BinBase or another repository — no synthetic fixture is needed. skills.summary: Generate in-task synthetic metadata-annotated intensity fixtures that mimic GC–TOF MS metabolomics data (FAME-normalized intensities per metadata triad) to validate OGDA-style ontologically grouped differential analysis pipelines end-to-end before running on real BinBase data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a real, ontology-mapped dataset from BinBase or another repository — no synthetic fixture is needed. When the goal is to validate statistical machinery that does not consume metadata-annotated intensity matrices (e.g. pure spectral processing tools). When the analysis requires realistic noise/detector saturation effects that a simple synthetic fixture cannot replicate (e.g. coelution-driven abundance underestimation).

skills.search_text: synthetic-nmr-spectrum-generation Use when no public annotated NMR spectra database exists and labeled training spectra are needed for deep-learning-based metabolite identification/quantification in 1H plasma NMR. When experimentally acquired NMR spectra with expert annotations (e.g. Chenomx-fitted reports) are already available — simulation is only motivated by the absence of a public annotated NMR spectra database When the target biofluid is not plasma — the article notes a biofluid-specific analysis pipeline for other biofluids was not yet developed, and lipoprotein/EDTA clusters are plasma-specific When a calibrated spectral deconvolution on a small sample set suffices (e.g. Bayesian tools like Batman or ASICS linear-combination fitting) rather than training data synthesis for deep learning http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates synthetic annotated 1H NMR plasma spectra for training the NMRQNet CRNN model by rendering metabolite reference-library peak signatures as Lorentzian curves, applying data augmentation (shift jitter, multiplet variation, noise), and mixing concentrations sampled from a gamma distribution. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.03.01.530642

skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimentally acquired NMR spectra with expert annotations (e.g. Chenomx-fitted reports) are already available — simulation is only motivated by the absence of a public annotated NMR spectra database When the target biofluid is not plasma — the article notes a biofluid-specific analysis pipeline for other biofluids was not yet developed, and lipoprotein/EDTA clusters are plasma-specific When a calibrated spectral deconvolution on a small sample set suffices (e.g. Bayesian tools like Batman or ASICS linear-combination fitting) rather than training data synthesis for deep learning

skills.search_text: synthetic-nmr-spectrum-simulation Use when you must validate that an NMR fitting implementation reproduces documented lineshape equations — e.g. testing MultiNMRFit's mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian singlet, doublet, triplet, doublet-of-doublets, or quadruplet models against ground truth. Input is real experimental 1H/13C/31P spectra with unknown true parameter values — this skill targets synthetic validation against predefined ground truth, not routine spectrum fitting Analysis goal is pseudo-2D series fitting or biological interpretation rather than verifying that signal-model equations are correctly reconstructed Spectra require user-defined custom signal models outside the five built-in multiplicities (singlet through quadruplet) Simulate synthetic 1D NMR spectra with known ground-truth multiplet parameters and validate that signal-model fitting software (MultiNMRFit) recovers them, by implementing the built-in mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian singlet-to-quadruplet models and quantifying per-parameter recovery error. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental 1H/13C/31P spectra with unknown true parameter values — this skill targets synthetic validation against predefined ground truth, not routine spectrum fitting Analysis goal is pseudo-2D series fitting or biological interpretation rather than verifying that signal-model equations are correctly reconstructed Spectra require user-defined custom signal models outside the five built-in multiplicities (singlet through quadruplet)

skills.search_text: synthetic-noise-spike-in-validation Use when benchmarking a spectral denoising or noise-removal method and you need a quantitative recovery metric from spectra with known ground truth (clean reference plus controlled spiked noise). When no clean reference spectrum exists for the compound — similarity to ground truth cannot be computed and you must instead use Denoising Search against reference libraries When evaluating annotation performance on real experimental data (e.g., AD plasma samples) where ground-truth noise labels are unavailable; use Denoising Search metrics instead For instruments other than Orbitrap without retuning — the paper notes parameters are optimized for Orbitrap instruments and adaptation requires revalidation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Validates an MS/MS denoising method by contaminating clean reference spectra with synthetic electronic/chemical noise ions, then quantifying recovery via spectral entropy similarity between the denoised output and the pristine reference. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02646-x

skills.search_text: synthetic-omics-count-matrix-generation Use when benchmarking the computational cost of correlation-based network construction across R packages (e.g. MetaNet vs WGCNA or NetCoMi) and reproducible, identical synthetic count-matrix inputs are needed. skills.description: Use when benchmarking MetaNet (or a comparable correlation-network tool) across a range of feature counts and you need controlled synthetic count tables spanning below and above the 1,000-feature threshold rather than real data.

skills.search_text: synthetic-omics-table-generation Use when benchmarking MetaNet (or a comparable correlation-network tool) across a range of feature counts and you need controlled synthetic count tables spanning below and above the 1,000-feature threshold rather than real data. The goal is to reproduce a published case-study network on real data (e.g. the longitudinal airborne microbiome or the >40,000-feature exposome–transcriptome integrative network) rather than to measure computational scaling. skills.description: Use when benchmarking pathway-ranking methods (ORA, mPLAGE/PLAGE, GSEA) for robustness to missing or spurious compound annotations, e.g. simulating degraded peak-annotation completeness before trusting method rankings on real metabolomics peak data.
skills.name: synthetic-pathway-simulation
skills.search_text: synthetic-pathway-simulation Use when benchmarking pathway-ranking methods (ORA, mPLAGE/PLAGE, GSEA) for robustness to missing or spurious compound annotations, e.g. simulating degraded peak-annotation completeness before trusting method rankings on real metabolomics peak data. Input is real experimental peak data with verified compound annotations — the synthetic simulation is for method benchmarking, not for pathway ranking of an actual study. The goal is a single pathway-activity ranking rather than a controlled comparison of method robustness under injected annotation noise. The pathway database is not KEGG-compound-based (e.g. Reactome via UniProt/ENSEMBL for proteomics or transcriptomics), since the synthetic decoy design targets KEGG compound annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds a synthetic metabolomics benchmark (seven significantly changing target pathways plus 100 background pathways in PALS peak-intensity/KEGG-annotation format) with injected decoy features at 0–1000% levels, to quantify how robustly ORA, mPLAGE, and GSEA recover true pathway activity as annotation completeness degrades. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Builds a synthetic metabolomics benchmark (seven significantly changing target pathways plus 100 background pathways in PALS peak-intensity/KEGG-annotation format) with injected decoy features at 0–1000% levels, to quantify how robustly ORA, mPLAGE, and GSEA recover true pathway activity as annotation completeness degrades.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental peak data with verified compound annotations — the synthetic simulation is for method benchmarking, not for pathway ranking of an actual study. The goal is a single pathway-activity ranking rather than a controlled comparison of method robustness under injected annotation noise. The pathway database is not KEGG-compound-based (e.g. Reactome via UniProt/ENSEMBL for proteomics or transcriptomics), since the synthetic decoy design targets KEGG compound annotation.

skills.description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML data lacks standardized experimental QC samples (common for public metabolomics datasets) yet feature intensities must be corrected for batch, run-order, and intensity drift before statistical analysis or pre-training a model like the VAE.
skills.name: synthetic-qc-drift-correction
skills.search_text: synthetic-qc-drift-correction Use when raw LC/MS mzML data lacks standardized experimental QC samples (common for public metabolomics datasets) yet feature intensities must be corrected for batch, run-order, and intensity drift before statistical analysis or pre-training a model like the VAE. Input is already a normalized feature table (e.g. the 2,736-column CSV matrix accepted by mzEmbed) — re-running drift correction is unnecessary and would duplicate mzLearn's preprocessing. A study provides its own standardized experimental QC samples and a traditional QC-based normalization pipeline is preferred — synthetic QC is a replacement for, not an addition to, experimental QC correction. Downstream analysis requires de-isotoping or MS/MS identification — mzLearn results are at the ion MS1 level only and mapping ion features to MS/MS spectra must be carried out with downstream workflows. The LC mode is not HILIC positive mode (e.g. reverse-phase or negative mode) — the current pre-trained drift model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 A data-driven drift-correction skill that normalizes LC/MS feature intensities across large cohorts using mzLearn's internally generated synthetic QC samples instead of experimental QC injections, achieving RSD comparable to QC-based normalization without requiring pooled or blank QC runs. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: A data-driven drift-correction skill that normalizes LC/MS feature intensities across large cohorts using mzLearn's internally generated synthetic QC samples instead of experimental QC injections, achieving RSD comparable to QC-based normalization without requiring pooled or blank QC runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized feature table (e.g. the 2,736-column CSV matrix accepted by mzEmbed) — re-running drift correction is unnecessary and would duplicate mzLearn's preprocessing. A study provides its own standardized experimental QC samples and a traditional QC-based normalization pipeline is preferred — synthetic QC is a replacement for, not an addition to, experimental QC correction. Downstream analysis requires de-isotoping or MS/MS identification — mzLearn results are at the ion MS1 level only and mapping ion features to MS/MS spectra must be carried out with downstream workflows. The LC mode is not HILIC positive mode (e.g. reverse-phase or negative mode) — the current pre-trained drift model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode.

skills.search_text: t-test-differential-metabolite-detection Use when two-group metabolomics intensity data (e.g. case vs control, imputed or complete) must be reduced to a significant-metabolite list, and that list's stability across imputation methods must be quantified via MLCI. The RAW files are from a non-Thermo vendor — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo Fisher RAW files QC requires peptide-level or identification-based metrics — this skill is search-free and uses only acquisition-side signals like TIC You need full spectral peak arrays (m/z, intensity, resolution, noise, charge state) for modelling rather than scan-level summary metrics — use MetaXtract's peak-list (Parquet) export instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes search-free QC metrics from MetaXtract-extracted Thermo RAW-file scan headers, comparing MS1 and MS2 'Total Ion Current' medians between underperforming and reference QC runs to localize signal loss (e.g. 8.4% MS1 drop vs 9.2-fold MS2 reduction pointing to isolation/fragment transmission). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.687968
skills.summary: Computes search-free QC metrics from MetaXtract-extracted Thermo RAW-file scan headers, comparing MS1 and MS2 'Total Ion Current' medians between underperforming and reference QC runs to localize signal loss (e.g. 8.4% MS1 drop vs 9.2-fold MS2 reduction pointing to isolation/fragment transmission).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The RAW files are from a non-Thermo vendor — MetaXtract currently supports only Thermo Fisher RAW files QC requires peptide-level or identification-based metrics — this skill is search-free and uses only acquisition-side signals like TIC You need full spectral peak arrays (m/z, intensity, resolution, noise, charge state) for modelling rather than scan-level summary metrics — use MetaXtract's peak-list (Parquet) export instead

skills.description: Use when a feature/compound table with multi-tool annotations (GNPS, Sirius 6, ISDB-LOTUS) must be scored with the decision-theory k function and sorted by increasing k to rank natural products for novelty prioritization.
skills.name: tabular-ranking-and-sorting
skills.search_text: tabular-ranking-and-sorting Use when a feature/compound table with multi-tool annotations (GNPS, Sirius 6, ISDB-LOTUS) must be scored with the decision-theory k function and sorted by increasing k to rank natural products for novelty prioritization. Input lacks the three annotation sources (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) or their reconstructed indicators — k cannot be aggregated from a single-tool annotation list. Data are raw spectra rather than an FBMN quantitative .csv plus .mgf plus Sirius structure_identifications.tsv. The goal is a generic statistical ranking (e.g., p-value sorting) unrelated to decision-theory knownness scoring of natural product novelty. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Aggregate multiannotated tandem MS data (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) into a decision-theory knownness score k and sort compounds in increasing k order to produce a prioritization ranking, as MS2DECIDE does for its 95-NP chemodiverse library (Table 3). metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Aggregate multiannotated tandem MS data (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) into a decision-theory knownness score k and sort compounds in increasing k order to produce a prioritization ranking, as MS2DECIDE does for its 95-NP chemodiverse library (Table 3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks the three annotation sources (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) or their reconstructed indicators — k cannot be aggregated from a single-tool annotation list. Data are raw spectra rather than an FBMN quantitative .csv plus .mgf plus Sirius structure_identifications.tsv. The goal is a generic statistical ranking (e.g., p-value sorting) unrelated to decision-theory knownness scoring of natural product novelty.

skills.summary: Assemble statistical result outputs into structured CSV tables that pair each compound or category with its metadata annotations, so that downstream chemical-ontology or pathway queries can consume the hit list directly.

skills.description: Use when a research question asks to reproduce specific reported counts from an article — e.g. how many metabolites from each MS1-only database (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) were retained in the PM database after plant-specific filtering — into a small verified table.
skills.name: tabular-result-reproduction
skills.search_text: tabular-result-reproduction Use when a research question asks to reproduce specific reported counts from an article — e.g. how many metabolites from each MS1-only database (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) were retained in the PM database after plant-specific filtering — into a small verified table. Input is raw LC-MS metabolomics data requiring peak picking, data cleaning, or metabolite annotation — MetMiner's upstream tidyMass-driven workflow handles that, not this skill The goal is to independently recompute the retained-metabolite counts by re-running plant-specific filtering over KEGG/KNApSAcK/PlantCyc, rather than extracting and verifying the article's reported numbers http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces published summary tables from a scientific article into a small, validated machine-readable table. Here, it reconstructs the per-source MS1 metabolite counts of MetMiner's integrated plant-specific PM database (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) after plant-specific filtering, as reported in the paper's Results. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: Reproduces published summary tables from a scientific article into a small, validated machine-readable table. Here, it reconstructs the per-source MS1 metabolite counts of MetMiner's integrated plant-specific PM database (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) after plant-specific filtering, as reported in the paper's Results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS metabolomics data requiring peak picking, data cleaning, or metabolite annotation — MetMiner's upstream tidyMass-driven workflow handles that, not this skill The goal is to independently recompute the retained-metabolite counts by re-running plant-specific filtering over KEGG/KNApSAcK/PlantCyc, rather than extracting and verifying the article's reported numbers

skills.name: tabular-result-table-construction
skills.search_text: tabular-result-table-construction Use when a weighted meta-analysis (e.g. amanida's Fisher-method P-value combination) has produced per-compound statistics held in an S4 result object and they must be exported as a structured table such as sample_combined_pvalues.csv. Raw per-study data with disclosed standard deviations are available — then conventional meta-analysis tools using effect sizes and variance apply, not overall-results-only tables The input is qualitative only (identifier plus trend labels with no P-values or fold-changes) and only vote-counting via amanida_vote is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assembles per-compound meta-analysis outputs (combined P-values, fold-change averages, and vote-counts) produced by the amanida package into flat tabular result files, such as a per-compound combined-P-value CSV, so they can be shared or downstream-consumed. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab591

skills.description: Decision support for validating parameter-tuning tables when a grid search over assignment radii and detection thresholds has produced F1 scores per MCF setup and reported optima must be cross-checked.
skills.name: tabular-result-verification
skills.search_text: tabular-result-verification Decision support for validating parameter-tuning tables when a grid search over assignment radii and detection thresholds has produced F1 scores per MCF setup and reported optima must be cross-checked. Input is a single fitted result (one r, one theta) rather than a scanned grid — there is no landscape to verify optima against. The metric is compound concentration reconstruction accuracy rather than F1 — the reported optima and degradation patterns are specific to the F1 classification task on 2D 1H,13C HSQC artificial mixtures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3337 http://edamontology.org/topic_3570 Assembles a per-setup table of optimal (assignment radius r, detection threshold theta) pairs and stability summaries from a scanned F1 grid, verifying that each row reproduces the reported optimum (e.g. setup C: r=0.08, theta=0.003, F1=0.83). metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01652
skills.summary: Assembles a per-setup table of optimal (assignment radius r, detection threshold theta) pairs and stability summaries from a scanned F1 grid, verifying that each row reproduces the reported optimum (e.g. setup C: r=0.08, theta=0.003, F1=0.83).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single fitted result (one r, one theta) rather than a scanned grid — there is no landscape to verify optima against. The metric is compound concentration reconstruction accuracy rather than F1 — the reported optima and degradation patterns are specific to the F1 classification task on 2D 1H,13C HSQC artificial mixtures.

When the goal is to export an intermediate artifact such as the MEMO dissimilarity matrix or the cleaned GNPS annotation table rather than the final ranked extract results When the consumer requires a structured interchange format (e.g. mzML, JSON) rather than Inventa's flat tab-separated output Writes Inventa's computed components (FC, LC, CC, SC) and the final priority rank for each extract to a tab-separated (.tsv) results file, alongside the sample identifiers. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Writes Inventa's computed components (FC, LC, CC, SC) and the final priority rank for each extract to a tab-separated (.tsv) results file, alongside the sample identifiers.
