skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (CSV with samples as rows, metabolite concentration columns, a group/factor column) with two or more sample groups and you need per-metabolite ANOVA and pairwise Tukey p-values assembled into one results table.
skills.name: tabular-statistical-results-assembly
skills.search_text: tabular-statistical-results-assembly Use when you have a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (CSV with samples as rows, metabolite concentration columns, a group/factor column) with two or more sample groups and you need per-metabolite ANOVA and pairwise Tukey p-values assembled into one results table. The dataset has fewer than two groups — Viime restricts multivariate ANOVA to data with two or more groups. Input is not a preprocessed concentration table (e.g. raw platform output or spectra that have not been through Viime's upload, error correction, and imputation steps). The goal is a non-parametric group comparison — Viime's univariate option is the Wilcoxon rank sum test, not ANOVA. http://edamontology.org/topic_3570 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assembles a metabolite-keyed results table from group-comparison statistics (ANOVA plus post-hoc Tukey HSD p-values for every pairwise inter-group comparison), produced by Viime's R-backed statistical analysis pipeline on a preprocessed concentration CSV. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Assembles a metabolite-keyed results table from group-comparison statistics (ANOVA plus post-hoc Tukey HSD p-values for every pairwise inter-group comparison), produced by Viime's R-backed statistical analysis pipeline on a preprocessed concentration CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has fewer than two groups — Viime restricts multivariate ANOVA to data with two or more groups. Input is not a preprocessed concentration table (e.g. raw platform output or spectra that have not been through Viime's upload, error correction, and imputation steps). The goal is a non-parametric group comparison — Viime's univariate option is the Wilcoxon rank sum test, not ANOVA.

skills.description: Use when a tabular dataset (e.g. Excel/csv with a numerical measurement column and a categorical Condition column) needs two-group or multi-group parametric/non-parametric comparisons, and the named test, statistic and p-value per column must be collected into one machine-readable CSV.
skills.name: tabular-statistical-results-export
skills.search_text: tabular-statistical-results-export Use when a tabular dataset (e.g. Excel/csv with a numerical measurement column and a categorical Condition column) needs two-group or multi-group parametric/non-parametric comparisons, and the named test, statistic and p-value per column must be collected into one machine-readable CSV. The data are not tabular group-comparison data with a numerical measurement plus a categorical group column (e.g. raw omics peak lists or image data) Only one group is present per comparison — the t-test/U-test activities are enabled only for columns with exactly two groups and ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis for more than two groups The goal is batch-effect correction or prediction modelling (e.g. ComBat via pyComBat or scikit-learn pipelines) rather than group-comparison testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Dispatch interactive group-comparison statistical tests (t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) in Instant Clue on a loaded dataset such as Tutorial_Data_01.xlsx and export the per-column test statistics and p-values as a flat statistical_tests_results.csv table for reuse. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6
skills.summary: Dispatch interactive group-comparison statistical tests (t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) in Instant Clue on a loaded dataset such as Tutorial_Data_01.xlsx and export the per-column test statistics and p-values as a flat statistical_tests_results.csv table for reuse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not tabular group-comparison data with a numerical measurement plus a categorical group column (e.g. raw omics peak lists or image data) Only one group is present per comparison — the t-test/U-test activities are enabled only for columns with exactly two groups and ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis for more than two groups The goal is batch-effect correction or prediction modelling (e.g. ComBat via pyComBat or scikit-learn pipelines) rather than group-comparison testing

skills.description: Use when a benchmark/runtimes table must be reduced to per-tool summary statistics (means, speedup fold-change) and cross-checked against values reported in a publication's figure or abstract.
skills.name: tabular-summary-statistics-aggregation
skills.search_text: tabular-summary-statistics-aggregation Use when a benchmark/runtimes table must be reduced to per-tool summary statistics (means, speedup fold-change) and cross-checked against values reported in a publication's figure or abstract. The goal is to benchmark annotation accuracy or coverage (annotated metabolite counts) rather than computational runtime — different source data columns are needed Only a single tool's runtimes are available with no paired MetDNA2/MetDNA3 dataset column, so no fold-speedup can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates per-dataset wall-clock runtime tables (e.g. MetDNA2 vs MetDNA3 across 12 datasets from 3 biological samples) into per-tool mean runtimes and a fold-speedup statistic, verifying that computed summaries match the reported benchmark (~1082 min vs ~77 min, >14-fold) within rounding tolerance. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Aggregates per-dataset wall-clock runtime tables (e.g. MetDNA2 vs MetDNA3 across 12 datasets from 3 biological samples) into per-tool mean runtimes and a fold-speedup statistic, verifying that computed summaries match the reported benchmark (~1082 min vs ~77 min, >14-fold) within rounding tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark annotation accuracy or coverage (annotated metabolite counts) rather than computational runtime — different source data columns are needed Only a single tool's runtimes are available with no paired MetDNA2/MetDNA3 dataset column, so no fold-speedup can be computed

skills.description: Use when the input is a table with a time axis and per-trace signal columns (e.g. intensities from optical recordings like the bundled Example Data 03), and you need to baseline-correct, transform, smooth or quantify traces before plotting or export.
skills.name: tabular-time-series-data-manipulation
skills.search_text: tabular-time-series-data-manipulation Use when the input is a table with a time axis and per-trace signal columns (e.g. intensities from optical recordings like the bundled Example Data 03), and you need to baseline-correct, transform, smooth or quantify traces before plotting or export. skills.summary: Manipulate signal-over-time measurements held in tabular data frames (e.g. optical recordings of POMC neuron activity) by applying column-level transformations such as baseline correction, normalization, smoothing and rolling-window calculations, then interactively determining metrics like area under the curve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is high-dimensional molecular data (e.g. proteomics/omics matrices) where multi-block omics integration or dimensional reduction is needed rather than signal-over-time correction. Raw image stacks or detector vendor files that are not yet converted into a tabular signal-over-time layout — the transformation layer only operates on columns in the dataset. The task is hypothesis testing across groups (ANOVA, regressions) rather than trace manipulation; the statistical tests are toggled by drag & drop from the Analysis toolbox, not by column activities.

skills.description: Use when messy tabular spreadsheet data (Excel or CSV) must be turned into key-based JSON records for a relational database or Metabolomics Workbench deposition, and a tag layer can be inserted into the sheet.
skills.name: tabular-to-json-record-extraction
skills.search_text: tabular-to-json-record-extraction Use when messy tabular spreadsheet data (Excel or CSV) must be turned into key-based JSON records for a relational database or Metabolomics Workbench deposition, and a tag layer can be inserted into the sheet. The input is already a clean, validated JSON file — in that case use the MESSES validate or convert commands instead of extract The target output format is not supported — conversion from extracted JSON relies on the data being in a specific schema, and currently only mwTab (Metabolomics Workbench) is a supported format The data cannot accept an inserted tag layer (e.g., non-tabular or locked spreadsheets), since the tagging system is the key mechanism of extraction http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Transforms messy, arbitrarily organized tabular spreadsheet data (Excel or CSV) into clean, well-structured JSONized metadata by adding a layer of extraction tags (#export, #automate, #modify directives) to the spreadsheet and running MESSES's extract command. This is the first step of the MESSES extract-validate-convert workflow aimed at Metabolomics Workbench depositions. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13070842
skills.summary: Transforms messy, arbitrarily organized tabular spreadsheet data (Excel or CSV) into clean, well-structured JSONized metadata by adding a layer of extraction tags (#export, #automate, #modify directives) to the spreadsheet and running MESSES's extract command. This is the first step of the MESSES extract-validate-convert workflow aimed at Metabolomics Workbench depositions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a clean, validated JSON file — in that case use the MESSES validate or convert commands instead of extract The target output format is not supported — conversion from extracted JSON relies on the data being in a specific schema, and currently only mwTab (Metabolomics Workbench) is a supported format The data cannot accept an inserted tag layer (e.g., non-tabular or locked spreadsheets), since the tagging system is the key mechanism of extraction

skills.description: Use when reviewing or reproducing protein–protein interaction evidence from a paper that relies on endogenously tagged worm strains, and you need a structured table linking construct pairs (tag type and fusion position) to the assay outcomes and their figure locations.
skills.name: tagged-protein-strain-annotation
skills.search_text: tagged-protein-strain-annotation Use when reviewing or reproducing protein–protein interaction evidence from a paper that relies on endogenously tagged worm strains, and you need a structured table linking construct pairs (tag type and fusion position) to the assay outcomes and their figure locations. When the paper's interaction claims rely on genetic or phenotypic data only (e.g. crossover frequency counts, GFP::MSH-5 focus timing) and no tagged-protein physical-interaction assay is described. When a proteomics database (UniProt, WormBase) already provides the tagged-strain and assay annotations you need and re-deriving them from full text adds no value. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates C. elegans strains by the fluorescent or epitope tags carried by their proteins (e.g. RMH-2::mCherry, TOP-3::HA, GFP::MSH-5, RMH-2::FLAG) and maps each tagged construct pair to the physical-interaction assay that depends on it, enabling reproducible evidence tracking. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac408
skills.summary: Annotates C. elegans strains by the fluorescent or epitope tags carried by their proteins (e.g. RMH-2::mCherry, TOP-3::HA, GFP::MSH-5, RMH-2::FLAG) and maps each tagged construct pair to the physical-interaction assay that depends on it, enabling reproducible evidence tracking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the paper's interaction claims rely on genetic or phenotypic data only (e.g. crossover frequency counts, GFP::MSH-5 focus timing) and no tagged-protein physical-interaction assay is described. When a proteomics database (UniProt, WormBase) already provides the tagged-strain and assay annotations you need and re-deriving them from full text adds no value.

skills.search_text: tailoring-reaction-library-enumeration Use when you must quantify RAIChU's built-in biosynthetic reaction coverage — tailoring reactions, RiPP PTM families, NRPS A-domain substrates/starter units, and PKS KS subtypes/extender units — before relying on it to visualise fully maturated pathways. skills.description: Use when you have a taxonomic profiler output and a ground-truth profile for the same sample (e.g., CAMI2 marine marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and need to find which specific clades a high-scoring profiler misses.
skills.name: tampa-contrast-mode-configuration
skills.search_text: tampa-contrast-mode-configuration Use when you have a taxonomic profiler output and a ground-truth profile for the same sample (e.g., CAMI2 marine marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and need to find which specific clades a high-scoring profiler misses. Input is amplicon microbial data — tools like metacoder are for amplicon data, but TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic profiles; conversely metacoder should not be substituted here. No ground-truth profile exists for the sample — contrast mode requires a gold standard to flag false positives/false negatives; without one use TAMPA's normal mode to compare profiler outputs. Goal is a single-value benchmarking score rather than identifying specific discordant clades — use a benchmarking platform like OPAL for aggregate metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Configure and run TAMPA in contrast mode (-c True) to compare a profiler's taxonomic profile against a gold-standard profile at a chosen taxonomic rank, highlighting clades present in only one profile (false positives/false negatives) that single-value metrics such as the F1 score miss. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Configure and run TAMPA in contrast mode (-c True) to compare a profiler's taxonomic profile against a gold-standard profile at a chosen taxonomic rank, highlighting clades present in only one profile (false positives/false negatives) that single-value metrics such as the F1 score miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is amplicon microbial data — tools like metacoder are for amplicon data, but TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic profiles; conversely metacoder should not be substituted here. No ground-truth profile exists for the sample — contrast mode requires a gold standard to flag false positives/false negatives; without one use TAMPA's normal mode to compare profiler outputs. Goal is a single-value benchmarking score rather than identifying specific discordant clades — use a benchmarking platform like OPAL for aggregate metrics.

skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-candidate-ranking
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-candidate-ranking Use when you have tandem mass spectra and database-retrieved candidate structures and need a fragmentation-only candidate ranking baseline, e.g. to benchmark in silico fragmenters before adding reference, retention-time, or user-defined scores. Reference (literature/patent counts) or retention-time information is available and intended for scoring — this skill isolates the fragmentation-only baseline, so including those terms here would confound the comparison Candidates come from a spectral library (e.g. MassBank) search rather than in silico fragmentation of database candidates — library matching is a different identification strategy Spectra contain no fragment peaks other than the precursor (e.g. spectra dominated by a single water loss) — such spectra 'simply do not contain enough information' to distinguish candidates http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Ranks candidate structures retrieved from PubChem against merged HR-MS/MS spectra (473 merged Orbitrap spectra from the HILL dataset) using fragmentation information only, comparing MetFrag2.2's in silico bond dissociation against CFM-ID's competitive fragment modelling. It reproduces the fragmentation-only baseline (30 vs 43 Top 1 ranks) that motivates MetFrag2.2's additional scoring terms. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: Ranks candidate structures retrieved from PubChem against merged HR-MS/MS spectra (473 merged Orbitrap spectra from the HILL dataset) using fragmentation information only, comparing MetFrag2.2's in silico bond dissociation against CFM-ID's competitive fragment modelling. It reproduces the fragmentation-only baseline (30 vs 43 Top 1 ranks) that motivates MetFrag2.2's additional scoring terms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference (literature/patent counts) or retention-time information is available and intended for scoring — this skill isolates the fragmentation-only baseline, so including those terms here would confound the comparison Candidates come from a spectral library (e.g. MassBank) search rather than in silico fragmentation of database candidates — library matching is a different identification strategy Spectra contain no fragment peaks other than the precursor (e.g. spectra dominated by a single water loss) — such spectra 'simply do not contain enough information' to distinguish candidates

skills.description: Use when you have experimental high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of putative NRP/PK natural products and a curated sequence database (e.g., 146 NRP/siderophore sequences, 85 building blocks) and need ranked compound identifications or dereplication accuracy metrics.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-database-search
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-database-search Use when you have experimental high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of putative NRP/PK natural products and a curated sequence database (e.g., 146 NRP/siderophore sequences, 85 building blocks) and need ranked compound identifications or dereplication accuracy metrics. When the query compounds are non-peptidic natural products better handled by Dereplicator+ in-silico fragmentation rather than building-block sequences When users need custom NRP/PK building-block/sequence databases but NRPro is the target engine — NRPro users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences When spectra are low-resolution, since the method is validated with 5 ppm precursor and fragment ion m/z error tolerances http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Dereplication of high-resolution tandem mass spectra of NRPs/polyketides by searching them against a custom building-block/sequence database in CycloBranch, ranking candidate structures and computing top-1 and top-10 retrieval accuracy. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00530-2
skills.summary: Dereplication of high-resolution tandem mass spectra of NRPs/polyketides by searching them against a custom building-block/sequence database in CycloBranch, ranking candidate structures and computing top-1 and top-10 retrieval accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query compounds are non-peptidic natural products better handled by Dereplicator+ in-silico fragmentation rather than building-block sequences When users need custom NRP/PK building-block/sequence databases but NRPro is the target engine — NRPro users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences When spectra are low-resolution, since the method is validated with 5 ppm precursor and fragment ion m/z error tolerances

skills.description: Use when evaluating a structure-annotation confidence score (e.g. COSMIC) on reference MS/MS spectra and you need to emulate the lower quality of biological-sample spectra at controlled distortion levels.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-distortion-simulation
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-distortion-simulation Use when evaluating a structure-annotation confidence score (e.g. COSMIC) on reference MS/MS spectra and you need to emulate the lower quality of biological-sample spectra at controlled distortion levels. The input spectra are already real biological-sample spectra with authentic low quality — no simulation of noise is needed The goal is scoring confidence on pristine library spectra without evaluating robustness to degradation The task is spectral library search or de-replication rather than calibration of confidence-score evaluation under distortion http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Simulates the lower quality of biological-sample tandem MS/MS by adding medium or high levels of distortion (mass shifts, intensity variations, noise-peak injection) to reference fragmentation spectra, calibrated so the median cosine similarity to the originals matches 0.880 (medium) and 0.714 (high). This lets a confidence score such as COSMIC be evaluated under realistic spectrum degradation. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Simulates the lower quality of biological-sample tandem MS/MS by adding medium or high levels of distortion (mass shifts, intensity variations, noise-peak injection) to reference fragmentation spectra, calibrated so the median cosine similarity to the originals matches 0.880 (medium) and 0.714 (high). This lets a confidence score such as COSMIC be evaluated under realistic spectrum degradation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input spectra are already real biological-sample spectra with authentic low quality — no simulation of noise is needed The goal is scoring confidence on pristine library spectra without evaluating robustness to degradation The task is spectral library search or de-replication rather than calibration of confidence-score evaluation under distortion

skills.description: Use when pairwise distances between proteomics samples must be quantified directly from peak-listed tandem mass spectra (MGF) without peptide identification or spectral libraries, e.g. to build a distance matrix for molecular phylogenetics or data quality control.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-dot-product-computation
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-dot-product-computation Use when pairwise distances between proteomics samples must be quantified directly from peak-listed tandem mass spectra (MGF) without peptide identification or spectral libraries, e.g. to build a distance matrix for molecular phylogenetics or data quality control. Input spectra must be identified against a sequence database or spectral library — compareMS2 deliberately does not use existing sequence data or spectra assigned to specific peptide sequences (that is the Mascot/Comet or SpectraST/BiblioSpec class of tools) The goal is de novo peptide sequencing from spectra with no genomic or spectral prior — a LUTEFISK/PepNovo-style tool is the right class instead Samples contain no similar spectra at all: the distance tends to +infinity as set size grows, so the metric is uninformative for completely unrelated datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes the distribution of dot products (cosine-type similarities) between all pairs of unannotated tandem mass spectra from two LC-MS/MS datasets, as in compareMS2, then summarizes it as a shared-peptide fraction that is inverted into a pairwise distance metric. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.6162
skills.summary: Computes the distribution of dot products (cosine-type similarities) between all pairs of unannotated tandem mass spectra from two LC-MS/MS datasets, as in compareMS2, then summarizes it as a shared-peptide fraction that is inverted into a pairwise distance metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra must be identified against a sequence database or spectral library — compareMS2 deliberately does not use existing sequence data or spectra assigned to specific peptide sequences (that is the Mascot/Comet or SpectraST/BiblioSpec class of tools) The goal is de novo peptide sequencing from spectra with no genomic or spectral prior — a LUTEFISK/PepNovo-style tool is the right class instead Samples contain no similar spectra at all: the distance tends to +infinity as set size grows, so the metric is uninformative for completely unrelated datasets

skills.description: Use when you have embedded a set of tandem mass spectra (e.g. NIST20, MoNA) into a vector space and need to quantify whether that space reflects molecular structural similarity or supports analog retrieval.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-embedding-evaluation
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-embedding-evaluation Use when you have embedded a set of tandem mass spectra (e.g. NIST20, MoNA) into a vector space and need to quantify whether that space reflects molecular structural similarity or supports analog retrieval. The spectra are unannotated and no reference molecular structures/fingerprints exist, so Tanimoto or MCES ground-truth similarity cannot be computed The goal is de novo spectrum-to-structure annotation (fingerprint prediction) rather than evaluating similarity/embedding quality — use fingerprint prediction benchmarks such as the MIST retrieval benchmark instead The evaluation targets non-positive-mode or multiply charged precursors, outside the scope of the reported benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmark the quality of MS/MS spectral embeddings by testing whether cosine similarity in the embedding space correlates with molecular structural similarity (Tanimoto of fingerprints) and supports library retrieval, comparing against MS2DeepScore, spectral entropy and other standard spectral similarity measures. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Benchmark the quality of MS/MS spectral embeddings by testing whether cosine similarity in the embedding space correlates with molecular structural similarity (Tanimoto of fingerprints) and supports library retrieval, comparing against MS2DeepScore, spectral entropy and other standard spectral similarity measures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are unannotated and no reference molecular structures/fingerprints exist, so Tanimoto or MCES ground-truth similarity cannot be computed The goal is de novo spectrum-to-structure annotation (fingerprint prediction) rather than evaluating similarity/embedding quality — use fingerprint prediction benchmarks such as the MIST retrieval benchmark instead The evaluation targets non-positive-mode or multiply charged precursors, outside the scope of the reported benchmark

skills.description: Use when raw GNPS/MassIVE .mzML experiments must be converted into deduplicated, quality-filtered, paired or unpaired MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g. GeMS, MoNA, NIST20) for self-supervised pre-training or supervised fine-tuning of spectrum annotation models.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-library-preparation
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-library-preparation Use when raw GNPS/MassIVE .mzML experiments must be converted into deduplicated, quality-filtered, paired or unpaired MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g. GeMS, MoNA, NIST20) for self-supervised pre-training or supervised fine-tuning of spectrum annotation models. The input is already a curated, paired spectral library in HDF5 or MGF format — re-running mining and LSH clustering would waste compute and could duplicate existing quality control. The analysis targets MS1 isotopic patterns, adduct distributions, negative ionization mode, or multiply charged precursor ions — the GeMS/DreaMS pipeline focuses solely on positive-mode, singly charged tandem mass spectra. The goal is to build spectral similarity measures (e.g. spectral entropy, MS2DeepScore) on already-clean spectra rather than to prepare raw repository-scale libraries. Prepare curated tandem MS/MS training and evaluation libraries by mining LC–MS/MS experiments from the MassIVE GNPS repository, quality-filtering spectra into GeMS-A/B/C subsets, deduplicating via LSH clustering, and storing compact HDF5 files for downstream DreaMS fine-tuning. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Prepare curated tandem MS/MS training and evaluation libraries by mining LC–MS/MS experiments from the MassIVE GNPS repository, quality-filtering spectra into GeMS-A/B/C subsets, deduplicating via LSH clustering, and storing compact HDF5 files for downstream DreaMS fine-tuning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated, paired spectral library in HDF5 or MGF format — re-running mining and LSH clustering would waste compute and could duplicate existing quality control. The analysis targets MS1 isotopic patterns, adduct distributions, negative ionization mode, or multiply charged precursor ions — the GeMS/DreaMS pipeline focuses solely on positive-mode, singly charged tandem mass spectra. The goal is to build spectral similarity measures (e.g. spectral entropy, MS2DeepScore) on already-clean spectra rather than to prepare raw repository-scale libraries.

skills.description: Use when you have a molecular structure dataset (e.g., NIST20 labels.tsv + mgf_files + spec_files.hdf5) and need to predict MS/MS spectra or compare spectrum simulators under matched covariates and hyperparameter sweeps.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-prediction
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-prediction Use when you have a molecular structure dataset (e.g., NIST20 labels.tsv + mgf_files + spec_files.hdf5) and need to predict MS/MS spectra or compare spectrum simulators under matched covariates and hyperparameter sweeps. You only need a FAST heuristic for high-throughput screening — ICEBERG costs ~1 CPU second per molecule, nearly an order of magnitude more than SCARF. You need guaranteed-correct physical fragment explanations — the paper notes there are no guarantees that generated fragment explanations are the correct physical explanations due to equivalent-mass atom and bond rearrangements. You are working with the NPLIB1/CANOPUS dataset on the main branch — support for NPLIB1 is retired; use the legacy iceberg_1.0 branch instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Predict molecular tandem MS/MS spectra from structures using the ICEBERG two-part pipeline (a DAG fragment generator followed by a Transformer intensity model), alongside baselines like MassFormer and SCARF, and evaluate predictions by average cosine similarity against reference spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Predict molecular tandem MS/MS spectra from structures using the ICEBERG two-part pipeline (a DAG fragment generator followed by a Transformer intensity model), alongside baselines like MassFormer and SCARF, and evaluate predictions by average cosine similarity against reference spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a FAST heuristic for high-throughput screening — ICEBERG costs ~1 CPU second per molecule, nearly an order of magnitude more than SCARF. You need guaranteed-correct physical fragment explanations — the paper notes there are no guarantees that generated fragment explanations are the correct physical explanations due to equivalent-mass atom and bond rearrangements. You are working with the NPLIB1/CANOPUS dataset on the main branch — support for NPLIB1 is retired; use the legacy iceberg_1.0 branch instead.

skills.description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra in MGF format must be converted to h5py and normalized/denoised before spectral similarity computation, spectral library search, or training/testing TransExION on GNPS/GNPS_MassBank/mergedGNPS data.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-preprocessing
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-preprocessing Use when raw MS/MS spectra in MGF format must be converted to h5py and normalized/denoised before spectral similarity computation, spectral library search, or training/testing TransExION on GNPS/GNPS_MassBank/mergedGNPS data. The input is already an h5py (.db) spectrum file that was preprocessed under the same protocol — re-running conversion/filtering would alter peak lists inconsistently with prior processing. The downstream task is structural (Tanimoto) similarity on molecular fingerprints via RDKit, not spectral peak-list processing — ms_compute_structural_similarity.py is the relevant entry point instead. The goal is computing spectral similarity scores themselves (ms_test_spectral_similarity.py or baseline Cosine/Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore scoring) rather than preparing the spectra those tools consume. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocess MS/MS tandem mass spectra into the normalized, denoised h5py representation required by TransExION-style spectral similarity pipelines: convert MGF files to h5py, round m/z to two decimals, convert intensities to relative abundance (%), filter fragments (0.1% ≤ intensity, 10 ≤ m/z ≤ 1000 Da), and denoise by keeping only the highest peak within a 3-Da sliding window. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-024-00858-5
skills.summary: Preprocess MS/MS tandem mass spectra into the normalized, denoised h5py representation required by TransExION-style spectral similarity pipelines: convert MGF files to h5py, round m/z to two decimals, convert intensities to relative abundance (%), filter fragments (0.1% ≤ intensity, 10 ≤ m/z ≤ 1000 Da), and denoise by keeping only the highest peak within a 3-Da sliding window.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an h5py (.db) spectrum file that was preprocessed under the same protocol — re-running conversion/filtering would alter peak lists inconsistently with prior processing. The downstream task is structural (Tanimoto) similarity on molecular fingerprints via RDKit, not spectral peak-list processing — ms_compute_structural_similarity.py is the relevant entry point instead. The goal is computing spectral similarity scores themselves (ms_test_spectral_similarity.py or baseline Cosine/Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore scoring) rather than preparing the spectra those tools consume.

skills.description: Use when two or more LC-MS/MS datasets exported as MGF tandem mass spectra need a set-level similarity and distance (not peptide identification) — e.g. species identification, mixture characterization, phylogenetics, or batch-effect QC on spectral content.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-set-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-set-overlap-analysis Use when two or more LC-MS/MS datasets exported as MGF tandem mass spectra need a set-level similarity and distance (not peptide identification) — e.g. species identification, mixture characterization, phylogenetics, or batch-effect QC on spectral content. The goal is peptide/protein identification against a sequence database or a spectral library of peptides with assigned sequences — compareMS2 compares spectra sets directly, not to predicted or annotated spectra The input is already a protein quantitation or feature table rather than raw tandem mass spectral peak lists in MGF format Only a single spectrum pair must be scored (e.g. library search of one query spectrum) — this skill computes set-level overlap S and D, not per-spectrum identification http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes the global similarity S and symmetric distance D between two sets of tandem mass spectra as implemented in compareMS2 2.0: pairwise spectral-angle similarity (eq 1), similar-spectrum subsets (eqs 2-3), averaged matching fraction S (eq 4), and D = 1/S - 1 (eq 6) with a half-matching-spectrum convention so the metric stays symmetric when S = 0. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00457
skills.summary: Computes the global similarity S and symmetric distance D between two sets of tandem mass spectra as implemented in compareMS2 2.0: pairwise spectral-angle similarity (eq 1), similar-spectrum subsets (eqs 2-3), averaged matching fraction S (eq 4), and D = 1/S - 1 (eq 6) with a half-matching-spectrum convention so the metric stays symmetric when S = 0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peptide/protein identification against a sequence database or a spectral library of peptides with assigned sequences — compareMS2 compares spectra sets directly, not to predicted or annotated spectra The input is already a protein quantitation or feature table rather than raw tandem mass spectral peak lists in MGF format Only a single spectrum pair must be scored (e.g. library search of one query spectrum) — this skill computes set-level overlap S and D, not per-spectrum identification

skills.description: Use when you have positive and/or negative ionization mode MS/MS peak spectra (mgf, msp, mzML, mzXML, json, usi) and need predicted chemical similarity scores, e.g., to build a unified cross-mode molecular network.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectra-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectra-similarity-scoring Use when you have positive and/or negative ionization mode MS/MS peak spectra (mgf, msp, mzML, mzXML, json, usi) and need predicted chemical similarity scores, e.g., to build a unified cross-mode molecular network. The task is structure annotation from a single spectrum (SIRIUS, MS-Finder or MS2Query are the appropriate annotation tools, not a pairwise similarity metric) Only negative-vs-negative mode similarity at very low scores is critical: pair sampling over ionization modes was unbalanced, so negative/negative prediction performance may be limited The spectra are of a very specific chemical class or task: the paper notes a risk that the general model is not well-suited to very specific tasks or chemical classes http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Predicts pairwise chemical similarity (Tanimoto-score proxy) between tandem mass spectra — including spectra acquired in different ionization modes — using the MS2DeepScore 2.0 Siamese neural network, enabling cross-mode molecular networking. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Predicts pairwise chemical similarity (Tanimoto-score proxy) between tandem mass spectra — including spectra acquired in different ionization modes — using the MS2DeepScore 2.0 Siamese neural network, enabling cross-mode molecular networking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is structure annotation from a single spectrum (SIRIUS, MS-Finder or MS2Query are the appropriate annotation tools, not a pairwise similarity metric) Only negative-vs-negative mode similarity at very low scores is critical: pair sampling over ionization modes was unbalanced, so negative/negative prediction performance may be limited The spectra are of a very specific chemical class or task: the paper notes a risk that the general model is not well-suited to very specific tasks or chemical classes

skills.description: Use when experimental tandem mass spectra of natural products (e.g. NRPs/PK siderophores like desferrioxamine B) must be matched against a custom in-silico fragment database to identify the compound producing each spectrum.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectral-dereplication
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectral-dereplication Use when experimental tandem mass spectra of natural products (e.g. NRPs/PK siderophores like desferrioxamine B) must be matched against a custom in-silico fragment database to identify the compound producing each spectrum. When the input is already an annotated compound assignment and no spectral comparison against a theoretical database is needed. When the target molecules are not linear, cyclic, branched, or branch-cyclic nonribosomal peptides/polyketides representable as building-block sequences in CycloBranch. When custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences cannot be created (e.g. NRPro cannot create custom databases). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Dereplicate unknown nonribosomal peptide and polyketide spectra by exporting a custom sequence/building-block database from MassSpecBlocks into CycloBranch and searching experimental tandem spectra against theoretically derived fragment lists. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00530-2
skills.summary: Dereplicate unknown nonribosomal peptide and polyketide spectra by exporting a custom sequence/building-block database from MassSpecBlocks into CycloBranch and searching experimental tandem spectra against theoretically derived fragment lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already an annotated compound assignment and no spectral comparison against a theoretical database is needed. When the target molecules are not linear, cyclic, branched, or branch-cyclic nonribosomal peptides/polyketides representable as building-block sequences in CycloBranch. When custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences cannot be created (e.g. NRPro cannot create custom databases).

skills.description: Use when multiple ESI-MS2 records of a single compound exist at different collision-induced dissociation energies and you must merge them into one reference spectrum or score searches with a weighted cosine correlation optimized for ESI-MS2 data.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-data-processing
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectrometry-data-processing Use when multiple ESI-MS2 records of a single compound exist at different collision-induced dissociation energies and you must merge them into one reference spectrum or score searches with a weighted cosine correlation optimized for ESI-MS2 data. Input is EI-MS or other single-spectrum data without multiple collision-energy measurements — there is nothing to merge across CID conditions You need to query MassBank records via the modern REST API/web app (MassBank3) rather than perform offline spectrum merging and similarity scoring The records are not in the specified MassBank record format (each file must contain its own accession ID, peaks, etc.) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Processing of ESI-MS2 records from MassBank by merging spectra of the same compound measured at multiple collision energies (e.g. 10–50 V) into one artificial merged spectrum per compound and instrument class, which improves compound identification precision by 21–23% at a similarity score of 0.6. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.1777
skills.summary: Processing of ESI-MS2 records from MassBank by merging spectra of the same compound measured at multiple collision energies (e.g. 10–50 V) into one artificial merged spectrum per compound and instrument class, which improves compound identification precision by 21–23% at a similarity score of 0.6.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is EI-MS or other single-spectrum data without multiple collision-energy measurements — there is nothing to merge across CID conditions You need to query MassBank records via the modern REST API/web app (MassBank3) rather than perform offline spectrum merging and similarity scoring The records are not in the specified MassBank record format (each file must contain its own accession ID, peaks, etc.)

skills.description: Use when pairwise alignment of tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra (m/z arrays with precursor m/z) must be scored with statistical significance (z-test p-values) for structurally related metabolites, e.g. in molecular networking.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-fragment-matching
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectrometry-fragment-matching Use when pairwise alignment of tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra (m/z arrays with precursor m/z) must be scored with statistical significance (z-test p-values) for structurally related metabolites, e.g. in molecular networking. Input spectra are not protonation/deprotonation tandem MS/MS — SIMILE is currently limited to protonation/deprotonation analysis and does not handle additional adducts. Goal is compound identification where cosine-based scoring alone is appropriate and expected — the article recommends complementing SIMILE with cosine-based scoring rather than replacing it. Only a single spectrum's internal fragment structure is needed without pairwise alignment across spectra — the z-test null is built from intra- and inter-spectral permutations across spectrum combinations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Interrelate fragmentation spectra of small molecules using SIMILE's fragment-ion similarity matrix, max-weight matching, and symmetric comparison to discover statistically significant spectral alignments robust to multiple structural differences, beyond cosine-based scoring. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-30118-9
skills.summary: Interrelate fragmentation spectra of small molecules using SIMILE's fragment-ion similarity matrix, max-weight matching, and symmetric comparison to discover statistically significant spectral alignments robust to multiple structural differences, beyond cosine-based scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not protonation/deprotonation tandem MS/MS — SIMILE is currently limited to protonation/deprotonation analysis and does not handle additional adducts. Goal is compound identification where cosine-based scoring alone is appropriate and expected — the article recommends complementing SIMILE with cosine-based scoring rather than replacing it. Only a single spectrum's internal fragment structure is needed without pairwise alignment across spectra — the z-test null is built from intra- and inter-spectral permutations across spectrum combinations.

skills.description: Use when raw tandem MS (MS2/MSn) spectra—especially low-resolution spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer—must be converted into candidate molecular structures and scored by fingerprint Tanimoto similarity against known SMILES.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-spectrum-processing
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectrometry-spectrum-processing Use when raw tandem MS (MS2/MSn) spectra—especially low-resolution spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer—must be converted into candidate molecular structures and scored by fingerprint Tanimoto similarity against known SMILES. Spectra were recorded in negative ion mode—TeFT was trained only on positive ion mode (H+) spectra, so applicability is restricted High-resolution, high-mass-accuracy spectra from large instruments—models like MassGenie or SIRIUS4 are better suited for high-quality resolution spectra Compounds outside the <500 Da / ten-element (C,H,O,N,P,S,Cl,Br,I,F) chemical constraint space http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Process low-resolution MS2 spectra from miniaturized mass spectrometers and generate de novo candidate molecular structures using the TeFT (Transformer enabled Fragment Tree) pipeline, scoring predictions against reference SMILES with MACCS/Morgan fingerprint Tanimoto similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0
skills.summary: Process low-resolution MS2 spectra from miniaturized mass spectrometers and generate de novo candidate molecular structures using the TeFT (Transformer enabled Fragment Tree) pipeline, scoring predictions against reference SMILES with MACCS/Morgan fingerprint Tanimoto similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra were recorded in negative ion mode—TeFT was trained only on positive ion mode (H+) spectra, so applicability is restricted High-resolution, high-mass-accuracy spectra from large instruments—models like MassGenie or SIRIUS4 are better suited for high-quality resolution spectra Compounds outside the <500 Da / ten-element (C,H,O,N,P,S,Cl,Br,I,F) chemical constraint space

skills.description: Use when raw shotgun proteomics MS/MS data (e.g. PRIDE PXD000561-style datasets with millions of spectra in mzML, mzXML, or MGF files) must be reduced to cluster representatives for more efficient downstream identification.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectrum-clustering
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectrum-clustering Use when raw shotgun proteomics MS/MS data (e.g. PRIDE PXD000561-style datasets with millions of spectra in mzML, mzXML, or MGF files) must be reduced to cluster representatives for more efficient downstream identification. When clustering metabolomics or top-down data with default preprocessing: the defaults (min_peaks=5, min_mz_range=250, min_mz=101, max_mz=500) are intended for bottom-up proteomics and min_peaks/min_mz_range should be reduced for metabolomics data. When exact (non-approximate) pairwise spectrum similarities are required: falcon approximates cosine distances via feature hashing and nearest neighbor indexes, trading a small accuracy cost for speed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Cluster large collections of tandem mass spectra (millions of MS/MS spectra) into groups of similar spectra using falcon, which combines feature hashing, fast nearest neighbor searching on inverted Voronoi indexes, and DBSCAN density-based clustering to avoid exhaustive pairwise comparisons. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.9153
skills.summary: Cluster large collections of tandem mass spectra (millions of MS/MS spectra) into groups of similar spectra using falcon, which combines feature hashing, fast nearest neighbor searching on inverted Voronoi indexes, and DBSCAN density-based clustering to avoid exhaustive pairwise comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When clustering metabolomics or top-down data with default preprocessing: the defaults (min_peaks=5, min_mz_range=250, min_mz=101, max_mz=500) are intended for bottom-up proteomics and min_peaks/min_mz_range should be reduced for metabolomics data. When exact (non-approximate) pairwise spectrum similarities are required: falcon approximates cosine distances via feature hashing and nearest neighbor indexes, trading a small accuracy cost for speed.

skills.description: Use when you need to describe the size of a set of LC-MS/MS acquisitions, e.g. reporting the default compareMS2 QC metric or validating that downloaded ProteomeXchange files are complete.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectrum-counting
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectrum-counting Use when you need to describe the size of a set of LC-MS/MS acquisitions, e.g. reporting the default compareMS2 QC metric or validating that downloaded ProteomeXchange files are complete. When the goal is pairwise spectral similarity or phylogenetic distance between datasets — use compareMS2's distance metric instead of simple counts.
