skills.description: Use when LC-MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzXML, mzML, or mzData) need to be identified against a database of known natural product structures, especially when exact-formula dereplication by precursor mass alone is ambiguous.
skills.name: tandem-mass-spectrum-database-search
skills.search_text: tandem-mass-spectrum-database-search Use when LC-MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzXML, mzML, or mzData) need to be identified against a database of known natural product structures, especially when exact-formula dereplication by precursor mass alone is ambiguous. The compounds of interest fall outside the metabolite classes DEREPLICATOR+ covers — the paper states 'DEREPLICATOR+ is not applicable to all the classes of compounds.' The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than dereplication against known structures. Spectra are peak-picked poorly or profile-mode, since NPDtools requires centroided spectra in an open format. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Dereplicate LC-MS/MS spectra by searching them against chemical structure databases using DEREPLICATOR+, which matches spectra to metabolite fragmentation graphs and estimates FDR via decoy matches. Extends peptidic natural product search to polyketides, terpenes, benzenoids, alkaloids, flavonoids, and other classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-018-06082-8
skills.summary: Dereplicate LC-MS/MS spectra by searching them against chemical structure databases using DEREPLICATOR+, which matches spectra to metabolite fragmentation graphs and estimates FDR via decoy matches. Extends peptidic natural product search to polyketides, terpenes, benzenoids, alkaloids, flavonoids, and other classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compounds of interest fall outside the metabolite classes DEREPLICATOR+ covers — the paper states 'DEREPLICATOR+ is not applicable to all the classes of compounds.' The goal is de novo structure elucidation rather than dereplication against known structures. Spectra are peak-picked poorly or profile-mode, since NPDtools requires centroided spectra in an open format.

skills.description: Use when comparing MS/MS formula-prediction methods on a labeled test set (e.g. NPLIB1, CASMI2022) and need rigorous metrics such as top-1 accuracy, joint formula+adduct accuracy, and per-spectrum concordance.
skills.name: tandem-ms-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-accuracy-benchmarking Use when comparing MS/MS formula-prediction methods on a labeled test set (e.g. NPLIB1, CASMI2022) and need rigorous metrics such as top-1 accuracy, joint formula+adduct accuracy, and per-spectrum concordance. When the test set is unlabeled or ground-truth formulae are unavailable — accuracy benchmarking requires per-spectrum annotations When only a single method's predictions need rescoring rather than a head-to-head comparison across competing pipelines When evaluating negative-ion-mode data — models in this paper were trained only on positive-mode spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Head-to-head benchmarking of de novo chemical formula annotation models (MIST-CF vs SIRIUS 5.6.3) on tandem MS test sets like NPLIB1, comparing top-1 formula accuracy, joint formula+adduct accuracy, and failure rates. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jcim.3c01082
skills.summary: Head-to-head benchmarking of de novo chemical formula annotation models (MIST-CF vs SIRIUS 5.6.3) on tandem MS test sets like NPLIB1, comparing top-1 formula accuracy, joint formula+adduct accuracy, and failure rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the test set is unlabeled or ground-truth formulae are unavailable — accuracy benchmarking requires per-spectrum annotations When only a single method's predictions need rescoring rather than a head-to-head comparison across competing pipelines When evaluating negative-ion-mode data — models in this paper were trained only on positive-mode spectra

skills.description: Use when a feature-level annotation table contains top candidate structures and scores from multiple MS/MS annotation tools (GNPS FBMN, Sirius 6, ISDB-LOTUS) and per-ion agreement/match indicators are needed for prioritization.
skills.name: tandem-ms-annotation-score-extraction
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-annotation-score-extraction Use when a feature-level annotation table contains top candidate structures and scores from multiple MS/MS annotation tools (GNPS FBMN, Sirius 6, ISDB-LOTUS) and per-ion agreement/match indicators are needed for prioritization. When only one annotation tool is used — pairwise Tanimoto indicators between tool annotations are undefined without at least two structural candidates When the input is already the aggregated K-ranked output table rather than raw multi-tool annotation results When candidate molecules lack SMILES/InChI structures, since Morgan fingerprints and Tanimoto similarities cannot be computed Extracts the six MS2DECIDE indicators per MS/MS feature: the closest-molecule match scores from GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS (c_g, c_s, c_i) plus the three pairwise Morgan/Tanimoto similarities between the tools' structural annotations (t_gs, t_gi, t_si), which feed the decision-theory aggregation and K-value prioritization. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Extracts the six MS2DECIDE indicators per MS/MS feature: the closest-molecule match scores from GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS (c_g, c_s, c_i) plus the three pairwise Morgan/Tanimoto similarities between the tools' structural annotations (t_gs, t_gi, t_si), which feed the decision-theory aggregation and K-value prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one annotation tool is used — pairwise Tanimoto indicators between tool annotations are undefined without at least two structural candidates When the input is already the aggregated K-ranked output table rather than raw multi-tool annotation results When candidate molecules lack SMILES/InChI structures, since Morgan fingerprints and Tanimoto similarities cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when a trained formula-identification model must be evaluated on held-out MS/MS spectra to quantify top-5 accuracy, compare against SIRIUS/BUDDY baselines, or reveal performance stratification across molecular properties.
skills.name: tandem-ms-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-benchmark-evaluation Use when a trained formula-identification model must be evaluated on held-out MS/MS spectra to quantify top-5 accuracy, compare against SIRIUS/BUDDY baselines, or reveal performance stratification across molecular properties. Spectra are chimeric (co-eluting) mixtures — FIDDLE's performance decreases as spectral mixing increases, so benchmark numbers will not be comparable The goal is de novo structural elucidation rather than formula identification benchmarking — top-5 formula ranking alone does not resolve structures Compounds contain rare elements outside the retained atom set (C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K) or exceed 1500 m/z — outside the benchmark's explainable space http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmark-evaluates deep learning molecular formula identification (FIDDLE) on held-out tandem MS/MS test spectra (NIST23), reporting top-1/top-5 accuracy on Q-TOF and Orbitrap instruments and stratifying performance by molecular properties such as LogP polarity, precursor mass, and ClassyFire superclass. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Benchmark-evaluates deep learning molecular formula identification (FIDDLE) on held-out tandem MS/MS test spectra (NIST23), reporting top-1/top-5 accuracy on Q-TOF and Orbitrap instruments and stratifying performance by molecular properties such as LogP polarity, precursor mass, and ClassyFire superclass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are chimeric (co-eluting) mixtures — FIDDLE's performance decreases as spectral mixing increases, so benchmark numbers will not be comparable The goal is de novo structural elucidation rather than formula identification benchmarking — top-5 formula ranking alone does not resolve structures Compounds contain rare elements outside the retained atom set (C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K) or exceed 1500 m/z — outside the benchmark's explainable space

skills.description: Use when assigning ranks to candidate structures for an HR-MS/MS peak with no spectral-library match, especially when candidate lists come from PubChem/ChemSpider and reference or retention-time information is available.
skills.name: tandem-ms-candidate-ranking
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-candidate-ranking Use when assigning ranks to candidate structures for an HR-MS/MS peak with no spectral-library match, especially when candidate lists come from PubChem/ChemSpider and reference or retention-time information is available. The mass spectrum is dominated by one or only a few fragments (e.g. a single water loss) explainable by most candidates, so it lacks information to distinguish candidates. A confirmed reference standard or direct spectral-library match already establishes the identity, making re-ranking unnecessary. The analysis has no retention-time or reference information and relies only on fragmentation of very large databases, where candidate ranking becomes increasingly hard (PubChem has doubled since 2009). http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Rank candidate molecular structures for tandem MS (HR-MS/MS) spectra by combining in silico bond-dissociation fragment explanation scores with reference/patent counts and retention-time (log P) scoring, as implemented in MetFrag2.2 and benchmarked on the Hill 102-compound and 473-spectrum Eawag Orbitrap XL datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9
skills.summary: Rank candidate molecular structures for tandem MS (HR-MS/MS) spectra by combining in silico bond-dissociation fragment explanation scores with reference/patent counts and retention-time (log P) scoring, as implemented in MetFrag2.2 and benchmarked on the Hill 102-compound and 473-spectrum Eawag Orbitrap XL datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mass spectrum is dominated by one or only a few fragments (e.g. a single water loss) explainable by most candidates, so it lacks information to distinguish candidates. A confirmed reference standard or direct spectral-library match already establishes the identity, making re-ranking unnecessary. The analysis has no retention-time or reference information and relies only on fragmentation of very large databases, where candidate ranking becomes increasingly hard (PubChem has doubled since 2009).

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a tandem-MS structure-annotation confidence score against known ground truth — reference spectra at 10/20/40 eV, merged spectra, and no/medium/high noise — to quantify correct hits versus annotation rate (hop plots) and FDR at a score threshold.
skills.name: tandem-ms-confidence-score-evaluation
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-confidence-score-evaluation Use when benchmarking a tandem-MS structure-annotation confidence score against known ground truth — reference spectra at 10/20/40 eV, merged spectra, and no/medium/high noise — to quantify correct hits versus annotation rate (hop plots) and FDR at a score threshold. Annotating biological samples without ground-truth structures — hop-plot correct-hit counting requires reference measurements, since 'we do not know the correct answers for biological datasets'. The goal is spectral-library de-replication rather than benchmarking a confidence score against known structures. Compounds lack all three collision energies or yield a spectrum with at most one peak at some collision energy/noise level — the protocol discards such compounds from all libraries. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Structure-disjoint evaluation of the COSMIC confidence score for tandem-MS structure annotation: ten-fold cross-validation on Orbitrap reference spectra (MassBank/GNPS/NIST 2017, n = 3,721) and an independent Agilent PCDL QTOF set (n = 3,013), rendered as hop plots of correct hits versus annotation rate across 10/20/40-eV and merged spectra under no/medium/high noise. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-021-01045-9
skills.summary: Structure-disjoint evaluation of the COSMIC confidence score for tandem-MS structure annotation: ten-fold cross-validation on Orbitrap reference spectra (MassBank/GNPS/NIST 2017, n = 3,721) and an independent Agilent PCDL QTOF set (n = 3,013), rendered as hop plots of correct hits versus annotation rate across 10/20/40-eV and merged spectra under no/medium/high noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotating biological samples without ground-truth structures — hop-plot correct-hit counting requires reference measurements, since 'we do not know the correct answers for biological datasets'. The goal is spectral-library de-replication rather than benchmarking a confidence score against known structures. Compounds lack all three collision energies or yield a spectrum with at most one peak at some collision energy/noise level — the protocol discards such compounds from all libraries.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw untargeted LC-MS2 .mzML files (e.g. the bryophytes MTBLS709 dataset) that must be preprocessed and dereplicated against spectral databases before SIRIUS/MAW-Py annotation.
skills.name: tandem-ms-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-data-preprocessing Use when starting from raw untargeted LC-MS2 .mzML files (e.g. the bryophytes MTBLS709 dataset) that must be preprocessed and dereplicated against spectral databases before SIRIUS/MAW-Py annotation. Input is already a preprocessed feature table or MS1DATA_SiriusP.tsv output from a previous MAW-R run rather than raw .mzML files Data is MS1-only or not in .mzML format (the workflow takes MS2 .mzML files as input in R) http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 The first MAW stage: pre-process untargeted tandem MS (MS2) .mzML input files in R before spectral and compound database dereplication, converting raw instrument output into per-feature data suitable for SIRIUS-based annotation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00695-y
skills.summary: The first MAW stage: pre-process untargeted tandem MS (MS2) .mzML input files in R before spectral and compound database dereplication, converting raw instrument output into per-feature data suitable for SIRIUS-based annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed feature table or MS1DATA_SiriusP.tsv output from a previous MAW-R run rather than raw .mzML files Data is MS1-only or not in .mzML format (the workflow takes MS2 .mzML files as input in R)

skills.description: Use when you have centroided tandem MS/MS spectra in an open format (e.g. after OpenMS file conversion and centroiding) and need peptide/protein identifications via database searching before feature detection, retention-time alignment, protein inference, and FDR control.
skills.name: tandem-ms-database-searching
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-database-searching Use when you have centroided tandem MS/MS spectra in an open format (e.g. after OpenMS file conversion and centroiding) and need peptide/protein identifications via database searching before feature detection, retention-time alignment, protein inference, and FDR control. Spectra are raw, unconverted, and still in vendor profile mode — run OpenMS file conversion and centroiding first. The analysis goal is de novo identification without a reference protein database; OpenMS also offers de novo algorithms, which this database-search skill does not cover. The question is quantification (label-free, SILAC, iTRAQ, TMT, SRM, SWATH) rather than peptide identification — database searching alone does not answer that. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Search centroided tandem mass spectra against a protein sequence database using OpenMS database-searching tooling to identify peptides and proteins, as one step of the OpenMS proteogenomics workflow described by the article. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/nmeth.3959
skills.summary: Search centroided tandem mass spectra against a protein sequence database using OpenMS database-searching tooling to identify peptides and proteins, as one step of the OpenMS proteogenomics workflow described by the article.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are raw, unconverted, and still in vendor profile mode — run OpenMS file conversion and centroiding first. The analysis goal is de novo identification without a reference protein database; OpenMS also offers de novo algorithms, which this database-search skill does not cover. The question is quantification (label-free, SILAC, iTRAQ, TMT, SRM, SWATH) rather than peptide identification — database searching alone does not answer that.

skills.description: Use when a downstream annotation/prioritization task needs the P. mutica MIA alkaloid extract MS/MS data referenced by MassIVE accession MSV95596, or when reproducing the article's 754-feature k-ranking.
skills.name: tandem-ms-dataset-acquisition-from-massive
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-dataset-acquisition-from-massive Use when a downstream annotation/prioritization task needs the P. mutica MIA alkaloid extract MS/MS data referenced by MassIVE accession MSV95596, or when reproducing the article's 754-feature k-ranking. The tandem MS data are already available locally as MGF plus quantitative .csv — proceed directly to annotation and K_estimation instead of re-downloading. The analysis targets a different organism/extract or a synthetic benchmark dataset rather than the P. mutica real-case dataset under accession MSV95596. Only raw vendor instrument files without the MZmine FBMN export (.csv quantitative table) are needed for a workflow outside the MS2DECIDE input format. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retrieves the real-case Pleiocarpa mutica LC-MS/MS alkaloid extract tandem mass spectrometry dataset from the MassIVE repository (accession MSV95596) so that the MS2DECIDE k pipeline (GNPS + Sirius + ISDB-LOTUS) can be applied to its 754 ion features. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Retrieves the real-case Pleiocarpa mutica LC-MS/MS alkaloid extract tandem mass spectrometry dataset from the MassIVE repository (accession MSV95596) so that the MS2DECIDE k pipeline (GNPS + Sirius + ISDB-LOTUS) can be applied to its 754 ion features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tandem MS data are already available locally as MGF plus quantitative .csv — proceed directly to annotation and K_estimation instead of re-downloading. The analysis targets a different organism/extract or a synthetic benchmark dataset rather than the P. mutica real-case dataset under accession MSV95596. Only raw vendor instrument files without the MZmine FBMN export (.csv quantitative table) are needed for a workflow outside the MS2DECIDE input format.

skills.description: Use when you have raw LC-MS/MS dataset files (e.g. MGF with tens of thousands of tandem spectra) and need dataset-level similarity, species-level phylogenetic reconstruction, or QC/batch-effect detection before any database search.
skills.name: tandem-ms-dataset-pairwise-comparison
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-dataset-pairwise-comparison Use when you have raw LC-MS/MS dataset files (e.g. MGF with tens of thousands of tandem spectra) and need dataset-level similarity, species-level phylogenetic reconstruction, or QC/batch-effect detection before any database search. When the goal is peptide or protein identification — compareMS2 compares sets of tandem mass spectra to each other rather than to predicted spectra of specific peptides as when identifying proteins from tandem mass spectra When spectra-to-peptide cluster structure is needed — spectral clustering tends to produce large globs of spectra rather than a distinct cluster for each peptide, making results sensitive to the precise definition of when two spectra are considered identical When datasets have no overlapping spectral content at all — similarity tends to 0 (distance +∞) as set size grows, giving no discriminative information http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Compute pairwise global-similarity distances between tandem MS/MS (MGF) datasets directly from spectra, assemble them into a symmetric distance matrix, and build a UPGMA phylogenetic tree — the core compareMS2 2.0 workflow for species identification, QC, and molecular phylogenetics. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00457
skills.summary: Compute pairwise global-similarity distances between tandem MS/MS (MGF) datasets directly from spectra, assemble them into a symmetric distance matrix, and build a UPGMA phylogenetic tree — the core compareMS2 2.0 workflow for species identification, QC, and molecular phylogenetics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is peptide or protein identification — compareMS2 compares sets of tandem mass spectra to each other rather than to predicted spectra of specific peptides as when identifying proteins from tandem mass spectra When spectra-to-peptide cluster structure is needed — spectral clustering tends to produce large globs of spectra rather than a distinct cluster for each peptide, making results sensitive to the precise definition of when two spectra are considered identical When datasets have no overlapping spectral content at all — similarity tends to 0 (distance +∞) as set size grows, giving no discriminative information

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending benchmark comparisons of tandem MS annotation tools (CycloBranch, NRPro, Dereplicator, Dereplicator+) on matched CID/HCD spectrum sets, where per-condition accuracy deltas and exact recomputation checks are needed.
skills.name: tandem-ms-evaluation-set-bookkeeping
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-evaluation-set-bookkeeping Use when reproducing or extending benchmark comparisons of tandem MS annotation tools (CycloBranch, NRPro, Dereplicator, Dereplicator+) on matched CID/HCD spectrum sets, where per-condition accuracy deltas and exact recomputation checks are needed. The goal is single-spectrum dereplication or de novo NRP analysis rather than cross-tool benchmark bookkeeping on an evaluation set Input spectra have no matched CID/HCD pair structure or no per-tool accuracy values to reconcile across conditions Custom building block databases must be created in NRPro — the article notes NRPro users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A bookkeeping skill for curating and validating evaluation sets of high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of NRPs and PK siderophores, tracking annotation/comparison accuracy per tool per fragmentation condition (CID vs HCD), and assembling reproducible comparison tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00530-2
skills.summary: A bookkeeping skill for curating and validating evaluation sets of high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of NRPs and PK siderophores, tracking annotation/comparison accuracy per tool per fragmentation condition (CID vs HCD), and assembling reproducible comparison tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-spectrum dereplication or de novo NRP analysis rather than cross-tool benchmark bookkeeping on an evaluation set Input spectra have no matched CID/HCD pair structure or no per-tool accuracy values to reconcile across conditions Custom building block databases must be created in NRPro — the article notes NRPro users cannot create custom databases of building blocks and NRP sequences

skills.description: Use when you have unfiltered high-resolution MS/MS spectra (plus MS1 isotope pattern) of a small molecule and need its molecular formula and candidate structure without a reference mass spectral database.
skills.name: tandem-ms-formula-identification
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-formula-identification Use when you have unfiltered high-resolution MS/MS spectra (plus MS1 isotope pattern) of a small molecule and need its molecular formula and candidate structure without a reference mass spectral database. A reference mass spectral database already gives a confident library match — SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID is designed for cases 'beyond elemental composition without requiring compound structures or a mass spectral database'. Input is a complex LC-MS/MS feature table needing peak picking/alignment first; SIRIUS expects preprocessed peak lists per compound, not raw vendor files of an entire run. The query is a structure with no chance of being structure-disjoint from CSI:FingerID's training data, so performance numbers will not be comparable to published benchmarks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 SIRIUS-based workflow that identifies the molecular formula of an unknown compound from high-resolution LC-MS/MS data by combining isotope pattern analysis of the parent peak with fragmentation tree computation, then hands ranked candidates to CSI:FingerID for structure search. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8
skills.summary: SIRIUS-based workflow that identifies the molecular formula of an unknown compound from high-resolution LC-MS/MS data by combining isotope pattern analysis of the parent peak with fragmentation tree computation, then hands ranked candidates to CSI:FingerID for structure search.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference mass spectral database already gives a confident library match — SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID is designed for cases 'beyond elemental composition without requiring compound structures or a mass spectral database'. Input is a complex LC-MS/MS feature table needing peak picking/alignment first; SIRIUS expects preprocessed peak lists per compound, not raw vendor files of an entire run. The query is a structure with no chance of being structure-disjoint from CSI:FingerID's training data, so performance numbers will not be comparable to published benchmarks.

skills.description: Use when per-sample MGF MS2 spectra have been clustered and cleaned into consensus spectra and structural annotations must be assigned by spectral-library matching, ranked by MQscore and m/z error.
skills.name: tandem-ms-fragment-ion-matching
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-fragment-ion-matching Use when per-sample MGF MS2 spectra have been clustered and cleaned into consensus spectra and structural annotations must be assigned by spectral-library matching, ranked by MQscore and m/z error. Input is raw LC–MS/MS vendor data that has not yet been preprocessed — the pre_process step must first detect MS1 features and extract MS2 spectra into MGF files The spectra are MS1-only features with no MS2 fragmentation, so there are no fragment ions to match against a spectral library The goal is molecular-network visualization alone (SSMN in Cytoscape) rather than structural annotation of consensus spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotates clean consensus MS2 spectra by matching their fragment ions against spectral libraries (In Silico MS2 DataBase / GNPS) using the Tremolo tool within the NP3 MS Workflow, ranking candidates by MQscore and precursor m/z error in ppm. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05829
skills.summary: Annotates clean consensus MS2 spectra by matching their fragment ions against spectral libraries (In Silico MS2 DataBase / GNPS) using the Tremolo tool within the NP3 MS Workflow, ranking candidates by MQscore and precursor m/z error in ppm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC–MS/MS vendor data that has not yet been preprocessed — the pre_process step must first detect MS1 features and extract MS2 spectra into MGF files The spectra are MS1-only features with no MS2 fragmentation, so there are no fragment ions to match against a spectral library The goal is molecular-network visualization alone (SSMN in Cytoscape) rather than structural annotation of consensus spectra

skills.description: Use when identifying isomeric metabolites in untargeted LC-MS/MS data acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (NCE 1–100% or stepped 20/40/60%), where single-CE cross-sectional spectral similarity misranks isomers with similar predominant fragments.
skills.name: tandem-ms-fragment-longitudinal-profiling
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-fragment-longitudinal-profiling Use when identifying isomeric metabolites in untargeted LC-MS/MS data acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (NCE 1–100% or stepped 20/40/60%), where single-CE cross-sectional spectral similarity misranks isomers with similar predominant fragments. MS/MS spectra were acquired at only a single collision energy, so no longitudinal fragment profile (fragment intensity trajectory across CEs) can be constructed The goal is raw peak detection or feature quantification rather than isomer-level metabolite identification — this skill does not replace MS1 full-scan feature processing No reference library with multi-CE spectra of candidate isomers is available (the CQMD/CQMU databases are in-house and no public accession is stated) A metabolite-identification skill that matches experimental MS/MS spectra to a reference library using longitudinal fragment profiles (LFPs) — each fragment's relative-intensity trajectory across 13 collision energies (e.g., NCE 1–100% or stepped 20/40/60%) — scored with an optimized Jaccard similarity and calibrated by ROC-derived I/N-ratio cutoffs, improving isomer accuracy by 8.7–25.9% over cross-sectional profiling. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01414
skills.summary: A metabolite-identification skill that matches experimental MS/MS spectra to a reference library using longitudinal fragment profiles (LFPs) — each fragment's relative-intensity trajectory across 13 collision energies (e.g., NCE 1–100% or stepped 20/40/60%) — scored with an optimized Jaccard similarity and calibrated by ROC-derived I/N-ratio cutoffs, improving isomer accuracy by 8.7–25.9% over cross-sectional profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MS/MS spectra were acquired at only a single collision energy, so no longitudinal fragment profile (fragment intensity trajectory across CEs) can be constructed The goal is raw peak detection or feature quantification rather than isomer-level metabolite identification — this skill does not replace MS1 full-scan feature processing No reference library with multi-CE spectra of candidate isomers is available (the CQMD/CQMU databases are in-house and no public accession is stated)

skills.description: Use when you have consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g. from MZmine3 feature extraction) with a precursor mass and need to rank molecular candidates retrieved from FoodDB, HMDB, MassSpecGym, NIST23, or GNPS libraries to annotate metabolites.
skills.name: tandem-ms-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: tandem-ms-metabolite-annotation Use when you have consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g. from MZmine3 feature extraction) with a precursor mass and need to rank molecular candidates retrieved from FoodDB, HMDB, MassSpecGym, NIST23, or GNPS libraries to annotate metabolites. When spectra lack precursor mass information, since candidate retrieval depends on a 0.01 Da mass tolerance. When the analysis goal is de novo structure generation or spectrum simulation rather than candidate ranking — MassSpecGym defines these as separate challenges. When reference library coverage is sufficient for direct spectral matching, since ML-based ranking is motivated by limited library coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Annotate MS/MS spectra by ranking molecular candidates with MVP, a multiview contrastive model that jointly aligns molecular graphs, fingerprints, spectra, and consensus spectra in a shared embedding space. The skill covers the full inference pipeline from data preprocessing through pretrained-model scoring to high-confidence annotation filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.11.12.688047
skills.summary: Annotate MS/MS spectra by ranking molecular candidates with MVP, a multiview contrastive model that jointly aligns molecular graphs, fingerprints, spectra, and consensus spectra in a shared embedding space. The skill covers the full inference pipeline from data preprocessing through pretrained-model scoring to high-confidence annotation filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When spectra lack precursor mass information, since candidate retrieval depends on a 0.01 Da mass tolerance. When the analysis goal is de novo structure generation or spectrum simulation rather than candidate ranking — MassSpecGym defines these as separate challenges. When reference library coverage is sufficient for direct spectral matching, since ML-based ranking is motivated by limited library coverage.

When evaluating de novo structure generation or spectrum-prediction accuracy itself — this skill benchmarks identification-by-retrieval against a candidate pool, not peak-level spectral prediction When molecular formulae for candidates or query spectra are unavailable — the decoy construction requires exact same-formula isomer filtering When only the main branch of ms-pred is available and NPLIB1 is the target dataset — NPLIB1 support has been retired from the main branch and requires the iceberg_1.0 branch http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assembles fair retrieval candidate pools for retrospective metabolite identification by combining each test spectrum's true structure with up to 49 top-Tanimoto structural-isomer decoys sharing the same molecular formula (drawn from PubChem), then ranks candidates by predicted-vs-experimental spectral similarity to compute top-k hit rates. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04654
skills.summary: Assembles fair retrieval candidate pools for retrospective metabolite identification by combining each test spectrum's true structure with up to 49 top-Tanimoto structural-isomer decoys sharing the same molecular formula (drawn from PubChem), then ranks candidates by predicted-vs-experimental spectral similarity to compute top-k hit rates.

skills.description: Use when comparing spectral similarity measures (e.g., DreaMS embedding cosine, MS2DeepScore, spectral entropy) against molecular structural similarity on tandem MS/MS spectra, or when building a library-retrieval benchmark with precursor m/z constraints.
skills.name: tanimoto-fingerprint-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: tanimoto-fingerprint-correlation-analysis Use when comparing spectral similarity measures (e.g., DreaMS embedding cosine, MS2DeepScore, spectral entropy) against molecular structural similarity on tandem MS/MS spectra, or when building a library-retrieval benchmark with precursor m/z constraints. When the goal is de novo structure annotation or fingerprint prediction from a single spectrum rather than similarity/benchmarking — use DreaMS fine-tuned prediction, MIST, or SIRIUS instead. When spectra are in negative ionization mode or from multiply charged precursors — DreaMS training did not incorporate such data. When the task requires MS1 isotopic patterns or adduct distributions — this method focuses solely on tandem mass spectra. Benchmarks spectral similarity measures (embeddings, supervised models, and 44 standard measures) by correlating them with Tanimoto similarity of molecular fingerprints and by AUROC for same-molecule/analog retrieval, reproducing the DreaMS Fig. 4a–c comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Benchmarks spectral similarity measures (embeddings, supervised models, and 44 standard measures) by correlating them with Tanimoto similarity of molecular fingerprints and by AUROC for same-molecule/analog retrieval, reproducing the DreaMS Fig. 4a–c comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo structure annotation or fingerprint prediction from a single spectrum rather than similarity/benchmarking — use DreaMS fine-tuned prediction, MIST, or SIRIUS instead. When spectra are in negative ionization mode or from multiply charged precursors — DreaMS training did not incorporate such data. When the task requires MS1 isotopic patterns or adduct distributions — this method focuses solely on tandem mass spectra.

skills.description: Use when evaluating de novo or database-search structure predictions by structural similarity — e.g., computing Tanimoto similarity of top incorrect candidates to the true structure in MS2-based structure elucidation benchmarks.
skills.name: tanimoto-fingerprint-similarity-evaluation
skills.search_text: tanimoto-fingerprint-similarity-evaluation Use when evaluating de novo or database-search structure predictions by structural similarity — e.g., computing Tanimoto similarity of top incorrect candidates to the true structure in MS2-based structure elucidation benchmarks. Isomeric compounds whose fragmentation is indistinguishable — a high Tanimoto similarity cannot resolve them and structural elucidation from the MS2 data is not possible The goal is exact identification accuracy (top-1/overall retrieval rates) rather than characterizing near-miss chemical similarity of incorrect candidates Fingerprints come from a different prediction system than the one the model was trained on (e.g., the experimental Morgan 4096-bit 'mist' branch work, which was not completed) http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Quantifies how chemically close predicted or de novo–generated structures are to a reference by computing Tanimoto similarity between their molecular fingerprints. In MSNovelist this characterizes the best incorrect de novo candidates against training-set and database-search baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01486-3
skills.summary: Quantifies how chemically close predicted or de novo–generated structures are to a reference by computing Tanimoto similarity between their molecular fingerprints. In MSNovelist this characterizes the best incorrect de novo candidates against training-set and database-search baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Isomeric compounds whose fragmentation is indistinguishable — a high Tanimoto similarity cannot resolve them and structural elucidation from the MS2 data is not possible The goal is exact identification accuracy (top-1/overall retrieval rates) rather than characterizing near-miss chemical similarity of incorrect candidates Fingerprints come from a different prediction system than the one the model was trained on (e.g., the experimental Morgan 4096-bit 'mist' branch work, which was not completed)

skills.summary: Evaluate de novo molecule generation candidates against ground-truth structures using top-k accuracy, top-k maximum Tanimoto similarity (RDKit Morgan fingerprints), and top-k minimum MCES distance, as defined for MassSpecGym-style de novo generation benchmarks such as NPLIB1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When evaluating fingerprint prediction itself (e.g., MIST encoder fingerprint accuracy) rather than generated molecular structures When candidates have not been filtered for validity/connectivity — scoring invalid structures against the MassSpecGym metrics is undefined and will distort rankings When the task is spectrum-to-fingerprint pretraining evaluation on DSSTox/HMDB/COCONUT/MOSES pairs rather than de novo generation benchmarking

skills.description: Use when a task requires quantifying structural relatedness between small molecules (e.g., ECFP fingerprint pairs) to group validation-set molecules by whether they have a training-set counterpart above a Tanimoto threshold such as 90% or 95%.
skills.name: tanimoto-molecular-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: tanimoto-molecular-similarity-computation Use when a task requires quantifying structural relatedness between small molecules (e.g., ECFP fingerprint pairs) to group validation-set molecules by whether they have a training-set counterpart above a Tanimoto threshold such as 90% or 95%. When the task concerns the DLM architecture or training itself (Keras layers, L2 regularization 0.0001, adam lr 0.01) rather than similarity-based grouping of molecules. When molecules lack computable ECFP fingerprints or the dataset is not the METLIN SMRT/METLIN library RT dataset, since the thresholds reported (e.g., n=5607 at 90%) are specific to that dataset split. http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Computes Tanimoto similarity on ECFP fingerprints between validation and training molecules from the METLIN SMRT dataset to stratify molecules by structural similarity at 95/90/80/70/50% thresholds, enabling k-NN baselines and error-stratified significance testing for RT prediction. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Computes Tanimoto similarity on ECFP fingerprints between validation and training molecules from the METLIN SMRT dataset to stratify molecules by structural similarity at 95/90/80/70/50% thresholds, enabling k-NN baselines and error-stratified significance testing for RT prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task concerns the DLM architecture or training itself (Keras layers, L2 regularization 0.0001, adam lr 0.01) rather than similarity-based grouping of molecules. When molecules lack computable ECFP fingerprints or the dataset is not the METLIN SMRT/METLIN library RT dataset, since the thresholds reported (e.g., n=5607 at 90%) are specific to that dataset split.

skills.description: Decision support for evaluating whether generated SMILES resemble known metabolites: use when a generative chemical model's samples must be judged for metabolite-likeness against matched PubChem controls.
skills.name: tanimoto-nearest-neighbor-similarity-vs-pubchem-controls
skills.search_text: tanimoto-nearest-neighbor-similarity-vs-pubchem-controls Decision support for evaluating whether generated SMILES resemble known metabolites: use when a generative chemical model's samples must be judged for metabolite-likeness against matched PubChem controls. When the goal is to assess novelty rather than metabolite-likeness — nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity vs PubChem controls measures proximity to the known metabolome, not how new the generated structures are. When generated molecules must be compared against arbitrary synthetic compounds rather than formula-matched PubChem controls — an unformula-matched control set would confound structural proximity with mass/formula differences. When the language model was trained on non-human metabolites (e.g. plant or bacterial metabolism) — the article notes its model was trained/evaluated only on human metabolites, so the metabolite-likeness reference set may not transfer. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 Quantifies how structurally close a language model's generated molecules are to the known metabolome by comparing each generated molecule's nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity (RDKit fingerprints) against formula-matched PubChem control molecules, rather than against an unstructured chemical universe. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Quantifies how structurally close a language model's generated molecules are to the known metabolome by comparing each generated molecule's nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity (RDKit fingerprints) against formula-matched PubChem control molecules, rather than against an unstructured chemical universe.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to assess novelty rather than metabolite-likeness — nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity vs PubChem controls measures proximity to the known metabolome, not how new the generated structures are. When generated molecules must be compared against arbitrary synthetic compounds rather than formula-matched PubChem controls — an unformula-matched control set would confound structural proximity with mass/formula differences. When the language model was trained on non-human metabolites (e.g. plant or bacterial metabolism) — the article notes its model was trained/evaluated only on human metabolites, so the metabolite-likeness reference set may not transfer.

skills.description: Use when a trained MS2DeepScore (or similar Siamese spectral similarity) model must be validated for Tanimoto prediction accuracy on held-out spectra from compounds absent from training, and you need an RMSE plus per-similarity-bin error profile.
skills.name: tanimoto-score-prediction-rmse-evaluation
skills.search_text: tanimoto-score-prediction-rmse-evaluation Use when a trained MS2DeepScore (or similar Siamese spectral similarity) model must be validated for Tanimoto prediction accuracy on held-out spectra from compounds absent from training, and you need an RMSE plus per-similarity-bin error profile. The goal is exact compound identification — MS2DeepScore cannot reliably discriminate high Tanimoto scores (0.8–0.9) from a near-complete chemical match The query spectra are strongly outside the training library's biased compound classes or instrumentation types, where prediction error is unquantified You already have molecular fingerprints/structures and only need a classical chemical similarity — compute Tanimoto directly with RDKit instead of predicting it from spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Benchmark a trained MS2DeepScore Siamese model by computing RMSE between predicted and true Tanimoto scores on a molecule-disjoint held-out test set (3601 GNPS-derived spectra of 500 unseen compounds), expecting overall RMSE ~0.15 (range 0.13–0.2) with per-bin error breakdown. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00558-4
skills.summary: Benchmark a trained MS2DeepScore Siamese model by computing RMSE between predicted and true Tanimoto scores on a molecule-disjoint held-out test set (3601 GNPS-derived spectra of 500 unseen compounds), expecting overall RMSE ~0.15 (range 0.13–0.2) with per-bin error breakdown.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exact compound identification — MS2DeepScore cannot reliably discriminate high Tanimoto scores (0.8–0.9) from a near-complete chemical match The query spectra are strongly outside the training library's biased compound classes or instrumentation types, where prediction error is unquantified You already have molecular fingerprints/structures and only need a classical chemical similarity — compute Tanimoto directly with RDKit instead of predicting it from spectra

skills.description: Use when comparing prediction accuracy of similarity models across Tanimoto bins — e.g. checking whether a dual-ionization-mode model matches single-mode baselines within each mode, or locating which Tanimoto bin (low vs 0.9–1.0) drives performance differences.
skills.name: tanimoto-similarity-bin-comparison
skills.search_text: tanimoto-similarity-bin-comparison Use when comparing prediction accuracy of similarity models across Tanimoto bins — e.g. checking whether a dual-ionization-mode model matches single-mode baselines within each mode, or locating which Tanimoto bin (low vs 0.9–1.0) drives performance differences. Spectra lack annotated structures, so no ground-truth Tanimoto scores exist to bin predictions against The goal is cross-ionization-mode prediction quality rather than within-mode baseline comparison The custom dataset is too small for training from scratch (<~100,000 spectra) — fine-tune the pre-trained model instead of running single- vs dual-mode training comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A benchmarking pattern that evaluates spectral-similarity models per Tanimoto similarity bin rather than only on aggregate loss, used here to compare single-ionization-mode (positive-only, negative-only) Siamese models against the dual-mode MS2DeepScore 2.0 model with identical hyperparameters. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: A benchmarking pattern that evaluates spectral-similarity models per Tanimoto similarity bin rather than only on aggregate loss, used here to compare single-ionization-mode (positive-only, negative-only) Siamese models against the dual-mode MS2DeepScore 2.0 model with identical hyperparameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra lack annotated structures, so no ground-truth Tanimoto scores exist to bin predictions against The goal is cross-ionization-mode prediction quality rather than within-mode baseline comparison The custom dataset is too small for training from scratch (<~100,000 spectra) — fine-tune the pre-trained model instead of running single- vs dual-mode training comparisons

skills.description: Use when the same MS/MS feature has structural annotations from multiple tools (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) and you need pairwise chemical-similarity concordance indicators to feed MS2DECIDE aggregation.
skills.name: tanimoto-similarity-calculation
skills.search_text: tanimoto-similarity-calculation Use when the same MS/MS feature has structural annotations from multiple tools (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) and you need pairwise chemical-similarity concordance indicators to feed MS2DECIDE aggregation. Only one tool produced a structural annotation for a feature — no pairwise Tanimoto can be computed (defaults, not real similarities, would be reported) You need spectral similarity (cosine/greedy scores) rather than structural similarity between candidate molecules Annotations lack SMILES/InChI structures (e.g., empty GNPS entries), so Morgan fingerprints cannot be generated Computes the three pairwise Tanimoto similarity indicators (t_g,s, t_g,i, t_s,i) between the top structural annotations returned by GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS for each MS/MS feature, using Morgan fingerprints. These structural-concordance indicators are core inputs to the MS2DECIDE decision-theory aggregation. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/cmtd.202400088
skills.summary: Computes the three pairwise Tanimoto similarity indicators (t_g,s, t_g,i, t_s,i) between the top structural annotations returned by GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS for each MS/MS feature, using Morgan fingerprints. These structural-concordance indicators are core inputs to the MS2DECIDE decision-theory aggregation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one tool produced a structural annotation for a feature — no pairwise Tanimoto can be computed (defaults, not real similarities, would be reported) You need spectral similarity (cosine/greedy scores) rather than structural similarity between candidate molecules Annotations lack SMILES/InChI structures (e.g., empty GNPS entries), so Morgan fingerprints cannot be generated

skills.description: Use when assembling a large pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule or spectrum–molecule pairs where unlabeled sources (e.g. PubChem) could structurally overlap held-out test molecules of MassSpecGym or NPLIB1, inflating benchmark scores via memorization.
skills.name: tanimoto-similarity-deduplication-across-benchmarks
skills.search_text: tanimoto-similarity-deduplication-across-benchmarks Use when assembling a large pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule or spectrum–molecule pairs where unlabeled sources (e.g. PubChem) could structurally overlap held-out test molecules of MassSpecGym or NPLIB1, inflating benchmark scores via memorization. skills.description: Use when designing or validating a targeted lipidomics assay where you must decide how many fragment transitions per lipid (plus which polarity modes) suffice for unambiguous identification against a known background lipidome, and when reproducing a target-decoy accuracy figure from a PRM/MRM.
skills.name: target-decoy-accuracy-estimation
skills.search_text: target-decoy-accuracy-estimation Use when designing or validating a targeted lipidomics assay where you must decide how many fragment transitions per lipid (plus which polarity modes) suffice for unambiguous identification against a known background lipidome, and when reproducing a target-decoy accuracy figure from a PRM/MRM. LipidCreator provides no dedicated scoring algorithm to determine false discovery rates and intentionally does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids or peak area integration, so do not use this skill as an FDR scoring or peak-picking substitute. The background lipidome is unknown or the study system has no species list (e.g. uncharacterized bacterial/archaeal lipidomes where standards are lacking), since unambiguous-match probability cannot be computed without a background matrix. The assay involves stereoisomer resolution — the article notes no large-scale methods exist to cope with stereoisomers due to the lack of isotope-coded standards. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Estimates how many MS/2 fragments (and polarity modes) are needed to unambiguously identify lipid species by computing target-decoy random-match probabilities over a background lipidome (yeast), and compares those probabilities against the reported LC/ESI-PRM target-decoy identification accuracy (e.g. 98% with three fragments). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-020-15960-z
skills.summary: Estimates how many MS/2 fragments (and polarity modes) are needed to unambiguously identify lipid species by computing target-decoy random-match probabilities over a background lipidome (yeast), and compares those probabilities against the reported LC/ESI-PRM target-decoy identification accuracy (e.g. 98% with three fragments).
skills.when_to_use_negative: LipidCreator provides no dedicated scoring algorithm to determine false discovery rates and intentionally does not address coeluting/isobaric lipids or peak area integration, so do not use this skill as an FDR scoring or peak-picking substitute. The background lipidome is unknown or the study system has no species list (e.g. uncharacterized bacterial/archaeal lipidomes where standards are lacking), since unambiguous-match probability cannot be computed without a background matrix. The assay involves stereoisomer resolution — the article notes no large-scale methods exist to cope with stereoisomers due to the lack of isotope-coded standards.

skills.description: Use when assigning FDR-controlled confidence values to metabolite ion annotations from METASPACE-ML prediction scores, requiring a single weighted target-decoy ranking and Laplace-smoothed per-ion FDR output.
skills.name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: target-decoy-fdr-estimation Use when assigning FDR-controlled confidence values to metabolite ion annotations from METASPACE-ML prediction scores, requiring a single weighted target-decoy ranking and Laplace-smoothed per-ion FDR output. The scoring model has not been trained and raw METASPACE-ML prediction scores for targets and SD-sampled decoys are not yet available — this skill only post-processes existing scores. The annotation task uses the rule-based Metabolite Signal Matching (MSM) scoring path rather than METASPACE-ML prediction scores. Data types such as QTOF-based or single-cell metabolomics datasets that are underrepresented in the model, where FDR estimates may not be statistically reliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs the METASPACE-ML target-decoy False Discovery Rate estimation, which ranks target and SD-sampled decoy ions by machine-learning prediction score and converts the cumulative decoy-weight/target-count ratio into a smoothed, continuous per-ion FDR confidence value. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-52213-9
skills.summary: Reconstructs the METASPACE-ML target-decoy False Discovery Rate estimation, which ranks target and SD-sampled decoy ions by machine-learning prediction score and converts the cumulative decoy-weight/target-count ratio into a smoothed, continuous per-ion FDR confidence value.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scoring model has not been trained and raw METASPACE-ML prediction scores for targets and SD-sampled decoys are not yet available — this skill only post-processes existing scores. The annotation task uses the rule-based Metabolite Signal Matching (MSM) scoring path rather than METASPACE-ML prediction scores. Data types such as QTOF-based or single-cell metabolomics datasets that are underrepresented in the model, where FDR estimates may not be statistically reliable.

skills.description: Use when filtering SSMs from a library search (standard or open/modified) to a confident set at 1% FDR, especially when modified matches must be evaluated separately from unmodified ones via target-decoy decoy-to-target ratios.
skills.name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: target-decoy-fdr-estimation Use when filtering SSMs from a library search (standard or open/modified) to a confident set at 1% FDR, especially when modified matches must be evaluated separately from unmodified ones via target-decoy decoy-to-target ratios. When only unmodified/standard-search SSMs are being analyzed, the charge-normalized mass-difference subgrouping is unnecessary — a single pooled target-decoy FDR estimate suffices. When subgroups are too small (fewer than 20 SSMs even after pooling), FDR may be underestimated and results should be interpreted with caution rather than treated as reliable. When using a search engine that does not append decoy spectra (1:1 shuffle-and-reposition), the decoy/target ratio cannot be computed and this skill does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimate and control the false discovery rate of spectrum–spectrum matches (SSMs) from spectral library searches — including open modification searches — using the target–decoy strategy, with subgroup FDR estimation for open-search matches grouped by charge-normalized precursor mass difference. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00359
skills.summary: Estimate and control the false discovery rate of spectrum–spectrum matches (SSMs) from spectral library searches — including open modification searches — using the target–decoy strategy, with subgroup FDR estimation for open-search matches grouped by charge-normalized precursor mass difference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only unmodified/standard-search SSMs are being analyzed, the charge-normalized mass-difference subgrouping is unnecessary — a single pooled target-decoy FDR estimate suffices. When subgroups are too small (fewer than 20 SSMs even after pooling), FDR may be underestimated and results should be interpreted with caution rather than treated as reliable. When using a search engine that does not append decoy spectra (1:1 shuffle-and-reposition), the decoy/target ratio cannot be computed and this skill does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you have per-dataset METASPACE/METASPACE-ML target and decoy annotation results and need to decide which of the default FDR thresholds (e.g. 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%) is most reliable for a sample-type group such as animal testing datasets.
skills.name: target-decoy-fdr-threshold-sweep
skills.search_text: target-decoy-fdr-threshold-sweep Use when you have per-dataset METASPACE/METASPACE-ML target and decoy annotation results and need to decide which of the default FDR thresholds (e.g. 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%) is most reliable for a sample-type group such as animal testing datasets. skills.when_to_use_negative: When no target-decoy annotation results are available — e.g. you are still designing the decoy generation method, which the article flags as needing further investigation because decoy ions show heterogeneity in similarity to target ions When the goal is to train or tune the METASPACE-ML GBDT ranking model itself rather than to evaluate annotation reliability at FDR thresholds When the data are not imaging-MS annotation results from METASPACE — the article notes the training/evaluation selection is biased towards public datasets represented in METASPACE, so thresholds may not transfer to other pipelines

skills.summary: Recovers missing feature intensities in untargeted metabolomics by building a target library from consensus features that have missing values and running OpenMS FeatureFinderMetaboIdent targeted extraction, replacing the entire feature matrix intensities rather than only the gaps.

skills.summary: Quality-control and batch-correct targeted LC-MS dMRM peak-area data using the mzQuality R package, which computes compound-to-internal-standard area ratios, corrects between-batch drift from pooled study QC (SQC) samples, and flags unreliable compounds and samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need raw peak deconvolution, baseline noise filtering, or retention time alignment from vendor/centroided data - mzQuality processes peak-integrated data and does not replace tools like OpenMS or MZmine. skills.name: targeted-metabolite-feature-matching
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolite-feature-matching Use when you have augmented CE-MS/HILIC-MS feature intensity tables (treated vs. control Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and must assign down/stable/up/knock out/induced calls to a known list of target metabolites and count detections per augmentation group. Input is already a processed feature table needing only statistics — AriumMS's ROI search, false-positive filter, and augmentation pipeline is for untargeted multi-platform raw data Data are single-platform only — existing tools such as XCMS Online, MetaboAnalystR, or MZmine are designed for single-platform analysis and suffice Analysis goal is MS/MS spectral networking or spectroscopic-data augmentation — the article lists both as not yet implemented (future developments) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Matches features from AriumMS-processed multi-platform CE-MS and HILIC-MS data against a predefined list of 40 target metabolites in yeast extracts, producing per-metabolite fold-change regulation calls and per-augmentation detection counts. This connects untargeted multi-platform feature detection to a targeted, tabular reporting layer. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s00216-023-04715-6
skills.summary: Matches features from AriumMS-processed multi-platform CE-MS and HILIC-MS data against a predefined list of 40 target metabolites in yeast extracts, producing per-metabolite fold-change regulation calls and per-augmentation detection counts. This connects untargeted multi-platform feature detection to a targeted, tabular reporting layer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed feature table needing only statistics — AriumMS's ROI search, false-positive filter, and augmentation pipeline is for untargeted multi-platform raw data Data are single-platform only — existing tools such as XCMS Online, MetaboAnalystR, or MZmine are designed for single-platform analysis and suffice Analysis goal is MS/MS spectral networking or spectroscopic-data augmentation — the article lists both as not yet implemented (future developments)

skills.description: Use when performing semi-targeted quantification of metabolites in LC-MS data (e.g. TripleTOF or QE HF .aird files) where EICs must be extracted, peaks selected/integrated, and compounds identified against mz/rt libraries with per-stage method choices.
skills.name: targeted-metabolite-peak-integration
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolite-peak-integration Use when performing semi-targeted quantification of metabolites in LC-MS data (e.g. TripleTOF or QE HF .aird files) where EICs must be extracted, peaks selected/integrated, and compounds identified against mz/rt libraries with per-stage method choices. Input is vendor raw data (e.g. .raw, .wiff2, .d) that has not yet been converted to Aird format by AirdPro — run file conversion first The analysis is untargeted feature discovery rather than semi-targeted detection against a defined mz/rt library Acquisition is not DDA; MetaPro's documented workflow 'supports MS data acquired with the data-dependent acquisition (DDA) method' http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs MetaPro's eight-step automatic quantification pipeline (EIC extraction, smoothing, noise estimation, peak selection, integration, screening, identification, batch optimization) for semi-targeted LC-MS metabolomics, exposing configurable method counts at each stage: 4 smoothing, 3 noise estimation, 3 peak selection, 2 integration, 5 screening criteria, and 3 identification methods. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-023-02018-6
skills.summary: Reconstructs MetaPro's eight-step automatic quantification pipeline (EIC extraction, smoothing, noise estimation, peak selection, integration, screening, identification, batch optimization) for semi-targeted LC-MS metabolomics, exposing configurable method counts at each stage: 4 smoothing, 3 noise estimation, 3 peak selection, 2 integration, 5 screening criteria, and 3 identification methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is vendor raw data (e.g. .raw, .wiff2, .d) that has not yet been converted to Aird format by AirdPro — run file conversion first The analysis is untargeted feature discovery rather than semi-targeted detection against a defined mz/rt library Acquisition is not DDA; MetaPro's documented workflow 'supports MS data acquired with the data-dependent acquisition (DDA) method'

skills.description: Use when you have vendor LC-MS/MS raw files for a defined panel of small-molecule targets (with or without heavy-labeled internal standards) and need calibrated concentrations rather than a discovery feature table.
skills.name: targeted-metabolite-quantification
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolite-quantification Use when you have vendor LC-MS/MS raw files for a defined panel of small-molecule targets (with or without heavy-labeled internal standards) and need calibrated concentrations rather than a discovery feature table. You have unlabeled full-scan data needing unsupervised feature finding, alignment, and annotation — a non-targeted workflow (XCMS, MZmine, MS-DIAL) is the better fit, and the paper itself cautions that no single tool is best for all workflows. Input is already a curated feature/quantification table rather than raw vendor acquisitions — Skyline's chromatogram extraction and peak picking would be redundant. You need GC-MS or ion-mobility small-molecule workflows today; the article states support for those is still ongoing, so Skyline may lag commercial software. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 Quantify targeted metabolites (e.g., polyamines, amino acids, purines/pyrimidines) from LC-MS/MS raw data using Skyline's small-molecule workflows, which handle selected reaction monitoring (SRM) and HRMS extraction, retention-time scheduling, stable-isotope dilution, and calibrated quantification in a single vendor-independent project. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.9b00640
skills.summary: Quantify targeted metabolites (e.g., polyamines, amino acids, purines/pyrimidines) from LC-MS/MS raw data using Skyline's small-molecule workflows, which handle selected reaction monitoring (SRM) and HRMS extraction, retention-time scheduling, stable-isotope dilution, and calibrated quantification in a single vendor-independent project.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have unlabeled full-scan data needing unsupervised feature finding, alignment, and annotation — a non-targeted workflow (XCMS, MZmine, MS-DIAL) is the better fit, and the paper itself cautions that no single tool is best for all workflows. Input is already a curated feature/quantification table rather than raw vendor acquisitions — Skyline's chromatogram extraction and peak picking would be redundant. You need GC-MS or ion-mobility small-molecule workflows today; the article states support for those is still ongoing, so Skyline may lag commercial software.

skills.description: Use when a completed vendor raw file (e.g., Thermo .raw) from an active LC-MS/MS run must be converted to mzML and its user-defined targets quantified/annotated as part of Rapid QC-MS quality control.
skills.name: targeted-metabolite-quantification-with-ms-dial
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolite-quantification-with-ms-dial Use when a completed vendor raw file (e.g., Thermo .raw) from an active LC-MS/MS run must be converted to mzML and its user-defined targets quantified/annotated as part of Rapid QC-MS quality control. Input is already an mzML or other open-format file that bypasses MSConvert conversion — this skill targets vendor raw files (only extensively tested on Thermo .raw). Goal is monitoring/viewing instrument run data on MacOS, where the MSConvert/MS-DIAL-dependent processing cannot run (Rapid QC-MS is designed for Windows). Only MSConvert conversion is needed without downstream targeted quantification/annotation — this skill covers the full raw-to-MS-DIAL stage.  http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Convert completed Thermo .raw files to open mzML via MSConvert and process the mzML with MS-DIAL to perform quantification and annotation of user-defined targets, feeding QC metrics (instrument sensitivity, retention time shifts, mass accuracy) to the Rapid QC-MS dashboard. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Convert completed Thermo .raw files to open mzML via MSConvert and process the mzML with MS-DIAL to perform quantification and annotation of user-defined targets, feeding QC metrics (instrument sensitivity, retention time shifts, mass accuracy) to the Rapid QC-MS dashboard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an mzML or other open-format file that bypasses MSConvert conversion — this skill targets vendor raw files (only extensively tested on Thermo .raw). Goal is monitoring/viewing instrument run data on MacOS, where the MSConvert/MS-DIAL-dependent processing cannot run (Rapid QC-MS is designed for Windows). Only MSConvert conversion is needed without downstream targeted quantification/annotation — this skill covers the full raw-to-MS-DIAL stage.

skills.description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files from targeted metabolomics runs must be processed by multiple peak-detection tools and their signal counts and TP/FP rates compared to choose a detector.
skills.name: targeted-metabolomics-benchmarking
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolomics-benchmarking Use when raw LC/MS mzML files from targeted metabolomics runs must be processed by multiple peak-detection tools and their signal counts and TP/FP rates compared to choose a detector. Input is already a curated feature table (the mzLearn/mzEmbed CSV format) rather than raw mzML Only one peak-detection tool is being used with no intent to compare against alternatives http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Benchmarks MS1 signal-detection tools (mzLearn, XCMS, ASARI) on 15 public targeted-metabolomics mzML datasets by comparing average detected signals, true-positive rates, and false-positive rates against peak-shape ground-truth labels. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Benchmarks MS1 signal-detection tools (mzLearn, XCMS, ASARI) on 15 public targeted-metabolomics mzML datasets by comparing average detected signals, true-positive rates, and false-positive rates against peak-shape ground-truth labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table (the mzLearn/mzEmbed CSV format) rather than raw mzML Only one peak-detection tool is being used with no intent to compare against alternatives

skills.description: Use when you have targeted metabolomics peak-intensity tables with internal-standard and nominal-concentration (calibration curve point) information and need absolute concentrations plus curve/QC accuracy and internal-standard CV metrics.
skills.name: targeted-metabolomics-data-elaboration
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolomics-data-elaboration Use when you have targeted metabolomics peak-intensity tables with internal-standard and nominal-concentration (calibration curve point) information and need absolute concentrations plus curve/QC accuracy and internal-standard CV metrics. Input is an untargeted feature table from patRoon or MS-DIAL — use the GetFeatistics untargeted functions (feature import, annotation confidence levels, pooled QC filtering) instead Raw mass-spectrometry data files requiring feature extraction (e.g. via XCMS) — targeted elaboration starts from peak-intensity tables, not raw data Input already contains calibrated absolute concentrations and you only need downstream statistics such as mixed-effects or Tobit regression models http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies the GetFeatistics R-package targeted-analysis pipeline, using get_targeted_elaboration to fit calibration curves from intensity and nominal-concentration tables with internal-standard normalization and different weighting options, converting raw peak intensities into calibrated absolute concentrations with QC accuracy metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Applies the GetFeatistics R-package targeted-analysis pipeline, using get_targeted_elaboration to fit calibration curves from intensity and nominal-concentration tables with internal-standard normalization and different weighting options, converting raw peak intensities into calibrated absolute concentrations with QC accuracy metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an untargeted feature table from patRoon or MS-DIAL — use the GetFeatistics untargeted functions (feature import, annotation confidence levels, pooled QC filtering) instead Raw mass-spectrometry data files requiring feature extraction (e.g. via XCMS) — targeted elaboration starts from peak-intensity tables, not raw data Input already contains calibrated absolute concentrations and you only need downstream statistics such as mixed-effects or Tobit regression models

skills.description: Use when LC-MS data contain compounds with known m/z and RT (e.g., the 12-narcotics demonstration set) and you need targeted peak detection plus S/N quantification rather than untargeted feature finding.
skills.name: targeted-metabolomics-peak-detection
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolomics-peak-detection Use when LC-MS data contain compounds with known m/z and RT (e.g., the 12-narcotics demonstration set) and you need targeted peak detection plus S/N quantification rather than untargeted feature finding. The analysis goal is untargeted metabolomics: SMART 2.0's targeted module requires predefined m/z and RT targets, so unannotated feature discovery should use the untargeted peak analysis modules instead. Direct one-to-one identification of narcotics without prior drug information is needed — the article notes this is not feasible due to the potential presence of other metabolites with identical m/z values. The compound of interest is not covered by reference databases (e.g., HMDB does not encompass heroin and nimetazepam), limiting downstream peak identification support. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Detect known metabolite targets (e.g., narcotics) in LC-MS data by supplying predefined m/z and retention-time targets to SMART 2.0's targeted peak analysis module, then compute per-peak S/N ratios from the MS1/MS2 abundance tables. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03225
skills.summary: Detect known metabolite targets (e.g., narcotics) in LC-MS data by supplying predefined m/z and retention-time targets to SMART 2.0's targeted peak analysis module, then compute per-peak S/N ratios from the MS1/MS2 abundance tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is untargeted metabolomics: SMART 2.0's targeted module requires predefined m/z and RT targets, so unannotated feature discovery should use the untargeted peak analysis modules instead. Direct one-to-one identification of narcotics without prior drug information is needed — the article notes this is not feasible due to the potential presence of other metabolites with identical m/z values. The compound of interest is not covered by reference databases (e.g., HMDB does not encompass heroin and nimetazepam), limiting downstream peak identification support.

skills.description: Use when MRM chromatogram files (mzML or NetCDF from vendor raw data) plus a method file of targeted compounds need automated peak detection, coeluted-peak deconvolution, and absolute quantitation with optional QC-based batch-effect correction.
skills.name: targeted-metabolomics-peak-quantitation
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolomics-peak-quantitation Use when MRM chromatogram files (mzML or NetCDF from vendor raw data) plus a method file of targeted compounds need automated peak detection, coeluted-peak deconvolution, and absolute quantitation with optional QC-based batch-effect correction. Input is already a quantified abundance/feature table — re-running peak detection would be redundant. No method file with targeted compound transitions and RTs exists — targeted quantitation cannot proceed reliably. The goal is purely to flatten batch drift in BQC regression (slope/R2) after abundances are computed — use QC-RLSC batch-effect correction rather than re-quantitation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Automated peak detection, deconvolution, and quantitation of LC-MRM chromatograms (mzML/NetCDF) against a method file of targeted compounds, using MRMQuant's MATLAB findpeaks-based peak detection, dynamic signal smoothing, coeluted-peak deconvolution, and absolute quantitation via standard curves and/or internal standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462
skills.summary: Automated peak detection, deconvolution, and quantitation of LC-MRM chromatograms (mzML/NetCDF) against a method file of targeted compounds, using MRMQuant's MATLAB findpeaks-based peak detection, dynamic signal smoothing, coeluted-peak deconvolution, and absolute quantitation via standard curves and/or internal standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantified abundance/feature table — re-running peak detection would be redundant. No method file with targeted compound transitions and RTs exists — targeted quantitation cannot proceed reliably. The goal is purely to flatten batch drift in BQC regression (slope/R2) after abundances are computed — use QC-RLSC batch-effect correction rather than re-quantitation.

skills.description: Use when processing targeted or semi-targeted CE-, GC-, LC-MS(/MS) or HPLC metabolomics experiments (mzML acquisitions plus transition/sequence CSVs) where peak picking, calibration, feature QC and quantitation should be automated.
skills.name: targeted-metabolomics-qc
skills.search_text: targeted-metabolomics-qc Use when processing targeted or semi-targeted CE-, GC-, LC-MS(/MS) or HPLC metabolomics experiments (mzML acquisitions plus transition/sequence CSVs) where peak picking, calibration, feature QC and quantitation should be automated. When a vendor-specific proprietary integration algorithm is required and cannot be replaced by SmartPeak's OpenMS-based Gaussian-Mixtures methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Automated quality-control and quantitation of targeted metabolomics data using SmartPeak on top of OpenMS, covering peak picking, calibration-curve optimization, feature QC, and report generation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.0c03421
skills.summary: Automated quality-control and quantitation of targeted metabolomics data using SmartPeak on top of OpenMS, covering peak picking, calibration-curve optimization, feature QC, and report generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature table or quantified matrix with no raw chromatograms — the skill assumes mzML peak picking through report writing. Untargeted full-scan DDA/DIA discovery workflows without a defined transition list or internal-standard scheme (use the FIA-MS/DDA BFAIR notebooks instead). When a vendor-specific proprietary integration algorithm is required and cannot be replaced by SmartPeak's OpenMS-based Gaussian-Mixtures methods.
