skills.search_text: targeted-metabolomics-workflow-configuration Use when you need to quantitate targeted LC-MS/MS MRM data (e.g., vendor raw files for bile acids or phospholipids converted to mzML/mzXML) with automatic coelution handling, standard-curve absolute quantitation, and QC-based batch-effect correction. When the input is already a processed feature table or normalized abundance matrix (no peak detection or deconvolution is needed) When the tool produces error messages for not finding the specified transitions (as occurred with MRMPROBS) rather than switching to a different pipeline When unquantifiable coeluting or noisy peaks dominate the dataset and another tool (e.g., TargetLynx) reports the smallest average STD but at the cost of the highest number of unquantifiable compounds Configure and execute the MRMQuant end-to-end targeted metabolomics quantitation pipeline, from vendor raw-data conversion through peak detection, deconvolution, absolute quantitation, and batch-effect correction to inspection-ready Excel output. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02462

skills.description: Use when you have peak-integrated targeted MRM/dMRM LC-MS metabolomics data (tab-delimited or SummarizedExperiment) needing QC, batch correction, outlier flagging, compound filtering, or absolute concentration calculation.
skills.name: targeted-mrm-data-handling
skills.search_text: targeted-mrm-data-handling Use when you have peak-integrated targeted MRM/dMRM LC-MS metabolomics data (tab-delimited or SummarizedExperiment) needing QC, batch correction, outlier flagging, compound filtering, or absolute concentration calculation. Input is unprocessed raw MS vendor files needing peak integration — mzQuality processes peak-integrated data and requires prior integration (e.g. by SCIEX OS, OpenMS, MZmine) rather than processing peaks itself. Unbiased/untargeted feature table without isotope-labeled internal standards per compound or pooled QC samples across batches — batch correction and ratio QC depend on the stable-isotope-labeled IS and SQC design. A compound is not detected in LQC or SQC samples — it is assumed absent and will not be reported, so absolute quantification on that compound is inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Skill for handling targeted LC-MS/MS MRM (dynamic Multiple Reaction Monitoring) metabolomics peak-integrated data through mzQuality: reading tab-delimited peak tables, computing compound/internal-standard ratios, batch-correcting against pooled study QC samples, assessing compound quality via QC RSD and blank background signal, and optionally quantifying absolute concentrations from calibration lines. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00073
skills.summary: Skill for handling targeted LC-MS/MS MRM (dynamic Multiple Reaction Monitoring) metabolomics peak-integrated data through mzQuality: reading tab-delimited peak tables, computing compound/internal-standard ratios, batch-correcting against pooled study QC samples, assessing compound quality via QC RSD and blank background signal, and optionally quantifying absolute concentrations from calibration lines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unprocessed raw MS vendor files needing peak integration — mzQuality processes peak-integrated data and requires prior integration (e.g. by SCIEX OS, OpenMS, MZmine) rather than processing peaks itself. Unbiased/untargeted feature table without isotope-labeled internal standards per compound or pooled QC samples across batches — batch correction and ratio QC depend on the stable-isotope-labeled IS and SQC design. A compound is not detected in LQC or SQC samples — it is assumed absent and will not be reported, so absolute quantification on that compound is inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas show injection-order intensity drift and concentrations must be computed via external calibration, comparing correction strategies (IS, QC-based, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing).
skills.name: targeted-ms-matrix-data-processing
skills.search_text: targeted-ms-matrix-data-processing Use when targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas show injection-order intensity drift and concentrations must be computed via external calibration, comparing correction strategies (IS, QC-based, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing). Input is raw, un-integrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey 'works as an additional software to already integrated mass spectrometry data, and does not provide any integration cabailities' Dataset shows no intensity drift and no internal standards unavailable — commercial platform IS correction alone may suffice Compound's IS shows differing drift trends from the analyte (e.g. 4-hydroxy-proline vs proline, methionine sulfoxide vs methionine) — IS correction introduces bias and a compound-specific strategy must be chosen instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Processes vendor-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak area tables through QuantyFey's drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) with external calibration to produce comparable concentration matrices and cross-method agreement metrics. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Processes vendor-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak area tables through QuantyFey's drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) with external calibration to produce comparable concentration matrices and cross-method agreement metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, un-integrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey 'works as an additional software to already integrated mass spectrometry data, and does not provide any integration cabailities' Dataset shows no intensity drift and no internal standards unavailable — commercial platform IS correction alone may suffice Compound's IS shows differing drift trends from the analyte (e.g. 4-hydroxy-proline vs proline, methionine sulfoxide vs methionine) — IS correction introduces bias and a compound-specific strategy must be chosen instead

skills.description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence has been quantified under one or more drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) and you must verify whether residual drift remains, per compound, before reporting concentrations.
skills.name: targeted-ms-quantification-qc-evaluation
skills.search_text: targeted-ms-quantification-qc-evaluation Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence has been quantified under one or more drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) and you must verify whether residual drift remains, per compound, before reporting concentrations. Input is still un-integrated chromatographic data: QuantyFey works as additional software to already integrated mass spectrometry data and provides no integration capabilities The dataset lacks injection-order metadata or calibration/QC block structure, so position-vs-concentration testing and bracketing strategies are undefined Only a single correction strategy was applied and no raw uncorrected baseline exists, so the drift-reduction effect cannot be assessed comparatively http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quality-control evaluation of targeted LC-MS/MS quantification outputs, using Spearman rank correlation of determined concentration vs injection position (plus mean bias, limits of agreement, Passing-Bablok regression, and Pearson correlation) to detect residual intensity drift across correction strategies. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Quality-control evaluation of targeted LC-MS/MS quantification outputs, using Spearman rank correlation of determined concentration vs injection position (plus mean bias, limits of agreement, Passing-Bablok regression, and Pearson correlation) to detect residual intensity drift across correction strategies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still un-integrated chromatographic data: QuantyFey works as additional software to already integrated mass spectrometry data and provides no integration capabilities The dataset lacks injection-order metadata or calibration/QC block structure, so position-vs-concentration testing and bracketing strategies are undefined Only a single correction strategy was applied and no raw uncorrected baseline exists, so the drift-reduction effect cannot be assessed comparatively

skills.description: Use when the goal is to find homologue series at a known m/z increment (e.g. 44.02628) in an LC-MS peak table with mz, rt, and intensity columns, and each detected peak should receive a homologue_id annotation.
skills.name: targeted-mz-increment-series-search
skills.search_text: targeted-mz-increment-series-search Use when the goal is to find homologue series at a known m/z increment (e.g. 44.02628) in an LC-MS peak table with mz, rt, and intensity columns, and each detected peak should receive a homologue_id annotation. When the m/z increment is unknown and you want to discover all homologue series in a window — use untargeted 'increment' step mode with mz_min/mz_max (e.g. 10-20) instead When the peak table already carries homologue_id annotations or series are shorter than min_series_length, since those series will be silently dropped When the expected retention-time gaps between consecutive homologues fall outside the rt_min/rt_max window (1-100 s here), as chain extension will fail Detects homologue series in LC-MS peak tables when a specific m/z increment is known a priori, using homologueDiscoverer's detectHomologues in targeted 'increment' step mode. It initializes peak 2-tuples from the given increment and extends them under ppm and retention-time constraints. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac647
skills.summary: Detects homologue series in LC-MS peak tables when a specific m/z increment is known a priori, using homologueDiscoverer's detectHomologues in targeted 'increment' step mode. It initializes peak 2-tuples from the given increment and extends them under ppm and retention-time constraints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the m/z increment is unknown and you want to discover all homologue series in a window — use untargeted 'increment' step mode with mz_min/mz_max (e.g. 10-20) instead When the peak table already carries homologue_id annotations or series are shorter than min_series_length, since those series will be silently dropped When the expected retention-time gaps between consecutive homologues fall outside the rt_min/rt_max window (1-100 s here), as chain extension will fail

skills.description: Use when validating a discovery-trained MS feature classifier on an independent targeted (sPRM/Skyline peak-area) cohort, requiring peak-area extraction, feature-group mapping, and AUC reproduction.
skills.name: targeted-proteomics-peak-area-quantification
skills.search_text: targeted-proteomics-peak-area-quantification Use when validating a discovery-trained MS feature classifier on an independent targeted (sPRM/Skyline peak-area) cohort, requiring peak-area extraction, feature-group mapping, and AUC reproduction. Input is already identified peptide/protein-level quantification rather than raw or aligned MS feature peak areas — the article found aligned MS features carry more predictive information than peptides/proteins. The targeted features have not been mapped to DeepRTAlign-aligned feature groups; applying the classifier to unmapped Skyline areas without group correspondence from information_target.csv is out of scope. The goal is retention time alignment itself rather than downstream targeted quantification and classifier validation — use the DeepRTAlign alignment workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Extract and map Skyline-exported sPRM peak areas for a targeted feature panel (e.g., 15 HCC early-recurrence features) onto DeepRTAlign-aligned feature groups, then apply a trained classifier and score it by independent-test ROC/AUC. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43909-5
skills.summary: Extract and map Skyline-exported sPRM peak areas for a targeted feature panel (e.g., 15 HCC early-recurrence features) onto DeepRTAlign-aligned feature groups, then apply a trained classifier and score it by independent-test ROC/AUC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already identified peptide/protein-level quantification rather than raw or aligned MS feature peak areas — the article found aligned MS features carry more predictive information than peptides/proteins. The targeted features have not been mapped to DeepRTAlign-aligned feature groups; applying the classifier to unmapped Skyline areas without group correspondence from information_target.csv is out of scope. The goal is retention time alignment itself rather than downstream targeted quantification and classifier validation — use the DeepRTAlign alignment workflow instead.

Raw, unintegrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey works only as an add-on to already integrated MS data and provides no integration capabilities Datasets acquired on macOS via the standalone version — QuantyFey standalone is Windows-only (use R/RStudio or Apptainer routes instead) When a validated internal standard exists for every compound and no drift is observed — IS correction alone may suffice; this skill's bracketing variants matter most when IS are unavailable or unsuitable http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Post-integration quantification of targeted LC-MS/MS analytes by external calibration regression (linear or quadratic, with weight/level selection) combined with drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing), as implemented in the QuantyFey Shiny app. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2025.344571
skills.summary: Post-integration quantification of targeted LC-MS/MS analytes by external calibration regression (linear or quadratic, with weight/level selection) combined with drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing), as implemented in the QuantyFey Shiny app.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw, unintegrated chromatographic data — QuantyFey works only as an add-on to already integrated MS data and provides no integration capabilities Datasets acquired on macOS via the standalone version — QuantyFey standalone is Windows-only (use R/RStudio or Apptainer routes instead) When a validated internal standard exists for every compound and no drift is observed — IS correction alone may suffice; this skill's bracketing variants matter most when IS are unavailable or unsuitable

skills.search_text: targeted-serum-metabolomics-matrix-handling Use when the input is a targeted serum metabolomics intensity matrix (samples x metabolites, e.g. 234 clinical samples, 113 metabolites) plus a sample table with SampleID and group labels, and the goal is automated feature selection such as Boruta before predictive model building. skills.search_text: targetedmsqc-metric-adaptation Use when XCMS-pre-processed untargeted LC–MS data needs per-peak quality features from apex-boundary ratio, jaggedness, symmetry, modality, FWHM2base, elution shift, and retention time consistency. The input is not an XCMS object (e.g. uniquely formatted vendor-processed outputs from MassHunter Profinder, Progenesis QI, or Compound Discoverer), since MetaClean requires an XCMS object input The analysis targets targeted MS data with reference standards, where the original TargetedMSQC package (not its repurposing for untargeted data) is appropriate Only a reproducibility-based filter is needed (RSD < 30% on pooled QC samples) and no peak-shape quality classification is desired http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Repurposes the seven chromatographic quality metrics from TargetedMSQC (Eshghi et al. 2018) — designed for targeted MS — to untargeted LC–MS metabolomics by computing them per EIC from XCMS-extracted chromatograms, forming the M7 metric set used as classifier features in MetaClean. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Repurposes the seven chromatographic quality metrics from TargetedMSQC (Eshghi et al. 2018) — designed for targeted MS — to untargeted LC–MS metabolomics by computing them per EIC from XCMS-extracted chromatograms, forming the M7 metric set used as classifier features in MetaClean.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not an XCMS object (e.g. uniquely formatted vendor-processed outputs from MassHunter Profinder, Progenesis QI, or Compound Discoverer), since MetaClean requires an XCMS object input The analysis targets targeted MS data with reference standards, where the original TargetedMSQC package (not its repurposing for untargeted data) is appropriate Only a reproducibility-based filter is needed (RSD < 30% on pooled QC samples) and no peak-shape quality classification is desired

skills.description: Use when a CASMI-style MS/MS challenge has the correct structure present in the PubChem candidate list but several fragment peaks stay unexplained under the 10 ppm/0.002 Da tolerance and tautomers exist in the candidate set.
skills.name: tautomer-candidate-ranking
skills.search_text: tautomer-candidate-ranking Use when a CASMI-style MS/MS challenge has the correct structure present in the PubChem candidate list but several fragment peaks stay unexplained under the 10 ppm/0.002 Da tolerance and tautomers exist in the candidate set. The unexplained peaks are due to the correct structure being absent from the candidate list (e.g. a halogenated or unusual molecule outside the C,H,N,O,P,S element filter) — relax the candidate retrieval or in silico fragmentation depth instead of only the mass tolerance. The peak list contains only stable, high-abundance fragments already matched under the default 10 ppm/0.002 Da tolerance with no tautomer ambiguity in the candidate set. The goal is molecular formula prediction (category 1 CASMI challenge), where the structure-level tautomer ranking is not the deliverable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Ranks chemically equivalent tautomer candidates by MAGMa penalty score rather than accepting a failed annotation as a missing candidate: when MS/MS peaks remain unexplained under the default mass tolerance (10 ppm, absolute minimum 0.002 Da), re-run candidate scoring with a relaxed minimum mass tolerance (0.005 Da) so alternative tautomers of the correct structure surface at the top of the ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.5702/massspectrometry.s0033
skills.summary: Ranks chemically equivalent tautomer candidates by MAGMa penalty score rather than accepting a failed annotation as a missing candidate: when MS/MS peaks remain unexplained under the default mass tolerance (10 ppm, absolute minimum 0.002 Da), re-run candidate scoring with a relaxed minimum mass tolerance (0.005 Da) so alternative tautomers of the correct structure surface at the top of the ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unexplained peaks are due to the correct structure being absent from the candidate list (e.g. a halogenated or unusual molecule outside the C,H,N,O,P,S element filter) — relax the candidate retrieval or in silico fragmentation depth instead of only the mass tolerance. The peak list contains only stable, high-abundance fragments already matched under the default 10 ppm/0.002 Da tolerance with no tautomer ambiguity in the candidate set. The goal is molecular formula prediction (category 1 CASMI challenge), where the structure-level tautomer ranking is not the deliverable.

skills.description: Use when building standardized SMILES for MS/MS library entries whose source SMILES may depict the same molecule as different tautomers, and a single canonical tautomer is needed before neutralization and downstream matching.
skills.name: tautomer-canonicalization
skills.search_text: tautomer-canonicalization Use when building standardized SMILES for MS/MS library entries whose source SMILES may depict the same molecule as different tautomers, and a single canonical tautomer is needed before neutralization and downstream matching. The structures are already standardized or come from a library whose tautomers were canonicalized upstream — re-applying the enumerator may switch representations. The goal is spectral processing (peak filtering, adduct correction, similarity scoring) rather than chemical structure standardization; use the matchms library_cleaning yaml filters instead. The molecule is not a small molecule with ionizable tautomers, or the SMILES cannot be parsed/sanitized by RDKit — these records are rejected before this stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Canonicalize tautomers with RDKit's TautomerEnumerator as one stage of the Spectraverse chemical-structure standardization pipeline, so that the same compound appearing in different tautomeric forms across MGF-derived records collapses to a single standardized SMILES representation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06256
skills.summary: Canonicalize tautomers with RDKit's TautomerEnumerator as one stage of the Spectraverse chemical-structure standardization pipeline, so that the same compound appearing in different tautomeric forms across MGF-derived records collapses to a single standardized SMILES representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The structures are already standardized or come from a library whose tautomers were canonicalized upstream — re-applying the enumerator may switch representations. The goal is spectral processing (peak filtering, adduct correction, similarity scoring) rather than chemical structure standardization; use the matchms library_cleaning yaml filters instead. The molecule is not a small molecule with ionizable tautomers, or the SMILES cannot be parsed/sanitized by RDKit — these records are rejected before this stage.

Amplicon microbial data — metacoder-style amplicon tools are the wrong fit and this WGS-oriented taxdump mapping is designed for metagenomic taxonomic profiles Profiles that already carry full lineage strings and precomputed relative abundances and need no taxID-to-taxon resolution or tree placement Analyses on real biological data with no ground truth where the goal is validated performance ranking rather than hypothesis generation http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Resolve NCBI taxonomy identifiers from standardized taxonomic profiler outputs (e.g., CAMI-style profile files) against the NCBI taxdump database to build per-taxon percentage relative abundances and lineage-annotated trees, as done in the TAMPA pipeline. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Resolve NCBI taxonomy identifiers from standardized taxonomic profiler outputs (e.g., CAMI-style profile files) against the NCBI taxdump database to build per-taxon percentage relative abundances and lineage-annotated trees, as done in the TAMPA pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Amplicon microbial data — metacoder-style amplicon tools are the wrong fit and this WGS-oriented taxdump mapping is designed for metagenomic taxonomic profiles Profiles that already carry full lineage strings and precomputed relative abundances and need no taxID-to-taxon resolution or tree placement Analyses on real biological data with no ground truth where the goal is validated performance ranking rather than hypothesis generation

skills.description: Use when a prioritization or novelty score needs the number of compounds already reported for a given species, genus, or family, or when the chemotaxonomic breadth of a family must be quantified from a database like LOTUS.
skills.name: taxon-compound-census-counting
skills.search_text: taxon-compound-census-counting Use when a prioritization or novelty score needs the number of compounds already reported for a given species, genus, or family, or when the chemotaxonomic breadth of a family must be quantified from a database like LOTUS. The input is already a prioritized extract list or MZmine quantification table — this skill enumerates literature-reported compounds from a database dump, not spectral features. The analysis requires scoring novel spectral annotations (Feature, Class, or Similarity components); the census only supplies the Literature Component baseline. The target organism lacks reliable family-level taxonomy in the database; filtering on family would silently drop entries — resolve names via Open Tree of Life first. Enumerate the chemotaxonomic scope of a plant family — unique natural products, genera, species, and chemical classes — by filtering reported compound–organism pairs in a natural-products database dump (e.g. LOTUS) to entries whose family-level taxonomy matches the target family, then counting distinct identifiers per axis. Provides the reported-compound baseline that Inventa's Literature Component compares against. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Enumerate the chemotaxonomic scope of a plant family — unique natural products, genera, species, and chemical classes — by filtering reported compound–organism pairs in a natural-products database dump (e.g. LOTUS) to entries whose family-level taxonomy matches the target family, then counting distinct identifiers per axis. Provides the reported-compound baseline that Inventa's Literature Component compares against.

skills.description: Use when annotating LC-MS/MS features of a biological extract against an in silico structure database and you want to reweight spectral matches by how closely the candidate's source organism relates taxonomically to the sample's biosource.

skills.search_text: taxonomic-distance-reranking-of-candidates Use when annotating LC-MS/MS features of a biological extract against an in silico structure database and you want to reweight spectral matches by how closely the candidate's source organism relates taxonomically to the sample's biosource. The molecules of interest are ubiquitous (primary) metabolites — taxonomic scoring mostly benefits specialized metabolites, not ubiquitous molecules Candidate annotations come from a tool whose spectral scores should remain independent and you only want hard taxonomic filtering — the paper argues taxonomically informed scoring conserving score independence is preferable to basic filtering, so filtering is a different skill Organism taxonomy cannot be resolved down to the species level against the taxonomy backbone (e.g. Catalogue of Life) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Re-ranks candidate metabolite annotations by complementing each tool's normalized spectral score with taxonomic-similarity contributions at the family, genus and species taxa levels, so that candidates from organisms taxonomically close to the biological source rank higher. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329

skills.when_to_use_negative: The molecules of interest are ubiquitous (primary) metabolites — taxonomic scoring mostly benefits specialized metabolites, not ubiquitous molecules Candidate annotations come from a tool whose spectral scores should remain independent and you only want hard taxonomic filtering — the paper argues taxonomically informed scoring conserving score independence is preferable to basic filtering, so filtering is a different skill Organism taxonomy cannot be resolved down to the species level against the taxonomy backbone (e.g. Catalogue of Life)

skills.name: taxonomic-hit-aggregation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-hit-aggregation Use when microbeMASST/jobs.py batch search output (_matches.tsv, _datasets.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) must be parsed and condensed into a per-compound table of taxa and unique sample counts to answer which organisms match a molecule. The raw Fast Search API JSON or single-spectrum web app results have not yet been written to _matches.tsv/_datasets.tsv files by jobs.py The goal is spectral library annotation level assignment from _library.tsv rather than taxonomic attribution of matches The question requires interactive visualization rather than a flat aggregated table (use the generated _domain.html trees or metadataMASST instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aggregates per-scan MASST/microbeMASST search hits into a structured taxonomic table, listing for each searched compound the matched taxa and unique sample counts (e.g., lovastatin uniquely to Aspergillus, salinosporamide A only to Salinispora tropica). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Aggregates per-scan MASST/microbeMASST search hits into a structured taxonomic table, listing for each searched compound the matched taxa and unique sample counts (e.g., lovastatin uniquely to Aspergillus, salinosporamide A only to Salinispora tropica).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The raw Fast Search API JSON or single-spectrum web app results have not yet been written to _matches.tsv/_datasets.tsv files by jobs.py The goal is spectral library annotation level assignment from _library.tsv rather than taxonomic attribution of matches The question requires interactive visualization rather than a flat aggregated table (use the generated _domain.html trees or metadataMASST instead)

skills.description: Use when curating or rebuilding a chemical classification ontology from OBO-format term stanzas, and each term must be assigned to a taxonomic level with preferred names and synonyms resolved.
skills.name: taxonomic-level-assignment-of-chemical-categories
skills.search_text: taxonomic-level-assignment-of-chemical-categories Use when curating or rebuilding a chemical classification ontology from OBO-format term stanzas, and each term must be assigned to a taxonomic level with preferred names and synonyms resolved. When the goal is to classify individual compound structures into categories — use ClassyFire's rule-based structural classification instead, not dictionary curation. When the taxonomy is already level-annotated and only structural feature extraction or category reduction is needed for a query compound. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Assigns each category in the ChemOnt chemical taxonomy to its correct taxonomic level (Kingdom, SuperClass, Class, SubClass, etc.) and records competing term choices as synonyms, producing the computable Chemical Classification Dictionary underlying ClassyFire. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-016-0174-y
skills.summary: Assigns each category in the ChemOnt chemical taxonomy to its correct taxonomic level (Kingdom, SuperClass, Class, SubClass, etc.) and records competing term choices as synonyms, producing the computable Chemical Classification Dictionary underlying ClassyFire.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to classify individual compound structures into categories — use ClassyFire's rule-based structural classification instead, not dictionary curation. When the taxonomy is already level-annotated and only structural feature extraction or category reduction is needed for a query compound.

skills.description: Use when microbeMASST batch-search outputs (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) must be aggregated per NCBI lineage rank and rendered as an interactive D3 taxonomic tree (microbe_tree.html) showing which microbes may produce a queried metabolite.
skills.name: taxonomic-lineage-aggregation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-lineage-aggregation Use when microbeMASST batch-search outputs (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) must be aggregated per NCBI lineage rank and rendered as an interactive D3 taxonomic tree (microbe_tree.html) showing which microbes may produce a queried metabolite. A rendered _microbe.html tree from the microbeMASST web app already exists — no need to re-derive the lineage aggregation. No batch search outputs exist yet (only raw .mgf spectra or USI lists) — run the jobs.py Fast Search API batch search first; aggregation cannot precede matching. The queried spectra match plant-, tissue-, or foodMASST domains rather than microbial taxa — use the corresponding domain lineage and _count_domain.tsv instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Aggregates per-scan spectral search matches (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) onto the NCBI lineage hierarchy of microbeMASST taxa (8 kingdoms through 542 strains) and renders the filtered taxonomy as an interactive D3 taxonomic tree in microbe_tree.html, mirroring the _microbe.html output of microbeMASST. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Aggregates per-scan spectral search matches (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) onto the NCBI lineage hierarchy of microbeMASST taxa (8 kingdoms through 542 strains) and renders the filtered taxonomy as an interactive D3 taxonomic tree in microbe_tree.html, mirroring the _microbe.html output of microbeMASST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A rendered _microbe.html tree from the microbeMASST web app already exists — no need to re-derive the lineage aggregation. No batch search outputs exist yet (only raw .mgf spectra or USI lists) — run the jobs.py Fast Search API batch search first; aggregation cannot precede matching. The queried spectra match plant-, tissue-, or foodMASST domains rather than microbial taxa — use the corresponding domain lineage and _count_domain.tsv instead.

skills.description: Use when you need to validate or re-tune taxonomically informed re-ranking scores (e.g., taxo_scorer weights) under degraded or incomplete taxonomic metadata, testing robustness of the scoring strategy.
skills.name: taxonomic-metadata-degradation-simulation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-metadata-degradation-simulation Use when you need to validate or re-tune taxonomically informed re-ranking scores (e.g., taxo_scorer weights) under degraded or incomplete taxonomic metadata, testing robustness of the scoring strategy. Your annotations already have complete, reliably resolved taxonomy and you only need to apply pre-computed scores (0.81/1.62/2.55) rather than re-optimize them Your metabolites are mostly ubiquitous rather than specialized, since taxonomically informed scoring mostly benefits specialized metabolites Your candidate structures come from a tool other than ISDB-DNP without re-validating that the optimized weights transfer to that tool's output distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Simulates incomplete taxonomic knowledge by randomly degrading the taxonomic metadata of ISDB-DNP annotations into four independent blocks, then uses Bayesian optimization to recover the optimal taxonomically informed scoring weights at family, genus, and species taxa levels. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Simulates incomplete taxonomic knowledge by randomly degrading the taxonomic metadata of ISDB-DNP annotations into four independent blocks, then uses Bayesian optimization to recover the optimal taxonomically informed scoring weights at family, genus, and species taxa levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your annotations already have complete, reliably resolved taxonomy and you only need to apply pre-computed scores (0.81/1.62/2.55) rather than re-optimize them Your metabolites are mostly ubiquitous rather than specialized, since taxonomically informed scoring mostly benefits specialized metabolites Your candidate structures come from a tool other than ISDB-DNP without re-validating that the optimized weights transfer to that tool's output distributions

skills.description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics samples sample-wise and the input metadata only contains free-text organism binomial names that must be standardized to stable taxonomic identifiers before RDF/SPARQL integration.
skills.name: taxonomic-metadata-resolution
skills.search_text: taxonomic-metadata-resolution Use when processing LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics samples sample-wise and the input metadata only contains free-text organism binomial names that must be standardized to stable taxonomic identifiers before RDF/SPARQL integration. Input metadata already carries resolved OTT/Wikidata identifiers, so re-resolution would add no value Samples have no associated organism metadata (e.g., purely spectral or environmental feature lists), since the enhancer resolves producing-organism binomial names Data are not LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics samples processed in the ENPKG sample-wise architecture http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Resolves the producing-organism binomial names attached to each metabolomics sample against the Open Tree of Life (v3.5) taxonomy (ottID) and Wikidata, using the ENPKG 02_enpkg_taxo_enhancer scripts, so taxonomic metadata becomes semantically linkable in the RDF knowledge graph. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.3c00800
skills.summary: Resolves the producing-organism binomial names attached to each metabolomics sample against the Open Tree of Life (v3.5) taxonomy (ottID) and Wikidata, using the ENPKG 02_enpkg_taxo_enhancer scripts, so taxonomic metadata becomes semantically linkable in the RDF knowledge graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metadata already carries resolved OTT/Wikidata identifiers, so re-resolution would add no value Samples have no associated organism metadata (e.g., purely spectral or environmental feature lists), since the enhancer resolves producing-organism binomial names Data are not LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics samples processed in the ENPKG sample-wise architecture

skills.description: Use when a structural database or annotation output contains free-text organism names and you need each name resolved to a species/genus/family position on a taxonomy backbone (Catalogue of Life) before taxonomically informed re-ranking of candidates.
skills.name: taxonomic-name-resolution-against-backbone
skills.search_text: taxonomic-name-resolution-against-backbone Use when a structural database or annotation output contains free-text organism names and you need each name resolved to a species/genus/family position on a taxonomy backbone (Catalogue of Life) before taxonomically informed re-ranking of candidates. The input already carries machine-readable, backbone-resolved taxonomy (species/genus/family columns) and only needs scoring, not name resolution The target molecules are ubiquitous primary metabolites with no taxonomic linkage — taxonomic resolution adds little value for such annotations The biological-source text is not scientific names (e.g. common names or commercial product names), which gnfinder's dictionary/NLP detection will not reliably resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Resolves biological-source names found in structural databases (e.g. DNP organism fields) against the Catalogue of Life taxonomy backbone using the gnfinder program, so that candidate annotations can be scored by taxonomic distance to the sample's organism. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Resolves biological-source names found in structural databases (e.g. DNP organism fields) against the Catalogue of Life taxonomy backbone using the gnfinder program, so that candidate annotations can be scored by taxonomic distance to the sample's organism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input already carries machine-readable, backbone-resolved taxonomy (species/genus/family columns) and only needs scoring, not name resolution The target molecules are ubiquitous primary metabolites with no taxonomic linkage — taxonomic resolution adds little value for such annotations The biological-source text is not scientific names (e.g. common names or commercial product names), which gnfinder's dictionary/NLP detection will not reliably resolve

skills.description: Use when a metadata table's ATTRIBUTE_Species (or genus/family) names may be outdated or synonymized and those names will drive taxon-level database queries such as LOTUS compound counting for the Inventa LC score.
skills.name: taxonomic-name-resolution-opentree
skills.search_text: taxonomic-name-resolution-opentree Use when a metadata table's ATTRIBUTE_Species (or genus/family) names may be outdated or synonymized and those names will drive taxon-level database queries such as LOTUS compound counting for the Inventa LC score. Taxon names are already curated to currently recognized names (e.g., already passed through OTL or another synonym resolver) — re-resolution adds no value The downstream score does not depend on taxon identity, e.g., computing only the Feature Component (FC) or Similarity Component (SC), which are taxon-independent http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Resolves species, genus, and family names in a GNPS-format metadata table to currently recognized taxa using the Open Tree of Life taxonomy service, so that downstream literature queries (e.g., LOTUS compound counts for Inventa's Literature Component) match the correct taxon. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Resolves species, genus, and family names in a GNPS-format metadata table to currently recognized taxa using the Open Tree of Life taxonomy service, so that downstream literature queries (e.g., LOTUS compound counts for Inventa's Literature Component) match the correct taxon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Taxon names are already curated to currently recognized names (e.g., already passed through OTL or another synonym resolver) — re-resolution adds no value The downstream score does not depend on taxon identity, e.g., computing only the Feature Component (FC) or Similarity Component (SC), which are taxon-independent

skills.description: Use when you have a directory of structured JSON database entries with taxonomy fields and need to compute diversity counts (distinct phyla/kingdoms) to validate reported database statistics.
skills.name: taxonomic-phylum-kingdom-counting
skills.search_text: taxonomic-phylum-kingdom-counting Use when you have a directory of structured JSON database entries with taxonomy fields and need to compute diversity counts (distinct phyla/kingdoms) to validate reported database statistics. The input is raw DNA/GenBank sequence files (e.g. the `genbanks` directory) rather than structured JSON annotation entries — taxonomy fields are only present in the JSON standard The database version is not MIBiG 3.0 (or a release with matching entry set), since the expected counts (16 phyla, 5 kingdoms) are version-specific and will not reconcile against older releases http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Aggregates taxonomy fields across all MIBiG JSON entry files to count the distinct phyla and kingdoms spanned by the database, enabling reproduction of the MIBiG 3.0 reported coverage (16 phyla across 5 kingdoms of life). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkac1049
skills.summary: Aggregates taxonomy fields across all MIBiG JSON entry files to count the distinct phyla and kingdoms spanned by the database, enabling reproduction of the MIBiG 3.0 reported coverage (16 phyla across 5 kingdoms of life).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw DNA/GenBank sequence files (e.g. the `genbanks` directory) rather than structured JSON annotation entries — taxonomy fields are only present in the JSON standard The database version is not MIBiG 3.0 (or a release with matching entry set), since the expected counts (16 phyla, 5 kingdoms) are version-specific and will not reconcile against older releases

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively rank taxonomic profilers by L1 norm error against a known ground-truth profile for a specific CAMI sample, at a chosen taxonomic rank.
skills.name: taxonomic-profile-l1-error-computation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-profile-l1-error-computation Use when you need to quantitatively rank taxonomic profilers by L1 norm error against a known ground-truth profile for a specific CAMI sample, at a chosen taxonomic rank. When no ground-truth taxonomic profile exists (real biological data) — TAMPA is then used only for hypothesis generation rather than error-based ranking When a single aggregate metric such as UniFrac or F1 is insufficient and you need visualization of which specific clades contributed to metric values — use TAMPA's contrast/normal visualization modes instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Computes per-tool L1 norm error between taxonomic profiler output and a ground-truth CAMI profile using TAMPA, enabling ranking of profilers (e.g. MetaPhyler top, mOTU bottom) on a specific sample such as CAMI_HIGH_S001. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Computes per-tool L1 norm error between taxonomic profiler output and a ground-truth CAMI profile using TAMPA, enabling ranking of profilers (e.g. MetaPhyler top, mOTU bottom) on a specific sample such as CAMI_HIGH_S001.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth taxonomic profile exists (real biological data) — TAMPA is then used only for hypothesis generation rather than error-based ranking When a single aggregate metric such as UniFrac or F1 is insufficient and you need visualization of which specific clades contributed to metric values — use TAMPA's contrast/normal visualization modes instead

skills.description: Use when input is a CAMI-format taxonomic profile (taxID, rank, abundance per taxon) that must be mapped onto the NCBI taxdump tree, e.g. for TAMPA-style tree annotation or profiler comparison.
skills.name: taxonomic-profile-parsing
skills.search_text: taxonomic-profile-parsing Use when input is a CAMI-format taxonomic profile (taxID, rank, abundance per taxon) that must be mapped onto the NCBI taxdump tree, e.g. for TAMPA-style tree annotation or profiler comparison. Input is amplicon microbial data — metacoder-style tools and this WGS-focused pipeline are not interchangeable; TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles Input profiles are not in CAMI standardized format or lack taxIDs, so taxa cannot be attached to the NCBI taxdump tree Only a single-value metric comparison (e.g. F1 score, UniFrac) is needed without per-clade abundance visualization http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Parses CAMI-format taxonomic profile files (e.g. sample CAMI_HIGH_S001) to extract per-taxon taxonomic rank assignments and percentage abundances, and attaches each taxon to the NCBI taxonomy using the ete3 toolkit's NCBI taxonomy interface so abundances can be placed on taxonomy tree nodes. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Parses CAMI-format taxonomic profile files (e.g. sample CAMI_HIGH_S001) to extract per-taxon taxonomic rank assignments and percentage abundances, and attaches each taxon to the NCBI taxonomy using the ete3 toolkit's NCBI taxonomy interface so abundances can be placed on taxonomy tree nodes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is amplicon microbial data — metacoder-style tools and this WGS-focused pipeline are not interchangeable; TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles Input profiles are not in CAMI standardized format or lack taxIDs, so taxa cannot be attached to the NCBI taxdump tree Only a single-value metric comparison (e.g. F1 score, UniFrac) is needed without per-clade abundance visualization

skills.description: Use when you have one or more taxonomic profiler profiles plus a ground-truth CAMI-style profile and need to visualize which clades at a chosen rank (e.g., class, phylum) drive profiler errors or abundance differences.
skills.name: taxonomic-rank-constrained-tree-plotting
skills.search_text: taxonomic-rank-constrained-tree-plotting Use when you have one or more taxonomic profiler profiles plus a ground-truth CAMI-style profile and need to visualize which clades at a chosen rank (e.g., class, phylum) drive profiler errors or abundance differences. Input is amplicon (16S) microbial data rather than WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles — metacoder-style tools aside, TAMPA is designed for WGS profiles You need a single summary metric (e.g., F1 score, L1 norm, UniFrac) rather than a clade-level visualization of where profilers disagree No ground-truth profile exists for contrast mode, which specifically requires comparing a tool profile against a gold standard http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Render taxonomic profiler output as a rank-constrained (e.g., phylum/class) tree using TAMPA's ete3-based pipeline, optionally in contrast mode where false-positive taxa appear as red circles and false-negative taxa as blue circles, revealing biological differences that single-valued metrics like F1 score miss. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Render taxonomic profiler output as a rank-constrained (e.g., phylum/class) tree using TAMPA's ete3-based pipeline, optionally in contrast mode where false-positive taxa appear as red circles and false-negative taxa as blue circles, revealing biological differences that single-valued metrics like F1 score miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is amplicon (16S) microbial data rather than WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles — metacoder-style tools aside, TAMPA is designed for WGS profiles You need a single summary metric (e.g., F1 score, L1 norm, UniFrac) rather than a clade-level visualization of where profilers disagree No ground-truth profile exists for contrast mode, which specifically requires comparing a tool profile against a gold standard

skills.description: Use when you have a taxonomy-structured abundance or biomarker table (MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN output, BIOM v1/v2, e.g. 16S vaginal microbiota) and need a GraPhlAn tree + annotation pair for circular rendering.
skills.name: taxonomic-tree-generation-for-graphlan
skills.search_text: taxonomic-tree-generation-for-graphlan Use when you have a taxonomy-structured abundance or biomarker table (MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN output, BIOM v1/v2, e.g. 16S vaginal microbiota) and need a GraPhlAn tree + annotation pair for circular rendering. Input is an unrooted phylogenetic tree or non-taxonomic hierarchy with no abundance/annotation table — export2graphlan expects taxonomy-labeled abundance/biomarker rows You need interactive exploration of large-scale phylogenies rather than a static publication figure — tools like iTOL target interactive analyses No biom-format library installed and input is BIOM — the README states BIOM ver. 2.0.1 is required only if input files are in BIOM format http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Converts taxonomic abundance tables (MetaPhlAn, LEfSe, HUMAnN outputs, or BIOM v1/v2 feature matrices such as 16S rRNA vaginal microbiota profiles) into a GraPhlAn tree file and annotation file, enabling circular, publication-quality phylogenetic visualizations via export2graphlan, graphlan_annotate.py, and GraPhlAn/matplotlib. metabolomics/v3 10.7717/peerj.1029
skills.summary: Converts taxonomic abundance tables (MetaPhlAn, LEfSe, HUMAnN outputs, or BIOM v1/v2 feature matrices such as 16S rRNA vaginal microbiota profiles) into a GraPhlAn tree file and annotation file, enabling circular, publication-quality phylogenetic visualizations via export2graphlan, graphlan_annotate.py, and GraPhlAn/matplotlib.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unrooted phylogenetic tree or non-taxonomic hierarchy with no abundance/annotation table — export2graphlan expects taxonomy-labeled abundance/biomarker rows You need interactive exploration of large-scale phylogenies rather than a static publication figure — tools like iTOL target interactive analyses No biom-format library installed and input is BIOM — the README states BIOM ver. 2.0.1 is required only if input files are in BIOM format

skills.description: Use when standardized taxonomic profiles (profiler output plus a gold-standard profile with TaxIDs) need a rank-resolved tree visualization of per-clade relative abundances, e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample.
skills.name: taxonomic-tree-plotting-ete3
skills.search_text: taxonomic-tree-plotting-ete3 Use when standardized taxonomic profiles (profiler output plus a gold-standard profile with TaxIDs) need a rank-resolved tree visualization of per-clade relative abundances, e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample. A single-value metric (e.g., F1 score or UniFrac) already answers the comparison question and no clade-level biological interpretation is needed Input is raw sequencing reads or binning output rather than a standardized taxonomic profile with TaxIDs that can be compared to a ground-truth profile A definitive, validated quantitative result on real (non-simulated) biological data is required, since TAMPA output is hypothesis-generating http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 TAMPA renders taxonomic abundance profiles as abundance-annotated taxonomic trees using the ete3 toolkit, comparing up to 3 profilers against a gold-standard profile (e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample) to expose per-clade differences that single-value metrics like the F1 score miss. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: TAMPA renders taxonomic abundance profiles as abundance-annotated taxonomic trees using the ete3 toolkit, comparing up to 3 profilers against a gold-standard profile (e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample) to expose per-clade differences that single-value metrics like the F1 score miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A single-value metric (e.g., F1 score or UniFrac) already answers the comparison question and no clade-level biological interpretation is needed Input is raw sequencing reads or binning output rather than a standardized taxonomic profile with TaxIDs that can be compared to a ground-truth profile A definitive, validated quantitative result on real (non-simulated) biological data is required, since TAMPA output is hypothesis-generating

skills.description: Use when MS/MS annotations from ISDB-DNP, Sirius or MS-Finder exist for spectra of a taxonomically known biological source and correct structures sit at low spectral-matching ranks, so re-ranking with taxonomic distance can boost rank-1 recall.
skills.name: taxonomically-informed-annotation-reranking
skills.search_text: taxonomically-informed-annotation-reranking Use when MS/MS annotations from ISDB-DNP, Sirius or MS-Finder exist for spectra of a taxonomically known biological source and correct structures sit at low spectral-matching ranks, so re-ranking with taxonomic distance can boost rank-1 recall. The biological source organism has no taxonomy resolvable against the Catalogue of Life (taxo bonuses cannot be computed for unresolved candidates) The analytes are ubiquitous/primary metabolites rather than specialized metabolites — the scoring 'will mostly benefit the annotation process of specialized metabolites and not ubiquitous molecules' You need a fair cross-tool performance comparison on compounds not uniformly present in the DNP — the benchmarking design favors ISDB-DNP since all benchmark compounds are in the DNP http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Re-ranks computational metabolite annotation candidates (ISDB-DNP, Sirius, MS-Finder) by combining their normalized spectral scores with taxonomy-based bonuses at family, genus and species levels, exploiting the fact that specialized metabolites are strongly linked to the taxonomic position of the producing organism. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Re-ranks computational metabolite annotation candidates (ISDB-DNP, Sirius, MS-Finder) by combining their normalized spectral scores with taxonomy-based bonuses at family, genus and species levels, exploiting the fact that specialized metabolites are strongly linked to the taxonomic position of the producing organism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological source organism has no taxonomy resolvable against the Catalogue of Life (taxo bonuses cannot be computed for unresolved candidates) The analytes are ubiquitous/primary metabolites rather than specialized metabolites — the scoring 'will mostly benefit the annotation process of specialized metabolites and not ubiquitous molecules' You need a fair cross-tool performance comparison on compounds not uniformly present in the DNP — the benchmarking design favors ISDB-DNP since all benchmark compounds are in the DNP

skills.description: Use when a metabolite or natural-products database stores organism information as free text (e.g., DNP Biological Source field) and you need accepted scientific names with a resolved, species-complete lineage for downstream taxonomic scoring.
skills.name: taxonomy-backbone-name-resolution
skills.search_text: taxonomy-backbone-name-resolution Use when a metabolite or natural-products database stores organism information as free text (e.g., DNP Biological Source field) and you need accepted scientific names with a resolved, species-complete lineage for downstream taxonomic scoring. The input is already structured taxonomy (e.g., KNApSAcK species-metabolite mappings or pre-resolved rank columns) rather than free text — gnfinder name detection is unnecessary You only need names detected without backbone resolution, e.g., simple name harvesting where Catalogue of Life lineage completeness is not required Your analysis does not require species-level completeness (e.g., only family-level scoring), since this skill explicitly discards entries whose lineage is incomplete down to the species level http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Detects scientific organism names embedded in free-text biological-source fields (e.g., Dictionary of Natural Products source strings) using gnfinder, then resolves them against a taxonomy backbone (Catalogue of Life) via the Global Names index to produce normalized, rank-structured taxonomy. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fpls.2019.01329
skills.summary: Detects scientific organism names embedded in free-text biological-source fields (e.g., Dictionary of Natural Products source strings) using gnfinder, then resolves them against a taxonomy backbone (Catalogue of Life) via the Global Names index to produce normalized, rank-structured taxonomy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already structured taxonomy (e.g., KNApSAcK species-metabolite mappings or pre-resolved rank columns) rather than free text — gnfinder name detection is unnecessary You only need names detected without backbone resolution, e.g., simple name harvesting where Catalogue of Life lineage completeness is not required Your analysis does not require species-level completeness (e.g., only family-level scoring), since this skill explicitly discards entries whose lineage is incomplete down to the species level

skills.description: Use when a set of consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g., .mgf from MZmine molecular networking) must be labeled as putatively microbial and deconvoluted from host or human-cell-line spectral matches before downstream metabolomics interpretation.
skills.name: taxonomy-based-spectrum-filtering
skills.search_text: taxonomy-based-spectrum-filtering Use when a set of consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g., .mgf from MZmine molecular networking) must be labeled as putatively microbial and deconvoluted from host or human-cell-line spectral matches before downstream metabolomics interpretation. Input is a single spectrum for one-off annotation — use the standalone microbeMASST web app (https://masst.gnps2.org/microbemasst/) instead of the batch filtering cascade The goal is plant, food, or tissue attribution — those require plantMASST, foodMASST, or tissueMASST rather than the microbial filtering cascade Spectra lack a .mgf or USI (.csv/.tsv) representation and cannot be batch-searched via the Fast Search API http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Filters a consensus MS/MS spectrum set by taxonomic origin using microbeMASST batch search results: spectra matching microbial references are retained, those also matching human cell lines are removed, and survivors are partitioned into bacteria-only, fungi-only, and both-kingdom classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Filters a consensus MS/MS spectrum set by taxonomic origin using microbeMASST batch search results: spectra matching microbial references are retained, those also matching human cell lines are removed, and survivors are partitioned into bacteria-only, fungi-only, and both-kingdom classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single spectrum for one-off annotation — use the standalone microbeMASST web app (https://masst.gnps2.org/microbemasst/) instead of the batch filtering cascade The goal is plant, food, or tissue attribution — those require plantMASST, foodMASST, or tissueMASST rather than the microbial filtering cascade Spectra lack a .mgf or USI (.csv/.tsv) representation and cannot be batch-searched via the Fast Search API

skills.description: Use when you have a species-level abundance table (e.g. skin microbiome relative abundances) plus sample metadata groups, and want enrichment at a custom taxonomic level (genus) rather than KEGG pathway/module enrichment.
skills.name: taxonomy-hierarchy-modulelist-construction
skills.search_text: taxonomy-hierarchy-modulelist-construction Use when you have a species-level abundance table (e.g. skin microbiome relative abundances) plus sample metadata groups, and want enrichment at a custom taxonomic level (genus) rather than KEGG pathway/module enrichment. The goal is standard KEGG pathway or module enrichment of KO/compound abundance data — use the built-in KOlist/CPDlist databases instead of a custom taxonomy modulelist The abundance table has been prefiltered to background features, violating the threshold-free GRSA assumption There is no grouping variable or metadata to define the contrast (GRSA supports multi-group, longitudinal, and continuous groupings, but a comparison is required) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs a custom genus-to-species hierarchical module list with ReporterScore's custom_modulelist() so that GRSA can aggregate species-level abundance statistics into genus-level reporter scores, extending functional enrichment to taxonomy-level enrichment as demonstrated on the IHSMGC skin microbiome dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Constructs a custom genus-to-species hierarchical module list with ReporterScore's custom_modulelist() so that GRSA can aggregate species-level abundance statistics into genus-level reporter scores, extending functional enrichment to taxonomy-level enrichment as demonstrated on the IHSMGC skin microbiome dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standard KEGG pathway or module enrichment of KO/compound abundance data — use the built-in KOlist/CPDlist databases instead of a custom taxonomy modulelist The abundance table has been prefiltered to background features, violating the threshold-free GRSA assumption There is no grouping variable or metadata to define the contrast (GRSA supports multi-group, longitudinal, and continuous groupings, but a comparison is required)

When the input already carries OTU/ASV or resolved taxonomy identifiers rather than free-text species names needing synonym reconciliation When the goal is chemical novelty prioritization of extracts (Inventa scoring) rather than taxon-level counting or name normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Normalizes organism taxon names (especially species binomials) against currently recognized names using the Open Tree of Life, and filters/facets records by taxonomic rank (family, genus, species) before counting unique natural products, genera, or species in datasets such as LOTUS. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Normalizes organism taxon names (especially species binomials) against currently recognized names using the Open Tree of Life, and filters/facets records by taxonomic rank (family, genus, species) before counting unique natural products, genera, or species in datasets such as LOTUS.

skills.description: Use when a NP occurrence pipeline contains raw organism name strings (vernacular, TCM, common names, organ names) that must be mapped to canonical taxa before structure-organism pair harmonization.
skills.name: taxonomy-resolution-open-tree-of-life
skills.search_text: taxonomy-resolution-open-tree-of-life Use when a NP occurrence pipeline contains raw organism name strings (vernacular, TCM, common names, organ names) that must be mapped to canonical taxa before structure-organism pair harmonization. The organism table already contains canonical scientific names directly resolvable without approximate string matching Only a small number of known organism names must be matched manually rather than via automated translation The paper describes this mechanism but does not independently validate it; do not rely on it without expert review of mapping plausibility http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Harmonizes heterogeneous organism name strings into a unified taxonomy by first translating common/vernacular/TCM names to scientific names via approximate string matching, then resolving accepted scientific names to Open Tree of Life taxonomy nodes with rotl to build a name-to-taxon SQLite dictionary. metabolomics/v3 10.7554/elife.70780
skills.summary: Harmonizes heterogeneous organism name strings into a unified taxonomy by first translating common/vernacular/TCM names to scientific names via approximate string matching, then resolving accepted scientific names to Open Tree of Life taxonomy nodes with rotl to build a name-to-taxon SQLite dictionary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism table already contains canonical scientific names directly resolvable without approximate string matching Only a small number of known organism names must be matched manually rather than via automated translation The paper describes this mechanism but does not independently validate it; do not rely on it without expert review of mapping plausibility

skills.search_text: tcga-gtex-sample-metadata-integration Use when reproducing or extending a pooled TCGA/GTEx RNA-Seq compendium that requires sample-level filtering (organ-size cutoffs, duplicate removal, metadata completeness) and integration into MetaOmGraph's metadata-aware project structure. The input dataset is already a filtered MOG project (e.g. the published 18,212 x 7,412 matrix) and only downstream analysis is needed The analysis targets a single-study expression table without pooled TCGA/GTEx structure, so organ-size, duplicate-sample, and cross-study gene-intersection filters do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assembles the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset from the Wang et al. combined TCGA/GTEx RNA-Seq resource (PMR) by applying the paper's sample and gene filters and attaching organ/tumor-status/study metadata, then encoding the result as a savable MetaOmGraph (MOG) project of 18,212 genes x 7,412 samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Assembles the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset from the Wang et al. combined TCGA/GTEx RNA-Seq resource (PMR) by applying the paper's sample and gene filters and attaching organ/tumor-status/study metadata, then encoding the result as a savable MetaOmGraph (MOG) project of 18,212 genes x 7,412 samples.
