skills.description: Use when bridging TCM prototype components to their predictable metabolites in MS data, and a reaction catalog including deglycosylation plus scored m/z and MS2-similarity matching is needed.
skills.name: tcm-deglycosylation-reaction-annotation
skills.search_text: tcm-deglycosylation-reaction-annotation Use when bridging TCM prototype components to their predictable metabolites in MS data, and a reaction catalog including deglycosylation plus scored m/z and MS2-similarity matching is needed. The target metabolite cannot be rationalized as a one- or two-step product of a prototype via Metworks 1.3.0.200 reactions or deglycosylation (i.e., unpredictable metabolites requiring background subtraction approaches like PATBS instead) Only single-metabolite-to-prototype-database matching via secondary MS spectral similarity is needed (the MTSF-style scenario), rather than scored multi-dimension bridging http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs the MDRB predictable-metabolite reaction catalog by combining known metabolic reactions from Metworks 1.3.0.200 with TCM-specific deglycosylation reactions, then scores one- and two-step metabolite-prototype assignments (m/z within ±5 ppm = 70 points; MS2 similarity degree 1/≥2/0 = 20/30/0 points). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs the MDRB predictable-metabolite reaction catalog by combining known metabolic reactions from Metworks 1.3.0.200 with TCM-specific deglycosylation reactions, then scores one- and two-step metabolite-prototype assignments (m/z within ±5 ppm = 70 points; MS2 similarity degree 1/≥2/0 = 20/30/0 points).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target metabolite cannot be rationalized as a one- or two-step product of a prototype via Metworks 1.3.0.200 reactions or deglycosylation (i.e., unpredictable metabolites requiring background subtraction approaches like PATBS instead) Only single-metabolite-to-prototype-database matching via secondary MS spectral similarity is needed (the MTSF-style scenario), rather than scored multi-dimension bridging

skills.description: Use when a low-resolution MS2 spectrum of a marker peak from a TCM/herbal extract was acquired on a miniaturized mass spectrometer and the goal is de novo structural annotation of the contained compound without a library match.
skills.name: tcm-extract-compound-identification
skills.search_text: tcm-extract-compound-identification Use when a low-resolution MS2 spectrum of a marker peak from a TCM/herbal extract was acquired on a miniaturized mass spectrometer and the goal is de novo structural annotation of the contained compound without a library match. Input spectra are high-resolution/high-accuracy MS2 — models like MassGenie, SIRIUS4, or MSNovelist are geared toward that regime and TeFT may not show performance advantages there. Spectra were recorded in negative ion mode — TeFT was only trained on positive ion mode (H+) spectra. The compound's fragmentation behavior lacks clear fragmentation rules, or prior mass spectrometry library search already yields a confident identification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Identifies the unknown compound in a traditional Chinese medicine extract (e.g., the m/z 269 marker peak of Anweiyang capsules) by running TeFT fragmentation-tree simulation on low-resolution MS2 spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer and ranking candidates by SMILES fragment-tree similarity. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0
skills.summary: Identifies the unknown compound in a traditional Chinese medicine extract (e.g., the m/z 269 marker peak of Anweiyang capsules) by running TeFT fragmentation-tree simulation on low-resolution MS2 spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer and ranking candidates by SMILES fragment-tree similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are high-resolution/high-accuracy MS2 — models like MassGenie, SIRIUS4, or MSNovelist are geared toward that regime and TeFT may not show performance advantages there. Spectra were recorded in negative ion mode — TeFT was only trained on positive ion mode (H+) spectra. The compound's fragmentation behavior lacks clear fragmentation rules, or prior mass spectrometry library search already yields a confident identification.

skills.description: Use when you have a mouse/in vivo feature list and an in vitro prototype list (RT + accurate m/z per component) and must annotate prototypes, isomers, and metabolites of TCM components sharing a parent nucleus.
skills.name: tcm-in-vivo-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: tcm-in-vivo-metabolite-annotation Use when you have a mouse/in vivo feature list and an in vitro prototype list (RT + accurate m/z per component) and must annotate prototypes, isomers, and metabolites of TCM components sharing a parent nucleus. Input is still raw LC-MS data requiring background subtraction/peak detection — apply the PATBS non-targeted identification step first, since MDRB is a post-processing technique operating on already-detected components There is no in vitro prototype list to bridge against — MTSF-style single-metabolite-vs-database matching or metabolomics approaches are the relevant alternatives Annotates in vivo TCM metabolites and links them to in vitro prototypes using the R-based MDRB post-processing technique, which bridges prototype–metabolite relationships on three dimensions of mass spectral data (m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, MS2 fragment similarity). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Annotates in vivo TCM metabolites and links them to in vitro prototypes using the R-based MDRB post-processing technique, which bridges prototype–metabolite relationships on three dimensions of mass spectral data (m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defect, MS2 fragment similarity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw LC-MS data requiring background subtraction/peak detection — apply the PATBS non-targeted identification step first, since MDRB is a post-processing technique operating on already-detected components There is no in vitro prototype list to bridge against — MTSF-style single-metabolite-vs-database matching or metabolomics approaches are the relevant alternatives

skills.description: Use when you have a PATBS-processed feature table (m/z, MS1, MS2, retention) for prototypes and candidate metabolites and need to score/bridge metabolite–prototype relationships using MS1/MS2 mass-defect windows (±25 mmu) and fragment matching.
skills.name: tcm-metabolite-bridging
skills.search_text: tcm-metabolite-bridging Use when you have a PATBS-processed feature table (m/z, MS1, MS2, retention) for prototypes and candidate metabolites and need to score/bridge metabolite–prototype relationships using MS1/MS2 mass-defect windows (±25 mmu) and fragment matching. The input is raw vendor LC-MS data rather than a PATBS-processed feature table with m/z, MS1, MS2, and retention columns Only single-metabolite-to-prototype MS2 map similarity matching is needed (MTSF-style matching suffices) rather than multi-dimensional mass-defect bridging Metabolites follow predictable, known metabolic responses that are already handled by tools such as Metworks 1.3.0.200 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 An R-based MDRB (mass dataset relevance bridging) post-processing skill that scores metabolite–prototype pairs from PATBS-processed LC-MS feature tables by integrating m/z, MS1/MS2 mass-defect windows, and MS2 fragment similarity, enabling bridging of in vivo TCM metabolites to in vitro prototypes and construction of a component relationship network. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: An R-based MDRB (mass dataset relevance bridging) post-processing skill that scores metabolite–prototype pairs from PATBS-processed LC-MS feature tables by integrating m/z, MS1/MS2 mass-defect windows, and MS2 fragment similarity, enabling bridging of in vivo TCM metabolites to in vitro prototypes and construction of a component relationship network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw vendor LC-MS data rather than a PATBS-processed feature table with m/z, MS1, MS2, and retention columns Only single-metabolite-to-prototype MS2 map similarity matching is needed (MTSF-style matching suffices) rather than multi-dimensional mass-defect bridging Metabolites follow predictable, known metabolic responses that are already handled by tools such as Metworks 1.3.0.200

skills.description: Use when you have LC-MS feature lists from in vivo TCM dosing (plasma, urine, feces, tissue) plus an in vitro prototype component list and need to characterize metabolites and bridge them to parent prototypes.
skills.name: tcm-metabolite-characterization
skills.search_text: tcm-metabolite-characterization Use when you have LC-MS feature lists from in vivo TCM dosing (plasma, urine, feces, tissue) plus an in vitro prototype component list and need to characterize metabolites and bridge them to parent prototypes. The analysis only requires matching a single metabolite against a prototype database using MS2 map similarity alone (e.g., MTSF-style matching) rather than integrated m/z + mass defect + fragment scoring The in vivo feature list has no corresponding in vitro prototype/component data to bridge against, so prototype matching and metabolic-pathway matching cannot be performed You need statistical validation or quantitative performance metrics of the identification strategy — the paper reports none and acknowledges in vivo component identification remains difficult http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Characterize traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) metabolites in vivo by bridging them to in vitro prototypes using the MDRB R-based data post-processing technique, which sequentially scores m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defects, and MS2 fragment similarity. It raises characterization rates substantially over manual annotation (e.g., 227 metabolites at 65% vs 110 at 31% for semen Armeniacae Amarum/CKXR in mice). metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13020-024-01031-8
skills.summary: Characterize traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) metabolites in vivo by bridging them to in vitro prototypes using the MDRB R-based data post-processing technique, which sequentially scores m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defects, and MS2 fragment similarity. It raises characterization rates substantially over manual annotation (e.g., 227 metabolites at 65% vs 110 at 31% for semen Armeniacae Amarum/CKXR in mice).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only requires matching a single metabolite against a prototype database using MS2 map similarity alone (e.g., MTSF-style matching) rather than integrated m/z + mass defect + fragment scoring The in vivo feature list has no corresponding in vitro prototype/component data to bridge against, so prototype matching and metabolic-pathway matching cannot be performed You need statistical validation or quantitative performance metrics of the identification strategy — the paper reports none and acknowledges in vivo component identification remains difficult

skills.description: Use when training a formula-prediction deep learning model from matched MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g., MoNA Q-TOF, NIST23 Orbitrap) or when reproducing the paper's cross-instrument generalization experiment (Fig. 4j).
skills.name: tcn-model-training-on-tandem-msms
skills.search_text: tcn-model-training-on-tandem-msms Use when training a formula-prediction deep learning model from matched MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g., MoNA Q-TOF, NIST23 Orbitrap) or when reproducing the paper's cross-instrument generalization experiment (Fig. 4j). The goal is formula inference on new spectra with existing weights — use pre-trained checkpoints or the msfiddle CLI instead of retraining Spectra fall outside the paper's filter space (fewer than five peaks, m/z above 1500, non-frequent atoms, >300 atoms, or uncommon precursor types) The task is structural elucidation or fingerprint prediction (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID territory), not molecular formula prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train FIDDLE's temporal convolutional network (TCN) models to predict molecular formulas from tandem MS/MS spectra, separately for Q-TOF and Orbitrap instrument types using the FIDDLE repository's train_tcn_gpus.py with instrument-specific YAML configs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Train FIDDLE's temporal convolutional network (TCN) models to predict molecular formulas from tandem MS/MS spectra, separately for Q-TOF and Orbitrap instrument types using the FIDDLE repository's train_tcn_gpus.py with instrument-specific YAML configs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is formula inference on new spectra with existing weights — use pre-trained checkpoints or the msfiddle CLI instead of retraining Spectra fall outside the paper's filter space (fewer than five peaks, m/z above 1500, non-frequent atoms, >300 atoms, or uncommon precursor types) The task is structural elucidation or fingerprint prediction (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID territory), not molecular formula prediction

skills.description: Use when individual concentration records and dosing history (times, amounts, infusion rates, covariates) must be assembled into an NM-TRAN dataset to feed mapbayest() from a mrgsolve-coded population PK model.
skills.name: tdm-data-formatting-nmtran
skills.search_text: tdm-data-formatting-nmtran Use when individual concentration records and dosing history (times, amounts, infusion rates, covariates) must be assembled into an NM-TRAN dataset to feed mapbayest() from a mrgsolve-coded population PK model. You already have a complete, correctly coded NM-TRAN dataset with evid/cmt/amt/mdv columns — feed it directly as the data argument of mapbayest() The task is population (NLME) model fitting rather than individual MAP-BE — nlmixr or saemix are the dedicated packages cited for population PK/PD modeling The model is not coded in mrgsolve or fails check_mapbayr_model() validation — mapbayr requires mrgsolve-formatted models Format therapeutic drug monitoring dosing and observation records into an NM-TRAN-style dataset suitable for MAP-Bayesian estimation with mapbayr, using the pipe-friendly adm_rows(), obs_rows(), and add_covariates() helpers instead of hand-building the data frame. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/psp4.12689
skills.summary: Format therapeutic drug monitoring dosing and observation records into an NM-TRAN-style dataset suitable for MAP-Bayesian estimation with mapbayr, using the pipe-friendly adm_rows(), obs_rows(), and add_covariates() helpers instead of hand-building the data frame.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a complete, correctly coded NM-TRAN dataset with evid/cmt/amt/mdv columns — feed it directly as the data argument of mapbayest() The task is population (NLME) model fitting rather than individual MAP-BE — nlmixr or saemix are the dedicated packages cited for population PK/PD modeling The model is not coded in mrgsolve or fails check_mapbayr_model() validation — mapbayr requires mrgsolve-formatted models

skills.description: Use when you have UK Biobank NMR biomarker data (249 biomarkers plus sample QC fields) and need to quantify, per biomarker, the percentage of concentration variance attributable to each technical covariate to decide which measurements need technical-variation removal.
skills.name: technical-covariate-regression-analysis
skills.search_text: technical-covariate-regression-analysis Use when you have UK Biobank NMR biomarker data (249 biomarkers plus sample QC fields) and need to quantify, per biomarker, the percentage of concentration variance attributable to each technical covariate to decide which measurements need technical-variation removal. The goal is to actually remove technical variation from the 107 non-derived biomarkers rather than quantify it — use the ukbnmr remove_technical_variation() robust-regression pipeline instead The data are already corrected concentrations (output of remove_technical_variation()) and you want to verify residual technical effects — the regression should be run on the original data as reported Input is biomarker measurement QC flags rather than concentrations — R-squared regression on covariates applies to the concentration matrix, not the flag columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how much variance in each of the 249 UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations is explained by each recorded technical covariate (plate row/column, shipment batch, spectrometer, degradation time, measurement-date bins) by fitting one linear model per biomarker-covariate pair and recording R-squared, to identify biomarkers most affected by technical variation before applying the ukbnmr removal procedure. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: Quantifies how much variance in each of the 249 UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations is explained by each recorded technical covariate (plate row/column, shipment batch, spectrometer, degradation time, measurement-date bins) by fitting one linear model per biomarker-covariate pair and recording R-squared, to identify biomarkers most affected by technical variation before applying the ukbnmr removal procedure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to actually remove technical variation from the 107 non-derived biomarkers rather than quantify it — use the ukbnmr remove_technical_variation() robust-regression pipeline instead The data are already corrected concentrations (output of remove_technical_variation()) and you want to verify residual technical effects — the regression should be run on the original data as reported Input is biomarker measurement QC flags rather than concentrations — R-squared regression on covariates applies to the concentration matrix, not the flag columns

skills.description: Use when per-file human QC annotations from multiple raters must be reduced to consensus labels and quantified for inter-rater agreement, especially on embedded technical replicates.
skills.name: technical-replicate-agreement-analysis
skills.search_text: technical-replicate-agreement-analysis Use when per-file human QC annotations from multiple raters must be reduced to consensus labels and quantified for inter-rater agreement, especially on embedded technical replicates. Input is already a single-label ground truth (e.g. AI model predictions) — this skill requires multiple independent rater labels to form a majority vote; applying it to model output conflates prediction with consensus. Data are DDA files or targeted SRM assays rather than DIA acquisition — the annotation consensus and replicate structure described here were established for the 2754 DIA QC files from 21 multivendor instruments, and the paper notes SRM-based QC tools cannot be applied directly to large-scale experiments. Fewer than three raters per file are available — majority voting and meaningful observed-agreement statistics need a rater panel comparable to the 21-expert panel; with a single annotator the consensus degenerates to one opinion. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes how consistently multiple expert annotators (and embedded technical replicates) agree on qualified/unqualified QC labels for DIA mass-spectrometry files, using majority-vote consensus as the reference label. Validates that the annotation layer of the iDIA-QC workflow is reproducible before that layer is used to train or benchmark AI QC models. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-54871-1
skills.summary: Computes how consistently multiple expert annotators (and embedded technical replicates) agree on qualified/unqualified QC labels for DIA mass-spectrometry files, using majority-vote consensus as the reference label. Validates that the annotation layer of the iDIA-QC workflow is reproducible before that layer is used to train or benchmark AI QC models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single-label ground truth (e.g. AI model predictions) — this skill requires multiple independent rater labels to form a majority vote; applying it to model output conflates prediction with consensus. Data are DDA files or targeted SRM assays rather than DIA acquisition — the annotation consensus and replicate structure described here were established for the 2754 DIA QC files from 21 multivendor instruments, and the paper notes SRM-based QC tools cannot be applied directly to large-scale experiments. Fewer than three raters per file are available — majority voting and meaningful observed-agreement statistics need a rater panel comparable to the 21-expert panel; with a single annotator the consensus degenerates to one opinion.

skills.description: Use when an LC-MS/MS feature table contains repeated technical replicate injections (annotated via 'technical_rep' in the sample annotation file) and downstream per-feature tests such as ANOVA must be run over biological replicates only.
skills.name: technical-replicate-collapsing
skills.search_text: technical-replicate-collapsing Use when an LC-MS/MS feature table contains repeated technical replicate injections (annotated via 'technical_rep' in the sample annotation file) and downstream per-feature tests such as ANOVA must be run over biological replicates only. The feature table already contains one row per biological replicate (no technical_rep column or no repeated injections), so collapsing would drop real samples The goal is QC or drift assessment at injection level, where per-technical-replicate measurements are the units of interest Input is not margheRita/mRList-format MS-DIAL output with the required id, injection_order, batch, class, biological_rep, technical_rep annotation columns http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Collapses technical replicate injections into single biological-replicate samples in an mRList object using margheRita's collapse_tech_rep function, grouping all samples that share the same concatenation of 'class' and 'biological_rep' values before dataset-wide statistical testing. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.06.20.599545
skills.summary: Collapses technical replicate injections into single biological-replicate samples in an mRList object using margheRita's collapse_tech_rep function, grouping all samples that share the same concatenation of 'class' and 'biological_rep' values before dataset-wide statistical testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table already contains one row per biological replicate (no technical_rep column or no repeated injections), so collapsing would drop real samples The goal is QC or drift assessment at injection level, where per-technical-replicate measurements are the units of interest Input is not margheRita/mRList-format MS-DIAL output with the required id, injection_order, batch, class, biological_rep, technical_rep annotation columns

skills.description: Use when starting an mpactR workflow: you have a Progenesis peak table CSV and a sample metadata CSV with Injection, Sample_Code, and Biological_Group columns, and technical replicates must be linked to biological groups before filtering.
skills.name: technical-replicate-metadata-mapping
skills.search_text: technical-replicate-metadata-mapping Use when starting an mpactR workflow: you have a Progenesis peak table CSV and a sample metadata CSV with Injection, Sample_Code, and Biological_Group columns, and technical replicates must be linked to biological groups before filtering. Your peak table is not from Progenesis pre-processing (e.g. MS-DIAL or Bruker Metaboscape exports handled by the Python MPACT tool) — import_data with format = "Progenesis" expects Progenesis-format columns. You only need to run filters without replicate-aware grouping — filters such as filter_mispicked_ions() are independent of metadata grouping. Metadata lacks the required Injection, Sample_Code, and Biological_Group columns — the downstream CV filter between technical replicates cannot be applied correctly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Ingest a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table and its sample metadata CSV into an mpactR R6 object so that each injection (including technical replicates) is mapped to its Sample_Code and Biological_Group, enabling downstream replicate-reproducibility (CV) filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1128/mra.00997-24
skills.summary: Ingest a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table and its sample metadata CSV into an mpactR R6 object so that each injection (including technical replicates) is mapped to its Sample_Code and Biological_Group, enabling downstream replicate-reproducibility (CV) filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your peak table is not from Progenesis pre-processing (e.g. MS-DIAL or Bruker Metaboscape exports handled by the Python MPACT tool) — import_data with format = "Progenesis" expects Progenesis-format columns. You only need to run filters without replicate-aware grouping — filters such as filter_mispicked_ions() are independent of metadata grouping. Metadata lacks the required Injection, Sample_Code, and Biological_Group columns — the downstream CV filter between technical replicates cannot be applied correctly.

skills.description: Use when input is centroided, peak-picked replicate MS data (e.g. mzML-derived peak lists, one CSV per replicate injection) and a denoised list of unique MS features is needed before bioactivity scoring in NP Analyst.
skills.name: technical-replicate-peak-filtering
skills.search_text: technical-replicate-peak-filtering Use when input is centroided, peak-picked replicate MS data (e.g. mzML-derived peak lists, one CSV per replicate injection) and a denoised list of unique MS features is needed before bioactivity scoring in NP Analyst. skills.description: Use when building a searchable 4D sterol lipid database that requires predicted fragment ions for N-Me derivatized (C=C bond-targeted) unsaturated sterols, e.g. to support LC-IM-MS/MS based identification at the isomer level.
skills.name: theoretical-fragment-ion-cataloging
skills.search_text: theoretical-fragment-ion-cataloging Use when building a searchable 4D sterol lipid database that requires predicted fragment ions for N-Me derivatized (C=C bond-targeted) unsaturated sterols, e.g. to support LC-IM-MS/MS based identification at the isomer level. Input molecules lack C=C bonds (e.g. saturated sterols or non-unsaturated lipids), since the N-Me fragmentation logic depends on double bond recognition The goal is CCS prediction rather than fragment-ion generation — that task uses the separate QCC-assisted scikit-learn (LASSO + SVR) workflow The goal is experimental data processing and sterol identification rather than in-silico fragment prediction — use the LC-IM-MS/MS data processing part of the pipeline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate theoretical MS/MS fragment-ion information (m/z and relative intensity) for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids by recognizing C=C double bond positions in each sterol backbone and applying N-Me fragmentation patterns encoded via RDkit built-in functions. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/anie.202507483
skills.summary: Generate theoretical MS/MS fragment-ion information (m/z and relative intensity) for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids by recognizing C=C double bond positions in each sterol backbone and applying N-Me fragmentation patterns encoded via RDkit built-in functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input molecules lack C=C bonds (e.g. saturated sterols or non-unsaturated lipids), since the N-Me fragmentation logic depends on double bond recognition The goal is CCS prediction rather than fragment-ion generation — that task uses the separate QCC-assisted scikit-learn (LASSO + SVR) workflow The goal is experimental data processing and sterol identification rather than in-silico fragment prediction — use the LC-IM-MS/MS data processing part of the pipeline instead

skills.description: Use when you have experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. CID or HCD, positive mode) of candidate NRP/PK compounds and building-block sequences exported from MassSpecBlocks, and you need to identify the compound whose theoretical b-/a-ion fragment pattern matches the spectrum.
skills.name: theoretical-fragment-spectrum-matching
skills.search_text: theoretical-fragment-spectrum-matching Use when you have experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. CID or HCD, positive mode) of candidate NRP/PK compounds and building-block sequences exported from MassSpecBlocks, and you need to identify the compound whose theoretical b-/a-ion fragment pattern matches the spectrum. The spectra are of ordinary peptides and you only need standard search — NRPro or Dereplicator may suffice, since MassSpecBlocks/CycloBranch exist for custom NRP/PK sequences that those tools cannot handle You need modification-tolerant search of spectra against a broad public spectral database (GNPS) rather than a custom sequence database of a few dozen candidate compounds The building blocks of your molecules cannot be decomposed from SMILES (e.g. sequences with flipped peptide-bond orientation in PK siderophores) — MassSpecBlocks first determines the block structure before matching is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Match experimental tandem MS/MS spectra of linear, cyclic, branched, and branch-cyclic nonribosomal peptides and polyketide siderophores against theoretical fragment spectra generated from building-block sequences exported from MassSpecBlocks, using CycloBranch's comparator for dereplication. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-021-00530-2
skills.summary: Match experimental tandem MS/MS spectra of linear, cyclic, branched, and branch-cyclic nonribosomal peptides and polyketide siderophores against theoretical fragment spectra generated from building-block sequences exported from MassSpecBlocks, using CycloBranch's comparator for dereplication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are of ordinary peptides and you only need standard search — NRPro or Dereplicator may suffice, since MassSpecBlocks/CycloBranch exist for custom NRP/PK sequences that those tools cannot handle You need modification-tolerant search of spectra against a broad public spectral database (GNPS) rather than a custom sequence database of a few dozen candidate compounds The building blocks of your molecules cannot be decomposed from SMILES (e.g. sequences with flipped peptide-bond orientation in PK siderophores) — MassSpecBlocks first determines the block structure before matching is possible

skills.description: Use when confirming RT-dimension peaks detected for primary ion m/z traces against candidate molecular formulae: a theoretical A/A+1/A+2 intensity pattern is needed to accept or reject detected peaks.
skills.name: theoretical-isotope-distribution-calculation
skills.search_text: theoretical-isotope-distribution-calculation Use when confirming RT-dimension peaks detected for primary ion m/z traces against candidate molecular formulae: a theoretical A/A+1/A+2 intensity pattern is needed to accept or reject detected peaks. Input is already a confirmed, isotopologue-filtered feature table — the theoretical distribution is only needed for the confirmation step after peak picking. The analysis does not require isotope-envelope confirmation (e.g. you only need theoretical exact masses or CCS values without RT-peak confirmation of detected chromatographic peaks). The mzML file is profile LC-IM-MS data that has not yet been peak-picked in the RT dimension — peak picking (e.g. biosaur2) must precede isotopologue matching. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes theoretical isotopologue distributions (A, A+1, A+2 relative intensities) for candidate molecular formulae with molmass, accounting for the selected ion species and optionally multiply charged ions, to serve as the reference pattern for CCSfind's isotopologue-matching confirmation filter. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/jms.5040
skills.summary: Computes theoretical isotopologue distributions (A, A+1, A+2 relative intensities) for candidate molecular formulae with molmass, accounting for the selected ion species and optionally multiply charged ions, to serve as the reference pattern for CCSfind's isotopologue-matching confirmation filter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a confirmed, isotopologue-filtered feature table — the theoretical distribution is only needed for the confirmation step after peak picking. The analysis does not require isotope-envelope confirmation (e.g. you only need theoretical exact masses or CCS values without RT-peak confirmation of detected chromatographic peaks). The mzML file is profile LC-IM-MS data that has not yet been peak-picked in the RT dimension — peak picking (e.g. biosaur2) must precede isotopologue matching.

skills.search_text: theoretical-isotope-distribution-computation Use when high-resolution MS1 isotope peak lists (peak masses and abundances) must be assigned a molecular formula by ranking candidate isotope patterns, or when reimplementing SIRIUS 4's isotope pattern intensity scoring. Input is already a ranked formula/structure list from SIRIUS and no intensity-based formula re-scoring is needed Only MS2 fragmentation spectra are available without MS1 isotope peak data — use fragmentation tree computation instead Spectra are low-resolution, where SIRIUS's isotope pattern analysis of 'mass spectra of high resolution' does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Computes theoretical isotope patterns for candidate molecular formulas by convolving per-element natural isotope abundances, and scores measured MS1 isotope peak intensities against them using SIRIUS 4's closed-form maximum-likelihood intensity error model (σ_abs = 0.01, σ_rel = 0.08) to rank formulas by summed log-odds. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-019-0344-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a ranked formula/structure list from SIRIUS and no intensity-based formula re-scoring is needed Only MS2 fragmentation spectra are available without MS1 isotope peak data — use fragmentation tree computation instead Spectra are low-resolution, where SIRIUS's isotope pattern analysis of 'mass spectra of high resolution' does not apply

The acquisition sequence or raw files are from Agilent, Bruker, Sciex, or Waters — Rapid QC-MS has only been tested extensively on Thermo acquisition sequences and Thermo RAW files and may have vendor-format bugs. Data are already converted feature tables or processed peak lists — this skill assumes vendor RAW input is available for MSConvert-to-mzML conversion and MS-DIAL processing. The platform is not Windows and vendor RAW conversion is required — Rapid QC-MS depends on MSConvert and MS-DIAL and was designed for Windows; MacOS users can only monitor/view run data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Rapid QC-MS is configured against a Thermo acquisition sequence .csv so that each newly written Thermo RAW file is automatically converted to mzML, processed via MS-DIAL against a .msp library, and scored per specimen and per internal standard (Pass/Fail/Warn) on a live dashboard. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00786
skills.summary: Rapid QC-MS is configured against a Thermo acquisition sequence .csv so that each newly written Thermo RAW file is automatically converted to mzML, processed via MS-DIAL against a .msp library, and scored per specimen and per internal standard (Pass/Fail/Warn) on a live dashboard.

skills.name: thermo-raw-to-mzml-conversion
skills.search_text: thermo-raw-to-mzml-conversion Use when the input is a Thermo (or other vendor) proprietary RAW file from a mass spectrometry repository and the goal is an open, Parquet-compatible spectral table matching the arcMS Waters-UNIFI schema (rt, scanid, mslevel, mz, intensity). Input is already an arcMS Parquet or mzML file — conversion of RAW to mzML is unnecessary Data originates from Waters UNIFI — use arcMS's native UNIFI API collection (create_connection_params / convert_one_sample_data) instead The goal is direct in-memory analysis without a persisted columnar file — HDF5 output via arcMS may be preferable when large filesize is acceptable Extends the arcMS columnar-conversion approach beyond Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE data to Thermo proprietary RAW files by first converting the vendor RAW file to open mzML with Proteowizard msconvert, then using arcMS mzML functions to write a long-format Apache Parquet table. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae160
skills.summary: Extends the arcMS columnar-conversion approach beyond Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE data to Thermo proprietary RAW files by first converting the vendor RAW file to open mzML with Proteowizard msconvert, then using arcMS mzML functions to write a long-format Apache Parquet table.

skills.description: Use when a compartmentalized community metabolic model (SBML, PyCoMo/COBRApy) predicts exchange fluxes or cross-feeding interactions absent from a reference analysis, suggesting a thermodynamically infeasible cycle.
skills.name: thermodynamically-infeasible-cycle-detection
skills.search_text: thermodynamically-infeasible-cycle-detection Use when a compartmentalized community metabolic model (SBML, PyCoMo/COBRApy) predicts exchange fluxes or cross-feeding interactions absent from a reference analysis, suggesting a thermodynamically infeasible cycle. The model is a single-organism model with no community cross-feeding compartment, so no inter-member formate/H2/CO2 loops can form The discrepancy between model prediction and reference analysis is due to differing model content or bounds, not internal loops — loopless FVA will not change the exchange fluxes Only maximum growth rate or feasible community composition is needed, not exchange/cross-feeding flux feasibility http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Detects thermodynamically infeasible internal cycles in PyCoMo-generated community metabolic models by contrasting standard FVA with loopless FVA (COBRApy), then traces the full reaction path of the isolated loop to explain spurious cross-feeding predictions such as the D. vulgaris H2 uptake artifact. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae153
skills.summary: Detects thermodynamically infeasible internal cycles in PyCoMo-generated community metabolic models by contrasting standard FVA with loopless FVA (COBRApy), then traces the full reaction path of the isolated loop to explain spurious cross-feeding predictions such as the D. vulgaris H2 uptake artifact.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is a single-organism model with no community cross-feeding compartment, so no inter-member formate/H2/CO2 loops can form The discrepancy between model prediction and reference analysis is due to differing model content or bounds, not internal loops — loopless FVA will not change the exchange fluxes Only maximum growth rate or feasible community composition is needed, not exchange/cross-feeding flux feasibility

skills.description: Use when a rule-based network expansion (e.g. Pickaxe over EcoCyc with JN1224min rules) yields more reactions than needed and thermodynamic plausibility should be used to prune physiologically infeasible reactions before metabolomics peak annotation.
skills.name: thermodynamics-filtering-of-generated-reactions
skills.search_text: thermodynamics-filtering-of-generated-reactions Use when a rule-based network expansion (e.g. Pickaxe over EcoCyc with JN1224min rules) yields more reactions than needed and thermodynamic plausibility should be used to prune physiologically infeasible reactions before metabolomics peak annotation. When reactions lack a computable Gibbs free energy (eQuilibrator returns nothing outside its prediction scope) — these cannot be judged and are retained by design When the goal is peak annotation without thermodynamic pruning, since Figure 6 shows thermodynamics plus metabolomics matches a similar number of unannotated peaks as metabolomics alone, so it adds no annotation gain in that setting When pruning by reaction feasibility (DeepRFC) is intended instead — that is a separate filter with its own skill http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Prunes a Pickaxe-generated reaction network by computing physiological Gibbs free energies with eQuilibrator and removing reactions whose ΔG′ exceeds 50 kJ/mol, while retaining reactions with no computable Gibbs energy. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05149-8
skills.summary: Prunes a Pickaxe-generated reaction network by computing physiological Gibbs free energies with eQuilibrator and removing reactions whose ΔG′ exceeds 50 kJ/mol, while retaining reactions with no computable Gibbs energy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reactions lack a computable Gibbs free energy (eQuilibrator returns nothing outside its prediction scope) — these cannot be judged and are retained by design When the goal is peak annotation without thermodynamic pruning, since Figure 6 shows thermodynamics plus metabolomics matches a similar number of unannotated peaks as metabolomics alone, so it adds no annotation gain in that setting When pruning by reaction feasibility (DeepRFC) is intended instead — that is a separate filter with its own skill

skills.name: three-level-kmeans-image-segmentation
skills.search_text: three-level-kmeans-image-segmentation Use when an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. 56Fe from a MassHunter batch) needs automatic background/ROI separation without hand-set thresholds, as in Pew2's segmentation tool. The input is already a segmented or labeled image — Pew2's segmentation step is meant to produce the mask from a raw elemental image. Supervised ROI definition where user-defined thresholds are required — use the manual thresholding path in Pew2 rather than the unsupervised k-means path. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Unsupervised three-level k-means segmentation of LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g. 56Fe) in Pew2 to isolate ROIs from background for downstream feature selection, without manual threshold tuning. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138

Supervised ROI definition where user-defined thresholds are required — use the manual thresholding path in Pew2 rather than the unsupervised k-means path.

skills.name: threshold-based-edge-filtering
skills.search_text: threshold-based-edge-filtering Use when you have a processed samples-by-metabolites intensity table from Viime and want a network diagram revealing correlated metabolite behavior, including cross-platform (MS/NMR fused) relationships. Your goal is a heatmap or volcano plot view of significant metabolites rather than pairwise metabolite-metabolite edge structure — use Viime's Heatmaps or volcano plot pages instead. The input table is still raw/unnormalized: Viime expects the workflow to pick up after preprocessing, imputation (MCAR/MNAR), normalization, transformation, and scaling, before correlation-based network construction. You need pairwise correlations between samples rather than between metabolites; the skill computes metabolite x metabolite correlations only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Build a metabolite correlation network by computing pairwise metabolite correlations (Pearson, Kendall Tau, or Spearman) on the Viime intensity table and drawing edges only for metabolite pairs whose absolute correlation exceeds a configurable minimum threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410

skills.description: Use when a binary classifier produces continuous scores (e.g. GNN reaction-pair predictions in MetDNA3) and you need a data-driven decision cutoff rather than the default 0.5, especially when class balance or asymmetric costs make a single operating point critical.
skills.name: threshold-optimization-weighted-youden-index
skills.search_text: threshold-optimization-weighted-youden-index Use when a binary classifier produces continuous scores (e.g. GNN reaction-pair predictions in MetDNA3) and you need a data-driven decision cutoff rather than the default 0.5, especially when class balance or asymmetric costs make a single operating point critical. The classifier outputs hard binary labels rather than continuous scores — no threshold sweep is meaningful. There is no labeled validation set to tune against (e.g. the curated MRN candidate set itself lacks clearly defined non-RPs, so the article explicitly refrains from reporting an FDR there). You need calibration of the score's probability meaning rather than a single operating-point cutoff (threshold optimization does not calibrate probabilities). http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Optimizes the decision threshold of a binary classifier (here, a GNN reaction-pair predictor) by sweeping candidate cutoffs on a validation set and selecting the threshold that maximizes the weighted Youden index, as done in MetDNA3 for its metabolic reaction network (MRN) model. It converts raw prediction scores into a fixed operating cutoff (reported as 0.7) used downstream for filtering candidate reaction pairs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Optimizes the decision threshold of a binary classifier (here, a GNN reaction-pair predictor) by sweeping candidate cutoffs on a validation set and selecting the threshold that maximizes the weighted Youden index, as done in MetDNA3 for its metabolic reaction network (MRN) model. It converts raw prediction scores into a fixed operating cutoff (reported as 0.7) used downstream for filtering candidate reaction pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The classifier outputs hard binary labels rather than continuous scores — no threshold sweep is meaningful. There is no labeled validation set to tune against (e.g. the curated MRN candidate set itself lacks clearly defined non-RPs, so the article explicitly refrains from reporting an FDR there). You need calibration of the score's probability meaning rather than a single operating-point cutoff (threshold optimization does not calibrate probabilities).

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a ΔCCS threshold when validating a CCS-prediction-based annotation filter over a set of standards with known PubChem candidate lists.
skills.name: threshold-sweep-statistics-analysis
skills.search_text: threshold-sweep-statistics-analysis Decision support for choosing a ΔCCS threshold when validating a CCS-prediction-based annotation filter over a set of standards with known PubChem candidate lists. When candidate lists have not been generated from PubChem at a defined mass tolerance (e.g. 10 ppm) — the sweep statistics are meaningless without a reproducible candidate pool. skills.summary: Sweep a ΔCCS filtering threshold from 0% to 15% while recording the fraction of true annotations retained and the median fraction of candidate structures filtered, to quantify the sensitivity-specificity trade-off of CCS-based metabolite annotation filtering.

skills.description: Use when HRMS data has been converted to Parquet with arcMS and you need a TIC (or similar chromatogram) without loading the full profile-mode file into RAM, e.g. for Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE acquisitions with ion mobility.
skills.name: tic-aggregation-from-arrow-datasets
skills.search_text: tic-aggregation-from-arrow-datasets Use when HRMS data has been converted to Parquet with arcMS and you need a TIC (or similar chromatogram) without loading the full profile-mode file into RAM, e.g. for Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE acquisitions with ion mobility. The data is still in Waters UNIFI or proprietary format and has not yet been converted to Parquet/HDF5 with arcMS — convert it first. You need the full point-level dataset in memory for custom modeling, not aggregated chromatograms/spectra — read_parquet() may be more appropriate despite the ~1.9 Gb footprint. The file is HDF5 output from arcMS (ms1/ms2 datasets read via rhdf5), where the Arrow dataset workflow does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Compute total ion chromatograms (TIC) from arcMS-converted Parquet HRMS data using Apache Arrow on-disk queries (filter mslevel == 1, group by rt, sum intensity), avoiding full in-memory loading. This exploits Parquet columnar storage so a ~1.9 Gb dataset yields only ~64 Kb of aggregated chromatogram data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae160
skills.summary: Compute total ion chromatograms (TIC) from arcMS-converted Parquet HRMS data using Apache Arrow on-disk queries (filter mslevel == 1, group by rt, sum intensity), avoiding full in-memory loading. This exploits Parquet columnar storage so a ~1.9 Gb dataset yields only ~64 Kb of aggregated chromatogram data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is still in Waters UNIFI or proprietary format and has not yet been converted to Parquet/HDF5 with arcMS — convert it first. You need the full point-level dataset in memory for custom modeling, not aggregated chromatograms/spectra — read_parquet() may be more appropriate despite the ~1.9 Gb footprint. The file is HDF5 output from arcMS (ms1/ms2 datasets read via rhdf5), where the Arrow dataset workflow does not apply.
