Input is not a pixel-by-ion peak table matrix with spatial coordinates (e.g. already a feature table, raw spectra, or imaging file without a pixel grid) No user-annotated tissue and background regions exist, so the two pixel groups required for the rank-sum comparison cannot be formed The goal is noise ion or isotopic/adduct ion filtering (other SMQVP modules), not background pixel removal http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Identifies spatial-metabolomics ion peaks that are significantly enriched in user-delineated tissue regions versus background regions using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (fold change > 1, p < 0.05). These tissue-enriched ions are the basis of SMQVP's Process 2 background pixel removal on AFADESI mouse brain data. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Identifies spatial-metabolomics ion peaks that are significantly enriched in user-delineated tissue regions versus background regions using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (fold change > 1, p < 0.05). These tissue-enriched ions are the basis of SMQVP's Process 2 background pixel removal on AFADESI mouse brain data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a pixel-by-ion peak table matrix with spatial coordinates (e.g. already a feature table, raw spectra, or imaging file without a pixel grid) No user-annotated tissue and background regions exist, so the two pixel groups required for the rank-sum comparison cannot be formed The goal is noise ion or isotopic/adduct ion filtering (other SMQVP modules), not background pixel removal

skills.description: Use when you have a peak table matrix of pixels by ion intensities with spatial coordinates and need to quantify the proportion of ions with higher expression in a tissue region versus background, as in SMQVP's QVP3 module.
skills.name: tissue-enriched-ion-proportion-analysis
skills.search_text: tissue-enriched-ion-proportion-analysis Use when you have a peak table matrix of pixels by ion intensities with spatial coordinates and need to quantify the proportion of ions with higher expression in a tissue region versus background, as in SMQVP's QVP3 module. Input is already a preprocessed or feature-summarized matrix without per-pixel intensities, so tissue vs background pixel groups cannot be compared per ion The goal is noise ion filtering or background pixel removal rather than quantifying the proportion of tissue-enriched ions Data lacks spatial coordinates or delineated tissue/background regions, so the rank-sum grouping cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Classifies each ion in an AFADESI spatial metabolomics peak table as tissue-enriched via a Wilcoxon rank-sum test between tissue and background pixel groups (fold change > 1, p < 0.05), reproducing SMQVP's QVP3 ion expression proportion metric (37% of 2,654 ions in the mouse brain dataset). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo15060354
skills.summary: Classifies each ion in an AFADESI spatial metabolomics peak table as tissue-enriched via a Wilcoxon rank-sum test between tissue and background pixel groups (fold change > 1, p < 0.05), reproducing SMQVP's QVP3 ion expression proportion metric (37% of 2,654 ions in the mouse brain dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a preprocessed or feature-summarized matrix without per-pixel intensities, so tissue vs background pixel groups cannot be compared per ion The goal is noise ion filtering or background pixel removal rather than quantifying the proportion of tissue-enriched ions Data lacks spatial coordinates or delineated tissue/background regions, so the rank-sum grouping cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when building or extending the tissueMASST reference index: public MS/MS files must be tagged with tissue-associated metadata (organism, tissue, disease status) before spectral search queries can be mapped to biological context.
skills.name: tissue-metadata-annotation
skills.search_text: tissue-metadata-annotation Use when building or extending the tissueMASST reference index: public MS/MS files must be tagged with tissue-associated metadata (organism, tissue, disease status) before spectral search queries can be mapped to biological context. When the goal is to search a query spectrum against existing tissueMASST data (spectral search), not to build or extend the underlying tissue-annotated reference database. When input MS/MS files already carry complete tissue-associated metadata and only need spectral scoring — annotation is done; proceed directly to scoring. When the reference data is not public MS/MS from the three supported repositories (e.g., proprietary or non-public datasets); tissueMASST's annotation pipeline assumes MassIVE/MetaboLights/Workbench provenance. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assemble and annotate a tissue-aware MS/MS reference database for tissueMASST by collecting public MS/MS files from GNPS/MassIVE, MetaboLights, and Metabolomics Workbench and attaching tissue-associated metadata so query spectra can be matched back to organism, tissue, and disease-status context. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Assemble and annotate a tissue-aware MS/MS reference database for tissueMASST by collecting public MS/MS files from GNPS/MassIVE, MetaboLights, and Metabolomics Workbench and attaching tissue-associated metadata so query spectra can be matched back to organism, tissue, and disease-status context.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to search a query spectrum against existing tissueMASST data (spectral search), not to build or extend the underlying tissue-annotated reference database. When input MS/MS files already carry complete tissue-associated metadata and only need spectral scoring — annotation is done; proceed directly to scoring. When the reference data is not public MS/MS from the three supported repositories (e.g., proprietary or non-public datasets); tissueMASST's annotation pipeline assumes MassIVE/MetaboLights/Workbench provenance.

skills.description: Use when a processed MALDI/imzML spatial metabolomics dataset (e.g. murine urinary bladder) must be segmented into anatomical regions and each cluster annotated using known region-defining lipid m/z markers plus differentially expressed m/z peaks.
skills.name: tissue-region-annotation-from-lipid-co-localisation
skills.search_text: tissue-region-annotation-from-lipid-co-localisation Use when a processed MALDI/imzML spatial metabolomics dataset (e.g. murine urinary bladder) must be segmented into anatomical regions and each cluster annotated using known region-defining lipid m/z markers plus differentially expressed m/z peaks. Input is a feature/annotation table or the goal is m/z metabolite annotation refinement rather than spatial region annotation — use SpaMTP's annotation functions (AnnotateBigData, RefineLipids, CalculateAnnotationStatistics) instead The data has not yet been processed into imzML/SpaMTP Seurat object form, so no per-pixel m/z matrix exists to cluster High-resolution instrument data suited to METASPACE/pySM annotation workflows, which the article notes are 'optimised for SM data generated via high resolution instruments' and 'do not yet apply to most data obtained with time-of-flight (TOF) analysers' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates spatial-metabolomics tissue regions by combining metabolite-PCA-based Louvain clustering (SpaMTP/Seurat) with known region-defining lipid masses (e.g. PC(34:1) m/z-798.541, SM(34:1) m/z-741.5037, PE(38:1) m/z-812.5566) and EdgeR-based differential m/z testing via FindAllDEMs. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.31.621429
skills.summary: Annotates spatial-metabolomics tissue regions by combining metabolite-PCA-based Louvain clustering (SpaMTP/Seurat) with known region-defining lipid masses (e.g. PC(34:1) m/z-798.541, SM(34:1) m/z-741.5037, PE(38:1) m/z-812.5566) and EdgeR-based differential m/z testing via FindAllDEMs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature/annotation table or the goal is m/z metabolite annotation refinement rather than spatial region annotation — use SpaMTP's annotation functions (AnnotateBigData, RefineLipids, CalculateAnnotationStatistics) instead The data has not yet been processed into imzML/SpaMTP Seurat object form, so no per-pixel m/z matrix exists to cluster High-resolution instrument data suited to METASPACE/pySM annotation workflows, which the article notes are 'optimised for SM data generated via high resolution instruments' and 'do not yet apply to most data obtained with time-of-flight (TOF) analysers'

skills.description: Use when a labeled metabolomics feature table (samples x features with tissue/group labels) needs a check that one group forms a distinct cluster in unsupervised PCA space, e.g. buccal gland vs. other tissues.
skills.name: tissue-separation-verification-in-ordination-space
skills.search_text: tissue-separation-verification-in-ordination-space Use when a labeled metabolomics feature table (samples x features with tissue/group labels) needs a check that one group forms a distinct cluster in unsupervised PCA space, e.g. buccal gland vs. other tissues. The input is raw instrument data (e.g. mzML/NetCDF) rather than a processed feature table — peak picking and alignment must precede PCA A supervised group-difference test is required — PCA is unsupervised and only demonstrates visual/structural separation, not statistical significance The question concerns feature-level relationships (e.g. metabolite annotation or clustering) rather than sample-level group separation http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Verify that a tissue of interest separates from other tissues in ordination space by running PCA on a variance-stabilized, autoscaled LC-MS feature table (e.g. the lamprey spatial metabolomics dataset, 94 samples across 14 tissues, negative ion mode) and inspecting the PC1-vs-PC2 score plot colored by tissue, as demonstrated with MetaboReport. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Verify that a tissue of interest separates from other tissues in ordination space by running PCA on a variance-stabilized, autoscaled LC-MS feature table (e.g. the lamprey spatial metabolomics dataset, 94 samples across 14 tissues, negative ion mode) and inspecting the PC1-vs-PC2 score plot colored by tissue, as demonstrated with MetaboReport.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw instrument data (e.g. mzML/NetCDF) rather than a processed feature table — peak picking and alignment must precede PCA A supervised group-difference test is required — PCA is unsupervised and only demonstrates visual/structural separation, not statistical significance The question concerns feature-level relationships (e.g. metabolite annotation or clustering) rather than sample-level group separation

skills.description: Use when a negative-ion-mode LC-MS feature table spans multiple tissue groups and you need features with extreme, statistically controlled enrichment in one tissue versus every other group.
skills.name: tissue-specific-metabolite-enrichment-filtering
skills.search_text: tissue-specific-metabolite-enrichment-filtering Use when a negative-ion-mode LC-MS feature table spans multiple tissue groups and you need features with extreme, statistically controlled enrichment in one tissue versus every other group. The goal is generic between-tissue differential abundance at moderate effect sizes (e.g. 2-fold, P<0.05) rather than extreme single-tissue enrichment Input data is raw mass-spectrometry signal that still requires MetaboReport's preprocessing step — this skill starts from an already-processed feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Identifies mass features drastically enriched in one tissue versus all others in an LC-MS spatial metabolomics dataset by combining between-group statistical testing with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment and an extreme fold-change cutoff (e.g. >1000-fold, FDR P<0.001), as demonstrated for 182 buccal-gland-enriched features in lamprey. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae373
skills.summary: Identifies mass features drastically enriched in one tissue versus all others in an LC-MS spatial metabolomics dataset by combining between-group statistical testing with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment and an extreme fold-change cutoff (e.g. >1000-fold, FDR P<0.001), as demonstrated for 182 buccal-gland-enriched features in lamprey.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is generic between-tissue differential abundance at moderate effect sizes (e.g. 2-fold, P<0.05) rather than extreme single-tissue enrichment Input data is raw mass-spectrometry signal that still requires MetaboReport's preprocessing step — this skill starts from an already-processed feature table

skills.description: Use when a list of statistically significant up/down-regulated ion m/z values from an MSI region comparison needs putative metabolite IDs restricted to those plausible for the imaged tissue.
skills.name: tissue-specific-metabolite-filtering
skills.search_text: tissue-specific-metabolite-filtering Use when a list of statistically significant up/down-regulated ion m/z values from an MSI region comparison needs putative metabolite IDs restricted to those plausible for the imaged tissue. When the ion list has not been filtered by rMSIKeyIon first — annotation of an unfiltered peak table will not target differentially regulated ions between ROIs When metabolites from any biological origin are acceptable and no tissue-specificity constraint is desired When mass accuracy exceeds the 20 ppm tolerance achievable here (e.g., low-resolution data) — matches would be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Annotates up- or down-regulated ion lists from rMSIKeyIon ROI comparisons by matching m/z values against HMDB 4.0 with common positive-mode adducts at a 20 ppm tolerance, then retaining only metabolites biologically plausible for the tissue under study (e.g., liver). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9080162
skills.summary: Annotates up- or down-regulated ion lists from rMSIKeyIon ROI comparisons by matching m/z values against HMDB 4.0 with common positive-mode adducts at a 20 ppm tolerance, then retaining only metabolites biologically plausible for the tissue under study (e.g., liver).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the ion list has not been filtered by rMSIKeyIon first — annotation of an unfiltered peak table will not target differentially regulated ions between ROIs When metabolites from any biological origin are acceptable and no tissue-specificity constraint is desired When mass accuracy exceeds the 20 ppm tolerance achievable here (e.g., low-resolution data) — matches would be unreliable

skills.description: Use when a LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g., a 1.5 mm TMA core imaged at 10 µm beam, 40 µm/s) needs automatic tissue-vs-background separation without manual threshold tuning, using multi-level k-means segmentation.
skills.name: tma-core-background-removal
skills.search_text: tma-core-background-removal Use when a LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g., a 1.5 mm TMA core imaged at 10 µm beam, 40 µm/s) needs automatic tissue-vs-background separation without manual threshold tuning, using multi-level k-means segmentation. The elemental image already contains a clean binary tissue mask or the user prefers manual thresholding on a clearly separated signal. The dataset is not LA-ICP-MS line-by-line data importable into Pew2 (e.g., already a preprocessed feature table or a non-imaging spectral file). Only a single cluster level is needed and simpler thresholding (mean or Otsu) would suffice, making multi-level k-means unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Isolates regions of interest (ROIs) from background in LA-ICP-MS elemental images—such as a 1.5 mm pancreatic adenocarcinoma tissue microarray core—by applying multi-level k-means (plus mean or Otsu thresholding) segmentation within Pew2, then masking the elemental data (e.g., 56Fe) to the highest k level for background removal and feature selection. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02138
skills.summary: Isolates regions of interest (ROIs) from background in LA-ICP-MS elemental images—such as a 1.5 mm pancreatic adenocarcinoma tissue microarray core—by applying multi-level k-means (plus mean or Otsu thresholding) segmentation within Pew2, then masking the elemental data (e.g., 56Fe) to the highest k level for background removal and feature selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The elemental image already contains a clean binary tissue mask or the user prefers manual thresholding on a clearly separated signal. The dataset is not LA-ICP-MS line-by-line data importable into Pew2 (e.g., already a preprocessed feature table or a non-imaging spectral file). Only a single cluster level is needed and simpler thresholding (mean or Otsu) would suffice, making multi-level k-means unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how many compounds in a spectral library are new relative to open (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA) and commercial (mzCloud, NIST23) libraries, and visualize the overlap pattern as an UpSet plot and TMAP projection.
skills.name: tmap-structural-similarity-projection
skills.search_text: tmap-structural-similarity-projection Use when you must quantify how many compounds in a spectral library are new relative to open (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA) and commercial (mzCloud, NIST23) libraries, and visualize the overlap pattern as an UpSet plot and TMAP projection. You need full stereochemical identity counts — first-InChIKey-block (14-character) truncation deliberately conflates stereoisomers, which is not the right granularity for stereo-specific questions. Your goal is spectral (peak-level) library matching rather than compound-list coverage comparison. The reference library structures lack InChIKeys or resolvable identifiers, so first-block truncation and set-difference cannot be applied consistently. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compares compound coverage of the MSn Lib spectral library against reference libraries (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA, mzCloud, NIST23) by truncating InChIKeys to their first 14-character block, computing set-difference overlap counts, and projecting the shared/unique chemical space as an UpSet intersection matrix and a TMAP layout over first-InChIKey-block classes. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0
skills.summary: Compares compound coverage of the MSn Lib spectral library against reference libraries (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA, mzCloud, NIST23) by truncating InChIKeys to their first 14-character block, computing set-difference overlap counts, and projecting the shared/unique chemical space as an UpSet intersection matrix and a TMAP layout over first-InChIKey-block classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need full stereochemical identity counts — first-InChIKey-block (14-character) truncation deliberately conflates stereoisomers, which is not the right granularity for stereo-specific questions. Your goal is spectral (peak-level) library matching rather than compound-list coverage comparison. The reference library structures lack InChIKeys or resolvable identifiers, so first-block truncation and set-difference cannot be applied consistently.

skills.description: Use when samples have been vectorized into a MEMO MS2-fingerprint matrix and you need an RT-agnostic tree layout to explore clustering, overlay annotations, or cross-check UMAP/PCoA groupings of chemodiverse samples.
skills.name: tmap-tree-visualization-of-metabolomics-samples
skills.search_text: tmap-tree-visualization-of-metabolomics-samples Use when samples have been vectorized into a MEMO MS2-fingerprint matrix and you need an RT-agnostic tree layout to explore clustering, overlay annotations, or cross-check UMAP/PCoA groupings of chemodiverse samples. Input is raw MS/MS spectra or an unaligned feature table — MEMO fingerprints must be counted and aligned first Samples are not chemodiverse and overlap well with retention-time alignment available — a standard feature-based ordination may be more appropriate You need intensity-aware distance metrics (e.g., Bray-Curtis on a feature table) rather than MS2-occurrence-based sample comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds a TMAP tree layout of metabolomics samples from an aligned MEMO matrix, offering a retention-time-agnostic, structure-aware alternative to UMAP/MDS/PCoA scatter ordination for exploring chemodiverse LC-MS/MS datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Builds a TMAP tree layout of metabolomics samples from an aligned MEMO matrix, offering a retention-time-agnostic, structure-aware alternative to UMAP/MDS/PCoA scatter ordination for exploring chemodiverse LC-MS/MS datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS/MS spectra or an unaligned feature table — MEMO fingerprints must be counted and aligned first Samples are not chemodiverse and overlap well with retention-time alignment available — a standard feature-based ordination may be more appropriate You need intensity-aware distance metrics (e.g., Bray-Curtis on a feature table) rather than MS2-occurrence-based sample comparison

skills.description: Use when a MEMO sample-by-MS2-fingerprint matrix has been aligned and you must visualize whether samples cluster retention-time-agnostically, including across different LC gradients and MS instruments.
skills.name: tmap-umap-embedding-visualization-of-sample-vectors
skills.search_text: tmap-umap-embedding-visualization-of-sample-vectors Use when a MEMO sample-by-MS2-fingerprint matrix has been aligned and you must visualize whether samples cluster retention-time-agnostically, including across different LC gradients and MS instruments. The input is raw LC-MS/MS spectra or an unaligned feature table — MEMO fingerprints must first be computed and aligned before embedding. The analysis goal requires retention-time-aware or feature-alignment-based sample comparison rather than RT-agnostic MS2-fingerprint clustering. Only two or very few samples are available, where MDS/PCoA or heatmap-style views may be more informative than UMAP/TMAP embeddings. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Projection of aligned MS2-based sample vectors (MEMO matrix rows) into 2D embeddings using UMAP and TMAP to visually assess sample clustering across chemodiverse LC-MS/MS datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Projection of aligned MS2-based sample vectors (MEMO matrix rows) into 2D embeddings using UMAP and TMAP to visually assess sample clustering across chemodiverse LC-MS/MS datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw LC-MS/MS spectra or an unaligned feature table — MEMO fingerprints must first be computed and aligned before embedding. The analysis goal requires retention-time-aware or feature-alignment-based sample comparison rather than RT-agnostic MS2-fingerprint clustering. Only two or very few samples are available, where MDS/PCoA or heatmap-style views may be more informative than UMAP/TMAP embeddings.

skills.description: Use when recomputing or verifying dysregulated-metabolite statistics from an eRah compound table in which one metabolite occurs in several TMS-derivatized rows (e.g., leucine 1TMS/2TMS) and two-group class comparisons are required.
skills.name: tms-derivative-metabolite-accounting
skills.search_text: tms-derivative-metabolite-accounting Use when recomputing or verifying dysregulated-metabolite statistics from an eRah compound table in which one metabolite occurs in several TMS-derivatized rows (e.g., leucine 1TMS/2TMS) and two-group class comparisons are required. Input is raw GC-TOF MS profile data rather than an eRah-aligned identification table — deconvolution and alignment (deconvolveComp, alignComp) must be run first before metabolite-level accounting is possible The comparison involves more than two sample classes — the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney rank-sum test used in this workflow is defined only for a two-group HIAE vs CTR comparison The metabolite table lacks TMS-derivative annotations, so derivatized rows cannot be attributed to a parent metabolite and derivative-level accounting cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Correctly accounts for GC/MS metabolites that appear as multiple TMS-derivative rows (e.g., leucine 1TMS and leucine 2TMS) when recomputing percent-variation and Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney statistics for dysregulated metabolites identified by eRah in the HIAE vs. control serum comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.6b02927
skills.summary: Correctly accounts for GC/MS metabolites that appear as multiple TMS-derivative rows (e.g., leucine 1TMS and leucine 2TMS) when recomputing percent-variation and Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney statistics for dysregulated metabolites identified by eRah in the HIAE vs. control serum comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw GC-TOF MS profile data rather than an eRah-aligned identification table — deconvolution and alignment (deconvolveComp, alignComp) must be run first before metabolite-level accounting is possible The comparison involves more than two sample classes — the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney rank-sum test used in this workflow is defined only for a two-group HIAE vs CTR comparison The metabolite table lacks TMS-derivative annotations, so derivatized rows cannot be attributed to a parent metabolite and derivative-level accounting cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when preparing GC-EI MS chromatograms (netCDF or mzXML) for eRah deconvolution and column bleed or derivatization-reagent fragments (e.g. m/z 73:75, 147:149, 35:69) would otherwise seed spurious deconvolved compounds.
skills.name: tms-fragment-mz-exclusion
skills.search_text: tms-fragment-mz-exclusion Use when preparing GC-EI MS chromatograms (netCDF or mzXML) for eRah deconvolution and column bleed or derivatization-reagent fragments (e.g. m/z 73:75, 147:149, 35:69) would otherwise seed spurious deconvolved compounds. When the m/z range to exclude overlaps analyte-informative fragments required for spectral library matching, excluding it would degrade compound identification. When data are not GC-MS chromatograms undergoing eRah deconvolution — the exclusion is a setDecPar parameter of eRah's CMLC/OSD pipeline, not a general filtering step for other peak-picking tools like XCMS or MetAlign. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Excludes fragment ion m/z ranges associated with column bleed, derivatization reagents, and background interference from eRah's spectral deconvolution, using setDecPar(avoid.processing.mz=...) so CMLC/OSD only resolve genuine compound spectra rather than artifacts. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.6b02927
skills.summary: Excludes fragment ion m/z ranges associated with column bleed, derivatization reagents, and background interference from eRah's spectral deconvolution, using setDecPar(avoid.processing.mz=...) so CMLC/OSD only resolve genuine compound spectra rather than artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the m/z range to exclude overlaps analyte-informative fragments required for spectral library matching, excluding it would degrade compound identification. When data are not GC-MS chromatograms undergoing eRah deconvolution — the exclusion is a setDecPar parameter of eRah's CMLC/OSD pipeline, not a general filtering step for other peak-picking tools like XCMS or MetAlign.

skills.description: Use when metabolomics intensities contain values censored at detection limits (requiring Tobit) or repeated measures requiring mixed effects, and per-metabolite effect estimates with FDR-corrected p-values are needed.
skills.name: tobit-censored-data-regression
skills.search_text: tobit-censored-data-regression Use when metabolomics intensities contain values censored at detection limits (requiring Tobit) or repeated measures requiring mixed effects, and per-metabolite effect estimates with FDR-corrected p-values are needed. The input is already a processed statistical result table rather than raw metabolite intensities with sample metadata The outcome is not censored and there are no repeated measures, so a plain fixed-effects lm suffices without the Tobit/mixed-effect machinery The goal is untargeted feature extraction or pooled QC filtration from raw mass spectrometry files rather than statistical regression on an existing feature table http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Fits one regression model per metabolite from a long-format metabolomics feature table using the GetFeatistics regression mechanism, selecting lm for fixed effects, lmer for mixed-effects longitudinal data, or Tobit regression (via AER) when values are censored at limits of detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Fits one regression model per metabolite from a long-format metabolomics feature table using the GetFeatistics regression mechanism, selecting lm for fixed effects, lmer for mixed-effects longitudinal data, or Tobit regression (via AER) when values are censored at limits of detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed statistical result table rather than raw metabolite intensities with sample metadata The outcome is not censored and there are no repeated measures, so a plain fixed-effects lm suffices without the Tobit/mixed-effect machinery The goal is untargeted feature extraction or pooled QC filtration from raw mass spectrometry files rather than statistical regression on an existing feature table

skills.description: Use when metabolite intensity values are censored because they fall below/above limits of detection and you need regression associations that correctly handle censoring rather than discarding or imputing those values.
skills.name: tobit-censored-regression-with-detection-limits
skills.search_text: tobit-censored-regression-with-detection-limits Use when metabolite intensity values are censored because they fall below/above limits of detection and you need regression associations that correctly handle censoring rather than discarding or imputing those values. Intensity data contain no censored values (all measurements within the linear detection range) — the fixed-effects linear-model mode of gentab_lm_long is the simpler correct choice The goal is feature extraction or QC-based feature filtration from raw MS data (e.g. with XCMS or patRoon import) rather than statistical association modelling Input is a raw, unprocessed feature table — pre-processing (missing values, normality) must precede the regression step http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit Tobit regression models for metabolomics intensities that are censored at detection limits, using the GetFeatistics package (which wraps AER's tobit) alongside its fixed-effects and mixed-effects regression modes, returning effect estimates, CIs, and p-values per molecule–covariate pair. metabolomics/v3 10.1515/jib-2025-0047
skills.summary: Fit Tobit regression models for metabolomics intensities that are censored at detection limits, using the GetFeatistics package (which wraps AER's tobit) alongside its fixed-effects and mixed-effects regression modes, returning effect estimates, CIs, and p-values per molecule–covariate pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Intensity data contain no censored values (all measurements within the linear detection range) — the fixed-effects linear-model mode of gentab_lm_long is the simpler correct choice The goal is feature extraction or QC-based feature filtration from raw MS data (e.g. with XCMS or patRoon import) rather than statistical association modelling Input is a raw, unprocessed feature table — pre-processing (missing values, normality) must precede the regression step

skills.description: Use when processing peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC peak tables from complex natural product mixtures prior to spin system construction and filtering out solvent, water, and illegitimate-region artifacts is needed.
skills.name: tocsy-hsqc-spectral-filtering
skills.search_text: tocsy-hsqc-spectral-filtering Use when processing peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC peak tables from complex natural product mixtures prior to spin system construction and filtering out solvent, water, and illegitimate-region artifacts is needed. The target compound classes (e.g. sterols, low molecular weight isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) have exclusively shielded 1H signals — the < 2.5 ppm TOCSY quadrant exclusion precludes their analysis unless the user supplies reference spectra outside this pipeline's scope Input is already a cleaned, spin-system feature table (e.g. spin_system_features.csv) rather than raw peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC tables The data are 1D or heteronuclear experiments other than paired phase-sensitive TOCSY/HSQC, since filters rely on the TOCSY/HSQC 1H correspondence http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Preprocessing filter cascade that cleans peak-picked 2D TOCSY and HSQC tables (solvent/water bands, illegitimate HSQC regions, TOCSY shielded quadrant, orphaned TOCSY signals) before spin system graph construction in the MADByTE platform. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Preprocessing filter cascade that cleans peak-picked 2D TOCSY and HSQC tables (solvent/water bands, illegitimate HSQC regions, TOCSY shielded quadrant, orphaned TOCSY signals) before spin system graph construction in the MADByTE platform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target compound classes (e.g. sterols, low molecular weight isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) have exclusively shielded 1H signals — the < 2.5 ppm TOCSY quadrant exclusion precludes their analysis unless the user supplies reference spectra outside this pipeline's scope Input is already a cleaned, spin-system feature table (e.g. spin_system_features.csv) rather than raw peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC tables The data are 1D or heteronuclear experiments other than paired phase-sensitive TOCSY/HSQC, since filters rely on the TOCSY/HSQC 1H correspondence

skills.description: Use when processing peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC tables from complex mixture NMR (e.g. MADByTE) and f1/f2 chemical shifts are asymmetric, so TOCSY data must be symmetrized and filtered before spin system construction.
skills.name: tocsy-symmetrization
skills.search_text: tocsy-symmetrization Use when processing peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC tables from complex mixture NMR (e.g. MADByTE) and f1/f2 chemical shifts are asymmetric, so TOCSY data must be symmetrized and filtered before spin system construction. The input is already a spin system feature table or similarity network — symmetrization operates on raw TOCSY peak lists only The sample's compounds contain exclusively shielded 1H signals (e.g. sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) — the <2.5 ppm quadrant exclusion precludes their analysis Absolute-value HSQC data is being used without proper phase-sensitive acquisition, since this workflow was designed around phase-sensitive HSQC peak lists http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Symmetrize phase-sensitive 2D TOCSY spectra by correcting f1 chemical shifts against the corresponding f2 values, then exclude the shielded quadrant (<2.5 ppm) and TOCSY signals lacking HSQC counterparts, before building spin system graphs in MADByTE. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.0c01076
skills.summary: Symmetrize phase-sensitive 2D TOCSY spectra by correcting f1 chemical shifts against the corresponding f2 values, then exclude the shielded quadrant (<2.5 ppm) and TOCSY signals lacking HSQC counterparts, before building spin system graphs in MADByTE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a spin system feature table or similarity network — symmetrization operates on raw TOCSY peak lists only The sample's compounds contain exclusively shielded 1H signals (e.g. sterols, low MW isoprenoids, lipids, volatile terpenes) — the <2.5 ppm quadrant exclusion precludes their analysis Absolute-value HSQC data is being used without proper phase-sensitive acquisition, since this workflow was designed around phase-sensitive HSQC peak lists

skills.description: Use when scoring lipid species predictions against labels for held-out MS2 spectra and you need both strict whole-sequence accuracy and token/component-level diagnostics rather than a single overall match rate.
skills.name: token-level-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: token-level-accuracy-evaluation Use when scoring lipid species predictions against labels for held-out MS2 spectra and you need both strict whole-sequence accuracy and token/component-level diagnostics rather than a single overall match rate. When the model output is a single class label rather than a multi-token lipid shorthand sequence — a plain accuracy metric suffices and token decomposition is meaningless. When evaluating spectral similarity (e.g. cosine/matching scores between spectra) rather than identity of the decoded lipid notation string. When the input spectra are raw profile data that has not been preprocessed (smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, base peak normalization, m/z 50–1600 trimming) — token evaluation presupposes preprocessed peak lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates transformer lipid-identification predictions by decomposing the lipid shorthand notation into tokens (headgroup, fatty acid side chains, adduct) and scoring exact token-sequence matches, plus per-token component accuracy, per-lipid-class precision/recall/F1, and a confusion matrix. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.07.617094
skills.summary: Evaluates transformer lipid-identification predictions by decomposing the lipid shorthand notation into tokens (headgroup, fatty acid side chains, adduct) and scoring exact token-sequence matches, plus per-token component accuracy, per-lipid-class precision/recall/F1, and a confusion matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the model output is a single class label rather than a multi-token lipid shorthand sequence — a plain accuracy metric suffices and token decomposition is meaningless. When evaluating spectral similarity (e.g. cosine/matching scores between spectra) rather than identity of the decoded lipid notation string. When the input spectra are raw profile data that has not been preprocessed (smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, base peak normalization, m/z 50–1600 trimming) — token evaluation presupposes preprocessed peak lists.

skills.summary: Scores LipiDetective lipid species predictions at token level, treating each shorthand-notation token (headgroup, fatty acid chains, adduct) as a unit and reporting strict total prediction accuracy (all tokens correct) alongside lenient lipid component accuracy (correct tokens / total tokens).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw profile spectra (mzML) that still need smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking, base peak normalization, and trimming to 50–1600 m/z before inference Scoring is needed at the peak/fragment level (e.g. Alex123 fragment matching) rather than at the lipid species token level The task is blank/no-lipid detection, where the expected output is the end-of-sequence token rather than a scored species prediction

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics concentration matrix (e.g., introgression-line metabolite profiles) contains missing values and must be completed before computing pairwise correlations such as the |r| >= 0.3, p <= 0.01 Metabolite CN edges.
skills.name: tomato-pericarp-metabolomics-data-handling
skills.search_text: tomato-pericarp-metabolomics-data-handling Use when a metabolomics concentration matrix (e.g., introgression-line metabolite profiles) contains missing values and must be completed before computing pairwise correlations such as the |r| >= 0.3, p <= 0.01 Metabolite CN edges. The matrix already contains no missing values — imputation is unnecessary and would distort observed concentrations The goal is graph auralization or M5 classifier training on an existing Metabolite CN — this skill only covers upstream preprocessing of the raw profiles matrix The dataset is not a metabolite concentration matrix (e.g., it is a pathway/compound list from TomatoCyc or MetaCyc) http://edamontology.org/topic_3383 Preprocessing routine that prepares the tomato pericarp metabolite profiles matrix (2001, 2003, 2004 harvesting seasons) for metabolite correlation-network construction by normalizing data at sample and metabolite levels and imputing missing values with probabilistic PCA from the pcaMethods package in R/RStudio. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2410.22030
skills.summary: Preprocessing routine that prepares the tomato pericarp metabolite profiles matrix (2001, 2003, 2004 harvesting seasons) for metabolite correlation-network construction by normalizing data at sample and metabolite levels and imputing missing values with probabilistic PCA from the pcaMethods package in R/RStudio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix already contains no missing values — imputation is unnecessary and would distort observed concentrations The goal is graph auralization or M5 classifier training on an existing Metabolite CN — this skill only covers upstream preprocessing of the raw profiles matrix The dataset is not a metabolite concentration matrix (e.g., it is a pathway/compound list from TomatoCyc or MetaCyc)

skills.search_text: tonsil-b-cell-population-subsetting Use when a scSpaMet single-cell feature table (protein + co-registered SIMS metabolite intensities) from tonsil tissue must be narrowed to germinal-center B cells before pseudotime or metabolite-trajectory analysis. The tissue is lung adenocarcinoma or endometrium rather than tonsil — GC B-cell markers are not the relevant gating scheme The input is raw IMC/SIMS images that have not yet passed single-cell segmentation and intensity extraction (notebooks 03/04) The downstream goal is metabolite-competition or spatial-interaction analysis across all cell types, not lineage-specific trajectory analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Isolate germinal-center B-cell populations from scSpaMet single-cell protein-metabolite intensity matrices of healthy human tonsil tissue using the IMC protein marker panel, so that downstream trajectory (DPT/Palantir pseudotime) and metabolite-projection analyses operate only on the relevant cell lineage. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43917-5
skills.summary: Isolate germinal-center B-cell populations from scSpaMet single-cell protein-metabolite intensity matrices of healthy human tonsil tissue using the IMC protein marker panel, so that downstream trajectory (DPT/Palantir pseudotime) and metabolite-projection analyses operate only on the relevant cell lineage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue is lung adenocarcinoma or endometrium rather than tonsil — GC B-cell markers are not the relevant gating scheme The input is raw IMC/SIMS images that have not yet passed single-cell segmentation and intensity extraction (notebooks 03/04) The downstream goal is metabolite-competition or spatial-interaction analysis across all cell types, not lineage-specific trajectory analysis

skills.description: Use when benchmarking chemical formula identification from tandem MS/MS spectra against published baselines (e.g., reproducing FIDDLE's 88.3% top-1 / 93.6% top-5 accuracy on NIST23 against SIRIUS and BUDDY).
skills.name: top-k-accuracy-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-accuracy-benchmark-evaluation Use when benchmarking chemical formula identification from tandem MS/MS spectra against published baselines (e.g., reproducing FIDDLE's 88.3% top-1 / 93.6% top-5 accuracy on NIST23 against SIRIUS and BUDDY). Spectra contain chimeric (co-eluting) compounds — FIDDLE's performance decreases as spectral mixing increases, so benchmark numbers will not match clean-spectra expectations Precursor m/z values exceed 1500 — the m/z range is confined to (0, 1500] due to the rarity of spectra above that value Molecules contain rare atoms outside C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K, or exceed 300 total atoms — they are outside the training/model scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Evaluates molecular formula prediction methods (FIDDLE, SIRIUS, BUDDY) on held-out NIST23-only test spectra by computing top-1 and top-5 (and higher-K) accuracies per instrument type (Q-TOF vs. Orbitrap), with optional stratification by precursor mass (e.g., compounds >800 Da). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Evaluates molecular formula prediction methods (FIDDLE, SIRIUS, BUDDY) on held-out NIST23-only test spectra by computing top-1 and top-5 (and higher-K) accuracies per instrument type (Q-TOF vs. Orbitrap), with optional stratification by precursor mass (e.g., compounds >800 Da).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra contain chimeric (co-eluting) compounds — FIDDLE's performance decreases as spectral mixing increases, so benchmark numbers will not match clean-spectra expectations Precursor m/z values exceed 1500 — the m/z range is confined to (0, 1500] due to the rarity of spectra above that value Molecules contain rare atoms outside C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K, or exceed 300 total atoms — they are outside the training/model scope

skills.description: Use when spectra have known correct structures (spectral library or labeled benchmark) and you need to compare database-search methods by whether the true structure appears in the top-k ranked candidates.
skills.name: top-k-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-accuracy-evaluation Use when spectra have known correct structures (spectral library or labeled benchmark) and you need to compare database-search methods by whether the true structure appears in the top-k ranked candidates. Spectra lack ground-truth structure annotations, so top-k correctness cannot be verified (e.g., unannotated GNPS repository searches) Evaluating discovery at a fixed FDR on unknown samples (e.g., the 3185 unique molecules at 0% FDR GNPS search), which is a different metric than top-k library accuracy De novo structure prediction workflows that do not produce a ranked candidate list from a structure database http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Protocol for benchmarking small-molecule spectral database search methods (e.g., molDiscovery vs. Dereplicator+, MAGMa+, CFM-ID, MetFrag) by computing top-1/3/5/10 identification accuracies on spectra with known ground-truth structures, as in the GNPS-vs-DNP, MoNA-vs-MoNA, and PNNL-lipid-vs-LMSD benchmarks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-021-23986-0
skills.summary: Protocol for benchmarking small-molecule spectral database search methods (e.g., molDiscovery vs. Dereplicator+, MAGMa+, CFM-ID, MetFrag) by computing top-1/3/5/10 identification accuracies on spectra with known ground-truth structures, as in the GNPS-vs-DNP, MoNA-vs-MoNA, and PNNL-lipid-vs-LMSD benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra lack ground-truth structure annotations, so top-k correctness cannot be verified (e.g., unannotated GNPS repository searches) Evaluating discovery at a fixed FDR on unknown samples (e.g., the 3185 unique molecules at 0% FDR GNPS search), which is a different metric than top-k library accuracy De novo structure prediction workflows that do not produce a ranked candidate list from a structure database

skills.description: Use when a candidate-generation model outputs ranked SMILES predictions per spectrum and you need Acc_k and Sim_k metrics for k=1,10,50 on held-out EI-MS test splits.
skills.name: top-k-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-accuracy-evaluation Use when a candidate-generation model outputs ranked SMILES predictions per spectrum and you need Acc_k and Sim_k metrics for k=1,10,50 on held-out EI-MS test splits. Spectra are MS/MS rather than GC-EI-MS: existing de novo models like MassGenie rely on precursor ion mass or molecular formula cues SpecTUS does not use, so cross-comparison with this protocol is not straightforward. Input spectra come from poorly curated libraries (e.g. Cayman, MONA) whose quality differs from rigorously curated NIST/SWGDRUG splits — headline numbers will not transfer. You need intermediate explanations such as peak annotations, fragmentation trees, or reference spectra for candidates; the top-k metrics do not provide model justification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluate structure-annotation models by computing top-k accuracy (Acc_k) and average top-k Tanimoto similarity (Sim_k) of Morgan fingerprints between ground-truth SMILES and ranked candidates, following the SpecTUS evaluation protocol. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.05114
skills.summary: Evaluate structure-annotation models by computing top-k accuracy (Acc_k) and average top-k Tanimoto similarity (Sim_k) of Morgan fingerprints between ground-truth SMILES and ranked candidates, following the SpecTUS evaluation protocol.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are MS/MS rather than GC-EI-MS: existing de novo models like MassGenie rely on precursor ion mass or molecular formula cues SpecTUS does not use, so cross-comparison with this protocol is not straightforward. Input spectra come from poorly curated libraries (e.g. Cayman, MONA) whose quality differs from rigorously curated NIST/SWGDRUG splits — headline numbers will not transfer. You need intermediate explanations such as peak annotations, fragmentation trees, or reference spectra for candidates; the top-k metrics do not provide model justification.

skills.description: Use when a spectral-to-structure model outputs multiple candidate molecules per compound and you must quantify ranking quality as top-1/top-3 accuracy against known test-set structures.
skills.name: top-k-accuracy-evaluation-of-structure-prediction
skills.search_text: top-k-accuracy-evaluation-of-structure-prediction Use when a spectral-to-structure model outputs multiple candidate molecules per compound and you must quantify ranking quality as top-1/top-3 accuracy against known test-set structures. The pipeline returns a single deterministic prediction with no candidate set, so no ranking exists to evaluate as top-k You need experimental performance metrics other than top-k ranking accuracy (e.g. spectral reconstruction error or optimization objectives) Ground-truth structures are unavailable for the compounds being predicted, making accuracy computation impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Evaluation skill for the MultiModalSpectralTransformer (MMST) structure-prediction pipeline: candidates generated by multinomial sampling are ranked (e.g. by SGNN-simulated HSQC spectral matching) and scored as top-1 and top-3 accuracy against ground-truth structures. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/ange.202517611
skills.summary: Evaluation skill for the MultiModalSpectralTransformer (MMST) structure-prediction pipeline: candidates generated by multinomial sampling are ranked (e.g. by SGNN-simulated HSQC spectral matching) and scored as top-1 and top-3 accuracy against ground-truth structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline returns a single deterministic prediction with no candidate set, so no ranking exists to evaluate as top-k You need experimental performance metrics other than top-k ranking accuracy (e.g. spectral reconstruction error or optimization objectives) Ground-truth structures are unavailable for the compounds being predicted, making accuracy computation impossible

skills.description: Use when you have predicted fingerprints for test spectra plus candidate InChIKey lists per compound and need to quantify annotation accuracy as top-1/top-k hit rate on structure-disjoint test sets.
skills.name: top-k-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-annotation-accuracy-evaluation Use when you have predicted fingerprints for test spectra plus candidate InChIKey lists per compound and need to quantify annotation accuracy as top-1/top-k hit rate on structure-disjoint test sets. When the task is spectral-library matching against curated reference MS/MS spectra (the 'known unknowns' scenario the authors contrast with fingerprint prediction) When candidate lists are not structure-disjoint from the training compounds — accuracy will be inflated and not comparable to the reported ~50% top-1 rate When you need false discovery rate estimation for rankings — the article's discussion does not address specificity or FDR in candidate ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Evaluates metabolite annotation performance by ranking candidate compounds by fingerprint-similarity score and computing the fraction of testing compounds whose true InChIKey appears in the top-k ranked list, benchmarked against MetFrag, ChemDistiller, and CSI:FingerID. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01726-7
skills.summary: Evaluates metabolite annotation performance by ranking candidate compounds by fingerprint-similarity score and computing the fraction of testing compounds whose true InChIKey appears in the top-k ranked list, benchmarked against MetFrag, ChemDistiller, and CSI:FingerID.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is spectral-library matching against curated reference MS/MS spectra (the 'known unknowns' scenario the authors contrast with fingerprint prediction) When candidate lists are not structure-disjoint from the training compounds — accuracy will be inflated and not comparable to the reported ~50% top-1 rate When you need false discovery rate estimation for rankings — the article's discussion does not address specificity or FDR in candidate ranking

skills.search_text: top-k-candidate-ranking-evaluation Use when a tandem-MS candidate-ranking tool has been parameterized on one dataset and you must verify Top 1/3/5 hit rates on independent HR-MS/MS spectra with known compound identities. skills.summary: Evaluate MetFrag2.2 candidate rankings by counting correct compound identities in Top 1, Top 3 and Top 5 positions across merged HR-MS/MS spectra datasets, verifying that optimized scoring weights (ωFrag+ωRT+ωRefs=1) generalize to independent validation data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a ranked candidate list with no known ground-truth compound identities to score against — the skill requires verified compound identities for Top-k counting. You need de novo structure elucidation without any candidate database, since this skill evaluates rankings of pre-retrieved candidate structures from PubChem/ChemSpider rather than generating candidates. skills.description: Use when evaluating de novo structure generation models (e.g., DiffMS on NPLIB1/MassSpecGym) whose raw sampler emits many molecules per spectrum and a ranked top-1/top-10 candidate list is needed for benchmark scoring.
skills.name: top-k-candidate-selection-for-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-candidate-selection-for-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating de novo structure generation models (e.g., DiffMS on NPLIB1/MassSpecGym) whose raw sampler emits many molecules per spectrum and a ranked top-1/top-10 candidate list is needed for benchmark scoring. The formula pool is not yet predicted — this filter assumes the per-spectrum candidate pool (100 molecules across 5 formulae) already exists; run formula inference first (e.g., MIST or SIRIUS). Post-processing filter that converts DiffMS's raw diffusion sampling output (100 sampled molecules per spectrum across 5 predicted formulae) into frequency-ranked top-k candidate lists (k=1,10) by removing invalid or disconnected molecules with RDKit, enabling apples-to-apples benchmark comparison against baselines. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Post-processing filter that converts DiffMS's raw diffusion sampling output (100 sampled molecules per spectrum across 5 predicted formulae) into frequency-ranked top-k candidate lists (k=1,10) by removing invalid or disconnected molecules with RDKit, enabling apples-to-apples benchmark comparison against baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The formula pool is not yet predicted — this filter assumes the per-spectrum candidate pool (100 molecules across 5 formulae) already exists; run formula inference first (e.g., MIST or SIRIUS). Evaluating a baseline whose ranking mechanism is intrinsic to the method, e.g., MSNovelist, which uses beam search with width 100 and log-likelihood ranking instead of frequency-based top-k selection.
