skills.search_text: top-k-molecular-structure-matching Use when evaluating conditional molecular generators that output multiple candidate structures per spectrum and you need rank-based exact-match accuracy (top-k) against ground-truth reference structures. Evaluating unconditional molecular generators where each sample has no paired ground-truth structure — use distribution-level metrics (FCD, validity) instead Comparing generated structures at the 3D conformation level rather than exact structural identity — use the RMSD evaluation script (eval_sampled_mols/rmsd.py) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes top-1 and top-10 structure elucidation accuracy by matching diffusion-generated molecules to ground-truth structures via SMILES identity, the primary accuracy metric for spectra-conditioned generation in DiffSpectra. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2507.06853
skills.summary: Computes top-1 and top-10 structure elucidation accuracy by matching diffusion-generated molecules to ground-truth structures via SMILES identity, the primary accuracy metric for spectra-conditioned generation in DiffSpectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating unconditional molecular generators where each sample has no paired ground-truth structure — use distribution-level metrics (FCD, validity) instead Comparing generated structures at the 3D conformation level rather than exact structural identity — use the RMSD evaluation script (eval_sampled_mols/rmsd.py) instead

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics annotation workflow must be scored by how often the true compound appears in the top-k ranked candidates, where ranking combines accurate mass search (e.g., 10 ppm m/z tolerance) with predicted RT error.
skills.name: top-k-rank-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-rank-accuracy-evaluation Use when a metabolomics annotation workflow must be scored by how often the true compound appears in the top-k ranked candidates, where ranking combines accurate mass search (e.g., 10 ppm m/z tolerance) with predicted RT error. No experimental RTs exist for the target chromatographic method, so no quartic projection model can be fitted on ~50 identified molecules Candidate filtering relies on MS/MS spectral matching or other orthogonal evidence rather than accurate mass plus predicted RT ranking The evaluation goal is standalone RT prediction performance (e.g., RMSE against measured RT) rather than candidate ranking/filtering accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Evaluates whether predicted retention times from a deep learning model (trained on the METLIN SMRT dataset) can rank the correct molecular identity among the top 3 candidates retrieved by accurate mass search, across experimental chromatographic methods (PredRet ECMs 1-4). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Evaluates whether predicted retention times from a deep learning model (trained on the METLIN SMRT dataset) can rank the correct molecular identity among the top 3 candidates retrieved by accurate mass search, across experimental chromatographic methods (PredRet ECMs 1-4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No experimental RTs exist for the target chromatographic method, so no quartic projection model can be fitted on ~50 identified molecules Candidate filtering relies on MS/MS spectral matching or other orthogonal evidence rather than accurate mass plus predicted RT ranking The evaluation goal is standalone RT prediction performance (e.g., RMSE against measured RT) rather than candidate ranking/filtering accuracy

skills.description: Use when two ranked-match output files over the same labeled test substances exist and you need to decide whether integrating a second similarity component (e.g., Jaccard fingerprint similarity with cosine spectral similarity) moves correct hits into the top ranks.
skills.name: top-k-retrieval-metric-comparison
skills.search_text: top-k-retrieval-metric-comparison Use when two ranked-match output files over the same labeled test substances exist and you need to decide whether integrating a second similarity component (e.g., Jaccard fingerprint similarity with cosine spectral similarity) moves correct hits into the top ranks. The analyte spectra already match established reference spectra in conventional library screening (NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG), so no re-ranking of synthetic NPS candidates is needed. The chemical structure of the novel substance is already known, since in silico prediction (e.g., NEIMS) can be applied directly and metric comparison of anonymous retrieval is moot. Rankings come from different candidate sets or different test substances per metric, making the top-1 proportions not directly comparable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Quantifies whether adding a fingerprint-based similarity (Jaccard) to a spectral similarity metric (cosine/SMSF) improves top-k retrieval accuracy, by recomputing the proportion of correct compounds ranked at position 1 (and within top 20) for a labeled test set such as SWGDRUG substances. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05019
skills.summary: Quantifies whether adding a fingerprint-based similarity (Jaccard) to a spectral similarity metric (cosine/SMSF) improves top-k retrieval accuracy, by recomputing the proportion of correct compounds ranked at position 1 (and within top 20) for a labeled test set such as SWGDRUG substances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analyte spectra already match established reference spectra in conventional library screening (NIST/Wiley/SWGDRUG), so no re-ranking of synthetic NPS candidates is needed. The chemical structure of the novel substance is already known, since in silico prediction (e.g., NEIMS) can be applied directly and metric comparison of anonymous retrieval is moot. Rankings come from different candidate sets or different test substances per metric, making the top-1 proportions not directly comparable.

skills.description: Use when an annotation engine has scored known-compound tandem MS spectra against reference chemical databases and you need to quantify how often the correct metabolite appears in the top-k ranked candidates.
skills.name: top-k-retrieval-rate-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-retrieval-rate-evaluation Use when an annotation engine has scored known-compound tandem MS spectra against reference chemical databases and you need to quantify how often the correct metabolite appears in the top-k ranked candidates. Spectra are from unknown/novel compounds with no ground-truth structure, so no correct-answer rank can be determined for retrieval statistics The task is de novo formula prediction or peak annotation rather than ranking candidates against a reference chemical database Only MS1 data is available without tandem MS fragmentation evidence needed by FingerScorer/FragScorer http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates a tandem MS metabolite annotation engine by computing top-k retrieval rates (top-1/top-5 on a small database, top-20 on a large database) over a held-out test split of known-compound spectra, comparing FingerScorer, FragScorer, and their combination under baseline, +Element, and +Known formula conditions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty080
skills.summary: Evaluates a tandem MS metabolite annotation engine by computing top-k retrieval rates (top-1/top-5 on a small database, top-20 on a large database) over a held-out test split of known-compound spectra, comparing FingerScorer, FragScorer, and their combination under baseline, +Element, and +Known formula conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are from unknown/novel compounds with no ground-truth structure, so no correct-answer rank can be determined for retrieval statistics The task is de novo formula prediction or peak annotation rather than ranking candidates against a reference chemical database Only MS1 data is available without tandem MS fragmentation evidence needed by FingerScorer/FragScorer

skills.description: Use when you have a trained NMR2Struct checkpoint (substructure-to-structure transformer or multitask model), a loaded alphabet.npy, and need per-input candidate SMILES sets sized for top-15 exact-match evaluation.
skills.name: top-k-sampled-smiles-generation
skills.search_text: top-k-sampled-smiles-generation Use when you have a trained NMR2Struct checkpoint (substructure-to-structure transformer or multitask model), a loaded alphabet.npy, and need per-input candidate SMILES sets sized for top-15 exact-match evaluation. You need deterministic single-structure output rather than a ranked candidate set — this protocol deliberately samples 15 candidates with k=5 nondeterminism Inferring substructures rather than SMILES — use pred_gen_fn 'infer_multitask_model_substructures' instead of the SMILES-generation inference configuration Molecules beyond the model's training scope (heavier than 19 heavy atoms, elements beyond C, N, O as non-hydrogen atoms, or stereochemistry-dependent queries) Generates candidate molecular structures as SMILES strings by sampling from a transformer decoder (structure-assembly or multitask spectrum-to-structure model) using top-k random sampling with k=5 and emitting 15 predictions per input, which is the decoding protocol underlying the paper's reported exact-match accuracies. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.4c01132
skills.summary: Generates candidate molecular structures as SMILES strings by sampling from a transformer decoder (structure-assembly or multitask spectrum-to-structure model) using top-k random sampling with k=5 and emitting 15 predictions per input, which is the decoding protocol underlying the paper's reported exact-match accuracies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need deterministic single-structure output rather than a ranked candidate set — this protocol deliberately samples 15 candidates with k=5 nondeterminism Inferring substructures rather than SMILES — use pred_gen_fn 'infer_multitask_model_substructures' instead of the SMILES-generation inference configuration Molecules beyond the model's training scope (heavier than 19 heavy atoms, elements beyond C, N, O as non-hydrogen atoms, or stereochemistry-dependent queries)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a generative seq2seq model that emits SMILES strings (or similar token sequences) and you need top-n exact-match accuracy rather than single-greedy-output accuracy.
skills.name: top-k-sequence-decoding-evaluation
skills.search_text: top-k-sequence-decoding-evaluation Use when benchmarking a generative seq2seq model that emits SMILES strings (or similar token sequences) and you need top-n exact-match accuracy rather than single-greedy-output accuracy. You need the end-to-end spectrum-to-structure accuracy of the multitask model (69.6% top-15 from spectra) rather than the substructure-to-structure task upper bound (93.2%). Inputs are molecules with more than 19 heavy atoms, which are outside the model's demonstrated scope. You need single deterministic predictions rather than a distribution of sampled candidates; greedy decoding with a single output would not measure top-n coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates a generative sequence-to-sequence model (e.g., the NMR2Struct substructure-to-structure transformer) by decoding multiple candidate outputs with top-k random sampling and scoring whether the canonical target appears among the top-n predictions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.4c01132
skills.summary: Evaluates a generative sequence-to-sequence model (e.g., the NMR2Struct substructure-to-structure transformer) by decoding multiple candidate outputs with top-k random sampling and scoring whether the canonical target appears among the top-n predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the end-to-end spectrum-to-structure accuracy of the multitask model (69.6% top-15 from spectra) rather than the substructure-to-structure task upper bound (93.2%). Inputs are molecules with more than 19 heavy atoms, which are outside the model's demonstrated scope. You need single deterministic predictions rather than a distribution of sampled candidates; greedy decoding with a single output would not measure top-n coverage.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a substructure-to-structure or spectrum-to-structure NMR2Struct transformer: you need stochastic SMILES generation from an input vector and a canonical, order-invariant way to count exact-match accuracy.
skills.name: top-k-smiles-sampling-and-canonicalization
skills.search_text: top-k-smiles-sampling-and-canonicalization Use when evaluating a substructure-to-structure or spectrum-to-structure NMR2Struct transformer: you need stochastic SMILES generation from an input vector and a canonical, order-invariant way to count exact-match accuracy. You need a single deterministic structure per input rather than a ranked/stochastic candidate set — the 15-sample protocol is inherently probabilistic and does not guarantee the exact molecule. The task is substructure inference from spectra (use infer_multitask_model_substructures instead of SMILES generation). Molecules exceed the model's validated scope of 19 heavy atoms, where substructure-to-structure accuracy falls below 80%. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates multiple candidate molecular structures from a trained NMR2Struct transformer by sampling SMILES token-by-token with top-k random sampling (k=5), then canonicalizes the 15 predictions per input with RDKit to enable exact-match scoring against the target molecule. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acscentsci.4c01132
skills.summary: Generates multiple candidate molecular structures from a trained NMR2Struct transformer by sampling SMILES token-by-token with top-k random sampling (k=5), then canonicalizes the 15 predictions per input with RDKit to enable exact-match scoring against the target molecule.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a single deterministic structure per input rather than a ranked/stochastic candidate set — the 15-sample protocol is inherently probabilistic and does not guarantee the exact molecule. The task is substructure inference from spectra (use infer_multitask_model_substructures instead of SMILES generation). Molecules exceed the model's validated scope of 19 heavy atoms, where substructure-to-structure accuracy falls below 80%.

skills.description: Use when a full NxN spectral similarity matrix (e.g. 12,797 x 12,797) has been computed and the goal is to quantify how well each score's top matches reflect molecular structural similarity.
skills.name: top-percentile-pair-selection
skills.search_text: top-percentile-pair-selection Use when a full NxN spectral similarity matrix (e.g. 12,797 x 12,797) has been computed and the goal is to quantify how well each score's top matches reflect molecular structural similarity. You want correlation across the full score range rather than the extreme high-scoring end — the paper's Fig 3 analyses score distributions separately from this top-tail comparison Spectra lack InChIKey annotations, so Tanimoto structural similarity cannot be derived for the paired molecules The similarity matrix is sparse or pre-thresholded, so the full ~82M-pair population needed to define a genuine top 0.1% is unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Selects the very highest-scoring spectral pairs (top 0.1% of all ~82M non-self pairs in the UniqueInchikey dataset) from a full pairwise similarity matrix, so that the structural (Tanimoto) similarity of those best-matching pairs can be averaged per score and compared across Spec2Vec, cosine, and modified cosine as in Fig 3B of the paper. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Selects the very highest-scoring spectral pairs (top 0.1% of all ~82M non-self pairs in the UniqueInchikey dataset) from a full pairwise similarity matrix, so that the structural (Tanimoto) similarity of those best-matching pairs can be averaged per score and compared across Spec2Vec, cosine, and modified cosine as in Fig 3B of the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want correlation across the full score range rather than the extreme high-scoring end — the paper's Fig 3 analyses score distributions separately from this top-tail comparison Spectra lack InChIKey annotations, so Tanimoto structural similarity cannot be derived for the paired molecules The similarity matrix is sparse or pre-thresholded, so the full ~82M-pair population needed to define a genuine top 0.1% is unavailable

skills.description: Use when evaluating a gene prioritization method against known causative genes on ranked candidate lists of varying length (e.g., 281-609 genes/patient), where a percentile-based success cutoff is fairer than absolute rank thresholds.
skills.name: top-percentile-prioritization-thresholding
skills.search_text: top-percentile-prioritization-thresholding Use when evaluating a gene prioritization method against known causative genes on ranked candidate lists of varying length (e.g., 281-609 genes/patient), where a percentile-based success cutoff is fairer than absolute rank thresholds. When candidate lists have uniform, fixed length and an absolute rank cutoff (e.g., top 50 genes) is meaningful and simpler When no known causative gene/diagnosis is available for the patient, since the percentile criterion cannot be scored When the goal is ranked-list evaluation without a reference gene (e.g., purely exploratory prioritization) - percentile-of-causative-gene scoring does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Judges gene prioritization success by whether at least one causative gene falls in the top 20th percentile of a patient's ranked candidate list, rather than requiring an absolute rank. Applied to metPropagate and Exomiser rankings over Exomiser-filtered candidate gene lists (281-609 genes per TIDEX patient). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41525-020-0132-5
skills.summary: Judges gene prioritization success by whether at least one causative gene falls in the top 20th percentile of a patient's ranked candidate list, rather than requiring an absolute rank. Applied to metPropagate and Exomiser rankings over Exomiser-filtered candidate gene lists (281-609 genes per TIDEX patient).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When candidate lists have uniform, fixed length and an absolute rank cutoff (e.g., top 50 genes) is meaningful and simpler When no known causative gene/diagnosis is available for the patient, since the percentile criterion cannot be scored When the goal is ranked-list evaluation without a reference gene (e.g., purely exploratory prioritization) - percentile-of-causative-gene scoring does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have ranked metabolite annotation candidates with per-query cosine scores for the top two hits plus top-1 correctness labels, and need to test whether a larger Δcos gap increases annotation reliability.
skills.name: top1-accuracy-visualization
skills.search_text: top1-accuracy-visualization Use when you have ranked metabolite annotation candidates with per-query cosine scores for the top two hits plus top-1 correctness labels, and need to test whether a larger Δcos gap increases annotation reliability. Candidate lists contain only a single hit per query, so Δcos = cos(top-1) − cos(top-2) cannot be computed No ground-truth correctness labels are available, so top-1 accuracy per Δcos bin cannot be estimated The goal is to produce the ranked annotations themselves (spectra prediction and candidate ranking) rather than evaluate the reliability of an existing ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Stratifies top-1 metabolite annotation correctness by the cosine-similarity gap (Δcos = cos(top-1) − cos(top-2)) between the two highest-ranked candidates, and visualizes binned correctness to test whether a larger gap (e.g. Δcos > 0.2) indicates the top candidate is the true metabolite. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.04.621329
skills.summary: Stratifies top-1 metabolite annotation correctness by the cosine-similarity gap (Δcos = cos(top-1) − cos(top-2)) between the two highest-ranked candidates, and visualizes binned correctness to test whether a larger gap (e.g. Δcos > 0.2) indicates the top candidate is the true metabolite.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate lists contain only a single hit per query, so Δcos = cos(top-1) − cos(top-2) cannot be computed No ground-truth correctness labels are available, so top-1 accuracy per Δcos bin cannot be estimated The goal is to produce the ranked annotations themselves (spectra prediction and candidate ranking) rather than evaluate the reliability of an existing ranking

skills.description: Use when you need to characterize how a formula-prediction model's top-5 accuracy varies with compound polarity (LogP), precursor mass (e.g., <200 Da bins), or ClassyFire superclass on tandem MS/MS test spectra.
skills.name: top5-formula-accuracy-stratification
skills.search_text: top5-formula-accuracy-stratification Use when you need to characterize how a formula-prediction model's top-5 accuracy varies with compound polarity (LogP), precursor mass (e.g., <200 Da bins), or ClassyFire superclass on tandem MS/MS test spectra. You need overall top-1/top-5 benchmark accuracy against SIRIUS or BUDDY — use the standard NIST23 evaluation instead of property-stratified analysis. Input spectra are chimeric (co-eluting) or come from external metabolomics datasets with no SMILES/superclass annotations available for stratification. Compounds contain atoms outside the frequent-element set (C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K) or exceed the 300-atom cap, since FIDDLE's test space excludes them. Stratifies FIDDLE's top-5 molecular formula identification accuracy over the NIST23 held-out test set by molecular properties — LogP-derived polarity, precursor mass bins, and ClassyFire superclass — for both Q-TOF and Orbitrap instrument types. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-66060-9
skills.summary: Stratifies FIDDLE's top-5 molecular formula identification accuracy over the NIST23 held-out test set by molecular properties — LogP-derived polarity, precursor mass bins, and ClassyFire superclass — for both Q-TOF and Orbitrap instrument types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need overall top-1/top-5 benchmark accuracy against SIRIUS or BUDDY — use the standard NIST23 evaluation instead of property-stratified analysis. Input spectra are chimeric (co-eluting) or come from external metabolomics datasets with no SMILES/superclass annotations available for stratification. Compounds contain atoms outside the frequent-element set (C, H, O, N, F, S, Cl, P, B, I, Br, Na, K) or exceed the 300-atom cap, since FIDDLE's test space excludes them.

skills.description: Use when raw imzML spectra from a MALDI-MSI experiment exhibit a slowly varying chemical background that must be subtracted pixel-wise before downstream dimensionality reduction, clustering, or MS image generation.
skills.name: tophat-baseline-subtraction
skills.search_text: tophat-baseline-subtraction Use when raw imzML spectra from a MALDI-MSI experiment exhibit a slowly varying chemical background that must be subtracted pixel-wise before downstream dimensionality reduction, clustering, or MS image generation. The spectra have already been baseline-corrected upstream, so applying tophat subtraction would strip genuine broad signal The task concerns the H&E histology image or LC-MS/MS peptide-confirmation workflows, which use MSIght's separate pre-processing pipelines rather than the MSI spectral pre-processing module Input is not an imzML-backed MSI pixel matrix (e.g., peak-picked peak lists or LC-MS chromatograms), where the pixel-wise spectrum assumptions of this step do not hold Removes broad chemical background from each pixel's spectrum in MALDI-MSI imzML data using a white tophat morphological filter with a structuring element of size 10, as implemented in the MSIght MSI pre-processing pipeline before dimensionality reduction and segmentation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.4c01140
skills.summary: Removes broad chemical background from each pixel's spectrum in MALDI-MSI imzML data using a white tophat morphological filter with a structuring element of size 10, as implemented in the MSIght MSI pre-processing pipeline before dimensionality reduction and segmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra have already been baseline-corrected upstream, so applying tophat subtraction would strip genuine broad signal The task concerns the H&E histology image or LC-MS/MS peptide-confirmation workflows, which use MSIght's separate pre-processing pipelines rather than the MSI spectral pre-processing module Input is not an imzML-backed MSI pixel matrix (e.g., peak-picked peak lists or LC-MS chromatograms), where the pixel-wise spectrum assumptions of this step do not hold

skills.description: Use when a tool's annotation quality must be quantified against known metabolite identities — e.g. comparing MetDNA3 vs MetDNA2 coverage/correct rate on feature tables with known ground-truth annotations split into seed and validation sets.
skills.name: topk-accuracy-and-fdr-evaluation
skills.search_text: topk-accuracy-and-fdr-evaluation Use when a tool's annotation quality must be quantified against known metabolite identities — e.g. comparing MetDNA3 vs MetDNA2 coverage/correct rate on feature tables with known ground-truth annotations split into seed and validation sets. The dataset has no known metabolite annotations to serve as seeds and validation targets, so no ground-truth correct rate or FDR can be computed The goal is de novo annotation of unknown metabolites (e.g. discovery of metabolites absent from databases), not tool benchmarking against reference annotations Data are not untargeted metabolomics feature tables (MS1/MS2 from Orbitrap-type acquisition); the seed/validation propagation framework requires feature-level MS1 and MS2 inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Benchmarking protocol for metabolite annotation accuracy: run 10-fold cross-validation (30% seed / 70% validation) over 20 Orbitrap datasets and compute annotation coverage, Top 1/3/10 correct rates, and Top 3 FDR to quantify whether MetDNA3's two-layer network propagation beats a baseline such as MetDNA2. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for metabolite annotation accuracy: run 10-fold cross-validation (30% seed / 70% validation) over 20 Orbitrap datasets and compute annotation coverage, Top 1/3/10 correct rates, and Top 3 FDR to quantify whether MetDNA3's two-layer network propagation beats a baseline such as MetDNA2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no known metabolite annotations to serve as seeds and validation targets, so no ground-truth correct rate or FDR can be computed The goal is de novo annotation of unknown metabolites (e.g. discovery of metabolites absent from databases), not tool benchmarking against reference annotations Data are not untargeted metabolomics feature tables (MS1/MS2 from Orbitrap-type acquisition); the seed/validation propagation framework requires feature-level MS1 and MS2 inputs

Spectra lack known library annotations, so no ground truth exists for computing top-k accuracy The goal is variant/discovery search (variable mode) rather than exact-mode benchmarking against a reference accuracy figure Input spectra target PubChem-scale searches where the reference baselines do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmark a mass spectral search tool's top-k identification accuracy by ranking per-scan best hits and comparing accuracy against published baselines (e.g., Dereplicator+ and molDiscovery in Extended Data Fig. 4 of the VInSMoC paper). metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Benchmark a mass spectral search tool's top-k identification accuracy by ranking per-scan best hits and comparing accuracy against published baselines (e.g., Dereplicator+ and molDiscovery in Extended Data Fig. 4 of the VInSMoC paper).

skills.description: Use when a candidate-ranking or annotation method must be compared against an MS/MS-only baseline (e.g., SIRIUS or MS-DIAL) to quantify whether integrating an additional scorer (e.g., retention scores) improves identification accuracy.
skills.name: topk-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: topk-accuracy-evaluation Use when a candidate-ranking or annotation method must be compared against an MS/MS-only baseline (e.g., SIRIUS or MS-DIAL) to quantify whether integrating an additional scorer (e.g., retention scores) improves identification accuracy. When the chromatographic system is HILIC rather than RPLC — ROASMI retention scores that feed this evaluation currently apply only to RPLC systems When candidates fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S covered by the ROASMI models When candidate pairs have retention peaks so close that the retention order is inconsistent across experiments (indistinguishable pairs should be excluded from identification) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark protocol for evaluating candidate-ranking improvements in small-molecule identification by computing top-k accuracy (top-1, top-3, top-5) for MS/MS-only baselines versus retention-score-integrated rankings, as used to validate ROASMI on CASMI 2022 and dataset_38. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for evaluating candidate-ranking improvements in small-molecule identification by computing top-k accuracy (top-1, top-3, top-5) for MS/MS-only baselines versus retention-score-integrated rankings, as used to validate ROASMI on CASMI 2022 and dataset_38.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the chromatographic system is HILIC rather than RPLC — ROASMI retention scores that feed this evaluation currently apply only to RPLC systems When candidates fall outside the elemental restrictions of C, H, N, O, P, and S covered by the ROASMI models When candidate pairs have retention peaks so close that the retention order is inconsistent across experiments (indistinguishable pairs should be excluded from identification)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking compound-to-spectrum (C2MS) prediction models on a retrieval-based compound identification task where candidate sets are built from PubChem neighbors and Top-k hit rates must be reported with seed-level variance.
skills.name: topk-accuracy-statistics-over-seeds
skills.search_text: topk-accuracy-statistics-over-seeds Use when benchmarking compound-to-spectrum (C2MS) prediction models on a retrieval-based compound identification task where candidate sets are built from PubChem neighbors and Top-k hit rates must be reported with seed-level variance. The task is formula annotation or peak-prediction error evaluation rather than retrieval-based MS2C ranking Candidate sets cannot be constructed from PubChem fingerprints (e.g. the query molecule has no PubChem coverage), so Tanimoto-similar negatives are unavailable Only a single fixed split with one candidate ranking is needed and no seed-level variance reporting is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates retrieval-based compound identification (MS2C) by ranking candidate compounds by spectral similarity to a real MS/MS spectrum and computing Top-1/Top-3/Top-5 accuracy as mean ± standard deviation over 5 random seeds. Used to compare C2MS spectrum-prediction models against spectral-library-only retrieval on the NIST20 held-out test set. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2404.02360
skills.summary: Evaluates retrieval-based compound identification (MS2C) by ranking candidate compounds by spectral similarity to a real MS/MS spectrum and computing Top-1/Top-3/Top-5 accuracy as mean ± standard deviation over 5 random seeds. Used to compare C2MS spectrum-prediction models against spectral-library-only retrieval on the NIST20 held-out test set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is formula annotation or peak-prediction error evaluation rather than retrieval-based MS2C ranking Candidate sets cannot be constructed from PubChem fingerprints (e.g. the query molecule has no PubChem coverage), so Tanimoto-similar negatives are unavailable Only a single fixed split with one candidate ranking is needed and no seed-level variance reporting is intended

skills.description: Use when a trained CNN predicts molecular embeddings from MS/MS spectra and you must quantify annotation accuracy as top-1 and top-5 correctness against a reference database of 520,083 compounds.
skills.name: topk-annotation-rate-evaluation
skills.search_text: topk-annotation-rate-evaluation Use when a trained CNN predicts molecular embeddings from MS/MS spectra and you must quantify annotation accuracy as top-1 and top-5 correctness against a reference database of 520,083 compounds. The compound under study is not present in the 520,083-compound reference database — candidate matching cannot return molecules outside it, so top-k rates would be meaningless. skills.description: Use when correcting fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) for natural abundance and tracer isotopic impurity without resolution effects, e.g. building a baseline correction matrix for a compound with Nt tracer atoms.
skills.name: tracer-isotopic-impurity-matrix-parameterization
skills.search_text: tracer-isotopic-impurity-matrix-parameterization Use when correcting fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) for natural abundance and tracer isotopic impurity without resolution effects, e.g. building a baseline correction matrix for a compound with Nt tracer atoms. When the instrument's high resolving power can resolve isotopologs with the same nominal mass — including all isotopologs in the correction matrix is then no longer justified, and resolution-dependent methods (MDT/ULS) are preferred. When FAM data come from an unlabeled sample so tracer-impurity combinatorics are unnecessary — deconvolution of the unlabeled-sample FAM supplies the correction directly. When the selected tracer element is absent from the compound formula — the algorithm will report an error, e.g. selecting C or S as tracer for 15N-labeled data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Constructs the theoretical natural-abundance/isotopic-impurity correction matrix (C1 x C2 x C3) for isotope-labeling correction by combinatorial convolution of isotope distributions over non-tracer elements, tracer-element natural abundance, and nutrient isotopic purity, as implemented in ElemCor's non-resolution-effect (NRE) baseline. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Constructs the theoretical natural-abundance/isotopic-impurity correction matrix (C1 x C2 x C3) for isotope-labeling correction by combinatorial convolution of isotope distributions over non-tracer elements, tracer-element natural abundance, and nutrient isotopic purity, as implemented in ElemCor's non-resolution-effect (NRE) baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the instrument's high resolving power can resolve isotopologs with the same nominal mass — including all isotopologs in the correction matrix is then no longer justified, and resolution-dependent methods (MDT/ULS) are preferred. When FAM data come from an unlabeled sample so tracer-impurity combinatorics are unnecessary — deconvolution of the unlabeled-sample FAM supplies the correction directly. When the selected tracer element is absent from the compound formula — the algorithm will report an error, e.g. selecting C or S as tracer for 15N-labeled data.

skills.description: Use when assigning a sample list to fixed-capacity plates/batches (e.g. 96-well plates, max 96 experimental samples/plate) where the sample count is not an exact multiple of the batch capacity, and per-batch strata balance must be preserved including the remainder.
skills.name: trailing-sample-random-interspersion
skills.search_text: trailing-sample-random-interspersion Use when assigning a sample list to fixed-capacity plates/batches (e.g. 96-well plates, max 96 experimental samples/plate) where the sample count is not an exact multiple of the batch capacity, and per-batch strata balance must be preserved including the remainder. The goal is within-batch run-order or within-plate position design (block randomization, QC-sample placement) rather than distributing samples across batches — use the intra-batch randomization / intra-batch position design steps instead The sample count is an exact multiple of the batch capacity, so there is no trailing remainder — ordinary inter-batch balancing without remainder interspersion suffices One dimension has too many groups under special numerical distributions, where the algorithm's averaging step can cause local aggregation and a different strategy is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3369 A sub-behavior of InjectionDesign's inter-batch balancing algorithm: when the cohort size does not divide evenly by the batch (plate) capacity, the trailing leftover samples are randomized and interspersed across batches rather than being appended as a lopsided final batch, so every plate's group distribution stays close to the overall cohort ratio. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.02.26.530140
skills.summary: A sub-behavior of InjectionDesign's inter-batch balancing algorithm: when the cohort size does not divide evenly by the batch (plate) capacity, the trailing leftover samples are randomized and interspersed across batches rather than being appended as a lopsided final batch, so every plate's group distribution stays close to the overall cohort ratio.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is within-batch run-order or within-plate position design (block randomization, QC-sample placement) rather than distributing samples across batches — use the intra-batch randomization / intra-batch position design steps instead The sample count is an exact multiple of the batch capacity, so there is no trailing remainder — ordinary inter-batch balancing without remainder interspersion suffices One dimension has too many groups under special numerical distributions, where the algorithm's averaging step can cause local aggregation and a different strategy is needed

skills.search_text: transcript-massfeature-correlation-network-construction Use when you have a paired transcriptomic–metabolomic dataset (e.g., the Jeon 2020 tomato dataset) and need to derive statistically integrated, overlapping functional clusters linking co-abundant transcripts and mass features. Transcript and metabolite samples are not paired across the same conditions, so Pearson/MR correlation across samples cannot be computed The goal is reaction-rules-based pathway prediction (RetroRules/LOTUS adduct matching) rather than statistical transcript–metabolite co-abundance clustering A clustering result already exists and the task is pathway-level significance assignment, which ClusterONE's co-expression-derived statistics do not address http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs edge-weighted transcript–mass feature networks from paired transcriptomic–metabolomic data by converting Pearson correlations to mutual ranks (MRs), applying an exponential decay function with adjustable decay parameter DR, and clustering nodes with ClusterONE to obtain overlapping feature clusters (FCs). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Constructs edge-weighted transcript–mass feature networks from paired transcriptomic–metabolomic data by converting Pearson correlations to mutual ranks (MRs), applying an exponential decay function with adjustable decay parameter DR, and clustering nodes with ClusterONE to obtain overlapping feature clusters (FCs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Transcript and metabolite samples are not paired across the same conditions, so Pearson/MR correlation across samples cannot be computed The goal is reaction-rules-based pathway prediction (RetroRules/LOTUS adduct matching) rather than statistical transcript–metabolite co-abundance clustering A clustering result already exists and the task is pathway-level significance assignment, which ClusterONE's co-expression-derived statistics do not address

skills.description: Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset must be integrated without a known 'bait' metabolite or enzyme to surface feature clusters containing biosynthetic genes.
skills.name: transcript-metabolite-integration
skills.search_text: transcript-metabolite-integration Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset must be integrated without a known 'bait' metabolite or enzyme to surface feature clusters containing biosynthetic genes. Prior knowledge of a bait compound or enzyme is already available and a targeted bait-based co-expression approach suffices The input is not a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset with matched samples (MR correlation and FC construction require both data types) The goal is enzyme-level pathway reconstruction requiring multi-substrate or stereospecific reactions, which RetroRules single-substrate rules and MS data cannot capture http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Unsupervised integration of paired transcriptomic and metabolomic data using MEANtools: MAD-rescaled inputs, mutual rank (MR)-based correlations converted to exponential-decay edge weights, and ClusterONE clustering into overlapping feature clusters (FCs) that can be mapped to known biosynthetic genes (e.g., HCAA, alpha-tomatine, chlorogenic acid pathways in tomato). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Unsupervised integration of paired transcriptomic and metabolomic data using MEANtools: MAD-rescaled inputs, mutual rank (MR)-based correlations converted to exponential-decay edge weights, and ClusterONE clustering into overlapping feature clusters (FCs) that can be mapped to known biosynthetic genes (e.g., HCAA, alpha-tomatine, chlorogenic acid pathways in tomato).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Prior knowledge of a bait compound or enzyme is already available and a targeted bait-based co-expression approach suffices The input is not a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset with matched samples (MR correlation and FC construction require both data types) The goal is enzyme-level pathway reconstruction requiring multi-substrate or stereospecific reactions, which RetroRules single-substrate rules and MS data cannot capture

skills.description: Use when running repeated ICA (e.g. FastICA) decompositions on a transcriptomic expression matrix and you need to choose the decomposition order from stability behavior rather than arbitrarily.
skills.name: transcriptomic-dimensionality-estimation
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-dimensionality-estimation Use when running repeated ICA (e.g. FastICA) decompositions on a transcriptomic expression matrix and you need to choose the decomposition order from stability behavior rather than arbitrarily. The decomposition order has already been fixed by downstream constraints and no stability-based dimensionality choice is needed The data are not transcriptomic/omics matrix-factorization inputs (e.g. already-reduced feature tables or non-matrix data), where ICA order selection via MSTD does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Determines the optimal number of independent components (decomposition order) for ICA applied to transcriptomic data using the MSTD criterion, where the order is chosen as the point at which the distribution of independent-component stability indices is no longer dominated by highly unstable components. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/ijms20184414
skills.summary: Determines the optimal number of independent components (decomposition order) for ICA applied to transcriptomic data using the MSTD criterion, where the order is chosen as the point at which the distribution of independent-component stability indices is no longer dominated by highly unstable components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The decomposition order has already been fixed by downstream constraints and no stability-based dimensionality choice is needed The data are not transcriptomic/omics matrix-factorization inputs (e.g. already-reduced feature tables or non-matrix data), where ICA order selection via MSTD does not apply

skills.description: Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset is available and the goal is de novo, bait-free reconstruction or hypothesis generation for specialized-metabolite biosynthetic pathways.
skills.name: transcriptomic-metabolomic-integration
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-metabolomic-integration Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset is available and the goal is de novo, bait-free reconstruction or hypothesis generation for specialized-metabolite biosynthetic pathways. The analysis requires MS/MS-based annotation: MEANtools does not currently support loading MS/MS data or mass spectral library/networking-based annotation approaches. The pathway of interest involves multi-substrate reactions or stereoisomeric conversions: RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions only, and stereoisomers are not captured by mass spectrometric data. Prior knowledge of a bait compound or enzyme is already available and a bait-driven co-expression approach is sufficient for the goal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Unsupervised integration of paired transcriptomic and metabolomic data with MEANtools to connect correlated enzyme-coding transcripts and mass features and predict biosynthetic reaction steps using RetroRules reaction rules and LOTUS structure annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003307
skills.summary: Unsupervised integration of paired transcriptomic and metabolomic data with MEANtools to connect correlated enzyme-coding transcripts and mass features and predict biosynthetic reaction steps using RetroRules reaction rules and LOTUS structure annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires MS/MS-based annotation: MEANtools does not currently support loading MS/MS data or mass spectral library/networking-based annotation approaches. The pathway of interest involves multi-substrate reactions or stereoisomeric conversions: RetroRules-based rules are designed for single-substrate reactions only, and stereoisomers are not captured by mass spectrometric data. Prior knowledge of a bait compound or enzyme is already available and a bait-driven co-expression approach is sufficient for the goal.

skills.description: Use when you have a transcriptomics expression matrix (counts or normalized) plus a curated gene panel (e.g. 26 IFN-induced genes) and need to split samples into biologically defined subgroups for downstream DGE and pathway exploration.
skills.name: transcriptomics-gene-panel-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: transcriptomics-gene-panel-activity-scoring Use when you have a transcriptomics expression matrix (counts or normalized) plus a curated gene panel (e.g. 26 IFN-induced genes) and need to split samples into biologically defined subgroups for downstream DGE and pathway exploration. Input has no curated gene panel — the activity-score subgrouping requires a user-defined panel; for unsupervised clustering of multi-omics use BiomiX's MOFA/SNF/NEMO integration instead Data are metabolomics, methylomics, or proteomics — this panel-Z-score subgroup workflow applies to transcriptomics expression matrices The goal is outlier/QC filtering rather than subpopulation analysis — use the Preview-QC interface's outlier removal based on PCA centroid distances instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Stratify transcriptomics samples using a user-defined gene panel activity score: Z-score normalize each panel gene across samples, call samples panel-positive/negative by the Z>1 criterion (Kirou-style), then run per-subgroup DGE and enrichment. This is the BiomiX subgroup analysis demonstrated on a 26 IFN-induced gene panel in preterm birth (PTB) transcriptomes. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Stratify transcriptomics samples using a user-defined gene panel activity score: Z-score normalize each panel gene across samples, call samples panel-positive/negative by the Z>1 criterion (Kirou-style), then run per-subgroup DGE and enrichment. This is the BiomiX subgroup analysis demonstrated on a 26 IFN-induced gene panel in preterm birth (PTB) transcriptomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has no curated gene panel — the activity-score subgrouping requires a user-defined panel; for unsupervised clustering of multi-omics use BiomiX's MOFA/SNF/NEMO integration instead Data are metabolomics, methylomics, or proteomics — this panel-Z-score subgroup workflow applies to transcriptomics expression matrices The goal is outlier/QC filtering rather than subpopulation analysis — use the Preview-QC interface's outlier removal based on PCA centroid distances instead

skills.description: Reference for building multiomics databases that ingest RNA-seq and microarray transcriptomics datasets into per-level statistics.
skills.name: transcriptomics-rnaseq-microarray-harmonization
skills.search_text: transcriptomics-rnaseq-microarray-harmonization Reference for building multiomics databases that ingest RNA-seq and microarray transcriptomics datasets into per-level statistics. Input is single-cell or spatial transcriptomics — those modalities follow a separate GutUDB ingestion path, not the bulk RNA-seq/microarray harmonization rules. The goal is querying or browsing the already-built GutUDB statistics page rather than reconstructing or re-deriving the ingestion pipeline. Input omics type is genomic variation (SNPs, CNVs, SVs), methylation, proteomics, or metabolomics — those levels require their own per-level constants and aggregation rules. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Normalizes and merges bulk transcriptomics data types (RNA-seq and microarray) into per-level statistics within GutUDB's multiomics database framework, enabling consistent counts and browsing across intestinal disease datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/imt2.195
skills.summary: Normalizes and merges bulk transcriptomics data types (RNA-seq and microarray) into per-level statistics within GutUDB's multiomics database framework, enabling consistent counts and browsing across intestinal disease datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or spatial transcriptomics — those modalities follow a separate GutUDB ingestion path, not the bulk RNA-seq/microarray harmonization rules. The goal is querying or browsing the already-built GutUDB statistics page rather than reconstructing or re-deriving the ingestion pipeline. Input omics type is genomic variation (SNPs, CNVs, SVs), methylation, proteomics, or metabolomics — those levels require their own per-level constants and aggregation rules.

skills.description: Use when a pretrained 3DMolMS encoder (e.g. molnet_pre_geobond.pt) should be transferred to a new property-prediction head (CCS, RT) instead of training from scratch, and you must decide between frozen-encoder and full fine-tune.
skills.name: transfer-learning-encoder-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-encoder-fine-tuning Use when a pretrained 3DMolMS encoder (e.g. molnet_pre_geobond.pt) should be transferred to a new property-prediction head (CCS, RT) instead of training from scratch, and you must decide between frozen-encoder and full fine-tune. You only need standard MS/MS, RT, or CCS predictions from existing checkpoints — use molnet_engine.pred_msms/pred_rt/pred_ccs directly instead of fine-tuning. The downstream dataset is too small for the head alone to converge — the frozen-encoder default may underfit, and full fine-tuning (freeze_encoder=False) is the explicit alternative. Your target spectra or properties fall outside the model's stated input scope (atom number ≤ 300, atom types C/O/N/H/P/S/F/Cl/B/Br/I, supported precursor types). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Adapts the molecular encoder pretrained by 3DMolMS on MS/MS spectra prediction to a downstream chemical-property task (e.g. CCS or RT) by loading only the encoder.* weights and training a fresh task head, improving over training from scratch. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad354
skills.summary: Adapts the molecular encoder pretrained by 3DMolMS on MS/MS spectra prediction to a downstream chemical-property task (e.g. CCS or RT) by loading only the encoder.* weights and training a fresh task head, improving over training from scratch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need standard MS/MS, RT, or CCS predictions from existing checkpoints — use molnet_engine.pred_msms/pred_rt/pred_ccs directly instead of fine-tuning. The downstream dataset is too small for the head alone to converge — the frozen-encoder default may underfit, and full fine-tuning (freeze_encoder=False) is the explicit alternative. Your target spectra or properties fall outside the model's stated input scope (atom number ≤ 300, atom types C/O/N/H/P/S/F/Cl/B/Br/I, supported precursor types).

skills.description: Use when predicting retention times on a new liquid-chromatography dataset (e.g., a PredRet dataset with 'InChI' and 'RT' columns) under chromatographic conditions different from the pre-training data, and a pre-trained RT-Transformer checkpoint is available.
skills.name: transfer-learning-encoder-freezing
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-encoder-freezing Use when predicting retention times on a new liquid-chromatography dataset (e.g., a PredRet dataset with 'InChI' and 'RT' columns) under chromatographic conditions different from the pre-training data, and a pre-trained RT-Transformer checkpoint is available. When no suitable pre-trained checkpoint exists for the molecular domain — retrain from scratch with train.py instead of freezing a mismatched encoder When the target dataset's retention behavior is expected to require re-learning molecular representations, not just re-calibrating the prediction head When the input is not molecule-RT pairs (e.g., raw LC-MS mzML data or already-predicted retention times) — this skill operates on InChI/RT CSV tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Transfer the pre-trained RT-Transformer (ResGAT + 1D-Transformer encoder, pre-trained on the 80,038-molecule SMRT dataset) to a new chromatographic-method retention-time dataset by freezing the encoder weights and re-initializing/fine-tuning only the Output-Block. This preserves the general retention-time representation learned from SMRT while adapting the prediction head to the target chromatographic conditions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Transfer the pre-trained RT-Transformer (ResGAT + 1D-Transformer encoder, pre-trained on the 80,038-molecule SMRT dataset) to a new chromatographic-method retention-time dataset by freezing the encoder weights and re-initializing/fine-tuning only the Output-Block. This preserves the general retention-time representation learned from SMRT while adapting the prediction head to the target chromatographic conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no suitable pre-trained checkpoint exists for the molecular domain — retrain from scratch with train.py instead of freezing a mismatched encoder When the target dataset's retention behavior is expected to require re-learning molecular representations, not just re-calibrating the prediction head When the input is not molecule-RT pairs (e.g., raw LC-MS mzML data or already-predicted retention times) — this skill operates on InChI/RT CSV tables

skills.description: Reference for benchmarking a transfer-learned retention time predictor on candidate compound lists: you have spectra with measured retention times, MS-Finder or similar candidate annotations, and want to quantify filtering correctness and annotation rank changes.

skills.search_text: transfer-learning-rt-model-evaluation Reference for benchmarking a transfer-learned retention time predictor on candidate compound lists: you have spectra with measured retention times, MS-Finder or similar candidate annotations, and want to quantify filtering correctness and annotation rank changes. skills.summary: Evaluates RT-Transformer retention-time predictions under transfer learning on a target chromatographic dataset (e.g. Metabobase candidates from MoNa with MS-Finder annotations) by filtering candidates whose predicted RT deviates beyond the model tolerance and measuring correct identifications, erroneous filterings, and rank improvements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is pre-training a general RT predictor from scratch on the large SMRT dataset rather than evaluating transfer-learned performance on a target chromatographic method with candidate filtering. The dataset lacks measured retention times, so candidate filtering by RT deviation cannot be performed. Candidates come from a source other than MS-Finder-style annotation lists without a defined ranking to track rank improvement.

Input is a raw feature table or suspect-screening result before TP componentization — prioritization operates on components, not on unlinked features or candidate TP lists The analysis goal is initial TP structure prediction or parent selection (target list, suspect screening, or feature compound annotation) rather than filtering already-formed parent/TP components The workflow needs the patRoon 3.0 ion mobility separation (IMS) functionality or other post-2.0 features; this skill is grounded in the patRoon 2.0 prioritization filters http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Prioritizes transformation product (TP) components in patRoon 2.0 after parent and TP features have been grouped into components, by applying five complementary filters (RT direction, structure similarity, explained transformation, remove isomers, duplicates) that reduce false-positive parent/TP assignments in LC-HRMS non-target analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.04029

skills.search_text: transformation-product-feature-prioritization Use when you have a pre-processed HRMS feature table (e.g., Agilent .csv export with blank/control-subtracted features) across a time-course or dilution series, and you need to prioritize features — such as transformation products — that share similar abundance trends without supervised labels. Input is raw .mzML data that still requires feature extraction — run mssmain.get_scans and mssmain.peak_pick (with peak width, replicated peak, and background subtraction filters) first to obtain a feature table The dataset lacks time-course/dilution structure, so feature abundance trends carry no grouping signal for DBSCAN You need isotope/adduct/in-source-fragment feature grouping — the article lists this as future work, not an implemented capability of this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Prioritizes candidate transformation-product features from HRMS time-course feature tables by unsupervised clustering of abundance trends with MSS's dm.ms_cluster (DBSCAN), grouping features whose normalized intensities co-vary across time points and flagging outliers for exclusion. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00741-9

skills.description: Use when implementing or modifying the denoising network of a discrete graph diffusion model that must output per-edge bond-type probabilities (k=5 classes) while respecting fixed heavy-atom composition from a chemical formula.
skills.name: transformer-architecture-coding
skills.search_text: transformer-architecture-coding Use when implementing or modifying the denoising network of a discrete graph diffusion model that must output per-edge bond-type probabilities (k=5 classes) while respecting fixed heavy-atom composition from a chemical formula. The target is a continuous (non-categorical) graph representation — DiGress/DiffMS use discrete diffusion on one-hot adjacency, not continuous node-coordinate diffusion Node counts or atom types are unknown and must be generated — this decoder conditions on fixed formula-derived node features X, so it cannot produce structures violating the given heavy-atom composition You only need generic sequence transformers (e.g., for spectra encoding) — this skill covers the graph denoising network, not the MIST spectrum-transformer encoder Implement the Graph Transformer denoising network phi_theta at the heart of DiffMS's discrete diffusion decoder, which takes noised adjacency A^t, formula-fixed node features X, and a structural condition y and predicts denoised adjacency probabilities p_theta(A^0 | M^t) in R^{n x n x k}. The architecture follows Dwivedi & Bresson (2021) as coded in DiGress, which DiffMS adapts. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.09571
skills.summary: Implement the Graph Transformer denoising network phi_theta at the heart of DiffMS's discrete diffusion decoder, which takes noised adjacency A^t, formula-fixed node features X, and a structural condition y and predicts denoised adjacency probabilities p_theta(A^0 | M^t) in R^{n x n x k}. The architecture follows Dwivedi & Bresson (2021) as coded in DiGress, which DiffMS adapts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target is a continuous (non-categorical) graph representation — DiGress/DiffMS use discrete diffusion on one-hot adjacency, not continuous node-coordinate diffusion Node counts or atom types are unknown and must be generated — this decoder conditions on fixed formula-derived node features X, so it cannot produce structures violating the given heavy-atom composition You only need generic sequence transformers (e.g., for spectra encoding) — this skill covers the graph denoising network, not the MIST spectrum-transformer encoder

skills.summary: Run the pretrained substructure-to-structure encoder-decoder transformer from NMR2Struct to autoregressively generate candidate SMILES strings from a 957-element binary substructure array, using top-k random sampling (k=5) with 15 predictions per input to reconstruct exact molecular structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a 1H/13C NMR spectrum rather than a precomputed substructure array — use the multitask spectrum-to-structure model or nmr_infer_single_spectrum instead, as this entry point only works for substructure-to-structure inference. skills.description: Use when the goal is to predict retention times for small molecules under a given chromatographic method from InChI/graph inputs, or to transfer a pre-trained RT-Transformer to a new chromatographic condition and benchmark its accuracy.

skills.search_text: transformer-sequence-regression Use when the goal is to predict retention times for small molecules under a given chromatographic method from InChI/graph inputs, or to transfer a pre-trained RT-Transformer to a new chromatographic condition and benchmark its accuracy. The task requires predicting retention times under multiple different chromatographic conditions from a single model without transfer learning — the article notes current methods 'lack sufficient scalability to transfer from one specific chromatographic method to another', and this skill's transfer path requires per-condition fine-tuning. The molecules of interest are not retained under the chromatographic method (RT ≤ 300 s) and the retained-data evaluation protocol is required — in that case the full-data checkpoint (33.41 s MAE) or a different evaluation condition is more appropriate. Input data lacks 'InChI' and 'RT' columns in the expected CSV format and cannot be converted, e.g. raw chromatographic peak tables without molecular identifiers. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Trains and fine-tunes RT-Transformer, a deep neural network coupling a graph attention network with a 1D-Transformer, to predict liquid chromatography retention times of metabolites and evaluate MAE/MedAE on SMRT-derived test partitions. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084
skills.summary: Trains and fine-tunes RT-Transformer, a deep neural network coupling a graph attention network with a 1D-Transformer, to predict liquid chromatography retention times of metabolites and evaluate MAE/MedAE on SMRT-derived test partitions.

The molecules of interest are not retained under the chromatographic method (RT ≤ 300 s) and the retained-data evaluation protocol is required — in that case the full-data checkpoint (33.41 s MAE) or a different evaluation condition is more appropriate. skills.description: Use when raw FT-ICR mass spectrometry transients acquired with short transient duration (<10% of full collection time) must be reconstructed to high-mass-resolution, high-SNR spectra, as in MEISTER MSI and SCMS pipelines.
skills.name: transient-signal-reconstruction
skills.search_text: transient-signal-reconstruction Use when raw FT-ICR mass spectrometry transients acquired with short transient duration (<10% of full collection time) must be reconstructed to high-mass-resolution, high-SNR spectra, as in MEISTER MSI and SCMS pipelines. Input transients are already acquired at full duration (high resolution) — reconstruction offers no throughput benefit and the regressor expects short transients. skills.description: Use when a metabolomics workflow step (normalization, missing-value imputation, blank masking, batch correction, annotation) must read a feature table from or write one to a TSV file with samples as rows and features as columns.
skills.name: tsv-feature-table-input-output
skills.search_text: tsv-feature-table-input-output Use when a metabolomics workflow step (normalization, missing-value imputation, blank masking, batch correction, annotation) must read a feature table from or write one to a TSV file with samples as rows and features as columns. The data are still raw instrument files (.raw or .mzML) that have not yet been converted to mzML and processed by Asari into a feature table. The output must be consumed by a tool that does not parse tab-separated text (e.g. a JSON-only consumer such as empCpd.json); use the JSON serialization of empirical compounds instead. The table already contains annotation columns or non-numeric metadata that would break a strict numeric feature-intensity layout. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 This skill covers the PCPFM convention of persisting curated feature tables as tab-separated value (TSV) files—each row is a sample and each column is a feature (empirical compound or Asari feature)—so that downstream statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst or R/Python workflows can consume them directly. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011912
skills.summary: This skill covers the PCPFM convention of persisting curated feature tables as tab-separated value (TSV) files—each row is a sample and each column is a feature (empirical compound or Asari feature)—so that downstream statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst or R/Python workflows can consume them directly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are still raw instrument files (.raw or .mzML) that have not yet been converted to mzML and processed by Asari into a feature table. The output must be consumed by a tool that does not parse tab-separated text (e.g. a JSON-only consumer such as empCpd.json); use the JSON serialization of empirical compounds instead. The table already contains annotation columns or non-numeric metadata that would break a strict numeric feature-intensity layout.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a missing value imputation method (e.g., GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN) preserves the ability to detect differential variables between two groups on MNAR-degraded metabolomics data.
skills.name: ttest-differential-variable-detection
skills.search_text: ttest-differential-variable-detection Use when evaluating whether a missing value imputation method (e.g., GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN) preserves the ability to detect differential variables between two groups on MNAR-degraded metabolomics data. When the goal is imputation accuracy (NRMSE) or distribution preservation rather than downstream statistical power — use the dedicated accuracy/distribution evaluations instead When missing values are MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored MNAR — the TPR sensitivity comparison in the paper is designed for MNAR (LOD/LOQ-type) missingness When the data has no defined two-group comparison, since S and S' depend on t-tests between group labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assess how an imputation method affects statistical sensitivity by comparing t-test-detectable differential variables between complete and imputed data, using TPR = |S ∩ S'| / |S| at p-cut 0.05 and 0.01 across increasing MNAR missingness. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005973
skills.summary: Assess how an imputation method affects statistical sensitivity by comparing t-test-detectable differential variables between complete and imputed data, using TPR = |S ∩ S'| / |S| at p-cut 0.05 and 0.01 across increasing MNAR missingness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is imputation accuracy (NRMSE) or distribution preservation rather than downstream statistical power — use the dedicated accuracy/distribution evaluations instead When missing values are MCAR/MAR rather than left-censored MNAR — the TPR sensitivity comparison in the paper is designed for MNAR (LOD/LOQ-type) missingness When the data has no defined two-group comparison, since S and S' depend on t-tests between group labels

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics concentration table (CSV with sample rows, metabolite columns, and a group/factor column) has two or more sample groups and you need, per metabolite, an ANOVA p-value plus pairwise Tukey p-values for every inter-group comparison.
skills.name: tukey-posthoc-pairwise-pvalue-computation
skills.search_text: tukey-posthoc-pairwise-pvalue-computation Use when a metabolomics concentration table (CSV with sample rows, metabolite columns, and a group/factor column) has two or more sample groups and you need, per metabolite, an ANOVA p-value plus pairwise Tukey p-values for every inter-group comparison. The dataset has only two groups and a nonparametric comparison is intended — Viime applies the univariate Wilcoxon rank sum test for two-group data and reserves multivariate ANOVA for two or more groups Data have not yet been through Viime's preprocessing chain (error correction, MCAR/MNAR imputation, normalization, transformation, scaling), so concentration values are not comparable across groups The goal is model-based multivariate statistics (e.g. PLS-DA) rather than per-metabolite group significance testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes pairwise inter-group p-values with the Tukey HSD post-hoc test following a multivariate ANOVA, reproducing Viime's statistical significance testing for metabolomics concentration data with two or more groups. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Computes pairwise inter-group p-values with the Tukey HSD post-hoc test following a multivariate ANOVA, reproducing Viime's statistical significance testing for metabolomics concentration data with two or more groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has only two groups and a nonparametric comparison is intended — Viime applies the univariate Wilcoxon rank sum test for two-group data and reserves multivariate ANOVA for two or more groups Data have not yet been through Viime's preprocessing chain (error correction, MCAR/MNAR imputation, normalization, transformation, scaling), so concentration values are not comparable across groups The goal is model-based multivariate statistics (e.g. PLS-DA) rather than per-metabolite group significance testing

skills.description: Use when a trained probabilistic encoder yields a compact latent representation (e.g., 5-D from a VAE Code layer) of high-dimensional spectra and you need to visually confirm class separation between normal and tumor groups.
skills.name: tumor-normal-class-separation-visualization
skills.search_text: tumor-normal-class-separation-visualization Use when a trained probabilistic encoder yields a compact latent representation (e.g., 5-D from a VAE Code layer) of high-dimensional spectra and you need to visually confirm class separation between normal and tumor groups. The input is raw high-dimensional mass spectra rather than a learned low-dimensional latent variable — the article applies UMAP to the latent code specifically to avoid the curse of dimensionality, not directly on 85,062 m/z variables. The goal is quantitative classification or performance metrics (ROC, accuracy, F1-score) — that is the role of massNet's probabilistic pixel-based classifier, not this visualization step. No trained VAE/encoder exists yet; the Code-layer latent variable must first be extracted from an optimized model before UMAP can be applied. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Embeds a trained VAE's low-dimensional latent variable (e.g., massNet's 5-dimensional Code layer output from MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra) in 2D via UMAP to visually verify separation between normal and tumor tissue classes and inspect inter-tumor heterogeneity. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Embeds a trained VAE's low-dimensional latent variable (e.g., massNet's 5-dimensional Code layer output from MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra) in 2D via UMAP to visually verify separation between normal and tumor tissue classes and inspect inter-tumor heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw high-dimensional mass spectra rather than a learned low-dimensional latent variable — the article applies UMAP to the latent code specifically to avoid the curse of dimensionality, not directly on 85,062 m/z variables. The goal is quantitative classification or performance metrics (ROC, accuracy, F1-score) — that is the role of massNet's probabilistic pixel-based classifier, not this visualization step. No trained VAE/encoder exists yet; the Code-layer latent variable must first be extracted from an optimized model before UMAP can be applied.

skills.name: tumor-region-annotation-overlay
skills.search_text: tumor-region-annotation-overlay Use when raw imzML/HDF5 MSI pixel data (e.g. 100 µm FT-ICR acquisitions with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be visualized as an ion image and compared against expert-annotated tumor regions from a consecutive H&E-stained section. skills.summary: Reconstructs a 2D ion image for a specific m/z channel from raw MALDI FT-ICR MSI data and overlays the pathologist-derived tumor annotation transferred from a consecutive H&E section, enabling spatial localization of ion signal to tumor versus normal tissue.

The goal is probabilistic pixel-level tumor classification by massNet itself, not spatial visualization/localization of a single m/z ion image. Input is already an aggregated per-peak feature or correlation table with no spatial pixel coordinates, so no 2D ion image can be reconstructed.

skills.search_text: tutorial-dataset-reproduction Use when a task asks to reproduce a bundled tutorial or canonical benchmark dataset (e.g. iris from Fisher 1936) with a published tool's statistical workflow, such as unsupervised PCA on small feature tables. skills.description: Use when you have TWAS/PrediXcan gene-level association results and a set of condition-responsive DEGs, and need to quantify whether the DEGs are enriched (or depleted) among significant trait-tissue-gene associations with uncertainty quantification.

skills.search_text: twas-deg-enrichment-intersection-analysis Use when you have TWAS/PrediXcan gene-level association results and a set of condition-responsive DEGs, and need to quantify whether the DEGs are enriched (or depleted) among significant trait-tissue-gene associations with uncertainty quantification.
