skills.name: two-dimensional-histogram-pixel-classification
skills.search_text: two-dimensional-histogram-pixel-classification Use when a background-corrected two-channel (e.g., red/green CFP/YFP) confocal image or time series needs automatic, threshold-free classification of which pixels are colocalized, and when subsequent proportion-colocalized coefficients must be computed per region or time point. The question is direct protein-protein interaction distance (<10 nm) rather than colocalization — FRET is the appropriate readout, as FRET alone detects interaction only if the average distance between binding proteins is <10 nm The image is single-channel or the two channels cannot be represented as a joint red/green intensity histogram Adjacent pixel intensities are being scrambled as individual pixels without block scrambling when texture/PSF-scale correlations exist — this violates the method's assumption and biases the random-overlap distribution Automatic statistical classification of colocalized pixels in two-color fluorescence images by building a red/green two-dimensional histogram, setting the colocalization threshold from 200 block-scrambling randomizations, and selecting pixels near the diagonal to compute proportion-colocalized coefficients. Validated at ~5% pixel misclassification and shown to detect colocalization not obvious to the eye. metabolomics/v3 10.1529/biophysj.103.038422
skills.summary: Automatic statistical classification of colocalized pixels in two-color fluorescence images by building a red/green two-dimensional histogram, setting the colocalization threshold from 200 block-scrambling randomizations, and selecting pixels near the diagonal to compute proportion-colocalized coefficients. Validated at ~5% pixel misclassification and shown to detect colocalization not obvious to the eye.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is direct protein-protein interaction distance (<10 nm) rather than colocalization — FRET is the appropriate readout, as FRET alone detects interaction only if the average distance between binding proteins is <10 nm The image is single-channel or the two channels cannot be represented as a joint red/green intensity histogram Adjacent pixel intensities are being scrambled as individual pixels without block scrambling when texture/PSF-scale correlations exist — this violates the method's assumption and biases the random-overlap distribution

skills.description: Use when raw GC×GC-MS data (NetCDF folded into a 2D-TIC) shows noise or baseline drift and must be smoothed, baseline-corrected, or aligned (e.g. wsmooth with penalty=1, lambda=1e1) prior to MPCA.
skills.name: two-dimensional-signal-preprocessing
skills.search_text: two-dimensional-signal-preprocessing Use when raw GC×GC-MS data (NetCDF folded into a 2D-TIC) shows noise or baseline drift and must be smoothed, baseline-corrected, or aligned (e.g. wsmooth with penalty=1, lambda=1e1) prior to MPCA. The chromatograms are already preprocessed and the goal is downstream multivariate analysis (MPCA via m_prcomp) rather than signal enhancement The data is one-dimensional chromatography or non-chromatographic signal — the RGCxGC pipeline assumes a two-dimensional 2D-TIC from GC×GC-MS The input has not yet been imported from NetCDF into a 2D-TIC chromatogram object, since preprocessing functions operate on folded chromatogram objects http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Preprocessing pipeline for GC×GC-MS 2D-TIC chromatograms implemented in the R RGCxGC package: signal enhancement via Whittaker smoothing, asymmetric-least-squares baseline correction, and 2D-COW peak alignment before multivariate analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2020.104830
skills.summary: Preprocessing pipeline for GC×GC-MS 2D-TIC chromatograms implemented in the R RGCxGC package: signal enhancement via Whittaker smoothing, asymmetric-least-squares baseline correction, and 2D-COW peak alignment before multivariate analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chromatograms are already preprocessed and the goal is downstream multivariate analysis (MPCA via m_prcomp) rather than signal enhancement The data is one-dimensional chromatography or non-chromatographic signal — the RGCxGC pipeline assumes a two-dimensional 2D-TIC from GC×GC-MS The input has not yet been imported from NetCDF into a 2D-TIC chromatogram object, since preprocessing functions operate on folded chromatogram objects

skills.description: Use when an expression matrix is split into two sample groups and the goal is to detect features whose Pearson correlation with a target feature changes significantly between the groups, as in MOG's differential correlation analysis.
skills.name: two-group-correlation-comparison
skills.search_text: two-group-correlation-comparison Use when an expression matrix is split into two sample groups and the goal is to detect features whose Pearson correlation with a target feature changes significantly between the groups, as in MOG's differential correlation analysis. The goal is differential expression (mean-level change between groups), which MOG handles via fold-change >= 2 and BH-corrected Mann–Whitney U test P < 10^-3 rather than correlation testing The analysis compares overall co-expression across all samples (e.g. Spearman >= 0.60 across all samples) rather than testing whether correlations differ between two groups More than two sample groups are involved; the Fisher z-test for equality of two coefficients is defined only for a two-group contrast http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Statistical skill for identifying features whose Pearson correlation with a user-selected feature differs significantly between two groups of samples, as implemented in MetaOmGraph (MOG) via a Fisher transformation followed by a z-test for equality of correlation coefficients. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: Statistical skill for identifying features whose Pearson correlation with a user-selected feature differs significantly between two groups of samples, as implemented in MetaOmGraph (MOG) via a Fisher transformation followed by a z-test for equality of correlation coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression (mean-level change between groups), which MOG handles via fold-change >= 2 and BH-corrected Mann–Whitney U test P < 10^-3 rather than correlation testing The analysis compares overall co-expression across all samples (e.g. Spearman >= 0.60 across all samples) rather than testing whether correlations differ between two groups More than two sample groups are involved; the Fisher z-test for equality of two coefficients is defined only for a two-group contrast

skills.description: Use when a numerical measurement column must be compared across exactly two groups defined by a categorical column (e.g. Condition) in Instant Clue, and a parametric t-test is appropriate for the data distribution.
skills.name: two-group-parametric-t-testing
skills.search_text: two-group-parametric-t-testing Use when a numerical measurement column must be compared across exactly two groups defined by a categorical column (e.g. Condition) in Instant Clue, and a parametric t-test is appropriate for the data distribution. The grouping column has more than two groups — use the ANOVA (parametric) or Kruskal-Wallis (non-parametric) activity instead The parametric assumption is not justified for the data — dispatch the U-test (non-parametric Mann-Whitney) activity instead of the t-test The data has no categorical grouping column to assign to the categorical receiver box, so no two-group comparison can be defined via drag & drop http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Dispatches a two-group parametric t-test inside Instant Clue by dragging the t-test activity from the Analysis toolbox onto a chart built from a numerical column and a categorical grouping column (e.g. Body weight vs Condition); the resulting p-value is annotated directly on the chart above the line connecting the tested groups. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6
skills.summary: Dispatches a two-group parametric t-test inside Instant Clue by dragging the t-test activity from the Analysis toolbox onto a chart built from a numerical column and a categorical grouping column (e.g. Body weight vs Condition); the resulting p-value is annotated directly on the chart above the line connecting the tested groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The grouping column has more than two groups — use the ANOVA (parametric) or Kruskal-Wallis (non-parametric) activity instead The parametric assumption is not justified for the data — dispatch the U-test (non-parametric Mann-Whitney) activity instead of the t-test The data has no categorical grouping column to assign to the categorical receiver box, so no two-group comparison can be defined via drag & drop

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites x samples) with two group labels must be converted into a significant-metabolite query set for downstream pathway enrichment analysis.
skills.name: two-group-statistical-testing-metabolomics
skills.search_text: two-group-statistical-testing-metabolomics Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites x samples) with two group labels must be converted into a significant-metabolite query set for downstream pathway enrichment analysis. Input is already a curated list of KEGG IDs/names or a pre-computed query set — pass it directly as inputMetabolites to enrichmet() instead of running run_de() The metabolomics matrix has more than two groups or repeated measures — run_de() is defined for a two-group control vs mutant comparison The goal is MetSEA on ranked metabolite lists without differential selection — fgsea-based MetSEA can use summary statistics directly rather than the filtered query set http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential analysis stage (run_de) in the EnrichMet R package that computes per-metabolite fold change between two metabolomics groups (e.g. control vs mutant lung cancer) and applies Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment to select the significant-metabolite query set feeding Fisher's Exact Test pathway enrichment. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.08.28.672951
skills.summary: Differential analysis stage (run_de) in the EnrichMet R package that computes per-metabolite fold change between two metabolomics groups (e.g. control vs mutant lung cancer) and applies Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment to select the significant-metabolite query set feeding Fisher's Exact Test pathway enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated list of KEGG IDs/names or a pre-computed query set — pass it directly as inputMetabolites to enrichmet() instead of running run_de() The metabolomics matrix has more than two groups or repeated measures — run_de() is defined for a two-group control vs mutant comparison The goal is MetSEA on ranked metabolite lists without differential selection — fgsea-based MetSEA can use summary statistics directly rather than the filtered query set

skills.description: Use when you have PLAGE pathway activity levels per sample and need to identify pathways whose mean activity differs significantly between two pre-defined groups (e.g., smokers vs non-smokers, diabetic vs non-diabetic).
skills.name: two-group-t-statistic-pathway-testing
skills.search_text: two-group-t-statistic-pathway-testing Use when you have PLAGE pathway activity levels per sample and need to identify pathways whose mean activity differs significantly between two pre-defined groups (e.g., smokers vs non-smokers, diabetic vs non-diabetic). When the goal is differential expression of individual genes rather than predefined pathway activity levels — the article notes pathway-based results are complementary, not a substitute, for gene-focused analyses. When expression data has not yet been reduced to pathway activity levels via SVD (e.g., raw microarray intensities); PLAGE decomposition is a prerequisite step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Performs pairwise two-group significance testing of SVD-derived pathway activity levels (PLAGE) by computing a t statistic for each pathway's mean activity difference and evaluating significance against a permutation-based null that tracks the most significant pathway per permutation. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/1471-2105-6-225
skills.summary: Performs pairwise two-group significance testing of SVD-derived pathway activity levels (PLAGE) by computing a t statistic for each pathway's mean activity difference and evaluating significance against a permutation-based null that tracks the most significant pathway per permutation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential expression of individual genes rather than predefined pathway activity levels — the article notes pathway-based results are complementary, not a substitute, for gene-focused analyses. When expression data has not yet been reduced to pathway activity levels via SVD (e.g., raw microarray intensities); PLAGE decomposition is a prerequisite step.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to reconstruct the metabolisms of one or two KEGG organisms from KGML pathway files and compare them at structural (graph) and functional (reaction-set) levels using MetNet's similarity indexes.
skills.name: two-level-metabolic-network-reconstruction
skills.search_text: two-level-metabolic-network-reconstruction Use when the goal is to reconstruct the metabolisms of one or two KEGG organisms from KGML pathway files and compare them at structural (graph) and functional (reaction-set) levels using MetNet's similarity indexes. When the input is raw genomic data rather than KEGG organism codes — MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and would need significant extension When reconstruction from a non-KEGG source is required — the method is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which limits the represented information When pathway comparison results must be integrated across databases like BioCyc or BioModels rather than KEGG reference pathways http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Automatically reconstruct the metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms using MetNet's two-level representation — a structural graph of pathways and a functional set of reactions per pathway — so that the metabolisms can be compared quantitatively and visually with local and global similarity indexes. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Automatically reconstruct the metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms using MetNet's two-level representation — a structural graph of pathways and a functional set of reactions per pathway — so that the metabolisms can be compared quantitatively and visually with local and global similarity indexes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw genomic data rather than KEGG organism codes — MetNet does not currently support input of genomic data and would need significant extension When reconstruction from a non-KEGG source is required — the method is based uniquely on the KEGG database, which limits the represented information When pathway comparison results must be integrated across databases like BioCyc or BioModels rather than KEGG reference pathways

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether retention-time drift for monitored compounds in a pooled QC pool is dominated by batch-level offsets rather than by short-term (within-batch) scatter, e.g. to justify batch-wise RT recalibration.
skills.name: two-regime-threshold-comparison
skills.search_text: two-regime-threshold-comparison Use when you need to quantify whether retention-time drift for monitored compounds in a pooled QC pool is dominated by batch-level offsets rather than by short-term (within-batch) scatter, e.g. to justify batch-wise RT recalibration. Input is already a post-correction feature table or intensity drift data rather than raw RT deviations from module_TrackCmp The goal is to monitor contaminant levels or m/z calibration offsets instead of retention-time drift regimes The QC pool has not been acquired across multiple batches, so the interbatch regime cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces the QC4Metabolomics observation that short-term (within-batch) RT deviations for a long-term QC pool are normally below 0.05 min while interbatch RT offsets can be at least twice as large, by grouping per-compound RT deviations by batch and comparing the two regimes. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c07078
skills.summary: Reproduces the QC4Metabolomics observation that short-term (within-batch) RT deviations for a long-term QC pool are normally below 0.05 min while interbatch RT offsets can be at least twice as large, by grouping per-compound RT deviations by batch and comparing the two regimes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a post-correction feature table or intensity drift data rather than raw RT deviations from module_TrackCmp The goal is to monitor contaminant levels or m/z calibration offsets instead of retention-time drift regimes The QC pool has not been acquired across multiple batches, so the interbatch regime cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when an agent must test whether altered metabolite levels causally affect a phenotype by combining mGWAS summary statistics for a metabolite with a GWAS dataset (e.g. OpenGWAS ID finn-b-E4_DM2) via two-sample MR.
skills.name: two-sample-mr-causal-effect-estimation
skills.search_text: two-sample-mr-causal-effect-estimation Use when an agent must test whether altered metabolite levels causally affect a phenotype by combining mGWAS summary statistics for a metabolite with a GWAS dataset (e.g. OpenGWAS ID finn-b-E4_DM2) via two-sample MR. Input is raw MS spectra or a metabolite feature table — use the Spectra Processing or Statistical Analysis modules of MetaboAnalyst 6.0 instead (this skill addresses causal analysis, not peak detection/annotation or multi-factor statistical testing). The task is dose-response risk assessment of chemical exposures — the Dose-Response Analysis module with benchmark dose calculations is the correct module, not two-sample MR. No GWAS/mGWAS summary statistics are available (e.g. only cohort-level metabolite measurements), since MR requires genotype-metabolite and genotype-phenotype associations to define instruments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimates causal relationships between a metabolite (exposure) and a phenotype/disease (outcome) by two-sample Mendelian randomization, using the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 Causal Analysis module to integrate metabolite GWAS (mGWAS) summary statistics with phenotype GWAS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkae253
skills.summary: Estimates causal relationships between a metabolite (exposure) and a phenotype/disease (outcome) by two-sample Mendelian randomization, using the MetaboAnalyst 6.0 Causal Analysis module to integrate metabolite GWAS (mGWAS) summary statistics with phenotype GWAS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS spectra or a metabolite feature table — use the Spectra Processing or Statistical Analysis modules of MetaboAnalyst 6.0 instead (this skill addresses causal analysis, not peak detection/annotation or multi-factor statistical testing). The task is dose-response risk assessment of chemical exposures — the Dose-Response Analysis module with benchmark dose calculations is the correct module, not two-sample MR. No GWAS/mGWAS summary statistics are available (e.g. only cohort-level metabolite measurements), since MR requires genotype-metabolite and genotype-phenotype associations to define instruments.

skills.description: Use when you have a sample x metabolite relative concentration matrix produced by NMR quantification (NMRQNet csv output) and need to determine which metabolites separate two sample groups, e.g. MDS patients vs. healthy family controls.
skills.name: two-sample-t-test-biomarker-testing
skills.search_text: two-sample-t-test-biomarker-testing Use when you have a sample x metabolite relative concentration matrix produced by NMR quantification (NMRQNet csv output) and need to determine which metabolites separate two sample groups, e.g. MDS patients vs. healthy family controls. When the input is still raw 1H NMR spectra rather than a NMRQNet-estimated concentration matrix — use NMRQNet identification/quantification first. When you need to pre-filter metabolites with false-positive NMRQNet predictions before statistics — the article notes this requires a final manual visualization check rather than an automated post-processing step. When comparing more than two sample groups or when the goal is unsupervised clustering rather than patient-vs-control biomarker testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Statistical biomarker extraction skill that runs PCA outlier screening, supervised OPLS-DA group separation, and per-metabolite two-sample t-tests on the NMRQNet-estimated relative concentration matrix (e.g. 40 Mecp2 duplication syndrome family plasma samples x 38 metabolites) to identify metabolites that differ significantly between patient and control groups, such as acetate with t-test p = 0.016. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2023.03.01.530642
skills.summary: Statistical biomarker extraction skill that runs PCA outlier screening, supervised OPLS-DA group separation, and per-metabolite two-sample t-tests on the NMRQNet-estimated relative concentration matrix (e.g. 40 Mecp2 duplication syndrome family plasma samples x 38 metabolites) to identify metabolites that differ significantly between patient and control groups, such as acetate with t-test p = 0.016.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is still raw 1H NMR spectra rather than a NMRQNet-estimated concentration matrix — use NMRQNet identification/quantification first. When you need to pre-filter metabolites with false-positive NMRQNet predictions before statistics — the article notes this requires a final manual visualization check rather than an automated post-processing step. When comparing more than two sample groups or when the goal is unsupervised clustering rather than patient-vs-control biomarker testing.

skills.description: Use when two reproducibility methods (e.g., MaRR top-k sets vs. copula mixture model sets) yield different top-k transcript sets and you need to judge which method's method-specific genes are more biologically relevant against a quantitative gold-standard rank list.
skills.name: two-sample-t-test-rank-comparison
skills.search_text: two-sample-t-test-rank-comparison Use when two reproducibility methods (e.g., MaRR top-k sets vs. copula mixture model sets) yield different top-k transcript sets and you need to judge which method's method-specific genes are more biologically relevant against a quantitative gold-standard rank list. When no external gold-standard ranking with per-transcript quantitative measurements exists — the t-test compares PCR ranks, so without such measurements there is nothing to test When both methods declare the same top-k transcript sets (no method-specific genes), leaving zero genes on one side of the t-test When the goal is to determine which transcripts are reproducible in the first place — use the MaRR procedure itself rather than this post-hoc validation comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A rank-comparison validation procedure that scores method-specific gene sets against an external gold-standard ranking (e.g., Taqman PCR ranks on SEQC transcripts) using two-sample t-tests on the PCR-measurement ranks of each method's uniquely identified genes. metabolomics/v3 10.1080/01621459.2017.1397521
skills.summary: A rank-comparison validation procedure that scores method-specific gene sets against an external gold-standard ranking (e.g., Taqman PCR ranks on SEQC transcripts) using two-sample t-tests on the PCR-measurement ranks of each method's uniquely identified genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no external gold-standard ranking with per-transcript quantitative measurements exists — the t-test compares PCR ranks, so without such measurements there is nothing to test When both methods declare the same top-k transcript sets (no method-specific genes), leaving zero genes on one side of the t-test When the goal is to determine which transcripts are reproducible in the first place — use the MaRR procedure itself rather than this post-hoc validation comparison

skills.description: Use when ranked metabolite sets (e.g. KEGG pathways from PiMP_KEGG) need p-values based on activity-level changes between case and control groups, from a log2-transformed, standardised metabolomics intensity matrix with known experimental groups.
skills.name: two-sample-tstatistic-testing
skills.search_text: two-sample-tstatistic-testing Use when ranked metabolite sets (e.g. KEGG pathways from PiMP_KEGG) need p-values based on activity-level changes between case and control groups, from a log2-transformed, standardised metabolomics intensity matrix with known experimental groups. Peaks lack compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) — unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis, so coverage will be too sparse for meaningful activity testing The goal is overrepresentation or rank-enrichment testing on membership lists only (use ORA or GSEA in PALS instead of activity-level decomposition) There is no case/control contrast defined — t-statistics and the permutation null require two-sample comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes two-sample t-statistics on the leading singular vector (first metacompound) of each metabolite set's standardised intensity matrix, builds a permutation null, and calibrates set-level p-values with a GEV distribution fitted by maximum likelihood. This is the statistical core of the mPLAGE method in PALS. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo11020103
skills.summary: Computes two-sample t-statistics on the leading singular vector (first metacompound) of each metabolite set's standardised intensity matrix, builds a permutation null, and calibrates set-level p-values with a GEV distribution fitted by maximum likelihood. This is the statistical core of the mPLAGE method in PALS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks lack compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) — unannotated peaks are excluded from pathway analysis, so coverage will be too sparse for meaningful activity testing The goal is overrepresentation or rank-enrichment testing on membership lists only (use ORA or GSEA in PALS instead of activity-level decomposition) There is no case/control contrast defined — t-statistics and the permutation null require two-sample comparisons

skills.name: two-step-attachment-retrieval-workflow
skills.search_text: two-step-attachment-retrieval-workflow Reference for retrieving PubChem resources that are not directly addressable by CID alone — biologic depiction images (SVG) and annotation attachments (e.g. Mass Spectrometry) — via the two-step PUG-View /data/ → /image/ or /data/key/ pattern. When the target is a standard PUG-REST computed property (e.g. molecular formula, molecular weight) that is directly addressable by CID in a single call — PUG-REST is the better interface When multiple annotation headings must be retrieved in one request, since PUG-View does not support multi-heading or multi-identifier requests except via full-annotation retrieval When retrieving specialized tabular data served from other backend services that are not accessible through PUG-View at all http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 A PUG-View retrieval pattern for biologic depiction images and annotation attachments where the target resource is addressed by an internal identifier (e.g. biologic ID 138308 or attachment key 3413726_1) that must first be obtained from an intermediate /data/ JSON request before issuing the second call that returns the SVG image or attachment payload. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-019-0375-2
skills.summary: A PUG-View retrieval pattern for biologic depiction images and annotation attachments where the target resource is addressed by an internal identifier (e.g. biologic ID 138308 or attachment key 3413726_1) that must first be obtained from an intermediate /data/ JSON request before issuing the second call that returns the SVG image or attachment payload.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target is a standard PUG-REST computed property (e.g. molecular formula, molecular weight) that is directly addressable by CID in a single call — PUG-REST is the better interface When multiple annotation headings must be retrieved in one request, since PUG-View does not support multi-heading or multi-identifier requests except via full-annotation retrieval When retrieving specialized tabular data served from other backend services that are not accessible through PUG-View at all

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a pathway enrichment method (e.g. NetGSA REHE or REML) maintains type-I error control under null conditions while retaining power on dysregulated gene groups in simulated replicate studies.
skills.name: type-i-error-control-assessment
skills.search_text: type-i-error-control-assessment Use when evaluating whether a pathway enrichment method (e.g. NetGSA REHE or REML) maintains type-I error control under null conditions while retaining power on dysregulated gene groups in simulated replicate studies. When the goal is running pathway enrichment on real (non-simulated) expression data rather than assessing method-level statistical properties When no null (undysregulated) condition can be simulated, since type-I error control cannot be evaluated without a 'None' dysregulation group http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Empirically assess type-I error control (and power) of topology-based pathway enrichment methods — here NetGSA REHE (with and without clustering) vs REML — by simulating null and dysregulated signal conditions and measuring mean power per dysregulation-group bin. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979
skills.summary: Empirically assess type-I error control (and power) of topology-based pathway enrichment methods — here NetGSA REHE (with and without clustering) vs REML — by simulating null and dysregulated signal conditions and measuring mean power per dysregulation-group bin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is running pathway enrichment on real (non-simulated) expression data rather than assessing method-level statistical properties When no null (undysregulated) condition can be simulated, since type-I error control cannot be evaluated without a 'None' dysregulation group

skills.description: Use when validating that a proposed association test (e.g. PaIRKAT on simulated metabolite pathway graphs) holds its nominal type I error rate before assessing power.
skills.name: type-i-error-rate-estimation
skills.search_text: type-i-error-rate-estimation Use when validating that a proposed association test (e.g. PaIRKAT on simulated metabolite pathway graphs) holds its nominal type I error rate before assessing power. The goal is to estimate statistical power or detect sensitivity to alternatives — this skill only calibrates the null-hypothesis rejection rate, not power under true associations. Data are real experimental results (e.g. COPDGene metabolomics) rather than null simulations; empirical rejection rates of real data cannot validate calibration. The test of interest is not a kernel machine score test and no pathway graph structure is involved. Empirical type I error rate calibration for a pathway kernel score test: run 1000 null simulations per scenario and verify the proportion of rejections at alpha=0.05 is approximately 0.05. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2021.04.23.440821
skills.summary: Empirical type I error rate calibration for a pathway kernel score test: run 1000 null simulations per scenario and verify the proportion of rejections at alpha=0.05 is approximately 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to estimate statistical power or detect sensitivity to alternatives — this skill only calibrates the null-hypothesis rejection rate, not power under true associations. Data are real experimental results (e.g. COPDGene metabolomics) rather than null simulations; empirical rejection rates of real data cannot validate calibration. The test of interest is not a kernel machine score test and no pathway graph structure is involved.

skills.description: Use when a freetext sample metadata table (e.g. csv) contains non-numeric strings like 'allergen exposure' or 'ozone' that must be mapped onto fixed vocabularies such as zeroTimeEvent, drugName, or drugDoseUnit.
skills.name: typographical-error-fixing-in-metadata
skills.search_text: typographical-error-fixing-in-metadata Use when a freetext sample metadata table (e.g. csv) contains non-numeric strings like 'allergen exposure' or 'ozone' that must be mapped onto fixed vocabularies such as zeroTimeEvent, drugName, or drugDoseUnit. The metadata fields are purely numeric (the passes target non-numeric freetext strings; numeric values are not vocabulary-mapped). The metadata already conforms to the fixed vocabularies with no freetext remnants — re-running adds no value. You need to build new vocabularies/ontologies from scratch rather than map existing freetext onto them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Applies SMetaS's n-grams/nearest-neighbors (tf-idf/nnm) transformation with synonym matching and typographical fixing to replace freetext sample metadata strings with terms from fixed, ontology-derived vocabularies, escalating only truly unmapped strings to a user-confirmation step. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941
skills.summary: Applies SMetaS's n-grams/nearest-neighbors (tf-idf/nnm) transformation with synonym matching and typographical fixing to replace freetext sample metadata strings with terms from fixed, ontology-derived vocabularies, escalating only truly unmapped strings to a user-confirmation step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metadata fields are purely numeric (the passes target non-numeric freetext strings; numeric values are not vocabulary-mapped). The metadata already conforms to the fixed vocabularies with no freetext remnants — re-running adds no value. You need to build new vocabularies/ontologies from scratch rather than map existing freetext onto them.

skills.description: Use when sample metadata contains freetext terms (e.g. 'allergen exposure', 'ozone', 'hours/day') that must be resolved to standardized vocabulary entries despite synonyms or typographical errors, or when newly confirmed terms must be added and models retrained.
skills.name: typographical-error-tolerance-matching
skills.search_text: typographical-error-tolerance-matching Use when sample metadata contains freetext terms (e.g. 'allergen exposure', 'ozone', 'hours/day') that must be resolved to standardized vocabulary entries despite synonyms or typographical errors, or when newly confirmed terms must be added and models retrained. Input metadata already conforms to a fixed vocabulary, so no synonym matching or typographical fixing is needed The freetext term is not user-confirmed and has no clear correspondence to an existing vocabulary entry, risking mappings to unrelated entries http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps user-supplied freetext sample metadata terms to fixed vocabulary entries in SMetaS using synonym matching and typographical fixing within an n-grams/nearest-neighbors model over tf-idf term vectors, and retrains the model when users confirm new vocabulary terms. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13080941
skills.summary: Maps user-supplied freetext sample metadata terms to fixed vocabulary entries in SMetaS using synonym matching and typographical fixing within an n-grams/nearest-neighbors model over tf-idf term vectors, and retrains the model when users confirm new vocabulary terms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metadata already conforms to a fixed vocabulary, so no synonym matching or typographical fixing is needed The freetext term is not user-confirmed and has no clear correspondence to an existing vocabulary entry, risking mappings to unrelated entries

skills.description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with U13C-labeled standards and you need to monitor or correct CCSN2 bias without additional external calibrant measurements, e.g. TIM-MS data with 0.78%/0.33% mode-dependent bias.
skills.name: u13c-labeled-internal-standard-ccs-qc
skills.search_text: u13c-labeled-internal-standard-ccs-qc Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with U13C-labeled standards and you need to monitor or correct CCSN2 bias without additional external calibrant measurements, e.g. TIM-MS data with 0.78%/0.33% mode-dependent bias. When the lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 detected U13C-labeled lipids, since linear correction functions cannot be built and only CCS bias calculation is possible When samples have not been spiked with U13C-labeled standards — the DTCCSN2 library matching and internal standardization approach cannot be applied For lipid classes outside the supported list (AcCa, Cer, Co, DG, HexCer, LPC, LPE, PA, PC, PE, PG, PI, PS, SPH, TG) or adducts other than [M+H], [M+NH4], [M+Na], [M-H], [M+HCOO] http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Internal CCS quality control and correction for IM-MS lipidomics using U13C-labeled yeast lipid standards and the MobiLipid R Markdown, which computes CCS bias against a DTCCSN2 library and builds lipid class-adduct-specific linear correction functions. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c01253
skills.summary: Internal CCS quality control and correction for IM-MS lipidomics using U13C-labeled yeast lipid standards and the MobiLipid R Markdown, which computes CCS bias against a DTCCSN2 library and builds lipid class-adduct-specific linear correction functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the lipid class-adduct combination has fewer than 3 detected U13C-labeled lipids, since linear correction functions cannot be built and only CCS bias calculation is possible When samples have not been spiked with U13C-labeled standards — the DTCCSN2 library matching and internal standardization approach cannot be applied For lipid classes outside the supported list (AcCa, Cer, Co, DG, HexCer, LPC, LPE, PA, PC, PE, PG, PI, PS, SPH, TG) or adducts other than [M+H], [M+NH4], [M+Na], [M-H], [M+HCOO]

skills.description: Use when building pathway adjacency from KEGG KGML compound sets: compounds shared by many pathways (water, ATP, phosphate) would otherwise connect nearly every node and must be excluded before edge creation.
skills.name: ubiquitous-compound-filtering
skills.search_text: ubiquitous-compound-filtering Use when building pathway adjacency from KEGG KGML compound sets: compounds shared by many pathways (water, ATP, phosphate) would otherwise connect nearly every node and must be excluded before edge creation. When building the functional level of MetNet (reaction-content representation per pathway), which relies on reactions rather than compound-sharing edges. When the downstream analysis depends on cofactor-mediated connectivity itself (e.g. energy-transfer analysis) rather than discriminative pathway topology. When working with compound sets from sources other than KEGG reference pathways whose ubiquitous-compound semantics (H2O, phosphate, ATP, ADP) may differ. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Removes ubiquitous metabolites (e.g. H2O, phosphate, ATP, ADP) when deriving pathway–pathway relations from KEGG KGML compound sets, so that shared-compound edges in MetNet's structural level reflect meaningful metabolic overlap rather than universal cofactors. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0246962
skills.summary: Removes ubiquitous metabolites (e.g. H2O, phosphate, ATP, ADP) when deriving pathway–pathway relations from KEGG KGML compound sets, so that shared-compound edges in MetNet's structural level reflect meaningful metabolic overlap rather than universal cofactors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When building the functional level of MetNet (reaction-content representation per pathway), which relies on reactions rather than compound-sharing edges. When the downstream analysis depends on cofactor-mediated connectivity itself (e.g. energy-transfer analysis) rather than discriminative pathway topology. When working with compound sets from sources other than KEGG reference pathways whose ubiquitous-compound semantics (H2O, phosphate, ATP, ADP) may differ.

skills.description: Use when processing raw UK Biobank NMR metabolomics field exports (fields #23651-23948) to remove plate-, spectrometer-, and time-driven technical variation, or to detect non-biological outlier 96-well shipment plates before genetic/epidemiological analyses.
skills.name: ukbiobank-nmr-data-processing
skills.search_text: ukbiobank-nmr-data-processing Use when processing raw UK Biobank NMR metabolomics field exports (fields #23651-23948) to remove plate-, spectrometer-, and time-driven technical variation, or to detect non-biological outlier 96-well shipment plates before genetic/epidemiological analyses. Data has been pre-filtered to samples or biomarker columns before adjustment — remove_technical_variation() expects all the data to be present and no prefiltering should be performed Input is already QC-adjusted NMR biomarker data with technical covariates removed; re-running would regress out signal a second time Goal is to analyze composite biomarkers/ratios directly — those (61 composites, 81 ratios) must be recomputed from the 107 adjusted non-derived biomarkers post-adjustment http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 End-to-end R workflow using the ukbnmr package to quality-control UK Biobank NMR metabolic biomarker data: extracting exported field data, removing technical variation via sequential robust regressions, and identifying/removing outlier shipping plates of non-biological origin. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: End-to-end R workflow using the ukbnmr package to quality-control UK Biobank NMR metabolic biomarker data: extracting exported field data, removing technical variation via sequential robust regressions, and identifying/removing outlier shipping plates of non-biological origin.

skills.summary: Aggregates the UK Biobank NMR biomarker measurement QC flags of underlying non-derived biomarkers into QC flags for each recomputed composite biomarker, biomarker ratio, and extended ratio after removal of technical variation.

skills.description: Use when a raw two-column ion mass / intensity peak list from ultrahigh-resolution MS needs a defensible noise cutoff prior to formula assignment, and the analyst must choose and validate an S/N threshold.
skills.name: ultrahigh-resolution-ms-noise-threshold-application
skills.search_text: ultrahigh-resolution-ms-noise-threshold-application Use when a raw two-column ion mass / intensity peak list from ultrahigh-resolution MS needs a defensible noise cutoff prior to formula assignment, and the analyst must choose and validate an S/N threshold. Input spectra are not ultrahigh-resolution mass spectra (e.g. low-resolution unit-mass data) where Kendrick-mass-defect noise separation is unreliable A noise threshold has already been established and validated for the dataset — re-running noise estimation on pre-filtered Mono peak lists is out of scope The data are very discontinuous MS/MS spectra; the MFAssign 'MSMS' parameter path bypasses pre-filtering of ions below the de novo threshold instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Estimate the noise level of an ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrum (FT-ICR / Orbitrap) using MFAssignR's KMDNoise (Kendrick mass defect based) or HistNoise (natural log intensity histogram, Zhurov et al. 2014) methods, then apply the resulting S/N threshold to retain only peaks above noise before isotope filtering and molecular formula assignment. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.envres.2020.110114
skills.summary: Estimate the noise level of an ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrum (FT-ICR / Orbitrap) using MFAssignR's KMDNoise (Kendrick mass defect based) or HistNoise (natural log intensity histogram, Zhurov et al. 2014) methods, then apply the resulting S/N threshold to retain only peaks above noise before isotope filtering and molecular formula assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not ultrahigh-resolution mass spectra (e.g. low-resolution unit-mass data) where Kendrick-mass-defect noise separation is unreliable A noise threshold has already been established and validated for the dataset — re-running noise estimation on pre-filtered Mono peak lists is out of scope The data are very discontinuous MS/MS spectra; the MFAssign 'MSMS' parameter path bypasses pre-filtering of ions below the de novo threshold instead

skills.description: Use when you have SMILES sampled from a chemical language model checkpoint and need to verify metabolite-likeness: generated structures should be indistinguishable from withheld test-fold metabolites in fingerprint space.
skills.name: umap-chemical-space-overlap-visualization
skills.search_text: umap-chemical-space-overlap-visualization Use when you have SMILES sampled from a chemical language model checkpoint and need to verify metabolite-likeness: generated structures should be indistinguishable from withheld test-fold metabolites in fingerprint space. The language model was trained on a non-human metabolome (e.g., plant or bacterial metabolism) — the article notes evolutionarily distant applications likely require bespoke models, so human-metabolome benchmarks like this do not transfer directly. Your goal is to prioritize generated structures by mass-to-charge ratio against MS/MS data rather than to assess overall metabolite-likeness of the sampled set. Sampled molecules have not been de-duplicated against the training fold via InChIKey — memorized training structures will deflate the apparent novelty and distort the overlap assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates whether molecules sampled from a trained chemical language model (DeepMet/CLM) occupy the same chemical space as real metabolites by embedding RDKit molecular fingerprints with UMAP and confirming that a random forest classifier can only separate generated from withheld metabolites at chance level (AUC ~0.48). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.11.13.623458
skills.summary: Evaluates whether molecules sampled from a trained chemical language model (DeepMet/CLM) occupy the same chemical space as real metabolites by embedding RDKit molecular fingerprints with UMAP and confirming that a random forest classifier can only separate generated from withheld metabolites at chance level (AUC ~0.48).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The language model was trained on a non-human metabolome (e.g., plant or bacterial metabolism) — the article notes evolutionarily distant applications likely require bespoke models, so human-metabolome benchmarks like this do not transfer directly. Your goal is to prioritize generated structures by mass-to-charge ratio against MS/MS data rather than to assess overall metabolite-likeness of the sampled set. Sampled molecules have not been de-duplicated against the training fold via InChIKey — memorized training structures will deflate the apparent novelty and distort the overlap assessment.

skills.description: Use when you have SMILES structure annotations from two or more MGF-format MS/MS spectral libraries and want to visualize and compare their chemical-space coverage and overlap via dimensionality reduction.
skills.name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have SMILES structure annotations from two or more MGF-format MS/MS spectral libraries and want to visualize and compare their chemical-space coverage and overlap via dimensionality reduction. You need a quantitative, statistically rigorous chemical-space comparison (e.g., descriptor-space diversity metrics) rather than a qualitative 2D visualization Input spectra lack SMILES structure annotations, so no molecular feature matrix can be built from the libraries You are comparing spectra-level properties (peaks, adducts, ionization modes) rather than structure-level chemical-space coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Compute a 2D UMAP embedding of standardized, deduplicated chemical structures (SMILES) pooled from Spectraverse, MassSpecGym, and NPLIB1, then render per-library 2D density shading to qualitatively compare chemical-space coverage across MS/MS spectral libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06256
skills.summary: Compute a 2D UMAP embedding of standardized, deduplicated chemical structures (SMILES) pooled from Spectraverse, MassSpecGym, and NPLIB1, then render per-library 2D density shading to qualitatively compare chemical-space coverage across MS/MS spectral libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a quantitative, statistically rigorous chemical-space comparison (e.g., descriptor-space diversity metrics) rather than a qualitative 2D visualization Input spectra lack SMILES structure annotations, so no molecular feature matrix can be built from the libraries You are comparing spectra-level properties (peaks, adducts, ionization modes) rather than structure-level chemical-space coverage

skills.description: Use when you have a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (CSV with X/Y pixel coordinates plus m/z intensity columns) and need pixel-level clustering to identify tissue regions, e.g. k=25 clusters over a mouse brain coronal section.
skills.name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (CSV with X/Y pixel coordinates plus m/z intensity columns) and need pixel-level clustering to identify tissue regions, e.g. k=25 clusters over a mouse brain coronal section. Input is raw IMS spectra or imzML rather than the required pre-extracted feature matrix CSV (X/Y columns + m/z intensity columns) The goal is metabolite-level (ion) clustering by spatial co-expression, not pixel-level tissue-region clustering The tissue region number is known in advance to differ substantially from k=25, or clusters must be smaller than pixel-scale anatomical divisions — SMAnalyst also offers Seurat-LV, Seurat-LM, and Seurat-SLM as alternative pixel clustering algorithms http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 UMAP-based dimensionality reduction embedded in SMAnalyst's UMAP-kmeans pixel-clustering option, which projects high-dimensional spatial metabolomics feature matrices (e.g., 14,260 pixels × 3,044 m/z ion columns) into a low-dimensional space so that k-means can delineate tissue regions, reproducing anatomical divisions such as cortex, hippocampus, midbrain, hindbrain, and fiber tracts. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: UMAP-based dimensionality reduction embedded in SMAnalyst's UMAP-kmeans pixel-clustering option, which projects high-dimensional spatial metabolomics feature matrices (e.g., 14,260 pixels × 3,044 m/z ion columns) into a low-dimensional space so that k-means can delineate tissue regions, reproducing anatomical divisions such as cortex, hippocampus, midbrain, hindbrain, and fiber tracts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw IMS spectra or imzML rather than the required pre-extracted feature matrix CSV (X/Y columns + m/z intensity columns) The goal is metabolite-level (ion) clustering by spatial co-expression, not pixel-level tissue-region clustering The tissue region number is known in advance to differ substantially from k=25, or clusters must be smaller than pixel-scale anatomical divisions — SMAnalyst also offers Seurat-LV, Seurat-LM, and Seurat-SLM as alternative pixel clustering algorithms

skills.description: Use when learned ion-image embeddings (e.g., 512-d vectors from a contrastive encoder) must be compressed to a low-dimensional dense vector before ranking top colocalized ions by distance in an MSI analysis.
skills.name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction Use when learned ion-image embeddings (e.g., 512-d vectors from a contrastive encoder) must be compressed to a low-dimensional dense vector before ranking top colocalized ions by distance in an MSI analysis. The representation is already a low-dimensional feature table (reducing again risks discarding the information the 20-d trade-off was calibrated for). The task is isotope-ion identification with DeepION's ISO mode where the goal is intensity-dependent missing-value augmentation rather than COL-mode colocalization retrieval. You intend to train or evaluate the encoder itself — UMAP is a post-hoc dimensionality-reduction step, not a training objective. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reduce high-dimensional ion-image representations (e.g., 512-d ResNet18 encoder outputs from DeepION) to a 20-dimensional dense vector with UMAP, then min–max scale to [0,1] so distance-based colocalized-ion similarity retrieval can be performed. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c05002
skills.summary: Reduce high-dimensional ion-image representations (e.g., 512-d ResNet18 encoder outputs from DeepION) to a 20-dimensional dense vector with UMAP, then min–max scale to [0,1] so distance-based colocalized-ion similarity retrieval can be performed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The representation is already a low-dimensional feature table (reducing again risks discarding the information the 20-d trade-off was calibrated for). The task is isotope-ion identification with DeepION's ISO mode where the goal is intensity-dependent missing-value augmentation rather than COL-mode colocalization retrieval. You intend to train or evaluate the encoder itself — UMAP is a post-hoc dimensionality-reduction step, not a training objective.

skills.description: Use when raw imzML MALDI MSI pixel spectra need unsupervised grouping by spectral similarity — e.g. for tissue segmentation, matrix/off-tissue pixel detection, or resolving molecular heterogeneity of a cell population — and no cluster number is known a priori.
skills.name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-of-msi-pixel-spectra
skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction-of-msi-pixel-spectra Use when raw imzML MALDI MSI pixel spectra need unsupervised grouping by spectral similarity — e.g. for tissue segmentation, matrix/off-tissue pixel detection, or resolving molecular heterogeneity of a cell population — and no cluster number is known a priori. Input is already a reduced/feature table (e.g. peak list or ROI intensity matrix) rather than pixel-level spectra — use region_group_analysis_flow or statistical workflows instead A supervised comparison between sample groups is the goal (use molecular_signatures_flow ML classification), since UMAP is an unsupervised exploratory embedding The dataset lacks sufficient pixels per sample or memory (the segmentation example data requires at least 120 GB RAM), making a full-sample UMAP embedding infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reduce each sample's MALDI MSI pixel spectra (e.g. t-MALDI-2 imzML data) to a 2-dimensional UMAP embedding that groups pixels by spectral similarity, as implemented in msiFlow's segmentation and molecular-heterogeneity workflows prior to HDBSCAN clustering. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-024-55306-7
skills.summary: Reduce each sample's MALDI MSI pixel spectra (e.g. t-MALDI-2 imzML data) to a 2-dimensional UMAP embedding that groups pixels by spectral similarity, as implemented in msiFlow's segmentation and molecular-heterogeneity workflows prior to HDBSCAN clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced/feature table (e.g. peak list or ROI intensity matrix) rather than pixel-level spectra — use region_group_analysis_flow or statistical workflows instead A supervised comparison between sample groups is the goal (use molecular_signatures_flow ML classification), since UMAP is an unsupervised exploratory embedding The dataset lacks sufficient pixels per sample or memory (the segmentation example data requires at least 120 GB RAM), making a full-sample UMAP embedding infeasible

skills.description: Use when a trained VAE has produced a low-dimensional latent variable (e.g. 5-dim Code layer output) for tens of thousands of MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra and you need a 2D embedding to visually assess normal/tumor class separation.
skills.name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization Use when a trained VAE has produced a low-dimensional latent variable (e.g. 5-dim Code layer output) for tens of thousands of MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra and you need a 2D embedding to visually assess normal/tumor class separation. When the goal is classification accuracy metrics (ROC, accuracy, recall, precision, F1) — use the massNet classifier evaluation on the test set instead; UMAP here is only a visualization of the training-set latent space When you only have raw mass spectra (85,062 m/z variables) and no trained encoder — applying UMAP directly to the high-dimensional spectra is exactly the curse-of-dimensionality situation this skill avoids When multi-class or quantitative cluster statistics are required — the paper demonstrates only binary normal vs tumor visualization and notes multi-class extension is future work Applies UMAP, a non-linear dimensionality reduction method, to the 5-dimensional latent variable captured at the Code layer of the trained massNet VAE to embed MALDI FT-ICR mass spectra in a 2D space for visualizing normal vs tumor class separation. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Applies UMAP, a non-linear dimensionality reduction method, to the 5-dimensional latent variable captured at the Code layer of the trained massNet VAE to embed MALDI FT-ICR mass spectra in a 2D space for visualizing normal vs tumor class separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is classification accuracy metrics (ROC, accuracy, recall, precision, F1) — use the massNet classifier evaluation on the test set instead; UMAP here is only a visualization of the training-set latent space When you only have raw mass spectra (85,062 m/z variables) and no trained encoder — applying UMAP directly to the high-dimensional spectra is exactly the curse-of-dimensionality situation this skill avoids When multi-class or quantitative cluster statistics are required — the paper demonstrates only binary normal vs tumor visualization and notes multi-class extension is future work

skills.search_text: umap-embedding-of-metabolic-profiles Use when you have a per-cell normalized metabolic profile matrix (e.g. SpaceM's MORPHnMOL.csv with ~30k cells) and need a 2D visualization of resolved metabolic states after graph-based clustering. skills.description: Use when you have an aligned MEMO matrix of MS2 fingerprints (e.g. 1,600 plant extracts) and need a 2D ordination to check whether biologically active samples co-cluster or appear as singletons.
skills.name: umap-embedding-of-ms2-fingerprint-matrices
skills.search_text: umap-embedding-of-ms2-fingerprint-matrices Use when you have an aligned MEMO matrix of MS2 fingerprints (e.g. 1,600 plant extracts) and need a 2D ordination to check whether biologically active samples co-cluster or appear as singletons. The samples are not chemodiverse but share strong feature overlap and were acquired under identical LC conditions — MEMO is positioned for poor feature overlap, RT shifts, or cross-platform (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) comparisons You need a quantitative distance matrix rather than a 2D visualization (use MDS/PCoA on the aligned fingerprints instead) The MS2 spectra have not yet been vectorized into an aligned MEMO matrix — fingerprint generation and alignment must precede UMAP embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Embed a sample-wise normalized MEMO matrix (MS2 peak/neutral-loss fingerprints) into 2D UMAP space using the memo_ms visualization module, optionally alongside an RT-agnostic TMAP tree, to expose sample clustering in chemodiverse LC-MS/MS datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fbinf.2022.842964
skills.summary: Embed a sample-wise normalized MEMO matrix (MS2 peak/neutral-loss fingerprints) into 2D UMAP space using the memo_ms visualization module, optionally alongside an RT-agnostic TMAP tree, to expose sample clustering in chemodiverse LC-MS/MS datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples are not chemodiverse but share strong feature overlap and were acquired under identical LC conditions — MEMO is positioned for poor feature overlap, RT shifts, or cross-platform (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) comparisons You need a quantitative distance matrix rather than a 2D visualization (use MDS/PCoA on the aligned fingerprints instead) The MS2 spectra have not yet been vectorized into an aligned MEMO matrix — fingerprint generation and alignment must precede UMAP embedding

skills.description: Use when a trained FIORA checkpoint and a test compound set are available and you need to verify that graph embeddings encode chemical class structure (Fig. 4) by UMAP clustering plus per-superclass cosine similarity medians.
skills.name: umap-embedding-visualization

skills.description: Use when you have peak-listed tandem mass spectra (e.g. MGF files) from two or more samples and need a quantitative distance matrix of peptide sharing without peptide identifications or a sequence database.
skills.name: unannotated-spectral-dataset-similarity-analysis
skills.search_text: unannotated-spectral-dataset-similarity-analysis Use when you have peak-listed tandem mass spectra (e.g. MGF files) from two or more samples and need a quantitative distance matrix of peptide sharing without peptide identifications or a sequence database. You need peptide sequence identifications or quantification of specific proteins — compareMS2 deliberately skips database or spectral library searches and gives only a global dataset-level similarity You only have a small annotated subset of identified spectra rather than all acquired unannotated MS2 spectra — the method's power comes from using all acquired data You need to distinguish samples where only protein abundance/coverage differs from the same species — the distance metric is affected by both amino acid sequences and protein abundance http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Implements the compareMS2 approach of computing global similarity between tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) datasets by comparing unannotated MS2 spectra directly via dot products, then inverting the shared-peptide fraction into a pairwise distance metric for phylogenetics, QC, or species identification. metabolomics/v3 10.1002/rcm.6162
skills.summary: Implements the compareMS2 approach of computing global similarity between tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) datasets by comparing unannotated MS2 spectra directly via dot products, then inverting the shared-peptide fraction into a pairwise distance metric for phylogenetics, QC, or species identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need peptide sequence identifications or quantification of specific proteins — compareMS2 deliberately skips database or spectral library searches and gives only a global dataset-level similarity You only have a small annotated subset of identified spectra rather than all acquired unannotated MS2 spectra — the method's power comes from using all acquired data You need to distinguish samples where only protein abundance/coverage differs from the same species — the distance metric is affected by both amino acid sequences and protein abundance

skills.description: Use when performing stability selection for differential GGM network estimation (DNEA/Filigree-style) on two-condition metabolomics data where group sizes are unbalanced and per-edge selection probabilities must weight the lambda penalty in final network estimation.
skills.name: unbalanced-group-subsampling-protocol
skills.search_text: unbalanced-group-subsampling-protocol Use when performing stability selection for differential GGM network estimation (DNEA/Filigree-style) on two-condition metabolomics data where group sizes are unbalanced and per-edge selection probabilities must weight the lambda penalty in final network estimation. Groups are already balanced — the article's TEDDY demo ran stability selection 'without additional subsampling' when subsampling was not needed, and unnecessary subsampling discards samples Datasets too small for the BIC tuning protocol (~500 or more samples per group required) — switch to the Eq. 3 lambda approximation instead of the tuned-lambda + subsampling pipeline Input is a single experimental condition with no group comparison — joint two-group estimation and its subsampling protocol do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A subsampling scheme inside the DNEA stabilitySelection() step that equalizes group representation when the two experimental conditions are unbalanced (e.g., 50 DM:case vs 272 DM:control TEDDY samples), so per-edge selection probabilities for GGM regularization reflect both groups fairly. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-05994-1
skills.summary: A subsampling scheme inside the DNEA stabilitySelection() step that equalizes group representation when the two experimental conditions are unbalanced (e.g., 50 DM:case vs 272 DM:control TEDDY samples), so per-edge selection probabilities for GGM regularization reflect both groups fairly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Groups are already balanced — the article's TEDDY demo ran stability selection 'without additional subsampling' when subsampling was not needed, and unnecessary subsampling discards samples Datasets too small for the BIC tuning protocol (~500 or more samples per group required) — switch to the Eq. 3 lambda approximation instead of the tuned-lambda + subsampling pipeline Input is a single experimental condition with no group comparison — joint two-group estimation and its subsampling protocol do not apply

skills.description: Use when MS2DeepScore-predicted Tanimoto similarities contain unreliable spectra (low information content, chimeric spectra, or spectra dissimilar to training data) and you need to filter them using per-spectrum embedding-quality estimates.
skills.name: uncertainty-based-spectrum-filtering
skills.search_text: uncertainty-based-spectrum-filtering Use when MS2DeepScore-predicted Tanimoto similarities contain unreliable spectra (low information content, chimeric spectra, or spectra dissimilar to training data) and you need to filter them using per-spectrum embedding-quality estimates. The MS2DeepScore model you use was trained without an embedding evaluator (SettingsEmbeddingEvaluator left as None), so no per-spectrum predicted MSE is available. All input spectra are known to closely match the training data with high spectral quality, so uncertainty filtering would remove informative spectra without benefit. You need similarities for a model trained on only one ionization mode (e.g., DreaMS, trained only on positive-mode spectra), where the cross-mode quality-estimation setup does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ranks tandem mass spectra by a per-spectrum predicted MSE from the InceptionTime embedding evaluator wrapped around MS2DeepScore 2.0, then iteratively removes the highest-uncertainty spectra to raise the accuracy of predicted Tanimoto similarities on the retained spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.03.25.586580
skills.summary: Ranks tandem mass spectra by a per-spectrum predicted MSE from the InceptionTime embedding evaluator wrapped around MS2DeepScore 2.0, then iteratively removes the highest-uncertainty spectra to raise the accuracy of predicted Tanimoto similarities on the retained spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The MS2DeepScore model you use was trained without an embedding evaluator (SettingsEmbeddingEvaluator left as None), so no per-spectrum predicted MSE is available. All input spectra are known to closely match the training data with high spectral quality, so uncertainty filtering would remove informative spectra without benefit. You need similarities for a model trained on only one ionization mode (e.g., DreaMS, trained only on positive-mode spectra), where the cross-mode quality-estimation setup does not apply.

skills.description: Use when a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (any nucleus, e.g. 1H, 13C, 31P) needs per-signal fitted parameters with reported standard-deviation uncertainties, such as monitoring metabolite signals over a real-time assay.
skills.name: uncertainty-estimation-of-fitted-spectral-parameters
skills.search_text: uncertainty-estimation-of-fitted-spectral-parameters Use when a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (any nucleus, e.g. 1H, 13C, 31P) needs per-signal fitted parameters with reported standard-deviation uncertainties, such as monitoring metabolite signals over a real-time assay. The data are full multi-dimensional (nD) NMR spectra rather than a series of 1D or pseudo-2D spectra, which is outside MultiNMRFit's scope Only raw peak positions are needed without quantitative fitting or uncertainty estimates (use simple peak picking instead) The spectra require higher-order baseline correction beyond zero-order baseline, which is what the models account for Estimates NMR signal parameters (intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, coupling constants) together with their standard-deviation uncertainties by fitting 1D or pseudo-2D spectra with MultiNMRFit's built-in multiplet signal models, demonstrated on 1H, 13C, and 31P datasets such as real-time glycolysis assays. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf463
skills.summary: Estimates NMR signal parameters (intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, coupling constants) together with their standard-deviation uncertainties by fitting 1D or pseudo-2D spectra with MultiNMRFit's built-in multiplet signal models, demonstrated on 1H, 13C, and 31P datasets such as real-time glycolysis assays.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are full multi-dimensional (nD) NMR spectra rather than a series of 1D or pseudo-2D spectra, which is outside MultiNMRFit's scope Only raw peak positions are needed without quantitative fitting or uncertainty estimates (use simple peak picking instead) The spectra require higher-order baseline correction beyond zero-order baseline, which is what the models account for

skills.description: Use when computing Spec2Vec similarity scores for spectra against a pretrained Word2Vec model and you must decide whether the score is trustworthy because query peaks/losses fall outside the model vocabulary.
skills.name: uncovered-peak-missing-fraction-computation
skills.search_text: uncovered-peak-missing-fraction-computation Use when computing Spec2Vec similarity scores for spectra against a pretrained Word2Vec model and you must decide whether the score is trustworthy because query peaks/losses fall outside the model vocabulary. Scoring with plain cosine or modified cosine similarity — these do not depend on a learned vocabulary, so missing fractions are irrelevant The model was trained on a small dataset or with high m/z decimal precision, where most query words may be missing and the <0.05 threshold would flag nearly everything — retraining including the new experimental spectra may be needed The training set does not include a large fraction of the fragment-ion and neutral-loss features seen in the query data (e.g. far-out-of-model compound classes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Quantifies how much of a spectrum's intensity-weighted peak/loss signal is represented by tokens absent from a trained Spec2Vec (Word2Vec/gensim) model vocabulary, so that Spec2Vec cosine scores are only returned for spectra actually 'in-model'. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Quantifies how much of a spectrum's intensity-weighted peak/loss signal is represented by tokens absent from a trained Spec2Vec (Word2Vec/gensim) model vocabulary, so that Spec2Vec cosine scores are only returned for spectra actually 'in-model'.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scoring with plain cosine or modified cosine similarity — these do not depend on a learned vocabulary, so missing fractions are irrelevant The model was trained on a small dataset or with high m/z decimal precision, where most query words may be missing and the <0.05 threshold would flag nearly everything — retraining including the new experimental spectra may be needed The training set does not include a large fraction of the fragment-ion and neutral-loss features seen in the query data (e.g. far-out-of-model compound classes)

skills.search_text: undirected-graph-connected-component-decomposition Use when a preprocessed LC-MS peak table contains multiple correlated features per metabolite (e.g. adducts/isotopes) that must be collapsed into one representative per compound before statistics or identification. Input is raw LC-MS instrument data rather than a preprocessed peak table — notame expects data already peak-picked (e.g. by MS-DIAL) The feature table has already been aggregated so that each metabolite is a single unique feature with no adduct/isotope multiplicity left to group The goal is clustering of samples (phenotypes) rather than grouping molecular features that originate from the same metabolite http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Groups molecular features originating from the same metabolite in an LC-MS data matrix by building an undirected correlation graph (nodes = features, edges = Pearson correlations within a retention-time window) and recursively extracting clusters from its connected components, as implemented in the notame R package. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo10040135

skills.description: Use when a LipiDex 2 Peak Finder peak table contains unidentified features (possible lipid adducts, isotopes, dimers, or co-eluting spurious peaks) that need to be distinguished from genuine novel lipids sharing a retention time with an identified feature.
skills.name: unidentified-feature-qc-criteria
skills.search_text: unidentified-feature-qc-criteria Use when a LipiDex 2 Peak Finder peak table contains unidentified features (possible lipid adducts, isotopes, dimers, or co-eluting spurious peaks) that need to be distinguished from genuine novel lipids sharing a retention time with an identified feature. Input is a fully identified feature table with no unidentified peaks — this skill's filter logic targets unidentified features only You need to filter identified lipid annotations (e.g., >30% RSD in QC samples flagging or RT-model filtering); those are handled by other LipiDex 2 results-filtering criteria Sample count across non-QC, non-blank biosamples is below 10, making the minimum-appearances criterion untestable Applies LipiDex Peak Finder QC to unidentified chromatographic features: only features co-eluting with an identified lipid within a retention-time window, present in ≥10 biosamples, and strongly correlated with the identified feature (default r = 0.99) are retained as potential new lipids rather than filtered as spurious. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.4c00359
skills.summary: Applies LipiDex Peak Finder QC to unidentified chromatographic features: only features co-eluting with an identified lipid within a retention-time window, present in ≥10 biosamples, and strongly correlated with the identified feature (default r = 0.99) are retained as potential new lipids rather than filtered as spurious.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a fully identified feature table with no unidentified peaks — this skill's filter logic targets unidentified features only You need to filter identified lipid annotations (e.g., >30% RSD in QC samples flagging or RT-model filtering); those are handled by other LipiDex 2 results-filtering criteria Sample count across non-QC, non-blank biosamples is below 10, making the minimum-appearances criterion untestable

skills.description: Use when two taxonomic profilers report identical single-value metrics (e.g., UniFrac) against a gold standard and you need to verify the tie and identify which clades actually differ in relative abundance.
skills.name: unifrac-phylogenetic-distance-computation
skills.search_text: unifrac-phylogenetic-distance-computation Use when two taxonomic profilers report identical single-value metrics (e.g., UniFrac) against a gold standard and you need to verify the tie and identify which clades actually differ in relative abundance. When the profiles of interest already have distinct single-value scores — a tie is the trigger for this deep comparison When analyzing amplicon data: TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles, and tools like metacoder are not suitable for WGS profiles When no gold-standard/ground-truth profile exists — UniFrac against ground truth requires simulated data where the true distribution is known http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Compute and verify tied UniFrac phylogenetic distances between taxonomic profiler outputs and a gold-standard profile (e.g., Taxy-Pro vs MetaPhyler on CAMI_HIGH_S001), then use TAMPA to reveal per-taxon abundance differences that the identical single-value score conceals. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad008
skills.summary: Compute and verify tied UniFrac phylogenetic distances between taxonomic profiler outputs and a gold-standard profile (e.g., Taxy-Pro vs MetaPhyler on CAMI_HIGH_S001), then use TAMPA to reveal per-taxon abundance differences that the identical single-value score conceals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the profiles of interest already have distinct single-value scores — a tie is the trigger for this deep comparison When analyzing amplicon data: TAMPA is designed for WGS metagenomic taxonomic profiles, and tools like metacoder are not suitable for WGS profiles When no gold-standard/ground-truth profile exists — UniFrac against ground truth requires simulated data where the true distribution is known

skills.description: Use when a metabolite-to-protein step yields UniProt IDs (e.g., scraped from HMDB metabolite pages) and downstream over-representation analysis requires current human gene symbols instead.
