skills.search_text: uniprot-to-gene-symbol-mapping Use when a metabolite-to-protein step yields UniProt IDs (e.g., scraped from HMDB metabolite pages) and downstream over-representation analysis requires current human gene symbols instead. Identifiers are already gene symbols or HGNC IDs — re-mapping adds no information and risks symbol drift. The downstream analysis uses a background gene universe other than the HMDB-derived discoverableGenes list, so consistency checks against discoverableGenes_akaAllGenesInHMDB_2021_10_14.RData would be invalid. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts UniProt protein identifiers retrieved from metabolite interaction records (e.g., HMDB metabolite pages) into a deduplicated set of current human gene symbols, producing the metabolite-interacting gene set that metGWAS 1.0 uses for over-representation analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad523
skills.summary: Converts UniProt protein identifiers retrieved from metabolite interaction records (e.g., HMDB metabolite pages) into a deduplicated set of current human gene symbols, producing the metabolite-interacting gene set that metGWAS 1.0 uses for over-representation analysis.

The downstream analysis uses a background gene universe other than the HMDB-derived discoverableGenes list, so consistency checks against discoverableGenes_akaAllGenesInHMDB_2021_10_14.RData would be invalid.

skills.description: Use when a model produces a probability distribution over molecular fragments with exact atomic-composition masses and you need to convert it into a final mass spectrum at 1 Da (or 0.1 Da) resolution.
skills.name: unit-dalton-spectrum-normalization
skills.search_text: unit-dalton-spectrum-normalization Use when a model produces a probability distribution over molecular fragments with exact atomic-composition masses and you need to convert it into a final mass spectrum at 1 Da (or 0.1 Da) resolution. Input is already a measured or library spectrum (e.g. NIST-format spectrum) — no probability-weighted fragment summation is needed; use it only when reconstructing from a fragment probability distribution. Fragments carry only nominal (integer) masses without isotope/mass-defect information — the method requires exact masses computed with isotopic variability at natural abundance. The number of unique fragment formulae exceeds the RASSP filter cap (≤4096 unique fragment formulae, molecules ≤48 atoms for HCONFSPCl) — outside this regime the described enumeration/observation model was not validated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reconstructs a predicted EI–MS spectrum by binning probability-weighted fragment mass spectra into integer-Dalton (or 0.10 Da) bins, mirroring RASSP's observation model that sums formula/subset spectra weighted by the model's output probability. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c02093
skills.summary: Reconstructs a predicted EI–MS spectrum by binning probability-weighted fragment mass spectra into integer-Dalton (or 0.10 Da) bins, mirroring RASSP's observation model that sums formula/subset spectra weighted by the model's output probability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a measured or library spectrum (e.g. NIST-format spectrum) — no probability-weighted fragment summation is needed; use it only when reconstructing from a fragment probability distribution. Fragments carry only nominal (integer) masses without isotope/mass-defect information — the method requires exact masses computed with isotopic variability at natural abundance. The number of unique fragment formulae exceeds the RASSP filter cap (≤4096 unique fragment formulae, molecules ≤48 atoms for HCONFSPCl) — outside this regime the described enumeration/observation model was not validated.

skills.description: Use when comparing raw vs. signal-drift-corrected feature matrices from LC-MS metabolomics or proteomics (e.g., XCMS or Skyline outputs) to count significant features via Welch's T-test with BH FDR and assess how correction improves statistical accuracy.
skills.name: univariate-differential-feature-testing
skills.search_text: univariate-differential-feature-testing Use when comparing raw vs. signal-drift-corrected feature matrices from LC-MS metabolomics or proteomics (e.g., XCMS or Skyline outputs) to count significant features via Welch's T-test with BH FDR and assess how correction improves statistical accuracy. Input is a single already-corrected feature matrix and the goal is only descriptive QC (RSD distributions) rather than raw-vs-corrected differential-feature comparison — QC-RFSC correction and statAnalysis on one matrix alone does not yield the enlargement metric. Data have not been peak-extracted into a statTarget-compatible feature table (e.g., still vendor MS raw files); use the transX function to convert XCMS/MZmine2/SIEVE/SKYLINE outputs to statTarget input format first. The comparison targets batch-integration quality (e.g., Combat-based QC-free correction via shiftCor_dQC) rather than QC-injection-anchored signal drift correction; mixing correction modes undermines the raw-vs-QC-RFSC enlargement interpretation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs statTarget's statAnalysis function (Welch's T-test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment, 80% rule filtering, KNN imputation, glog transform, Pareto scaling) on raw and QC-RFSC-corrected metabolomics/proteomics feature matrices to count differential features and quantify how signal drift correction enlarges the number of statistically significant features. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.aca.2018.08.002
skills.summary: Runs statTarget's statAnalysis function (Welch's T-test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment, 80% rule filtering, KNN imputation, glog transform, Pareto scaling) on raw and QC-RFSC-corrected metabolomics/proteomics feature matrices to count differential features and quantify how signal drift correction enlarges the number of statistically significant features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single already-corrected feature matrix and the goal is only descriptive QC (RSD distributions) rather than raw-vs-corrected differential-feature comparison — QC-RFSC correction and statAnalysis on one matrix alone does not yield the enlargement metric. Data have not been peak-extracted into a statTarget-compatible feature table (e.g., still vendor MS raw files); use the transX function to convert XCMS/MZmine2/SIEVE/SKYLINE outputs to statTarget input format first. The comparison targets batch-integration quality (e.g., Combat-based QC-free correction via shiftCor_dQC) rather than QC-injection-anchored signal drift correction; mixing correction modes undermines the raw-vs-QC-RFSC enlargement interpretation.

Raw MS data still requiring peak picking and annotation — iMAP deliberately did not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking/annotation modules The input matrix has not passed through data-processing (missing values, normalization, batch effect correcting, QC-based removal of unstable variables), so univariate statistics would be computed on unfiltered data The goal is phenotype prediction/model building rather than metabolite selection — use iMAP's automatic train-test separation, feature selection, and predictive model construction module instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 A metabolites-selection step from the iMAP framework (Zhou et al., 2021, Frontiers in Chemistry) in which statistical analysis on the processed peak-intensity matrix identifies/select significantly changed or phenotype-correlated metabolites using user-set P-value/FDR/|log2FC| thresholds, optionally combined with multivariate VIP-based selection via Union/Intersection summary modules. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fchem.2021.659656
skills.summary: A metabolites-selection step from the iMAP framework (Zhou et al., 2021, Frontiers in Chemistry) in which statistical analysis on the processed peak-intensity matrix identifies/select significantly changed or phenotype-correlated metabolites using user-set P-value/FDR/|log2FC| thresholds, optionally combined with multivariate VIP-based selection via Union/Intersection summary modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw MS data still requiring peak picking and annotation — iMAP deliberately did not implement raw data preprocessing or peak picking/annotation modules The input matrix has not passed through data-processing (missing values, normalization, batch effect correcting, QC-based removal of unstable variables), so univariate statistics would be computed on unfiltered data The goal is phenotype prediction/model building rather than metabolite selection — use iMAP's automatic train-test separation, feature selection, and predictive model construction module instead

skills.description: Use when you have a QC-passed LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, intensities) with infected vs. control/baseline sample groups and need to select significantly altered features before pathway analysis.

skills.search_text: univariate-statistical-feature-selection Use when you have a QC-passed LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, intensities) with infected vs. control/baseline sample groups and need to select significantly altered features before pathway analysis. skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a statistically tested feature table with p-values that mummichog can consume directly (re-running selection would duplicate work) The analysis goal is metabolite identification from fragmentation spectra, which this skill does not address The data require multivariate or in vivo study design analysis, where the paper notes validation is particularly challenging and this simple univariate cutoff approach is insufficient

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized m/z peak table from MS metabolomics data with a two-group (or paired) design variable and need to rank m/z values by differential intensity.
skills.name: univariate-ttest-mz-screening
skills.search_text: univariate-ttest-mz-screening Use when you have a normalized m/z peak table from MS metabolomics data with a two-group (or paired) design variable and need to rank m/z values by differential intensity. The data are raw, un-normalized peak intensities that have not gone through MetaboShiny's filtering/normalization/imputation pipeline The design involves more than two groups or multi-factor variables — use ANOVA, ASCA, MEBA, or two-factor analysis modes instead The goal is metabolite annotation of all m/z values rather than screening for significant hits — MetaboShiny performs annotation only on significant hits from the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Run MetaboAnalystR-backed two-group t-tests directly on m/z peak intensities to rank which m/z values differ significantly between two experimental groups (e.g. lung cancer vs. control urine DI-MS samples). metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01717-8
skills.summary: Run MetaboAnalystR-backed two-group t-tests directly on m/z peak intensities to rank which m/z values differ significantly between two experimental groups (e.g. lung cancer vs. control urine DI-MS samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw, un-normalized peak intensities that have not gone through MetaboShiny's filtering/normalization/imputation pipeline The design involves more than two groups or multi-factor variables — use ANOVA, ASCA, MEBA, or two-factor analysis modes instead The goal is metabolite annotation of all m/z values rather than screening for significant hits — MetaboShiny performs annotation only on significant hits from the analysis

skills.description: Use when a specific tandem MS spectrum (e.g., a GNPS library entry CCMSLIB accessions, a MassIVE/MetaboLights MSV dataset scan, a MassBank accession, or an MS2LDA motif) must be addressed by URL for retrieval or visualization.
skills.name: universal-spectrum-identifier-construction
skills.search_text: universal-spectrum-identifier-construction Use when a specific tandem MS spectrum (e.g., a GNPS library entry CCMSLIB accessions, a MassIVE/MetaboLights MSV dataset scan, a MassBank accession, or an MS2LDA motif) must be addressed by URL for retrieval or visualization. When a database-independent, content-hashed identifier is required — SPLASH identifiers exist for that purpose, but 'generating a SPLASH identifier includes a complex hashing operation', so they are not trivially produced. When the spectrum is not held in a USI-supported source (GNPS, MassBank, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MS2LDA/MOTIFDB, ProteomeXchange) or lacks a resolvable scan/accession locator. When stable, finalized identifiers are required — the README warns these metabolomics identifiers are draft ('mzdraft') and subject to change. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Construct USI-formatted identifiers (mzspec:...) to address individual MS/MS spectra held in metabolomics and proteomics repositories — GNPS, MassBank, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MS2LDA, MOTIFDB, ProteomeXchange — so they can be retrieved and rendered by the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver web service. USIs are easy to build by hand, unlike SPLASH hashes, which require a complex hashing operation. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Construct USI-formatted identifiers (mzspec:...) to address individual MS/MS spectra held in metabolomics and proteomics repositories — GNPS, MassBank, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MS2LDA, MOTIFDB, ProteomeXchange — so they can be retrieved and rendered by the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver web service. USIs are easy to build by hand, unlike SPLASH hashes, which require a complex hashing operation.

When the spectrum is not held in a USI-supported source (GNPS, MassBank, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MS2LDA/MOTIFDB, ProteomeXchange) or lacks a resolvable scan/accession locator. skills.description: Use when a workflow needs to fetch a specific public MS/MS spectrum — e.g. a ProteomeXchange dataset scan like mzspec:PXD004732:...:scan:41840 or a GNPS library entry like mzspec:GNPSLIBRARY:CCMSLIB00000840351 — without downloading the source raw files.
skills.name: universal-spectrum-identifier-spectrum-retrieval
skills.search_text: universal-spectrum-identifier-spectrum-retrieval Use when a workflow needs to fetch a specific public MS/MS spectrum — e.g. a ProteomeXchange dataset scan like mzspec:PXD004732:...:scan:41840 or a GNPS library entry like mzspec:GNPSLIBRARY:CCMSLIB00000840351 — without downloading the source raw files. You already have local spectrum data (mzML, MGF, or in-memory peak arrays) — spectrum_utils does not provide raw-file reading functionality and you should use a reader such as pymzML or Pyteomics instead. You need bulk retrieval of entire datasets or chromatograms rather than individual spectra identified by USI. You are offline or the hosting resource for the USI is unreachable — from_usi fetches spectra over the network and will fail without connectivity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retrieves MS/MS spectra from online proteomics and metabolomics resources (ProteomeXchange, PRIDE, GNPS spectral library) by resolving a Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) via spectrum_utils's MsmsSpectrum.from_usi, eliminating local raw-file handling. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.9b04884
skills.summary: Retrieves MS/MS spectra from online proteomics and metabolomics resources (ProteomeXchange, PRIDE, GNPS spectral library) by resolving a Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) via spectrum_utils's MsmsSpectrum.from_usi, eliminating local raw-file handling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have local spectrum data (mzML, MGF, or in-memory peak arrays) — spectrum_utils does not provide raw-file reading functionality and you should use a reader such as pymzML or Pyteomics instead. You need bulk retrieval of entire datasets or chromatograms rather than individual spectra identified by USI. You are offline or the hosting resource for the USI is unreachable — from_usi fetches spectra over the network and will fail without connectivity.

skills.description: Use when you have a real/observed mzML file (e.g. output of a prior Top-N run) and want ViMMS 2.0 chemical input derived from empirically detected peaks rather than synthetically sampled compounds from HMDB.
skills.name: unknown-chemical-identification-free-construction
skills.search_text: unknown-chemical-identification-free-construction Use when you have a real/observed mzML file (e.g. output of a prior Top-N run) and want ViMMS 2.0 chemical input derived from empirically detected peaks rather than synthetically sampled compounds from HMDB. You need fully specified chemicals with known identities/formulae for simulation — use ChemicalMixtureCreator with HMDB sampling (hmdb_compounds.p) instead Your input is not mzML scan data (e.g. already a pickled chemical list, MGF spectra, or an MZmine aligned feature table like multibeers_2_aligned.csv) You want a fast, low-memory simulation and cannot afford the high object counts produced by low min_intensity thresholds Builds a chemical dataset for ViMMS 2.0 simulation by extracting ROIs from an existing mzML file (e.g. Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.mzML) via ChemicalMixtureFromMZML and converting each picked ROI into an UnknownChemical object, avoiding synthetic sampling from databases like HMDB. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Builds a chemical dataset for ViMMS 2.0 simulation by extracting ROIs from an existing mzML file (e.g. Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.mzML) via ChemicalMixtureFromMZML and converting each picked ROI into an UnknownChemical object, avoiding synthetic sampling from databases like HMDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need fully specified chemicals with known identities/formulae for simulation — use ChemicalMixtureCreator with HMDB sampling (hmdb_compounds.p) instead Your input is not mzML scan data (e.g. already a pickled chemical list, MGF spectra, or an MZmine aligned feature table like multibeers_2_aligned.csv) You want a fast, low-memory simulation and cannot afford the high object counts produced by low min_intensity thresholds

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains unannotated peaks (unknowns) lacking KEGG/PubChem identifiers, and the goal is to connect them to annotated compounds using mass spectral similarity rather than enzymatic or structural relationships.
skills.name: unknown-metabolite-annotation-linking
skills.search_text: unknown-metabolite-annotation-linking Use when a metabolomics feature table contains unannotated peaks (unknowns) lacking KEGG/PubChem identifiers, and the goal is to connect them to annotated compounds using mass spectral similarity rather than enzymatic or structural relationships. The metabolites of interest already have KEGG or PubChem CIDs and can be connected via KEGG RPAIR biochemical transformation networks instead The goal is structural similarity between known compounds (use PubChem Substructure Fingerprints with Tanimoto score >0.7, the paper's structural network threshold) The data are non-spectral empirical measurements (e.g. clinical covariates) where Pearson/biweight or Spearman empirical dependency networks, not cosine spectral similarity, are appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Links structurally unknown metabolites into a metabolic network via pairwise mass spectral similarity (cosine correlation) edges, as implemented in MetaMapR's spectral similarity network module, so that unannotated GC-TOF-MS features inherit biochemical context from identified neighbors. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv194
skills.summary: Links structurally unknown metabolites into a metabolic network via pairwise mass spectral similarity (cosine correlation) edges, as implemented in MetaMapR's spectral similarity network module, so that unannotated GC-TOF-MS features inherit biochemical context from identified neighbors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites of interest already have KEGG or PubChem CIDs and can be connected via KEGG RPAIR biochemical transformation networks instead The goal is structural similarity between known compounds (use PubChem Substructure Fingerprints with Tanimoto score >0.7, the paper's structural network threshold) The data are non-spectral empirical measurements (e.g. clinical covariates) where Pearson/biweight or Spearman empirical dependency networks, not cosine spectral similarity, are appropriate

skills.description: Use when LC-MS/MS peak tables and MS2 spectra from an S9 incubation (or similar in vitro enzymatic reaction) need KGMN unknown-peak annotations reproduced and validated, e.g. expected 39+69/700 pos and 41+106/741 neg peaks.
skills.name: unknown-metabolite-cascade-validation
skills.search_text: unknown-metabolite-cascade-validation Use when LC-MS/MS peak tables and MS2 spectra from an S9 incubation (or similar in vitro enzymatic reaction) need KGMN unknown-peak annotations reproduced and validated, e.g. expected 39+69/700 pos and 41+106/741 neg peaks. Non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles, since organism-specific databases are not yet incorporated and caution is advised Distinguishing structurally similar isomers of unknowns (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot discriminate effectively Cases where the input is already a fully annotated feature table with no unknown peaks requiring cascade annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Validates KGMN-annotated unknown metabolites in the 46std_mix human liver S9 incubation by reproducing the known-to-unknown annotation cascade per ionization mode and confirming IMP-derived unknowns (inosine and inosine 5'-sulfate) with authentic chemical standards. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Validates KGMN-annotated unknown metabolites in the 46std_mix human liver S9 incubation by reproducing the known-to-unknown annotation cascade per ionization mode and confirming IMP-derived unknowns (inosine and inosine 5'-sulfate) with authentic chemical standards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Non-model organisms or environmental/exposomics profiles, since organism-specific databases are not yet incorporated and caution is advised Distinguishing structurally similar isomers of unknowns (e.g., isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers), which KGMN cannot discriminate effectively Cases where the input is already a fully annotated feature table with no unknown peaks requiring cascade annotation

skills.description: Use when a list of putatively annotated unknown metabolites with precursor m/z and MS/MS spectra (e.g., from KGMN on NIST urine data) needs external corroboration via public-data recurrence rather than spectral-library or standard-based validation.
skills.name: unknown-metabolite-recurrence-analysis
skills.search_text: unknown-metabolite-recurrence-analysis Use when a list of putatively annotated unknown metabolites with precursor m/z and MS/MS spectra (e.g., from KGMN on NIST urine data) needs external corroboration via public-data recurrence rather than spectral-library or standard-based validation. The metabolites are knowns already matched against standard spectral libraries — recurrence mining targets unknowns absent from MS/MS libraries The goal is discriminating structurally similar isomers (e.g., glucuronidation product isomers of isocitrate), which the article states cannot be effectively distinguished by KGMN/MS2 similarity approaches No MS/MS spectra are available for the unknowns (MS1-only features cannot be searched via MASST) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Repository-mining of putatively annotated unknown MS/MS spectra by submitting them to GNPS MASST against all public GNPS/MassIVE datasets, then aggregating recurrence statistics (datasets, files, species, sample types) to corroborate KGMN unknown annotations absent from standard spectral libraries. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Repository-mining of putatively annotated unknown MS/MS spectra by submitting them to GNPS MASST against all public GNPS/MassIVE datasets, then aggregating recurrence statistics (datasets, files, species, sample types) to corroborate KGMN unknown annotations absent from standard spectral libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metabolites are knowns already matched against standard spectral libraries — recurrence mining targets unknowns absent from MS/MS libraries The goal is discriminating structurally similar isomers (e.g., glucuronidation product isomers of isocitrate), which the article states cannot be effectively distinguished by KGMN/MS2 similarity approaches No MS/MS spectra are available for the unknowns (MS1-only features cannot be searched via MASST)

skills.description: Use when a metabolic feature peak (e.g. M153T555, M182T541) is claimed by multiple overlapping KGMN subnetworks with conflicting annotations or base peaks, and annotations must be merged or pruned into one consolidated subnetwork.
skills.name: unknown-peak-annotation-consolidation
skills.search_text: unknown-peak-annotation-consolidation Use when a metabolic feature peak (e.g. M153T555, M182T541) is claimed by multiple overlapping KGMN subnetworks with conflicting annotations or base peaks, and annotations must be merged or pruned into one consolidated subnetwork. When constructing the global networks themselves rather than extracting/merging subnetworks from an already-built KGMN result When the feature is claimed by only a single non-overlapping subnetwork, so no consolidation decision is needed When distinguishing structurally similar isomers is the goal — KGMN cannot effectively discriminate such isomers (e.g. isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers) http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Consolidates overlapping KGMN peak-annotation subnetworks (metabolic-reaction, peak-to-peak, MS2-similarity layers) by merging redundant ion-form peaks and retaining the larger self-consistent subnetwork when conflicting base peaks arise, resolving claims of a metabolic feature by multiple subnetworks. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-022-34537-6
skills.summary: Consolidates overlapping KGMN peak-annotation subnetworks (metabolic-reaction, peak-to-peak, MS2-similarity layers) by merging redundant ion-form peaks and retaining the larger self-consistent subnetwork when conflicting base peaks arise, resolving claims of a metabolic feature by multiple subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When constructing the global networks themselves rather than extracting/merging subnetworks from an already-built KGMN result When the feature is claimed by only a single non-overlapping subnetwork, so no consolidation decision is needed When distinguishing structurally similar isomers is the goal — KGMN cannot effectively discriminate such isomers (e.g. isocitrate glucuronidation product isomers)

skills.description: Use when you have feature maps detected separately in multiple LC-MS runs (e.g., technical replicates or a dilution/spike-in series) and need a consensus feature map to extract per-run intensities for label-free quantification and reproducibility analysis.
skills.name: unlabeled-feature-linking-across-replicates
skills.search_text: unlabeled-feature-linking-across-replicates Use when you have feature maps detected separately in multiple LC-MS runs (e.g., technical replicates or a dilution/spike-in series) and need a consensus feature map to extract per-run intensities for label-free quantification and reproducibility analysis. Input is already a linked consensus feature table or a tabular intensity matrix — re-linking would duplicate the workflow step Runs contain labeled spike-in/protein markers that support correspondence-based linking rather than unlabeled (QS-based) feature linking Only a single LC-MS measurement needs feature detection — link across replicates is unnecessary; use FeatureFinderMetabo alone http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Links unlabeled features detected independently in each LC-MS run into a consensus feature map, so that the same metabolite can be quantified consistently across replicates and concentration levels. In the source study this step (FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT) underpins label-free quantification of 33 human plasma measurements from an 11-level spike-in series. metabolomics/v3 10.1074/mcp.m113.031278
skills.summary: Links unlabeled features detected independently in each LC-MS run into a consensus feature map, so that the same metabolite can be quantified consistently across replicates and concentration levels. In the source study this step (FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT) underpins label-free quantification of 33 human plasma measurements from an 11-level spike-in series.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a linked consensus feature table or a tabular intensity matrix — re-linking would duplicate the workflow step Runs contain labeled spike-in/protein markers that support correspondence-based linking rather than unlabeled (QS-based) feature linking Only a single LC-MS measurement needs feature detection — link across replicates is unnecessary; use FeatureFinderMetabo alone

skills.description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM data from a high-resolution analyzer (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000/280,000 nominal resolution) and an unlabeled-sample spectrum is available, especially for high-mass metabolites where resolution effects are strong.
skills.name: unlabeled-sample-based-correction
skills.search_text: unlabeled-sample-based-correction Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM data from a high-resolution analyzer (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000/280,000 nominal resolution) and an unlabeled-sample spectrum is available, especially for high-mass metabolites where resolution effects are strong. No unlabeled-sample measurement is available — ULS requires an additional experimental measurement; use the MDT-only path instead (ElemCor runs on mass difference theory when unlabeled data are not loaded). Small/low-mass metabolites — the article recommends MDT for low-mass compounds for cost efficiency, reserving ULS for high-mass compounds. The tracer element selected is not present in some compounds' formulas (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N data), which makes the algorithm report errors. The ULS correction method (as improved in ElemCor) builds the natural-abundance correction matrix by deconvolving the fractional abundance of measured isotopologs (FAM) of an unlabeled sample for the tracer element Nt times, then applies non-negative linear regression to recover the mass distribution vector (MDV) and isotopic enrichment at a specified instrument resolution. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: The ULS correction method (as improved in ElemCor) builds the natural-abundance correction matrix by deconvolving the fractional abundance of measured isotopologs (FAM) of an unlabeled sample for the tracer element Nt times, then applies non-negative linear regression to recover the mass distribution vector (MDV) and isotopic enrichment at a specified instrument resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No unlabeled-sample measurement is available — ULS requires an additional experimental measurement; use the MDT-only path instead (ElemCor runs on mass difference theory when unlabeled data are not loaded). Small/low-mass metabolites — the article recommends MDT for low-mass compounds for cost efficiency, reserving ULS for high-mass compounds. The tracer element selected is not present in some compounds' formulas (e.g., selecting C or S as tracer for 15N data), which makes the algorithm report errors.

skills.description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope labeling data on high-resolving-power instruments (e.g. Orbitrap) where an unlabeled sample standard for each compound is available and the correction matrix must reflect the instrument's nominal resolution.
skills.name: unlabeled-sample-correction-matrix-estimation
skills.search_text: unlabeled-sample-correction-matrix-estimation Use when correcting LC-MS isotope labeling data on high-resolving-power instruments (e.g. Orbitrap) where an unlabeled sample standard for each compound is available and the correction matrix must reflect the instrument's nominal resolution. When no unlabeled-sample measurements are available — without Step 2 data, ElemCor runs on mass difference theory (MDT) only, so use MDT instead For low-mass compounds where MDT is recommended for cost efficiency, since ULS requires additional experimental measurement of unlabeled samples When the tracer element is not present in some compounds' formulas — the algorithm reports an error if the wrong tracer is selected (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S) http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Estimate the natural-abundance/tracer-impurity correction matrix by deconvolving the fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) from unlabeled samples, as implemented in ElemCor's ULS method for high-resolution LC-MS stable isotope labeling data. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-019-2669-9
skills.summary: Estimate the natural-abundance/tracer-impurity correction matrix by deconvolving the fractional abundances of measured isotopologs (FAM) from unlabeled samples, as implemented in ElemCor's ULS method for high-resolution LC-MS stable isotope labeling data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no unlabeled-sample measurements are available — without Step 2 data, ElemCor runs on mass difference theory (MDT) only, so use MDT instead For low-mass compounds where MDT is recommended for cost efficiency, since ULS requires additional experimental measurement of unlabeled samples When the tracer element is not present in some compounds' formulas — the algorithm reports an error if the wrong tracer is selected (e.g. loading 15N data but selecting C or S)

skills.description: Use when a source metabolomics dataset reports metabolite names (e.g. study ST001039 from Metabolomics Workbench) and some PubChem Identifier Exchange lookups return no InChIKey match that must be tracked.
skills.name: unresolved-identifier-flagging
skills.search_text: unresolved-identifier-flagging Use when a source metabolomics dataset reports metabolite names (e.g. study ST001039 from Metabolomics Workbench) and some PubChem Identifier Exchange lookups return no InChIKey match that must be tracked. Identifiers in the source dataset are already systematic (e.g. InChIKeys), so no translation or flagging is needed The dataset uses RefMet names from Metabolomics Workbench, which are already standardized and are used directly in MMS harmonization The task is Step 2 attribute retrieval or Step 3 curation (conjugated base/acid rectification, missing attributes, synonym checking) rather than Step 1 translation http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 A Step-1 bookkeeping practice from the Metabolites Merging Strategy (MMS): after translating metabolite names to InChIKeys via the PubChem Identifier Exchange Service, names for which the service returns no match are left with an empty InChIKey cell and explicitly flagged in a dedicated status column instead of being silently dropped. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo13121167
skills.summary: A Step-1 bookkeeping practice from the Metabolites Merging Strategy (MMS): after translating metabolite names to InChIKeys via the PubChem Identifier Exchange Service, names for which the service returns no match are left with an empty InChIKey cell and explicitly flagged in a dedicated status column instead of being silently dropped.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Identifiers in the source dataset are already systematic (e.g. InChIKeys), so no translation or flagging is needed The dataset uses RefMet names from Metabolomics Workbench, which are already standardized and are used directly in MMS harmonization The task is Step 2 attribute retrieval or Step 3 curation (conjugated base/acid rectification, missing attributes, synonym checking) rather than Step 1 translation

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolite (or other feature) concentration table with biological replicates per population and need to verify, without supervision, that the populations are biochemically distinct before downstream pathway/network analyses.
skills.name: unsupervised-cell-population-clustering-visualization
skills.search_text: unsupervised-cell-population-clustering-visualization Use when you have a metabolite (or other feature) concentration table with biological replicates per population and need to verify, without supervision, that the populations are biochemically distinct before downstream pathway/network analyses. The goal is supervised classification or biomarker selection rather than an unsupervised distinctness check — PCA does not use labels to optimize separation. The input is not a normalized feature-by-sample concentration table (e.g., raw spectra or FID files); spectra must first be processed via TopSpin and Chenomx peak identification. Only one or two sample groups with very few replicates are present, where unsupervised clustering cannot demonstrate distinctness. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Unsupervised PCA of metabolite abundance tables (z-score scaled) to test whether biological sample groups—here the five hESC-derived neural stages (hESCs, EBs, rosettes, hNPCs, neurons)—separate into distinct clusters without labels, plus score-plot visualization. metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fnins.2024.1520982
skills.summary: Unsupervised PCA of metabolite abundance tables (z-score scaled) to test whether biological sample groups—here the five hESC-derived neural stages (hESCs, EBs, rosettes, hNPCs, neurons)—separate into distinct clusters without labels, plus score-plot visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is supervised classification or biomarker selection rather than an unsupervised distinctness check — PCA does not use labels to optimize separation. The input is not a normalized feature-by-sample concentration table (e.g., raw spectra or FID files); spectra must first be processed via TopSpin and Chenomx peak identification. Only one or two sample groups with very few replicates are present, where unsupervised clustering cannot demonstrate distinctness.

skills.description: Use when an unlabeled feature table (rows = samples, columns = numerical measurements) needs pattern discovery, e.g. grouping samples by multiple morphological or omics features without ground-truth labels.
skills.name: unsupervised-clustering-of-multidimensional-data
skills.search_text: unsupervised-clustering-of-multidimensional-data Use when an unlabeled feature table (rows = samples, columns = numerical measurements) needs pattern discovery, e.g. grouping samples by multiple morphological or omics features without ground-truth labels. The samples already carry class labels and the goal is supervised prediction rather than pattern discovery — Instant Clue's estimator pipeline with grid search is the appropriate path there The table is not a numerical feature matrix (e.g. only categorical annotation columns); k-means and DBSCAN require numerical measurements The task is dimensionality reduction or visualization of the data (e.g. PCA) rather than cluster membership assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies unsupervised clustering (k-means and DBSCAN, the same estimator style Instant Clue builds on scikit-learn) to a multidimensional tabular dataset such as the 150-sample, 4-feature iris data to identify underlying patterns and assign cluster memberships. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples already carry class labels and the goal is supervised prediction rather than pattern discovery — Instant Clue's estimator pipeline with grid search is the appropriate path there The table is not a numerical feature matrix (e.g. only categorical annotation columns); k-means and DBSCAN require numerical measurements The task is dimensionality reduction or visualization of the data (e.g. PCA) rather than cluster membership assignment

skills.description: Use when a RDKit conformer ensemble (e.g. ~990-996 conformers per protonation state) has been geometry-relaxed with ASE-ANI and must be condensed to structurally distinct representatives before QM-level optimization and CCS calculation.
skills.name: unsupervised-conformer-clustering
skills.search_text: unsupervised-conformer-clustering Use when a RDKit conformer ensemble (e.g. ~990-996 conformers per protonation state) has been geometry-relaxed with ASE-ANI and must be condensed to structurally distinct representatives before QM-level optimization and CCS calculation. Input is an unrelaxed RDKit conformer ensemble that has not yet been minimized with the ASE-ANI model — cluster on optimized geometries only The goal is exhaustive CCS sampling of every conformer rather than reduction to structurally distinct representatives before QM optimization Elements beyond CHNO are present: ANI-1x/ANI-1ccx potentials only provide predictions for CHNO elements, so other systems need a different potential or clustering route http://edamontology.org/topic_3047 Reduces large RDKit-generated conformer ensembles to a small set of structurally distinct conformations by running in-house AutoGraph unsupervised clustering on conformers previously relaxed with the ASE-ANI (ANI-1ccx) machine-learning QM model, one representative per cluster feeding downstream DFT optimization and CCS calculation. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.1c00315
skills.summary: Reduces large RDKit-generated conformer ensembles to a small set of structurally distinct conformations by running in-house AutoGraph unsupervised clustering on conformers previously relaxed with the ASE-ANI (ANI-1ccx) machine-learning QM model, one representative per cluster feeding downstream DFT optimization and CCS calculation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unrelaxed RDKit conformer ensemble that has not yet been minimized with the ASE-ANI model — cluster on optimized geometries only The goal is exhaustive CCS sampling of every conformer rather than reduction to structurally distinct representatives before QM optimization Elements beyond CHNO are present: ANI-1x/ANI-1ccx potentials only provide predictions for CHNO elements, so other systems need a different potential or clustering route

skills.description: Use when a batch of raw MS runs (LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, or direct infusion, DDA/DIA) needs rapid, identification-free quality assessment and you want outliers to emerge from an unsupervised projection rather than per-run metrics.
skills.name: unsupervised-dimensionality-reduction-of-spectral-images
skills.search_text: unsupervised-dimensionality-reduction-of-spectral-images Use when a batch of raw MS runs (LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, or direct infusion, DDA/DIA) needs rapid, identification-free quality assessment and you want outliers to emerge from an unsupervised projection rather than per-run metrics. Input is already a processed feature table or identification-based metrics (e.g., spectral match counts) rather than raw MS1 data — PeakQC's PCA works on time-vs-m/z images from MS1, not on annotation tables. skills.description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature table (XCMS output) contains poorly integrated peaks that manual quality assessment would otherwise need to catch, and you want automated Pass/Fail flagging before downstream statistics.
skills.name: untargeted-lcms-feature-labeling
skills.search_text: untargeted-lcms-feature-labeling Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature table (XCMS output) contains poorly integrated peaks that manual quality assessment would otherwise need to catch, and you want automated Pass/Fail flagging before downstream statistics. Input is vendor-processed output rather than an XCMS object, since MetaClean in its current form does not accept uniquely formatted vendor-processed results. The dataset contains few examples of low-abundance Pass peaks — the source study reports the classifier is conservative and performs worse on the Fail class when the development set lacks such examples. You only need reproducibility filtering on pooled QC samples rather than integration-quality assessment; a simple RSD < 30% cutoff on pooled QCs may suffice and is the alternative baseline the paper compares against. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Labels each XCMS-derived LC-MS feature in an untargeted metabolomics run as high-quality (Pass) or low-quality (Fail) using peak-quality metrics from Zhang et al. and TargetedMSQC paired with machine learning classifiers, as implemented in the MetaClean R package. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Labels each XCMS-derived LC-MS feature in an untargeted metabolomics run as high-quality (Pass) or low-quality (Fail) using peak-quality metrics from Zhang et al. and TargetedMSQC paired with machine learning classifiers, as implemented in the MetaClean R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is vendor-processed output rather than an XCMS object, since MetaClean in its current form does not accept uniquely formatted vendor-processed results. The dataset contains few examples of low-abundance Pass peaks — the source study reports the classifier is conservative and performs worse on the Fail class when the development set lacks such examples. You only need reproducibility filtering on pooled QC samples rather than integration-quality assessment; a simple RSD < 30% cutoff on pooled QCs may suffice and is the alternative baseline the paper compares against.

skills.search_text: untargeted-metabolomics-annotation-validation Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated individual and aligned peak tables (mzXML/mzML/netCDF inputs) and need to validate molecular formula assignments against MS/MS-confirmed identities or report median-rank statistics. Input is already a feature table without underlying raw MS1 data — IDSL.UFA requires raw mzXML/mzML/netCDF to match theoretical isotopic profiles; it is not a post-hoc annotation add-on for preprocessed tables. skills.summary: Validates molecular formula annotations on untargeted LC/HRMS peak tables by matching theoretical against experimental isotopic profiles (MS1) via IDSL.UFA, and independently cross-checks them against MS/MS library hits (e.g. NIST 2020) to quantify how often MS/MS-confirmed compounds receive a high-ranked formula hit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table without underlying raw MS1 data — IDSL.UFA requires raw mzXML/mzML/netCDF to match theoretical isotopic profiles; it is not a post-hoc annotation add-on for preprocessed tables. Data are MS2-only or DIA/SWATH without MS1 isotopic envelopes — the isotopic profile matching approach assumes MS1-level isotope patterns for carbon-containing compounds.

skills.description: Use when raw full-scan LC/HRMS data from population-scale untargeted metabolomics or exposomics studies (e.g. mzXML/mzML files from Orbitrap instruments) must be converted into a peak table without MS2 adduct/fragment handling.

skills.search_text: untargeted-metabolomics-data-processing Use when raw full-scan LC/HRMS data from population-scale untargeted metabolomics or exposomics studies (e.g. mzXML/mzML files from Orbitrap instruments) must be converted into a peak table without MS2 adduct/fragment handling. Data are non-LC/HRMS (e.g. direct infusion MS or non-small-molecule proteomics data) since the pipeline is specifically built for organic small molecules in LC/HRMS untargeted studies. http://edamontology.org/topic_0153 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 IDSL.IPA is an R package that processes raw untargeted LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) into comprehensive peak-intensity data matrices for carbon-containing organic small molecules, using 12C/13C isotopologue pairing in individual mass spectra followed by EIC peak detection, mass and retention-time correction, and peak quality filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00120
skills.summary: IDSL.IPA is an R package that processes raw untargeted LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) into comprehensive peak-intensity data matrices for carbon-containing organic small molecules, using 12C/13C isotopologue pairing in individual mass spectra followed by EIC peak detection, mass and retention-time correction, and peak quality filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed/aligned feature table (the article notes IDSL.IPA aligned data matrices need to be further processed for adducts, fragments, statistics filtering and formula annotation by separate tools such as IDSL.UFA/UFAx/CSA). Input is only a spectral library search result or single-sample spectrum without an extract set — FC specificity and MEMO-based SC require a multi-extract set to compare against No GNPS job or MZmine quantification table exists; the Feature Component cannot be computed and only optional components (LC, CC, SC) would run The goal is de novo structure elucidation of a single annotated compound rather than extract-level prioritization for novelty http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Rank natural extracts for chemical novelty by combining four Inventa components — Feature Component (FC), Literature Component (LC), Class Component (CC), and Similarity Component (SC) — into a weighted Priority Score over untargeted MS data (MZmine quant table, GNPS annotations, SIRIUS/CANOPUS, timaR, MEMO). metabolomics/v3 10.3389/fmolb.2022.1028334
skills.summary: Rank natural extracts for chemical novelty by combining four Inventa components — Feature Component (FC), Literature Component (LC), Class Component (CC), and Similarity Component (SC) — into a weighted Priority Score over untargeted MS data (MZmine quant table, GNPS annotations, SIRIUS/CANOPUS, timaR, MEMO).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only a spectral library search result or single-sample spectrum without an extract set — FC specificity and MEMO-based SC require a multi-extract set to compare against No GNPS job or MZmine quantification table exists; the Feature Component cannot be computed and only optional components (LC, CC, SC) would run The goal is de novo structure elucidation of a single annotated compound rather than extract-level prioritization for novelty

skills.description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics MS1 feature table (.csv with name/mz/rt columns) must be linked onto a curated metabolic reaction network before annotation propagation.
skills.name: untargeted-metabolomics-feature-table-processing
skills.search_text: untargeted-metabolomics-feature-table-processing Use when an untargeted metabolomics MS1 feature table (.csv with name/mz/rt columns) must be linked onto a curated metabolic reaction network before annotation propagation. You only have raw LC-MS/MS files and no feature table yet — peak picking with XCMS, MS-DIAL, or MZmine2 must first produce the name/mz/rt MS1 peak table. No curated MRN exists yet — this step consumes the igraph MRN produced by the prior GNN-based reaction-network construction task. The goal is MS2 spectral-similarity networking (e.g., GNPS FBMN/IIMN) rather than MS1-constrained feature-to-metabolite mapping onto a reaction network. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Pre-maps experimental MS1 feature tables from untargeted metabolomics onto the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (MRN) using 15 ppm m/z matching plus 30% relative-RT matching, pruning redundant nodes/edges to produce the MS1-constrained MRN that anchors MetDNA3's two-layer annotation topology. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63536-6
skills.summary: Pre-maps experimental MS1 feature tables from untargeted metabolomics onto the knowledge-based metabolic reaction network (MRN) using 15 ppm m/z matching plus 30% relative-RT matching, pruning redundant nodes/edges to produce the MS1-constrained MRN that anchors MetDNA3's two-layer annotation topology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw LC-MS/MS files and no feature table yet — peak picking with XCMS, MS-DIAL, or MZmine2 must first produce the name/mz/rt MS1 peak table. No curated MRN exists yet — this step consumes the igraph MRN produced by the prior GNN-based reaction-network construction task. The goal is MS2 spectral-similarity networking (e.g., GNPS FBMN/IIMN) rather than MS1-constrained feature-to-metabolite mapping onto a reaction network.

skills.description: Use when you have per-tissue untargeted metabolomics peak-area feature tables with sample metadata (study, cohort, genotype) and need to verify whether samples cluster across conditions before running differential or ML analyses.
skills.name: untargeted-metabolomics-ordination-analysis
skills.search_text: untargeted-metabolomics-ordination-analysis Use when you have per-tissue untargeted metabolomics peak-area feature tables with sample metadata (study, cohort, genotype) and need to verify whether samples cluster across conditions before running differential or ML analyses. Longitudinal fecal samples lack associated animal IDs (collected randomly per cage), so ordination cannot be interpreted as single-animal developmental trajectories Cohort clustering may reflect collection method (fresh fecal vs. colon after sacrifice) rather than biology, so do not interpret PC separation as a genotype effect without checking cohort balance Input is already ordinated or the goal is MS/MS spectral annotation — use GNPS library spectral matching instead of PCA on peak areas http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Ordination (PCA on RCLR-transformed untargeted metabolomics peak-area matrices) to test whether samples cluster by experimental variables such as study, cohort, or tissue, and to decide if downstream analyses must be stratified accordingly. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.04.28.651123
skills.summary: Ordination (PCA on RCLR-transformed untargeted metabolomics peak-area matrices) to test whether samples cluster by experimental variables such as study, cohort, or tissue, and to decide if downstream analyses must be stratified accordingly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Longitudinal fecal samples lack associated animal IDs (collected randomly per cage), so ordination cannot be interpreted as single-animal developmental trajectories Cohort clustering may reflect collection method (fresh fecal vs. colon after sacrifice) rather than biology, so do not interpret PC separation as a genotype effect without checking cohort balance Input is already ordinated or the goal is MS/MS spectral annotation — use GNPS library spectral matching instead of PCA on peak areas

skills.description: Use when you have an XCMS-processed untargeted LC–MS feature table with peak-quality metrics and want to automatically flag low-quality peak integrations without manual curation.
skills.name: untargeted-metabolomics-peak-classifier-inference
skills.search_text: untargeted-metabolomics-peak-classifier-inference Use when you have an XCMS-processed untargeted LC–MS feature table with peak-quality metrics and want to automatically flag low-quality peak integrations without manual curation. Input is a feature table already manually curated or produced by vendor software (MassHunter Profinder, Progenesis QI, Compound Discoverer) — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input and cannot consume uniquely formatted vendor-processed outputs. The dataset was generated on a platform or in an ionization mode very different from the classifier's development data (e.g. Test 2-like conditions with few RSD-passing peaks) — cross-platform generalization may degrade, as observed for low-abundance Fail peaks. Goal is targeted metabolomics with a priori known analytes — the M11 metrics were repurposed from targeted QC specifically for untargeted LC–MS, not for confirming known compounds. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Applies a pre-trained machine-learning peak-quality classifier (e.g. the MetaClean AdaBoost model built on the 11-metric M11 set) to an XCMS feature table to binarize every integrated chromatographic peak as Pass (high-quality) or Fail (low-quality), replacing manual inspection of peak integrations. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-020-01738-3
skills.summary: Applies a pre-trained machine-learning peak-quality classifier (e.g. the MetaClean AdaBoost model built on the 11-metric M11 set) to an XCMS feature table to binarize every integrated chromatographic peak as Pass (high-quality) or Fail (low-quality), replacing manual inspection of peak integrations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature table already manually curated or produced by vendor software (MassHunter Profinder, Progenesis QI, Compound Discoverer) — MetaClean requires an XCMS object input and cannot consume uniquely formatted vendor-processed outputs. The dataset was generated on a platform or in an ionization mode very different from the classifier's development data (e.g. Test 2-like conditions with few RSD-passing peaks) — cross-platform generalization may degrade, as observed for low-abundance Fail peaks. Goal is targeted metabolomics with a priori known analytes — the M11 metrics were repurposed from targeted QC specifically for untargeted LC–MS, not for confirming known compounds.

skills.description: Use when starting from centroided (or raw Thermo/Agilent/Bruker) LC-MS/MS mzML files in an untargeted metabolomics study and you need a per-sample feature table with m/z, RT, adduct, and intensities for downstream FBMN/IIMN or statistics.
skills.name: untargeted-metabolomics-preprocessing
skills.search_text: untargeted-metabolomics-preprocessing Use when starting from centroided (or raw Thermo/Agilent/Bruker) LC-MS/MS mzML files in an untargeted metabolomics study and you need a per-sample feature table with m/z, RT, adduct, and intensities for downstream FBMN/IIMN or statistics. Input is already a consensus feature table (e.g. from XCMS or a prior UmetaFlow run) rather than raw/centroided mzML — use downstream annotation or re-quantification instead. The goal is structural annotation or molecular networking — those are handled by the SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID, GNPS FBMN/IIMN, and spectral matching steps, not the pre-processing module. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 UmetaFlow's pre-processing module converts centroided LC-MS/MS mzML files into a consensus feature table using OpenMS 3.0 algorithms (feature detection, RT alignment, adduct annotation, feature linking) orchestrated by Snakemake or pyOpenMS notebooks. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-023-00724-w

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a consensus feature table (e.g. from XCMS or a prior UmetaFlow run) rather than raw/centroided mzML — use downstream annotation or re-quantification instead. Input is already a processed features table or peak list — AutoTuner performs statistical inference on raw data, not on processed results Fewer than 3 samples of raw data are available, since AutoTuner requires at least 3 samples for parameter estimation The goal is estimating retention time correction parameters by comparing EIC peaks across samples — AutoTuner's divide-and-conquer approach comes at a loss of cross-sample EIC peak comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Optimize dataset-specific peak-picking parameters for untargeted metabolomics by running AutoTuner, which performs statistical inference on raw data in a single step to estimate the seven continuous centWave parameters (used by XCMS and MZmine2) plus a key grouping parameter, replacing days-long iterative parameter sweeps. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/812370

skills.search_text: untargeted-screening-identification-tallying Use when a completed MS-DIAL/MS-FINDER screening yields a list of identified features whose library annotations and unknown IDs must be counted, cross-checked against a reported total (e.g. 83 compounds), and exported as a per-identification-status table. When the goal is quantification or risk ranking of detected migrants (e.g. octocrylene or 2-ethylhexyl-4-methoxycinnamate levels) rather than simply counting identifications — use the pseudo-MRM targeting or quantification workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Aggregate the feature-level identification results of an untargeted LC-HRMS screening (e.g. the rHDPE milk-bottle study) into a structured summary table that tallies total identified compounds and partitions them into library-annotated versus in-silico-only (unknown) identifications. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.2c05389

skills.description: Use when an MSI peak matrix has been segmented into clusters/ROIs and you need the statistically significant up- or down-regulated ions between two specific regions, with undetected (null) peaks handled explicitly.
skills.name: up-down-regulated-ion-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: up-down-regulated-ion-statistical-testing Use when an MSI peak matrix has been segmented into clusters/ROIs and you need the statistically significant up- or down-regulated ions between two specific regions, with undetected (null) peaks handled explicitly. The data are already an annotated feature table with statistical test results — the filtering workflow expects a raw MSI peak matrix and clustering. The analysis is a simple p-value/fold-change test where undetected peaks are not an issue — rMSIKeyIon's third null-peak method targets datasets with a high percentage of pixels where an ion is not detected. The goal is image visualization only — rMSIproc::plotClusterImage/plotPeakImage handle that without the statistical selection step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Statistical ion filtering for untargeted LDI-MS imaging using the rMSIKeyIon R package: it combines a null-peak threshold, a Mann-Whitney U ion concentration test, and ion concentration fold-change to report up- and down-regulated ions between pairs of image regions. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/metabo9080162
skills.summary: Statistical ion filtering for untargeted LDI-MS imaging using the rMSIKeyIon R package: it combines a null-peak threshold, a Mann-Whitney U ion concentration test, and ion concentration fold-change to report up- and down-regulated ions between pairs of image regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already an annotated feature table with statistical test results — the filtering workflow expects a raw MSI peak matrix and clustering. The analysis is a simple p-value/fold-change test where undetected peaks are not an issue — rMSIKeyIon's third null-peak method targets datasets with a high percentage of pixels where an ion is not detected. The goal is image visualization only — rMSIproc::plotClusterImage/plotPeakImage handle that without the statistical selection step.

skills.description: Use when you have predicted molecular fingerprints (e.g., CSI:FingerID probability vectors over 2936 molecular properties) for LC-MS/MS chemical features and need a chemical tree for downstream tree-informed metrics like Weighted UniFrac or Faith's PD.
skills.name: upgma-hierarchical-clustering
skills.search_text: upgma-hierarchical-clustering Use when you have predicted molecular fingerprints (e.g., CSI:FingerID probability vectors over 2936 molecular properties) for LC-MS/MS chemical features and need a chemical tree for downstream tree-informed metrics like Weighted UniFrac or Faith's PD. The input features lack MS/MS data (features with only MS1 are not considered, since no fragmentation spectra means no fingerprints). You already have spectral library annotations for enough features that a ClassyFire-taxonomy-based hierarchy would suffice; the paper notes only 1–20% of features typically have library matches, so fingerprint clustering is for summarizing the unannotated majority. You need a phylogenetic tree of organisms/DNA sequences — this skill clusters molecular fingerprints, not sequence data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Builds a rooted chemical hierarchy ('Qemistree') by hierarchically clustering CSI:FingerID molecular fingerprint vectors with UPGMA, so that MS1 features occupy a one-to-one correspondence with tree tips and tree-based ecological tools can be applied to metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41589-020-00677-3
skills.summary: Builds a rooted chemical hierarchy ('Qemistree') by hierarchically clustering CSI:FingerID molecular fingerprint vectors with UPGMA, so that MS1 features occupy a one-to-one correspondence with tree tips and tree-based ecological tools can be applied to metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input features lack MS/MS data (features with only MS1 are not considered, since no fragmentation spectra means no fingerprints). You already have spectral library annotations for enough features that a ClassyFire-taxonomy-based hierarchy would suffice; the paper notes only 1–20% of features typically have library matches, so fingerprint clustering is for summarizing the unannotated majority. You need a phylogenetic tree of organisms/DNA sequences — this skill clusters molecular fingerprints, not sequence data.

skills.description: Use when you already have a pairwise distance matrix over datasets/samples and need a rooted tree in Newick format, as compareMS2 2.0 does with its LC-MS/MS dataset distances.
skills.name: upgma-hierarchical-clustering-from-distance-matrix
skills.search_text: upgma-hierarchical-clustering-from-distance-matrix Use when you already have a pairwise distance matrix over datasets/samples and need a rooted tree in Newick format, as compareMS2 2.0 does with its LC-MS/MS dataset distances. skills.search_text: uptake-reaction-perturbation-simulation Use when gap-filled community GEMs exist and you must determine which exchanged metabolites each member depends on, by blocking one uptake reaction at a time and recording biomass-flux reduction. The input is raw draft reconstructions that have not yet been gap-filled with COMMIT — dependencies computed on incomplete models will be artifacts of missing reactions rather than true cross-feeding dependencies. The goal is draft reconstruction quality assessment (e.g. memote test suite or structural comparison by distance measures) rather than interrogation of metabolic interactions. The analysis concerns gap-filling reaction weights or permeability classification of metabolites, which belongs to the COMMIT gap-filling step, not uptake-perturbation simulation. Simulates single-uptake-reaction removals in gap-filled community metabolic models using COBRA toolbox FBA (LP solved with CPLEX or Gurobi) to quantify, for each soil-community member, the biomass flux reduction caused by losing access to each exchanged metabolite. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009906
