skills.search_text: usi-identifier-construction Use when you need a machine-readable, cross-repository identifier for an MS/MS spectrum held in a metabolomics or proteomics repository (e.g. MassIVE MSV accession, MassBank accession) to fetch or render that spectrum. The spectrum is local (raw vendor file, mzML, MGF) and not deposited in a supported repository — no USI can resolve it You need a stable, database-independent identifier for publication — SPLASH hashes, not USIs, are the database-independent option (though they require a complex hashing operation to produce) You need finalized, stable identifiers for long-term archival: the README warns metabolomics USIs are draft ('mzdraft') and 'subject to change' http://edamontology.org/topic_3344 Constructs metabolomics-aware Universal Spectrum Identifiers (USI, mzspec:...:/mzdraft:...) for MS/MS spectra stored in MassIVE/GNPS, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MassBank, MS2LDA, and ProteomeXchange, so spectra can be retrieved and rendered via the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver endpoints (/json/, /png/, /svg/, /csv/, /mirror/). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Constructs metabolomics-aware Universal Spectrum Identifiers (USI, mzspec:...:/mzdraft:...) for MS/MS spectra stored in MassIVE/GNPS, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MassBank, MS2LDA, and ProteomeXchange, so spectra can be retrieved and rendered via the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver endpoints (/json/, /png/, /svg/, /csv/, /mirror/).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectrum is local (raw vendor file, mzML, MGF) and not deposited in a supported repository — no USI can resolve it You need a stable, database-independent identifier for publication — SPLASH hashes, not USIs, are the database-independent option (though they require a complex hashing operation to produce) You need finalized, stable identifiers for long-term archival: the README warns metabolomics USIs are draft ('mzdraft') and 'subject to change'

skills.description: Use when you have USIs (e.g. `mzspec:GNPS2:TASK-<id>-nf_output/clustering/specs_ms.mgf:scan:<n>`) and need to fetch the corresponding MS/MS spectra to feed a molecular-networking or spectral-alignment pipeline.
skills.name: usi-spectra-retrieval-from-public-repositories
skills.search_text: usi-spectra-retrieval-from-public-repositories Use when you have USIs (e.g. `mzspec:GNPS2:TASK-<id>-nf_output/clustering/specs_ms.mgf:scan:<n>`) and need to fetch the corresponding MS/MS spectra to feed a molecular-networking or spectral-alignment pipeline. You only have raw LC-MS/MS vendor files (e.g. Thermo .RAW, mzML) that are not indexed in a USI-resolvable public repository — ingest them through molecular-networking tasks first. You need de novo library search or spectral matching only, without multiple alignment across a molecular family. The source dataset is not exposed through a USI-supporting public source (MassIVE/GNPS, Metabolomics Workbench, PRIDE, GNPS2). http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Retrieves tandem mass spectra from public MS/MS data sources (MassIVE/GNPS, Metabolomics Workbench, PRIDE, GNPS2) via Universal Spectrum Identifiers, feeding spectral-alignment and molecular-networking workflows such as MMSA. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/jasms.5c00237
skills.summary: Retrieves tandem mass spectra from public MS/MS data sources (MassIVE/GNPS, Metabolomics Workbench, PRIDE, GNPS2) via Universal Spectrum Identifiers, feeding spectral-alignment and molecular-networking workflows such as MMSA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw LC-MS/MS vendor files (e.g. Thermo .RAW, mzML) that are not indexed in a USI-resolvable public repository — ingest them through molecular-networking tasks first. You need de novo library search or spectral matching only, without multiple alignment across a molecular family. The source dataset is not exposed through a USI-supporting public source (MassIVE/GNPS, Metabolomics Workbench, PRIDE, GNPS2).

skills.description: Use when aggregating MASST matches per synthesized compound — e.g., N-acyl amides searched in MSV000089491 or acyl esters in MSV000089493 — where match records must be keyed by USI and MASST job identifier.
skills.name: usi-spectrum-identifier-handling
skills.search_text: usi-spectrum-identifier-handling Use when aggregating MASST matches per synthesized compound — e.g., N-acyl amides searched in MSV000089491 or acyl esters in MSV000089493 — where match records must be keyed by USI and MASST job identifier. The analysis needs a single one-off spectral library search rather than per-compound aggregation of repository-scale MASST results. The spectra of interest have no deposited USI or MASST job identifiers (e.g., purely local or computationally predicted spectra never searched in public data). The goal is definitive isomer-level structure elucidation requiring isolation and NMR or X-ray analyses, rather than tracking spectral matches of known synthesized compounds. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Retrieves and aggregates repository-scale MASST search results for synthesized compound MS/MS spectra, keying every match record by the compound's Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) and its MASST job identifier, as used in reverse metabolomics to recover spectral matches from public metabolomics data. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41586-023-06906-8
skills.summary: Retrieves and aggregates repository-scale MASST search results for synthesized compound MS/MS spectra, keying every match record by the compound's Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) and its MASST job identifier, as used in reverse metabolomics to recover spectral matches from public metabolomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis needs a single one-off spectral library search rather than per-compound aggregation of repository-scale MASST results. The spectra of interest have no deposited USI or MASST job identifiers (e.g., purely local or computationally predicted spectra never searched in public data). The goal is definitive isomer-level structure elucidation requiring isolation and NMR or X-ray analyses, rather than tracking spectral matches of known synthesized compounds.

skills.description: Use when you have one or a few MS/MS spectra (a single .mgf from MZmine or a USI list in .csv/.tsv) and want to identify which publicly deposited microbial monoculture datasets or GNPS library entries match those spectra.
skills.name: usi-spectrum-searching
skills.search_text: usi-spectrum-searching Use when you have one or a few MS/MS spectra (a single .mgf from MZmine or a USI list in .csv/.tsv) and want to identify which publicly deposited microbial monoculture datasets or GNPS library entries match those spectra. You need taxonomically restricted, curated microbeMASST sample counts only — the _matches.tsv output also contains samples outside the curated domain-specific MASSTs, so a separate curated-domain analysis is needed. Your input is raw LC-MS centroided data rather than an already deconvoluted .mgf or USI list — spectral preprocessing with MZmine is a prerequisite, not part of this search step. You cannot run Python 3.10 or repeatedly retry the search — the Fast Search API can silently drop entries, so a single incomplete run may leave some spectra unsearched. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Search a user-supplied MS/MS spectrum, given as a USI-formatted .csv/.tsv or an MZmine .mgf file, against publicly indexed monoculture MS/MS data via the Fast Search API to find matching microbial datasets, samples, and GNPS library annotations. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41564-023-01575-9
skills.summary: Search a user-supplied MS/MS spectrum, given as a USI-formatted .csv/.tsv or an MZmine .mgf file, against publicly indexed monoculture MS/MS data via the Fast Search API to find matching microbial datasets, samples, and GNPS library annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need taxonomically restricted, curated microbeMASST sample counts only — the _matches.tsv output also contains samples outside the curated domain-specific MASSTs, so a separate curated-domain analysis is needed. Your input is raw LC-MS centroided data rather than an already deconvoluted .mgf or USI list — spectral preprocessing with MZmine is a prerequisite, not part of this search step. You cannot run Python 3.10 or repeatedly retry the search — the Fast Search API can silently drop entries, so a single incomplete run may leave some spectra unsearched.

skills.description: Use when a task requires parsing mzspec:<collection>:<msRun>:<indexType>:<indexNumber> strings from GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA/MOTIFDB, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, or ProteomeXchange into fields and mapping each to its backing resource.
skills.name: usi-string-parsing
skills.search_text: usi-string-parsing Use when a task requires parsing mzspec:<collection>:<msRun>:<indexType>:<indexNumber> strings from GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA/MOTIFDB, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, or ProteomeXchange into fields and mapping each to its backing resource. The identifier is a SPLASH hash — the paper notes SPLASH generation requires a complex hashing operation and is a different, database-independent scheme, not a colon-delimited USI to parse. The USI is a proteomics-specific construct outside the metabolomics extension's supported sources — the standard 'natively' supports ProteomeXchange but the resolver only handles the listed metabolomics collection types. The goal is spectrum rendering or figure styling rather than parsing/routing — use the resolver's /png/, /svg/, /json/, /csv/ endpoints with plotting parameters (mz_min, mz_max, annotate_peaks) instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Decompose metabolomics Universal Spectrum Identifiers (USIs) into their four colon-delimited fields (collection, msRun, indexType, indexNumber) and route each identifier to the correct backing data service (repository or spectral library) as implemented in the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2020.05.09.086066
skills.summary: Decompose metabolomics Universal Spectrum Identifiers (USIs) into their four colon-delimited fields (collection, msRun, indexType, indexNumber) and route each identifier to the correct backing data service (repository or spectral library) as implemented in the Metabolomics Spectrum Resolver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The identifier is a SPLASH hash — the paper notes SPLASH generation requires a complex hashing operation and is a different, database-independent scheme, not a colon-delimited USI to parse. The USI is a proteomics-specific construct outside the metabolomics extension's supported sources — the standard 'natively' supports ProteomeXchange but the resolver only handles the listed metabolomics collection types. The goal is spectrum rendering or figure styling rather than parsing/routing — use the resolver's /png/, /svg/, /json/, /csv/ endpoints with plotting parameters (mz_min, mz_max, annotate_peaks) instead.

skills.description: Use when you have raw, high-dimensional MSI spectra (e.g. 85,062 m/z variables in HDF5) and need a low-dimensional latent embedding (5-D Code layer) for classification, UMAP visualization, or feature extraction.
skills.name: vae-latent-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: vae-latent-feature-extraction Use when you have raw, high-dimensional MSI spectra (e.g. 85,062 m/z variables in HDF5) and need a low-dimensional latent embedding (5-D Code layer) for classification, UMAP visualization, or feature extraction. When the goal is multi-class tumor classification or precise tumor-margin ground truthing — the demonstrated model only covers binary normal-vs-tumor classification and histology-based annotation is an approximation, especially with intra-tumor heterogeneity When input is already a reduced feature/peak table — the VAE is designed to operate on raw, TIC-normalized spectra without prior peak picking http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts a compact latent representation from a VAE trained on raw (non-peak-picked) MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging data, enabling downstream visualization, peak identification, and tumor-correlated feature ranking without spectral preprocessing. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Extracts a compact latent representation from a VAE trained on raw (non-peak-picked) MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging data, enabling downstream visualization, peak identification, and tumor-correlated feature ranking without spectral preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is multi-class tumor classification or precise tumor-margin ground truthing — the demonstrated model only covers binary normal-vs-tumor classification and histology-based annotation is an approximation, especially with intra-tumor heterogeneity When input is already a reduced feature/peak table — the VAE is designed to operate on raw, TIC-normalized spectra without prior peak picking

skills.description: Use when you have an mzLearn-generated MS1 ion-feature matrix for a patient cohort plus survival (OS time/event), IMDC risk class, or treatment-response labels and need VAE-latent-based prognostic/predictive stratification.
skills.name: vae-latent-representation-risk-scoring
skills.search_text: vae-latent-representation-risk-scoring Use when you have an mzLearn-generated MS1 ion-feature matrix for a patient cohort plus survival (OS time/event), IMDC risk class, or treatment-response labels and need VAE-latent-based prognostic/predictive stratification. Input data is raw mzML files rather than an mzLearn-derived feature table — run mzLearn signal detection first; the VAE expects the 2,736-feature MS1 matrix Data was acquired outside HILIC positive mode LC-MS — the pre-trained model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode and other LC modes/modalities are not covered De-isotoping or MS/MS-level compound identification is the goal — mzLearn outputs are ion MS1 level only and downstream mapping/annotation workflows must be applied separately http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Fine-tunes a VAE pre-trained on mzLearn MS1 feature matrices (2,736 robust metabolite features from 20,548 blood samples) on task-specific clinical data (e.g., ccRCC serum metabolomics) to produce latent representations used for risk stratification, overall-survival prediction, and treatment-response classification that are benchmarked against IMDC criteria. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Fine-tunes a VAE pre-trained on mzLearn MS1 feature matrices (2,736 robust metabolite features from 20,548 blood samples) on task-specific clinical data (e.g., ccRCC serum metabolomics) to produce latent representations used for risk stratification, overall-survival prediction, and treatment-response classification that are benchmarked against IMDC criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw mzML files rather than an mzLearn-derived feature table — run mzLearn signal detection first; the VAE expects the 2,736-feature MS1 matrix Data was acquired outside HILIC positive mode LC-MS — the pre-trained model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode and other LC modes/modalities are not covered De-isotoping or MS/MS-level compound identification is the goal — mzLearn outputs are ion MS1 level only and downstream mapping/annotation workflows must be applied separately

skills.description: Use when a microbial genome-metabolome linking score has been computed over candidate BGC/spectrum links and you need to quantify whether the score's upper tail is enriched for literature-validated links, as in Table 1 / Fig 6.
skills.name: validated-link-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: validated-link-benchmark-comparison Use when a microbial genome-metabolome linking score has been computed over candidate BGC/spectrum links and you need to quantify whether the score's upper tail is enriched for literature-validated links, as in Table 1 / Fig 6. No literature-validated link list exists for the data set, so no benchmark subset can be defined The scoring method being evaluated is not one of the link-scoring functions available via npl.get_links() The data set is not assembled in the NPLinker fixed directory structure (gnps/, antismash/, bigscape/, strain_mappings.json), since load_data() expects it http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Benchmarks a computed link-scoring function (e.g. IOKR) against literature-validated BGC-spectrum links by comparing score distributions over all candidate links versus the validated subset, replicating the Crüsemann data set evaluation in the NPLinker framework. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Benchmarks a computed link-scoring function (e.g. IOKR) against literature-validated BGC-spectrum links by comparing score distributions over all candidate links versus the validated subset, replicating the Crüsemann data set evaluation in the NPLinker framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No literature-validated link list exists for the data set, so no benchmark subset can be defined The scoring method being evaluated is not one of the link-scoring functions available via npl.get_links() The data set is not assembled in the NPLinker fixed directory structure (gnps/, antismash/, bigscape/, strain_mappings.json), since load_data() expects it

skills.description: Use when a GCF with established homology to a MIBiG BGC (e.g. BGC0001228, BGC0000241) must be scored against all molecular families, and the validated link's rank under each scoring function is needed to judge which score prioritises true links .
skills.name: validated-link-rank-evaluation
skills.search_text: validated-link-rank-evaluation Use when a GCF with established homology to a MIBiG BGC (e.g. BGC0001228, BGC0000241) must be scored against all molecular families, and the validated link's rank under each scoring function is needed to judge which score prioritises true links . The GCF of interest has no established homology to a validated MIBiG BGC, so there is no ground-truth link to rank against. The goal is de novo prioritisation of all GCF–molecular-family links rather than evaluation of known validated links. Genomics or metabolomics data lack strain-level mapping (no strain_mappings.json), so standardised strain-correlation scores cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Ranks validated GCF–molecular-family links under combined ℓ1, ℓ2, and ℓ1.5 scores built from standardised strain-correlation (metcalf) and IOKR scores, and compiles the rank counts into a Table 4-style comparison for the Crüsemann data set. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008920
skills.summary: Ranks validated GCF–molecular-family links under combined ℓ1, ℓ2, and ℓ1.5 scores built from standardised strain-correlation (metcalf) and IOKR scores, and compiles the rank counts into a Table 4-style comparison for the Crüsemann data set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The GCF of interest has no established homology to a validated MIBiG BGC, so there is no ground-truth link to rank against. The goal is de novo prioritisation of all GCF–molecular-family links rather than evaluation of known validated links. Genomics or metabolomics data lack strain-level mapping (no strain_mappings.json), so standardised strain-correlation scores cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing NPClassScore-based prioritisation on PoDP paired omics datasets where known validated BGC–metabolite links (e.g. from MIBiG/PoDP records) must be checked for retention and rank improvement after filtering.
skills.name: validated-link-rank-tracking
skills.search_text: validated-link-rank-tracking Use when reproducing or auditing NPClassScore-based prioritisation on PoDP paired omics datasets where known validated BGC–metabolite links (e.g. from MIBiG/PoDP records) must be checked for retention and rank improvement after filtering. Datasets whose validated metabolites lack MS/MS spectra entirely — no spectrum could be found for retimycin and nocardimicin, so no rank can be tracked for them Analyses that cannot compute structure-based classes: 1988 MS/MS spectra across the datasets had no CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer prediction, and filtering behaviour differs substantially in that case Linking tasks without prior co-occurrence candidate generation (e.g. no Metcalf-scored candidate list) — rank tracking is defined relative to the Metcalf-scored candidate ordering http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Tracks the ranked positions of experimentally validated BGC–MS/MS spectrum links before and after NPClassScore filtering within the NPLinker platform, to verify that chemical class matching retains and prioritises known genome–metabolome links while reducing candidate lists. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s40168-022-01444-3
skills.summary: Tracks the ranked positions of experimentally validated BGC–MS/MS spectrum links before and after NPClassScore filtering within the NPLinker platform, to verify that chemical class matching retains and prioritises known genome–metabolome links while reducing candidate lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets whose validated metabolites lack MS/MS spectra entirely — no spectrum could be found for retimycin and nocardimicin, so no rank can be tracked for them Analyses that cannot compute structure-based classes: 1988 MS/MS spectra across the datasets had no CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer prediction, and filtering behaviour differs substantially in that case Linking tasks without prior co-occurrence candidate generation (e.g. no Metcalf-scored candidate list) — rank tracking is defined relative to the Metcalf-scored candidate ordering

skills.description: Use when predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters or sub-cluster motifs must be validated/annotated against experimentally characterised sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast, MIBiG) and quantified genome-wide.
skills.name: validated-subcluster-overlap-assessment
skills.search_text: validated-subcluster-overlap-assessment Use when predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters or sub-cluster motifs must be validated/annotated against experimentally characterised sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast, MIBiG) and quantified genome-wide. When sub-clusters of length one are expected to be biologically meaningful — the article treats these as 'almost definitely noise' and excludes them When characterised reference sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast / MIBiG) are unavailable, since the overlap-based validation and substructure annotation depend entirely on them http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Anchors unsupervised PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster predictions to experimentally validated sub-clusters by requiring a 0.6 overlap with SubClusterBlast sub-clusters, then annotates motifs with substructures via MIBiG instances — yielding 45 annotated motifs across 24 substructure types and 83% confirmation of known sub-clusters. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010462
skills.summary: Anchors unsupervised PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster predictions to experimentally validated sub-clusters by requiring a 0.6 overlap with SubClusterBlast sub-clusters, then annotates motifs with substructures via MIBiG instances — yielding 45 annotated motifs across 24 substructure types and 83% confirmation of known sub-clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sub-clusters of length one are expected to be biologically meaningful — the article treats these as 'almost definitely noise' and excludes them When characterised reference sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast / MIBiG) are unavailable, since the overlap-based validation and substructure annotation depend entirely on them

skills.description: Reference for choosing hyperparameters (learning rate, number of convolutional layers, epochs) and the final checkpoint for a CNN trained on augmented NMR mixture spectra, based on validation accuracy.
skills.name: validation-accuracy-model-selection
skills.search_text: validation-accuracy-model-selection Reference for choosing hyperparameters (learning rate, number of convolutional layers, epochs) and the final checkpoint for a CNN trained on augmented NMR mixture spectra, based on validation accuracy. Input spectra are single-compound rather than mixtures, so compound identification does not need the pSCNN mixture model being tuned No labeled ground truth is available to compute a validation accuracy, so grid selection cannot be scored The goal is evaluating real-world performance on experimental spectra (e.g., flavor mixtures benchmarking) rather than selecting training hyperparameters Selects the final pSCNN model (M3) for compound identification in NMR mixture spectra by sweeping learning rates (10^-2 to 10^-5) and convolutional layer counts (5–10) at 100 epochs, then choosing the configuration with the highest validation accuracy (0.9990). metabolomics/v3 10.3390/molecules27123653
skills.summary: Selects the final pSCNN model (M3) for compound identification in NMR mixture spectra by sweeping learning rates (10^-2 to 10^-5) and convolutional layer counts (5–10) at 100 epochs, then choosing the configuration with the highest validation accuracy (0.9990).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are single-compound rather than mixtures, so compound identification does not need the pSCNN mixture model being tuned No labeled ground truth is available to compute a validation accuracy, so grid selection cannot be scored The goal is evaluating real-world performance on experimental spectra (e.g., flavor mixtures benchmarking) rather than selecting training hyperparameters

skills.description: Use when retraining the GLEAMS Siamese network from gleams/config.py and you must decide whether precursor, fragment, and reference-spectrum feature blocks each contribute — or when comparing trained-model variants by validation loss.
skills.name: validation-loss-model-selection
skills.search_text: validation-loss-model-selection Use when retraining the GLEAMS Siamese network from gleams/config.py and you must decide whether precursor, fragment, and reference-spectrum feature blocks each contribute — or when comparing trained-model variants by validation loss. You only need to embed or cluster new spectra with the released pretrained weights (gleams_82c0124b.hdf5) rather than retrain and compare model variants The goal is tuning clustering parameters such as --distance_threshold 0.3 for gleams cluster, not selecting input feature blocks by validation loss No CUDA-enabled GPU or Linux environment is available, since GLEAMS explicitly requires Python 3.8, Linux, and a CUDA GPU http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Select among GLEAMS encoder configurations (all-features baseline vs. feature-type ablations) by comparing validation loss after convergence, using the 32-dimensional Siamese embedding network trained on MassIVE-KB (v1) Human HCD PSMs. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Select among GLEAMS encoder configurations (all-features baseline vs. feature-type ablations) by comparing validation loss after convergence, using the 32-dimensional Siamese embedding network trained on MassIVE-KB (v1) Human HCD PSMs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to embed or cluster new spectra with the released pretrained weights (gleams_82c0124b.hdf5) rather than retrain and compare model variants The goal is tuning clustering parameters such as --distance_threshold 0.3 for gleams cluster, not selecting input feature blocks by validation loss No CUDA-enabled GPU or Linux environment is available, since GLEAMS explicitly requires Python 3.8, Linux, and a CUDA GPU

skills.description: Use when evaluating a trained RT prediction model on a held-out validation set and you need to determine whether prediction error is smaller for molecules that have a structurally similar molecule (e.g. ≥90% Tanimoto on ECFP fingerprints) in the training set.
skills.name: validation-set-stratification-by-structural-similarity
skills.search_text: validation-set-stratification-by-structural-similarity Use when evaluating a trained RT prediction model on a held-out validation set and you need to determine whether prediction error is smaller for molecules that have a structurally similar molecule (e.g. ≥90% Tanimoto on ECFP fingerprints) in the training set. The goal is training or hyperparameter tuning of the RT prediction model rather than post-hoc evaluation of error dependence on training-set similarity The input structures lack SMILES/ECFP-computable representations, so Tanimoto similarity thresholds cannot be computed The validation table includes non-retained molecules or lacks paired predicted vs experimental RT values needed to compute relative RT prediction error http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Tests whether a DLM's RT prediction error depends on structural similarity to the training set by stratifying validation-set molecules into 'with similar counterpart' vs 'without counterpart' groups at ECFP/Tanimoto thresholds (95, 90, 80, 70, 50%) and comparing relative RT errors with a repeated, Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon rank test. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7
skills.summary: Tests whether a DLM's RT prediction error depends on structural similarity to the training set by stratifying validation-set molecules into 'with similar counterpart' vs 'without counterpart' groups at ECFP/Tanimoto thresholds (95, 90, 80, 70, 50%) and comparing relative RT errors with a repeated, Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon rank test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is training or hyperparameter tuning of the RT prediction model rather than post-hoc evaluation of error dependence on training-set similarity The input structures lack SMILES/ECFP-computable representations, so Tanimoto similarity thresholds cannot be computed The validation table includes non-retained molecules or lacks paired predicted vs experimental RT values needed to compute relative RT prediction error

skills.description: Use when tandem mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a chemical database like COCONUT or NPAtlas in a mode that can explain precursor mass differences via known variant mass shifts, not just exact matches.
skills.name: variable-mode-molecular-variant-search-configuration
skills.search_text: variable-mode-molecular-variant-search-configuration Use when tandem mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a chemical database like COCONUT or NPAtlas in a mode that can explain precursor mass differences via known variant mass shifts, not just exact matches. When the goal is exact search of known molecules only, since exact mode already matches spectra to molecules whose masses match the precursor m/z without variant interpretation When the input spectra have already been locally pre-processed and peak-thresholded — the advanced settings (Peak Merge Threshold, Minimum Peak Count, Peaks Per Window, Peak Filtering Window) should be adjusted rather than left at defaults When ion/adduct assignment requires charges above 2, since the form supports a maximum absolute charge of only 1 or 2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Configure and run a VInSMoC variable-mode database search on the run.npanalysis.org server so that query mass spectra are matched to database molecules whose structural variants explain the precursor-to-molecule mass difference, enabling identification of unreported molecule variants. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Configure and run a VInSMoC variable-mode database search on the run.npanalysis.org server so that query mass spectra are matched to database molecules whose structural variants explain the precursor-to-molecule mass difference, enabling identification of unreported molecule variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is exact search of known molecules only, since exact mode already matches spectra to molecules whose masses match the precursor m/z without variant interpretation When the input spectra have already been locally pre-processed and peak-thresholded — the advanced settings (Peak Merge Threshold, Minimum Peak Count, Peaks Per Window, Peak Filtering Window) should be adjusted rather than left at defaults When ion/adduct assignment requires charges above 2, since the form supports a maximum absolute charge of only 1 or 2

skills.description: Use when running NetGSA pathway enrichment where exact REML variance component estimation on the entire weighted, directed pathway network is required, or when benchmarking REHE/clustered-REHE runtime and power against the REML gold standard.
skills.name: variance-component-estimation-reml
skills.search_text: variance-component-estimation-reml Use when running NetGSA pathway enrichment where exact REML variance component estimation on the entire weighted, directed pathway network is required, or when benchmarking REHE/clustered-REHE runtime and power against the REML gold standard. When computational speed is the priority and the REHE approximation suffices — REML on the entire network is several times slower than REHE and much slower than clustered REHE When the input expression matrix contains genes not belonging to any tested pathway — variables must first be filtered to pathway members before running NetGSA http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Variance component estimation for NetGSA topology-based pathway enrichment using REML (NetGSA.REML.All) on the full pathway network, serving as the reference (slow but full-network) estimator against which the REHE approximation is benchmarked for power, type-I error, and runtime. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008979

skills.description: Use when two preprocessed omics matrices from the same samples (e.g. DNA methylation beta values and urine metabolite intensities) need shared latent factors and a per-view variance-explained breakdown.
skills.name: variance-decomposition-across-omics-views
skills.search_text: variance-decomposition-across-omics-views Use when two preprocessed omics matrices from the same samples (e.g. DNA methylation beta values and urine metabolite intensities) need shared latent factors and a per-view variance-explained breakdown. Only one omics view is available — MOFA2 multi-view modeling requires the two views (DNAm and metabolomics) from the same samples The goal is to obtain factors from behavioral/phenotype data — the paper uses MCA via the R library FactoMineR (2.4) for behavioral data, not MOFA Metabolomics data have not yet been creatinine-normalized and filtered for missing values (samples/metabolites with ≥15% missing values discarded) — preprocessing must happen first Train a multi-view factor analysis model (R/Bioconductor MOFA2 v1.3.4) that jointly decomposes buccal DNA methylation and creatinine-normalized urine metabolomics data into 10 latent factors, exporting factor values and variance-explained (R2) per view per factor for each cohort. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/gigascience/giad115
skills.summary: Train a multi-view factor analysis model (R/Bioconductor MOFA2 v1.3.4) that jointly decomposes buccal DNA methylation and creatinine-normalized urine metabolomics data into 10 latent factors, exporting factor values and variance-explained (R2) per view per factor for each cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one omics view is available — MOFA2 multi-view modeling requires the two views (DNAm and metabolomics) from the same samples The goal is to obtain factors from behavioral/phenotype data — the paper uses MCA via the R library FactoMineR (2.4) for behavioral data, not MOFA Metabolomics data have not yet been creatinine-normalized and filtered for missing values (samples/metabolites with ≥15% missing values discarded) — preprocessing must happen first

skills.description: Use when you have a metabolomics matrix (e.g. the 158-lipid, 59-CRC-patient adipose dataset) processed both before and after linear mixed-effects model fitting and need to demonstrate improved group separation via PC1 explained variance.
skills.name: variance-explained-comparison
skills.search_text: variance-explained-comparison Use when you have a metabolomics matrix (e.g. the 158-lipid, 59-CRC-patient adipose dataset) processed both before and after linear mixed-effects model fitting and need to demonstrate improved group separation via PC1 explained variance. The data matrix has not been fit per metabolite with the LMM (fixed effects Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue; random intercept (1|Id)), so no before/after contrast exists The analysis goal is class prediction or feature selection (VIP > 1) rather than demonstrating improved variance structure via PCA The dataset lacks paired/subject metadata needed to formulate the LMMs, so the LMM-processed counterpart cannot be generated http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies the benefit of LMM-based metabolite-signal readjustment by running PCA on original vs. LMM-fitted metabolomics data and comparing the PC1 explained-variance proportion, validated in the CRC adipose lipid tutorial as a ~6 percentage-point increase with improved SAT/VAT separation. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.csbj.2019.04.009
skills.summary: Quantifies the benefit of LMM-based metabolite-signal readjustment by running PCA on original vs. LMM-fitted metabolomics data and comparing the PC1 explained-variance proportion, validated in the CRC adipose lipid tutorial as a ~6 percentage-point increase with improved SAT/VAT separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data matrix has not been fit per metabolite with the LMM (fixed effects Sex, Age, BMI, Stage, Location, Tissue; random intercept (1|Id)), so no before/after contrast exists The analysis goal is class prediction or feature selection (VIP > 1) rather than demonstrating improved variance structure via PCA The dataset lacks paired/subject metadata needed to formulate the LMMs, so the LMM-processed counterpart cannot be generated

skills.name: variance-explained-verification
skills.search_text: variance-explained-verification Use when you have original (pre-correction) UK Biobank NMR biomarker data plus sample QC fields and need to quantify which technical covariates drive biomarker variance, e.g. to justify or verify QC correction. When the goal is to correct/remove technical variation rather than quantify it — use ukbnmr::remove_technical_variation() instead When the input biomarker data has already been QC-corrected by ukbnmr — variance explained by technical covariates should be assessed on the original data only When the data are not UK Biobank NMR metabolomics fields with the Nightingale sample QC structure (plates, spectrometers, degradation time) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies how much variance in each of the 249 original UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations is explained by recorded technical covariates (plate well, batch, spectrometer, drift, degradation time) via per-covariate linear models, reproducing the Ritchie et al. 2023 variance-explained analysis that motivated the ukbnmr QC procedure. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41597-023-01949-y
skills.summary: Quantifies how much variance in each of the 249 original UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations is explained by recorded technical covariates (plate well, batch, spectrometer, drift, degradation time) via per-covariate linear models, reproducing the Ritchie et al. 2023 variance-explained analysis that motivated the ukbnmr QC procedure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to correct/remove technical variation rather than quantify it — use ukbnmr::remove_technical_variation() instead When the input biomarker data has already been QC-corrected by ukbnmr — variance explained by technical covariates should be assessed on the original data only When the data are not UK Biobank NMR metabolomics fields with the Nightingale sample QC structure (plates, spectrometers, degradation time)

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics data table (already normalized and log/sqrt/cube-root transformed) still spans a large dynamic range across metabolites and must be variance-scaled before statistical analysis or PCA-guided data treatment review.
skills.name: variance-scaling-parameter-selection
skills.search_text: variance-scaling-parameter-selection Use when a preprocessed metabolomics data table (already normalized and log/sqrt/cube-root transformed) still spans a large dynamic range across metabolites and must be variance-scaled before statistical analysis or PCA-guided data treatment review. The data table has not yet been through Viime's earlier treatment steps (error correction/imputation, normalization, and transformation such as Log10/Log2/square root/cube root) — scaling is the final step, not a substitute for them. The goal is missing-data imputation (MNAR/MCAR classification via missForest/impute) or normalization to a reference sample — those precede scaling in Viime's workflow. The task is multi-platform data integration (simple/mid-level/multi-block fusion) rather than per-column variance scaling of a single table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 The final data treatment step in Viime, which addresses the large dynamic range of metabolomics data by scaling the variance of each metabolite column, with options including autoscaling, Pareto scaling, range scaling, vast scaling and level scaling. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: The final data treatment step in Viime, which addresses the large dynamic range of metabolomics data by scaling the variance of each metabolite column, with options including autoscaling, Pareto scaling, range scaling, vast scaling and level scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data table has not yet been through Viime's earlier treatment steps (error correction/imputation, normalization, and transformation such as Log10/Log2/square root/cube root) — scaling is the final step, not a substitute for them. The goal is missing-data imputation (MNAR/MCAR classification via missForest/impute) or normalization to a reference sample — those precede scaling in Viime's workflow. The task is multi-platform data integration (simple/mid-level/multi-block fusion) rather than per-column variance scaling of a single table.

skills.description: Use when a metabolite concentration table (post-imputation and post-normalization, from a .csv or .xlsx upload) is right-skewed or spans a wide dynamic range and needs an element-wise log/power transform before scaling and PCA-based treatment selection.
skills.name: variance-stabilizing-log-transform
skills.search_text: variance-stabilizing-log-transform Use when a metabolite concentration table (post-imputation and post-normalization, from a .csv or .xlsx upload) is right-skewed or spans a wide dynamic range and needs an element-wise log/power transform before scaling and PCA-based treatment selection. The concentration table still contains missing values or has not been normalized — imputation (e.g., missForest/impute) and normalization precede transformation in Viime's workflow Only common statistical algorithms are needed — Viime implements those with Scikit-learn rather than the specialized R transformation functions The data are already approximately normal with a compressed dynamic range — the transformation step in Viime is optional http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Element-wise data transformation step from Viime's data treatment workflow that applies Log10, Log2, square root, or cube root to metabolite concentration columns, bringing the distribution closer to normality and compressing the dynamic range before scaling. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.02410
skills.summary: Element-wise data transformation step from Viime's data treatment workflow that applies Log10, Log2, square root, or cube root to metabolite concentration columns, bringing the distribution closer to normality and compressing the dynamic range before scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The concentration table still contains missing values or has not been normalized — imputation (e.g., missForest/impute) and normalization precede transformation in Viime's workflow Only common statistical algorithms are needed — Viime implements those with Scikit-learn rather than the specialized R transformation functions The data are already approximately normal with a compressed dynamic range — the transformation step in Viime is optional

skills.description: Use when you need to annotate coding variants with multiple tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP), normalize their impact terms to SO, and quantify agreement against ClinVar-annotated coding impact.
skills.name: variant-coding-impact-annotation
skills.search_text: variant-coding-impact-annotation Use when you need to annotate coding variants with multiple tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP), normalize their impact terms to SO, and quantify agreement against ClinVar-annotated coding impact. The goal is variant nomenclature (HGVSc/HGVSp) concordance rather than predicted coding impact — the paper reports these as separate metrics (HGVSc 58.52%, HGVSp 84.04%). The variant set is not phased and normalized, or contains unnormalized multi-nucleotide variants (MNVs), which produce inconsistent HGVS notation and unreliable impact calls. Only a single annotation tool is available — the skill's core value is cross-tool concordance against ClinVar, not single-tool annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates a benchmark variant set (164,549 two-star ClinVar variants) with ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP, normalizes each tool's predicted coding-impact terms to a common Sequence Ontology vocabulary, and computes per-tool concordance against ClinVar-reported impact (overall coding-impact agreement 85.58%). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Annotates a benchmark variant set (164,549 two-star ClinVar variants) with ANNOVAR, SnpEff, and VEP, normalizes each tool's predicted coding-impact terms to a common Sequence Ontology vocabulary, and computes per-tool concordance against ClinVar-reported impact (overall coding-impact agreement 85.58%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is variant nomenclature (HGVSc/HGVSp) concordance rather than predicted coding impact — the paper reports these as separate metrics (HGVSc 58.52%, HGVSp 84.04%). The variant set is not phased and normalized, or contains unnormalized multi-nucleotide variants (MNVs), which produce inconsistent HGVS notation and unreliable impact calls. Only a single annotation tool is available — the skill's core value is cross-tool concordance against ClinVar, not single-tool annotation.

skills.description: Use when building a variant benchmark from a ClinVar VCF for cross-tool (ANNOVAR/SnpEff/VEP) annotation comparison, where caller-dependent left/right shifts of nucleotide-repeat indels would produce inconsistent HGVS notation.
skills.name: variant-left-alignment-normalization
skills.search_text: variant-left-alignment-normalization Use when building a variant benchmark from a ClinVar VCF for cross-tool (ANNOVAR/SnpEff/VEP) annotation comparison, where caller-dependent left/right shifts of nucleotide-repeat indels would produce inconsistent HGVS notation. The input VCF is already left-aligned and normalized against the same reference genome and transcript annotation as the downstream annotation tools. The analysis uses a single annotation tool and does not compare HGVS nomenclature or coding-impact predictions across callers, so caller-dependent repeat-shift ambiguity does not affect results. The task involves natural-products data mining (NPLinker/GNPS/AntiSMASH workflows) rather than germline variant normalization. Left-aligns (normalizes) VCF records with bcftools so that repeat-region indels are represented identically regardless of the original variant caller, then applies a filtering chain (dedup, degenerate-base removal, indel/record exclusions) to produce a clean ClinVar-derived test set for cross-tool annotation comparison. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.10.11.617756
skills.summary: Left-aligns (normalizes) VCF records with bcftools so that repeat-region indels are represented identically regardless of the original variant caller, then applies a filtering chain (dedup, degenerate-base removal, indel/record exclusions) to produce a clean ClinVar-derived test set for cross-tool annotation comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input VCF is already left-aligned and normalized against the same reference genome and transcript annotation as the downstream annotation tools. The analysis uses a single annotation tool and does not compare HGVS nomenclature or coding-impact predictions across callers, so caller-dependent repeat-shift ambiguity does not affect results. The task involves natural-products data mining (NPLinker/GNPS/AntiSMASH workflows) rather than germline variant normalization.

skills.description: Use when a small labeled metabolomics cohort (e.g., binary classification, multi-class, or survival task) must be predicted and a pre-trained metabolomics VAE checkpoint exists to transfer from, outperforming randomly initialized or traditional ML baselines.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-fine-tuning-metabolomics
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-fine-tuning-metabolomics Use when a small labeled metabolomics cohort (e.g., binary classification, multi-class, or survival task) must be predicted and a pre-trained metabolomics VAE checkpoint exists to transfer from, outperforming randomly initialized or traditional ML baselines. The input is already raw LC/MS data (mzML files) — signal detection must first be done with mzLearn to produce the MS1 feature matrix No pre-trained checkpoint is available and the task is not a transfer-learning comparison — finetune_VAE_unsupervised_main with pretrained_dir=None reduces to random initialization The new data is from an LC mode other than HILIC positive mode — the current pre-trained model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fine-tunes a VAE pre-trained on an mzLearn-derived 2,736-feature MS1 metabolomics matrix from 20,548 blood samples onto a new cohort (e.g., CheckMate025 ccRCC serum data), using transfer learning of the final encoder layer plus a task head, with Optuna hyperparameter search. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Fine-tunes a VAE pre-trained on an mzLearn-derived 2,736-feature MS1 metabolomics matrix from 20,548 blood samples onto a new cohort (e.g., CheckMate025 ccRCC serum data), using transfer learning of the final encoder layer plus a task head, with Optuna hyperparameter search.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already raw LC/MS data (mzML files) — signal detection must first be done with mzLearn to produce the MS1 feature matrix No pre-trained checkpoint is available and the task is not a transfer-learning comparison — finetune_VAE_unsupervised_main with pretrained_dir=None reduces to random initialization The new data is from an LC mode other than HILIC positive mode — the current pre-trained model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode

skills.description: Use when you need to learn a compressed latent representation of high-dimensional, TIC-normalized MSI spectra stored in HDF5 (tens of thousands of m/z variables) as the probabilistic feature layer of a pixel-based tissue classification model.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-training Use when you need to learn a compressed latent representation of high-dimensional, TIC-normalized MSI spectra stored in HDF5 (tens of thousands of m/z variables) as the probabilistic feature layer of a pixel-based tissue classification model. The analysis goal is multi-class tissue classification — the article demonstrates only binary (normal vs. tumor) classification and defers multi-class to future development. Input data has already been peak-picked or reduced to a feature/peak table — this skill is designed to learn directly from full, raw TIC-normalized spectra to avoid user preprocessing bias. Ground-truth annotations for the tissue/tumor type of interest cannot be reliably established (e.g., intra-tumor heterogeneity or tumor-margin cases requiring further pathological investigation). http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a probabilistic VAE (Keras/TensorFlow) on raw TIC-normalized MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging spectra (85,062 m/z variables) to learn a 5-dimensional latent representation used for downstream tumor classification, with no prior preprocessing or peak picking. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Trains a probabilistic VAE (Keras/TensorFlow) on raw TIC-normalized MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging spectra (85,062 m/z variables) to learn a 5-dimensional latent representation used for downstream tumor classification, with no prior preprocessing or peak picking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is multi-class tissue classification — the article demonstrates only binary (normal vs. tumor) classification and defers multi-class to future development. Input data has already been peak-picked or reduced to a feature/peak table — this skill is designed to learn directly from full, raw TIC-normalized spectra to avoid user preprocessing bias. Ground-truth annotations for the tissue/tumor type of interest cannot be reliably established (e.g., intra-tumor heterogeneity or tumor-margin cases requiring further pathological investigation).

skills.description: Use when paired ST-SM samples (e.g., human ccRCC, GBM, or mouse brain) need cross-modal, cross-sample integration into a joint low-dimensional embedding for downstream clustering, deconvolution-based annotation, or benchmarking against integration tools.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-training-for-spatial-data
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-training-for-spatial-data Use when paired ST-SM samples (e.g., human ccRCC, GBM, or mouse brain) need cross-modal, cross-sample integration into a joint low-dimensional embedding for downstream clustering, deconvolution-based annotation, or benchmarking against integration tools. Data are single-cell or subcellular resolution ST/SM — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only More than two modalities must be integrated — SpatialMETA currently supports integration of only two modalities SM and ST are measured on the same tissue section at cellular resolution requiring precise cell segmentation — computational alignment at cellular/subcellular levels is not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE), to jointly embed spatial transcriptomics (ST) and spatial metabolomics (SM) data for vertical and horizontal integration, producing latent embeddings and normalized expression used for benchmarking and spatial cluster analysis. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z
skills.summary: Train SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE), to jointly embed spatial transcriptomics (ST) and spatial metabolomics (SM) data for vertical and horizontal integration, producing latent embeddings and normalized expression used for benchmarking and spatial cluster analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell or subcellular resolution ST/SM — SpatialMETA is designed for low-resolution ST and SM data only More than two modalities must be integrated — SpatialMETA currently supports integration of only two modalities SM and ST are measured on the same tissue section at cellular resolution requiring precise cell segmentation — computational alignment at cellular/subcellular levels is not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when you have a standardized LC/MS1 feature table of blood-sample metabolite intensities (e.g. [n_samples, 2736] floats) and want unsupervised latent embeddings that organize samples by disease or age without supervision.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-training-on-metabolomics-feature-matrix
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-training-on-metabolomics-feature-matrix Use when you have a standardized LC/MS1 feature table of blood-sample metabolite intensities (e.g. [n_samples, 2736] floats) and want unsupervised latent embeddings that organize samples by disease or age without supervision. Your goal is raw LC/MS signal detection: use mzLearn to generate the feature matrix first — it works from mzML files and its outputs are ion MS1 level only, without de-isotoping or MS/MS identification Your data are not HILIC positive-mode metabolomics feature vectors: the pre-trained model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode, and multi-modal integration of other LC types/modes is not yet developed You already have a fine-tuned task model and need supervised predictions (binary/multiclass/survival) — use the fine-tuning workflow with pretrained_dir rather than pretraining from scratch http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train an unsupervised variational autoencoder (VAE) on the mzLearn MS1 ion-feature matrix (2,736 robust metabolite signals across 20,548 blood samples from 22 public studies) to learn latent metabolite representations that capture demographic and disease structure, yielding a reusable pre-trained checkpoint (vae_pretrained.pt / best_model.pt) for downstream fine-tuning. metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2025.01.26.634927
skills.summary: Train an unsupervised variational autoencoder (VAE) on the mzLearn MS1 ion-feature matrix (2,736 robust metabolite signals across 20,548 blood samples from 22 public studies) to learn latent metabolite representations that capture demographic and disease structure, yielding a reusable pre-trained checkpoint (vae_pretrained.pt / best_model.pt) for downstream fine-tuning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is raw LC/MS signal detection: use mzLearn to generate the feature matrix first — it works from mzML files and its outputs are ion MS1 level only, without de-isotoping or MS/MS identification Your data are not HILIC positive-mode metabolomics feature vectors: the pre-trained model was developed specifically for HILIC positive mode, and multi-modal integration of other LC types/modes is not yet developed You already have a fine-tuned task model and need supervised predictions (binary/multiclass/survival) — use the fine-tuning workflow with pretrained_dir rather than pretraining from scratch

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed bag-of-fragments MS/MS spectra (e.g. a GNPS MGF set of 5,670 spectra or a ~1,000-peak beer extract) and need unsupervised decomposition into Mass2Motifs rather than supervised spectral matching.
skills.name: variational-bayes-inference-training
skills.search_text: variational-bayes-inference-training Use when you have preprocessed bag-of-fragments MS/MS spectra (e.g. a GNPS MGF set of 5,670 spectra or a ~1,000-peak beer extract) and need unsupervised decomposition into Mass2Motifs rather than supervised spectral matching. Input is already a spectral-similarity feature table or a Molecular Networking result — MS2LDA is unsupervised and needs raw bag-of-fragments documents, not precomputed similarities Spectra come from simple mixtures with sparse, information-poor MS2 (single fixed collision energy and few fragments) — the paper notes MS2LDA 'works best for complex mixtures where a large number of metabolites are fragmented and information-rich MS2 spectra are available (e.g., generated by ramped or stepped collision energy)' MS1-to-MS2 matching is unreliable — the workflow depends on 'reliable matching of MS1 peaks to MS2 spectra' before topic inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Train an MS2LDA latent Dirichlet allocation model on preprocessed MS/MS spectra using variational Bayes inference so the whole fragmentation dataset is decomposed into co-occurring fragment/neutral-loss sets called Mass2Motifs, enabling unsupervised substructure discovery and spectral connectivity in metabolomics. metabolomics/v3 10.1073/pnas.1608041113
skills.summary: Train an MS2LDA latent Dirichlet allocation model on preprocessed MS/MS spectra using variational Bayes inference so the whole fragmentation dataset is decomposed into co-occurring fragment/neutral-loss sets called Mass2Motifs, enabling unsupervised substructure discovery and spectral connectivity in metabolomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a spectral-similarity feature table or a Molecular Networking result — MS2LDA is unsupervised and needs raw bag-of-fragments documents, not precomputed similarities Spectra come from simple mixtures with sparse, information-poor MS2 (single fixed collision energy and few fragments) — the paper notes MS2LDA 'works best for complex mixtures where a large number of metabolites are fragmented and information-rich MS2 spectra are available (e.g., generated by ramped or stepped collision energy)' MS1-to-MS2 matching is unreliable — the workflow depends on 'reliable matching of MS1 peaks to MS2 spectra' before topic inference

skills.description: Use when high-dimensional, TIC-normalized mass spectrometry imaging spectra (e.g. 85,062 m/z variables from MALDI FT-ICR MSI) must be compressed into a low-dimensional latent space and reconstructed to a target MSE, without prior peak picking or preprocessing.
skills.name: variational-lower-bound-optimization
skills.search_text: variational-lower-bound-optimization Use when high-dimensional, TIC-normalized mass spectrometry imaging spectra (e.g. 85,062 m/z variables from MALDI FT-ICR MSI) must be compressed into a low-dimensional latent space and reconstructed to a target MSE, without prior peak picking or preprocessing. The goal is supervised pixel classification (tumor vs. normal) rather than unsupervised spectral reconstruction — use the full massNet classification pipeline with benchmarking against SVM instead. Input spectra are raw and unnormalized or require prior preprocessing/peak picking — massNet's VAE operates directly on TIC-normalized data without prior preprocessing. The task requires multi-class tissue classification — the article demonstrates only binary class classification and leaves multi-class extension to future development. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a probabilistic encoder–decoder (variational autoencoder, as implemented in the massNet VAE module) by maximizing the variational lower bound over TIC-normalized MSI spectra, yielding a compact latent representation that reconstructs the original spectra at sub-1e-7 MSE. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac032
skills.summary: Train a probabilistic encoder–decoder (variational autoencoder, as implemented in the massNet VAE module) by maximizing the variational lower bound over TIC-normalized MSI spectra, yielding a compact latent representation that reconstructs the original spectra at sub-1e-7 MSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is supervised pixel classification (tumor vs. normal) rather than unsupervised spectral reconstruction — use the full massNet classification pipeline with benchmarking against SVM instead. Input spectra are raw and unnormalized or require prior preprocessing/peak picking — massNet's VAE operates directly on TIC-normalized data without prior preprocessing. The task requires multi-class tissue classification — the article demonstrates only binary class classification and leaves multi-class extension to future development.

skills.description: Use when preparing a ClinVar or other VCF as a benchmark for comparing variant annotation tools and you must define a reproducible, high-review-status variant set with known clinical-significance composition.
skills.name: vcf-variant-filtering
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-filtering Use when preparing a ClinVar or other VCF as a benchmark for comparing variant annotation tools and you must define a reproducible, high-review-status variant set with known clinical-significance composition. The variant set is trans-QTL or lacks proxy/LD information — the sentinel-proxy IMPACT annotation scheme assumes LD-defined proxies for each sentinel Variants are not on GRCh37 coordinates — VEP must be run against the GRCh37 assembly for ProGeM's gene model (Homo_sapiens.GRCh37.82.gtf) to align The goal is top-down candidate scoring only — IMPACT annotation feeds the bottom-up component and is redundant if no positional/cis-eQTL candidates are being evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Annotate sentinel and proxy variants of molecular QTLs with Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) IMPACT categories (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/MODIFIER) and use these to flag bottom-up candidate causal genes whose function the variant is expected to alter. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gky837
skills.summary: Annotate sentinel and proxy variants of molecular QTLs with Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) IMPACT categories (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/MODIFIER) and use these to flag bottom-up candidate causal genes whose function the variant is expected to alter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant set is trans-QTL or lacks proxy/LD information — the sentinel-proxy IMPACT annotation scheme assumes LD-defined proxies for each sentinel Variants are not on GRCh37 coordinates — VEP must be run against the GRCh37 assembly for ProGeM's gene model (Homo_sapiens.GRCh37.82.gtf) to align The goal is top-down candidate scoring only — IMPACT annotation feeds the bottom-up component and is redundant if no positional/cis-eQTL candidates are being evaluated

skills.search_text: vep-variant-impact-annotation Use when sentinel/proxy variants for molecular QTLs need functional consequence annotation (VEP IMPACT HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/MODIFIER) as input to bottom-up causal gene prioritization. The analysis targets trans-pQTLs, where ProGeM's local-window and top-down strategy would need a fundamentally different approach Sentinel/proxy coordinates are not on GRCh37 — VEP must be run against GRCh37 for compatibility with the GRCh37_genes.RData gene model The goal is regulatory/intergenic interpretation only: VEP MODIFIER consequences (e.g. intron_variant, upstream_gene_variant) are scored 0 and not used to highlight candidate genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Run Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) on molecular QTL sentinel and proxy variants and feed the IMPACT-annotated output into ProGeM so that bottom-up candidate causal genes containing a HIGH or MODERATE IMPACT variant can be highlighted. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gky837
skills.summary: Run Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) on molecular QTL sentinel and proxy variants and feed the IMPACT-annotated output into ProGeM so that bottom-up candidate causal genes containing a HIGH or MODERATE IMPACT variant can be highlighted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets trans-pQTLs, where ProGeM's local-window and top-down strategy would need a fundamentally different approach Sentinel/proxy coordinates are not on GRCh37 — VEP must be run against GRCh37 for compatibility with the GRCh37_genes.RData gene model The goal is regulatory/intergenic interpretation only: VEP MODIFIER consequences (e.g. intron_variant, upstream_gene_variant) are scored 0 and not used to highlight candidate genes

Evaluating horizontal (cross-sample) integration of ST-SM data rather than vertical integration of paired modalities on the same section Input ST/SM data are at single-cell or subcellular resolution — SpatialMETA and this benchmark are designed for low-resolution ST and SM data No manually annotated ground-truth labels are available, since the scIB biological conservation evaluation requires the H&E-derived label key http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3922 Benchmark vertical integration of paired spatial transcriptomics (ST) and spatial metabolomics (SM) samples by computing scIB-style reconstruction accuracy, continuity, marker, and biological conservation metrics for SpatialMETA and seven baseline methods, then aggregating them into an overall score ranking. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-63915-z

skills.description: Use when reproducing or adapting the GLEAMS neural architecture that embeds MS/MS spectra into a 32-dimensional space, or when training a Siamese contrastive model on PSM pairs.
skills.name: vgg-inspired-multi-branch-network-architecture
skills.search_text: vgg-inspired-multi-branch-network-architecture Use when reproducing or adapting the GLEAMS neural architecture that embeds MS/MS spectra into a 32-dimensional space, or when training a Siamese contrastive model on PSM pairs. Input spectra lack reliable peptide identifications (PSMs) — the pair-construction step needs same-peptide positives from MassIVE-KB annotations The goal is inference/annotation with pre-trained embeddings rather than (re)training — use the released gleams_82c0124b.hdf5 weights directly instead No CUDA-enabled GPU or Linux environment is available, which the GLEAMS training setup requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstruct the GLEAMS embedder: parallel VGG-inspired branches for precursor, fragment-peak, and reference-spectrum features, concatenated and mapped through dense layers to a 32-dimensional L2-regularized output, trained as a Siamese pair network with contrastive loss. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41592-022-01496-1
skills.summary: Reconstruct the GLEAMS embedder: parallel VGG-inspired branches for precursor, fragment-peak, and reference-spectrum features, concatenated and mapped through dense layers to a 32-dimensional L2-regularized output, trained as a Siamese pair network with contrastive loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra lack reliable peptide identifications (PSMs) — the pair-construction step needs same-peptide positives from MassIVE-KB annotations The goal is inference/annotation with pre-trained embeddings rather than (re)training — use the released gleams_82c0124b.hdf5 weights directly instead No CUDA-enabled GPU or Linux environment is available, which the GLEAMS training setup requires

skills.description: Use when you need to stand up or reconfigure a ViMMS 2.0 simulation: installing the framework in a Python 3.0+ virtualenv, choosing a chemical source (HMDB-sampled synthetic or UnknownChemical extraction from an existing mzML like Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.
skills.name: vimms-framework-configuration
skills.search_text: vimms-framework-configuration Use when you need to stand up or reconfigure a ViMMS 2.0 simulation: installing the framework in a Python 3.0+ virtualenv, choosing a chemical source (HMDB-sampled synthetic or UnknownChemical extraction from an existing mzML like Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS. Input is an experimental mzML you want to analyze directly for metabolite identification — ViMMS is a simulator of the acquisition process, not a data-analysis pipeline. You need to run fragmentation strategies unchanged on an actual Thermo Tribrid Fusion instrument — that requires the separate IAPI bridging code (thermofisherlsms/iapi) rather than the simulator configuration alone. A validated pickled chemical list already exists for your mzML — regenerating chemicals via ChemicalMixtureFromMZML is redundant unless the ROI threshold or source file changed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Configure and set up the ViMMS 2.0 Python framework to simulate tandem MS fragmentation strategies in LC-MS metabolomics, from dependency installation through chemical-source selection (synthetic sampling or mzML ROI extraction) to running controllers in an Environment and exporting mzML. metabolomics/v3 10.21105/joss.03990
skills.summary: Configure and set up the ViMMS 2.0 Python framework to simulate tandem MS fragmentation strategies in LC-MS metabolomics, from dependency installation through chemical-source selection (synthetic sampling or mzML ROI extraction) to running controllers in an Environment and exporting mzML.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an experimental mzML you want to analyze directly for metabolite identification — ViMMS is a simulator of the acquisition process, not a data-analysis pipeline. You need to run fragmentation strategies unchanged on an actual Thermo Tribrid Fusion instrument — that requires the separate IAPI bridging code (thermofisherlsms/iapi) rather than the simulator configuration alone. A validated pickled chemical list already exists for your mzML — regenerating chemicals via ChemicalMixtureFromMZML is redundant unless the ROI threshold or source file changed.

skills.description: Use when query spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) may come from molecule variants — precursor m/z differs from any database molecule by an explainable modification delta — and you need variant identification plus modification-site localization.
skills.name: vinsmoc-variable-mode-spectral-search
skills.search_text: vinsmoc-variable-mode-spectral-search Use when query spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) may come from molecule variants — precursor m/z differs from any database molecule by an explainable modification delta — and you need variant identification plus modification-site localization. The precursor mass of the query spectrum exactly matches a known database molecule — use VInSMoC's exact search mode instead of variable mode Spectra were already peak-merged and peak-filtered before upload — in that case the server's default preprocessing settings should be adjusted rather than left at defaults A generalized-peptide search is inappropriate because the candidates are generic small molecules (or vice versa) — the fragmentation mode must match the molecule class http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Run VInSMoC on the npanalysis.org server in variable search mode so query mass spectra match candidate molecules whose variants explain the precursor mass difference, then extract and evaluate the predicted modification sites. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s43588-025-00923-5
skills.summary: Run VInSMoC on the npanalysis.org server in variable search mode so query mass spectra match candidate molecules whose variants explain the precursor mass difference, then extract and evaluate the predicted modification sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The precursor mass of the query spectrum exactly matches a known database molecule — use VInSMoC's exact search mode instead of variable mode Spectra were already peak-merged and peak-filtered before upload — in that case the server's default preprocessing settings should be adjusted rather than left at defaults A generalized-peptide search is inappropriate because the candidates are generic small molecules (or vice versa) — the fragmentation mode must match the molecule class

skills.search_text: violin-plot-grouped-attribute-visualization Use when comparing a distribution of pair-level replicability or similarity scores (e.g., CCRS between retention orders) across categorical chromatographic configuration attributes such as organic-phase modifier or column temperature difference. The comparison variable is continuous (e.g., ΔpH or ΔF vs CCRS) — use a scatter plot with Pearson r and 95% confidence interval instead of grouped violins Data are per-compound RTs rather than per-pair replicability scores; compute CCRS between paired retention orders of shared compounds first The system is HILIC rather than RPLC — the article's replicability analysis (and ROASMI) applies only to the RPLC system http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates violin plots of per-pair CCRS (correlation coefficient of retention sequences) grouped by chromatographic configuration attributes (e.g., organic-phase modifier, Δ column temperature) to visually assess which factors drive retention-order replicability across paired RPLC datasets. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s13321-025-00968-8
skills.summary: Generates violin plots of per-pair CCRS (correlation coefficient of retention sequences) grouped by chromatographic configuration attributes (e.g., organic-phase modifier, Δ column temperature) to visually assess which factors drive retention-order replicability across paired RPLC datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison variable is continuous (e.g., ΔpH or ΔF vs CCRS) — use a scatter plot with Pearson r and 95% confidence interval instead of grouped violins Data are per-compound RTs rather than per-pair replicability scores; compute CCRS between paired retention orders of shared compounds first The system is HILIC rather than RPLC — the article's replicability analysis (and ROASMI) applies only to the RPLC system
