skills.description: Use when analyzing a pseudotargeted metabolomics feature/peak-area table (metabolites × samples) across a mutant or treatment panel to find co-abundance modules and rank samples by module eigenmetabolite for biomarker metabolite screening.
skills.name: wgcna-module-eigenmetabolite-screening
skills.search_text: wgcna-module-eigenmetabolite-screening Use when analyzing a pseudotargeted metabolomics feature/peak-area table (metabolites × samples) across a mutant or treatment panel to find co-abundance modules and rank samples by module eigenmetabolite for biomarker metabolite screening. Input is raw LC-MS data (mzML etc.) rather than a peak table — upstream peak picking and data cleaning by tidyMass within MetMiner must be run first Input file is .csv, .xlsx or .xls — the WGCNA-shinyApp only accepts tab-delimited .txt/.tsv files, so convert the format first The analysis goal is metabolite annotation from spectra rather than co-abundance network mining — use MetMiner's annotation pipeline with the plant-specific MS database instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 An iterative weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) strategy, delivered through MetMiner's Shiny interface, that clusters metabolite abundance features into modules and uses module eigenmetabolites to rank mutants and screen for biomarker metabolites such as hub glucosinolates. metabolomics/v3 10.1111/jipb.13774
skills.summary: An iterative weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) strategy, delivered through MetMiner's Shiny interface, that clusters metabolite abundance features into modules and uses module eigenmetabolites to rank mutants and screen for biomarker metabolites such as hub glucosinolates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw LC-MS data (mzML etc.) rather than a peak table — upstream peak picking and data cleaning by tidyMass within MetMiner must be run first Input file is .csv, .xlsx or .xls — the WGCNA-shinyApp only accepts tab-delimited .txt/.tsv files, so convert the format first The analysis goal is metabolite annotation from spectra rather than co-abundance network mining — use MetMiner's annotation pipeline with the plant-specific MS database instead

skills.description: Use when a set of MS/MS feature spectra in .mgf format needs a 2D similarity-based overview embedding, or when reproducing the paper's wheat-data t-SNE grouping of features around reference standards like Procyanidin-A2.
skills.name: wheat-metabolomics-feature-handling
skills.search_text: wheat-metabolomics-feature-handling Use when a set of MS/MS feature spectra in .mgf format needs a 2D similarity-based overview embedding, or when reproducing the paper's wheat-data t-SNE grouping of features around reference standards like Procyanidin-A2. Datasets larger than ~5000 features — the article anticipates the dashboard will face difficulties for larger data sets and liberal settings Goal is library annotation or analog search (MS2Query library search) rather than similarity-matrix embedding and local connectivity exploration Only a static overview is needed and no expert visual follow-up is possible — the t-SNE overview figure is difficult to read on its own http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Reproduce the two-dimensional t-SNE overview embedding of pairwise ms2deepscore similarities for LC-MS/MS feature data (e.g. the wheat dataset), as used by the specXplore dashboard as its quantitative backbone. This yields a per-feature 2D layout in which high-similarity spectral features group locally, e.g. around the Procyanidin-A2 reference standard. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.3c04444
skills.summary: Reproduce the two-dimensional t-SNE overview embedding of pairwise ms2deepscore similarities for LC-MS/MS feature data (e.g. the wheat dataset), as used by the specXplore dashboard as its quantitative backbone. This yields a per-feature 2D layout in which high-similarity spectral features group locally, e.g. around the Procyanidin-A2 reference standard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets larger than ~5000 features — the article anticipates the dashboard will face difficulties for larger data sets and liberal settings Goal is library annotation or analog search (MS2Query library search) rather than similarity-matrix embedding and local connectivity exploration Only a static overview is needed and no expert visual follow-up is possible — the t-SNE overview figure is difficult to read on its own

skills.description: Use when a group-delay-corrected FID dataframe from 1H-NMR metabolomics data still contains a dominant residual solvent decay that must be separated from the sample signal before apodization and Fourier transform.
skills.name: whittaker-penalized-least-squares-smoothing
skills.search_text: whittaker-penalized-least-squares-smoothing Use when a group-delay-corrected FID dataframe from 1H-NMR metabolomics data still contains a dominant residual solvent decay that must be separated from the sample signal before apodization and Fourier transform. The data are already frequency-domain spectra — baseline issues there are handled by px.baseline_correction(spectra_df, method='airpls'), not by this FID-domain solvent removal. The FIDs have not yet been group-delay corrected, so the solvent decay cannot be modeled as a smooth component of grpd_df. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Estimates and removes residual solvent (water) signals from 1H-NMR FID data by fitting a smooth component via discrete penalized least squares with second-order differences (Whittaker smoother), as implemented in Protomix's solvent_residuals_removal function. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae192
skills.summary: Estimates and removes residual solvent (water) signals from 1H-NMR FID data by fitting a smooth component via discrete penalized least squares with second-order differences (Whittaker smoother), as implemented in Protomix's solvent_residuals_removal function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already frequency-domain spectra — baseline issues there are handled by px.baseline_correction(spectra_df, method='airpls'), not by this FID-domain solvent removal. The FIDs have not yet been group-delay corrected, so the solvent decay cannot be modeled as a smooth component of grpd_df.

skills.description: Use when a GCxGC-MS chromatogram (e.g., a baseline-corrected 2D-TIC from the MTBLS579 dataset) still contains noise after baseline correction and signal smoothing along the first chromatographic dimension is required before multivariate analysis.
skills.name: whittaker-smoother-parameterization
skills.search_text: whittaker-smoother-parameterization Use when a GCxGC-MS chromatogram (e.g., a baseline-corrected 2D-TIC from the MTBLS579 dataset) still contains noise after baseline correction and signal smoothing along the first chromatographic dimension is required before multivariate analysis. The chromatogram has not yet been baseline-corrected — the RGCxGC pipeline applies baseline correction (asymmetric least squares) before smoothing variants like MTBLS08_sm1 are generated. The goal is peak misalignment correction rather than noise reduction — use the 2D-COW alignment (batch_2DCOW / twod_cow) skill instead of smoothing. The input is 1D chromatography data or a feature table rather than a folded two-dimensional GCxGC 2D-TIC chromatogram. http://edamontology.org/topic_3954 Applies the Whittaker smoother (Eilers' penalized least-squares smoother) to a 2D-TIC GCxGC chromatogram via the RGCxGC wsmooth function, with an explicit penalty order and lambda. The linear-penalty variant (penalty=1, lambda=1e1) applied to the baseline-corrected 08GB chromatogram reproduces the smoothed variant MTBLS08_sm1. metabolomics/v3 10.1016/j.microc.2020.104830
skills.summary: Applies the Whittaker smoother (Eilers' penalized least-squares smoother) to a 2D-TIC GCxGC chromatogram via the RGCxGC wsmooth function, with an explicit penalty order and lambda. The linear-penalty variant (penalty=1, lambda=1e1) applied to the baseline-corrected 08GB chromatogram reproduces the smoothed variant MTBLS08_sm1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The chromatogram has not yet been baseline-corrected — the RGCxGC pipeline applies baseline correction (asymmetric least squares) before smoothing variants like MTBLS08_sm1 are generated. The goal is peak misalignment correction rather than noise reduction — use the 2D-COW alignment (batch_2DCOW / twod_cow) skill instead of smoothing. The input is 1D chromatography data or a feature table rather than a folded two-dimensional GCxGC 2D-TIC chromatogram.

skills.description: Use when IMC nuclear channel (DNA-intercalator/Histone 3) segmentation exists but whole-cell boundaries are needed to profile per-cell protein and metabolite signals in spatially crowded tissue.
skills.name: whole-cell-cytosol-segmentation-mesmer
skills.search_text: whole-cell-cytosol-segmentation-mesmer Use when IMC nuclear channel (DNA-intercalator/Histone 3) segmentation exists but whole-cell boundaries are needed to profile per-cell protein and metabolite signals in spatially crowded tissue. Input is already a per-cell feature/intensity table rather than raw multiplexed IMC images Data lack a nuclear channel (DNA-intercalator/Histone 3) or membrane/cytosolic markers, so neither Cellpose nuclei nor Mesmer whole-cell expansion can be seeded Goal is metabolite-only pixel clustering of SIMS data without single-cell resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Expands Cellpose-derived nuclear masks into whole-cell/cytosol segmentation masks using the Mesmer pipeline via the scSpaMet wrapper, enabling per-single-cell extraction of protein (IMC) and metabolite (TOF-SIMS) intensities in crowded human tissues. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-43917-5
skills.summary: Expands Cellpose-derived nuclear masks into whole-cell/cytosol segmentation masks using the Mesmer pipeline via the scSpaMet wrapper, enabling per-single-cell extraction of protein (IMC) and metabolite (TOF-SIMS) intensities in crowded human tissues.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-cell feature/intensity table rather than raw multiplexed IMC images Data lack a nuclear channel (DNA-intercalator/Histone 3) or membrane/cytosolic markers, so neither Cellpose nuclei nor Mesmer whole-cell expansion can be seeded Goal is metabolite-only pixel clustering of SIMS data without single-cell resolution

skills.description: Use when the input is a wide-formatted metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) plus a design file, to be fed into any SECIMTools tool or Galaxy-wrapped step.
skills.name: wide-format-data-loading
skills.search_text: wide-format-data-loading Use when the input is a wide-formatted metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) plus a design file, to be fed into any SECIMTools tool or Galaxy-wrapped step. The input is a raw instrument file or peak-picked output — SECIMTools expects a feature table produced after peak picking / feature identification, not vendor formats. The table is long/stacked format (one observation per row) rather than wide format with samples as columns. The analysis is not a metabolomics feature-table workflow (SECIMTools is scoped to metabolomics data processing, which the authors note spans sample preparation, data acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis). http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Loads SECIMTools-style metabolomics feature tables in wide format — samples as columns, metabolomics features as rows — together with the companion design file, so downstream SECIMTools tools (hierarchical clustering heatmap, PCA, flags, etc.) receive a consistent, tool-parseable input. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Loads SECIMTools-style metabolomics feature tables in wide format — samples as columns, metabolomics features as rows — together with the companion design file, so downstream SECIMTools tools (hierarchical clustering heatmap, PCA, flags, etc.) receive a consistent, tool-parseable input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw instrument file or peak-picked output — SECIMTools expects a feature table produced after peak picking / feature identification, not vendor formats. The table is long/stacked format (one observation per row) rather than wide format with samples as columns. The analysis is not a metabolomics feature-table workflow (SECIMTools is scoped to metabolomics data processing, which the authors note spans sample preparation, data acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis).

skills.description: Use when the input is a wide-format feature intensity table (unique feature identifiers as rows, samples as columns) plus a companion design file, and the goal is blank-based quality-control filtering of metabolomic features.
skills.name: wide-format-feature-table-processing
skills.search_text: wide-format-feature-table-processing Use when the input is a wide-format feature intensity table (unique feature identifiers as rows, samples as columns) plus a companion design file, and the goal is blank-based quality-control filtering of metabolomic features. The data are still raw instrument acquisitions needing peak picking/feature identification, which the article treats as a platform-specific step upstream of SECIMTools feature-table QC The goal is a QC check other than blank-based detection (e.g. Threshold Based Flags, CV Flags, Run Order Regression, retention time flags), which use group statistics or run-order rather than blank-sample intensities There are no blank samples in the design file, so no per-feature limit of detection from blanks can be computed Loading, annotating, and quality-filtering a wide-format metabolomic feature intensity table (samples as columns, features as rows) using SECIMTools-style QC steps such as Blank Feature Filtering (BFF), which computes a per-feature limit of detection from blank samples. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1

skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are still raw instrument acquisitions needing peak picking/feature identification, which the article treats as a platform-specific step upstream of SECIMTools feature-table QC The goal is a QC check other than blank-based detection (e.g. Threshold Based Flags, CV Flags, Run Order Regression, retention time flags), which use group statistics or run-order rather than blank-sample intensities There are no blank samples in the design file, so no per-feature limit of detection from blanks can be computed

skills.description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (post peak-picking, samples-as-columns/features-as-rows) contains missing values that must be filled before downstream statistical analysis or tool linkage in SECIMTools/Galaxy.
skills.name: wide-format-metabolomics-data-handling
skills.search_text: wide-format-metabolomics-data-handling Use when a metabolomics feature table (post peak-picking, samples-as-columns/features-as-rows) contains missing values that must be filled before downstream statistical analysis or tool linkage in SECIMTools/Galaxy. Input is raw instrument output (pre peak-picking / feature identification) rather than a feature table — the article assigns peak picking to upstream platforms such as Galaxy-M and Workflow4Metabolomics, not SECIMTools The table has no missing values and only needs re-scaling — use the Data Normalization and Re-Scaling tool (sample mean, median, or sum of all features as scaling factors) instead Features should be removed rather than imputed — flag-and-filter tools (Blank Feature Filtering, Threshold Based Flags) are the correct choice for low-quality or below-detection features http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Handles metabolomics feature tables in SECIMTools' standard wide format — samples as columns, features as rows — and fills missing values via group mean, group median, or K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) imputation, emitting a completed table with a per-feature imputation flag column. This enforces the standard data formats that allow arbitrary linkages between SECIMTools tools for novel workflow designs. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-018-2134-1
skills.summary: Handles metabolomics feature tables in SECIMTools' standard wide format — samples as columns, features as rows — and fills missing values via group mean, group median, or K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) imputation, emitting a completed table with a per-feature imputation flag column. This enforces the standard data formats that allow arbitrary linkages between SECIMTools tools for novel workflow designs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw instrument output (pre peak-picking / feature identification) rather than a feature table — the article assigns peak picking to upstream platforms such as Galaxy-M and Workflow4Metabolomics, not SECIMTools The table has no missing values and only needs re-scaling — use the Data Normalization and Re-Scaling tool (sample mean, median, or sum of all features as scaling factors) instead Features should be removed rather than imputed — flag-and-filter tools (Blank Feature Filtering, Threshold Based Flags) are the correct choice for low-quality or below-detection features

skills.description: Use when raw AEMS data are in Sciex .wiff/.wiff.scan format and you need full-scan (precursor ion or neutral loss) spectra per acoustic ejection rather than vendor MRM output.
skills.name: wiff-scan-block-binary-parsing
skills.search_text: wiff-scan-block-binary-parsing Use when raw AEMS data are in Sciex .wiff/.wiff.scan format and you need full-scan (precursor ion or neutral loss) spectra per acoustic ejection rather than vendor MRM output. The acquisition is MRM (targeted transitions) rather than full-scan PI/NL mode — rtmsEcho processes MRM runs through its own targeted-transition pipeline instead of full-scan block reconstruction The data are already in an open interchange format (e.g. mzML) and do not require parsing proprietary .wiff.scan binary blocks The goal is chromatographic peak processing on conventional LC-MS data rather than AEMS shot-to-ejection spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Parses Sciex .wiff/.wiff.scan binary blocks from full-scan (PI or NL mode) AEMS acquisitions by locating per-detection-time-point scan blocks, decompressing their binary m/z and intensity arrays, and reconstructing per-ejection spectra compatible with the rtms R package data structure. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c03730
skills.summary: Parses Sciex .wiff/.wiff.scan binary blocks from full-scan (PI or NL mode) AEMS acquisitions by locating per-detection-time-point scan blocks, decompressing their binary m/z and intensity arrays, and reconstructing per-ejection spectra compatible with the rtms R package data structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The acquisition is MRM (targeted transitions) rather than full-scan PI/NL mode — rtmsEcho processes MRM runs through its own targeted-transition pipeline instead of full-scan block reconstruction The data are already in an open interchange format (e.g. mzML) and do not require parsing proprietary .wiff.scan binary blocks The goal is chromatographic peak processing on conventional LC-MS data rather than AEMS shot-to-ejection spectra

skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-testing Use when pixels from an MSI feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ion peaks) have been assigned to biological regions via UMAP-kmeans clustering and you need a non-parametric per-ion differential test between two region groups (e.g., MB clusters 6/1 vs HIP clusters 23/12). When regions have not been defined — if no UMAP-kmeans or manual ROI assignment exists yet, run SMAnalyst's pixel clustering or ROI drawing first rather than testing on arbitrary groupings When the comparison requires parametric modeling of covariates or replicate-level design rather than pixel-level univariate ranking When input is raw IMS mass-spec data rather than an already-picked, QC-filtered feature matrix of ion intensities per pixel http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Univariate Wilcoxon rank-sum differential testing between pixel clusters defined on spatial metabolomics (MSI) data, used in SMAnalyst's workflow to identify metabolites significantly upregulated in midbrain (MB) vs hippocampal (HIP) regions of a mouse brain DESI section, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction and fold-change filtering. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: Univariate Wilcoxon rank-sum differential testing between pixel clusters defined on spatial metabolomics (MSI) data, used in SMAnalyst's workflow to identify metabolites significantly upregulated in midbrain (MB) vs hippocampal (HIP) regions of a mouse brain DESI section, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction and fold-change filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When regions have not been defined — if no UMAP-kmeans or manual ROI assignment exists yet, run SMAnalyst's pixel clustering or ROI drawing first rather than testing on arbitrary groupings When the comparison requires parametric modeling of covariates or replicate-level design rather than pixel-level univariate ranking When input is raw IMS mass-spec data rather than an already-picked, QC-filtered feature matrix of ion intensities per pixel

skills.description: Use when comparing a numeric spectral or ranking feature between two independent groups (e.g., correct rank #1 vs lower-ranked FSA formula assignments) where the feature is non-normally distributed, so a rank-based test like Wilcoxon rank-sum with medians/quartiles is required.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison Use when comparing a numeric spectral or ranking feature between two independent groups (e.g., correct rank #1 vs lower-ranked FSA formula assignments) where the feature is non-normally distributed, so a rank-based test like Wilcoxon rank-sum with medians/quartiles is required. The feature is normally distributed and a two-sample t-test is statistically appropriate — the rank-sum test is chosen here specifically because fragment numbers were not normally distributed The comparison involves paired/matched observations rather than two independent groups (Wilcoxon rank-sum assumes independence) Input is raw MS/MS peak lists rather than already-computed per-spectrum feature records from an FSA ranking run http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum testing of per-spectrum spectral features (fragment count, inter-peak-distance SD, CF ratio, top-two-score gap) split by formula-ranking outcome (rank #1 vs rank 2+) to identify which features statistically discriminate correct formula assignments made by FSA. metabolomics/v3 10.1007/s11306-025-02379-0
skills.summary: Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum testing of per-spectrum spectral features (fragment count, inter-peak-distance SD, CF ratio, top-two-score gap) split by formula-ranking outcome (rank #1 vs rank 2+) to identify which features statistically discriminate correct formula assignments made by FSA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature is normally distributed and a two-sample t-test is statistically appropriate — the rank-sum test is chosen here specifically because fragment numbers were not normally distributed The comparison involves paired/matched observations rather than two independent groups (Wilcoxon rank-sum assumes independence) Input is raw MS/MS peak lists rather than already-computed per-spectrum feature records from an FSA ranking run

skills.description: Use when comparing relative-abundance metabolomics features (e.g. bile-amidate intensities) across three unordered phenotype groups (non-IBD control, CD, UC) without assuming normality, and per-feature adjusted p-values are needed.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison Use when comparing relative-abundance metabolomics features (e.g. bile-amidate intensities) across three unordered phenotype groups (non-IBD control, CD, UC) without assuming normality, and per-feature adjusted p-values are needed. Input is raw MS/MS spectra or mzML files rather than a processed relative-quantification feature table The metabolites of interest lack prior structural confirmation (feature-to-conjugate assignment), e.g. candidates only found via MASST spectral matching without synthesis validation Groups have paired or matched designs requiring a signed-rank test rather than the independent-sample rank-sum test http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Non-parametric two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney) testing of metabolite feature abundances across phenotype groups, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction, used here to validate that microbial bile acid amidates are elevated in Crohn's disease in the iHMP2 and PRISM cohorts. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41586-023-06906-8
skills.summary: Non-parametric two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney) testing of metabolite feature abundances across phenotype groups, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction, used here to validate that microbial bile acid amidates are elevated in Crohn's disease in the iHMP2 and PRISM cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw MS/MS spectra or mzML files rather than a processed relative-quantification feature table The metabolites of interest lack prior structural confirmation (feature-to-conjugate assignment), e.g. candidates only found via MASST spectral matching without synthesis validation Groups have paired or matched designs requiring a signed-rank test rather than the independent-sample rank-sum test

skills.description: Use when comparing two unpaired groups on numeric features (metabolomics peak intensities, omics abundances) or when relating a MOFA factor to binary clinical metadata, without assuming normality.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing Use when comparing two unpaired groups on numeric features (metabolomics peak intensities, omics abundances) or when relating a MOFA factor to binary clinical metadata, without assuming normality. The comparison involves more than two groups or paired/matched samples — the Wilcoxon rank-sum test as implemented here covers two unpaired groups only The goal is RNA-seq count differential expression, for which BiomiX uses DESeq2/Limma instead of the metabolomics Wilcoxon pipeline Input is transcriptomics count data or methylation arrays, handled by DESeq2/Limma or ChAMP respectively rather than peak-level Wilcoxon testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Non-parametric Wilcoxon (Mann-Whitney) rank-sum testing as implemented in BiomiX to detect differential omics features between two groups (e.g., PTB vs HC metabolomics peaks) and to test binary clinical variables against MOFA factors, with False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) correction of p-values. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-024-06022-y
skills.summary: Non-parametric Wilcoxon (Mann-Whitney) rank-sum testing as implemented in BiomiX to detect differential omics features between two groups (e.g., PTB vs HC metabolomics peaks) and to test binary clinical variables against MOFA factors, with False Discovery Rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) correction of p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison involves more than two groups or paired/matched samples — the Wilcoxon rank-sum test as implemented here covers two unpaired groups only The goal is RNA-seq count differential expression, for which BiomiX uses DESeq2/Limma instead of the metabolomics Wilcoxon pipeline Input is transcriptomics count data or methylation arrays, handled by DESeq2/Limma or ChAMP respectively rather than peak-level Wilcoxon testing

skills.description: Use when comparing ion intensities between two spatial metabolomics regions (auto-clustered or manually drawn ROIs) on a feature matrix, and metabolite intensity distributions cannot be assumed normal.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-with-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-with-fdr-correction Use when comparing ion intensities between two spatial metabolomics regions (auto-clustered or manually drawn ROIs) on a feature matrix, and metabolite intensity distributions cannot be assumed normal. Input is raw imaging MS data (e.g., imzML) rather than a processed pixel-by-m/z feature matrix — peak picking and QC must come first Comparison requires more than two regions or repeated-measures design — Wilcoxon rank-sum is a two-group test Pixels are spatially autocorrelated and must be treated as independent samples — the benchmark treats all pixels in a group as samples, which can inflate significance http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A non-parametric differential analysis for spatial metabolomics pixels: run the Wilcoxon rank-sum test on ion intensities between two regions of interest (e.g., midbrain vs hippocampal pixel groups), then correct p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and filter by fold-change/significance. metabolomics/v3 10.3390/biom15111562
skills.summary: A non-parametric differential analysis for spatial metabolomics pixels: run the Wilcoxon rank-sum test on ion intensities between two regions of interest (e.g., midbrain vs hippocampal pixel groups), then correct p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and filter by fold-change/significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw imaging MS data (e.g., imzML) rather than a processed pixel-by-m/z feature matrix — peak picking and QC must come first Comparison requires more than two regions or repeated-measures design — Wilcoxon rank-sum is a two-group test Pixels are spatially autocorrelated and must be treated as independent samples — the benchmark treats all pixels in a group as samples, which can inflate significance

skills.description: Use when two models are evaluated on the SAME set of features (e.g. the 466 annotated metabolites of the IBD PRISM dataset) under paired CV settings, and you need a nonparametric test on paired per-feature SCC differences.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing Use when two models are evaluated on the SAME set of features (e.g. the 466 annotated metabolites of the IBD PRISM dataset) under paired CV settings, and you need a nonparametric test on paired per-feature SCC differences. The two SCC distributions come from independent, unpaired evaluations (e.g. different metabolite sets or different CV folds), since the signed-rank test requires metabolite-level pairing Comparing more than two models simultaneously, where a Friedman test would be the appropriate paired nonparametric alternative Metabolites with zero SCC difference dominate the pairs, invalidating rank-based inference on the signed differences http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Nonparametric paired significance test applied to per-metabolite Spearman correlation coefficients (SCC) from two MiMeNet models trained under identical cross-validation, to determine whether full-metabolome multivariate learning significantly improves prediction of the annotated metabolite subset. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009021
skills.summary: Nonparametric paired significance test applied to per-metabolite Spearman correlation coefficients (SCC) from two MiMeNet models trained under identical cross-validation, to determine whether full-metabolome multivariate learning significantly improves prediction of the annotated metabolite subset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two SCC distributions come from independent, unpaired evaluations (e.g. different metabolite sets or different CV folds), since the signed-rank test requires metabolite-level pairing Comparing more than two models simultaneously, where a Friedman test would be the appropriate paired nonparametric alternative Metabolites with zero SCC difference dominate the pairs, invalidating rank-based inference on the signed differences

skills.description: Use when two structure-prediction methods have been run on the same paired set of MS2 spectra (e.g., 93 CASMI 2017 spectra or a 660-spectrum test set) and you need a significance test on their per-spectrum similarity distributions.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-test
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-test Use when two structure-prediction methods have been run on the same paired set of MS2 spectra (e.g., 93 CASMI 2017 spectra or a 660-spectrum test set) and you need a significance test on their per-spectrum similarity distributions. The two methods were applied to different, non-paired sets of spectra — the signed-rank test requires paired per-spectrum observations on the identical spectrum set. The comparison is between a single method's score distribution and a fixed reference value rather than two paired per-spectrum methods. The input is high-resolution-spectrum benchmarking where the paper itself does not claim a performance advantage for TeFT (quantitative comparison with SIRIUS4/MSNovelist/MassGenie is not provided). http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies the Wilcoxon signed-rank test to paired per-spectrum performance scores (e.g., Tanimoto/Dice structure-similarity values) to test whether two mass-spectrometry structure-prediction tools, such as TeFT vs SIRIUS4 or MetFrag, differ significantly on the same benchmark spectra. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s42004-024-01189-0
skills.summary: Applies the Wilcoxon signed-rank test to paired per-spectrum performance scores (e.g., Tanimoto/Dice structure-similarity values) to test whether two mass-spectrometry structure-prediction tools, such as TeFT vs SIRIUS4 or MetFrag, differ significantly on the same benchmark spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two methods were applied to different, non-paired sets of spectra — the signed-rank test requires paired per-spectrum observations on the identical spectrum set. The comparison is between a single method's score distribution and a fixed reference value rather than two paired per-spectrum methods. The input is high-resolution-spectrum benchmarking where the paper itself does not claim a performance advantage for TeFT (quantitative comparison with SIRIUS4/MSNovelist/MassGenie is not provided).

skills.description: Use when two classifiers (e.g., MSMCE-ResNet50 vs. ResNet50 baseline) have been evaluated on the same N = 6 stratified CV folds and you must test whether the paired metric improvement (Accuracy, F1) is statistically significant.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing Use when two classifiers (e.g., MSMCE-ResNet50 vs. ResNet50 baseline) have been evaluated on the same N = 6 stratified CV folds and you must test whether the paired metric improvement (Accuracy, F1) is statistically significant. Metrics come from independent (unpaired) runs rather than the same fold splits — the paired signed-rank assumption is violated The comparison involves ablation variants trained on the entire training set (not k-fold split) and evaluated only on the hold-out test set, so no per-fold paired samples exist Sample size or class balance is extreme (e.g., severely imbalanced class distributions or too-few samples), which the paper flags as limiting model performance and hence the reliability of the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies the paired, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test to determine whether performance metrics of MSMCE-integrated models differ significantly from their single-channel baselines across k-fold cross-validation splits, using p < 0.05 as the significance threshold. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pone.0321239
skills.summary: Applies the paired, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test to determine whether performance metrics of MSMCE-integrated models differ significantly from their single-channel baselines across k-fold cross-validation splits, using p < 0.05 as the significance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Metrics come from independent (unpaired) runs rather than the same fold splits — the paired signed-rank assumption is violated The comparison involves ablation variants trained on the entire training set (not k-fold split) and evaluated only on the hold-out test set, so no per-fold paired samples exist Sample size or class balance is extreme (e.g., severely imbalanced class distributions or too-few samples), which the paper flags as limiting model performance and hence the reliability of the comparison

skills.description: Use when ranked candidate structures from a de novo model and one or more database-search methods exist for the same spectra and you must quantify which method is better per spectrum and at k = 1, 10, 50.
skills.name: win-rate-statistical-comparison
skills.search_text: win-rate-statistical-comparison Use when ranked candidate structures from a de novo model and one or more database-search methods exist for the same spectra and you must quantify which method is better per spectrum and at k = 1, 10, 50. Comparing de novo models designed and trained for MS/MS spectra against GC-EI-MS results — the article notes such head-to-head comparison is challenging because all existing de novo approaches target MS/MS, not GC-EI-MS Predictions that cannot be decoded to SMILES, since the comparison metric is Tanimoto similarity of Morgan fingerprints computed from structures Spectra sets whose compounds overlap the training data — all test sets must be filtered to exclude compounds present in the synthetic or experimental training datasets before comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Protocol for statistically comparing de novo structure predictions (e.g., SpecTUS) against database-search methods (HSS, SSS, BDC) on an EI-MS test set, using top-k accuracy (Acc_k), Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity, and per-spectrum win / at-least-as-good rates. metabolomics/v3 10.48550/arxiv.2502.05114
skills.summary: Protocol for statistically comparing de novo structure predictions (e.g., SpecTUS) against database-search methods (HSS, SSS, BDC) on an EI-MS test set, using top-k accuracy (Acc_k), Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity, and per-spectrum win / at-least-as-good rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing de novo models designed and trained for MS/MS spectra against GC-EI-MS results — the article notes such head-to-head comparison is challenging because all existing de novo approaches target MS/MS, not GC-EI-MS Predictions that cannot be decoded to SMILES, since the comparison metric is Tanimoto similarity of Morgan fingerprints computed from structures Spectra sets whose compounds overlap the training data — all test sets must be filtered to exclude compounds present in the synthetic or experimental training datasets before comparison

skills.description: Use when a peak-based NMR feature/sample/peak-value matrix (e.g. from speaq 2.0 peak picking, grouping and BuildFeatureMatrix) must be tested for features that significantly differ between two or more sample classes.
skills.name: wine-metabolomics-class-discrimination
skills.search_text: wine-metabolomics-class-discrimination Use when a peak-based NMR feature/sample/peak-value matrix (e.g. from speaq 2.0 peak picking, grouping and BuildFeatureMatrix) must be tested for features that significantly differ between two or more sample classes. Input is raw 1D spectra rather than a peak-grouped feature matrix — peak picking, grouping and peak filling (getWaveletPeaks/PeakGrouper/BuildFeatureMatrix) must run first. The analysis goal is spectral alignment or quantitation of raw spectra (CluPA alignment, BW-ratio quantitation), which are separate speaq workflows for versions <= 1.2.3 features. Class labels are unknown or the goal is unsupervised exploration — use PCA as in the paper's wine data supplementary analysis instead of the class-based linear model. http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Apply speaq 2.0's linear-model differential analysis to a Pareto-scaled NMR feature matrix (e.g. the wine spectra dataset) to identify features that significantly discriminate between predefined sample classes (red vs white wines). metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1006018
skills.summary: Apply speaq 2.0's linear-model differential analysis to a Pareto-scaled NMR feature matrix (e.g. the wine spectra dataset) to identify features that significantly discriminate between predefined sample classes (red vs white wines).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 1D spectra rather than a peak-grouped feature matrix — peak picking, grouping and peak filling (getWaveletPeaks/PeakGrouper/BuildFeatureMatrix) must run first. The analysis goal is spectral alignment or quantitation of raw spectra (CluPA alignment, BW-ratio quantitation), which are separate speaq workflows for versions <= 1.2.3 features. Class labels are unknown or the goal is unsupervised exploration — use PCA as in the paper's wine data supplementary analysis instead of the class-based linear model.

skills.description: Use when a tabular dataset with a categorical class label (e.g. wine quality rating) must be turned into a class-prediction pipeline whose pre-processing, feature selection and estimator settings are optimised by exhaustive grid search and validated on unseen samples.
skills.name: wine-quality-supervised-classification
skills.search_text: wine-quality-supervised-classification Use when a tabular dataset with a categorical class label (e.g. wine quality rating) must be turned into a class-prediction pipeline whose pre-processing, feature selection and estimator settings are optimised by exhaustive grid search and validated on unseen samples. The target variable is continuous and the task is regression rather than categorical class prediction. There is no class label available, so the problem is unsupervised (clustering, dimensionality reduction only). The dataset has substantial missing values that should be imputed rather than reduced to complete cases, since the mirrored software automatically filters missing values before activities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds a supervised class-prediction pipeline on the UCI wine quality table, mirroring Instant Clue's scikit-learn-based prediction module: chained pre-processing, feature selection/reduction and estimator steps exhaustively tuned by grid search and evaluated on a held-out test partition. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-018-31154-6
skills.summary: Builds a supervised class-prediction pipeline on the UCI wine quality table, mirroring Instant Clue's scikit-learn-based prediction module: chained pre-processing, feature selection/reduction and estimator steps exhaustively tuned by grid search and evaluated on a held-out test partition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target variable is continuous and the task is regression rather than categorical class prediction. There is no class label available, so the problem is unsupervised (clustering, dimensionality reduction only). The dataset has substantial missing values that should be imputed rather than reduced to complete cases, since the mirrored software automatically filters missing values before activities.

skills.description: Use when a vendor-locked Windows executable (Agilent .d, Thermo .raw converter) must run on Ubuntu or another Unix-like OS and no native port exists.
skills.name: wine-windows-executable-deployment
skills.search_text: wine-windows-executable-deployment Use when a vendor-locked Windows executable (Agilent .d, Thermo .raw converter) must run on Ubuntu or another Unix-like OS and no native port exists. You are already on Windows 10 or another Windows host — run the executable directly with no dependencies. The tool provides a native Linux binary or the vendor library supports cross-platform compilation — Wine would add unnecessary overhead. The task is pure data access on already-converted .mza files (just use h5py/rhdf5; no Wine needed). http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Run Windows-only command-line MS data tools (e.g., the MZA executable) on Unix-like systems by building a Wine-based Docker container or installing Wine plus wine-mono, so vendor raw files can be converted on Linux without a Windows host. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00313
skills.summary: Run Windows-only command-line MS data tools (e.g., the MZA executable) on Unix-like systems by building a Wine-based Docker container or installing Wine plus wine-mono, so vendor raw files can be converted on Linux without a Windows host.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are already on Windows 10 or another Windows host — run the executable directly with no dependencies. The tool provides a native Linux binary or the vendor library supports cross-platform compilation — Wine would add unnecessary overhead. The task is pure data access on already-converted .mza files (just use h5py/rhdf5; no Wine needed).

skills.description: Use when quality-controlling an expression dataset where samples should cohere within biological conditions — e.g. before differential-expression analysis, to verify same-organ, same-tumor-status samples show pairwise Pearson correlations >0.70 and to flag low-expression outlier samples.
skills.name: within-condition-correlation-threshold-screening
skills.search_text: within-condition-correlation-threshold-screening Use when quality-controlling an expression dataset where samples should cohere within biological conditions — e.g. before differential-expression analysis, to verify same-organ, same-tumor-status samples show pairwise Pearson correlations >0.70 and to flag low-expression outlier samples. Input is not sample-level expression data with condition metadata — this skill groups by organ/tumor status and is meaningless without it Goal is gene-level rather than sample-level assessment — e.g. Spearman correlation of a single gene (such as CDKN2A) against all genes is a different analysis The dataset has already been filtered and all within-condition pairwise Pearson correlations are known to exceed 0.70 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A sample-level QC skill that uses MOG to compute pairwise Pearson correlations among samples from the same biological condition (organ and tumor status) and screens them against a >0.70 acceptance threshold to detect aberrant samples such as the LUAD outlier removed from the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/nar/gkz1209
skills.summary: A sample-level QC skill that uses MOG to compute pairwise Pearson correlations among samples from the same biological condition (organ and tumor status) and screens them against a >0.70 acceptance threshold to detect aberrant samples such as the LUAD outlier removed from the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not sample-level expression data with condition metadata — this skill groups by organ/tumor status and is meaningless without it Goal is gene-level rather than sample-level assessment — e.g. Spearman correlation of a single gene (such as CDKN2A) against all genes is a different analysis The dataset has already been filtered and all within-condition pairwise Pearson correlations are known to exceed 0.70

skills.description: Use when comparing directed vs mixed reporter_score modes on a KO abundance table and you must confirm that directed-mode enriched pathways show consistent within-pathway KO directions while mixed-mode sign cancellation precludes trend interpretation.
skills.name: within-pathway-trend-consistency-checking
skills.search_text: within-pathway-trend-consistency-checking Use when comparing directed vs mixed reporter_score modes on a KO abundance table and you must confirm that directed-mode enriched pathways show consistent within-pathway KO directions while mixed-mode sign cancellation precludes trend interpretation. The KO abundance table has been prefiltered before enrichment — GRSA is threshold-free and expects the full background You need quantitative pathway trend direction from mixed-mode reporter score signs — those signs are uninterpretable due to cancellation of opposing-trend KOs The task is differential KO testing only, with no pathway-level aggregation or mode comparison required http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Verifies that pathways enriched in directed-mode GRSA (ReporterScore) carry concordant within-pathway KO trend directions, whereas mixed-mode reporter score signs are uninterpretable because opposing-trend KOs cancel. Grounded in the directed/mixed mode distinction of Peng et al. 2024, Briefings in Bioinformatics (doi:10.1093/bib/bbae116). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bib/bbae116
skills.summary: Verifies that pathways enriched in directed-mode GRSA (ReporterScore) carry concordant within-pathway KO trend directions, whereas mixed-mode reporter score signs are uninterpretable because opposing-trend KOs cancel. Grounded in the directed/mixed mode distinction of Peng et al. 2024, Briefings in Bioinformatics (doi:10.1093/bib/bbae116).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The KO abundance table has been prefiltered before enrichment — GRSA is threshold-free and expects the full background You need quantitative pathway trend direction from mixed-mode reporter score signs — those signs are uninterpretable due to cancellation of opposing-trend KOs The task is differential KO testing only, with no pathway-level aggregation or mode comparison required

skills.description: Use when comparing feature-detection/quantification consistency of preprocessing workflows (e.g. two-stage apLCMS vs traditional apLCMS vs XCMS) on replicated multi-batch LC/MS data with known replicate triplets.
skills.name: within-replicate-cv-consistency-evaluation
skills.search_text: within-replicate-cv-consistency-evaluation Use when comparing feature-detection/quantification consistency of preprocessing workflows (e.g. two-stage apLCMS vs traditional apLCMS vs XCMS) on replicated multi-batch LC/MS data with known replicate triplets. Data are not generated in multiple batches or lack replicate triplets, so within-triplet CV and batch-aware comparison are not meaningful Input is already a processed feature table with no access to the raw CDF profile files needed to re-run the preprocessing sweeps being compared The goal is differential-ablation or biological interpretation rather than evaluating preprocessing consistency across methods/thresholds http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates consistency of LC/MS metabolomics preprocessing pipelines by computing the proportion of zeros in the aligned feature matrix and the within-replicate-triplet coefficient of variation (CV), as used to compare two-stage batch-aware apLCMS against traditional apLCMS and XCMS across min.exp threshold sweeps on the multi-batch ST000868 yeast dataset. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41598-020-70850-0
skills.summary: Evaluates consistency of LC/MS metabolomics preprocessing pipelines by computing the proportion of zeros in the aligned feature matrix and the within-replicate-triplet coefficient of variation (CV), as used to compare two-stage batch-aware apLCMS against traditional apLCMS and XCMS across min.exp threshold sweeps on the multi-batch ST000868 yeast dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not generated in multiple batches or lack replicate triplets, so within-triplet CV and batch-aware comparison are not meaningful Input is already a processed feature table with no access to the raw CDF profile files needed to re-run the preprocessing sweeps being compared The goal is differential-ablation or biological interpretation rather than evaluating preprocessing consistency across methods/thresholds

skills.description: Use when the same subjects contribute paired/longitudinal metabolomics measurements (e.g., venous and arterial samples at matched time points) and you need to rank metabolites by significance for within-subject differential analysis or feature selection.
skills.name: within-subject-correlation-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: within-subject-correlation-statistical-testing Use when the same subjects contribute paired/longitudinal metabolomics measurements (e.g., venous and arterial samples at matched time points) and you need to rank metabolites by significance for within-subject differential analysis or feature selection. Measurements are from independent, unrelated groups with no within-subject pairing — use a between-groups model (e.g., Mixed ANOVA) instead The metabolite values are not numeric or the data are still in wide format — checking data types and wide-to-long transformation must happen first The dataset has unaddressed missing values — imputation is required before analysis in MeTEor http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Statistical testing of metabolite features across multiple paired measurements taken within the same subjects — implemented in MeTEor's Repeated Measures ANOVA module — used for feature selection and to identify metabolites differing between within-subject conditions (e.g., venous vs arterial blood in the covid_data study). metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioadv/vbae178
skills.summary: Statistical testing of metabolite features across multiple paired measurements taken within the same subjects — implemented in MeTEor's Repeated Measures ANOVA module — used for feature selection and to identify metabolites differing between within-subject conditions (e.g., venous vs arterial blood in the covid_data study).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Measurements are from independent, unrelated groups with no within-subject pairing — use a between-groups model (e.g., Mixed ANOVA) instead The metabolite values are not numeric or the data are still in wide format — checking data types and wide-to-long transformation must happen first The dataset has unaddressed missing values — imputation is required before analysis in MeTEor

skills.description: Use when you have a lipidomics MS/MS dataset with a reference list of reported lipids and need to measure the recall gain contributed by WMYn-regenerated (5th-level) fingerprints versus a truncated 1st–4th-level library and the MS-DIAL public database.
skills.name: wmys-regenerated-fingerprint-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: wmys-regenerated-fingerprint-recall-evaluation Use when you have a lipidomics MS/MS dataset with a reference list of reported lipids and need to measure the recall gain contributed by WMYn-regenerated (5th-level) fingerprints versus a truncated 1st–4th-level library and the MS-DIAL public database. The input dataset has no MS/MS spectra (MS1-only features cannot be scored by the EQ-module MS2 library search). The goal is C=C double-bond localization — use the Paternò–Büchi (PB) derivatization workflow instead of this recall benchmark. The analytes are non-lipid metabolites outside LipidIN's 121-subclass lipid coverage; the 168.6-million-entry lipid fragmentation library does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3369 Quantifies how much lipid recall is gained by adding the WMYn-regenerated 5th-level fingerprint library to LipidIN's hierarchical (1st–4th level) library, benchmarked against the MS-DIAL public database. The benchmark case is the mouse aging-associated lipidome atlas, where the 5-level library must reproduce 93.64% recall of 2704 reported lipids. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-025-59683-5
skills.summary: Quantifies how much lipid recall is gained by adding the WMYn-regenerated 5th-level fingerprint library to LipidIN's hierarchical (1st–4th level) library, benchmarked against the MS-DIAL public database. The benchmark case is the mouse aging-associated lipidome atlas, where the 5-level library must reproduce 93.64% recall of 2704 reported lipids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input dataset has no MS/MS spectra (MS1-only features cannot be scored by the EQ-module MS2 library search). The goal is C=C double-bond localization — use the Paternò–Büchi (PB) derivatization workflow instead of this recall benchmark. The analytes are non-lipid metabolites outside LipidIN's 121-subclass lipid coverage; the 168.6-million-entry lipid fragmentation library does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you need learnt spectral embeddings from a large MS/MS corpus (e.g. GNPS-derived UniqueInchikey or AllPositive datasets) instead of peak-matching cosine scores, to compare spectra or detect structurally related molecules.
skills.name: word2vec-embedding-inference
skills.search_text: word2vec-embedding-inference Use when you need learnt spectral embeddings from a large MS/MS corpus (e.g. GNPS-derived UniqueInchikey or AllPositive datasets) instead of peak-matching cosine scores, to compare spectra or detect structurally related molecules. When no training data are available — unlike cosine scores, Spec2Vec needs training data to learn fragment peak relationships When the training set does not include a large fraction of the fragment/loss features present in the query data (e.g. small training corpora, or peak words with more m/z decimals, causing many missing words) When only structural similarity between known molecules is needed — Tanimoto on InChIKey-derived structures is the direct measure, not spectral embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Adapts Word2Vec (natural language processing) to MS/MS data by training on documents of peak and loss words so that related fragments and neutral losses are embedded as vectors pointing in similar directions, enabling learnt spectral similarity scores such as Spec2Vec. metabolomics/v3 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008724
skills.summary: Adapts Word2Vec (natural language processing) to MS/MS data by training on documents of peak and loss words so that related fragments and neutral losses are embedded as vectors pointing in similar directions, enabling learnt spectral similarity scores such as Spec2Vec.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no training data are available — unlike cosine scores, Spec2Vec needs training data to learn fragment peak relationships When the training set does not include a large fraction of the fragment/loss features present in the query data (e.g. small training corpora, or peak words with more m/z decimals, causing many missing words) When only structural similarity between known molecules is needed — Tanimoto on InChIKey-derived structures is the direct measure, not spectral embeddings

skills.description: Use when predicted or measured EI mass spectra must be converted into fixed-length dense vectors for approximate nearest-neighbor library matching, e.g. before building or querying an HNSW index over a million-scale in-silico EI-MS library.
skills.name: word2vec-spectral-embedding
skills.search_text: word2vec-spectral-embedding Use when predicted or measured EI mass spectra must be converted into fixed-length dense vectors for approximate nearest-neighbor library matching, e.g. before building or querying an HNSW index over a million-scale in-silico EI-MS library. When the task is raw experimental-spectrum comparison against an experimental library (e.g., NIST 2017 alone) rather than fast matching of a million-scale in-silico library — a direct similarity method may suffice. When spectra were not generated in the same peak-token format used to train the Word2vec model; mismatched tokenization/embedding spaces will corrupt nearest-neighbor results. When the downstream index is an exact brute-force vector search rather than HNSW-based FastEI matching and embedding training cost is not justified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Transforms electron ionization mass spectra into low-dimensional spectral embeddings by treating each spectrum as a 'sentence' of peak tokens and summing peak embeddings from a gensim Word2vec model (CBOW, dim 500, window 1000), enabling more accurate compound identification via FastEI's HNSW matching. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41467-023-39279-7
skills.summary: Transforms electron ionization mass spectra into low-dimensional spectral embeddings by treating each spectrum as a 'sentence' of peak tokens and summing peak embeddings from a gensim Word2vec model (CBOW, dim 500, window 1000), enabling more accurate compound identification via FastEI's HNSW matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is raw experimental-spectrum comparison against an experimental library (e.g., NIST 2017 alone) rather than fast matching of a million-scale in-silico library — a direct similarity method may suffice. When spectra were not generated in the same peak-token format used to train the Word2vec model; mismatched tokenization/embedding spaces will corrupt nearest-neighbor results. skills.name: word2vec-spectrum-embedding-training
skills.search_text: word2vec-spectrum-embedding-training Use when you need to build a Spec2Vec spectral similarity score and must train (or select a pretrained) Word2Vec embedding from a large processed MS/MS library such as the AllPositive GNPS dataset. When only a tiny spectral dataset is available: missing words become a relevant issue when models are trained on smaller datasets, and the training set must include a large fraction of the fragment ions and losses seen in the query data When a training-data-free metric is required (e.g. quick pairwise cosine/modified cosine on raw peaks) — Spec2Vec, unlike cosine scores, needs training data to learn fragment peak relationships For GC-MS data: the study only demonstrated performance on LC-MS data http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains a Word2Vec (gensim) model on mass spectra converted to documents of peak/loss words so that related fragments and neutral losses learn similar vector directions, enabling the learned Spec2Vec similarity score. skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a tiny spectral dataset is available: missing words become a relevant issue when models are trained on smaller datasets, and the training set must include a large fraction of the fragment ions and losses seen in the query data When a training-data-free metric is required (e.g. quick pairwise cosine/modified cosine on raw peaks) — Spec2Vec, unlike cosine scores, needs training data to learn fragment peak relationships For GC-MS data: the study only demonstrated performance on LC-MS data

skills.description: Use when one or more normalized peak tables produced by candidate processing workflows (S1–S4 outputs) must be evaluated for study-specific performance and ranked via the five-criterion Good/Fair/Poor scheme of NOREVA.
skills.name: workflow-good-fair-poor-classification
skills.search_text: workflow-good-fair-poor-classification Use when one or more normalized peak tables produced by candidate processing workflows (S1–S4 outputs) must be evaluated for study-specific performance and ranked via the five-criterion Good/Fair/Poor scheme of NOREVA. Any class or timepoint in the dataset has fewer than 6 samples — criterion Cc (CWrel) is unsuitable and must be skipped No reference metabolites (e.g., spike-ins/internal standards) are available — criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied, so the full five-criterion labeling is not feasible The input is still raw instrument data (e.g., vendor-format MS files) — the skill expects an already-normalized peak table, and raw-to-open-format conversion/preparation is handled upstream (Proteowizard, XCMS, NMRProc Flow) NOREVA's final (S5) performance-assessment stage: score each candidate metabolomic processing workflow with five independent criteria — Ca (PMAD), Cb (purity), Cc (CWrel), Cd (AUC), Ce (LogFC) — and label it Good/Fair/Poor. This is how the protocol picks the study-specific optimal workflow instead of relying on a single metric. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41596-021-00636-9
skills.summary: NOREVA's final (S5) performance-assessment stage: score each candidate metabolomic processing workflow with five independent criteria — Ca (PMAD), Cb (purity), Cc (CWrel), Cd (AUC), Ce (LogFC) — and label it Good/Fair/Poor. This is how the protocol picks the study-specific optimal workflow instead of relying on a single metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Any class or timepoint in the dataset has fewer than 6 samples — criterion Cc (CWrel) is unsuitable and must be skipped No reference metabolites (e.g., spike-ins/internal standards) are available — criterion Ce (LogFC) cannot be applied, so the full five-criterion labeling is not feasible The input is still raw instrument data (e.g., vendor-format MS files) — the skill expects an already-normalized peak table, and raw-to-open-format conversion/preparation is handled upstream (Proteowizard, XCMS, NMRProc Flow)

skills.description: Use when LC-HRMS feature tables (accurate m/z, RT, MS2) from xenobiotic incubation or exposure samples need reaction-guided metabolite annotation without authentic standards or reference spectral libraries.
skills.name: xenobiotic-metabolite-annotation
skills.search_text: xenobiotic-metabolite-annotation Use when LC-HRMS feature tables (accurate m/z, RT, MS2) from xenobiotic incubation or exposure samples need reaction-guided metabolite annotation without authentic standards or reference spectral libraries. The goal is bottom-up identification against existing reference spectral libraries for known compounds with authentic standards — CMDN is designed for previously uncharacterized, reaction-derived metabolites lacking standards. Input is raw vendor files without prior peak picking — CMDN expects peak-picked feature tables (e.g., from MS-Dial 4.80) with m/z, RT, and MS2 peak lists. The analytes are intact parent chemicals only, with no biotransformation (metabolic derivatization) hypothesis to test. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 High-throughput, 'top-down' annotation of reaction-derived xenobiotic metabolites using the CMDN framework, which couples enzymatic biotransformation assays (e.g., human liver S9 fractions over 1,021 pesticides) with a triple-layered MS data processing architecture (DMS, RCS, SSN) on LC-HRMS data. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.est.5c08558

skills.description: Use when you have an MZmine-preprocessed full-scan feature table (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area) and need to statistically filter which features are real chromatographic signals worth targeting for MS/MS fragmentation.
skills.name: xic-based-feature-assessment
skills.search_text: xic-based-feature-assessment Use when you have an MZmine-preprocessed full-scan feature table (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area) and need to statistically filter which features are real chromatographic signals worth targeting for MS/MS fragmentation. The input is MS/MS or DDA data rather than an MZmine full-scan MS1 feature table — RegFilter is applied to full-scan mode features to build SPLs for targeted fragmentation Features are already filtered or curated (e.g., coming from a scheduled precursor list) and no regression-based XIC assessment is needed The feature table lacks peak-area chromatographic information required for XIC extraction and linear regression fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assesses MZmine full-scan MS1 features by fitting linear regressions to their extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) and retaining only features meeting objective statistical criteria (R2 >= 0.9 with negative slope) using the RegFilter Python package, to build a curated scheduled precursor list (SPL). metabolomics/v3 10.1101/2024.08.07.607073
skills.summary: Assesses MZmine full-scan MS1 features by fitting linear regressions to their extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) and retaining only features meeting objective statistical criteria (R2 >= 0.9 with negative slope) using the RegFilter Python package, to build a curated scheduled precursor list (SPL).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is MS/MS or DDA data rather than an MZmine full-scan MS1 feature table — RegFilter is applied to full-scan mode features to build SPLs for targeted fragmentation Features are already filtered or curated (e.g., coming from a scheduled precursor list) and no regression-based XIC assessment is needed The feature table lacks peak-area chromatographic information required for XIC extraction and linear regression fitting

skills.description: Use when you have Thermo .raw files containing spiked-in Biognosys iRT peptides and need observed retention times or an rt-vs-iRT-score calibration line for use-case style targeted analysis in R.
skills.name: xic-derived-retention-time-annotation
skills.search_text: xic-derived-retention-time-annotation Use when you have Thermo .raw files containing spiked-in Biognosys iRT peptides and need observed retention times or an rt-vs-iRT-score calibration line for use-case style targeted analysis in R. The input is not a vendor .raw file (e.g. already-converted mzML or a precomputed chromatogram) — rawrr's readChromatogram wraps the vendor RawFileReader API and requires proprietary Thermo raw files. You need retention times from MS2-level fragment ion XICs rather than MS1 precursor XICs — then the filter string must be an MS2 filter (e.g. 'FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00 [100.0000-1015.0000]'), not filter = 'ms'. Your sample lacks spiked iRT peptide standards, so no iRT-score calibration reference exists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Derives observed retention times for iRT peptide precursors by computing extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) directly from Thermo Fisher Orbitrap raw files with the rawrr R package, then fits a linear rt-vs-iRT-score calibration model. It anchors spectral data to a shared retention-time scale for targeted proteomics workflows. metabolomics/v3 10.1021/acs.jproteome.0c00866
skills.summary: Derives observed retention times for iRT peptide precursors by computing extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) directly from Thermo Fisher Orbitrap raw files with the rawrr R package, then fits a linear rt-vs-iRT-score calibration model. It anchors spectral data to a shared retention-time scale for targeted proteomics workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a vendor .raw file (e.g. already-converted mzML or a precomputed chromatogram) — rawrr's readChromatogram wraps the vendor RawFileReader API and requires proprietary Thermo raw files. You need retention times from MS2-level fragment ion XICs rather than MS1 precursor XICs — then the filter string must be an MS2 filter (e.g. 'FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00 [100.0000-1015.0000]'), not filter = 'ms'. Your sample lacks spiked iRT peptide standards, so no iRT-score calibration reference exists.

skills.description: Use when you have a repository-scale collection of LC–MS/MS experiments (e.g. mzML files mined from MassIVE GNPS) and need to filter out files/spectra with unreliable precursor m/z before model training, grouping them into quality tiers.
skills.name: xic-instrument-mass-accuracy-filtering
skills.search_text: xic-instrument-mass-accuracy-filtering Use when you have a repository-scale collection of LC–MS/MS experiments (e.g. mzML files mined from MassIVE GNPS) and need to filter out files/spectra with unreliable precursor m/z before model training, grouping them into quality tiers. When the input is already a curated spectral library (e.g. MoNA or NIST20) with known-good reference spectra — the accuracy filter is designed for uncurated repository-scale mining output, not validated library entries. When analyzing a single small experiment where per-file m/z accuracy can be assessed directly by standard QC — the two-algorithm pipeline is aimed at repository-scale redundancy and quality triage. When downstream tasks require multiply charged or negative-mode spectra, since the GeMS mining and filtering pipeline targets predominantly positive-mode, singly charged metabolomics spectra. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimates the m/z accuracy of each LC–MS/MS experiment by inspecting extracted-ion chromatograms (XICs) and uses the resulting instrument-level accuracy scores to partition ~700 million mined MassIVE GNPS spectra into the GeMS-A, GeMS-B and GeMS-C quality subsets. metabolomics/v3 10.1038/s41587-025-02663-3
skills.summary: Estimates the m/z accuracy of each LC–MS/MS experiment by inspecting extracted-ion chromatograms (XICs) and uses the resulting instrument-level accuracy scores to partition ~700 million mined MassIVE GNPS spectra into the GeMS-A, GeMS-B and GeMS-C quality subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a curated spectral library (e.g. MoNA or NIST20) with known-good reference spectra — the accuracy filter is designed for uncurated repository-scale mining output, not validated library entries. When analyzing a single small experiment where per-file m/z accuracy can be assessed directly by standard QC — the two-algorithm pipeline is aimed at repository-scale redundancy and quality triage. When downstream tasks require multiply charged or negative-mode spectra, since the GeMS mining and filtering pipeline targets predominantly positive-mode, singly charged metabolomics spectra.

skills.description: Decision support for distinguishing co-eluting glycan isomers sharing an identical m/z in LC-MS extracted ion chromatograms, where mass accuracy alone cannot separate them and slope-based edge detection plus a relative intensity threshold is needed.
skills.name: xic-isomer-peak-detection-slope-criteria
skills.search_text: xic-isomer-peak-detection-slope-criteria Decision support for distinguishing co-eluting glycan isomers sharing an identical m/z in LC-MS extracted ion chromatograms, where mass accuracy alone cannot separate them and slope-based edge detection plus a relative intensity threshold is needed. Isomer peaks are separated by more than the fixed ±1.75 min retention-time window, so a different deconvolution or chromatographic-resolution approach is needed. The user needs de novo glycan identification rather than detection of isomers for glycans already in the MS1 Database. The sample is O-linked glycans; the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A chromatographic peak-calling method that detects isomer peaks co-eluting at the same m/z within a fixed ±1.75 min retention-time window by scanning the extracted ion chromatogram for a rising edge (3-of-4 consecutive positive intensity slopes) followed by a falling edge (3-of-4 consecutive negative slopes), then applying a relative-intensity threshold filter. metabolomics/v3 10.1186/s12859-023-05346-5
skills.summary: A chromatographic peak-calling method that detects isomer peaks co-eluting at the same m/z within a fixed ±1.75 min retention-time window by scanning the extracted ion chromatogram for a rising edge (3-of-4 consecutive positive intensity slopes) followed by a falling edge (3-of-4 consecutive negative slopes), then applying a relative-intensity threshold filter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Isomer peaks are separated by more than the fixed ±1.75 min retention-time window, so a different deconvolution or chromatographic-resolution approach is needed. The user needs de novo glycan identification rather than detection of isomers for glycans already in the MS1 Database. The sample is O-linked glycans; the app's scope is limited to N-linked glycans.

skills.description: Use when an aligned DBDI-MS feature table (one column per scan, one row per feature) contains np.nan fields from scans where a signal was not detected, and downstream identify_adducts() analysis requires uniform-length XICs.
skills.name: xic-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: xic-missing-value-imputation Use when an aligned DBDI-MS feature table (one column per scan, one row per feature) contains np.nan fields from scans where a signal was not detected, and downstream identify_adducts() analysis requires uniform-length XICs. Input is already a raw list of matchms.Spectra or an unaligned spectra file — align_spectra() must be applied first; impute_intensities() expects the 2D aligned feature DataFrame. The aligned table contains no missing values (specs_aligned.isnull().values.any() is False) — imputation is unnecessary and baseline padding could distort complete traces. The downstream analysis does not require uniform-length XICs, e.g. pure spectrum-level matchms preprocessing pipelines with optional noise-reduction filters that bypass feature-table construction. DBDIpy's impute_intensities() performs two-stage missing-value imputation on aligned DBDI-MS feature tables: it interpolates missing intensities within each feature's signal region (method='linear') and pads with a noisy baseline, yielding uniform-length extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) ready for pointwise-correlation adduct/fragment detection. metabolomics/v3 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad088
skills.summary: DBDIpy's impute_intensities() performs two-stage missing-value imputation on aligned DBDI-MS feature tables: it interpolates missing intensities within each feature's signal region (method='linear') and pads with a noisy baseline, yielding uniform-length extracted ion chromatograms (XICs) ready for pointwise-correlation adduct/fragment detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a raw list of matchms.Spectra or an unaligned spectra file — align_spectra() must be applied first; impute_intensities() expects the 2D aligned feature DataFrame. The aligned table contains no missing values (specs_aligned.isnull().values.any() is False) — imputation is unnecessary and baseline padding could distort complete traces. The downstream analysis does not require uniform-length XICs, e.g. pure spectrum-level matchms preprocessing pipelines with optional noise-reduction filters that bypass feature-table construction.

skills.summary: Detects in-source adducts and fragments (e.g. [M-H2O+H]+, [M+O+H]+, [M+2O+H]+) in direct-injection plasma ionization MS datasets by combining pointwise Pearson correlation of extracted ion chromatograms with exact mass-difference filtering, as implemented in DBDIpy.identify_adducts().
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data still consists of raw unaligned mass spectra — alignment (align_spectra) and imputation (impute_intensities) must be done first to obtain uniform-length XICs.
